translation:
Wan Shijun's name was Fen, and his father was from the state of Zhao and his surname was Shi.
After the fall of Zhao State, he moved to Wen County.
Gaozu attacked Xiang Yu in the east and passed through Hanoi County. Shi Fen was fifteen years old at that time and was a minor official serving Gaozu.
Emperor Gaozu talked with him and liked his respectful and cautious attitude. He asked him: Who are the people in your family?
He replied: My mother is the only one in my family and unfortunately she is blind.
The family is very poor.
There is also a sister who can play the piano.
Gaozu asked again: Can you follow me?
He replied: I am willing to serve with all my strength.
Therefore, Emperor Gaozu called his sister into the palace to be a beauty, and asked Shi Fen to be the official in charge of receiving documents and interviews from the ministers. He moved his family to the middle family in Chang'an because his sister had become a beauty.
When Shi Fen served as an official until Emperor Xiaowen, he became a high-ranking official by accumulating merit.
He didn't know much about Confucianism, but he was as respectful and cautious as anyone else.
During the reign of Emperor Wen, Zhang Xiangru, Marquis of Dongyang, served as the Crown Prince and Tutor, but was later dismissed.
Emperor Wen chose someone who could be the prince's tutor. Everyone recommended Shi Fen, and Shi Fen became the prince's tutor.
When Emperor Jing came to the throne, he was appointed to the position of Jiuqing. Because he was too respectful and cautious and approached him, Emperor Jing was also afraid of him and made him the prime minister of the princes.
His eldest son Shi Jian, his second son Shi Jia, his third son Shi Yi, and his fourth son Shi Qing all had official positions of two thousand shi because of their docile temperament, respect for their elders, and caution in doing things. So Emperor Jing said: "Shi Jun and his four sons all have official positions of two thousand shi, and the honor and glory of being ministers is concentrated in their family."
He called Shi Fen the King of Wan Shi.
In the last years of Emperor Jing's reign, Wan Shijun enjoyed the salary of a doctor and returned home in old age. When the imperial court held grand ceremonies and issued orders, he attended as a minister.
When passing the palace gate, Wan Shijun must get out of the car and walk quickly to show respect. When seeing the emperor's driver, he must put his hand on the driver's chariot to express his greetings.
When his descendants and grandchildren serve as minor officials and come home to visit him, Wan Shijun must wear court clothes to receive them and not call them by their names.
When some of his descendants made mistakes, he would not scold them. Instead, he would sit on a side seat and face the table and refuse to eat.
After this, other descendants will blame the person who made the mistake one after another, and then ask for mercy from the elders of the clan. They will bare their upper body to express their apology and resolutely correct themselves, and then they will agree to their request.
When his adult children and grandchildren are around him, he must dress neatly and show a serious and tidy look, even if he is staying at home.
His servants are also very respectful and cautious.
Sometimes when the emperor would reward food and send it to his home, he would always kowtow and bow before eating it, just like in front of the emperor.
When he was attending the funeral, he was very sad and mournful.
Future generations will follow his teachings and do as he did.
Wan Shijun's family was famous in all counties and vassal states for their filial piety and prudence. Even the simple Confucian scholars in Qi and Lu thought that they were inferior to them.
summary: The lives of several officials from the Han Dynasty, focusing on their conduct and family traditions. Wan Shijun, originally from Zhao, served under Emperor Gaozu and rose through ranks due to his respectful and cautious nature. He became a tutor to the prince and later a high-ranking official, with his four sons also holding significant posts. His family was renowned for filial piety and prudence, influencing even Confucian scholars. Wan Shijun’s strict household rules included requiring descendants to show respect, and he would refuse to eat if they erred. His son Shi Jian was notably filial, washing his father’s clothes secretly and being meticulous in his duties. Another son, Shi Qing, became prime minister but struggled during turbulent times, eventually dying in office. The family’s tradition declined after his death.

translation:
When Emperor Jing was the crown prince, he invited the emperor's closest officials to a banquet, but Wei Wan refused to go because he was ill.
When Emperor Wen was about to die, he told Emperor Jing: Wei Wan is a loyal man, you should treat him well.
When Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing came to the throne, Emperor Jing did not reprimand Wei Wan for more than a year. Wei Wan just performed his duties more cautiously day by day.
Emperor Jing once visited Shanglinyuan and ordered Wei Wan, the lieutenant general, to ride in a carriage with him. When he came back, he asked Wei Wan: Do you know why you can ride in the same carriage with me?
Wei Wan said: From a small charioteer, I was lucky enough to be promoted to a lieutenant general due to my meritorious service. I don’t know why.
Emperor Jing asked again: When I became the crown prince, I invited you to a banquet, but you refused to come. Why?
He replied: I deserve to die, I was really sick at that time!
Emperor Jing gave him a sword.
Wei Wan said: The late Emperor once gave me a total of six swords. I dare not accept any more rewards from His Majesty.
Emperor Jing said: Swords are a favorite thing among people and are often used as gifts or in exchange for other things. How can you keep it until now? Wei Wan said: They are all still there.
The emperor sent someone to fetch the six swords. The swords were intact in their sheaths and had never been used.
When the Lang officers under the Zhong Lang general made mistakes, Wei Wan would often accept the consequences for them without arguing with others; when he had merit, he would always humbly give it to others.
The emperor believed that he was of upright character and loyal to himself, so he appointed him as the Taifu of Liu De, King of Hejian.
During the Seven Kingdoms Rebellion between Wu and Chu, the emperor appointed Wei Wan as a general. He led the army of the King of Hejian to attack the rebels of Wu and Chu, and made him a lieutenant.
Three years later, because of his military exploits, he was granted the title of Marquis of Jianling in the sixth year of Emperor Jing's reign.
The next year, Emperor Jing deposed Prince Li Liu Rong and killed the prince's uncle and others.
Emperor Jing thought Wei Wan was a loyal person and couldn't bear to let him handle this big case, so he gave him leave to go home. And let Zhi Du arrest and interrogate the Li clan members.
After handling this case, Emperor Jing appointed Liu Che, King of Jiaodong, as the crown prince, recruited Wei Wan, and appointed him as the crown prince and tutor.
After a long time, he was promoted to the imperial censor.
Five years later, he replaced Liu She, Taohou, as prime minister, and only reported matters within his duties to the court.
However, from the time he first became an official until he became prime minister, there was nothing to praise or blame.
The emperor thought that he was kind-hearted and could assist the young master. He respected and loved him very much and rewarded him with many things.
Wei Wan served as prime minister for three years, Emperor Jing died, and Emperor Wu ascended the throne.
During the Jianyuan period, when Emperor Jing was ill, many of the prisoners in various government offices were innocent people who had been wronged. As prime minister, he failed to fulfill his duties and was dismissed from his position as prime minister.
Later, Wei Wan died, and his son Wei Xin inherited the title of Marquis of Jianling.
Later, he lost his title because the aide's donation was irregular. There is no doubt that Saihou is from Nanyang.
He served Emperor Wen as a Langguan.
summary: Wei Wan, Marquis of Jianling, served Emperors Wen and Jing with loyalty and prudence. He refused a banquet invitation from the future Emperor Jing, claiming illness, and kept six swords given by Emperor Wen unused. He took blame for subordinates’ mistakes and deflected credit. During the Seven Kingdoms Rebellion, he led troops and was made marquis. He later became prime minister but was dismissed for failing to address injustices during Emperor Jing’s illness. Zhi Buyi, Marquis of Sai, was known for honesty, once apologizing for a mistaken accusation of theft. He served as imperial censor and was dismissed during Emperor Wu’s reign. He followed Laozi’s teachings and governed without seeking fame.

translation:
The person who lived in the same room with him asked for leave to visit his family and mistakenly took other people's gold. After some time, the owner of the gold found out and made random suspicions about Zhi Buyi. Zhi Buyi apologized to him and admitted the incident, and bought gold to repay him.
When the person who took leave to visit the family came back and returned the gold, the person who had lost the gold was extremely ashamed, so people said that he was undoubtedly an honest person.
Emperor Wen also praised and promoted him, and he was gradually promoted to Taizhong doctor.
One time when he went to the court, someone slandered him and said: "Zhi is very beautiful, but there is no way to deal with the fact that he likes to have an affair with his sister-in-law!"
After Zhi Buyi heard about it, he said, "I don't have an elder brother."
After all, he made no other excuses.
During the Seven Kingdoms Rebellion between Wu and Chu, Zhi Busuo led troops to attack the rebels with an official position of two thousand stones.
In the first year of Emperor Jing's reign, he was appointed as the imperial censor.
Emperor Jing commended the meritorious personnel who put down the rebellion of Wu and Chu, and made Zhi Busuo the Marquis of Sai.
During the Jianyuan period of Emperor Wu, both he and Prime Minister Wei Wan were dismissed from their official posts due to negligence.
I have no doubts about studying Laozi’s teachings.
When he governed every place, he held official positions in the same way as his predecessors, lest people know his official deeds.
He doesn't like to build up his reputation and be called an elder.
After Zhi Buyi's death, his son Xiangru inherited the position of marquis.
When the grandson was looking forward to it, he lost his position as marquis because the aide's donation did not meet the requirements.
The doctor named Zhou Wen was named Ren, and his ancestors were originally from Rencheng.
Relying on his medical skills to visit the emperor.
When Emperor Jing became the crown prince, he appointed him as a minister. His accumulated merits gradually improved, and during the reign of Emperor Wen, he became a senior official in Taizhong.
As soon as Emperor Jing succeeded to the throne, he appointed Zhou Ren as doctor.
Zhou Ren was very reserved and did not reveal other people's words. He often wore shabby and patched clothes and underwear that could absorb urine, deliberately making his clothes unclean, so that the concubines would not come close to him, so he was favored by Emperor Jing.
When Emperor Jing entered the palace and played obscenely with his concubines, Zhou Ren was often by his side.
When Emperor Jing died, Zhou Ren was still serving as the doctor, but he never said anything.
Sometimes when the emperor asked about other people's situation, Zhou Ren always said: The emperor should examine him personally.
But he didn't say anything bad to others.
Therefore, Emperor Jing visited his home many times, and his family later moved to Yangling.
The emperor rewarded many things, but he often declined and did not dare to accept them.
He never accepted the gifts from the princes and officials.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he considered him a minister of the late emperor and respected him.
Zhou Ren was dismissed from his post due to illness and the court allowed him to enjoy a salary of two thousand dan per year to return to his hometown for retirement. His descendants all became high officials.
Uncle Zhang, the imperial censor, was named Ou, and he was the concubine of Zhang Shuo, the Marquis of Anqiu.
During the reign of Emperor Wen, he served the prince by studying Legalist theory.
summary: Zhou Wen, a doctor, served Emperor Jing with reserve, wearing shabby clothes to avoid concubines. He never revealed others’ words and declined gifts. He retired with a salary under Emperor Wu. The historian concludes that Wan Shijun, Wei Wan, and Zhang Ou exemplified Confucian ideals of cautious speech and action, while Zhi Buyi and Zhou Wen, though flawed, were still honest gentlemen.

translation:
Although Zhang Ou studied Legalism, he was very loyal.
During the reign of Emperor Jing, he was very respected and was often ranked among the nine ministers.
In the fourth year of Yuanshuo, Emperor Wu, Han Anguo was dismissed, and the emperor appointed Zhang Ou as the imperial censor.
Since Zhang Ou became an official, he has never said anything about punishing people. He has been an official with honesty and loyalty.
His subordinates all thought that he was a loyal person and did not dare to deceive him too much.
The emperor handed over the cases to be tried to him, and if they could be returned for retrial, he would return them; if they could not be returned for retrial, he had no choice but to look at the sealed documents with tears in his eyes.
This is how he loves and cares for others.
Later, he became old and seriously ill and asked to be removed from his official position.
The emperor also issued an edict, granted his request, and allowed him to return to his hometown for retirement according to the doctor's salary. He lives in Yangling.
His descendants have all become high officials.
Tai Shigong said: Confucius once said: A gentleman should be slow in speech but quick in action. This sentence refers to Lord Wan Shi, Marquis Jianling and Uncle Zhang!
Therefore, they are not hurried but can make things successful, and their measures are not harsh but can make society stable.
Saihou Zhibu was too cunning and deceitful, but Zhou Wen failed to be humble and flattering. Gentlemen ridiculed them because they were close to flattery.
But they can also be regarded as gentlemen with honest behavior.
summary: Zhang Ou, imperial censor, studied Legalism but was loyal and merciful, often weeping over cases he could not retry. He retired due to illness.

translation:
King Wuzhu of Minyue was the same as King Yao of Yuedonghai. Their ancestors were all descendants of King Goujian of Yue, and their surname was Zou.
After the Qin Dynasty annexed the world, they all had their royal titles abolished and became rulers, and their place was set up as Minzhong County.
When the princes rebelled against the Qin Dynasty, Wu Zhuheyao led the Yue people to join Wu Rui, the magistrate of Poyang County, who was known as Pojun, and followed the princes to destroy the Qin Dynasty.
At that time, Xiang Ji had the power to command the princes and did not make Wu Zhu and Yao kings. Therefore, they did not join the King of Chu.
The King of Han attacked Xiang Ji, but Wu Zhu and Yao led the Yue people to assist the King of Han.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Wu Zhu was re-established as the King of Minyue. He was proclaimed king in the original place of Minyue and established his capital in Dongye.
In the third year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, he listed the contributions of the Yue people during the reign of Emperor Gao. The court believed that Lord Yao of Fujian had the most credit and his people were willing to join him, so Yao was appointed King of Donghai and established his capital in Dongou. The world called him King of Dongou.
Several generations later, in the third year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, King Wu Liu Bi rebelled and wanted Minyue to follow him to rebel against the Han Dynasty. Minyue was unwilling to follow, so only Dongou followed King Wu to rebel.
When King Wu failed, Dong Ou accepted the heavy bribes from the Han Dynasty and killed King Wu Liu Bi in Dantu. Therefore, he was not killed and returned to his own country.
Ziju, the son of King Wu Liu Bi, fled to Minyue. He resented Dongou for killing his father and often persuaded Minyue to attack Dongou.
In the third year of the founding of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Minyue sent troops to besiege Dongou.
Dongou ran out of food and was in great distress. He was about to surrender, so he sent someone to ask for help from the Emperor of Han.
The emperor asked Tian Fu about this, and Tian Fu replied: It is common for the Yue people to attack each other, and their attitudes are capricious. It is not worth bothering the Central Plains court to come to the rescue.
From the Qin Dynasty, they began to abandon them and did not treat them as subordinate countries.
So Zhuang Zhu, the Chinese doctor, questioned Tian Fu and said: "I am just worried that my strength is not enough to save them, and my kindness is shallow and cannot cover them. If you really have the ability to save them, why abandon them?"
Moreover, the Qin State even abandoned the entire Xianyang, so how could it just abandon the Yue State?
Nowadays, when small countries encounter difficulties and have no other choice, they come to the emperor for help. If the emperor does not come to rescue them, where will they go to complain and ask for help?
How can the emperor raise and protect the people of all nations?
The emperor said: The captain's opinion is not worthy of discussion.
I had just ascended the throne, and I didn't want to take out the tiger talisman to mobilize troops from the county to fight.
So he sent Zhuangzhu to Kuaiji with the talisman to mobilize troops for the expedition.
The prefect of Kuaiji wanted to resist the order and refused to send troops to Zhuang Zhu for the expedition. Zhuang Zhu killed an army commander and clearly stated the emperor's will, and then the prefect of Kuaiji sent troops from the sea to rescue Dong Ou.
Before the army reached Dongou, Minyue led his troops to evacuate.
Dong Ou requested that the entire country be moved to areas that the imperial court could directly manage, so he led all the people to move here and live in the Jianghuai area.
summary: The history of the Minyue and Dongou kingdoms, descendants of King Goujian of Yue, with the surname Zou. After the Qin Dynasty annexed their lands, they were demoted to rulers and their territory became Minzhong County. During the rebellion against Qin, Wu Zhu and Yao led the Yue people to join Wu Rui and helped destroy Qin, but Xiang Ji refused to make them kings, so they later supported the King of Han against Xiang Ji. In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Wu Zhu was reinstated as King of Minyue, with his capital at Dongye. In the third year of Emperor Hui's reign, Yao was made King of Donghai, known as King of Dongou, for his contributions. During Emperor Jing's reign, King Wu Liu Bi of Wu rebelled. Minyue refused to join, but Dongou followed. After Wu's defeat, Dongou killed him in Dantu under Han bribery and returned home. Liu Bi's son, Ziju, fled to Minyue and urged attacks on Dongou. In the third year of Emperor Wu's reign, Minyue besieged Dongou. Dongou sought Han aid; after debate, Zhuang Zhu was sent to mobilize troops from Kuaiji. Before the army arrived, Minyue withdrew. Dongou then relocated its people to the Jianghuai region.

translation:
In the sixth year of Jianyuan, Fujian and Vietnam attacked South Vietnam.
South Vietnam abided by the emperor's restrictions and did not dare to send troops to fight back without authorization, but reported the matter to the emperor.
The emperor sent Wang Hui, a great general, to lead his troops from Yuzhang, and Han Anguo, a great farmer, from Kuaiji. They both served as generals.
Before their army crossed the Yangshan Mountains, King Ying of Minyue sent troops to guard the dangerous place to fight against the Han army.
Ying's younger brother Yu Shan discussed with the Prime Minister of Dongyue and the clan members and said: Our king sent troops to attack South Vietnam without authorization without asking the emperor for instructions, so the emperor sent troops to attack.
Now that the Han Dynasty's army is numerous and powerful, if we can defeat them by luck now, the emperor will definitely send more troops in the future until our country is wiped out.
Now if we kill the king and apologize to the emperor, if the emperor accepts our request, the war will be stopped and our country will be preserved intact. If the Emperor does not accept our apology, we will fight hard; if we cannot win, we will flee to the sea. Everyone said: Good attention!
So he killed Ying with a spear and halberd, and sent an envoy with his head to Daxing Wang Hui.
Wang Hui said: Our army came here to kill the King of Dongyue. Now that the head of the King of Dongyue has been delivered, Dongyue has also apologized. The disaster has been eliminated without fighting. There is no greater benefit than this.
He stopped the military operation in a flexible and convenient way, informed Han Anguo of the situation, and sent an envoy to Chang'an with the head of the King of Dongyue to report to the emperor.
The emperor issued an edict to stop the military operations of Wang Hui and Han Anguo's troops, saying: Wang Ying and others of Dongyue were the first to commit evil, and only Wu Zhu's grandson Yao Junchou did not participate in this conspiracy.
The emperor then sent a lieutenant general to establish Chou as the king of Yue Yao to perform the sacrificial rituals to the king of Minyue.
After Yu Shan killed Ying, his prestige spread throughout the country, and most of the people in the country belonged to him, so he secretly proclaimed himself king.
King Yao could not correct the mistakes of his people and keep them on the right path.
After the emperor heard this, he thought it was not worth raising troops for Yu Shan's cause, saying: "Yu Shan conspired with Ying many times to cause trouble, and later killed Ying first, so that the Han army could avoid hardship."
So he appointed Yu Shan as the king of Dongyue and lived with King Yao at the same time.
In the fifth year of Yuanding, South Vietnam rebelled. King Yu Shan of East Vietnam wrote to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, requesting that he lead eight thousand soldiers to follow General Lou Chuan to attack Lu Jia and others.
When his army arrived in Jieyang, he used the storm at sea as an excuse to stop advancing and adopted a wait-and-see attitude. He secretly sent people to contact South Vietnam.
When the Han army captured Panyu, the East Vietnamese army did not come.
At this time, Yang Pu, the general of Louzhou, sent an envoy to write to the emperor, willing to lead troops to attack East Vietnam.
The emperor said that the soldiers were tired and tired, so he did not approve the request of General Lou Chuan. He stopped the military operation and ordered the officers to garrison at Meiling in Yuzhang to wait for orders.
In the autumn of the sixth year of Yuan Ding, Yu Shan heard that General Lou Chuan requested to attack him, and that the Han army had advanced to the border of East Vietnam and was about to attack, so he rebelled and sent troops to resist the Han army's only route.
summary: In the sixth year of Jianyuan, Minyue attacked South Vietnam. The Han emperor sent generals Wang Hui and Han Anguo to intervene. King Ying of Minyue resisted, but his brother Yu Shan killed him and surrendered, ending the conflict. Yu Shan later proclaimed himself king, and the emperor appointed him King of Dongyue alongside King Yao. In the fifth year of Yuanding, Yu Shan feigned support for a Han campaign against South Vietnam but secretly aided the enemy. After the Han victory, General Yang Pu sought to attack Dongyue, but the emperor initially declined. In the sixth year of Yuanding, Yu Shan rebelled, attacked Han forces, and proclaimed himself emperor. The Han sent multiple generals to suppress him. Yu Shan was killed by his own people, including King Yao Jugu, who surrendered. The Han emperor then relocated the Dongyue population to the Jianghuai region, leaving the area empty. Tai Shigong reflects on the Yue kingdom's longevity, attributing it to ancestral merits and the legacy of Dayu, despite Yu Shan's treachery leading to its downfall.

translation:
Le Yi, his ancestor was named Le Yang.
Leyang once served as the general of Wei Wenhou and once led troops to capture the Zhongshan Kingdom. Wei Wenhou gave Lingshou as a fief to Leyang.
After Le Yang died, he was buried in Lingshou, and his descendants settled there.
Later, Zhongshan was restored to the state, and it was destroyed by King Wuling of Zhao, and the descendants of the Le family gave birth to a famous man named Le Yi.
Le Yi was a virtuous man who loved military affairs. The people of Zhao once recommended him to serve as an official.
After King Wu Ling was besieged and starved to death in his palace in the sand dunes, he left Zhao and went to Wei.
Later, he heard that King Yan Zhao was defeated by Qi due to the chaos in Yan State due to his son's rule. Therefore, King Yan Zhao hated Qi State and never forgot to take revenge on Qi State.
The State of Yan was a weak country, located in a remote area, and its national power could not defeat the enemy, so King Zhao of Yan lowered his status and treated virtuous corporals. He first treated Guo Wei with thoughtful etiquette, so as to recruit more virtuous people.
At this time, Le Yi came to Yan State as an envoy for King Zhao of Wei, and King Yan received him with the courtesy of a guest.
Le Yi refused to give in, and finally presented a gift to King Yan Zhao to express his willingness to dedicate himself as a minister. King Yan Zhao appointed him as Yaqing, a position he held for a long time.
At that time, King Min of Qi was very powerful. In the south, he defeated Chu Prime Minister Tang Wei at Chongqiu, and in the west, he defeated Wei and Zhao at Guanjin. He then united with Han, Zhao and Wei to attack Qin. He also helped Zhao to destroy Zhongshan and defeated Song, which increased Qi's territory by more than a thousand miles.
He and King Zhao of Qin jointly fought for the title of emperor. Soon after, he canceled the title of Eastern Emperor on his own and still claimed the title of king.
All the vassal states planned to desert Qin and submit to Qi.
However, King Qi Min was very arrogant and arrogant, and the people could no longer tolerate it.
King Yan Zhao thought that the opportunity to attack Qi had come, so he asked Le Yi about attacking Qi.
Le Yi replied: Qi State was originally a hegemonic country and still retains its foundation. This country has a vast land and a large population. We cannot easily attack it alone.
If the king must attack it, it is better to unite Zhao, Chu and Wei to attack it.
So King Yan Zhao sent Le Yi to form an alliance and treaty with King Zhao Huiwen, and also sent envoys to unite Chu and Wei, and asked Zhao to persuade Qin with the benefit of attacking Qi.
Because the princes believed that King Qi Min was arrogant and tyrannical, which would eventually be harmful to them, they all rushed to join forces with Yan to attack Qi.
Le Yi came back to report on his mission. King Yan Zhao mobilized the country's troops and sent Le Yi as general. King Zhao Huiwen awarded Le Yi the seal of the Prime Minister.
Le Yi then unified the armies of Zhao, Chu, Han, Wei, and Yan to attack Qi, and defeated the Qi army west of Jishui.
At this time, the armies of various princes stopped attacking and retreated to their own countries. The Yan army, under the command of Le Yi, pursued the fleeing enemy alone until they reached Linzi, the capital of Qi.
After King Min of Qi was defeated west of Jishui, he fled to Juyi and held the city.
summary: Le Yi, a descendant of Le Yang who served Wei Wenhou and captured Zhongshan, was a virtuous man fond of military affairs. After King Wuling of Zhao died, Le Yi left Zhao for Wei. Hearing that King Yan Zhao sought revenge against Qi, Le Yi went to Yan as an envoy and became a minister. King Min of Qi grew arrogant and powerful, prompting King Yan Zhao to consult Le Yi about attacking Qi. Le Yi advised forming an alliance with Zhao, Chu, and Wei. King Yan Zhao sent Le Yi to forge alliances, and the allied forces defeated Qi at Jishui. The other states withdrew, but Le Yi’s Yan army pursued Qi to Linzi, capturing treasures and ritual objects. King Yan Zhao granted Le Yi the title of King of Chang Kingdom. Over five years, Le Yi captured over 70 Qi cities, leaving only Ju and Jimo unconquered.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/乐毅列传

translation:
Le Yi stayed alone and led troops to patrol the occupied areas. All the cities in Qi State held fast and refused to surrender.
Le Yi concentrated his forces to attack Linzi. After taking Linzi, he seized all the treasures and property of Qi and the ritual objects of the ancestral temple and transported them to Yan.
King Yan Zhao was overjoyed and rushed to the shore of Jishui to express his condolences to the army. He rewarded and rewarded the soldiers with wine and meat. He granted the Chang Kingdom to Leyi and named him the King of Chang Kingdom.
At that time, King Yan Zhao brought the spoils captured in Qi State back to Yan State, and asked Le Yi to continue to lead troops to attack the Qi State cities that had not yet been captured.
Le Yi stayed in the Qi State for five years and patrolled and fought. He captured more than 70 cities and towns in the Qi State. They were all classified as counties and belonged to the Yan State. Only Ju and Jimo were not conquered.
At this time, King Zhao of Yan died, and his son became King Hui of Yan.
King Hui had been dissatisfied with Le Yi since he was the crown prince. After he came to the throne, Tian Dan of Qi State learned that he had conflicts with Le Yi, so he implemented counterintuitive tactics against Yan State and spread rumors that there were only two cities in Qi State that were not captured.
The reason for the delay in conquering was said to be that Le Yi had a grudge against the new king of Yan State. Le Yi used troops intermittently to deliberately delay the time and stay in Qi State, preparing to proclaim himself king in Qi State.
What the people of Qi were most worried about was that King Yan would send a general to replace Le Yi.
At that time, King Yan Hui had already suspected Le Yi, and was provoked by Qi's counterintuitive plot, so he sent Qi Jie to replace Le Yi as general and recalled Le Yi.
Le Yi knew in his heart that King Yan Hui had bad intentions in sending someone to replace him. He was afraid that he would be killed when he returned home, so he went west and surrendered to Zhao.
The State of Zhao granted the place of Guanjin to Le Yi, with the title Wangzhujun.
The State of Zhao respected Le Yi very much and used it as a favor to shock and intimidate the States of Yan and Qi.
Tian Dan of the Qi State later fought against the Qi Jie, and he indeed set up a trap to confuse the Yan army. As a result, the Qi Jie army was defeated at the gate of Jimo City. He then chased the Yan army in many battles and chased north to the Yellow River. He recovered all the cities of the Qi State and welcomed King Xiang of Qi back to the capital Linzi from Juyi.
King Yan Hui regretted that he sent cavalry to replace Le Yi, which caused the Yan army to be defeated and lost the captured land of Qi. However, he also resented Le Yi for surrendering to Zhao and worried that Zhao would use Le Yi to take advantage of Yan's defeat and fatigue to attack Yan.
King Yan Hui sent someone to Zhao to blame Le Yi and apologize to him, saying: The late king entrusted the entire Yan State to the general. The general defeated Qi for the Yan State and avenged the late king. Everyone in the world was shocked. How can I dare to forget the general's achievements one day!
Just when the late king passed away, I came to the throne for the first time, but the people around me delayed me.
The reason why I sent the cavalry to replace the general is because the general has been away from home all year round and slept in the open air. Therefore, I recalled the general to rest for a while and discuss the government affairs together.
I didn't want the general to misunderstand the rumors and think that there was something incompatible with me, so he abandoned the state of Yan and joined the state of Zhao.
It's okay for the general to plan for himself, but how can he cope with the deep affection that the late king showed towards the general?
Le Yi wrote a reply to King Hui, saying:
I am incapable of obeying your orders and obeying the wishes of those around you. I am afraid that something unexpected will happen when I return home, which will damage the wisdom of the late king and your moral character. Therefore, I ran away from Qi and defected to Zhao.
summary: After King Yan Zhao died, King Yan Hui, who resented Le Yi, fell for Qi’s counterintelligence and replaced Le Yi with Qi Jie. Fearing execution, Le Yi surrendered to Zhao, which granted him Guanjin. Qi’s Tian Dan defeated Qi Jie, recovering all Qi cities. King Yan Hui regretted his actions and blamed Le Yi for defecting. Le Yi replied with a letter explaining his loyalty to the late king, his strategic advice, and his fear of unjust punishment. He compared himself to Wu Zixu, emphasizing the importance of preserving the late king’s achievements. King Yan Hui later appointed Le Yi’s son Le Jian as King of Chang State. Le Yi traveled between Zhao and Yan, dying in Zhao.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/乐毅列传

translation:
Lejian and Lecheng resented the King of Yan for not following their plan, so they finally stayed in Zhao.
Zhao Guo granted Lecheng the title of Lord Wuxiang.
The next year, Lecheng and Lian Po besieged the Yan State for the Zhao State. The Yan State asked Zhao for peace with generous gifts, and the Zhao army began to besiege the Yan State.
Five years later, King Zhao Xiaocheng died.
King Mouxiang sent Lecheng to replace Lian Po's official position.
Lian Po attacked Le Cheng, but Le Cheng fled, and Lian Po also fled to Wei.
Sixteen years later, Qin destroyed Zhao.
More than twenty years later, Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty passed by the original territory of Zhao and asked the people there: "Does Le Yi have any descendants?"
He replied: There is Uncle Le.
Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty gave him the title of Yueqing, and he was called Huachengjun.
Hua Chengjun is Le Yi's grandson.
The Le family also included Duke Le Xia and Duke Le Chen. They fled to Qi Gaomi when Zhao was about to be destroyed by Qin.
Duke Lechen was good at studying the theories of Huangdi and Laozi. He was very famous in Qi State, and people called him a wise teacher.
Tai Shigong said: When Kuai Tong and his father-in-law Yan read Le Yi's letter to King Yan, they couldn't help but shed tears when they put down the letter.
Lechengong studied the theories of Huangdi and Laozi. His master was called Heshang Zhangren. It is still unclear where Heshang Zhangren was from.
Heshang's father-in-law taught An Qisheng, An Qisheng taught Duke Mao Xi, Duke Mao Xi taught Duke Lexia, and Duke Lexia taught Duke Lechen. Le Chen taught Gai Gong.
Gaigong taught in Gaomi and Jiaoxi areas of Qidi and was Cao Xiangguo's teacher.
summary: Le Jian advised against attacking Zhao but was ignored. Zhao’s Lianpo defeated Yan, capturing Lifu and Lecheng. Le Jian fled to Zhao. King Yan regretted his decision. Later, Lecheng and Lian Po besieged Yan, forcing Yan to sue for peace. After King Zhao Xiaocheng died, Lecheng replaced Lian Po, but both fled. Qin eventually destroyed Zhao. Han Gaozu later granted Le Yi’s grandson, Uncle Le, the title of Huachengjun. The Le family also included Duke Le Xia and Duke Le Chen, who fled to Qi Gaomi. Duke Le Chen studied Huangdi and Laozi, becoming a renowned teacher. Sima Qian noted that reading Le Yi’s letter moved him to tears.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/乐毅列传

translation:
Confucius said: There are seventy-seven disciples who have studied with me and become proficient in the six arts. They are all people with extraordinary talents.
Outstanding in virtue: Yan Yuan, Min Ziqian, Ran Boniu, Zhong Gong.
Those who are good at handling political affairs: Ran You, Ji Lu.
In terms of language: Zaiwo, Zigong.
Articles on erudition: Ziyou, Zixia.
Master Zhuan Sun was extreme, Zeng Shen was slow, Gao Chai was stupid, Zhong You was rude, and Yan Hui was often poor and had nothing.
Duanmuci did not accept the mercy of fate and went into business, but his predictions on the market were often accurate.
The people whom Confucius respected: in the Zhou Dynasty, it was Laozi; in the Wei Kingdom, it was Zang Boyu; in the Qi Kingdom, it was Yan Zhongping; in the Chu Kingdom, it was Laolaizi; in the Zheng Kingdom, it was Zichan; in the Lu Kingdom, it was Meng Gongchuo.
He also often praised Zang Wenzhong, Liu Xiahui, Tongtan Bohua, and Jieshan Ziran. Confucius was born later than them and was not of the same era.
Yan Hui was from the state of Lu, his courtesy name was Ziyuan.
Thirty years younger than Confucius.
Yan Yuan asked what benevolence was, and Confucius said: Restrain yourself and make your words and deeds conform to etiquette, and people in the world will praise you as a virtuous person.
Confucius said: Yan Hui! What a virtuous person!
He ate a small bamboo basket of rice, drank a ladle of water, and lived in a simple alley. Most people couldn't bear this kind of hardship, but Yan Hui didn't change his joy.
When he was listening to my teachings, Yan Hui seemed like a stupid person. After class, I examined his private conversations and showed that he was able to express himself deliberately. Yan Hui was really not stupid.
When you are employed, you will save the world; when you are not employed, you will hide your secrets. Only you and I have such an attitude towards life!
Yan Hui was only twenty-nine years old, his hair turned completely white, and he died prematurely.
Confucius cried very sadly and said: Since I had Yan Hui, the students have become closer and closer to me.
Duke Ai of Lu asked: Who among the students is the best at learning?
Confucius replied: There is a man named Yan Hui who had better learn from others and never transfer his anger to others and never make the same mistake again.
Unfortunately, life was short, and after death, there are no such people anymore.
Min Sun, also known as Ziqian, was fifteen years younger than Confucius.
Confucius said: Min Ziqian is too filial!
He serves his parents and obeys his brothers. Others praise him without any criticism.
He does not want to be a retainer of a high official, and he does not want to receive a salary from an emperor. So he said: If someone calls me again, I will definitely flee to the north of Wenshui River.
Ran Geng, courtesy name Boniu.
Confucius thought he was virtuous.
Boniu was suffering from an incurable disease. Confucius went to greet him, shook his hand from the window, and said: This is life!
Such a good person got such a disease, what a fate! Ran Yong, courtesy name Zhong Gong.
Zhong Gong asked how to handle political affairs. Confucius said: When going out to do things, be as courteous and courteous as receiving distinguished guests, and use the people as piously and cautiously as hosting a grand ceremony.
In this way, no one will resent you if you serve in the feudal state of a prince, and no one will resent you if you serve in the home of a high official.
summary: Confucius identified seventy-seven disciples proficient in the six arts, categorizing them by virtue (Yan Yuan, Min Ziqian, Ran Boniu, Zhong Gong), political skill (Ran You, Ji Lu), eloquence (Zaiwo, Zigong), and erudition (Ziyou, Zixia). He noted individual traits: Zhuan Sun was extreme, Zeng Shen slow, Gao Chai stupid, Zhong You rude, and Yan Hui poor. Zigong, rejecting fate, became a successful merchant. Confucius respected figures like Laozi, Zang Boyu, Yan Zhongping, Laolaizi, Zichan, and Meng Gongchuo, and praised others from earlier eras. Yan Hui (Yan Yuan), thirty years younger than Confucius, was praised for virtue, living frugally without changing his joy. Confucius said he restrained himself to conform to etiquette, was not stupid, and shared a philosophy of serving when employed and hiding when not. Yan Hui died prematurely at twenty-nine, causing Confucius great grief. Duke Ai of Lu was told Yan Hui was the best learner, never transferring anger or repeating mistakes.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/仲尼弟子列传

translation:
Confucius thought that Zhong Gong had achieved great achievements in virtue and said: Ran Yong, you can make him a high official like a senior official.
Zhong Gong's father was a man of humble status.
Confucius used an analogy and said: A mottled cow gives birth to a red calf with round and straight horns. Even if you don't want to use it as a sacrifice, will the gods of the mountains and rivers abandon it?
Ran Qiu, also known as Zi You, was twenty-nine years younger than Confucius.
As the head of Li family's retainers.
Ji Kangzi asked Confucius: Is Ran Qiu virtuous?
Confucius replied: There is a city with a thousand households and a fief with a hundred chariots. Ran Qiu can manage the military and political affairs there well.
As for whether he is benevolent or not, I don't know.
Ji Kangzi asked again: Is Zilu virtuous?
Confucius replied: Just like Ran Qiu.
Ran Qiu asked Confucius: Do you act immediately when you hear what you should do?
Confucius replied: Act immediately.
Zilu asked Confucius: When you hear something you should do, should you act immediately?
Confucius replied: How can you act immediately when you hear something when your father and brothers are here?
Zihua felt that this was strange and said in confusion: "I boldly ask, why do you ask the same question but get different answers?"
Confucius replied: Ran Qiu was timid and worried, so I encouraged him.
Zhong Yu has the courage of two people to do things, so I have to restrain him.
Zhong Yuan, named Zi Lu, was from Bian.
Nine years younger than Confucius.
Zilu had a rough temperament, liked to show off his strength, had a strong ambition, and was straightforward. He wore a rooster-style hat and a sword decorated with boar skin. He once bullied Confucius.
Confucius slowly induced him with ritual music. Later, Zilu dressed in Confucian clothes and brought a gift for apprenticeship. Through the recommendation of Confucius's students, Zilu asked to be Confucius's student.
Zilu asked how to deal with political affairs. Confucius said: You must first set an example for the people, and then you can make the people work hard.
Zilu asked for further explanation.
Confucius said: Be persistent.
Zilu asked: Does a gentleman value bravery?
Confucius said: What a gentleman values ​​most is righteousness.
A gentleman who has no choice but to be brave but does not uphold righteousness will become rebellious and rebellious. A villain who has no choice but to be brave but not uphold righteousness will become a robber.
Zi Lu wanted to hear some truth, but he didn't act immediately, for fear of hearing another truth.
Confucius said: The only person who can decide a case by just listening to one side's words is Zhong You!
Zhong Yu advocates bravery more than I can use it, so it does not apply.
People with a temperament like Zhongyou's will not end well.
I'm afraid Zhong You is the only one who doesn't feel ashamed to stand next to people wearing fur coats while wearing a shabby robe made of tangled linen.
Zhong Yuan's knowledge seems to have reached the main hall, but he has not yet been able to enter the inner room.
Ji Kangzi asked: Is Zhong You virtuous?
Confucius replied: A country with a thousand chariots can let him manage military and political affairs. As for whether he has benevolence, I don't know.
Zilu liked to travel with Confucius and met hermits such as Changju, Jieyou, and an old man carrying farm tools.
Zilu became Ji's retainer. Ji Sun asked Confucius: Can Zilu be said to be a retainer?
Confucius replied: It can be said that he is a minister who is ready to fill his position.
Zilu was appointed as the official of Pucheng and bid farewell to Confucius.
Confucius said: There are many brave warriors in Pu Yi, and it is difficult to govern them.
However, I tell you: if you are respectful and humble, you can control brave people; if you are generous and honest, you can bring everyone close to you; if you are respectful and honest and the society is quiet, you can use it to serve your superiors.
At first, Duke Linggong of Wei had a favorite concubine named Nanzi.
summary: Min Ziqian, fifteen years younger, was deemed exceptionally filial, avoiding official service. Ran Boniu suffered an incurable disease; Confucius lamented his fate. Zhong Gong, asked about governance, was advised to be courteous and cautious; Confucius deemed him fit for high office despite his humble father. Ran Qiu, twenty-nine years younger, managed military affairs for the Ji family; Confucius encouraged his timidity. Zilu (Zhong You), nine years younger, was bold and straightforward, initially bullying Confucius but later becoming a disciple. Confucius taught him to prioritize righteousness over bravery, and he died in Wei during a rebellion, tying his hat before death.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/仲尼弟子列传

translation:
King Wu was very happy, so he sent Zigong to Yue.
The King of Yue cleared the road and went to the outskirts to greet Zigong. He personally drove his car to the residence where Zigong was staying and asked, "This is a remote and backward country. Why did the doctor humiliate his solemn status and come here?"
Zigong replied: Now I have persuaded King Wu to rescue Lu and attack Qi. He wanted to do this but was afraid of Yue and said, "Wait until I capture Yue."
Like this, it is inevitable to conquer the Yue Kingdom.
Besides, it would be too clumsy to make people suspicious of someone without the intention to retaliate; it would be unsafe to have people know about it if he has the intention to seek revenge; it would be too dangerous to let people know about it before the matter has started.
These three situations are the biggest disaster in getting things done.
After hearing this, Gou Jian kowtowed to the ground and bowed again and said: I once overestimated my capabilities and went to war with Wu. I was besieged in Kuaiji. I hated him so much that my lips were parched day and night. I only wanted to fight to the death with the King of Wu. This is my wish.
So he asked Zigong what to do.
Zigong said: The king of Wu was ferocious and cruel, and the ministers could not bear it; the country fought many wars, which made it exhausted and decayed, and the soldiers could not bear it; the people resented the king, and there were internal disturbances among the ministers; Wu Zixu was killed for his remonstrances, and the chief minister came to power, complied with the fault of the king, and used it to protect his own selfish interests. This is a political manifestation of harming the country.
Now if the king can really send troops to assist the king of Wu, appeal to his will, use heavy gold and treasures to win his favor, and honor him with humble words to show respect for him, he will definitely attack Qi.
If that war cannot be won, it will be your great blessing.
If he wins, he will definitely lead his troops to approach Jin. Please let me go north to meet the king of Jin and let him attack it together. This will definitely weaken the power of Wu.
When all their elite troops were consumed in the Qi State, the heavy troops were restrained by the Jin State, and the king took advantage of its exhaustion to attack it, which would surely destroy the Wu State.
The King of Yue was very happy and agreed to act according to the plan.
He gave Zigong a hundred yi of gold, a precious sword, and two good spears.
Zigong didn't accept it and left.
Zigong reported back to the King of Wu and said: I solemnly told the King of Yue what you said. The King of Yue was very frightened and said: I am very unlucky. I lost my father when I was young.
Five days later, Wen Zhong, a senior official from the State of Yue, kowtowed to the ground and said to the King of Wu: Gou Jian, the minister of the East China Sea Service, would like to send the envoy Wen Zhong to repair your subordinates and ask them to send greetings to the king.
Now I heard privately that the king is going to launch an army of justice to attack the violent, support the weak and tyrannical Qi State and appease the Zhou royal family. I request to send out the entire army of 3,000 people in Yue State. Gou Jian requested to personally wear armor and carry sharp weapons, and was willing to risk the danger of arrows and stones in front.
Therefore, Wen Zhong, a humble minister of the Yue Kingdom, was sent to present the treasures treasured by his ancestors, including twelve pieces of armor, axes, Qulu spears, and light swords, as gifts to the noble military officials.
The King of Wu was very happy after hearing this and told Zigong what Wen Zhong had said: The King of Yue wants to follow me personally to attack Qi. Is that okay?
Zigong replied: No.
It is unethical to make someone else's country empty, mobilize all his troops, and ask his king to follow him on an expedition.
You accept his gift and allow him to send his army without his king accompanying him.
The king of Wu agreed and thanked the king of Yue.
So King Wu mobilized the troops from nine counties to attack Qi.
Zigong therefore left the state of Wu and went to the state of Jin. He said to the king of Jin: I heard that if you don't plan a strategy in advance, you can't cope with sudden changes, and if you don't manage the army well in advance, you can't defeat the enemy.
Now the state of Qi and the state of Wu are about to go to war. If the state of Wu cannot win the war, the state of Yue will definitely take the opportunity to disrupt it; after winning the battle with the state of Qi, the king of Wu will definitely lead his army to approach the state of Jin. Jin was very panicked and said: What should we do?
Zigong said: Prepare your weapons, recuperate your soldiers, and wait for the arrival of the Wu army.
Jin Jun did as he said.
Zigong left Jin and went to Lu.
Sure enough, the King of Wu fought a battle with the Qi people in Ailing and defeated the Qi army. He captured seven generals' soldiers and refused to return home. Sure enough, he led his troops to approach the Jin state and met the Jin people in Huangchi.
Wu and Jin were competing for supremacy. The Jin people attacked Wu and defeated the Wu army.
When the King of Yue heard the news of the Wu army's disastrous defeat, he crossed the river to attack the state of Wu. He did not set up camp until he was seven miles away from the capital of the state of Wu.
When King Wu heard the news, he left Jin and returned to Wu, where he fought with the Yue army in the Five Lakes area.
Many battles failed, and even the city gate could not be defended. So the Vietnamese army surrounded the palace and killed King Wu Fucha and his minister.
Three years after the destruction of the Wu State, the Yue State dominated the east.
Therefore, Zigong's trip saved the state of Lu, disrupted the state of Qi, destroyed the state of Wu, made the state of Jin strong, and enabled the state of Yue to dominate.
Zigong's mission caused corresponding changes in the situation of various countries. Within ten years, the situations of Qi, Lu, Wu, Jin, and Yue each changed.
Zigong was good at hoarding rare things, buying at low prices and selling at high prices, and changing hands to make profits according to the supply and demand situation.
summary: Zaiwo, eloquent, questioned the three-year mourning period, suggesting one year sufficed; Confucius rebuked him for lacking benevolence. Zaiwo later died in a rebellion in Qi. Zigong, thirty-one years younger, was articulate and wealthy. Confucius compared him to a vessel and praised his humility. Zigong’s diplomatic mission saved Lu, disrupted Qi, destroyed Wu, strengthened Jin, and enabled Yue’s dominance, altering the balance of power among states.

translation:
He likes to promote the strengths of others and does not hide the faults of others.
He once served as the prime minister of Lu and Wei, and his family fortune accumulated thousands of gold. He eventually died in Qi.
Yan Yan was from the state of Wu and his courtesy name was Ziyou.
Forty-five years younger than Confucius.
After Ziyou received his profession, he served as the governor of Wucheng.
Confucius passed by Wucheng and heard the sound of playing the harp and singing.
Confucius smiled slightly and said: Why use a knife to kill a chicken?
Ziyou: Once upon a time, I heard my husband say: Talented people who learn rituals and music will cultivate their benevolence and love the people; ordinary people who learn rituals and music will abide by laws and regulations and be easy to control.
Confucius said to the accompanying students: Everyone, what Yan Yan said is correct.
What I just said was just a joke.
Confucius believed that Ziyou was familiar with articles and erudite.
Bu Shang, courtesy name Zixia.
Forty-four years younger than Confucius.
Zixia asked: "The beautiful smile is charming and moving, the bright eyes are flowing and shining, and the pure white hair of the Buddha is dyed with brilliant literary colors. What do these three sentences mean?"
Confucius replied: Painting must first have a pure white background, and then decorate the picture with color.
Zixia said: Did the emergence of ritual and music come after benevolence and righteousness?
Confucius said: Fortune teller, now I can discuss the Book of Songs with you.
Zigong asked: Which one is stronger, master Zhuan Sun or the diviner?
Confucius said: Master, it's a little too much, Shang, it's a little behind.
Zigong said: Is Master Zhuan Sun any better?
Confucius said: Excess and failure to catch up are equally imperfect.
Confucius said to Zixia: You must aspire to be a talented and virtuous scholar, not a shallow and dishonest scholar.
After the death of Confucius, Zixia settled in Hexi to teach students and became the teacher of Wei Wenhou.
Zixia's son died, and he cried his eyes out. Master Zhuan Sun was a native of Chen State, his courtesy name was Zizhang.
Forty-eight years younger than Confucius.
Zizhang learned from Confucius how to obtain official salary. Confucius said: Listen more to what others say, and do not make rash comments about unsolved problems. Others should be cautious when speaking out, so that you can make fewer mistakes; watch more people's actions, and don't act rashly about unsolved problems. Others should act cautiously, which can reduce regrets.
The fewer mistakes you make in your words and the fewer regrets in your actions, the official salary you seek will be contained in it.
One day Zizhang followed Confucius and was besieged between the states of Chen and Cai. Zizhang asked how to make everything work.
Confucius said: If you are honest and trustworthy in your words and sincere and respectful in your actions, it will work even in the southern barbarians and Beidi; if you are not loyal and trustworthy in your words and sincere and respectful in your actions, will it work even in your own hometown?
When standing, the words "loyalty, trust and reverence" appear before your eyes; when sitting in the car, the words "loyalty, trust and reverence" are hung on the crossbar in front of the car. Once you reach this point, it will work everywhere.
Zizhang wrote these words on the big belt around his waist.
Zizhang asked: What can a scholar do to be called enlightened?
Confucius said: What do you mean by mastery?
Zizhang replied: "You must have a good reputation among the princes' states, and you must also have a good reputation in the families of ministers and officials."
Confucius said: This is reputation, not understanding.
The so-called understanding should be upright and righteous, consider other people's words, observe other people's expressions, and always think about humility and concession. In this way, you will be able to gain access in the states of princes and the fiefdoms of ministers and officials.
summary: Ziyou, forty-five years younger, governed Wucheng with music and ritual; Confucius joked about using a “knife to kill a chicken” but later praised him. Zixia, forty-four years younger, discussed the Book of Songs with Confucius, who noted his slight deficiency. After Confucius’s death, Zixia taught in Hexi. Zizhang, forty-eight years younger, learned about gaining office through caution and about achieving success through loyalty and respect. Zeng Shen, forty-six years younger, understood filial piety and wrote the Book of Filial Piety.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/仲尼弟子列传

translation:
The reputation mentioned above seems to be pursuing benevolence, but in actual actions it violates benevolence. You have to deal with it calmly. There is no doubt that such a person will definitely gain fame in the states of princes and the fiefdoms of ministers and officials.
Zeng Shen was a native of Nanwucheng, named Liaoyu, and was forty-six years younger than Confucius.
Confucius thought that he could understand filial piety, so he taught him his studies.
He wrote a "Book of Filial Piety".
He died in the state of Lu.
Tantai Mieming was a native of Wucheng, named Ziyu.
Thirty-nine years younger than Confucius.
His body and appearance were ugly.
He wanted to serve Confucius, but Confucius thought that he had low qualifications.
After studying as a teacher, he devoted himself to self-cultivation practice when he returned home. He dealt with things openly and honestly, and did not take evil paths. It was not for official business and he never met with officials or officials.
He traveled south to the Yangtze River, and there were three hundred students who followed him. He was flawless in acquiring, giving, abandoning, and pursuing, and his reputation spread to the princes in all directions.
Confucius heard these things and said: If I judge people by words only, my judgment of Jaeyu is wrong; if I judge people by appearance alone, my judgment of Ziyu is wrong.
The words are not neat and the characters are cheap.
Thirty years younger than Confucius.
Confucius talked about Mi Zi Jian and said: Zi Jian is really a gentleman!
If there are no gentlemen in the state of Lu, where did this person learn such good character?
Zi Jian was appointed as Shanfu's local governor. He came back and reported to Confucius, saying: "There are five people in this place who are more talented than me. They taught me how to govern the people."
Confucius said: What a pity! The areas that are not managed uniformly are too small. If the areas that are managed are large, it will be almost the same.
Yuan Xian, courtesy name Zisi.
Zisi asked what shame was.
Confucius said: If the country's politics are clear, you can be an official and receive a salary, but you can't see trees.
The country's politics are dark, and it is a shame to be an official and receive a salary but not be able to stand alone.
Zisi said: If competitiveness, self-praising, resentment, and greed are not revealed, can it be regarded as benevolence?
Confucius said: It can be said to be commendable. Whether it can be regarded as benevolence, I don't know.
After Confucius passed away, Yuan Xian went to live in seclusion in a low-lying place with water and overgrown weeds.
Zigong became the Prime Minister of Wei State, and there was a continuous stream of carriages and horses when he went out, pushing through the thick weeds, and came to a remote, simple and dilapidated hut to visit Yuan Xian.
Yuan Xian tidied up his shabby clothes and met Zigong.
Seeing this, Zigong felt ashamed for him and said, "Are you embarrassed?"
Yuan Xian replied: I have heard that those who have no property are called poverty, and those who have learned principles but cannot implement them are called embarrassment.
Like me, poverty is not embarrassment.
Zigong felt very ashamed and left unhappy. He felt ashamed for his whole life that he had said the wrong thing this time. Gongye Chang was a native of Qi State, with the courtesy name Zichang.
Confucius said: If Gong Ye is the leader, you can marry your daughter to him. Even if he is in prison, it is not his fault.
summary: Other disciples included Tantai Mieming, initially judged poorly by appearance but later renowned; Mi Zijian, praised as a gentleman; Yuan Xian, who valued poverty over shame; Gongye Chang, married to Confucius’s daughter; Nangong Kuo, praised for morality; and Gao Chai, deemed stupid. Youruo, resembling Confucius, was briefly treated as a teacher but failed to answer questions. The text lists thirty-five disciples with recorded ages and deeds, and forty-two without, concluding that later accounts vary, with the author relying on The Analects for accuracy.

translation:
Wu Zixu, a native of Chu State, was a famous official.
Wu Yuan's father is Wu She, and Wu Yuan's brother is Wu Shang.
His ancestor was named Wu Ju, who gained prominence because he served King Zhuang of Chu with his upright and outspoken advice, so his descendants were very famous in Chu State.
King Chu Ping's crown prince was named Jian. King Chu Ping appointed Wu She as his Tai Fu and Fei Wuji as his Young Fu.
Fei Wuji was not loyal to Prince Jian.
King Ping sent Wuji to Qin to marry the prince. Because the Qin girl was beautiful, Wuji hurried back and reported to King Ping: "That woman is a peerless beauty. The king can marry her himself and give the prince another wife."
King Ping married the daughter of Qin himself, doted on her extremely, gave birth to a son named Zhen, and married Prince Jian.
After Fei Wuji used Qin's beauties to flatter King Ping of Chu, he took the opportunity to leave the prince and serve King Ping.
He was also worried that one day King Ping would die and Prince Jian would kill him if he succeeded to the throne, so he tried his best to slander Prince Jian.
Prince Jian's mother was from the state of Cai and was not favored by King Ping of Chu.
King Ping also became more and more alienated from Prince Jian, and sent Prince Jian to garrison the city father and defend the border.
Soon, Fei Wuji spoke ill of Prince Jian in front of King Ping day and night. He said: The prince will not be without resentment because of Qin Nu. I hope the king will be more defensive.
Since the prince has been stationed in the city, commanding the army and communicating with the princes, he is preparing to enter the capital to cause trouble.
King Ping of Chu summoned his tutor Wu She back for interrogation.
Wu She knew that Fei Wuji had said bad things about the prince in front of King Ping, so he said: How can the king alienate his close relatives just by bad words about a villain who is trying to stir up trouble?
Fei Wuji said: If the king doesn’t stop it now, their conspiracy will succeed and the king will be arrested!
So King Ping became angry and imprisoned Wu She. At the same time, he ordered Sima Fenyang, the father of the city, to kill Prince Jian.
Before they arrived, Fenyang sent someone to tell the prince in advance: The prince should leave quickly, otherwise he will be killed.
So Prince Jian fled to the Song Dynasty.
Fei Wuji said to King Ping: Wu She has two sons, both of whom are virtuous. If they are not killed, they will become a disaster to the Chu State.
You can use his father as a hostage to summon them, otherwise it will become a future trouble for the Chu State.
King Ping sent an envoy to Wu She and said: If you can call your two sons, they will live. If you don't call, you will be killed.
Wu She said: Wu Shang is a generous and kind man. If you call him, he will definitely come; Wu is a rebellious person who endures humiliation and heavy burdens and can achieve great things. He knows that if he comes and is captured, he will definitely not come.
King Ping refused to listen and sent for Wu She's two sons, saying: "Come, I will save your father's life; if you don't come, I will kill Wu She now."
Wu Shang planned to go, but the military officer said: The King of Chu summoned us brothers, but he did not intend to let our father live. He was worried that we would escape and cause trouble in the future, so he used our father as a hostage to deceive us.
As soon as we arrive, we will be executed together with our father.
What good can come from my father's death?
If we go, we will not be able to take revenge.
summary: Wu Zixu, a native of Chu, was a famous official whose father Wu She and brother Wu Shang were killed by King Ping of Chu due to the slander of Fei Wuji. Fei Wuji, originally the young tutor of Prince Jian, manipulated King Ping into marrying the prince's intended bride from Qin, then slandered Prince Jian, leading to his exile. Wu She was imprisoned, and his sons were summoned under threat of death. Wu Shang chose to go and die with his father, while Wu Zixu escaped, vowing revenge. He fled to Song, then Zheng, and eventually to Wu after Prince Jian was killed in Zheng. Wu Zixu arrived in Wu, where he befriended Prince Guang and recommended Zhuanzhu to assassinate King Liao, allowing Prince Guang to become King Helu of Wu.

translation:
Prince Guang said to the King of Wu: Wu Zixu's father and brother were killed by the Chu State, and I persuaded the king to attack the Chu State in order to avenge his personal revenge.
Attacking Chu may not necessarily defeat it.
Wu Zixu knew that Gongzi Guang had domestic ambitions and wanted to kill King Liao of Wu and establish himself as king. In this case, he could not persuade him with external military actions, so he recommended Zhuanzhu to Gongzi Guang, while he left the court and went to the countryside to farm with Prince Jian's son Sheng.
Five years later, King Ping of Chu died.
At the beginning, the beauty of Qin State that King Ping took from Prince Jian gave birth to a son named Zhen. When King Ping died, Zhen succeeded King Ping to the throne. This was King Zhao.
King Liao of Wu took advantage of Chu's funeral and sent Zhu Yong and Gai Yu to lead troops to attack Chu.
The Chu State sent troops to cut off the Wu army's retreat, preventing the Wu army from returning home.
The Kingdom of Wu was empty, so Prince Guang ordered Zhuan Zhu to assassinate King Liao of Wu and proclaimed himself king. This was the King's House of Wu.
After Helu became independent, and his wish came true, he recalled his military officers, worshiped him as a pedestrian, and discussed national affairs with him.
Chu State killed its ministers Pei Wan and Bozhou Li. Bo Zhouli's grandson Bo Pei fled to Wu State, and Wu State also appointed Bo Pei as a high official.
Previously, the two princes sent by King Liao of Wu to attack the Chu State were cut off and could not return home. Later, when they heard that Helu had killed King Liao of Wu and proclaimed himself king, he led his army and surrendered to the State of Chu. The State of Chu granted Shu land to them.
In the third year after Helu proclaimed himself king, he mobilized his army, Wu Zixu, and Bo Pei to attack Chu State, occupied Shudi, and captured the two generals who had betrayed Wu State.
So Helu wanted to take advantage of the victory and march into the capital of Ying. General Sun Wu said: "The people are very tired and cannot continue. Let's wait for the opportunity."
He withdrew his troops and returned home.
In the fourth year of Helu, the state of Wu attacked the state of Chu and captured the six lands and the land of Hao.
In the fifth year of Helu, the State of Wu attacked the State of Yue and defeated it.
In the sixth year of Helu, King Zhao of Chu sent his son Nang Wa to lead an army to attack Wu.
The state of Wu sent Wu Zixu to fight, defeated the army of the state of Chu in Yuzhang, and captured the Chu state's Juchao.
In the ninth year of Helu, King Helu of Wu said to Zixu and Sun Wu: At first you said that Ying was not to be invaded. What is the situation now?
Zixu and Sun Wu replied: General Nang Wa of Chu is greedy for money, and both Tang and Cai resent him.
If the king must attack Chu on a large scale, he must first get help from Tang and Cai.
Helu listened to their advice and dispatched all the troops to attack Chu together with Tang and Cai, and faced off with the Chu army on both sides of the Han River.
King Wu's younger brother Fu Gai led the army and asked to accompany him on the expedition. King Wu refused, so Fu Gai used five thousand of his men to attack Chu general Zichang. Zichang was defeated and fled, heading straight to Zheng.
So the Wu army took advantage of the victory and advanced, and after five battles, they reached the capital of Ying.
On Ji Mao day, King Zhao of Chu fled.
The next day, King Wu entered the capital of Ying.
After King Zhao of Chu fled, he came to Yunmeng. Here King Zhao was attacked by bandits and fled to Yundi.
Dou Huai, the younger brother of Duke Yun Douxin, said: "King Ping killed our father. Isn't it also okay for us to kill his son?"
Duke Yun was worried that his brother would kill King Zhao, so he fled to other places with King Zhao.
Wu soldiers surrounded everywhere and said to the people everywhere: The descendants of the Zhou Dynasty in the Han River Basin were all wiped out by the Chu State.
When the others wanted to kill King Zhao, Wang Ziqi hid him and pretended to be King Zhao to frustrate them.
The hexagrams showed that it would be unlucky to hand over King Zhao to the Wu army, so he declined the offer and did not hand over King Zhao.
At first, Wu Zixu and Shen Baoxu were close friends. When Wu Zixu escaped, he said to Baoxu: I must overthrow the state of Chu.
Bao Xu said: I must save Chu State.
When Wu soldiers invaded the capital of Ying, Wu Zixu searched for King Zhao but could not find him, so he dug up King Ping's grave, dragged out his body, and whipped him three hundred times before stopping.
Shen Baoxu fled to the mountains and sent people to say to Wu Zixu: "You are going too far to take revenge like this!"
summary: Under Helu, Wu Zixu became a key advisor, leading campaigns against Chu. In 506 BCE, Wu, with allies Tang and Cai, defeated Chu at the Battle of Boju, capturing the capital Ying. King Zhao of Chu fled. Wu Zixu, unable to find King Zhao, exhumed King Ping's corpse and whipped it 300 times in revenge. Shen Baoxu, a friend of Wu Zixu, sought aid from Qin, crying for seven days until Qin agreed to help. Qin forces defeated Wu, and internal strife forced Helu to return to Wu. Wu Zixu and Sun Wu's strategies made Wu dominant over Chu, Qi, Jin, and Yue.

translation:
He sent an envoy to give Wu Zixu the engraved sword and said: "You use this sword to commit suicide."
Wu Zixu looked up at the sky and sighed: Alas!
I slandered the villain Bo Pei and wanted to cause trouble, but the king came to kill me.
I made your father king.
Before you were confirmed as the heir to the throne, the princes were vying to be crown prince. I fought to the death in front of the late king and could hardly get the crown prince's position.
After you became the crown prince, you also promised to give me a portion of the Kingdom of Wu, but I have no hope that you will repay me. But now you actually listened to the bad words of a flattering villain and killed your elders.
So he told his close followers: You must plant a catalpa tree on my tomb so that it can grow up and make a coffin. Goug out my eyeballs and hang them on the east gate of Wu's capital to watch how the Yue invaders enter the capital and destroy Wu.
So he committed suicide and died. When the king of Wu heard this, he was furious, so he put Wu Zixu's body in a leather bag and floated it in the river.
The people of Wu State sympathized with him and built an ancestral hall for him by the river. Therefore, they named this place Xushan.
After King Wu killed Wu Zixu, he attacked Qi.
The Bao family of Qi killed their king, Duke Ai, and assisted Yang Sheng as king.
King Wu planned to attack the Bao family, but he withdrew his troops before winning.
Two years later, King Wu summoned the kings of Lu and Wei to meet at Lugao for an alliance.
The next year, he headed north and gathered the princes in Huangchi to give orders to the Emperor of Zhou.
At this time, King Gou Jian of Yue attacked the state of Wu, killed the prince of the state of Wu, and defeated the army of the state of Wu.
When King Wu heard the news, he returned to his country and sent envoys to negotiate peace with Yue with rich and valuable gifts.
Nine years later, King Gou Jian of Yue finally destroyed the state of Wu, killed King Wu Fu Chai, and killed Dazai Pei because he was disloyal to his king, accepted valuable bribes from foreign countries, and secretly became close to the state of Yue.
The son of Prince Jian of Chu, who had fled with Wu Zixu, lived in the state of Wu.
When King Wu Fu Chai was in power, King Hui of Chu wanted to summon Sheng back to Chu.
Ye Gongju advised: Sheng loves bravery and secretly seeks out warriors who dare to die. He may have selfish motives!
King Hui didn't listen to his advice, so he finally called Sheng back and let him live in Yan, the border town of Chu. Known as Bai Gong.
Three years after Duke Bai returned to Chu, King Wu killed Wu Zixu.
Not long after Duke Bai returned to Chu State, he resented Zheng Guo for killing his father, so he secretly recruited warriors who dared to die to avenge Zheng Guo.
After returning to Chu State for five years, he asked the King of Chu to attack Zheng State. Yin Zixi, the order of Chu State, agreed to his request.
However, Jin had already sent troops to attack Zheng before it sent troops. Zheng sent people to Chu to ask for rescue. King Chu sent Zixi to rescue Zheng and made an alliance with Zheng before returning.
Bai Gongsheng was angry and said: My enemy is not Zheng Guo, my enemy is Zixi!
Bai Gongsheng sharpened the sword himself. Someone asked him: What do you use it for?
Bai Gongsheng replied: "I want to use it to kill Zixi."
When Zixi heard about this, he smiled and said: "Bai Gongsheng is like a bird's egg, what can he do!"
Four years later, Bai Gongsheng and Shi Qi suddenly assassinated Ling Yin Zixi and Sima Ziqi in the court.
summary: After Helu's death, his son King Fucha of Wu succeeded. Wu Zixu warned against sparing King Goujian of Yue after a victory, but Fucha, influenced by the corrupt official Bo Pi, accepted Yue's surrender. Wu Zixu repeatedly advised against attacking Qi, urging the elimination of Yue first, but was ignored. Fucha sent Wu Zixu as an envoy to Qi, where he entrusted his son to the Bao family, foreseeing Wu's doom. Bo Pi slandered Wu Zixu, leading Fucha to order his suicide. Wu Zixu, before dying, asked for his eyes to be hung on the eastern gate to watch Yue's invasion. Fucha, enraged, had his body placed in a leather bag and thrown into the river. The people of Wu built a shrine for him. Years later, Yue destroyed Wu, fulfilling Wu Zixu's prophecy. Prince Jian's son, Bai Gong Sheng, returned to Chu but later rebelled, killing officials Zixi and Ziqi, and kidnapping King Hui. Ye Gong suppressed the rebellion, and Bai Gong Sheng committed suicide. Sima Qian commented on Wu Zixu's endurance and revenge, contrasting his fate with Bai Gong Sheng's failed rebellion.
