translation:
Yuan Gusheng retorted: No.
In the Xia Dynasty, Jie and Yin Zhou were violent and confused, and the hearts of the people in the world all surrendered to Shang Tang and Zhou Wu. Shang Tang and Zhou Wu agreed with the wishes of the people and killed Jie and Zhou. The people of Jie and Zhou refused to serve them and turned to Tang and Wu. Tang and Wu had no choice but to establish themselves as emperors. What else is this but upholding the destiny of heaven?
Huang Sheng said: Although the hat is old, it must be worn on the head; although the shoes are new, they must be worn on the feet.
Why? This is why there is a difference between up and down.
Although Jie and Zhou were immoral, they were in the upper position as monarchs; although Tang and Wu were sages, they were in the lower position as ministers.
When the monarch makes a mistake, the ministers cannot directly advise and correct it to maintain the dignity of the emperor. Instead, they use the fault to kill the monarch and replace him as the king in the south. What is this if not regicide and usurpation of the throne?
Yuan Gusheng replied: If we have to judge right and wrong according to your statement, then is it not right for Emperor Gao to replace Qin Dynasty as the emperor?
Then Emperor Jing said: If you eat meat but not horse liver, it is not not ignorant of the delicious taste of meat; if a scholar does not talk about whether Tang and Wu are destined to succeed to the throne, it is not considered stupid.
So the argument ceased.
Since then, no scholar has dared to argue whether Tang and Wu were established by destiny or whether they exiled Jie and Zhou to usurp the monarchy.
Empress Dowager Dou liked the book "Laozi" and summoned Yuan Gusheng to ask him about his experience in reading this book.
Yuan Gusheng said: These are just ordinary people's remarks.
Empress Dowager Dou said angrily: How can it compare with Confucian poetry and books that control prisoners!
So he asked Yuan Gu to enter the animal pen and kill the wild boar.
Emperor Jing knew that the Queen Mother was angry and Yuan Gu said she was not guilty, so he lent him sharp weapons. He went down to the animal pen to stab the wild boar, and hit it right in the heart. With one stab, the wild boar fell to the ground.
The Queen Mother remained silent. There was no reason to punish him anymore, so she had to give up.
Soon after, Emperor Jing believed that Yuan Gu was honest and upright, and worshiped him as the tutor of Liu Cheng, the king of Qinghe.
After a long time, he was discharged from office due to illness.
The current emperor has just ascended the throne and recruited Yuan Gu to join the court because of his virtuous character.
Many Confucian scholars who liked to flatter Yuan Gu were jealous and slandered Yuan Gu, saying that Yuan Gu was old, so he was dismissed from office and sent home.
Yuan Gu was already over ninety years old at this time.
When he was recruited, Gongsun Hong from Xue Yi was also recruited, but he did not dare to face Yuan Gu.
Yuan Gu said to him: Mr. Gongsun, you must discuss things with upright knowledge and don't use evil theories to cater to the world.
Since then, people in Qi have always discussed the Book of Songs based on Yuan Gusheng's insights.
Some Qi people became famous because of their achievements in studying the Book of Songs. They were all disciples of Yuan Gu.
Han Sheng was from Yanjun.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, he was a doctor, and during the reign of Emperor Jing, he was the tutor of Liu Shun, the king of Changshan.
summary: Yuan Gusheng of Qi debated Huang Sheng before Emperor Jing about whether Tang and Wu usurped the throne. Yuan argued they followed heaven's mandate, while Huang insisted on hierarchical propriety. Emperor Jing ended the debate. When Empress Dowager Dou questioned Yuan about "Laozi," he dismissed it as common talk, angering her. She ordered him to kill a wild boar, which he did with the emperor's help. Later, he became tutor to King Qinghe but retired due to illness. Recruited by the current emperor, he was slandered and sent home at over ninety, advising Gongsun Hong to uphold uprightness.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/儒林列传

translation:
Han Sheng deduced the purpose of "Shi" and wrote "Nei Zhuan" and "Wai Zhuan" with tens of thousands of words. The terms in the book are quite different from those in Qi and Lu, but the purpose is the same.
Huainan Bensheng received his inheritance from him.
From then on, people who talked about "Poetry" in Yanzhao area all followed Han Sheng's views.
Han Sheng's grandson Han Shang is a doctor appointed by the current emperor.
Fusheng was from Jinan County.
I had previously been a doctor of Qin Dynasty.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, he wanted to find someone who could study "Shang Shu", but he searched all over the world and found no one. Later, he heard that Fu Shenghui taught it, so he planned to recruit him.
Fu Sheng was already over ninety years old at that time. He was very old and could not walk, so Emperor Wen ordered Taichang to send his master Chao Cuo to Fu Sheng to learn from him.
When the Qin Dynasty burned Confucian books, Fu Sheng hid "Shang Shu" in the wall.
Later, when the war broke out, Fu Sheng went into exile. After the Han Dynasty pacified the world, he returned to look for the "Shang Shu" in his collection. He had lost dozens of articles and only got twenty-nine articles. So he taught the remaining "Shang Shu" in the Qilu area.
Since then, scholars have become very good at explaining "Shang Shu", and all famous scholars east of Miaoshan have dabbled in "Shang Shu" to teach students.
Fu Sheng taught Zhang Sheng and Ouyang Sheng from Jinan, and Ouyang Sheng taught Qiancheng Ren Kuan.
After Kuan became proficient in "Shangshu", he participated in the county election based on his achievements in Confucian classics, went to study under a doctorate official, and studied under Kong Anguo.
Erkuan's family was poor and had no resources, so he often worked as a kitchen worker for the students, and often went out to work secretly to earn money to provide for his own food and clothing needs.
He often read the scriptures when he went out, and read and reviewed them aloud when he was resting.
According to the ranking of the examination results, he filled the vacancy of Yan Weishi.
At that time, Zhang Tangzheng was fond of Confucianism, so he asked Erkuan to be his agent and responsible for reporting the case. Erkuan judged difficult and major cases based on classics and ancient methods, so Zhang Tang favored him.
Erkuan was gentle and kind-hearted, with integrity and intelligence. He was able to control his own words and deeds. He was also good at writing books and drafting memorials. He was agile in writing and thinking, but he was clumsy in speech and could not explain.
Zhang Tang thought that he was a loyal person and praised him many times.
When Zhang Tang became the imperial censor, he appointed Er Kuan as an official and recommended him to the emperor.
After the emperor summoned Erkuan to inquire about him, he liked him very much.
Six years after Zhang Tang's death, Erkuan became a royal official and died after nine years in office.
Erkuan was one of the three princes. He had a long career as an official because of his gentle and kind temperament, his ability to obey the emperor's will, and his ability to mediate disputes. However, he did not correct the emperor's mistakes. During his tenure as an official, his subordinate officials looked down upon him and did not do their best for him.
Zhang Sheng also became a doctoral officer.
Fu Sheng's grandson was also recruited for studying "Shang Shu", but he could not clarify the meaning of "Shang Shu".
summary: Han Sheng of Yan, a doctor under Emperor Xiaowen, wrote "Nei Zhuan" and "Wai Zhuan" on the "Shi," with terms differing from Qi and Lu but similar purposes. His grandson Han Shang became a doctor. Fusheng of Jinan, a former Qin doctor, hid "Shangshu" during the book burning. After the Han, he recovered twenty-nine chapters and taught them. His students included Zhang Sheng and Ouyang Sheng, who taught Erkuan. Erkuan, despite poverty, studied diligently, became an official, and served under Zhang Tang, rising to a high position but failing to correct the emperor's mistakes. Fusheng's grandson also studied "Shangshu" but couldn't clarify it. Kong Anguo re-copied ancient "Shangshu" in modern script, adding lost chapters.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/儒林列传

translation:
From then on, Zhou Ba and Kong Anguo from Lu and Jia Jia from Luoyang were all good at teaching the contents of Shangshu.
The Kong family had the Shangshu written in ancient pre-Qin script, and Kong Anguo re-copied and read them using the current official script font, thus giving rise to his own academic school.
Kong Anguo obtained more than a dozen lost chapters in "Shang Shu", and the number of "Shang Shu" probably increased gradually from this time on.
Many scholars have interpreted the "Book of Rites", but Gao Tangsheng's opinion from Lu County is the closest to the original meaning.
The Book of Rites was originally incomplete since the time of Confucius. After Qin Shihuang burned the book, more chapters of the book were lost. Today, only the Book of Rites survives, and Gao Tangsheng can explain it.
Xu Sheng of Lu State was good at practicing etiquette.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, Xu Sheng served as a ceremonial official.
He passed down etiquette to his sons and grandsons Xu Yan and Xu Xiang.
Xu Xiang was naturally good at practicing etiquette, but he was not proficient in the "Book of Rites"; Xu Yan was very familiar with the "Book of Rites", but was not good at practicing etiquette.
Xu Xiang became a ceremonial official in the Han Dynasty because of his good practice of etiquette and rituals, and he served as an official in Guangling Neishi.
Xu Yan and his disciples Gonghu Yiyi, Huansheng and Shanchang all served as ceremonial officials in the Han Dynasty.
Xiao Fen, a native of Xiaqiu, became the governor of Huaiyang because he was proficient in the Book of Rites.
From then on, those who were able to explain the Book of Rites and practice etiquette and rituals were all from the Xu family.
Ever since Shang Qu of Lu State studied the Book of Changes from Confucius, after Confucius died, Shang Qu taught the Book of Changes. After six generations, it was passed down to Tian He, a native of Qi County. Tian He was named Zizhuang, and then the Han Dynasty was established.
Tian He taught it to Wang, a native of Dongwu, whose given name was Zizhong, who taught it to Yang He, a native of Shichuan.
Because Yang He was proficient in the "Book of Changes", he was recruited by the imperial court in the first year of Yuanguang and became a senior official.
Jimo, a native of Qi, was proficient in the Book of Changes and became the prime minister of Chengyang.
Meng Dan, a native of Guangchuan, became the prince's official because he was proficient in the "Book of Changes".
Zhou Ba from Lu people. Heng Hu from Ju and Fu Yan from Linyi were all due to their proficiency in the Book of Changes.
But the most accurate teaching of the "Book of Changes" comes from the teachings of Yang He's family.
Dong Zhongshu is from Guangchuan County.
Because of his study of "Spring and Autumn", he became a doctor during the reign of Emperor Xiaojing.
He taught at home, and many people came to learn from him, so he could not teach them one by one in person. Instead, his disciples passed it on from generation to generation, and some of them had never even met him in person. Dong Zhongshu stayed at home and never visited the garden next to his house for three years. He was so dedicated to his studies.
His appearance and behavior when he came in and out were all in line with etiquette. The students followed his example and respected him.
After the current emperor ascended the throne, he served as the Prime Minister of Jiangdu.
He deduced the reasons for the alternating movement of yin and yang based on the changes in natural disasters and special phenomena recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Therefore, when praying for rain, he shut down all kinds of yang qi and released all kinds of yin qi, and when he stopped rain, he used the opposite method.
This approach was implemented in Jiangdu State and all achieved the expected results.
summary: Gaotangsheng of Lu best interpreted the "Book of Rites," which was incomplete after Qin's burning. Xu Sheng of Lu practiced rituals, passing them to his sons Xu Yan and Xu Xiang. Xu Xiang excelled in practice, while Xu Yan knew the text. Their disciples became ceremonial officials. Tian He of Qi taught the "Book of Changes," passed down from Confucius through six generations. His teachings influenced Yang He, who became a senior official.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/儒林列传

translation:
Later, he was demoted to a middle doctor and wrote "The Chronicle of Disasters" at home.
At this time, a fire broke out in the Gaodi Temple in Liaodong. The master's father Yan was jealous of him, so he stole his book and wrote it to the emperor.
The emperor summoned the Confucian scholars and showed them the book. The Confucian scholars believed that it contained accusations and ridicules of the government.
Dong Zhongshu's student Lu Bushu didn't know that this was his teacher's work and thought it was extremely stupid. So he handed Dong Zhongshu over to the judge and sentenced him to death. However, the emperor issued an edict and pardoned him.
Therefore, Dong Zhongshu never dared to talk about the theory of disasters.
Dong Zhongshu is honest and upright.
During this period, the imperial court was using troops to eliminate the intrusion of ethnic minorities inside and outside the four borders. Gongsun Hong's research on "Spring and Autumn" was not as successful as Dong Zhongshu's, but he was good at catering to the secular world, so he was able to occupy a high position and became a minister.
Dong Zhongshu thought that Gongsun Hong was a flatterer.
Gongsun Hong hated him and told the emperor: Only Dong Zhongshu can serve as the prime minister of King Jiaoxi.
The King of Jiaoxi was vicious and violent, but he had always heard that Dong Zhongshu was virtuous and treated him well.
Dong Zhongshu was afraid that he would get into trouble if he stayed in an official position for a long time, so he resigned and went home.
Until his death, he never managed private property, but devoted himself to researching knowledge and writing treatises.
Therefore, since the founding of the Han Dynasty, it has gone through five dynasties. During this period, only Dong Zhongshu was the most proficient in the Spring and Autumn Annals and had a high reputation. He taught Gongyang Studies in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Hu Wusheng was from Qijun.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, he became a doctor. Later, he returned to his hometown to teach "Spring and Autumn" due to his old age.
Many people who discussed "Spring and Autumn" in Qi were taught by Hu Wusheng, and Gongsun Hong also received his teachings.
Jiang Sheng, a native of Xiaqiu, studied Guliang studies in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Since Gongsun Hong was put in high office, he had collected and compared the scriptures and meanings of Guliang School and Gongyang School, and finally adopted Gongyang's theory taught by Dong Zhongshu.
The most successful disciples of Dong Zhongshu were: Chu Da from Lanling, Yin Zhong from Guangchuan, and Lu Bushu from Wen.
Chu Daguan became Prime Minister of Liang Kingdom.
Lu Bushu, who was a long-time official, went out as an envoy with a talisman in hand to decide the crime of rebellion by Liu An, the king of Huainan. He dared to judge the princes and kings on his own without asking for instructions. He judged the case fairly according to the "Spring and Autumn" classics, and the emperor thought it was right.
Among the disciples, those who have good official career have achieved the position of great officials; there are more than a hundred people who pay homage to him and have anecdotes.
Dong Zhongshu's sons and grandsons also became high-ranking officials because of their proficiency in Confucianism.
summary: Dong Zhongshu of Guangchuan, a doctor under Emperor Xiaojing, taught "Spring and Autumn" with such dedication that he didn't visit his garden for three years. He served as Prime Minister of Jiangdu, using yin-yang theory for rain prayers. After a fire at Gaodi Temple, his book on disasters was seen as accusatory, and he was nearly executed but pardoned. He resigned as Prime Minister of Jiaoxi due to fear of trouble, dying at home. He was the most proficient in "Spring and Autumn" during the Han, teaching Gongyang studies. His disciples included Chu Da, Yin Zhong, and Lu Bushu, who judged cases fairly.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/儒林列传

translation:
When fighting with others, you cannot completely win without grabbing him by the throat and hitting him on the back.
If your Majesty enters Hangu Pass and builds a capital, he will control the original areas of Qin. This is to grab the world by its throat and hit it on the back.
Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty sought the opinions of his ministers, who were all from the Shandong area. They argued one after another that the Zhou Dynasty established its capital in Luoyang and ruled the world for hundreds of years, while the Qin Dynasty established its capital in Guan Nei and perished after only two generations. It was better to establish its capital in the capital of the Zhou Dynasty.
The emperor hesitated.
After Zhang Liang, the remaining marquis, clearly explained the favorable conditions for entering Guanzhong and establishing the capital, the emperor took a car westward to establish the capital in Guanzhong that day.
At that time, the emperor said: Originally it was Liu Jing who advocated establishing the capital in Qin, and Lou is Liu.
So he changed Liu Jing's surname to Liu, granted him the official position of doctor, and gave him the title Fengchun Jun.
In the seventh year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, King Xin of Han rebelled, and Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty personally went to defeat him.
When he arrived in Jinyang, he learned that Han Wangxin was colluding with the Xiongnu to attack the Han Dynasty. The emperor was furious and sent envoys to the Xiongnu.
The Xiongnu hid their strong and capable soldiers and their fat cattle and horses, leaving only old and weak soldiers and thin livestock exposed.
More than ten batches of envoys were sent back, and they all said that the Huns could attack.
The emperor sent Liu Jing to go on an envoy to the Xiongnu again. He came back and reported: The two countries are at war, and it is time to show off their strengths.
Now when I go there, I see only emaciated livestock and old and weak soldiers. This must be a deliberate attempt to show shortcomings and ambush surprise troops to win.
I think the Huns cannot attack.
By this time, the Han army had crossed Gouzhu Mountain, and an army of 200,000 soldiers had set out to fight.
The emperor was very angry after hearing Liu Jing's words and scolded Liu Jing: "Qi is a coward!"
I got the official position by relying on my words, but now I dare to stop me from sending troops by talking nonsense.
Liu Jing was imprisoned in shackles and imprisoned in Guangwu County.
Emperor Gao led his army to Pingcheng, and when they arrived at Pingcheng, the Huns unexpectedly sent out troops to siege Emperor Gao on Baishan Mountain. They were besieged for seven days before they were able to relieve the siege.
When Emperor Gao returned to Guangwu County, he pardoned Liu Jing and said to Liu Jing: I didn't listen to your opinion, so I was besieged in Pingcheng.
I have beheaded all the ten people who were approved by the Huns to attack.
So Liu Jing was rewarded with a settlement of 2,000 households, and was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei, also known as Marquis of Jianxin.
Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty withdrew from Pingcheng and returned to the court, while King Xin of Han fled to Hu Di.
At this time, Maodun was the Xiongnu Chanyu. He had a powerful army with 300,000 warriors and repeatedly invaded the northern border.
The emperor was very worried about this situation and asked Liu Jing what to do.
Liu Jing said: The Han Dynasty had just settled down, and the soldiers were tired of fighting. They could not use force to subdue the Xiongnu.
summary: Liu Jing, a native of Qi, advised Emperor Gao of Han against establishing the capital in Luoyang, arguing that the Han Dynasty's rise differed from the Zhou Dynasty's gradual accumulation of virtue over generations. He noted that the Zhou built Luoyang as a central capital during their peak, but their decline showed that a weak situation, not just virtue, led to loss of control. In contrast, the Han emerged from warfare, with countless battles and suffering, making it unsuitable to emulate the Zhou. Liu Jing advocated for capitalizing in Guanzhong, protected by mountains and the Yellow River, with fertile land and a strategic position to "grab the world by its throat." Despite opposition from ministers favoring Luoyang, Zhang Liang's support led Emperor Gao to establish the capital in Guanzhong, rewarding Liu Jing with a surname change to Liu, the title of doctor, and the name Fengchun Jun. Later, in the seventh year of Emperor Gao, Liu Jing was sent to scout the Xiongnu before a campaign against the rebellious King Xin of Han. He warned that the Xiongnu's display of weak soldiers and livestock was a ruse to ambush the Han army, advising against attack. Emperor Gao ignored this, imprisoned Liu Jing, and marched to Pingcheng, where he was besieged for seven days. After escaping, he released Liu Jing, rewarded him with 2,000 households, and granted him the title of Marquis of Guannei. To address Xiongnu threats, Liu Jing proposed a peace marriage alliance, suggesting Emperor Gao marry his eldest princess to Maodun Chanyu to ensure future submission through kinship. Emperor Gao agreed but, due to Empress Lu's protests, sent a palace maid instead, with Liu Jing negotiating the treaty.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传

translation:
Maodun killed his father and proclaimed himself a Chanyu, and took many of his father's concubines as his wives. He relied on force to establish his power, but he could not be persuaded by benevolence, righteousness, and morality.
We can only make long-term plans to make his descendants surrender to the Han Dynasty, but I'm afraid your Majesty can't do it.
The emperor said: If it is really feasible, why can't it be done?
What to do?
Liu Jing replied: If your majesty can marry the eldest princess born to the empress to Moton as his wife, and give him rich gifts. He knows that it is the daughter of the empress of the Han Dynasty who has sent rich gifts. The rough foreigners will definitely envy the use of Han women as Yan family members, and the son they will give birth to will definitely be the prince and will succeed the throne in the future.
Why do this?
Because the Xiongnu coveted the Han Dynasty's generous wealth and gifts.
His Majesty repeatedly inquired about and presented gifts to the Han Dynasty that were superfluous throughout the year but rare to the Xiongnu. He also sent eloquent people to enlighten him with etiquette.
When Maodun reigns, of course he is the son-in-law of the Han Dynasty; after his death, his grandson of the Han Dynasty is the monarch.
Who has ever heard of a grandson who dared to stand up to his grandfather?
The army could gradually make the Xiongnu surrender without going to war.
If His Majesty cannot send the eldest princess, but lets a royal woman or a concubine pretend to be a princess, he will know about it and will not respect her and get close to her. There will be no good in that.
After hearing this, Emperor Gao said: OK.
He wanted to send the eldest princess to the Huns.
When Empress Lu learned about it, she cried day and night and said to the emperor: I only have a prince and a daughter, how can I bear to abandon her to marry the Huns!
After all, the emperor could not send the eldest princess, so he found a palace maid to marry Lord Moton as his wife in the name of the eldest princess.
At the same time, Liu Jing was sent to conclude a peace and marriage alliance with the Xiongnu.
When Liu Jing came back from the Huns, he said that the two tribes of the Huns in Henan, Aiyang and Loufan, were only 700 miles away from Chang'an, and light cavalry could reach the Guanzhong area in one day and one night.
The Guanzhong area had just gone through the war and was still very depleted, with a sparse population, but the land was fertile and could be gradually enriched by immigrants.
When the princes from all over the country raised armies to attack, they would not have prospered if it had not been for the participation of the Tian clan of Qi State and the Zhao, Qu and Jing clans of Chu State.
Now, although His Majesty built the capital in Guanzhong, there is actually a lack of population.
The north is close to the Huns and the enemy, and the east is the old nobles of the six countries. The clan power is very strong. If anything happens, your majesty cannot rest easy.
I hope that your majesty will move the Tian clan of Qi State, the three major clans of Zhao, Qu and Jing of Chu State, the descendants of Yan, Zhao, Han, Wei and other countries, as well as the wealthy and famous people, to live in Guanzhong.
If there is peace in the country, you can guard against the Xiongnu; if there is trouble in the vassal states, you can also lead them eastward to attack.
This is a strategy to strengthen central power and weaken local power. The emperor said: Very good.
summary: Upon returning, Liu Jing warned that Xiongnu tribes near Chang'an posed a threat and recommended strengthening Guanzhong's population by moving powerful clans from Qi, Chu, and other states, as well as wealthy families, to bolster defenses against both the Xiongnu and potential rebellions. Emperor Gao approved, and Liu Jing relocated over 100,000 people.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传

translation:
So Liu Jing was sent to move more than 100,000 people to Guanzhong according to his own suggestions.
Shu Suntong was from Xuexian County.
During the Qin Dynasty, he was recruited into the palace for being good at articles and knowledgeable, waiting to be appointed as a doctor.
A few years later, Chen Sheng raised troops in Shandong, and envoys reported the situation to the court. Qin II summoned doctors and Confucian scholars and asked: The soldiers guarding the border in Chu captured Qi County and entered Chen County. What do you think of this matter?
More than thirty doctors and Confucian scholars came forward and said, "The ministers cannot gather in crowds. Gathering in crowds is rebellion. This is a capital crime that cannot be pardoned. I hope your Majesty will send troops to attack them as soon as possible."
Qin II became angry when he heard this, and his expression suddenly changed.
At this time Shusun Tong walked forward and said: What all the Confucian scholars said is wrong.
Now that the world has become one, we have destroyed counties, cities, and cities, and sold all kinds of weapons to make it clear to the world that they will no longer use them.
What's more, when a wise monarch reigns over the world and formulates complete laws and regulations for those below, so that everyone obeys the law and obeys their duties, and everyone from all directions submits to the court, how can anyone dare to rebel?
This is just a group of thieves stealing, nothing to worry about. The county officials are hunting them down and punishing them, which is not worth worrying about.
Qin Er said happily: "Okay."
I asked every Confucian scholar again. Some Confucian scholars said they were rebels, and some said they were thieves.
So Qin II ordered the censors to examine what every Confucian scholar said, and anyone who said they were rebels would be handed over to officials for punishment. Qin II believed that they should not say such things.
Those who were said to be thieves were removed from their posts.
But he gave Shusun Tong twenty pieces of silk, a set of clothes, and the title of doctorate.
Shusun Tong walked out of the palace and returned to his residence. Some Confucian scholars asked: What flattering words did the master say?
Shusun Tong said: You don’t know, I can hardly escape from the tiger’s mouth!
So he fled the capital and arrived at Xue County. At that time, Xue County had surrendered to the Chu army.
When Xiang Liang arrived in Xue County, Shusun Tong took refuge with him.
Later, Xiang Liang died in battle in Dingtao, and Shusun Tong followed Xiong Xin, King Huai of Chu.
King Huai was conferred the title of Righteous Emperor by Xiang Yu and moved to Changsha. Shusun Tong stayed behind to serve Xiang Yu.
In the second year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, Liu Bang, the king of Han, led five princes and kings to attack Pengcheng, and Shusun Tong surrendered to the king of Han.
The King of Han was defeated and went west, and Shusun Tong followed him and finally joined the King of Han.
Shusun Tong always wore the clothes of a Confucian scholar, which the King of Han disliked very much. So he changed his clothes and put on a short coat, which was made according to the custom of Chu. The King of Han was very happy to see him.
When Shusun Tong surrendered to the King of Han, he had more than a hundred Confucian disciples, but Shusun Tong never recommended them, but only praised and recommended those warriors who had gathered together to steal.
The Confucian disciples all secretly scolded him: "I served Mr. Feng for several years, and I was lucky enough to defect to the King of Han with him. Now I can't recommend us, but I praise a particularly cunning person. What's the point?"
When Shusun Tong heard the words scolding him, he said to the Confucian scholars: The king of Han is fighting for the world with sharp arrows and strong rocks. Can you Confucian scholars fight?
summary: Shusun Tong, a scholar from Xue County, served under Qin II, where he flattered the emperor by dismissing a rebellion as mere thievery, earning rewards but fleeing after Qin II punished those who spoke truthfully. He later served Xiang Liang, King Huai of Chu, and Xiang Yu before surrendering to Liu Bang, the King of Han. Disliking Confucian robes, Shusun Tong adopted Chu-style short coats, pleasing the king. He recommended warriors over his own disciples, explaining that the king needed fighters, not scholars, during wartime. After the Han unification, Emperor Gao abolished strict Qin rituals, leading to chaotic court behavior. Shusun Tong proposed creating a simplified court etiquette, blending ancient and Qin practices. He recruited 30 Confucian scholars, despite two refusing, and practiced for a month. In the seventh year, the Changle Palace ceremony impressed Emperor Gao, who remarked, "Only today do I know the dignity of being an emperor." Shusun Tong was made Taichang, rewarded with gold, and his disciples received official posts.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/刘敬叔孙通列传

translation:
Shusun Tong said: The prince is the foundation of the world. When the foundation is shaken, the world will shake. How can you use the foundation of the world as a joke?
Emperor Gao said: I listen to your opinion.
When the emperor set up a banquet to entertain the guests, he saw that the four senior scholars invited by Zhang Liang followed the prince into the palace to pay respects. The emperor had no idea of ​​replacing the prince anymore.
When Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty passed away and Emperor Xiaohui came to the throne, he said to Mr. Shusun: None of the officials are familiar with the etiquette of the late emperor's cemetery and ancestral temple.
So he was appointed as Taichang and formulated the ceremonial regulations of the ancestral temple.
After that, many ceremonial systems of the Han Dynasty were successively formulated, all of which were recorded and recorded by Shusun Tong when he was appointed Taichang.
Emperor Xiaohui of the Han Dynasty wanted to go to the Changle Palace in the east to pay homage to the Empress Dowager Lu, and he often had small visits. Every time he went out, he had to clear the way. It was very annoying to block the passage, so he built a pavilion road just south of the arsenal of Weiyang Palace.
Shusun Tong reported to Emperor Xiaohui about his work, and took the opportunity to ask for a confidential talk with the emperor: How could your Majesty build a flyover without authorization over the passage from Gaobin to Gaomiao every month?
Gaodi Temple is the ancestral temple of the founder of the Han Dynasty. How can future generations be allowed to walk above the passage of the ancestral temple?
Emperor Xiaohui was horrified when he heard this and said: Destroy it quickly.
Mr. Shusun said: A monarch must not make wrong moves.
Now that it has been built, the people are all aware of it. If you want to destroy this overpass again, it will show that you have made a mistake.
I hope that your majesty will build another original ancestral temple to the north of the Wei River, send Emperor Gao's clothes there when he travels every month, and further expand and increase the ancestral temple. This is a fundamental measure of great filial piety.
The emperor then issued an edict to the relevant officials to build another ancestral temple.
This separate ancestral temple was built because of the pavilion road.
Emperor Xiaohui once traveled to the palace in the spring. Mr. Shusun said: In ancient times, there was a spring ritual of presenting cherries to the ancestral temple. Now is the season when cherries are ripe, so you can donate them. I hope that your majesty will pick some cherries to present to the ancestral temple when you travel.
The emperor agreed to do this.
Later, the ritual of offering various fruits flourished from this.
Tai Shigong said: Youdao is a fur coat worth a thousand gold, not the armpit skin of a fox; the rafters of a pavilion are not the branches of a tree; the achievements of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties at that time are not the wisdom of a wise man.
Indeed!
Emperor Gaozu rose up from the humble common people, pacified the world, planned great plans, and fought with troops. It can be said that he did his best.
However, Liu Jing took off the crossbar of the cart and went to see the emperor for advice, which established a stable and great cause that will be passed down from generation to generation. How can talent and wisdom be exclusive to a few people?
Shusun Tong was good at watching the wind and steering the ship, weighing affairs, formulating etiquette and regulations, or adopting or discarding them. He was able to change with the times, and eventually became the master of Confucianism in the Han Dynasty. The most upright thing seems to be crooked, and the truth is always tortuous and forward. This is probably what we are talking about, right?
summary: As crown prince tutor in the ninth year, Shusun Tong opposed Emperor Gao's plan to replace Crown Prince Liu Ying with Zhao Wang Liu Ruyi, citing historical disasters from such actions. He emphasized the prince's virtue and Empress Lu's shared hardships, threatening death if the change proceeded. Emperor Gao relented, especially after seeing four scholars supporting the prince. Under Emperor Xiaohui, Shusun Tong served as Taichang, formulating ancestral temple rituals. He advised against a pavilion road built over the Gaodi Temple passage, suggesting a new temple instead, and introduced cherry offerings to the temple. Sima Qian concluded that Liu Jing's strategic advice and Shusun Tong's adaptable ritual-making were crucial to the Han's stability, highlighting their unique contributions.

translation:
Cao Mo was from the state of Lu, and served Duke Zhuang of Lu with bravery and strength.
Duke Zhuang loves brave people.
Cao Mo served as the general of Lu and fought with Qi, being defeated many times and fled.
Duke Zhuang of Lu was afraid, so he offered up Suiyi area to seek peace.
But Cao Mo was still appointed as general.
Duke Huan of Qi agreed to meet with Duke Zhuang of Lu in Ke Di and make an alliance.
After Duke Huan and Duke Zhuang made an alliance on the altar, Cao Mo threatened Duke Huan with a dagger. No one in Duke Huan's bodyguard dared to move rashly. Duke Huan asked, "What are you going to do?"
Cao Mo replied: Qi is strong and Lu is weak, so it would be too much to invade Lu with a big country.
Now if the capital of Lu falls, it will hit the border of Qi. You need to consider this issue.
So Duke Huan of Qi promised to return all the occupied land of Lu.
After he finished speaking, Cao Mo dropped his dagger, walked down from the altar, and returned to where the courtiers were sitting, facing north, his expression unchanged, and his conversation calm as usual.
Duke Huan was very angry and planned to break the covenant.
Guan Zhong said: No.
If you covet small profits for temporary pleasure, you will lose credibility in front of the princes and lose the support of the people in the world. It is better to return the land to Lu.
So, Duke Huan of Qi returned the occupied land of Lu as agreed, and all the land that Cao Mo had lost in many battles returned to Lu.
One hundred and sixty-seven years later, there were Zhuan Zhu's deeds in the state of Wu.
Zhuanzhu was from Wu Guotang. When Wu Zixu fled Chu and went to Wu, he knew that Zhuan Zhu had skills.
After Wu Zixu went to see King Liao of Wu, he persuaded him about the benefits of attacking Chu.
Wu Gongziguang said: That Wu Yuan's father and brother were all killed by the Chu State. Wu Yuan just wanted to attack the Chu State. He did it to avenge his own personal revenge and did not really think about the Wu State.
The king of Wu no longer discussed the attack on Chu.
Wu Zixu knew that Young Master Guang planned to kill King Liao of Wu, so he said: That Young Master Guang has an attempt to seize the throne at home, and we cannot persuade him to send troops abroad yet.
So he recommended Zhuanzhu to Gongzi Guang.
The father of Prince Guang was Zhufan, King of Wu.
Zhufan had three younger brothers: in order of brotherhood, the eldest brother was called Yuji, the second brother was called Yimei, and the youngest brother was called Ji Zha.
Zhufan knew that Ji Zha was a virtuous man, so he did not make his son the crown prince. Instead, he wanted to pass on the throne in the order of brothers, and finally pass the throne to Ji Zha.
After Zhufan died, the throne was passed to Yuji.
After Yuji's death, he passed it on to Yimei.
After Yimei's death, it should have been passed down to Jiziza, but Jiziza avoided and refused to be made king, so the people of Wu made Yimei's son Liao their king.
Prince Guang said: If the order of brothers is to be followed, the youngest son should be established; if it must be passed on to the son, then I am the real legitimate son, and I should be made the king.
Therefore, he often secretly supported some wise people in order to obtain the throne with their help.
After Prince Guang got Zhuanzhu, he treated him well like a guest.
In the ninth year of King Liao of Wu, King Ping of Chu died.
In the spring of this year, King Liao of Wu wanted to take advantage of the funeral of Chu State and sent his two younger brothers, Gongzi Gaiyu and Shuyong, to lead an army to surround the city of Ji of Chu State. He also sent the youngest son of Yanling to Jin State to observe the activities of various vassal states.
The Chu State sent out its troops and cut off Wu generals Gaiyu and Shuyong's retreat. The Wu army could not return.
At this time, Gongzi Guang said to Zhuan Zhu: This opportunity cannot be missed. If you don't fight for it, you will never get it!
Besides, I am the true heir and should be made king. Even if Ji Zi comes back, he will not depose me.
Zhuan Zhu said: Wang Liao can be killed. Mother and son were weak, so the two younger brothers led the army to attack the Chu State. The Chu State army cut off their retreat.
At present, the Wu army is besieged by the Chu State outside, but there are no loyal ministers who are upright and outspoken in the country. What else can King Liao do to us?
Gongzi Guang kowtowed his head and said: My Gongzi Guang's body is your body, and I will be responsible for everything after your death.
On Bingzi day in April of this year, Gongzi Guang ambushed the warriors in armor in the basement and prepared a banquet for King Wu. King Liao sent guards to line up from the palace to Gongzi Guang's home. On both sides of the door and steps were King Liao's cronies.
summary: The deeds of five assassins from ancient China, spanning over four centuries. Cao Mo of Lu, a general who, after military defeats against Qi, threatened Duke Huan of Qi with a dagger during a peace alliance. Cao Mo forced the duke to promise the return of all occupied Lu lands. Though the duke initially wanted to break the promise, his advisor Guan Zhong convinced him that keeping his word was crucial for maintaining credibility among the feudal lords, and the lands were returned. One hundred and sixty-seven years later, Zhuan Zhu of Wu was recommended to Prince Guang by Wu Zixu. Prince Guang believed he was the rightful heir to the Wu throne, which had passed through brothers instead of to him. He plotted to kill King Liao of Wu. During a banquet, Zhuan Zhu hid a dagger inside a grilled fish and assassinated the king. Prince Guang's warriors then killed the king's guards, and Prince Guang became King Helu of Wu, rewarding Zhuan Zhu's son.

translation:
They stood in the aisle, all holding spears.
When the wine was intoxicating, Prince Guang pretended to have a foot problem, went into the basement, and asked Zhuanzhu to put the dagger into the belly of the grilled fish, and then presented the fish to him.
When he came to King Liao, Zhuan Zhu broke open the fish and stabbed King Liao with his dagger. King Liao died at that time.
The guards also killed Zhuan Zhu, and King Liao's men were in chaos for a while.
Prince Guang sent out an ambush of warriors to attack King Liao's men, and wiped them all out. He then proclaimed himself king, and became King Helu of Wu.
Helu then granted Zhuanzhu's son the title of Shangqing.
Over the next seventy years, Yurang's deeds were recorded in the state of Jin.
Yu Rang was a native of Jin. He had served the Fan family and the Zhongxing family in the past, but he had no reputation. He left them to serve Zhibo, who respected and favored him very much.
When Zhibo attacked Zhao Xiangzi, Zhao Xiangzi, Han and Wei jointly planned to destroy Zhibo. After Zhibo was destroyed, the three families divided his territory.
Zhao Xiangzi hated Zhibo the most, so he painted his skull into a drinking vessel.
Yurang fled to the mountains and said, "Oh!
A man should die for someone who understands him, and a good woman should dress up for someone who loves her.
Now that Uncle Zhi is my confidant, I will definitely avenge him and sacrifice my life to repay Uncle Zhi. Then even if I die, my soul will have nothing to be ashamed of.
So he changed his name and surname, pretended to be a person who had been tortured, entered Zhao Xiang's womb to repair the toilet, and hid a dagger on his body, intending to use it to assassinate Zhao Xiangzi.
Zhao Xiangzi went to the toilet, his heart palpitated, and he questioned the prisoner who was repairing the toilet, and found out that it was Yu Rang, with a sharp knife hidden in his clothes. Yu Rang said: "I want to avenge Zhibo!"
The guards want to kill him.
Xiangzi said: He is a righteous man, I just need to avoid him cautiously.
Moreover, after Zhibo died without an heir, and his retainers wanted to avenge him, he was a wise man in the world.
Finally he left.
Not long after, Yurang smeared paint on his body again, making his skin swollen and rotten, as if he had leprosy. He swallowed charcoal and his voice became hoarse, making his body and appearance unrecognizable, and he begged for food on the street.
Even his wife doesn't recognize him anymore.
I met his friend on the road, recognized him, and said, "Aren't you Yu Rang?" Answered: It's me.
His friend shed tears for him and said: With your talents, you will devote yourself to serving Zhao Xiangzi. Xiangzi will definitely be close to you and love you.
Isn’t it easy to be close to you and do whatever you want?
Why bother to mutilate your body and disfigure your appearance? Isn't it more difficult to achieve the purpose of revenge against Zhao Xiangzi in this way?
Yurang said: "After entrusting yourself to serve someone, you then want to kill him. This is a monarch who serves him with a different intention."
I know that it is very difficult to choose this approach, but the reason why I chose this approach is to make future generations of ministers in the world feel ashamed who serve the king with different intentions!
After Yurang finished speaking, he left. Soon, Xiangzi was catching up to go out, and Yurang hid under the bridge that he must pass by.
When Xiangzi came to the bridge, the horse was frightened. Xiangzi said: "This must be Yurang."
summary: Seventy years later, Yu Rang of Jin sought to avenge his master Zhibo, who was killed by Zhao Xiangzi. Yu Rang first attempted assassination while disguised as a prisoner repairing a toilet, but was discovered and released. He then disfigured himself by painting his skin and swallowing charcoal to change his appearance. He hid under a bridge, but Zhao Xiangzi's horse was startled, revealing him. Zhao Xiangzi confronted him, and Yu Rang explained that Zhibo treated him as a national scholar, so he must repay him accordingly. He asked to stab Zhao Xiangzi's robe to fulfill his revenge, then committed suicide.

translation:
I sent someone to check, and it turned out to be Yu Rang. So Xiangzi listed his sins and accused him, saying: Didn't you once serve the Fan family and the Zhongxing family?
Zhibo wiped them all out, but instead of avenging them, you pretended to be Zhibo's retainer. Zhibo is dead, why are you so eager to avenge him?
Yu Rang said: I serve the Fan family and the Zhongxing family, and they treat me as an ordinary person, so I repay them like an ordinary person.
As for Zhibo, he treats me as a national scholar, so I repay him like a national scholar.
Xiangzi sighed and said with tears: Oh, Mr. Yurang!
You have become famous by avenging Uncle Zhi; and it is enough for me to forgive you.
You should make your own plan, I can't let you go anymore!
Order the soldiers to surround him.
Yu Rang said: I have heard that a wise monarch does not bury the reputation of others, and loyal ministers are willing to die for their reputation.
You forgave me before, and no one in the world did not praise your wisdom.
I should have suffered the death penalty for what happened today, but I hope I can get your clothes and prick it a few times. This will fulfill my desire for revenge. Then, even if I die, I will have no regrets.
I dare not expect you to agree to my request, but I still venture to speak my mind!
So Xiangzi admired his chivalry very much and sent someone to bring his clothes to Yurang.
Yu Rang pulled out his sword, jumped up and stabbed it many times, saying: "I can use it to repay Uncle Zhi for being under the Nine Springs!"
So he committed suicide with his sword.
On the day of his suicide, all the people with lofty ideals in Zhao State cried for him when they heard the news.
More than forty years have passed since then, and there are stories of Nie Zheng in Zhi.
Nie Zheng was a native of Shenjing, Zhiyi.
In order to avoid killing people, he fled to Qi State with his mother and sister, and slaughtered livestock as a profession.
After a long time, Yan Zhongzi of Puyang served Han Aihou and developed a grudge against Xia Lei, the Prime Minister of South Korea.
Yan Zhongzi was afraid of being killed and ran away. He traveled around, looking for someone who could avenge Xia Lei on his behalf.
When he arrived in Qi State, some people in Qi State said that Nie Zheng was a brave man because he avoided his enemies and hid among the butchers.
Yan Zhongzi visited Nie Zheng's house and made many trips. Then he prepared a banquet and personally held a cup to toast Nie Zheng's mother.
When he was very happy after drinking, Yan Zhongzi presented a hundred yi of gold to his mother Nie Zheng to celebrate her birthday.
Nie Zheng was surprised by the generous gift and refused Yan Zhongzi firmly. However, Yan Zhongzi insisted on giving it away. Nie Zheng declined and said: I am fortunate to have my mother alive. Although my family is poor, she lives here as a guest and kills pigs and dogs. I buy some sweet and crunchy things in the morning and evening to feed my mother. My mother's support is quite complete, but I dare not accept Zhongzi's reward.
Yan Zhongzi avoided others and took the opportunity to say to Nie Zheng: I have an enemy. I traveled to many vassal states and could not find anyone to avenge me. But when I came to Qi, I heard privately that you are very loyal, so I offered a hundred gold as the cost of some coarse grain for your mother. I can also make friends with you. How dare I ask for anything else!
Nie Zheng said: The reason why I have humbled my ambition and humiliated my status and become a butcher in this market is just to support my mother. While my mother is still alive, I dare not commit myself to others.
Yan Zhongzi insisted on giving it as a gift, but Nie Zheng still refused to accept it.
summary: More than forty years later, Nie Zheng of Zhi was sought out by Yan Zhongzi, who had a grudge against the Korean prime minister Xia Lei. Nie Zheng initially refused because his mother was alive, but after her death, he agreed. He went alone to the Korean court, killed Xia Lei, and then disfigured his own face before dying to protect his family. His sister Nie Rong identified his body, proclaiming his honor, and died of grief beside him.

translation:
Fan Yuqi exposed one shoulder, held the other wrist tightly with one hand, approached Jing Ke and said, "This is something I have been grinding my teeth on day and night, and I can only hear your advice today!"
Fan Yuqi committed suicide.
When the prince heard the news, he drove there and cried bitterly on General Fan's body. He was extremely sad.
There was no other way, so Fan Yuqi's head was put into a box and sealed.
At that time, the prince had already searched for the sharpest dagger in the world. He found the dagger of Mrs. Xu from Zhao State, spent a hundred gold on it, and asked the craftsmen to quench it with poisonous water. He tested it on people and found that as long as there was a trace of blood, everyone would die immediately.
So he prepared his luggage and sent Jing Ke off.
There was a warrior named Qin Wuyang in the Yan State. He killed people when he was thirteen years old. No one dared to look at him face to face.
So Qin Wuyang was sent as an assistant.
Jing Ke was waiting for a man and planned to set off together. The man lived far away and had not arrived yet, but Jing Ke had already prepared his luggage for him.
A few days later, Jing Ke had not yet set out. The prince thought that he was stalling for time and suspected that he was going back on his word, so he urged him again: "The days are running out, does Jing Qing have any plans to leave?"
Please allow me to send Qin Wuyang first.
Jing Ke got angry and rebuked the prince: "What does the prince mean by sending him like this?"
If you just go and don't care about completing your mission and come back, you are a worthless boy!
What's more, he entered the unpredictable and violent Qin State with a dagger. The reason why I stayed temporarily was to wait for another friend to go with me.
Now that the prince thinks that I have delayed the time, let's say goodbye!
So we set off.
The prince and the guests who knew about this all dressed up in ordinary people's clothes and went to see Jing Ke off.
Arriving at the bank of Yishui, after bidding farewell, we set out on the road. Gao Jianli was building the building. Jing Ke sang in time with the beat, emitting a desolate and melancholy tone. Those who saw him off shed tears and sang as they walked forward: The wind is rustling, the Yishui is cold, and the strong men will never return once they are gone!
He made an impassioned tone again, and the people seeing him off had their eyes widened with anger, their hair stood on end, and their hats were raised.
So Jing Ke got in the car and drove away without even looking back.
As soon as he arrived in Qin, Jing Ke brought a gift worth thousands of gold and gave it generously to Meng Jia, the concubine among the favored ministers of the King of Qin.
Meng Jia first spoke to the King of Qin on behalf of Jing Ke: The King of Yan was really frightened by the majesty of the King and did not dare to send out troops to resist the King's soldiers. He preferred that all the people in the country be the ministers of the Qin State, ranked among the other vassal states, and pay taxes as if they were directly under the jurisdiction of counties and counties, so that they could guard the ancestral temple of the late king.
I was too scared to come forward and make a statement in person. I hereby cut off Fan Yuqi's head and present a map of the Dukang area of ​​the Yan Kingdom, and seal it in a box. King Yan also held a farewell ceremony at the court and sent envoys to report the situation to the king and ask for his instructions.
summary: Two hundred and twenty years later, Jing Ke of Wei was recruited by Prince Dan of Yan to assassinate the King of Qin. Jing Ke gained the king's trust by presenting the head of a fugitive general and a map of Yan territory. During the audience, he attempted to stab the king but failed, being wounded and killed. The king then attacked Yan, eventually destroying it. Jing Ke's friend Gao Jianli later attempted to assassinate the First Emperor with a weighted lute but also failed and was executed. The text concludes with the historian's commentary, affirming that despite varying outcomes, these assassins' intentions were clear and their reputations endure.

translation:
The ancestor of the Xiongnu was a descendant of the Xiahou family, named Chunwei.
Before Yao and Shun of the Tang Dynasty, there were Shanrong, yangxu and Xunzhu, who lived in the wild land in the north and moved with the livestock activities.
Most of their livestock are horses, cattle, and sheep, and their unique livestock are camels, donkeys, and mules? Fan Jun, Fan Dao.
They migrated in pursuit of water and grass. They did not have permanent urban settlements or agricultural production, but they also had their own share of pasture land.
There are no words or books, only words are used to restrain each other.
A child can ride a sheep, draw a bow and shoot birds and mice; an older child can shoot foxes and rabbits for food.
The men all had the strength to draw their bows, and they were all cavalry in armor.
Their custom is that they nomadically roam at will and take hunting animals as their occupation; when the situation is urgent, everyone will practice combat and carry out invasions and conquests. This is their nature.
Their long weapons were bows and arrows, and their short weapons were knives and small spears with iron handles.
Attack when the situation is favorable, retreat when the situation is unfavorable, and do not be ashamed of running away.
If you can get benefits, you don't know what etiquette is.
From the king down, everyone eats the meat of livestock, wears the leather of livestock, and wears fur coats.
Strong people eat rich food, and old people eat leftovers.
Respect the strong and look down upon the old and the infirm.
When the father dies, the son takes his stepmother as his wife; when the brother dies, the surviving brothers all take the wife of the deceased brother.
Their customs are famous but not taboo, and they have no surnames or given names.
When the Xia Dynasty was in political decline, Gong Liu lost his position as Ji official, implemented reforms in Xirong, built a city in Bindi and settled there.
More than 300 years later, the Rongdi tribe attacked Zhou Tai Wang Dan's father, and his father fled to the foot of Qishan. The people of Bindi followed his father to the foot of Qishan, built a city here, and established the Zhou Kingdom.
More than a hundred years later, Jichang, Bo of the Western Zhou Dynasty, attacked the Yi clan.
More than ten years later, King Wu of Zhou attacked King Zhou of Shang and built Luoyi. He returned to live in Fengjing and Haojing. He expelled the Rongyi to the north of Jingshui and Luoshui, and asked them to pay tribute to Zhou on time, which was called "Huangfu".
Over the next two hundred years, when the Zhou Dynasty was in political decline, King Mu of Zhou conquered the Dog Rong and returned after obtaining four white wolves and four white deer.
From then on, the Rong and Yi people in Huangfu no longer came to Haojing to pay tribute.
So the Zhou Dynasty formulated the regulations of "Fu Xing".
More than two hundred years after King Mu, King You of Zhou had a grudge against Marquis Shen because of his favor with Bao Si.
The Marquis of Shen was angry, so he and Quan Rong attacked and killed King Zhou You under Mount Li. The Quan Rong captured the Jiaohuo land of the Zhou Dynasty, and the monarch invaded the Central Plains area along the Jing River and the Wei River.
At this time, Qin Xianggong came to the rescue of the Zhou Dynasty, so King Zhou Ping left Fengjing and Haojing and moved eastward to Luoyi.
At this time, Qin Xianggong attacked the Rong people and came to Qishan, and began to be named a prince.
summary: The Xiongnu, whose ancestor was Chunwei, a descendant of the Xia dynasty, were a nomadic people living in the northern wilds. They moved with their livestock—horses, cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys—in search of water and pasture, without permanent cities or agriculture. They had no written language, relying on oral agreements. From childhood, they learned archery and riding, and all men were armored cavalry. Their customs prioritized warfare and plunder, favoring attack when advantageous and retreating without shame. They respected the strong and disdained the weak, practiced levirate marriage, and had no taboo against using personal names. Their leaders were called Chanyu, and they held seasonal gatherings for sacrifices and censuses. Laws were harsh, with punishments for murder and theft, and burial practices included human sacrifice for the Chanyu.

translation:
At this time, Donghu was strong and Yuezhi was prosperous.
The Xiongnu's Chanyu was called Touman. Touman could not defeat Qin, so he moved north.
More than ten years later, Meng Tian died, the princes betrayed Qin, the Central Plains was in chaos, and those who were exiled by Qin to guard the borders also left here. So the Xiongnu got a chance to relax, and gradually crossed the Yellow River, and connected with the old pass in the Central Plains to the south of the Yellow River.
The Chanyu had a prince named Maodun. Later, the Yu family whom the Chanyu loved gave birth to a young son.
The Chanyu wanted to depose Mao Dun and make his younger son the crown prince, so he sent Mao Dun to Yuezhi as a hostage. Mao Dun had already come to Yuezhi as a hostage, but Touman rushed to attack Yuezhi. Yuezhi wanted to kill Mao Dun, but Mo Dun stole Yuezhi's good horse and rode it back to the Huns.
Touman thought he was brave and ordered him to command ten thousand cavalry.
Mao Dun made a kind of sounding arrow, trained his men in horseback archery, and ordered: "Anyone who does not follow me and shoot at the target with my sounding arrow will be beheaded."
First, he shot at birds and beasts. If someone failed to hit the target with his arrow, Mao Dun killed him.
Soon, Mao Dun shot his own good horse with a resounding arrow. Those on his left and right did not dare to shoot, so Mao Dun immediately killed them.
After some time, Mao Dun shot his beloved wife with a loud arrow again. Some of the people around him were frightened and did not dare to shoot, so Mao Dun killed them again.
A few days later, Maodun went out hunting and shot Shanyu's good horse with a loud arrow, and everyone on the left and right followed suit.
So Modu knew that the people around him were all useful people.
He went hunting with Shan Yu Tou Man and shot Tou Man in the head with a ringing arrow. The people on his left and right also followed the sound arrows and shot Shan Yu Tou Man to death. Then he killed all his stepmother, younger brother and disobedient ministers.
Maodun established himself as a Chanyu.
After Mao Dun became a chanyu, Donghu was powerful and prosperous at that time. When he heard that Mao Dun had killed his father and established himself, he sent an envoy to Mao Dun to tell him that he wanted to get Tou Manshi's thousand-mile horse.
Mao Dun asked the officials, and they all said: "The Chollima is the Xiongnu's BMW, don't give it to me."
Mao Dun said: How can we be stingy of a horse even though we are neighboring countries?
So he gave the Chollima to Dong Hu.
After a while, Dong Hu thought that Mao Dun was afraid of him, so he sent an envoy to Mao Dun to tell him that he wanted one of Shan Yu's clans.
Mao Dun asked the ministers on the left and right again, and they all got angry and said: Donghu is unreasonable. He actually wants the Yan family. Please send troops to attack him.
Mao Dun said: How can you be the leader of a country with someone else but begrudge a woman?
So he gave his beloved Yan family to Donghu.
King Donghu became more and more proud and invaded and invaded westward.
There is an open space between the Donghu and the Xiongnu, which is more than a thousand miles away. No one lives in it. Both sides have built outposts on both sides of the open space.
Donghu sent an envoy to Modu and said: You Xiongnu cannot go to the open space outside the border post between the Xiongnu and us. We want to occupy it.
Mao Dun asked the officials for their opinions. Some of them said: This is an abandoned vacant land. You can give it to them or not.
So Modu was furious and said: Land is the foundation of the country, how can we give it to them!
Those who said they would give Donghu free space were killed.
Maodun mounted his horse and ordered anyone in the country who retreated to be beheaded, so he headed east to attack Donghu.
Donghu initially despised the Xiongnu and therefore did not take precautions.
When Mao Dun arrived with his troops, he defeated Donghu as soon as the war started, wiped out the king of Donghu, captured the people of Donghu and plundered their livestock and property.
After the Huns returned from Maodun, they defeated the Yuezhi in the west and annexed Loufan and the Aries Henan King in the south.
And completely recovered the land that Meng Tian of the Qin faction had taken from the Huns, and the original Henan fortress was the boundary with the Han Dynasty, as far as Chao and Fushi, and then invaded Yan and Dai.
At this time, the Han army was fighting against Xiang Yu's troops. The Central Plains area was exhausted by the war, so Maodun was able to become strong on his own, with an army of more than 300,000 people who could draw bows and shoot arrows.
It was more than a thousand years from Chunwei to Touman. The power of the Xiongnu grew and fell, and they often dispersed and differentiated. Because of the long time, their lineages cannot be arranged in sequence.
But when Maodun was the Chanyu, the Huns were the most powerful, making the northern barbarians completely submit to their rule and becoming an enemy of China in the south. After that, their lineage and national official titles could be recorded.
summary: Historically, the Xiongnu and their predecessors, such as the Shanrong and Xunzhu, interacted with Chinese dynasties. During the Zhou dynasty, King Mu of Zhou campaigned against the Dog Rong, and later, King You of Zhou was killed by the Quanrong, leading to the Zhou capital's eastward move. The Qin dynasty, under Qin Shihuang, sent Meng Tian to drive the Xiongnu from the Ordos region and built the Great Wall. After Qin's fall, the Xiongnu regained strength under Chanyu Touman, who was killed by his son Modun. Modun, after training his troops with a signaling arrow, usurped power and expanded Xiongnu territory, defeating the Donghu, Yuezhi, and other tribes, and amassing over 300,000 cavalry. He established a hierarchical structure with left and right kings, generals, and officials, and his rule marked the Xiongnu's peak, making them a major threat to the Han dynasty. The historian Sima Qian notes that the Xiongnu's nomadic lifestyle and martial culture made them formidable adversaries. He criticizes Han officials for short-sighted policies and emphasizes the importance of selecting capable generals, as even wise rulers like Yao needed talented ministers to achieve success. The Xiongnu's lineage, from Chunwei to Modun, spanned over a thousand years, with their power fluctuating until Modun unified them. Their social structure, with hereditary titles and a focus on warfare, allowed them to dominate the northern steppes and challenge Chinese authority for centuries.

translation:
Later, Maodun conquered the Hungeng, Qushe, Dingling, Gekun, and Xinli kingdoms in the north.
So the nobles and ministers of the Xiongnu were convinced of Mao Dun, thinking that Mao Dun was a virtuous man.
At this time, the Han Dynasty had just pacified China and sent Han Wangxin to Dai to establish the capital city of Mayi.
The Huns attacked Mayi on a large scale, and King Xin of Han surrendered to the Huns.
The Xiongnu got Han Xin, so they led their troops southward across Juzhu Mountain and attacked Taiyuan until they reached the city of Jinyang.
Emperor Gao personally led his troops to attack the Xiongnu. It was so cold and snowy in winter that two or three tenths of the soldiers lost their fingers due to the cold, so Mao Dun pretended to be defeated and escaped to lure the Han army.
The Han army pursued Mao Dun, but Mao Dun hid his elite troops, leaving only some old and weak soldiers. So the Han Dynasty dispatched its entire army, mostly infantry, totaling 320,000 people, to pursue the Xiongnu northward.
Gaodi arrived at Pingcheng first. Before all the infantry arrived, Mao Dun commanded his 400,000 elite cavalry to surround Gaodi on Baishan Mountain. Within seven days, the Han army and the outside world could not help each other with supplies.
The Huns' cavalry was all white horses in the west, green horses in the east, black horses in the north, and red horses in the south.
Emperor Gao sent envoys to secretly give many gifts to the Yan family. The Yan family said to Mao Dun: The kings of the two sides cannot besiege each other.
If he gets the land of the Han Dynasty, Chanyu will not be able to live there after all.
Moreover, the king of Han also had the help of gods and hoped that Shanyu would seriously consider this matter.
Mao Dun and Han Wangxin's generals Wang Huang and Zhao Li agreed on a date for the meeting, but Wang Huang and Zhao Li's troops did not arrive on time. Mao Dun suspected that they had premeditated plans with the Han army, so he adopted Yan's suggestion and lifted a corner of the encirclement.
So Emperor Gao ordered the soldiers to draw their bows fully, string their arrows, face outward, and rush out from the passage where Maodun was relieved, and finally met up with the Han army. Maodun then led his troops away, and Emperor Gao also returned with his troops and sent Liu Jing to the Xiongnu to conclude a peace treaty.
After that, Han Wangxin became the general of the Xiongnu. He, Zhao Li and Wang Huang repeatedly violated the covenant between Han and the Xiongnu and invaded and plundered Daijun and Yunzhongjun.
Not long after, Chen Xi, a general of the Han Dynasty, rebelled and conspired with Han Xin to attack Daidi.
The Han Dynasty sent Fan Kuai to stop them and re-captured Daijun, Yanmen and Yunzhong counties, but did not cross the border fortress.
At this time, because some generals of the Han Dynasty came to surrender to the Xiongnu, Maodun often traveled to Dai to carry out intrusion and robbery activities.
So the Han Dynasty was worried about this, and Emperor Gao sent Liu Jing to send the princess of the Han Dynasty royal family to the Chanyu family, and gave a certain amount of cotton wool, bamboo silk, wine, rice and food to the Xiongnu every year.
Later, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled and led thousands of his followers to surrender to the Huns. They traveled east of the Shanggu and caused suffering to the local people.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, during the period of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Dowager Lu, the Han Dynasty had just settled down, so the Xiongnu seemed proud.
Maodun wrote to the Empress Dowager Lu, talking nonsense.
Empress Dowager Lu wanted to attack him, but the generals said: With Emperor Gao's wisdom and martial arts, he was besieged in Pingcheng.
So Queen Mother Lu gave up her idea of ​​attacking and made peace with the Xiongnu.
When Emperor Xiaowen just succeeded to the throne, he promoted the marriage plan.
In May of the third year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, King Youxian of the Xiongnu entered Henan to live, harassed and plundered the barbarians in the small border towns, and massacred and plundered the people.
So Emperor Xiaowen ordered Prime Minister Guan Ying to dispatch 85,000 chariots and cavalry to Gaonu to attack King Youxian.
King Youxian fled outside the wall.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty came to Taiyuan in person. At this time, King Liu Xingju of Jibei rebelled. Emperor Wen returned to the capital and disbanded the army sent by the prime minister to fight the Huns.
The next year, the Chanyu of the Xiongnu sent a letter to the Han Dynasty, saying: The Great Chanyu of the Xiongnu, appointed by heaven, respectfully wishes the emperor peace. Some time ago, the emperor said about the marriage, which was consistent with the meaning of the letter, and both parties were happy.
The officials on the border of the Han Dynasty harassed and insulted King Youxian. King Youxian did not ask the Shanyu for instructions, but listened to the plot of Houyi Luhou Nan and others, resisted the Han Dynasty officials, severed the treaty between the Xiongnu and the Han emperor, and alienated the close brotherly relationship between the Han and the Xiongnu.
The emperor's letter reproaching the Xiongnu came for the second time. We sent an envoy to report the situation, but the envoy was detained by the Han Dynasty and did not return. The Han Dynasty's envoy did not come to the Huns. For this reason, the Han Dynasty did not reconcile with us, and our neighboring countries could not surrender.
Now because the petty officials broke the peace treaty, I punish King Youxian and send him to the west to find the Yuezhi and attack them.
Thanks to the blessing of God, the officials and soldiers were all excellent, and the horses were strong and powerful. Therefore, the Yuezhi were wiped out, all those who resisted and disobeyed were killed, and the common people were subjugated.
Loulan, Wusun, Hujie and the twenty-six countries beside them were pacified, and they all became subjects of the Xiongnu.
Those who were good at bending bows and shooting arrows merged into one family.
summary: The Han dynasty, after its founding, faced constant Xiongnu raids. Emperor Gaozu was besieged at Pingcheng by Modun but escaped through bribery and a peace treaty involving marriage and tribute. Subsequent rulers, including Empress Dowager Lu and Emperor Wen, maintained this policy despite Xiongnu provocations. The Xiongnu, under Chanyu Laoshang and later Junchen, continued to raid border regions, while Han envoys like Zhonghang Yue, who defected to the Xiongnu, advised them to resist Han cultural influence. The Han dynasty alternated between appeasement and military campaigns, with Emperor Wu launching large-scale offensives led by generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, who defeated the Xiongnu in the Ordos and Gobi, capturing key territories and forcing them northward.

translation:
The Han Dynasty general Wang Hui's army came out of Daijun to attack the Xiongnu's baggage. He heard that the Chanyu army had returned and there were many soldiers, so he did not dare to attack.
The Han Dynasty believed that Wang Hui was the one who planned the ambush but did not dare to attack, so he killed Wang Hui.
From then on, the Xiongnu broke off their fraternal relations, attacked the frontier fortresses leading to important roads, and often invaded the Han Dynasty's borders to plunder, too many times to count.
However, the Xiongnu were greedy and still liked to exchange customs and markets with the Han Dynasty. They liked the Han Dynasty's property very much. The Han Dynasty still maintained customs and market trade relations with the Xiongnu and catered to their wishes.
In the autumn of the fifth year after the Mayi military campaign, the Han Dynasty sent Wei Qing and other four generals with 10,000 cavalry each to attack the Xiongnu near Guan City.
General Wei Qing led his troops out of Shanggu County and arrived at Fucheng, where they killed and captured more than 700 Xiongnu people.
Gongsun He led his troops out of Yunzhong County, but gained nothing.
Gongsun Ao led his troops out of Daijun and was defeated by the Xiongnu, losing more than 7,000 people.
Li Guang led his troops out of Yanmen County and was defeated by the Huns. The Huns captured Li Guang alive. Later, Li Guang was able to escape and return to the Han Dynasty.
The Han Dynasty imprisoned Gongsun Ao and Li Guang. Gongsun Ao and Li Guang paid a ransom and became common people.
This winter, the Xiongnu repeatedly broke into the border and plundered, and Yuyang suffered particularly badly.
The Han Dynasty sent General Han Anguo to garrison Yuyang to defend against the Xiongnu.
In the autumn of the next year, 20,000 Xiongnu cavalry invaded the Han Dynasty, killed the prefect of Liaoxi and took away more than 2,000 people.
The Huns invaded Yuyang again, defeated more than a thousand troops of the Yuyang prefect, and besieged Han Anguo, the general of the Han Dynasty. At this time, Han Anguo's more than a thousand cavalry were about to be wiped out. King Yan's reinforcements happened to arrive, and the Huns left.
The Xiongnu invaded Yanmen County again, killing and taking away more than a thousand people.
So the Han Dynasty sent General Wei Qing to lead 30,000 cavalry out of Yanmen. Li Xi led his troops to force out of Dai County and attacked the Huns, killing and capturing thousands of them.
The next year, Wei Qing went out to the west of Yunzhong County and the Longxi area in the west, and attacked Loufan and Aries Wang under the Xiongnu on the south bank of the Yellow River Hetao. He killed and captured thousands of people and obtained more than one million cattle and sheep.
So the Han Dynasty captured the area on the south bank of the Yellow River Hetao, built Shuofang City, and repaired the pass built by Meng Tian of the Qin Dynasty in the past, relying on the Yellow River as a solid defense line.
The Han Dynasty also gave up the twists and turns of Shanggu County and remote counties such as Zaoyang to the Xiongnu.
This year is the second year of Yuanshuo, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
In the winter of the following year, the Xiongnu military official Chanyu died.
The younger brother of the military minister Chanyu, King Zuoguli Yizhixie, established himself as a Chanyu and defeated the military minister Shanyu's prince Yu Shan.
Yu Dan fled and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty named Yu Shan the Marquis of She'an. He died a few months later.
In the summer after Yi Zhixie Chanyu succeeded to the throne, tens of thousands of Xiongnu cavalry invaded Dai County, killed the prefect Gongyou and looted more than a thousand people.
In the autumn of that year, the Xiongnu invaded Yanmen again, killing and taking away more than a thousand people.
summary: Despite these victories, the Xiongnu remained resilient. After Huo Qubing's death, the Han halted major campaigns, and the Xiongnu, under Chanyu Uwei and his successors, continued to raid and negotiate. The Han attempted to sow discord among Xiongnu leaders and used diplomacy with western states like Wusun to isolate them. However, internal strife and harsh winters weakened the Xiongnu. Later Chanyu, such as Er Chanyu and Huyan, faced rebellions and military defeats, including the capture of Han general Li Ling and the defection of Li Guangli. The Han built fortifications and expanded into the Hexi Corridor, but the Xiongnu persisted in their raids, leading to a prolonged stalemate.
