translation:
The king of Nanyue, Wei Tuo, was from Zhending and his surname was Zhao.
The Qin State annexed the six countries, captured and pacified Yang Yue, established Guilin, Nanhai and Xiangjun, and resettled the people who had committed crimes and migrated to these places, and lived together with the Yue people for thirteen years.
Wei Tuo was appointed as the magistrate of Longchuan County in Nanhai County during the Qin Dynasty.
During the second year of Qin Dynasty, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai County, fell ill and was about to die. He summoned Zhao Tuo, the commander of Longchuan, and said to him: I heard that Chen Sheng and others had launched a rebellion, and that the Qin Dynasty was pursuing cruel and unjust policies, and the people of the world were resentful of this. Xiang Yu, Liu Bang, Chen Sheng, Wu Guang, etc. all gathered people in their respective states and counties at the same time, formed armies, and fought for the world like tigers. The Central Plains region was in turmoil, and it was unknown when peace would be restored. Heroes betrayed the Qin Dynasty and opposed each other.
Nanhai County is remote and remote, and I am afraid that the bandit army will invade the land. When I attack here, I want to mobilize the army to cut off the newly built road to the Central Plains. I have taken precautions in advance and wait for the changes in the princes. It happens that I am seriously ill.
Let’s talk about Panyu. There are dangerous mountains behind us to rely on, and there is the sea as a barrier to the south. It is thousands of miles away from east to west. We have some Central Plains people to assist us. We can also be the lord of a state and establish a country.
There is no one among the governors of Nanhai County who is worthy of me to study these things with him, so I have summoned you to tell you these things.
Ren Xiao immediately issued an appointment document to Zhao Tuo, asking him to act on behalf of Nanhai County.
After Ren Xiao died, Zhao Tuo sent a message to Hengpu, Yangshan, and Huangxiguan, saying: The bandit army is coming, so we must quickly cut off the road, gather the army, and defend ourselves.
Zhao Tuo took this opportunity to gradually use the law to kill the officials installed by the Qin Dynasty, and use his cronies as acting governors.
After the Qin Dynasty was destroyed, Zhao Tuo attacked and annexed Guilin and Xiangjun, and established himself as King Wu of South Vietnam.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had already pacified the world. Because the people in the Central Plains were tired and miserable, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty spared Zhao Tuo and did not kill him.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, he sent Lu Jia to South Vietnam and ordered Zhao Tuo to inherit his title of King of South Vietnam, make an agreement with him, exchange envoys, and let him coordinate Baiyue so that they can live in harmony and not become a scourge to the south of the Han Dynasty. South Vietnam borders Changsha to the north.
During the post-Gao period, officials from relevant departments requested that South Vietnam be prohibited from purchasing ironware in border markets.
Zhao Tuo said: Emperor Gao made me the king of South Vietnam, and the two sides exchanged envoys and supplies. Now Gao Hou listens to the opinions of the slanderers, treats the barbarians as aliens, and cuts off the source of the artifacts we need. This must be the idea of ​​King Changsha. He wants to follow the Han Dynasty in the Central Plains, eliminate South Vietnam, double as the king of South Vietnam, and establish his own merits.
So Zhao Tuo took advantage of the title and called himself Emperor Wu of Nanyue. He sent troops to attack the border cities of Changsha and defeated several counties before leaving.
summary: The king of Nanyue, Wei Tuo (Zhao Tuo), was from Zhending. During the Qin dynasty, after conquering the six states, the Qin annexed Yang Yue, establishing Guilin, Nanhai, and Xiangjun, and resettled criminals there to live with the Yue people for thirteen years. Zhao Tuo served as the magistrate of Longchuan County in Nanhai. In the second year of the Qin dynasty, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai, fell ill. He summoned Zhao Tuo and explained that with Chen Sheng’s rebellion and the Qin’s cruel policies, the Central Plains were in chaos. He noted that Nanhai was remote and could be defended by mountains and sea, and suggested Zhao Tuo could establish a state. Ren Xiao appointed Zhao Tuo as acting captain. After Ren Xiao’s death, Zhao Tuo cut off roads, gathered troops, killed Qin-appointed officials, and replaced them with his cronies. Following the Qin’s fall, he annexed Guilin and Xiangjun and declared himself King Wu of Nanyue. Emperor Gaozu of Han, due to the people’s exhaustion, spared Zhao Tuo. In the eleventh year of Gaozu, he sent Lu Jia to confirm Zhao Tuo as King of Nanyue, with an agreement for envoys and harmony with Baiyue. During Empress Lü’s reign, officials banned ironware trade with Nanyue. Zhao Tuo suspected King Changsha’s influence, declared himself Emperor Wu of Nanyue, and attacked Changsha’s border cities. Empress Lü sent General Zhou Zao to attack, but heat and illness halted the army. After her death, the Han stopped. Zhao Tuo expanded his territory to over 10,000 miles, bribing Minyue, Xiou, and Luoyue, and acted as an emperor.

translation:
Empress Gao sent General Longlu Hou Zhou Zao to attack Zhao Tuo.
In the hot and humid climate, most of the soldiers became seriously ill, making it impossible for the army to cross Yangshan Mountains.
More than a year later, Queen Gao died, and the Han army stopped attacking.
Therefore, Zhao Tuo relied on his army to show off his power on the border, and bribed Minyue, Xiou and Luoyue with property to make them all belong to South Vietnam, making his territory more than 10,000 miles long from east to west.
Zhao Tuo actually rode in Huangwu Zuohu's chariot and issued orders as the emperor, which was equal to the status of the Han Dynasty.
In the first year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, when the emperor had just ruled the world, he sent envoys to the princes and the rulers of the barbarians from all over the world to inform them of his intention to come to Beijing from Dai to ascend the throne, and to let them know the emperor's saintly virtues.
So for the tomb of Zhao Tuo's parents in Zhending, a tomb guard was set up, and sacrifices were held on time every year. His cousins ​​were also summoned, and they were given honorable official positions and generous rewards to show their favor.
The emperor ordered Prime Minister Chen Ping to recommend people who could be sent as envoys to South Vietnam. Chen Ping said that Lu Jia, a native of Haochou, had served as envoys to South Vietnam many times during the late emperor's reign.
The emperor summoned Lu Jia, appointed him Taizhong doctor, and went to South Vietnam as an envoy. He took the opportunity to blame Zhao Tuo for proclaiming himself emperor and not sending an envoy to report to the emperor.
When Lu Jia arrived in South Vietnam, the South Vietnamese king Zhao was particularly frightened and wrote an apology to the emperor, saying: The barbarian chief husband Chen Tuo used to isolate and discriminate against South Vietnam. I secretly suspected that the king of Changsha was a slanderous minister. I also heard in this distant place that the high queen killed Zhao Tuo's clan and dug and burned the graves of his ancestors. Therefore, he abandoned himself and invaded the border area of ​​​​Changsha.
Moreover, in the low and humid land in the south, among the barbarians, Minyue in the east only had thousands of people, but they called their ruler king; in the west, naked countries like Xiou and Luoyue also had to call themselves kings.
So I arrogantly stole the emperor's title to comfort myself. How dare I report this to the emperor!
Zhao Tuo kowtowed deeply and apologized, saying that he would remain a vassal minister of the Han Dynasty for a long time and abide by his duty to pay tribute to the emperor.
So Zhao Tuo issued an order to the whole country, saying: I heard that two heroes cannot coexist, and two sages cannot live together in the same world.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty was a wise emperor. From now on, I will get rid of the imperial system and will no longer ride in Huangwu Zuohu's car.
Lu Jia returned to Beijing to report the matter, and Emperor Wen of Han was very happy.
Continuing to the era of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Zhao Tuo professed his vassalage to the Han Dynasty and sent people to Chang'an to meet the emperor in the spring and autumn.
However, in South Vietnam, Zhao Tuo always stole the title of emperor. He only became king when he sent envoys to meet the emperor, and accepted the emperor's orders just like the princes.
In the fourth year of Jianyuan, Zhao Tuo died.
Zhao Tuo's grandson Zhao Hu became the king of South Vietnam.
summary: In the first year of Emperor Wen of Han, the emperor honored Zhao Tuo’s parents’ tomb and his cousins. He sent Lu Jia to rebuke Zhao Tuo for claiming the emperor title. Zhao Tuo apologized, citing fear of King Changsha and the queen’s actions, and claimed he used the title for self-comfort among barbarians. He pledged vassalage to Han, removed imperial trappings, and continued as a vassal. During Emperor Jing’s era, Zhao Tuo outwardly submitted but secretly kept the emperor title. He died in the fourth year of Jianyuan, succeeded by his grandson Zhao Hu.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/南越列传

translation:
At this time, King Ying of Minyue launched a war to attack the border towns of South Vietnam. Zhao Hu sent people to write to the Emperor of Han, saying: South Vietnam and Minyue are both vassals of the Han Dynasty and cannot send troops to attack each other without permission.
Now that Fujian and Yue have invaded me, I dare not send troops to fight. I hope that the emperor will issue an edict to deal with this matter.
So the emperor praised the South Vietnamese for their loyal behavior and abiding by their duties and covenants, sent troops for them, and sent two generals to attack Minyue.
Before the Han army crossed the Yangshan Mountains, Yu Shan, the younger brother of the King of Minyue, killed Ying and surrendered to the Han Dynasty, thus stopping the crusade.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty sent Zhuang Zhu to explain the court's intentions to the King of Nanyue. Zhao Hu kowtowed deeply and said: The emperor sent troops to attack Fujian and Yue for me. Even if I die, I can't repay the emperor's kindness!
Zhao Hu sent Prince Yingqi to the court to serve as a bodyguard.
He then said to Zhuang Zhu: The country has just been invaded by the enemy. Please leave first.
Zhao Hu was preparing his bags day and night to go to the capital to meet the emperor.
After Zhuang Zhu left, his ministers admonished Zhao Hujin and said: The Han Dynasty sent troops to kill Ying, and they also used this action to warn South Vietnam.
Moreover, the late king once said in the past that when serving the emperor, one only hopes not to be rude. The most important thing is not to go to the emperor just because you like to listen to the good words of the messenger.
If you go to court to see the emperor, you will not be able to come back. This is a situation of national subjugation.
So Zhao Hu used illness as an excuse and did not go to see the Emperor of Han in the end.
More than ten years later, Zhao Huzhen became seriously ill, and Prince Yingqi asked to return to the country.
When Zhao Hu died, he was given the posthumous title of King Wen.
After Ying Qi Dai was established as the King of Nanyue, he hid the seal of Emperor Wu of his ancestor.
When Yingqi went to Chang'an to serve as a guard, he took a daughter from Handan's family as his wife and gave birth to a son named Zhao Xing.
When he ascended the throne and became king, he wrote to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, requesting that his wife Xi be made the queen and Zhao Xing be the prince.
The Han Dynasty repeatedly sent envoys to tactfully advise Ying Qi to go to the emperor. Ying Qi liked to kill people arbitrarily and was afraid that if he went to the capital to worship the emperor, he would be forced to follow the laws of the mainland and implement the laws of the Han Dynasty. Therefore, he used illness as an excuse to not go to the emperor and only sent his son Cigong to the capital to serve as a guard.
When Yingqi died, he was given the posthumous title of King Ming.
Prince Zhao Xingdai was established as the King of Nanyue, and his mother became the Queen Mother.
When the Queen Mother was not married to Yingqi as her concubine, she had committed adultery with Anguo Shaoji, a native of Baling.
After Yingqi's death, in the fourth year of Yuanding, the Han Dynasty sent Anguo Shaoji to persuade the King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother to go to Beijing to worship the emperor like the princes in the interior. He ordered the debaters to admonish the official Zhongjun and others to publicize this idea, and asked the warrior Wei Chen and others to assist him where they were insufficient. Guard Lu Bode led his troops to garrison in Guiyang, waiting for the envoy.
summary: Zhao Hu faced an attack from Minyue’s King Ying. He requested Han intervention, and Emperor Wu sent troops, leading to Ying’s death. Zhao Hu thanked the emperor but, advised by ministers, avoided visiting the capital, fearing captivity. He died as King Wen. His son Yingqi, who had married a woman from Handan and fathered Zhao Xing, became king. Yingqi hid his grandfather’s emperor seal, refused to visit the capital due to fear of Han laws, and died as King Ming. Zhao Xing succeeded, with his mother as queen mother.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/南越列传

translation:
The King of Nanyue is young, and the Queen Mother is from the Central Plains. She once committed adultery with Anguo Shaoji. This time Anguo Shaoji came to serve as an envoy and committed adultery with her again.
Most people in South Vietnam knew about this, and most of them did not rely on the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother was afraid of unrest and wanted to rely on the power of the Han Dynasty. She repeatedly persuaded the King of Nanyue and his ministers to request to belong to the Han Dynasty.
So he sent a letter to the emperor through an envoy, requesting that the princes in the interior should meet with the emperor once every three years and remove the border barriers.
So the emperor agreed to their request and gave the silver seal to Lu Jia, the prime minister of South Vietnam, and also gave the official seals such as internal history, lieutenant, and master, and the rest of the official positions were placed by South Vietnam himself.
They abolished their previous punishments of tattoos and torture, and used the laws of the Han Dynasty to compare with the princes in the interior.
The envoys stayed to pacify South Vietnam.
The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother packed their belongings and valuables in preparation for going to Beijing to meet the Emperor.
Lu Jia, the prime minister of South Vietnam, was very old and had assisted three kings. There were more than 70 officials and officials in his clan. The men all married the princess's wives, and the women married the princes and their brothers' clan members. They were related by marriage to the King of Qin in Cangwu County.
His position in South Vietnam is very prominent, and the South Vietnamese people trust him. Many people have become his cronies, surpassing the King of South Vietnam in terms of popular support.
The King of Nanyue wanted to write to the emperor. He repeatedly suggested that the king give up this move, but the King of Nanyue did not listen.
He had the idea of ​​​​treason against the King of Nanyue, and repeatedly excused himself from meeting the Han Dynasty envoys due to illness.
The envoys paid great attention to Lu Jia's words and deeds, but due to the situation, they did not execute Lu Jia.
The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother were also afraid that Lu Jia would be the first to attack, so they arranged a banquet and planned to use the power of the Han Dynasty envoys to kill Lu Jia and others.
At the banquet, the envoys all faced east, the Queen Mother faced south, the king faced north, and Prime Minister Lu Jia and the ministers all faced west, sitting and drinking with them.
Lu Jia's younger brother was a general and led his troops to wait outside the palace.
While drinking, the Queen Mother said to Lu Jia: It is in the interests of the country that South Vietnam belongs to the Han Dynasty, but Prime Minister, you complain that this is not good. Why?
The Queen Mother wanted to anger the Han Dynasty envoy.
The envoy hesitated and did not dare to kill Lu Jia.
Lu Jia saw that the people around him were not his cronies, so he stood up and walked out.
The queen mother got angry and wanted to hit Lu Jia with a spear, but the king stopped her.
Lu Jia went out, divided some of his brother's soldiers, and arranged them around his residence. He refused to meet the king and the envoy because of his illness.
Lu Jia secretly prepared to launch a rebellion with his ministers.
The King of Nanyue had no intention of killing Lu Jia. Lu Jia knew this, so he did not launch a rebellion for several months.
The Queen Mother had engaged in promiscuous behavior and no one in the South Vietnam country would join her. She wanted to kill Lu Jia alone, but she was unable to do it.
The Emperor heard that Lu Jia disobeyed the King of Nanyue. The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother were weak and could not control Lu Jia, and the envoys were timid and incapable of decision-making.
summary: The queen mother, who had previously committed adultery with Anguo Shaoji, sought to submit to Han. Emperor Wu sent Anguo Shaoji to persuade them. The young king and queen mother agreed to become vassals, but Prime Minister Lu Jia, who had served three kings and held great influence, opposed. He feared losing power and plotted rebellion. At a banquet, the queen mother tried to provoke the Han envoy to kill Lu Jia, but the envoy hesitated. Lu Jia left, gathered troops, and refused to meet the king. The queen mother’s efforts failed.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/南越列传

translation:
In the autumn of the fifth year of Yuan Ding, Weiwei Lu Bode became General Fubo and led his troops out of Guiyang and went straight down to the Huishui River; Lieutenant Yang Pu, the Lord Commander, became the general of the building and ship, left Yuzhang and went straight down to Hengpu; two people who had returned to the Han Dynasty and were made marquises A South Vietnamese man became General Ge Chuan and General Xia Li and led his troops out of Lingling. Then one army went straight to Lishui and the other to Cangwu. He asked Chiyihou to use the sinners of Bashu to mobilize Yelang's soldiers and go straight to the Zoke River. In the end, they all met up in Panyu.
In the winter of the sixth year of Yuanding, General Lou Chuan led his elite troops to first capture Xunshan, then broke through Shimen, paid the warships and grain of South Vietnam, took the opportunity to advance forward, defeated the vanguard of South Vietnam, and led tens of thousands of troops to wait for General Fubo.
General Fubo led the pardoned sinners. The road was far away, and the date of rendezvous happened to be missed. Therefore, only more than a thousand people joined General Louchuan, so they moved forward together.
General Lou Chuan was in front and fought straight to Panyu.
Zhao Jiande and Lu Jia were both defending in the city.
General Louchuan chose a favorable place to garrison in the southeast of Panyu; General Fubo garrisoned in the northwest of Panyu.
Just when it was dark, General Lou Chuan attacked and defeated the South Vietnamese and set fire to Panyu City.
The South Vietnamese have heard the name of General Fubo in normal times, but now that it's dark, they don't know how many troops he has.
General Fubo set up camp, sent envoys to summon those who surrendered, gave them official seals, and then sent them back to recruit others.
General Lou Chuan fought hard and burned the enemy, but drove the rebels into General Fubo's camp to surrender.
At dawn, all the enemy soldiers in the city surrendered to General Fubo.
Lu Jia and Zhao Jiande had fled into the sea with hundreds of their subordinates at night and took a boat to the west.
General Fubo took the opportunity to ask the South Vietnamese nobles who had surrendered, and then he knew Lu Jia's whereabouts and sent people to hunt him down.
Su Hong, a former school captain who is now an officer of General Fubo, captured Zhao Jiande and was named Chang Haihou; Nanyue native Lang Guan Duji captured Lu Jia and was named Lincai Marquis.
Zhao Guang, King of Cangwu, had the same surname as the King of Nanyue. Hearing that the Han Dynasty troops had arrived, the Jieyang County magistrate named Ding of Nanyue decided to join the Han Dynasty. Weng, the governor of Guilin County in Nanyue, informed Ou Luo to surrender to the Han Dynasty. They were all sealed.
Before the troops of General Ge Chuan and General Xia Li, as well as the Yelang army so called mobilized by Marquis Chiyi, had arrived, South Vietnam had been pacified.
So the Han Dynasty established nine counties here.
General Fubo increased the number of fiefs, and General Louchuan's army broke through the enemy's strong defense, so he was granted the title of General Lianghou.
After Zhao Tuo first became king, the Kingdom of Nanyue was destroyed for five generations, a total of ninety-three years.
Tai Shigong said: Wei Tuo became the king of Nanyue because of Ren Xiao's promotion and persuasion.
Just as the Han Dynasty was initially stabilized, he was made a prince.
Longluhou led his troops to attack South Vietnam. They encountered a hot and humid climate. Many of the soldiers were infected with diseases and were unable to march, which made Zhao Tuo even more proud.
summary: The emperor sent Han Qianqiu with 2,000 troops to South Vietnam. Lu Jia rebelled, killed the king, queen mother, and Han envoys, and installed Zhao Jiande as king. Han Qianqiu’s army was ambushed and destroyed. The emperor then launched a large-scale attack in the fifth year of Yuanding, with generals Lu Bode, Yang Pu, and others leading forces from multiple directions. In the sixth year, Yang Pu’s troops captured Panyu, and Lu Bode’s forces accepted surrenders. Lu Jia and Zhao Jiande fled by sea but were captured. South Vietnam was pacified, and the Han established nine counties. The kingdom lasted five generations for ninety-three years. The historian notes that Zhao Tuo’s rise was due to Ren Xiao, and the kingdom’s fall stemmed from internal conflicts and Lu Jia’s actions.

translation:
General Wei Qing was a native of Pingyang County. His father Zheng Ji served as a minor official in the county and served in the family of Pingyang Marquis Cao Shou. He had an affair with Pingyang Marquis's concubine Wei Wei and gave birth to Wei Qing.
Wei Qing's half-brother is called Wei Changzi, and his half-sister is called Wei Zifu. Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty in Princess Pingyang's family, so he pretended to be surnamed Wei. Wei Qing, whose given name is Zhongqing.
The eldest son of Wei changed his surname to Changjun.
Changjun's mother is Wei Yu.
Wei's eldest daughter is called Wei Ru, her second daughter is Wei Shaoji, and her third daughter is Wei Zifu.
Later, Wei Zifu's younger brothers Bu and Guang both pretended to be surnamed Wei.
Wei Qing was a servant of the Hou family in Pingyang. When he was a child, he returned to his father Zheng Ji's house, and his father asked him to shepherd sheep.
Zheng Ji's sons from his first marriage all treated him as a slave, not as a brother.
Wei Qing once followed someone to the living room of Ganquan Palace. A prisoner with an iron shackle around his neck came to Wei Qing and said, "You are a noble man. You will be a high official and a marquis in the future!"
Wei Qing smiled and said, "I was born of a slave. I would be satisfied if I didn't get beaten or scolded by others. How could I think of becoming a marquis?"
When Wei Qing grew up, he became a cavalryman of the Pingyang Hou family and often followed Princess Pingyang.
In the spring of the second year of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Wei Qing's sister Wei Zifu entered the palace and was favored by Emperor Wu.
Queen Chen Ajiao is the daughter of Liu Piao, the eldest princess of Tangyi. She has no sons and is jealous.
The eldest princess heard that Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu and was pregnant. She was jealous of her and sent people to arrest Wei Qing.
At that time, Wei Qing was serving in Jianzhang Palace and was not yet famous.
The eldest princess arrested and imprisoned Wei Qing and wanted to kill him.
Wei Qing's friend Qi Lang Gongsun Ao and some strong men snatched him out. For this reason, Wei Qing did not die.
When Emperor Wu heard the news, he summoned Wei Qing and appointed him as the supervisor of Jian Zhang, with the title of Shizhong. Together with his half-brothers, they all received high status, and the emperor's rewards for them accumulated as much as a thousand pieces of gold in a few days.
Wei Ru became the wife of Grand Servant Sun He.
It turned out that Wei Shaoer had an affair with Chen Zhang, so Emperor Wu summoned Chen Zhang and made him a noble person.
As a result, Gongsun Ao became more and more prominent.
Wei Zifu became Emperor Wu's wife.
Wei Qing was promoted to Dazhong doctor.
In the fifth year of Yuanguang, Wei Qing served as the general of cavalry and attacked the Xiongnu, marching out of the fortress from Shanggu; Sun He, the imperial servant, served as the general of light chariots and marched out of the fortress from Yunzhong; Gongsun Ao, the Dazhong doctor, served as the general of cavalry and marched out from Daijun; Wei Wei Li Guang served as the general of heroic cavalry and marched out of the fortress from Yanmen; each army had ten thousand cavalry.
Wei Qing led his troops to Fucheng and killed hundreds of enemies.
summary: Wei Qing, a native of Pingyang County, was the illegitimate son of Zheng Ji and a concubine of the Pingyang Marquis household. His half-sister Wei Zifu gained favor with Emperor Wu of Han, leading Wei Qing to adopt the surname Wei. As a youth, he served as a servant and shepherd, enduring mistreatment from his half-brothers. A prisoner once prophesied his future nobility, but Wei Qing dismissed it. He later became a cavalryman for the Pingyang Marquis. When Wei Zifu entered the palace and became pregnant, Empress Chen, jealous, attempted to kill Wei Qing. His friend Gongsun Ao rescued him, and Emperor Wu subsequently appointed Wei Qing as a palace supervisor, elevating his status. Wei Zifu later became empress, and Wei Qing was promoted to Dazhong doctor.

translation:
Four years later, General Wei Qing died, and the imperial court gave him the posthumous title Liehou.
Wei Qing's son Wei Qian took over the title and became Marquis of Changping.
Fourteen years passed since the general besieged Shanyu and he died. The reason why he did not attack the Xiongnu again during this period was because the Han Dynasty had few horses and was in the process of conquering East Vietnam and South Vietnam in the south, Korea in the east, and attacking the Qiang and Southwest Yi. Therefore, there was no attack on the Xiongnu for a long time.
Because General Wei Qing married Princess Pingyang, the Marquis of Changping and his wife could succeed the Marquis.
But six years later, he broke the law and lost the marquis.
The following is the list of the two generals and their lieutenants:
In total, General Wei Qing attacked the Xiongnu seven times and captured more than 50,000 enemy soldiers.
He fought with Chanyu once and regained the Henan area, so he established Shuofang County and enfeoffed it twice, granting a total of 11,800 households.
His three sons were all granted the title of marquis, and each of them was granted the title of 1,300 households.
Combined, the number of households in the Wei family that were granted a title was 15,700.
A total of nine of Wei Qing's lieutenants and lieutenants were granted the title of marquis for their meritorious services following Wei Qing, and a total of fourteen of his lieutenants and lieutenants had become generals.
One of the lieutenants was Li Guang, who has his own biography.
Others that have not been passed on include:
General Gongsun He.
He is from Yiqu, and his ancestors are Huns.
Gongsun He's father Qingxie was granted the title of Marquis of Pingqu during the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, but lost the title for breaking the law.
Gongsun He served as a minister when Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was the prince.
In the eighth year after Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, Gongsun He became a general of Qingchao as a servant and garrisoned in Mayi.
Four years later, Gongsun He set out from the clouds as a light chariot general to attack the Xiongnu.
Five years later, Gongsun He served as a cavalry general and followed the general to defeat the Huns, and was granted the title of Marquis of Nanxu.
A year later, Gongsun He, as General Zuo, sent troops from Dingxiang to attack the Xiongnu twice with the general, but without success.
Four years later, he lost the Marquis because he committed the crime of insufficient gold and insufficient weight.
Eight years later, as General Fuju, he sent troops from Wuyuan and went on an expedition of more than 2,000 miles to defeat the Xiongnu, but with no success.
Eight years later, he became prime minister as a servant and was granted the title of Marquis Ge Yi.
Gongsun He served as a general seven times, but failed to achieve great success in attacking the Xiongnu. He was made a prince twice and became a prime minister.
Later, because his son Gongsun Jingsheng had an affair with Princess Yangshi and engaged in witchcraft, he was exterminated and left no descendants.
General Li Xi is from Yuzhi.
He once served Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, and when Emperor Wu of the Han came to the throne for eight years, he became a general officer and garrisoned in Mayi. Six years later, he became a general and sent troops from Daijun to fight against the Huns. Three years later, Li Xi became a general and followed the general to send troops from Shuofang to attack the Huns.
No credit. Li Xi served as a general three times in total, and later he often held senior positions.
General Gongsun Ao was from Yiqu.
summary: In 129 BCE, Wei Qing led a cavalry attack on the Xiongnu, achieving modest success. Subsequent campaigns saw him capture the Henan region, driving out Xiongnu kings and establishing Shuofang Commandery. For these victories, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changping. Further campaigns against the Xiongnu resulted in significant victories, including the capture of King Youxian's forces and vast numbers of livestock. Emperor Wu granted Wei Qing additional households and enfeoffed his sons as marquises, though Wei Qing humbly declined, crediting the emperor and his officers.

translation:
In addition, many of the petty officials and soldiers under the Hussars General Huo Qubing served as officials and received rewards.
However, the general Wei Qing failed to get the title, and none of the officials and soldiers in the army were granted the title of marquis.
When the two armies led by Wei Qing and Huo Qubing left the fortress, they had a military parade at the frontier fortress. At that time, there were 140,000 government and private horses. However, when they returned to the fortress, there were less than 30,000 horses left.
So the imperial court added the official position of Grand Sima, and both the General and the Hussars became Grand Sima.
And a decree was made to make the rank and salary of the hussar general equal to that of the general.
From then on, the power of General Wei Qing declined day by day, while the Hussars General became more powerful day by day.
Most of the general's old friends and retainers left him and went to serve the hussar generals. These people often received titles for this, but Ren An was the only one who refused to do so.
The hussar general is a man of few words, silent, courageous and courageous.
Emperor Wu once wanted to teach Sun Tzu and Wu Qi the art of war. He replied: In war, it only depends on the policy and strategy. There is no need to learn ancient war art.
Emperor Wu built a mansion for him and asked General Hussar to take a look. He replied: The Huns have not been eliminated yet, so they have no intention of considering private matters.
From then on, Emperor Wu valued and favored Hussar General Huo Qubing more.
However, Huo Qubing had been serving the emperor in the palace since he was a boy, receiving dignitaries, but he did not know how to show sympathy to the soldiers.
When he went to war, the emperor sent his eunuchs to give him dozens of carts of food. When he came back, there was a lot of leftover rice and meat thrown away on the carts, and some of his soldiers were starving.
When he was fighting outside the wall, the soldiers were short of food, and some were so hungry that they could not stand up, while the hussar generals were still drawing pitches and playing football games.
Most of what he does is like this.
General Wei Qing was kind-hearted and had a spirit of compromise. He pleased the emperor with his tolerance and gentleness, but no one in the world praised him.
General Hussar passed away three years after his attack on the Xiongnu in the fourth year of Yuanshou, that is, in the sixth year of Yuanshou.
Emperor Wu was very sad about his death, and dispatched the armored troops from the five border counties to form a formation from Chang'an to Maoling, so that the outside of the tomb built by Huo Qubing would look like praying for the mountains.
He was given a posthumous title, combining the two principles of bravery and territorial expansion, and called him Marquis Jinghuan.
Huo Qubing's son Yan succeeded the title of Champion Marquis.
Huo Shen was young and named Zihou. The emperor liked him and hoped to appoint him as a general when he grew up.
Six years later, in the first year of Yuanfeng, Huo Huan died, and the emperor gave him the posthumous title of Aihou.
He had no sons, so his descendants were cut off and the feudal state was abolished.
Since the death of General Hussar, the general's eldest son, the Houwei couple of Yichun, lost their marquis title for breaking the law.
Five years later, the two younger brothers of the Wei couple, the Marquis of Yin'an Wei Buyi and the Marquis of Fagan Weideng, both lost their marquis titles because they were guilty of insufficient gold and insufficient weight.
Two years after losing the marquis, the feudal state of the champion marquis was abolished.
summary: Wei Qing's nephew, Huo Qubing, emerged as a brilliant commander, earning the title of Champion Marquis for his daring raids. Huo Qubing's campaigns were marked by deep penetrations into Xiongnu territory, capturing kings and vast numbers of enemies. He became increasingly favored by the emperor, eventually matching Wei Qing in rank and power. Huo Qubing famously declined a mansion, stating, "The Xiongnu have not yet been eliminated, so I have no intention of considering private matters." However, he was known for his lack of concern for his soldiers' welfare, often discarding food while they starved. After Huo Qubing's death, Wei Qing's influence waned. Wei Qing died four years later, and his descendants lost their titles due to legal infractions. The text concludes with a list of Wei Qing's and Huo Qubing's subordinates, many of whom became generals or marquises. The historian Sima Qian notes that Wei Qing, despite his nobility, refrained from recruiting scholars, fearing the emperor's displeasure, a principle Huo Qubing also followed.

translation:
Sima Xiangru was born in Chengdu, Shu County, and his courtesy name was Changqing.
When he was a boy, he liked to read and learn swordsmanship, so his parents named him Quanzi.
After Sima Xiangru completed his studies, he admired Lin Xiangru's character and changed his name to Xiangru.
Initially, due to his family's wealth, he was awarded the position of Langguan, guarded Emperor Xiao Jing, and became a regular servant of martial arts, but this was not his hobby.
It happened that Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty did not like Ci Fu. At this time, King Liang Xiao came to the capital to see Emperor Jing. He was accompanied by people who were good at lobbying, including Zou Yang from Qijun, Meicheng from Huaiyin, and Mr. Zhuang Ji from Wuxian. Xiangru fell in love with these people when he saw them, so he resigned from his official position on the pretext of illness and lived in Liang State.
King Liang Xiao asked Xiangru and other scholars to live together. Xiangru had the opportunity to get along with scholars and lobbyists for several years, so he wrote "Zixu Fu".
Just when King Liang Xiao died, Xiangru had to return to Chengdu. However, his family was poor and he had no occupation that could support his life.
Xiangru always got along well with Wang Ji, the magistrate of Linqiong County. Wang Ji said: Chang Qing, you have been away from home for a long time and are seeking an official position. It is not satisfactory. You can come to see me.
So Xiangru went to Linqiong and lived in the capital pavilion in the city.
The Linqiong County Magistrate pretended to be respectful and visited Xiangru every day.
At first, Xiangru still met each other with courtesy. Later, he lied about being ill and asked his entourage to refuse Wang Ji's visit. However, Wang Ji was more cautious and respectful.
There are many rich people in Linqiong County. For example, the Sun family of King Zhuo has 800 slaves, and the Cheng Zheng family has hundreds of people. The two discussed with each other and said: The county magistrate has a distinguished guest, and we are going to prepare a banquet for him.
The county magistrate was also invited.
When the county magistrate arrived at the Zhuo family, there were already hundreds of guests in the Zhuo family.
At noon, I went to invite Sima Changqing, but he refused to come, saying that he was ill. Linqiong ordered to see Xiangru not come and did not dare to eat. He went to greet Xiangru himself.
Xiangru had no choice but to come to Zhuo's house. All the guests were amazed and envious of his charisma.
When the wine was in full swing, the Linqiong County Magistrate stepped forward, placed the harp in front of Xiangru, and said, "I heard that Chang Qing likes to play the harp very much, and I hope to listen to a piece of music to cheer you up."
After thanking Xiangru, he played one or two pieces of music.
At this time, Zhuo Wangsun had a daughter named Wenjun, who was newly widowed and loved music. So Xiangru pretended to respect each other with the county magistrate, and secretly aroused her love with the sound of the piano.
When Xiangru came to Qiong, he was followed by carriages and horses. He was dignified in appearance, quiet and elegant, and very generous. When Zhuo Wang and Sun's family were drinking and playing piano music, Zhuo Wenjun secretly looked at him through the crack in the door. He was very happy and liked him very much, but he was afraid that he would not understand his feelings.
After the banquet, Xiangru asked someone to reward Wenjun's waiter with a large sum of money to convey his admiration to her.
So Zhuo Wenjun ran away from home at night and eloped with Xiangru. Xiangru and Wenjun hurried back to Chengdu.
summary: Sima Xiangru, courtesy name Changqing, was born in Chengdu, Shu County. As a youth, he studied literature and swordsmanship, and later admired Lin Xiangru, changing his name accordingly. He initially served as a Langguan under Emperor Jing of Han due to family wealth, but disliked his post. When Emperor Jing showed little interest in rhapsodies (Ci Fu), Xiangru befriended scholars like Zou Yang and Mei Cheng during a visit from King Xiao of Liang. He resigned on pretence of illness and lived in Liang, where he wrote "Zixu Fu." After King Xiao's death, Xiangru returned to Chengdu impoverished. Xiangru's friend Wang Ji, magistrate of Linqiong, invited him to stay. Wang Ji feigned deference, but Xiangru eventually refused visits, feigning illness. Wealthy locals, including Zhuo Wangsun and Cheng Zheng, hosted a banquet for the magistrate. Xiangru initially declined but attended after the magistrate personally invited him. During the feast, Xiangru played the zither, captivating Zhuo Wangsun's newly widowed daughter, Wenjun, who secretly admired him. After the banquet, Xiangru bribed her attendants to convey his feelings, and Wenjun eloped with him to Chengdu, where they lived in poverty with only four walls.

translation:
When I entered the house, I saw nothing but four walls.
When Zhuo Wangsun learned about his daughter's elopement, he was furious and said: "My daughter is extremely unqualified. I can't bear to hurt her, but I won't give her a cent either."
Some people tried to persuade Zhuo Wangsun, but he still refused to listen.
After a long time, Wenjun felt unhappy and said: "Chang Qing, as long as you go to Linqiong with me, you can make a living by borrowing money from your brothers. Why have you made yourself so miserable?"
Xiangru came to Linqiong with Wenjun, sold all his carriages and horses, and bought a hotel to sell wine.
He also asked Wenjun to personally take charge of the wine shop business in Longqian, while he put on his calf-nosed trousers and worked with the employees, washing wine vessels in the busy city.
When Zhuo Wangsun heard about this, he felt so ashamed that he stayed behind closed doors.
Some brothers and elders talked to Zhuo Wangsun and said, "You have a son and two daughters. What the family lacks is not money."
Now, Wenjun has become the wife of Sima Changqing. Changqing was tired of running away from home. Although he was poor, he was indeed a talent and could be completely relied on. Besides, he is a distinguished guest of the county magistrate, why do you despise him like this!
Zhuo Wangsun had no choice but to give Wenjun 100 slaves, 1 million in money, clothes, bedding and various belongings when she got married.
Wenjun returned to Chengdu with Xiangru, bought land and houses, and became a wealthy family.
After a long period of time, Yang Deyi, a native of Shu County, served as a dog supervisor to serve the emperor.
One day, Emperor Wu read "Zixu Fu" and thought it was well written. He said: "I cannot be at the same time as this author."
Yang Deyi said: My fellow countryman Sima Xiangru claimed that he wrote this poem.
Emperor Wu was very surprised and summoned Xiangru to ask.
Xiangru said: There is such a thing.
However, this Fu only describes the affairs of the princes and is not worth reading.
Please ask me to write a poem about the emperor's hunting trip. After the poem is completed, I will present it to the emperor.
Emperor Wu agreed and ordered the minister to give him a pen and wooden slips.
Xiangru used the fictitious words "Zixu" to state the beauty of the Chu State; "Mr. Wu You" means that there is no such thing, and uses it to refute the Chu State for the Qi State; "Wu Shi Gong" means that there is no such person to clarify the principle of being the emperor.
Therefore, an article was written under the guise of these three people to deduce the prosperous scenes of the emperor and the princes.
The theme of the last chapter of the Fu comes down to frugality, in order to exhort the emperor.
After presenting the gift to the emperor, the emperor was very happy.
The text of the poem says:
The King of Chu sent Zixu as an envoy to the State of Qi. The King of Qi dispatched all the soldiers in the territory, prepared many chariots and horses, and went hunting with the envoy.
After the hunting was over, Zixu went to visit Mr. Wu You and boasted about the incident to him. Wu Shigong happened to be present.
After everyone sat down, Mr. Wu You asked Zixu: "Are you happy hunting today?"
Zixu said: Happy. Is there a lot of prey?
Zixu replied: Very few.
If this is the case, where does the joy come from?
Zixu replied: I am happy that King Qi wanted to boast to me about his many chariots and horses, but I answered him with the grand scene of King Chu hunting in Yunmengze.
Mr. Wuyou said: Can you tell me and listen? Zixu said, "Okay."
The King of Qi commanded thousands of chariots and selected tens of thousands of riders to hunt on the shores of the East China Sea.
summary: Zhuo Wangsun was furious and refused to support them. Wenjun suggested they return to Linqiong, where they sold their possessions and opened a tavern. Wenjun managed the shop while Xiangru worked publicly in menial tasks. Ashamed, Zhuo Wangsun, persuaded by relatives, eventually gave them 100 slaves, money, and belongings, enabling them to become wealthy. Later, Emperor Wu of Han read "Zixu Fu" and admired it. Yang Deyi informed him that Xiangru was the author. Summoned, Xiangru offered to write a grander rhapsody about the emperor's hunting grounds. He composed "Shanglin Fu," using fictitious characters—Zixu (Chu), Mr. Wuyou (Qi), and Wu Shigong (the emperor's perspective)—to contrast princely extravagance with imperial virtue. The rhapsody described vast landscapes, hunting scenes, and concluded with a call for frugality and benevolence. The emperor was delighted and appointed Xiangru as Langguan.

translation:
They followed the emperor's teachings, obeyed government orders, followed the trend of the times, and accepted education. The way of sage is vigorously revitalized, the people turn to benevolence and righteousness, and punishments are abandoned and not used. The king's kindness is higher than that of the three emperors, and his achievements surpass those of the five emperors. If political performance reaches this point, safari is a gratifying thing. If you spend all day exposed and galloping in the gardens, mentally exhausted, physically exhausted, abandoning the function of the chariots and horses, damaging the energy of the soldiers, and wasting money from the treasury, but showing no kindness or kindness to the people, only focusing on personal happiness, not caring about the many people, forgetting the affairs of the country, and coveting the hunting of pheasants and rabbits, this is what a benevolent king is not willing to do.
From this point of view, isn’t the hunting behavior of Qi and Chu sad?
Each of the two countries has a land area of ​​only a thousand miles, but the garden covers an area of ​​900 miles. As a result, the grassy fields cannot be turned into cultivated fields, and the people have no food to eat.
They rely on their humble status as princes to enjoy the luxurious pleasures of the emperor. I am afraid that the people will suffer disaster.
So the two gentlemen, Zixu and Wu You, changed their expressions, felt lost, wandered back, left their seats, and said: I am shallow and ignorant, and have no scruples, but I have received a lesson today, and I want to learn from it seriously.
After this fu was written and presented to the emperor, the emperor appointed Xiangru as Lang Guan.
Wu Shi publicly said that Shanglin Garden was vast, with valleys, springs and all things, and Zi Xu said that Yun Mengze had many things. It was extravagant and exaggerated, and it was not what etiquette advocated. Therefore, he deleted the key points, attributed them to the right way, and commented on them.
Xiangru served as Langguan for several years. At that time, Tang Meng was ordered to plunder and open up Yelang and Bozhong to the west. He recruited thousands of officials and soldiers from Ba and Shu counties, and more than 10,000 land and water transportation personnel from Xijun. He also used wartime laws to kill the commander, and the people of Ba and Shu were shocked and frightened.
When the emperor heard about this situation, he sent Xiangru to blame Tang Meng and took the opportunity to tell the people of Ba and Shu that what Tang Meng did was not the emperor's original intention.
The message said:
Announcement to the governors of Ba and Shu: The barbarians have taken military power for themselves, disobeyed the imperial court, and have not been attacking for a long time. They often invade the borders and cause hardships to the scholar-bureaucrats.
Now that the emperor has ascended the throne, he is trying to appease the world and make China peaceful and harmonious.
Then he mobilized his troops and went north to attack the Xiongnu, which shocked the Xiongnu. They surrendered and bowed their knees to seek peace.
Kangju and other countries in the Western Regions also went through translations, communicated with each other, requested to see Emperor Wu, kowtowed reverently, and presented tributes.
Then the army pointed directly to the east, and the king of Minyue was killed by his younger brother.
Then the army arrived at Panyu, and the King of Nanyue sent Prince Yingqi to the court.
The monarchs of Nanyi and the leaders of Xibo often paid tribute and taxes, and did not dare to neglect them. Everyone stretched their necks, raised their heels, admired the court, strived for benevolence and righteousness, and wanted to be the servants of the Han Dynasty. However, the road was far away and mountains and rivers blocked them, so they could not come to pay tribute to the Hanjun in person.
Now, those who disobey have been killed, but those who have done good deeds have not yet been rewarded, so the Zhonglang general is sent to treat them politely and make them submit. As for the levying of 500 soldiers and civilians from Ba and Shu, it was just to offer gifts and protect the envoys from accidents. They did not expect to start a war and cause the disaster of war.
Now, the emperor heard that General Zhonglang actually used wartime laws, which frightened the children of Ba and Shu, and made the fathers and elders of Ba and Shu worried about disaster. The two counties of Ba and Shu also transferred grain to General Zhonglang without authorization. This was not the emperor's original intention.
summary: Xiangru served as an envoy to blame Tang Meng for harsh policies in Ba and Shu, issuing an imperial proclamation reassuring the people. He later advocated for reopening southwestern territories, becoming Zhonglang General to pacify the region. Despite opposition, he succeeded, and the emperor was pleased. However, accusations of bribery led to his dismissal, though he was later reinstated as Langguan.

translation:
At this time, the princes of Qiong and Zeo heard that Nanyi had interacted with the Han Dynasty and received many rewards. Therefore, most of them wanted to be the servants of the Han Dynasty. They hoped to compare the treatment of Nanyi with the Han Dynasty and asked the Han Dynasty to appoint them to official positions.
The emperor asked Xiangru about this, and Xiangru said: Qiong Ze, Ran, Zhen, etc. are all very close to Shu, and the roads are easy to open. Prefectures and counties were already established during the Qin Dynasty and were abolished only after the founding of the Han Dynasty.
Now that it is really going to be reopened and set up as counties, its value exceeds that of Nanyi.
The emperor thought that Xiangru was right, so he appointed Xiangru as Zhonglang General and ordered Chijie to go on an envoy.
Deputy envoys Wang Ranyu, Hu Chongguo, Lu Yueren and others rode forward in a carriage driven by four horses, relying on officials and property from Ba and Shu to win over the southwestern barbarians.
When Xiangru and others arrived at Shu County, the prefect of Shu County and his officials went to the outskirts to greet Xiangru. The county magistrate, carrying a bow and arrow, opened the way in front of him. The people of Shu were all proud of this.
So Zhuo Wangsun and Linqiong elders all came to Xiangru's door through their connections, offered cattle and wine, and talked happily with Xiangru.
Zhuo Wangsun sighed and thought that it was too late to marry his daughter to Sima Xiangru, so he gave Wen Jun a generous piece of property to share equally with his son.
Sima Xiangru then pacified the southwestern barbarians. The princes of Qiong, Zuo, Ran, Zhen, and Siyu all requested to become ministers of the Han Dynasty.
So the old passes were demolished, and the border was expanded to reach Moshui and Ruoshui in the west, and Zangke in the south. Using this as the boundary, the Lingguan Road was opened, and a bridge was built on Sunshui River, leading directly to Qiong and Zeo.
Xiangru returned to Beijing to report to the emperor, who was very happy.
When Xiangru was sent as an envoy to the southwestern barbarians, most of the elders in Shu County said it was useless to open the door to the southwestern barbarians. Even the court ministers thought this was the case.
Xiangru also wanted to remonstrate with the emperor, but the suggestion had already been made by himself, so he did not dare to remonstrate further, so he wrote an article, pretending to be an elder in Shu County, and used it to challenge the other party.
The article said:
It has been seventy and eight years since the founding of the Han Dynasty. The virtues are abundant and exist in the political affairs of the six generations of kings. The country is powerful and grand. The imperial favor passed down through time is far-reaching and vast. Not only the people at home have benefited, but also foreign countries have received residual favors.
Therefore, the emperor ordered the envoys to march westward. Those who obstructed the army retreated in accordance with the situation. Wherever the wind of morality and education went, they all fell with the wind.
As a result, Ran Yi surrendered, Zou Yi obeyed, Zhe was pacified, Qiong was saved, Siyu was captured, and Baoman was captured. Then he turned the endless stream of chariots and horses around and set off eastward, returning to Beijing to report to the emperor and arriving in Chengdu, Shu County.
At this time, a total of twenty-seven elders, doctors, recommended gentry, and gentlemen came to visit seriously.
After the greetings were over, he took the opportunity to speak: I heard that the emperor's attitude towards the Yi and Di people was just to contain them and prevent them from severing relations.
But now the soldiers of the three counties are exhausted to open the road to Yelang. It has been three years since the road construction was finally completed. The soldiers are already tired from hard work, and the people are no longer rich. Now we have to continue to open the Western Yi, and the people's labor has been exhausted. I am afraid that this matter will not be completed in the end. This is also the burden of the envoy. I am privately worried about you.
Moreover, it has been many years since Qiong, Zuo, and Xibo were aligned with China, and I can no longer remember them clearly.
summary: Xiangru suffered from diabetes and avoided court debates. He advised the emperor against dangerous hunting, writing a remonstrance. He also composed "Ode to the Immortals" and "Adult Fu," depicting celestial journeys. His final work, a treatise on the Feng and Shan sacrifices, urged the emperor to perform these rites. The emperor later conducted them after Xiangru's death.

translation:
Tian Fu Rui has made it clear that there is no need to warn him again.
It should be entrusted accordingly and tell the king to hold a Zen ceremony. Looking through the classics, we can see that there is a relationship between nature and human society, and the two inspire each other and are harmonious.
The virtue of a wise king is to act conscientiously and cautiously.
Therefore, we must consider decline when we are prosperous, and be aware of danger when we are peaceful and happy.
Therefore, although King Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou were in the highest position, they still maintained the virtue of seriousness and respect. During the ceremony, Yu Shun still observed and reflected on his shortcomings and mistakes.
That's the truth. Sima Xiangru had been dead for five years before the emperor began to worship the earth god.
Eight years after his death, the emperor finally offered sacrifices to Zhongyue Mountain first, then to Mount Tai, and then to Liangfu Mountain and Zen Suran Mountain.
Xiangru's other works, such as "The Book of the Marquis of Pingling", "The Dilemma with the Five Young Masters", and "The Book of Caomu" are not included, but his works that are particularly famous among public ministers are included.
Tai Shigong said: "Spring and Autumn" can delve into the most subtle aspects of things, "Book of Changes" is originally subtle but can be explained in a simple way, "Daya" talks about the virtues of princes and the common people, "Xiaoya" ridicules the gains and losses of humble authors, but its rumors can affect court politics.
Therefore, although the external manifestations of words are different, their gentle and enlightening effect is the same.
Although the similar articles contain many false words and exaggerated statements, their main theme is frugality. How is this different from the satirical remonstrance in the Book of Songs?
Yang Xiong believes that among Xiangru's gorgeous poems, there is a one hundred to one relationship between words that encourage luxury and words that advocate frugality. This is like playing the sounds of Zheng and Wei to your heart's content, but playing a little elegant music at the end of the piece.
Doesn’t this detract from the value of Xiangru’s words? I have collected some of his explanatory words and written them in this article.
summary: Sima Qian noted that Xiangru's works, though ornate, promoted frugality, akin to the "Book of Songs." Yang Xiong criticized their imbalance between luxury and admonition, but Sima Qian defended their value.

translation:
Sima Ranju is a descendant of Tian Wan.
During the period of Qi Jinggong, the Jin State sent troops to attack Qi State's Dong'a and Zhencheng, and the Yan State invaded Qi State's territory on the south bank of the Yellow River.
Qi's army was defeated.
Qi Jinggong was very worried about this. So Yan Ying recommended Tian Rangju to Qi Jinggong, saying: Although Rangju is the bastard of the Tian family, his literary talent can make everyone join him; his military strategy can make the enemy fear him. I hope the king can give him a try.
So Qi Jinggong summoned Rangju and discussed military and state affairs with him. After discussing with him, Qi Jinggong was very happy and immediately appointed him as a general and ordered him to lead troops to resist the armies of Yan and Jin.
Rangju said: "I am of a humble status. The king promoted me from the common people and placed me above the officials. The soldiers will not obey and the people will not trust me. If a person has little qualifications, authority cannot be established. I hope the king can send a minister who is favored by the king and respected by the people to supervise the army. That will be enough."
So Qi Jinggong agreed to his request and sent Zhuang Jia to supervise the army.
After Rang Ju bid farewell to Jinggong, she made an agreement with Zhuang Jia: "We will meet at the camp gate at noon tomorrow."
The next day, Rang Ju rushed to the military gate first and set up a wooden watch and a clepsydra to wait for Zhuang Jia.
However, Zhuang Jia has always been arrogant and dignified. He thinks that he is leading his own army and he is the supervisor of the army, so he is not particularly anxious. His relatives and friends bid farewell to him and invited him to drink wine.
It was already noon, but Zhuang Jia had not yet arrived.
Rangju knocked down the wooden watch, broke the clepsydra, entered the military camp, inspected the camp, organized the army, and issued various rules and orders.
By the time he finished his deployment, it was already dusk when Zhuang Jia arrived.
Rangju said: Why are you late even if you agree on the time?
Zhuang Jia apologized and explained: My friends and relatives sent me off, so I was delayed.
Rangju said: As a general, you should forget about your family from the moment you receive an order. When you come to the army and issue the prescribed orders, you should forget about personal friendships. When you beat the drum and march, you should forget about your own life when the battle is urgent.
Now that the enemy's invasion has penetrated deep into the country, there is unrest in the country, the soldiers have been exposed on the frontline battlefield, and there is no place to hide, the monarch has trouble sleeping and eating sweetly, and the lives of the people in the country are hanging on you, so why talk about farewell!
So he called the military judge and asked: According to military law, what is said about people who are late for the agreed time? The answer was: He should be beheaded.
Zhuang Jia was very frightened and sent Pegasus to report to Qi Jinggong and ask him to rescue him.
Not long after the messenger left, but before he could return, Zhuang Jia was beheaded and paraded in front of the three armies. The entire army was shocked and frightened.
After a long time, the envoy sent by Qi Jinggong came to pardon Zhuang Jia with the festival talisman. The carriages and horses galloped straight into the military camp.
Rangju said: "Generals are in the army, and they do not have to accept some of the king's orders."
He also asked the military judge: "What is the military law stipulating that driving a chariot and horse galloping in the military camp?" The military judge said: He should be beheaded.
The messenger was extremely frightened.
Rangju said: The king's envoy cannot be beheaded.
So he beheaded the servants of the messenger, cut off the wooden carriage on the left side, killed the horses driving the carriage on the left side, and paraded in front of the three armies.
He asked the envoy to go back and report to Qi Jinggong, and then set off.
summary: Sima Ranju, a descendant of Tian Wan, was recommended by Yan Ying to Qi Jinggong during a crisis when Jin and Yan attacked Qi. Despite his humble status, Ranju’s literary and military talents impressed the king, who appointed him general. Ranju requested a trusted minister, Zhuang Jia, to supervise the army. They agreed to meet at the camp gate at noon. Ranju arrived early and set up timing devices, but Zhuang Jia, delayed by farewell feasts, arrived at dusk. Ranju condemned his lateness, citing that a general must forsake family, friendships, and personal safety in war. He executed Zhuang Jia under military law, shocking the army.

translation:
The native soldiers set up camp, dug wells and set up stoves, drank water and ate food, inquired about diseases, and arranged medicine. Tian Rangju personally checked and cared for them.
He also used all the supplies and food he had as a general to entertain the soldiers. He and the soldiers shared the food equally.
Count up the weak and sick. Three days later, the army was reorganized and prepared for battle.
The sick and weak soldiers also asked to go to the battlefield together and competed to fight for him bravely.
When the Jin army learned of this situation, they withdrew their troops.
The Yan army knew about this situation and was dispersed as it retreated northward across the Yellow River. The Qi army took advantage of the situation to pursue them, regained all the fallen territory, and then led its troops in triumph.
Before reaching the capital, war preparations were lifted and wartime regulations and orders were cancelled. After swearing an alliance, they entered the capital.
Duke Jinggong of Qi led all the civil and military officials to greet him outside the city. After comforting the soldiers according to etiquette, he returned to the palace.
Duke Jinggong of Qi met Tian Ranju and appointed him as Grand Sima with great respect and admiration.
From then on, Tian's status in Qi State became more and more prominent day by day.
Later, the officials Bao, Gao and Guo were jealous of him and slandered and framed him in front of Qi Jinggong.
Qi Jinggong dismissed him from his official position, and Rangju died of illness soon after.
Tian Qi, Tian Bao and others therefore resented the people of the Gao and Guo families.
After that, when Tian Chang killed Duke Jian of Qi, he killed all the Gao and Guo families.
When Tian Chang's great-grandson Tian He arrived, he established himself as king and was named King Qi Wei. When he led his troops in battles and exercised his authority, he widely imitated Rang Ju's methods, and princes from all over the world came to Qi to pay homage.
King Wei of Qi sent officials to study and discuss the ancient "Sima's Art of War", and also included the great Sima Tian Ranju's art of war in it, so it was named "Sima Ranju's Art of War".
Tai Shigong said: When I read "The Art of War of Sima", I felt that it was grand, broad and far-reaching. Even the wars of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties failed to fully develop its connotations. It would be too much to recommend it if the text of "Sima Ranju's Art of War" is attached to it now.
As for Tian Ranju, he was just leading troops to fight for a small vassal state. How could it be compared with "Sima's Art of War"?
Since there are many "The Art of War of Sima" left in the world, I will not comment on them anymore and only write this "Biography of Sima Ranju".
summary: When Qi Jinggong’s envoy arrived with a pardon, racing into camp, Ranju declared that generals in the field need not accept all royal orders. He executed the envoy’s servants and horses, parading them before the troops. Ranju then personally cared for soldiers, sharing provisions and tending to the sick. After three days, the army was revitalized. The Jin and Yan forces withdrew upon learning of this discipline, and Qi reclaimed lost territory. Returning in triumph, Ranju was appointed Grand Sima by Qi Jinggong, elevating the Tian family’s status. However, officials Bao, Gao, and Guo slandered him, leading to his dismissal and death from illness. The Tian family later retaliated, killing the Gao and Guo clans. Tian He, a descendant, became King Qi Wei, who imitated Ranju’s methods and incorporated his strategies into the “Sima’s Art of War.” Sima Qian notes that while Ranju’s achievements were for a small state, the “Sima’s Art of War” is profound, and he refrains from further commentary, presenting only this biography.

translation:
Lu Buwei was a big businessman in Yangzhai. He traveled around, buying at low prices and selling at high prices, so he accumulated a fortune worth thousands of gold.
In the fortieth year of King Zhao of Qin, the prince passed away.
In the 42nd year of King Zhao, King Zhao established his second son An Guojun as the prince.
Lord An Guo had more than twenty sons.
Lord An Guo had a concubine whom he loved very much. He made her his wife and called her Mrs. Huayang.
Mrs. Huayang has no son.
An Guojun had a middle-ranking son named Zichu. Zichu's mother was named Xia Ji, who was not favored.
Zi Chu was sent to Zhao as a hostage as the son of Qin.
Qin State attacked Zhao State many times, and Zhao State did not treat Zi Chu politely.
Zichu was the grandson of the concubine of the King of Qin and was a hostage in the State of Zhao. He was not rich in carriages, horses and daily necessities, and his life was difficult and very unhappy.
Lu Buwei went to Handan to do business. After seeing Zi Chu, he felt very fond of him and said: Zi Chu is like a rare commodity that can be hoarded.
So he went to visit Zi Chu and persuaded him: I can expand your family.
Zi Chu smiled and said: "For now, let's expand your own family first, and then come and expand mine!"
Lu Buwei said: "You don't understand. My family has to wait for your family to grow before it can grow."
Zi Chu knew what Lu Buwei meant, so he sat him down together and had an in-depth conversation.
Lu Buwei said: The King of Qin is old, and Lord An Guo was made the crown prince.
I heard privately that Lord An Guo dotes on Mrs. Huayang very much. Mrs. Huayang has no son, so only Mrs. Huayang can choose the prince.
Now you have more than twenty brothers, and you are ranked in the middle. You are not favored by the King of Qin and have been left as a hostage in the vassal states for a long time. Even if the King of Qin dies and An Guojun succeeds to the throne, you should not expect to compete with your eldest brother and other brothers who are by the King of Qin's side sooner or later.
Zichu said: That's true, but what should we do?
Lu Buwei said: "You are very poor and embarrassed, and you are living here as a guest. You can't give anything to your relatives and make friends with the guests."
Although I, Lu Buwei, am not rich, I am willing to spend thousands of dollars to lobby for you to the west, serve Lord An Guo and Mrs. Huayang, and ask them to make you the crown prince.
Zichu then kowtowed and thanked him and said: If your plan comes true, I am willing to entrust the land of Qin to share it with you.
Lu Buwei then gave 500 gold to Zichu for daily life and making friends with guests. He also took 500 gold to buy rare things. He took these things with him and went west to the Qin State to lobby. He first paid a visit to Mrs. Huayang's sister and dedicated all the things he brought to Mrs. Huayang.
By the way, I mentioned that Zi Chu was smart and virtuous, and he made friends with princes and guests all over the world. He often said, "I, Zi Chu, regard my wife as the same as the sky. I cry day and night and miss the prince and his wife."
Madame was very happy.
Lu Buwei took the opportunity and asked Mrs. Huayang's sister to persuade Mrs. Huayang: "I heard that if you use your beauty to serve others, once your beauty fades, your favor will also decrease."
summary: Lu Buwei, a wealthy merchant from Yangzhai, amassed a fortune through low-cost buying and high-price selling. During the reign of King Zhao of Qin, the crown prince died, and An Guojun was appointed as the new prince. An Guojun had many sons, including Zichu, a middle-ranking son sent as a hostage to Zhao. Zichu, neglected and impoverished, caught Lu Buwei's attention. Lu Buwei saw him as a rare commodity to be hoarded and offered to help him gain power. Lu Buwei traveled to Qin to lobby An Guojun and his favored concubine, Mrs. Huayang, who had no son. He persuaded Mrs. Huayang to adopt Zichu as her heir, ensuring her future influence. An Guojun agreed, and Zichu became the designated heir. Lu Buwei gave Zichu funds and married him to a beautiful dancer, Zhao Ji, who bore a son, Ying Zheng.

translation:
Now, madam, you are serving the prince, and you are very favored, but you have no son. If you don't take advantage of this opportunity to make a capable and filial person among the prince's sons, make him his heir and treat him like your own son, then your husband will be respected when he is alive, and after his death, your son will succeed to the throne and he will not lose power in the end. This is what people say, and it will be beneficial for all generations.
Instead of laying the foundation when the appearance is beautiful, if you wait until the appearance fades and the favor is lost, even if you want to have a word with the prince, is it still possible?
Now that Zi Chu is capable, and he knows that he is in the middle, he cannot be appointed as heir according to the order, and his biological mother is not favored, so he will take the initiative to attach himself to Madam. If Madam can really promote him as heir at this time, Madam, you will be respected and favored in Qin all your life.
After hearing this, Mrs. Huayang thought it was so. While flattering the prince, she tactfully said that Zichu, who was a hostage in Zhao State, was very talented and everyone who came and went praised him.
Then he cried and said: I am lucky enough to be in the harem, but it is a pity that I have no son. I hope to make Zichu my heir so that I can have someone to rely on in the future.
An Guojun agreed, and he and his wife carved jade talismans and decided to make Zi Chu his heir. Both An Guojun and Mrs. Huayang gave many things to Zi Chu, and asked Lu Buwei to be his teacher. Therefore, Zi Chu's reputation among the princes grew.
Lu Buwei married the most beautiful woman from Handan who was good at singing and dancing. He lived with her and found out that she was pregnant.
Zi Chu once drank with Lu Buwei. After seeing the girl, he liked the girl very much, so he stood up and toasted to Lu Buwei, asking for the girl to be given to him.
Lu Buwei was very angry, but then he thought about it and realized that he had spent a lot of money on Zi Chu in order to catch rare goods, so he sacrificed this woman.
Zhao Ji concealed her pregnancy and gave birth to her son Mingzheng twelve months later.
Zi Chu made this concubine his wife.
In the fiftieth year of King Zhao of Qin, he sent Wang Jue to besiege Handan. The situation was very urgent and Zhao wanted to kill Zi Chu.
Zi Chu conspired with Lu Buwei and gave six hundred kilograms of gold to the officials guarding the city. They were able to escape and fled to the Qin army's camp before successfully returning to Qin.
The State of Zhao also wanted to kill Zi Chu's wife and son. Because Chu's wife was the daughter of a wealthy family in the State of Zhao, he was able to hide it, so the mother and son survived.
King Zhao of Qin passed away in the fifty-sixth year. Prince An Guojun succeeded to the throne as king, Mrs. Huayang became queen, and Zi Chu became prince.
The State of Zhao also escorted Zi Chu's wife and son Ying Zheng back to the State of Qin.
King Qin died a year after he succeeded to the throne, and his posthumous title was King Xiaowen.
Prince Chu succeeded to the throne, and he became King Zhuang Xiang.
King Zhuang Xiang honored his mother, Queen Huayang, as the Queen Mother of Huayang, and his biological mother Xia Ji was honored as the Queen Mother of Xia.
In the first year of King Zhuang Xiang's reign, Lu Buwei was appointed prime minister, granted the title of Marquis Wenxin, and made 100,000 households in Luoyang, Henan, his food town.
King Zhuang Xiang died three years after he ascended the throne. Prince Ying Zheng succeeded him as king, respected Lu Buwei as the prime minister, and called him "Zhongfu".
The King of Qin was still young, so the Queen Mother often had an affair with Lu Buwei. Lu Buwei's family has ten thousand servants.
At that time, there was Lord Xinling in Wei, Lord Chunshen in Chu, Lord Pingyuan in Zhao, and Lord Mengchang in Qi. They all treated virtuous officials and made friends with guests.
And we have to compete in this regard. Lu Buwei thought that the Qin State was so powerful that it was a shame to be inferior to them, so he also recruited literati and bachelors and gave them generous treatment. There were as many as 3,000 diners under his disciples.
At that time, there were many talented debaters in various princely states, like Xunqing, who wrote books and established theories that were popular in the world.
summary: During a siege of Handan, Zichu escaped to Qin with Lu Buwei's help. After King Zhao's death, An Guojun became king, and Zichu became prince. An Guojun died shortly after, and Zichu ascended as King Zhuang Xiang, appointing Lu Buwei as prime minister. King Zhuang Xiang died three years later, and Ying Zheng became king, with Lu Buwei as regent.

translation:
Lu Buwei ordered his diners to write down what they saw and heard, and combined them into eight readings, six treatises, and twelve disciplines, totaling more than 200,000 words.
I think it includes the history of heaven and earth and all things from ancient times to the present, so it is called "Lu's Spring and Autumn Annals".
He published it at the city gate of Xianyang, with a reward of one thousand gold hanging on it, and invited tourists and guests from all over the world. If anyone could add or delete a word, he would be rewarded with one thousand gold.
Qin Shihuang gradually grew up, but the Queen Mother continued to be promiscuous.
Lu Buwei was afraid that the matter would be exposed and disaster would befall him, so he secretly sought out a man with a large penis, Lao Ai, as a guest. He often indulged in sexual pleasures and asked Lao Ai to run his penis through a small wheel made of Paulownia wood to walk. He also tried to let the Queen Mother know about this and use it to seduce her.
After the Queen Mother heard about it, she really wanted to possess him secretly.
Lu Buwei offered him Lao Ai, pretending to have someone accuse him of committing a crime worthy of castration.
Lu Buwei secretly said to the Queen Mother: You can let Lao Ai pretend to be castrated, and you can get him among the people working in the palace.
The Queen Mother secretly gave many things to the officials who presided over the palace punishment, and pretended to punish Lao Ai. She plucked out his beard and pretended to be a eunuch, so that he could serve the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother secretly committed adultery with him and was especially fond of him.
Later, the Queen Mother was pregnant. She was worried that others would know about it and pretended to have bad fortune. She needed a change of environment to avoid it, so she moved to the palace in Yongdi.
Lao Ai always followed him around, and received very generous rewards. Lao Ai decided everything.
Lao Ai's family has thousands of servants. There were more than a thousand people who came to Lao Ai's family in order to obtain official positions.
In the seventh year of Qin Shi Huang's reign, King Zhuang Xiang's biological mother, the Queen Mother Xia, passed away.
Queen Xiaowen was called Queen Mother Huayang and was buried in Shouling together with King Xiaowen.
The Empress Dowager Xia's son, King Zhuang Xiang, was buried in Zhiyang, so the Empress Dowager Xia was buried separately to the east of Duyuan. She once said during her lifetime: You can see my son to the east, and my husband to the west.
In a hundred years, there will definitely be a city with ten thousand households nearby.
In the ninth year of Emperor Qin Shihuang's reign, someone reported that Lao Ai was not actually a eunuch. He often had fornications with the Queen Mother and gave birth to two sons. They hid them. He also conspired with the Queen Mother that if the King of Qin died, we would support our son to succeed him.
So Qin Shihuang ordered relevant officials to investigate the matter strictly and find out all the truth. The matter implicated Prime Minister Lu Buwei.
In September of that year, he killed all the three tribes of the Lao Ai family, killed the two sons born to the Queen Mother, and moved the Queen Mother to live in Yongdi.
The diners of Lao Ai's family had their property confiscated and moved to Shu.
The King of Qin wanted to kill the Prime Minister Lu Buwei, but because of his great service to the late king and the many guests and debaters who interceded and put in good words for him, the King of Qin could not bear to bring him to justice.
summary: Lu Buwei, competing with other lords, hosted 3,000 scholars and compiled the *Lüshi Chunqiu*, a comprehensive text. He later introduced Lao Ai, a man with a large penis, to the Queen Mother, who had an affair with him. Lao Ai gained power and fathered two sons with her. When discovered, Lao Ai rebelled but was executed. Lu Buwei was implicated, dismissed, and exiled. Fearing further persecution, he committed suicide by drinking poison.
