translation:
King Wu Liu Bi was the son of Liu Zhong, the brother of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
Seven years after Emperor Gaozu pacified the world, he named Liu Zhong the acting king.
Later, when the Xiongnu attacked Dai, Liu Zhong could not hold on, so he abandoned the country and fled. He took a small road to Luoyang and surrendered to the emperor.
Because the emperor was a brother of flesh and blood, he could not bear to be punished according to law, so he only deposed the king and demoted him to be the Marquis of Heyang.
In the autumn of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu, King Yingbu of Zhunnan rebelled, annexed the Jing territory to the east, hijacked the troops of the local princes, crossed the Huai River to the west, and attacked Chu State. Emperor Gaozu personally led the army to punish him.
Liu Zhong's son, Peihou Liu Bi, was twenty years old and strong. As a cavalry commander, he followed Gaozu and defeated Yingbu's army at Huizhen in the west of Qixian County. Yingbu fled.
King Liu Jia of Jing was killed by Yingbu and had no heirs.
The emperor was worried that the people in Wu and Kuaiji were frivolous and aggressive, and there was no brave king to restrain them. His sons were young, so he made Liu Bi the king of Wu in Pei, with jurisdiction over three counties and fifty-three counties.
After he had received his official seal, Emperor Gaozu asked Liu Bi to come and see him. After seeing him, he said: "You have a rebellious appearance."
At the same time, he felt regret in his heart, but he had already appointed him, so he patted him on the back and warned him: "There will be a rebellion in the southeast in the fifty years after the founding of the Han Dynasty. Is it you?"
However, everyone with the same surname is one family, so you must not rebel!
Liu Bi kowtowed and said, "I don't dare."
By the time of Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao, the world had just stabilized, and the princes of some counties were working hard to appease their own people.
Wu State owned the copper mines in Yuzhang County, so Liu Bi recruited desperadoes from all over the world to mint money privately and boil seawater to make salt. Because of this, the state did not levy taxes and the state expenses were very abundant.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, the Crown Prince of Wu came to Beijing for an audience and was able to accompany the Crown Prince to drink and play chess.
Prince Wu's teachers were both from Chu. They were frivolous, strong, and arrogant. When they were playing chess with the crown prince, they had an argument over the chess game and their attitude was disrespectful. The crown prince picked up the chessboard and threw the chessboard at Prince Wu, killing him. Afterwards, his body was sent back to Wu for burial.
When they arrived at the state of Wu, King Wu said angrily: If a family with the same surname in the world died in Chang'an, they should be buried in Chang'an. Why should they be sent to the state of Wu for burial?
The body was then sent to Chang'an for burial.
From then on, the King of Wu gradually disobeyed the etiquette that his vassals should abide by, claiming to be ill and refusing to enter the court.
The people in the capital knew that he claimed to be ill and refused to enter the court because his son had died. After questioning, he was indeed not ill. After that, when the envoys of the King of Wu came, they detained him, questioned him, and punished him.
The King of Wu was frightened and even more actively planned rebellion.
Later, the King of Wu sent someone to Beijing for the autumn invitation, and the emperor questioned the envoy again. The envoy told the emperor: The King of Wu is indeed not sick. The imperial court detained and punished several envoys, so he claimed that he was ill and could not come back.
summary: King Wu Liu Bi was the son of Liu Zhong, brother of Emperor Gaozu of Han. After Gaozu pacified the realm, he named Liu Zhong acting king, but Liu Zhong abandoned his post during a Xiongnu attack and was demoted to marquis. In the eleventh year of Gaozu, Yingbu rebelled, and Liu Bi, then twenty, served as a cavalry commander, helping defeat Yingbu. Gaozu, concerned about the unruly people of Wu and Kuaiji and lacking mature sons, appointed Liu Bi King of Wu over three counties. However, Gaozu noted Liu Bi's rebellious appearance and warned him against rebellion, which Liu Bi denied. During Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao's reigns, Wu prospered by minting coins from copper mines and making salt from seawater, avoiding taxes and attracting desperadoes. Under Emperor Xiaowen, a chess dispute led to the Crown Prince of Wu's death at the hands of the Han crown prince. The King of Wu, angered, buried his son in Chang'an and began feigning illness to avoid court, gradually disobeying etiquette. The court detained Wu envoys, prompting the King of Wu to plan rebellion. Emperor Xiaowen later pardoned Wu's envoys and granted the king leniency, easing tensions. However, Wu continued to harbor fugitives and control its people for over forty years.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传

translation:
So he sent envoys to join forces with the King of Qi, the King of Sichuan, the King of Jiaodong, the King of Jinan, and the King of Jibei. They all agreed and said: For the sake of justice, King Chengyang Jing will attack those surnamed Lu. Don't let him participate in the army. After the incident is completed, just give him some land.
The princes were shocked and frightened by the recent punishment of reducing their land, and most of them resented Chao Cuo.
When the documents to reduce the Wu Guoji and Yuzhang counties were sent to the state of Wu, the king of Wu first launched an army to rebel. On Bingwu of the first month, the king of Jiaoxi killed the officials sent by the court with less than 2,000 shi, as did the kings of Jiaodong, Sichuan, Jinan, Chu, and Zhao, so they marched westward.
King Qi later regretted it and committed suicide by taking poison, violating the covenant.
The King of Jibei's city wall was damaged and had not been repaired, so his lieutenant ordered him to be kidnapped and guarded so that he could not send troops.
The King of Jiaoxi was the leader, and together with the King of Jiaodong, the King of Sichuan and the King of Jinan, they led troops to besiege Linyi.
King Liu Sui of Zhao also rebelled and secretly sent envoys to the Xiongnu to discuss joint operations.
When the Seven Kingdoms launched a rebellion, the King of Wu conscripted all his soldiers and ordered the whole country: I am sixty-two years old and personally command the army.
The youngest son is fourteen years old and also leads the way.
Therefore, people who are the same age as me, and the same age as my youngest son at the lowest level, all have to go to war.
More than 200,000 people were conscripted.
He sent envoys to Minyue and Dongyue to the south, and Dongyue also sent troops to follow the king of Wu.
In the first month of the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, King Wu first set out from Guangling.
He crossed the Huaihe River to the west and joined the Chu army.
The letter sent by an envoy to the princes said: King Wu Liu Bi respectfully greets the king of Jiaoxi, King of Jiaodong, King of Suichuan, King of Jinan, King of Zhao, King of Chu, King of Huainan, King of Hengshan, King of Lujiang, and the son of the late King of Changsha: I hope to get your advice!
Because there are treacherous ministers in the court who have done nothing for the world, but they invade the land of the princes, send officials to impeach, arrest, interrogate and punish the princes, and only insult the princes. They do not treat the Liu family's relatives with the etiquette of princes and kings. They ignore the meritorious officials of the late emperor, promote and appoint bad people, confuse the world, and want to harm the country.
Your Majesty is frail, sick and mentally disturbed, and cannot clearly understand the political situation.
I want to raise an army to punish them, and I respectfully follow your advice.
Although our country is small, the land is only three thousand miles in radius; although the population is small, we can prepare 500,000 elite soldiers.
I have been serving South Vietnam for more than thirty years, and their monarchs have not refused to recruit and assign soldiers to follow me into the army, and I can get more than three hundred thousand people.
Although I am not talented, I am willing to follow all the princes personally.
Yue is bordering Changsha. They can follow the son of the King of Changsha to pacify the north of Changsha, and then attack Shu and Hanzhong westward.
I sent people to tell the King of Dongyue, the King of Chu, and the King of Huainan to attack westward with me. After the kings of Qi and King Zhao pacified Hejian and Hanoi, some of them entered Linjin Pass and some joined me in Luoyang. King Yan and King Zhao originally had an alliance with the Xiongnu.
summary: Chao Cuo, favored by Emperor Jing, repeatedly urged reducing Wu's territory, arguing that rebellion was inevitable. In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Chao Cuo reduced the lands of Chu, Zhao, Jiaoxi, and Wu. King Wu Liu Bi, fearing further losses, plotted rebellion. He sent Ying Gao to recruit King Jiaoxi, citing Chao Cuo's tyranny and promising joint action. King Jiaoxi agreed, and alliances formed with Qi, Sichuan, Jiaodong, Jinan, and Jibei. The Seven Kingdoms rebelled, with Wu conscripting over 200,000 men and gaining support from Dongyue. King Wu issued a letter to the princes, denouncing Chao Cuo and calling for a punitive campaign, offering rewards for capturing Han officials.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传

translation:
Zhou Qiu was from Xiapi and fled to Wu. He liked drinking and had bad conduct. King Liu Bi of Wu despised him and did not appoint him.
Zhou Qiu paid homage to King Wu and said to him: Because I have no talent, I cannot serve in the army.
I dare not ask to lead the army. I hope that if you get a Han Dynasty talisman from your Majesty, I will be able to repay you.
The king of Wu gave him the talisman.
Zhou Qiu got the talisman and drove into Xiapi overnight.
When Xiapi heard that King Wu had rebelled, they all defended the city.
Zhou Qiu arrived at the guest house and summoned the magistrate of Xiapi County.
The county magistrate walked in and asked his entourage to kill him on the pretext of the crime.
Then he summoned the wealthy officials who were friends with his brothers and told them: King Wu's rebel army is coming. After arriving, the people in Shajinpi City will only have time to eat.
If you surrender now, your family will be saved, and talented people will be granted the title of marquis.
After these people went out, they told each other that all the people in Xiapi surrendered.
Zhou Qiu got 30,000 men in one night, sent someone to report to the king of Wu, and led his army to the north to capture the city.
By the time they reached Chengyang, the army had grown to more than 100,000 people and they defeated Lieutenant Chengyang's army.
Later, when he heard that King Wu was defeated and fled, he thought that no one would be able to achieve success with him, so he led the army back to Xiapi.
Before arriving, he died of a sore attack on his back.
In mid-February, King Wu's army was defeated and fled, so the emperor issued an order to the generals: I heard that those who do good will be rewarded with blessings by God; those who do evil will be rewarded with disaster.
Emperor Gaozu personally commended his merits and granted titles to princes. The titles of King You and King Mouhui were cut off. Emperor Xiaowen took pity on them and gave them special favors. He named Sui, the son of King You, and Yan, the son of King Mouhui, as kings. They allowed them to worship their ancestors in their ancestral temples and became vassal states of the Han Dynasty. Their kindness matched that of heaven and earth, and their light was as bright as the sun and moon.
King Wu Liu Bi violated kindness and morality, seduced the world's fugitive sinners, disturbed the world's coins, and refused to attend court in Beijing for more than 20 years, claiming to be ill. The ministers in charge petitioned many times to punish Liu Bi for his crimes. Emperor Xiaowen forgave him and hoped that he could change his ways and become a good person.
Now he actually made a covenant with King Liu Wu of Chu, King Liu Sui of Zhao, King Liu Xian of Jiaoxi, King Liu Piguang of Jinan, King Liu Xian of Sichuan, and King Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong, and committed rebellious and immoral acts. He sent troops to endanger the ancestral temple, massacred ministers and envoys of the Han Dynasty, coerced tens of millions of people, killed innocent people indiscriminately, burned down civilian houses, dug graves, and was extremely cruel.
Now Liu Xun, the king of Jiaoxi, and others are even more rebellious and unruly, burning down the ancestral temple and plundering the royal utensils in the ancestral temple. I hate them very much.
I wore white clothes and avoided the main hall. The generals wanted to encourage the scholar-bureaucrats to attack the rebels.
When attacking a rebel enemy, it is meritorious to go deep into the enemy's army and kill as many enemies as possible. The captured officials must be killed if their salary is more than 300 dan and do not release them.
Anyone who dares to discuss the imperial edict or do not act in accordance with the edict will be punished by being cut in half.
summary: Emperor Jing responded by sending Zhou Yafu to attack Wu and Chu, and other generals against Qi and Zhao. Yuan An advised killing Chao Cuo to appease the rebels, and Chao Cuo was executed. Yuan An then attempted to negotiate with Wu, but King Wu refused, declaring himself the Eastern Emperor. Zhou Yafu, following a strategy to avoid direct confrontation, cut off Wu's food supplies. Wu's army, led by King Wu, failed to adopt effective strategies, such as a surprise attack on Wuguan or a swift march to Luoyang. After a prolonged siege of Liang, Wu's forces starved and scattered. King Wu fled to Dongyue but was assassinated by Dongyue forces bribed by Han. Other rebel kings, including those of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Sichuan, Jinan, and Zhao, were defeated or committed suicide, and their states were abolished.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/吴王濞列传

translation:
The King of Jiaoxi knelt down and replied: At that time, Chao Cuo was the emperor's minister. He changed the laws of Emperor Gaozu and usurped the land of the princes.
We thought this was unjust and worried that he would bring chaos to the world, so the seven kingdoms sent troops to kill Chao Cuo.
Now that we heard that Chao Cuo had been killed, we withdrew our troops and returned.
The general said: If your Majesty thinks Chao Cuo is not good, why don't you report it to the emperor?
Without getting the emperor's edict, he sent troops to attack the righteous princes who abided by the king's law.
From this point of view, your original intention is not to kill Chao Cuo.
He took out the edict and read it to him.
After reading it, he said: Your Majesty, please think about what you should do!
King Jiaoxi said: People like me deserve to die.
Just committed suicide.
The Queen Mother and the Prince also died.
King Jiaodong, King Sichuan, and King Jinan also died successively, and the feudal state was abolished and returned to the Han Dynasty.
General Li besieged the capital of Zhao for ten months before conquering it, and King Zhao committed suicide.
Because the King of Jibei was kidnapped, he was not executed and was moved to the title of King of Sichuan.
At the beginning, Wu King Liu Bi took the lead in the rebellion and led the Chu and Wu armies together, uniting the armies of Qi and Zhao.
In the first month of the year, the army started a rebellion, and in March the whole army was defeated. Only Zhao State was finally conquered.
Emperor Jing also named Pingluhou Liu Li, the youngest son of King Chu Yuan, as King of Chu, as the successor of King Chu Yuan.
Liu Fei, the king of Runan who moved to Wu, took over the original fiefdom of Wu and became the king of Jiangdu.
Tai Shigong said: King Wu Liu Bi was granted the title of King of Wu because his father was demoted.
The King of Wu was able to exempt taxes and support the people because he had the convenience of copper mines and sea salt.
The idea of ​​​​rebellion came from the death of his son.
He got into trouble because of a chess dispute, and eventually his country was destroyed and he died; he got close to the foreign Yue people and murdered his fellow clan, and finally he died.
Chao Cuo made great plans for the country, but disaster befell him instead.
Yuan An was good at contingency lobbying. He was favored at first, but suffered humiliation in the end.
Therefore, in ancient times, the land of the princes did not exceed a hundred miles, and the mountains and seas were not divided among the princes. If you don't get close to the Yi and Di, you will alienate your clan members. This was probably what you said to the King of Wu, right? Those who don't make plans will be punished. Isn't that what Yuan Ang and Chao Cuo said?
summary: The rebellion lasted from January to March, with Zhao falling later. Emperor Jing reinstated some royal lines and granted Wu's territory to others. The historian concludes that Liu Bi's rebellion stemmed from his son's death and greed, while Chao Cuo's plans led to his own death, and Yuan Ang's strategies brought initial favor but eventual disgrace.

translation:
Lord Shang was the son of the concubine Ji of the Kingdom of Wei. His name is Yang Yang and his surname is Gongsun. His ancestor’s original surname was Ji.
When he was young, Gongsun Yang was interested in the study of criminal names and magic. He served his uncle, the Prime Minister of Wei State, and served as the middle concubine.
The uncle knew that he was a virtuous man, but he had not yet had time to recommend him to the king of Wei.
Just when the uncle was sick, King Wei Hui went to visit him personally and said, "What will happen to the country if something unexpected happens to your illness?"
The uncle replied: My bastard son Gongsun Yang is young, but he is talented. I hope that the king can hand over all the affairs of the country to him and let him govern.
King Wei Hui was silent after hearing this.
When King Hui of Wei was about to leave, the uncle withdrew his entourage and said: If the king does not use Gongsun Yang, he must be killed and not allowed to leave the country.
King Wei agreed to his request and left.
The uncle summoned Gongsun Yang and apologized: Just now, the king asked about people who could serve as prime minister, and I recommended you. Judging from the look on his face, the king will not agree with my suggestion.
I must first be loyal to the king and then consider the position of the minister, so I advise the king that if Gongsun Martingale is not appointed, he should be killed.
The king agreed to my request.
You should leave quickly, otherwise you will be captured soon.
Gongsun Yang said: Since the king cannot listen to you and appoint me, how can he listen to you and kill me?
In the end, he did not leave Wei State.
After King Hui left, he said to his attendants: "The uncle's illness is very serious, which is really sad. He wants me to hand over all the affairs of the country to Gongsun Yang, and after that, he persuades me to kill him. Isn't this very confusing?"
Shortly after Gongshu Zuo's death, Gongsun Yang heard that Duke Xiao of Qin ordered to search for talented people throughout the country in order to restore the hegemony of Duke Mu of Qin and regain the lost territory in the east. He went west to enter the Qin State and relied on Duke Xiao's favored minister Jing Jian to seek an audience with Duke Xiao.
Duke Xiao summoned Wei Yang and asked him to talk about state affairs for a long time. Duke Xiao fell asleep while listening and couldn't listen at all.
Afterwards, Duke Xiao was angry with Jingjian and said: "Your guest is a bully. How can you appoint such a person?"
Jing Jian again used Xiao Gong's words to blame Wei Yang.
Wei Yang said: I used the methods of Yao and Shun to persuade the king, but his mind could not understand.
A few days later, Jing Jian asked Duke Xiao to summon Wei Yang.
When Wei Yang met with Duke Xiao, he explained the way of governing the country incisively and vividly, but it was not in line with Duke Xiao's wishes.
Afterwards, Duke Xiao blamed Jing Jian again, and Jing Jian also blamed Wei Yang.
Wei Yang said: I used the methods of Yu, Tang, Wen and Wu to persuade the king, but he would not listen.
Ask him to summon me again.
Wei Yang met Duke Xiao again. Duke Xiao was very friendly to him, but he did not use him.
After exiting the meeting, Xiaogong said to Jingjian: Your guest is good. I can talk to him.
Jing Jian told Wei Yang, and Wei Yang said: I used the Five Hegemons' methods of governing the country to convince the king, and I saw that he was ready to adopt it.
If you summon me again, I'll know what to say.
So Wei Yang met Duke Xiao again, and Duke Xiao had a very good conversation with him. He unknowingly moved his knees forward on the mat, and they talked for several days without feeling tired.
Jing Jian said: How can you win over the king? Our king is very happy.
Wei Yang replied: I advised the king to adopt the imperial method of governing the country and establish a prosperous age like Xia, Shang and Zhou. However, the king said: The time is too long, I can't wait, let alone a wise king. Who doesn't want to be famous when he is in power? How can I be asked to wait in obscurity for decades or hundreds of years to achieve the great cause of becoming an emperor?
Therefore, I used the method of enriching the country and strengthening the army to persuade him, and he was very happy.
However, this cannot be compared with the virtues of Yin and Zhou.
Shortly after Qin Xiaogong appointed Wei Yang, he planned to change the laws, but he was also worried that people in the world would talk about him.
Wei Yang said: If you hesitate in action, you will not become famous; if you hesitate in doing things, you will not succeed.
summary: Lord Shang, originally named Gongsun Yang, was the son of a concubine of the Kingdom of Wei. As a youth, he studied criminal law and magic, serving under his uncle, the Prime Minister of Wei. When his uncle fell ill, King Wei Hui visited and asked about a successor. The uncle recommended Gongsun Yang, but the king remained silent. The uncle then privately advised the king to kill Gongsun Yang if he was not appointed, to prevent him from leaving the country. However, Gongsun Yang refused to flee, reasoning that the king would not heed advice to kill him if he ignored advice to appoint him. After his uncle's death, Gongsun Yang heard that Duke Xiao of Qin sought talented individuals to restore Qin's former glory. He entered Qin through the recommendation of Duke Xiao's favored minister, Jing Jian. Initially, Duke Xiao was unimpressed, falling asleep during discussions of ancient imperial methods. After several attempts, Gongsun Yang shifted to strategies for enriching the state and strengthening the army, which pleased Duke Xiao. Despite concerns about public opinion, Gongsun Yang convinced Duke Xiao to enact legal reforms, arguing that extraordinary actions often face criticism but are necessary for success. He was appointed as Zuo Shu Chang and implemented a new legal code, organizing households into mutual surveillance groups, rewarding military merit, punishing private disputes, and promoting agriculture. To build trust, he erected a log at the market and rewarded a man who moved it, demonstrating his commitment to the law.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/商君列传

translation:
The new law was ready but had not yet been announced. Worried that the people would not believe it, Wei Yang erected a three-foot-long log at the south gate of the market behind the capital, and recruited people who could move the log to the north gate and rewarded them with ten gold coins.
The people thought this was strange and no one dared to touch it.
He also announced that anyone who could move the wood to the north gate would be rewarded fifty gold.
A man moved it away and immediately gave him fifty gold to show that he would do what he ordered and would never cheat.
New laws were enacted afterwards.
The new law was implemented among the people for a whole year. Thousands of people from Qin State came to the country and said that the new law was not suitable.
At this time, the prince violated the new law.
Wei Yang said: The new law cannot be implemented smoothly because the people at the top violate it.
The prince will be punished according to the new law.
The prince was the heir to the monarch and could not impose punishment, so he punished Gongzi Qian, the teacher who supervised his behavior, and Gongsun Jia, the teacher who imparted knowledge to him, with ink punishment.
The next day, all the people of Qin implemented the new law.
Ten years after the new law was implemented, the people of Qin were very happy. No one picked up other people's lost things on the road, there were no thieves in the mountains and forests, and every family was rich and sufficient.
The people have the courage to fight for the country and dare not fight for personal gain. There is order in the villages and towns.
The people of Qin who initially said that the new law was not suitable also said that the law was suitable. Wei Yang said: "These are the people who disturb the enlightenment, so he moved them all to the border areas."
After that, no one among the people dared to discuss the new law.
So Wei Yang was appointed as Daliang Zao.
He led the army to besiege Anyi of Wei State and forced them to surrender.
Three years later, the Qin State built a palace city in Xianyang and moved the capital from Yongdi to Xianyang.
It was ordered that fathers, sons, and brothers of the common people were not allowed to live in the same room.
Sporadic towns and villages were merged into counties, and county magistrates and county magistrates were set up. A total of thirty-one counties were merged and divided.
Abolish well fields and redraw the boundaries of farmland, encourage the reclamation of wasteland, and balance taxes.
Unify the national weights and measures system.
After four years of implementation, Gongzi Qian violated the new law again and was sentenced to death.
Five years later, when the Qin state became prosperous and powerful, the Emperor of Zhou gave the sacrificial meat to Duke Xiao of Qin, and princes from all over the world came to congratulate him.
The next year, Qi's army defeated Wei's army in Maling, captured Wei's crown prince Shen, and killed general Pang Juan.
Another year later, Wei Yang persuaded Qin Xiaogong: The relationship between Qin and Wei is like a person suffering from a heart disease. Either Wei annexes Qin, or Qin annexes Wei.
Why do you say that?
The Wei State was located to the west of the high mountains, with its capital in Anyi. The Yellow River was the boundary with the Qin State and it monopolized the geographical advantage east of Mount Wei.
When the situation is favorable, they will invade the Qin State to the west, and when the situation is unfavorable, they will expand their territory eastward.
Now, with the help of the king's virtuous and sage wisdom, Qin is prosperous.
The Wei State was severely defeated by Qi last year, and the princes betrayed it one after another. They can take this opportunity to attack Wei State.
Wei cannot resist Qin and will definitely retreat eastward.
summary: The new law faced opposition, including from the crown prince. Gongsun Yang punished the prince's tutors, Qian and Gongsun Jia, with facial tattooing, after which the law was widely accepted. Over ten years, Qin prospered: lost items were not stolen, families became wealthy, and the people were courageous in public duty but avoided private conflicts. Gongsun Yang was promoted to Da Liang Zao and led campaigns against Wei, capturing Anyi. He later oversaw the construction of Xianyang, reorganized territories into counties, abolished well-fields, and standardized weights and measures.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/商君列传

translation:
Once it retreats to the east, Qin will occupy the dangerous terrain of the Yellow River and Huashan Mountain, and can control the princes and countries to the east. This is the great cause of the emperor to unify the world.
Qin Xiaogong thought it was right and sent Wei Yang to lead an army to attack Wei.
The state of Wei sent its son Yan to lead troops to attack the Qin army.
When the two armies met and confronted each other, Wei Yang sent someone to send a letter to the general of the Wei army, Gongzi Yan, writing: I had a good relationship with the young master at the beginning, but now you and I are generals of two hostile countries and cannot bear to attack each other. Can we meet the young master in person, conclude an alliance, have a few drinks, and then withdraw our troops, so that both Qin and Wei will be in peace.
Wei Gongzi Yan thought that Wei Yang was right.
The two made an alliance, and then held a banquet and drank wine. However, the armored warriors who had been ambushed by Wei Yang suddenly attacked and captured Wei Gongzi Yan. They took the opportunity to attack his army, completely defeated the Wei army, and escorted Gongzi Yan back to the country.
King Wei Hui's army was defeated by Qi and Qin many times, leaving the country empty. Wei was getting weaker day by day. King Wei Hui was very panicked, so he sent envoys to cede the Hexi region to Qin in order to seek reconciliation.
Wei then evacuated Anyi and moved its capital to Daliang.
King Wei Hui said: I really regret not taking the advice of Gongshu Zuo.
After Wei Yang returned from defeating the Wei army, Qin Xiaogong granted him fifteen cities in the Yu and Shang areas, with the title Lord Shang.
Lord Shang served as Prime Minister of Qin for ten years, and many princes and nobles resented him.
Zhao Liang went to see Shang Jun.
Shang Jun said: I can see you because of Meng Langao's introduction. Now I ask to make friends with you, is that okay?
Zhao Liang replied: I don't dare to hope.
Confucius said: Recommend the virtuous and those who are supported by the people will come; gather the unworthy, and even those who can become kings will retreat.
I am not talented, so I dare not obey my orders.
I have heard this saying: Holding a position you shouldn't have is called position greed, and enjoying a reputation you shouldn't have is called fame greed.
If I accept your friendship, I am afraid that I am greedy for both position and fame.
So I dare not obey my orders.
Shang Yang said: Are you unhappy with how I govern Qin?
Zhao Liang said: Being able to listen to other people's opinions is called cleverness, being able to self-examine is called Ming, and being able to restrain oneself is called strong.
Yu Shun once said: People who are humble are respected by others.
You might as well follow Yu Shun's advice without asking me.
Shang Yang said: At the beginning, the customs of Qin were the same as those of Rong and Di. Father and son were not separated, and men, women, old and young lived in the same room.
Now I have changed the culture of Qin, made them separate men and women, and made them live separately. I built a large palace and city, and made Qin look like Lu and Wei.
Do you think I am more capable in governing the state of Qin than Dr. Wuxi?
Zhao Liang said: A thousand sheepskins are not as valuable as a fox armpit, and a thousand people who follow the advice are not as valuable as one person who speaks out.
King Wu allowed his ministers to express their opinions frankly, and the country prospered. King Zhou did not like his ministers to give advice, so he perished.
If you don't object to King Wu of Zhou's actions, then please allow me to speak frankly in my poem without being blamed, okay?
Shang Jun said: As the saying goes, words that appear pleasant are like flowers, words that are true and sincere are like fruits, words that are bitter and unpleasant to the ear are good medicine for curing diseases, and words that are flattering are diseases.
summary: After further victories, Gongsun Yang persuaded Duke Xiao to attack Wei, exploiting Wei's recent defeat by Qi. He tricked Wei's general, Gongzi Yan, into a meeting, captured him, and defeated the Wei army. King Wei Hui ceded land and regretted not heeding the uncle's advice. Gongsun Yang was granted fifteen cities and titled Lord Shang. As prime minister for ten years, he faced resentment from nobles. Zhao Liang warned him of his dangerous position, criticizing his reliance on harsh methods and lack of virtue, but Lord Shang ignored the advice.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/商君列传

translation:
Then why not return Shang's fiefdom of fifteen cities to the State of Qin, go to remote and desolate places to water gardens and cultivate their own land, and persuade the King of Qin to reuse those talents who live in seclusion in the mountains and forests to support the elderly and raise orphans, so that father and brother can respect each other, rank according to merit, and respect virtuous people. Only in this way can peace be guaranteed.
You also want to covet Shang Yu's wealth, take monopolizing the political and religious affairs of Qin as an honor and favor, and arouse the resentment of the people. Once the king of Qin abandons his guests and cannot be in power, how many people will Qin want to arrest you?
The day of your death will come as quickly as you lift your feet.
But Shang Jun did not follow Zhao Liang's advice.
Five months later, Qin Xiaogong died and the prince ascended the throne.
Gongzi Qian and his gang reported that Shang Jun wanted to rebel, and the monarch sent people to arrest Shang Jun.
Shang Jun fled to the border crossing and wanted to stay in a hotel.
The owner of the inn did not know that he was Lord Shang, and said: Lord Shang has an order, and the owner of the hotel will jointly and severally sentence the people staying in the hotel without documents.
Shang Jun sighed longly and said: Alas! The legacy of enacting new laws has reached such an extent!
He left Qin and fled to Wei.
The people of Wei resented him for deceiving the young master Yan and defeating the Wei army, and refused to take him in.
Shang Jun plans to go to other countries.
The people of Wei said: Lord Shang is a fugitive from Qin. Qin is powerful, but its fugitive comes to Wei. It is impossible not to return him.
So he sent Lord Shang back to Qin.
After Lord Shang returned to Qin, he fled to his fiefdom of Shang. He and his subordinates mobilized the soldiers in the city to attack Zheng in the north to seek a way out. Qin sent troops to attack Lord Shang and killed him in Lingchi of Zheng.
King Hui of Qin divided Shang Jun into five pieces and showed it to the public, saying: Don't rebel like Shang Yang!
So he killed the whole clan of Lord Shang.
Tai Shigong said: Mr. Shang is a cruel and merciless person by nature. It should be considered that when he used the way of an emperor to persuade Duke Xiao, he relied on pretentious talk and it was not his own qualifications.
Besides, relying on the recommendation of the king's favorite minister Jing Jian, when he was appointed, he punished the prince Qian, deceived the Wei general, the prince Xian, and refused to listen to Zhao Liang's advice, which is enough to prove that Lord Shang was cruel and ungrateful.
I once read a book about Shang Jun's Kasai farming campaign, and the content is similar to his own actions.
But in the end, he got a bad reputation in Qin State for treason. There is a reason for this!
summary: Five months after Duke Xiao's death, the new prince ascended. Gongzi Qian accused Lord Shang of rebellion. Lord Shang fled but was turned away by innkeepers due to his own laws requiring identification. He escaped to Wei, but the Wei people, angry over his deception, returned him to Qin. He attempted to raise troops in his fiefdom but was captured and executed by dismemberment. His entire clan was killed. Sima Qian concluded that Lord Shang's cruel and ungrateful nature, reliance on deceit, and refusal to heed wise counsel led to his downfall.

translation:
Dawan was discovered by Zhang Qian.
Zhang Qian was from Hanzhong and served as a Langguan during the Jianyuan reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
At this time, the emperor asked the surrendered Huns. They all said that the Huns attacked and defeated King Yuezhi and used his skull as a drinking vessel. The Yuezhi fled and often resented the Huns, but they had no friends to fight with them.
At this time, the Han Dynasty was about to attack the Xiongnu. After hearing these statements, it wanted to send an envoy to Yuezhi to contact them.
But to go to Yuezhi, you have to pass through the Xiongnu, so you recruited people who could be sent as envoys.
Zhang Qian responded to the call as a Langguan and was sent as an envoy to the Yuezhi. He left Longxi with a former Huns slave named Ganfu from Tangyi. When passing by the Huns, he was captured by the Huns and handed over to the Chanyu.
The Chanyu retained Zhang Qian and said, "The Yueshi are to the north of us. How can the Han Dynasty send envoys there?"
If we want to send an envoy to South Vietnam, will the Han Dynasty allow us?
He detained Zhang Qian for more than ten years, married him, and gave birth to children. However, Zhang Qian kept the talisman of the Han Dynasty envoy and did not lose it.
Zhang Qian stayed with the Xiongnu, and the Xiongnu's care for him gradually relaxed. As a result, Zhang Qian and his followers fled to the Yueshi, and ran westward for dozens of days until they arrived in Dawan.
Dawan heard that the Han Dynasty was rich in money and wanted to communicate with the Han Dynasty, but failed. Now that I saw Zhang Qian, I felt happy and asked Zhang Qian: "Where do you want to go?"
Zhang Qian said: I sent an envoy to the Yuezhi for the Han Dynasty, but the Huns blocked my way.
Now that we have escaped from the Huns, I hope the king will send someone to guide and escort us to Yuezhi.
If we can really reach Yuezhi, we can return to the Han Dynasty. The wealth that the Han Dynasty presented to the king cannot be described in words.
Dawan believed that Zhang Qian's words were true, so he asked Zhang Qian to set off and sent him a guide and translator to reach Kangju. Kangju transferred him to Dayuezhi again.
At this time, the king of Dayuezhi had been killed by the Xiongnu, and his prince was appointed king.
This king had conquered Bactria and settled here. The land here is fertile and fertile, and there are few enemies to invade it, so the mood is comfortable and happy. I also thought that I was far away from the Han Dynasty and had no intention of revenge against the Huns.
Zhang Qian arrived in Daxia from the Yueshi, but after all he did not get the clear attitude of the Yueshi towards uniting the Han to attack the Huns.
Zhang Qian lived in Yueshi for more than a year and returned home. He traveled along the Nanshan Mountains and wanted to return to Chang'an from where the Qiang people lived, but he was captured by the Huns again.
He lived with the Xiongnu for more than a year. When the Chanyu died, King Zuoguli of the Xiongnu attacked the prince and proclaimed himself the Chanyu. The country was in chaos. Zhang Qian took the opportunity to escape back to the Han Dynasty with his Hu wife and Tangyi father.
In the Han Dynasty, Zhang Qian was granted the title of Taizhong Dafu, and Tang Yifu was granted the title of Envoy Lord.
Zhang Qian was strong, powerful, broad-minded, honest and trustworthy, and all the barbarians liked him.
Tangyi's father was a Huns and was good at archery. Whenever he was in poverty and danger, he would shoot birds and animals for food.
Initially, Zhang Qian had more than a hundred followers when he was sent as an envoy. Thirteen years after leaving the Han Dynasty, only he and Gan Fu returned to the Han Dynasty.
Zhang Qian visited Dayuan, Dayuezhi, Daxia, and Kangju. Legend has it that there were five or six big countries next to these countries. He stated the situation to the Emperor of Han one by one, saying: Dayuan is southwest of the Xiongnu, due west of the Han Dynasty, about 10,000 miles away from the Han Dynasty.
summary: Zhang Qian, a Langguan from Hanzhong during the Jianyuan reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, discovered Dawan. The emperor, learning from surrendered Xiongnu that the Yuezhi had been defeated by the Xiongnu and sought allies, recruited envoys to contact the Yuezhi. Zhang Qian responded, leaving Longxi with Ganfu, a former Xiongnu slave. Captured by the Xiongnu, he was detained for over ten years, married, and had children, but kept his envoy's talisman. Eventually, he escaped westward to Dawan. Dawan, eager to connect with the wealthy Han Dynasty, welcomed Zhang Qian and provided guides to Kangju, then to Dayuezhi. The Yuezhi king, having conquered Bactria, was content and unwilling to attack the Xiongnu. After over a year, Zhang Qian returned via the Nanshan Mountains but was recaptured by the Xiongnu. He escaped during internal Xiongnu chaos, returning to the Han Dynasty with his Hu wife and Ganfu. He was granted the title Taizhong Dafu.

translation:
Their custom is to settle in one place, cultivate the fields, grow rice and wheat, and produce wine.
Its towns are like Dawan.
It has hundreds of towns and cities under its jurisdiction and a land area of ​​thousands of miles. It is the largest country.
There is a market near Guishui, and people use cars and ships to transport goods for business, sometimes to nearby countries or places thousands of miles away.
They used silver to make coins, and the coins were minted to resemble the king's appearance. When the king died, they changed the coins because they wanted to imitate the king's appearance.
They drew horizontal lines on the leather as text.
To the west is Tiaozhi, to the north are Yancai and Lixuan.
The branches are thousands of miles west of Parthia, near the Western Sea.
The weather there is hot and humid.
People tilled the fields and grew rice.
There arose a great bird whose eggs were as big as an urn.
With a large population, some places often had small princes, and Parthian servants governed them.
Think of it as a peripheral country.
The people of Tiaozhi are good at magic. The old people in Anxi said that there was Weushui and Queen Mother of the West in Tiaozhi State, but they had never seen them.
Daxia is located south of the Guishui River, more than 2,000 miles southwest of Dawan.
The local custom is that people settle in one place, with towns and houses. The custom is the same as that of Dawan.
There is no grand governor, instead each town has a small governor.
The country's military is weak and afraid of war.
People are good at doing business.
When the Da Yuezhi moved westward, they defeated Da Xia and ruled the entire Da Xia.
There are many people in Daxia, about one million.
Its capital is called Lanshi City. There is a trade market here. Sells various items.
There is a poisonous country in the southeast of Daxia.
Zhang Qian said: When I was in Daxia, I saw Qiong bamboo sticks and Shu cloth, so I asked them: Where did they get these things?
People from the Daxia Kingdom said: Our merchants bought it from the Shendu Kingdom.
Shendu Country is about several thousand miles southeast of Daxia.
The custom there is for people to settle in one place, which is roughly the same as in Daxia, but the terrain is low and humid and the weather is hot.
Its people fought on elephants.
It is near a flood.
I estimate that Daxia is twelve thousand miles away from the Han Dynasty and is in the southwest of the Han Dynasty.
Shendu Country is located thousands of miles southeast of Daxia and has products from Shu County, which means that it is not far from Shu County.
Nowadays, if an envoy is sent to Daxia, if he passes through the Qiang residential area, the terrain is dangerous and the Qiang people hate it; if he goes slightly north, he will be captured by the Huns. The road from Shu should be straight and free from intruders.
The emperor has heard that Dawan, Daxia, Anxi, etc. are all big countries that produce many strange things. The people live in one place and their lives are quite similar to those of the Han Dynasty. However, their armies are weak and they value the property of the Han Dynasty. There are countries such as Dayuezhi and Kangju in the north. Their armies are powerful, but you can use gifts and benefits to induce them to come to pay homage to the Emperor of Han.
And if we can really get them and make them our own with morality, then we can expand the territory of thousands of miles, and through many translations, attract people with different customs, so that the prestige and kindness of the emperor of the Han Dynasty can be spread all over the world.
summary: Zhang Qian reported on Dawan and neighboring states: Dawan, southwest of the Xiongnu, had settled agriculture, wine, and fine horses. It had over 70 towns and hundreds of thousands of people. Kangju, a nomadic state with 80,000-90,000 warriors, served the Yuezhi and Xiongnu. Dayuezhi, west of Dawan, was nomadic with 100,000-200,000 warriors, having defeated Daxia. Anxi, a large settled state with towns and trade, used silver coins. Tiaozhi, near the Western Sea, was hot and humid. Daxia, south of the Guishui River, had weak military but strong commerce, ruled by the Yuezhi.

translation:
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was happy and thought Zhang Qian's words were right, so he ordered Zhang Qian to send secret envoys from Shu County and Jianwei County to set off in four groups at the same time: one from Zhan, one from Ran, one from Qi, and one from Qionbo, each traveling one or two thousand miles.
As a result, the northern route was blocked by Di and Zuo, and the southern route was blocked by Xi and Kunming.
Countries like Kunming had no rulers and were good at robbing and stealing. They often killed and robbed the Han Dynasty envoys, but the Han Dynasty envoys failed to pass.
However, I heard that more than a thousand miles west of Kunming, there was a country called Dianyue where the people rode elephants. Some of the merchants from Shu County who smuggled goods out of the country had been there, so the Han Dynasty began to communicate with the Dian Kingdom because they wanted to find a way to Daxia.
At first, the Han Dynasty wanted to open up the southwestern barbarians, but it wasted a lot of money and the road was not opened, so they gave up.
When Zhang Qian said that it was possible to connect to Daxia from the southwestern barbarians, the Han Dynasty resumed the work of opening up the southwestern barbarians.
Zhang Qian followed the general Wei Qing to attack the Xiongnu as a captain. Because he knew where there were water and grass, the army could not be exhausted. The emperor named Zhang Qian the Marquis of Bowang.
This happened in the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
The next year, Zhang Qian became a guard and set out from Youbeiping with General Li Guang to attack the Xiongnu.
The Xiongnu soldiers surrounded General Li. His army suffered many casualties. However, Zhang Qian was sentenced to death because he missed the agreed time. He spent money to atone for his sin and became a civilian.
In this year, the Han Dynasty sent Hussar General Huo Qubing to defeat tens of thousands of Huns in the west and came to the foot of the Qilian Mountains.
The next year, King Hunxie of the Xiongnu led his people to surrender to the Han Dynasty. From then on, there were no more Huns in the area from Jincheng, west of Hexi and Nanshan to Yanze.
The Huns sometimes sent scouts here, but this rarely happened.
For two full years after this, the Han Dynasty drove the Xiongnu Chanyu to the north of the desert.
After that, the emperor repeatedly asked Zhang Qian about the affairs of Daxia and other countries.
At this time, Zhang Qian had lost his marquis, so he said: When I was in the Xiongnu, I heard that King Wusun was called Kunmo. Kunmo's father was the king of a small country to the west of the Xiongnu.
The Xiongnu attacked and killed Kunmo's father, and Kunmo was abandoned in the wilderness after he was born.
Birds flew to him with meat in their mouths and fed him; wolves came and fed him.
The Chanyu felt strange and thought he was a god, so he took him in and let him grow up.
When he came of age, he was asked to lead troops in battles. After many meritorious service, the Shanyu gave him his father's people and ordered him to stay in the Western Regions for a long time.
Kunmo adopted his people and attacked nearby small towns. Gradually, he had tens of thousands of soldiers who could draw bows and fight, and they were familiar with the skills of offensive warfare.
After Shanyu's death, Kunmo led his people to move far away, maintaining their independence and refusing to worship the Huns.
The Xiongnu sent a commando to attack Kunmo, but failed to win. They believed that Kunmo was a god and stayed away from him. They restrained and controlled him instead of launching a major attack on him.
Now Shan Yugang was very tired after being beaten by the Han Dynasty, and the place controlled by King Hunxie was unguarded.
summary: Zhang Qian noted that in Daxia, he saw Qiong bamboo sticks and Shu cloth, bought from Shendu (India), suggesting a route from Shu. The emperor, intrigued by these wealthy states, sent envoys from Shu, but they were blocked by tribes like Kunming. Zhang Qian later joined General Wei Qing against the Xiongnu, earning the title Marquis of Bowang. After a failed campaign with Li Guang, he was reduced to commoner status.

translation:
The custom of the barbarians is to covet the property of the Han Dynasty. If Wusun can be gifted with rich property at this time to attract him to move eastward, live in the place formerly controlled by King Hunxie, and become brothers with the Han Dynasty, Kunmo should be able to accept it according to the situation. If he accepts this arrangement, then it will be like cutting off the right arm of the Huns.
After uniting Wusun, Daxia and other countries to its west can be recruited as foreign vassals.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty believed that Zhang Qian was right and appointed him as Zhonglang General. He led 300 people, each with two horses, tens of thousands of cattle and sheep, and carried money, cloth and silk worth tens of millions. He also appointed many deputy envoys holding talismans. If the road could be opened, he would send them to neighboring countries.
Zhang Qian had arrived at Wusun, and King Kunmo of Wusun received the envoys of the Han Dynasty with the same etiquette as he treated the Xiongnu Chanyu. Zhang Qian felt ashamed in his heart. He knew that the barbarians were greedy, so he said: The emperor gives gifts, and if the king does not thank him, the gifts will be returned.
Kunmo stood up, thanked him, accepted the gift, and continued to do other things as usual.
Zhang Qian explained the purpose of his mission to Kunmo and said: If Wusun can move eastward to King Hunxie's old land, then the Han Dynasty will send a daughter of a prince to marry Kunmo as his wife.
At this time, the Wusun Kingdom had been divided. The king was old and far away from the Han Dynasty. He did not know its size. It had been owned by the Xiongnu for a long time, and it was also close to the Xiongnu. The ministers were afraid of the Xiongnu and did not want to move. The king could not make the decision alone.
Therefore, Zhang Qian failed to get a clear attitude from King Wusun.
Kunmo had more than ten sons, one of whom was named Dalu. He was strong and good at leading troops. He led more than 10,000 cavalry and lived in another place.
Dalu's brother is the prince. The prince has a son named Cen Marry. The prince has died long ago.
When he was dying, he said to his father Kunmo: He must marry Cen as the prince and don't let anyone else take his place.
Kunmo sadly agreed to him, and finally let Cen marry and become the prince.
Da Lu was angry that he had failed to replace the prince, so he recruited his brothers and led his army to rebel, planning to attack Cen Maru and Kunmo.
Kunmo was old and often feared that Da Lu would kill Cen Marry, so he gave Cen Marry more than 10,000 cavalry and lived in another place.
And Kunmo himself has more than 10,000 cavalry for self-defense. In this way, the Wusun Kingdom was divided into three parts, but still generally belonged to Kunmo. Therefore, Kunmo did not dare to discuss this matter with Zhang Qian alone. Zhang Qian then assigned deputy envoys to Dayuan, Kangju, Dayuezhi, Daxia, Anxi, Shendu, Yutian, Chuyi and several nearby countries.
Wusun State sent a guide and translator to send Zhang Qian back to his country. Zhang Qian and the Wusun Kingdom sent dozens of envoys, bringing dozens of horses to return and thank the Emperor of Han. By the way, they allowed them to have a peek at the situation of the Han Dynasty and understand the vastness of the Han Dynasty.
Zhang Qian returned to the Han Dynasty and was appointed Daxing, ranking among the nine ministers.
More than a year later, he died.
Wusun's envoy had seen that the Han Dynasty had many people and rich property, so he went back and reported to the king. Wusun Kingdom paid more and more attention to the Han Dynasty.
summary: The emperor, seeking to ally with Wusun, sent Zhang Qian as Zhonglang General with 300 men, gifts, and deputy envoys. Wusun's king, Kunmo, was hesitant due to Xiongnu influence and internal divisions. Zhang Qian dispatched deputies to various states. Wusun sent envoys to the Han Dynasty, impressed by its wealth. Zhang Qian died as Daxing, a high official.

translation:
When the Han army arrived at Yucheng, only a few thousand soldiers followed, and they were all hungry and tired.
They attacked Yu Cheng, and Yu Cheng defeated them. Many Han soldiers were killed and wounded.
General Ershi discussed with Li Duo, Zhao Shicheng and others and said: If we can't capture Yucheng, let alone the king's capital?
So he led his troops back and went back and forth for two years.
When they retreated to Dunhuang, only one-tenth of the remaining soldiers were left.
They sent envoys to report to the emperor: The road is far away and there is often a lack of food. Moreover, the soldiers are not afraid of fighting, but only worried about starvation.
There are few people, not enough to capture Dawan.
I hope to temporarily withdraw our troops. In the future, more troops will be sent to attack.
After hearing this, the emperor was furious and sent an envoy to stop them at Yumen Pass, saying that anyone in the army who dared to enter Yumen Pass would be beheaded.
General Ershi was afraid, so he stayed in Dunhuang.
In the summer of the second year of Taichu, the Han Dynasty lost more than 20,000 troops of the Hou Yehou to the Xiongnu.
The ministers and deliberation officials all hoped to stop the military campaign against Dawan and concentrate their efforts on attacking the Xiongnu.
The emperor has attacked Dayuan, but Wan is a small country but failed to capture it. Then Daxia and other countries will despise the Han Dynasty, and Dayuan's good horses will never be obtained. Wusun and Luntai will easily cause trouble to the Han Dynasty envoys and be laughed at by foreigners.
So they punished Deng Guang and others who said that the crusade against Dawan was particularly unfavorable, pardoned prisoners and brave soldiers who had committed crimes, and sent more young men with bad conduct and border cavalry. In more than a year, 60,000 soldiers set out from Dunhuang, not including those who brought their own food and clothing to join the war.
These soldiers carried 100,000 cattle, more than 30,000 horses, and countless donkeys, camels and other items.
They also brought a lot of food and all kinds of weapons. At that time, the whole country was in turmoil. According to legend, there were more than fifty captains who were ordered to conquer Dawan.
There were no wells in King Wan's city, so they had to draw water from outside the city into the city. The Han Dynasty army sent hydraulic workers to change the water channels in the city so that there was no water available in the city.
The Han Dynasty also sent an additional 180,000 armored soldiers to garrison north of Jiuquan and Zhangye, and set up two counties, Juyan and Xiutu, to protect Jiuquan. The Han Dynasty also dispatched seven types of criminals across the country to carry dry food to supply the generals of the second division.
There was an endless stream of people transporting supplies, all the way to Dunhuang.
He also appointed two people who were familiar with horses as driving captains, preparing to select the best horses from Dawan after conquering it.
So the General of the Second Division went on another expedition, leading a large number of soldiers. Every small country he went to welcomed him, and they all provided food to the Han army.
They arrived at Lundou Kingdom, which refused to surrender. They attacked for several days and bloodbathed the country.
We went west from Luntou and arrived at the royal city safely. The Han army arrived with 30,000 people.
The Wan army attacked the Han army, and the Han army defeated the Wan army with arrows. The Wan army retreated into the city and guarded it against the city wall.
summary: Subsequently, the Han Dynasty established ties with Western Regions states, though envoys faced challenges from Xiongnu and local resistance. The emperor launched campaigns against Dawan for its horses, leading to two expeditions under Li Guangli. The first failed due to lack of supplies, but the second succeeded with a large army, capturing Dawan and securing horses. The Han Dynasty expanded its influence, setting up commanderies and protecting trade routes.

translation:
In the past, when Zhuanxu ruled the world, he appointed Nan Zhengzhong to be in charge of astronomy and Bei Zhengli to be in charge of geography.
During the Tang and Yu dynasties, the descendants of Chong and Li continued to be in charge of astronomy and geography until the Xia and Shang dynasties. Therefore, the Chongli family was in charge of astronomy and geography for generations.
During the Zhou Dynasty, Cheng Boxiu Fu was their descendant.
During the reign of King Xuan of Zhou Dynasty, the Chongli family became the Sima family because they lost their official position.
The Sima family has been in charge of Zhou history for generations.
During the reigns of King Zhou Hui and King Zhou Xiang, the Sima family left the capital of Zhou and went to the Kingdom of Jin.
Later, the marshal of the Jin army fled to Qin, and the Sima family also moved to Shaoliang.
Since the Sima clan left Zhou and came to Jin, the clan members were scattered in various places, some in Wei State, some in Zhao State, and some in Qin State.
In the Wei State, he became the Prime Minister of the Zhongshan State.
In the State of Zhao, they were famous for teaching the theory of swordsmanship, and Kuai Kuai was their descendant.
A man named Sima Cuo who lived in Qin State once had a dispute with Zhang Yi, so King Qin Hui sent Sima Cuo to lead an army to attack Shu State. After the capture, he made him the governor of Shu.
Sima Jin, the grandson of Sima Cuo, served Wu Xinjun Bai Qi.
Shaoliang has been renamed Xia Yang.
Sima Jin and Wu Xinjun killed the Changping Army of Zhao State. After returning, they were killed in Duyou together with Wu Xinjun and buried in Huachi.
Sima Chang, the grandson of Sima Jin, was an official in charge of iron smelting in the State of Qin. He lived in the era of Qin Shihuang.
Sima Xian, the great-great-grandson of Kuai Chi, was a general under Wu Xinjun and led troops to capture Chaoge.
When the princes were vying to be king, Sima An became king in Yin.
When Liu Bang, the king of Han, attacked Xiang Yu, the overlord of Chu, Sima An surrendered to the king of Han, and the Han Dynasty made the Yin region Hanoi County.
Sima Chang gave birth to Sima Wuze, who served as the mayor of the Han Dynasty.
Wuze gave birth to Sima happy. Sima happy was awarded the title of five great officials. After his death, they were all buried in Gaomen.
Sima Xi gave birth to Sima Tan, who became Grand Historian.
Tai Shigong studied astronomy from Tang Du, the Book of Changes from Yang He, and Taoist theory from Huang Zi.
Tai Shigong was an official from Jianyuan to Yuanfeng. He was worried that scholars could not understand the essence of each school and what they learned was contradictory, so he discussed the essence of the six schools of Yin and Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Ming, Dharma and Taoism:
"Zhouyi·Xici Zhuan" says: People all over the world pursue the same thing, but their specific plans are diverse; they achieve the same goal, but the methods they take are different.
Yin-Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Mingjia, Legalism and Taoism are all schools dedicated to how to achieve peace and order in the world, but the doctrines they follow are not the same, some are explicit and some are not.
I have studied the art of Yin and Yang in private, and found that it focuses on the omens of good and bad luck, and has many taboos, which makes people restrained and fearful. However, the Yin and Yang family's principles on the order of the four seasons of the year cannot be discarded.
summary: In ancient times, when Zhuanxu ruled the world, he appointed Nan Zhengzhong to oversee astronomy and Bei Zhengli to oversee geography. During the Tang and Yu dynasties, the descendants of Chong and Li continued these duties through the Xia and Shang dynasties, with the Chongli family holding these positions for generations. During the Zhou Dynasty, Cheng Boxiu Fu was their descendant. Under King Xuan of Zhou, the Chongli family became the Sima family after losing their official position. The Sima family then managed Zhou history for generations. During the reigns of Kings Hui and Xiang of Zhou, the Sima family left the Zhou capital for the Kingdom of Jin. Later, when the Jin army marshal fled to Qin, the Sima family moved to Shaoliang. From there, clan members scattered to Wei, Zhao, and Qin states. In Wei, a Sima became Prime Minister of Zhongshan. In Zhao, they were known for teaching swordsmanship. In Qin, Sima Cuo disputed with Zhang Yi, leading King Hui of Qin to send him to attack Shu, where he became governor. Sima Jin, Sima Cuo's grandson, served Wu Xinjun Bai Qi and participated in killing the Changping Army of Zhao. Both were later killed and buried in Huachi. Sima Chang, Sima Jin's grandson, served as an iron-smelting official during Qin Shihuang's era. Sima Xian, a descendant of Kuai Chi, was a general under Wu Xinjun who captured Chaoge. When princes vied for kingship, Sima An became king in Yin. When Liu Bang, King of Han, attacked Xiang Yu, Sima An surrendered, and the Han made Yin into Hanoi County. Sima Chang fathered Sima Wuze, who served as mayor of Han. Wuze fathered Sima Xi, who was awarded the title of five great officials. Sima Xi fathered Sima Tan, who became Grand Historian. Tai Shigong studied astronomy from Tang Du, the Book of Changes from Yang He, and Taoist theory from Huang Zi. He served from Jianyuan to Yuanfeng and worried that scholars could not understand each school's essence, so he discussed the six schools: Yin-Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Ming, Legalism, and Taoism. He noted that while all sought peace and order, their doctrines differed. Yin-Yang focused on good and bad omens with many taboos, making people fearful, but its principles on the four seasons could not be discarded. Confucianism was broad but rarely grasped essentials, taking much effort with little effect, yet its etiquette on君臣父子 relationships could not be changed. Mohism was frugal and difficult to follow, but its emphasis on utility could not be discarded. Legalism advocated harsh punishments without kindness, but its correction of status relationships could not be changed. Famous scholars made people constrained and lost authenticity, but the relationship between names and reality required examination. Taoism made minds focused and actions consistent with the invisible Tao, absorbing strengths from other schools and adapting to times and changes.

translation:
The official position of Taishi is in charge of astronomy and does not care about civil affairs.
Taishi Gong had a son named Qian.
Sima Qian was born in Longmen and lived a life of farming and animal husbandry in the north of the Yellow River and south of Longmen Mountain.
When he was only ten years old, he already learned to recite ancient Chinese prose.
At the age of 20, he began to travel south to the Jiang and Huai areas, climbed Mount Kuaiji, explored the Yu Cave, visited Mount Jiuyi, and rafted on the Yuan River and Xiang River. He crossed north to Wenshui and Sishui, studied learning in the cities of Qi and Shandong, investigated the legacy of Confucius, and performed the ritual of shooting in Zouxian and Yishan. He was trapped in Po, Xue, and Pengcheng, and returned to his hometown through the land of Liang and Chu.
So Sima moved out to serve as a doctor, and was ordered to go west to conquer the south of Bashu. He went south through Qiong, Zuo and Kunming, and returned to the court to return his orders.
In this year, the emperor began to hold the Han Dynasty's Zen ceremony, but Tai Shigong was stranded in Zhounan and could not participate in the ceremony. Therefore, he was so angry that he fell ill and was about to die.
His son Sima Qian happened to return from a mission and visited his father between the Yellow River and Luoshui.
Taishi Gong held Sima Qian's hand and cried and said: Our ancestor was Taishi of the Zhou Dynasty.
As far back as the ancient Yu and Xia Dynasties, he had gained fame and was responsible for astronomical affairs.
Will the decline of future generations be cut off in my hands today?
If you continue to be Taishi, you will continue the work of our ancestors.
Now the emperor has inherited the great cause of the thousand-year unification of the Han Dynasty and is holding a Zen ceremony in Mount Tai, but I cannot accompany him. This is fate, it is fate!
After I die, you must become Taishi; when you become Taishi, don't forget the writings I want to write.
Furthermore, filial piety begins with serving parents, then serves the emperor, and finally establishes one's reputation.
It is the greatest filial piety to make one's name known to future generations to show off one's parents.
The world praises the Duke of Zhou, saying that he can expound and praise the merits of King Wen and King Wu, promote the customs of Zhou and Shao, understand the thoughts of Taiwang and Wang Ji, and even the achievements of Gong Liu, and respect the ancestor Hou Ji.
After King You and King Li of Zhou Dynasty, the royal way declined and the rituals and music declined. Confucius studied and sorted out the old classics, repaired and revitalized the abandoned and destroyed rituals and music, discussed the "Book of Songs" and "Book of Books", and wrote "Spring and Autumn", which scholars still use as a guideline.
In the more than four hundred years since Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, the princes have merged with each other and all the history books have been discarded.
Nowadays, the rise of the Han Dynasty, the unification of the country, the Ming Dynasty, the wise king, the loyal ministers, and the righteous people, I, as the Taishi, have not been able to comment on and record it, cutting off the world's history-making tradition. I am very scared about this, you must keep it in mind!
Sima Qian lowered his head and shed tears and said: "Although my son is stupid, I will detail the historical news compiled by my ancestors and dare not make any omissions."
Three years after Sima Tan's death, Sima moved to the post of Taishi Ling and began to collect historical books and archives collected by the state.
In the fifth year of Sima Qian's appointment as Taishi Ling, which was the first year of Taichu in the Han Dynasty, during the winter solstice on Jiazishuo day in November, the Han Dynasty's calendar began to use Xia Zheng, that is, the first month of the lunar calendar was the first month. The emperor held a ceremony to implement the new calendar in the Mingtang, and all the gods received auspiciousness.
Tai Shigong said: The ancestors said: Confucius came into being five hundred years after the death of Duke Zhou.
Five hundred years after the death of Confucius, is there anyone who can inherit the Qingming Dynasty, correct the "Yi Zhuan", continue the "Spring and Autumn", and interpret the "Poetry", "Book", "Ritual" and "Music"?
summary: Tai Shigong had a son named Qian. Sima Qian was born in Longmen, farming and herding north of the Yellow River. At ten, he learned ancient prose. At twenty, he traveled south to Jiang and Huai, climbed Kuaiji, explored Yu Cave, visited Jiuyi, rafted on Yuan and Xiang rivers, crossed north to Wenshui and Sishui, studied in Qi and Shandong, investigated Confucius's legacy, performed shooting rituals in Zou and Yi, was trapped in Po, Xue, and Pengcheng, and returned through Liang and Chu. He then served as a doctor, went west to conquer south of Bashu, traveled south through Qiong, Zuo, and Kunming, and returned to report. That year, the emperor began the Han Zen ceremony, but Tai Shigong was stranded in Zhounan and could not participate, becoming ill and near death. When Sima Qian visited his father between the Yellow River and Luoshui, Tai Shigong held his hand and wept, saying their ancestor was Taishi of Zhou, responsible for astronomical affairs since Yu and Xia. He urged Sima Qian to continue as Taishi and not forget the writings he wanted to complete. He emphasized that filial piety begins with serving parents, then the emperor, and finally establishing one's reputation. He cited the Duke of Zhou for expounding King Wen and King Wu's merits, and Confucius for studying old classics, writing the Spring and Autumn Annals. He lamented that for over four hundred years since Confucius, history had been discarded, and with the Han rise, he feared cutting off the historical tradition. Sima Qian wept and promised to detail the historical news compiled by their ancestors without omission. Three years after Sima Tan's death, Sima Qian became Taishi Ling and began collecting historical books. In the first year of Taichu, the Han calendar began using Xia Zheng with the first month as the new year. Tai Shigong reflected on Confucius appearing five hundred years after the Duke of Zhou, and wondered if someone would now inherit the Qingming, correct the Yi Zhuan, and continue the Spring and Autumn. He discussed with Doctor Hu Sui why Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, explaining that when Zhou kingship declined, Confucius praised and criticized 242 years of history as a standard for judging right and wrong, belittling unrighteous emperors, reprimanding wrong princes, and denouncing chaotic officials. The Spring and Autumn Annals explained the governance of three kings, distinguished personnel rules, and allowed ruined countries to exist and severed lineages to continue. Sima Qian then began compiling documents. In the seventh year, he suffered disaster from Li Ling and was imprisoned. He sighed that this was his sin, but reflected that King Wen deduced the Book of Changes while imprisoned, Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals when distressed, Qu Yuan wrote Li Sao when exiled, and others wrote when frustrated. He finally resolved to record history from the Tao and Tang dynasties to Emperor Wu's Huolin year, starting from the Yellow Emperor. He organized his work into twelve basic annals, ten tables, eight books, thirty hereditary houses, and seventy biographies, totaling 130 chapters and 526,500 words, called "Tai Shi Gong Shu." He stored it in a famous mountain and left a copy in Kyoto for future sages and gentlemen to see.

translation:
Sun Tzu, named Wu, was from the state of Qi.
Because he was proficient in the art of war, he was received by King Wu in his house.
Helu said: I have read all thirteen of your military books. Can you use them to try to command the army on a small scale?
Sun Tzu replied: Yes.
Helu said: Can it be tested on women?
Answer: Yes.
So Helu agreed to his experiment and called out the beauties in the palace, a total of about one hundred and eighty people.
Sun Tzu divided them into two teams, and asked King Wu's two most beloved concubines to serve as captains of each team respectively. He also asked all the beauties to hold a halberd.
Then he commanded them: Do you know your heart, your left and right hands, and your back?
The women replied: Yes.
Sun Tzu said: When I say forward, you look in the direction your heart is facing; when I say left, you look in the direction your left hand is facing; when I say right, you look in the direction your right hand is facing; when I say backward, you look in the direction your back is facing. The women replied: Yes.
After the order was announced, the axes and other instruments of torture were set up, and the order that had been announced was clearly explained many times.
He beat the drums and gave orders, telling them to turn to the right, and the women all laughed.
Sun Tzu said: It is the general's fault that discipline is unclear and orders are unfamiliar.
He explained it clearly several times, and then beat the drums and ordered them to turn to the left. The women all laughed again.
Sun Tzu said: It is the fault of the general if he does not understand the discipline and is unfamiliar with the orders; now it is the fault of the officers and soldiers if he does not follow the orders even though he has given them clearly.
So we have to kill the captains of the left and right teams.
King Wu was watching from the stage and was shocked to see that his grandson was about to kill his concubine.
He hurriedly sent an envoy to convey the order and said: I already know that the general is good at using troops. If I don't have these two concubines, my food will not taste sweet. I hope you won't kill them.
Sun Tzu replied: I have accepted the order as a general, and the general is in the army. It is not necessary to accept some orders from the king.
So he killed two captains in public.
Then the second person from the two teams was appointed as the captain in order, and then the drums were beaten to give orders. Whether the women moved left or right, forward or backward, kneeled or stood up, they all complied with the orders and discipline requirements. No one dared to speak out.
So Sun Tzu sent an envoy to report to the King of Wu: The team has been drilled in order. Your Majesty, you can come down and inspect their drills. You can use them however you want, even if you ask them to go through fire and water.
King Wu replied: Let the general stop the drill and go back to the hotel to rest. I don't want to go down and take a look.
Sun Tzu sighed and said: Your Majesty only appreciates my military theory, but cannot let me put it into practice.
From then on, King Wu Helu knew that Sun Tzu was really good at using troops, and finally appointed him as a general.
Later, Wu State defeated the powerful Chu State in the west, conquered the capital of Ying, and shocked Qi and Jin in the north. It became famous among the princes and countries. During this period, Sun Tzu not only participated, but also contributed a lot.
After the death of the grandson, another Sun Bin appeared after more than a hundred years.
summary: Sun Tzu, from Qi, demonstrated his military expertise to King Helu of Wu by training 180 palace women. After repeated orders failed due to laughter, he executed the two favorite concubines serving as captains, despite the king's plea. The drill then succeeded perfectly. Helu later appointed Sun Tzu as general, leading Wu to defeat Chu, capture Ying, and intimidate Qi and Jin.
