translation:
Sun Bin was born in Acheng and Juancheng, and he was also a descendant of Sun Wu.
He once studied the art of war with Pang Juan.
After Pang Juan served the Wei State, he became a general of King Wei Hui, but he knew that his talents were not as good as Sun Bin. So he secretly found Sun Bin.
When Sun Bin arrived, Pang Juan was afraid that he was more talented than himself and hated him, so he cut off his feet on the pretext of being guilty and tattooed his face, hoping that he would hide him and not dare to show his face.
The envoy of Qi State came to Daliang, and Sun Bin secretly met with the envoy of Qi as a prisoner to lobby.
The envoys of Qi State thought that he was a rare talent, so they secretly drove him back to Qi State.
General Qi Tian Ji not only appreciated him but also treated him like a guest.
Tian Ji often raced horses with the nobles of Qi State and placed huge bets.
Sun Bin found that their horses had almost the same foot power and could be divided into three grades: upper, middle and lower.
So Sun Bin said to Tian Ji: Just place a big bet and I can make you win.
Tian Ji believed this and placed thousands of gold bets in a competition with the King of Qi and the nobles.
When the game came, Sun Bin said to Tian Ji: Now use your low-grade horses against their high-grade horses, your high-grade horses against their medium-grade horses, and your medium-grade horses against their low-grade horses.
After three games, Tian Ji lost once and won twice, and finally won the Qi King's daughter's bet.
So Tian Ji recommended his grandson to King Wei of Qi.
After King Wei asked him about the art of war, he regarded him as his teacher.
Later, Wei State attacked Zhao State. Zhao State was in a critical situation and asked Qi State for help.
King Qi Wei planned to appoint Sun Bin as a general, but Sun Bin declined and said: "A person who has been tortured cannot be a general."
So he appointed Tian Ji as the commander-in-chief and Sun Bin as the military adviser. They sat in a car with a tent and planned secretly.
Tian Ji wanted to lead the reinforcements to Zhao, but Sun Bin said: Those who want to untie the tangled threads should not clench their fists and pull forcefully; those who are rescuing a fight should not get involved in random fights. To seize the vital points of the combatants, the combatants have to untie themselves due to the constraints of the situation.
Now that Wei and Zhao are attacking each other, Liang's elite troops will be exhausted abroad, and the old, weak and remnant troops will be exhausted at home.
You might as well lead the army to advance towards Daliang quickly, occupy its main transportation routes, and attack its empty areas. Wei will definitely abandon Zhao and return to save itself.
In this way, we saved the siege of Zhao State in one fell swoop, and at the same time reaped the effects of Wei State's own defeat.
Tian Ji listened to Sun Bin's advice. Sure enough, the Wei army left Handan and returned to the army. They fought in Guiling and were severely defeated.
Thirteen years later, Wei and Zhao jointly attacked South Korea, and South Korea asked Qi for help.
The King of Qi sent Tian Ji to lead the army to rescue and marched directly to Daliang.
Wei general Pang Juan heard the news and led his troops to withdraw from South Korea and return to Wei. However, the Qi army had already crossed the border and advanced westward.
Sun Bin said to Tian Ji: The Wei army has always been fierce and brave, but looks down on the Qi soldiers. The Qi soldiers are called timid and cowardly. Generals who are good at commanding battles must follow this trend and guide them.
summary: Over a century later, Sun Bin, a descendant, studied warfare with Pang Juan. Jealous of Sun Bin's talent, Pang Juan had his feet cut off and face tattooed. Sun Bin secretly met Qi envoys, who smuggled him to Qi. Advising General Tian Ji, Sun Bin used clever horse-racing tactics to win bets, impressing King Wei of Qi, who made him a teacher. When Wei attacked Zhao, Sun Bin proposed attacking Daliang to force Wei's retreat, leading to victory at Guiling. Years later, when Wei and Zhao attacked Han, Sun Bin feigned weakness by reducing camp stoves daily. Pang Juan, believing Qi soldiers deserted, pursued with light troops to Maling, where Sun Bin ambushed him. Pang Juan, seeing a carved tree, lit a torch and was killed by arrows, saying, "This boy has made his name!" Sun Bin's fame spread.

translation:
Moreover, the State of Lu and the State of Wei are fraternal countries. If Lord Lu re-employs Wu Qi, it would be equivalent to abandoning the State of Wei.
Lu Jun suspected Wu Qi and alienated Wu Qi.
At this time, Wu Qi heard that Wei Guowen was a wise man and wanted to serve him.
Marquis Wen asked Li Ke: "What is Wu Qi like?"
Li Ke replied: Wu Qi is greedy for fame and loves women. However, when it comes to leading troops in war, even Sima Ranju cannot surpass him.
So Wei Wenhou appointed him as the chief general, attacked Qin and captured five cities.
Wu Qi acted as the commander-in-chief, wearing the same clothes as the lowest soldiers, eating the same food, sleeping without mattresses, marching without riding horses, and personally carrying the bundled grain on his back and sharing the joys and sorrows with the soldiers.
A soldier had a malignant sore, and Wu Qi sucked the liquid for him.
When the soldier's mother heard about it, she burst into tears.
Some people say: Your son is a nobody, but the general sucks his juice for him. Why are you still crying?
The mother replied: "That's not the case. In the past, General Wu sucked the sores for his father. His father marched bravely on the battlefield and died at the hands of the enemy."
Now General Wu sucked his son's sores again. I don't know when and where he will die, so I cry for him.
Marquis Wen of Wei appointed Wu Qi as the governor of the Xihe area to resist Qin and South Korea because Wu Qi was good at using soldiers, honest and fair, and could win the favor of all the soldiers.
After Wei Wenhou died, Wu Qi served his son Wei Wuhou.
Marquis Wu was boating down the Yellow River. Halfway through the boat, he turned back to Wu Qi and said, "The mountains and rivers are so dangerous and magnificent. This is the treasure of Wei!"
Wu Qi replied: The stability of state power lies in benevolence to the people, not in the dangerous geographical situation.
In the past, the Sanmiao clan bordered Dongting Lake on the left and Pengli Lake on the right. Because it did not practice virtue and was not trustworthy, Xia Yu was able to destroy it.
Xia Jie's territory borders the Yellow River and Jishui on the left, Mount Tai and Mount Hua on the right, Mount Yique to the south, and Yangchang Ban to the north. Because he did not implement benevolent governance, Shang Tang banished him.
Yin Zhou's territory had Mengmen Mountain on the left, Taihang Mountain on the right, Changshan Mountain to the north, and the Yellow River flowing to the south. Because he was not benevolent, King Wu killed him.
From this point of view, the stability of the political power lies in the kindness given to the people, not in the dangerous geographical situation.
If you don't show kindness, even people in the same boat will become your enemies! Wuhou replied: Well said.
Wu Qi became the guardian of Xihe and gained a high reputation.
The state of Wei set up a phase system and appointed Tian Wen as prime minister.
Wu Qi was very unhappy and said to Tian Wen: Please let me compare my merits with you, can you?
Tian Wen said: Yes.
Wu Qi said: "Command the three armies so that the soldiers are willing to fight to the death for the country and the enemy does not dare to plot against Wei. Who is better between you and me?"
Tian Wen said: Not as good as you.
Wu Qi said: "How can you and I manage the civil and military officials, keep the people attached to them, and enrich the treasury?"
Tian Wen said: Not as good as you.
Wu Qi said: If the Qin army refuses to defend the Xihe River and does not dare to invade the east, South Korea and Zhao will surrender. Who can compare with me?
Tian Wen said: Not as good as you.
Wu Qi said: You are inferior to me in these aspects, but your position is above mine. Why?
Tian Wen said: The king of Wei is still young, the people of the country are worried, the ministers are not friendly, and the people do not trust me. At this time, should I entrust the political affairs to you or to me?
Wu Qi was silent for a long time, and then said: "I should leave it to you."
Tian Wen said: This is why my position is higher than yours.
Only then did Wu Qi realize that he was inferior to Tian Wen in this aspect.
After Tian Wen's death, his uncle became the prime minister and married Wei Jun's daughter, but he was afraid of Wu Qi.
The uncle's servant said: "It is not difficult to drive Wu Qi away."
The uncle asked: What should I do?
The servant said: Wu Qi is a man of character and loves fame and prestige.
You can find an opportunity to say to Marquis Wu first: Wu Qi is a virtuous man, but your country is too small and borders the powerful Qin State. I am privately worried that Wu Qi has no plans to stay in Wei State for a long time.
Marquis Wu would say: What should we do?
You take the opportunity to say to Wu Hou: Please test him by marrying the princess. If Wu Qi has the intention to stay in Wei for a long time, he will definitely agree to marry the princess. If Wu Qi does not have the intention to stay in Wei for a long time, he will definitely refuse.
This method can be used to infer his will.
You find an opportunity to invite Wu Qi to go home with you, deliberately making the princess angry and despising you in person. Seeing that the princess despises you like this, Wu Qi will definitely not marry the princess.
At that time, Wu Qi saw how the princess despised the prime minister, so he politely declined the offer to Marquis Wu of Wei.
Marquis Wu doubted Wu Qi and no longer trusted him.
Wu Qi was afraid of causing disaster, so he left Wei and immediately went to Chu.
King Chu Mourning had always heard that Wu Qi was a capable person, so he appointed him as the prime minister as soon as he arrived in Chu.
summary: Wu Qi, from Wei, served Lu after killing his Qi wife to gain trust, defeating Qi. Slandered for cruelty, he fled to Wei, where Marquis Wen appointed him general. He shared soldiers' hardships, even sucking pus from a soldier's sore, causing the soldier's mother to weep, recalling her husband's similar fate. Wu Qi governed Xihe, resisting Qin and Han. He advised Marquis Wu that state security relies on benevolence, not terrain. After Tian Wen became prime minister, Wu Qi felt slighted but accepted Tian Wen's reasoning about political stability. Later, a plot by the new prime minister made Marquis Wu suspect Wu Qi, who fled to Chu. King Mourning made him prime minister; he reformed laws, cut redundancies, and strengthened the military, pacifying Baiyue and defeating Qin and Han. After the king's death, nobles attacked Wu Qi, who hid on the king's corpse, causing arrows to strike both. The new prince executed over seventy families for this. Sima Qian notes Sun Tzu and Wu Qi's writings are famous, but Sun Bin couldn't avoid mutilation, and Wu Qi's harshness led to his death.

translation:
Tai Shigong said: When I read "Mencius", whenever I read that King Hui of Liang asked how to make profits for our country, I couldn't help but put down the book and sigh.
Said: Alas, seeking profit is really the beginning of all troubles!
Confucius rarely talked about the issue of profit. The reason was that he wanted to fundamentally prevent this source of trouble.
So he said that acting based on personal interests will lead to a lot of resentment.
From the emperor down to the common people, the disadvantages of being greedy for profit exist. What's the difference?
Meng Ke was from the state of Zou.
He once studied with Zisi's disciples.
After he became proficient in his studies, he went to lobby King Xuan of Qi, but King Xuan of Qi did not appoint him.
So when he arrived in Wei State, King Hui of Liang not only did not listen to his ideas, but also believed that his ideas were unrealistic and far from reality.
At that time, all the vassal states were implementing reforms. Qin appointed Shang Yang, which made the country rich and powerful; Chu and Wei also appointed Wu Qi, who defeated some countries and weakened powerful enemies; King Wei and Xuan of Qi appointed Sun Bin and Tian Ji, etc., so that the country was strong, and all the vassal states came east to pay homage to Qi.
When the vassal states were working on the offensive strategy of "joining vertical and horizontal lines" and regarded those who were good at attacking as virtuous, Mencius praised the virtues of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties. Therefore, it did not meet the needs of the countries he traveled around.
So he returned to his hometown and worked with Wan Zhang and others to sort out the Classics and Shujing, elucidate Confucius' thoughts and doctrines, and write a book called "Mencius", a total of seven chapters.
After him, scholars Zou Zi and others appeared.
There are three Zouzi in the state of Qi.
The earliest one was named Zou Ji. He used his piano playing skills to seek an audience with King Qi Wei. He then participated in state affairs, was named Chenghou, accepted the seal of the prime minister, and became prime minister. He lived in an era earlier than Mencius.
The second one is Zou Yan, who lived after Mencius.
Zou Yan witnessed that the princes who held the power of a country became more and more dissolute and extravagant, and could not advocate virtue and governance. They did not clean themselves up first and then extend it to the people as required in the "Book of Songs".
So he deeply observed the ebb and flow of yin and yang of all things, and recorded the strange and mysterious changes, such as "The End and the Beginning" and "The Great Sage", totaling more than 100,000 words.
His words are grand, vast, absurd and unreasonable. We must start by verifying small things, and then generalize to big things, and even reach infinity.
His theory starts from the present day and then goes forward to the Yellow Emperor's era, which is discussed by scholars. Then, it generally follows the rise and fall of the generations, recording the bad and bad systems of different generations, and then pushes forward from the Yellow Emperor's era to far, far away, until the heaven and earth have not yet been formed. It is really profound and mysterious and cannot be investigated, but it is necessary to trace its origin.
He first listed China's famous mountains and rivers, deep valleys, animals, water and soil vegetation, and precious species, and then promoted it to overseas countries where people could not even see it.
He stated that since the beginning of the world, the five virtues of metal, wood, water, fire, and earth have been mutually reinforcing and restraining each other, and the replacement of emperors in the past dynasties has coincided with them.
This is how auspiciousness from heaven corresponds to human affairs. He believes that China as mentioned by Confucianism is only one eighty-one percent of the world.
summary: The historian Tai Shigong reflects on Mencius, noting that King Hui of Liang’s focus on profit troubled him, as Confucius rarely discussed profit to prevent resentment. Mencius, a student of Zisi’s disciples, failed to gain favor with King Xuan of Qi or King Hui of Liang, who found his ideals impractical. During an era of reforms—where states like Qin, Chu, Wei, and Qi thrived through figures like Shang Yang, Wu Qi, and Sun Bin—Mencius advocated ancient virtues, which did not align with the prevailing strategies of alliances and warfare. He returned home to compile the *Mencius* with Wan Zhang.

translation:
It is called Chixian Shenzhou in China.
There are nine states within Chixian Shenzhou, which are the nine states arranged by Xia Yu in order, but they cannot be counted as the full number of states.
Outside of China, there are nine other places like Chixian Shenzhou. This is the so-called Kyushu.
There are small seas surrounding this place. People and animals cannot communicate with other states. It is like an independent area. This is one state.
There are nine states like this, and the sea surrounds it, which means it reaches the edge of heaven and earth.
Zou Yan's theories are all of this type of statement.
However, to sum up its essence, it must all boil down to benevolence, righteousness, frugality, and be implemented among the king, his ministers, and their relatives. However, the description at the beginning is indeed too rambling.
When princes and princes first saw his teachings, they were surprised and thought about it. They were inspired to learn it, but in the end they could not put it into practice.
Therefore, Zou Yan was respected in Qi State.
When he arrived in Wei State, King Hui of Liang met Gao Ying from afar and performed the courtesy of guest and host with him.
When he arrived at the State of Zhao, Lord Pingyuan accompanied him and personally brushed his seat for him.
When he arrived in Yan State, King Zhao of Yan took a broom to clear the road as a guide for him, and asked to sit on the disciple's seat to learn from him. He also built a Jieshi Palace for him and went to worship him as his teacher in person. He wrote the chapter "Main Movement".
Zou Yan traveled to various countries and received such courtesy and respect. How can this be the same as Confucius and Chen Cai who were starving when they had no food supplies, and Meng Ke was in trouble in Qi and Liang? How can it be the same?
In the past, King Wu of Zhou used benevolence and righteousness to defeat King Zhou of Yin and became the king of the world. Boyi would rather starve to death than eat the food of the Zhou Dynasty; Duke Ling of Wei asked about the battle formation, but Confucius did not answer; King Hui of Liang wanted to attack Zhao, but Meng Ke praised the king for leaving Pidi.
Are the actions of these famous figures just to cater to the world and please their masters?
If you hold a square tenon but have to insert a round mortise, how can you fit it in?
Some people say that Yi Yin carried a cauldron on his back to cook for Tang, but he encouraged Tang to behave in a royal way, and Tang unified the world; Baili Xi was feeding cattle under the cart, but Duke Mu of Qin appointed him, and thus dominated the princes. Their approach is to first cater to the owner's wishes, and then guide the owner onto the upright path.
Although Zou Yan's words are unreasonable, maybe they have the meaning of Yi Yin carrying the tripod and Baili Xifanniu?
From Zou Yan to Qi Guoji, many scholars, such as Chunyu Kun, Shen Dao, Huanyuan, Jiezi, Tian Pian, Zou Shi, etc., each wrote books and talked about the rise and fall of the country and the chaos, and used it to gain the trust of the monarch. How can they say all this?
Chunyu Kun was a native of Qi.
He is knowledgeable and strong in memory, and he is not an expert in his studies.
Judging from his words of persuasion to the king, it seems that he admires Yan Ying's outspokenness and courage to admonish, but in fact he specializes in observing words and emotions and trying to figure out the master's mind.
Once, a guest recommended Chunyu Kun to King Hui of Liang. King Hui dismissed his attendants and sat alone to receive him twice, but he never said a word.
summary: After Mencius, Zou Yan emerged in Qi, observing princes’ decadence and developing theories on yin-yang and the five virtues (metal, wood, water, fire, earth). His writings, such as *The End and the Beginning*, were vast and speculative, tracing history from the present to before heaven and earth formed. He divided the world into nine continents like Chixian Shenzhou, surrounded by seas, and linked dynastic changes to cosmic cycles. Despite their grandiosity, his ideas emphasized benevolence and frugality, impressing rulers like King Zhao of Yan, who treated him with high respect—unlike Confucius and Mencius, who faced hardship.

translation:
King Hui felt very strange, so he scolded the guest and said, "You praised Mr. Chunyu and said that even Guan Zhong and Yan Ying could not catch up with him. When he saw me, I gained nothing."
Am I not worthy of talking to him?
What is the reason?
The guest told Chunyu Kun what King Hui had said.
Chunyu Kun said: "That's right."
The last time I saw the king, the king's mind was entirely on the horse; the next time I saw the king, the king's mind was on his looks and sounds, so I remained silent.
The guest reported all what Chunyu Kun said to King Hui. King Hui was greatly surprised and said, "Oh, Mr. Chunyu Kun is such a saint!"
When Mr. Chunyu came last time, someone presented a fine horse. Before I could take a look at it, Mr. Chunyu happened to come.
The last time I came here, another person offered me a karaoke. Before I had a chance to try it out, I met Mr. Chunyu.
When I met Mr. Chunyu, although I shouted and dismissed the attendants around me, I was thinking about horses and singers. This is what happened.
Later, Chunyu Kun met King Hui, and the two talked intently for three days and three nights without getting tired.
King Hui planned to grant Chunyu Kun the position of prime minister, but Chunyu Kun politely declined and left.
At that time, King Hui gave him an exquisite carriage with four horses, five pieces of silk and jade, and a hundred yi of gold.
Chunyu Kun never held an official position throughout his life.
Be careful, he is from Zhao.
Tian Pian and Jiezi were from Qi State.
Huanyuan is from the Chu state.
They all specialize in the moral theories of Huangdi and Laozi, and elaborate on the meaning of Huangdi's theory.
Therefore, they all wrote. Shen Dao wrote twelve treatises, Huan Yuan wrote the first and second chapters, and Tian Pian and Jie Zi also wrote treatises.
Zou Shi was one of several Zou disciples in Qi State. He used Zou Yan's theories to write articles.
At that time, the King of Qi admired these scholars very much, and appointed everyone from Chunyu Kun to the next to be senior officials. He built residences for them along the thoroughfares with high gates and high gates, to show his respect and preference for them.
In this way, we can attract guests from various vassal states and promote Qi as the best country to attract talented people from all over the world.
Xunqing is from the state of Zhao.
When he was fifty years old, he came to Qi to lobby and give lectures.
Zou Yan's teachings were tortuous, exaggerated and full of empty arguments; Zou Shi's articles were complete and thorough but difficult to implement; Chunyu Kun, if you stayed with him for a long time, you would often learn some penetrating remarks.
Therefore, the people of Qi praised them and said: "Zou Yan is the one who talks eloquently, Zou Shi is the one who is exquisite in craftsmanship, he is wise and eloquent, and Chunyu Kun is the one who talks endlessly."
Tian Pian and others all died during the reign of King Xiang of Qi. At this time, Xunqing was the oldest and most senior master.
At that time, the state of Qi was still filling the vacancy of the senior officials. Xun Qing served as the master of the Jixia bachelor's ceremony three times.
Later, someone in Qi State slandered Xun Qing, so Xun Qing went to Chu State, and Lord Chun Shen appointed him as the Lanling Order.
After the death of Lord Chun Shen, Xun Qing was dismissed from office and settled in Lanling.
Li Si was once his student and later served as prime minister in the Qin Dynasty.
Xun Qing hated the dark politics of the troubled times, and the chaotic monarchs appeared one after another. They did not understand the common sense and right ways, but were deceived by the witches who pretended to be gods.
After his death, he was buried in Lanling.
At that time, the State of Zhao also had Gongsun Long, who argued with Hui Shi's theory of "Li Jian Bai" and "Contracts and Variations", as well as the writings of Juzi; the State of Wei once had Li Kui, who proposed the idea of ​​encouraging farming to maximize the power of the land; the State of Chu once had Xizi and Changlu, and there was a Xuzi in Dong'e of Qi State.
summary: Other scholars included Chunyu Kun of Qi, known for his wit and ability to read minds; he remained silent before King Hui of Liang until the king focused on governance, later conversing for three days but declining a prime minister post. Shen Dao, Tian Pian, and Jiezi wrote on Huang-Lao doctrines, while Zou Shi expanded on Zou Yan’s work. The King of Qi honored these scholars with high positions and grand residences to attract talent. Xunqing of Zhao, at age fifty, lectured in Qi, criticizing Zou Yan’s empty theories and Chunyu Kun’s cleverness. He became the eldest Jixia scholar, serving as Lanling magistrate in Chu after slander in Qi. His student Li Si became Qin’s prime minister. Xunqing condemned chaotic times and was buried in Lanling. Other figures like Gongsun Long, Hui Shi, Li Kui, and Mo Zhai—who advocated defense and cost-saving—also contributed to the era’s diverse philosophies.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/孟子荀卿列传

translation:
Mengchangjun's surname is Tian Mingwen. Tian Wen's father is Jingguo Jun Tian Ying.
Tian Ying is the youngest son of King Qi Wei and the younger brother of King Qi Xuan's concubine.
Tian Ying has been in power since he was King Wei. He once led troops with Chenghou Zou Ji and Tian Ji to rescue South Korea and attack Wei.
Later, Chenghou and Tian Ji competed for the favor of King Qi and had a deep rift. As a result, Chenghou betrayed Tian Ji.
Tian Ji was very frightened, so he launched a surprise attack on the city on the border of Qi. He failed to capture it and ran away.
At this time, King Wei of Qi passed away and King Xuan came to the throne. King Xuan knew that it was Chenghou who framed Tian Ji, so he recalled Tian Ji and made him a general.
In the second year of King Xuan of Qi, Tian Ji, Sun Bin and Tian Ying attacked the state of Wei, defeated the state of Wei in Maling, captured the prince Shen of the state of Wei, and killed the general Pang Juan of the state of Wei.
In the seventh year of King Xuan, Tian Ying was ordered to go to South Korea and Wei as an envoy. After some of his activities, South Korea and Wei were surrendered to Qi.
Tian Ying accompanied Han Zhaohou and King Wei Hui to meet with King Qi Xuan in Dong'anan. The three countries formed an alliance and signed a treaty before leaving.
The next year, King Xuan met with King Hui of Liang again in Zhendi.
This year, King Hui of Liang passed away.
In the ninth year of King Xuan's reign, Tian Ying became prime minister of Qi.
King Xuan of Qi and King Xiang of Wei respected each other as kings at the Xuzhou League.
After King Chu Wei learned about this incident, he was very angry with Tian Ying and thought that he was the one who planned it.
The next year, Chu attacked Qi and defeated the Qi army in Xuzhou, so they sent people to hunt down Tian Ying.
Tian Ying sent Zhang Chou to persuade King Chu Wei, and King Chu Wei finally gave up.
Tian Ying served as prime minister of Qi for eleven years. King Xuan died and King Min came to the throne.
Three years after King Min came to the throne, he granted Tian Ying the title of "Xue Yi".
At first, Tian Ying had more than forty sons. One of his concubines gave birth to a son named Wen. Tian Wen was born on May 5th.
Tian Ying told Tian Wen's mother: Don't raise him.
But Tian Wen's mother still secretly raised him.
When he grew up, his mother introduced Tian Wen to Tian Ying through Tian Wen's brother.
When Tian Ying saw the child, he angrily said to his mother: I asked you to throw this child away, but you dared to feed him. Why?
Before Tian Wen's mother could answer, Tian Wen immediately kowtowed and then asked Tian Ying: "Why are you not allowed to raise a child born in May?"
Tian Ying replied: A child born in May will be disadvantageous to his parents when he grows to be as tall as the door.
Tian Wen said: Is human destiny granted by God?
Or is it awarded by the portal?
Tian Ying didn't know how to answer, so he remained silent.
Tian Wen continued: If it is granted by God, why should you worry?
If it is granted by the portal, then as long as the portal is raised, who can grow so tall!
Tian Ying was speechless and scolded: "Stop talking!"
After a long time, Tian Wen took the opportunity to ask his father: "What is the name of your son's son?"
Tian Ying replied: "Call me grandson."
Tian Wen then asked: What is the name of your grandson’s grandson?
Tian Ying replied: "My name is Great-grandson."
Tian Wen asked again: What is the name of your great-great-grandson's grandson?
Tian Ying said: I don’t know anymore.
Tian Wen said: You have held great power and served as the prime minister of Qi. You have been kings for three generations. However, the territory of Qi has not expanded, but your private family has accumulated tens of thousands of gold, and there is not a single virtuous person under your family.
summary: Mengchangjun, whose surname was Tian and given name Wen, was the son of Jingguo Jun Tian Ying. Tian Ying, the youngest son of King Qi Wei, served as a general and later as prime minister of Qi, leading campaigns against Wei and forming alliances with Han and Wei. He had over forty sons, but Tian Wen was born on May 5th, a date considered inauspicious. Tian Ying ordered the child abandoned, but his mother secretly raised him. When Tian Wen grew up, he confronted his father, arguing that fate was determined by heaven, not by the doorframe, and criticized Tian Ying for accumulating wealth while neglecting the state's welfare. Impressed, Tian Ying made Tian Wen his heir.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传

translation:
I heard that the general’s court must have a general, and the prime minister’s court must have the prime minister.
Now your concubines can trample silk and satin, but the wise men cannot wear coarse clothes; your male and female slaves have leftover meat soup, but the wise men cannot even eat bran.
Now you are still trying to save more and more, wanting to leave it to those who can't even be called, but you have forgotten that the country is losing power among the princes day by day. I'm secretly weird.
From then on, Tian Ying changed his attitude towards Tian Wen, valued him, and asked him to take charge of housekeeping and receive guests.
The number of guests kept coming and going, and Tian Wen's reputation spread to all the vassal states.
All the vassal states sent people to ask Tian Ying to make Tian Wen the crown prince, and Tian Ying agreed.
After Tian Ying's death, he was given the posthumous title of Jing Guojun.
As expected, Tian Wen inherited Tian Ying's title in Xue Yi. This is Lord Mengchang.
Lord Mengchang was in Xue Yi, soliciting guests from various vassal states and people who had committed crimes and fled. Many people joined Lord Mengchang.
Lord Mengchang was willing to give up his family fortune and give them generous treatment, so scholars from all over the world came here to admire his reputation.
He has thousands of diners, and all are treated the same as Tian Wen, regardless of high or low.
Whenever Mr. Mengchang receives guests and sits and talks with them, he always arranges an attendant behind the screen to record the conversation between Mr. Mengchang and the guests, as well as the residence of the guests' relatives.
As soon as the guests left, Lord Mengchang sent envoys to the homes of the guests' relatives to comfort them and offer them gifts.
Once, Meng Changjun entertained guests for dinner, and someone blocked the light. The guest was very annoyed, thinking that the quality of the food must be unequal, so he put down his bowls and chopsticks and was about to say goodbye.
Lord Mengchang immediately stood up and compared his own food with his. The guest was so ashamed that he cut his neck and committed suicide as an apology. Therefore, many of the wise men were willing to join Lord Mengchang.
Mr. Mengchang warmly accepted all the guests who came to his door, without being picky or familiar, and gave them all generous treatment.
Therefore, everyone among the guests thought that Lord Mengchang was close to them.
When King Zhao of Qin heard that Lord Mengchang was a virtuous man, he first sent Lord Jingyang to Qi as a hostage and asked to see Lord Mengchang.
Lord Mengchang was about to go to Qin, but the guests did not approve of his trip and tried to persuade him, but he refused to listen and insisted on going.
At this time, a guest, Su Dai, said to him: I came out this morning and saw a puppet man and a clay puppet talking.
The puppet man said: As soon as it rains, you will collapse.
The earth puppet said: I was born from the earth. Even if it collapses, I will return to the earth.
If it really rains and the water rushes towards you, I don’t know where it will take you.
Today's Qin State is a country as fierce as a tiger or a wolf. If you insist on going there, if you cannot come back, will you not be laughed at by the local puppets?
After hearing this, Lord Mengchang realized the truth and stopped preparing for the trip.
In the twenty-fifth year of King Min of Qi, he finally sent Lord Mengchang to Qin. King Zhao of Qin immediately appointed Lord Mengchang as the prime minister of Qin.
summary: After Tian Ying's death, Tian Wen inherited the title of Lord Mengchang in Xue Yi. He generously hosted thousands of guests, treating them equally regardless of status. He recorded their conversations and sent gifts to their relatives. Once, a guest suspected unequal treatment, but Lord Mengchang compared his own meal to prove fairness, leading the guest to commit suicide in shame. Lord Mengchang accepted all guests without discrimination, earning their loyalty.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传

translation:
Someone among the officials persuaded the King of Qin: Lord Mengchang is indeed a virtuous man, but he is a member of the Qi clan and now serves as the prime minister of the Qin State. When planning things, he must first plan for the Qi State and then consider the interests of the Qin State. This will put the Qin State in danger.
So King Zhao of Qin dismissed Lord Mengchang from his position as prime minister.
He imprisoned Lord Mengchang and wanted to kill Lord Mengchang.
Lord Mengchang knew that the situation was critical, so he sent someone to see King Zhao's concubine to ask for help.
The concubine made a condition and said: I hope to get Lord Mengchang's white fox fur. When Lord Mengchang came, he brought with him a white fox fur, which was worth thousands of gold. There was no second one in the world. When he arrived in Qin, he presented it to King Zhao, and there was no other fur.
Lord Mengchang was worried about this matter. He asked all the guests, but no one could think of a solution.
There was a man who was not very capable but could steal things in dog skins. He said: I can get that white fox fur.
So that night, he disguised himself as a dog, went into the warehouse of the Qin Palace, took out the fox white fur that was presented to King Zhao, and took it back and presented it to King Zhao's concubine.
After getting the concubine, she interceded with King Zhao on behalf of Lord Mengchang, and King Zhao released Lord Mengchang.
After Mengchangjun was released, he immediately fled by express train, changed his exit certificate, changed his name and escaped from the city pass.
We arrived at Hangu Pass at midnight.
King Zhao regretted releasing Lord Mengchang and sent people to look for him again. When he found that he had escaped, he immediately sent people to chase him.
Mengchangjun and his party arrived at Hangu Pass. According to the customs law, guests can only be let out when the rooster crows. Mengchangjun was worried that his pursuers would arrive. Among the guests, there was a person who was of low rank but could imitate the rooster's crow. As soon as he imitated the rooster's crow, the nearby chickens also crowed, and he immediately showed his documents and escaped from Hangu Pass.
After about a meal after leaving the pass, Qin's pursuers arrived at Hangu Pass, but fell behind Lord Mengchang, so they had to go back.
When Lord Mengchang accepted these two people as guests, the guests all felt ashamed and disgraced. When Lord Mengchang suffered a disaster in Qin, he finally relied on these two people to escape.
From then on, the guests all admired Mengchangjun's approach of recruiting guests regardless of their status. Lord Mengchang passed by the State of Zhao, and Lord Pingyuan of the State of Zhao treated him as a distinguished guest.
When the people of Zhao heard about Mengchang's talents, they all came out to watch and see him. When they saw him, they all laughed and said: "I thought Mengchang was a tall man, but now I see him, he is just a skinny man."
Mengchangjun was very angry after hearing these teasing words.
The guests who were traveling with him jumped out of the car, killed hundreds of people, and left after destroying a county.
King Qi Min felt guilty for sending Lord Mengchang to Qin.
After Lord Mengchang returned to Qi State, the King of Qi made him prime minister of Qi State and in charge of state affairs.
Lord Mengchang resented Qin and planned to unite South Korea and Wei to attack Qin on the grounds that Qi had helped South Korea and Wei attack Chu. To this end, he borrowed weapons and rations from the Western Zhou Dynasty.
summary: King Zhao of Qin, hearing of Lord Mengchang's virtue, invited him to Qin and appointed him prime minister. However, officials warned that Lord Mengchang, being a Qi noble, would prioritize Qi's interests, so King Zhao imprisoned him. Lord Mengchang's concubine demanded his white fox fur as a bribe for her intercession. A guest skilled in thievery disguised himself as a dog, stole the fur from the palace, and gave it to the concubine, who secured Lord Mengchang's release. As he fled, another guest imitated a rooster's crow to open the Hangu Pass gates before pursuers arrived. Though initially ashamed of these lowly guests, Lord Mengchang's reliance on them earned admiration for his inclusive recruitment.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传

translation:
On behalf of the Western Zhou Dynasty, Su said to Lord Mengchang: You used the troops of Qi to help Han and Wei attack Chu for nine years, and gained the area north of Wan and Ye. As a result, Han and Wei became stronger. Now if you attack Qin, it will further strengthen the power of Han and Wei.
If South Korea and Wei have no worries from Chu in the south, and no troubles from Qin in the north, then Qi will be in danger.
When Korea and Wei become stronger, they will despise Qi and fear Qin. I really feel uneasy about this situation for you.
It is better for you to let the Western Zhou Dynasty have a deep friendship with Qin State. You should not attack Qin State and do not borrow weapons and food.
You send your army to Hangu Pass but do not attack. Let the Western Zhou Dynasty tell King Zhao of Qin your feelings and say that Duke Xue will definitely not attack Qin to strengthen the power of Han and Wei.
His purpose in attacking Qin was just to ask the king to instruct Chu to cede the Eastern Kingdom to Qi, and to ask you to release King Huai of Chu to reach a reconciliation.
You asked the Western Zhou Dynasty to use this method to benefit Qin. Qin could not be attacked and used Chu's territory to protect itself. Qin must want to do this.
If the King of Chu could be released, he would definitely be grateful to the State of Qi.
The Qi State will naturally become stronger and stronger after acquiring the Dong Kingdom, and Xue Yi will be free from worries for generations.
Qin will not be overly weakened, and it is located to the west of South Korea and Wei. South Korea and Wei must rely on Qi.
After hearing this, Lord Mengchang immediately said: "Okay."
So Han and Wei were asked to congratulate Qin, which prevented a military disaster. Qi, Han, and Wei no longer sent troops to attack, and Qi stopped borrowing weapons and rations from the Western Zhou Dynasty.
At this time, King Huai of Chu had already arrived in Qin, and Qin detained him, so Lord Mengchang must ask Qin to release him.
But Qin did not do this.
When Mengchang Jun was the prime minister of Qi, his attendant Wei Zi went to collect the tax from the feudal city for him. He made three trips back and forth, but he never got the tax back once.
Lord Mengchang asked him what was the reason for this, and Wei Zi replied: There is a virtuous man. I donated the tax to him privately in your name, so I did not take it back.
After hearing this, Lord Mengchang became angry and dismissed Wei Zi.
A few years later, someone spread rumors about Lord Mengchang to King Min of Qi, saying that Lord Mengchang was about to launch a rebellion.
When Tian Junjia kidnapped King Min, King Min suspected that it was Master Mengchang who planned it, and fled to avoid disaster.
The sage who had received food as a gift from Wei Zi heard about this and wrote to King Min to state that Lord Mengchang would not cause rebellion and asked for his own life as a guarantee. He then cut his neck and committed suicide at the gate of the palace to prove Lord Mengchang's innocence.
King Min was shocked, so he investigated and inquired about the actual situation. As expected, Lord Mengchang had no rebellion conspiracy, so he recalled Lord Mengchang.
Lord Mengchang therefore excused himself from illness and asked to resign and return to Xue Yi to retire.
King Min agreed to his request.
After that, Qin's fugitive general Lu Li came to Qi to serve as Qi's prime minister. He wanted to put Su Dai in trouble.
Su Dai said to Lord Mengchang: Zhou Zui was extremely loyal to the King of Qi, but the King of Qi expelled him and listened to the advice of his relatives and made Lu Li the prime minister. The reason was that he planned to unite with Qin.
summary: Later, Lord Mengchang became Qi's prime minister and planned to attack Qin with Han and Wei. Su Dai advised him to avoid strengthening Han and Wei, instead using the Western Zhou to negotiate with Qin for Chu's eastern territory and the release of King Huai of Chu. Lord Mengchang agreed, averting war. When dismissed as prime minister due to slander, he retired to Xue Yi. After Qin's general Lu Li became Qi's prime minister, Lord Mengchang, following Su Dai's advice, marched north to secure alliances, causing Lu Li to flee. When King Qi Min grew proud and sought to eliminate him, Lord Mengchang fled to Wei, became prime minister, and allied with Qin and Zhao to attack Qi, leading to King Min's death. King Xiang of Qi later reconciled with Lord Mengchang, who remained neutral among the states. After his death, his sons fought over the title, and Qi and Wei destroyed Xue Yi, ending his lineage.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传

translation:
When Lord Mengchang heard that Feng Chen had burned the deed, he was very angry and immediately sent someone to recall Feng Chen.
As soon as Feng Chen arrived, Lord Mengchang asked: "I have three thousand diners, so I lend money in Xue Yi."
My fiefdom is small to begin with, but the people still do not repay the interest on time, and the guests are afraid that they will not have enough to eat, so I asked you, sir, to collect the debts.
I heard that after receiving the money, my husband held a banquet of wine and meat and burned the deed. Why is this?
Feng Xuan replied: Yes.
If there is no way to gather all the debtors together without throwing a feast of wine and meat, there will be no way to know who is rich and who is poor.
If he is wealthy, he will be given a set date to repay his debts.
The poor will not be able to repay their debts even if they are detained for ten years. The longer the time, the higher the interest.
If you are too hasty, they will not be able to repay you in the end. On the one hand, you will be thought to be greedy for small profits and not caring for the people. On the other hand, the people will have a reputation of abandoning the emperor and relying on debts. This is not a way to encourage scholars and people and show your reputation.
I burned the useless IOUs and discarded the nominal account books to make the common people of Xue Yi trust you and promote your good reputation for kindness. What else do you have to doubt?
After hearing this, Lord Mengchang clapped his hands and thanked him repeatedly.
The King of Qi was bewitched by the slanderous remarks of Qin and Chu, and believed that Lord Mengchang's reputation was higher than his own and that he would monopolize the power of Qi, so he dismissed Lord Mengchang from his official position.
When the guests saw that Lord Mengchang had been dismissed, they all left him.
Only Feng Xuan planned for him and said: Lend me a car and let me go to Qin. I will definitely make you more prominent in Qi and your city will be wider. Do you think it's okay?
So Mengchangjun prepared a carriage and gifts to send Feng Xuan on the road.
Feng Chen then drove west to the state of Qin to lobby the king of Qin, saying: All lobbyists in the world who drive west to the state of Qin all want to make Qin strong and make Qi weak; everyone who rides east to enter the state of Qi all want to make Qi strong and make Qin weak.
These are two countries with no distinction between superior and inferior. It is impossible for them to stand side by side and dominate. The one who dominates can unify the world.
The King of Qin was fascinated by what he heard. He straightened up and knelt down and asked Feng Xuan: "What do you think should be done to prevent Qin from becoming a weak country?"
Feng Chen replied: Your Majesty also knows that the State of Qi has dismissed Lord Mengchang from his position, right?
King Qin said: I heard about this.
Feng Xuan said: The person who made Qi respected by the world was Lord Mengchang.
Now that the king of Qi has listened to the slander and dismissed Lord Mengchang, Lord Mengchang is extremely resentful and will definitely betray Qi. If he betrays Qi and enters Qin, then the national conditions of Qi and the situation in the court, from the king to the officials, will be under the control of Qin.
You will get the entire land of Qi, and you will be more than just the hero! Hurry up and send an envoy with gifts to meet Lord Mengchang secretly. Don't miss this opportunity.
If King Qi comes to his senses and appoints Lord Mengchang again, then it is impossible to predict who will win or lose.
The King of Qin was very happy after hearing this, and sent ten carriages carrying a hundred yi gold to meet Lord Mengchang.
Feng Xuan said goodbye to the King of Qin and rushed to the State of Qi ahead of the envoy. When he arrived at the State of Qi, he persuaded the King of Qi: The lobbyists from all over the world who drive east to Qi State all want to make Qi strong and make Qin weak; those who ride west to Qin State all want to make Qin strong and make Qi weak.
Qin and Qi are equally superior and inferior. If Qin is strong, Qi must be weak. These two countries will inevitably not be able to dominate at the same time.
Now I heard privately that the Qin State has sent an envoy with ten carriages carrying a hundred yi gold to greet Lord Mengchang.
It's fine if Lord Mengchang doesn't go west. If he goes west and serves as the prime minister of Qin, then the world will belong to Qin. If Qin becomes the lord, Qi will have no choice but to succumb to it. Then Linzi and Jimo will be in danger.
Why didn't the king quickly restore Mengchang to his official position and increase his fiefdom to apologize to him before the Qin envoy arrived?
If this is done, Lord Mengchang will be happy and willing to accept it.
Although Qin is a powerful country, how can it arbitrarily go to other countries to welcome other people's prime ministers?
It is necessary to thwart Qin's conspiracy and cut off its plan to seek strength and hegemony.
After hearing this, King Qi immediately understood and said: OK.
So he sent people to the border to wait for the Qin envoy.
As soon as the Qin envoy's car entered the Qi border, the Qi envoy at the border immediately changed his car and drove back to report the situation. The King of Qi recalled Mengchang Jun and restored his position as prime minister. At the same time, he also gave him the land of the original fiefdom and added a thousand households to him.
When the envoy from Qin heard that Lord Mengchang had restored his position as prime minister of Qi, he changed his carriage and went back.
Since the King of Qi dismissed Lord Mengchang because of the slander, all the guests have left him.
Later, the King of Qi recalled and restored Lord Mengchang to his official position, and Feng Chen went to greet him.
summary: Feng Chen, a poor scholar, joined Lord Mengchang's household. Initially placed in low-class quarters, he sang about lacking fish, a carriage, and means to support his family, prompting Lord Mengchang to upgrade his status. When Lord Mengchang needed to collect debts in Xue Yi, Feng Chen was sent. Instead of collecting, he burned the deeds of the poor, arguing that this would earn the people's trust and enhance Lord Mengchang's reputation. Though initially angry, Lord Mengchang later thanked him. When Lord Mengchang was dismissed as prime minister, his guests abandoned him. Feng Chen went to Qin, convincing King Zhao to send gifts to recruit Lord Mengchang. He then urged King Qi to restore Lord Mengchang's position before the Qin envoy arrived, which King Qi did. When Lord Mengchang expressed bitterness toward his former guests, Feng Chen explained that people naturally flock to the wealthy and abandon the poor, advising him to forgive them. Lord Mengchang accepted this counsel.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传

translation:
Before arriving in the capital, Mengchang Jun sighed deeply and said: I always like to make friends with guests and take care of people. I never dare to be rude when receiving guests. There are more than 3,000 diners, as you know, sir.
As soon as the guests saw that I was dismissed from office, they all turned their backs on me and left. No one cared about me.
Now that I have been restored to my position as prime minister thanks to my husband, how can those departing guests have the dignity to see me again?
If anyone sees me again, I will spit on his face and humiliate him severely.
After hearing these words, Feng Xuan stopped the reins, got off the car and bowed.
Mr. Mengchang also immediately got out of the car and returned the courtesy, saying: Sir, are you apologizing for those guests?
Feng Xuan said: I'm not apologizing for the guests, it's because your words were wrong.
Generally speaking, everything has its inevitable end, and everything in the world has its routine. Do you understand the meaning of this sentence?
Lord Mengchang said: I don’t understand what you mean.
Feng Xuan said: All living things will die at some point. This is the inevitable result of living things. Rich people have many guests, while poor people have few friends. This is how it is.
Don't you see people rushing to the market?
At dawn, people crowded into the market, squaring their shoulders to get in; after sunset, people passing by the market waved their arms without even looking back.
It's not that people like morning and hate evening, but because what they expected is no longer available in the East and West markets.
Now that you have lost your official position and all your guests have left, you cannot resent your guests and cut off their access to you.
I hope you treat your guests like you used to.
Lord Mengchang bowed down twice and said, "I respectfully follow your advice."
Listen to your teacher, do you dare to accept instruction without respect?
Tai Shigong said: I once passed through Xuedi, where the folk customs were very different from those in Zoudi and Lu.
I asked the people there what was the reason for this, and they said: Lord Mengchang once attracted many righteous people from all over the world, and there were probably more than 60,000 people who violated laws and regulations and entered Xuedi alone.
It is said that Mr. Mengchang was very proud of his pleasure in entertaining guests, and his reputation was indeed well-deserved.
summary: Sima Qian noted that Xue's unique customs stemmed from Lord Mengchang's hospitality, which attracted over sixty thousand lawbreakers, affirming his well-deserved reputation for entertaining guests.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/孟尝君列传

translation:
Ji Bu was from the Chu region. He was ambitious and chivalrous, and was very famous in the Chu region.
Xiang Yu sent him to lead the army, which embarrassed Liu Bang, the king of Han, many times.
After Xiang Yu's death, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty offered a thousand gold reward for Ji Bu's capture, and ordered anyone who dared to harbor Ji Bu to be punished for his crime.
Ji Bu hid in the home of a family named Zhou in Puyang.
The Zhou family said: It is very urgent that the Han Dynasty offers a reward for your capture. The tracking and search will come to my house. General, if you can obey my words, I will dare to give you a plan; if not, I would rather commit suicide first.
Ji Bu agreed to him.
The Zhou family then shaved off Ji Bu's hair, tied his neck with an iron hoop, put him in coarse cloth, put him in a cart, and sold him to the Zhu family of Lu, along with dozens of Zhou family's slaves.
The Zhu family knew in their hearts that it was Jibu, so they bought it and put it in the fields for farming. They also warned his son: "Everything about farming in the fields must be obeyed by this slave, and he must eat the same food as him."
The Zhu family took a light carriage to Luoyang and paid a visit to Ruyin Marquis Teng Gong.
Duke Teng left the Zhu family to drink for several days.
The Zhu family took the opportunity to ask Duke Teng: What serious crime did Ji Bu commit that made the emperor so eager to pursue him?
Teng Gong said: Ji Bu embarrassed the emperor many times on behalf of Xiang Yu. The emperor resented him, so he had to catch him before he could rest.
Zhu Jia said: What kind of person do you think Ji Bu is?
Teng Gong said: He is a talented person.
The Zhu family said: Each minister is sent by his master, and Ji Bu is sent by Xiang Yu. This is entirely within the scope of his official duties.
Can Xiang Yu's ministers be killed all?
Now that the emperor has just conquered the world, why should he show his narrowness to the world when he pursues a person based solely on his personal resentment?
Moreover, because of Ji Bu's talents, the Han Dynasty pursued him so urgently that he would either flee north to the Huns or south to Yue.
This behavior of hating the warriors and going to support the enemy country was the reason why Wu Zixu wanted to whip the body of King Ping of Chu.
Why don't you look for an opportunity to explain it to the emperor?
Teng Gong, the Marquis of Ruyin, knew that the Zhu family was a great knight, and guessed that Ji Bu must be hiding in his place, so he agreed and said, "Okay."
Teng Gong waited for the opportunity and reported to the emperor exactly what the Zhu family wanted.
The emperor then pardoned Ji Bu.
At this time, many famous people praised Ji Bu for his ability to turn toughness into suppleness, and the Zhu family became famous at that time.
Later, Ji Bu was summoned by the emperor to plead guilty, and the emperor appointed him as a doctor.
During the reign of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, Ji Bu served as Zhonglang General.
Chanyu, the king of the Huns, once wrote a letter to insult Empress Lu and made rude remarks. Empress Lu was very angry and summoned all the generals to discuss the matter.
General Fan Kuai said: I am willing to lead 100,000 troops to sweep away the Xiongnu.
All the generals catered to Empress Lu's wishes and said in unison: "Okay."
Ji Bu said: Fan Kuai really deserves to be beheaded!
Back then, Emperor Gao led an army of 400,000 people and was besieged in Pingcheng. How could Fan Kuai sweep the Xiongnu with 100,000 troops now? This is lying to your face!
Besides, it was precisely because the Qin Dynasty used troops against the Huns that Chen Sheng and others rebelled.
Until now, the wound has not been cured, and Fan Kuai flatters him in person, hoping to make the world uneasy.
At this time, the generals in the palace were frightened, so Queen Lu retreated from the court and finally stopped talking about attacking the Xiongnu.
Ji Bu became the governor of Hedong County. During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, some people said that he was very talented, so the Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty summoned him and planned to appoint him as the imperial censor.
summary: Ji Bu, a man from Chu known for his ambition and chivalry, served under Xiang Yu and frequently embarrassed Liu Bang, the King of Han. After Xiang Yu's death, Emperor Gaozu of Han offered a thousand gold for Ji Bu's capture and punished anyone who harbored him. Ji Bu hid with the Zhou family in Puyang, who shaved his head, bound him with an iron hoop, and sold him as a slave to the Zhu family of Lu. The Zhu family, recognizing Ji Bu, treated him well and arranged for him to work in the fields. Zhu Jia then visited Ruyin Marquis Teng Gong in Luoyang, persuading him that pursuing Ji Bu out of personal resentment would harm the emperor's reputation and potentially drive Ji Bu to flee to the Huns or Yue. Teng Gong relayed this to the emperor, who pardoned Ji Bu. Ji Bu was later appointed as a doctor and served as Zhonglang General under Emperor Hui. When the Xiongnu insulted Empress Lu, General Fan Kuai proposed a military campaign, but Ji Bu condemned him, citing past failures and the risk of unrest, leading Empress Lu to abandon the plan. Ji Bu became Governor of Hedong County. During Emperor Wen's reign, he was summoned for a potential promotion but was sent back due to slander. Ji Bu criticized the emperor for being swayed by praise and slander, embarrassing him. A Chu man named Cao Qiu, known for rhetoric, sought Ji Bu's favor despite initial rejection. Ji Bu eventually welcomed him after Cao Qiu praised his reputation, and Cao Qiu helped spread Ji Bu's fame. Ji Bu's brother Ji Xin was also renowned for bravery and chivalry. Ji Bu's uncle Ding Gong, a former Chu general, was executed by Emperor Gaozu for disloyalty. Luan Bu, a friend of Liang King Peng Yue, was captured after Peng Yue's execution for treason. Luan Bu mourned Peng Yue publicly, was arrested, and faced execution. He defended Peng Yue's loyalty, arguing that his death was unjust, and was pardoned by the emperor, later becoming a general and prime minister. Luan Bu died in the fifth year of Emperor Jing's reign. Sima Qian commented that Ji Bu's endurance of humiliation to achieve greatness made him a famous Han general, while Luan Bu's willingness to die for righteousness surpassed even ancient heroes.

translation:
Qu Yuan, named Ping, has the same surname as the Chu king's family.
Served as the left disciple of King Huai of Chu.
Qu Yuan was well-informed, had a strong memory, understood the principles of national stability and turmoil, and was good at rhetoric.
When Qu Yuan was at court, he discussed state affairs with King Huai of Chu in order to issue orders; when outside the court, he received guests and dealt with the affairs of the marquis.
King Huai of Chu trusted him very much.
The official Shangguan had the same position as Qu Yuan. In order to gain the favor of King Huai, he was very jealous of Qu Yuan's talents.
Once, King Huai ordered Qu Yuan to formulate a national law. Qu Yuan had just finished writing the draft but had not yet completed the final revision.
When Shangguan saw it, he wanted to take it for himself, but Qu Yuan refused to give it to him. He spoke ill of Qu Yuan to King Huai of Chu: Your Majesty, you asked Qu Yuan to make a decree. No one at the top or bottom did not know about it. Every time a decree was issued, Qu Yuan boasted of his achievements, saying that no one could make it except me.
King Huai was very angry after hearing this, so he alienated Qu Yuan.
Qu Yuan felt extremely sad that King Huai was unable to distinguish right from wrong, that his vision was blinded by flatterers and unable to distinguish truth from falsehood, that evil harmed justice, and that upright people were not tolerated by the court. Therefore, he wrote "Li Sao" with deep sorrow and deep thought.
The so-called "Li Sao" means encountering sorrow.
God is the origin of man; parents are the foundation of man.
When people are in a difficult situation, they have to remember their roots. Therefore, when the fatigue and hardship are extreme, there is no one who does not call God; when the pain is unbearable, there is no one who does not call for the parents.
Qu Yuan insisted on notarization, acted upright, was loyal to the king, and used his talents to the best of his ability. However, he was provoked by villains, and his situation could be said to be extremely embarrassing.
How can one not feel grief and indignation when one is doubted by the king because one is sincere for the country, and one is slandered by villains because one is loyal to the master?
Qu Yuan wrote "Li Sao" precisely to express this feeling of grief and indignation.
Although "The Book of Songs: Guofeng" contains many works describing the love between men and women, it is not chaotic; although "The Book of Songs: Xiaoya" reveals the people's slander and resentment against the government, it does not advocate open rebellion. Qu Yuan's "Li Sao" can be said to have the advantages of both.
In "Li Sao", Qu Yuan traced the deeds of Emperor Ku upwards, praised Qi Huan's great achievements in modern times, and described the virtues of Shang Tang and Zhou Wu in the middle to criticize current affairs.
It explains the breadth and depth of moral content and the inevitable cause and effect of the rise and fall of ordering chaos. These are all explained in great detail.
Its language is simple and concise, but its content has profound meanings, its emotions are noble, and its conduct is honest. Although its sentences are about small things, its meaning is extremely grand and profound. Although the examples it cites are common examples, the meaning they entrust is extremely far-reaching.
His emotions are noble, so he likes to use vanilla as a metaphor.
His character was upright, so he would not relax his demands on himself even until his death.
Being able to be washed clean in the muddy water is like a cicada being able to be freed from the turbidity and filth. It floats outside the dust and is not stained by the turbidity of the world. It is pure and noble, emerging from the mud without being stained.
Inferring his noble emotions, it is appropriate to compete with the sun and the moon.
summary: Qu Yuan, named Ping, shared the same surname as the Chu royal family and served as a left disciple under King Huai of Chu. He was knowledgeable, had a strong memory, understood statecraft, and was skilled in rhetoric. King Huai trusted him deeply, but the official Shangguan, jealous of Qu Yuan's talents, slandered him by claiming Qu Yuan boasted about his own decrees. King Huai believed this and alienated Qu Yuan. Grief-stricken by the king's inability to discern truth from falsehood, Qu Yuan wrote "Li Sao," a work expressing his sorrow and indignation. The text praises "Li Sao" for combining the virtues of "The Book of Songs: Guofeng" and "Xiaoya," using metaphors like vanilla to symbolize noble character, and comparing Qu Yuan's purity to the sun and moon.

translation:
Qu Yuan had been demoted. After that, Qin planned to attack Qi, and Qi and Chu joined forces to have a blind date. King Qin Hui was worried about this, so he sent Zhang Yi to pretend to leave Qin and bring rich gifts to serve Chu. He said: Qin hates Qi very much.
King Huai of Chu greedily listened to Zhang Yi's words, broke off diplomatic relations with Qi, and sent envoys to Qin to accept the land.
Zhang Yi deceived the envoy of the Chu State and said: I, Zhang Yi, agreed with King Huai of Chu to be six miles, but I have never heard of six hundred miles.
The Chu envoy left Qin angrily and returned to report to King Huai of Chu.
King Huai of Chu was angry and raised troops to attack Qin.
The Qin State sent troops to attack the Chu army, and defeated the Chu army in the Danshui and Xishui areas. It killed 80,000 Chu soldiers, captured the Chu general Qu, and took advantage of the situation to seize the Hanzhong area of ​​the Chu state.
King Huai of Chu dispatched all the troops from across the country to attack Qin and fought in Lantian.
When Wei heard the news, he sent troops to attack Chu and penetrated as far as Deng Yi.
The Chu army was frightened, so they withdrew from Qin and returned home.
However, the state of Qi finally refused to rescue the state of Chu because of anger, and the state of Chu was in great distress.
The next year, Qin proposed to cede the land in Hanzhong to make peace with Chu, but King Huai of Chu said: I don't want to get the land, I just want Zhang Yi and I will be content.
When Zhang Yi heard this, he said: "I, Zhang Yi, can come to Hanzhong and ask the king to allow me to go to Chu."
After Zhang Yi arrived in Chu State, he gave generous gifts to Jin Shang, the powerful minister of Chu State, and used sweet words to deceive King Huai's concubine Zheng Xiu. King Huai actually listened to Zheng Xiu's words and let Zhang Yi run away again.
At this time, Qu Yuan had been alienated and no longer held important official positions. He had just been sent as an envoy to Qi State. After returning, he admonished King Huai and said: Your Majesty, why don't you kill Zhang Yi?
King Huai felt very regretful and sent people to chase him, but it was too late.
After that, all the vassal states jointly attacked the Chu State, defeated the Chu army, and killed the Chu general Tang Wei.
At that time, King Zhao of Qin was married to Chu and wanted to meet King Huai of Chu. King Huai of Chu wanted to go. Qu Yuan advised him: Qin is a greedy and violent country like tigers and wolves. It cannot be trusted, so it is better not to go.
But King Huai's youngest son Zilan persuaded King Huai to go, saying: "Why do you want to cut off King Qin's good intentions?"
King Huai finally went.
But as soon as he entered Wuguan, the Qin Dynasty's ambush cut off his return and detained King Huai in order to make him agree to cede the land.
King Huai was furious and refused to agree.
He fled to the State of Zhao, but the State of Zhao refused to accept him.
Then he came to the State of Qin and finally died in the State of Qin. His body was transported back to the State of Chu for burial.
King Huai's eldest son, King Qingxiang, succeeded to the throne and appointed his younger brother Zilan as Ling Yin.
Zilan persuaded King Huai to enter Qin and eventually died in Qin. People in Chu blamed Zilan for this.
Qu Yuan also hated Zilan very much for what he did. Although he was exiled, he was still attached to the Kingdom of Chu, missed King Huai, and always thought about returning to the court. He always hoped that the king would suddenly wake up and change his bad customs.
He always remembered the king, revived the country, and reversed the situation, so he expressed this feeling many times in a work.
However, there was nothing he could do, so it was impossible to return to the court. This also shows that King Huai did not wake up in the end.
As a king, no matter he is smart or stupid, talented or not, he hopes to find loyal ministers and wise men to assist him in governing the country. However, the destruction of the country and the destruction of the family continue to happen, but the sage king and the peaceful country have not been seen for many generations. The fundamental reason is that the so-called loyal ministers are not loyal, and the so-called wise men are not wise.
Because King Huai did not know the duties of a loyal minister, he was deceived by Zheng Xiu internally and deceived by Zhang Yi externally. He alienated Qu Yuan and trusted Shangguan officials and Ling Yin Zilan.
As a result, the army was defeated miserably, the country was invaded, and the territory of six counties was lost. He also lived in a foreign country, died in Qin, and was ridiculed by the people of the world.
summary: After Qu Yuan's demotion, Qin, fearing the Qi-Chu alliance, sent Zhang Yi to deceive Chu. King Huai, swayed by greed, broke ties with Qi and was tricked into believing Qin would cede six hundred miles of land, only to receive six. Enraged, King Huai attacked Qin but suffered a devastating defeat, losing 80,000 soldiers and the Hanzhong region. Wei also attacked Chu, and Qi refused aid. Later, Qin proposed peace, but King Huai demanded Zhang Yi. Zhang Yi bribed Chu officials and King Huai's concubine, Zheng Xiu, to secure his release. Qu Yuan, then an envoy to Qi, urged King Huai to kill Zhang Yi, but it was too late. Subsequently, vassal states defeated Chu, killing General Tang Wei. King Zhao of Qin invited King Huai for a meeting; Qu Yuan warned against it, but King Huai's son Zilan persuaded him to go. King Huai was captured, refused to cede land, fled to Zhao (which rejected him), and died in Qin. His body was returned to Chu. King Qingxiang succeeded King Huai and appointed Zilan as Ling Yin. Qu Yuan, exiled but still loyal, blamed Zilan for King Huai's death and hoped for reform. However, Zilan and Shangguan slandered Qu Yuan to King Qingxiang, leading to his banishment. Qu Yuan wandered by the river, disheveled and gaunt. A fisherman asked why he was exiled; Qu Yuan replied that he alone was pure in a corrupt world. The fisherman advised adapting to the times, but Qu Yuan refused to taint his integrity, preferring to die in the river. He wrote "Huaisha," expressing his resolve to maintain his principles despite injustice. He then drowned himself in the Miluo River.

translation:
I am rough on the outside but simple on the inside, but no one knows my brilliance. The uncarved material was thrown away, and no one knew the wisdom and virtue I possessed.
I pay attention to the cultivation of benevolence and righteousness, and strengthen it with respect and loyalty. Yu Shun will never be seen again, and who knows that I can calmly persist in my ambition.
It is rare for ancient sages to be born in the same world. Who can understand the reason?
Shang Tang and Xia Yu are so far away from us now. It is so vast and boundless that it is difficult to catch up.
Suppress your grief and anger, suppress your heart and make yourself stronger. I will not change my original intention despite suffering. I just hope that my ambition will become an example for future generations to follow.
I followed the road north again, facing the fading sunlight. Containing melancholy and forcing a happy face, death is not far ahead.
Epilogue: The mighty Yuanjiang and Xiangjiang rivers are constantly flowing and surging with waves.
The road is long and dark, and the future is so unclear.
I keep singing with long-lasting sadness, sighing with emotion to end this life.
No one in the world understands me. Who can listen to my heart?
The sentiment is noble, the quality is beautiful, and the fragrance is pure and unparalleled in the world.
Bole has died a long time ago. Who can identify the Chollima horse as Junliang?
Life is a destiny, and everyone has different arrangements.
With a firm heart and a broad mind, there is nothing else to be afraid of!
Heavy sadness and long sigh, sighing and mourning forever.
The world is turbid and there are few close friends. People's hearts are unpredictable and difficult to guess.
You must die in this world, so don't cherish your own life too much. Tell this clearly to the world, gentlemen, that I will always be a role model for others.
So Qu Yuan threw himself into the Miluo River with stones in his arms and committed suicide.
After Qu Yuan's death, there were Song Yu, Tang Le, Jing Cha and others in the Chu State. They all loved literature and were famous for their good poetry and poetry. But they all only learned the euphemistic and implicit side of Qu Yuan's speech, and in the end no one dared to express his advice as bluntly as Qu Yuan did.
After that, the Chu State became weaker and weaker day by day, and was finally eliminated by the Qin State decades later.
More than a hundred years after Qu Yuan sank into the river and died, there was a man named Jia Sheng in the Han Dynasty who passed by the Xiang River when he was serving as the Prince of Changsha. He wrote a poem and threw it into the river to pay homage to Qu Yuan.
Jia Sheng's name is Jia Yi, and he is from Luoyang.
At the age of eighteen, he became famous locally for reciting poetry and writing articles.
When Wu Tingwei was serving as the governor of Henan County, he heard that Jia Yicai had excellent academic performance, so he summoned him to serve in the Yamen and regarded him very highly.
When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he heard that Wu Gong, the governor of Henan Province, had outstanding political achievements and was ranked first in the country. He was from the same hometown as Li Si and had learned from Li Si, so he recruited him as a court captain.
Wu Tingwei recommended that Jia Yi was young and talented, and could be proficient in the knowledge of hundreds of schools of thought.
In this way, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty recruited Jia Yi to serve as a doctor.
At that time, Jia Yi was more than 20 years old and the youngest among the Ph.D.
summary: After Qu Yuan's death, Chu scholars like Song Yu imitated his style but lacked his boldness. Chu weakened and was conquered by Qin decades later. Over a century later, Jia Yi of the Han Dynasty, while serving as Grand Tutor of Changsha, wrote a poem to honor Qu Yuan. Jia Yi, a talented young scholar from Luoyang, was favored by Emperor Wen of Han but slandered by officials like Zhou Bo, leading to his demotion. He wrote "Ode to the Birds" to console himself, reflecting on the cyclical nature of fortune and the futility of worldly concerns. Later, he served as tutor to King Liang Huai, who died in a riding accident. Jia Yi, blaming himself, died of grief at age 33. The historian Sima Qian, after reading Qu Yuan's works and Jia Yi's poems, initially criticized Qu Yuan for not seeking refuge elsewhere but later, after reading "Ode to the Birds," understood his equanimity toward life and death.

translation:
Zhao Sheng, Lord of Pingyuan, was a young master of the State of Zhao.
Among the many princes, Zhao Sheng was the most virtuous and talented. He was hospitable and cultivated scholars. There were about thousands of guests who came to his sect.
Lord Pingyuan served as the prime minister of King Zhao Huiwen and King Xiaocheng. He left the position of prime minister three times and was reinstated three times. His fiefdom was in Dongwu City.
Mr. Pingyuan's house has a tall building facing the houses below.
There was a lame man in the house who always limped out to fetch water.
A beautiful concubine of Mr. Pingyuan lived upstairs. One day she looked down and saw the lame man fetching water, and she burst out laughing.
The next day, the cripple came to Lord Pingyuan's house and asked: "I heard that you love scholars. The reason why scholars are not afraid of traveling thousands of miles to join your family is because you value scholars and despise concubines."
I was unfortunately ill and disabled, but your concubine was laughing at me from a high building. I wanted to get the head of the person who laughed at me. Mr. Pingyuan smiled and replied: "Okay."
After the lame man left, Lord Pingyuan smiled again and said: Look at this boy, he wants to kill my concubine just because of a smile. Isn't it too much?
I didn't kill that person after all.
More than a year later, more than half of the guests and diners on errands left one after another.
Mr. Pingyuan felt very strange about this situation and said: I, Zhao Sheng, never dare to be rude in all aspects of my treatment of gentlemen, but why are so many people leaving me?
A retainer stepped forward and replied: Because you did not kill the concubine who laughed at the cripple, everyone thought that you liked beauty and despised the scholars, so the scholars left one after another.
So Lord Pingyuan cut off the head of the concubine who laughed at the cripple. He personally visited the lame man's house and offered it to him, and took the opportunity to apologize to him.
From then on, the original guests came back one after another.
At that time, Qi State had Lord Mengchang, Wei State had Lord Xinling, and Chu State had Lord Chunshen. They were all hospitable to scholars, so they competed to be more courteous to scholars than others in order to attract more talents to themselves.
When the Qin State besieged Handan, King Zhao sent Lord Pingyuan to ask for help. At that time, he planned to recommend Chu as the leader of the alliance and make a joint alliance to fight against Qin. Lord Pingyuan agreed to go to Chu State with twenty of his followers who were brave, resourceful, and capable of both civil and military affairs.
Mr. Pingyuan said: It would be best if we can succeed through polite negotiations.
If the negotiation fails to succeed, then the king of Chu will be coerced to confirm the alliance in public, and he must confirm the alliance before returning home.
The civil and military people who are going with me don’t have to look outside. It’s enough to choose from the diners under my sect.
In the end, nineteen people were selected, and there was nothing left to choose from. There was no way to gather twenty people.
At this time, a man named Mao Sui among the diners walked up to the front and recommended himself to Lord Pingyuan: I heard that you are going to Chu State, and let Chu State be the leader of the alliance to make an alliance. You also agreed to go with twenty diners, and no one will go outside to search.
There is still one person missing now, I hope you can use me to recharge and go together.
Mr. Pingyuan asked: How many years has it been since Mr. Wang stayed with me?
Mao Sui replied: It has been three years now.
Mr. Pingyuan said: A talented wise man living in the world is like an awl placed in a pocket, its sharp edge will be revealed immediately.
It has been three years since your husband has been under my care for three years now. None of my close ministers have ever praised or recommended you, and I have never heard of you. This is because your husband has no expertise.
Sir, you can't go. Sir, please stay.
summary: Zhao Sheng, Lord of Pingyuan, was a virtuous and talented young master of the State of Zhao, known for hosting thousands of scholars. He served as prime minister under Kings Huiwen and Xiaocheng, leaving and returning to the position three times, with his fief in Dongwu City. A crippled man fetching water near his home was laughed at by one of Lord Pingyuan’s concubines. The cripple demanded her head, but Lord Pingyuan initially refused, causing many scholars to leave. He later killed the concubine and apologized to the cripple, regaining his guests.
