translation:
Mao Sui said: I just want to put it in my pocket today.
If I had been placed in the pocket, the entire cone would have been exposed, not just the tip.
Lord Pingyuan finally agreed to let Mao Sui go with him.
The nineteen people winked at each other and laughed at Mao Sui secretly, but did not make a sound.
When Mao Sui arrived in Chu, he discussed and argued with the nineteen people about the situation in the world. All nineteen people admired him.
The Lord of Pingyuan negotiated with the King of Chu to establish a joint alliance. They repeatedly stated their interests. They negotiated from morning until noon until no decision was made. The nineteen people encouraged Mao Sui and said: "Sir, please come to the court."
So Mao Sui gripped the hilt of his sword tightly, trotted all the way up the steps to the palace, and said to Lord Pingyuan: Talking about cooperation is either beneficial or harmful, just two sentences.
Now we have been talking about the marriage since the morning, but by noon we still can’t decide. What’s the reason?
When the King of Chu saw Mao Sui coming to the court, he said to Lord Pingyuan: "What does this man do?"
Lord Pingyuan replied: "This is my retainer."
The King of Chu shouted sternly: "Why don't you let me go down?"
I'm negotiating with your master, what are you doing here?
Mao Sui clenched the hilt of his sword and stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty, you dare to scold me, but you are relying on the large number of people in Chu."
Now I am only ten steps away from you. Within ten steps, the king cannot rely on the large number of people in Chu. The king's life is in my hands.
My master is right in front of me. Why are you scolding me like this in front of him?
Moreover, I heard that Shang Tang once ruled the world with a land of seventy miles, and King Wen of Zhou made the world surrender with a land of a hundred miles. Is it because they had many soldiers? In fact, it was because they were good at grasping the situation and exerting their power.
Nowadays, the Chu State has a territory of 5,000 miles and millions of soldiers. This is the capital it relies on to strive for kingship and hegemony.
With the Chu State being so powerful, no one in the world could stop its power.
Bai Qi of the Qin State was just a child. With tens of thousands of troops, he sent troops to fight against the Chu State. In the first battle, he captured Yancheng and Yingdu, in the second battle, he burned Yiling, and in the third battle, the king's ancestors were greatly humiliated.
This is a hatred that has lasted for centuries in the Chu Kingdom. Even King Zhao felt ashamed, but the king did not feel ashamed.
The alliance alliance is for the Chu State, not for the Zhao State.
My master is right in front of me, why are you scolding me like this?
After hearing Mao Sui's words, the King of Chu immediately changed his attitude and said: Yes, yes, it is indeed as the gentleman said. I will do my best to fulfill the alliance covenant.
Mao Sui pressed further and asked: Is the alliance agreement confirmed?
King Chu replied: "It's confirmed."
So Mao Sui said to the king of Chu's ministers in a commanding tone: "Bring the blood of chickens, dogs, and horses."
Mao Sui knelt down with the copper plate in his hands, presented it to the King of Chu and said: Your Majesty, you should suck the blood first to show your sincerity in confirming the alliance. The next one is my master, and the next one is me.
In this way, the alliance alliance was confirmed in the palace of Chu State.
At this time, Mao Sui held up a plate of blood with his left hand and called to the nineteen people with his right hand: "Everyone in the audience will also suck the blood from the plate. Although you are mediocre, you have completed your task. This is what is called relying on the strength of others to complete your task."
summary: When Qin besieged Handan, Lord Pingyuan sought help from Chu to form an alliance. He needed twenty followers but could only find nineteen. Mao Sui, a retainer for three years, volunteered. Lord Pingyuan doubted his abilities, but Mao Sui argued that if placed in a pocket, the entire awl would show, not just its tip. Mao Sui joined and impressed the others. In Chu, negotiations stalled until Mao Sui confronted the King of Chu, threatening him and highlighting Chu’s past defeats by Qin. The king agreed to the alliance, and Mao Sui sealed it with a blood oath. Lord Pingyuan later praised Mao Sui as more powerful than an army.

translation:
Lord Pingyuan confirmed the alliance and returned to Zhao State. After returning to Zhao State, he said: I don't dare to observe and identify talents anymore.
When I observe and identify talents, I say thousands at most and hundreds at least. I thought I would not miss out on all the talented people in the world, but now I have missed Mr. Mao.
Mr. Mao's first visit to the Chu State made the status of the Zhao State more noble than the national treasure of Jiuding Dalu.
Mr. Mao, with his eloquent mouth, was actually more powerful than an army of millions.
I no longer dare to observe and identify talents.
So he treated Mao Sui as a distinguished guest.
After Lord Pingyuan returned to the State of Zhao, the State of Chu sent Lord Chunshen to lead troops to rescue Zhao State. Lord Xinling of Wei State also pretended to ask for his orders and seized the military power of Jin Bi to lead troops to rescue State of Zhao, but none of them arrived yet.
At this time, Qin State quickly besieged Handan. Handan was in a hurry and was about to surrender. Lord Pingyuan was extremely anxious.
Li Tong, the son of an official at the Handan Hotel, persuaded Lord Pingyuan: "Aren't you worried about the demise of Zhao?"
Lord Pingyuan said: If Zhao is destroyed, then I will be a prisoner. Why not worry?
Li Tong said: "The people of Handan are using human bones as firewood and exchanging children for food. It can be said that they are in extreme danger. However, you have hundreds of concubines and maids in your harem. The maids wear silk embroidered clothes and cannot eat the fine food. However, the people are unable to cover themselves with coarse shorts and cannot eat enough wine dregs and grain husks."
The people are tired and their weapons are exhausted. Some people sharpen wood to use as spears and arrows, but your precious playthings, copper bells and jade, are still intact.
If the Qin army breaks Zhao, how can you have these things?
If the State of Zhao can be preserved, why would you worry about not having these things?
Now you can really order all the members below the wife to be organized into the soldiers, and they will be responsible for the labor of guarding the city, and distribute all the things in the house for the soldiers to enjoy. When the soldiers are in crisis and hardship, it is easy to be grateful.
So Pingyuan Jun adopted Li Tong's advice and got 3,000 soldiers who dared to risk their lives.
Li Tong joined a team of 3,000 people and rushed to the Qin army for a decisive battle. As a result, the Qin army was pushed back thirty miles.
At this time, it happened that reinforcements from Chu and Wei arrived, and the Qin army withdrew, and Handan was preserved.
Li Tong was killed in battle with the Qin army, and his father was granted the title of Marquis Li.
Yu Qing wanted to request additional fiefdoms for Lord Pingyuan on the grounds that Lord Xinling sent troops to save Zhao and saved Handan.
When Gongsun Long heard the news, he drove overnight to see Lord Pingyuan and said: I heard that Yu Qing wanted to ask for additional fiefs on your behalf on the grounds that Lord Xinling sent troops to save Zhao and saved Handan. Is this true?
Mr. Pingyuan replied: Yes.
Gongsun Long said: This is very inappropriate.
It is said that the monarch appointed you as the prime minister of Zhao State, not because your intelligence and talent are unique to Zhao State and no one else has them.
The title of Dongwu City is granted to you not because of your meritorious deeds, but because you are a close relative of the monarch.
summary: After returning, Chu and Wei sent reinforcements, but Handan remained in danger. Li Tong advised Lord Pingyuan to mobilize his household and distribute resources to the people, gaining 3,000 volunteers. Li Tong died in battle, pushing Qin back thirty miles, and Handan was saved when reinforcements arrived. Yu Qing sought additional fiefs for Lord Pingyuan, but Gongsun Long argued against it, noting Lord Pingyuan’s position and fief were due to kinship, not merit, and that Yu Qing’s proposal was self-serving. Lord Pingyuan rejected the request.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传

translation:
You didn't refuse to accept the seal because you were incompetent, and you didn't refuse to accept the title because you had no merit. It was also because you considered yourself a close relative of the monarch.
Now Lord Xinling has sent troops to save Handan and you ask for an increase in the number of fiefs. This is because you accepted the fiefs as close relatives when you had no merit, but when you did meritorious service, you asked for rewards based on ordinary people's merits.
This is obviously very inappropriate.
Moreover, Yu Qing holds the initiative on both sides of success and failure. If the thing succeeds, he will ask for compensation like a deed to collect debt; if the thing does not succeed, he will use the false name of claiming credit for you to make you grateful to him.
You must not listen to his advice.
Lord Pingyuan then rejected Yu Qing's suggestion.
Lord Pingyuan died in the fifteenth year of King Zhao Xiaocheng's reign.
Lord Pingyuan's descendants inherited his title from generation to generation, and his descendants were finally cut off when the Zhao Kingdom was destroyed.
Lord Pingyuan treated Gongsun Long very kindly.
Gongsun Long was good at debating the "Li Jian Bai" proposition. When Zou Yan visited Zhao State, he discussed the most upright principles and refuted Gongsun Long's famous debate proposition. After that, Lord Pingyuan dismissed Gongsun Long.
Yu Qing was a talented person who was good at lobbying. He wore straw sandals and an umbrella on his shoulders and came all the way to lobby King Zhao Xiaocheng.
When he visited King Zhao for the first time, King Zhao gave him a hundred yi of gold and a pair of white jade. When he visited King Zhao for the second time, he became the minister of Zhao, so he was called Yu Qing.
Qin and Zhao fought in Changping. Zhao was unfavorable in the first battle and lost one captain.
King Zhao summoned Lou Chang and Yu Qing to discuss the situation and said: "Our army did not go well in the first battle and the captain died in battle. I will roll up my armor and go to the enemy to fight the Qin army. What do you think?"
Lou Chang said: If there is no benefit, it is better to send important envoys to seek peace.
Yu Qing said: The reason why Lou Chang advocated for peace was that he believed that if he did not seek peace, our army would be defeated.
But the initiative to control the peace talks lies with Qin.
Moreover, Your Majesty, please estimate Qin's war intention. Is it to defeat Zhao's army, or not?
King Zhao replied: Qin has tried its best without reservation and will definitely defeat Zhao Jun.
Yu Qing went on to say: Your Majesty listened to my words and sent envoys to bring valuable treasures to unite Chu and Wei. If Chu and Wei want to get your Majesty's valuable treasures, they will definitely accept our envoys.
When envoys from the State of Zhao enter Chu and Wei, the State of Qin will definitely suspect that all the princes in the world are united to fight against Qin, and will definitely panic.
In this way, peace talks can proceed.
King Zhao did not listen to Yu Qing's advice and negotiated peace with Pingyang Lord Zhao Bao, so he sent Zheng Zhuxian to Qin to contact Qin.
Qin accepted Zheng Zhu.
King Zhao summoned Yu Qing again and said: I sent Lord Pingyang to Qin to seek peace. Qin has accepted Zheng and Zhu. What do you think?
Yu Qing replied: If the king's peace talks cannot succeed, Zhao Jun will definitely be defeated.
The envoys from all the princes in the world to congratulate Qin on its victory are all in Qin.
Zheng Zhu is a noble person. When he enters Qin, the king of Qin and the princes of Ying will definitely publicize Zheng Zhu's arrival in Qin and show it to all the princes in the world.
summary: Lord Pingyuan died in the fifteenth year of King Xiaocheng’s reign, and his descendants held the title until Zhao’s fall. He treated Gongsun Long well but dismissed him after Zou Yan refuted his debates. Yu Qing, a skilled lobbyist, advised King Zhao against ceding land to Qin after the Changping defeat, proposing instead to ally with Qi. King Zhao initially agreed but later followed Lou Huan’s advice to cede land, leading to further conflict. Yu Qing eventually fled to Daliang, where he wrote “Yu’s Spring and Autumn Annals,” criticizing political failures.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/平原君虞卿列传

translation:
Your Majesty, spread the word about the alliance between Qi and Zhao. Our troops will not have to go to the border to conduct reconnaissance. I will see Qin's valuable gifts sent to Zhao and in turn sue for peace from your Majesty.
Once peace is made with the King of Qin, when Han and Wei hear the news, they will try their best to respect the King. Since they want to respect the King, they must take out precious treasures and rush to pay tribute to the King.
In this way, the king's move can establish friendship with the three countries of Han, Wei, and Qi, and thus change the status of dealing with Qin. After hearing this, King Zhao said: Great.
So he sent Yu Qing east to visit the King of Qi and discuss with him the issue of attacking Qin.
Before Yu Qing returned to Qi, Qin's envoys were already in Zhao.
When Lou Huan learned the news, he immediately ran away.
King Zhao then granted a city to Yu Qing. Soon after, Wei State requested a treaty with Zhao State.
King Zhao Xiaocheng summoned Yu Qing to discuss the matter.
Yu Qing first went to visit Lord Pingyuan. Lord Pingyuan said: I hope to hear you discuss the way of combining vertical and horizontal lines.
Yu Qing entered the palace to meet King Zhao.
King Zhao said: The state of Wei requested an alliance.
Yu Qing said: Wei Guo was wrong.
King Zhao said: I didn't agree to it at first.
Yu Qing said: Your Majesty is wrong.
King Zhao said: Wei Guo asked for alliance, but you said Wei Guo was wrong; I did not agree to it, and you said I was wrong again. In this case, is it impossible to form a vertical alliance after all?
Yu Qing replied: I heard that small countries work together with big countries. If there are benefits, the big countries will enjoy the fruits, and if there are disadvantages, the small countries will bear the disasters.
The current situation is that Wei is willing to bear the disaster as a small country, but you refuse to enjoy the fruits as a big country. So I say that the king is wrong, and the state of Wei is also wrong.
I personally think that a vertical alliance is beneficial. King Zhao said: OK.
So he made an alliance with Wei State.
Because of Wei Qi, the Prime Minister of Wei State, Yu Qing preferred to abandon the title of Marquis of Wanhu and the Prime Minister's seal, and fled from a small road with Wei Qi. Finally, he left Zhao State and was trapped in Daliang of Wei State.
After Wei Qi's death, Yu Qing became even more dissatisfied. He wrote a book, collected historical facts from "Spring and Autumn", observed the modern world situation, and wrote a total of eight articles: "Jieyi", "Title", "Speculation" and "Political Strategy".
It is used to criticize the success and failure of national politics. It has been circulated in the world and is called "Yu's Spring and Autumn Annals".
Tai Shigong said: Mr. Pingyuan is a handsome and talented son in troubled times, but he cannot understand the overall situation.
As the saying goes: greed for personal gain will lead to loss of reason. Lord Pingyuan believed in Feng Ting's heresy and coveted the Shangdang he gave, which led to the Zhao State's defeat in Changping, more than 400,000 Zhao soldiers were killed, and the Zhao State was almost destroyed.
Yu Qing analyzed the affairs, speculated on the situation, and made suggestions for the State of Zhao. How thoughtful and ingenious he was!
In the end, I couldn't bear to watch Wei Qi being hunted down, and finally found himself in trouble in Daliang. Ordinary people knew they couldn't do this, let alone talented people.
But if Yu Qing had not been poor and sad, he would not have been able to write books and make his reputation known to the world and pass on to future generations.
summary: Tai Shigong noted that Lord Pingyuan, though talented, failed to grasp the bigger picture, leading to Zhao’s defeat at Changping and the loss of 400,000 soldiers. Yu Qing’s plans were thoughtful, but his inability to avoid trouble in Daliang highlighted his flaws, though his writings ensured his legacy.

translation:
Prime Minister Gongsun Hong was from Xue County, Sichuan State, Qi Prefecture, and his cousin's name was Ji.
When he was young, he worked as a prison officer in Xue County, but was dismissed due to his crimes.
His family was poor and had to go to the beach to herd pigs.
It wasn’t until he was in his forties that he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals and various works explaining the Spring and Autumn Annals.
He raised his stepmother with filial piety and prudence.
In the first year of Emperor Wu's founding, as soon as the emperor came to the throne, he recruited virtuous and literary people.
At this time, Gongsun Hong was sixty years old. He was recruited to Beijing as a virtuous person and became a doctor.
He was ordered to go on a mission to the Huns and reported the situation to Emperor Wu when he came back. The situation did not suit the emperor's wishes. The emperor was angry and thought Gongsun Hong was incompetent, so Gongsun Hong was excused from his post and returned home on the pretext of illness.
In the fifth year of Emperor Yuanguang's reign, the emperor issued an edict to recruit literature, and the Sichuan Kingdom recommended Gongsun Hong.
Gongsun Hong refused to give in to the people and said: I have gone west to the capital to accept the emperor's appointment, but I resigned from office because of incompetence and returned. Hope to change the recommended candidate.
However, the people of the country resolutely recommended Gongsun Hong, and Gongsun Hong went to Taichang.
Taichang asked the more than 100 Confucian scholars recruited to make countermeasures respectively, and Gongsun Hong's countermeasures articles were ranked last.
All countermeasure articles were sent to the emperor, and Emperor Wu promoted Gongsun Hong's countermeasure article to first place.
Gongsun Hong was summoned to see the emperor. Emperor Wu saw that he was very beautiful and made him a doctor.
At this time, the Han Dynasty opened a road to the southwestern Yi and set up counties and counties there. The people of Bashu felt poor about this, and the emperor ordered Gongsun Hong to inspect it.
Gongsun Hong returned from his inspection and reported to the emperor that it was useless to try his best to slander the southwestern barbarians. The emperor did not adopt his opinions.
Gongsun Hong was a majestic and strange man with extensive knowledge. He often said that the fault of the master is that he is not broad-minded, and the fault of the minister is that he is not frugal.
Gongsun Hong covered himself with a quilt and did not eat more than two kinds of meat or vegetables when eating.
When his stepmother died, he stayed in mourning for three years.
Every time he went to court to discuss political affairs with everyone, he always stated various things at the beginning and let the emperor make his own decisions. He refused to refute him face to face or argue in court.
So the emperor observed him and found that he was honest in character, good at talking, familiar with documents, laws and official affairs, and he could also use Confucian views to embellish him. The emperor liked him very much.
Within two years, he was promoted to Zuo Neishi.
Gongsun Hong reported matters to the emperor, but sometimes they were not accepted and he did not argue in the court.
He once asked the emperor to meet him in his spare time with his lord lieutenant Ji An. Ji An first asked the emperor a question, and Gongsun Hong then explained the problem clearly, and the emperor was often very happy.
Everything he said was accepted. From then on, Gongsun Hong became closer to the emperor day by day, and his status became more prominent.
summary: Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, from Xue County in Qi Prefecture, began his career as a prison officer but was dismissed due to crimes. His family was poor, and he herded pigs until his forties, when he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals. He raised his stepmother with filial piety. At age sixty, during Emperor Wu's reign, he was recruited as a virtuous person and became a doctor. After a mission to the Xiongnu displeased the emperor, he was dismissed and returned home. In the fifth year of Yuanguang, he was recommended again, despite initial reluctance, and his countermeasure essay was promoted to first place by Emperor Wu, who made him a doctor. He inspected the southwestern Yi region but advised against further development, which the emperor ignored.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传

translation:
He had made an agreement in advance with the ministers about the issues he wanted to discuss with the emperor, but when he came before the emperor, he broke the agreement and obeyed the emperor's will. Ji An rebuked Gongsun Hong at the court and said: Most of the people in Qi are deceitful and have no true feelings. He made this suggestion with us at the beginning, but now they have all violated it and are not loyal.
The emperor asked Gongsun Hong, and Gongsun Hong apologized and said: People who know me think I am loyal, people who don't know me think I am disloyal.
The emperor agreed with Gongsun Hong's statement.
The favored ministers around the emperor often slandered Gongsun Hong, but the emperor treated Gongsun Hong more and more favorably.
In the third year of Emperor Wu's Yuanshuo reign, Zhang Ou was dismissed from office, and the emperor appointed Gongsun Hong as the imperial censor.
At this time, the Han Dynasty was opening up the southwestern barbarians, setting up Canghai County in the east and Shuofang County in the north.
Gongsun Hong repeatedly advised the emperor, believing that these practices were exhausting China and running useless places, and hoped to stop doing these things.
Therefore, Emperor Wu asked Zhu Maichen and others to use the favorable situation of setting up Shuofang County to question Gongsun Hong.
Zhu Maichen and others asked ten questions, but Gongsun Hong couldn't answer any of them.
Gongsun Hong apologized and said: I am a humble person from Shandong. I didn't know the benefits of building Shuo County. I hope to stop connecting with the southwestern Yi and setting up Canghai County, and concentrate on running Shuofang County.
The emperor agreed.
Ji An said: Gongsun Hong is in the position of the third Duke and has a lot of salary, but he is covered with quilt. This is fraud.
The emperor asked Gongsun Hong, and Gongsun Hong apologized and said: "There is such a thing."
Among the nine ministers, there is no one who is as good to me as Ji An, but he really hit on my fault when he challenged me in court today.
I have the noble status of the Three Lords but I cover myself with a blanket. It is indeed a clever deception in an attempt to gain a good reputation.
Moreover, I heard that Guan Zhong was the prime minister of Qi and had three residences. His luxury was comparable to that of the king of Qi. Duke Huan of Qi relied on Guan Zhong to dominate, which was also an act of disrespect for the superior king.
Yan Ying was the prime minister of Qi Jinggong. He did not eat more than two kinds of meat and vegetables during meals, and his concubines did not wear silk clothes. Qi State was governed very well. This is because Yan Ying looked after the people below.
Now that I am a royal censor, I am covered with a quilt. This means that there is no distinction between high and low among officials from Jiuqing and below, just like what Ji An said.
Besides, without Ji An's loyalty, how could His Majesty hear these words!
Emperor Wu thought that Gongsun Hong was humble and courteous, so he treated him more favorably. Finally, he made Gongsun Hong the prime minister and granted him the title of Marquis of Pingjin.
Gongsun Hong was suspicious and jealous, magnanimous on the outside, but deep inside.
Those who had enmity with Gongsun Hong, although Gongsun Hong got along well with them on the surface, he secretly caused trouble to others and took revenge.
It was Gongsun Hong's idea to kill his father Yan and reassign Dong Zhongshu to Jiaoxi as prime minister.
He only ate a meat dish and shelled coarse rice for each meal. His old friends and his favorite hangers-on all relied on him to provide food and clothing. Gongsun Hong's salary was used to provide for them, and the family had no money left.
summary: Gongsun Hong was known for his frugality, covering himself with a quilt and eating simple meals. He mourned his stepmother for three years. In court, he avoided direct confrontation, letting the emperor decide. He was promoted to Zuo Neishi within two years. He often agreed with the emperor's will, even breaking prior agreements with ministers, leading to accusations of deceit from Ji An. Gongsun Hong apologized, claiming loyalty was misunderstood. Despite slander, the emperor favored him. In the third year of Yuanshuo, he became imperial censor. He advised against expanding into the southwestern barbarians and Canghai County, focusing on Shuofang County instead. When questioned by Zhu Maichen, he couldn't answer and apologized. Ji An accused him of fraud for his frugality, but Gongsun Hong defended himself, citing historical examples. The emperor made him prime minister and Marquis of Pingjin.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传

translation:
Scholars all thought he was wise for this reason.
The king of Huainan and the king of Hengshan rebelled, and when the court was in a hurry to investigate the accomplices, Gongsun Hong became seriously ill. He felt that he had no merit and was made a marquis. His official position was promoted to prime minister. He should assist the wise king to appease the country and make everyone follow the principles of being a minister.
Nowadays, the princes have plots to rebel against the imperial court. This is all the result of the prime minister's incompetence in his work. He is afraid that if he dies of illness silently, there will be no way to evade the responsibility.
So he wrote to the emperor and said: I heard that there are five kinds of normal ways in the world, and there are three kinds of virtues used to implement these five kinds of normal ways.
The order of king and minister, father and son, brother, husband and wife, and elder and younger are the common principles of the world.
Wisdom, benevolence and courage, these three aspects are the common virtues in the world and are used to practice the common way.
Therefore Confucius said: Working hard to practice is close to benevolence, liking to inquire is close to wisdom, knowing shame is close to courage.
If you know these three situations, you will know how to cultivate yourself. Know how to cultivate yourself, and then know how to govern others.
There is no one in the world who cannot cultivate himself but can govern others. This is a truth that remains unchanged for generations.
Now His Majesty personally practices great filial piety and uses the three kings as a reference to establish a way of governing the country like that of the Zhou Dynasty. It combines the talents and virtues of King Wen and King Wu, encourages talented people, gives them salaries, and awards official positions according to their talents.
Now that my talents are low and I have no hard work, Your Majesty specially promoted me from the ranks, made me a prince, and placed me in the position of the three princes.
My character and ability are not commensurate with this high official position, and I am often sick. I am afraid that I will die before your majesty's dogs and horses, and I will ultimately be unable to repay your majesty's kindness and prevarication.
I hope to return Hou Yin, resign and return home to make way for the sage.
Emperor Wu replied to him: In ancient times, people with meritorious service were rewarded and people with virtue were praised. To preserve the achievements of our ancestors, we must advocate literary and moral education, and when encountering disasters, we must advocate martial arts. This principle has not changed.
I was lucky enough to inherit the throne in the past, but I was afraid of being unrest and wanted to rule the world together with all the ministers. You should know this.
Gentlemen like kind people and hate ugly people. If you act carefully, you can always stay by my side.
Unfortunately, you are suffering from frost, dew, wind and cold. Why worry about not being cured? You actually submitted a letter to Hou Yin, resigned and returned home. This is to show my immorality!
Now that things are a little less complicated, you should reduce your thoughts, concentrate, and use medical assistance for treatment.
Therefore, Emperor Wu allowed Gongsun Hong to continue his leave and gave him cattle, wine and various cloths.
After a few months, Gongsun Hong's condition improved greatly, and he began to deal with political affairs.
The year before last, Gongsun Hong fell ill and eventually died as prime minister.
His son Gongsun Du inherited the title of Marquis of Pingjin.
Gongsun Du had been the governor of Shanyang for more than ten years, but he lost his title as a marquis for breaking the law.
summary: Gongsun Hong was outwardly magnanimous but inwardly vengeful, causing harm to enemies like Dong Zhongshu. He supported old friends with his salary, leaving no savings. During the Huainan and Hengshan rebellions, he fell ill and wrote to the emperor, citing his inadequacy and offering to resign. The emperor refused, granting him leave and gifts. He recovered but eventually died as prime minister. His son Gongsun Du inherited the title but lost it for breaking the law.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传

translation:
Zhu Fuyan was a native of Linyi, Qidi. He studied the theories of political advisors during the Warring States Period. In his later years, he began to study the Zhouyi, Spring and Autumn Annals, and the theories of hundreds of schools of thought.
He traveled among many scholars in Qi, but no one was willing to treat him favorably.
Many scholars in Qi State rejected him together, making it impossible for him to stay in Qi State.
His family was poor and he couldn't borrow money from others, so he went to Yan, Zhao and Zhongshan in the north to study. No one in any place treated him favorably, so it was difficult to be a guest.
In the first year of Emperor Xiaowu's Yuanguang year, he thought that all the vassal states were not worthy of study tours, so he went west to Hanguguan to meet General Wei Qing.
General Wei Qing recommended him to the emperor many times, but the emperor refused to summon him.
The money he brought had been spent, and he had been staying in Chang'an for a long time. The guests of the princes hated him, so he wrote to the emperor.
In the morning he presented the memorial, and in the evening the emperor summoned him.
Of the nine things he said, eight were about laws and regulations, and one was about the conquest of the Huns.
The original text says this:
I heard that a wise monarch does not dislike deep advice but observes widely, and a loyal minister does not dare to escape heavy punishment but speaks out advice. Therefore, good policies in handling national affairs cannot be lost, and the reputation will be passed down to the ages.
Now I dare not hide my loyalty and escape death, but I want to state my foolish thoughts to you. I hope that your majesty will forgive my sins and examine my thoughts a little.
"Sima Fa" says: Although the country is big, if it likes war, it will surely perish; although the world is peaceful, if it forgets war, it will be in danger.
The world has been peaceful, the emperor plays the music of "Dakai", and hunting activities are held in spring and autumn. The princes reorganize the army in spring and train the army in autumn, so as not to forget the war.
Moreover, anger is an act of rebellion, weapons are ominous, and fighting is the worst moral integrity.
In ancient times, whenever a ruler got angry, his corpse would lie on the ground and blood would spread all over the land. Therefore, the wise emperor was very cautious in dealing with anger.
Those who are committed to winning wars and resorting to militarism will always regret it in the end.
In the past, Qin Shihuang relied on his military power to defeat his opponents, encroaching on the world, annexing various warring countries, and unifying the world. His achievements were the same as those of the founding kings of the Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties.
But he was determined to win and refused to give up. He actually wanted to attack the Huns. Li Si advised: "You cannot attack the Xiongnu."
The Xiongnu had no city to live in and no accumulation of property to defend. They moved around like birds flying, making it difficult to catch and control them.
If a light army is sent deep into the Xiongnu, the army's food supplies will be cut off; if a large amount of food is sent into the Xiongnu, it will be heavy and difficult to transport, and it will not help.
Even if we get the land of the Xiongnu, there is no profit to be gained, and when we encounter the Xiongnu people, we cannot use them to protect them.
To defeat them is to kill them, which is not what a king who is the father of his people should do.
summary: Zhu Fuyan, from Linyi, studied political theories and later the Zhouyi and Spring and Autumn Annals. Poor and rejected by scholars, he traveled to various states without success. In Yuanguang's first year, he sought an audience with General Wei Qing, who recommended him, but the emperor ignored him. After spending his money, he wrote a memorial, which led to an immediate summons. His advice included warnings against war with the Xiongnu, citing Qin and Han failures. He advocated for frugality and caution, referencing historical precedents. The emperor appointed him and others as doctors, and Zhu Fuyan was promoted four times in a year.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传

translation:
The master's father, Yan Sheng, said that the land in Shuofang was fertile and fertile, and the Yellow River was a danger outside. Meng Tian built a city here to expel the Xiongnu, and introspected the manpower and material resources for transshipment and guarding water transportation. This was the basis for expanding China's land and wiping out the Xiongnu.
After the emperor read his suggestion, he handed it over to the ministers for discussion. Everyone said it was unfavorable.
Gongsun Hong said: During the Qin Dynasty, 300,000 people were mobilized to build the city north of the Yellow River, but it was not completed and was soon abandoned.
Zhufu Yansheng thought it was beneficial, but the emperor actually adopted Zhufu Yan's strategy and established Shuofang County.
In the second year of Yuanshuo, the master's father Yan told the emperor about Qi King Liu Cijing's promiscuous and eccentric behavior in the palace, and the emperor appointed him as the prime minister of Qi.
The master's father came to the state of Qi, summoned his brothers and guests, distributed five hundred gold to them, and scolded them: "When I was poor at first, my brothers did not give me food and clothing, and my guests did not let me in. Now that I have made a formal appearance, some of the kings have gone thousands of miles away to welcome me."
I have severed all relations with you. Please do not enter my master's father's house again!
So he sent someone to touch King Qi with the adultery between King Qi and his sister. King Qi thought that he could not escape the blame after all, and was afraid of being sentenced to death like King Yan Liu Dingguo, so he committed suicide.
The official in charge reported the matter to the emperor.
When Zhufu Yan first became a commoner, he traveled to Yan and Zhao. When he became a high official, he exposed the secrets of King Yan.
The King of Zhao was afraid that he would become a scourge to the State of Zhao, and wanted to write to the emperor to tell his secrets, because his father was buried in the court and he did not dare to expose it.
When he became the Prime Minister and walked out of Hangu Pass, the King of Zhao sent a letter to accuse his father Yan of accepting bribes from the princes. Therefore, many of the princes' sons were made princes for this reason.
When the King of Qi committed suicide, the emperor was furious when he heard about it. He thought that the master father Yan had threatened his king to commit suicide, so he handed it over to the officials for interrogation.
Zhu Fuyan admitted to accepting bribes from the princes, but actually did not threaten the King of Qi to commit suicide.
The emperor did not want to kill Zhufu Yan. At this time, Gongsun Hong, the imperial censor, said to the emperor: The King of Qi committed suicide and had no descendants. The feudal state was abolished and turned into a county and returned to the imperial court. Zhufu Yan is the chief culprit in this matter. Your Majesty will not be able to explain it to the people of the world unless he kills Zhufu Yan.
So the emperor killed everyone in the father's family.
When the master's father Yan was being favored by dignitaries, there were thousands of guests. When he was exterminated and died, no one collected his body. Only Kongche, a man from Mixian County, collected his body and buried him.
The emperor later heard about this and thought that Kong Che was an elder.
Tai Shigong said: Although Gongsun Hong's moral behavior is beautiful, it is also because he encountered a good opportunity.
It has been more than eighty years since the founding of the Han Dynasty. The emperor was advocating Confucianism and recruiting talents with outstanding talents to develop Confucianism and Mohism. Gongsun Hong was the selected person.
Master Fu Yan was in an important position, and all the high-ranking officials in the court praised him. But when his reputation was ruined and he was killed, the scholars were all vying to talk about his bad qualities. How sad!
The Empress Dowager Wang Zhengjun issued an edict to the Grand Situ Ma Palace and the Grand Sikong Zhenfeng: I heard that the way to govern a country is to first make the people rich; the key to making the people rich is frugality.
summary: Zhu Fuyan advised dividing the territories of princes to weaken their power, which the emperor adopted. He also suggested moving powerful families to Maoling. He exposed secrets of King Yan and King Qi, leading to their deaths. Accused of bribery, he was executed after Gongsun Hong argued his guilt. His guests abandoned him, but Kong Che buried him. Tai Shigong noted Gongsun Hong's success due to timing and Zhu Fuyan's tragic end. Empress Dowager Wang Zhengjun praised Gongsun Hong's frugality and virtue, citing his example as a model for officials. His descendants were granted titles and lands.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/平津侯主父列传

translation:
Lian Po was an outstanding general of Zhao State.
In the sixteenth year of King Zhao Huiwen, Lian Po led the Zhao army to conquer Qi, defeated the Qi army, captured Yangjin, and was named Shangqing by King Zhao. He was famous among the princes and countries for his bravery in battle.
Lin Xiangru was a native of the State of Zhao and a retainer of the family of the eunuch Ling Muxian of the State of Zhao.
During the reign of King Zhao Huiwen, he obtained the Heshi Bi from Chu State.
When King Zhao of Qin heard about this, he sent a letter to King Zhao, expressing his willingness to exchange fifteen cities for He's Bi.
King Zhao discussed with General Lian Po and his ministers: If he gave the jade to Qin, it would be impossible for Qin's cities to be obtained and they would be deceived in vain; if he didn't give it, he would be afraid that the Qin army would attack Zhao immediately.
The countermeasures were not discussed, and I tried to find an envoy who could be sent to Qin to reply, but I couldn't find one.
The eunuch ordered Miao Xian to say: "My retainer Lin Xiangru can go to Qin as an envoy."
King Zhao asked: How do you know he can do it?
Miao Xian replied: "I have committed a crime, and I secretly planned to flee to Yan State. My retainer Xiangru stopped me and said: How do you know that the King of Yan will definitely take you in?"
I said to him: I followed the king to meet with King Yan on the border. King Yan held my hand in private and said that he was willing to make friends with you.
Therefore, I knew that He could take me in, so I wanted to go to Him.
Xiangru said to me: Zhao is strong and Yan is weak, but you are favored by King Zhao, so King Yan wants to make friends with you.
Now you are fleeing from the State of Zhao to the State of Yan. The State of Yan is afraid of the State of Zhao. In this situation, the King of Yan will not dare to take you in, and will tie you up and send you back to the State of Zhao.
Why don't you take off your shirt, expose your shoulders and back, lie under the axe, and beg the king to punish you, and you may be lucky enough to be pardoned.
The minister listened to his advice, and the king graciously pardoned the minister.
I privately thought that this man was a warrior and resourceful, and it was appropriate to send him as an envoy.
So King Zhao immediately summoned him and asked Lin Xiangru: "The King of Qin asked for fifteen cities in exchange for my He's Bi. Can you give it to him?"
Xiangru said: Qin is strong and Zhao is weak, so we have to agree to it.
King Zhao said: But what if King Qin gets my jade but doesn't give me the city?
Xiangru said: Qin asked for a city in exchange for bi, and if Zhao refused, Zhao would be at a loss; if Zhao gave the bi but Qin did not give Zhao a city, Qin would be at a loss.
After weighing the two countermeasures, I would rather agree to it and let Qin bear the responsibility for the loss. King Zhao said: Who can be sent as an envoy?
Xiangru said: If your Majesty really has no one to send, I would like to hold the precious jade and go as an envoy.
If the city belongs to the State of Zhao, I will leave the jade to the State of Qin; if the city cannot be returned to the State of Zhao, I will definitely bring He's Bi back to the State of Zhao intact.
King Zhao then sent Lin Xiangru to take He's Bi and march westward to Qin.
summary: Lian Po, a renowned general of Zhao, conquered Qi and captured Yangjin, earning the title of Shangqing. Lin Xiangru, a retainer of eunuch Miao Xian, was sent as an envoy to Qin after King Zhao of Qin offered fifteen cities for the He's Bi jade. Lin Xiangru successfully returned the jade intact to Zhao after King Qin failed to honor the exchange. Later, at the Mianchi meeting, Lin Xiangru forced King Qin to play a fou, maintaining Zhao's dignity. For his efforts, he was named Shangqing, ranking above Lian Po.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传

translation:
Lian Po said: I am a general of the State of Zhao, with great achievements in sieges and field battles. Lin Xiangru only achieved some merit through his eloquence, but his status is higher than mine. Besides, Lin Xiangru is a humble person. I feel ashamed and cannot bear to be below him.
He also threatened: If I meet Lin Xiangru, I will definitely humiliate him.
After hearing this, Xiangru refused to meet him.
Whenever Lin Xiangru went to court, he often used illness as an excuse to hide at home, unwilling to compete with Lian Po for ranking.
Not long after, Xiangru went out, and Lin Xiangru went out in a carriage. He saw Lian Po from a distance, and Lin Xiangru quickly asked someone to turn the car around to avoid it.
So Xiangru's disciples came together to express their admonition, saying: "The reason why we leave our relatives to serve you is because we admire your noble integrity."
Now you and Lian Po have the same official position. Mr. Lian speaks evil words, but you are afraid to hide from him. Your fear is too much. A mediocre person is ashamed, let alone a general!
We people have no talent, please let us say goodbye!
Lin Xiangru resolutely persuaded them to stay and said: Who do you think is more powerful than General Lian or the King of Qin?
He replied: General Lian cannot compare with King Qin.
Xiangru said: With the power of the King of Qin, I dare to scold him in the court and humiliate his ministers. Although I, Lin Xiangru, are incompetent, can I be afraid of General Lian?
But I thought that the reason Qiang Qin did not dare to use troops against Zhao was because of the two of us. Now that the two tigers are fighting, they will inevitably not be able to coexist.
The reason why I was so tolerant was to put the country's emergencies first and my personal grievances behind.
When Lian Po heard these words, he took off his shirt, exposed his upper body, carried a thorn stick on his back, and was led by the guests to Lin Xiangru's door to apologize.
He said: I am a rough and humble person, but I never thought that you, General, are so generous!
The two finally reconciled and became friends through life and death.
This year, Lian Po attacked Qi eastward and defeated one of its troops.
Two years later, Lian Po attacked several cities in Qi State and captured them.
In the next three years, Lian Po attacked Wei's Fangling and Anyang and captured them all.
Four years later, Lin Xiangru led his troops to attack Qi and withdrew his troops when they reached Pingyi.
The next year, Zhao She defeated the Qin army at the foot of Yanyu City.
Zhao She was originally an official in the State of Zhao who collected land rent.
When he was collecting taxes, Pingyuan Jun's family refused to pay. Zhao She punished him according to law and killed nine people in charge of Pingyuan Jun's family.
Lord Pingyuan was furious and wanted to kill Zhao She.
Zhao She took the opportunity to persuade and said: "You are a noble son in the State of Zhao. If you allow your retainers to disobey the government's laws now, the laws will be weakened. If the laws are weakened, the country will be weak. When the country is weak, the princes will send troops to invade. If the princes send troops to invade the Zhao country, it will perish. How can you keep this wealth?"
With your status and honor, being able to abide by the law will make the country fair, and fairness will make the country strong. When the country is strong, the Zhao family's regime will be stable. As a noble relative of the Zhao country, will you be despised by the world?
summary: Lian Po, resentful of Lin Xiangru's higher rank, threatened to humiliate him. Lin Xiangru avoided conflict, prioritizing national unity over personal grievances. When Lian Po learned of this, he apologized, and the two became close friends. Lian Po later led successful campaigns against Qi and Wei. Tai Shigong praised Lin Xiangru's courage and wisdom, noting his ability to intimidate enemies and later yield to Lian Po, prioritizing the state's interests.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传

translation:
Lord Pingyuan thought he was very talented and recommended him to King Zhao.
King Zhao appointed him in charge of the country's taxation. The country's taxation was very fair and reasonable, the people lived a prosperous life, and the national treasury was also very full.
Qin attacked South Korea and stationed its troops in Lianyu.
King Zhao summoned Lian Po and asked, "Can we send troops to rescue him?"
Lian Po replied: The road is long, dangerous and narrow, making it difficult to rescue.
King Zhao summoned Le Cheng again to ask about this matter, and Le Cheng's answer was the same as Lian Po's.
Zhao She was summoned again to ask. Zhao She replied: "The road is long and dangerous, and the road is narrow. It's like two mice fighting in a hole. Whoever is braver will win."
King Zhao then sent Zhao She to lead the troops to rescue Yan Yu.
军队离开邯郸三十里，赵奢就在军中下令说： 有谁来为军事进谏的就处以死刑。
The Qin army was stationed to the west of Wu'an. The sound of the Qin army beating drums and shouting for military training shook the roof tiles in Wu'an city.
A scout in Zhao's army asked for urgent help from Wu'an, and Zhao She immediately beheaded him.
Zhao Jun held on to the camp and stayed for twenty-eight days without advancing. Instead, he built more fortresses.
A Qin army spy sneaked into the Zhao army's camp, and Zhao She treated him well with food and drink before sending him back.
The spies reported the situation to the generals of the Qin army. The Qin generals were overjoyed and said: The army stopped advancing thirty miles away from the capital and built additional forts. Yanyu will no longer be owned by Zhao.
After Zhao She dispatched the spies of the Qin army, he ordered the soldiers to take off their armor and quickly march towards Yanyu. It took two days and one night to reach the front line, and ordered the cavalry who were good at shooting to camp at Lilan and Fifuli.
After the military camp was built, the Qin army learned of the situation and immediately rushed to the camp.
A sergeant named Xu Li asked for military advice, and Zhao She said: "Let him come in."
Xu Li said: The people of Qin did not expect that the Zhao army would come here. Now they have come to confront the enemy. Their morale is very high. The general must concentrate his troops and prepare for them.
Otherwise, it will definitely fail.
Zhao She said: Please accept my teachings on military law.
Xu Li said: I request to accept the death penalty.
Zhao She said: I will give the order after I return to Handan.
Xu Li asked for another suggestion, saying: The one who takes the northern hill first will win, and the one who arrives later will fail.
Zhao She agreed and immediately sent 10,000 people to rush up the mountain to the north.
The Qin soldiers arrived later and competed with the Zhao army on Beishan but could not attack it. Zhao She commanded the soldiers to attack fiercely and defeated the Qin army.
The Qin army scattered and fled, so the siege of Yan Yu was lifted and the Zhao army returned home.
King Zhao Huiwen gave Zhao She the title of Ma Fujun and appointed Xu Li as the country's captain.
Zhao She then had the same position as Lian Po and Lin Xiangru.
Four years later, King Zhao Huiwen died and his son King Xiaocheng came to the throne.
summary: Zhao She, a tax official, gained King Zhao's favor after punishing Lord Pingyuan's family for tax evasion. He was appointed to oversee national taxation, which prospered the people and treasury. During the Qin siege of Yanyu, Zhao She led a daring rescue, defeating the Qin army and earning the title of Ma Fujun.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传

translation:
In the seventh year of King Zhao Xiaocheng's reign, the Qin army and the Zhao army faced each other in Changping. Zhao She was dead at that time and Lin Xiangru was critically ill. King Zhao sent Lian Po to lead his troops to attack the Qin army. The Qin army defeated the Zhao army several times, but the Zhao army held on to the camp and did not fight.
The Qin army repeatedly challenged. Lian Po ignored it.
King Zhao believed the rumors spread by spies of the Qin army.
A spy of the Qin army said: What the Qin army hates and taboos is that they are afraid that Zhao Kuo, the son of Ma Fujun Zhao She, will become a general.
Therefore, King Zhao appointed Zhao Kuo as his general, replacing Lian Po.
Lin Xiangru said: Your Majesty appointing Zhao Kuo based solely on his reputation is like using glue to seal the tuning posts and then trying to play the harp.
Zhao Kuo can only read the books left by his father and does not know how to be flexible.
King Zhao refused to listen and ordered Zhao Kuo to be his general.
Zhao Kuo has been studying the art of war since he was a child. When it comes to the use of war, he thinks that no one in the world can match him.
He once discussed the use of troops with his father Zhao She. Zhao She couldn't trouble him, but he didn't say he was good either.
Zhao Kuo's mother asked Zhao She what was the reason for this. Zhao She said: Fighting with soldiers is a matter of life and death, but he made it so easy.
It would be fine if the State of Zhao did not use Zhao Kuo as a general, but if he was definitely allowed to be a general, he would definitely be the one who caused the failure of the Zhao army.
When Zhao Kuo was about to leave, his mother wrote to King Zhao saying: Zhao Kuo cannot be made a general.
King Zhao said: Why?
He replied: When I served his father, he was a general at that time. He personally served and served tens of people with food and drink, and he treated hundreds of people as friends. All the rewards given by the king and the royal family were distributed to the military officials and subordinates. From the day he accepted the order, he no longer interfered with family affairs.
Now that Zhao Kuo had suddenly become a general, he faced east to receive his audience. No one in the army dared to look up at him. He took all the gold and silk that the king had rewarded him home and kept them. He also checked for cheap and suitable land and real estate every day, and bought whatever was available.
How does the king think he resembles his father?
The father and son have different minds and hope that the king will not send him to lead the army.
King Zhao said: Just put this matter aside. I have already decided.
Zhao Kuo's mother then said: You must send him to lead the army. If he is incompetent, can I not be implicated?
King Zhao agreed.
After Zhao Kuo replaced Lian Po, he changed all the original rules and regulations and replaced the original military officials.
When Qin general Bai Qi heard about this, he dispatched a surprise force, pretended to be defeated and fled, then cut off the Zhao army's food transport road, split the Zhao army in half, and separated the Zhao soldiers.
After more than forty days, the Zhao army was hungry. Zhao Kuo sent out elite soldiers to fight the Qin army personally. The Qin army shot Zhao Kuo to death.
Zhao Kuo's army was defeated, and hundreds of thousands of troops surrendered to the Qin army. The Qin army buried them all alive.
From the beginning to the end of the Battle of Changping, Zhao State suffered a total of 450,000 losses.
The next year, the Qin army surrounded Handan. The siege lasted for more than a year. Zhao could hardly survive. It was only through the rescue of the Chu and Wei armies that the siege of Handan was lifted.
King Zhao finally did not implicate Zhao Kuo's mother because of her words.
Five years after the siege of Handan was relieved, the Yan State adopted Li Fu's strategy. It was said that all the mature men of the Zhao State died in the Battle of Changping, and their orphans were not yet adults, so the King of Yan sent troops to attack Zhao.
summary: After King Zhao Huiwen's death, King Xiaocheng ascended. In the Changping campaign, Lian Po initially held defensive positions against Qin. King Xiaocheng replaced him with Zhao Kuo, despite warnings from Lin Xiangru and Zhao Kuo's mother. Zhao Kuo's arrogance led to a disastrous defeat, with 450,000 Zhao soldiers killed. The Qin army later besieged Handan, which was relieved by Chu and Wei forces.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传

translation:
King Zhao sent Lian Po to lead the troops to counterattack, defeated the Yan army in Hacheng, killed Li Fu, and surrounded the capital of Yan.
Yan State ceded five cities and asked for peace, and King Zhao agreed to a truce.
King Zhao gave Wei Wen the title of Lord Xinping to Lian Po, and appointed him as acting prime minister.
Lian Po was dismissed from his post in Changping and returned home. When he lost power, all his original followers left him.
When he was appointed as a general again, the retainers came back again.
Lian Po said: Gentlemen, please come back! The diners said: Alas!
Why are your opinions so backward?
Everyone in the world makes friends based on market transactions. If you have power, we will follow you. If you no longer have power, we will leave. This is a very common truth. What is there to complain about?
After another six years, the State of Zhao sent Lian Po to attack Fanyang of the State of Wei and captured it.
When King Zhao Xiaocheng passed away, Prince Miaoxiang came to the throne and sent Lecheng to replace Lian Po.
Lian Po was furious and attacked Lecheng, but Lecheng escaped.
Lian Po then fled to Daliang in Wei.
The next year, Zhao State attacked Yan State with Li Mu as general and captured Wu Sui and Fangcheng.
Lian Po had lived in Daliang for a long time, and Wei could not trust him.
Since the State of Zhao was besieged by Qin soldiers many times, the King of Zhao wanted to use Lian Po as a general again, and Lian Po also wanted to be appointed by the State of Zhao again.
King Zhao sent envoys to visit Lian Po to see if he could still be employed.
Lian Po's enemy Guo Kai bribed the envoy with a large amount of money, asking him to speak ill of Lian Po when he came back.
After the Zhao envoy met Lian Po, Lian Po ate a bushel of rice and ten kilograms of meat in front of him. He also put on his armor and mounted his horse, indicating that he could still be employed.
The envoy from the State of Zhao went back and reported to King Zhao: Although General Lian is old and still has a good appetite, he pooped three times in a short period of time while sitting with me.
King Zhao thought Lian Po was old and stopped recalling him.
Chu State heard that Lian Po was in Wei State and secretly sent people to meet him.
Although Lian Po became a general of the Chu State, he had no military exploits. He said: I want to command the soldiers of the Zhao State.
Lian Po finally died in Shouchun.
Li Mu was a good general on the northern border of Zhao State.
He was stationed at Yanmen County in Dai for a long time to guard against the Huns.
He had the power to appoint officials as needed, and all taxes and fees from the cities within the defense area were sent to Li Mu's shogunate to fund the army.
He slaughtered several cows every day to reward the soldiers, taught them archery and horseback riding, carefully guarded the beacon tower, sent more personnel to detect the enemy's situation, and treated the soldiers well.
The rules were drawn up and said: If the Huns invade, they must quickly gather their troops and retreat into the camp to defend themselves. Anyone who dares to capture the enemy will be beheaded.
Every time the Xiongnu invaded, the beacon sent an alarm, and they immediately gathered their troops and retreated into the camp to defend themselves, not daring to go out to fight.
After several years like this, there was no loss of men, horses or supplies.
However, the Xiongnu thought that Li Mu was timid, and even the officers and soldiers guarding the border of Zhao State thought that their general was timid.
summary: Lian Po later defeated Yan, earning the title of Lord Xinping. After King Xiaocheng's death, Lian Po fled to Wei following a conflict with Lecheng. Zhao attempted to recall him, but a bribed envoy falsely reported his frailty, and he was not reinstated. Lian Po died in Chu.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传

translation:
King Zhao blamed Li Mu, but Li Mu remained the same.
King Zhao became angry, recalled him, and sent others to lead the army on his behalf.
For more than a year, every time the Huns came to invade, new generals would send troops to fight.
They sent out troops to fight, but suffered repeated defeats, resulting in many losses and casualties. Farming and grazing on the border were impossible.
King Zhao had no choice but to ask Li Mu to serve again.
Li Mu stayed behind closed doors and insisted that he was sick.
King Zhao then forced him to command the troops.
Li Mu said: Your Majesty must use me. I should do what I did before, only then can I dare to obey the order.
King Zhao agreed to his request.
When Li Mu came to the border, he still followed the original regulations.
The Huns had nothing to gain for several years, but they still thought Li Mu was timid.
The officers and soldiers on the border receive rewards every day but have no use for them, so they are willing to fight.
So Li Mu prepared 1,300 carefully selected chariots, 13,000 selected war horses, 50,000 warriors who dared to charge into battle, and 100,000 soldiers who were good at shooting, and organized them all for training and combat.
At the same time, large numbers of livestock were allowed to graze everywhere, and the entire wilderness was filled with people grazing.
When a small group of Huns invaded, Li Mu pretended to be defeated. Li Mu deliberately abandoned thousands of people to the Huns.
When Chanyu heard about this situation, he led a large number of troops to invade.
Li Mu ambushed many strange soldiers, spread out his left and right wings to outflank the enemy and counterattacked, defeating the Xiongnu and killing more than 100,000 horses.
He destroyed Xiu, defeated Donghu, surrendered Linhu, and Shanyu fled.
For more than ten years after that, the Huns no longer dared to approach the border towns of Zhao.
In the first year of King Zhao Daoxiang, after Lian Po had fled to Wei State, Zhao State sent Li Mu to attack Yan State and captured Wu Sui and Fangcheng.
Two years later, Pang Nuan defeated the Yan army and killed Ju Xin.
After another seven years, the Qin army defeated and killed the Zhao general Hu Zou at Wu Sui, and killed 100,000 Zhao soldiers.
The State of Zhao then appointed Li Mu as its general, attacked the Qin army in Yi'an, defeated the Qin army, and drove away the Qin general Huan Jue.
Li Mu was named Lord Wu'an.
Three years later, the Qin army attacked Fanwu. Li Mu defeated the Qin army and moved south to resist South Korea and Wei.
In the seventh year since King Zhao moved, the State of Qin sent Wang Jian to attack the State of Zhao, and the State of Zhao sent Li Mu and Sima Shang to resist the Qin army.
The State of Qin bribed King Zhao's favored minister Guo Kai with a lot of money to let him carry out counterintuitive schemes and spread rumors that Li Mu and Sima Shang were going to rebel.
The king of Zhao sent Zhao Cong and Qi general Yan Ju to replace Li Mu, but Li Mu refused to accept the order.
King Zhao sent people to secretly arrest Li Mu, killed him, and removed Sima Shang from his official position.
Three months later, Wang Jian took the opportunity to attack the State of Zhao, defeated the Zhao army, killed Zhao Cong, captured Zhao Wangqian and his general Yan Ju, and finally destroyed the State of Zhao.
Tai Shigong said: If you know you are about to die and are not afraid, you must be very courageous; death is not difficult, but how to deal with this death is difficult.
summary: Li Mu, a capable general, defended Zhao's northern border against the Xiongnu. Initially perceived as timid, he later ambushed and defeated the Xiongnu, securing peace for over a decade. He also achieved victories against Qin, earning the title of Lord Wu'an. However, King Zhao, influenced by rumors, executed Li Mu and removed Sima Shang. Three months later, Qin destroyed Zhao.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/廉颇蔺相如列传

translation:
Prime Minister Zhang Cang is from Yangwu. He likes books, music and calendars very much.
During the Qin Dynasty, he served as the censor and was in charge of various documents and files in the palace.
Later, because of the crime, he ran away and went home.
When Pei Gong conquered the city and passed Yangwu, Zhang Cang followed Pei Gong as a guest to attack Nanyang.
Later, Zhang Cang should be beheaded for breaking the law. When he took off his clothes and leaned on the instrument of torture, he was tall and big, with skin as plump and fair as gourd seeds. Wang Ling happened to see him and marveled at how good Zhang Cang was. Therefore, Wang Ling interceded with Pei Gong and pardoned his death penalty.
In this way, Zhang Cang followed Pei Gong westward into Wuguan and arrived at Xianyang.
Pei Gong was established as the king of Han, entered Hanzhong, and soon returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties.
Chen Yu defeated Zhang Er, the king of Changshan, and Zhang Er surrendered to the king of Han. The king of Han appointed Zhang Cang as the governor of Changshan.
He also followed Han Xin to attack Zhao, and Zhang Cang captured Chen Yu.
After Zhao Di was pacified, the king appointed Zhang Cang as the Prime Minister of the country to guard against border enemies.
Soon after, he was transferred to Zhao Guo Xiangguo to assist Zhao Wang Zhang Er.
After Zhang Er died, he assisted Zhao Wang Zhang Ao.
Then he was transferred to Dai Guo Xiangguo to assist Dai Wang.
When King Zang Tu of Yan rebelled, Emperor Gaozu led troops to attack. Zhang Cang followed Emperor Gaozu as the acting prime minister for his meritorious service in attacking Zang Tu. In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Beiping, with a settlement of 1,200 households.
Later, Zhang Cang was promoted to the position of Prime Minister in charge of financial management. Instead, he served as chief accountant as Liehou, a position he held for four years.
At this time, Xiao He was serving as the prime minister, and Zhang Cang had been serving as the historian since the Qin Dynasty. He was very familiar with the world's books and various books. In addition, he was proficient in calculations, music and calendars, so he was ordered to stay in the prime minister's mansion as a prince and be responsible for managing the accounting books handed over by various counties.
When Yingbu failed to rebel and fled, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty appointed his son Liu Chang as king of Huainan and ordered Zhang Cang to assist him as prime minister.
Fourteen years later, Zhang Cang was promoted to the imperial censor.
Zhou Chang was a native of Peixian County. He and his cousin Zhou Ke both served as soldiers of Surabaya during the Qin Dynasty.
When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty raised an army in Pei County, he defeated the governor and eunuch of Sishui County. In this way, the two brothers Zhou Chang and Zhou Ke followed Pei Gong with their qualifications as soldiers. Pei Gong appointed Zhou Chang to be in charge of the flag, and Zhou Ke was temporarily a guest in his tent.
Later, they all followed Pei Gong into the Pass and overthrew the rule of Qiang Qin.
Pei Gong was granted the title of King of Han, and the King of Han appointed Zhou Ke as Yushi Dafu and Zhou Chang as Lieutenant.
In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, the Chu army surrounded the Han Dynasty in Xingyang. The situation was urgent. The Han Dynasty quietly escaped and ordered Zhou Ke to stay in Xingyang City.
The Chu army conquered Xingyang and wanted to appoint him as a general. Zhou Ke scolded him: You people should surrender to the king of Han quickly, otherwise you will be prisoners soon!
Xiang Yu was furious after hearing this and immediately cooked and killed Zhou Ke.
Therefore, the king of Han worshiped Zhou Chang as the imperial censor.
Zhou Chang often followed the King of Han and defeated Xiang Yu's army many times.
Therefore, in the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu, Zhou Chang was granted the title of Marquis of Fenyin together with Xiao He and Cao Shen. Zhou Ke's son Zhou Cheng was also granted the title of Marquis of Gao Jing because his father died for the country.
Zhou Chang is a stoic and strong man who dares to speak his mind. People like Xiao He, Cao Shen and others were in great awe of Zhou Chang.
Zhou Chang once entered the palace to perform business when Emperor Gao was resting. Emperor Gao was hugging Qi Ji. Seeing this, Zhou Chang turned around and ran away. Emperor Gao quickly chased after him. After catching up, he rode on Zhou Chang's neck and asked, "What kind of emperor do you think I am?"
summary: The lives and careers of several prominent officials in the early Han Dynasty, focusing on their roles, achievements, and interactions with emperors. Prime Minister Zhang Cang, from Yangwu, was a scholar of books, music, and calendars. After serving as a Qin censor, he fled home due to a crime. He later joined Pei Gong (Emperor Gaozu) and was saved from execution by Wang Ling, who was impressed by his appearance. Zhang Cang served in various posts, including governor and prime minister of several states, and was granted the title of Marquis of Beiping. He became chief accountant and later imperial censor. As prime minister, he revised music and calendars, adhering to the Qin calendar and the virtue of water. He lived to over a hundred years old, relying on wet nurses in his old age. Zhou Chang, from Peixian, served as a soldier under Pei Gong and became a lieutenant. After his cousin Zhou Ke was killed by Xiang Yu for refusing to surrender, Zhou Chang became imperial censor. He was known for his bluntness, once comparing Emperor Gaozu to tyrants. He opposed the emperor's plan to depose the crown prince, earning gratitude from Empress Lu. Later, he was appointed prime minister of Zhao to protect the young King Ruyi, despite his reluctance. After Gaozu's death, Empress Lu summoned King Zhao to court, leading to his death. Zhou Chang then feigned illness and died three years later.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张丞相列传

translation:
After Zhou Chang left, a long time passed. Gaozu held the official seal of the imperial censor in his hand, gently caressed it and said: Who is the most suitable candidate for the imperial censor?
Then he looked at Zhao Yao carefully and said: No one is more suitable than Zhao Yao.
In this way, Zhao Yao was appointed as the imperial censor.
Zhao Yao also had military merits and food in the past. When he followed the imperial censor to attack Chen Xi and made meritorious service, he was named the Marquis of Jiangyi.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Empress Dowager Lu sent an envoy to summon King Zhao to the court. Prime Minister Zhou Chang asked King Zhao to say that he was not in good health and could not go.
The envoy went back and forth three times, but Zhou Changdu always insisted not to send King Zhao to Beijing.
So Empress Lu was very worried and sent an envoy to summon Zhou Chang to the capital.
After Zhou Chang came to Beijing, he met with Empress Lu. Empress Lu scolded him very angrily: Don't you know that I hate Mrs. Qi very much?
But you didn't let King Zhao enter the capital, why?
After Zhou Chang was summoned to the capital, Empress Lu sent an envoy to summon King Zhao. Soon, King Zhao came to the capital.
More than a month after he arrived in Chang'an, he was forced to drink poison and died.
Therefore, Zhou Chang claimed that he was recovering from illness and no longer went to court to see the Queen Mother. Three years later, he too died.
Five years later, Gao Hou heard that the imperial censor Zhao Yao, the Marquis of Jiangyi, had made a plan to protect King Zhao Ruyi during the reign of Emperor Gaozu, so he removed his title of Marquis of Jiangyi to compensate for his crime, and made Ren Ao, Marquis of Guang'a, the censor.
Ren Ao turned out to be a jailer in Peixian County.
When Emperor Gaozu was still an ordinary citizen, he avoided lawsuits. The jailers could not find Emperor Gaozu himself, so they captured Empress Lu and disrespected her.
Ren Ao, who had always been close to Emperor Gaozu, was very angry when he saw this, so he wounded the jailer who was detaining Empress Lu.
When Emperor Gaozu began to raise troops, Ren Ao followed him as a guest, and later served as censor, stationed in Fengyi for two years. Emperor Gaozu established himself as King of Han, marched eastward to attack Xiang Yu, and promoted Ao to the post of governor of Shangdang County.
When Chen Kui rebelled, Ren Ao held on to the city and was not captured by the rebels. For his meritorious service, he was granted the title of Marquis of Guang'a, with a settlement of 1,800 households.
When he was in high school, he served as the imperial censor.
Three years later, he was dismissed and appointed Pingyang Marquis Cao Cheng as the imperial censor.
After the death of Empress Gao, Cao Cheng and his ministers jointly killed Lu Lu and others. Afterwards, he was removed from his official position and appointed Zhang Cang, the prime minister of the King of Huainan, as the imperial censor.
Zhang Cang, Jianghou Zhou Bo and others jointly honored Dai Wang as Emperor Xiaowen.
In the fourth year of Emperor Wen's reign, Prime Minister Guan Ying passed away and Zhang Cang succeeded him as Prime Minister.
It had been more than twenty years since the establishment of the Han Dynasty to Emperor Xiaowen. At that time, the world was just peaceful, and all the civil and military officials in the court were soldiers. However, Zhang Cang was the only one who devoted himself to exploring and revising music and calendars from the time he served as Prime Minister.
Because Emperor Gaozu entered the Pass in October and defeated the Qin Dynasty and reached Ba Shang, the old calendar of the Qin Dynasty that started the year in October was still followed.
He also speculated on the operation of the five virtues of metal, wood, water, fire, and earth, and believed that the Han Dynasty was in the period when the virtue of water was strong, so it still advocated black like the Qin Dynasty.
summary: Zhao Yao, a young censor, advised Gaozu to appoint Zhou Chang as Zhao's prime minister. He later became imperial censor and was named Marquis of Jiangyi. After Gaozu's death, Empress Lu stripped him of his title for his role in protecting King Zhao. Ren Ao, a former jailer who aided Empress Lu, succeeded him as censor and was named Marquis of Guang'a. He was later dismissed, and Cao Cheng briefly served as censor before Zhang Cang was reappointed.

translation:
In the first year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, officials who had followed Emperor Gao in the Northern and Southern Wars and whose current salary was two thousand shi were all selected and granted the title of Marquis of Guannei. A total of twenty-four people were awarded this title, and Shen Tujia received five hundred households.
After Zhang Cang became prime minister, Shen Tujia was promoted to the imperial censor.
After Zhang Cang dismissed him as prime minister, Emperor Xiaowen wanted to appoint the queen's brother Dou Guangguo as prime minister, but he said: I am afraid that doing so will make the world think that I favor Guangguo.
Dou Guangguo was a man of great talent and good moral character, so the emperor wanted to appoint him as prime minister. But after long consideration, Emperor Xiaowen still thought he was not suitable. However, many ministers during the reign of Emperor Gao were dead, and there seemed to be no suitable candidate among the living people, so he appointed Shen Tujia as prime minister and made him a Marquis of Anhu in his original city.
Shen Tujia was an honest and upright person and did not accept private visits at home.
At that time, Deng Tong, the Taizhong doctor, was the most favored, and the emperor rewarded him with tens of millions of money.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty once went to his house to drink and have fun, which shows how much the emperor loved him.
At that time, the Prime Minister Shen Tujia went to the court to pay homage to the emperor, but Deng Tong stood beside the emperor and neglected his etiquette.
After Shen Tujia finished his speech, he continued: Your Majesty, you love your favorite and you can make him rich, but as for the etiquette in the court, you must take it seriously.
The emperor said: Please stop talking, I just have a preference for Deng Tong.
Shen Tujia came back from the court and sat in the Prime Minister's Mansion. He issued an order asking Deng Tong to come to the Prime Minister's Mansion. If he didn't come, Deng Tong would be beheaded.
Deng Tong was very frightened and went to the palace to tell Emperor Wen.
Emperor Wen said: "It's okay for you to go. I will send someone to summon you to the palace immediately."
Deng Tong came to the Prime Minister's Mansion, took off his hat and shoes, kowtowed to Shen Tujia and apologized.
Shen Tujia sat there casually, deliberately not treating him with courtesy, and at the same time scolded him: "The court is the court of Emperor Gaozu."
You, Deng Tong, are just a minor minister, but you dare to play in the main hall. You are guilty of disrespect and should be beheaded.
Whoever comes, execute it now and kill him!
Deng Tong kowtowed and his head was bleeding, but Shen Tujia still didn't say spare him.
Emperor Wen estimated that the prime minister had made Deng Tong suffer a lot, so he sent an envoy to summon Deng Tong into the palace with the emperor's official certificate. He apologized to the prime minister and said: "This is my dear minister, please spare him!"
After Deng Tong returned to the palace, he cried and said to Emperor Wen: The prime minister almost killed me!
Five years after Shen Tujia served as prime minister, Emperor Xiaowen died and Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne.
In the second year of Emperor Jing's reign, Chao Cuo served as internal historian. Because he was favored by the emperor, he had a high status and great power. He petitioned the emperor to change many laws and regulations. At the same time, they also discussed how to use demotion and punishment to weaken the power of the princes.
Prime Minister Shen Tujia also felt that what he said was not adopted, so he hated Chao Cuo.
summary: Shen Tujia, from Liang, was a warrior who followed Emperor Gaozu and became prime minister under Emperor Wen. He was known for his honesty and strict adherence to court etiquette. He once ordered the execution of the favored courtier Deng Tong for disrespect, but Emperor Wen intervened. As prime minister, he clashed with Chao Cuo, who changed laws and cut through a temple wall. Shen Tujia sought to execute Chao Cuo but was thwarted by Emperor Jing. He died of anger after being outmaneuvered.
