translation:
During the reign of Emperor Xiaoxuan, because of his old friendship with the emperor, he was named a prince, and then became the prime minister.
He was sensible and had intelligence and wisdom beyond ordinary people, and was praised by later generations.
He died of illness while serving as prime minister, and his son Bing Xian inherited the title.
Later, Bing Xian also broke into the ancestral temple on horseback and committed the crime of disrespect. The emperor issued an edict to demote him one level and became a Marquis of Guannei. He lost the title of a prince, but he still enjoyed the former fiefdom of his hometown.
Bing Xian served as an official until he became a servant. Because he was confused and unclear as an official, and he and his son committed malpractice and corruption for personal gain, he was dismissed from office and demoted to civilians.
After the death of Prime Minister Bing Ji, Prime Minister Huang succeeded him.
Once upon a time, there was a man in Chang'an who was good at reading faces. His name was Tian Wen. He met Prime Minister Wei, Prime Minister Wei, and Prime Minister Bing, who were not high-ranking officials at that time, when they were guests. Tian Wen said: "The three gentlemen here now will all be prime ministers in the future."
Later, these three people became prime ministers one after another. How could this man have such foresight!
Prime Minister Huang's name is Huang Ba, and he is from Huaiyin.
Because he liked reading, he became an official and became the prefect of Yingchuan.
When governing Yingchuan, he used etiquette, regulations and decrees to teach and influence the people.
If someone is guilty of a serious crime and should be beheaded, Xiao Zhi will rationally let him commit suicide.
His teachings spread throughout the world, and his reputation was known far and near.
Emperor Xiaoxuan specially issued a document for this purpose, saying: Huang Ba, the prefect of Yingchuan, used propaganda laws to govern the people, so no one picked up relics on the road, men and women went their own way, and there were no prisoners who committed serious crimes in the prison.
The title of Marquis of Guannei is specially given and one hundred catties of gold.
In this way, he was recruited by the emperor to the capital as Jing Zhaoyin, and later became prime minister. During his tenure as prime minister, he still governed the country with etiquette and justice, and finally died of illness while serving as prime minister.
After his death, his son inherited the title and was later made a prince.
After Prime Minister Huang died, the emperor appointed Yu Dingguo, the imperial censor, to take his place.
Prime Minister Yu Dingguo already has a biography of Tingwei, which is included in the biography of "Zhang Tingwei".
After Prime Minister Yu resigned, Wei Xuancheng, the imperial censor, took over his position.
Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng is the son of the Prime Minister Wei Xian mentioned earlier.
He inherited his father's title, but later lost his title due to breaking the law.
Wei Xuancheng has loved reading since he was a child and is very familiar with "The Classics" and "The Analects of Confucius".
When he reached the rank of Weiwei as an official, he was promoted to Prince Taifu.
After Mr. Xue, the imperial censor, was dismissed, Wei Xuancheng became the censor.
After the Prime Minister requested to retire and return to his hometown, and the Emperor agreed to his resignation, Wei Xuancheng became the Prime Minister again. The emperor named him Fuyang Marquis after his old feudal city of Fuyang.
A few years later, he died of illness. Emperor Xiaoyuan personally attended his funeral and gave him a particularly generous reward.
Wei Xuancheng governed the country in a harmonious and unconventional way. He was able to follow the world and be ups and downs, but some people called him flattery and opportunistic.
The fortune teller had long said that he should replace his father and inherit the title, but he lost it after he got it. Then, he wandered around again and made a comeback, reaching the rank of prime minister.
At the same time, both father and son became prime ministers. Both father and son were prime ministers, and people talked about it well at that time. Isn't this destiny?
summary: The text also lists later prime ministers, including Che Qianqiu, Wei Xian, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Huang Ba, Yu Dingguo, Wei Xuancheng, and Kuang Heng. Many were scholars who rose through official ranks, with some losing their titles for crimes like riding into temples. The historian notes that while some achieved high office through fate, others schemed in vain, and many talented individuals remained unrecognized.

translation:
Zhang Yi is a native of Wei.
At first, he and Su Qin studied under Mr. Gui Guzi and learned the art of lobbying. Su Qin thought that he was not as talented as Zhang Yi.
After Zhang Yi completed his studies, he went to lobby the princes.
He once drank with Prime Minister Chu. During the dinner, Prime Minister Chu lost a piece of jade. The guests suspected Zhang Yi and said, "Zhang Yi is poor and has bad conduct. He must have stolen the prime minister's jade."
So, everyone arrested Zhang Yi and tortured him hundreds of times.
Zhang Yi never admitted it and had to release him.
His wife said sadly and hatefully: Alas! If you had never gone to study and lobby, how could you have suffered such humiliation?
Zhang Yi said to his wife: Look, is my tongue still there?
His wife smiled and said: The tongue is still there.
Zhang Yi said: This is enough.
At that time, Su Qin had persuaded King Zhao to agree to form a vertical alliance with the other six countries except Qin, but he was afraid that Qin would take the opportunity to attack the vassal states and the alliance would be destroyed before it was even concluded. He also considered that there was no suitable person to send to Qin, so he sent someone to secretly guide Zhang Yi and said: "You and Su Qin had a good relationship at the beginning. Now that Su Qin is in power, why don't you make friends with him to realize your wish of success?"
So Zhang Yi went to Zhao State, submitted a famous invitation, and requested to meet Su Qin.
Su Qin warned his disciples not to inform Zhang Yi, and kept him from leaving for several days.
Soon Su Qin received him. He made him sit in the hall, gave him food for his servants and concubines, and repeatedly scolded him: "With your talents, you have made yourself so poor."
Don’t I have the ability to recommend you and make you rich? It's just that you don't deserve to be hired.
After saying that, Zhang Yi was sent away.
Zhang Yi came to seek refuge with Su Qin, thinking that they were old friends and could get benefits, but unexpectedly he was humiliated and was very angry. He also considered that no one among the princes was worthy of serving, and only Qin could invade Zhao, so he went to Qin.
Soon Su Qin said to those close to him: Zhang Yi is the most talented person in the world. I probably can't compare with him.
Now, fortunately, I was reused before him, and only Zhang Yi can control the power of Qin.
However, he is currently very poor and has no way to enter the society.
I was worried that in order to satisfy small interests, he would no longer be enterprising and would not be able to achieve great achievements, so I summoned him to humiliate him and use it to stimulate his will. You serve him secretly on my behalf.
Su Qin reported to the King of Zhao, took out money, property, chariots and horses, sent people to follow Zhang Yi secretly, stayed in the same inn with him, and gradually got closer to him. He also gave him chariots, horses, money, and whatever he needed, but did not explain who gave it.
So Zhang Yi had the opportunity to meet King Qin Hui.
King Hui appointed him as a guest minister and discussed with him how to attack the princes of various countries.
At this time, the retainer sent by Su Qin was about to say goodbye and leave. Zhang Yi said: Thanks to your help, I gained a distinguished position. I am about to repay your kindness, why do I have to leave?
The doorman said: I don't know you well. The one who really knows you is Mr. Su.
Mr. Su was worried that Qin would attack Zhao and destroy the alliance. He believed that no one but you could control the power of Qin, so he angered Mr. Su and sent me to secretly provide you with money. This was Mr. Su's strategy.
Now that my husband has been reused, please let me go back and resume my life!
Zhang Yi said: Alas, these tactics were originally within the scope of my study, but I didn't realize it. I'm not as clever as Mr. Su!
summary: Zhang Yi, a native of Wei, studied lobbying under Guiguzi alongside Su Qin, who acknowledged his own inferiority to Zhang Yi. After completing his studies, Zhang Yi faced humiliation when he was falsely accused of stealing a jade during a dinner with the Prime Minister of Chu, resulting in torture. Despite his wife's lament, Zhang Yi remained undeterred, noting that his tongue—his tool for persuasion—was still intact. Su Qin, having secured a vertical alliance against Qin, secretly aided Zhang Yi by provoking him through public humiliation, which spurred Zhang Yi to seek fortune in Qin. Su Qin provided Zhang Yi with resources, enabling him to gain favor with King Hui of Qin and become a guest minister. Zhang Yi later realized Su Qin's strategy and refrained from attacking Zhao, honoring their unspoken pact.

translation:
Besides, I have just been appointed, so how can I plan to attack Zhao?
Please thank Mr. Su for me. As long as Mr. Su is in power, how can I, Zhang Yi, dare to talk about attacking Zhao?
After Zhang Yi became the prime minister of Qin, he wrote a letter to warn the prime minister of Chu: When I drank with you, I didn't steal your jade, but you whipped me.
You have to protect your country well, I will steal your city soon! Ba and Shu attacked each other, and they went to Qin for help. King Hui of Qin wanted to send out troops to attack Shu, but he also believed that the road was dangerous, narrow and difficult to reach. At this time, South Korea came to invade Qin again. King Qin Hui wanted to attack South Korea first, and then attack Shu, which might be disadvantageous; he wanted to attack Shu first, but he was worried that South Korea would take advantage of the fatigue of the long battle to launch a sneak attack, so he hesitated and could not make a decision.
Sima Cuo and Zhang Yi argued endlessly in front of King Hui. Sima Cuo advocated attacking Shu, but Zhang Yi said: It is better to attack South Korea first.
King Hui said: I am willing to hear your respective reasons.
Zhang Yi said: We will first have a blind date with the Wei State and be friendly with the Chu State, and then march to Sanchuan to block the pass of Shigu and block the main road of Tunliu. In this way, the passage from Wei to Nanyang was cut off, allowing the Chu State to send troops to approach Nanzheng. The Qin army attacked Xincheng and Yiyang, approaching the suburbs of the Western Zhou and Eastern Zhou Dynasties to attack the king of Zhou for his crimes, and then captured the lands of Chu and Wei.
King Zhou himself knew that there was no way to save it, so he would definitely donate the nine-cauldron treasure passed down to the country.
The Qin State possesses the treasure of Jiuding and controls the map and household registration of the world. It can control the emperor of Zhou and issue orders to the world. No one in the world dares not to obey. This is the great cause of unifying the world!
Nowadays, Shu is a remote country in the west. It is a backward nation like the Rong and Di. Attacking them will make our soldiers tired and the people toiled, and we will not be able to become famous in the world. We will not gain any practical benefits by seizing their land.
I heard that those who pursue fame and status should go to the court, and those who pursue profit should go to the market.
Nowadays, Sanchuan and Zhou Dynasty are like the imperial court and the market, but the king does not compete there. Instead, he competes in backward areas such as Rongdi and Di. This is too far away from the emperor's achievements.
Sima Cuo said: That's not the case.
I heard that those who want to make the country rich and powerful must expand its territory; those who want to make the army strong must make the people rich; those who want to unify the world must extend kindness. If these three conditions are met, the great cause of the emperor will be a matter of course.
Today, the king's territory is still small and the people are still poor, so I hope that the king will do something easy to do first.
The Kingdom of Shu is a remote country in the west, but it is the leader of Rong and Di. Disasters similar to those of Xia Jie and Shang Zhou have already occurred.
Sending out Qin's powerful army to attack it is like asking jackals to drive away sheep.
Occupying its land can expand Qin's territory, and seizing its wealth can enrich the people and improve the army. They had already surrendered without losing any troops or generals.
If we conquer a country, people in the world will not think of us as cruel; if we take away all the wealth of the West, people in the world will not think of us as greedy. By sending out troops, we will gain prestige and real profits, and we will also enjoy a good reputation for prohibiting riots.
Today, attacking South Korea and kidnapping the emperor will bring a very bad reputation and may not necessarily bring benefits. It will also bear the ugly name of injustice. Moreover, it is a country that no one in the world wants to attack, so it will be dangerous.
summary: As Qin's prime minister, Zhang Yi advised King Hui on military strategy, initially advocating an attack on Han to seize the Nine Tripods and control the Zhou emperor, while Sima Cuo argued for conquering Shu to expand territory and enrich the state. King Hui chose Sima Cuo's plan, capturing Shu and strengthening Qin. Zhang Yi later persuaded Wei to ally with Qin, leading to Wei ceding territory and Zhang Yi becoming Qin's prime minister.

translation:
Therefore, King Ai broke the alliance agreement and requested reconciliation with Qin through Zhang Yi.
Zhang Yi returned to Qin and became prime minister again.
Three years later, Wei betrayed Qin and joined the Co-Vertical Covenant.
Qin sent troops to attack Wei and captured Quwo.
The next year, Wei State surrendered to Qin State again.
Qin wanted to attack Qi, but Qi and Chu formed a vertical alliance, so Zhang Yi went to Chu to serve as prime minister.
When King Huai of Chu heard that Zhang Yi had come to Chu, he vacated a high-quality hotel and went to the hotel himself to arrange accommodation for him.
Said: Chu is a remote and humble country. Do you have anything to teach me?
Zhang Yi lobbied the King of Chu and said: If the king really wants to listen to my advice, he will cut off all ties with Qi and terminate the alliance. I am willing to ask the King of Qin to donate 600 miles of land to the Shang Dynasty, and let the women of Qin serve as concubines to serve the king.
The king of Chu was very happy to agree to his request.
The ministers came to congratulate the King of Chu, but only Chen Zhen mourned for him.
The King of Chu said angrily: I gained 600 miles of land without deploying troops or generals. My ministers congratulated me, but you were the only one who mourned for me. Why?
Chen Zhen replied: No, in my opinion, the land in Shangyu area will not only be unavailable, but Qi and Qin may also unite.
If Qi and Qin unite, great disaster will come to Chu. The king of Chu said: Can you explain the reason?
Chen Zhen replied: The reason why Qin valued Chu was because Chu had an alliance with Qi.
Now that all ties with Qi are cut off and the alliance is abrogated, Chu will be isolated.
Why did Qin not be content with pursuing an isolated and helpless Chu State, but gave it 600 miles of land?
When Zhang Yi returns to Qin, he will definitely break his promise to the king. This means severing diplomatic relations with Qi to the north and inviting disaster from Qin to the west. The armies of the two countries will inevitably attack Chu together.
I have properly come up with a countermeasure for the king. It is better to secretly unite with Qi State and sever relations on the surface, and send people to follow Zhang Yi to Qin State.
If Qin gives us land, it is not too late to sever diplomatic relations with Qi; if Qin does not give us land, it is in line with our strategy.
The King of Chu said: I hope Mr. Chen will shut up, stop talking, and wait until I get the land of Qin.
He gave Zhang Yi the seal of approval and also gave him a large amount of property.
So he severed relations with Qi, abolished the alliance, and sent a general to follow Zhang Yi to Qin to take over the land.
Zhang Yi returned to Qin State and pretended not to hold on to the rope of the carriage. He fell off the carriage and was injured. He did not go to court for three months. When the King of Chu heard about this, he said, "Isn't Zhang Yi because I have not completely severed ties with Qi State?"
He sent warriors to the Song Dynasty, borrowed Song's talisman, and went to the northern Qi State to insult the King of Qi. The Qi King was angry, cut off the talisman, and aggrievedly made friends with Qin.
Qin and Qi established diplomatic relations, and Zhang Yi came to court. He said to the envoy of the Chu State: I have a six-mile fiefdom granted by the King of Qin, and I am willing to dedicate it to the King of Chu.
The envoy from the Chu State said: I am here to take over Shang Yu's land of six hundred miles under the order of the King of Chu. I have never heard of six miles.
The envoy reported back to the King of Chu. The King of Chu was so angry that he immediately sent out troops to attack Qin.
Chen Zhen said: Can I open my mouth and speak?
Instead of attacking Qin, it is better to cede land to bribe Qin and join forces with him to attack Qi. We will take back the land we ceded to Qin and take it back from Qi as compensation. In this way, your country can still survive.
The King of Chu refused to listen and finally sent out his army and general Qu Gai to attack Qin.
Qin and Qi jointly attacked Chu, killing 80,000 officers and soldiers, and Qu Gai, and then seized the lands of Danyang and Hanzhong.
The State of Chu sent more troops to attack the State of Qin. They went to Lantian and launched a large-scale battle. The Chu army was defeated, so the State of Chu ceded two more cities and made peace with Qin.
Qin threatened Chu and wanted to get the land in Guizhou, and wanted to exchange it for land outside Wuguan.
The King of Chu said: I am not willing to exchange land. As long as I get Zhang Yi, I am willing to give up the central Guizhou area.
The King of Qin wanted to send Zhang Yi away, but he couldn't bear to say it.
Zhang Yi asked to go.
King Hui said: "The King of Chu is angry that your husband broke his promise to give Shang land, and he is deliberately retaliating against you."
Zhang Yi said: Qin is strong and Chu is weak. I have a good relationship with Jin Shang, the official of Chu. Jin Shang can flatter Zheng Xiu, the wife of Chu, and the king of Chu will obey all Zheng Xiu's words.
Besides, I was sent as an envoy to the State of Chu on the order of the king. How dare the king of Chu kill me?
If you kill me and obtain the land in central Guizhou for Qin, this is also my highest wish.
So he went to Chu as an envoy.
King Huai of Chu imprisoned Zhang Yi as soon as he arrived, intending to kill him.
Jin Shang said to Zheng Xiu: Do you know that you will be despised by the king?
Zheng Xiu said: Why?
Jin Shang said that the King of Qin loved Zhang Yi very much and planned to rescue him from captivity. Now he would use the land of the six counties of Shangyong to bribe the Chu State, marry a beautiful woman to the King of Chu, and use the women in the palace who are good at singing as dowries.
If the king of Chu values ​​the land, he will respect Qin. The beauties of Qin will be favored and honored, but the ladies will also be despised.
It is better to intercede for Zhang Yi and release him from prison.
So Zheng Xiu appealed to King Huai day and night, saying: As ministers, each serves his country.
Now that the land has not been handed over to Qin, King Qin sent Zhang Yi here, showing his respect for the king to the extreme.
If the king kills Zhang Yi before he returns the favor, the king of Qin will definitely be furious and send troops to attack Chu.
I request that we, mother and son, be allowed to move to the south of the Yangtze River and not be bullied and slaughtered by the Qin State like fish.
King Huai regretted it, pardoned Zhang Yi, and entertained him as generously as before.
Not long after Zhang Yi was released from prison, but before he left, he heard that Su Qin had passed away, so he persuaded King Huai of Chu: "Qin's land occupies half of the world, its military strength can withstand countries in all directions, its borders are dangerous, the Yellow River flows across it, and there are fortified areas on all sides that can be defended."
summary: Zhang Yi's diplomatic efforts extended to Chu, where he promised 600 li of land in exchange for Chu severing ties with Qi. King Huai of Chu agreed, but Zhang Yi reneged, offering only six li. This led to war, with Qin and Qi defeating Chu, seizing Danyang and Hanzhong. Zhang Yi later returned to Chu as an envoy, narrowly escaping execution through the intercession of Zheng Xiu, and convinced King Huai to ally with Qin. Zhang Yi also lobbied Han, Qi, Zhao, and Yan to submit to Qin, emphasizing Qin's military superiority and the futility of resistance. Each state eventually agreed to serve Qin, but after King Hui's death, King Wu of Qin distrusted Zhang Yi, leading to his departure to Wei, where he died as prime minister.
