translation:
King Qin Hui planned to reconcile them and asked his close associates for their opinions.
Some of the cronies on the left and right said it would be beneficial for them to reconcile, while others said it would be beneficial not to reconcile. King Hui could not make a decision on this matter.
Chen Zhen happened to return to the state of Qin. King Hui said: Sir, you left me and went to the state of Chu. Do you also miss me?
Chen Zhen replied: "Has your Majesty heard of Zhuang Fan, a native of Yue?"
King Hui said: I haven't heard of it.
Chen Zhen said: Zhuang Fan, a Yue man, became ill soon after he attained the title of Zhi Gui as an official in the State of Chu.
The King of Chu said: Zhuang Fan was originally a low-status person in the Yue Kingdom. Now he has reached the title of Zhigui and has become rich. I wonder if he still misses the Yue Kingdom?
Zhong Xie replied: Generally, people miss their hometown when they are sick. If Zhuang Xi misses the country of Yue, he will use the accent of the country of Yue when he groans. If he does not miss the country of Yue, he will use the tune of the state of Chu.
The King of Chu sent people to eavesdrop, but Zhuang Shun still spoke in the Yue accent.
Now, even if I am abandoned and run to Chu, will I lose the Qin accent? King Hui said: Well said.
Now Korea and Wei are at war, which has not been resolved for a whole year. Some people say to me that it is beneficial for them to reconcile, and some people say it is beneficial for them not to reconcile. I cannot make a decision. I hope that besides making suggestions for your monarch, you can also give me some advice.
Chen Zhen replied: Has anyone ever told the king about Bian Zhuangzi's murder of a tiger?
Zhuangzi was about to kill the tiger, but a boy in the hotel stopped him and said: Two tigers are eating cows. When they get the taste of the cow, they will definitely fight. Once they fight, the big one will be injured and the small one will die. If you chase the injured tiger and assassinate it, you will definitely gain the reputation of assassinating both tigers.
Bian Zhuang thought what he said made sense, and stood aside to wait for them. Soon, the two tigers fought. As a result, the older one was injured and the younger one died. Zhuangzi caught up with the injured tiger and killed it. As expected, he got the credit for killing both tigers.
Nowadays, the war between Han and Wei cannot be resolved for a year. This will inevitably damage the big country and perish the small country. If you pursue the injured country and attack it, this crusade will definitely gain two fruits of victory.
This is like Zhuangzi killing a tiger.
What is the difference between me advising for my king and advising for the king?
King Hui said: Well said.
Finally they were not reconciled.
As expected, the big countries were hurt and the small ones were in danger. Qin took the opportunity to send troops to attack them and defeated them. This was Chen Zhen's strategy.
Xishou was from the Yin and Jin Dynasties of the Wei State. His name is Yan and his surname is Gongsun. She has a bad relationship with Zhang Yi.
Zhang Yi went to Wei for the sake of Qin, and the king of Wei appointed Zhang Yi as prime minister.
Xishou thought it was disadvantageous for him, so he sent people to tell Han Gongshu: Zhang Yi has asked Qin and Wei to unite. He threatened: Wei will attack Nanyang, and Qin will attack Sanchuan.
The reason why King Wei valued Zhang Yi was because he wanted to obtain the land of Korea.
Besides, Nanyang in South Korea has been occupied. Why don't you entrust some political affairs to Gongsun Yan and ask him to go to the King of Wei to ask for credit? Then the exchanges between Qin and Wei will stop.
If this is the case, then Wei must seek to conquer Qin and abandon Zhang Yi, make friends with South Korea, and let Gongsun Yan serve as prime minister.
summary: Chen Zhen, a rival strategist, defended his loyalty to Qin against Zhang Yi's slander and later advised King Hui on the Han-Wei conflict, using the parable of Bian Zhuangzi killing two tigers to advocate non-intervention until both sides were weakened. This strategy succeeded, allowing Qin to attack and defeat both states.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传

translation:
The person who persuades all countries in the world to unite and stick to their covenants by faith is Su Qin. He was named Lord Wu'an and served as the prime minister of Yan, but he secretly planned with King Yan to conquer Qi and divide its land. He pretended to be guilty of King Yan and fled to Qi. King Qi took him in and made him prime minister. Two years later, when he was discovered, King Qi was furious and cut Su Qin's five horses into pieces on the execution ground.
It is obvious that Su Qin, a treacherous and hypocritical man, wants to run the whole world and unite the princes into one body. His strategy cannot succeed.
Today, the State of Qin and the State of Chu are adjacent to each other, and they should be close countries geographically.
If the king can listen to my suggestion, I would like to ask the king of Qin to send the prince to the state of Chu to be a hostage. The state of Chu will send the prince to the state of Qin to be a hostage. The daughter of the king of Qin will be married to the king, and a city with 10,000 households will be donated to the king. It will be the place where the king collects taxes and supplies Tang and Mu's tools. We will always be brothers and neighbors and never fight each other for life.
I don’t think there is a more appropriate strategy than this.
At this time, although the King of Chu had obtained Zhang Yi, it was difficult for him to give up the land in central Guizhou to Qin, and he wanted to agree to Zhang Yi's suggestion.
Qu Yuan said: The last time the king was deceived by Zhang Yi, when Zhang Yi came to Chu, I thought the king would boil him to death with a cauldron. Now that he has been released, I can't bear to kill him and still listen to his evil words. This is not good.
King Huai said: Agreeing to Zhang Yi's suggestion can save the land in central Guizhou, which is a good and beneficial thing.
It's not okay to betray him after you've already promised.
So he finally agreed to Zhang Yi's suggestion and formed an alliance with Qin.
Zhang Yi left Chu State and took the opportunity to go to South Korea and persuaded the King of Han: South Korea has a dangerous terrain and people live in mountainous areas. The food produced is either wheat or beans. Most of the food people eat is bean rice and bean leaf soup.
If there is no income for a year, people will not be able to eat even such poor food as chaff.
The land is less than 900 miles, and the food stored cannot last two years.
It is estimated that the total number of the king's soldiers does not exceed 300,000, including those orderlies and logistics personnel.
Excluding the soldiers guarding the posthouses and border fortresses, the existing army is only 200,000.
The Qin State's armed forces numbered more than one million, with thousands of chariots and tens of thousands of horses. The brave warriors galloped and leaped forward, without helmets and armed with weapons, and they threw themselves at the enemy in anger, too many to count.
The war horses of the Qin State are excellent. The horses gallop with their front hooves raised and their hind hooves in the air. They can jump more than two feet in one leap. There are so many such horses that they are countless.
The soldiers of the Six Kingdoms of Shandong wore helmets and armor to fight, but the Qin army threw off their shirts, barefooted and pounced on the enemy, holding heads in their left hand and prisoners in their right.
Compared with the soldiers of the Six Kingdoms of Shandong, the soldiers of Qin are like the brave strongman Meng Ben and the weak cowards; pressing down with huge power is like the brave strongman Wu Huo fighting against a baby.
summary: Xishou, another strategist, undermined Zhang Yi's influence in Wei by aligning with Han, eventually becoming Wei's prime minister and forcing Zhang Yi's departure. After Zhang Yi's death, Xishou served as Qin's prime minister and led a five-state alliance.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传

translation:
The uncle thought this was beneficial, so he entrusted political affairs to Xishou and asked him to contribute.
As expected, Xishou became the prime minister of Wei, and Zhang Yi left Wei.
Lord Yiqu came to pay homage to King Wei.
Xishou heard that Zhang Yi had become the prime minister of Qin again, and he was very jealous.
Xishou said to Mr. Yiqu: "Your country is far away. Today we are parting ways. It will be difficult to meet here again. Please allow me to tell you something."
He continued: If all the countries in the Central Plains do not unite to attack Qin, Qin will burn and plunder your country. If all the countries in the Central Plains unite to attack Qin, Qin will send lightly-armed envoys with valuable gifts to serve your country.
After that, the five kingdoms of Chu, Wei, Qi, Han, and Zhao jointly attacked Qin. Just then, Chen Zhen said to the king of Qin: Lord Yiqu is a wise monarch among the barbarian countries. It is better to give him money to appease his aspirations. King Qin said: OK.
So he presented a thousand pieces of brocade and a hundred beauties to Lord Yiqu. Lord Yiqu summoned his ministers for discussion and said, "Is this what Gongsun Yan told me?"
So he raised troops to attack Qin and defeated the Qin army under Li Bo City.
After Zhang Yi died, Xishou went to Qin to serve as prime minister.
He once wore the seals of five countries and became the leader of the Five-Nation Alliance.
Tai Shigong said: The Three Jin Dynasties produced many adaptable people. Those who advocated vertical and horizontal alliances to make Qin strong were mostly from the Three Jin Dynasties.
Zhang Yi's actions were worse than Su Qin's, but the reason why the society hates Su Qin is because he died first and Zhang Yi's publicity exposed the shortcomings of his collusive policy, which was used to echo his own ideas and promote the border policy.
All in all, these two are truly sinister people.
summary: Sima Qian concluded that Zhang Yi's actions were inferior to Su Qin's, but both were cunning figures whose strategies shaped the era.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张仪列传

translation:
Zhang Er was a native of Daliang, Wei State.
When he was young, he was a guest at the gate of Wei Gongzi Wuji.
Zhang Er was once expelled from the local register and fled to Waihuang.
There was a daughter of a wealthy family in Waihuang. She was very beautiful, but she married a stupid and mediocre husband. She therefore ran away from her husband and went to live with her father's old friend.
Her father's friend knew Zhang Er well, so he said to the woman: If you must marry a talented husband, marry Zhang Er.
The woman listened to his advice, finally severed her relationship with her husband, and remarried Zhang Er.
At this time, Zhang Er was freed from his embarrassment and began to travel extensively. The bride's family provided Zhang Er with generous supplies, so Zhang Er could attract guests from thousands of miles away.
So Huang became the county magistrate outside Wei.
His reputation grew.
Chen Yu was also a native of Daliang in Wei State. He loved Confucianism and had visited Kuxing in Zhao State many times.
A very wealthy Gongcheng family married his daughter to him because he knew that Chen Yu was not an ordinary mediocre person.
When Chen Yu was young, he served Zhang Er like his father, and the two established a friendship through adversity that they would never regret.
When the Qin Dynasty destroyed Daliang, Zhang Er's family lived in Waihuang. When Han Emperor Gaozu was still an ordinary commoner, he had many contacts with Zhang Er and lived in Zhang Er's family for several months at a time.
A few years after the fall of the Qin State and the Wei State, it was heard that these two men were famous people in the Wei State, and a reward was offered for their arrest. Anyone who captured Zhang Er would be rewarded with a thousand gold coins, and whoever captured Chen Yu would be rewarded with a reward of five hundred gold coins.
Zhang Er and Chen Yu changed their names and fled to Chendi together, where they worked as guards to support themselves. They lived opposite each other.
A minor official once whipped Chen Yu for a minor offense. Chen Yu was about to resist, but Zhang Er quickly stepped on him to signal him not to move and accept the whipping. After the minor official left, Zhang Er took Chen Yu under the mulberry tree and scolded him: "What did I tell you in the first place?"
Now that I have suffered a little humiliation, am I going to die at the hands of an official?
Chen Yu thought he was right.
The State of Qin issued an order proclamation, offering a reward for the arrest of the two of them. They also used their status as Li Zhengwei to convey the order to the residents of Lizhong.
Chen She revolted in Qizhou and when he invaded Chen, his army had expanded to tens of thousands.
Zhang Er and Chen Yu asked to see Chen She.
Chen She and his cronies had heard that Zhang Er and Chen Yu were talented many times, but they had never met them, and they were very happy after meeting them.
The heroes and elders of Chendi persuaded Chen She: "The general wears strong armor and holds sharp weapons. He leads the soldiers to attack the tyrannical Qin State, reestablishes the power of Chu State, revives the destroyed country, and continues the extinct heirs. Such merits should be called the king."
Moreover, we have to supervise and lead all the generals in the world. It is impossible not to call ourselves kings. I hope that the generals will be established as kings of Chu.
Chen She asked Chen Yu and Zhang Er for their opinions on this, and they replied: The Qin State is unethical and has occupied other people's countries, destroyed their country, cut off their descendants, and plundered the people's property.
summary: Zhang Er, a native of Daliang in Wei State, was once a guest of Wei Prince Wuji. After being expelled from the local register, he fled to Waihuang, where a wealthy woman left her foolish husband to marry him on the advice of her father's friend. With her family's support, Zhang Er traveled widely and gained fame, eventually becoming a county magistrate. Chen Yu, also from Daliang, was a Confucian scholar who married into a wealthy family. He served Zhang Er like a father, and they formed a close bond.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传

translation:
Today, the general has captured dozens of cities with 3,000 men and horses, and alone occupies a vast area of ​​Hebei. If he does not become king, it will not be enough to stabilize society.
Moreover, King Chen listened to the slander. If someone goes back to report it, he may be in trouble.
It is better to support his brother as king; otherwise, he will support the descendants of Zhao.
General, don't miss the opportunity. The time is tight and there is no time to breathe.
The military officials listened to their advice and proclaimed themselves King of Zhao.
Chen Yu was appointed as the general, Zhang Er as the prime minister on the right, and Shao Sao as the prime minister on the left.
He sent someone to report to King Chen. King Chen was furious after hearing this and wanted to kill all the families of the military officials and others, so he sent troops to attack King Zhao.
King Chen's Prime Minister Fang Jun dissuaded him and said: "To kill the families of military officials and others before Qin is destroyed is to establish another enemy as powerful as Qin."
It is better to take this opportunity to congratulate him and let him quickly lead the army to advance westward and attack Qin.
King Chen thought he was right and followed his plan. He moved the family members of Wu Chen and others to the palace and placed them under house arrest. He also made Zhang Er's son the King of Chengdu.
King Chen sent an envoy to congratulate King Zhao and asked him to quickly mobilize his troops westward into Guanzhong.
Zhang Er and Chen Yu advised the military officials: This is not the original intention of Chu State, but it is just a trick to congratulate the king.
After the King of Chu destroyed Qin, he would definitely add troops to Zhao.
I hope that the king will not march to the west, but send troops to the north to capture Yan and Dai, and to march south to capture Hanoi to expand his sphere of influence.
In this way, Zhao State relies on the river to the south and Yan and Dai to the north. Even if the King of Chu defeats Qin, he will not dare to force Zhao State.
King Zhao thought they were right, so instead of sending troops westward, he sent Han Guang to capture Yan, Li Liang to capture Changshan, and Zhang Xiao to capture Shangdang.
Han Guang's army arrived in Yan territory, and the Yan people took advantage of the situation to support Han Guang as king of Yan.
King Zhao, Zhang Er and Chen Yu went north to attack the border of Yan.
King Zhao once went out in his free time and was captured by the Yan army.
The generals of the State of Yan imprisoned him and demanded that they divide half of the land of the State of Zhao with him before releasing King Zhao.
The State of Zhao sent envoys to negotiate, but the Yan army killed them and demanded the division of the land.
Zhang Er and Chen Yu were worried about this matter.
A diligent soldier said to his comrades in the same dormitory: I want to lobby the Yan army on behalf of Zhang Er and Chen Yu, and come back in the chariot with King Zhao.
His companions who lived together laughed at him and said: "I sent more than a dozen envoys, but they were killed immediately when they arrived. How can you save King Zhao?"
So he ran to the Yan army's camp.
When the general of the Yan army saw him, he asked the Yan general: "Do you know what I am here for?"
General Yan replied: "You plan to rescue King Zhao." He asked again: "Do you know what kind of people Zhang Er and Chen Yu are?"
General Yan said: He is a wise man.
He continued: Do you know what their intentions are?
General Yan replied: "It's just King Zhao who wants to save them."
Zhao's orderlies smiled and said: "You still don't understand the plans of these two people."
Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu held riding whips and commanded the army to conquer dozens of cities in Zhao. Each of them wanted to face the south and become king. Are they willing to be someone else's minister for the rest of their lives?
Can ministers and kings be compared? He was just worried that the general situation was firm and he did not dare to divide the world into three parts and establish each as a king. Instead, he first established military ministers as kings in order of age to maintain the hearts and minds of the people of Zhao.
Now that the Zhao land has been pacified and the people have surrendered, these two people also want to divide the Zhao land and become kings on their own, but the time is not yet ripe.
Now, you have imprisoned the King of Zhao. These two people are nominally trying to save the King of Zhao, but in fact they want the Yan army to kill him so that they can divide the land of Zhao and become kings on their own.
The original strength of the Zhao State could easily capture the Yan State, not to mention the two virtuous kings supporting each other and attacking with the crime of killing King Zhao, and it would be even easier to destroy the Yan State.
The general of Yan thought what he said was reasonable, so he released King Zhao, and the soldiers drove King Zhao's chariot back together.
summary: After Qin destroyed Wei, both men became wanted fugitives. They changed their names and worked as guards in Chendi. When a minor official whipped Chen Yu, Zhang Er restrained him from resisting, advising patience. When Chen She rebelled, Zhang Er and Chen Yu advised him not to proclaim himself king too early but to restore the Six Kingdoms to weaken Qin. Chen She ignored them and made himself king. They then helped Wu Chen lead an army to conquer Zhao, where they persuaded him to declare himself King of Zhao. Chen Yu became general, and Zhang Er became prime minister.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传

translation:
After several months of stalemate with no reinforcements, Zhang Er was furious and resentful of Chen Yu. He sent Zhang Xiao and Chen Ze to rebuke Chen Yu, saying: "You and I formed a life-and-death friendship at the beginning, but now King Zhao and I may die overnight, and you have tens of thousands of troops and refuse to rescue us. Where is the friendship of life and death?"
If you want to keep your promise, why don't you fight the Qin army to the death?
There may still be a 1/20 chance of winning.
Chen Yu said: I consider that even if we advance forward, not only will we not be able to save Zhao, but our entire army will be wiped out in vain.
Besides, I don’t go and die together because I want to avenge King Zhao and Jun Zhang from Qin in the future.
Now we must die together, just like giving meat to a hungry tiger. What is the benefit?
Zhang Xian and Chen Ze said: The matter is imminent. We need to die together to establish integrity. How can we care about the future?
Chen Yu said: I have no regrets about dying, it is just that it will be useless, but I will definitely do what you two said.
So he sent 5,000 troops under the leadership of Zhang Xian and Chen Ze to attack the Qin army. When they reached the front line, the entire army was wiped out.
At this time, Yan, Qi, and Chu heard that Zhao was in danger and came to rescue him.
Zhang Ao also gathered more than 10,000 troops from Daidi to the north. They all set up camp next to Chen Yu and did not dare to attack the Qin army.
Xiang Yu's army cut off Zhang Han's tunnel many times, and Wang Li was short of military supplies. Xiang Yu led all his troops across the Yellow River and defeated Zhang Han.
Zhang Han led his troops to retreat, and then the armies of various princes dared to attack the Qin army that besieged Julu, and finally captured Wang Li.
Qin general Shejian committed suicide.
In the end, it was the State of Chu that saved the giant deer.
At this time, King Zhao Xie and Zhang Er were able to leave Julu City to thank the princes from all over the world.
When Zhang Er and Chen Yu met, they blamed Chen Yu for refusing to save Zhao and asked about the whereabouts of Zhang Xu and Chen Ze. Chen Yu said angrily: Zhang Xu and Chen Ze blamed me for dying together. I sent them to lead five thousand troops to try to attack the Qin army first. As a result, the entire army was wiped out and no one was spared.
Zhang Er didn't believe it and thought Chen Yu had killed them, so he questioned Chen Yu many times.
Chen Yu was furious and said: I didn't expect your resentment towards me to be so deep!
Do you think I am reluctant to give up my position as general?
He untied the seal and pushed it to Zhang Er.
Zhang Er was also shocked and refused to accept it.
Chen Yu stood up and went to the toilet.
Some guests advised Zhang Er: I heard that if you don't accept the gift from heaven, you will suffer disaster.
Now, General Chen has given you the seal. If you do not accept it, it is unlucky to go against God's will.
Hurry and receive it!
Zhang Er wore Chen Yu's seal and accepted his subordinates.
When Chen Yu came back, he was also resentful that Zhang Er had taken the seal without giving up, so he walked out quickly.
Zhang Er then gathered his army.
Chen Yu went alone with hundreds of his followers to fish and hunt in the lakes near the Yellow River.
From then on, there was an emotional rift between Chen Yu and Zhang Er.
Zhao Wangxie returned to Xindu to live, and Zhang Er followed Xiang Yu and other princes into Guanzhong.
summary: When Qin forces besieged Julu, Zhang Er and King Zhao Xie were trapped inside. Chen Yu, with insufficient troops, hesitated to rescue them. Zhang Er sent messengers to rebuke him, but Chen Yu's cautious approach led to a rift. After Xiang Yu defeated Qin at Julu, Zhang Er blamed Chen Yu for the deaths of his messengers. Chen Yu angrily offered his seal, which Zhang Er accepted, deepening their enmity.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传

translation:
In February of the first year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu enfeoffed the princes and kings. Zhang Er had always had many friends and many people spoke well of him. Xiang Yu also heard that Zhang Er was talented, so he divided the land of Zhao State and made Zhang Er the king of Changshan. He established Xindu and renamed Xindu Xiangguo.
Many of Chen Yu's old guests advised Xiang Yu: "Chen Yu and Zhang Er have also contributed to Zhao."
However, because Chen Yu did not follow him into Guanzhong, and because Xiang Yu heard that Chen Yu was in Nanpi, he granted him the three counties around Nanpi, moved King Zhao Xie's capital to Dai County, and changed his title to Dai Wang.
When Zhang Er went to his feudal state, Chen Yu became even more angry and said, "Zhang Er and I have equal merits. Zhang Er can be granted the title of king, but I can only be granted the title of marquis. This is unfair to Xiang Yu."
When King Tian Rong of Qi betrayed Chu, Chen Yu sent Xia Yuan to persuade Tian Rong: Xiang Yu, as the ruler of the world, is unfair. He enfeoffs good places to generals to be kings, and moves those who were kings to bad places. Now he has moved King Zhao to Dai County!
I hope your Majesty will lend me your troops and use Nanpi as a shield for your defense.
Tian Rong planned to establish a faction in Zhao State to oppose Chu State, so he sent troops to follow Chen Yu's command.
Therefore, Chen Yu mobilized all the troops from his three counties to attack Changshan King Zhang Er.
Zhang Er was defeated and fled. He thought that there was no one among the princes who could defect to him, so he said: Although the King of Han has an old friendship with me, Xiang Yu's power is strong, and he entrusted me, so I want to defect to Chu.
Duke Gan said: When the king of Han entered the pass, the five stars gathered in the Jingsu sky area.
Jingsutian District is the branch star of Qin State.
Whoever arrives first will definitely succeed.
Even if Chu is strong now, it will definitely belong to Han in the future.
Therefore, Zhang Er decided to go to Han.
The King of Han also returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, and was besieging Zhang Han's army in Feiqiu.
Zhang Er came to see the King of Han, who received him with great courtesy.
After Chen Yu defeated Zhang Er, he recovered all the land of Zhao State, brought King Zhao back from Dai County, and became the king of Zhao State. King Zhao was grateful to Chen Yu and made Chen Yu the king of Dai.
Because King Zhao was weak and the domestic situation had just stabilized, Chen Yu did not go to the feudal state and stayed to assist King Zhao, while he sent Xia Yue to garrison Daiguo as the prime minister.
In the second year of the Han Dynasty, the king of Han attacked the Chu State eastward and sent an envoy to inform the State of Zhao that he would attack Chu together with the State of Zhao.
Chen Yu said: As long as the king of Han kills Zhang Er, Zhao will obey.
So the king of Han found a man who looked similar to Zhang Er and beheaded him, and sent someone to take the head to Chen Yu.
Chen Yu then sent troops to help Han.
The King of Han was defeated west of Pengcheng. Chen Yu realized that Zhang Er was still alive, so he betrayed the King of Han.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, not long after Han Xin pacified Wei, he sent Zhang Er and Han Xin to break through Jingxing of Zhao State, kill Chen Yu on the banks of the Sashui River, and pursue Xiang State to kill Zhao Wangxie.
The Han Dynasty granted Zhang Er the title of King of Zhao.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Zhang Er died, and his posthumous title was King Jing.
Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao succeeded his father as King of Zhao, and Princess Lu Yuan, the eldest daughter of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, married King Ao of Zhao and became his queen.
In the seventh year of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gaozu passed by the State of Zhao from Pingcheng. The King of Zhao took off his coat, put on his sleeves, and personally served food and drinks from morning to night. His attitude was very humble, and he had the etiquette of a son-in-law.
However, Emperor Gaozu sat on the ground with his feet spread out like a dustpan and cursed King Zhao, being very arrogant to him.
Zhao Guoguo, Xiang Guangao, Zhao Wu and others were all over sixty years old and were Zhang Er's former disciples. They were bold and impulsive by nature, so they said angrily: Our king is a cowardly king!
He advised King Zhao: "When the heroes of the world came together, the talented ones were the first to be kings."
summary: Xiang Yu enfeoffed Zhang Er as King of Changshan but gave Chen Yu only three counties. Chen Yu, resentful, allied with Qi to attack Zhang Er, who fled to Han. Han Xin helped Zhang Er defeat and kill Chen Yu, and Zhang Er was made King of Zhao. He died in the fifth year of Han, succeeded by his son Zhang Ao.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传

translation:
Now that all three of my clans have been sentenced to death because of this incident, will I sacrifice my relatives for the sake of King Zhao?
But King Zhao did not resist, only we people participated.
He explained in detail his original intention to murder the emperor and the situation that King Zhao did not know the inside story.
So Duke Xie went to the palace and reported in detail what he had learned, and the emperor pardoned King Zhao.
The emperor appreciated Guangao as a man of faith, so he sent Duke Xie to tell him about the pardon of King Zhao, saying: King Zhao has been released from imprisonment.
Therefore, Guan Gao was also pardoned.
Guan Gao said happily: Is our King Zhao really released? Xie Gong said: Yes.
Duke Xie said again: The emperor praised you, so he pardoned you.
Guan Gao said: The reason why I survived being beaten to death was to prove that King Zhang Ao did not commit rebellion. Now that King Zhang Ao has been released, my responsibility has been remedied, and I will not regret it even if I die.
Besides, if a minister has a reputation of usurping, how can he have the dignity to serve the emperor again?
Even if the emperor does not kill me, am I not ashamed in my heart?
So he raised his head and cut his throat and died.
By this time, he was already famous throughout the world.
Not long after Zhang Ao was released, he was named Marquis of Xuanping because he married Princess Lu Yuan.
Therefore, the emperor praised Zhang Ao's guests. All the guests who followed King Zhang into the pass as slaves were all princes, ministers, and county guards.
Until the time of Xiaohui, Gaohou, Emperor Wen, and Xiaojing, the descendants of King Zhang's guests had become high-ranking officials with a salary of two thousand stone.
Zhang Ao died in the sixth year of high school.
Zhang Ao's son Zhang Yan was named King of Lu Yuan.
And because Zhang Yan's mother was Empress Lu's daughter, Empress Lu named him King of Lu Yuan.
The king of the Yuan Dynasty was weak and his brothers were small, so he divided the two sons of Zhang Ao's other concubines: Zhang Shou was named the Marquis of Lechang, and Zhang Chi was named the Marquis of Xindu.
After the death of Empress Gao, the Lu family did evil and did not follow the right path, so they were killed by the ministers. They also deposed King Lu Yuan, Marquis Lechang and Marquis Xindu.
After Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, he enfeoffed Zhang Yan, the original king of Lu Yuan, as Marquis of Nangong to continue the Zhang family's descendants.
Tai Shigong said: Zhang Er and Chen Yu are both virtuous people in world legends; their guests and servants are all heroes in the world, and all of them have achieved the status of minister in the country where they live.
However, when Zhang Er and Chen Yu were poor and frustrated, they trusted each other and vowed to live and die together. Isn't it true that they had no hesitation?
When they gained territory and fought for power, they ended up killing each other, hoping to eliminate each other.
Why did they sincerely admire and trust each other in the past, but then betrayed each other, and their attitudes towards each other were so perverse and violent? Aren’t they interacting with each other for the sake of power and interests? Although they have a high reputation and many guests, their actions are probably very different from Taibo Wu and Jizi Yanling.
summary: Zhang Ao married Princess Lu Yuan, daughter of Emperor Gaozu. When Gaozu treated him arrogantly, Zhang Ao's retainers Guan Gao and Zhao Wu plotted to assassinate the emperor. The plot was discovered, and Zhang Ao was arrested. Guan Gao took full responsibility, enduring torture to prove Zhang Ao's innocence. Gaozu eventually pardoned Zhang Ao, and Guan Gao committed suicide. Zhang Ao was later made Marquis of Xuanping. His descendants held high offices until the Lu clan's downfall led to their demotion, though some were later restored.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传

translation:
The general's eyes widened with anger, he let go of his courage and risked his life, just to eliminate cruelty and cruelty in the world.
Now he has just conquered Chen Di and proclaimed himself king, showing his selfishness in front of everyone in the world.
I hope the general will not become king. He quickly led his troops to the west and sent people to support the descendants of the Six Kingdoms as his own party members to increase the hostility to Qin.
The more enemies we make for it, the more dispersed its power will be. The more members we have, the stronger our troops will be. If this is the case, there will be no need to fight each other in the vast wilderness, and there will be no county towns to defend and attack. After eradicating the tyrannical Qin State, we can occupy Xianyang and issue orders to the princes.
The various vassal states can be reestablished after their destruction, and they can be inspired by kindness. If this can be done, then the great cause of the emperor will be successful.
Now that I am only king of Chen, I am afraid that all the princes in the world will become slack and disobedient.
Chen She did not listen to their opinions and proclaimed himself king.
Chen Yu once again advised King Chen and said: Your Majesty has dispatched the armies of Liang and Chu to advance westward. The top priority is to break through Hangu Pass. It is too late to recover the area north of the Yellow River. I have traveled extensively in Zhao State and am familiar with the outstanding people and geographical conditions there. I volunteered to lead an army to seize the land of Zhao State by surprise in the north.
Therefore, King Chen appointed his old friend Wu Chen from Chen as the general, Shao Sao as the guard, Zhang Er and Chen Yu as the left and right captains, and allocated an army of 3,000 people to seize the land of Zhao to the north.
Wu Chen and others crossed the Yellow River from Baimajin and went to various counties to lobby the local heroes and said: Qin's chaos and torture have been killing the people of the world for decades.
There were hard laborers building the Great Wall on the northern border, and soldiers were being recruited to garrison the Five Ridges in the south. There was turmoil at home and abroad, and the people were exhausted. Grains were collected on a per capita basis and collected with dustpans to support the expenses of the army. All the money was exhausted, and the people were in dire straits.
Coupled with severe harsh laws and torture, fathers and sons in the world have no peace.
King Chen rose up and first advocated for the world. He became king in Chu land. There was no one in the area of ​​two thousand miles who did not respond. Every family was filled with indignation and everyone was full of fighting spirit. Those who had grievances complained and those who had grievances took revenge. Each county killed their magistrates and magistrates, and each county killed their governors and lieutenants.
Now the great Chu State has been established, proclaimed king in Chen, and sent Wu Guang and Zhou Wen to lead a million troops to the west to attack the Qin army.
At this time, if you are not able to achieve the feat of becoming a prince, then you are not a hero among men.
Please plan for each other!
Everyone in the world agrees that they have suffered from the tyranny of Qin for a long time.
Using the power of the people of the world to attack the unprincipled king, avenge the father and brother, and complete the great cause of dividing the land, this is an opportunity that ambitious people cannot miss.
All the heroes thought this was correct.
So while marching and fighting, he gathered his troops. The army expanded to tens of thousands, and the military official named himself Lord Wu Xin.
summary: The historian comments that Zhang Er and Chen Yu, once loyal friends, became bitter enemies over power and territory, revealing that their bond was rooted in self-interest rather than true virtue.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张耳陈馀列传

translation:
Tingwei Zhang Shizhi was from Duyang, with the courtesy name Ji.
Lives with his brother Zhong.
Because his family had a lot of money, he became a knight and served Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty. He was not promoted within ten years and became unknown.
Zhang Shizhi said: Being a Langguan for a long time has depleted my brother's wealth and made people uneasy.
I want to resign and go home.
The lieutenant general Yuan Ang knew that he had both political integrity and talent, and regretted his departure. He asked Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty to appoint him as a visitor.
After Zhang Shizhi met with Emperor Wen, he stepped forward to state the big plans and policies that would benefit the country and the people. Emperor Wen said: Talk about things close to real life, don't talk lofty words, what you say should be implemented now.
So Zhang Shizhi talked about the Qin and Han Dynasties again, and talked for a long time about the reasons for the demise of the Qin Dynasty and the prosperity of the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Wen admired him very much and appointed him as an emissary.
Once, Zhang Shizhi followed Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty on a trip to the tiger enclosure. Emperor Wenwen of Han Dynasty asked about the status of various animals registered in the book. He asked more than a dozen questions. Lieutenant Shang Lin could only look here and there, but could not answer any of them.
The stingy man who was in charge of the tiger enclosure answered the questions raised by the emperor on behalf of Lieutenant Lin, and he answered them very comprehensively. I want to use this to show that I answer questions like a voice response and that I can't answer questions.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty said: Shouldn't an official be like this?
Lieutenant Shang Lin could not rely on him.
So Zhang Shizhi was ordered to let the stingy man serve as Lin Ling.
After a while, Zhang Shizhi stepped forward and said, "What kind of person does your Majesty think Jianghou Zhou Bo is?"
Emperor Wen said: He is an elder!
Asked again: What kind of person is Dongyang Hou Zhang Xiangru?
Emperor Wen once again replied: He is an elder.
Zhang Shizhi said: Both Jianghou and Dongyanghou are called elders, but these two are not good at talking when discussing things. If we do this now, will people follow this stingy man who talks endlessly and speaks sharply?
In the Qin Dynasty, officials who used dance-style tactics were reused, so the officials strived to be quick, harsh, and accountable. However, the disadvantage of this was that it only had the superficial form of official documents without the essence of compassion and sympathy.
Because of this, the king of Qin could not hear his own mistakes, and the country's power declined day by day. By the time of Qin II, the Qin country also collapsed.
Now that Your Majesty has promoted a stingy man to a higher level because of his sharp tongue, I am afraid that people all over the world will follow this trend and rush to use their rhetorical skills without pursuing reality.
Moreover, people in lower positions are influenced by those in higher positions as quickly as shadows follow the body and respond to sounds. Your Majesty must not be irrational in anything you do! Emperor Wen said: OK!
Therefore, the original plan was cancelled, and Shifu was no longer appointed as Shanglin Ling.
Emperor Wen got into the car and asked Zhang Shizhi to ride beside him. The car moved forward slowly.
Emperor Wen asked Zhang Shizhi about the shortcomings of Qin's government, and Zhang Shizhi told him truthfully. When he arrived at the palace, Emperor Wen appointed Zhang Shizhi as the bus commander.
summary: Zhang Shizhi, a Tingwei from Duyang, served Emperor Wen of Han but remained unknown for a decade. Yuan Ang recommended him as a visitor. Zhang advised the emperor on practical governance, discussing Qin's fall and Han's rise. Emperor Wen appointed him as an emissary. During a visit to a tiger enclosure, a keeper answered questions fluently while the Shanglin Lieutenant faltered. The emperor wanted to promote the keeper, but Zhang warned against valuing eloquence over substance, citing Qin's decline due to such practices. The emperor agreed and canceled the promotion. The historian comments that Zhang Shizhi's integrity and Feng Tang's insights on generalship are admirable, aligning with the principle of impartial governance.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传

translation:
Soon, the prince and King Liang entered the court in the same car, and they did not get off the car when they arrived at Simamen outside the palace. At that time, Zhang Shizhi stepped forward to stop the prince and King Liang from entering the palace.
They also reported to the emperor that they had committed the crime of "disrespect" by not getting out of the car outside the palace gate.
When Empress Dowager Bo learned about this, Emperor Wen took off his hat and said, "I blame my lax teaching of my son."
Empress Dowager Bo also sent envoys with her edict to pardon the sins of Prince Liang, so that Prince Liang and Prince Liang could enter the palace.
From this, Emperor Wen even more saw Zhang Shizhi's uniqueness and appointed him as a middle doctor.
After some time, Zhang Shizhi was promoted to Zhonglang General.
Following the emperor to Ba Ling, Emperor Wen of Han stood on the north side of Ba Ling and looked out.
At this time, Mrs. Shen also followed. The emperor showed her the road to Xinfeng with his hand and said: This is the road to Handan.
Then, he asked Mrs. Shen to play the harp, and Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty sang to the melody of the harp himself. He felt very miserable and sad, and turned back to the ministers and said: Alas!
Use the stone from Beishan to make a coffin, fill the gaps in the stone coffin with chopped ramie silk wadding, and then apply paint on it. How can it still be opened?
The attendants around me all said: That’s right.
Zhang Shizhi stepped forward and said: If there is something inside that can cause people to be greedy, even if the coffin is made of Nanshan, there will still be gaps; if there is nothing inside that can cause people to be greedy, even if there is no stone coffin, there will be no need to worry!
Emperor Wen praised him for speaking well.
Later he was appointed Tingwei.
Shortly thereafter, when the emperor was on patrol and passed the Zhongwei Bridge in the north of Chang'an City, a man suddenly ran out from under the bridge. The horse that the emperor was driving was frightened.
So he ordered the knights to capture the man and hand him over to Ting Wei Zhang Shizhi.
Zhang Shizhi interrogated that person.
The man said: I am a countryman from Chang'an County. I hid under the bridge when I heard the order to close the Qingdao Road.
After a long time, I thought the emperor's team had passed by, so I came out from under the bridge. I saw the emperor's motorcade and started running immediately.
Then the Tingwei reported to the emperor the punishment that the man deserved, saying that he had violated the prohibitions of Qingdao and should be fined.
Emperor Wen was angry and said: This man frightened my horse. Fortunately, my horse is tame and gentle. If it had been another horse, it might have injured me, but it was the Tingwei who sentenced him to a fine!
Zhang Shizhi said: The law is something that the emperor and the people of the world should abide by.
Now the law stipulates this, but the punishment must be increased, so the law cannot win the trust of the people.
At that time, your Majesty, you can just ask someone to kill him immediately.
Now that this person is handed over to Tingwei, who is the leader of fair law enforcement in the world, if there is a slight deviation, the law enforcers in the world will be arbitrarily light or heavy, won't the people be at a loss?
May your Majesty understand clearly.
After a long time, the emperor said: Ting Wei's sentence is correct.
Later, someone stole the jade ring in front of the throne of Gaozu Temple and was caught. Emperor Wen was angry and handed it over to Tingwei for punishment.
summary: Zhang later stopped the prince and King Liang from entering the palace without dismounting, reporting them for disrespect. The empress dowager pardoned them, and Emperor Wen promoted Zhang to Zhonglang General. At Ba Ling, the emperor lamented about his coffin, but Zhang argued that greed, not the coffin, determines security. The emperor praised him. As Tingwei, Zhang judged a man who startled the emperor's horse. The emperor wanted severe punishment, but Zhang insisted on the legal fine, stating the law must be trusted. The emperor relented. When someone stole from Gaozu Temple, the emperor demanded execution of the entire family, but Zhang argued the law prescribed only death for the thief. The emperor agreed after consulting the empress dowager.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传

translation:
Zhang Shizhi reported to the emperor the crime of stealing the ancestral temple's clothing and equipment according to the law and was sentenced to death.
The emperor was furious and said: "This man has acted so lawlessly that he stole the artifacts from the temple of the late emperor. I handed him over to the Tingwei for trial and wanted to punish him with genocide, but you blindly reported the punishment to me in accordance with the provisions of the law. This is not my original intention to respect and flatter the ancestral temple."
Zhang Shizhi took off his hat, kowtowed and apologized, saying: "This punishment is enough according to the law."
Moreover, when the charges are the same, the severity of the crime must also be distinguished.
Now if he steals the artifacts from the ancestral temple, he will be punished with genocide. If a stupid person digs up a handful of earth from Changling, what punishment will your Majesty use to punish him?
After some time, Emperor Wen and Empress Dowager Bo discussed the matter and agreed to Tingwei's verdict.
At that time, Lieutenant Tiaohou Zhou Yafu and Liang Guoguo's Prime Minister Shandu Hou Wang Tiankai saw Zhang Shizhi's impartiality in enforcing the law and became close friends with him.
Zhang Shizhi was praised by people all over the world.
Later, Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing ascended the throne. Zhang Shizhi was frightened and pretended to be sick.
He wanted to resign and leave, but he was worried that he would be executed. He wanted to apologize to Emperor Jing in person, but he didn't know what to do.
After using Wang Sheng's strategy, he finally saw Emperor Jing apologize and apologize, but Emperor Jing did not blame him.
Wang Sheng is a virgin who likes Huang Lao's theory.
Once he was called into the court, where all the three princes and nine ministers were standing. Wang Sheng, an old man, said: My garter is loose. He turned around and said to Zhang Tingwei: Kie the garter for me!
Zhang Shizhi knelt down and tied his garters.
Afterwards, someone asked Wang Sheng: Why did he humiliate Zhang Tingwei in the court and make him kneel to tie his garters?
Wang Sheng said: I am old and of low status. I expected that I would not be able to benefit Zhang Tingwei in the end.
Zhang Tingwei is a famous official in the world. I deliberately humiliated Zhang Tingwei and made him kneel down to tie his garters, hoping to use this method to strengthen his reputation.
After hearing this, all the ministers praised Wang Sheng's virtue and respected Zhang Tingwei.
Zhang Tingwei served Emperor Jing for more than a year and was demoted to the position of Prince of Huainan. This was because he had offended Emperor Jing in the past.
After some time, Zhang Shizhi died.
His son's name was Zhang Zhi, named Changgong. His official position was until he was a doctor, and he was later dismissed.
Because he could not cater to the powerful and prominent people at that time, he did not serve as an official again until his death.
Feng Tang, his grandfather was from Zhao during the Warring States Period.
His father immigrated to Daidi.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, it moved to Anling.
Feng Tang was famous for his filial piety at that time, and was recommended as the director of Zhonglang to serve Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty.
Once Emperor Wen passed by the official office where Feng Tang worked and asked Feng Tang: Why is this old man still working as a Langguan? Where is home?
Feng Tangdu answered truthfully.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty said: When I was in Daijun, my food supervisor Gao Qu talked to me many times about the talents of Zhao general Li Qi and told me about his fighting under Julu City.
summary: After Emperor Wen's death, Zhang feared Emperor Jing and sought Wang Sheng's advice. Wang humiliated Zhang in court by asking him to tie his garters, which elevated Zhang's reputation. Zhang later served Emperor Jing but was demoted and died.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传

translation:
They only know how to fight hard all day long, kill the enemy and capture prisoners, and go to the shogunate to report their merits. As long as one sentence is not consistent with the actual situation, the judge will punish them with the law.
The reward you deserve cannot be honored, but the judge will pursue it according to the law.
I foolishly thought that His Majesty's laws were too strict, the rewards too light, and the punishments too severe.
Moreover, Wei Shang, the governor of Yunzhong County, was only guilty of falsely reporting that he had killed six more enemies. Your Majesty handed him over to the judge, deprived him of his title, and sentenced him to one year in prison.
From this point of view, even if His Majesty gets Lian Po and Li Mu, he cannot reuse them.
I am indeed stupid, I have violated a taboo, I deserve the death penalty, I deserve the death penalty!
Emperor Wen was very happy and asked Feng Tang to go on a Hanjie envoy that day to pardon Wei Shang and re-appoint him as the governor of Yunzhong County. He appointed Feng Tang as the chariot and cavalry captain, in charge of the lieutenants and the chariot warriors of each county.
In the seventh year after Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty came to the throne and asked Feng Tang to be the prime minister of Chu State. He was soon dismissed.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he was looking for virtuous people, and everyone recommended Feng Tang.
Feng Tang was already over ninety years old and could no longer serve as an official, so he appointed his son Feng Sui as Lang Guan.
Feng Sui, courtesy name Wang Sun, is also an outstanding talent and is friendly to me.
Tai Shigong said: What Zhang Shizhi said about the elders, how he strictly abided by the law and did not cater to the emperor's wishes, and what Feng Gong said about appointing generals, are interesting!
Tasty!
As the saying goes: If you don't know a person well, you can tell by looking at the friends he makes.
The words of the two senior generals that they praised should be marked in the court.
"Shangshu" says: If there are no partialities and no cliques, the royal way will be smooth and broad; if there are no parties and no partialities, the royal way will be clear and clear.
Zhang Ji and Feng Gong are similar to this statement!
summary: Feng Tang, known for filial piety, served Emperor Wen. He compared Zhao generals Li Qi, Lian Po, and Li Mu, stating the emperor could not use them due to strict laws. He cited Wei Shang, a governor punished for minor errors despite his success against the Xiongnu. Emperor Wen pardoned Wei Shang and appointed Feng Tang as chariot and cavalry captain. Under Emperor Jing, Feng became prime minister of Chu but was dismissed. Under Emperor Wu, he was recommended but too old to serve; his son Feng Sui became an official.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/张释之冯唐列传

translation:
Tai Shigong said: Laws are used to guide people to do good, and punishments are used to prevent people from doing evil.
When the grammar and criminal laws were incomplete, kind-hearted people still exercised self-restraint and self-cultivation with fear, because the officials behaved well and never violated the rules and regulations.
As long as officials fulfill their duties and act according to principles, they can use it as an example to govern the world. Why must we use severe punishments?
Sun Shuao was a hermit from Chu State.
The Prime Minister Yu Qiu recommended him to King Zhuang of Chu, hoping that he would succeed him.
Sun Shuao was promoted to the state minister in three months after he became an official. He administered politics and taught the people, which made the officials and people harmonious and united, and the customs were very pure and beautiful. His administration was lenient and not harsh, but he always stopped prohibitions. Officials did not do evil or deceitful things, and there were no thieves among the people.
In autumn and winter, he encouraged people to go into the mountains to cut trees, and in spring and summer, he used the rising river water to transport the wood out of the mountains.
The people all have convenient ways to make a living and live happily. King Zhuang believed that the original coins of Chu State were too light, so he ordered the small coins to be minted into large coins. It was very inconvenient for the people to use them, and they gave up their own business one after another.
The chief executive in charge of the market reported to Prime Minister Sun Shuao: The market is in chaos, no one can do business there with peace of mind, and the order is very unstable.
Sun Shuao asked: How long has this been going on?
The city order replied: It has been three months.
Sun Shuao said: Needless to say, I will try to restore the market to its original state now.
Five days later, he went to the court to advise King Zhuang: "The reason why I changed the coins before was because I thought the old coins were too light."
Now the city magistrate has come to report that the market is in chaos, no one can make a living there with peace of mind, and the order is very unstable.
I request an immediate order to restore the old currency.
King Zhuang agreed and issued the order for three days, and the market returned to its original state.
The people of Chu State liked to ride in low carriages. The King of Chu thought that low carriages were not convenient for driving horses, so he wanted to order the low carriages to be raised.
Sun Shuao, the Prime Minister of the State, said: It is not good to issue government orders repeatedly, leaving the people at a loss as to what to do.
If you definitely want to raise the height of your car, I would like to ask the villagers to raise the threshold.
The passengers are all respectable gentlemen. They cannot get out of the car frequently just to pass the threshold, so naturally the base of the car will be made higher.
The king of Chu agreed to his request.
After half a year, people took the initiative to raise the height of their cars.
This is why Sun Shuao naturally obeyed his teachings without giving orders to control the people. People around him saw his words and deeds with their own eyes and imitated him. People who were far away watched the changes in the people around him and imitated him.
Therefore, Sun Shuao was not complacent in being in the position three times, because he understood that he had achieved it with his talents; he had no regrets in leaving the position three times, because he knew that he was not at fault.
Zichan was a senior official in the state of Zheng.
summary: Tai Shigong observed that laws guide people toward good, while punishments deter evil. Even when legal codes were incomplete, virtuous people exercised self-restraint because officials upheld rules. He argued that if officials fulfill their duties with integrity, severe punishments are unnecessary. Sun Shuao, a hermit from Chu, became prime minister after three months. His lenient yet effective governance fostered harmony, pure customs, and no deceit among officials or theft among people. He encouraged seasonal woodcutting and river transport, improving livelihoods. When King Zhuang replaced small coins with large ones, causing market chaos, Sun Shuao advised restoring the old currency, which stabilized the market within three days. To address low carriages, he suggested raising thresholds instead of issuing decrees; within half a year, people voluntarily raised their carriages. Sun Shuao remained humble in office and unregretful in dismissal, knowing his abilities and lack of fault.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传

translation:
When Zheng Zhaojun was in power, he appointed his favorite Xu Zhi as the prime minister of the country. The government was in chaos, the officials and the people were not in harmony, and the father and son were not harmonious.
Dagong Ziqi told Zheng Zhaojun about these situations, and Zhaojun appointed Zichan as the prime minister.
After Zichan was in power for one year, the libertines no longer played frivolously, the elderly no longer had to carry heavy loads, and the children no longer had to work in the fields.
After two years, transactions in the market will be fair and high prices will no longer be reserved.
Three years later, people did not close their homes at night and did not pick up lost items on the road.
Four years later, farmers will not have to take their farm tools home after work. Five years later, men will not need to perform military service. In case of a funeral, they will consciously perform funeral rites.
Zichan passed away in the twenty-sixth year of his rule in Zheng. The young men cried bitterly, and the old people wept like children, saying: "Zichan has left us and died. Who will the people rely on in the future?"
Gongyixiu was a doctor from the state of Lu.
Because of his outstanding talent and learning, he became the prime minister of the state of Lu.
He obeyed the laws and acted according to the principles without changing the regulations at all, so the officials behaved themselves in a correct manner.
He ordered officials not to compete for interests with the people, and high officials not to take advantage.
A guest brought fish to the Prime Minister Gong Yixiu's door, but he refused to accept it.
The guest said: I heard that you love fish very much, so why don’t you accept it?
Gong Yixiu replied: "It's because I love fish so much that I can't accept it."
Now that I am the Prime Minister, I can afford fish. If I am dismissed from office because I accepted your fish today, who will be willing to give me fish in the future?
So I can't accept it.
Gongyixiu ate the vegetables and thought they tasted good, so he pulled out all the mallow vegetables in his home and threw them away.
When he saw that the cloth he had woven was good, he immediately kicked his wife out of the house and burned the loom. He said: Are we going to leave farmers and weavers with nowhere to sell the goods they produce?
Shi She was the Prime Minister of King Zhao of Chu. He was strong, upright, honest and just. He was neither flattering nor timid.
On a trip to inspect various counties, a murderer happened to kill someone on the way. He pursued the murderer, who turned out to be his own father.
He let his father go and imprisoned himself when he returned.
He sent someone to tell King Zhao: The murderer is my father.
If you punish your father to establish political achievements, this is unfilial; if you abandon the law and condone crime, it is disloyal; therefore, I deserve the death penalty.
King Zhao said: "You chased the criminal but did not catch him. You should not prosecute the crime. You should go and manage the affairs of the country."
Shi She said: If you do not favor your father, you are not a filial son; if you do not abide by the king's law, you are not a loyal minister.
Your forgiveness of my sins is a favor from the Lord; serving your sentence and dying is your duty as a minister.
So Shi She refused to obey the king of Chu's order and cut his neck to death.
Li Li was a judge of Duke Wen of Jin.
He heard that the case was wrong and the murder was in vain. When he found out, he imprisoned himself and sentenced him to death.
summary: Zichan, a senior official in Zheng, became prime minister under Zheng Zhaojun after prior mismanagement. In one year, frivolity ceased, elders and children were relieved of burdens. In two years, market transactions became fair. In three years, people left doors unlocked and returned lost items. In four years, farmers left tools in fields. In five years, military service was unnecessary, and funerals were conducted properly. After 26 years, Zichan died; young and old mourned, lamenting the loss of their reliance. Gongyixiu, prime minister of Lu, upheld laws without alteration, ensuring officials behaved correctly. He forbade officials from competing with people for profit. When offered fish, he refused, fearing dismissal would end future gifts. He discarded tasty vegetables and burned his wife’s loom to avoid harming farmers and weavers. Shi She, prime minister of Chu, pursued a murderer who was his father. He released his father and imprisoned himself, stating that punishing his father was unfilial and condoning crime disloyal. Despite King Zhao’s pardon, he committed suicide to uphold duty. Li Li, a judge of Jin, discovered a wrongful execution. He imprisoned himself and sentenced himself to death. Duke Wen offered pardon, but Li Li insisted on accountability, refusing to shift blame. He committed suicide to uphold legal integrity.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传

translation:
Duke Wen said: Official positions vary, and punishments vary in severity.
This is the fault of your officials, not your fault.
Li Li said: My official position is that of a senior official, and I have never given up my high position to my subordinates. I have received a lot of official salary, and I have never given any benefits to them.
Now, I have made mistakes in investigating the case and a life was wasted, but I have to shift the blame to my subordinates. I have never heard of such a theory.
He refused to accept Duke Wen's order.
Duke Wen said: If you think you are guilty, am I guilty too?
Li Li said: There are laws and regulations for judges to decide cases. If you are wrongly sentenced, you will be punished personally, and if you are wrongly killed, you will be punished with death.
You made me a judge because I can listen to subtle details and decide difficult cases.
Now I heard the case wrongly and killed someone in vain, so I should be sentenced to death.
So he refused to accept Duke Wen of Jin's pardon and committed suicide with his sword.
Tai Shigong said: Sun Shuao said something, and the market order in Yingdu was restored.
Zichan died of illness, and the people of Zheng State burst into tears.
When Gongyixiu saw that his wife had finished weaving the cloth, he drove her out of the house.
Shi She let his father go and committed suicide to take the blame, which established King Zhao of Chu's reputation.
Li Li was wrongly convicted of murder and died with his sword, helping Duke Wen of Jin to rectify the country's laws.
summary: Tai Shigong concluded that Sun Shuao restored market order, Zichan’s death moved Zheng, Gongyixiu drove out his wife, Shi She’s suicide honored King Zhao, and Li Li’s death rectified Jin’s laws.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/循吏列传

translation:
Bian Que was from Miao, Bohai County. His surname was Qin and his name was Yue.
When he was young, he was the manager of a guesthouse.
A guest named Chang Sang came to the guest house. Only Bian Que thought he was a strange person and always treated him respectfully.
Chang Sangjun also knew that Bian Que was not an ordinary person. He had been coming and going for more than ten years. One day, he asked Bian Que to sit with him and quietly said to Bian Que: I have a secret medical prescription. I am old and I want to pass it on to you. Please don't leak it.
Bian Que said: "I respectfully obey my orders."
Then he took out the medicine in his arms and gave it to Bian Que, and said: Take this medicine with the dew on the grass and trees, and you will know many things in thirty days.
Then he took out all his secret recipes and gave them to Bian Que.
Suddenly the person disappeared, maybe he was not a mortal.
Bian Que took the medicine as he said for thirty days, and he could see the people on the other side of the wall.
Therefore, when diagnosing other people's diseases, you can see all the symptoms in the five internal organs, but on the surface, you are still taking the patient's pulse.
Sometimes he practiced medicine in the state of Qi, and sometimes he practiced medicine in the state of Zhao.
When he was in Zhao State, his name was Bian Que.
During the reign of Duke Zhao of Jin, the power of many officials was strong but the power of the monarch was weak. Zhao Jianzi was a doctor, but he was in charge of state affairs alone.
Zhao Jianzi fell ill and was unconscious for five days. The doctors were very worried and summoned Bian Que.
Bian Que came into the room to examine the patient and walked out. Doctor Dong Anyu asked Bian Que about his condition. Bian Que said: "His blood is normal, why should you be surprised!"
Once upon a time, Duke Mu of Qin was in this situation and fell into a coma for seven days before he woke up.
The day he woke up, he told Gongsun Zhi and Ziyu: I am very happy when I arrive at the Emperor of Heaven.
The reason why I stayed there for such a long time was that the Emperor of Heaven wanted to teach me.
The Emperor of Heaven told me that the Jin Kingdom was about to be in chaos and that the Five Dynasties would not be able to live in peace.
Then someone will become the overlord, and he will die soon after becoming the overlord.
The sons of overlords will make their country's men and women promiscuous. Gongsun Zhi wrote down these words and kept them. Later, the history books of Qin recorded this matter.
You have heard of the promiscuity of Duke Xian of Jin, the dominance of Duke Wen of Jin, and the indulgence of Duke Xiang of Jin after defeating the Qin army in Miao Mountain. You have heard of these.
Now your lord's illness is the same as his, and he will be cured in less than three days. He will definitely say something after he recovers.
After two and a half days, Zhao Jianzi woke up and told the doctors: I was very happy when I went to the Emperor of Heaven. I played with the gods in the center of the sky, where various musical instruments played many music and dances were performed. It was not like the music and dance of the three ancient times. The music was heart-stirring.
There was a bear trying to catch me, and the Emperor of Heaven ordered me to shoot it. I shot the bear, and it died.
A crab came over, I shot it again, and hit it again, and the crab died.
The Emperor was very happy and gave me two bamboo baskets with jewelry inside.
I saw my son beside the Emperor of Heaven. The Emperor of Heaven entrusted me with a Zhai dog and said: Give it to your son when he grows up.
The Emperor of Heaven told me: The Jin Kingdom will decline from generation to generation, and will perish after seven generations.
The Qin people will defeat the Zhou people to the west of Fan Kui, but they will not be able to possess his power. After hearing these words, Dong Anyu recorded and collected them.
People told Zhao Jianzi what Bian Que had said, and Zhao Jianzi gave Bian Que 40,000 acres of land.
Later, Bian Que passed through Guo State.
When the prince of the Guo Kingdom died of illness, Bian Que came to the gate of the palace of the King of Guo and asked a concubine who was fond of medicine: What disease did the prince have? Why did the capital hold rituals to ward off evil spirits and diseases more than many other things?
summary: Bian Que, a physician from Bohai County, was originally named Qin Yue. As a young innkeeper, he met a mysterious guest named Chang Sang, who recognized his potential and gave him a secret medical prescription. After taking the medicine for thirty days, Bian Que gained the ability to see through walls and diagnose illnesses internally. He practiced medicine in Qi and Zhao, where he became known as Bian Que. During the reign of Duke Zhao of Jin, Zhao Jianzi fell unconscious for five days. Bian Que diagnosed him, noting his blood was normal, and predicted he would recover in three days, similar to a past episode involving Duke Mu of Qin. Zhao Jianzi indeed woke up after two and a half days, recounting a vision of the Emperor of Heaven. He rewarded Bian Que with 40,000 acres of land.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传

translation:
The concubine said: The prince's disease is caused by the irregular circulation of blood and qi, the intertwining of yin and yang and the inability to drain it. It violently breaks out on the surface of the body, but in fact the internal organs are damaged.
The human body's righteous energy cannot stop the evil energy, and the evil energy accumulates and cannot be released. Therefore, the yang energy weakens and the yin evil becomes strong, so the person suddenly faints and dies.
Bian Que asked: When did he die?
The concubine replied: From the time the rooster crows to now.
Asked again: Has it been buried?
He replied: Not yet, he died less than half a day ago.
Please inform Mr. Guo that I am a Qinyue native of Bohai County, and my home is in Midi. I was unable to look up to the king's majesty and pay homage to him.
I heard that the prince passed away unfortunately and I can revive him.
The concubine said: Sir, are you not talking nonsense?
Why do you say the prince can be resurrected!
I heard that in ancient times, there was a doctor named Yu Fu. He did not use decoctions, medicinal wine, trowels, needles, needles, guides, massages, medicinal irons, etc. He could identify the location of the disease as soon as he undressed and examined the acupoints of the five internal organs, then cut the skin and muscles, dredged the meridians, and tied them Tendons, massage the brain, touch the bones, straighten the diaphragm, cleanse the stomach, cleanse the five internal organs, cultivate the essence, and change the expression and complexion. If the gentleman's medical skills can be like this, then the prince can be reborn; if he can't do this, but you want to resurrect him, you can't deceive the baby who just learned to laugh.
After a long time, Bian Que looked up at the sky and sighed and said: The treatment methods you mentioned are like looking at the sky through a bamboo tube or looking at patterns through the gaps.
The treatment method I use can tell the cause of the disease without taking the patient's pulse, looking at the face, listening to the voice, or observing the patient's posture and expression.
If you know the external manifestations of a disease, you can infer the internal causes; if you know the internal causes of the disease, you can infer the external manifestations.
Diseases in the human body will be reflected from the body surface, and based on this, patients thousands of miles away can be diagnosed. I have many ways to make decisions, and I cannot just look at the problem from one angle.
If you think what I said is untrue, try going in and examining the prince. You should hear his ears ringing, see his nose flaring, and feel his legs and genitals, which should still be warm.
After hearing Bian Que's words, the concubine's eyes were dull and he could not blink, his tongue was stuck out and he could not speak. Later, he went in and told Guo Jun what Bian Que had said.
Guo Jun was very surprised after hearing this. He went out of the inner court to meet Bian Que at the middle gate of the palace and said, "I have heard about your noble moral character for a long time, but I have never had the opportunity to meet you."
This time, sir, you are passing through our small country. I hope you can help us. I, the king of this remote country, am so lucky.
As long as the husband is here, my son can be saved. Without the husband, he will throw his body into the wild and fill the ravines, and he will never come back.
Before he finished speaking, he started sobbing with sadness, his mind was in a daze, and he shed tears for a long time. The teardrops rolled down and stuck to his eyelashes. He couldn't restrain his sorrow, and his appearance and expression changed.
summary: In Guo State, Bian Que encountered a prince who had seemingly died. He explained the prince suffered from "corpse disease," caused by an imbalance of yin and yang, and was not truly dead. Using acupuncture and medicinal applications, Bian Que revived the prince, though he insisted he could not resurrect the dead, only help those who could recover.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传

translation:
Bian Que said: Your prince's disease is what people call corpse disease.
That's because the Yang Qi sinks into the Yin vessels, and the pulse Qi entangles and impinges on the stomach. The meridians are damaged and the meridians are blocked. They flow into the lower burner and the bladder respectively. Therefore, the Yang vessels sink and the Yin Qi rises. The Yin and Yang Qi converge, block each other, and cannot be unblocked. The yin energy reverses upward movement, and the yang energy has to move inward. The yang energy is in vain stirring in the lower part but cannot rise. The upper part is blocked and cannot be driven by the yin energy. There are veins above that isolate the yang energy, and there are muscles and joints below that destroy the yin energy. In this way, the yin energy is destroyed and the yang energy is isolated, making the person's complexion decayed and the blood vessels confused, so the person's body becomes as quiet as if he was dead.
The prince actually did not die.
Because if yang attacks yin and blocks the internal qi, it can be cured; if yin attacks yang and blocks the internal qi, it will die.
These conditions will suddenly occur when the five internal organs are reversed.
A good doctor can cure the disease, a bad doctor can endanger the patient through confusion.
Bian Que then asked his disciple Ziyang to sharpen the needle stone and use Sanyang and Wuhui to inject needles.
After a while, the prince woke up.
He also asked his disciple Zi Bao to prepare a medicinal iron that could penetrate into the body for five minutes, and then mix and boil the medicine with eight prescriptions, and then apply it alternately under the two flanks.
The prince was able to sit up.
After further harmonizing the yin and yang, my body returned to the same as before after just taking the decoction for twenty days.
Therefore, people all over the world believe that Bian Que can resurrect the dead.
Bian Que said, "I can't resurrect the dead. He should live. All I can do is help him recover."
When Bian Que arrived in Qi, Marquis Huan of Qi treated him as a guest.
He went to the court to pay homage to Marquis Huan and said, "You have a small illness between your skin and muscles. If it is not treated, it will go deep into your body."
Marquis Huan said: I am not sick.
After Bian Que walked out of the palace, Huan Hou said to the people around him: Doctors love utilitarianism and want to attribute the cure of people to their own merits.
Five days later, Bian Que went to see Huan Hou again and said, "Your disease is already in your blood. If you don't treat it, it may go deep into your body."
Marquis Huan said: I am not sick.
After Bian Que went out, Marquis Huan was unhappy.
Five days later, Bian Que went to see Huan Hou again and said, "Your disease is already in the intestines and stomach. If it is not treated, it will invade deeper into the body."
Marquis Huan refused to answer.
After Bian Que went out, Marquis Huan was unhappy.
Five days later, Bian Que went there again. When he saw Huan Hou, he backed away and ran away.
Marquis Huan sent someone to ask him why he ran away.
Bian Que said: If the disease is between the skin and flesh, decoctions and medicinal irons can cure it; if the disease is in the blood, acupuncture and stone can cure it; if the disease is in the intestines and stomach, medicinal wine can cure it; if the disease enters the bone marrow, even the God in charge of life can do nothing.
Now that the disease has entered the bone marrow, I dare not ask for treatment.
Five days later, Marquis Huan fell seriously ill and sent for Bian Que. Bian Que had already fled Qi.
Marquis Huan fell ill and died.
If Marquis Huan could know in advance the hidden symptoms and let good doctors diagnose and treat them as early as possible, then the disease could be cured and his life could be saved.
People worry that there are too many diseases, and doctors worry that there are too few treatments.
summary: When visiting Qi, Bian Que warned Marquis Huan of a minor illness between his skin and muscles. The marquis ignored him, and over successive visits, the disease progressed to his blood, then intestines and stomach, and finally to his bone marrow, where it became incurable. Marquis Huan died five days after Bian Que fled, illustrating the importance of early treatment.
