translation:
Therefore, there are six types of illness that cannot be cured: those who are arrogant, indulgent and unreasonable are the first incurable; those who despise the body and value money are the two incurable; those who dress inappropriately and eat improperly are the three incurable; those who have Yin and Yang disorder and the five internal organs are not functioning properly are the four incurable; those who are very weak and unable to take medicine are the five incurable; those who are superstitious in witchcraft and do not believe in medical skills are the six incurable.
It is very difficult to cure a situation like this.
Bian Que's reputation spread throughout the world.
When he arrived in Handan, he heard that the local people respected women, so he became a doctor to treat women's diseases; when he arrived in Luo, he heard that Zhou people respected the elderly, so he became a doctor specializing in treating deafness, blindness, limbs, and pain; when he arrived in Xianyang, he heard that Qin people loved children, so he became a doctor to treat children's diseases; he changed the scope of his treatment according to the customs of various places.
Li Xi, the imperial physician of Qin, knew that his medical skills were not as good as Bian Que's, so he sent someone to assassinate Bian Que.
Up to now, people all over the world who talk about pulse diagnosis methods follow Bian Que's theory and practice.
This man in Taicang was the chief officer in charge of the granary in the capital of Qi State. He was from Lingan, his surname was Chunyu, and his given name was Yi.
Young but fond of medical skills.
Eight years after Han Gao's death, he once again studied medicine with Gongcheng Yangqing from Yuanli in the same county.
At this time, Yang Qing was over seventy years old and had no descendants who could inherit the medical skills, so he asked Chunyu Yi to put aside all the medical prescriptions he had learned before, and then gave him all the secret recipes he had mastered. He also taught him the pulse books of Huangdi and Bian Que, and the method of diagnosing diseases by observing different colors on the face, so that he could know the patient's life and death in advance, determine difficult diseases, judge whether they could be cured, and the theory of pharmaceuticals.
After studying for three years, he cured people's illnesses, predicted death and life, and accomplished many things.
However, he traveled among the vassal states to practice medicine and study, and did not take care of his family. Sometimes he refused to treat others, so many patients resented him.
In the fourth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, someone wrote to the court to accuse him. According to the criminal law, he had to be escorted to Chang'an in a carriage.
Chunyu Yi had five daughters who followed him and cried.
He got angry and cursed: If you don't give birth to a boy, there will be no one available at the critical moment!
So the youngest daughter Tiying was very sad after hearing her father's words, so she followed her father westward to Chang'an.
She wrote to the court and said: My father is an official of the court. The people of Qi State praise him for his integrity and justice. Now he has violated the law and been sentenced.
I am very sad that people who are executed cannot regenerate, and those who are disabled by torture cannot recover. Even if they want to change their ways, there is no way to do it, and in the end they cannot do so.
I would rather join the government and become a slave to atone for my father's sins and give him a chance to reform.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty read Tiying's petition, felt compassion for her, and pardoned Chunyu Yi, and abolished corporal punishment that year.
Chunyu Yi lived at home, and the emperor issued an edict asking him how many people had cured people and made decisions about life and death, and what their names were.
The question asked by Chunyu Yi of Taicang before the imperial edict was: What are the specialties of medical skills and what diseases can they cure?
summary: Bian Que's fame spread, and he adapted his practice to local customs—treating women in Handan, the elderly in Luo, and children in Xianyang. However, Li Xi, the Qin imperial physician, jealous of his skills, had him assassinated. Despite this, Bian Que's methods in pulse diagnosis endured. The text then shifts to Chunyu Yi, a Taicang official from Qi, who studied medicine under Gongcheng Yangqing. Yangqing taught him the pulse books of Huangdi and Bian Que, along with diagnostic methods. After three years, Chunyu Yi became skilled but faced legal trouble in the fourth year of Emperor Wen's reign. His daughter Tiying petitioned the emperor, offering to become a slave to atone for his crimes. Moved by her plea, the emperor pardoned Chunyu Yi and abolished corporal punishment. The historian concluded that Bian Que suffered due to his medical skills, while Chunyu Yi faced punishment but was saved by his daughter Tiying's petition, reflecting Laozi's saying that beautiful things are unlucky.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/扁鹊仓公列传

translation:
A man named Xin from the Imperial Palace of Qi State was ill. I went to his house for diagnosis and treatment. After taking his pulse, I told him: It is the pulse Qi of a fever. However, due to summer heat, excessive sweating and weak pulse, it will not lead to death.
He also said: I got this disease when I bathed in running water when the weather was very cold, and my body became hot after bathing. He said: Well, that's it!
Last winter, when I was on an envoy to the State of Chu for the King of Qi, I walked to the Yangzhou River in Ju County. I saw that the Ju Bridge was badly damaged.
I immediately prepared a liquid decoction and fire medicine for him to drive away the heat evil. After taking one dose of the medicine, he no longer sweated. After taking two doses of the medicine, the fever subsided. After taking three doses, the disease stopped.
After letting him take the medicine for another twenty days, he felt like a healthy person.
The reason why I knew about his illness was because when I checked his pulse, I found that his pulse belonged to the "Bingyin pulse" where heat evil merges into the body.
Pulse theory says: Death caused by internal heat and external heat being confused and intertwined.
When I took his pulse, I found no internal heat and external heat mixed together, but they were both Yin pulses.
Those with Yin pulse and smooth pulse can be cured by Qing method. Although the heat evil is not completely eliminated, it can still be cured and life saved.
I diagnosed that his kidney qi was sometimes heavy and turbid. I could vaguely detect this situation at Taiyin Cunkou, which was water qi.
The kidneys are responsible for the movement of fluids, so we know his condition from this.
If it is not treated for a while, it will become a disease with alternating colds and hotness.
The Queen Mother of the King of Qi was ill and summoned me to check her pulse. I said: It is a disease caused by wind-heat attacking the bladder, making it difficult to defecate and defecate, and the urine is red in color.
I gave her the gunpowder decoction. After one dose, she was able to defecate. After two doses, she was cured and her urine was the same color as before.
This is a disease caused by urinating while sweating. The disease is caused by taking off clothes and letting the sweat dry.
The reason why I knew about the illness of the Queen Mother of Qi was because when I took her pulse, I found that the opening of the Taiyin was moist, which was due to wind-induced pulse energy.
Pulse theory says: The pulse is large, solid and strong when the pulse is cut forcefully, and is large, tense and strong when the pulse is cut gently, which indicates kidney disease.
But when I took the pulse at the kidney area, the situation was opposite. The pulse was thick and restless.
A thick pulse indicates a disease in the bladder; a restless pulse indicates heat in the middle burner, and the urine is red in color.
Cao Shantao in Zhangburi, Qi State, fell ill. After checking his pulse, I said: This is Fei Xiaobing disease, combined with cold and heat syndrome.
I told his family: This disease is fatal and cannot be cured.
You just satisfy the sick person's request and provide for him, and there is no need to treat him any more.
Medical theory says: This disease will cause you to go crazy and run around in three days, and you will die in five days.
Then he died as expected.
Shanta's illness was caused by having sex after being angry.
The reason I knew about Shantao's illness was because I took his pulse and found out from the pulse that he had lung-qi heat.
summary: Chunyu Yi later detailed his medical cases to the emperor. He diagnosed a censor with gangrene from excessive drinking and sexual activity, predicting death in eight days, which occurred. He treated the King of Qi's son for a gas diaphragm disease caused by melancholy, curing him with a qi decoction. Another patient, Xun, had a hernia from sexual intercourse, treated successfully with fire medicine. A palace official named Xin had a fever from bathing in cold water, cured with a liquid decoction. The Queen Mother of Qi suffered from wind-heat affecting the bladder, treated with gunpowder decoction. Cao Shantao had a fatal lung disease from anger and sexual activity, dying as predicted. Pan Manru died from a mast disease caused by drinking and sex, as diagnosed. Zhao Zhang had wind disease from alcoholism, dying later than predicted due to his porridge diet. The King of Jibei had wind syndrome from sweating on the ground, cured with medicinal wine. Sikong Chu's wife had a hernia from suppressed urination and sex, treated with moxibustion and decoction. A wet nurse had fever from excessive drinking, cured with acupuncture. A maid named Shu died from spleen damage due to sweating, as predicted. A doctor had dental caries from poor hygiene, treated with moxibustion and rinses. A pregnant woman with dystocia was given hyoscyamus powder to deliver. A servant with spleen damage died in spring, as foreseen. King Shichuan had a fever from washing hair, cured with cold water and acupuncture. Song Jian had kidney paralysis from lifting heavy objects, treated with a soft decoction. A maid named Han had internal cold from unfulfilled desire, cured with medicine and moxibustion. A woman with pinworm disease was treated with a purgative. Sima Chunyu had Dongfeng disease from overeating and running, cured with fire agent soup. A man named Po Shi died from lung damage after a fall, as predicted. A doctor named Sui developed gangrene from improper use of Five Stone Powder, dying as warned. The King of Qi, as Marquis of Yangxu, had paralysis from sexual intercourse, cured with gunpowder porridge. Cheng Kaifang developed tracheitis from drinking and wind, becoming paralyzed and mute. Xiang Chu died from male hernia after strenuous activity, as predicted.

translation:
Asked again: Who did your teacher Yang Qing study from?
Do the princes of Qi know about him?
He replied: I don’t know who Yang Qing’s teacher is?
Yangqing's family was very wealthy. He was proficient in medical skills, but he refused to treat people. Perhaps because of this, he was not famous.
Yang Qing told me again: Never let my descendants know that you learned medical skills from me.
Asked again: How did your teacher Yang Qing fall in love with you? Why do you want to teach you all the secret medical skills?
He replied: I didn’t know that my teacher Yang Qing’s medical skills were exquisite.
I later learned that it was because when I was young, I liked various medical techniques and prescriptions. I tried his prescriptions, and most of them were effective and exquisite.
I heard that Gongsun Guang of Tangli in Shichuan was good at using ancient medical prescriptions, so I went to see him.
I can be his student and learn from him the medical prescriptions for regulating yin and yang and the medical theories passed down orally, and I will record them all.
I want to learn all his exquisite medical skills. Gongsun Guang said: I have brought out all my secret medical skills. I will not be gracious to you. I am already old and there is nothing left for you to learn.
These are the exquisite medical prescriptions I learned when I was young. I teach them all to you. Don’t teach them to others.
I said: I am very lucky to be able to serve and study in front of you and get all the secret recipes.
Even if I were to die, I would not dare to pass it on to others casually.
After a few days, Gongsun Guang had nothing to do, so I made an in-depth analysis and discussion of medical prescriptions. He thought that my discussion of the medical prescriptions of the past dynasties was wise.
He said happily: You will definitely become a Chinese doctor.
The medical skills I am good at are all neglected. My compatriots who live in Linyi are good at medical skills, but I am not as good as him. His medical prescriptions are very wonderful and cannot be understood by ordinary people.
When I was middle-aged, I wanted to ask him for advice. My friend Yang Zhongqian disagreed and said: You are not the kind of person who can learn medical skills.
I must go with you to see him, and he will know that you love medicine. He is also old, but his family is wealthy.
Before I went there, it happened that Yang Yin, the son of Yang Qing, came to present a horse to the King of Qi, and presented it to the King of Qi through my teacher Gongsun Guangjin. Because of this, I became familiar with Yang Yin.
Gongsun Guang entrusted me to Yang Yin again and said: Chunyu Yi likes medical skills. You must treat him well. He admires the way of saints.
So he wrote a letter recommending me to Yang Qing, so I got to know Yang Qing.
I served Yang Qing respectfully and cautiously, so he liked me.
He also asked: Have any officials or common people ever learned medical skills from you? Has anyone learned all your medical skills? Where are they from?
He replied: Linshan was born in Songyi. He asked me for advice, and I taught him how to look at his face and diagnose diseases. He studied for more than a year.
Gao Ming and Wang Yu, the imperial doctors sent by the King of Jibei, asked me for advice. I taught them the distribution of meridians up and down and the connection positions of abnormal meridians. I often discussed the location of acupoints and the direction of evil and good and reverse when the energy of the meridians circulates. I taught them how to select the acupoints that need meteorite acupuncture treatment for diseases. I learned it for more than a year.
King Sichuan often sent Feng Xin, an officer in charge of horses in the Taicang Department, to ask me to teach him medical skills. I taught him the massage techniques, how to use medicines, and how to determine the nature and taste of medicines and their compatibility to prepare decoctions.
Gao Yonghou's family minister was named Du Xin. He liked diagnosing pulses and came to study. I taught him the distribution of upper and lower meridians and "Five Color Diagnosis", and he studied for more than two years.
Linyi called a man named Tang An to study. I taught him "Five Color Diagnosis", the location of the upper and lower meridians, "Odd Cough Technique", and the principles of the four seasons and the corresponding yin and yang. Without success, he was appointed as the doctor of the King of Qi.
He also asked: Can you make no mistakes when diagnosing and treating people's illnesses and determining their life and death?
He replied: When I treat a patient, I must first feel his pulse and then treat him.
summary: Chunyu Yi explained that disease names often overlap, requiring careful pulse diagnosis to distinguish them. He noted that patients' deaths sometimes deviate from predictions due to diet or improper treatment. He avoided serving as a court physician, traveling to learn from multiple teachers. His teacher Yangqing, from a wealthy family, taught him secretly. Chunyu Yi also taught several students, including Songyi, Gao Ming, Wang Yu, Feng Xin, Du Xin, and Tang An, though not all mastered his skills. He admitted that errors in pulse diagnosis could lead to mistakes in predicting outcomes.

translation:
Since ancient times, only those who have received destiny can become kings, and the rise of kings does not depend on destiny through divination!
This situation was particularly prevalent in the Zhou Dynasty and can still be seen in the Qin Dynasty.
When the kings of the Han Dynasty came to Beijing to inherit the throne, they were also left to the fortune tellers.
As for the emergence of diviners, they began to appear since the rise of the Han Dynasty.
Lord Sima Ji is from Chu State.
He was doing divination in the east city of Chang'an.
At this time, Song Zhong was appointed as a doctor, and Jia Yi was appointed as a doctor. One day, the two of them went out to the court to take a bath and take a break. While walking, they discussed and learned the governance methods of the previous kings and saints, and extensively explored the world and human affairs. The two looked at each other and sighed.
Jia Yi said: I heard that ancient saints, if they were not officials in the court, must be among the ranks of diviners and doctors.
Now, I have seen the three princes, nine ministers and the sergeants and officials of the court, and I can know their talents, learning and character.
Let’s try to observe the soothsayer’s style.
The two of them went to the city in the same car and visited the divining restaurant.
It had just rained, and there were very few people on the road. Lord Sima Ji was sitting leisurely in the pavilion, with three or four disciples accompanying him, explaining the principles of heaven and earth, the movement of the sun and the moon, and the origin of good and bad luck in yin and yang.
The two doctors bowed twice to Lord Sima Ji.
Master Sima Ji looked at their appearance and saw that they seemed to be knowledgeable people, so he returned the courtesy and asked his disciples to lead them to sit down.
After sitting down, Sima Jizhu re-explained what he had said before, analyzed the origin and end of heaven and earth, the movement of the sun, moon and stars, distinguished the differences between benevolence and righteousness, listed the signs of good and bad luck, and talked about thousands of words, all of which were logical.
Song Zhong and Jia Yi were surprised and understood. They adjusted their crowns and belts, straightened their clothes, sat respectfully, and said, "I see your appearance and listen to your conversation. I have never seen anything like this in the world of today."
But why is your current status so low and why is your career so dirty?
Sima Jizhu laughed loudly and said: "It seems that the two doctors are people with Taoism. How could they say such superficial words and use such crude words now?"
What kind of person do you think a sage is?
Who do you think is a noble person?
Why do you regard me, an elder, as humble and dirty?
Song Zhong and Jia Yi said: Noble official positions and generous salaries are valued by the world, and worthy people enjoy them.
The position your husband is in now is not that kind of status, so he is considered to be in a lowly position.
What is said is not true, what is done is not effective, and what is taken is inappropriate, so it is dirty.
Diviners are despised by the world.
People all over the world say: fortune tellers often use exaggerated and grotesque words to cater to people's wishes; they falsely raise people's fortunes to please people's hearts; they fabricate disasters to make people sad; they use ghosts and gods to defraud money; they are greedy for rewards to benefit themselves.
These are behaviors that we consider shameful, so we say they are lowly and dirty. Lord Sima Ji said: "You two sit quietly for now."
Have you seen those wholesale boys?
summary: The role of divination in ancient China, particularly during the Zhou and Han dynasties. Kings historically received destiny without relying on divination, but by the Han dynasty, diviners had emerged. Lord Sima Ji, a diviner from Chu, practiced in Chang'an's east city. Two officials, Song Zhong and Jia Yi, visited him after discussing governance and saints. They questioned why Sima Ji, despite his wisdom, held a lowly position. Sima Ji defended divination, contrasting it with corrupt officials who exploit power for personal gain. He argued that diviners follow moral principles, aiding people through predictions and advice, unlike officials who engage in deceit and greed. He cited historical figures like Fuxi and King Wen of Zhou to highlight divination's value in governance. Sima Ji criticized the hypocrisy of those who judge diviners while ignoring their own ethical failings. He emphasized that diviners serve society by promoting virtue and preventing harm, often without recognition. The officials were humbled by his words. Later, Song Zhong and Jia Yi faced personal misfortunes—Song was convicted for a failed mission, and Jia Yi died after a student's accident. The text concludes with reflections on diviners' wisdom and their role in society, noting that many skilled individuals, like Sima Ji, remain unrecognized. It advises that elders should nurture children's talents and that diverse skills, including divination, are valuable. The narrative underscores the tension between worldly status and moral integrity, advocating for humility and the pursuit of virtuous living.

translation:
Chun Shenjun is a native of Chu State, his name is Xie and his surname is Huang.
He once traveled around to learn from his teachers, gained profound knowledge, and served King Qingxiang of Chu.
King Qingxiang thought Huang Xie was eloquent and asked him to go on a mission to Qin.
At that time, King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to attack Hanhe, defeated Han and Wei in Huayang, and captured Wei general Mang Mao. Han and Wei surrendered to Qin and served Qin.
King Zhao of Qin had ordered Bai Qi to attack Chu with South Korea and Wei, but the Qin army had not yet set off. At this time, King Chu sent Huang Xie to Qin by chance and heard about Qin's plan.
At this time, the State of Qin had occupied a large area of ​​Chu State, because before this King Qin had sent Bai Qi to attack the State of Chu, captured Wu County, Qianzhong County, captured the capital of Yancheng and Ying, and marched eastward to Jingling. King Qingxiang of Chu had to move the capital eastward to Chen County.
Huang Xie saw that King Huai of Chu was lured by Qin and went to Qin's court for negotiation. As a result, he was deceived, detained and died in Qin.
King Qingxiang was the son of King Huai of Chu, and the state of Qin did not pay attention to him at all. Huang Xie was worried that the state of Chu would perish if a war started.
So he wrote a letter to persuade King Qin:
Among the princes in the world, no one is more powerful than Qin and Chu.
Now I heard that your Majesty is going to conquer Chu State, which is like two tigers fighting each other.
When two tigers fight each other and the inferior dog takes advantage of it, it is better to be friendly with Chu.
Please allow me to state my opinion: I have heard that when things develop to their peak, they will inevitably go to the opposite direction, as is the case with the changes between winter and summer; when things accumulate to extremely high levels, they will be dangerous, as is the case with stacked chess pieces.
Now the land of Qin occupies the western and northern borders of the world. This has never been the case since the beginning of mankind, not even the territory of the emperor.
However, for three generations, the first emperors, King Wen, King Zhuang, and the king himself, never forgot to connect the land of Qin with Qi, so as to cut off the key parts of the alliance between the countries.
Now the king sent Shengqiao to serve as a garrison in South Korea. Shengqiao annexed the land of South Korea to the Qin State. This was a good way to obtain hundreds of miles of land without using any soldiers or force.
The king can be said to be talented.
The king sent troops to attack the Wei State again, blocking the access roads to and from the Wei capital Daliang, captured Hanoi, captured Yan, Suanzao, Xu, Tao and other places, and then invaded Xing. The Wei troops fled in all directions like white clouds blown by the wind and did not dare to save each other.
The king has accomplished enough.
The king stopped the campaign to rest and reorganize his troops, and sent troops again two years later; he also captured Pu, Yan, Shou, Yuan and other places, and then marched to Ren and Pingqiu, while Huang and Jiyang retreated and defended themselves. As a result, Wei surrendered to Qin;
It can be said that the power of the king has been exerted to the extreme.
If your Majesty maintains your merits, masters your power, gets rid of the desire to conquer, and spreads benevolence and righteousness, so that there will be no future disasters, your career will be equal to that of the three kings, and your power will be equal to that of the five hegemons.
If your Majesty, relying on the large number of strong men, relying on the strength of the military, and taking advantage of the power of destroying the Wei State, wants to use force to make the princes of the world submit, I am afraid you will be in trouble in the future.
summary: Chun Shenjun, a native of Chu named Huang Xie, served King Qingxiang of Chu. He was sent to Qin after King Qingxiang recognized his eloquence. At that time, Qin, under King Zhao, had been attacking Chu's allies, and Huang Xie learned of Qin's plan to invade Chu. Worried for Chu's survival, he wrote to King Zhao, arguing that Qin and Chu, as the two strongest states, should not fight each other, as this would benefit weaker states like Han and Wei. He warned that Qin's past victories had made it powerful, but attacking Chu would strengthen its enemies and lead to future trouble. Citing historical examples, he advised Qin to ally with Chu instead.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/春申君列传

translation:
I hope you, Xiangguo, will consider this matter carefully.
Ying Hou Fan Ju reported what Huang Xie said to the King of Qin.
The King of Qin said: Let the teacher of the Prince of Chu go back to inquire about King Chu's condition first, and then make a plan after he comes back.
Huang Xie made plans for the prince of Chu and said: The purpose of Qin detaining the prince is to obtain benefits.
Now the prince is powerless to benefit Qin. I am very worried about you.
Moreover, Yang Wenjun's two sons are both in the Chu Kingdom. If the king unfortunately dies and the prince is not in the Chu Kingdom, Yang Wenjun's son will definitely be his successor, and the prince will not be able to enjoy the country.
It is better to flee Qin and go out with the envoy; please let me stay and bear the consequences of this with my life.
The Prince of Chu changed his clothes and pretended to be the driver of an envoy from the Chu State to get out of the customs. Huang Xie stayed in the guest house, always refusing to receive guests on the pretext that the Prince was ill.
It was estimated that the prince had gone far and Qin could not catch up, so Huang Xie took the initiative to report to King Zhao of Qin: The prince of Chu has gone back and is far away.
I deserve death, please grant me death.
King Zhao was very angry and wanted to allow Huang Xie to commit suicide.
Ying Hou said: "As a minister, Huang Xie sacrificed his life for his master. If the prince is established as the king of Chu, he will definitely use Huang Xie in an important position. Therefore, it is better to spare him the death penalty and let him return to his country to show his goodwill towards the Chu country."
The King of Qin listened to the advice of Marquis Ying and sent Huang Xie back to his country.
Three months after Huang Xie returned to Chu, King Qingxiang of Chu passed away, and Prince Wan was appointed King of Chu. This was King Kaolie.
In the first year of King Kaolie's reign, Huang Xie was appointed prime minister, granted the title Lord Chunshen, and was rewarded with twelve counties in Huaibei.
Fifteen years later, Huang Xie proposed to the King of Chu: The area north of the Huaihe River is close to the State of Qi. The situation there is urgent. Please classify this area as a county to make governance more convenient.
At the same time, he offered twelve counties in Huaibei and asked for the seal to be transferred to Jiangdong.
King Kaolie agreed to his request.
Chun Shenjun built cities in the old capital of Wu and made them his own capital.
Chun Shenjun has already served as the prime minister of the Chu State. At this time, Qi State has Mengchang Lord, Zhao State has Pingyuan Lord, and Wei State has Xinling Lord. They are all vying to treat virtuous corporals, attract guests, compete with each other for wise men, and assist the king in controlling the state affairs.
In the fourth year when Chun Shenjun served as the prime minister of Chu, Qin defeated and killed more than 400,000 Zhao Changping garrison.
In the fifth year, Handan, the capital of Zhao State, was surrounded.
Handan asked for help from the Chu State. Chu State sent Chun Shenjun to lead troops to rescue Handan. After the Qin army retreated, Chun Shenjun led his troops back to Chu State.
In the eighth year when Chun Shenjun served as the prime minister of Chu State, he marched northward for Chu State, destroyed Lu State, and appointed Xunqing as the magistrate of Lanling County.
At this time, the Chu State became prosperous and powerful again.
Once, Lord Pingyuan of the State of Zhao sent envoys to visit Lord Chunshen, and Lord Chunshen arranged for them to stay in a first-class guesthouse.
The envoy of the State of Zhao wanted to show off the wealth of the State of Zhao to the State of Chu, so he specially put a tortoise shell hairpin in his crown, showed off his sword scabbard decorated with pearls and jade, and asked to invite the guests of Lord Chun Shen to meet him. The distinguished guests of Lord Chun Shen all came to see the envoy of the State of Zhao wearing shoes made of pearls, which made the envoy of the State of Zhao feel ashamed.
summary: King Zhao agreed, halted the attack, and formed an alliance with Chu. Huang Xie returned with Prince Wan of Chu as a hostage in Qin. When King Qingxiang fell ill, Huang Xie persuaded the Qin prime minister to let Prince Wan return, arguing it would secure Chu's loyalty. When Qin hesitated, Huang Xie helped Prince Wan escape disguised as a charioteer, staying behind to face punishment. King Zhao initially wanted to execute him but, on advice, spared him and sent him back. Three months later, King Qingxiang died, and Prince Wan became King Kaolie of Chu, appointing Huang Xie as prime minister and granting him the title Lord Chunshen with twelve counties. As prime minister, Chun Shenjun governed effectively, moving his fief to Jiangdong and building a capital in the old Wu city. He competed with other lords in attracting talented guests. In his fifth year, he led Chu forces to relieve the siege of Handan, Zhao's capital. In his eighth year, he conquered Lu for Chu, restoring Chu's strength. However, in his twenty-second year, a six-state alliance against Qin, led by Chu, was defeated at Hangu Pass, leading to his alienation by King Kaolie.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/春申君列传

translation:
Now I know I'm pregnant, but no one else knows.
I have only been favored by you for a short time. If you offer me to the King of Chu based on your noble status, the King of Chu will definitely favor me. I rely on God's blessing to give birth to a son. This will mean that your son will become the King of Chu, and the whole country of Chu will be yours. How is this compared with the unexpected disaster you suffer?
Chun Shenjun thought that what he said was very right, so he sent Li Yuan's sister away from home, arranged her in a strict residence, and then told the King of Chu that he wanted to donate Li Yuan's sister.
The King of Chu summoned Li Yuan's sister into the palace and favored her very much. He gave birth to a son, made him a prince, and made Li Yuan's sister a queen.
The King of Chu valued Li Yuan, so Li Yuan participated in the government affairs.
Li Yuan sent his sister to the palace, made her a queen, and made her son a prince. Worried that Lord Chun Shen would reveal his secret and become more arrogant, he secretly raised an assassin. He planned to kill Lord Chun Shen to silence him, and some people in the capital knew about it.
In the twenty-fifth year of Chunshenjun's tenure as prime minister, King Kaolie of Chu fell seriously ill.
Zhu Ying said to Chun Shenjun: There are unexpected blessings and unexpected disasters in the world.
Now that you are in a world where life and death are uncertain, and you serve a moody monarch, how can you not have people come unexpectedly?
Chun Shenjun asked: What is unexpected blessing?
Zhu Ying replied: You have been the prime minister of Chu for more than 20 years. Although you are the prime minister in name, you are actually the king of Chu.
Now the king of Chu is seriously ill and is about to die. You assist the young king and control the state affairs on his behalf, just like Yi Yin and Zhou Gong. When the king grows up and then hand over the power to him, doesn't it mean that you go south to claim the king and occupy the Chu country?
This is what is called unexpected blessings.
Chun Shenjun asked again: What is an unexpected disaster?
Zhu Ying replied: Li Yuan is your enemy if he is not in charge of national affairs. He has been raising assassins for a long time without caring about the military. As soon as the King of Chu is born, Li Yuan will definitely enter the palace first to seize power and kill you to silence you.
This is what is called an unexpected disaster.
Chun Shenjun then asked: What do you mean by someone who comes unexpectedly?
Zhu Ying replied: If you arrange for me to be the doctor, when the King of Chu is born, Li Yuan will be the first to enter the palace. I will kill Li Yuan for you.
This is what is called an unexpected person.
After hearing this, Chun Shenjun said: "You have to give up this plan." Li Yuan is a weak person, and I am very friendly to him. Besides, how could he get to this point!
Zhu Ying knew that his suggestions were not adopted, and he was afraid that disaster would affect him, so he ran away.
Seventeen days later, King Chu Kaolie passed away. As expected, Li Yuan entered the palace first and ambushed the assassin at Thorny Gate.
When Chun Shenjun entered the Thorny Gate, the assassins raised by Li Yuan caught him from both sides and killed him. He cut off his head and threw it outside the Thorny Gate.
At the same time, he sent officials to kill everyone in Chunshenjun's family.
Li Yuan's sister was favored by Lord Chun Shen and became pregnant. Then she entered the palace and was favored by Queen Chu Kaolie. The son born to her was established as King of Chu. This was King Chu You.
This year, Qin Shihuang has been on the throne for nine years.
summary: Chun Shenjun later became involved with Li Yuan, who presented his pregnant sister to him. She convinced Chun Shenjun to offer her to the childless King Kaolie, ensuring his son would become king. The king favored her, and she bore a son, who became prince. Li Yuan, fearing Chun Shenjun would reveal the secret, secretly raised assassins. When King Kaolie fell ill, a guest named Zhu Ying warned Chun Shenjun of Li Yuan's plot, but he dismissed it. Seventeen days after the king's death, Li Yuan ambushed and killed Chun Shenjun at the palace gate, then massacred his family. Li Yuan's sister's son became King You of Chu. The historian comments that Chun Shenjun's early wisdom in persuading Qin and risking his life for the prince was admirable, but he later fell victim to Li Yuan's schemes, failing to act on Zhu Ying's advice, which led to his downfall.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/春申君列传

translation:
King Weiman of North Korea was originally from the state of Yan.
Initially, when the Yan Kingdom was in its heyday, it conquered Zhenfan and North Korea, made them belong to the Yan Kingdom, appointed officials for them, and built defensive castles at the border fortresses.
Later, the Qin State destroyed the Yan State, and North Korea became a border country outside Liaodong County.
After the founding of the Han Dynasty, because North Korea was far away and difficult to defend, the previous passes in Liaodong County were renovated until they were bounded by the Xishui River, which was under the jurisdiction of the State of Yan.
Later, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled and went to the Huns. Weiman also went into exile, gathered more than a thousand of his companions, wore cone-shaped buns and barbarian clothes, walked out of the Great Wall in the east, crossed the Xu River, and lived in the original empty land of Qin called Shangxiazhang.
During the time of Emperor Hui and Queen Gao of the Han Dynasty, when the world had just stabilized, the governor of Liaodong County agreed that Wei Man would be the foreign minister of the Han Dynasty to protect the barbarians outside the border fortresses and not allow them to come to the border to harass and plunder. The barbarian leaders wanted to see the emperor from the Han Dynasty and did not prohibit it.
The governor of Liaodong reported this situation to the emperor, who agreed to the condition. Therefore, Weiman was able to use his military power and wealth to invade and surrender the small countries around him. Zhenfan and Lintun both surrendered and belonged to Weiman. The area under his control was thousands of miles in radius.
Weiman passed the rule to his son, and then to his grandson Youqu. During this period, more and more refugees from the Han Dynasty were lured to North Korea, and Youqu never went to see the emperor of the Han Dynasty. Many small countries around Zhenfan wanted to submit letters requesting an audience with the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, but were blocked from letting the Emperor know about their request.
In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Han Dynasty sent He He to blame and inform Youqu, but Youqu refused to accept the Han Dynasty's edict.
Shehe left North Korea and came to the border. Facing the Xu River, he sent a driver to assassinate the North Korean Pi Xiaowang who was escorting Shehe. Then he immediately crossed the river, galloped back, and entered the Han Dynasty border fortress. So he returned to the capital and reported to the emperor: I killed a North Korean general.
The emperor believed that he had a good reputation for killing Korean generals, so he no longer pursued his fault, but awarded him the official position of captain of eastern Liaodong.
North Korea resented Shehe and dispatched troops to make a surprise attack and killed Shehe.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty ordered the recruitment of prisoners whose crimes had been pardoned to attack North Korea.
In the autumn of the second year of Yuanfeng, the Han Dynasty sent general Yang Pu of Louzhou to cross the Bohai Sea by boat with an army of 50,000 people. General Xunshe of the left led his troops out of Liaodong County to attack Youqu.
Youqu mobilized troops to defend strategic locations to resist the Han army.
General Zuo's pawn named Duo was the first to lead the Liaodong troops to attack the enemy. As a result, the team failed and became separated. Most of them ran back and were executed for violating military law.
General Lou Chuan led 7,000 soldiers from Qi to arrive at Wangxian City first.
Youqu was guarding the city and heard the news that General Lou Chuan's army was small, so he went out to attack General Lou Chuan. General Lou Chuan's army failed and fled in all directions.
summary: King Weiman of North Korea, originally from the state of Yan, settled in the empty region of Shangxiazhang after Yan's fall and Lu Wan's rebellion. During the reigns of Emperor Hui and Queen Gao of Han, the Liaodong governor appointed Weiman as a foreign minister to protect border barbarians, allowing him to use military power to subdue nearby states like Zhenfan and Lintun, expanding his territory. Weiman's rule passed to his son and grandson Youqu, who lured Han refugees and blocked smaller states from contacting the Han emperor. In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Han sent Shehe to reprimand Youqu, but Youqu rejected the edict. Shehe assassinated a Korean general on his return, earning a promotion but provoking a Korean attack that killed him. The Han emperor then recruited pardoned prisoners to attack Korea. In autumn, General Yang Pu led 50,000 troops by sea, while General Xun She led forces from Liaodong. Youqu defended strategic points. Yang Pu's initial assault on Wangxian City failed, and his army scattered. Xun She also failed to break through Korean defenses.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/朝鲜列传

translation:
General Yang Pu lost his army and fled to the mountains to hide for more than ten days. He gradually recovered his scattered soldiers and reunited them.
General Xun Shen of the left attacked the Korean army stationed west of the Xu River, but failed to break through the enemy from the front.
Because the two generals failed to achieve military victory, the emperor sent Weishan to use his military prowess to tell Youqu clearly.
Youqu met with the Han Dynasty envoy and kowtowed to apologize: I am willing to surrender, but I am afraid that Generals Yang and Xun will kill me through deception. Now that I see the symbol of integrity, please allow us to surrender.
Youqu then sent the prince to the Han Dynasty to apologize, offering five thousand horses, and also presented military rations to the Han army in Korea.
There were more than 10,000 Korean people with weapons in their hands, and they were about to cross the Xu River. The envoy and General Zuo suspected that the Koreans had rebelled, and said that the prince had surrendered and submitted, and they should order the people not to carry weapons.
The prince also suspected that the Han envoys and General Zuo wanted to deceive and kill him, so he stopped crossing the river and led the Korean people back.
Weishan returned to the capital and reported to the emperor, who killed Weishan.
General Zuo defeated the North Korean army on the Haishui River and then advanced until he reached the foot of Wangxian City and surrounded the northwest of the city.
General Lou Chuan also went to join forces and garrisoned in the south of the city.
Youqu then held on to Wangxian City. Several months passed, but the Han army failed to capture Wangxian City.
General Zuo has always served the emperor in the palace and is favored. He led soldiers from Yan and Dai who were very fierce and took advantage of the opportunity to win the battle. Most of the soldiers in the army were very proud.
General Lou Chuan led his troops to cross the sea to fight, and there were many casualties in the battle. When they fought against Youqu, they suffered difficulties and humiliation, and suffered many casualties. The soldiers were frightened, and the generals felt ashamed in their hearts. When they surrounded You Can, General Lou Chuan often held peace talismans.
General Zuo tried his best to attack the enemy city, and the North Korean ministers secretly sought an opportunity to contact General Lou Chuan to discuss North Korea's surrender. The two sides exchanged talks, but no decision had been made.
General Zuo repeatedly agreed with General Lou Chuan on the date of simultaneous attacks. General Lou Chuan wanted to reach a reduction in the treaty with North Korea as soon as possible, so he did not send troops to join General Zuo. General Zuo also sent people to look for opportunities for North Korea to surrender. North Korea refused to surrender to General Zuo, but wanted to surrender to General Louchuan. Therefore, the two generals cannot coordinate with each other to fight the enemy together.
General Zuo thought about General Lou Chuan's fault for losing the battle in the past. Now he was secretly friendly with the North Korean minister, but North Korea refused to surrender, so he suspected that General Lou Chuan had a rebellion conspiracy, but he did not dare to take action.
The emperor said that the general was incompetent. Not long ago, I sent Weishan to tell Youqu to surrender. Youqu sent the prince to apologize, but Weishan, the messenger, could not handle the matter decisively and made mistakes in his plans with General Zuo, which finally broke the agreement of North Korea's surrender.
Now the two generals are besieging Wangxian City, but they are contradicting each other and cannot act in unison, so the problem cannot be solved for a long time.
summary: The emperor sent Weishan to negotiate, and Youqu agreed to surrender, sending his prince with tribute. However, suspicions arose between the Han envoys and the Korean prince, leading to a breakdown. Weishan was executed for mishandling the situation. Xun She then defeated the Korean army at Haishui River and besieged Wangxian City, joined by Yang Pu. The two generals disagreed on strategy: Xun She favored aggressive attack, while Yang Pu sought peaceful surrender. This discord prolonged the siege.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/朝鲜列传

translation:
Gongsun Sui, the governor of Jinan, was sent to correct their mistakes. If there is a convenient and favorable opportunity, he can handle the affairs on his own at any time.
After Gongsun Sui arrived in North Korea, General Zuo said: North Korea could have been captured long ago. There is a reason why it has not been captured yet.
He also told Gongsun Sui that he had agreed with General Lou Chuan on the date of march, but General Lou Chuan did not come to join forces. He also told Gongsun Sui that he had always suspected General Lou Chuan of treason, and said, "If we don't arrest him now, I'm afraid it will be a big harm. Not only will General Lou Chuan rebel, but he will also unite with North Korea to destroy our army."
Gongsun Sui also thought that this was the case, so he used the talisman to summon General Lou Chuan to General Zuo's camp to discuss the matter. He ordered General Zuo's men to capture General Lou Chuan on the spot, merge his troops under General Zuo, and then reported the incident to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty.
The emperor killed Gongsun Sui.
General Zuo merged the two armies and tried his best to attack North Korea.
Korean Prime Minister Lu Ren, Prime Minister Han Yin, Prime Minister Nixi, and General Wang Xi discussed with each other: At first, General Lou Chuan was wanted to surrender, but now General Lou Chuan has been arrested, and only General Zuo leads the combined army. The war is becoming more and more urgent. We may not be able to persist, and the king refuses to surrender.
Han Yin, Wang Yi, and passers-by all fled to the Han army and surrendered to the Han Dynasty.
Passers-by died on the road.
In the summer of the third year of Yuanfeng, Nixi Xiangcan sent people to kill the Korean king Youqu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty.
Before Wang Xiancheng was captured, Cheng Si, the former minister of Youqu, rebelled again and attacked the Korean officials who did not rebel with him.
General Zuo sent Youqu's son Changjian and Xiangluren's son Lu Zui to tell the Korean people clearly that they would kill him. Therefore, the Han Dynasty finally pacified Korea and established four counties.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty granted Shen the title of Marquis of Qingqing, Han Yin as the Marquis of Diju, Wang Xi as the Marquis of Pingzhou, and Chang demoted them to Jihou.
Lu Zui was named Marquis of Wenyang because of his meritorious service after his father died.
General Zuo was recalled to the capital. He committed the crime of competing for merit, becoming jealous of each other, and violating the battle plan, and was publicly executed.
General Lou Chuan was also sentenced to death because he committed the crime of attacking the enemy first without authorization when his troops arrived at Lukou. He should have waited for General Zuo, resulting in many casualties. He atone for his crime with money, was exempted from the death penalty, and became a civilian.
Tai Shigong said: King Youqu of Korea relied on the rugged terrain and the country was wiped out.
She He's deception to gain credit became the beginning of sending troops to attack North Korea.
General Lou Chuan acts with a narrow mind and suffers disaster when in danger.
I regretted that I had failed in the capture of Panyu, but was suspected of rebelling.
Xun Zhen and Gong Sun Sui were both beheaded as they fought for merit.
The two armies of Yang Pu and Xun Shen who conquered Korea suffered humiliation, and the generals were not granted the title of marquis.
summary: The emperor sent Gongsun Sui to mediate, but Xun She convinced him to arrest Yang Pu on suspicion of treason. Gongsun Sui complied, but the emperor later executed him. Xun She merged the armies and intensified the attack. Korean officials, fearing defeat, killed King Youqu and surrendered. The Han established four counties, granting titles to defectors. Xun She was executed for rivalry and violating battle plans, while Yang Pu was reduced to civilian status after paying a fine. The historian notes that Korea's reliance on terrain led to its fall, and the generals' conflicts caused their downfall.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/朝鲜列传

translation:
General Li Guang was a native of Chengji County, Longxi County.
His ancestor was Li Xin, a general of the Qin State who captured Prince Dan of Yan.
His home was originally in Huaili County, but later moved to Chengji.
The art of archery has been passed down from generation to generation in Li Guang's family.
In the fourteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, the Huns invaded Xiaoguan with great force. Li Guang joined the army to fight against the Huns as a son of a good family. Because he was good at riding and archery, and killed many enemy heads, he was appointed Zhonglang.
Li Guang's cousin Li Cai was also appointed as Zhonglang. Both of them were appointed as regular servants of the martial arts, with an annual salary of 800 shi of food.
Li Guang once traveled with the emperor, often charging into battle, resisting enemies, and killing ferocious beasts. Emperor Wen said: What a pity! You haven't encountered a good opportunity. If you catch up with the Emperor Gaozu's era and be granted the title of Marquis of Ten Thousand Households, what's the point?
After Emperor Jing came to the throne, Li Guang was appointed as the Captain of Longxi, and then as the Cavalry General.
During the rebellion of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu, Li Guang served as the captain of Xiaoqi and followed the Taiwei Zhou Yafu to fight back against the Wu and Chu rebels. He captured the enemy's flag at the foot of Changyi City and became famous.
However, because King Xiao of Liang privately awarded Li Guang the General's Seal, the court did not reward him after he returned to the court.
He was appointed as the governor of Shanggu, and the Huns came to fight every day.
Sun Kunxie, the Duke of Dian, cried to the emperor and said: Li Guang's talent is unparalleled in the world. He relies on his talent to fight the enemy head-on many times. I'm afraid he will lose this good general.
So he was appointed as the prefect of Shangjun.
Later, Li Guang was transferred to the prefecture of the border counties, and then to the prefecture of Shangjun.
He served as the prefect of Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen, Daijun, and Yunzhong, and was famous for his vigorous fighting.
The Huns invaded Shangjun in a large scale, and the emperor sent a eunuch to study military affairs with Li Guang and fight against the Huns.
The eunuch led dozens of cavalry on horseback. When they encountered three Huns, they fought with them. The three Huns turned around and fired arrows, wounding the eunuch and almost killing all his cavalry.
The eunuch fled back to Li Guang. Li Guang said: "This must be a Xiongnu expert in shooting vultures."
Li Guang then took a hundred cavalry to chase the three Huns.
The three men had no horses and traveled on foot.
After walking for dozens of miles, Li Guang ordered his cavalry to spread out to the left and right and outflank them in two directions. He personally shot the three men, shot two to death and captured one alive. As expected, it was the Huns' eagle shooter.
After tying him onto his horse, he saw thousands of Huns cavalry in the distance. When they saw Li Guang, they thought he was a cavalryman luring the enemy. They were surprised and ran up the mountain to set up their formation.
Li Guang's hundreds of cavalry were also frightened and wanted to run back.
Li Guang said: We are dozens of miles away from the main army. According to the current situation, as soon as our hundred cavalry run away, the Huns will chase and shoot us, and they will be killed immediately.
summary: General Li Guang, a native of Chengji County, Longxi, descended from Li Xin, a Qin general. Skilled in archery from a young age, he joined the army during Emperor Wen's reign, distinguishing himself against the Xiongnu and becoming a Zhonglang. Emperor Wen lamented his unlucky timing, suggesting he would have been a marquis in Emperor Gaozu's era. Under Emperor Jing, Li Guang served as a cavalry general, capturing enemy flags during the Rebellion of the Seven States but receiving no reward due to a private seal from the King of Liang. He later governed several border commanderies, earning fame for his fierce fighting.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传

translation:
If we stay, the Xiongnu will definitely think that we are a large army coming to lure the enemy, and they will not dare to attack us.
Li Guang ordered the cavalry: Advance!
The cavalry moved forward, and when they reached a place about two miles away from the slave position, they stopped and ordered: Everyone, dismount and unsaddle!
The cavalry said: There are so many enemies and they are so close. What should we do if there is an emergency?
Li Guang said: Those enemies thought that we would run away, but now we have taken off our saddles to show that we will not run away. This will make them more convinced that we are soldiers who lure the enemy.
So the Huns cavalry finally did not dare to attack.
A Hun general riding a white horse came out to guard his soldiers. Li Guang immediately mounted his horse and galloped with more than a dozen cavalry. He shot the Hun general riding a white horse to death. Then he returned to his cavalry team, took off the saddle, and asked the soldiers to let go of their horses and lie down casually.
It was dusk at this time, and the Xiongnu army always felt strange and did not dare to attack.
In the middle of the night, the Xiongnu soldiers thought that the Han Dynasty had an ambush nearby and wanted to sneak up on them at night, so the Xiongnu troops retreated.
The next morning, Li Guang returned to his army camp. The army did not know where Li Guang was going, so they were unable to respond later.
Several years later, Emperor Jing died and Emperor Wu ascended the throne. All the ministers on the left and right thought that Li Guang was a famous general, so Li Guang was transferred from the prefect of Shangjun to the chief of the imperial guard of Weiyang Palace, and Cheng Bushi also came to be the chief of the imperial guard of Changle Palace.
Cheng Bushi and Li Guang both served as governors of border counties and were also in charge of military garrison.
When it came time to attack the Xiongnu, Li Guang marched without strict formations and formations. He stationed troops near places with abundant water and lush grass, and set up camps and lodgings, which was convenient for everyone. He did not call for self-defense at night. The shogunate simplified various documents and books, but he placed sentries far away, so he did not encounter danger.
Cheng Bushi had strict requirements on the organization of the troops, marching columns, and garrison formations. He kept watch at night, and the military clerks had to wait until dawn to process performance appraisals and other official documents and books. The troops had no rest, but they never encountered danger.
Cheng Bushi said: Li Guang's army is simple and easy, but if the enemy suddenly attacks him, he will be unable to stop him; but his soldiers are comfortable and happy, and they are willing to die for him.
Although my army is busy with military affairs, the enemy does not dare to invade me.
At that time, Li Guang and Cheng Bushi at the border of the Han Dynasty were both famous generals, but the Huns were afraid of Li Guang's strategy, and most of the soldiers were willing to follow Li Guang and suffered the hardship of following Cheng Bushi.
During the reign of Emperor Jing, Cheng Bushi was awarded the title of Taizhong Dafu because he repeatedly spoke out and remonstrated. He was an honest man and strictly abided by the court documents and laws.
Later, the Han Dynasty used the city of Mayi to lure Chanyu and sent a large army to ambush in the valley near Mayi. Li Guang was appointed as the general of Xiaoqi and was controlled by the guard general Han Anguo.
At that time, Shanyu discovered the Han army's plan and ran away.
summary: During a Xiongnu invasion of Shangjun, Li Guang, with only a hundred cavalry, encountered thousands of Xiongnu. He cleverly dismounted and unsaddled his men, feigning a lure, which deterred the enemy from attacking. At night, the Xiongnu retreated, suspecting an ambush. Under Emperor Wu, Li Guang became a palace guard chief alongside Cheng Bushi. While Cheng's army was strict and disciplined, Li Guang's was simple and flexible, earning soldiers' loyalty. The Xiongnu feared Li Guang's strategy, though his lax approach sometimes led to danger.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传

translation:
None of the Han troops had any military exploits. Four years later, Li Guang was appointed as a general from the guard and went out to Yanmen Pass to attack the Huns.
The Huns had more troops and defeated Li Guang's army and captured Li Guang alive.
Shan Yu usually heard that Li Guang was very talented, so he ordered: If Li Guang is captured, he must be brought alive.
The Huns cavalry captured Li Guang. At that time, Li Guang was injured and injured, so they placed Li Guang between two horses and placed him in a rope net bag to lie down.
After walking for more than ten miles, Li Guang pretended to be dead and squinted when he saw a Hun boy riding a good horse next to him. Li Guang suddenly jumped on the Hun boy's horse, took advantage of the situation to push the boy off, took his bow, and galloped southward for dozens of miles. He met the remaining troops of his again, and led them into the pass.
The Huns dispatched hundreds of cavalry to chase him. As Li Guang fled, he picked up the bow of the Hun boy and shot the chasing cavalry, so he was able to escape.
So he returned to the capital of the Han Dynasty, and the court handed Li Guang over to the law enforcement officials.
The law enforcement officer ruled that Li Guang had suffered too many casualties, and he himself was captured alive by the enemy and should be beheaded. Li Guang used money and materials to atone for his death penalty and reduced his position to serve the people.
In the blink of an eye, Li Guang has been living at home for several years. Li Guang's family and Guan Qiang, the grandson of the late Yingyin Hou Guanying, live in seclusion in Lantian and often go hunting in Nanshan.
One night he went out with an entourage on horseback and drank with others in the fields.
When he came back, he walked to Ba Ling Pavilion. Ba Lingwei was drunk and shouted loudly, prohibiting Li Guang from passing.
Li Guang's entourage said: This is the former General Li.
Tingwei said: The current general is not allowed to pass, let alone his predecessor!
So he detained Li Guang and asked him to stay under Ba Ling Pavilion.
Not long after, the Xiongnu invaded and killed the prefect of Liaoxi and defeated General Han. General Han moved to Youbeiping.
So the emperor summoned Li Guang and appointed him as the right governor of Beiping.
Li Guang immediately asked to send Lieutenant Ba Ling to join him, and he was killed when he arrived in the army.
Li Guang was stationed in Youbeiping. When the Xiongnu heard about it, they called him the "Flying General of the Han Dynasty" and avoided him for several years, not daring to invade Youbeiping.
Li Guang went out hunting and saw a stone in the grass. He thought it was a tiger and shot at it.
Then he ejaculated again, but after all, he couldn't ejaculate anymore.
Li Guang had been stationed in various counties. When he heard about tigers, he often went to shoot them himself.
When he was stationed in Youbeiping, he went to shoot the tiger again. The tiger jumped up and injured Li Guang. Li Guang also shot the tiger to death in the end.
Li Guang was an upright official, and he distributed rewards to his subordinates. He always shared food and drink with the soldiers.
From his life to his death, Li Guang served as an official with a salary of two thousand stone for more than forty years. He had no extra property in his family and never talked about family property.
Li Guang was tall and had ape-like arms. He was good at archery and was gifted. Even if his descendants or outsiders learned from him, no one could compare with him.
Li Guang's speech was slow and he didn't talk much. When he was with others, he would draw military formations on the ground, and then shoot arrows. Whoever hit the denser rows or the wider rows would be punished with drinking.
He specialized in archery as a pastime until his death.
When Li Guang led his troops, he encountered a place where food and water were short of food. He found water, but the soldiers had not drank all of it, so he did not go near the water. The soldiers had not yet fully eaten, and Li Guang did not taste a morsel of food.
Li Guang was kind, gentle and not harsh to the soldiers, so the soldiers loved him and were willing to use him.
Li Guang's method of archery is to not shoot if he sees the enemy approaching and if he is not within a few dozen steps, he will probably miss the target. As soon as it is fired, the enemy will immediately fall to the ground with the sound of the bowstring.
Therefore, he led his troops to be trapped and humiliated several times, and he was also injured by wild beasts when shooting at them.
Not long after, Shi Jian passed away, so the emperor summoned Li Guang and asked him to succeed Shi Jian as Lang Zhongling.
In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Li Guang was appointed as the rear general. He followed General Che Weiqing's army out of Dingxiang to conquer the Xiongnu.
Many generals were made marquises for their military merits because they killed the enemy's heads in compliance with the prescribed amount, but Li Guang's army had no military merits.
Two years later, Li Guang, who held the title of Langzhongling, led 4,000 cavalry from Youbeiping. Bowang Marquis Zhang Qian led 10,000 cavalry to join Li Guang in two separate routes.
After marching for several hundred miles, King Zuoxian of the Xiongnu led 40,000 cavalry and surrounded Li Guang. Li Guang's soldiers were very frightened, so Li Guang sent his son Li Gan to ride towards the Xiongnu army.
Li Gan galloped alone with dozens of cavalry, passed through the Xiongnu cavalry formation, and protruded from its left and right wings. He came back and reported to Li Guang: "The enemy Huns are very easy to deal with!"
The soldiers felt relieved.
Li Guang formed a circular formation, facing outward. The Huns attacked fiercely, and arrows rained down.
More than half of the Han soldiers were dead, and their arrows were all used up.
Li Guang ordered the soldiers to draw their bows fully and not to release arrows. Li Guang personally used the big yellow crossbow to shoot at the Huns' lieutenants, killing several of them, and the Huns army gradually dispersed.
It was getting late at this time, and the officers and soldiers were all expressionless, but Li Guang looked calm and paid more attention to rectifying the army.
From then on, everyone in the army admired his bravery.
The next day, they went to fight hard again. Bowang Hou's army also arrived, and the Huns retreated.
The Han army was very tired and could not pursue him.
At that time, Li Guang's army was almost completely wiped out, so he had to withdraw his troops and return to the court.
According to the laws of the Han Dynasty, if Bowang Hou marched slowly and delayed the deadline, he should be sentenced to death, use money to atone for his crime, and be reduced to a civilian.
Li Guang's merits and demerits were equal to each other, so he was not rewarded.
At first, Li Guang's cousin Li Cai and Li Guang served Emperor Wen together.
summary: Li Guang was captured by the Xiongnu but escaped by feigning death, stealing a horse, and shooting pursuers. He was sentenced to death for losses but redeemed himself with money, becoming a commoner. Later, as Right Beiping governor, he killed a disrespectful Ba Ling guard and was called the "Flying General of Han," causing the Xiongnu to avoid him for years. He once mistook a stone for a tiger and shot it, but could not repeat the feat. Li Guang was generous, sharing rewards and food with soldiers, and lived simply despite decades of high office. In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Li Guang joined General Wei Qing's campaign but had no military merits. Two years later, he was surrounded by 40,000 Xiongnu with 4,000 cavalry. His son Li Gan's bravery calmed the troops, and Li Guang's personal archery killed several enemy officers, forcing a retreat. Despite heavy losses, Li Guang's calmness earned admiration. His cousin Li Cai, though less talented, became a marquis and prime minister, while Li Guang remained unenfeoffed. Astrologer Wang Shuo attributed this to Li Guang's past massacre of 800 surrendered Qiang rebels.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/李将军列传

translation:
The general did not agree to his request, and ordered the chief historian to write a document and send it to Li Guang's shogunate, and said to him: Hurry up to the right general's chariot troops and follow the document.
Li Guang set off without saying goodbye to the general. He was very angry and went to the military headquarters. He led his troops and joined forces with Zhao Shiqi, the right general of the chariot army, and set off from the east road.
The army has no guide and sometimes loses its way and ends up falling behind the general.
The general fought with Shanyu, but Shanyu fled, and Wei Qing had no choice but to return his troops.
The general traveled south across the desert and met the former general and the right general.
After Li Guang paid an audience with the general, he returned to his army.
The general sent Chang Shi to bring dry food and wine to Li Guang. The envoy asked Li Guang and Zhao Shiqi about the situation of losing their way. Wei Qing wanted to write a letter to the emperor reporting detailed military information.
Li Guang didn't answer. The general sent Chang Shi to urgently order the personnel of Li Guang shogunate to go for trial and confrontation.
Li Guang said: The captains are not guilty. It was me who lost my way. Now I will personally go to the shogunate to be tried and confronted.
When he arrived at the shogunate of the general, Li Guang said to his subordinates: I have fought more than seventy battles with the Xiongnu since I was a boy, and now I have the honor to follow the general on an expedition to fight the Shanyu army. However, the general sent my troops to take a circuitous and long road, and they lost their way. Isn't it God's will?
Besides, I am already over sixty years old. After all, I can no longer bear the insults of those swordsmen and pen officials.
So he drew his sword and killed himself.
All the soldiers in Li Guang's army cried bitterly.
When the people heard the news, whether they knew him or not, whether they were old or young, they all shed tears for Li Guang.
The right general Zhao Shiqi was handed over to the law enforcement officials alone, and he should be sentenced to death. He should use property to atone for his crime and be reduced to a civilian.
Li Guang had three sons named Danghu, Jiao and Gan, all of whom were appointed Langguan.
Once the emperor was playing with the jester Han Yan, and Han Yan acted a little wanton. Li Danghu went to beat Han Yan, but Han Yan ran away, so the emperor thought Danghu was brave.
Li Danghu died early, and Li Jiao was named the prefect of Daijun. Both of them died before Li Guang.
Li Danghu had a posthumous son named Li Ling.
When Li Guang died in the army, Li Gan was following the hussar general Huo Qubing.
In the second year after Li Guang's death, Li Cai used his position as prime minister to occupy the open space on both sides of the road in front of Emperor Jing's mausoleum. He was convicted and should be sent to law officials for investigation. However, Li Cai did not want to be tried and confronted and committed suicide. His feudal state was abolished.
Li Gan served as a school lieutenant and accompanied General Hussar to attack King Zuoxian of the Huns. He fought hard, captured King Zuoxian's war drums and flags, and beheaded many enemies. As a result, he was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei and granted 200 households in the city. He succeeded Li Guang as Langzhongling.
Soon, Li Gan resented the general Wei Qing for causing his father to die of hatred, so he wounded the general. The general concealed the incident and did not make it public.
Not long after that, Li Gan followed the emperor to Yong County and went hunting in Ganquan Palace.
General Huo Qubing was related to Wei Qing, so he shot Li Gan to death.
Huo Qubing was a noble and favored man at the time, so the emperor concealed the truth and said that Li Gan was killed by a deer.
More than a year later, Huo Qubing passed away.
Li Gan had a daughter who was the prince's concubine and was very favored. Li Gan's son Li Yu was also favored by the prince. However, he was greedy for money and profit, and the Li family gradually declined.
When Li Ling reached his prime, he was appointed as the supervisor of Jianzhang Camp, supervising all the cavalry.
summary: In the fourth year of Yuanshou, Li Guang, now a former general, joined Wei Qing's campaign against the Xiongnu. Wei Qing, warned by the emperor about Li Guang's age and bad luck, ordered him to take a circuitous eastern route. Li Guang protested but was overruled, leading to his army losing its way. After the campaign, Wei Qing demanded an inquiry. Li Guang, refusing to face humiliation, declared, "I have fought over seventy battles. Now, at over sixty, I cannot bear the insults of clerks," and committed suicide. His death caused widespread mourning. Li Guang's sons—Danghu, Jiao, and Gan—served as officials. Danghu died young, and Jiao became a prefect. Li Gan, a marquis, wounded Wei Qing in revenge but was later killed by Huo Qubing, who claimed it was a deer accident. Li Guang's grandson Li Ling, a skilled archer, led 5,000 infantry against 80,000 Xiongnu, killing over 10,000 before surrendering due to lack of supplies. The Han executed his family, ending the Li family's reputation. The historian concluded that Li Guang's honest character, like peach and plum trees, naturally drew people to him, despite his lack of eloquence.

translation:
Li Si was a native of Shangcai, State of Chu.
When he was young, he worked as a minor official in the county. He saw rats eating dirty things in the toilet near his office. Whenever someone or a dog came near, he would be frightened and run away.
Later, Li Si walked into the granary and saw the rats in the granary eating the stored grain and living under the big house without having to worry about being disturbed by people or dogs.
So Li Si sighed with emotion: A person's talent or incompetence is determined by his environment, just like a mouse.
So Li Si learned from Xunzi how emperors governed the world.
After completing his studies, Li Si estimated that the King of Chu was not worthy of serving, and that the six kingdoms were already weak and there was no hope of making contributions to them, so he wanted to go west to Qin.
Before leaving, he said goodbye to Xunzi: I heard that if a person encounters an opportunity, he should not slack off. Nowadays, all the vassal states are striving for opportunities so that lobbyists can make meritorious deeds and gain real power.
Now that the King of Qin wants to annex other countries and proclaim himself emperor to govern the world, this is a good time for political activists and lobbyists from civilian backgrounds to travel around and express their ambitions.
Being in a humble position and not thinking about seeking fame and wealth is like an animal. It only wants to eat meat when it sees it. It only has a human face but can barely walk.
Therefore, the greatest shame is humble status, and the greatest sorrow is poverty.
Being in a humble position and difficult situation for a long time, yet still criticizing society, hating fame and wealth, and slandering oneself as uncontested is not the original wish of a scholar.
So I am going west to lobby the King of Qin.
After Li Si arrived in Qin, just as King Zhuangxiang of Qin passed away, Li Si asked to be a retainer of Lu Buwei, the prime minister of Qin. Lu Buwei appreciated him very much and appointed him Lang Guan.
As a result, Li Si got the opportunity to lobby. He said to the King of Qin: Mediocre people often lose opportunities, but those who can achieve great achievements are those who can take advantage of opportunities and be ruthless.
In the past, although Duke Mu of Qin dominated the world, he did not move eastward and annex the six kingdoms of Shandong. What was the reason?
The reason was that the number of princes was still large and the prestige of the Zhou Dynasty had not completely declined. Therefore, the five hegemons emerged alternately and successively promoted the Eastern Zhou royal family.
Since Qin Xiaogong, the royal family of the Eastern Zhou Dynasty has been weak and weak, and the princes have merged with each other. The area east of Hangu Pass has been transformed into six kingdoms. Qin State took advantage of the victory to gradually conquer the six kingdoms. It has been about six generations now.
Nowadays, the princes obey Qin just like the counties obey the imperial court.
With the power of Qin and the wisdom of the king, just like sweeping away the dust on the stove, it is enough to wipe out the princes, achieve the emperor's cause, and realize the unification of the world. This is the only opportunity that comes once in a lifetime.
If we are slack now and do not take action on this matter, when the princes become stronger again and enter into alliance alliances, even if they are as capable as Huang Di, they will not be able to annex them.
Qin Shihuang appointed Li Si as the chief historian, followed his plan, and secretly sent counselors to various countries with gold and jade treasures to lobby.
summary: Li Si was a native of Shangcai in the State of Chu. As a young county official, he observed rats in the toilet fleeing from people and dogs, contrasting them with granary rats that ate stored grain undisturbed. This led him to conclude that a person's competence depends on their environment. He studied under Xunzi to learn the art of governing an empire. Afterward, deeming the King of Chu unworthy and the six kingdoms too weak for him to achieve merit, he decided to go west to Qin. He told Xunzi that opportunity must be seized, and that the King of Qin's ambition to unify the world was a perfect chance for a commoner to gain fame and wealth. He considered humble status the greatest shame and poverty the greatest sorrow, rejecting the notion of a scholar who claims to be above worldly pursuits. Upon arriving in Qin, Li Si became a retainer of Prime Minister Lü Buwei, who appointed him as a Lang official. He then advised the King of Qin that while Duke Mu of Qin had dominated the world, he could not annex the six kingdoms because the Zhou dynasty's prestige had not yet declined. Since Duke Xiao of Qin, the Zhou had weakened, and the six kingdoms had formed. Now, with Qin's power and the king's wisdom, the time was ripe to unify the world. He warned that hesitation would allow the princes to strengthen and form alliances, making conquest impossible. The King of Qin appointed Li Si as Chief Historian, following his plan to bribe or assassinate key figures in other states to alienate them from their rulers, followed by military attacks. Li Si was later made a Guest Minister.
