translation:
If famous figures from various countries can be bribed, they will be bribed with gifts; if they cannot be bribed, they will be killed with sharp swords.
These are all strategies to alienate the relationship between the princes and their ministers. Then, the King of Qin sent good generals to attack later.
The King of Qin appointed Li Si as his guest minister.
At this time, the Korean Zheng Guo came to Qin as a spy in the name of building channels, and was soon discovered.
The royal family and ministers of the State of Qin all said to the King of Qin: Most of the people who come from various vassal states to serve the King of Qin are lobbying for their king, just to alienate the State of Qin. They ask the King to expel all the guests.
Li Si was also among the guests planned to be expelled.
So Li Si wrote a letter saying:
I heard that officials were talking about expelling guest guests. I privately thought that this was wrong.
In the past, Duke Mu of Qin recruited talented people, and he obtained Yu Yu from Xirong, Baili Xi from the garden of Chu in the east, Uncle Jian from Song, and Pi Bao and Gongsun Zhi from Jin.
None of these five people were born in Qin, but Duke Mu of Qin used them to annex more than 20 countries, and then dominated Xirong.
Qin Xiaogong adopted Shang Yang's new method and changed customs. As a result, the people prospered and the country became rich and powerful. The people were willing to serve the country and the princes sincerely submitted. He defeated the armies of Chu and Wei and captured thousands of miles of land. To this day, the country is politically stable and strong.
King Qin Hui adopted Zhang Yi's strategy and captured the Sanchuan area, annexed Ba and Shu to the west, occupied Shangjun to the north, captured Hanzhong to the south, captured Jiuyi, controlled Yan and Ying, and occupied the dangerous Chenggao in the east, seizing fertile land, and further disintegrated the alliance of the six countries, making them face the west and serve the Qin State. Their achievements continue to this day.
King Zhao of Qin won Fan Sui, deposed Ranghou, expelled King Huayang, strengthened the public house, and eliminated the power of private dignitaries. Like silkworms eating mulberry leaves, he gradually annexed the lands of the princes, and finally laid the foundation for Qin to unify the world.
These four monarchs all relied on the power of guest ministers from other countries.
From this point of view, in what way does Ke Qing feel sorry for Qin?
If these four monarchs refuse guests rather than accept them, and alienate scholars without using them in important positions, this will make Qin neither rich nor powerful.
Now, Your Majesty, you have obtained the beautiful jade from Kunshan, the pearl of Suihou, the jade of the He family. You hang the bright moon pearl, wear the Tai'a sword, ride a Xianli horse, erect the green phoenix flag, and place the Lingnu drum.
None of the above treasures were produced in Qin, but Your Majesty loves them very much. Why is this?
If it must be produced by Qin and then used, then the luminous jade cannot be used to decorate the court, rhino horn and ivory products cannot be admired by you, the beauties of Zheng and Wei cannot be listed in your harem, and good horses cannot fill your stable. Gold and tin from Jiangnan should not be used, and paintings from Xishu should not be used as paint.
If the things you use to decorate your harem, serve as your concubine, and please your eyes and ears, must come from the Qin State, then the hairpins decorated with Wandi pearls, the earrings inlaid with jade beads, the clothes sewn from Dong'a white silk, and the gorgeous embroidered ornaments cannot be presented to you, and the fashionable and elegant, beautiful and quiet Zhao women cannot stand by your side.
And those who bang the earthen altars and pots, play the zither, slap their thighs, and scream to satisfy the appreciation requirements, this is the authentic music of the Qin Dynasty. Musical pieces such as "Zheng", "Wei", "Sangjian", "Zhao", "Yu", "Wu" and "Xiang" are music from other countries.
Now you abandon the set of Qin music of banging earthen altars and pots and listen to the sounds of "Zheng" and "Wei"; you don't listen to playing the zither but enjoy the music of "Zhao" and "Yu". What's the reason for this?
To put it bluntly, it is just for the pleasure of the eyes to satisfy the viewing needs of the ears and eyes.
But this is not the case when you employ people now. You don't ask whether the person can be used or not, and you don't ask about the merits of the person. As long as he is not a native of Qin, he will be dismissed, and as long as he is a guest, he will be expelled.
summary: When the Korean spy Zheng Guo was discovered, Qin's nobles urged the king to expel all foreign guests, including Li Si. Li Si wrote a letter arguing against this. He cited Duke Mu of Qin, who used five non-Qin officials to dominate Xirong; Duke Xiao, who used Shang Yang to make Qin rich and powerful; King Hui, who used Zhang Yi to expand territory and break up alliances; and King Zhao, who used Fan Sui to strengthen the royal house. He argued that these four rulers relied on guest ministers. He then compared the king's love for foreign treasures, music, and women to his rejection of foreign talent, stating this was not the way to unify the world. He concluded that expelling guests would weaken Qin and aid its enemies. The king abolished the expulsion order, restored Li Si's position, and later promoted him to Tingwei. Over twenty years, Qin unified the world, and Li Si became Prime Minister.

translation:
It seems that what your Majesty values ​​​​is beauty, music, pearls, and gems, and what he despises is talent.
This is not a way to unify the world and subdue the princes.
I have heard that the vastness of the land means abundant food, the vastness of the country means the large population, and the strongness of the army means the bravery of the soldiers.
That's why Mount Tai can be so tall without rejecting soil; rivers and seas can become so deep and wide without being picky about small streams; and only those who achieve kingly status can show their great virtue by not abandoning the masses.
Therefore, regardless of whether the land is southeast or northwest, the people do not distinguish one country from another. The grains are abundant all year round, and ghosts and gods grant blessings. This is why the Five Emperors and Three Kings are invincible in the world.
And now, Your Majesty, you have abandoned the people to help the enemy, rejected the guests and made them contribute to other vassal states, made the talented people in the world retreat and dare not go west, stop and dare not enter Qin. This is exactly what people say: lending weapons to the enemy and sending food to thieves!
There are many items not produced in Qin that are worth cherishing; there are also many scholars who were not born in Qin who are willing to be loyal.
Now you are expelling guests to support the enemy, harming the people to help the enemy, weakening yourself internally, and creating resentment with the princes externally. If you continue like this, it is impossible to keep the country from danger.
Therefore, the King of Qin abolished the order of expelling guests, restored Li Si's official position, finally adopted his strategy, and his official position was also promoted to that of Tingwei.
After more than twenty years, he finally unified the world and honored the king as "Emperor". The emperor also appointed Li Si as prime minister.
They also demolished the city walls of counties and counties in various countries, destroyed weapons in various places, and stated that they would no longer be used.
The Qin State did not have an inch of enfeoffed land, nor did it make the emperor's sons or brothers kings, nor did it confer meritorious officials as princes, so that the country would never have the scourge of war from now on.
In the thirty-fourth year of Qin Shi Huang's reign, he held a banquet in Xianyang Palace to entertain officials. Dr. Zhou Qingchen and others praised Qin Shi Huang's military might and virtue.
Chun Yuyue, a native of Qi State, advised: I heard that the Yin, Shang and Zhou dynasties ruled for more than a thousand years, and they enfeoffed clan members and heroes as their own auxiliary forces.
And now, although Your Majesty has unified the world, your children are still common people. If there is a disaster like Tian Chang and Liu Qing seizing power and usurping the throne, and there are no strong assistant ministers in the court, who will come to rescue them?
I have never heard of a dynasty that could maintain a long-term rule without learning from ancient experience.
Now Zhou Qingchen and others are flattering you in person to aggravate your mistake. They are not loyal.
The First Emperor handed over this memorial to Li Si. Li Si thought this argument was absurd, so he discarded it, and wrote to the emperor: In ancient times, the world was scattered and chaotic, and they did not obey each other, so the princes rose up together. General public opinion praised the ancient times for denying the present and decorating some exaggerated words to disturb the reality of society. People thought that their own school had the best knowledge to deny the emperor's policies and decrees.
Now His Majesty has unified the world, distinguished right from wrong, and made the emperor a common person in the country. However, hundreds of schools of thought have come together to criticize the imperial court's laws and regulations. When they heard that the imperial court issued an order, they immediately discussed it from the viewpoint of their own school.
If this continues without prohibition, the power and prestige of the monarch above will decline, and private gangs will form below. Therefore, it is better to ban it.
I request that all the "Poems", "Books" and works of various schools of thought be swept away.
summary: In the 34th year of Qin Shi Huang's reign, Dr. Zhou Qingchen praised the emperor, but Chun Yuyue advised enfeoffing clan members, warning that without strong assistants, the dynasty could not last. The First Emperor asked Li Si, who dismissed the argument. Li Si wrote that in ancient times, scholars used the past to criticize the present, undermining the emperor's authority. He requested that all "Poems," "Books," and works of the hundred schools be banned, with punishment for those who disobeyed, except for books on medicine, divination, and planting. The emperor approved, confiscating these texts to make the people ignorant. Li Si also contributed to unifying the writing system and building imperial villas. His sons married Qin princesses, and his daughters married Qin royalty. At a banquet, Li Si lamented that his wealth and status had reached their peak, and he feared the decline that must follow.

translation:
When the eldest son arrives, he ascends the throne and becomes emperor, but you don’t even have a fief of any size. What should you do?
Hu Hai said: That’s how it is.
I have heard that a wise monarch knows his ministers best, and a wise father knows his son best.
When my father died, he did not issue an order to divide the princes, so what else could he say?
Zhao Gao said: Not so.
The power in the world today, no matter who's life or death, is in the hands of you, me and Li Si!
I hope you will think about it carefully. What's more, can controlling ministers and surrendering to others, ruling others and being ruled by others, be the same thing?
Hu Hai said: It is unrighteous to abolish an elder brother and establish a younger brother; it is unfilial to disobey the father's edict and fear death; it is incompetent to rely on the help of others because one's talents are shallow. These three things are treason and unethical, and the people in the world will not obey them. I will suffer disaster myself, and the country will perish.
Zhao Gao said: I have heard that Shang Tang and Zhou Wu killed their monarchs, and everyone in the world praised their actions as moral, and it cannot be regarded as disloyal.
King Wei killed his father, and the people of Wei praised his merits. Confucius recorded this incident, which cannot be regarded as unfilial.
What's more, you can't stick to small details when doing big things, and you don't need to be humble enough to do great virtues. The customs in the countryside are different, and the working methods of officials are also different.
Therefore, worrying about small things and forgetting big things will cause disaster in the future; being hesitant at critical moments will definitely regret it in the future.
If you do it decisively and boldly, you will avoid even ghosts and gods, and you will definitely succeed in the future.
I hope you do as I say.
Hu Hai sighed and said: Now that the emperor has just passed away and the funeral has not yet ended, how can we use this matter to appeal to the prime minister?
Zhao Gao said: Time, time, too short to plan!
Just like carrying dry food to drive a fast horse on the road, lest the opportunity be delayed!
After Hu Hai agreed with Zhao Gao's words, Zhao Gao said: If you don't discuss it with the Prime Minister, I'm afraid the matter will not succeed. I hope I can discuss it with the Prime Minister for you.
Zhao Gao said to Prime Minister Li Si: When the First Emperor passed away, he gave his eldest son Fusu an edict, ordering him to attend the funeral in Xianyang and establish him as his heir.
The emperor died before the edict was sent, and no one knew about it.
The imperial edict and talisman given to the eldest son by the emperor are all in Hu Hai's hands. Who should be appointed as the prince only depends on a word between you and me.
What should you do about this?
Li Si said: How can you say such words of subjugation to the country!
This is not something you should discuss as a minister!
Zhao Gao said: "Evaluate for yourself, who is more capable than Meng Tian?"
Who gets more credit? Who has more far-reaching plans and never makes mistakes? Who do the people of the world support more?
Who has a better relationship with the eldest son Fusu?
Li Si said: I am not as good as Meng Tian in these five aspects, but why are you so demanding on me?
Zhao Gao said: I was originally a slave of the eunuch. I was lucky enough to enter the Qin Palace because I was familiar with the prison law documents. I have been in charge for more than 20 years. I have never seen the prime ministers who were dismissed by the King of Qin get titles and pass them on to the next generation. In the end, they all ended up being killed.
The emperor had more than twenty sons, as you know.
The eldest son Fusu is resolute and brave, trusting and good at motivating scholars. After taking the throne, he must use Meng Tian as prime minister. Obviously, you will not be able to resign and return home with the seal of Tonghou in the end.
I have been ordered by the emperor to educate Hu Hai and let him study law for several years, and I have never seen him make any mistakes.
He was compassionate and kind, honest and kind, despised money, respected scholars, was smart but not good at words, and respected the wise with every courtesy. Among Qin Shihuang's sons, no one could catch up with him and could be established as his successor.
summary: In the 37th year, the First Emperor died at Shaqiu. Li Si, Zhao Gao, and Hu Hai kept his death secret. Zhao Gao withheld the emperor's edict to Fusu and persuaded Hu Hai to usurp the throne, arguing that power was in their hands and that great deeds required decisive action. Hu Hai agreed, and Zhao Gao convinced Li Si by warning that Fusu would replace him with Meng Tian, leading to his death. Li Si wept but complied. They forged an edict making Hu Hai crown prince and another ordering Fusu and Meng Tian to commit suicide. Fusu obeyed, but Meng Tian was imprisoned. Hu Hai became the Second Emperor, and Zhao Gao gained great power.

translation:
The Second Emperor believed that Zhao Gao's words were correct, so he revised the law.
So the ministers and princes were found guilty and handed over to Zhao Gao, who ordered him to be interrogated and brought to justice.
Minister Meng Yi and others were killed, ten princes were beheaded in the streets of Xianyang, and twelve princesses were also cut into pieces and executed in Du County. Their property was confiscated and returned to the emperor, and countless others were jointly punished.
Young Master Gao wanted to escape for his life, but he was afraid of being executed by the whole family, so he wrote a letter saying: When the late emperor was alive, I would give him food when he entered the palace and give him a ride when he left the palace.
The clothes in the emperor's palace were given to me by the late emperor; the horses in the stables in the palace were also given to me by the late emperor.
I should have died with the late Emperor but failed to do so. This is my unfilial piety as a son of man and my disloyalty as a minister.
There is no reason for a disloyal person to live in this world. Please allow me to die with the late emperor, hoping to bury me at the foot of Mount Li.
I just ask the emperor to pity me and agree to it.
After the book was presented, Hu Hai was very happy. He called Zhao Gao and showed him the book, saying: "This can be said to be embarrassing and helpless, right?"
Zhao Gao said: How can you plot a rebellion when the ministers are worried all day long that they will die before it is too late!
Hu Hai agreed to Gongzi Gao's request and gave him 100,000 yuan for burial.
At that time, the laws and punishments became more and more cruel day by day. Everyone among the ministers was in danger, and there were many people who wanted to rebel.
The second generation also built the Epang Palace, straight roads and galloping roads, taxes became heavier and heavier, and military service was endless.
So Chen Sheng, Wu Guang and others, who were recruited from Chu to guard the border, rebelled and raised troops to the east of Xiaoshan. Heroes and heroes swarmed up, proclaimed themselves princes and rebelled against the Qin Dynasty. Their troops attacked until Hongmen before retreating.
Li Si wanted to find opportunities to remonstrate many times, but the second emperor did not allow him.
Instead, the Second Emperor blamed Li Si and said: I have an opinion that I heard from Han Feizi. He said that when Yao ruled the world, the palace was only three feet high, the oak rafters were used without cutting them, and the thatched roofs were made without trimming. Even the accommodation conditions in the hotels were not more difficult than this.
Wearing deerskin coats in winter and linen clothes in summer, making coarse rice for rice and wild vegetables for soup, eating from earthen pots and drinking water from earthen bowls, even a janitor's life cannot be more miserable than this.
Xia Yu opened the dragon gate, opened the Great Xia Waterway, dredged many rivers, built many dikes in twists and turns, and channeled the stagnant water into the sea. There was no white meat on the thighs, no hair on the calves, thick calluses on the palms and soles, and a dark face. In the end, he died of exhaustion and was buried on Kuaiji Mountain. Even a slave's labor would not be worse than this.
However, does the purpose of those who regard ruling the world as a noble thing just want to worry about it, live in a dormitory like a hotel, eat the food of a janitor, and do the work of a slave?
These things are done by people with low talents, not by wise people.
summary: The Second Emperor wanted to indulge his desires, but Zhao Gao warned that the princes and former ministers were suspicious and might rebel. He advised implementing harsh laws, killing all opponents, and replacing them with loyalists. The Second Emperor agreed, revising the law. Many princes and ministers were executed, including ten princes beheaded in Xianyang and twelve princesses dismembered. Prince Gao requested to die with the First Emperor, which the Second Emperor approved. Laws grew crueler, taxes heavier, and corvée endless, leading to rebellions like that of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang. Li Si tried to remonstrate but was blamed by the Second Emperor, who argued that a ruler should use the world to satisfy his own desires, not labor like Yao or Yu.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/李斯列传

translation:
Zhao Gao was originally an eunuch, but he did not do whatever he wanted just because he was in a comfortable situation, nor did he change his loyalty because he was in a dangerous situation. He was honest and devoted to good deeds. He got where he is today through his own efforts. He was promoted because of his loyalty and kept his position because of his faith. I do think he is a talented person, but you doubt him. What is the reason?
In addition, I lost my father at a young age and have little knowledge and do not know how to manage people. And you are old, so I am worried that you will be isolated from the people of the world.
If I don't entrust the state affairs to Zhao Gao, who else should I use?
Besides, Mr. Zhao is a shrewd and honest man, he does his best, understands the people's conditions below, and adapts to my wishes above, please don't doubt it.
Li Si said: Not so.
Zhao Gao used to be a humble man who didn't understand the truth, was greedy and constantly seeking profit. His status and power were second only to His Majesty, but his desire for status and power was endless, so I say it was very dangerous.
The second son had believed Zhao Gao in the morning and was worried that Li Si would kill him, so he secretly told Zhao Gao these words.
Zhao Gao said: The prime minister is only worried about me, Zhao Gao. After my death, the prime minister can do what Tian Chang did.
So the Second Emperor said: Let Li Si be handed over to you, the doctor, to investigate and deal with it!
Zhao Gao investigates Li Si.
After Li Si was arrested, he was put on a torture device and imprisoned in prison. He looked up to the sky and sighed: Oh! How sad!
How can the ignorant and foolish king advise him!
In the past Xia Jie killed Guan Longfeng, Shang Zhou killed Prince Bigan, and Wu Wang Fucha killed Wu Zixu.
Are these three ministers disloyal? However, death was inevitable. Although they died loyally, it was a pity that they were not loyal to the people they were.
Now my wisdom cannot keep up with these three people, and the cruelty and cruelty of the second generation exceeds that of Jie, Zhou, and Fu Cha. It is right for me to die because of my loyalty.
Besides, isn’t it nonsense to govern the country in the second generation?
Not long ago, he killed his brother and established himself as the emperor. He also killed loyal people, reused lowly people, built the Epang Palace, and levied tyrannical taxes on the people of the world.
It's not that I don't give advice, it's that he doesn't listen to me.
All ancient sages and emperors had a certain degree of restraint in their diet, a certain number of vehicles, horses, and utensils, and a certain limit in their palaces. They issued orders and did things, and prohibited anything that increased expenses and was not conducive to the people, so that long-term peace and stability could be achieved.
Now the second generation is using unnatural and cruel methods on his brothers, without considering what disasters will happen. He persecutes and kills loyal ministers without considering what disasters will happen. He vigorously builds palaces, increases taxes on the people of the world, and does not hesitate to spend money. After these three measures were implemented, the people of the world did not obey.
Now the rebels have accounted for half of the people in the world, but the second generation has not yet awakened in his heart, and actually appointed Zhao Gao as his assistant. I will definitely see the thieves invade Xianyang and turn the court into a place where elk roam.
So the Second Emperor sent Zhao Gao to examine the prime minister's case, punish him, inquire about Li Si and his son Li You's rebellion, and arrest all his guests and family members.
Zhao Gao punished Li Si and tortured him more than a thousand times. Li Si could not bear the painful torture and unjustly confessed.
The reason why Li Si did not commit suicide was that he was arrogant and eloquent, and he had made great contributions to the Qin State. He really had no intention of rebellion. He hoped to write a letter to defend himself, and hoped that the Second Emperor would wake up and pardon him.
Li Si then wrote a letter in prison saying: I have been serving as prime minister to govern the people for more than thirty years.
summary: Li Si, fearing for his position, wrote a letter flattering the Second Emperor, advocating strict supervision and severe punishments to ensure the ruler's absolute power and pleasure. He cited Shen Buhai, Han Fei, and Shang Yang, arguing that harsh penalties for minor crimes prevent greater offenses. The Second Emperor was pleased and intensified supervision and taxation, leading to half the population being prisoners and corpses piled in the markets. Zhao Gao, fearing exposure, persuaded the Second Emperor to stay in the palace and not meet ministers, allowing Zhao Gao to control all affairs. Zhao Gao then tricked Li Si into seeking an audience during the emperor's leisure, angering the Second Emperor. Zhao Gao accused Li Si of involvement in the Shaqiu conspiracy and of colluding with rebels through his son Li You. The Second Emperor ordered an investigation. Li Si wrote to expose Zhao Gao's ambition, comparing him to usurpers like Tian Chang. The Second Emperor defended Zhao Gao, but Li Si warned of his greed. The Second Emperor told Zhao Gao, who accused Li Si of plotting rebellion. Li Si was arrested and tortured into confessing. In prison, he lamented that the Second Emperor was worse than Jie and Zhou, killing brothers and loyal ministers, building the Epang Palace, and overtaxing the people. He wrote a letter listing his seven crimes, which were actually achievements, but Zhao Gao suppressed it. When the Second Emperor sent investigators, Li Si, fearing torture, did not change his confession. He was sentenced to five punishments and executed in the Xianyang market, along with his entire clan.

translation:
The Second Emperor asked his attendants: Is this a deer?
Everyone said: It's a horse.
The second generation panicked, thinking that he was confused, so he summoned the fortune teller and asked him to calculate a divination. Taibu said: Your Majesty goes to the countryside to offer sacrifices in the spring and autumn, and worships the ghosts and gods of the ancestral temple. He is not pious when fasting, and that is why he is like this.
You can fast again sincerely according to the appearance of a sage monarch.
So the second generation went to Shanglin Garden to fast.
He spent the whole day playing hunting in Shanglin Garden. Once a pedestrian walked into Shanglin Garden, and he shot him to death with his own hands.
Zhao Gao asked his son-in-law Yan Le of Xianyang to come forward to impeach, saying that someone unknown killed the person and moved the body into Shanglin Garden.
Zhao Gao advised the Second Emperor to say: The emperor kills innocent people for no reason. This is not allowed by God, and ghosts and gods will not accept your sacrifice. God will bring disasters, and you should stay away from the palace to pray for relief.
The second generation left the palace and went to live in Wangyi Palace.
The Second Emperor stayed in Wangyi Palace for three days. Zhao Gao pretended to be the Second Emperor's order and asked the guards to wear white clothes and face the palace with weapons in hand. He entered the palace and told the Second Emperor: Bandits from all walks of life in Shandong are coming in large numbers!
The Second Emperor went to the balcony to watch and saw the guards heading into the palace with weapons. He was very frightened. Zhao Gao immediately forced the Second Emperor to commit suicide.
Then he took the jade seal and carried it with him. None of the civil and military officials around him followed him. When he ascended the hall, it seemed to collapse several times.
Zhao Gao knew that God would not grant him the position of emperor, and the officials would not agree, so he called the younger brother of Qin Shihuang's younger brother and handed the jade seal to him.
After Ziying came to the throne, he was worried that Zhao Gao would cause trouble again, so he pretended to be ill and did not go to court to handle government affairs. He discussed with the eunuch Han Tan and his son how to kill Zhao Gao.
Zhao Gao came to see him and asked about his condition. Ziying summoned him to the palace and ordered Han Tan to assassinate him and annihilate his three clans.
Three months after Ziying came to the throne, Liu Bang's army invaded from Wuguan and arrived in Xianyang. All civil and military officials revolted against Qin and did not resist Pei Gong.
Ziying, his wife and children all tied ribbons around their necks and went to Zhidao Pavilion to surrender.
Liu Bang handed them over to the custody of his subordinate officials.
Xiang Yu killed them after arriving in Xianyang, and Qin lost the world.
Tai Shigong said: As a commoner in an alley, Li Si traveled to the princes, entered the customs to serve the Qin State, seized the opportunity, assisted Qin Shihuang, and finally completed the great cause of unification. Li Si occupies the position of the Three Officials and can be said to be very important.
Li Si knew the gist of the Confucian "Six Classics", but he did not devote himself to political clarity to make up for the emperor's faults. Instead, relying on his noble status, he flattered and followed at will, implemented harsh methods of torture, listened to Zhao Gao's heresy, abolished his legitimate son Fusu and established his concubine Hu Hai.
summary: After Li Si's death, Zhao Gao became Prime Minister. He tested his power by presenting a deer and calling it a horse, which all officials affirmed. The Second Emperor, confused, went to fast in Shanglin Garden, where he killed a pedestrian. Zhao Gao advised him to leave the palace to pray, then forced him to commit suicide. Zhao Gao tried to take the throne but failed, so he installed Ziying, a younger brother of the First Emperor. Ziying, fearing Zhao Gao, feigned illness and had him assassinated, annihilating his clan. Three months later, Liu Bang's army entered Xianyang, and Ziying surrendered. Xiang Yu later killed them, and Qin fell. The Grand Historian commented that Li Si, though a commoner, achieved great success but failed to correct the emperor's faults, instead flattering him and implementing harsh laws. He listened to Zhao Gao, deposed the rightful heir, and when rebellions arose, his belated advice was foolish. His loyalty was questionable, and his achievements, while great, were not comparable to those of the Duke of Zhou.

translation:
Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to attack the rebellious King of Yan Zang Tu, captured Zang Tu, and pacified the Yan territory.
King Han Xin of Chu launched a rebellion. Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to Chen County, arrested Han Xin, and pacified Chu.
Emperor Gaozu changed Fan Kuai's title to that of a noble prince and established a trustworthy relationship with the princes, so that they could be passed down from generation to generation. Emperor Gaozu removed Fan Kuai's former food town and gave him food in Wuyang, naming him Marquis of Wuyang.
Later, Fan Kuai followed Gaozu to Daidi as a general to attack the rebellious King Xin of Han.
From the Huo people to Yunzhong, Fan Kuai, Jianghou Zhoubo and others jointly pacified it, so an additional 1,500 households were added.
Later, Fan Kuai led his troops to attack the armies of the rebels Chen Xi and Manqiuchen, and fought in Xiangguo. When he captured Bairen County, he took the lead in ascending the city. He also surrendered and pacified twenty-seven counties in Qinghe and Changshan counties, and destroyed Dongyuan County. He was promoted to Prime Minister Zuo for his merits.
In Wujing and Guangchang, he defeated the armies of Qi Wuyan and Yin Pan and captured them alive.
In the south of Daidi, the army led by the Hu general Wang Huang under Chen Xi was defeated. Then, he marched to join forces and attacked Han Wangxin's army. Fan Kuai's men killed Han Wangxin.
In Henggu, Chen Xi's Hu cavalry troops were defeated, general Zhao Ji was killed, and ten people including the Prime Minister Han Liang, the governor Sun Fen, the general Wang Huang, Tai Pu Xie and the general were captured.
Together with the generals, he pacified seventy-three villages and towns in Dai.
After that, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled. Fan Kuai led the army to attack Lu Wan as prime minister, defeated the army led by Prime Minister Lu Wan in the south of Jixian County, and pacified a total of 18 counties and 51 townships in Yan.
So Emperor Gaozu gave Fan Kuai an additional 1,300 households, confirming that he would be the Marquis of Wuyang with a total of 5,400 households.
When Fan Kuai followed Gaozu in the battle, he beheaded 176 enemies and captured 188 enemy soldiers.
He led the troops to fight alone, defeated seven enemy armies, captured five cities, pacified six counties and fifty-two counties, and captured one enemy prime minister, 12 generals, and 11 officials ranging from 2,000 to 300 shi.
Because Fan Kuai married Empress Lu's sister Lu Xu and gave birth to a son, Mr. and Mrs. Fan, Gaozu was closer to Fan Kuai than other generals.
During the Yingbu rebellion, Gaozu was very ill and hated seeing people. He lay in the palace confinement and ordered the gatekeepers not to let the officials in to see him.
Among the officials, such as Jianghou Zhou Bo, Guan Ying and others did not dare to enter the palace.
After more than ten days of this, Fan Kuai once pushed open the palace door and rushed in, followed closely by the officials.
I saw Gaozu lying alone with a eunuch on his pillow.
After Fan Kuai and others saw the emperor, they cried bitterly and said: I think your majesty joined us in raising troops from Fengpei to pacify the world. What a feat it was!
And now that the world has settled down, how exhausted you are!
Besides, you are seriously ill, the ministers are panicking, and you are unwilling to meet us to discuss state affairs. Do you just want to decide with a eunuch?
Besides, haven't you seen anything about Zhao Gao?
After hearing this, Emperor Gaozu smiled and got up from the bed.
Later, Lu Wan rebelled, and Gaozu ordered Fan Kuai to attack Yan as prime minister.
At this time, Emperor Gaozu was very ill again. Some people slandered Fan Kuai and the Lu family for forming a party. If the emperor died one day, Fan Kuai would lead his troops to kill Madam Qi and King Zhao Ruyi.
When Emperor Gaozu heard about it, he became furious and immediately ordered Chen Ping to drive Jianghou Zhou Bo in a chariot to replace Fan Kuai, and immediately beheaded Fan Kuai in the army.
Because Chen Ping was afraid of Empress Lu, he did not carry out Gaozu's order, but sent Fan Kuai to Chang'an.
When they arrived in Chang'an, Gaozu had passed away, so Empress Lu released Fan Kuai and restored his title and fiefdom.
summary: Fan Kuai, a native of Peixian County, initially made a living by killing dogs and selling meat. He joined Liu Bang (later Emperor Gaozu of Han) in raising troops, capturing Peixian, and serving as a servant. Throughout numerous battles, Fan Kuai consistently demonstrated valor, often leading assaults on cities and beheading enemy soldiers. His military exploits included defeating Qin forces at Puyang, Chengyang, and Kaifeng, among others, earning him successive titles and promotions from Pei Gong (Liu Bang). A pivotal moment occurred at the Hongmen Banquet, where Xiang Yu plotted to kill Pei Gong. Fan Kuai, stationed outside, burst into the camp with an iron shield, confronted Xiang Yu, and condemned his actions, ultimately saving Pei Gong's life. Following Xiang Yu's defeat, Fan Kuai continued to serve Gaozu, suppressing rebellions by Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Lu Wan, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang with 5,400 households. He married Empress Lü's sister, Lü Xu, and remained close to Gaozu. During Gaozu's illness, Fan Kuai boldly entered the palace to urge him to attend to state affairs. Later, slandered for conspiring with the Lü clan, Gaozu ordered his execution, but Chen Ping delayed, and after Gaozu's death, Empress Lü released him. Fan Kuai died in the sixth year of Emperor Hui's reign, posthumously titled Marquis Wu. His descendants held the title until it was revoked in Emperor Jing's time due to legal transgressions. Guan Ying, a silk merchant from Suiyang, joined Pei Gong and fought in numerous campaigns, including against Qin forces and Xiang Yu. He distinguished himself as a cavalry commander, defeating Chu forces and capturing key figures like Zhou Lan. After Xiang Yu's death, Guan Ying pursued and killed him, leading to his enfeoffment as Marquis of Yingyin with 5,000 households. He later suppressed rebellions by Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Yingbu. During the Lü clan crisis, he feigned support but secretly allied with Zhou Bo to establish Emperor Wen, becoming Taiwei and later Prime Minister. He died in office, posthumously titled Yihou. His descendants held the title until it was revoked for bribery.

translation:
Because of his meritorious service in killing the enemy, he was promoted to the right prime minister, and was given the title of a lord. Like other princes, he cut the talisman as a letter, and it will never be extinguished from generation to generation. He took the five thousand households in Zhuoyi as his food town and was titled Zhuohou. As prime minister on the right, he led troops to pacify Shanggu alone, and then attacked Dai. Gaozu granted him the seal of the prime minister of Zhao.
As the Prime Minister of the Right and the Prime Minister of the State of Zhao, he led his troops, together with Jianghou Zhou Bo and others, to pacify Dai Heyanmen, and captured alive the Prime Minister of Dai Cheng Zong, the Prime Minister Guo Tong, and a total of 19 officials ranging from generals to 600 shi.
After the victory, he served as the bodyguard of the Supreme Emperor as a general for one year and seven months.
Then he used his position as Prime Minister You to attack Chen Xi and destroy the Dongyuan city wall.
As Prime Minister of the Right, he followed Emperor Gao to attack the rebellious Yingbu. Li Shang led his troops to storm the enemy's forward positions and captured two positions, allowing the Han army to defeat Yingbu's army. Emperor Gao changed his fiefdom to Quzhou, increasing it to 5,100 households, and took back the food fiefdoms he had previously granted. In total, Li Shang defeated three enemy armies, surrendered and pacified six counties and seventy-three counties, and captured the prime minister, the prime minister, one general each, two junior generals, and nineteen officials ranging from 2,000 shi to 600 shi.
Li Shang was serving Xiaohui. When he was a queen, he was unable to take care of political affairs due to poor health.
His son Li Ji was very close to Lu Lu.
In this year, Li Shang passed away, and his posthumous title was Jinghou.
His son Li Ji succeeded to the throne, and everyone in the world said that he had betrayed his friends.
In the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, the vassal states of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao jointly rebelled. The emperor appointed Li Ji as general and besieged Zhao City, but it was not conquered for ten months.
After Yu Hou Luanbu pacified the Qi State and came to help in the war, he took the city of Zhao and wiped out the Zhao State. King Liu Sui of Zhao committed suicide and the feudal state was abolished.
In the second year of Emperor Jing's reign, Li Ji planned to marry Pingyuan Jun, the mother of Emperor Jing and his wife. Emperor Jing was furious and handed Li Ji over to judicial officials for trial. He was found guilty and deprived of his title of marquis.
Emperor Jing named Li Shang's other son Li Jian the Marquis of Mu to continue the Li family's descendants.
After the death of Miao Jinghou Li Jian, his son Kanghou Li Suicheng succeeded to the throne.
After Li Suicheng died, his son Huaihou Li Shizong succeeded to the throne.
After the death of Li Shizong, his son Li Zhonggen inherited the throne and served as Taichang. Later, the feudal state was revoked because of breaking the law.
Xia Houying, Marquis of Ruyin, was from Peixian County.
He began to take charge of horse breeding and driving in the stable of Peixian County.
Whenever he drove back after seeing off envoys or guests, he would go to Sishang Pavilion in Peixian County to chat with Gaozu, and they would chat for most of the day.
Later, Xia Houying served as a probationary county official and became closer to Gao Zu.
Once, Gaozu accidentally injured Xia Houying because of a joke, and was reported to the government.
summary: Li Shang, from Gaoyang, initially gathered followers during Chen Sheng's rebellion and later joined Pei Gong with over 4,000 soldiers. He distinguished himself in battles, capturing cities like Changshe and Wan, and was appointed Lord of Xincheng and later Captain of Longxi. Li Shang fought against Xiang Yu, defeated forces of Yong King Zhanghan, and pacified regions including Beidi and Shangjun. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuoxian with 5,000 households, later serving as Right Prime Minister and leading campaigns against Chen Xi and Yingbu. His fief was changed to Quzhou with 5,100 households. Li Shang served under Emperor Xiaohui but was unable to govern due to illness. His son Li Ji succeeded but was executed for treason during the Rebellion of the Seven States. Another son, Li Jian, continued the lineage until it was eventually revoked for legal violations.

translation:
Emperor Gao changed the title of Xia Houying's food to Ruyin and cut the talisman into a letter so that the title could be passed down from generation to generation.
He also used his position as a servant to follow Emperor Gao to attack Daidi, and fought as far as Wuquan and Yunzhong. Emperor Gao gave him an additional 1,000 households.
Then he followed the King of Han to the vicinity of Jinyang and defeated the Huns cavalry belonging to Han Xin.
When chasing the defeated troops to Pingcheng, they were surrounded by Huns cavalry and were trapped for seven days without being able to escape.
Later, Emperor Gao sent people to give many gifts to the Queen of the Xiongnu King Maodun, and then the Xiongnu King Modu opened a corner of the encirclement.
As soon as Gaodi escaped from the siege and came out of Pingcheng, he wanted to drive away quickly. Xia Houying resolutely stopped the carriage and horses and walked slowly, ordering the archers to draw their bows fully and draw outwards. Finally, they were out of danger.
With this merit, Emperor Gao granted Xiahou Ying a title to a thousand households in Xiyang as a food town.
He also followed Emperor Gao as a servant to attack the Huns cavalry in the area north of Gouzhu Mountain and won a great victory.
As a servant, he attacked the Huns cavalry in the south of Pingcheng and broke through the enemy's formation many times. He made the most contributions. Emperor Gao gave him 500 households in the captured city as food.
He also used his position as a servant to attack the rebel armies of Chen Xun and Yingbu. He charged into battle and repelled the enemy troops. He also granted a settlement to a thousand households. Finally, the emperor designated Xia Houying's food town in Ruyin, with a total of 6,900 households, and revoked other food towns that had been sealed before.
Xia Houying followed Emperor Gao to raise troops in Peixian County and served as a servant for a long time until Emperor Gao's death.
Later, he served Emperor Xiaohui as a royal servant.
Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu were very grateful to Xia Houying for rescuing Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan on the road to Xiayi, so they gave him a first-class mansion close to the north of the palace, named "near me", which meant that he could be closest to me, and expressed their special respect for Xia Houying.
After the death of Emperor Xiaohui, he served the Empress Gao as a servant.
When Empress Gao passed away and King Dai came to the capital, Xia Houying went to the palace as a servant to clean up the palace together with Dongmou Hou Liu Xingju, deposed the young emperor, and used the emperor's method to drive to the palace of King Dai to welcome King Dai. Together with the ministers, he established King Dai as Emperor Xiaowen.
He died eight years later and was given the posthumous title Wenhou.
His son Yihou Xiahou Zao succeeded to the throne and died seven years later.
His son, Gonghou Xiahouci, inherited the title and died thirty-one years later.
His son Xia Houpo married Princess Pingyang. In the 19th year after he inherited the throne, that is, the second year of Yuanding, he committed adultery with his father's maid and committed suicide in fear of crime. The feudal state was also revoked.
Yingyinhou Guanying was originally a small businessman selling silk silk in Suiyang.
summary: Xiahou Ying, from Peixian, began as a stable hand and befriended Gaozu, even taking a false imprisonment for him. He joined Gaozu's uprising, serving as a chariot commander and fighting in key battles such as Dong'a and Kaifeng. After Xiang Yu's defeat, Xiahou Ying rescued Gaozu's children during a retreat and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ruyin with 6,900 households. He served as a servant under Gaozu, Xiaohui, and Empress Lü, and played a role in welcoming Emperor Wen to the throne. He died posthumously titled Wenhou. His descendants held the title until it was revoked for adultery.

translation:
Wuyang Hou Fan Kuai was a native of Peixian County. He made a living by killing dogs and selling their meat. He once hid in the countryside with Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
At first, Fan Kuai followed Gaozu and raised troops in Fengyi and captured Peixian County.
When Emperor Gaozu was the Duke of Pei, he used Fan Kuai as his servant.
He followed Pei Gong to attack Huling and Fangyu, then returned to guard Fengyi. He attacked the army of the Sishui County Supervisor in Fengyi and defeated them.
Then he went east to pacify Peixian County, and defeated the army of Sishui County Governor to the west of Xue County.
Fighting with Sima in the east of Dang County, he defeated the enemy and beheaded fifteen people. Pei Gong granted him the title of a senior official in other countries.
Pei Gong attacked Zhang Han's army in Puyang. When he attacked the city, Fan Kuai took the lead in ascending the city and beheaded twenty-three Qin soldiers. Pei Gong also gave him the title of Duke Dafu.
After that, he often followed Pei Gong. When he attacked Chengyang, he took the lead in ascending the city and captured Hufu. He defeated Li You's army, beheaded sixteen people, and was awarded the title of Shangjian.
When the follower Pei Gong besieged the governor of Dongjun in Chengwu, he repulsed the enemy, beheaded fourteen people, captured eleven people, and granted the title of five great officials.
Following Pei Gong, he attacked the Qin army and passed south of Boyi.
The troops of the governor of Hejian were in the camp, and Fan Kuai defeated them.
They also defeated Zhao Bi's army in the north of Kaifeng. Fan Kuai defeated the enemy and took the lead in ascending the city. He beheaded one of the military commanders, beheaded 68 people and captured 27 people. Pei Gong gave him the title of Qing.
Following Pei Gong, he defeated Yang Xiong's army in Quyu.
When attacking Wanling, Fan Kuai took the lead in ascending the city, beheaded eight people and captured 44 people. Peigong gave him the title of Xian Chengjun.
He followed Pei Gong to attack Changshe and Sheyuan, blockaded the Yellow River ferry, went east to attack the Qin army in Shixiang, and went south to attack the Qin army in Taoyi.
Defeat Lu , the governor of Nanyang County, in Yangcheng. When attacking Wancheng to the east, Fan Kuai took the lead in ascending the city.
Arriving at Li County in the west, Fan Kuai repelled the enemy, beheaded 24 of them and captured 40, and was rewarded by Pei Gong with an increase in rank and salary.
Attacked Wuguan, and when they reached Bashang, they killed one captain, beheaded ten people, captured 146 people, and surrendered 2,900 enemy soldiers.
Xiang Yu garrisoned under the stage and prepared to attack Peigong.
Pei Gong sent more than a hundred cavalry with him to meet Xiang Yu through Xiang Bo, and stated that he had not blocked the pass.
Xiang Yu held a banquet in honor of the army lieutenants. While they were drinking heavily, Yafu wanted to murder Pei Gong. He sent Xiang Zhuang to draw his sword and perform a dance in front of the banquet, hoping to take the opportunity to assassinate Pei Gong. However, Xiang Bo repeatedly protected Pei Gong.
At that time, only Pei Gong and Zhang Liang could enter the camp and sit down. Fan Kuai stayed outside the camp. Hearing that Pei Gong's situation was urgent, he entered the camp with an iron shield.
The guards of the military camp stopped Fan Kuai, but Fan Kuai ran straight in and stood under the tent.
summary: Sima Qian notes that these figures, originally humble commoners, rose to prominence and established lasting legacies through their service to the Han dynasty.

translation:
Chuilizi, named Ji, was the younger brother of King Hui of Qin. He and King Hui were not born to the same mother.
His mother is a Korean woman.
Chuilizi was eloquent and resourceful in dealing with people, so the people of Qin called him "the wise man".
In the eighth year of King Hui of Qin, Chuilizi was granted the title of Yougeng. The King of Qin sent him to lead an army to attack Quwo in the State of Wei. He drove away all the people there and occupied the city. The land around Quwo was annexed to the State of Qin.
In the twenty-fifth year of King Hui of Qin, the King of Qin appointed Chuilizi as a general to attack the State of Zhao. He captured General Zhuang Bao of the State of Zhao and captured Linyi.
The next year, he assisted Wei Zhang in attacking Chu, defeated Chu general Qu Gai, and captured the Hanzhong area.
The King of Qin granted him the title Chuilizi, with the title Yan Jun.
After the death of King Hui of Qin, Prince Wu came to the throne, expelled Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang, and appointed Chuilizi and Gan Mao as the left and right prime ministers.
The King of Qin sent Gan Mao to attack South Korea and captured Yiyang in one fell swoop. At the same time, he sent Chuilizi to lead a hundred chariots to the Zhou Dynasty capital.
The king of Zhou sent soldiers to line up to greet him with a very respectful attitude.
When the King of Chu learned about it, he was furious and scolded the King of Zhou because the King of Zhou should not be so respectful to Qin's uninvited guests.
In this regard, You Teng persuaded the King of Chu on behalf of the King of Zhou: When Zhibo attacked Qiu You before, he used the method of giving away carts to take the opportunity to let the army follow behind, but Qiu You was destroyed.
Why?
It’s just because I’m unprepared.
When Duke Huan of Qi attacked Cai, he claimed that he was punishing Chu, but in fact he was attacking Cai secretly.
Now the Qin State is a country as fierce as a tiger and a wolf. He sent Chuilizi into the Zhou capital with hundreds of chariots, with ulterior motives. The King of Zhou viewed this matter based on the lessons of Qiu You and Cai Guo, so he sent soldiers with halberds in front and sergeants with strong bows in the back. On the surface, they were guarding Chuilizi, but in fact they were keeping him under guard to prevent any unexpected events.
Besides, how could the King of Zhou not worry about the Zhou Dynasty?
I'm afraid that once subjugated, it will bring trouble to you, Your Majesty.
King Chu became happy after hearing this.
After King Wu of Qin died and King Zhao came to the throne, Chuilizi was even more respected.
In the first year of King Zhao, Chuilizi led his troops to attack Pucheng in Weiguo.
The chief of Pucheng was very frightened and asked Hu Yan for advice.
Hu Yan stepped forward and said to Chuilizi on behalf of the chief of Pucheng: Are you attacking Pucheng for the sake of Qin or Wei?
If it is for Wei, then of course it is good; if it is for Qin, it is not advantageous.
The reason why Weiguo became Weiguo was because of the existence of Pucheng.
Now if you attack it and force it to be included in the territory of Wei State, the entire Wei State will surrender and attach itself to Wei State.
Wei lost the cities outside Xihe but was unable to regain them because its military strength was too weak.
Now the attack on Pucheng will merge the Wei State into the Wei State, and the Wei State will definitely become stronger.
When Wei is strong, the cities occupied by your country are in danger.
Moreover, the King of Qin wants to observe your actions. If it harms the State of Qin and benefits the State of Wei, the King of Qin will definitely punish you.
summary: Chuilizi, named Ji, was the younger brother of King Hui of Qin, born to a Korean mother. Known for his eloquence and resourcefulness, he was called "the wise man" by the people of Qin. In the eighth year of King Hui's reign, he was granted the title of Yougeng and led an army to attack Quwo in Wei, driving out the inhabitants and annexing the land. In the twenty-fifth year, he captured General Zhuang Bao of Zhao and seized Linyi. The following year, he assisted Wei Zhang in defeating Chu, capturing the Hanzhong area. King Hui granted him the title Chuilizi, with the title Yan Jun. After King Hui's death, King Wu expelled Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang, appointing Chuilizi and Gan Mao as left and right prime ministers. King Wu sent Gan Mao to attack South Korea, capturing Yiyang, while Chuilizi led a hundred chariots to the Zhou capital. The King of Zhou greeted him respectfully, angering the King of Chu. You Teng persuaded the King of Chu that the Zhou king's actions were precautionary, not disrespectful, and the King of Chu became appeased.

translation:
After hearing these words, Qilizi said thoughtfully: What should we do?
Hu Yan took advantage of the situation and said: "You give up Pucheng and don't attack. I will try to go to Pucheng for you to tell you this, so that the king of Wei will not forget the kindness you have given him." Qilizi said: Okay.
After Hu Yan entered Pucheng, he said to the officer: Chuilizi has grasped Pucheng's difficult situation, and he promised to capture Pucheng.
However, I, Hu Yan, can make him abandon Pucheng and stop attacking.
Chief Pucheng was very frightened. After hearing Hu Yan's words, he felt as if he had seen a savior. He worshiped again and again and said, "Please help me."
So he offered three hundred catties of gold and said: The Qin army has really retreated. Please allow me to report your achievements to the king of Wei, so that you can enjoy the same treatment as a king.
Therefore, Hu Yan received a large sum of money from Pucheng and became a prominent figure in Weiguo.
At this time, Chuilizi had relieved the siege and evacuated Pucheng, and returned to attack Pishi, the city of Wei State. Pishi did not surrender, so he withdrew again.
In the seventh year of King Zhao, Chuilizi died and was buried east of Zhangtai, south of the Wei River.
Before his death, he prophesied: A hundred years from now, there will be the emperor's palace sandwiching my tomb here.
Chuilizi Yingji's home is in Chuili, Yinxiang, south of the Wei River, west of Zhaowang Temple, so people commonly call him Chuilizi.
With the rise of the Han Dynasty, the Changle Palace was built to the east of his tomb, while the Weiyang Palace was to the west of his tomb, and the arsenal was directly opposite his tomb, just as it was said.
There is a proverb from the Qin people: If you are strong, you should be considered Renbi, and if you are resourceful, you should be considered Qili.
Gan Mao was from Xiacai.
Mr. Shi Ju, who once served Xia Cai, learned from him the theories of various schools of thought.
Later, he got the opportunity to meet King Qin Hui through the introduction of Zhang Yi and Chuilizi.
After King Hui met him, he liked him very much and sent him to lead troops to help Wei Zhang seize the Hanzhong area.
After King Hui died, King Wu came to the throne.
At that time, Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang had left the State of Qin and ran to the State of Wei in the east.
Soon, Qin Gongzi Shuhou Hui and his assistant Chen Zhuang rebelled, and King Wu assigned Gan Mao to pacify Shu.
After returning to Qin, King Wu appointed Gan Mao as the prime minister of the left and Chulizi as the prime minister of the right.
In the third year of King Wu of Qin, King Wu said to Gan Mao: I have a wish to ride in a carriage with hanging curtains, pass through the land of Sanchuan, and see the capital of the Zhou Dynasty. Even if I die, I will be considered satisfied.
Gan Mao understood this and said, "Please allow me to go as envoy to the Wei State and make an appointment with the Wei State to attack South Korea. Please allow Xiang Shou to assist me in going together."
King Wu agreed to Gan Mao's request. After Gan Mao arrived in Wei, he said to Xiang Shou: Go back and report the situation to King Wu. Wei has listened to my advice, but I hope the king will not attack South Korea first.
Once the work is done, it will be all your credit.
Xiang Shou returned to Qin and reported Gan Mao's words to King Wu. King Wu went to Xirang to greet Gan Mao.
Gan Mao arrived at Xirang, and King Wu asked him why he didn't attack South Korea first.
Gan Mao replied: Yiyang is a large county. Shangdang and Nanyang have accumulated wealth for a long time.
The name is county, but it is actually a county.
summary: Under King Zhao, Chuilizi was even more respected. In the first year of King Zhao's reign, he attacked Pucheng in Weiguo. Hu Yan, on behalf of Pucheng's chief, argued that attacking Pucheng would strengthen Wei and endanger Qin, leading Chuilizi to abandon the siege. Chuilizi later attacked Pishi but withdrew when it did not surrender. He died in the seventh year of King Zhao and was buried east of Zhangtai, south of the Wei River. Before his death, he prophesied that an emperor's palace would flank his tomb, which came true with the construction of Changle and Weiyang Palaces during the Han Dynasty. Gan Mao, from Xiacai, studied under Mr. Shi Ju and met King Hui through Zhang Yi and Chuilizi. He helped capture Hanzhong and later pacified Shu under King Wu, who appointed him left prime minister. King Wu wished to pass through Sanchuan to see the Zhou capital, so Gan Mao proposed attacking Yiyang. Despite doubts from Chuilizi and Gongsun Shi, Gan Mao captured Yiyang after five months, killing 60,000 enemies. King Wu died after reaching the Zhou capital.

translation:
Now that the Yong family is under siege, and the Qin army refuses to go out to Mt. Miao to rescue them, Gong Zhongchi will look down upon Qin and not come to court.
Uncle Han will also ask South Korea to move south to unite with Chu. Once Chu and South Korea unite, Wei will not dare to disobey it. In this way, the situation of attacking Qin will be formed.
What do you think is more advantageous than waiting for others to attack versus taking the initiative to attack others? King Zhao of Qin said: OK.
So the army was sent down Miao Mountain to rescue South Korea.
The Chu army immediately withdrew.
The King of Qin asked Xiang Shou to pacify Yiyang, and at the same time sent Chuilizi and Ganmao to attack the Pi family of Wei.
Xiang Shou was a relative of Empress Dowager Xuan. She had been close to King Zhao since they were young, so she was appointed by King Zhao.
Xiang Shou arrived in Chu State first. The King of Chu heard that King Qin respected Xiang Shou very much, so he treated Xiang Shou generously.
Xiang Shou garrisoned Yiyang for Qin, preparing to attack South Korea accordingly.
Han Xianggong Zhongchi sent Su Dai to say to Xiang Shou: A wild beast can knock over a hunter's car if it is in a hurry.
Although you conquered South Korea and humiliated Gong Zhongchi, Gong Zhongchi could still clean up the situation in South Korea and then serve Qin. He would think that he would definitely get a grant from Qin.
Now you give Jie Kou to the State of Chu, and give Du Yang to Xia Xiaoling Yin, so that Qin and Chu can have good relations.
The alliance between Qin and Chu is nothing more than attacking South Korea again, and South Korea will definitely perish.
If South Korea is to perish, Gong Zhongchi will personally lead his private disciples to resist Qin tenaciously.
I hope you've given this a lot of thought.
Xiang Shou said: I unite Qin and Chu not to deal with South Korea. Please explain this to Gong Zhongchi for me, saying that the relationship between Qin and South Korea can be cooperative.
Su Dai replied: I would like to tell you something further.
People say that only by respecting what others respect can you win the respect of others.
The King of Qin is not as close to you as he is to Gongsun Xi; the King of Qin does not appreciate your wisdom and talent as much as he appreciates Gan Mao.
But now these two people cannot directly participate in the major affairs of the Qin State, but you can only make decisions on the major affairs of the Qin State with the King of Qin. What is the reason for this?
They each have their own places where they lose trust.
Gongsun Shi favored South Korea, while Gan Mao favored Wei, so the King of Qin did not trust them.
Now the state of Qin is competing with the state of Chu, but you favor the state of Chu. This is the same path as Gongsun Shi and Gan Mao.
How do you differentiate yourself from them? People say that the Chu State is a country that is good at adapting to changes. You will definitely have trouble making friends with the Chu State, and you will be asking for trouble.
You might as well plan a contingency strategy with the King of Qin to deal with Chu's changes, be friendly with South Korea and guard against Chu, so that there will be no worries.
If South Korea forms a good relationship with Qin, it must first hand over state affairs to Gongsun Shi and obey his opinions, and then entrust the country to Gan Mao.
South Korea is your enemy.
Now you propose to be friendly with South Korea and guard against Chu. This is a diplomatic alliance without avoiding enemies.
Xiang Shou said: That's right, I really want to cooperate with South Korea.
Su Dai replied: Gan Mao once promised Gong Zhongchi to return Wu Sui to South Korea and let the people of Yiyang return to Yiyang. Now you are only thinking about taking back Wu Sui, which is difficult to do.
summary: Under King Zhao, Queen Mother Xuan, a Chu native, initially refused to aid South Korea against Chu. Gan Mao advised sending troops, and the Chu army withdrew. Xiang Shou, a relative of the Queen Mother, was sent to pacify Yiyang. Su Dai advised Xiang Shou to ally with South Korea against Chu, but Xiang Shou hesitated. Gan Mao eventually fled to Qi after conflicts with Xiang Shou and Gongsun Shi. Su Dai persuaded King Zhao to welcome Gan Mao back, but Gan Mao refused and served Qi instead. He later died in Wei.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/樗里子甘茂列传

translation:
Zhang Tang said to Marquis Wenxin: I once attacked the State of Zhao for King Zhao, so the State of Zhao resented me. He once said: "Whoever can capture Zhang Tang will be rewarded with a hundred miles of land."
Now to go to Yan State, you must pass through Zhao State, and I can't go there.
Marquis Wenxin was unhappy after hearing this, but there was nothing he could do to force him to go.
Gan Luo said: Junhou, why are you so depressed?
Marquis Wenxin said: I asked Cai Ze, Lord Gangcheng, to serve the State of Yan for three years. Prince Dan of Yan has come to Qin as a hostage. I personally invited Zhang Qing to serve as Prime Minister of the State of Yan, but he was unwilling to go.
Gan Luo said: Please allow me to persuade him to go to Yan State.
Marquis Wenxin scolded and said: "Go away!"
I personally asked him to go, but he was unwilling. How could you let him go?
Gan Luo said: Xiang Luo became Confucius's teacher at the age of seven.
Now that I am twelve years old, you still let me give it a try. Why are you so anxious to scold me?
So Wenxinhou agreed. Gan Luo went to see Zhang Qing and said: "Compared with your contribution and that of Lord Wu'an Bai Qi, who has greater contribution?"
Zhang Qing said: Lord Wu An defeated the powerful Chu State in the south, used his power to intimidate Yan and Zhao in the north, was able to win in battle, conquered in attack, and captured countless cities and towns. My achievements cannot compare with him.
Gan Luo said again: When Yinghou Fan Sui was the prime minister of Qin, who had greater power compared with the current Marquis Wenxin?
Zhang Qing said: Marquis Ying is not as powerful as Marquis Wenxin.
Gan Luo then said: Do you really understand that Marquis Ying is not as powerful as Marquis Wenxin?
Zhang Qing said: I really understand this.
Gan Luo went on to say: Marquis Ying planned to attack the State of Zhao, but Lord Wu An deliberately made things difficult for him. As a result, Lord Wu An died in Duyou as soon as he left Qili of Xianyang.
Now that Marquis Wenxin has personally invited you to serve as Prime Minister of the State of Yan but you insist on refusing, I don't know where you are going to die.
Zhang Tang said: Then follow your boy's advice and go to Yan State.
So people packed their bags and prepared to go on the road.
The departure date had been set, and Gan Luo said to Marquis Wenxin: Lend me five carriages, and please allow me to say hello to Zhao when Zhang Tang goes to Yan.
Marquis Wenxin went into the palace and reported Gan Luo's request to Qin Shihuang, saying: In the past, Gan Mao had a grandson named Gan Luo. He was very young, but he was a descendant of a famous family, so the princes all heard about it.
Recently, Zhang Tang wanted to excuse himself from going to Yan State because he was ill, but Gan Luo persuaded him and made him go resolutely.
Now Gan Luo is willing to go to Zhao State first to inform Zhang Tang about Zhang Tang, and please agree to send him there.
Qin Shihuang summoned Gan Luo and sent him to Zhao.
King Zhao Xiang went to the outskirts to welcome Gan Luo.
Gan Luo persuaded King Zhao and asked, "Has your Majesty heard that Prince Dan of Yan went to Qin as a hostage?"
King Zhao replied: I heard about it.
Gan Luo asked again: Have you heard that Zhang Tang is going to Yan State to serve as prime minister?
King Zhao replied: I heard about it.
Gan Luo then said: Prince Dan of Yan came to Qin, which shows that Yan will not deceive Qin.
Zhang Tang went to Yan State to serve as prime minister, which showed that Qin State would not deceive Yan State.
summary: Gan Mao's grandson, Gan Luo, served Lu Buwei at age twelve. He persuaded Zhang Tang to go to Yan as prime minister and then convinced King Zhao of Zhao to cede five cities to Qin, leading to Zhao's attack on Yan and Qin's gain of eleven cities. Gan Luo was rewarded with a ministerial position and Gan Mao's former lands.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/樗里子甘茂列传

translation:
Yan and Qin do not bully each other. They obviously want to attack Zhao together, and Zhao will be in danger.
Yan and Qin did not bully each other for no other reason than to attack Zhao to expand their territory in the Hejian area.
Your Majesty, why don't you give me five cities first to expand Qin's territory in Hejian? I ask the King of Qin to send back the Prince of Yan, and then help the powerful Zhao State attack the weak Yan State.
King Zhao immediately set aside five cities to expand Qin's territory in the river.
Qin State sent back Prince Yan, and Zhao State had no fear and attacked Yan State. As a result, Zhao State obtained thirty cities in the upper valley, allowing Qin State to occupy eleven of them.
After Gan Luo came back, he reported the situation to the King of Qin. The King of Qin then rewarded Gan Luo and made him a minister. He also gave Gan Luo the land and house that belonged to Gan Mao.
Tai Shigong said: It is common sense that Chuilizi was favored because he was a brother of the King of Qin. However, the people of Qin praised his intelligence and recorded more of his deeds.
Gan Mao was born among the common people in Xiacai, and his reputation was well-known among the princes, and he was highly respected by the powerful Qi and Chu states.
Gan Luo was very young, but he came up with an ingenious plan and his reputation will be remembered by future generations.
Although he is not a loyal gentleman, he is also a veritable counselor during the Warring States Period.
It should be noted that when the Qin State became strong and prosperous, the world became more and more inclined to pursue the art of contingency and deception!
summary: Tai Shigong noted that Chuilizi's favor came from his royal lineage, while Gan Mao rose from commoner status to fame. Gan Luo's youthful ingenuity earned him lasting renown, though neither was a loyal gentleman, both were true counselors of the Warring States period, reflecting the era's trend toward cunning strategies.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/樗里子甘茂列传

translation:
Ji An, whose courtesy name is Changru, was born in Puyang County.
His ancestors were favored by the king of the ancient Wei Kingdom.
By the time he was the seventh generation, he had been serving as ministers and officials in the court for generations.
Ji An relied on his father's recommendation. During the reign of Emperor Xiao Jing, Ji An became the prince Xima. He was respected by others because he was a serious man.
When Emperor Jing died, the prince succeeded to the throne and appointed him as the official of the audience.
There was an attack between the Minyue and Ouyue people in East Vietnam, and the emperor sent Ji An to inspect.
Before he reached Dongyue, he turned back when he reached Wuxian and reported: The Dongyue people are attacking each other because the local folk customs are so aggressive that it is not worth bothering the emperor's envoys to inquire.
A fire broke out in Hanoi County, burning more than a thousand households. The emperor sent Ji An to inspect.
He came back and reported: Ordinary people there accidentally catch fire. Because the houses are densely packed, the fire spreads, so there is no need to worry.
When I passed through Henan County, I saw that the local poor were suffering from floods and droughts. There were more than ten thousand families affected by the disaster, and some even went as far as father and son eating each other. So I took advantage of the talisman I held and ordered the distribution of grain stored in the official warehouse of Henan County to provide relief to the local victims.
Now I request that the talisman be returned and bear the responsibility of falsely preaching the imperial edict.
The emperor believed that Ji An was a virtuous person, so he was exempted from guilt and was transferred to Xingyang County Magistrate.
Ji An thought it was a shame to be a county magistrate, so he resigned and returned home claiming illness.
When the emperor heard the news, he summoned Ji An to serve as a senior official in the imperial court.
Because he repeatedly expressed his opinions to the emperor, he was still not allowed to stay in the court for a long time and was released as the prefect of Donghai County.
Ji An admired Taoism, managed the government and handled civil affairs. He liked to be clean and tidy, and entrusted all matters to the capable county magistrates and book historians he selected.
When he manages county affairs, he just supervises his subordinates to act in accordance with general principles and does not pay attention to details.
He was frail and sickly and often lay indoors without going out.
In more than a year, Donghai County became very peaceful and peaceful, and people praised him very much.
After the emperor learned about it, he summoned Ji'an back to the capital to serve as the Lord Commander, and he was treated similarly to Jiu Qing's treatment.
He strives to govern by doing nothing, and promotes the big ideas without adhering to the legal provisions.
Ji An is very arrogant when dealing with others, does not pay attention to etiquette, contradicts people in person, and cannot tolerate other people's mistakes.
He would be close to and friendly to those who were congenial to him; he would be impatient to meet those who were incompatible with him, and therefore the scholars would not want to rely on him.
But Ji An was eager to learn and good at doing chivalry, and he paid great attention to his ambition and integrity. He usually lives at home and has good and pure conduct; when he enters the court, he likes to speak out and give advice, repeatedly offending the emperor's face, and often admires the conduct of Fu Bai and Yuan An.
summary: Ji An, courtesy name Changru, was born in Puyang County, with ancestors serving as ministers for seven generations. During Emperor Xiao Jing's reign, he became a prince Xima through his father's recommendation and was respected for his seriousness. After Emperor Jing's death, the new emperor appointed him as an official of the audience. Sent to inspect conflicts between the Minyue and Ouyue peoples, he turned back at Wuxian, deeming the local aggression unworthy of imperial attention. Similarly, after a fire in Hanoi County burned over a thousand households, he reported it as an accident due to dense housing. While passing through Henan County, he saw severe flood and drought suffering, with over ten thousand families affected and reports of cannibalism. Using his talisman, he distributed grain from official stores for relief, then returned the talisman and accepted responsibility for falsely preaching the imperial edict. The emperor, considering him virtuous, exempted him from guilt and transferred him to Xingyang County Magistrate. Ji An, ashamed of the role, resigned claiming illness. The emperor then summoned him as a senior official in the imperial court, but due to his frequent outspoken opinions, he was released as the prefect of Donghai County. Ji An admired Taoism, managed affairs cleanly, and delegated to capable subordinates, focusing on general principles rather than details. Despite frail health, he often stayed indoors, and within a year, Donghai County became peaceful and praised. The emperor recalled him as Lord Commander, treating him similarly to Jiu Qing. He governed by doing nothing, promoting big ideas without strict legal adherence. Arrogant and blunt, he contradicted people openly, befriending only those congenial to him and shunning others, causing scholars to avoid him. Yet he was eager to learn, chivalrous, and principled, often speaking out in court and offending the emperor, admiring figures like Fu Bai and Yuan An. He associated with Guan Fu, Zheng Shi, Zong Zheng, and Liu Qi, who also faced demotions for remonstrance.

translation:
He had good relations with Guan Fu, Zheng Shi and Zong Zheng and Liu Qi.
They were also unable to stay in their official positions for a long time because of their repeated remonstrances.
Just when Ji An was appointed Lord Commander and Lieutenant-in-Chief, the Queen Mother's younger brother Wu'anhou Tianfu became prime minister. When high-ranking officials with an annual salary of two thousand dan came to visit him, they all knelt down and bowed down, but Tian Fu actually refused to return the courtesy.
But when Ji An asked to see Tian Fu, he never bowed down and often bowed to him.
At this time, the emperor was recruiting literary scholars and Confucian scholars, saying what I wanted, Ji An replied: "Your Majesty has many desires in his heart and only practices benevolence and righteousness on the surface. How can he truly imitate the political achievements of Tang Yao and Yu Shun!"
The emperor was silent, angry in his heart, and then stopped courting with a sudden change of expression. The ministers were all frightened and worried about Ji An.
After the emperor retired from the court, he said to the ministers around him: This is too much, Ji An is too stupid and straightforward!
Someone among the ministers blamed Ji An, and Ji An said: Is it true that the emperor appointed ministers such as public ministers and hundreds of officials to be submissive and flattery, and put the monarch in a dilemma that goes against the right path?
What's more, I am already in the position of Jiuqing. Even though I cherish my life, what if I harm the important affairs of the court?
Ji An was sick and had been ill for three months. The emperor had repeatedly granted him leave to recuperate, but his illness never recovered.
The last time he was very ill, Zhuang Zhu asked for leave on his behalf. The emperor asked: How is Ji An?
Zhuang Zhu said: There is nothing extraordinary about letting Ji An become an official and deacon.
However, he can assist the young monarch, stick to the established cause, use inducements to prevent him from coming, use threats to prevent him from leaving. Even if someone claims to be as brave as Meng Ben and Xia Yu, he cannot regret his integrity. The emperor said: Yes.
In ancient times, there were so-called loyal ministers who ensured peace and security, and Ji An was very similar to them.
General Wei Qing entered the palace, and the emperor sat beside the bed to see him.
Prime Minister Gongsun Hong usually asked to see him for something, but the emperor sometimes didn't even wear his hat.
As for Ji An's visit, the emperor would not receive him without wearing a good hat.
The emperor was once sitting in a majestic military tent. When Ji An came to report on official business, the emperor was not wearing a hat. When he saw him, he hurriedly hid in the tent and sent a close servant to approve his memorial.
Ji An was respected and respected by the emperor to this extent.
As soon as Zhang Tang became a court official by changing the criminal law, Ji An repeatedly questioned and accused Zhang Tang in front of the emperor, saying: As a minister, you are unable to carry forward the achievements of the late emperor, and you are unable to curb the evil desires of the people in the world. Safeguarding the country and enriching the people, and keeping the prisons empty of criminals are neither of these two things.
On the contrary, you try your best to do the wrong thing and make others guilty in order to achieve your own career. How dare you change the rules and regulations set by Emperor Gaozu?
If you do this, you will lose your descendants.
summary: When Wu'anhou Tianfu became prime minister, high-ranking officials knelt to him, but Ji An only bowed. The emperor, recruiting literary scholars, was rebuked by Ji An for having many desires while feigning benevolence. The emperor grew angry, and ministers feared for Ji An. Later, the emperor remarked on Ji An's stupidity, but Ji An defended his integrity, stating he would not harm court affairs. Ill for three months, Ji An's condition persisted. Zhuang Zhu, requesting leave on his behalf, told the emperor that Ji An could assist a young monarch steadfastly, unswayed by inducements or threats. The emperor agreed, comparing Ji An to ancient loyal ministers.
