translation:
Ji An often argued with Zhang Tang. When Zhang Tang argued, he always deliberately delved into the provisions and demanded details. Ji An, on the other hand, was upright and serious in his speech, high-spirited and unwilling to give in. He scolded Zhang Tang angrily and said: "Everyone in the world said that an official with swords and pens should never be allowed to hold the position of public minister. It is true."
If we act according to what Zhang Tang said, people in the world will be so frightened that they will stand with their feet together and not dare to take a step, and they will not dare to look directly at him!
At this time, the Han Dynasty was conquering the Xiongnu and recruiting ethnic minorities in various places.
Ji An tried to keep the country in peace, and often took the opportunity to advise the emperor to propose peace with the Huns instead of raising troops to fight.
The emperor was devoted to Confucianism and respected Gongsun Hong, but he didn't care about it.
When domestic troubles arose, and low-level officials and lawless people tried their best to evade justice, the emperor decided to separate the laws and enforce strict laws. Zhang Tang and others continued to report important cases to win the emperor's favor.
And Ji An often slandered Confucianism and criticized Gongsun Hong and others face to face for being treacherous at heart but clever outside, in order to please the emperor to win favor; the swordsman and penman were dedicated to studying the legal provisions and slandering them with clever words to frame others as guilty. , preventing the truth from being revealed, and using victory in prison as capital to claim credit, so the emperor relied more and more on Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang. Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang hated Ji An deeply, and even the emperor disliked him and wanted to kill him for an excuse.
Gongsun Hong became the prime minister and suggested to the emperor: There are many dignitaries and royal family members living in the right inner history area, which is difficult to manage. It is not that a minister with a good reputation cannot take on this important task. Please appoint Ji An as the right inner history.
Ji An served as the internal history of You for several years. During his tenure, his political affairs were in order and never neglected.
The general Wei Qing has become more and more noble. His sister Wei Zifu became the queen, but Ji An still treated him as an equal.
Someone advised Ji An: "The emperor wanted all the officials to be subordinate to the general. Now that the general is respected and valued by the emperor, his status is even more noble. You must kneel down and worship him."
Ji An replied: "Because the general has guests who bow his hands and salute, does that make him disrespected?"
When the general heard what he said, he thought Ji An was even more virtuous. He asked him many times for advice on difficult matters in the country and the court, and regarded him better than people he had always known.
Liu An, the king of Huainan, conspired to rebel and was afraid of Ji An. He said: "Ji An loves to speak out and give advice. He sticks to his integrity and is willing to die for justice. It is difficult to tempt him with unfair things."
As for persuading Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, it was as easy as removing a covering or shaking off the falling leaves.
When today the emperor has conquered the Xiongnu many times and achieved great success, and Ji An advocated making peace with the foreigners without raising troops to conquer, he would not listen even more.
When Ji An was enjoying the treatment of Jiuqing, Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang were just ordinary petty officials.
When Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang became more prominent and equaled Ji An in official positions, Ji An again accused and slandered them.
Soon, Gongsun Hong was promoted to prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Pingjin; Zhang Tangguan was promoted to Yushi Dafu; the former county magistrates and book historians under Ji An were also at the same level as Ji An, and some were re-employed and even surpassed him in status.
Ji An was narrow-minded and impetuous, and it was impossible not to complain at all. When he met with the emperor, he stepped forward and said: Your Majesty appoints ministers like a pile of firewood, and the later ones are piled on top.
summary: General Wei Qing entered the palace with the emperor seated by his bed, while Prime Minister Gongsun Hong sometimes saw the emperor without a hat. For Ji An, the emperor always wore a hat, once hiding in a tent when unprepared. Ji An was highly respected. When Zhang Tang became a court official, Ji An accused him of failing to uphold the late emperor's achievements and changing rules set by Emperor Gaozu, warning of lost descendants. They often argued, with Ji An scolding Zhang Tang for causing fear. The Han Dynasty was then conquering the Xiongnu, and Ji An advised peace, but the emperor favored Confucianism and Gongsun Hong. Ji An criticized Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang as treacherous, leading to their deep hatred. Gongsun Hong suggested Ji An as Right Internal History to manage dignitaries, a role Ji An handled well for years. General Wei Qing's status rose, but Ji An treated him as an equal. When advised to kneel, Ji An replied that bowing did not diminish respect. Wei Qing valued Ji An's virtue, seeking his advice. Liu An, the king of Huainan, feared Ji An's integrity, noting it was hard to tempt him. As Ji An enjoyed Jiuqing treatment, Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang rose to equal ranks, then surpassed him. Ji An complained to the emperor about later officials being piled on top, but the emperor dismissed his stupidity. When King Hunxie of the Xiongnu surrendered, the court borrowed horses from the people, causing unrest. Ji An defended the magistrate of Chang'an, suggesting gradual preparations. Later, over 500 merchants were sentenced to death for trading with the Huns. Ji An argued against harsh laws, but the emperor disagreed. Months later, Ji An was convicted of a minor law, dismissed, and retired.

translation:
The emperor said: "Don't you look down on the position of the governor of Huaiyang County?"
I now summon and appoint you.
Due to the tense relationship between the local government and the people in Huaiyang, I have no choice but to use your authority and ask you to stay at home and manage it.
After Ji An said goodbye to the emperor, he went to visit Li Xi, the great minister. He said: I was abandoned in a foreign county and can no longer participate in the affairs of the imperial court.
However, Zhang Tang, the imperial censor, was clever enough to block other people's criticism, and cunning enough to cover up his own mistakes. He used clever flattery words and strong arguments to find faults. He refused to speak uprightly for the people of the world, and devoted himself to catering to the emperor's thoughts.
If the emperor didn't want it, he would slander it; if the emperor wanted it, he would take the opportunity to praise it.
He likes to cause trouble and fiddle with laws and regulations. In court, he is deeply treacherous to cater to the Lord's will, and outside the court, he blackmails officials who harm society to strengthen his power.
You are the ninth minister. If you don't advise the emperor as soon as possible, both you and him will be killed.
Li Xi was afraid of Zhang Tang and never dared to remonstrate with the emperor.
Ji An managed the county affairs as he had in the past, and the politics of Huaiyang County became clear.
Later, Zhang Tang was indeed ruined. After the emperor learned what Ji An had said to Li Xi, he found Li Xi guilty and ordered Ji An to enjoy the salary treatment of the princes and ministers and still be in charge of Huaiyang County.
Ji An died seven years later.
After Ji An's death, because of Ji An's relationship, the emperor appointed his younger brother Ji Ren to be promoted to the rank of Jiu Qing, and his son Ji Yan to be promoted to the minister of the princes and states.
Ji An's aunt's son Sima An was also the prince Xima when he was young. He was good at juggling legal provisions and was skillful in serving as an official. His official position reached Jiuqing four times, and he died while serving as the governor of Henan County.
Because of him, ten of his brothers were promoted to the rank of two thousand shi at the same time.
Duan Hong from Puyang initially served Gaihou Wang Xin. Wang Xin recommended Duan Hong, and Duan Hong was promoted to Jiuqing twice.
But the officials in Puyang's hometown all respected Ji An and were content to live under him.
Zheng was born in Chen County with a courtesy name of Zhuang.
His ancestor Zheng Jun once served as a general under Xiang Ji. Soon after Xiang Ji died, he belonged to the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Gaozu ordered all Xiang Ji's former subordinates to call him by his first name when referring to Xiang Ji. Zheng Jun alone refused to accept the edict.
Emperor Gaozu decreed that those who were willing to address Xiang Ji by his first name would be worshiped as senior officials, and Lord Zheng was driven away.
Zheng Jun died during the reign of Emperor Xiaowen.
Zheng Zhuang took pleasure in being a chivalrous man and rescuing Zhang Yu from danger, and his reputation spread throughout Liang and Chu.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, he served as Prince Sheren.
During every five-day holiday, he often bought horses in the suburbs of Chang'an, rode on horseback to visit old friends, invited and thanked guests and friends, and stayed up all night long, always worrying about omissions.
Zheng Zhuang loves Taoism and admires elderly and virtuous people. His affection is as intense as if he is afraid that he will never see them again.
summary: Years later, the emperor appointed Ji An as prefect of Huaiyang County due to private coin minting. Ji An declined but was forced to accept. He managed the county well, and after Zhang Tang's ruin, the emperor ordered Ji An to enjoy princes' salary while governing Huaiyang. Ji An died seven years later. His brother Ji Ren and son Ji Yan were promoted, and his aunt's son Sima An reached Jiuqing four times. Duan Hong from Puyang also rose to Jiuqing, but officials respected Ji An more.

translation:
He is young and has a humble official position, but his close friends are all from his grandfather's generation and are famous people in the world.
After Emperor Wu came to the throne, Zhengzhuang was promoted step by step from the lieutenant of Lu State, the prefect of Jinan Qun, and the prime minister of Jiangdu to the right internal history of Jiuqing.
Due to his improper opinions on the dispute between Wu'an Hou Tianfan and Wei Qihou Dou Ying, he was demoted to Zhan Shi and was later transferred to Da Nong Ling.
When Zheng Zhuang was doing the internal history of You, he warned his subordinate officials: If there are visitors, no matter they are noble or lowly, they are not allowed to wait at the door.
He respects the host's hospitality and subordinates himself to the guests with his noble status.
Zheng Zhuang was an upright person and did not purchase any private property. He only relied on his official salary and rewards to provide for his elderly friends. The gifts he gave to others were only a few meals in bamboo utensils.
Whenever he goes to court and has the opportunity to give advice to the emperor, he will be praised by the most respected people in the world.
He recommended scholars and his subordinates, prime ministers and officials, and talked about them with great interest. He often praised them as more capable than himself.
He never addressed the officials by their first names, and when talking to his subordinates, he was so humble as if he was afraid of hurting them.
When I heard that others had good ideas, I recommended them to the emperor for fear of delaying the matter.
Therefore, scholars and well-known elders in the vast area east of Miao Mountain all praised his virtues.
Zheng Zhuang was sent to inspect the breach of the Yellow River, and he asked for five days to prepare his luggage.
The emperor said: I heard that Zheng Zhuang traveled thousands of miles without food. Why did he ask for time to prepare his luggage?
Although Zheng Zhuang was popular with outsiders, he often agreed to obey his master's wishes in court and did not dare to express his views on right and wrong too clearly.
In his later years, the Han Dynasty conquered the Xiongnu and recruited ethnic minorities in various places. The world spent a lot of money and the country's financial and material resources were even more scarce.
The people recommended by Zheng Zhuang and their guests were responsible for transportation for the great peasant order, and they owed a lot of money.
Sima An was appointed as the prefect of Huaiyang County and reported the matter. Zheng Zhuang was held responsible for this. After atonement, he was demoted to a civilian.
Soon, he entered the Prime Minister's Mansion and held the temporary post of chief historian.
The emperor thought that he was old and asked him to be the governor of Runan County.
A few years later, he died in office.
Zheng Zhuang and Ji An were originally ranked among the nine ministers. They were honest in government and had pure conduct at home.
Both of them were dismissed from office during the process, their families were poor, and their guests gradually declined.
When he became a county magistrate, there was no property left in his family after his death.
Because of him, as many as six or seven of Zheng Zhuang's brothers and descendants have reached the rank of two thousand shi.
Tai Shigong said: Because Ji An and Zheng were so virtuous at that time, when they were powerful, the number of guests would be ten times greater, but when they were powerless, the situation was completely the opposite. If they were like this, let alone ordinary people!
Zhai Gong of Xiajun County once said that when he first served as a court official, his house was full of guests; but when he lost his official position, the outside became so deserted that people could gather to catch birds.
summary: Zheng Zhuang, courtesy name Zhuang, was born in Chen County. His ancestor Zheng Jun served under Xiang Ji and refused to address him by his first name, as ordered by Emperor Gaozu, leading to his dismissal. Zheng Zhuang was chivalrous, rescuing Zhang Yu, and gained fame in Liang and Chu. During Emperor Xiao Jing's reign, he served as Prince Sheren, often visiting friends and hosting guests. He loved Taoism, admired elders, and was humble. Under Emperor Wu, he rose to Right Internal History of Jiuqing but was demoted for improper opinions. As Right Internal History, he treated visitors equally, was upright, and had no private property, using his salary to support friends. He recommended scholars, praising them as better than himself, and was praised by elders east of Miao Mountain. Sent to inspect the Yellow River breach, he asked for five days to prepare, but the emperor noted his reputation for traveling without food. In later years, due to debts from recommended guests, he was demoted to civilian, then served as governor of Runan County until death. Zheng Zhuang and Ji An were both honest, dismissed, and poor, with no property after death. Six or seven of Zheng Zhuang's descendants reached two thousand shi. Tai Shigong noted that Ji An and Zheng Zhuang's virtue attracted many guests when powerful, but few when powerless. Zhai Gong of Xiajun County wrote on his gate: "One death and one life show friendship; one poor and one rich show acquaintance; one noble and one humble show friendship." Ji An and Zheng Zhuang suffered this misfortune, which was sad.

translation:
Liu Chang, King Li of Huainan, was the youngest son of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty. His mother was the concubine of Zhang Ao, the former king of Zhao.
In the eighth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Emperor Gao passed by Zhao from Dongyuan County, and King Zhao dedicated King Li's mother to him.
She was favored by the emperor and became pregnant.
From then on, King Zhao Zhang Ao did not dare to let her live in the palace, so he built another palace for her to live in.
The following year, the imperial court discovered that Zhao Xiangguan and others were plotting to kill Emperor Gaozu in Bairen County. King Zhao was also arrested and charged. His mother, brothers and concubines were all arrested and imprisoned in the Hanoi County government.
King Li's mother said to the jailer in prison: I am favored by the emperor and am pregnant.
The jailer reported truthfully that the emperor was angry because of King Zhao's incident and ignored the complaint of King Li's mother.
Zhao Jian, the younger brother of King Li's mother, asked Piyang Hou Shenshi to inform Empress Lu. Queen Lu was jealous and refused to plead with the emperor, so Piyang Hou stopped trying to persuade him.
King Li's mother was resentful after giving birth to Queen Li, so she committed suicide.
The jailer carried King Li to the emperor. The emperor regretted it and ordered Queen Lu to raise him and bury King Li's mother in Zhending County.
Zhending is the hometown of King Li's mother, and her ancestors lived there.
In July of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu, King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled, so the emperor appointed his son Liu Chang as King of Huainan, putting him in charge of the four counties and fiefdoms that were formerly under Yingbu's territory.
The emperor personally led an army to go out and annihilated Yingbu, so King Li took the throne of Huainan.
King Li lost his mother when he was young and grew up dependent on Empress Lu. Therefore, he was able to avoid political disasters during the reign of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu. However, he always resented Marquis Piyang in his heart and did not dare to take action.
When Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, King Huainan considered himself the closest to the emperor. He was arrogant and arrogant, and repeatedly violated laws and disciplines.
The emperor thought of his brother-sister relationship and often tolerated and pardoned his faults.
In the third year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, King Huainan professed his own country and entered the dynasty. His attitude was very arrogant.
He followed the emperor to the imperial garden for hunting, rode in the same car with the emperor, and often called the emperor "big brother".
King Li was talented and brave, and could lift a heavy cauldron with all his strength, so he went to the mansion of Piyang Hou to seek an audience.
When Marquis Piyang came out to see him, he took out an iron mallet from his sleeve and struck Marquis Piyang, and ordered his attendant Wei Jing to cut off Marquis Piyang's head.
Afterwards, King Li galloped to the palace and apologized to the emperor, saying: "My mother should not have been convicted of Zhao's rebellion. At that time, if Marquis Piyang had tried his best to save her, he would have been able to get help from Empress Lu, but he did not try hard. This was the first crime." King Zhao Ruyi and his son were not guilty. Empress Lu deliberately killed them, but Marquis Piyang did not try to dissuade them. This was the second crime. Empress Lu made a relative of the Lu family king, intending to threaten the Liu family, and Marquis Piyang did not stand up to fight. This is the third crime.
I killed the treacherous minister Piyanghou for the people of the world, and avenged my mother. I came to the court to kneel down and plead guilty.
The emperor's desire to pity King Li, and out of brotherly love, did not punish him and pardoned him.
During this period, the Empress Dowager Bo, the Crown Prince, and all the ministers were all afraid of King Li. Therefore, King Li became more arrogant and unruly after returning to the country. He did not act in accordance with the court decrees. He issued orders to warn Qingdao when entering and leaving the palace. He also called the orders he issued "zhi" and made laws by himself, imitating the emperor.
summary: Liu Chang, King Li of Huainan, was the youngest son of Emperor Gaozu of Han. His mother, a concubine of the former King of Zhao, was favored by Emperor Gaozu and became pregnant. After the King of Zhao was implicated in a plot against the emperor, she was imprisoned and, despite being pregnant, her pleas for help were ignored due to the emperor's anger and Empress Lü's jealousy. After giving birth to Liu Chang, she committed suicide. The emperor regretted this and had Empress Lü raise the child. Liu Chang was later made King of Huainan after suppressing a rebellion. Growing up under Empress Lü's protection, Liu Chang escaped political disasters but harbored resentment against Marquis Piyang for not helping his mother. After Emperor Xiaowen ascended, Liu Chang became arrogant, calling the emperor "big brother" and violating laws. He eventually killed Marquis Piyang in revenge, claiming three crimes against him. The emperor pardoned him out of brotherly love, but Liu Chang grew more unruly, imitating imperial decrees and plotting rebellion.

translation:
In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, King Li asked seventy men without official titles to discuss with Chai Qi, the son of Chai Wu, Marquis of Jipu, and planned to use forty large trucks to rebel in Gukou County, and sent envoys to Minyue and Xiongnu to contact various places.
The imperial court found out about this, punished the rebels, and sent envoys to summon King Huainan to the capital. King Huainan came to Chang'an.
Prime Minister Zhang Bao, Dian Kechen Feng Jing, Imperial Censor Shizong Zhengchenyi, Tingwei Chenhe, and the thief Lieutenant Chenfu risked death. They reported: Huainan King Liu Chang abandoned the grammar of the late emperor, disobeyed the emperor's edict, and engaged in non-compliance with the law in daily life. He made his own chariot with a yellow satin umbrella that the emperor rode.
He appointed officials without authorization, appointed his doctor Zhongchun as the prime minister of the country, collected people from various counties and vassal states, as well as fugitives who had committed crimes, hid them in places to live, settled their families, and granted them money, materials, titles, salaries, and houses. Some people were even granted titles to marquises in Guannei, enjoying the favor of two thousand shi. King Huainan wanted to do evil by giving them everything they didn't deserve.
The doctor Dan, together with seventy people including the guilty and disgraced official Kaizhang, conspired with Chai Qi, the son of Chai Wu, the Marquis of Ji Pu, to cause harm to the ancestral temple and the state.
They asked Kai Zhang to secretly report to Liu Chang and discuss sending people to contact Minyue and the Huns to send troops to respond.
Kai Zhang went to Huainan to meet Liu Chang. Liu Chang met and had banquets with him many times, and also helped him get married and marry him, and provided him with a salary of two thousand dan.
Open the chapter and tell people to report to the doctor that everything has been settled with the King of Huainan.
Prime Minister Chun also sent envoys to inform Dan.
After the officials in the DPRK discovered this, they sent Wei Qi and others from Chang'an County to arrest Kai Zhang.
Liu Changzang refused to make friends with the people, and secretly discussed with the former lieutenant Ji, and killed Kaizhang and silenced him.
They bought a coffin, mourning clothes, and blankets, and buried Kai Zhang in Feiling. They deceived the officials handling the case and said they didn't know where Kai Zhang was.
Later, a tomb was forged and a mark was erected on the tomb, saying "Kaizhang's body is buried here."
Liu Chang also personally killed one innocent person; ordered officials to kill six innocent people based on the crime; hid escaped death row prisoners and captured those who did not escape to take the blame for them; he added crimes arbitrarily, leaving the victims with nowhere to redress their grievances, and sentenced 14 people to more than four years of hard labor; he also pardoned the criminals without authorization and exempted 18 people from the death penalty. Fifty-eight people have served four years or less of hard labor; ninety-four people have been given the title of Guannei Marquis or less.
Some time ago, Liu Chang was seriously ill. Your Majesty was worried about him and sent envoys to give him letters and preserved dates.
Liu Chang did not want to accept the gift, so he refused to receive the envoy.
The Nanhai people living in Lujiang County rebelled, and the officers and soldiers of Huainan County were ordered to conquer them.
His Majesty was sympathetic to the poverty of the people in Huainan, and sent an envoy to give Liu Chang five thousand pieces of cloth, ordering them to be forwarded to the hardworking and poor among the officers and soldiers.
Liu Chang did not want to accept it and lied that there were no hard workers in the army.
Wang Zhi, a native of Nanhai, wrote a letter to offer the jade jade to the emperor. He should not burn the letter and refuse to submit it.
Officials in the DPRK requested to summon Ji to discuss the crime, but Liu Chang refused to order, falsely claiming that "Ji was ill."
The Prime Minister of the State Chun asked Liu Chang for permission. Liu Chang was angry and said that you wanted to betray me and join the Han Dynasty, so he sentenced Chun to death.
The ministers and others request your majesty to punish Liu Chang according to law.
summary: In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Liu Chang conspired with seventy men to rebel, contacting Minyue and Xiongnu. The plot was discovered, and he was summoned to Chang'an. Officials reported his numerous crimes, including forging imperial chariots, appointing unauthorized officials, harboring fugitives, and killing innocents. The emperor, unable to bear punishing him, deposed him and exiled him to Shu County. Liu Chang went on a hunger strike and died en route. The emperor later posthumously honored him as King Li and enfeoffed his sons.

translation:
So the King of Hengshan summoned the prince and planned to tie him up and beat him severely.
The prince knew that his father often wanted to depose him and establish his younger brother Liu Xiao, so he said to him: Liu Xiao has committed adultery with his father's favored maid, and Wucai has committed adultery with his slaves. Father, please try your best to have more food. I request to write a letter to the court.
After that, he turned his back to King Hengshan and left.
The King of Hengshan sent people to stop him, but it failed, so he drove himself to hunt down the prince.
The prince talked nonsense, and the King of Hengshan imprisoned him in the palace with shackles.
Liu Xiao became increasingly close and favored by the King of Hengshan.
The King of Hengshan was amazed at Liu Xiao's talents, so he gave him the royal seal, called him a general, let him live in a mansion outside the palace, and gave him a lot of money to attract guests.
The guests who came to seek refuge secretly knew that both the King of Huainan and the King of Hengshan had plans to betray the imperial court, so they welcomed and encouraged the King of Hengshan day and night.
So the King of Hengshan ordered Liu Xiao's guests Jiangdu people to rescue He and Chen happy to make chariots and arrows, and to engrave the emperor's seal and the official seals of the generals and military officials.
The King of Hengshan visited day and night for heroes like Zhou Qiu. He repeatedly praised and gave examples of Wu Chu's strategies during the rebellion, and used them to standardize his own rebellion plans.
The King of Hengshan did not dare to imitate the King of Huainan and hope to usurp the throne of emperor. He was afraid that the King of Huainan would rise up and annex his country. He thought that after the King of Huainan moved westward, he could take advantage of the situation and send troops to pacify and occupy the territory between the Yangtze River and the Huai River. He hoped that he would be able to do so.
In the autumn of the fifth year of Yuan Shuo, King Hengshan was about to go to Beijing to see the emperor. When passing through the Huainan Kingdom, the King of Huainan actually said some words of brotherhood, which eliminated the previous resentment and agreed to jointly create tools for rebellion.
The King of Hengshan wrote a letter saying that he was ill, and the emperor gave him a letter allowing him not to enter the court.
In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, King Hengshan sent people to write to the emperor requesting that the crown prince Liu Shuang be deposed and Liu Xiao be established as the crown prince.
After Liu Shuang heard the news, he sent Bai Ying, who was close to him, to Chang'an to write a letter accusing Liu Xiao of secretly making chariot arrows and committing adultery with the Huainan King's maid, intending to thwart Liu Xiao.
When Bai Ying came to Chang'an, before he could submit a letter, the officials arrested him and imprisoned him because he was involved in the rebellion of the King of Huainan.
When the King of Hengshan heard that Liu Shuang sent Bai Ying to write a letter, he was afraid that he would reveal the secrets of the country, so he wrote a letter accusing the prince Liu Shuang of committing treason and committing treason and should be punished with death. The court handed the matter over to Pei County for trial.
In the winter of the first year of Yuanshou, the minister responsible for handling the case went to Pei County to search for the criminals who had conspired with the King of Huainan. He was not arrested, but Chen happy was captured at the home of Liu Xiao, the son of the King of Hengshan.
Officials accused Liu Xiao of taking the lead in hiding Chen happy.
Liu Xiao thought that Chen Xiping had repeatedly plotted rebellion with the King of Hengshan, and was very afraid that he would confess the matter. He heard that the law stipulated that those who surrendered in advance would be exempted from guilt, and he suspected that the prince had instructed Bai Ying to report the rebellion, so he surrendered first and accused Jiu He, Chen happy and others of participating in the rebellion.
The interrogation by Tingwei confirmed that it was true, and the minister requested the arrest and interrogation of King Hengshan. The emperor said: Do not arrest.
He sent Lieutenant Sima An and General Li Xi to Hengshan Kingdom to interrogate King Hengshan on the spot, and King Hengshan answered truthfully one by one.
The officials surrounded the palace and guarded it closely.
The lieutenant and Daxing returned to the court and reported the situation. The minister requested that Zongzheng, Daxing and Peijun be sent to jointly try the King of Hengshan.
When the King of Hengshan heard the news, he cut his neck and committed suicide.
Liu Xiao was acquitted because he voluntarily surrendered and rebelled; but he was still sentenced to death for committing adultery with the maid of the Prince of Hengshan.
Queen Xu Lai was also guilty of murdering the former Queen Chengshu by falsely accusing her of poison, and Prince Liu Shuang was accused of unfilial piety by the King of Hengshan, so they were all executed and abandoned in the market.
All the criminals who participated in the rebellion of King Hengshan were killed.
Hengshan State was abolished and became Hengshan County.
Tai Shigong said: "The Book of Songs" says: "Fight the Rong and Di, punish the Chu people. This is true!"
Although the King of Huainan and the King of Hengshan were close relatives, owned thousands of miles of territory, and were granted the title of vassal, they did not devote themselves to abide by the duties of vassals to assist the emperor. Instead, they blindly harbored evil plans and plotted rebellion. As a result, father and son were subjugated for the second time in succession. No one was able to enjoy the full life of his life, and was ridiculed by the world.
summary: Liu Chang's son, Liu An, became King of Huainan. He was cultured and sought to win over the people, but he resented his father's death and plotted rebellion. He befriended guests, accumulated weapons, and bribed officials. His daughter, Liu Ling, spied in Chang'an. The king's advisor, Wu Bei, warned against rebellion, citing the failures of Wu and Chu and the stability of the Han dynasty. Despite this, Liu An continued preparations, forging seals and planning to assassinate officials. Liu An's brother, Liu Ci, King of Hengshan, also plotted rebellion. He feuded with his brother and prepared for war, forging documents and building weapons. His internal conflicts, including disputes over succession and adultery, led to his downfall. After his son Liu Xiao surrendered and revealed the plot, Liu Ci committed suicide. His kingdom was also abolished.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传

translation:
The emperor handed the case to the ministers for trial. The case implicated several thousand princes, two thousand stones, and local tycoons who had conspired with the Huainan King. They were all sentenced to death according to the severity of the crime.
Liu Ci, the king of Hengshan, was the younger brother of the king of Huainan. He was found guilty of the same crime and should be arrested. The official responsible for handling the case requested the arrest of the king of Hengshan.
The Emperor said: Each prince and king regards his own feudal state as the foundation of his life and should not involve each other.
You, together with the princes and princes, go to meet with the prime minister to discuss.
After discussion, forty-three people including King Pengzu of Zhao and Cao Xiang, the princes of Lieutenant, all said: King Liu An of Huainan is extremely treasonous and immoral. His crime of rebellion is clear and he should be punished without mercy.
Liu Duan, the king of Jiaoxi, expressed his opinion: Liu An, the king of Huainan, ignored the king's law and did evil things. He was deceitful, disrupted the world, confused the people, betrayed his ancestors, and spread heresy.
"Spring and Autumn" once said that ministers should not lead the people to cause chaos, and they should be killed if they lead the people to cause chaos.
Liu An's crime was more serious than the rebellion, and his rebellion was a foregone conclusion.
I have seen clear evidence of his forged documents, talismans, seals, maps and other treasonous and immoral facts. His crime is extremely treasonous and immoral, and he should be executed according to law.
As for the officials in the Huainan Kingdom with an official rank of more than 200 shi and less than 200 shi, as well as the favored ministers of the clan who have not violated the law, if they cannot fulfill their duties to correct the Huainan King and prevent the rebellion of the King of Huainan, they should be removed from their posts, have their titles reduced, and be demoted to soldiers, and they will not be allowed to serve as officials again in the future.
Those other criminals who are not officials can use two pounds and eighty taels of gold to pay for the death penalty.
The imperial court should publicly expose Liu An's crimes so that everyone in the world will clearly understand the way of being a minister and will not dare to have evil ambitions to betray the emperor.
Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, Tingwei Zhang Tang and others reported everyone's opinions, and the emperor sent Zongzheng holding a talisman to judge the Huainan King.
Before Zongzheng arrived in Huainan, King Liu An of Huainan had committed suicide in advance.
Queen Tu, Prince Liu Qian and all those who collaborated in the rebellion were all killed.
When the emperor of Huainan, Liu An, was dissuaded from rebelling because of Wu, his words were elegant and upright. He said a lot of good things about the government and wanted not to kill him.
Ting Wei Zhang Tang said: Wu Ban was the first to plot a rebellion for the King of Huainan, and his crime cannot be forgiven.
So Wu Bei was killed.
Huainan Kingdom was abolished as Jiujiang County.
The king of Hengshan was named Liu Ci, and Queen Chengshu gave birth to three children. The eldest son Liu Shuang was established as the prince, the second son Liu Xiao, and the third daughter Liu Wucai.
Concubine Xu Lai also gave birth to four children, and concubine Jue Ji gave birth to two children.
The two brothers, the King of Hengshan and the King of Huainan, blamed each other and complained about etiquette. Their relationship was estranged and they were not harmonious.
summary: The plot was exposed when Liu An's grandson, Liu Jian, informed on the prince. The court investigated, and Liu An, fearing exposure, hesitated to act. His advisor Wu Bei again urged caution, but Liu An persisted. Eventually, the court arrested the conspirators, and Liu An committed suicide before his arrest. His queen and prince were executed, and Huainan was reduced to a commandery. Sima Qian comments that despite their noble status, the kings of Huainan and Hengshan failed in their duties and plotted rebellion, leading to their ruin. Their faults were compounded by the influence of unruly subordinates and local customs.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/淮南衡山列传

translation:
Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, was from Huaiyin.
When he was a commoner, he was poor, had no good character, could not be elected to be an official, and could not make a living by doing business. He often lived in other people's homes and had nothing to do, so most people hated him.
I went to the countryside many times to have a casual meal at the pavilion in Nanchang. For several months, the pavilion chief's wife was worried about Han Xin, so she made breakfast in advance and took it to the bed in the inner room to eat.
When it was time to eat, Han Xin went, but no food was prepared for him.
Han Xin also understood their intentions. In a rage, he actually left and never came back.
Han Xin was fishing under the city, and there were several old ladies rinsing the silk cotton. One of them saw that Han Xin was hungry, so she gave Han Xin food to eat. This continues for dozens of days until rinsing is complete.
Han Xin was very happy and said to the aunt: I will repay you heavily in the future.
The aunt said angrily: "A man can't support himself. I give you food out of pity for you, the young master. Do I hope you will repay me?"
A young man among the Huaiyin butchers insulted Han Xin and said: Although you are tall and like to carry a sword, you are actually a coward.
He insulted him in public and said: If you are not afraid of death, stab me with a sword; if you are afraid of death, crawl under my crotch.
So Han Xin looked at him carefully, lowered himself to the ground, and crawled under his crotch.
People all over the street laughed at Han Xin and thought he was timid.
When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huaihe River, Han Xin followed him with a sword, but he had no reputation among Xiang Liang's men.
Xiang Liang was defeated, and Han Xin was subordinated to Xiang Yu, who made him a doctor.
He repeatedly offered suggestions to Xiang Yu in order to be reused, but Xiang Yu did not adopt them.
Liu Bang, the king of Han, entered Shu, and Han Xin left the Chu army and submitted to the king of Han. Because he had no reputation, he only served as a minor official receiving guests.
Later, he was sentenced to beheading for breaking the law, and all thirteen people who were accomplices in the crime were killed. When it was Han Xin's turn, he looked up and happened to see Teng Gong and said: Doesn't the King of Han want to achieve the feat of unifying the world?
Why do you want to kill the strong man?
Teng Gong felt that his words were extraordinary and saw that he was handsome, so he let him go.
Talked with Han Xin, admired him very much, and reported the matter to the King of Han, who appointed Han Xin as the Commander-in-Chief of Su Su. But the king of Han did not see that he had any special talents.
Han Xin talked to Xiao He many times, and Xiao He thought he was a genius.
When they arrived at Nanzheng, dozens of generals from all walks of life fled on the way.
Han Xin speculated that Xiao He and others had recommended him to the King of Han many times, but the King of Han did not use him and ran away.
Xiao He heard that Han Xin had escaped and had no time to report to the King of Han, so he chased him personally.
Someone reported to the King of Han that: Prime Minister Xiao He has escaped.
The king of Han was furious because losing Xiao He was like losing his right and left hands.
A day or two later, Xiao He came to see the King of Han. The King of Han was both angry and happy. He scolded Xiao He and said: Why did you run away?
Xiao He said: I don't dare to run away, I will chase the escaping person.
summary: Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, was a native of Huaiyin. In his youth, he was poor, lacked good character, and could not secure an official position or make a living through business. He often relied on others for meals, which made him disliked. He frequently ate at a pavilion in Nanchang, but the pavilion chief's wife, annoyed by his presence, began eating breakfast early in the inner room. When Han Xin arrived, no food was prepared for him. Angered, he left and never returned. While fishing under the city, an old woman rinsing silk cotton pitied his hunger and fed him for dozens of days. Han Xin promised to repay her heavily, but she rebuked him, saying she did not expect repayment. A young butcher insulted Han Xin, calling him a coward and challenging him to either stab him or crawl under his crotch. Han Xin chose to crawl, and the crowd mocked him for his timidity. When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huai River, Han Xin followed but gained no reputation. After Xiang Liang's defeat, he served under Xiang Yu as a doctor, offering suggestions that were ignored. He then joined Liu Bang, the King of Han, but was only made a minor official. Sentenced to death for breaking the law, he caught the attention of Teng Gong, who spared him after a bold speech. Teng Gong recommended him to Liu Bang, who appointed him as a commander, though without recognizing his talents. Han Xin frequently conversed with Xiao He, who considered him a genius. When Han Xin fled due to lack of recognition, Xiao He chased him personally. Liu Bang initially suspected Xiao He of desertion but learned he was pursuing Han Xin. Xiao He argued that Han Xin was unparalleled and essential for Liu Bang's ambitions to conquer the world. Liu Bang agreed to make Han Xin a general, and after a formal ceremony, Han Xin was appointed.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传

translation:
When the princes saw that King Xiang had moved Emperor Yi to a remote place in the south of the Yangtze River, they all went back and expelled their own kings, occupied good places and made themselves kings.
Every place King Xiang's army passed through was devastated and destroyed. Most of the people in the world were resentful. The common people were unwilling to surrender, but they were forced to obey by force.
Although he was the hegemon in name, he actually lost the support of the people in the world.
Therefore, his advantages can easily be turned into disadvantages.
Now the king can really do the opposite: appointing the brave and capable talents in the world, what can't be punished?
If all the cities in the world are given to meritorious ministers, who wouldn't be convinced?
As a righteous teacher, obeying the soldiers' wish to return eastward, what kind of enemy cannot be defeated?
Moreover, the three kings that Xiang Yu enfeoffed were all generals of the Qin Dynasty. They led the children of Qin to fight for several years, and many of them were killed and escaped. They also deceived their subordinates to surrender to the princes.
Upon arriving at Xin'an, King Xiang cunningly buried alive more than 200,000 Qin troops who had surrendered. Only Zhang Han, Sima Xin, and Dong Yi survived. The fathers and brothers of Qin hated these three men to their bones.
Now, relying on his power, Xiang Yu forcibly made these three kings, and no one in Qin loved them.
When the king entered Wuguan, Qiu did not commit any crime. He abolished the harsh laws of the Qin Dynasty and made a three-part agreement with the people of Qin. All the people of Qin did not want the king to be king in Qin.
According to the agreement made by the princes, the king should be the king in Guanzhong. The people in Guanzhong all know this. The king lost the title he deserved and entered Hanzhong. The people of Qin all regretted it.
Now that the king has mobilized his army to advance eastward, the Sanqin fiefdom can be pacified with just one document.
So the King of Han was very happy, thinking that it was too late to get Han Xin.
Just follow Han Xin's plan and deploy various generals to attack targets.
In August, the King of Han sent troops to advance eastward through Chencang and pacified the Three Qin Dynasties.
In the second year of the Han Dynasty, troops went out of Hangu Pass and subdued the king of Wei and the king of Henan. The king of Han and Yin also surrendered one after another.
The king of Han then joined forces with the king of Qi and the king of Zhao to attack the Chu army.
In April, when they arrived at Pengcheng, the Han army was defeated and returned in disarray.
Han Xin gathered the scattered troops and met the King of Han in Xingyang, and defeated the Chu army between Jingxian and Suoting. Therefore, the Chu army was never able to advance westward.
After the Han army was defeated in Pengcheng, King Sima Xin of Sai and King Dong Yi of Zhai rebelled against Han and surrendered to Chu. Qi and Zhao also rebelled against Han and reconciled with Chu.
In June, King Bao of Wei asked for leave to return to his hometown on the pretext of visiting his mother's illness. As soon as he arrived in the feudal state, he immediately cut off the main transportation road at Linjin Pass at the Yellow River ferry, rebelled against the king of Han, and made peace with the Chu army.
The king of Han sent Li Sheng to lobby Wei Bao, but failed.
In August of this year, the King of Han appointed Han Xin as Prime Minister Zuo to attack King Bao of Wei.
summary: Han Xin analyzed Xiang Yu's weaknesses, such as his inability to delegate, his reluctance to reward subordinates, and his harsh rule, which alienated the people. He advised Liu Bang to adopt the opposite approach, emphasizing the loyalty of the Qin people due to Liu Bang's merciful policies. Liu Bang followed Han Xin's plan, and in August, they advanced eastward through Chencang, pacifying the Three Qin regions. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, they subdued the kings of Wei and Henan. However, in April, the Han army was defeated at Pengcheng. Han Xin regrouped and met Liu Bang at Xingyang, defeating the Chu army. Later, King Bao of Wei rebelled, and Han Xin captured him, pacifying Wei. He then attacked Zhao with Zhang Er, defeating a 200,000-strong Zhao army at Jingxing by using a river-backed formation and a surprise cavalry attack. Han Xin spared Li Zuoche, who advised him to subdue Yan and Qi through diplomacy rather than force. Han Xin followed this advice, and Yan surrendered.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传

translation:
It is better to have a deep trench and a high base, unable to hold on. Let the King of Qi send his trusted ministers to pacify the cities that have fallen. If the officials and people of these cities know that their king is still there and the Chu army comes to rescue them, they will definitely rebel against the Han army.
The Han army lives two thousand miles away, and the people in Qi's cities and towns rise up to rebel against them. They will inevitably lose food, which will force them to surrender without a fight.
Long Qie said: I have always understood Han Xin's character and it is easy to deal with him.
Moreover, I rescued Qi and made Han Xin surrender without a fight. What credit do I have for that?
Now that I have defeated him, half of Qi's land can be entrusted to me. Why not fight?
So he decided to start a war and set up a battle array with Han Xin across the Weishui River.
Han Xin ordered more than 10,000 bags to be made overnight, filled with sand and soil, blocked the upper reaches of the Weishui River, led half of the army across the river, attacked Long Qie, pretended to be defeated, and ran back.
Long Qie said happily: "I have known that Han Xin is timid."
So he crossed the Weishui River to pursue Han Xin.
Han Xin ordered the sandbags blocking the Weishui River to be excavated. The river surged forward, and more than half of Long Qie's army had not yet crossed the river. Han Xin immediately returned to the army and counterattacked fiercely, killing Long Qie.
Long Qie's troops on the east bank of the Weishui River that had not yet crossed the river scattered and fled. King Tian Guang of Qi also fled.
Han Xin pursued the defeated troops as far as Chengyang and captured all the Chu soldiers.
In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, Han Xin surrendered and pacified the entire Qi State.
He sent someone to write to the King of Han, saying: Qi is cunning and capricious, and its southern border borders Chu. If a temporary acting king is not set up to pacify it, the situation will not be stable.
In order to facilitate the current situation, I hope that I will be allowed to temporarily act as King Qi.
At this time, the Chu army was tightly besieging the King of Han in Xingyang. Han Xin's envoy arrived. The King of Han opened the letter and read it. He became furious and cursed: I am besieged here and I am waiting for you to help me day and night, but you want to make yourself king!
Zhang Liang and Chen Ping secretly stepped on the King of Han's feet, leaned into the King of Han's ear and said: "The Han army is currently in a disadvantageous situation. How can we prevent Han Xin from becoming king?"
It is better to take the opportunity to make him king, treat him well, and let him guard Qi by himself.
Otherwise, an accident may occur.
The King of Han woke up and deliberately cursed again: Since a man has conquered the feudal lords, he must be the real king. Why should he be a temporary acting king?
He sent Zhang Liang to appoint Han Xin as King of Qi and mobilized his army to attack the Chu army.
After the Chu army lost Long Qi, King Xiang was frightened and sent Wu She from Xuyi to persuade King Han Xin of Qi, saying: "The people of the world have suffered from Qin's tyranny for a long time, so we all work together to attack it."
After the collapse of the Qin Dynasty, the land was divided according to merit, and each became a king in order to stop the war.
Now the King of Han is marching east again, invading other people's realms and plundering other people's fiefdoms. He has broken through the Three Qin Dynasties, led his army out of Hangu Pass, gathered the armies of various princes, and marched eastward to attack Chu State. His intention is not to stop until he annexes the entire world. He is too greedy to go so far.
Moreover, the King of Han could not be trusted. He had fallen into King Xiang's hands many times. It was King Xiang's mercy that allowed him to survive. However, once he escaped, he broke his alliance and attacked King Xiang again. He was so unapproachable and untrustworthy.
Now, even if you think you have a deep friendship with the King of Han and fight for him with all your strength, you will still be captured by him in the end.
The reason why you can continue to this day is because King Xiang still exists.
At present, the victory or defeat of Liu and Xiang's battle for the world is yours.
If you stand to the right, then King Han wins; if you stand to the left, then King Xiang wins.
If King Xiang is eliminated today, you will be eliminated next.
You have an old friendship with King Xiang. Why don't you rebel against Han and unite with Chu, divide the world into three parts, and make yourself king?
Now, if we let this opportunity go, we will inevitably side with the King of Han and attack King Xiang. Should a smart and wise man do this?
Han Xin declined and said: "I serve King Xiang, but my official position is no more than a doctor, and my position is just that of a guard holding a halberd. I don't listen to his words, and I don't use his plans, so I carry the Chu State and return to the Han Dynasty."
The King of Han granted me the title of general, gave me tens of thousands of horses, took off his clothes for me to wear, gave me good food to eat, and listened to his words, so I can be where I am today.
summary: Han Xin requested that Zhang Er be made King of Zhao, which Liu Bang approved. The Chu army besieged Liu Bang at Xingyang, but he escaped and seized Han Xin's troops. Han Xin was ordered to attack Qi, and despite Liu Bang's envoy Li Shiqi persuading Qi to surrender, Han Xin, urged by Kuai Tong, attacked and conquered Qi. Chu sent Long Qie to aid Qi, but Han Xin defeated him by damming the Wei River and then releasing the water, killing Long Qie. Han Xin then requested to be made acting King of Qi. Liu Bang, initially furious, was persuaded by Zhang Liang and Chen Ping to grant the title to secure Han Xin's loyalty. Kuai Tong later advised Han Xin to rebel and divide the world into three parts, but Han Xin refused, citing Liu Bang's generosity. Despite Kuai Tong's warnings about the dangers of his position, Han Xin hesitated and ultimately remained loyal.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传

translation:
I have something on my mind that I want to talk to you about. Chen Xi said: Everything is at the command of the general!
The Marquis of Huaiyin said: The area under your jurisdiction is where the best soldiers from all over the world gather; and you are His Majesty's trusted and favored minister.
If someone reports that you are rebelling, Your Majesty will not believe it; if someone reports you again, Your Majesty will become suspicious; if someone reports you three times, Your Majesty will be furious and personally lead his troops to encircle and suppress you.
If I work as an internal agent in the capital for you, the world can get it.
Chen Xi has always known Han Xin's talents and strategies. I am convinced and say: I will definitely follow your advice!
In the tenth year of the Han Dynasty, Chen Xi rebelled.
The emperor personally led his troops there, but Han Tuo was ill and had no followers.
Secretly sent someone to Chen Xi and said: Just raise troops, I am here to assist you.
Han Xin discussed with his retainers and falsely issued an edict at night to pardon the criminals and slaves serving in various government offices, intending to mobilize them to attack Empress Lu and the prince.
The deployment is completed and we are waiting for news from Chen Xi.
One of his retainers offended Han Xin, who imprisoned him and planned to kill him.
His younger brother wrote a letter of rebellion and reported to Empress Lu that Han Xin was preparing to rebel.
Empress Lu planned to summon Han Xin, but was afraid that he would not submit, so she conspired with Xiao Xiangguo to pretend that Chen Xi was coming from the emperor, saying that Chen Xi had been captured and executed, and all the princes and ministers came to congratulate him.
Xiao Xiangguo deceived Han Xin and said: Even if he is ill, he must work hard to go to the palace to congratulate him.
When Han Xin entered the palace, Empress Lu ordered the warriors to tie Han Xin up and kill him in the bell chamber of Changle Palace.
When Han Xin was about to be executed, he said: I regret that I did not adopt Kuai Tong's plan and was deceived by women and boys. Isn't it God's will?
So he killed the three Han and Xin tribes.
Emperor Gaozu returned to the capital from the army that suppressed Chen Xi's rebellion. When he saw that Han Xin was dead, he was happy and pitied him, and asked: What did Han Xin say before he died?
Queen Lu said: Han Xin said he regretted not adopting Kuai Tong's plan.
Emperor Gaozu said: That man is a lobbyist of Qi State.
He ordered Qi to capture Kuai Tong.
Kuai Tong was brought, and the emperor said: "Did you instigate the Marquis of Huaiyin to rebel?"
Answer: Yes. I did teach him that the boy would perish by not following my plan.
If that kid adopts my plan, how can Your Majesty destroy him?
The emperor said angrily: "Cook him."
Kuai Tong said: Oh, boil me to death, it is unfair!
The emperor said: You instigated Han Xin to rebel. What injustice is there?
Kuai Tong said: When the laws of the Qin Dynasty were corrupted and the political power collapsed, the six kingdoms of Shandong were in chaos. The princes from all walks of life revolted one after another. For a time, the heroes of the world gathered like crows.
The Qin Dynasty lost its throne, and all the heroes in the world came to snatch it, so those with high intelligence and quick actions were the first to get it.
Zhi's dog barked at Yao. Yao was not unkind, just because he was not the owner of the dog.
At this time, I only knew that there was Han Xin, but not His Majesty.
Moreover, there are too many people in the world who are sharpening their weapons and holding sharp knives in their hands who want to do what Your Majesty is doing, but they are just not up to the task.
How can you cook them all to death? Emperor Gaozu said: Let him go.
Kuai Tong's sins were forgiven.
Tai Shigong said: When I went to Huaiyin, the Huaiyin people told me that even when Han Xin was a commoner, his ambition was different.
summary: After Xiang Yu's defeat, Liu Bang demoted Han Xin to King of Chu and later, fearing his influence, arrested him during a visit to Yunmeng. Han Xin was pardoned but reduced to Marquis of Huaiyin. He grew resentful and avoided court. When Chen Xi rebelled, Han Xin conspired with him but was betrayed by a retainer. Empress Lu and Xiao He tricked Han Xin into the palace, where he was executed. Before his death, he regretted not following Kuai Tong's advice. Kuai Tong was captured but spared after arguing that he only served his master. The historian comments that Han Xin's early ambition was evident, but his failure to remain humble and his eventual rebellion led to his downfall.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/淮阴侯列传

translation:
Han Feizi said: Confucian scholars quoted ancient texts to disturb the rule of law, while chivalrous men violated laws by using force.
Han Fei ridiculed both types of people, but Confucian scholars were mostly praised by the world.
As for using power to obtain the position of prime minister, minister, and official, assisting the contemporary emperor, and his achievements are recorded in history books, there is nothing to say about this.
As for Ji Ci and Yuan Xian, they were ordinary people who studied hard, cherished the unique virtues of gentlemen, adhered to morality, and did not go along with the contemporary secular world. Contemporary people also laughed at them.
Therefore, Ji Ci and Yuan Xian lived in empty thatched houses all their lives, wearing coarse clothes and not even having enough to eat.
They have been dead for more than four hundred years, but their disciples from generation to generation miss them tirelessly.
Although the current rangers' actions do not conform to the standards of morality and law, they must keep their word and be resolute in their actions. They must fulfill what they have promised to show their honesty and are willing to sacrifice their lives to save others in danger. He has gone through the test of life and death, but he does not boast of his abilities and is ashamed to show off his merits. This is probably something worthy of praise!
Besides, critical things happen to people from time to time.
Tai Shigong said: In the past, Yu Shun encountered dangers when digging wells and building houses, Yi Yin once carried Ding Chu as a cook, Fu Yue once hid in Fu Yan and did hard labor, Lu Shang once suffered hardship in Jijin, Guan Zhong once wore shackles and handcuffs, Baili Xi once fed cattle as a slave, Confucius once was besieged in Kuangdi, and suffered starvation in Chen and Kui.
These people are all virtuous and benevolent people praised by Confucian scholars, but they have encountered such disasters, let alone ordinary people with moderate talents who have encountered troubled times?
How can we finish talking about the disasters they encountered?
Secular people have this saying: Why bother distinguishing between benevolence and righteousness? Those who have benefited are virtuous.
Therefore, Boyi thought it was shameful to eat Zhou millet and starved to death in Shouyang Mountain; but King Wen and King Wu did not harm the reputation of the kings. Pirates Zhi and Zhuang Qi were cruel and brutal, but their followers praised them for their boundless morality.
It can be seen from this that those who steal clothes and belt hooks will be beheaded, while those who steal state power are made marquises. People who are made marquises have benevolence and righteousness. These words are not false or untrue.
Nowadays, those who stick to one-sided views, some clinging to narrow principles, and have been isolated from the world for a long time, how can they compare with those who adapt to the world with low views and follow the ups and downs of the world to gain glory and fame?
As for ordinary people, they value the virtue of taking and giving in accordance with morality and fulfilling their promises. They follow morality thousands of miles away and die for morality regardless of worldly criticism. This is also their strength and cannot be done casually.
Therefore, when scholars are in poverty and embarrassment, they can devote themselves to learning and face their fate. Isn't this what people call the wise and heroic people?
If we compare the power, talent, and contribution of folk knight-errants to Ji Ji and Yuan Xian, they cannot be the same.
In short, from the perspective of the appearance of things and the fact that one must keep one's word, how can the knight's just behavior be missing?
I have never heard of civilian chivalrous people in ancient times.
summary: Han Feizi's critique of Confucian scholars and chivalrous men for undermining law and order, contrasting them with figures like Ji Ci and Yuan Xian, who lived in poverty but were remembered for their virtues. It praises rangers for their integrity, willingness to sacrifice for others, and modesty, despite their actions not always aligning with moral and legal standards. The text cites historical figures like Yu Shun, Yi Yin, and Confucius who faced hardships, emphasizing that even virtuous individuals encounter disasters. It critiques societal hypocrisy, where minor thieves are punished while those who seize power are honored, and notes that true chivalry involves keeping promises and aiding others without boasting.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/游侠列传

translation:
In modern times, people such as Yanling Jizi, Mengchang Lord, Chunshen Lord, Pingyuan Lord, and Xinling Lord were all relatives of the kings. They relied on the wealth of their feudal states and ministers to recruit talents from all over the world, and they became famous among the vassal states. It cannot be said that they were not talents.
This is like shouting against the wind. The sound is not louder, but the listener feels clearly that this is due to the strong wind.
As for the commoner knight in Luxiang, he has cultivated his moral character and honed his reputation, and his reputation has spread all over the world. No one will not praise his virtue, which is difficult to do.
However, both Confucianism and Mohism rejected them and did not record them in their documents.
Since the Qin Dynasty, the deeds of civilian knights have been buried and cannot be seen. I am very sorry.
According to what I heard, since the founding of the Han Dynasty, there have been people such as Zhu Jia, Tian Zhong, Wang Gong, Ju Meng, and Guo Xie. Although they often violated the laws and prohibitions of the dynasty, their personal behavior was moral, honest and modest, and they were commendable.
Their reputation was not falsely established, and scholars did not echo them without basis.
As for those powerful people who form gangs, collude with each other, rely on their wealth to enslave the poor, use their power and violence to bully the lonely and weak, indulge their desires and satisfy themselves for their own pleasure, this is also considered shameful by the knight-errants.
I feel sad that secular people cannot understand the true meaning of this, but mistakenly regard the Zhu family, Guo Xie and others as the same kind as the violent and powerful people and ridicule them together.
The Zhu family of Lu State and Gaozu were of the same era.
The people of Lu were educated with Confucianism, but the Zhu family was famous for being a knight.
He has hid and rescued hundreds of heroes, and countless ordinary people he has saved.
But he never boasted of his talents or was complacent about his kindness. Those to whom he had given favors were afraid of seeing them again.
He helped others in need, starting with the poor and lowly.
There was no money left in his family, his clothes were torn and incomplete, he didn't have more than two kinds of meat dishes for each meal, and his ride was just an ox-drawn cart.
He was more interested in rescuing others in distress than doing anything private for himself.
He once secretly saved General Ji Bu from the misfortune of being killed. However, after General Ji Bu became honored, he refused to see him again for the rest of his life.
From Hangu Pass to the east, people craned their necks hoping to make friends with him.
Tian Zhong of Chu was famous for being a knight. He liked swordsmanship and served the Zhu family like his father. He thought that his conduct could not keep up with the Zhu family.
After Tian Zhong's death, a drama Meng appeared in Luoyang.
The people of Luoyang made a living by doing business, and Ju Meng became famous among the princes because of his chivalry.
When the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, Zhou Yafu, the marquis of Tiao, was a Taiwei. He rushed to Luoyang in a post car, found Ju Meng, and said happily: The seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu launched a rebellion without asking Ju Meng for help. I know they have done nothing.
The world is in turmoil, and the Taiwei getting him is like getting an equal country.
Ju Meng's behavior is roughly similar to that of the Zhu family, but he likes to play chess. Most of what he does is a teenager's game.
summary: The narrative then focuses on civilian knights from the Han Dynasty, such as Zhu Jia, Tian Zhong, Ju Meng, and Guo Xie. Zhu Jia, a knight from Lu, hid and rescued hundreds without boasting, living frugally. Tian Zhong served Zhu Jia like a father. Ju Meng, from Luoyang, was sought after by Zhou Yafu during the Wu-Chu rebellion, and his mother's funeral drew thousands. Guo Xie, initially cruel, later reformed, repaying hatred with kindness and saving lives without boasting. He mediated disputes, avoided taking credit, and maintained humility, earning widespread respect. However, his past crimes and a murder by his disciples led to his execution under Emperor Wu, with Gongsun Hong arguing his influence made him more dangerous than if he had committed the murders himself. The text concludes by noting that later knights were often arrogant, except for a few like Fan Zhongzi, and laments that Guo Xie's reputation outshone his unremarkable appearance and speech.

translation:
Confucius said: The Six Classics have the same role in governing the country.
"Li" is used to regulate people's words and deeds, "Music" is used to promote people's harmony, "Book" is used to record past deeds and regulations, "Poetry" is used to express emotions, "Yi" is used to spy on the magical changes of heaven and earth, and "Spring and Autumn" is used to understand the meaning of subtle words and weigh the right and wrong.
Tai Shigong said: The truth in the world is vast and boundless, isn't it great!
If the words can be slightly to the point, it can also resolve a lot of troubles.
Chunyu Kun was a son-in-law of Qi State.
Less than seven feet tall, he is funny and eloquent. He has been on many missions to the princes and has never been humiliated.
When King Wei of Qi was in power, he liked to talk in argot, feast all night long, indulge in excessive drinking, ignored state affairs, and entrusted political affairs to the officials.
The civil and military officials are dissolute and indulgent, and the princes and countries invade and invade. The country is in danger and is in danger in a matter of seconds. None of the ministers around King Qi dared to give advice.
Chunyu Kun used argot to admonish and admonish King Wei of Qi, saying: There is a big bird in the capital that landed in the king's courtyard. It has not flown or screamed for three years. Does the king know what happened to this bird?
King Wei of Qi said: If this bird does not fly, it will go straight to the sky; if it does not scream, it will amaze people.
So he ordered all the chiefs of the seventy-two counties in the country to come to the court to report. They rewarded one person and killed another. They also sent troops to defend against the enemy. The princes and states were shocked and returned the occupied land to Qi.
Qi's prestige lasted for thirty-six years.
All these things are recorded in "Tian Wan Family".
In the eighth year of King Wei of Qi's reign, the State of Chu sent a large army to invade its borders.
The King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun as an envoy to the State of Zhao to request reinforcements, and asked him to carry a gift of a hundred catties of gold and ten four-horse carriages.
Chunyu Kun looked up to the sky and laughed so hard that the string holding his hat broke.
King Wei said: Sir, do you think the gift is too little?
Chunyu Kun said: How dare you think too little!
King Wei said: Then you laugh, do you have any excuse?
Chunyu Kun said: Today I came from the east and saw a man worshiping the God of the Fields by the roadside. He held a pig's trotter and a glass of wine and prayed: "The grain harvested in the highlands fills the bonnet, and the crops harvested in the low fields fill the vehicles; the grains are lush and ripe, and the rice grains are piled up in the warehouse."
I saw that he brought few sacrifices and prayed for many things, so I laughed at him.
So King Wei of Qi increased the gifts to a thousand pieces of gold, ten pairs of white jade stones, and a hundred four-horse carriages.
Chunyu Kun said goodbye and set off for the Kingdom of Zhao.
King Zhao allocated him 100,000 elite soldiers and 1,000 leather-wrapped chariots.
When the Chu State heard the news, they withdrew their troops overnight.
King Qi Wei was very happy. He set up wine and food in the harem, summoned Chunyu Kun and gave him wine to drink.
Ask him: How much wine can you drink before you get drunk?
summary: Confucius stated that the Six Classics serve the same purpose in governing a country: "Li" regulates conduct, "Music" promotes harmony, "Book" records past deeds, "Poetry" expresses emotions, "Yi" explores cosmic changes, and "Spring and Autumn" discerns subtle meanings and right from wrong. Tai Shigong remarked on the vastness of truth, noting that concise words can resolve many troubles. Chunyu Kun, a short, witty son-in-law of Qi, often served as an envoy without disgrace. During King Wei of Qi's reign, the king neglected state affairs, indulging in feasting and drinking, leading to invasions and national peril. No minister dared to advise. Chunyu Kun used an allegory of a great bird that neither flew nor cried for three years. King Wei understood, summoned all county chiefs, rewarded one, executed another, and repelled invaders, restoring Qi's prestige for 36 years. Later, when Chu invaded, Chunyu Kun was sent to Zhao for reinforcements with modest gifts. He laughed at a farmer praying for abundant harvests with meager offerings, prompting King Wei to increase the gifts. Zhao then sent 100,000 elite troops, causing Chu to withdraw. King Wei asked Chunyu Kun about his drinking capacity. Chunyu Kun explained that his drunkenness varied by context: fear made him drunk after one measure, while joy allowed him to drink eight measures. He warned against excess, as it leads to decline. King Wei ceased nightly drinking and appointed Chunyu Kun as a guest official.
