translation:
King Zhuang asked: What should we do?
You Meng replied: I requested that the coffin be made of beautiful jade with carved patterns, the cover of fine catalpa wood, and the coffin blocks made of valuable woods such as urin, maple, hemp, and camphor. I sent soldiers to dig a grave for it, and asked the elderly and children to carry earth to build the tomb.
When the princes heard this, they all knew that the king despised people and valued horses.
King Zhuang said: "Has my fault reached this level?"
What to do about it?
Umeng said: Please allow me to bury it in the same way as an animal: pile an earth stove on the ground as a set, use a large copper pot as a coffin, use ginger and dates to season, use spices to relieve the smell, use rice as a sacrifice, use fire as clothes, and bury it in the human belly.
So King Zhuang sent someone to give the horse to the eunuch in charge of the palace's meals, so that the people in the world would not spread the matter for a long time.
Sun Shuao, the prime minister of Chu, knew that Youmeng was a wise man and treated him well.
When Sun Shuao was seriously ill and about to die, he told his son: After I die, you will definitely be poor.
At that time, you go to see Youmeng and say that I am Sun Shuao's son.
A few years later, Sun Shuao's son was indeed so poor that he had to rely on firewood to survive. Once I met Youmeng on the road, he said to Youmeng: I am Sun Shuao's son.
Before my father died, he asked me to go see Youmeng when I was in poverty.
Youmeng said: Don't go far away.
So, he immediately sewed clothes and hats similar to Sun Shuao's and wore them, imitating Sun Shuao's speech, behavior, voice and smile.
After more than a year, he imitated Sun Shuao so much that even the officials around King Zhuang of Chu could not tell him apart.
King Zhuang of Chu held a banquet, and Youmeng came forward to toast and bless King Zhuang. King Zhuang was shocked, thinking that Sun Shuao had come back to life again, and wanted to make him Prime Minister of Chu.
Youmeng said: "Please allow me to go back and discuss this matter with my wife, and come back in three days to take up the post of Prime Minister of Chu."
King Zhuang agreed to him.
Three days later, Youmeng came to see King Zhuang again.
King Zhuang asked: What did your wife say?
Youmeng said: My wife told me not to do it. It is not worthy to be the prime minister of Chu State.
Like Sun Shuao, who was the prime minister of the Chu State and governed the Chu State with loyalty and integrity, the king of Chu was able to dominate.
Now that he is dead, his son has no place to stand and is so poor that he has to carry firewood to make a living every day.
If you want to be the prime minister of Chu like Sun Shuao, you might as well commit suicide.
Umeng then sang: Living in the mountains and fields, it is difficult to live in the fields and suffer hardships.
Those who go out to serve as officials, are themselves corrupt and despicable, accumulate excess wealth, and have no regard for their integrity.
After his death, although his family was wealthy, he was afraid of corruption, bending the law, doing illegal things, and committing serious crimes. He was killed and his family was also destroyed.
What can a corrupt official do?
I want to be an upright official, abide by the law, be loyal to my duties, and never dare to do anything illegal until my death.
Alas, what can an upright official do?
For example, Sun Shuao, Prime Minister of Chu, insisted on integrity throughout his life, but now his wife, children and children are so poor that they have to collect firewood for a living.
It’s really not worth being an upright official! So King Zhuang expressed his apology to You Meng, and immediately summoned Sun Shuao's son and granted him the city of Qiuqiu with 400 households for the purpose of worshiping Sun Shuao.
summary: Over a century later, You Meng, a tall Chu performer, used humor to advise King Zhuang. When the king wanted to bury his beloved horse with grand rites, You Meng suggested an even grander burial to expose the king's folly. King Zhuang relented and had the horse cooked. Later, You Meng impersonated the deceased prime minister Sun Shuao to advise King Zhuang. He highlighted Sun Shuao's poverty despite his integrity, leading the king to grant Sun's son land and households for ancestral worship.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传

translation:
Since then, there has been no interruption for ten generations.
It can be said that Youmeng's intelligence was just right and he seized the opportunity to display it.
More than two hundred years after You Meng, Qin State gave birth to You Zhan.
Youzhan is a singing and dancing artist from the Qin State. He is very short.
He is good at telling jokes, but they all make sense. During the reign of Qin Shihuang, a banquet was held in the palace. It was raining, and the guards standing guard under the palace steps were all wet with rain and cold.
When Youzhan saw them, he felt very sorry for them and said to them: "Do you want to rest?"
The guards all said: Very much so.
Youzhan said: If I call you, you must answer me quickly.
After a while, people in the palace toasted Qin Shihuang and shouted long live the emperor.
Youzhan approached the railing and shouted loudly: Guard!
The guard replied: Yes.
Youzhan said: Although you are tall, what good is it?
I was lucky enough to stand in the open air and get soaked in the rain. Although I am short, I am lucky enough to rest here.
Therefore, Qin Shihuang allowed the guards to reduce their duty by half and take over in turns.
Qin Shihuang once planned to expand the hunting area to Hangu Pass in the east and Yong County and Chencang in the west.
Youzhan said: OK.
Keep more animals inside. If the enemy invades from the east, it will be enough to let the elk use their horns to resist them.
After hearing this, Qin Shihuang stopped his plan to expand the hunting grounds.
Emperor Qin II came to the throne and wanted to paint the city walls with paint.
Youzhan said: OK.
Even if your Majesty did not say it, I would have asked you to do so.
Although the lacquered city wall brings sorrow and expense to the people, it is beautiful!
The walls were painted so slippery that enemies could not climb up even if they came.
To accomplish this, it is easy to paint, but what is difficult is to find a big house, put the painted city wall in it, and let it dry in the shade.
The second emperor laughed and canceled the plan.
Soon, the second emperor was killed, Youzhan surrendered to the Han Dynasty, and died a few years later.
Tai Shigong said: Chunyu Kun looked up to the sky and laughed, and King Wei of Qi followed his example throughout the world.
You Meng shook his head and sang, and those who carried firewood for a living were rewarded.
Youzhan leaned on the railing and shouted, so the guards holding shields under the palace steps were able to reduce their duty by half and take turns to rest.
Aren’t these all great and praiseworthy!
Mr. Chu Shaosun said: I am fortunate to be a doctor because I am proficient in Confucian classics. I also like to read historical biographies other than the Six Classics.
I couldn't be humble and conceding, so I wrote six more chapters of funny stories and compiled them at the back of Tai Shigong's original work.
It can be read and expanded, so that it can be passed on to future generations who are not afraid of troubles to read, so as to relax their minds and alert them to listen. It is specially attached to the back of the three funny stories of Tai Shigong above.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, there was a favored artist named Guo. Although his speeches were not reasonable, he could make the emperor feel happy after listening to them.
When Emperor Wu was young, the mother of Marquis Dongwu nursed him. When Emperor Wu grew up, he called her the "Big Wet Nurse".
I visit the DPRK about twice a month.
summary: Two centuries later, You Zhan, a short Qin performer, used wit to aid others. During a rainstorm, he joked about guards being wet while he was dry, leading Qin Shihuang to halve their duty. He also dissuaded the emperor from expanding hunting grounds and Qin Ershi from painting city walls, using humor to highlight impracticality.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传

translation:
General Wei stopped in front of the car, and Mr. Dong Guo said beside the car: Mrs. Wang has recently been favored by the emperor, and her family is poor.
Now that the general has received a thousand catties of gold, if he uses half of it to give to Mrs. Wang's parents, the emperor will be very happy to know it.
This is what is called a clever and convenient strategy.
General Wei thanked him and said: Fortunately, sir, you told me this convenient strategy. I will definitely follow the advice.
So General Wei used five hundred kilograms of gold as a gift to Mrs. Wang's parents.
Mrs. Wang told Emperor Wu about this.
Emperor Wu said: The general does not know how to do this.
When Wei Qing was asked where he got the strategy, he replied: "I got it from Mr. Dongguo who was on duty."
So he ordered Mr. Dongguo to be summoned and appointed him as the county captain.
Mr. Dongguo has been waiting for work at the bus station for a long time. He is poor, hungry and cold. His clothes are shabby and his shoes are not intact.
When walking in the snow, the shoes have sides but no soles, and the feet are all on the ground.
The passers-by laughed at him, and Mr. Dongguo answered them: Who can wear shoes and walk in the snow, and let people see that the top of the shoe is a shoe, and the bottom of the shoe looks like a human foot?
When he was appointed as an official with a salary of two thousand dan, wore a green ribbon, walked out of the palace gate to say goodbye to his master, all those who had been waiting with him in the past came to bid farewell to him in batches on the outskirts of the capital.
Glorious and glorious all the way, famous in the contemporary era.
This is what is called a man wearing coarse clothes but carrying a treasure in his arms.
When he was poor, everyone ignored him; when he became famous, everyone rushed to depend on him.
As the saying goes: A fortune teller misses a good horse because of his skinny appearance, and a fortune teller misses a talented person because of his poor appearance.
Is this the scenario you are talking about?
Mrs. Wang was seriously ill, and the emperor visited her in person and asked her: Your son should be crowned king. Where do you want to crown him?
He replied: I hope to be sealed in Luoyang.
The emperor said: No.
Luoyang has arsenals, large granaries, and is located at a transportation junction. It is the choke point of the world.
Since the late emperor, it is said that no king has been granted the title of king in Luoyang.
However, none of the feudal states in the Guandong area is larger than Qi, so he can be crowned King of Qi.
Mrs. Wang patted her head with her hands and exclaimed: So lucky.
After the death of Mrs. Wang, it was called the death of the Queen Mother of Qi.
Once upon a time, the King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun to the State of Chu to offer yellow swans.
After leaving the capital gate, the yellow swan flew away on the way. He had no choice but to hold the empty cage, fabricate a lie, and go to see the king of Chu, saying: The king of Qi sent me to offer the yellow swan. When he passed by the water, he couldn't bear the yellow swan to dry up, so he let it drink water. Unexpectedly, it left me and flew away.
I want to stab the abdomen or strangle the neck to death, but I am also worried that others will criticize the king for causing the scholars to commit suicide because of birds and beasts.
Yellow swans are feathered things that are very similar. I want to buy a similar one to replace it. This is dishonest and deceives the king.
He wanted to flee to other countries, but he was also sad that the communication between the monarchs of Qi and Chu was cut off.
summary: Tai Shigong praised these three for their clever advice. Mr. Chu Shaosun added six more tales, including that of Guo Sheren, who helped a wet nurse avoid exile by prompting her to show reluctance, moving Emperor Wu to pity. Dongfang Shuo, a learned scholar, used humor to gain favor with Emperor Wu, often receiving rewards but spending them on marriages. He defended his behavior as "court reclusion" and advised against slander on his deathbed. Mr. Dong Guo advised General Wei Qing to gift gold to Empress Wang's parents, earning himself an official post. Other tales include a clever envoy who lost a swan but gained rewards, a prefect coached by a drunkard to credit the emperor for peace, and Ximen Bao, who stopped the practice of sacrificing girls to the River God by throwing the corrupt priests into the river, then dug irrigation canals that benefited the people for generations.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/滑稽列传

translation:
Tian Dan was a native of Di County and a sibling of the Tian family, King of Qi during the Warring States Period.
Tian Dan's cousin and Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng was a powerful figure in the local area, and his clan was strong and very popular.
When Chen She began to raise troops and claim to be the King of Chu, he sent Zhou Shi to capture and pacify the Wei region, and then marched north to Di County, which was defended.
Tian Dan pretended to tie up his own slave and led his young men to the county government, claiming to kill the guilty slave after meeting with the county magistrate.
When they saw the magistrate of Di County, they took the opportunity to kill him, and then summoned powerful officials and young people to say: "The princes from all over the country have rebelled against Qin and established themselves. Qi is a country established in ancient times, and I, Tian Dan, am a member of Qi Wang Tian's clan and should be the king."
So Tian Dan proclaimed himself King of Qi and raised troops to attack Zhou City.
After Zhou Shi's army withdrew, Tian Dan took the opportunity to lead his troops eastward, seize and pacify the land of Qi.
Qin general Zhang Han led his troops to besiege King Jiu of Wei in Linji. The situation was urgent, and King Wei sent people to Qi to ask for rescue. King Tian Dan of Qi led the army to rescue Wei.
Zhang Han let his soldiers and horses hold the coins in their mouths at night, and took advantage of the cover of night to launch a sneak attack. He defeated the Qi and Wei coalition forces and killed Tian Dan at the foot of Linji City.
Tian Dan's cousin Tian Rong gathered the remaining troops of Tian Dan and fled eastward to Dong'a.
After the people of Qi heard the news that Tian Dan had died in battle, they supported Tian Jia, the younger brother of the former King of Qi Tian Jian, as King of Qi, Tian Jiao as prime minister, and Tian Jian as general, in order to resist the princes.
When Tian Rong fled to Dong'a, Zhang Han pursued and intercepted him.
Xiang Liang heard that Tian Rong was in critical condition, so he led his troops to Dong'a City and defeated Zhang Han in one fell swoop.
Zhang Han fled to the west, while Xiang Liang took advantage of the victory to pursue him.
However, Tian Rong was very angry about the fact that the Qi people made Tianjie the king of Qi, so he led his troops back and attacked and chased Qi King Tianjie. Tianjie fled to Chu State, and Prime Minister Tian Jiao fled to Zhao State. Tian Jiao's younger brother Tian Jian had gone to Zhao State for help before, so he stayed in Zhao State and did not dare to go back.
Tian Rong then made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi the king of Qi and appointed himself prime minister. Tian Heng was made a general and the land of Qi was pacified.
After Xiang Liang pursued Zhang Han, Zhang Han's army became increasingly powerful, so Xiang Liang sent envoys to inform Qi and Zhao, asking the two countries to jointly send troops to attack Zhang Han.
Tian Rong said: If Chu kills Tianjia and Zhao kills Tianjiao and Tianjian, we will send troops.
King Huai of Chu said: Tianjia is the king of our ally. He came to us when we were desperate. It is unethical to kill him.
Zhao State was also unwilling to trade with Qi State by killing Tian Jiao and Tian Jian Lai.
The people of Qi said: If the hand is bitten by a viper, the hand must be cut off; if the foot is bitten by the viper, the foot must be cut off.
Why?
Because if not, it will harm the whole body.
But now Tianjia, Tianjiao, and Tianjian are not flesh and blood relatives to Chu and Zhao. Why not kill them?
summary: Tian Dan, a member of the Qi royal family, proclaimed himself King of Qi during the Warring States period after killing the Di County magistrate. He raised troops but was later killed by Qin general Zhang Han at Linji. His cousin Tian Rong gathered the remnants and fled east. After Tian Dan's death, the Qi people installed Tian Jia as king, but Tian Rong, angered by this, attacked and drove Tian Jia and his ministers into exile. Tian Rong then made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi king and appointed himself prime minister, with Tian Heng as general.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/田儋列传

translation:
Moreover, if the Qin Dynasty succeeds in conquering the world, not only will we be humiliated, but even our ancestors' graves may have to be dug up.
Neither Chu nor Zhao were willing to obey Qi, and Qi was very angry and eventually refused to send troops to rescue.
Zhang Han indeed defeated the Chu army and killed Xiang Liang. The Chu army fled eastward, and Zhang Han took the opportunity to cross the Yellow River and besiege Zhao's Julu.
Xiang Yu went to rescue Zhao State, and therefore resented Tian Rong very much.
Xiang Yu had already protected Zhao State and surrendered Zhang Han and other generals of the Qin Dynasty, so he went west to Xianyang to kill, destroyed the Qin Dynasty, and then divided the princes and kings among themselves. So he changed the title of King Qi Tianshi to King Jiaodong and ruled in Jimo.
Qi general Tian Du followed Xiang Yu to rescue Zhao and then marched into Guanzhong. Therefore, Xiang Yu made Tian Du the king of Qi and ruled in Linzi.
Tian An, the grandson of Tian Jian, the former Qi king, captured many cities in Jibei one after another when Xiang Yu was crossing the river to rescue Zhao, and then led his troops to surrender to Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu therefore made Tian An the king of Jibei, and his seat was Boyang.
Because Tian Rong disobeyed Xiang Yu and refused to send troops to assist Chu and Zhao in attacking the Qin Dynasty, he could not be crowned king; Zhao general Chen Yu was also not crowned king because of his dereliction of duty. Both of them resented Xiang Yu.
After Xiang Yu returned to Chu, the feudal princes also returned to their own fiefdoms. Tian Rong sent troops to help Chen Yu and asked him to rebel against Xiang Yu in Zhao. Tian Rong himself also sent troops to fight against Tian Du, who fled to Chu.
Tian Rong detained Qi Wang Tianshi and refused to allow him to go to the administrative office of Jiaodong.
Tian Shi's men said: Xiang Yu is powerful and ferocious, and as the king of Qi, you should go to your own kingdom of Jiaodong. If you don't go, there will be danger.
Tian Shi was very frightened, so he ran away to Jiaodong.
When Tian Rong learned about it, he was furious and led his men to chase King Qi Tianshi and killed him in Jimo. When he came back, he attacked Tian'an, the king of Jibei, and killed him.
Therefore, Tian Rong proclaimed himself the king of Qi and occupied all the lands of Sanqi.
After Xiang Yu heard the news, he was very angry, so he launched an army to attack Qi in the north.
King Tian Rong of Qi was severely defeated and fled to Pingyuan. The people of Pingyuan killed Tian Rong.
Afterwards, Xiang Yu burned and leveled the walls of Qi's capital, and massacred everyone he passed. The people of Qi couldn't bear it, so they all gathered to rebel against him.
Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng gathered Qi's scattered soldiers and obtained tens of thousands of troops to counterattack Xiang Yu in Chengyang.
At this time, Liu Bang, king of Han, led the army of the princes to defeat the Chu army and entered Pengcheng.
After Xiang Yu heard the news, he let go of the Qi army and went back, launching an attack on the Han soldiers in Pengcheng. Then there were many battles with the Han army, and they were locked in a stalemate in Xingyang.
Therefore, Tian Heng was able to regain the large and small cities of Qi again, and established Tian Guang, Tian Rong's son, as the king of Qi. Tian Heng assisted him as prime minister and arbitrarily ruled the country. All political affairs, no matter how big or small, were decided by Tian Heng.
summary: When Xiang Liang requested Qi's aid against Zhang Han, Tian Rong demanded the execution of the exiled Qi leaders as a condition, which Chu and Zhao refused. Qi withheld support, and Zhang Han subsequently defeated and killed Xiang Liang. Later, Xiang Yu, after defeating Qin, divided the territories, demoting Tian Shi to King of Jiaodong and installing Tian Du as King of Qi. Tian Rong, resentful at being excluded, attacked and killed Tian Du and Tian An, proclaiming himself King of Qi. Xiang Yu retaliated, defeating and killing Tian Rong. Tian Heng then gathered forces, regained Qi territory, and installed Tian Rong's son Tian Guang as king, with himself as de facto ruler.

translation:
Three years after Tian Heng pacified Qi, King Liu Bang of Han sent Li Shiqi to Qi to lobby Qi King Tian Guang and Prime Minister Tian Heng to submit to the Han Dynasty.
Tian Heng believed that this was feasible, so he lifted Qi's defense against the Han army in Lixia.
Han Xin, the general of the Han Dynasty, was going to attack Qi State eastward.
At first, Qi State sent troops led by Hua Wushang and Tian Jie to station in Lixia to resist the Han army. When the Han envoys arrived, they abandoned their war preparations to defend the city, allowed the soldiers to drink, and sent envoys to make peace with the Han Dynasty.
However, after the Han general Han Xin pacified Zhao and Yan, he used Kuai Tong's strategy to cross the plains and make a sudden attack, defeating the Qi garrison stationed in Lixia, and then invaded Linzi.
When Qi King Tian Guang and Prime Minister Tian Heng saw the sudden appearance of the Han army, they were very angry. They thought they had been betrayed by Li Sheng and immediately cooked and killed Li Sheng.
King Tian Guang of Qi fled east to Gaomi, Prime Minister Tian Heng fled to Boyang, Prime Minister Tian Guang fled to Chengyang, and General Tian Ji led the army to garrison in Jiaodong.
At this time, Chu State sent Long Qie to lead the army to rescue Qi State. Qi Wang Tian Guang and Long Qie met in Gaomi.
Han generals Han Xin and Cao Shen defeated the Qi-Chu coalition forces in Gaomi, killed Chu general Long Qie, and captured Qi King Tian Guang.
Han general Guan Ying continued the pursuit and captured Tian Guang, the prime minister of Qi.
Guan Ying continued to march and arrived at Boyang. When Tian Heng heard that King Qi Tian Guang was dead, he proclaimed himself King of Qi and turned to fight Guan Ying. Under Yingxia, Tian Heng's army was severely defeated by Guan Ying. Tian Heng fled to Liangdi and surrendered to Pengyue.
At this time, Peng Yue supported the army and remained neutral between Chu and Han, as if for the king of Han and for the king of Chu.
After Han Xin killed Chu General Long Qie, he ordered Cao Shen to continue marching to Jiaodong, where he defeated Tian Ji and killed him in battle. Han Xin also ordered Guan Ying to pursue Qi General Tian Sui, defeat him in Qiancheng and kill him.
In this way, Han Xin pacified Qi and wrote to Liu Bang, asking him to make himself the false king of Qi. Liu Bang also took advantage of the situation and made Han Xin the king of Qi.
More than a year later, Liu Bang, king of Han, destroyed Xiang Yu, proclaimed himself emperor, and made Pengyue King of Liang.
Tian Heng was afraid of being killed, so he led more than 500 of his men to flee into the sea and live on a small island.
After Liu Bang, the emperor of the Han Dynasty, heard the news, he thought that Brother Tian Heng had already pacified Qi State, and most of the wise men of Qi State were attached to him. If he was left to wander in the sea without being taken in, he might be in trouble in the future.
Therefore, he sent an envoy to pardon Tian Heng's crime and summoned him to the court. However, Tian Heng declined and said: I once cooked and killed your majesty's envoy Li Sheng. Now I heard that Li Sheng's younger brother Li Shang was a very talented Han Dynasty general. So I was very afraid and did not dare to go to Beijing to follow the imperial edict. I asked you to allow me to be a commoner and stay on this island.
When the envoy came back to report, Emperor Gaozu immediately issued an edict to Weiwei Li Shang: King Tian Heng of Qi is about to arrive in Beijing. Anyone who dares to touch his entourage will be executed immediately!
Then he sent an envoy with a talisman to inform Tian Heng of the imperial edict issued by the emperor to tell Li Shang's situation exactly as it was. He also said: "If Tian Heng comes to Beijing, the largest one can be made a king and the smallest one can be made a marquis; if he does not come, an army will be sent to kill him."
Tian Heng and his two retainers took the stage carriage to Luoyang.
Thirty miles away from Luoyang, there is a place called Corpse Township. On this day, Tian Heng and others came to this inn. Tian Heng said to the Han envoy: As a human minister, you should take a refreshing bath before paying homage to the emperor.
So he stayed.
Tian Heng said to his disciples: At first, I, Tian Heng, and the King of Han were both lonely kings in the south. But now that the King of Han has become the emperor, I, Tian Heng, have become a slave of the subjugated country. It would be a great shame to have to serve him in the north.
summary: Years later, Han king Liu Bang sent Li Shiqi to negotiate Qi's submission. Tian Heng agreed and lifted defenses, but Han general Han Xin launched a surprise attack, capturing Linzi. Believing Li Shiqi had betrayed them, Tian Guang and Tian Heng executed him. Han forces defeated Qi and Chu allies, killing General Long Qie and capturing Tian Guang. Tian Heng then proclaimed himself king but was defeated by Han forces and fled to Liang. After Liu Bang became emperor, Tian Heng, fearing execution, fled to an island with 500 followers. Summoned by the emperor, Tian Heng committed suicide near Luoyang, ashamed to serve under Liu Bang after having killed Li Shiqi. His two retainers and later the 500 followers also died, demonstrating his ability to inspire loyalty. The historian Sima Qian praised Tian Heng's virtue, noting that despite his death, no painter has depicted his story.

translation:
Tian Dan is the distant descendant of the Tian family in Qi State.
During the reign of King Qi Min, Tian Dan served as a minor official in charge of the municipal administration in Linyi City, the capital, and was not reused by the King of Qi.
Later, Yan State sent general Le Yi to attack Qi State, and King Qi Min was forced to flee from the capital, and soon retreated to Jucheng.
When the Yan army marched in to conquer Qi, Tian Dan also left the capital and fled to Anping. He asked his people to saw off all the protruding parts of the axles at both ends and wrap them in iron sheets.
Soon, the Yan army besieged Anping again, and the city was breached. The Qi people scrambled to escape. Many people were captured by the Yan army because their axles were broken. Only Tian Dan and his clansmen were able to escape because they wrapped the axle with iron hoops and retreated eastward to Jimo.
At this time, the Yan army had surrendered all the cities of Qi, and only two cities, Ju and Jimo, had not yet been conquered.
When the Yan army heard that King Qi Min was in Jucheng, they gathered their troops and attacked Jucheng with all their strength.
Minister Nao Chi killed King Qi Min in Jucheng and defended the city against the Yan army. The Yan army did not break the city for several years.
As a last resort, General Yan could only lead his troops eastward and besiege Jimo. The officials guarding the city of Jimo went out to fight with the Yan army, but were defeated and killed.
The soldiers and civilians in Jimo City elected Tian Dan as their leader, saying: In the battle of Anping, Tian Dan and his fellow tribesmen were able to escape safely because they wrapped the axles with iron hoops, which shows that he knows the art of war.
Therefore, everyone supported Tian Dan as general, defended Jimo, and resisted the Yan army.
Not long after, King Yan Zhao died and King Yan Hui came to the throne. There was a rift between him and Le Yi.
After Tian Dan heard the news, he sent people to Yan State to implement countermeasures and threatened: King Qi Min has been killed, and there are only two Qi State cities that have not been conquered.
Le Yi did not dare to return home because he was afraid of being killed by the king. In the name of attacking Qi, he actually wanted to join forces with Qi's troops and become king of Qi.
The people of Qi have not yet surrendered, so they are stalling for time and delaying the attack on Jimo in order to wait for the time to mature before claiming the throne.
What the people of Qi are worried about is that they are afraid that Yan will send other generals. In that case, Mo City will definitely be destroyed.
King Yan Hui thought these words were correct and sent his general Qi Jie to replace Le Yi.
As a result, Le Yi fled to Zhao State, and the Yan officers and soldiers were very angry about this.
Tian Dan also ordered the soldiers and civilians in the city to offer sacrifices to their ancestors in the courtyard before eating, causing many birds to fly around the city as they competed for the sacrificial food.
Yan Jun outside the city felt strange when he saw it.
Tian Dan threatened again: "This is a god descending from the sky to guide us in defeating the enemy and winning."
And the people in the city said: There must be a man of god who will be my military advisor.
A soldier said: Can I be your military advisor?
After saying that, he walked away.
Tian Dan stood up quickly, pulled him over, asked him to sit on the upper seat facing east, and served him with the etiquette of serving a teacher.
The soldier said: I lied to you, I actually have no skills. Tian Dan said: Stop talking.
Then he became his teacher.
Every time you give an order, you must say it is the master's idea.
He also threatened: What I fear most is that the Yan army will cut off the noses of the captured Qi soldiers, put them at the front of the team, and then fight with us, then Jimo will definitely be conquered.
summary: Tian Dan, a distant descendant of the Qi royal family, initially served as a minor official in Linyi but was not favored by King Qi Min. When Yan's general Le Yi attacked Qi, Tian Dan fled to Anping, where he advised his people to reinforce their chariot axles with iron sheets. This precaution allowed him and his clan to escape when Anping fell, while others were captured due to broken axles. They retreated to Jimo, one of only two Qi cities not conquered by Yan. After King Qi Min was killed in Ju, Yan besieged Jimo. The city's defenders were defeated, and the soldiers elected Tian Dan as their leader, citing his tactical foresight. When King Yan Zhao died and King Yan Hui succeeded him, a rift with Le Yi emerged. Tian Dan exploited this by sending agents to spread rumors that Le Yi planned to become king of Qi, leading Yan Hui to replace him with Qi Jie. Le Yi fled to Zhao, angering Yan troops.

translation:
When Yan Jun heard this, he acted accordingly.
When the people in the city saw that many surrendered soldiers from Qi had their noses cut off, everyone was filled with indignation and defended even more firmly, fearing that they would be caught by the enemy.
Tian Dan sent someone to counterattack and said: "I am very afraid that the Yan people dug up our ancestral graves outside the city and insulted our ancestors. This is really chilling."
After the Yan army heard about it, they dug up all the graves of the Qi people and burned the dead bodies.
When the people of Jimo saw this scene from the city, they all cried bitterly and asked to go out of the city to fight. They were very angry.
Tian Dan knew that now was the best time to go to war, so he personally took the plywood and shovel, and built fortifications with the soldiers. He also included his wife and concubines in the team, and took out all the food to reward the soldiers.
He ordered the well-equipped elite troops not to ambush, and allowed the old, weak, remnant soldiers and women to defend at the top of the city. He also sent envoys to the Yan army's camp to agree on the surrender with the Yan army. After learning the news, the Yan army soldiers all shouted long live.
Tian Dan collected gold from the people and got a thousand yi in total, and asked the rich and powerful people in Jimo City to go and give it to General Yan, requesting: Jimo is about to surrender. I hope that after you enter the city, you will not kidnap our wives and concubines, so that they can be safe.
The general of the Yan army was very happy and agreed to him.
The Yan army became more relaxed as a result.
Tian Dan collected more than a thousand cows from the city, covered them with bright red silk quilts with colorful dragon patterns painted on them, tied sharp knives to the horns, tied grease-soaked reeds to the cows' tails, and lit the reeds on the cows' tails.
He also dug dozens of caves into the city wall, drove the cattle out of the caves at night, and sent five thousand strong soldiers to follow the fire cattle.
Because their tails were burned, the fire oxen went straight to the Yan army's camp in a rage. All of this happened suddenly at night, causing the Yan army to panic.
The torches on the tails of the oxen illuminated the night as brightly as day. Yan Jun saw that their bodies were covered with dragon patterns, and those who touched them were either dead or injured.
Five thousand warriors attacked silently with coins in their mouths, while the people in Mo City took the opportunity to beat drums and shout, following closely behind. Even the old and weak women and children held bronze utensils and beat the sound loudly, which combined with the shouts outside the city to form an earth-shattering sound.
The Yan army was frightened and fled in defeat.
The people of Qi killed Yan's general Qi Jie in the rebellion.
The Yan army was in chaos and fled for their lives. The Qi army pursued the fleeing enemy troops closely. The towns they passed through betrayed the Yan army and surrendered to Tian Dan. Tian Dan's troops also increased day by day, taking advantage of the military power of victory to pursue them all the way. The Yan army fled in panic, its combat effectiveness weakening day by day, and retreated to the edge of the Yellow River. More than 70 cities that had originally been lost to Qi were recovered by Qi.
So Tian Dan went to Jucheng to greet King Xiang of Qi, and King Xiang returned to the capital Linzi to handle government affairs.
King Xiang of Qi granted him the title of Land Dan and the title of Lord Anping.
Tai Shigong said: When fighting with troops, we should not only engage in head-on confrontation, but also use surprise troops to attack and win.
People who are good at using troops can always use surprise and variety to create endless changes.
The combination of head-on confrontation and surprise victory is as unpredictable as a circle with no beginning and end.
At the beginning of the war, you should be as calm and weak as a virgin, luring the enemy to open the door wide and be unprepared; then when the time comes, be as fast and agile as an escaped rabbit, leaving the enemy with no time to defend. This is exactly how Tian Dan uses his troops!
summary: Tian Dan then employed psychological tactics. He had soldiers offer sacrifices in courtyards, attracting birds that Yan soldiers mistook for divine signs. He declared a god had descended and appointed a soldier as a "spiritual teacher," attributing all orders to him. He also provoked Yan into mutilating Qi captives and desecrating ancestral graves, which enraged Jimo's defenders. When morale peaked, Tian Dan joined his troops in labor, shared food, and hid elite soldiers while displaying weak defenders. He feigned surrender and bribed Yan's general to spare families, lulling Yan into complacency. At night, Tian Dan unleashed a thousand oxen with painted dragon patterns, sharp knives on horns, and burning reeds on tails through holes in the city wall. The fiery oxen charged Yan's camp, followed by 5,000 silent warriors and townspeople making noise. Panicked, Yan fled, and Qi killed Qi Jie. Tian Dan pursued, recovering over 70 lost cities. He then welcomed King Xiang of Qi back to Linzi, who granted Tian Dan the title Lord Anping.

translation:
At the beginning, when Naochi killed King Qi Min, the people of Jucheng were looking for King Qi Min's son Fazhang, and found him at Tai Shiyan's home. He was plowing and watering the fields for others.
Tai Shi's daughter liked him and was very kind to him.
Later, Fazhang told her his situation, and she had an affair with Fazhang.
When the people of Jucheng jointly supported Fa Zhang as the king of Qi and used Jucheng to fight against the Yan army, Taishi Yan's daughter was made the queen. This is what people call the "queen queen".
When the Yan army first invaded the Qi State, they heard that Wang Yu, a native of Huayi, was a talented man, so he ordered the army to say: No entry is allowed within thirty miles around Huayi. This is because of Wang Li.
Soon, the Yan State sent someone to say to Wang Zhu: "Many people in the Qi State praise your noble character. We will appoint you as a general and grant you 10,000 households of food."
Wang Yi firmly refused and refused to accept.
The people of Yan said: If you are unwilling to accept it, we will lead the army and slaughter the city!
Wang Pei said: A loyal minister cannot serve two monarchs, and a loyal woman will not remarry a second husband.
The King of Qi did not listen to my advice, so I lived in seclusion and farmed in the countryside.
Now the state of Qi has been destroyed, and I cannot revive it. Now you are using force to kidnap me to be your general. If I agree, it will mean that I am helping King Jie to commit violence.
Rather than live and do this unjust thing, it would be better to be cooked to death!
Then he hung his neck on a branch, struggled hard, broke his neck and died.
When the fleeing officials of Qi heard about this, they said: "Wang Zhu is just a commoner. He can still stick to his moral integrity and refuse to surrender to the Yan people, let alone us serving officials who enjoy state salaries!"
So they gathered together and rushed to Jucheng to seek the son of King Qi Min and support him as King Qi Xiang.
summary: The text concludes with Tai Shigong praising Tian Dan's use of surprise tactics, and recounts two subplots: the discovery of King Xiang (Fazhang) and his marriage to Tai Shi's daughter, and the martyrdom of Wang Yu, a recluse who refused Yan's offer to become a general, inspiring Qi officials to rally behind King Xiang.

translation:
Uncle Tian is a native of Xingcheng, Zhao State, and his ancestors are descendants of the Tian family of Qi State.
Uncle Tian liked swordsmanship and once studied Huang and Lao's theories at Le Jugong's residence.
Uncle Tian is a strict and honest man, and he takes great pride in this. I like to hang out with those people who are highly respected. The people of Zhao recommended him to Zhao Wu, the prime minister, and Zhao Wu praised him to King Zhao Zhang Ao, who appointed him as a doctor.
After serving for several years, he has always been upright, honest and fair. Although King Zhao appreciated him, he did not have time to promote him.
It happened that Chen Xi was rebelling in Dai. In the seventh year of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gaozu went to punish him. When passing by Zhao State, King Zhao Zhang Ao personally brought a plate of food to offer food. The etiquette was very respectful, but Emperor Gaozu of Han arrogantly sat with his legs stretched out and cursed him.
At that time, Zhao Prime Minister Zhao Wu and dozens of others were very angry, and said to Zhao Wang Zhang Ao: You served the emperor with complete etiquette, but now you are treated like this. We ask for rebellion.
King Zhao bit his finger and it bled, and said: My father has lost his country. Without Your Majesty, our bodies will be infested with maggots and no one will collect them after we die. How can you say such things?
Say no more! So Guan Gao and others discussed and said: King Zhao is a loyal and honest man, and he is unwilling to betray the kindness of the emperor.
They secretly plotted against each other to kill the emperor.
Just as the matter was discovered, the Han Dynasty ordered the arrest of King Zhao and the officials who had rebelled.
So Zhao Wu and others committed suicide, and only Guan Gao was willing to be imprisoned.
At this time, the Han Dynasty issued another edict saying: Zhao Guo dares to follow King Zhao to Beijing and is guilty of the crime of three tribes.
Only Meng Shu, Tian Shu and more than a dozen people wore auburn prison clothes, shaved their own hair, and wore torture instruments around their necks. They pretended to be the slaves of King Zhao and followed King Zhao Zhang Ao to Chang'an.
After the rebellion of Guan Gao and others was clarified, King Zhao Zhang Ao was released from prison and deposed as Marquis of Xuan Ping. He recommended and praised Uncle Tian and other ten people.
The emperor summoned them all and talked with them. He thought that none of the ministers in the court could surpass them. The emperor was very happy and appointed them all as county guards or ministers of the princes.
Uncle Tian had been the governor of Hanzhong County for more than ten years. When Empress Gao died, the princes rebelled, and the ministers killed them and established Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty.
After Emperor Wen of Han came to the throne, he summoned Uncle Tian and asked him: Sir, do you know who is a loyal and virtuous person in the world?
Uncle Tian replied: How could I know?
The emperor said: You are a loyal elder and should be able to know.
Uncle Tian kowtowed and said: Meng Shu, the former governor of Yunzhong County, was a loyal and honest man.
At that time, Meng Shu violated the criminal law because he failed to resist the Huns' invasion and robbery. The invasion and robbery in Yunzhong County was particularly serious, so he was dismissed from his post.
Emperor Wen said: The late emperor appointed Meng Shu as the prefect of Yunzhong County for more than ten years. The Huns invaded, and Meng Shu could not hold on and sent hundreds of soldiers to the army for no reason.
Should a loyal and virtuous elder kill someone?
How can you say that Meng Shu is an elder?
Uncle Tian kowtowed and replied: This is why Meng Shu is an elder.
Guan Gao and others rebelled, and the emperor issued a clear and clear edict. Anyone in Zhao State who dared to follow Zhao Wang Zhang Ao would be punished and the three clans would be punished.
However, Meng Shu shaved off his hair and tied a torture device around his neck, followed Zhao Wang Zhang Ao to where he was going, and wanted to die for him. How could he have expected that he would become the governor of Yunzhong County?
Han and Chu had a long-term confrontation, and the soldiers were tired and distressed.
The Xiongnu King Maodun had just conquered the Northern Yi and came to harm the border. Meng Shu knew that the soldiers were tired and miserable and could not bear to order them to fight again. The soldiers went to the city to fight to the death, just like a son fighting for his father and a younger brother fighting for his elder brother. Therefore, there were hundreds of warriors.
How could Meng Shu deliberately drive them to fight!
This is why Meng Shu is a loyal elder.
So the emperor said: Meng Shu is so virtuous!
He recalled Meng Shu and made him the governor of Yunzhong County again.
A few years later, Uncle Tian lost his position as the prefect of Hanzhong County because of a crime.
King Xiao of Liang sent people to assassinate Yuan Ang, the former prime minister of Wu. Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty recalled Uncle Tian and asked him to go to Liang to review the case. Uncle Tian found out all the facts of the case and reported back to the court.
Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty said: Did the King of Liang send someone to assassinate Yuan Ang?
He replied: I will be punished by death!
There is such a thing!
The emperor said: Is there any evidence of guilt?
Uncle Tian said: Your Majesty, please don't ask about King Liang's affairs. The emperor said: Why?
Uncle Tian said: If the King of Liang does not obey the law and is executed, the criminal law of the Han Dynasty cannot be implemented. If he fails to obey the law and dies, the Queen Mother will have trouble sleeping and eating. This is your worry again!
Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty appreciated him very much and made him the prime minister of Lu.
When Uncle Tian took office, more than a hundred people came to him and accused King Lu of taking their property.
Uncle Tian caught the leading twenty men and beat them with fifty big sticks each, and the rest of them each slapped twenty on their palms. He got angry at them and said, "Isn't King Lu your monarch?"
How dare you slander the monarch!
summary: Uncle Tian, a native of Xingcheng in Zhao State and a descendant of the Tian family of Qi, was a strict and honest man who studied Huang-Lao theories and swordsmanship. Recommended by Zhao Wu, he served as a doctor under King Zhao Zhang Ao, known for his uprightness. During Emperor Gaozu of Han’s campaign against Chen Xi’s rebellion, the emperor insulted King Zhao, angering Zhao Wu and others who plotted rebellion. King Zhao refused, but Guan Gao secretly conspired to kill the emperor. When discovered, Zhao Wu committed suicide, and Guan Gao was imprisoned. An edict threatened the three-clan punishment for anyone following King Zhao to Chang’an. Meng Shu, Tian Shu, and over a dozen others shaved their heads, wore prison clothes, and pretended to be King Zhao’s slaves to accompany him. After Guan Gao’s rebellion was resolved, King Zhao was deposed as Marquis of Xuan Ping and recommended these men. The emperor appointed them all as county governors or ministers. Uncle Tian served as governor of Hanzhong for over ten years. After Empress Gao’s death, Emperor Wen of Han ascended and asked Uncle Tian about loyal and virtuous men. Uncle Tian praised Meng Shu, who had shaved his head and followed King Zhao to die for him, and who, as governor of Yunzhong, spared his tired soldiers from fighting the Xiongnu, leading to his dismissal. Emperor Wen reinstated Meng Shu. Later, Uncle Tian lost his position due to a crime. Emperor Jing of Han sent him to investigate King Xiao of Liang’s assassination of Yuan Ang. Uncle Tian advised against pursuing the case to avoid upsetting the Queen Mother, and was made prime minister of Lu. There, he punished those accusing King Lu of theft, and King Lu returned the property. Uncle Tian refused to rest in pavilions while King Lu hunted, curbing the king’s excess. He died as prime minister of Lu. His son Tian Ren refused gold offerings, preserving his father’s reputation. Tian Ren became General Wei Qing’s retainer, later a doctor, and served as prime minister with a two-thousand-stone salary. He lost his position, then became Jingfu Duwei and Si Zhi. Implicated in the prince’s rebellion, he let the prince escape the city gate and was executed. Ren An, from Xingyang, rose from poverty to become a retainer of General Wei Qing alongside Tian Ren. Both were recommended by Zhao Yu for their talents. Emperor Wu of Han appointed Ren An to supervise the Northern Army and Tian Ren to oversee border farming. Ren An became governor of Yizhou. Tian Ren, as prime minister, inspected Sanhe, executing corrupt officials, and became Prime Minister Sizhi. During the prince’s rebellion, Tian Ren let the prince escape and was executed. Ren An, as Northern Army protector, refused the prince’s summons but was later accused of duplicity and executed. The text warns against failing to retreat from wealth and power, citing Fan Li as a model.

translation:
Bai Qi is from Yidi.
He was good at using troops and served King Zhao of Qin.
In the thirteenth year of King Zhao's reign, Bai Qi was granted the title of Zuo Shu Zhang and led troops to attack Xincheng in South Korea.
In this year, Ranghou served as the prime minister of Qin. He appointed Ren Bi as the governor of Hanzhong County.
The next year, Bai Qi was granted the title Zuogeng, attacked the allied forces of Han and Wei, fought in Yique, killed 240,000 enemies, captured their general Gongsun happy, and captured five cities.
Bai Qi was promoted to captain of the country.
He led his troops across the Yellow River and captured a large area of ​​land east of Anyi in South Korea up to Wadi River.
In the third year, Bai Qi was granted the title of Daliangzao again.
Defeated the Wei army and captured sixty-one cities, large and small.
In the fourth year, Bai Qi and Ke Qing attacked Yuan City by mistake and captured it immediately.
In the fifth year after that, Bai Qi attacked Zhao and captured Guanglang City.
In the seventh year after this, Bai Qi attacked Chu and occupied five cities including Yan and Deng.
The next year, he attacked Chu again, captured Ying, the capital of Chu, burned the tombs of the Chu kings, and headed east to Jingling.
The king of Chu fled the capital of Ying and fled eastward, moving his capital to Chen.
The Qin State established Yingdi as Nanjun.
Bai Qi was named Lord Wu'an. He took advantage of the situation to attack Chu and pacified Wu and Qianzhong counties.
In the thirty-fourth year of King Zhao, Bai Qi attacked Wei and captured Huayang, causing Mangmao to flee. He also captured the generals of Zhao and Wei and killed 130,000 enemies.
At that time, Bai Qi fought with Zhao's general Jia Yan and sank 20,000 Zhao soldiers into the Yellow River.
In the forty-third year of King Zhao, Bai Qi attacked Xingcheng in South Korea, captured five cities, and killed 50,000 enemies.
In the forty-fourth year, Bai Qi attacked Nanyang Taihang Road in South Korea and blocked this passage.
In the forty-fifth year of King Zhao, Bai Qi sent troops to attack the Yewang City in South Korea. The Yewang surrendered, cutting off the connection between Shangdang County in South Korea and South Korea.
Feng Ting, the governor of Shangdang County, planned with the people and said: The road to the capital Zheng is cut off, and South Korea will definitely not be able to control us.
The Qin army is advancing day by day, and South Korea cannot rescue it, so it is better to surrender Shangdang to Zhao.
If Zhao State accepts us, Qin State will be angry and will definitely attack Zhao State.
Zhao State was attacked by force and must be close to South Korea.
If Han and Zhao unite, they can resist Qin.
So he sent someone to inform Zhao State.
King Zhao Xiaocheng studied this matter with Pingyang Jun and Pingyuan Jun. Pingyang Jun said: It is better not to accept it.
The consequences of accepting it will be far greater than the benefits.
Lord Pingyuan expressed his dissent and said: "I got a county for nothing, it would be beneficial to accept it."
As a result, King Zhao accepted Shangdang and named Feng Ting Lord of Huayang.
In the forty-sixth year of King Zhao, the Qin State captured Goushi and Linyi in South Korea.
In the forty-seventh year of King Zhao, the State of Qin sent Wang Lu, the chief of the left concubine, to attack South Korea and capture Shangdang.
The people of Shangdang fled to Zhao State one after another.
The State of Zhao stationed troops in Changping to support the people of Shangdang.
In April, Wang Lu used this opportunity to attack Zhao.
summary: Bai Qi, a skilled military commander from Yidi, served King Zhao of Qin. His early campaigns included victories against Han, Wei, and Zhao, capturing cities and killing tens of thousands of enemies. He was promoted through ranks, eventually becoming Lord Wu'an after conquering Chu's capital Ying and burning its royal tombs. His most notable battle was against Zhao at Changping in the 47th year of King Zhao's reign. After initial setbacks, Zhao replaced General Lian Po with Zhao Kuo. Bai Qi used deception, cutting off Zhao's supply lines and surrounding their army. After 46 days without food, Zhao Kuo was killed, and 400,000 Zhao soldiers surrendered. Bai Qi, fearing rebellion, ordered them buried alive, shocking Zhao. Following this, Qin planned to besiege Handan, but Su Dai, sent by Han and Zhao, persuaded Prime Minister Yinghou to halt, arguing that Bai Qi's growing fame threatened Yinghou's position. King Zhao agreed to a truce, but Bai Qi's resentment toward Yinghou grew. When Qin later attacked Handan under Wang Ling, Bai Qi refused to lead, citing the army's exhaustion and the risk of allied reinforcements. Despite King Zhao's orders, Bai Qi feigned illness. After Qin's defeat, Bai Qi's remarks angered the king, who demoted him and ordered his exile. Accused of discontent, Bai Qi was forced to commit suicide in the 50th year of King Zhao's reign.

translation:
So he removed Lord Wu'an from his rank and reduced him to a soldier, and asked him to leave Xianyang and move to Yinmi.
But Lord Wu An was ill and could not make the trip.
Three months later, it became more urgent for the allied forces of the princes to attack the Qin army. The Qin army retreated many times, and messengers reporting the defeat came every day.
The King of Qin sent people to expel Bai Qi and could not let him stay in Xianyang City.
Wu Anjun was already on his way, walking ten miles from the west gate of Xianyang, to Duyou.
King Zhao of Qin discussed with Marquis Ying and other officials: Bai Qi was ordered to move out of Xianyang, but he showed that he was not satisfied, unconvinced, and complained.
The King of Qin sent an envoy to give him a sword and ordered him to commit suicide.
Wu Anjun took the sword and was about to kill himself. He looked up to the sky and sighed: What sin have I committed against God to end up like this?
After a while, he said: I was meant to die.
In the Battle of Changping, hundreds of thousands of Zhao soldiers surrendered. I used deception to bury them all alive. This was a death penalty.
Then committed suicide.
Lord Wu An died in the eleventh month of the fiftieth year of King Zhao of Qin.
Lord Wu'an died innocently, and the people of Qin sympathized with him, so they worshiped him in both urban and rural areas.
Wang Jian was from Dongxiang, Pinyang.
He was fond of military affairs when he was young, and later served Qin Shihuang.
In the eleventh year of the First Emperor's reign, Wang Jian led troops to attack Yanyu of Zhao State. Not only did he capture it, but he also captured nine cities in a row. In the eighteenth year of the First Emperor's reign, Wang Jian led troops to attack Zhao.
In just over a year, the State of Zhao was captured, King Zhao surrendered, and all parts of the State of Zhao were pacified and set up as counties.
The next year, the State of Yan sent Jing Ke to the State of Qin to murder the King of Qin, and the King of Qin sent Wang Jian to attack the State of Yan.
King Yan fled to Liaodong, and Wang Jian finally pacified Ji, the capital of Yan State, and returned victorious.
The King of Qin sent Wang Jian's son Wang Ben to attack Chu, but the Chu army was defeated.
He turned around and attacked Wei again. The king of Wei surrendered, and finally all parts of Wei were pacified.
Qin Shihuang destroyed the three kingdoms of Han, Zhao, and Wei, drove away King Xi of Yan, and defeated the Chu army many times.
Qin general Li Xin was young, energetic, brave and mighty. He once led thousands of soldiers to pursue Prince Dan of Yan to Yanshui, and finally defeated the Yan army and captured Prince Dan. Qin Shihuang believed that Li Xinxian was brave.
One day, Qin Shihuang asked Li Xin: I plan to attack Chu State. How many people do you think the general can mobilize?
Li Xin replied: No more than 200,000 people.
Qin Shihuang asked Wang Jian again, and Wang Jian replied: "We must have 600,000 people."
Qin Shihuang said: General Wang, how cowardly you are!
General Lee was really decisive and brave, and what he said was right.
So he sent Li Xin and Meng Tian to march south with 200,000 troops to attack Chu.
Wang Jian's words were not accepted, so he excused himself from illness and returned to his hometown in Pinyang for retirement.
Li Xin attacked Pingyu, and Meng Tian attacked Xinyi, defeating the Chu army.
Li Xin then attacked Yanying and captured it again, so he led his troops to move west to meet Meng Tian at Chengfu.
In fact, the Chu army was tracking and pursuing them for three days and three nights. As a result, they defeated Li Xin's troops, invaded two military camps, and killed seven captains. The Qin army was defeated and fled.
When Qin Shihuang heard the news, he was furious and rushed to Pinyang by express train. When he saw Wang Jian, he apologized and said: Because I did not adopt your strategy, Li Xin really brought shame to the Qin army.
summary: Wang Jian, from Pinyang, served Qin Shihuang. He conquered Zhao, Yan, and other states, often requesting 600,000 troops for campaigns. After Li Xin's failed attack on Chu with 200,000 men, Wang Jian was recalled. He led 600,000 troops, avoided direct engagement, and waited for Chu's army to weaken before striking, defeating them and capturing King Chu. Wang Jian's son Wang Ben and Li Xin later conquered Yan and Qi, unifying China. Wang Jian's grandson Wang Li, a third-generation general, was captured by Xiang Yu during Chen Sheng's rebellion, fulfilling a saying that general families often fail by the third generation due to accumulated killings.

translation:
Ying Hou replied: Yes.
Su Dai asked again: Are we going to besiege Handan?
Ying Hou replied: Yes.
So Su Dai said: If Zhao is destroyed, King Qin will rule the world, and Lord Wu'an should be named the Three Dukes.
Lord Wu'an captured more than 70 cities for Qin. In the south, he pacified Chu's Yan, Ying and Hanzhong areas, and in the north, he captured Zhao Kuo's 400,000 troops. Even the famous Dukes of Zhou, Duke of Zhao and Lu Wang in history could not surpass these achievements.
If the State of Zhao is destroyed and the King of Qin takes over the world, then it is certain that Lord Wu An will be the third Duke. Can you succumb to him?
Even if you are not willing to succumb to the lower position, you have to submit to the fact.
The Qin army once attacked South Korea, besieged Xingqiu, and trapped Shangdang to death. The people of Shangdang all turned to Zhao. It has been a long time since the people of the world were unwilling to be Qin's subjects.
If the Zhao State is destroyed, its northern land will fall to the Yan State, its eastern land will be merged with the Qi State, and its southern land will be merged with the Han and Wei States, then you will not get many people.
Therefore, it is better to take advantage of the panic of South Korea and Zhao to let them cede their land and stop letting Lord Wu An establish his merits.
After hearing Su Dai's words, Ying Hou proposed to the King of Qin and said: Qin's soldiers are too tired. Please agree to allow South Korea and Zhao to cede territory to make peace, and let the soldiers rest for the time being.
The King of Qin listened to the advice of Marquis Ying and made peace with Yuanyong of South Korea and six cities of Zhao.
In the first month of the year, the two sides stopped fighting.
When Wu An heard the news of the truce, he had his own ideas, and he and Ying Hou had a bad feeling about each other.
In September of this year, the State of Qin once again sent troops and ordered the five officials Wang Ling to attack Handan of the State of Zhao.
At that time, Lord Wu'an was ill and could not go to war.
In the first month of the forty-ninth year of King Zhao, Wang Ling attacked Handan, but with little success and little progress, Qin sent additional troops to help Wang Ling continue the attack.
As a result, Wang Ling's troops lost five military camps.
Lord Wu An recovered from his illness, and the King of Qin planned to send Lord Wu An to lead the troops instead of Wang Ling.
Wu'an Jun further said: Handan is really not easy to capture.
Moreover, reinforcements from the princely states arrived every day, and their resentment against Qin had been accumulated for a long time.
Although the Qin State has now wiped out the Zhao army in Changping, more than half of the Qin army's soldiers have died, leaving the country empty of troops.
Traveling thousands of miles across rivers and mountains to compete for other people's capitals, the Zhao army will fight in the city, and the princes' armies will attack outside the city. They will cooperate with each other inside and outside, and attack from both inside and outside. The defeat of the Qin army is certain.
This battle cannot be fought.
The King of Qin personally gave the order, but Wu Anjun refused to go to his post. So he sent Marquis Ying to invite him, but Wu An Jun refused to go to his post, and since then he said he was ill and could not afford it.
The King of Qin had no choice but to send Wang Lu to lead the troops instead of Wang Ling. In August and September, he besieged Handan but failed to capture it.
Chu State sent Chunshen Jun and Wei Gongzi Xinling Jun to lead hundreds of thousands of soldiers to attack the Qin army. The Qin army suffered many losses and casualties.
Lord Wu An had something to say: Qin did not listen to my opinion, what will happen now?
When King Qin heard about it, he was furious and ordered Wu Anjun to take office. Wuan Jun said that his condition was serious.
Ying Hou invited him again, but he still refused to take up his post.
summary: Sima Qian noted Bai Qi's strategic brilliance but inability to avoid Yinghou's schemes, and Wang Jian's military success but failure to promote moral governance, leading to his grandson's capture.

translation:
Ranghou Wei Ran was the younger brother of the Queen Mother Xuan, the mother of King Zhao of Qin.
His ancestor was from the Chu state and his surname was Mi.
After the death of King Qin Wu, he had no sons, so he made his younger brother the king of the country, namely King Zhao.
King Zhao's mother was originally a female official in the palace and was called Mi Bazi. When King Zhao came to the throne, Mi Bazi was revered as Queen Mother Xuan.
Queen Mother Xuan was not King Wu’s biological mother.
King Wu's mother was Queen Huiwen, who died before King Wu died.
Empress Dowager Xuan has two younger brothers: her eldest half-brother is named Ranghou, whose surname is Wei and given name is Ran; her half-brother is named Mirong, who is Huayang Jun.
King Zhao also has two younger brothers with the same mother: one is called Gaolingjun and the other is named Jingyangjun.
Among many people, Wei Ran was the most virtuous. He had been in power since the time of King Hui and King Wu.
After King Wu died, his younger brothers competed to inherit the throne. Only Wei Ran was capable and supported King Zhao.
After King Zhao ascended the throne, he appointed Wei Ran as general to guard Xianyang.
He once put down the rebellion of Ji Jun Gongzi Zhuang and some ministers, and expelled Queen Wu to the state of Wei. All the brothers of King Zhao who had evil intentions were killed. Wei Ran's prestige shocked the state of Qin for a while.
At that time, King Zhao was still young, so Empress Dowager Xuan personally presided over the affairs of the court, leaving Wei Ran in charge.
In the seventh year of King Zhao, Chuilizi died, and the State of Qin sent Lord Jingyang to Qi State as a hostage.
Zhao Guoren Lou slowly came to Qin State to serve as prime minister, which was obviously not good for Zhao State, so Zhao State sent Qiu Lie to Qin State to lobby, requesting that Wei Ran be allowed to serve as Qin State's prime minister.
Qiu Ye was about to leave, and his retainer Song Gong said to Qiu Ye: If the King of Qin does not listen to your persuasion, Lou Huan will definitely resent you.
Why don't you tell Lou Huan, please plan for you, I will have some reservations in persuading the King of Qin to appoint Wei Ran as prime minister.
The King of Qin must be surprised to see that the envoy from Zhao is not eager to appoint Wei Ran, and will not listen to your suggestion.
You said this, if things don't work out, the King of Qin will appoint Lou Huan as his prime minister, and you will gain Lou Huan's favor; if things succeed, and the King of Qin will appoint Wei Ran as his prime minister, then Wei Ran will be grateful to you.
So Qiu Ye listened to Song Gong's advice.
As expected, the State of Qin deposed Lou Huan and made Wei Ran the prime minister.
King Zhao of Qin wanted to kill Lu Li, so Lu Li fled to Qi.
In the fourteenth year of King Zhao, Wei Ranju appointed Bai Qi as general and sent him to lead the army to attack Han and Wei instead of Xiang Shou. He defeated them at Yique, killed 240,000 enemies, and captured Wei general Gongsun happy.
The next year, he captured the two cities of Wan and Ye in Chu State.
After that, Wei Ran was dismissed due to illness, and the King of Qin appointed his guest Qing Shouzhu as the prime minister.
The next year, Shouzhu was dismissed and Wei Ran was appointed as prime minister. Wei Ran was granted the title of Rangdi, and later he was granted the title of Taoyi and was called Ranghou.
Four years after Ranghou was granted the title, he served as the general of Qin and led troops to attack Wei.
Wei was forced to surrender four hundred miles of land east of the river.
summary: Ranghou Wei Ran, younger brother of Queen Mother Xuan, was a key figure in the Qin state during King Zhao's reign. After King Wu died without heirs, Wei Ran supported King Zhao's ascension, quelled rebellions, and eliminated rivals. King Zhao appointed him general to guard Xianyang, and later prime minister, a position he held multiple times. Wei Ran's military campaigns expanded Qin's territory significantly, including victories over Han, Wei, and Chu, capturing numerous cities and killing hundreds of thousands of enemies. His wealth and power rivaled the royal family's. Later, Wei Ran led further campaigns against Wei, Zhao, and Han, but was eventually dismissed after Fan Sui warned King Zhao about the excessive power of Queen Mother Xuan and her relatives. Wei Ran died in Taoyi, which was later reclaimed by Qin as a county. Sima Qian noted that Wei Ran's efforts were crucial to Qin's expansion and dominance, yet his downfall came swiftly after losing royal favor.

translation:
Later, he occupied the Hanoi area of ​​Wei State and captured more than 60 cities, large and small.
In the 19th year of King Zhao, Wei Ran was in charge. King Zhao of Qin claimed to be the West Emperor, and King Qi Min was the East Emperor.
More than a month later, Lu Li came to Qin again. The kings of Qi and Qin canceled their imperial titles and still claimed the title of king.
Wei Ran once again served as the prime minister of Qin, but was dismissed six years later.
Two years after he was dismissed, he became prime minister of Qin for the third time.
Four years later, Wei Ran sent Bai Qi to capture Chu's Ying capital, and Qin established Nanjun.
So he granted Bai Qi the title of Lord Wu'an.
Bai Qi is the general recommended by Marquis Rang, and they have a good relationship.
At that time, Marquis Rang's wealth even exceeded that of the monarch's family.
In the thirty-second year of King Zhao of Qin, Marquis Rang was appointed prime minister and led troops to attack Wei. Wei general Mangmao was defeated and fled, entered Beizhai, and then surrounded Daliang, the capital of Wei.
Xu Jia, a senior official in the Wei State, persuaded Marquis Rang: I heard an official from the Wei State say to the King of Wei: Once upon a time, King Hui of Liang attacked the State of Zhao, captured the Three Liangs, and captured Handan. However, King Zhao refused to cede the land even though he was defeated. Later, Handan was finally recovered.
The people of Qi attacked Wei, captured Chuqiu, the capital, and killed Ziliang; but the Wei people would never cede territory even if they were humiliated, and the capital they lost later still belonged to the Wei people.
The reason why Wei and Zhao have complete countries, strong armies, and their lands are not annexed by princes is because they can endure hardships and cherish every inch of their land.
Song and Zhongshan were invaded and ceded territory repeatedly, resulting in the country's immediate demise.
I think the practices of Wei and Zhao are worth emulating, while the practices of Song and Zhongshan should be taken as a warning.
Qin is a greedy, vicious and violent country. Don't get too close to it.
It encroached on the Wei State and swallowed up all the land that originally belonged to the Jin State. After defeating the Korean general Baoyuan, it took as many as eight counties. There was no time to incorporate all the land, so the army was dispatched again.
How can Qin be satisfied?
Now Mangmao was defeated and entered Beizhai. This was not because they wanted to attack the capital of Wei, but to threaten the king and ask for more land to be ceded.
Your Majesty, do not accept its request.
Now if the king abandons Chu and Zhao and makes peace with Qin, Chu and Zhao will definitely be resentful and betray the king, and compete with the king to serve Qin, and Qin will definitely accept it.
If Qin hijacks the armies of Chu and Zhao and then attacks Wei's capital, it will be impossible for Wei to survive.
I hope the king will not make peace.
If the king intends to make peace, he must cede less land and have hostages as guarantee; otherwise, he will definitely be deceived.
This is what I heard in Wei State. I hope you will consider besieging Daliang based on this. "Book of Zhou" says to remember that God's will is not fixed.
This means that God-given luck cannot be obtained multiple times. Qin's victory over Bao Yuan and the capture of eight counties was not due to superior military strength or clever strategies, but mainly to luck.
Now Qin defeated Mangmao again, marched into Beizhai, and then besieged Daliang. It seems that he took the good fortune of being in heaven as the norm. Wise people are not like this.
summary: In the 32nd year of King Zhao, while besieging Daliang, Wei Ran was persuaded by Wei official Xu Jia to withdraw, citing the risks of overextension and the wisdom of accepting smaller territorial concessions. Xu Jia argued that Qin's successes were due to luck, not superior strategy, and that attacking Daliang with 300,000 defenders was unwise. Wei Ran heeded this advice and lifted the siege.

translation:
Guan Zhong, whose name was Yiwu, was from Yingshang.
When he was young, he often interacted with Bao Shuya, and Bao Shuya knew that he was wise and talented.
Guan Zhong's family was poor and he often took advantage of Bao Shuya, but Bao Shuya was always very kind to Guan Zhong and had no complaints because of these things.
Soon, Bao Shuya served the young master Xiaobai of Qi State, and Guan Zhong served the young master Jiu.
After Xiaobai came to the throne and was established as Duke Huan of Qi, Duke Huan asked the state of Lu to kill Prince Jiu and Guan Zhong was imprisoned.
So Bao Shuya recommended Guan Zhong to Duke Huan of Qi.
After Guan Zhong was appointed, he came to power in Qi. Duke Huan relied on Guan Zhong to dominate, and as the overlord, he united with the princes many times to bring the world into unity. This was all achieved through Guan Zhong's wisdom.
Guan Zhong said: When I was poor, I used to do business together with Bao Shuya. When we shared the profits, I always asked for more. Bao Shuya did not think that I was greedy for money. He knew that my family was poor.
I once planned things for Bao Shuya, but it made him even more difficult and embarrassed. Bao Shuya didn't think I was stupid, because he knew that there were good times and bad times in fortune.
I had served as an official many times and was expelled by the king many times. Bao Shuya did not think that I had no talent. He knew that I had not met a good opportunity.
I have run away from many battles. Bao Shuya doesn't think I'm timid. He knows that I have an old mother at home who needs support.
Prince Jiu failed in the struggle for the throne of the king, Zhaohu died for him, and I was imprisoned and suffered humiliation. Bao Shuya did not think that I was a shameless person, because he knew that I was not ashamed of small mistakes, but felt ashamed of not being famous in the world.
It was my parents who gave birth to me, and it was Bao Shuya who really understood me.
After Bao Shuya recommended Guan Zhong, he was willing to work under Guan Zhong.
His descendants have enjoyed salaries in Qi for generations, and more than a dozen generations have received fiefs, most of whom are famous officials.
Therefore, people in the world did not praise Guan Zhong's talents, but praised Bao Shuya for his ability to recognize talents.
After Guan Zhong became the Prime Minister of Qi, he relied on the conditions of the small Qi State on the seaside to circulate goods and accumulate wealth, making the country rich and powerful, and sharing the same likes and dislikes with the people.
Therefore, he said in his book "Guanzi": Only when the warehouses are full of food can the people understand etiquette; when food and clothing are abundant, can the people distinguish between honor and disgrace; only when the king's actions are in line with the law can the six relatives be stable; if etiquette, justice and integrity are not promoted and carried forward, the country will perish.
Government decrees issued by the state are like the source of flowing water, flowing down the minds of the people.
Therefore, government orders can be easily implemented if they are consistent with the situation.
Whatever the people want, give it to them; whatever the people object to, abolish it.
When Guan Zhong was in power, he was good at turning disaster into good fortune and failure into success.
He pays attention to the priorities of things and carefully weighs the pros and cons of things.
Duke Huan of Qi actually resented Shaoji's remarriage and wanted to attack Cai. Guan Zhong took this opportunity to attack Chu and blamed it for not paying tribute to the Zhou royal family.
Duke Huan actually wanted to send troops to the north to attack Shanrong, but Guan Zhong took the opportunity to let Yan rebuild the political and religious system of the Zhaogong period.
During the alliance meeting at Ke, Duke Huan wanted to break the treaty that Cao Mo had forced him to make, but Guan Zhong followed the situation and persuaded him to abide by the treaty, and the princes therefore submitted to Qi.
Therefore, it is said: Knowing that giving is just for getting, this is the magic weapon for governing the country.
Guan Zhong's wealth was comparable to that of the monarch, and he had a gorgeous Sangui Terrace and banquet facilities for the monarch, but the people of Qi did not think that he was extravagant and arrogant.
After Guan Zhong's death, Qi still followed his policies and was often stronger than other vassal states.
More than a hundred years later, Yan Ying came out of Qi State.
Yan Pingzhong, named Ying, was a Yiwei native of Lai, Qi State.
He assisted three generations of Qi Dukes Linggong, Zhuanggong and Jinggong. He was respected by people in Qi because of his frugality and hard work.
When he became the prime minister of Qi, he did not eat more than two kinds of meat at each meal, and his wives and concubines did not wear silk clothes.
summary: Guan Zhong, also known as Yiwu, was from Yingshang. In his youth, he frequently interacted with Bao Shuya, who recognized his wisdom and talent. Despite Guan Zhong's poverty and tendency to take advantage of him, Bao Shuya remained kind and without complaint. Bao Shuya later served Prince Xiaobai of Qi, while Guan Zhong served Prince Jiu. After Xiaobai became Duke Huan of Qi, he had Prince Jiu killed and imprisoned Guan Zhong. Bao Shuya then recommended Guan Zhong to Duke Huan. Appointed to power, Guan Zhong helped Duke Huan become an overlord, uniting the princes and bringing order to the realm through his wisdom. Guan Zhong reflected that Bao Shuya never judged him harshly: when Guan Zhong took more profit in their business, Bao Shuya understood his poverty; when his plans failed, Bao Shuya knew fortune's ups and downs; when he was dismissed from office, Bao Shuya saw missed opportunities; when he fled battles, Bao Shuya recognized his duty to his mother; when he endured imprisonment, Bao Shuya knew he valued fame over minor shame. Guan Zhong declared, "My parents gave me life, but Bao Shuya truly understands me." After recommending Guan Zhong, Bao Shuya served under him. Their descendants received fiefs for generations, producing many famous officials. The world praised Bao Shuya's ability to recognize talent over Guan Zhong's abilities. As Prime Minister, Guan Zhong enriched Qi by circulating goods and accumulating wealth, aligning with the people's desires. He wrote that ample food leads to understanding etiquette, and abundant clothing allows distinction between honor and disgrace. He emphasized that government decrees should flow like water, easily implemented when consistent with circumstances. He turned disaster into fortune and failure into success, such as using Duke Huan's desire to attack Cai as an opportunity to blame Chu for not paying tribute to Zhou, or persuading Duke Huan to honor a treaty at Ke, winning the princes' submission. Guan Zhong's wealth rivaled a monarch's, but the people did not consider him extravagant. After his death, Qi followed his policies and remained strong.
