translation:
In the court, if the king's words involve him, he should express his opinions honestly; if the king's words do not involve him, he should act honestly.
If the king can do the right thing, he should follow his orders. If he can't do the right way, he can act according to his orders.
Therefore, during the three generations of Qi Linggong, Zhuanggong and Jinggong, his reputation was well-known among the princes of various countries.
Yue Shi's father is a talented man who is being imprisoned and serving hard labor.
Yanzi went out and met him on the road. He untied the horse on the left side of the carriage, ransomed him, and then drove him home.
After leaving Taoism, Yan Zi went into the inner room without saying goodbye to Yue Shi's father. After a long time, Yue Shi's father asked to break off the relationship with Yan Zi.
Yanzi was shocked, and hurriedly packed his clothes and apologized, saying: Even though I can't be said to be kind and generous, I finally helped you get out of your predicament. Why did you ask to break off the relationship so quickly?
Father Yue Shi said: That's not the case. I heard that a gentleman will be wronged by people who don't understand him, but his will will be upheld in front of people who understand him.
When I was in captivity, those people didn't understand me.
Since you have been moved and awakened, and bought me out, this means you understand me; if you understand me but do not treat me politely, it is better to let me continue to be imprisoned and serve as a slave.
So Yanzi invited him into the house and treated him as an honored guest.
When Yanzi was the prime minister of Qi, he was going out in a carriage. The coachman's wife secretly looked at her husband through the crack in the door.
He saw his husband driving the car for the prime minister, with a big umbrella covering his head, waving a whip and driving four horses, looking very proud and proud.
Soon after returning home, his wife asked to leave him. The coachman asked her why she left. The wife said: Yanzi was only six feet tall, but he became the prime minister of Qi State and his reputation was famous in various countries. I saw that when he went out, his ambitions and thoughts were very deep, and he often had the attitude of being inferior to others.
Now you are eight feet tall and can only be a coachman. Judging from your expression, you think you are quite satisfied, so I beg you to let me leave.
From then on, the coachman became humble and respectful.
Yanzi noticed his change and felt strange, so he asked him about it, and the driver told him the truth.
Yanzi recommended him to become a doctor.
Tai Shigong said: I have read Guan Zhong's "Herdsmen", "High Mountains", "Riding Horses", "Light and Heavy", "Jiufu" and "Yanzi Chunqiu". These books are really written in too much detail!
After reading their works, I also wanted people to know about their deeds, so I wrote biographies for them in turn.
As for their works, there are already many in the society, so I will not discuss them here, but only record their unknown things.
Guan Zhong is what the world calls a virtuous minister, but Confucius despises him. Is it because the Zhou Dynasty's rule is declining? Since Huan Gong is a virtuous minister, Guan Zhong does not encourage him to practice the royal way but assists him to become the overlord?
An old saying goes: It is necessary to take advantage of the situation to help cultivate a gentleman's virtues and correct his mistakes, so that the monarch, his ministers and the people can be close to each other.
This is probably Guan Zhong, right?
summary: More than a century later, Yan Ying, also known as Yanzi, emerged from Qi. He served Dukes Ling, Zhuang, and Jing, respected for his frugality and hard work. As prime minister, he ate no more than two meats and his family wore no silk. He acted honestly in court and followed orders when the ruler was righteous. Yanzi once ransomed Yue Shi's father from imprisonment. When Yue Shi's father criticized Yanzi for not treating him politely after understanding him, Yanzi apologized and honored him as a guest. Yanzi's coachman, initially proud, became humble after his wife threatened to leave him for his arrogance compared to Yanzi's modesty. Yanzi recommended the coachman to become a doctor. Tai Shigong noted that he read Guan Zhong's and Yanzi's works but focused on their unknown deeds. He questioned whether Confucius despised Guan Zhong for not encouraging Duke Huan to practice the kingly way, instead assisting him as an overlord. He praised Yanzi for crying over Duke Zhuang's body and daring to offend the monarch, expressing a wish to serve Yanzi if he were alive.

translation:
I am a native of Qurenli, Li Township, Kuxian County, Chu State. His surname was Li, his given name was Er, and his courtesy name was Dan. He was a historian in charge of the library in the Zhou Dynasty.
Confucius went to the capital of Zhou and wanted to ask Laozi about etiquette.
Lao Tzu said: The etiquette you are talking about, the person and the bones of the person who advocated it have rotted away, only his words remain.
Moreover, a gentleman will drive his car and go out to be an official when his fortune comes. If he is born at the wrong time, he will be blown away by the wind like a fluffy grass.
I have heard that people who are good at business hide their goods as if they were nothing. A gentleman has a noble character, but his appearance is as humble as a dull person.
Abandon your arrogance and excessive desires, abandon your artificial moods and unrealistic ambitions, these are not good for yourself.
That's all I can tell you.
After Confucius left, he said to his disciples: I know birds are good at flying; fish, I know they are good at swimming; animals, I know they are good at running.
Those that can run can weave a net to catch it, those that can swim can be made into silk thread to catch it, and those that can fly can shoot it with arrows.
As for the dragon, I don't know what to do. It is said that it rides the wind and soars into the sky.
The Lao Tzu I saw today probably looks like a dragon!
Lao Tzu studied moral knowledge, and his teachings aimed at concealing traces and not seeking to be heard.
He lived in Zhoudu for a long time. Seeing that the Zhou Dynasty was declining, he left Zhoudu.
When he arrived at Hangu Pass, Guan Ling Yinxi said to him: You are going to live in seclusion and try your best to write a book for us.
So I wrote a book, divided into two parts, expounding the original meaning of morality, with a total of more than 5,000 words. Then I left. No one knows where he went in the end.
Some people say: Lao Laizi was also from the Chu state. He wrote fifteen books on how to apply Taoist knowledge. He was a contemporary of Confucius.
It is said that I lived for more than 160 years, and some people say that I lived for more than 200 years. This is because he can cultivate his mind and live a long life.
One hundred and twenty-nine years after the death of Confucius, historical records record that when Taishi Dan of Zhou met with Duke Xiang of Qin, he prophesied: When the Qin State and the Zhou Dynasty were united, they were united for five hundred years and then separated. After seventy years of separation, there will be people who will become kings and hegemons.
Some people say that Taishi Dan is Lao Tzu, and some people say that he is not. No one in the world knows which statement is correct.
In short, I am a true hidden gentleman.
Lao Tzu's son is called Li Zong. He served as a general of Wei State and his fiefdom was in Duanqian.
Li Zong's son is called Li Zhu, Li Zhu's son is called Li Gong, and Li Gong's great-great-grandson is called Li Jie. Li Jie served as an official during the reign of Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty.
Li Jie's son Li Jie served as the Taifu of Jiaoxi King Liu Xuan, so the Li family settled in Qidi.
Anyone in the world who studies Laozi's knowledge will disparage Confucian thought and doctrine; and those who study Confucianism will also disparage Laozi's doctrine. People with different opinions cannot agree with each other. Is this the case?
Lao Tzu believes that if you govern by doing nothing, the people will naturally become corrupt; if you are quiet and do nothing, the people will naturally return to righteousness.
summary: A biographical account of Laozi, a native of Chu State who served as a Zhou dynasty librarian. When Confucius sought his advice on etiquette, Laozi dismissed the topic, noting that its proponents had long since perished, and advised Confucius to abandon arrogance and excessive desires. Confucius later likened Laozi to a dragon, elusive and transcendent. Laozi, observing Zhou's decline, wrote a book of over 5,000 words on morality at the request of a gatekeeper before disappearing. Some claim he lived over 160 years, while others identify him with the historian Taishi Dan, who prophesied about Qin and Zhou's future. Laozi's son, Li Zong, became a Wei general, and his descendants served in Han times. The text contrasts Laozi's philosophy of non-action with Confucianism, noting mutual criticism between followers.

translation:
Zhuangzi was a native of Mengyi, and his name was Zhuangzhou.
He once served as a minor official in Mengdi Lacquer Garden, and was a contemporary of King Hui of Liang and King Xuan of Qi.
He is knowledgeable and has covered all-encompassing areas of research, but his central idea originated from the teachings of Laozi.
He wrote more than 100,000 words of works, most of which are allegorical fables. He wrote "The Fisherman", "The Stealer" and "The Suit" were used to slander the Confucius school of thought. The purpose is to express Laozi's teachings.
"Wei Leixu" and "Kang Sangzi" are all made up out of thin air and have no basis in fact.
However, Zhuangzi was good at writing words and describing the situation of things to attack and refute Confucianism and Mohism. Even the most knowledgeable people in the world were inevitably attacked by him.
His language was vast, arbitrary, and arbitrary, and he spoke casually, so no one from the princes to the princes wanted to reuse him.
King Wei of Chu heard that Zhuang Zhou was a capable man and sent envoys with generous gifts to hire him and promised him to be the prime minister of Chu.
Zhuang Zhou smiled and said to the Chu envoy: A thousand pieces of gold is indeed a generous gift; the minister is indeed a noble and high position.
Have you never seen the cattle used in sacrifices to heaven and earth?
After feeding it for several years, covering it with patterned silk and satin, and taking it to the Ancestral Temple as a sacrifice, at this time, even if it wants to be a lonely little pig, can it be done?
Please leave quickly and don't taint me.
I would rather play happily in the ditch than be bound by the king. I will not be an official for the rest of my life to make myself happy.
Shen Buhai was a native of Jingyi and was originally a low-level official in the state of Zheng.
Later, he studied the knowledge of criminal names and magic, and asked for an official position from Han Zhaohou, who appointed him as prime minister.
He cultivated politics and religion internally and dealt with the princes externally. He was in power for fifteen years.
Until the death of Shenzi, Korea was well governed, with clear politics and a strong military. No country dared to invade Korea.
The origin of Shen Buhai's theory is Huangdi and Laozi, who mainly follow the name and fulfill the responsibility. He has two works called "Shenzi".
Han Fei is a Korean son.
He likes the knowledge of criminal names and magic. The theoretical basis of his theory comes from the theories of Huangdi and Laozi.
Han Fei has a stuttering defect and is not good at speaking, but he is good at writing books and explaining things.
He and Li Si were both students of Xun Qing, and Li Si thought he was not as knowledgeable as Han Fei.
Seeing that South Korea was gradually weakening, Han Fei repeatedly wrote to the King of Han to persuade him, but the King of Han did not adopt his opinions.
Under this situation, Han Fei hated that the monarch who governed the country did not devote himself to improving the legal system, could not use the power in the king's hands to control his ministers, could not enrich the country and strengthen the army, and sought to appoint virtuous people. Instead, he appointed literary lobbyists who were rhetorical and harmful to the country, and made their status higher than those who emphasized utilitarianism and effectiveness.
He believed that Confucians used classic texts to disrupt state laws, while knights violated state prohibitions by using force.
When the country is at peace, the monarch will favor those who have false reputations. When the situation is critical, he will use those armored warriors.
summary: Zhuangzi, from Mengyi, served as a minor official and wrote extensively in allegorical style, critiquing Confucianism and Mohism. He rejected a lucrative offer from King Wei of Chu, preferring freedom over officialdom. Shen Buhai, a Zheng native, studied legalist philosophy and served as Han prime minister for 15 years, strengthening the state. Han Fei, a Korean prince and student of Xun Qing, wrote prolifically on legalism, including works like "Shuo Nan" on the difficulties of persuasion. Despite his insights, Han Fei was executed in Qin after being slandered by Li Si and Yao Jia. The text details the perils of lobbying, using historical anecdotes to illustrate how understanding a ruler's psychology is crucial. It concludes with Sima Qian's reflections, praising Laozi's profound teachings, Zhuangzi's freedom, Shenzi's diligence, and Hanzi's legal rigor, while lamenting Han Fei's tragic fate.

translation:
Su Qin was a native of Luoyang in the Eastern Zhou Dynasty. He went east to Qi State to study under Mr. Guiguzi.
After traveling for many years, he was impoverished and returned home in embarrassment.
Brothers and sisters-in-law, younger brothers and sisters, wives and concubines all laughed at him privately, saying: "It is the custom of the Zhou people that people manage their industries, work hard in industry and commerce, and pursue the two-tenths of profits as their career."
Now you have abandoned your profession and gone to talk, and you are in poverty, isn't that right?
After hearing these words, Su Qin felt secretly ashamed and sad, so he stayed behind closed doors and read all his books.
Said: Since a scholar has been taught by a teacher and immersed himself in reading, but he cannot obtain status and glory through it, no matter how much he reads, what is the use?
So I found a book called "Yin Fu" and sat down at my desk to study it.
After working hard for a whole year, he searched for the truth and found a way to get along with the king. He said excitedly: With these alone, I can persuade the king of today.
He asked to see and lobby King Xian of Zhou.
However, the ministers around King Xian always knew Su Qin's character and looked down upon him. Therefore, King Xian of Zhou did not trust him either.
So he went west to the state of Qin.
Duke Xiao of Qin is dead.
He persuaded King Hui and said: Qin is a country surrounded by dangerous mountains. The Wei River flows like a belt, with Hangu Pass and the Yellow River in the east, Hanzhong in the west, Bashu in the south, Daima and Mayi in the north. This is really a dangerous, fertile and abundant natural treasury.
With its numerous people and well-trained soldiers, the Qin State was able to annex the world, establish an empire, and rule all directions.
King Hui of Qin said: It is impossible for a bird to fly in the sky before its feathers are full; the country's political and religious affairs are not on the right track, and it is impossible to annex the world.
At this time, the state of Qin had just executed Shang Yang and hated the lobbyists very much, so it did not appoint Su Qin.
So, he went east to the state of Zhao.
Zhao Suhou appointed his younger brother Zhao Cheng as the prime minister of the country, with the title Fengyang Jun.
Lord Fengyang doesn't like Su Qin.
Su Qin left Zhao State again and traveled to Yan State. It took more than a year before he had the opportunity to meet Yan Wenhou.
He advised Marquis Wen of Yan: The country of Yan is bounded by Korea and Liaodong to the east, Linhu and Loufan to the north, Yunzhong and Jiuyuan to the west, and Tuohe and Yishui to the south. The country stretches for more than two thousand miles, has hundreds of thousands of soldiers, 600 chariots, and 6,000 horses, and has enough food stored for several years.
In the south, the land in Jieshi Mountain and Yanmen Mountain is fertile and rich in products; in the north, you can grow red dates and chestnuts to gain income. Even if the people do not farm, the income from red dates and chestnuts alone can ensure that they live a prosperous life.
This is the so-called natural treasury.
The people can live and work in peace and contentment, there is no war, and they will not face the danger of the army being destroyed and the generals and soldiers being killed. No one can compare with the Yan State in this regard.
Does your Majesty know the reason for this?
The reason why Yan State was not invaded by enemies was that Zhao State was Yan State's barrier in the south.
summary: Su Qin, a native of Luoyang in the Eastern Zhou Dynasty, studied under Mr. Guiguzi in Qi State. After years of travel left him impoverished, he returned home in embarrassment, where his family mocked him for abandoning practical trades to pursue rhetoric. Ashamed, he secluded himself to study, discovering the "Yin Fu" text. After a year of intense effort, he sought to persuade rulers. He first approached King Xian of Zhou, but was dismissed due to the ministers' disdain. He then went west to Qin, where King Hui declined his advice, citing the state's recent execution of Shang Yang and distrust of lobbyists.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/苏秦列传

translation:
Qin and Zhao launched five wars, Qin won twice and Zhao won three times.
The two countries are killing each other and destroying each other, but the king can rely on the intact power of the Yan State to control them from behind. This is the reason why the Yan State is not invaded by enemy countries.
Moreover, if Qin wanted to attack Yan, it would have to travel through Yunzhong and Jiuyuan, pass through Daijun and Shanggu, and travel thousands of miles. Even if it could capture Yan's city, Qin would consider that it had no way to defend it.
It is already very obvious that Qin cannot invade Yan.
Now that the State of Zhao wants to attack the State of Yan, as long as it issues an order, it will not take ten days for hundreds of thousands of troops to be stationed in the Donghuan area on the border. The Zhao army will then cross the Tuo River and ford the Yishui River. It will not take more than four or five days to reach the capital of the State of Yan.
Therefore, when Qin attacked Yan, it had to fight thousands of miles away; when Zhao attacked Yan, it only fought within a hundred miles.
There is no more wrong strategy than not worrying about disasters within a hundred miles, but focusing on enemies thousands of miles away.
Therefore, I hope that your Majesty can unite with the State of Zhao and unite all countries into one, so that there will be no trouble for the State of Yan.
Marquis Yan Wen said: Of course you are right, but my country is weak, close to the powerful Zhao State in the west, and close to Qi and Zhou in the south. Qi and Zhao are both powerful countries.
You must use the method of marriage and marriage to make the Yan country safe and sound. I am willing to surrender the country to you.
So he funded Su Qin's carriage, horses and money to travel to Zhao.
Lord Fengyang was dead, so he took the opportunity to lobby Zhao Suhou: "Every minister in the world, right down to the scholars in rough clothes, all admire you as a wise king for your benevolence and righteousness, and they all hope to listen to your teachings and give your loyal advice in front of you. It has been a long time."
Even so, Lord Fengyang is jealous of talents and you ignore political affairs, so no guests or lobbyists dare to speak freely in front of you.
Now that Lord Fengyang has passed away, you can get close to the scholars and the people again, so I dare to state my humble opinion to you.
I think for you privately, there is nothing more important than the peace of the people's lives, the peace of the country, and the absence of the need for the people to be involved in wars.
The foundation for the stability of the people lies in the choice of diplomatic relations. If the diplomatic relations are properly chosen, the people will be stable; if the diplomatic relations are not chosen appropriately, the people will be unstable for life.
Please allow me to analyze Zhao's foreign aggression: If Zhao is enemies with Qi and Qin, the people will not have peace. If they rely on Qin to attack Qi, the people will not have peace. If they rely on Qi to attack Qin, the people will still have no peace.
Therefore, if you want to plot against the kings of other countries and attack other countries, you often have to publicly declare to sever diplomatic relations with other countries. I hope you will be careful and don't say this easily.
Please let me analyze for you the pros and cons of this extremely clear black and white, yin and yang.
summary: Su Qin next traveled to Zhao, but Lord Fengyang disliked him, so he proceeded to Yan. After over a year, he met Marquis Wen of Yan, arguing that Yan's safety depended on Zhao as a southern barrier. He noted that Qin would struggle to attack Yan from afar, while Zhao could strike within days. He urged an alliance with Zhao to secure Yan. Marquis Wen agreed, funding Su Qin's mission to Zhao. There, Lord Fengyang had died, so Su Qin lobbied Zhao Suhou, emphasizing the importance of diplomatic choices for stability. He proposed a united front of six states against Qin, detailing how each state would support the others if attacked. King Zhao accepted, providing resources for Su Qin to persuade other states.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/苏秦列传

translation:
I heard that Tang Yao was not given a reward of 300 acres, and Yu Shun was not given a foot of fiefdom, but he could own the whole world; Yu and Xia could become king among the princes with less than a hundred people; Shang Tang and Zhou Wu had less than 3,000 ministers, less than 300 chariots, and less than 30,000 soldiers, but they could become the emperor: they have indeed mastered the strategy of conquering the world.
Therefore, a wise monarch should be able to predict the strength of the enemy's country externally, and estimate the quality of his soldiers internally. In this way, the key to victory, defeat, and survival will already be clear to him without waiting for the armies of both sides to come into contact. How could one be blinded by everyone's opinions and make decisions on national affairs in a confused manner?
I have privately examined the map of the world. The land of each vassal state is five times that of Qin. It is estimated that the soldiers of each vassal state are ten times that of Qin. If the six countries form a whole and work together to attack Qin westward, Qin will definitely be defeated.
Now, instead, he serves Qin in the west and becomes a minister of Qin.
Defeating others and being defeated by others, asking others to surrender to oneself and oneself to surrendering to others, are they the same thing?
Anyone who advocates the policy of continuous balance wants to cede the land of various vassal states to Qin.
When Qin's hegemony is successful, they can build tall pavilions and pavilions, build magnificent palaces, and enjoy the music played by the lute. There are balconies and palaces in front, and spacious and gorgeous cars; behind there are graceful and beautiful beauties. As for the harm done by Qin to other countries, they will not share their worries.
Therefore, those who advocate Lianheng rely on the power of Qin to threaten the princes and countries day and night and seek to cede land. Therefore, I hope your Majesty will consider it carefully.
I heard that a wise monarch resolves doubts, rejects slander, abandons the channels of gossip, and blocks the channels of partying and selfish pursuits. That is why I have the opportunity to state before you the strategy to honor the monarch, expand the territory, and strengthen the army.
Privately, I think for your Majesty, it is better to make Han, Wei, Qi, Chu, Yan, and Zhao form a coherent whole to fight against Qin.
Let the generals of the world gather on the Huan River, communicate with each other about their old grudges, kill the white horse and swear a blood oath, and agree with each other: If Qin attacks Chu, then Qi and Wei will send elite troops to help Chu, South Korea will cut off Qin's main grain transportation route, Zhao's army will cross the river to the south to support, and Yan's army will stick to the north of Changshan.
If Qin attacks South Korea and Wei, then the Chu army will cut off Qin's support, and Qi will send elite troops to help Han and Wei. Zhao Jun crossed the river and Zhang to support, while Yan Guo held on to the Yunzhong area.
If Qin attacks Qi, Chu will cut off Qin's support, South Korea will defend Chenggao, Wei will block Qin's main roads, Zhao's army will cross the river and Zhang to advance to Boguan for support, and Yan will send elite troops to coordinate operations.
If the Qin State attacks the Yan State, then the Zhao State will stick to Changshan, the Chu State troops will be stationed in Wuguan, the Qi Army will cross the Bohai Sea, and Han and Wei will send elite troops to coordinate the battle.
If Qin attacks Zhao, South Korea's troops will be stationed in Yiyang, Chu's troops will be stationed in Wuguan, Wei's troops will be stationed outside the river, Qi's troops will cross the Qinghe River, and Yan's elite troops will be sent to coordinate operations.
If some princes do not act in accordance with the covenant, the armies of the other five countries will be used to attack him.
If the six kingdoms were united to resist Qin, then Qin would not dare to send troops from Hanguguan to invade the six kingdoms of Shandong.
In this way, your overlord's cause is successful.
King Zhao said: I am still young and have only been in charge of the country for a short time. I have never heard of strategies for long-term peace and stability in the country.
Now that you intend to ensure the survival of the world and the stability of the various vassal states, I am willing to sincerely surrender to you.
So he decorated a hundred carriages, loaded with a thousand pieces of gold, a hundred pairs of white jade stones, and a thousand bolts of silk and satin, to persuade the vassal states to join.
At this time, the Emperor of Zhou gave King Hui of Qin the meat used in sacrifices to King Wen and King Wu.
King Hui sent rhinoceros heads to attack Wei, captured Wei general Long Jia alive, captured Wei's Diaoyin, and planned to march eastward.
Su Qin was afraid that Qin's troops would attack Zhao, so he used a trick to anger Zhang Yi and force him to defect to Qin.
So Su Qin went to persuade King Xuan of Han and said: Korea has strong Gongyi and Chenggao in the north, the fortresses of Yiyang and Shangban in the west, Wan, Rang, and Mishui in the east, and Xingshan in the south. The area is more than 900 miles in length and breadth, and there are hundreds of thousands of armed forces. All the strong bows and crossbows in the world are made from Korea.
summary: Su Qin then approached King Xuan of Han, highlighting Korea's military strength and warning that serving Qin would lead to endless land demands. King Han angrily refused to serve Qin. He similarly persuaded King Wei of Wei, stressing Wei's power and the folly of ceding land to Qin. King Wei agreed to follow Su Qin's plan. In Qi, he advised King Xuan that Qin could not easily attack Qi due to geographical barriers, and that serving Qin was a strategic error. King Qi consented. Finally, he lobbied King Wei of Chu, arguing that Chu and Qin could not coexist and that alliance would bring glory. King Wei, fearing Qin's ambition, entrusted his state to Su Qin.

translation:
I couldn't sleep well while lying on the bed, and I couldn't feel the sweetness when I ate. My mind was in a trance, like a flag hanging in the sky with no where to go.
Now that you intend to unify the world, unite the princes, and preserve the country in danger, I am willing to respectfully entrust the entire country to you and obey your arrangements.
As a result, the six countries united successfully and worked together.
Su Qin became the leader of the United Vertical Alliance and concurrently served as the Prime Minister of the Six Nations.
Su Qin went north to return his order to King Zhao. On the way, he passed Luoyang. The accompanying vehicles and horses were fully loaded with luggage. There were many envoys sent by the princes to see him off, and they were as grand as the emperor.
King Xian of Zhou Dynasty was frightened when he heard the news. He quickly found someone to clear the road for him and sent envoys to the suburbs to greet him.
Su Qin's brothers, wife, and sister-in-law squinted and did not dare to look up at him. They all fell down on the ground and served him with great respect.
Su Qin smiled and said to his sister-in-law: Why were you so arrogant to me before, but now you are so deferential to me?
His sister-in-law quickly fell to the ground, bent her body, and crawled in front of him. She put her face to the ground and apologized, saying: "Because I saw that uncle, you have a high status and a lot of money."
Su Qin sighed with emotion and said: I am the same person. When I am rich, my relatives will respect me, but when I am poor, they will despise me. Not to mention ordinary people!
If I had two hectares of fertile farmland in the suburbs of Luoyang back then, would I still be able to wear the seals of six countries now?
At that time, he distributed thousands of gold coins and gave them to relatives and friends.
When Su Qin went to the State of Yan, he borrowed one hundred gold from someone for travel expenses. Now that he was rich, he borrowed one hundred gold to repay that person.
And he repaid all those who had been kind to him in the past.
Among his entourage, there was only one person who did not receive the reward, so he went forward to plead his case.
Su Qin said: "I have not forgotten you. When you came to Yan State with me, you tried to leave me again and again by the Yishui River. At that time, I was in dire straits, so I deeply blamed you, so I put you last. Now you can also get the reward." After Su Qin agreed on the alliance of the six countries, he returned to the State of Zhao. Marquis Su of Zhao named him Lord Wu'an, so Su Qin sent the alliance to Qin.
From then on, Qin State did not dare to spy on countries outside Hangu Pass for fifteen years.
Later, Qin State sent envoy Xishou to deceive Qi State and Wei State, and joined forces with them to attack Zhao State, intending to destroy the alliance.
Qi and Wei attacked Zhao, and the king of Zhao blamed Su Qin.
Su Qin was afraid and asked to send an envoy to Yan State to take revenge on Qi State.
After Su Qin left Zhao, the alliance collapsed.
King Hui of Qin married his daughter to the prince of Yan as his wife.
In this year, Marquis Wen of Yan died and the prince ascended the throne. This was King Yi of Yan.
King Yi had just ascended the throne, and King Xuan of Qi took advantage of Yan's mourning to attack Yan and captured ten cities in a row.
summary: The six states united, with Su Qin as their leader and prime minister. On his return to Luoyang, his family, once scornful, now bowed in awe. He distributed wealth to relatives and repaid debts. The alliance kept Qin from invading for fifteen years. However, Qin later deceived Qi and Wei into attacking Zhao, breaking the pact. Su Qin fled to Yan, where King Yi sought his help to recover ten cities lost to Qi. Su Qin persuaded King Qi to return them by warning of Qin's enmity. Despite slander, Su Qin regained King Yan's trust, though he had an affair with the king's mother. Fearing death, he feigned offense and fled to Qi, where he served as a guest minister. He secretly plotted to weaken Qi for Yan, advising King Min to waste resources on grand projects. Eventually, rivals assassinated him. Before dying, he told King Qi to display his body publicly, promising the assassin would be caught. The ruse worked, and the assassin was executed.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/苏秦列传

translation:
Later, the Qin State captured Anyi of the Wei State and besieged Nuji. Instead, it regarded the defeat of the Song State as Qi's crime.
Qin planned to attack South Korea and was worried that the princes of the world would rescue it, so it promised Qi to the princes of the world to attack it, saying: The king of Qi made an alliance with me four times, deceived me four times, and resolutely led the army of the world to attack our country, many times.
As long as Qi exists, there will be no Qin. As long as Qin exists, there will be no Qi. It must be conquered and destroyed.
When the Qin State captured Yiyang and Shaoqu in South Korea and conquered Linyi and Lishi, it regarded defeating the Qi State as a sin among the vassal states in the world. Qin planned to attack Wei, so he first respected Chu and promised Nanyang to Chu.
Said: I had already severed ties with South Korea.
If it is beneficial to the state of Chu to destroy Junling and besiege it, then I will be as happy as if I had it.
When the state of Wei abandoned the alliance and joined forces with the state of Qin, the state of Qin charged Chu with siege.
Qin's army was trapped in the forest, so he respected Yan and Zhao, and promised Jiaodong to Yan and Jixi to Zhao.
When Qin and Wei reconciled, they took Gongzi Yan as a hostage and used rhinoceros troops to attack Zhao one after another.
Qin's army suffered heavy losses at Qiaoshi and was defeated at Yangma, so he respected Wei and granted the land of Ye and Cai to Wei.
After he reconciled with Zhao, he threatened Wei and refused to divide the land as agreed.
When the Qin army was in trouble, they sent the Queen Mother's brother Ranghou to make peace. When he won, even his uncle and mother were deceived.
Outside Xihe, the Shangluo area and Sanchuan area are often attacked by the Qin State. This is a disaster for the Jin State!
The Qin State invaded half of the land of Han, Zhao, and Wei. The disasters caused by the Qin State were so serious! However, people from Yan, Zhao and other countries who went to Qin to persuade their kings tried to persuade their own monarchs by serving Qin. This is something that worries me very much.
King Yan Zhao did not go to Qin, and Su Dai was reused by King Yan again.
The King of Yan sent Su Dai to contact the various countries to unite and establish a blind date. Just like when Su Qin was alive, some princes joined the alliance and some did not. People from all over the world respected the alliance advocated by Su Qin from then on.
Both Su Dai and Su Li lived to a very old age, and their reputations became prominent in various vassal states.
Tai Shigong said: The three brothers Su and Qin are famous all over the world for lobbying the princes. Their theories are good at maneuvering and maneuvering.
However, Su Qin was killed on the charge of counter-intentional conspiracy. Everyone in the world laughed at him and tabooed the study of his teachings.
However, there are many differences in the deeds of Su Qin circulated in society. All deeds similar to Su Qin in different periods are attached to Su Qin.
Su Qin was born among the common people, but he was able to unite six countries and have a blind date. This shows that his intelligence is beyond ordinary people. Therefore, I will list his experiences and state them in the correct chronological order, so as not to let him only suffer a bad reputation.
summary: Su Qin's brothers, Su Dai and Su Li, later pursued similar careers. After Su Qin's death, Su Dai served Yan, advising King Yan on strategy against Qi. He noted Qi's exhaustion from wars and suggested using bribes to manipulate Qi into attacking Song, weakening itself. King Yan agreed. Su Li also served Qi, but faced suspicion due to Su Qin's past. The brothers eventually fled to Qi after Yan's internal chaos. Su Dai later returned to Yan, helping King Zhao plan and execute a successful attack on Qi, forcing King Min to flee. Su Dai later advised King Yan against visiting Qin, warning of Qin's violent tactics. King Yan heeded this advice. Both Su Dai and Su Li lived to old age, renowned for their diplomatic skills. The historian concludes that the Su brothers were famous for their lobbying, but Su Qin's death from conspiracy led to widespread ridicule. However, his ability to unite six states from humble origins shows extraordinary intelligence. The historian compiled his deeds in correct order to preserve his legacy.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/苏秦列传

translation:
He lobbied the princes and wanted to serve the king of Wei, but his family was very poor and had no way to raise funds, so he first went to serve Xu Jia, a senior official in the state of Wei.
Once, Xu Jia went to Qi State as an envoy for King Zhao of Wei, and Fan Ju also went with him.
They stayed in Qi for several months, but were unable to complete their mission.
At that time, King Qi Xiang learned that Fan Ju was very eloquent, so he sent a special person to give Fan Ju gifts such as ten pounds of gold, beef and wine, but Fan Ju repeatedly refused and did not dare to accept.
When Xu Jia found out about this, he was very angry. He thought that Fan Ju must have sold the secrets he knew about Wei to Qi, so he got such a gift. So he asked Fan Ju to accept food such as beef, wine, and return the gold.
After returning to the state of Wei, Xu Jia was angry and jealous of Fan Ju, so he reported the matter to the prime minister of the state of Wei.
The prime minister of Wei State is one of the sons of Wei State, named Wei Qi.
Wei Qi was furious after hearing this, and ordered his ministers to beat Fan Ju with boards and thorns, breaking Fan Ju's ribs and teeth.
At that time, Fan Ju pretended to be dead, so Wei Qi sent someone to roll him up in a mat and threw him in the toilet.
He also made the guests at the banquet drunk and took turns urinating on Fan Ju, deliberately humiliating him to punish the police and prevent people from revealing state secrets.
Fan Ju, who was wrapped in the mat, said to the guard: "If you let me go, I will thank you very much in the future."
The guard wanted to let Fan Ju go, so he asked Wei Qi for instructions to throw the dead people out of the mat.
Wei Qi was already very drunk at this time, so he agreed smoothly and said: "Okay."
Fan Ju was able to escape.
Later Wei Qi regretted it and sent people to search for Fan Ju again.
Zheng Anping, a native of Wei, heard about this, so he ran away with Fan Ju. They hid, and Fan Ju changed his name to Zhang Lu.
At this time, King Zhao of Qin sent his envoy Wang Jizheng to Wei.
Zheng Anping pretended to be a servant and served Wang Ji.
Wang Ji asked him: "Would any of the talented people in Wei State be willing to travel with me to the Qin State in the west?"
Zheng Anping replied: There is a Mr. Zhang Lu in my hometown who would like to see you and discuss world affairs with you.
However, he has enemies and dare not come out to meet you during the day.
Wang Ji said: You should come with him at night.
Zheng Anping brought Zhang Lu to visit Wang Ji at night.
Before the two of them finished talking, Wang Ji realized that Fan Ju was a talented person, so he said to him: Sir, please wait for me south of Santang Gang.
Fan Ju and Wang Ji made a private appointment to meet and left.
After Wang Ji said goodbye to Wei and went on the road, when he passed the south of Sanding Gang, he loaded up Fan Ju and quickly entered the border of Qin.
When the car arrived at Huyi, we saw a group of carriages and horses galloping from the west.
Fan Ju asked: "Who is coming over there?"
Wang Ji replied: That was when Ranghou, the Prime Minister of Qin State, went to the east to inspect the counties and cities.
As soon as Fan Ju heard that it was Ranghou, he said: I heard that Ranghou has monopolized the power of the Qin State. He hates accepting lobbyists from various countries. I am afraid that such a meeting will insult me. I would rather hide in the car for a while.
After a while, Marquis Rang arrived as expected. After greeting Wang Ji, he stopped the car and asked, "How has the situation in Guandong changed?"
Wang Ji replied: No.
Marquis Rang said to Wang Ji again: "Isn't it possible that the envoy came to Qin with the lobbyists from the princes?"
summary: Fan Ju, a man of eloquence, initially sought to serve the King of Wei but was too poor to fund his journey. He first served under Xu Jia, a senior official in Wei. When Xu Jia was sent as an envoy to Qi, Fan Ju accompanied him. King Qi Xiang, impressed by Fan Ju's eloquence, sent him gifts of gold, beef, and wine, which Fan Ju refused. Xu Jia suspected Fan Ju had betrayed Wei secrets to Qi and reported this to the Wei prime minister, Wei Qi. Wei Qi had Fan Ju beaten severely, breaking his ribs and teeth, then wrapped him in a mat and threw him in a toilet, where drunken guests urinated on him. Fan Ju convinced a guard to let him escape, and later hid with the help of Zheng Anping, changing his name to Zhang Lu.

translation:
Such people are not good to Qin and will only disturb other people's countries.
Wang Ji quickly replied: "I don't dare."
The two then said goodbye and left.
Fan Ju said to Wang Ji: I heard that Ranghou is a wise man and has many doubts about how to deal with things. Just now he suspected that there was someone hiding in the car, but he forgot to search it.
So Fan Ju jumped out of the car and walked on foot, saying: "Ranghou will not let this matter go. He will regret not searching the car."
After walking for about ten miles, Marquis Rang sent cavalry to chase and search the car. No one was found, so he gave up.
Wang Ji then entered Xianyang City with Fan Ju.
After Wang Ji reported the envoy situation to the King of Qin, he took the opportunity to say: There is a Mr. Zhang Lu in Wei State. This man is a rare eloquent person in the world.
He said that King Qin's country is in danger, just like stacking eggs one on top of another. If King Qin can get and reuse me, it will make the country safe.
But he needed to be interviewed in person and could not be conveyed by letter, so I brought him to Qin. The King of Qin did not believe what Fan Ju said, so he only let Fan Ju live in a guest house and gave him poor food.
In this way, Fan Ju waited for more than a year to be received by King Qin. At that time, King Qin Zhao had been on the throne for thirty-six years.
The State of Qin captured the important towns of Yan and Ying of the State of Chu in the south. King Huai of Chu was imprisoned in the State of Qin and finally died in the State of Qin.
He conquered Qi in the east.
Previously, King Qi Min once called himself the Eastern Emperor, but soon canceled this title.
Qin also besieged Han, Zhao and Wei many times and expanded its territory. King Zhao of Qin was a man of great martial arts, so he hated those lobbyists and did not believe what they said.
Ranghou and Huayangjun are the younger brothers of King Zhao's mother, Queen Mother Xuan, while Lord Jingyang and Lord Gaoling are both brothers of King Zhao.
Marquis Rang served as the prime minister, and Lord Huayang, Lord Jingyang, and Lord Gaoling served as generals. They all had their own fiefdoms. Due to the protection of Queen Mother Xuan, their private wealth even exceeded that of the country.
When Ranghou became the general of Qin, he wanted to cross Korea and Wei to attack Gangyi and Shouyi of Qi, hoping to expand his Taoyi fiefdom.
For this reason, Fan Ju wrote to the King of Qin and said:
I heard that when a sage monarch carries out administrative affairs, he must not fail to reward those who have meritorious service, and he must not refrain from granting official positions to those who are talented. Those who have made great contributions will have generous salaries, those who have made many achievements will have high titles, and those who can manage many affairs will have high official positions.
Therefore, people with insufficient ability dare not take up official positions, and those with talent will not be buried.
If your Majesty thinks that my words are applicable, I hope you will implement and further realize this idea; if you think that my words are not applicable, then there is no point in keeping me in Qin for a long time.
As the saying goes: A mediocre monarch rewards those he loves and punishes those he dislikes; this is not the case with a wise monarch. Rewards must be given to those who have meritorious service, and punishments must be imposed on guilty people.
Now my chest cannot withstand the guillotine and chopping board, and my waist cannot withstand the chopping of an axe. How dare I test the king with baseless and uncertain claims?
summary: When King Zhao of Qin sent envoy Wang Ji to Wei, Zheng Anping arranged a secret meeting between Fan Ju and Wang Ji. Recognizing Fan Ju's talent, Wang Ji took him to Qin. On the way, they encountered Marquis Rang, the powerful Qin prime minister, but Fan Ju hid to avoid detection. Once in Qin, Wang Ji recommended Fan Ju to King Zhao, but the king was skeptical and housed Fan Ju poorly for over a year. During this time, Qin had expanded its territory significantly, but the king distrusted lobbyists. Marquis Rang and other relatives of the queen mother held immense power, with private wealth exceeding the state's. Fan Ju wrote to King Zhao, arguing that a wise ruler rewards merit and talent, and that he was willing to die if his advice proved useless. Impressed, King Zhao summoned Fan Ju. At the palace, Fan Ju deliberately provoked the king by claiming Qin only had a queen mother and Marquis Rang, not a king. King Zhao apologized for the delay and sought Fan Ju's counsel. After three rounds of questioning, Fan Ju finally spoke, citing historical examples to emphasize the importance of trust and the dangers of powerful relatives. He outlined a strategy of befriending distant states and attacking nearby ones, starting with Han and Wei, to consolidate Qin's power. The historian comments that Fan Ju and Cai泽 succeeded in Qin due to the state's strength and their own perseverance through hardship, noting that many talented individuals fail without such opportunities.

translation:
I have committed a serious crime that deserves to be boiled and killed. I am willing to throw me into the desolate and barbaric Hurao area. Let me live or die. It is just up to your decision! Fan Ju said: How many crimes are you guilty of?
Xu Jia quickly replied: Even if you pluck out my hair to count my sins, it won't be enough.
Fan Ju said: You have three charges.
In the past, when King Zhao of Chu, Shen Baoxu planned for the Chu State and defeated the Wu army. The King of Chu granted him five thousand households in the Chu area as a settlement. Shen Baoxu declined and refused to accept it because his ancestral tomb was buried in the Chu State. Defeating the Wu army could also preserve his ancestral tomb.
Now my ancestral tomb is in the State of Wei, but you thought that I had an affair with the State of Wei and secretly communicated with the State of Qi, so you said bad things about me in front of Wei Qi. This is your first crime.
When Wei Qi threw me into the toilet and insulted me wantonly, you did not stop him. This is the second crime.
What's more, you peed on me when you were drunk. How could you bear it?
This is the third count.
But the reason why you can avoid being executed is because today you gave me a thick silk robe and it seems that you are still attached to me as an old friend, so I will give you a way to live and let you go.
So he resigned from Xu Jia and ended the meeting.
Immediately, Fan Ju went to the palace and reported the whole story to King Zhao. He decided not to accept Wei's envoy and ordered Xu Jia to return home.
Xu Jia went to say farewell to Fan Ju. Fan Ju held a banquet and invited all the envoys from various princely states in Qin to sit with him in the hall. There were lavish food and wine.
But Fan Ju made Xu Jia sit down in the hall, put a trough of feed mixed with grass beans in front of him, and ordered two prisoners who had been tortured to sandwich him in the middle and feed him like a horse.
Fan Ju ordered him: "Go back and tell King Wei what I said, and quickly offer Wei Qi's head!"
Otherwise, I will kill Daliang.
Xu Jia returned to the State of Wei and told Wei Qi about the situation. Wei Qi was greatly frightened, so he fled to the State of Zhao and hid in the home of Lord Pingyuan.
After Fan Ju became the Prime Minister of Qin, Wang Ji once said to Fan Ju: There are three things that are unpredictable and there are three things that are impossible to do.
The king may die one day. This is the first unpredictable thing.
You die suddenly and that's the second thing that's unpredictable.
If I go suddenly, this is the third unpredictable thing.
If the king dies one day, even if you feel sorry that I was not reused by the king, there is nothing you can do about it.
If you die suddenly, there is nothing you can do even if you regret that you have not repaid me.
If I die suddenly, even if you regret not recommending me in time, there is nothing you can do.
Fan Ju was unhappy after hearing this, so he went to the palace to speak to the King of Qin and said: Without Wang Ji's loyalty to you, no one would have brought me into Hangu Pass; but for the king's wisdom and wisdom, I would not have been able to make me so noble.
Now my official position is that of prime minister, and my title has been extended to the rank of marquis. However, Wang Ji is still just a visitor conveying orders to the king. This is not his original intention of bringing me to Qin.
King Qin Zhao summoned Wang Ji, appointed him as the governor of Hedong County, and allowed him not to report to the court on the political and economic conditions of the county for three years.
summary: King Zhao appointed Fan Ju as a guest minister and followed his advice, capturing cities from Wei and Han. Over time, Fan Ju gained the king's trust and exposed the overreach of the queen mother and Marquis Rang, leading to their expulsion. Fan Ju became prime minister, and the king granted him the title of Marquis Ying. When Xu Jia later visited Qin as an envoy, Fan Ju humiliated him for past wrongs but spared his life due to a gift of a robe. Fan Ju also recommended Zheng Anping as a general and repaid all who had helped him.

translation:
Cai Ze knew that Tang Ju was joking with him, so he said, "I already have wealth. What I don't know is the length of life. I want to hear your opinion."
Tang Ju said: Sir, your life span will be forty-three years from now on.
Cai Ze smiled and expressed his gratitude and walked away. Then he said to his coachman: I am carrying rice and eating fat meat, driving the carriage at a gallop, holding a gold seal in my hand, and wearing a purple ribbon around my waist. I am highly respected in front of my master and enjoy glory and wealth. I should be satisfied for forty-three years.
He left Yan State and went to Zhao State, but was driven out by Zhao State.
Then he went to South Korea and Wei State. On the way, he encountered robbers who robbed him of his cooking utensils such as pots and tripods.
He heard that both Zheng Anping and Wang Ji recommended by Fan Ju had committed serious crimes in the Qin State. Fan Ju felt ashamed and could not lift his head, so Cai Ze went west to the Qin State.
He was going to visit King Zhao of Qin. He first sent someone to make a speech in front of Fan Ju to provoke Fan Ju, saying: Cai Ze, a guest from the state of Yan, is a wise and eloquent man with extraordinary knowledge and eloquence in the world.
As soon as he sees the King of Qin, the King of Qin will definitely put you in trouble and deprive you of your power.
Fan Ju heard these words and said: I am familiar with the affairs of the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties and the theories of various schools of thought. I can convince many people with their eloquent words. How can this person embarrass me and take away my power?
So he sent someone to summon Cai Ze.
Cai Ze came in and bowed to Fan Ju.
Fan Ju was unhappy at first. When he met Cai Ze and saw how arrogant he was, Fan Ju reprimanded him and said, "You once threatened to replace me as Qin's prime minister. Has this ever happened to you?" Cai Ze replied: Yes.
Fan Ju said: Let me hear what you have to say. Cai Ze said: Yo!
Why are you so slow to understand the problem? The four seasons of spring, summer, autumn and winter change in a year, and each one completes its mission and then recedes automatically.
All parts of a person's body are strong, his hands and feet are nimble, his ears can hear clearly, his eyes can see clearly, and his mind is intelligent. Isn't this the scholar's wish? Fan Ju said: Yes.
Cai Ze said: He is based on benevolence, upholds justice, promotes the right path, spreads kindness, and is willing to realize his ambitions in the world. People in the world support, love, respect and admire him, and all hope to make him a monarch. Isn't this what a wise and eloquent person expects? Fan Ju said: Yes.
Cai Ze also said: He who is in a position of wealth and glory, governs everything so that everything can be in its proper place; lives a long life, spends his life safely without dying; the world inherits his tradition, sticks to his career, and passes it on forever; his reputation is in perfect harmony with reality, his kindness is extended thousands of miles away, and he is praised from generation to generation as never ending and as long as heaven and earth: Isn't this the effect of promoting the right way and spreading kindness and the auspicious and good deeds mentioned by the saints? Fan Ju said: Yes.
Cai Ze said: As for Shang Yang of Qin, Wu Qi of Chu, and Wen Zhong, the great official of Yue, are their tragic endings enviable?
Fan Ju knew that Cai Ze wanted to use these words to block his mouth and convince himself, so he deliberately quibbled and said: Why not?
That Gongsun Yang served Qin Xiaogong without any second thoughts throughout his life. He devoted himself to the public affairs and did not care about himself. He set up tortures with knives and saws to suppress treachery and evil, and implemented rewards and punishments to achieve peace in the country. He showed his loyalty and true feelings, suffered resentment and accusations, deceived old friends, captured Wei Gongzi Yan, stabilized the country of Qin, and benefited the people. Finally, he captured enemy generals for Qin, defeated the enemy troops, and opened up the territory thousands of miles away.
summary: However, Fan Ju's later years were troubled. Zheng Anping surrendered to Zhao, and Wang Ji was executed for colluding with other states. King Zhao expressed concern about Qin's lack of capable generals, unsettling Fan Ju. Cai Ze, a strategist from Yan, then arrived and warned Fan Ju of the dangers of holding power too long, citing historical figures like Shang Yang and Wu Qi who died after their achievements. Fan Ju heeded the advice and recommended Cai Ze to King Zhao, eventually resigning as prime minister. Cai Ze served briefly but also resigned due to slander, living on in Qin for many years.

translation:
Meng Tian, ​​his ancestor was from Qi State.
Meng Tian's grandfather, Meng Ao, came to Qin from Qi to serve King Qin Zhao, and became a high official.
In the first year of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, Meng Ao served as the general of the Qin State, attacked South Korea, occupied Chenggao and Xingyang, and established Sanchuan County.
In the second year of King Zhuang Xiang's reign, Meng Ao attacked Zhao and captured thirty-seven cities.
In the third year of Qin Shihuang's reign, Meng Ao attacked South Korea and captured thirteen cities.
In the fifth year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Ao attacked Wei, captured twenty cities, and established Dongjun.
In the seventh year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Ao passed away.
Meng Ao's son was named Meng Wu, and Meng Wu's son was named Meng Tian.
Meng Tian once worked in prison litigation records and was responsible for managing relevant documents and prison litigation files.
In the 23rd year of the First Emperor of Qin, Meng Wu served as a general of the Qin State. He and Wang Jian attacked the Chu State, defeated the Chu army and killed Xiang Yan.
In the twenty-fourth year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Wu attacked Chu State again and captured the King of Chu.
Meng Tian's younger brother is called Meng Yi.
In the twenty-sixth year of the First Emperor of Qin, Meng Tian became a general of the Qin State because of his background. He led his troops to attack the Qi State and defeated the Qi army. He was given the official position of internal history.
After the Qin State annexed the world, it sent Meng Tian to lead a huge army of 300,000 people to drive away the Rong and Di to the north and recover the land south of the Yellow River.
The Great Wall was built, taking advantage of the geographical situation, and setting up fortresses, stretching from Lintao in the west to Liaodong in the east, stretching for more than 10,000 miles.
So he crossed the Yellow River, occupied Yangshan Mountain, and extended zigzag to the north.
In the scorching sun, frost, wind and rain, I have been stationed in Shangjun for more than ten years.
At this time, Meng Tian's reputation shocked the Xiongnu.
Qin Shihuang particularly respected and admired the Meng family, trusting and appreciating their talents.
Therefore, he became close to Meng Yi and became the highest official. When he went out, he would ride in the same carriage with the First Emperor, and when he returned to the court, he would serve the king.
Meng Tian was responsible for military responsibilities outside the country, while Meng Yi often made suggestions in the court and was known as a loyal minister. Therefore, even other generals did not dare to compete with them for favor.
Zhao Gao is an estranged relative of King Zhao's family.
The Zhao Gao brothers were all castrated at birth and became eunuchs. His mother was also punished for breaking the law, so her status was low for generations.
When the King of Qin heard that Zhao Gao was very capable and proficient in criminal and prison laws, he promoted him to the post of Zhongche Mansion Order.
Zhao Gao then served his son Hu Hai privately and taught him how to decide lawsuits.
Zhao Gao committed a serious crime, and King Qin asked Meng Yi to punish him in accordance with the law.
Meng Yi did not dare to bend the law. According to the law, he should be sentenced to death and deprived of his official status.
The First Emperor pardoned Zhao Gao because of his diligence and hard work. His original official position was restored.
The First Emperor planned to tour the world, passing through Jiuyuan County and going directly to Ganquan Palace. He sent Meng Tian to open a road for him, from Jiuyuan to Ganquan, opening up the mountains and filling in the deep valleys, a total length of 1,800 miles.
summary: Meng Tian, a Qin general, hailed from Qi through his grandfather Meng Ao, who served Qin under King Zhao and later as a general under King Zhuangxiang and the First Emperor, conquering territories in Han, Zhao, and Wei before his death in 7 BCE. Meng Tian’s father, Meng Wu, also a general, defeated Chu alongside Wang Jian. Meng Tian began as a legal clerk, became a general in 26 BCE, and led 300,000 troops to expel northern nomads, reclaim land south of the Yellow River, and construct the Great Wall from Lintao to Liaodong. He garrisoned Shangjun for over a decade, intimidating the Xiongnu. His brother Meng Yi served as a trusted advisor to the First Emperor.

translation:
However, the passage was not completed.
In the winter of the thirty-seventh year of the First Emperor's reign, the royal chariot went out on a tour of Kuaiji, leaning on the sea, heading north to Langye.
He got seriously ill halfway through, so Meng Yi turned back to pray to the gods of mountains and rivers.
Before Meng Yi could return, the First Emperor walked to the sand dunes and died. The news of the death of the First Emperor was blocked, and none of the civil and military officials knew about it.
At this time, Prime Minister Li Si, Prince Hu Hai, and Zhao Gao, the magistrate of CRRC, often served Qin Shihuang.
Zhao Gao usually received Hu Hai's favor and planned to appoint Hu Hai to inherit the throne. However, he resented Meng Yi for punishing him according to the law instead of protecting him, so he wanted to kill him.
He secretly planned with Prime Minister Li Si and Prince Hu Hai to make Hu Hai the crown prince.
After the crown prince was established, he sent envoys to fabricate charges and prepare the death penalty for Prince Fusu and Meng Tian.
After Fusu committed suicide, Mengtian became suspicious and asked for an appeal.
The envoy handed Meng Tian over to the officials in charge, and sent someone else to take over his duties.
Hu Hai used Li Si's retainers as military guards.
When the envoy came back to report, Hu Hai had heard the news of Fusu's death and immediately planned to release Meng Tian.
Zhao Gao was afraid that the Meng family would become powerful again and resented them.
Meng Yi returned after praying to the gods of the mountains and rivers. Zhao Gao took the opportunity to express his loyalty to Hu Hai and wanted to eradicate the Meng brothers, so he said to Hu Hai: I heard that the late emperor selected talents and made you the crown prince a long time ago, but Meng Yi tried to dissuade him and said: No.
If he knows that you are wise and capable and delays your registration for a long time, then he is being unfaithful and deceiving the late Emperor.
In my ignorant opinion, it is better to kill him. Hu Hai obeyed Zhao Gao's words and imprisoned Meng Yi in Daijun.
Before that, Meng Tian had been imprisoned in Yang Zhou.
After Qin Shihuang's hearse returned to Xianyang and was buried, the prince ascended the throne and became the second emperor. Zhao Gao gained the most favor and slandered the Meng family day and night, collecting their crimes, reporting and impeaching them.
Ziying advised: I heard that in the past, King Zhao Qian killed his wise minister Li Mu and appointed Yan Ju, King Yan secretly adopted Jing Ke's strategy and betrayed Qin's alliance, and King Jian of Qi killed his loyal ministers from the previous generation and adopted the strategy of later victory.
These three kings each lost their country and brought great disaster to themselves because of changing the old rules.
Now the Meng brothers are ministers and counselors of the Qin State, and the monarch intends to abandon them all at once. I think it is not allowed. I have heard that people who think about problems hastily cannot govern the country, and people who are arbitrary and self-righteous cannot protect the monarch.
Killing loyal ministers and appointing those without moral integrity will make the ministers unable to trust each other internally and weaken the fighting spirit of the soldiers externally. I think it is not allowed.
Hu Hai couldn't listen to Ziying's advice.
However, he sent Yushi Qugong to take a post to Dai County and ordered Meng Yi to say: "First of all, you wanted to appoint a prince, but you blocked it. Now the prime minister thinks that you are disloyal and your crime has implicated your family. I can't bear it, so I will grant you suicide. You are very lucky."
summary: Zhao Gao, a eunuch of Zhao royal descent, rose to favor due to legal expertise, teaching Prince Hu Hai. When Zhao Gao committed a serious crime, Meng Yi sentenced him to death, but the First Emperor pardoned him. During the First Emperor’s fatal illness in 37 BCE, Meng Yi was sent to pray; after the emperor’s death, Zhao Gao conspired with Li Si and Hu Hai to install Hu Hai as crown prince, fabricating charges against Fusu and Meng Tian. Fusu committed suicide; Meng Tian was imprisoned. Zhao Gao, fearing the Meng family’s resurgence, falsely accused Meng Yi of opposing Hu Hai’s appointment, leading to his imprisonment in Dai. After Hu Hai became the Second Emperor, Zhao Gao slandered the Mengs daily. Ziying advised against killing them, warning of past disasters from killing loyal ministers, but Hu Hai ignored him.
