translation:
Think about it again and again!
Meng Yi replied: If you think that I cannot win the favor of the late Lord, then by serving as an official and a eunuch when I was young, I was able to gain favor until the late Lord passed away. It can be said that I was able to comply with the will of the late Lord.
If you think that I don't understand the prince's talents, then only the prince can accompany the late lord and travel around the world. Compared with other princes, there is a huge difference. I have no doubts.
The First Master's appointment of the prince was a result of many years of careful consideration. What else can I dare to say and what strategies can I dare to devise?
This is not an excuse for me to avoid the death penalty. I am just afraid that I will be implicated and dishonor the reputation of my late lord. I hope the doctor will seriously consider this and let me die as a result of the crime I deserve.
Moreover, the fulfillment of laws and regulations is what morality advocates; severe punishment and killing are not tolerated by morality.
In the past, Duke Mu of Qin killed Sanliang of the Che family and buried him, and sentenced Baili Xi to an undeserved crime. Therefore, he was given the title of "Miao" after his death.
King Zhaoxiang killed Bai Qi, Lord Wu'an, and King Ping of Chu killed Wu She.
King Wu Fu Chai killed Wu Zixu.
These four kings all made serious mistakes and were criticized by people all over the world, thinking that their kings were unwise. Therefore, he had a bad reputation among the princely states.
Therefore, it is said: Those who govern the country with morality will not kill innocent subjects, and punishment will not be imposed on innocent people.
I hope the doctor will seriously consider it!
The envoy knew Hu Hai's intention and refused to listen to Meng Yi's complaint, so he killed him.
The second emperor sent an envoy to Yang Zhou again and ordered Meng Tian to say: "You have committed too many sins, and your brother Meng Yi has committed a serious crime and will implicate you according to the law."
Meng Tian said: From my ancestors to their descendants, it has been three generations since I accumulated great achievements and established prestige for the Qin State.
Now I lead more than 300,000 troops. Even though I am imprisoned, I am powerful enough to rebel. However, I knew that I would definitely die, but I persisted in my integrity. I did not dare to insult the teachings of my ancestors, and I did not dare to forget the grace of my late lord.
Once upon a time, King Cheng of Zhou had just ascended the throne and could not completely break away from the child's sling and cloth bag. Duke Ji Dan of Zhou carried King Cheng on his back to accept the audience of the ministers, and finally brought peace to the world.
When King Cheng's condition became serious and dangerous, Gongdan cut off his own nails and sank them into the Yellow River, praying and saying: "The king is young and ignorant. This is because I am in power. If there is any fault or disaster, I should bear the punishment."
Just write down these prayers and store them in the archives. This can be said to be very honest.
When King Cheng was able to govern the country in person, some treacherous ministers spread rumors: Duke Zhou had been planning to cause rebellion for a long time. If the king was not on guard, something big would happen.
When King Cheng heard this, he became furious and Duke Zhou fled to Chu.
King Cheng went to the archives to review the files and found Zhou Gongdan's prayer book. He shed tears and said: Who said Zhou Gongdan wanted to cause chaos!
Kill the minister who spread the rumors and caused trouble, and invite Duke Zhou to return.
Therefore, the "Book of Zhou" says: We must inquire from multiple parties and review repeatedly.
Now our Meng clan has had no two minds from generation to generation, but things ended up like this. This must be because the ministers who planned the rebellion rebelled and deceived the emperor.
King Zhou Cheng made mistakes but was able to correct his mistakes and finally made the Zhou Dynasty prosperous; Xia Jie killed Guan Longfeng, and Shang Zhou killed Prince Bigan without regrets, and finally died.
Therefore, I say that if you make mistakes, you can correct them and cheer up. If you listen to others' advice, you can be aware of them and be vigilant. These are the principles for a sage king to govern his country.
In general, the words I say are not to evade responsibility, but to die with loyal advice. I hope that Your Majesty will thoughtfully find the correct path to follow for the people of Li.
The envoy said: I accepted the order to impose punishment on the general, but I dare not report the general's words to the emperor.
Meng Tian sighed heavily and said: What crime have I committed against God that I should be executed for no fault of my own?
After a long time, he slowly said: My sin should have been punished by death.
summary: Meng Yi was ordered to commit suicide; he defended his loyalty and criticized unjust executions, citing historical examples, but was killed. Meng Tian, ordered to die, declared his innocence and loyalty, recounting the Duke of Zhou’s story to urge the emperor to reconsider. The envoy refused to relay his words. Meng Tian lamented his sin of cutting earth’s veins while building the Great Wall and poisoned himself. Sima Qian criticized Meng Tian for failing to counsel the First Emperor to aid the people after conquests, instead building the Great Wall, which led to his and his brother’s deaths.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/蒙恬列传

translation:
Yuan Ang is from Chu, and his courtesy name is Si.
His father once worked with bandits and later moved to Anling.
During the period of Empress Lu, Yuan An once served as Lu Lu's retainer.
When Emperor Wen of Han came to the throne, Yuan An's brother Yuan Kuai recommended him to be the lieutenant.
Jianghou Zhou Bo became the prime minister. After the pilgrimage, he hurried out of the court, very satisfied with his ambitions.
The emperor was very respectful to him and often sent him off in person.
Yuan Ang remonstrated and said: What kind of person do you think Prime Minister Jianghou is?
The emperor said: He is an important minister of the country.
Yuan An said: Jianghou is what is usually called a hero, not an important minister of the country. The important ministers of the country can live and die with the emperor.
When Empress Lu was in power, the Lu family was in power and granted the title of king without authorization. As a result, the Liu family's world was barely held together like a thin ribbon and was almost severed.
During this period, Jianghou Zhou Bo was the Taiwei and held military power, but could not correct the collapse of the Han Dynasty.
After Empress Lu died, the ministers jointly opposed the Lu family. The Taiwei took control of the military and happened to have the opportunity to succeed, so he was what is usually called a hero, not an important official of the country.
If the Prime Minister shows a proud look towards the Emperor, but His Majesty humbly gives in, both the minister and the Lord are violating etiquette. I privately think that Your Majesty should not adopt this attitude.
Later in the court meeting, the emperor gradually became more majestic, and the prime minister gradually became more awe-inspiring.
Soon after, the prime minister resented Yuan Ang and said: I have a relationship with your brother Yuan Kuai, but now you are slandering me in the court!
Yuan An also did not apologize to him.
When Jianghou was dismissed from his position as prime minister and returned to his feudal state, someone in the feudal state wrote a letter accusing him of treason, so Jianghou was summoned to Beijing and imprisoned in prison. Some princes in the royal family did not dare to speak for him. Only Yuan Ang declared that Jianghou was not guilty.
Jianghou was released, and Yuan An made a lot of efforts.
Jianghou then made a heart-to-heart friendship with Yuan An.
When Liu Chang, the king of Huainan, came to Beijing to see him, he killed Piyanghou. He was also quite arrogant in his dealings with others.
Yuan Ang advised the emperor: If the princes are too arrogant, disaster will inevitably occur. Their fiefdoms can be appropriately reduced.
The emperor did not adopt his opinion, and King Huainan became even more arrogant.
When it was discovered that the prince of Chaiwu, the Marquis of Jipu, was preparing to rebel, he was investigated and punished. This incident implicated King Huainan, who was recruited, and the emperor demoted him to Shu and transported him in a prison car.
Yuan An was serving as Zhonglang General at that time, so he advised him: Your Majesty has always been arrogant and indulgent to the King of Huainan without any restrictions, which has led him to the current situation, and now he has suddenly defeated him.
The King of Huainan is an upright man. If he encounters a cold wind and dies on the way, his Majesty will be thought that the world is too big to tolerate him, and he will be infamous for killing his younger brother. What will he do then?
The emperor refused to listen and finally did so.
King Huainan died of illness when he arrived at Yongdi. When the news came, the emperor neither ate nor drank, and cried very sadly.
Yuan An entered and kowtowed to apologize.
summary: Yuan Ang, courtesy name Si, was from Chu and later moved to Anling. He served as a retainer under Lü Lu during Empress Lü’s reign and was recommended as a lieutenant by his brother after Emperor Wen ascended. Yuan Ang remonstrated with Emperor Wen about his excessive respect for Prime Minister Zhou Bo, arguing that Zhou Bo was a “hero” rather than a true “important minister” for failing to prevent the Lü clan’s usurpation. The emperor heeded his advice, and Zhou Bo later resented Yuan Ang but reconciled after Yuan Ang defended him when Zhou Bo was imprisoned for treason.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传

translation:
The emperor said: Because your opinions were not adopted, this result was reached.
Yuan An said: Your Majesty, please relax yourself. This is already in the past. Can you still regret it?
Besides, Your Majesty has three behaviors that are above the world. This incident is not enough to ruin your reputation.
The emperor said: What are the three behaviors that make me higher than others?
Yuan An said: When Your Majesty was living in Dai, the Queen Mother was ill. For three years, Your Majesty never closed his eyes or took off his clothes to sleep. Any decoction that His Majesty had not personally tasted was not allowed to be given to the Queen Mother.
It was difficult for Zeng Shen to do this as a poor man, but now His Majesty has practiced it as a king, which is much better than Zeng Shen's filial piety.
When Zhu Lu was in power, ministers acted arbitrarily, but Your Majesty rode six inferior horse-drawn carriages from Dai to the capital where disaster and fortune were unpredictable. Even brave men like Meng Ben and Xia Yu could not compare with Your Majesty.
His Majesty arrived at Dai Guo's guest house in the capital. He resigned to the throne of emperor twice while facing west, and resigned to the throne of emperor three times while sitting facing south.
Xu You resigned to the world only once, but His Majesty resigned to the world five times, which was more than Xu You's four times.
Besides, Your Majesty demoted the King of Huainan to make him suffer some hardship and make him correct his mistakes. However, because the officials were not cautious in protecting him, he died of illness.
Then the emperor felt relieved and said: What should we do in the future?
Yuan Ang said, "The King of Huainan has three sons. It's just up to your Majesty's arrangement."
So Emperor Wen made all three sons of King Huainan kings.
As a result, Yuan Ang became famous in the court.
Yuan An often praised righteousness and spoke impassionedly.
Because the eunuch Zhao Tong was favored by the emperor more than once, he often secretly hurt Yuan Ang, which made Yuan Ang worried.
Yuan An's nephew Yuan Zhong served as an attendant knight, guarding the emperor with talismans. Yuan Zhong persuaded Yuan Ang: "Fight with him and insult him in the court, so that his slanderous words will have no effect."
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty went on a tour, and Zhao Tong accompanied him in the car. Yuan Ang lay in front of the car and said: I heard that the people who accompany the emperor on the tall chariot are all heroes in the world.
Although the Han Dynasty lacks talents today, why does Your Majesty only want to ride in the same carriage with people who have been cut by swords and saws?
So the emperor smiled and asked Zhao Tong to get off, and Zhao Tong got out of the car with tears in his eyes.
Emperor Wen went up the mountain from Baling and planned to run down the steep slope in the west.
Yuan An was riding a horse, leaning against the car and holding the horse's reins.
The emperor said: Is the general afraid?
Yuan An said: I have heard that people with rich families do not sit close to the eaves when they sit, and people with rich families do not lean on the railings of the balcony when standing. A wise monarch does not take chances when facing danger.
Now Your Majesty lets the six horses of the driver gallop down the high slope. If the horses are frightened and the vehicle is damaged, even if Your Majesty looks down on yourself, how can you be worthy of the Emperor and the Queen Mother?
The emperor finally stopped.
The emperor arrived at Shanglin Garden, followed by Queen Dou and Mrs. Shen.
summary: Yuan Ang advised against indulging Liu Chang, the King of Huainan, whose arrogance led to rebellion and exile. When the king died en route, Yuan Ang consoled the grieving emperor by citing his three virtuous acts: filial piety to his mother, bravery during the Lü crisis, and humility in refusing the throne. The emperor later made the king’s three sons rulers. Yuan Ang’s outspokenness caused friction with eunuch Zhao Tong, whom he publicly humiliated to prevent him from riding in the emperor’s carriage. He also dissuaded the emperor from reckless chariot racing and corrected seating arrangements that favored a concubine over the queen.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传

translation:
What is this for?
He wanted to use this method to attract the wise scholar-bureaucrats in the world.
Every day the emperor hears things he has never heard before, understands truths he has never understood before, and becomes wiser and wiser day by day; now that you have closed the mouths of the people in the world, you are becoming more stupid day by day.
If you use a wise monarch to supervise a foolish prime minister, the day when you will suffer disaster is not far away!
The prime minister then bowed twice and said: I am a vulgar and vulgar person, but I am not smart. Fortunately, I have been taught by the general.
Shen Tujia invited Yuan An into the inner room to sit with him and treated him as an honored guest.
Yuan An had always disliked Chao Cuo. As long as Chao Cuo was around, Yuan An would leave. As long as Yuan An was around, Chao Cuo would also leave. The two never talked together.
When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty passed away and Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne, Chao Cuo became the imperial censor. He sent officials to investigate Yuan An's acceptance of Wu Wang Liu Bi's property and punish him according to the seriousness of the crime.
The emperor issued an edict to demote Yuan An to a commoner. News of Wu Chu's rebellion reached the capital, and Chao Cuo told the Prime Minister: Yuan An received a lot of money from the King of Wu and specifically covered it for him, saying that he would not rebel.
Now that the rebellion has become a fact, I plan to request Yuan Ang be punished. He must have known the plot of rebellion.
The Prime Minister said: Punishing him before the matter is exposed may interrupt the rebellion conspiracy.
Now that the rebels are marching westward, what is the benefit of punishing Yuan Ang! Besides, Yuan Ang shouldn't have any conspiracy.
Chao Cuo hesitated.
Someone told Yuan Ang about this. Yuan Ang was afraid and went to see Dou Ying overnight to explain to him the reasons for King Wu's rebellion, hoping to confront him personally in front of the emperor.
Dou Ying went to the palace to report to the emperor, and the emperor summoned Yuan Ang to the palace to meet him.
Chao Cuo was right in front of him. When Yuan An asked the emperor to meet him alone without others, Chao Cuo retreated, feeling very resentful.
Yuan Ang explained in detail that the King of Wu rebelled because of Chao Cuo. Only by killing Chao Cuo immediately to apologize to the King of Wu could the Wu army stop.
These words of his are all recorded in "The Biography of Wu Wangbi".
The emperor appointed Yuan An as Taichang and Dou Ying as general.
The two men have always been friends.
When the King of Wu rebelled, the prestigious people living in the mausoleums and the wise officials in Chang'an City were vying to attach themselves to the two of them, and hundreds of cars followed behind them every day.
After Chao Cuo was executed, Yuan Ang went to Wu as an envoy as Taichang.
The King of Wu wanted him to serve as a general, but Yuan Ang refused.
The king of Wu killed him and sent a captain to lead 500 men to surround Yuan Ang in the army.
When Yuan An was the Prime Minister of the State of Wu, a Cong Shi secretly had an affair with Yuan An's maid. Yuan An knew about it but did not reveal it, and treated Cong Shi as before.
Someone told Cong Shi that Yuan Ang knew about his affair with his maidservant, and Congshi fled home. Yuan Ang chased Congshi in his car, and gave him his maidservant, still calling him Congshi.
summary: Transferred to Longxi, Yuan Ang won soldiers’ loyalty through kindness. As prime minister of Wu, he followed his nephew’s advice to avoid conflict by drinking daily and persuading the king not to rebel. He later confronted Prime Minister Shen Tujia for arrogance, warning that closing off advice would lead to disaster. Shen Tujia apologized and treated him as an honored guest.

translation:
When Yuan An was sent as an envoy to Wu and was besieged, Sima happened to be the captain who besieged Yuan An. Sima sold all the belongings he carried and used the money to buy two loads of strong-flavored wine. It happened to be cold and the besieging soldiers were hungry and thirsty. They drank too much wine and the soldiers guarding the southwest corner of the city were drunk. Sima Cheng led Yuan An up at night and said: You can go, the King of Wu expects to kill you tomorrow.
Yuan Ang didn't believe it and said, "What do you do?"
Sima said: I am the one who originally had an affair with your maid in the history.
Yuan Ang then thanked him in surprise and said: "You are lucky to have your parents here, I can't let you get in trouble because of this."
Sima said: Just leave. I will run away and hide my parents. Why should you worry?
So he cut the tent of the military camp open with a knife and led Yuan Ang out of the road blocked by the drunken soldiers.
Sima and Yuan Ang parted ways and went in opposite directions. Yuan Ang took off his knot and carried it in his arms. He leaned on his staff and walked for seven or eight miles. At dawn, he encountered Liang's cavalry and fled on horseback. Finally, he returned to the court to report.
The Wu-Chu rebels had been defeated, and the emperor changed the title of Pingluhou Liu Li, the son of King Chu Yuan, to the king of Chu, and Yuan An became the prime minister of Chu.
Yuan Ang once wrote a letter to make suggestions, but they were not accepted.
Yuan Ang was exempted from official duties due to illness and lived at home, hanging out with the villagers and playing cockfighting and dog racing games with them.
Ju Meng, a native of Luoyang, once visited Yuan An, who received him warmly.
A rich man from Anling said to Yuan An: I heard that Ju Meng is a gambler. Why do you want to associate with him?
Yuan An said: Although Ju Meng was a gambler, when his mother passed away, there were more than a thousand guest cars at the funeral. This was also because of his extraordinary qualities.
Besides, everyone is in danger.
When you are in danger or something urgent knocks on the door, you don't use the excuse of having your parents around to shirk it, and you don't have to refuse by not being at home because of something. The only people the world looks up to are Ji Xin and Ju Meng.
Nowadays, you are often followed by several cavalrymen. If there is an emergency, can these people be relied upon?
Yuan An scolded the rich man and stopped communicating with him.
After everyone heard this, they all praised Yuan An.
Although Yuan Ang stayed at home, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty often sent people to ask him about strategies.
The King of Liang wanted to become the heir to Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, and Yuan An persuaded him. After that, the discussion stopped. The King of Liang resented Yuan An and once sent someone to assassinate Yuan An.
The assassin came to Guanzhong and asked what kind of person Yuan An was. Everyone was full of praise.
The assassin then went to see Yuan An and said: I accepted the money from King Liang to assassinate you. You are a generous man and I cannot bear to assassinate you.
But there will be more than ten groups of people coming to assassinate you in the future. I hope you will be more prepared!
Yuan Ang felt very unhappy, and many strange things happened one after another at home, so he went to Mr. Piao to ask for fortune telling.
When returning home, the assassins from Liang Kingdom who were sent later stopped Yuan An outside the outer city gate of Anling and assassinated him.
Chao Cuo was from Yingchuan.
I once studied the punishment naming theories of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang from Mr. Zhang Hui of Zhi County, and I was classmates with Song Meng and Liu Li from Luoyang.
summary: Yuan Ang clashed with Chao Cuo, who investigated him for accepting bribes from the King of Wu, leading to his demotion. When Wu rebelled, Yuan Ang blamed Chao Cuo and urged his execution to appease the rebels. After Chao Cuo’s death, Yuan Ang was sent as an envoy to Wu but was besieged. A former subordinate, whom Yuan Ang had forgiven for an affair with his maid, helped him escape. Yuan Ang later served as prime minister of Chu but retired due to illness, living humbly and befriending gambler Ju Meng despite criticism. He opposed making the King of Liang the emperor’s heir, prompting assassination attempts. Warned by an assassin who spared him, Yuan Ang was eventually killed by Liang’s agents outside Anling.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传

translation:
With his proficiency in classics, he served as Taichang's anecdote.
Chao Cuo was an upright and severe man.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, there was no one in the world who studied "Shangshu". I only heard that Mr. Fu from Jinan was a doctor from the original Qin Dynasty and had studied "Shangshu". He was too old to answer the call, so Emperor Wen ordered Taichang to send people to study with him.
Taichang sent Chao Cuo to Mr. Fu to study Shangshu.
After he came back from his studies, he took the opportunity to report to the emperor things that benefited the country and the people, and quoted and explained "Shang Shu".
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty issued an edict and appointed Chao Cuo as the prince's family minister, family official, and prince's family magistrate.
Chao Cuo won the favor of the prince with his eloquence, and the prince's family called him "the wise man".
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Chao Cuo wrote many times about reducing the power of the princes and amending the laws.
After dozens of petitions, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty did not accept them, but he believed that he had unique talents and was promoted to a middle doctor.
At that time, the prince praised Chao Cuo's strategy, but Yuan Ang and most of the other great heroes did not like Chao Cuo.
After Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne, he appointed Chao Cuo as his internal historian.
Chao Cuo repeatedly requested the emperor to discuss political affairs with him alone. Emperor Jing always obeyed and favored him more than Jiu Qing. Chao Cuo revised many laws.
Prime Minister Shen Tujia was dissatisfied, but did not have enough power to harm him.
I plan to write a memorial about Chao Cuo's fault this time and request that Chao Cuo be executed. Chao Cuo heard the news and asked to go to the emperor alone that night and explained the matter to the emperor in detail. Prime Minister Shen Tujia went to court and took the opportunity to report Chao Cuo for cutting open the wall of Taishang Temple to make a door without permission, and asked the emperor to hand him over to the Tingwei for execution. The emperor said: The wall that Chao Cuo built was not the wall of Taishang Temple, but the wall on the open space outside the temple, so that it would not violate the law.
The Prime Minister apologized.
After leaving the court, he angrily said to Chang Shi: I should have killed him first and then reported it to the emperor, but instead I reported him first and was betrayed by this guy. It was a big mistake.
The prime minister finally fell ill and died, making Chao Cuo even more prominent.
Chao Cuo was promoted to the imperial censor, and requested that the feudal lords' fiefdoms be reduced accordingly for their crimes, and the counties and cities on the borders of each vassal state be recovered.
After the memorial was submitted, the emperor ordered the ministers, princes and royal family to discuss it together. No one dared to criticize Chao Cuo's suggestion. Only Dou Ying argued with him, so there was a gap between him and Chao Cuo.
The decree revised by Chao Cuo had thirty chapters, and the princes all shouted against it and hated Chao Cuo.
When Chao Cuo's father heard the news, he came from Yingchuan and said to Chao Cuo: The emperor has just succeeded to the throne, and you have taken power, infringing and weakening the power of the princes, alienating other people's flesh and blood, and people are talking and resenting you. Why do you do this?
Chao Cuo said: Things should be like this. Otherwise, the emperor will not be respected and the country will not be peaceful.
Chao Cuo's father then said: If this continues, the Liu family will be at peace, but our Chao family will be in danger. I will leave you and go back.
summary: Chao Cuo, from Yingchuan, studied Legalist doctrines and Shangshu under Master Fu. He gained favor as a prince’s tutor during Emperor Wen’s reign, advocating for reducing princely power. Emperor Jing promoted him, and he revised laws, angering nobles. His father warned him of danger but Chao Cuo insisted on centralizing authority. The Wu-Chu rebellion used his execution as a pretext. After his death, Deng Gong argued that Chao Cuo’s policies were for the empire’s benefit, and Emperor Jing regretted the execution. Deng Gong later became a high official but retired.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传

translation:
He took poison and died. Before he died, he said: I can't bear to see disaster involving myself.
Ten days after Chao Cuo's father died, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, in the name of killing Chao Cuo.
When Dou Ying and Yuan Ang came forward, the emperor ordered Chao Cuo to wear court clothes and execute him in Dongshi.
After the death of Chao Cuo, Duke Deng of Yezhe Pushe served as a school captain. When he attacked Wu Chu's army, he served as a general.
After returning to the capital, he wrote a letter reporting the military situation and went to see the emperor.
The emperor asked: "You came from the army and heard that Chao Cuo was dead. Did Wu Chu's army retreat?"
Deng Gong said: The King of Wu has been deliberately rebellious for decades. He was angry because you reduced his fiefdom, so in the name of killing Chao Cuo, his original intention was not Chao Cuo.
Besides, I'm worried that all the scholars in the world will shut up and never dare to speak out again.
The emperor said: Why?
Deng Gong said: Chao Cuo was worried that the princes would become too powerful and could not be subdued, so he asked to reduce the fiefdoms of the princes in order to favor the court. This is the benefit of all generations.
The plan had just started to be implemented, but he was actually killed, which blocked the mouths of loyal ministers internally, and avenged the princes externally. I privately think that it is not advisable for your Majesty to do this.
At this time Emperor Jing was silent for a long time and said: "What you said is right. I also regret this."
So Deng Gong was appointed as the lieutenant of Chengyang.
Deng Gong was from Chenggu and had many unexpected ideas.
During the Jianyuan period, the emperor recruited virtuous people, and the ministers all recommended Deng Gong. At that time, Deng Gong was dismissed from office, and he became the ninth minister from his leisure time at home.
A year later, he resigned and returned home, claiming to be ill. His son Deng Zhang was very famous among the court ministers for studying the theories of Huangdi and Laozi.
Tai Shigong said: Although Yuan Ang is not easy to learn, he is good at understanding and understanding. He takes benevolence as his essence and often praises righteousness and is impassioned.
When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty had just ascended the throne, his talents happened to be at the right time, so they could be put to use.
The current situation was constantly changing. When Wu Chu rebelled, he proposed to kill Chao Cuo.
Although his suggestions were adopted and implemented, he was no longer used by the court.
People who love fame and show off their talents end up getting into trouble because of their pursuit of fame. When Chao Cuo was making the prince's family orders, he made many suggestions but they were not adopted. Later, he took power and revised many laws of the country.
The princes launched a rebellion, but Chao Cuo was not eager to correct the crisis, but wanted to avenge himself, which resulted in his death.
As the saying goes: If you change the ancient laws and mess up the routine, you will either die or escape. Are you talking about people like Chao Cuo?
summary: Tai Shigong commented that Yuan Ang, though unlearned, was benevolent and outspoken, but his fame-seeking led to downfall. Chao Cuo, despite his talents, failed to adapt and died due to his rigidity, as the saying goes: altering ancient laws brings ruin.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/袁盎晁错列传

translation:
The people of these Yi countries wear their hair in buns, cultivate fields, and live together in towns and villages. The places outside them, from Tongshi in the west to Yiyu in the north, are called Xi and Kunming. The people here put their hair on their heads and move around with the grazing livestock. They have no fixed place of residence and no commander. They move for thousands of miles.
Going northeast from Wei, there are so many rulers that one can count them by ten, among which Yi and Zuo are the most powerful. Going northeast from Zuo, there are so many rulers that one can count them by ten, among which Ran Zhen is the most powerful.
Their custom is that some are indigenous people and some are immigrants, all in the west of Shu County.
Going northeast from Ranjun, there are so many kings that you need to count them by ten. Among them, Baima is the most powerful, and they are all of the same kind as the Di tribe.
These are all barbarians outside Bajun and southwest of Shujun.
When King Wei of Chu was king, he sent General Zhuang Qi to lead his army up the Yangtze River and captured the areas west of Bajun, Shujun and Qianzhong County.
Zhuang Qi is a descendant of the former King Zhuang of Chu.
Zhuang Qi arrived at Dianchi Lake, which has a radius of three hundred miles, is surrounded by flat land, and is fertile and rich for thousands of miles.
Zhuang Qi relied on the power of his army to pacify the place and made it subordinate to the Chu State. Zhuang Qi wanted to return to Chu State to report the situation, but just as Qin State attacked and captured Bajun and Qianzhong County of Chu State, the road was blocked and could not pass, so he returned to Dianchi Lake and became the king of Dian with the help of his army. He changed his clothes and obeyed local customs, so he became the ruler of the Dian people.
During the Qin Dynasty, Chang Yan briefly opened the Five Feet Road and set up some officials in these countries.
After more than ten years, the Qin Dynasty perished.
When the Han Dynasty was established, these countries were abandoned, and the original boundaries of Shu County were used as fortresses.
Some people from Bajun and Shujun secretly went out to trade in exchange for horses from Zuo, boy servants and yaks from Bo. Therefore, Bajun and Shujun were particularly wealthy.
In the sixth year of the founding of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Wang Hui of Daxing attacked Dongyue. The Dongyue people killed Ying, the king of Dongyue, and reported to the Han Dynasty.
Wang Hui relied on his military power to send Fan Yang to Tang Meng to tactfully inform South Vietnam of the Han Dynasty's intention to send troops.
Nanyue gave Tang Meng some wolfberry sauce produced in Shu County. Tang Meng asked where it came from. Nanyue said: It came via the Zoke River in the northwest. The Zoke River is several miles wide and flows under Panyu City.
Tang Meng returned to Chang'an and asked the merchants in Shu County. The merchants said: Only Shu County produces wolfberry sauce, and many people secretly take it out to make deals with Yelang.
Yelang is close to the Zoke River. The river is hundreds of paces wide and can be used for boating.
Nanyue wanted to use property to make Yelang belong to him, but his power reached directly to his fellow soldiers in the west, and he could not use Yelang like his subordinates.
Tang Meng wrote to the emperor and said: The King of Nanyue rides in the yellow house's carriage, with the flag of Zuohu flying on the carriage. His land is more than 10,000 miles from east to west. In name, he is a foreign minister, but in fact he is the lord of a state.
Nowadays, most of the waterways from Changsha and Yuzhang County are blocked, making it difficult to move forward.
summary: Various Yi tribes and their customs. Some wear hair in buns, cultivate fields, and live in towns, while others, like the Xi and Kunming, move with livestock and have no fixed residence or commander. From Wei northeast, many rulers exist, with Yi and Zuo being most powerful, followed by Ran Zhen. These are barbarians outside Bajun and southwest of Shujun. King Wei of Chu sent General Zhuang Qi, a descendant of King Zhuang of Chu, to capture areas west of Bajun, Shujun, and Qianzhong County. He reached Dianchi Lake, a fertile area, and pacified it for Chu. Unable to return due to Qin's capture of Bajun and Qianzhong, he became king of Dian, adopting local customs. During Qin, Chang Yan briefly opened the Five Feet Road and set officials. After Qin's fall, Han abandoned these areas, using Shu County's boundaries as fortresses. Bajun and Shujun grew wealthy through secret trade with Zuo, Bo, and others.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传

translation:
I have privately heard that Yelang has more than 100,000 elite soldiers. He can take boats down the Zoko River and attack them while they are not paying attention. This is a wonderful trick to subdue South Vietnam.
If we can really use the power of the Han Dynasty and the wealth of Bashu to open the road to Yelang and set up officials there, it will be very easy.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty agreed with Tang Meng's proposal and appointed him Lieutenant General Lang. He led a thousand troops and more than 10,000 people in charge of food and baggage. He entered Yelang from Bafu Pass and met Yelang Hou Duotong.
Tang Meng gave him many rewards, enlightened him with the power and kindness of the Han Dynasty, and agreed to set up officials for them, making his son an official equivalent to a county magistrate.
People in the small towns next to Yelang were all coveting the silk fabrics of the Han Dynasty. They thought that the road from the Han Dynasty to Yelang was difficult and they would not be able to possess them after all, so they temporarily accepted Tang Meng's covenant.
Tang Meng returned to the capital and reported to the emperor, who then changed Yelang to Qianwei County.
After that, soldiers from Ba and Shu counties were dispatched to build a road from Bo to the Zoke River.
Sima Xiangru, a native of Shu County, also told the emperor that Qiong and Zeo in Xiyi could be established as counties. The emperor sent Sima Xiangru to Xiyi as a lieutenant general and told them clearly that the imperial court would treat them in the same way as Nanyi and set up a captain and more than a dozen counties for them to belong to Shu County.
At this time, Bajun, Shujun, Guanghanjun, and Hanzhongjun opened roads to the southwestern Yi, and there were many soldiers guarding the border and people transporting supplies and military rations.
After several years, the road was not repaired. The soldiers were tired, hungry, and suffered from dampness, and many died. The southwestern barbarians rebelled many times, dispatching troops to attack, spending money and manpower, but there was no commotion.
The emperor was worried about this, so he sent Gongsun Hong to observe and inquire in person.
Gongsun Hong returned to Beijing to report to the emperor, claiming that it was unfavorable.
When Gongsun Hong became the censor, the Han Dynasty was building Shuofang County in order to use the Yellow River to expel the Huns. Gongsun Hong took the opportunity to repeatedly state the harm of developing the southwestern barbarians, so he could temporarily stop development activities and concentrate on dealing with the Xiongnu.
The emperor ordered the cessation of activities against the Western Yi, and only set up two counties and one captaincy in Yelang, Nanyi. He ordered Qianwei County to protect itself and gradually improve its county system.
In the first year of Yuanshou, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Bowang Hou Zhang Qian returned from his mission to Daxia. He said that when he was in Daxia, he had seen cloth produced in Shu County and bamboo sticks from Qiongdu. He asked people about the origin of these things. The person who answered said: They were obtained from the Shendu Kingdom in the southeast. The road from here to there is thousands of miles, and you can do business with merchants in Shu.
Some people heard that there was a country called Shendu about two thousand miles west of Qiongdi.
Zhang Qian took the opportunity to talk about how Daxia was in the southwest of the Han Dynasty, admired China, and was worried that the Xiongnu would block their main transportation routes with China. If a road to Shu could be opened, the road to Shendu would be convenient and short, which would be beneficial and harmless to the Han Dynasty.
So Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty ordered Wang Ranyu, Bai Shichang, Lu Yueren and others to find a shortcut from the west of Xiyi to find the Shendu Kingdom.
summary: In Emperor Wu's sixth year, Wang Hui attacked Dongyue, and Tang Meng learned from Nanyue about wolfberry sauce from Shu, traded via Yelang and the Zoke River. Tang Meng proposed using Yelang's elite troops to attack Nanyue, and Emperor Wu agreed. Tang Meng entered Yelang, made agreements, and established Qianwei County. Roads were built, but difficulties and rebellions led to temporary cessation of development. Later, Zhang Qian reported seeing Shu cloth and Qiong bamboo sticks in Daxia, suggesting a route to Shendu. Emperor Wu sent envoys to find Shendu via Dian, but they were blocked by Kunming. Dian and Yelang kings, unaware of Han's size, questioned its magnitude.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/西南夷列传

translation:
When they arrived in the Dian Kingdom, King Changqiang of Dian stayed with them and sent more than ten groups of people to the west to find a way for them.
More than a year later, all those who were looking for a way were blocked by the Kunming Kingdom and could not reach the Shendu Kingdom.
The King of Dian said to the envoys of the Han Dynasty: Which one is bigger, the Han Dynasty or our Dian Kingdom?
When the Han Dynasty envoy arrived at Yelang, Yelang also raised such a question.
This is because the roads are impassable. Each of them thought he was the master of a state and did not know the vastness of the Han Dynasty.
When the envoys of the Han Dynasty returned to the capital, they tried their best to say that Dian was a great country and worthy of getting close to them and joining the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty paid attention to this matter.
When the South Vietnamese rebelled, the emperor sent Marquis Chiyi to dispatch the Nanyi troops in the name of Jianwei County.
Qie Lanjun was afraid that after his army traveled far, neighboring countries would take the opportunity to plunder his old and weak people, so he rebelled with his army and killed the Han Dynasty envoys and the prefect of Jianwei County.
The Han Dynasty mobilized eight captains from Bajun and Shujun who originally wanted to attack South Vietnam, and led the criminals who had been pardoned to join the army to attack Qielan and pacify it.
Just as South Vietnam had been conquered, the eight lieutenants of the Han Dynasty had not yet moved south along the Zangke River, so they led their troops to withdraw and killed Tou Lan during the march.
Toulan was a country that often blocked the transportation routes between the Han Dynasty and the Dian Kingdom.
After Toulan was pacified, Nanyi was pacified and Zoke County was established there.
Yelanghou began to rely on Nanyue. After Nanyue was destroyed, just as the Han army came back to kill the rebels, Yelanghou went to the capital of the Han Dynasty to meet the emperor.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty named him King Yelang.
After the destruction of Nanyue, and the execution of Lord Qielan and Lord Qiong by the Han Dynasty, as well as the death of Marquis Zhe, Ran and Zhen were shocked and panicked, and they asked the Han Dynasty to become ministers and appoint officials for them.
In the Han Dynasty, Qiongdu was set up as Yuesi County, Zhedu was set up as Shenli County, Ran and Zhan were set up as Lunshan County, and Baima in the west of Guanghan was set up as Wudu County.
The emperor sent Wang Ranyu to use the military power of destroying Nanyue and killing the Nanyi rulers to tactfully persuade the Dian king to come to see the emperor.
The King of Dian had an army of tens of thousands. Next to him in the northeast were Lao Jin and Mi Mo. They both had the same surname as the King of Dian. They relied on each other and refused to listen to advice.
Lao Jin and Mi Mo repeatedly offended Han Dynasty envoys and officers and soldiers.
In the second year of Yuanfeng reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the emperor mobilized the troops from Bajun and Shujun to attack and destroy Laojin and Mimo, and the army approached the Dian Kingdom.
The King of Dian had good intentions towards the Han Dynasty from the beginning, so he was not executed.
The King of Dian then left Xiyi, led the country to surrender to the Han Dynasty, requested to appoint officials for them, and went to Beijing to meet Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
So the Han Dynasty established the Dian Kingdom as Yizhou County, gave the Dian King a royal seal, and still ruled over his people.
summary: When Nanyue rebelled, Qielan rebelled and killed Han envoys. Han forces conquered Qielan and Nanyue, establishing Zoke County. Yelanghou submitted and was named king. Other tribes, shocked, requested Han officials. Han set up Yuesi, Shenli, Lunshan, and Wudu counties. The Dian king, with tens of thousands of troops, initially refused to submit. After Han destroyed Laojin and Mimo, Dian surrendered, becoming Yizhou County. The Dian king received a royal seal, favored by Han.

translation:
There were hundreds of princes in southwestern Yi, but only the princes of Yelang and Dian accepted the royal seal.
Dian is a small country that was most favored by the Han Dynasty.
Tai Shigong said: Did the ancestors of Chu have a salary and position given by God?
During the Zhou Dynasty, their ancestor Wan Xiong became the teacher of King Zhou Wen. Later, Xiong Yi was granted the title of King Zhou Cheng to the land of Chu barbarians and established his country. By the time the Zhou Dynasty declined, the territory of Chu State was known as five thousand miles.
The Qin State destroyed its princes, and only the descendants of the Chu State still had the King of Dian.
The Han Dynasty killed the southwestern barbarians, and most of the countries there were wiped out. Only the King of Dian was favored by the Emperor of Han.
But the beginning of the pacification of Nanyi was the sight of Gojiang in Panyu and the sight of Qiong Bamboo Staff in Daxia.
Xiyi was later divided into the west and south, and was finally divided into seven counties by the King of Han.
summary: Tai Shigong noted that Chu's descendants, including the Dian king, survived Qin's destruction. Han pacified southwestern barbarians, with Dian favored. The pacification began with sightings of Gojiang in Panyu and Qiong bamboo sticks in Daxia, leading to the division of Xiyi into seven counties.

translation:
Lao Tzu said: When the world is at its most prosperous, although neighboring countries can see each other and can hear the crows of cocks and dogs, the people of each country will consider their own food to be the most delicious and their own clothes to be the most beautiful. They will be content with the customs of their hometowns and love their own industries, and they will not interact with each other until they grow old and die.
In modern times, if we continue to act in this way, it will be equivalent to blocking the people's ears and eyes, and it will be almost impossible to work.
Tai Shigong said: I don’t know anything about Shennong’s past.
As for the situation since the Yu and Xia dynasties described in the "Poems" and "Books", the ears and eyes want to enjoy the beauty of music and female sex, the mouth wants to taste all kinds of meat and delicacies, and they live in debauchery and pleasure, and their hearts boast about the glory of power.
This evil custom has been used to infect the people for a long time. Even if you use Lao Tzu's wonderful theories to persuade and enlighten them door to door, you will never be able to change them.
So the best way is to let nature take its course, the second is to take advantage of the situation, the third is to educate them, the third is to correct their behavior, and the worst way is to fight with them.
The west of Mount Wei is rich in wood, bamboo, mulberry, wild hemp, oxtail, and jade; the east of Mount Mount is rich in fish, salt, lacquer, silk, and beauties; the south of the Yangtze River is rich in nanmu, catalpa, ginger, osmanthus, gold, tin, lead, cinnabar, Rhinoceros, tortoise shells, beads, and ivory skins; Longmen and the area north of Jieshi Mountain are rich in horses, cattle, sheep, felt fur, animal sinews and horns; copper and iron are distributed thousands of miles around, and the mountains are everywhere, like chess pieces.
This is the general situation about the distribution of products in various places. These are the things that the Chinese people like and use to wear, eat, maintain health, and prepare for death.
Therefore, people rely on farmers to cultivate and obtain food, they rely on Yu people to mine in the mountains and fishermen to hunt in the water to obtain items, they rely on craftsmen to manufacture and obtain utensils, and they rely on merchants to trade and circulate goods.
Does this still require the government to issue a decree, recruit people, and gather within a time limit?
People rely on their own talents and do their best to satisfy their own desires.
Therefore, low-priced goods can be sold at high prices, and high-priced goods can be purchased at low prices. People work hard at their own business and are happy to do their own work, just like water flowing from high to low. Day and night without end, they will come automatically without being called, and they will be produced without asking.
Isn’t this proof that it follows the laws and develops naturally?
"Book of Zhou" says: If farmers don't farm, there will be a shortage of food; if craftsmen don't work and produce, there will be a shortage of utensils; if merchants don't do business, the three treasures of food, use, and money will be cut off; if the Yu people don't develop mountains and rivers, there will be a shortage of resources. If resources are scarce, mountains and rivers cannot be further developed.
The four fields of agriculture, industry, commerce, and agriculture are the sources of food and clothing for the people.
summary: It argues that human desires for pleasure, wealth, and power are deeply ingrained and cannot be changed by persuasion. The best governance, therefore, is to let nature take its course, followed by guiding, educating, and correcting, with conflict as the last resort. The text then describes the natural distribution of resources across different regions of China, from the west of Mount Wei to the east of Mount Tai, the south of the Yangtze River, and the north of Longmen. It explains that people rely on farmers, miners, fishermen, craftsmen, and merchants to meet their needs, and that this economic activity occurs naturally without government decree, driven by self-interest and the pursuit of profit. The "Book of Zhou" is cited to emphasize that agriculture, industry, commerce, and resource extraction are the four pillars of a nation's wealth.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/货殖列传

translation:
If the source is large, the country will be rich; if the source is small, the country will be poor; if the source is large, it can make the country rich and strong, and if it is small, it can make the family rich.
Rich or poor, no one can take away or give to others, but smart people always have more than enough wealth, while stupid people often have insufficient food and clothing.
Therefore, when Jiang Taigong was sealed in Yingqiu, it was mostly saline-alkali land and sparsely populated. So Jiang Taigong encouraged women to devote themselves to textile and embroidery, strongly promoted craft skills, and asked people to transport fish and sea salt back to other areas. As a result, people and property from other countries flowed back to Qi State, like ropes connected to each other, in an endless stream, like the spokes of a car gathered at the hub, gathering there from all directions.
Therefore, because Qi State can make crowns, belts, clothes and shoes for the world, the princes from the East China Sea and Mount Tai all dress up and go to Qi State to worship.
Later, when the state of Qi declined, Guan Zhong re-established Jiang Taigong's career and established nine offices to manage finances, allowing Duke Huan of Qi to dominate. He joined the princes as the overlord many times and rectified the world's politics. Guan Zhong himself also had three returns. Although his official position was only that of a minister, he was richer than the monarchs of other countries.
From then on, Qi became prosperous and strong until the era of King Wei and King Xuan.
Therefore, it is said: If the warehouse is abundant, one will know etiquette; if one has sufficient food and clothing, one will know honor and disgrace.
Ritual comes from wealth and is discarded from poverty.
Therefore, when a gentleman is rich, he likes to do virtuous things; when common people are rich, they will do what they can.
When rivers are deep, fish will live in them; when mountains and forests are deep, wild animals will hide there; when a person is rich, benevolence and righteousness will benefit him.
When a rich man gains power, he becomes more prominent, but when he loses power, the guests who rely on him will have nowhere to stay, so they will feel unhappy.
In Yi Di, this situation is even more prominent.
The proverb says: A person with a rich family will not break the law and be punished and die in a busy city.
This is not empty talk.
Therefore, it is said: People in the world are bustling with each other, all coming and leaving for profit.
Those kings who own thousands of chariots, the princes who enjoy the fiefdoms of ten thousand households, and the officials who own hundreds of fiefdoms. If you are worried that you will become poor, let alone the ordinary people who are registered in the household registration!
Once upon a time, King Gou Jian of Yue was besieged on Kuaiji Mountain, so he appointed Fan Li and Ji Ran.
If you are good at comparing time and usage, you can clearly see the supply and demand of various goods. Therefore, when the year is in gold, there will be a good harvest; when it is in water, there will be a poor harvest; when it is in wood, there will be famine; when it is in fire, there will be drought.
When there is a drought, boats must be prepared to wait for floods; when there are floods, vehicles must be prepared for drought. This is in line with the laws of development of things.
Generally speaking, there is a good harvest every six years, a drought every six years, and a great famine every twelve years.
If grain is sold for 20 qian per dou, farmers will suffer losses; if the price is 90 qian per dou, merchants will suffer losses.
If businessmen suffer losses, money cannot circulate to society; if farmers suffer losses, their fields will become barren.
The maximum price of grain per bucket should not exceed eighty yuan and the minimum price should not be less than thirty yuan, so both farmers and businessmen can benefit. Selling food at a fair price, stabilizing and adjusting the prices of other commodities, and ensuring that there is no shortage of customs tax revenue and market supply is the way to govern a country.
As for the stored goods, they should be in good condition and reliable, and there should be no stranded monetary funds.
When buying and selling goods, do not hide items that are susceptible to corruption and corrosion for a long time, and do not risk hoarding them in order to get a higher price.
If you study the situation of surplus or shortage of goods, you will understand the reason why prices rise and fall. If the price reaches the extreme, it will return to dependence; if the price reaches the extreme, it will return to the expensive side.
When goods are extremely expensive, they should be sold in time and treated as dirt; when goods are extremely expensive, they should be purchased in time and treated as jewelry.
The circulation of goods and coins should be like running water.
summary: Historical examples illustrate the principles of wealth creation. Jiang Taigong turned the barren, sparsely populated state of Qi into a prosperous center of trade and manufacturing by encouraging textile production and commerce. Later, Guan Zhong continued this work, enabling Duke Huan of Qi to become a hegemon. The text emphasizes that a full granary leads to knowledge of etiquette, and that wealth enables virtuous behavior. It also details the strategies of Ji Ran, who advised King Gou Jian of Yue on managing resources and prices based on cyclical patterns of good and bad years, leading to Yue's wealth and eventual victory over Wu. Fan Li, who implemented these strategies, later applied them to personal business, becoming immensely wealthy as Tao Zhugong.

translation:
If he wanted to increase his financial income, he would buy inferior grain; if he wanted to increase the weight of each bushel of grain, he would buy the best grain.
He can not pay attention to food and drink, control his hobbies, save on clothing, share the joys and sorrows with his hired servants, and seize opportunities to make money as quickly as beasts of prey seize food.
Therefore, he said: I do business to get rich, just like Yi Yin and Lu Shang planned strategies, like Sun Tzu and Wu Qi in using military tactics, and like Shang Yang in promoting reforms.
Therefore, if a person is not wise enough to adapt to changes, courageous enough to make decisive decisions, benevolent enough to make correct choices, and strong enough to persist, even if he wants to learn my skills in doing business and getting rich, I will not teach him.
Therefore, people all over the world follow Bai Gui's example when talking about how to get rich in business.
Bai Gui probably tried something, and he was able to achieve something by trying. This is not something that can be done casually.
Yidun started his business by operating Chiyan.
However, Guo Zong of Handan built his family business by smelting iron, and his wealth was comparable to that of princes.
There was a famous man in Wushi County who was engaged in animal husbandry. When the livestock multiplied in large numbers, he sold them all, then purchased various strange things and silk fabrics, and secretly presented them to King Rong.
King Rong gave him ten times the amount of the things he had donated, and gave him livestock. The livestock were so numerous that the number of cattle and horses was measured in the valley.
Qin Shihuang decreed that Wu Shiluo's status should be the same as that of the feudal lord, and he should go to the palace to pay homage with other ministers at the specified time.
However, the ancestors of Widow Qing of Bajun obtained the cinnabar mine and monopolized its profits for several generations, and their family property was also numerous.
Qing is a widow who can keep her ancestors' family property and use money to protect herself from being invaded by others.
Qin Shihuang thought she was a chaste woman and treated her as a guest. He also built a female concubine Qingtai for her.
Wu Shiluo was just a humble man from the frontier and a master of livestock. Widow Qing of Bajun was a widow from a poor country, but she could stand up to a monarch with thousands of military chariots and become famous all over the world. Isn't this relying on their wealth?
With the rise of the Han Dynasty and the unification of the world, they opened up key roads and lifted the ban on mining mountains and rivers. As a result, wealthy merchants and merchants were able to travel around the world, and all goods traded were smooth, and their desires were satisfied. The Han government also moved heroes, princes, and wealthy families to the capital.
The Guanzhong area stretches from Qian and Yong counties to the east to the Yellow River and Huashan, with fertile soil and fields covering thousands of miles in radius. From the time when the Yu clan and the Xia Hou clan paid tribute, this land was classified as high-quality land. Later Gong Liu moved to Pi, King Tai and Wang Ji of Zhou moved to Qishan, King Wen of Zhou built Fengyi, and King Wu of Zhou governed Haojing. Therefore, the people in these places still have the legacy of their ancestors. They like farming, plant grains, attach great importance to the land, and take doing bad things very seriously.
Until Qin Wen Gong, De Gong, and Mu Gong established their capital in Yongyi, it was located on the main road for the exchange of goods between Long and Shu, so there were many merchants.
summary: The text profiles several other successful individuals, including Bai Gui, who mastered market timing and price speculation; Yi Dun, who made a fortune from salt; and Guo Zong, who profited from iron smelting. It also notes the rise of Wu Shiluo, a livestock trader who gained favor with King Rong and was later honored by Qin Shi Huang, and Widow Qing of Bajun, who maintained her family's cinnabar monopoly and was also respected by the emperor. These examples demonstrate that wealth can elevate even humble individuals to a status comparable to feudal lords.

translation:
However, Handan is also a city between Zhangshui and the Yellow River.
It connects Yan and Zhuo to the north, and Zheng and Wei to the south.
The customs of Zheng and Wei are similar to those of Zhao, but they are close to Liang and Lu, and the people are a little more solemn and pay attention to moral integrity.
Wei Yuanjun moved from Diqiu, the city of Pushang, to Yewang. The people in the Yewang area liked fighting spirit and allowed chivalrous people to commit crimes, which was a legacy of the Wei Dynasty.
Ji, the ancient capital of Yan State, is also a city between Bohai Sea and Jieshi Mountain.
It borders Qi and Zhao in the south, and borders the Hu people in the northeast.
The area from Shanggu to Liaodong is far away, sparsely populated, and has been repeatedly invaded. The folk customs are generally similar to those in the Zhao and Dai areas, but the people are agile and fierce, lacking in thought. The local area is rich in fish, salt, dates, and chestnuts.
It is adjacent to Wuhuan and Fuyu to the north, and is in a favorable position to control Guhugu, Korea and Zhenfan to the east.
If you go east from Luoyang, you can do business in Qi and Lu, and if you go south, you can do business in Liang and Chu.
Therefore, the southern part of Mount Tai is the hometown of Lu State, and the northern part is the hometown of Qi State.
The land is surrounded by mountains and seas, and there is fertile soil for thousands of miles, suitable for growing mulberry and hemp. The people have many colorful silks, cloth and fish salt.
Linzi is also a city between the East China Sea and Mount Tai.
The local folk customs are tolerant and open-minded, but also resourceful and love to talk. They have strong local values ​​and are not easy to drift out. They are timid in gathering crowds to fight, but dare to hurt others secretly. Therefore, they often rob other people's property. This is the custom of a big country.
Here there are all kinds of people including scholars, farmers, workers, merchants and businessmen.
Zou and Lu are adjacent to the Zhu River and the Sishui River, and still retain the legacy of Zhou Gong. The folk customs favor Confucianism and complete etiquette, so the local people are cautious and restrained.
Many people are engaged in the mulberry and hemp industry, but do not have the resources of mountains, forests, and rivers.
The land is small and the population is large. People are stingy, afraid of crime, and avoid evil.
When it declines, people like to do business and pursue wealth, which is even more powerful than the people in the surrounding areas.
From the east of Honggou, to the north of Mangshan and Dangshan, to Juye, this was the hometown of Liang and Song Dynasties.
Taoyi and Suiyang are also cities.
In the past, Tang Yao rose up in Chengyang, Yu Shun fished in Leize, and Shang Tang established his capital in Hao.
The folk customs here still have the legacy of the previous kings. They are generous and dignified, and there are many gentlemen who like farming. Although there are no rich mountains and rivers, people can live frugally in order to accumulate wealth.
The Yue and Chu regions have different customs from the three regions of Western Chu, Eastern Chu and Southern Chu.
From Peijun in Huaibei to Chenjun, Runan, and Nanjun, this is the Western Chu region.
The folk customs here are strong and agile, easy to anger, the land is barren, and there is little accumulation of wealth.
Jiangling was originally the capital of Chu State, connected to Wu County and Ba County in the west, and Yunmeng in the east, which was rich in products.
Chen is at the junction of Chu and Xia, where fish and salt goods are circulated, and most of the residents are merchants.
summary: The text then surveys the economic geography and customs of various regions under the Han Dynasty, from the fertile Guanzhong area to the remote Bashu region, and from the central plains of Hedong, Hanoi, and Henan to the northern frontiers of Yan and Dai. It describes how local products, trade routes, and historical legacies shape the economic activities and social character of each area. For instance, the people of Qi are resourceful and love to talk, while those of Zou and Lu are cautious and favor Confucian etiquette. The text concludes that all people, whether officials, merchants, farmers, or outlaws, are ultimately driven by the pursuit of wealth.

translation:
The ancestor of the Ren family in Xuanqu was a guard in charge of Daocang.
When the Qin Dynasty was defeated, the heroes all competed for gold, silver and jewels, while the Ren family alone used the cellar to store rice and millet.
Later, the armies of Chu and Han were at war in Xingyang. Farmers were unable to cultivate their fields. The price of rice rose to ten thousand yuan per stone. Ren made a fortune by selling grain. All the gold, silver and jewelry of the heroes belonged to Ren, and Ren made a fortune.
Most wealthy people strive for luxury, but the Ren family is submissive, advocating frugality, and devoting themselves to farmland and animal husbandry.
Most people compete to buy fields and livestock at low prices, but Ren specializes in buying expensive and good ones.
The Ren family has been wealthy for generations.
However, the Ren family's family contract stipulates that they cannot wear or eat items that are not obtained from their own farming and raising livestock, and they are not allowed to drink alcohol or eat meat until their official duties are completed.
He set an example for his fellow villagers, so he was rich and the emperor respected him.
When the frontier areas were opened up, only Qiao Yao obtained a thousand horses, two thousand cattle, ten thousand sheep, and tens of thousands of grains.
When the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled against the central court of the Han Dynasty, the princes and princes in Chang'an wanted to go out for the army and needed to borrow money with interest. The loan sharks believed that the princes and princes' food capitals were all in Guandong, and the outcome of the war in Guandong had not yet been decided, so no one was willing to lend them money.
Only the Wuyan clan loaned them thousands of gold, and the interest was ten times the principal.
Three months later, Wu Chu was pacified. In one year, the Wuyan family received ten times the interest on their principal, making them as wealthy as the wealthy people in Guanzhong.
Most of the wealthy businessmen in the Guanzhong area are from families named Tian, ​​such as Tian Si and Tian Lan.
There are also the Li family of the Wei family, the Du family of Anling and Du County, and their family assets also amount to tens of millions of money.
The above people are all famous and unique people.
None of them had titles, titles, salaries, or made fortunes by dancing, writing, or breaking laws. They all relied on speculation, making choices, adapting to circumstances, and making profits. They became rich by running commerce and industry, purchased land and engaged in agriculture to keep money, seized everything with various powerful means, and maintained it through written methods such as laws and decrees. The changes were like this, so it is worth recording.
As for those who devote themselves to agriculture, animal husbandry, handicrafts, mountains and forests, fishing and hunting, or business, they have become rich by virtue of their power and wealth. The big ones can overwhelm a county, the medium ones overwhelm a county, and the small ones overwhelm the villages. There are countless people.
Careful planning, hard work and frugality are the right ways to get rich, but those who want to get rich must also succeed unexpectedly.
Farming is a cumbersome industry, but Qin Yang relied on it to become the richest man in a state.
Tomb robbing was originally a criminal activity, but Uncle Tian made his fortune through it.
Gambling is a bad behavior, but Huan Fa made a fortune by relying on it.
Walking hawking is a despicable job for men, but Yong Lecheng made a fortune from it.
Selling grease was a shameful business, but Yong Bo made a fortune from it.
Selling water slurry was originally a small business, but Zhang made 10 million yuan from it.
Knife sharpening is a small craft, but the Zhi family relied on it to become rich and prosperous.
Selling sheep tripe was a trivial matter, but Zhuo became so rich through it that he could travel with horses and carriages.
Treating horses is a superficial skill, but Zhang Li became so rich by it that he struck the bell for food.
These people became rich because of their single-mindedness.
From this point of view, getting rich does not depend on a fixed industry, and wealth does not have a certain owner. People with skills can accumulate wealth, while people without skills will destroy their wealth.
A family with a thousand pieces of gold can be as good as the king of a city, and a rich man with a fortune of tens of millions can enjoy the same enjoyment as a king.
summary: The final section provides a detailed account of various profitable enterprises and the individuals who excelled at them. It lists the annual output of goods—such as wine, vinegar, livestock, grain, and timber—that can generate wealth comparable to a noble household. It then profiles specific successful families, like the Zhuo family of Shu, who prospered through iron smelting after being relocated, and the Ren family of Xuanqu, who stored grain during a famine and became wealthy. The text emphasizes that wealth can be achieved through diverse means, from farming and commerce to seemingly humble trades like selling water or sharpening knives, and that success depends on skill and adaptability rather than a fixed profession. Ultimately, it asserts that a wealthy person can enjoy a status akin to a king, a condition it calls "Su Feng."

translation:
Li Shiqi was from Gaoyang, Chenliu.
He likes to study very much, but his family is poor and destitute. He doesn't even have a property that can afford to clothe and feed himself, so he has to work as a lowly clerk looking after the inner door.
But despite this, the wise men and powerful men in the county did not dare to use him casually. People in the county called him "Kangsheng".
When Chen Sheng, Xiang Liang and others rebelled against the Qin Dynasty, dozens of generals passed through Gaoyang when they attacked the city. However, Li Shiqi heard that these people were narrow-minded, liked trivial etiquette, were self-willed, and could not listen to open-minded words. So he lived in seclusion and hid himself, not to cater to these people.
Later, he heard that Pei Gong led troops to capture the city and came to the outskirts of Chenliu. One of Pei Gong's cavalrymen happened to be the son of an old friend of Li Shi's neighborhood. Pei Gong often asked him about the wise men and heroes in his hometown.
One day, when the cavalry came home, Li Shiqi saw him and said to him: I heard that Pei Gong was arrogant and looked down upon others, but he had many far-reaching strategies. This is the person I really want to follow, but I have no one to introduce him to him.
When you see Pei Gong, you can say this to him: There is a Mr. Li in my hometown who is over sixty years old and eight feet tall. People call him a crazy person, but he himself says that he is not a crazy person.
The cavalryman replied: Pei Gong does not like Confucian scholars. Many people came to see him wearing Confucian scholar hats. He immediately took off their hats and urinated in them.
When he talked to people, he often cursed.
So you'd better not lobby him as a Confucian scholar.
Li Shiqi said: Just say it like I taught you.
After the knight returned, he told Pei Gong according to Li Sheng's instructions.
Later, Pei Gong came to Gaoyang, stayed in an inn, and sent someone to summon Li Shiqi to come and see him.
When Li Sheng came to the hotel, Pei Gong sat on the bed with his legs spread apart and asked two women to wash his feet. He called Li Sheng to see him.
Li Sheng went in, only made a long salute without leaning down to worship, and said: "Do you want to help Qin attack the princes, or do you want to lead the princes to destroy Qin?"
Pei Gong scolded: You Confucian scholar!
The people of the world have been suffering from the Qin Dynasty for a long time, so the princes have raised armies to resist the violent Qin one after another. How can you help the Qin Dynasty attack the princes?
Li Sheng said: If you are determined to gather the people and call for volunteers to overthrow the tyrannical and cruel Qin Dynasty, you should not receive the elders in such a arrogant and disrespectful manner.
So Pei Gong immediately stopped washing his feet, tidied his clothes, invited Li Sheng to the guest's seat, and apologized to him.
Li Sheng talked about the strategy used by the six kingdoms to unite vertically and horizontally. Pei Gong was very happy and ordered people to bring rice for Li Sheng to eat. Then he asked: "Then how do you think we should formulate our strategy today?"
Li Sheng said: If you gather the rabble and scattered soldiers, the total is less than 10,000 people. If you use this to directly confront the powerful Qin, it will be what people often say is exploring the tiger's mouth.
Chenliu is an important transportation thoroughfare in the world, extending in all directions. Now there is a lot of grain in the city.
I am very close to the magistrate of Chenliu. Please send me to him to ask him to surrender to you.
If he doesn't obey, you can send troops to attack the city again, and I can act as an internal response in the city.
So Pei Gong sent Li Sheng there and followed closely with his own troops. In this way, he captured Chenliu and gave Li Sheng the title of Lord of Guangye.
Li Sheng recommended his younger brother Li Shang to lead thousands of people to follow Pei Gong to the southwest to capture the city.
Li Sheng himself often served as a lobbyist and traveled among the princes as an envoy.
summary: Li Shiqi, a learned man from Gaoyang, Chenliu, lived in poverty and worked as a lowly clerk. Despite his humble status, local elites dared not employ him casually, calling him "Kangsheng." During the rebellions against Qin, he avoided serving narrow-minded generals until he heard of Pei Gong (Liu Bang). Through a cavalryman, he arranged a meeting. When they met, Pei Gong was washing his feet with two women, but Li Shiqi criticized his disrespect, prompting Pei Gong to apologize. Li Shiqi advised capturing Chenliu for its strategic location and grain stores, offering to persuade the magistrate to surrender. Pei Gong agreed, and with Li Shiqi's help, Chenliu was taken. Li Shiqi was titled Lord of Guangye and later recommended his brother Li Shang to serve Pei Gong. An alternate account describes Li Shiqi's earlier meeting with Pei Gong, where he insisted on being called a "drunkard" rather than a scholar, criticized Pei Gong's disrespect, and again advised capturing Chenliu. He killed the magistrate at night, enabling Pei Gong to take the city and raise troops. Sima Qian notes that later accounts misplace Li Shiqi's role, but he confirms the details through his friendship with Pingyuanjun's son.
