translation:
Li Sheng replied: King Han and King Xiang jointly marched westward to attack the Qin Dynasty. They had clearly agreed in front of Emperor Yi that the one who conquered Xianyang first would be crowned king there.
The King of Han first invaded Xianyang, but King Xiang broke the covenant and refused to allow him to become king in Guanzhong, instead allowing him to go to Hanzhong to become king.
King Xiang moved Emperor Yi and sent people to assassinate him. After the King of Han heard the news, he immediately mobilized the Shu Han army to attack the Three Qin Dynasties. He went out of Hangu Pass to inquire where Emperor Yi had moved, gathered the troops from all over the world, and supported the descendants of the former six kingdoms.
When a city is captured, he will immediately grant marquisships to the meritorious generals, and immediately distribute the treasures to the soldiers, sharing the benefits with the world, so those heroes and talented people are willing to serve him.
The armies of the princes came from all directions, and the grain ships of the Shu Han were continuously sent down the river next to the ships.
King Xiang not only had a bad reputation for betraying the covenant, but also had the unjust act of killing the Righteous Emperor; he never remembered the merits of others, but never forgot the sins of others; the soldiers won no rewards for winning battles, and they did not receive titles for capturing cities; it was not their Xiang family. No one in the world is given important treatment; he carves the seal of marquis for those who have meritorious service, and plays with it repeatedly in his hands, unwilling to grant it; he would rather pile up the wealth obtained by attacking the city than give it to everyone; therefore, the people of the world betray him, the outstanding people resent him, and no one is willing to serve him.
Therefore, all the scholars in the world have surrendered to the King of Han, and the King of Han can command them from his seat.
The King of Han led the army of Shu Han to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, occupied a large area of ​​land outside the Xihe River, led the elite troops of the Shangdang who surrendered, captured Jingxing, and killed Lord Cheng'an; he defeated Wei Bao of Hebei and occupied thirty-two cities: just like the invincible Chi You's army, it did not rely on human strength, but was the result of God's blessing.
Now the king of Han has seized the grain of Aocang, blocked the dangerous fortress of Chenggao, guarded the White Horse Ferry, blocked the main road of Daxing, and guarded the Fehu Pass. If the princes of the world want to surrender in the end, they will be destroyed first.
If you surrender to the King of Han quickly, the state of Qi can still be preserved; if you do not surrender to the King of Han, the moment of peril will come soon.
Tian Guang believed that Li Sheng's words were right, so he obeyed Li Sheng, removed all military defense and war preparations, and drank and had fun with Li Sheng every day.
Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, heard that Li Sheng had made a trip in the car without any effort, and had captured more than 70 cities in Qi State with his sharp tongue. He was very unconvinced, so he took advantage of the cover of night to lead his troops across the plains to secretly attack Qi State.
King Tian Guang of Qi heard that the Han soldiers had arrived and thought that Li Sheng had betrayed him, so he said to Li Sheng: If you can stop the Han army from attacking, I will let you live. If not, I will cook you to death!
Li Sheng said: People who do great things do not stick to trivial matters, and people with great virtues are not afraid of others' criticism.
Your father will not lobby Han Xin on your behalf!
In this way, the King of Qi killed Li Sheng and led his troops to escape eastward.
In the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Li Shang, the Marquis of Quzhou, led troops to attack Yingbu in his capacity as prime minister.
When Emperor Gaozu was enfeoffing feudal princes and attacking his ministers, he missed Li Shiqi very much.
Li Shiqi's son Li Shi led troops to fight many times, but his military exploits did not reach the level of a marquis. The emperor made Li Shi a Marquis of Gaoliang because of his father.
summary: During the Chu-Han conflict, Li Shiqi advised the King of Han to hold Aocang's grain and key fortresses instead of retreating. He then volunteered to persuade the King of Qi to submit to Han. The King of Han agreed. Li Shiqi convinced King Tian Guang of Qi that the world's hearts turned to Han due to Han's generosity and Xiang Yu's failures. Tian Guang surrendered and removed defenses. However, Han Xin, jealous of Li Shiqi's success, attacked Qi by night. Tian Guang, believing Li Shiqi betrayed him, threatened to boil him alive. Li Shiqi refused to lobby Han Xin and was executed. Later, Emperor Gaozu enfeoffed Li Shiqi's son as Marquis of Gaoliang, a title passed for three generations until it was revoked.

translation:
Later, the place of residence was changed to Wusui, and the title was passed down to three generations.
In the first year of Yuanshou, Li Ping, Marquis of Wu Sui, defrauded King Hengshan of one hundred kilograms of gold by falsely claiming the emperor's order. The crime he committed should have been executed on the street, but at this time, he died of illness and the fiefdom was revoked.
Lu Jia was a native of the Chu State. He followed Emperor Gaozu to pacify the world as a guest of staff. People at that time called him a very eloquent lobbyist, so he accompanied Emperor Gaozu and often traveled to various vassal states as envoys.
When Emperor Gaozu had just pacified the Central Plains, Wei Ta also pacified South Vietnam and established himself as king there.
Emperor Gaozu considered that the world had been settled for the first time, so he did not execute Wei Ta. He also sent Lu Jia with the seal of the King of South Vietnam given to Wei Ta to appoint him.
When Lu Sheng arrived in South Vietnam, he wore his hair in an awl-like bun popular in the area, sat with his legs spread like a dustpan, and met Lu Sheng.
Lu Sheng said to Wei Ta: You are from the Central Plains, and the graves of your relatives, brothers and ancestors are all in Zhending.
But now that you have gone against the customs of the Central Plains people, abandoned your clothes and scarves, and want to use Xiaonan, who has only a small place, to compete with the emperor and become an enemy country, then your disaster will be imminent.
Moreover, the Qin Dynasty was tyrannical and ruthless, and all the princes and heroes rose up one after another. Only the King of Han entered the pass first and occupied Xianyang.
Xiang Yu betrayed the alliance and established himself as the overlord of Western Chu. The princes all belonged to him, and he could be said to be extremely powerful.
But after the King of Han sent troops from Bashu, he conquered the world, pacified the princes, killed Xiang Yu, and destroyed Chu.
Within five years, the world was at peace. This is not something that humans can do, but is the result of God’s help.
Now the Emperor of the Han Dynasty has heard that you are proclaimed king in South Vietnam and is unwilling to help the people of the world to quell the rebellion. The generals and ministers of the Han Dynasty want to lead their troops to destroy you. But the emperor cherishes the people and thinks that they have just experienced the hardships and chaos of the war, so he temporarily stopped the army and sent me to grant you the gold seal of the King of Nanyue, cut the talisman into a letter, and exchange envoys.
You should go to the outskirts to welcome us, face the north, and prostrate yourself as my vassal, but you want to be arrogant and unruly as a small South Vietnam that has just been established and has not yet gathered the people.
If the imperial court finds out about this, digs and burns the tombs of your ancestors, exterminates your clan, and then sends a general to lead a hundred thousand troops to Vietnam, then the South Vietnamese will kill you and surrender to the Han Dynasty, as easy as turning the back of their hand.
After Wei Ta heard this, he immediately stood up and apologized to Lu Sheng: "I have lived among the barbarians for a long time, so it is too rude."
Then, he asked Lu Sheng: Who is more virtuous and talented among me and Xiao He, Cao Shen, and Han Xin?
Lu Sheng said: You seem to be a little stronger than them.
He asked again: "How do I compare with the emperor?"
summary: Lu Jia, a Chu native and eloquent lobbyist, served Emperor Gaozu as an envoy. He was sent to appoint Wei Tuo as King of South Vietnam. Lu Jia criticized Wei Tuo's barbarian customs and warned that Han could destroy him. Wei Tuo apologized, acknowledged Han's superiority, and submitted. Lu Jia returned, was appointed Taizhong doctor, and wrote "New Speech" at the emperor's request, discussing statecraft. During Empress Dowager Lü's reign, he retired, distributed wealth to his sons, and traveled. He later advised Chancellor Chen Ping to ally with General Zhou Bo against the Lü clan, using gifts to secure their cooperation. After the Lü clan's fall, Lu Jia was sent to South Vietnam again, succeeding in enforcing Han rituals. He died of old age.

translation:
After Zhu Lu was killed and Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, Lu Sheng contributed a lot to this.
After Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, he wanted to send envoys to South Vietnam.
Prime Minister Chen Ping and others recommended Lu Sheng as the Taizhong doctor, sent him as an envoy to South Vietnam, and ordered the South Vietnamese king Wei to cancel the Yellow House title system and other Vietnamese rituals, and let him adopt the same etiquette and rituals as other princes.
After Lu Sheng went on his mission, he acted accordingly and the emperor's requirements were met, so Emperor Wen was very satisfied.
The specific plot of this matter is recorded in "Biographies of South Vietnam".
Lu Sheng finally died of old age. Pingyuan Marquis Zhu Jian was a native of Chu. At first, he served as the state minister of Huainan King Yingbu, but he left because of his guilt.
Later, he worked under Ying Bu again. When Ying Bu wanted to rebel, he asked Zhu Jian what he thought of the matter, and Zhu Jian strongly opposed it. But Yingbu did not listen to his advice, but did what Liang Fuhou said, so he rebelled.
After the Han Dynasty put down the rebellion and killed Yingbu, I heard that Zhu Jian, the king of Pingyuan, had advised Yingbu not to rebel. At the same time, he did not participate in the conspiracy of rebellion, so he did not kill Zhu Jian.
This matter is recorded in "The Biography of Qingbu".
Zhu Jian, Lord of Pingyuan, was eloquent and eloquent. At the same time, he was upright and adhered to the integrity and selfless integrity. Home is in Chang'an.
He never agrees casually with his words or deeds, adheres to moral principles and refuses to bend to please others.
Piyanghou Shenshi's behavior was not upright, and he won the favor of Empress Dowager Lu through flattery.
At that time, Marquis Piyang wanted to be on good terms with Lord Pingyuan, but Lord Pingyuan refused to see him.
When Pingyuanjun's mother passed away, Lu Sheng and Pingyuanjun had always been very close, so they went to express their condolences.
Mr. Pingyuan was from a poor family and did not even have the money to pay for his mother's funeral. He was about to borrow money to buy funeral supplies, but Lu Sheng told Mr. Pingyuan to just pay for the funeral without borrowing money.
Then Lu Sheng went to Piyanghou's home and congratulated him, saying: Pingyuanjun's mother passed away.
Marquis Piyang said in confusion: Mr. Pingyuan's mother is dead, why do you congratulate me?
Lu Sheng said: "You have always wanted to be on good terms with Mr. Pingyuan before, but he was a moral person and refused to associate with you. This was because of his mother."
Now that his mother has passed away, if you give him generous gifts for his mother's funeral, then he will definitely be willing to work desperately for you.
So Piyanghou sent a generous gift worth one hundred gold to Pingyuanjun.
At that time, many princes and nobles also sent money and goods worth a total of five hundred gold because of the heavy gifts given by the Marquis of Piyang.
Marquis Piyang was particularly favored by Empress Dowager Lu. Some people spoke ill of him in front of Emperor Xiaohui. Emperor Xiaohui was furious and arrested him and handed him over to the officials for interrogation, and wanted to take this opportunity to kill him.
Empress Dowager Lu felt ashamed and could not intercede for him.
Most of the ministers hated Piyanghou's scandalous behavior and wanted to take this opportunity to kill him.
Marquis Piyang was very anxious, so he sent someone to send a message to Lord Pingyuan, saying that he wanted to see him.
But Mr. Pingyuan declined and said: Your case is very tight now, and I dare not meet you.
Then Lord Pingyuan asked to see Hong Jiru, Emperor Xiaohui's favorite, and persuaded him: "Everyone in the world knows the reason why the emperor loves you."
summary: Pingyuanjun (Zhu Jian), a Chu native, served Yingbu but opposed his rebellion. After Yingbu's defeat, he was spared. He was upright, refusing to associate with the corrupt Piyanghou. When Pingyuanjun's mother died, Lu Jia advised Piyanghou to give generous funeral gifts, winning his favor. Later, when Piyanghou was imprisoned, Pingyuanjun persuaded the emperor's favorite Hong Jiru to intercede, securing his release. After Empress Dowager Lü's death, Pingyuanjun helped save Piyanghou again. Under Emperor Wen, Pingyuanjun was implicated in Piyanghou's crimes and committed suicide to protect his family. His son was appointed Taizhong doctor but died on a mission to the Xiongnu.

translation:
Confucius said: Use political laws to guide the people, and use punishments to restrain the people. The people can avoid committing crimes, but they will have no shame.
If you use morality to guide the people and use etiquette to restrain the people, then the people will feel ashamed and change their ways.
Laozi said: People with high morals do not show formal virtue, so they have virtue; people with low morals stick to formal virtue, so they have no actual virtue.  The more stringent the laws, the more thieves there are.
Tai Shigong said: These words are credible! Han Ling is a tool of politics, not the source of political turmoil.
In the past, the legal net in the world was very tight, but evil and deceitful things began to occur. When the situation reached its most serious state, officials and people actually deceived each other, reaching the point where the country was in ruins.
At this time, the management of government affairs by officials is like putting out fires with salary and quelling the boiling water. How can they be competent and happy without strong and powerful people and strict laws and regulations?
If people who advocate morality are allowed to do these things, they will definitely be derelict in their duties.
Therefore, Confucius said: When it comes to hearing lawsuits, I am the same as everyone else; if there must be a difference, then let people stop lawsuits. Lao Tzu said: Stupid and superficial people will laugh when they hear moral words.
These words are not false.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, the square ones were destroyed and replaced by round ones, and major changes were made to the laws of the Qin Dynasty, just like cutting off the external carvings to reveal the simple and natural essence. The laws were changed from complicated to lenient and simple, just like a fishing net that could catch the fish that swallowed the boat. However, the officials' performance was pure and prosperous, and they would not do evil things, and the people were safe.
It can be seen from this that the beauty of national politics lies in the generosity of the king, not in the harshness of the law.
In the High Empress era, the only cruel officials were Hou Feng, who harshly oppressed the royal family, violated and humiliated meritorious ministers.
After Zhu Lu's complete defeat, the court killed Hou Feng's entire family.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, Chao Cuo was harsh and cruel, and used magic to display his talents. As a result, the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, and others rebelled and vented their anger on Chao Cuo, who was killed.
After that, there were people like Zhidu and Ningcheng.
Zhi was a native of Yang County and served Emperor Xiaowen as a Langguan.
During the reign of Emperor Jing, Zhi Du became a lieutenant general. He dared to speak out and give advice to the court, and convinced people in person at the court.
He once followed the emperor to Shanglinyuan. When Jia Ji went to the toilet, a wild boar suddenly broke into the toilet.
The emperor signaled Zhidu with his eyes, but Zhidu refused to act.
The emperor wanted to save Jia Ji with weapons in person. Zhi Du knelt in front of the emperor and said: If you lose a concubine, another concubine will come into the palace. Is there a shortage of people like Jia Ji in the world?
Even if Your Majesty looks down upon yourself, what will happen to the Ancestral Temple and the Queen Mother?
The emperor turned around and the wild boar left.
The Queen Mother heard about this and rewarded Zhidu with a hundred catties of gold. From then on, she paid great attention to Zhidu.
summary: Laozi adds that strict laws increase theft. Tai Shigong affirms these views, noting that harsh legal nets in the past led to deceit and ruin. He observes that after the Han Dynasty simplified Qin laws, officials became honest and people peaceful, concluding that good governance relies on the ruler’s generosity, not legal severity.

translation:
There were more than 300 clans with the Jinan surname. They were powerful and slippery, and the governor of Jinan could not control them, so Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty appointed Zhi Du as the governor of Jinan.
When Zhidu came to Jinan County, he killed the whole family of the head of the family, and the rest of the bad guys were so frightened that their thighs trembled.
After more than a year, there are no more items found on the roads in Jinan County.
The governors of more than ten surrounding counties were as afraid of Zhi as they were of the superior officials.
Zhidu was brave, powerful, fair and honest. He would not open private letters asking for mercy or accept gifts, and he would not listen to personal requests.
He often said to himself: Since I have left my parents to become an official, I should fulfill my duties in the official position and die with integrity. After all, I cannot care about my wife and children.
Zhidu was promoted to the rank of lieutenant. Prime Minister Zhou Yafu had the highest rank and was arrogant. However, when Zhidu saw him, he only bowed to him and did not kneel down.
At this time, the people were simple, fearful of committing crimes, and were law-abiding and self-respecting. However, Zhidu took the initiative to implement harsh criminal laws, so that the law enforcement was not afraid of dignitaries and royal relatives. Even the princes and the royal family looked sideways and called him "Goshawk" when they saw him.
King Linjiang was summoned to the Lieutenant's Mansion for interrogation. King Linjiang wanted to get writing tools and wrote a letter to the emperor to express his apology. However, Zhidu told the officials not to give him writing tools.
Wei Qihou sent someone to secretly deliver writing tools to King Linjiang.
King Linjiang wrote a letter of apology to the emperor and committed suicide.
When Empress Dowager Dou heard the news, she became angry and used severe methods to slander Zhidu. Zhidu was dismissed from office and returned home.
Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty sent an envoy with a talisman to appoint Zhidu as the governor of Yanmen, and asked him to take the road directly to Yanmen to take office and handle political affairs independently according to the actual situation.
The Huns had always heard that Zhi Du had a moral integrity, and now he was guarding the border. Therefore, the Huns led their troops and left the Han Dynasty border. They did not dare to approach Yanmen until Zhi Du died.
The Huns even made puppets that looked like Zhidu and asked the cavalry to run and shoot. No one could hit them, and they were so afraid of Zhidu.
The Huns regarded Zhidu as a disaster.
Empress Dowager Dou finally used the laws of the Han Dynasty to slander Zhidu. Emperor Jing said: Zhidu are loyal ministers.
Want to free him.
Queen Mother Dou said: Isn't King Linjiang a loyal minister?
So they killed all Zhi.
Ning Cheng was a native of Rang County and served Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty as a bodyguard.
He is competitive, and when he is someone else's junior official, he must bully his superiors; when he is someone else's superior, he is as easy to control as tying wet sticks.
He was cunning, cruel, willful and powerful, and gradually rose to the rank of captain of Jinan. At this time, Zhi was also the prefect of Jinan.
Before this, several captains walked into the prefect's mansion, conveyed it through the lower-level officials, and then went to see the prefect, just like the county magistrate meeting the prefect. They were afraid of Zhidu and this was the way.
When Ning Cheng came, he crossed Zhidu and reached his superior position.
Zhidu had always heard of his reputation, so he treated him well and formed a friendly relationship with him.
After a long time, Zhidu died. Later, many people in the royal family near Chang'an committed violent crimes, so the emperor summoned Ning Cheng to become a lieutenant. His governance methods were imitated by Zhidu. His integrity was not as good as Zhidu, but everyone in the royal family was afraid of the powerful.
summary: The narrative then details cruel officials from the Han era. During Empress Gao’s reign, Hou Feng oppressed the royal family and was executed after the Lu clan’s fall. Under Emperor Jing, Chao Cuo’s harshness sparked the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms, leading to his death. Zhi Du, a lieutenant, was known for his bravery and integrity. He refused to save a concubine from a boar, earning the Empress Dowager’s favor. As governor of Jinan, he executed a powerful clan, ending crime. He was fair, refused bribes, and prioritized duty over family. He later arrested King Linjiang, who committed suicide, leading to Zhi Du’s dismissal and eventual execution by Empress Dowager Dou. Ning Cheng, a captain, was cunning and cruel, bullying superiors and subordinates alike. He imitated Zhi Du but lacked his integrity, though he intimidated the royal family. Under Emperor Wu, he was punished but later became wealthy through land rental, wielding influence over officials.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/酷吏列传

translation:
He and Zhang Tang jointly formulated various laws and made "knowledge laws" to allow officials to monitor and report each other.
The laws in the Han Dynasty became increasingly strict, probably starting from this time.
Zhang Tang is from Du County.
His father, who was the magistrate of Chang'an County, once went out. Zhang Tang was a child at the time, so his father asked him to stay at home and look after the door.
After his father came home, he saw that the mouse had stolen the meat. He became angry with Zhang Tang and beat him with a whip.
Zhang Tang dug a rat hole and found the rat that stole the meat and the uneaten meat. He accused the rat of the crime, tortured and interrogated it, recorded the interrogation process, repeatedly interrogated, reported the verdict to his superiors, took the rat and the leftover meat, and finally decided the case in court, and cut the rat into pieces and executed it.
His father was particularly surprised when he saw this scene and saw that the verdict looked like it was written by an experienced judge, so he asked him to learn Xing prison documents.
After his father's death, Zhang Tang became an official in Chang'an for a long time.
When Zhou Yang Hou Tian Sheng began to serve as an official of Jiuqing, he was detained in Chang'an, and Zhang Tang tried his best to rescue him.
After Tian Sheng was released from prison and made a marquis, he kept close contact with Zhang Tang and introduced the powerful officials of the dynasty to Zhang Tang one by one, so that Zhang Tang could get acquainted with them.
Zhang Tang served in the internal history and served as an official subordinate to Ning Cheng. Because Zhang Tang was unparalleled in talent, Ning Cheng recommended it to the superior government. Zhang Tang was promoted to Maolingwei and was in charge of the civil engineering of the tomb.
Tian Fan, Marquis of Wu'an, became the prime minister and recruited Zhang Tang as the internal historian. He often recommended him to the emperor and was appointed as the censor, allowing him to inspect and handle prison affairs.
When he presided over the handling of Queen Chen's witchcraft case, he investigated his accomplices in depth.
So Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty thought that he had the ability to do things, and gradually promoted him to Taizhong doctor.
Together with Zhao Yu, he formulated various legal provisions to be strict and strict to restrain the officials in office.
Soon, Zhao Yu was promoted to lieutenant and then to Shaofu, while Zhang Tang became a court lieutenant. The two had a friendly relationship, and Zhang Tang treated Zhao Yu with the same etiquette as he treated his elder brother.
Zhao Yu was an honest and arrogant man. Since he became an official, he has had no guests at home.
The Three Gongs and Nine Qings came to visit him, but Zhao Yu never returned the visit to thank him. He tried to cut off all contact with close friends and guests and handle his official affairs alone.
When he saw the legal provisions, he took them without reviewing them, in order to pursue the hidden sins of subordinate officials.
Zhang Tang is cunning and good at controlling others with his wisdom.
When he first became a minor official, he liked to use his power for personal gain. He once colluded with the wealthy businessmen Tian Jia and Yu Wengshu in Chang'an.
When he became the ninth minister, he made friends with famous scholars and officials all over the world. Although he disagreed with them in his heart, he pretended to admire them on the surface.
At this time, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was serious about Confucianism. When Zhang Tang decided on major cases, he wanted to adopt Confucian views, so he asked his PhD disciples to study "Shangshu" and "Spring and Autumn".
summary: Zhou Yangyou, a relative of the Huainan king, was tyrannical, bending laws to favor friends and kill enemies. He clashed with the governor Shentu Gong, leading to Shentu’s suicide and Zhou’s execution. Zhao Yu, a censor, co-created strict laws with Zhang Tang, increasing legal severity. Zhang Tang, from Du County, showed early talent in legal cases. He befriended powerful figures and rose to censor, crafting laws to control officials. He was cunning, pretending to admire Confucianism while using harsh methods. He handled major rebellions, minted coins, and monopolized salt and iron, draining state resources. His arrogance led to his downfall: after conflicts with officials and accusations of corruption, he committed suicide, leaving minimal wealth. His mother refused a lavish burial, and the emperor later executed his accusers.

translation:
He was fair in his work as an official, and was gradually promoted to Yushi and Zhongcheng.
The emperor assigned him to handle the rebellion case of Zhufu Yan and King Huainan. He used subtle legal provisions to investigate and slander, so many people were killed and he was praised for his courage to judge difficult cases.
He was dismissed and appointed many times, and he served as an official of Yushi and Zhongcheng for almost twenty years.
Wang Wenshu was relieved of his post of lieutenant and was reduced to the position of internal history officer.
He manages rice and salt matters, no matter how big or small, he has to personally handle them. He arranges the property and utensils of each specific department in the county by himself. Officials such as the county magistrate and county magistrate are not allowed to change them without authorization, and even use heavy laws to control them.
In the few years since he was an official, other counties have done some small things, but only reducing propaganda can turn small things into big things, and he can implement them with his own strength. Of course, his method cannot be regarded as a normal method.
He was dismissed from office midway, and later became You Fufeng. Because he was resentful of his subordinate Chengxin, Chengxin fled and hid in Shanglin Garden. The magistrate of Yi County was sent to kill Chengxin. When officials and soldiers shot Chengxin, they shot at the gate of Shanglinyuan. Jiaxuan was handed over to the judge for sentencing. The judge believed that he had committed treason and sentenced him to genocide, so Jiaxuan committed suicide.
Du Zhou was appointed.
Du Zhou was a native of Du Yan, Nanyang.
Yi Zong became the governor of Nanyang and regarded Du Zhou as his right assistant and recommended him to be the official of the imperial court.
He served Zhang Tang. Zhang Tang repeatedly said that he was extremely talented and his official position was promoted to censor.
He was assigned to examine the cases of deserted border soldiers, and many of them were sentenced to death.
The things he reported were in line with the emperor's wishes, and he was appointed. He was succeeded by Tongjiaxuan, and was appointed Zhongcheng for more than ten years.
Du Zhou's management of political affairs was similar to that of reducing propaganda, but he was cautious in handling affairs, slow in making decisions, loose in appearance, and deep in heart.
Jia Xuan became Zuo Neishi, and Du Zhou became Tingwei. He imitated Zhang Tang in governing political affairs, and was good at spying on the emperor's intentions.
If the emperor wants to exclude someone, he will take advantage of the opportunity to frame him; if the emperor wants to release him, he will imprison him for a long time pending trial and secretly reveal his grievances.
Some of the disciples scolded Du Zhou, saying: "I decided the case fairly for the emperor. I did not follow the five-foot law, but decided the case based on the emperor's will."
Is this what a judge is supposed to do?
Du Zhou said: How did the three-foot law come about?
In the past, what the king thought was right would be written into laws, and what later kings thought was right would be written down into decrees. What is appropriate for the situation at that time is correct. Why should we follow ancient laws?
When Du Zhou became a court lieutenant, the emperor ordered more and more cases to be handled.
Officials of the 2,000 stone level were arrested, old and new, no less than 100 people.
County officials and higher-level officials send more than a thousand cases to the Wei in a year.
summary: Yi Zong, a former robber, became a harsh official, executing hundreds in Dingxiang and terrorizing Nanyang. Wang Wenshu, a tomb robber, rose to governor, using informants and brutal tactics to eliminate thieves, boasting he needed more winter days to kill. He later became lieutenant, flattering the powerful while crushing the weak. He committed suicide after corruption charges. Yin Qi, a rigid official, killed without mercy, dying in poverty. The text concludes with a surge in banditry, leading to the “Senior Law” punishing officials for failing to catch thieves, which ironically increased crime. Jiaxuan and Du Zhou continued harsh practices, with Du Zhou justifying decisions based on the emperor’s will rather than law. Tai Shigong reflects that while some cruel officials like Zhi Du were principled, others like Du Zhou were sycophantic, leading to legal decay and corruption.

translation:
King Han Xin of Han was the concubine grandson of the original King Xiang of Han. He was eight feet five inches tall.
When Xiang Liang supported King Chu Huai, the descendant of King Chu, Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei had already established their own kings. Only South Korea had no successor, so Hancheng, Lord Hengyang among the Korean princes, was made King of Han, hoping to appease the land of the original South Korea.
Xiang Liang was defeated and died in Dingtao, and Han Cheng defected to King Huai of Chu.
When Pei Gong led the army to attack Yangcheng, he ordered Zhang Liang to surrender the original territory of South Korea as the Korean Situ. He obtained Han Xin and appointed him as the general of South Korea. He led his army to follow Pei Gong into Wuguan.
Pei Gong was appointed as the king of Han. Han Xin followed Pei Gong into Hanzhong and persuaded the king of Han: "Xiang Yu has sealed all his subordinates in the areas near the Central Plains, but you, the king, are in this far away place. This is tantamount to demotion!"
The soldiers under your command are all from the east of Mount Laoshan. They stand on tiptoe, eager to return to their hometown, so that while they are strong and strong, they can march eastward and compete for the world.
When the King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, he agreed to make Han Xin the King of Han. He first appointed him as Taiwei Han to lead troops to capture the old land of Korea.
The princes and kings granted by Xiang Yu all went to their respective fiefdoms. King Han Cheng of Han did not follow Xiang Yu in the battle and had no military exploits, so he was not sent to the fiefdom and instead made him a prince.
When he heard that the king of Han sent Han Xin to attack Han, he ordered Zheng Chang, the magistrate of Wu County when he was traveling in Wu, to be the king of Han to resist the Han army.
In the second year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Han Xin pacified more than a dozen cities in Korea.
When the King of Han arrived in Henan, Han Xin violently attacked King Zheng Chang of Han in Yangcheng.
When Zheng Chang surrendered, the King of Han made Han Xin the King of Han, and he often led the Korean army to follow the King of Han.
In the third year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han withdrew from Xingyang, and King Han Xin, Zhou Ke and others guarded Xingyang.
When the Chu army conquered Xingyang, Han Xin surrendered to the Chu army, escaped soon, and surrendered to the King of Han. The King of Han again made him King of Han, and finally followed the King of Han to defeat Xiang Yu and pacify the world.
In the spring of the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty cut the talisman with Han Xin as a letter and officially named him King of Han, with the fiefdom in Yingchuan.
In the spring of the next year, Emperor Gaozu thought that Han Xin was strong and brave, and his fief Yingchuan was close to Gongxian and Luoyang in the north, Wanxian and Yexian in the south, and the important town of Huaiyang in the east. These were all strategic places in the world, so he issued an edict and ordered Han Xin, the king of Han, to move to the north of Taiyuan to prepare for resistance to the Xiongnu and establish Jinyang as his capital.
Han Xin wrote: "My kingdom is close to the border. The Huns have invaded many times. Jinyang is far from the border. Please allow me to establish Mayi as the capital."
The emperor agreed, and Han Xin moved the capital to Mayi.
In the autumn of this year, the Xiongnu Maodun Shanyu surrounded Han Xin heavily. Han Xin sent envoys to the Xiongnu many times to sue for peace.
The Han Dynasty sent people to lead troops to rescue, but they suspected that Han Xin had sent envoys privately many times and had the intention of betraying the Han Dynasty, so he sent people to blame Han Xin.
Han Xin was afraid of being killed, so he made an agreement with the Xiongnu to jointly attack the Han Dynasty, raised an army to rebel, surrendered the capital of Mayi to the Xiongnu, and led his army to attack Taiyuan.
In the winter of the seventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the emperor personally led an army to attack Han Xin, defeated Han Xin's army in Tongdan, and beheaded his general Wang Xi.
Han Xin fled and defected to the Huns. His generals Manqichuchen, Wang Huang and others from the Bai Tu people supported Zhao Li, a descendant of King Zhao, as king. They also gathered Han Xin's defeated and fled army, and negotiated with Han Xin and the Xiongnu Maodun Shanyu to attack the Han Dynasty.
The Xiongnu sent the right and left wise kings to lead more than 10,000 cavalry and Wang Huang and others to station in the area south of Guangwu. When they arrived in Jinyang, they fought with the Han army. The Han army defeated them. They took advantage of the victory and pursued them to Lishi, where they were defeated again.
The Xiongnu again gathered troops in the Xijiang area of ​​Loufan, and Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty ordered chariot troops and cavalry to defeat them.
The Xiongnu were always defeated and fled, and the Han army took advantage of the victory to pursue the defeated troops. I heard that Maodun Shanyu was stationed in Daigu. Han Emperor Gaozu was in Jinyang at the time and sent people to scout Maodun. The scouts came back and reported that they could attack.
The emperor also arrived at Pingcheng.
When the emperor left the city and climbed Baishan Mountain, he was surrounded by the Huns' cavalry. The emperor sent people to give many gifts to the Queen of the Huns.
The Yan family then advised Maodun Shanyu, saying: Now that the land of the Han Dynasty has been captured, it is still impossible to live there; let alone the monarchs of the two countries do not besiege each other.
After seven days, the Huns cavalry gradually dispersed.
At that time, heavy fog fell from the sky, and the Han Dynasty sent people to travel between Baishan Mountain and Heping City. The Xiongnu did not notice at all.
Chen Ping, the lieutenant of the guard, said to the emperor: The Huns all use long spears and bows. Please order the soldiers to shoot two sharp arrows outwards with each strong crossbow, and slowly withdraw from the encirclement.
After retreating into Pingcheng, reinforcements from the Han Dynasty also arrived, and the Huns' cavalry finally relieved the siege and left.
The Han Dynasty also withdrew its troops and returned.
Han Xin led troops for the Huns to attack the Han army along the border.
In the tenth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, Han Xin ordered Wang Huang and others to persuade Chen Xi, causing him to misbelieve and rebel.
In the spring of the eleventh year, Han Xin, the former king of Han, invaded Shenhe together with the Huns cavalry to fight against the Han Dynasty.
The Han Dynasty sent General Chai to lead troops to attack. General Chai first wrote to Han Xin: Your Majesty the Emperor is generous and kind. Although some princes rebelled and fled, when they returned to submission again, they always restored their original titles and titles and did not execute them.
summary: King Han Xin of Han, a concubine grandson of the original King Xiang of Han, was a tall man. Initially, after Xiang Liang's defeat, Han Cheng was made King of Han to appease the region. Han Xin later served under Pei Gong (future Emperor Gaozu), persuading him to march eastward. He was eventually made King of Han after capturing Korean cities and defeating rival King Zheng Chang. However, fearing execution due to suspicions of betrayal, Han Xin allied with the Xiongnu, rebelled, and attacked Taiyuan. Emperor Gaozu personally defeated him, and Han Xin fled to the Xiongnu. He continued to lead Xiongnu forces against Han until General Chai killed him in battle. His descendants later surrendered to Han and were granted marquisates, though some titles were eventually revoked.

translation:
When Lu Wan came to his senses, he found some substitutes and executed them, freed Zhang Sheng's family members and made Zhang Sheng a spy for the Huns. He also secretly sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi's place, hoping to make him defect away for a long time, so that the war would continue year after year.
In the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, during the Eastern Campaign against Yingbu, Chen Kuai often led his troops to station in Dai. The Han Dynasty sent Fan Kuai to attack Chen Kuai and kill him.
One of his lieutenants surrendered and said that King Lu Wan of Yan sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi to exchange information and discuss plans.
Emperor Gaozu sent an envoy to summon Lu Wan to Beijing, but Lu Wan refused to go because he was ill.
The emperor also sent the Marquis of Piyang to review the food, and Zhao Yao, the imperial censor, went to greet King Yan, and also questioned King Yan's ministers.
Lu Wan was even more frightened and couldn't hide behind closed doors. He said to his favorite ministers: The only ones who were named kings without the surname Liu are me, Lu Wan, and Wu Rui, the king of Changsha.
Last spring, the Han Dynasty executed the entire family of Huaiyin Marquis Han Xin, and in the summer, they killed Peng Yue. This was Empress Lu's plan.
Now the emperor was seriously ill and handed over all state affairs to Queen Lu.
And Queen Lu was a woman who always wanted to find an excuse to kill princes, kings with different surnames and ministers with high achievements.
So Lu Wan still refused to go to Beijing, claiming to be ill.
Lu Wan's subordinates and ministers all fled and hid.
But some of Lu Wan's words leaked out. Marquis Piyang heard about it and reported all this to the emperor, who became even more angry.
Later, the Han Dynasty got some surrendered Huns and said that Zhang Sheng had fled to the Huns and was the envoy of King Yan.
So the emperor said: Lu Wan has really rebelled!
He sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan.
King Lu Wan of Yan settled all his family members and thousands of cavalry under the Great Wall, waiting for an opportunity, hoping that after the emperor recovered from his illness, he would come to Beijing to apologize in person.
In April, Emperor Gaozu passed away, and Lu Wan led his men to flee to the Huns, who named him King of Donghulu.
Lu Wan was invaded and plundered by the Huns, and always wanted to return to the Han Dynasty.
More than a year later, Lu Wan died in Xiongnu.
When he was the Queen of Gao, Lu Wan's wife and children escaped from the Xiongnu and returned to the Han Dynasty. Just as the Queen of Gao was seriously ill and could not see each other, they lived in King Yan's palace in Beijing and planned to hold a banquet to see each other after they recovered from the illness.
But Empress Gao passed away unexpectedly and could not meet.
Lu Wan's wife also died of illness.
In the sixth year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Lu Tazhi, the grandson of Lu Wan, surrendered to the Han Dynasty as King of Donghu and was named Marquis of Yagu.
Chen Xi was from Wanqu, and he didn't know why he followed Gaozu in the first place.
In the winter of the seventh year of Emperor Gaozu, King Han Xin of Han rebelled and fled to the Xiongnu. The emperor returned to Pingcheng and made Chen Xi a marquis. As the prime minister of Zhao State, he led the border defense troops of Zhao State and Dai State. The troops guarding the border in this area were under his jurisdiction.
summary: Lu Wan, a close childhood friend and neighbor of Emperor Gaozu, was exceptionally favored, serving as a general and Taiwei. After the empire was pacified, he was made King of Yan, the most favored among non-Liu princes. During Chen Xi's rebellion, Lu Wan sent Zhang Sheng to the Xiongnu, who secretly aided Chen Xi. Lu Wan later realized this and continued to prolong the war. When Emperor Gaozu discovered Lu Wan's collusion with Chen Xi and the Xiongnu, he sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan. Lu Wan fled to the Xiongnu, becoming King of Donghulu, but always wished to return. After Gaozu's death, Lu Wan died among the Xiongnu. His family later returned to Han, but his wife died before meeting Empress Gao. His grandson eventually surrendered and was made a marquis.

translation:
Chen Xi once asked for leave to return home. When passing through the State of Zhao, Zhou Chang, the Prime Minister of Zhao State, saw that Chen Xi's accompanying guests had more than a thousand cars and filled all the official residences in Handan.
Chen Xi treated his guests with the same etiquette among common people, and he was always humble and respectful, and he treated others with humility.
When Chen Xi returned to Dai, Zhou Chang asked to come to Beijing to see him.
After meeting the emperor, he told the whole story that Chen Xi had many guests and had been in sole control of the military for several years. He was afraid that something might happen.
The emperor ordered people to investigate Chen Xi's guests for their violations of laws and regulations regarding property and property, many of which implicated Chen Xi.
Chen Xi was very frightened and secretly sent guests to Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen to inform them.
In July of the tenth year of Emperor Gaozu, the Supreme Emperor passed away. The emperor sent someone to summon Chen Wei to Beijing, but Chen Wei said that his condition was serious.
In September, he rebelled with Wang Huang and others, proclaimed himself the king of Dai, and plundered Zhao and Dai two places.
After the emperor heard about it, he pardoned all Zhao and Dai officials who were implicated by Chen Xi and committed plunder. The emperor went there in person and said happily after arriving at Handan: "Chen Xi will not occupy Zhangshui in the south and guard Handan in the north. From this we know that he will not do anything."
Zhao Xiangguo submitted a memorial requesting that the governors and lieutenants of Changshan be beheaded, saying: Changshan had a total of twenty-five cities, but Chen Xi rebelled and lost twenty of them.
The emperor asked: Have the county guards and county lieutenants rebelled?
Zhao Xiangguo replied: No rebellion.
The emperor said: This is because of insufficient troops.
They were pardoned and their duties as captains were restored.
The emperor asked Zhou Chang: Does Zhao still have generals who can lead troops to fight?
Zhou Chang replied: There are four people.
Then these four people were asked to meet the emperor. When the emperor saw it, he cursed: Can you boys lead troops to fight?
The four people lay on the ground in shame.
However, the emperor still granted each of them a thousand households and appointed them as generals.
The ministers admonished and advised: "Many people followed you into Shu County and Hanzhong, and then conquered Western Chu. They had meritorious service but were not generally rewarded. What merits do these people have now and why should they be rewarded?"
The emperor said: This is beyond what you can understand!
Chen Xi rebelled and occupied everything north of Handan. I sent an emergency proclamation to recruit troops from various places, but no one has arrived yet. The only troops available now are from Handan.
Why should I begrudge the four thousand households granted to four people and not use it to appease the young people of Zhao! All the ministers on the left and right said, "Okay."
So the emperor asked again: Who are Chen Xi's generals?
The left and right people replied: Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen were both merchants in the past. The emperor said: I understand.
So each offered a thousand gold rewards to buy the heads of Wang Huang, Manchuchen and others.
In the winter of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the Han army attacked and killed Chen Xi's generals Hou Chang and Wang Huang at Quni City. They also defeated Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun in Liaocheng, killing more than 10,000 people.
Taiwei Zhou Bo marched and pacified Taiyuan and Daijun.
In December, the emperor personally led an army to attack Dongyuan, but failed to capture it. The rebel soldiers insulted the emperor. Soon Dongyuan surrendered. All soldiers who insulted the emperor were beheaded, and other soldiers who did not insult were sentenced to tattoos and tattoos on their foreheads.
Change Dongyuan's name to Zhending.
All Wang Huang and Manqiuchen's men who were offered rewards were captured alive, so Chen Xi's army was completely defeated.
The emperor returned to Luoyang.
The emperor said: Daijun is located to the north of Changshan Mountain, but Zhao Guo controls it from the south of the mountain. It is too far away.
So he named his son Liu Yuan the king of Dai, made Zhongdu the capital, and Daijun and Yanmen were all subordinate to Daiguo.
In the winter of the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Fan Kuai's soldiers chased Chen Kuai to Lingqiu and beheaded him.
Tai Shigong said: Han Xin and Lu Wan were not a family that had always accumulated good deeds. Instead, they were lucky enough to improvise and succeeded through deception and violence. Just as the Han Dynasty was just established, they were able to divide the territory and make the south the king.
Internally, it was suspected because of its strong power, and externally, it relied on foreigners for assistance. Therefore, he was increasingly alienated by the emperor, found himself in danger, had no choice but to surrender to the Huns. Isn't it sad?
Chen Xi was a native of Liang. When he was young, he always praised and admired Wei Gongzi Xinlingjun. Later, he led the army to guard the border, gathered guests, and treated virtuous corporals, and his reputation exceeded his actual status.
Zhou Chang doubted him, and many mistakes occurred from here. Fearing that disaster would come, the treacherous villain took the opportunity to speak again, and finally fell into a treasonous situation.
Oh, how sad!
It can be seen from this that the maturity and success or failure of the plan have a profound impact on a person!
summary: Chen Xi, a marquis and prime minister of Zhao, commanded border troops. Suspected by Zhou Chang, he feared investigation and rebelled with Wang Huang, proclaiming himself King of Dai. Emperor Gaozu personally campaigned, pardoning many officials and rewarding Zhao generals. The Han army defeated Chen Xi's forces, killing his generals and eventually Chen Xi himself in Lingqiu. The Grand Historian comments that Han Xin and Lu Wan, lacking accumulated virtue, succeeded through deception and violence during the Han's founding. Suspected internally and relying on foreigners, they were alienated and forced to surrender to the Xiongnu—a tragic fate. Chen Xi, admiring Lord Xinling, gathered guests and exceeded his reputation. Zhou Chang's suspicions, fear of disaster, and treacherous whispers led to his rebellion. Thus, the success or failure of plans profoundly impacts a person's destiny.

translation:
Han Anguo, the imperial censor, was a native of Cheng'an County, Liang State, and later settled in Suiyang.
I once studied "Han Feizi" and the doctrines of Zajia from Mr. Tian in Zouxian County. He served King Xiao of Liang and served as a middle official.
When the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, King Xiao of Liang sent Han Anguo and Zhang Yu as generals to resist the Wu army on the eastern front.
Because Zhang Yu fought hard and Han Anguo defended firmly, the Wu army could not cross Liang's defense line.
The Wu Chu rebellion was put down, and the reputations of Han Anguo and Zhang Yu became prominent.
King Xiao of Liang was the half-brother of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty. Empress Dowager Dou liked him very much and allowed him to have the power to nominate the Prime Minister of Liang and two thousand stone-level officials.
The scene of his coming in and out and playing games was more like that of an emperor than that of a minister.
When Emperor Jing heard about it, he was very unhappy. Empress Dowager Dou knew that Emperor Jing was dissatisfied, so she became angry with the envoys sent by Liang Guo and refused to receive them. Instead, she asked them about what King Liang had done.
At that time, Han Anguo was the envoy of the Liang Kingdom, so he went to see the eldest princess and cried: Why can't the Queen Mother clearly understand the filial piety of the Liang King as a son and the loyalty as a minister?
In the past, when the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao rebelled, the princes from the east of Hanguguan all united and marched westward. Only Liang was the most loyal to the court and became an obstacle to the rebels' attack.
King Liang thought that the Queen Mother and the Emperor were in Guanzhong, and the princes were in trouble. When he talked about it, tears streamed down his face. He knelt down and saw me and six other people off, leading the troops to repel the Wu Chu rebels. For this reason, the Wu Chu rebels did not dare to march westward, and finally failed and perished. This was all the power of King Liang.
Now the Queen Mother is blaming and complaining about Liang Wang for some strict etiquette.
King Liang's father and brother were both emperors, and the scenes he saw were great, so they cleared the way when traveling and prohibited people from passing through. When he returned to the palace, he emphasized vigilance. King Liang's car and flags were all gifts from the emperor. He just wanted to use these to show off in remote counties, let cars and horses gallop back and forth in the country, and let everyone in the world know that the queen mother and the emperor loved him.
Now when Liang envoy arrives, he will inquire and blame him.
King Liang was frightened and cried and missed him day and night, not knowing what to do.
Why was the King of Liang filial as a son and loyal as a minister, but the Queen Mother showed no mercy?
The eldest princess told Queen Mother Dou these words in detail, and Queen Mother Dou happily said: I will tell the emperor these words for him.
After telling the story, the knot in Emperor Jing's heart was relieved. He took off his hat and confessed his mistake to the Queen Mother, saying: We brothers cannot advise each other, which actually adds sorrow to the Queen Mother.
So he received all the envoys sent by King Liang and rewarded them heavily.
From then on, King Liang became even more favored.
Empress Dowager Dou and Princess Dachang rewarded Han Anguo with property worth about a thousand gold.
As a result, his reputation became prominent and he became connected with the imperial court.
Later, Han Anguo was convicted of breaking the law, and Meng County jailer Tian Jia insulted Han Anguo.
summary: Han Anguo, a native of Liang State and a student of Han Feizi and Zajia, served as a middle official under King Xiao of Liang. During the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms, he and Zhang Yu defended Liang’s eastern front, preventing the Wu army from crossing. After the rebellion, their reputations grew. King Xiao of Liang, favored by Empress Dowager Dou, acted with imperial-like grandeur, angering Emperor Jing. As Liang’s envoy, Han Anguo pleaded with the eldest princess, explaining King Liang’s filial piety and loyalty during the rebellion, and his use of imperial gifts to display the emperor’s favor. The empress dowager relented, and Emperor Jing reconciled, rewarding Han Anguo generously.

translation:
Han Anguo said: Will the ashes of death not resurface?
Tian Jia said: If it burns again, just urinate to put it out.
Soon after, the position of domestic history of Liang was vacant. The Han court sent envoys to appoint Han Anguo as domestic history of Liang. He started as a prisoner and served as an official with a rank of 2,000 stone.
Tian Jia abandoned his official position and ran away.
Han Anguo said: If Tian Jia doesn't come back and take office, I will destroy your clan.
Tian Jia took off his clothes and exposed his chest to apologize.
Han Anguo smiled and said: You can pee now!
Do people like you deserve my punishment?
Finally treat him nicely.
When the internal history of Liang was vacant, King Xiao of Liang had just recruited Gongsun Gui from Qi. He liked him very much and planned to request his appointment as internal history.
Queen Mother Dou heard this and ordered King Xiao of Liang to appoint Han Anguo as internal history.
Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng lobbied King Xiao of Liang and asked him to ask Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty to be the heir to the throne and increase the fiefdom. They were afraid that the court ministers would not agree and secretly sent people to assassinate the advisors in power.
Even after Yuan Ang, the former Prime Minister of Wu State, was killed, Emperor Jing heard about the plans of Gongsun Gui, Yang Sheng and others, so he sent envoys to capture Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng.
More than a dozen groups of Han sent envoys to the Liang State, and a nationwide search was conducted from Liang State Prime Minister down, but still no one was caught for more than a month.
Han Anguo, the internal historian, heard that Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng were hiding in the palace of Liang Xiaowang. Han Anguo entered the palace and met with Liang Xiaowang, crying and saying: My lord has been humiliated and I deserve to die for my crime.
The king has no good ministers, so things are in such chaos.
Now that I can't catch Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng, please let me say goodbye to you and give me permission to commit suicide.
King Xiao of Liang said: Why are you doing this?
Han Anguo burst into tears and said: Your Majesty, think about it for yourself, which one is closer between you and the Emperor, the Supreme Emperor and Emperor Gao, or the Emperor and King Linjiang?
King Xiao of Liang said: "It's not as close as them."
King Liang Xiao said: The relationship between the Supreme Emperor, King Linjiang, Emperor Gao and the Emperor is between father and son. However, Emperor Gao said: I am the one who takes over the world with a three-foot sword, so the Supreme Emperor could not interfere in political affairs in the end and lived in Yueyang Palace.
King Linjiang was the eldest prince, but he was deposed and demoted to King Linjiang just because of his mother's mistake. He also committed suicide in the Lieutenant's Mansion because he occupied the open space within the wall of the ancestral temple when building a palace.
Why is this so?
Because in governing the world, public affairs cannot be compromised by private affairs.
If you want to say: Even if you are your biological father, how do you know that he will not turn into a tiger?
How do even brothers know he won't turn into a wolf?
Now, Your Majesty, you are among the princes, but you listened to the false words of an evil minister, violated the emperor's prohibition, and obstructed the sage's law.
Because of the Queen Mother, the Emperor cannot bear to use laws against you.
The Queen Mother cried day and night, hoping that the king would change his mind, but the king never realized it.
If the Queen Mother dies suddenly, who can you rely on, Your Majesty?
summary: Later, Han Anguo was imprisoned for a crime but became Liang’s domestic history after a jailer’s insult. He forgave the jailer. When Liang’s internal history post opened, the empress dowager ordered King Liang to appoint Han Anguo. Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng plotted to make King Liang heir, assassinating Yuan Ang. Emperor Jing sent envoys to capture them, but they hid in King Liang’s palace. Han Anguo warned King Liang of the dangers, citing historical precedents, and the king surrendered the conspirators, who committed suicide. This resolved the crisis, and Han Anguo gained favor.
