translation:
Han Anguo was a man of great strategy, and his intelligence was enough to cater to the world, but he did so out of a loyal heart.
He is greedy for money.
Those he recommended were all honest scholars who were more worthy than himself.
In the Liang Kingdom, Hu Sui, Zang Gu, and Zhi Ta were recommended, and they were all famous scholars in the world. The scholars also praised and admired him very much, and even the emperor thought that he was a talented person in governing the country.
Han Anguo served as the imperial censor for more than four years. When the Prime Minister Tian Fu passed away, Han Anguo acted as the prime minister. He fell off the car while guiding the emperor's car and became lame.
The emperor discussed appointing the prime minister and planned to appoint Han Anguo. He sent someone to visit him and found that he was severely lame, so he appointed Pingji Hou Xue Ze as the prime minister.
Han Anguo was dismissed from his post due to illness for several months. His foot injury recovered, and the emperor appointed Han Anguo as lieutenant.
More than a year later, he was transferred to the rank of guard.
The chariot general Wei Qing attacked the Xiongnu, marched from Shanggu County, and defeated the Xiongnu in Longcheng.
General Li Guang was captured by the Xiongnu and escaped; Gongsun Ao's soldiers suffered heavy casualties; they all deserved beheading, but later paid for their sins and became commoners.
The next year, the Xiongnu invaded the border and killed the governor of western Liaoning. When they invaded Yanmen, they killed and took thousands of people captive. The chariot and cavalry general Wei Qing sent troops to pursue them and marched out of Yanmen County.
Weiwei Han Anguo served as general Caiguan and was stationed in Yuyang.
Han Anguo captured prisoners, who confessed that the Huns had gone far away.
Han Anguo immediately wrote to the emperor saying that it was the farming season and requested that the army be temporarily suspended.
After stopping their military garrison for more than a month, the Xiongnu invaded Shanggu and Yuyang on a large scale.
There were only more than 700 people in the military camp of Han Anguo. They went out to meet the Xiongnu and fought with them. However, they failed to win and returned to the military camp.
The Huns captured more than a thousand people, livestock and property and left.
After the emperor heard the news, he was very angry and sent an envoy to blame Han Anguo.
Tiaohan Anguo moved further east and stationed in Youbeiping.
Because at that time the prisoners of the Huns confessed that they wanted to invade the east.
Han Anguo initially served as a royal censor and a general protecting the army, but was gradually ostracized and alienated, demoted and demoted; while the newly favored young generals Wei Qing and others had military merits and were even more favored by the emperor.
After being alienated, Han Anguo felt very frustrated; he led troops to garrison and was bullied by the Xiongnu. He suffered many losses and casualties, and felt very guilty.
He hoped to return to the court, but he was even transferred to the east to garrison, and he felt depressed.
A few months later, he fell ill and vomited blood and died.
Han Anguo died in the second year of Yuanshuo.
Tai Shigong said: Hu Sui and I reviewed the calendar and observed Han Changru's behavior. Judging from Hu Sui's deep and reserved kindness, the world said that Liang Guo has many loyal and loyal elders. This is indeed true!
summary: After King Xiao’s death, Han Anguo lost his post but later became a chief minister. During the Xiongnu peace debate, he argued against war, favoring peace. The emperor agreed. In the Mayi incident, Nie Wengyi lured the Xiongnu, but the plan failed when the Chanyu retreated. Wang Hui, who proposed the plan, was executed despite pleas. Han Anguo, known for strategy and loyalty but greedy, recommended many scholars. He served as imperial censor for four years, then as lieutenant and guard. After Wei Qing’s campaigns, Han Anguo was stationed in Yuyang but was deceived by prisoners, leading to Xiongnu raids. Demoted and alienated, he died of illness in 123 BCE. Sima Qian praised his loyalty and the integrity of Liang’s elders.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/韩长孺列传

translation:
Mr. Wei's name is Wuji, he is the youngest son of King Wei Zhao and the half-brother of King Wei Anli.
After the death of King Zhao, King Anli came to the throne and named the son Lord Xinling.
At that time, Fan Sui fled from Wei to Qin and served as Qin Prime Minister. Because he was resentful that Wei Qi Qu beat him almost to death, he sent Qin troops to besiege Daliang and defeated the Wei troops stationed in Huayang, causing Wei general Mang Mao to flee in defeat.
The king of Wei and his son were very anxious about this matter.
The prince was kind, generous, courteous and virtuous. Regardless of whether the scholars had talent or talent, he interacted with them courteously. He never dared to look down on the scholars because of his wealth.
Therefore, scholars from thousands of miles around rushed to join him, and he attracted 3,000 diners.
At that time, the princes and states did not dare to invade Wei for more than ten years because of the virtuous son and the large number of guests.
One time, the young master and the King of Wei were playing chess, and an alarm came from the northern border, saying that Zhao State was sending troops to invade and would enter the border.
The king of Wei immediately put down his chess pieces and summoned the ministers to discuss countermeasures.
The prince dissuaded the king of Wei and said: "The king of Zhao is just hunting, not invading the border."
Then he continued to play chess with King Wei as if nothing had happened.
But the king of Wei was frightened and did not focus on playing chess at all.
After a while, news came from the north saying: King Zhao is just hunting, not invading the border.
King Wei was greatly surprised when he heard this and asked: How did the young master know this?
The young master replied: One of my diners can go deep into the secrets of King Zhao. If King Zhao takes any action, he will report it to me immediately, so I know about it.
From then on, the king of Wei was afraid of the young master's talents and did not dare to use him to handle national affairs.
There was a hermit named Hou Ying in the state of Wei. He was seventy years old and came from a poor family. He was the gatekeeper of the east gate of Daliang City.
When the prince heard about this man, he sent someone to see him and wanted to give him a generous gift.
But Hou Ying refused to accept it, saying: I have cultivated my moral character and insisted on integrity for decades, but after all, I cannot accept the prince's financial gift because I am a poor janitor.
The young master then held a banquet and entertained the guests.
After everyone came and sat down, the young master took the carriage, horses and entourage, vacated the left seat in the carriage, and went to the east gate in person to greet Mr. Hou.
Mr. Hou tidied up his shabby clothes and hats, then got into the car and sat in the distinguished seat vacated by the young master. He had no intention of being humble at all, and wanted to observe the young master's attitude.
But the young master held the horse's reins more respectfully.
Mr. Hou said to the young master again: I have a friend who is in the slaughterhouse in the market. I would like to give him a ride and take me to visit him.
The young master immediately drove to the market. Mr. Hou got out of the car and went to meet his friend Zhu Hai. He squinted at the young master and deliberately stood there for a long time, chatting with his friend and secretly observing the young master.
The young master's face became more cheerful.
summary: Lord Xinling, named Wei Wuji, was the youngest son of King Wei Zhao and half-brother of King Wei Anli. After King Zhao's death, King Anli enfeoffed him as Lord Xinling. Fan Sui, who fled to Qin and became prime minister, resented Wei's mistreatment and led Qin forces to besiege Daliang, defeating Wei troops at Huayang. The king and lord were deeply troubled. The lord was generous, humble, and virtuous, attracting three thousand retainers from across the realm. For over a decade, no feudal lords dared invade Wei due to his reputation. Once, while playing chess with the king, a false alarm about a Zhao invasion arose. The lord correctly identified it as a hunting expedition, revealing he had a spy in Zhao's court. This frightened the king, who thereafter feared the lord's abilities and refused him state affairs.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传

translation:
At this time, the generals, prime ministers, clan ministers and distinguished guests from Wei State were all sitting in the hall, waiting for the young master to raise their glasses to start the banquet.
Everyone in the market saw the young master holding the reins and driving the car for Mr. Hou.
The young master's entourage secretly scolded Mr. Hou.
Mr. Hou saw that the young master's expression remained unchanged, so he said goodbye to his friend and got into the car.
After arriving home, the young master led Mr. Hou to sit on the upper seat and introduced Mr. Hou to all the guests with praise. All the guests in the hall were surprised.
When everyone was drunk, the young master stood up and walked to Mr. Hou to toast his birthday.
Mr. Hou took the opportunity and said to the young master: Today I, Hou Ying, have made things difficult for the young master.
I am just a man who holds the gate and locks it at the east gate of the city, but the young master has resigned himself to carriages and horses and personally welcomes me in the public. I should not visit my friend again, but today the young master condescends to accompany me to visit him.
But I also wanted to make the young master famous, so I deliberately stopped the young master's carriage and horse in the market for a long time, and used the opportunity to visit friends to observe the young master. As a result, the young master became more humble.
People in the market thought that I was a villain, but they thought that the young master was a noble person who could treat the corporal with courtesy.
After the banquet ended, Mr. Hou became the prince's distinguished guest.
Mr. Hou said to the young master: The butcher Zhu Hai I visited is a virtuous man, but people don't understand him, so he is hidden among the butchers.
The young master went to visit Zhu Hai many times, but Zhu Hai deliberately refused to pay his respects and thank him. The young master thought this person was strange.
In the 20th year of King Anli of Wei, King Zhao of Qin had defeated the Zhao army in Changping, and then marched to besiege Handan.
The young master's sister is the wife of King Zhao Huiwen's brother Pingyuan Jun. She has sent letters to the King of Wei and the young master many times, asking for reinforcements from Wei.
The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi to lead an army of 100,000 people to rescue Zhao.
After King Zhao of Qin learned the news, he sent an envoy to warn King Wei: I am about to capture Zhao. It is only a matter of time. Who among the princes dares to save Zhao will definitely mobilize troops to attack it first after capturing Zhao.
The King of Wei was very frightened, so he sent people to stop Jin Bi from advancing further. He left the army to camp in Yecheng, nominally to save Zhao, but in fact he adopted a two-sided strategy to wait and see how the situation would develop.
The envoys of Lord Pingyuan came to Wei one after another, and they were often in urgent need. They blamed Mr. Wei and said: "The reason why I, Zhao Sheng, voluntarily rely on Wei to marry with Wei is because you have noble moral principles and can enthusiastically help others out of danger."
Now Handan is in danger, and sooner or later it will surrender to Qin, but Wei's reinforcements have not come yet. How can the young master help others get out of danger?
Besides, even if you don't take Zhao Sheng seriously, and abandon me to surrender to Qin, wouldn't you pity your sister?
The young master was extremely worried about this matter and repeatedly asked the King of Wei to send troops as soon as possible. He also asked the guests and debaters to try their best to persuade the King of Wei.
Because the King of Wei was afraid of Qin, he always refused to listen to the prince's opinion.
The prince estimated that he would not be able to obtain the consent of the King of Wei to send troops after all, so he decided that he could not let Zhao fall while alive, so he invited guests, gathered more than a hundred chariots, and planned to rush to the battlefield with the guests to fight to the death with the Qin army and die together with the Zhao people.
When the young master led the convoy through the east gate, he went to see Mr. Hou and told Mr. Hou everything about his plan to fight the Qin army to the death.
summary: The lord befriended Hou Ying, a seventy-year-old gatekeeper, by personally driving his carriage to fetch him for a banquet. Hou Ying tested the lord's humility by sitting in the honored seat and visiting a friend, Zhu Hai, in the market. The lord remained respectful, winning Hou Ying's loyalty. Hou Ying later recommended Zhu Hai as a capable man. In the twentieth year of King Anli's reign, Qin besieged Handan, Zhao's capital. The lord's sister, married to Zhao's Lord Pingyuan, begged Wei for aid. King Wei sent General Jin Bi with 100,000 troops but halted at Ye, fearing Qin's threats. Despite the lord's pleas, the king refused to advance. Determined to die with Zhao, the lord gathered retainers and chariots to attack Qin.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传

translation:
Then he said goodbye to Mr. Hou and prepared to go on the road. Before leaving, Mr. Hou said: "Young master, please work hard, I can't accompany you, old minister."
The young master walked for several miles, feeling unhappy, and said to himself: I have treated Mr. Hou well enough, and everyone in the world knows it. Now I am about to die, but Mr. Hou didn't say a word to see me off. Did I treat him wrongly?
So I drove back and wanted to ask Mr. Hou.
When Mr. Hou saw the young master, he smiled and said, "I knew the young master would come back."
He went on to say: The young master is famous all over the world for being hospitable and loving people.
Now that there is a crisis, the army that wants to go to Qin is like throwing meat to a hungry tiger. What is the use?
If this is the case, why are we guests used?
The young master treated me with great affection, but I did not see him off when he left, so I knew that he would be angry and I would come back.
The young master bowed to Mr. Hou twice in a row and then asked for countermeasures.
Mr. Hou asked the others to leave and talked secretly with the young master, saying: I heard that Jin Bi's military talismans are often placed in the King of Wei's bedroom. Among the wives and concubines, Ru Ji is the most favored.
I also heard that Ru Ji's father was killed. Ru Ji's desire for revenge had been building up for three years. All the ministers from the King of Wei on down wanted to avenge Ru Ji, but they failed.
For this reason, Ruji once cried to the prince, and the prince sent a retainer to cut off the enemy's head and present it to Ruji respectfully.
If Ru Ji wanted to die for the young master, she had no choice but to do so, but she just had no chance to act.
If the young master really asks Ru Ji for help, Ru Ji will definitely agree, and then he will be able to obtain the tiger talisman and seize the military power of Jin Bi. The north can save the Zhao State, and the west can resist the Qin State. This is the achievement of the Five Hegemons of the Spring and Autumn Period.
The young master followed Hou Ying's plan and asked Ruji for help.
Sure enough, Ruji stole Jin Bi's military talisman and gave it to the young master.
The young master got the military talisman and was about to go on the road. Mr. Hou said: When a general is fighting abroad, he has the power to make decisions. He may not accept some of the king's orders in order to benefit the country.
When the young master arrives there, even if the two numbers match and are verified to be correct, Jin Bi still refuses to hand over the military power to the young master and instead asks the King of Wei for instructions. Then things will be in danger.
My friend the butcher Zhu Hai can go with you. This man is a strong man.
If Jin Bi obeys, that would be the best; if he doesn't obey, Zhu Hai can kill him.
After hearing these words, the young master cried.
Upon seeing this, Mr. Hou asked: "Master, are you afraid of death?"
Why are you crying?
The young master replied: Jin Bi is a brave, powerful and experienced veteran of Wei State. When I went to him, I was afraid that he would not obey orders and would definitely kill him. Therefore, I cried sadly. Why am I afraid of death?
So the young master went to ask Zhu Hai to go with him.
Zhu Hai smiled and said: I am just a butcher who kills animals in the market, but the young master came to greet me many times. The reason why I did not return my greetings and thank you is because I think small etiquette is of no use.
Now that the young master is in danger, it is time for me to sacrifice my life for him.
So he set out on the road with the young master.
The young master went to say goodbye to Mr. Hou.
Mr. Hou said: I should have gone with you, but I am too old to make the trip.
summary: Passing through the east gate, the lord informed Hou Ying, who offered no farewell. Suspicious, the lord returned. Hou Ying explained the futility of a direct assault and proposed stealing Jin Bi's military tally from the king's favored concubine, Ruji, whom the lord had previously helped. The lord obtained the tally through Ruji. Hou Ying also advised taking Zhu Hai to kill Jin Bi if he resisted. The lord wept, foreseeing Jin Bi's death.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传

translation:
Please allow me to calculate the date of your journey. On the day you arrived at the Jinbi Military Headquarters, I faced the north and cut my neck to death to express my loyalty to see the young master off.
The young master then set out on the road. When he arrived at Yecheng, the young master took out his military talisman and pretended to send an order from King Wei to replace Jin Bi as the general.
Jin Bi combined the military talisman and verified that it was correct, but he still doubted the matter. He raised his hand and stared at the young master and said: Now I command an army of one hundred thousand troops stationed on the border. This is an important task related to the fate of the country. Today you come to replace me alone. What's going on?
About to refuse to accept the order.
At this time, Zhu Hai took out the forty kilograms of iron vertebrae hidden in his sleeves and killed Jin Bi with one vertebrae. The young master then took command of Jin Bi's army.
Then he organized the troops and issued an order to the army: If father and son are in the army, the father should go home; if brothers are in the army, the eldest brother should go home; and if the only son has no brothers, he should go home to support his parents.
After reorganization and selection, 80,000 elite soldiers were obtained. Kaiba attacked the Qin army on the front line.
The Qin army broke up the siege and retreated, so Handan was saved and Zhao was saved.
King Zhao and Lord Pingyuan came to the suburbs to greet the young master. Mr. Pingyuan led the way, carrying a pouch full of arrows for the young master.
King Zhao thanked him twice and said: "None of the wise men from ancient times can catch up with the young master."
At this time, Mr. Pingyuan no longer dared to compare himself with others.
After the young master said goodbye to Mr. Hou, on the day he arrived at the Yecheng military camp, Mr. Hou actually faced north and cut his throat to death.
The King of Wei was angry that the young master had stolen his military talisman, and falsely conveyed the king's order to kill Jin Bi. The young master knew this.
Therefore, after repelling the Qin army and saving the Zhao State, he asked his generals to return to the Wei State with their troops, while the young master himself and his retainers stayed in the Zhao State.
King Zhao Xiaocheng was grateful to the young master for his righteous deed of seizing the military power of Jin Bi under the pretext of entrusting the king's orders to protect the Zhao state, so he discussed with Lord Pingyuan and awarded five cities to the young master.
After hearing the news, the young master felt arrogant and complacent.
One of the disciples persuaded the young master: There are things that cannot be forgotten, and there are things that cannot be forgotten.
If others are kind to you, you should not forget it; if you are kind to others, please forget it.
Moreover, under the pretense of King Wei's order, he seized the military power of Jin Bi to rescue Zhao State. This was considered a meritorious service to Zhao State, but it was not considered a loyal minister to Wei State.
However, the young master felt that he had achieved merit and felt that it was great. I privately thought that the young master really shouldn't do it.
After hearing this, the young master immediately blamed himself, as if he was ashamed.
The State of Zhao held a grand welcome banquet. The King of Zhao cleaned the steps of the palace, went to the door to greet the distinguished guests in person, performed the host's etiquette, and led the young master into the west steps of the palace.
The young master walked sideways, repeatedly refusing to give in, and took the initiative to ascend the hall from the east steps.
summary: At Ye, Jin Bi verified the tally but refused to surrender command. Zhu Hai killed him with a hidden iron mallet. The lord reorganized the army, sending home fathers, elder brothers, and only sons, then led 80,000 elite troops to break the Qin siege, saving Handan. Hou Ying fulfilled his promise by cutting his own throat.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传

translation:
At the banquet, the young master said that he was guilty, sorry for the Wei State, and had no merit in the Zhao State.
King Zhao drank with the young master until evening. He was still embarrassed to talk about the conferment of five cities because the young master always blamed himself for giving in.
The young master finally stayed in Zhao State.
King Zhao rewarded the prince with the city of Haoyi. At this time, the king of Wei also returned the city of Xinling to the prince.
The young master is still in the state of Zhao.
The young master heard that there were two talented and virtuous people in Zhao who were not engaged in politics. One was Mao Gong who was hiding among the gamblers, and the other was Xue Gong who was hiding in the hotel. The young master wanted to see these two people, but the two men hid and refused to see the young master.
When the young master found out where they were hiding, he walked quietly to interact with these two people. They both enjoyed their acquaintance and were very happy.
Lord Pingyuan learned about this situation and said to his wife: At first I heard that my wife's brother Wei Gongzi was an unparalleled sage, but now I heard that he was doing random things and associating with the gang of gamblers and hotel clerks. The young master is just an ignorant and reckless person.
Lord Pingyuan's wife told the young master these words.
After hearing this, the young master said goodbye to his wife and prepared to leave, saying: "I heard that Lord Pingyuan was virtuous, so I betrayed King Pingyuan and rescued Zhao State, which satisfied Lord Pingyuan's request."
Now I know that Mr. Pingyuan's interactions with others are just a bold act to show his wealth. He is not looking for wise men and talents.
Since I was in Daliang, I have often heard that these two people are talented. When I arrived in Zhao State, I was afraid that I would not be able to see them.
I am still afraid that they will not want me when I am dating them. Now Mr. Pingyuan actually regards dating them as a humiliation. Mr. Pingyuan is not worth getting to know.
So I packed my bags and prepared to leave.
The lady told Lord Pingyuan everything the young master said. After hearing this, Lord Pingyuan felt ashamed and took off his hat to the young master to apologize, resolutely retaining the young master.
When the guests of Lord Pingyuan heard about this, half of them left Lord Pingyuan and joined the young master. All the scholars in the world also went to the young master and joined his family.
Mr. Pingyuan's guests were so admired by his conduct that they all came to his door.
The young master stayed in the State of Zhao for ten years and did not return to the State of Wei. When Qin heard that the young master was staying in Zhao, he sent troops eastward to attack Wei day and night.
The king of Wei was extremely anxious about this matter, so he sent envoys to invite the young master to return to his country.
The young master was still worried that the King of Wei would be angry with him, so he warned his guests: "Anyone who dares to deliver the message for the envoys of the King of Wei will be put to death."
Since all the guests had deserted Wei and came to Zhao, no one dared to persuade the young master to return to Wei.
At this time, Duke Mao and Duke Xue went to see the young master and said: The reason why the young master is respected in Zhao and famous among the princes is just because of the existence of Wei.
Now the Qin State is attacking the Wei State. The Wei State is in danger, but the young master does not care. If the Qin State breaks through the beams and razes the ancestral temple of your ancestors, how can the young master still have the face to live in the world?
Before he finished speaking, the young master's expression immediately changed and he told the driver to quickly hitch up the carriage and go back to rescue Wei Guo.
summary: Fearing the king's wrath, the lord remained in Zhao. King Zhao offered five cities, but the lord, humbled by a retainer's rebuke, refused credit. He later befriended recluses Mao Gong and Xue Gong, angering Lord Pingyuan, who deemed them unworthy. The lord defended his actions, causing many of Pingyuan's retainers to defect to him.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传

translation:
When the King of Wei saw the young master, the two of them couldn't help but shed tears. The King of Wei gave the young master the seal of general, and the young master officially assumed the highest position of commanding the army, the general.
In the thirtieth year of King Anli of Wei, the prince sent envoys to inform various princely states of his appointment as general.
When the princes learned that the young master had become the general, they all dispatched their own troops and generals to rescue Wei.
The young master led the armies of the five vassal states and defeated the Qin army south of the Yellow River, causing the Qin general Meng Ao to flee.
Then they took advantage of the victory and pursued it as far as Hangu Pass, trapping the Qin army in Hangu Pass, so that they did not dare to leave the pass again.
At that time, the reputation of the young master shocked the world, and guests from various princely states presented their art of war. The young master put them together and signed his name, so it is commonly known as "Wei Gongzi's Art of War" in the world.
The King of Qin was worried that the young master would further threaten the state of Qin, so he used thousands of kilograms of gold to go to Wei for bribes, find Jin Bi's former retainers, and asked them to slander him in front of the King of Wei: The young master has been in exile for ten years and is now a general of Wei.
The young master will also take this opportunity to decide to become king. The princes are afraid of the young master's power and prestige, and are planning to come together to support him as king.
The Qin State carried out rebellion many times, using the spies of the Wei State in the Qin State, pretending not to know anything and asking them to congratulate the young master and ask if he had been established as the king of Wei.
The king of Wei heard these slanderous words about the young master every day and could not help but believe them. Later, he actually sent someone to replace the young master as general.
The prince himself knew that he was being deposed for slander again, so he excused himself from going to court because he was ill. He feasted with the guests at home all night long, drank hard liquor, and often hung out with women. He spent four years having fun day and night, and finally died of illness due to excessive drinking. In this year, King Wei Anli also passed away.
When the King of Qin received the news that the young master was dead, he sent Meng Ao to attack Wei, captured twenty cities, and began to establish Dongjun.
From then on, Qin gradually invaded Wei's territory like eating mulberry leaves. After eighteen years, it captured Wei Wangjia, massacred the soldiers and civilians of Daliang, and destroyed the capital.
When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was in a low status, he heard many times that Mr. Wei was virtuous and talented.
After he ascended the throne and became emperor, he often went to worship the prince every time he passed by Daliang.
In the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, he returned from the front line where he defeated the rebel general Yingbu. When he passed through Daliang, he settled five families for the young master to guard his tomb and let them worship the young master according to the four seasons every year from generation to generation.
Tai Shigong said: When I passed by the ruins of Daliang, I looked for the so-called Yimen.
It turns out that Yimen is the east gate of Daliang City.
There are indeed many gentlemen in the world who are hospitable and like people, but only Lord Xinling can make friends with those people who are hidden in every corner of society. It makes sense that he does not feel ashamed to make friends with the lower class.
His reputation far exceeds that of the princes, and it is indeed true.
Therefore, every time Gaozu passed through Daliang, he ordered the people to offer sacrifices to him without interruption.
summary: After ten years, Qin attacked Wei. The king begged the lord's return. Mao and Xue convinced him to go back. The lord became general, rallied five allied states, and defeated Qin at the Yellow River, pursuing them to Hangu Pass. His fame spread, and he compiled "Wei Gongzi's Art of War." Qin bribed slanderers to claim the lord aimed for kingship. The king believed them and replaced him. The lord feigned illness, indulged in wine and women, and died four years later. King Anli died the same year. Qin then conquered twenty Wei cities and eventually destroyed Wei. Emperor Gaozu of Han, who admired the lord, ordered five families to guard his tomb and offer seasonal sacrifices. Sima Qian noted the lord's unique ability to befriend humble folk, ensuring his lasting renown.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏公子列传

translation:
Wei Qihou Dou Ying was the son of the cousin of Empress Dou, Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty.
His father's generation and above have been Guanjin people for generations.
He loves guests.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Dou Ying served as the Prime Minister of Wu State, but was dismissed due to illness.
When Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he took charge of Zhan.
King Xiao of Liang was the younger brother of Emperor Jing of Han Dynasty, and his mother, Queen Mother Dou, loved him very much.
One time when King Xiao of Liang entered the court, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty had a banquet with him as a brother. At this time, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty had not yet established a prince.
When the wine was in full swing, Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty said casually: After my death, I will pass the throne to King Liang.
Queen Mother Dou was very happy to hear this.
At this time, Dou Ying offered a glass of wine to the emperor and said: The world was created by Emperor Gaozu, and the throne should be passed down from father to son. This is the system established by the Han Dynasty. Why should the emperor pass it on to King Liang without authorization?
Queen Mother Dou hated Dou Ying for this reason.
Dou Ying also felt that Zhan Shi's official position was too small, so he resigned on the pretext of illness.
Empress Dowager Dou then expelled Dou Ying from entering and exiting the palace, and did not allow him to enter the palace to see him during festivals.
In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign in the Han Dynasty, seven kingdoms including Wu and Chu rebelled. The emperor found that no one in the royal family or anyone with the surname Dou was as capable as Dou Ying, so he summoned Dou Ying.
Dou Ying went to the palace to see him, but refused firmly, saying that he was ill and incompetent.
Empress Dowager Dou also felt ashamed.
So the emperor said: The world is in crisis, how can you refuse?
So he appointed Dou Ying as the general and rewarded him with a thousand catties of gold.
At this time, Yuan Ang, Luan Bu and other famous generals and wise men retired from their posts and stayed at home, so Dou Ying recommended them to the emperor.
The gold rewarded by the emperor was all displayed in the corridor. When the subordinate officers passed by, they were allowed to use it as they saw fit. None of the gold rewarded by the emperor was taken home.
When Dou Ying was stationed in Xingyang, he supervised the troops of Qi and Zhao. After all the rebellions in the seven countries were put down, the emperor granted Dou Ying the title of Marquis of Wei.
At this time, all the tourists and guests rushed to join Wei Qihou.
During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, every time the court discussed major military and political affairs, all the princes did not dare to sit on an equal footing with Zhou Yafu, the Marquis of Tiao, and Dou Ying, the Marquis of Wei Qi.
In the fourth year of Emperor Jing's reign in the Han Dynasty, he established Prince Li and appointed Wei Qihou as his tutor.
In the seventh year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Prince Li was deposed. Wei Qihou argued for Prince Li many times, but to no avail.
Wei Qihou pretended to be ill and lived in seclusion at the foot of Nanshan Mountain in Lantian County for several months. Many guests and debaters came to persuade him, but no one could persuade him to return to the capital.
Gao Sui, a native of Liang, came to persuade Wei Qihou and said: The one who can make you rich is the emperor, and the one who can make you a confidant of the court is the queen mother.
Now you are the master of the prince. The prince was deposed and could not fight for it. His efforts could not succeed, and he could not die in the line of duty.
He retired due to illness, embraced the beautiful singer, and retired to live in seclusion instead of attending court meetings.
summary: Dou Ying, the Marquis of Weiqi, was a relative of Empress Dowager Dou during the Han Dynasty. He served as the Prime Minister of Wu but was dismissed due to illness. During Emperor Jing's reign, he opposed the emperor's suggestion to pass the throne to his brother, King Xiao of Liang, angering Empress Dowager Dou. When the seven kingdoms rebelled, Emperor Jing appointed Dou Ying as a general. He recommended talented men, distributed his gold reward to subordinates, and successfully suppressed the rebellion, earning the title of Marquis of Weiqi. He later served as the tutor of Prince Li but was deposed after arguing for the prince. He retired but was persuaded to return to court. Despite Empress Dowager Dou's recommendation, Emperor Jing refused to make him prime minister, citing his arrogance.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏其武安侯列传

translation:
Comparing these situations with each other, this is your own statement that you want to publicize the emperor's fault.
If both the Emperor and the Queen Mother harm you, then your wife and children will all be killed.
Wei Qihou thought he was right, so he went back to the court and met the emperor as before.
When Taohou Liu She was dismissed from the post of prime minister, Empress Dowager Dou recommended Wei Qihou to be prime minister many times.
Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty said: Does the Queen Mother think that I am stingy in not letting Wei Qihou become prime minister?
Wei Qihou is a proud and complacent person, prone to self-admiration, careless and frivolous in doing things, making it difficult for him to serve as prime minister and assume important responsibilities.
Finally, he was not appointed, and Wei Wan, Marquis of Jianling, was appointed as prime minister.
Tianfen, Marquis of Wu'an, was the half-brother of Emperor Jing and Queen of the Han Dynasty. He was born in Changling.
After Wei Qihou became a general, when he was at the height of his prominence, Tian Fu was still an official, not a distinguished person. He went to and from Wei Qihou's home, attended banquets, knelt down and stood up like Wei Qihou's descendants.
In the later years of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Tian Fu also became prominent, favored and became a Taizhong doctor.
Tian Fu was eloquent and eloquent. He had studied books such as "Pan Yu" and the Queen Mother thought he had talent.
When Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty passed away, the prince ascended the throne and the Queen Mother became regent. Her suppression and appeasement actions throughout the country mostly adopted the strategy of Tian Fu's guests. Tian Fu and his younger brother Tian Sheng were both named Marquis of Wu'an and Marquis of Zhou Yang respectively in the same year that Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty died because they were the younger brothers of the Queen Mother.
Marquis Wu'an had just come to power and wanted to be prime minister, so he was very humble to his guests. He recommended famous people who were idle at home to become officials and make them prominent, hoping to overwhelm the power of generals such as Dou Ying.
In the first year of Jianyuan, Prime Minister Wei Wan was dismissed due to illness, and the emperor was planning to arrange for the prime minister and Taiwei.
Ji Fu persuaded Marquis Wu'an: "Wei Qihou has been a prominent figure for a long time, and the talented people in the world have always attached themselves to him."
Now that you have just made a fortune, you cannot compare with Wei Qihou. Even if the emperor appoints you as prime minister, you must give it to Wei Qihou.
If Wei Qihou becomes prime minister, you will definitely become Taiwei.
The noble status of the Taiwei and the Prime Minister are equal, and you have a good reputation of giving your position to the wise.
Marquis Wu'an then tactfully told the Queen Mother to hint to the emperor, so he appointed Marquis Wei Qi as prime minister and Marquis Wu'an as Taiwei.
Ji Fu went to congratulate Wei Qihou and reminded him: Your nature is to like good people and hate bad people. Today, good people praise you, so you become prime minister. However, you also hate bad people. There are many bad people, and they will slander you.
If you can tolerate both good and bad people, then your position as prime minister can be maintained for a long time; if you cannot, you will be slandered and resigned immediately.
Wei Qihou did not listen to him.
Dou Ying, the Marquis of Wei Qi, and Tian Fu, the Marquis of Wu'an, both loved Confucianism. They recommended Zhao Wan to be the imperial censor, and Wang Zang to be the doctor's order.
Welcoming Shen Pei, a native of Lu, to the capital, he prepared to set up a Mingtang, ordered the princes to return to their own fiefdoms, abolished confinement, and stipulated good and bad clothing and systems according to etiquette and law, so as to show the atmosphere of peace.
summary: Tian Fen, the Marquis of Wu'an, was the half-brother of Emperor Jing's queen. Initially humble, he rose to prominence after Emperor Jing's death, becoming a favored official. He became prime minister and Taiwei, promoting Confucianism and clashing with Empress Dowager Dou's preference for Taoism. After her death, Tian Fen became prime minister, growing arrogant and powerful. He built lavish residences and accumulated wealth, while Dou Ying lost influence and was alienated.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏其武安侯列传

translation:
Since Wei Qihou lost Empress Dowager Dou, he was further alienated by the emperor and was not reused. He had no power. All the guests gradually left of their own accord, and even became lazy and arrogant towards him. Only General Guan did not change his original attitude.
Wei Qihou was unhappy every day, but he treated General Guan particularly well.
General Guan is from Yingyin.
Guan Fu's father was Zhang Meng, who once served as a retainer of Yingyin Marquis Guan Ying. Because of Guan Ying's favor, he recommended him to an official of two thousand stone level, so he pretended to be named Guan Meng after Guan's family name.
During the rebellion of Wu and Chu, Yingyin Marquis Guan He served as a general and was a subordinate of Taiwei Zhou Yafu. He recommended Guan Meng to the Taiwei as a school captain.
Guan Fu led a thousand men to join the army with his father.
Guan Meng was already old, and Marquis Yingyin reluctantly recommended him. Therefore, Guan Meng was depressed and frustrated. During battles, he often attacked the enemy's strong positions and died in the Wu army.
According to the provisions of the military law at that time, father and son joined the army together and participated in the war. If one died fighting for the country, the surviving son could escort the coffin back.
But Guanfu refused to go back with his father's coffin. He expressed impassionedly that he hoped to behead the King of Wu or the general of Wu to avenge his father.
So Guan Fu put on his armor and held a halberd in his hand, and summoned dozens of warriors in the army who had always been friendly with him and were willing to go with him.
After walking out of the military gate, no one dared to move forward.
Only the two of them and Guan Fu's slaves, a total of more than ten cavalry, rushed into the Wu army until they reached the Wu army's general flag, killing and wounding dozens of enemy soldiers.
Unable to move forward any further, he flew back to the Han camp. All the slaves he brought with him were killed, and he was the only one who returned.
Guan Fu suffered more than ten serious injuries on his body, but he happened to have precious medicine, so he survived.
Guan Fu's wounds improved a little, and he asked the general again: "I now know more about the twists and turns in the Wu army camp. Please let me go back again."
The general thought that Guan Fu was brave and loyal, and he was afraid that Guan Fu would die in the battle, so he reported it to the Taiwei Zhou Yafu, who resolutely stopped him.
When the Wu army was defeated, Guan Fu became famous all over the world.
Marquis Yingyin reported Guan Fu's situation to the emperor, and the emperor appointed Guan Fu as Zhonglang General.
A few months later, he lost his official position because of a violation of the law.
Later he settled in Chang'an, and many dignitaries in Chang'an praised him.
During the reign of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Guan Fuguan became the Prime Minister of the country.
Emperor Jing passed away and Emperor Wu, the current emperor, had just ascended the throne. He believed that Huaiyang was the transportation hub of the world and must be defended by strong troops, so he appointed Guan Fu as the governor of Huaiyang.
In the first year of Jianyuan's reign, he transferred Guan Fu Nei to the rank of imperial servant.
In the second year, Guan Fu was drinking with Changle guard Dou Fu. Guan Fu got drunk and beat Dou Fu.
Dou Fu is the brother of Queen Mother Dou.
The emperor was afraid that Empress Dowager Dou would kill Guan Fu, so he appointed him as the prime minister of Yan State.
A few years later, he was disgraced for breaking the law and lived idle at home in Chang'an.
Guan Fu is a strong and straightforward person, he is prone to drunkenness and does not like to flatter people in person.
summary: Guan Fu, a brave general, gained fame during the seven kingdoms' rebellion by charging into enemy lines. He later became a governor but was dismissed for legal violations. He was known for his straightforwardness, generosity to the poor, and disdain for the powerful. He accumulated wealth and became tyrannical in Yingchuan. After losing power, he befriended Dou Ying, and they supported each other. Tian Fen once promised to visit Dou Ying but failed to show, causing Guan Fu to confront him. Tian Fen later sought to seize Dou Ying's land, leading to a feud. Tian Fen accused Guan Fu of tyranny, and Guan Fu retaliated by exposing Tian Fen's corruption. At a banquet, Guan Fu insulted Tian Fen, who had him arrested and charged with disrespect. Dou Ying tried to save Guan Fu but failed. Tian Fen slandered Dou Ying, leading to his imprisonment. Dou Ying claimed to have an imperial edict from Emperor Jing, but it was not found in records, resulting in his execution for forgery. Guan Fu and his family were also executed. Tian Fen later fell ill, haunted by the ghosts of Dou Ying and Guan Fu, and died. His son's title was revoked after a crime.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏其武安侯列传

translation:
In the spring of this year, Marquis Wu'an fell ill and kept shouting, saying things like apology.
He asked a wizard who could see ghosts to diagnose his illness. The wizard saw the ghosts of Wei Qihou and Guan Fu guarding Wu'anhou and wanted to kill him.
Finally died.
His son Tian Tian inherited the title.
In the third year of Yuan Shuo, Hou Tiantian of Wu'an committed the crime of "disrespect" because he entered the palace wearing short clothes, and his title was revoked.
The rebellion of Huainan King Liu An was discovered, and the emperor ordered the matter to be investigated.
The last time King Huainan came to court, Marquis Wu'an was appointed as Taiwei. At that time, he came to Ba Shang to greet King Huainan and said: The emperor has no prince, and the king is the wisest and the grandson of the great ancestor. Once the emperor dies, who else should inherit the throne instead of the king?
The King of Huainan was very happy and gave Marquis Wu'an many gold and silver items.
Ever since the incident involving Marquis Wei Qi happened, the Emperor did not think that Marquis Wu An was right, and it was just because of the Queen Mother's hindrance.
When he heard that King Huainan sent gold and silver to Marquis Wu'an, the emperor said: If Marquis Wu'an is still alive, it's time to exterminate the clan.
Tai Shigong said: Wei Qihou and Wu'anhou were both in prominent positions due to their relatives. Guan Fu became famous at that time because he made up his mind to take risks and perform meritorious deeds.
Wei Qihou was re-employed because he put down the rebellions of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu; Wu'an Hou was promoted because he took advantage of the opportunity that the emperor had just ascended the throne and the Queen Mother came to power.
However, Wei Qihou really didn't understand the changes in the situation, and Guan Fu was neither knowledgeable nor humble. The two protected each other, which caused this disaster.
Marquis Wu'an relied on his noble status and liked to play with power; because of his resentment over a glass of wine, he framed two wise men.
How sad!
Tian Fu transferred his anger towards Guan Fu to Dou Ying, and his own life was short-lived.
Guan Fu was not supported by the people and eventually lost a bad reputation. How sad!
From this we can see the source of Guanfu’s disaster!
summary: The historian comments that Dou Ying and Tian Fen rose through family connections, while Guan Fu gained fame through bravery. Dou Ying failed to adapt to changing circumstances, and Guan Fu lacked humility, leading to their downfall. Tian Fen abused his power and framed innocent men, resulting in his own demise.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏其武安侯列传

translation:
Wei Bao was originally the son of the Wei Kingdom during the Six Kingdoms period.
His elder brother is Wei Jiu, who was named Lord Ningling when he was in Wei State.
After the Qin State destroyed the Wei State, he was exiled to other places and became a commoner.
Chen Sheng rebelled and proclaimed himself king, and Wei Jiu followed him.
King Chen sent Zhou Shi, a native of Wei, to lead troops to seize the land of Wei. After Wei was captured, everyone discussed with each other and wanted to make Zhou Shi the king of Wei. Zhou Shi said: Only when the world is in chaos can loyal ministers be revealed.
Now that the whole world is rebelling against Qin, morally speaking, we must support the descendants of King Wei.
Qi and Zhao each sent fifty chariots, hoping to establish Zhoushi as the king of Wei.
Zhou Shi refused to accept the offer and sent people to Chen County to meet Wei Jiu.
After five trips in total, King Chen agreed to send Wei Jiu back and establish him as King of Wei.
Not long after Zhang Han defeated King Chen, he marched to Linji to attack King Wei. King Wei sent Zhou Shi to Qi and Chu to request reinforcements.
Qi and Chu sent Xiang Ta and Tian Ba ​​to lead the army to follow Zhou City to rescue Wei.
Zhang Han actually defeated the reinforcements, killed Zhou Shi, and surrounded Linji.
Wei Jiu proposed conditions for surrender for the sake of the soldiers and people in the city.
After the negotiation was successful, Wei Jiu set himself on fire and died.
Wei Bao fled to Chu. King Huai of Chu gave Wei Bao thousands of troops and went back to capture Wei.
By this time Xiang Yu had defeated the Qin army and surrendered to Zhang Han.
Wei Bao captured more than 20 cities one after another. Xiang Yu made Wei Bao King of Wei.
Wei Bao led his elite troops and followed Xiang Yu into the pass.
In the first year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu divided the princes among the feudal lords. He planned to occupy the Liang land, so he moved King Bao of Wei to Hedong, established his capital in Pingyang, and named him King of the Western Wei Dynasty.
The King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties and led his troops across the Yellow River from Linjin. Wei Bao surrendered the entire country to the King of Han and followed the King of Han to Pengcheng to attack the Chu army.
The king of Han was defeated and returned to Xingyang. Wei Bao asked for leave and went home to visit his mother's condition. After returning home, he immediately cut off the crossing of the Yellow River and betrayed the King of Han.
Although the King of Han heard the news of Wei Bao's rebellion, he was worried about the Chu State in the east. He had no time to attack him, so he said to Li Sheng: Go and persuade Wei Bao for me. If you can persuade him, I will make you the Marquis of Wanhu.
Li Sheng went to lobby Wei Bao.
Wei Bao politely refused and said: Life is as short as the shadow of the sun passing through the crack in the wall.
Now the King of Han is arrogant and insults others at will. He scolds the princes and ministers as if they were slaves. He has no etiquette at all. I can't bear to see him.
So the King of Han sent Han Xin to attack Wei Bao, captured Wei Bao in Hedong, and escorted him to Xingyang in a post car, and changed Wei Bao's original territory into three counties.
The King of Han ordered Wei Bao to garrison Xingyang.
When the Chu army tightened its siege, Zhou Ke killed Wei Bao.
Peng Yue was from Changyi, with the courtesy name Zhong.
He often fishes in Juye Lake and joins a group of people to commit robberies.
Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose up, and a young man said to Peng Yue: Many heroes are rushing to raise banners to resist the violent Qin Dynasty. You can stand up, and we will follow their example.
summary: Wei Bao, son of the Wei Kingdom during the Six Kingdoms period, had his elder brother Wei Jiu named Lord Ningling. After Qin destroyed Wei, Wei Bao became a commoner. When Chen Sheng rebelled, Wei Jiu followed him. Chen Sheng sent Zhou Shi to seize Wei land; after capturing it, others wanted Zhou Shi as king, but he insisted on supporting Wei descendants. Qi and Zhao sent chariots to back Zhou Shi, who refused and fetched Wei Jiu from Chen County. Chen Sheng agreed, making Wei Jiu King of Wei. Zhang Han defeated Chen Sheng, attacked Wei, and killed Zhou Shi. Wei Jiu surrendered to save his people, then set himself on fire. Wei Bao fled to Chu, received troops from King Huai of Chu, and captured over 20 cities. Xiang Yu made Wei Bao King of Wei, then moved him to Hedong as King of Western Wei. Wei Bao surrendered to the King of Han, followed him to attack Chu, but later betrayed him by cutting off the Yellow River crossing. The King of Han sent Li Sheng to persuade him, but Wei Bao refused, citing the King of Han's arrogance. Han Xin captured Wei Bao, who was later killed by Zhou Ke during a Chu siege. Tai Shigong comments: Though Wei Bao and Peng Yue rose from poverty to become kings, their failure to die for honor and willingness to be prisoners led to their deaths. Their endurance of humiliation stemmed from superior strategy and fear for their lives, hoping to seize power as circumstances changed.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏豹彭越列传

translation:
Peng Yue said: Now is the time for the two dragons to fight, so let's wait.
More than a year later, more than a hundred young people from Zezhong gathered to follow Peng Yue and said, "Please be our leader."
Peng Yue refused and said: I don't want to work with you.
The young people persisted in their request, and he agreed.
Make an appointment with them to gather when the sun rises the next day, and those who are late will be beheaded.
When the sun came up the next day, more than ten people were late, and the last one didn't come until noon.
At that time, Peng Yue said apologetically: I am old and you insist on making me the leader.
Now, if there are many people late at the appointed time, we cannot behead all of them, but only the last person to come.
Order the captain to kill him.
Everyone laughed and said: "Why bother? I just don't dare to be late again from now on."
So Peng Yue took the last person who arrived and killed him. Set up an earthen altar, use human heads to offer sacrifices, and give orders to everyone who belongs to them.
Everyone was shocked and afraid of Peng Yue. No one dared to look up at him.
So he led everyone to seize the land and collected more than a thousand soldiers who had fled from the princes.
Peigong went north from Dang to attack Changyi, and Peng Yue assisted him.
Changyi was not captured, so Pei Gong led the army to march west.
Peng Yue also led his troops to garrison in Juye Ze to collect the fleeing soldiers of Wei.
Xiang Ji entered Guanzhong and divided the feudal lords, and then returned. Peng Yue's army had grown to more than 10,000 people, but he had no one to belong to.
In the autumn of the first year of Han Dynasty, King Tian Rong of Qi betrayed King Xiang, so he sent someone to give General Peng Yue a seal and asked him to march to Jiyin to attack the Chu army.
The Chu army ordered Xiao Gongjiao to lead his troops to attack Peng Yue, but was severely defeated by Peng Yue.
In the spring of the second year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han, King Bao of Wei and various princes went east to attack Chu. Peng Yue led more than 30,000 troops to join the King of Han in Waihuang.
The King of Han said: General Peng has recovered more than a dozen cities in Wei and is eager to support the descendants of King Wei.
Today, King Bao of Wei is the cousin of King Jiu of Wei and a descendant of the real King of Wei.
He appointed Peng Yue as the Prime Minister of Wei State, monopolizing military power and pacifying the Liang Dynasty.
After the King of Han was defeated in Pengcheng, he retreated westward. At this time, Peng Yue abandoned all the cities he had captured and led his army alone to the north to station along the Yellow River.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, Peng Yue often traveled and sent troops on behalf of the Han Dynasty, attacked the Chu army, and cut off their supply of food and grass in Liang.
In the winter of the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, King Xiang and King Han were at a stalemate in Xingyang, and Peng Yue captured seventeen cities including Suiyang and Waihuang.
When King Xiang heard the news, he sent Cao Jiu to garrison Chenggao, and he led his army eastward to recover the cities that Pengyue had conquered, returning them to Chu.
Peng Yue led his team north to Gucheng.
In the autumn of the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, King Xiang's army retreated south to Xia Yang. Peng Yue captured more than 20 cities near Changyi and seized more than 100,000 bushels of grain, which was used as ration for the King of Han.
The king of Han was defeated and sent an envoy to ask Peng Yue to join forces to attack the Chu army.
Peng Yue said: Wei has just been pacified, but it is still afraid of the Chu army and cannot go there.
The king of Han raised his troops to pursue the Chu army, but was defeated by Xiang Ji in Guling.
summary: Peng Yue, from Changyi, fished and robbed in Juye Lake. After Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose, youths urged him to lead, but he delayed. Over a year later, over a hundred youths insisted, and he agreed, executing a latecomer to enforce discipline. He gathered followers and assisted Peigong (Liu Bang) in attacking Changyi. After Xiang Ji divided the lords, Peng Yue's army grew to over 10,000. In the first year of Han, Qi's King Tian Rong gave him a seal to attack Chu. Peng Yue defeated Chu's Xiao Gongjiao. In the second year, he joined the King of Han with 30,000 troops and was made Prime Minister of Wei. After the King of Han's defeat, Peng Yue stationed along the Yellow River, harassing Chu's supply lines. In the fourth year, he captured 17 cities, but Xiang Ji recovered them. In the fifth year, he seized grain for the King of Han. Following Zhang Liang's advice, the King of Han promised Peng Yue land to become king, leading him to join the Han army at Gaixia, defeating Chu. Peng Yue was made King of Liang. In the tenth year, Chen Xi rebelled; Peng Yue feigned illness, angering Emperor Gao. Accused of conspiracy, he was arrested, pardoned to commoner status, and exiled. Empress Lu, fearing his influence, had him executed and his family exterminated.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/魏豹彭越列传

translation:
Lu Zhonglian was a native of Qi.
He is good at analyzing unique, grand and extraordinary strategies, but he is unwilling to serve as an official and is willing to maintain high integrity.
He once visited Zhao State.
When Zhao Xiaocheng was king, King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to lead an army to defeat Zhao Changping's army, killing more than 400,000 people in total. As a result, Qin's army advanced eastward and besieged Handan, the capital of Zhao.
King Zhao was very afraid, and no one from the reinforcements from the vassal states dared to attack the Qin army.
King Anli of Wei sent General Jin Bi to lead troops to rescue Zhao. However, he was afraid of the Qin army and stationed in Tangyin and did not dare to advance.
The king of Wei sent his guest general Xinyuan Yan into Handan through a hidden path, and met with the king of Zhao through Pingyuan Jun. He said: The reason why the Qin army is eager to besiege Zhao is because it used to compete with King Qi Min to become emperor, and soon King Qi Min revoked the title of emperor.
If Zhao can send envoys to honor King Qin Zhao as emperor, King Qin will be very happy and will withdraw his troops.
Mr. Pingyuan was hesitant and unable to make a decision.
At this time, Lu Zhonglian traveled to the State of Zhao and caught up with the Qin army to besiege Handan. He heard that the State of Wei wanted Zhao to honor King Qin Zhao and proclaim himself emperor, so he went to Jin to see Lord Pingyuan and said: "What are we going to do about this?"
Mr. Pingyuan said: How dare we talk about such a big event in our country!
Not long ago, 400,000 troops were lost abroad, and now they are surrounded by the Qin army in Handan, and they cannot make them retreat.
The King of Wei sent the guest general Xinyuan Yan to ask the State of Zhao to honor King Qin Zhao as emperor. This man is still here.
How dare I talk about such a big thing!
Lu Zhonglian said: I used to think that you were the most virtuous son in the world, but today I know that you are not the most virtuous son in the world.
Where is Wei Guo's guest Xinyuan Yan?
I will blame him for you and send him back.
Mr. Pingyuan said: I would like to introduce you to Mr. Pingyuan.
So Mr. Pingyuan met Xinyuan Yan and said: "There is a Mr. Lu Zhonglian in Qi State. He is here now. Please let me introduce him to you so that he can get to know the general and make friends."
Xinyuan Yan said: I heard that Mr. Lu Zhonglian is a noble person in Qi State.
I am a minister of the King of Wei, and I have been ordered to be an envoy and bear my responsibilities. I do not want to see Mr. Lu Zhonglian.
Mr. Pingyuan said: I have revealed the news that you are here.
Niiguan Yan had no choice but to agree.
Lu Zhonglian saw Xinyuan Yan but said nothing.
Xinyuan Yan said: I think those who stay in this besieged city are all people who seek help from Lord Pingyuan. But now, I don’t think Mr.’s appearance looks like someone who wants help from Lord Pingyuan. Why do you stay in this besieged city for a long time and not leave?
Lu Zhonglian said: The world thinks that Bao Jiao committed suicide because of his narrow-mindedness. This view is completely wrong.
Most people don't understand his shame in living in a troubled world, and think he just has personal agenda.
The Qin State was a country that abandoned etiquette and only valued military merit. It treated its soldiers with power and deceit and enslaved its people like slaves.
summary: Lu Zhonglian, a native of Qi, was skilled in grand strategies but refused to serve as an official, valuing integrity. During the siege of Handan by Qin, Zhao sought aid. Wei sent General Jin Bi, who hesitated, and envoy Xinyuan Yan proposed Zhao honor King Zhao of Qin as emperor to secure peace. Pingyuan Jun hesitated. Lu Zhonglian confronted Xinyuan Yan, arguing that submitting to Qin would bring disaster. He cited historical examples, such as King Wei of Qi’s humiliation by Zhou and the fates of Jiuhou and Ehou under Yin Zhou, to illustrate the dangers of imperial ambition. Lu declared he would rather die than serve Qin. Xinyuan Yan was convinced and withdrew his proposal. The Qin army retreated after Wei’s Prince Wuji rescued Zhao. Pingyuan Jun offered Lu a reward, but he refused, stating that a worthy person resolves conflicts without seeking payment, and left forever.

translation:
I heard that those who seek small details cannot achieve a glorious reputation, and those who are ashamed of small things cannot achieve great achievements.
In the past, Guan Zhong shot Duke Huan's belt hook, which was a crime. Giving up Prince Jiu instead of letting him die was cowardly. Being imprisoned with instruments of torture was a shame.
For a person with these three conditions, the king will not use him as a minister and the villagers will not associate with him.
If Guanzi had been imprisoned for a long time and died in prison without being able to return to Qi, he would have had a shameful and despicable reputation.
Even Nu Bei is ashamed to have the same name as him, let alone the public opinion in society!
Therefore, Guan Zhong did not feel ashamed because he was in prison, but he felt ashamed that the world could not be at peace. He did not feel ashamed that he could not die with his son Jiu, but he felt ashamed that he could not show his prestige among the princes. Therefore, although he had the triple fault of committing crimes, fearing death, and being humiliated, he assisted Duke Huan of Qi to become the leader of the five hegemons. His reputation was higher than anyone else in the world, and his glory shone on neighboring countries.
After Cao Mo became a general of Lu, he failed in many battles and lost 500 miles of land.
If Cao Mo had cut his throat and committed suicide without careful consideration and hastily made a plan, he would have been infamous as a defeated general.
Cao Mo ignored the humiliation of being defeated many times and came back to discuss matters with Lord Lu.
Taking advantage of Duke Huan's opportunity to convene the princes of the world, Cao Mo used a dagger to get close to Duke Huan's heart on the altar. His face remained unchanged and his speech was calm. He defeated the lost land many times and regained it in a short time. The world was shaken, the princes were horrified, and the reputation of Lu was higher than that of Wu and Yue.
Like these two patriots, it is not that they disregard the honor and integrity of the whole family and think that if they die, their reputation will be destroyed and their achievements will not be established. This is not a wise approach.
Therefore, give up temporary anger and establish a lifelong reputation; give up temporary anger and establish achievements for generations to come.
Therefore, these deeds and the achievements of the three kings compete to spread, and their reputation coexists with heaven and earth.
I hope you will choose one of these options and take action!
General Yan read Lu Zhonglian's letter and cried for several days, but still hesitated to make a decision.
He wanted to return to the Yan State, but there was already a rift, and he was afraid of being killed; he wanted to surrender to the Qi State, but too many Qi people had been killed and captured, and he was afraid that he would be humiliated after surrendering.
He sighed deeply and said: It is better to commit suicide than to let others kill me.
Just committed suicide.
Liaocheng was in chaos, so Tian Dan marched into Liaocheng and bloodbathed Liaocheng.
When he returned, he reported Lu Zhonglian's affairs to the King of Qi. The King of Qi wanted to knight him.
After hearing this, Lu Zhonglian fled to the seaside and lived in seclusion. He said: Instead of being rich and serving others, it is better for me to be poor and despise the world and let my own ambitions go.
Zou Yang is from Qi State.
When he traveled to Liang State, he interacted with Zhuang Ji, a native of Wu State, and Mei Cheng, a native of Huaiyin.
summary: Over twenty years later, a Yan general held Qi’s Liaocheng. Lu Zhonglian wrote him a letter, urging him to choose wisely: return to Yan or surrender to Qi. He argued that clinging to a besieged city was unwise, citing Guan Zhong and Cao Mo as examples of those who overcame disgrace to achieve greatness. The general, torn between fear of execution and shame, committed suicide, leading to Qi’s capture of Liaocheng. Qi’s king offered Lu a title, but he fled to the seaside, preferring poverty to serving others.

translation:
He wrote a letter of self-recommendation and was a disciple of King Liang Xiao among Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui.
Yang Sheng and others were jealous of Zou Yang and spoke ill of him in front of King Xiao of Liang.
King Xiao of Liang was very angry. He handed Zou Yang over to his subordinate officials and wanted to kill him.
Zou Yang traveled in the Liang Kingdom and was arrested for being slandered. Worried about being accused of unwarranted charges after his death, he wrote a letter to King Xiao of Liang from prison. He wrote: I heard that loyal people will be rewarded and honest people will not be suspected. I always thought it was right in the past, but today it seems to be just an empty talk.
In the past, Gao Yi, whom Jing Ke admired from Prince Dan of Yan, went to assassinate the King of Qin. Although there was a sign of a white rainbow penetrating the sun in the sky, Prince Dan of Yan was still worried that Jing Ke would regret it and did not dare to go; Mr. Wei planned the Changping event for the King of Qin, and there was also a sign that Venus would cover the Pleiades, but King Zhao of Qin was still full of doubts.
Their sincerity moved the world and showed signs, but they were not understood by the two masters Yan Dan and Zhao Wang. Isn't this sad!
Now I am trying my best to be loyal and give my best advice, hoping that your Majesty will adopt it. The people around you did not understand the situation and finally handed me over to the officials for interrogation. I was misunderstood by the world. Even if Jing Ke and Wei were resurrected, King Yan Dan and Qin Zhao would not wake up.
I hope your Majesty will examine this situation carefully.
In the past, Bian He offered jade, and the king of Chu chopped off his feet; Li Si tried his best to be loyal, but Hu Hai had him executed.
So Jizi pretended to be crazy and took his father into seclusion to hide from the world. They were all afraid of suffering such a disaster.
I hope your Majesty will carefully examine the sincerity of Bian He and Li Si, and don't believe in slander like King Chu and Hu Hai, and don't let me be ridiculed by Ji Zi and Jie Yu.
I heard that Bigan was disemboweled and Wu Zixu's body was put into a leather bag and thrown into the river. I didn't believe it at first, but now I know that such a thing happened.
I hope your Majesty will examine it carefully and show me a little mercy!
As the saying goes: Some people are strangers even after getting along with them for a long time, while some people feel like old friends as soon as they stop and talk.
What is this wish for?
It lies in knowing one's heart and not knowing one's heart.
Therefore, in the past, Fan Yuqi fled from Qin to Yan, and lent his head to Jing Ke to carry out Yan Dan's mission of assassinating the King of Qin; Wang She left Qi for Wei, and committed suicide on the city wall to retreat the Qi army and protect Wei.
Wang She and Fan Yuqi were not new friends with Qi and Qin, but old acquaintances with Yan and Wei. The reason why they left Qi and Qin to die for the two kings of Yan and Wei was because their actions and aspirations were consistent and they had infinite admiration for justice!
Therefore, Su Qin was not trusted by the people of the world, but he was as trustworthy to the Yan State as his first son; Bai Gui was defeated and lost the cities of the Six Kingdoms, but he captured Zhongshan for the Wei State.
Why is this?
It's really because of mutual acquaintance.
Su Qin was appointed as the Prime Minister of the Yan State. Someone from the State of Yan slandered him in front of the king. The King of Yan was angry with his sword and slaughtered his beloved horse and gave him the meat to eat.
summary: Zou Yang, also from Qi, served King Xiao of Liang but was slandered by rivals and imprisoned. From prison, he wrote a letter defending his loyalty, citing historical figures like Bian He, Li Si, and Bigan, who suffered unjustly. He argued that true understanding between ruler and subject transcends slander, as seen with Su Qin and Yan, or Baili Xi and Duke Mu of Qin. He warned that listening to flattery leads to ruin, as with Lu and Song. King Xiao released him, and Zou became his honored guest.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/鲁仲连邹阳列传

translation:
This letter was presented to King Xiao of Liang, who sent someone to release Zou Yang from prison, and finally became King Xiao of Liang's honored guest.
Tai Shigong said: Even if the main purpose of Lu Zhonglian's discussion is not righteous, I applaud him for being a common man, free and easy, not yielding to the princes, commenting on the current world, but he has convinced the powerful ministers and prime ministers.
Even though Zou Yang's words are not modest enough, his comparisons between similar things are indeed touching. He can also be said to be frank, honest and unyielding, so I attach him to this biography.
summary: Sima Qian comments that while Lu Zhonglian’s arguments may not be entirely righteous, his independence and ability to sway powerful figures are admirable. Zou Yang’s words, though immodest, are sincere and compelling, earning him a place in this biography.
