translation:
Qingbu is from Liuxian County and his surname is Ying. During the Qin Dynasty, he was a common man.
When he was a child, a guest showed him a fortune and said: After being tortured, I will be king.
When he reached his prime, he broke the law and was sentenced to tattoo.
Tingbu smiled happily and said: Someone showed me a picture and said that I should be king after being tortured. Now, this is probably the situation, right?
Everyone who heard him say this laughed at him.
Not long after his conviction, Yingbu was sent to Lishan for hard labor. There were hundreds of thousands of prisoners in Lishan.
When Chen Sheng rebelled, Ying Bu went to see Wu Rui, the magistrate of Fan County, and rebelled against the Qin Dynasty with his men, gathering a team of several thousand people.
Magistrate Fan even married his daughter to him.
After Zhang Han eliminated Chen Sheng and defeated Lu Chen's army, Yingbu led his troops north to attack Qin's left and right schools, defeated them at Qingbo, and then led his troops to advance eastward.
Yingbu heard that Xiang Liang had pacified Kuaiji in the east of the Yangtze River and crossed the Yangtze River to march west. Chen Ying led his army to Xiang Liang because Xiang had been the general of the Chu State for generations, and crossed the Huai River southward. Generals Yingbu and Pu also led their troops to join Xiang Liang.
Xiang Liang led his troops across the Huaihe River and marched westward. In the battles against Jingju, Qin Jia and others, Qingbu was brave and good at fighting and was always ranked first among the troops.
Xiang Liang arrived in Xuedi and heard that King Chen was indeed dead, so he supported King Huai of Chu.
Xiang Liang was called Wu Xinjun, and Yingbu was called Dangyang Lord.
Xiang Liang was defeated and died in Dingtao. King Huai of Chu moved his capital to Pengcheng, and the generals and Yingbu also gathered in Pengcheng to guard it.
At this time, the Qin army stepped up its siege on Zhao State, and Zhao State repeatedly sent people to ask for help.
King Huai of Chu sent Song Yi as the top general, Fan Zeng as the last general, Xiang Ji as the second general, Yingbu and Pu as generals, all under Song Yi's command, to rescue Zhao State in the north.
When Xiang Ji killed Song Yi on the bank of the Yellow River, King Huai took advantage of the situation and appointed Xiang Ji as general, and all generals were under Xiang Ji's control.
Xiang Ji sent Yingbu to take the lead in crossing the Yellow River to attack the Qin army. Yingbu had the advantage due to his repeated military exploits. Xiang Ji led all his troops across the Yellow River and fought in coordination with Yingbu. They defeated the Qin army and forced Zhang Han and others to surrender.
The Chu army won many battles and conquered all the princes.
The reason why the armies of various princes can gradually surrender to Chu is because Yingbu can command the army to defeat many with less, which is impressive!
Xiang Ji led his troops westward to Xin'an, and sent Yingbu and others to attack at night and bury more than 200,000 Zhang Han's subordinates alive.
When they arrived outside Hangu Pass and could not enter, they sent Yingbu and others to take a small path to attack the defenders under the pass before entering the pass and reaching Xianyang City.
Yingbu often served as a pioneer.
King Xiang granted titles to the generals, named Yingbu the King of Jiujiang, and made six counties his capital.
In April of the first year of Han Dynasty, all the princes left the theater and returned to their respective feudal states.
King Xiang supported King Huai as the righteous emperor and moved the capital to Changsha, but secretly ordered Wang Yingbu of Jiujiang and others to sneak attack him on the way.
In August of that year, Yingbo sent generals to attack Emperor Yi and chased him to Chen County and killed him.
In the second year of the Han Dynasty, King Tian Rong of Qi betrayed the State of Chu. King Xiang went to attack Qi and mobilized troops to Jiujiang. The King of Jiujiang excused himself because he was seriously ill and could not go, so he only sent generals with several thousand people to enlist.
The king of Han defeated the Chu army in Pengcheng, and Yingbu excused himself from assisting Chu due to illness.
King Xiang resented Yingbu and repeatedly sent envoys to blame Yingbu and summon him to go. Yingbo became more and more frightened and did not dare to go.
King Xiang was worried about Qi and Zhao in the north, and worried about the Han Dynasty in the west. The only one he knew well was the King of Jiujiang. The King of Han particularly valued Yingbu's talents and planned to get close to him and appoint him, so he did not attack him.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han attacked Chu and launched a large-scale war in Pengcheng. After the defeat, he retreated from Liang and came to Yu County. He said to those close to him: People like you are not worthy of planning world affairs together.
summary: Yingbu, a commoner from Liuxian County with the surname Ying, was predicted in his youth to become a king after being tortured. After being sentenced to tattooing for breaking the law, he laughed at the prophecy's fulfillment. Sent to hard labor at Lishan, he later rebelled against the Qin Dynasty with Wu Rui, the magistrate of Fan County, gathering thousands of troops. Yingbu joined Xiang Liang, proving himself brave in battle, and was titled Dangyang Lord. After Xiang Liang's death, he served under Xiang Ji (Xiang Yu), leading attacks that defeated the Qin army and forced Zhang Han's surrender. Yingbu buried over 200,000 Qin soldiers alive and helped Xiang Yu enter Xianyang. He was named King of Jiujiang and later killed the Righteous Emperor on Xiang Yu's orders.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/黥布列传

translation:
I don't think Huainan's army is enough to destroy Chu.
As long as the king sends troops to betray the Chu State, King Xiang will definitely be restrained. As long as he is restrained for a few months, the King of Han will be able to seize the world without fail.
I request you to carry a sword and surrender to the Han Kingdom. The King of Han will definitely divide the land and grant it to the king. Not to mention Huainan. Huainan will definitely belong to the king.
Therefore, the king of Han seriously sent envoys to propose immature strategies, hoping that the king would seriously consider them.
King Huainan said: I will follow your advice.
He secretly agreed to betray Chu and return to Han, but did not dare to reveal this secret.
At this time, the Chu State's envoy was still in Huainan, urging Yingbu to send troops and stayed in a guest house.
Sui He rushed in, sat on the table of Chu's envoys, and said, "The king of Jiujiang has surrendered to the king of Han. Why should Chu let him send troops?"
Yingbu looked surprised.
The envoy from Chu State stood up to leave.
Sui He took the opportunity to persuade Yingbu: "The important thing has been accomplished. We can kill the Chu envoy immediately. We cannot let him go back. Let's move closer to the Han Dynasty and fight together."
Yingbu said: Just follow your instructions and send troops to attack Chu.
So he killed the envoy and sent troops to attack Chu.
Chu State then sent Xiang Sheng and Long Qie to attack Huainan, while King Xiang stayed to attack Xiayi.
The war lasted for several months, and Long Qie defeated Yingbu's army in the battle of Huainan.
Yingbu wanted to lead his troops to retreat to Han, but he was afraid that Chu's army would intercept and kill him, so he and Suihe fled back to Han through a hidden trail.
When King Huainan arrived, the King of Han was sitting on the bed washing his feet, so he asked Yingbu to see him. When Yingbu saw this, he was so angry that he regretted coming and wanted to commit suicide.
When he exited and came to the hotel prepared for him, Yingbu was overjoyed again when he saw that the curtains, utensils, food, and attendant officials were as luxurious as those of the King of Han.
So he sent people to Jiujiang.
At this time, the King of Chu had sent Xiang Bo to recruit Jiujiang's troops and killed Yingbu's wife and children.
The people sent by Yingbu found Yingbu's friends and close subordinates, and took thousands of people to defect to the king of Han.
The king of Han gave Yingbu more troops and went north with him to recruit troops at Chenggao.
In July of the fourth year of Han Dynasty, the king of Han granted Yingbu the title of King of Huainan, and together with him he attacked Xiang Ji.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu sent people into Jiujiang and captured several counties.
In the sixth year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu and Liu Jia entered Jiujiang and lured the great Sima Zhou Yin to surrender. After Zhou Yin rebelled against the Chu State, he mobilized the Jiujiang army and the Han army to jointly attack the Chu State and defeated the Chu army in Gaixia.
After Xiang Ji's death, the world was at peace. The emperor held a banquet, but belittled Sui He's achievements, saying that Sui He was a pedantic, conservative, and out-of-date scholar. How could such a person be used to govern the world.
Sui He knelt before the emperor and said: When your Majesty led troops to attack Pengcheng, the King of Chu had not yet left Qi. Your Majesty mobilized 50,000 infantry and 5,000 cavalry. Can you capture Huainan with this small force?
The emperor said: No.
Sui He said: Your Majesty sent me and 20 people as an envoy to Huainan. As soon as we arrived, Your Majesty got what he wanted. My contribution is greater than the 50,000 infantry and 5,000 cavalry.
But Your Majesty said that I am a pedantic, conservative and outdated scholar. Why is this? The emperor said: I am considering your contribution.
So he appointed Sui He as the guard lieutenant.
Yingbu cut off his talisman and became the king of Huainan. He established six counties as his capital. Jiujiang, Lujiang, Hengshan and Yuzhang counties all belonged to Yingbu.
In the seventh year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu went to Chen County to meet the emperor.
In the eighth year of the Han Dynasty, he went to Luoyang to meet with him.
In the ninth year of Han Dynasty, he went to Chang'an to meet with him.
In the eleventh year of the Han Dynasty, Empress Gao executed Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, and Yingbu was frightened.
In the summer of this year, the king of Han killed Peng Yue, the king of Liang, and chopped him into meat paste. He packed the meat paste and gave it to the princes.
When he was sent to Huainan, the king of Huainan was hunting. He was particularly frightened when he saw the meat paste. He secretly made arrangements to gather troops to wait and detect the unexpected emergency in neighboring counties.
summary: During the Chu-Han conflict, Yingbu feigned illness to avoid aiding Xiang Yu, who grew resentful. The Han king, valuing Yingbu's talents, sent Sui He to persuade him to defect. Sui He argued that Chu was weak and unjust, while Han was strong, promising Yingbu land and titles. Yingbu agreed, killed the Chu envoy, and attacked Chu. After being defeated by Long Qie, he fled to Han with Sui He. Initially angered by the Han king's casual reception, he was pleased by the luxurious treatment. The Han king granted him the title King of Huainan, and Yingbu helped defeat Xiang Yu at Gaixia.

translation:
The emperor said: Which strategy will Yingbu choose?
Ling Yin replied: Choose the next best thing.
The emperor said: Why did he give up the best policy or the middle policy and choose the worst policy?
Ling Yin said: Yingbu was originally a prisoner of Lishan, and he worked hard to become the master of ten thousand chariots. This was all for his own wealth, without caring about the current people or future generations, so he chose the wrong strategy. The emperor said: Well said.
Grant Xue Gong the title of Marquis of Thousand Households.
The prince Liu Chang was canonized as King of Huainan.
The emperor mobilized the army and personally led the eastward attack on Yingbu.
At the beginning of the rebellion, Yingbu said to his generals: The emperor is old and hates fighting. He must not be able to lead troops in person and send generals. The generals are only afraid of Huaiyin and Peng Yue. Now that they are dead, the other generals have nothing to fear.
So rebelled.
As Duke Xue expected, he went east to attack Jing State. King Liu Jia of Jing fled and died in Fuling.
Yingbu hijacked all his troops and crossed the Huaihe River to attack Chu.
The state of Chu mobilized its troops to fight Yingbu between Xu and Tong. The state of Chu divided its troops into three groups and tried to adopt a strange strategy of mutual rescue.
Someone advised the Chu general: Yingbu is good at using troops to fight, and the people have always been afraid of him.
Moreover, the Art of War says: When princes fight the enemy in their own territory, once the soldiers are in danger, they will flee.
Now the troops are divided into three groups. As long as they defeat one of our troops, the rest will run away. How can they rescue each other?
The Chu general did not listen to the advice.
Sure enough, Yingbo defeated one of the armies, and the other two armies fled in all directions.
Yingbu's army advanced westward and met the emperor's army at Huizhen, west of Qixian County.
Yingbu's army was very elite, so the emperor hid in the fortress of Yongcheng and could not get out. When he saw that Yingbu's formation was just like Xiang Ji's army, the emperor was very disgusted with him.
Seeing Yingbu from a distance, he said to Yingbu from a distance: Why bother to rebel?
Yingbu said: I want to be the emperor!
The emperor was furious and scolded him, and then the two armies fought.
Yingbu's army was defeated and fled, crossing the Huaihe River. They stopped and fought several times, but all failed, so they had to flee to the south of the Yangtze River with more than a hundred people.
Yingbu was originally married to the magistrate of Fan County. Therefore, King Ai of Changsha sent someone to trick Yingbu into fleeing to South Vietnam. Yingbu believed him and followed him to Fanyang. The Fanyang people killed Yingbu in the houses of the people in Zixiang and finally destroyed Yingbu.
The emperor appointed Prince Liu Chang as the King of Huainan, and granted Benhe the title of Marquis of Si. Most of the generals were rewarded for their military exploits.
Tai Shigong said: Yingbu, are his ancestors the descendants of the British and Six Kingdoms Gaotao who were destroyed by the Chu Kingdom as recorded in the "Spring and Autumn"?
He himself was tattooed, so why could he rise to prominence so quickly?
Xiang killed thousands of people and buried them alive, and Yingbu was often the culprit.
His merits were ranked highest among the princes, so he was able to become king, but he could not avoid suffering the greatest humiliation in the world.
The root of the disaster is caused by concubine love. Jealousy leads to disaster, which actually leads to the destruction of the country.
summary: After peace, Yingbu grew fearful upon seeing the execution of Han Xin and Peng Yue. His favored concubine's praise of a doctor's neighbor, Ben He, led to suspicion of adultery. Ben He fled to Chang'an and reported Yingbu's rebellion. Despite initial disbelief, Yingbu killed Ben He's family and rebelled. The emperor consulted Xue Gong, who predicted Yingbu would choose a poor strategy—attacking Wu and Chu but fleeing to Changsha. Yingbu indeed attacked Jing and Chu, defeating them, but was routed by the emperor's army at Huizhen. He fled south with a hundred men, was tricked by King Ai of Changsha, and killed by Fanyang people. The emperor made Prince Liu Chang King of Huainan. The historian notes Yingbu's rise from tattooing to kingship, his role in massacres, and his downfall due to jealousy over a concubine.
rel_path: 史记/七十列传/黥布列传

translation:
Tai Shigong said: Since ancient times, the sage kings are about to establish a country, accept the destiny of heaven, and establish a cause. How can they not respect the use of divination to help achieve good deeds?
It is impossible to record what happened before Tang Yao and Yu Shun.
Judging from the rise of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, they were all based on auspicious omens from divination.
Dayu's marriage to the daughter of the Tushan clan was auspicious, so Xia Qi established the Xia Dynasty, which has been passed down from generation to generation; Jian Di swallowed the eggs of flying swallows, and the auspicious predictions were favorable, so the Yin Dynasty rose; Houji, who was good at sowing hundreds of grains, got auspiciousness, so the king of Zhou finally became the king of the world.
When the king decided on difficult matters, he would refer to the results of divination made with the turtle to make the final decision. This was an unchanging traditional procedure.
Although the Barbarians, Barbarians, Di and Qiang did not have the Chinese-style hierarchy of monarchs and ministers, they also had the custom of divination for making decisions and doubts.
Some use gold and stone, some use plants and trees, and divination customs vary from country to country.
But they can all be used to guide war operations, research, and achieve victory in wars. Each worships the gods of divination to predict future events.
I have heard a little bit: During the Xia and Yin Dynasties, yarrow turtles were found when it was time to perform divination, and they were discarded after the divination, because they believed that turtle shell yarrow would not be effective if stored.
In the Zhou Dynasty, diviners always collected yarrow and tortoise shells for later use. In addition, who is more intelligent and who is less intelligent? When using Turtleweed, which one comes first and which one comes last?
Every dynasty has different values. But in summary, the purpose of using turtle divination methods to help people predict the future is the same. Some people believe that there was never a time when the Holy King was undecided when encountering something; there was never a time when the Holy King lacked insights when solving problems. The reason why they set up the method of praying to gods and asking for divination is because they are worried that future generations will decline and decline. Foolish people will not learn from smart people. Everyone will be satisfied with their own knowledge. Differences in education will arise. The big principles will be broken into pieces and cannot be grasped. Therefore, they push the physical and emotional affairs to the most subtle realm, that is, the gods, and seek purity in the spirit.
Some people also think that what the tortoise is good at, the saint cannot catch up with.
It judges good and bad, distinguishes right from wrong, and is often more accurate than human predictions.
After Emperor Gaozu succeeded to the throne, he followed the system of the Qin Dynasty and established diviners.
At that time, the country had just been unified and the war had not stopped.
As for Emperor Xiaohui, his reign was short, Empress Lu was the heroine, and Emperor Xiaowen and Emperor Xiaojing just followed the old system and did not have time to study the divination in depth. Therefore, although fortune-telling has been passed down from father to son and passed down from generation to generation, many of its subtle and profound principles and methods have been lost.
Now that the emperor has ascended the throne, he has opened up the path for talented people to advance, and has recruited various scholars. Anyone who is proficient in a certain skill will have the opportunity to contribute, and those with outstanding skills will receive preferential treatment. He is pragmatic and has no partiality. In the past few years, the Taibu official office has gathered many talents.
At this time, the emperor was about to attack the Xiongnu in the north, Dawan in the west, and Baiyue in the south. Divination could predict changes in events and suggest ways to gain advantages and avoid disadvantages.
Later, fierce generals were ordered to lead troops to charge and win on the battlefield, which also included the contribution of divination's pre-planning in the temple.
As a result, the emperor paid more attention to the fortune-telling officials, and the rewards sometimes amounted to tens of millions of dollars.
For example, Qiu Ziming and others' wealth increased dramatically, and they were greatly favored, overwhelming the ministers of the court.
Even divination is used to guess the behavior of witches and Gu, and the behavior of witches and Gu can sometimes be guessed accurately.
summary: Tai Shigong observed that since ancient times, sage kings establishing states and accepting heaven's mandate have always respected divination to aid good deeds. Evidence from Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties shows their rises were based on auspicious divination omens: Dayu's marriage to the Tushan daughter was auspicious, leading to Xia Qi's dynasty; Jian Di swallowing a swallow's egg brought favorable predictions for Yin's rise; Houji's agricultural skill brought auspiciousness for Zhou kingship. Kings consulted turtle divination for difficult decisions as an unchanging tradition. Even barbarian tribes without Chinese hierarchy had divination customs using various materials like gold, stone, plants, and wood, all guiding warfare and predicting events. During Xia and Yin, yarrow and turtle shells were discarded after divination, but Zhou collectors preserved them. Different dynasties valued divination differently, but all used it to predict the future. Some believed holy kings never lacked insights but established divination to guide future generations who might decline in wisdom. Others thought turtles' judgment surpassed human predictions. After Emperor Gaozu succeeded, he followed Qin's system to establish diviners, but the country's unification and ongoing wars prevented deep study. Emperors Xiaohui, Empress Lu, Xiaowen, and Xiaojing merely followed old systems, causing subtle divination methods to be lost. When the current emperor ascended, he opened paths for talented people, recruiting scholars proficient in various skills. The Taibu office gathered many talents. The emperor planned attacks on Xiongnu, Dawan, and Baiyue, using divination to predict changes and suggest advantages. Generals' battlefield successes included divination's contributions. The emperor rewarded divination officials heavily, with some like Qiu Ziming gaining enormous wealth and favor, overwhelming court ministers. Divination even predicted witch and Gu behaviors accurately. Those who offended diviners faced revenge and family destruction, causing officials to flatter turtle and yarrow theories. Eventually, false accusations were exposed, and the diviners' three clans were wiped out.

translation:
For those who had offended them even slightly, they would seek opportunities to avenge themselves and persecute them wantonly. As a result, the number of people who had their families destroyed was incalculable.
All civil and military officials were in panic, and they all flattered him that the theory of turtles and yarrow was effective.
Later, the true nature of the false accusation by the fortune teller was exposed, and the three clans were also wiped out.
Since yarrow is used to predict good and bad luck, and tortoise shells are burned to observe the omens, the changes are endless. Therefore, wise men are selected as divination officials. This can be said to be the importance that the saints attach to the important matter of divination!
Duke Zhou used tortoise shells for divination three times, so King Wu of Zhou could recover from his illness.
King Zhou was tyrannical, so even using a big turtle would not bring good luck.
Duke Wen of Jin was about to restore King Zhou Xiang to the throne. During the divination, he got a good omen that "The Yellow Emperor fought at Banquan". He finally succeeded and received the Tong Bow from King Zhou Xiang with the order of conquest, and became Hou Bo.
Duke Xian of Jin was covetous of Li Ji's beauty and wanted to attack Li Rong. He predicted that victory would be an unlucky omen. The disaster of attacking Li Rong actually extended to the fifth king of Jin.
King Ling of Chu was about to betray the Zhou royal family, and the divination was unlucky, which finally led to Qianxi's defeat.

After getting in the car. The axle is broken and the car is useless.

summary: Emperor Xiaojing had thirteen sons by five mothers, all named kings. Liu Rong, once crown prince, was deposed and later died by suicide after being convicted of expanding his palace onto temple grounds. His kingdom was abolished. Liu Yu, King of Lu, built palaces and loved music but stuttered. Liu Fei, King of Jiangdu, was a brave military leader who defeated Wu in the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms. His son Liu Jian committed suicide after plotting rebellion, adultery, and witchcraft. Liu Duan, King of Jiaoxi, was cruel and impotent, often killing officials who followed Han laws. He lived between the Yellow River and Qishui River, which was the ancient capital of the Shang Dynasty, Yinxu.
Zhou Gongdan was worried that Uncle Kang was young and would have difficulty maintaining his rule, so he repeatedly warned Uncle Kang: You must find talented, prestigious, and experienced people in the Yin Dynasty, and learn from them the history of the rise and fall of the Yin Dynasty, and you must care for and care for your own people.
He also warned Kang Shu that the reason for Zhou's demise was that he drank excessively, indulged in pleasure, and indulged in female sex. Therefore, the chaos in the reign of King Zhou began from here.
Zhou Gongdan also wrote "Zi Cai" in accordance with the principle that craftsmen must use rules when making woodenware, as a guideline for rulers to follow.
Therefore, it was called "Kang Gao", "Jiu Gao" and "Zicai", and was used to teach Uncle Kang.
Uncle Kang used these principles to govern the feudal country, stabilize and harmonize his people, and the people were very happy.
After King Cheng came of age, he personally took charge of the political power, appointed Uncle Kang as the Sikou of the Zhou Dynasty, and gave him many treasures and sacrificial vessels to commend Uncle Kang's virtues.
After Uncle Kang's death, his son Kang Bo became the king.
After Kang Bo's death, his son Kao Bo became the king.
After Kaobo's death, his son Sibo became the king.
After the death of Sibo, his son Boli became the king.
After Bo's death, his son Jing Bo became the king.
After the death of Jingbo, his son Zhenbo became the king.
After the death of Zhenbo, his son Qinghou was established as the king.
Because the Marquis of Qing bribed the King of Zhou Yi with generous gifts, the King of Yi ordered the King of Wei to be named Marquis.
Qinghou died in the twelfth year after he became the king, and his son Lihou became the king.
In the thirteenth year of Lihou's reign, King Li of Zhou fled to the land of Hu, and Duke Zhao and Duke of Zhou took charge of the political power together, which was named "Republican Administration".
In the twenty-eighth year of Lihou, King Xuan of Zhou was established as the emperor.
In the forty-second year, Marquis Li died, and Prince Gong Boyu became the king.
summary: Uncle Kang of Wei, named Feng, was the half-brother of King Wu of Zhou. After King Wu defeated the Shang dynasty, he granted the remnants of Yin to Wu Geng, King Zhou's son, but worried about rebellion. He sent Guan Shu and Cai Shu to monitor Wu Geng. After King Wu's death, King Cheng was young, and Zhou Gongdan ruled as regent. Guan Shu and Cai Shu, suspecting Zhou Gongdan, rebelled with Wu Geng. Zhou Gongdan suppressed the rebellion, killed Wu Geng and Guan Shu, exiled Cai Shu, and granted the Yin remnants to Kang Shu, making him ruler of Wei. Zhou Gongdan warned Kang Shu to learn from Yin's history, avoid excessive drinking and pleasure, and wrote "Kang Gao," "Jiu Gao," and "Zi Cai" as guidelines. Kang Shu governed well, and the people were content. After King Cheng came of age, he appointed Kang Shu as Sikou and honored him.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/卫康叔世家

translation:
Gongbo's younger brother He Zeng was favored by Marquis Li. Marquis Li gave He a lot of property. He then used these properties to bribe warriors and attacked Gongbo Yu in Lihou's cemetery. Gongbo was forced to flee to the tomb of Lihou and commit suicide.
The people of Wei buried Gongbo next to Lihou's tomb and called him Gongbo. They established He as the king of Wei, and he was named Wu Gong.
After Duke Wu came to the throne, he reorganized Uncle Kang's government affairs, and the people lived in peace and harmony.
In the 42nd year, Quan Rong killed King You of Zhou. Duke Wu personally commanded the generals to assist the Emperor of Zhou in quelling the invasion of Quan Rong and established military exploits. King Ping of Zhou ordered Duke Wu to declare himself duke.
In the fifty-fifth year, Duke Wu passed away, and his son Zhuang Gongyang became the king.
In the fifth year of Duke Zhuang's accession to the throne, he married a daughter of the State of Qi as his wife. The daughter of Qi was beautiful but childless.
Duke Zhuang then married Chen Guonv, who gave birth to a son who died in infancy.
Chen Nu's sister was also favored by Duke Zhuang and gave birth to a son named Wan.
After Wan's mother passed away, Duke Zhuang asked his wife Qi to raise Wan and made Wan the prince.
Duke Zhuang also had a beloved concubine who gave birth to a son named Zhouxu.
In the eighteenth year of Duke Zhuang, Zhouxu grew up and liked military affairs, so Duke Zhuang appointed him as a general in the army.
Shi Jue, the high minister of the Wei State, kindly came to admonish Duke Zhuang and said, "My son is fond of military affairs. Please make him a general. From now on, troubles will arise."
Duke Zhuang refused to listen. In the twenty-third year, Duke Zhuang passed away and the crown prince was established as the king. This is Duke Huan.
In the second year of Duke Huan, his younger brother Zhou Xu was arrogant and extravagant. Duke Huan deposed him and Zhou Xu fled abroad.
In the thirteenth year, Duan, Zheng Bo's younger brother, attacked his elder brother but failed to win and fled. Zhouxu asked for friendship with him.
In the 16th year, Zhouxu gathered the fugitives of Weiguo to attack and kill Duke Huan. Zhouxu himself established himself as the king of Weiguo.
Because Zheng Bo's brother Duan wanted to attack the state of Zheng, Zhouxu asked Song, Chen, and Cai to jointly support Duan, and the three countries all agreed to this request.
Zhouxu had just ascended the throne. Because he was fond of military affairs and killed Duke Huan, all the people in the Wei Dynasty hated him.
Because Duke Huan's mother lived in Chen State, Shi Que pretended to be friendly with Zhouxu. The Wei army marched to the outskirts of the capital of Zheng State. Shi Que and Chen Hou conspired and sent their right minister Chou to offer food to Zhouxu. They took the opportunity to kill Zhouxu in Pu, and brought Duke Huan's younger brother Jin back to Wei State from Xingdi and established him as king. This is Duke Xuan.
In the seventh year of Xuangong's reign, the people of Lu killed their king Yin Gong.
In the ninth year, the governor of the Song Dynasty killed his own monarch Shang Gong and his doctor Kong Fu.
In the tenth year, Zhuangbo Quwo of Jin State also killed his own king Aihou.
In the eighteenth year, Yi Jiang, the beloved wife of Duke Xuan, gave birth to a son named Ji, who was made the crown prince. Xuan Gong sent You Gongzi to teach him.
The right prince married a beautiful girl from Qi for the prince. The beauty was not married to Ji Baitang, but she was seen by Duke Xuan. Seeing the beauty of the girl from Qi, Duke Xuan liked her very much, so he married her himself and married another girl for the prince.
After Duke Xuan got the daughter of Qi, the daughter of Qi gave birth to sons Zishou and Zishuo. Duke Xuan sent Mr. Zuo to teach them.
After the death of Prince Ji's mother, Mrs. Xuan Gong and Zi Shuo jointly slandered and framed Prince Ji in front of Duke Xuan.
Duke Xuan originally hated the prince because he had snatched his wife, and he had long wanted to destroy him.
summary: After Kang Shu's death, his descendants ruled Wei for generations. Qinghou bribed King Yi of Zhou to have the ruler of Wei titled Marquis. During Lihou's reign, King Li of Zhou fled, and the "Republican Administration" began. Later, Gongbo Yu was forced to commit suicide by his brother He, who became Duke Wu. Duke Wu reformed governance, and the people prospered. He assisted King Ping of Zhou against Quan Rong and was declared duke. After his death, Duke Zhuang succeeded him. Duke Zhuang married a Qi woman who was childless, then married a Chen woman who bore a son who died. Another Chen woman bore Wan, who was made prince. Duke Zhuang also had a son, Zhouxu, who loved military affairs. Minister Shi Que warned Duke Zhuang, but he ignored him. After Duke Zhuang's death, Prince Wan became Duke Huan. Zhouxu, arrogant and extravagant, was deposed and fled. Later, Zhouxu gathered fugitives, killed Duke Huan, and declared himself ruler. He sought to support Zheng Bo's brother Duan, but the people hated him for killing Duke Huan. Shi Que conspired with Chen Hou to kill Zhouxu and established Duke Huan's brother Jin as Duke Xuan.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/卫康叔世家

translation:
Duke Huan of Qi led the princes to attack Zhai because of the many turmoils in the Wei State. He built a castle in Chuqiu for the Wei State.
Duke Wen fled to Qi due to the turmoil in the Wei Dynasty, and the people of Qi sent him back home.
At first, when the people of Zhai killed Duke Yi, the people of Wei took pity on him and wanted to raise another descendant of the prince Ji who was murdered by Duke Xuan. However, Ji's son had died, and Zishou, who died in Ji's place, had no children.
Prince Ji had two brothers of the same mother: one was named Qian Mou. Qian Mou had been the king of Wei for eight years in place of Duke Hui, and was later driven out of Wei by Duke Hui. The other was named Zhao Bo.
Both Zhaobo and Qian Mou had died long ago, so the Wei people made Zhaobo's son Shen the Duke of Dai. After the death of Duke Dai, the Wei people made his younger brother Rui the Duke Wen.
When Duke Wen came to the throne, he reduced the people's taxes, clearly judged the crimes of prisoners, worked hard, and shared the joys and sorrows with the people, thus winning the hearts of the people.
In the sixteenth year, Jin Gongzi Chong'er passed by Weiguo. Duke Wen did not treat Chong'er politely.
In the seventeenth year, Duke Huan of Qi passed away.
In the twenty-fifth year, Duke Wen died, and his son Cheng Gong Zheng became the king.
In the third year of Chenggong's reign, Jin wanted to borrow a road from Wei in order to save Song Dynasty, but Chenggong refused.
Jin then changed its route and crossed the Nanhe River to rescue Song.
The Jin State conscripted troops from Wei. Doctor Wei wanted to agree, but Duke Cheng refused.
The official Yuan Yao attacked Duke Cheng, who fled to the state of Chu.
In order to avenge Duke Wen's rudeness when he passed by Wei State and Wei's failure to rescue Song State, Jin Wengong Chong'er attacked Wei State and gave part of Wei State's land to Song State. Duke Cheng of Wei had to flee to Chen.
Two years later, Duke Cheng went to Emperor Zhou to ask for help in returning to his country and met Duke Wen of Jin.
Jin sent people to kill Chenggong with poisoned wine. Chenggong bribed the person in charge of the poisoning in the Zhou royal family to let him use less poison, so that he could avoid death.
Soon, the King of Zhou petitioned Duke Wen of Jin on behalf of Duke Cheng. Duke Cheng was finally sent back to Wei, where he killed Yuan Yao and Wei Jun fled.
In the seventh year, Duke Wen of Jin passed away.
In the twelfth year, Duke Cheng went to see Duke Xiang of Jin.
In the fourteenth year, Duke Mu of Qin passed away.
In the twenty-sixth year, Qi Bingzha killed his king Yigong.
In the thirty-fifth year, Duke Cheng passed away, and his son Mu Gongtian became the king.
In the second year of Duke Mu's reign, King Zhuang of Chu attacked Chen and killed Xia Zhengshu.
Three years later, King Zhuang of Chu besieged the state of Zheng, and the Marquis of Zheng surrendered.
King Zhuang of Chu released him again. In the eleventh year, Sun Liangfu crusaded against Qi to rescue Lu and regained the invaded territory.
After the death of Duke Mu, his son Ding Gong Zang was established as the king.
In the twelfth year of the reign of Duke Dinggong, he passed away, and his son Xian Gong became the king.
In the thirteenth year, Duke Xian asked the musician Cao Cao to teach his concubine to play the piano. The concubine played poorly, so Cao Fei beat her as punishment.
Because the concubine Xian Gong favored him, she spoke ill of Cao in front of him and deliberately slandered Cao. Gong Xian also whipped Cao three hundred times.
summary: Duke Xuan's beloved wife Yi Jiang bore a son, Ji, who was made prince. Duke Xuan married a beautiful Qi woman for the prince but took her for himself. She bore Zishou and Zishuo. After Prince Ji's mother died, Zishuo slandered Ji. Duke Xuan, resenting Ji, sent him as envoy to Qi and ordered thieves to kill him. Zishou warned Ji, but Ji refused to disobey his father. Zishou stole Ji's envoy token and was killed first. Ji then arrived and was also killed. Duke Xuan made Zishuo crown prince. After Duke Xuan's death, Zishuo became Duke Hui. The left and right sons resented him, attacked, and made Qian Mou, Ji's brother, ruler. Duke Hui fled to Qi. Later, Duke Xiang of Qi, under Zhou orders, attacked Wei, restored Duke Hui, and killed the left and right sons. Qian Mou fled to Zhou. Duke Hui later attacked Zhou with Yan, forcing King Hui of Zhou to flee. Zheng later restored King Hui. After Duke Hui's death, his son Duke Yi succeeded. Duke Yi loved cranes and indulged in pleasure. When Zhai attacked, soldiers rebelled, and Zhai killed Duke Yi. The people, long dissatisfied with Duke Hui's line, made Zhao Bowan's son Shen, Duke Dai. After his death, his brother Rui became Duke Wen. Duke Wen reduced taxes, judged crimes fairly, and won the people's hearts. He later treated Jin's Chong'er rudely. After Duke Wen's death, his son Duke Cheng succeeded. Duke Cheng refused Jin passage to rescue Song, leading to conflict. Jin attacked Wei, and Duke Cheng fled. He later bribed Zhou officials to avoid poisoning and was restored after Zhou interceded. After Duke Cheng's death, his son Duke Mu succeeded. Duke Mu's reign saw Chu attacks on Chen and Zheng. After his death, his son Duke Ding succeeded, then Duke Xian. Duke Xian whipped musician Cao, who later slandered him. Duke Xian's rude behavior angered Sun Wenzi, who drove him out. Duke Xian fled to Qi. Sun Wenzi and Ning Huizi made Qiu, Duke Xian's brother, Duke Shang. Later, Ning and Sun fought, and Sun fled to Jin, asking Jin to restore Duke Xian. Jin attacked Wei, arrested Duke Shang, and restored Duke Xian. Duke Xian executed Ning happy. After his death, his son Duke Xiang succeeded. Duke Xiang's concubine dreamed of Uncle Kang, who said her son would rule Wei. She bore a son named Yuan, who became Duke Ling. Duke Ling's reign saw Confucius visit Wei. Prince Kuai Chi, resenting Duke Ling's wife Nan Zi, tried to kill her but failed and fled. After Duke Ling's death, his wife made Zi Ying ruler, but he declined, and the people made Zhe, Kuai Chi's son, Duke Chu. Zhao Jianzi tried to restore Kuai Chi, but Wei forces repelled him. Later, Kuai Chi, with help from Kong Kui's mother, returned, hijacked Kong Kui, and became Duke Zhuang. He wanted to kill ministers but relented. After his death, his son succeeded, but Wei faced turmoil. Eventually, Wei was demoted to a small state under Zhao. In the Qin dynasty, Weijun was deposed, ending the Wei lineage.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/卫康叔世家

translation:
In the sixth year of Zhaogong's reign, Prince Qi killed Duke Zhao and established himself as king. This was Duke Huai.
In the eleventh year of Duke Huai's reign, the prince killed Duke Huai and established himself as king. This was Duke Shen.
Duke Shen's father was Gongzi Shi. The suitable father is Mr. Jing.
In the forty-second year, Duke Shen passed away, and his son declared himself the king of the country.
In the eleventh year, Duke Sheng died, and his son Chenghou Tianli became the king.
In the eleventh year of Chenghou's reign, Gongsun Yang entered Qin.
In the sixteenth year, Wei was demoted to Hou.
In the twenty-ninth year, Chenghou passed away, and his son Pinghou became the king.
Pinghou died in the eighth year, and his son Heijun became the king.
In the fifth year of his reign, the successor was demoted to the title of "Jun", and he only had the title of "Puyang".
In the forty-second year, the heir passed away, and his son Huaijun became the king.
In the thirty-first year, Huaijun paid homage to Wei, and Wei imprisoned and killed Huaijun.
Wei changed and established a successor, Jun's younger brother, who was Yuan Jun.
Yuan Jun was the son-in-law of Wei State, so Wei State established him.
In the fourteenth year of Yuanjun, Qin captured the eastern territory of Wei, and Qin began to set up Dongjun in this area. He also moved Weijun to Yewang County and merged Puyang into Dongjun.
In the twenty-fifth year, Yuanjun passed away, and his son Junjiao became the king.
In the ninth year of Junjiao, Qin annexed the world and Ying Zheng was established as the first emperor.
In the twenty-first year of the Qin Dynasty, the second emperor of Qin deposed Weijun, Junjiao became an ordinary commoner, and the Weiguo lineage was completely cut off.
Tai Shigong said: I read the records of the family and read that the crown prince of Duke Xuan of Wei was killed because of his wife. His younger brother Zishou and the crown prince gave in to each other and fought to die. This is the same as the prince Shen Sheng of Jin who did not dare to declare Li Ji's fault because he was afraid of hurting his father's feelings.
However, it is so sad to finally die!
Some fathers and sons kill each other, and some brothers destroy each other. Why is this?
summary: Tai Shigong remarked on the tragic deaths of Prince Ji and Zishou, noting the sorrow of fathers and sons killing each other and brothers destroying one another.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/卫康叔世家

translation:
Taibo Wu and his younger brother Zhong Yong were both sons of Gu Gong Danfu, King Tai of Zhou, and brothers of Ji Li, King of Zhou.
Ji Li was very virtuous and had a virtuous son Chang. The Taiwang wanted to establish Ji Li in order to pass the throne to Chang, so Tai Bo and Zhong Yong went to the land of Jingman. Like the local barbarians, they covered their bodies with tattoos and cut their hair to show that they could no longer inherit the throne, so as to avoid Ji Li.
Ji Li succeeded to the throne as Wang Ji, and Chang later became King Wen.
After Taibo fled to Jingman, he called himself Wu Ju.
The Jingman people believed that he was very righteous, and more than a thousand households followed him and respected him as Taibo Wu.
Taibo died without a son, and his younger brother Zhongyong succeeded him; he was Wu Zhongyong.
Zhongyong died and his son Ji Jian succeeded to the throne.
Ji Jian died and his son Shuda succeeded him.
Shuda died and his son Zhou Zhang succeeded to the throne.
At that time, King Wu defeated Yin Zhou and was looking for the descendants of Tai Bo and Zhong Yong, and found Zhou Zhang.
Zhou Zhang was already the monarch of Wu, so King Wu officially granted him the land of Wu.
He also enfeoffed Zhou Zhang's younger brother Yu Zhong to the former site of the Xia capital in the north of Zhou Dynasty. He was named Yu Zhong and ranked among the princes.
Zhou Zhang died and his son Xiong Sui succeeded to the throne.
Xiong Sui died, and his son Ke succeeded him.
Ke Xiang died and his son Qiang Jiuyi succeeded to the throne.
Qiang Jiuyi died, and his son Yu Qiaoxinwu succeeded to the throne.
Yu Qiao Xinwu died, and his son Ke Lu succeeded to the throne.
Ke Lu died and his son Zhou Yao succeeded him.
Zhou Yao died and his son Qu Yu succeeded him.
Qu Yu died and his son Yi Wu succeeded him.
Yiwu died and his son Qinchu succeeded him.
Qin Chu died and his son succeeded him.
After his death, his son Po Gao succeeded him.
Po Gao died and his son Goubei succeeded him.
At this time, Duke Xian of Jin destroyed Duke Yu who was north of the Zhou Dynasty, because Duke Yu lent a road to the Jin State, allowing the Jin army to destroy the Guo State.
Goubei died, and his son went to Qi to succeed him.
Qu Qi died, and his son Shou Meng succeeded to the throne.
After Shou Meng succeeded to the throne, the Kingdom of Wu began to become stronger, and Shou Meng called himself the king.
Counting from Taibo's founding of the Kingdom of Wu to the fifth generation, King Wu defeated the Yin Dynasty and named his descendants two kingdoms: one was the Kingdom of Yu, in the Central Plains, and the other was the Kingdom of Wu, in the barbarian zone.
By the twelfth generation, the Jin State destroyed the Yu State in the Central Plains.
Two more generations later, the state of Wu in the barbarian region became prosperous.
In total, it has been passed down to nineteen generations from Taibo to Shoumeng.
In the second year of King Shoumeng of Wu, the exiled official Shen Gong Wuchen of the Chu State defected to the Jin State because he was resentful of the generals of the Chu State.
Later, Wu State began to send troops to conquer Chu State.
In the 16th year, the king of the Communist Party of Chu conquered the state of Wu and reached Mount Heng.
In the twenty-fifth year, King Wu Shoumeng passed away.
Shoumeng had four sons: the eldest son was named Zhufan, the second son was named Yuji, the third son was named Yumei, and the fourth son was named Jizha.
Ji Zha was a virtuous man, and Shou Meng wanted him to succeed him during his lifetime, but Ji Zha evaded and refused to agree, so he let his eldest son Zhufan succeed him, prime minister of various affairs, and take charge of state affairs on his behalf.
In the first year of King Zhufan of Wu, Zhufan removed his mourning clothes after the period of mourning and wanted to give up the throne to Jizha.
Ji Zha declined and said: When Cao Xuangong passed away, the princes of various countries and the people of Cao State thought that the newly established Lord Cao was unjust, and wanted to make Zang Zang the Lord of Cao. Zizang left the State of Cao so that Lord Cao could continue to reign. The gentleman commented on Zizang that he was able to observe integrity.
As the eldest son, you are the legitimate successor. Who dares to offend you?
Being a king is not what I should be doing.
summary: Taibo Wu and his younger brother Zhong Yong were sons of Gu Gong Danfu, King Tai of Zhou. Because their father wished to pass the throne to their younger brother Ji Li, and eventually to Ji Li's virtuous son Chang, Taibo and Zhong Yong fled to the land of Jingman. There, they adopted local customs by tattooing their bodies and cutting their hair to show they could not inherit the throne. The Jingman people, finding Taibo righteous, followed him and respected him as Taibo Wu. Taibo died without a son, and Zhong Yong succeeded him. The lineage continued until Zhou Zhang, who was officially granted the land of Wu by King Wu of Zhou after he defeated the Yin dynasty. The kingdom of Wu was passed down through generations, eventually becoming prosperous under King Shoumeng, who was the nineteenth generation from Taibo.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/吴太伯世家

translation:
In the seventeenth year, Wang Yuji died and his younger brother Yu Mei succeeded to the throne.
The year before last, Chu Gongzi abandoned his illness and killed King Ling of Chu, and made himself king on his behalf.
In the fourth year, Wang Yumei died and wanted to pass it on to his younger brother Jizha.
Jizha avoided the situation and fled away.
So the people of Wu said: According to the decree of the late king, if a brother dies and a brother succeeds to the throne, the kingdom must be passed on to Ji Zi.
Ji Zi now escaped from the throne, and Wang Yumei became the last of his brothers to become king.
Now that he is dead, his son should be king in his stead.
So he established Yu Mei's son Liao as King of Wu.
In the second year of King Liao's reign, Prince Guang led an army to conquer Chu, but was defeated and lost the ship of King Wu.
Prince Guang was afraid of being punished for this, so he attacked the Chu army secretly and recaptured Wang Zhou before returning to the army.
In the fifth year, Wu Zixu, an exiled minister of Chu State, fled to Wu State. The young master treated him as a guest.
Prince Guang was the son of King Zhufan of Wu.
He has always believed that my father and four brothers should be passed on to the Jizi.
Now Ji Zi is no longer the king, but my father is the first to be the king.
Since the kingdom is not passed on to Ji Zi, I should succeed my father as the king.
So he secretly recruited the Magi, hoping to use them to attack King Liao.
In the eighth year, the King of Wu sent his son Guang to conquer the Chu State, defeated the Chu army, and brought the mother of the former Chu Crown Prince Jian back to the State of Wu from Juchao.
Taking advantage of the Northern Expedition, he defeated Chen and Cai's armies.
The year before last, Prince Guang conquered Chu State again and captured the two cities of Juchao and Zhongli.
At the beginning, a girl from the Beiliang clan in the border town of Chu State competed with a woman from Wu border town to pick mulberry leaves. The families of the two women were angry and attacked each other. When the officials of the two border towns heard about it, they attacked each other in anger, and the border town of Wu State was destroyed.
The State of Wu was furious upon hearing this, so it attacked the State of Chu, captured the two cities of Juchao and Zhongli, and returned.
When Wu Zixu fled to Wu, he told King Liao of Wu about the benefits of attacking Chu.
Prince Guang said: Zixu's father and brother were killed by the King of Chu. He advised you to attack Chu to avenge your own personal revenge. Attacking Chu will not be beneficial to Wu.
Wu Zixu then understood that Gongzi Guang had an ulterior motive. Zixu found a warrior named Zhuan Zhu and introduced him to Gongzi Guang.
Prince Guang was very happy and treated Wu Zixu with courtesy.
Zixu retreated to the countryside to earn a living, waiting for Zhuanzhu to take action.
In the winter of the twelfth year, King Ping of Chu passed away.
In the spring of the year before last, the King of Wu wanted to take advantage of the state mourning in Chu to attack Chu. He sent his sons Gaiyu and Zhuyong to lead troops to surround Chu's Liu and Hao towns, and sent Ji Zha as an envoy to Jin to observe the movements of the princes.
Unexpectedly, the Chu State sent a surprise army to cut off its retreat, and the Wu soldiers were prevented from returning home.
At this time, Prince Guang of Wu State said: This opportunity cannot be lost.
Tell Zhuan Zhu: If you don't take action, you won't get anything.
I am the true heir to the throne and should be made king. This is what I want to pursue.
Even if Ji Zi comes back, he will not oppose me.
Zhuan Zhu said: The conditions for killing Wang Liao have been met. There are only his mother and young son in the country, but his two younger brothers led troops to attack Chu and were blocked from returning.
Now King Wu is besieged by the State of Chu outside the country, and there are no upright and loyal ministers in the country. No one can stop us.
Gongzi Guang said: My body is your body, sharing weal and woe.
On the day Bingzi of the fourth month, Prince Guang ambushed the soldiers in the basement, and then invited King Liao to a banquet.
King Liao sent troops to line up along the road. From the palace to Prince Guang's house, to the gate, steps, door and seats of Guang's house, they were all covered with King Liao's personal soldiers, each holding a sharp sword.
After King Liao arrived, Prince Guang pretended to have a pain in his feet and hid in the basement. He sent Zhuanzhu to hide the dagger in the belly of the whole roasted fish and pretend to serve it.
When Zhuan Zhu brought the fish to King Liao, he took out a dagger from the fish's belly and stabbed Wang Liao. The guards on the left and right hurriedly stabbed Zhuan Zhu's chest with their swords, but Wang Liao was already killed.
Prince Guang was indeed appointed King of Wu on his behalf, and he became the King of Wu's house.
summary: Shoumeng had four sons: Zhufan, Yuji, Yumei, and the virtuous Jizha. Shoumeng wanted Jizha to succeed him, but Jizha refused. The throne was then passed from brother to brother with the intention that it would eventually reach Jizha. After Yumei died, Jizha again fled, so the people established Yumei's son Liao as king. Prince Guang, the son of Zhufan, believed he should be king and secretly recruited a warrior named Zhuan Zhu. During a banquet, Zhuan Zhu assassinated King Liao, and Prince Guang became King Helu. Jizha, upon returning, accepted the new king, stating that as long as the ancestral sacrifices continued, the new king was his sovereign.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/吴太伯世家

translation:
Helu appointed Zhuanzhu's son as minister.
Jizha returned to the state of Wu and said: As long as the sacrifices to the ancestors are not abolished, the people will not be without a king, and the god of the country is enshrined, then he will be my king.
Who can I blame?
I can only mourn the dead and serve the living to deal with the destiny arrangements.
If you do not create trouble yourself, you should obey the newly established king. This is the principle of our ancestors.
So Jizha went to King Liao's tomb, reported how he completed his diplomatic mission, cried bitterly to King Liao, and then returned to his place in the court to wait for the new king's orders. Prince Gaiyu and Zhu Yong of the State of Wu were besieged by the Chu army with their troops. When they heard that Prince Guang had killed King Liao and proclaimed himself king, they led their troops to surrender to the State of Chu. The King of Chu sealed them in Shu.
In the first year of the reign of King Wu of Helu, Wu Zixu was appointed as an official of Xingren and participated in state affairs.
The King of Chu killed Bo Zhouli, and his grandson Bo Pei fled to the State of Wu. The King of Wu appointed him as a doctor.
In the third year, King Helu of Wu, Wu Zixu, and Bo Pei led an army to conquer Chu, captured Shuyi, and killed Gaiyu and Zhuyong, the young masters of Wu who had fled.
Helu planned to attack Ying, the capital of Chu State. General Sun Wu said: The army and the people are very tired from fighting. We cannot attack the capital of Ying now. We must wait for the time to mature.
In the fourth year, Wu attacked Chu again and captured Liuyi and Yayi.
In five years, the state of Wu attacked the state of Yue and defeated the Yue army.
In the sixth year, the state of Chu sent his son Chang Nangwa to conquer the state of Wu. Wu Jun sent troops to fight and defeated the Chu army in Yuzhang. He captured Juchao of Chu state and returned to Wu with his troops.
In the ninth year, King Wu Helu asked Wu Zixu and Sun Wu: At first you said you could not attack Yingdu, what is the situation now?
The two men replied: The general of Chu State is often greedy, and both Tang and Cai States hate him.
If your Majesty is determined to attack Chu on a large scale, you must unite Tang and Cai to succeed.
Helu obeyed them, dispatched all the troops, and marched westward with Cai State of Tang Dynasty to attack Chu, and came to the edge of Han River.
Chu State also sent troops to resist, and the two sides formed formations across the water.
King Wu's younger brother Fugai wanted to fight, but Helu wouldn't allow it.
Fugai said: Your Majesty has entrusted me with the army. The best way to fight is to seize the favorable opportunity. What are you waiting for!
So he led his five thousand men to attack the Chu army. The Chu army was defeated and fled.
King Wu sent troops to pursue him.
When they arrived at Yingdu, they fought five times in total, and the Chu soldiers were defeated five times.
King Zhao of Chu escaped from Yingdu and ran to Yun County.
Duke Yun's brother wanted to kill King Zhao, but King Zhao fled to Sui with Duke Yun.
Wu soldiers entered the capital of Ying.
Wu Zixu and Bo Pei dug up the body of King Chu Ping from the tomb and whipped it to avenge their father's murder.
In the spring of ten years, the king of Yue heard that the king of Wu was stationed in Yingdu and that the country was empty, so he raised his troops to attack Wu.
summary: Under King Helu, Wu Zixu and Bo Pei were appointed to official positions. Helu, with the help of Wu Zixu, Sun Wu, and the states of Tang and Cai, launched a major attack on Chu, defeating the Chu army five times and capturing the capital, Ying. Wu Zixu and Bo Pei dug up the body of King Ping of Chu to avenge their fathers. Later, Helu's brother Fugai attempted to usurp the throne but was defeated and fled to Chu. In the nineteenth year, King Helu attacked Yue but was wounded and died. Before his death, he told his son Fuchai to remember that Gou Jian of Yue killed his father.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/吴太伯世家

translation:
Instead of taking this opportunity to completely eliminate the Yue forces now, we must forgive them. This is setting up trouble for the future!
Moreover, Gou Jian was a man who was tenacious and endured hardships. If he is not eliminated now, he will regret it in the future.
The King of Wu did not listen to Zixu's plan, but listened to Dazai Pei's words, and finally ceased war with the State of Yue. After the two countries signed a peace treaty, the State of Wu withdrew its troops and returned home.
The year before last, King Fu Chai of Wu heard that ministers were vying for power after the death of Qi Jinggong, and that the new king was young and powerless, so he launched an army to attack Qi State in the north.
Wu Zixu advised him: King Gou Jian of Yue did not eat more than two kinds of dishes, and did not wear more than two colors. He mourned the dead and comforted the sick. This was because he wanted to use the people to take revenge on Wu.
If Gou Jian does not die, he will definitely be a great trouble to the state of Wu.
Now the country of Yue is a serious problem for our country, but you don't pay attention to it and instead use your strength to the country of Qi. Isn't it a big mistake?
The King of Wu refused to listen and went north to attack Qi and defeated the Qi army in Ailing.
When the troops arrived at Zhuanyi, they summoned Duke Ai of Lu and asked for a hundred prisons.
Ji Kangzi sent Zigong to list the Zhou rites to persuade Dazai Pei, and King Wu stopped.
So King Wu stayed to seize the southern territories of Qi and Lu.
In the ninth year, he crusaded against Lu for Zuo and arrived in Lu. He made an alliance with Lu and left.
The year before last, he took advantage of the situation to attack Qi and return.
The year before last, there was another northern expedition to Qi.
King Gou Jian of Yue led his ministers to pay homage to the King of Wu and presented him with generous tributes. The King of Wu was overjoyed.
Only Wu Zixu was afraid and said: The Kingdom of Wu is going to be abandoned.
So he admonished the King of Wu and said: The Yue Kingdom is close to its heart. Although our country can defeat Qi now, it is like a field of stones, which is of no use.
Moreover, "Pangeng's Edict" said that the Shang Dynasty can only prosper if the chaotic and arrogant people are eliminated.
The King of Wu refused to listen and sent Wu Zixu as an envoy to Qi. Zixu entrusted his son to the Bao family of Qi to repay the King of Wu.
When the king of Wu heard about it, he was furious and gave Zixu a sword to commit suicide.
When Zixu was about to die, he said: If you plant catalpa trees on my grave and let them grow enough to make utensils, the Kingdom of Wu will be destroyed.
Plug out my eyes and place them on the east gate of the capital of Wu, so that I can see how the Yue Kingdom destroyed the Wu Kingdom.
Later, the official of Qi State, Bao Shi, killed Qi Daugong.
When King Wu found out, he cried bitterly outside the military gate for three days and then led his army to attack Qi from the sea.
The Qi army defeated the Wu army, and the king of Wu had no choice but to lead the defeated troops back home.
The year before last, King Wu convened the kings of Lu and Wei for an alliance meeting in Lugao.
In the spring of the year before last, King Wu went north to meet with the princes in Huangchi, hoping to dominate the Central Plains and protect the Zhou Dynasty.
In the sixth month of the sixth month, King Gou Jian of Yue attacked Wu.
On Yiyou day, five thousand Yue soldiers fought against Wu soldiers.
Bingxu, captured the prince friend of Wu.
In Dinghai, the Vietnamese army entered the state of Wu.
The Wu people reported the news of their failure to Fu Chai. The King of Wu was afraid that someone would leak the news and let the alliance princes hear the news, so he furiously killed seven people in front of the tent.
In the seventh month of Xinchou, the King of Wu and Duke Ding of Jin competed for the position of leader of the alliance.
King Wu said: My ancestor is the largest among the Zhou clan.
summary: King Fuchai avenged his father by defeating Yue at Fujiao. King Gou Jian of Yue was forced to hide in Kuaiji Mountain and sought peace through the Grand Prime Minister Bo Pei. Wu Zixu advised against this, comparing Gou Jian to Shaokang, who restored the Xia dynasty from a small territory. He warned that Gou Jian was a threat, but the King of Wu listened to Bo Pei and made peace with Yue. Fuchai then focused on northern campaigns against Qi, ignoring Zixu's warnings about the greater threat from Yue. Zixu was eventually forced to commit suicide, asking for his eyes to be placed on the east gate of Wu's capital to see Yue's invasion. While Fuchai was at the Huangchi meeting vying for supremacy with Jin, Yue attacked Wu, capturing the crown prince. After the meeting, Fuchai sought peace with Yue. Eventually, Yue grew stronger, defeated Wu in battle, and besieged its capital. King Fuchai, regretting not listening to Zixu, committed suicide. The King of Yue destroyed Wu and killed Dazai Bo Pei for his disloyalty.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/吴太伯世家

translation:
Since ancient times, the founding emperors who were appointed by heaven and the monarchs who inherited the orthodox and abided by the laws of the late emperors were not only intrinsically noble in character, but also mostly had the help of their relatives.
The rise of the Xia Dynasty was due to the daughter of the Tushan family, and Xia Jie's exile was also related to Moxi.
The rise of the Yin Dynasty also relied on the Nu family, and the murder of King Zhou of Shang was also related to his favoring Daji.
The rise of the Zhou Dynasty also relied on Jiang Yuan and Tai Ren, and the capture of King You was also related to his fornication with Bao Si.
Therefore, the "Book of Changes" is based on the two hexagrams "Qian" and "Kun", the "Book of Songs" begins with "Guan Ju", the "Shang Shu" praises Yao for marrying his daughter to Shun, and the "Spring and Autumn" ridicules those who marry their wives without going to meet them in person.
The relationship between husband and wife is the most important ethical relationship in human nature.
In the application of etiquette, only marriage is the most cautious.
When music harmonizes the four seasons, it becomes harmonious. The changes of yin and yang are the rulers of the growth and change of all things. How can we not be cautious?
People can promote human relations, but they can do nothing about destiny.
Indeed, a king cannot get the love of his spouse from his ministers, nor can a father get it from his son, let alone those of low status!
After couples get together, some are unable to produce children and grandchildren; after they are able to produce children, some cannot find a good home.
Isn't this destiny?
Confucius rarely talked about the destiny of heaven, probably because it was difficult to explain clearly.
If we cannot understand the changes of yin and yang, how can we understand the principles of human nature and destiny?
Tai Shigong said: The situation before Qin was too ancient, and the details could not be recorded.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, Lu Ehuang became the empress of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, and her son was the prince.
In her later years, her appearance deteriorated and she fell out of favor. As Mrs. Qi gained favor, her son Ruyi almost replaced the prince several times.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Empress Lu executed the Qi family and killed King Zhao Ruyi. However, the concubines in Emperor Gaozu's harem could only be safe if they were not favored and alienated.
Empress Lu's eldest daughter was the wife of Zhang Ao, the Marquis of Xuanping, and Zhang Ao's daughter was the queen of Emperor Hui.
Because of their close relationship, Empress Dowager Lu tried every means to try to get her to have a child, but she never had a child. She had to bring someone else's son from the harem and falsely claimed it was her son.
After the death of Emperor Xiaohui, the world had just stabilized and the person who would succeed the throne was not yet clear.
So he raised the status of his relatives, made the Lu brothers kings as assistants, and made Lu Lu's daughter the queen of the young emperor, hoping to make the foundation stronger, but it was of no use.
Empress Lu died and was buried in Changling with Gaozu.
Lu Lu, Lu Chan and others were afraid of being killed, so they plotted to cause trouble.
The ministers conquered them, and heaven guided the Han family's imperial line, and finally eliminated the Lu family.
Only Queen Xiaohui was placed in the North Palace.
The minister ushered the king into the throne, who was Emperor Xiaowen, and he enshrined the ancestral temple of the Han family.
Isn't this destiny?
If it were not destiny, who could take on this important task?
summary: The crucial role of marriage and imperial consorts in the rise and fall of dynasties. Founding emperors and orthodox monarchs often relied on their relatives for support. The Xia Dynasty rose through the Tushan family's daughter and fell with Moxi; the Yin Dynasty rose through the Nu family and fell due to Daji; the Zhou Dynasty rose through Jiang Yuan and Tai Ren, while King You's downfall involved Bao Si. The text emphasizes that husband-wife relationships are the most important ethical bond, and marriage is the most cautious ritual application. The narrative then details several Han Dynasty empresses and their families. Empress Lu, wife of Emperor Gaozu, lost favor in her later years as Lady Qi gained prominence. After Gaozu's death, Empress Lu executed the Qi family and killed Prince Ruyi. She tried to secure succession through her daughter's child but failed, eventually elevating her Lu relatives. After her death, the Lu clan plotted rebellion but were eliminated by ministers, who installed Emperor Xiaowen. The text concludes with Emperor Wu's later consorts and his controversial execution of Lady Gou Yi, mother of his youngest son. He explained that young monarchs with living mothers caused chaos, citing Empress Lu as an example. All mothers of Emperor Wu's children were executed to prevent such problems.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家

translation:
Empress Dowager Bo, whose father was a Wu man and whose surname was Bo, had an affair with Wei Wei, a woman from the original Wei king's clan during the Qin Dynasty, and gave birth to Bo Ji. Bo Ji's father died in Shanin and was buried there.
When the princes rebelled against the Qin Dynasty, Wei Bao proclaimed himself King of Wei, and Wei sent her daughter to the palace of the King of Wei.
Wei Lao went to Xu Fu's place to see her fortune teller and asked him to see Bo Ji. Xu Fu said that she would definitely be able to give birth to the emperor.
At that time, Xiang Yu and Liu Bang, the king of Han, were fighting over the world in Xingyang, and it was not yet certain who would own the world.
Wei Bao initially joined the King of Han in attacking the King of Chu, but when he heard Xu Negi's words, he felt happy alone, so he betrayed the King of Han, first remaining neutral, and then allied with the King of Chu.
The king of Han sent Cao Shen and others to attack and imprison King Bao of Wei, changed the Gui land he occupied into a county, and sent Bo Ji to Zhizao mansion where criminals were housed.
After the death of King Bao of Wei, the King of Han once entered the Zhizao Mansion and saw Bo Ji's beautiful appearance. He issued an edict to take her into the harem, but she was not favored for more than a year.
When Bo Ji was young, she was very close to Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier. The three of them made a vow: Whoever gets rich first will not forget the others.
Later, Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier were both favored by the King of Han.
One time when the King of Han was sitting on the Chenggao Platform in the Henan Palace, the two beauties laughed at each other as they talked about their vows with Bo Ji.
When the King of Han heard about it, he asked them why, and they both told the King of Han the truth.
The king of Han felt a little sad and felt sorry for Bo Ji, so he summoned her and stayed with her that day.
Bo Ji said: Last night I dreamed of a blue dragon occupying my belly.
Emperor Gaozu said: This is a sign of a noble person. Let me fulfill it for you.
Fortunately, a boy was born, and he became the king.
After that, Bo Ji rarely saw Gaozu.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Empress Dowager Lu was very resentful of the concubines such as Mrs. Qi and others who were favored to serve as Emperor Gaozu's bedtime, so she imprisoned them all and were not allowed to leave the palace.
Because Bo Ji rarely saw Gaozu, she was able to leave the palace and follow her son to the Kingdom of Dai, becoming the Queen Mother of Dai.
The Queen Mother's younger brother Bo Zhao also followed him to Dai.
During the seventeenth year of King Dai's reign, Empress Lu passed away.
The ministers discussed the establishment of a new king. They all hated the powerful power of their relative, the Lu family, and praised Bo's benevolence and kindness. Therefore, they welcomed back the king and established him as Emperor Xiaowen. Empress Dowager Bo changed her title to Empress Dowager, and her younger brother Bo Zhao was named Marquis of Zhi.
Empress Dowager Bo's mother had died before that and was buried in the north of Yueyang.
At this time, Empress Dowager Bo's father was honored as Lingwen Marquis, and a garden of 300 households was set up in Kuaiji County. People below Changcheng were sent to serve and guard the tomb. The sacrifices and ceremonies in the ancestral temple were carried out in accordance with the prescribed etiquette.
There is also a cemetery for Mrs. Lingwenhou in the north of Yueyang. All the etiquette is the same as that at the Lingwenhou Cemetery.
Empress Dowager Bo believed that her mother's family was the descendant of King Wei. Her parents died young, and there were people in the Wei family who served Empress Dowager Bo diligently, so she ordered that the status of the Wei family be restored, and rewards were received according to the degree of closeness.
Only one person in the Bo family was granted the title of Marquis.
Empress Dowager Bo died two years later than Emperor Wen, in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign, and was buried in Nanling.
Since Empress Lu was buried with Emperor Gaozu in Changling, she specially built a separate mausoleum for herself, close to Emperor Xiaowen's Ba Mausoleum.
Empress Dowager Dou was a native of Guanjin County, Qinghe County, Zhao State.
summary: Empress Dowager Bo's story follows. Her mother had an affair with a Wei clan member during Qin times, producing Bo Ji. A fortune-teller predicted she would bear an emperor. Wei Bao, hearing this, betrayed the King of Han but was defeated. Bo Ji entered the harem but remained unfavored for over a year. Through friends' intervention, she gained the king's favor, dreamed of a blue dragon in her belly, and bore a son. After Gaozu's death, because she was rarely favored, she escaped Empress Lu's persecution and followed her son to the Kingdom of Dai, becoming Queen Mother of Dai. After Empress Lu's death, ministers chose her son as Emperor Xiaowen.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/外戚世家

translation:
During the reign of Queen Mother Lu, Concubine Dou was selected from a good family to serve the Queen Mother in the palace.
Later, the Queen Mother sent the maids out of the palace and gave them to the princes and kings, five for each king. Dou Ji was among these maids.
Dou Ji's family was in Qinghe. Thinking that Zhao State was close to her home, she asked the eunuch in charge of the deportation: "My name must be put on the list of people going to Zhao State."
The eunuch forgot about this and mistakenly put her on the list of people going to Dai.
The roster was read, the edict said it was okay, and it was time to set off.
Dou Ji burst into tears and complained that the eunuch didn't want to go, so he forced her to leave before she was willing to leave.
When he arrived in the Kingdom of Dai, the King of Dai only favored Concubine Dou, and gave birth to a daughter called Prostitute, and later gave birth to two boys.
The queen gave birth to four boys.
The queen died before the king entered the court and became the emperor. When the king became the emperor, the four boys born to the queen also died of illness one after another.
A few months after Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, the ministers requested the establishment of a prince. Dou Ji's eldest son was the oldest and was established as the prince.
Dou Ji was also made the queen, and her daughter Liu Piao was the eldest princess.
The next year, he established his youngest son Liu Wu as the acting king, and soon moved to Liang State. This was King Xiao of Liang.
Queen Dou's parents had died long ago and were buried in Guanjin.
At this time, Empress Dowager Bo issued an edict to relevant officials to honor Empress Dou's father as Marquis Ancheng and his mother as Mrs. Ancheng.
He ordered a garden town of 200 households to be set up in Qinghe, which was served and guarded by the local chief minister. Everything was done in accordance with the practices of Lingwen Garden.
Queen Dou's elder brother is Dou Changjun, and his younger brother is Dou Guangguo, also known as Shaojun.
When Shaojun was four or five years old, his family was poor and he was robbed and sold. His family did not know where he was sold.
He resold a dozen more houses and sold them to Yiyang. He went into the mountain to burn charcoal for his master. At night, more than a hundred people were sleeping under the cliff. The cliff collapsed and crushed all the people sleeping below to death. Only Shaojun escaped and was not crushed to death.
He made his own calculations and concluded that he would be made a marquis within a few days, so he went to Chang'an from his master's house.
I heard that Queen Dou was newly ennobled. Her hometown is Guanjin and her surname is Dou.
Although Guangguo was young when he left home, he still knew the name of the county and his family's surname. He also picked mulberries with his sister and fell from a tree. He used these things as evidence and wrote a letter to state his experience.
Queen Dou told Emperor Wen about this, and Guang Guo was summoned and asked him. He explained the situation in detail, and it was indeed good.
Asked what else he could use to prove it, he replied: When my sister left me to go west, she said goodbye to me in the post dormitory. My sister asked for rice soup to wash my hair and food for me to eat, and then she left.
So Queen Dou held her brother and cried bitterly, with tears streaming down her cheeks.
The attendants on the left and right also fell on the ground and cried, helping the queen to mourn together.
So he was rewarded with a lot of land, houses and money, and the Dou brothers, who had the same ancestor as the queen, were enfeoffed and allowed to move to Chang'an.
Jianghou Zhou Bo, General Guan Ying and others said: We people are not going to die, but our lives hang in the hands of the Dou brothers.
These two people were of humble origins, so they had to choose masters and guests, otherwise they would follow Lu's example and conspire to rebel again.
So he chose an older, virtuous and upright scholar to be with them.
From then on, Dou Changjun and Shaojun became humble and courteous gentlemen, and did not dare to rely on their dignity to be arrogant and arrogant towards others.
Queen Dou fell ill and became blind.
summary: Empress Dowager Dou was selected for palace service during Empress Lu's reign. When palace maids were distributed to princes, she wanted to go to Zhao but was mistakenly sent to Dai. There, the King of Dai favored her, and she bore two sons. After the queen and her sons died, Dou Ji's eldest son became crown prince, and she became empress. Her brother Dou Guangguo, sold as a child, later identified himself through shared memories and was reunited with her. The Dou family received honors, and Empress Dowager Dou promoted Huang-Lao teachings.
