translation:
Emperor Wen favored Mrs. Shen and Yin Ji of Handan, but neither of them gave birth to children.
After Emperor Xiaowen died, Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne and granted Guangguo the title of Marquis Zhangwu.
Chang Jun died first, so he named his son Peng Zu the Marquis of Nanpi.
When Wu, Chu and other seven kingdoms rebelled, Dou Ying, the son of Queen Mother Dou's party brothers, liked to act chivalrously and led the army to put down the rebellion. He was named Wei Qihou for his military exploits.
A total of three members of the Dou family were granted the title of marquis.
Empress Dowager Dou loved the teachings of Huang Emperor and Lao Tzu. The emperor, the prince and all the children of the Dou family had to read "Huang Emperor" and "Lao Tzu" and respect Huang Lao's scholarship.
Empress Dowager Dou died six years later than Emperor Jing, and she was buried with Emperor Wen in Ba Ling.
He left an edict and gave all the money and property in the East Palace to the eldest princess Liu Piao.
The Queen Mother is from Huaili, and her mother's name is Zang'er.
Zang'er is the granddaughter of Zang Tu, the original king of Yan.
Zang'er first married Wang Zhong of Huaili and gave birth to a son named Xin and two daughters.
Later, Wang Zhong died, and Zang'er remarried to the Tian family in Changling and gave birth to sons Tian Fu and Tian Sheng.
Zang'er's eldest daughter married Jin Wangsun and gave birth to a daughter. Zang'er considered her children a title, and it turned out that her two daughters were both noble people.
So she wanted to rely on her two daughters, so she forcibly took her daughter back from the Jin family's home.
Jin was very angry and refused to break up with his wife, so Zang'er sent his daughter to the prince's womb.
The prince loved her very much and gave birth to three daughters and one son.
When the boy was still pregnant, Beauty Wang dreamed that the sun fell into her arms.
She told the prince about this dream, and the prince said: This is a sign of great wealth.
Emperor Xiaowen died before he was born. After Emperor Xiaojing came to the throne, Mrs. Wang gave birth to the boy.
Previously, Zang'er sent her youngest daughter Erjiao to the palace, and Erjiao gave birth to four boys.
When Emperor Jing was crown prince, Empress Dowager Bo chose a woman from the Bo family to be his concubine.
When Emperor Jing came to the throne, this concubine was made Queen Bo.
The queen had no children and was not favored.
As soon as Queen Mother Bo died, Queen Bo was deposed.
Liu Rong, the eldest son of Emperor Jing, and his mother was Li Ji.
Li Ji is from Qi.
Liu Rong was established as the prince.
The eldest princess Liu Piao has a daughter who plans to be the prince's concubine.
Li Ji was jealous, and it was only through the eldest princess that the beauties of Emperor Jing met Emperor Jing. They received more honor and favor than Li Ji. Li Ji was resentful every day, so she declined the eldest princess's request and refused to marry.
The eldest princess wanted to betroth her daughter to Mrs. Wang's son, and Mrs. Wang agreed.
The eldest princess was angry about this incident, so she often spoke ill of Li Ji in front of Emperor Jing: When Li Ji gathered with ladies and concubines, her attendants would often spit and curse behind them, and use evil and deceptive techniques.
Emperor Jing was angry with Li Ji because of this.
Emperor Jing was once in poor health and unhappy, so he entrusted his sons who were crowned kings to Li Ji and said to her: After I die, you must take good care of them.
Li Ji was angry, refused to agree, and spoke rudely.
summary: The text also covers Empress Wang, whose mother Zang'er forcibly took her daughter from her husband Jin Wangsun and sent her to the prince's womb. She dreamed of the sun falling into her arms and bore a son who became Emperor Wu. Lady Li Ji, mother of the eldest son, refused the eldest princess's marriage proposal for her daughter, leading to conflict. Through manipulation, Mrs. Wang's son became crown prince instead.

translation:
The emperor loved her and favored her again, so she became pregnant and became more respected and favored day by day.
Emperor Wu summoned her elder brother Wei Changjun and younger brother Wei Qing to serve as ministers.
Later, Zifu became very favored by Emperor Wu and gave birth to three daughters and one son. The son's name was Zhu.
When Emperor Wu was still the crown prince, he married the eldest princess's daughter as his concubine. When he ascended the throne as emperor, the concubine was made empress, with the surname Chen, and she had no children.
The emperor can inherit the throne, and the eldest princess has contributed a lot, so Queen Chen is arrogant and arrogant.
Hearing that Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu, he was very angry and sought death many times.
The emperor also became even more angry.
Empress Chen used women's witchcraft to deceive people. Emperor Wu was quite aware of this, so he deposed Empress Chen and made Wei Zifu the empress.
Empress Chen's mother, Princess Dachang, was the sister of Emperor Jing. She repeatedly reproached Emperor Wu's sister, Princess Pingyang, saying: The emperor could not ascend the throne without me. After he ascended the throne, he actually abandoned my daughter. Why don't you feel lucky and forget your duty?
Princess Pingyang said: It was because he had no sons that he was abandoned.
Empress Chen was eager to have a child and spent as much as 90 million on medical expenses, but she was unable to have a child.
When Wei Zifu was made queen, Wei Changjun was already dead, so Emperor Wu appointed Wei Qing as general. Wei Qing made Wei Qing the Marquis of Changping because of his military exploits against the Hu people.
His three sons were still in their infancy, and they were all named princes.
Empress Wei had an older sister, Wei Shaoer, and her son Huo Qubing was named a champion marquis because of his military exploits, and was known as the Cavalry General.
Wei Qing is known as the general.
Empress Wei's son Liu Zheng was made the crown prince.
The Wei family's relatives started their careers with military exploits, and five of them were granted the title of marquis.
When Queen Wei's beauty grew old, Mrs. Wang of Zhao was favored, had a son, and was named King of Qi.
Mrs. Wang died young.
Mrs. Li of Zhongshan was favored and gave birth to a son, who was named King of Changyi.
Mrs. Li died young, and her brother Li Yannian was favored because of his proficiency in music and was named a co-regulator.
The so-called Xielu refers to the former singing and dancing artists.
Their brothers were all exterminated for committing adultery in the harem.
At that time, her eldest brother Li Guangli was the general of the Second Division and was conquering Dayuan. He was not killed. When he returned to Chang'an, the emperor had already killed the Li family. Later, he showed mercy to his family and named him Marquis of Haixi.
The other imperial concubines also have two sons, King Yan and King Guangling.
Their mother was unloved and died of sorrow.
After Mrs. Li's death, Yin Jie and others were alternately favored. However, they all met Emperor Wu as singing girls. They were not women from princely families with fiefdoms and should not be matched with the emperor.
Mr. Chu said: When I was appointed Langguan, I asked Zhong Lisheng, who was familiar with the old affairs of the Han family.
According to him, the Queen Mother gave birth to a daughter when she was among the people, and her father was the grandson of King Jin.
Wang Sun was dead. After Emperor Jing's death, Emperor Wu came to the throne. Only the Queen Mother was still there.
Han Wang's grandson named Yan was usually favored by Emperor Wu. He took the opportunity to talk about the Queen Mother having a daughter in Changling.
Emperor Wu said: Why didn't you tell me earlier?
summary: Wei Zifu, a singer from Princess Pingyang's household, caught Emperor Wu's attention. After initial neglect, she became pregnant and gained favor, eventually becoming empress after Empress Chen was deposed for witchcraft. Her brother Wei Qing became a general, and her family produced five marquises.

translation:
Confucius was born in Zouyi, Changping Township, Lu State.
His ancestor was from the Song Dynasty, named Uncle Kong Fang.
Uncle Fang gave birth to Bo Xia, and Bo Xia gave birth to Shu Liang He.
Shu Lianghe and Yehe, a woman named Yan, gave birth to Confucius. They got Confucius after they went to Niqiu Mountain to pray to the gods.
Confucius was born in the 22nd year of Duke Xiang of Lu.
The top of his head was concave when he was born, so he was named Qiu. The courtesy name is Zhongni and the surname is Kong.
Shortly after Confucius was born, his uncle Liang He died and was buried in Fangshan.
Fangshan was in the east of Lu State, so Confucius could not know for sure where his father's tomb was. His mother did not tell him where his father was buried.
When Confucius was a child, he played games, often setting up various sacrificial vessels and learning the ritual movements of sacrificial offerings.
After Confucius's mother died, she temporarily placed her coffin in the Five Fathers' Road without burying her. This was out of prudent consideration.
The mother of Wan's father, who was from Zouyi, told him the burial place of Confucius's father, and then Confucius moved his mother to Fangshan to be buried with his father.
When Confucius was mourning with a filial piety belt tied around his waist, Ji Sun held a banquet to entertain celebrities, and Confucius went to attend.
Ji Sun's retainer Yang Hu stopped him and said: "Ji's family is entertaining celebrities, but you are not invited."
Confucius withdrew because of this.
When Confucius was seventeen years old, Lizi, a senior official in the state of Lu, was critically ill. Before his death, he warned his son Yizi: Confucius is a descendant of a saint, and his ancestors perished in the Song Dynasty.
His ancestor Fufu He was supposed to succeed as the king of Song Dynasty, but he gave way to his younger brother Li Gong.
When another of his ancestors, Zheng Kao's father, assisted Song Dai Gong, Song Wu Gong, and Song Xuangong in three dynasties, he was more respectful every time he was given orders. Therefore, the inscription on Zheng Kao's father's tripod says: The first appointment was received with a bow, the second appointment was received with a bow, and the third appointment was bowed and received.
When I walked, I avoided the middle of the road and walked against the wall, and no one dared to bully me. I just made batter and porridge in this cauldron to survive.
His frugality has reached this point.
I heard that although the descendants of saints may not necessarily become kings and govern, there will definitely be people with outstanding talents and virtues.
Now Confucius is young and courteous. Isn't he a man of outstanding talents and virtue?
If I die, you must take him as your teacher.
After Meng Lizi died, Meng Yizi and Nangong Jingshu, a native of Lu, went to Confucius to learn etiquette.
This year, Ji Wuzi died, and Pingzi succeeded to the throne.
Confucius' family was poor and of low status.
When he came of age, he worked as a clerk in charge of the Ji family's warehouse, and he was a cashier who could calculate money and grain fairly and accurately. He also worked as a clerk in charge of pastures, and he was able to breed livestock well.
Therefore, he was promoted to Sikong in charge of construction projects.
summary: Confucius was born in Zouyi, Changping Township, Lu State, to Shu Lianghe and a woman named Yan after they prayed at Niqiu Mountain. His head was concave at birth, so he was named Qiu, with the courtesy name Zhongni and surname Kong. His father died shortly after his birth and was buried in Fangshan, but his mother did not reveal the location. As a child, Confucius played at setting up sacrificial vessels and learning ritual movements. After his mother died, he temporarily placed her coffin at the Five Fathers' Road until a neighbor told him his father's burial place, allowing him to bury them together. At seventeen, Meng Lizi, a senior official, warned his son Yizi that Confucius, a descendant of saints, should be taken as a teacher. After Lizi's death, Yizi and Nangong Jingshu learned etiquette from Confucius.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家

translation:
Not long after, he left the state of Lu, was ostracized in the state of Qi, was expelled in the states of Song and Wei, was besieged between the states of Chen and Cai, and finally returned to the state of Lu.
Confucius was nine feet six inches tall. People called him "The Long Man" because they thought he was different from ordinary people.
The State of Lu was still very kind to him, so he returned to the State of Lu.
Nangong Jingshu, a native of Lu, said to Duke Zhao of Lu: Please allow me to go on a mission to Zhou with Confucius.
Duke Zhao of Lu gave him a carriage, two horses, and a boy servant, and set off with him to the Kingdom of Zhou to learn etiquette and pay a visit to Lao Tzu.
When they were saying goodbye, Lao Tzu came out to see them off and said: I heard that wealthy people give gifts with property, and people with noble moral character give gifts with words.
I am not a wealthy person, so I can only steal the name of a noble person and send you off with words. These sentences are: A wise and thoughtful person is often threatened with death because he likes to talk about others; a knowledgeable, eloquent and insightful person is often in trouble and endangers himself, because he likes to expose the sins of others.
Children should not have selfish motives, and ministers should not think only of themselves but the monarch. After Confucius returned to the state of Lu from Zhou Dynasty, more and more disciples followed him.
At this time, Jin Pinggong was promiscuous and immoral, and the six ministers of the Han, Zhao, Wei, Zhonghang, Fan, and Zhi families controlled the state affairs and constantly sent troops to attack the feudal states in the east. King Ling of Chu had a strong army and often invaded other countries in the Central Plains; Qi was a big country and close to Lu.
The state of Lu was small and weak. If it surrendered to the state of Chu, it would anger the state of Jin. If it surrendered to the state of Jin, it would cause the state of Chu to attack. If it did not serve Qi well, Qi's army would invade the state of Lu.
Lu Zhaogong was twenty years old and Confucius was thirty years old.
Duke Jinggong of Qi and Yan Ying came to the state of Lu. Duke Jinggong asked Confucius: "In the past, Duke Qin's country was small and remote. Why was he able to dominate?"
Confucius replied: Although the Qin State is small, its ambitions are great; although its location is remote, its governance is very appropriate.
Duke Mu of Qin personally pulled Baili Xi, who had been redeemed with five black ram skins, and awarded him the title of a great official. As soon as he was released from detention, Qin Jun discussed with him for three days, and then let him take charge of the state affairs.
Using this spirit to govern the country can even rule the entire world. Being an overlord is not a big deal.
Jinggong was very happy after hearing this.
When Confucius was thirty-five years old, Ji Pingzi offended Lu Zhaogong for having a cockfight with Li Zhaobo. Zhaogong led his army to attack Pingzi. Pingzi, the Mengsun family and the Shusun family allied with him to attack Zhaogong. Zhaogong's army was defeated and fled to Qi State. Qi State placed Zhaogong in Qianhou.
Not long after that, an incident occurred in the state of Lu.
Confucius came to Qi State and became Gao Zhaozi's retainer, hoping to use Gao Zhaozi's relationship to get close to Jinggong.
summary: Confucius' family was poor and of low status. He worked as a clerk managing the Ji family's warehouse and pastures, where he was fair and efficient, leading to his promotion to Sikong. He later left Lu, was ostracized in Qi, expelled in Song and Wei, besieged between Chen and Cai, and finally returned to Lu. At nine feet six inches tall, he was called "The Long Man." Nangong Jingshu requested Duke Zhao of Lu to allow Confucius to travel to Zhou to learn etiquette from Lao Tzu, who advised him to avoid speaking of others' faults and to act without selfish motives. After returning, Confucius gained many disciples. At thirty, Confucius advised Duke Jing of Qi that Qin's success came from its ambitious governance and use of talents like Baili Xi. At thirty-five, after political turmoil in Lu, Confucius went to Qi, where he studied music and advised Duke Jing on governance, emphasizing proper roles and frugality. However, Yan Ying dissuaded the duke from employing Confucius, criticizing Confucian rituals as impractical. Confucius left Qi and returned to Lu.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家

translation:
The envoy from Wu State asked again: "Who is the god?"
Confucius said: The gods of mountains and rivers can stir up the clouds and cause rain, which is enough to benefit the world. The gods are responsible for supervising the mountains and rivers and offering sacrifices on time. Those who guard the land and grain are princes, and they are all subordinate to the king.
Wu envoy asked again: What is the Fangfeng family responsible for offering sacrifices to?
Confucius said: The county chief of the Wanggong family, who supervises the sacrifices in Fengshan and Yushan areas, has the surname Li.
In Yu, Xia, and Shang Dynasties, he was called Wang Yi, in Zhou Dynasty, he was called Chang Zhai, and now he is called adults.
Wu Shi asked: How tall can a person be?
Confucius replied: The Ruohui family is three feet tall and is the shortest among them; the one who is only three feet tall is the tallest among them.
After hearing this, the envoy from the State of Wu said: What a great saint!
Ji Huanzi had a favorite named Zhongliang Huai, who had a grudge against Yang Hu.
Yang Hu wanted to expel Zhong Liang Huai, but Ji's retainer Gong Shan Buxu stopped him.
In the autumn of this year, Zhongliang Huai became even more arrogant, and Yang Hu captured Zhong Liang Huai.
Ji Huanzi was very angry about this, so Yang Hu imprisoned Ji Huanzi. He was not released until Ji Huan admitted defeat and made a covenant.
From then on, Yang Hu looked down upon Ji's family even more.
Ji's family also acted above Lu Jun, and the state of Lu had a situation where ministers had exclusive power. Therefore, the people of Lu did not observe etiquette from the officials down, and exceeded their authority and violated the right path.
Therefore, Confucius no longer wanted to be an official in the state of Lu. He retired at home and concentrated on studying and sorting out the classics such as "Poems", "Books", "Rites" and "Music". More and more students, some even coming from far away, all humbly asked Confucius for advice.
In the eighth year of Lu Dinggong's reign, Gongshan Buxuan failed under Ji Huanzi, so he took advantage of Yanghu's rebellion and planned to abolish the legitimate heirs of Jisun, Mengsun, and Shusun families, and establish a bastard son who Yanghu had always loved, so he arrested Ji Huanzi.
Huanzi designed to deceive him and was able to escape.
In the ninth year of Duke Dinggong of Lu, Yang Hu failed in his rebellion and fled to Qi.
At this time, Confucius was fifty years old.
Gongshan Buxuan used Philadelphia to rebel against the Ji family, and he sent people to summon Confucius to help.
Confucius has been exploring the way to govern the country for a long time, but he was depressed and had nowhere to apply it. No one could use him, so he said: In the beginning, King Wen and King Wu of Zhou arose from Feng and Hao and established the royal industry. Although Philadelphia is small now, it should be about the same!
Confucius wanted to go, but Zilu was unhappy and stopped Confucius.
Confucius said: If they invite me to go, will my trip be in vain?
If I am reused, I will establish a dynasty like Zhou Dynasty in the East! However, it didn't happen in the end. Later, Duke Dinggong of Lu appointed Confucius as the governor of the central capital. A year later, all places followed his example.
Confucius was promoted from the chief of Zhongdu to Sikong, and from Sikong to the great Sikou.
In the spring of the tenth year of Lu Dinggong, Lu and Qi reconciled.
In the summer, Li Kuan, an official of the Qi State, said to Jinggong: The Lu State has appointed Confucius, and this situation will endanger the Qi State.
So Qi Jinggong sent an envoy to tell the state of Lu that he would have a friendly meeting with Lu Dinggong, and the agreed meeting place was Jiagu.
summary: At fifty, Confucius was appointed governor of Zhongdu, then promoted to Sikong and later to Grand Sikou. In the tenth year of Duke Ding of Lu, he organized a meeting at Jiagu between Lu and Qi, where he confronted Qi's disruptive performances and had performers executed. Qi returned invaded lands to Lu. In the thirteenth year, Confucius ordered the demolition of the city walls of Ji, Meng, and Shu families to curb their power, but the Meng family resisted, and the city of Cheng could not be captured.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家

translation:
The Jisun family was also preparing to demolish the city wall of Feiyi. Gongshan Buxuan and Shusunsu led Feiyi's people to attack Lu.
Lu Dinggong, Ji Sun, Meng Sun, and Shu Sun hid in Ji Sun's house and climbed to the high altar of Ji Sun Wuzi.
The Feiyi people led by Gongshan Buxuan attacked them and failed to penetrate, but some people had already broken into the near side of Lu Dinggong's high altar.
Confucius ordered Shen Gouxu and Leqi to step down and attack them. The Feiyi people failed and fled. The Lu people took advantage of the victory to pursue them and completely defeated them in Gumi.
Gongshan Buxuan and Shusun Zhui fled to Qi State, and the city wall of Feiyi was finally demolished.
Then the city was ready to be demolished. Meng Sun's retainer Gong Lian Chufu told Meng Sun: "If the city wall of Cheng Yi is demolished, the people of Qi will definitely advance to our north gate."
Moreover, Chengcheng is also a barrier for your Meng family. Without Chengcheng, there is no Meng family. I'm not going to tear it down.
In December, Lu Dinggong led his troops to surround Chengcheng but could not capture it.
In the fourteenth year of Lu Dinggong, Confucius was fifty-six years old. He acted as the chief minister in the affairs of the prime minister, with a look of joy on his face.
His disciples said: I heard that a gentleman will not be afraid when a great disaster comes, nor will he be overjoyed when a great blessing comes.
Confucius said: There is this saying, but isn't there another saying: "Being in a high position and treating the virtuous but a lowly person is content with yourself?"
So Confucius killed the official Shaozhengmao who was disturbing the state affairs.
Three months after Confucius participated in state affairs, merchants selling pigs and sheep no longer dared to ask for high prices; men and women walked separately; no one picked up things dropped on the road; travelers from all over the country came to the cities of Lu, and they did not need to ask for favors or gifts from officials, they could get what they needed and go back satisfied.
When the Qi State heard the news, they became frightened and said: "As long as Confucius is in power in the Lu State, he will definitely dominate. Once the Lu State becomes hegemonic, we are the closest and will definitely take the lead in annexing us."
Why not give them some land first?
Li Kuan said: Let's try to stop them first. If that doesn't work, then give them the land. Is it too late?
So he selected 80 beautiful women from Qi, put them all in gorgeous clothes, taught them how to dance "Kangle", and gave them to Lord Lu together with 120 horses with patterns on their bodies.
First, place the female musicians and the patterned horse float outside the high gate in the south of Lucheng. Ji Huanzi wore casual clothes and went to watch it again. He planned to accept it, so he told Jun Lu that he would go out to inspect various places. He would take the opportunity to go to the south gate all day long to watch the beauties and horses of Qi State. He didn't even bother to manage the political affairs of the country. Seeing this, Zilu said to Confucius: Teacher, we can leave here.
Confucius said: The State of Lu is about to hold a suburban ceremony. If the barbecue after the ceremony can be distributed to the officials according to the law, then I can stay here.
Ji Huanzi finally accepted the women's band sent by Qi State and did not attend to government affairs for three days. After the suburban sacrifice, he violated common etiquette and did not give the sacrificial meat and the ritual utensils used in the suburban sacrifice to the doctor.
So Confucius left the state of Lu and stayed in the camp overnight that day.
summary: At fifty-six, Confucius acted as chief minister, killing the official Shaozhengmao. Within three months, Lu's markets became honest, men and women walked separately, and lost items were not taken. Qi, fearing Lu's rise, sent eighty beautiful women and 120 horses to Lu. Ji Huanzi accepted them, neglecting state affairs. Confucius left Lu after the suburban sacrifice was mishandled, traveling to Wei, where he received a salary of 60,000 dou but left after slander. He was besieged in Kuang, mistaken for Yang Hu, but escaped. He returned to Wei, met Nanzi, and left after Duke Linggong's behavior disgusted him.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家

translation:
So he was disgusted with what Wei Linggong did, so he left Wei State and went to Cao State.
This year, Lu Dinggong passed away.
Confucius left the State of Cao and arrived in the State of Song, where he practiced etiquette with his disciples under a big tree.
Sima Huan of the Song Dynasty wanted to kill Confucius, so he cut down the tree.
Confucius had no choice but to leave this place.
The disciples urged: We can leave quickly.
Confucius said: Since God has given me the mission of preaching morality, what can Huan Miao do to me?
When Confucius arrived in the state of Zheng, he became separated from his disciples. Confucius stood alone at the east gate of the outer city.
When the people of Zheng saw it, they said to Zigong: There is a man at the east gate. His forehead is like Yao, his neck is like Gaotao, and his shoulders are like Zheng Zichan. But from the waist down, he is three inches shorter than Yu. He looks embarrassed and listless, really like a lost dog.
When Zigong met, he told Confucius the truth.
Confucius said happily: He may not be right when he describes my appearance, but he is absolutely right when he says that I look like a lost dog! Absolutely right.
Confucius then arrived in the state of Chen and stayed at the home of Sadako in Sicheng.
More than a year later, King Wu Fucha came to attack Chen State and captured three cities before retreating.
Zhao Yang attacked Chaoge.
Chu State surrounded Cai State, and Cai State moved to Wu.
The state of Wu defeated King Gou Jian of Yue in Kuaiji.
One day, many falcons fell down and died in the palace of Chen State. They were pierced by arrows made of falcon wood. The arrowheads were made of stone and were one foot and eight inches long.
Chen Minggong sent an envoy to ask Confucius for advice. Confucius said: These falcons flew from a very far away place. They are arrows from the Sushen tribe.
In the past, King Wu of the Zhou Dynasty conquered the Zhou Dynasty and destroyed the Shang Dynasty, which established ties with the various ethnic groups and allowed all ethnic groups of the Nine Barbarians and Barbarians to contribute their own local specialties, so that they could not forget their responsibilities and obligations.
So the Sushen tribe presented arrows made of mulberry wood and arrowheads made of stone, one foot and eight inches long.
In order to show his virtue, King Wu of Zhou gave the arrows of the Sushen tribe to his eldest daughter Taiji. Later, Taiji married Duke Yuhu, and Duke Yuhu granted him a title in the state of Chen.
At the beginning, the royal family distributed treasures and jades to the princes with the same surname to show that they valued their relatives; the tributes from distant places were given to princes with the same surname to show that they valued their relatives; the tributes from distant places were given to princes with the same surname to remind them not to forget to obey the Zhou Dynasty.
Therefore, the arrows from the Sushen tribe were distributed to Chen Guo.
After hearing this, Chen Minggong asked people to search in the warehouse where tributes from all parties were stored, and sure enough, they found this kind of arrow.
Confucius lived in the State of Chen for three years, which coincided with the struggle for hegemony between the State of Jin and the State of Chu. The two countries took turns attacking the State of Chen. Until the State of Wu attacked the State of Chen, the State of Chen was often invaded.
Confucius said: Go back, go back!
The disciples in my hometown all have high aspirations, they are all enterprising, and they have not forgotten their original intentions.
So Confucius left the state of Chen.
Confucius passed by a place called Pu, and happened to meet the Gongshu family who occupied Pu and rebelled against the country. The people of Pu detained Confucius.
One of Confucius's disciples named Gong Liangru brought five cars to follow Confucius around the world.
He was a tall man, talented, virtuous, and brave. He said to Confucius: I used to travel around Kuang with my teacher and encountered dangers. Now I encounter dangers here again. This is destined to happen.
My teacher and I once again encountered disaster and died fighting.
Gong Liangru fought fiercely with the Pu people. The Pu people were frightened and said to Confucius: If you don't go to Weiguo, I will let you go.
Confucius made a covenant with them, and then he let Confucius and the others go out through the east gate.
Confucius then went to Weiguo.
summary: Confucius traveled to Song, where Sima Huan tried to kill him, then to Zheng, where he was described as a lost dog. In Chen, he identified arrows from the Sushen tribe. After three years, he left due to invasions. At Pu, he was detained but escaped after a covenant. He returned to Wei, but Duke Linggong did not use him. He considered going to Jin but turned back after learning of the deaths of two virtuous officials. He returned to Wei, then left for Chen after Duke Linggong ignored him.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家

translation:
Gong Zhiyu said: We must summon Ranqiu.
So he sent someone to recall Ran Qiu.
Ran Qiu was about to get up and go, but Confucius said: This time the State of Lu summoned Ran Qiu back, he will not be used lightly, he should be used in a big way.
On this day, Confucius said: Go back, go back!
Those disciples in my hometown have lofty ambitions but broad-minded actions, and are rich in literary talents. I really don’t know where to start to educate them.
Zigong knew that Confucius missed his hometown and wanted to go back. When sending Ranqiu off, he told him that if he was re-employed, he should think about inviting the teacher back.
After Ran Qiu left, Confucius moved from the state of Chen to the state of Cai the next year.
Cai Zhaogong was preparing to go to the State of Wu, and it was the king of the State of Wu who summoned him.
Previously, Duke Zhao deceived his ministers and moved the capital to Zhoulai. This time he was going to the Kingdom of Wu again. The officials were worried that he would move the capital again. Gongsun Pian shot Duke Zhao with an arrow on the way.
Then, the Chu army came to invade Cai.
In the autumn of the same year, Qi Jinggong passed away.
In the second year, Confucius went from Cai State to Ye Yi.
Ye Gong asked Confucius how to govern. Confucius said: The key to governing is to recruit wise men from far away and make people nearby join.
One day, Lord Ye asked Zilu what Confucius was like, but Zilu didn't answer.
Confucius heard about this and said: Zhong Yu, why don't you answer him? He is a man who never gets tired when he studies principles, never gets tired of teaching others, forgets to eat when he is studying hard, forgets sorrow when he is happy, doesn't know that aging is coming, etc.
Confucius left Ye Di of Chu State and returned to Cai State.
On the road, he met Chang Ju and Jie Zhong, who were plowing the fields side by side. Confucius thought they were hermits, so he sent Zi Lu to find out where the ferry was.
Chang Ju said: Who is the man holding the reins of the horse?
Zilu replied: It is Confucius.
Chang Ju asked again: "Is he Confucius from Lu?"
Zilu said: Yes.
Chang Ju said: Then he should know where the ferry is. Jie Dong asked Zi Lu again: "Who are you?" Zilu said: I am Zhong Yu.
Jie Dun said: Are you a disciple of Confucius?
Zilu said: Yes.
Jie Dun said: The world is in turmoil everywhere, and who can change this situation?
Besides, instead of running around with those who are fleeing from the rioters, why not follow those of us who are fleeing from the troubled times?
After saying that, he continued to plow the fields non-stop.
Zilu told Confucius this, and Confucius said disappointedly: We can't live in the mountains and forests with the birds and beasts. If the world were peaceful, I wouldn't have to run around trying to change this situation.
One day, when Zi Lu was walking alone, he met an old man carrying a weeding tool on his shoulder. Zilu asked him: Have you seen my teacher?
The old man said: You people are not diligent in your limbs and cannot distinguish the grains. How can I know who your teacher is?
After saying that, he went to pull weeds on crutches.
Later, Zilu told Confucius what happened. Confucius said: This is a hermit.
I asked Zilu to look there again, but the old man was gone.
Three years after Confucius moved to the state of Cai, the state of Wu attacked the state of Chen.
The State of Chu rescued the State of Chen, and the army was stationed in Chengfu.
Hearing that Confucius lived on the border of Chen and Cai, Chu sent people to hire Confucius.
Confucius was about to go to see and accept the betrothal gift. The officials of Chen and Cai discussed and said: Confucius is a talented and virtuous man, and what he criticizes and satirizes are all about the shortcomings of the princes.
Now we have been stuck between Chen and Cai for a long time. The administration and actions of the officials are not in line with Zhongni's wishes.
Today's Chu State is a big country, but it came to hire Confucius.
If Confucius is reused in Chu State, then our officials in power in Chen and Cai will be in danger.
So both sides sent some laborers to besiege Confucius in the wild.
Confucius and his disciples were unable to move and their food supply was cut off.
The disciples who followed him were sick from hunger and could not stand up.
But Confucius continued to give lectures, recite poems, sing, and play the piano to everyone.
Zilu came to see Confucius angrily: Is there a time when a gentleman is in trouble?
Confucius said: A gentleman can maintain his integrity and remain unwavering in the face of adversity, while a young man will not exercise restraint when faced with adversity and will do anything that goes too far.
At this time, Zigong's expression also changed.
Confucius said: Ci, do you think I am a man of erudition and memorization?
Zigong replied: Yes.
summary: At sixty, Confucius was in Chen. After Ji Huanzi's death, Ji Kangzi recalled Ran Qiu, and Confucius hoped to return. He moved to Cai, then to Ye, where he advised on governance. He met hermits Chang Ju and Jie Ni, who criticized his efforts. He was besieged between Chen and Cai, running out of food, but continued teaching. His disciples questioned their plight, but Confucius maintained his principles. King Zhao of Chu planned to grant him land, but Zixi dissuaded him, and the king died soon after. Confucius returned to Wei, then to Lu after fourteen years.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/孔子世家

translation:
Although I had meritorious service in the military and was granted a total of 2,500 families, Confucius would not be tempted. Kangzi said: I want to summon him back, is that okay?
Ran You said: If you want to invite him back, as long as you don't let villains hinder him, that's all.
At that time, Kong Wenzi, the official of the Wei State, was preparing to attack Taishu and asked Confucius for advice.
Confucius refused and said he didn't know. When he returned to his residence, he immediately ordered his carriage to leave Weiguo, saying: Birds can choose trees to live in, but how can trees choose birds?
Kong Wenzi firmly detained him.
It happened that Ji Kangzi sent Gonghua, Gongbin, and Gonglin to greet Confucius with gifts, and Confucius returned to the state of Lu.
Confucius left the State of Lu for fourteen years and returned to the State of Lu.
Duke Ai of Lu asked Confucius about the principles of government. Confucius replied: The most important thing in government is to choose ministers.
Ji Kangzi also asked Confucius about the principles of government. Confucius said: Use upright people and discard people with evil intentions, so that people with evil intentions can become upright.
Ji Kangzi was worried about stealing. Confucius said: If you have no desire, people will not steal even if you give them rewards.
However, the State of Lu failed to appoint Confucius in the end, and Confucius did not ask to be an official.
In the time of Confucius, the king of Zhou was in decline, rituals and music were in ruins, and the "Poems" and "Books" were also in short supply.
Confucius studied the etiquette system of the Xia, Shang, and Western Zhou dynasties, and compiled the chapters of Shuzhuan, starting from the time of Yao and Shun of Tang Dynasty, to Duke Mu of Qin Dynasty, and arranged them according to the order of events.
Confucius said: I can still describe the etiquette system of the Xia Dynasty, but the Qi State, a descendant of the Xia Dynasty, did not leave enough documents to prove it.
I can also tell you about the etiquette system of the Yin and Shang Dynasties, but the post-Song Dynasty of the Yin and Shang Dynasties did not leave enough documents to prove these systems.
If there are enough documents from Qi and Song, I can prove these systems.
After examining the additions and deletions made by the Yin Dynasty to the Xia Dynasty in the etiquette system, Confucius said: Even after a hundred years in the future, the increases and decreases can be predicted, because one kind of emphasis is on literary talent, and the other is on simplicity.
The etiquette system of the Zhou Dynasty was formulated based on the Xia Dynasty and the Yin Dynasty. It is so rich and colorful. I advocate using the etiquette of the Zhou Dynasty. Therefore, "Shu Zhuan" and "Book of Rites" were both compiled by Confucius.
Confucius once said to the music official Taishi of Lu: Music can be understood.
At the beginning of the performance, they should cooperate with each other, and continue to have a harmonious rhythm, clear and continuous sound, until the whole piece of music is completed.
Confucius also said: After I returned to Lu from Wei, I began to correct the poetry and music, restoring the original tunes of "Ya" and "Song".
There are more than 3,000 poems handed down from ancient times. At the time of Confucius, he deleted the repetitive ones and selected those that were consistent with the meaning for etiquette education. The earliest ones traced the ancestors of Yin, Qi, and the ancestors of Zhou, Houji. The second ones described the prosperity of the Yin and Zhou dynasties, until the political absence of King Zhou You and King Li of Zhou. The beginning was a poem describing the relationship and feelings between men and women, so it is said: The movement "Guan Sui" is the first chapter of "Guofeng", "Lu Ming" is the first chapter of "Xiao Ya", "King Wen" is the first chapter of "Daya", and "Qing Temple" is the first chapter of "Ode".
Confucius was able to play and sing the three hundred and five poems in order to match the tunes of the music "Shao", "Wu", "Ya" and "Song".
From then on, the music system of the former kings was restored to the old view and could be described. The king's way was complete, and Confucius also completed the compilation of "Poetry", "Book", "Yue", "Yi" and "Spring and Autumn" which are known as the "Six Arts". In his later years, Confucius liked to study "The Book of Changes". He explained in detail the "Yun Ci", "Xici", "Gua", "Classic Chinese", etc.
Confucius read the "Book of Changes" so diligently that he broke the cowhide rope that woven the slips through many times. He also said: If I live a few more years, I will be able to fully understand the diction and meaning of "The Book of Changes".
Confucius used "Poems", "Books", "Li" and "Music" as teaching materials to educate his disciples. There were about 3,000 disciples studying there, and 72 of them were proficient in the six skills of etiquette, music, archery, charioteering, arithmetic, and shu.
As for people like Yan Zhuozou, there are even more disciples who were taught by Confucius in many aspects but were not formally naturalized. Confucius educated his disciples in four aspects: knowledge, words and deeds, loyalty and forgiveness, and faith.
Set four prohibitions for disciples: don’t speculate, don’t be arbitrary, don’t be stubborn, and don’t be self-righteous.
summary: In Lu, Confucius was not appointed to office. He compiled the "Shu Zhuan" and "Book of Rites," corrected poetry and music, and studied the "Book of Changes," wearing out the binding cords. He taught about 3,000 disciples, with 72 mastering the six arts. He educated in knowledge, conduct, loyalty, and faith, avoiding profit unless linked to fate and benevolence. He was humble in his hometown but eloquent in court. He avoided spoiled food and improper seating, and showed sympathy to mourners and the blind.

translation:
When a person from Xia died, his coffin was placed on the steps of the east chamber, when a person from Zhou died, his coffin was placed on the steps of the west chamber, and when a person from Yin died, his coffin was placed between the two pillars of the hall.
Last night I dreamed that I was sitting between two pillars and being worshiped. My ancestor was the Yin Shang Dynasty.
After that, Confucius died.
Confucius was seventy-three years old and died on Ji Chou day in April of the sixteenth year of Duke Ai of Lu.
Duke Ai of Lu wrote a eulogy for him and said: God is not kind and refuses to keep this old man. He leaves me alone and I am lonely and hurt. ah!
How painful! Nifu, there is no one who can serve as a role model for me to learn from!
Zigong said, "Master of Lu, can't he stay in Lu forever?"
The teacher said: Loss of Dharma will lead to confusion, and loss of status will lead to faults.
If you lose your will, you will become confused; if you lose your ability, you will make mistakes.
You cannot use the teacher while he is alive, but it is not appropriate to mourn him after he is dead.
It is inappropriate to call him "Yu Yiren" as a prince.
After his death, Confucius was buried on the shore of Surabaya, north of Lucheng. His disciples mourned him in their hearts for three years.
After three years of mourning, when everyone said goodbye and left, they all cried to each other and mourned each other; some even stayed.
Only Zigong lived in a small room next to the tomb and guarded the tomb for a total of six years before leaving.
His disciples and others from the state of Lu led more than a hundred people who lived near the tomb. So this place was named Kongli.
It has been passed down from generation to generation in the State of Lu that they regularly visit Confucius's tomb every year to worship. Confucian scholars also come here at this time to learn etiquette, go to the countryside for academic examinations, have drinking ceremonies, and perform archery competitions and other ceremonies. Confucius's tomb is an area of ​​one hectare.
The main hall of Confucius's former residence and the inner rooms where his disciples lived were later converted into temples to store the clothes, hats, musical instruments, cars, books, etc. that Confucius wore during his lifetime. Until the Han Dynasty, it was not abandoned for more than 200 years.
Emperor Liu Bang of Gao Dynasty passed through the land of Lu and sacrificed Confucius with Tailao, which was equipped with cattle, sheep and pigs.
When princes, ministers, officials, and prime ministers arrive at their posts, they often visit the tomb of Confucius before taking office and handling government affairs.
Confucius gave birth to a carp, named Boyu.
Boyu died at the age of fifty, before Confucius.
Boyu gave birth to Ji, whose name was Zisi. Guo was sixty-two years old.
Once trapped in the Song Dynasty.
Zisi wrote "The Doctrine of the Mean".
Zisi gave birth to Bai, named Zishang, at the age of forty-seven.
Zishang gave birth to Qiu, named Zijia, at the age of forty-five.
Ji was born in Zi's family, named Zijing, and he died at the age of forty-six.
Zijing gave birth to Chuan Chuan, named Zi Gao, at the age of fifty-one.
Zigao gave birth to Shen, who died at the age of fifty-seven. He once served as the prime minister of Wei.
Zishen gave birth to Yu, and died at the age of fifty-seven. He was a doctor of King Sheng of Chen, and died in Chen.
Yu's younger brother is named Zixiang, who died at the age of fifty-seven.
He once served as a doctor for Emperor Xiaohui of the Han Dynasty and was later promoted to the prefect of Changsha County.
summary: In his later years, Confucius compiled the "Spring and Autumn Annals" based on Lu's history, covering twelve rulers. He used subtle writing to praise and criticize, making rebellious officials fearful. He died at seventy-three in the sixteenth year of Duke Ai of Lu. Duke Ai mourned him, but Zigong criticized the eulogy. Confucius was buried north of Lucheng. Disciples mourned for three years, with Zigong staying six years. His tomb became a site of annual worship, and his former residence was turned into a temple, preserved for over 200 years. Emperor Liu Bang of Han sacrificed to him. Confucius' descendants continued his lineage, including his son Boyu, who died before him, and grandson Zisi, who wrote "The Doctrine of the Mean." The historian concluded that Confucius, though a commoner, became the supreme sage, with his teachings enduring for generations.

translation:
Wei Zikai was the eldest son of Emperor Yi of the Yin Dynasty and the half-brother of King Zhou.
After Shang Zhou came to the throne, his rule was dark, he did not care about the affairs of the country, he was licentious and extravagant, and his followers repeatedly came to the throne, but King Zhou did not listen.
When Zuyi destroyed Xu due to Zhou Xibochang's virtuous governance, Weizi was worried that disaster would befall the Yin Dynasty, so he repeatedly advised King Zhou.
But King Zhou said: Wasn't it my destiny to be in Gastrodia when I was born?
Who can do anything to me?
Wei Zi then expected that King Zhou would not listen to his advice until his death, and planned to die or leave King Zhou. But he could not make a decision, so he went to ask the Taishi and Shaoshi, saying: The Yin Dynasty no longer has clear politics and cannot govern the four directions well.
Our ancestors created great achievements in the previous life, but King Zhou indulges in wine and banquets today, only obeying the words of women, disrupting and corrupting King Tang's good governance.
Everyone in the Yin Dynasty, big and small, was keen on thefts and rebellions in the grasslands. The ministers also imitated each other and violated laws and disciplines. Almost all of them were guilty, so their honors and titles could not continue. Since the imperial court was in chaos, the people began to rise up in all directions and became enemies of each other, and the world lost harmony.
Now, the Yin Dynasty has lost its national code, just like crossing a river by boat and not being able to find a ferry.
The demise of the Yin Dynasty is just around the corner.
Wei Zi continued: Master, Master, where will I go?
Can our Yin Dynasty be saved? You have no intention of warning me. What should I do if I fall into injustice?
The Grand Master followed suit and said: Prince, the Emperor of Heaven has brought disaster and destroyed the Yin Dynasty, but King Zhou is not afraid of the punishment of Heaven, nor does he listen to the advice of his elders.
Now, the subjects of the Yin Dynasty actually violated and falsely accused the gods of their will.
Now, if the Yin Dynasty can really be saved and the country is well managed, even if he dies, there will be no resentment left.
I'm afraid that even if you die for the country, the country still can't be governed, so it's better to go far away.
So Wei Zi left the Yin Dynasty.
Jizi is a relative of King Zhou.
When King Zhou first made ivory chopsticks, Jizi lamented: If he makes ivory chopsticks now, he will definitely make jade cups in the future; if he makes jade cups, he will definitely want to take possession of rare treasures from far away.
The luxury of carriages, horses and palaces will definitely start from here, and the country will definitely not be able to revitalize.
Because of King Zhou's excessive sexual behavior, Jizi came to remonstrate with him, but King Zhou still refused to listen.
Someone said: You can leave now.
Jizi said: When a minister remonstrates with the monarch, the monarch ignores him and then leaves him. This is to publicize the monarch's evil deeds and to flatter the people by grandstanding. I cannot bear to do this.
So Jizi disheveled his hair, pretended to be crazy and became a slave.
He lived in seclusion and masturbated by playing the piano, so people praised his song as "Ji Zi Cao".
Prince Bigan was also a relative of King Zhou. When he saw that Jizi was admonishing, but the monarch did not listen and became a slave, he said: "The monarch has sins, and if he cannot persuade him directly with death, the people will suffer, and what crime do the people have?"
So, he bluntly remonstrated with King Zhou.
King Zhou was furious and said: I heard that the saint's heart has seven orifices. Is this true?
So King Zhou killed Bigan and dug out his heart to verify.
Wei Zi said: Father and son are connected by flesh and blood, while ministers and ministers are connected by morality.
Therefore, if a father is at fault and his son refuses to listen to his advice over and over again, he should cry accordingly; if a minister refuses to listen to his advice after repeated advice, then morally speaking, the minister can leave the king.
So, the Grand Master and the Young Master advised Wei Zi to leave, and Wei Zi left.
King Wu of Zhou attacked King Zhou and defeated the Yin Dynasty. Weizi came to King Wu's military gate with his sacrificial weapon in hand. He exposed his right arm and tied his hands behind his back. He had someone on the left holding the sheep and someone on the right holding a straw. He knelt on the ground and went forward to beg King Wu.
So King Wu released Wei Zi and restored his original title.
King Wu made Wu Geng, the son of Shang Zhou, his father and asked him to inherit the sacrifices of the Yin Dynasty. He also sent Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai to assist him.
After King Wu destroyed the Yin Dynasty, he went to visit Jizi.
King Wu said: Alas!
summary: Wei Zikai, eldest son of Emperor Yi of Yin and half-brother of King Zhou, repeatedly advised King Zhou against his dark, licentious rule but was ignored. Fearing Yin's downfall, Wei Zi consulted the Grand Master and Junior Master, who advised him to leave when the kingdom became irredeemable. He then departed. Jizi, a relative of King Zhou, lamented King Zhou's extravagance with ivory chopsticks, foreseeing ruin. After King Zhou ignored his remonstrations, Jizi feigned madness and became a slave rather than publicize the king's evil. Prince Bigan, another relative, bluntly admonished King Zhou, who killed him and ripped out his heart to check for seven orifices. Wei Zi concluded that ministers may leave a king who refuses repeated advice.

translation:
Various signs: whether it is rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, or wind, these five natural phenomena should occur on time.
If all five natural phenomena are present and appear according to certain rules, crops will flourish.
If too much of one phenomenon occurs, the harvest will fail.
If a phenomenon is lacking, the harvest will also fail.
Regarding good omens: if the emperor is humble, it will rain on time; if the emperor is clear in government affairs, the sun will be abundant; if the emperor is wise, warmth will come on time; if the emperor is foresighted, cold will come on time; if the emperor is wise, the wind will blow on time.
There are all kinds of evil signs: if the emperor is arrogant, there will be too much rain; if the emperor is presumptuous, the sky will be dry; if the emperor is greedy for pleasure, the weather will be too hot; if the emperor is violent and impatient, the sky will be too cold; if the emperor is dim and unclear, the wind will blow continuously; if the emperor makes mistakes in his decision-making, it will affect the whole year; if the emperor's management is wrong, it will affect the whole month; if the officials are wrong in doing things, it will affect the whole day.
If there are no abnormalities in the year, month, and day, all kinds of crops will grow luxuriantly, politics will be clear, worthy people will be promoted, and the country will be safe and stable.
On the contrary, if there are abnormalities in the year, month, and day, the crops will not grow well, the politics will be gloomy, the capable people will be suppressed, and the country will be in turmoil. The people are like stars, and some stars like wind and some like rain.
The sun and the moon move according to rules, resulting in winter and summer.
If the moon obeys the stars, it will be windy sometimes and rainy sometimes.
Five blessings: first, longevity, second, wealth, third, peace, fourth, virtue, and fifth, a good death.
Six disasters: one is premature death, the other is illness, the third is sadness, the fourth is poverty, the fifth is ugliness, and the sixth is cowardice.
After hearing Jizi's statement, King Wu granted North Korea to Jizi and no longer regarded him as a subject.
Later, Jizi paid homage to the King of Zhou and passed by his old capital Yinxu. He was saddened by the ruins of the palace and the overgrown crops. Jizi was very sad and wanted to cry loudly, but he couldn't. He wanted to cry quietly, but he also felt that he was close to a woman's character, so he recited "Mai Xiu" in response to the scene. The poem said: The wheat awns are sharp and the grass seedlings are green.
That boy is not friendly to me!
The so-called boy is King Zhou.
When the people of Yin saw this poem, they all cried for it.
After King Wu died and King Cheng was still young, Zhou Gongdan took charge of the state power as an acting administrator.
Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai suspected Zhou Gongdan, so they started a rebellion with Wu Geng and wanted to attack King Cheng and Duke Zhou.
Zhou Gong borrowed the order from King Cheng to kill Wu Geng and Guan Shu, and banished Cai Shu. He also asked Wei Zikai to take charge of Yin in Wu Geng's place to continue the sacrifice of Yin's ancestors. He also warned him with the "Wei Zi's Order" and sealed Wei Zi in the Song Dynasty.
Weizi was originally benevolent, righteous and capable. After replacing Wu Geng, the people in the old land of the Yin Dynasty loved him very much.
summary: King Wu of Zhou defeated Yin, and Wei Zi surrendered, bearing sacrificial vessels. King Wu restored Wei Zi's title and appointed Wu Geng, son of Shang Zhou, to continue Yin sacrifices, with Guan Shu and Cai Shu as assistants. King Wu visited Jizi, who explained the nine great laws of heaven: the Five Elements, Five Matters, Eight Political Rules, Five Epochs, Imperial Principles, Three Virtues, Divination, Various Signs, and Five Blessings with Six Extremes. King Wu granted Jizi Korea, no longer treating him as a subject. Jizi later composed a poem mourning Yin's ruins.

translation:
After Wei Zikai died, he made his younger brother Yan the king of the country. This is Wei Zhong.
After Weizhong's death, his son Song Gongji came to the throne.
After the death of Song Gongji, his son Ding Gongshen came to the throne.
After the death of Ding Gongshen, his son Min Gong came to the throne.
After Min Gong died, his younger brother Yang Gongxi came to the throne.
After Duke Yang ascended the throne, Min Gong's son Yusi killed Duke Yang and seized the throne, and announced: "I should ascend the throne." This is Duke Li.
After Li Gong died, his son Li Gongju came to the throne.
In the seventeenth year of Ligong's reign, King Li of Zhou fled to pig.
In the twenty-eighth year, after Duke Li died, his son Hui Gong came to the throne.
In the fourth year of Duke Hui, King Xuan of Zhou came to the throne.
In the thirtieth year, Duke Hui passed away and Duke Ai came to the throne.
Ai Gong died in the first year, and his son Dai Gong came to the throne.
In the twenty-ninth year of Dai Gong, King You of Zhou was killed by Quan Rong, and Qin began to be classified as a vassal state.
In the thirty-fourth year, Duke Dai died, and his son Wu Gong came to the throne empty.
Duke Wu gave birth to a daughter, who later became the wife of Duke Hui of Lu and gave birth to Duke Huan of Lu.
In the eighteenth year, Duke Wu died and his son Xuan Gongli came to the throne.
Xuan Gong's prince's name is Yi.
In the 19th year, Duke Xuan fell ill and gave up the throne to his younger brother He, saying: "When the father dies, the son succeeds to the throne; when the elder brother dies, the younger brother succeeds to the throne. This is the universal morality in the world." I want to establish He as the king of the country.
He gave in many times before finally accepting.
After the death of Duke Xuan, his younger brother He ascended the throne and became Duke Mu.
In the ninth year, Duke Mu fell seriously ill. He summoned Grand Sima Kongfu and said, "The late king, Duke Xuan, abandoned the crown prince and the barbarians and passed the throne to me. I will never forget it."
After I die, I must support Yu Yi as the king.
Father Confucius said: All the ministers want to establish Prince Feng.
Duke Mu said: "Don't support Feng. I can't let Duke Xuan down."
So Duke Mu ordered his son Feng to go and live in the state of Zheng.
On Gengchen Day in August, Duke Mu died, and his brother Xuangong's son Yi succeeded him as Duke Shang.
When the gentlemen heard about this, they said: Song Xuan Gong knew people well and fulfilled his morality by passing the throne to his younger brother. However, in the end it was his son who got the throne.
In the first year of Shang Dynasty, Duke Zhouxu of Wei killed his own king Wan and established himself as king. Wanting to get the support of the princes, he sent someone to tell the king of Song: "Young Master Feng is in Zheng, and he will be a trouble in the future. You can work with me to attack him."
The king of Song State agreed, and he and Wei State jointly attacked Zheng State. The army returned after reaching the east gate of Zheng State.
The next year, Zheng Guo attacked the Song State and avenged the hatred of the Dongmen soldiers.
After that, the princes came to invade the Song Dynasty many times.
One day in the ninth year, the beautiful wife of the Grand Sima Kong Fujia went out and met Dazai Hua Du on the road. Hua Du took a fancy to Zhongjia's wife and looked at her intently.
summary: After King Wu's death, Zhou Gongdan, acting as regent, suppressed a rebellion by Guan Shu, Cai Shu, and Wu Geng. He killed Wu Geng, exiled Cai Shu, and appointed Wei Zikai to rule Yin, later enfeoffing him in Song. Wei Zi's benevolent rule endeared him to the people. His successors included Wei Zhong, Song Gongji, Ding Gongshen, Min Gong, Yang Gongxi, Li Gong, Li Gongju, Hui Gong, Ai Gong, Dai Gong, Wu Gong, Xuan Gongli, and Mu Gong. Mu Gong, honoring his brother Xuan Gong's wish, passed the throne to Xuan Gong's son Yi (Duke Shang) instead of his own son.

translation:
So, he supported the young son of Gong Gong, who became Ping Gong.
In the third year of Ping Gong's reign, the King of the Communist Party of Chu captured Pengcheng of the Song Dynasty and granted Pengcheng to Yushi, Zuo Shi of the Song Dynasty.
In four years, the princes united to kill Yushi and returned Pengcheng to the Song Dynasty.
In the thirty-fifth year, the prince of Chu besieged the king who killed him and ascended the throne. This was King Ling of Chu.
In the forty-fourth year, Duke Ping died, and his son Yuan Gongzuo came to the throne.
In the third year of Duke Yuan, Chu Gongzi abandoned his illness and killed the king and ascended the throne, becoming King Ping.
In eight years, a fire broke out in Song Dynasty.
In the past ten years, Duke Yuan was dishonest and used deceptive means to kill all the princes.
The officials Hua and Xiang raised armies one after another to cause chaos.
Prince Jian of King Ping of Chu fled to the State of Song. Seeing Hua and others attacking each other, he left the State of Song and ran to the State of Zheng.
In the fifteenth year, because Lu Zhaogong was living abroad to avoid the Ji family, Yuan Gong prayed for Lu Zhaogong to return to Lu. As a result, he died on the way, and his son Jinggong Touman came to the throne.
In the 16th year of Jinggong, Yang Hu of the state of Lu fled to the state of Song, and soon left again.
In the twenty-fifth year, Confucius passed by the Song Dynasty. Sima Huanxi of the Song Dynasty hated Confucius and wanted to kill him. Confucius put on civilian clothes and escaped from the Song Dynasty.
Thirty years later, Cao State broke its alliance with Song State and then broke its alliance with Jin State. Song State then attacked Cao State, but Jin State did not come to rescue, so Song State destroyed Cao State and occupied Cao State's territory.
In the thirty-sixth year, Qi State official Tian Chang killed the monarch Jian Gong.
In the thirty-seventh year, King Hui of Chu lost the Kingdom of Chen, and Mars invaded the Antares star region.
Xinsu District is the territory of the Song Dynasty, and Jinggong is very worried about it.
Ziwei, who is in charge of the stars, said: The disaster can be transferred to the prime minister.
Jinggong said: "No, the Prime Minister is like my brothers and feet."
Ziwei added: "It can be passed on to the people."
Jinggong said: "No, the king relies on the people."
Ziwei said again: It can be transferred to annual achievements.
Jinggong said: "Not to mention, the harvest will fail and the people will be poor. Whose king should I be then?"
Ziwei said: Although the sky is high, you can still hear the subtle sounds of the lower world. You have said the three words that a king should say, and the Mars should have moved.
So I observed Mars carefully and found that Mars indeed moved three degrees.
In the sixty-fourth year, Jinggong passed away.
Song Gongzi killed the prince and ascended the throne. This was Zhao Gong.
Duke Zhao is the great-grandson of Duke Yuan.
Zhao Gong's father was Gongsun Jiu, Jiu's father was Gongzi Chu Qin, and Chu Qin was the youngest son of Duke Yuan.
Duke Jinggong killed Duke Zhao's father, Gongsun Jiu, so Duke Zhao resented the prince, so he killed him and took the throne himself.
Duke Zhao died in his forty-seventh year, and his son mourned him and made you the king.
After reigning for eight years, Duke Du passed away, and his son Xiu Gongtian came to the throne.
Xiu Gongtian died in the 23rd year of his reign, and his son came to the throne.
Pi Gong died after three years in office, and his son Ticheng came to the throne.
summary: Duke Shang's reign saw turmoil: Hua Du killed Kong's father and Duke Shang, installing Duke Zhuang. Subsequent rulers included Min Gong, Huan Gong, Xiang Gong, Cheng Gong, Zhao Gong, Wen Gong, Gong Gong, Ping Gong, Yuan Gong, Jing Gong, Zhao Gong, Duke Du, Xiu Gongtian, Pi Gong, Ticheng, and Yan. Yan, known as "Jie Song," indulged in cruelty and debauchery, shooting advisors. The princes allied with Qi to attack Song, killing Yan and dividing its territory in his forty-seventh year.

translation:
During the forty-one year of Ticheng's reign, Ticheng's younger brother Yan attacked Ticheng. Ticheng failed and fled to Qi, where Yan established himself as the king of Song.
In the eleventh year, Yan himself was crowned king.
He defeated the State of Qi to the east and captured five cities; he defeated the State of Chu to the south and occupied more than 300 miles of Chu land; he defeated the State of Wei to the west and became enemies with Qi and Wei.
Jun Yan used a cowhide bag to hold the blood, hung it up and shot it with arrows, which was called "shooting the sky".
Jun Yan indulged in wine and sex all day long.
All ministers who gave advice and advice were shot to death by him with arrows.
So the princes all called him Jie Song. Song Junyan followed in the footsteps of King Zhou and did whatever he wanted, so he had to kill him.
The princes asked Qi to attack Song.
When King Yan of the Song Dynasty came to the throne forty-seven years, King Min of Qi joined forces with Wei and Chu to attack the Song State, killed Yan, destroyed the Song State, and divided the Song State's territory.
Tai Shigong said: Confucius said: Weizi left, Jizi became a slave, Bigan was killed when he came to remonstrate, and there were three benevolent people in the Yin Dynasty.
"Spring and Autumn" ridiculed that the turmoil in the Song Dynasty began when Duke Xuan deposed the prince and allowed his younger brother to take the throne. The country was unstable for ten generations.
When Duke Xiang was in power, he practiced benevolence and righteousness and wanted to be the leader of the alliance.
In order to praise him, his doctor Zheng Kaofu traced the reasons for the prosperity of the Yin Dynasty in the Qi, Tang and Gaozong periods and wrote "Ode to Shang".
Song Xianggong was defeated at Hongshui, but some gentlemen still thought he was worthy of praise. This was because the gentlemen lamented that the countries in the Central Plains region lacked etiquette at that time, so they commended him because Song Xianggong had a spirit of courtesy.
summary: Tai Shigong concluded that Confucius recognized three benevolent men of Yin: Wei Zi, Jizi, and Bigan. The "Spring and Autumn" noted Song's instability began when Duke Xuan deposed the prince for his brother. Duke Xiang's benevolent attempts at leadership were praised, though he was defeated at Hongshui; gentlemen commended his adherence to ritual propriety amidst the era's lack of etiquette.
