translation:
Tang Shuyu of Jin State was the son of King Zhou Wu and the younger brother of King Zhou Cheng.
At first, when King Wu of Zhou was with Shu Yu's mother, Shu Yu's mother dreamed that God said to King Wu of Zhou: I will give you a son named Yu, and I will give him the land of Tang.
When Mrs. Wu Wang gave birth to the baby, she saw that the word "Yu" was written on the palm of her hand, so she named her son Yu.
After the death of King Zhou Wu, King Zhou Cheng succeeded to the throne, civil strife broke out in Tang Dynasty, and Duke Zhou destroyed Tang Dynasty.
One day, King Cheng of Zhou and Shu Yu were playing together. King Cheng cut a tung tree leaf into the shape of a jade and gave it to Shu Yu, saying: Use this to entrust you.
Shi Yi then asked to choose an auspicious day to make Shu Yu a prince.
King Zhou Cheng said: I was joking with him!
Shi Yi said: The emperor has no jokes.
As long as it is said, the historian must record it truthfully, complete it according to etiquette, and play music to praise it.
So King Cheng of Zhou granted the land of Tang to Shu Yu.
Tang Dynasty is located east of the Yellow River and Fen River, with a radius of hundreds of miles, so Shuyu is also called Tang Shuyu. His surname is Ji and his courtesy name is Ziyu.
Uncle Tang's son Xie was the Marquis of Jin.
The son of the Marquis of Jin, Ning, was the Marquis of Wu.
The son of Marquis Wu was the Marquis of Cheng.
Chenghou's son Fu was Lihou.
Lihou's son Yijiu was Jinghou.
After Jinghou, the age of Jin can be calculated.
From Tang Shuyu to Jinghou in the Five Dynasties, there is no record of the number of years they reigned.
In the 17th year of Jinghou, King Li of Zhou was brutal and violent, and the people of the country were in turmoil. King Li fled to the pigs, and the ministers presided over government affairs, so it was called "Republic".
In the eighteenth year, Jinghou passed away and his son Lihou Situ succeeded to the throne.
In the fourteenth year of Lihou, King Xuan of Zhou had just ascended the throne.
In the eighteenth year, Marquis Li died, and his son Xianhou came to the throne.
Xianhou died in the eleventh year, and his son Muhou, King Fei, came to the throne.
In the fourth year after Mu Hou ascended the throne, he married Qi's daughter Jiang as his wife.
In the seventh year, Muhou conquered the territory.
The lady gave birth to the prince and was angry.
In ten years, he conquered thousands of acres and made great achievements.
Mu Hou also had a younger son, named Chengshi.
The teacher from Jin Dynasty said: "What a strange name the king gave to his child!"
The prince's name is Qiu, and Qiu means hatred.
The younger son is called Chengshi. Chengshi is a big name and means success.
The name is given by itself, but things have their own rules.
Now, the names of the eldest son and the concubine are exactly the same. Will Jin be able to avoid chaos in the future?
In the twenty-seventh year, Hou Mu died, and his younger brother Uncle Shang established himself as king, and Prince Qiu was forced to flee.
In the third year of Uncle Shang's reign, King Xuan of Zhou passed away.
In the fourth year, Muhou's prince Qiu led his followers to attack Uncle Shang and established himself as the king of the country. This was Wenhou.
In the tenth year of Marquis Wen, King You of Zhou was ignorant and immoral. Dogs and soldiers killed King You of Zhou, and the royal family of Zhou moved eastward.
summary: Tang Shuyu of Jin was the son of King Wu of Zhou and younger brother of King Cheng. His mother dreamed that God would give her a son named Yu who would receive the land of Tang. When born, the character "Yu" was found on his palm, so he was named Yu. After King Wu died, King Cheng succeeded and destroyed the rebellious Tang state. While playing, King Cheng cut a tung tree leaf into a jade shape and gave it to Shuyu, saying he would enfeoff him. When asked to formalize this, King Cheng claimed he was joking, but Shi Yi insisted the emperor has no jokes. Thus, Tang was granted to Shuyu, who became known as Tang Shuyu. The succession continued through generations: Xie became Marquis of Jin, followed by Marquis Wu, Marquis Cheng, Marquis Li, and Marquis Jing. From Tang Shuyu to Jinghou across five generations, reign lengths were unrecorded. In Jinghou's 17th year, King Li of Zhou fled due to popular unrest, and ministers governed during the "Republic" period. After Jinghou died, his son Lihou succeeded. The line continued through Xianhou, Muhou, and others. During Muhou's reign, his wife gave birth to a prince named Qiu (meaning hatred) and a younger son named Chengshi (meaning success). A Jin teacher warned these names would bring chaos.

translation:
Qin Xianggong began to be classified as a prince. In the thirty-fifth year, Wenhou Qiu died, and his son Zhaohou Bo came to the throne. In the first year of the reign of Emperor Zhaohou, Marquis Wen conferred the title of Quwo to his younger brother.
Quwo City is larger than Yicheng.
Yicheng was the capital of Jinjun.
When he became a master, he was granted the title of Uncle Huan in Quwo.
Jinghou's concubine Luan Bin assisted Uncle Huan.
At that time, Uncle Huan was already old and respected virtue, so the people of Jin State all attached themselves to him.
The gentleman said: The turmoil in Jin State is in Quwo.
It is bigger than its roots and has won the hearts of the people. If there is no chaos, what are you waiting for!
In the seventh year of Zhaohou, Pan's father, the minister of Jin, killed the king Zhaohou and was going to meet Uncle Huan Quwo.
Uncle Huan also wanted to go to the Jin capital, but the Jin people sent troops to attack Uncle Huan.
Uncle Huan was defeated and returned to Quwo.
The people of Jin jointly established Ping, the son of Zhaohou, as the king of the country. This is Xiaohou.
Xiaohou killed Pan's father.
In the eighth year of Xiaohou's reign, Uncle Huan of Quwo passed away, and his son Huan inherited Uncle Huan's title. He became Uncle Zhuang of Quwo.
In the fifteenth year of Xiaohou's reign, Quwo Zhuangbo killed the king of Jin Xiaohou in Yicheng.
The Jin people attacked Quwo Zhuangbo, and Zhuangbo returned to Quwo again.
The people of Jin also made Xiaohou's son Qie their king, and he became the Marquis of E.
In the second year of Ehou's reign, Duke Yin of Lu had just ascended the throne.
Ehou passed away in the sixth year of his reign.
When Quwo Zhuangbo heard that the Marquis of E of Jin had passed away, he raised troops to attack the capital of Jin.
King Ping of Zhou sent Duke Guo to lead an army to attack Zhuangbo in Quwo, but Zhuangbo fled back to Quwo to defend himself.
The people of Jin jointly established Guang, the son of Ehou, as the king of the country. This is Aihou.
In the second year of Aihou's reign, Uncle Zhuang of Quwo passed away, and his son succeeded him to the throne. This was Duke Wu of Quwo.
In the sixth year of Aihou's reign, the people of Lu killed their own king, Duke Yin of Lu.
In the eighth year of Aihou's reign, the Jin State invaded Xingting.
Xingting and Quwo Wu Gong planned together. In the ninth year, they arrived at the Fen River to attack Jin and captured Jin Aihou.
So the Jin people made Aihou's son Xiaozi their king, and he became Xiaozihou.
In the first year of Xiaozi's reign, Duke Wu of Quwo ordered Han Wan to kill the captured Jin Aihou.
Quwo became more and more powerful, and Jin had nothing to do with it.
In the fourth year of Jin Xiaozi's reign, Quwo Wu Gong deceived Jin Xiaozi and killed him.
King Huan of Zhou sent Guo Zhong to attack Duke Wu of Quwo. Duke Wu fled back to Quwo, and Marquis Ai of Jin's younger brother Min was made Marquis of Jin.
In the fourth year of Jin Houmin's reign, the Song Dynasty arrested Zheng Zhong's Ji Zhong and forced him to establish Tu as the king of Zheng.
In the 19th year of the Marquis of Jin, the Qi people Guan Zhifu killed his own monarch Qi Xianggong.
In the twenty-eighth year of the Marquis of Jin, Duke Huan of Qi began to dominate.
Duke Wu of Quwo attacked Jin Hou Min, destroyed Jin, and dedicated all the treasures of Jin to King Zhouli. King Li appointed Duke Wu of Quwo as the king of Jin and listed him as a prince, so Duke Wu annexed the entire land of Jin and made it his own.
Duke Wu of Quwo had been on the throne for thirty-seven years before he changed his title to Duke Wu of Jin.
Duke Wugong of Jin began to move to the capital of Jin State, including the previous accession to the throne in Quwo, for a total of thirty-eight years.
Duke Wu claimed to be the great-grandson of the late king Muhou of Jin and the grandson of Uncle Huan Quwo.
Uncle Huan was the first to be granted the title of Quwo.
Duke Wu is the son of Uncle Zhuang.
It was a total of sixty-seven years from the time when Uncle Huan was first granted the title of Quwo to the time when Duke Wu destroyed the state of Jin. Duke Wu finally replaced the state of Jin and became a vassal.
Duke Wu died in the second year after he replaced the king of Jin. Including his reign in Quwo, he died in a total of thirty-nine years.
His son Xian Gong Gui Zhu came to the throne. In the first year of Xian AD, King Hui of Zhou's brother Tuan attacked King Hui. King Hui fled and lived in Liyi of Zheng State.
In the fifth year, Duke Xian of Jin attacked Li Rong and obtained Li Ji and Li Ji's sister, whom he loved very much. In the eighth year of the Jin Dynasty, many princes from Jin State had fled to Guo State. Therefore, Guo Gong once again attacked Jin State, but failed to win.
In the tenth year of Xiangong's reign, Jin wanted to attack Guo, but Shi Jiang said: Let's wait until it has its own civil strife!
In the twelfth year, Li Ji gave birth to Xi Qi.
Duke Xian planned to depose the prince, so he said: Quwo is the place where the ancestral temple of our ancestors is located, while Pu is close to Qin and Qu is close to Zhai. If the princes are not allowed to guard those places, I will be worried.
So Duke Xian asked Prince Shen Sheng to garrison Quwo, Prince Chong'er to garrison Pu, and Prince Yiwu to garrison Qu.
Xi Qi, the son of Duke Xian and Li Ji, lived in Jiang, the capital of the country.
Therefore, the people of Jin knew that the prince would not be able to ascend the throne.
Prince Shen Sheng's mother was Qi Huangong's daughter, named Qi Jiang, who had died long ago.
Shen Sheng's half-sister is Mrs. Mu Gong of Qin.
Chong'er's mother was a woman of the Hu family in Zhai.
Yiwu's mother is the sister of Chong'er's mother.
Duke Xian had eight sons in total. Prince Shen Sheng, Chong'er, and Yi Wu were all virtuous and of high moral character.
After Duke Xiang had Li Ji, he alienated his three sons.
In the 16th year, Duke Xiang of Jin established two armies.
Xian Gong commanded the upper army, Prince Shen Sheng commanded the lower army, Zhao Su drove the chariot, and Bi Wan served as the right guard. They successively conquered and destroyed Huo, Wei, and Geng.
After the whole army returned to Jin, Xian Gong helped the prince build a city in Quwo, gave the land of Geng to Zhao Su, and gave the land of Wei to Bi Wan, making them officials.
summary: After Muhou died, his brother Uncle Shang seized power, forcing Prince Qiu to flee. In the fourth year of Uncle Shang's reign, Prince Qiu attacked and established himself as Wenhou. In Wenhou's 10th year, King You of Zhou was killed, and the Zhou royal family moved eastward. Wenhou's son Zhaohou granted Quwo to his younger brother, who became Uncle Huan of Quwo. Quwo grew larger than the capital, and a gentleman predicted turmoil would originate there. In Zhaohou's seventh year, Pan's father killed Zhaohou and tried to install Uncle Huan, but Jin forces defeated him and established Zhaohou's son as Xiaohou. The conflict between Quwo and Jin continued for generations. Quwo Zhuangbo killed Xiaohou, and later Quwo Wugong killed Aihou and Xiaozi. Finally, in the 28th year of Hou Min, Duke Wu of Quwo destroyed Jin, presented its treasures to King Li of Zhou, and was appointed ruler of Jin. Duke Wu had reigned 37 years in Quwo before becoming Duke Wu of Jin. He died two years after replacing the Jin ruler, and his son Xian Gong succeeded. Duke Xian attacked Li Rong, obtained Li Ji and her sister, and favored them greatly. Li Ji gave birth to Xi Qi. Duke Xian planned to depose Crown Prince Shen Sheng, sending him to garrison Quwo while sending Chong'er and Yiwu elsewhere. Li Ji falsely accused Shen Sheng of poisoning food meant for Duke Xian. Unable to prove his innocence, Shen Sheng committed suicide. Chong'er and Yiwu fled in fear. Duke Xian sent troops against them, and Chong'er escaped to Di while Yiwu fled to Liang.

translation:
Li Ji's sister gave birth to a son.
In the summer of the twenty-sixth year, Duke Huan of Qi held a grand alliance meeting with the princes in Kuiqiu.
Duke Xiang of Jin left late due to illness. Before he arrived at Kuiqiu, he met Zai Kong of Zhou Dynasty.
Zaikong said: Duke Huan of Qi has become more and more arrogant and domineering. He does not try his best to practice virtuous government but tries every means to invade far away places. The princes are not satisfied.
It's better not to go. Duke Huan of Qi can't do anything to Jin.
In addition, Xian Gong was ill and returned to Jin.
Soon, Duke Xiang fell seriously ill, so he said to Xun Xi: I asked Xi Qi to inherit the throne, but he is still young and the ministers are not convinced. I am afraid there will be trouble. Can you support him? Xun Xi said: Yes.
Duke Xian said: "What do you use as proof?"
Xun Xi replied: Even if you come back after death, I will still not feel ashamed when I am alive. This is the proof.
Therefore, Duke Xian entrusted Xi Qi to Xun Xi.
Xun Xi served as the prime minister and presided over state affairs.
In the ninth month of autumn, Duke Xiang passed away.
Rick and Pi Zheng wanted to take Chong'er back and use the three princes' followers to cause trouble, so they said to Xun Xi: The three resentful families are about to cause trouble. There are Qin people outside and Jin people inside to help them. What are you going to do?
Xun Xi said: I cannot break my promise to the late king.
In October, Rick killed Xi Qi in the mourning place. At that time, Duke Xian had not yet been buried.
Xun Xi planned to die, but someone suggested that he should make Xi Qi's younger brother mourn his son and assist him. Xun Xi then made a mourning son and buried Duke Xian.
In November, Rick killed his mourning son in the court, and Xun Xi also committed suicide.
The gentleman said: "The Book of Songs" says that if a white stone has spots, it can be polished, but if it is wrong, it cannot be saved. This is Xun Xi!
Xun Xi did not break his promise.
At the beginning, when Duke Xian was about to attack Li Rong, Turtle Bu said, "Slanderous words can cause harm."
After defeating Li Rong and getting Li Ji, Duke Xian doted on her so much that he actually caused chaos in the Jin Kingdom.
Rick and others have killed Xi Qi and Dao Zi, and sent people to Zhai State to welcome the young master Chong'er, intending to support him.
Chong'er thanked him and said: "I escaped from Jin against my father's orders. After my father passed away, I couldn't attend the funeral according to the etiquette of a son. How could I dare to return to my country and take the throne? Please ask the doctor to appoint someone else instead."
The person sent came back to report to Rick, who sent someone to Liang Kingdom to meet Yi Wu.
Yiwu wanted to return to Jin, but Lu Sheng and Cherui said: "It is hard to believe that there are still young masters in the country who can ascend the throne, but they go abroad to find them."
I guess it would be very dangerous not to go to Qin in order to use the power of a powerful country to return to Jin.
So Yiwu asked Cherui to bribe Qin with generous gifts, and agreed: If I can return to Jin, I am willing to dedicate Hexi of Jin to Qin.
Yiwu also wrote a letter to Rick saying: If I can really ascend the throne, I am willing to seal the city of Fenyang to you.
Duke Mu of Qin sent troops to escort Yi Wu back to Jin.
When Duke Huan of Qi heard about the civil strife in Jin, he also led the princes to Jin.
The Qin army and Yi Wu also arrived at the Jin State at this time. The Qi State asked Peng Peng to join the Qin State in sending Yi Wu back to the Jin State and made him the king of Jin. This is Hui Gong.
Duke Huan of Qi returned to Qi after arriving at Gaoliang of Jin.
In the first year of Yiwu, Hui Gong sent Pi Zheng to apologize to the King of Qin and said: I promised you the land of Hexi. Now I am fortunate to return to the country and become the king.
The minister said: The land was left by the ancestors. You are on the run, so why should you arbitrarily grant it to Qin?
My efforts were in vain, so I apologized to Qin.
At the same time, Yiwu did not grant Fenyang City to Rick, but instead took away his power.
In April, King Zhou Xiang sent Duke Zhou's father-in-law to meet the officials of Qi and Qin to visit Duke Hui of Jin.
Because Chong'er was on the run, Duke Hui was afraid that Rick would launch a coup, so he ordered Rick to die and said to him: Without you Rick, I cannot ascend the throne.
Even so, you have also killed two kings and a high official. Isn’t it too difficult to be your king?
summary: After Duke Xian died, Li Ke killed Xi Qi and his brother, then invited Chong'er to return, but he refused. Yiwu was brought back with Qin's help and became Duke Hui. He broke promises to grant land to Qin and reward Li Ke, instead forcing Li Ke to commit suicide. When Qin suffered famine, Jin refused aid and attacked Qin instead. Duke Hui was captured at the Battle of Han Yuan but later released. After Duke Hui died, his son Duke Huai succeeded but was killed by Qin forces escorting Chong'er back.

translation:
Jie Zitui's followers felt pity for him, so they hung a sign at the entrance of the palace, which read: If a dragon wants to go to heaven, it needs the help of five snakes.
The dragon has gone deep into the clouds, and the four snakes have each entered their own palaces. Only one snake is sad and resentful alone, and ultimately cannot find its own place.
When Duke Wen came out of the palace, he saw these words and said: This is Jie Zitui.
I was worried about the royal family and had not yet been able to consider his merits.
So Duke Wen sent someone to call Jie Zitui, but Jie Zitui had already escaped.
Duke Wen asked about Jie Zitui's residence and heard that he had entered Mianshang Mountain. So, Duke Wen sealed the entire Mianshang Mountain to Jie Zitui, and called it Jie Tui Field as his fief, and named it Jieshan, in order to record my sins and commend talented people.
Uncle Hu, an incompetent man who fled with Duke Wen, said: Your Majesty, you have rewarded the meritorious officials three times but it has not been my turn. May I ask what I am guilty of?
Duke Wen reported back: Teach me with benevolence and righteousness, advise me with morality and kindness, and you should be highly rewarded.
Assisting me with actions finally brought me success, which deserves a lesser reward.
He took on the danger of bows and arrows and made great contributions to me, which should be rewarded again.
If you only use your labor to serve me without making up for my mistakes, you should be rewarded again.
After these three rewards are over, it will be your turn.
The people of Jin were very happy when they heard Duke Wen's words.
In the spring of the second year, the Qin army was stationed by the Yellow River and was about to escort the King of Zhou back to Beijing.
Zhao Shui said: If you want to become the overlord, it is better to escort the King of Zhou back to the capital and respect the King of Zhou.
Zhou and Jin have the same surname. If Jin does not escort King Zhou back to the capital first and falls behind Qin, it will not be able to issue orders in the world.
Today, respecting the king of Zhou is the capital of Jin's dominance.
On the first day of the third month, Jin sent troops to Yangfan, surrounded Wen, and escorted King Xiang of Zhou to the capital of Zhou.
In April, Jin killed Wang Zidai, the younger brother of King Xiang.
King Zhou Xiang gave the land of Hanoi and Yangfan to the State of Jin.
In four years, King Chu Cheng and other princes surrounded Song State. Gongsun Gu of Song State rushed to Jin State to ask for help.
Xian Zhen said: To repay Song Xianggong's kindness of gifting horses and make Jin dominate the princes, this is the battle today.
Hu Yan said: Chu State has just occupied Cao State, and has married Wei State for the first time. If we attack Cao State and Wei State, Chu State will definitely rescue us, and Song State will be saved from disaster.
So the Jin State organized three armies. Zhao Shuai recommended Que Gu to command the middle army, and Que Zhen assisted him; Hu Yan was sent to command the upper army, and Hu Mao assisted him, and Zhao Shuai was appointed minister; Luan Zhi commanded the lower army, and Xian Zhen assisted him;
In December of winter, the Jin army first captured the east of Taihang Mountain and granted the original city to Zhao Shuai.
In the spring of the fifth year, Duke Wen of Jin wanted to attack the state of Cao and asked the state of Wei to borrow a road, but the people of the state of Wei refused.
The Jin army had no choice but to cross the Yellow River from the south to attack Cao State and crusade against Wei State.
summary: Chong'er, Duke Wen, had fled for 19 years, traveling through Di, Qi, Cao, Song, Zheng, Chu, and finally Qin. He returned at age 62 and was welcomed by most Jin people. After securing his position, he rewarded followers but initially forgot Jie Zitui, who hid in Mianshang Mountain and died there. Duke Wen later granted the mountain to Jie Zitui's memory. Duke Wen became hegemon after assisting King Xiang of Zhou and defeating Chu at Chengpu. After his death, his son Duke Xiang succeeded.

translation:
In the fifteenth year, Wei Wenhou ascended the throne.
In the eighteenth year, Duke You raped a woman and went out of the city at night, where he was killed by bandits.
Marquis Wen of Wei sent troops to quell the civil strife in Jin, and appointed Duke You's son Zhi, who was Duke Lie.
In the nineteenth year of Duke Lie, King Weilie of Zhou granted the states of Zhao, Han, and Wei the title of prince, and made them all princes.
In the twenty-seventh year, Lie Gong passed away, and his son Xiao Gongqi came to the throne.
In the ninth year of Duke Xiao's reign, Marquis Wu of Wei had just ascended the throne and attacked Handan. He failed to win and left.
In the seventeenth year, Duke Xiao passed away and his son, Duke Jing, came to the throne.
This year is the first year of King Qi Wei.
In the second year of Jinggong, Marquis Wu of Wei, Marquis Han Ai, and Marquis Zhao Jing destroyed the Jin Kingdom and divided the Jin land into three parts.
Jinggong became a commoner, and the state of Jin stopped offering sacrifices.
Tai Shigong said: Jin Wengong was a wise monarch in ancient times. He lived in exile for nineteen years and lived in extreme poverty. When he came to the throne, he gave rewards and forgot about Jie Zitui. What about those arrogant and extravagant monarchs?
After Duke Linggong was killed, Duke Cheng and Duke Jin were extremely strict, and Duke Li was even more harsh. The officials were afraid of execution, so troubles occurred frequently.
After the mourning of Duke Jin, the state of Jin became weaker and weaker day by day, and the six ministers took over the power exclusively.
Therefore, it is not easy for a king to control his subjects!
summary: The text continues through many generations of Jin rulers, including Duke Ling (who was killed for his tyranny), Duke Cheng, Duke Jing, Duke Li, and Duke Mourning. The power of the six ministerial families grew while the ducal house weakened. Eventually, Zhao, Han, and Wei divided Jin among themselves. In the second year of Duke Jing, these three families destroyed Jin, reduced the duke to commoner status, and ended the state's sacrifices.

translation:
Cao Shen, Marquis of Pingyang, was born in Peixian County.
During the Qin Dynasty, Cao Shen served as the warden of Peixian County, and Xiao He was the chief official. They were already well-known officials in the county.
When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was the Duke of Pei, Cao Shen followed him as Zhongjuan.
Cao Shen led his army to attack Huling and Fangyu, and attacked the Qin Dynasty's county supervisors' army, greatly defeating the enemy.
He took Xuexian County to the east and attacked the army of the Sishui County Governor to the west of the outer city of Xuexian County.
Then he attacked Huling and successfully captured it.
Cao Shen led his army to move to guard Fang Yu.
Fang Yu had rebelled and surrendered to the king of Wei, so Cao Shen attacked Fang Yu.
Fengyi also rebelled and surrendered to the king of Wei, and Cao Shen went to attack Fengyi again.
Duke Pei bestowed upon Cao Shen the title of Seventh Doctor.
Cao Shen attacked Qin Dynasty Sima Yí's army east of Dang County, defeated him, and captured Shanzhiyi in Dang County, Hufu County, and Qi County.
Cao Shen then attacked the area west of Xiayi, as far as Yu County, and attacked Zhang Han's army.
When attacking Yuan Qi and Kang Fu, Cao Shen was the first to climb the tower.
Cao Shen was promoted to the fifth official position.
He went north to rescue Dong'a, attacked Zhang Han's army, captured Chen County, and pursued to Puyang.
He attacked Dingtao and captured Linji.
He went south to rescue Yongqiu, attacked Li You's army, defeated it, killed Li You, and captured one of the Qin Dynasty's military commanders.
At this time, Qin general Zhang Han defeated Xiang Liang's army and killed Xiang Liang. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu led their troops back east.
King Chu Huai appointed Pei Gong as the governor of Dang County and commanded the army of Dang County.
Peigong granted Cao Shen the title of Silk Holder and was known as Jiancheng Lord.
Later, Cao Shen was promoted to the magistrate of Yuanqi County and was subordinate to Dang County.
From there, Cao Shen followed Pei Gong to attack the army of the prefect of Dongjun and defeated the enemy south of Chengwu.
They attacked Wang Li's army in the south of Chengyang and fought Wang Li's army in Gangli, defeating them severely.
Chasing the fleeing enemy troops, he went west to Kaifeng, attacked Zhao Bi's army, defeated it, and surrounded Zhao Bi in the city of Kaifeng.
Going west, he encountered the Qin Dynasty general Yang Xiong's army in Qu, defeated it, and captured one of the Qin Dynasty's Sima and Yushi.
Cao Shen was promoted to Zhigui and followed Pei Gong to attack Yangwu, captured the Yuan and Feng clans, blocked the Yellow River ferry, returned to attack Zhao Ben's army, and defeated it to the north of Xixiang.
Following Pei Gong, he went south to attack Jiyi, and fought with Lu Xun, the governor of Nanyang County, east of the outer city of Yangcheng. He broke through Lu Xun's army, captured Wan County, captured Lu Xun, and completely pacified Nanyang County.
Following Pei Gong, he went west to attack Wuguan and Yaoguan, and captured these two passes.
He first attacked the Qin army in the south of Lantian, and then attacked the north of Lantian at night, defeating the Qin army. Then he reached Xianyang and destroyed the Qin Dynasty.
After Xiang Yu came to Guanzhong, he named Liu Bang King of Han.
The king of Han granted Cao Shen the title of Marquis of Jiancheng.
Cao Shen followed the King of Han to Guanzhong and was promoted to general.
summary: Cao Shen, Marquis of Pingyang, was born in Peixian County and served as a warden there during the Qin Dynasty. He followed Emperor Gaozu of Han (then Duke of Pei) as a Zhongjuan, leading military campaigns against Qin forces, including attacks on Huling, Fangyu, Xuexian, and Dang County. He defeated generals such as Zhang Han, Li You, and Wang Li, capturing cities and officials. After Xiang Yu named Liu Bang King of Han, Cao Shen was granted the title Marquis of Jiancheng and later promoted to general. He helped pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, capturing territories like Xiabian and Yongxian, and besieged Zhang Han in Feiqiu.

translation:
The state of Qi was pacified and more than seventy counties were obtained in total.
They captured the Prime Minister Tian Guang of the former Qi King Tian Guang, Xu Zhang who stayed behind in place of the Prime Minister, and the former Qi State Jiaodong General Tian Ji.
Han Xin became the king of Qi, led his troops to Chen County, joined the king of Han, and defeated Xiang Yu together, while Cao Shen stayed to pacify the unconquered areas of Qi.
Xiang Yu was dead, the world was at peace, the King of Han became emperor, Han Xin was renamed King of Chu, and the state of Qi was divided into counties.
Cao Shen returned the seal of the Han Prime Minister.
Emperor Gao made his eldest son Liu Fei the King of Qi and appointed Cao Shen as the Prime Minister of Qi.
In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the titles of the princes were enfeoffed. The imperial court and the princes cut the talismans as proof, so that the titles of the enfeoffed persons could be passed down from generation to generation without being extinguished.
Emperor Gaozu granted Cao Shen 10,630 households in Pingyang as a fiefdom, with the title Marquis of Pingyang, and took back the fiefdoms previously entrusted to Cao Shen.
As the Prime Minister of Qi, Cao Shen led troops to attack Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun's army and defeated the enemy.
Yingbu rebelled. As the Prime Minister of Qi, Cao Shen followed Qi Hui King Liu Fei and led 120,000 troops. Together with Gaozu, he attacked Yingbu's army and defeated the enemy.
They marched southward to Qi County, then returned to the army and pacified Zhuyi, Xiangxian, Xiaoxian and Liuxian.
Cao Shen's achievements: he conquered two vassal states and 122 counties in total; captured two vassal kings, three prime ministers of the vassal states, six generals, and one each of the county guard, Sima, military marquis, and censor.
In the first year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, he abolished the decree of establishing a prime minister's state in the vassal states and appointed Cao Shen as the prime minister of Qi.
When Cao Shen was the prime minister of Qi, there were seventy cities in Qi.
At that time, the world had just been peaceful, and King Huihui was very young. Cao Shen summoned the elderly and scholars to ask for ways to appease the people. But there were hundreds of scholars in Qi State, and they had different opinions. Cao Shen didn't know how to make a decision.
He heard that there was a Duke Gai in Jiaoxi who studied Huang Lao's theory intensively, so he sent someone to invite him with generous gifts.
After meeting Gai Gong, Gai Gong told Cao Shen that the most important way to govern the country is to be pure and inactive, allowing the people to settle down on their own. He recommended similar things in this regard and stated them all to Cao Shen.
Cao Shen then gave up his main hall and let Gai Gong live in it.
From then on, Cao Shen's method of governing the country was to adopt Huang Lao's teachings, so he served as the prime minister of Qi for nine years. The country of Qi was stable, and people greatly praised him as a wise prime minister.
In the second year of Emperor Hui's reign, Xiao He passed away.
When Cao Shen heard the news, he told his disciples to pack their bags quickly and said: I am going to the court to become the prime minister.
Soon after, people sent by the imperial court came to summon Cao Shen.
When Cao Shen left, he told the subsequent prime minister of Qi: The prison lawsuits and markets of Qi should be regarded as the sustenance of certain people's actions. These actions should be treated with caution and not interfere easily.
The later prime minister said: Is there nothing more important than governing the country? Cao Shen said: That's not the case.
summary: Cao Shen served as acting Prime Minister Zuo, suppressing rebellions by King Bao of Wei and others, capturing Wei and Zhao territories. He followed Han Xin to defeat Qi, pacifying over seventy counties. After Xiang Yu's death, Cao Shen became Prime Minister of Qi under King Liu Fei, governing with Huang Lao principles of purity and inaction for nine years, stabilizing the state. When Xiao He died, Cao Shen succeeded him as Han Prime Minister, adhering strictly to Xiao He's laws without changes. He selected steady officials, dismissed those seeking reputation, and spent his time drinking, avoiding interference in minor affairs. When Emperor Hui questioned his governance, Cao Shen argued that following the established laws of Emperor Gaozu and Xiao He was sufficient.

translation:
Cao Shen served as the Prime Minister of the Han Dynasty for three years.
After his death, he was posthumously named Yihou.
Cao Shen's son, Cao Cheng, succeeded his father as the marquis.
The common people praised Cao Shen's deeds and said: Xiao He formulated laws that were clear and consistent; Cao Shen succeeded Xiao He as prime minister and abided by Xiao He's laws without changing them.
Cao Shen implemented his pure and inactive approach, and the people were peaceful and undisturbed.
Cao Cheng, Marquis of Pingyang, was the imperial censor at that time.
Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne and was dismissed as a marquis.
Cao Cheng died after 29 years as a marquis, and his posthumous title was Jinghou.
Cao Cheng's son Cao Qi took over the throne and died after seven years of service. His posthumous title was Marquis Jian.
Cao Qi's son Cao Shi succeeded him.
Cao Shi married Princess Pingyang and gave birth to a son, Cao Xiang.
Cao Shi got sick and returned to the feudal country.
Cao Shi died in his 23rd year as a Marquis, and his posthumous title was Yihou.
Cao Shi's son Cao Xiang succeeded him.
Cao Xiang married Princess Wei Chang and had a son, Cao Zong.
Cao Xiang died in his sixteenth year as a marquis, and his posthumous title was Gonghou.
Cao Xiang's son Cao Zong succeeded him.
In the second year of Zhenghe, Cao Zong was implicated in the mutiny launched by Emperor Wu's crown prince. He was convicted and executed, and the feudal state was abolished.
Tai Shigong said: The reason why Cao Shen, the Prime Minister of Cao, has so many military exploits is because he worked with Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin.
When Han Xin was eliminated, only Cao Shen was credited with the military exploits accomplished by other princes.
As the prime minister of the Han Dynasty, Cao Shen strongly advocated purity and inaction, which was completely in line with Taoist doctrine.
After the people suffered from the cruel rule of the Qin Dynasty, Cao Shen gave them a chance to recuperate, so everyone in the world praised his virtue.
summary: Cao Shen served as Prime Minister for three years, dying with the posthumous title Yihou. His descendants inherited the title until Cao Zong was executed for involvement in a mutiny, ending the feudal state. The people praised Cao Shen for maintaining Xiao He's clear laws and allowing peace through non-interference.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/曹相国世家

translation:
Liang Xiaowang Liu Wu was the son of Emperor Xiaowen and his half-brother to Emperor Xiaojing.
His mother is Queen Mother Dou.
Emperor Xiaowen had four sons: the eldest son was the prince, who was Emperor Xiaojing; the second son was named Wu; the third son was named Ginseng; and the fourth son was named Mingsheng.
In the second year after Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, he named Liu Wu the acting king, Liu Shen the king of Taiyuan, and Liu Sheng the king of Liang.
Two years later, Emperor Wen changed the title of King Dai to King of Huaiyang.
All the fiefdoms of Dai State were assigned to King Taiyuan, and he was named King of Dai.
Liu Shen reigned for seventeen years and died in the second year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign. His posthumous title was King Xiao.
Liu Deng, the son of King Xiao, succeeded to the throne and became King Dai Gong.
King Dai Gong reigned for twenty-nine years and died in the second year of Emperor Wu Yuanguang's reign.
Liu Yi, the son of King Gong, succeeded to the throne and is the current acting king.
Nineteen years later, the Han Dynasty expanded the pass, with Changshan as the boundary, and moved King Dai to King Qinghe.
The relocation took place in the third year of Emperor Wu Yuanding's reign.
Initially, in the tenth year when Liu Wu was granted the title of King of Huaiyang, King Liu Sheng of Liang passed away, and his posthumous title was King Huai of Liang.
King Huai was the youngest son of Emperor Xiaowen and was favored more than the other sons.
The next year, Emperor Wen changed the title of King Liu Wu of Huaiyang to King of Liang.
Liu Wu was first granted the title of Prince of Liang in the twelfth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign.
It took eleven years from the time when King Liang was first named King of Dai to when he was changed to King of Liang.
In the fourteenth year of King Liang's reign, he entered the dynasty.
In the seventeenth and eighteenth years, he entered the court for two consecutive years and stayed in the capital. He did not return to his feudal country until the second year.
In the twenty-first year, he entered the court again.
In the twenty-second year, Emperor Xiaowen died.
He entered the DPRK in the twenty-fourth year and entered the DPRK again in the twenty-fifth year.
At that time, Emperor Jing had not yet established a prince.
When the Emperor was having a banquet with the King of Liang, he once said in a casual conversation: After thousands of years, I will pass on you, the King of Liang.
After hearing this, King Liang quickly declined.
Although he knew that what Emperor Jing said was not true, he was secretly happy.
The Queen Mother was equally happy.
That spring, the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao rebelled.
Wu and Chu first attacked Liang's Jibi and killed tens of thousands of people.
King Xiao of Liang guarded Suiyang City and appointed Han Anguo, Zhang Yu and others as generals to resist the troops of Wu and Chu.
Wu and Chu were blocked by Liang and did not dare to cross the Liang Kingdom to march westward. They had a stalemate with Taiwei Yafu and others for three months.
Wu and Chu were destroyed, and the number of Wu and Chu troops killed and captured by Liang was roughly as many as the imperial court. The following year, the imperial court established a prince.
Later, because the King of Liang was the emperor's brother and had made great achievements, he was granted the title of a great country and occupied the fertile land in the world.
Its fiefdom is bounded by Mount Tai in the north and reaches Gaoyang in the west. There are more than 40 cities in total, most of which are large counties.
King Xiao of Liang was the youngest son of Empress Dowager Dou. He was very favored and received countless rewards.
Therefore, King Xiao of Liang built Dongyuan with a radius of more than 300 miles and expanded Suiyang City to 70 miles.
summary: Liu Wu, King Xiao of Liang, was the son of Emperor Xiaowen and half-brother to Emperor Xiaojing, with Queen Mother Dou as his mother. Emperor Xiaowen had four sons: the eldest became Emperor Xiaojing; Liu Wu was the second, followed by Liu Shen and Liu Mingsheng. Liu Wu was initially made acting king, later King of Huaiyang, and eventually King of Liang in the twelfth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign. He ruled for eleven years from his first title as King of Dai to becoming King of Liang. During his reign, he frequently entered the court, staying in the capital for extended periods. Emperor Jing once casually promised to pass the throne to him, which secretly pleased Liu Wu and the Queen Mother. In the spring of the rebellion of the seven kingdoms, Wu and Chu attacked Liang, killing tens of thousands. King Xiao defended Suiyang with generals like Han Anguo, blocking Wu and Chu from advancing westward. After three months of stalemate with Taiwei Yafu, Wu and Chu were destroyed, with Liang's casualties and captures roughly equal to the imperial court's. The following year, a prince was established. Due to his merits and relation to the emperor, King Xiao was granted a large, fertile fiefdom with over forty cities. He was deeply favored by Empress Dowager Dou, receiving countless rewards. He built Dongyuan over 300 li in radius, expanded Suiyang City to 70 li, and constructed palaces and elevated passages over 30 li long. His splendor rivaled an emperor's, with banners, thousands of attendants, and hunting expeditions. Heroes and lobbyists from across the country, including Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui, flocked to Liang. Gongsun Gui, given a thousand pieces of gold and a lieutenant position, was called General Gongsun. Liang forged many weapons and amassed nearly a trillion in money, plus countless jewels.

translation:
A great deal of construction work was carried out, palaces were built, and overhead passages were built, which were more than thirty miles long from the palace to the platform.
There are banners awarded by the emperor, and thousands of people are accompanying them when they go out.
Horses are galloping and hunting everywhere, and the splendor of the scene is like that of an emperor.
When entering and exiting the palace, pedestrians are prohibited from clearing the road, and people are warned and warned.
The heroes from all over the country and the lobbyists from the east of Mount Laoshan, such as Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, Zou Yang and others from Qi, all returned to Liang.
Gongsun Guiduo had many strange and bizarre plans. When he first visited the King of Liang, the King of Liang gave him a thousand pieces of gold and an official position of lieutenant. The Liang State called him General Gongsun. The Liang Kingdom forged many weapons, including hundreds of thousands of bows, arrows, and spears. The treasury had nearly one trillion yuan in money, and there were even more pearls, jade, and treasures in the capital.
In October of the 29th year, King Xiao of Liang came to Beijing to meet Emperor Jing.
Emperor Jing sent an envoy to hold the talisman and drive the emperor's horse-drawn carriage to the pass to greet King Liang.
After meeting Emperor Jing, he submitted a memorial requesting to stay in the capital, and was allowed to do so because the Queen Mother loved Prince Xiao very much.
When King Xiao entered the palace, he accompanied Emperor Jing on a chariot. When he left the palace, he went hunting with the chariot and went to Shanglin Garden to shoot birds and beasts.
Liang Guo's ministers, Langguan, and visitors only need to register their names in the name book so that they can enter and leave the emperor's palace, no different from the officials of the imperial court.
In November, the emperor deposed Prince Li, and Empress Dowager Dou wanted to make Prince Xiao his successor.
The ministers, Yuan An and others dissuaded Emperor Jing, and Empress Dowager Dou's motion was blocked. From then on, she no longer mentioned the matter of making Prince Liang his successor.
Because this matter is very secret, no one in the world knows about it.
The King of Liang then bid farewell to the court and returned to the feudal state.
In April of this summer, the emperor made King Jiaodong the crown prince.
The King of Liang resented Yuan An and the ministers who participated in the heir discussion, so he planned with Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and others to secretly assassinate Yuan An and more than ten other ministers who participated in the heir discussion.
The court searched for the murderer, but failed to find it.
So the emperor suspected King Liang and captured the murderer, who was indeed the mastermind.
So Emperor Jing sent envoys constantly on the road to Liang State, where they repeatedly conducted inspections and arrested Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng.
Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng were hiding in the harem of King Liang.
The envoy was urgent to question the officials of Erqianshi. Liang Xiangxuan Qiu Bao and Nei Shi Han Anguo came to admonish the king of Liang. The king of Liang ordered Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to commit suicide, and then handed them over.
The emperor resented King Liang for this.
The King of Liang was frightened, so he sent Han Anguo to confess to the Queen Mother through the eldest princess and ask for forgiveness, and then he was forgiven.
The emperor's anger gradually dissipated, and King Liang wrote a letter requesting an audience.
After arriving at Hangu Pass, Mao Lan persuaded King Liang to take a cloth chariot and bring only two cavalry to the capital, hiding in the eldest princess's garden.
The imperial court sent envoys to welcome King Liang, but King Liang had already entered the pass. All his entourage, chariots and horses were outside the pass, and he did not know where he was.
summary: In October of the 29th year, King Xiao visited Emperor Jing, who sent an imperial carriage to greet him. He requested to stay in the capital, which was granted due to the Queen Mother's love. He accompanied the emperor in chariots and hunted at Shanglin Garden. Liang's ministers could enter the palace freely. In November, after the prince was deposed, the Queen Mother wanted King Xiao as successor, but ministers like Yuan An dissuaded Emperor Jing, blocking the motion. The matter remained secret. King Xiao then returned to his state. In April, the emperor made King Jiaodong the crown prince. Resentful, King Xiao plotted with Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to assassinate Yuan An and over ten other ministers. The court failed to find the murderer initially but eventually suspected King Xiao. After capturing the assassins, the emperor sent envoys to Liang, arresting Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng, who hid in the harem. Liang's officials urged the king to have them commit suicide, which he did. The emperor remained resentful, but after Han Anguo pleaded for forgiveness through the eldest princess, King Xiao was forgiven. He later entered the capital in disguise, hiding in the eldest princess's garden, causing the Queen Mother to weep, thinking the emperor had killed him. King Xiao then confessed, and brotherly relations were restored, though the emperor gradually alienated him.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家

translation:
The Queen Mother cried: Your Majesty killed my son!
Emperor Jing was worried about this.
So the King of Liang, carrying the instrument of torture on his back, prostrated himself before the palace gate, confessed his crime and asked for punishment. The Queen Mother and Emperor Jing were very happy, and wept relative to each other. The brotherhood was as good as before.
Then the officials accompanying King Liang were summoned into the pass.
However, Emperor Jing gradually alienated King Liang and no longer rode with him in chariots.
In the winter of the thirty-fifth year, King Liang went to Beijing again to see the emperor.
He submitted a memorial requesting to retain the capital, but the emperor did not agree.
After King Liang returned to his feudal state, he felt confused and depressed.
When he went hunting in the Liangshan Mountains in the north, someone offered him a cow. The cow's feet were long on his back. King Xiao was disgusted by it.
In mid-June, King Liang fell ill with fever and died six days later. His posthumous title is King Xiao.
King Xiao of Liang was very filial. Every time he heard that the Queen Mother was ill and couldn't eat or sleep well, he often wanted to stay in Chang'an to serve the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother also loved him.
When she learned that King Liang had died, Empress Dowager Dou cried very sadly and refused to eat or drink, saying: Your Majesty really killed my son!
Emperor Jing was sad and worried about it, and didn't know what to do.
Emperor Jing discussed with the eldest princess and divided the Liang Kingdom into five kingdoms. All five sons of King Xiao were granted the title of king, and all five daughters were also granted the title of Tang Muyi to them.
After reporting these measures to the Queen Mother, the Queen Mother became happy and added an extra meal because of Emperor Jing's treatment.
The eldest son of King Liang Xiao, Liu Mai, inherited the throne and was named the King of Gong; the second son, Liu Ming, was named the King of Jichuan; the third son, Liu Pengli, was named the King of Jidong; the fourth son, Liu Ding, was named the King of Shanyang; and the youngest son, Liu Bushi, was named the King of Jiyin.
Before the death of King Xiao of Liang, his property amounted to hundreds of millions and was incalculable.
After his death, there were still more than 400,000 kilograms of gold left in his treasury, and other properties were also equivalent to this.
In the third year of Liang Gong's reign, Emperor Jing died.
King Gong died after reigning for seven years and was succeeded by his son Liu Xiang, who became King Ping.
In the fourteenth year of Liang Ping King Liu Xiang's reign, Liang Ping King's mother was the Queen Mother Chen.
The mother of King Gong is Queen Mother Li.
Queen Mother Li is the biological grandmother of Prince Ping.
King Ping's queen's surname was Ren, and she was called Queen Ren.
Queen Ren was very favored by King Ping Liu Xiang.
At first, when King Xiao was still alive, he had a bottle worth thousands of gold.
King Xiao warned his descendants to take good care of the bottle and not give it to others.
After Queen Ren heard about it, she wanted to get the bottle.
The Queen Mother Li, the grandmother of King Ping, said: The late king had a will not to give away the bottles to others.
Even if other things are worth hundreds of millions, you can take them for yourself.
Queen Ren insisted on getting this bottle.
King Ping Liu Xiang directly asked people to open the treasury to get the bottles and gave them to Queen Ren.
summary: In the winter of the 35th year, King Xiao visited again but was denied permission to stay. After returning, he became depressed. While hunting, a cow with feet on its back disgusted him. He fell ill with fever in mid-June and died six days later, posthumously titled King Xiao. He was filial, often wanting to serve the Queen Mother when she was ill. Her grief was immense, but Emperor Jing divided Liang into five kingdoms, granting all five sons and five daughters titles, which pleased her. King Xiao's eldest son, Liu Mai, inherited as King Gong; others became kings of Jichuan, Jidong, Shanyang, and Jiyin. His wealth was immense, with over 400,000 kilograms of gold left after death.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/梁孝王世家

translation:
Empress Dowager Li was furious. The imperial envoy came to the Liang Kingdom. Empress Dowager Li wanted to tell the envoy personally about the matter. King Ping Liu Xiang and Queen Ren stopped her and closed the door. Empress Dowager Li struggled to open the door, and her fingers were caught in the crack of the door. Finally, she could not see the envoy from the imperial court.
Empress Dowager Li secretly committed adultery with the Chief Food Officer and the doctor Yin Ba, so King Ping and Queen Ren sent people to dissuade Empress Dowager Li with this hint. Empress Dowager Li gave up because of her lewd behavior.
Later, Queen Mother Li died of illness.
When she was ill, Queen Ren did not ask for her health; after her death, she did not pay homage to her.
During the Yuanshuo period, there was a Suiyang man named Lei Anfan. Someone insulted his father. This man went out in the same car with the retainer of the Huaiyang prefect. The prefect's retainer got out of the car and left. Lei Anfan killed his enemy in the car and ran away.
The governor of Huaiyang was furious and blamed Liang Guo's two thousand stone officials.
Officials with less than 2,000 dan were very urgent to arrest the rebels, so they arrested the relatives of the rebels.
Lei Lian knew the secrets in Liang's palace, so he reported to the court in detail the events surrounding the dispute between King Ping and his grandmother over the Lei Zun.
At that time, officials below the prime minister knew about this incident and wanted to use it to attack the senior officials of Liang State, so they submitted a petition to the emperor.
The emperor handed the matter over to the officials for investigation and interrogation, and it was indeed true.
The minister asked the emperor to depose King Ping Liu Xiang and make him a commoner.
The Emperor said: Empress Dowager Li committed adultery, and Liang Wang Liu Xiang did not have a good master, so she fell into such an unjust situation.
So the fiefdoms of eight cities in Liang were reduced, and Queen Ren was beheaded in the city.
There are still ten cities left in the Liang Kingdom.
Liu Xiang died in the 39th year of his reign and was posthumously named King Ping.
His son Liu Wushang was established as King of Liang.
King Liu Ming of Jichuan was the second son of King Xiao of Liang. In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was granted the title of King of Jichuan by the Marquis of Huanyi.
Seven years later, due to the crime of shooting the lieutenant, the relevant officials in the court petitioned to kill King Jichuan. The emperor could not bear to kill him, so he deposed Liu Ming as a civilian and demoted him to Fangling. The fiefdom belonged to the court and became a county.
King Liu Pengli of Jidong was the son of King Xiao of Liang. He was named King of Jidong in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
Twenty-nine years later, Liu Pengli was arrogant and fierce, without the demeanor of a human king. He secretly went out at night with dozens of his slaves and desperate youths to rob, kill, and plunder other people's property for fun.
More than a hundred people were found to have been killed by him. The whole country knew about it and no one dared to go out at night.
The son of the man he killed wrote a letter to report.
Relevant officials in the imperial court petitioned to have him executed. The emperor couldn't bear it and deposed him as a commoner and demoted him to Shangyong. The fiefdom belonged to the imperial court and became Dahe County.
Liu Ding, the Ai King of Shanyang, was the son of Liang Xiaozi. He was named King of Shanyang in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
After reigning for nine years, he died without a son. The feudal state was abolished and the land belonged to the imperial court and became Shanyang County.
Liu Bushi, the Ai King of Jiyin, was the son of King Xiao of Liang. He was named King of Jiyin in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
He died after one year in office without any sons. The feudal state was abolished and the land belonged to the imperial court and became Jiyin County.
Tai Shigong said: Although King Xiao of Liang was granted the title of king in a fertile land because he was the brother of the emperor and the beloved son of the queen mother, he also coincided with the prosperity of the country and the prosperity of the people, so he was able to accumulate wealth, expand the palace, and his carriages, horses and clothing were similar to those of the emperor.
summary: King Gong died after seven years, succeeded by his son Liu Xiang as King Ping. A dispute over a valuable bottle led to conflict between King Ping, his grandmother Queen Mother Li, and Queen Ren. Queen Ren took the bottle despite Queen Mother Li's objections. Queen Mother Li later died, with Queen Ren neglecting her in illness and death. A man named Lei Anfan, seeking revenge, revealed palace secrets to the court. Investigations confirmed Queen Mother Li's adultery and King Ping's mismanagement. The emperor reduced Liang's fiefdom by eight cities and executed Queen Ren. Liu Xiang died after 39 years, succeeded by his son Liu Wushang. Other sons of King Xiao faced fates: Liu Ming was deposed for shooting a lieutenant; Liu Pengli was deposed for robbery and murder; Liu Ding died without an heir; Liu Bushi died after one year without an heir. Their fiefdoms became counties.

translation:
As the saying goes: Arrogant children do not know how to be filial.
This is a good thing to say. Therefore, we should set up good masters and tutors for the princes and kings, and let loyal and upright people to speak out to assist them, just like Ji An, Han Changru and others. If they dare to speak out and give advice, how can disaster happen?
I heard that Prince Liang went to the capital to pay homage to the Empress Dowager Dou, and his family members met each other. He and Emperor Jing sat together in front of the Empress Dowager, and their mother, son, and brothers happily exchanged intimate words.
The Queen Mother said to Emperor Jing: I heard that the system of the Yin and Shang Dynasties respected their brothers, and the system of the Zhou Dynasty respected their ancestors. This principle is the same.
A hundred years later, I entrust King Liang Xiao to you.
Emperor Jing knelt on the seat, raised his body and said, "Yes."
After leaving the palace after the banquet, Emperor Jing summoned Yuan An and other ministers who were proficient in Confucian classics and said: "What does the Queen Mother mean when she says such a thing?"
Yuan Ang and others all replied: The Queen Mother wants to make Prince Liang the emperor's crown prince.
Emperor Jing asked about the reason, and Yuan Ang and others said: According to the tradition of the Yin and Shang Dynasties, one's brothers are close to each other, so the inheritance is passed down to his younger brothers.
The tradition of the Zhou Dynasty respected its ancestors, so it was passed down to their sons.
The tradition of the Yin and Shang Dynasties advocates simplicity. Simplicity means imitating heaven and being close to relatives, so it is passed down to the younger brother.
The tradition of the Zhou Dynasty advocates beauty, and beauty imitates the earth. Zun means respect, respecting its origin, so it is passed down to the eldest son.
According to the system of the Zhou Dynasty, when the prince dies, a legitimate grandson is established.
According to the system of the Yin Dynasty, when the prince dies, his younger brother is appointed.
Emperor Jing said: What do you think?
Everyone answered together: The current system of the Han Dynasty is modeled after the Zhou Dynasty. The system of the Zhou Dynasty cannot establish brothers, but should establish sons.
Because of this, "Spring and Autumn" accused Song Xuangong of this.
After Song Xuangong died, he passed the throne to his younger brother instead of having a son.
After his brother succeeded to the throne and died, the throne was given to his elder brother's son.
His younger brother's son fought for the throne and thought he should succeed his father, so he killed Xuangong's son.
So the country was in chaos. Disasters continue.
Therefore, "Spring and Autumn" says: A gentleman respects and follows the right path, and the chaos in the Song Dynasty was caused by Duke Xuan.
The ministers and others asked to see the Queen Mother to explain this truth.
Yuan An and others went to the palace to see the Queen Mother and said: The Queen Mother said that she would establish King Liang. So, who will be established after King Liang dies?
The Queen Mother said: I will raise the emperor's son again.
Yuan An and others stated the following historical facts to the Queen Mother: Duke Xuangong of the Song Dynasty did not establish a legitimate son who should succeed to the throne, which led to troubles. The troubles lasted for five generations without ending, and failure to restrain petty selfishness would harm the great righteousness.
After hearing this, the Queen Mother understood the truth and was happy. She immediately asked King Liang to return to the feudal country.
When the King of Liang heard that this opinion came from Yuan An and other ministers, he became resentful of them and sent people to kill Yuan An.
summary: Tai Shigong noted that King Xiao's wealth and splendor, though due to his position and the prosperous times, constituted transgression. Chu Shaosun added that the trouble stemmed from the court's failure to properly address succession issues, with ministers like Yuan Ang and Dou Ying providing wise counsel. He emphasized the importance of adhering to ritual and law, as exemplified by the Han system of limited court visits. The Queen Mother's desire to make King Xiao heir was ultimately thwarted by ministers citing historical precedents, such as the chaos in Song caused by Duke Xuan. After the assassination of Yuan An, the case was handled by officials who burned evidence, preserving King Xiao's reputation and calming the Queen Mother.
