translation:
The ancestors of the Chu State came from Gaoyang, Emperor Zhuanxu.
Gao Yang is the grandson of Huangdi and the son of Changyi.
Gao Yang gave birth to Cheng, Cheng gave birth to Juan Zhang, and Juan Zhang gave birth to Chong Li.
Chongli became the Huozheng of Emperor Ku's Gaoxin family. He was very meritorious and could illuminate the world. Emperor Ku gave him the title of Zhu Rong.
The Gonggong clan launched a civil strife, and Emperor Ku asked Chong Li to kill the rebels, but he did not kill them all.
Emperor Ku killed Chongli on the day of Gengyin, and asked his younger brother Wu Hui to succeed Chongli and also take up the post of Huozheng, still called Zhurong.
Wu Hui gave birth to Lu Zhong.
Lu Zhong had six sons, all born by caesarean section.
The eldest son is called Kunwu, the second son is called Shenhu, the third son is called Pengzu, the fourth son is called Huiren, the fifth son is named Cao, the sixth son is named Jilian, and Jilian's surname is Mi. He is the ancestor of the Chu king's family.
Kunwu once served as Hou Bo during the Xia and Shang Dynasties, but was destroyed by Tang during the Jie Dynasty.
Peng Zu once served as Hou Bo during the Yin Dynasty. At the end of the Yin Dynasty, Peng Zu was destroyed.
Ji Lian gave birth to Fuju, and Fuju gave birth to Cave Bear.
His descendants declined midway. Some were in the Central Plains, and some were in barbarians, and history books failed to record their lineages.
During the reign of King Wen of Zhou Dynasty, there was a descendant of Ji Lian called Wan Xiong.
Wu Xiong served King Wen like a son and died young.
His son's name is Xiong Li.
Xiong Li gave birth to Xiong Kuang, and Xiong Kuang gave birth to Xiong Yi.
Xiong Yi was in the era of King Cheng of Zhou Dynasty. King Cheng wanted to use the descendants of the heroes of King Wen and King Wu, so he granted Xiong Yi the title of baron in Chu Man. His surname was Mi and he lived in Danyang.
Xiong Yi, the son of Chu, served the king together with Bo Qin, the Duke of Lu, Zi Mou, the uncle of Wei Kang, Xie, the Marquis of Jin, and Lu Ji, the prince of Qi.
Xiong Yi gave birth to Xiong Ai, Xiong Ai gave birth to Xiong Ai, and Xiong Ai gave birth to Xiong Sheng.
Xiong Sheng made his younger brother Xiong Yang his successor.
Xiong Yang gave birth to Xiong Qu.
Xiong Qu has three sons.
During the reign of King Zhou Yi, the Zhou royal family declined. Some princes refused to pay homage to the emperor, and the princes attacked each other.
Xiong Qu won the support of the people along the Yangtze River and Han River, so he sent troops to attack Yong and Yang Yue, all the way to Hubei.
Xiong Qu said: I am located in a barbarian land, so I don’t have to have the same names and posthumous titles as those of other countries in the Central Plains.
So he named his eldest son Xiong Kang King of Judan, his second son Xiong Hong as King of E, and his youngest son Xiong Zhizhen as King of Yue Zhang, all in the Chuman area along the Yangtze River.
When King Li of Zhou came to power, Xiong Qu was worried that King Li would attack Chu due to his violent temper, so he removed his title as king.
Xiong Qu's successor was his eldest son Xiong Wukang, who died early.
After Xiong Qu's death, his second son Xiong Zhihong came to the throne.
Zhihong's younger brother killed him and took the throne himself. This was Xiong Yan.
Xiong Yan gave birth to Xiong Yong.
In the sixth year of Xiong Yong's reign, the Zhou people provoked civil strife and attacked King Li, who was forced to flee to Pig.
Xiong Yong reigned for ten years, passed away, and his younger brother Xiong Yan succeeded to the throne.
Xiong Yan reigned for ten years and passed away.
Xiong Yan has four sons, the eldest son is called Bo Shuang, the second son is called Zhong Xue, the second son is called Shu Kan, and the younger son is called Ji Liu.
Xiong Yan passed away. The eldest son Bo Shuang came to the throne, this is Xiong Shuang.
In the first year of Xiong Shuang, King Xuan of Zhou just ascended the throne.
Xiong Shuang died after six years of reign, and his three younger brothers competed with each other for the throne.
Zhongxue died, Shukan fled to Pu, and his youngest brother Ji Liu came to the throne, this is Xiong Liu.
In the sixteenth year of Xiong's reign, Duke Huan of Zheng had just been granted a title to Zheng.
In the 22nd year, Xiong You passed away and his son Xiong Ji came to the throne.
Xiong Jie passed away in the ninth year of his reign, and his son Xiong Yi came to the throne. This is Ruao.
In the 20th year of Ruao Ao, King You of Zhou was killed by Quan Rong, the capital of Zhou moved eastward, and Duke Xiang of Qin began to become a vassal.
In the twenty-seventh year, Ruo Ao died and his son Xiong Kan came to the throne. This was Xiao Ao.
Xiao Ao died in the sixth year of his reign, and his son Xiong Zhen came to the throne. This is Fimao.
summary: The ancestors of the Chu State originated from Gaoyang, Emperor Zhuanxu, who was the grandson of Huangdi. The lineage passed through several generations to Chongli, who served as Huozheng under Emperor Ku and was granted the title Zhurong. After Chongli failed to completely suppress the Gonggong rebellion, Emperor Ku executed him and appointed his younger brother Wu Hui as his successor. Wu Hui fathered Luzhong, who had six sons by caesarean section. The youngest son, Jilian, whose surname was Mi, became the ancestor of the Chu royal family. Jilian's descendants included Yuxiong, who served King Wen of Zhou like a son but died young. During King Cheng of Zhou's reign, Yuxiong's descendant Xiong Yi was granted the title of baron in the Chu Man region with Danyang as his residence. Xiong Yi served the Zhou king alongside other noble descendants. The lineage continued through several generations until Xiong Qu, who gained support from people along the Yangtze and Han Rivers. He conquered territories including Yong and Yangyue, and declared his three sons kings of various regions in the Chu Man area. When King Li of Zhou ascended, Xiong Qu removed his kingly title out of fear.

translation:
In the thirteenth year of Fu Mao's reign, the state of Jin began to be in turmoil because of Quwo.
Fu Mao died in the seventeenth year of his reign.
Fu Mao's younger brother Xiong Tong killed Fu Mao's son and ascended the throne. This was King Wu of Chu.
In the seventeenth year of King Wu's reign, Prince Quwo of Jin State killed Jin Xiaohou, the king of the suzerain state.
In the nineteenth year, Zheng Bo's younger brother Duan provoked civil strife.
In the twenty-first year, Zheng Guo invaded the emperor's fields.
In the twenty-third year, the people of Wei killed their king Huan Gong.
In the twenty-ninth year, the people of Lu killed their king Yin Gong.
In the thirty-first year of the Song Dynasty, Hua Du, the governor of the Song Dynasty, killed his own monarch Shang Gong.
In the thirty-fifth year, the Chu State attacked Sui State.
Sui Guojun said: I have no sin.
The King of Chu said: I am in a barbarian area.
Today, all the princes have betrayed the royal family, invaded and killed each other.
I have an army and want to use it to participate in the political affairs of the Central Plains. I request the Zhou royal family to respect my name.
The people of Sui went to the Zhou royal family to ask for a title on his behalf, but the Zhou royal family refused, so the people of Sui came back and reported to Chu.
In the thirty-seventh year, Chu Xiongtong said angrily: My ancestor Wu Xiong was the teacher of King Wen, but it was a pity that he died early.
King Zhou Cheng promoted my late grandfather, but only gave him the land with the title of baron and let him live in the Chu region. Now the barbarian tribes are submissive, but King Zhou still does not grant him a title, so I have no choice but to claim my title!
So he called himself King Wu and made an alliance with the people of Sui before withdrawing his troops.
From then on, he began to cultivate Pu land and occupy it.
In the fifty-first year, the king of Zhou summoned Sui Hou and scolded him for supporting the king of Chu to become king.
King Wu of Chu was very angry and thought that Sui Hou had betrayed him, so he attacked Sui.
King Wu died of illness on the march, and Chu State stopped its march.
King Wu's son King Wen Xiong Yu came to the throne, and the Chu State began to move its capital to Ying.
In the second year of King Wen's reign, the state of Chu attacked the state of Shen and passed by Deng. Deng's people said: It is easy to capture the king of Chu at this moment.
Deng Hou did not agree. In the sixth year, the Chu State attacked the Cai State, captured Cai Aihou, returned to the country, and soon released him.
The State of Chu became powerful and bullied the small countries in the Yangtze and Han River basins. The small countries were all afraid of the State of Chu.
In the eleventh year, Duke Huan of Qi began to dominate, and the state of Chu also began to become powerful.
In the twelfth year, the Chu State attacked the Deng State and destroyed the Deng State.
In the thirteenth year, King Wen passed away and his son Xiong Jin came to the throne. This is Zhuang Ao.
In the fifth year of Zhuang Ao's reign, he wanted to kill his younger brother Xiong Yun. Xiong Yun fled to Sui, attacked and killed Zhuang Ao with his followers, and became king.
In the first year of the reign of King Cheng Yun, as soon as he came to the throne, he extended kindness and morality to the people and restored the old friendly relations among the princes.
summary: After several successions and internal conflicts, Xiong Tong killed his nephew and ascended the throne as King Wu of Chu. He declared himself king after the Zhou royal family refused to grant him a higher title, stating that his ancestor had served King Wen and that the Zhou had only given his family a baron's title in the Chu region. King Wu attacked Sui and died of illness during the campaign. His son King Wen Xiong Yu moved the capital to Ying. Under King Wen, Chu attacked Shen, Cai, and Deng, becoming powerful and intimidating smaller states in the region.

translation:
He sent people to pay tribute to the emperor, and the emperor rewarded him with meat. Said: Take good care of the turmoil in the Yiyue region in your south, and do not invade the Central Plains.
So the Chu State expanded to a thousand miles in radius.
In the 16th year, Duke Huan of Qi sent troops to invade the state of Chu, all the way to Xingshan.
King Cheng of Chu asked General Qu Wan to lead his army to resist, and made an alliance with Duke Huan of Qi.
Duke Huan scolded King Chu Cheng for not paying tribute to the Zhou royal family. King Chu Cheng agreed and he withdrew his troops from Chu.
In the eighteenth year, King Cheng led his army to attack the state of Xu in the north. The king of Xu State took off his shirt and exposed his arms to plead guilty, and King Cheng of Chu released him.
In the twenty-second year, Chu State attacked Huang State.
In the twenty-sixth year, Chu State destroyed Britain.
In the thirty-third year, Duke Xianggong of the Song Dynasty wanted to form an alliance with the princes and summoned King Cheng of Chu to attend.
The King of Chu said angrily: "How dare you summon me? I will go with a friendly attitude, and then take the opportunity to attack and insult him."
So the King of Chu sent troops to Yu, arrested and humiliated Song Xianggong, and soon let him return to his country.
In the thirty-fourth year, Zheng Wengong went south to pay homage to the King of Chu.
King Chu Cheng went north to attack the Song Dynasty, defeated the Song army at Hongshui, and shot and wounded Song Xianggong. Xianggong died of the arrow wound soon after.
In the thirty-fifth year of the Jin Dynasty, Chong'er, the prince of Jin Dynasty, passed through the state of Chu. King Cheng entertained Chong'er according to the etiquette of entertaining guests from princes, gave Chong'er many gifts, and escorted him to the state of Qin.
In the 39th year, Duke Xi of Lu asked Chu State to send troops to attack Qi State. Chu State sent Marquis Shen to lead an army to attack Qi State, captured the valley, and settled Qi Huangong's son Yong in the valley.
The seven sons of Duke Huan of Qi all fled to the State of Chu, and all of them in the State of Chu worshiped them as senior officials.
The Chu State destroyed Kui because Kui did not sacrifice to Zhu Rong and Wan Xiong.
In the summer, Chu State attacked Song State. Song State asked Jin State for help. Jin State sent troops to rescue Song State. King Chu Cheng had to give up and return to Chu State.
General Ziyu asked to continue fighting, and King Cheng said: Chong'er has been on the run for many years and finally returned to Jin. God is blessing him and cannot stop him.
Ziyu resolutely asked for a battle, so King Chu Cheng left with only a small army.
As expected, Jin defeated Ziyu in Chengpu. King Chu Cheng was very angry and killed Ziyu.
In the forty-sixth year, at first, King Cheng planned to establish Shang Chen as the crown prince and told Ling Yin Zishang.
The Master said: Your Majesty is still young, and you have many lovely wives and concubines. If you establish the crown prince now, he may be deposed in the future, and the country will be in trouble. The crown prince of Chu State is often born to his young son.
Moreover, the merchant's eyes were like poisonous bees and his voice was like that of a jackal. He was an extremely cruel person and it was not suitable for him to be crown prince.
The King of Chu refused to listen and finally appointed Shang Chen.
Later, the King of Chu wanted to establish the position of son, and abandoned the prince and merchant.
Shang Chen heard some rumors but had not confirmed it, so he told his teacher Pan Chong: How can we get the real situation?
Pan Chong said: Treat Jiang Miji, whom King Cheng loves, but do not respect her.
summary: King Cheng Xiong Yun extended kindness to the people and restored relations with other states. He expanded Chu's territory to a thousand miles in radius. When Duke Huan of Qi invaded Chu, King Cheng made an alliance with him. King Cheng later captured and humiliated Duke Xiang of Song, attacked Song, and entertained the Jin prince Chong'er. After Chong'er returned to Jin, Chu's general Ziyu was defeated at Chengpu, and King Cheng executed him. King Cheng initially established Shang Chen as crown prince despite warnings about his cruel nature. When King Cheng planned to replace him, Shang Chen surrounded the palace, and King Cheng hanged himself.

translation:
The merchants followed his plan.
Jiang Mi said angrily: The king wants to kill you and make you the crown prince.
The merchant told Pan Chong: The king really wants to depose me and replace me with another official.
Pan Chong asked: Can you serve?
The merchant replied: No!
Can you escape from here?
The merchant replied: No.
Can you do what it takes to kill a king? The merchant replied: Yes.
In October of winter, the merchants asked the palace guards to surround King Cheng. King Cheng asked to eat bear paws before dying, but the merchants refused. On the day of Ding Wei, King Cheng hanged himself.
Shang Chen came to the throne, and this was King Mu.
After King Mu ascended the throne, he gave Pan Chong his royal palace and made him the grand master to preside over state affairs.
In the third year of King Mu, Chu State was destroyed by Jiang State.
In four years, the Chu State destroyed the Six Kingdoms and the Liao Kingdom.
6. The king of Liao is a descendant of Gaotao.
In the eighth year, Chu State attacked Chen State.
In the twelfth year, King Mu passed away.
His son Zhuang Wanglu came to the throne.
King Zhuang has been on the throne for three years. He has never issued any political orders to the country. He has had fun day and night. He also issued an edict to the country: Anyone who dares to remonstrate will be killed!
Wu Ju entered the palace to admonish him.
King Zhuang holds Zheng Ji in his left hand and Yue Nu in his right hand, sitting among the singers and dancers.
Wu Ju said: I hope to give you a hidden word.
Then he said: There was a bird that landed on the mountain. It did not fly or sing for three years. What kind of bird was it?
King Zhuang said: If you don't fly for three years, you will soar into the sky; if you don't sing for three years, you will become a blockbuster.
Go down, I know what you mean.
After a few months, King Zhuang became even more lewd and indulgent.
Su Cong, the doctor, went to the palace to give advice.
King Zhuang of Chu said: Didn't you hear my edict?
Su Cong replied: It is my long-cherished wish to sacrifice myself to make you wise.
The king of Chu then stopped his lewdness and pleasure and began to handle government affairs. He killed hundreds of criminals, promoted hundreds of meritorious ministers, and appointed Wu Ju and Su Cong to manage government affairs, which was supported by the whole country.
At that time, the state of Chu was destroyed.
In six years, Chu State attacked Song State and obtained 500 chariots.
In the eighth year, the Chu State attacked Lu Hunrong and arrived at Luo, where they held a military parade on the outskirts of the Zhou capital.
King Zhou Ding sent Wang Sunman to reward King Chu.
The King of Chu asked Wang Sunman about the size of the tripod. Wang Sunman replied: Ruling a country depends on whether the government is virtuous, not on the size of the tripod.
King Zhuang said: Don't rely on owning Jiuding!
The state of Chu only had to destroy the tip of the sword to make the Jiuding. Wang Sunman said: Hey!
Has the king forgotten this?
In the past, when the Yu and Xia Dynasties were prosperous, all the remote countries came to pay tribute, and asked the chiefs of Kyushu to pay tribute to the metal and cast it into a Jiuding. Many mountains and rivers were painted on it, and all kinds of weird things were there, so that the people could know the harm done by the weird things.
Jie's morals deteriorated, so Ding was moved to the Yin Dynasty, which lasted for six hundred years.
summary: King Mu Shang Chen ascended and destroyed several states. His son King Zhuang Lu initially indulged in pleasure but reformed after remonstrance from Wu Ju and Su Cong. King Zhuang attacked Lu Hunrong, paraded troops near the Zhou capital, and asked about the Nine Tripods. Wang Sunman replied that ruling depends on virtue, not tripods, and that the Zhou dynasty's mandate was difficult to change. King Zhuang withdrew. He later attacked Chen, captured it, but restored it after Shen Shu's advice. He besieged Zheng, accepted its surrender, and defeated Jin at the Yellow River. He besieged Song for five months until its people resorted to cannibalism, then withdrew.

translation:
When King Ling heard the news that Prince Lu had been killed, he lost his mind and fell under the car, saying: Do people love their sons as much as I do?
The waiter said: Even more than you.
The Spiritual King said: I have killed too many other people's sons, how can I avoid falling into this situation?
You Yin said: Please go to the outskirts of the capital and obey the people's decision.
The Spiritual King said: Don’t offend everyone’s anger.
You Yin said: "Let's take shelter in a big county for now, and then ask for troops from the princes."
King Ling said: All the princes have betrayed me.
You Yin then said: For the time being, we should flee to the vassal states to listen to the opinions of the great kings.
The Spiritual King said: Great blessing cannot come again, it is just an insult to oneself.
So King Ling wanted to enter Yan City by boat.
You Yin estimated that King Ling would never listen to his advice, and feared that he would be killed together with King Ling, so he left King Ling and ran away. The Spirit King then wandered alone in the mountains, and no villagers dared to take him in.
On the way, King Ling met Juan Ren who had been in the palace and said to him: "Please find something to eat for me. I have been hungry for three days."
Juan said: The new king has just issued an edict to kill any of the three tribes who dare to give you food and flee with you, not to mention there is no food to be found here.
The Ling King then fell asleep with his head on his lap.
Juanren replaced it with a clod of earth, pulled out his legs and ran away.
After King Ling woke up, he could not find Juan Ren. He was so hungry that he could not sit up.
Shen Hai, the son of Shen Wuyu, the local magistrate of Tudi, said: My father violated the king's law twice, but King Ling pardoned him both times. There is no greater kindness than this!
So he searched everywhere for the Spirit King, and finally found the hungry and fainting Spirit King in Lize, and served the Spirit King all the way to his own home.
On the day of Guichou in the fifth month of summer, King Ling passed away at Shen Hai's house. Shen Hai had two women buried in sacrifice and buried King Ling.
At this time, although the Chu State had already elected Prince Bi as King of Chu, it was afraid that King Ling would return again and had not heard the news of King Ling's death. Therefore, Guan Cong said to the new prince Bi: If you don't kill Qiji, even if you own the entire country, you will still suffer disaster.
The king of Chu said: I can't bear to kill him.
Guan Cong said: Others can't bear to kill you.
The new king did not obey, so Guan Cong left.
After Qi Ji returned to the capital, the people in the capital were frightened every night, saying: King Ling has entered the city.
On the night of Yimao day, Qiji asked the boatmen to run along the bank of the Yangtze River and shout: "The King of Spirits is coming!"
People in the capital were even more frightened.
Qiji then asked Man Chengran to tell the new prince Bi and his ling Yin Zixi: King Ling is here!
The people in the capital will kill you, Sima is coming!
You should think of a solution as soon as possible and don't insult yourself.
The anger of the people is like floods and fires, which cannot be saved.
The new king and Zixi committed suicide.
On Bingchen day, Qiji ascended the throne and became the king of Chu, and changed his name to Xiong Ju. He was the king of Ping.
King Ping used deception to kill two kings and ascended the throne. He was afraid that the people in the capital and the princes would betray him, so he extended favors to the people.
summary: King Gong Shen was defeated by Jin at Yanling and shot in the eye. After several successions, King Ling Xiong Wei gathered the princes, built Zhanghua Terrace, and asked about obtaining the Zhou tripod. He became arrogant but faced rebellion when his brother Qiji conspired with Guan Cong. King Ling's soldiers abandoned him, and he died of starvation at Shen Hai's house. Qiji ascended as King Ping, who deceived and killed two kings to gain the throne. He extended favors to the people, returned territories, and improved governance.

translation:
Shuxiang replied: Duke Huan of Qi is the son of Wei Ji, and he is favored by Duke Li.
There are Bao Shuya, Bin Xuwu, and Xi Peng as assistants, Ju and Wei as external aid, and Gao and Guo as internal support.
He listens to correct opinions like running water and is tireless in giving kindness to the people.
He enjoys the throne, doesn’t he deserve it?
In the past, our Duke Wen was the son of Hu Jiji and was favored by Duke Xian. He is eager to learn.
At the age of only seventeen, he made friends with five talented people, including the former great masters Ziquan and Zifu as his confidants, Wei Ji and Jia Tuo as his right-hand men, Qi, Song, Qin and Chu as foreign aids, and Luan, Que, Hu and Xian as internal responders.
Duke Wen had been on the run for nineteen years, and his ambition to return was very firm.
Because Hui Gong and Huai Gong lost the support of the people, the people all followed each other and turned to Wen Gong. In this way, shouldn't it be appropriate for Wen Gong to enjoy the country?
Zibi had nothing to give to the people, and he received no foreign aid. When he left Jin, the Jin people did not escort him; when he returned to Chu, the Chu people did not welcome him.
Why do you enjoy the country?
As expected, Zibi's reign as king did not last long, and it was Qiji who finally ascended the throne, just as Shu Xiang predicted.
In the second year of King Ping's reign, Fei Wuji was sent to the State of Qin to marry Prince Jian.
This woman was extremely beautiful. Before she could reach the capital of Chu, Wuji hurried back and encouraged King Ping: "The woman of Qin is as beautiful as the king. You can stay here and find another one for the prince."
King Ping listened to Wuji's persuasion and finally married Qin's daughter and gave birth to Xiong Zhen.
He married another woman for the prince.
At that time, Wu She was the prince's tutor and Wuji was the young tutor.
Wuji was not favored by the prince and often slandered and slandered the prince Jian.
Prince Jian was fifteen years old at the time. His mother was a woman from Cai State, and was not favored by King Ping. King Ping gradually became more distant from Prince Jian.
In the sixth year, King Ping asked the prince to live with his father in the city and guard the border.
Wuji again slandered Prince Jian in front of King Ping day and night, saying: Ever since I sent the Qin women to your harem, the Prince has resented me very much, and it is impossible not to have resentment towards you. You should also be careful.
Moreover, the prince lives in the city father, monopolizes military power, makes friends with foreign princes, and always wants to invade the capital.
King Ping called Tai Fu Wu She to scold him.
Wu She knew that this was the result of Wuji's rumors, so he said: Your Majesty, why have you alienated your own flesh and blood because of a villain?
Wuji said to King Ping: If you don't punish Wu She today, you will regret it in the future.
So King Ping imprisoned Wu She.
Let Sima Fenyang summon Prince Jian back and want to kill the Prince.
The prince heard the news and fled to Song Dynasty.
Fei Wuji said: Wu She has two sons. If they are not killed, they will become a disaster to the Chu State.
Why not summon them on the condition of exempting their father from the death penalty, so that they will definitely return to Chu.
So King Ping sent an envoy to Wu She and said: If you can recall your two sons, you can live, otherwise you will be executed.
summary: King Ping listened to Fei Wuji's slander against Prince Jian, imprisoned Wu She, and forced Prince Jian to flee. Wu She's son Wu Zixu escaped to Wu. King Ping married the woman intended for Prince Jian and fathered Xiong Zhen, who became King Zhao. Fei Wuji's slander caused Prince Jian's exile and Wu She's execution. King Zhao fled when Wu invaded, and Wu Zixu desecrated King Ping's tomb. King Zhao eventually returned with Qin's help.

translation:
Possessing the land of Chu is enough to make the country strong; condemning the reputation of Chu is enough to make the monarch noble.
Today, you are going to kill the king respected by all the princes in the world, take possession of the treasures passed down from three generations, swallow up the nine tripods, and look down upon all the kings. Isn't this greed?
"Book of Zhou" says that if you want to get started in politics, you should not initiate chaos first. Therefore, if the sacrificial vessels were moved south to the Chu State, large armies would follow.
So Chu State gave up its original plan.
In the 19th year, Qin attacked Chu. The Chu army was defeated and ceded Shangyong and Hanbei to Qin.
Twenty years later, Bai Qi, the general of Qin State, captured Xiling of Chu State.
In the 21st year, Bai Qi, the general of Qin State, captured Ying of Chu State and burned Yiling, the tomb of the late king.
King Chu Xiang's army was defeated and could no longer fight, so he retreated to the northeast and defended Chencheng.
In the 22nd year, Qin State captured Wu County and Qianzhong County of Chu State.
In the twenty-third year, King Xiang gathered the soldiers from the east, a total of more than 100,000 people, and went west to capture the fifteen cities on the Yangtze River that Qin had captured, and divided them into counties to resist Qin.
In the twenty-seventh year, Chu sent 30,000 men to help the Three Jins attack Yan.
Chu made peace with Qin again and asked the prince to serve as a hostage in Qin.
The state of Chu asked Zuo Tu to serve the prince in the state of Qin.
In the thirty-sixth year, King Qingxiang fell ill, and the prince fled back to Chu. In autumn, King Qingxiang died, and prince Xiong Yuan came to the throne. This was King Kaolie.
King Kaolie appointed Zuo Tu as his Ling Yin and granted him the title of Lord Chunshen of Wu.
In the first year of King Kaolie's reign, he gave the state to Qin in order to make peace with Qin.
At this time, the state of Chu was getting weaker and weaker.
In the sixth year, the State of Qin surrounded Handan. The State of Zhao asked the State of Chu for help. The State of Chu sent the late general Jingyang to rescue the State of Zhao.
In seven years, Chu State invaded Xinzhong.
The Qin army left.
In the twelfth year, King Zhao of Qin passed away, and the King of Chu asked Chun Shenjun to come to Qin to express his condolences.
In the 16th year, King Zhuangxiang of Qin passed away, and King Zhao Zheng of Qin came to the throne.
In the twenty-second year, the Chu State and the vassal states jointly attacked the Qin State, failed in the battle and withdrew their troops.
The Chu State moved its capital eastward to Shouchun, which was called Ying.
In the twenty-fifth year, King Kaolie passed away, and his son You Wanghan came to the throne.
Li Yuan killed Chun Shenjun.
In the third year of King You, Qin and Wei attacked Chu.
Lu Buwei, the prime minister of Qin, passed away.
In the ninth year, Qin destroyed South Korea.
In the tenth year, King You passed away, and his younger half-brother, You, came to the throne. This was King Ai.
More than two months after King Ai came to the throne, the gangsters of King Ai's brother, Fu Chu, attacked and killed King Ai, and made Fu Chu king of Chu.
At that time, Qin captured Zhao Wangqian.
In the first year of Wang Fuchu's reign, Prince Dan of Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate the King of Qin.
In the second year, Qin sent generals to attack Chu, defeated the Chu army and captured more than ten cities.
In three years, Qin State destroyed Wei State.
In the fourth year, the Qin general Wang Jian defeated the Chu army in Qi and killed the general Xiang Yan.
In the fifth year, the Qin generals Wang Jian and Meng Wu invaded the capital of Chu, captured the Chu king Fu Chu, destroyed the Chu state, and established three counties in Chu.
Tai Shigong said: When King Ling of Chu gathered the princes in Shen, killed Qi Qingfeng, built Zhanghua Terrace, and asked for the nine tripods of the Zhou royal family, he had lofty ambitions and looked down on the world. When he died of starvation at Shenhai's house, he was ridiculed by the people of the world.
summary: King Hui was kidnapped by Bai Gongsheng but rescued by Ye Gong. After several more successions, King Huai was deceived by Zhang Yi into breaking relations with Qi, then attacked Qin and was defeated. He was later tricked into meeting King Zhao of Qin, who detained him. King Huai died in Qin, causing Chu to break relations with Qin. King Qingxiang moved the capital eastward as Qin captured Chu territories. The Chu state continued to weaken, eventually moving its capital to Shouchun. Qin generals Wang Jian and Meng Wu captured the Chu king, destroyed the state, and established three commanderies in Chu territory.

translation:
Liu Jiao, King of Chu Yuan Dynasty, was the younger half-brother of Emperor Gaozu. His courtesy name was You.
There were four Gaozu brothers, the eldest brother was a famous uncle, and his uncle had died long ago.
When Gao Zuwei was a child, in order to avoid trouble, he often passed by his sister-in-law's house to have dinner with guests.
The eldest sister-in-law hated her brother-in-law. When the uncle and guests came to the house, the eldest sister-in-law pretended that she had finished the soup and scraped the pot with a spoon, so the guests left.
Later, when he saw that there was still soup in the pot, Emperor Gaozu resented his sister-in-law from then on.
When Emperor Gaozu became emperor, he divided his brothers into feudal lords, except for the eldest brother's son.
The Emperor interceded for his grandson, and Emperor Gaozu said: It's not that I forgot to confer him a title, because his mother is so unlike her elders.
So her son Xin was granted the title of Genjiehou.
He named his second brother Zhong as acting king.
In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, after arresting King Han Xin of Chu in Chen County, he made his younger brother King of Chu and made his capital Pengcheng.
Jiao died in the 23rd year of his reign, and his son Ying, King of Yi, succeeded him.
King Yi died in the fourth year of his reign and was succeeded by his son Wang Wu. Twenty years after Wang Wu took the throne, in winter, he committed a private crime during the mourning period for Empress Dowager Bo, and the fiefdom of Donghai County was cut off.
In the spring of the next year, Wu conspired with the King of Wu to rebel, but his prime minister Zhang Shang and Taifu Zhao Yiwu tried to stop him and refused to listen.
Wu killed Zhang Shang and Zhao Yiwu, raised an army and went westward with King Wu to attack Liang State, and captured Jibi.
He went to the south of Changyi and engaged the Han general Zhou Yafu.
The Han army cut off the food routes of the Wu and Chu armies, and the soldiers were hungry. King Wu was defeated, King Wu of Chu committed suicide, and the Wu and Chu armies surrendered to the Han army.
The Han army had put down the rebellions of Wu and Chu. Emperor Xiaojing wanted Dehou Guang's son to inherit the throne of Wu and King Yuan's son Li to inherit the throne of Chu.
Empress Dowager Dou said: King Wu is of the older generation and should be loyal to the clan and do good deeds.
Now he is leading the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms and disrupting the world. Why should he continue his descendants!
It is not allowed to establish the descendants of the King of Wu, but only the descendants of the King of Chu.
At that time, Li was the Zongzheng of the Han Dynasty, so Li was named King of Chu and enshrined in the ancestral temple of King Yuan. This was King Wen of Chu.
King Wen died three years after he took the throne, and his son An Wangdao succeeded him.
King An died in the 22nd year of his reign, and his son Jian Wangzhu succeeded him.
King Xiang died in the fourteenth year of his reign, and his son Wang Chun succeeded him.
After Wang Chun succeeded to the throne, in the second year of Dijie, the eunuchs complained to the King of Chu of rebellion. The King of Chu committed suicide, the country's title was abolished, and the fiefdom was returned to the Han Dynasty and changed to Pengcheng County.
Zhao Wang Liu Sui, his father ranked in the middle among Gaozu's sons, was famous as a friend, and his posthumous name was "You".
King You died of sorrow, so his posthumous name was You.
Empress Gao made Lu Lu the king of Zhao, and Empress Gao died a year later.
The ministers executed Lu Lu and other Lu family members, and then made King You's son King of Zhao.
In the second year after Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, Li Sui's younger brother Piqiang cut off the Hejian County of Zhao State and became the King of Hejian. This was King Wen.
He died in the thirteenth year of his reign and was succeeded by his son Ai Wangfu.
Fu died in the first year, without any children, and had no descendants. The title of the country was abolished, and the fiefdom was returned to the Han Dynasty.
Sui had been king of Zhao for twenty-six years. During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, Chao Cuo deprived him of Changshan County because of his negligence.
Wu and Chu rebelled, and King Zhao conspired with them to raise troops.
His prime minister, Jian De, and his internal history king fiercely resisted and refused to obey.
He burned Jiande and Wang Han to death, and stationed troops on the western border of Zhao State, hoping to wait for the Wu army to advance westward.
He also sent people to the Xiongnu in the north, hoping to unite with the Xiongnu to attack the Han Dynasty.
The Han Dynasty sent Quzhou Hou Liji to attack Zhao.
King Zhao then retreated and defended Handan. They faced off for seven months. The Wu and Chu armies were defeated in Liang State and could not advance westward.
When the Xiongnu heard the news, they also stopped sending troops and refused to enter the Han border.
After Luan Bu returned from the front line where he defeated Qi, he joined forces with Li Ji to divert water to the capital of Zhao.
Zhao's capital city was destroyed by water, King Zhao committed suicide, and Handan surrendered.
King Zhao You cut off his descendants.
summary: Liu Jiao, King of Chu Yuan, was the younger half-brother of Emperor Gaozu. As a child, Gaozu often brought guests to his sister-in-law’s house for meals. She resented him and once scraped the pot to pretend no soup was left, causing guests to leave. Gaozu later saw soup remained, fostering resentment. When he became emperor, he enfeoffed his brothers but initially excluded his eldest brother’s son, citing the mother’s unworthiness, though he later granted the son the title of Genjiehou. His second brother Zhong was made acting king. In the sixth year of his reign, after arresting King Han Xin of Chu, Gaozu made Jiao King of Chu, with his capital at Pengcheng. Jiao reigned 23 years, succeeded by his son Ying, then grandson Wang Wu. Wu, during mourning for Empress Dowager Bo, committed a private crime, losing Donghai County. The next spring, Wu conspired with the King of Wu to rebel. His prime minister Zhang Shang and Taifu Zhao Yiwu opposed him; Wu killed them and marched west with the King of Wu, attacking Liang and capturing Jibi. At Changyi, they fought General Zhou Yafu. The Han army cut off Wu and Chu’s food routes; starving, the King of Wu was defeated, and the King of Chu committed suicide. Their armies surrendered. Emperor Xiaojing initially wanted to restore their descendants, but Empress Dowager Dou opposed it for the King of Wu. Only the King of Chu’s descendant, Li, then Zongzheng, was named King Wen of Chu. He reigned three years, succeeded by An Wangdao, then Jian Wangzhu, then Wang Chun. In the second year of Dijie, eunuchs accused Chun of rebellion; he committed suicide, and Chu’s territory became Pengcheng County. Zhao Wang Liu Sui, a son of Gaozu, was posthumously named You. King You died of sorrow. Empress Gao made Lu Lu King of Zhao; after her death, ministers executed the Lu clan and made King You’s son king. In Emperor Xiaowen’s second year, Sui’s younger brother Piqiang became King Wen of Hejian. He reigned 13 years, succeeded by Ai Wangfu, who died heirless, ending the kingdom. Sui ruled Zhao for 26 years. During Emperor Xiaojing’s reign, Chao Cuo deprived him of Changshan County. When Wu and Chu rebelled, King Zhao conspired with them. His prime minister Jian De and internal history Wang Han resisted; he burned them to death and stationed troops on Zhao’s western border, awaiting the Wu army. He also sought Xiongnu aid. The Han sent Quzhou Hou Liji to attack Zhao. King Zhao defended Handan for seven months. After Wu and Chu were defeated, Xiongnu withdrew. Luan Bu, returning from Qi, joined Liji to divert water against Zhao’s capital. The city fell; King Zhao committed suicide, and his line ended.

translation:
Tai Shigong said: When a country is about to rise, there must be auspicious omens. Gentlemen will be valued and villains will be dismissed.
When the country is about to perish, the wise men retire and the treacherous officials become dignified.
If King Wu of Chu did not punish Duke Shen and listened to his words, how could King Zhao appoint Mr. Fang Yu to have a conspiracy to usurp him and be killed by everyone in the world?
Wise man! Wise man!
How can a king who is not inherently virtuous use you?
So important! The safety of the country depends on the decrees issued, and the survival of the country depends on the ministers appointed. This is so true.
summary: Tai Shigong remarked: A rising nation shows auspicious signs, with valued gentlemen and dismissed villains. A perishing nation sees wise men retreat and treacherous officials rise. Had King Wu of Chu heeded Duke Shen, or King Zhao appointed Mr. Fang Yu, they might have avoided usurpation and death. A king without inherent virtue cannot use wise men. The nation’s safety depends on decrees and appointments—this is profoundly true.

translation:
Zhao Gongxi has the same surname as the Zhou royal family, Ji.
After King Wu of Zhou destroyed King Zhou of Shang, he granted Duke Zhao a title in Northern Yan.
When King Cheng of Zhou was on the throne, Duke Zhao was in charge of the three Dukes: from the west of Shaanxi, Duke Zhao was in charge; from the east of Shaanxi, Duke Zhou was in charge.
At that time, King Cheng was still young, and Duke Zhou presided over the affairs of state on his behalf and held the power of the country, just like the emperor. Duke Zhao was suspicious of Duke Zhou's actions, so Duke Zhou wrote an article "Jun Shi" to express his confession.
Duke Zhao was still very dissatisfied with Duke Zhou.
Duke Zhou then praised the relevant historical facts of the Yin and Shang Dynasties and said: During the reign of Shang Tang, there was Yi Yin, whose merits reached heaven; during Taiwu's reign, there were people like Yi Zhi and Chen Hu, whose merits reached heaven, and Wu Xian managed the government; during Zu Yi's reign, there were people like Wu Xian; during Wu Ding's era, there were people like Gan Ban: these ministers all had the merit of assisting the king and presiding over governance, and the Yin Dynasty was governed and stabilized.
After hearing these words, Duke Zhao became happy.
Duke Zhao governed the western region and was deeply loved by the people.
When Zhao Gong went to inspect villages and towns, he saw a Tangli tree, and he judged lawsuits and handled political affairs under the tree. From marquises, counts to civilians, everyone has been properly accommodated, and there has been no neglect of duty.
After the death of Duke Zhao, the people missed his political achievements and the time when Duke Zhao handled political affairs under the Tangli tree. They were reluctant to cut down the trees and praised Duke Zhao, writing a poem called "Gantang".
After Zhao Gong, it was passed down to Huihou through nine generations.
The reign of Yan Huihou coincided with the time when King Zhou Li fled to Pig, and when Zhou Dinggong and Zhaomu Gong were in power together.
Huihou died and his son Lihou came to the throne.
This year, King Zhou Xuan had just ascended the throne.
In the 21st year of Lihou, Duke Huan of Zheng was granted the title of Zheng.
In the thirty-sixth year, Lihou died and his son Qinghou came to the throne.
In the 20th year of Qinghou's reign, King You of Zhou committed adultery and was killed by Quan Rong.
Qin State began to be classified as vassals at this time.
Qinghou died in the twenty-fourth year of his reign, and his son Aihou came to the throne.
Marquis Ai died after reigning for two years, and his son Marquis Zheng came to the throne.
Zheng Hou died in the thirty-sixth year of his reign, and his son Miao Hou came to the throne.
The seventh year of Yan Muhou's reign was the first year of Lu Yin's reign.
Marquis Mu of Yan died in the eighteenth year of his reign, and his son Marquis Xuan came to the throne.
Xuanhou died in the thirteenth year of his reign, and his son Huanhou came to the throne.
Huan Hou died after reigning for seven years, and his son Zhuang Gong came to the throne.
In the twelfth year of Duke Zhuang, Duke Huan of Qi began to dominate.
In the 16th year, Yan State, Song State, and Wei State jointly attacked King Hui of Zhou. King Hui fled to Wendi. The three kingdoms supported King Hui's younger brother Decai as King of Zhou.
In the seventeenth year, Zheng Guo arrested Yan Zhongfu and escorted King Hui of Zhou back to Zhou Guo.
summary: The history of the Yan state, beginning with its founder, Zhao Gongxi, a member of the Zhou royal family granted the title in Northern Yan by King Wu. During King Cheng's reign, Zhao Gong governed west of Shaanxi, while the Duke of Zhou governed the east. Suspicious of the Duke of Zhou's regency, Zhao Gong was appeased by the Duke's historical references to virtuous Yin ministers. Zhao Gong governed the western region with great popularity, famously adjudicating under a Tangli tree, which the people later honored in the poem "Gantang" after his death.

translation:
In the twenty-seventh year, the Shan Rong invaded the Yan State. Duke Huan of Qi went to rescue the Yan State, so he led his troops north to attack the Shan Rong and then returned home.
Duke Zhuang of Yan sent Duke Huan of Qi out of the country, and Duke Huan of Qi ceded the place where Duke Zhuang of Yan went to the state of Yan. He asked Duke Zhuang of Yan and the princes to pay tribute to the emperor of Zhou, just like Duke Zhao of Yan during the reign of King Cheng of Zhou.
In the thirty-third year, Duke Zhuang died, and his son Duke Xiang came to the throne.
In the twenty-sixth year of Duke Xiang, Duke Wen of Jin convened the princes to meet in Jiantu to form an alliance and to dominate the princes.
In the thirty-first year, the Qin army was defeated by the Jin army in Miaoshan.
In the thirty-seventh year, Duke Mu of Qin passed away.
Forty years later, Duke Xiang of Yan died and Duke Huan ascended the throne.
Duke Huan died in the sixteenth year of his reign, and Duke Xuan ascended the throne.
Duke Xuan died in his fifteenth year and Duke Zhao ascended the throne.
Duke Zhao died in the thirteenth year of his reign, and Duke Wu ascended the throne.
This year, the Jin State executed Dr. Sanque.
Duke Wu died in the 19th year of his reign, and Duke Wen ascended the throne.
Duke Wen passed away in the sixth year of his reign, and Duke Yi ascended the throne.
In the first year of Yi AD, Cui Zhu of Qi killed his king Zhuang Gong.
Duke Yi died in the fourth year of his reign, and his son Duke Hui came to the throne.
In the first year of Huigong, Gaozhi of Qi State fled and came to Yan State.
In the past six years, Duke Hui had many concubines whom he favored. He planned to get rid of the officials and install a concubine named Song. The officials killed the concubine named Song together. Duke Hui was afraid and fled to Qi.
In the fourth year after he arrived in Qi State, Qi State sent Gao Yan to Jin State to request a joint attack on Yan State and send Duke Hui of Yan back to his country to become king.
Duke Ping of Jin agreed and joined Qi in attacking Yan and sent Duke Hui of Yan back to Yan.
Duke Hui died just after arriving in Yan State.
The people of Yan State supported Duke Mourning.
After reigning for seven years, Duke Du passed away and Duke Gong ascended the throne.
Duke Gong passed away after five years of reign, and Duke Ping ascended the throne.
At this time, the monarchy of Jin State was weakened, and the power of the six families including Fan, Zhongxing, Zhi, Zhao, Han and Wei began to grow.
In the eighteenth year of Ping Gong, King Helu of Wu conquered Chu and entered the capital of Ying.
Duke Ping died in the 19th year of his reign, and Duke Jian came to the throne.
Duke Jian died in the 12th year of his reign, and Duke Xian ascended the throne.
Zhao Yang of Jin State besieged Fan and Zhonghang families in Chaoge.
In the twelfth year of Xiangong's reign, Tian Chang of Qi State killed his king Jian Gong.
In the fourteenth year, Duke Xian died and Duke Xiao came to the throne.
In the twelfth year of Duke Xiao's reign, the three families of Han, Wei, and Zhao destroyed Zhibo and divided up his fiefdom. These three families gradually became stronger.
In the fifteenth year, Duke Xiao died and Duke Cheng ascended the throne.
Duke Cheng died in the sixteenth year of his reign, and Duke Min ascended the throne.
Duke Min died in the thirty-first year of his reign, and Duke Li ascended the throne.
In this year, Han, Zhao and Wei were classified as princes.
In the 30th year of Li Gong, Yan State conquered and defeated Qi State in Linying. Duke Li died and Duke Huan ascended the throne.
Duke Huan died in the eleventh year of his reign, and Duke Wen ascended the throne.
This year, Duke Xiang of Qin passed away, and the state of Qin became stronger.
In the nineteenth year of Duke Wen, King Wei of Qi passed away.
In the twenty-eighth year, Su Qin came to Yan State for the first time to pay homage to Duke Wen and talk about Duke Wen.
Duke Wen gave him vehicles, horses, gold and silk and asked him to go to Zhao. Marquis Su of Zhao reused him.
So Su Qin implemented a joint vertical policy with the six countries, and he became the vertical commander.
At this time, King Qin Hui married his daughter to the prince of Yan as his wife.
In the twenty-ninth year, Duke Wen died and the prince came to the throne. This was King Yi.
As soon as King Yi came to the throne, King Xuan of Qi took advantage of the opportunity to hold a funeral for Duke Wen to attack Yan and capture ten cities. Su Qin went to Qi to lobby and persuaded King Qi to return ten cities to Yan.
Ten years later, the king of Yan State officially became king.
Su Qin committed adultery with the wife of Duke Wen of Yan and was afraid of being killed, so he lobbied King Yi to send him as an envoy to Qi to stir up rebellion and disrupt Qi.
King Yi died in the 12th year, and his son King Kuai of Yan came to the throne.
After King Kuai of Yan came to the throne, the people of Qi killed Su Qin.
When Su Qin was in the State of Yan, he married his son-in-law, the Prime Minister of the state, Zi Zhi. Su Qin's younger brother Su Dai also had a close relationship with Zi Zhi.
After Su Qin's death, King Qi Xuan appointed Su Dai again.
In the third year of King Kuai of Yan, Yan united with Chu, Han, Zhao, and Wei to attack Qin, but failed to win and returned home.
summary: The succession of Yan rulers is then detailed, from Huihou through numerous generations, with key events interspersed: the flight of King Zhou Li, the rise of Qin as vassals, and the reign of King Xuan. The narrative covers Yan's interactions with other states, including attacks on King Hui of Zhou, invasions by Shan Rong (aided by Duke Huan of Qi), and participation in alliances against Qin. Internal strife emerges under King Kuai, who ceded power to his minister Zizhi, leading to chaos, Qi's invasion, and the death of King Kuai. King Zhao of Yan restored stability by recruiting talents like Le Yi, Zou Yan, and Ju Xin, leading to a prosperous period and a successful campaign against Qi, capturing its capital Linzi.

translation:
King Yan called King Lejian of Chang State to inquire about this matter.
Lejian replied: Zhao is a country that is surrounded by enemies and often fights wars. Its people are familiar with military affairs and cannot attack.
King Yan said: We are attacking one of them with five people.
Le Jian still replied: No.
King Yan was very angry. At this time, all the ministers thought it was okay to attack.
The State of Yan finally sent out two armies with 2,000 chariots. Li Fu led the army to attack Hao, and Qing Qin led the army to attack Daidi.
Only the doctor told the king of Yan: "We communicated with others, made an alliance, took out five hundred yi of gold to toast their king, and then turned around and attacked them as soon as the envoy came back to report. This is unlucky, and the battle will not succeed."
King Yan couldn't listen, so he personally led the flanking troops and set off with the army.
He grabbed the seal belt around King Yan's waist to stop him and said: Your Majesty, you must not go there in person, otherwise you will not succeed!
King Yan kicked him away with his feet.
Jiang Qu cried and said: I am not doing it for myself, but for the king!
When the Yan army arrived at Songzi, Zhao sent Lian Po to lead his troops and defeated Li Fu at Cha.
Le Cheng also defeated Qing Qin in Dai Di. Lejian fled to Zhao State.
Lian Po pursued Yan for more than five hundred miles and surrounded the capital of Yan.
The people of Yan requested peace talks, but the people of Zhao refused, so they had to ask General Qu to come forward to preside over the peace talks.
The State of Yan appointed General Qu as prime minister and went to preside over the peace talks.
The State of Zhao listened to General Qu's request and lifted the siege of the State of Yan.
In the sixth year of King Yan's reign, the Qin State destroyed the Eastern Zhou Dynasty and established Sanchuan County.
In seven years, Qin State captured 37 cities including Yulin of Zhao State and established Taiyuan County.
In the ninth year, King Qin Yingzheng had just ascended the throne.
In the tenth year, the State of Zhao sent Lian Po to lead an army to attack Fanyang of the State of Wei and occupied it.
At this time, King Zhao Xiaocheng passed away and King Mouxiang came to the throne.
King Mouxiang sent Lecheng to take over Lianpo's command, but Lianpo refused to obey orders and attacked Lecheng. Lecheng escaped, and Lianpo also fled to Daliang, the capital of Wei.
In the twelfth year, Zhao State sent Li Mu to attack Yan State and captured Wu Sui and Fangcheng.
When Ju Xin lived in the State of Zhao, he was very close to Pang Nuan, but later fled to the State of Yan.
King Yan saw that Zhao was besieged by Qin soldiers many times and Lian Po left Zhao. At this time, Pang Nuan was leading the army to fight, so he wanted to take advantage of Zhao's fatigue to attack it.
King Yan asked Ju Xin at this time, and Ju Xin said: Pang Nuan is easy to deal with.
The King of Yan sent Ju Xin to lead an army to attack the State of Zhao. The State of Zhao sent Pang Nuan to fight, captured 20,000 Yan troops, and killed Ju Xin.
At this time, Qin State captured twenty cities of Wei State and established Dongjun.
In the 19th year, Qin State captured nine cities including Ye of Zhao State.
King Zhao Daoxiang passed away.
In the twenty-third year, Prince Dan of Yan was sent to Qin as a hostage, but he escaped back to Yan.
In the twenty-fifth year, Qin captured Han Wangan, destroyed Han, and established Yingchuan County.
In the twenty-seventh year, Qin captured Zhao Wangqian and destroyed Zhao.
summary: After King Zhao's death, King Hui's distrust of Le Yi led to Qi's recovery under Tian Dan. Subsequent rulers faced defeats by Zhao, including a failed attack advised by Ju Xin, resulting in heavy losses. The state weakened as Qin expanded, destroying Han and Zhao. Prince Dan of Yan's failed assassination attempt on Qin's king via Jing Ke prompted Qin's invasion, capturing Ji and forcing King Yan to flee to Liaodong. Eventually, Qin captured Liaodong, ending the Yan state. The historian concludes that Yan's survival for eight or nine hundred years, despite external pressures and near destruction, was due to Zhao Gong's virtuous legacy.

translation:
Chen Wan is Chen Ligong's son.
When Wan was born, Taishi of Zhou happened to pass by the state of Chen. Chen Ligong asked him to divine divination for Chen Wan. The hexagram obtained was "Guan Gua" changed to "No Gua". Taishi said: The meaning of the hexagram is: observing the customs and sentiments of the country is helpful for being the king's guest.
Does this mean that he will obtain the throne of Chen and own the country?
Maybe it's not in Chen country but in another country?
Or it may not be fulfilled on others, but be fulfilled on his descendants.
If it is in another country, it must be the country with the surname Jiang.
The surname Jiang is a descendant of the Four Mountains during the reign of Emperor Yao.
It is impossible for two things to be powerful at the same time. After the decline of Chen State, his branch will prosper!
Li Gong is the youngest son of Chen Wengong, and his mother is a woman from Cai State.
After Duke Wen died, Duke Li's brother Chen Bao came to the throne, and this was Duke Huan.
Duke Huan and his younger brother Chen were not born from the same mother.
When Duke Huan was ill, the people of Cai killed Duke Huan Chen Bao and Prince Chen Min on behalf of Chen Ta, and made Chen Ta the king. This is Duke Li.
After Li Gong came to the throne, he married a woman from Cai State.
This Cai woman committed adultery with a Cai man and returned to Cai many times. Duke Li also frequently went to Cai.
Chen Lin, the youngest son of Duke Huan, resented Duke Li for killing his father and brother, so he asked the people of Cai to trick Duke Li and kill him.
Chen Lin established himself as king, this is Duke Zhuang.
Therefore, Chen Wan could not be established as the king, but only as the official of the state of Chen.
Duke Li was killed because he went abroad for promiscuity, so the Spring and Autumn Annals said that "Cai people killed Chen Ta", which was an accusation against him.
After Zhuang Gong died, his younger brother Chujiu came to the throne. This was Chen Xuangong.
In the 21st year of Xuangong's reign, Chujiu killed the prince Yu Kou.
Yu Kou and Chen Wan were close, and he was afraid that the disaster would involve him, so Chen Wan fled to Qi State.
Duke Huan of Qi wanted to appoint him as minister, but he declined and said: "As a humble minister living abroad, I am fortunate enough to be exempted from all kinds of burdens. It is already a favor given to me by you. I dare not hold such a high position again."
Duke Huan of Qi appointed him as Gongzheng in charge of hundreds of workers.
Qi Yizhong wanted to marry his daughter to Chen Wan, so he conducted a divination for this matter. The result of the divination said: This is called the flying phoenix, with a harmonious sound.
The descendants of the Gui family will grow up under the Jiang family.
After the Five Dynasties, he will be prosperous and have the same status as Zhengqing.
After eight generations, no one can be higher than him.
He finally married his daughter to Chen Wan.
When Chen Wan fled to Qi, Duke Huan of Qi had been in power for fourteen years.
After Chen Wan's death, his posthumous title was Jingzhong.
Jingzhong gave birth to Yu Mengyi.
After Jingzhong arrived in Qi State, he changed the Chen family name to the Tian family name.
Tian Zhen Meng Yi gave birth to Min Meng Zhuang, and Tian Min Meng Zhuang gave birth to Wen Zi Xu Wu.
Tian Wenzi served Duke Zhuang of Qi.
Luan Cheng, a senior official of the Jin State, caused trouble in the Jin State and fled to the Qi State. Duke Zhuang of Qi gave him generous treatment.
Yan Ying and Tian Wenzi advised him, but Duke Zhuang did not listen.
summary: Chen Wan, son of Chen Ligong, was born with a prophecy from a Zhou diviner: his descendants would prosper in a state ruled by the Jiang clan, likely after Chen’s decline. Chen Wan’s father, Ligong, became ruler after a series of violent successions involving the murder of Duke Huan and his son by Cai conspirators. Ligong was later killed for his promiscuity, and Chen Wan, unable to claim the throne, served as an official. Fearing for his life after a prince’s murder, he fled to Qi, where Duke Huan appointed him as a minister overseeing craftsmen. A divination for his marriage foretold that his Gui descendants would thrive under the Jiang clan, rising to prominence over generations. Chen Wan changed his surname to Tian, and his lineage grew influential in Qi. The historian concludes that the Tian family’s rise, from Chen Wan’s flight to Qi to their seizure of power, may have been guided by the divinations of the Zhou priest and Yizhong, fulfilling prophecies over generations.

translation:
After Duke Mourning ascended the throne, Tian Qi was appointed prime minister and took over the political power of Qi.
Four years later, Tian Qi died and his son Tian Chang took over the position. This is Tian Chengzi.
Bao Mu had a disagreement with Duke Dao of Qi and killed Duke Dao of Qi.
The people of Qi jointly supported Ren, the son of Duke Ai, who was Duke Jian of Qi.
Tian Changchengzi and Jianzhi served as prime ministers and assisted Duke Jian.
Tian Chang was jealous of Jian Zhi, because Jian Zhi was very favored by Duke Jian of Qi and his power could not be removed.
So Tian Chang reused his father Lizi's method, using big buckets to lend grain to the people and small buckets to take it back.
The people of Qi State sang in praise of him and said: The old lady picked raspberries and gave them to Tian Chengzi!
When the officials of Qi State went to court, Yu Martingale admonished Duke Jian and said: Tian Chang and Jian Zhi cannot be appointed at the same time. Let the monarch choose!
Duke Jian didn't listen.
Ziwo is of the same clan as Jian Zhi, and is usually at odds with the Tian family.
Tian Bao, a distant relative of the Tian family, served Ziwo and was favored.
Ziwo said: I want to kill all the direct descendants of the Tian family and let you continue the Tian family line.
Tian Bao said: I am just Tian’s distant relative.
I won't listen.
Soon Tian Bao said to Tian, ​​"I am going to kill Tian. If Tian doesn't take action first, disaster will come."
I live in Duke Jian's palace, and the four Tian Chang brothers also rode to the palace and wanted to kill me.
I shut the door.
Justice Jian and his beloved concubine were drinking and having fun in Tantai, so they wanted to attack Tian Chang.
Taishi Ziyu said: Tian Chang did not dare to cause trouble, he wanted to eliminate harm for the country.
Only then did Mr. Jian stop.
After Tian Chang came out of the palace, he heard that Duke Jian had sent Nu, and he was afraid that he would be killed, so he wanted to flee.
Tian Zixing said: Hesitation is the enemy of career.
Tian Chang then attacked me.
Ziwo led his men to attack the Tian family, but could not win and had to flee.
Tian's men chased and killed Ziwo and Jianzhi.
Duke Jian fled, and Tian's men chased him to Xuzhou and captured him.
Duke Jian said: If I had listened to Yu Yang earlier, I would not have suffered such a disaster.
Tian's subordinates were worried that Duke Jian would kill them after he was restored to the throne, so they killed Duke Jian.
Duke Jian was killed four years after he ascended the throne.
So Tian Chang supported Ao, the younger brother of Duke Jian, to the throne. This was Duke Qi Ping.
After Ping Gong ascended the throne, he appointed Tian Chang as prime minister.
After Tian Chang killed Duke Jian, he was afraid that the princes from all over the world would unite to kill him, so he returned all the lands that he had occupied in Lu and Wei. The west made treaties with Jin, Han, Wei, and Zhao, and the south exchanged envoys with Wu and Yue to cultivate meritorious deeds, give rewards, and get close to the people. As a result, Qi regained stability.
Tian Chang said to Qi Pinggong: "To perform kindness is what people want, you should implement it yourself; if punishment is what people hate, please let me carry it out."
After five years of doing this, the political power of Qi State was controlled by Tian Chang.
So Tian Chang killed all the more powerful of the Bao, Yan, Jianzhi, and Gong clans, and divided the land of Qi from the east of Anping to Langye as his own fiefdom.
summary: Tian Wenzi served Duke Zhuang of Qi, but his son Tian Huanzi gained favor. Tian Lizi, a doctor under Duke Jing, won popular support by using unequal measures to lend and collect grain, amassing power. After Duke Jing’s death, Tian Qi opposed the appointed heir Yan Ruzi, instead installing Yangsheng as Duke Mourning. Tian Qi became prime minister, and his son Tian Chang continued consolidating power. Tian Chang killed rivals like Jian Zhi and Duke Jian, then installed Duke Ping, returning lands to appease other states. He controlled Qi’s government, executed powerful clans, and expanded his fiefdom. His harem of over a hundred concubines bore him seventy sons. Tian Chang’s son Tian Pan succeeded him, and the Tian family dominated Qi, with descendants like Tian He eventually becoming marquises, recognized by the Zhou emperor.

translation:
In the thirty-eighth year, the State of Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate the King of Qin. The King of Qin found out and killed Jing Ke.
The next year, the Qin army captured the capital of Yan, and the king of Yan fled to Liaodong.
In another year, the Qin State destroyed the Wei State, and the Qin army was stationed in Lixia.
In the forty-two years, Qin State destroyed Chu State.
In the second year, he captured Dai Wangjia, killed Yan Wangxi, and destroyed the Yan Kingdom.
In the forty-fourth year of King Qi's founding, Qin attacked Qi.
The king of Qi followed the prime minister's plan to win later and led his army to surrender to Qin without fighting.
Qin captured King Jian of Qi and moved him to Gongcheng.
Finally, the state of Qi was destroyed and turned into a county.
The world was unified by Qin, and the Qin king established the title of emperor.
At first, the king and queen were virtuous, cautious in serving Qin, and had good relations with the princes. Qi was located on the eastern seaboard, and Qin attacked Jin, Yan, and Chu day and night. Facing Qin's attacks, the five countries had to seek self-rescue. Therefore, King Jian of Qi did not suffer from war for more than 40 years in his reign.
After the queen died, Hou Sheng became the prime minister of Qi. He accepted a lot of money from Qin spies and sent many guests to Qin. Qin gave them a lot of money. The guests all came back to carry out counterinsurgency activities and persuaded the king of Qi to give up the alliance and return to Qin. Qin was able to destroy the five kingdoms.
After the five kingdoms were destroyed, the Qin army finally invaded Linzi, and no one dared to resist.
King Jian of Qi surrendered and was moved to Gongcheng.
Therefore, the people of Qi complained that Wang Jian did not join forces with the princes to attack Qin early, and listened to the words of treacherous ministers and guests, which led to the destruction of the country. They made up a song and said: Where is the pine tree or the cypress tree?
Wasn't it the guest who asked Wang Jian to live in Gongcheng?
It means that he hates Wang Jian for using guests without paying attention to inspection.
Tai Shigong said: Probably Confucius liked to read the "Book of Changes" in his later years.
As a piece of knowledge, the Book of Changes predicts the future from tangible and intangible objects. The principles are very profound. Who can focus on it if he is not a wise and reasonable person who is knowledgeable about the past and the present!
Therefore, when Taishi of Zhou Dynasty made divination for Tian Jingzhong, he could make divination for ten generations later. When Tian Wan fled to Qi, Yizhong also made divination for him.
The reason why Tian Qi and Tian Chang killed the two monarchs one after another and took over the power of Qi State is not necessarily because the situation has gradually developed to this point. It may be that they are following or complying with the divination omens!
summary: Tian He’s line continued through Huan Gong and King Wei of Qi. King Wei initially neglected governance, facing invasions, but reformed after executing corrupt officials and rewarding the virtuous. He defeated Wei and Zhao, stabilizing Qi. His minister Zou Ji advised him on governance through music metaphors, and later became a marquis. King Wei’s successors, including King Xuan and King Min, expanded Qi’s influence, with King Min briefly claiming the title of Eastern Emperor. However, King Min’s arrogance led to a coalition attack by Yan, Qin, and others, resulting in his death. His son King Xiang, hidden as a servant, was restored with help from Tian Dan, who defeated Yan. King Xiang’s reign saw Qi’s recovery, but his son King Jian eventually surrendered to Qin without resistance, ending Qi’s independence. The people blamed King Jian’s reliance on corrupt advisors and Qin spies for the fall.
