translation:
Liu Hou Zhang Liang, his ancestors were Koreans.
His grandfather served as the prime minister of Han Zhaohou, King Xuanhui and King Xiangai in Kaidi.
His father, Zhang Ping, served as prime minister to King Li and King Tuohui.
In the twenty-third year of King Hui's reign, his father Zhang Ping passed away.
Twenty years after Zhang Liang's father died, the Qin State destroyed South Korea.
Zhang Liang was young at the time and had not been an official in Korea.
After the fall of Korea, Zhang Liang's family had 300 servants. When Zhang Liang's younger brother died, he was not buried well. He used all his property to find warriors to assassinate the King of Qin and avenge Korea. This was because his grandfather and father had served as the kings of Korea for five generations.
Zhang Liang once studied etiquette in Huaiyang and went to the East to meet Lord Canghai.
He found a strong man and made a hammer weighing 120 kilograms.
Qin Shihuang went on a tour to the East. Zhang Liang and Hercules attacked Qin Shihuang at Bolangsha, and accidentally hit the auxiliary car.
Qin Shihuang was furious and launched a massive search across the country, hoping to catch the assassin quickly. This was exactly what Zhang Liang had caused.
Zhang Liang then changed his name and surname, fled to Xiapi and hid.
Zhang Liang was wandering on the Xiapi Bridge in his spare time. He met an old man wearing coarse clothes. He walked up to Zhang Liang and deliberately threw his shoes under the bridge. He looked at Zhang Liang and said to him: Boy, go down and pick up the shoes!
Zhang Liang was a little surprised and wanted to beat him, but seeing that he was old, he reluctantly endured it and went down to pick up the shoes.
The old man said: Put on my shoes!
Since Zhang Liang had picked up the shoes for him, he knelt down and put them on for him.
The old man stretched out his feet and put on his shoes, smiled and left.
Zhang Liang was very surprised and followed the old man's figure and stared at him.
The old man left for about a mile, then returned and said, "You, my boy, can teach."
Meet me here at dawn five days later. Zhang Liang thought this was strange, knelt down and said, "Yeah."
At dawn five days later, Zhang Liang went there.
The old man was already there first and said angrily: "I date an old man, but I arrive late. Why?"
The old man left and said: Come and meet early in five days.
Five days later, when the rooster crows, Zhang Liang goes.
The old man was there first and said angrily: "I'm late again. Why is this?"
The old man left and said: Come back early in five days.
Five days later, Zhang Liang left before midnight.
After a while, the old man also came and said happily: It should be like this.
The old man took out a book and said: After reading this book, you can become the emperor's teacher.
There will definitely be some development in ten years.
Thirteen years later, when your boy comes to Jibei to meet me, the yellow stone at the foot of Gucheng Mountain will be me.
After saying that, he left without leaving anything else, and he never saw the old man again.
At dawn, I looked at the book given by the old man and found it was "Tai Gong's Art of War".
Zhang Liang felt that this book was extraordinary and often studied and recited it.
When Zhang Liang lived in Xiapi, he was a chivalrous and righteous man.
Xiang Bo once killed someone and hid with Zhang Liang.
Ten years later, Chen She and others rebelled against Qin, and Zhang Liang also gathered more than a hundred young people.
Jing Ju established himself as the acting King of Chu and stationed in Liu County.
summary: Zhang Liang, also known as Liu Hou, was a descendant of Korean nobility. His grandfather and father served as prime ministers to five generations of Korean kings. After Qin destroyed Korea, Zhang Liang, though young and never an official, used his family's wealth to hire an assassin to attack Qin Shi Huang at Bolangsha, but mistakenly struck an auxiliary carriage. Forced to flee, he changed his name and hid in Xiapi. While wandering on a bridge in Xiapi, Zhang Liang encountered an old man who tested him by throwing his shoes and demanding Zhang Liang retrieve and put them on. After passing this test, the oldman gave him the "Tai Gong's Art of War," declaring Zhang Liang would become the emperor's teacher. Zhang Liang studied the book diligently.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家

translation:
Zhang Liang planned to follow him, but met Pei Gong on the way.
Peigong led thousands of men to seize the area west of Xiapi, and Zhang Liang joined him.
Pei Gong appointed Zhang Liang as the stable general.
Zhang Liang offered suggestions to Pei Gong based on "Tai Gong's Art of War" many times. Pei Gong appreciated him and often adopted his strategies.
Zhang Liang taught "Tai Gong's Art of War" to others, but no one could understand it.
Zhang Liang said: Pei Gong was probably bestowed on earth by heaven.
So Zhang Liang followed Pei Gong instead of joining Jingju.
When Pei Gong arrived at Xuedi, he met with Xiang Liang.
Xiang Liang supported King Huai of Chu.
Zhang Liang then persuaded Xiang Liang: "You have already supported the descendants of the King of Chu, and Han Cheng, Lord of Hengyang among the Korean princes, can be made king and increase the strength of his allies."
Xiang Liang sent Zhang Liang to find Han Cheng and made him king of Han.
Appointed Zhang Liang as the Situ of South Korea, and led more than a thousand people to the west to attack South Korea's original territory with the King of Han, and captured several cities. The Qin army soon recaptured them, and the Han army only conducted guerrilla operations in the Yingchuan area.
When Pei Gong passed through the Sheyuan Mountain south from Luoyang, Zhang Liang led his troops to follow Pei Gong, captured more than ten cities in Han, and defeated Yang Xiong's army.
Peigong then asked Han Wangcheng to stay in Yangzhai, and he and Zhang Liang went south to attack Wan County and westward into Wuguan.
Peigong wanted to attack Qin's army at Yaoguan with 20,000 troops. Zhang Liang advised: The Qin army is still very strong and should not be underestimated.
I heard that the guard at Yongguan was the son of a butcher, and it was easy for the philistines to lure him with profit.
He hoped that Pei Gong would stay in the camp for the time being and send people to prepare food for 50,000 people. He also hung more flags on the hills and ordered Li Shi to bring valuable treasures to lure the generals of the Qin army.
As expected, the generals of the Qin army rebelled and planned to join forces with Pei Gong to attack Xianyang westward. Pei Gong wanted to follow the Qin general's plan.
Zhang Liang said: This is just a rebellion by the general at Yaoguan. I am afraid that the soldiers under his command will not listen.
Disobedience of soldiers will definitely bring harm, so it is better to attack them while they are slack.
Peigong then led his troops to attack the Qin army and defeated the enemy.
Then they chased the defeated army to Lantian and fought for the second time. The Qin army finally collapsed.
Then Pei Gong arrived in Xianyang, and Qin Prince Ying surrendered to Pei Gong.
Pei Gong entered the Qin Palace. There were thousands of palaces, tents, dogs and horses, precious treasures, and beautiful women. Pei Gong's intention was to stay in the palace.
Fan Kuai advised Pei Gong to go out and live there, but Pei Gong refused to listen.
Zhang Liang said: The Qin Dynasty was tyrannical and immoral, so Pei Gong was able to come here.
To eradicate cruel tyranny from the world, we should be honest and simple.
Now that we have just invaded the capital of Qin, we have to enjoy it in peace. This is what people say, "helping Jie to do harm."
Moreover, good advice is unpleasant to the ear but beneficial to action, and good medicine is bitter to the mouth and beneficial to the patient. I hope Pei Gong will listen to Fan Kuai's opinion.
summary: During the rebellions against Qin, Zhang Liang gathered followers and joined Pei Gong (Liu Bang), becoming his trusted advisor. He used strategies from the Art of War to advise Pei Gong, who appreciated his counsel. Zhang Liang persuaded Xiang Liang to restore Han Cheng as King of Han, and Zhang Liang served as his Situ. He later rejoined Pei Gong, advising him against attacking the Qin army at Yao Pass directly, instead suggesting bribery and deception, leading to Qin's surrender.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/留侯世家

translation:
Only then did Pei Gong return to his carriage and stop at Bashang.
Xiang Yu came to Hongmen and wanted to attack Pei Gong. Xiang Bo rushed to Pei Gong's camp overnight and met with Zhang Liang privately, hoping that Zhang Liang would leave with him.
Zhang Liang said: I am escorting Pei Gong on behalf of the King of Han. Now the situation is urgent and it is unethical to escape.
So he told Pei Gong everything.
Pei Gong was very surprised and said: "What will we do about this?"
Zhang Liang said: Does Pei Gong really want to betray Xiang Yu?
Pei Gong said: "The ignorant villain taught me to block Hangu Pass and prevent the princes from entering. He said that in this way the land of the Qin Dynasty could be completely controlled, so I followed this advice."
Zhang Liang said: Pei Gong thinks for himself, can he defeat Xiang Yu?
Pei Gong was silent for a while and then said, "It shouldn't be possible. What should we do now?"
Zhang Liang then firmly invited Xiang Bo to see Pei Gong.
Xiang Bo met with Pei Gong.
Pei Gong drank with Xiang Bo, toasted and blessed him, and married him.
Pei Gong asked Xiang Bo to explain to Xiang Yu in detail that Pei Gong did not dare to betray Xiang Yu. The reason why Pei Gong blocked Hangu Pass was to prevent other bandits.
After Pei Gong met with Xiang Yu, the two parties reached a reconciliation, which was recorded in "The Notes of Xiang Yu".
In the first month of the first year of the Han Dynasty, Peigong became the king of Han and ruled the Bashu region.
The king of Han rewarded Zhang Liang with a hundred yi of gold and two measures of pearls. Zhang Liang gave them all to Xiang Bo.
Therefore, the King of Han asked Zhang Lianghou to give Xiang Bo a gift, so that Xiang Bo asked King Xiang to allocate the Hanzhong area to him on his behalf.
King Xiang agreed to the request of the King of Han, and the King of Han obtained the Hanzhong area.
The King of Han went to Fengguo, Zhang Liang sent the King of Han to Baozhong, and the King of Han asked Zhang Liang to return to Korea.
Zhang Liang then advised the King of Han: "Why don't you burn down the plank road you pass by to express your determination not to come back to the world, so as to stabilize King Xiang's heart?"
The king of Han then asked Zhang Liang to return to Korea.
When the king of Han was marching, he burned down the plank road he passed.
Zhang Liang arrived in South Korea. Because Han Wangcheng asked Zhang Liang to follow the king of Han, King Xiang did not send Han Cheng to the feudal country, but asked him to follow him eastward.
Zhang Liang explained to King Xiang: The King of Han burned down the plank road and has no intention of returning.
Zhang Liang then wrote to King Xiang about the rebellion of King Tian Rong of Qi.
King Xiang no longer worried about the King of Han in the west, so he raised his troops north to attack Qi.
King Xiang still refused to send King Han back to Korea. Instead, he demoted King Han to the rank of Marquis and killed him in Pengcheng.
Zhang Liang fled and secretly returned to the King of Han by taking a small road. At this time, the King of Han had returned to his army to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties.
The king of Han also granted Zhang Liang the title of Marquis Chengxin and followed him eastward to conquer Chu.
When they arrived at Pengcheng, the Han army was defeated and returned.
When he arrived at Xiayi, the King of Han dismounted and leaned on the saddle and asked: I plan to give up some places east of Hanguguan and other places as rewards. Who can join me in making achievements?
Zhang Liang Jin said: King Yingbu of Jiujiang is a fierce general of Chu, and there is a barrier with King Xiang; Peng Yue and Qi King Tian Rong rebelled against Chu in Liang. These two are available immediately.
summary: After entering Xianyang, Zhang Liang convinced Pei Gong to leave the Qin palace and avoid luxury, warning it would harm his cause. At the Hongmen Banquet, Zhang Liang helped Pei Gong reconcile with Xiang Yu. When Pei Gong became King of Han, Zhang Liang advised burning the plank road to show no intention of returning east, stabilizing Xiang Yu. He later recommended using Yingbu, Peng Yue, and Han Xin to defeat Chu.

translation:
Zhang Liang said: This is the third reason why the descendants of the Six Kingdoms cannot be enfeoffed.
King Wu of Zhou once distributed grain from the Juqiao warehouse and money from the Lutai treasury to the poor.
Can your Majesty now distribute the money and food in the treasury to the poor?
The king of Han said: No.
Zhang Liang said: This is the fourth reason why the descendants of the Six Kingdoms cannot be enfeoffed.
After King Wu of Zhou destroyed the Shang Dynasty, he abandoned the chariots and modified them into manned vehicles. He stacked all war weapons upside down, covered them with tiger skins, and told everyone in the world that they would never fight again.
Can your Majesty now give up force, advocate civil rule, and stop fighting?
The king of Han said: No.
Zhang Liang said: This is the fifth reason why the descendants of the Six Kingdoms cannot be enfeoffed.
King Wu of Zhou once put all his war horses south of Mount Hua to be pastured, as a sign that he would no longer fight.
Can your Majesty now allow the war horses to rest and not be used again?
The king of Han said: No.
Zhang Liang said: This is the sixth reason why the descendants of the Six Kingdoms cannot be enfeoffed.
King Wu of Zhou once put the cattle transporting grain and grass to the north of Taolin for grazing, to show that he no longer needed to transport and store military grain.
Can your Majesty now graze cattle instead of using them to transport and store grain?
The king of Han said: No.
Zhang Liang said: This is the seventh reason why the descendants of the Six Kingdoms cannot be enfeoffed.
Travelers all over the world stay away from their relatives, abandon their ancestral graves, say goodbye to their hometown friends, and follow His Majesty to fight everywhere, looking forward to it day and night just to get a fiefdom.
Now your Majesty has re-divided the descendants of the Six Kingdoms and established the descendants of Han, Wei, Yan, Zhao, Qi and Chu as princes and kings. The wanderers in the world have returned to serve their monarchs, reunite with their long-lost relatives, and return to their old friends and hometowns where their ancestral graves are. Who will your Majesty go with to conquer the world?
This is the eighth reason why the descendants of the Six Kingdoms cannot be enfeoffed.
Moreover, the Chu State is currently invincible in the world. The descendants of the six kingdoms you have re-enfranchised will all surrender to the Chu State. What method can your Majesty have to make them surrender?
If your majesty really adopts the diner's plan, your majesty's great affairs will be ruined.
The King of Han stopped eating, spit out the food in his mouth, and cursed: This ignorant person almost ruined my big event!
Immediately ordered the seal to be destroyed immediately.
In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, Han Xin wanted to proclaim himself king of Qi after conquering Qi, but the king of Han was furious.
Zhang Liang advised the King of Han, and the King of Han sent Zhang Liang to grant Han Xin the seal of King Xin of Qi. This matter was recorded in the "Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin".
In the autumn of this year, the king of Han pursued the Chu army to the south of Yangxia. Because of the defeat in the battle, he held fast to the Guling camp. The princes did not come on the appointed day.
Zhang Liang proposed a plan to the king of Han, and the king of Han adopted his plan, and all the princes came.
This incident is recorded in "The Chronicles of Xiang Yu".
In the first month of the sixth year of Han Dynasty, Emperor Gao rewarded the meritorious officials.
Zhang Liang had no military exploits. Emperor Gao said: "It is the contribution of Zifang to make plans in the camp and decide the victory or defeat thousands of miles away."
Zhang Liang was asked to select 30,000 households from Qi State as fiefdoms.
summary: Zhang Liang opposed enfeoffing descendants of the six kingdoms, arguing it would undermine Liu Bang's support. He convinced Liu Bang to grant Han Xin the title of King of Qi. After the Han dynasty was established, Liu Bang praised Zhang Liang's strategic contributions and offered him 30,000 households, but Zhang Liang accepted only a county, becoming Marquis of Liu.

translation:
He was frail and sickly by nature, so he practiced Tao Yin's technique and refused to eat grains. He stayed in seclusion for more than a year.
The emperor wanted to depose the prince and establish Ruyi, the son of Mrs. Qi's son, King Zhao.
Many ministers tried to dissuade him, but they failed to change Emperor Gao's unwavering mind.
Queen Lu was frightened and didn't know what to do.
Someone said to Queen Lu: Marquis Liu is good at making suggestions, and the emperor trusts him very much.
Empress Lu sent Lu Ze, the Marquis of Jiancheng, to coerce Marquis Liu, saying: "You have always been the emperor's adviser. Now the emperor plans to replace the prince. How can you sit back and relax?"
Liuhou said: The emperor was in crisis many times and adopted my strategy.
Now that the world is at peace, if I want to change the crown prince due to my preference, what good will it do even if more than a hundred people like me come to remonstrate with me about these matters between close relatives?
Lu Ze tried his best to threaten and said: You must give me an idea.
Liu Hou said: This matter is difficult to argue with words.
There are four people in the world who cannot be provoked by the emperor.
These four people were already old, and they all thought that the emperor was arrogant, so they fled and hid in the mountains. They refused to be ministers of the Han Dynasty according to morality.
But the emperor respected these four people very much.
Now if you can really spare no expense on money and silk, ask the prince to write a letter, be polite in your words, prepare a carriage, and send eloquent people to earnestly invite them, they should come.
After arriving, treat them as distinguished guests, let them follow you into the court from time to time, and ask the emperor to see them. Then the emperor will be surprised and ask about them.
When he asked them, the emperor knew that these four people were capable, so this would be a help to the prince.
So Empress Lu asked Lu Ze to send someone to carry the prince's letter and greet the four people with humble words and generous gifts.
Four people came and stayed as guests in the mansion of Marquis Jiancheng.
In the eleventh year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu rebelled. The emperor was seriously ill at this time and planned to send the prince to lead his troops to attack the rebels.
The four people discussed with each other and said: The reason why we are here is to protect the prince. If the prince leads troops to suppress the rebellion, things will be dangerous.
So he advised Marquis Jiancheng: If the prince leads his troops to battle and achieves success, his position will not be higher than that of the prince; if he returns without success, he will suffer disaster from now on.
Besides, the generals who went on the expedition with the prince were all fierce generals who once conquered the world with the emperor. Now letting the prince lead these people is no different from letting a sheep command a wolf. They will never work hard for the prince. It is certain that the prince cannot make achievements.
We heard that if you love your mother, you must embrace your son. Now Mrs. Qi serves the emperor day and night, and Zhao Wang Ruyi is often held in front of the emperor. The emperor said, "After all, I cannot let my incompetent son be placed above my beloved son. Obviously, it is inevitable that Zhao Wang Ruyi will replace the crown prince."
Why don't you quickly ask Empress Lu to take the opportunity to cry to the emperor: Ying Bu is a fierce general in the world and is very good at using troops. All the generals today are your Majesty's contemporaries in the past, but you let the prince lead these people. This is no different from letting a sheep command a wolf. No one is willing to serve the prince, and if Ying Bu hears about this situation, he will invade westward with great fanfare.
Although the emperor was ill, he could still manage to ride in a carriage and command the army while lying down, and the generals dared not fail to do their best.
Although the emperor has suffered some hardships, he still has to work hard for his wife and children.
So Lu Ze immediately went to see Empress Lu that night. Empress Lu found an opportunity to cry to the emperor and said what the four people had instructed her to do.
The emperor said: "I just thought that this guy couldn't be sent. I should go myself."
So the emperor personally led the troops to march eastward, while all the officials stayed behind and sent them to Ba Shang.
When Liuhou fell ill, he managed to support himself and sent him to Quyou. He went to see the emperor and said, "I should have gone with you, but I was seriously ill."
The Chu people and horses are very fast and agile. I hope the emperor will not compete with the Chu people.
Liuhou took the opportunity to persuade the emperor: Let the prince be a general and oversee the army in Guanzhong.
The emperor said: Although the ovary is sick, she still has to help the prince while he is in bed and recuperating.
At this time, Shusun Tong was appointed as Taifu, and Liu Hou was appointed as Shaofu.
In the twelfth year of the Han Dynasty, the emperor returned with the army that defeated Yingbu. His illness became more serious and he wanted to replace the prince even more.
The emperor refused to listen to Liu Hou's advice, so Liu Hou excused himself from the affairs because of illness.
Taifu Shusun quoted ancient and modern examples to persuade him, and fought desperately to protect the prince.
The emperor pretended to agree to him, but still wanted to change the prince.
When there is leisure, a banquet will be set up, and the prince will be waiting on him.
The four men followed the prince. They were all in their eighties, with white men and eyebrows, and very magnificent and unique clothes.
The emperor felt strange and asked: "What do they do?"
The four people came forward to answer each other's questions, and each said his name: Dong Yuan Gong, Mr. Jiao Li, Qili Ji, and Xia Huang Gong.
The emperor was shocked and said: I have been visiting you for several years, but you have all avoided me. Why do you voluntarily follow me to socialize with me now?
All four said: Your Majesty is contemptuous of scholars and likes to curse. We are righteous and do not want to be humiliated, so we fled in fear.
We have heard privately that the prince is benevolent, filial, courteous, and loves scholars. There is no one in the world who would not stretch their neck to serve the prince to the death. So here we are.
The emperor said: Please take good care of and protect the prince.
The four people finished toasting and blessing, and walked away quickly.
The emperor watched them off, summoned Mrs. Qi, pointed to the four people, and said, "I want to replace the prince. The four of them will assist him. The prince's wings have already been formed and it is difficult to change them."
Queen Lu is truly your master.
Qi Fu began to cry, and the emperor said: You dance Chu dances for me, and I sing Chu songs for you.
The emperor sang: The swan flies high, fluttering its wings for thousands of miles.
The wings are ready, soaring all over the world.
Soaring all over the world, there is nothing you can do!
summary: Zhang Liang advised moving the capital to Guanzhong for its strategic advantages. When Liu Bang wanted to depose the crown prince, Zhang Liang suggested inviting four reclusive sages to support the prince. Their presence convinced Liu Bang the prince's position was secure. Zhang Liang later practiced Taoist techniques, abstained from grain, and sought to travel with the immortal Chisongzi. He died eight years after Liu Bang, posthumously named Wencheng Hou. His son inherited the title but lost it due to misconduct.

translation:
Guan Shuxian and Cai Shudu were both sons of King Wen of Zhou and younger brothers of King Wu of Zhou.
There were ten brothers from the same mother of King Wu of Zhou.
Their mother's name was Taisi, who was King Wen's wife.
Her eldest son is Boyikao, followed by Wu Wangfa, Guan Shuxian, Zhou Gongdan, Cai Shudu, Cao Shuzhenduo, Cheng Shuwu, Huo Shuchu, Kang Shufeng, and the youngest is Ran Jizai.
Among the ten brothers, only Wu Wangfa and Zhou Gongdan were highly virtuous and talented, and they were the right-hand men to assist King Wen. Therefore, King Wen did not establish Boyikao, but made his second son Fa the crown prince.
After King Wen died, Prince Fa came to the throne and became King Wu.
Boyikao had passed away before this.
After King Wu defeated King Zhou of Yin and pacified the world, he granted great titles to his heroes and brothers.
So he enfeoffed the administrative land to Shuxian and the Cai land to Shudu; and made them ministers to the father of Wu Genglu, the son of Zhou, to govern the remnants of the Yin people together.
He enfeoffed the land of Lu to Shu Dan, and at the same time made Shu Dan the prime minister of the Zhou Dynasty, so he was called Zhou Gong.
Shu Zhenduo was granted the title of Cao Di, Shu Wu was granted the title of Cheng Di, and Shu Chu was granted the title of Huo Di.
Uncle Kang and Ran Jizai were young at that time, so they were not awarded the title.
After King Wu died, King Cheng succeeded to the throne at a young age, and Duke Zhou took control of the country.
Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai suspected that Duke Zhou's actions were not conducive to becoming king, so they supported Wu Geng in the rebellion.
Zhou Gongdan conquered the rebels according to the decree of King Cheng, executed Wu Geng, killed Guan Shu and exiled Cai Shu. During the exile, Cai Shu was only given a carriage and seventy prisoners as his entourage.
The survivors of the Southern Dynasties were also divided into two parts: part of the Song Dynasty was granted to Wei Ziqi to continue the sacrifices of the Yin Dynasty; and part of the Wei Dynasty was established to establish the Wei Kingdom and appointed Uncle Kang as the king of the Wei Kingdom, which was Uncle Kang of Wei.
He also entrusted the land of Ran to Ji Zai.
Ran Ji and Uncle Kang had good conduct, so Duke Zhou recommended Uncle Kang to be the Sikong of the Zhou Dynasty, and Ran Ji to be the Sikong of the Zhou Dynasty. The two assisted King Cheng in governing the country, and their reputation spread throughout the world.
Cai Shudu died after being exiled.
His son's name was Hu. Hu changed his father's old behavior, followed moral precepts, and practiced good deeds.
After Duke Zhou heard about it, he recommended him to be a minister of the state of Lu. The state of Lu was governed very well.
The Duke of Zhou suggested to King Cheng that Hu should be granted a title in the land of Cai, in order to perform the annual sacrificial ceremony for Uncle Cai, who was Cai Zhong. The other five uncles returned to their respective kingdoms and did not serve as officials in the Zhou court.
Cai Zhong died and his son Cai Bohuang succeeded him.
Cai Bohuang died and his son Gonghou succeeded to the throne.
Gong Hou died and his son Li Hou succeeded to the throne.
Marquis Li died and his son Marquis Wu succeeded him.
When Wuhou was on the throne, King Zhou Li lost his throne and fled to the land of Hu. Duke Zhou and Duke Zhao were in power together, and many princes rebelled against the Zhou family.
Wuhou died and his son Yihou succeeded to the throne.
summary: The lineage and history of the sons of King Wen of Zhou, focusing on Guan Shuxian and Cai Shudu, younger brothers of King Wu. King Wu had ten brothers from the same mother, Taisi. Among them, only King Wu and Zhou Gongdan were virtuous and talented, leading King Wen to make Fa (King Wu) crown prince. After King Wu conquered the Yin, he enfeoffed lands to his brothers: Shuxian received Guan, Shudu received Cai, and they were made ministers to Wu Geng, son of the Yin king. Zhou Gongdan was enfeoffed in Lu and served as prime minister. Other brothers received Cao, Cheng, and Huo. Kang Shu and Ran Jizai were too young for titles.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/管蔡世家

translation:
In the 19th year, Chenghou died and his son Shenghou Chan succeeded to the throne.
Shenghou died in the fifteenth year, and his son Yuanhou succeeded to the throne.
Yuan Hou died in the sixth year, and his son Hou Qi succeeded to the throne.
In the fourth year of Hou Qi's reign, King Hui of Chu destroyed the State of Cai, and Hou Qi of Cai fled. From then on, the sacrifices of the State of Cai were cut off, and the country was destroyed, thirty-three years later than the State of Chen.
Boyikao's descendants don't know where they were sealed.
The descendant of Wu Wangfa was Zhou Wang, which is recorded in "Benji".
Guan Shuxian rebelled and was killed, leaving no descendants.
The descendants of Zhou Gongdan were the monarchs of Lu State, which are recorded in "Shijia".
The descendants of Cai Shudu are the monarchs of Cai State, which are recorded in "Guan Cai Family".
The descendants of Cao Shu Zhenduo are the monarchs of Cao State, which are recorded in "Guan Cai Family".
The whereabouts of Cheng Shuwu's descendants are unknown.
The descendants of Huo Shuchu were enfeoffed in Huo Di and were later destroyed by Duke Xian of Jin.
The descendants of Kang Shufeng are the monarchs of Wei State, which are recorded in "Wei Kangshu Family".
The whereabouts of Ran Jizai's descendants are unknown.
Tai Shigong said: There is nothing worth recording about the rebellion of Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai.
However, after King Wu of Zhou died and King Cheng was young, everyone in the world doubted Duke Zhou. It was only with the help of Cheng Shu, Ran Ji and ten other people, including his mother and brothers, that all the princes in the world respected the Zhou family, so their deeds were appended to the "Aristocratic Family".
Cao Shu Zhenduo was the younger brother of King Wu of Zhou. After King Wu defeated Shang Zhou, he enfeoffed the land of Cao to Shu Zhenduo.
Shu Zhenduo died, and his son Taibo Pi succeeded to the throne.
Tai Bo died and his son Zhong Junping came to the throne.
Zhong Junping died, and his son Xian Bohou succeeded to the throne.
When Xian Bohou passed away, his son Xiao Boyun succeeded him.
Xiao Boyun died, and his son Yi Boxi succeeded him.
In the twenty-third year of Yibo, King Li of Zhou fled to the land of pigs.
Yi Bo died in the 30th year, and his younger brother You Boqiang succeeded to the throne.
In the ninth year of Youbo's reign, his younger brother Su killed Youbo and established himself as the king of the country. He was Daibo.
In the first year of Dai Bo, King Zhou Xuan had been on the throne for three years.
Thirty years later, Dai Bo died and his son Hui Boyi succeeded him.
In the twenty-fifth year of Huibo's reign, King You of Zhou was killed by Quan Rong. The royal family moved eastward and became increasingly weak. The princes betrayed the royal family one after another.
Qin State began to be classified as a vassal state in this year.
In the thirty-sixth year, Hui Bo died and his son Shi Fu succeeded to the throne. His younger brother Wu killed Shi Fu and made himself king, namely Duke Mu.
Duke Mu died after reigning for three years, and his son Duke Huan succeeded him for life.
In the thirty-fifth year of Duke Huan, Duke Yin of Lu succeeded to the throne.
Forty-five years ago, the people of Lu killed Duke Yin.
In the forty-sixth year, Governor Hua Fu of the Song Dynasty killed Song Shang Gong and the doctor Kong Fu.
In the fifty-fifth year, Cao Huan Gong passed away, and his son Zhuang Gong Xi Gu succeeded to the throne.
summary: After King Wu died, King Cheng succeeded as a child, and Zhou Gongdan ruled as regent. Guan Shu and Cai Shu, suspecting Zhou Gong's intentions, rebelled with Wu Geng. Zhou Gong crushed the rebellion, executing Wu Geng and Guan Shu, and exiling Cai Shu. Cai Shu died in exile, but his son Hu reformed and was later enfeoffed in Cai by Zhou Gong's recommendation. The text then traces the succession of Cai rulers through generations, including conflicts with Chu and Qi. Key events include Cai Aihou's capture by Chu, Cai Miao Hou's conflict with Duke Huan of Qi over a marriage dispute, and Cai's eventual destruction by King Hui of Chu after 33 years. The text also covers the lineage of Cao Shu Zhenduo, another brother, whose descendants ruled Cao until its destruction by Song. It notes that Guan Shu left no descendants, while Zhou Gongdan's descendants ruled Lu, and Kang Shu's descendants ruled Wei. The historian concludes that Guan and Cai's rebellion was unremarkable, but Zhou Gong's regency stabilized the Zhou dynasty. The dream of a Cao man predicting the state's fall is recounted, ending with Cao's destruction due to poor governance under Boyang and Gongsun Qiang.

translation:
After Xiang Yu's death, he took the opportunity to move east to pacify Chu Sishui and Donghai counties, occupying a total of 22 counties.
He then returned to guard Luoyang and Yueyang. The king of Han gave Zhongli to Zhou Bo and Guan Ying as a common food town for them.
Zhou Bo followed Gaozu as a general to conquer Zang Tu, King of Yan, who rebelled against the Han Dynasty, and defeated them at the gate of Yi County.
The soldiers led by Zhou Bo resisted the enemy on the carriage road and made many military exploits.
Zhou Bo was granted the title of Marquis, and Emperor Gaozu split the talisman to ensure that Zhou Bo's title would be passed down from generation to generation and would never be extinguished.
8,180 households in Jiang County were given as food towns, known as Jianghou.
Zhou Bo followed Gaozu as a general to conquer Han Wangxin who rebelled against the Han Dynasty in Dai, and surrendered Huoren County.
Then move forward to Wuquan, attack the Hu cavalry, and defeat them north of Wuquan.
Then he moved to Tongtian to attack Han Wangxin's army and defeated them.
He returned to the army and surrendered six cities in Taiyuan County.
At the foot of Jinyang City, the Hu cavalry attacked King Xin of Han, defeated them, and captured Jinyang.
Then he attacked King Xin of Han's army at Rangshi, defeated them, and chased the defeated soldiers for eighty miles.
Returning to attack the three cities in Loufan, they took advantage of the situation to attack the Hu cavalry under Pingcheng. The soldiers led by Zhou Bo resisted the enemy troops on the carriage road and gained the most military exploits.
Zhou Bo was promoted to Taiwei.
Zhou Bo attacked the rebel general Chen Xi and massacred the city in Mayi County.
The soldiers he led beheaded Chen Xi's general on horseback.
Attacked Han Wangxin, Chen Xi, and Zhao Li's troops in Loufan, defeated them, and captured Chen Xi's general Song Zui and Yanmen County Guards.
Taking advantage of the situation, he turned to attack Yunzhong County and captured the county governor, Prime Minister Ji Si and General Xun.
The seventeen counties of Yanmen County and the twelve counties of Yunzhong County were pacified.
Taking advantage of the situation, he attacked Chen Xi in Lingqiu, defeated his army, beheaded Chen Xi, and captured Chen Xi's prime minister Cheng Zong, general Chen Wu, and captain Gao Si.
Pingding Daijun nine counties.
King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled, and Zhou Bo led the troops on Fan Kuai's behalf as Prime Minister, captured Jixian, captured Lu Wan's general Da, Prime Minister Yan, County Shou Xing, Tai Wei Ruo, and Yushi doctor Shi, etc., and massacred Hundu City.
Defeated Lu Wan's rebels in Shanglan, and defeated Lu Wan's rebels in Juyang.
They pursued to the Great Wall and pacified twelve counties in Shanggu County, sixteen counties in Youbeiping County, twenty-nine counties in western and eastern Liaoning, and twenty-two counties in Yuyang County.
He followed Gaozu on the expedition and captured one prime minister and two prime ministers, three officials each with an annual salary of two thousand dan. He also defeated two armies, captured three cities, pacified five counties and seventy-nine counties, and captured one prime minister and one general.
Zhou Bo was a simple, strong, honest and loyal man. Emperor Gaozu believed that he could entrust him with important matters.
Zhou Bo didn't like literature and learning. Whenever he summoned Confucian scholars and lobbyists, he would sit facing east and ask them: Tell me quickly!
His simple young literary talent is like this.
After Zhou Bo pacified Yan, he returned to the dynasty. Gaozu had passed away, and he served Emperor Hui as a prince.
In the sixth year of Emperor Hui's reign, the official position of Taiwei was established and Zhou Bo was appointed as Taiwei.
summary: Zhou Bo, a native of Peixian County, began his career as a weaver and funeral musician before becoming a warrior. He followed Liu Bang (later Emperor Gaozu) from the early days of his uprising, participating in numerous battles against the Qin dynasty and other forces. Zhou Bo distinguished himself in combat, often being the first to scale city walls, and was granted titles and rewards, including the Marquis of Weiwu and later the Marquis of Jiang, with a fief of 8,180 households. He continued to serve as a general under Gaozu, suppressing rebellions by Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Lu Wan, pacifying many counties and capturing numerous enemy officials. Zhou Bo was known for his simplicity, strength, and loyalty, though he had little regard for scholarly learning.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/绛侯周勃世家

translation:
Ten years later, Empress Lu died.
Lu Lu served as the general of the Han Dynasty as King Zhao, and Lu Chan served as the Prime Minister of the Han Dynasty as King Lu. They controlled the political power of the Han Dynasty and wanted to overthrow the Liu family.
Zhou Bo, as a lieutenant, could not enter the military camp; Chen Ping, as a prime minister, could not handle government affairs.
So Zhou Bo and Chen Ping planned to finally annihilate the Lu family and establish Emperor Xiaowen.
The intercession on this matter is recorded in "The Chronicles of Empress Dowager Lu" and "The Chronicles of Xiaowen".
After Emperor Wen came to the throne, he appointed Zhou Bo as the right prime minister, and gave him five thousand catties of gold and ten thousand households with food. More than a month later, someone persuaded Zhou Bo: You have killed the Lu family and established King Dai as the emperor, which is powerful in the world.
You receive generous rewards and are in a distinguished position. If you are favored like this, disaster will befall you over time. Zhou Bo was afraid and felt that he was in danger, so he resigned and asked for the return of the seal.
The emperor agreed to his request.
More than a year later, Prime Minister Chen Ping passed away. The emperor appointed Zhou Bo as prime minister.
After more than ten months, the emperor said: A few days ago, I ordered all the princes to go to their fiefdoms. Some of them have not left yet. Prime Minister, you are a person I value very much. I hope you will take the lead and go first!
So he was relieved of his position as prime minister and returned to his fiefdom.
After returning to the fiefdom for more than a year, whenever the governor and lieutenants of Hedong visited Dajiang County in various counties, Zhou Bo, the Marquis of Jiang, was afraid of being killed. He often wore armor and ordered his family members to hold weapons to meet the governor and lieutenants.
Later, someone wrote a letter to accuse Zhou Bo of rebelling. The emperor handed over the matter to Tingwei, the chief officer in charge of the prison. Tingwei in turn handed the matter over to Chang'an. The prison officer in Chang'an arrested Zhou Bo for interrogation.
Zhou Bo was scared and didn't know how to answer.
The jailers gradually bullied and humiliated him.
Zhou Bo gave a thousand pieces of gold to the jailer, and the jailer wrote on the back of the wooden slip to remind him: Let the princess bear witness for you.
The princess was the daughter of Emperor Wen, and Zhou Bo's eldest son Shengzhi married her, so the jailer taught Zhou Bo to let her come out to testify.
Zhou Bo gave all the rewards he received to Empress Dowager Bo's brother Bo Zhao.
When the case came to a critical juncture, Bo Zhao interceded with Empress Dowager Bo on behalf of Zhou Bo, and the Empress Dowager also believed that there would be no rebellion.
Emperor Wen met with the Empress Dowager. The Empress Dowager grabbed the scarf and threw it at Emperor Wen, saying: It turns out that Jianghou was carrying the emperor's seal and was leading the troops in the Northern Army. He didn't rebel at that time. Now he lives in a small county. Will he rebel instead?
Emperor Wen had already seen Jianghou's confession, so he apologized to the Queen Mother and said: The jailer just found out clearly and wanted to let him out.
So he sent an envoy with a talisman to pardon Jianghou and restore his title and food.
After Jianghou was released from prison, he said: I am leading an army of millions, but how do I know the dignity of the jailer?
Jianghou returned to his fiefdom.
He died in the eleventh year of Emperor Wen's reign, and his posthumous title was Marquis Wu.
His son Katsuyuki inherited the title.
Six years later, the princess he married was at odds with him, and because he committed murder, the fiefdom was abolished.
The title was suspended for a year before Emperor Wen selected Zhou Yafu, the virtuous governor of Hanoi County, from the sons of Jianghou Zhou Bo, and named him Tiaohou to succeed Jianghou's title.
When Zhou Yafu, the Marquis of Tiao, was still serving as the governor of Hanoi County without the title of Marquis, Xu Negation looked at his prime minister and said: You will be granted the title of Marquis in three years. After eight years of being granted the title of Marquis, you will be appointed as general and prime minister. You will be in charge of the power of the country.
summary: After Gaozu's death, Zhou Bo served Emperor Hui as a prince and later as Taiwei. Following Empress Lu's death, the Lu family attempted to seize power. Zhou Bo, alongside Chen Ping, plotted to annihilate the Lu clan and established Emperor Wen. For this, he was appointed Right Prime Minister and given generous rewards. However, fearing his own power, he resigned and returned to his fief. Later, he was falsely accused of rebellion, imprisoned, and humiliated by jailers. He was eventually released after his daughter (the emperor's daughter-in-law) and Empress Dowager Bo interceded. He died in the eleventh year of Emperor Wen's reign, posthumously titled Marquis Wu.

translation:
When my brother Dou Changjun was alive, he could not be granted the title of marquis. After his death, his son Peng Zu was granted the title of marquis instead. I regret this very much. Your Majesty, please make Wang Xin a marquis as soon as possible!
Emperor Jing said: This matter needs to be discussed with the Prime Minister.
Emperor Jing discussed with the prime minister, and Zhou Yafu said: Emperor Gao had stipulated that people who were not from the Liu family could not be crowned kings, and people who had not made meritorious deeds could not be crowned marquis. Anyone who did not abide by this rule could be attacked by everyone in the world.
Although Wang Xin is the elder brother of the queen, he has no meritorious service. Making him a marquis is against the Emperor Gaozu's protocol.
Emperor Jing was speechless after hearing this and had to give up.
Later, the Xiongnu king Wei Xulu and five others surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Emperor Jing wanted to make them marquis to encourage those who came after them.
Prime Minister Zhou Yafu said: A few of them betrayed their monarch and surrendered to Your Majesty. If Your Majesty makes them marquis, how can you blame the unruly ministers?
Emperor Jing said: The Prime Minister's opinion cannot be adopted.
So Wei Xulu and others were all made marquises.
Zhou Yafu therefore claimed to be ill and retired to his home.
In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Zhou Yafu was dismissed as prime minister due to illness.
Soon, Emperor Jing summoned Tiaohou in the palace and rewarded him with food and wine.
There was only a large piece of meat on the table, no chopped meat, and no chopsticks.
Tiao Hou was dissatisfied, turned around and asked the official in charge of the banquet to bring chopsticks.
Emperor Jing smiled when he saw it and said, "Can't these meet your needs?"
Tiaohou took off his hat to apologize.
The emperor stood up, and Tiao Hou took the opportunity to retreat quickly.
Emperor Jing watched him go out. Said: People like this who show dissatisfaction when encountering things cannot be the servants of the young master!
Soon after, Tiaohou's son bought five hundred pieces of armor and shields for his father from a worker who specialized in making household supplies.
The moving workers were very tired, but they were not paid.
When the employees found out that he secretly bought the utensils for the emperor, they became angry and sued Zhou Yafu's son to rebel. Naturally, the matter involved Marquis Tiao.
The employee's petition was submitted to Emperor Jing, who handed it over to the officials for investigation.
The officials questioned Tiaohou one by one according to the contents of the document, but Tiaohou refused to answer.
Emperor Jing scolded him and said, "I won't use you anymore."
And ordered Zhou Yafu to be handed over to Tingwei.
Tingwei asked: "Do you want to rebel?"
Zhou Yafu said: The utensils I bought are all for burial. How can I say that I want to rebel?
The jailer said: Even if you don't rebel above ground, you should go underground to rebel!
The jailer's persecution became more and more intense.
At first, when the jailer arrested Tiao Hou, Tiao Hou wanted to commit suicide, but his wife stopped him. Therefore, he did not die and went to Tingwei's prison.
Zhou Yafu didn't eat for five days, vomited blood and died.
His fiefdom was removed.
summary: Zhou Bo's son Zhou Shengzhi inherited the title but lost it due to murder. Emperor Wen then selected Zhou Yafu, another son, as Marquis of Tiao. Xu Negation predicted Zhou Yafu would be a marquis, general, and prime minister but would starve to death. Zhou Yafu became a general, famously commanding the Xiliu camp with strict discipline, impressing Emperor Wen. During the Rebellion of the Seven States, he served as Taiwei, successfully defeating Wu and Chu by cutting off their food supplies, though this earned him the enmity of King Xiao of Liang. He later became prime minister but fell out of favor with Emperor Jing over disputes regarding the appointment of marquises, including opposing the enfeoffment of the queen's brother Wang Xin and Xiongnu defectors. Zhou Yafu was eventually dismissed as prime minister. After a banquet where he showed dissatisfaction with the lack of chopsticks, Emperor Jing viewed him as unfit for service. His son's purchase of burial armor led to accusations of rebellion. Zhou Yafu was imprisoned, refused to eat for five days, and died of vomiting blood. His fief was abolished. Sima Qian commented that while Zhou Bo saved the state from crisis, Zhou Yafu, despite his military dignity, lacked humility and met a tragic end.

translation:
King Jing Liu Jia is from the Liu clan, but it is not known which branch of the Liu clan he belongs to. When the trouble first broke out, it was the first year of the Han Dynasty.
The King of Han returned from Hanzhong to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, appointed Liu Jia as general, and asked him to pacify the Sedi, and then followed the King of Han to attack Xiang Yu from the east.
In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han was defeated at Chenggao. He crossed the Yellow River north and got the troops of Zhang Er and Han Xin. They stationed themselves in Xiuwu. They dug deep trenches and built high forts. He sent Liu Jia to lead two armies and hundreds of cavalry to cross Baima Jin and enter the Chu land. They burned the grain and grass stored there and destroyed the industry there so that they could not supply King Xiang with military grain.
Soon the Chu army attacked Liu Jia. Liu Jia always held fast to the camp and maintained a mutual dependence with Peng Yue.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, the Han Dynasty pursued Xiang Yu to Guling and sent Liu Jianan to cross the Huai River to surround Shouchun.
Liu Jia arrived soon and sent people to look for opportunities to recruit Zhou Yin, the great Sima of Chu.
Zhou Yin betrayed King Xiang and helped Liu Jia capture Jiujiang. The army of King Wu Yingbu met at Gaixia and jointly attacked Xiang Yu.
The king of Han then Liu Jia led the Jiujiang army and together with Taiwei Lu Wan, attacked Linjiang Wang Gongwei to the southwest.
After Wei Gong died, Linjiang was renamed Nanjun.
In the spring of the sixth year of the Han Dynasty, the Han King Liu Bang met with the princes in Chen County, deposed the Chu King Han Xin, and imprisoned him. His territory was divided into two countries.
At this time, Emperor Gaozu's son was young, had few brothers, and had no talents. He wanted to make a member of the same family the king to control the world, so he issued an edict saying: General Liu Jia has military exploits, and he should select the disciples of the Liu family who have military exploits to be crowned king.
All the ministers said: Liu Jia should be made King of Jing, commanding fifty-two cities in the east of Huaihe; Liu Jiao, Gaozu's younger brother, should be made King of Chu, commanding thirty-six cities in the west.
Liu Bang then appointed his son Liu Fei as King of Qi.
Only then did the Liu brothers begin to be crowned kings.
In the autumn of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled and went east to attack Jingdi.
Liu Jia, king of Jing, fought with him but failed to win. He fled to Fuling and was killed by Yingbu's army.
Gaozu personally defeated Yingbu.
In the twelfth year, Peihou Liu Bi was named King of Wu and ruled over the former homeland of King Jing.
King Liu Ze of Yan was a distant relative of the Liu family.
In the third year of Emperor Gaodi's reign, Liu Ze was appointed as a doctor.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaodi's reign, Liu Ze used his position as a general to attack Chen Xi, captured the enemy general Wang Huang, and was granted the title of Marquis of Yingling.
During the reign of Emperor Gao, Tian Sheng, a native of Qi, was traveling abroad and lacked travel funds, so he asked Liu Ze, Marquis of Yingling, for help by offering suggestions.
Liu Ze was very happy and used 200 kilograms of gold to celebrate Tian Sheng's birthday.
After Tian Sheng got the money, he immediately returned to Qi.
The next year, Liu Ze sent someone to tell Tian Sheng: "Don't you want to interact with me anymore?"
When Tian Sheng came to Chang'an, he did not go to see Liu Ze. Instead, he borrowed a large mansion and asked his son to see and serve Zhang Ziqing, the great emissary who was favored by Empress Lu.
A few months later, Tian Sheng's son invited Zhang Qing to his home as a guest. Zhang Qing personally prepared a banquet.
Zhang Qing agreed to go.
Tian Sheng hung up luxurious curtains and arranged exquisite utensils, just like a prince.
Zhang Qing was surprised when he saw it.
While the wine was in full swing, Tian Sheng asked the left and right to step back and persuaded Zhang Qing: "I have seen more than a hundred residences of princes and kings, all of whom were meritorious officials during the reign of Emperor Gaozu."
summary: King Jing Liu Jia was a member of the Liu clan, though his specific branch is unknown. During the early Han Dynasty, he served as a general under the King of Han, pacifying territories and joining campaigns against Xiang Yu. In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, after the King of Han’s defeat at Chenggao, Liu Jia crossed the Yellow River into Chu territory, burning grain supplies and disrupting enemy logistics. He held his position against Chu attacks, coordinating with Peng Yue. By the fifth year, Liu Jia crossed the Huai River, recruited Chu’s Grand Sima Zhou Yin, who betrayed Xiang Yu, and captured Jiujiang. He then joined King Yingbu at Gaixia to attack Xiang Yu. Later, Liu Jia led the Jiujiang army with Taiwei Lu Wan against Linjiang King Gongwei, who died, leading to the renaming of Linjiang to Nanjun. In the sixth year, Emperor Gaozu deposed the Chu King Han Xin and divided his territory. Seeking to install family members as kings, Gaozu appointed Liu Jia as King of Jing, commanding fifty-two cities east of the Huai, while his brother Liu Jiao became King of Chu. Liu Jia was killed in battle against the rebellious King Yingbu in the eleventh year. His territory later passed to Liu Bi, King of Wu. Tai Shigong noted that Liu Jia was made king for his military exploits during the Han’s early instability, while Liu Ze gained his title through political maneuvering, enabling his line to rule for three generations.

translation:
Now the Lu family has always helped Gaozu complete the great cause of unifying the world. His contribution is very great, and he is honored by his relative the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother was old and the Lu clan was weak. The Queen Mother wanted to make Lu Chan the king and the king of the vassals on behalf of the land.
The Queen Mother wants to speak out about this matter seriously, but she is afraid that the ministers will not agree.
Now that you are most favored by the Queen Mother and respected by the ministers, why not politely persuade the ministers to report this matter to the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother will definitely be happy.
After Zhu Lu is crowned king, all the princes will also be yours.
The Queen Mother wants to do this in her heart, but you are a minister. If you don't propose it quickly, I'm afraid disaster will befall you.
Zhang Qing agreed very much with this, so he politely persuaded the minister to report the matter to the Queen Mother.
When the Queen Mother went to court, she asked the ministers about this matter.
The ministers petitioned to establish Lu Chan as King Lu.
The Queen Mother gave Zhang Qing a thousand catties of gold, and Zhang Qing gave half of it to Tian Sheng.
Tian Sheng did not accept the gift, and took the opportunity to persuade Zhang Qing: "Lü Chan was crowned king, but the ministers were not completely convinced."
Now the Marquis of Yingling, Liu Ze, is a member of the Liu clan and serves as a general. He is the only one who is still dissatisfied.
Now you report to the Queen Mother and designate more than a dozen counties to make him king. He will get the throne and leave happily. The throne of the Lu family will be more consolidated.
Zhang Qing went to the palace to report the matter, and the Queen Mother thought it was right.
So Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, was granted the title of King Langxie.
King Langxie and Tian Sheng went to the fiefdom.
Tian Sheng advised Liu Ze to leave quickly and not to stay.
As soon as they left Hangu Pass, the Queen Mother indeed sent people to chase and stop them, but Liu Ze had already left the pass, so the pursuers had to go back.
After the death of the Queen Mother, Langxie King Liu Ze said: The emperor is young, Zhu Lu controls the government, and the Liu family is lonely and weak.
So he led the army and planned with Qi King Liu Xiang to march westward, intending to kill the Lu family.
When he arrived in Liangdi, he heard that the imperial court had sent General Guan Ying to garrison troops in Xingyang, so Liu Ze returned to strengthen the defense of his western border, and then quickly rushed to Chang'an.
King Dai also happened to arrive from Dai.
The generals, ministers and King Langxie jointly supported King Dai as the emperor.
The emperor then moved Liu Ze to the title of King of Yan, returned Langxie to King Qi, and restored King Qi's original territory.
Liu Ze died in his second year as King of Yan, and his posthumous title was King Jing.
The throne was passed to his son Liu Jia, who became King Kang.
When the throne passed to Liu Ze's grandson Liu Dingguo, he committed adultery with his father, King Kang's concubine, and gave birth to a boy.
He also took his younger brother's wife as his concubine.
He also committed adultery with his three daughters.
Liu Dingguo planned to kill the Ying people, the magistrate of Feiru County. The Ying people and others reported Liu Dingguo's crimes. Liu Dingguo sent envoys to report, arrest and kill the Ying people under the pretext of other laws to silence him.
In the second year of Yuanshuo, the brothers of the Ying people once again wrote to report Liu Dingguo's ulterior scandal, and Dingguo's crimes were exposed.
The emperor ordered the ministers to discuss the case, and the ministers all commented: "Liu Dingguo acted like a beast, corrupted human relations, violated the laws of nature, and should be executed for his crime."
The emperor granted permission.
Liu Dingguo committed suicide, the feudal state was abolished and changed to a county.
Tai Shigong said: King Jing was granted the title of king because the Han Dynasty had just been established and the world had not yet been completely unified. Therefore, although Liu Jia was a distant relative of the Liu family, he was granted the title of king for his military exploits and held a powerful position between the Jiang and Huaihe Rivers.
Liu Ze was named king because he used power and intrigue to arouse the Lu family, so that Liu Ze could be king in the south for three generations.
Isn't it wonderful and great that things have been interfering with each other from the beginning!
summary: King Liu Ze of Yan, a distant Liu relative, began as a doctor and later became Marquis of Yingling for capturing an enemy general. During Empress Lu’s reign, Tian Sheng, a Qi native, advised Liu Ze to gain favor by supporting the Lu clan’s rise. Through Zhang Qing, a favored emissary, Tian Sheng persuaded the court to make Lu Chan king, then proposed making Liu Ze a king to secure Lu power. Liu Ze was thus made King of Langxie. After Empress Lu’s death, Liu Ze allied with Qi King Liu Xiang to oppose the Lu clan, eventually supporting King Dai as emperor. He was then made King of Yan, dying in his second year. His descendants included his son Liu Jia and grandson Liu Dingguo, who committed heinous crimes—adultery with relatives and murder—leading to his suicide and the abolition of his state.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/荆燕世家

translation:
Xiao Xiangguo Xiao He was born in Fengyi, Peixian County.
His knowledge of the law was unparalleled, and he was an official under the magistrate of Peixian County.
When the great ancestor Liu Bang was still a commoner, Xiao He relied on his authority as an official to protect him many times.
Liu Bang became the chief of the pavilion, and Xiao He often helped him.
Liu Bang went to Xianyang to serve as an official. All the officials gave him three hundred coins, but Xiao He gave him five hundred coins.
When the censor of the Qin Dynasty went to Sishui County to supervise the work of the county, Xiao He followed his subordinate officials and always handled things in an orderly and clear manner.
Xiao He then took on the job of being the historian of Sishui County, and ranked first in the official assessment.
The censor of the Qin Dynasty planned to enter the court to make suggestions to recruit Xiao He, but Xiao He repeatedly declined and refused to be transferred.
When the great ancestor Liu Bang rose up and became Pei Gong, Xiao He often served as his assistant to supervise the affairs.
When Pei Gong entered Xianyang, the generals rushed to the Qin Dynasty's treasury to collect gold and silk property. Only Xiao He entered the palace first to collect legal documents, geographical atlases, household registration files and other documents and materials in charge of the Qin Dynasty's prime ministers and censors, and treasured them.
Pei Gong became the queen of Han Dynasty and appointed Xiao He as prime minister.
Xiang Yu and the princes' troops entered Xianyang, slaughtered and burned them, and then left.
The reason why the King of Han was able to have a detailed understanding of the world's dangerous fortresses, the number of families and populations, the strength and weakness of various places, the sufferings of the people, etc. was all because Xiao He had completely obtained the maps, books and other materials of the Qin Dynasty.
Xiao He recommended Han Xin to the King of Han, and the King of Han appointed Han Xin as general.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin".
The King of Han led his troops eastward and pacified the Three Qin Dynasties. Xiao He stayed behind as prime minister to govern Bashu, pacify the people, issue decrees, and provide food and fodder for the army.
In the second year of the Han Dynasty, the king of Han and other princes attacked the Chu army. Xiao He guarded Guanzhong, served the prince, and governed Yueyang.
When formulating laws and regulations, establishing ancestral temples, communities, palaces, and counties, Xiao He would report everything he did to the King of Han in advance and only implement it with the King of Han's approval. If it was too late to report to the King of Han, he would handle certain matters as appropriate and report to him again when the King of Han came back.
Xiao He managed the registered population in Guanzhong and collected grain and grass to transport to the army at the front. Large numbers of soldiers fled from the Han army many times, so Xiao He often recruited soldiers from Guanzhong to make up for the shortfalls in the army.
Therefore, the King of Han specially appointed Xiao He to handle the political affairs in Guanzhong.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, the army of the King of Han and Xiang Yu's army faced off between Jingxian and Suocheng. The King of Han sent envoys many times to express condolences to Prime Minister Xiao He.
A man named Bao Sheng said to Xiao He: The King of Han is living in the open air on the front line, but he has sent envoys to comfort you many times. This is because he doubts your intentions.
For your sake, it is better to send all your descendants and brothers who are capable of fighting to serve in the military camp. The King of Han will definitely trust you more.
So Xiao He followed his plan, and the king of Han was indeed very happy.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu was eliminated and the world was pacified, so he was rewarded based on his merits.
summary: Xiao He, born in Fengyi, Peixian County, was a legal expert and official under the county magistrate. He protected Liu Bang when Liu Bang was a commoner and later as a pavilion chief. When Liu Bang served in Xianyang, Xiao He gave him five hundred coins, more than others. Xiao He became historian of Sishui County, ranking first in assessments, but declined a transfer recommended by a Qin censor. When Liu Bang became Pei Gong, Xiao He assisted him. After entering Xianyang, while others seized treasure, Xiao He collected Qin legal documents, maps, and household records. This allowed Liu Bang to understand the realm's geography and population. Xiao He recommended Han Xin as general. As prime minister, he governed Bashu and Guanzhong, managing laws, temples, and supplies. He reported to Liu Bang or acted as needed, recruiting soldiers to replenish the army. In the third year of Han, Liu Bang sent envoys to Xiao He, suspecting him. Bao Sheng advised Xiao He to send his family to the army, which Liu Bang approved. After Xiang Yu's defeat, Liu Bang ranked Xiao He first among heroes, comparing him to a hunter versus hounds, and citing Xiao He's clan contributions. E Qianqiu supported this, noting Xiao He's consistent support during crises. Xiao He was ranked first, allowed special court privileges, and granted fiefs.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/萧相国世家

translation:
Emperor Gaozu said: I heard that recommending talented people will receive high rewards.
Although Xiao He's contribution was very high, it became even more prominent after being commended by E Jun.
So based on the original title of Marquis of Guannei, E Jun was granted the title of Marquis of Anping.
On that day, more than ten people including Xiao He, his father, his son and his brothers were granted food fiefs.
Later, Xiao He was granted the title of two thousand households. This was because when Gaozu went to serve in Xianyang, Xiao He gave him an extra two hundred coins.
In the eleventh year of the Han Dynasty, Chen Xi rebelled, and Gaozu personally led his army to Handan.
Before the suppression of the rebellion was over, Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, rebelled again in Guanzhong. Empress Lu adopted Xiao He's strategy and killed the Marquis of Huaiyin. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin".
Emperor Gaozu had already heard that the Marquis of Huaiyin had been killed, so he sent an envoy to worship Prime Minister Xiao He as the Prime Minister, granted five thousand households, and ordered 500 soldiers and a captain to serve as the Prime Minister's bodyguard.
Many people came to congratulate him, but Zhao Ping expressed his condolences.
Zhao Pingyuan was the Marquis of Dongling in the Qin Dynasty.
After the fall of the Qin Dynasty, he became a commoner, his family was poor, and he grew melons in the east of Chang'an City. The melons he planted tasted sweet, so people in society called them "Aventurine melons", which was named after Zhao Ping's title.
Zhao Ping said to the Prime Minister Xiao He: The disaster began from now on.
Your Majesty is out in the cold weather, and your troops are outside, but you stay in the middle of the court and are not in danger of war. Instead, you increase your fiefdom and set up guards. This is because the Marquis of Huaiyin has just rebelled in the capital and has doubts about your heart.
The purpose of setting up a guard to protect you is not to favor you. I hope that you will refuse the reward and donate all your property and assets to the army. Then the emperor will be happy.
Xiao Xiangguo followed his plan. Emperor Gao was indeed very happy.
In the autumn of the twelfth year of the Han Dynasty, Yingbu rebelled. Gaozu personally led an army to conquer him and sent people many times to ask what Xiao Xiangguo was doing.
Because the emperor was in the army, Xiao Xiangguo comforted and encouraged the people in the rear and donated all his wealth to the army, just like when he attacked Chen Xi.
A retainer advised Xiao Xiangguo: The day when your clan will be exterminated is not far away.
You are in the prime minister's position and have the highest number of merits. Can you add more merits?
You won the hearts of the people when you first entered Guanzhong. It has been more than ten years since the people have attached themselves to you. You are still so diligent in your work, have a harmonious relationship with the people, and are loved.
The reason why the emperor has repeatedly asked about your situation is that he is afraid that you will shock Guanzhong.
Now why don't you buy more land, use low prices, borrow money, etc. to ruin your reputation?
In this way, the emperor's heart will be at peace.
So Xiao Xiangguo followed his plan, and Gaozu was very happy.
When Emperor Gaozu returned from conquering the Taibu army, the people blocked the road and wrote a letter saying that the prime minister had forcibly bought a large number of people's fields and houses at low prices.
Emperor Gaozu returned to the capital and met with the Prime Minister.
summary: During Chen Xi's rebellion, Xiao He helped Empress Lu kill Han Xin. Liu Bang rewarded him with guards, but Zhao Ping warned this indicated suspicion. Xiao He refused the reward and donated to the army, pleasing Liu Bang. During Yingbu's rebellion, a retainer advised Xiao He to ruin his reputation by buying land cheaply to ease Liu Bang's fears. Xiao He complied, and Liu Bang was happy. Later, Liu Bang imprisoned Xiao He for requesting Shanglin Garden for the people, but a guard argued Xiao He's duty, and Liu Bang released him.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/萧相国世家

translation:
Emperor Gaozu smiled and said: You, the prime minister, are so beneficial to the people!
Emperor Gaozu handed all the people's petitions to the Prime Minister and said: "You can apologize to the people yourself."
The Prime Minister took this opportunity to ask for orders and said: The land in Chang'an is narrow, and there are many open spaces in Shanglin Garden, which have been abandoned and deserted. I hope that the people can go in to cultivate and harvest grain, leaving the straw as feed for animals.
Emperor Gaozu was furious and said: Prime Minister, you accepted a large amount of property from merchants, and then requested for them to occupy my Shanglin Garden!
So he handed Xiang Guo over to Tingwei and imprisoned him in shackles.
A few days later, when a guard surnamed Wang was serving Emperor Gaozu, he came forward and asked: What heinous crime did the Prime Minister commit, and your Majesty detained him so harshly?
Emperor Gaozu said: I heard that when Li Si assisted Qin Shihuang, any achievements he made were attributed to the Lord, and any mistakes he made were his own responsibility.
Now the Prime Minister accepts a large amount of money from profiteers and asks them to occupy my garden and forest in order to please the people, so he is handcuffed and punished.
Wang Weiwei said: Within the scope of his duties, if it is beneficial to the people and he pleads for them, this is indeed the prime minister's duty. How can your majesty suspect that the prime minister accepts money from businessmen!
Moreover, Your Majesty resisted the Chu army for several years. When Chen Xun and Yingbu rebelled, Your Majesty personally led troops to quell the rebellion. At that time, the Prime Minister stayed in Guanzhong, and he only moved a foot, so the territory west of Hangu Pass would no longer belong to Your Majesty.
Didn’t the Prime Minister take advantage of this opportunity to benefit himself, but now he is coveting the money of businessmen?
Besides, Qin Shihuang lost the world because he couldn't hear his own faults. How could Li Si share his faults and be worthy of imitation?
Why does Your Majesty doubt the Prime Minister to such a shallow level!
Gaozu was not very happy after hearing this.
On the same day, Gaozu sent someone to pardon and release the prime minister.
The Prime Minister was old and always humble and cautious. When he came to see Gao Zu, he walked barefoot to apologize.
Emperor Gaozu said: Forget it, Prime Minister!
The prime minister asked for a garden for the people, but I refused. I am just a monarch like Jie and Zhou, and you are a wise prime minister.
The reason why I put you in chains is to let the people know my fault.
Xiao He and Cao Shen had never been on good terms with each other. When Xiao He was seriously ill, Emperor Xiaohui personally went to check on Xiang Guo's condition and asked by the way: "If you pass away, who can replace you?"
Xiao He replied: There is no one who understands his subordinates better than the monarch.
Emperor Xiaohui said: How about Cao Shen?
Xiao He kowtowed and said: Your Majesty has found a suitable candidate!
Even if I die, I will have no regrets!
Xiao He's purchase of land and housing must be in a poor and remote area, and he did not build a house with low walls when building his home.
He said: If my descendants are worthy, they can learn from my frugality; if their descendants are not worthy, they can avoid being taken away by powerful people.
In the second year of Xiaohui's reign, Prime Minister Xiao He passed away, and his posthumous title was Wen Zhonghou.
summary: Xiao He and Cao Shen were not on good terms, but on his deathbed, Xiao He recommended Cao Shen as his successor. Xiao He bought land in poor areas and built simple homes to teach frugality. He died in the second year of Xiaohui's reign, posthumously named Wenzhong Hou. His descendants lost the title four times but were reinstated, unmatched among heroes. Sima Qian noted Xiao He's rise from a minor official to a prominent figure, adapting laws to people's needs and achieving lasting fame.
