translation:
The ancestor of Korea has the same surname as Emperor Zhou, Ji.
His descendants were entrusted to the Jin State and were sealed in Han Yuan, known as Han Wuzi.
After Han Wuzi, Han Jue was born in three generations, and the name of his fiefdom was Han Weishi.
When Han Jue was in Duke Jinggong's third year in Jin Dynasty, Tu'anjia, the chief minister of Jin State, was going to cause trouble, saying that he wanted to kill Zhao Dun, the traitor of Duke Linggong.
Zhao Dun was already dead, so he wanted to kill his son Zhao Shuo.
Han Jue tried to stop Tu'anjia, but Tu'anjia refused to listen.
Han Jue went to tell Zhao Shuo and let him escape.
Zhao Shuo said: "You must not cut off the descendants of the Zhao family, and there will be no regrets after my death."
Han Jue agreed to him.
When Tu'anjia killed the Zhao family, Han Jue claimed that he was ill and could not leave home.
Cheng Ying and Gongsun Jiu hid Zhao Wu, the orphan of the Zhao family, and Han Jue knew about it.
In the eleventh year of Jin Jinggong's reign, Han Jue and Chuke led a force of 800 chariots to conquer Qi. They defeated Qi Qinggong in An and captured Feng Chou's father.
From this time on, the Jin State established six ministers, and Han Jue ranked first, named Xianzi.
In the seventeenth year of Jin Jinggong's reign, Jinggong fell ill, and the divination results said that there were unfavorable people among Daye's descendants who were causing trouble.
Han Jue praised Zhao Shui's achievements and said that he had no one to continue the incense, so as to impress Jinggong.
Jinggong asked: "Does he have any descendants?"
Han Jue talked about Zhao Wu at that time, and Jinggong gave him the original Tianyi of Zhao family again, so that he could continue Zhao family's incense.
In the seventh year of Jin's reign, Han Xianzi grew old.
After Xianzi's death, his son Xuanzi inherited the title.
Xuanzi moved to Zhouyi.
In the fourteenth year of Jin Ping Gong's reign, Jizha of Wu State went to Jin State as an envoy. He said: The political power of Jin State will eventually belong to the three families of Han, Wei and Zhao.
In the twelfth year of Jin Qinggong's reign, Han Xuanzi, Zhao and Wei families divided themselves into ten counties of Qi and Yangyu.
In the fifteenth year of Duke Dinggong of Jin Dynasty, Han Xuanzi and Zhao Jianzi attacked Fan and Zhonghang families.
Xuanzi died, and his son Sadako inherited the title.
Sadako moved to Pingyang.
Han Zhenzi died and his son Jianzi succeeded to the throne.
Han Jianzi died and his son Zhuangzi succeeded to the throne.
Han Zhuangzi died and his son Kangzi succeeded him.
Han Kangzi, Zhao Xiangzi and Wei Huanzi defeated Zhibo and divided his territory. The territories of the three families were larger than those of other princes.
After Han Kangzi died, his son Wuzi succeeded to the throne.
In the second year of Wuzi's reign, he attacked the state of Zheng and killed their king Zheng Youhui.
In the sixteenth year, Han Wuzi died, and his son Jinghou came to the throne.
In the first year of Han Jinghou Qian's reign, he attacked Zheng State and occupied Yongqiu.
In the second year, Zheng Jun defeated Zhao Jun in Fushu.
In the sixth year of Jinghou, Han, Zhao and Wei were recognized as vassal states.
In the ninth year of Jinghou, Zheng Guo surrounded Yangzhai in South Korea.
Jinghou passed away. His son Liehou Han took the throne.
In the third year of Lihou's reign, Nie Zheng assassinated Xia Lei, the prime minister of South Korea.
summary: The ancestor of Korea shared the surname Ji with Emperor Zhou. His descendants were enfeoffed in Jin State at Han Yuan, becoming known as Han Wuzi. After three generations, Han Jue emerged, and his fief was called Han Weishi. During Duke Jinggong’s third year in Jin, Tu'anjia sought to kill Zhao Shuo, son of the deceased Zhao Dun. Han Jue tried to stop him but failed, then warned Zhao Shuo, who begged him not to let the Zhao line end. Han Jue agreed. When Tu'anjia massacred the Zhao family, Han Jue feigned illness. Cheng Ying and Gongsun Jiu hid the orphan Zhao Wu, which Han Jue knew. In the eleventh year, Han Jue and Chuke led 800 chariots to defeat Qi, capturing Feng Chou’s father. Jin then established six ministers, with Han Jue first, titled Xianzi. In the seventeenth year, Jinggong fell ill; divination blamed Daye’s descendants. Han Jue praised Zhao Shui’s deeds, prompting Jinggong to restore Zhao Wu to the Zhao line. Han Xianzi grew old and died, succeeded by his son Xuanzi, who moved to Zhouyi. In the fourteenth year of Jin Ping Gong, Jizha of Wu predicted Jin’s power would go to Han, Wei, and Zhao. Later, Han Xuanzi, Zhao, and Wei divided Qi and Yangyu counties, then attacked Fan and Zhonghang families. Xuanzi died, succeeded by Sadako, who moved to Pingyang. Subsequent rulers included Jianzi, Zhuangzi, Kangzi, and Wuzi. In Wuzi’s second year, Korea attacked Zheng, killing King Zheng Youhui. After Wuzi died, Jinghou reigned, attacking Zheng and occupying Yongqiu. In the sixth year of Jinghou, Han, Zhao, and Wei were recognized as vassal states. Later rulers included Liehou, Wenhou, Aihou, Yihou, Zhaohou, King Xuanhui, King Xiang, King Li, King Huanhui, and finally King Han, who was captured by Qin in the ninth year of his reign, ending Korea. Sima Qian noted that Han Jue’s act of restoring Zhao Wu was a rare virtue, and the Han family’s rise to princely status over ten generations was deserved.

translation:
The ancestors of the Wei family are descendants of Bi Gonggao.
Bi Gonggao has the same surname as Emperor Zhou.
After King Wu defeated Zhou, Gao was granted the title Bi, so he took Bi as his surname.
His descendants had their titles discontinued and became commoners, some living in the Central Plains and some living in Yi and Di.
One of his descendants was named Bi Wan, who served Duke Xiang of Jin.
In the sixteenth year of Duke Xiang of Jin, Zhao Su drove a chariot with Bi Wan as the right guard to conquer Huo, Geng, and Wei, and destroyed them all.
Duke Xian granted Geng to Zhao Su and Wei to Bi Wan, and both of them became high officials.
Bu Yan, who was in charge of divination, said: Bi Wan's descendants must be very prosperous. Wan is the full number; Wei is the name of tall people.
Starting a reward with such a name is God's sponsorship for him. What the emperor rules is called Zhaomin, and what the princes rule is called Wanmin.
Now that his name is Da, followed by the full number, he will definitely have the people.
At the beginning, Bi Wan divined the good and bad fortune of serving Jin Jun, and obtained the tunzhūn, and the Yin Ping Zhun hexagram became the Bi hexagram.
Xin Liao concluded: Good luck.
Tun Gua symbolizes solidity and Bi Gua symbolizes entry. What could be more auspicious than this? It will be prosperous and prosperous in the future.
Eleven years after Bi Wan was granted the title, Duke Xiang of Jin died. His four sons competed with each other for the throne, and Jin was in civil strife.
There were more and more descendants of Bi Wan, and the country was named Wei after them.
Bi Wan gave birth to Wu Zi.
Wei Wuzi served Jin Gongzi Chong'er as a member of the Wei family.
In the 21st year of Duke Xiang of Jin, Wei Wuzi followed Chong'er into exile. Nineteen years later, when he returned to China, Chong'er ascended the throne as Duke Wen of Jin, allowing Wei Wuzi to inherit the titles of the descendants of the Wei family and rise to the status of a high official. His official residence was located in Wei Yi.
Wei Wuzi gave birth to a son.
Wei Daozi moved the government office to Huoyi.
He gave birth to Wei Jiang.
Wei Jiang served Duke Ao of Jin.
In the third year of mourning for the Duke, he made an alliance with the princes.
Yang Qian, the younger brother of the duke, caused chaos in the queue, and Wei Jiang killed Yang Qian's servants to humiliate him.
Duke Mourning said angrily: "I am proud of joining the princes, but now I am insulting my brother!"
Wei Jiang will be killed.
Some people tried to persuade him to mourn, but he gave up.
Later, Wei Jiang was finally appointed to be in power, and he was sent to repair with Rong and Di. From then on, Rong and Di became close and attached to Jin.
In the eleventh year of the reign of Duke Mourning, Duke Mourning said: Since I appointed Wei Jiang, in eight years, I have met with the princes nine times, and Rong and Di have made peace with us. This is all due to your efforts!
Wei Jiang was given musical instruments and a band, but Wei Jiang declined three times before accepting.
Wei Jiang moved his government to Anyi.
After Wei Jiang's death, his posthumous title was Zhaozi.
He gave birth to Wei Ying, and Wei Ying gave birth to Wei Xianzi.
Wei Xianzi served Duke Zhao of Jin.
After the death of Duke Zhao, the six ministers of Jin became stronger and stronger, while the official family declined.
In the twelfth year of Jin Qinggong's reign, Han Xuanzi became old and Wei Xianzi took charge of state affairs.
The Qi clan and the Yangyu clan of the Jin State slandered each other. The Six Qing Dynasties killed them, took back all their fiefdoms and divided them into ten counties. The Six Qing Dynasties sent their sons to serve as officials in the ten counties.
Wei Xianzi, Zhao Jianzi, Zhongxing Wenzi, and Fan Xianzi were all ministers of Jin.
For the next fourteen years, Confucius served as acting prime minister of the State of Lu.
Four years later, due to the Jinyang Rebellion, Zhao Jianzi, together with the Han family and the Wei family, attacked the Fan family and the Zhonghang family.
Wei Xianzi gave birth to Wei Chi, who together with Zhao Yang attacked the Fan family and the Zhongxing family.
Wei Chi's grandson was Wei Huanzi. He, Han Kangzi and Zhao Xiangzi joined forces to defeat Zhibo and divide his territory.
Huanzi's grandson was Wenhou Weisi.
The first year of Wei Wenhou was the first year of Qin Ling.
Wei Wenhou was at the same time as Han Wuzi, Zhao Huanzi, and Zhou Weilie.
summary: The Wei family traces its ancestry to Bi Gonggao, a descendant of the Zhou royal family. After King Wu of Zhou defeated the Shang, Gao was granted the territory of Bi and adopted Bi as his surname. His descendants eventually became commoners, with some living in the Central Plains and others among the Yi and Di peoples. One descendant, Bi Wan, served Duke Xian of Jin and was granted the territory of Wei after military victories. A diviner predicted that Bi Wan's descendants would prosper greatly, and indeed the Wei family grew increasingly powerful within the state of Jin. Wei Wuzi followed Chong'er into exile and later served him as Duke Wen of Jin. The family continued through generations: Wei Daozi, Wei Jiang, Wei Ying, and Wei Xianzi. During Wei Jiang's service to Duke Mourning of Jin, he killed a servant of the duke's brother who had caused disorder, initially angering the duke but eventually earning his trust. Duke Mourning credited Wei Jiang with eight years of successful alliances and peace with the Rong and Di tribes. As the Jin state declined, the six ministers grew stronger. Wei Xianzi served as a minister of Jin alongside Zhao Jianzi, Zhongxing Wenzi, and Fan Xianzi. Later generations including Wei Chi, Wei Huanzi, and eventually Wei Wenhou continued the family's rise.

translation:
In the sixth year of Marquis Wen's reign, he built a city in Shaoliang.
In the thirteenth year, he sent his subordinates to attack Fan and Pang and move out the people there.
In the 16th year, he attacked Qin and built cities in Linjin and Yuanli.
In the seventeenth year of Marquis Wen's reign, he attacked and destroyed the Zhongshan Kingdom, and sent Ziqi to garrison there, asking Zhao Cangtang to assist him.
Zicheng met Wenhou's teacher Tian Zifang in Chaoge. He stepped back from his car to make way, and got out of the car to pay his respects.
Tian Zifang did not return the favor.
Zijing asked him, "Are rich people arrogant to others, or are poor people arrogant to others?"
Tian Zifang said: It's just that poor and humble people are arrogant towards others.
If a prince is arrogant to others, he will lose his feudal kingdom; if a great official is arrogant to others, he will lose his family.
If the poor and humble people do not agree with their behavior and their opinions are not accepted, they will leave here and go to Chu and Yue, just like taking off their straw sandals. How can they be the same as the rich and noble people!
Zicheng left unhappy.
He attacked the Qin State to the west, returned to the Zheng State, and built cities in Luoyin and Heyang.
In the 22nd year of Marquis Wen, Wei, Zhao and Han were recognized as princes.
In the twenty-fourth year of Marquis Wen's reign, the Qin army attacked Wei and reached Yanghu.
In the twenty-fifth year of Marquis Wen's reign, his son gave birth to a son.
Marquis Wen studied the Confucian classics under Zixia and treated Duan Qianmu as a guest. When he passed through his hometown, he never failed to pay tribute to Ping Shi.
Qin once wanted to attack Wei. Some people say: The king of Wei has special respect for wise men. People in Wei praise his benevolence and he is harmonious and united, so he cannot have any intentions against him.
As a result, Marquis Wen received praise from the princes.
Ximen Bao was appointed as the governor of Ye County, so Hanoi was known as peaceful and stable.
Marquis Wen of Wei said to Li Ke: My husband once taught me: If your family is poor, you want a good wife; if your country is in chaos, you want a wise prime minister.
Now we have to appoint a prime minister, either Chengzi or Zhai Huang. What do you think of these two people?
Li Ke replied: I have heard that humble people do not plan for noble people, and distant people do not plan for those who are close to them.
My responsibilities lie outside the palace, and I dare not take on this mission.
Marquis Wen said: Sir, don't refuse when faced with this matter.
Li Ke said: This is because you did not pay attention to inspection.
Look at who he is close to in normal times, who he associates with when he is rich, who he recommends when he is powerful, what he does not do when he is frustrated, and what he does not want when he is poor. With these five things, you can decide who will be the prime minister. Why wait for me, Li Ke!
Marquis Wen said: Sir, please go home, my prime minister has decided.
Li Ke walked out quickly and visited Zhai Huang at his home.
Zhai Huang said: Today I heard that the monarch summoned Mr. to choose the prime minister. Who will be the prime minister?
Li Ke said: Wei Chengzi has become prime minister.
Zhai Huang's face changed with anger, and he said: Based on what I saw and heard with my ears and eyes, in what way am I worse than Wei Chengzi?
The defender of Xihe is my recommendation.
The monarch is most worried about Yejun in the mainland, so I recommended Ximen Bao.
summary: Wei Wenhou's reign marked the formal establishment of Wei as a state. He studied under Zixia, treated Duan Qianmu as a guest, and gained praise from the princes for his respect toward worthy men. When selecting a prime minister, he consulted Li Ke, who advised examining five aspects of candidates: whom they associate with, whom they recommend when powerful, what they avoid when frustrated, and what they reject when poor. Li Ke determined that Wei Chengzi was the better choice over Zhai Huang, noting that Wei Chengzi spent nine-tenths of his income on employing worthy men like Bu Zixia, Tian Zifang, and Duan Qianmu.

translation:
When the Wei army passed by Waihuang, Xuzi said to Prince Shen: I have a way to win every battle.
The prince said: Can you let me hear it?
Xu Zi said: I originally wanted to present it to you.
He went on to say: The prince personally leads the troops to attack Qi. Even if he wins a great victory and captures the land of Ju, his wealth will only be that of owning the Kingdom of Wei, and his wealth will only be that of being the king of Wei.
If we cannot defeat Qi, our descendants will not be able to capture Wei for eternity.
This is my winning formula.
Prince Shen said: Well, I will definitely follow your advice and return to China.
Xu Zi said: Although the prince wants to go back, it is no longer possible.
There are too many people who persuade the prince to fight and want to benefit from it.
Although the prince wants to go back, I'm afraid it's impossible.
The prince then wanted to go back, but his driver said: "Going back as soon as the general leads the troops is the same as losing the battle."
As expected, Prince Shen fought against the Qi army and was defeated at Maling.
The Qi army captured Wei Prince Shen and killed general Pang Juan. The Wei army was finally defeated.
In the 31st year of King Hui, Qin, Zhao, and Qi attacked Wei together. Qin general Shang Yang defrauded and captured Wei general Gongzi Yan, and then attacked and captured his army, defeating the Wei army.
Qin appointed Shang Yang, and the territory to the east reached the Yellow River. Qi and Zhao defeated Wei many times, and Anyi was close to Qin, so Wei moved its capital to Daliang.
Prince He was made the crown prince.
In the thirty-third year of King Hui, Duke Xiao of Qin passed away. Shang Yang fled from Qin and went to Wei. The people of Wei were angry and did not take him in.
In the thirty-fifth year, King Wei and King Xuan of Qi met in the south of Pingyang.
King Hui suffered repeated military defeats, so he used courteous etiquette and generous gifts to recruit wise men. Zou Yan, Chunyu Kun, and Meng Ke all came to Wei.
King Hui of Liang said: I have no talent, my army suffered setbacks abroad three times, the prince was captured, the general died in battle, the country was empty, and the ancestral temple and the country were humiliated, and I was very ashamed. The old gentleman condescended to visit the court of our country in person. How will he benefit our country?
Meng Ke said: A monarch cannot talk about interests like this.
If the monarch wants to make a profit, then the officials also want to make a profit; if the officials want to make a profit, then the people also want to make a profit. If everyone from top to bottom strives for profit, the country will be in danger.
As a monarch of a country, it is enough to be benevolent and righteous. Why should we be concerned about profit?
In the thirty-sixth year of King Hui's reign, he met King Qi again in Zhenyi.
In this year, King Hui died and his son King Xiang came to the throne.
In the first year of King Xiang, King Wei and the princes met in Xuzhou to proclaim each other king.
King Xiang pursued and honored his father, King Hui, as king.
In the fifth year of King Xiang, the Qin army defeated the 45,000-strong army led by Long Jia of Wei State in Diaoyin, and besieged Jiaocheng and Quwo of Wei State.
Wei State ceded the land west of Hexi to Qin State.
In the sixth year of King Xiang, King Wei and King Qin met in Yingcheng.
The Qin army captured Wei's Fenyin, Pishi and Jiaocheng.
The Wei army conquered Chu and defeated the Chu army at Xingshan.
In seven years, the State of Wei gave all Shangjun to the State of Qin.
summary: After Wei Wenhou's death, his son Wei Wuhou succeeded him. The state faced various military campaigns against Qi, Zhao, Qin, and Chu. Following Wuhou's death, a succession dispute arose between Ziyi and Gongzhong Xu. The states of Han and Zhao disagreed on how to handle the situation, which ultimately saved Wei from partition. King Hui of Wei suffered repeated military defeats and sought to recruit worthy men, attracting Zou Yan, Chunyu Kun, and Meng Ke. Meng Ke advised the king that a ruler should focus on benevolence and righteousness rather than profit.

translation:
In the thirty-first year of King Anli's reign, King Qin began to ascend the throne.
In the thirty-fourth year of King Anli, King Anli died, and Prince Zeng ascended the throne. This was King Jingmin.
Xinlingjun Wuji passed away.
In the first year of King Jingmin, the Qin army captured 20 cities in the Wei State and established them as the East Commandery of the Qin State.
In the second year, the Qin army captured Chaoge of Wei State.
Weiguo moved to Yewang.
In three years, the Qin army captured Jiyi in the state of Wei.
In five years, the Qin army captured Wei's Yuandi, Puyang, and Yanyi.
In the fifteenth year, King Jingmin died, and his son King Wei assumed the throne.
In the first year of King Wei's holiday, Prince Dan of Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate King Qin, but King Qin discovered it.
Three years after King Jie of Wei, the Qin army flooded Daliang and captured King Jie of Wei. Finally, the state of Wei was destroyed and established as prefectures and counties.
Tai Shigong said: I have been to the old city site of Daliang. The people there said: The Qin army conquered Daliang by diverting water from the chasm to flood Daliang. After three months, the city was destroyed, and the King of Wei asked for surrender, thus destroying the Wei state.
Those who discussed it all said that because King Wei did not reuse Lord Xinling, the country was weakened and even destroyed. I don't think so.
God's will is for the Qin State to pacify the sea, but its achievements have not yet been completed. Even if the Wei State is assisted by wise ministers like A Heng, what is the use?
summary: The later reigns of King Xiang, King Ai, King Zhao, King Anli, King Jingmin, and King Wei saw Wei's gradual decline. The Qin state repeatedly attacked Wei, capturing cities and territories. Despite efforts by figures like Lord Xinling Wuji, who successfully led a coalition of five states against Qin, Wei continued to lose ground. In the third year of King Wei's reign, the Qin army diverted water from the chasm to flood Daliang, capturing King Wei and destroying the Wei state, which was then established as prefectures and counties.

translation:
The Qin army occupied Puyang in the Wei state.
In the eighth year, Qin returned Jiaocheng and Quwo to Wei.
In the twelfth year of King Xiang, the Chu army defeated the Wei army in Xiangling.
The ruling ministers of the various vassal states met with Qin Prime Minister Zhang Yi at Zhisang.
In the thirteenth year, Zhang Yi was appointed prime minister of Wei.
A woman in Wei State turned into a man.
The Qin army captured Quwo and Pingzhou in Wei.
In the sixteenth year of King Xiang, King Xiang died, and his son King Ai came to the throne.
Zhang Yi returned to Qin.
In the first year of King Ai, the five kingdoms jointly attacked Qin, but they withdrew their troops without victory.
In the second year of King Ai's reign, the Qi army defeated the Wei army in Guanjin.
In the fifth year, the State of Qin sent Chuilizi to attack Quwo of the State of Wei, and drove away Gongsun Yan, the rhinoceros leader, at Anmen.
In the sixth year, the state of Qin sent people to the state of Wei to establish Wei Gongzi Zheng as the crown prince.
The King of Wei and the King of Qin met in Linjin.
In the seventh year, the Wei army attacked Qi.
Together with the Qin army, he conquered the State of Yan.
In the eighth year of King Ai's reign, the Wei army attacked Weiguo and captured two cities.
The King of Wei was very worried. The official of Wei, Ru Er, went to see King Wei and said, "Is it okay for me to make Wei withdraw its troops and remove King Chengling?"
Wei Jun said: If you really can do it, I am willing to serve you with the defense of the country from generation to generation.
Ru'er saw Chenglingjun and said: In the past, the Wei army attacked Zhao, cut off the Yangchang Ban, captured Yanyu, and prepared to split the Zhao State into two halves. However, the reason why the Zhao State did not perish was because the Wei State was the leader of the alliance.
Now that Wei is on the verge of destruction, it will ask the west to serve Qin.
Rather than letting Qin rescue Wei, it is better for Wei to release Wei. In this way, Wei will always be grateful for Wei's kindness. Cheng Lingjun said: Yes.
Ru'er went to see King Wei again and said: "I once went to see Lord Wei."
Weiguo was originally a branch of the Zhou royal family. Although it was known as a small country, it had many treasures.
Now that the country is in danger, but the treasures have not been donated, the reason is that they believe that it is not up to the king to attack the Weiguo or release the Weiguo, so even if the treasures are offered, they will definitely not reach the hands of the king.
The minister secretly guessed that the person who first proposed to release Wei Guo must be the person who accepted Wei Guo's bribe.
After Ru'er went out, Lord Chengling came in and paid homage to King Wei as Ru'er said.
The King of Wei listened to his opinion and withdrew the Wei army. At the same time, he was relieved of his position as Lord Chengling and never saw him again for life.
In the ninth year of King Ai's reign, King Wei and King Qin met in Linjin.
Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang both surrendered to Wei.
Wei's prime minister Tian Xian died, and Chu was afraid that Zhang Yi, Xishou or Xue Gong would become Wei's prime minister.
Zhao Yu, the prime minister of Chu, said to Su Dai: Tian Xian is dead, I'm afraid one of Zhang Yi, Xishou and Xue Gong will become the prime minister of Wei.
Su Dai said: Then who is the prime minister who is beneficial to you?
Zhaoyu said: I want the crown prince of Wei to be the prime minister himself.
summary: The Grand Historian concluded that while some blamed King Wei's failure to employ Lord Xinling for Wei's destruction, he believed the Qin state was destined by Heaven to unify the realm, and even wise ministers could not have prevented Wei's fall.

translation:
Duke Dan of Zhou was the younger brother of King Wu of Zhou.
When King Wen was still alive, Dan, as his son, was very filial, loyal and kind, better than his other brothers.
When King Wu came to the throne, Dan often assisted King Bi Wu and handled many government affairs.
In the ninth year of King Wu's reign, he personally marched eastward to Mengjin, and Duke Zhou accompanied the army to assist him.
In the eleventh year, King Wu crusaded against Yin Zhou and the army reached Muye. Duke Zhou assisted King Wu and issued the "Oath of Mu" to mobilize the battle.
The Zhou army broke through the capital of Yin and entered the palace of Yin.
After killing Yin Zhou, Duke Zhou held a big axe, and Duke Zhao held a small axe. They flanked King Wu on their left and right, held the ceremony of provoking the community, and announced King Zhou's guilt to heaven and the people of Yin Dynasty.
Release the imprisoned Jizi.
Wu Genglu, the son of King Zhou, was granted the title of Father, and ordered Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai to assist him in order to continue the sacrifices of Yin.
After that, he was awarded the title of meritorious officials and relatives of the Zhou royal family.
The Duke of Zhou was granted the title of Duke of Lu in Qufu, Shaohao's former ruins.
However, Duke Zhou was not allowed to go to his own kingdom, but stayed in Chaoyan to assist King Wu.
In the second year after King Wu defeated Yin Zhou, the unification of the world had not yet succeeded. King Wu fell ill and was unwell, and the ministers were frightened. Taigong and Zhaogong wanted to perform divination piously to know good and bad luck.
Duke Zhou said: "You cannot make our late king worry and grieve."
Duke Zhou then used himself as a pledge and set up three altars. Standing facing the north, holding a jade and a gui, he prayed to the spirits of King Tai, Wang Ji and King Wen.
The historian was ordered to write a congratulatory message saying: Your eldest grandson, King Zhou, will be sent to you. Hard work leads to illness.
If the three former kings owe God a son, please send Dan instead of Zhou Wangfa.
Dan is smart, capable, versatile, and able to serve ghosts and gods.
King Fa of Zhou was not as versatile as Dan and could not serve ghosts and gods.
But King Fa of Zhou was ordered by Heaven to help the whole world, and to enable your descendants to live peacefully in the world. People everywhere will respect him.
He can ensure that the heaven-given treasures are preserved for a long time, and our late king can be enshrined forever.
Now I obey the orders of the late king through the divination turtle. If you can agree to my request, I will offer the jade and obey your orders.
If you don't agree, I will hide the jade.
After Zhou Gong ordered the historian to write a book to congratulate King Tai, Wang Ji, and King Wen that he would replace King Wu with his own body, he went to the altar of the three kings to divine fortune.
People in fortune-telling said it was auspicious. When I opened the omen book, I found that it was indeed auspicious.
Duke Zhou was very happy, so he opened the lock and looked at the divination book hidden in the cabinet, which was also an auspicious sign.
The Duke of Zhou immediately entered the palace to congratulate King Wu and said: "You are not in trouble. I have just accepted the orders of the three ancestors, so that you only need to consider the long-term plan of the Zhou Dynasty and the world, and have nothing else to worry about."
This is what is called God’s thoughtful consideration for the Emperor. Duke Zhou put the scroll into a gold-wired cabinet and sealed it, warning the keepers not to leak it.
The next day, King Wu suddenly recovered.
summary: Duke Dan of Zhou, younger brother of King Wu of Zhou, was known for his filial piety and virtue. He assisted King Wu in military campaigns, including the conquest of Yin Zhou at Muye. After Yin Zhou's death, Duke Zhou participated in ceremonies announcing King Zhou's guilt, released the imprisoned Jizi, and helped grant territories to various nobles. Though granted the title of Duke of Lu in Qufu, he remained in the capital to assist King Wu.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家

translation:
Later, King Wu died and King Cheng was still in his infancy.
Duke Zhou was worried that people in the world would betray the court when they heard about King Wu's death, so he ascended the throne to handle government affairs on behalf of King Cheng and preside over the power of the country.
Guan Shu and his brothers spread rumors in the country: Duke Zhou will be detrimental to the king.
The Duke of Zhou then told Taigong Wang and Zhao Gongsi: The reason why I do not avoid suspicion and act in the affairs of the country is because I am afraid that the people in the world will betray the Zhou family and cannot explain to our ancestors Taiwang Taiwang, Wang Ji and King Wen.
The three ancestors have worked hard for the cause of the world for a long time, and they have just succeeded.
King Wu died young and King Cheng was young. I only did this to complete the great cause of stabilizing the Zhou Dynasty.
So he eventually assisted in becoming king, and ordered his son Boqin to go to the State of Lu to be granted a title on his behalf.
Zhou Gong warned Bo Qin: I am the son of King Wen, the younger brother of King Wu, and the uncle of King Cheng. My status among the people in the world is not low.
But I had to pull up my hair three times once I washed my hair, spit out the food I was chewing three times after eating a meal, and got up to receive the wise men. Even so, I was afraid of missing out on the wise men in the world.
After you arrive in Lu, don't be arrogant because you have a land.
Sure enough, Guan Shu, Cai Shu, Wu Geng and others led Huaiyi to launch a rebellion.
The Duke of Zhou followed the orders of King Cheng, raised his troops to march eastward, and wrote the "Great Edict".
So Guan Shu was executed, Wu Geng was killed, and Cai Shu was exiled.
Collect the remnants of Yin, grant Kang Shu to Wei, and Wei Zi to Song, and let him perform Yin's sacrifices.
It took another two years to pacify Huaiyi and other areas in the east.
The princes all followed the Zhou Dynasty.
God sent blessings, and Uncle Tang received two stalks of millet and one ear, which he dedicated to King Cheng. King Cheng ordered Uncle Tang to go to the eastern part of the garrison where Duke Zhou's army was stationed and present it to Duke Zhou, and wrote "Feeding Grain".
After Zhou Gong accepted it, he expressed gratitude and praised the emperor's order and wrote "Jiahe".
After the East became stable, Duke Zhou reported back to King Cheng and wrote a poem as a gift to King Cheng. His poem was called "Owl".
King Cheng did not dare to blame Duke Zhou.
On the last day of February in the seventh year of King Cheng, King Cheng went to Haojing to pay homage to Wuwang Temple, and then walked to Fengjing to pay homage to Wenwang Temple. He ordered Taibao Zhaogong to go to Luoyi first to survey the terrain.
In March, Duke Zhou went to Luoyi to build the capital city of Zhou and conducted divination. The results showed good luck, so he made Luoyi the capital.
King Cheng grew up and was able to handle state affairs.
So Zhou Gong returned the political power to King Cheng, who came to the court to listen to the government.
In the past, when the Duke of Zhou replaced King Cheng in governing the world, he faced the south and his back to the wall to accept the worship of the princes.
Seven years later, when King Cheng returned the throne, Duke Zhou faced north and stood in the position of a minister, still cautious and respectful as if he were walking on thin ice.
summary: When King Wu fell ill, Duke Zhou offered himself as a sacrifice to the ancestral spirits, praying to die in King Wu's place. He performed divination, received auspicious signs, and King Wu recovered. After King Wu's death, with King Cheng still an infant, Duke Zhou assumed regency to prevent rebellion. His brothers Guan Shu and Cai Shu spread rumors that he would harm the young king. Duke Zhou explained his actions were to preserve the Zhou legacy, and eventually suppressed a rebellion led by Guan Shu, Cai Shu, and Wu Geng, executing Guan Shu and exiling Cai Shu.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家

translation:
When King Cheng was young, he fell ill once. Duke Zhou cut off his fingernails and sank them into the river. He prayed to the gods and said: "The king has no opinions when he is young, and he offends the gods."
He also hid the blessing notice in the secret palace, and the illness of King Cheng was indeed cured.
After King Cheng came to the throne, some people said bad things about Duke Zhou, so Duke Zhou fled to the state of Chu.
King Cheng opened the secret palace and found the prayer book written by Duke Zhou. He was moved to tears and immediately invited Duke Zhou back.
After Zhou Gong returned to the country, he was afraid that the young king would indulge in debauchery while governing the country, so he wrote "Toast" and "Wuyi".
"Wu Yi" says: As parents, it is extremely difficult to start a business for a long time. Their descendants are arrogant and extravagant and forget the hardships of their ancestors, ruining the family business. Sons of man must be cautious!
Therefore, in the past, King Zhongzong of Yin solemnly and respectfully feared the mandate of heaven, was strict with himself when governing the people, competed in the industry and did not dare to neglect his career for his own pleasure, so Zhongzong owned the country for seventy-five years.
Emperor Gaozong of Yin worked hard among the people for a long time and lived with the common people. After he came to the throne, he went into mourning and remained silent for three years. Once he spoke, he won the support of his subjects and did not dare to indulge in debauchery. This made the country of Yin stable and the ministers of the common people had no complaints. Therefore, Emperor Gaozong reigned for fifty-five years.
King Zujia of Yin felt that he was not the eldest son and it was not morally right to be a king, so he escaped from the people for a long time. He was well aware of the people's needs. He stabilized the country and benefited the people. He did not regret being arrogant to a widowed and lonely man. Therefore, Zujia owned the country for thirty-three years.
"Toushi" said: From Tang Dynasty to Emperor Yi, all the kings of the Yin Dynasty followed the etiquette system to perform sacrifices, worked hard to be virtuous, and were able to live up to the destiny.
Later, when he came to Yin and Zhou Dynasty, he was very dissolute and indulgent, regardless of the will of God and the people. All the people thought that he should be killed.
King Wen of Zhou had no time to eat when the sun turned west every day, and he owned the country for fifty years.
Duke Zhou wrote these to warn King Cheng.
King Cheng lived in Fengjing. Although the world was stable at that time, the official system of the Zhou Dynasty had not yet been properly arranged, so Zhou Gong wrote "Zhou Officials" to delineate the responsibilities of hundreds of officials. He wrote "Establishing Government" to benefit the people and make them happy.
Duke Zhou fell ill in Fengjing and said before his death: I must be buried in Chengzhou to show that I dare not leave King Cheng.
After the death of Duke Zhou, King Cheng also showed humility, and finally buried Duke Zhou in Biyi, accompanying King Wen, to show that King Cheng did not dare to treat Duke Zhou as his minister.
After the death of Duke Zhou, just before the harvest in the autumn, suddenly there was a strong wind, thunder and lightning, all the crops fell down, and the big trees were uprooted.
The whole state of Zhou was greatly frightened.
At this time, King Cheng and the officials put on their formal attires, opened the Book of Golden Ribbons, and saw the brief letter stating that Duke Zhou was willing to take himself as a hostage and die for King Wu.
Taigong, Zhaogong and Chengwang asked the historian and other officials for confirmation. They replied: "This is indeed the case. At that time, Duke Zhou ordered us not to tell it."
King Cheng held the slip and cried: "I'm afraid there will never be such pious divination from now on."
In the past, Duke Zhou worked hard for the royal family, but a young person like me didn't know it yet.
Now that God is showing his majesty to commend Zhou Gong for his virtue, I will personally go to greet the God. According to the etiquette of our country, I should do the same.
So King Cheng went out of the city to hold a ceremony to worship the sky on the outskirts of the city. It started to rain immediately, the wind direction reversed, and the fallen crops stood upright again.
Taigong and Zhaogong asked people to pick up all the big trees that had been blown down, and use soil to build up the roots of the trees and tamp them firmly.
This year the whole country received a bumper harvest.
So King Cheng ordered the king of Lu to hold suburban sacrifices and worship King Wen.
The state of Lu had the emperor's rituals and music, which were used to praise Zhou Gong's virtues.
summary: Duke Zhou governed for seven years, then returned power to King Cheng when the king came of age. He wrote admonitions including "Wu Yi" and "Toushi" to warn King Cheng against indulgence, citing examples of Yin Dynasty rulers who prospered through diligence or fell through decadence. After Duke Zhou's death, King Cheng buried him beside King Wen. When a storm destroyed crops, King Cheng opened the golden-bound cabinet containing Duke Zhou's prayer to die for King Wu, realized his virtue, and performed ceremonies that restored the harvest.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家

translation:
So he defeated Duke Zhao's army.
When Meng Yizi heard that Shusun's family had won the battle, he also pursued Bo Zhaobo.
Zhaobo Li was sent to the Meng family as an envoy of Duke Zhao, so the Meng family captured him.
The three families jointly attacked Duke Zhao, who fled abroad.
On the day of Jihai, Duke Zhao fled to Qi.
Duke Jin of Qi said to Duke Zhao: I am willing to give a thousand houses to receive the king.
Zi Jia said: "Is it okay to give up Zhou Gong's inheritance and surrender to Qi?"
So this behavior stopped.
Zi Jia said: Qi Jinggong is not trustworthy, so it is better to go to Jin as soon as possible.
Duke Zhao did not listen.
Shusun went to the state of Qi to see Duke Zhao and then returned to the state of Lu. He went to see Pingzi, and Pingzi kowtowed.
At first, they wanted to welcome Duke Zhao back, but Meng Sun and Ji Sun regretted it and did not do so.
In the spring of the 26th year, Qi attacked Lu and occupied Yunyi, allowing Duke Zhao of Lu to live there.
In the summer, Duke Jin of Qi wanted to escort Duke Zhao back to his country by force, and ordered his subordinates not to accept gifts from Lu.
Doctors Shen Feng and Ru Jia of Lu promised to give 80,000 dou of grain to Doctor Gao Lu and Zijiang of Qi.
The general said to the Marquis of Qi: The ministers of Lu disobey the Lord of Lu, and there are strange phenomena.
Duke Yuan of Song Dynasty went to Jin State to ask for help for Duke Zhao of Lu, and wanted to support Duke Zhao in returning to the country, but died on the way.
Uncle Sun Zhaozi asked Lu Jun to return to his country and died without illness.
I wonder if God abandoned Lu Jun, or did he offend ghosts and gods?
Please wait and see.
Qi Jinggong obeyed his words.
In the twenty-eighth year, Duke Zhao went to Jin and asked for support in returning to the country to become king.
Ji Pingzi bribed the six ministers of Jin. The six ministers accepted Ji's gift and went to admonish the king of Jin. The king of Jin no longer insisted and only allowed Zhaogong to live in Qianhou.
In the twenty-ninth year, Duke Zhao came to Yunyi.
Duke Jinggong of Qi sent someone to deliver a letter to Duke Zhao, in which he called Duke Zhao "the Lord".
Duke Zhao felt it was a shame and went to Qianhou again in anger.
In the thirty-first year, the people of Jin wanted to support Duke Zhao in returning to Lu, so they summoned Ji Pingzi.
Ji Pingzi walked barefoot in common clothes and apologized to the six ministers.
Liuqing spoke for Ji Pingzi and said: Although Jin supports Duke Zhao, the people of Lu are unwilling.
Jin Jun gave up.
In the thirty-second year, Duke Zhao died in Qianhou.
The people of Lu jointly established Zhaogong's younger brother Song as their king, who was named Dinggong.
After Duke Ding was established, Zhao Jianzi asked Shi Mo: Will the Ji family perish?
Shi Mo replied: It will not perish.
Ji You made great contributions to the state of Lu, and was granted the title of Shangqing in Eyi. He continued to expand his business through generations until Wenzi and Wuzi.
After Duke Wen of Lu passed away, Dongmen killed his legitimate son and made his concubine the king of Lu. The king of Lu lost his political power.
The national affairs are controlled by the Ji family, and so far there have been four monarchs.
The people don't know their king. How does the king control the administrative power of the country?
Because of this, the monarch should treat the country's vehicles, equipment, titles and titles with caution, and should not give them to others easily.
summary: The state of Lu continued through successive dukes. Duke Boqin, Duke Zhou's son, governed Lu and suppressed rebellions. The state experienced periods of stability and turmoil, with conflicts over succession and the growing power of the Three Huan families (Mengsun, Shusun, Jisun). Duke Zhao was forced into exile after attacking the Ji family, dying in Qianhou. The state declined as the Three Huan families grew increasingly powerful, reducing subsequent rulers to figureheads. The state of Lu lasted for thirty-four generations from Duke Zhou to Duke Qing, when King Kaolie of Chu conquered Lu. The historian Sima Qian noted that despite Lu's reputation for ritual propriety, its actual history was marked by chaos, including the murder of legitimate heirs and ministers attacking their rulers, revealing a contradiction between their ceremonial observance and political reality.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/鲁周公世家

translation:
Taigong looked at Lu Shang, who was from the East China Sea.
His ancestors once served as officials in the Four Mountains, assisting Xia Yu in water management and made great contributions.
Shun and Yu were granted the title of Lu, and some were granted the title of Shen, with the surname Jiang.
During the Xia and Shang dynasties, some places in Shen and Lu were granted to descendants of other branches, and some descendants became commoners. Lu Shang is their descendant.
Lu Shang's original surname was Jiang. Because he took the name of his fiefdom, he was called Lu Shang.
Lu Shang was once very famous. When he was old, he took the opportunity of fishing to ask to see Zhou Xibo.
Before going out hunting, Xibo made a divination, and the hexagram said: The prey obtained is neither a dragon nor a chi, nor a tiger nor a bear; what he obtains is the assistant minister who will become the overlord.
So Xibohou went out hunting, and sure enough he met Taigong on the north bank of the Wei River. After talking with Taigong, Xibo was overjoyed and said: I have long heard the Taigong, the ancestor of our country, say: A saint will definitely come to Zhou, and Zhou will prosper.
That's you, right?
Our grandpa has been waiting for you for a long time.
So he called Lu Shang "Tai Gong Wang", and the two of them rode back together and respected him as military advisor.
Some people say that Taigong was very knowledgeable and once assisted King Zhou of Shang Dynasty.
Because King Zhou was unruly, Taigong left.
He went around lobbying the princes of various countries, but failed to find a king, so he finally went west to join Zhou Xibo.
Some people say that Lu Shang was a scholar who lived in seclusion by the sea.
When Zhou Xibo was imprisoned in Youli by King Zhou, Xibo's ministers San Yisheng and Hong Yao knew about Lu Shang, so they asked him to come out.
Lu Shang also said this: I heard that Xibo was virtuous and always respected and cared for the elderly. Why not go there?
In order to rescue Uncle Xi, these three people searched for beautiful women and rare treasures, and presented them to King Zhou to redeem Uncle Xi.
As a result, Xibo was released and returned to Zhou.
Although there are different legends about Lu Shang's return to the Zhou Dynasty, the general consensus is that he was the teacher and assistant minister of King Wen and King Wu.
After Zhou Xibochang escaped from Youli and returned to the country, he and Lu Shang secretly planned how to implement virtue and overthrow the rule of the Shang Dynasty. Many of them were military tactics and cunning tactics. Therefore, future generations who talked about military tactics and the secret power of the Zhou Dynasty all respected the basic strategies of the Grand Duke.
Zhou Xibo was upright and peaceful. Especially after the territorial dispute between the Yu and Rui kingdoms, he was praised as King Wen who was destined to receive the destiny.
Xibo also conquered Chongguo, Mixu and Quanyi, and built Fengyi on a large scale.
Two-thirds of the princes in the world turned their hearts to the Zhou Dynasty, which was mostly the result of the Taigong's planning.
After King Wen died, King Wu came to the throne.
In the ninth year, King Wu wanted to continue to complete King Wen's great cause and campaigned eastward against Shang Zhou to see if the princes gathered to respond.
When the army was leaving, Lu Shang, who was respectfully called "Master Shangfu", held a yellow ax in his left hand and a Bingbai jade in his right hand, swearing to be the master, and said: Cang Si Cang Si, command the troops, assemble the ships, and behead those who are late.
So the army arrived at Mengjin.
There were as many as eight hundred princes who came without being summoned. The princes all said: It is time to conquer Shang Zhou. King Wu said: Not yet.
summary: Taigong Wang, originally named Lu Shang and surnamed Jiang, was a descendant of officials who assisted Yu in flood control during ancient times. In his old age, he met Zhou Xibo (later King Wen of Zhou) while fishing on the Wei River. Xibo, having received a divination that he would find an assistant to become overlord, recognized Lu Shang as the sage his ancestors had predicted would come to Zhou. He called him "Taigong Wang" and respected him as military advisor. Some accounts say Lu Shang had previously served King Zhou of Shang but left due to his unruliness, while others claim he was a recluse recruited by Xibo's ministers to help rescue Xibo from imprisonment. Regardless of the legends, all agree he became teacher and assistant to both King Wen and King Wu. Taigong secretly planned with King Wen to implement virtue and overthrow Shang rule, employing military tactics that later generations would honor. After King Wen's death, King Wu succeeded him. In the ninth year of King Wu's reign, he campaigned eastward with Taigong as his commander, gathering eight hundred princes at Mengjin. Two years later, despite unfavorable divination and a storm, Taigong persuaded King Wu to march. They defeated Shang Zhou at Muye, and King Zhou was killed. King Wu then distributed Shang's wealth to the poor, honored loyal ministers, and established Zhou governance—all following Taigong's advice.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家

translation:
He returned as a teacher and wrote "Tai Oath" with Tai Gong.
Two years later, Shang Zhou killed Prince Bigan and imprisoned Jizi.
King Wu was preparing to conquer the Shang Dynasty again, and a divination revealed that the tortoise sign was unlucky, with a sudden storm coming.
The ministers were frightened, and only Taigong persuaded King Wu to march, so King Wu led his troops to fight.
On the first day of the eleventh year, King Wu swore an oath in Muye to attack Shang Zhou.
Shang Zhou's army collapsed completely.
Shang Zhou turned around and fled, boarding Lutai, whereupon his pursuers killed King Zhou.
The next day, King Wu stood on the social altar, and the ministers held water in their hands. Wei Kangshufeng laid out the colorful mats, and Master Shangfu brought the animals for sacrifice. Shi Yi prayed according to the policy book and reported to the gods about the crusade against the evil Shang Zhou.
Distribute the coins accumulated by Shang Zhou in Lutai and distribute the grain accumulated by Shang Zhou in Juqiao to help the poor.
Build and raise the height of Bigan's tomb, and release the imprisoned Jizi.
He moved the Jiuding, which symbolizes the highest power in the world, to the Zhou Dynasty, fixed the government affairs of the Zhou Dynasty, and started to create a new era together with the people of the world.
Most of the above-mentioned matters were based on the advice of Master Shangfu.
At this time, King Wu had pacified Shang Zhou and became the king of the world, so he awarded the title of Yingqiu of Qi State to his master Shangfu.
Master Shangfu went east to his own feudal country, living and traveling at a very slow pace.
The people in the guest house said to him: I heard that opportunities are hard to come by but easy to lose.
This guest slept so peacefully, I'm afraid he didn't go to the feudal country to take up his post.
After hearing this, the Grand Duke dressed up overnight and set out on the road, arriving at his own kingdom at dawn.
Just when Laihou led his troops to attack, he wanted to compete with Taigong for the camp.
Yingqiu is adjacent to Laiguo.
The Lai people were a Yi tribe. They took advantage of the chaos of Shang and Zhou and the Zhou Dynasty had just settled down. There was no time to pacify the remote areas, so they competed with Taigong for territory.
After Taigong arrived in his feudal country, he straightened political affairs, followed its customs, simplified etiquette, opened up industry and commerce, and developed the advantages of fishery and salt industry. As a result, more people joined Qi State, and Qi State became a great power.
When King Cheng of Zhou came to the throne at a young age, Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai rebelled, and Huaiyi also rebelled against the Zhou Dynasty. King Cheng sent Zhao Kanggong and ordered Tai Gong to say: From the sea in the east, to the Yellow River in the west, to Muling in the south, and to Wudi in the north, the five-level princes here are guarded by local officials. If there is any crime, I order you to attack.
Therefore, Qi can conquer other countries and form a great country, with its capital at Yingqiu.
Taigong was already more than a hundred years old when he died, and his son Dinggong Lu Ji succeeded to the throne.
When Ding Gong died, his son Yi Gong succeeded him.
When Duke Yi died, his son Gui Gong and his loving mother succeeded him.
When Duke Gui passed away, his son Aigong Buchen succeeded him.
summary: King Wu enfeoffed Taigong with the state of Qi at Yingqiu. When Taigong traveled slowly to his fief, a lodging house keeper warned him that opportunities are easily lost. He immediately hurried and arrived just as the Lai people attacked for the territory. Taigong governed by simplifying customs, opening commerce, and developing fishery and salt industries, making Qi a great power. King Cheng later granted Taigong authority to conquer any rebellious nobles within vast territories. Taigong died over one hundred years old.
