translation:
When Duke Ai was in power, the Marquis of Ji framed Duke Ai to the king of Zhou. The king of Zhou boiled Duke Ai to death in a big cauldron, and appointed Duke Ai's younger brother Jing as the king of Qi, namely Duke Hu.
Duke Hu moved the capital to Bogu during the reign of King Zhou Yi.
Shan, the younger brother of Duke Ai, resented Duke Hu, so he and his followers led the people from Yingqiu to attack and kill Duke Hu, and established themselves as Duke Xian of Qi.
In the first year of Xian's reign, they all expelled Hu Gong's disciples and took the opportunity to move the capital from Bogu to Linzi.
In the ninth year, Duke Xian died and his son, Duke Wu, succeeded him.
In the ninth year of Duke Wu, King Li of Zhou fled and lived in Sheyi.
Ten years later, the Zhou royal family was in chaos, and the ministers presided over the state affairs, which was known as the "Republic".
In the twenty-fourth year, King Zhou Xuan ascended the throne.
In the twenty-sixth year, Duke Wu died and his son Li Gong Wuji succeeded him.
Duke Li was ruthless and wreaking havoc, so Duke Hu's son returned to Qi. The people of Qi wanted to make Duke Hu's son their king, so they attacked and killed Duke Li together.
Hu Gong's son also died in the battle.
The people of Qi then appointed Chi, the son of Duke Li, as Duke Wen of Qi. He killed more than seventy people who attacked and killed Duke Li.
Duke Wen died in the 12th year, and his son Cheng Gongtu succeeded to the throne.
Chenggong died in the ninth year, and his son Zhuang Gonggu succeeded to the throne.
In the twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhuang, Quan Rong killed King You, and the Zhou royal family moved its capital eastward to Luoyi.
Qin began to rank among its princes.
In the fifty-sixth year, the Jin people killed their king, Jin Zhaohou.
In the sixty-fourth year, Duke Zhuang died and his son Li Gong Lufu succeeded him.
In the ninth year of Duke Li, Duke Yin of Lu came to the throne.
In the 19th year, Duke Huan of Lu killed his brother Yin Gong and established himself as Lord of Lu.
In the twenty-fifth year, Beirong attacked Qi.
The prince of Zheng suddenly came to rescue Qi, and the Marquis of Qi wanted to marry his daughter to him.
The prince suddenly said: Zheng is small and Qi is big, I am not worthy of your daughter.
I declined.
In the thirty-second year, Li Gong's brother Yi Zhongnian passed away.
His son's name was Gongsun Wuzhi. Li Gong doted on him and gave him the same level of care, clothing, life and treatment as the prince.
In the thirty-third year, Li Gong died, and the prince's sons came to the throne, namely Xianggong.
In the first year of Xiang AD, when Duke Xiang was still the prince, he had a fight with Wuzhi. After he came to the throne, he lowered Wuzhi's salary, carriages, horses and clothing, and Wuzhi was very resentful.
In the fourth year, Duke Huan of Lu and his wife came to Qi.
Duke Xiang of Qi had an affair with Mrs. Lu in the past.
Mrs. Lu is the sister of Duke Xiang. She married Duke Huan of Lu as his wife during the reign of Duke Li of Qi. This time she came to Qi with Duke Huan of Lu and committed adultery with Duke Xiang.
When Duke Huan of Lu found out about this, he scolded his wife angrily, and she told Duke Xiang of Qi.
Duke Xianggang of Qi hosted a banquet for Duke Huan of Lu, got him drunk, and sent his strongman Peng Sheng to carry Duke Huan of Lu into the chariot. He then broke Duke Huan's ribs and killed Duke Huan. Duke Huan was already dead when he got out of the car.
The people of Lu blamed Qi for this, and Qi Xianggong killed Peng Sheng to apologize to Lu and atone for his sins.
In the eighth year, Qi State conquered Ji State, and Ji State was forced to move its capital.
summary: The succession continued through Dinggong, Yigong, Guigong, and Aigong, whom the Marquis of Ji falsely accused, leading to his execution by boiling. His brother Jing became Duke Hu but was killed by Aigong's brother Shan, who became Duke Xian and moved the capital to Linzi. Subsequent rulers included Duke Wu, Duke Li (killed by the people for his tyranny), Duke Wen, Duke Cheng, and Duke Zhuang. During Duke Zhuang's reign, the Zhou royal family moved east to Luoyi after Quan Rong killed King You.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家

translation:
In the twelfth year, Duke Xiang sent Lian Cheng and Guan Zhifu to garrison in Kuiqiu. They agreed to go there when the melons ripened in July, and sent someone to replace them when the melons ripened the next year.
They went to garrison for a year, but after the ripening period passed, Duke Xiang still did not send anyone to replace them.
Someone asked Duke Xiang to send someone to replace them, but Duke Xiang refused.
So the two were angry and planned a rebellion through Gongsun Wuwu.
Lian said that he had a cousin who was not favored in the palace of Duke Xiang, so he asked her to spy on Duke Xiang secretly and said to her: "When the matter is completed, I will let you be Gongsun Wuzhi's wife."
In the twelfth month of winter, Duke Xiang visited Gufen and went hunting in Peiqiu.
He saw a wild boar, and the attendant said it was Peng Sheng.
Duke Xiang was furious and shot the wild boar away with an arrow. The wild boar then stood up and barked like a human being.
Duke Xiang was so frightened that he fell off the carriage and injured his foot. His shoes also fell off.
After returning, he whipped the shoekeeper named Fu three hundred times.
Fu left the palace.
When Wuzhi, Lian Cheng, Guan Zhifu and others heard that Duke Xiang was injured, they led their troops to attack Duke Xiang's palace.
He happened to meet Fu who was helping Duke Xiang put on his shoes. Fu said, "Don't go in yet so as not to disturb the palace. Once the palace is disturbed, it will be difficult to attack again."
Wu Wu didn't believe this, so Fu asked him to check his wounds, and then Wu Wu believed it.
They waited outside the palace and asked Fu Xian to go in and inquire.
After Fu first entered, he immediately hid Mr. Xiang behind the door of the house.
After a long time, Wuzhi and others felt a little scared and went into the palace.
Fu Gui, the people in the palace and the trusted ministers of Duke Xianggang counterattacked Wuzhi and others, but failed to win and were all killed.
When I entered the palace ignorantly, I could not find Duke Xiang.
Someone saw human feet exposed under the door of the house. When he opened the door, he saw that it was Duke Xiang who was behind the door. He killed Duke Xiang and made himself king of Qi out of ignorance.
In the spring of the first year of Emperor Huan's reign, Lord Qi Wuzhi went to Yonglin for a visit.
Some people in Yonglin once resented Wuzhi. When Wuwu went to play, the people of Yonglin attacked and killed Wuzhi. They announced to the officials of Qi: Wuzhi killed Duke Xiang and established himself as king. I have put him to death.
Please ask the officials to appoint the other princes who should take the throne. I will obey your orders.
At the beginning, Duke Xiang got Duke Huan of Lu drunk and killed him, and he committed adultery with Lady Lu. He also repeatedly killed and punished inappropriately, indulged in womanizing, and bullied ministers many times. His younger brothers were afraid of being implicated in the disaster, so Duke Xiang's second brother, Gong Zijiu, fled to the state of Lu. His mother was the daughter of the state of Lu.
Guan Zhong and Zhao Hu assisted him.
Prince Xiaobai, the third younger brother of Duke Xiang, fled to Ju State, and Bao Shuya assisted him.
Xiaobai's mother was the daughter of the King of Wei, and she was favored by Duke Li of Qi.
Xiaobai has been friends with the doctor Gao Xi since he was a child.
After the Yonglin people killed Wuzhi, the ministers discussed the matter of establishing a king. The Gao family and the Guo family secretly recalled Xiaobai from Ju.
summary: Duke Li was succeeded by Duke Xiang, who had conflicts with his cousin Wuzhi and committed adultery with his sister, Lady Lu of Lu. When Duke Huan of Lu discovered this, Duke Xiang had him killed. Later, Duke Xiang was killed by Wuzhi and conspirators after failing to replace garrison troops as promised. Wuzhi was then killed by the people of Yonglin.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家

translation:
When the State of Lu heard that Wuzhi was dead, it also sent troops to escort the young master Jiu back to Qi, and ordered Guan Zhong to lead another army to block the passage of Ju State. Guan Zhong shot an arrow at the belt hook of Xiaobai's waist.
Xiaobai pretended to be dead, so Guan Zhong sent someone to report to Lu.
The troops escorting Prince Jiu from the state of Lu slowed down, and it took them six days to reach the state of Qi. Xiaobai had already entered the state of Qi first, and Gao Xi made him the king, Duke Huan.
After Duke Huan was shot in the hook of his belt, he pretended to be dead to confuse Guan Zhong, and then hid in Wen's chariot and drove quickly. Because he had the two major families of the Gao family and the Guo family as internal agents, he was able to enter Qi first and ascend the throne, and sent troops to resist the Lu army.
In autumn, the Qi soldiers fought with the Lu soldiers at Qianshi. The Lu soldiers were defeated and fled, but the Qi soldiers cut off the Lu soldiers' retreat.
The State of Qi wrote to the State of Lu, saying: Zijiu is my brother. I cannot bear to kill him with my own hands. Please ask the State of Lu to kill him.
Zhao Hu and Guan Zhong were my enemies. I asked for them to be handed over to me alive, and I was willing to chop them into pieces. Otherwise, Qi soldiers will besiege Lu.
The people of Lu were afraid and killed Zijiu in Shengdu. Zhao Hu committed suicide and Guan Zhong asked for his imprisonment.
When Duke Huan came to the throne, he sent troops to attack Lu, intending to kill Guan Zhong.
Bao Shuya said: I am honored to follow you, and you finally became the king.
I can no longer help you improve your exalted status.
If you only want to govern Qi, Gao Xi and I will be enough.
If you want to become an overlord, don't worry about Yiwu.
The country where Yiwu lives must be strong and cannot lose this talent.
So Duke Huan listened to this.
He pretended to recall Guan Zhong to take revenge, but in fact he wanted to let him rule.
Guan Zhong knew it, so he asked for Qi to be returned.
Bao Shuya welcomed Guan Zhong. As soon as he arrived at Tangfu in Qi State, he removed Guan Zhong's shackles and asked him to fast, bathe and see Duke Huan.
Duke Huan rewarded him with generous gifts and appointed Guan Zhong as a doctor to preside over government affairs.
After Duke Huan got Guan Zhong, he worked with Bao Shu, Xi Peng, and Gao Xi to manage the political affairs of Qi State, implemented the military service system with five families as the basic units, developed the advantages of commercial circulation, fishery and salt industry, used them to relieve the poor, reward the capable people, and everyone in Qi State was happy.
In the second year of Duke Huan, Qi conquered and destroyed Tan, and the king of Tan fled to Ju.
When Duke Huan fled in the early years, he visited the country of Tan. The king of Tan was rude to Duke Huan, so he attacked him.
Five years later, the Lu army was defeated.
Duke Zhuang of Lu asked for the city of Sui to be used for peace, and Duke Huan agreed to make an alliance with the Lu people in Ke.
When the oath was about to be made, Cao Mo of Lu kidnapped Duke Huan of Qi with a dagger on the altar and said: "Return the occupied land of Lu!"
Duke Huan agreed.
Then Cao Mo threw away the dagger and returned to his seat of ministers facing north.
Duke Huan regretted not returning the occupied territory of Lu and had Cao Mo killed.
Guan Zhong said: If you agree to someone else's request when you are kidnapped, and then break your promise and kill someone, you are satisfied with a small pleasure, but you have lost your trust among the princes, and you have lost the support of the people in the world. You cannot do this.
Duke Huan then returned all the territory that Cao Mo had lost after three defeats to Lu.
summary: After Duke Xiang's death, his brothers competed for the throne. Prince Xiaobai, with support from the Gao and Guo families, returned first and became Duke Huan of Qi. He initially wanted to kill Guan Zhong, but Bao Shuya convinced him that Guan Zhong was essential for becoming overlord. Duke Huan appointed Guan Zhong as minister, and together with Bao Shu, Xi Peng, and Gao Xi, they reformed Qi's government, implemented military systems, developed commerce and fisheries, and relieved the poor, bringing happiness to the people.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家

translation:
When the princes heard about it, they all believed that Qi was trustworthy and were willing to surrender.
In the seventh year, the princes and Duke Heng of Qi met in Zhendi for an alliance. From then on, Duke Huan of Qi became the overlord of the princes in the world.
In the fourteenth year, Chen Ligong's son Chen Wan, named Jingzhong, fled to Qi.
Duke Huan of Qi wanted to appoint him as a minister, but he humbly declined; so he was appointed Gongzheng in charge of hundreds of works.
This is the ancestor of Tian Chengzi and Tian Chang.
In the twenty-third year, Shan Rong invaded Yan State, and Yan asked Qi State for help.
Duke Huan of Qi sent troops to rescue Yan, and then attacked Shanrong. He only returned to Guzhu after arriving at Guzhu.
King Yanzhuang sent Duke Huan into the territory of Qi again.
Duke Huan said: Except for the emperor, the princes cannot send each other out of their own borders. I cannot be rude to Yan.
So the territory of Qi State where Yan Jun went was divided with ditches and given to Yan State, so that Yan Jun could rebuild the government of Zhao Gong and pay tribute to the Zhou royal family, just like in the days of King Cheng and King Kang of Zhou.
After the princes heard about it, they all obeyed Qi.
In the twenty-seventh year, Duke Min of Lu's mother was called Ai Jiang, and she was the sister of Duke Huan of Qi.
Aijiang had an affair with Qingfu, the son of Lu Gong, and Qingfu killed Duke Min. Aijiang wanted to make Qingfu the king, but the Lu people instead made Duke Li.
Duke Huan called Ai Jiang back to Qi and killed him.
In the twenty-eighth year, Duke Wen of Wei was invaded by the Di people and asked Qi for help.
The state of Qi led the princes to build a city in Chuqiu and placed the king of Wei there.
In the twenty-ninth year, Duke Heng and his wife Cai Ji took a boat trip.
Cai Ji was familiar with the nature of water, so she rocked the boat and jolted Duke Huan. Duke Huan was afraid and ordered her to stop, but she still did not stop. After getting off the boat, Duke Huan was angry and sent Cai Ji back to Cai State, but he did not break off the marriage.
The king of Cai State was also very angry, so he married Cai Ji to someone else.
After hearing this, Duke Huan became even more angry and raised troops to attack Cai Guo.
Thirty years ago in the spring, Duke Huan of Qi led the princes to attack Cai State, and Cai State was defeated.
Duke Huan continued to attack Chu.
King Chu Cheng led his troops to meet the enemy and asked: "Why did you enter my country?"
Guan Zhong replied: In the past, Duke Kang ordered me to be the first king of Taigong: "You have the right to conquer the fifth-level princes and guard the officials in various places to assist the Zhou Dynasty."
The territory that my late king has the authority to conquer extends to the sea in the east, the Yellow River in the west, Muling in the south, and Wudi in the north.
Baomao, who was supposed to pay tribute from the Chu State, did not pay tribute, resulting in incomplete sacrificial supplies for the emperor, so he came to hold him accountable.
Once upon a time, King Zhao of Zhou did not return from his southern expedition and died in the south, so he came to question him.
The King of Chu said: "I did not pay the tribute. It is indeed my fault. I dare not not pay it in the future."
As for King Zhao of Zhou, he never returned and was not in our territory of Chu. Please go to the bank of Han River to question him.
The Qi army continued to march in Xingdi.
In the summer, King Chu ordered Qu Wan to lead his army to resist the Qi army, and the Qi army retreated to Zhaoling.
Duke Huan met Qu Wan and showed off to him that he had many soldiers and generals.
Qu Wan said: Only if you are righteous can you win; otherwise, the Chu State will use Fangcheng Mountain as the city wall and the Yangtze River and Han River as the moat. How can you attack it?
Duke Huan of Qi made an agreement with Qu Wan and then led his troops to retreat.
Passing through the State of Chen, Yuan Taotu, the official of the State of Chen, deceived Duke Huan and asked the Qi army to take the difficult road to the east, but was discovered by the State of Qi.
In autumn, Qi State attacked Chen State.
This year, the king of Jin killed Prince Shen Sheng.
In the summer of the thirty-fifth year, Duke Huan and the princes met at Kuiqiu.
King Xiang of Zhou sent his strategist Kong to reward Duke Huan with the meat used to sacrifice King Wen and King Wu, bows and arrows decorated with red color, and the carriages used by the emperor. He also gave Duke Huan permission not to bow down to express his gratitude. Duke Huan wanted to agree, but Guan Zhong said, "No."
Duke Huan then bowed down and accepted the reward. In autumn, he met with the princes again at Kuiqiu, and Duke Huan of Qi became more and more proud.
summary: Duke Huan became the first overlord of the Spring and Autumn period. He kept his promise to return territory to Lu after Cao Mo's kidnapping, earning trust among princes. He rescued Yan from Shanrong, gave Yan territory, and restored Zhao Gong's governance. He defended Wei against Di invaders and built a city for them. He attacked Cai and Chu for failing to pay tribute, though he eventually made peace with Chu. He convened multiple alliances, including the famous Kuiqiu meeting, where King Xiang of Zhou rewarded him. Despite Guan Zhong's opposition, Duke Huan wanted to perform the fengshan sacrifices but eventually abandoned the idea.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家

translation:
Duke Huan asked: "How is this person doing?"
He replied: He abandoned his parents to cater to the king, which is unkind and unapproachable.
Duke Huan said: "How is this man Shudao?"
He replied: Castrating yourself to please the king is unkind and cannot be trusted.
After Guan Zhong's death, Duke Huan did not listen to Guan Zhong's words, but still closely appointed these three people, who had exclusive power.
In the forty-second year, the Rong people attacked Zhou, and Zhou asked Qi for help. Qi ordered all the princes to send troops to defend the Zhou royal family.
In this year, Prince Chong'er of Jin came to Qi, and Duke Huan of Qi married his daughter to Chong'er.
Forty-three years.
At first, Duke Huan of Qi had three wives: Wang Ji, Xu Ji, and Cai Ji. None of them gave birth to a son.
Duke Huan was lustful and had many favored concubines, among whom there were six concubines with the same status as his wives: Changwei Ji, born to Wu Gui; Shao Wei Ji, born to Hui Gong; Zheng Ji, born to Xiao Gong Zhao; Ge Ying, born to Xiao Gong Pan; Mi Ji, born to Yi Gong Shang; Song Huazi, born to Gongzi Yong.
Duke Huan of Qi and Guan Zhong once entrusted Duke Xiao Gong Zhao to Duke Xiang of Song Dynasty and established him as the crown prince.
Yi Ya was favored by Duke Huan's eldest son, Wei Ji, and through the eunuch Shu Diao, he gave generous gifts to Duke Huan, so he was also favored by Duke Huan. Duke Huan agreed to make Yi Ya the crown prince.
After Guan Zhong's death, the five princes all asked to be crown princes.
On the day of Yihai in the tenth month of winter, Duke Huan of Qi died.
Yi Ya entered the palace, and Shu Dao killed the officials with the help of his favored ministers, and established the young master Wu Gui as the king of Qi.
Prince Zhao fled to the Song Dynasty.
When Duke Huan was seriously ill, the five princes each formed a party and demanded to be crowned prince.
After Duke Huan died, they fought against each other, so that no one in the palace dared to bury Duke Huan in the coffin.
Duke Huan's body lay on the bed for sixty-seven days, and all the maggots on the body crawled outside the door.
On Yihai day of the twelfth month, Wu Gui ascended the throne, and then he put the coffin in and announced the funeral to all countries.
At night on Xinsi day, I put on my clothes and put my coffin in the hall.
There were more than ten sons of Duke Huan, and a total of five of them had ascended the throne: Wugui died three months after he ascended the throne, without a posthumous title; then came Duke Xiao; then Duke Zhao; then Duke Yi; and finally Duke Hui.
In March of the first year of Xiaogong, Song Xianggong led the army of princes to send Prince Zhao of Qi back to the country and attacked Qi.
The people of Qi were afraid and killed their king Wugui.
When the people of Qi were about to make Prince Zhao the king of Qi, the tribes of the other four princes attacked the prince again. The prince fled to the Song Dynasty, and the Song Dynasty fought against the troops of the four princes of Qi.
In May, the Song army defeated the army of the fourth prince and made Prince Zhao the king, who was Qi Xiaogong.
Song Jun was the fourth prince who came to conquer the rebellion because Duke Huan and Guan Zhong had entrusted the prince to him.
Because of the war, Duke Huan of Qi was not buried until August.
In the spring of the sixth year, Qi State attacked Song Dynasty because Song State did not participate in the alliance meeting in Qi State.
In the summer, Song Xianggong passed away.
summary: After Guan Zhong's death, Duke Huan ignored his advice and appointed Yi Ya, Shu Diao, and Kaifang, who seized power. Duke Huan had six favored concubines bearing sons, and after his death, his sons fought for succession. His body lay unburied for sixty-seven days, with maggots crawling outside the door. Five of his sons eventually became rulers: Wugui, Xiaogong, Zhaogong, Yigong, and Huigong.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家

translation:
In the seventh year, Duke Wen of Jin came to the throne.
In the tenth year, Xiaogong passed away. Pan, Xiaogong's younger brother, asked his son to make a prescription to kill Xiaogong's son and made Pan the king, who was Zhaogong.
Duke Zhao is the son of Duke Huan, and his mother's name is Ge Ying.
In the first year of Zhaogong, Duke Wen of Jin defeated the Chu army in Chengpu. He called the princes to make an alliance in Jiantu and met with the emperor of Zhou. The emperor made Jin the overlord of the princes.
In the sixth year, he invaded Qi.
Duke Wen of Jin passed away.
The Qin army was defeated in Huodi.
In the twelfth year, Duke Mu of Qin passed away.
In May of the 19th year, Duke Zhao died, and his son She was made King of Qi.
She's mother was not favored by Duke Zhao, so no one in Qi was afraid of him.
Duke Zhao's younger brother, Merchant, failed to become king after Duke Huan's death. He secretly befriended wise men and cared for the people, so he was very popular among the people.
After the death of Duke Zhao, his son She succeeded to the throne, but he was weak. The merchants and others killed Qi Junshe in front of Zhaogong's grave in October. The merchants established themselves as kings, namely Duke Yigong.
Duke Yi was the son of Duke Huan, and his mother's name was Miji.
In the spring of the fourth year of Duke Yi, when he was still a son, Duke Yi and Bingrong's father hunted together and competed with each other for the prey, but Duke Yi failed to win. After he came to the throne, Duke Yi cut off Bingrong's father's foot and asked Bingrong to drive for him.
Yongzhi's wife was very beautiful, so Duke Yi snatched her into the palace and made Yongzhi his companion.
In the fifth month, Duke Yi was playing in Shenchi. Bingrong and Yongzhi were joking with each other while taking a bath.
Yongzhi said that Bingrong was the son of the man who cut off his feet, while Bingrong said that Yongzhi was the husband who had his wife taken away from him.
Both of them were ashamed of these words and hated Duke Yi together.
So the two of them planned for Yi Gong to go to the bamboo forest to play. They killed Yi Gong in the car, threw the body in the bamboo forest and escaped.
After Yigong came to the throne, he became arrogant and arrogant, and the people did not join him.
The people of Qi deposed the son of Duke Yi and welcomed the prince Yuan from Wei to return to Qi. He made him the king of the country, namely Duke Hui.
Duke Hui was the son of Duke Huan. His mother was a daughter of Wei State named Shao Wei Ji. She fled to Wei State to avoid civil strife in Qi.
In the second year of Duke Hui, Chang Zhai came to Qi. Prince Chengfu attacked and killed Chang Zhai and buried him at the north gate.
Zhao Chuan, the official of Jin State, killed the king of Jin Linggong.
In ten years, Duke Hui died, and his son Qinggong Wuye succeeded him.
At first, Cui Zhu was favored by Duke Hui. After Hui Gong's death, the Gao family and the Guo family were afraid of being coerced by him, so they expelled Cui Zhu from the country, and Cui Zhu fled to Weiguo.
In the first year of Qing AD, King Zhuang of Chu became stronger and conquered the State of Chen. In the second year, the State of Chu besieged the State of Zheng. Zheng Bo surrendered and soon restored Zheng Bo.
summary: The state experienced continued turmoil through various rulers. Duke Yi was killed by Bingrong and Yongzhi after mutilating them. Duke Hui was established after Yigong's death. Duke Qing faced invasion from Jin after his mother laughed at Jin envoy Chuke. Duke Zhuang was killed by Cui Zhu for adultery with his wife. Cui Zhu and Qingfeng then controlled the government until the Tian family rose to power.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家

translation:
The doctors all obeyed him.
In June, Tian Qi, Bao Mu and other officials led troops into the palace to attack Gao Zhaozi.
When Zhaozi heard about it, he and Guohuizi rescued the king.
The king was defeated and Tian Qi's disciples pursued him. Guo Huizi fled to Ju State, but Tian Qi came back and killed Gao Zhaozi.
Yan Yu fled to the state of Lu.
In August, Qi doctor Bingyi fled to Lu.
After Tian Qi defeated the two prime ministers of Gao and Guo, he sent people to Lu to welcome back Yang Sheng.
After Yang Sheng arrived, he hid in Tian Qi's home.
On the Wuzi day of the tenth month, Tian Qi invited all the doctors and said: "Chan'er's mother will hold a meager ceremony at home today. Please come and drink."
During the banquet, Tian Qi put Yang Sheng in a big bag and placed it in the center of the seat. Then he opened the bag and released Yang Sheng, saying: "This is the king of Qi!"
All the doctors paid their respects on the spot.
Then he had to make an oath with all the officials to make Yangsheng the king. At this time, Bao Mu was already drunk, so Tian Qi deceived everyone and said: Bao Mu and I made a plan to make Yangsheng the king.
Bao Mu said angrily: "Have you forgotten Jing Gong's decree that Tu be the king?"
All the officials looked at each other and wanted to regret it. Yang Sheng came forward, kowtowed and said: If you can help me, I will do it, otherwise I will give up.
Bao Mu was also afraid of causing trouble, so he said: "We are all the sons of Jinggong, what's the big deal?"
So he made an alliance with everyone and established Yangsheng as the king of Qi, which was the duke's mourning.
Duke Ai entered the palace and sent people to exile Yan Ruzi to Ni. On the way, he set up a tent and killed Yan Ruzi inside, and expelled Ruizi, his mother.
Ruizi was originally humble and a young boy, so he had no power and the people of the country despised them.
In the first year of mourning, the state of Qi attacked Lu and captured the two places of Xi and Chan.
At first, Yang Sheng fled to Lu, and Ji Kangzi married his sister to him.
After Yang Sheng returned to the country and ascended the throne, he sent someone to the state of Lu to welcome his wife.
His wife Ji Ji had an affair with Marquis Ji Yi and told the truth to her family. The Lu people did not dare to give Ji Ji to the Qi State, so the Qi State attacked the Lu State and finally took Ji Ji to Qi.
Ji Ji was favored by Duke Mourning, and Qi State returned the occupied land of Lu State.
Bao Zi had conflicts with Duke Ai, and their relationship was not harmonious.
In the fourth year, Wu and Lu attacked the southern part of Qi.
Bao Zi killed Duke Mourning and reported his mourning to the State of Wu.
King Wu Fu Chai cried and mourned outside the military gate for three days according to etiquette. He was about to march by sea to attack Qi.
The Qi army defeated the Wu army and the Wu army retreated.
Zhao Yang of Jin State attacked Qi State and withdrew his troops after reaching Lai.
The people of Qi unanimously supported Duke Yu's son Ren as the king of Qi, which was Duke Jian.
In the spring of the fourth year of Duke Jian, at first, when Duke Jian of Qi and his father, Duke Du, were both in the state of Lu, they favored the officials and supervised them.
After Duke Jian ascended the throne, he was asked to preside over state affairs.
Tian Chengzi was very worried about this and went to court several times to inquire about the situation.
summary: Tian Chang eventually killed Duke Jian and established Duke Ping, becoming prime minister and dividing Qi's territory for the Tian family. The Tian family ultimately took full possession of Qi, and when Tian He became a prince, the state continued under the Tian clan until King Wei of Qi ruled as a hegemon.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家

translation:
After Ping Gong came to the throne, Tian Chang became the prime minister, specializing in the power of Qi State, and divided the vast land east of Anping of Qi State into the territory of the Tian family.
In the eighth year of Ping Gong's reign, the State of Yue destroyed the State of Wu.
In the twenty-fifth year of the reign of Emperor Pinggong, his son Xuan Gongji succeeded him.
In the fifty-first year of Xuangong's reign, Xuangong died and his son Kang Gongdai succeeded to the throne.
Tian Hui rebelled in Linqiu.
In the second year of Kanggong's reign, Han, Zhao and Wei began to become princes.
In the 19th year, Tian Chang's great-grandson Tian He began to become a prince and exiled Kang Gong to the seaside.
In the twenty-sixth year, Duke Kang passed away, and the Lu family stopped offering sacrifices.
The Tian family finally took possession of the Qi State, and when King Qi Wei was king, he became the lord of the world.
Tai Shigong said: When I arrived in Qi, I saw that the land of Qi starts from Mount Tai in the west, connects Langye in the east, and reaches the sea in the north. There are two thousand miles of fertile land in between. Its people are broad-minded and deep and wise. This is their nature.
Because of Taigong's sage, he established the foundation of the country, and because of Huangong's virtue, he implemented good governance, so he summoned the princes to form an alliance and became the overlord. Isn't it logical?
Guangsheng and Boda, indeed have the style of a great country!
summary: Sima Qian observed that Qi's fertile land and broad-minded people, combined with Taigong's foundation and Duke Huan's virtuous governance, naturally led to its position as overlord among the princes.
rel_path: 史记/三十世家/齐太公世家

translation:
Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi Dynasty, was the eldest son of Emperor Gaozu.
His mother was Gaozu's former mistress, whose surname was Cao.
Six years ago, Emperor Gaozu granted Liu Fei the title of King of Qi and granted him seventy cities. All people who spoke the Qi language belonged to the King of Qi.
King Qi is the elder brother of Emperor Xiaohui.
In the second year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, King Liu went to Beijing to see the emperor.
Emperor Hui and the King of Qi had a banquet, and the two treated each other with the same etiquette as family members and brothers.
Empress Dowager Lu was angry about this and wanted to kill King Qi.
The King of Qi was afraid that he would not be able to avoid disaster, so he adopted the strategy of his internal historian Xun and donated Chengyang County as Tang Muyi to Princess Lu Yuan.
Empress Dowager Lu was very happy, and King Qi was able to resign and return to Qi.
Thirteen years after King Hui ascended the throne, he died in the sixth year of Emperor Hui.
His son Liu Xiang came to the throne and became King Ai.
In the first year of King Ai, Emperor Xiaohui passed away, and Empress Dowager Lu began to take charge of the government. All affairs in the world were decided by Empress Lu.
In the second year, Empress Gao conferred the title of King Lu on her brother's son Lihou Lutai, and set up Jinan County in Qi State as the fiefdom of King Lu.
In the third year of King Ai's reign, his younger brother Liu Zhang entered the Han Palace for guard duty. Empress Dowager Lu named him Zhu Xuhou and married Lu Lu's daughter to him.
Four years later, Empress Dowager Lu granted Liu Zhang's younger brother Xingju the title of Marquis of Dongmou, and both of them served as guards in Chang'an Palace.
In the eighth year of King Ai's reign, Empress Gao divided Langxie County of Qi State and named Liu Ze, Marquis of Yingling, as King Langxie.
The next year, King Zhao Liuyou entered the court and was imprisoned in his mansion and died.
The three Zhao kings were deposed one after another.
After Gao, the descendants of the Lu family were granted the title of King of Yan, King of Zhao, and King of Liang, and they monopolized power and arbitrarily ruled the government.
When Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang was twenty years old, he was a man of great courage and bravery. He was angry because the Liu family could not get a position.
He once served the banquet of the Queen of Gao, who ordered Zhu Xuhou and Liu Zhang to serve as wine stewards.
Liu Zhang personally requested: "I am a descendant of a military general. Please allow me to supervise the behavior at the banquet in accordance with military law." Empress Gao said: Yes.
When the wine was in full swing, Liu Zhang performed songs and dances to add to the fun.
Then he said: Please let me sing a plowing song for the Queen Mother.
The queen treated him as a child and said with a smile: "I think your father knows about farming. You were born as a prince, how could you know about farming?" Liu Zhang said: I know.
The Queen Mother said: "Try to tell me about farming."
Liu Zhang said: If you plow deeply and plant densely, you will leave sparse seedlings. They are not the same kind, so you must shovel and hoe them resolutely.
Queen Lu was silent after hearing this.
After a while, one of the Lu clan members got drunk and ran away from the banquet. Liu Zhang chased him, drew his sword and beheaded him. Then he came back and reported: "There is a man who escaped from the banquet. I would like to kill him according to military law."
summary: Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi, was Emperor Gaozu's eldest son, granted the title of King of Qi with seventy cities. In the second year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, he visited the capital and dined with the emperor as equals, angering Empress Dowager Lu, who sought to kill him. Following his internal historian Xun's advice, he donated Chengyang County to Princess Lu Yuan, appeasing the empress dowager and allowing his safe return to Qi. He died thirteen years into his reign, succeeded by his son Liu Xiang, King Ai.

translation:
The Queen Mother and her officials were greatly surprised. Since he had been allowed to act in accordance with military law, he could not be punished.
The banquet also ended.
From then on, everyone in the Lu family was afraid of Zhu Xuhou, and even the ministers obeyed Zhu Xuhou. Liu's momentum gradually became stronger again.
The next year, Queen Gao died.
King Lu Lu of Zhao was appointed as the general, and King Lu Chan was appointed as the prime minister. Both of them lived in Chang'an City. They gathered troops to threaten the ministers and wanted to launch a rebellion.
Because his wife was Lu Lu's daughter, Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang knew about their plot, so he sent someone to sneak out of Chang'an to report to his brother King Qi, hoping that he would send troops to the west. Zhu Xuhou and Dongmuhou acted as internal correspondents in order to kill the Lu clan and take the opportunity to make King Qi the emperor.
After the King of Qi heard about this plan, he secretly planned to send troops with his uncle Si Jun, Lang Zhongling Zhu Wu, and Lieutenant Wei Bo.
Zhao Ping, the Prime Minister of Qi, heard about this and sent troops to guard the palace.
Wei Bo lied to Zhao Ping and said: The king wants to send troops, but there is no tiger talisman from the court to verify it.
Now the Prime Minister has surrounded the palace, which is a good thing.
I request you to lead the troops to protect King Qi.
Zhao Ping believed what he said and asked Wei Bo to lead troops to surround the palace.
After Wei Bo led the army, he sent troops to surround the Prime Minister's Mansion.
Zhao Ping said: Alas!
The words of Taoism should be discontinued, but they will be confused by it. This is exactly the case.  Finally committed suicide and died.
At that time, the King of Qi appointed Si Jun as the prime minister, Wei Bo as the general, Zhu Wu as the internal history officer, and sent out all the troops in the country.
He sent Zhu Wu to the east to deceive King Langxie, saying: The Lu clan rebelled, and the King of Qi sent troops to march west to kill them.
The King of Qi thought that he was a junior, young and not familiar with the war, and he was willing to entrust the entire army of the feudal country to the King.
The king has been a general since the time of Emperor Gao and is familiar with war.
The King of Qi did not dare to leave the army, so he sent his ministers to invite the King to Linzi to meet with the King of Qi to discuss important matters, and together they could lead the troops westward to quell the chaos in Guanzhong.
King Langye believed it and thought it was right, so he flew to see King Qi.
King Qi, Wei Bo and others took the opportunity to detain King Langxie. Zhu Wu was sent to send out all the troops of Langye Kingdom and command them.
After Langxie King Liu Ze was deceived, he could not return to his feudal kingdom, so he persuaded King Qi and said: King Qi Huihui is the eldest son of Emperor Gao. From the original source, the king is the eldest grandson of Emperor Gao and should inherit the throne.
Now the ministers are still undecided, and I am the eldest among the Liu family. The ministers are waiting for me to decide the big plan.
Now that the king has detained me here, I can't do anything. Why not let me enter the customs to discuss the important matter of establishing a new emperor.
King Qi thought it was right, so he prepared many cars to send King Langxie to the court.
After King Langxie left, King Qi raised troops to attack Jinan in the west of Lu State.
At this time, King Liu Ai sent a letter to the princes and kings, saying: After Emperor Gaozu pacified the world, he made his descendants kings, and King Hui Hui made them kings in Qi.
After the death of King Hui Hui, Emperor Hui sent Zhang Liang, the remaining marquis, to establish his minister as King of Qi.
After the death of Emperor Hui, Empress Gao took over the dictatorship. She was old and allowed Zhu Lu to depose the kings appointed by Emperor Gao without permission. She also killed three kings of Zhao, destroyed the three kingdoms of Liang, Yan and Zhao, let the Lu people become kings, and divided Qi into four kingdoms.
The loyal ministers came to remonstrate, but the Lord was confused and refused to listen.
Now that Empress Gao has passed away, the emperor is still young and cannot govern the world. Of course, he must rely on his ministers and princes.
Now Zhu Lu is proud of himself as a high official, gathers troops to show off his power, intimidates princes and loyal ministers, and falsely delivers imperial edicts to command the world. The Han court is therefore in great danger.
Now I am leading an army into the pass to kill those who should not be kings.
When the court heard that the King of Qi was sending troops to march westward, Prime Minister Lu Chan sent General Guan Ying to lead his troops eastward to intercept the Qi troops.
When Guan Ying arrived at Xingyang, he thought in his mind: Zhu Lu led his troops to gather in Guanzhong, intending to harm the Liu family and establish himself as emperor.
If I defeat Qi and return to the DPRK to report victory, it will be equivalent to increasing the capital of the Lu family.
So he ordered the army to stop and garrison in Xingyang, and sent envoys to inform the king of Qi and the princes that they were willing to unite with each other and wait for Lu's rebellion to be executed together.
After the King of Qi heard about this, he marched westward to recapture their hometown of Jinan County, and stationed troops on the western border of Qi State to wait for the fulfillment of the alliance.
Lu Lu and Lu Chan wanted to rebel in Guanzhong. Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, Taiwei Zhou Bo, and Prime Minister Chen Ping killed them.
Zhu Xuhou first beheaded Lu Chan, and then Taiwei Zhou Bo and others were able to kill all the Lu clan members.
King Langxie also happened to come to Chang'an from Qi.
The ministers discussed letting King Qi succeed the emperor, but King Langxie and some ministers said: King Qi's mother-uncle Sijun is ferocious and cruel, like a tiger wearing a hat.
We almost caused chaos in the world just now because of the Lu family, and now we want to establish the King of Qi because we want another Lu family to appear.
summary: During King Ai's reign, Empress Dowager Lu took control, appointing Lu family members as kings and dividing Qi's territories. Liu Zhang, Marquis of Zhuxu and King Ai's younger brother, boldly challenged the Lu clan's power. At a banquet, he used a farming song to criticize their rule and later executed a drunken Lu clan member under military law, instilling fear in the Lu family and reviving Liu clan influence. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, Lu Lu and Lu Chan plotted rebellion. Liu Zhang, aware of their plans, urged his brother King Qi to raise troops westward while he and Dongmou Hou served as internal allies. King Qi mobilized forces, detaining King Langxie to command his troops, and sent letters to princes condemning the Lu clan's usurpation. However, General Guan Ying, sent to intercept Qi, halted at Xingyang and allied with Qi instead. Liu Zhang, along with Taiwei Zhou Bo and Prime Minister Chen Ping, killed Lu Chan and Lu Lu in Guanzhong, ending the Lu clan's threat. The ministers debated succession; King Langxie and others opposed King Qi due to his cruel maternal uncle, Sijun, and instead chose Dai Wang, Emperor Gaozu's son with the virtuous Bo family, as Emperor Xiaowen. King Qi withdrew his troops. Wei Bo, who had instigated Qi's rebellion, was spared but dismissed after Guan Ying deemed him incompetent. Wei Bo's background included serving Cao Shen, who recommended him to King Huihui.

translation:
A year later, Emperor Xiaowen divided the land of Qi and made several sons of King Hui Hui originally named kings. General Lu of King Xiao of Qi was promoted to King of Qi as Yang Xuhou, the son of King Hui Hui.
It turned out that all other counties in the Qi State were entrusted to the sons of King Huihui as kings: Liu Zhi was the King of Jibei, Liu Biguang was the King of Jinan, Liu Xian was the King of Sichuan, Liu Xian was the King of Jiaoxi, Liu Xiongqu was the King of Jiaodong, and together with the King of Chengyang and the King of Qi, they were seven kings in total.
In the eleventh year of King Xiao of Qi, King Liu Bi of Wu and King Liu Wu of Chu rebelled. They raised their troops and marched westward, telling the princes: We are going to kill the traitor Chao Cuo of the Han Dynasty to stabilize the country.
The kings of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Sichuan, and Jinan all sent troops without authorization in response to the actions of the kings of Wu and Chu.
They also wanted to unite with Qi State, but King Xiao of Qi was hesitant and always defended the city and did not listen to them. The armies of the three countries jointly surrounded Qi.
The King of Qi sent Dr. Lu Zhong to report to the emperor, and the Emperor asked Dr. Lu Zhong to go back and tell the King of Qi: "Hold on, the troops I sent have now defeated Wu and Chu."
On the way, the doctor returned to Qi State. The armies of the Three Kingdoms surrounded Linzi heavily, and the doctors on the road were unable to enter the city.
The generals of the Three Kingdoms kidnapped the doctor in Luzhong and made an alliance with him, saying: You turn around and say that the Han court has been breached, and Qi should surrender to the Three Kingdoms as soon as possible, otherwise it will be massacred.
The doctor on the way had no choice but to agree to them, and when he came to the city, he saw the King of Qi from a distance and said: The imperial court has sent millions of troops, and sent Lieutenant Zhou Yafu to defeat the Wu Chu rebels. He is leading troops to rescue Qi State. Qi State must hold on and not surrender!
The generals of the Three Kingdoms killed the doctor on the road.
When the state of Qi was first besieged and reached a critical stage, it secretly contacted the three kingdoms. The alliance had not yet been concluded. Just when they heard that Dr. Lu Zhong had returned from the court, the king of Qi was very happy, and the ministers once again advised the king of Qi not to surrender to the three kingdoms.
Soon after, the troops led by Han generals Luan Shi and Pingyang Hou Caoqi came to Qi State, defeated the armies of the three countries, and lifted the siege of Qi State.
Soon, the emperor heard that Qi had conspired with the Three Kingdoms at first, and wanted to move troops to attack Qi.
King Xiao of Qi was afraid and committed suicide by taking poison.
After Emperor Jing heard about it, he thought that Qi was the best. It was not his fault that he conspired with the Three Kingdoms because he was threatened by persecution. So Liu Shou, the prince of King Xiao, was made King of Qi. This was King Yi, who continued the descendants of King Qi.
The King of Jiaoxi, King of Jiaodong, King of Jinan and King of Sichuan were all executed, and their territories were all assigned to the Han court.
Moved the King of Jibei to Suichuan and became the king.
In the twenty-second year of King Qi Yi's reign, his son Cijing came to the throne. This was King Li.
King Qi Li, his mother is Queen Mother Ji.
The Queen Mother married her brother Ji's daughter to King Li as his queen. King Li did not like Ji's daughter.
summary: In Emperor Xiaowen's first year, Qi regained Chengyang, Langye, and Jinan counties. Liu Zhang was made King of Chengyang, and Liu Xingju King of Jibei. King Ai of Qi died, succeeded by his son Liu Ze, King Wen. King Wen died without heirs, and his territory reverted to the court. Emperor Xiaowen then divided Qi among King Huihui's sons: Liu Zhi as King of Jibei, Liu Biguang as King of Jinan, Liu Xian as King of Sichuan, Liu Xian as King of Jiaoxi, Liu Xiongqu as King of Jiaodong, alongside the King of Chengyang and King of Qi, totaling seven kings. In King Xiao of Qi's eleventh year, the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms erupted, with Wu and Chu leading the revolt. Kings of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Sichuan, and Jinan joined, besieging Qi. King Xiao hesitated but defended the city. Dr. Lu Zhong, sent to the emperor, returned with orders to hold out, but was captured by the rebels. He falsely reported the Han court's defeat to the city but secretly urged resistance, leading to his execution. Qi held until Han forces under Luan Bu and Cao Qi defeated the rebels and lifted the siege. Suspected of collusion, King Xiao committed suicide, but Emperor Jing later cleared his name, making his son Liu Shou King Yi of Qi. The rebel kings were executed, and their territories annexed. King Hui of Qi's descendants also ruled Chengyang and Suichuan. Liu Zhang, King of Chengyang Jing, was rewarded for killing Lu Chan. His lineage continued through several generations. Liu Xingju, King of Jibei, rebelled after feeling slighted by Emperor Wen, who reduced his promised territory. He was defeated and committed suicide. Later, Liu Zhi, King of Jibei, remained loyal during the Seven Kingdoms Rebellion and was renamed King of Sichuan. Other sons of King Huihui—Liu Biguang, Liu Xian, Liu Xian, and Liu Xiongqu—were made kings but rebelled and were killed, their territories becoming counties.

translation:
The Queen Mother wanted the Ji family to be favored for generations to come, so she let her eldest daughter Ji Wengzhu enter the palace to straighten out the order in the harem and not allow the maids to approach King Qi. She wanted King Li to like Ji's daughter.
King Li took the opportunity to commit adultery with his sister Wengzhu.
There was a eunuch named Xu Jia from the State of Qi who entered the court to serve the Empress Dowager of Han Dynasty.
The Empress Dowager has a beloved daughter, whose title is Xiuchengjun. Xiuchengjun is not from the Liu family, but the Empress Dowager loves her.
Xiuchengjun had a daughter named E, and the Queen Mother wanted to marry her off to the princes. The eunuch Xu Jia asked to be sent to Qi as an envoy, saying that he would let the King of Qi write a letter asking for E to be his queen.
The Queen Mother was very happy and sent Xu Jia to Qi State.
At that time, the leader of the Qi State, Fu Yan, knew that Xu Jia was on a mission to the State of Qi to marry the queen. He also took the opportunity to say to Xu Jia: If the matter succeeds, I hope you can tell the boss that my daughter is willing to serve in the Queen of Qi's harem.
After Xu Jia arrived in Qi State, he first spread the matter secretly.
When the Queen Mother Ji heard this, she was furious and said, "The King of Qi already has a queen, and all the concubines in the harem are ready."
Moreover, Xu Jia was originally a poor man from Qi State. He became an eunuch after he was extremely poor. He entered the court to serve the Han Palace. He did not get any benefits. He also wanted to disturb our royal family of Qi State!
As for who the master father Yan is?
He actually wants his daughter to enter the harem!
Xu Jia was very embarrassed and returned to the court to report to the Empress Dowager: King Qi is willing to marry E as his queen, but there is a problem, maybe like King Yan.
The King of Yan had just been sentenced to death for committing adultery with his daughters and sisters, and the feudal country was destroyed, so Xu Jia deliberately used the story of King Yan to offend the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother said: "Don't talk about marrying your granddaughter to Qi anymore."
The matter gradually spread to the emperor's ears.
From then on, the master father Yan also had a gap with the King of Qi.
Zhufu Yanzheng was favored by the emperor, and he arbitrarily determined political affairs. He took the opportunity to say to the emperor: Linzi of Qi has one hundred thousand households, trade taxes amount to a thousand gold per day, and the population is large and wealthy, even more than Chang'an. If he is not the emperor's brother or beloved son, he should not be king here.
Nowadays, the relationship between King Qi and his royal relatives is becoming increasingly estranged.
Then he said calmly: Qi wanted to rebel when Empress Dowager Lu was there, and King Xiao almost participated in the rebellion during the Seven Kingdoms Rebellion between Wu and Chu.
Now I heard about Qi's affair with his sister.
So the emperor appointed his father Yan as the prime minister of Qi and wanted to investigate and deal with the matter.
After Master Yan came to Qi State, he stepped up the interrogation of the eunuchs in Queen Qi's harem who helped King Qi reach the residence of his sister Wengzhu, and ordered them to implicat King Qi in their confessions and circumstantial evidence.
When the King of Qi was young, he drank poison and committed suicide because he was afraid that he would be arrested and executed by the officials for serious crimes.
His heirs were cut off and he had no descendants.
summary: King Yi reigned for twenty-two years, succeeded by his son Liu Ci, King Li. King Li's mother, Queen Mother Ji, arranged his marriage to her niece, but he disliked her. She then had her daughter Wengzhu oversee the harem, leading to an incestuous relationship. Eunuch Xu Jia, sent by Empress Dowager to propose a marriage for her granddaughter E, was rebuffed by Queen Mother Ji. Xu Jia later slandered Qi, comparing it to the fallen King of Yan. Master Father Yan, favored by the emperor, accused Qi of rebellion and incest, becoming prime minister to investigate. Under pressure, King Li committed suicide, ending his line. Emperor Jing executed Master Father Yan after King Zhao's complaint.

translation:
He sent General Chai Puhou to defeat and capture the King of Jibei. The King of Jibei committed suicide, and the fiefdom was transferred to the imperial court and changed to a county.
Thirteen years later, in the sixteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, he granted the title of King of Jibei to Anduhou Liu Zhi, the son of King Hui Hui of Qi.
Eleven years later, when Wu and Chu rebelled, Liu Zhi always stood firm in the city and did not conspire with the princes of the seven countries to cause rebellion.
After the Wu and Chu rebellions were put down, the emperor changed the title of Liu Zhi to King Sichuan.
Jinan King Liu Biguang, the son of King Qi Hui, was named King of Jinan in the 16th year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign as a Lehou.

The Han army defeated the rebels, killed Liu Piguang, made Jinan a county, and transferred the fiefdom to the Han court.

The emperor therefore moved and granted the title of King of Jibei, Liu Zhi, as King of Sichuan.
Liu Zhi was also the son of King Qi Hui, and the emperor named him King of Jibei from the Marquis of Andu.
Liu Xian, the king of Sichuan, rebelled and had no descendants, so he changed the title of King Jibei to King Sichuan.
King Sichuan died after reigning for thirty-five years, and his posthumous title was King Yi.
His son Liu Jian succeeded to the throne and became King Jing.
King Jing died after reigning for twenty years, and his son Liu Yi succeeded to the throne. He was King Qing.
King Qing died in his thirty-sixth year, and his son Liu Zhonggu came to the throne. This was King Si.
King Si died in the twenty-eighth year of his reign, and his son Liu Shang came to the throne. This was King Xiao.
King Xiao died in the fifth year of his reign, and his son Liu Heng ascended the throne. He died in the eleventh year of his reign in the third year of Jianshi.
King Liu Xing of Jiaoxi was the son of King Hui of Qi. In the 16th year of Emperor Wen's reign, he was granted the title of King of Jiaoxi by the Marquis of Changping.

The Han army defeated the rebels and killed Liu Xian. The fiefdom was transferred to the Han court and renamed Jiaoxi County.
Liu Xiongqu, King of Jiaodong, was the son of King Qi Mouhui. In the 16th year of Emperor Wen's reign, he was granted the title of King of Jiaodong by the Marquis of Baishi.
Eleven years later, he rebelled with the kings of Wu and Chu. The Han army defeated the rebels and killed Xiongqu. The fiefdom was transferred to the Han court and changed to Jiaodong County.
Tai Shigong said: Among the princes, no one in the great country surpasses King Qi Yuhui.
Since the world had just been pacified and the Liu family had fewer children, the emperor of the Han Dynasty felt that the Qin Dynasty did not grant large-scale land to clan members, so he enfeoffed people with the same surname in large numbers to calm the hearts of the people.
It was only natural that it was later split into several countries.
summary: Sima Qian noted that King Hui of Qi's domain was the largest among princes, initially granted to stabilize the realm after the Qin dynasty's failure to support clan members, though it was later divided.

translation:
Huangdi is a descendant of the Shaodian tribe, and his surname is Gongsun and Xuanyuan.
He was born with great spirituality. He was good at speaking at a very young age. He was clever and alert as a child. He was honest and agile when he grew up. He was wise and judicious as an adult.
When Xuanyuan was in power, the descendants of the Shennong clan had declined. The princes fought against each other and abused the people with violence, but the Shennong clan had no power to conquer them.
So Xuanyuan practiced military training and went to conquer those princes who did not come to pay tribute. Only then did all the princes come to submit.
Chiyou was the most violent among the princes, and no one could conquer him.
Emperor Yan wanted to attack and oppress the princes, and all the princes came to Xuanyuan.
So Xuanyuan practiced virtue, rectified his army, studied the changes in the four seasons, planted grains, appeased the people, measured the land in all directions, trained bears, 罴, 貔, 貅, 貲, tigers and other beasts, and fought with Emperor Yan in the countryside of Banquan. After several battles, he conquered Emperor Yan and won as he wished.
Chiyou launched a rebellion and refused to obey Huangdi's orders.
So Huang Di mobilized the troops of the princes and fought with Chi You in the suburbs of Zhuolu, and finally captured and killed him.
In this way, the princes all respected Xuanyuan as the emperor, replacing Shennong. This was the Yellow Emperor.
When there were disobedient people in the world, the Yellow Emperor went to conquer them. After pacifying a place, he left, splitting mountains and clearing roads along the way, and never lived in peace anywhere.
Huang Di went east to the East China Sea and climbed Mount Maru and Mount Tai.
Went west to Kongtong and climbed to Jitou Mountain.
Went south to the Yangtze River and climbed Xiong Mountain and Xiang Mountain.
He expelled the Hunzhou tribe to the north, came to Busan, signed the talisman contract with the princes, and built a city at the foot of Zhulu Mountain.
The Yellow Emperor moved around and had no fixed residence. Wherever he led his troops, he set up military camps for self-defense.
All the official positions granted by the Yellow Emperor were named after Yun, and the army was called Yunshi.
He set up left and right supervisors to supervise the various vassal states.
At this time, all countries were in peace, so since ancient times, the number of people offering sacrifices to ghosts and gods in mountains and rivers was the highest during the Yellow Emperor's time.
The Yellow Emperor received the tripod given by God, so he observed the movement of the sun, used yarrow for divination to calculate the calendar, and predicted the solar terms and dates. He appointed Fenghou, Limu, Changxian, Dahong and others to govern the people.
The Yellow Emperor complied with the laws of the four seasons of heaven and earth, speculated on the changes of yin and yang, explained the principles of life and death, and discussed the causes of existence and death. He sown grains and grasses according to the seasons, domesticated birds, beasts, and silkworms, measured the sun, moon and stars to determine the calendar, collected earth, stone, gold, and jade for civilian use.
When he was the emperor, he had the auspicious sign of the attribute of earth. The earth was yellow in color, so he was called the Yellow Emperor.
Huangdi had twenty-five sons, fourteen of whom established their own surnames.
The Yellow Emperor lived in Xuanyuan Mountain and married a daughter of the Xiling Kingdom, who was Leizu.
Leizu was the Yellow Emperor's concubine and had two sons. Their descendants all ruled the world: one was named Xuanxiao, also known as Qingyang. Qingyang was named a prince and settled in Jiangshui; the other was named Changyi, who was also named a prince and settled in Ruoshui.
Changyi married a daughter of the Shushan clan, named Changpu, and gave birth to Gao Yang, who had the character of a saint.
After the death of Huangdi, he was buried in Qiaoshan. His grandson, Changyi's son Gaoyang, ascended the throne and became Emperor Zhuanxu.
Emperor Zhuanxu Gaoyang was the grandson of Huangdi and the son of Changyi.
summary: Huangdi (Yellow Emperor), a descendant of the Shaodian tribe with the surname Gongsun and name Xuanyuan, displayed remarkable intelligence from birth. During his rise to power, the Shennong clan had declined, and princes were fighting violently. Xuanyuan trained his army, conquered rebellious princes, and eventually all submitted except the violent Chiyou. After Emperor Yan attacked the princes, they turned to Xuanyuan, who cultivated virtue, organized his forces, and defeated Emperor Yan at Banquan. He later captured and killed Chiyou at Zhuolu, after which the princes recognized him as emperor, replacing Shennong. The Yellow Emperor traveled extensively—east to Mount Tai, west to Kongtong, south to the Yangtze River, and north驱逐 the Hunzhou tribe. He had no fixed residence, establishing military camps wherever he went. He appointed officials named after clouds, created supervisory positions, and received a divine tripod for calendar-making. He observed celestial movements, calculated seasons, and appointed ministers to govern. Following the laws of heaven and earth, he studied yin and yang, explained life and death, cultivated grains, domesticated animals, and collected resources for public use. Because of the earth attribute's auspicious sign, he was called the Yellow Emperor. He had twenty-five sons, fourteen of whom established surnames. After his death, his grandson Gaoyang ascended as Emperor Zhuanxu.

He is as kind as heaven and as wise as God.
Being close to him warms the heart like the sun; looking up to him is like clouds covering the earth.
He is rich but not proud, noble but not indulgent.
He wears a yellow hat, black clothes, a scarlet chariot and a white horse.
He can respect virtuous people and make nine generations of the same clan love each other.
Since the people of the same clan were at peace, they went to inspect the officials.
All officials have outstanding achievements, and all princes and states can live in harmony.
Emperor Yao ordered the Xi family and the He family to follow the will of God, draw up a calendar based on the appearance and appearance of the sun and the moon, and the position of the stars, and carefully teach the people the production seasons.
In addition, he ordered Xizhong, who lived in Yuyi, a place called Yanggu, to greet the sunrise respectfully and arrange the spring farming in different steps.
summary: Emperor Zhuanxu Gaoyang was calm, resourceful, and knowledgeable. He cultivated crops, calculated seasons, followed ghosts and gods to establish rituals, and educated the people. His domain extended north to Youling, south to Jiaozhi, west to Liusha, and east to Panmu, pacifying all creatures. After his death, his nephew Gao Xin became Emperor Ku. Gao Xin was born with great aura, benevolent and dignified, understanding both divine will and people's concerns. He governed impartially, and all under heaven submitted. After his death, his son Zhi ruled without achievement, so his brother Fangxun became Emperor Yao.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪

translation:
On the vernal equinox, the day is as long as the night. The stars in Suzaku's seven constellations appear in the south at dusk. This is used to determine the time of mid-spring.
At this time, people dispersed to work, and birds and animals gave birth and mated.
He also ordered Uncle Xi, who lived in Nanjiao, to arrange the summer farm work step by step and do it carefully.
On the summer solstice, the day is the longest, and the heart constellation among the seven constellations of Canglong appears in the south when it is first twilight. Accordingly, the time of midsummer is determined.
At this time, the people are in high places, and the feathers of birds and animals are sparse.
He also ordered He Zhong, who lived in the Western Land, that place was called Shibuya, to respectfully send the sun down and arrange the autumn harvest in a step-by-step manner.
On the autumnal equinox, the night is as long as the day. The virtual constellation among the seven constellations of Xuanwu appears in the due south at the beginning of dusk. Based on this, the time of mid-autumn is determined.
At this time, people moved to the plains, and birds and animals regenerated new hair.
He also ordered Uncle He, who lives in the north, that place is called Youdu, to carefully arrange the winter collection.
On the winter solstice, the day is the shortest, and Pleiades, one of the seven constellations of the White Tiger, appears in the due south when it is first twilight, and the time of midwinter is determined based on this.
At this time, people go into their houses to keep warm, and birds and animals are covered with fine hair.
There are 366 days in a year, and leap moons are used to correct the four seasons of spring, summer, autumn and winter.
Emperor Yao sincerely warned all officials to keep their duties, and all kinds of things were done.
Yao said: Who can inherit my career?
Fang Qi said: Your son Danzhu is a master of affairs.
Yao said: Hum!
Danzhu, he is stupid, vicious and cannot be used.
Yao asked again: Then who else can?
Huandou said: Gonggong has gathered people extensively and made achievements, which can be used.
Yao said: Gonggong likes to talk nice words, but his intentions are not right. When he speaks, he seems to be very respectful, but his heart is absent and cannot be used.
Yao asked again: Alas, the Four Mountains, now the floods are surging and mighty, surrounding the mountains and covering the hills. The people are extremely miserable. Who can be sent to control them?
Everyone said Gun could do it.
Yao said: Gun violated the destiny of heaven and destroyed his own people, so he cannot be used.
The four mountains all said: Just use him. If it doesn't work, then remove him.
Yao therefore followed Siyue's advice and appointed Gun.
Gun controlled the flood for nine years without achieving any results. Yao said: Alas!
Dear leaders, I have been on the throne for seventy years. Which of you can follow the destiny and succeed me as emperor?
Siyue replied: Our virtues are very despicable and we are not worthy of being on the throne of God.
Yao said: "Then let's recommend him from among all the ministers near and far with the same surname and different surnames, as well as those who live in seclusion.
Everyone said to Yao: There was a single man living among the people, named Yu Shun.
Yao said: Yes, I have heard of him. What is he like?
Siyue replied; He is the son of a blind man.
summary: Emperor Yao was kind as heaven and wise as God, rich but not proud. He united his clan, inspected officials, and ordered the Xi and He families to create a calendar based on celestial observations. He appointed officials to oversee spring, summer, autumn, and winter farming, establishing a 366-day year with leap months. When Yao sought a successor, his son Danzhu was deemed unworthy, and Gonggong was rejected for insincerity. Despite warnings, Gun was appointed to control floods but failed after nine years. The Four Mountains recommended Yu Shun, a filial man living among commoners. Yao tested Shun by marrying his daughters to him, observing his virtue, and assigning him various duties, which Shun performed excellently.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪

translation:
His father was fierce and stubborn, his mother was stupid and stubborn, and his brother was arrogant, but Shun was able to live in harmony with them, practice filial piety, and manage the family business with virtue to prevent them from going evil.
Yao said: Then I will give him a try.
So Yao married his two daughters to him and observed his virtues from his two daughters.
Shun asked them to lower their noble hearts and live in their homes by the Gui River, observing the ways of being wives.
Yao thought this was a good thing, so he asked Shun to take the post of Situ. He carefully followed the five ethics and morals: fatherly righteousness, motherly kindness, brother-friendship, brotherly respect, and son's filial piety. The people followed them and never violated them.
Yao also asked him to participate in the affairs of the officials, and the affairs of the officials became orderly.
Let him receive guests at the four gates of the Mingtang. The four gates are in harmony, and the guests from the princes and guests from far away are respectful.
Yao then sent Shun into the mountains, jungles, rivers and swamps, and encountered a storm and thunderstorm, but Shun did not get lost or make any mistakes.
Yao even thought that he was very smart and virtuous, so he called him over and said: "In the past three years, you have done things carefully and can do what you say."
Now you can ascend to the throne of emperor.
Shun Tui said that his virtue was not enough and he was unwilling to accept the throne.
On the first day of the first lunar month, Shun accepted Yao's abdication in Wenzu Temple.
Wenzu was also the Taizu of Yao.
At this time, Yao was already old and asked Shun to act as the emperor's political agent, so as to observe whether Shun was in line with God's will as emperor.
Shun then used instruments for observing astronomical phenomena to locate the sun, the moon, and the five stars of metal, wood, water, fire, and earth. He then held temporary ceremonies to offer sacrifices to heaven. He used the ritual of burning sacrifices on fire to worship the four seasons of heaven and earth.
He collected five types of jade talisman letters from Huan Gui, Xin Gui, Gong Gui, Gu Bi, and Pu Bi held by the fifth-ranking marquis, Bozi, the Duke and the Prince. He chose a good month and an auspicious day, summoned the four mountains and the prefects of each state, and issued them to them.
In February, Shun went to the East for inspection. When he arrived at Mount Tai, he used the ceremony of burning firewood to worship Dongyue, and used the ceremony of distant sacrifice to worship the famous mountains and rivers in various places.
Then, he summoned the princes from the East to coordinate and correct the four seasons, the size of the moon, and the sun. He unified the rhythm and the standards of length, capacity, and weight. He revised the five etiquettes of good luck, bad luck, guest, military, and honor. He stipulated that the princes should use five kinds of Guibi and three kinds of colored silk.
In May, he went on a tour to the south; in August, he went to the west; in November, he went to the north: all the same as when he first went to the east.
After returning, he went to the ancestral temple and father's temple and used a cow as a sacrifice.
From now on, inspections will be held every five years. During the four years, all princes and kings will come to the capital on time to pay homage.
Shun generally explained the principles of governing the country to the princes, clearly inspected them according to their achievements, and gave chariots and horses clothes according to their merits.
Shun began to divide the world into twelve states and dredge the rivers.
summary: Shun accepted Yao's abdication and began governing. He established rituals, standardized measurements, and conducted inspections every five years. He divided the world into twelve states, dredged rivers, and implemented a penal system with reduced punishments. He exiled the four evil ministers—Gonggong, Huandou, Sanmiao, and Gun—satisfying the world. After Yao's death, Shun initially yielded to Danzhu, but the people universally supported Shun, who then ascended the throne.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/五帝本纪

translation:
So Yu composed the music "Nine Moves" to praise Shun's merits, which attracted auspicious things, and the phoenix also flew in, circling and dancing with the music.
The Qingming Dynasty and its virtues all started from the time of Yu and Shun.
Shun was famous for his filial piety when he was twenty years old. He was appointed by Yao when he was thirty years old.
Thirty-nine years after he ascended the throne, he toured the south and died in the Cangwu countryside in the south.
Buried in Jiuyi Mountain on the south bank of the Yangtze River, this is Lingling.
After Shun ascended the throne, he rode in a car with the emperor's flag to pay homage to his father Gusou. He behaved humbly and cautiously and followed the principles of being a son.
He also made his younger brother Xiang a prince.
Shun's son Shangjun was also unqualified, so Shun recommended Yu to heaven in advance.
Shun died seventeen years later.
After three years of mourning, Yu also abdicated the throne to Shun's son, just as Shun abdicated to Yao's son.
The princes surrendered to Yu, and Yu ascended to the throne of emperor.
Yao's son Danzhu and Shun's son Shangjun were granted fiefs in Tang and Yu respectively to worship their ancestors.
Yu also asked them to wear their own family's clothes and use their own family's rituals and music.
They met the emperor with the courtesy of guests, and the emperor did not treat them as his ministers to show that he did not dare to monopolize the world.
From the Yellow Emperor to Shun and Yu, they all had the same surname, but they had different national titles in order to highlight their respective bright virtues.
Therefore, Huangdi was named Youxiong, Emperor Zhuanxu was named Gaoyang, Emperor Ku was named Gaoxin, Emperor Yao was named Taotang, and Emperor Shun was named Youyu.
Emperor Yu's title was Queen of Xia, and he was given another surname, Si.
The descendants of Qi founded Shang, with the surname Zi.
The descendants of Qi founded the Zhou Dynasty, and their surname was Ji.
Tai Shigong said: Many scholars refer to the Five Emperors, and the Five Emperors have been around for a long time.
"Shangshu" only records historical facts since Yao; while each school's description of the Yellow Emperor is rough and not typical, and it is difficult for the scholar-officials to explain clearly.
Some scholars do not pass on the "Zaiyu Asks the Virtues of the Five Emperors" and "Emperor Lineage Surnames" handed down by Confucius.
I once went to Kongtong in the west, Zhuolu in the north, the sea in the east, and crossed the Yangtze River and Huai River in the south. Wherever I went, I went to places where old people praised the deeds of the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun. Although the customs and teachings were different, the statements that were consistent with ancient records were relatively credible.
I have studied "Spring and Autumn" and "Guoyu", and their explanations of "Five Emperors' Virtues" and "Emperor's Lineage" are very clear, but people have not studied them in depth. In fact, their descriptions are not false theories.
"Shangshu" is incomplete and intermittent, but scattered anecdotal records can often be found in other books.
If you are not eager to learn and think deeply, and truly understand their meaning in your heart, it will definitely be difficult to explain it to those who have shallow knowledge and limited knowledge.
I reviewed and sorted these materials, selected those with particularly elegant and correct writing, and wrote this chapter as the first chapter of the book.
summary: Shun's lineage traced back to Emperor Zhuanxu, though his immediate ancestors were commoners. Despite his father Gusou, stepmother, and brother Xiang repeatedly attempting to kill him, Shun remained filial and respectful. His virtue attracted people, and wherever he lived, communities grew. Yao tested him thoroughly before entrusting him with governance. Shun appointed worthy descendants of ancient families—the Eight Kai and Eight Yuan—to manage agriculture and education, while exiling four evil families. He appointed Yu to control floods, Gaotao as judge, and other capable ministers. Yu's contributions were greatest: opening mountains, dredging rivers, and delineating nine provinces. The territory expanded five thousand miles, and all regions submitted. Shun died while touring south and was buried at Jiuyi Mountain. His son Shangjun being unworthy, Shun recommended Yu to heaven. After Shun's death, Yu ascended the throne, continuing the pattern of abdication. The historian notes that while records of the Five Emperors are ancient and sometimes unclear, careful study of various texts and oral traditions confirms their authenticity. This account selects the most elegant and correct materials as the first chapter of the historical record.
