translation:
Empress Dowager Lu was Gaozu's humble wife and gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and his daughter, Empress Dowager Lu Yuan.
When Emperor Gaozu became the king of Han, he found Qi Ji in Dingtao. He loved her very much and gave birth to King Ruyi of Zhao Yin.
Emperor Xiaohui was kind and weak, but Gaozu thought he was not like him, so he often wanted to depose the prince and make Qi Ji's son Ruyi, thinking that Ruyi was similar to himself.
Qi Ji was favored and often followed Emperor Gaozu to Guandong. She cried day and night and wanted to make her son the crown prince to replace the original crown prince.
Empress Lu was getting older and often stayed behind. She rarely saw Gaozu, and their relationship became increasingly estranged.
Ruyi was granted the title of Queen Zhao, and almost replaced the prince many times. Fortunately, the ministers' remonstrances and Liu Hou's strategy prevented the prince from being abolished.
Empress Lu was a strong and resolute person. She assisted Emperor Gaozu in pacifying the world and killing ministers, mostly thanks to Empress Lu.
Empress Lu had two older brothers, both of whom were generals.
The eldest brother Zhou Luhou died in the line of duty, and his sons Lu Tai were granted the title of Lihou, Lu Chan was granted the title of Jiaohou; the second brother Lu Shizhi was granted the title of Jiancheng Marquis.
On April 25, the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he died in Changle Palace. The prince inherited the title of Emperor Gaozu and succeeded him as emperor.
At this time, Emperor Gaozu had eight sons: the eldest son Liu Fei, who was the brother of Emperor Xiaohui and had a different mother than Emperor Xiaohui, was named King of Qi; the rest were younger brothers of Emperor Xiaohui. Liu Ruyi, the son of Qi Ji, was named King of Zhao, Mrs. Bo's son Liu Heng was named King of Dai, the other sons of Ji's concubines were Liu Huifeng, King of Liang, Liu Youfeng, King of Huaiyang, Liu Changfeng, King of Huainan, and Liu Jianfeng, King of Yan.
Gaozu's younger brother Liu Jiao was granted the title of King of Chu, and his elder brother's son Liu Bi was granted the title of King of Wu.
Wu Chen, the son of Fan Jun Wu Rui, a hero who was not a descendant of the Liu family, was granted the title of King of Changsha.
Empress Lu resented Madam Qi and her son King Zhao the most, so she ordered Madam Qi to be imprisoned in Yongxiang, and summoned King Zhao to the capital.
The envoy went back and forth several times. Zhao Xiang Jianpinghou Zhou Chang said to the envoy: Emperor Gao entrusted King Zhao to me. King Zhao is still young.
I heard that the Queen Mother resented Mrs. Qi and wanted to summon King Zhao to kill him together. I dare not send King Zhao away.
Moreover, King Zhao was also ill and could not go there according to the imperial edict.
Empress Lu was furious and sent someone to summon Prime Minister Zhao to the capital.
When Prime Minister Zhao was summoned to Chang'an, he sent someone to summon King Zhao again.
King Zhao came and had not yet reached the capital.
Emperor Xiaohui was kind and knew that the Queen Mother was angry, so he went to Ba Shang to greet King Zhao in person, and returned to the palace with King Zhao, where he ate and lived with King Zhao.
The Queen Mother wanted to kill King Zhao, but could not find a chance.
In December of the first year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, Emperor Xiaohui went out to hunt in the morning.
King Zhao is young and cannot get up early.
The queen mother heard that King Zhao was alone at home, so she sent someone to give him poisoned wine to drink.
When Emperor Xiaohui returned at dawn, King Zhao was already dead.
So Liu You, the king of Huaiyang, was moved to the throne of Zhao.
In the summer, an edict was issued to pursue Yi Lihou's father as Lingwuhou.
summary: Empress Dowager Lu was the humble wife of Emperor Gaozu and mother of Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan. Gaozu favored Concubine Qi, who bore King Ruyi of Zhao, and often considered deposing the kind and weak Crown Prince Xiaohui in favor of Ruyi. Empress Lu, growing estranged from Gaozu, was resolute and assisted in pacifying the realm and killing ministers. After Gaozu's death in 195 BCE, Xiaohui succeeded him. Empress Lu resented Concubine Qi and King Ruyi. She imprisoned Concubine Qi and summoned Ruyi to the capital. Emperor Xiaohui protected Ruyi, but during a hunt, the Queen Mother poisoned Ruyi. She then mutilated Concubine Qi, calling her a "human pig." Xiaohui, horrified, fell ill and abandoned court affairs, dying in 188 BCE. During his funeral, the Queen Mother cried without tears until ministers, following advice, appointed Lu family members as generals, securing her power. The ministers, fearing the young emperor was not truly Xiaohui's son, chose Liu Heng, King of Dai, as emperor due to his maturity and virtue. He became Emperor Xiaowen, reigning for 23 years. The historian notes that during Empress Lu's rule, the people recovered from war, punishments were rare, and agriculture flourished, despite her cruelty and nepotism.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪

translation:
In the first year, all orders from the imperial court came from the Queen Mother.
The mother-in-law is exercising the authority of the emperor and intends to make the Lu family's children kings. She first inquires about the royal mausoleum of the right prime minister.
Wang Ling said: Emperor Gao killed the white horse and swore an oath with the ministers: If he is not a descendant of the Liu family and becomes king, everyone in the world will destroy him.
It is against the oath to make a descendant of the Lu family king now.
The Queen Mother was very unhappy.
Ask Zuo Prime Minister Chen Ping and Jianghou Zhou Bo.
Zhou Bo and others replied: Emperor Gao brought peace to the world and made his children kings. Now that the Queen Mother is in charge of the court, she can make her brothers and the children of the Lu family kings. There is nothing wrong with that.
The Queen Mother became happy and returned to the palace.
Wang Ling scolded Chen Ping and Jianghou, saying: Were you not present when we made a blood oath with Emperor Gao?
Now that Emperor Gao is dead, the Queen Mother comes to court as a heroine and intends to make the children of the Lu family kings. Even if you want to flatter and break your oath, how can you have the face to go to Jiuquan to see Emperor Gao after your death?
Chen Ping and Jianghou said: "Today we openly oppose in front of the Queen Mother and fight hard in the court, we are not as good as you; when it comes to protecting the country and stabilizing the kingship of Liu's descendants, you are not as good as us."
Wang Ling was speechless.
In November, the Queen Mother wanted to depose Wang Ling, so she made him the emperor's tutor and deprived him of his powers as prime minister.
Therefore, Wang Ling claimed that he was ill and was dismissed from office and returned home.
Then Chen Ping, the prime minister of the left, was made the prime minister of the right, and Marquis Piyang Shenshi was made the prime minister of the left.
Prime Minister Zuo did not manage government affairs and asked him to supervise the affairs of the palace, just like a doctor.
Therefore, Shen Shiqi was favored by the Queen Mother and often made decisions on government affairs. The ministers relied on him to decide important matters.
Then he pursued Li Hou's father as the King of Wuwu, intending to use this as the beginning of making the Lu family's children kings.
In April, the Queen Mother planned to make the children of the Lu family a marquis, so she first made Feng Wuze, a great minister of the Great Ancestor, the Marquis of Bocheng.
Princess Lu Yuan died and was given the posthumous title of Queen Mother Lu Yuan.
Her son was named King of Lu.
The father of King Lu was Zhang Ao, Marquis of Xuanping.
Liu Zhang, the son of King Hui of Qi, was granted the title of Zhu Xuhou, and Lu Lu's daughter was married to him.
Prime Minister Qi Shou was granted the title of Marquis of Pingding.
Yang Chengyan of Shaofu was granted the title of Wuhou.
Then they named Lu Zhong as Peihou, Lu Ping as Fuliuhou, and Zhang Mai as Nangonghou.
The Queen Mother wanted to make Lu's children kings, so she first made Liu Qiang, the son of Emperor Xiaohui's harem, the King of Huaiyang, Liu Buyi the King of Changshan, Liu Shan the Marquis of Xiangcheng, Liu Chao the Marquis of Zhi, and Liu Wu the Marquis of Huguan.
The Empress Dowager signaled to the ministers in a low voice, and the ministers requested that Li Hou Lutai be granted the title of King Lu, and the Empress Dowager agreed.
After the death of Lu Shizhi, Marquis of Kang in Jiancheng, his son who had inherited the title was found guilty and was deposed. His younger brother Lu Lu was granted the title of Marquis of Huling and succeeded Kang Marquis.
summary: The Queen Mother then ruled as regent, intending to make Lu family members kings. She consulted ministers; Wang Ling opposed, citing Gaozu's oath, while Chen Ping and Zhou Bo supported her. She deposed Wang Ling and promoted Chen Ping. She made Lu Tai King of Lu, and after his death, Lu Jia succeeded. She also made several of Xiaohui's sons kings, though they were not his biological children. The Queen Mother deposed and killed a young emperor who threatened rebellion, replacing him with Liu Yi, renamed Hong.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪

translation:
King Zhao came to the capital and placed him in his official residence. He did not receive him and ordered his guards to surround him and deny him anything to eat.
Some of his subordinates secretly brought him food, and they were arrested and tried for crimes. King Zhao was hungry, so he sang: "Zhu Lu has the power, the Liu family is in danger; you are coercing the princes, forcing me to marry the Lu family's daughter as my concubine."
My concubine is jealous and slanders me for committing a crime; she slanders my daughter and brings chaos to the country, but the emperor doesn't understand.
I have no loyal ministers, otherwise why would I lose my feudal kingdom?
In the wilderness of suicide, Heaven must uphold justice in its affairs!
Alas, I have no regrets. I would rather kill myself as soon as possible.
I starve to death for the sake of the king, who has mercy on me?
Lu is unreasonable and has no choice but to ask God to avenge me.
On the 18th, King Zhao was imprisoned and died, and he was buried next to the graves of the people of Chang'an using the etiquette of ordinary people.
On the 30th, there was a solar eclipse and the day was dark.
The Queen Mother was disgusted and unhappy, so she said to the attendants: "It must be because of me."
In February, Liu Hui, the king of Liang, became the king of Zhao.
King Lu Lu Chan moved to the throne and became King Liang. King Liang did not go to the feudal state to take office, but stayed in the capital as the emperor's tutor.
The emperor's son Liu Tai, Marquis of Changping, was made King Lu.
Liang was renamed Lu, and Lu was renamed Jichuan.
The Queen Mother's sister Lu Yu had a daughter who was the wife of Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, who was a general.
The Empress Dowager conferred the title of king on a descendant of the Lu family. She was afraid that General Liu would cause chaos after her death, so she named Liu Ze King Langxie to comfort him.
Liu Hui, the king of Liang, was moved to the state of Zhao and became king. He was very unhappy.
The Queen Mother took Lu Chan's daughter as King Zhao's queen.
The queen's attendant officials are all members of the Lu family. They use their power exclusively to spy on King Zhao, but King Zhao cannot do whatever he wants.
King Zhao had a beloved concubine, and the queen sent someone to kill her with poisoned wine.
So King Zhao composed four chapters of poetry and asked the musicians to sing.
King Zhao was deeply saddened and committed suicide in June.
When the Queen Mother heard about this, she thought that King Zhao had abandoned the ancestral ethics for women and would no longer allow his descendants to inherit the throne.
Zhang Ao, Marquis of Xuanping, died. Because his son Zhang Yan was the King of Lu, Zhang Ao was given the posthumous title of King Lu Yuan.
In autumn, the Queen Mother sent an envoy to tell King Dai that she wanted to move him to Zhao to become king.
King Dai declined, hoping to guard the borders of Dai's country.
Grand Tutor Lu Chan and Prime Minister Chen Ping all said that Marquis Lu Lu of Wu Xin was in the highest position and ranked first in the order. Please make him the King of Zhao.
The Queen Mother agreed and honored Lu Lu's father, Kanghou, as King Zhao Zhao.
In September, King Liu Jian of Yan Ling died. He had a son born from beauty. The Queen Mother sent people to kill the son. King Yan Ling had no heirs and the kingdom was abolished.
summary: The Queen Mother continued to consolidate Lu power, killing or deposing several Zhao kings, including Liu You, who starved to death after opposing the Lu family. She made Lu Lu King of Zhao and Lu Chan King of Liang. In 180 BCE, she fell ill and warned Lu Chan and Lu Lu to control the army, fearing rebellion. She died, leaving edicts for rewards and amnesty.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪

translation:
When King Hui Hui passed away, Emperor Xiaohui sent Zhang Liang, the Marquis of Liu, to make me the King of Qi.
Emperor Xiaohui passed away and Empress Gao came to power. She was old and listened to the opinions of Lu's group and deposed the emperor without authorization. She also killed three Zhao kings one after another, abolished Liang, Zhao and Yan, and used the title of Lu's children as kings. Qi was also divided into four parts.
The loyal ministers gave advice, but the empress was confused and refused to accept it.
Now that Empress Gao has passed away, the emperor is still young and cannot govern the world, so he can only rely on ministers and princes. However, the Lu family prides itself on its position, gathers troops, uses its majesty to intimidate the loyal ministers of the princes, and orders the world under the pretext of imperial edicts. Therefore, the Liu family's ancestral temple is in danger.
I led the army to the court to eliminate those who should not be king.
When the Han court heard the news, Prime Minister Lu Chan and others sent Yingyin Marquis Guanying to lead an army to attack the King of Qi.
When Guan Ying arrived in Xingyang, he discussed with others that the Lu family had taken control of the army in Guanzhong and wanted to eliminate the Liu family and establish themselves as emperor.
If I defeat Qi's army now and go back to resume my life, this will further strengthen the Lu family's power.
So Guan Ying stationed troops in Xingyang and sent envoys to inform the king of Qi and the princes of other countries. We must unite with them, wait for Lu's rebellion, and get rid of Lu together.
After the King of Qi heard the news, he withdrew his army to the western border of Qi State, waited for the news, and acted as agreed.
Lu Lu and Lu Chan wanted to launch a rebellion in Guanzhong, but they were afraid of Suihou, Zhu Xuhou and others internally, and externally they were afraid of the armies of Qi and Chu. They were also worried about Guan Ying's rebellion, so they planned to wait until Guan Ying's army fought with Qi's army before launching a rebellion.
At this time, King Liu Tai of Jichuan, King Liu Wu of Huaiyang, King Liu Chao of Changshan, and King Lu Yuan, grandson of Empress Lu, who were nominally younger brothers of the Young Emperor, all did not return to the country due to their young age and lived in Chang'an.
Zhao Wang Changlu and Liang Wang Lu Chan each commanded troops and lived in the Northern and Southern Army. They were both from the Lu family.
No one among the princes and ministers felt that they would be able to save their lives.
Taiwei Jianghou Zhou Bo could not enter the military camp to take control of the army.
The Marquis of Qu Zhou, Li Shang, was old and sick, and his son Li Ji was friendly with Lu Lu.
Jianghou discussed the strategy with Chen Ping, the prime minister, and sent people to kidnap Li Shang, and asked Li Ji to deceive Lu Lu and say: Emperor Gao and Queen Lu jointly pacified the world. The Liu family was granted nine kings, and the Lu family was granted three kings. They were all agreed upon by the ministers. This matter has been notified to the princes, and they all think it is appropriate.
Now that the Queen Mother is dead and the Emperor is young, and you wear the seal of King Zhao, you do not return home quickly to defend the country, but as a general, you lead the army to stay here, and you are suspected by the ministers and princes.
Why don't you return the general's seal and hand over the army to the Taiwei?
And ask the King of Liang to return the seal and ribbon of the Prime Minister, make an alliance with the ministers, and go to his own kingdom. In this way, the King of Qi will definitely stop his troops, the ministers can be stable, and you can sit back and relax, and be king for thousands of miles, which will be beneficial to future generations.
summary: After her death, the Lu family plotted rebellion. King Qi of Liu led forces against them, and ministers like Zhou Bo and Chen Ping conspired to remove the Lu. Zhou Bo, using deception, gained command of the Northern Army, and the soldiers supported the Liu family. Lu Lu surrendered his command, and Lu Chan was killed. The Lu family was exterminated, including Lu Lu and Lu Yu.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/吕太后本纪

translation:
Hou Ji, the ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty, was named Qi.
His mother was a woman of Tai family named Jiang Yuan.
Jiang Yuan was the emperor's concubine.
Jiang Yuan went out to the countryside and saw a giant footprint. He was so happy that he wanted to step on it. When he stepped on it, he felt his body vibrating as if he was pregnant.
When they were ten months old, they gave birth to a son. Jiang Yuan thought that the child was unlucky, so he threw him into a narrow alley, but horses and cows passed by him and avoided stepping on him, so he threw him in the woods. There were many people in the woods, so he moved to another place.
Jiang Yuan thought this was so magical, so he took him back and raised him as a human being.
Since I wanted to throw him away at first, I named him Abandoned.
When Qi was a child, he had the lofty ambitions of a great man.
When he was playing games, he liked to plant hemp and beans, and the hemp and beans he planted grew very luxuriantly.
When he grew up, he liked farming. He could observe the characteristics of the land and choose suitable grains to plant. The people followed his example.
When Emperor Yao heard about these things, he appointed Qi as a farmer to teach people how to grow crops. People all over the world benefited from this, and he made great contributions.
Emperor Shun said: "Sir, the people were suffering from hunger, thanks to you being the Houji to sow all kinds of grains."
Therefore, the enfeoffment was abandoned in Tai, known as Houji, and Ji was the surname.
Hou Ji is famous because during the Tao, Tang, Yu, and Xia generations, this family was very virtuous.
After Hou Ji died, his son Buchu succeeded to the throne.
In Buchu's later years, the Xia Hou family's state affairs declined, and they gave up the official post of Houji and no longer paid attention to agriculture. Buchu fled to the Rongdi area because he lost his official position.
After Bucheng died, his son Ju succeeded to the throne.
After Ju's death, his son Gong Liu succeeded to the throne.
Although Gong Liu was in the Rong and Di, he resumed the business of repairing Houji's foundation, engaged in farming, and planted crops according to the cultivation characteristics of the land. He crossed the Wei River from Qishui and Ju Rivers, felled and obtained timber for use, so that those who went out had travel expenses, those at home had savings, and the people's lives improved thanks to him.
The people were grateful and loved him, and many moved to join him.
The great prosperity of Zhou Dynasty's statecraft started from here, so poets composed poems and music to praise and commemorate his kindness.
After Gong Liu died, his son Qingjie succeeded to the throne and established the capital in Bin.
After Qingjie's death, his son Huangpu succeeded to the throne.
After the death of the imperial servant, his son Chafu succeeded to the throne.
After Chafu's death, his son Ruihe succeeded to the throne.
After the death of Ruihe, his son Gongfei succeeded to the throne.
After Gong Fei's death, his son Gao Yu succeeded to the throne.
After Gao Yu's death, his son Ya Yu succeeded to the throne.
After Yayu's death, his son Gongshu Zulei succeeded to the throne.
After the death of Gongshu Zulei, his son Gu Gongdanfu succeeded to the throne.
Gu Gongdanfu re-established the foundations of Houji and Gongliu, accumulated virtues, and spread benevolence and righteousness. The people in the capital all supported him.
summary: Hou Ji, ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty, was named Qi. His mother Jiang Yuan, a concubine of the emperor, became pregnant after stepping on a giant footprint. She bore a son but tried to abandon him multiple times. Miraculously, animals protected him, so she raised him and named him "Abandoned." As a child, Qi showed great ambition, excelling at planting crops. When he grew up, he became skilled at farming, observing land characteristics to choose suitable grains. Emperor Yao appointed him as a farmer to teach agriculture, and Emperor Shun enfeoffed him in Tai, calling him Hou Ji, with Ji as his surname. After Hou Ji died, his son Buchu succeeded. During Buchu's later years, the Xia dynasty declined and abandoned agriculture. Buchu fled to the Rongdi region. His descendant Gong Liu revived Hou Ji's agricultural practices, crossing rivers to obtain timber, improving people's lives. Many people moved to join him, marking the beginning of Zhou's prosperity. Gong Liu's descendant Gu Gongdanfu further accumulated virtues and benevolence. When Rongdi tribes attacked, seeking land and people, Gu Gong refused to fight, saying he could not bear sacrificing people for his own sake. He moved with his relatives to the foot of Qishan Mountain, where many people followed him. He built cities, established towns, and created five official positions.

translation:
Xunyu and other Rongdi tribes came to attack them and wanted to plunder their property, so Gu Gong and Danfu gave it to them.
Soon after, the Rongdi tribe came to attack again, wanting to get the land and people.
The people were very angry and wanted to go out and fight.
Gu Gong said: The people support the monarch because they want him to seek benefits for everyone.
Now Rong and Di are coming to invade, with the purpose of wanting my land and people.
What difference does it make if the people follow me or follow them?
The people went to war because of me and relied on fathers, sons and brothers who sacrificed the people to be the monarch. I really couldn't bear to do this.
So Gu Gongdanfu and his relatives left Bin, crossed Qishui and Jushui, crossed Liangshan, and settled at the foot of Qishan.
And all the people in Bindi brought their old and young to the foot of Qishan Mountain, and all returned to Gu Gong's side.
Nearby countries heard that the ancient Duke was benevolent, and many people came to follow him.
So Gu Gong abandoned the customs of Rong and Di, built cities and houses, and set up towns for the people to settle down.
Five official offices were established: Situ, Sima, Sikong, Sushi, and Sikou. The people composed poems and music to praise him and praise his kindness.
The eldest son of Duke Gu was called Taibo, and the second son was called Yu Zhong.
Taijiang gave birth to a younger son, Ji Li, who married Tairen. Both Taijiang and Tairen were virtuous wives. Tairen gave birth to a prosperous son, which was a sign of sagehood.
Gu Gong said: My descendants will achieve great things, probably Chang, right?
The eldest son Taibo and Yu Zhong knew that Gu Gong wanted to establish Ji Li so that he could pass on to Chang in the future, so they fled to Jingman, got tattoos on their bodies, cut their hair short, and gave way to Ji Li.
After the death of Gu Gong, Ji Li succeeded to the throne and became Gong Ji.
Gong Ji practiced the way of governing the country left by the ancient Duke and resolutely implemented benevolence and righteousness, and the princes all obeyed him.
After Gong Ji died, his son Chang succeeded to the throne and became Xibo.
Xibo was called King Wen. He inherited the cause of Hou Ji and Gong Liu, followed the laws of Gu Gong and Gong Ji, practiced benevolence and righteousness, respected the elderly, and was kind to the young.
He treated the wise men with courtesy. In order to receive the wise men, he sometimes did not bother to eat at noon, so the scholars all attached themselves to him.
Boyi and Shuqi were in Guzhu country. They heard that Xibo was very respectful and took care of the elderly, so they went together to join Xibo.
Tai Dian, Hong Yao, San Yisheng, Huan Zi, Xin Jia and other officials also went to submit to him.
Chonghou Hu spoke ill of Xibo in front of King Zhou of Yin: Xibo has accumulated virtues and done good deeds, and all the princes have submitted to him, which will be detrimental to you.
So Yin Zhou imprisoned Xibo in Youli.
Hong Yao and others were very worried about Xi Bo, and tried their best to find beauties from the Xin family, colorful horses from the Lirong region, nine carriages from the Xiong Kingdom, and various other rare treasures, and presented them to King Zhou through Fei Zhongjin, a favored minister of the Yin Shang Dynasty.
King Zhou was very happy and said: "Anything in this is enough for me to free Xibo, not to mention there are so many other good things!"
So he pardoned Count Xi and gave him bows, arrows, axes and axes, giving him the right to conquer the neighboring princes.
King Zhou told Xibo: The person who framed Xibo was Chonghou Hu.
After Xibo returned home, he offered the land west of Luoshui and asked Zhou to abolish the criminal law of Paoluo.
Zhou agreed to him.
Xibo secretly did good deeds, and the princes came to ask him to judge right and wrong.
At that time, people from Yu and Rui had lawsuits that could not be adjudicated, so they went to Zhou.
They entered the realm of Zhou and saw that those who farmed fields gave way to each other, and the people regarded humility as a virtue.
Before the people of Yu and Rui saw Xibo, they felt ashamed and said to each other: "What we are fighting for is what the people of Zhou are ashamed of. Why are we going to do it? We are just bringing shame on ourselves."
So they returned and left with humility to each other.
When the princes heard about it, they all said: Xibo must be a monarch who has received orders from heaven.
In the second year, Xibo conquered Quanrong.
The next year, Mi Xu was conquered.
summary: Gu Gong's eldest son Taibo and second son Yu Zhong fled to Jingman, giving way to their younger brother Ji Li, whose son Chang (King Wen) would achieve greatness. King Wen inherited the legacy of Hou Ji and Gong Liu, practicing benevolence, respecting elders, and treating wise men with courtesy. Many scholars and officials submitted to him. Chonghou Hu slandered him to King Zhou of Yin, who imprisoned him in Youli. Officials presented rare treasures to King Zhou, who freed King Wen and gave him the right to conquer neighboring princes. King Wen secretly did good deeds, and when people from Yu and Rui came to him with disputes, they saw the humility of Zhou's people and felt ashamed, resolving their conflicts peacefully.

translation:
The next year, he defeated Qi.
When Zuyi of the Yin Dynasty heard about it, he was very frightened and reported the situation to King Zhou.
King Zhou said: Isn't it destiny to help me?
What can he do!
The next year, Xibo conquered Xin.
The next year, he conquered Chonghou Hu.
Fengyi was built and the capital was moved from Qixia to Feng.
The next year, Uncle Xi died, and Prince Fa ascended the throne, becoming King Wu.
Siebo reigned for about fifty years.
When he was imprisoned in Youli, he probably increased the eight hexagrams in "Yi" to sixty-four.
Judging from the praise of Count Xi by the author of "Poetry", it was probably in that year that Count Xi was appointed king and adjudicated the lawsuits between Yu and Rui.
He died ten years later, and his posthumous title was King Wen.
He once changed the legal system of Yin and formulated the calendar.
Zeng Zhui respected Gu Gong as the Taiwang, and Gongji as the Wangji: It probably means that the auspicious sign of the emperor began from the time of the Taiwang.
When King Wu came to the throne, Taigong Wang was appointed as Grand Master, Duke Zhou became assistant prime minister, and Duke Zhao and Duke Bi assisted King Wu and followed King Wen's legacy.
In the ninth year of King Wu's appointment, King Wu first offered sacrifices to King Wen in Bi, and then went to the east to hold a military parade and arrived at Mengjin.
Let King Wen's wooden master be carried on a cart and placed in the central army's tent.
King Wu claimed to be Prince Fa, indicating that he was conquering in the name of King Wen and did not dare to act arbitrarily.
He declared to Sima, Situ, Sikong and other officials who were ordered by the king to hold the talisman festival: Be careful and do what you say!
I am an ignorant person, but because my ancestors were virtuous, I inherited their achievements. Various reward and punishment systems have now been established to ensure that the achievements of ancestors are completed.
So he sent troops.
Master Shi Shangfu ordered: Gather your men and take advantage of the oars. Anyone who is late will be killed.
King Wu crossed the Yellow River, and when the boat reached the middle of the river, a white fish jumped into King Wu's boat. King Wu leaned over and picked it up for sacrifice.
After crossing the river, a ball of fire fell from the sky and landed on King Wu's roof. It solidified into the shape of a crow, was red in color, and made a soulful cry.
At that time, eight hundred princes came to Mengjin to form an alliance.
The princes all said: Zhou can be defeated.
King Wu said: You don't understand the destiny of heaven, not yet.
So he led the army back.
Two years later, I heard that Zhou was more chaotic and violent than before, so he killed Prince Bigan and imprisoned Jizi.
Tai Shizhen and Shao Shiqiang took their musical instruments and fled to the state of Zhou.
At this time, King Wu announced to all the princes: King Yin has committed serious crimes and must work together to defeat him!
So he followed King Wen's decree and led 300 chariots, 3,000 warriors, and 45,000 armored warriors to march eastward to defeat Zhou.
On the Wuwu day of the twelfth month of the eleventh year, all the troops crossed Mengjin, and all the princes came to join them.
King Wu said: "You must be diligent and don't slack off!"
summary: King Wen conquered several states and moved the capital to Feng. After his death, his son King Wu ascended. In the ninth year of his reign, King Wu marched eastward to Mengjin, where eight hundred princes formed an alliance. Two years later, hearing of Yin Zhou's increasing tyranny, King Wu led 300 chariots, 3,000 warriors, and 45,000 armored soldiers eastward. At Muye, he swore an oath condemning King Zhou for listening to women, abandoning ancestors, and oppressing the people. Although King Zhou's army numbered 700,000, they had no will to fight and turned their weapons against him. King Zhou fled to the Deer Platform and burned himself to death. King Wu shot arrows at his corpse and beheaded him.

translation:
When King Wu came to the capital of Shang, the people in the city were waiting to welcome him on the outskirts of the city.
So King Wu sent his ministers to tell the people of Shang: God will bless everyone!
The people of Shangdu all kowtowed to King Wu and thanked him, and King Wu also bowed and thanked him respectfully.
So King Wu entered the city and found the place where Zhou burned himself.
King Wu personally fired arrows at Zhou's corpse, shot three arrows and then stepped off the chariot. He stabbed Zhou's corpse with a light Lu sword, chopped off Zhou's head with a yellow axe, and hung it on the big white flag.
Then he went to Zhou's two concubines and found that both of them had hanged themselves.
King Wu shot three more arrows at them, stabbed them with his sword, chopped off their heads with a black axe, and hung their heads on small white flags.
After doing all this, King Wu left the city and returned to the army.
The next day, King Wu ordered people to clear the roads and repair the temples and palaces of Shang Zhou.
On the appointed day, a hundred soldiers walked in front carrying Han flags with streamers.
King Wu's younger brother Shu Zhenduobu escorted the chariot and lined up to drive the chariot. Zhou Gongdan held a big ax and Bi Gong held a small ax, standing on both sides of King Wu.
San Yisheng, Tai Dian, and Hong Yao all held swords to guard King Wu.
King Wu entered the city and stood to the left of the general in the south of the temple. The ministers on the left and right followed him.
Mao Shuzheng held the dew collected on the moonlit night in his hands, Wei Kangshufeng spread out the straw mat, Zhao Gongxi helped to get the colorful silk, and Shi Shangfu led the sacrificial animal.
Yin Yi read aloud the sacrificial inscription on the bamboo slips and said: The last descendant of Yin, Ji Zhou, abandoned the virtues of the previous king, despised the gods, refused to perform sacrifices, and treated the people in the mall with confusion and cruelty. These things were clearly shown before the Emperor of Heaven.
So King Wu paid homage to the chief inspector again and said: I accept the destiny of God to eradicate the bad government of the Yin Dynasty and accept the bright destiny from heaven.
King Wu paid homage to Jishou again before leaving the city.
King Wu granted the remaining people of Yin to Lu Fu, the son of Shang Zhou.
King Wu sent his younger brothers Guan Shuxian and Cai Shudu to assist Lu's father in governing Yin because the world had just settled down and was not yet peaceful and harmonious.
Then he ordered Duke Zhao to release Jizi from prison.
Bi Gong was ordered to release the imprisoned people from prison and commend the people in Shangronglu Lane.
Nangong Kuo was ordered to distribute the money gathered in Lutai and the food in Juqiao to help the poor savages and untouchables.
Nangong Kuo and Shi Yi were ordered to remove the Jiuding and Baoyu belonging to the Yin people.
Hongyao was ordered to build soil and repair Bigan's tomb.
Zongzhu was ordered to offer sacrifices to the fallen soldiers in the army.
Then withdrew troops back to the west.
Along the way, King Wu visited various vassal states, recorded political affairs, and wrote the "Wucheng" chapter, announcing the achievement of Wu's victory over Yin.
He divided the feudal princes and rewarded them with the sacrificial vessels of the Yin ancestral temple. He wrote the chapter "Dividing the Vessels of Yin" to record his orders and the vessels obtained by the feudal princes.
King Wu recalled the ancient saint kings, so he honored the descendants of Shennong in Jiao, the descendants of Yellow Emperor in Zhu, the descendants of Emperor Yao in Ji, the descendants of Emperor Shun in Chen, and the descendants of Dayu in Qi.
Then he was awarded the title of hero and counselor, and Master Shangfu was the first one to be awarded the title.
King Wu granted his father the title of Qi in Yingqiu.
His younger brother Tong Gongdan was granted the title of Qufu, and his country was named Lu.
He was granted the title of Duke Zhao and died in Yan.
His younger brother Shu Xian was granted the title of Guan, and his younger brother was granted the title of Du in Cai.
Others were also sealed in turn.
King Wu summoned the chief officials of Jiuzhou, climbed to the high ground of Bin, and looked at the capital of Shang in the distance.
summary: After conquering Yin, King Wu released prisoners, distributed wealth to the poor, repaired Bigan's tomb, and divided feudal territories. He honored descendants of ancient sage kings and granted lands to his brothers and officials. King Wu could not sleep at night, worrying about stabilizing the kingdom. He planned to build Zhou city in Luoyi. Two years after defeating Yin, King Wu fell ill and died. His young son King Cheng ascended, with Duke Zhou acting as regent. Guan Shu and Cai Shu rebelled with Wu Geng, but Duke Zhou suppressed the rebellion, killed Wu Geng and Guan Shu, and exiled Cai Shu.

translation:
Property is the product of all things in the world. If you want to monopolize it, it will do too many harms. Everything in heaven and earth is for everyone to take, how can it be monopolized?
He offended many people, but did not prepare for disaster.
If you use these to teach the king, will the king be able to maintain peace and stability for a long time?
A person who calls himself a king should develop financial resources and extend his benefits everywhere.
Although God, man, and all things are given their proper place, they are still on tenterhooks every day, fearing to cause dissatisfaction.
Therefore, "Ode" says: "Remembering the ancestor Hou Ji, who can be as virtuous as heaven and stabilize my numerous people, is not inconsistent with its principles." "Daya" says: Give generously and become my Zhou state.
Isn’t this just giving away money and benefit while fearing disaster? Therefore, it can become my Zhou Dynasty and continues to this day.
Now what Wang is studying is to monopolize financial profits. How can this be allowed?
If an ordinary person monopolizes wealth and profits, it can be called "stealing". If a king does this, there will be very few people willing to join him.
If Duke Rongyi was reused, the Zhou Dynasty would definitely decline.
King Li refused to listen, and finally appointed Rongyi Gong as a minister and asked him to preside over national affairs.
King Li was tyrannical, extravagant and arrogant, and the people of the country openly discussed his faults.
Duke Zhao remonstrated: The people can no longer stand your decree.
King Li was furious and found a sorcerer who was defending the country and sent him to monitor those who criticized the king.
Anyone reported to have committed this crime will be killed. In this way, the criticism was reduced, and the princes no longer came to see him.
In the thirty-fourth year, King Li became even more strict. No one in the country dared to speak anymore, and they could only exchange glances when meeting on the road. King Li was very proud and told Duke Zhao: I can quell people's criticism so that they dare not even speak.
Duke Zhao said: "This is because you have blocked their mouths."
Blocking people's mouths is more dangerous than blocking water.
If the water is blocked, the embankments will burst and flood, which will definitely hurt a lot of people, including the people.
Therefore, those who manage water must channelize the water, and those who manage the people must let them speak freely.
Therefore, in order to understand the situation, the emperor asked everyone from the ministers to the nobles to contribute poems, blind musicians to present music, historians to present books, masters to give instructions, blind people without eyes to narrate, blind people with eyes to recite, and all craftsmen to Let the common people talk in the streets, let the ministers admonish, let the relatives correct mistakes, let the blind musicians and historians teach, let the old people admonish, and then let the emperor consider it, so that political affairs can be carried out without violating reason.
The people have mouths, just like the land has mountains and rivers, which are the source of wealth, and just like the land has plains and fertile fields, which are the source of food and clothing.
Let people speak freely, and good and bad things can be reflected.
Doing good deeds and guarding against bad deeds is the true source of wealth, food and clothing.
The people consider it in their hearts and speak it out with their mouths, and then do it after the matter is decided.
How can it last long if their mouths are blocked? The king refused to listen.
Therefore, no one in the country dared to speak. Three years later, they rebelled and attacked King Li.
summary: King Cheng and King Kang's reigns saw peace for over forty years without using punishments. The Zhou royal family declined during King Zhao's reign. King Mu, who ascended at age fifty, restored order but foolishly attacked the Quanrong, causing distant states to stop paying tribute. King Li was greedy and tyrannical, suppressing criticism by killing those who spoke out. Duke Zhao warned him that blocking people's mouths was more dangerous than blocking water, but King Li refused to listen. After three years, the people rebelled and King Li fled. The country was governed by two dukes during the Republic period.

translation:
Guo Shi's father was a eloquent man who liked flattery and was greedy for wealth, but King You put him in high regard.
In addition, he deposed Empress Shen and removed the prince.
Marquis Shen was very angry and joined forces with Zhen and Quan Rong, who belonged to Xiyi, to attack King You.
King You raised beacon fire to recruit the armies of the princes, but none of them came.
Marquis Shen killed King You at the foot of Mount Li, captured Bao Si, and took away all Zhou's treasures before leaving.
At that time, all the princes came to Shenhou to jointly establish Yijiu, the prince of the former Youwang, as Pingwang, in order to maintain the Zhou Dynasty's sacrificial tradition.
King Ping ascended the throne and moved the capital east to Luoyi to avoid the invaders.
During the reign of King Ping, the Zhou royal family declined, and powerful states annexed weak ones. Qi, Chu, Qin, and Jin began to become powerful, and political orders often came from the hegemonic monarch.
In the forty-ninth year, Duke Yin of Lu came to the throne.
In the fifty-first year, King Ping passed away, and the prince's father died early, so he made his son Lin the king, who was King Huan.
King Huan is the grandson of King Ping.
In the third year of King Huan's reign, Duke Zhuang of Zheng came to court, but King Huan did not give him any courtesy.
In the fifth year, Zheng sent Wan to exchange Xu Tian with Lu.
Xutian is the land used by the emperor to worship Mount Tai.
In the eighth year, the state of Lu killed Duke Yin and established Duke Huan.
In the thirteenth year, when Zheng was attacked, Zheng shot and wounded King Huan, and King Huan fled back.
In the twenty-third year, King Huan died and his son, King Zhuang Tuo, ascended the throne.
In the fourth year of King Zhuang's reign, Duke Zhou Heijian wanted to kill King Zhuang and support Prince Ke.
Xin Bo reported the news to King Zhuang, who killed Duke Zhou, and Prince Ke fled to Yan.
In the fifteenth year, King Zhuang died, and his son King Li, Hu Qi, came to the throne.
In the third year of King Li's reign, Duke Huan of Qi began to dominate.
In the fifth year, King Li died and his son, King Hui Lang, came to the throne.
In the second year of King Hui's reign, King Zhuang's favorite concubine, Yao Shi, gave birth to a son named Dai, who was favored by him.
When King Hui came to the throne, King Hui seized the gardens of his ministers and used them as his own hunting grounds. Therefore, Bian Bo, the official, and five other people made a rebellion and planned to summon the troops of Yan and Wei to attack King Hui.
King Hui fled to Wen, and soon lived in Yue, Zheng State.
They made King Li's younger brother Dai king.
A full set of dance music was played. The kings of Zheng and Guo were very angry.
Four years later, the kings of Zheng and Guo came to attack, killed Wang Dai, and re-elected King Hui.
In the tenth year of King Hui's reign, he granted Duke Huan of Qi the title of uncle.
In the twenty-fifth year, King Hui passed away, and his son King Xiang Zheng ascended the throne.
King Xiang's mother has passed away long ago. The stepmother is Empress Hui.
Empress Hui gave birth to her uncle, who was favored by King Hui, but King Xiang did not trust him.
In the third year, Shudai negotiated with Rong and Zhai to attack King Xiang. King Xiang wanted to kill Shudai, so Shudai fled to Qi.
Duke Huan of Qi sent Guan Zhong to persuade Rong to make peace with Zhou, and Xi Peng to persuade Rong to make peace with Jin.
summary: King Xuan restored Zhou's prestige, but King You foolishly lit beacon fires to amuse his concubine Bao Si, causing the princes to lose trust. He deposed his queen and prince, provoking Marquis Shen to join with Quanrong to attack and kill King You. King Ping moved the capital east to Luoyi. The Zhou royal family declined as powerful states like Qi, Chu, Qin, and Jin grew strong. Over subsequent generations, Zhou kings lost authority, with political orders coming from hegemonic monarchs. Eventually, Qin conquered the Western Zhou, obtaining the sacred nine tripods. Seven years later, Qin destroyed the Eastern Zhou, ending the Zhou Dynasty's sacrificial traditions.

translation:
Xia Yu's name was Wen Ming.
Yu's father was Gun, Gun's father was Emperor Zhuanxu, Zhuanxu's father was Changyi, and Changyi's father was Huangdi.
Yu is the great-great-grandson of Huangdi and the grandson of Emperor Zhuanxu.
Neither Yu's great-grandfather Changyi nor his father Gun ascended to the throne, but served as ministers to the emperor.
When Emperor Yao was in power, the floods were so powerful that they surrounded the mountains and covered the hills. The people were very worried about this.
Yao was looking for someone who could control the floods, and all the ministers in the four mountains said that Gun could do it.
Yao said: Gun, a man who disobeyed the destiny and destroyed his own people, is of no use.
The four mountains all said: In comparison, among the ministers, no one is stronger than him. I hope you will let him try.
So Yao followed Siyue's advice and appointed Gun to control the flood.
Nine years later, floods are still raging and water control has not achieved any results.
At this time, Emperor Yao asked someone else to control the floods, and he found Shun again.
Shun was appointed to take charge of the emperor's government affairs and visited all directions.
During his inspection, Shun saw that Gun was ineffective in controlling the floods, so he killed Gun at Yushan.
Everyone in the world believed that Shun's punishment of Gun was correct.
Shun also promoted Gun's son Yu to continue his father Gun's career in flood control.
After Yao's death, Emperor Shun asked Siyue: Is there anyone who can fulfill Yao's cause well and hold an official position?
It is said that if Boyu is allowed to be Sikong, he will definitely be able to complete Yao's deeds well. Emperor Shun said: Yes!
That's it!
Therefore, he appointed Yu and said: Go and calm down the water and soil, and work hard!
Yu bowed his head and thanked him, and humbly gave way to Qi, Houji and Gaotao.
Shun said: You'd better go and handle your affairs quickly!
Yu was smart, quick-witted, and diligent. He abided by morality and was kind and amiable. His speech was honest and trustworthy, his voice was in tune, his behavior was in line with the law, and the standards of weighing were set by Yu.
He is diligent and serious, and is a model for all officials. Yu accepted Emperor Shun's order and took office together with Yi and Hou Ji. He ordered the princes and officials to recruit civilians to carry out water and soil control work. He set up signs along the way and measured the appearance of mountains and rivers.
Yu was saddened by the fact that his father Gun was killed for failing to control the floods. Therefore, regardless of fatigue and exhaustion, Yu did not dare to enter his house even after passing by his house several times for thirteen years.
He lived simply in food and clothing, and tried his best to worship ghosts and gods.
They lived in simple houses and spent their money on water conservancy projects such as building canals and digging ditches. He traveled by car on land, took a boat by water, rode a sled on muddy roads, and wore toothed shoes when walking on mountain roads. He holds a yardstick and a rope in his left hand, a rule and a rule in his right hand, and also carries instruments for measuring the four seasons and determining directions, which he uses to develop Kyushu, open up roads to Kyushu, build embankments of Kyushu lakes, and measure the veins of mountains in Kyushu.
He asked Boyi to distribute rice seeds and teach the people to plant them in low-lying and humid places.
Later, Houji was asked to provide relief to the people who could not ensure food and clothing.
summary: Xia Yu, also known as Wen Ming, was the great-great-grandson of Huangdi and grandson of Emperor Zhuanxu. His father Gun and great-grandfather Changyi served as ministers rather than emperors. During Emperor Yao's reign, devastating floods surrounded mountains and covered hills, causing great distress. Yao sought flood control experts, and despite his reservations about Gun's character, appointed him based on ministers' recommendations. After nine years of failed efforts, Shun, who had been appointed to manage government affairs, executed Gun at Yushan—a decision widely approved—and appointed Gun's son Yu to continue the work. Yu, described as intelligent, diligent, and morally upright, accepted Shun's appointment alongside Yi and Hou Ji. Grieving his father's execution, Yu worked tirelessly for thirteen years, passing his home multiple times without entering. He lived frugally, invested resources in water conservancy, and used various transportation methods to survey terrain. Yu distributed rice seeds, provided relief to the needy, and facilitated food transfers between regions. His flood control journey began in Jizhou, where he managed rivers and lakes, classified soil types, and established tax and tribute systems based on land fertility.

translation:
In places where food is scarce, some regions are allowed to transfer their surplus grain to food-deficient areas, so that all princes have food to eat within their borders.
Yu also inspected the unique products of various places to determine their tribute, and also inspected the convenient transportation conditions of mountains and rivers in various places.
Yu's journey to supervise flood control began in Jizhou.
Jizhou: Hukou has been controlled, and Liangshan and its branches will be controlled next.
After managing Taiyuan, it was then repaired to the south of Taiyue Mountain.
After controlling Qinhuai, they continued to the Hengshui and Zhangshui areas.
The soil in Jizhou is white and soft. The taxes here belong to the upper class, that is, the first class, sometimes mixed with the second class. The fields belong to the middle class, that is, the fifth class.
The Changshui and Weishui rivers have been dredged, and the land around Daluze can be cultivated.
The Tori tribe in the northeast paid tribute to the nobles for the skins of exotic animals.
They followed the sea route to pay tribute, and when sailing south along the coast, they saw the Jieshi at the right corner, so they turned west and sailed straight into the Yellow River channel.
Between Jishui and the Yellow River is Yanzhou: the nine rivers in this area have been unblocked, Leixia has accumulated into a large lake, and Yongshui and Jushui will also flow into this lake. Mulberries are planted on the land and silkworms are raised, so the people can live in the flatlands from the highlands where they moved to avoid floods.
The soil of Yan is black and fertile, the vegetation on it is lush and the trees are tall.
The fields here are listed in the sixth class, and the taxes are in the ninth class.
After thirteen years of farming, we can be like other states.
The soil here is white and fertile, the seashore is wide and contains alkali, and the fields are mostly saline-alkali land.
The fields belong to the upper and lower classes, that is, the third class, and the taxes belong to the middle and upper classes, that is, the fourth class.
The tributes in this area include salt, fine kudzu cloth, seafood, and stones for grinding jade, as well as silk, hemp, lead, pine, and jade-like stones from the Tai Valley. The Laiyi area can be used for grazing, so livestock products are tribute there, as well as baskets containing tussah silk used to make piano strings.
Its tribute route was shipped directly from Wenshui to Jishui.
The area between the coast in the east, Mount Tai in the north, and Huai River in the south is Xuzhou. The Huai River and Yishui River in this area have been controlled, and crops can be grown in Mengshan and Yushan.
Ohnozawa has accumulated into a lake, the water in the Dongyuan area has receded, and the land has leveled off.
The soil here is red, sticky and fertile, and the vegetation growing here is very lush.
The fields were ranked in the second class, and the taxes were in the fifth class.
The tributes in this area are the five-color soil used by the emperor to build altars to worship heaven, the five-color pheasant feathers from the Yu Valley, the solitary tung tree that is a specialty of the south of Yishan Mountain and can be used to make harps, the floating rock on the shore of Surabaya, the pearl oysters and fish products from Huaiyi, and the fine and clean black and white silk held in bamboo baskets.

summary: Yu's efforts spanned nine provinces, each with distinct characteristics. In Jizhou, white soft soil was taxed at upper-first class with middle-fifth class fields. Yanzhou featured black fertile soil with sixth-class fields and ninth-class taxes. Xuzhou had red sticky fertile soil with second-class fields and fifth-class taxes. Yangzhou's moist soil ranked ninth-class fields with seventh-class taxes. Jingzhou's moist soil had lower-middle eighth-class fields and upper-lower third-class taxes. Yuzhou's soft fertile soil featured upper-middle fourth-class fields and upper-middle second-class taxes. Liangzhou's blue-black soil had lower-upper seventh-class fields and lower-middle eighth-class taxes. Yongzhou's yellow soft fertile soil had upper-first class fields and middle-lower sixth-class taxes. Each province contributed specific tributes, including metals, fabrics, stones, and exotic goods, transported via designated waterways.

translation:
Each tax official has his or her own responsibilities, and taxes must be collected in various places. Taxes must be collected with caution and based on the fertility of the land, and must be collected within the nine states of China. He divided the princes among the nine states, gave them land and surnames, and ordered: "You must respect my virtues first, and you must not violate my various measures."
The area five hundred miles away from Suifu is the key service, that is, the area that is bound and obeyed by the emperor: within three hundred miles of Suifu, one must abide by the teachings and live in peace; the area within two hundred miles away is the place where prisoners are exiled.
The area five hundred miles away should be conquered as desolate areas, that is, the remote areas on the far side were guarded by the emperor; the areas within three hundred miles closer should be conquered as desolate and backward, where people could come and go without restriction; and the area within two hundred miles further away would be the place where prisoners were exiled.
In this way, with the sea to the east, the desert to the west, and from north to south, the emperor's prestige and education reached the remote frontiers in all directions.
So Emperor Shun gave Yu a piece of black jade representing the color of water in recognition of his merits in flood control, announcing to the world that the flood control was successful. The world will be peaceful and stable from now on.
Gaotao held the official position of law enforcement sergeant and governed the people.
When Emperor Shun went to court, Yu, Boyi, and Gaotao talked together in front of Emperor Shun.
Gao Tao expressed his opinion and said: If you follow morality unswervingly, you can achieve wise strategies and unite your ministers.
Yu said: That’s right, but what should we do?
Gao Tao said: Oh, you must be careful about your self-cultivation and have long-term plans to make all tribes honest, loving, obedient and orderly. In this way, many knowledgeable people will work hard to assist you. From the near to the far, you must start from yourself. Yu thanked Gao Tao for his kind words and said: "Yes."
Gao Tao said: Oh, and achieving virtue lies in being able to understand people and appease the people. Yu said: Ha!
Like this, even Emperor Yao would probably find it difficult.
If you can understand people, you are wise, and you can properly arrange official positions for them; if you can appease the people, you are benevolent, and the people will love you.
If you can understand people and be benevolent, why worry about Huan Dou? Why exile Youmiao? Why worry about the hypocritical and flattering villain who speaks sweet words?
Gao Tao said: Yes, that's true.
A person's behavior should be checked based on nine virtues. Let's talk about these nine virtues now.
He went on to say: The nine virtues begin with action. They are generous yet dignified, gentle yet firm, honest yet respectful, talented yet cautious, kind yet resolute, upright yet kind, easy yet sharp, decisive yet practical, strong yet reasonable. If you carry forward these nine virtues and stick to them for a long time, that will be great!
If you can declare three of these virtues every day and work hard morning and night, the minister will be able to keep his fief.
If you solemnly and respectfully practice the six virtues every day, and conscientiously assist the king in his affairs, the princes will be able to keep their feudal kingdoms.
If these nine moral qualities can be fully possessed and implemented universally, talented and virtuous people can be appointed as officials, and all officials can handle their government affairs seriously.
Don't let evil tricks succeed.
If an unsuitable person is placed in an official position, it is called disrupting a major event ordained by God.
God punishes the guilty with five types of punishments.
Most of what I said is feasible, right?
summary: Yu opened nine mountain roads and channeled nine major rivers, including the Yellow River, Yangtze River, Huai River, and Wei River, directing waters to the sea. This unified the nine provinces, enabling peaceful habitation, road construction, and tributary systems. Emperor Shun recognized Yu's achievements by granting him a black jade symbol. Yu, Boyi, and Gaotao discussed governance before Shun, with Gaotao emphasizing moral cultivation, understanding people, and appeasing the populace through nine virtues. Yu recounted his diligent efforts in flood control, food distribution, and land management. Shun stressed the importance of capable ministers and moral leadership, warning against decadence like Danzhu's. Yu noted his own sacrifices, including marrying Tushan's daughter and leaving his son Qi unraised, to complete water control.

translation:
Therefore, Shun's moral education was further developed.
At this time, Kui played music, the spirits of the ancestors came to appreciate it, the princes showed courtesy to each other, birds and beasts flew and danced around the palace, and after playing "Xiao Shao" nine times, the phoenix was summoned. All the beasts danced, and all the officials were loyal and harmonious.
Emperor Shun then sang: "Follow the mandate of heaven, implement virtuous government, comply with the times of heaven, and act with caution and prudence."
He also sang: The ministers are high-spirited, the emperor is working hard, and the careers of all officials are prosperous!
Gao Taozuo bowed his head and said loudly: You must remember to take the lead and work hard to do your duty, be careful about your laws, and handle all kinds of affairs seriously!
So he continued to sing: The emperor is wise and wise, the ministers are all virtuous, and everything in the world is prosperous!
He also sang: The emperor has no big ideas, the ministers are slack, and everything in the world is ruined!
Emperor Shun paid homage and said, "Yes!" We will all work hard to handle our respective affairs from now on!
At this time, the world respected Yu for his expertise in scale and music, and respected him as the Lord of the Gods of Mountains and Rivers, meaning an emperor who could issue orders on behalf of the Gods of Mountains and Rivers.
Emperor Shun recommended Yu to heaven as the heir to the throne.
Seventeen years later, Emperor Shun died.
After three years of mourning, Yu took refuge in Yangcheng in order to give up the throne to Shun's son Shangjun.
But all the princes in the world did not go to worship Shang Jun and came to worship Yu.
Only then did Yu inherit the throne of the Son of Heaven, and he accepted the worship of all the princes from the south. His country name was Queen of Xia, and his surname was Si.
After Emperor Yu established himself as emperor, he appointed Gao Tao as his successor, recommended him to heaven, and entrusted him with state affairs. However, Gao Tao died without succeeding him.
Yu sealed the descendants of Gaotao in Ying and Liu, and some in Xu.
Later, he used his benefits and granted him state affairs.
Ten years later, Emperor Yu visited the east and arrived at Kuaiji, where he died.
Spread benefit to the world.
After three years of mourning, Yi gave up the throne to Yu's son Qi and went to the south of Jishan Mountain to escape.
Yu's son became virtuous, and all the people in the world turned to him.
When Yu died, although he passed the throne of emperor to Yi, because Yi had not been assisting Yu for long, the world did not obey him.
Therefore, all the princes left Yi and went to pay homage to Qi, saying: "We will make Emperor Yu's son king."
So Qi inherited the position of emperor, and this was Emperor Qi of Xia.
Emperor Qi of the Xia Dynasty was the son of Yu, and his mother was a daughter of the Tushan clan.
After Qi ascended the throne, some members of the Hu clan did not come to join him, so Qi went on an expedition and fought a battle at Gandi.
Before the battle began, Qi made an oath called "Gan's Oath" and summoned the generals of the six armies for admonishment. Qi said: Sigh!
Generals of the Sixth Army, I declare an oath to you: Mr. Youhu despises the five constant principles of benevolence, righteousness, etiquette, wisdom, and faith, and deviates from the righteous way of heaven, earth, and man. Therefore, God will cut off his great destiny.
Now I respectfully carry out God's punishment for him.
summary: After Shun's death, Yu initially yielded to Shun's son Shangjun but ascended the throne when all princes paid homage to him, establishing the Xia dynasty with the surname Si. Yu appointed Gaotao as successor, but Gaotao died before inheriting. Yu later granted state affairs to Yi. Ten years into his reign, Yu died during an eastern inspection at Kuaiji. Yi yielded to Yu's son Qi, who became Emperor Qi of Xia after gaining universal support. Qi suppressed the Youhu clan's rebellion, issuing the "Gan's Oath" to enforce discipline. Subsequent Xia rulers included Taikang, who lost his country due to neglect; Zhongkang; and others down to Jie, the final emperor. Jie's tyranny led to his defeat by Tang, who replaced the Xia dynasty. Tang enfeoffed Xia descendants, who later received Qi in the Zhou dynasty. Sima Qian noted Yu's surname Si, with descendants adopting various clan names, and Confucius' correction of the Xia calendar. Yu's burial site at Kuaiji Mountain, meaning "accounting," commemorates his assessment of princes' merits.

translation:
Emperor Xiaowen was the eldest son of Emperor Gaozu.
In the spring of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Chen Xi's army was defeated and Dai was pacified. Emperor Xiaowen was made King of Dai and his capital was Zhongdu.
He is the son of Queen Mother Bo.
In the seventeenth year of his reign as King of Dai, it was the eighth year of the reign of Emperor Gao. In July of this year, Queen Gao passed away.
In September, Lu Chan and others from Empress Lu's family wanted to rebel and overthrow the Liu family's regime. The ministers annihilated the Lu family together and discussed summoning the king to come to the capital and establish him as emperor. This incident is recorded in "The Chronicles of Empress Dowager Lu".
Prime Minister Chen Ping, Taiwei Zhou Bo and others sent people to greet the king.
The king asked his ministers, Lang Zhongling, Zhang Wu and others for their opinions.
Zhang Wu and others suggested: The ministers in the Han Dynasty were all generals from the time of Emperor Gao. They were familiar with military affairs and were scheming and deceitful. Their real intention was not just that, they were just afraid of the power of Emperor Gao and Empress Dowager Lu.
Now that the Lu family has been annihilated and the capital has been bloodbathed, they are here to greet the king in name, but in fact they cannot be trusted.
I hope that the king will pretend to be ill, not go to the capital, and sit back and watch the situation change.
Lieutenant Song Chang said: The opinions of the ministers are all wrong.
When the corruption of the Qin Dynasty collapsed, the princes and heroes rose up at the same time, thinking that they could conquer the world. There were tens of thousands of people. However, it was the Liu family who finally ascended to the position of emperor. Those who competed in the world cut off the hope of becoming emperor. This is the first point.
Emperor Gao made his children kings, and the territories of the kingdoms were intertwined. This is what people call a clan that is as solid as a rock. Everyone in the world succumbed to the strength of the Liu family. This is the second point.
The rise of the Han Dynasty abolished the harsh decrees of the Qin Dynasty, simplified the laws, and benefited the people. Everyone lived peacefully and unshakably. This is the third point.
With the majesty of the Empress Dowager Lu, she established three of Lu's children as kings, who excelled in power and autocratic power. However, the Taiwei entered the Northern Army with integrity. When he called out, the soldiers all bared their left arms to support the Liu family and betrayed the Lu family. As a result, the Lu family was wiped out.
This is a gift from God and cannot be achieved by human beings.
Now even if the ministers want to rebel, the people are unwilling to be driven by them. Can their party members unite together wholeheartedly?
Today, there are relatives like Zhu Xuhou and Dongmuhou in the capital, and outside the capital there are people who are afraid of the power of the King of Wu, the King of Chu, the King of Huainan, the King of Langxie, the King of Qi, and the King of Dai.
At present, the only sons of Emperor Gao are the King of Huainan and the Great King. The Great King is older, famous for his virtuousness, saintliness, benevolence, and filial piety. Therefore, the ministers comply with the wishes of the people in the world and want to welcome the Great King as the emperor. The Great King has no doubts.
The king reported to the queen mother and held consultations, but he hesitated and did not make up his mind.
Use tortoise shells for divination, and the omens of the hexagrams will be great.
The omen said: Daheng heralds a change. I will become the king of heaven and carry forward the cause of the late emperor like Xia Qi.
summary: Emperor Xiaowen, the eldest son of Emperor Gaozu, was made King of Dai after Chen Xi's defeat in the spring of Gaozu's eleventh year, with his capital at Zhongdu. In the eighth year of Emperor Gao's reign, Empress Gao died, and the Lu family plotted rebellion. The ministers annihilated them and summoned the king to become emperor. The king consulted his ministers; Zhang Wu advised caution, suspecting the ministers' intentions, while Song Chang argued that the Liu family's rule was divinely ordained, the people were loyal, and the king, as the eldest surviving son of Emperor Gaozu, was the rightful choice. After divination showed a favorable omen, the king sent his uncle Bo Zhao to verify the ministers' sincerity. Confirmed, he traveled to Chang'an, where he was greeted by officials. He initially refused the throne three times but eventually accepted, becoming Emperor Xiaowen.

translation:
The officials all said: The emperor's kindness to the people is so great and his virtue is so profound that it cannot be matched by our ministers.
Let us sincerely follow the edict and abolish the laws that prohibit one person from committing a crime, confiscate his wife as a servant of the government, and some other laws that are linked to each other.
In the first month of the year, officials came forward and said: The purpose of confirming the prince earlier is to respect the ancestral temple.
Please install a prince now.
The emperor said: I am already a man of poor virtue. The gods do not enjoy my sacrifices, and the people of the world are not satisfied.
Now that I cannot widely seek for the wise, sage and virtuous people in the world and surrender to the world, I say that I want to establish the prince in advance. This makes me even more virtuous. How should I explain it to the people of the world?
Let’s talk about it slowly later.
Officials said: To establish the prince in advance is to put the ancestral temple and the country first and not forget the world.
The emperor said: The King of Chu is my uncle. He is old and experienced. He understands many principles of the world and the general outline of the country.
King Wu is my elder brother. He is a benevolent man and likes to treat others with kindness.
King Huainan is my younger brother, and he comes to assist me with virtue. Doesn't this pre-solve the emperor's heir?
The princes, kings, clans, brothers, and meritorious ministers are all wise and virtuous people. If you recommend people with moral integrity to help and succeed me, who cannot die, this will be a blessing for the gods of the country and the people of the world.
If I don't mention it now, but I think it must be passed on to my son, people will think that I have forgotten the wise and virtuous people, and am focusing on my own son instead of thinking about the world.
I strongly disapprove of this approach.
The officials all requested resolutely: In ancient times, the Yin and Zhou dynasties established the country and brought peace and order to the world for more than a thousand years. In ancient times, no one who owned the world had a longer-term rule than Yin and Zhou. This is because Yin and Zhou adopted the method of passing on the throne to the son.
He must make his son his heir, as he did so a long time ago.
Emperor Gao personally led the soldiers and generals to pacify the world, feudal princes, and became the ancestor of all emperors.
The princes, kings and princes who initially accepted the feudal kingdom also became the ancestors of their own feudal kingdom.
The succession of descendants to the throne continues from generation to generation, which is the great justice of the world. Therefore, Emperor Gao established the system of succession to the throne to stabilize the country.
It is not Gao Di's idea to give up the candidates who should be appointed as successors and choose others from the princes and clans.
It is not appropriate to change someone else's practice.
Zi is the eldest son, he is kind and kind, please make him the prince.
The emperor agreed.
Therefore, the eldest son of the people in the world who should inherit his father's inheritance was given a rank of nobility. General Bo Zhao was granted the title of Marquis of Zhi.
In March, officials requested the title of queen.
Empress Dowager Bo said: "The princes and kings all have the same surname, so let's make the prince's mother the queen."
The queen's surname is Dou.
Because of the establishment of a queen, the emperor gave a certain amount of cloth, silk, rice, and meat to the widowed, lonely and poor people in the world, as well as the elderly over eighty years old and orphans under nine years old.
The emperor came to the capital from the state of Dai. Not long after he took the throne, he extended kindness to the people of the world and appeased the princes and ethnic minorities from all directions. They were all happy and harmonious, so they rewarded the meritorious officials who came to the capital from the state of Dai in turn.
The emperor said: When the ministers killed the descendants of the Lu family to welcome me, I was hesitant and everyone blocked me. Only Lieutenant Song Chang persuaded me so that I could serve the ancestral temple.
He already respected Song Chang as General Wei, and then named Song Chang as Zhuang Wuhou.
The six people who followed me to the capital were all promoted to the rank of Jiuqing.
The emperor said: Among the sixty-eight princes who followed Emperor Gao to Shu and Hanzhong, each of them was granted a city of 300 households. In the past, the officials who followed Emperor Gao for more than 2,000 shi, including the governor of Yingchuan County, were granted 600 households each. Ten people including Shen Tujia, the governor of Huaiyang County, were granted 500 households each. Ten people such as Wei Wei Ding were granted 400 households each.
Zhao Jian, the uncle of the King of Huainan, was granted the title of Marquis of Zhou Yang, and Si Jun, the uncle of the King of Qi, was granted the title of Marquis of Guo of the Qing Dynasty.
In autumn, Cai Jian, the prime minister of the original Changshan Kingdom, was granted the title of Marquis of Fan.
Someone advised the right prime minister: You originally killed the descendants of the Lu family and welcomed the king as the emperor. Now you rely on these merits to accept the greatest rewards and are in a distinguished position. Disaster will soon come.
Zhou Bo, the right prime minister, dismissed the right prime minister on the pretext of illness, leaving Chen Ping, the left prime minister, to serve as prime minister.
In October of the second year, the prime minister Chen Ping died, and Jianghou Zhou Bo was appointed as the prime minister.
The emperor said: I heard that in ancient times, there were more than a thousand princes who established kingdoms. Each of them guarded his own territory and paid tribute to the emperor according to the prescribed time. The people did not work hard, they were happy and rejoiced, and there was no loss of morality.
Nowadays, most of the princes go to Chang'an, which is far away from the feudal towns. The officials and soldiers there provide and transport the necessary materials, which is laborious and laborious, and the princes have no way to educate and train their people.
The princes were ordered to return to the feudal state, and those who held official positions in the court and had edicts to stay were sent to send the princes to the feudal state.
summary: Upon ascending the throne, the emperor granted amnesty, rewarded officials, and restored lands to Qi and Chu. He abolished the law of punishing innocent family members, stating it harmed the people and contradicted good governance. He initially hesitated to appoint a crown prince, suggesting his uncles or brothers instead, but officials insisted on his son, citing tradition. He agreed, and his eldest son became prince. He also established a queen and rewarded the poor and elderly. He honored meritorious officials from Dai, including Song Chang, and granted lands to followers of Emperor Gaozu.
