translation:
In the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, the emperor said: I am not wise and cannot spread virtue far away, so the countries outside the Central Plains are unrest.
The people in the remote areas around me cannot live peacefully, and the people in the country work hard and cannot live in peace. Both of these faults are due to my lack of morality and my inability to spread my virtue far away.
Recently, the Huns have been invading the border for many years, killing many officials and people. The officials and generals in the border area cannot understand my inner thoughts, which aggravates my bad behavior.
With such long-term wars and inexplicable disasters, how can the countries inside and outside the Central Plains find peace?
Now I get up early and go to bed late, working hard on the world's major affairs, feeling sad for thousands of people, feeling worried and uneasy in my heart, and I can't forget this matter even one day. Therefore, I sent envoys, with crowns and canopies facing each other on the road and rutted roads, to explain my thoughts to the Xiongnu Chanyu.
Now the Chanyu has returned to the correct path of ancient times, considering the peace of the country, seeking the interests of millions of people, personally abandoning those small mistakes with me, uniting on the correct principles, and forming a brotherly relationship to protect the good people of the world.
The marriage has been decided and will start this year.
In the winter of AD 6, 30,000 Xiongnu entered Shangjun, and 30,000 Xiongnu entered Yunzhong.
The emperor appointed Ling Mian, a senior official in the army, as the general of chariots and cavalry, stationed at Feihu; he appointed Su Yi, the former Prime Minister of Chu, as the general, stationed at Juzhu; General Zhang Wu garrisoned the north; Zhou Yafu, the governor of Hanoi County, garrisoned at Xiliu; Zongzheng Liu Li as the general, garrisoned at Ba Shang; Zhu Zihou garrisoned at Jimen to jointly defend against the Huns.
After a few months, the Huns withdrew, and the various armies also withdrew.
There was a drought and locust infestation across the country.
The emperor favored the world, ordered the princes not to pay tribute to the court, abolished the ban on mountains, forests and lakes, reduced the emperor's clothing, utensils, and dogs and horses for play, reduced the number of ministers, opened granaries, provided relief to the poor, and the people could sell their titles to buy food.
Emperor Xiaowen came to the capital from Daiguo and reigned for twenty-three years. Nothing was added to the palaces, gardens, dogs and horses, clothing, and utensils. If there were any inconveniences to the people, they were changed to benefit the people.
I once planned to build a terrace and asked a craftsman to calculate the cost. One hundred pounds of gold was needed.
The emperor said: One hundred kilograms of gold is equivalent to the property of ten families of ordinary people. I enjoy the palace of the late emperor, and I am often worried that I will humiliate the late emperor. Why build this terrace?
The emperor often wore thick silk clothes, and his beloved Mrs. Shen was not allowed to drag her clothes to the ground, and her draperies were not allowed to have embroidery or brocade in order to show her honesty and simplicity, and to set an example for the world.
All mausoleums are built with earthenware, and gold, silver, copper, and tin are not allowed to be used for decoration. No tall tombs are built, in order to save some money and not disturb the people.
The king of Nanyue, Wei Tuo, proclaimed himself Emperor Wu, but the emperor called Wei Tuo's brother and gave high-ranking officials generous salaries in return. Wei Tuo canceled his imperial title and professed himself to the Han Dynasty.
After making peace with the Xiongnu, the Xiongnu violated the treaty and invaded the border to plunder. However, the emperor only ordered the border fortresses to strengthen their defense and did not send troops deep into the hinterland of the Xiongnu for fear of disturbing the people.
King Wu pretended to be ill and did not go to the capital to attend court. The emperor immediately rewarded him with a sitting table and a cane.
Although ministers such as Yuan An and others discussed matters sharply and urgently, the emperor often adopted their suggestions with a tolerant attitude.
Among the ministers, Zhang Wu and others accepted money bribes. When they found out, the emperor took out the money from his treasury and rewarded them, which made them feel ashamed and did not hand it over to the officials for punishment.
The emperor devoted himself wholeheartedly to educating the people with morality. Therefore, there was prosperity and a culture of paying attention to etiquette and justice in the four seas.
On June 1, the seventh year of AD, the emperor died in Weiyang Palace.
summary: The emperor faced natural disasters, interpreting solar eclipses as divine warnings. He urged officials to correct his faults, reduced expenses, and promoted agriculture. He abolished laws against defamation to encourage free speech. He dealt with rebellions, such as that of the King of Jibei, and conflicts with the Xiongnu, often opting for defense over aggression. He showed leniency to the King of Huainan, exiling him instead of executing him, and later honored his sons. He abolished corporal punishment after Tiying's plea for her father, emphasizing education over harsh penalties. The emperor's reign was marked by frugality; he avoided building a terrace costing 100 pounds of gold, wore simple clothes, and forbade extravagance. He maintained peace with Nanyue and the Xiongnu through diplomacy, and tolerated critical ministers. His policies fostered moral education and stability. He died in Weiyang Palace in the seventh year of his reign, leaving a will urging simple mourning, minimal burial, and the release of harem women. He was honored as Emperor Xiaowen, and his temple was designated Taizong, with the "Zhaode Dance" created to commemorate his virtues. Historians praised his benevolence, humility, and effective governance, noting that his reign brought prosperity and moral clarity to the Han dynasty.

translation:
Emperor Xiaojing was the eldest son of Emperor Xiaowen.
His mother is Queen Mother Dou.
When Emperor Xiaowen was in Daiguo, the former queen gave birth to three boys. When Empress Dowager Dou became favored, the former queen died, and her three sons also died one after another, so Emperor Xiaojing could succeed to the throne.
On April 22, the first year of Emperor Jing's reign, a general amnesty was granted to the whole world.
On the Yisi day, the people were given the first rank of nobility.
In May, half of farmers’ land rent will be reduced. The Taizong Temple was built for Emperor Xiaowen.
Order ministers not to congratulate him on his accession to the throne.
The Xiongnu were allowed to enter the land of Dai and signed a peace treaty with the Xiongnu.
In the spring of the second year, Xiao Xi, the grandson of Xiao He, the original Prime Minister, was ennobled as Marquis of Wuling, and it was stipulated that men should be registered in the book when they were twenty years old.
On April 25, Queen Mother Xiaowen passed away.
The kings of Guangchuan and Changsha both went to their respective kingdoms.
Prime Minister Shen Tujia passed away.
In August, Kaifeng Hou Taoqing, the imperial censor, was appointed prime minister.
The comet appears in the northeast.
In autumn, hailstorms hit Hengshan Mountain like rain. The largest hailstones were five inches long and the deepest ones were two feet deep.
Yinghuo moved backwards, approaching Beichen's position, and the moon appeared in the middle of Beichen.
The year star moves in reverse direction in heaven.
The emperor established Nanling, Neishi and Qiyi as counties.
On the twenty-second day of the first month of the third year, a general amnesty was granted to the whole world.
A comet with a long ray appears in the west.
The sky fire burned down the main hall and tower of Luoyang East Palace.
King Liu Bi of Wu, King Liu Wu of Chu, King Liu Sui of Zhao, King Liu Xian of Jiaoxi, King Liu Biguang of Jinan, King Liu Xian of Zichuan, and King Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong launched a rebellion and sent troops to the west.
The emperor executed Chao Cuo because of this incident and sent Yuan Ang to inform the seven kingdoms. However, the seven kingdoms still did not stop their march and continued to besiege Liang State to the west.
Therefore, the emperor sent General Dou Ying and Taiwei Zhou Yafu to lead troops to attack them and finally eliminated them.
On June 25, the emperor pardoned the defeated soldiers and those who participated in the rebellion, including Liu Pei, the son of King Chu Yuan.
The general Dou Ying was granted the title of Marquis of Wei.
He established Pingluhou Liu Li, the son of King Yuan of Chu, as King of Chu.
Prince Liu Duan was made King of Jiaoxi, and Prince Liu Sheng was made King of Zhongshan.
Liu Zhi, the king of Jibei, was renamed the king of Zichuan, Liu Yu, the king of Huaiyang, was the king of Lu, and Liu Fei, the king of Runan, was the king of Jiangdu.
The king of Qi, Liu Jianglu, and the king of Yan, Liu Jia, both died.
In the summer of four years, the crown prince was established.
The prince Liu Che was granted the title of King of Jiaodong.
On June 29th, a general amnesty was granted to the whole world.
In leap September, Geyang was changed to Yangling.
Checkpoints were also set up at ferries and passes, and entry and exit were based on talismans.
In winter, the state of Zhao was renamed Handan County.
In March of the fifth year, Yangling and Wei Bridge were built.
In May, two hundred thousand coins were allocated to recruit people from all over the country to move to Yangling.
The Jiangdu area encountered a big storm from the west, destroying twelve feet of the city wall.
On the 28th, the emperor conferred the title of Longluhou on the son of the eldest princess.
The title of King Guangchuan was changed to King Zhao.
In the spring of the sixth year, Lieutenant Wei Wan was granted the title of Marquis of Jianling, Prime Minister Cheng Jia of Jiangdu was granted the title of Marquis of Jianping, Grand Administrator Gongsun Hunxie of Longxi County was granted the title of Marquis of Pingqu, Prime Minister Su Jia of Zhao was granted the title of Marquis of Jiangling, and the original general Luan Bu was granted the title of Marquis of Tuan.
King Liang and King Chu both died.
summary: Emperor Xiaojing, eldest son of Emperor Xiaowen and Queen Mother Dou, succeeded to the throne after the former queen and her three sons died. In his first year, he granted amnesty, reduced land rent, built Taizong Temple, and signed a peace treaty with the Xiongnu. In the second year, he ennobled Xiao He's grandson and set the age of registration for men at twenty. Queen Mother Dou died, and officials like Shen Tujia passed away. Comets, hailstorms, and celestial anomalies occurred. In the third year, a rebellion by seven kings, including Wu and Chu, was suppressed after executing Chao Cuo. The emperor appointed Dou Ying and Zhou Yafu to lead troops, defeating the rebels. He then established new kings and marquises.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪

translation:
In leap September, the trees along the Chi Road were cut down and the orchid pond was filled in.
In the winter of the seventh year, Prince Li Liu Rong was deposed and was granted the title of King of Linjiang.
On the last day of November, there was a solar eclipse.
In the spring, the prisoners and slaves who built Yangling were pardoned.
Prime Minister Tao Qing was dismissed from his post.
On February 16, Taiwei Tiaohou Zhou Yafu was appointed prime minister.
On April 17, the mother of King Jiaodong was made queen.
On the 29th, King Jiaodong was established as the crown prince.
The crown prince's name is Toru.
In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, Zhou Ping, the grandson of the original censor Zhou Ke, was granted the title of Shenghou, and Zhou Zuoche, the grandson of the original censor Zhou Chang, was granted the title of Anyanghou.
On April 23, a general amnesty was granted to the people, and the people were given first-class titles.
The prohibition against merchants and bridal sons-in-law being allowed to serve as officials, and the prohibition against officials who have committed crimes being allowed to serve as officials again, were abolished. There was an earthquake. There was hail in Hengshan and Yuandu, with the largest diameter being one foot and eight inches.
In February of the second year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, the Xiongnu invaded Yan territory, so they no longer made peace with the Xiongnu.
In March, he ordered King Linjiang to be summoned to the capital for questioning. Soon King Linjiang died in the Lieutenant's Mansion.
In the summer, Prince Liu Yue was made King of Guangchuan, and Prince Liu Ji was made King of Jiaodong.
Four princes were enfeoffed.
On September 30, there was a solar eclipse.
In the winter of the third year of Zhongyuan, the official position of Yushi Zhongcheng in the princely kingdoms was abolished.
In the spring, the two kings of the Xiongnu came and surrendered with their tribes, and they were both named princes.
The prince Liu Fangcheng was made King of Qinghe.
In March, the comet appears in the northwest.
Prime Minister Zhou Yafu was dismissed from his post and Taohou Liu She, the imperial censor, was appointed as prime minister.
In April, there was an earthquake.
On the last day of September, there was a solar eclipse.
Troops were stationed outside the Dongdu Gate of the capital.
In March of the fourth year of Zhongyuan, Deyang Palace was built.
A serious locust plague occurred.
In autumn, the prisoners who built Yangling were pardoned.
In the summer of the fifth year of Zhongyuan, Prince Liu Shun was made King of Changshan.
Ten people were enfeoffed as marquises.
On June 29th, a general amnesty was granted to the people, and the common people were given first-class titles.
Severe waterlogging occurred across the country.
Change the name of the prime minister of the vassal kingdom to prime minister.
In the fall, there was an earthquake.
On February 25, the sixth year of Zhongyuan, the emperor came to Yong County to worship the Five Emperors in the suburbs.
In March, there was hail.
In April, King Xiao of Liang, King Gong of Chengyang, and King of Runan all died.
Liu Ming, the son of King Xiao of Liang, was made King of Jichuan, Liu Pengli was named King of Jidong, Liu Ding was named King of Shanyang, and Liu Bushi was named King of Jiyin.
The original Liang Kingdom was divided into five kingdoms.
Confess four people as marquis.
The official title of Jiangting Wei should be Dali, Jiangzuo Shaofu should be renamed Jiangzuo Dajiang, Lord Lieutenant should be renamed Duwei, Changxin Zhanshi should be renamed Changxin Shaofu, Jiangxing should be renamed Dachangqiu, Daxing should be renamed Xingren, Fengchang should be renamed Taichang, Dianke should be renamed Daxing, and Zhisu Neishi should be renamed Danong.
The official rank of Ouchi was determined to be two thousand stones, and the left inner officer and the right inner officer were set up to make them subordinate to Ouchi.
summary: In the fourth year, the crown prince was established, and Liu Che was made King of Jiaodong. Reforms included setting up checkpoints at ferries. In the fifth year, Yangling was built, and people were recruited to move there. In the sixth year, several officials were ennobled. In the seventh year, Prince Li was deposed, and Zhou Yafu became prime minister. The crown prince was renamed Toru. In the first year of Zhongyuan, amnesty was granted, and restrictions on merchants and criminals were lifted. Earthquakes and hail occurred. In the second year, the Xiongnu invaded, and King Linjiang died. In the third year, Xiongnu kings surrendered, and Zhou Yafu was dismissed. In the fourth year, Deyang Palace was built, and locusts plagued the land. In the fifth year, severe flooding led to renaming officials. In the sixth year, the emperor worshipped the Five Emperors, and the Liang Kingdom was divided. Official titles were reformed.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪

translation:
On July 29, there was a solar eclipse.
In August, the Huns invaded Shangjun.
In the winter of the first year of Houyuan, he was renamed Zhongdafu Ling as Weiwei.
On March 19, a general amnesty was granted to the people, and the people were given the title of first class. Officials with two thousand shi and the prime ministers of the princely states were given the title of right concubine.
In April, people are allowed to gather and have feasts.
On May 9, there was an earthquake, and there was another earthquake during breakfast.
The Shangyong earthquake lasted for twenty-two days and destroyed the city wall.
On July 29, there was a solar eclipse.
Prime Minister Liu She was dismissed from his post.
In August, Wei Wan, the imperial censor, was appointed prime minister and granted the title of Marquis of Jianling.
In the first month of the next two years, three earthquakes occurred in one day.
General Zhi led his troops to attack the Xiongnu.
The people were allowed to gather and feast for five days.
Neishi County was ordered not to feed the horses with grain, but to return the horses to the government.
Criminals and slaves were required to wear only the most coarse clothing. It is forbidden to use horses to pound rice.
Due to the poor harvest that year, the people of the world were prohibited from eating the food harvested that year in advance within one year.
Reduce the number of princes in the capital and send them to their own fiefdoms.
In March, the Huns invaded Yanmen.
In October, the cultivated land around Changling, the mausoleum of Emperor Gaozu, was rented to farmers.
A severe drought occurred.
The plague spread among the people of Hengshan Kingdom, Hedong County, and Yunzhong County.
In October of the third year of AD, a solar and lunar eclipse occurred. The sun and moon were red for five consecutive days.
On the last day of December, there was a thunderstorm.
The sun appears purple.
The five stars are retrograde and invade Taiweiyuan.
The moon crosses the sky.
On the seventeenth day of the first lunar month, Crown Prince Liu Che held a coronation ceremony.
On the 27th, Emperor Xiaojing passed away.
The imperial edict granted everyone from the princes to the common people who were his father's heirs a first-class title, and each household in the world received one hundred coins.
Release the palace maids and let them return to their homes, exempting them from taxes and corvee for life.
The prince ascended the throne and became Emperor Xiaowu.
In March, Tian Fu, the younger brother of the Empress Dowager, was granted the title of Marquis of Wu'an, and Tian Sheng was granted the title of Marquis of Zhou Yang.
Yangling was set up as the mausoleum of Emperor Jing.
Tai Shigong said: After the rise of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Xiaowen extended his kindness and kindness, and the people of the world were grateful and at peace. By the time of Emperor Xiaojing, there was no longer any need to worry about the rebellion of princes and kings with different surnames.
However, Chao Cuo deprived the princes and kings of the same surname of their fiefdoms, causing the seven kingdoms to rebel together and jointly attack the imperial court in the west. This is because the power of the princes and kings is too strong, and Chao Cuo did not gradually weaken it when taking action.
It was not until Zhufu Yan made suggestions that the power of the princes and kings weakened, and the country was finally stabilized.
Isn’t the key to national security relying on strategy?
summary: In the first year of Houyuan, officials were renamed, and amnesty was granted. Earthquakes and solar eclipses occurred. In the second year, General Zhi attacked the Xiongnu, and restrictions on grain and clothing were imposed. Drought and plague spread. In the third year, celestial anomalies appeared, and Crown Prince Liu Che was crowned. Emperor Xiaojing died, granting titles and coins to the people, releasing palace maids. Prince ascended as Emperor Xiaowu. Tai Shigong noted that Emperor Xiaojing faced the seven kingdoms' rebellion due to strong princely power, which was later stabilized by Zhufu Yan's strategies.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝景本纪

translation:
Emperor Xiaowu was the middle son of Emperor Xiaojing, and his mother was the Queen Mother.
In the fourth year of Xiaojing's reign, Emperor Wu was granted the title of King of Jiaodong as a prince.
In the seventh year of Xiaojing's reign, Prince Li was deposed as King Linjiang and King Jiaodong was established as Crown Prince.
Emperor Xiaojing died after reigning for sixteen years, and the prince ascended the throne, becoming Emperor Xiaowu.
When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, he paid special attention to worshiping ghosts and gods.
In the first year of Jianyuan, the Han Dynasty had been established for more than sixty years, and the world was peaceful and peaceful. Officials all hoped that the emperor would hold a Zen ceremony and change the new year-end kimono color system.
The emperor also believed in Confucian scholarship and recruited talented people. Zhao Wan, Wang Zang and others were granted the title of minister because of their knowledge. They wanted to imitate ancient times and suggested that the emperor build a Mingtang in the south of the city to clarify politics and religion, and use it as a place for princes to meet the emperor. The plans they drafted for hunting tours, conferring Zen, and reforming the calendar and uniforms have not yet been completed.
Encountering that Empress Dowager Dou liked the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi, but disliked Confucian scholarship, she sent people to secretly observe Zhao Wan and others' illegal profit-seeking deeds, and summoned Zhao Wan and Wang Zang to investigate the case. Zhao Wan and Wang Zang committed suicide, and many of the measures they proposed were abolished.
Six years later, Queen Mother Dou died.
The next year, the emperor recruited Gongsun Hong and others, who were knowledgeable people.
In the second year, the emperor came to Yong County for the first time and held a suburban sacrifice in Wujie.
From then on, the Suburban Festival was often held every three years.
At that time, the emperor invited a divine monarch to enshrine her in the Tishi Temple in Shanglin Garden.
This divine king was actually a woman from Changling who died of grief over the death of her son. After her death, the spirit appeared in her sister-in-law Wanruo.
It was as if he worshiped her in his own home, and later many people went to worship her.
The emperor's maternal grandmother Pingyuan Jun also went to worship the country, and her descendants became prominent officials.
After Emperor Wu came to the throne, he invited her to the palace with generous gifts to worship her in the temple. But I could only hear her voice, but couldn't see her person.
At that time, Li Shaojun came to see the emperor because he knew how to bring good fortune to the ancestral stove, eat grains instead of fire, guide spiritual energy and achieve immortality. The emperor respected him very much.
Li Shaojun was recommended by the late Marquis Shenze to manage the alchemy affairs.
He concealed his true age and place of birth. He often said that he was seventy years old and could drive ghosts and make people immortal.
He traveled everywhere and relied on his alchemy skills to make friends with princes.
He has no wife or children.
People heard that he could drive away ghosts and make people immortal, so they rushed to give him gifts, so he had a lot of money, silk fabrics, clothes and food.
Everyone thought that he was rich without managing the property, and did not know where he was from, so they believed in him even more and rushed to serve him.
Li Shaojun is good at alchemy and is good at guessing hidden things and telling some secrets of the target person.
summary: Emperor Xiaowu, the middle son of Emperor Xiaojing, ascended the throne after his father's sixteen-year reign. Upon becoming emperor, he showed particular devotion to worshipping ghosts and gods. During the early years of his reign, the Han Dynasty had enjoyed over sixty years of peace, and officials hoped the emperor would perform the Feng and Shan sacrifices to heaven and earth. The emperor, favoring Confucian scholarship, recruited talented individuals like Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, who proposed building a Mingtang for political and religious clarification. However, Empress Dowager Dou, who favored Huang-Lao teachings, opposed Confucianism, leading to Zhao Wan and Wang Zang's suicides and the abandonment of their plans. After the empress dowager's death six years later, the emperor recruited Gongsun Hong and others, and began performing suburban sacrifices every three years.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪

translation:
He once had a banquet with Wu'an Hou Tianfan. There was an old man in his nineties sitting with him. Li Shaojun then said that he and the old man's grandfather visited an archery place. The old man had been with his grandfather when he was a child and recognized the place. This surprised all the guests.
One time, Li Shaojun met the emperor. The emperor had an old copperware hidden in his possession and asked Shaojun.
Shaojun said: This bronze vessel was displayed on the cypress bed in the tenth year of Duke Huan of Qi.
Then he looked at the words engraved on the bronze vessel and found that it was indeed from the era of Duke Huan of Qi.
Everyone in the palace was very surprised, thinking that Shaojun was a god and a person who was hundreds of years old.
Shaojun said to the emperor: By worshiping the stove, you can attract the gods and turn the cinnabar into gold. After the gold is refined, it can be used to make eating utensils. Using these utensils can prolong your life. When you live longer, you can see the immortals on Penglai Mountain in the sea. After meeting the immortals, you can hold a Zen ceremony and you can live forever. This is what the Yellow Emperor did.
I once traveled to the sea and met An Qisheng. He brought me dates to eat, which were as big as melons.
An Qisheng is an immortal who can travel to and from Penglai Mountain. He only sees people who are consistent with his Taoism and hides those who are not.
So the emperor personally worshiped the Kitchen God, and sent alchemists to the East China Sea to visit immortals like Penglai Mountain and An Qisheng, and to turn cinnabar and other medicines into gold.
After a long time, Li Shaojun fell ill and died.
The emperor thought that he had transformed and ascended instead of dying, so he asked Kuanshu, an official in Donglai County, to continue to study Shaojun's alchemy. He searched for Penglai Mountain and Anqisheng, but he could not find it. The weird and sophisticated alchemists from Yan and Qi along the coast followed suit and wrote letters one after another about gods.
Bo Youji, a native of Hao County, reported the method of worshiping Taiyi, saying: The most noble among the gods is Taiyi, and Taiyi's auxiliary gods are the five emperors.
In ancient times, the emperor worshiped the Taiyi God in the southeastern suburbs in spring and autumn. He used Tailao, a complete animal of cattle, sheep, and pigs, to worship for seven days, and set up channels on all sides of the altar to walk on behalf of ghosts and gods.
So the emperor ordered Taizhu to build the kind of ancestral altar he mentioned in the southeastern suburbs of Chang'an, and often worshiped according to the method of Bo Yuji.
Later, someone wrote a letter saying that in ancient times, the emperor used Tailao every three years to worship the three gods: the god of heaven, the god of earth, and the god of Tai.
The emperor agreed and ordered Taizhu to worship in this way on the Taiyi altar built by Miji.
Later, someone wrote a letter saying that in ancient times, the emperor often held sacrifices to eliminate disasters and seek blessings in spring and autumn. An owl and a broken mirror were used to sacrifice the Yellow Emperor;
The emperor ordered the ancestral officials to accept sacrifices according to this method and to offer sacrifices next to the Taiyi altar built by Miu Ji.
Later, the emperor's palace kept a white deer. Some people said that making leather coins from its skin could induce auspiciousness, so platinum coins were minted.
In the second year, the emperor held a suburban sacrifice in Yong County and captured a unicorn that looked like a harpoon. The official in charge said: Your Majesty respectfully held a suburban sacrifice. In return for your sacrifice, God will give you a unicorn. This should be Qilin!
So he dedicated it to five plots, adding an ox to each plot, and burned them to repay God's gift.
For this reason, white gold was given to the princes to indicate that this auspicious omen should be in line with the will of heaven and earth.
From this, the King of Jibei thought that the emperor was going to hold a ceremony to enshrine the Zen, so he wrote to offer Mount Tai and the surrounding counties. The emperor accepted the offer and gave him other counties as compensation.
King Changshan was deposed because of his guilt and moved to Fangling. The emperor named his younger brother King Zhending to continue the sacrifice to his ancestors and set up Changshan as a county.
From then on, all the five mountains were in the counties directly under the emperor's jurisdiction.
The next year, a young man from the Qi people came to the emperor with the help of alchemy to communicate with ghosts and gods. The emperor's favorite Mrs. Wang died. The young man used the alchemy to summon the appearance of Mrs. Wang and the Kitchen God at night. The emperor saw Mrs. Wang from the curtain.
So he conferred the title of General Wencheng on the young man, rewarded him with many things, and received him with the etiquette of receiving guests.
summary: The emperor invited a divine spirit, originally a woman from Changling who died grieving for her son, to be worshipped in the Shanglin Garden. He also honored Li Shaojun, an alchemist who claimed to be seventy years old and capable of driving ghosts and making people immortal. Li Shaojun demonstrated his powers by identifying an ancient bronze vessel and advised the emperor to worship the stove, turn cinnabar into gold, and seek immortals on Penglai Mountain to achieve immortality. The emperor followed his advice, worshipping the stove and sending alchemists to the sea. After Li Shaojun's death, the emperor believed he had ascended to immortality and continued seeking alchemists.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪

translation:
General Wencheng said: If the emperor wants to communicate with the gods, the palace, bedding and other daily necessities are different from those used by the gods, and the gods will not come.
So they made cars with clouds painted on them, and drove cars of different colors on different days to drive away evil spirits. They also built Ganquan Palace. In the middle of the palace was a stage room with paintings of many gods such as Tianyi, Earthly One, and Taiyi. Sacrificial utensils were placed to attract the gods.
More than a year later, the young man's alchemy became less and less effective, and the god never came.
General Wencheng wrote some words on a piece of silk and let the cow eat it. He pretended that he didn't know anything about it, and told others that there was something strange in the belly of the cow. He killed the cow and looked at it, and got the silk book. The words in the book were very weird.
After that, white beam platforms, copper pillars and dew-bearing cactus were built.
In the second year after Wencheng's death, the emperor became seriously ill in Dinghu Palace. The witch doctors used all kinds of prescriptions, but they could not cure his illness.
A man named You Shui Fagen wrote a letter saying: There was a wizard in Shangjun, and the ghosts and spirits possessed him when he was ill.
The emperor summoned him and placed him in Ganquan Palace.
When the wizard gets sick, he sends someone to ask the god.
Shenjun said: The emperor does not need to worry about his illness. When the illness is better, please cheer up and meet me in the sweet spring.
So the emperor's illness improved a lot. He went to Ganquan Palace to offer sacrifices in person, and his illness was completely cured.
The emperor granted pardon to the whole world and placed the divine king in the longevity palace.
The most noble among the gods is Taiyi, and his assistants are Da Jin, Siming, etc., who all follow him.
The appearance of these gods is invisible, but their voices can be heard, just like human voices.
Sometimes I go and sometimes I come, and when I come there is a rustling sound of wind.
The gods lived indoors in tents and sometimes spoke during the day, but often at night.
The emperor held a ceremony to eliminate disasters and evil spirits, and then entered the room.
The emperor regarded the wizard as his master and asked him to take care of the diet of the god.
After the king of gods said what he wanted, he handed it over to the people below for processing.
They also built the Longevity Palace and the North Palace, hung feather flags, furnished utensils for worshiping the gods, and welcomed the gods with noble etiquette.
The emperor ordered someone to record what the god said and named it "Painting".
But what the Lord God said was known to ordinary people, and there was nothing special about it, but the Emperor liked it alone.
These things are very secret and unknown to the world.
Three years later, the official in charge suggested that the year name should be named with the auspiciousness sent from heaven, instead of counting one or two.
The first year of the era is called Jianyuan, the second year of Jianyuan is called Yuanguang because of the long star flowing in the sky, and the third era is called Yuanshou because of the unicorn captured during the suburban festival.
In the winter of the next year, the emperor went to the outskirts of Yong County to offer sacrifices. He discussed with the ministers and said: Now I personally offer sacrifices to heaven in the outskirts of Yong County, but I have not yet worshiped Hou Tu, the God of Earth. This is inconsistent with etiquette.
The officials in charge discussed with Taishi Ling Sima Tan, ancestral official Kuanshu and others: The horns of the calf used to offer sacrifices to heaven and earth should be as small as silkworm cocoons and chestnuts.
Now your majesty personally offers sacrifices to Hou Tu. Hou Tu should build five altars on the circular high ground in the middle of the lake. Each altar should use a small ox to sacrifice to Dalao. After the sacrifice, all the sacrifices must be buried, and those who accompany the sacrifice must also wear yellow clothes.
So the emperor drove eastward, and in accordance with the method agreed upon by Kuan Shu and others, he erected the Houtu Temple on the high hill of Fenyin. The emperor personally looked at the Houtu and worshiped it, which was the same etiquette as offering sacrifices to heaven.
After the sacrifice, the emperor went to Xingyang and then returned to Chang'an.
summary: Various alchemists presented methods for worshipping gods, including Bo Youji's teachings on Taiyi, the most noble god. The emperor built altars and performed sacrifices accordingly. Later, a young man named General Wencheng claimed to summon spirits and was rewarded, but his methods eventually failed, and he was executed after being caught deceiving the emperor. The emperor fell ill but recovered after consulting a wizard in Ganquan Palace, where he built the Longevity Palace and continued worshipping gods. The emperor adopted year names based on auspicious signs, such as Yuanguang and Yuanshou. He performed the Hou Tu sacrifice at Fenyin and inspected various counties. Luan Da, recommended by Marquis Lecheng, claimed to have met immortals and was granted high honors, including marriage to a princess. However, his methods also failed, leading to his execution. The emperor continued seeking immortals, building temples and altars, and eventually performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices at Mount Tai in the first year of Yuanfeng.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪

translation:
In the south, there are statues such as the Jade Hall, the Bimen and the Divine Bird.
Shenming Terrace and Jinggan Tower were also built, both of which were more than fifty feet high, with driveways connecting the pavilions.
In the summer, the Han Dynasty reformed the calendar, using the first month of the lunar calendar as the beginning of the year. The color was still yellow, and the official seal was changed to five characters, so the era name was changed to the first year of Taichu.
This year, the Western Expedition to Dayuan was launched.
A massive locust plague occurred.
Mrs. Ding, Luoyang Yuchu and others used alchemy to offer sacrifices, and during the sacrifices, they begged ghosts and gods to bring disaster to the Xiongnu and Dawan.
The next year, officials in charge said that no cooked livestock or other sacrifices were used during the Wuju sacrifice in Yong County, and no fragrant fragrance appeared.
The emperor then ordered the ancestral officials to sacrifice cooked calves to the five emperors in the colors used for food, and use puppet horses instead of ponies as sacrifices.
Ponies were only used when offering sacrifices to the Five Emperors, and ponies were used when the emperor personally offered sacrifices in the countryside.
Those who used ponies to worship famous mountains and rivers were all replaced by puppet horses.
The emperor used ponies to offer sacrifices when he was on patrol.
Other etiquette are the same as before.
Another year later, the emperor traveled eastward, inspected the seaside, and examined things about gods and immortals, but nothing came true.
Some alchemists said that the purpose of building five cities and twelve towers during the Yellow Emperor's reign was to wait for the immortals during the execution period, which was called "welcoming the new year".
The emperor allowed it to be built as he said, calling it next year.
The emperor also put on yellow clothes and personally offered sacrifices to heaven according to the ceremony.
Gong Yingdai said: Although the Yellow Emperor held a ceremony for conferring Zen in Mount Tai, Feng Hou, Feng Ju and Qi Bo asked the Yellow Emperor to confer sacrifices on Mount Tai in the East and set up a place to offer sacrifices in Mount Fan to match Fu Rui, so that they could live forever.
The emperor ordered the preparation of sacrificial utensils, and when he came to Dongtai Mountain, he saw that Dongtai Mountain was short and incompatible with its reputation, so he ordered the ancestral officials to worship according to the etiquette and not hold a Zen ceremony.
Later, the public servants were ordered to offer sacrifices there and wait for the gods.
In the summer, the emperor returned to Mount Tai and held the five-year Zen ceremony. The etiquette was the same as before, with the addition of the etiquette of worshiping the land at Shilu Mountain.
Shilu Mountain is located to the south of the foot of Mount Tai. Many alchemists said that this is where immortals live, so the emperor personally worshiped it.
Five years later, the emperor went to Mount Tai to offer sacrifices, and on his way back he also offered sacrifices to Mount Chang.
When the emperor built the temples Taiyi and Houtu, the emperor himself would offer sacrifices in the suburbs every three years. The Han family's Zen system established by the emperor would be held every five years.
Bo Youji also petitioned to build five shrines, Taiyi, Sanyi, Mingyang, Maxing and Chixing, and the temple official Kuanshu held sacrificial ceremonies according to the prescribed time.
These five temples, together with Taiyi and Houtu Temples, total six temples, all of which are managed by Taizhu.
summary: The emperor established a system of suburban sacrifices every three years and Feng and Shan ceremonies every five years. Despite numerous efforts by alchemists to find immortals, none succeeded. The emperor grew tired of their claims but continued hoping to meet real immortals. Taishi Gong, who accompanied the emperor on his tours, recorded these events to reveal the true nature of the worship practices, noting that specific details of rituals were handled by the responsible officials.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/孝武本纪

translation:
Yin Qi's mother's name was Jian Di. She was the daughter of the You'u family and the second concubine of Emperor Ku.
Jian Di and three other people went to the river to take a bath. When they saw an egg dropped by a black bird, Jian Di picked it up and swallowed it. As a result, she became pregnant and gave birth to Qi.
When Qi grew up, he assisted Yu in flood control.
Emperor Shun then made an appointment deed and said: Now the common people are not in harmony and the relationship between the five ethics is not smooth. If you are to serve as Situ, you must respectfully promote the education of the five ethics and take generosity as the foundation.
The deed was sealed in Shang Land and given the surname Zi.
Qi arose in the era of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and Xia Yu. Its achievements were outstanding in the hearts of the people, and the people lived a stable life as a result.
After Qi's death, his son Zhaoming succeeded to the throne.
After Zhaoming's death, his son Xiangtu succeeded to the throne.
After Xiangtu died, his son Changruo succeeded to the throne.
After Chang Ruo died, his son Cao Yu succeeded to the throne.
After Cao Yu's death, his son Ming succeeded to the throne.
After Ming's death, his son Zhen succeeded to the throne.
After Zhen died, his son Wei succeeded to the throne.
After Wei's death, his son Baoding succeeded to the throne.
After Baoding died, his son Baoyi succeeded him.
After Bao Yi died, his son Bao B succeeded to the throne.
After Bao Bing died, his son Zhu Ren succeeded to the throne.
After the death of Zhu Ren, his son Zhu Gui succeeded to the throne.
After Zhugui died, his son Tianyi succeeded to the throne. This is the soup.
Chengtang, from Qi to Tang, had moved its capital eight times.
Chengtang wrote the "Emperor's Edict" for this purpose, reporting to Emperor Ku on the situation of moving the capital.
Chengtang was Fangbo in the Xia Dynasty and had the power to conquer the princes.
Ge Bo did not offer sacrifices to ghosts and gods, so Cheng Tang conquered him first.
Chengtang said: I have said this: People can see their own appearance from the water, and the state of governance of the country can be known from the mental outlook of the people. Yi Yin said: How wise!
Only when good words are heard can moral progress be made.
To govern the country and nurture the people, all those who are virtuous and do good deeds should be appointed as officials of the court. Work hard, work hard!
Chengtang said to Ge Bo: If you cannot respect the destiny of heaven, I will punish you severely without mercy.
So he wrote "Tang Zheng", recording the situation of Zheng Ge. Yiyin's name is Aheng.
A Heng wanted to meet Cheng Tang but had no way, so he went to serve as a married servant of the Youshen family. He carried a rice pot and chopping board and used the opportunity of talking about the taste of cooking to advise Cheng Tang and persuade him to practice the royal way.
Some people also say that Yi Yin was originally a hermit who was talented and virtuous but refused to be an official. Cheng Tang sent someone to hire him. After five trips, he agreed to follow Tang and tell Cheng Tang what the ancient emperors and the nine types of monarchs had done.
Chengtang then appointed him to manage the state affairs.
Yi Yin once left Shang Tang and went to the Xia capital. Because he saw the ugliness of the Xia Dynasty's lack of justice, he returned to Bo, the Shang capital.
When he entered the city from the north gate, he met Nu Jiu and Nv Fang, the virtuous ministers of Shang Tang, so he wrote "Nv Jiu" and "Nv Fang" to describe his feelings when he left the Xia Dynasty and returned to the Shang capital.
summary: Yin Qi's mother, Jian Di, was the daughter of the You'u family and the second concubine of Emperor Ku. While bathing in a river with three others, she swallowed an egg dropped by a black bird, became pregnant, and gave birth to Qi. Qi grew up to assist Yu in flood control. Emperor Shun appointed him as Situ to promote the education of the five ethics, sealed him in Shang Land, and gave him the surname Zi. Qi's achievements during the eras of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and Xia Yu brought stability to the people. After his death, his descendants succeeded him in a long lineage, culminating in Chengtang (Tang), who moved the capital eight times.

translation:
Chengtang went out and saw someone in the wild with a net set up on all sides. The person setting up the net prayed and said: May everything from heaven, everything from the earth, and everything from the four directions enter my net!
Chengtang heard this and said: Hey, this way we can catch all the animals!
So he asked the man to remove the three-sided net, and asked the person who set up the net to pray: If you want to go to the left, go to the left, and if you want to escape to the right, run to the right.
Anyone who disobeys orders will enter my snare.
When the princes heard about this, they all said: Tang Zhen is so kind and virtuous that even animals have been favored by him.
At that time, Xia Jie implemented a tyrannical rule and was immoral and immoral, and the princes Kunwu and his family were in trouble again.
Shang Tang then raised his troops and led the princes to conquer, and Yi Yin followed Tang. Shang Tang personally held a big ax to attack Kunwu, and then went to attack Xia Jie.
Shang Tang said: You people, come here and listen to me.
It's not that I dare to raise troops to cause trouble, it's because Xia Jie's crimes were extremely heinous. I also heard you say that Xia Jie was guilty.
I am afraid of God and dare not not conquer.
Now that Xia Jie has committed so many crimes, God ordered me to come and destroy him.
Now you people are all saying: Our king does not care about us and leaves our farm work behind, but goes to conquer and fight.
You also say: Xia Jie is guilty, so what can we do?
The king of Xia exhausted the country's people and stole the entire country's wealth.
The people of Xia State were lazy, passive, resentful and discordant. They all asked, "When will this sun perish?"
We would rather perish with you!
King Xia's virtue has reached this point, and now I must go to conquer him.
I hope you will join me in fulfilling the punishment sent by God, and I will reward you heavily.
Don't believe me, I will never fail to keep my word.
If you disobey my oath, I will punish you without mercy!
Shang Tang told these words to the chief messenger and wrote the "Tang Oath".
So Shang Tang said that I was very brave, so I was called King Wu.
Xia Jie was defeated in the old territory of the You'u family and fled to Mingtiao. The Xia army was defeated.
Shang Tang then attacked Sanke who were loyal to Xia Jie and seized their treasures, pearls and jade. Yibo and Zhongbo therefore wrote the "Dianbao", indicating that these were the fixed property of the country.
After Shang Tang defeated the Xia Dynasty, he wanted to replace the Xia Dynasty's social god. However, the social god was Zijulong, the ancient Gonggong clan. No one could compare with him, so he did not replace it. So he wrote "Xia She" to explain the reason why Xia She cannot be replaced.
Yi Yin reported this victory to Xiang. From then on, all the princes surrendered, and Shang Tang ascended to the throne of emperor and brought peace to the world.
Chengtang passed by Taijuan Tao on his way back, and the minister Zhong Hui made an edict.
Tang overthrew the Xia Dynasty, returned to the capital Bo, and wrote the "Tang Gao": In March of this year, King Yin personally arrived in the eastern suburbs.
Warning to all princes and kings: You must seek meritorious services for the people, and you must work hard to run your duties well.
Otherwise, I will punish you severely, so don’t blame me then.
summary: Chengtang, a Fangbo under the Xia Dynasty, first conquered Ge Bo for failing to offer sacrifices. He wrote "Tang Zheng" to record this. Yi Yin (Aheng) served Chengtang, either as a married servant or after being hired following five invitations. Yi Yin advised Chengtang on governance, left for the Xia capital, and returned to Bo, writing "Nv Jiu" and "Nv Fang." Chengtang's kindness was shown when he ordered a net set on all sides to be reduced to three, allowing animals to escape, which impressed the princes. Xia Jie's tyranny led Chengtang to raise troops, with Yi Yin following. Chengtang issued the "Tang Oath," defeated Xia Jie at Mingtiao, and conquered Sanke. He replaced the Xia social god but wrote "Xia She" to explain why it was not replaced. After the princes submitted, Chengtang ascended the throne, wrote "Tang Gao" to warn the princes, and revised the calendar to favor white.

translation:
He also said: In the past, Yu and Gaotao worked outside all year round. They established achievements for the people, and the people were able to live in peace.
They managed the Yangtze River in the east, the Jishui River in the north, the Yellow River in the west, and the Huai River in the south. They managed and dredged the four important rivers so that the people could live and work in peace and contentment.
Hou Ji taught the people to sow and cultivate, and then the people knew how to plant various crops.
All three of them served the people well, so their descendants were able to establish the country.
In the past, when Chi You and his ministers disturbed the people, God would not bless them. Such things really happened.
The teachings of the late king must be used to encourage yourself!
He also said: If any of you does something unethical and moral, then you will not be allowed to govern the people in the country. Then you should not resent me.
Tang warned the princes with these words.
Yi Yin wrote "Xian Yi De", explaining that monarchs and ministers should have pure moral character; Jiu Shan wrote "Ming Ju", which talked about the laws that the people should abide by.
Shang Tang then revised the calendar, changed the color of clothing, advocated white, and held court meetings during the day.
After the death of Shang Tang, the prince Taiding died before he ascended the throne, so Taiding's younger brother Waibing was made emperor. This was Emperor Waibing.
Emperor Waibing ascended the throne for three years. After his death, he made Waibing's younger brother Zhongren the emperor. This was Emperor Zhongren.
Four years after Zhongren ascended the throne, after his death, Yiyin supported Taiding's son Taijia as emperor.
Taijia, the eldest grandson of Chengtang, is Emperor Taijia.
In the first year of Taijia, Yi Yin wrote "Yi Xun", "Si Ming", and "Xu Hou", which stated what should be done according to the political and religious laws.
Emperor Taijia reigned for three years. His politics were unclear, his behavior was tyrannical, he did not abide by King Tang's laws, and his morals were corrupted. So Yi Yin exiled him to Tong Palace, where Tang is buried.
In the next three years, Yi Yin handled government affairs on behalf of the emperor, presided over state affairs, and accepted visits from princes.
Taijia lived in Tonggong for three years, reflected on and repented of his mistakes, and tried to be good again. So Yiyin welcomed Emperor Taijia back to the court and handed over the power to him.
Emperor Taijia practiced virtuous government, and the princes came to submit to the Yin and Shang Dynasties, and the people were peaceful.
Yi Yin admired Emperor Taijia very much, so he wrote three chapters of "Taijia Xun" to praise Emperor Taijia and called him Taizong.
After Taizong's death, his son Woding succeeded to the throne.
During the reign of Woding, Yi Yin passed away.
Yi Yin was buried in Bodi, so Jiu Shan wanted to use Yi Yin's deeds to instruct future generations, so he wrote "Woding".
When Woding died, his younger brother Tai Geng succeeded to the throne. This was Emperor Tai Geng.
After Taigeng died, his son Xiaojia came to the throne; after Emperor Xiaojia passed away, his younger brother Yongji succeeded to the throne, and this was Emperor Yongji.
At this time, the power of the Yin Dynasty had declined, and some princes stopped coming to court.
After Yong's death, his younger brother Taiwu came to the throne. This is Emperor Taiwu.
Taiwu appointed Yi Zhi as his prime minister.
At that time, there was a strange phenomenon of mulberry and mulberry trees growing together in the court hall in the capital, and they grew as thick as two hands together overnight.
summary: After Chengtang's death, his son Taiding died before ascending, so Waibing and then Zhongren ruled briefly. Yi Yin then supported Taijia, Chengtang's grandson. Taijia's tyranny led Yi Yin to exile him to Tong Palace for three years, during which Yi Yin governed. Taijia repented, returned to power, and practiced virtuous government, earning the title Taizong. After Taizong's death, Woding succeeded, and Yi Yin died. Subsequent rulers like Tai Geng, Yong Ji, and Tai Wu saw decline, but Tai Wu's appointment of Yi Zhi and response to a strange mulberry tree event revived Yin, earning him the title Zhongzong. Later rulers like Zhong Ding, Wai Ren, He Dan Jia, and Zu Yi saw further decline and revival, with Wu Xian playing a key role.

translation:
Wu Ding did not publish any political opinions for three years. Political matters were decided by Tsukasa, and he carefully observed the country's atmosphere.
Wu Ding dreamed of a saint named Shuo at night.
He observed the ministers and officials according to the appearance of the saint he saw in his dream, but none of them looked like the man in the dream.
So he sent hundreds of officials to search among the people, and finally found him in Fu Xian.
At that time, it was said that he was a slave working in Fuxian building roads.
The official brought the story to Wu Ding, and Wu Ding said it was this person.
After finding out the story, Wu Ding talked with him and found that he was really a sage, so he appointed him as the prime minister of the country, and the Yin country prospered in peace.
Therefore, the place name Fu Xian was used as the surname of Fu Shuo, and it became Fu Shuo.
Wu Ding offered sacrifices to the soup. The next day, a pheasant flew up and crowed on the ears of the tripod. Wu Ding was very frightened.
Zu Ji said: Your Majesty, don’t worry, let’s handle the political affairs first.
Zu Ji also taught Wu Ding: God examines the people of the world mainly to see whether they abide by morality. The life span given to humans by God may be long or short. It is not that God allows some people to die short-lived, but that they themselves end their lives midway.
Some people do not follow morals and do not obey judgments and punishments. God has decreed to correct their morals. Only then did he think of it and said: What should I do?
Alas, Your Majesty, you inherit the throne and treat the people respectfully. None of them are descendants of God. You must always offer sacrifices and do not worship those things that betray morality!
Wu Ding practiced virtuous government, and the people of the country were happy, and the Yin Dynasty prospered again.
Emperor Wu Ding passed away and his son Emperor Zu Geng came to the throne.
Zu Ji admired Wu Ding's virtuous administration because of the strange phenomenon of pheasants, built a temple for him, and called him Gaozong, so he wrote "Gaozong Xiri" and "Gaozong's Instructions".
Emperor Zu Geng passed away, and his younger brother Zu Jia came to the throne. This was Emperor Jia.
Emperor Jia became promiscuous and the Yin Dynasty declined again.
After the death of Emperor Jia, his son Lin Xin came to the throne.
Lin Xin died, and his younger brother Geng Ding came to the throne. This was Emperor Geng Ding.
After Geng Ding's death, his son Wu Yi came to the throne.
The capital of Yin State left Bo and moved to the north of the Yellow River.
Emperor Wu Yi was tyrannical and cruel. He made a puppet and called it a god.
He played chess with the puppet and let others make the moves for it.
If the god doesn't win, insult it.
He also made a leather pouch, filled it with blood, raised his head to the sky and shot arrows at it, calling it "shooting the sky".
Wu Yi went hunting between the Yellow River and the Wei River. There was a sudden thunder in the sky, and Wu Yi was killed.
His son Emperor Taiding ascended the throne.
After the death of Emperor Taiding, his son Yi came to the throne. When Emperor Yi came to the throne, the Yin Dynasty declined even more.
The eldest son of Emperor Yi was called Wei Ziqi. Qi's mother was of low status, so Qi was not qualified to inherit the throne.
Emperor Yi's youngest son was named Xin. Xin's mother was the queen, so Xin was appointed as his heir.
After the death of Emperor Yi, Xin succeeded to the throne. This was Emperor Xin, and the world called him Zhou.
summary: From Zhong Ding onward, succession disputes among brothers and sons caused nine generations of chaos, weakening Yin. Pan Geng moved the capital to Bo, Chengtang's former residence, and revived Yin by following Chengtang's decrees. After Pan Geng's death, Xiao Xin and Xiao Yi ruled weakly. Wu Ding, seeking to revive Yin, dreamed of a sage named Shuo, found him as a slave in Fu Xian, and appointed him prime minister, bringing prosperity. A pheasant crowing on a tripod during a sacrifice led Zu Ji to advise Wu Ding on morality, further strengthening Yin. Wu Ding was later called Gaozong.

translation:
When Xibo attacked the hungry country and destroyed it, Zuyi, the minister of Zhou, heard about it and resented Zhou. He was very frightened and went to Zhou to report: God has cut off the longevity of our Yin country. People who know good and bad luck use big tortoises for divination, but there are no good omens. It’s not that the late king didn’t protect our descendants, but that you, the great king, were licentious and tyrannical and cut yourself off from heaven. Therefore, God abandoned us, so that we can’t live in peace of mind. If we don’t understand God’s will, we can’t follow the ordinary laws. As a result, the people of our country all hope that the Yin Kingdom will perish. They say: Why doesn’t God show its majesty? Why haven’t God’s orders come yet?
Your Majesty, what do you want to do now?
Zhou said: Wasn't it that I was blessed by heaven when I was born?
After Zuyi returned home, he said: Zhou can no longer be persuaded!
After the death of Xibochang, King Wu of Zhou led his army to the east. When they arrived at Mengjin, the princes betrayed Yin and Zhou and came to join King Wu from eight hundred countries.
The princes all said: It's time to attack Zhou!
King Wu of Zhou said: You don’t know the destiny of heaven.
So the class teacher returned to China.
Zhou became even more promiscuous and had no end.
Wei Zi repeatedly advised Zhou, but Zhou refused to listen. Wei Zi discussed with the Grand Master and the Young Master and left Yin.
Bigan said: As a minister, I have to risk my life to advise.
So he tried his best to persuade Zhou.
Zhou was furious and said: I heard that the saint's heart has seven holes.
So he cut open Bigan's chest and took out his heart to see.
Jizi was frightened when he saw it, so he pretended to be crazy and became a slave. Zhou imprisoned Jizi again.
The grand masters and young masters of Yin State took the sacrificial vessels and musical instruments and fled to Zhou State in a hurry.
King Wu of Zhou led the princes to attack Yin Zhou.
Zhou also sent troops to resist the Zhou army in Muye.
On the day of Jiazi, Zhou's army was defeated. Zhou fled into the city, climbed to the deer platform, put on his precious jade clothes, ran to the fire and burned himself to death.
King Wu of Zhou cut off Zhou's head and hung it on a white flagpole.
King Zhou Wu executed Daji again, released the imprisoned Jizi, repaired Bigan's tomb, and commended Shang Rong's alleys.
He also enfeoffed Zhou's son Wu Geng and his father, allowing him to continue to worship Yin's ancestors and order him to implement Pan Geng's virtuous government. The people of Yin were very happy.
So King Wu of Zhou became the emperor.
Because descendants of the Yin and Shang dynasties devalued the title of emperor, he was called king.
King Wu of Zhou made the descendants of Yin princes and subordinated them to Zhou.
After the death of King Wu of Zhou, Wu Geng, Uncle Guan, and Uncle Cai launched a rebellion. King Cheng of Zhou ordered Zhou Gongdan to kill them, and made Wei Zi the king of the Song Dynasty to continue the incense of the Yin Dynasty.
Tai Shigong said: I compiled the deeds of the Deed based on "Song of Shang". Since the Tang Dynasty, many historical facts have been collected from "Shang Shu" and "The Book of Songs".
summary: After Wu Ding's death, Zu Geng and Zu Jia ruled, with Zu Jia's promiscuity causing decline. Subsequent rulers like Lin Xin, Geng Ding, and Wu Yi saw further decline. Wu Yi's cruelty, including making a puppet and shooting a blood-filled pouch, led to his death by lightning. His son Tai Ding and then Yi ruled, with Yi's son Xin (Zhou) succeeding. Zhou was talented but tyrannical, indulging in debauchery with Daji, increasing taxes, and inventing the Pao Ge torture. He killed Jiu Hou and E Hou, imprisoned Xibo (later King Wen), who was released after bribes. Xibo practiced virtuous governance, attracting princes. Zhou's minister Bigan was killed for advising, and Jizi was imprisoned. King Wu of Zhou led a revolt, defeated Zhou at Muye, and Zhou burned himself to death. King Wu executed Daji, released Jizi, and enfeoffed Zhou's son Wu Geng. Later, Wu Geng rebelled, and King Cheng made Wei Zi the king of Song to continue Yin's lineage.

translation:
The First Emperor of Qin was the son of King Zhuangxiang of Qin.
When King Zhuang Xiang was a hostage of Qin in Zhao, he saw Lu Buwei's concubine and liked her very much, so he married her and gave birth to the first emperor.
The First Emperor was born in Handan in the first month of the forty-eighth year of King Zhao of Qin.
When he was born, he was named Zheng and his surname was Zhao.
At the age of thirteen, King Zhuang Xiang died, and Zheng succeeded him as King of Qin.
At that time, the Qin State had annexed Ba, Shu, and Hanzhong, crossed Wan, occupied Ying, and established Nanjun; went north to the east of Shangjun, and occupied Hedong, Taiyuan, and Shangdang counties; east to Rongyang, eliminated the Western Zhou and Eastern Zhou Dynasties, and established Sanchuan County.
Lu Buwei became prime minister, granted a fief of 100,000 households, and was named Marquis Wenxin.
Recruiting guests and tourists, intending to annex the world.
Li Si was Shiren, and Meng Ao, Wang Jue, Hegong and others were generals.
The King of Qin was young and in the early days of his accession to the throne, state affairs were left to the ministers.
Jinyang rebelled, and in the first year of Qin Wangzheng's reign, General Meng Ao put down the rebellion.
In the second year, Duke He led his army to attack Juanyi and killed 30,000 people.
In three years, Meng Ao attacked South Korea and captured thirteen cities.
Wang Ye is dead.
In the tenth month, General Meng Ao attacked Wei's Yi and Yougui.
This year the food harvest failed.
In four years, he conquered Yi and Yougui.
In March, the troops were withdrawn.
The hostages of Qin returned from Zhao, and the prince of Zhao left Qin and returned to Zhao.
In October Gengyin, locusts flew from the east and covered the sky.
Plague in the world.
The common people paid a thousand stones of corn to pay one level of nobility.
In the fifth year, General Meng Ao attacked the Wei State and pacified the cities of Suanzao, Yanyi, Xuyi, Changping, Yongqiu, and Shanyang. They all conquered them by force, and captured twenty cities in total.
Start setting up East County.
Thunder in winter.
In six years, South Korea, Wei, Zhao, Wei, and Chu attacked Qin together and captured Shouling.
Qin sent troops, and the armies of the five countries withdrew.
The Qin State conquered the Wei State and invaded Dongjun. Wei Junjiao led his relatives to move to Yewang, relying on the mountain dangers to defend the Hanoi area within the Wei State.
In seven years, the comet first appeared in the east. Appeared again in the north. Appears in the West in May.
General Meng Ao died.
It was because he attacked Longyi, Guyi and Qingdu, and then returned to attack Jiyi.
The comet appeared in the west for another sixteen days.
Queen Mother Xia is dead.
In the eighth year, Zhao Chengyu, the younger brother of King Zhao Zheng of Qin, led an army to attack Zhao. Tunliu rebelled. As a result, all his officers were killed and the people there were moved to Lintao.
The general who came to attack Cheng Xi died, and the soldier Pu Hao who stayed in the camp rebelled again and died in battle. After his death, he was tortured by whipping his body.
Fish from the Yellow River rushed to the shore in large numbers, and people drove carriages to the east to find food.
Lao Ai was granted the title of Marquis Changxin.
Give him the Shanyang region to live in.
There are no restrictions on Lao Ai in terms of palaces, carriages and horses, clothing, gardens, and hunting.
summary: The First Emperor of Qin, son of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, was born Zheng in Handan in the first month of the forty-eighth year of King Zhao of Qin. At thirteen, he succeeded as King of Qin after his father's death. The Qin state had already expanded significantly, annexing territories like Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and establishing commanderies. Lu Buwei served as prime minister, with Li Si as a retainer and Meng Ao, Wang Jue, and others as generals. Due to the king's youth, state affairs were managed by ministers. In the early years of his reign, Qin faced rebellions and military campaigns. Meng Ao suppressed a revolt in Jinyang and later attacked Wei, capturing twenty cities. The king faced challenges including a locust plague, famine, and a coalition attack from five states. In the eighth year, Lao Ai was granted the title of Marquis Changxin and given extensive authority. The following year, his conspiracy to rebel was discovered, leading to a battle in Xianyang. Lao Ai was captured, and his followers were executed or exiled. Lu Buwei was removed as prime minister due to his involvement.

translation:
At this time, Li Si was in charge of the government.
In the eleventh year, Wang Jian, Huan , and Yang Duanhe attacked Ye Yi and captured nine cities.
Wang Jian attacked Dinglanyu and Puyang, and combined all the soldiers into one army.
Wang Jian took command of the entire army. After eighteen days, he deported the useless personnel in the army who were below the level of fighting, and elected two out of ten people to join the army. Huan  led the troops to capture Yeyi and Puyang.
In the twelfth year, Wenxinhou Lu Buwei died and was buried privately.
If Lu Buwei's family members come to mourn, if they are Jin people, they will be expelled; if they are Qin people, those with a salary of more than 600 shi will have their title removed and moved away from their old residence. If no one comes to mourn him with a salary of less than 500 shi, they will also move away from their old residence without losing their title.
From then on, those who govern the country's political affairs, like Lao Ai and Lu Buwei, are rebellious and unruly, and their whole family will be confiscated, and they will be dealt with in this way.
In autumn, Lao'ai's family members who were supposed to move to Shu were pardoned.
At that time, there was a severe drought for six months, and it didn't rain until August.
In the thirteenth year, Huan  attacked Pingyang of the State of Zhao, killed the general of the State of Zhao, Hu Zou, and beheaded 100,000 people.
King Zhao fled to Henan.
In the first month of the year, comets appear in the east.
In October, Huan  attacked Zhao.
In the fourteenth year, he attacked the Zhao army in Pingyang, captured Yi'an, defeated the Zhao army and killed its general.
Huan  pacified Pingyang and Wucheng.
Han Fei went to Qin as an envoy, and Qin adopted Li Si's plan and detained Han Fei in Qin. Han Fei died in Yunyang.
The King of Han requested to be a vassal of Qin.
In the fifteenth year, the State of Qin sent out a large number of troops. One army arrived in Yeyi and another army arrived in Taiyuan and captured Langmeng.
An earthquake occurs.
In September of the 16th year, troops were sent to take over the Nanyang area of ​​South Korea, and Teng temporarily acted as the county governor.
Men were ordered to register their age.
Wei State donated land to Qin State.
Qin established Liyi.
In the seventeenth year, Neishiteng attacked South Korea, captured Han Wangan, annexed all South Korean territory, and set up a county in its territory, named Yingchuan.
An earthquake occurs.
Queen Mother Huayang died.
The people suffered from severe famine.
In the eighteenth year, a large number of troops were sent to attack the State of Zhao. Wang Jian led the soldiers from Shangdi to capture Jingxing. Yang Duanhe led the Hanoi soldiers, Qiang Yu also led his army to attack Zhao, and Yang Duanhe besieged Handan City.
In the 19th year, Wang Jian and Qiang You all captured and pacified the Dongyang area of ​​​​Zhao and captured the king of Zhao.
He led his troops to prepare to attack Yan State and stationed his troops in Zhongshan.
When the King of Qin came to Handan, he killed all those who had a grudge against his mother's family when he was born in the State of Zhao.
The King of Qin returned to Qin from Taiyuan and Shangjun.
The Empress Dowager, the mother of the First Emperor, passed away.
summary: The king implemented policies to strengthen Qin, including expelling guest officials, though Li Si's counsel led to the revocation of this order. Wei Liao advised bribing enemy officials, a strategy the king adopted. Military campaigns continued, with Wang Jian and others attacking Zhao and capturing cities. In the seventeenth year, Qin conquered Han, establishing Yingchuan Commandery. The conquest of Zhao followed, with the king personally executing those who had wronged his mother's family in Handan.

translation:
Prince Jia of the State of Zhao led several hundred people from his clan to Dai, proclaimed himself King of Dai, and united with the army of the State of Yan eastward, stationed in Shanggu.
A severe famine occurred during this year.
Twenty years ago, Crown Prince Dan of Yan State was worried about Qin's army coming to Yan State. He was panic-stricken and sent Jing Ke to assassinate the King of Qin.
The King of Qin noticed this, dismembered Jing Ke's body and paraded it to the public, and sent Wang Jian and Xin Sheng to attack Yan.
Yan and Dai sent troops to attack the Qin army, and the Qin army defeated the Yan army west of Yishui.
In the twenty-first year, Wang Ben attacked Jingdi.
He dispatched more soldiers to Wang Jian's army, defeated Prince Yan's army, captured Jicheng of Yan State, and obtained Prince Dan's head.
King Yan went east to gather troops from Liaodong and proclaimed himself king there.
Wang Jian excused himself from illness and retired to his hometown. Xinzheng rebelled.
Lord Changping moved to Yingdi.
It snowed heavily, the snow was two feet five inches deep.
In the 22nd year, Wang Ben attacked Wei and dug ditches to divert water from the river to flood Daliang. The city wall of Daliang was destroyed. King Wei asked for surrender, and Qin occupied all Wei territory.
In the twenty-third year, the King of Qin recruited Wang Jian again, insisted on using him, and sent him to lead the army to attack Jing State.
They captured the area from the south of Chendi to Pingyu and captured King Jing.
The king of Qin arrived at Yingchen on his parade.
Jing general Xiang Yan established Lord Changping as King of Jing and raised troops south of the Huai River to rebel against Qin.
In the twenty-fourth year, Wang Jian and Meng Wu attacked Jingdi and defeated the Jing army. Lord Changping died in the battle, and Xiang Yan committed suicide.
In the twenty-fifth year, he sent out a large number of troops, sent Wang Ben as general, led the army to attack the Liaodong area of ​​Yan State, and captured King Xi of Yan.
He returned to attack the state of Dai and captured Dai Wangjia.
Wang Jian pacified the Jiangnan area of ​​Jing State, surrendered Yuejun, and established Kuaiji County.
In May, the whole world gathers for a feast.
In the twenty-sixth year, King Jian of Qi and Prime Minister Housheng of Qi dispatched troops to defend the western border and not to have any contact with Qin.
Qin State sent general Wang Bi from Yan State to the south to attack Qi State and captured Qi Wang Jian.
Qin had just annexed the world and ordered the prime minister and censor to say: Some time ago, the king of Han handed over the land, dedicated the king's seal, and asked to become a vassal. Soon he broke the agreement and joined forces with Zhao and Wei to betray Qin, so I raised an army to attack and captured the king of South Korea.
I thought this was a good thing, and we could probably stop fighting.
King Zhao sent his prime minister Li Mu to sign the treaty, so he sent back his son who was a hostage.
Soon the State of Zhao betrayed the alliance and raised an army to resist in Taiyuan, our country, so I launched an army to attack and captured its king.
Prince Jia of Zhao established himself as the acting king, so I sent troops to destroy him. King Wei initially agreed to surrender to Qin, but soon conspired with South Korea and Zhao to attack Qin. Qin officials went to attack and destroyed Wei.
King Jing offered the land west of Qingyang, but soon broke the agreement and attacked Nanjun of our country. So I sent troops to attack, captured the king of Jing, and pacified the land of Jing.
The King of Yan was fatuous and chaotic, and his Crown Prince Dan secretly ordered Jing Ke to be an assassin. The officials of Qin went to attack him and destroyed his country.
The King of Qi adopted the strategy of victory later and did not allow the Qin envoys to enter the Qi State. He planned to raise troops to cause chaos. I sent officers to attack, captured the King of Qi, and pacified the Qi State.
With my insignificant body, I sent out troops to suppress the rebellion. Relying on the power of the ancestral temple, the kings of the six countries have all accepted their crimes, and the world is completely peaceful.
summary: The assassination attempt by Jing Ke of Yan failed, leading to Qin's attack on Yan. Wang Jian and others captured Yan's capital and obtained Prince Dan's head. Wei was conquered by diverting rivers to flood Daliang. Jing (Chu) was attacked, with Wang Jian capturing King Jing. Xiang Yan's rebellion was suppressed, and by the twenty-fifth year, Yan, Dai, and Qi were all conquered, unifying China.
