translation:
If we don't change the name now, we can't praise the achievements of the establishment and pass them on to future generations.
Please agree on an imperial title.
Prime Minister Wang Wan, Imperial Censor Feng Jie, and Tingwei Li Si all said: In the past, the Five Emperors governed an area thousands of miles square. Outside this area, some princes paid tribute and some princes did not pay tribute, so the emperor could not control them.
Now His Majesty is dispatching rebels to punish thieves, pacify the world, set up counties and counties within the four seas, and unify laws. This has never happened since ancient times, and it is beyond the reach of the five emperors.
We discussed it carefully with the doctors, and they all said that in ancient times, there were emperors of heaven, emperors of earth, and emperors of Thailand, and the emperor of Thailand was the noblest.
We risked the death penalty to offer our title, and the king was called "Emperor of Thailand".
The emperor's order is called "Zhi", the emperor's order is called "Zhao", and the emperor calls himself "Zhen".
The King of Qin said: Remove the word "Tai" and leave the word "huang". Use the ancient word "emperor" to express status and title, and call it "emperor".
Other opinions as agreed.
Give the order and say: OK.
Pursuing King Zhuang Xiang as the Supreme Emperor.
The emperor issued an order and said: I heard that in ancient times, there were titles but no posthumous titles. In the Middle Ages, there were titles. Posthumous titles were determined after death based on the deeds during life.
Doing this means that the son will talk about his father and the ministers will talk about the king. This is very meaningless. I will not adopt this approach.
From then on, the posthumous law was abolished.
I am the First Emperor.
Counting the descendants, from the second and third generations to the ten thousand generations, the inheritance will be endless.
The First Emperor deduced based on the order of succession of the five virtues, and believed that the Zhou Dynasty obtained the fire virtue, and the Qin Dynasty replaced the fire virtue of the Zhou Dynasty. Following the law of the victory of the five elements, the water virtue should now be the beginning.
At the beginning of October, the first month of the new year, a group of ministers came to the court to celebrate. Clothes, banners, and festival flags are all black.
Six is ​​used as the standard for number, the talisman and the dharma crown are all six inches, the chariot is six feet wide, the steps are six feet, and the chariot is driven by six horses.
The river was renamed Deshui as the beginning of water virtue.
Being tough and decisive in politics, being violent and harsh, deciding everything in accordance with the law, being harsh and severe, without kindness, kindness, warmth and morality, this is in line with the principles of the evolution of the Five Virtues.
So the law was strict and criminals who had been imprisoned for a long time were not pardoned.
Prime Minister Wang Wan and others suggested: The princes of various countries have just been wiped out, and the lands of Yan, Qi, and Jing are far away. If there is no king there, there will be no one to pacify Yan, Qi, and Jing.
Please make the emperor's sons kings, hoping to get the emperor's approval.
The First Emperor submitted Wang Wan and others' suggestions to the ministers for discussion, and they all thought it was appropriate.
Tingwei Li Si suggested: King Wen of Zhou and King Wu of Zhou had many children with the same surname. However, later on, the clansmen became estranged and attacked each other like enemies. The princes fought against each other and the emperor of Zhou could not stop them.
Now, relying on His Majesty's spirit, the world has been unified and divided into counties and counties. The emperor's children and meritorious officials are heavily rewarded with state taxes, making it easy to govern.
There is no two minds in the world. This is the way to stabilize the country.
It is not appropriate to create feudal lords.
The First Emperor said: The world is suffering from endless wars because of the princes and kings. Relying on the spirit of the ancestral temple, we have just pacified the world and then established the princely states. This is creating enemies for ourselves, and seeking peace is not very difficult!
Tingwei's suggestion is correct.
Divide the country into thirty-six counties, with guards, lieutenants, and prisons in each county.
The people renamed it Qianshou.
summary: The king declared himself the First Emperor, abolishing posthumous titles and establishing a system of succession for ten thousand generations. He adopted water virtue, with black as the color, six as the standard, and harsh laws. The empire was divided into thirty-six commanderies, with unified laws, weights, measures, and writing. Wealthy families were moved to Xianyang, and palaces were built imitating those of conquered states.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪

translation:
The First Emperor fought with Poseidon in his dream, and Poseidon looked like a human being.
I asked the doctor who divined dreams, and the doctor said: The water god cannot be seen, and his signs are represented by big fish and mosquito dragons.
Now your Majesty is thoughtful and respectful in your prayers and sacrifices, but this vicious sea god has appeared. He should be eradicated, and then the good god can come.
So he asked those who went to the sea to carry equipment for catching big fish, while he used a repeating crossbow to wait for the big fish to appear and shoot it to death.
From Langye to the north to Rongcheng Mountain, no big fish was seen.
When he arrived at Zhifu, he saw big fish and shot one to death.
So we headed west along the coast.
He fell ill when he arrived in Pingyuanjin.
The First Emperor hated talking about death, and no one among his ministers dared to mention it.
The First Emperor's illness worsened day by day, so he wrote an edict with the emperor's seal to his son Fusu, saying: Come back to attend my funeral and bury me together in Xianyang.
The edict had been sealed and placed at the place where Zhao Gao, the commander of the Zhongche Mansion, was in charge of the seal and talisman affairs instead of Fu Xilang. It was not sent to the envoy responsible for delivering it.
In July Bingyin, the First Emperor died on the sand dune platform.
Because the First Emperor died outside, Prime Minister Li Si was afraid that the First Emperor's sons and the people in the country would cause trouble, so he blocked the news and did not hold a funeral.
The coffin was placed in a rolling carriage, accompanied by the eunuchs who were close to him, and meals were delivered as usual wherever he went.
The officials reported state affairs as before, and the eunuchs approved what they reported from their carriages.
Only the First Emperor's sons Hu Hai, Zhao Gao and five or six close eunuchs knew that the First Emperor was dead.
Zhao Gao used to teach Hu Hai writing and prison laws, and Hu Hai was very close to him in private.
Zhao Gao conspired with Prince Hu Hai and Prime Minister Li Si to defeat the imperial edict sealed by the First Emperor and sent it to Prince Fusu. At the same time, he falsely claimed that Prime Minister Li Si was in the sand dunes to accept the imperial edict from the First Emperor and make his son Hu Hai the crown prince.
He also wrote another edict to the young masters Fusu and Mengtian, listing their crimes and ordering them to commit suicide.
These things are recorded in "The Biography of Li Si".
Hu Hai and others continued to move forward, so they arrived at Jiuyuan from Jingxing.
Just in time for the hot weather, the First Emperor's carriages started to smell bad, so he ordered the officials to load each carriage with a stone of abalone to mix up the stench of the First Emperor's body.
Hu Hai and others returned to Xianyang from Zhidao and announced the death of the First Emperor.
Prince Hu Hai succeeded to the throne and became the second emperor.
In September, the First Emperor was buried in Mount Li.
When the First Emperor first came to the throne, he dug caves in Mount Li. After unifying the country, he sent more than 700,000 prisoners from all over the world to Mount Li. He dug tunnels until they reached the water, sealed them with copper, and then placed coffins inside. Imitation palaces, hundreds of palaces, and various rare treasures were moved in and filled with treasures.
Let the craftsman make a crossbow with a mechanism. When someone digs a grave and approaches the tomb, it will automatically shoot at the target.
Use mercury to make thousands of rivers, hundreds of streams, rivers and seas, and use machinery to permeate and circulate each other. All kinds of celestial phenomena are complete above the tomb, and there are thousands of scenes on the ground below. The fat of the mermaid is used as a candle, and it is estimated that it will not be extinguished for a long time.
summary: The First Emperor toured extensively, erecting stone tablets praising his achievements. He sought immortality, sending Xu Shi with boys and girls to find the elixir. He burned books and buried Confucian scholars alive, enforcing strict laws. The construction of the Epang Palace and the Lishan tomb involved hundreds of thousands of workers. The emperor's death was concealed, and a forged edict made Hu Hai the Second Emperor, forcing Fusu to commit suicide.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪

translation:
Now that the six countries have established their own political power, Qin's territory is shrinking day by day, but it is still claiming the title of emperor in vain. This is unacceptable.
It is more appropriate to be king as in the past.
He made the son of his second brother, Gong Ziying, the king of Qin.
The second generation was buried in Yichun Garden in the south of Du County with common people's rites.
Zhao Gao asked Ziying to fast, visit his ancestors in the ancestral temple, and receive the seal of King Qin.
After fasting for five days, Ziying discussed with his two sons: Prime Minister Zhao Gao killed the second son in Wangyi Palace. He was afraid that the officials would punish him, so he pretended to make me king in the name of righteousness.
I heard that Zhao Gao made an agreement with Chu that he would destroy the Qin clan and become king in Guanzhong.
Now they ask me to fast and visit the ancestral temple. They want to kill me while I am in the ancestral temple.
I told him that if he didn't go away if he was ill, the prime minister would come to me personally and kill him when he came.
Zhao Gao sent people several times to invite Ziying, but Ziying refused to go. Zhao Gao came in person and said, "Visiting the ancestral temple is a big event. Why doesn't the king go?"
Ziying stabbed Zhao Gao to death in the fasting palace, executed all three members of Zhao Gao's family, and showed them to the public in Xianyang.
Ziying was the king of Qin for forty-six days. The Chu general Pei Gong defeated the Qin army, entered Wuguan, came to Bashang, and sent people to ask Ziying to surrender.
Ziying tied his neck with a ribbon, rode on a white horse, held the emperor's seal and talisman, and surrendered beside Zhi Road.
So Pei Gong entered Xianyang, closed the official offices and treasury, and returned to the army. More than a month passed.
The armies of various princes arrived, and Xiang Yu, the leader of the alliance, killed Ziying and the clan of Prince Qin.
Xianyang was massacred, the palaces were burned, the sons and women of Qin were captured, the treasures were plundered, and the princes divided them among themselves.
After the Qin State was eliminated, its land was divided into three parts, named King Yong, King Sai, and King Zhai, known as the Three Qins.
Xiang Yu was the overlord of Western Chu and was responsible for dividing the world's princes and kings. The Qin Dynasty finally perished.
Five years later, the Han Dynasty unified the country.
Tai Shigong said: Boyi, the ancestor of the Qin State, had made great achievements during the Tang and Yu periods, acquired land, and was given the surname Ying.
Between Xia and Yin, the power was weakened and dispersed.
When the Zhou Dynasty declined, the Qin State emerged and built a city in Xicui.
Since Duke Mu, he has gradually encroached on the princes, and the unification project was finally completed by the First Emperor.
The First Emperor believed that his merits exceeded those of the Five Emperors, and his territory was broader than the Three Kings, and he was ashamed to be compared with the Three Kings and Five Emperors.
Jia Sheng's discussion is very good. He said:
Qin annexed various vassal states and more than thirty counties in Shandong, repaired and managed Jindu and passes, occupied dangerous passes and fortresses, trained troops, and defended them.
summary: The Second Emperor's reign was marked by cruelty and rebellion. Chen She's uprising spread, and Zhang Han suppressed it with convicts. Zhao Gao gained power, killing officials and princes. The Second Emperor was eventually forced to commit suicide by Zhao Gao's agents. Ziying, made king, killed Zhao Gao but soon surrendered to Liu Bang. Xiang Yu killed Ziying and the Qin clan, burning Xianyang. The Qin dynasty ended after 610 years from Duke Xiang to the Second Emperor.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/秦始皇本纪

translation:
The ancestor of Qin was the granddaughter of a descendant of Emperor Zhuanxu, named Nuxiu.
While the nun was weaving, a swallow dropped an egg. The nun swallowed it and gave birth to a son.
Daye married a daughter of the Shaodian tribe, named Nuhua.
Nuhua gave birth to Dafei, who assisted Xia Yu in managing the soil and water.
After the flood control was successful, Emperor Shun gave Yu a black jade gui in recognition of his contribution.
Yu accepted the reward and said: "I can't control the floods alone, and it's also because I have a lot of money to serve as an assistant." Emperor Shun said: Ah!
Dafei, you helped Yu successfully control the flood! I will give you a black flag pendant.
Your descendants will prosper.
Therefore, the beautiful woman named Yao was given to him as his wife.
Da Fei worshiped and accepted the reward, and helped Shun tame birds and beasts. Many birds and beasts were tamed, and this person was Bai Yi.
Shun gave him the surname Ying.
Da Fei had two sons: one was named Dalian, the ancestor of the Niaosu family; the other was named Ruomu, the ancestor of the Fei family.
Ruomu's great-great-grandson was called Fei Chang. Some of his descendants lived in the Central Plains and some in Yidi.
When Fei Changsheng was Xia Jie, he left Xia and went to Shang. He drove for Shang Tang and defeated Xia Jie at Mingtiao.
Dalian's great-great-grandsons were named Meng Xi and Zhong Yan. Zhong Yan looked like a bird and could speak human language.
When Emperor Taiwu heard about it, he asked someone to divine it, and the result was that he would be lucky to drive the car for him, so he invited him to drive the car and marry him a wife.
Since Taiwu, the descendants of Zhongyan have served the Yin State for generations, so many of the Ying surnames have become famous in the world and have become princes.
Zhong Yan's great-great-grandson was named Zhong Yan, who lived in the Xirong area and defended Xicui.
Feilian was born in Zhongyi.
Feilian was born evil.
When evil comes, he has great strength, but Fei is honest and good at running. Father and son both serve King Zhou of Yin with their bravery.
King Wu of Zhou defeated Zhou and killed the evil ones together.
Feilian went to the north as an envoy to Zhou. When he came back, because Zhou was dead and there was no place to report, he built an altar in Huotai Mountain to report to King Zhou. During the sacrifice, he received a stone coffin with an inscription that said: The angel Chufu survived the rebellion of the Yin Dynasty and gave you the stone coffin to glorify the clan.
After Feilian died, he was buried in Huo Taishan.
Feilian also had a son named Ji Sheng.
Ji Sheng gave birth to Meng Zeng.
Meng Zeng was favored by King Zhou Cheng and was entrusted to Gaolang.
Meng Zeng gave birth to Father Heng. Hengfu gave birth to Zaofu.
Zaofu was favored by King Mu of Zhou because he was good at driving. King Mu of Zhou obtained horses named Chiji, Pirates, Hualiu, Luo'er, etc., and drove them to the west for inspections. He was so happy that he never returned.
When King Xu Yan rebelled, Zaofu drove King Mu for a long time, traveling thousands of miles in a day, and rushed back to Zhou to put down the rebellion.
King Mu granted the city of Zhao to Zaofu, and the Zaofu family was called the Zhao family from then on.
From the fifth generation of Ji Shengzhuan, the birth of Feilian, he came to Zaofu and began to live in Zhaocheng separately.
Zhao Shuai is his descendant.
Erelaige was Feilian's son and died young.
He has a son named Nvfang.
Nüfang gave birth to Pang Gao, Pang Gao gave birth to Tai Ji, Tai Ji gave birth to Da Luo, and Da Luo gave birth to Feizi.
They were all favored by Zaofu and lived in Zhaocheng with the surname Zhao.
Feizi lived in Quanqiu. He loved horses and other livestock and was good at raising and breeding them.
The people in Quanqiu told King Xiao of Zhou about this, and King Xiao summoned Feizi and asked him to manage the horses between the Mihe and Weihe rivers.
Horses were bred in large numbers. King Xiao wanted Feizi to be Daluo's heir.
summary: The ancestor of Qin originated from Nuxiu, a granddaughter of Emperor Zhuanxu's descendant. While weaving, Nuxiu swallowed a swallow's egg and gave birth to Daye. Daye married Nuhua, who gave birth to Dafei. Dafei assisted Yu in flood control, and Emperor Shun rewarded him, granting him the surname Ying and a wife. Dafei's descendants included Feilian and Elai, who served King Zhou of Yin. When King Wu of Zhou defeated Zhou, Elai was killed, while Feilian died later and was buried on Huotai Mountain. Feilian's son Jisheng began a lineage that produced Zaofu, who was favored by King Mu of Zhou for his driving skills. Zaofu drove King Mu westward and later rushed back to suppress a rebellion, earning the city of Zhao as his fief, establishing the Zhao family. Feizi, a descendant, lived in Quanqiu and excelled at raising horses. King Xiao of Zhou appointed him to manage horses, and later granted him the land of Qin as a vassal state, known as Qin Ying. Qin Ying's descendants included Qin Hou, Qin Zhong, and Zhuang Gong. Qin Zhong was killed by Xirong, but his son Zhuang Gong, with Zhou's help, defeated Xirong. Zhuang Gong's son Xiang Gong succeeded him. The Grand Historian noted that Qin's ancestors were surnamed Ying, with descendants scattered across various states, taking their fiefs as surnames. Qin was granted Zhao City due to Zaofu, so they were also called the Zhao family.

translation:
Marquis Shen's daughter was Da Luo's wife. She gave birth to a son, Cheng, who became his heir.
Marquis Shen said to King Xiao: "In the past, my ancestor was the daughter of Lishan. She became the wife of Xuxuan, the great-grandson of Zhongyan of the Xirong tribe, and gave birth to Zhongyi. Because she was in love with the Zhou Dynasty, she joined the Zhou Dynasty and guarded the western border. Therefore, the western border was harmonious and peaceful."
Now I will marry my daughter to Da Luo and give birth to an heir.
The Marquis of Shen and Da Luo marry again, and all the Xirong tribe submits. Only in this way can you be crowned king.
I hope you will consider it.
Then King Xiao said: In the past, Boyi was in charge of livestock for Emperor Shun, and his livestock multiplied a lot, so he was granted a land grant and given the surname Ying.
Now his descendants are also taming and breeding horses for me, and I will also give them land as a vassal state.
He was given the land of Qin as a fief, and asked him to take over the sacrifices of the Ying family, known as Qin Ying.
But he did not abolish the son born from the daughter of Marquis Shen as the heir of Daluo, so as to reconcile with Xirong.
Qin Ying gave birth to Qin Hou.
The Marquis of Qin died after ten years in office.
The Marquis of Qin gave birth to an uncle.
The uncle died after three years in office.
The uncle gave birth to Qin Zhong.
In the third year of Qin Zhong's reign, King Li of Zhou was immoral, and some princes rebelled.
Xirong also rebelled against the royal family and destroyed the Daluo clan who lived in Quanqiu.
After King Xuan of Zhou ascended the throne, he appointed Qin Zhong as a doctor to attack Xirong.
Xirong killed Qin Zhong.
Twenty-three years after Qin Zhong ascended the throne as Houwang, he died in the hands of Xirong.
Qin Zhong had five sons, the eldest son was named Zhuang Gong.
King Xuan of Zhou summoned the five Zhuang Gong brothers and gave them 7,000 soldiers. He ordered them to attack Xirong and defeated Xirong.
King Xuan of Zhou then rewarded Qin Zhong's descendants again, including the fiefdom of their ancestor Daluo, Quanqiu, and appointed them as officials of Xicui.
Zhuang Gong lived in Quanqiu, Xixi, Daluo's hometown. He had three sons. The eldest son was called Shifu.
Shifu said: Xirong killed my grandfather Qin Zhong. I will never enter the city until I kill the king of Rong.
So he led his troops to attack Xirong and gave up the position of heir to his younger brother Xiang Gong.
Therefore, Duke Xiang was established as the crown prince.
Duke Zhuang died in his forty-fourth year, and Prince Xiang Gong came to the throne.
In the first year of Xiang AD, Duke Xiang married his sister Miao Ying to King Feng as his wife.
In the second year of Duke Xiang, the Xirong besieged Quanqiu. Shifu fought against him and was finally captured by the Rong.
After more than a year, the Rong people released Shifu again.
In the spring of the seventh year, King You of Zhou appointed Bao Si as his queen, deposed him as the crown prince, and instead appointed Bao Si's son as the crown prince. He broke trust with the princes many times, so the princes rebelled.
Quan Rong of Xirong and Shen Hou attacked the Zhou Dynasty together and killed King You at the foot of Mount Li.
Qin Xianggong led his troops to rescue the Zhou Dynasty, fought effectively and achieved military exploits.
In order to avoid the harassment of dog soldiers, King Ping of Zhou moved the capital eastward to Luoyi. Duke Xiang led troops to escort King Ping of Zhou.
King Ping of Zhou made Duke Xiang a prince and gave him the land west of Qishan.
King Ping said: Xirong is unjust and has invaded our lands in Qishan and Fengshui. If Qin can drive Xirong away, the land of Xirong will belong to Qin.
King Ping made an oath with him, granted him a fiefdom, and awarded him a title.
Only then did Duke Xiang make Qin a vassal state, exchange envoys with other vassal states, and send gifts of invitation and greetings to each other. They also used three black-maned and naked ponies, three oxen, and three rams to sacrifice to the Emperor of Heaven in the Western Border.
In the twelfth year, Duke Xiang attacked Xirong and reached Qi, where he died.
summary: Duke Xiang rescued the Zhou dynasty from Quan Rong attacks and escorted King Ping of Zhou eastward to Luoyi. King Ping granted Duke Xiang the title of prince and the land west of Qishan, making Qin a vassal state. Duke Xiang died in battle against Xirong. His son Wen Gong expanded territory, built cities, established rituals, and set up historians. Wen Gong's descendants included Ning Gong, Wu Gong, De Gong, Xuan Gong, Cheng Gong, and Mu Gong.

translation:
Duke Mu treated him like a guest and respected him very much. He asked him under what circumstances he should attack the Rong people.
In the thirty-sixth year, Duke Mu treated Meng Ming and others even more favorably and sent them to lead an army to attack Jin. When they crossed the Yellow River, they even burned their boats. They finally defeated the Jin people and occupied Wangguan and Chao as revenge for the Battle of Confucius.
The people of Jin stayed in the city and did not dare to come out.
So Duke Mu crossed the river from Maojin, buried the corpses in Mt. Confucius, and mourned for them for three days.
Duke Mu issued an oath to the entire army and said: Hey, soldiers!
Listen, don't make any noise, I swear to you.
I want to tell you that the ancients listened humbly to the opinions of the elderly, so they made no mistakes.
Duke Mu once again reflected on his fault for not following Uncle Jian and Baili Xi's plan, so he made this oath to let future generations remember his fault.
When the gentlemen heard about this, they all shed tears and said: Ah!
Duke Mu of Qin was so considerate to others that he was finally blessed with the victory of Meng Ming and others.
In the thirty-seventh year, Qin adopted Youyu's strategy to attack the Rong king, annexed twelve countries, opened up thousands of miles of land, and finally dominated Xirong.
The emperor sent Duke Zhao to give Duke Mu a golden drum to express his congratulations.
In the thirty-ninth year, Duke Mu died and was buried in Yong.
A total of 177 people were buried with him. Three virtuous ministers of Qin, belonging to the Ziyu family, named Yanxi, Zhongxing, and Zhenhu, were also among the martyrs.
The people of Qin mourned and wrote the poem "Yellow Bird" for him.
The gentleman said: Duke Mu of Qin expanded his territory and united the country, defeated the powerful Jin in the east, and dominated the Rong and Yi in the west. However, it is appropriate that he should not be the leader of the princes and allies.
After death, he did not cherish his subjects, but even took his virtuous ministers to be buried with him.
After the death of the late king, it is necessary to leave behind good morals and institutions, let alone good people and virtuous ministers who win the sympathy of the people? This shows that Qin could not conquer the east.
Duke Mu had forty sons, and his crown prince named him as Duke Kang.
The first year of Kanggong.
The previous year, when Duke Mu passed away, Duke Xianggong of Jin also died; Duke Xianggang of Jin's younger brother was named Yong, who was born to a daughter of Qin and lived in Qin.
Zhao Dun, the Qing of Jin, wanted to make him king and sent a retinue to pick him up. The Qin State sent troops to escort Yong to Linghu.
However, the Jin State had already established the son of Duke Xiang, but he came to attack the Qin Army. The Qin Army was defeated and fled to the Qin State.
In the second year, Qin attacked Jin and occupied Wucheng to retaliate for the Battle of Linghu.
In the fourth year, Jin conquered Qin and occupied Shaoliang.
In the sixth year, Qin attacked Jin and occupied Jima.
The two armies fought at Hequ and defeated the Jin army.
The people of Jin were worried that Sui Hui would bring war to Jin State in the Qin State, so they sent Wei Yuyu to pretend to be a rebel, conspired with Sui Hui, and obtained Sui Hui through deception, so Sui Hui returned to Jin State.
Duke Kang died in the twelfth year of his reign, and his son Gong Gong came to the throne.
summary: Duke Mu of Qin was a notable ruler. He married a daughter of Jin, captured the virtuous minister Baili Xi, and appointed him along with Jian Shu. During a famine, Qin aided Jin despite previous betrayals. When Jin attacked Qin, Duke Mu was nearly captured but was rescued by 300 men who had previously eaten his horse and been forgiven. Duke Mu captured Jin's ruler but released him after negotiations. He later helped Chong'er become Duke Wen of Jin. Duke Mu attacked Zheng but withdrew after learning of Zheng's preparedness. The Qin army was defeated by Jin at Miao Mountain. Duke Mu later adopted Youyu's strategies, attacked the Rong king, annexed twelve countries, and dominated Xirong. He died and was buried with 177 people, including three virtuous ministers.

translation:
In the 16th year, trenches were dug beside the Yellow River.
He sent 20,000 troops to attack the Dali Kingdom and captured the city of Dali King.
In the 21st year, a county began to be established in Pinyang.
Jin occupied Wucheng.
In the twenty-fourth year, there was civil strife in Jin, Zhibo was killed, and his territory was divided among the three kingdoms of Zhao, Han, and Wei.
In the twenty-fifth year, Zhikai and the people in Zhishi's fiefdom fled to Qin.
In the thirty-third year, he attacked Yiqu and captured the king of Yiqu.
In the thirty-fourth year, a solar eclipse occurred.
Duke Li died and his son Duke Cao ascended the throne.
In the second year of Cao Gong's reign, Nan Zheng rebelled.
In the thirteenth year, Yiqu came to attack Qin and arrived in Weinan.
In the fourteenth year, Duke Cao died and his younger brother, Duke Huai, succeeded him.
In the fourth year of Duke Huai's reign, the concubine Chao and his ministers besieged Duke Huai, who committed suicide.
The prince Huai Gong's name was Zhaozi. He died early, so the ministers made Zhaozi's son king, who was Duke Ling.

In the sixth year of Linggong, the Jin State built a city in Shaoliang, and the Qin army attacked the Jin State.
In the thirteenth year, the Qin State built a city in Jigu.

In the sixth year of Duke Jian's reign, he issued an order to allow lower-level officials to carry swords.
The embankments of Luoshui were cut and built, and the walls of Chongquan City were built.
After his death in the sixteenth year, his son Hui Gong came to the throne.
In the twelfth year of Duke Hui's reign, his son Chuzi was born.
In the thirteenth year, he attacked Shu and occupied Nanzheng.
Duke Hui died and his son came to the throne.
In the second year after the birth of his son, the concubine Zhang Jun took Duke Linggong's son Xiangong back from Hexi and established him as the king.
Kill the son and his mother and sink them into the abyss.
In the past period, the state of Qin frequently changed its monarchs, and the status of monarchs and ministers was reversed. Therefore, the state of Jin became stronger again and took away Qin's land west of the Yellow River.
In the first year of Xian AD, burials with people were abolished.
In the second year, the city wall of Yueyang City was built.
In the first month of the fourth year, Gengyin, Duke Xiao was born.
In the eleventh year, Zhou Taishi Danjin met with Duke Xiang and said: Zhou used to be one with Qin, but later they separated. After five hundred years of separation, they will merge again. In seventeen years together, there will be an overlord.
In the sixteenth year, the peach trees bloomed in winter.
In the eighteenth year, it rained gold in the oak sun.
In the 21st year, he fought with Jin at Shimen and beheaded 60,000 people. The emperor gave Fu Fu as a congratulation.
In the twenty-third year, he fought with the state of Wei in Shaoliang and captured Wei general Gongsun Cuo.
In the twenty-fourth year, Duke Xian died, and his son, Duke Xiao, came to the throne at the age of twenty-one.
summary: After Duke Mu, his descendants included Kang Gong, Gong Gong, Huan Gong, Jing Gong, Ai Gong, Hui Gong, Dao Gong, Li Gong, Cao Gong, Huai Gong, Ling Gong, Jian Gong, Hui Gong, Chu Zi, and Xian Gong. During this period, Qin frequently changed rulers, and Jin grew stronger, taking Qin's land west of the Yellow River. Duke Xian abolished live burials and built cities. His son Duke Xiao ascended the throne at age 21.

translation:
In the first year of Xiaogong, there were six powerful states east of the Yellow River and Mount Wei. Qin Xiaogong was also known as King Wei of Qi, King Xuan of Chu, King Hui of Wei, King Yan Du, Han Aihou, and Zhao Chenghou.
There are more than ten small countries between Huai River and Surabaya River.
Chu, Wei and Qin bordered.
Wei built the Great Wall and went north from Zheng along the Luoshui River to occupy the land of Shangjun.
Chu occupied Bajun and Qianzhong County from Hanzhong to the south.
The Zhou royal family declined, and the vassal states conquered and merged with each other by force.
Qin is located in Yongzhou, a remote area. He does not participate in the alliances between the Central Plains countries and is regarded as a barbarian.
The Duke of Filial Piety then extended his favors widely, provided relief to orphans and widows, recruited soldiers, and rewarded people based on their merits.
He ordered the king to say: In the past, our ancestor Mu Gong rose up between Qi and Yong. He focused on literature, virtue and martial arts. To the east, he quelled civil strife in Jin and demarcated the border with Jin by the Yellow River. To the west, he dominated Rongzhai and expanded the area to thousands of miles. The emperor named him Fang Bo, and the princes came to congratulate him. He started a business for future generations. It was a great honor.
Unfortunately, it happened to be an unstable period during the reigns of Duke Li, Duke Cao, Duke Jian, and Chuzi. The country was worried about domestic affairs and could not care about foreign affairs. The three Jin Dynasties took the opportunity to capture the land of our ancestors in Hexi. The princes all despised the Qin State. There is no greater shame than this.
Duke Xian ascended the throne, pacified the border, moved the capital to Yueyang, and planned to send troops to march eastward, regain Duke Mu's old territory, and reorganize Duke Mu's political orders.
I feel sad every time I think of your late king's wishes.
If any of the guests and ministers can come up with clever ideas to make Qin strong, I will make them high officials and give them land.
Then he sent troops to surround Shaanxi City in the east and kill King Xian of the Rong tribe in the west.
When Wei Yang heard that this order had been issued, he came to Qin from the west and asked to see Duke Xiao through the introduction of Jingjian.
In the second year, the emperor rewarded King Qin with sacrificial meat.
In the third year, Wei Yang persuaded Duke Xiao to implement reforms, formulate punishments, promote agriculture internally, strictly enforce rewards and punishments externally, and encourage soldiers to fight hard and fight to the death. Duke Xiao expressed his appreciation.
But Qianlong, Du Zhi and others disagreed and started arguing with him.
In the end, Wei Yang's new method was adopted. The people felt it was very hard, but after three years, they got used to it.
So he made Wei Yang the chief of Zuo Shu.
These things are introduced in "The Biography of Shang Jun".
In the seventh year, he met with King Hui of Wei at Du Ping.
In the eighth year, he fought with Wei in Yuanli and won.
In the tenth year, Wei Yang was granted the title of Daliang Zao, and he led his troops to surround Anyi in Wei State, and Anyi surrendered.
In the twelfth year, the city of Xianyang was built, Jique was built, and the Qin Dynasty moved its capital to Xianyang.
The small villages were merged into large counties, and each county was appointed with a county magistrate, for a total of 41 counties.
Plan the acres of land, set up fences, and expand the territory to the east of Luoshui.
summary: Duke Xiao issued an order to recruit talents to strengthen Qin. Wei Yang (Shang Yang) came from Wei and implemented reforms, establishing laws, promoting agriculture, and enforcing strict rewards and punishments. Despite opposition, the new laws were adopted. Qin built Xianyang, established counties, and expanded territory. Duke Xiao died, and his son Huiwen Jun executed Wei Yang.

translation:
The king met with the king of Wei in Yiyang, and with the king of Han in Xincheng.
In the twenty-fourth year, he met with the King of Chu, Yu Yan, and then with Yu Rang.
Qin captured Wei's Ancheng and marched to Daliang. Yan and Zhao rescued Wei. The Qin army retreated.
Wei Ran was dismissed as prime minister.
In twenty-five years, two Zhao cities were captured.
The King of Qin and the King of Han met in Xincheng, and the King of Wei met in Xinmingyi.
In the twenty-sixth year, the criminals were pardoned and moved to Rang, and Ranghou was appointed prime minister again.
In the twenty-seventh year, Sima Cuo attacked Chu.
The criminals were pardoned and moved to Nanyang.
Bai Qi attacked Zhao and occupied the Guanglang City of Dai.
He also sent Sima Cuo to send troops to Longxi County to attack Chu's Qianzhong County via Shu and captured it.
In the twenty-eighth year, Daliang Zaobai attacked Chu, occupied Yan and Deng, and pardoned the criminals and moved to that place.
In the 29th year, Daliang Zaobai attacked Chu, occupied Ying and established it as Nanjun. The king of Chu fled.
Zhou Jun came to congratulate.
The King of Qin and the King of Chu met in Xiangling.
Bai Qi was named Lord Wu'an.
In the 30th year, Zhang Ruo, the governor of Shu County, attacked Chu, occupied Wu County and Jiangnan, and established it as Qianzhong County.
In the thirty-first year, Bai Qi attacked Wei and captured two cities.
The Chu people rebelled in the land south of the Yangtze River occupied by our country.
In the 32nd year, Prime Minister Ranghou attacked Wei and reached Daliang. He defeated Baoyuan's army and beheaded 40,000 people. Baoyuan was defeated and fled, and Wei ceded three counties to seek peace.
In the thirty-third year, Hu Yang, the guest minister, attacked Juan, Caiyang, and Changshe of Wei State and occupied them.
Attacked Mangmao in Huayang, defeated the enemy army, and beheaded 150,000 people.
Wei ceded Nanyang to seek peace.
In the thirty-fourth year, Qin merged Wei, Han and Shangyong into one county, and moved the pardoned criminal officials of Nanyang to this place.
Thirty-five years later, he helped Han, Wei, and Chu defeat Yan.
Nanyang County was established.
In the thirty-sixth year, Ke Qingzao attacked Qi, occupied Gang and Shou, and granted Ranghou.
In the thirty-eighth year, Zhong Geng Hu Shang attacked Zhao Yu and failed to capture it.
Forty years later, the crown prince died in Wei and was buried in Zhiyang.
In the summer of the 41st year, he attacked Wei and occupied Xingqiu and Huai.
In the forty-second year, An Guojun was established as the prince.
In October, Empress Dowager Xuan died and was buried in Lishan Mountain in Zhiyang.
In September, Marquis Rang left the court and returned to Taodi.
Forty-three years. Wu'an Junbai attacked Han, captured nine cities, and beheaded 50,000 people.
In the forty-fourth year, he attacked Han Nanyang and occupied it.
In the forty-fifth year, Ben, the fifth official, attacked Han and captured ten cities.
Ye Yangjun's son Kui ran away to his feudal country, but died before he arrived.
In the forty-seventh year, Qin attacked Han's Shangdang County. Shangdang County surrendered to Zhao. Qin attacked Zhao again. Zhao sent troops to meet Qin. The two armies were at a stalemate.
Qin sent Bai Qi, Lord Wu'an, to attack and defeated the Zhao army in Changping. All 400,000 surrendered soldiers were killed.
In October of the 48th year, South Korea presented Yuan Yong.
summary: Huiwen Jun's reign saw further expansion. Zhang Yi served as prime minister. Qin attacked Shu, captured Hanzhong, and defeated Chu. King Wu succeeded Huiwen Jun but died after a weightlifting accident. His half-brother Zhaoxiang Wang became king, with Queen Mother Xuan as regent. Zhaoxiang Wang's reign was marked by extensive military campaigns. Bai Qi defeated Han and Wei at Yique, killing 240,000. Qin attacked Chu, occupied Ying, and established Nanjun. Bai Qi defeated Zhao at Changping, killing 400,000 surrendered soldiers. Qin attacked the Western Zhou, whose king surrendered. The nine tripods were moved to Qin, and the Zhou dynasty was destroyed.

translation:
In the first year of King Zhuang Xiang's reign, he granted a general amnesty to criminals. He still reused the heroes of the previous king, extended benevolence, treated relatives favorably, and extended grace to the people.
The king of Eastern Zhou and the princes planned to attack Qin. Qin sent Prime Minister Lu Buwei to attack him and merge all his lands into Qin's territory.
However, Qin did not interrupt his sacrificial tradition and gave the land of Yangren to Zhou Jun, allowing him to continue his sacrificial rituals.
He sent Meng Ao to attack Han, and Han sacrificed Cheng Gao and Gong.
Qin's territory expanded to Daliang, and Sanchuan County was established.
In the second year, he sent Meng Ao to attack Zhao and pacify Taiyuan.
In the third year, Meng Ao attacked Wei's Gaodu and Ji and captured them.
Meng Ao also attacked Yuci, Xincheng and Langmeng of Zhao State, capturing thirty-seven cities.
A solar eclipse occurs in April.
Wang Lu attacked Shangdang and began to establish Taiyuan County.
Wei general Wuji led the troops of the five countries to counterattack the Qin army, and the Qin army retreated to the south of the Yellow River.
Meng Ao lost the battle, got rid of the siege and evacuated.
On Bingwu in the fifth month, King Zhuang Xiang died, and his son Ying Zheng ascended the throne, becoming the first emperor of Qin.
In the twenty-sixth year after King Yingzheng of Qin came to the throne, he began to unite the world and establish thirty-six counties, known as the First Emperor.
The First Emperor died at the age of fifty-one, and his son Hu Hai ascended the throne and became the second emperor.
In the third year of the Second Emperor's reign, the princes rebelled against the Qin Dynasty one after another. Zhao Gao killed the Second Emperor and made Ziying emperor.
More than a month after Ziying took the throne, the princes killed him again, and the Qin Dynasty was destroyed.
The detailed description can be found in "The Chronicles of Qin Shihuang".
Tai Shigong said: The ancestors of Qin were named Ying.
His descendants were divided into various places and took the feudal country as their surname. They include the Xu family, the Tan family, the Ju family, the Zhongli family, the Yunxiang family, the Tuqiu family, the Jiangliang family, the Huang family, the Jiang family, the Xiuyu family, the Baiming family, the Feilian family, and the Qin family.
However, Qin was granted the title of Zhao City because of his ancestor Zaofu, who was also called the Zhao family.
summary: Zhaoxiang Wang died, and his son Xiaowen Wang reigned only three days before dying. Zhuang Xiang Wang succeeded him, attacking Eastern Zhou and merging its lands. He died, and his son Ying Zheng became king, later known as Qin Shi Huang. He united the world, established thirty-six counties, and became the First Emperor. After his death, his son Hu Hai became the Second Emperor. In the third year of the Second Emperor's reign, princes rebelled. Zhao Gao killed the Second Emperor and made Ziying emperor. Ziying was killed by princes, and Qin was destroyed.

translation:
Xiang Ji, Xia Xiangren, named Yu.
He was twenty-four years old when he started to fight.
His uncle was Xiang Liang, and Xiang Liang's father was Chu general Xiang Yan, who was killed by Qin general Wang Jian.
The Xiang family has been a general of Chu for generations and was granted the title of Xiang, hence the surname Xiang.
When Xiang Ji was a child, he learned to read and write but failed.
He gave up learning calligraphy and switched to fencing, but failed again.
Xiang Liang was very angry with him.
Xiang Ji said: Characters are only used to remember names.
A sword can only withstand one enemy, so it is not worth learning. You must learn to be able to withstand ten thousand people.
So Xiang Liang taught Xiang Ji the art of war. Xiang Ji was very happy and roughly understood the general idea of ​​the art of war, but he refused to finish it seriously.
Xiang Liang was once implicated in the Yueyang crime case, so he asked Cao Jiu, the warden of Qixian County, to write to Sima Xin, the warden of Yueyang, and the matter was settled.
Xiang Liang killed someone, and he and Xiang Ji went to Wuzhong to avoid their enemies.
None of the talented scholar-bureaucrats in Wuzhong could compare with Xiang Liang.
Whenever there was a large-scale military service or funeral in Wuzhong, Xiang Liang often took charge of the arrangements and secretly used military arrangements to arrange guests and children, so he understood everyone's abilities.
When the First Emperor of Qin visited Kuaiji and crossed Zhejiang, Xiang Liang and Xiang Ji went to watch it together.
Xiang Ji said: I can replace that emperor.
Xiang Liang covered his mouth and said, "Don't talk nonsense, or the whole clan will be beheaded!"
Xiang Liang therefore felt that Xiang Ji was different from ordinary people.
Xiang Ji is more than eight feet tall, can lift a cauldron, and is so talented that the children of Wuzhong already fear him.
In July of the first year of Qin II, Chen She and others revolted in Daze Township.
In September of that year, Yin Tong, the governor of Kuaiji County, told Xiang Liang that Jiangxi had rebelled, and that this was also the time when God would destroy the Qin Dynasty.
I heard that those who strike first can control others, and those who strike last are controlled by others.
I want to send troops and send you and Huan Chu to lead them.
At that time, Huan Chu fled to Zezhong.
Xiang Liang said: Huan Chu died and was hiding outside. No one knew his whereabouts. Only Xiang Ji knew.
Xiang Liang came out and told Xiang Ji to wait outside with his sword.
Xiang Liang went in again and sat with the county guard. Xiang Liang said: "Please allow me to call Xiang Yu in and let him accept the order to recall Huan Chu." The Sheriff said: Okay.
Xiang Liang called Xiang Ji in.
After a while, Xiang Liang winked at Xiang Ji and said, "It's time to take action!"
So Xiang Yu drew his sword and chopped off the head of the governor.
Xiang Liang took the county governor's head and tied the official seal of the county governor on his body.
The guards of the county guard were greatly alarmed and in chaos, Xiang Yu killed more than a hundred people.
Everyone in the mansion was in a state of fear and submission, and no one dared to resist.
Xiang Liang summoned the courageous and powerful officials he was familiar with in the past and made it clear to everyone what he was going to do to raise an army against Qin, so he recruited the soldiers of Wu Zhong to revolt.
He sent people to recruit strong men from the subordinate counties and got 8,000 elite soldiers.
Xiang Liang arranged for the heroes of Wuzhong to be school captains, marquises, and Sima.
summary: Xiang Ji, also known as Xiang Yu, was a man from Xiaxiang who began his military career at age twenty-four. His uncle was Xiang Liang, son of Chu general Xiang Yan, who was killed by Qin general Wang Jian. The Xiang family had served as Chu generals for generations and were granted the title of Xiang. As a child, Xiang Ji failed at learning calligraphy and fencing, dismissing them as insufficient for facing ten thousand enemies. He studied the art of war under Xiang Liang but refused to master it completely. After Xiang Liang killed someone, they fled to Wuzhong, where Xiang Liang organized military and funeral services, secretly assessing people's abilities. When Qin Shi Huang visited Kuaiji, Xiang Ji declared he could replace the emperor, prompting Xiang Liang to cover his mouth and warn against such talk. Xiang Liang then recognized Xiang Ji's exceptional nature. Xiang Ji was over eight feet tall, could lift a cauldron, and was feared by the youth of Wuzhong.
