translation:
One person was not appointed and went to complain to Xiang Liang himself.
Xiang Liang said: There was a funeral some time ago and I asked you to take charge of something. You couldn't handle it, so I didn't appoint you.
So everyone admired Xiang Liang.
Xiang Liang was the governor of Kuaiji, and Xiang Ji was the general. Zhenfu subordinate counties and cities.
Zhao Ping, a native of Guangling, was trying to capture the territory of Guangling for King Chen, but he did not surrender.
Hearing that King Chen was defeated and fled, and that Qin soldiers were about to arrive, he crossed the river and asked King Chen to give him orders to worship Xiang Liang as the king of Chu's Shangzhu Kingdom.
Zhao Ping said: Jiangdong has been pacified, so quickly lead troops to the west to attack the Qin army.
Xiang Liang crossed the river with eight thousand men and headed west.
He heard that Chen Ying had captured Dongyang, so he sent an envoy to join forces with Chen Ying to advance westward.
Chen Ying turned out to be the governor of Dongyang. He had always been honest and prudent in the county, and people called him a loyal elder.
Young people in Dongyang killed their county magistrate and gathered thousands of people to elect a leader. When no one was found, they asked Chen Ying to take over.
Chen Ying refused and said he was not qualified, so everyone forcibly elected him as the leader, with 20,000 followers in the county.
The young people planned to elect Chen Ying to be king. In order to distinguish himself from other armies, the soldiers wore green scarves on their heads to signify the sudden rise of the army.
Chen Ying's mother said to Chen Ying: Since I became the daughter-in-law of the Chen family, I have never heard that your predecessors had high officials or noble titles.
It's not a good sign to suddenly gain a lot of fame now.
It's better to belong to something. If things succeed, you can still get a title. If things fail, it's easier to escape because you won't attract the attention of the world.
Therefore, Chen Ying did not dare to become king.
He said to his military officers: The Xiang family has been a general for generations and is famous in Chu.
Now if you want to accomplish great things, you have to use the right general.
If we rely on famous families, we will definitely destroy the Qin Dynasty.
So everyone listened to him and gave the army to Xiang Liang.
Xiang Liang crossed the Huai River, and generals Yingbu and Pu also led their troops to surrender.
Xiang Liang had a total of sixty or seventy thousand men stationed in Xiapi.
At this time, Qin Jia had established Jingju as King of Chu and stationed himself east of Pengcheng, hoping to resist Xiang Liang.
Xiang Liang said to the soldiers: King Chen started the rebellion first, and the battle was not successful. His whereabouts are unknown.
Now Qin Jia betrayed King Chen and established Jingju, which was a treasonous act.
Xiang Liang then marched to attack Qin Jia.
Qin Jia's army was defeated and fled, and Xiang Liang pursued him to Hu Ling.
Qin Jia returned to the army and fought for a day. Qin Jia was killed in battle and his soldiers surrendered.
Jingju fled and died in Liangdi.
Xiang Liang has merged Qin Jia's army and is stationed in Huling, and will lead the army westward.
Zhang Han's army arrived at Li County, and Xiang Liang sent generals Zhujishi and Yu Fanjun to fight with him.
Yu Fanjun died in battle, Zhujishi's army was defeated and fled to Huling.
Xiang Liang then led his troops into Xue County and killed Zhujishi.
summary: In July of Qin II's first year, Chen She rebelled in Daze Township. In September, Yin Tong, the governor of Kuaiji, proposed raising troops with Xiang Liang and Huan Chu. Xiang Liang, knowing Huan Chu's whereabouts, had Xiang Ji wait with a sword. After entering the governor's chambers, Xiang Liang called Xiang Ji in, who beheaded the governor. Xiang Yu killed over a hundred guards, and the rest submitted. Xiang Liang raised an army of 8,000 elite soldiers from Wuzhong, appointing local heroes as officers. He became governor of Kuaiji, with Xiang Ji as general. Zhao Ping of Guangling urged Xiang Liang to lead troops west to attack Qin. Xiang Liang crossed the river with 8,000 men, joined forces with Chen Ying of Dongyang, and gained 60,000-70,000 troops at Xiapi. He defeated Qin Jia, who had betrayed King Chen, and merged his army. After defeating Qin forces at Dong'a, Xiang Liang grew arrogant, ignoring Song Yi's warnings. Qin reinforced Zhang Han, who defeated and killed Xiang Liang at Dingtao.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪

translation:
It was cold and raining heavily, and the soldiers were freezing and hungry.
Xiang Yu said: Originally, we planned to attack Qin together, but we stopped for a long time.
Nowadays, there is famine and hunger, and the people are poor. The soldiers can only eat half a liter of beans, and there is no food in the army. However, Song Yi still holds banquets and receives guests. Instead of leading the army across the river to take Zhao's food on the spot, he says "wait for the Qin army to be exhausted."
With Qin's powerful troops attacking the newly established Zhao State, the result of the development of the situation must be that the Qin army defeats the Zhao army.
Zhao's army was defeated, and Qin's army was stronger. What opportunity could there be to take advantage of exhaustion!
Moreover, the Chu army had been defeated recently, and the king was restless, so he concentrated all the troops in the country under the general's command. The safety of the country was at stake.
Nowadays, we do not care about the soldiers, but only seek selfish interests. This is not a minister who shares the same interests with the country.
Xiang Yu met General Song Yi in the morning, cut off Song Yi's head in his tent, and came out to give orders to the army: Song Yi and Qi State conspired against Chu, and the King of Chu secretly ordered me to kill him.
At this time, the generals were all afraid and surrendered, and no one dared to resist.
It is said that the generals and their families founded the State of Chu.
Now it was the general who executed the rebels again.
The generals jointly elected Xiang Yu as acting general.
He sent people to chase Song Yi's son, and caught up with him in Qi State and killed him.
Xiang Yu sent Huan Chu to report to King Huai of Chu.
King Huai of Chu made Xiang Yu the general, and both Dangyang Jun and General Pu belonged to Xiang Yu.
Xiang Yu had killed the champion of Qingzi, which shocked the Chu country and became famous among the princes. He sent Lord Dangyang and General Pu to lead 20,000 soldiers across the river to rescue Julu.
After the war was somewhat successful, Chen Yu asked Xiang Yu for more troops.
Xiang Yu led his entire army across the river, scuttled the ships, smashed the cooking utensils, burned the camps, and carried three days of rations to show that the soldiers fought to the death and no one had any intention of coming back alive.
As soon as the army arrived, they surrounded Wang Li, encountered the Qin army, fought nine battles, cut off the Qin army's corridors, and defeated the Qin army. Killed Su Jiao and captured Wang Li.
Shejian refused to surrender to the Chu army and burned himself to death.
At that time, the Chu army was famous among the princes.
At that time, the various princes who came to rescue Zhao had more than a dozen large camps, but they did not dare to send troops easily.
When the Chu army attacked, the princes and generals were watching the battle on the camp.
The soldiers of the Chu army were all equal to ten. The shouts of the Chu soldiers shook the sky, and the soldiers of the princes were frightened.
Having defeated the Qin army, Xiang Yu summoned all the princes and generals. They entered the camp gate and walked forward on their knees, not daring to look up.
From then on, Xiang Yu became the general of the princes' armies, and all the princes surrendered to him.
Zhang Han was stationed at Jiyuan and Xiang Yu was stationed at the south bank of Zhangshui River. The two armies were in a stalemate and there was no fighting.
The Qin army retreated many times, and the Second Emperor sent someone to punish Zhang Han.
summary: After Xiang Liang's death, King Huai of Chu appointed Song Yi as supreme general to rescue Zhao, with Xiang Yu as second-in-command. Song Yi stalled at Anyang for 46 days. Xiang Yu killed him for incompetence and took command, leading the army across the river after sinking ships and burning camps. They defeated the Qin army at Julu, killing Su Jiao and capturing Wang Li. The Chu army's victory made Xiang Yu the commander of all allied forces. Zhang Han, facing pressure from Zhao Gao, surrendered to Xiang Yu after negotiations. Xiang Yu appointed Zhang Han as King Yong but later executed over 200,000 Qin soldiers at Xin'an due to fears of rebellion.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪

translation:
Before this, Xiang Liang sent Xiang Yu to lead another army to attack Xiangcheng, but Xiangcheng held on and refused to surrender.
After the capture, all the soldiers and civilians who defended the city were killed, and they came back to report to Xiang Liang.
Xiang Liang heard that King Chen was indeed dead, so he summoned all the generals to Xue County to discuss important matters.
At this time, Pei Gong also raised troops from Pei and went to Xue County.
Fan Zeng, a Juhuan, is seventy years old. He has always lived at home and likes to come up with clever ideas. He went to lobby Xiang Liang and said: Chen Sheng's failure was the right thing to do.
Qin destroyed the six kingdoms, and Chu was the least at fault.
Since King Huai of Chu entered Qin and never returned, the people of Chu still miss him. Therefore, Duke Nan of Chu said, "Although Chu has three households, if Qin is destroyed, it will be Chu."
Now that Chen Sheng is the first to start the rebellion and proclaim himself king instead of a descendant of Chu, his situation will not last long.
Now that you have launched an army to the east of the Yangtze River, the people of Chu are like swarms of bees, all vying to join you. This is because the Xiang family has been Chu generals for generations and can once again establish the descendants of Chu.
Xiang Liang thought he was right, so he found the grandson of King Huai of Chu among the people. He was tending sheep for people. Xiang Liang made him King Huai of Chu and obeyed the people's wishes.
Chen Ying ruled the Shangzhu Kingdom of Chu and had five counties in his fiefdom. Together with King Huai of Chu, he established Xutai as the capital.
Xiang Liang called himself Lord Wu Xin.
A few months later, Xiang Liang led troops to attack Kangfu, and together with the troops of Tian Rong and Sima Longqie of Qi State, he rescued Dong'a and defeated the Qin army in Dong'a.
Tian Rong led his army back to his old place and drove away King Tianjia of Qi.
Tianjia fled to Chu State.
Tian Jiao, the prime minister of Tianjia, fled to Zhao.
Tian Jiao's younger brother Tian Jian turned out to be a general of Qi State, but he stayed in Zhao State and did not dare to go back.
Tian Rong made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi the king of Qi.
Xiang Liang had already defeated the Qin army in Dong'e, so he pursued him.
He sent envoys many times to urge the Qi army, intending to join forces with it to march westward.
Tian Rong said: Chu killed Tianjia, and Zhao killed Tianjiao and Tianjian, so I will send troops.
Xiang Liang said: Tianjia is the king of a country friendly to Chu. He came to rely on me when he was desperate. I couldn't bear to kill him.
Zhao also did not kill Tianjiao and Tianjian as a condition of exchange with Qi.
So Qi refused to send troops to help Chu.
Xiang Liang sent Pei Gong and Xiang Yu to lead another army to attack Chengyang and massacred the county seat.
Xiangxi defeated the Qin army east of Puyang, and the Qin army withdrew its troops and entered Puyang.
Pei Gong and Xiang Yu attacked Dingtao.
After failing to capture Dingtao, he led his army to leave, marched westward and captured the territory, reaching Yongqiu, where he defeated the Qin army and killed Li You.
He returned to attack Waihuang but failed to capture it.
Xiang Liang set out from Dong'a and marched westward. When he arrived at Dingtao, he defeated the Qin army again. Xiang Yu and others killed Li You again. Therefore, Xiang Liang despised the Qin army more and more and looked arrogant.
Song Yi advised Xiang Liang: If you win a battle but your generals are arrogant and your soldiers are lazy, you will lose.
Now the soldiers are a little slack and the number of Qin soldiers is increasing day by day. I am worried about you.
Xiang Liang did not listen to the advice.
So he sent Song Yi as envoy to Qi.
On the way, I met Gaoling Junxian, the envoy of Qi State, and asked him: Are you going to see Mr. Wu Xin?
summary: Xiang Yu entered Hangu Pass and camped at Hongmen, where Pei Gong (Liu Bang) had already taken Xianyang. Fan Zeng urged Xiang Yu to kill Pei Gong, but Xiang Bo warned Pei Gong, who apologized at the Hongmen feast. Xiang Zhuang's sword dance failed to assassinate Pei Gong, who escaped with Fan Kuai's help. Xiang Yu later entered Xianyang, killed Ziying, burned the Qin palace, and collected treasures. He divided the empire, making Pei Gong King of Han and himself Hegemon-King of Western Chu. He moved Emperor Yi to Chen County and had him killed. Conflicts arose as Tian Rong rebelled in Qi and Chen Yu attacked Changshan. The King of Han conquered the Three Qins and marched east, leading to a prolonged war with Xiang Yu.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪

translation:
Zhang Han was frightened and sent Chief Shi Simaxin to ask for instructions.
When he arrived in Xianyang, he waited outside the door for three days. Zhao Gao did not receive him, which was a sign of distrust.
Chief Shi Sima Xin was frightened and hurriedly fled back to the army. He didn't dare to take the original route. As expected, Zhao Gao sent people to chase him, but he failed to catch up.
Sima Xin arrived in the army and reported to Zhang Han: Zhao Gao has great power in the DPRK, and the people below cannot make a difference.
Now that the battle can be won, Zhao Gao must be jealous of our achievements; if the battle cannot be won, he will inevitably be executed.
I hope the general will think this through.
Chen Yu also sent a letter to Zhang Han saying: Bai Qi was the general of Qin. He attacked Yan and Ying to the south, killed horses and soldiers to the north, attacked the city and lost ground. He was countless, and in the end he was killed.
Meng Tian was a Qin general who drove the Xiongnu from the north and opened up an area of ​​thousands of miles in Yuzhong. He was eventually killed in Yangzhou.
Why?
There was too much merit, and Qin could not grant titles according to merit, so it used national laws to kill them.
Now that the general has been the general of Qin for three years, he has lost hundreds of thousands of soldiers, and the princes' armies have risen at the same time, increasing their numbers.
That Zhao Gao has always been flattering for a long time. Now the situation is critical, and he is afraid that the second generation will kill him, so he plans to use the national law to kill the general to shirk his responsibility, and to send someone from outside to replace the general to get rid of the disaster.
The general has been away for a long time, and many people in the court are alienated from you. Even if you have merit, you will be killed, and if you have no merit, you will be killed.
Besides, Qin is going to be destroyed, and both the stupid and the smart people know it.
Nowadays, the general cannot express his opinions directly at home, but outside he is the general of a country that is about to perish. He is isolated and helpless and wants to stay for a long time. Isn't it sad?
Why don't the general defect and join forces with various princes, sign a peace treaty, jointly attack Qin, cede the land to the king, sit facing south, and claim to be a lonely Taoist and a widower? Which one is better, or to be killed on the anvil and have his wife killed?
Zhang Han hesitated and secretly sent military commander Shicheng to Xiang Yu's camp to sign a peace treaty.
The peace treaty was not negotiated, so Xiang Yu asked General Pu to lead his troops across Sanhujin day and night, camped on the south bank of Zhang River, fought with the Qin army, and defeated the Qin army again.
Xiang Yu led the entire army to attack the Qin army on the sewage, and defeated the Qin army.
Zhang Han sent people to see Xiang Yu and planned to make a peace treaty.
Xiang Yu summoned the military officials to discuss: The army is short of food and wants to allow him to sign a peace treaty.
All the military officers said, "Okay."
Xiang Yu and Zhang Han made an appointment to meet at the Yin Ruins on the south bank of Huan River.
The alliance had been concluded. When Zhang Han saw Xiang Yu, he broke down in tears and told Xiang Yu all the deeds of Zhao Gao.
Xiang Yu then appointed Zhang Han as King Yong and placed him in the Chu army camp.
The envoy commander Shi Sima Xin was appointed as the general and led the Qin army as the advance force.
The army arrived at Xin'an.
The officers and soldiers of the princes' armies had previously passed through Guanzhong because of their corvee service and guarding the border areas. The Qin soldiers often insulted them. When the Qin army surrendered to the princes' army, the officers and soldiers of the princes' army took advantage of the victory in the war and treated them like slaves and prisoners, torturing and humiliating the Qin officers and soldiers at will.
Most of the Qin officers and soldiers discussed privately: General Zhang and others deceived us into surrendering to the princes' armies. Now we can enter the pass and defeat Qin, which is good; if we can't, the princes' troops will capture us and go eastward; Qin will definitely put our parents and wives to death.
The generals of the princes' armies secretly heard their plan and reported it to Xiang Yu.
Xiang Yu went to Generals Ying Bu and Pu to discuss: There were still many Qin officers and soldiers, and they were dissatisfied. If they did not obey orders when they arrived at Guanzhong, things would be in danger. It would be better to kill them, and only enter Qin with Zhang Han, Chang Shi Sima Xin, and Captain Dong Yi.
So the Chu army executed more than 200,000 Qin soldiers at night and buried them in the south of Xin'an City.
Xiang Yu is about to capture the Qin Guanzhong area.
Hangu Pass is guarded by soldiers and cannot enter.
summary: The war saw numerous battles, including the Han defeat at Pengcheng and the siege of Xingyang. Xiang Yu's forces were weakened by defections and food shortages. After a stalemate at Guangwu, Xiang Yu agreed to divide the empire at the Hong Canal, releasing the King of Han's family. However, the King of Han broke the treaty and pursued Xiang Yu. At Gaixia, Xiang Yu's army was surrounded, and hearing Chu songs, he realized defeat was imminent. He fled with 800 cavalry, but only 28 remained at Dongcheng. After killing hundreds of Han soldiers, he committed suicide, refusing to cross the Wu River. His body was divided among five Han officers for rewards. The city of Lu surrendered only after seeing his head, and he was buried with the rites of a duke. The Han king did not kill the Xiang clan, granting some titles. Sima Qian noted Xiang Yu's rise from obscurity to dominance in three years but criticized his arrogance, abandonment of Guanzhong, and failure to learn from the past, attributing his downfall to his own faults rather than divine will.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/项羽本纪

translation:
Gaozu was born in Zhongyangli, Fengyi, Peixian County. The surname is Liu and the courtesy name is Ji.
The father's name is Taigong, and the mother's name is Liu Yu.
Previously, Lady Liu had rested on the shore of the Great Lake and met God in her sleep.
At this time, there were thunder and lightning, and the sky was dark and the earth was dark. Grandpa Gong went to see Lady Liu and saw a dragon on her body. Later Lady Liu became pregnant and gave birth to Gaozu.
Gaozu had a high nose, a plump forehead like a dragon, a beautiful beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left leg.
He is kind and loving to others, likes to give charity, and is broad-minded.
They often have lofty ambitions and do not engage in ordinary people's production operations.
When he reached his prime, he tried to be an official and became the chief of the Sishui Pavilion. Every official in the court was familiar with him and was teased by him.
He likes drinking and women.
He often borrowed wine from Wang Lao and Wu Fu and slept drunk. Wu Fu and Wang Lao often saw a dragon above him and felt very strange.
Every time Emperor Gaozu came to buy wine and stayed in the hotel to drink, the wine in the hotel sold several times more than usual.
When a strange phenomenon was discovered, at the end of the year, these two hotels often wrote off the credit debts of Gao Zu.
Emperor Gaozu once went to Xianyang to perform corvées and allowed people to watch. When he saw Qin Shihuang, he sighed and said: Ah, a real man should look like this!
Lu Gong, a single father, was friendly with the magistrate of Peixian County. In order to avoid his enemies from visiting the magistrate's house, he moved his family to Peixian County.
When the outstanding officials in Pei County heard that the county magistrate had a distinguished guest, they all went to send gifts to congratulate him.
Xiao He is the chief official of the county and is in charge of collecting gifts. He said to all distinguished guests: "Those whose gifts are less than one thousand yuan should sit down in the hall."
When Emperor Gaozu was the chief of the pavilion, he always looked down upon the officials. So he deceitfully said "Congratulations on thousands of dollars" on his name card, but in fact he didn't take out any money.
When the famous assassin was handed in, Lu Gong was shocked, stood up, and went to the door to greet Gaozu.
Lu Gong was a good person, so when he saw Gaozu's appearance, he respected him especially and led him to sit in the hall.
Xiao He said: Liu Ji originally talked a lot but rarely achieved anything.
Emperor Gaozu then teased the guests in the hall and sat at the top of the table, showing no humility.
The banquet was about to end, and Duke Lu signaled Gao Zu not to leave with his eyes.
Gaozu finished his drink and stayed behind.
Lu Gong said: I have been good at meeting people since I was young. I have met many people, but none of them is as noble as you, Liu Ji. I hope you, Liu Ji, take care of yourself.
I have a biological daughter who is willing to be your wife, Liu Ji, who holds a broom and sweeps.
After the banquet, Mrs. Lu was angry with Mr. Lu and said: "At first you always wanted to make this daughter different and marry her to a noble man."
Pei Ling was friendly with you and asked to marry your daughter, but you didn't agree. Why did you arbitrarily decide to marry Liu Ji?
Lu Gong said: This is not what you women and children can understand.
So he married his daughter to Liu Ji.
The daughter of Duke Lu was Empress Lu, who gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.
summary: Emperor Gaozu, born Liu Ji in Peixian County, was the son of Taigong and Liu Yu. His mother became pregnant after dreaming of meeting a god while resting by a lake, during which a dragon appeared on her body. Gaozu possessed distinctive physical features including a high nose, dragon-like forehead, beautiful beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left leg. He was generous, charitable, and broad-minded, with lofty ambitions that set him apart from ordinary people. As an adult, Gaozu served as the chief of Sishui Pavilion, where he became familiar with local officials and enjoyed drinking and women. He frequently borrowed wine from local establishments, where shopkeepers observed a dragon above him when he was drunk. During a corvée trip to Xianyang, he saw Qin Shihuang and expressed his desire to achieve similar greatness. Lu Gong, impressed by Gaozu's appearance at a gathering, married his daughter to him despite his wife's objections. This daughter became Empress Lu, mother of Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪

translation:
When Emperor Gaozu was the director of the pavilion, he once asked for leave to go home.
Queen Lu and her two children were weeding in the field. An old man passed by and asked for some water. Queen Lu gave him some food.
The old man met Empress Lu and said, "My wife is a noble person in the world."
Empress Lu asked him to read the faces of the two children. The old man looked at Xiaohui and said: Madam, the reason why she is so noble is because of this child.
After seeing Lu Yuan, he was also a noble prime minister.
The old man had already left, and Gaozu happened to come to the field from someone else's house. Empress Lu told him that a guest was passing by and showed our faces to mother and son, saying that we would both be noble people in the future. Gaozu asked where my father was, and Empress Lu said: "It's not far away."
Gaozu caught up with the old man and asked him.
The old man said: I met my wife and children just now, and they are all similar to you. Your appearance is beyond words.
Emperor Gaozu thanked me and said: If it is true as my father said, I will never forget your kindness to me.
When Emperor Gaozu became famous, he didn't even know where the old man was.
When Emperor Gaozu was the director of the pavilion, he used bamboo skin as a hat. This hat was made by a thief he sent to Xue County, and he often wore it. When he became a distinguished person, he still often wore it. The so-called "Liu's crown" refers to this kind of hat.
Emperor Gaozu served as the pavilion chief and sent servants to Mount Li for the county. Many of the servants fled on the way.
He estimated that by the time they reached Lishan Mountain, everyone would have fled. He went to the swamp area west of Fengyi and stopped to drink. At night, Gaozu released the slaves he had escorted.
Emperor Gaozu said: "Everyone, let's go. I'm running away from now on!"
Among the servants, there were more than ten young and strong men who were willing to follow Gaozu.
Emperor Gaozu was drunk, so he took a small road through the swamp that night and sent a man to explore the way.
The person who went out to explore the road came back and reported: There is a big snake lying across the road ahead. Please go back.
Emperor Gaozu was drunk and said: "When a hero walks, there is nothing to be afraid of!"
So he stepped forward, drew his sword and struck the snake, cutting it into two pieces, and the road was opened.
After walking for a few miles, he got drunk and lay down to sleep.
The people behind came to the place where the snake was killed and saw an old lady crying at night.
People asked why she was crying. The old lady said: Someone killed my son, so I cried.
People said again: Old lady, why was your son killed?
The old lady said: My son, the son of the White Emperor, turned into a snake and was lying on the road. Now he was killed by the son of the Red Emperor, so I cried.
People thought the old lady was dishonest and wanted to give her a hard time. The old lady suddenly disappeared.
Those who were left behind arrived at the place where Gaozu was resting, and Gaozu had already woken up.
They told Gaozu what had just happened. Gaozu was secretly happy and felt arrogant.
Those who followed him grew in awe of him.
Qin Shihuang often said that "there is the emperor's energy in the southeast", so he traveled to the east to suppress the emperor's energy in the southeast.
Emperor Gaozu suspected that the incident was related to him, so he ran away and hid among the rocks in the Mangshan and Dangshan areas.
Queen Lu searched with others, and often found Gaozu as soon as they arrived.
Emperor Gaozu felt strange and asked Empress Lu. Empress Lu said: There are often clouds where you are. If you look for the clouds, you can often be found.
Gaozu was very happy.
summary: While serving as pavilion chief, Gaozu encountered an old man who predicted that Empress Lu and their children would become noble, and that Gaozu's own appearance was beyond description. When escorting servants to Mount Li, many fled, so Gaozu released the remaining servants and became a fugitive. Drunk one night, he killed a large snake blocking his path. An old woman later claimed the snake was the son of the White Emperor, killed by the son of the Red Emperor, which made Gaozu secretly proud and increased his followers' awe of him.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪

translation:
When some of the children in Pei County heard about this, many wanted to join him.
In the autumn of the first year of Qin II, Chen Sheng and others revolted in Qixian County and established themselves as kings in Chenxian County, known as Zhang Chu.
Most of the counties and counties killed their chiefs in response to Chen Sheng.
The magistrate of Peixian County was frightened and wanted to respond to Chen Sheng with Peiju. The chief official Xiao He and the jailer Cao Shen said to him: As an official of the Qin Dynasty, you are now rebelling against Qin and leading the children of Peixian County. I am afraid they will not obey your orders.
I hope you can gather hundreds of people who are fleeing outside. Use this power to intimidate the masses, and they will not dare to disobey your orders.
The county magistrate sent Fan Kuai to summon Liu Ji. Liu Ji's team already numbered nearly a hundred people.
So Fan Kuai followed Liu Ji to Peixian County.
The magistrate of Peixian County regretted it again. Fearing that something might happen to Liu Ji, he closed the city gates and sent people to defend him, intending to kill Xiao He and Cao Shen.
Xiao He and Cao Shen were frightened and climbed over the city wall to attach themselves to Liu Ji.
Liu Ji wrote a letter on silk and sent it to the city, telling the elders of Peixian County: The world has been suffering from the tyranny of the Qin Dynasty for a long time.
Now the elders are guarding the city for Pei Ling, but the princes from all over the world have revolted and want to massacre Pei County.
If the elders of Peixian County unite to kill Pei Ling and select the leader among their children who can be appointed as the leader to respond to the princes' army, then the lives of the whole family can be saved.
Otherwise, both father and son would be killed and their deaths would be meaningless.
The elders led their children to kill Pei Ling, opened the city gate, and welcomed Liu Ji, hoping to make him the magistrate of Pei County.
Liu Ji said: The world is in chaos, and all the princes are in rebellion. If the elected generals are not qualified, they will be completely defeated.
I am not begrudging my own life, but I am afraid that my talents are too weak to save my father, brothers and children.
This is a big deal, and I hope we can jointly elect someone who can do the job.
Xiao He, Cao Shen and others were civil servants who valued their wealth and life, and were afraid that the Qin Dynasty would exterminate their entire clans if the matter failed, so they all recommended Liu Ji.
The elders all said: We usually hear many strange things about Liu Ji. It seems that Liu Ji should be honored. And after divination, no one is more auspicious than Liu Ji.
At this time, Liu Ji repeatedly made concessions, but no one dared to take up the post. Finally, Liu Ji was appointed Duke of Pei.
In the courtyard of the Pei County Yamen, they offered sacrifices to the Yellow Emperor and Chi You, and used the blood of sacrifices to raise drum flags.
The flags are all red, because the snake Liu Ji killed was the son of the White Emperor, and the one who killed the snake was the son of the Red Emperor, so he respected red.
So the young men and powerful officials, such as Xiao He, Cao Shen, Fan Kuai and others, recruited soldiers for Pei Gong. They gathered two to three thousand people to attack Hu Ling and Fang Yu, and then returned to defend Fengyi.
In the second year of Qin II, General Chen Sheng led Zhou Zhang's army to the west to play in the water and return.
Yan, Zhao, Qi, and Wei all established themselves as kings.
Xiang Liang and Xiang Yu raised troops in Wu.
summary: During the Qin II period, Chen Sheng's rebellion inspired the magistrate of Peixian County to consider revolt. Following advice from Xiao He and Cao Shen, Fan Kuai was sent to summon Liu Ji. After the magistrate reneged, the elders killed him and welcomed Liu Ji, who became Duke of Pei after initially declining. They raised two to three thousand soldiers, attacked nearby areas, and returned to defend Fengyi. When Yong Chi betrayed Pei Gong by surrendering to Wei, Pei Gong failed to recapture Fengyi and sought help from Xiang Liang, who provided additional troops.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪

translation:
Song Yi warned him, but he didn't listen.
Qin sent troops to reinforce Zhang Han and secretly attacked Xiang Liang at night. They defeated Xiang Liang in Dingtao and died in the battle.
Pei Gong and Xiang Yu were attacking Chenliu. When they heard that Xiang Liang was dead, they led their troops and marched eastward with General Lu.
Lu Chen was stationed to the east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu was stationed to the west of Pengcheng, and Peigong was stationed in Dang.
Zhang Han had defeated Xiang Liang's army and thought that the enemies in Chu did not need to worry, so he crossed the Yellow River and attacked Zhao from the north, defeating the Zhao army.
At this time, Zhao Xie was the king of Zhao, and Qin general Wang Li besieged Zhao Xie in Julu City. This is the so-called Hebei Army.
In the third year of Qin II, King Huai of Chu saw that Xiang Liang's army was defeated. He was frightened, moved away from Xutai, established his capital in Pengcheng, merged the armies of Lu Chen and Xiang Yu, and took command personally.
Peigong was appointed as the governor of Dang County and was granted the title of Marquis of Wu'an, commanding the army of Dang County.
Xiang Yu was granted the title of Marquis of Chang'an and his title was Duke of Lu.
Lu Chen was appointed Situ, and his father Lu Qing was appointed Ling Yin.
Zhao requested rescue many times, so King Chu Huai sent Song Yi as his general, Xiang Yu as his second general, and Fan Zeng as his junior general, and went north to rescue Zhao.
He ordered Pei Gong to march west and invade Guanzhong.
An agreement was made with the generals: whoever conquers Guanzhong first will be crowned king in Guanzhong.
At this time, the Qin army was strong and often took advantage of the victory to pursue, but the generals did not think it was advantageous to enter the pass first.
Only Xiang Yu hated Qin for defeating Xiang Liang's army, and was so angry that he was willing to enter the pass with Peigong west.
King Huai's veterans all said: Xiang Yu is agile but fierce, cunning and cruel.
Xiang Yu once attacked Xiangcheng, but no one was left alive in Xiangcheng. They were all buried alive. Wherever they passed, they were slaughtered and destroyed.
Moreover, the Chu army attacked and conquered many times, and King Chen and Xiang Liang failed before.
It is better to send another kind-hearted elder to march westward with the call of justice and explain the truth clearly to Qin's father and brothers.
Qin's father and brothers have suffered from their monarch's rule for a long time. Now if they can really get a generous elder to go to Guanzhong without bullying and tyranny, they should be able to win Guanzhong.
Now Xiang Yu is so fierce that he cannot be dispatched.
Only Pei Gong, who has always been a tolerant elder, can be dispatched.
In the end, King Huai did not agree to Xiang Yu's request and sent Peigong to the west to attack Qin. Collecting the scattered troops of King Chen and Xiang Liang, they passed through Dang and arrived at Chengyang. They faced off against the Qin army in Gangli and defeated the two Qin troops.
The Chu army sent troops to attack Wang Li and severely defeated his army.
Peigong led his troops to the west, met Peng Yue in Changyi, and joined him to attack the Qin army. The battle was not won.
Returning to Li County, I met Marquis Gangwu and captured his army, about 4,000 people, and merged them together.
Peigong, together with the troops of Wei General Huang Xin and Wei Shentu Wu Pu, jointly attacked Changyi, but Changyi was not captured.
summary: Pei Gong joined forces with Xiang Yu, and together they achieved military successes while suffering setbacks. After Xiang Liang's death, King Huai of Chu appointed Pei Gong as governor of Dang County and ordered him to march west into Guanzhong, promising kingship to whoever entered first. Despite Xiang Yu's desire to join, King Huai's advisors favored Pei Gong's reputation as a tolerant elder. Pei Gong collected scattered troops, defeated Qin forces, and through strategic decisions including sparing the governor of Nanyang County, gained widespread surrenders.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪

translation:
When the troops are led westward, no one will fail to surrender.
Arriving at Danshui, Gaowu Houyi and Xianghou Wangling surrendered in Xiling.
When he returned to attack Hu Yang, he met Fan Jun's general Mei Rong, and together with him, they forced Xixian and Lixian to surrender.
Ningchang of Wei was sent as an envoy to Qin Guanzhong, but the envoy did not come back.
By this time, Zhang Han had led the entire army to surrender to Xiang Yu in Zhao.
At first, Xiang Yu and Song Yi marched north to rescue Zhao. When Xiang Yu killed Song Yi, he replaced him as general. Many generals, such as Qing Bu, were subordinate to Xiang Yu. He defeated Qin general Wang Li's army and made Zhang Han surrender, and all the princes joined him.
When Zhao Gao had killed Qin II, he sent people to see Pei Gong and wanted to make an agreement to carve up Guanzhong and claim the throne. Pei Gong thought it was a fraud, so he adopted Zhang Liang's strategy and sent Li Sheng and Lu Jia to lobby the Qin generals. They lured them with their own interests and took the opportunity to attack Wuguan and break the pass.
He also fought with the Qin army in the south of Lantian. He added more suspects and planted more flags. No looting was allowed in the places he passed. The people of Qin were very happy. The Qin army collapsed and the Qin army was defeated.
They fought again in the north of Lantian and defeated the Qin army again.
Taking advantage of the victory, he pursued and completely defeated the Qin army.
In October of the first year of the Han Dynasty, Pei Gong's army arrived at Bashang before the princes.
The Prince of Qin rode on a plain carriage with a white horse, tied his neck with a ribbon, sealed the emperor's seal and talisman, and surrendered beside Zhi Road.
Some generals advocated killing the King of Qin.
Pei Gong said: King Huai of Chu sent me originally because I can be tolerant. Besides, it is unlucky to kill someone after they have already surrendered.
So he handed the King of Qin over to the officials and headed west into Xianyang.
Pei Gong wanted to stay in the palace to rest, but after being persuaded by Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang, he sealed off the valuable treasures, property and storehouses in the Qin Palace and returned to the army.
He summoned the elders and heroes from each county and said: "The elders have suffered from the harsh punishments of the Qin Dynasty for a long time. Those who slander the government will be exterminated, and those who gather to discuss will be beheaded in the streets."
I made an agreement with the princes that whoever enters Guanzhong first will be crowned king in Guanzhong, and I should be crowned king in Guanzhong.
It was agreed with the elders that the law has only three chapters: the death penalty for murder, and the punishment for injury and robbery commensurate with the crime committed.
All other laws of the Qin Dynasty were abolished.
Officials and people should live in peace and harmony.
The reason why I am here is to eliminate harm for the elders. There will be no bullying or cruel behavior. Don't be afraid.
The reason why I returned to Junba was to wait for the princes to arrive and formulate a common agreement.
Peigong sent people and officials from the Qin Dynasty to patrol the county and countryside to inform the people.
The people of Qin were very happy and rushed to entertain the soldiers with cattle and sheep, wine and food.
Pei Gong refused to accept it again, saying: "There is a lot of grain in the warehouse, there is no shortage, and I don't want to waste it on the people."
summary: Pei Gong's army arrived at Bashang in October of the first Han year, where the King of Qin surrendered. After initially wanting to rest in the palace, Pei Gong heeded advice to seal the treasures and return to camp. He established the three-chapter law code, abolished harsh Qin laws, and won the people's support by refusing their offerings. When Xiang Yu's forces approached, Pei Gong's subordinate Cao Wushang informed Xiang Yu of his intentions, but Xiang Bo's intervention and Pei Gong's apology at Hongmen prevented conflict.
rel_path: 史记/十二本纪/高祖本纪

translation:
King Xie of Zhao moved to another place and became king.
Zhang Er, the general of Zhao, was granted the title of King of Changshan and established the capital of Xiangguo.
He granted Dangyang Lord Yingbu the title of King of Jiujiang and established six counties as his capital.
King Huai of Chu named Zhu Guo Gong Ao the title of King of Linjiang and established his capital in Jiangling.
Wu Rui of Fan County was granted the title of King of Hengshan and Zhu County was established as his capital.
Zang Tu, the general of Yan, was made King of Yan and his capital was established in Ji County.
Han Guang, the original king of Yan, moved to Liaodong and became king.
Han Guang refused to obey, and Zang Tu attacked and killed Han Guang without end.
He was granted the title of Anjun, Chenyu, and three counties in Hejian, and lived in Nanpi.
One hundred thousand households were granted to Mei Yi.
In April, Xiang Yujing dismissed his troops and dispersed, and the princes returned to their feudal states.
When the King of Han returned to his country, King Xiang sent 30,000 troops to follow him. The soldiers of Chu and other vassal states admired the King of Han and followed him with tens of thousands of soldiers.
They entered Eclipse from the south of Du County. After leaving, they burned down the plank road to prevent attacks by the princes' armies and bandits. They also expressed to Xiang Yu that they had no intention of marching eastward.
When they arrived at Nanzheng, many of the generals and soldiers fled back on the way. The soldiers all sang songs and wanted to return to the east.
Han Xin advised the King of Han: Xiang Yu made the meritorious generals kings, while the king was made alone in Nanzheng. This was actually demoting him.
The officers and soldiers in the army were all from the east of Mount Laoshan, and they were eager to return home day and night. If you take advantage of them when they are strong, you can achieve great success.
When the world is at peace and everyone naturally feels at ease, it can no longer be exploited.
It is better to decide to march eastward and fight for the power of the world.
Xiang Yu left Hangu Pass and sent people to move to Emperor Yi.
Said: In ancient times, emperors ruled over thousands of miles of land and had to live upstream.
He sent envoys to move Emperor Yi to Chen County in Changsha and urged him to leave quickly. The ministers gradually betrayed Emperor Yi, so Xiang Yu secretly asked the kings of Hengshan and Linjiang to attack him and kill Emperor Yi in the south of the Yangtze River.
Xiang Yu resented Tian Rong and made Qi general Tian Du the king of Qi. Tian Rong was angry and proclaimed himself king of Qi. He killed Tian Du and rebelled against Xiang Chu. He gave the general's seal to Peng Yue and asked him to raise troops in Liang to rebel against Chu.
Chu sent Xiao Gongjiao to attack Peng Yue, and Peng Yue defeated Xiao Gongjiao.
Chen Yu resented Xiang Yu for not making him king, so he sent Xia Sui to lobby Tian Rong and borrow troops to attack Zhang Er.
Qi lent troops to Chen Yu and defeated Zhang Er, king of Changshan. Zhang Er fled and joined the king of Han.
Chen Yu took King Zhao Xie back from Dai and established him as King of Zhao. King Zhao then named Chen Yu the Dai King.
Xiang Yu was furious and sent troops north to attack them.
In August, the King of Han used Han Xin's strategy to return from the old route and attack King Yong Zhanghan.
Zhang Han met the Han army in Chencang, but King Yong was defeated and retreated. He stopped to engage in battle at Haozhen, but failed again and fled to Feiqiu.
The king of Han immediately pacified Yongdi.
He went east to Xianyang, led his army to besiege King Yong in Feiqiu, and sent generals to capture Longxi, Beidi and Shangjun.
He sent generals Xue Ou and Wang Xiu out of Wuguan, and with the help of Wang Ling's troops stationed in Nanyang, they met the Taigong and Empress Lu in Peixian County.
summary: Xiang Yu later broke the agreement, making Pei Gong King of Han in Ba, Shu, and Hanzhong. The King of Han used Han Xin's strategy to march eastward, attacking and defeating King Yong Zhanghan. Over subsequent years, the Han and Chu forces engaged in prolonged warfare with shifting fortunes. The King of Han survived assassination attempts, built alliances, and eventually defeated Xiang Yu at Gaixia, where Xiang Yu's forces heard Chu songs and were routed.

translation:
So Gaozu set out.
The people of Peixian County came out in large numbers and went to the west of the city to contribute cattle and wine.
Emperor Gaozu stayed again, pitched a tent, and feasted for three days.
The fathers and brothers of Pei County all kowtowed and asked, "Pei County is fortunate enough to be exempted from the corvee, but Fengyi has not yet been exempted from the corvee. Please show mercy to Fengyi."
Emperor Gaozu said: Fengyi is the place where I grew up, and I will never forget it. I only went to help the Wei state because Fengyi rebelled against me because of Yong Chi. The fathers and brothers of Peixian County insisted on their request, and then they exempted Fengyi from the corvee. Like Peixian County, they made Peihou Liu Bi the king of Wu.
The generals of the Han army pursued Yingbu's army on both the north and south sides of the Taoshui River. They defeated Yingbu's army and captured and killed Yingbu in Poyang.
Fan Kuai led another army to pacify Daidi and killed Chen Xi in the city.
In November, Emperor Gaozu returned to Chang'an from the army that conquered Yingbu.
In December, Emperor Gaozu said: The First Emperor of Qin, King Chen She of Chu Yin, King Anli of Wei, King Qi Min, and King Zhao Daoxiang all died without heirs, and were given to ten families to guard their tombs, twenty families of Qin Shihuang, and five families of Wei Gongzi Wuji.
All local officials and people who were coerced by Chen Xi and Zhao Li were pardoned.
When Chen Xi's surrendered generals said that Chen Xi was rebelling, King Lu Wan of Yan sent people to Chen Xi to participate in the conspiracy.
Emperor Gaozu sent Marquis Piyang to pick up Lu Wan, but Lu Wan refused to come because he was ill.
Marquis Piyang came back and explained in detail that there were signs of Lu Wan's rebellion.
In February, Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo were sent to lead an army to attack Lu Wan, King of Yan. Pardon the officials and people of Yan who participated in the rebellion.
The prince Liu Jian was granted the title of King of Yan.
When Emperor Gaozu attacked Yingbu, he was shot by a stray arrow and fell ill during the march.
The condition was serious, so Empress Lu invited a good doctor. The doctor went in to see Gaozu. Gaozu asked the doctor. The doctor said: The disease can be cured.
So Emperor Gaozu scolded the doctor and said: I conquered the world as a commoner with a three-foot sword. Isn't this destiny?
Destiny is in the sky, even if there is a Bian Que, what's the use!
Emperor Gaozu refused to let the doctor cure the disease, rewarded him with fifty pounds of gold, and told him to leave.
Soon Empress Lu asked Gaozu: If your Majesty, Xiao Xiangguo, dies in a hundred years, who will succeed him?
Emperor Gaozu said: Cao Shen can do it.
When asked about the next step, Emperor Gaozu said: "The royal tomb is fine."
However, Wang Ling is a bit naive and Chen Ping can help him.
Chen Ping is very wise, but it is difficult for him to act alone.
Zhou Bo is steady and kind, but lacks literary talents, but the one who can stabilize the Liu family must be Zhou Bo, and he can be made a Taiwei.
Empress Lu asked the next question, and Gaozu said: This is not something I will be able to know in the future.
Lu Huo and thousands of cavalry stayed at the frontier and waited, hoping that Gaozu would recover from his illness and go to apologize to Gaozu himself.
On the first day of the fourth month, Emperor Gaozu died in Changle Palace.
After four days there was no mourning.
summary: After establishing the Han Dynasty, Gaozu faced rebellions from various kings including Zang Tu, Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Yingbu. He personally led campaigns against them, executing or defeating the rebels. During a visit to his hometown Peixian County, Gaozu composed the famous Song of the Great Wind and exempted the county from corvée service. He died from an arrow wound sustained during the campaign against Yingbu, refusing medical treatment by declaring his fate determined by heaven. Before death, he designated successors for key positions, including Cao Shen, Wang Ling, Chen Ping, and Zhou Bo. Gaozu was buried in Changling with the posthumous title Emperor Gao, having established the Han Dynasty from humble beginnings.

translation:
"Kingdom" says: The east is called barbarians.
Yi means root, which means that God is benevolent and cherishes all living beings, and all things grow out of the ground against the soil.
Therefore, people in the East are docile by nature and can be easily controlled by morality, so that a country of gentlemen and a country of immortality appeared.
The Yi are divided into nine branches, they are the Yi, Yu, Fang, Huang, Bai, Chi, Xuan, Feng and Yang.
So Confucius wanted to live in the Jiuyi area.
In the past, Yao ordered Xizhong to live in Woyi. There was a place called Yanggu, where the sun rose.
Emperor Taikang of the Xia Dynasty lost his virtue and the Yi people began to rebel.
Since Shaokang, the Yi people have admired the teachings of the imperial court for generations, so they submitted themselves to the emperor and presented their music and dance.
Jie's rule was brutal, and barbarians from various tribes invaded the interior. Chengtang of the Yin Dynasty changed the destiny, attacked and pacified Xia.
By the time of Zhongding, Lan Yi invaded the interior.
In the more than three hundred years since then, the Yi people sometimes surrendered and sometimes rebelled.
When Wu Yi declined, Dongyi gradually became stronger and stronger, so they moved to the Huaihe River and Mount Tai areas respectively, and gradually lived in the Central Plains.
When King Wu of Zhou destroyed Zhou, Sushen came to contribute arrowheads made of stone and arrows made of wood.
Guan Shu and Cai Shu betrayed the Zhou court, so they recruited and seduced the Yi Di. Zhou Gong conquered Guan Shu and Cai Shu and finally pacified Shu Yi.
During the reign of King Kang of Zhou, Sushen came again.
Later, Xu Yi usurped the title of emperor and led the nine barbarians to attack Zongzhou and attack westward to the bank of the Yellow River.
King Mu of Zhou was afraid that Xu Yi would be strong, so he separated the princes in the east and asked King Xu Yan to rule them.
King Xu Yan lived in Shumian, Huangchi. The land was five hundred miles in circumference. King Yan promoted benevolence and righteousness, and thirty-six countries came to worship him from all over the land.
King Zhou Mu later got the horses Chiji and Quer, so he sent Zaofu to ride the horses to inform the Chu State and order the Chu State to attack the Xu State. They arrived in one day.
So King Wen of Chu raised a large number of troops to attack Xu State and destroyed Xu State.
King Xu Yan was kind but ignorant of political skills and could not bear to let his countrymen fight, so he failed.
King Xu Yan was finally defeated at the foot of Shushan Mountain in Wuyuan County, Pengcheng City. Tens of thousands of people followed him, so Shushan Mountain was called Xushan Mountain.
King Zhou Li was cruel and unruly, and Huaiyi invaded. The emperor sent Guo Zhong to attack Huaiyi, but failed to win. King Xuan of Zhou ordered Duke Zhao to go and conquer Huaiyi, and pacified Huaiyi.
When King You of Zhou became debauched and violent, the barbarians from all sides invaded alternately. It was not until Duke Huan of Qi established his hegemony that he repelled the barbarians.
When King Chu Ling was applying for an alliance, Huaiyi also came to participate in the alliance.
Later, the Yue Kingdom moved to Langye and fought with the Huaiyi. From then on, they invaded and harmed all the countries in the Central Plains and invaded and destroyed small countries.
Qin State annexed the six countries, and Huaiyi and Siyi were scattered into ordinary people's houses.
Chen She raised an army and the world collapsed. Weiman, a native of Yan State, took refuge in North Korea and thus ruled North Korea.
More than a hundred years later, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty destroyed North Korea, and since then the Yicai have been banned from visiting Kyoto.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, the Qi people invaded the border. In the early years of Jianwu, the Qi people came to pay tribute again.
At that time, the Liaodong governor's sacrifice to Xu was very powerful in the north, and his reputation was very high overseas. So Jia, Qi, Wa, and Han came to the court from thousands of miles away to contribute. Therefore, after Emperor Zhang and Emperor He, envoys communicated with each other.
At the time of trouble in Yongchu, Shu Yi began to invade and plunder; Emperors Huan and Ling were in political chaos, and Shu Yi gradually spread.
Since the Zhongxing Dynasty, barbarians from all over the world came to submit. Although there were frequent rebellions, the envoys did not stop. Therefore, the customs, customs, and geographical environment of these countries can be roughly described.
Dongyi generally have settled in one place for generations and like to drink, sing and dance. Sometimes they wear crowns, silk clothes, and utensils such as zu and beans.
This is the reason why China lost its etiquette and can be found in Siyi.
The barbarians, barbarians, Rong, and Di are collectively called the four barbarians, just like the dukes, lords, uncles, sons, and men are all called princes.
Fuyu country is a thousand miles north of Xuantu.
It borders Gaoguli to the south, Yilou to Shumian, Xianbei to the west, and Weishui to the north.
The area has a radius of two thousand miles, and it is originally a territory for reducing people.
At first, the king of the Northern Yi Suoli Kingdom went out on a tour, and his maid became pregnant. When the king came back, he planned to kill her.
summary: The historical and cultural evolution of the Eastern Yi peoples, beginning with their origins and characteristics. The Yi, meaning "root," were considered docile and easily governed by morality, leading to the emergence of a "country of gentlemen" and a "country of immortality." They were divided into nine branches, and Confucius once expressed a desire to live among them. Early interactions with Chinese dynasties included Yao sending Xizhong to Woyi and the Yi submitting to Xia rulers, though rebellions occurred under tyrants like Jie. Over centuries, the Yi fluctuated between submission and revolt, with notable events such as Xu Yi usurping the title of emperor and attacking Zongzhou, only to be defeated by King Wen of Chu. Later, during the Zhou and Han dynasties, the Yi peoples, including Huaiyi and Siyi, were scattered, conquered, or assimilated, with periods of tribute and conflict under rulers like Wang Mang and Emperor Wu of Han. Korea, originally granted to Jizi by King Wu of Zhou, had a culture of etiquette and prohibitions. Over time, it was influenced by Chinese refugees and eventually conquered by Emperor Wu of Han, who established four commanderies. The text describes the three Han states: Mahan, Chenhan, and Benchen, each with distinct customs, including farming, iron trade, and rituals. Japan, southeast of Korea, comprised over a hundred island states, with Yamatai as the leading kingdom. Japanese customs included tattooing, polygamy, and divination. The text concludes with a reflection on Jizi's influence on Korean customs and the gradual decline of these traditions due to Chinese contact.

translation:
The maid said: I saw an air mass in the sky as big as an egg before, and it landed on my body, and I became pregnant.
The king imprisoned her and she later gave birth to a boy.
The king ordered the boy to be thrown into a pigsty, and the pigs breathed on him to prevent him from dying.
Then he threw him into the stable to be breaded, and the horse also panted at him like a pig.
The king thought he was a god, so he allowed the child's mother to adopt him and named him Shuming.
When Shuming grew up, he was good at archery. The king hated his bravery and wanted to kill him.
Dongming escaped, went south to Yishui, and struck the water with his bow. As a result, all the fish and turtles gathered and floated to the surface. Shuming was able to cross the river on the fish and turtles, and he went to Fuyu and became the king there.
The land of Fuyu State is the flattest and most open among the Dongyi regions, and the soil is suitable for growing grains.
That bundle produced famous horses, red jade, mink uranium, and jade beads as big as jujubes.
They built a walled city with palisades, and within the city were palaces, warehouses, and prisons.
The people there are strong and brave but cautious and kind-hearted, and do not engage in invasion and looting.
They used bows and arrows and swords and spears as weapons.
They use the six animals as their official names, including horse, ox, and dog, and the cities and villages are all under the jurisdiction of each official. They use Zu and Dou to eat and drink. During court meetings, they practice the etiquette of paying homage, washing titles, and bowing to ascenders and descenders.
They worship the gods in the twelfth lunar month and hold grand gatherings for many days, eating, drinking, singing and dancing together, which is called "Yinggu".
At this time, we should stop using torture and arresting people in prison, and release the prisoners.
When a war breaks out, they also sacrifice to heaven, kill cows, and use their hooves to predict good or bad luck.
Pedestrians on the road like to sing and shout, no matter day or night, and their singing never stops.
The custom in Nabu was to use severe punishment, and all the family members of those who were executed were taken into slavery.
The penalty for stealing something is twelve times the amount.
Adultery between men and women was punished to death, especially vicious and jealous women. After being killed, their bodies were placed on the mountain.
When the elder brother dies, the younger brother takes his sister-in-law as his wife.
After death, there is an outer coffin but no inner coffin.
They killed living people and buried them in hundreds of people.
The king was buried in a jade box. The Han court often gave the jade box to Xuantu County in advance. When the king died, he sent people to pick up the jade box and bury the king.
During the Jianwu period, all the countries in Dongyi came to contribute and pay homage.
In the twenty-fifth year, King Fuyu sent envoys to offer tribute, and Guangwu rewarded them generously. From then on, the envoys communicated with each other every year.
In the fifth year of Emperor An's reign, King Fuyu led seven or eight thousand infantry and cavalry troops to invade and plunder Lelang for the first time, killing and injuring officials and people, and later surrendered again.
summary: The text then details specific Yi groups, starting with Fuyu, located north of Xuantu. Fuyu was a flat, fertile land producing horses, jade, and mink. Its people were strong, brave, and kind, using bows and swords, and practicing rituals like the "Yinggu" festival. They had severe punishments, including execution for adultery and theft, and practiced levirate marriage. Burial customs involved jade boxes for kings, provided by the Han court. Fuyu engaged in tribute and conflict with Han, including invasions under King An and later defeats by Gongsunyu.

translation:
Shuwoju is located on the side of Gaima Mountain in Gaoguli, with the sea to the east, bordering Yilou and Fuyu to the north, and Guqi to the south.
Shuwoju is narrow in the east-west direction and long in the north-south direction, which can be equivalent to a thousand miles square.
The land there is fertile, backed by mountains and facing the sea, and is suitable for grain growth. The people are good at farming and have village leaders.
The people in Nabu are naturally upright, brave and tenacious, and are good at fighting on foot with a spear in hand.
There are similarities between speech, food, shelter, clothing and sentences.
For their funeral, a large wooden coffin was built. It is more than ten feet long. One end of the wooden coffin is dug out to serve as a door. The newly deceased is buried temporarily to let the skin and flesh rot away, and then the bones are taken out and put into the coffin.
The whole family was put into a coffin. They used wood to carve the image of the deceased in life, and the number of images they carved increased with the number of dead people.
Emperor Wu subtracted North Korea and made the Woju area Xuantu County.
Later, it was invaded by barbarians, and Xuantu County was moved to the northwest of Gaoguli, while Woju was changed to a county, under the jurisdiction of the eastern Lelang Commandery.
At the time of Guangwu, the captaincy officers were removed, and later these places were granted the title of Wojuhou, the leader of Woju.
Woju's land was small and sandwiched between big countries, so it belonged to Gouli.
Gouli also appointed the chief among them as envoys to supervise Woju, requiring Woju to pay taxes, mink, cloth, fish, salt, and food from the sea, and recruit Woju's beauties as maids and concubines.
There is also Beiwoju, also known as Zhigoulou, which is more than 800 miles away from Nanwoju.
The customs of North Woju are the same as those of South Woju.
The southern part of the border is connected with Yilou.
The Yilou people like to invade and plunder by boat, and the people in Beiwoju are afraid. Every summer, they often hide in rock caves and wrap their faces. In winter, when the waterway for boats is blocked, they go down the mountains and live in villages.
The old man who wrapped it said that he once got a piece of coarse cloth in the sea. The shape of the clothes was like that worn by a man of average height, but the two sleeves were three feet long.
On the shore, I saw a man riding a broken boat with a face on his head. He and he couldn't understand each other. He died without eating.
He also said that there is a kingdom of girls in the sea, where there are no men.
Some legends say that there is a sacred well in the Daughter Kingdom, and you can give birth to a child if you look at the sacred well. It borders Gaoguli and Shuanghui in the far north, borders Lihan in the south, connects directly to the sea on the far side, and leads to Lelang in the west.
Zi, Woju, and Gouli were originally places in Korea.
In the past, King Wu of Zhou Dynasty granted Korea to Jizi. Jizi taught the people etiquette and the techniques of farming and raising silkworms, and also formulated eight prohibitions.
People there never steal from each other, and there is no need to close their doors.
Women are chaste and trustworthy.
When eating and drinking, use canopies and beans as ritual utensils.
More than forty generations later, Hou Zhun came to North Korea and claimed the title of king.
summary: Yilou, northeast of Fuyu, was a mountainous, cold region where people lived in caves and wore pigskin. They were brave archers using poisoned arrows and were known for plundering. Gaoguli, south of Fuyu, had five tribes and a history of conflict with Han, including invasions and tribute missions. Their customs included sacrifices to heaven, singing and dancing, and severe punishments. Woju, near Gaoguli, was fertile and known for farming and foot combat. Their burial practices involved large wooden coffins and bone collection.

translation:
Wuhuan was originally from the Donghu tribe.
In the early Han Dynasty, the Xiongnu Maodun eliminated Donghu, and the remaining people guarded Wuhuan Mountain, so they took Wuhuan as their tribal title.
The custom of Wuhuan is to be good at horseback riding and archery. Wuhuan people are mainly engaged in hunting birds and animals.
The Wuhuan people graze on water and grass and have no fixed residence.
They used felt tents as houses, with doors opening eastward toward the sun.
They ate meat, drank cheese, and made clothes from the hairs of birds and animals.
They attach great importance to young people and despise the elderly. They have a strong temperament and are not open-minded.
When he gets angry, he kills his father and brothers, but never kills his mother, because her mother has her own tribe and her father and brothers have no one to take revenge.
Anyone who is brave and strong and can handle decisive battles and lawsuits is elected as the leader of the tribe. The leader is not inherited from generation to generation.
Each town has its own small leader, and hundreds or thousands of towns form a tribe.
When the tribal leader called for something, he would carve wood as a talisman. Although there was no writing, the tribesmen did not dare to violate it.
The Wuhuan people do not have a fixed surname, and the surname is the name of the strong leader.
From the leader down, people herd livestock and run their own industries, and they did not rely on each other.
In terms of marriage, they first rob the woman and live together, sometimes for half a year or hundreds of days, and then give the woman cattle, horses, sheep and other livestock as betrothal gifts.
When a son-in-law follows his wife back to his parents' home, he pays homage to the people in his wife's family every day, regardless of his superiority or inferiority, but does not pay homage to his wife's parents.
After working as a servant in his wife's house for a year or two, his wife's house gave them many things to send their daughter away, and all daily necessities and belongings were prepared for them.
The custom of the Wuhuan people is to marry their stepmother and have an affair with their widowed sister-in-law. However, after their death, the stepmother and sister-in-law are buried together with their original husbands.
In terms of strategy, they listen to women's opinions, and only make their own decisions when fighting.
Father and son, men and women sit face to face.
They think it is easy to shave off their hair.
Women only grow their hair when they get married, and it is separated and coiled on both sides of the head. The headdress is made of Jujue, which is decorated with gold and jade, just like the Gebuyao in the Central Plains.
Women could embroider leather and weave woolen fabrics.
Men can make bows and arrows, saddles and harnesses, and smelt copper and iron to make weapons.
The boring land is suitable for planting Biaozi and Aunt.
The bunches are like fluffy grass, and the fruits are like rice. They will mature in ten months.
When the Wuhuan people saw the flying black beasts being pregnant and giving birth, they used this to distinguish the four seasons.
Wuhuan's custom is to respect death in battle. They use coffins to collect corpses and have mourning and crying rituals, but when they are buried, they send them off with singing and dancing.
summary: The Wuhuan originated from the Donghu tribe. After the Xiongnu leader Maodun defeated Donghu in the early Han Dynasty, the survivors took refuge in Wuhuan Mountain and adopted the name as their tribal title. They were skilled horsemen and archers, primarily hunting birds and animals, and practiced nomadic pastoralism without fixed residences. Their felt tents faced east, and they subsisted on meat, cheese, and clothing made from animal hairs. They valued youth over the elderly, had fierce tempers, and would kill fathers and brothers in anger but never mothers, as mothers had their own tribes for revenge. Leaders were chosen based on bravery and strength, not heredity, with towns forming tribes under small leaders. They used carved wood as talismans for commands, lacked writing, and had no fixed surnames, adopting the names of strong leaders instead. Marriage involved abducting women, cohabiting for months, then paying betrothal gifts in livestock. Sons-in-law served their wives' families for one to two years before receiving dowries. They practiced levirate marriage, burying stepmothers and sisters-in-law with their original husbands. Women’s opinions were heeded in strategy, but men decided in battle. They shaved their heads, with women growing hair only after marriage, and wore headdresses decorated with gold and jade. Women embroidered leather and wove wool; men made bows, arrows, saddles, and smelted copper and iron for weapons. They cultivated crops like Biaozi and Aunt, which matured in ten months, and used the pregnancy of black beasts to distinguish seasons. They honored death in battle, used coffins, and conducted mourning rituals with singing and dancing, burning a fat dog with a colored rope along with the deceased’s possessions to guide the soul to Chishan, akin to the Central Plains’ Mount Tai. They sacrificed cattle and sheep to gods, ghosts, heaven, earth, and ancestors, burning the offerings completely. Disobedience to the leader was punishable by death; feuds could be settled with livestock. Wuhuan was located southwest of Dingling and northeast of Wusun, with many vipers.
