translation:
The Wuhuan people live close to the border. They set out from their felt tents in the morning and arrived at the city at dusk. Every household in the five counties was harmed. Counties were destroyed and people were displaced.
Wuhuan in Baishan, outside the Shanggu border fortress, was the most powerful and wealthy.
In the 21st year of Jianwu's reign, the imperial court sent Fubo General Ma Yuan to lead 3,000 cavalry from Wuruan Pass to attack Wuhuan.
Wuhuan learned the news in advance and all fled one after another. Ma Yuan chased them and killed more than a hundred Wuhuan people and returned to the army.
The Wuhuan people followed Ma Yuan to attack again, but Ma Yuan fled back day and night. By the time he entered the border fortress, more than a thousand horses were dead.
In the 22nd year, the Xiongnu were in civil unrest. Wuhuan took advantage of the Xiongnu's weakness and defeated the Xiongnu. The Xiongnu moved thousands of miles north, and the area south of the desert was completely empty. The emperor bribed Wuhuan with money and cloth.
In the twenty-fifth year, Hao Dan, the leader of Wuhuan in western Liaoning, and other 922 people led his tribe to Fumo and went to the court to pay tribute, offering slaves, cattle and horses, bows and arrows, and the skins of tigers, leopards, and minks.
When he was sent, ethnic minorities from all over came to worship and celebrate in an endless stream. The emperor ordered a grand banquet to be held to express condolences to them and reward them with treasures.
Some Wuhuan people were willing to stay as guards, so the emperor named eighty-one Wuhuan leaders as princes and commanders, letting them live in the fortress and distribute them in the border counties. He asked them to recruit people from their own tribes and provide them with clothing and food. The Wuhuan people then scouted for enemy movements for the Han and helped Mo attack the Xiongnu and Xianbei.
At that time, Situ Peng Ban Biao reported: The Wuhuan people are naturally frivolous and cunning, and like to be bandits. If they are indulged for a long time without anyone to supervise them to surrender and gather, they will definitely invade and plunder the people living there. I am afraid that I will not be able to control them if they are only given to the subordinates who accept the surrender.
I foolishly thought that it would be best to re-establish the Wuhuan captain, which would indeed be beneficial to the Wuhuan people's surrender and gathering, and reduce the country's worries about the border.
The emperor accepted this suggestion. So in Micheng in Shanggu, Wuhuan captains were established again, a military general's office was opened, and Xianbei was also commanded. He also rewarded the sons of the Wuhuan people who were held hostage, and traded with them all year round.
By the time of Emperor Ming, Emperor Zhang, and Emperor He, the Wuhuan people were guarding the frontier and nothing happened.
In the summer of the third year of Emperor An's reign, more than a thousand Wuhuan people from Yuyang and Hu people from Youbeiping invaded Daijun and Shanggu.
In the autumn of this year, Wuhuan of Yanmen led the king Wuhe, together with the Xianbei leader Qiulun and others, and the Guduhou of the Southern Xiongnu, with more than 7,000 cavalry, they invaded Wuyuan and fought with the Wuyuan prefect at Gaoqu Valley in Jiuyuan. The Han army was defeated and the county officials were killed.
The imperial court then sent the cavalry general He Xi, the Liao general Liang Dong and others to attack Wuhe, and they were defeated.
There was no need to beg for surrender, and the Xianbei people fled back beyond the frontier fortress.
From then on, the Wuhuan people gradually became closer to the Han, and the imperial court granted the Wuhuan tribal leader Rong Zhumo the title of pro-Han captaincy.
In the winter of the fourth year of Emperor Shun's reign in Yangjia, Wuhuan invaded Yunzhong and intercepted more than a thousand ox-carts of merchants on the road. Geng Ye, the general of Liao Dynasty, led more than 2,000 people to pursue the Wuhuan people. The battle was unfavorable, and they fought again in Shanan, killing 500 people.
The Wuhuan people then surrounded Geng Ye in Lanchi City. The imperial court then mobilized 2,000 trace-seeking soldiers and 1,000 soldiers from the Duliao camp to cooperate with the garrison in Shangjun to conquer Wuhuan, and the Wuhuan people retreated.
In the fifth year of Yonghe, Wuhuan's tribal leaders Ajian, Qiangqu and others and Julongwusi from the left of the southern Xiongnu rebelled. Zhang Dan, the central general, defeated and killed them, and the rest all surrendered.
During the Yongshou period of Emperor Huan, the Wuhuan people in Shuofang rebelled with Xiuzhu Tuge. Zhonglang attacked Zhang Huan and pacified the enemy.
In the summer of the ninth year of Yanxi, Wuhuan, together with Xianbei and the Southern Xiongnu, invaded nine counties along the border. They rebelled at the same time. Zhang Huan conquered the enemy, and they all left the border fortress.
In the early years of Emperor Ling, there was a tribal leader named Nanlou in Shanggu, who had more than 9,000 tribes of tribes, and there was a leader named Qiu Liju in western Liaoning, with more than 5,000 tribes of tribes, and they all called themselves kings. In addition, Su Puyan in Liaodong had more than a thousand tribes and called himself King Qiao; Wuyan in Youbeiping had more than 800 tribes and called himself King Hanlu: they were both brave and strong and had many strategies.
In the fourth year of Chongchuo, the governor of Protozoa Mountain rebelled. He joined Qiu Liju's tribe and proclaimed himself King Mitian Anding. He then became the marshal of the Wuhuan people in each county and invaded and plundered the four prefectures of Qingzhou, Xuzhou, Youzhou and Jizhou.
In the fifth year, the imperial court appointed Liu Yu as the shepherd of Youzhou. Liu Yu offered a reward for recruiting people to cut off Zhang Chun's head, and the northern states were pacified.
During the Chuping reign of Emperor Xian, Qiu Liju died. His son Lou Ban was young, and his nephew Tadun, who knew how to use troops and had strategies, succeeded Lou Ban and took charge of the Wuhuan people in three counties. All the people obeyed his orders.
In the early years of Jian'an, Yuan Shao, the shepherd of Jizhou, was at loggerheads with former general Gongsun Zan. Tadun sent an envoy to Yuan Shao to request peace, and then sent troops to help Yuan Shao attack Gongsun Zan and defeated Gongsun Zan.
In the name of the imperial court, Yuan Shao granted Tadun, Nanlou, Su Puyan, Wuyan and others the Chanyu seal and ribbon.
Later, Nanlou and Su Puyan led their troops to support Louban as Chanyu and Tadun as king, but Tadun was still responsible for making suggestions.
Yan Rou from Guangyang was trapped in Wuhuan and Xianbei since childhood, and was attached and trusted by the Wuhuan and Xianbei people. Yan Rou then used the Xianbei tribe to kill Wuhuan captain Xing Ju and replace him.
Yuan Shao favored Yan Rou and comforted her, so as to stabilize the northern border.
When Yuan Shao's son Yuan Shang failed, he defected to Tadun.
summary: After Maodun’s defeat, Wuhuan remained weak, often submitting to the Xiongnu and paying annual tribute. Emperor Wu moved them outside the five counties of Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, and Liaodong to spy on the Xiongnu. Their leaders paid homage to the emperor annually, and Wuhuan captains were established to supervise them. During Emperor Zhao’s reign, Wuhuan grew stronger, desecrated a Xiongnu chanyu’s tomb, and was attacked by the Xiongnu. General Huo Guang sent Fan Mingyou to intercept, but the Xiongnu had retreated; Fan then attacked Wuhuan, killing over 6,000. Under Emperor Xuan, Wuhuan gradually surrendered and guarded the border. When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he conscripted Wuhuan troops, holding their families hostage, leading to rebellion and hatred. The Xiongnu lured Wuhuan leaders to join them. In the early Guangwu period, Wuhuan and Xiongnu jointly invaded, devastating border counties. In the 21st year of Jianwu, Ma Yuan attacked Wuhuan but achieved little. In the 22nd year, Wuhuan defeated the weakened Xiongnu, and the emperor bribed them with money and cloth. In the 25th year, Hao Dan and 922 others paid tribute, and the emperor appointed 81 Wuhuan leaders as princes and commanders, settling them in border counties to scout for the Han. Later, Wuhuan captains were re-established to supervise them. From Emperor Ming to Emperor He, Wuhuan guarded the frontier peacefully. During Emperor An’s reign, Wuhuan invaded Daijun and Shanggu, and later Yanmen Wuhuan joined Xianbei and Southern Xiongnu in attacking Wuyuan, defeating the Han. The court sent He Xi and Liang Dong to defeat them, and Wuhuan gradually became closer to the Han. Under Emperor Shun, Wuhuan invaded Yunzhong, but Geng Ye repelled them. In the 5th year of Yonghe, Wuhuan leaders rebelled but were defeated by Zhang Dan. During Emperor Huan’s Yongshou period, Wuhuan in Shuofang rebelled but were pacified by Zhang Huan. In the 9th year of Yanxi, Wuhuan, Xianbei, and Southern Xiongnu invaded nine counties, but Zhang Huan drove them out. Under Emperor Ling, leaders like Nanlou and Qiu Liju claimed kingship. In the 4th year of Zhongping, Zhang Chun rebelled, joined Qiu Liju, and invaded four provinces. Liu Yu pacified the north. During Emperor Xian’s Chuping period, Tadun succeeded Qiu Liju and controlled three counties. Yuan Shao granted Tadun and others Chanyu seals. Later, Yan Rou killed the Wuhuan captain and replaced him. When Yuan Shang failed, he fled to Tadun. Cao Cao conquered Wuhuan in the 12th year of Jian’an, killed Tadun, captured 200,000, and moved the remaining people to the Central Plains. Xianbei, also a Donghu branch, relied on Xianbei Mountain. Their customs were similar to Wuhuan, but they shaved their heads for marriage and gathered by the Raole River in spring. Their region had unique animals like wild horses and horned oxen, whose horns were used for bows. Mink and mole furs were valuable. In the early Han, Xianbei was defeated by Maodun and fled to Liaodong, with no contact with the Han. In the early Jianwu period, they invaded the north. In the 21st year, Ji Xu defeated them, and they later exchanged envoys with Han. Ji Xu bribed them to attack the Northern Xiongnu, and they received rewards. During the Ming and Zhang reigns, they guarded the border peacefully. Under Emperor He, Dou Xian defeated the Xiongnu, and Xianbei occupied their territory, absorbing 100,000 Xiongnu remnants and growing strong. They invaded Liaodong, Youbeiping, and Yuyang, with mixed results. During Emperor An’s Yongchu period, Yan Liyang paid tribute, and the court built facilities for trade and hostages. Xianbei alternately surrendered and rebelled, clashing with Xiongnu and Wuhuan. In the 2nd year of Yuanchu, they surrounded Wulu County but gained nothing. In the 4th year, Lianxiu invaded, but Wuhuan leader Yu Zhiju defeated him. In the 5th year, 10,000 Xianbei cavalry invaded Daijun, burning government offices. The court mobilized troops to guard Shanggu. In the 6th year, Deng Zun defeated Xianbei. In the 1st year of Yongning, Wulun and Qizhi Tar surrendered. In the 1st year of Jianguang, Qizhi Tar rebelled, invaded Juyong, and killed the prefect. Geng Kui relieved the siege. Qizhi Tar grew stronger, invading Yanmen, Dingxiang, and Taiyuan. In the 2nd year of Yanguang, he invaded the east, killing over 1,000. In the 3rd year, he invaded Gaoliu. Under Emperor Shun, Qizhi Tar invaded Dai County, killing the prefect. Zhang Guo defeated him in the 2nd year of Yongjian. Xianbei from Liaodong invaded but were repelled by Geng Ye. In the 3rd and 4th years, they invaded Yuyang and Shuofang. In the 6th year, Geng Ye defeated them. In the 1st year of Yangjia, Geng Ye sent Rong Zhumo to attack Xianbei successfully. Xianbei later invaded Liaodong, and Geng Ye moved to Wulu City. In the 2nd year, Zhao Chou defeated Xianbei. Under Emperor Huan, Tanshihuai emerged. His father Touluhou doubted his birth, but his wife claimed a miraculous conception. Tanshihuai grew brave and resourceful, recovering stolen cattle and becoming leader. He established a royal court by the Geqiu River, subdued tribes, and expanded territory from Dingling to Wusun, covering 14,000 miles east-west. In the 2nd year of Yongshou, he invaded Yunzhong. In the 1st year of Yanxi, Zhang Huan killed 200 Xianbei. In the 2nd year, they invaded Yanmen. In the 6th year, they invaded Liaodong. In the 9th year, tens of thousands invaded nine counties, but Zhang Huan drove them out. The court tried to make Tanshihuai king, but he refused and intensified raids. He divided Xianbei into three parts: east, middle, and west. Under Emperor Ling, Xianbei invaded the three provinces of Youzhou, Bingzhou, and Liangzhou annually. In the 3rd year of Xiping, Xia Zhi defeated them. In the 5th year, they invaded Youzhou. In the 6th year, they invaded three borders. Xia Yu proposed a winter-spring campaign, but the court disagreed. Tian Yan sought to lead an expedition, but Cai Yong advised against it, citing past failures and current poverty. The court ignored him, sending Xia Yu, Tian Yan, and Zang Man with 10,000 cavalry each. Tanshihuai’s forces defeated them, killing 70-80% of the troops. The generals were imprisoned. In the 1st year of Guanghe, Xianbei invaded Jiuquan. Tanshihuai, facing food shortages, attacked the Japanese eastward, capturing over 1,000 to fish. He died at 45, succeeded by his son Helian, who was less capable and lost half his people. Helian was killed by a Han archer. His son Qianman was young, and his nephew Kuixi succeeded. Later, Qianman competed with Kuixi, dividing the tribe. Budugen succeeded after Kuixi’s death. From Tanshihuai, leadership became hereditary. The text concludes that Wuhuan and Xianbei caused continuous border troubles, with no effective strategies to control them.

translation:
◆Ren Guangchuan Ren Guangzi Boqing was born in Wan County, Nanyang County.
He was loyal and loyal in his youth and loved by the villagers.
At first he was a local miser and a county official.
When the Han soldiers arrived in Wan, the soldiers saw Ren Guang's bright uniform and ordered him to take off his clothes, preparing to kill him and seize his clothes.
Just then Guang Luxun and Liu Ci arrived. Seeing that Ren Guang looked like an elder, he rescued him.
Ren Guang led his disciples to follow Liu Ci, to secure the governorship, and to worship him as a partial general. Together with his ancestors, he defeated Wang Xun and Wang Yi.
Gengshi arrived in Luoyang and appointed Ren Guang as the governor of Xindu.
When Wang Lang rose up, all the prefectures and states surrendered to Wang Lang. Ren Guangdu refused, so he and the captains Li Zhong, Ling Wanxiu, Gong Cao Ruan Kuang, Wu Guan Yu Guo Tang and others stood firm.
Ting Ping took Wang Lang's message to Ren Guang's house to persuade Ren Guang. Ren Guang beheaded Ting Ping in the city to declare to the people, and sent 4,000 elite soldiers to strengthen the city defense.
In the spring of the second year of Gengshi, Shizu came back from Ji and was so embarrassed that he didn't know where to go. Hearing that Xindu was alone in the Han Dynasty and rejected the prince, he rushed to Xindu.
Ren Guang and others were guarding the isolated city alone, fearing that they would not be able to save it. When they heard that Shizu had arrived, they were overjoyed. The officials and the people all said long live the city. They immediately opened the door and, together with Li Zhong and Wan Xiu, led the officials to welcome Jin Ye.
When Shizu arrived at his residence, he said to Ren Guang: "Boqing, we are now alone and weak. I want to go with you to the soldiers at Chengtouzi Road and Lizidu. What do you think?" Ren Guang said: No. Shizu said: You have few soldiers, what should you do? Ren Guang said: We can recruit quick troops to attack neighboring counties. If they do not surrender, we will let them plunder.
People are greedy for money, so soldiers can be recruited. Shizu obeyed.
He appointed Ren Guang as the General of the Left and granted him the title of Marquis of Wucheng. He left Nanyang Zongguang to take over the position of prefect of Xindu, allowing Ren Guang to lead his troops to follow him.
Ren Guang wrote more propaganda articles and said: Grand Sima Liu Gong led Chengtou Zilu and Lizidu and millions of soldiers came from the east to conquer the rebels from various ministries. He sent his horse galloping into the realm of giant deer.
Officials and the people received the proclamation and circulated it to each other.
Shizu then entered Tangyang Realm with Ren Guang and others at dusk, and ordered the cavalry to each hold a torch, so that the fire filled the lake and illuminated the sky and the earth. Everyone in the city was shocked and horrified, and they surrendered that night.
In ten days, the army's strength increased greatly, so they turned to attack the city and captured Handan, so they sent Ren Guang back to the county.
Chengtou Zilu was from Dongping, his surname was Yuan, his given name was Zeng, and his given name was Zilu. He and Liu Xu of Feicheng set up an army in Chengtou, so he called his army Chengtou Zilu.
Zilu claimed that he was engaged in military affairs, and Liu Xu called him the three elders of the school. He invaded and plundered between the Yellow River and Jishui, and his troops numbered more than 200,000.
summary: Ren Guang, from Wan County, was loyal in his youth. When Han soldiers arrived, they tried to kill him for his clothes, but Liu Ci rescued him. Ren Guang then led his followers to serve Liu Ci. When Wang Lang rebelled, all prefectures surrendered except Xindu, where Ren Guang, Li Zhong, Wan Xiu, and others held firm. Ren Guang beheaded Wang Lang's messenger and sent elite troops to defend the city. When Shizu (Emperor Guangwu) arrived from Ji, Ren Guang and his officials welcomed him. Shizu wanted to go to Chengtou Zilu and Lizidu for soldiers, but Ren Guang advised against it, suggesting they recruit troops by plundering neighboring counties. Shizu agreed, made Ren Guang General of the Left, and Marquis of Wucheng. Ren Guang wrote propaganda claiming Shizu had millions of soldiers, causing many to surrender. After capturing Handan, Shizu sent Ren Guang back to his county. Ren Guang was later made Marquis of Aling and died in the fifth year of Jianwu.

translation:
When Gengshi was established, Yuan Zeng sent envoys to surrender. Gengshi worshiped Yuan Zeng as the prefect of Donglai County and Liu Xu as the prefect of Jinan, both of whom exercised military power as generals.
In this year, Yuan was killed by his subordinates, and Liu Xu was elected as the leader. Liu Xu was granted the title of Marquis of Help, and ordered him to withdraw his troops and return to his county.
Li Zidu, a native of Donghai, raised troops in the countryside, plundered and attacked Xuzhou and Yanzhou, with a tribe of 60,000 to 70,000 people.
Gengshi was established, and his envoys were sent to surrender. They all worshiped Lizi as the shepherd of Xuzhou.
He was killed by his subordinates, and the rest of the party gathered again to meet the thieves in Tanxiang, so they were named Tanxiang.
Dong Cizhong, the commander-in-chief of Tanxiang, started from Chiping County, crossed the river into Qinghe, Wei County, and joined the five schools with more than 100,000 troops.
In the first year of Jianwu, Shizu entered Luoyang and sent the Grand Sima Wu Han army to attack Tanxiang. In the spring of the next year, Tanxiang failed and surrendered.
In this year, Ren Guang was granted the title of Marquis of Aling, with a population of over 10,000 households.
In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, he was recruited to the capital and invited by the court.
He died in the winter of that year.
The son was appointed as the heir to the throne.
◆Li Zhongchuan
Li Zhong, courtesy name Zhongdu, was from Huang County, Donglai County.
His father is the captain of Gaomi. During the reign of Emperor Li Zhongping, his father was appointed as the minister, and he had dozens of people in his office. However, Li Zhong was famous for his good manners and neat grooming. Wang Mang was the chief of Xinbo at that time, and everyone in the county respected and trusted him.
After Gengshi ascended the throne, he sent envoys to patrol the prefecture and the country, and then worshiped Li Zhong as the captain.
Li Zhong and Ren Guang jointly worshiped the ancestors of the world and became the right generals, and they were granted the title of Wu Guhou.
At that time, Shizu took off the ribbon he was wearing and put it on for Li Zhong, so he attacked the subordinate counties from Shizu and arrived at Kushan County. Shizu met with the generals and asked them what property they had obtained, but Li Zhong was the only one who did not plunder it.
Shizu said: I want to reward Li Zhong specially. You won't have any resentment, right? He gave Li Zhong a large horse and embroidered quilt and clothes.
All the generals were horrified and said: "Your mother and wife are still in the hands of others. Isn't it too much to kill his brother?" Li Zhong said: If you don't punish the rebels, you are having second thoughts. After hearing this, Shizu praised Li Zhong and said: Now that my army is ready, the general can go back to save your mother and wife. I want to recruit officials and people who can save their families. I will give you a reward of tens of millions. Come to me to receive it. Li Zhong said: I am so grateful to Duke Ming. I only think about serving the public and I really don't dare to take care of my family. Shizu ordered Ren Guang to lead his troops to rescue Xindu. Ren Guang's troops scattered on the road and surrendered to Wang Lang. Ren Guang returned without success.
It happened that Gengshi sent generals to conquer Xindu, and Li Zhong's family was safe.
Shizu then asked Li Zhong to return to Xindu and perform the duties of governor. Li Zhong killed hundreds of people in the county who had surnamed Wang Lang.
When Ren Guang returned to the county, Li Zhong was restored to the rank of captain.
summary: Li Zhong, from Huang County, was known for his good manners. He and Ren Guang jointly served Shizu, becoming a general and marquis. Shizu praised Li Zhong for not plundering. When Li Zhong's mother and wife were captured by Wang Lang, Shizu offered a reward for their rescue, but Li Zhong refused to care for his family. Ren Guang's attempt to rescue them failed, but Gengshi's generals later conquered Xindu, saving Li Zhong's family. Li Zhong then returned to Xindu and killed hundreds of Wang Lang's supporters. He later became the prefect of Danyang, where he established schools and promoted agriculture, attracting over 50,000 refugees. He was later moved to Yuzhang and died in the 19th year of Jianwu.

translation:
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Zhongshui, with a settlement of 3,000 households.
In this year, Zheng was worshiped as Wugan Zhonglang General, and followed to pacify Pang Meng, Dong Xian and others.
In the sixth year of Jianwu's reign, he moved to Danyang to be the prefect.
At this time, the country had just been calmed down, and many people in the Jianghuai area along the southern coast were supporting troops to seize control.
Li Zhong went to the county and recruited envoys to join him. All those who disobeyed were killed, and they were all put down within ten days.
Li Zhong thought Danyang was more vulgar and did not like to study, and the wedding ceremony was not as grand as that in the Central Plains, so he set up a school to learn etiquette, held ceremonies in the Spring and Autumn Period, selected people who were proficient in classics, and presided over it by people who admired him in the county.
As a result, more land was cultivated, and within three years, more than 50,000 refugees became local indigenous people.
In the 14th year of Jianwu's reign, he was ranked first in the world in the Sangong assessment and was moved to Yuzhang as the prefect. He was dismissed from office due to illness and was recruited to the capital.
Jianwu died in the 19th year.
◆Wan Xiu Chuan Wan Xiu, named Junyou, was from Maoling, Fufeng County.
At the time of Gengshi, in order to obey the capital order, he guarded the city together with the prefect Ren Guang and the captain Li Zhong, welcomed the ancestors, worshiped him as a partial general, and created a righteous marquis.
After Handan was defeated, he was appointed as the right general and followed him to pacify Hebei.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Huaili.
He and General Jiantan of Yanghua attacked Nanyang together, but failed to capture it and fell ill and died in the army.
Zi Wanpu succeeded to the throne and was granted the title of Marquis of the Hu clan.
Wan Pu died, his son Wan Qin succeeded him to the throne, and he moved to Fuliu Hou.
Ten thousand relatives died, no children, the feudal state was abolished.
In the seventh year of Yongchu's reign, Mrs. Deng later granted Wanxiu's great-grandson Wanfeng the title of Marquis of Qupingting.
Wan Feng died, and his son Wan Chi succeeded him.
In the first year of Yongjian's reign, Wan Chi died without any children, and the feudal state was abolished.
In the second year of Yanxi, Emperor Huan renewed the title of Wan Gong, the great-great-grandson of Wan Xiu, as Marquis of Mendeting.
◆Pi Tong Biography: Pi Tong, courtesy name Weijun, was a native of Xindu.
His father, Pi Ji, was the governor of western Liaoning.
Pitong initially served as Wang Mang and Cheng Zuzheng.
Shizu captured Hebei and reached Xiaquyang. Pitong surrendered the city, and Shizu made Pitong the governor and stayed for a few days.
Shizu went north to Ji, and it happened that Wang Lang's army rose up and sent generals to conquer the land. Every county he went to welcomed him, but Hecheng and Xin could not hold on.
When Pitong heard that Shizu had lost his army when he returned from Ji and was preparing to go to Xindu, he first sent Zhang Wan, the Five Officials Commander, and Yin Sui, the Superintendent of Posts, to select more than 2,000 horses to meet Shizu's army along the road.
Pitong soon met Shizu in Xindu.
Although Shizu received help from the two counties, the soldiers did not gather. Many of his subordinates said that they could send him back to Chang'an west by letter.
summary: Wan Xiu, from Maoling, guarded Xindu with Ren Guang and Li Zhong, welcoming Shizu. He was made a general and marquis. He followed Shizu to pacify Hebei and was later made Marquis of Huaili. He died of illness while attacking Nanyang. His descendants inherited his title, but the fief was eventually abolished and later re-granted to his descendants by Empress Dowager Deng and Emperor Huan.

translation:
Pi Tong immediately replied: What the commentators said is wrong.
The officials and the people had been praising the Han Dynasty for a long time, so when Gengshi came to the throne, the whole country responded. The third auxiliary of the Qing Dynasty swept the couches and cleared the roads to welcome him.
If one man raises his halberd and shouts, all the generals from thousands of miles away will offer their city and flee, and the thieves will prostrate themselves and beg to surrender.
Since ancient times, no animal or human has reached this level of sensitivity.
That prince was just a fortune-teller who took advantage of the chaos in the world under the guise of the Liu clan and mobilized a mob to frighten the land of Yan and Zhao. What's more, Ming Gong raised the troops of the two counties and promoted the power of response. If you want to attack, no city can be conquered, if you want to fight, no army can't surrender!
If you abandon this and return now, you will not only lose Hebei, but also alarm the three assistants. Once the prestige and reputation are lost, this is not a good plan.
If Duke Ming had no intention of conquest again, then even if there were soldiers from Xindu, it would be difficult to meet him.
Why?
Now that Ming Gong has returned to the west, the people of Handan are unwilling to abandon their parents and the city lord, and send the Duke back to the west after thousands of miles. Their separation and flight is inevitable.
The founder of Shizu did good deeds and stopped returning to the west.
Immediately, I appointed Pi Tong as the general of the rear, and asked him to lead the troops in front as the prefect did in the past.
When they arrived at Tangyang, Tangyang belonged to Wang Lang. Pitong sent Zhang Wan and Yin Sui to inform the officials and people first. When Shizu arrived at night, Tangyang opened the door to welcome him.
He also led troops to defeat the Baishe bandits in Zhongshan.
From then on, Pitong often attacked and fought from Shizu.
Xindu was restored and surrendered to Wang Lang. The Xindu king set up by Wang Lang arrested and imprisoned Pitong's uncle, wife and children, and asked them to call Pitong in handwriting and say: If you surrender, you will be crowned, if you don't surrender, your clan will be exterminated. Pitong cried and reported: "Those who serve the king should not take care of their families."
It is Liu Gong's kindness that Pitong's relatives are still able to settle down in Xindu.
Liu Gong is currently busy with state affairs, and I, Pi Tong, must not worry about private matters. It happened that the generals sent by Gengshi captured Xindu, and Wang Lang's troops were defeated, so Pitong's family was spared.
After capturing Handan, he granted Pitong the title of Marquis of Wuyi.
In the first year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Marquis Lingshou and acted as the chief minister in charge of affairs.
When the emperor entered Luoyang, he worshiped Pi Tong as Taichang. He transferred to the Shaofu in the remaining months of the month and was exempted from Taichang's duties this year.
Then he served as Zuo Cao's servant and often went on expeditions.
In the sixth year of Jianwu, he returned to the feudal state.
When Pitong died, his son Pitang succeeded him. In the ninth year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Leling.
In the 19th year of Jianwu's reign, Pitang died, and his son Pi took the throne. He had no children, and the feudal state was abolished.
summary: Pi Tong, from Xindu, initially served Wang Mang. When Shizu reached Xiaquyang, Pi Tong surrendered the city. When Wang Lang rose up, Pi Tong heard Shizu was going to Xindu and sent horses to meet him. When Shizu's subordinates suggested returning to Chang'an, Pi Tong argued against it, praising the Han dynasty's popularity and Wang Lang's weakness. Shizu agreed and made Pi Tong a general. Pi Tong later led troops to defeat bandits and often fought alongside Shizu. When Wang Lang captured Xindu, Pi Tong's family was imprisoned, but he refused to surrender, saying he must not care for his family. His family was spared when Gengshi's generals captured Xindu. Pi Tong was made a marquis and held various official positions, including Taichang and Shaofu. He died, and his title passed to his descendants, though the fief was later abolished and re-granted.

translation:
In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, Mrs. Deng subsequently granted Pitong and Sun Piyin the title of Pingtinghou.
When Pi Yin died, his son Pi Chai succeeded him.
At first, Zhang Wan, Yin Sui and Pi Tong welcomed Shizu, and they all worshiped him as partial generals and followed him in the expedition.
Zhang Wan was granted the title of Chongping Marquis, and Yin Sui was granted the title of Platform Marquis.
The historian commented: Anyone who talks about success is easy to become famous because of his outstanding achievements; those who plan things in advance are difficult to be known because of their obscure reasons.
This is of course based on actual comparison and should be reasoned and investigated.
As for Shizu, although he had gained the people of the two counties, he still wanted to return to Chang'an in the west, abandon his achievements, and face unexpected situations, but Shizu did not realize it, and all those who made suggestions agreed to follow him. In this case, aren't Pitong's words prescient!
The Analects of Confucius says, "One sentence can make a country prosperous." Pi Tong's words are very close.
◆Biography of Liu Zhi Liu Zhi, courtesy name Boxian, was a native of Changcheng, Julu.
After Wang Lang's uprising, Liu Zhi, his younger brother Liu happy, and his elder brother Liu Xin led thousands of clan guests to occupy Changcheng.
When Shizu heard that Shizu had returned from Ji, he opened the city gate to welcome Shizu. Shizu made Liu Zhi his valiant cavalry general, Liu happy and Liu Xin his partial generals, and they were all granted the title of marquis.
At this time, Liu Yang, the king of Zhending, raised an army to surrender to Wang Lang. There were more than 100,000 people. The ancestor of the emperor sent Liu Zhi to persuade Liu Yang, and Liu Yang surrendered.
Therefore, Shizu stayed in Zhending and took in Empress Guo. Empress Guo was Liu Yang's niece, so she made a strong connection with her.
So he and Liu Yang and other generals held a banquet to celebrate at Guo's home in Qili. Liu Yang was so happy that he built a building for it, so he had to march to capture Handan and follow him to pacify Hebei.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, Liu Zhi was granted the title of Marquis of Changcheng.
He defeated the bandits in Mi County and died in the war.
His son Liu Xiang succeeded him.
The emperor's envoy Liu happy led Liu Zhi's army on his behalf, and was granted the title of General Xiaoqi and the title of Marquis of Guanjin.
After Liu happy's death, Liu Xin was made a heroic cavalry general and was granted the title of Marquis of Fuyang.
Liu happy and Liu Xin followed the expedition and both passed down the feudal state to their descendants.
Liu Xiang was granted the title of Marquis of Dongwuyang. After his death, his son Liu Shu succeeded to the throne. In the fifteenth year of Yongping, the feudal state was abolished because of his involvement in the rebellion of Chu King Liu Ying.
◆The biography of Geng Chun Geng Chun, courtesy name Boshan, was born in the Song Dynasty in Julu.
His father, Geng Ai, is Wang Mang Ji Pingyin.
Geng Chun studied in Chang'an, so he was awarded the title of Nayanshi.
Wang Mang was defeated and Gengshi ascended the throne, causing Wuyang King Li Yi to surrender to various counties. Geng Chun's father Geng Ai surrendered and returned to serve as the prefect of Jinan.
At that time, brother Li Yi was in power and acted arbitrarily, and there was a lot of lobbying from guests.
summary: Liu Zhi, from Julu, led clan guests to occupy Changcheng. He opened the city to welcome Shizu and was made a general. He persuaded Liu Yang, the King of Zhending, to surrender. He followed Shizu to capture Handan and pacify Hebei. He was made Marquis of Changcheng and died in battle. His brother Liu happy and Liu Xin succeeded him in command and were also made marquises. Geng Chun, from Julu, studied in Chang'an. He advised Li Yi against arrogance, and Li Yi made him a cavalry captain. When Shizu arrived in Handan, Geng Chun went to see him. When Wang Lang rebelled, Geng Chun led over 2,000 clan guests to welcome Shizu. He was made a general and marquis. To prevent his clan from having second thoughts, he burned their houses. He defeated Li Yun and followed Shizu to pacify Handan. When attacked at night, he held firm and sent a death squad to attack the thieves from behind. Shizu later made him Marquis of Gaoyang. He was secretly ordered to arrest Liu Yang, the King of Zhending, and killed Liu Yang and his brothers. He later requested to govern a county and became the prefect of Dongjun, pacifying the region. He was later made Marquis of Dongguang. When bandits arose in Dongjun, he was sent to help, and over 9,000 thieves surrendered to him. He died in office in the 13th year of Jianwu.

translation:
◆It is said in Fu Zhan's biography that Fu Zhan was named Hui Gong and was a native of Dongwu, King of Lang.
The ninth generation ancestor Fu Sheng, whose courtesy name was Zi Jian, was the so-called Jinan Fu Sheng.
Fu Zhan's great-great-grandfather Fu Ru was a visiting professor at Dongwu during the reign of Emperor Wu, so he made Dongwu his home.
His father, Fuli, was a famous Confucian in the world. He became an emperor by teaching "Poems" and was a tutor in Gaomi. He became a famous scholar in his own family.
Fu Zhan respected his parents and loved his brothers. He taught his father's business from an early age and taught hundreds of people.
When he became emperor, he accepted his father as his doctorate disciple.
He was transferred to the official position five times. When he arrived at Wang Mang, he was enforcing the law in Xiu Yi, which made the inspector a traitor.
Gengshi was established, and Fu Zhan was appointed as the prefect of Pingyuan.
At that time, there was a hasty war, and the world was in panic, but Fu Zhan was very quiet and continued to teach.
He said to his wife and children: If the harvest is not harvested in the new year, the king should withdraw from the banquet. Now the people are starving, how can they be fed alone?
So they ate coarse grains together and used the income from their salaries to provide relief to the village. There were more than a hundred visitors.
At that time, the governor was very powerful and planned to raise troops for Fu Zhan. Fu Zhan hated him for confusing people, so he was about to behead him and hang his head on the city wall to show the people. As a result, the officials and the people were convinced and admired him, and the county was stable.
A county in Pingyuan was preserved by Fu Zhan.
When Guangwu came to the throne, he knew that Fu Zhan was a well-known Confucian old official, so he wanted to make him take charge of the internal affairs, worship the minister, and let him review the old laws and regulations.
At that time, Deng Yu, the Great Situ, was on an expedition to the west of Guanzhong. The emperor appointed Fu Zhancai as Prime Minister and worshiped him as Sizhi, performing the duties of the Great Situ.
Whenever Guangwu went on an expedition, he was often left to guard the capital and take photos of all the divisions.
In the third year of Jianwu's reign, he succeeded Deng Yu as the Great Situ and was granted the title of Marquis of Yangdu.
At that time, Peng Chong rebelled against Yuyang, and Guangwu wanted to conquer it himself. Fu Zhan advised him: "I heard that King Wen was ordered to conquer the five countries. I must first consult the opinions of the people with the same surname, and then seek advice from the officials, and then seize the turtle to decide what to do. Therefore, planning will succeed, divination will be auspicious, and war will win."
His "Poetry" said: God said to King Wen: It is necessary to obtain the support of friendly countries, to unite brothers and friendly countries, to prepare siege ladders, to prepare approaching chariots and rushing chariots, in order to attack the vicious Chongguo.
The city of Chongguo was fortified and did not fall for thirty days. It retreated to repair the government and resumed the attack. Therefore, it valued human life and moved when the time came. Therefore, it was able to divide the world into two parts.
Your Majesty inherited the great chaos and was appointed emperor to revive the great ancestors. He spent four years in and out of town, destroyed Tan Township, controlled five schools, surrendered bronze horses, defeated red eyebrows, and killed Deng Feng's subordinates. It was not for nothing.
Nowadays, the capital is short of space and resources, so it is unable to conquer those close to home and conquers the outside world first. Moreover, in the land of Yuyang, approaching Beidi, Peng Chong is in dire straits and must seek help from him.
summary: Fu Zhan, also known as Hui Gong, was a native of Dongwu. He was a descendant of the scholar Fu Sheng. Fu Zhan was a filial and learned man who taught his father's teachings to hundreds of students. During the chaos of the Gengshi era, he served as the Prefect of Pingyuan, where he remained calm, ate coarse grains, and used his salary to relieve the starving people. He beheaded a powerful governor who planned to raise troops, which stabilized the county. When Guangwu came to the throne, Fu Zhan was appointed to high office, eventually becoming the Grand Situ and Marquis of Yangdu. He advised the emperor against personally conquering the rebel Peng Chong, arguing that the emperor should first secure the central territories. The emperor heeded his advice. A thief named Xu Yiqing, who could not be defeated by officers, surrendered specifically to Fu Zhan. Fu Zhan was later dismissed from his post for a minor fault. He was later recommended for reinstatement but died of heatstroke before he could take office.

translation:
From the time when a child makes a determination, to the time when his head turns gray, his determination will never fade.
His actions are enough to guide the royal family, and his reputation is enough to enlighten people from afar.
In ancient times, princes were selected as ministers, so everyone looked back and looked up at the capital.
The ministers of the pillars should occupy the position of assistant ministers and go in and out of the palace to remedy deficiencies and correct mistakes.
My minister Du Shi is too stupid to know the talent of the prime minister. I only have a small talent and dare not to do my best to be loyal.
In front of the minister, I served as the censor, and presented a sealed memorial, saying that Fu Zhan was fair, upright, caring for his subordinates, had clear likes and dislikes, had studied Confucianism for generations, had a good reputation, was knowledgeable in classics, cultivated virtues, and had a good understanding of national affairs. In particular, he should be a close minister and receive advice from his left and right. According to the old system, nine states would elect a total of five people to serve as ministers. According to the order, there are two people in a county, and Fu Zhan can replace one person.
This attracted considerable criticism from the deacons. However, the minister Du Shi was deeply favored and said that as long as it was beneficial to the country, he would have no regrets even if he died, so he once again overstepped his duties and risked the memorial.
In the summer of the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, he was summoned to return to the court, and the minister was ordered to choose a date to confer an official position. Before he could take office, he died of heat stroke due to the summons and banquet. He was given a coffin, the emperor went to express his condolences in person, and sent envoys to attend the funeral and build the tomb.
◆Hou Ba's biography: Hou Ba's courtesy name Junfang was from Mi County, Henan County.
Hou Yuan, the father of the clan, was a talented official and served in the Yuan Dynasty. He assisted Shi Xian and others to become Zhongshu, and was called the Great Changshi.
When he became emperor, he appointed Hou Ba to sacrifice his life for the prince.
Hou Ba is reserved, serious and majestic. His family has a lot of money and he is not engaged in property.
Dedicated and eager to learn, he took Fang Yuan, the prefect of Jiujiang, as his teacher. He wrote the "Guliang Spring and Autumn Annals" and taught it for Fang Yuan.
At the beginning of Wang Mang's reign, Chen Chong, the commander of Wuwei, recommended Hou Ba Dexing and moved to the county magistrate.
The county borders are far away, with rivers and lakes on the coast, and most of the desperadoes are bandits.
When Hou Ba arrived, he immediately opened a case to kill the powerful and cunning people, and arrested the bandits separately. The county was quiet and peaceful.
Then he moved to law enforcement, assassinated rapes, reported and exposed powerful people, without any suspicion or fear.
Later he became Dayin of Huaiping, and he was known for his ability in political governance.
When Wang Mang failed, Hou Ba defended himself and made the whole county safe.
In the first year of Gengshi, envoys were sent to summon Hou Ba. The common people, old and weak, cried and blocked the envoys' vehicles, or lay down in the road.
They all said: I would like to beg to stay in office for another year.
The people even warned young women not to have children. If Hou Jun left, it would be difficult to save the children in the future.
The envoy was afraid that Hou Ba would leave due to the conquest, which would lead to chaos in Linhuai, so he did not dare to grant the seal to Hou Ba, so he wrote a memorial to report the situation to the court.
It happened that the reform failed and the road was blocked.
summary: Hou Ba, courtesy name Junfang, was from Mi County. He was a serious and dedicated student of the "Guliang Spring and Autumn Annals." As a county magistrate, he killed powerful criminals and arrested bandits, bringing peace to the region. As the Grand Administrator of Huaipei, he was known for his capable governance. When Wang Mang failed, he defended the county. The people begged for him to stay when he was summoned by Gengshi. Under Guangwu, he became a minister and established many good governance laws. He succeeded Fu Zhan as Grand Situ. He was known for being clear-minded and selfless. After his death, the emperor posthumously named him Marquis Ai of Zixiang, and the people of Linhuai built a temple for him.

translation:
In the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, Guangwu summoned Hou Ba to meet him in Shouchun and worshiped him as Shangshu Ling.
There were no historical classics at that time, and there were few old ministers in the court. Hou Baming studied the affairs of the previous court, collected the posthumous documents, and wrote down the good governance laws of the previous life that were beneficial to the time, and they were all implemented.
The lenient edicts issued every spring and the political orders of the four seasons were all established by Hou Ba.
In the second year, he was appointed Grand Situ on behalf of Fu Zhan and was granted the title of Marquis of Guan Nei.
When in office, he is clear-minded, upright, and selfless.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, Hou Ba passed away. Emperor Guangwu was deeply saddened and paid his respects in person.
The edict said: Hou Ba has accumulated good deeds and has been in charge of the court for nine years. According to the old system of the Han Dynasty, on the day when he was granted the title of Prime Minister, he was also granted the title of Lieutenant Commander.
I have been exposed to the outside world all year round due to my military service, and my meritorious service has not yet been rewarded. I do not want to exceed the obligation of loyalty, but before I could be awarded a title, Hou Ba passed away.
Alas!
So he named Hou Ba the posthumous title of Aihou of Zixiang, with a settlement of 2,600 households. Zihou Yu succeeded to the throne.
Linhuai officials and people jointly built a temple for him and offered sacrifices at all times.
◆Song Hong's biography: Song Hong's courtesy name was Zhongzi, and he was a native of Chang'an, Jingzhao.
His father, Shang Shang, had the lowest official rank when he became emperor. When Emperor Ai was established, he disobeyed Dong Xian and was punished because he did not attach himself to Dong Xian.
Song Hong was young and docile. He served as an attendant during the reign of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, and served as Gonggong during the reign of Wang Mang.
Chimei entered Chang'an and sent envoys to recruit Song Hong. He had no choice but to commit suicide. When he reached Weiqiao, he threw himself into the water. His family rescued him and he was spared by pretending to be dead.
Guangwu ascended the throne and was worshiped as Taizhong doctor.
In the second year of Jianwu, Wang Liang was granted the title of Grand Sikong and was granted the title of Marquis of Yi.
The rent earned is divided among the nine clans. The family has no assets and is known for its honesty.
He was granted the title of Marquis of Xuanping.
The emperor once asked Song Hong who was the most knowledgeable scholar, so Song Hong recommended Huan Tan of Pei State, who was rich in knowledge and knowledge, almost comparable to Yang Xiong and Liu Xiang and his son.
So he called Huan Tan to worship him as Yilang and gave him the title of Shizhong.
The emperor ordered him to play drums and harps every time he held a banquet, and he loved the sound of the music.
Song Hong was unhappy when he heard that he regretted recommending him. When Huan Tan came out, Song Hong sat in his house wearing neat court clothes and sent someone to summon Huan Tan.
When Huan Tan arrived, he criticized him before he could sit down and said: "The reason why I recommend you is that you can help the country with morality. Now you have interfered with Zheng Sheng several times to mess with "Ya" and "Song". This is not a sign of loyalty."
Can you correct it yourself?
Or should we use Dharma to uplift others?
Huan Tan thanked him and waited for a long time before letting him go.
summary: Song Hong, courtesy name Zhongzi, was from Chang'an. He served under several emperors and Wang Mang. When Chimei entered Chang'an, he attempted suicide by drowning to avoid serving them but was rescued. Under Guangwu, he became Grand Sikong and was known for his honesty, distributing his rent among his clan. He once recommended Huan Tan to the emperor, but later criticized Huan Tan for playing secular music at court banquets, which Song Hong felt was inappropriate. When the emperor tried to arrange a marriage between Song Hong and his widowed sister, Princess Huyang, Song Hong refused, stating that a friend from humble times should not be forgotten, and a wife from poverty should not be cast aside. He was later dismissed from his post.

translation:
When the world was in turmoil, Cai Mao had always been friendly with Dou Rong, so he took refuge with Dou Rong. Dou Rong wanted to make him the prefect of Zhangye, but Cai Mao refused to take office. He only took enough rations every time he was paid.
Later, he and Dou Rong were both recruited, and then paid homage to Yilang, and then moved to Guanghan as governor, with good political achievements.
At that time, guests of the Yin family often violated official bans in the county. Cai Mao did not avoid any dispute cases.
It happened that Luoyang ordered Dong Xuan to correct Princess Huyang. The emperor became angry and arrested Dong Xuan, but later pardoned her.
Cai Mao liked Dong Xuan's uprightness and wanted the court to prohibit and restrict the illegal behavior of his relatives, so he wrote a letter saying: "When I hear that people are enlightened and want to teach, they must start with doing good; for people in Kang Guoning, the most important thing is to deal with evil people."
His Majesty's virtue has flourished, and he has once again inherited his great mission. Since he came to the throne, he has been prosperous all over the world.
You should get up early and go to bed late, and don't rest when you should.
However, recently, the family of nobles, concubines, and concubines have relied on their favors many times to violate official regulations, killing people without the death penalty, and injuring others without punishment.
I am afraid that laws and regulations will be abandoned and punishments will not be used.
Recently, the slave of the Princess of Huyang killed someone in the Western Market, and he rode in a carriage with the princess, going in and out of the palace, and escaped for many days without being punished.
Luoyang ordered Dong Xuan to handle the case according to the right way, regardless of the powerful, and to attack the murderer of the princess.
Your Majesty did not investigate first, but wanted to flog him more.
When Dong Xuan was angry with His Majesty, the capital paid close attention to him; when Your Majesty pardoned him, everyone in the world watched.
Nowadays, the foreign relatives are arrogant and have too many guests. We should order someone to handle the crime of adultery so that the just officials can always gain credibility and restrain illegal activities near and far.
Guangwu accepted it.
In the 20th year of Jianwu's reign, he replaced Dai She as Situ. He was honest, frugal and uncompromising in his duties.
He died in his post in the twenty-third year at the age of seventy-two. He was given a coffin in Dongyuan, and the funeral money was generous.
◆Feng Qin's biography: Feng Qin was named Wei Bo and was a native of Fanyang, Wei County.
Great-grandfather Feng Yang was the prefect of Hongnong during the reign of Emperor Xuan.
He had eight sons, each with two thousand stones. Zhao and Wei were very proud of him and called him Lord Wanshi.
All the brothers were strong, but Feng Qin's grandfather, Feng Yan, was less than seven feet tall. He was often ashamed of his short stature, fearing that his descendants would also be short, so he married his son Feng and his wife to a tall wife.
Feng Qin, the son of Feng and his wife, was eight feet three inches tall.
You can do arithmetic at the age of eight.
At first, he was the governor of Yaoqi, a meritorious officer, and had the title of capable person.
Yaoqi often went on expeditions from Guangwu, and entrusted all political affairs to Feng Qin.
summary: Cai Mao, courtesy name Zili, was from Hanoi. He was a renowned Confucian who refused to serve under Wang Mang. He took refuge with Dou Rong. Under Guangwu, he became the Grand Administrator of Guanghan. He wrote a memorial criticizing the illegal behavior of imperial relatives and praising the uprightness of Luoyang's magistrate, Dong Xuan. He later became Situ and was known for his honesty and frugality. He died in office.

translation:
Feng Qin and the county people Feng Xun and others raised troops to respond to Guangwu, but the plan failed and was opposed by the powerful right Jiao Lian and others. Feng Qin then led his mother, brothers and clan relatives to join Yaoqi. Yaoqi regarded them as confidants and recommended them to Guangwu.
He was not appointed at first, but later he was appointed as a doctor and served as a minister.
He was able to negotiate military supplies and was shrewd and diligent in doing things, so he was valued by Guangwu's cronies.
Every time he was introduced, the emperor always said to his left and right: "What a good official!"
As a result, Feng Qin was asked to examine the Jin feudal issues of the princes.
Feng Qin weighed the importance of merit, the distance of the country, the richness of the terrain, and made the reward consistent with the merit without exceeding it, which convinced everyone.
From then on, the system of nobility had to be reviewed and approved by Feng Qin.
The emperor thought that he was capable and ordered him to record all the affairs of the minister.
Situ Houba recommended Yan Yang, the former Liang commander.
Yan Yang was always ridiculed, and the emperor disliked him very much. When he saw Hou Ba's memorial, he suspected him of treachery. He was furious and sent a seal to Hou Ba, saying: "Do you think there is any place in Chongshan or Youdu that I can settle down?" Huang Yue suddenly had no place to go.
Do you want to test the law with your own body, or do you want to kill yourself to achieve benevolence?
He sent Feng Qin to Situ's mansion with the policy letter.
Feng Qin came back, stated Hou Ba's original intention, and explained the reasons for it. The emperor was a little more lenient and worshiped Feng Qin as the minister.
After serving for fifteen years, he was awarded the title of Marquis of Guannei for his hard work.
He moved to Shangshu Ling and became a minister of agricultural affairs. Three years later, he moved to Situ.
First, many of the three princes resigned because of their crimes. The emperor regarded Feng Qin as a virtuous person and wanted him to start well and end well. So he calmly warned him during the banquet and said: "Zhu Fu was not loyal to the emperor above and bullied his colleagues below. He actually slandered him until now. It is unknown whether he will live or die. Isn't it a pity!"
The ministers were exiled and punished, and although they were given additional rewards and sacrifices, they were still not enough to repay the immeasurable body.
Loyal ministers and filial sons look at their past lives as a warning.
If you can be loyal to the country and serve the emperor without any second thoughts, then the honors and honors will be glorious in this world, and the fame will be immortal. Shouldn't you encourage it?
Feng Qin became more respectful and conscientious in serving the country with loyalty, and was known as his official.
Feng Qin's mother was eighty years old. Every time she met, he ordered her not to bow. She ordered her attendants to help her go to the palace and face the kings and princesses and say: "It is this old mother who favors Feng Qin."
He is so respected. When he passed away in the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, the emperor mourned him and sent envoys to express his condolences. He also gave him a coffin in Dongyuan, which was a generous gift.
◆Zhao Xi's biography: Zhao Xi's courtesy name is Boyang, and he was a native of Wan, Nanyang County.
There is integrity when you are young.
His cousin was killed and he had no children. Zhao Xi was only fifteen years old and often wanted to take revenge.
summary: Feng Qin, courtesy name Wei Bo, was from Fanyang. He was tall and capable with arithmetic. He served as a meritorious officer under Yaoqi and was recommended to Guangwu. He was valued for his skill in negotiating military supplies and was put in charge of examining the fiefs of the princes, a system he established. He later became Situ. The emperor warned him to be a loyal minister, using the example of Zhu Fu. Feng Qin served with respect and conscientiousness. His mother was honored by the emperor. He died in office.

translation:
So he practiced weapons, entertained guests, and later went out for revenge.
The enemies were all sick and no one could resist.
Zhao Xi thought that killing someone in revenge for illness was not the behavior of a benevolent person, so he let him go for the time being.
Turn back and say to your enemies: If you recover from your illness, you should stay away from me.
The enemies all lay down and kowtowed to apologize.
After they recovered from their illness, they all came to see Zhao Xi. Zhao Xi refused to meet them and later killed them.
Gengshi came to the throne, and the Li family of Wucheng held the city and refused to surrender. Gengshi sent General Li Bao of Zhutian to recruit him to surrender, but Li refused and said: I heard that the Zhao family of Wan has an orphan grandson Zhao Xi who is famous for his faith and is willing to surrender to him.
Gengshi recruited Zhao Xi, who was less than twenty years old. After the introduction, Gengshi smiled and said: "You are still a child, how can you carry a heavy burden and carry a long distance?"
He was appointed as a doctor and acted as a military general. He was asked to go to Wuyin, and Li surrendered to him.
Therefore, Zhao Xi entered Yingchuan, attacked those who refused to surrender, reached the border of Runan, and returned to Wan.
Gengshi was overjoyed and said to Zhao Xi: "You are really a great talent, please work hard and encourage me."
It happened that Wang Mang sent Wang Xun and Wang Yi to lead their troops out of the pass. Gengshi worshiped Zhao Xi as the five powerful partial generals and asked him to assist the generals in resisting Wang Xun and Wang Yi in Kunyang.
Guangwu defeated Wang Xun and Wang Yi, Zhao Xi was wounded, and had meritorious service. After returning, he was worshiped as Zhonglang General and a Marquis for bravery.
The reform failed, and Zhao Xi was besieged by the red-browed soldiers, so he climbed up the house and escaped. He and his friend Han Zhongbo and dozens of others, carrying children and the infirm, climbed the mountain to overcome obstacles and left Wuguan.
Han Zhongbo thought that his wife was beautiful, but he was worried that someone would rape her and he would be harmed, so he wanted to abandon his wife on the road.
Zhao Xi was angry and refused to listen, so he smeared mud on Han Zhongbo's wife's face, put her on a cart, and pushed the cart with his own body.
Whenever she met a thief or wanted to persecute her, Zhao Xi would tell her that she was seriously ill and thus be spared.
When they arrived in Danshui County, they met Gengshi's family members. They were all naked, covered in mud, hungry and trapped, and could no longer move forward.
When Zhao Xi saw this, he was filled with sorrow and gave them all the clothes, silk and supplies he had packed, and escorted them back to their hometown.
At this time, Deng Feng was working in Nanyang. Zhao Xi was always friendly with Deng Feng and wrote to him several times to accuse him. However, the rumor maker falsely accused Zhao Xi of conspiring with Deng Feng, which the emperor used as suspicion.
When Deng Feng failed, the emperor searched for the letter written by Zhao Xi to Deng Feng, and was shocked and said: Zhao Xi is really an elder.
That is to say, he summoned Zhao Xi, received him, gave him a saddle and horse, and waited for the imperial edict to be placed in the public carriage.
summary: Zhao Xi, courtesy name Boyang, was from Wan. As a youth, he sought revenge for his cousin but delayed the act until his enemies recovered from illness. He was recruited by Gengshi to persuade the Li family of Wucheng to surrender. He fought at Kunyang and was wounded. After Gengshi's failure, he helped friends and Gengshi's family escape, protecting them from bandits. He was falsely accused of conspiracy but was cleared by the emperor. He served as a county magistrate and governor, suppressing bandits and punishing the powerful. He was known for his mercy, moving surrendered bandits to other counties. He became Taiwei and managed frontier affairs, ordering immigrants to return to their original lands. He presided over the funeral of Emperor Guangwu and established proper court etiquette for the princes. He died at age eighty-four.

translation:
In the first year of Zhongyuan, he followed Feng Chan Taishan.
Later, when the emperor died, Zhao Xi accepted the imperial edict and presided over the funeral.
At that time, all the vassal kings were in the capital. Since Wang Mang usurped the throne, the old rules and regulations no longer existed. The Crown Prince and the King of Donghai sat at the same table, and the charter was out of order.
Zhao Xi then looked upright, raised his sword across the palace steps, and helped the kings down to show their superiority and inferiority.
At that time, the officials of the vassal state came in and out of the palace and provinces, and they were no different from the other officials. Zhao Xi reported that he was escorted by his close servants and separated into other counties. The kings returned to their respective residences and only came in the morning and evening.
Clean the etiquette, strictly guard the door, and be solemn inside and outside.
In the first year of Yongping, he was granted the title of Marquis of the Countryside.
In the spring of three years, he was dismissed from office because he found out the truth about Zhongshan Prime Minister Xue.
In the winter of this year, Dai Dou Rong became a guard.
In the eighth year, he took over the affairs of the Taiwei on behalf of Yu Yan and lived in the mansion as if it were true.
Later, when his mother died, Shangshu requested to go home for the funeral, but Xianzong refused. He sent an envoy to take off his mourning clothes and rewarded him with great favors.
Zhao Xun presided over the imperial guards internally and held the position of prime minister externally.
When the emperor passed away, he presided over the funeral and performed the ceremony again, and the ceremony was complete.
Suzong ascended the throne, became Taifu, and took charge of the affairs of the Shangshu.
Among the seven people who promoted his sons to be officials, the eldest son Zhao Dai served in Huangmen.
In the fifth year of Jianchu's reign, Zhao Xi fell ill, and the emperor came to visit him in person.
After he died of illness, the emperor personally went to pay his respects. He was eighty-four years old, and his posthumous title was Zhenghou.

Mou Rong was well versed in classics and had great talent, and he was good at discussion. The court admired his talent. The emperor sighed many times, thinking that Mou Rong had the talent of a prime minister.
In the second year, Dai Fugong became Sikong. His actions were upright and prudent, and he was highly respected as a minister.
When Suzong came to the throne, Mou Rong was a famous official in the previous dynasty. He replaced Zhao Xi as the Taiwei, and participated in the affairs of the general minister with Zhao Xi.

The great ancestor Wei Xian was the prime minister during the reign of Emperor Xuan.
Zu Wei rewarded him, and he was the Grand Sima during the reign of Emperor Ai.

At the end of Jianwu's reign, he promoted filial piety and honesty, eliminated doctors, avoided retirement due to illness, and returned to teaching.
He lives in poverty and loves Taoism, but is indifferent to progress. All the Confucian scholars in the three auxiliaries admire him.
Xianzong heard about Wei Biao's reputation. In the sixth year of Yongping, he called him to pay homage to him, gave him carriages, horses and clothes, and moved him to be the prefect of Wei County.
Suzong ascended the throne and was relieved of his duties as prefect due to illness.
He was appointed as Zuo Zhonglang General and Changle Weiwei. He studied political skills and returned to the government every time.
He went to Shu several times to ask for his resignation, and he was appointed Captain of Fengche, with a rank of two thousand stones, and was rewarded with favors equal to those of his relatives.
In the seventh year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the emperor went on a hunting tour to the west. Wei Biao replaced Taichang Cong. He was summoned several times to ask about the old affairs, etiquette and customs of the three assistants.
Wei Biao therefore suggested: When inspecting the old capital in the west today, the heroes of Gaozu and Zhongzong should be traced, the heroes of Rongxian the first emperor should be praised, and their descendants should be recorded.
The emperor accepts.
When he arrived in Chang'an, he ordered Jing Zhaoyin and You Fufeng to seek the descendants of Xiao He and Huo Guang.
At that time, Huo Guang had no descendants, so he only named Xiao Xiong, a descendant of Xiao He, the Marquis of Zan.
In the second year of Jianchu, Cao Zhan, a descendant of Cao Shen, was granted the title of Marquis of Pingyang, so he no longer granted the title of descendant of Cao Shen.
So he gave Wei Biao money and delicacies and asked him to go back to Pingling to sweep the tomb and go to the tomb.
After returning, he worshiped him as Da Honglu.
At this time, many people who wrote letters said that most of the tributes from counties and counties were not in the order of merit, so that the duties were increasingly slack and the officials were neglected. The fault lies with the states and counties.
The emperor issued an edict and ordered the ministers to discuss the matter.
Wei Biao submitted a proposal and said: Your Majesty has issued an edict to care about the people, and you will be gracious to elect them to ensure that they are selected.
The country's top priority is to select talented people, and talented people should first act with filial piety.
Confucius said: If you are filial to relatives, your loyalty can be transferred to the king, so loyal ministers must be in the door of filial sons.
People rarely have both talent and behavior. Therefore, Meng Gongchuo is better than Zhao and Wei Lao, so he cannot be the doctor of Teng and Xue. Because Teng and Xue have small and complicated political affairs, they cannot bear it.
A person who is loyal and filial has a heart that is close to being generous; a person who has been trained and mature has a heart that is close to being mean.
The reason why the three generations have been able to follow a straight path is that the wise men in ancient times have been tempered and selected.
summary: Wei Biao, courtesy name Mengda, was from Pingling. He was a descendant of the prime minister Wei Xian. He was known for his filial piety, mourning his parents for three years. He was a learned Confucian who lived in poverty. He was summoned by Emperor Xianzong and became the Prefect of Wei County. He later served as Da Honglu. He submitted a memorial arguing that the selection of officials should prioritize filial piety and conduct over talent. He also advised the emperor to reduce harsh punishments and select officials with experience as state governors. He was known for his frugality and charity, leaving his family with no money. He wrote a twelve-chapter work titled "Wei Qingzi."

◆Preface to the Biographies of Scholars: Once upon a time, during the reigns of Wang Mang and Gengshi, the world was in turmoil, rituals and music collapsed, and domestic documents were incomplete. Guangwu Zhongxing was fond of classics. Before he ascended the throne, he visited refined scholars, collected incomplete classics, repaired omissions, and collected prose. In the past, scholars from all over the world mostly fled into the mountains and forests with their books in their arms.
From then on, they all gathered in the capital carrying books. Fan Sheng, Chen Yuan, Zheng Xing, Du Lin, Wei Hong, Liu Kun, Huan Rong and others also came one after another.
Therefore, the country established doctors of the Five Classics, and each taught students according to his own family method. There were Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing in the Yi, Ouyang, and Xiaoxiahou in the Shangshu, Qi, Lu, and Han in the Shi, Dai and Dai in the Rites, and Yan and Yan in the Spring and Autumn. There were fourteen doctors in total, and Taichang took the lead in turn.
In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, Taixue was built, and ancient models were studied. Bamboo bamboo rafts, wooden beans, and shields and axes used for dancing were all listed in Taixue. Students wearing straight collars and learning square steps walked slowly in it.
In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, Piyong, Mingtang and Lingtai were built.
Emperor Ming ascended the throne and saluted in person.
The emperor began to wear a crown that reached the sky, and wore the clothes of the sun, moon and stars. He was a chariot with dharma objects.
After the guests were dined and the rituals with the princes were completed, the emperor was sitting down to give a lecture. Confucian scholars were holding scriptures and asking questions. There were countless ministers and scholar-bureaucrats who walked around the bridge gate to watch and listen to the lecture.
After that, for the descendants of the meritorious officials and the last members of the four surnames, separate schools were established, and talented people were selected to teach. All the people from Yulin in Qimen were taught the chapters and verses of the "Book of Filial Piety", and the Xiongnu also sent their children to school.
Beautiful! So grand! It flourishes in Yongping! When the junior high school was built, the Confucians gathered at Baihu Temple to assess similarities and differences for several months.
Suzong personally came to give instructions. For example, in the third year of Emperor Xuan's Ganlu, he discussed the story in Shiqu Pavilion with Confucian scholars Wei Xuancheng, Liang Qiuhe and others. He ordered Shi Chen to write "White Tiger Tongyi".
He also ordered the talented students to receive "Guwen Shangshu", "Mao Shi", "Gu Liang" and "Zuo Shi Chun Qiu". Although they did not establish academic officials, they all promoted Gao Di to be a lecturer and give them a close handle. This was to catch the omissions and recluse, and to attract many families.
Xiaohe also visited Dongguan many times and read many books.
When Empress Deng exercised the power of the emperor, many scholars were slack.
At this time, both Fan Zhun and Xu Fang wrote letters stating the importance of teaching, and saying that there were too many Confucian positions for which they were not qualified, so they ordered the ministers to carefully select, and all the doctors in the three departments who were proficient in Confucian classics were elected.
After Emperor An took over the government, he did not pay attention to art and literature. Doctors reclined on seats without giving lectures. Friends looked at me and I looked at you. They were lazy and undisciplined. The school building was also ruined and became a vegetable garden. Here, shepherds and woodcutter gathered firewood and cut grass.
Emperor Shun was inspired by Zhai Youfu's words, so he rebuilt the school and built a total of 240 rooms and 1,850 rooms.
After taking the Ming Jing examination, the first disciples were recruited, and ten members of the first and second departments were added. Except for the senior scholars in the county and country, all the disciples were recruited.
In the first year of Benchu, the Empress Dowager Liang issued an edict: All the generals, down to six hundred stones, would send their children to school. Every year, they would dine with guests and gather with the princes in this month. This was a common practice.
Since then, the number of people studying abroad has increased, reaching more than 30,000 students.
However, the chapters and sentences gradually became sparse and more pompous, and the Confucian spirit declined.
The party members were executed, and most of the famous and philanthropic people were exiled and abandoned. Later, they accused each other out of anger, some secretly traded gold goods, and changed the characters of the Lantai lacquer script to match his private documents.
In the fourth year of Xiping's reign, Emperor Ling ordered all the Confucian scholars to rectify the Five Classics and engrave them on stone tablets, using ancient Chinese, seal script, and official calligraphy to verify each other.
At first, Guangwu moved the capital back to Luoyang, and those documents and secretaries were carried in 2,000 vehicles. From then on, the number was three times as many as before.
When Dong Zhuo moved the capital, the officials and the people were disruptive, and the classics and articles collected in Piyong, Dongguan, Lantai, Shishi, Xuanming, and Hongdu were lost one after another. The large ones were connected into curtains, and the small ones were made into bags.
summary: During the reigns of Wang Mang and Gengshi, the world fell into chaos, causing the collapse of rituals and music and the loss of documents. Emperor Guangwu, who favored classical studies, gathered scholars and restored texts. Scholars from across the land brought their books to the capital. The state established fourteen doctors for the Five Classics, each teaching according to their family methods. In the fifth year of Jianwu, the Imperial Academy was built, and later, structures like Piyong, Mingtang, and Lingtai were erected. Emperor Ming personally performed rituals, lectured on classics, and established separate schools for descendants of meritorious officials. The Xiongnu even sent their children to study. During Emperor Zhang’s reign, Confucians gathered at the White Tiger Hall to discuss texts, resulting in the "White Tiger General Meaning." However, under Empress Deng’s regency, scholarly activity waned. Emperor An neglected arts and literature, leading to the decay of school buildings. Emperor Shun rebuilt the academy, adding 240 rooms and 1,850 houses, and recruited students. By the time of Empress Dowager Liang, the number of students exceeded 30,000, but scholarly rigor declined. After the execution of party members, corruption and textual alterations spread. In the fourth year of Xiping, Emperor Ling ordered the Five Classics to be engraved on stone tablets in multiple scripts. When Dong Zhuo moved the capital, many texts were lost or destroyed, with only seventy carts remaining after transport to Chang'an, half of which were lost. Later, all were burned in the chaos of Chang'an.

In the spring of the fourth year, the emperor drove out to inspect the houses in the city. Soon he heard that he was going to Hanoi for hunting. Liu Cang wrote to dissuade him, saying: "I heard that the season is in season and farming is very busy in the peak spring, so we should not gather people to make meritorious deeds."
Ancient books say: If there is no place to stay in the field while hunting, no food and drink to enjoy, and no regularity in going in and out, then the trees will not be straight.
summary: Liu Kang, King An of Jinan, was known for not following laws and socializing with guests. He was accused of conspiracy, but the emperor, due to their kinship, only reduced his fief. He later became extravagant, with many slaves, horses, and private lands. A governor admonished him, but he did not change his ways. He died after 59 years of rule. Liu Cang, King Xian of Dongping, was intelligent and well-read. He served as General of Hussars under Emperor Xianzong and helped establish ritual systems. He often advised the emperor, once persuading him to cancel a hunting trip. He repeatedly asked to resign from his high post, which the emperor eventually allowed. He was known for his virtue and was greatly respected. The emperor frequently sought his advice on state matters. He died in the 2nd year of Jianchu, and his son succeeded him.
