translation:
Feng Yi and Chimei met in Huayin. They resisted each other for more than sixty days and fought for dozens of rounds. Chimei surrendered Liu Shi, Wang Xuan and more than 5,000 people to Feng Yi.
In the spring of the third year of Jianwu, the envoys sent by Guangwu worshiped Feng Yi as the general for the expedition to the west.
It happened that Deng Yu and his cavalry general Deng Hong and others returned with troops and met Feng Yi. Deng Yu and Deng Hong asked Feng Yi to attack Chimei together.
Feng Yi said: I have been at odds with the thieves for dozens of days. Although I have repeatedly captured their heroes, there are still many people left. I can slowly lure them with kindness and trust, but it is difficult to defeat them quickly with troops.
Now the emperor has the generals stationed at Lianchi to block his way back east, while Feng Yi attacks the west and captures it in one fell swoop. This is a surefire plan. Deng Yu and Deng Hong refused.
Deng Hong fought with Chimei for many days, but Chimei pretended to be defeated, abandoned his baggage and fled.
The cart was loaded with soil and covered with beans. The soldiers were hungry and scrambled to get the beans for food.
Chimei led his troops back to attack Deng Hong, but Deng Hong's army collapsed and ran away.
Feng Yi and Deng Yu joined forces to rescue him, and Chimei Shao retreated.
Feng Yi thought that the soldiers were hungry and tired and should rest for a while, but Deng Yu refused to listen and fought again. He was defeated by Chimei, killing more than 3,000 people.
Deng Yu was able to escape and return to Yiyang. Feng Yi abandoned his horse and walked back to Xiguban on foot, and returned to camp with several of his men.
Then hold on to the fortress, take back the scattered soldiers, recruit tens of thousands of soldiers from various camps, and make an appointment with the thieves to fight at a time.
Let the strong men under the tent wear the same clothes as Red Eyebrow and lie in ambush on the side of the road.
Early in the morning, Chimei sent ten thousand people to attack Feng Yi's front. Feng Yi deliberately sent out a small number of troops to rescue him.
Seeing that Feng Yi's army was weak, the thieves attacked Feng Yi from all fronts, and Feng Yi launched a battle.
When the sun turned to the west, the vigor of the thieves was weak, and Feng Yi's ambush troops suddenly came out. Their clothes were the same as those of Red Eyebrows. Red Eyebrows could not be recognized, so the thieves were frightened and routed.
Feng Yi pursued and defeated the bandits at the bottom of Guodi. Eighty thousand men and women surrendered to Feng Yi.
There were still more than 100,000 people left, and they walked eastward to Yiyang and surrendered.
Guangwu's seal sent condolences to Feng Yi and said: Chimei was defeated and pacified, and the officials worked hard. Although they were defeated at first and returned to Xiguban, they finally achieved great success in Lianchi. It can be said that the east corner was lost and the mulberry tree was gained.
I am giving you rewards based on your merits to reward you for your great contributions.
Although Chimei had surrendered at this time, many bandits were still in power; Yancen occupied Lantian, Wang Xin occupied Xiaguiquan, Fangdan occupied Xinfeng, Jiang Zhen occupied Baling, Zhang Han occupied Chang'an, Gongsun Shou occupied Changling, and Yang Zhou They occupied the mouth of the valley, Lu Qian occupied Chencang, Jiao Hong occupied Wei, Luo Yan occupied Ji, Ren Liang occupied Huaili, and each of them was called a general. Some had more than 10,000 men, and some had thousands of men. They attacked each other.
Feng Yi marched while fighting and stationed troops in Shanglin Garden.
After Yancen defeated Chimei, he claimed to be the king of Wu'an and set up prefectural and animal governors. He wanted to occupy Hanzhong and led Zhang Han and Ren Liang to jointly attack Feng Yi.
Feng Yi defeated him and beheaded more than a thousand people. Those who were attached to Yancen from all the camps came to surrender to Feng Yi.
Yancen went to attack Xixian County. Feng Yi sent General Deng Ye of Fuhan and General Yu Kuang of Fuhan to attack Yancen. They defeated Yancen. His general Su Chen and more than 8,000 people surrendered to the Han army.
Yancen fled from Wuguan to Nanyang.
At this time, the people were hungry, people were eating each other, and a pound of gold could only be exchanged for five liters of beans.
Roads were cut off and transportation was inaccessible, so the soldiers relied on fruits as food.
He issued an edict and appointed Zhao Kuang of Nanyang as You Fufeng. He led the army to assist Feng Yi and sent silk and millet. Everyone in the army called him Long Live.
As the food for Feng Yi's soldiers gradually increased, he gradually punished and attacked the heroes who disobeyed the orders, and commended and rewarded those who had made meritorious service after surrendering. All the generals were sent to the capital, and all the tribesmen were dispersed back to their hometowns. Might and virtue prevailed in Guanzhong.
Only Lu Tuna, Zhang Han, and Jiang Zhen sent envoys to surrender to Shu, and the rest were all pacified.
The next year, Gongsun Shu sent general Cheng Yan and led tens of thousands of people out of Lutun to station in Chencang.
Feng Yi and Zhao Kuang met the attack and defeated Cheng Yan. Cheng Yan retreated back to Hanchuan.
Feng Yi pursued and fought in Jigu, and again defeated Cheng Yan. He returned to attack and defeated Lu Tuna, and many of the camp guards surrendered.
Later, Shu sent generals to take advantage of the opportunity many times, and Feng Wenbu defeated him.
It only took three years to recruit the people and redress their grievances. Many people came to Shanglin to join him.
summary: Feng Yi faced Chimei in Huayin, fighting for over sixty days. Despite initial setbacks, he used an ambush strategy, dressing his troops like Chimei to cause confusion, and defeated them, forcing 80,000 to surrender. He then pacified Guanzhong, defeating various bandit leaders like Yancen and Zhang Han. Feng Yi governed with justice, recruiting people and redressing grievances. When rumors arose that he was acting arrogantly, Guangwu showed him the accusations, and Feng Yi wrote a humble apology, reaffirming his loyalty. Guangwu reassured him of their bond.

translation:
All the generals said: "Kuihuo has a strong army and is coming to seize victory. Do not fight with him." The army should be stopped at a convenient place and slowly think about the strategy. Feng Yi said: When Wei Xiao's troops came to the border, they were accustomed to fighting for small profits, so they wanted to take advantage of the situation and go deeper.
If we capture the city, it will shake the three assistants, which is my worry.
The Art of War says that if there are not enough attackers, there will be more than enough defenders.
Now, occupying the city first and waiting for work is not a matter of competing with him. So he entered the city secretly, closed the city gates, silenced his flags and drums, and went on patrol without knowing it, and rushed to the city.
Feng Yi took advantage of his surprise and suddenly beat the drums and flags to rush out. The patrol troops panicked and ran around in confusion. Feng Yi pursued them for dozens of miles and defeated the patrol troops.
Ji Zun is also attacking Wang Yuan.
So all the powerful leaders in the north, Geng Ding and others, rebelled against Kuai Xiao and surrendered to the Han.
Feng Yi wrote a letter explaining the situation and did not dare to be proud of his own merits.
Some generals want to share their achievements. Guangwu felt worried.
Then he issued a seal saying: The imperial edict was issued to the commander-in-chief, generals Huya, Jianwei, Hanzhong, Qilu, and Wuwei: The prisoners led their troops to march down to Long, and the three assistants were frightened.
The city is in danger and is in danger.
All the camps and security guards in the north stood still and watched.
Now that the outlying city has been preserved and the captive troops have suffered a setback, Geng Ding and his followers have regained their righteousness as kings and ministers.
The general's achievements in conquering the West are like mountains and hills, but he still thinks that he is not reserved enough.
What is the difference between Meng Zhi who rebelled against the Queen and rejected the Qi troops without claiming his merit?

The text notes that Feng Yi avoided disaster by leaving a place with an ominous name, while Cen Peng was unable to do so and met his end, suggesting that fate may play a role in such matters.

translation:
"The Book of Songs" and "Shangshu" have discussed women's moral character for a long time.
As for the virtuous concubines who help the king handle political affairs, the wise women who are prosperous in running the family, the noble men who promote the honest and honest customs, and the chaste women who show their pure conduct, then their virtues are no different, but the records of this aspect are omitted in the classics of the past dynasties.
Therefore, since the ZTE, the existing deeds of women have been synthesized into "Lienv Pian".
Empress Ma, Empress Deng, and Empress Liang were separately recorded in the previous "Queen's Notes", and Liang's daughter-in-law and Li Ji were included in their respective family biographies. This situation will not be described again.
Others only search for people whose Chinese talents and conduct are particularly outstanding, and do not necessarily focus on the moral aspect.
Biography of Bao Xuan's Wife, Bohai Bao Xuan's wife, Huan's daughter, named Shaojun.
Bao Xuan once studied under Shaojun's father. His father thought that he was poor, so he married his daughter to him with a lot of dowry and wealth.
Bao Xuan was unhappy and said to his wife: "Young Master was born in a rich family. He is arrogant and accustomed to dressing up beautifully. But I am too poor and humble to receive such a gift."
The wife said: My master thinks that my husband is a good man and keeps his promise, so I make my concubine serve as a turban.
Since I am married to you, I will obey your arrangements in everything. Bao Xuan laughed and said: "This is my ambition."
His wife then returned all the imperial clothes, put on short cloth clothes, and returned to the countryside with Bao Xuan's deer cart.
After paying homage to my aunt, I took the urn to fetch water. She practiced women's ways, and people in her country praised her.
Bao Xuan, during the reign of Emperor Ai, became Sili Xiaowei.
His son Bao Yong served as the prefect of Lu County in the early years of the Zhongxing Dynasty.
Bao Yong's son Bao Yu calmly asked the young gentleman: "Does Madam still remember what happened when the deer cart was pulled?"
Answer: My late aunt has a saying: Don’t forget death when you are alive, don’t forget danger when you are safe.
How dare I forget?
Bao Yong and Bao Yu have already seen the prequel.
The Legend of Wang Ba's Wife, the wife of Taiyuan Wang Ba, is a girl from an unknown family.
When Wang Ba was a young man, he established high moral standards, and when he was powerful, he was repeatedly summoned but could not become an official.
Ba's deeds can be found in "The Biography of Yi Min".
My wife also has good intentions.
At first, Wang Ba became friends with Zibo, a fox from the same county. Later, Zibo became the prime minister of Chu, and his son became a meritorious official.
Zibo then sent his son to deliver a message to Wang Ba, with carriages, horses, clothing, and servants looking elegant and luxurious.
Ba's son was farming in the fields. When he heard that the guests were coming, he left his grass behind and came back. When he saw Linghu's son, he was so depressed and ashamed that he did not dare to look up at anyone.
Wang Ba felt ashamed when he saw it. The guest left and he couldn't get up for a long time.
summary: The moral and virtuous deeds of women from historical records, compiled into "Lienv Pian" since the ZTE period. It includes biographies of notable women, emphasizing their conduct and contributions.

translation:
The wife felt strange and asked why. At first he refused to say anything, but his wife apologized, and then said: "Zibo and I have always been different. Just now I saw his son's appearance and clothing are very glorious, and his behavior is very appropriate. But my son has sharp hair and sharp teeth, does not understand etiquette rules, and looks ashamed when meeting guests."
The love between father and son is so deep that I feel a little embarrassed.
My wife said: You should cultivate your integrity and disregard your honor and salary.
How can Zibo's nobility compare to your aloofness now?
Why did you forget your ambition and feel ashamed for your son?
Wang Ba stood up and smiled and said: Is there such a thing?
So he lived in seclusion for the rest of his life.
Biography of Jiang Shi's Wife, Jiang Shi's wife in Guanghan, and the daughter of Pang Sheng in the same county.
Jiang Shi's mother was extremely filial, and her wife was even more submissive.
My mother likes to drink from the river. The water is six or seven miles away from home, and my wife often goes against the current to fetch water.
Later, there was a wind and she could not return home on time. Her mother was thirsty, so Jiang Shi blamed his wife and sent her home.
The wife then stayed in the neighbor's house, spinning crops day and night, buying some good vegetables, and asking the neighbor's mother to give them to her mother-in-law as she wished.
After doing this for a long time, my mother-in-law felt strange and asked her neighbor's mother, who told her the truth.
The mother-in-law felt ashamed and called her back, and Ennuang became even more diligent.
Later, her son drowned while fetching water from a distant place. The wife was afraid that her mother-in-law would be sad and did not dare to tell him about it, so she pretended that she was not at home because she had gone to school.
The mother-in-law likes to eat fish, but she cannot eat it alone. The couple often works hard to provide for the fish and asks the neighboring mothers to eat together. Suddenly there is a spring next to the house, with the same taste as river water. A pair of carp appears every morning, which is often used to feed the two mothers-in-law.
The skirmishers of the Red Eyebrow Army passed by Jiang Shi's hometown and said: "To disturb a filial person will definitely offend the ghosts and gods."
At that time, there was a famine, so the thief sent some rice and meat to Jiang Shi. Jiang Shi accepted it and buried it, and the neighboring vassal was also safe.
In the third year of Yongping, Xiaolian was inspected, and Xianzong issued an edict: "When a person of great filial piety enters the court, all whistleblowers will be punished by him."
From then on, they all became doctors.
Jiang Shi was soon appointed Jiangyin Order and died in his official position.
Wherever he lives, the villagers set up sacrifices for him.
Biography of Zhou Yu's wife, Zhou Yu's wife in Pei County, daughter of Zhao Xiao in the same county, named A.
When he was young, he studied ancient etiquette and became accustomed to the ways of women. However, Zhou Yu was proud, lazy, impatient, and often did rude things.
Zhou Yu's father, Zhou Wei, said to Zhao A: The bride is the daughter of a wise man and should correct her husband with the right way.
If Zhou Yu doesn't correct his mistakes, it's the bride's fault.
summary: Bao Xuan's wife, Shaojun, married him despite his poverty, returned her dowry, and lived frugally, earning praise for her virtue. Wang Ba's wife encouraged him to maintain his integrity over worldly honors, leading him to a life of seclusion. Jiang Shi's wife fetched river water for her mother-in-law daily, and when sent away, secretly provided food through a neighbor. Her filial piety moved bandits to spare her family, and she was later honored.

translation:
After Zhao Abai accepted the order, he stepped back and said to the people around him: I don't have the character of Fan Ji of Chu State or Wei Ji of Qi State, so my father-in-law blames me. If I say something but he doesn't listen, my father-in-law will say that I don't follow the orders, so the fault is mine.
If it is said and it works, it means that the son disobeys his father and obeys the woman, and then the sin is his.
What’s the point of life like this!
So he committed suicide.
People at the time did not sympathize with her.
According to the biography of Cao Shishu's wife in Fufeng, Cao Shishu's wife was the daughter of Ban Biao from the same county. His name is Zhao, his courtesy name is Huiban, and he is also known as Ji. He is knowledgeable and talented.
Uncle Shi died early, but Ban Zhao had good moral integrity and behaved according to etiquette.
His elder brother Ban Gu was the author of the "Book of Han", but he died before finishing the Eight Tables and "Tianwen Zhi". Emperor He ordered Ban Zhao to go to the Dongguan Library to continue writing it.
The emperor summoned Zhao to the palace many times, and asked the queen and other nobles to worship Ban Zhao as their teacher, and called him "Everyone". Whenever valuable items from various places contributed to Ban Zhao, he asked everyone to write poems to praise him.
When Empress Dowager Deng came to court to listen to politics, she asked Ban Zhao to participate in the handling of political affairs.
Thinking that Ban Zhao was very diligent, he made an exception and made Ban Zhao's son Cao a Marquis of Guannei, and he became the prime minister of Qi.
At that time, the "Book of Han" had just come out, and many people could not read it. Ma Rong from the same county worshiped you and learned from Ban Zhao to read the "Book of Han". Later, the emperor issued an edict asking Ma Rong's brother Ma Xu to finish the book after Ban Zhao.
During the Yongchu period, the Queen Mother's brother, General Deng Zhi, requested to retire due to the death of his mother. The Queen Mother did not intend to approve it and asked Ban Zhao. Ban Zhao went to Shudao and said: "I believe that Her Majesty the Queen Mother has perfect moral character. She conducted the affairs of the Tang Dynasty and Yu-like times, opened up her opinions, listened to the advice of mad men and blind old men, and accepted the opinions of villagers in the mountains and wild villages."
I am a foolish concubine who lives in the age of sage and dare not speak boldly to repay the emperor's kindness just in case.
I heard that humility has been a very high virtue since ancient times. Therefore, ancient books record that gods send blessings.
Once upon a time, the brothers Boyi and Shuqi gave up their country, and the world admired their high style. The Taibo gave up his throne to his younger brother, and Confucius praised them again and again.
This is the reason why one has noble moral character and is famous for future generations.
The Analects of Confucius says: If you can govern the country with courtesy, what difficulties will it face in politics?
From this point of view, the meaning of giving in is very far-reaching.
Now the Fourth Uncle General insists on the principle of loyalty and filial piety and requests to retire, but Your Majesty considers that the border areas are still uneasy and refuses to agree. If today's virtues are covered up due to some small mistakes in the future, I am afraid that the reputation of resignation will never be achieved again.
This is a villain's opinion, and I dare to express it at my own risk.
summary: Zhou Yu's wife, Zhao A, committed suicide after her father-in-law blamed her for her husband's rudeness, unable to correct him. Ban Zhao, a learned widow, completed the "Book of Han" and advised Empress Dowager Deng on political matters, including accepting General Deng Zhi's retirement. She wrote "Female Commandments" and died at seventy, mourned by the empress dowager.

translation:
Yangzi's wife raised her head and sighed to the sky. She cut her neck with a knife and died. The robbers did not kill her mother-in-law. When the prefect heard about this, he immediately killed the robbers, rewarded Yangzi's wife with some silk cloth, buried her with etiquette, and called her "Zhenyi".
Biography of Cheng Wenju's wife, Cheng Wenju's wife in Hanzhong, sister of Li Fa from the same county.
The courtesy name is Mu Jiang. He has two sons and his ex-wife has four sons.
Wen Ju died in his official position while serving as an order for peace.
The four sons thought their mother was their stepmother, and their hatred grew day by day. However, Mu Jiang was kind and gentle, and raised her more devotedly, providing twice as much food, clothing, and money as her biological sons. Someone said to the mother: The four children are very unfilial, why not let them live in another place to alienate them?
Answer: I am using righteousness to guide them and let them change for the better.
Later, the eldest son of his ex-wife, Cheng Xing, became seriously ill. The stepmother felt uneasy and personally prepared the medicine and meals. She was extremely kind.
Cheng Xing was ill for a long time before he recovered, so he called his three younger brothers and said: "My stepmother is kind and kind, which comes from instinct." We brothers don't know how to be filial and have the hearts of animals.
Although maternal love is stronger, our sins are also deeper. So he sent his three younger brothers to Nanzheng Prison to explain his mother's kindness and his own faults, and asked for punishment.
The county magistrate reported to the county warden, who commended his mother, exempted his family from serving as a servant, sent his four sons home, and allowed them to change their ways. From then on, their discipline became clearer and they all became good men.
Mu Jiangnian died in his eighties. Before he died, he told his sons: My younger brother Bodu is a wise and understanding man. The thin burial he mentioned has a profound meaning.
There are also some dying decrees from the previous dynasty. They are all decrees of the sages. I ask you to abide by them and not be the same as the customs and increase my burden.
All the sons did as he was told. The biography of the filial daughter Cao E, the filial daughter Cao E, was born in Shangyu, Kuaiji.
His father, Cao Xu, could play strings, sing, and did witchcraft.
On May 5, the second year of Han'an, Yu Xianjiang danced against the current to welcome the gods and drowned. His body was not found.
When Cao E was just fourteen years old, she cried along the river day and night. Seventeen days later, she threw herself into the river and died.
In the first year of Yuanjia, the county magistrate buried Cao E next to Jiangnan Road and erected a monument in her honor. Biography of Wu Xusheng's wife, Wu Xusheng's wife, the daughter of the Lu family, named Rong. When Wu Xusheng was young, he was fond of gambling and neglected his moral conduct. Lu Rong often did housework to support his mother-in-law.
I persuaded my husband to study several times, and every time he found something wrong, I cried to persuade him.
Lu Rong's father hated his son-in-law for not living up to expectations, so he asked his daughter to remarry someone else. Lu Rong sighed: This is how life should be, not divorce.
Still refused to go home. Wu Xusheng was grateful and encouraged himself, so he went far away to study with a teacher, and later became famous. Soon he was recruited by Honshu and went to Shouchun. He was killed by bandits on the way.
summary: Leyangzi's wife urged her husband to return found gold and complete his studies, cutting cloth to illustrate wasted effort. She supported her mother-in-law and died defending her honor from robbers. Cheng Wenju's wife, Mu Jiang, treated her stepchildren kindly, leading them to reform and become virtuous. Cao E, a filial daughter, drowned seeking her father's body and was honored with a monument.

translation:
The governor Yin Yao caught the thieves and found their whereabouts. Lu Rong was on the way to attend the funeral. After hearing the news, he went to the state and asked to see the enemy before he was willing to do so. Yin Yao agreed.
Lu Rong then cut off his head with his own hands as a sacrifice to her husband's spirit.
Later, the county was attacked by bandits who wanted to invade her. Lu Rong jumped over the wall to escape, but the bandits chased her with swords drawn.
The thief said: If you obey me, you will live; if you don't obey, I will die.
Lu Rong said: I will never be insulted by robbers.
So the thief killed her. It was a stormy day with thunder and lightning. The thieves kowtowed in fear and apologized, so they buried Lu Rong. Biography of Yuan Wei's Wife: Yuan Wei's wife from Runan was the daughter of Fufeng Ma Rong, named Lun.
Yuan Wei's deeds have been revealed in the prequel. Mullen has little eloquence.
Ma Rong comes from a wealthy family and has a lot of dowry materials.
When it was time for her wedding, Yuan Wei asked her: "It's okay for a woman to just carry a dustpan and broom. Why should she dress up too beautifully?"
He replied: My dear relatives love me so much that I dare not go against my orders.
If you want to admire the noble moral character of Bao Xuan and Liang Hong, I will also ask you to follow Shaojun and Meng Guang.
Yuan Wei added: "My dear brother held a wedding, and the world thought it was a joke." Your sister is not married yet. Is it okay for you to get married first? Answer: My sister has noble moral character and special appearance. She has not found a good spouse, unlike some despicable people who just find someone at random.
He also asked: "Your father is the governor of Nanjun. He has profound knowledge and his articles have become the most popular in the world. However, his position is often damaged by goods and wealth. Why?"
Answer: Confucius, the great sage, was inevitably destroyed by his uncle Wushu; Zilu, the great sage, was also accused by Gong Boliao. My father should have been in this situation.
Yuan Wei remained silent and could not make his wife understand. The people listening outside the tent felt ashamed. Yuan Wei was favored at that time, and Ma Lun was also famous.
He died in his sixties.
Ma Lun's sister Ma Zhi is also talented and righteous. When I was young, I was bereaved, but I kept feeling it in my heart for a long time, so I wrote "Shen Qing Fu".
According to the legend of Pang Ao's mother, Pang Ao's mother in Jiuquan is the daughter of Zhao.
The word E. His father was killed by people from the same county, and the three Zhao E brothers all died of illness at that time. The enemy was happy and congratulated himself, thinking that no one would take revenge.
Zhao E was secretly very angry, so she secretly prepared weapons and often rode in a curtained carriage to wait for her enemies.
I couldn't do it for more than ten years.
Later, when they met in Duting, they assassinated their enemy.
So he surrendered to the county. He said: My father's revenge has been avenged, and I beg to be punished.
Yin Jia, the head of Lu, thought that Zhao E was very loyal, so he took off his seal and wanted to escape with her. Zhao E refused to leave and said: "It is your duty as a concubine to hold resentment in your heart to the point of death. It is your common sense to settle crimes and try cases." How dare you live an ignoble existence and violate the law?
summary: Wu Xusheng's wife, Lu Rong, supported her mother-in-law, encouraged her husband to study, and avenged his death. She died resisting bandits. Yuan Wei's wife, Ma Lun, defended her family's wealth and her father's reputation, matching her husband's wit. Pang Ao's mother, Zhao E, avenged her father's murder after years, surrendered, and was pardoned.

translation:
Later, he was pardoned and exempted from the death penalty. The state and county commended her village.
Taichang Zhang Huan sighed in praise and treated her with the gift of tying silk. Biography of Liu Changqing's Wife: The wife of Liu Changqing in Pei County and the daughter of Huan Luan in the same county. A boy was born, who was just five years old, and the chief minister died. His wife was far away from suspicion and refused to return to her parents' home.
When the son reached the age of fifteen, he died again. The wife considered that she would inevitably marry again, so she punished her ears in advance to show her determination. The women of the same clan all sympathized with her and said: "Your family has no other intentions. If so, you can still express your sincerity through your sister. Why should you value your righteousness at the expense of your own body?"
Answer: In the past, I was the emperor of Wu Geng. My knowledge was taught by Confucianists, and I was so noble that I became the emperor's teacher.
Since the fifth watch, throughout the ages, men have been known for their loyalty and filial piety, while women have been known for their chastity and obedience. "The Book of Songs" says: There is no such thing as an ancestor, and Yu Jue is virtuous.
Therefore, I punished myself in advance to show my mood.
Wang Ji, the prime minister of Pei, reported her noble character and showed off her family name. She was known as "Xingyi Huanli". If there were sacrifices in the county, she would definitely send her the remaining meat.
According to the biography of Huangfu Gui's wife, An Ding Huangfu Gui's wife was an unknown surname.
After Huangfugui's first wife died, he married her again.
His wife can write articles and cursive script, and often works as secretary for Huangfu Gui. Everyone is amazed by her talent.
When Huangfu Gui died, his wife was still young and beautiful.
Later, when Dong Zhuo became prime minister, he heard that his wife was beautiful, so he used a hundred floats, twenty horses, and a lot of money from slaves as betrothal gifts to marry her.
Gui's wife went to Dong Zhuo in plain clothes, knelt down and stated her difficulties, speaking very sadly. Dong Zhuo ordered his servants to draw their steel swords and surround him, and said: My prestige will make the people of the world surrender. Can it not work on a woman like you? Gui's wife knew that she could not escape death, so she stood up and cursed loudly: "You are a wild bastard, and you have harmed many people in the world. Isn't that enough?"
The integrity of my ancestors is known to the whole world. My husband, Huangfu, is a versatile man in both civil and military affairs. He was a loyal minister of the Han Dynasty. Weren't you his pawn in the past?
How dare you do something indecent in front of your wife? Dong Zhuo then pushed the cart into the court, hung the woman's head on the yoke of the cart, and asked his slaves to beat her with whips and sticks. Huangfu Gui's wife said to the man holding the stick: "Why don't you hit him hard?" The sooner you die, the better.
So he was beaten to death under the car. Later generations drew her image and inscribed it with the word "Li Zong". The Biography of Yin Yu's Wife, the wife of Yin Yu in Nanyang, the daughter of Xun Shuang in Yingchuan. Ming Cai, whose courtesy name is Nu Xun, is smart and talented.
At the age of seventeen, she married into the Yin family. A daughter was born at the age of nineteen, and Yin Yu died.
summary: Liu Changqing's wife mutilated her ear to avoid remarriage after her son's death, earning recognition for chastity. Huangfu Gui's wife cursed Dong Zhuo for his atrocities and was beaten to death, later honored. Yin Yu's wife, Xun Cai, resisted remarriage and hanged herself after being forced to Guo's house. Shengdao's wife, Yuanjiang, took her husband's place in prison, allowing his escape, and was executed.

translation:
Xun Cai was still young at the time and was often worried that her family would force her to remarry, so she defended herself very resolutely.
Later, when Guo Yi, a native of the same county, lost his wife, Xun Shuang promised Cai Cai to him, so he falsely claimed that he was seriously ill and called Cai home.
Xun Cai had no choice but to go home and vowed his determination with a knife in his hand.
Xun Shuang ordered Fu's maid to snatch her knife and help her get into the car. He was also worried that she would be angry and was very defensive.
When the daughter arrived at Guo's house, she pretended to be happy and said to the people around her: "I was determined to die on the same acupuncture point as my husband Yin Yu, but I was forced by my family to come here. What should I do if I can't fulfill my wish?" So he ordered the servant girl to build four lanterns and dress up. Guo Yi came in and met each other, and they talked together without stopping.
Guo Yi was in awe of her, so he didn't dare to force her to get married. He didn't come out until dawn. Xun Cai then ordered everyone to prepare a bath. After entering the bathroom, he closed the door, ordered the waiter to get out of the way, and wrote on the door in pink: "The body returns to the grave."  The word Yin was not written, and he was afraid that someone would come, so he hanged himself with his clothes belt.
The people around her didn't take it seriously. When they found out she had passed away, people felt pity for her at that time.
According to the biography of Shengdao's wife, Qian was the wife of Shengdao and the daughter of the Zhao family in the same county.
The word Yuanjiang. In the fifth year of Jian'an, the Yizhou tribe was in chaos. Shengdao gathered a crowd to raise troops. However, the matter failed and the couple was arrested and sentenced to death.
Yuanjiang sued Shengdao in the evening and said: The law has certain penalties and there will be no hope of survival. You can escape quickly and establish a family. I will stay in prison and bear the responsibility for your crimes.
Shengdao didn't make up his mind, so Yuanjiang released Shengdao's shackles and helped him get some food.
His son Sheng Xiang was five years old at the time, so Sheng Dao took him and fled.
Yuanjiang took the place of her husband and held the night, coping well. It was estimated that Shengdao had gone far away, so he told the jailer the truth and was killed when the time came.
Shengdao and his son met Amnesty and returned home.
Shengdao was grateful for her loyalty and never married again. The filial daughter's uncle preceded the male, the filial daughter's uncle preceded the male, Qianwei was born.
His father, Uncle Nihe, was a county meritorious official in the early years of Yongjian. The county magistrate sent Ni and a letter of worship to see the governor of Bajun. The boat fell into the turbulent water and drowned. The zombies did not return home.
Uncle Xianxiong was filled with resentment and grief. He cried day and night and did not want to live. He often thought of drowning himself.
The two children were a few years old, a boy and a girl. Xiong made a bag each, filled it with beads and tied it to the child. He said goodbye several times. Every time the family tried to prevent her, but after more than a hundred days they relaxed a little, Xiong took a small boat and cried at the place where his father fell into the water. Then he threw himself into the water and died. My younger brother, Shuxian, dreamed that night that his sister told him: Stay back for six days and emerge from the water at the same time as your father. When the time came, I waited, and sure enough, I was floating on the river with my father. The counties commended him, erected monuments in his honour, and painted his portrait.
According to the biography of Dong Si's wife, Chen Liu, Dong Si's wife, was the daughter of Cai Yong from the same county. Her name was Yan and her courtesy name was Wenji.
summary: The filial daughter Uncle Xianxiong drowned herself after her father's death, emerging with his body. Dong Si's wife, Cai Wenji, was captured by Xiongnu, bore children, and was ransomed by Cao Cao. She saved her husband from execution and recited ancient texts from memory. Her poems recount her suffering and loss. The text praises these women's virtues and deeds.

translation:
◆Liu Yanchuan, Liu Yan, courtesy name Junlang, was from Jingling, Jiangxia, and was a descendant of King Lu Gong.
During the reign of Emperor Suzong, the Liu family moved to Jingling.
When Liu Yan was young, he served in prefectures and counties, and was awarded the position of doctor because he was a member of the emperor's clan.
After leaving office, Liu Yan lived in Yangcheng Mountain, focusing on learning and teaching his disciples.
Later, he was recommended as a virtuous and upright person, and was gradually promoted to Nanyang Prefect, Zongzheng, and Taichang.
At that time, Emperor Ling's political education was in decline and there were military rebellions everywhere. Liu Yan believed that the power of the governor was small and he had no ability to stop it, and the people he appointed were incompetent, so the rebellions often increased. So he suggested that the governor should be appointed to control one side and carefully select ministers who hold important positions as shepherds.
Liu Yan secretly sought help from the governor of Jiaozhi to avoid the chaos at that time.
His suggestions were not implemented in time, but Xi Jian, the governor of Yizhou, was disturbing the people with his administration. Rumors spread far and wide, and Zhang Yi, the governor of Bingzhou, and Geng Bi, the governor of Liangzhou, were both killed by bandits, so Liu Yan's proposal was adopted.
Liu Yan was sent to serve as the envoy to supervise the army and lead the shepherd of Yizhou. Huang Wan, the imperial servant, served as the shepherd of Yuzhou, and Zongzheng Liu Yu served as the shepherd of Youzhou. They all served as the shepherd of the state with the salary of their original positions.
The importance of the status of the state pastor begins here.
At this time, Yizhou's thieves and horses also called themselves "Yellow Turbans", gathered thousands of people who were suffering from labor, first killed Mianzhu Ling, attacked Luo County, killed Xi Jian, and then attacked Shu County and Qianwei. Within a month, they captured and destroyed three counties.
Ma Xiang called himself the Son of Heaven and had a tribe of more than 100,000 people. Ma Xiang sent troops to conquer Bajun and killed Tangbu, the prefect of Bajun.
Jia Long, a minister of Yizhou, originally led hundreds of soldiers to garrison in Jianwei, so he gathered the officials and people to attack Ma Xiang and defeated him. Jia Long sent officials and soldiers to meet Liu Yan.
After Liu Yan took office, he appointed Jia Long as the school captain and moved him to Mianzhu.
Liu Yan comforted and sheltered those who escaped and rebelled, and tried his best to implement a policy of tolerance and kindness, but in his heart he planned to rebel.
Zhang Lu, a native of Pei State, had a beautiful mother, and was familiar with the myths of gods and ghosts. He had contacts with Liu Yan's family. Liu Yan appointed Zhang Lu as the governor of the Sima. He and other Sima Zhang Xiu led troops to kill Su Gu, the prefect of Hanzhong, by surprise. They cut off the Xie Valley and killed the envoys who came and went.
Zhang Lu had occupied Hanzhong, so he killed Zhang Xiu and merged his troops.
Liu Yan wanted to achieve his arrogance by establishing strict criminal laws, so he used other things as an excuse to kill more than a dozen powerful people in the state, which made the scholars and the people complain.
In the second year of Chuping, Jianwei governor Ren Qi and Jia Long rebelled together. They were defeated by Liu Yan and all the rebels were killed.
From then on, Liu Yan's spirit gradually became stronger and stronger, and he built the emperor's carriage and more than a thousand baggage vehicles.
summary: Liu Yan, a descendant of King Lu Gong, served as a local official and later as Nanyang Prefect, Zongzheng, and Taichang. During Emperor Ling's reign, rebellions spread due to weak governors. Liu Yan proposed appointing powerful governors to control regions, a suggestion initially ignored but later adopted after several governors were killed. He was sent to lead Yizhou as shepherd. In Yizhou, he faced a rebellion led by Ma Xiang, who claimed to be the Son of Heaven, but it was suppressed by Jia Long. Liu Yan appointed Zhang Lu, who later seized Hanzhong and killed the prefect. Liu Yan grew arrogant, built imperial carriages, and killed powerful locals, causing resentment. After losing two sons in a failed plot, he died of illness. His son Liu Zhang succeeded him but lacked authority, leading to internal strife and rebellion. Liu Zhang eventually surrendered to Liu Bei after a siege, and died later.

translation:
Liu Zhang was able to block the passes, accumulate strength, guard and govern the territory of his ancestors, and could persist as the years changed. However, he hurriedly handed over power and waited to be exiled and ostracized. He was really a so-called sheep in tiger skin. He was scared to death at the sight of a jackal. What a shame!
◆The biography of Yuan Shu, Yuan Shu, courtesy name Gongdao, was born in Ruyang, Runan, and was the son of Sikong Yuan Feng.
When he was young, he was famous for his chivalrous spirit, and he often went hunting with his young master buddies. Later, he changed a lot.
He was recommended as Xiaolian and was transferred to Henan Yin and Huben Zhonglang generals many times.
At that time, Dong Zhuo was preparing to change his position as emperor and appointed Yuan Shu as the post-general.
Yuan Shu was afraid of being involved in Dong Zhuo's troubles and ran to Nanyang.
It happened that Sun Jian, the governor of Changsha, killed Zhang Zi, the governor of Nanyang, and led his troops to obey Yuan Shu.
Liu Biao wrote a letter recommending Yuan Shu to be the governor of Nanyang. Yuan Shu also wrote a letter recommending Sun Jian to be the governor of Yuzhou. Sun Jian was asked to lead the troops in Jingzhou and Yuzhou and defeated Dong Zhuo in Yangren.
Yuan Shu's cousin Yuan Shao took advantage of the fact that Sun Jian had not returned from his crusade against Dong Zhuo and was far away, so he sent his general Zhou Xin to capture Sun Jian's Yuzhou.
Yuan Shu was very angry and beat Zhou Xin away.
Yuan Shao discussed making Liu Yu the emperor, but Yuan Shu liked to indulge and was afraid of making an older person emperor, so he refused to agree on the grounds of public opinion. When they got together, there was a gap between the two.
So the two of them each made friends as foreign aid to influence each other's ideas. Yuan Shu befriended Gongsun Zan, while Yuan Shao allied with Liu Biao.
Most of the heroes attached themselves to Yuan Shao. Yuan Shu got angry and said: "Are these princes not following me, but following my servants?"
He also wrote to Gongsun Zan, saying that Yuan Shao was not born to the Yuan family. Yuan Shao was furious when he found out.
In the third year of Chuping, Yuan Shu sent Sun Jian to attack Liu Biao in Xiangyang, and Sun Jian died in the battle.
Gongsun Zan wanted Liu Bei to conspire with Yuan Shu to force Yuan Shao, but under the joint attack of Yuan Shao and Cao Cao, they were all defeated.
In the fourth year, Ai Shu led his troops into Chenliu and stationed in Fengqiu.
The remaining bandits in Montenegro and the Xiongnu Yu Fuluo and others helped Yuan Shu and fought with Cao Cao in Kuangting, but they were defeated.
Yuan Shu withdrew his troops to defend Yongqiu, then led the remaining troops to Jiujiang, killed Chen Wen, the governor of Yangzhou, and became the governor of Yangzhou himself, also known as Xuzhou Bo.
Li Ji entered Chang'an and wanted to make friends with Yuan Shu as a foreign aid, so he appointed Yuan Shu as the general of the left. During the holiday, he made him the Marquis of Yangzhai.
At first, when Yuan Shu was in Nanyang, there were still hundreds of thousands of households and a population of several million. However, he did not pay attention to regulating the legal system. He relied on plundering to save money, was extravagant and indulgent, and was greedy. The people were disgusted with him.
When Yuan Shu was young, he saw a prophecy book that said that the one who replaced the Han Dynasty would be Dang Tu Gao, which meant that his name matched the prophecy book.
And because the Yuan family came from the state of Chen, they were descendants of Shun. Replacing red virtue with yellow virtue is in line with the order of operation of the five virtues, so he has the idea of ​​​​transgression and rebellion.
When he heard that Sun Jian had obtained the imperial seal, he imprisoned Sun Jian's wife to obtain the imperial seal.
In the winter of the second year of Xingping, the emperor was exiled and was defeated in Caoyang.
Yuan Shu gathered his subordinates and said to them: The current situation in the country is chaotic and chaotic, and the Liu family is weak.
summary: Yuan Shu, son of Sikong Yuan Feng, was known for chivalry but later changed. He fled to Nanyang after Dong Zhuo's coup and allied with Sun Jian. Conflicts arose with his cousin Yuan Shao over leadership. Yuan Shu declared himself emperor in 197 CE, citing prophecies and his family's lineage. His rule was marked by extravagance and cruelty, leading to widespread discontent. After defeats by Cao Cao and Lu Bu, his army weakened, and he died in 199 CE, vomiting blood in despair. His family sought refuge with Sun Ce.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/刘焉袁术吕布列传

translation:
Lu Bu failed in the battle with Li Cui, so he led hundreds of cavalry, tied Dong Zhuo's head to the saddle, escaped from Wuguan, and rushed to Nanyang.
Yuan Shu treated Lu Bu very well, and Lu Bu relied on himself to kill Dong Zhuo. If you are kind to the Yuan family, you will indulge your subordinates in looting.
Yuan Shu had a headache, and Lu Bu felt uneasy, so he left Yuan Shu and went to Hanoi to join Zhang Yang.
At that time, Li Jie and others were very concerned about offering a reward for Lv Bu's capture, and Zhang Yang's generals were all plotting against Lv Bu.
Lu Bu was afraid and said to Zhang Yang: I am from the same hometown as you. If you kill me now, you may not get much credit.
It's better to sacrifice me alive, so that I can gain the title and favor of Li Ji and others.
Zhang Yang thought Lu Bu was right.
Soon, Lu Bu was able to escape and defected to Yuan Shao. Yuan Shao and Lu Bu attacked Zhang Yan in Changshan.
Zhang Yan had more than 10,000 elite soldiers and several thousand cavalry.
Lu Bu often rode a good horse named Red Rabbit that could leap over city walls and fly across trenches. He and his fierce generals Cheng Lian, Wei Yue and dozens of others rode to attack Zhang Yan's military formation. Sometimes they went three or four times a day and came back each time with the enemy's heads chopped off.
After fighting for more than ten days, Zhang Yan's army was finally defeated.
Lu Bu relied on his military exploits and once again asked Yuan Shao to increase his army, but Yuan Shao refused. Most of Lu Bu's generals and soldiers were vicious and brutal, which gave Yuan Shao a headache.
Lu Bu felt uneasy and asked to return to Luoyang.
Yuan Shao agreed to his request and appointed Lu Bu as the Sili Xiaowei in the name of the emperor. He sent warriors to escort Lu Bu and secretly asked him to kill Lu Bu.
Lu Bu suspected that Yuan Shao was plotting against him, so he sent Jin to play the zheng in the camp while he quietly escaped.
When Yuan Shao's troops rushed towards him late at night, Lu Bu had already escaped.
After Yuan Shao found out, he was worried that Lu Bu would be harmful to him, so he sent people to chase Lu Bu with a reward, but none of them dared to approach Lu Bu, so that Lu Bu could surrender to Zhang Yang.
Passing by Chenliu on the way, the prefect Zhang Miao sent someone to meet Lu Bu and treated him well. When they were about to part, the two held each other's arms and vowed to be good friends.
◆Zhang Miao, courtesy name Meng Zhuo, was from Shuping. He was known as a chivalrous person since childhood.
At first he was summoned by the government, and soon he was promoted to the prefect of Chenliu.
During Dong Zhuo's rebellion, Zhang Miao and Cao Cao raised rebels together.
When Yuan Shao became the leader of the alliance and showed a proud look, Zhang Miao rebuked Yuan Shao with his upright morality. Yuan Shao already resented Zhang Miao and learned that he had a close relationship with Lu Bu, so he asked Cao Cao to kill Zhang Miao.
Cao Cao ignored him, but Zhang Miao felt uneasy.
The first year of Xingping. Cao Cao went east to attack Tao Qian and sent general Chen Gong from Wuyang to garrison Cambodia County.
Chen Gong took the opportunity to persuade Zhang Miao: Now the world is divided and heroes are rising at the same time. You have a team of 100,000 people. You are in a place where you can fight on all sides. You can look down on the world with your sword. You can be a hero among people, but you are controlled by others. Isn't it too despicable?
Now the troops in this state are at war, and the land is empty. Lu Bu is a fierce warrior, good at fighting, and brave and invincible. Take him and occupy Yanzhou together, wait and see the situation in the world, and wait for the changes in the current situation. This can last for a lifetime.
Zhang Miao listened to Chen Gong's advice, so he, his younger brother Zhang Chao, Chen Gong and others welcomed Lu Bu and asked him to be the herdsman of Yanzhou and occupy Puyang. All counties and counties of Yanzhou responded.
After Cao Cao found out, he led his army to attack Lu Bu. The two sides fought many times and lasted for more than a hundred days.
At this time, there was a drought, locusts were infested, food was insufficient, and people began to eat people. Lu Bu moved his troops to Shanyang and garrisoned them.
In the second year of Xingping, Cao Cao regained all the cities in Yanzhou and defeated Lu Bu in Juye. Lu Bu fled to Liu Bei.
Zhang Miao went to Yuan Shu's house to ask for help, leaving Zhang Chao with his family and subordinates to garrison Yongqiu.
Cao Cao surrounded Zhang Chao for several months and killed Zhang Chao and the Zhang family.
Zhang Miao was killed by his soldiers before he arrived in Shouchun.
At this time, Liu Bei led Xuzhou Mu and lived in Xiapi, and he and Yuan Shu were confronting each other on the Huaihe River.
Yuan Shu wanted to unite with Lu Bu to attack Liu Bei, so he wrote to Lu Bu, saying: I sent troops to the capital, but failed to kill Dong Zhuo and dismembered him.
The general killed Dong Zhuo and avenged Yuan Shu. This was his first credit.
Once upon a time, Jin Yuanxiu went south to Fengqiu and was defeated by Cao Cao. The general's attack on Cao Cao made my eyes bright and I could see clearly both far and near. This is the second credit.
Since Yuan Shu was born, he has never heard of Liu Bei in the world, but Liu Bei actually sent troops to fight with me.
With the general's power, he was able to defeat Liu Bei. This is the third achievement.
The general has three great contributions to Yuan Shu. Although Yuan Shu has no talent, he is willing to serve you until his death.
summary: Lu Bu, a skilled warrior from Wuyuan, served under Ding Yuan but killed him to join Dong Zhuo. He later killed Dong Zhuo with Wang Yun's persuasion but fled after Li Cui's attack. He allied with various warlords, including Yuan Shu and Liu Bei, but frequently betrayed them. Known for his prowess, he defeated Zhang Yan but alienated allies due to his brutality. He eventually surrendered to Cao Cao after a siege at Xiapi, but was executed along with his generals Chen Gong and Gao Shun. His life was marked by shifting loyalties and ultimate failure.

translation:
Liu Xuan, also known as Shenggong, was the elder brother of Emperor Guangwu.
Because his younger brother was killed, he made friends with guests and prepared to avenge his brother.
The guests broke the law, and Liu Xuan fled to Pinglin to avoid being pursued by the officials.
Officials arrested his father Liu Zizhang.
Liu Xuan pretended to be dead and had his coffin carried back to Chongling. The officials released Liu Zizhang, and Liu Xuan fled.
In the last years of Wang Mang, there was a famine in the south. People went to the wild swamps in groups to dig some water chestnuts to satisfy their hunger, and even robbed each other.
Wang Kuang and Wang Feng from Xinshi often mediate for them and were promoted as leaders, followed by hundreds of people.
So some people who were on the run, such as Ma Wu, Wang Chang, Cheng Dan and others, went to join them to attack Li Xiangju and hid in the green forest mountains. In a few months, the team grew to seven or eight thousand people.
In the second year of Emperor Wang Mang's reign, someone from Jingzhou Mu sent 20,000 "Ben Ming soldiers" to attack them. Wang Kuang and others led their troops to attack them in Yundu. They defeated Jingzhou Mu's army, killed thousands of people, seized all the enemy's military equipment, and then captured Jingling.
They turned to attack Yundu and Anlu, plundered many women, and returned to the Green Forest Mountains. By now there were more than 50,000 people, and the prefectures and counties could no longer control them.
In the third year of the Emperor's reign, a great plague occurred. Nearly half of the people in Green Forest Mountain died, and the teams dispersed.
Wang Chang and Cheng Dan went west to Nanjun and were known as "Xiajiang soldiers"; Wang Kuang, Wang Feng, Ma Wu and their followers Zhu Tun, Zhang Xian and others marched north to Nanyang and were known as "Xinshi soldiers"; the generals all called themselves generals.
In July, Wang Kuang and others attacked Suixian but failed to capture it.
Chen Mu and Liao Zhan from Pinglin gathered more than a thousand people, known as "Pinglin soldiers", to respond to Wang Kuang's troops.
Liu Xuan defected to Chen Mu and others, and served as an Jipu in the army.
At the same time, Emperor Guangwu and his brother Liu Boxheng also raised troops in Chongling and joined forces with various insurrectionary forces to attack.
In the first month of the fourth year of Emperor Di Huang's reign, he defeated the troops commanded by Wang Mang's former officer Zhen Fu and Zhengliang Qiuci, and killed them. Liu Xuan was promoted to General Gengshi.
Although there were many troops in the uprising, there was no unified leadership, so the generals discussed together to make Liu Xuan the emperor.
On the Xinsi day of February, a mandala was set up on the beach of Feishui to gather troops and horses.
Liu Xuan ascended the throne of God and stood facing south to meet the officials.
Liu Xuan has always been a coward, and he was so ashamed that he was sweating profusely. He raised his hands but couldn't even say a word.
After that, a general amnesty was given to the whole country, and Jianyuan was the first year of Gengshi.
All the generals were granted official titles, including his uncle Liu Liang as the third elder of the country, Wang Kuang as the Grand Duke of Dingguo, Wang Feng as the Grand Duke of Chengguo, Zhu Kun as Grand Sima, Liu Bo was promoted to Grand Situ, Chen Mu was promoted to Grand Sikong, and the rest were granted the title of Jiuqing or General.
In May, Liu Boxheng captured Wancheng.
summary: Liu Xuan, also known as Shenggong, was the elder brother of Emperor Guangwu. After his younger brother was killed, he sought revenge but fled to Pinglin when his guests broke the law. He later pretended to be dead to secure his father's release and escaped. During the famine in Wang Mang's last years, Wang Kuang and Wang Feng from Xinshi became leaders of groups foraging for food, and their following grew. Fugitives like Ma Wu joined them, and they attacked Li Xiangju, hiding in the Green Forest Mountains. Their force swelled to seven or eight thousand within months. In the second year of Wang Mang's reign, they defeated Jingzhou Mu's 20,000 troops, seized equipment, captured Jingling, and plundered Yundu and Anlu before returning to the mountains with over 50,000 men, beyond local control. In the third year, a plague killed nearly half of the Green Forest force, causing dispersal. Wang Chang and Cheng Dan went west as "Xiajiang soldiers"; Wang Kuang, Wang Feng, and Ma Wu went north as "Xinshi soldiers." In July, they failed to take Suixian. Chen Mu and Liao Zhan from Pinglin gathered over a thousand "Pinglin soldiers" to support them. Liu Xuan joined Chen Mu as a supply officer. Emperor Guangwu and his brother Liu Boxheng also raised troops in Chongling and allied with the insurgents. In the first month of the fourth year, they defeated Wang Mang's officers, killing them, and Liu Xuan was promoted to General Gengshi. The generals, lacking unified leadership, made Liu Xuan emperor on the Xinsi day of February at Feishui. Liu Xuan, a coward, sweated profusely and could not speak. He granted amnesty, established the first year of Gengshi, and appointed officials, including his uncle Liu Liang, Wang Kuang, Wang Feng, Zhu Kun, Liu Bo, and Chen Mu.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/刘玄刘盆子列传

translation:
In June, Emperor Gengshi entered Wancheng to establish his capital. His fellow clan members and generals all conferred titles to him one by one, and more than 100 people were granted the title of marquis.
Emperor Gengshi was jealous of Liu Boxheng's prestige and reputation, so he killed him and appointed Guanglu Xun and Liu Ci as the chief disciple.
Liu Wang, Marquis of Zhongwu in the former Han Dynasty, also led an uprising and captured Runan.
At this time, Wang Mang's Nayan general Yan You and Zhizong general Chen Mao were defeated miserably in the battle of Kunyang and surrendered to Liu Wang.
In August, Liu Wang established himself as emperor, with Yan You as Grand Sima and Chen Mao as Prime Minister.
Wang Mang sent Grand Master Wang Kuang and General Aizhang to defend Luoyang.
Emperor Gengshi sent Prince Kuang of Dingguo to attack Luoyang, General Shen Tujian of Xiping, and Prime Minister Sizhi Li Song attacked Wuguan. The entire Sanfu area was shaken.
At this time, heroes from all over the country rose up in response, killed the governors of the prefectures and counties, proclaimed themselves generals, adopted the reign name of Gengshi, and waited for the emperor's edict. In less than a month, supporters of Emperor Gengshi spread all over the country.
The rebels in Chang'an City also attacked Weiyang Palace.
In September, the Duke of Donghai killed Wang Mang in Jiantai, confiscated the jade seal and ribbon, and sent Wang Mang's head to Wancheng.
Emperor Gengshi was sitting in the public hall at that time. He took the head and looked at it, and said happily: If Wang Mang had not usurped the power of the Han Dynasty, his merits should be the same as Huo Guang. Mrs. Han, the concubine, smiled and said: If he didn't do this, how could you get this position? Emperor Gengshi was very happy and hung Wang Mang's head in the market of Wancheng.
That month, they captured Luoyang, captured Wang Kuang and Aizhang alive, sent them to Wancheng, and beheaded them all.
In October, he sent Fenwei General Liu Xin to Runan to attack Liu Wang and killed Yan You and Chen Mao.
So Emperor Gengshi went north to make his capital Luoyang and appointed Liu Ci as prime minister.
Shen Tujian and Li Song sent the emperor's vehicles, clothing and utensils from Chang'an, and sent officials from Zhonghuangmen to welcome Gengshi's move to the capital.
In February of the second year of Gengshi, Emperor Gengshi moved west from Luoyang.
Before setting off, Li Song guided the carriages and horses for Emperor Gengshi. The horses were frightened and ran wildly, hitting the iron pillars of the North Palace Gate. All three horses were killed.
When Wang Mang was defeated, only Weiyang Palace was burned down, while the rest of the palace buildings were intact.
There are still thousands of maids left in the harem, and everything from the bells and drums, curtains, carriages, utensils, and clothing to Taicang, arsenals, government offices, streets, and lanes are all the same as in the old days.
After Emperor Gengshi entered the palace, he lived in Changle Palace and met hundreds of officials in the front hall. The ministers and officials in the palace lined up and stood in the courtyard.
Emperor Gengshi was very shy. He lowered his head and scratched the seats with his hands, not daring to look at them.
Several generals were late, and Emperor Gengshi asked them how much they had looted. The officials on the left and right, all old guards in the palace, were surprised and looked at each other. Emperor Gengshi married Zhao Meng's daughter as his wife and doted on her very much, so he entrusted Zhao Meng with the government and drank and had fun with the woman in the back court day and night.
summary: In May, Liu Boxheng captured Wancheng. In June, Emperor Gengshi made it his capital and granted titles to over a hundred clan members and generals. Jealous of Liu Boxheng's prestige, he killed him. Liu Wang, Marquis of Zhongwu, led an uprising and captured Runan. After Wang Mang's generals Yan You and Chen Mao were defeated at Kunyang, they surrendered to Liu Wang, who declared himself emperor in August. Wang Mang sent Wang Kuang and Aizhang to defend Luoyang. Emperor Gengshi sent forces to attack Luoyang and Wuguan, shaking the Sanfu region. Heroes nationwide rose, killed local officials, and adopted Gengshi's reign name, spreading support within a month. Rebels in Chang'an attacked Weiyang Palace. In September, the Duke of Donghai killed Wang Mang and sent his head to Wancheng. Emperor Gengshi, pleased, hung it in the market. That month, Luoyang was captured, and Wang Kuang and Aizhang were beheaded. In October, Liu Xin killed Liu Wang, Yan You, and Chen Mao. Emperor Gengshi moved his capital to Luoyang, appointing Liu Ci as prime minister. In February of the second year, he moved west to Chang'an, but his horses were spooked before departure. After Wang Mang's defeat, only Weiyang Palace was burned; other buildings remained intact. Emperor Gengshi lived in Changle Palace but was shy and incompetent, entrusting government to Zhao Meng and indulging in drink. Zhao Meng became dictatorial, killing a critic. Li Yi and Zhu Kun acted dictatorially in Shandong, while Wang Kuang and Zhang Yan were tyrannical in Sanfu. Appointed officials were lowly, causing public ridicule. Li Shu advised reform but was imprisoned, leading to widespread resentment and betrayal.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/刘玄刘盆子列传

translation:
At the beginning, Fang Wang saw the political chaos in Gengshi and speculated that he would be defeated, so he told Gong Lin and others from Anling: The former Ding'an Duke Liu Ying was a descendant of Emperor Ping. Although Wang Mang usurped the throne, Liu Ying was also the leader of the Han Dynasty.
Now people are saying that the direct descendant of the Liu family should be appointed emperor. Let's come together to build a great cause with him. What do you think? Gong Lin and others agreed. So he found Liu Ying in Chang'an and took him to Linjing to formally establish him as emperor.
Gathering thousands of party members, Fang Wang became Prime Minister and Gong Lin became Grand Sima.
Gengshi sent Li Song and general Su Mao to defeat Fang Wang and others, killing several of them.
He also ordered Su Mao to resist Chimei in Hongnong. Su Mao's army was defeated and more than a thousand people died.
In March, Li Song was sent to join Zhu Tuna and Chimei to fight in Guixiang. Li Song and others were defeated, abandoned the army and fled, with more than 30,000 people killed.
At this time, Wang Kuang and Zhang Xuan were stationed in Hedong. They were defeated by Deng Yu and rushed back to Chang'an.
Zhang discussed with the generals and said: "Red Eyebrow is close to the underworld of Zheng and Hua, and will be here day and night."
Now there is only Chang'an, which is about to be wiped out. It is better to command the army to plunder the property in the city to make a fortune, then attack the places along the way from here, return east to Nanyang, and collect the soldiers of King Wan and others.
If things don't work out, just go into the lake and become a robber again. Shen Tujian, Liao Zhan and others all agreed, so they went together to persuade Gengshi.
Gengshi was furious after hearing this and refused to agree. Zhang Xun and others did not dare to say anything more.
When Chi Mei made Liu Penzi emperor, Gengshi sent Wang Kuang, Chen Mu, Cheng Yue and Zhao Meng to garrison Xinfeng and Li Song to garrison the city to resist them.
Zhang Xian, Liao Zhan, Hu Yin, Shen Tujian and others conspired with the imperial censor Kui Xiao to use force to hijack Gengshi during the Liqiu Festival in order to complete the plan proposed above.
Attendant Liu Nengqing learned of their plot and reported it to Gengshi.
Gengshi pretended to be ill and did not leave the palace, so he summoned Zhang Xuan and others.
Zhang Xuan and others came in, and Gengshi prepared to kill them all, but only Wei Xiao could not reach them.
Gengshi was suspicious and ordered Zhang Xian and four others to wait in the house outside temporarily.
Zhang Xun, Liao Zhan, and Hu Yin suspected that something had happened and rushed out. Only Shentu Jian was there, and Gengshi killed him.
Zhang Xuan, Liao Zhan, and Hu Yin then led their troops to plunder the east and west cities.
When it was dark, they broke into the palace and fought in the palace. Gengshi was defeated.
Early the next morning, he led his wife and more than a hundred chariots and rode eastward to Zhao Meng's place in Xinfeng.
Gengshi also suspected that Wang Kuang, Chen Mu, Cheng Dan and Zhang Xuan were conspiring, so he summoned them at the same time.
Chen Mu and Cheng Dan arrived first and were beheaded immediately.
Wang Kuang could not be frightened and led his army to Chang'an to meet Zhang and others.
Li Song returned to Gengshi and joined forces with Zhao Meng to attack Wang Kuang and Zhang Xuan in the city.
After fighting for more than a month, Wang Kuang and others were defeated and Gengshi moved to Changxin Palace.
When Chimei arrived at Gaoling, Wang Kuang and others surrendered to Chimei, so he and Chimei marched together.
Gengshi defended the city and sent Li Song to fight, but failed and more than two thousand people died. Chimei captured Li Song alive.
summary: In December, the Red Eyebrow Army entered the pass. In the first month of the third year, Fang Wang made Liu Ying emperor. Gengshi sent forces to defeat them but was later defeated by Red Eyebrow. Wang Kuang and Zhang Xuan proposed plundering and retreating east, but Gengshi refused. When Red Eyebrow made Liu Penzi emperor, Gengshi sent generals to resist. Zhang Xuan and others plotted to hijack Gengshi but were discovered. Gengshi killed some conspirators, but Zhang Xuan and others plundered the city and attacked the palace, defeating Gengshi. Gengshi fled to Zhao Meng, suspected Wang Kuang and others, and killed Chen Mu and Cheng Dan. Wang Kuang joined Zhang Xuan. After a month of fighting, Gengshi moved to Changxin Palace. Red Eyebrow arrived, and Wang Kuang surrendered. Gengshi defended the city but was defeated; Li Song was captured. Li Fan opened the city gate, and Red Eyebrow entered in September. Gengshi fled but was captured by Yan Ben. He surrendered to Red Eyebrow in October, was made Marquis of Weiwei, then King of Changsha. He lived with Xie Lu but was strangled on Xie Lu's orders. Guangwu buried him at Ba Ling. Gengshi had three sons, later enfeoffed by Guangwu.

translation:
Fan Chong led more than 100,000 troops and returned to surround Ju County for several months.
Someone said to Chong: Ju is the hometown of our parents, why should we attack it? Fan Chongnai came to the rescue and left.
At this time, Lu's mother died of illness, and her subordinates joined the Red Eyebrow, Qingdu, and Bronze Horse tribes.
The Red Eyebrow Army invaded Donghai County and fought against Wang Mang Dayin of Yiping County. They failed and thousands of people died. Then they left Donghai and plundered Chu, Pei, Runan, and Yingchuan. They returned to Chenliu, captured Lu City, and moved to Puyang.
It happened that Gengshi decided to make his capital Luoyang and sent envoys to persuade Fan Chong to surrender.
When Fan Chong and others heard that the Han Dynasty was revived, they left their troops behind and personally led more than 20 generals to accompany the envoys to Luoyang to surrender and reform. They were all granted the title of marquis.
Fan Chong and others did not have their own fiefdom, and the tribesmen who stayed behind slowly began to rebel. Fan Chong left Luoyang and returned to his barracks. He led his army into Yingchuan County and divided his tribe into two divisions, one with Fan Chong and Pang An, and one with Xu Xuan, Xie Lu, and Yang Yin.
Fan Chong and Pang An captured Changshe County, attacked Wancheng in the south, and beheaded the county magistrate; while Xu Xuan, Xie Lu, and others also captured Yangzhai County and led their troops to Liang County to kill the Henan prefect.
Although the Red Eyebrow tribe had won many battles, they were exhausted and tired of fighting. They cried day and night and wanted to return eastward.
Fan Chong and others discussed and considered that once they returned eastward, the tribe would inevitably disperse, so it was better to attack Chang'an westward.
In the winter of the second year of Gengshi, Fan Chong and Pang An arrived at Wuguan, while Xu Xuan and others advanced from Luhun Pass in two directions.
In the first month of the third year, they all arrived in Hongnong County and won consecutive battles with Gengshi generals, and the army developed greatly.
So ten thousand people were divided into one battalion, and a total of thirty battalions were built. Each battalion had three elders and one person in charge; they entered Huayin.
In the army, Qi witches often played drums and danced to worship King Cheng Yangjing for blessings and peace.
The wizard was talking nonsense, and King Jing was furious and said: When you are the emperor, why should you be a thief? Those who laughed at the witches became ill, and the army was frightened.
At this time, Fang Wang's younger brother Fang Yang resented Gengshi for killing his brother, so he wrote to Fan Chong and others, saying: Gengshi was in chaos and the government's orders were ineffective, which is why the general reached this point.
Now the general has millions of people marching west to the imperial capital Chang'an, but he has no title and is called a group of thieves. This cannot last long.
It is better to establish the Liu clan and carry out executions under the banner of justice.
Who dares to disobey this order? Fan Chong and others thought this was good. Fan Chong advanced to Zheng County and discussed with the generals: Now that our army is approaching Chang'an, and ghosts and gods appear like this, we should ask the Liu clan to jointly establish him as emperor. In June, Liu Penzi was made emperor and named himself the first year of the founding of the world.
At first, Chimei passed through Shixian County and captured Liu Penzi and his two brothers Liu Gong and Liu Mao, all of whom remained in the army.
summary: Liu Penzi, a descendant of Liu Zhang, King of Chengyangjing, was captured by Red Eyebrow. Lu's mother, seeking revenge for her son, gathered followers and killed a county magistrate before returning to the sea. Fan Chong raised troops in Ju, and with others, formed the Red Eyebrow Army, painting their eyebrows red. They defeated Wang Mang's forces and grew to over 100,000. After Lu's mother died, her followers joined Red Eyebrow. They fought across regions, and when Gengshi made Luoyang his capital, Fan Chong and others surrendered but later rebelled. In the winter of the second year, they advanced west to Chang'an. In the first month of the third year, they arrived in Hongnong, winning battles. They divided into thirty battalions. Following a witch's prophecy, they made Liu Penzi emperor in June. Penzi, fifteen, was terrified. Xu Xuan became prime minister, Fan Chong imperial censor, and others held high ranks. They entered Chang'an, and Gengshi surrendered. Penzi lived in Changle Palace, but the generals were disorderly, robbing and killing. Penzi cried daily. Liu Gong taught him to resign, but Fan Chong refused. After more plundering, they left Chang'an westward, suffering heavy losses from snow. They returned, looted tombs, and insulted Empress Lu's body. Deng Yu attacked but was defeated. In September, they returned to Chang'an. After battles with Yancen and others, a great famine struck Sanfu. In December, they returned east, losing many. Guangwu intercepted them, and in the first month of the second year, they surrendered. Guangwu spared them, gave them land in Luoyang, but Fan Chong and Pang An later rebelled and were executed. Liu Penzi became blind and was given land in Xingyang for life.

translation:
◆The biography of Liu Ping, named Gongzi, was from Pengcheng, Chu County.
His real name was Kuang, but it was changed to Ping after he became emperor.
During Wang Mang's time, he became a county official, guarding the Qiu chief, and flourished in politics and religion.
Later, when there were thieves in each county, Liu Ping was sent to guard them. Wherever he went, he was controlled. From then on, every county praised his ability.
During the Gengshi period, the world was in chaos, and Liu Ping's younger brother Liu Zhong was killed by thieves.
Later, the thieves suddenly arrived. Liu Ping supported his mother and ran away.
Liu Zhong's posthumous daughter was only one year old. Liu Ping embraced Zhong's daughter and abandoned his biological son.
The mother wanted to go back to get her son, but Liu Ping refused to listen and said: "I cannot support two children, and the second child cannot have offspring." So he left without caring, and hid in Nozawa with his mother.
Liu Ping went out to look for food in the morning. He met a hungry thief and was about to cook him. Liu Ping kowtowed and said, "I will find some wild vegetables for my mother to satisfy her hunger this morning. My mother is waiting for me to survive. I wish I could go back first. When my mother finishes eating, I will definitely come back and let you kill her."
So the tears continued. The thief saw that he was sincere, sympathized with him and let him go home.
When Liu Ping went back, after his mother finished eating, he said to his mother: "I just made an appointment with a thief, so I can't deceive others."
So he returned to the thief. Everyone was shocked and talked to each other: "I often hear about martyrs, but today I actually saw them."
Just go away, we can't bear to eat you. As a result, Liu Ping's life was saved.
In the early years of Jianwu, General Pang Meng of Pingdi made troops in Pengcheng and defeated the governor of the county, Sun Meng.
Liu Ping was working as a county official at that time. He risked his life by lying on Sun Meng's body and suffered seven stab wounds. He was so trapped that he didn't know what to do, so he cried and begged: "I am willing to replace the king with my body." The thieves gathered their weapons and stopped killing, saying, "This man is a righteous man, don't kill him." So dismissed and walked away.
Sun Meng was seriously injured and died. After a while, he came back to life. He was thirsty and looked for water. Liu Ping took blood from his own wound and gave it to him to drink.
After a few days, Sun Meng finally died, so Liu Ping bandaged the stab wound, helped carry Sun Meng's coffin, and sent it back to the county.
Later, Liu Ping was promoted to Xiaolian and became the Prime Minister of Jiyin County. The prefect Liu Yu attached great importance to him and appointed him to the county position.
When the mourning clothes are full, Quanjiao Chang is awarded.
People are grateful for political favors. Some increase wages or taxes, and some reduce the age and enter the service earlier.
The governor and the prefect came to inspect, but there were no prisoners in the prison. Everyone was in his place, and he didn't know what to ask. He just issued the edict and left.
Later he was dismissed due to illness.
In the early years of Emperor Xianzong's reign, Shangshu Pushe Zhongliyi wrote a letter recommending Liu Ping, Wang Wang of Langfu, and Fu Dao, King of Donglai: I personally saw that Liu Kuang, Wang Wang of Langfu, and Fu Wang of Donglai were both seventy years old.
I don't understand them well enough, I just envy them for promoting talented people. In the memorial, there was an edict to recruit Liu Ping and others, and they were given special money to do the work.
After arriving at the imperial court, they all worshiped him as Yilang and were introduced to him many times. Liu Ping was promoted to minister again, and in the third year of Yongping he was promoted to Zongzheng. He recommended famous scholars such as Chenggong and Xun Xun several times.
After eight years in office, Shangshu asked to retire and go home due to old age and illness, and died at home. ◆Zhao Xiaozhuan, Zhao Xiao was named Changnian and was from Peiguoqi.
His father, Zhao Pu, served as General Tianhe during Wang Mang's reign and appointed Zhao Xiao as Lang.
summary: Biographies of several individuals from the Han dynasty. Liu Ping, originally named Kuang, was from Pengcheng. During Wang Mang's time, he was a county official. During the Gengshi period, when thieves arrived, he fled with his mother, abandoning his own son to save his orphaned niece. He later encountered a hungry thief who wanted to eat him, but Liu Ping begged to feed his mother first and promised to return. The thief, moved by his sincerity, let him go. Liu Ping kept his promise and returned, but the thief spared him. In the early Jianwu years, he risked his life to protect the wounded governor Sun Meng, suffering seven stab wounds and even offering his own blood to the thirsty Sun Meng. Liu Ping was later promoted to Xiaolian and became Prime Minister of Jiyin County. He was later recommended by Zhongliyi and served as Yilang and Zongzheng, recommending famous scholars. He died at home after requesting retirement due to old age and illness.
