translation:
Every time I go home on leave, I often walk in white clothes and carry my own luggage.
I once returned home from Chang'an and wanted to stay overnight at the post office.
The chief of the pavilion first heard that Zhao Xiaohui was passing by and thought that an elderly guest was coming, so he swept the room and waited.
When Zhao Xiao arrived, he did not announce his name. The pavilion chief refused to accommodate him, so he asked: "I heard that the son of General Tian He is coming from Chang'an. When will he arrive?" Zhao Xiao said: It will arrive soon. So he left.
Later, the world was in chaos, and people were eating people.
Zhao Xiao's younger brother Zhao Li was captured by a hungry thief. When Zhao Xiao heard about it, he tied himself up and went to the thief, saying: "Zhao Li has been hungry for a long time and is very thin. He is not as fat as me." The thieves were shocked, so they released them and said to their brothers: "You can go home temporarily and get some food." Zhao Xiao searched for food but failed to find it, so he went back and told the thieves that he was willing to let them cook food.
Everyone found it strange and did not harm him.
The township party admired his loyalty.
When recruiting from prefectures and counties, etiquette must be observed when advancing or retreating.
He was promoted to be filial and honest, so he should not be drafted.
During the Yongping period, he was drafted into the Taiwei Mansion. Xianzong had always heard that Zhao Xiao had good conduct, and issued an edict to grant him the title of admonishing the officials. He was promoted to the rank of Attendant, and then to the rank of Changle Guardsman.
He also called his younger brother Zhao Li to be the censor Zhongcheng.
Zhao Li was also respectful, modest and restrained himself, similar to Zhao Xiao.
The emperor commended their brothers for their virtue and wanted to treat them specially. Zhao Li was ordered to go to Weiwei's Mansion once every ten days, and the eunuch delivered the offerings and told them to have a good time together.
A few years later, Zhao Li died, and the emperor ordered Zhao Xiao to attend the funeral and bury him as an official.
More than a year later, he returned home on leave from the Weiwei. Died at home. ◆ Chunyu Gongzhuan, Chunyu Gong's courtesy name is Meng Sun, Chunyu Ren in Beihai.
He is good at speaking about "Laozi", he is quiet and does not envy fame.
There are fruit trees in the mountains at home. If someone steals the fruit, he will help him harvest it.
He also saw someone stealing seedlings. Chun Yugong was worried that others would be ashamed, so he hid in the grass and waited for the thief to leave before coming out. The villagers were moved.
In Wang Mang's last years, there was famine and war. Chun Yugong's brother Chun Yuchong was about to be cooked by bandits. Chun Yugong asked to be replaced, and both of them were spared from death.
Later, Chunyu Chong died. Chunyu Gong raised his orphans and children, and taught them to learn. If they did not follow the law, he would beat himself with a stick to make the children understand. The children were indeed ashamed and changed their ways. At the beginning, thieves invaded, and the people could not engage in farming. Chunyugong often plowed the fields alone. The villagers tried to dissuade him, saying: The current situation is in great chaos, and life and death are still unknown. Why work in vain and ask for trouble? Chunyu Gong said: Even if I can't gain anything, what loss will it cause to others? Keep on plowing.
summary: Zhao Xiao, named Changnian, was from Peiguo. His father served under Wang Mang. Zhao Xiao was known for his humility, traveling in plain clothes. During a famine, his brother Zhao Li was captured by hungry thieves. Zhao Xiao bound himself and went to the thieves, offering his own fatter body in exchange. The thieves released them. He was later recruited and served as an admonishing official and Changle Guardsman. His brother Zhao Li also became an official. The emperor favored them, but Zhao Li died a few years later. Zhao Xiao died at home after returning from leave. Chunyu Gong, named Meng Sun, was from Beihai. He was a quiet man who studied Laozi. When someone stole his fruit, he helped them harvest it. When he saw a thief stealing seedlings, he hid to avoid shaming him. During a famine, he offered to replace his brother Chunyu Chong who was about to be cooked by bandits, and both were spared. He raised his brother's children, disciplining them by beating himself. He continued to farm despite chaos. He refused multiple calls to serve, living in seclusion for decades. Emperor Suzong eventually summoned him, made him a counselor, and later promoted him. He died in office, and the emperor ordered a stone carving to commend him.

Later, the states and counties called for continuous recruitment, but none of them responded. So he lived in seclusion to cultivate his ambition, hiding in the mountains and rivers.
Every move and every turn of the week must be done according to etiquette.
During the Jianwu period, the county promoted him as a filial and honest person, and Sikong promoted him, but he was not worthy. The guest lived in seclusion in Langfu, Guizhou, and Zou Mountains for several decades.
In the first year of Jianchu's reign, Emperor Suzong issued an edict praising Chunyu Gong for his ordinary conduct, notifying the county to grant him twenty pieces of silk, dispatching a public carriage, and worshiping him as a counselor.
The introduction lasted a whole day, asking him many political questions, and promoted him to the rank of captain of the cavalry in the palace. He was treated with great courtesy.
All the famous people he recommended were recruited by the imperial court.
In the court, he always responded to the political affairs presented by the emperor based on morality. There was not a single conversation between the emperor and him without a good word.
Five years later, he became seriously ill, and the emperor sent people to express condolences. He died in his official position.
The imperial edict was written with praise and praise, and he was given a thousand dendrobium grains and carved stones in the palace to commend him.
His son was given the title of filial piety and the title of Prince Sheren.
◆Jiang Ge's biography, Jiang Ge's courtesy name was Cweng, and he was a native of Linzi, Qi State.
His father died when he was young, and he lived alone with his mother.
When the world was in chaos and thieves broke out, Jiang Ge fled with his mother on his back. He encountered many dangers and often picked wild fruits to survive.
Several times he met thieves, and some wanted to kidnap him. Jiang Ge cried and begged, saying that his mother relied on him to support him. His tone was very sincere and touching.
The thief couldn't bear to invade him, and someone even showed him where to escape, so both mother and son had to survive the disaster safely.
When Jiang Ge arrived in Xiapi, he was so poor that he was barefoot and shirtless. He relied on working to support his mother. He tried his best to provide the necessary things around him.
In the last years of Jianwu, he returned to his hometown with his mother.
At the end of every year, interviews were held in the county. Jiang Ge didn't want to move around because his mother was there, so he pulled the cart by himself in the shaft without using oxen or horses. From then on, the village called him "Jiang Da Duozi".
The prefect once prepared a gift to invite him, but Jiang Ge refused because his mother was old.
After his mother's death, his true nature was about to be extinct. He used to sleep next to the tomb, and when the mourning period expired, he couldn't bear to get rid of her.
The county governor sent a minister to take off his mourning clothes and asked him to become an official.
In the early years of Yongping, Jiang Ge was promoted to Xiaolian and was awarded the title of Taipu of Chu.
After more than a month, he voluntarily abandoned his official position and left.
Chu Wangying sent people to chase him quickly and refused to go back.
He also asked his master to give him gifts, but he refused to accept them.
Later, I went several times in response to Sangong's orders.
In the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Taiwei Mou Rong promoted virtuous and upright people, and Jiang Ge was promoted to Sikong Changshi again.
Suzong treated him with great respect and courtesy, and promoted him to the rank of General of the Five Features.
summary: Jiang Ge, named Cweng, was from Linzi. He fled with his mother on his back during chaos, picking wild fruits to survive. When thieves tried to kidnap him, he cried and begged, saying his mother depended on him, and the thieves spared him. He worked to support his mother in poverty. After returning home, he pulled his mother in a cart himself, earning the nickname "Jiang Da Duozi." He refused official invitations due to his mother's age. After her death, he slept by her tomb. He was later promoted to Xiaolian and served as Taipu of Chu, but abandoned the post. He later served as Sikong Changshi and General of the Five Features. The emperor treated him with great respect. He refused gifts from nobles. He requested retirement and was made an admonishing doctor. The emperor later issued an edict praising his filial piety and ordered the county to give him gifts.

translation:
During every court meeting, the emperor often sent tiger tigers to assist him, and often kept an eye on him when he came to worship.
At this time, Jiang Ge was ill and could not attend court, so the emperor sent an eunuch to bring him wine and food. The favor was very special.
Therefore, Ma Liao, a noble of the capital, and Dou Xian, a lieutenant in the capital, were envious of Jiang Ge's character, and each sent him letters and gifts. Jiang Ge neither replied nor accepted gifts.
The emperor praised him even more.
Later, Jiang Ge wrote a letter requesting to retire and return to his hometown. The imperial court turned him into an admonishing doctor and granted him the title of "Resigning to his hometown." However, Xie fell seriously ill.
During the Yuanhe period, the emperor missed Jiang Ge's good conduct and drafted an edict to Prime Minister Qi: I would like to advise the doctor Jiang Ge. He returned home due to illness. How is his daily life now?
Filial piety is the first of all actions and the beginning of all good deeds.
Whenever the country misses people with lofty ideals, they always think of Jiang Ge.
The county was ordered to use Dendrobium dendrobium as a gift to Juxiao. Every August, officials were sent to express condolences and give him sheep wine until his lifetime.
If something unfortunate happens, use the middle prison to offer sacrifices. From then on, the title of "Ju Xiao" became popular all over the world.
After his death, the imperial edict granted him a thousand dendrobium grains.
◆Liu Banchuan, also known as Liu Banxing, was the great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan.
Emperor Xuan granted his son Liu Xiao to Chu, making him the Xiaowang.
The filial king gave birth to Wang Yan, which gave rise to Wang Yu, and Yu gave rise to commonness.
From Liu Xiao to Liu Ban, they accumulated benevolence and righteousness, and were famous for generations, and Liu Yu was especially kind and kind.
His mother died in his early years, and his brother Hou Ping from Yuanxiang was still young. Liu Yu raised him personally and often slept and ate with him.
When he became a man, he never left his side.
After Liu Ping died of illness, Liu Yu cried and vomited blood and died a few months later.
At first, Liu Yu was granted a title by the king, but when Wang Mang usurped the throne, he was deposed as an ordinary citizen and lived in Pengcheng.
Liu Ban's father died when he was several years old, and he lived alone with his mother.
Wang Mang failed and the world was in chaos. When Tai Fu heard that Emperor Gengshi had ascended the throne, she went to Chang'an with Liu Ban.
When Gengshi failed, he and Liu Ban turned around during the military revolution. They traveled westward to Long and lived in Wuwei.
Although Liu Ban was young, he was determined to cultivate his moral character and never neglected to recite poems and books.
His mother and uncles believed that living in a remote area, where life and death were unpredictable, they should not study hard and meditate like this. They preached to Liu Ban several times, but Liu Ban still did not change his career.
In the eighth year of Jianwu's reign, Kuai Xiao was defeated and Hexi was able to communicate with the mainland. Liu Ban moved his family east to Luoyang and studied Confucian classics under his teacher.
In the second year, Emperor Guangwu issued an edict, conferring Liu Ban the title of Qiuhou, enshrining him as King Xiao, and sending him to the capital.
Later, because the country belonged to the King of Chu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Zhu Qiu.
summary: Liu Ban was the great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan. His father Liu Yu raised his younger brother Liu Ping after their mother died, and died of grief after Liu Ping's death. Liu Ban lived with his mother during Wang Mang's failure. He studied diligently despite his family's concerns. In the eighth year of Jianwu, he moved to Luoyang to study. He was later enfeoffed as a marquis. The emperor commended him for his good conduct. He served as Jinwu and captain of the cavalry school. He advised against establishing the Changpingcang, arguing it would harm the people. He also argued against a ban on farmers engaging in fishing and hunting, and against officials inflating land cultivation figures. He died at age sixty.

translation:
◆In the biography of Zhou Pan, Zhou Pan's courtesy name was Jianbo, and he was an adult in Runan. A member of the same tribe as the conqueror Zhou Xie.
His grandfather Zhou Ye was the prefect of Tianshui in the early years of Jianwu.
Zhou Pan traveled to the capital when he was young and studied "Guwen Shangshu", "Five Elements of Hong Fan" and "Zuo Shi Zhuan". He liked to talk about etiquette and had good conduct. He would not speak anything that was not in line with the classics. Most Confucian students regarded him as their master.
The family was poor, and it was not enough to support his mother.
I once recited "Poetry" to the last chapter of "Ru Tomb", which was very generous and lamentable, so I dismissed Wei Dai and participated in the recommendation of Xiaolian.
In the early years of Emperor He's reign, he paid homage to him, was appointed city mayor, and was promoted to magistrate of Yangcheng and Chonghe counties. He experienced good political achievements in the three cities. Later, he missed his mother and abandoned his official position and returned to his hometown.
When his mother died, her body was almost destroyed by grief, and her mourning period expired, so she took up residence next to the grave.
The professor often has thousands of disciples.
The government called Zhou Pan three times, and they all thought Zhou Pan was a virtuous man and invited him to come out. Zhou Pan said to his friends: In the past, Fang Hui and Zhifu rejected Yao and Shun and rested their minds at home, not disturbing their health care for glory and profit.
My mother is dead, why do I need foreign objects? So he didn't apply.
In the first year of Jianguang, he was seventy-three years old. Every New Year's Day, the court gathered all the students and gave lectures all day long. So he said to his two sons: The day before yesterday, I dreamed that my master, Mr. Dongli, was talking to me in the underworld. Then he sighed and said: Is my age already over?
If the tomb coffin is large enough to contain the body at the end of life, the outer coffin can be used to hold the inner coffin. Wrap it in clothes and hang it directly into the tomb. Use washed clothes and a scarf. Weave a two-foot-four-inch long bamboo slip and copy an article from "Yao Canon", together with a knife and pen, and place them in front of the coffin to show that you have not forgotten the holy way.
On the 15th of this month, he died without illness. Scholars believe that he was a man who understood destiny.
◆Zhao Zichuan, named Wenchu, was from Yan in Dongjun.
His father, Zhao Chang, has a doctorate.
Zhao Zi's father died when he was young. He behaved filially and was recommended by the prefectures and counties as filial and honest, but he refused.
In the first year of Yanxi's reign, Chen Qi, the chief minister, recommended Zhao Zi, saying that he was extremely filial and moral, so he was promoted to a doctorate.
In the early years of Emperor Ling's reign, Taifu Chen Fan and General Dou Wu were killed by eunuchs, so Zhao Zi resigned due to illness.
Taiwei Yang Ci specially invited him and asked him to use a scarf as jewelry and not add a crown to go in and give lectures to everyone.
Later, he was promoted to high rank and became the governor of Dunhuang several times.
Later, he was dismissed from his post due to illness and returned home, where he personally led his children and grandchildren to make a living in the fields.
One time, robbers came to his house at night to rob him. Zhao Zi was afraid of disturbing his mother, so he went to the door to greet the robbers. The robbers asked him to prepare meals. He declined and said, "My mother is eighty years old. She is sick and needs treatment. The family is very poor and has no food for shelter. Please leave some clothes and food." Apart from his wife, he had nothing. The robbers felt ashamed and sighed, knelt down and said goodbye: "We are too rude and should not intrude on the wise man."
After saying that, they all ran away.
Zhao Zi chased them out to give them something, but failed to catch up.
It became even more famous from then on. The imperial court summoned Yi Lang to pay homage to him, but he was unable to do so. He issued an imperial edict and reprimanded him, and the prefectures and counties greeted him with courtesy. He went back and forth several times before going to answer the call as a last resort.
He also worshiped Zhao Zi as the Prime Minister of the East China Sea.
When he was going to take office, he passed by Xingyang. The county magistrate Dunhuang Cao Fan and Zhao Zi's old Xiaolian were waiting for him on the roadside. So he dropped his seal and ribbon and pursued him to the East China Sea.
After meeting Zhao Zi, he resigned and returned home.
This is how he was valued by people at that time.
When Zhao Zi was an official, he was honest and simple. He paid his salary according to his time. The powerful party was afraid of his frugality.
After serving as an official for three years, he asked to be dismissed due to illness and was appointed as Yilang.
He arrived in the capital while ill, and when he was about to die, he sued his former officials Zhu Zhi, Xiao Jian and others, asking them to use a thin plain coffin and pad it with loess, hoping that the body would decay quickly and return to the earth as soon as possible, and not let his descendants change their plans.
So he wrote a suicide note to his son Zhao Yin and said: "Human beings are alive and must die. This is the decree of heaven and earth, and it is the natural end."
summary: Zhou Pan, named Jianbo, was from Runan. He studied classics and was known for his good conduct. He left his official post to return home when he missed his mother. After his mother died, he lived next to her grave and taught thousands of disciples. He refused multiple government calls, saying he had no need for external things after his mother's death. At age seventy-three, he predicted his death, gave his sons instructions for a simple burial with a copy of the "Yao Canon," and died without illness. Zhao Zi, named Wenchu, was from Dongjun. He was known for his filial piety. When robbers came to his house, he asked them to leave some food for his sick mother. The robbers, ashamed, left. He was later summoned to be an official and became Prime Minister of the East China Sea. He was known for his frugality. Before his death, he instructed his son to use a simple, thin coffin to allow his body to decay quickly and return to the earth. He wrote a long suicide note criticizing lavish burials and advocating for simplicity, citing ancient examples. His son followed his instructions.

translation:
At first, Zhuomao went to the county and ignored the government orders. The officials laughed at him, and those in neighboring cities despised him for his incompetence.
Henan County appointed a guardian for this purpose. Zhuomao did not mind this matter and still handled government affairs as before.
A few years later, enlightenment was widespread, and no relics were picked up along the way.
During the reign of Emperor Ping, a great locust plague broke out all over the country. More than 20 counties in Henan Province were affected by the locust plague, except that it did not enter the county boundaries of Mi County.
The postal supervisor reported it, but the prefect didn't believe it. He went to the county to investigate in person and was convinced only after seeing the true situation.
At this time, Wang Mang was in charge of the government and appointed six ministers of agriculture and agriculture to guide and assess farmers and mulberry trees. He moved Zhuomao to be the minister of the capital. The people of Mi County, old and young, cried to see each other off.
When Wang Mang was living in the country, he was exempted from returning to the county because of his illness. He often offered wine to his disciples and refused to serve as an official.
Gengshi was established, and Zhuomao was appointed as his attendant to offer wine. He followed him to Chang'an. Knowing that Gengshi was in political turmoil, he asked to resign and return home because of his old age.
At this time, when Guangwu came to the throne, he first went to visit Zhuomao, and Zhuomao went to Heyang to see him.
Guangwu issued an edict saying: Zhuomao, the former magistrate of Mi County, restrained and cultivated himself, was honest and steady in his duties, and could do things that others could not do.
At first, Zhuomao and his six comrades, Kong Xiu from the same county, Cai Xun from Chenliu, Liu Xuan from Anzhong, Gong Sheng from Chu, and Bao Xuan from Shangdang, did not serve in the reign of Wang Mang, but were famous at that time.
Kong Xiu, whose courtesy name was Ziquan, was the county magistrate of Xindu in the early days of Emperor Ai.
Later, when Wang Mang assumed power, Kong Xiu resigned from office and returned home.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he sent an envoy with Xuan Jinxun and silk to ask him to be the national advisor. Kong Xiu vomited blood and blamed his illness, and Du Men committed suicide.
When Guangwu came to the throne, he asked the descendants of Kong Xiu and Cai Xun to give him grain to show his power.
Liu Xuan, courtesy name Zigao, was a cousin of Anzhonghou Liu Chong. Knowing that Wang Mang would usurp the throne, he changed his name and hid in the mountains holding scriptures.
When Jianwu first came out of the mountain, Guangwu attacked Liu Xuan and granted him the title of Marquis of An.
Gong Ci, Gong Sheng's son, was promoted to be the prefect of Shanggu. The historian commented: At the beginning of the founding of the military, the heroes were quarreling, shouting and shouting, and those who defended themselves in the city looked at each other. This was the time when there were too many things to do.
Zhuomao, a small county magistrate with no other extraordinary talents and over seventy years old, was able to be appointed as the first to be appointed and receive great gifts and words. How is this different from King Wu of Zhou who appointed Bigan to watch Shang Rong and King Zhao of Yan to serve as Guo Wei's tutor in building a palace?
Therefore, many guests who harbored righteous indignation and hoped to return to the right path crossed the dangerous mountains and abandoned their clans in order to exclude the Jinmen embroidered households.
Being kind and lenient is closer to benevolence, and not repaying someone for committing a crime is closer to forgiveness. If you can do this, will anyone still be resentful?
summary: **Zhuomao Biography:** Zhuomao, a native of Wan in Nanyang County, studied in Chang'an under Dr. Jiang Weng, mastering the "Poetry," "Li," and Calendar, and was called a Tongru for exhausting his teacher's scholarship. He was tolerant and respectful. Once, a man mistakenly claimed Zhuomao's horse as his own; Zhuomao gave it to him without dispute. When the man later found his own horse, he returned Zhuomao's horse with apologies. As magistrate of Mi County, Zhuomao governed diligently, treating the people as his sons. When a man admitted to giving gifts to a pavilion chief, Zhuomao explained that such exchanges were part of human relationships, not illegal coercion, and the people accepted his teachings. During a locust plague under Emperor Ping, locusts did not enter Mi County, a fact confirmed by the prefect. Under Wang Mang, Zhuomao was appointed minister of the capital but later resigned due to illness. When Gengshi was established, Zhuomao served briefly but resigned, knowing the political turmoil. Guangwu later visited him, praising his integrity. Zhuomao and six comrades, including Kong Xiu and Liu Xuan, refused to serve Wang Mang. Kong Xiu committed suicide when Wang Mang usurped the throne. Liu Xuan hid in the mountains until Jianwu. The historian noted that Zhuomao, a small county magistrate over seventy, was honored by Guangwu, akin to ancient kings honoring virtuous men.

translation:
Lu Gong's biography, Lu Gong's courtesy name was Zhongkang, and he was a native of Pingling, Fufeng.
His ancestors came from Lu Qinggong, who was destroyed by Chu and moved to Xiayi, so he took Lu as his clan surname.
Generations are worth two thousand stones. During the Aiping years, they migrated from Lu.
During the reign of Wang Mang, his grandfather Lu Kuang was an official in charge of the four seasons. He had great authority and was known as the "think tank".
His father, Lu, was the prefect of Wuling in the early days of Jianwu, and he died in the official position.
At that time, Lu Gong was only twelve years old and his younger brother Lu Pi was only seven years old. The two brothers were crying and jumping day and night. They did not accept the funeral gifts from the county, so they went home to mourn. The etiquette was even more considerate than that of adults. The villagers were deeply surprised.
At the age of fifteen, he, his mother and his younger brother Lu Pi all lived in Taixue, where they studied "Lu Shi", lectured and recited it behind closed doors, and ignored external affairs. Both brothers were praised by the Confucian scholars, and the bachelors rushed to join them.
Taiwei Zhao admired his ambition and sent his son to ask if there was a shortage of wine or food during every year and festival, but he refused.
Lu Gong felt sorry for Lu Pi because he was young and wanted him to achieve his fame first. He pretended that he was ill and would not serve as an official.
The county invited him several times with courtesy, but Lu Gong thanked him and refused to respond. His mother forced him to send him out. Lu Gong had no choice but to go west, because he stayed in Xinfeng as a professor.
In the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Lu Pi was promoted to Fangzheng, and Lu Gong began to serve as a county official.
Taifu Zhao heard the news and called him out to serve.
Suzong gathered many Confucian scholars at Baihu Temple, and Lu Gongte summoned him with the Ming Sutra to participate in the discussion.
Zhao also recommended Lu Gong outspokenly and waited for the imperial edict to be sent to the public carriage to pay homage to Mou Ling.
Lu Gong specialized in moral transformation and did not regard punishment. The litigants Xu Bo and others were fighting for land, and successive orders could not be settled. Lu Gong commented on the merits of the case for them, but in the end they all retreated and blamed themselves, and stopped farming to give up the land to each other.
The director of the pavilion borrowed someone else's cow and refused to return it, so the owner of the cow sued Lu Gong.
He respectfully summoned the chief of the pavilion and ordered him to return the cow to its owner. He urged him repeatedly, but he still refused to return the cow.
Lu Gong sighed and said, "This is a teaching that doesn't work."
Prepare to resign and leave.
The ministers cried and tried to persuade each other to stay. The chief of the pavilion felt deeply regretful and returned the cow.
So the officials and the people were convinced.
In the seventh year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, borers were infested in the county and the crops were damaged. The boundaries of the counties were intertwined, but the borers could not enter the middle.
Henan Yin Yuan'an heard that the suspicion was not true, so he sent Renshu and his relatives to investigate.
Lu Gong followed him as he walked among the streets and sat under a mulberry tree. A pheasant flew by and stopped nearby. There happened to be a child next to him. The fat relative said to the child: "Why don't you catch the pheasant?"
Tong'er said: This pheasant is hatching chicks.
The fat relative stood up in alarm and said goodbye to Lu Gong: "I came here to inspect your political performance."
summary: **Lu Gong Biography:** Lu Gong, from Pingling, Fufeng, was orphaned at twelve. He and his younger brother Lu Pi mourned their father with exceptional propriety. They studied "Lu Shi" at Taixue, ignoring external affairs. Lu Gong let his brother achieve fame first, feigning illness to avoid office. He later served as a county official and was summoned by Suzong to discuss at Baihu Temple. As magistrate of Zhongmu, he focused on moral transformation, not punishment. When a pavilion chief refused to return a borrowed cow, Lu Gong prepared to resign, prompting the chief to return it. During a borer infestation, pests did not enter Zhongmu, and a child showed benevolence by not catching a pheasant hatching chicks. Lu Gong later became imperial censor and admonished Emperor He against attacking the Xiongnu, citing poor harvests, empty granaries, and the need for mourning. He argued that virtue conquers, not force, and warned of disaster. The emperor ignored him. Lu Gong later served as a doctor of "Lu Shi" and as a servant, speaking frankly. He became Situ but was dismissed due to a clan brother's affairs. He later served as Changle Guard and again as Situ. He remonstrated against harsh punishments in summer, advocating for seasonal justice. He died at eighty-one, known for his humble nature and reliance on classics.

translation:
The "Moon Order" was formulated by the Zhou Dynasty, and it was based on the time of the Xia Dynasty. The only changes were the Zhengshuo, clothing colors, and the livestock, emblems, and instruments used in sacrifices.
Therefore: Yin Yin copied Xia Li, Zhou Yin copied Yin Li, and the gains and losses of additions and deletions can be known.
The Book of Changes says: It symbolizes the lurking dragon, so it is better not to use it.
It means that the Yang Qi is hidden in November and December, making it inconvenient to use.
Although the gentle wind blows and warms all things and maintains the roots, there is still a lot of yin above, the ground is frozen and the water is frozen, and the yang energy is blocked and closed for the winter.
Therefore, it is said: If you walk on the frosty ground, you will know that the season of solid ice is coming, and the Yin Qi will begin to condense. If it goes down, it will naturally condense into solid ice.
It means that it starts to be slightly overcast in May and solid ice forms in November.
What the king does is based on the seasons.
Emperor Xiaozhang thought deeply about the ways of the ancients, and formulated laws and regulations to help his son Chou Yin's weak Yang Qi, hoping to be in harmony with the seasons in order to follow the heart of heaven and obey the fate of things.
However, judging from the reality since the reform, the years are not rich, the price of grain is very high, and people are uneasy.
If the county officials do not agree with the state, they will execute prisoners who have committed capital crimes in November. They will kill them without asking the merits. Even if the circumstances of some cases are suspicious, they will not be reviewed and corrected.
If one person complains about injustice, then the king's rule is wrong. What if many people are like this?
"Yi" November: A gentleman should review and suspend the death penalty for suspects.
Doubtful criminals can be ordered to follow this method in detail, and the death penalty subjects will not be terminated until the end of the winter month.
When the beginning of spring is in mid-December, you don’t need to file a petition for a report and still do it as before.
It was later implemented.
Lu Gong held the position of public minister, selected and appointed senior officials, and appointed dozens of ministers and county guards.
However, some elders with the same surname may be resentful because they were not recommended for promotion.
After Lu Gong heard this, he said: "The lack of learning is my worry."
Don’t all the students have their own villages to recommend them to?
So the complainer has nothing to say. Lu Gong had a humble nature and based his opinions on the classics. Although he benefited a lot, he never showed himself, so he was not known for his uprightness. After three years, he stopped writing due to old illness and illness. Six years later, at the age of eighty-one, he died at home.
◆In the biography of Wei Ba, Wei Ba's courtesy name is Qiao Qing, a native of Jiyinjuyang.
There is etiquette from generation to generation.
Wei Ba had been bereaved since childhood, and his brothers lived together. The state admired the harmony between their brothers.
In the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China, he was promoted to Xiaolian and moved eight times. By the time of Emperor He, he was the prefect of Julu.
Live by simplicity and forgiveness.
When a governor makes a mistake, Wei Ba first criticizes his mistakes, and only removes those who do not correct them.
summary: **Wei Ba Biography:** Wei Ba, from Jiyinjuyang, was known for family etiquette. He lived with his brothers harmoniously. As prefect of Julu, he governed with simplicity and forgiveness, praising officials' merits and ignoring shortcomings, which curbed false accusations. He oversaw construction of Shunling under Emperor He, comforting officials despite harsh palace envoys. He later served as Taichang and Guanglu doctor, dying in office.

translation:
Officials sometimes denounced each other's complaints, but Wei Ba always praised the merits of the officials and never mentioned their shortcomings. As a result, those who denounced each other felt ashamed, and the trend of bad words and false accusations subsided.
In the 16th year of Yongyuan, he was worshiped as an official in charge of building palaces.
In the second year, Emperor He died, and Wei Ba took charge of the construction of Shunling.
It was a severe winter and the envoys sent by the palace were very strict in urging and punished the county officials several times to encourage Wei Ba.
Wei Ba only comforted them and did not blame the people below him. He also comforted them and said: It is my master craftsman's fault that you are being insulted now.
The officials were grateful and tried their best to speed up the progress of the project.
In the first year of Yanping, Dai Yinqin was appointed Taichang.
In the second year, he resigned due to illness and became Doctor Guanglu.
In the fifth year of Yongchu, he worshiped Changle Weiwei, begged for his illness, and became Guanglu doctor again. He died in the official position.
◆Biography of Liu Kuan Liu Kuan, courtesy name Wenrao, was a native of Hongnong and Huayin.
His father, Liu Qi, was a Situ during the reign of Emperor Shun.
Liu Kuan once went out and someone lost his cow. He found a cow in Liu Kuan's car and said it was his.
Liu Kuan made no excuse and got out of the car and walked home.
Soon, the man who recognized the cow found his lost cow and returned it to Liu Kuan. He kowtowed and apologized, saying: "I am ashamed of my elders, and I am willing to accept your punishment for me."
Liu Kuan said: Things are similar, and mistakes are allowed. Please send it back. How can I thank you?
The people in the state admired his magnanimous and non-confrontational spirit.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, General Liang Ji conquered him and was promoted to Situ Changshi five times.
At that time, there was an earthquake in the capital, so he was specially interviewed and asked.
He moved again and left the capital to become the prime minister of Liu Zhen, King of the East China Sea.
In the eighth year of Yanxi's reign, he was worshiped as Shangshu Ling and moved to Nanyang to be the prefect.
In charge of the three counties, he was gentle, benevolent and forgiving. Although he was in a hurry and urgent, he was not quick to express his anger.
It is often thought that punishments are used to govern the people. Although the people do not commit punishments, they will inevitably behave shamelessly.
When officials and common people have offenses, they only use a few whips with grass whips to show insult, without causing any pain to the flesh.
Wherever there is merit, it is attributed to the following.
When disaster occurs, take responsibility yourself.
Every time he stopped at the Tingchuan Inn in the county, he would be greeted by academic officials offering wine and virgins holding scriptures in their hands to talk to each other.
When you see your elders, you comfort them with words from the farm; when you see young people, you encourage them with the words of filial piety and brotherhood.
People are motivated to practice virtue when they feel it, and education is becoming more and more popular.
At the beginning of Emperor Ling's reign, he was worshiped as Taizhong doctor and served as lecturer in Huaguang Palace.
When he moved to serve as a servant, he was given a set of clothes.
He was transferred to Tunqi Xiaowei, moved to Zongzheng, and transferred to Guangluxun.
In the fifth year of Xiping's reign, Xu Xun was appointed Taiwei.
summary: **Liu Kuan Biography:** Liu Kuan, from Huayin, was known for his magnanimity. When a man mistakenly claimed his cow, Liu Kuan gave it without argument; the man later returned it with apologies. As Nanyang prefect, he governed with gentleness, using only light whips for punishment and attributing merit to others. He taught filial piety and brotherhood, inspiring virtue. Under Emperor Ling, he served as Taiwei and lecturer. Once drunk at court, he claimed worry, not drunkenness. He disliked bathing, and when a maid spilled soup on him, he asked if she was hurt. He was called an elder. He died at sixty-six, with his son Liu Song succeeding him.

translation:
The southern Xiongnu Kuluo corpse chased Qian Chanyu, whose name was Bi. He was the grandson of Huhanxie Chanyu and the son of Wuzhu Liuruo Qian Chanyu.
After Huhanxie, his sons served as Chanyu in order. When Bi's youngest uncle Xiaochanyuyu was appointed, Bi was appointed as the stone king of Tatar and commanded the southern border and Wuhuan.
In the early years of Jianwu, Peng Chong rebelled in Yuyang. Chanyu joined forces with Peng Chong, and then he had the power to make Lu Fang the emperor and asked him to live in Wuyuan. In the early years of Guangwu, he was busy pacifying the Central Plains and had no time to deal with overseas affairs.
In the sixth year of Jianwu, Liu Sa, the Marquis of Guide, was ordered to send envoys to the Huns. The Huns also sent envoys to pay tribute. The Han Dynasty sent Zhonglang General Han Tong to pay a return visit to the Huns and presented them with gold coins to continue their former friendship.
However, the Shanyu was arrogant, compared himself to Maodun, and spoke arrogantly and arrogantly to the Han envoys. However, the emperor still treated the Xiongnu as usual.
At first, envoys from both sides had frequent exchanges, but the Huns, together with Lu Fang, invaded the northern border many times.
In the ninth year, the emperor sent Grand Sima Wu Mo and others to attack the Xiongnu. It lasted for a year without any achievements. Instead, the Xiongnu became more powerful, and their looting and cruelty increased day by day.
In the thirteenth year, the Xiongnu invaded Hedong, and the prefectures and counties were unable to stop it.
So the population on the borders of Youzhou and Bingzhou was gradually moved to Changshan Pass and Juyong Pass, but the left side of the Xiongnu then moved into the fortress.
The imperial court was very worried about this, so it added thousands of soldiers to each county in the border area, built a large number of sentry boxes and set up beacons for monitoring the enemy's situation.
The Xiongnu heard that the Han had offered a reward for Lu Fang's capture and were eager to obtain property and cloth, so they sent Lu Fang back to surrender in the hope of receiving a reward.
However, Lu Fang only claimed the credit for his return and did not say that he was sent by the Huns. Shanyu was too ashamed to reveal his plan, so the court did not reward the Huns.
Therefore, the Xiongnu was very angry. Within twenty years, the Xiongnu invaded and invaded Shangdang, Fufeng, and Tianshui.
In the winter of the 21st year, the Xiongnu invaded Shanggu and Zhongshan again. They killed and plundered a large number of people and looted many things. There was no longer peace in the northern border.
At the beginning, Shanyu's younger brother Shiguli King Yitu knew that the dental master should be King Zuoxian in order.
King Zuo Xian was Shanyu's successor.
Chanyu wanted to pass the throne to his son, so he killed Zhiya Master.
The dentist is Wang Zhaojun's son. Zhaojun, whose courtesy name is Qiang, is from Nanjun.
During the reign of Emperor Yuan, Zhaojun was selected into the harem as a woman from a good family.
At that time, Hu Hanxie came to court, and the emperor ordered five palace maids to be given to Hu Hanxie.
Zhaojun had been in the palace for several years, but he was not favored by the emperor. He was filled with grief and anger, so he requested to go to the Huns through the Yeting Order.
When Hu Hanxie was leaving, the court held a grand gathering, and the emperor summoned five maids to show Hu Hanxie.
Zhaojun was beautiful and well-dressed, and her beauty shone throughout the palace. Zhaojun wandered around, alarming everyone around the emperor.
The emperor was shocked when he saw it, and wanted to keep Zhaojun, but he could not break his promise, so he had to give Zhaojun to the Xiongnu.
Zhaojun had two sons.
After Hu Hanxie died, the son of the previous Pi clan succeeded to the throne and wanted to marry Zhaojun. Zhaojun wrote to the court asking for his return. Emperor Cheng asked Zhaojun to obey the customs of the Hu people, so Zhaojun became the Hou Shanyu Ban clan.
summary: The southern Xiongnu Kuluo corpse pursued Qian Chanyu, named Bi, grandson of Huhanxie Chanyu and son of Wuzhu Liuruo Qian Chanyu. After Huhanxie, his sons served as Chanyu in order. Bi was appointed as the stone king of Tatar, commanding the southern border and Wuhuan. In the early years of Jianwu, Peng Chong rebelled in Yuyang, and Chanyu allied with him, later making Lu Fang emperor in Wuyuan. Guangwu was busy pacifying the Central Plains and had no time for overseas affairs. In the sixth year of Jianwu, envoys were exchanged between Han and Xiongnu, but the Shanyu was arrogant, comparing himself to Maodun. Despite this, the emperor treated the Xiongnu as usual. However, the Xiongnu, together with Lu Fang, invaded the northern border many times. In the ninth year, an attack by Grand Sima Wu Mo failed, and the Xiongnu grew more powerful. By the thirteenth year, they invaded Hedong, and the border population was moved to Changshan Pass and Juyong Pass. The court added soldiers, built sentry boxes, and set up beacons. The Xiongnu, hearing of a reward for Lu Fang, sent him back to surrender, but Lu Fang claimed credit, and the court did not reward the Xiongnu, angering them. Over the next twenty years, the Xiongnu invaded Shangdang, Fufeng, and Tianshui. In the winter of the 21st year, they invaded Shanggu and Zhongshan, killing and plundering, ending peace in the northern border.

translation:
When Bi saw Zhiya Master being killed, he complained: According to the order of brothers, King Yougu Li should succeed to the throne; according to the identity of a son, I am the eldest son of the predecessor Shanyu, so I should succeed.
Therefore, he was filled with suspicion and fear, and rarely attended gatherings in the royal court.
The Chanyu became suspicious of him and sent two Guduhou to monitor Bi's army.
In the twenty-second year, Shanyu Yu died, and Yu's son Zuoxian Wang Wuda Qianhou became the Shanyu.
Wu Daqianhou died again, and his younger brother Zuoxian Wang Punu was established as Chanyu.
Bi failed to become a chanyu and was already filled with resentment.
Moreover, there have been droughts and locusts in the Xiongnu country for several consecutive years. Thousands of miles of land have become bare, all vegetation has died, and the population and livestock have no food to eat. Coupled with the plague, people! More than half were killed and attrited.
The Chanyu was afraid that the Han would take advantage of his weakness, so he sent an envoy to Yuyang to request peace.
So the imperial court sent Li Mao, the lieutenant general, to pay a return visit to the Huns.
Danbi secretly sent Han Guo Heng to take the Xiongnu map, and in the 23rd year of Jianwu, he went to the prefect of Xihe to demand submission to the Han.
The two Guduhous gradually became aware of Bi's intention, and they happened to hold a sacrifice in Longcheng in May, so they reported to Shanyu that King Dian Tarri Zhu had always wanted to do something unfavorable to Shanyu, and if he was not killed, the country would be in trouble.
At this time, Bi's younger brother gradually came to Shanyu's side. After hearing this, he immediately reported to Bi.
Bi was very frightened, so he gathered eight troops from the southern border under his control, numbering 40 to 50,000 people, and planned to wait for the two Gudu Hous to return and kill them.
When Guduhou was about to arrive, he discovered Bi's plan and fled on horseback alone, reporting the situation to Shanyu.
Shan Yu sent ten thousand cavalry to attack Bi. Seeing that Bi was outnumbered, he retreated without daring to advance.
In the spring of the 24th year of Jianwu, the eight ministers discussed together to establish Bi as Huhanxie Chanyu. Since Bi's grandfather once surrendered to the Han Dynasty and gained peace, they planned to use the name of Huhanxie Chanyu.
So Bi came to Wuyuan Fortress and expressed his willingness to be a barrier for the Han to resist the enemies in the north.
The emperor accepted the opinion of Geng Guo, the general of the Fifth Palace, and agreed.
In the winter of that year, Bi Zi established himself as Hu Hanxie Chanyu.
In the spring of the 25th year, Shanyu sent his younger brother Zuoxian Wang Mo to lead more than 10,000 troops to attack Beidan Shanyu's younger brother Zuoxian King Dianta, and captured Zuoxian King Dianta alive. He also defeated Beidan's army, merged more than 10,000 people from Beidan's tribe, and obtained 7,000 horses and 10,000 cattle and sheep.
Bei Shanyu was frightened and retreated a thousand miles.
At first, the emperor built chariots that could be driven by a few oxen. They built a watchtower on the chariot and placed it on the fortress to resist the Huns.
At that time, people who saw the chariot talked among themselves and said: The prophecy said that in the ninth generation of the Han Dynasty, Beidi would be retreated thousands of miles. Is this what it was talking about?
summary: Initially, Shanyu's younger brother Shiguli King Yitu knew he should be King Zuoxian, the successor. But Chanyu wanted to pass the throne to his son, so he killed Zhiya Master, Zhaojun's son. Zhaojun, from Nanjun, was given to Huhanxie during Emperor Yuan's reign. After Huhanxie died, Zhaojun married his successor according to Hu customs. Bi, seeing Zhiya Master killed, complained about the succession order, becoming suspicious and rarely attending court gatherings. The Chanyu sent two Guduhou to monitor Bi. In the 22nd year, Shanyu Yu died, and his son Wu Daqianhou became Shanyu, followed by his brother Punu. Bi, resentful at not becoming Chanyu, and with droughts and locusts devastating the Xiongnu, causing mass death, the Chanyu feared Han attack and sought peace. Bi secretly sent Han Guo Heng to demand submission to Han. The Guduhous discovered Bi's plan, and Bi, frightened, gathered 40,000-50,000 troops to kill them. The Guduhous fled and reported to Shanyu, who sent 10,000 cavalry to attack Bi, but Bi retreated. In the spring of the 24th year of Jianwu, Bi was established as Huhanxie Chanyu, seeking to be a barrier for Han. The emperor agreed. In winter, Bi proclaimed himself Chanyu. In the 25th year, Bi's brother attacked and captured Beidan Shanyu's brother, defeating Beidan's army. Beidan Shanyu retreated a thousand miles. The emperor built chariots with watchtowers to resist the Huns. People recalled a prophecy that in the ninth generation of Han, Beidi would retreat thousands of miles. The territory opened up, and many defected to Nandanyu, who proclaimed himself a vassal, presenting treasures and asking for envoys. In the 26th year, the emperor sent envoys to Nandanyu. The Chanyu, after hesitation, worshipped the edict and proclaimed his vassalage. The emperor gave him various gifts, including crowns, clothes, gold seals, and weapons, and transported food and cattle to help the southern Xiongnu. Zhonglang was ordered to set up an office to handle lawsuits and investigate news. The court established a routine of annual gifts and exchanges.

translation:
Every year as a routine.
According to the custom of the Xiongnu, there are dragon temples three times a year, usually on Wuyue of the first month, fifth month, and ninth month to worship the gods.
Since Nan Danyu surrendered to the Han Dynasty, he also offered sacrifices to the Han Emperor. He took this opportunity to convene various ministries to discuss state affairs and hold horse and camel races for fun.
The most honorable among the Xiongnu ministers is King Zuo Xian, followed by King Zuo Guli, followed by King You Xian, followed by King You Guli, which is called the Four Corners; followed by King Ri Zhui of the Left and Right, followed by the Thousand Kings of Wen Yu of the Left and Right, followed by King Jianjiang of the Left and Right, which is called the Six Corners: They are all sons and brothers of the Chanyu, and they will become the Chanyu in order.
Ministers with different surnames have the title of Left and Right Guduhou, followed by the Left and Right Zhizhuguduhou, and others have various official titles such as Rizhu, Qiequ, and Dangchu, each of which determines the position and order based on the power and the number of tribes.
Shanyu's surname is a virtual conjunction.
There are four different surnames: Huyan, Xub, Qiulin, and Lan. They are famous clans in the Xiongnu country and often intermarry with the Shanyu.
Hu Xian is on the left, Lan and Xu Bu are on the right. They are responsible for judging cases and accepting lawsuits. They will verbally inform Shanyu of the severity of the judgment. There are no documents or books in that bundle.
In the winter of the 26th year, the sons of the five Gudu lords who had rebelled before led 3,000 troops to defect to the south. The Northern Shanyu sent cavalry to pursue them and captured them all.
Nan Shanyu sent troops to resist, but the battle was unfavorable.
The imperial court then issued a letter from Shao asking Shanyu to move to Meiji, Xihe, and sent Zhonglang Duan Chen and deputy captain Wang Yu to stay in Xihe to protect Shanyu, and to set up an official office, engage in work, and make history for Shanyu.
He also ordered Xihe Changsheng to lead 2,000 cavalry and 500 unchained prisoners every year to help Zhonglang guard Shanyu, stationed in the winter and withdrawn in the summer. From then on, it was a regular practice.
It also exempted the eight border counties from all taxes and labor. After Nan Danyu settled in Xihe, he also set up various princes and princes to help the Han Dynasty resist and guard the border.
Nan Danyu sent the Gudu Marquis of Han clan to garrison in the north, King Youxian to garrison Shuofang, Dangyu Gudu Marquis to garrison Wuyuan, Huyan Gudu Marquis to garrison Yunzhong, Lang clan Gudu Marquis to garrison Dingxiang, General Zuo Nan to garrison Yanmen, and Li Ji Gudu Marquis to garrison Daijun. They all commanded their troops to serve as the eyes and ears of the county to detect movements.
Bei Shanyu was very frightened and returned many Han people who had been kidnapped as a sign of friendship.
Every time their plundering troops passed near the south, or turned back and passed the post where the desert soldiers were scouting the enemy's situation, they always apologized and said: We are fighting the fugitive Dian Tayue King Zhu, and we are not daring to invade the Han people.
In the twenty-seventh year, Bei Shanyu sent an envoy to Wuwei to request peace. The emperor summoned the ministers to discuss the matter in the palace, but they could not make a decision.
summary: According to Xiongnu custom, there were three dragon temples a year for worship. Since Nan Danyu surrendered, he also offered sacrifices to the Han Emperor, convening ministries to discuss state affairs. The most honorable ministers were the Four Corners and Six Corners, all sons and brothers of the Chanyu. Ministers with different surnames had various titles. Shanyu's surname was a virtual conjunction, with four different surnames: Huyan, Xub, Qiulin, and Lan. In the winter of the 26th year, the sons of the five Gudu lords defected to the south, but were captured by Bei Shanyu. Nan Shanyu's resistance was unfavorable. The court ordered Shanyu to move to Meiji, Xihe, and sent Zhonglang Duan Chen to protect him. They also exempted eight border counties from taxes. Nan Danyu set up various princes to guard the border. Bei Shanyu, frightened, returned many Han people. In the 27th year, Bei Shanyu requested peace, but the crown prince advised against it, fearing Nan Shanyu's second thoughts. The emperor agreed. In the 28th year, Bei Shanyu again sent envoys, offering horses and furs, begging for marriage and music. The emperor, following Ban Biao's advice, gave rewards but did not send envoys.

translation:
The crown prince said: Southern Danyu had just surrendered, and the enemies in the north were afraid of being attacked, so they listened attentively and tried to submit to justice.
Now that the imperial court cannot send troops, but instead communicates with the enemy captives in the north, I am afraid that Nan Shanyu will have second thoughts, and the enemy captives in the north who are willing to surrender will not come to surrender again.
The emperor thought it was reasonable and told the prefect of Wuwei not to accept Bei Shanyu's envoy.
In the twenty-eighth year, the Northern Huns once again sent envoys to the court, presenting horses and furs, begging for marriage again, and asking for music from the Han Dynasty. They also asked the Hu people from various countries in the west city to come together to pay tribute and worship. The emperor handed the matter over to the Sangong Mansion to discuss the matter of payment and reply.
Situ Peng wrote to Ban Biao, saying: I heard that Emperor Xiaoxuan ordered the generals guarding the border to say: The Xiongnu is a big country, full of changes and deceptions.
If you interact appropriately, you can win the negotiation; if you fall into their scheme, you will be despised and bullied by them in turn.
Now when the Northern Xiongnu saw that the Southern Danyu had come to surrender, they were afraid that we would plot against them, so they begged for peace many times, brought cattle and horses from far away to do business with the Han, and repeatedly dispatched famous princes and paid many tributes. These were all used to show their wealth and strength to the outside world and to deceive us.
The more I saw that the Xiongnu contributed more, the more empty the Xiongnu country became, and the more urgent the Xiongnu's request for surrender and closeness became, and the more powerful their fear became.
However, since it is unable to help the south, it is not appropriate to cut off contact with the north. According to the principle of Huairou, Yu Lishu cannot leave without reply.
The minister thought that he could give them some rewards, which were roughly equivalent to the value of what they had given, so he publicly informed them of the results of the actions of Huhanxie and Zhizhi of the previous generations.
The wording of your reply must be appropriate. Now submit the drafted manuscript together and say: The Chanyu has not forgotten the kindness of the Han, recalled the old alliance with his ancestors, and plans to establish peace with the Han in order to assist himself and stabilize the country. His strategy is very clever, and we express our appreciation for the Chanyu.
In the past, the Xiongnu rebelled many times, and Huhanxie and Zhizhi hated each other. They were both rescued and protected by Emperor Xiaoxuan, so each of them sent their sons to serve in the court and guard the borders in the name of the vassal state.
After that, Zhizhi was resentful and rebellious, cutting off the favor of the court. However, he returned to Han and became closer to him, and his loyalty and filial piety became more and more obvious.
By the time the Zhi branch was eliminated in the Han Dynasty, the Huhan family finally preserved the country and passed on the throne to their descendants, who inherited the throne from each other.
Now Nan Danyu led his troops to submit to the south and returned to the desert.
He thought that Huhan was the legitimate eldest son and should be established as a Chanyu in order. Instead, he was deprived of his position and was suspected of betraying him. He repeatedly asked Mo to send troops to send troops to wipe out Beidan in the royal court. All kinds of strategies were put forward.
The imperial court considered that it could not accept one-sided words, and because Northern Danyu had paid tribute in consecutive years and wanted to establish a peace marriage, it rejected Southern Danyu's request without agreeing, in order to fulfill Shanyu's idea of ​​loyalty and filial piety.
The Han Dynasty ruled all the nations with its might and faith. As long as the moon shined, all the people there were the concubines of Mo.
Many barbarians with different customs have no moral distinction between closeness and alienation. Those who obey and submit will be praised and rewarded, and those who betray and disobey will be punished with elimination. The consequences of good deeds and evil deeds are as follows: Huhanxie and Zhizhi are examples.
Now that Chanyu wants to make peace and has expressed his sincerity, why is he suspicious and wants to lead all the countries in the Western Region to pay tribute and meet with him?
The countries in the Western Regions belong to the Xiongnu, what is the difference between those belonging to the Han?
summary: Bi reigned for nine years. After his death, his brother succeeded him. The Han Dynasty established a routine of condolences and rewards for each Shanyu's death. Over the years, various Shanyu succeeded each other, with conflicts between the northern and southern Xiongnu. The Northern Xiongnu, weakened by internal strife and attacks from Xianbei and others, eventually collapsed. The Southern Xiongnu, under various Shanyu, sometimes rebelled and sometimes surrendered, causing ongoing border troubles. The Han Dynasty sent generals to attack and defend, with mixed results. Eventually, the Xiongnu split into northern and southern courts, with the southern court serving as a vassal to Han. The Han Dynasty established the Du Liao military camp to guard against both. Despite occasional rebellions, the southern Xiongnu remained largely submissive, while the northern Xiongnu gradually weakened and disappeared. The Han Dynasty's policy of using barbarians to attack barbarians proved effective, but also led to ongoing conflicts and instability.

translation:
In the past, the Quan Rong invaded during the reign of Gao Xin. The emperor was worried because of the cruelty of the Quan Rong, but he could not win against the Quan Rong. So he searched and recruited people all over the world. Anyone who could get the head of General Wu, the general of Quanrong, would be rewarded with a thousand yi of gold, a fief of 10,000 households, and his youngest daughter would be married to him.
At that time, the emperor had a dog with five-colored hair named Jiahu.
After the emperor gave the order, Panhu carried the head to the palace gate. The officials were surprised. When they looked at it, they found it was General Wu's head.
The emperor was very happy, but he considered that he could not marry his daughter to Panhu, and there was no reason to give an official title to a dog. He wanted to repay the dog but did not know how to do it.
When the daughter found out, she thought that the emperor had given an order and she could not violate her faith, so she asked to marry Panhu.
The emperor had no choice but to marry his daughter to Panhu.
After Panhu got the emperor's daughter, he carried her to Nanshan and lived in Shidongbao.
The place where Panhu is located is dangerous, isolated and inaccessible to humans.
So the emperor's daughter took off her clothes, combed her hair into a bun like a servant, and put on independent clothes.
The emperor missed his daughter and was very sad. He sent envoys to look for her, but they were always met with wind, rain, thunder and darkness, and the envoys could not move forward.
After three years, she gave birth to twelve children, six boys and six girls.
After Panhu died, the children married each other.
They weave clothes from tree bark and dye their clothes with fruits and vegetables. They like to wear colorful clothes, and the clothes are all shaped like tails.
Their mother later came back and informed the emperor of the situation, so the emperor sent envoys to fetch the children.
The colors of their clothes are mixed and bright, and their voices are difficult to distinguish. They like to hide in high mountains and deep valleys, and do not like to live in open areas.
The emperor complied with their wishes and gave them famous mountains and swamps.
From then on, their race multiplied and became known as barbarians.
They are dull on the outside but smart on the inside. They live in their own country and value old customs.
Because their father had meritorious service and their mother was the daughter of the emperor, they farmed and did business. They could enter and leave the Guanmen Bridge without a letter, and they did not need to pay taxes.
All the leaders of the city were given seals and ribbons by the imperial court, and their crowns were made of otter skin.
They call the big leader "Jingfu" and call each other "Quitu".
The current Changsha Wulingman are their descendants.
In the era of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, they established alliances with the barbarians, so they called the barbarians to be subdued.
During the Xia and Shang dynasties, barbarians gradually became a scourge on the border.
By the Zhou Dynasty, the barbarian race gradually became stronger.
King Xuan of Zhou Dynasty was resurrected, so he ordered Uncle Fang to go south to conquer the barbarian areas, which the poet called "the barbarians came in fear of submission".
He also said: The stupid and arrogant barbarians actually became enemies of the great country.
This shows that the barbarian race is prosperous, so it competes with the Chinese enemies.
summary: During the reign of Gao Xin, the Quan Rong invaded, and the emperor offered rewards for the head of their general, General Wu. The emperor's five-colored dog, Panhu, brought the general's head. Unable to marry his daughter to a dog, the emperor was troubled, but his daughter insisted on honoring the promise and married Panhu. They lived in Nanshan, where she bore twelve children, six boys and six girls. After Panhu's death, the children intermarried, and their descendants became known as barbarians. They wore colorful clothes with tail-like shapes, lived in remote mountains, and were granted famous mountains and swamps by the emperor. Their leaders received seals from the imperial court, and they were exempt from taxes. The current Changsha Wulingman are their descendants.

translation:
King Ping of Zhou moved away from home, and the barbarians invaded and ravaged the Central Plains.
Marquis Wen of Jin assisted the government and led Marquis Cai Gong to defeat the barbarians.
When King Wu of Chu arrived, the barbarians and Luo Zi defeated the Chu army and killed the Chu army general Qu Xia.
King Chuzhuang had just succeeded to the throne, the people were hungry, the army was weak, and he was invaded by barbarians again.
After the Chu army became stronger, the barbarians obeyed, and from then on the barbarians belonged to the Chu state.
After the battle at Yanling, the Luan people and King Chu Jie jointly attacked Zili.
He went to Yuqi to assist King Chu Miao, and annexed Manyue to the south, thus occupying Dongting and Cangwu.
King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to attack Chu, captured the barbarians, and began to establish Qianzhong County.
After the prosperity of the Han Dynasty, Qianzhong County was changed to Wuling County.
Every year, barbarian adults are required to pay a piece of cloth, and children are required to pay two feet of cloth. This is called Yuan cloth.
Although barbarians invaded from time to time, they were not enough to cause disaster to the county.
After the resurgence of Rentiao, Manlou in Gendi became particularly powerful.
In the 23rd year of Jianjian's reign, Jingfu Xiang Shancheng and others took advantage of the barbarian terrain to launch a massive attack on counties.
Guangwu sent Wuwei General Liu Shang to mobilize more than 10,000 troops from Nanjun, Changsha and Jianlu. They took boats upstream from Yuancheng to Wuxi to attack Xiang Xiang.
Liu Shang underestimated the enemy and entered a dangerous area. The mountains were deep and the water was fast, making it impossible for the ship to move forward.
The barbarians knew that Liu Shang did not have enough food, the road was far away, and they did not know the route, so they gathered troops to guard the dangerous terrain.
After Liu Shang ran out of food, he withdrew his troops. The barbarians intercepted them along the way. Liu Shang's army was defeated and the entire army was wiped out.
In the twenty-fourth year, Xiang Shancheng and others went downstream to attack Linyuan. The imperial court sent Li Song, the emissary, and Ma Cheng, the prefect of Zhongshan, to attack Xiang Shancheng, but they could not win.
In the spring of the next year, the imperial court sent Fubo General Ma Yuan, Zhonglang General Liu Kuang, Ma Wu, Sun Yong and others to lead their troops to Linyuan and defeated Xiang Shancheng.
Xiang Shancheng and others were hungry and impoverished, and asked for surrender. Ma Yuan happened to die of illness, and Yezhe Zongjun accepted the surrender of all their troops.
The imperial court established government officials among the barbarians, and the barbarians were pacified.
In the first year of Emperor Suzong's founding, Chen Cong and others from Wuling and Lizhong rebelled and entered the realm of Lingyang Barbarians.
In the winter of this year, Lingyang Man Wuli Jingfu defeated Chen Cong for the county, and Chen Cong and others all surrendered.
In the winter of the third year, Qin Erjian and others from Mizhong rebelled again and attacked and burned the boundaries of Linyang, Zuotang and Xiaoling.
In the spring of the next year, the imperial court recruited seven counties in Jingzhou and Runan and Ying! There were more than 5,000 prisoners, officials and soldiers who had been released from the shackles. They resisted the defense in Lingyang. They recruited 4,000 Wuli barbarians and barbarians who had not rebelled to attack the bandits in Lizhong.
In the spring of the fifth year, Qin Erjian and others requested surrender, but were not granted.
The county guard took this opportunity to march in and fight with Tan Erjian at Hongxia. He defeated Tan Erjian and beheaded him. The rest of the people abandoned the barracks and fled back to Qizhong. They sent people to ask for surrender, and then they accepted their surrender.
So he withdrew the garrison in Wuling and gave various rewards to the officers and soldiers. In the winter of the fourth year of Emperor Yongyuan, the Qizhong Man, Lizhong Man Tan Rong and others rebelled, burning down the posthouse, killing and plundering officials and people. The county troops defeated Tan Rong. Force him to surrender. In the second year of Emperor An's reign, the Lizhong barbarians were resentful because the county's corvée taxation was unfair, so they jointly charged more than 2,000 barbarians from various tribes, attacked the city, and killed state and county officials.
The prefectures and counties recruited troops from Wuli Man and Liuting to pursue them and defeated the Lizhong Man and others. They all broke up and surrendered.
The imperial court rewarded the leaders of Wuliman and Liuting with different amounts of gold and silk.
In the autumn of the second year, four thousand people from Zhongzhong and Lizhong became bandits together.
There were also more than a thousand people, including Lingling Man Yangsun and Chen Tang, who wore red scarves and claimed to be generals. They burned down the government offices and looted the people.
The states and counties recruited obedient barbarians to attack and pacify the rebellious barbarians.
summary: During the Zhou Dynasty, the barbarian race grew stronger. King Xuan sent Uncle Fang to conquer them. King Ping moved east, and barbarians invaded the Central Plains. Marquis Wen of Jin defeated them. King Wu of Chu faced barbarian attacks, and King Zhuang later subdued them. After the Han Dynasty's rise, Wuling County was established, and barbarian adults paid one piece of cloth annually, children two feet. During the Jianwu period, Jingfu Xiang Shancheng led a massive attack. General Liu Shang was defeated with his entire army. Ma Yuan later defeated Xiang Shancheng, who surrendered. In subsequent years, various barbarian groups rebelled, including Chen Cong, Qin Erjian, and Tan Rong. The court often recruited obedient barbarians to suppress rebellions. In Yonghe's first year, the prefect of Wuling proposed increasing taxes like those of Han people. Shangshu Ling Yu Xie Jin warned against this, but the emperor did not listen. The barbarians rebelled, killing officials. Li Jin was sent to pacify them, serving nine years in Wuling. The Yelang Kingdom originated from a woman finding a baby in bamboo. Emperor Wu established Yangke County. The King of Dian descended from Zhuang Qi. During Wang Mang's chaos, Dongcan rebelled. Wen Qi resisted Gongsun Shu and later submitted to Guangwu. In Jianwu's eighteenth year, Dongcan rebelled again, and Liu Shang pacified them. During Emperor Ling's Xiping period, Yi tribes rebelled, capturing the prefect. Li Yi and Pangzhi defeated them. The Ailaoyi originated from Sha Yi, who gave birth to ten sons after touching a submerged tree. In Jianwu's twenty-third year, King Xianli attacked Lu Dad but was defeated by storms. In the twenty-seventh year, Xianli surrendered. In Yong's twelfth year, King Liu Maung submitted with 553,711 people. Yongchang County was established. During Emperor Huan's reign, King Leilao rebelled and was killed. In Yongyuan's sixth year, King Mo Yan presented rhinos and elephants. In Yongning's first year, King Yongyou Diao presented musicians who performed illusions.

translation:
The custom in Nahuo is that men and women bathe in the river, so it is called cross-shame.
In the country of Kanren to the west of Jiao:, the first child is always dismembered and eaten, saying that it will be good for subsequent children.
If the food tastes sweet, he brings it to the king. The king is pleased and rewards the father of the child.
He married a beautiful wife and gave it to his brother.
Today's Wuyou people are their descendants.
There is Yueshang Kingdom to the south of Jiaotu.
In the sixth year of Zhou Gong's regency, etiquette was established, music was made, and the world was at peace. An envoy from the Yueshang Kingdom rode three elephants and came to offer white wild ducks through the interpreters, saying: The road is far away, the mountains and rivers are blocked, and the messengers are blocked, so the interpreters came to see him.
King Cheng of Zhou gave the white wild bird to Duke Zhou.
Duke Zhou said: If you do not show kindness to others, then the virtuous people will not enjoy the gifts of others; if the government decree is not implemented in that area, the virtuous person will not treat those people as subjects.
Why do I get such a reward!
The envoy from the Yueshang Kingdom asked: I accept the order from the elders of our country. They said: There have been no storms and thunderstorms in the sky for a long time. Is it possible that a saint has appeared in the Central Plains?
If there is a saint in the Central Plains, why not go to see him?
Duke Zhou gave the white pheasant to the emperor, praising the late king for his divine inspiration, and offered the white pheasant to the ancestral temple.
After the moral fortunes of the Zhou Dynasty weakened, the Yueshang Kingdom gradually cut off contact with them.
When the Chu State became hegemonic, it made Baiyue worship and pay tribute.
The Qin Dynasty annexed the world and used force to make the barbarians submit. Then they opened up the land outside the mountains and established Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiangjun.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, Wei Tuo established himself as the King of Nanyue, which was passed down for five generations.
In the fifth year of Emperor Wu Yuanding's reign, Nanyue was finally wiped out and nine counties were established separately, under the jurisdiction of Jiaoxi Governor.
Among them, Zhuya and Dan'er counties are on the island, one thousand miles long from east to west and five hundred miles long from north to south.
The barbarian chiefs in Nabu regarded long ears as noble, so they all pierced their ears and hung things on them, making their ears hang down to their shoulders, up to three inches long.
In the last years of Emperor Wu's reign, Sun Xing from Kuaiji, the prefect of Zhuya, collected broad sheets of cloth and presented them to the court. Unable to bear the labor, the barbarians attacked the county and killed Sun Xing.
Sun Xing's son Sun Bao united with the good people and defeated the barbarians. He took charge of the county's political affairs and conquered the remaining rebel parties. It took several years to pacify Zhuya.
Sun Bao sent an envoy to seal the seal and return it to the court, and wrote a letter explaining the situation. The emperor immediately appointed Sun Bao as the prefect of Zhuya after sending a letter to Shaoshu.
Prominent decrees were generally implemented, and tributes and envoys were received every year.
The Central Plains were greedy for their treasures and property and gradually bullied them, so Zhuya rebelled every few years.
In the third year of the Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Yuan finally abolished Zhuya County.
Zhuya was established as a county for a total of sixty-five years.
summary: During Emperor Huan's reign, Wuling Man Zhanshan rebelled, and Changsha barbarians looted counties with over 10,000 people. Wuling barbarians invaded Jiangling, causing officials to flee. Du Shang and Feng Yu were sent to pacify them. In Emperor Ling's third year, Wuling barbarians rebelled again. The Book of Rites describes southern barbarians as having tattooed foreheads and mixed bathing customs. In Kanren country, firstborn children were eaten, with the king receiving portions. Yueshang Kingdom sent white pheasants via elephant during Zhou Gong's regency. After Zhou's decline, Chu made Baiyue pay tribute. Qin established Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiangjun. Han conquered Nanyue in Yuanding's fifth year, establishing nine counties. Zhuya and Dan'er counties were on an island where chiefs pierced their ears to hang objects. After repeated rebellions, Zhuya was abolished in Yuan's third year.
