translation:
When Wang Mang assisted the government, in the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, Huang Zhiguo from the south of Rinan County came to donate rhinos.
Although there are counties and counties in the areas under the jurisdiction of Jiaoshi, the languages ​​​​are different and require translation before communication can occur.
The people wrapped there are like animals, there is no distinction between old and young.
They put their hair in a bun at the neck, bare their feet, and covered their bodies with a cloth from head to bottom.
Later, many criminals from the Central Plains were moved there, allowing them to live mixed with the locals. Only then did they gradually understand their language, and they were gradually civilized and learned etiquette.
Guangwu Zhongxing, Xiguang served as the prefect of Jiaoxi, and Ren Yan served as the prefect of Jiuzhen. They taught the local people to cultivate fields and crops, made crowns and shoes for them, and began to establish the etiquette of matchmaking and betrothal. Only then did they know about marriage. They also built schools for them to guide them with etiquette and justice.
In the twelfth year of Jianwu, Zhang You, a manli outside the Jiuzhen border, led his fellow tribesmen to admire Jiaohua and submit to the Central Plains, and was named the Lord of Guihanli.
The next year, barbarians outside the border of South Vietnam presented white wild harlequins and white rabbits.
In the 16th year of his reign, Zheng Tie, the daughter-in-law, and her younger sister Zheng Er rebelled against Jiao Sha.
Zheng Bian was the daughter of General Luo of Luling County.
Married to Zhu Zairen Shisuo as his wife, she was very brave.
Su Ding, the prefect of Jiaoshi, brought him to justice. Zheng was angry and rebelled.
In this way, the barbarians of Jiuzhen, Nan, and Hepu all responded to Zheng Bian. They captured a total of sixty-five cities, and Zheng Bian established himself as king.
The governor of Jiaosha and the governors of various counties could only defend themselves.
Guangwu then issued an edict asking Changsha, Hepu, and Jiaoshi to prepare vehicles and ships, build roads and bridges, open up road obstacles and valleys, and reserve grain.
In the eighteenth year, General Fubo Ma Yuan and Louchuan General Duan Zhi were sent to mobilize more than 10,000 troops from Changsha, Guiyang, Lingling, and Cangwu to conquer the side.
In April of the next summer, Ma Yuan captured Jiaoxi and killed Zheng Zhi, Zheng Er and others. The rest surrendered and dispersed.
Ma Yuan advanced to attack Jiuzhen bandit Kou Duyang and others, defeated Duyang and made Duyang surrender.
Ma Yuan moved more than 300 leaders of the bandits to live in Lingling.
In this way, everything outside the ridge was pacified.
In the first year of the Yuanhe period of Emperor Suzong, the chiefs of the barbarian tribes outside the southern border of Japan presented live rhinos and white pheasants.
In the summer and April of the twelfth year of Emperor Yongyuan, more than 2,000 barbarians from Rinan and Xianglin invaded, looted the people, and burned down the government offices. The prefectures and counties sent troops to attack and killed their leaders, and the remaining troops surrendered.
So the imperial court established a history of generals and soldiers in Xianglin to prevent the barbarians from harming them.
In the first year of Emperor An's Yongchu reign, the Yelang barbarians outside the Jiuzhen border surrendered all their territory, allowing the Han Dynasty to expand its territory by 1,840 miles.
In the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, the barbarians in Cangwu rebelled. The next year, they summoned and lured thousands of barbarians and Han people from Yulin and Hepu to attack Cangwu County.
Empress Dowager Deng sent Ren Lian, the imperial censor, to issue an edict to pardon the rebels, and all the bandits surrendered and dispersed.
In the first year of Yanguang, the barbarians outside the Jiuzhen border paid tribute and submitted.
Three years later, barbarians from outside Japan's southern border came to submit again.
In the sixth year of Yongjian reign of Emperor Shun, King Ye Tiao from outside the southern border of Japan sent an envoy to pay tribute, and the emperor gave King Ye Tiao a gold seal and purple ribbon.
In the second year of Yonghe, thousands of people including Lian Lian, a barbarian outside the border of Yunnan and Xianglin, attacked Xianglin County, burned down the city government offices, and killed county and county officials.
Fan Yan, the governor of Jiaosha, mobilized more than 10,000 troops from Jiaodu and Jiuzhen counties to rescue Xianglin.
summary: Wang Mang received rhino tributes. Guangwu中兴时期, Xiguang and Ren Yan taught farming and established marriage rites in Jiaozhi. In Jianwu's twelfth year, Zhang You submitted. In the sixteenth year, Zheng Bian rebelled, capturing sixty-five cities. Ma Yuan defeated her in the eighteenth year. During Emperor Suzong's Yuanhe period, barbarian chiefs presented rhinos and pheasants. In Yongyuan's twelfth year, Rinan barbarians attacked, and the court established military posts. In Yongchu's first year, Yelang barbarians surrendered territory. During Emperor Shun's Yongjian period, King Ye Tiao paid tribute. In Yonghe's second year, Lian Lian attacked Xianglin. Li Gu advised against sending troops from distant provinces, recommending local officials instead. Zhu Liang and Zhang Qiao were appointed, pacifying the region. During Emperor Huan's reign, Zhu Da rebelled, and Xia Fang pacified them. In Emperor Ling's third year, Gu Yong recruited 100,000 Wuyou people.

translation:
They had no leader and all served ghosts and gods, so they threw swords into a stone cave together and agreed that whoever could hit the target would be crowned king.
Only Ba's son, Wu Xiang, was in tune with each other, and everyone was amazed.
They also asked each person to ride on a boat made of clay, and agreed that whoever could float on the water would be the king of the country.
The boats of the children with other surnames all sank, but the boat of the Prime Minister floated on the water.
So everyone jointly made him the king of the country, that is, the king of Lin.
Lin Jun then took a boat made of clay from Yishui to Yanyang.
There was a goddess in Yanyan who said to Mr. Lin: This place is vast and produces fish and salt. I hope you will stay and live together.
Lin Jun refused.
The God of Salt always came to stay with him at night, and at dawn he turned into a bug and flew with many bugs, blocking the sun and making the world dark.
After more than ten days, Lin Jun saw an opportunity and shot the Salt God with an arrow, and the sky became bright.
Lin Jun then became the king of Yicheng, and the other four surnames surrendered to him.
After Lin Jun died, his soul became a white tiger for generations.
Because tigers drank human blood, Ba Shi sacrificed living people to Lord Lin.
When King Hui of Qin annexed Bazhong, he took the Bashi as the leader of the barbarians and married Qin women for generations. The barbarian people's titles were equivalent to no replacement. If they committed crimes, they could be offset by their titles.
The barbarian leader pays an annual rental tax of 2,016 yuan, and pays a compulsory rental tax of 1,800 yuan every three years.
The people of Ba's family gave out a frightened cloth of eight feet and two feet, and a piece of hair worth thirty silver.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, Jin Qiang, the governor of Nanjun, requested that all the old practices of the Qin Dynasty be followed.
In the 23rd year of Jianwu, Lei Qian and others from Lushan Mountain in Nanjun began to rebel and invade and plunder the people. The imperial court sent Wuwei General Liu Shang to lead more than 10,000 people to defeat Lei Qian, and moved more than 7000 Meishan barbarians to Jiangxia County, which is now the Mianzhong Barbarians.
In the thirteenth year of Emperor Yongyuan's reign, Wuman Xu Sheng and others believed that the county governor's tax collection was uneven, and they were resentful, so they gathered to rebel.
In the summer of the next year, the imperial court sent envoys to inspect the troops of more than 10,000 counties in Jingzhou to attack Xu Sheng.
Because Xu Sheng and others relied on the dangerous terrain, they could not capture it for a long time.
So the troops from various groups advanced in different directions, and some attacked from Bajun and Yufu. The barbarians dispersed and fled. The Han army killed the barbarian leader, took advantage of the victory and pursued them, and defeated Xu Sheng and others.
Xu Sheng and others begged to surrender, so they were all relocated to Jiangxia again.
In the second year of Emperor Ling's reign, the Jiangxia barbarians rebelled and were conquered and put down by the prefectures and counties.
In the third year of Guanghe's reign, the Jiangxia barbarians rebelled again and joined forces with the Lujiang bandit Huang Chang. They had more than 100,000 people and captured four counties. The invasion lasted for several years.
Lu Kang, the governor of Lujiang, conquered and defeated Jiangxia Man and Huang Zhang, and the others surrendered and collapsed.
summary: The Bajunnanjunman originated from Wuluo Zhongli Mountain, with five surnames. Ba's son Wu Xiang became king by hitting a stone cave with a sword and floating a clay boat. He married a salt goddess but later shot her. After death, his soul became a white tiger. King Hui of Qin made Ba leaders marry Qin women. During Han, Lei Qian rebelled, and Liu Shang moved 7,000 Meishan barbarians to Jiangxia. In Yongyuan's thirteenth year, Xu Sheng rebelled over taxes and was defeated. Banmei barbarians originated when a Yi man shot a white tiger for King Zhao of Qin. Emperor Gaozu mobilized them to attack the Three Qins, creating the Bayu Dance. During Emperor Huan's reign, they rebelled multiple times. In Guanghe's second year, they rebelled again. Cheng Bao advised that oppressive officials caused the rebellion, and the emperor sent Cao Qian to pardon them.

translation:
On the New Year's Day of the next year, Emperor An met with his ministers and asked him to perform music in the palace. He appointed Yong Youtiao as the Han Dynasty Commander-in-Chief, and gave him seals and ribbons as well as various amounts of gold, silver and colored silk.
Qiongdu Yi was developed by Emperor Wu, who designated it as Qiongdu County.
After a while, the ground sank and turned into a slop, so it was called Qiongchi, and people in the south called it Qionghe River.
Later, the Qiongdu Yi rebelled again.
In the sixth year of Yuanding, Han soldiers crossed the Jun River to conquer the Qiongdu Yi and made it Yue Mao County.
The land in Boguo is flat and there are rice fields.
On Yutong Mountain in Qingxie County, there are the Golden Horse Society and the Bade God, where light and shadow often appear.
The custom in Nahuo is that most people have fun and debauchery, but they also like to sing, which is roughly similar to the people of Pangke.
The Qiongdu Yi chieftains were very indulgent and it was difficult to control them.
During the reign of Wang Mang, the governor of the county, Mei Gen, recruited a noble from Qiondu and appointed him as a military marquis.
In the second year of Gengshi, Changgui led his tribe to attack and killed Meigen, and established himself as King of Qiong Valley, exercising the power of prefect.
Later he surrendered to Gongsun Shu.
After Gongsun Shu failed, Guangwu granted Changgui the title of King of Qiong Valley.
In the fourteenth year of Jianwu's reign, Changgui sent an envoy to present three years' accounting records to the court. Guangwu immediately awarded Changgui the seal and ribbon of the Yuelun Prefect.
In the 19th year, General Liu Shang of Wuwei attacked Yizhou Yi and passed through Yuelun.
After Changgui learned about it, he suspected that once Liu Shang pacified the south, authoritarian laws would be implemented, and he could not indulge at will. So he gathered people to build a fortress, called the leaders of various ministries, and brewed a large amount of poisonous wine. He wanted to use the poisonous wine to comfort the army first, and then took the opportunity to attack Liu Shang.
Liu Shang knew Chang Gui's plan, and immediately dispatched troops to occupy Qiongdu, then suddenly attacked Chang Gui, killed him, and moved his family to Chengdu.
In the first year of Yongping, Gu Fuyi rebelled again. The governor of Yizhou sent troops to conquer, defeated Gu Fuyi, killed Ding and their leader, and sent their heads to the capital.
Later, Zhang Xi, a native of Bajun, was the prefect. His political affairs and education were clean and fair, and he made the barbarians harmonious.
Zhang Xi had been the governor for seventeen years. When he died, the Yi people loved and admired him as if they had lost their parents.
More than 200 elderly people from Suqi County brought cattle and sheep to mourn Zhang Xi's birthplace, Anhan County, to build a tomb to worship him.
The emperor issued an edict to praise Zhang Xi and built an ancestral hall for him.
In the third year of Emperor An's reign, eight tribes including Dayang and other Yi people outside the Yue Mao border, with a total of 31,000 households and 167,620 people, admired virtue and righteousness and submitted.
At that time, there were many taxes in counties and counties. In the fifth year of the Yuan Dynasty, Zhuanyi Danniu Zhong Fengli and others rebelled and killed Sui Jiuling.
The next year, the Yi people in Yongchang, Yizhou and Shu counties all rebelled and responded to the siege. Their tribesmen numbered more than 100,000. They destroyed more than 20 counties, killed county officials, burned cities and towns, plundered the people, piled up corpses, and left no trace of human beings within a thousand miles.
The emperor sent a letter to Zhang Qiao, the governor of Yizhou, to select competent people to conquer the barbarians.
Zhang Qiao then sent his servant Yang Song to lead troops to Keyu to attack the bandits. However, the bandits were strong and Yang Song did not dare to advance. He first informed the three counties of Shao and secretly recruited warriors with heavy rewards.
Then he advanced to fight with Feng Li and others, and defeated Feng Li. He killed more than 30,000 people, captured 1,500 people alive, and gained more than 40 million in money, all of which was used to reward the soldiers.
Feng Li and others were frightened, killed the leader of the conspirators, and went to Yang Song to beg for surrender. Yang Song gave them special comfort and acceptance.
The other thirty-six tribes came to surrender.
Therefore, Yang Song reported that ninety people among the officials who were cunning and had invaded the barbarians were reduced to death.
Before the merit evaluation in the state could be reported to the court, Yang Song happened to be injured and died. Zhang Qiao was very sad and regretful, so he carved a stone to record his merit and painted a portrait of Yang Song.
Because Zhang Xi had left a benevolent impression among the barbarians, the emperor appointed his son Zhang Tuan as the prefect.
The Yi people were very happy and greeted him on the road, saying: "You look very much like our governor."
Later, Zhang Tuan lost the support of the people, and some Yi people wanted to rebel. An old man among the Yi people told them: Just for the sake of the former governor.
summary: The Qiongdu Yi were developed by Emperor Wu. During Wang Mang's reign, Changgui killed the prefect and later submitted to Gongsun Shu. Guangwu made him king, but Liu Shang killed him in Jianwu's nineteenth year. During Emperor An's reign, eight Yi tribes submitted. In Yuan's fifth year, Feng Li rebelled, and Zhang Qiao sent Yang Song to defeat him. The Yi capital was developed by Emperor Wu. During Yongping, Zhu Fu pacified over 100 countries including Bailang, with over 6 million people submitting. They presented three poems. During Emperor Ling's reign, the vassal state of Shu was changed to Hanjia. Ran Chiyi was developed by Emperor Wu as Wenshan County. The climate was cold, and Yi people worked in Shu during winter. They built stone houses called "Qiong Cong." The land produced wheat, livestock, and medicinal materials. Zhiwuya was developed in Yuangu's sixth year as Wudu County. The Di people were brave and greedy. During Yuanfeng's third year, they rebelled and were moved to Jiuquan. During Jianwu, the Di people surrendered to Han after Gongsun Shu's defeat.

translation:
Classics, starting from Shan Jing and Shui Zhi, also briefly mention this aspect.
Although the Yi people from all over the world surrendered and rebelled erratically, and the prestige and favor of the imperial court were often interrupted, as long as the education was implemented, whether it was a tribe with lop-eared eagle feet or a tribe that lived like wild beasts and spoke like a raven, they all submitted to the Central Plains as an entire tribe.
Therefore, their names are recorded in the official offices of Zhonglang General and Xiaowei, and their numbers are included in the official lists of meritorious officials under the Duhufu, Buduwei, and Prefectures. The population is often calculated in millions.
As for the divine objects hidden deep in the mountains, hidden under the sea, and the treasures buried in sand and stone and inhabiting the land, they all showed strange and gorgeous features and were decorated in the palace curtains.
Tributes such as warnings, fire orders, domesticated birds and tall beasts were gathered in the imperial treasury; arts with completely different sound and rhythm, such as Yi people's songs and Bayu dances, were displayed outside the palace gate.
Is the way of submission complete at this point?
However, it can also be said that it has attracted the submission of races from far away.
Although the barbarians lived on the mountains, rocks and valleys, most of them lived in certain areas, connected to Jingzhou and Jiaozhou areas, and were distributed and guarded outside Bajun and Yong. It is impossible to calculate their number.
However, the barbarians were ferocious and cunning and slightly weaker than the Qiang and Di, so the harm caused by their plundering and cruelty could not go far.
The barbarians outside the southwest border are especially weak.
Therefore, setting up a garrison in Yongchang was initially to guard against the barbarians from far away. Later, it opened up the land and made the people self-reliant. Now it has become a city.
Zan said: The area inhabited by various barbarians is very small, but it is spread all over the four borders.
Sculpted bodies, wearing straw clothes, relying on the deep and rugged mountain life.
There are also some Yi people living in the border areas of Shu County.
The scattered tribal villages have turned to Zhou Qi's path of morality and justice.
Once they gained trust by going to teach, the barbarians changed their clothes and brought treasures, which led the imperial court to establish Yongchang County and include the barbarians in household registers along with hundreds of millions of people in the mainland.
summary: The argument states that expeditions against barbarians generally succeeded within a year, opening lands of diverse races. Education reached all areas where the sun rises and sets. Although barbarians surrendered and rebelled inconsistently, those with various customs submitted to the Central Plains. Their names were recorded in official offices, and their population numbered in the millions. Precious objects from mountains and seas decorated palace curtains. Tributes of rare birds and beasts filled the imperial treasury. Barbarian songs and dances were performed outside the palace gate. The barbarians lived in mountainous areas connected to Jingzhou and Jiaozhou, distributed outside Bajun and Yong. Their ferocity was slightly weaker than Qiang and Di, so their plundering could not go far. Southwestern barbarians were especially weak. Yongchang garrison was established to guard against distant barbarians, later opening land and becoming a city. The eulogy notes that various barbarians spread across four borders, living in deep mountains, with some in Shu County border areas. Once they gained trust through teaching, they changed customs and brought treasures, leading to Yongchang County's establishment and their inclusion in household registers.

translation:
◆Biography of Wu You, courtesy name Ji Ying, a native of Changyuan County, Chenliu County.
His father, Wu Hui, was the governor of Nanhai.
When Wu You was twelve years old, he followed his father to the official residence.
Wu Hui wanted to use bamboo slips to write scriptures, but Wu You dissuaded him and said: "Now that you have passed Wuling, you will see the seaside in the distance. The customs here are simple, but there are many rare and rare things. The imperial court is suspicious of them above, and the powerful and powerful people below want to possess them."
If your book is finished, it will need many vehicles to carry it.
Once upon a time, Ma Yuan was falsely accused of transporting coix back home, saying that all he transported were pearls and rhinoceros. Wang Yang was good at carriages and horses, and was well-dressed. He was very good at traveling, but he could not carry anything more than a bag, and others said he could make gold.
Therefore, the place of suspicion was the most cautious place for ancient sages. After hearing what he said, Wu Hui stopped writing scriptures, stroked Wu You's back and said, "My surname is Wu, and I have had a son for generations!" At the age of twenty, Wu You's father died, and the family did not have a single stone of food savings, but he did not accept gifts from others.
He often herds pigs in the Changyuan swamp and hums scriptures.
When he met his father's friend, he was asked: You are the son of Erqianshi but you are doing such a despicable job. Even if you don't feel ashamed, how can you be worthy of your underground father? Wu You said thank you and herded the pigs as before.
Later, he was promoted to Xiaolian, and when he was about to leave, a wine ceremony was held in the county to see him off. Wu You went over the altar and talked and laughed with Xiaoshi Yongqiu Huang Zhen for a long time, and they became friends and said goodbye.
The county meritorious officer thought Wu You was arrogant and rude, so he asked the prefect to reprimand him.
The prefect said: Wu Jiying can know people, so don't talk about it for now. Huang Zhen later promoted him to Xiaolian and appointed him as the new chief of Cai. The world praised him for his integrity and integrity.
At this time, Gongshamu came to the capital to visit the Imperial Academy and had no food to eat, so he changed his clothes and worked to pound rice for Wu You.
Wu You was greatly surprised when he talked to him, so he arranged to meet him at a place where rice was pounded.
Wu You cited the four qualities of Guanglu, honesty, simplicity, humility and frugality, and moved to Jiaodong to be the Marquis.
At this time, Dai Hong's father was the county magistrate in Jibei Province. Dai Hong was sixteen years old and lived with him in the prime minister's house.
Whenever Wu You visited the garden, he often heard voices chanting, and he treated him strangely and kindly. He also made friends with him. After all, Dai Hong became a Confucian scholar, became famous in the East, and became the prefect of Jiuquan.
Wu You was a benevolent and simple person in politics and led by example.
When common people have disputes, they often reflect behind closed doors and then settle the case, admonishing them with morality, and sometimes going to the village in person to urge reconciliation.
From then on, there were fewer disputes among the people, and the officials were virtuous and refrained from deception.
summary: Wu You, courtesy name Ji Ying, was from Chenliu County. As a child, he advised his father against writing scriptures on bamboo slips while serving as an official in a distant region, warning that such actions might invite suspicion from the court and powerful families, citing historical examples like Ma Yuan and Wang Yang who were falsely accused. His father heeded this advice. After his father's death, Wu You lived in poverty, herding pigs and reciting scriptures, refusing gifts from others. When criticized for this humble work, he continued regardless.

translation:
The stingy husband Sun Xing secretly took money from the people and bought clothes for his father. His father took the clothes and got angry and said: "With such a good appearance, how can I have the heart to deceive him?" Urge him to confess his sins.
Sun Xing was ashamed and afraid, so he took his clothes and surrendered to the pavilion.
Wu You moved the people around him and asked him why. Sun Xing told him everything his father said.
Wu You said: You have received a bad reputation because of your father. It is said that you will know what kind of person you are by looking at your mistakes.  He sent him back to thank his father and gave him the clothes he bought.
Another man from Anqiu, Guanqiu Chang, was walking in the city with his mother. He met a drunkard and insulted his mother. Guanqiu Chang killed the drunkard and ran away. Qiu tracked him to Jiaodong and captured Guanqiu Chang.
Wu You called Chief Guanqiu and said: "My son's mother has been insulted. This is a shameful thing."
However, a filial son must consider the consequences of his anger, and his actions must not harm his parents.
Now you are angry behind your parents' back and kill people in daylight. It is unjust to pardon you; but you cannot bear to be punished even more. What should you do? Chief Guanqiu tied his hands with weapons and said: "The state makes laws, but I personally break the laws. Although you have pity on me, you cannot show mercy."
Wu You asked Guanqiu if he had a wife. Answer: I have a wife but no son. So he moved to Anqiu and arrested the wife of Chief Guanqiu. When his wife arrived, he released the shackles of Chief Guanqiu and made her sleep with him in prison. As a result, his wife became pregnant.
When the execution came at the end of winter, Chang Guanqiu cried and said to his mother: "I have failed my mother and deserve to die. How should I repay Jun Wu?" So he bit off a finger and swallowed it, and said with blood: If my wife gives birth to a son, I will name him Wu Sheng. He said that I will swallow my finger before I die as an oath, and I will tell my son to repay Mr. Wu. Hanged himself to death.
In the ninth year of Wu You's stay in Jiaodong, he was transferred to the post of Prime Minister of Qi, and General Liang Ji recommended him as Chang Shi.
Later, Liang Ji falsely accused Li Gu, the commander-in-chief, and Wu You heard about it. He went to see Liang Ji and argued for Li Gu, but Liang Ji refused to listen.
At that time, Ma Rong of Fufeng was sitting and writing a memorial for Liang Ji. Wu You said to Ma Rong: Mr. Li's crime was committed by your hands.
If Mr. Li is executed, how can you show your face to the world? Liang Ji got angry and went into the house, but Wu You left without saying goodbye.
Liang Ji appointed Wu You as Prime Minister of Hejian, so he resigned and returned home. He no longer worked as an official. He personally watered the garden vegetables and taught his disciples with scriptures.
Died at the age of ninety-eight.
The eldest son, Wu Feng, was the governor of Lelang; the youngest son, Wu Kai, was the new commander;
◆The biography of Yandu, whose courtesy name is Shujian, was born in Tao, Nanyang County.
When he was young, he learned "Zuo Shi Zhuan" from Tang Xidian in Yingchuan and could recite it in just ten days. Tang Xidian respected him very much.
He also learned from Ma Rong, had extensive knowledge of classics and hundreds of schools of thought, was able to write articles, and was very famous in the capital.
He was elected as Xiaolian and appointed as the Marquis of Pingyang.
When he arrived, he repaired Gong Sui's tomb, erected tomb inscriptions, and selected Gong Sui's descendants to serve as officials in the fields. Because the teacher passed away, he abandoned his official position to attend the funeral, and the five prefectures recruited him, but he failed.
Emperor Huan was recruited by doctors and given the post of Yilang, and he worked on writings in Dongguan with Zhu Mu and Bian Shao.
When he was promoted to minister, Emperor Huan asked him many times about political affairs. He did not tell others the actual situation, and his every move followed the rules and regulations.
He was promoted to Zuo Feng Yi and transferred to Jing Zhaoyin. Advocate for the government to be tolerant and benevolent, and care for the people. Selecting people with moral cultivation to participate in political affairs, the county and the people love each other, and the third assistant praised his political achievements.
In the past, Chen Liubianfeng was a Jingzhaoyin, and he also had a reputation for being capable. People in the county made up a colloquial saying: There are three kings in front of him, Zhao and Zhang, and two kings in the back are Bianyan.
At this time, the prince fell ill and ordered the counties to seek precious medicines. General Liang Ji sent guests with letters to sell bezoars in Jingzhao.
Yan Du opened a letter to arrest the guests, saying: "The general is the empress's maternal wife. The prince is sick and must submit a medical prescription. Should we send the guests thousands of miles to seek profit?"
So he killed the guests. Liang Ji felt ashamed, but he couldn't say that the officials followed Liang Ji's wishes and wanted to cause trouble.
Yandu was dismissed from his post due to illness and returned home, teaching in the alley where he lived to make ends meet.
summary: Later recommended as a Xiaolian, Wu You befriended Huang Zhen at a farewell ceremony, despite criticism for his informal behavior. He became known for his integrity. While serving as an official, he helped the impoverished scholar Gongshamu and befriended the young Dai Hong, who later became a renowned Confucian scholar. As an administrator, Wu You led by example, resolving disputes through moral instruction and personal intervention, which reduced litigation. He showed leniency in cases like Sun Xing, who stole money to buy clothes for his father, and Guanqiu Chang, who killed a man for insulting his mother. Wu You allowed Guanqiu Chang to be with his wife in prison so she could conceive a child before his execution. After serving in Jiaodong, Wu You became Prime Minister of Qi. He later argued for Li Gu against Liang Ji's false accusations, angering Liang Ji. He resigned from his final post as Prime Minister of Hejian, returning home to teach until his death at ninety-eight. Yan Du, courtesy name Shujian, was from Nanyang County. He studied under Tang Xidian and Ma Rong, mastering the classics and gaining fame in the capital. After becoming an official, he repaired Gong Sui's tomb and selected his descendants for office. He abandoned his post to attend his teacher's funeral. Emperor Huan appointed him as Yilang, where he worked on writings in Dongguan. He was promoted to Minister and later to Zuo Feng Yi and Jingzhao Yin, governing with tolerance and benevolence, earning praise from the people. When General Liang Ji sent guests to sell bezoars in Jingzhao, Yan Du arrested and killed them, angering Liang Ji. He was dismissed due to illness and returned home to teach. He wrote a detailed discussion on the relationship between benevolence and filial piety, arguing they share the same origin, with filial piety as the foundation and benevolence as its extension. He declined recommendations for higher office, preferring his scholarly life. Later imprisoned during the party proscriptions, he died at home in the first year of Yongkang. His image was painted in Qu Yuan Temple. He wrote numerous works and made corrections to the scriptures.

translation:
I heard that you wanted to request a return to Dongguan for me. Although you meant a lot, you really didn’t dare to take it seriously.
I usually get up before dawn and wash myself. After washing, I sit in the living room.
In the morning, I read Fu Xi and Wen Wang's "Yi", Yu and Xia's books, the laws and rituals of Gong Dan, and browsed Zhong Ni's "Spring and Autumn".
In the afternoon, I wandered around the inner steps, chanted the Book of Songs in the Nanxuan Hall, and read the books of hundreds of schools of thought in my spare time.
The voice is loud and clear, the ears are full of eloquence, the literary talent is brilliant and the eyes are full of things, and all things are numerous, and I am happy to enjoy it alone.
At this time, I didn’t know that heaven was the cover and the earth was the cover. I didn’t know that there were still people in the world and that I still had a body.
Although Gao Jianli sings while building a building as if no one else is around, Gao Feng reads a book and does not know that it is raining heavily, they are not comparable to me.
Since I was young, I have believed that as a minister, I must not fall into disloyalty; as a son, I must not fall into unfilial piety; when making friends with people whose status is higher than mine, I must not flatter myself; when making friends with those whose status is below me, I must not be contemptuous. If you do this to the point of death and meet your ancestors underground, you will not feel ashamed.
If you don't know how to do good things in this way, I'm afraid it's like teaching Yi to shoot and not being able to use small skills as merit.
You must not lose your roots and abandon what you have created.
Later, he was imprisoned by the party.
In the first year of Yongkang, he died at home.
The villagers painted his image in Qu Yuan Temple.
Yandu made many corrections to the scriptures. Post-Confucianism takes piety as the standard.
He has written a total of twenty poems, treatises, inscriptions, books, responses, tables and teachings.
◆Shi Bi's biography, Shi Bi's courtesy name was Gongqian, and he was a native of Kaocheng County, Chenliu County. His father was Chen Chang. During the reign of Emperor Shun, he was promoted to Shangshu and County Sheriff because of his eloquence and flattery.
Shi Bi was eager to learn when he was young and had hundreds of classmates.
He was appointed as an official in the state and county, recruited into the government, and promoted to the rank of Marquis of the Northern Army.
At this time, Emperor Huan's younger brother Bohai King Kui behaved sinisterly and eccentrically, did not abide by the law, and was arrogant and indulgent.
Shi Bi was afraid that his arrogance would lead to chaos, so he secretly wrote to Emperor Huan, saying: I heard that emperors should use power to show their relatives, even if they are close relatives, and restrain them with laws, even if they are in a noble position.
In this way, harmony will flourish and the kindness of flesh and blood will flourish.
In the past, King Xiang of Zhou indulged his younger brother Gan Zhaogong, and Emperor Xiaojing made King Xiao of Liang arrogant and arrogant. Both of these two younger brothers were doted on, which eventually led to rebellion, the disaster of exile in Zhou, and the assassination of Yuan An in Han.
summary: Shi Bi, courtesy name Gongqian, was from Chenliu County. He was eager to learn and served as an official. Concerned about the misconduct of Emperor Huan's younger brother, Prince Bohai Kui, Shi Bi secretly wrote to the emperor warning of potential rebellion and urging restraint. The emperor did not investigate due to family ties. Later, when Kui was convicted of treason, Shi Bi was promoted to Shangshu and became Pingyuan Prime Minister.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/吴延史卢赵列传

translation:
When Shi Bi was in power, he dealt hard blows to the powerful and bullies, but for the common people, if they committed crimes, he tolerated them and pardoned them.
Shi Bi was promoted to the governor of Hedong, and he was issued an expedient edict to promote filial piety and integrity. Shi Bi knew that many powerful people would seek connections and use the back door, so he ordered in advance to cut off correspondence.
As expected, Hou Lan, the minister in charge of Zhongchang, sent letters to express favors and asked to borrow salt tax, but he was not received for many days.
The person who sent the letter then said that he had other matters to visit Shi Bi, so he gave him Hou Lan's letter.
Shi Bi was furious and said: The governor has an important responsibility and should be elected as a soldier to serve the country. Who are you? It is unbecoming to cheat like this! He ordered the people around him to take him out and beat him with hundreds of blows. More than a dozen people from the government, including the prime minister and the governor, came to the court to persuade him, but Shi Bi ignored him.
He was handed over to Anyi Prison and tortured to death on the same day.
Hou Lan was very resentful, so he forged an urgent edict and sent it to Sili, slandering Shi Bi and slandering the court, and sent him to the court in a prison car.
None of the officials dared to approach him. Only the former Xiaolian Pei Yu was sent between Gu and Mian, and shouted loudly by the side of the road: The Ming Dynasty destroyed the tyrannical ministers and elected virtuous talents to serve the country. If you commit a crime in this way, you can be famous on bamboo and silk. I hope you don't be afraid. Shi Bi said: Who said tea tastes bitter? It is as sweet as shepherd's purse.
In the past, people cut their necks and died without regret. When Xia Tingwei ordered him to be imprisoned, officials from Pingyuan rushed to the court to complain.
Then Wei Xun, a filial and honest man, disfigured his appearance, changed his clothes, pretended to be a family boy, and looked after Shi Bi.
Shi Bi was framed and should abandon the market.
Wei Xun and the people in the same county sold the temple and residence in the county, paid bribes to Hou Lan, and were able to reduce the death penalty by one degree and sent him to Zuoxiao for labor reform. At that time, people ridiculed this matter and said: "Isn't it stupid for Pingyuan to bribe to avoid the king's crime?"
Tao Qiuhong said: Once upon a time, King Wen was imprisoned here by Zhou. Min Yao and San Yi gave birth to gold to Zhou, and Zhou absolved King Wen of his crime. Shi Bi suffered a disaster, and a righteous man offered a treasure because of it. What can be doubted about this!
The scoffers have nothing to say. Shi Bi returned home after serving his sentence and stayed behind closed doors due to illness.
He Xiu was recommended by the ministers many times. He Xiu also praised Shi Bi for his ability to govern the country and that he should be appointed prime minister and was recruited as Yilang.
Hou Lan and his group hated him.
In Guanghezhong, he became the Prime Minister of Pengcheng and died of illness.
Pei Yu ascended to the rank of Minister.
The historian commented: Strong characters are rarely tolerant and tolerant; benevolent and soft people, because they value emotions, mostly lack integrity.
When Wu Jiying sees other people's misfortune, she looks like a Confucian when she speaks with regret. How brave she is when she is jealous, passionate and generous, and destroys power and evil!
Benevolence means loving things, righteousness means retreating from oneself, what a moral person!
As the saying goes: If you save a thousand people, your descendants will be granted official titles. Shi Bi was a strict official, and more than a thousand so-called party members were implicated in the whole plain, and his descendants were declining. This cannot be regarded as a conclusion.
summary: During the party proscriptions, when other counties reported hundreds of party members, Shi Bi alone reported none. When pressured by an inspector, he refused to falsely accuse innocent people, stating he would rather die than do so. The inspector arrested county officials and reported Shi Bi to the court. When the party ban eased, Shi Bi used his salary to atone for over a thousand people. As an official, he harshly punished the powerful but showed leniency to commoners. As Governor of Hedong, he cut off correspondence from powerful families seeking favors. When Hou Lan sent a letter requesting favors, Shi Bi had the messenger beaten to death. Hou Lan retaliated by forging an edict and having Shi Bi arrested. Wei Xun, a former Xiaolian, disfigured himself to care for Shi Bi in prison. Fellow countrymen bribed Hou Lan to reduce Shi Bi's death sentence to labor reform. After serving his sentence, Shi Bi returned home. He was later recruited as Yilang but was hated by Hou Lan's faction. He became Prime Minister of Pengcheng and died of illness.

translation:
◆The biography of Lu Zhi, named Zigan, was a native of Zhuo County, Zhuo County.
He is eight feet two inches long and has a voice like a bell.
When he was young, he was a classmate of Zheng Xuan in Ma Rong. He was well versed in ancient and modern studies, and he liked to study intensively and did not like to carve out chapters and sentences.
Ma Rong belonged to a wealthy family, and in front of the lecture hall there were women singing and dancing. Lu Zhi studied with Ma Rong for several years without turning his eyes, so Ma Rong respected him.
After studying, he returned home and taught behind closed doors.
He has a resolute character and a strong sense of integrity. He often cherishes the ambition of making contributions and makes achievements. He is not good at exchanging gifts and can drink a stone at a time.
At that time, the queen's father, the general Dou Wu, had proclaimed himself Ling Emperor and had just taken charge of the country's confidential affairs. The court was discussing the idea of ​​ennobling Luzhi.
Although Lu Zhi was a commoner, he thought Dou Wu had a good reputation, so he wrote a letter to persuade him: I once heard that widows did not worry about their weft, and girls in lacquered houses leaned on pillars and lamented. What they were worried about was not their own affairs, but they were all worried about the country and thinking deeply. This is the noble and patriotic feeling of a gentleman.
Scholars should have upright friends, in order to discipline each other and prevent themselves from falling into injustice.
"The Book" says to consult with the common people. "Poetry" chants: Ask questions about people who collect firewood.
I, Lu Zhi, have been reading the late king’s books for a long time. How dare I begrudge my unreasonable words?
Now to the Han Dynasty, you are just like Zhou Gongdan and Zhao Gong in the Zhou Dynasty. You established the Holy Lord and had relations with the world. Public opinion considers your contribution and takes it as the most important thing.
The world is looking at you, listening to you with its ears, saying that based on the facts of the past, there will be blessings in scenery.
According to the principle of "Spring and Autumn", if a queen has no children, she should choose the elder among her relatives to be her prince; if they are of the same age, they should choose those with good moral cultivation; if they have the same moral cultivation, then it depends on divination.
Now that the same clan has succeeded him, he wears a pattern ultimatum and establishes it in an orderly manner, what credit does it have?
Is it possible to take credit for one's own strength?
You should resign from the great reward and preserve your reputation.
Moreover, in recent times, if Zuo is not strong enough, he still seeks heirs from outside, which can be said to be dangerous.
There is unrest in all directions, and thieves are taking advantage of the opportunity. Hengyue, Bojie, and thieves are particularly numerous. There may be a rebellion in which the Chu people threaten Zibi, and Zhou Qing and Yin Shili will seize the prince's throne.
We should arrange the official positions of the princes according to ancient rituals, recruit the prince's beloved sons, and recruit the talented people of the clan. We should promote moral education and righteousness externally, stop the greed for power internally, select talented people, and appoint and ennoble them at any time. This is a way to strengthen weak branches.
Dou Wu cannot use it.
The prefecture and county called for orders many times, but Lu Zhi refused to respond.
In Jianning, he was recruited as a doctor and then began to serve as an official.
summary: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Zigan, was from Zhuo County. He studied under Ma Rong alongside Zheng Xuan, mastering ancient and modern learning. He was known for his resolute character and integrity. When Dou Wu was about to be enfeoffed, Lu Zhi wrote advising him to decline the reward and preserve his reputation, but Dou Wu ignored him. Lu Zhi refused multiple calls to office until he was recruited as a doctor. As Prefect of Jiujiang, he pacified barbarian rebellions. He wrote "Shangshu Zhangju" and "Exegesis of the Three Body Problems" and requested to establish academic officials for various classics.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/吴延史卢赵列传

translation:
Lu Zhi knew that Dong Zhuo was vicious and difficult to control and would definitely cause trouble, so he firmly opposed it, but He Jin refused to listen to him.
When Dong Zhuo arrived in the capital, he indeed trampled the imperial court and ignored it. A meeting of hundreds of officials gathered in the court hall to depose the emperor and establish a new one.
No one from the officials came out to say a word, and Lu Zhi alone protested and disapproved.
Dong Zhuo became angry, dissolved the meeting, and prepared to kill Lu Zhi, as mentioned in the "Biography of Dong Zhuo".
Lu Zhi had always been friendly with Cai Yong. Cai Yong was previously exiled to Shuofang, and Lu Zhi alone wrote a letter to appeal for him.
Cai Yong was close to Dong Zhuo at this time, so he went to intercede for Lu Zhi.
He also said to Dong Zhuo, "Lu Shangshu is a great Confucian scholar in the country and is popular among the people. If we kill him first, the whole world will be shocked and frightened."
Dong Zhuocai did not kill him, but only removed Lu Zhi's official position. Lu Zhi asked to go home because he was old and sick. He was afraid that Dong Zhuo would plot against him, so he came out of the village in disguise.
Sure enough, Dong Zhuo sent people to chase him, but he couldn't catch up to him.
Lu Zhi lived in seclusion in Shanggu and did not interact with the world.
Yuan Shao, the shepherd of Jizhou, asked him to be his military advisor.
He died in the third year of Chuping.
When he was about to die, he ordered his son to bury him in a cave without a coffin, only with a single silk cloth attached to his body.
He wrote a total of six steles, edicts, tables and notes.
During the Jian'an period, Cao Cao went to the north to attack Liucheng. When he passed through Zhuo County, he told the guardian: "The late Beizhong Lang General Lu Zhi was famous all over the world. His knowledge was admired by Confucianists. He was a model for intellectuals and a pillar of the country."
Once upon a time, King Wu of Zhou Dynasty entered the Yin Dynasty and granted Shang Rong his residence. When Zheng Guozi was born, Zhongni shed tears for him.
When I come to this state, I like its lingering charm.
According to the great righteousness of "Spring and Autumn", the descendants of sages should be treated with special gifts.
Emergency officials were dispatched to clean the tomb, ask questions about his descendants, and hold memorial ceremonies to commend his virtues. Lu Zhi's son Lu Yu was also famous in his time.
The historian commented: Wind and frost can identify the nature of grass and trees, and when the country is in crisis, the integrity of the country can be revealed. Lu Gong's loyalty is obvious.
Bee stings arose in the arms, and thunder shook around the body. Even though they were brave and powerful, such as Meng Ben, Xia Yu, Jing Ke, and Zhuan Zhu, they did not hesitate to lose their normalcy.
When Lu Zhi drew his white sword under Yan Pavilion, he pursued the emperor in the Hejin area, braved the sword and went to kill him, regardless of life and death, without thinking about anything.
A gentleman's loyalty and righteousness are always consistent and unwavering, no matter in a hurry or emergency or in an extremely difficult and difficult environment.
◆The biography of Zhao Qi, whose courtesy name is Bingqing, was from Changling County, Jingzhao County.
His first name was Zhao Jia, and he was born in Yushitai, so he was given the nickname Taiqing. Later, he took refuge and changed his name to show that he would not forget his homeland.
summary: When the Yellow Turban rebellion arose, Lu Zhi was appointed General and defeated Zhang Jiao, capturing over ten thousand men. When the city was about to fall, he refused to bribe the imperial envoy Zuo Feng, who falsely reported him. Lu Zhi was recalled and sentenced to death, later reduced. After the emperor's death, he opposed summoning Dong Zhuo, warning of his dangerous nature. When Dong Zhuo deposed the emperor, Lu Zhi alone protested. Cai Yong interceded to save Lu Zhi's life, but he was removed from office. He fled in disguise and lived in seclusion until his death. On his deathbed, he ordered a simple burial. Cao Cao later honored his memory.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/吴延史卢赵列传

translation:
When Zhao Qi was young, he was a proficient in Confucian classics and had many talents. He married the daughter of Fufeng Ma Rong's brother.
Ma Rong was a relative of a wealthy family. Zhao Qi despised them and refused to meet Ma Rong. Shizhou County is feared by people for its integrity and evil.
When he was in his thirties, he fell seriously ill and was bedridden for seven years. He thought that he would not survive, so he made a will and told his brother's son: "A man is born in the world and lives in seclusion without the ethics of Xu You. Being an official does not have the merits of Yi Yin and Lu Shang. God has not granted me a long life, so what else can I say!"
You can place a round stone in front of the tomb and engrave a stele saying: There was a hermit in the Han Dynasty whose surname was Zhao Mingjia.
When there is ambition but no time, fate! No way!
Later he recovered from his illness.
In the second year of Yongxing's reign, he was conscripted as Sikong Peng. He suggested that Erqianshi should be removed from office and serve his parents, and the court accepted it.
Later, he was conquered by the general Liang Ji and suggested to Liang Ji a strategy of profit and loss to seek talents, but Liang Ji did not adopt it.
He was recommended to manage the drama and appointed as the chief of the Pi family.
It happened that Liu Lijun, the governor of Hedong, was replaced by Zuo Sheng, the elder brother of Zhongchang Shizuo. Zhao Qi hated eunuchs and thought it was shameful to work with him, so he returned to the west that day.
Jingzhao Yin Yandu once again regarded him as a meritorious officer.
At first, Tang Wangxuan, the elder brother of Tang Heng who served as a regular servant, was appointed as the captain of Huya in Jingzhao. People in the county thought that Tang Wangxuan was appointed the captain of Huya not because of his virtue, so they all despised him and insulted him.
Zhao Qi and his brother Zhao Xi belittled him many times, and Tang Wang Xuan hated him very much.
In the first year of Yanxi, Emperor Xuan of the Tang Dynasty was Zhaoyin of the capital. Zhao Qi was afraid of a disaster, so he ran away with his nephew Zhao Jian.
As expected, Wang Xuan of Tang Dynasty arrested Zhao Qi's family members, framed them for committing serious crimes, and killed them all.
Zhao Qi then fled in all directions, passing through Jiang, Huai, Hai, and Dai, hiding his name and selling cakes in Beihai City.
At this time, Anqiu Sun Song, who was more than 20 years old, saw Zhao Qi while wandering in the city. He thought he was not an ordinary person. He stopped the car and asked Zhao Qi to get in. Zhao Qi's face turned pale with fear. Sun Song then lowered the curtains on the car and ordered the driver to drive away the pedestrians.
He asked Zhao Qi quietly: "Looking at you, you are not a cake seller." He also asked Zhao Qi that your face suddenly changed. You either have a serious grudge or you are a desperado.
I, Beihai Sun Binshi, have a whole family and can help you. Zhao Qi had always heard of Sun Song's reputation, so he told Sun Song the actual situation and went to Sun's house together.
Sun Song first told his mother: When traveling, I gained a good friend. Then he welcomed Zhao Qi to the upper hall and entertained him very cordially.
He hid Zhao Qi in the compound wall for several years, and Zhao Qi wrote twenty-three chapters of "Etun Song".
Later, all the Tang clans died and the imperial court granted amnesty to Zhao Qi.
summary: Zhao Qi, courtesy name Bingqing, was from Jingzhao County. He was proficient in classics but despised his wealthy relative Ma Rong. After a severe seven-year illness, he recovered and served as an official. He hated eunuchs and resigned rather than work with one. When his brother offended a powerful eunuch's relative, Zhao Qi fled, and his family was killed. He hid in Beihai, selling cakes, where Sun Song recognized him as extraordinary and sheltered him for years. During this time, Zhao Qi wrote twenty-three chapters of "Etun Song."
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/吴延史卢赵列传

translation:
When the three mansions heard that Zhao Qi was back, they recruited him at the same time.
Nine years later, he responded to Situ Hu Guang's order.
When the Southern Xiongnu, Wuhuan, and Xianbei rebelled, Zhao Qi was promoted to the governor of Bingzhou.
Zhao Qi wanted to submit a strategy for guarding the frontier, but before he could do so, he was dismissed from office due to party affairs and wrote "On the Control of Bandits".
At the beginning of Emperor Ling's reign, he was imprisoned by the party for more than ten years.
In the first year of Zhongping, troops from all directions rose up, and the imperial edict was issued to select the former governor and those with civil and military talents among the two thousand stones. Zhao Qi was recruited and appointed as Yilang.
Chariot and Cavalry General Zhang Wen marched westward to Guanzhong, and asked Zhao Qi to be appointed as the chief official and to garrison An Ding.
General He Jin appointed Zhao Qi as the governor of Dunhuang. When they arrived at Xiangwu, Zhao Qi and several newly appointed governors of various counties were captured by the thief Bian Zhang and others.
The thief wanted to force Zhao Qi to become the commander, but Zhao Qi used deceit to avoid it and returned to Chang'an.
He presented the emperor to the Western Capital, was appointed Yilang again, and was promoted to imperial servant.
Li Chu took over the dictatorship and sent Taifu Ma Rishidan to appease and comfort the world, with Zhao Qi as his deputy.
Ma Rishi went to Luoyang alone, and did not send Zhao Qi to preach the country's orders. In the counties and counties he went to, the people said happily: "Today I saw the messenger riding on his horse."
At this time, Yuan Shao, Cao Cao and Gongsun Zan were competing for Jizhou. When Yuan Shao and Cao Cao heard that Zhao Qi had arrived, they personally led their troops hundreds of miles away to welcome him. Zhao Qi promoted the emperor's kindness and the principle of withdrawing troops to pacify the people. He also wrote to Gongsun Zan, explaining the pros and cons.
Yuan Shao and others led their troops back, and they all met Zhao Qi in Luoyang to welcome the emperor.
Zhao Qinan came to Chenliu and fell seriously ill. After two years, the date did not show up.
In the first year of Xingping, an imperial edict was issued to recruit Zhao Qi. Just as the emperor was about to return to Luoyang, he first sent General Dong Cheng to repair the palace.
Zhao Qi said to Dong Cheng: Now the country is divided into parts. Only Jingzhou has a large territory and a good local situation. It connects to Bashu in the west and ends in Jiaocheng in the south. It has a good harvest every year and the army's household registration is still intact.
Although I, Zhao Qi, am forced by Li Chu's order, I am determined to serve the country. I want to take an ox cart to the south to tell Liu Biao that he can lead troops to defend the court and work together with the general to assist the royal family.
This is a way to save the people. Dong Cheng sent Zhao Qi to Jingzhou to supervise the grain leasing.
When Zhao Qi arrived, Liu Biao sent troops to Luoyang to help repair the palace, and there was an endless stream of transportation of weapons, food and grass.
At this time, Sun Song was also a guest at Liu Biao's place, but Liu Biao did not treat him politely. Zhao Qi then told Liu Biao that Sun Song had extraordinary virtues, because they were both the governor of Qingzhou.
Zhao Qi stayed in Jingzhou because he was old and sick.
Cao Cao was now Sikong, so he appointed Zhao Qi as Sikong on his behalf.
Guang Luxun Huandian and Shaofu Kong Rong wrote to recommend Zhao Qi, so he appointed Zhao Qi as Taichang.
summary: After amnesty, he served as Governor of Bingzhou but was dismissed due to party affairs. He was imprisoned for over ten years. Later recruited as Yilang, he was captured by bandits but escaped. He served as an imperial envoy, promoting peace among warring factions. He suggested to Dong Cheng that Liu Biao of Jingzhou could support the court, and Liu Biao sent troops and supplies. Zhao Qi stayed in Jingzhou due to old age and illness. He was appointed Taichang and died at over ninety. He prepared his own tomb with paintings of historical figures and himself. He wrote "Mencius Chapters" and "Sanfu Juelu."
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/吴延史卢赵列传

translation:
Wu Hanzi Ziyan was born in Wan County, Nanyang County.
His family was poor and he worked as the county pavilion chief.
In Wang Mang's last years, because his guests broke the law, he took off his name and fled to Yuyang. Due to lack of funds, he made a living by selling horses. He traveled between Yan and Ji, and made friends with heroes wherever he went.
Gengshi ascended the throne and sent envoy Han Hong to Hebei to recruit surrender.
Someone said to Han Hong, "Wu Ziyan is a wonderful man. You can discuss matters with him." Han Hong summoned Wu Han and was very happy. He appointed him as the magistrate of Anle County according to the emperor's order.
Coinciding with the rise of Wang Lang, Beizhou was disturbed and confused.
Wu Han had always heard that Guangwu was an elder, and he wanted to return to Guangwu.
He told the prefect Peng Chong: The cavalry in Yuyang and Shanggu that attack the enemy are famous all over the world.
Why don't you gather the elites from the two counties and join Liu Gong to attack Handan? This is a rare achievement. Peng Chong thought it was right, but the officials below all wanted to join Wang Lang, and Peng Chong could not take away his ambition.
Wu Han then resigned and stayed in the outer pavilion, trying to blackmail everyone, but he still couldn't figure out a way.
Seeing a man who looked like a Confucian scholar on the road, Wu Han sent people to summon him, provided him with food, and asked him what he had heard.
Therefore, Confucian scholars said that wherever Liu Gong went, all counties and counties were devoted to him; the man in Handan who arrogantly claimed the title was indeed not a member of the Liu family.
Wu Han was overjoyed, so he pretended to be a letter written by Guangwu himself, and sent it to Yuyang. He sent a Confucian scholar to Peng Chong and asked him to convince Peng Chong of what he had heard. Wu Han also followed him to Yuyang.
Peng Chong was very satisfied.
So Wu Han was sent to lead his troops and the generals from Shanggu to the south, killing General Wang Lang wherever they went.
After chasing Guangwu in Guang'a, he worshiped Wu Han as a partial general.
After conquering Handan, he was given the title of Marquis Jiance.
Wu Han was a man of loyal nature but lacked literary talent and could not express his thoughts in words in a hurry.
Deng Yu and other generals knew him well and recommended him many times. When he was summoned, Guangwu trusted him and often lived under his door.
General Guang sent troops to Youzhou and summoned Deng Yu at night to ask who could take on the task.
Deng Yu said: I have talked with Wu Han many times. He is brave and resourceful. Few generals can match him. That is to say, Wu Han was appointed as the general and ordered to carry the talisman to the north to attack the enemy's cavalry from ten counties.
Gengshi Youzhou Mu Miao once heard that he secretly mobilized troops and ordered the counties not to send troops accordingly.
Wu Han led twenty horses and galloped to the end.
Miao Zeng thought that Wu Han was unprepared and came out to meet him on the road. Wu Han immediately commanded his troops and cavalry to capture Miao Zeng and kill him, seizing his troops and horses.
Beizhou was shaken and frightened, and all the cities and towns obeyed.
So he mobilized all his troops and led them southward to join forces with Guangwu at Qingyang.
When the generals saw Wu Han coming back and his troops were very strong, they all said: "Is he willing to divide his troops with others?" When Wu Han arrived at the place where the general was conducting business, he presented the name list of the sergeants, and the generals invited everyone to accept their troops.
Guangwu said: "I'm afraid he was unwilling to accept requests from others before. Why are there so many requests now?" All the generals felt ashamed.
At first, Gengshi sent Shangshu Ling Xie Gong and six generals to attack Wanglang, but they could not capture it.
summary: Wu Han, courtesy name Ziyan, was born into poverty in Wan County, Nanyang County, and served as a county pavilion chief. During Wang Mang's final years, he fled to Yuyang after his guests broke the law, supporting himself by selling horses and befriending heroes throughout Yan and Ji regions. When Gengshi ascended the throne, envoy Han Hong appointed Wu Han as magistrate of Anle County. During Wang Lang's uprising, Wu Han sought to join Guangwu, attempting to persuade Prefect Peng Chong to ally with Guangwu against Handan. When officials favored Wang Lang, Wu Han fabricated a letter from Guangwu and sent a Confucian scholar to convince Peng Chong, who ultimately agreed. Wu Han led troops south, killing Wang Lang's generals, and after pursuing Guangwu to Guang'a, was appointed partial general. Following the conquest of Handan, he was made Marquis Jiance. Wu Han was loyal but lacked literary talent. Deng Yu recommended him, and Guangwu trusted him deeply. When Guangwu needed a general for Youzhou, Deng Yu praised Wu Han's bravery and resourcefulness. Wu Han was appointed general and sent north with a talisman to mobilize troops from ten counties. When Gengshi's Youzhou governor Miao Zeng refused to comply, Wu Han captured and killed him, seizing his troops. All cities in Beizhou submitted. Wu Han then led his forces south to join Guangwu at Qingyang, presenting the roster of his troops to Guangwu, which shamed other generals who had doubted his willingness to share command.

translation:
Just as Guangwu arrived, they jointly pacified Handan, but Xie Gongbi looted and looted without asking for instructions to report, which Guangwu hated deeply.
Although they are both in Handan, they live in separate cities, but they often comfort him.
Xie Gong was diligent in his duties, and Guangwu often praised him and said: "Xie Shangshu is a real official." So I don’t doubt myself.
Xie Gong then led tens of thousands of his troops and returned to Ye.
At that time, Guang Wunan attacked Qingdu and said to Xie Gong: I will chase the thieves and shoot the dogs, and I will definitely defeat the thieves.
Anyone who comes to Shanyang will definitely be frightened away.
If you use your power to attack these scattered captives, you will definitely win. Xie Gong said: OK. When Qingdu was defeated, You Lai walked north to Longlu Mountain. After thanking him, he left the general Liu Qing and the governor of Wei County Chen Kang to guard Ye, while he led the generals to attack Qingdu.
The poor bandits fought hard, but their sharpness was unstoppable. Xie Gong was defeated and thousands of people died.
Since Guangwu was out of town, he sent Wu Han and Cen Peng to attack the city.
The Wu Han Dynasty sent debaters in advance to persuade Chen Kang: I heard that a wise person does not seek luck in danger, a moderately wise person can take advantage of danger as a merit, and a foolish person lives in danger as a means of self-destruction.
The arrival of danger is caused by human beings and cannot be ignored.
Now the capital is in chaos, and there are disturbances in all directions, and you know that.
King Xiao's soldiers were strong, and Hebei was under his command. This was seen by the public.
It is known to everyone that Xie Gong betrayed King Xiao internally and lost the hearts of the people externally.
The Duke is now guarding the isolated city, waiting for the disaster of destruction. There is no loyalty and integrity, and no integrity. It is better to open the door to welcome the Han soldiers, turn disaster into blessing, avoid the defeat of foolishness, and gain the merit of wisdom. This is the best plan!
Chen Kang thought so. So Chen Kang took Liu Qing and Xie Gong's wife and opened the door to welcome the Han soldiers into the city.
When Xie Gong returned to Ye from Longlu, he didn't know that Chen Kang had rebelled, so he entered the city lightly with hundreds of cavalry.
Han ambushes captured him and killed Xie Gong with his hands. All his troops surrendered.
Xie Gong, courtesy name Zizhang, was from Nanyang County.
At first, his wife knew that Guangwu could not live in harmony with him, so she often warned Xie Gong and said: You and Liu Gong are not harmonious together, but you believe his lies and make no preparations, and you will eventually be controlled by him. Xie Gong refused to accept it, so he suffered.
When Guangwu attacked groups of thieves in the north, Wu Han often led five thousand assault cavalry as the vanguard and attacked the bandits several times.
When Hebei was pacified, Wu Han and his generals held maps and books and paid tribute to the emperor.
Guangwu ascended the throne, worshiped Wu Han as Grand Sima, and was granted the title of Marquis of Wuyang.
summary: When Xie Gong, a Gengshi official, occupied Handan with his troops, Guangwu outwardly praised him while secretly planning against him. After Xie Gong was defeated by bandits at Qingdu, Guangwu sent Wu Han and Cen Peng to attack Ye. Wu Han sent debaters to persuade Chen Kang, the Wei county governor, to surrender, which he did, opening the gates to Han forces. When Xie Gong returned, he was captured and killed. Guangwu later attacked bandits in the north with Wu Han leading five thousand assault cavalry as vanguard. After Hebei was pacified, Guangwu ascended the throne and appointed Wu Han Grand Sima, granting him the title Marquis of Wuyang.

translation:
In the spring of the second year of Jianwu, Wu Han led the general Wang Liang, the general Zhu You of Jianyi, the general Du Mao, the Jin Wu Jiafu, the Yanghua general Jian Tan, the partial general Wang Ba, the cavalry captain Liu Long, Ma Wu, and Yinshi. They attacked the Tanxiang bandits on the Zhang River in the east of Ye. They defeated the bandits and more than 100,000 people surrendered.
The emperor sent envoys to seal Wu Han as the Marquis of Guangping, with four counties in total: Guangping, Kuizhang, Quzhou and Guangnian.
Wu Han again led his generals to attack the bandits Li Boxing and others in the western mountains of Ye, and pursued them to Hanoi Wu, where they defeated all the bandits' gatherings.
Guangwu personally came to express his condolences.
Wu Han was sent back to march into Nanyang County, attack Wan, Nie, Yang, Li, Rang and Xinye cities, and captured them all.
He led his troops to the south, fought with Qin Feng on the Huangyou River, and defeated Qin Feng.
He and the partial general Feng Yi attacked Zhang Wen and others on the fifth floor of Changcheng. They also attacked Bronze Horse and Five Flags in Xin'an, and defeated them all.
In the spring of the next year, Wu Han led Jianwei General Geng Yan and Huya General Gai Yan to attack Qingdu in the west of Zhejiang, defeating him and forcing him to surrender.
He also led the hussar general Du Mao, the strong crossbow general Chen Jun and others to surround Su Mao in Guangle.
Liu Yong recruited Zhou Jian and gathered more than 100,000 people to rescue Guangle.
Wu Han sent Qingqi to fight with him, but was unfavorable. He fell from his horse and injured his knee. When he returned to camp, Zhou Jian led his troops into the city.
The generals said to Wu Han: The enemy is in front, but the Duke is lying down due to his wounds, and everyone is afraid. Wu Hannai became angry, changed his color, wrapped up his knee wound, and rose up, killing cattle and feasting on the soldiers. He ordered the army to say: Although there are many thieves, they are just a group of robbers. When they win, they will not give in, and when they lose, they will not save each other. They are not loyal and willing to die for righteousness.
Today is a good opportunity to make meritorious deeds and become a lord, please give me more encouragement. The sergeant was enraged and his morale doubled.
Early in the morning, Zhou Jian and Su Mao sent troops to surround Wu Han.
Wu Han selected four elite soldiers, including Huangtou Wu He and others, as well as more than 3,000 Wuhuan cavalry, and advanced together with great noise.
Zhou Jianjun was defeated and ran back to the city.
Wu Han pursued them with a long drive, fought for the gate and entered with all their strength, and greatly defeated Jian and Mao's army. Su Mao and Zhou Jian broke through and left.
Wu Han left Du Mao, Chen Jun and others to guard Guangle, and led his own troops to help Gai Yan encircle Liu Yong in Suiyang.
After Liu Yong's death, both cities surrendered.
In the third year, he led Chen Jun and former general Wang Liang to defeat the bandits from the five schools in Linping, chased them to Jishan in Dongjun, and defeated the bandit army.
Then he attacked the Qinghe River and five miles north of the plain and defeated the bandits.
At that time, the five surnames in Li County jointly expelled the warden and occupied the county seat.
The generals were vying to attack, but Wu Han refused to listen and said: "Whoever caused Ge to rebel is the fault of the guard."
summary: In subsequent campaigns, Wu Han defeated the Tanxiang bandits, earning the title Marquis of Guangping. He conquered multiple cities in Nanyang County and defeated Qin Feng. He fought alongside Geng Yan and Gai Yan against Qingdu, forcing his surrender. During the siege of Guangle, Wu Han was wounded but rallied his troops, defeating Zhou Jian and Su Mao's forces. He later helped besiege Liu Yong in Suiyang, and after Liu Yong's death, both cities surrendered. Wu Han continued defeating bandits across multiple regions, including Linping, Dongjun, Qinghe, and Pingyuan. He pacified Li County by diplomatic means, convincing the five surnames to surrender without battle.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/吴盖陈臧列传

translation:
Anyone who dares to risk rashly and enter the army should be killed. Then he sent a notice to the county and asked them to arrest the chief guard and make people express their gratitude to the city.
The five surnames were overjoyed and led their people to surrender one after another.
The generals were convinced and said: "It is not possible for others to surrender the whole city without fighting."
In the winter, Wu Han led Jianwei General Geng Yan, Hanzhong General Wang Chang and others to attack Fuping and capture two thieves in the plain.
In the spring of the fourth year, the thieves led more than 50,000 people to attack the Han camp at night. The army was in panic, but Wu Han stood firm. It took a while for the army to calm down.
Then he sent elite soldiers out of the camp at night to attack and defeated his tribe.
Therefore, they further attacked the remnants of the party, entered Wuyan County, and attacked Bohai, but they were all put down.
He also attacked Dong Xian and besieged Qucheng. In the spring of the fifth year, Qu City was captured. Kill Dong Xian. Dongfang was all pacified, and the troops were reorganized and returned to the capital.
Coincidentally, Wei Xiao rebelled, and Xia sent Wu Han to the west to garrison Chang'an.
In the eighth year of Jianwu's reign, he followed Guangwu to Longlong and besieged Weixiao in Xicheng.
The emperor ordered Wu Han: "The soldiers in each county are wasting food. If they flee, they will be depressed and demoralized, so they should all be dismissed." Wu Han and others were greedy to use these people to attack Wei Xiao together, so they refused to send them away. As a result, the food supply was gradually reduced, the officials and soldiers were tired of hard work, and more people fled. When Gongsun Shu's troops arrived to rescue Wei Xiao, Wu Han was defeated.
In the spring of the 11th year of Jianwu's reign, he led the southern general Cen Peng and others to attack Gongsun Shu.
When Cen Peng broke through Jingmen and drove into Jiangguan, Wu Han stayed in Yiling, built short ships, and carried 30,000 Nanyang soldiers and recruited prisoners who had been released from shackles up the river.
When Cen Peng was killed by an assassin, Wu Han also led his army.
In the spring of the twelfth year of Jianwu's reign, he fought with Gongsun Shu's generals Wei Dang and Gongsun Yong in Yufujin and defeated his army, so he besieged Wuyang.
Gongsun Shu sent his son-in-law Shi Xing to lead five thousand people to rescue him.
Wu Han attacked Shi Xing and wiped out all his troops, thus entering the territory of Qianwei.
All counties guarded the city.
Wu Han then marched to Guangdu and captured it.
Qingqi was sent to burn the Chengdu city bridge, and all the small towns east of Wuyang surrendered.
Guangwu warned Wu Han: Chengdu has more than 100,000 troops and should not be underestimated.
Just hold Guangdu firmly and don't fight with them when they come to attack.
If they dare not attack, the public camp forces them to fight, and they must wait until they are exhausted before they can attack. Taking advantage of the victory, Wu Han advanced to Chengdu with more than 20,000 troops on foot and cavalry. He was more than ten miles away from the city. He established a camp at the dangerous point in the north of the Yangtze River and built a pontoon bridge. He sent his deputy general Wuwei General Liu Shang to lead more than 10,000 men to garrison in the south of the Yangtze River. The two camps were more than 20 miles apart.
The emperor was shocked when he heard the news and blamed Wu Han: "I have always given many orders to you, why did things go wrong again?"
summary: When Wei Xiao rebelled, Wu Han garrisoned Chang'an. In the eighth year of Jianwu, he disobeyed Guangwu's order to dismiss troops, leading to defeat when Gongsun Shu's forces arrived. In the eleventh year, Wu Han led forces against Gongsun Shu. After Cen Peng's assassination, Wu Han took command. Despite Guangwu's warnings, Wu Han advanced recklessly toward Chengdu, establishing two camps separated by twenty miles. When Gongsun Shu's forces attacked, Wu Han was defeated and surrounded. He secretly joined forces with Liu Shang in Jiangnan, defeated the Shu army, killing Xie Feng and Yuan Ji. After eight consecutive victories, Wu Han's forces killed Gongsun Shu in battle, and Chengdu surrendered.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/吴盖陈臧列传

translation:
Therefore, he can hold important positions permanently and spend his whole life with fame.

summary: In the Biography of the Eight Kings of Xiaoming, Emperor Xiaoming had nine sons, including Jia Gui, who became Emperor Zhang, and Yin Gui, who became Emperor Liu Chang of Liangjie. Liu Jian, the Qiancheng Ai King, was granted his title in the third year of Yongping but died the following year without sons, leading to the dissolution of his kingdom. Liu Xian, Chen Jing Wang, was initially made Guangping King in the third year of Yongping. In the third year of Jianchu, he was ordered to his fiefdom, but Suzong, unable to bear separation, kept him in the capital. Later, his title changed to Xiping King, and after the emperor's death, a posthumous edict made him King Chen. He died at age 37, succeeded by his son Liu Jun. Liu Gong, King Jing of Pengcheng, was titled King Lingshou in the ninth year of Yongping, later becoming Julu King, then Jiangling King, and finally Liu'an King before being posthumously made King Pengcheng. He was dignified and respected. In the sixth year of Yongchu, his son Anu was made a marquis. In the third year of the Yuan Dynasty, Liu Gong's son Liu Youfu committed suicide after angering him. Zhao Mu, the Prime Minister, falsely accused Liu Gong of treason, but an investigation cleared him, and Zhao Mu was imprisoned. Liu Gong died at 46, succeeded by his son Liu Daosi.
