translation:
When the emperor died, he went to the fief in the same year.
Liu Dang immediately disobeyed the law.
According to the old rules, palace people were prohibited from getting married and were not allowed to go to the fiefdom.
Ai Zhi, a skilled man from the old Yeting, married a man named Zhang Chu. Liu Dang summoned Ai Zhi to the palace and committed adultery with him. Zhang Chu wanted to write a letter to accuse him, but Liu Dang was afraid, so he secretly bribed Ai Zhi's sister Jiao to kill Zhang Chu. When the matter was discovered, Liu Dang hanged three eunuchs to silence him.
Liu Dangli died in the twenty-fifth year of his reign, and his son Liu Chongsi, the king of mourning, died.
Liu Yan, King of Xia Pi Hui, was granted the title in the 15th year of Yongping.
Liu Yan had good looks, and Suzong was always at his side when he came to the throne.
In the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Liu Yanggang held a crown ceremony and issued an imperial edict to Master Liu Yan with the following official items: gold, silk and other items, each with its own distinction.
In the third year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, a total of 17 counties including Linhuai County and Jiujiang's Zhongli, Dangtu, Dongcheng, Liyin and Quanjiao counties were added to the Xiapi Kingdom.
After the emperor died, he went to the fiefdom that year.
Later, Liu Yan had a heart problem, and Prince Liu was convicted and deposed. The concubines vied with each other to establish a son as their heir, and even wrote letters to tell each other.
Emperor He took pity on them and sent Liu Gong, King Jing of Pengcheng, to Xiapi to rectify his concubines and make his son Liu the crown prince. Liu Yanli died in the fifty-fourth year of his reign, and his son Liu Chengsi, King Zhen.
Liu Chang, the king of Liangjie, was named the king of Runan in the 15th year of Yongping.
The nobles in the maternal yin favored the emperor, and Liu Chang was especially favored. The rent of the land was double that of other countries.
When Suzong came to the throne, he followed the wishes of the late emperor and rewarded him with generous favors.
In the second year of Jianchu's reign, Liu Chang's uncle Yin Tang was granted the title of Marquis of Xiling.
In the fourth year, he moved to the throne of Liang and added six counties including Chenliu, Ningling, Jiyinzhibo, Shanfu, Jishi and Chengwu to the Liang fiefdom.
After the emperor died, he went to the fiefdom that year.
Liu Chang is intelligent and kind, but he is a arrogant young man and does not follow the rules very well.
After arriving in the fiefdom, he had nightmares many times. Bian Ji, an official, said that he could use Liu Ding to divine dreams, so Liu Chang asked him to use divination tools several times.
Liu Chang's wet nurse Wang Li and others also used this to say that they could see ghosts and gods, so they worked together to fortune-telling and offered sacrifices in the temple to pray for blessings.
Bian Ji and others flattered Liu Chang and said that King Shenyan should be the emperor.
Liu Chang was delighted and answered with them.
In the ninth year of Yongyuan, Liang Xiangju, the governor of Yuzhou, reported Liu Chang's rebellion and rebellion. He refused to accept his resignation when questioned.
Some officials requested that Liu Chang be summoned to be imprisoned by Tingwei, but He Di disagreed.
Yousi also reported that Liu Chang was exempted from the fiefdom and moved to Jiuzhen. The emperor couldn't bear it and only cut off Chengwu and Shanfu counties.
Liu Chang was ashamed and frightened, so he thanked me and said: "I am crazy and stupid by nature. I was born in a deep palace and grew up in the hands of my mother. I believe what I say."
summary: Liu Dang, the successful king of Jing, was titled King Chongxi in the ninth year of Yongping. He was intelligent and close to Suzong. After the emperor's death, he went to his fiefdom but broke the law by committing adultery with a palace woman named Ai Zhi and covering up the murder of her husband. He died at 25, succeeded by his son Liu Chongsi. Liu Yan, King of Xia Pi Hui, was granted his title in the 15th year of Yongping. He had good looks and was often with Suzong. After the emperor's death, he went to his fiefdom. He later had heart problems, and his concubines fought over succession. Emperor He sent Liu Gong to resolve the matter. Liu Yan died at 54, succeeded by his son Liu Chengsi. Liu Chang, the king of Liangjie, was made King of Runan in the 15th year of Yongping and was especially favored. He moved to Liang and added counties to his fiefdom. Intelligent but arrogant, he engaged in divination and was flattered by officials who said he should be emperor. In the ninth year of Yongyuan, he was reported for rebellion. The emperor spared him, only cutting off two counties. Liu Chang wrote a remorseful letter, offering to return lands and servants. The emperor refused his resignations. Liu Chang died at 27, succeeded by his son Liu Jian.

translation:
Liu Ribing, the king of Qing in Huaiyang, was granted the title of King of Changshan in the 15th year of Yongping. In the fourth year of Jianchu's reign, he moved to the throne of Huaiyang and added Xin'an and Xihua in Runan to the Huaiyin Kingdom. He died sixteen years after he was established, before he could have an heir.
Liu Chang, the mourning king of Jiyin, was granted the title in the fifteenth year of Yongping.
In the fourth year of Jianchu, Lihu of Dongjun and Changyuan of Chenliu were added to Jiyin Kingdom.
Thirteen years after he was established, he died in the capital, childless, and his fiefdom was abolished.
summary: Liu Ribing, the king of Qing in Huaiyang, was made King of Changshan in the 15th year of Yongping, later moving to Huaiyang. He died 16 years after his establishment without an heir. Liu Chang, the mourning king of Jiyin, was granted his title in the 15th year of Yongping and died 13 years later in the capital without children, leading to the abolition of his fiefdom.

translation:
◆Biography of Qi Wu King Liu Yan Qi Wu King Liu Yan, courtesy name Bosheng, was Guangwu's eldest brother.
He has a resolute character, is generous and generous.
Since Wang Mang usurped the Han Dynasty, he has always been filled with anger and indignation. With the long-term plan of restoring the Han Dynasty and the country, he did not engage in managing the family property, but used his family property to make friends with the heroes of the world.
In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, thieves and thieves arose, especially in the south. Bo Sheng summoned all the heroes to discuss matters: Wang Mang was tyrannical and the people were falling apart.
Now there have been droughts for many years and wars and revolutions have occurred.
This is also the time when King Mang died in heaven, and it was a good opportunity to restore the emperor's imperial legacy and determine the future for eternity. Everyone thought it was right.
So they sent relatives and guests respectively, so that Deng Chen raised troops in Xinye, and Guangwu, Li Tong, and Li Yi raised troops in Wan.
Bo Sheng personally mobilized the disciples of Chongling, a total of seven to eight thousand people, and arranged guests, calling themselves the Zhutiandu tribe.
The clan member Liu Jia was sent to lure Xinshi and Pinglin soldiers Wang Kuang, Chen Mu and others. They joined forces and advanced, massacred Changju and Tangzixiang, killed Huyang Wei, marched to capture Jiyang, and took advantage of the situation to attack Wan.
Arriving at Xiaochang'an, he fought with Zhen Fu, an officer of Wang Mang's front team, and Qiuci, who belonged to Zhengliang.
It was a dense fog at that time, and the Han army was defeated. My sister Liu Yuan and my brother Liu Zhong were killed. Dozens of people in the clan died following the uprising.
Bo Sheng then gathered the troops and returned to Jiyang to defend himself.
Zhenfu and Liangqiu took advantage of the victory and left their baggage in Lanxiang. They led one hundred thousand elite troops to cross the Huangchun River southward, close to the Pubi River. They established a camp between the two rivers and removed the bridge behind them to show that they would never retreat.
When the soldiers from Xinshi and Pinglin saw that the Han soldiers had suffered several defeats, and the armies of Zhenfu and Liangqiuci were approaching, they all wanted to disperse and leave. Bo Sheng was very worried.
It happened that more than 5,000 soldiers from Xiajiang arrived in Yiqiu, so they went to explain the situation of joint operations to them, and the soldiers from Xiajiang agreed.
Bo Sheng's words to convince Jiang Bing were recorded in "Wang Chang Zhuan".
Bo Sheng then held a banquet for the sergeants and established an alliance.
Let the soldiers rest for three days, divide them into six groups, secretly raise their troops at night, attack and capture Lanxiang, and seize all the baggage.
Early the next morning, the Han army attacked Zhenfu from the southwest, and the soldiers from Xiajiang attacked Liangqiuci from the southeast.
When it was time to eat, Liangqiu Ci's army was defeated. Seeing that Zhenfu's army was fleeing, the Han soldiers rushed to pursue it. The Fu army retreated and was blocked by the Huangchun River. More than 20,000 people were beheaded and drowned, so Zhenfu and Liangqiu Ci were beheaded.
Wang Mang's general Yan You and Zhizong's general Chen Mao heard that Zhenfu and Liangqiu Ci's armies were defeated and prepared to defend Wancheng.
Bo Sheng swore an oath to Chen Bing, burned the accumulated supplies, broke the cooking cauldron, beat drums and advanced. He met Yan You and Chen Mao in Yuyang, fought, defeated their army, and beheaded more than 3,000 people.
Yan You and Chen Mao abandoned their troops and fled, so Bo Sheng surrounded Wancheng and named himself General Zhutian.
Wang Mang was greatly shocked and frightened when he heard about Bo Sheng's fame. He offered a reward of 50,000 households, 100,000 jins of gold, and the title of Grand Duke to anyone who could kill Bo Sheng.
He made the official offices in Chang'an City and the rural pavilions all over the world paint Bo Sheng's image on the side hall of the door, and got up early to shoot the image with arrows.
Since the death of Zhen Fu and Liang Qiu Ci, people have come to surrender every day, up to more than 100,000 people.
The generals held a meeting to discuss establishing the Liu family in order to comply with everyone's expectations, and the heroes all focused on Bo Sheng. However, the generals of Xinshi and Pinglin were willing to indulge, fearing Bo Sheng's majesty and wisdom and liking Sheng Gong's cowardice, so they jointly planned to establish Sheng Gong in advance, and then sent people to summon Bo Sheng to announce the results of their discussion.
summary: **Qi Wu King Liu Yan (Bosheng)** was the eldest brother of Emperor Guangwu. Resolute and generous, he was angered by Wang Mang's usurpation of the Han dynasty and used his family wealth to befriend heroes, planning to restore the Han. During the chaos of Wang Mang's final years, Bosheng gathered heroes and raised troops with relatives and guests, including Deng Chen in Xinye and Guangwu, Li Tong, and Li Yi in Wan. He mobilized 7,000–8,000 disciples from Chongling, calling them the Zhutiandu tribe. After allying with Xinshi and Pinglin soldiers, they captured several locations and attacked Wan. At Xiaochang'an, they were defeated by Wang Mang's officers Zhen Fu and Liangqiu Ci in dense fog, resulting in the deaths of Bosheng's sister Liu Yuan and brother Liu Zhong. Bosheng regrouped at Jiyang. The enemy forces, with 100,000 elite troops, camped between the Huangchun and Pubi Rivers, removing their bridge to show no retreat. Xinshi and Pinglin soldiers wanted to disperse, but Bosheng convinced 5,000 arriving Xiajiang soldiers to join forces. After a three-day rest, they secretly attacked and captured Lanxiang, seizing enemy baggage. The next morning, the Han army attacked from the southwest and Xiajiang from the southeast, defeating Liangqiu Ci's army. Zhenfu's army fled but was blocked by the Huangchun River; over 20,000 were killed or drowned, and Zhenfu and Liangqiu Ci were beheaded. Bosheng then defeated Yan You and Chen Mao at Yuyang, beheading over 3,000, and besieged Wancheng, naming himself General Zhutian. Wang Mang offered a huge reward for Bosheng's death and had his image painted for archery practice. Over 100,000 people surrendered daily. When generals discussed establishing a Liu clan leader, they favored Bosheng but feared his strictness and preferred Sheng Gong (Gengshi), whom they established. Bosheng warned against premature enthronement, citing Chen Sheng and Xiang Ji as examples, and suggested waiting until after defeating Wang Mang and dealing with Chimei. Most agreed, but General Zhang drew his sword and forced the decision. Sheng Gong was enthroned, and Bosheng was made Grand Situ and Marquis of Han Xin, disappointing many heroes. After attacking Xinye and Bawan, Guangwu defeated Wang Xun and Wang Yi, increasing the brothers' fame. Gengshi and his ministers, feeling uneasy, conspired to kill Bosheng. Despite a warning from his uncle Fan Hong about a possible plot, Bosheng dismissed it. Li Yi, whom Guangwu had warned Bosheng against, and others persuaded Gengshi to arrest and kill Bosheng and his general Liu Ji on the same day. Bosheng's sons were later made kings by Guangwu.

translation:
Gengshi and the generals arranged thousands of troops to arrest Liu Ji first and were about to kill him. Bo Sheng firmly argued against it.
Li Yi and Zhu Kun persuaded Gengshi to arrest Bo Sheng at the same time. He was killed on the same day.
Bo Sheng had two sons. In the second year of Jianwu, Guangwu established Bo Sheng's eldest son Liu Zhang as King of Taiyuan, and his second son Liu Xing as King of Lu.
In the eleventh year of Jianwu, Liu Zhang was moved to the throne of Qi. In the fifteenth year of Jianwu's reign, his posthumous uncle was promoted to King Wu of Qi.
◆Beihai Jing Wang Liu Xing passed the throne to Beihai Jing Wang Liu Xing, who was named King of Lu in the second year of Jianwu and succeeded Guangwu's brother Liu Zhong.
At first, Lord Nanton married all the daughters of Fan Zhong from the same county.
All women have a docile temperament. Ever since she was a virgin, she has never dressed up or left the boudoir. She is respected and loved by the entire clan.
They gave birth to three sons and three daughters: the eldest son Bosheng, the second son Zhong, and the third son Guangwu; the eldest daughter Liu Huang, the second daughter Liu Yuan, and the third daughter Boji.
The emperor's concubine, Nvjiandu, died of illness when Bo Sheng's brothers first launched their army. Fan Jugong, a member of Fan Nvjiandu's tribe, buried her.
In the second year of Jianwu, Liu Huang was granted the title of eldest princess of Huyang, and Boji was granted the title of eldest princess of Shouping.
Both Liu Yuan and Liu Zhong died in Xiaochang'an, and Liu Yuanjue was given the title of Princess Xinye. In the fifteenth year of Jianwu's reign, Liu Zhong was posthumously named King of Lu Ai.
Liu Xing was tried as the magistrate of Fengshi County that year.
He is a wise and strategic man, good at handling lawsuits, and has a good reputation.
Later he was promoted to the prefect of Hongnong, and he also had good governance.
After serving for four years, he petitioned for resignation and was recalled to the capital to attend the court meeting.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu's reign, he returned to his country.
Next year, Yi Lu rented more than Donghai, so he moved Liu Xing to be the king of Beihai.
In the 30th year, Liu Xing's son Liu Fu was granted the title of Marquis of Linyi.
In the second year of Zhongyuan, Liu Xing's two sons were granted the title of county marquis.
Emperor Xianzong attached great importance to Liu Xing. Whenever he encountered major political issues, he often passed documents to Liu Xing for consultation.
He died in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, and was succeeded by King Zijing Liu Mu.
◆Biography of Zhao Xiaowang Liu Liang Zhao Xiaowang Liu Liang was named Cibo and the uncle of Emperor Guangwu.
During the reign of Emperor Ping, he was promoted to Xiaolian and became the magistrate of Xiao County.
Brother Guangwu lost his father when he was young, and Liu Liang took good care of him.
When Guangwu raised his troops and told Liu Liang what had happened, Liu Liang was furious and said: "You and Bo Sheng have different ambitions and ethics. Do you want your family to be in danger now?" Instead, they conspired to raise an army! Later, as a last resort, he joined the army and went to Xiaochang'an. The Han army was defeated and Liu Liang's wife and two sons were killed.
When Gengshi came to the throne, he made Liu Liang the third elder of the country and followed him into the pass.
summary: **Beihai Jing Wang Liu Xing** was named King of Lu in the second year of Jianwu, succeeding Guangwu's brother Liu Zhong. His mother, Lady Nanton, was gentle and respected, giving birth to three sons (Bosheng, Zhong, Guangwu) and three daughters (Liu Huang, Liu Yuan, Boji). She died of illness when Bosheng's brothers first raised troops. Liu Xing served as magistrate of Fengshi County, known for wisdom and good governance, later becoming prefect of Hongnong. After four years, he resigned and was recalled to court. In the 27th year of Jianwu, he returned to his state. The next year, he was moved to be King of Beihai. Emperor Xianzong valued him and consulted him on major issues. He died after 39 years of reign. **Zhao Xiaowang Liu Liang** was Guangwu's uncle. During Emperor Ping's reign, he became magistrate of Xiao County. He cared for the young Guangwu after his father's death. When Guangwu raised troops, Liu Liang was initially furious but later joined the army. At Xiaochang'an, his wife and two sons were killed. Gengshi made him the third elder of the state. After Gengshi's failure, Liu Liang fled to Luoyang upon hearing Guangwu's enthronement. He was made King of Guangyang in the second year of Jianwu, moved to Zhao Wang in the fifth year, demoted to Duke Zhao in the 13th year, and died in the capital in the 17th year after 16 years of reign.

translation:
When Guangwu raised his army and Liu Zhi's brothers led the army, Zhen Fu, the senior official of the front army, imprisoned all his family members in prison.
When the Han soldiers failed in Xiao Chang'an and Liu Zhi came back to protect Jiyang, Zhen Fu killed Liu Zhi's mother, brother, and wives.
Gengshi ascended the throne, and Liu Zhi was appointed Taichang General and succeeded Chonglinghou.
He followed him into the pass and was named King of Dingtao.
He also led his troops to defeat Liu Ying in Linjing.
When the revolution came to Chimei, Liu Zhi fled to Luoyang via a small road.
At this time, only Liu Zhi of the clan arrived first, and Guangwu was very happy when he saw it.
In the second year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of King of Chengyang and was given a carriage, royal objects, carriages, horses, and clothes.
Liu Chang was posthumously named Marquis of Kang.
In the eleventh year of Jianwu's reign, Liu Zhi fell ill and offered the seal and ribbon of King Chengyang, hoping that the princes would offer sacrifices to his ancestors.
Emperor Guangwu personally visited his illness. Liu Zhi died at the age of forty-three, with the posthumous title of Prince Gong. He was buried in Beimang, Luoyang, before he could return to his fiefdom.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, Liu Ping, Liu Zhi's legitimate son, was granted the title of Marquis of Caiyang to worship Liu Zhi; Liu Ping's younger brother Liu Jian was granted the title of Marquis of Gaoxiang.
◆Biography of Liu She, King of Sishui
Liu She, the king of Sishui, was the grandson of Emperor Guangwu.
Liu She's son Liu Zhong and Guangwu had been close to each other since childhood.
The rise of Han soldiers began to affect Tang Zi, and Liu Zhong trapped and killed Huyang Wei.
After Gengshi ascended the throne, Liu She followed him into the Pass and was named the King of the Yuan clan, with Liu Zhong as his attendant.
The reform failed, and Liu She and Liu Zhong fled east to Luoyang.
In the second year of Jianwu, Liu She was made king of Sishui, and Liu Zhong was made king of Zichuan.
In the tenth year of Jianwu's reign, Liu She passed away, and his youngest son Liu Huodan was granted the title of Marquis of Tangxi Valley, and was enshrined in the honor of Liu She.
Liu Zhong missed his late father during the funeral and cried for more than 20 days before he passed away.
The eldest son Liu Zhu was granted the title of Marquis of Ji'an to worship Liu Zhong, and Liu Zhong's son Liu Feng was granted the title of Marquis of Quyang.
Liu She followed his father's brother Liu Mao when he was eighteen years old. When the Han army rose, Liu Mao called himself Liu Derelict and gathered his troops in Jingxian and Mixian areas, calling him the new general.
He captured Yingchuan and Runan, and had more than 100,000 troops.
After Guangwu arrived in Hanoi, Liu Mao led his troops to surrender and was named King of Zhongshan.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, all those who were kings in the clan were demoted to the rank of marquis, and Liu Mao was granted the title of Marquis Rang.
Liu Mao's younger brother Liu Kuang also rose up with the Han soldiers.
In the second year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Yichun.
He is humble and upright in Yongping.
His son Liu Fu succeeded him and was granted the title of Marquis of Chaoyang. ◆The biography of Ancheng Xiaohou Liu Ci, named Ziqin, was the clan brother of Guangwu.
Grandfather Liu Li was the prefect of Cangwu.
Liu Ci lost his father when he was young.
His brother Liu Xian complained about the murder, and the officials captured Liu Xian and killed him.
summary: **Chengyang Gong Wang Liu Zhi** was the son of Liu Chang, Marquis of Kang Ling. Liu Chang's ancestor was granted Chongling Marquis. Liu Chang moved to Baishui Township due to low terrain and was praised for his modesty. During Wang Mang's usurpation, Liu Zhi was imprisoned for marrying Zhai Xuan's daughter but was pardoned. When Wang Mang usurped the throne, Liu Zhi's titles were abolished. When Guangwu raised troops, Zhen Fu imprisoned Liu Zhi's family. After the Han defeat at Xiaochang'an, Zhen Fu killed Liu Zhi's mother, brother, and wives. Gengshi made Liu Zhi Taichang General and King of Dingtao. After Gengshi's fall, Liu Zhi fled to Luoyang. Guangwu made him King of Chengyang in the second year of Jianwu. He died at 43, posthumously named Prince Gong. **Sishui Wang Liu She** was Guangwu's grandson. His son Liu Zhong was close to Guangwu since childhood. Liu Zhong killed Huyang Wei during the Han uprising. Gengshi made Liu She King of Yuan and Liu Zhong his attendant. After Gengshi's failure, they fled to Luoyang. In the second year of Jianwu, Liu She was made King of Sishui, and Liu Zhong King of Zichuan. Liu She died in the 10th year. Liu Zhong died of grief after 20 days of crying. Liu She's brother Liu Mao gathered over 100,000 troops, surrendered to Guangwu, and was made King of Zhongshan, later demoted to Marquis Rang.

translation:
Liu Ci and Liu Xian's son Liu Xin sold their rural residence, abandoned their property together, made friends with guests, and killed officials for revenge. They all fled for their lives, but were later pardoned and returned home.
It happened that Bo Sheng was raising troops, so he followed Bo Sheng to attack various counties.
After Gengshi ascended the throne, Liu Ci was granted the title of Guangluxun and the title of Marquis of Guanghan.
When Bo Sheng was killed, he acted as Da Situ and led troops to attack Runan.
Without pacification, Gengshi appointed Liu Xin as the powerful general to attack Runan on Liu Ci's behalf. Liu Ci and Gengshi both went to Luoyang.
Gengshi wanted to order a close general to seize Hebei, but he didn't know who to send. Liu Ci said that only Uncle Wen could be used among the Liu family's children, but the Grand Sima Zhu Tuna and others thought that was not possible. Gengshi was doubtful, but Liu Ci tried his best to persuade him.
On that day, Liu Ci was appointed as the prime minister and ordered to enter the pass first to repair the ancestral temple and palace.
He came back to welcome Gengshi and established his capital in Chang'an. He granted Liu Ci the title of King Wan, paid homage to the former Grand Sima, and asked him to hold the talisman to govern Guandong.
In the spring of the second year of Gengshi, Liu Ci named him Wan and put him in charge of the six military affairs.
Later, the Red Eyebrow broke the Gengshi, and the six tribes led by Liu Ci gradually dispersed and rebelled, so Liu Ci went to Wan to guard Yuyang.
When they heard that Guangwu had ascended the throne, they went west to Wuguan, where they were welcomed by Gengshi's wife who took them to Luoyang.
Emperor Guangwu commended Liu Ci for his loyalty and named him Marquis Shen in the second year of Jianwu.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, he added a new household, was named Anchenghou, and participated in court meetings.
Since Liu Ci had a good reputation, he was kind and affectionate. He hosted private banquets for many times. He also often visited Liu Ci's mansion and received particularly generous favors and rewards.
Liu Ci often donated money to his old friends, but he did not leave them as legacies.
The emperor built a tomb hall for him, erected an ancestral temple, and set up officials and soldiers in the style of Chung Ling Xiaohou.
Jianwu died in the 28th year of his life and was succeeded by his son Liu Min.
In the 30th year of Jianwu's reign, the emperor also granted Liu Min's younger brother Liu Song the title of Bainiuhou. Because the King of Chu conspired to rebel, he was implicated in Liu Min's confession, and his title was revoked. After Liu Min died, his son Liu Shang succeeded him and was granted the title of Bainiuhou.
After Liu Shang's death, his son Liu Chang succeeded him. ◆The biography of Liu Shun, the Xiaohou of Chengwu
Chengwu Xiaohou Liu Shun, courtesy name Pingzhong, was Guangwu's clan brother.
His father, Liu Qing, was the half-brother of Chongling Marquis Liu Chang.
Liu Shun and Guangwu were from the same hometown and had been close friends since childhood.
Gengshi ascended the throne, with Liu Qing as King of Yan and Liu Shun as General Huya.
When Gengshi surrendered to Chimei, Liu Qing was killed by the rebels. Liu Shun paid a visit to Guangwu and was named Nanyang Prefect. In the second year of Jianwu, he was named Chengwuhou. He had the largest household in the town and his land rent income was several times that of each clan member.
In the eighth year of Jianwu's reign, he was sent to defeat the Liu'an thieves, so he became the prefect of Liu'an.
A few years ago, Guangwu wanted to recruit him to Beijing, and officials from Lu'an wrote a letter asking him to stay. When he died in the eleventh year of Jianwu, the emperor sent envoys back to Beijing to pay his respects in person. His son Liu Zun inherited the title, but was demoted to the rank of Marquis Duan due to his involvement in dealings with other kings.
◆The Huaihou of Shunyang Liu Jia is said to be the Huaihou of Shunyang Liu Jia, courtesy name Xiaosun, and the clan brother of Emperor Guangwu.
His father, Liu Xian, was the half-brother of Chongling Marquis Liu Chang.
Liu Jia lost his father when he was young and had a kind and generous nature. Nan Dunjun raised him as his own son. Later, he and Bo Sheng both studied in Chang'an and studied "Shang Shu" and "Spring and Autumn".
summary: **Ancheng Xiaohou Liu Ci** was Guangwu's clan brother. After his brother Liu Xian was killed by officials, Liu Ci and his nephew Liu Xin killed the officials in revenge and fled, later pardoned. He followed Bosheng to attack counties. Gengshi made him Guangluxun and Marquis of Guanghan. After Bosheng's death, he acted as Da Situ. He recommended Guangwu to Gengshi for the Hebei mission. Gengshi made him King Wan and Grand Sima. After Chimei broke Gengshi, Liu Ci went to Luoyang. Guangwu made him Marquis Shen in the second year of Jianwu, later Anchenghou. He was kind and generous, often hosting banquets, and died in the 28th year. **Chengwu Xiaohou Liu Shun** was Guangwu's clan brother and childhood friend. Gengshi made his father Liu Qing King of Yan and Liu Shun General Huya. After Liu Qing was killed by rebels, Liu Shun visited Guangwu and was made Nanyang Prefect, later Chengwuhou. He defeated Liu'an thieves and became prefect of Liu'an. He died in the 11th year of Jianwu.

translation:
The rebels rose up, and Liu Jia followed Gengshi to fight.
When the Han army failed in Xiao Chang'an, Liu Jia's wife was killed.

The emperor then replaced him with Da Honglu and Wei Ying.
In the seventeenth year of Yongping, he paid homage to the attendant and offered wine.

His wife wrote a letter requesting that he be buried in his hometown and be given another 300,000 yuan.
◆Zheng Junchuan

When I was young, I loved Huang Lao's books.

Brother is grateful for his words and will be honest and honest in the future.
Zheng Junhao is a responsible person who takes care of his widowed sister-in-law and orphans. He is kind and courteous.
It is often said that he is staying at home due to illness and should not be called up by the state or county.

In the third year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Situ Baoyu recruited him. Later, he admitted that he had not arrived.

Later, he asked to retire because of his illness. He became Yilang and returned home. Because he was seriously ill, the emperor gave him clothes.
In the first year of Yuanhe, an edict was written to the governor of Lujiang and the prime minister of Dongping: "Yi Lang Zheng Jun, Xiu Xiu is in poverty, he is thrifty and tidy, he keeps secrets in front of him, he retires due to illness, he is good and chaste, and his hair is yellow."
He also went to Anyi to order Mao Yi, who behaved humbly and resigned from illness. His pure style was praised by Dongzhou as benevolent.
"Shangshu" does not say that commending those who have great virtues is good governance.
It is appropriate to give Zheng Jun and Mao Yigu each a thousand husks of dendrobium, and often send condolences to the chief official in August, and give sheep wine to show this unusual behavior.
In the second year, the emperor visited Rencheng in the east and visited Zheng Jun's house in person. He ordered the minister to be given a salary for the rest of his life, so people at that time called him the "white-robed minister".
Yongyuanzhong died at home.
◆Zhao Dianchuan
Zhao Dian, courtesy name Zhongjing, was from Chengdu, Shu County.
His father, Zhao Jie, was a Taiwei. Emperor Huan established him and granted him the title of Marquis of Chuting.
When Zhao Dian was young, he devoted himself to the practice of quietness and frugality, and was erudite in the classics. His disciples came from far away to seek advice from him.
At the beginning of the founding of the People's Republic of China, he was recommended by the four palaces and worshiped as Yilang, served as a minister in the palace, and then moved to serve as a minister.
When the emperor wanted to widen the Hongchi, Zhao Dian admonished him: "The water surface of the Hongchi has reached a hundred hectares, and it needs to be widened and dug deeper. This is not to respect Tang Yu and restrain himself, to abide by filial piety and to care for the people."
summary: Zheng Jun, a follower of Huang-Lao, dissuaded his brother from corruption by working to repay stolen money. He cared for his widowed sister-in-law and orphans. Refusing official posts, he was later appointed Yilang, known for loyal advice. The emperor praised his poverty and chastity, granting him gifts. He died at home.

translation:
◆In the preface to the biographies of eunuchs, "Book of Changes" says: Heaven shows down the image of the Dharma, and the saints imitate it.
There are four eunuch stars in the sky, next to the emperor star, so the "Book of Rites of Zhou" includes eunuchs to fill the number.
The eunuchs guard the inner gate of the palace, and the eunuchs guard the precepts of the female palace.
"The Rites of Zhou" also says: There are five servants in the king's bedroom.
The "Moon Order" records: In the middle of winter, the officials in charge of the eunuchs were ordered to inspect the gates and keep the doors open and closed.
There is also a poem called "Xiang Bo" written by an eunuch in "The Book of Songs·Xiaoya" that satirizes King You of Zhou for believing in slander.
It can be seen that eunuchs have been serving in the imperial court for a long time.
Probably because they have insufficient yang energy in their bodies, are single-minded in temperament, and have no evil thoughts. They are easy to interact with and manage the people in the palace, right?
However, later generations followed this system and the scope of their appointment gradually expanded. Among them, talented ones such as Bo Diao and Guan Su made contributions to the Jin and Chu states. Jing Jian and Miao Xian made contributions to the Qin and Zhao states because they recommended Shang Yang and Lin Xiangru respectively.
As for the disasters caused by eunuchs, they caused chaos to the Qi State and brought violence to the Song State. These are obvious examples.
When the Han Dynasty flourished, the system of the Qin Dynasty was still used, and the official position of Zhongchangshi was set up.
But it is also cited that scholars participated in the selection of regular servants. They all wear hats decorated with silver bells and sable tails, and work in the palace and Taiwan Province.
When Empress Lu came to the throne, she appointed Zhang Qing as her chief visitor, who came in and out of her bedroom to receive and convey her orders.
During the reign of Emperor Wen, there were uncles Zhao Tan and Beigong, who were very lucky to have relatives.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty also loved Li Yannian.
Emperor Wu had banquets in the harem many times, or secretly visited the villa outside the palace. Therefore, eunuchs were usually responsible for reporting confidential matters.
By the time of Emperor Yuan, Shi You was the magistrate of Huangmen. He was loyal and diligent, and was very helpful to political affairs.
Later, Hong Gong and Shi Xian relied on insidious flattery to get promoted, which finally led to the murder of Xiao Wangzhi and the deposed Zhou Kan, which damaged and tarnished the emperor's virtue.
At the beginning of the Eastern Han Dynasty when the dynasty was reestablished, all eunuchs were eunuchs and no longer mixed with other scholars.
During the Yongping period, the staff began to be recruited: four people from the Zhongchang sect and ten people from the Xiaohuang sect.
Emperor He ascended the throne at a young age, and the Dou Xian brothers controlled the government. Officials inside and outside were unable to approach Emperor He, and only eunuchs lived with Emperor He.
Therefore, the eunuch Zheng Zhong was able to make plans with Emperor He alone in the forbidden palace, and finally killed the traitorous minister Dou Xian. Zheng Zhong was named the Marquis of Chao'an Township and was given the title of Palace Minister.
The power of eunuchs began to grow.
From Emperor Ming to the Yanping period, the scope of eunuch appointments was gradually expanded, and the number of eunuchs was slightly increased. The number of eunuchs increased to ten, and the number of small Huangmen was twenty. The decorations on their hats were all changed to gold right mink, and they also served as Jiuqing and other foreign court officials.
Empress Dowager Deng presided over the government as a heroine, and there were many political affairs. The courtiers discussed national affairs and could not enter the inner palace to participate in planning and issue edicts without going beyond the queen's residence. Therefore, she had to appoint eunuchs and pin the fate of the country on them.
They hold the power of nobility in their hands and carry the royal decrees in their mouths. They no longer just hold positions in the palace and Yongxiang.
Later, the eunuch Sun Cheng made great achievements in supporting Emperor Shun, and Cao Teng participated in the plan to support Emperor Huan. Subsequently, the five marquises Shan Chao, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, Zuo Xuanguan, and Tang Heng conspired to have Liang Ji, a relative of his, executed. What they did was fair and just, and their kindness was in the emperor's heart, so they obeyed both inside and outside the court, and no one dared to criticize them.
Some people praise them for having the same achievements as Yi Yin and Huo Guang, and are worthy of the previous generations; some say that the strategies of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping have appeared again today.
Although there were loyal ministers who served the public affairs at that time, they were eventually rejected.
Their actions move mountains and oceans, and their breath turns frost into dew.
Those who try their best to satisfy their demands will bring glory to the three tribes; those who do not hide their feelings and go against their wishes will have their relatives near and far destroyed.
The laws and regulations of the Han Dynasty were extremely chaotic.
The eunuchs wearing high crowns, long swords, and red ribbons with gold seals were all over the palace; there were probably dozens of eunuchs who were granted the title of marquis, worshiped as county guards, and ruled over others in the south.
Their government offices and residences are dotted in large and small cities; their descendants, clans and their dependents account for more than half of the state; the treasure house is filled with gold, He's jade, thin and transparent silk yarn from the south; "playthings" such as concubines, maids, singers, and dancers fill the gorgeous rooms; dogs and horses are decorated with floral silks, and civil buildings are decorated with brocade silks and satins.
They plundered and exploited the common people, and were extravagant and lustful.
They framed virtuous people and specially built party members.
There are even some pulling each other's back, trying to follow others' trends, and not hesitate to embarrass themselves in order to show off.
They help each other and have similar odors, so the number of party members is increasing, and they have committed countless crimes that have ruined the country and harmed the government.
As a result, the whole country was filled with sighs and resentment, and there was no place for people with lofty ideals. Bandits and thieves took advantage of the opportunity to rise up and disrupt China.
Although loyal and good people were resentful and sometimes stood up to denounce the eunuchs, if they spoke out, they would be immediately arrested and killed.
The party's prisons were also established, and those who were convicted turned around and made false accusations.
Anyone who is called a good person is not immune to persecution.
summary: The preface to the biographies of eunuchs in the *Book of the Later Han* explains that eunuchs have served in imperial courts since ancient times, as evidenced by celestial signs and classical texts like the *Book of Changes* and the *Rites of Zhou*. Initially, they were employed for their perceived lack of evil thoughts and suitability for managing the inner palace. However, over time, their roles expanded. While some, like Bo Diao and Guan Su, made contributions to states, others caused disasters, such as in Qi and Song. During the Han Dynasty, the system continued, with eunuchs like Zhang Qing serving Empress Lü and later emperors. Their power grew significantly during the Eastern Han, starting with Zheng Zhong, who helped Emperor He eliminate the Dou Xian faction and was enfeoffed, marking the beginning of eunuch influence. This trend continued under subsequent rulers, with eunuchs like Sun Cheng playing key roles in supporting emperors, leading to their increased authority and the granting of titles and lands. Cai Lun, a eunuch known for his talent and integrity, served under several emperors and is credited with inventing paper. He supervised the production of imperial instruments and later oversaw the collation of classics. However, he was implicated in a past conspiracy and committed suicide after being ordered to confess. Sun Cheng, another prominent eunuch, led a coup to establish Emperor Shun, killing rival eunuchs and officials. He and eighteen others were enfeoffed as marquises for their efforts. Despite later being dismissed and recalled, Sun Cheng’s legacy included the formalization of eunuch adoption rights. Other eunuchs like Cao Teng served four emperors without error, recommending worthy officials and maintaining a reputation for integrity, even when falsely accused. The power of eunuchs peaked during the reign of Emperor Huan, when five eunuchs—Shan Chao, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, Zuo Xuanguan, and Tang Heng—helped the emperor eliminate the powerful Liang Ji family. They were all enfeoffed as marquises on the same day, becoming known as the "Five Marquises." Their influence led to widespread corruption, with their relatives and associates plundering the people and causing chaos. Despite some attempts at reform, the eunuchs’ power only grew, leading to the persecution of upright officials and the establishment of party prisons. The historian notes that while Yuan Shao later killed all eunuchs, this merely replaced one form of violence with another, and the Han dynasty ultimately fell due to its reliance on eunuchs. Lu Qiang, a eunuch known for his honesty, advised Emperor Ling to eliminate corrupt officials and grant amnesty to party members during the Yellow Turban rebellion. However, he was falsely accused by other eunuchs and committed suicide. Other eunuchs like Zhao and Li Xun were noted for their learning and integrity, but they were exceptions. Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong, who served under Emperor Ling, were among the most powerful eunuchs. They controlled the court, collected exorbitant taxes, and built lavish palaces. Their corruption and cruelty drove many to join the Yellow Turbans. After Emperor Ling’s death, Yuan Shao led a massacre of eunuchs, killing thousands. Zhang Rang and others fled with the emperor but eventually committed suicide by drowning. The historian concludes that the fall of the Eastern Han was due to the gradual accumulation of eunuch power, which corrupted the court and alienated the people. While some eunuchs were loyal and capable, the majority were self-serving and destructive. Their influence, combined with the weakness of young emperors and the machinations of female regents, led to the dynasty’s collapse. The historian emphasizes that the eunuchs’ ability to gain trust and manipulate the court, coupled with their lack of familial ties, made them particularly dangerous. The decline was not sudden but a slow process, as warned in the *Book of Changes*: "Walking on frost, solid ice will come."

◆Cao Jie's biography, Cao Jie's courtesy name is Hanfeng, a new savage from Nanyang.
He was originally from Weijun, and his family had two thousand shi from generation to generation.
In the early years of Emperor Shun's reign, Yixiyuanqi was promoted to Xiaohuangmen.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, he was promoted to regular attendant and served as captain of chariot.
In the first year of Jianning, the general Zhijie led thousands of soldiers from Huangmen to the Yulin to welcome Emperor Ling from the north and accompanied Emperor Ling's chariot into the palace.
Emperor Ling ascended the throne and was granted the title of Marquis of Chang'an Township and six hundred households due to his merits in making policies.

summary: The biographies of individual eunuchs detail their rise and fall. Hou Lan, a favorite of Emperor Huan, amassed immense wealth through bribery and corruption, with his brother Hou Shen committing atrocities. Hou Lan was eventually impeached by Zhang Jian, but he retaliated by having Zhang Jian killed. He later committed suicide after being stripped of his titles. Cao Jie, who served under Emperor Shun and Huan, helped Emperor Ling ascend the throne and was instrumental in the massacre of the Dou Wu and Chen Fan factions. He and his associates, including Wang Fu, were granted extensive titles and lands, leading to widespread corruption and abuse of power. Despite some opposition, Cao Jie died in office, and his adopted son inherited his title.

◆Cui Xiang's biography, Cui Xiang's courtesy name was Tingbo, and he was a native of Anping, Zhuo County.
My great-great-grandfather, Cui Chao, worked for Youzhou during the reign of Emperor Zhao, and he advised the governor not to associate with King Yan Ci.
Later, he failed to assassinate the king and was promoted to Shi Yushi.
He gave birth to a son named Cui Shu, who successively served as the governor of four counties. He was known as capable wherever he went.
Cui Shu's youngest son was named Cui Xiang. When Wang Mang was a county scholar, he was summoned to the bus by Ming Jing.
Zhen Feng, the Taibao, appointed him as an infantry captain. Cui Xiang said: I heard that when conquering a country, one does not ask for benevolent people, and when fighting, one does not visit Confucian scholars.
How can I find this move?
So he confessed his fault and went home.

At that time, Cui Fa, Cui Peng's brother, was favored by Wang Mang because of his cleverness, and his official position reached the rank of Da Sikong.
The mother was a master of Confucian classics and the language of hundreds of schools of thought. Wang Mang favored her with special gifts and gave her the title of Mrs. Yicheng, with a gold seal and purple ribbon, and a Wenxuan Danbo, which became apparent in the new Mang generation.
Later, Cui Xiang was appointed as the Grand Yin of Jianxin. Cui Xiang had no choice but to sigh and said: I was born in the age of Wuwang, and met such kings as Chu and Yi. I have an old mother above me and brothers below me. How can I put my body in danger by myself?
He went to the government office on his bicycle, claiming that he was ill and had nothing to do. He did not go to the county for three years to encourage farmers to grow mulberry trees.
Ni Chang, an official under his command, persuaded him, and Cui Cheng reluctantly stood up and issued the Spring Order.
In the counties I visited, the prisons, large and small, were full of people.
Cui Xiang cried and said: Oh!
If the punishment fails, the person is trapped in a trap.
What crime do these people have to be locked up here!
After a fair trial, more than 2,000 people were released.
The official kowtowed and advised: In the early days of the imperial government, the state pastoralists were in serious trouble.
Forgiving the criminal is indeed the heart of a benevolent person; however, if you are the only one who does this, will you regret it?
Cui Heng said: Duke Wen of Zhu would not change his life just because of one person, and a gentleman would say that he knew his fate.
For example, killing a large Yin to redeem two thousand people is what I want.
So he was sick and left.
In the early years of Jianwu, the imperial court recommended many people, and the governor of Youzhou also recommended Cui Heng as a virtuous person.
Cui Xiang felt ashamed that his clan was favored by Wang Mang, so he resigned and refused to serve as an official. Living in Xingyang, he reflected behind closed doors and wrote sixty-four chapters of "Book of Changes", which were used to judge good and bad fortunes, and many of them were used for predictions. Before his death, he wrote a poem to express his condolences, called "Comfort". Cui Heng gave birth to Cui Yi, who became invisible due to illness.
summary: Cui Xiang, courtesy name Tingbo, was from Anping, Zhuo County. His great-great-grandfather Cui Chao served Youzhou under Emperor Zhao, advising the governor against associating with King Yan Ci. After failing to assassinate the king, he was promoted to Shi Yushi. His son Cui Shu governed four counties capably. Cui Xiang, Cui Shu's youngest son, was summoned by Ming Jing during Wang Mang's era. When Taibao Zhen Feng appointed him infantry captain, Cui Xiang refused, stating that conquering a country does not require benevolent people or Confucian scholars, and resigned. Wang Mang, who hated dissent, favored Cui Xiang's brother Cui Fa, making him Da Sikong. Cui Xiang's mother was a Confucian scholar honored as Mrs. Yicheng. Later, Cui Xiang was forced to become Grand Yin of Jianxin. He reluctantly served, claiming illness and neglecting duties for three years. After releasing over 2,000 prisoners through fair trials, he resigned, saying he would rather die than harm innocents. In the early Jianwu years, he refused a recommendation due to shame over his clan's ties to Wang Mang, living in Xingyang and writing sixty-four chapters of the "Book of Changes" before his death.

When Empress Dowager Dou came to court, Dou Xian used his relatives as cashiers to receive orders.

None of the three items are suitable, but if you want to give it a try, you just want to imitate me, and you are angry and can't stop yourself.
I have seen privately that he has a pure and graceful posture, a masterful attitude, a beautiful mind and a powerful spirit, and has the demeanor of a virtuous person.
Ma was lucky enough to be admitted to the pavilion and ranked in the back row, so he tried his best to dare to say a word.
The ancients said: Those who are born rich are proud, and those who are born noble are proud.
There is no one who can be born into wealth and not be proud.
Now that the favor is rising and the officials are watching, when Yao and Shun were in their heyday and at the peak of their splendor, how could they not be concubine for a few days so as to make people's reputation last longer, promote the reputation of Shen Bo, and achieve the achievements of Zhou Gong and Zhao Gong?
An old saying goes: If you don't have trouble, you won't be in position; if you have trouble, you will be established.
In the past, the relatives of King Feng Ye held high positions and were called virtuous ministers; recently, the Yin Weiwei restrained himself and returned to ritual, and finally gained great blessings.
summary: Cui Xiang's son Cui Yi was reclusive due to illness. Cui Yi's son Cui Xiang (the younger) was proficient in classics at thirteen, studied at Taixue, and was famed alongside Ban Gu and Fu Yi. He wrote "Da Zhi" to defend his reclusive nature. During the Yuanhe period, he praised Emperor Suzong with "Ode to the Four Patrols." The emperor admired his work and urged Dou Xian to meet him. Cui Xiang became Dou Xian's guest, but after the emperor's death, he warned Dou Xian against arrogance, citing historical examples. When Dou Xian became general, he appointed Cui Xiang as a courier. Cui Xiang repeatedly admonished Dou Xian for his excesses, leading to alienation. He was made magistrate of Changling but refused and died at home in 92 AD, leaving numerous writings.
