He was attentive and eager to learn, even in bad times.
Later, when the matter was clarified, he was released home and was summoned by Deng Zun, the general of Liao Dynasty.
Soon, Deng Zun was killed and Cui Yuan was dismissed from his post and returned.
Later he was summoned to the palace of Yan Xian, the general of chariots and cavalry.
At that time, the Queen Mother Yan took the title of regent and acted on behalf of the emperor. Yan Xian entered the court to participate in political affairs.
First, Emperor An deposed the prince as King of Jiyin and made Beixiang Marquis his heir.
Cui Yuan believed that setting up a marquis was not correct. Knowing that Yan Xian would fail, he wanted to abolish the order, but Yan Xian was too drunk to see him.
So he told Chen Chan, the chief minister: "Zhongchang served Jiang Jing, Chen Da, etc., and bewitched the late emperor because of his favor, so he deposed the orthodox ones and supported the evil ones."
When the young emperor ascended the throne, he became ill in the temple, and Zhou Bo's autocratic power reappeared here.
Now I would like to seek an audience with Chang Shijun, and persuade the general to ask the Queen Mother to arrest Jiang Jing and others, depose the young emperor, and install King Jiyin. This will surely harmonize the hearts of heaven and the hopes of people.
Yi and Huo's meritorious deeds did not leave the table, and the generals and brothers would pass on their achievements to infinity.
If you refuse to disobey God's will and remain empty of the throne for a long time, your innocence will turn into a great evil.
This is the opportunity for misfortune and fortune, the time for division of merit.
Chen Chan hesitated and did not dare to obey.
When the Marquis of Beixiang died, Sun Cheng established himself as King Jiyin. This was Emperor Shun.
The Yan Xian brothers were all killed, and Cui Yuan was also ostracized.
Disciple Su Yuanshi knew all about Cui Yuan's intentions and wanted to write a letter to explain the situation clearly, but Cui Yuan stopped him immediately after hearing it.
At that time, Chen Chan became the captain of the Sili school and summoned Cui Yuan. He said to Yuan: "But after listening to Su Yu's letter, please let me bear witness for you."
Cui Yuan said: This is just like a son and a young wife talking privately. I hope you won't say it out loud.
So he resigned and returned home, no longer answering the orders of the state and county.
After a long time, General Liang Shangchu opened his mansion and summoned Cui Yuan.
Officials who thought they were noble relatives might be reprimanded again, so they resigned because of their illness.
In the middle of the year, he was promoted to Maocai and appointed county magistrate.
While in office, he talked about current affairs several times and cultivated hundreds of hectares of rice fields for the people.
After seven years in office, the people sang his praises.
In the early years of Han'an, Hu Guang, the chief minister, and Dou Zhang, the chief minister, jointly recommended Cui Yuan as a great scholar of virtue. He had made great achievements in politics and should not be in the lower position for a long time, so he was promoted to the prime minister of Jibei.
At this time, Li Gu was the governor of Taishan. He praised Cui Yuan for his elegance and presented him with a letter to express his hospitality.
For more than a year, Guanglu doctor Du Qiao served as eight envoys and traveled around the country. Cui Yuan was accused of embezzlement and summoned to Tingwei.
Cui Yuan filed a petition to sue himself and found out the facts of the case and released him.
Soon he died of illness at the age of sixty-six.
When he was dying, Cui Chen, Gu Ming's son, said: People live by the energy of heaven and earth. When they die, their essence returns to heaven and their bones return to earth.
summary: Cui Yuan, courtesy name Ziyu, lost his father early and studied under Jia Kui, mastering classics and astrology. He avenged his brother's murder by fleeing, later returning after an amnesty. Poor, he lived with brothers for decades. At forty, he became a county official but was imprisoned. During imprisonment, he studied the "Book of Rites." After release, he served under generals Deng Zun and Yan Xian. When Empress Dowager Yan regented, Cui Yuan advised Yan Xian to depose the young emperor and install King Jiyin, but Yan refused. After Emperor Shun's rise, Yan Xian was killed, and Cui Yuan was ostracized. He later served as county magistrate, cultivating rice fields for seven years. Recommended as a virtuous scholar, he became prime minister of Jibei. Accused of embezzlement, he defended himself and was released. He died at sixty-six, requesting a simple burial in Luoyang. He wrote fifty-seven works, including "Nanyang Literary Official Chronicle," and was known for his hospitality despite poverty.

translation:
Taisi Nongyang Fu and Shaofu He Bao wrote to recommend Cui Chen, saying that Cui Chen was very talented and capable and should be an official in the court.
So the emperor made Cui Yilang, promoted General Liang Ji to Sima, and wrote books and theories in Dongguan with Bian Shao, Yandu and others.
Later, Cui Chen became the governor of Wuyuan.
The soil in Wuyuan is suitable for growing hemp, but the local people do not know how to weave cloth. The people have no clothes to wear in winter, so they pile some fine grass to sleep in the grass, and when they see the officials, they come out covered with grass.
After Cui Chen took office, he asked the people to sell their stored grains, buy textiles, weave 纟第, 緺箷 and other tools for them and teach them how to use them, so that the people could avoid the suffering of cold and exhaustion.
At this time, the Xiongnu invaded Yunzhong and Shuofang successively, killing and plundering officials and people, and fled for their lives nine times in a year.
Cui Chen strengthened his troops and ordered beacon towers to conduct reconnaissance. The enemy did not dare to invade, making it the quietest place on the frontier.
When Cui Chen was ill, he was worshiped as Yilang, and he reviewed the Five Classics with famous Confucian doctors at the time.
It happened that Liang Ji was killed. Cui Chen was an old official of Liang Ji. He was implicated, dismissed from his official position, and was imprisoned for several years.
At that time, Xianbei invaded the border many times, and the emperor issued an edict to recommend powerful strategists to the three princes. Sikong Huang Qiong recommended Cui Chen, who was worshiped as the governor of Liaodong.
Halfway through the journey, his mother Liu died of illness. Cui Chen asked Shangshu to go home to attend to the funeral.
My mother, Mrs. Liu, was of very good character during her lifetime and read a lot of books.
At first, Cui Chen served as the prefect of Wuyuan, and his mother often taught him how to manage political affairs. Cui Chen's good achievements were very helpful to his mother.
After the mourning was over, the emperor made him minister again.
Cui Chen was dismissed from his post and returned home after a few months on the grounds that the current situation was in chaos and he was ill and could not work.
When Cui Chen's father died, Cui Chen sold his property, made a tomb, and erected a tombstone.
After the burial, all the family property was sold. Because of poverty, he made a living by selling wine and porridge.
At that time, many people ridiculed him for this, but he never changed.
When he does business, he just wants to make enough money, and he doesn't want to make more money.
Later, when they became officials, they were mostly in border areas, so they were even poorer.
He died during the Jianning period.
The family was very poor and had no money to bury him, so Guang Luxun Yang Ci, Imperial servant Yuan Feng, Shaofu Duan Yu and others prepared coffins and burial materials for him. Dahong Yuan Wei built a monument for him to praise his merits.
He wrote a total of fifteen inscriptions, essays, proverbs, inscriptions, answers, seven words, temples, essays, tables, notes and books.
summary: Cui Chen, courtesy name Zizhen, was quiet and studious. After his father's death, he mourned at the tomb. Refusing official invitations, he wrote "Political Commentary" criticizing contemporary governance. He argued for adapting policies to circumstances, citing historical examples like Emperor Xuan's strict laws versus Emperor Yuan's laxity. He advocated severe punishment for troubled times, comparing it to medicine. He served as governor of Wuyuan, teaching weaving to locals and strengthening defenses against Xiongnu. Later, as Yilang, he reviewed classics but was imprisoned for ties to Liang Ji. After release, he became governor of Liaodong but resigned due to his mother's death. He died during the Jianning period, impoverished, with his burial funded by officials. He wrote fifteen works.

translation:
◆Zuo Xiong's biography, Zuo Xiong's courtesy name is Bohao, a native of Nieyang, Nanyang.
During the reign of Emperor An, he was elected as Xiaolian and promoted to the governor of Jizhou.
There are a lot of people in the state who like to build relationships and go through the back door. Zuo Xiong often kept the door closed and did not interact with them.
Deal with those corrupt, cunning and ferocious Erqianshi without any respect.
In the early years of Yongjian's reign, public buses were sent to pay homage to Yilang.
At this time, Emperor Shun was newly established, and the ministers were following the rules, and many tasks in the court were not completed.
Zuo Xiong wrote several times with fierce words. Minister Pushe Yu Xu believed that Zuo Xiong was loyal and upright, and wrote a report to the emperor recommending him, saying: I have seen that most of the officials below the public minister are silent and self-respecting. They regard showing kindness as a virtue and loyalty to the court as a fool.
I saw that Zuo Xiong dared to mention the fact that the emperor was in trouble in several memorials, and I took it as a warning. He really has the loyalty and upright spirit of a minister, and has the high demeanor of Zhou Gong to assist the king. If he serves as an official, he will definitely get the benefits of correcting and assisting.
Therefore, he worshiped Zuo Xiong as minister and was promoted to minister. Zuo Xiong said in a memorial: I heard that we should adopt a tolerant policy towards remote areas and use peaceful means towards the inland. The most important thing in doing so is to ensure that the people can get peace, and the most important thing in order for the people to be peaceful is to appoint wise men. But using the wise man’s method, there must be rewards and punishments.
Therefore Gao Tao replied to Xia Yu: The most important thing is to know people. To make the people peaceful, you must love the people. In this way, the people will love you. When he was granted the title of Bo and built a marquis, he cared for the people on behalf of the emperor, so the people became harmonious and respectful, and the custom of courtesy and concessions flourished.
Therefore, "The Book of Songs" says: The clouds are cloudy and the good rain is like silk. Let it rain in the public fields first!
Fall into my private land again. In the chaotic era of King You and King Li, the country was not governed well and Baosi was dictatorial. The seven sons formed a gang and ran rampant. There was no distinction between the wise and the foolish. Deep valleys turned into high mountains.
Therefore, there is a poem that goes: In a country with four directions, political corruption is due to the lack of talented people. He also said: People nowadays are pitiful! Like a lizard, it runs away when it sees an official.
Although the Han Dynasty did not restore the ancient system, it was able to carefully select officials, abolish tyranny, correct shortcomings, appease the people, and solve their difficult problems.
In the Wen and Jing eras, the peace in the world was really the result of quietness and careful selection of officials.
Down to Emperor Xuan, because he came from a humble background, he followed his name and his responsibilities, and knew what was wrong with the politics at that time. Officials such as the governor and the prime minister should be introduced in person and their every word and deed should be scrutinized. If they believe in rewards, they must be punished.
Emperor Xuan sighed and said: The people are now peaceful and have no resentment because of good policies and good officials.
summary: Zuo Xiong, courtesy name Bohao, was a native of Nieyang, Nanyang. During Emperor An's reign, he was elected as Xiaolian and became governor of Jizhou. He kept his door closed to avoid those who sought connections through back channels and dealt harshly with corrupt officials. In the early Yongjian years, Emperor Shun appointed him as Yilang. Zuo Xiong submitted several fierce memorials, and Minister Pushe Yu Xu recommended him for his loyalty and uprightness. Zuo Xiong was promoted to minister and submitted a memorial discussing governance. He advocated for tolerant policies toward remote areas and peaceful methods inland, emphasizing that peace for the people required appointing wise men with proper rewards and punishments. He cited historical examples from the Wen and Jing eras through Emperor Xuan's reign, noting that careful selection of officials and long tenure led to good governance. He criticized the current state of affairs where officials were transferred too frequently, corruption flourished, and supervision was ineffective. He proposed that officials with outstanding achievements should be promoted on the spot and not transferred unless for parental death, while those who disobeyed laws should be banned from office for life.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/左周黄列传

translation:
The great cause of the rejuvenation of Zhongxing with articles and propaganda, and its virtues will be passed down to future generations and will never be extinguished.
Emperor Shun was moved by Zuo Xiong's words, and repeatedly ordered officials to check whether it was true or false and implement it prudently.
What Zuo Xiong said all clarified the principles of governance, but because eunuchs had exclusive power, they never adopted it.
From then on, recommendation replaced interaction, county magistrates changed every month, welcoming the new and seeing off the old, and the labor and harassment were endless. Some government offices are deserted and no one is doing anything. Whenever the election work becomes tense, some even run away.
In the third year of Yongjian's reign, the ground in the capital and Hanyang was cracked by earthquakes, and water springs gushed out.
In the fourth year, there was another flood in Si and Ji.
Zuo Xiong deduced the occurrence of the disaster and believed that the people below showed signs of rebellion. And Shangshu said: We should make strict preparations to deal with the occurrence of unexpected events. Soon, thieves from Qingzhou, Hebei, and Yangzhou became troubled one after another. Within a few years, the country was in chaos.
Later, the imperial court granted a general amnesty to the whole country. Although the thieves were slightly relieved, the officials were still unguarded. The remnants of the rebellious party in exile rose up to cause trouble again within a few months. Zuo Xiong and his servant Guo Qian jointly signed a petition, believing that the bandits had been bandits for many years, and most of them died. If one person broke the law, the whole clan would die together.
We should teach him to change his ways while his crime is still minor. If he exposes his accomplices, he can be exempted from the crime; if he can fight back and kill the criminal, he should be rewarded.
I sent it to him, but he didn't accept it. He also said: We should respect the classics and build the Imperial Academy. Emperor Shun listened to him.
In the first year of Yangjia, the Taixue was completed. The emperor ordered to add two types of disciples, A and B, with ten students each. Thirty-eight people from the capital and prefectures who were over sixty years old were awarded to be Lang, Sheren, and Lang of various kingdoms.
Zuo Xiong said again: "The filial piety and integrity of the county are the tribute officials in ancient times." When you become an official, you must help regulate customs and promote education.
If you don't have knowledge and skills, it will be of no use at all.
Confucius said: A person at the age of forty will no longer have any doubts.
"Li" states that "forty means strong and official", which means that when a man is forty, his intelligence, consideration and strength are strong, and he can become an official. Please, from now on, those who are under the age of 40 will not be recommended. They should all go to the government office first. They will study in the Confucian family, and the civil servants will take the official document examination. Duanmen re-examination, test his true and false, observe his special talents, and improve his customs.
Anyone who fails to comply with the law will be dealt with according to law.
If you meet someone with special talents, you can naturally do it regardless of age. Emperor Shun accepted it. So the county was promulgated.
The next year, there was Xu Shu, a filial and honest woman in Guangling who was not yet old enough to be elected. Tailang was suspicious and asked him what was going on.
Xu Shu replied: "What the edict said is like Yan Hui and Zi Qi, regardless of age." So our county asked me to serve as an elector. Lang couldn't give in to him.
Zuo Xiong asked him: "In the past, when Yan Hui heard one, he knew ten. When Xiaolian heard one, he knew how many?" Xu Shu had no answer, so she gave him a lecture and ordered him to return to the county.
Therefore, Hu Guang, the governor of Jiyin, and more than a dozen people were dismissed from office due to election errors. Only more than 30 people, including Chen Fan from Runan, Li Ying from Yingchuan, and Chen Qiu from Xiapi, were allowed to worship the doctor.
From then on, Mu Shou was afraid and did not dare to recommend Xiaolian casually.
By the time of Yongxi, the election was clean and many talents were hired.
Zuo Xiong also requested that famous Confucian scholars in the country be recruited as doctors, and the children of public ministers be recruited as students.
summary: Emperor Shun was moved by Zuo Xiong's words but never implemented them due to eunuch power. In the third year of Yongjian, earthquakes occurred, and in the fourth year, floods struck. Zuo Xiong warned of impending rebellion, and soon thieves arose in Qingzhou, Hebei, and Yangzhou. He later petitioned with Guo Qian about bandits but was not accepted. He also advocated for respecting classics and building the Imperial Academy, which Emperor Shun approved. In the first year of Yangjia, the Taixue was completed. Zuo Xiong proposed that those under forty should not be recommended as Xiaolian unless they had special talents, and they should first study at government offices. Emperor Shun accepted this. When Xu Shu of Guangling was elected underage, Zuo Xiong questioned him and dismissed him. Several officials, including Hu Guang, were dismissed for election errors, while only about thirty people like Chen Fan and Li Ying were approved. Thereafter, officials feared recommending Xiaolian carelessly.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/左周黄列传

translation:
Those who are ambitious and moral will receive an increase in salary.
Xie Lian of Runan and Zhao Jian of Henan were only twelve years old and both knew the art of Confucian classics. Zuo Xiong both petitioned to worship the boy.
Therefore, many people came to the capital to study with their schoolbags on their backs.
At first, Emperor Shun was deposed as King of Jiyin, and wet nurse Song E discussed with Huangmen Sun Cheng to establish an emperor. Later, the emperor believed that Song E had a plot, so he named her Lord of Shanyang, with a city of 5,000 households.
He also made Liang Ji, the general of Liang Shangzi, the Marquis of Xiangyi.
Zuo Xiong secretly wrote a letter saying: "It is a major event for the Wang family to entrust the land to the princes."
Emperor Gao once had a rule: no one with the surname Liu could be granted the title of king, and no one with the surname of Liu could be granted the title of marquis.
Emperor Xiaoan granted the title of Jiangjing, Wangsheng and others, which caused earthquake disasters.
In the second year of Yongjian's reign, there was another solar eclipse.
Some yin and yang scientists blame these strange things on the kings and princes.
Now there is a famine in Qingzhou, the bandits have not been subdued, the people are in dire straits, and they are asking for help from the state.
The emperor was diligent and thoughtful all day long, taking care of the sufferings of the people as his first priority.
We should abide by the ancient laws, stay quiet and do nothing, in order to seek God's will and eliminate disasters.
In fact, the national ceremony should not be ruined by remembering small favors. The emperor did not accept it.
Zuo Xiong also advised: I have heard that there is no monarch who does not love loyalty and integrity but hates flattery and flattery. However, there have been great troubles in the past dynasties, and there are always those who are not guilty of loyalty and integrity, but flattery and flattery. Probably because he likes to hear honest words but flattery.
Generally speaking, being sentenced and sentenced is always the most evil thing in human feelings, and being favored by the emperor and being promoted to a noble title is always the most desirable thing in human feelings.
Therefore, there are few loyal people in the world, but many people are imitators.
The master only hears good things about him and rarely hears about his shortcomings. He is confused and does not know how to wake up, and in the end he is in danger.
I saw that the edict cared about my mother's old virtues and kindness, and wanted to reward her specially.
According to the old rules of the Shangshu, there is no system of conferring titles and towns on wet nurses. Only during the reign of the late emperor, King Amu conferred the title of Ye Wangjun.
Wang Sheng caused the catastrophe of abolishing Li. When he was alive, he was hated by everyone in the world. After he died, no one in the world was unhappy.
Jie and Zhou are the emperors, but their servants are ashamed to be with them. This is because Jie and Zhou are unrighteous!
Boyi and Shuqi were ordinary people, but the princes and princes fought to be friends with them because Boyi and Shuqi were virtuous!
Nowadays, my mother lives a frugal life and sets an example. All officials and ordinary people follow her example. If I were to be knighted like Wang Sheng, I would be afraid that it would violate her ethics and instead violate her wishes.
I think that all people are the same, and the principles are not too far apart. Everything that is wrong has the same understanding in ancient and modern times.
The people deeply hated the great disaster that Wang Sheng brought to overthrow the country. The lives of the people were like stacking eggs, which was very dangerous.
summary: Zuo Xiong also requested recruiting famous Confucian scholars as doctors and increasing salaries for the virtuous. He petitioned to appoint twelve-year-old Xie Lian and Zhao Jian as boy scholars, attracting many students to the capital. Zuo Xiong secretly wrote against granting titles to wet nurse Song E and Liang Ji, citing Emperor Gao's rules and past disasters from such grants. He advised following ancient laws and not ruining national ceremonies for small favors. He repeatedly advised against granting titles, warning of disasters. Song E eventually asked to resign her title, but the emperor still made her Lord of Shanyang. She later lost her title due to conspiracy.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/左周黄列传

translation:
I often worry about something like this happening again.
Because the thoughts of vigilance are always in the chest, the words of fear are never far from the mouth.
Please follow the previous agreement and give tens of millions of dollars to your mother every year. On the one hand, you will show your love and love, and on the other hand, you will not be blamed by the officials and the people.
Liang Ji's appointment of a marquis is not an urgent matter at the moment. It should be judged whether it is appropriate or not after the disaster has passed.
It happened that there were strange earthquakes and Goushi landslides, and Zuo Xiong went to Shu to advise: "The previous emperor granted the king of Ye, and there was an earthquake in Hanyang. Now he seals the king of Shanyang, and there is another earthquake in the capital, and women interfere in politics, and the disaster is extremely serious."
My nonsense about the title of knight is of great importance. The king can give money to others, but he cannot give officials to others. Grandma's title should be restored and the source of disaster should be blocked.
Now that Liang Ji has given up the title, Lord Shanyang should also respect his own position and give up the title. Zuo Xiong repeatedly gave advice, and his words were very urgent. Song E was also afraid and asked to resign and be granted a title. The emperor was still in love with her and finally made her Lord of Shanyang.
Later, my mother finally lost her title due to conspiracy.
At this time, Liu Zhi, the chief minister, was reprimanded for dereliction of duty. He called him to the minister, shouted loudly, and chased and beat him.
Zuo Xiong said: Jiuqing's official position is second only to Sanshi, and he is a minister. He has the custom of wearing jade and behaves like a scholar.
Only Emperor Xiaoming had the punishment of beating, but it was not in line with the ancient legal system. The emperor listened to him and made corrections. From then on, Jiu Qing was never beaten again.
Ever since Zuo Xiong took charge of Na Yanguan, many things have been done to rectify things. Every time there was a chapter report, Taige regarded it as a model and was promoted to the rank of Sili Xiaowei.
First, Zuo Xiong recommended Zhou Ju as minister. Zhou Ju did a good job and everyone praised Zuo Xiong.
He was promoted to Sili, and Feng Zhi, the former Jizhou governor, was promoted to general. Feng Zhi was once convicted of accepting stolen money, and Zhou Ju took this matter to impeach Zuo Xiong.
Zuo Xiong said happily: I used to be a staff member of Feng Zhi's father, and I was very close to Feng Zhi. Now Zhou Ju is using this to impeach me. This is the behavior of the Jin and Han Dynasties in the Spring and Autumn Period! Therefore, everyone in the world is convinced.
The next year he was convicted and dismissed from office, and later he became minister.
Yonghe died three years ago.
◆Zhou Ju's biography, Zhou Ju's courtesy name is Xuanguang, a native of Ruyang County, Runan County. The son of Chenliu Prefect Zhou Fang.
Zhou Fang is in "The Scholars".
Zhou Ju was short in stature and ugly in appearance, but he was erudite and respected by Confucianists. Therefore, there is a popular saying in the capital: Zhou Xuanguang is governed by the Five Classics.
In the fourth year of Yanguang's reign, he was recruited to serve as an official in Situ Li He's mansion.
At that time, the eunuch Sun Cheng and others had already appointed Emperor Shun to annihilate all the Yan family members. Chen Chan, the eunuch, thought that the Empress Dowager Yan had no mother-child relationship with the emperor, so she should move to a separate residence and cut off any court visits.
summary: When Chief Minister Liu Zhi was beaten for dereliction, Zuo Xiong argued that beating Jiuqing was improper, and the emperor stopped the practice. Zuo Xiong was promoted to Sili Xiaowei. He recommended Zhou Ju as minister, and when Zhou Ju later impeached Zuo Xiong for Feng Zhi's crimes, Zuo Xiong praised Zhou Ju's integrity. He died in the third year of Yonghe. Zhou Ju, courtesy name Xuanguang, was from Ruyang, Runan, son of Chenliu Prefect Zhou Fang. He was short and ugly but erudite, respected by Confucianists. In the fourth year of Yanguang, he served in Situ Li He's mansion. When eunuch Chen Chan suggested moving Empress Dowager Yan to separate residence, Zhou Ju advised Li He to respect the Queen Mother, citing historical examples. Li He submitted this, and Emperor Shun later made peace with the Queen Mother.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/左周黄列传

translation:
All the ministers in the court thought it was appropriate.
Zhou Ju told Li: Once upon a time, Zheng Wujiang murdered Duke Yan, and Duke Yan swore to meet her underground. Qin Shihuang complained about his mother's bad behavior, and was isolated from his mother for a long time without contact. Later, he was inspired by the words of Ying Kaoshu and Mao Jiao, and restored his son's ways. Letters praised them.
Now that Zhu Yan has just confessed his crime, and the Queen Mother is in confinement and has left the palace, if she is sad and sick and dies, how will the emperor order the world?
If you follow Chen Chan's words, future generations will blame you.
You should secretly go to the court, respect the Queen Mother, lead the ministers, and meet in court as before, fulfilling the aspirations of the people and answering the hopes of the people. Li Jiushangshu stated the matter.
In the first month of the second year, Emperor Shun came to the East Palace, and the Queen Mother was at peace.
Later, Zhu Qian, the Shaofu of Changle, acted as Situ for Li. Zhou Ju was still an official.
At this time, Sun Cheng and others went to the palace to compete for merit because of their pocket watches. The emperor was angry and moved them all to Fengyuan County, and ordered Luoyang to send them away within a time limit.
Zhou Ju said to Zhu Qian: When the emperor was under the Western Bell, how could Sun Cheng and others be established as kings?
Now forget their great virtues and remember their small faults. If they die on the road, the emperor will kill the meritorious officials as a mockery. Before they leave, they should quickly go to court to persuade the emperor.
Zhu Qian said: Now the emperor is angry, the two ministers have already reported it, I am the only one to go to the table, I must be punished. Zhou Ju said: You are already over eighty years old, and you are serving as the Fu of Taiwan. If you don't serve the country with loyalty today, cherish your life and property, and rest assured of the favor you have gained, what else do you want to ask for?
Although he has a good salary and position, he must be the best in being framed and treacherous; if he is punished for admonishing, he must still have a reputation of loyalty.
If what I say is not acceptable, I will say goodbye to you from now on. Zhu Qian then came forward to advise him, and the emperor indeed listened to Zhu Qian's words.
Zhou Ju was later promoted to Maocai and appointed Pingqiu Ling. He wrote a letter describing the gains and losses of the world, and his words were very passionate and upright.
Shangshu Guo Qian, Ying He and others were filled with admiration after seeing this, and jointly wrote a letter to commend Zhou Ju for his loyalty and uprightness. They asked the emperor to place Zhou Ju's letter next to the emperor's seat as a warning.
Zhou Ju moved slightly and merged with the governor of the state.
In a county in Taiyuan, it was an old custom that Jie Zitui burned people to death, and there was a custom of prohibiting fire.
In the month when Jie Zitui died, it was said that the gods did not like to raise fire, so the people had to eat cold food for a month every winter and did not dare to light fires to cook. The old and young could not bear to eat cold food, and many people died every year.
Zhou Ju went to Bingzhou and posted a message in his temple to commemorate Jiezi, saying that the fire in midwinter would destroy the lives of the people. This was not the intention of a sage, so he promoted it to the people so that they could resume eating cooked food.
As a result, the confusion of the people was somewhat explained, and customs gradually changed.
Transferred to Jizhou governor.
In the third year of Yangjia, Zuo Xiong, the captain of the Sili school, recommended Zhou Ju to be appointed minister.
Zhou Ju and Pushe Huang Qiong worked together to assist the government, and their reputation was more important than that of the court. People around the court respected him.
summary: When Sun Cheng and others were exiled for competing for merit, Zhou Ju urged Zhu Qian to advise the emperor, saying they should not kill meritorious officials. Zhu Qian's advice was accepted. Zhou Ju was later promoted to Maocai and appointed Pingqiu Ling. He wrote passionately about governance, impressing Shangshu Guo Qian and Ying He. As governor of Taiyuan, Zhou Ju abolished the custom of prohibiting fire during Jie Zitui's death month, which caused many deaths from cold food. He posted messages explaining this was not a sage's intention, and customs gradually changed. In the third year of Yangjia, Zuo Xiong recommended Zhou Ju as minister. He worked with Pushe Huang Qiong, gaining court respect. During a severe drought, the emperor asked about governance. When they are buried with the emperor's rites, there will be a feeling of wind and rain, and the harvest will be exhausted.

Lu Bo is right. The Queen Mother issued an edict and agreed.

I narrated his meritorious deeds and listed him as the Nine Ministers.
Just when I was thinking of taking charge of all officials, coordinating moral integrity, and making use of health and welfare, he unfortunately died young and my ambitious plan could not be realized.
The court mourned and was extremely sad.
Didn't "Poetry" say it? Hurry up and tell me your merits and bless you.
Order the generals to come down to the day of mourning, and then gather together to mourn.
He was given an additional 100,000 yuan to show his integrity and impartiality. He has a son, Zhou Xie.

His father's old subordinate, Henan, summoned Kui as a county general and showed his respect to Zhou Xie with humility and courtesy.

He was also recruited on the bus, and money and silk were used to prepare gifts, and he said goodbye because of his illness.
He often lives in secluded places, enviing me for being quiet and inactive, not contacting anyone. The alley where I have lived for more than ten years is full of thorns.
It was not until the second year of Yanxi that he opened the door to receive guests, chat and have fun. In the autumn, Liang Ji was killed. At the end of the year, Zhou Xie died at the age of fifty.
summary: Zhou Xie, courtesy name Jusheng, liked Xuanxu studies. He resigned from office due to his father's connections. When his father's old subordinate summoned him, Zhou Xie secluded himself. He refused Liang Ji's conscriptions three times and later declined recruitment due to illness. He lived in seclusion for over ten years. In the second year of Yanxi, he opened his door to guests. translation:

From Zhou Xie's great-grandfather Zhou Yang to Zhou Xie's grandson Zhou Xun, they were all only sons for six generations, and they were all famous.

Huang Xiang in "Wenyuan Biography".

This is the treasure of a saint!

summary: Huang Qiong, courtesy name Shiying, was from Anlu, Jiangxia, son of Huang Xiang. He initially refused appointments due to illness. translation:

Shangfang Yufu wants to eliminate unnecessary expenses.
Tell your neighbors clearly to abide by the laws and disciplines, and if they don't listen, you must look good to them.

If we change our ways and adopt good policies, natural disasters will be eliminated and a peaceful age will come. The emperor summoned Huang Qiong's memorial to the Deyang Palace and ordered Chang Shi to take Huang Qiong's memorial to the competent authorities for execution.

The emperor upholds the great cause of his ancestors, responds to heaven's omens with respect and solemnity, honors the yuan at the right time, sacrifices to the gods, braves the dust on the road in the morning and evening, handles political affairs day and night, and cares for the people.
Although the "Book of Songs" praises Cheng Tang for not being arrogant or excessive, and not daring to neglect it, the "Book of Books" praises King Wen for being at the peak of the sun, not even having time to eat, nor exceeding it.
There is currently a shortage of sacrifices in the ancestral temple, and we are praying for a good harvest and fasting tomorrow.
I'm afraid of the people around the emperor and don't want to disturb you too much. I think the gift of plowing can be abolished.
summary: During disasters, Huang Qiong advised Emperor Shun to consult records, recruit Confucian scholars, and dismiss the unworthy. He recommended several scholars. Nowadays, the feudal lords are based on households and towns, not on the basis of miles.

After Liang Ji was executed, Huang Qiong ranked first in the court. The more than ten people who reported corruption in prefectures and counties to death all hope that Huang Qiong will rectify the government's affairs soon.

summary: Huang Qiong petitioned to resume the emperor's plowing ceremony, which had been abandoned. He argued it was a grand national ceremony and cited historical examples. The emperor accepted. Emperor Xuan regarded his grandson as the successor of his ancestors and did not dare to have a private relationship, so he built a temple for his father and only had a group of ministers attend the shrine.
summary: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Boren, was from Duling in Jingzhao. At that time, Nan Danyu and Wu Huan came to surrender, and there was nothing happening on the border. The people had just gotten rid of the military revolution. They were young and had enough money.

On the 30th year, Zhang Chun submitted a memorial that should hold a Zen ceremony. The memorial said: Since ancient times, those who have been appointed as emperors by fate must have the ceremony of Zen ceremony to declare their success in a time of peace. "Le Dong Sheng Yi" says: "Ya" is used to govern people, and "Wind" is formed from "Song".
In the prosperous days of the Zhou Dynasty, during the reigns of King Cheng and King Kang, there were historical facts showing that the suburbs were granted the title of Zen.
"Shu Jing" says: In the second month of the year, I patrolled east for hunting, and as for Daizong, this is what I said. It means Feng Chan.
Your Majesty saw that your Majesty accepted the destiny of ZTE, quelled the chaos in the country, repaired the temples of the ancestors, and maintained the peace of the people. The world was safe and sound, the people were reborn, kindness was like clouds traveling in the sky, benefits were like rain falling, the people lived and worked in peace and contentment, and Yi and Di envied benevolence and righteousness.
"The Book of Songs" says: Receiving blessings from heaven, congratulations come from all directions.
This year is the year of Yin, Cang Long Jiayin, Virtue is in the East Palace.
We should take advantage of the good time, follow the rules of Tang Yao, inherit the great cause of Emperor Xiaowu, hold an eastward hunting tour in February, seal Mount Tai, show the master of Zhongxing, record meritorious deeds, restore the traditions of our ancestors, report to the gods, pay homage to the fathers of Liang, worship the gods of the earth, and pass blessings to our descendants. This is the foundation of all generations.
In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, the emperor visited Mount Tai in the east, accompanied by Zhang Chun, the imperial censor, and the Yuan Dynasty sealed the music and carved stone inscriptions.
In March, Zhang Chun died and was given the posthumous title of Jiehou.
◆Cao Bao Biography, Cao Bao, courtesy name Shutong, was born in Xue, Lu State.
His father, Cao Chong, insisted on studying the "Qingshi Rites". During the Jianwu period, he became a doctor. He followed the emperor on a hunting trip to Mount Tai and established the Zen Rite. After returning, he was ordered to establish etiquette such as Qijiao, Sanyong, Dashe, and Elderly Care.
After Xianzong came to the throne, Cao Chong said: If the Han Dynasty receives the mandate of heaven again, there will still be a matter of enshrining Zen, but the rituals and music are incomplete and cannot be used as an example for future generations.
The five emperors did not inherit each other's music, and the three kings did not follow each other's old rituals. The great Han should make his own rituals and use them as examples for generations of descendants.
The emperor asked: How to make rituals and music?
Chong replied: "He Tu Kuo Di Xiang" says: "Elegance in rituals and music emerged in the Han Dynasty."
"Shang Shu·Ji Qian" says: There was an emperor who came out of the Han Dynasty. He was virtuous and happy, and his name was Yu.
The emperor appreciated it very much and issued an edict: Now the official name of Taiyue will be changed to Taiyule, and he will sing poems and perform music, and wait for future gentlemen to supplement it.
He worshiped Cao Chong as his servant.
It was difficult to argue chapters and sentences, so "Qingshi Xue" came out.
Cao Bao was ambitious and generous when he was young. When he was twenty, he inherited his father's studies. He was knowledgeable and especially fond of etiquette.
He often felt that the imperial system was incomplete and envied Shusun Tong for establishing etiquette for the Han Dynasty, so he studied it morning and night and concentrated on thinking. He held the letters in his arms when sleeping and recited the documents while walking. When he was so fascinated by his thoughts, he forgot which way he should go.
Cao Bao was first promoted to Xiaolian, and then to the magistrate of Yuxian County. He used etiquette to govern people and virtue to change customs.
At that time, five thieves from other counties came into Yuxian County and were captured by the officials. Ma Yan, the prefect of Chenliu, was very angry after hearing this and ordered to go to the county to kill them.
summary: Zhang Chun and Zhu Fu memorialized about ancestral temple matters, arguing for proper ritual order. They proposed abolishing the current Qin Temple and following old scriptures. The emperor consulted ministers who recommended replacing the ancestral temple with five emperors and four generations. The emperor complied. Zhang Chun later became imperial servant, then Great Sikong. He opened the Yang Canal for water transportation, benefiting the people. He established regulations for sacrificial ceremonies every three and five years. He proposed building schools and discussed establishing Piyong and Mingtang. In the 30th year, he submitted a memorial about holding a Zen ceremony. In the first Zhongyuan year, the emperor visited Mount Tai with Zhang Chun, who died in March and received the posthumous title Jiehou. Cao Bao, courtesy name Shutong, was from Xue in Lu State. His father Cao Chong studied the "Qingshi Rites" and became a doctor during Jianwu, establishing various rituals. After Xianzong ascended, Cao Chong discussed ritual and music matters with the emperor, who appreciated his views and appointed him as servant. Cao Bao was ambitious and generous, inheriting his father's studies at twenty. He was knowledgeable and fond of etiquette, often feeling the imperial system was incomplete. He studied morning and night, even forgetting directions while walking. He was first promoted to Xiaolian, then magistrate of Yuxian County, governing with etiquette. When five thieves were captured, he refused to kill them despite orders, saving their lives. He was dismissed for this but later recruited as a doctor.

translation:
The emperor then appointed Cao Bao as a doctor, and followed the emperor on a tour to the south. After returning, he handed over the matters concerning the etiquette to the Three Dukes. Before he had time to report, he summoned Xuanwu Sima Bangu to ask about changes to the etiquette system and other matters.
Ban Gu said: There are many Confucian scholars in the capital, and most of them are good at talking about etiquette. We should recruit them widely to discuss the pros and cons together.
The Emperor said: As the saying goes: It will take three years to build a house next to the road. When we gather at the house for ceremony, it is superficially a discussion, but in reality it is mutual suspicion, and we are delayed in writing.
In the past, Emperor Yao used a minister named Kui to compose the Great Chapter.
In the first month of the first year of Zhanghe, he summoned Cao Bao to Jiademen and ordered Xiaohuangmen to take the twelve chapters of "Han Yi" written by Shu Suntong, which Ban Gu had attended, and ordered Cao Bao to say: "This Han Yi is very loose and inconsistent with the meaning of the scriptures. Some modifications should be made now to make it practical."
You can concentrate on your work in Nangong and Dongguan.
After receiving the order, Cao Bao arranged the order of etiquette, based on the old scriptures, mixed with the prophecies of the Five Classics, and wrote out the system of etiquette from the emperor to the common people, including the good and bad luck of weddings, etc., a total of 150 articles, written on two-foot-four-inch bamboo sketches, and memorialized in December of that year.
The emperor thought that it was difficult for everyone to agree on the opinions, so he only accepted them and no longer asked the officials to comment.
When the emperor died and Emperor He ascended the throne, Cao Bao wrote chapters and sentences, and the emperor put the two chapters of "New Rites" at the top.
Cao Bao was promoted to supervise Yulin Zuoqi.
In the fourth year of Yongyuan's reign, he was promoted to the rank of Colonel Shesheng.
Later, Taiwei Zhang Youfu, Shangshu Zhang Min and others complained that he had made the "Han Rites" without authorization and that he should be beheaded if he broke the sacred law.
Although the emperor put down the memorial, the "Han Rites" was not implemented.
When Cao Bao was shooting the captain, there were more than a hundred coffins in the camp but no burials. Cao Bao personally investigated and asked what the reason was.
The official replied: Most of these people have no descendants since the founding of the military, so they cannot be buried after their death.
Cao Bao was very sad after hearing this, so he bought an open space and used it all to bury those without owners and set up sacrifices to worship them.
He was promoted to city gate captain and will be a great craftsman.
At that time, the epidemic was prevalent. Cao Bao visited the patients, found medicine for them, prepared thick porridge, and saved many people.
In seven years, he became the governor of Hanoi.
At this time, there was a severe drought in spring and summer, and food prices soared.
After Cao Bao took office, he laid off officials and eliminated bad guys. Rain fell several times.
There was a great harvest in autumn this year, the people's homes were well fed, and all the wandering people came back.
Later, Cao Bao was dismissed from his post for committing the crime of falsely reporting the disaster.
Soon he was recruited, promoted, and became a servant.
Cao Bao is knowledgeable and understands ancient culture and is the master of Confucianism.
summary: When Suzong wanted to formulate rituals and music, Cao Bao presented a memorial. The emperor appointed him as doctor. Later, the emperor ordered him to work on "Han Yi" in Nangong and Dongguan. Cao Bao wrote 150 articles on ritual systems from emperor to commoners. After the emperor died, Cao Bao was promoted to various positions. Some officials complained about his "Han Rites," which was not implemented. He bought land to bury unclaimed coffins, visited patients during epidemics, and saved many lives. He became governor of Hanoi, where rain fell during drought and harvests were abundant. He died in office in fourteen years, having written numerous works including "Tongyi" and "Exemplary Classics," teaching over a thousand students.

◆Zheng Xuan's biography, Zheng Xuan's courtesy name was Kangcheng, and he was a native of Gaomi, Beihai.
His eighth-generation ancestor Zheng Chong was the minister of public affairs at the time of Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty.
When Zheng Xuan was a boy, he worked as a small official in the countryside in charge of litigation and tax collection. Whenever he went home on vacation, he always had to go to school and was not happy to be a small official. His father was angry many times but could not stop him.
So he went to study at Taixue in Beijing, where he became a teacher under Wu Yuanxian, a native of Jingzhao, and then he became proficient in "Jingshi Yi", "Gongzhu Chunqiu", "Santong Calendar" and "Nine Chapters of Arithmetic".
He also studied "Zhou Guan", "Book of Rites", "Zuo Shi Chun Qiu", "Han Shi" and "Guwen Shangshu" from Zhang Gongzu of Dongjun.
Because there was no one in Shandong who could question him, he went west and entered the customs. After being introduced by Lu Zhi of Zhuojun, he became his disciple Fufeng Ma Rong.
Ma Rong had more than 400 students, and only about 50 people were taught by Ma Rong personally.
Ma Rong was an arrogant person, and Zheng Xuan had not seen him for three years under his tutelage. Ma Rong just sent his senior disciples to tutor Zheng Xuan.
Zheng Xuan studied day and night and never slackened off.
One day, Ma Rong summoned his students to study Tuwei. Hearing that Zheng Xuan was proficient in arithmetic, he summoned him upstairs. Zheng Xuan took this opportunity to ask Ma Rong many difficult questions.
After asking, he said goodbye to Ma Rong and returned to his hometown in Shandong. Ma Rong said to his students with emotion: Now that Zheng Sheng has left me, my teachings will spread eastward.
Since Zheng Xuan went out to study, it took more than ten years before he returned to his hometown.
His family was poor and he went to Donglai to work as a farmer. There are hundreds of students studying with him.
When the disaster of party imprisonment occurred, more than 40 people including Zheng Xuan and Sun Song from the same county were imprisoned. So he immersed himself in studying the classics and stayed behind closed doors.
At that time, He Xiu, a native of Rencheng, loved the theory of "Gongyang", so he wrote "Gongyang Mo Shou", "Zuo Shi's Death" and "Gu Liang's Failed Disease". Zheng Xuan wrote articles refuting "Mo Shou", "Gao Ming" and "Fei Ji".
He Xiu saw it and sighed: Zheng Kangcheng walked into my house, picked up my spear, and came to attack me!
In the early years of the Eastern Han Dynasty, Fan Sheng, Chen Yuan, Li Ming, and Jia Kui were debating ancient and modern theories. Later, Ma Rong replied to Liu Mo and Zheng Xuan, the prefect of the North. He Xiu said that because of the profound research on doctrine and theory, the ancient classics became prosperous from then on.
In the last years of Emperor Ling of the Han Dynasty, the party ban was lifted, and the general He Jin heard of Zheng Xuan's reputation and recruited him.
The prefectures and counties believed that He Jin was a powerful nobleman and did not dare to go against his wishes, so they forced Zheng Xuan to obey the call. Zheng Xuan had no choice but to go and answer the imperial edict.
He Jin set up several canes for him and treated him very generously.
Zheng Xuan did not accept the court robes, but came to see He Jin in Confucian attire wearing a turban.
He stayed one night and then escaped.
Zheng Xuan was already sixty years old at that time, and his students came from far away places, such as Zhao Shang from Hanoi, and there were thousands of them.
Later, General Yuan Wei recommended him as a minister, but he did not take up the post due to his father's death.
Kong Rong, the Prime Minister of the country, respected Zheng Xuan very much. He hurriedly came to his home and instructed the magistrate of Gaomi County to set up a special township for him. He said: In the past, Qi State had a "Scholar Township", and Yue State had a "Gentleman Army", etc., which meant treating the virtuous with courtesy.
Zheng Xuanjun was eager to learn and had noble virtues.
In the past, Taishi Gong, Tingwei Wu Gong, and Ye Zhipushe Deng Gong were all famous officials in the former Han Dynasty.
There are also Yuan Gong and Xia Huang Gong in the Four Hao Mountains of Nanshan. Their talents and virtues are hidden and not exposed. The world respects their nobleness and calls them "gong".
If this is the case, then the so-called "gong" is the proper name for a virtuous person. You don't have to be a Taiwei, Situ or Sikong to be called a public official.
Now the township of Zhengxuan should be named Zhenggong Township.
In the past, Donghai Yugong only had a moral character of ending prisons fairly. He also warned the villagers to expand the gates of their lanes in order to prepare future generations for high-ranking officials.
What's more, Zheng Xuan has such virtue, how could he not walk the road of a horse and a high chariot. The gate of Zhengxuanli Lane should be enlarged and the road in front of it should be widened so that it can pass high-covered vehicles. This can be named Tongdemen.
Dong Zhuo moved the capital to Chang'an, and the minister recommended Zheng Xuan as the prime minister of Zhao. However, he was unable to take office because of the road obstruction.
When the Yellow Turban Army attacked the Qingzhou area, Zheng Xuan took refuge in Xuzhou. Xuzhou Mu Tao Qian received him as a teacher and friend.
In the first year of Jian'an, Zheng Xuan returned to Gaomi from Xuzhou and encountered tens of thousands of Yellow Turban troops on the way. When the Yellow Turban Army saw Zheng Xuan, they all bowed down and agreed not to enter Gaomi County.
Later, Zheng Xuan suffered from a serious illness and feared that he would not die soon, so he wrote to his son Zheng Yien, saying: Our family used to be very poor, but with the tolerance and support of our parents and brothers, we resigned from the small officials like humble servants and went to Zhou, Qin and other places to study. What makes me most proud is that these Confucian scholars accepted my advice and taught me something.
summary: Zheng Xuan, courtesy name Kangcheng, was from Gaomi in Beihai. His eighth-generation ancestor Zheng Chong was minister of public affairs under Emperor Ai. As a boy, Zheng Xuan worked as a small official but preferred studying. He studied at Taixue in Beijing under various teachers, becoming proficient in multiple classics. He later studied under Ma Rong, who had over 400 students. Zheng Xuan studied diligently for three years before meeting Ma Rong personally, asking difficult questions before returning home. After more than ten years of study, he returned to farm in Donglai with hundreds of students. During the party imprisonment disaster, he was imprisoned but continued studying. He refuted He Xiu's theories, impressing He Xiu. When the party ban was lifted, General He Jin recruited him, but Zheng Xuan escaped after one night. At sixty, he had thousands of students. He declined various official positions.

translation:
So everyone rushed to imagine some tricky and weird questions, and various schools of thought put forward their opinions one after another.
Zheng Xuan answered and responded according to the orthodox Confucian views, and the content exceeded the scope of the question. Everyone gained knowledge that they had never heard of before, and no one did not admire and admire Zheng Xuan. At this time, Ying Shao from Runan also joined Yuan Shao, so he introduced himself: Ying Zhongyuan, the former governor of Qinshan, would you like to call me your disciple from the north? How about it?
Zheng Xuan smiled and said: Confucius's students had to take exams in four subjects: morality, speech, political affairs, and literature. Students like Yan Yuan and Zigong never claimed their official titles or family status.
Ying Shao felt ashamed after hearing this.
Therefore, Yuan Shao recommended Zheng Xuan as Maocai, and the above table recommended him as Zuo Zhonglang General. Zheng Xuan did not take office.
The imperial court conscripted him as the chief minister of agriculture, gave him a safe car, and stipulated that wherever he passed, officials in charge would greet him and see him off.
Zheng Xuandu requested to return home because he was ill.
Yuan Shao ordered his son Yuan Tan to send envoys to force Zheng Xuan to join the army. Zheng Xuan had no choice but to take his illness to Yuancheng County, where he was seriously ill and unable to advance. Zheng Xuan died in June of this year at the age of seventy-four.
Zheng Xuan's will was buried sparingly.
At that time, more than a thousand people who had been students under Zheng Xuan's sect, including county magistrates and officials, came to the funeral in solemn mourning clothes.
Zheng Xuan's students co-wrote Zheng Xuan's answers to questions raised by his disciples from the "Five Classics" during his lifetime, and compiled it into "Zheng Zhi" in eight chapters according to the style of "The Analects of Confucius".
In total, the books that Zheng Xuan annotated include "The Book of Changes", "Shangshu", "Mao Shi", "Ritual", "Book of Rites", "The Analects", "The Book of Filial Piety", "Shangshu Da Zhuan", "Zhonghou", and "Cheqi Xiangli". Zheng Xuan's self-authored books include "Seven Political Treatises on Astronomy", "The Comprehensive Theory of Lu Li and Emperor Xuan", "Six Art Theory", "Mao Shi Pu", "Refutation of the Different Meanings of Xu Shen's Five Classics", and "Reply to the Difficulty of Lin Xiao and Preserving Zhou Rites", with a total of more than one million words.
Zheng Xuan strived to be simple and realistic in his interpretation of classics. Many knowledgeable people ridiculed this approach as too cumbersome. As for his rich understanding of classics' annotations, he may be called a pure Confucian. People in Qilu respect him as their master.
His students, Xi Luguan from Shanyang, Wang Quan from Donglai, and Cui Yan from Qinghe were all famous in the local area.
Guoyuan and Rengu Duan, both of whom were also from Le'an, were very young at that time. Zheng Xuan praised Dao Guoyuan as a pillar of the country, Ren Gu Duan had noble moral character, and many others also commented and recommended him.
Later, the achievements of these people were as he said. Zheng Xuan only had one son named Zheng Yien. When Kong Rong was the Prime Minister of Beihai, he recommended him as Xiaolian. When Kong Rong was besieged by the Yellow Turban Army, Yi En died in danger.
Yi En had a posthumous son, and Zheng Xuan named him Zheng Xiaotong because his hand lines were similar to his own.
summary: During the Yellow Turban uprising, he took refuge in Xuzhou. In the first Jian'an year, he returned to Gaomi, encountering Yellow Turban troops who bowed and agreed not to enter the county. When seriously ill, he wrote to his son about his life, studies, and hopes for his son's cultivation. Yuan Shao invited him as a guest, where he impressed everyone with his knowledge. He declined Yuan Shao's recommendation as Zuo Zhonglang General. The imperial court conscripted him as chief minister of agriculture, but he requested to return home due to illness. Forced by Yuan Shao's son to join the army, he died at seventy-four in Yuancheng County, buried simply with over a thousand mourners. His students compiled his answers to questions into "Zheng Zhi." He annotated numerous classics including "The Book of Changes," "Shangshu," "Mao Shi," and "The Analects," writing over one million words. He was respected as a master in Qilu, and his students became famous in their regions.

translation:
◆Zhang Zongchuan, also known as Zhang Zongzi Zhujun, was born in Luyang, Nanyang.
During the reign of Wang Mang, he served as the assistant of Yangquan Township in this county.
When Wang Mang failed and rebels broke out, Zhang Zong led three to four hundred people from Yangquan to seize the territory and marched west to Chang'an. Emperor Gengshi appointed Zhang Zong as a partial general.
Zhang Zong saw the political chaos in Gengshi, so he sent his family to Anyi.
Later, the Great Situ Deng Yu went on an expedition to the west and settled Hedong. Zhang Zong went to Deng Yu's place and went back on his own.
Deng Yu heard that Zhang Zongsu was very powerful, so he recommended him to be a partial general.
When Deng Yu's army arrived at the city, the Red Eyebrow Army was approaching. Deng Yu thought that the city was not strong enough to defend and wanted to lead his troops to defend the city. However, everyone was afraid of being chased by thieves and afraid of being a rearguard.
Deng Yu then wrote the names of the generals on the bamboo slips in order, put them randomly in the box, and asked everyone to draw lots.
Zhang Zongdu refused to smoke. He said: Life and death are determined by fate. Is Zhang Zong a person who will give up when it is difficult? Deng Yu sighed and said: "The general has old relatives and weak sons in the camp, why don't you consider it?" Zhang Zong said: I heard that if a soldier tries his best, a hundred people cannot stop him; if ten thousand soldiers are willing to die, they can dominate the world.
Zhang Zongjin has thousands of troops and can withstand the power of the army. Why should he immediately expect defeat? So I stayed and refused.
After all the camps had led their troops and set off, Zhang Zong urged his soldiers to build strongholds and defend them without retreating.
When Deng Yu arrived at Qianxian County, he heard people commenting: "With General Zhang's manpower, trying to stop an army of millions is like throwing Xiaoxue into boiling water. No matter how hard he tries, he can't do it." So he sent 2,000 infantry and cavalry back to greet Zhang Zong.
Zhang Zong led his troops to set out, but the Red Eyebrow Army hurriedly arrived. Zhang Zong fought with him, drove them back, and then returned to the camp. The generals admired his bravery.
After returning to Chang'an, Zhang Zong led his warriors into the city at night to attack Chimei. He was shot between the arms by the enemy.
When Deng Yu was recalled to the capital, Guangwu appointed Zhang Zong as the capital's auxiliary captain. He led the sudden cavalry and conquered the west general Feng Yi to attack the various camps in Guanzhong. After defeating them, he was promoted to the captain of Henan.
In the sixth year of Jianwu's reign, he became the governor of the province and became a senior official in Taizhong.
In the eighth year, bandits arose in Yingchuan Sangzhong, and Zhang Zong led his troops to defeat them and put them down.
Later, bandits from Qingzhou and Jizhou gathered in the mountains and swamps, and Zhang Zong used his visitors to urge the soldiers of the counties to fight for peace.
In the 16th year, bandits from Langyi and Beibu broke out again. Zhang Zong supervised the soldiers of the two counties to attack them. He then formulated a strategy and clearly rewarded those who surrendered. The enemies were all broken up. The bandits in Pei, Chu, Donghai and Linhuai were afraid of his might and killed thousands of each other. The enemies in Qingzhou and Xuzhou were very afraid.
Later, Zhang Zong was promoted to Langfu Prime Minister. His policies were harsh and he dared to kill.
In the second year of Yongping, he died in his official position.
◆Faxiong's biography, Faxiong's courtesy name is Wenqiang, a native of Fufeng County. Descendants of King Qi Xiang Fa Zhang.
The Qin State destroyed the Qi State, and their descendants did not dare to use the surname Tian, ​​so they used the surname Tian.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan, he moved to Sanfu and made two thousand stones from generation to generation.
Faxiong initially served as a meritorious officer in the county, and later he was promoted to the mansion of Taifu Zhang Yu, where he was promoted to a high rank and appointed chief of the Ping clan.
summary: Zhang Zong, from Luyang, served as an assistant during Wang Mang’s reign. After Wang Mang’s fall, he led 300–400 people to seize territory and was appointed a partial general by Emperor Gengshi. Seeing political chaos, he moved his family to Anyi. Later, he joined Deng Yu, who recommended him as a partial general. When the Red Eyebrow Army approached, Deng Yu wanted to retreat, but Zhang Zong refused to draw lots for rearguard duty, declaring he would not abandon his post. He defended his camp, and Deng Yu sent reinforcements. Zhang Zong fought bravely, driving back the Red Eyebrows. He later attacked them at night in Chang'an and was wounded. Under Guangwu, he became a captain, fought in Guanzhong, and was promoted. He suppressed bandits in Yingchuan, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, and later in Langyi and Beibu. As Langfu Prime Minister, he governed harshly. He died in office in the second year of Yongping. Faxiong, from Fufeng, was a descendant of King Qi Xiang. After Qin destroyed Qi, his family used the surname Fa. He served as a meritorious officer and later as chief of Ping clan, known for exposing criminals. In the third year of Yongchu, pirate Zhang Bolu led 3,000 rebels, invading nine counties. Faxiong was promoted to Qingzhou governor to join Wang Zong in attacking them. After initial victories, a pardon arrived. Faxiong advised against immediate attack, suggesting withdrawal to lure the rebels into surrender. Wang Zong agreed, but Donglai soldiers kept their armor, causing rebels to flee to Liaodong. In spring of the fifth year, rebels returned, and Faxiong defeated them. He later became Nanjun prefect, where he reduced tiger attacks by ordering the destruction of traps and halting hunting. He died in office in the early Yuan Dynasty.
