translation:
In the most civilized era of ancient times, ferocious beasts did not invade, all because of the emperor's kindness and kindness, and his kindness spread to all birds and beasts.
Although the prefect was not benevolent enough, he did not dare to forget this meaning.
After the documents arrive, all the wells will be destroyed, and no wild animals will be hunted in the mountains and forests. From then on, the tiger damage stopped and the people lived in peace.
For several years in the county, there were good harvests year after year.
He died in official position in the early Yuan Dynasty.
◆Teng Fu's biography, Teng Fu's courtesy name Shufu, was a dramatist in Beihai.
At first he served as an official in a prefecture and county, and later he was promoted to the magistrate of Zhuo County. He had both civil and military talents.
The prefect thought that he was capable and appointed him to the county post, taking charge of six counties at the same time.
He is politically wise and deeply loved by the people. He has been in office for seven years and has not lost track of his mistakes.
In the last years of Emperor Shun's reign, thieves were everywhere in Yangzhou and Xuzhou, colluding with each other year after year.
In the first year of Jiankang, Fan Rong, Zhou Sheng and others from Jiujiang gathered to rebel and settled in Liyang, which caused a catastrophe in the Jianghuai River. The imperial court sent the Censor Zhongcheng General Feng Zui to urge Yangzhou Governor Yin Huozhai and Jiujiang Governor Deng Xian to attack them. Yao and Xian were defeated and killed by thieves.
Xu Feng, Ma Mian and others from Yinling also invaded counties and killed officials and people.
Xu Feng wore red clothes with a black ribbon and called himself the "Supreme General". Ma Mian wore a fur hat, yellow clothes, and a jade seal. He was called the Yellow Emperor and built a fort in Dangtu Mountain.
So he established a reign title, appointed hundreds of officials, and sent Marshal Huang Hu to capture Hefei.
The next year, Guangling thief Zhang Ying and others gathered thousands of people to rebel and occupied Guangling.
The imperial court extensively solicited generals, and the three princes recommended Teng Fu, saying that he had all-round talents in both civil and military affairs. He was appointed the captain of Jiujiang, and he and the general Zhao Xu assisted Feng Yu in the crusade together with tens of thousands of people from prefectures and counties.
They also widely opened up rewards, money, and towns, each with different levels.
The Empress Dowager Liang was worried that the generals would be unable to subdue the thieves who were stationed there and colluded, so she suggested sending Lieutenant Li Gu.
Before setting off, they encountered Teng Fu and others advancing to attack the thieves. They defeated them and beheaded one thousand and five of Ma Mian, Fan Rong, Zhou Sheng, etc. Xu Feng led the rest of the army to attack Dongcheng County.
Xie An, a native of Xiapi, responded to the call and led his clan members to set up an ambush to attack Xu Feng and beheaded him. The imperial court granted Xie An the title of Marquis of Pingxiang, with a city of 3,000 households.
He worshiped Teng Fu as Zhonglang General and supervised the affairs of Yangzhou and Xuzhou.
Teng Fu attacked Zhang Ying again and captured more than a thousand people.
Zhao Xu committed the crime of cowardice and falsely increased his rank, so he was recalled to have his head executed in public.
In addition, the Liyang thief Hua Meng claimed to be the "Black Emperor" and attacked Jiujiang, killing the county guard.
summary: Teng Fu, from Beihai, served as Zhuo County magistrate, known for civil and military talents. In the first year of Jiankang, rebels Fan Rong and Zhou Sheng rose in Jiujiang, and Xu Feng and Ma Mian rebelled in Yinling. The court sent Teng Fu as Jiujiang captain with General Zhao Xu to suppress them. They defeated the rebels, beheading 1,500, including Ma Mian and Fan Rong. Xu Feng was killed by Xie An. Teng Fu became Zhonglang General, overseeing Yangzhou and Xuzhou. He defeated Zhang Ying and later Hua Meng, pacifying the southeast. He was appointed Zuo Fengyi but was deposed by eunuchs due to his upright character. He died at home.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/张法滕冯度杨列传

translation:
Teng Fu took advantage of the victory to attack and defeated Hua Meng and other 3,800 people, and captured more than 700 people, including cattle, horses and property.
So everything in the southeast was pacified, and the army was reorganized and returned.
The imperial court appointed Zuo Fengyi as governor, except for one son who was appointed as Lang.
All the rewards Teng Fu received were given to his subordinates.
Teng Fu had an upright character and did not associate with powerful people, so the eunuchs held grudges.
When the time came to reward him based on his merits, the Taiwei Hu Guang recorded the minister's affairs and submitted an imperial edict to depose Teng. The whole world became resentful.
Later, Teng Fu died at home.
◆The biography of Feng Kui, whose courtesy name was Hongqing, was from Danqu, Ma County. When he was young, he studied "Spring and Autumn" and "Sima's Art of War".
His father, Feng Huan, served as the governor of Youzhou during the reign of Emperor An. He hated traitors and punished them many times for their crimes.
At that time, Yao Guang, the prefect of Xuantu, also had uncoordinated personnel relations.
In the first year of Jianguang, the resentful people forged seals to condemn Feng Huan and Yao Guang, and gave them European swords.
He also issued an edict to Pang Fen, the captain of Liaodong, to execute the punishment as soon as possible. Pang Fen executed Yao Guang and detained Feng Huan.
Feng Huan wanted to commit suicide. Feng Sui suspected that the edict was false, so he stopped Feng Huan and said: "When you were in the state, you wanted to get rid of the evildoers. There is really no other reason. The murderer must be blackmailing and using poisonous tricks."
I would like to report the matter to the higher authorities. If it is true, it is not too late to plead guilty. Feng Huan listened to his son's words and wrote a letter to tell the truth. It was indeed a cunning person. The emperor summoned Pang Fen to plead guilty.
It happened that Feng Huan died in prison, and the emperor sympathized with him. Feng Huan and Yao Guang were given 100,000 yuan each, and their sons were appointed as doctors.
Feng Cui became famous from then on.
Feng Nian's family was rich and he was fond of charity and helped the poor and needy, so he was loved by the people in the state.
At first, he was promoted as Xiaolian, promoted seven times to become the captain of the Guanghan vassal state, and was also recruited to be the censor Zhongcheng.
In the last years of Emperor Shun's reign, the imperial court sent Feng Kui to supervise the military affairs of the counties in Yangzhou. Together with Zhonglang General Teng Fu, he defeated the bandits and moved to Longxi as the prefect.
After telling everyone to surrender, the barbarians stopped their activities and dispersed back to their original places. Later, Feng Zui became Jing Zhaoyin and transferred to Sili Xiaowei, and established threats and punishments wherever he was.
Later he was promoted to Tingwei and Taichang.
At this time, the Changsha barbarians invaded Yiyang and gathered there for a long time. By the fifth year of Yanxi, there were more followers, and the Lingling barbarians also colluded with them. A total of more than 20,000 people attacked and burned the city, killing and wounding the officials.
In addition, all Wuling barbarians rebelled and plundered the Jiangling area. Liu Du, the governor of Jingzhou, and Li Su, the governor of Nanjun, both abandoned their posts and fled, and Jingnan fell into enemy hands.
The imperial court then appointed Feng Kui as the general of chariots and cavalry, and led more than 100,000 people to attack them. The edict was written to Feng Kui: The barbarians invaded China, and they did not attack them for a long time. They burned the capital and trampled on the officials and people.
The generals and officials of the prefectures and counties, and the ministers who were dead in their duties, ran away from each other and never looked back. How shameful.
The general had a reputation for being powerful, so he was promoted to the Sixth Division.
The disciples of Chen Tang, Feng and Fu in the previous generation used less to attack more. The enemies of Zhizhi, Yelang and Loulan had their heads hung in the streets for public display. Wei Qing and Huo Guang went to the north and made great achievements. This is all known to the general.
Now, if not the general, who can restore the achievements of the previous dynasty?
Advances and retreats, as well as strategies for power and time, are all under the exclusive control of the general, and matters outside the suburbs are no longer managed internally.
An official has been ordered to hold a farewell ceremony at the gate of the country.
summary: Feng Kui, from Ma County, studied *Spring and Autumn* and *Sima's Art of War*. His father Feng Huan was falsely accused and imprisoned. Feng Kui suspected the edict was forged and urged his father to appeal, revealing the truth. Feng Kui became famous for his charity. He served as Guanghan captain and censor, later defeating bandits with Teng Fu. As Longxi prefect, he pacified barbarians. He became Jing Zhaoyin and Sili Xiaowei, known for strictness. Later, as Tingwei and Taichang, he led 100,000 troops to suppress barbarian revolts in Changsha and Wuling, beheading 4,000 and surrendering 100,000. He refused rewards and retired, but was recalled. He was dismissed after bandits recurred but later reinstated as Henan Yin and Tingwei. He died in office.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/张法滕冯度杨列传

translation:
At that time, Zhu Mu, the governor of Jizhou, came to inspect and was very surprised to see Du Shang.
In the fifth year of Yanxi's reign, a total of seven or eight thousand bandits from Changsha and Lingling, who were called generals, invaded Guiyang, Cangwu, Nanhai, and Jiaozhi. The governor of Jiaozhi and the prefect of Cangwu Wangfeng fled, and both counties fell into the hands of thieves.
The imperial court sent the censor Zhongcheng Shengxiu to recruit troops to attack, but he could not win.
There were more than 600 people from Ai County in Yuzhang who applied for the army but did not receive any reward. Feeling resentful, they rebelled, burned the counties in Changsha, invaded Yiyang, killed the county magistrate, and the number of followers increased.
The imperial court also sent an envoy, Ma Mu, to supervise Liu Du, the governor of Jingzhou, to attack. The battle was defeated, and both Ma Mu and Liu Du fled.
Emperor Huan ordered the ministers to recommend someone to replace Liu Du, and Shangshu Zhu Mu recommended Du Shang, who was promoted from the right school magistrate to the governor of Jingzhou.
Du Shang personally led his men and worked and rested with them. At the same time, he recruited all kinds of barbarians and offered rewards. He attacked the thieves and defeated them. Tens of thousands of people surrendered.
The old bandit leaders in Guiyang, Bu Yang and Pan Hong, were afraid of Du Shang's majesty and fled to the valley.
Du Shang pursued for hundreds of miles, and the thieves arrived in the South China Sea. They broke into three villages and obtained many treasures.
However, there were still many party members such as Bu Yang and Pan Hong. Du Shang wanted to continue the pursuit, but the soldiers were proud and had no fighting spirit.
Du Shang thought that if he delayed his troops, he would not be able to fight, and if he was forced to fight, he would flee, so he threatened Buyang and Pan Hong who had been thieves for ten years and were accustomed to attacking and retreating. Now there are too few soldiers to attack easily. You should wait for all the troops from the counties to arrive before you attack with them.
He also ordered the troops to go hunting. The soldiers were so happy that they all went hunting together.
Du Shang then secretly sent his cronies to secretly burn down the fortress, destroying all his treasures and savings.
Everyone came back from hunting without crying.
Du Shang expressed his condolences to everyone and deeply blamed himself, so he said: "Bu Yang and others have enough wealth to support several generations, but you are just not doing your best."
There are so few things lost, so why bother. After hearing this, everyone was indignant and excited, and came forward. Du Shang ordered the horses to have breakfast, and early the next morning, they went straight to the thief's residence.
Bu Yang, Pan Hong and others thought that the fortress was deep and solid, so they no longer took precautions. The officials attacked with vigor, and then defeated the bandits and leveled the bandits' nest.
Three years after Du Shang sent troops, all the bandits were put down.
In the seventh year, he was granted the title of Marquis of Youxiang and promoted to the prefect of Guiyang.
The next year, the capital was recalled.
At this time, Jingzhou soldiers Zhu Shan and others had been out for a long time and had insufficient financial resources. The soldiers were resentful and started rebellion again. Together with the Guiyang thief Hu Lan and more than 3,000 people, they attacked Guiyang again and burned the counties. The prefect Ren Yin abandoned the city and fled, and the number of thieves increased to tens of thousands.
Turning to attack Lingling, the prefect Chen Qiu defended the city and resisted the enemy.
The imperial court then sent Du Shang as Zhonglang General, leading 26,000 infantry and cavalry from Youzhou, Jizhou, Liyang, and Wuhuan to rescue Chen Qiu. He also mobilized troops from various counties with Changsha Governor Kang Xu and others to attack together, and defeated the thieves, beheading Hu Lan and other 3,500 people. The remaining thieves fled to Cangwu.
The imperial court issued an edict to reward Du Shang with a million yuan, and the rest of the people received different rewards.
At this time, Kangxu and Dushang were both famous generals and had made many meritorious deeds.
Xu, courtesy name Boxu, was from Danyang, and his countrymen praised him for his courage and wisdom.
At the beginning of the trial of guarding Xuancheng, all the natives who were far away in the deep forest, with their vertebrae and chirping in their buns and chirping birds, moved to the county. From then on, there were no more thieves in the territory.
Later, he became the Sima of the Zhongzi branch of Zhonglang General, defeated the Taishan bandits Gongsun Ju and others, defeated them, beheaded more than 3,000 people, and was granted the title of Marquis of Dongxiang, Wucheng, and enjoyed the title of 500 households in the city.
Later, he was promoted to the captain of Taishan, and the bandit Wangfeng escaped.
After arriving in Changsha, all the old thieves were put down.
summary: Du Shang, from Shanyin, rose from poverty to become Yu chief, known for strictness. As Wen'an magistrate, he relieved famine. In the fifth year of Yanxi, bandits from Changsha and Lingling invaded several counties. Du Shang was appointed Jingzhou governor, personally leading troops and offering rewards. He defeated the bandits, pursuing them to Nanhai. To motivate his soldiers, he burned his own treasures, then led a surprise attack, destroying the bandits' nest. He was made Marquis of Youxiang and Guiyang prefect. Later, when rebels rose again, he was sent as Zhonglang General, defeating them and beheading 3,500. He became Jingzhou governor again but falsely accused Zhang Pan. After a trial, he was pardoned for prior merits. He later served as Liaodong governor, defeating the Xianbei. He died in office at age fifty.

translation:
At this time, cunning thieves from Cangwu and Guiyang gathered together to attack the counties. There were many thieves but Yang Xuan's troops were weak. The officials and the people were very worried. Yang Xuan then specially built dozens of carriages, filled the carriages with a row of bags filled with lime, and tied cloth ropes to the horses' tails. He also made military carriages, specially equipped with bows and crossbows, and agreed on a date for the battle.
So he ordered the carriage in front, blowing up the ashes with the wind, so that the thieves could not open their eyes, and burned the cloth with fire. The horses were frightened and rushed into the bandit formation. Then they called the carriage behind and fired their bows and crossbows. The sound of drums and drums shook the sky. The thieves scattered in fear. They chased, wounded and beheaded countless thieves, and the leader's head was displayed to the public. Peace was restored within the county.
Zhao Kai, the governor of Jingzhou, falsely accused Yang Xuan of not killing the thieves himself, but of claiming his merits.
Yang Xuanxiang and Zhang Zuo, Zhao Kai had party members to help, so the court used a carriage to recall Yang Xuan.
The ban was tight and there was no chance to explain the reason, so he bit his arm and it bled, and wrote a memorial in blood, detailing the situation of defeating the thief. He also talked about Zhao Kai's false accusation and secretly called his relatives to report to the court.
The imperial edict forgave Yang Xuan and worshiped him as Yilang, but Zhao Kai was accused of falsely accusing others.
Yang Xuan was promoted three times and became the prefect of Bohai. He showed signs of heterodoxy wherever he went, and was later dismissed due to circumstances.
Later, the minister ordered Zhang Wente to recommend him to the minister, Pushe.
He asked to retire due to illness and died at home.
summary: Yang Xuan, from Kuaiji, was a descendant of Yang Mao. His brother Yang Qiao refused to marry a princess and starved to death. Yang Xuan became Lingling prefect during Emperor Ling's reign. When thieves attacked, he used lime-filled carts and burning cloth to blind and scatter them, defeating the rebels. Governor Zhao Kai falsely accused him, but Yang Xuan wrote a blood memorial to the court, clearing his name. He was promoted to Yilang, and Zhao Kai was punished. He later became Bohai prefect but was dismissed. He retired due to illness and died at home.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/张法滕冯度杨列传

translation:
◆Zhang Hao's biography, Zhang Hao's courtesy name was Shuming, and he was a native of Wuyang, Qianwei County. Zhang Liang, the sixth generation ancestor, was the prince's young master during the reign of Emperor Gao and was granted the title of Liuhou.
When Zhang Hao was young, he traveled to the capital to study. In Yongyuanzhong, he returned to the prefecture and served as an official. He established the mansion of General Deng Zhi. He was promoted to Shangshu Pushe five times and served for eight years before becoming the prime minister of Pengcheng.
In the first year of Yongning, he was promoted to Tingwei.
Although Zhang Hao was not a Legalist, he paid attention to punishment and imprisonment, and often argued with ministers to correct doubts and doubts. Most of his opinions were adopted after careful consideration.
At this time, Emperor An deposed the crown prince as King of Jiyin, and Zhang Hao argued with Taichang Huanyan and Taipu about the origins of the throne in the court, but to no avail.
The matter has been recorded in the Biography of Origin.
Zhang Hao withdrew from the imperial court and wrote: "In the past, Jiang Chong, a traitor, made slanderous rumors and rebels, causing the military garden to raise troops, and finally disaster occurred."
Later, Linghu Mao, the third elder of Huguan, wrote a letter saying that the prince had been wronged, and Emperor Wu realized that although he could catch up on his previous mistakes, regretting it would be of no use!
Now that the crown prince is only ten years old, he still does not know the meaning of the nine virtues of the nanny master. He should choose virtuous people to assist him so that he can become the emperor.
The book was submitted but was not accepted.
Emperor Shun ascended the throne and appointed Zhang Hao as Sikong. He promoted many talents in office and the world called him a pusher.
At this time, Zhao Teng of Qinghe wrote a letter about the disaster, ridiculed the government, reported to those in charge, and arrested Zhao Teng and others for questioning. More than 80 party members were involved, all of whom should be severely punished for slandering the imperial court.
Zhang Hao's admonishment was: I heard that Yao and Shun set up drums for remonstrance, and three kings set up slander trees. The Spring and Autumn Annals collect good things and write about bad things, and the wise emperor does not inflict crimes on the common people in the grass.
Although Zhao Teng and others violated the law and violated the law, he spoke out of loyalty and integrity.
If he should be killed, the mouths of the people in the world would be blocked, and the source of remonstrances and disputes would be blocked. This is not a way to promote morality and set an example for future generations.
The emperor came to his senses and reduced Zhao Teng's death sentence to one degree, and the others were sentenced to two years of imprisonment.
Four years later, he was removed from office due to disagreement between yin and yang.
In the first year of Yangjia, he was promoted to Tingwei again.
He died in office this year at the age of eighty-three.
The imperial court sent envoys to offer condolences and gave him a burial place in Henan County.
Son Zhang Gang.
◆Zhang Gang's biography, Zhang Gang's courtesy name was Wen Ji, and he was proficient in Confucian classics when he was young.
Although he is a young master, he strictly enforces the integrity of common people.
If he was not praised for his filial piety and honesty, Situ, because of his excellent performance, appointed Gaodi as the imperial censor.
At this time, Emperor Shun indulged the eunuchs, which chilled the hearts of knowledgeable people.
summary: Zhang Hao, courtesy name Shuming, was from Wuyang, Qianwei County. His sixth-generation ancestor Zhang Liang served as prince's young master under Emperor Gao and was granted the title of Liuhou. Zhang Hao studied in the capital as a youth, later served as an official, and was promoted five times to Shangshu Pushe before becoming prime minister of Pengcheng. In Yongning's first year, he became Tingwei. Though not a Legalist, he emphasized proper punishment and often debated with ministers to correct doubts. When Emperor An deposed the crown prince, Zhang Hao argued unsuccessfully with officials. He later submitted a memorial citing historical examples of wrongful accusations and urging the selection of virtuous advisors for the young prince, but his advice was rejected. Under Emperor Shun, Zhang Hao became Sikong and promoted many talents. When Zhao Teng and others were arrested for criticizing the government, Zhang Hao admonished the emperor, citing ancient practices of accepting remonstrance, and persuaded him to reduce their sentences. He was removed from office due to natural disasters, reinstated as Tingwei in Yangjia's first year, and died in office at age eighty-three.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/张王种陈列传

translation:
Zhang Gang was excited and sighed with emotion: "The dynasty is full of filth and filth. I cannot step forward to eliminate the country's danger. Even though I am alive, I don't want to!"
So he wrote: "The Book of Songs" says: Don't make mistakes and don't forget, follow the old chapter.
It is said that Cheng Wang Lingde is just following the old regulations. The Han Dynasty was initially prosperous, and during the Zhongxing era, Emperor Wen and Emperor Ming had more prosperous moral education.
Looking at the governance measures at that time, it is obvious that it is not difficult to follow them, but it is just about promoting frugality, adhering to economy, and cultivating one's morality.
A middle official can only serve two people, and the people who serve on the left and right are rewarded with only a few gold coins. He cherishes expenses and respects people, so every family is rich.
Everyone has food and clothing. Yi Di knows that China is prosperous and strong, and upholds trust and morality, so treacherous plots are naturally eliminated and harmony is induced.
But recently, those who do not abide by the old rules and have no merit have been given official titles, making them rich, making them arrogant, and then punishing them. This is not loving people and valuing talents, flattering destiny, and obeying the great road.
Please give your Majesty some holy thought and organize your affairs in order to serve God's will.
The book was sent, but the emperor did not accept it.
In the first year of Han'an, eight envoys were selected to inspect social customs. They were all well-known old Confucian scholars with high status. Only Zhang Gang is young and has the lowest rank.
The rest of the people accepted the order and set off, but Zhang Gang buried his wheel alone in Duting, Luoyang, saying: "The jackals are in charge, why ask the fox!"
The report said: General Liang Ji, Henan Yin Bujie, cited by his relatives, enjoys the country's kindness, is a talent of the common people, and has the responsibility of tutoring the emperor and conducting state affairs. He cannot promote the five religions and support the emperor. He specializes in being a big pig and a snake. He is the chief culprit. He is greedy and cruel, devoted to good things, and indulges in unbridled and unbridled people. He cultivates a group of sycophants and frames Zhongliang.
This is something that cannot be pardoned by the emperor's authority and should be punished with death.
I would like to mention fifteen things about their unruly attitude, all of which are hated by the ministers.
The book came in and the capital was shocked.
At this time, Liang Ji's sister was the queen and was favored by the emperor. Zhu Liang's relatives were all over the court. Although the emperor knew that Zhang Gang was telling the truth, he finally couldn't bear to accept it.
At this time, Guangling thief Zhang Ying and tens of thousands of people killed the governor and two thousand stones, invaded and disturbed Yang and Xu Jian, and for more than ten years, the imperial court was unable to attack them.
Liang Ji then hinted to the minister to appoint Zhang Gang as the prefect of Guangling, hoping to attack and frame him.
In the past, the county guards sent there usually asked the court for more troops and horses, so Zhang Gang sent a bicycle alone to take office.
After arriving, he took only a dozen officials and soldiers to Zhang Ying's position, comforted them, and asked to meet their leader to explain the country's kindness to them.
Zhang Ying was surprised at first and saw Zhang Gang's sincerity, so he came out to pay Zhang Gang a visit.
Zhang Gang was invited to take a seat. Zhang Gang asked Zhang Ying what difficulties he had.
summary: Zhang Hao's son Zhang Gang, courtesy name Wen Ji, was proficient in Confucian classics and strictly maintained integrity. He became imperial censor under Emperor Shun. Distressed by the emperor's indulgence of eunuchs, Zhang Gang submitted a memorial contrasting the frugal governance of earlier Han emperors with current corruption, urging reform. The emperor did not accept it. In Han'an's first year, when eight envoys were selected to inspect customs, Zhang Gang alone buried his carriage wheel in Luoyang, declaring he would investigate the powerful rather than minor officials. He submitted a report condemning General Liang Ji and his relatives for corruption and tyranny. Though the emperor knew Zhang Gang was truthful, he did not act due to Liang Ji's influence. Liang Ji then appointed Zhang Gang as prefect of Guangling, hoping the bandit troubles there would destroy him. Zhang Gang went alone with few officials to meet the bandit leader Zhang Ying, persuading him to surrender through sincere discussion of loyalty and consequences. Over ten thousand people surrendered. Zhang Gang died at forty-six, with the people mourning deeply and Zhang Ying leading over five hundred in mourning attire to build his tomb.

translation:
◆The biography of Wang Gong, whose courtesy name is Bo Zong, was from Gaoping County, Shanyang County.
It has been a wealthy family for generations.
He was initially elected as Xiaolian and moved to the governor of Qingzhou. He impeached several people for embezzlement of two thousand dan. Emperor An commended him and conscripted him into Shangshu.
In the first year of Jianguang, he was promoted to Sili Xiaowei, and in the second year he was promoted to Runan prefect.
In order to advocate moderate politics and love talents, he introduced county people Huang Xian, Chen Fan and others.
Although Huang Xian refused to give in, Chen Fan became an official.
Chen Fan was a man of good temperament. When he first arrived at the house, Wang Gong did not summon him immediately.
So I left a note and went back saying I was sick.
Wang Gong was angry and wanted to remove Chen Fan's name.
The meritorious Cao Yuan Lang asked to see Wang Gong and said: I heard that there is a saying in "Zhuan": If a minister is not understood by the king, he will not dare to stand in the court. Since Chen Fan was introduced as a wise person, he should not be dismissed as inappropriate.
Wang Gong changed his color and said: It's my fault!
So he treated him politely.
Therefore, the late and famous people all admired Wang Gong.
Yuan Lang, whose courtesy name was Fenggao, resigned from the government service several times and did not seek any special conduct, but he enjoyed great fame at the time.
In the first year of Yongjian's reign, Wang Gong was recruited as his servant and transferred to Taichang.
In the fourth year, he was promoted to Sikong, but was dismissed due to the earthquake.
In the first year of Yonghe, he was appointed Taiwei.
He is serious and prudent when in office. It is not official business, and he does not communicate with the state or county by letters.
Those he appointed were all respected elders in the country.
Wang Gong was deeply concerned about the monopoly of eunuchs and was determined to save the situation. So he wrote a letter to express the harm caused by the eunuchs and asked the emperor to banish them.
The eunuch was so frightened that the guests submitted a petition to falsely accuse Wang Gong of being guilty. Emperor Shun ordered Wang Gong to confess his guilt as soon as possible.
Li Gu, the former minister, was working as a lieutenant for the general Liang Shang at this time, so he wrote to Liang Shang and said: Today I heard that the emperor ordered the prince to admit his guilt. I don't know the extent of the matter.
The prince cultivates himself, maintains strict moral integrity, loves art and literature, does not ask for things he does not deserve, and does not do things he does not do. In vain, because of his chastity and disobedience to the world, he was dissatisfied by some people, and was brutally slandered and framed. When everyone heard this, everyone sighed and trembled.
The three princes have high responsibilities, support the emperor, and are like three platforms. They have no reason to complain to the judge.
With a little bit of energy, just deal with it casually. Therefore, the old laws and regulations stipulate that unless there is a serious crime, there is no need to interrogate.
The prince is calm and intelligent, so he cannot be treated irrationally.
If something unexpected happens suddenly, then the court will have a reputation of being harmful to the virtuous, and all the ministers will lose their responsibility to save it!
In the past, Jianghou Zhou Bo was offended, and Yuan An appealed for him and was acquitted; Wei Shang was found guilty, and Feng Tang appealed for him. Emperor Wen at that time thought that they had done a good job, and this matter was recorded in the biography.
Now the general relies on the emperor in the court and controls the power of the country outside. His prestige is clear, his words are respected, and no one dares to disobey his command. He should come to the rescue and save the prince from difficulties.
As the saying goes: A good man is in trouble and waits for food when he is hungry.
This is the time. Liang Shang immediately told the emperor and the matter was resolved.
Wang Gong reigned for five years. Due to old age and illness, he asked to go home and died at home.
The son's name is Wang Chang. ◆Wang Changzhuan, Wang Chang's courtesy name is Shumao.
When he was young, he was praised for his honesty and integrity. Rarely socializes with people.
In the beginning, he was filial and honest, and he didn't respond to illness.
General Liang Shang was appointed as Maocai, moved to Shangshuling, and then sent as Prime Minister of Qi.
He was conscripted into Sili Xiaowei and transferred to Yuyang Prefect.
Wherever he went, he was praised for his seriousness and shrewdness.
He was convicted and dismissed from office.
At this time, most of the affairs of the imperial court were assigned to the minister. Emperor Huan specifically issued an order to the three Dukes to elect people with merit and ability as minister. Taiwei Chen Fan recommended Wang Chang, saying that he was honest, fair, and inviolable, so he was appointed minister again.
Soon, he was appointed as the governor of Nanyang.
summary: Wang Gong, courtesy name Bo Zong, was from Gaoping County, Shanyang. He served as Qingzhou governor, impeaching corrupt officials, and was promoted to Shangshu. He became Runan prefect, where he promoted moderate governance and introduced talented individuals like Huang Xian and Chen Fan. When Chen Fan left a note claiming illness after not being immediately received, Wang Gong initially wanted to dismiss him but was persuaded otherwise by meritorious official Yuan Lang. Wang Gong later became Taiwei, maintaining strict propriety and appointing respected elders. Concerned about eunuch power, he submitted a memorial requesting their banishment. Eunuchs retaliated by falsely accusing him, and Emperor Shun ordered him to confess. Li Gu wrote to General Liang Shang urging intervention, citing historical precedents, and the matter was resolved. Wang Gong served five years before retiring due to age and illness, dying at home.

translation:
The two thousand stones before him were all afraid of the noble relatives of the Imperial Township, and most of them were incompetent.
Wang Chang hated them deeply, and as soon as he took office, he showed his power. Those who were guilty among them were investigated and exposed one by one. When the imperial court granted amnesty, the matter was resolved.
Wang Chang's old grudges were still lingering, and he established another regulation. If each person who received more than 20 million stolen goods refused to surrender and admit it, all his property would be confiscated. If there was any concealment, officials would be sent to demolish houses, cut down trees, fill in wells and flatten stoves. Some evil forces were greatly shocked.
Zhang Chang, a meritorious scholar, wrote a letter to remonstrate: "The Five Religions are broad and have been written in the classics."
Shang Tang said that when the net is removed from three sides, all directions will submit to his benevolence.
When King Wu entered the Yin Dynasty, he first got rid of Zhou's punishment of cannon burning.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty saw the harsh governance of the Qin Dynasty and only made three chapters of the agreement.
Emperor Xiaowen was moved by Tiying's letter to redeem his father and removed the corporal punishment.
Zhuo Mao, Wen Weng, and Zhao Fu's disciples all hate evil as much as their enemies, but their masters are gentle and kind.
The political voice of benevolence and virtuousness will be passed down to future generations.
Those wise and sage monarchs have a sparse legal network and do not seek strictness. Then the three lights of the sun, moon and stars shine above, and the figures below are delighted.
These words may seem pedantic, but their effect is immediate.
Demolishing houses and cutting down trees is a preparation for harsh and violent measures. Although it is intended to punish bad people and bad deeds, I am afraid that it will have a bad impact on people in distant places.
You have the wisdom and talent, you are as bright as the sun and the moon, and you implement benevolent politics to change the old views in the country. It is as easy as breaking a branch, but it is not as difficult as carrying Mount Tai to cross the North Sea.

In the early days of Jian'an, he visited Xuchang and arrived in Yingchuan for the first time. He secretly had a business card in mind and was ready to meet the people he wanted to see.
In the end, no one could see it, and the words on the business card were also erased. At this time, Xuchang was newly built, and wise officials came from all directions.
Someone asked Mi Heng: Why not go and see Chen Changwen and Sima Boda?
Mi Heng replied: Where can I go to Tuguer?
He also asked: How are Xun Wenruo and Zhao Zhichang?
summary: Zhang Chao, named Zibing, was from Hejian. He had literary talent and served as Sima under Zhu Chi against the Yellow Turbans. He wrote nineteen pieces and was also skilled in cursive calligraphy.

translation:
Mi Heng came to a stop in front of Cao Cao, and the official scolded him: "Why didn't Drum Master remodel it?" Do you dare to come in casually like this? Mi Heng said: Yes.
So he first unbuttoned his underwear, then the rest of his clothes, stood naked, then slowly took out the ash grass and a single twist and put it on. After putting it on, he went out without any shame.
Cao Cao laughed and said, "I wanted to insult you, but I didn't expect to be humiliated by him."
Kong Rong came out to rebuke Ni Heng and said, "Zhengping is an elegant gentleman. Shouldn't he be like this?"
Just say that Cao Cao treats him well.
Mi Heng agreed to visit Cao Cao.
Kong Rong went to see Cao Cao again and said that Ni Heng was mentally ill. Now please go to see Cao Cao to apologize. Cao Cao was happy and ordered the gatekeeper to notify him if any guests came.
After waiting for a long time, Mi Heng sat at the gate of the camp, wearing single clothes and a sparse towel, holding a three-foot wooden stick, hitting the ground with the stick and cursing.
The official told Cao Cao that there was a madman sitting outside the camp gate and his words were reactionary. Please arrest him and punish him.
Cao Cao became angry and said to Kong Rong: "You Heng, if I kill him, it's just like killing a sparrow and a mouse."
But this man is usually a bit vain. Kill him and say I can't tolerate others. Now give it to Liu Biao. What do you think?
So he sent someone to escort you Heng.
Before leaving, everyone saw him off and set up a banquet in the south of the city. They agreed to each other: Mi Heng is rude and rude. Now because of his lateness, everyone should not get up to convince him.
When Mi Heng arrived, no one stood up. Mi Heng sat down and cried loudly.
Everyone asked him why? Mi Heng said: What is sitting is a tomb, and what is lying is a corpse. Can one not feel sad among the corpse and the tomb?
Liu Biao and the scholar-bureaucrats in Jingzhou both admired Mi Heng's talent and reputation at first, and were very polite to him. No one could finalize his articles and comments, not Mi Heng.
Liu Biao once drafted the chapter memorial together with other literati, using everyone's talents. At this time, Mi Heng went out and came back to read it. Before he finished reading it, he tore it up and threw it on the ground.
Liu Biao was greatly surprised.
Mi Heng asked Liu Biao for pen and ink, and he wrote it in a short time. The words and meanings are very good.
Liu Biao was very happy and valued him even more.
Later, he insulted Liu Biao, which Liu Biao thought was shameful and could not tolerate it. He thought Huang Zu, the governor of Jiangxia, was impatient, so he treated him well because he sent Ni Heng to him.
You Heng served as his secretary, and the severity and density were appropriate.
Huang Zu held Mi Heng's hand and said, "Virgin scholar, this is exactly what I want. It seems to be what I am thinking."
Huang Zu's eldest son, Huang She, served as the prefect of Zhangling and became close to Ni Heng.
He once went on a trip with Mi Heng and read the inscriptions written by Cai Yong together. Huang She liked the inscriptions, but it was a pity that he did not write them down.
Mi Heng said: Although I only read it once, I can still remember it. It’s just that there are two words missing on the stele and I don’t know it.
Just write it down. Huang She sent someone to copy the inscription and come back to proofread it. It was exactly as Mi Heng had written. Everyone was impressed.
summary: Mi Heng, named Zhengping, was from Pingyuan. He was good at debating and arrogant. He visited Xuchang but refused to see most officials, only respecting Kong Rong and Yang Xiu. Kong Rong recommended him to Cao Cao in a letter praising his talent. Mi Heng refused to meet Cao Cao and insulted him. Cao Cao made him a drum official to humiliate him, but Mi Heng humiliated Cao Cao by stripping naked. Cao Cao then sent him to Liu Biao. Mi Heng insulted Liu Biao, who sent him to Huang Zu. Mi Heng served as Huang Zu's secretary and impressed him. He later insulted Huang Zu, who ordered his execution. He was twenty-six years old.

translation:
◆Biography of Alchemy, Preface, Confucius talked about the "Book of Changes" which said that there are four principles of "the way of a gentleman", one of which is to use tortoise shell or divination grass for divination.
The so-called divination was used by the ancient kings to predict misfortunes and fortunes, to decide problems, and to let the gods give instructions to determine the meaning of everything in the future.
There are many records in ancient books about the theories of Yin and Yang that speculate on the future.
But the crazy ultimatum, the jade-cement golden rope, hidden in a mysterious place and sealed on the Yao altar, can no longer be seen.
As for the Hetu Luoshu, the images of turtles and dragons, Jizi's alchemy, Shikuang's secret book, Weihou, etc., and seal talismans, they are all used to speculate on unknown numbers and test the good and bad luck of personnel, and sometimes they are heard.
There are many schools of them, such as Feng Jiao, Dun Jia, Qi Zheng, Yuan Nian, Six Days and Seven Points, Feng Zhan, Ri Zhe, Ting Zhuan, Xu Yu, Luxu Technique, etc., as well as those who look at the clouds and calculate the energy, infer good and bad, sometimes it seems to be somewhat effective.
But after all, this kind of thing is a bit vague, profound and mysterious, and quite difficult to explore. Therefore, Confucius did not talk about monsters, gods and the like, and rarely talked about life.
Sometimes the ending is mentioned without mentioning its origin, and sometimes the main idea is mentioned in a roundabout way, just to let people follow it without letting people know the reason behind it!
Ever since Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the people in the Han Dynasty had been very fond of alchemy and other things. There was no one in the world who knew the art of alchemy but had come here with some advice on their backs.
Later, Wang Mang pretended to usurp the throne under the pretense of Fu Fu. In the Eastern Han Dynasty, Guangwu believed in the prophecy, and some people who were following the trend came to the emperor's side to discuss the matter and talk loudly.
Therefore, Wang Liang and Sun Xian became the Great Sikong and Great Sima based on their plans. Zheng Xing and Jia Kui became famous because they echoed appropriately, while Huan Tan and Yin Min failed because of their opposition.
From then on, there were many people who studied divination and studied strange texts and numbers.
Therefore, some knowledgeable people were very angry when they saw these grotesque things, and they made impassioned speeches to the emperor, thinking that they must be abandoned.
Sima Qian also said: Reading the books of the Yin and Yang family makes people restrained and have many taboos.
That’s what I’m talking about.
Everything has its biases and cannot be without faults. Even the way of a saint is generally the same.
Some people accuse the shortcomings of "The Book of Songs" of being too real and almost stupid; the historical records of "The Book of Songs" are untrue and almost exaggerated.
But isn’t the shortcoming of numerology the secret and deception?
If you only talk about gentle and sincere poetic teachings and remove some foolish things, you will have a deep understanding of the Book of Songs; if you read through the history of the Tang and Yu dynasties without pursuing those false accusations, you will have a deep understanding of the Book of Books; if you only follow the rules of change in magic and do not believe in those vulgar words, then you will have a deep understanding of the mystery of magic. The ancients said: If you are not a person who truly understands the truth, the Dao will not be implemented in an empty way.
This means that most people get lost in the confusion and therefore stray too far from the right path.
Zhang Heng is considered the orthodox member of the Yin Yang family, and Lang Qiye has studied the signs of evil in the most detailed way. There are also many famous people who are also talented, but they still lack the skills to study. Now, here are some people who are good at pushing forward changes and can make up for current events. I would like to commend them here.
summary: Confucius discussed the "Book of Changes," noting that a gentleman's way includes divination using tortoise shells or grass. Ancient kings used divination to predict fortunes, solve problems, and receive divine guidance. Many ancient records contain theories of Yin and Yang for predicting the future, though certain mystical texts like the jade-cement golden rope are now lost. Various schools of divination exist, including Feng Jiao, Dun Jia, Qi Zheng, and others, along with cloud-reading and energy-calculation methods. These practices are often vague and difficult to explore, which is why Confucius rarely discussed supernatural matters. Since Emperor Wu of the Han dynasty, alchemy became popular. Wang Mang used prophecies to justify his usurpation, and Emperor Guangwu of Eastern Han believed in them, leading to many practitioners gaining positions. Some knowledgeable people opposed these practices. Sima Qian noted that Yin and Yang books make people restrained with many taboos. The text concludes that while everything has biases, understanding the true principles of magic requires rejecting vulgar interpretations.

translation:
◆Biography of Ren Wengong, Ren Wengong was from Langzhong, Bajun.
His father, Ren Wensun, knew the secrets of Tianguan Fengjiao.
When Wen Gong was young, he learned from his father and was called to work in the state.
During the reign of Emperor Ai, some people said that the prefect of Yueyuan wanted to make trouble, and the governor was very afraid, so he sent Duke Wen and five other people to inspect the boundaries of the county and take a peek at the actual situation.
They were living in the guest house together, and a storm suddenly came. Wen Gong quickly asked other workers to leave, saying that something bad would happen to harm people, so he drove the carriage and ran away.
Those who were engaged could not leave quickly, so Jun Guo sent troops to kill them, and Duke Wen was spared.
Later, when Wen Gong was engaged in governing the country, there was a severe drought at that time. He reported to the governor: On May 1st, there will be a flood. The change has come and cannot be prevented. The officials and the people should be called to prepare early.
The governor refused to listen, so Wen Gong prepared a big boat alone. Some people heard about it, and some took precautions. When the drought was at its worst, Wen Gong hurriedly moved away and sent someone to report to the governor, who laughed it off.
The sun was about to hit the middle of the day, clouds started to rise in the north, and soon it rained heavily. By evening, the water suddenly rose by more than ten feet, destroying houses and injuring thousands of people.
Duke Wen became famous for his divination skills.
He was called Sikong Peng.
Emperor Ping ascended the throne and returned home claiming to be ill.
After Wang Mang usurped the throne, Duke Wen knew that a great chaos was coming, so he trained his family members to carry hundreds of kilograms of stuff and run around the house dozens of times a day. No one knew the reason at the time.
Later, when soldiers and bandits broke out, few of those who fled were able to escape. Only Wen Gong and his family carried food and walked quickly, and they were all spared.
So he ran to Zigong Mountain and survived the military revolution for more than ten years.
During Gongsun Shu's reign, a stone broke off at Wudan Mountain in Sichuan.
Duke Wen said: Alas!
When a wise man from Xizhou died, I met him.
From then on, his descendants often gathered together to have wine and food, and he died in the next three months.
Therefore, the Yibu people have a saying: Ren Wengong has unparalleled wisdom.
Guo Xian's biography, Guo Xian's courtesy name is Ziheng, and he was born in Runan Song Dynasty.
When he was young, he worshiped Zhongzi, the king of Donghai, as his teacher.
At that time, Wang Mang was the chief minister and summoned Zhongzi to go. Zhongzi wanted to go.
Guo Xian remonstrated: According to etiquette, only those who come to learn, not those who teach.
Nowadays, the king is humble, Taoist and fearful of the noble, so I don’t agree with him privately.
Zhongzi said: The prince is the most important person and he dare not disobey.
Xian said: Now is the time to talk about business and get things done.
Zhongzi obeyed, and Riyan went.
Wang Mang asked: Why are you late?
Zhongzi answered Guo Xian's words, and Wang Mang was secretly surprised.
Later, when he usurped the throne, he worshiped Guo Xian as a doctor and gave him clothes.
Guo Xian burned his clothes and fled to the coast of the East China Sea.
Wang Mang hated him very much and wanted to chase him but didn't know where he was.
When Guangwu came to the throne, he was looking for people with good moral principles in the world, so he called Xian to be a doctor.
He was promoted again, and in the seventh year of Jianwu, he served as Guang Luxun for Zhang Kan.
From driving to the southern suburbs.
When Guo Xian was in office, he suddenly looked back to the Northeast and took three sips of wine.
summary: Ren Wengong of Langzhong learned Tianguan Fengjiao from his father. During Emperor Ai's reign, he correctly predicted a storm that killed his companions. Later, he predicted a flood during a drought, saving his family while thousands died. He became famous for divination and fled to Zigong Mountain during the military revolution, surviving by training his family to carry food and run quickly. Guo Xian of Runan studied under Zhongzi. He advised Zhongzi against visiting Wang Mang, who later became emperor and appointed Guo Xian as a doctor. Guo Xian burned his clothes and fled. Under Emperor Guangwu, he served as Guang Luxun. He predicted a fire in Qi state and advised against military campaigns. He later resigned due to illness and died at home.

translation:
Law enforcement officers reported this as an act of disrespect.
The emperor issued an edict to ask why.
Xian replied: Qi is on fire, so use this to suppress it.
Later, Qi Guoguo reported a fire, which was the same date as the trip to the suburbs.
In the eighth year, the chariots marched westward to Kaihuo. Guo Xian admonished him: "The world has just settled down, and the chariots cannot move."
Guo Xian immediately pulled out his knife and cut off the chariot leather lead.
The emperor did not obey, so he went to Long.
Later, Yingchuan troops rose up and they returned.
The emperor sighed: "I regret not using Zi Heng's words."
At that time, the Xiongnu invaded the border fortress several times, and the emperor was very worried, so he summoned hundreds of officials to discuss it at the court.
Guo Xian believed that the world was exhausted and should not mobilize troops.
The remonstrance was not in line with his wishes, so he fell to the ground and said he was dizzy and stopped talking.
The emperor sent two men to help him go down to the palace, but Guo Xian did not bow.
The emperor said: I often hear that Guandong Gong Guo Ziheng, this is absolutely true.
Guo Xian then resigned due to illness and died at home.
Xu Yangzhuan, also known as Xu Yang, was named Weijun and was a native of Pingxing, Runan.
When I was young, I liked arithmetic.
When Wang Mang was assisting the government, he was called Lang, and soon he was promoted to Captain of Jiuquan.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, Xu Yang changed his name to become a witch doctor and fled to another place.
Wang Mang failed and returned to his hometown.
In the old days of Runan there was Honggu and Pipi. When he became emperor, Prime Minister Zhai Fang came forward to ask for its destruction.
During the Jianwu period, the prefect Deng Chen wanted to restore his merits. Hearing that Xu Yang knew about the water veins, he summoned him to discuss with him.
Xu Yang said: In the past, Emperor Cheng used Fang Jin's words. Not long ago, he dreamed of going to heaven. The Emperor of Heaven became angry and said: Why did you defeat me in Zhuo Longyuan?
From then on, the people lost their profits and suffered from hunger and poverty.
There was a ballad at that time: Zhai Ziwei, who defeated me, made me soybeans and cooked my taro.
If you use your backhand to overturn, you should make a comeback.
In the past, Dayu created rivers and dredged rivers to benefit the world. Today, the Ming Dynasty established waste industries to enrich the country and secure the people. The words of the nursery rhyme will be effective here.
I am really willing to die for this.
Deng Chen was overjoyed, so he appointed Yang as the governor of the capital and put him in charge of this matter.
The terrain of Xu Yangshun is high and low, and the pond is more than 400 miles away. It took several years to complete it.
The people benefited from it and had good harvests year after year.
At first, the surname Hao You wanted to take over the power of that area for the sake of repairing Bei, but Xu Yang refused to listen, so they jointly framed Yang for accepting bribes.
Deng Chen imprisoned Xu Yang. But the handcuffs will be released naturally.
The jailer was frightened and immediately reported to Deng Chen.
Deng Chen was shocked and said: "It's really bad. The prefect heard that loyalty can move the gods. Has it come true now?"
Xu Yang was immediately released that night and allowed to go home.
summary: Xu Yang of Runan, skilled in arithmetic, served under Wang Mang but fled when Wang usurped the throne. He helped restore irrigation systems in Runan, completing over 400 li of ponds over several years. Despite being falsely accused of bribery, his handcuffs miraculously opened, and he was released. He died of illness, and a temple was built in his honor.

translation:
It was very dark and there seemed to be firelight shining on him on the road, which made people feel very strange at the time.
Later Xu Yang died of illness.
Deng Chen built a temple for Xu Yang in the capital palace and painted portraits. The people remembered his achievements and went to worship him.
Gao Huozhuan, named Jinggong, was from Xinxi, Runan.
The appearance is that the four sides of the face are high and the middle is low.
When he was young, he studied in the capital and had an old relationship with Emperor Guangwu.
He worshiped Situ Ouyang She as his teacher.
Ouyang She was imprisoned and sentenced. Gao Huo, wearing an iron hat and torture tools, went to the court to beg for She's pardon.
Although the emperor did not pardon She, he introduced Gao Huo.
He said to Gao: "Jing Gong, I want to use you as an official, but you should change your normal behavior."
Gao Huo replied: I have inherited my nature from my parents and cannot change it with Your Majesty.
When he came out, he said goodbye and left. The three princes fought to summon him, but they refused.
Later, the prefect Bao Yu asked for Huo. When he arrived at the door, he sent the chief clerk to greet him. The chief clerk only sent the cavalry to greet him. Gao Huo heard this and left immediately.
Bao Yu pursued Gao Huo, but Gao Huo turned around and said, "The Lord of the House has been deceived by his master, and it is not enough to talk to him."
Will not stay.
At that time, there was a severe drought in the county. Gao Huo had always been good at astronomy, knew Dunjia, and could manipulate ghosts and gods.
Bao Yu himself went to ask how to get the rain. Gao Huo said: "I will immediately remove the three departments of postal supervision. The Ming government should go out from the north to Sansili Pavilion, and the rain can come."
Bao Xian complied, and sure enough he received heavy rain.
Every time he visits a county, he always greets his family with courtesy.
Gao Huo fled to the south of the Yangtze River and died in Shicheng.
The people of Shicheng missed him and built a shrine in his honour.
Biography of Wang Qiao, Wang Qiao, a native of Hedong.
During the reign of Emperor Xianzong, he became the magistrate of Ye County.
Wang Qiao has magical powers. On the first and fifteenth day of every month, he often travels from Ye County to the forbidden provinces of the imperial court to meet with the emperor.
The emperor saw that he came very quickly, but did not see his carriage and horses. He felt strange and secretly asked Taishi to spy on his whereabouts.
Taishi reported that when Wang Qiao arrived, two water birds often flew from the southeast.
So the emperor asked people to open a net to catch water birds, but only got one shoe.
Check the shoes. They are the shoes given to the minister's officials in four years. Whenever Wang Qiao goes to court, the drum at the gate of Ye County does not beat but plays by itself, so that the capital can hear it.
Later, a jade coffin dropped from the sky to the front of the hall. Officials stepped forward to push it, but they could not move it.
Wang Qiao said: Did God call me alone?
So he washed himself, got dressed, slept in the coffin, and the lid was immediately closed.
After two nights, the coffin was buried in the east of the city, and the soil naturally turned into a grave.
That night, the cattle in the county were sweating and panting, but people didn't know what was going on.
The people built a temple for him, called Ye Jun Temple.
summary: Gao Huo of Runan studied under Ouyang She and had an old relationship with Emperor Guangwu. He refused to change his behavior for an official position. Skilled in astronomy and Dun Jia, he helped bring rain during a drought. He later fled to Jiangnan and died in Shicheng, where a shrine was built for him. Wang Qiao of Hedong served as magistrate of Ye County during Emperor Xianzong's reign. He traveled to court magically every month, arriving with two water birds. When caught, only one shoe was found. A jade coffin descended from heaven, and Wang Qiao entered it, which closed immediately. The coffin was buried, and a temple called Ye Jun Temple was built. Local officials must pay homage upon arrival.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/方术列传上

translation:
Every time local officials arrive at their posts, they must first pay homage to it.
When officials pray for something, it is very effective.
If there is any violation of God's will, disaster will be imposed immediately.
The emperor then took the drum from Ye County and placed it under the capital pavilion. From then on, there was no more sound.
Some people say that this is the ancient immortal prince Qiao.
Xie Yiwu's biography, Xie Yiwu's courtesy name is Yaoqing, a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
When he was young, he worked as a county official and studied in style.
The prefect Wu Lun promoted him to postal supervisor.
At that time, Wu Chengchang was guilty of embezzlement, and Wu Lun sent him to imprison Wu Chengchang and try his crimes.
After Yiwu arrived at the county, he did not check it. He only looked at the pavilion and returned crying.
People in the county were surprised and didn't know what they were doing.
When he came back, he reported to Wu Lun: "I used Zhanhou to know that Chief Wu Cheng would die in thirty days but not in sixty days. He would rest as a wandering soul and would not be punished, so I did not arrest him."
Wu Lun listened to his words, and after a month or so, a post came and sent Chang Wu Cheng's seal and ribbon, saying that he died of a sudden illness.
Fifth Lun was more polite and convinced.
Xie Yiwu was promoted to Xiaolian and made the longevity magistrate. Soon he was promoted to the governor of Jingzhou and the prefect of Julu.
Care for people wherever you go and have good political achievements.
Later Wu Lun became a Situ and asked Ban Gu to write an article recommending Xie Yiwu Dao: I heard that Yao used Ji and Qi to achieve prosperity and peace in politics; Shun used Gao Tao to promote Yongxi.
Although the Yin and Zhou Dynasties had monarchs such as Gaozong, King Wen, and King Wu, they relied on the strategies of Fu Shuo and Lu Wang, so they were able to respect their careers and cooperate with Dazhong.
I personally saw Xie Yiwu, the governor of Julu, Kuaiji, who came from Dongzhou. He was covered with mud, but his appearance was very special and his majesty showed off.
Talent combines four subjects, conduct encompasses nine virtues, benevolence is enough to help every time, and wisdom encompasses all things.
At a young age, he learned to be refined and elegant, compiled six books, studied stars, comprehensively studied catalogues, studied sacred secrets, observed variations, divined the heaven and earth, became in harmony with God, and carried out royal affairs according to his morality.
In the past, I served as a companion, worked with the ministers, and upheld his loyalty and integrity. He helped me to uphold discipline. Apart from cowardice, I was exempted from violence. It is really due to his merits.
When he was selected as the prime minister, he benefited hundreds of miles, brought great blessings, and became a god, so he became the governor of Jingzhou and exercised authority over the country.
Administer according to the law, with the demeanor of Zhou Gong and Zhao Gong; live frugally and inherit the ethics of public etiquette.
In terms of ability, he can act as an external figure; if he listens to the truth and observes the truth, he can be the crown of the Kyushu, move to Julu, and have a harmonious government.
In terms of morality, performance, and planning, Yi Yin, Lu Shang, Guan Zhong, and Yan Ying had the talent, and they were equal to Shi Su, Jing Fang, and others. Although he is engaged in official duties, he is reclusive and does not seek fame or favor. He is humble and plays the role of Jishan. Compared with ancient sages, he is really ethical; compared with today's people, he is extraordinary and refined. He is indeed the great tortoise of the country and the pillar of the Han Dynasty. He should be promoted to Dingsi, to the three-chen court, and to the fifth-grade salt training. He will definitely be happy, not just abide by the law and serve his duties.
I am a stubborn servant with a talent that is different from others of the same kind. I sit in a plain position and am very vigilant. I am willing to ask for resignation and give way to Yiwu. I will show the light of the seven rays above and satisfy the people's hopes below. I have no regrets.
Later, during the spring trip, he took a chariot and followed two officials. The governor of Jizhou reported that he had failed in the ritual order and was damaging to the national code, so he was demoted to Xiapiling.
summary: Xie Yiwu of Kuaiji served as a county official and postal supervisor. He predicted a criminal's death within thirty days, which came true. He became governor of Jingzhou and prefect of Julu, known for good governance. Wu Lun recommended him highly, comparing him to ancient sages. He later knew his death date in advance and died as expected.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/方术列传上

translation:
He knew the day of his death in advance, and he died as expected.
His son said in his will: In the last years of the Han Dynasty, when there was chaos, graves would be dug up and corpses exposed.
He asked his son to be buried with a hanging official without leaving the top of the grave.
At that time, Dr. Bo Hai and Guo Feng were also good at prophesying and predicting disasters, and their divination of good and bad luck was very successful.
Know your death date first, and ask your disciples to buy coffins and burial materials in advance to die on that day.
Yang Youchuan, whose courtesy name is Aihou, was born in Chengdu, Shu County. When I was young, I studied the "Book of Changes", as well as the Qizheng, Yuanqi, Fengyunzhanhou, etc.
Became a county literary publisher.
At that time, there were big birds gathering in the warehouse at night. The prefect Lian Fan asked Yang You, who replied: According to the divination, there should be small soldiers in the county, but they will not cause harm.
More than twenty days later, barbarians invaded Guangrou County, killing and wounding officials. The county mobilized troops to attack them, and the chaos subsided.
Another wind blew and cut the food, and the prefect asked Yang You again.
You replied: When there is a person who recommends solid wood, his color is yellow.
Soon, Wu Guan offered several bags of oranges.
Yang You once went to someone's house to drink. He said to the coachman: If you drink for three hours, you should get up quickly.
Soon he was urged to leave.
Later, there was a fight and murder behind the master's room, and people asked Yang You how he knew.
You replied: Just now there were turtledoves fighting on the trees in the Tutu Temple. This is a sign of soldiers and thieves.
Many of his words came true.
Yang You wrote more than ten books called "Qi Ping".
Died at home.
Li Nan's biography, Li Nan's courtesy name is Xiaoshan, and he was born in Gourong, Danyang.
He was eager to learn when he was young and knew the wind angle very well.
During the reign of Emperor Yongyuan, the prefect Ma Leng was summoned for a theft case, and he had to go to Tingwei to handle the case. The officials and the people were uneasy, and Li Nante called in to congratulate him.
Ma Leng was a little unhappy and said to Li Nan: The prefect is immoral and must be punished now, but why do you congratulate me instead?
Li Nan said: There is good wind in the morning, and good news should arrive at noon tomorrow, so I come to congratulate you.
The next morning, Ma Leng stretched his neck to look at the shadow of the sun, thinking that it was not working. At noon, there was an edict from the post envoy to forgive Ma Leng.
Li Nan asked why he was late.
The messenger said: When passing through Wanling Puliyan the day before yesterday, the horse broke its foot, so it could not be reached quickly.
Ma Leng was convinced.
Later, he was promoted as a Taoist scholar and summoned to the palace. However, he was unable to travel due to illness and died at home.
Li Nan's daughter also knew family skills and became the wife of a native of Youquan County.
Arriving in the kitchen in the morning, a sudden storm broke out. The woman went to the main room to ask her mother-in-law for leave to go back and say goodbye to her parents. Her mother-in-law refused, so the daughter-in-law knelt down and cried: My family specializes in ancestral magic. A sudden strong wind blows the chimney and derrick of the stove first. This disaster will surely befall the woman who is in charge of cooking in the kitchen. This is a sign that I will die.
So the date of her death was stated.
Her mother-in-law asked her to go back, and she died of illness as expected.

Such is his righteousness.

In the middle of the year, he moved to Taishan Prefecture.
Zhu Hui asked Shangshu to stay in China, and the imperial edict agreed.
So he wrote a letter to talk about politics and tell secrets, which was deeply praised and adopted.
The imperial edict said: This is a good person who makes up for the shortcomings of the public and does not impair the quality of innocence.
The common officials are obedient, obedient, have no ambition to advance, but have no thought of retreat, and worry for a long time.
Only what I say now suits my wish.
Please encourage me, sir!
At this time, grain prices were high, county officials were short of funds, and the court was very anxious.
Shangshu Zhang Lin wrote: The reason why grain is expensive is because money is cheap.
You can seal off the money as much as possible, and use cloth and silk as rent, so that it can be used by the whole world.
Salt is also an urgently needed item in food. Although it is expensive, people cannot do without it, so it can be sold by the officials.
We should also buy treasures and harvest their benefits through the exchanges of officials in Jiaozhi and Yizhou. This is the so-called method of losing all during the reign of Emperor Wu.
So an edict was issued to the ministers for discussion.
Zhu Hui reported that Zhang Lin's plan was not feasible, so the matter was settled.
Later, some of the presenters repeated Zhang Lin's proposal and thought it would be beneficial to the country. The emperor agreed and the edict was implemented.
summary: During the Yuanhe period, Suzong summoned Zhu Hui as a minister. He later became Taishan Prefect but requested to remain in the capital. He wrote memorials on political matters, which were praised. When grain prices rose, Zhu Hui opposed Zhang Lin's proposal to control salt and currency, arguing it would harm the people. The emperor initially rejected his advice, and Zhu Hui asked to be imprisoned. After being pardoned, he claimed illness and refused to participate in politics. He died soon after.
