translation:
Zhu Hui then soloed and said: In the royal system, the emperor does not care about whether there is anything, the princes do not care about how much, and the officials do not compete with the people for profits.
Today's method of equalizing losses is no different from that of merchants. If salt and profits are returned to the officials, the people will be poor and urgent. If cloth is rented, many officials will cause trouble. It is indeed not a method that should be implemented by the Ming Dynasty.
The emperor finally thought that what Zhang Lin and others said was right. After Zhu Hui reconsidered, he became angry and blamed the ministers.
Zhu Hui and others asked themselves to be imprisoned.
Three days later, the imperial edict pardoned them.
The edict said: The country is willing to listen to different opinions. The veterans are not at fault. The edict is wrong. Why do you ask yourself to go to jail?
Zhu Hui then claimed that he was too ill and refused to participate in political discussions anymore.
The minister ordered the following people to be frightened, and said to Zhu Hui: Now that we are facing criticism, why do we claim to be ill and not come out? The disaster is not small!
Zhu Hui said, "I am already eighty years old. I have received the emperor's favor in secret, so I should repay him with death."
If you know it is impossible but follow the will, you will have the meaning of being a minister.
Today I hear nothing and see nothing, just wait and die.
So he kept silent and stopped talking.
The ministers didn't know what he was doing, so they impeached Zhu Hui together.
The emperor understood what everyone meant and would not pursue the matter further.
A few days later, the imperial edict Zhishilang asked about Zhu Hui's daily life, sent an imperial doctor to treat his illness, and the imperial official gave him food.
Zhu Hui then stood up to thank him and gave him another hundred thousand pieces of money, a hundred pieces of cloth, and ten sets of clothes.
Later, Zhu Hui was promoted to Shangshu Ling. Zhu Hui requested to retire because of his old age and illness. He was appointed as the Cavalry Captain and was given 200,000 yuan.
Emperor He came to the throne, Dou Xian went north to conquer the Xiongnu, and Zhu Hui went to Shu to give advice.
Soon, he died of illness.
His son Zhu Jie studied Confucianism and became prime minister at Chen during the reign of Emperor An.
Zhu Jie's son was Zhu Mu.
◆Zhu Mu's biography, Zhu Mu's courtesy name is Gongshu.
At the age of five, he had the reputation of being filial.
My parents are sick and often don't eat or drink. They only return to normal after recovering from the illness.
In the prime of life, it is easy to study and put more effort into speaking and reciting. Sometimes when thinking about a problem and concentrating on it, the clothes and clothes are missing without realizing it, and the team is in a state of confusion.
His father often thought that he was too attentive and almost stupid, and almost didn't know how to count the odds.
Zhu Mu studied his knowledge more carefully.
He began to be promoted as Xiaolian.
In the last years of Emperor Shun's reign, thieves arose in the Jianghuai area, and the prefectures and counties could not stop them.
Someone advised the general Liang Ji: "Uncle Zhu is a versatile man in both civil and military affairs and a great scholar in the country. If you use him as the mastermind, it will not be difficult to put down the thieves."
Liang Ji also often heard about Zhu Mu's reputation, so he promoted him to be in charge of military affairs. He was very close and valued.
When Emperor Huan came to the throne and Empress Dowager Shunlie came to the court to listen to the government, Zhu Mu believed that Liang Ji was powerful and hoped that he could support the royal family. So he deduced the source of the disaster and wrote a memorial to advise Liang Ji: Mu thought that next year will be the year of Ding Hai, and the punishment and virtue will be in line with the Qian position. The "Book of Changes" talks about the Dragon War Meeting. Its text says: When dragons fight in the wild, their path is exhausted.
It means that the Yang Dao will win and the vagina will lose.
The weather in September this year is depressing, and the five four-year-olds have lost their integrity. This is to explain each other's problems.
summary: Zhu Mu, courtesy name Gongshu, was known for filial piety at age five. He studied diligently, sometimes forgetting his appearance. During Emperor Shun's reign, he was recommended to General Liang Ji to suppress thieves. When Emperor Huan ascended, Zhu Mu advised Liang Ji to support the royal family, warning of disasters and recommending virtuous officials. Liang Ji partially heeded his advice.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/朱乐何列传

translation:
Most of the local shepherds and chief officials were not strictly selected people. They were greedy and treated everyone like prisoners. Some people died under beatings and torture, and some were forced to commit suicide.
In addition, officials plundered the people, all in the name of the government.
So the generals complained to the world, the officials were bitter and bitter, and the roads were full of sighs.
In the past, the politics of the Qin Dynasty were troubled and the people were in disarray. Chen Sheng raised his arms and shouted, and the whole world was abuzz, but the ministers who tried to please him in person said that everything was peaceful.
If you keep taboo on your evil deeds and do not change them, you will perish.
In the past, in the last years of Yonghe, the rules and regulations were slightly relaxed, which was quite disappointing.
In four or five years, the wealth is empty and the household is scattered, and there is a sense of disunity.
Ma Sen's followers took advantage of the situation and almost caused serious trouble between Jingzhou and Yangzhou.
Fortunately, Queen Shunlie had a peaceful administration in the early days and worked together internally and externally to bring peace.
Now the people are worried that the difficulties are greater than everlasting peace. Internally, it is not tolerated by a benevolent heart, and externally, it is not suitable for the long-term peace of the country.
The generals, ministers, ministers, and the head of state are one body. They ride in the same car and go out to sea in the same boat. If the car capsizes and the ship sinks, we will suffer hardships together.
Is it possible to let go of light and darkness, take risks, be alone and trapped, and no one comes to save you?
Incompetent people should be replaced in time, the cost of houses and gardens should be reduced, and the property donated by the county should be rejected.
It is self-explanatory internally and resolves people's doubts externally, so that the corrupt officials who kidnap people have no support, and the supervisory officials can fulfill their responsibilities as eyes and ears.
Once the laws are established and the laws are kept clear far and near, then the general will show his respect for his actions and his virtues will shine forever in future generations.
The way of heaven is clear and I don’t believe it. I hope you will read it carefully.
Liang Ji did not adopt it, but became even more indulgent. He also accepted gifts and bribes from left and right, had close contacts with the eunuchs, and appointed his children and guests to important positions in the state and county.
Zhu Mu wrote another letter to remonstrate, but Liang Ji never realized it.
Liang Ji reported a book and said: Doesn't this benefit me?
Although Zhu Mu spoke sincerely, he did not think he was guilty.
In the first year of Yongxing, the Yellow River swelled, hundreds of thousands of households were affected by floods, and the people were starved and displaced.
There were more thieves in Jizhou, so Zhu Mu was promoted to be the governor of Jizhou.
The people of Jizhou had three eunuchs who served as regular attendants and visited Zhu Mu with letters of appeal.
Zhu Mu hated them and refused to see them.
When the commander of the Ji Ministry heard that Zhu Mu had crossed the river, more than forty people took off their seals and ribbons and left.
When Zhu Mu took office, he impeached all the counties, and some of them committed suicide.
Zhu Mu used his might and expediency to kill all the bandit leaders.
The powerful were impeached, and some died in prison.
summary: As Imperial Censor, Zhu Mu wrote essays criticizing contemporary customs. He admonished Liang Ji about his arrogance and corruption, warning of potential rebellion. Liang Ji ignored him. During a flood, Zhu Mu became Governor of Jizhou, where he impeached corrupt officials and executed bandit leaders. He even exhumed eunuch Zhao Zhong's father's tomb for illegal burial items. The emperor imprisoned him, but scholars petitioned for his release.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/朱乐何列传

translation:
From then on, Zhongguan repeatedly issued edicts to slander Zhu Mu.
Zhu Mu was by nature upright and unhappy. Not long after he returned home, he developed ulcers out of anger.
Yanxi died in the sixth year of his reign at the age of sixty-four.
After working as an official for decades, he lived on a vegetarian diet and lived in ordinary clothes, and his family had no money left.
The ministers jointly stated that Zhu Mu should be favored because he was loyal to the Qing Dynasty, pious and respectful of secrets, and upheld the right path to death.
The imperial court issued an edict and praised it, and presented it posthumously to the governor of Yizhou.
He wrote a total of twenty articles, including treatises, strategies, memorials, teachings, books, poems, notes, and ridicules.
When Zhu Mu was in Jizhou before, the people he promoted were all elders of Qingde, and most of them became public ministers and prefectures and counties.
His son Zhu Ye, who was rarely famous, served as an official in Yin, Henan.
At first, Zhu Mu's father died. Zhu Mu and other Confucian scholars followed the ancient meaning and gave him the posthumous name Mr. Zhenxuan. After Zhu Mu's death, Cai Yong shared his virtues with his disciples and was posthumously named Mr. Wenzhong. ◆The biography of Le Hui, whose courtesy name is Boqi, was from Changling, Jingzhao.
My father, Leqin, was a county official. He offended the county magistrate and was arrested and executed.
Lehui was eleven years old. He often fell down at the temple gate and cried day and night.
The county magistrate heard this and took pity on him, and immediately released Leqin.
When Lehui grew up, he was fond of studying Confucian classics and took Dr. Jiao Yong as his teacher. When Jiao Yong became the governor of Hedong, Le Hui followed Jiao to his official residence, where he studied behind closed doors and did not interact with others.
Later, Jiao Yong was investigated for his crimes, and his students were all arrested for opening his joints. Le Hui, whose innocence was not contaminated by the law, decided to become a famous Confucian.
If Lehui is upright and upright by nature, but his behavior does not suit his own will, he will not be friends with him even if he is very powerful.
Hou Yin of Xinyang sent gifts to Hui many times to please Hui, but Hui never responded.
Later, when Le Hui became a minor official in the county, the prefect was killed for breaking the law. Old friends did not dare to interact with each other, so Le Hui went to the funeral alone to pay for his crime.
After he came back, he did meritorious deeds again, and the election was fair and unfair. Please ask for help.
Yang Zheng of the same county slandered Le Hui several times in public. Later, Le Hui still promoted Yang Zheng's son as a filial and honest man, and the whole village obeyed him.
Later he was promoted to Sikong Mourong Mansion.
It happened that the fifth Lun, the governor of Shu County, replaced Mou Rong as Sikong. Lehui thought that Lun was from the same county and refused to stay in the post. He recommended Du An of Yingchuan and resigned himself.
Many princes praised his conduct, and he was summoned several times but failed to respond.
Later, the imperial court recruited Le Hui to serve as a minister.
At the time when Dou Xian, the chariot general, was on an expedition against the Huns, Le Hui wrote several letters to remonstrate with him, and the court said he was loyal.
He became a servant of Shangshu.
At this time, Henan Yinwangdiao and Luoyang ordered Li Fu and Dou Xian to have a close friendship and give up their freedom.
Yue Hui impeached Wang Tiao and Li Fu, and also involved Sili Xiaowei.
He did not evade the people he exposed and reported, so the nobles hated him.
Dou Xian's younger brother, Xia Yanghou Dou Wangxiang, wanted to greet Le Hui, but Hui declined and would not associate with him.
Dou Xian's brother indulged in indulgence, but he hated Le Hui for not agreeing with him.
Le Hui's wife said to Le Hui: In ancient times, there were people who took shelter to avoid harm. Why should you complain with your words?
Le Hui sighed: How can I bear to eat free rice and stand in someone else's court?
So Shangshu remonstrated: "I heard that the faults of hundreds of kings were all caused by their falling in power."
summary: Zhu Mu later served as Minister, deeply hating eunuchs. He petitioned to dismiss them and restore old Han regulations, but the emperor refused. Zhu Mu fell to the ground in protest. After repeated slander from eunuchs, he returned home and died of illness at sixty-four. He lived frugally, leaving no wealth. The court posthumously honored him. Le Hui, courtesy name Boqi, was from Changling, Jingzhao. At eleven, he cried daily at the county magistrate's gate to save his father from execution, succeeding. He studied under Dr. Jiao Yong and became a renowned Confucian. He refused gifts from Xinyang Houyin. As a minor official, he alone attended his prefect's funeral after the prefect was executed. He promoted his slanderer's son as a filial candidate. Le Hui served as a minister and remonstrated against Dou Xian's expedition against the Xiongnu. He impeached officials connected to Dou Xian. When Dou Xian's brother sought his friendship, Le Hui refused. He wrote memorials warning against relatives holding power. When his advice was ignored, he claimed illness and retired. Dou Xian persecuted him, and Le Hui poisoned himself. When Liu Chang was murdered by Dou Xian's agents, He Chang investigated despite opposition, earning praise. As Imperial Censor, he remonstrated against Dou Xian's military campaigns and his brothers' extravagant building projects. He later became Taifu of Jinan, assisting King Liu Kang with moral principles. As Prefect of Runan, he governed with leniency, repaired irrigation canals, and increased cultivated land. After the Dou family fell, he was dismissed due to his son's friendship with them. He later served as Wugan Zhonglang General but was falsely accused by Cai Lun and died at home.

translation:
Ministers presiding over state affairs are often blamed for the prosperity of the country.
Thinking of the late emperor, his saintliness was not long enough and he abandoned all nations long ago.
Your Majesty is in his prime years and is inheriting a great cause. Your uncles should not interfere with the royal family to show the selfishness of the world.
The scriptures say: Heaven and earth behave in harmony with each other, and all things die prematurely.
If the ruler and his ministers are out of order, thousands of people will suffer.
If political mistakes are not corrected, unexpected disasters will occur.
The current measures should be based on righteousness at the top, and modesty at the bottom.
The fourth uncle can protect the honor of the nobility and the emperor forever, and the empress dowager will never have to worry about being ashamed of the ancestral temple. This is the best policy.
The book was ignored.
At that time, Empress Dowager Dou was in charge of the government, and Emperor He did not personally intervene in state affairs. Le Hui thought that his opinions were not accepted, so he claimed illness and asked to retire.
The imperial court issued an edict to grant money and send imperial doctors to treat patients.
Lehui recommended Ren Chengguojun and Chengyang Gaofeng, but he said he was seriously ill.
The imperial court worshiped Lehui as the Cavalry Commander, and Lehui wrote a letter of thanks, saying: "I still received a great favor, but I can't repay it."
Confucius hated the fact that politics fell into the hands of officials; when Shiqing held great power, the Spring and Autumn Annals warned against this.
What the saint worries about is not empty words.
In recent times, when relatives are rich and powerful, they will inevitably suffer from arrogance.
Today, Your Majesty is obsessed with the mountains and mausoleums and has no involvement in political affairs. His uncles favor him and his power extends to all directions.
If you cannot reduce your own losses, punishment will surely come.
My life is about to end, and I will try my best to be loyal before my death, hoping to be noticed.
After hearing the imperial edict, he returned to his hometown.
Dou Xian therefore ordered the prefectures and counties to persecute Le Hui, and Le Hui drank the medicine and died.
Hundreds of disciples were buried in mourning clothes, and the people were grieved.
Later, the Dou family was killed and the emperor began to rule personally. He Rong, one of Le Hui's disciples, and others wrote a letter stating Le Hui's loyalty, and the imperial court granted his son Le Ji the title of doctor.
◆Biography of He Chang, He Chang was a native of Pingling, Fufeng.
His ancestor's home is in Ruyin.
Bigan, the sixth generation ancestor, studied Shangshu by mistake from Chao Dynasty. During the reign of Emperor Wu, he served as Tingweizheng at the same time as Zhang Tang.
Zhang Tang upheld the Dharma deeply and was more benevolent and forgiving than Gan. He fought with Tang several times, and although he could not win all of them, he helped thousands of people live.
Later he was promoted to Danyang Captain. So he moved to Pingling.
He Chang's father, He Chong, served as a captain of Qiancheng during the Jianwu period. He was dismissed from his post due to illness, so he lived in seclusion and did not serve as an official.
He Chang's character advocates justice.
He thinks that his hobbies are not suitable for the current affairs. Whenever he is called upon, he often complains that he is ill.
During the Yuanhe period, he was appointed Taiwei Song Youfu, and Song You treated him with special etiquette.
He Chang's discussion was very high, and he often cited general ideas and made many corrections.
Situ Yuanan also respected him very much.
summary: He Chang was from Pingling, Fufeng. His ancestor Bigan studied Shangshu and served as Tingwei during Emperor Wu's reign. He Chang served under Taiwei Song You, offering high-level discussions. He warned against treating strange birds and plants as auspicious signs. He advised Song You to reduce excessive rewards and relieve the poor during floods and droughts.

translation:
◆Zhu Fu's biography, Zhu Fu's courtesy name is Shu Yuan, and he was a native of Xiao, Pei State.
At the beginning, he served as the chief secretary of the Grand Sima from Guangwu, then moved to the general position, and followed him to break Handan.
Guangwu sent Wu Han to punish Gengshi Youzhou Mu Miaozeng, so he worshiped Zhu Fu as the general Youzhou Mu and guarded Jicheng, so he settled the northern border.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Wuyang and was granted the title of Sanxian.
Zhu Funian had few talents, and he wanted to revive his reputation and win over the scholars. He recruited famous people like Wang Cen from Zhuo County in the state to serve as officials, and two thousand stones from Wang Mang's former officials.
Peng Chong, the prefect of Yuyang, believed that the world was uncertain and the divisions and brigade were booming, so it was not appropriate to hire more officials to damage the army's food reserves, so he did not listen to Zhu Fu's orders.
Zhu Fu has a reserved and impatient temperament and thinks very highly of himself. Very dissatisfied with Peng Chong. Because he slandered Peng Chong with harsh words; Peng Chong was also very strong and took the blame for his actions, so the resentment accumulated.
Zhu Fumi reported that Peng Chong sent officials to welcome his wife instead of his mother, he also accepted bribes, killed his friends, and gathered troops in many valleys. His intentions were unpredictable.
Peng Chong had a grudge in his heart and was furious when he heard about it, so he raised his troops to attack Zhu Fu.
Zhu Fu reproached him in a letter and said: I have heard that wise people plan according to the times, while fools act against reason. I often privately lamented that my uncle in the capital was not satisfied and had no wise people to help him. As a result, he abandoned himself to Zheng.
Botong presides over the county administration because of his prominent name. He has the function of assisting orders, attending to people's duties, and caring for warehouses. I am responsible for conquest, and I want to review and rescue emergencies. Both of them are for the sake of the country.
Since you suspect that I have falsely accused you, why not report it to the capital and plan to destroy your clan?
The imperial court has been very kind to you Bo Tong. You have been entrusted with the title of Grand Commandery and given the title of Grand General.
A common man and a concubine can sacrifice themselves to repay the kindness of a meal. How can there be a person who wears three ribbons and holds a prestigious position, but ignores kindness and righteousness and is rebellious?
What was Bo Tong's appearance when he was talking to the officials?
When you walk and bow down, why should you be ashamed?
Sit down and think about it, why is your heart?
Take a look at yourself in the mirror, where should you focus?
If you make meritorious deeds with your actions, why should you be considered a human being?
It's a pity that you abandoned the honor of the beautiful order, created the treacherous conspiracy of owl and owl eating the mother, abandoned the blessings passed down to future generations, and caused serious disasters of ruin. You talked about the ways of Yao and Shun, but did not abandon the nature of Jie and Zhou. You lived as a laughing stock in the world and died as a fool. Isn't it very sad!
Bo Tong and Geng Kuang both stood up to support the Han Dynasty and received the country's favor.
Geng Kuang was humble and often spoke down, while Botong boasted of his abilities and thought that his achievements were the highest in the world.
In the past, there were pigs in Liaodong, and a white pig was born. The owner of the pig offered it as a gift. When he traveled to Hedong, he saw that all the pigs were white, so he returned it in shame.
If your merits are brought to the court for discussion, then you are just a Liaodong pig.
summary: Zhu Fu, courtesy name Shu Yuan, was from Xiao, Pei State. He initially served under Guangwu, followed him to break Handan, and was later appointed General Youzhou Mu to guard Jicheng and settle the northern border. In the second year of Jianwu, he was made Marquis of Wuyang. Zhu Fu sought to revive his reputation by recruiting famous scholars and former officials of Wang Mang, which angered Peng Chong, the prefect of Yuyang, who refused to comply. Zhu Fu slandered Peng Chong, leading to resentment. Zhu Fu reported Peng Chong for various offenses, and Peng Chong, enraged, raised troops to attack Zhu Fu. Zhu Fu reproached Peng Chong in a letter, criticizing his rebellion and comparing his merits to a Liaodong pig. Peng Chong attacked more fiercely, and despite Zhu Fu’s pleas for imperial aid, the court only sent Deng Long to assist. Zhu Fu fled after his city fell, and his wife was killed. The emperor replaced him as Jinwu and later as Marquis of Chengdu. After Peng Chong and Zhang Feng failed, Zhu Fu wrote a memorial criticizing the emperor’s harsh governance, advocating for slower, more careful administration. The emperor agreed, reducing mobilizations. Zhu Fu later served as a servant and proposed expanding the selection of doctors for the Imperial Academy, which the emperor approved. In the Yongping period, Zhu Fu was sentenced to death on false accusations, but Fan Wei interceded, and the emperor repented. The historian noted that Zhu Fu’s criticism of haste led to his death.

translation:
From then on, Feng Li was respected and trusted by the county, so he was able to establish his own camp.
At that time, the world was uncertain, and there were many soldiers from all over the world who supported the army under false pretenses. Only Feng Li defended himself with caution and strategy.
Guangwu heard about it and commended him. In the third year of Jianwu's reign, he was summoned to the emperor's residence, met him at Yuntai, Nangong, and paid homage to the magistrate of Yu County.
He dares to kill in politics and is famous for his prestige.
Moved to Jiaxian County.
When Hou Guangwu went west to conquer Kaixiao, bandits from Yingchuan gathered together. Yanbao, the Jia thief, and three thousand others attacked the county building. Feng Li led more than seventy officials and fought hard for days. After all their bows and arrows were exhausted, the city fell, and Feng Li fled.
When the emperor heard that the county was rebelling, he rushed to Yingchuan. Feng Li arrived at the emperor's location.
The emperor inspected the place where the battle was taking place and found out that Feng Li had fought hard. He commended him and said: "This is a brave and strong county magistrate. He should attack immediately without being limited to the state and county."
When Yan Bao and others heard that the emperor had arrived, they all shaved their heads, sat on their backs, and led others to come to apologize.
The emperor temporarily pardoned his crime, ordered Feng Li to surrender all the settlements, and the county was pacified. He also ordered Yan Bao and others to be returned to Feng Li for execution.
Feng Li ordered the general to conduct military exercises. The thieves all kowtowed and said, "I will be punished today, and I will die without regret."
Feng Li said: "I know that I have repented of my sins. Now I am pardoning all my sins and allowing them to go back to farming and serve as the eyes and ears of the county magistrate."
All the thieves hailed him as long live him.
At this time, every thief was reported by Yan Bao and others, and no one dared to move. The county boundary was quiet.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, he moved to Wei County to be the prefect.
In the twenty-seventh year, he was appointed as the imperial servant of Zhao with outstanding talent and learning.
In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, he was granted the title of Taishan from the east of the emperor and acted as an agent for the Wei Wei.
After returning, he replaced Zhang Chun as Sikong and was given the title of Marquis of Guannei.
In the second year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, the emperor died, so Feng Yi held the Fujie to build the original mausoleum. He also granted Yang Yi the title of Marquis of the Township and granted him the title of 350 households.
In the fourth year of Yongping's reign, because he was scrutinizing Deng Rong, the governor of Longxi, he allowed traitors to be convicted, and he was dismissed from office and his land was reduced.
In the sixth year of Yongping, Xianzong was favored by Lu, and Feng Li resumed his duties as a guard.
In the seventh year, Yin Song was appointed as King Wu.
Feng Li was strict and fair in nature, and he gave loyal advice during his tenure. Commonly adopted and implemented.
In the fourteenth year, the imperial edict was issued to restore the title of land.
In the second year, the emperor visited the prefectures in the east and left Feng Yi to stay in Weinan Palace.
In the third year of Jianchu's reign, he begged to retire because of his old illness, and Suzong agreed. In the winter of this year, it was the fifth watch in Feng Yi's hometown. The emperor ordered Feng Yi to congratulate him and give him the title of marquis.
summary: Feng Li, courtesy name Xiaosun, was from Huyang, Nanyang. During Wang Mang’s reign, he gathered guests and built a camp. He once saved Shentu Ji from Yu Duwei’s cousin, earning respect. Guangwu summoned him in the third year of Jianwu, making him magistrate of Yu County, where he governed with prestige. Later, as magistrate of Jiaxian, he fought bandits led by Yan Bao, who surrendered after Guangwu’s arrival. Feng Li pardoned them, and they served as informants, pacifying the county. He later served as prefect of Wei County and was appointed imperial servant of Zhao. In the Zhongyuan period, he became Sikong and Marquis of Guannei. After Guangwu’s death, he built the original mausoleum. In Yongping, he was dismissed for scrutinizing Deng Rong but later resumed duties. He served as King Wu of Yin Song, giving loyal advice. He retired due to old age in Jianchu and died at eighty-six.

translation:
In the second year of Yuanhe, he died at the age of eighty-six. ◆The biography of Yu Yan, whose courtesy name is Zi Da, was born in Chen Liudong.
When Yu Yan was born, there was something like a piece of white silk on it, which slowly rose to the sky. The fortune teller thought it was auspicious.
When he grew up, he was eight feet six inches long, ten circumferences wide, and strong enough to lift a cauldron.
When he was young, he was the head of Hutiao Pavilion.
At that time, Wang Mang's nobleman Wei's guests indulged in indulgence, and Yu Yan led officials and soldiers to break into his home and arrest him. He was resented and could not be promoted.
Yu Yan has an honest and simple temperament, informal and does not have the reputation of country music.
In the last years of Wang Mang, the world was in chaos. Yu Yan often put on armor to defend his relatives and defended against bandits. Many people relied on him for safety.
Yu Yan's cousin was an infant and her mother could not feed her, so she abandoned her in a ditch. Yu Yan heard her cry, took pity on her, adopted her, and raised her up.
At the beginning of Jianwu period, he served as an official in Zhijinwu Mansion and was appointed as the magistrate of Xiyang County.
Every year when the year comes, Fula often sends prisoners home. The prisoners appreciate his kindness and return them as scheduled.
Some prisoners got sick at home and returned to prison by car. They died in prison after returning. Yu Yan led his troops to send the funeral outside the door, and the people were grateful and happy.
Later, when he resigned and returned to his hometown, the prefect Fu Zong heard about Yu Yan's reputation and called him to serve as a meritorious official.
The wealthy clan is extravagant and wasteful, and many of its cars, services and utensils are not in compliance with the law.
Yu Yan advised: "In the past, when Yan Ying assisted the Qi State, he wore cloth and deer fur, and Ji Wenzi was the prime minister of Lu. My concubines had no clothes, no silk horses, no grain, so it was very rare for me to suffer losses due to frugality."
Fu Zong was unhappy and Yu Yan resigned immediately.
Soon, Fu Zong was executed for his extravagance. Before he was executed, he cried and sighed: I only regretted that I did not accept the advice of Yu Yan, the meritorious Cao Cao!
Guangwu was surprised when he heard about it.
Twenty years later, when the emperor was patrolling the east, he passed by Xiaohuang and saw the tomb of Emperor Gao's mother, Zhaoling, in the Houyuan Garden. At that time, Yu Yan was the governor of the ministry. The emperor introduced him and asked about the garden and mausoleum.
Yu Yan advanced and stopped calmly, and the obeisance was impressive. The number of trees and tillers in his mausoleum were all in compliance with the regulations.
The emperor praised him as a good man and ordered Yu Yan to go from the emperor to Lu.
Returning through the Fengqiu city gate, the gate was so low that the emperor's car cover decorated with green feathers could not pass through. The emperor was angry and ordered people to whip the censor. Yu Yan got out of the car to pay homage to the emperor, thinking that the crime was on the postal supervisor.
The impassioned and high-pitched words moved the emperor, and he issued a decree saying: "For the sake of Chen Liudu's post to Yu Yan, the censor's sins should be pardoned."
Yu Yan followed the chariot and drove westward to the county boundary, and returned to the county with rewards of money and swords and sabers, and his reputation increased.
In the twenty-third year of Jianwu's reign, Situ Yukuang summoned Yu Yan.
On the first day of the first lunar month, when the emperor saw Yu Yan, he recognized him and sent Xiaohuangmen to ask him. On the same day, he summoned him as his bus commander.
In the second year, the order was moved to Luoyang.
At this time, the Yin family had a guest named Ma Cheng, who was often a treacherous thief, and Yu Yan was tortured.
The Yin family repeatedly asked for forgiveness, and Yu Yan received an additional letter of 200 blows.
When the Marquis of Xinyang arrived, he sued the emperor, falsely accusing Yu Yan of doing many things and wrongfully accusing good people.
The emperor went to the Yudao Hall in person to interrogate and record the prisoners' crimes. Yu Yan reported that the prison records could be studied and discussed in the east, and those that could not be discussed should be sent to the west.
Ma Cheng turned around and wanted to go east. Yu Yan stepped forward to catch him and said to him: "You are a giant beetle among people. You have relied on the protection of the powerful for a long time and are not afraid of being burned."
The truth test is not over yet and should be dealt with according to law!
Ma Cheng cried out that he was wronged, and the emperor's jilang stabbed Yu Yan with his halberd, scolding Yu Yan to let Ma Cheng go.
The emperor knew that Yu Yan was selfless and said to Ma Cheng: "You have violated the king's law and you brought it upon yourself."
Tell him to go quickly.
The Fa-rectification took place within a few days. So the relatives held back their hands and did not dare to break the law.
summary: Yu Yan, courtesy name Zi Da, was from Chenliu. Born with an auspicious sign, he was strong and tall. As a youth, he arrested a noble’s guests, earning resentment. During Wang Mang’s chaos, he defended his relatives. He adopted his cousin’s abandoned infant. As magistrate of Xiyang County, he let prisoners go home for the new year; they returned as promised. He resigned after advising Prefect Fu Zong against extravagance; Fu Zong was later executed. Guangwu, impressed, appointed Yu Yan as governor. He served as Luoyang magistrate, punishing the Yin family’s guest Ma Cheng despite pleas. He later became Nanyang governor. In Yongping, he recognized Deng Yan’s lack of manners, leading to Deng Yan’s shame. Yu Yan served as Taiwei and Situ, but when Liu Ying of Chu rebelled, Yu Yan failed to report contacts, leading to his suicide. His family was left poor.

translation:
Zheng Hongzou thought that although the position was prestigious, the reward was very meager. When the election came, most of them were unhappy and asked Shangshu Lang to supplement the Thousand Stone Order to make history longer.
The emperor followed his advice.
Things that Zheng Hong mentioned before and after that were beneficial to the king's government were all recorded in Nangong as stories.
He came out to be the king of Pingyuan and worshiped his ministers.
In the eighth year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, he replaced Zheng Zhong as the chief agricultural officer.
The goods contributed by the seven counties of old Jiaozhi were transferred across the sea from Dongye. The storms were difficult and shipwrecks often occurred.
Zheng Hongzou opened the Lingling and Guiyang mountain roads, so the mountain roads were widened and leveled to become future passages.
During Zheng Hong's two years in office, he saved 3 trillion yuan in assets.
At that time, the world was suffering from drought, there were police on the border, people had insufficient food, but there was a lot of money accumulated.
Zheng Hong also reported that the province should contribute and reduce corvee fees to benefit the hungry people.
The emperor accepted his suggestion.
In the first year of Yuanhe, Zheng Hong replaced Deng Biao as Taiwei.
At that time, Zheng Hong had elected his fifth Lun as Sikong, who was below him. Every time he went to court at Zhengshuo, Zheng Hong would bow down and feel inferior.
The emperor asked and knew the reason, so he listened to his words and put up a mica screen to separate Zheng Hong from the Fifth Lun. This became a system.
In the fourth year of his reign, he reported to Shangshu Zhang Lin that he flattered and supported Dou Xian, his attendant, but had always harbored filth. He also reported to Luoyang Ling Yang Guang that he was Dou Xian's guest. He was corrupt and disabled in office and should not stay in his original position.
The official who was in charge of the memorial was an old friend of Yang Guang, so he informed Yang Guang.
Yang Guang reported to Dou Xian, so Dou Xian reported that Zheng Hong had leaked secrets as a minister.
The emperor ordered Zheng Hong to take back his seal and ribbon.
Zheng Hong came to Tingwei to plead guilty and ordered him to leave. Because he asked to resign, he was not allowed to do so.
When he was seriously ill, he wrote a letter to express his gratitude and pointed out Dou Xian's shortcomings.
The emperor read the memorial and sent a doctor to see Zheng Hong's illness. By the time the doctor arrived, Zheng Hong had already died.
Before his death, he returned all the things the emperor had given him and ordered his wife and children to be buried in brown turbans and plain coffins before returning to his hometown.
◆Zhou Zhangzhuan, also known as Uncle Zhou Zhang, was a native of Sui County, Nanyang County.
At first, he was a meritorious official in the county.
At this time, the general Dou Xian was granted the title of champion and returned to the country.
Zhou Zhang went from the prefect to the championship, and the prefect also wanted to pay homage to Dou Xian.
Zhou Zhangjin remonstrated: "Today we are traveling for official business, how can we go beyond etiquette and make private friends with powerful people?"
Moreover, Dou Xian is a relative of the concubine and has great influence on the royal family. Now that he has retired to the vassal state, it is difficult to measure the blessings and misfortunes.
You are the Minister of Talisman Dissection, and you have a heavy responsibility of thousands of miles. How can you act rashly when you move forward or retreat?
The prefect refused to listen and wanted to raise the chariot.
Zhou Zhang went to draw his sword and cut the leather around the horse's neck, and the prefect was forced to stop.
When Dou Xian was executed, most of the officials below the public minister were offended for associating with Dou Xian, but the prefect was spared, so they valued Zhou Zhang.
He was promoted to be filial and honest, and he was promoted to the rank of Langjiang with five sense organs in the sixth year.
In the first year of Yanping, he was named Guang Luxun.
In the first year of Yongchu, he succeeded Wei Ba as Taichang.
In the winter of this year, Dai Yinqin was appointed Sikong.
At this time, the ministers Zheng Zhong and Cai Lun were using their power to intervene in the government affairs, and Zhou Zhang spoke out several times.
At first, after the death of Emperor He, Empress Dowager Deng thought that the prince Liu Sheng had a chronic illness and could not flatter the ancestral temple. Emperor Shang was a young child and was raised as her own son, so she made him the prince and made Liu Sheng the king of Pingyuan.
After the death of Emperor Shang, the ministers thought that Liu Sheng's illness was not a chronic illness, and all advocated the appointment of Liu Sheng. Since the Queen Mother had not established Liu Sheng before, fearing that the queen would resent her, she appointed Liu Sheng, the son of Prince Xiao of Qinghe, the emperor's brother, as Emperor An.
Zhou Zhang thought that the public was unwilling to follow him, so he conspired to close the palace gates, kill the brothers of Chariot and Cavalry General Deng Zhi, Zheng Zhong, and Cai Lun, hijack the minister, deposed the Queen Mother in the South Palace, made Emperor An the king of Yuan, and made Liu Sheng, the king of Pingyuan, the emperor.
The plot was discovered, the plan was dismissed, and Zhou Zhang committed suicide.
The family had no money left, so they changed their clothes and went out to eat by the sun.
summary: Zheng Hong, from Kuaiji, was a misfit as a youth but was recognized by Prefect Wu Lun. He studied under Jiao Kuang, who was implicated in Liu Ying’s rebellion. When Jiao Kuang died, Zheng Hong shaved his head and pleaded for his family, gaining fame. As magistrate of Zuxian, he governed benevolently. He became Shangshu Ling and proposed that Shangshu Lang supplement Thousand Stone Orders, which the emperor accepted. As chief agricultural officer, he opened mountain roads in Lingling and Guiyang, saving three trillion in assets. He reduced contributions and corvee fees during drought. As Taiwei, he deferred to the Fifth Lun, and the emperor set up a screen between them. He reported Zhang Lin and Yang Guang for corruption, but Dou Xian accused him of leaking secrets. Zheng Hong resigned and died, leaving instructions for a simple burial. Zhou Zhang, from Nanyang, was a meritorious official. He advised the prefect against privately visiting Dou Xian, cutting the horse’s leather to stop him. When Dou Xian was executed, the prefect was spared. Zhou Zhang became Guang Luxun and later Sikong. He criticized Zheng Zhong and Cai Lun’s power. After Emperor He’s death, Empress Dowager Deng made Liu Sheng king of Pingyuan and later Emperor An. Zhou Zhang plotted to kill Deng Zhi, Zheng Zhong, and Cai Lun, depose the queen, and make Liu Sheng emperor. The plot was discovered, and Zhou Zhang committed suicide, leaving no wealth. The historian warned against such usurpation, citing Mencius.

◆Zhu You Biography Zhu You, courtesy name Zhongxian, was a native of Wan County, Nanyang County.
When the young man lost his father, he returned to the home of his maternal grandparents Liu in Fuyang County and traveled to and from Chongling. Shizu and Bosheng were both dear to him.
After Bo Sheng paid homage to the Chief Situ, he appointed Zhu You as his guard.
Shizu was the Grand Sima, and when he conquered Hebei, he appointed Zhu You as his army guard. He often met his relatives and stayed there.
Zhu You accompanied the banquet and said calmly: Chang'an is in political chaos and the public has the status of an emperor. This is a destiny sent from heaven. Shizu said: Summon assassins to arrest you, the guardian! Zhu You didn't dare to say anything anymore.
He followed the expedition to Hebei and often fought hard to break the formation. He made Zhu You a partial general and was granted the title of Marquis of Anyang.
Shizu ascended the throne and was worshiped as General Jianyi.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, Yanghou was blocked.
In winter, he and his generals attacked Deng Feng in Yuyang, Zhu You was defeated and captured by Deng Feng.
The next year, Deng Feng was defeated, and Rouqi and Zhu You surrendered.
The emperor restored Zhu You's position and generously rewarded him with condolences.
He was sent to attack Xinye and Suixian, and they were all pacified.
Since Yancen was defeated by Rang, he joined Qin Feng's general Zhang Cheng. Zhu You led the conquering general Ji Zun to fight Yancen in Dongyang, defeated Yancen, and beheaded Zhang Cheng before the battle. Yancen was defeated and returned to Qin Feng.
Zhu You received ninety-seven seals and ribbons.
Attacked Huangyou, Huangyou surrendered and rewarded Zhu You with thirty kilograms of gold.
In the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, he led general Hou Jin and general Geng Zhi to attack the south and besieged Qin Feng in Liqiu, defeated his general Zhang Kang in Caiyang and beheaded Zhang Kang.
The emperor personally came to Liqiu and sent Li You, the censor Zhongcheng, with a seal to recruit Qin Feng to surrender. Qin Feng made bad words and refused to surrender.
The emperor returned and gave Zhu You strategies, and Zhu You tried his best to besiege.
In the summer of the next year, the city was impoverished, so Qin Feng led his mother and his wife, Jiurenzuchou, to surrender.
Zhu You took Qin Feng to Luoyang in a prison car and beheaded him.
The Grand Sima Wu Han impeached Zhu You for abolishing the imperial edict and accepting surrender, which violated the general's mission, and the emperor did not punish him.
After Zhu You returned, he joined forces with the Cavalry Commander Zang Gong to attack Yancen Yu and the bandits in Yin County, Zanhuang County and Zhuyang County, and they were all put down.
Zhu You was a simple and upright man who liked Confucianism.
Leading a large number of soldiers, accepting more surrenders, taking the ability to stabilize the city as the foundation, and not pursuing the merit of indiscriminate beheading.
The soldiers were also strictly prohibited from plundering the people. The soldiers were happy to indulge themselves, and they often complained about Zhu You.
In the ninth year of Jianwu, troops were stationed south to the Tang Dynasty to resist the Xiongnu.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, the number of fiefs was increased, and the title of Lihou was established, with 7,300 households living in the fiefs.
In the fifteenth year of Jianwu's reign, he went to the capital and presented the seal and ribbon of the general, because he stayed in the capital to serve the imperial invitation.
Zhu You reported that in ancient times, ministers were rewarded without royal titles, and suggested that all kings should be changed to Dukes.
summary: **Zhu You**, courtesy name Zhongxian, was from Wan County, Nanyang. Orphaned young, he lived with his maternal grandparents in Fuyang and traveled to Chongling, where Shizu and Bosheng held him dear. Bosheng appointed him guard, and Shizu later made him army guard during the Hebei campaign. Zhu You once suggested that Chang'an's chaos indicated heaven-sent destiny for Shizu, who threatened him. He fought bravely in Hebei, became a partial general, and was named Marquis of Anyang. After Shizu ascended, Zhu You became General Jianyi. He attacked Deng Feng but was captured; after Deng Feng's defeat, Zhu You surrendered, was restored, and pacified Xinye and Suixian. He defeated Yancen, beheading Zhang Cheng, and received ninety-seven seals. He besieged Qin Feng in Liqiu, who surrendered after a year. Wu Han impeached Zhu You for accepting surrender against orders, but the emperor did not punish him. Zhu You, simple and upright, liked Confucianism, stabilized cities, and prohibited plundering, though soldiers complained. He later resisted the Xiongnu, increased his fief to 7,300 households, and suggested changing kings to dukes, which the emperor adopted. He died in Jianwu 24.

translation:
The emperor immediately adopted it and implemented it.
He also reported that the three princes should be ordered to remove their royal titles in order to follow the example of past classics.
Later the emperor also accepted his suggestion.
Zhu You first studied in Chang'an, and the emperor went to greet him. Zhu You worked hard with him from time to time, but he was promoted to Tuoshe first.
Later, when the emperor came to Zhu You's mansion, he smiled and said, "Master, do you have to tell me without leaving me?" Because of old kindness, I have been rewarded many times.
In the twenty-fourth year of Jianwu's reign, he died.
His son Zhu Shang succeeded him.
Zhu Shang died, and his son Zhu Yan succeeded to the throne. In the 14th year of Yongyuan, his brother-in-law was implicated in the witchcraft of his grandson Queen Yin, so he was exempted from being a commoner.
In the seventh year of Yongchu's reign, Mrs. Deng granted Zhu Yan's son Zhu Chong the title of Marquis of Li.
◆Jingdan Biography: Jingdan was named Sun Qing, and Feng Yi was from Yueyang.
I studied Chang'an when I was young.
When Wang Mang took the exams in four subjects, Jing Dan was promoted to the title of Gudehou Xiang in the language subject. He was praised for his ability to do things and was moved to Shuo Diao Lian Lian Lie Vice-Secretary.
Gengshi ascended the throne and sent envoys to Shanggu to announce that Jingdan, Lian and Geng Kuang had surrendered to Gengshi, and then became the governor of Shanggu.
After Wang Lang got up, Jing Dan and Geng Kuang jointly planned to resist Wang Lang.
Geng Kuang sent Jingdan and his sons Geng and Kou Xun to lead their troops south to Shizu. Shizu introduced Jingdan and others and said with a smile: General Handan threatened to send troops to Yuyang and Shanggu several times. I just talked and dealt with it. I didn't expect the two counties to come for me!
This honor should be shared with the scholar-bureaucrats from the two counties. He worshiped Jingdan as a partial general and was named Fengyihou.
He followed and attacked Wang Lang's general Erhong, who was in the south. Lang's soldiers fought, but the Han army retreated. Jing Dan attacked with cavalry and defeated Wang Lang's army. They chased for more than ten miles, leaving many dead and wounded on the road.
When Jing Dan returned, Shizu said to him: I heard that the assault cavalry is the best soldier in the world. Now that I see the assault cavalry participating in the battle, how can I express my joy in words? So he followed in the expedition to Hebei.
When Shizu came to the throne, he used prophecies to appoint Sun Xian, the general of Ping Di, to act as Grand Sima. The tribesmen were unhappy.
The emperor issued an edict asking the officials to recommend who could be the Grand Sima, but the officials recommended only Wu Han and Jing Dan.
The emperor said: General Jing is the general of Beizhou, and Da Sima can be him.
However, General Wu had the merit of establishing great policies, and also killed Miao Hui and Xie Gong. His merits are great.
According to the old system, the rank of Hussar General and the rank of Grand Sima could be held concurrently. So Wu Han was appointed as the Grand Sima, and Jing Dan was appointed as the General of the Hussars.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, Jingdan was granted the title of Marquis of Yueyang.
The emperor said to Jingdan: Although the original kingdom of Guandong now has several counties, only Yueyang has a city of ten thousand households.
As the saying goes, if you don't return to your hometown, you will be like walking in the dark wearing brocade clothes, so I will call you the Marquis of Yueyang.
summary: **Jing Dan**, courtesy name Sun Qing, from Yueyang, studied in Chang'an. Wang Mang promoted him to Gudehou Xiang. Gengshi made him Shanggu governor. When Wang Lang rose, Jing Dan and Geng Kuang resisted, sending troops south to Shizu. Shizu appointed him partial general and Marquis of Fengyi. He defeated Wang Lang's general Erhong, and Shizu praised his cavalry. After Shizu's ascension, officials recommended Jing Dan for Grand Sima, but Wu Han received the post, and Jing Dan became Hussar General. He was named Marquis of Yueyang, with the emperor citing the saying about returning home in brocade. He joined Wu Han in defeating five schools in Yuyang. Ill, he was forced to serve as Hongnong governor to fight thieves, dying ten days later.

translation:
Jing Dan kowtowed his head to express his gratitude. In the autumn, Wu Han, General Geng of Jianwei, General Zhu You of Jianyi, Jia Fu of Zhijinwu, General Feng Yi, Qiannu General Chen Jun, Zuo Cao Wangchang, Cavalry Commander Zang Gong and other followers defeated the five schools in Yuyang, and 50,000 people surrendered.
It happened that the Shaanxi thief Su Kuang attacked Hongnong and captured the county guard alive.
Jing Dan was ill at that time, and because he was a returned general, the emperor wanted him to be forced to serve as the governor of Hongnong County, so he summoned him to see him at night and said to him: "Thieves are approaching the capital. It is enough to rely on the general's authority and sleep in bed to guard him." Jing Dan did not dare to refuse, so he reluctantly accepted the appointment and led his battalion west to Hongnong County. He died of illness more than ten days later.
Zijing succeeded to the throne and was granted the title of Marquis Yuwu.
When Jing Shang died, Zi Jingbao succeeded him.
When Jingbao died, his son Jinglin succeeded him. Jinglin had no children and the feudal state was abolished.
In the seventh year of Yongchu's reign, Mrs. Deng granted Jingbao's younger brother Jingjun the title of Marquis of Janting.
◆Biography of Wang Liang Wang Liang, courtesy name Junyan, was from Yaoyang County, Yuyang County.
As a county official, the prefect Peng Chong put Wang Liang in charge of the county magistrate of Hunu. Together with Gai Yan and Wu Han, he led troops south to pursue the ancestor Yu Guang'a and worshiped him as a partial general.
After conquering Handan, he was given the title of Marquis of Guannei.
Following the pacification of Hebei, he paid homage to the Wild King's order, and together with Kou Xun, the prefect of Hanoi, rejected Luoyang in the south and guarded Tianjing Pass in the north. Zhu Jun and others did not dare to send troops. Shizu thought it was Wang Liang's contribution.
When he came to the throne, it was discussed to elect the Great Sikong, and "Chi Fu Fu" said that Wang Liang's main guard was Xuanwu. The emperor thought that Ye Wang was the emigration of Wei Yuanjun, Xuanwu was the name of the water god, and Sikong was the official of water and earth, so he promoted Wang Liang to be the Great Sikong and granted him the title of Wu Qianghou.
In the second year of Jianwu, he and the Grand Sima Wu Han and others attacked Tanxiang together. The imperial edict was that all military affairs should belong to the Grand Sima. However, Wang Liang launched the wild king's troops without authorization. The emperor refused to obey the edict and ordered him to stop operations in the county where he was located, and Wang Liang marched without authorization.
The emperor was furious because Wang Liang had disobeyed orders before and after, and sent Minister Zong Guang to hold the talisman to kill Wang Liang in the army.
Zong Guang couldn't bear it, so he took Wang Liang back to the capital in a prison car.
After arriving in Beijing, the emperor pardoned him.
After more than a month, he was appointed as Zhonglang General and also in charge of Jinwu affairs.
Guard Jiguan in the north, attack Chimei Biejiao and surrender.
In the spring of the third year, he attacked the five schools, pursued Xindu and Zhao State, and defeated them. All the settlements were pacified.
In winter, an envoy was sent to hold the talisman festival to worship Wang Liang as the former general.
In the spring of the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, he attacked Feicheng and Wenyang and captured them both.
Jin and the hussar generals Du Mao attacked Jiaopi and Su Mao between Chu and Pei, and captured Daliang and Lisang. The captured general Ma Wu and the partial general Wang Ba also went their separate ways, and they were all put down in more than a year.
In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, he followed to rescue Taocheng, defeat Pang Meng and others. Wang Liang fought particularly effectively. He became the prefect of Shanyang, guarded and comforted the new converts, and led the troops as before.
A few months later, he was recruited to Beijing and replaced Ouyang She as Henan Yin.
Wang Liang opened a canal to divert the valley water into the city of Luoyang, then poured it eastward into Gongchuan River. When the canal was completed, the water stopped flowing.
In the seventh year of Jianwu's reign, an impeachment report was issued. Wang Liang was frightened and wrote a letter requesting to resign.
The emperor issued an edict saying: Wang Liang once led troops to conquer, and everyone praised him as a virtuous man, so he was promoted to the capital.
summary: **Wang Liang**, courtesy name Junyan, from Yuyang, was a county official under Prefect Peng Chong. He led troops south to Shizu, became a partial general, and Marquis of Guannei. He pacified Hebei, guarded Tianjing Pass, and Shizu credited him. After ascension, prophecies favored Wang Liang for Grand Sikong, which he received. He disobeyed orders by launching troops without authorization; the emperor sent Zong Guang to execute him, but Zong Guang brought him to the capital instead. The emperor pardoned him, made him Zhonglang General, and later Former General. He captured Feicheng and Wenyang, pacified regions with Du Mao, and rescued Taocheng. As Henan Yin, he dug a canal diverting water to Luoyang, but it failed. He resigned, became Jinan prefect, and died in Jianwu 14.

translation:
It is suggested to open a canal to benefit others, but all efforts have been made, but the success has not been achieved. The people complained and slandered, and the talkers made a loud noise.
Although he was forgiven, he still insisted on humbly retiring. Because of the beauty of a gentleman, Wang Liang was specially appointed as the prefect of Jinan. In the 13th year of Jianwu's reign, the fiefdom was increased and he was named Marquis of Fucheng.
In the 14th year of Jianwu's reign, he died in officialdom.
Prince Yu succeeded to the throne.
When Yu died, his son Wang Jianshi succeeded him.
Wang Jianshi was investigated because his father Wang Yu and his younger brother Wang Ping participated in the rebellion of Chu King Liu Ying. They were executed in the city and the feudal state was abolished.
◆Du Mao Biography: Du Mao, courtesy name Zhu Gong, was a champion of Nanyang County.
At first, he returned to Guangwu in Hebei and became a backbone general, often accompanying him on expeditions.
Shizu ascended the throne, was worshiped as a general, and was granted the title of Marquis of Lexiang.
Attack the five schools in Zhending from the north and advance to Guangping.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Kuxing.
Together with Zhonglang General Wang Liang, he attacked the bandits of the Five Schools in Weijun, Qinghe, and Dongjun, and pacified all the forts. More than thirty of his generals, Chijie, surrendered, and the three counties were quiet and the roads were smooth.
Next year, an envoy was sent to hold Du Mao as a hussar general, attack Peijun, and capture Mangxian.
At that time, the western defense was built again to welcome Jiaozhi.
In the spring of the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, Du Mao led the captured general Ma Wu to attack the western defense. After a few months, he was able to capture the enemy and escape to Dong Xian.
Dongfang had been pacified, and in the seventh year of Jianwu's reign, Du Mao was ordered to lead troops northward to garrison Jinyang and Guangwu to guard against Hu invaders.
In the ninth year of Jianwu, Guo Liang, the prefect of Yanmen, attacked Yin Yufan County, the general of Lu Fang. Jia Lan, the general of Lu Fang, led more than 10,000 Hu cavalry to rescue him. Du Mao fought with him, but the army was defeated and led into Loufan County.
At this time, Lu Fang occupied Gaoliu, joined forces with the Xiongnu soldiers, and invaded the border people many times, which made the emperor very worried.
In the twelfth year of Jianwu's reign, the emissary Duan Zhong was dispatched to distribute the prisoners who had been released from the shackles to Du Mao in each county to guard the north. He then mobilized the border soldiers to build pavilions and repair beacon fires. He also mobilized the transportation of gold, silk and silk to supply the sergeants and give them to the border residents. The officials kept looking at each other.
Du Mao also built farmland and used horse-drawn carts to transport the goods.
First, Jia Dan, Huo Kuang, Xie Sheng and others from Yanmen were plundered by Yin You. Yin You took them as generals and guarded Pingcheng with Yin You.
When Jia Dan and others heard that Lu Fang had failed, they killed Yin You with Huo Kuang, Xie Sheng and others to see Guo Liang. Guo Liang reported the situation and made them all princes. The emperor ordered that the transportation of gold and silk be given to Du Mao, Guo Liang's military officials and the people who surrendered in Pingcheng.
From then on, Lu Fang's cities gradually surrendered. Guo Liang killed the members of his powerful family, the Xun family, to appease the old and weak. Within a month, Yanmen was temporarily peaceful, and Lu Fang fled to the Xiongnu.
summary: **Du Mao**, courtesy name Zhugong, from Nanyang, joined Shizu in Hebei as a backbone general. After ascension, he became General and Marquis of Lexiang, later Marquis of Kuxing. He pacified bandits in Weijun, Qinghe, and Dongjun. As Hussar General, he attacked Peijun and captured Mangxian. He fought Lu Fang's general Jia Lan but was defeated. He built fortifications and beacon fires, transported supplies, and pacified Yanmen after Lu Fang fled to the Xiongnu. His fief increased, but he was dismissed for a soldier-killing incident, reduced to Marquis of Shenzang Township. He died in Jianwu 19.

translation:
The emperor promoted Guo Liang's son to the rank of Zhonglang, and he was placed on the guard's side.
Guo Liang's official name was from Beiping.
He is eight feet long and strong and brave. Although he is a military commander, he is proficient in scriptures and wise. He is especially knowledgeable about border affairs and is famous in the north.
At first, Youzhou Mu Zhu Fuzheng served as a soldier of Cao Cao. He had meritorious service in defeating Peng Chong and was granted the title of Marquis of Guangwu.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, Du Mao's settlement was increased and he was granted the title of Marquis.
In the fifteenth year of Jianwu's reign, because he was involved in the case of cutting off the cords of soldiers and horses and causing soldiers to kill people, he was dismissed from his official position, his household was cut off, and he was granted the title of Marquis of Shenzang Township.
Jianwu died in the 19th year.
His son Du Yuan succeeded him. In the 14th year of Yongping, because he was involved in a rebellion with King Dongping and others, his death was reduced by one degree, and the feudal state was abolished.
In the seventh year of Yongchu, Mrs. Deng later granted Du Maosun and Du Feng the title of Marquis of Anleting.
◆Biography of Ma Cheng Ma Cheng, whose courtesy name is Junqian, was born in Jiyang, Nanyang County.
He was a county official when he was young.
Shizu conquered Yingchuan, used his horse to become an Jidu, and transferred him to the magistrate of Jiaxian County.
When Shizu launched a crusade against Hebei, Ma Cheng abandoned his official post and went on foot to catch up with him in Puyang. He used Ma Cheng as a Qi gate to follow the expedition.
Shizu ascended the throne and moved to the guard of the army.
In the fourth year of Jianwu, he was promoted to General Yangwu and supervised the execution of General Liu Long, General Zhenwei Song Deng, and Shesheng Xiaowei Wang Shang. He sent soldiers from Kuaiji, Danyang, Jiujiang, and Lu'an to attack Li Xian. At that time, the emperor came to Shouchun and set up a mandala to offer sacrifices according to ancestral rites.
Encircling Li Xian in Shu, he ordered all armies to dig deep ditches and fortify themselves.
Li Xian challenged him many times, but Ma Cheng stood firm and refused to fight. He defended the area for more than a year.
In the spring of the sixth year of Jianwu, the city was depleted of food, so they attacked the city, massacred the residents of Shucheng, beheaded Li Xian, pursued his followers, and pacified the Jianghuai area.
In the summer of the seventh year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Pingshuhou.
In the eighth year, he followed the expedition and defeated Weixiao. He became the prefect of Tianshui with his horse and commanded the army as before.
In winter, the army was summoned to the capital.
In the ninth year of Jianwu, Dai Lai She was in charge of Zhonglang General, and led Wuwei General Liu Shang and others to conquer Hechi County and pacify Wudu County.
In the second year, Grand Sikong Li Tong resigned from office and appointed Ma Cheng as his deputy. He lived in Grand Sikong Mansion and performed his duties faithfully. He paid homage to General Yangwu again for several months.
In the 14th year of Jianwu's reign, troops were stationed in Changshan and Zhongshan to guard the northern border, and he led the troops of General Zhu You of Jianyi.
He also built fortifications on behalf of General Du Mao of the Hussars. From Xihe to Weiqiao, from Heshang to Anyi, from Taiyuan to Jingxing, from Zhongshan to Ye, he built forts, set off beacons, and built a lookout post ten miles away.
summary: **Ma Cheng**, courtesy name Junqian, from Nanyang, was a county official. Shizu made him Jidu and Jiaxian magistrate. He abandoned his post to join Shizu in Puyang, becoming Qi gate. After ascension, he became General Yangwu, attacking Li Xian in Shu for over a year, massacring the city and beheading Li Xian. He was named Marquis of Pingshu, defeated Weixiao, and became Tianshui prefect. He later guarded the northern border, building forts and beacons from Xihe to Ye. After five or six years, he returned to the capital but was sent back due to border petitions. He became Zhongshan governor, attacked Wuxi Valley barbarians, and died in Jianwu 32.

translation:
After five or six years of service, the emperor recognized Ma Cheng's hard work and summoned him back to Beijing.
Many people from the frontier wrote letters begging him to return to the border, so the emperor sent Ma Cheng back to the camp.
When Nandan was at peace in the fortress and the north was at peace, he worshiped Ma and became the governor of Zhongshan, presented the general's seal and ribbon, and continued to lead the troops as before.
In the 24th year of Jianwu's reign, he attacked the barbarians in Wuxi Valley in the south. Before he achieved military success, he presented himself with the seal and ribbon of the prefect.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Quanjiao and returned to the country.
He died in the 32nd year of Jianwu.
Zima Wei succeeded to the throne.
Ma Weizu, his son Ma Xiang succeeded him, and he was granted the title of Marquis of Jiling.
Ma Xiang died, and his son Ma Feng succeeded him.
Ma Feng died, and his son Ma Xuan succeeded him.
Ma Xuan died, and his son Ma Yi succeeded to the throne.
Ma Yi died, and his son Ma Chou succeeded him. During the reign of Emperor Huan, he deposed his feudal state because of his crime.
In the second year of Yanxi's reign, Ma Chang, the great-great-grandson of Ma Cheng, was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang Ting.
◆Biography of Liu Long Liu Long, courtesy name Boyuan, was from the clan of Nanyang Anzhonghou.
During Wang Mang's reign, Liu Long's father Liu Li and Anzhonghou Liu Chong launched an army to murder Wang Mang. The incident was revealed, and Liu Long was spared from the disaster because he was under seven years old.
When he was old, he studied in Chang'an and worshiped him as the captain of the cavalry.
He asked for leave and returned, welcoming his wife and children and settling them in Luoyang.
When he heard that Shizu was in Hanoi, he followed Shizu Yu Shedog and was appointed as the Cavalry Captain. Together with Feng Yi, he rejected Zhu Tuna, Li Yi and others. Li Yi killed Liu Long's wife and children.
In the second year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Kangfuhou.
In the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, he became the general who killed the captives and attacked Li Xian.
After Li Xian was defeated, Liu Long was sent to garrison Wudang.
In the eleventh year of Jianwu's reign, he acted as the governor of Nanyang. For more than a year, he presented the seal and ribbon of the general.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, the number of towns increased and he was granted the title of Marquis of Jingling.
At this time, the number of cultivated fields in the world was unrealistic, and the age of household registration increased and decreased.
In the fifteenth year of Jianwu's reign, the prefectures and counties were ordered to inspect and verify land reclamation. However, the governors and governors were unevenly distributed. They might give fine and fertile land to powerful families, while exploiting and exploiting the weak common people. The common people complained and filled the roads with howls and cries.
At that time, each county sent envoys to report the matter. The emperor saw that there was a book on Chen Liu's official slip. When he looked at it, he saw that it was written that "You can ask questions in Yingchuan and Hongnong, but not in Henan and Nanyang." The emperor questioned the book's origin, but the official refused to tell the truth and lied that he had picked it up on Changshou Street.
The emperor was angry.
At that time, Xianzong was the Duke of Donghai, and he was only twelve years old. He said behind the scenes: Officials who receive orders from the governor naturally want to cultivate land as a method. The emperor said: If this is the case, why do you say that Henan and Nanyang cannot be asked? Xianzong replied: Henan is the imperial city and there are many close ministers; Nanyang is the imperial hometown and there are many close relatives. The fields and houses exceed the regulations and cannot be used as standards. The emperor ordered General Huben to question the official, and the official explained it truthfully, just as Xianzong said.
summary: **Liu Long**, courtesy name Boyuan, from Nanyang, survived a family purge under Wang Mang. He studied in Chang'an, became Cavalry Captain, and joined Shizu in Hanoi. Li Yi killed his family. He became General Who Kills Captives, attacked Li Xian, and garrisoned Wudang. As Nanyang governor, he presented his general's seal. His fief increased to Marquis of Jingling. During land surveys, officials favored powerful families, causing complaints. Liu Long was imprisoned for fraud, demoted to commoner, later restored as Marquis of Fule Township. He attacked Jiaozhi barbarians, beheading over a thousand. After Wu Han's death, he became Hussar General and acting Grand Sima for eight years. He died in Zhongyuan 2, posthumously named Jinghou.

translation:
So he sent a close servant to investigate and verify, and reported the traitor.
The next year, Liu Long was imprisoned and more than ten of his peers died.
The emperor regarded Liu Long as a meritorious official and demoted him to a commoner.
In the 17th year of Jianwu's reign, Liu Long was granted the title of Marquis of Fule Township. He sent General Zhonglang, deputy general Fubo, Ma Yuan, to attack the Jiaozhi barbarian expedition. Liu Long also defeated their army at the entrance of Jinxi Valley, captured their commander Zheng Er, beheaded more than a thousand people, and surrendered more than 20,000 people.
After returning to Beijing, he was granted the title of Marquis of Changping.
After the death of the Grand Sima Wu Han, Liu Long became the Hussar General and acted as the acting general for the Grand Sima.
Liu Long followed the law and guarded himself, and took charge of the affairs for eight years. He presented the seal and ribbon of the general, dismissed from office, and was given cattle and ten bottles of wine, and was invited by the princes.
In the 30th year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis Shen.
He died in the second year of Zhongyuan, and his posthumous title was Jinghou.
His son Liu An succeeded him.
◆Fu Jun's biography Fu Jun's courtesy name was Ziwei, and he was a native of Xiangcheng, Yingchuan County.
Shizu captured Xiangcheng, and Fu Jun greeted the Han army as the county pavilion chief and worshiped him as a school captain. Xiangcheng arrested his mother, brother, and clan, and executed them all.
Follow and defeat Wang Xun and others, with Fu Jun as the partial general.
Another attack on Jing and Mi was defeated. He was sent back to Yingchuan to collect and bury his family members.
When Shizu was conquering Hebei, Fu Jun and more than ten guests pursued him northward. They caught up with him at Handan and paid a visit to Shizu. Shizu asked him to lead the Yingchuan troops and often follow him in the expedition.
Shizu ascended the throne and took Fu Jun as his attendant.
In the second year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Kunyang.
In the third year of Jianwu's reign, he appointed Fu Jun as General Jinu, and together with Cen Peng, the general who conquered the south, defeated Qin Feng, so he led his troops to conquer Jiangdong and pacified all of Yangzhou.
He died in the seventh year of Jianwu and was given the posthumous title of Weihou.
His son Fu Chang succeeded to the throne and was granted the title of Marquis of Wuhu.
During the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China, his mother was bereaved, so he wrote a letter saying that Wuhu was poor and unwilling to go to the country, and asked for a grant of 500,000 yuan to be made a Marquis of Guannei.
Suzong was angry and demoted Fu Chang to the title of Marquis of Guannei, but refused to reward him with money.
In the seventh year of Yongchu's reign, Empress Dowager Deng restored the title of Fu Tie, Fu Chang's son, to the title of Gaozhitinghou.
◆Jiantan's biography Jiantan's courtesy name is Zidanji, a native of Xiangcheng, Yingchuan.
As a county official.
When Shizu was campaigning against Hebei, someone recommended Jiantan, so Shizu summoned him.
Because of his ability to serve as a county official, he was appointed as the chief bookkeeper.
He also worshiped as a partial general and followed him to pacify Hebei. He also defeated the big gun Yu Lunu.
When Shizu ascended the throne, he worshiped Jiandan as General Yanghua and granted him the title of Qianghou of Xuyin.
summary: **Fu Jun**, courtesy name Ziwei, from Yingchuan, greeted the Han army as pavilion chief. Xiangcheng executed his family. He became a partial general, defeated Wang Xun, and collected his family's remains. He joined Shizu in Hebei, leading Yingchuan troops. After ascension, he became attendant, Marquis of Kunyang, and General Jinu. He defeated Qin Feng with Cen Peng, pacified Yangzhou, and died in Jianwu 7, posthumously named Weihou.

translation:
He and other generals attacked Luoyang, while Zhu Tuna's generals guarding the east city acted as counterattacks and made a private agreement to open the east gate in the early morning.
Jiantan and Jianyi General Zhu You took the opportunity to enter and fought with Zhu Tuna in Kuxia, killing many people. The fighting did not cease until breakfast, and Zhu Tun surrendered.
He attacked Neihuang again and calmed down.
In the second year of Jianwu, he and his right general Wan captured the counties of Nanyang, while Dong Jinjin, a native of Duxiang, built in Wancheng and captured Liu Ma, the prefect of Nanyang.
Jiantan then led his troops to Wan, and selected his own suicide squad to climb the city tower at night and cut through the pass. Dong Jinjin abandoned the city and returned to Duxiang.
Deng Feng built another army in Xinye and defeated Wu Han.
At this time, Wan died of illness, and Jiandan was alone and helpless. Deng Feng was blocked from the south, and Dong Tanjin was blocked from the north. For a year, the roads were blocked and food supplies were cut off. Jiantan ate only vegetables and worked hard with the soldiers.
Whenever he encounters a battle, he often acts as a target and is wounded in three places on his body, in order to save his troops.
When the emperor conquered Nanyang and defeated Dong Yujin and Deng Feng, he appointed Jiantan as his left cao and often followed him on expeditions.
In the sixth year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Marquis of Hefei.
Jianwu died in the twenty-sixth year of his reign.
Zijianhong succeeded to the throne.
Jianhong died, and Zijian succeeded to the throne.
Jianfu died, and Zijianya succeeded to the throne.
◆The biography of Ma Wu Ma Wu was named Zizhang and was a native of Huyang, Nanyang County.
When he was young, he lived in Jiangxia to avoid hatred.
In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, the three elders of Jingling and Xiyang raised troops at the county border. Ma Wu also participated. Later, they entered the green forest and joined the Han army.
When Gengshi was established, he appointed Ma Wu as his minister, and together with his ancestor Po Wang Xun and others, he worshiped him as General Zhenwei, and together with Shangshu Ling Xie Gong attacked Wang Lang.
Shizu conquered Handan and invited Xie Gong, Ma Wu and others to hold a grand cocktail party in an attempt to kill Xie Gong, but failed.
After the reception, Shizu and Ma Wu climbed up the Congtai alone and calmly said to Ma Wu: I have obtained the Yuyang and Shanggu assault cavalry and want you to command them. How about it?
Ma Wu said: I am dull, cowardly and have no strategy. Shizu said: "A general has been a general for a long time and has a deep knowledge of military affairs. Is it the same as my history?" From this, Ma Wu returned to Shizu in his heart. After Xie Gong was executed, Ma Wu rushed to She Quan and surrendered. Shizu was very happy to see him and led him to his side. Every time he held a condolence banquet with the generals, Ma Wu often got up and considered it before him. Shizu was very happy.
Then he asked Ma Wu to lead his troops to Ye. Ma Wu kowtowed and refused, saying that he was unwilling. Shizu praised his intention even more, and asked Ma Wu to follow him to attack the bandits.
Shizu attacked You Lai, Wu Ban and others, but failed at Shenshui. Ma Wu, the only rear army in the palace, returned to attack the enemy's position, so the rebels did not dare to catch up.
summary: **Jian Tan**, courtesy name Zidanji, from Yingchuan, was a county official. Shizu summoned him, made him chief bookkeeper and partial general. He pacified Hebei and defeated Yu Lunu. After ascension, he became General Yanghua and Marquis of Xuyin. He attacked Luoyang, opening the east gate with Zhu You, and fought Zhu Tuna until surrender. He pacified Neihuang, captured Nanyang counties, and fought Deng Feng while besieged for a year, eating only vegetables. He was wounded three times saving his troops. He became Marquis of Hefei in Jianwu 6 and died in Jianwu 26. **Ma Wu**, courtesy name Zizhang, from Nanyang, joined the Green Forest Army and later the Han. Gengshi made him General Zhenwei. Shizu invited him to command Yuyang and Shanggu cavalry, and Ma Wu secretly turned to Shizu. After Xie Gong's execution, Ma Wu surrendered. Shizu made him Shizhong, Qi Duwei, and Shandu Marquis. He attacked Liu Yong, captured Chengwu, defeated Pang Meng, and fought Wei Xiao, charging with a painted halberd to save the army. He became Marquis of Yu, guarded against Xiongnu, and was known for drinking and speaking frankly. The emperor tolerated his faults. He attacked Wuling barbarians and later Western Qiang, beheading 4,600. He died in Yongping 4.
