translation:
In Yongping, Xianzong recalled the heroes of his previous life, so he drew pictures of twenty-eight generals and hung them on the cloud platform of Nangong. In addition, there were Wang Chang, Li Tong, Dou Rong, and Zhuo Mao, a total of thirty-two people.
Here it is appended to the end of the chapter according to its original order to indicate the ranking of the meritorious officials.
Tai Fu Gaomi Hou Deng Yu, Grand Sima Guangping Hou Wu Han, Left General Jiaodong Hou Jia Fu, Jianwei General Haojue Hou Geng Yan, Hussar General Shen Zang Hou Du Mao, Zhijin Wu Yongnu Hou Kou Xun, Southern General Wuyang Hou Cenpeng, Western General Yangxia Hou Feng Yi, Jian The general of Yi is Zhu You, the marquis of Yingyang, the conquering general is Yingyang Hou Jizun, the hussar general is Yueyang Hou Jingdan, the Huya general is Anpinghou Gaiyan, the guard is Anchenghou Yaoqi, the prefect of Dongjun is Dongguang Hou Gengchun, the city gate captain is Langling Hou Zanggong, the captor general Yang Xu is Hou Mawu, Piao Cavalry General Shen Hou Liu Long, Zhongshan Governor Quanjiao Hou Ma Cheng, Henan Yin Fucheng Hou Wang Liang, Langfu Governor Zhu Ahou Chen Jun, Hussar General Shen Zanghou Du Mao, Ji Crossbow General Kunyang Hou Fu Jun, Zuo Cao Hou Jiantan, Shanggu Governor Huai Linghou Wang Ba, Xindu Governor Alinghou Renguang, Yuzhang prefect Zhongshuihou Li Zhong, right general Huailihou Wanxiu, Taichang Lingshouhou Pitong, Xiaoqi general Changchenghou Liu Zhi, Hengye general Shansanghou Wangchang, Grand Sikong Gushihou Li Tong, Grand Sikong Anfenghou Dou Rong, Taifu Xuande Hou Zhuomao.
summary: The historian comments that the twenty-eight Zhongxing generals were thought to correspond to constellations. Guangwu's policy of not appointing meritorious officials to high positions was foresighted, avoiding the disasters of Han Xin and Peng Yue. He rewarded heroes with fiefs but kept them from state affairs, maintaining peace. In Yongping, Xianzong painted thirty-two generals on Nangong's Cloud Platform, including Deng Yu, Wu Han, Jia Fu, Geng Yan, Du Mao, Kou Xun, Cen Peng, Feng Yi, Zhu You, Ji Zun, Jing Dan, Gai Yan, Yao Qi, Geng Chun, Zang Gong, Ma Wu, Liu Long, Ma Cheng, Wang Liang, Chen Jun, Du Mao, Fu Jun, Jian Tan, Wang Ba, Ren Guang, Li Zhong, Wan Xiu, Pi Tong, Liu Zhi, Wang Chang, Li Tong, Dou Rong, and Zhuo Mao.

translation:
◆The biography of Li Gu, whose courtesy name was Zijian, was from Nanzheng, Hanzhong, and the son of Situ Li Hui.
Li Hui's deeds are in "The Biography of Fang Shu".
The statue of Li Gu has a peculiar appearance. There are bones on the head that protrude like a tripod foot, which rise into the hairline, and there are turtle inscriptions on the feet.
When he was young, he was eager to learn and often traveled thousands of miles to find teachers on foot.
So I read many ancient books and made friends with many wise men.
People with lofty ideals from all over the world envy his style and come to learn from him.
Everyone in the capital admired and said: This is the second Mr. Li again. Both Sili and Yizhou ordered the county governors to promote Li Gu as Xiaolian and call him Sikongpu, but they did not take office.
In the second year of Yangjia, there were earthquakes, landslides, fires and other changes. The ministers recommended Li Gu to take countermeasures. The emperor issued an edict specifically asking him about the shortcomings of the contemporary era and what he should do for government.
Li Gu replied: "I heard that the king regards heaven as his father and earth as his mother, and possesses the treasures of mountains and rivers."
If the royal way works, then Yin and Yang will be harmonious; if politics is disobedient, landslides and earthquakes will become disasters.
This is all related to the heart of heaven, and the results are achieved in achieving things.
The so-called transformation is achieved by job, and officials are able to manage.
In ancient times, those who became officials were all virtuous and had titles; those who become officials today only have wealth and strength.
The ministers heard that the imperial edict sought to be lenient and generous, but resented harshness and cruelty.
However, today's chief officials have made a name for themselves by killing more, and they will definitely be promoted and rewarded; while those who are kind-hearted and have no support from party members are often ostracized and exiled.
Therefore, honest and honest customs cannot be promoted, and Zhou's thin customs cannot be reformed.
Even if we use heavy punishment and heavy prohibition, what is the benefit?
The former Emperor Xiao'an messed up the old rules and conferred a title on his mother, Wang Sheng, thus creating a monster, which allowed Fan Feng and others to take advantage of their power and usurp the majesty of the Lord.
Since he emerged from the crisis and became emperor, everyone in the world is looking up to him, hoping that the political system will change.
After a long time of accumulation, it is easy to revive, and one should indeed be generous and think about the way to do good; but the people who discuss it also say that the current things are the same as before.
The minister crouched among the mountains and grass, feeling very sad.
Recalling that since the rise of the Han Dynasty, for more than three hundred years, sages and ten and eight monarchs have appeared one after another.
Don’t you have the kindness of Ah Ru?
Have you forgotten the favor of the noble noble?
However, the superiors are afraid of the power of God, and the inferiors know according to the scriptures that they must not violate moral principles, so they do not add rewards.
Now, although Mrs. Song has the character of great merit and diligence, as long as she is rewarded, it will be enough to repay her hard work; as for the enfeoffment of land, it is really contrary to the old rules.
summary: Li Gu, courtesy name Zijian, was from Nanzheng, Hanzhong, and the son of Situ Li Hui. He had a peculiar appearance with bones on his head protruding like a tripod foot and turtle inscriptions on his feet. He was an eager learner who traveled thousands of miles to find teachers, befriended many wise men, and attracted students from across the land. He was promoted as Xiaolian but did not take office. In the second year of Yangjia, after earthquakes and landslides, the emperor asked Li Gu for advice. Li Gu replied that if the royal way works, Yin and Yang are harmonious; if politics are disobedient, disasters occur. He criticized that officials today only seek wealth and power, and that harsh officials are promoted while kind ones are ostracized. He advised against enfeoffing the emperor's grandmother, citing the danger of excessive power for relatives, and warned against the influence of the Liang family and eunuchs. He urged the emperor to select virtuous officials, dismiss eunuchs, and follow the laws of sages. Emperor Shun adopted many of his suggestions, but eunuchs framed Li Gu, leading to his dismissal. He later became a magistrate but resigned and returned home.

translation:
Confucius said: A wise man thinks of punishment when he sees a change, but a fool hides his name when he sees something strange. There is no distinction between closeness and distance in the way of heaven, which can be respected.
The recent lunar eclipse has been on the side of Duanmen. Moon, the symbol of the minister.
Generally speaking, if it is too high, it will be dangerous; if it is too full, it will overflow; if the moon is full, it will be short; and if the sun is at noon, it will shift.
These four items are natural numbers.
In the heart of heaven and earth, blessings should be modest and should not be prosperous. Therefore, virtuous people will retire after success, preserve their reputation, and live their lives well, without fear or worry.
If Wang Gang is kept intact, his conduct is loyal, Ming Gong follows the path of Bo Gao, and his immortal reputation is preserved, is it the same as these mediocre relatives who enjoy a good position?
I am a foolish person who is ignorant of the general situation. I secretly feel that the ancients repaid a favor with a meal. How much more can I not do my best to receive care and preferential treatment?
Liang Shang did not listen.
During the Yonghe period, bandits arose in Jingzhou and could not be pacified for many years, so the imperial court appointed Li Gu as the governor of Jingzhou.
After Li Gu took office, he sent officials to visit the territory to express condolences, pardon the bandits' previous crimes, and start over with them.
So the bandit leader Xia Mi and others recruited more than 600 of their gang members, tied themselves up, and came to surrender.
Li Gudu forgave them and asked them to go back, so that they could gather among themselves and start a demonstration.
Within half a year, all the thieves surrendered, and the state was at peace ever since.
Li Gu reported to Nanyang Governor Gao Ci and others about their corrupt behavior.
Gao Ci and others were afraid of being punished, so they jointly bribed the general Liang Ji with a large sum of money. Liang Ji sent the message thousands of miles for them, but Li Gu held on tighter.
Liang Ji then ordered Li Gu to be appointed as the prefect of Taishan.
At this time, the bandits in Taishan had been gathering for many years. There were often thousands of soldiers in the county, and they could not be suppressed by pursuit.
After Li Gu took office, he dismissed all the county soldiers and went back to farm. He only selected more than a hundred people with fighting ability to stay and used their kindness to lure the thieves to surrender.
Within a year, the thieves had all fled.
Li Gu was promoted to a general and a master craftsman.
Shangshu Chenshi said: I have heard that those with pure Qi are called gods, and those with pure Qi are called virtuous.
The most valuable thing for cultivating one's body is cultivating one's spirit, and the right way for governing a country is to accumulate virtues.
In ancient times, the Qin State wanted to attack the Chu State. Wang Sunyu set up an altar at the west gate and displayed the names of famous ministers. The Qin envoy was surprised and stopped the attack.
Wei Wenhou regarded Bu Zixia as his teacher and Tian Zifang as his friend, and paid tribute to Duan Qianmu. Therefore, all the wise men rushed to come, and their reputation exceeded that of Duke Huan of Qi. Qin did not dare to send troops to Xihe. This was probably the fate of Ji Xian.
His Majesty set things right and ascended the throne for the first time. He invited Fan Ying from Nanyang, Huang Qiong from Jiangxia, Yang Hou from Guanghan, and He Chun from Kuaiji. He praised them in policy letters and received them as officials.
Therefore, those who live in seclusion and those who are wise and skillful will celebrate each other with their hats and clothes, and will be willing to do their best for you. People all over the world will be happy and submit to the Holy Virtue.
summary: Liang Shang asked Li Gu to be a lieutenant. Li Gu wrote to Liang Shang, criticizing the corruption of previous reigns and urging him to rectify morals, reduce palace concubines, and establish a crown prince. He warned against building new ancestral halls and noted that disasters and eclipses indicated conspiracies within the palace. Liang Shang did not listen. During the Yonghe period, Li Gu was appointed governor of Jingzhou, where he pardoned bandits and pacified the region within half a year. He reported corrupt officials, who bribed Liang Ji, leading to Li Gu's transfer to Taishan. There, he dismissed most soldiers and used kindness to subdue bandits within a year.

translation:
After the letter was submitted, Liang Ji told the Queen Mother, please submit it to the people below for trial.
The queen mother refused to listen and was spared from death.
Liang Ji feared that the emperor's intelligence would cause future troubles, so he ordered people to poison him.
The emperor was distressed and depressed, so he sent someone to find Li Gu.
Li Gu went in, stepped forward and asked: How did your majesty get sick? The emperor was still able to speak and said: I ate boiled cakes and now I feel very stuffy in my stomach. I can still survive if I can find some water. Liang Ji was also there at the time and said: "I'm afraid I might vomit, so I can't drink water." He died before he finished speaking.
Li Gu lay down on the corpse and cried, and recommended him to serve as a doctor.
Liang Ji was worried that the matter would be leaked, and hated him especially.
So they discussed the establishment of an heir. Li Gu introduced Situ Hu Guang and Sikong Zhao Jie, and first wrote to Liang Ji: The world is unfortunate and still suffers from great worries.
The empress dowager was in power, the prime minister was full of opportunities, and the generals of the Ming Dynasty followed the principles of loyalty and filial piety and considered the safety of the country. However, in the past few years, the country was cut off three times.
Today is the time to establish an emperor. The throne is a valuable weapon in the world. The Queen Mother is very concerned about it. The general is careful to choose the right person and keep the sage.
However, Wu Qing thought twice and had his own thoughts in private.
Looking far away to see the old system that was abolished by our ancestors, and looking at the past events of the country's establishment of an emperor, we have never failed to visit the ministers and solicit opinions extensively. We must comply with the will of heaven and the wishes of everyone below.
Besides, since the Yongchu period, there have been many fallacies in political affairs, earthquakes in palaces and temples, and comets appearing in the sky. It is indeed the time for the general to put his mind to work. "Ancient Book" says: It is easy for the world to deal with people, but it is difficult for the world to win people. Once upon a time, when the king of Changyi was appointed, he was in a state of confusion. Huo Guang was so worried that he broke his bones with regret.
If it weren't for the loyalty and bravery of Huo Guang, the Marquis of Bolu, and the hard work of Da Si Farming Yannian, the country of the Han Dynasty would have almost collapsed.
It can be seen that the matter is of great importance and must be carefully considered!
Of all things, this is the biggest thing. The rise and fall of a country depends on this.
After Liang Ji got the letter, he summoned the three princes, Zhong Erqian Shi, and other princes to discuss who should be chosen.
Li Gu, Hu Guang, Zhao Jie and Dahonglu Du Qiao all believed that Liu Lian, the king of Qinghe, was well-educated and respected the most relatives, so he should be established as his heir.
First, Liwu Hou Liu Zhidang married Liang Ji's sister. At this time, he was in the capital, and Liang Ji wanted to marry him.
Everyone disagreed, and Liang Ji was angry, but there was no other reason to change everyone's mind. After hearing this, Cao Teng and others went to Liang Ji in the evening to persuade him: "The generals have been related to the queen for several generations and have great power. The guests behaved wildly and made many mistakes."
King Qinghe is a very strict man. If he is established as king, the general will not suffer disaster soon.
It is better to establish Li Wuhou, and the wealth and honor can be maintained for a long time. Liang Ji agreed with them. When he met with the ministers again the next day, Liang Ji was in high spirits and spoke excitedly.
There are no officials from Hu Guang and Zhao Jie who are not afraid.
They all say: Only the general gives orders. But Li Gu and Du Qiao still insisted on their original opinions.
Liang Ji loudly announced the strike. Li Gu's opinion was not listened to, but he still hoped that everyone would be convinced, and wrote to Liang Ji again.
Liang Ji became even more angry, so he persuaded the Queen Mother to remove Li Gu from his position first, and instead appointed Li Wuhou, who became Emperor Huan.
More than a year later, Liu Wen of Ganling and Liu Kun of Wei County each planned to make Liu Lian the emperor. Liang Ji therefore falsely accused Li Gu, Liu Wen, Liu Kun and others of spreading rumors and imprisoned them.
Li Gu's disciple Bohai Wang Tiao Guanzhi wrote a letter to prove Li Gu's injustice. Dozens of people including Zhao Cheng in Hanoi also asked the husband to go to the court to complain. The Queen Mother understood their intentions and pardoned the crime.
summary: Li Gu was promoted and recommended several scholars. He later became Taiwei under Emperor Chong. When the emperor died, Li Gu insisted on immediate mourning, opposing the Empress Dowager's delay. He advocated for establishing an older, virtuous emperor, but Liang Ji appointed the young Liu Zuan as Emperor Zhi. Li Gu reduced burial costs for the emperor. He dismissed over a hundred improperly appointed officials, who then slandered him to Liang Ji, accusing him of nepotism, extravagance, and lack of mourning. The Empress Dowager spared Li Gu from death. Liang Ji later poisoned Emperor Zhi. Li Gu cried over the emperor's body. When establishing a new emperor, Li Gu advocated for Liu Lian, the King of Qinghe, but Liang Ji, persuaded by eunuchs, chose Liu Zhidang (Emperor Huan) instead. Liang Ji later falsely accused Li Gu of plotting to make Liu Lian emperor and imprisoned him. Despite public support, Liang Ji had Li Gu killed at age 54. Before death, Li Gu wrote to Hu Guang and Zhao Jie, blaming them for following Liang Ji and causing the decline of the Han dynasty. His sons died in prison, and his body was exposed. His disciple Guo Liang and others mourned him, and the Empress Dowager eventually allowed his burial.

translation:
In the first year of Han'an, Du Qiao acted for Dr. Guanglu and sent him to inspect Yanzhou.
The above table reports that Li Gu, the prefect of Taishan, has the best political performance in the world; Liang Rang, the prefect of Chenliu, Si Gong, the prefect of Jiyin, and Cui Yuan, the prefect of Jibei, etc. embezzled more than ten million.
Liang Rang is the uncle of General Liang Ji, and Bangong and Cui Yuan are Liang Ji's cronies.
Returning to Beijing, he was awarded the title of Crown Prince and Tutor, and was promoted to Minister of Agriculture.
At this time, the five descendants of Liang Ji and the ministers of Zhongchang had no merit and were granted the title. Du Qiao wrote a letter to remonstrate: The emperor comes from the vassals, Long Fei ascends the throne, heaven and man return, and all nations rely on them.
However, instead of appointing loyal and virtuous people, they first appoint the left and right confidants. This harms good people, is harmful to virtue, and encourages the trend of flattery.
I heard that in ancient times, wise kings were rewarded for their merits and punished for their faults; the declining kings were dim and incompetent, and rewards and punishments were all based on selfish motives.
Nowadays, the Liang family, the eunuchs and evil sons, all wear seals and ribbons with no merit, and the fiefdoms for their hard work and merit are given to them. How can we fully explain the perverseness and disorder of this practice.
Merits are not rewarded, and good deeds are not rewarded as they should be; no one cares about treacherous people, allowing them to do evil and cause disaster.
Therefore, people are not afraid of the murderous butcher's knife placed in front of them, and conferring titles and titles will not serve as a reward.
If this continues for a long time, is it just harmful to political integrity? It is enough to cause chaos and ruin the country. It is worthy of vigilance! Please play, your Majesty does not need it.
Yizhou governor Zhongfan impeached Yongchang prefect Liu Junshi and sent a golden snake to Liang Ji. When the incident was discovered, he sent the golden snake to Sinong.
Liang Ji asked Du Qiao to borrow it for a look, but Du Qiao refused, and Liang Ji began to hold a grudge.
Du Qiao was promoted to Dahonglu.
At this time, Liang Ji's daughter died, and all the officials went to attend the funeral. Du Qiao could not go alone, and Liang Ji hated him even more.
Du Qiao was promoted to Guang Luxun.
In the first year of Jianhe, Hu Guang was appointed Taiwei on his behalf.
Emperor Huan planned to accept Liang Ji's sister as his queen. Liang Ji wanted to welcome his sister with generous gifts, but Du Qiao refused to listen to him according to the old regulations.
Liang Ji asked Du Qiao to appoint Si Gong as minister. Du Qiao believed that Si Gong was guilty of embezzlement and refused to use it. This greatly contradicted Liang Ji's wishes.
First, Li Gu was deposed, and everyone inside and outside the court was dejected. All the ministers were afraid and trembling. Only Du Qiao was serious and did not dare to offend.
Therefore, the whole country sighed for him, and both the government and the public looked at him and worried about him.
After a few months in office, he was dismissed from office due to an earthquake.
Eunuchs Tang Heng, Zuo and others jointly framed Du Qiao in front of Emperor Huan, saying: When the emperor ascended the throne, Du Qiao and Li Gu objected, saying that the emperor was not worthy of enshrining the ancestral temple of the Han Dynasty and inheriting the throne.
Emperor Huan also hated him. After the Qinghe King incident occurred, Liang Ji suggested that the supervisor should impeach Du Qiao and Li Gu for colluding with Liu Tuna, and ask for their arrest and prosecution.
The Empress Dowager Liang always knew that Du Qiao was loyal, so she only dismissed him from office.
Liang Ji became even more angry and sent someone to threaten Du Qiao, saying: "If you commit suicide early, your wife will be saved." Duccio refused.
The next day Liang Ji sent cavalry to his house, but when he heard no cries, he arrested him and died in prison.
summary: Du Qiao, courtesy name Shurong, was from Linli, Hanoi. He served as a prefect and later as a servant. He reported that Li Gu had the best political performance and that others, including Liang Ji's relatives, had embezzled money. He was promoted to Minister of Agriculture. He remonstrated against granting titles to Liang Ji's relatives and eunuchs without merit, warning it would cause chaos. He refused Liang Ji's requests to borrow evidence and attend his daughter's funeral, earning Liang Ji's hatred. As Guang Luxun, he opposed lavish gifts for Liang Ji's sister becoming queen and refused to appoint a corrupt official. After Li Gu was deposed, Du Qiao remained serious and unyielding. He was dismissed due to an earthquake. Eunuchs and Liang Ji framed him for opposing the emperor's ascension and colluding with Li Gu. He was arrested and died in prison. His body was exposed, but his former subordinate Yang Kuang mourned him and requested burial, which the Empress Dowager granted. The historian commented that Li Gu and Du Qiao sacrificed their lives for righteousness, unlike Hu Guang and Zhao Jie.

translation:
Li Tong, whose courtesy name was Ciyuan, was from Wan County, Nanyang County.
He has been famous for doing business for generations.
His father, Li Shou, was nine feet tall and his appearance was very different from ordinary people. He was serious and resolute, and his home was as if he were in a court.
At first, he worked with Liu Xin. He was fond of astronomical calculations and prophecies for predicting bad luck. He became Wang Mang's disciple.
Li Tong also worked for General Wuwei, and later became the magistrate of Wu County, with a reputation for being capable.
In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, the people were worried and resentful. Li Tong once heard his father's prophecy about the revival of the Liu family and the Li family as an assistant, and he often thought about it.
Because his family was very wealthy and ranked first in the township, he did not want to be an official, so he voluntarily resigned and returned home.
Later, Wang Chang's Xiajiang soldiers and Wang Kuang's Xinshi soldiers rose up, causing turmoil in Nanyang. Li Tong's cousin Li Yi, who had always been a good person, discussed together and said: Now that there is chaos from all directions, Wang Mang's regime is about to collapse, and the Han Dynasty should rise.
Among the Liu clan in Nanyang, only the Liu Boxheng brothers could love and accommodate the masses, and could conspire with them to destroy Wang Mang and revitalize the Han Dynasty. Li Tong smiled and said: My opinion is the same. When Guangwu took refuge in Wan, Li Tong heard about it and sent Li Yi to greet Guangwu.
Guang Wuchu admired Li Tong because he was a gentleman, so he went to thank him.
When they met, the two talked for a long time and shook hands happily.
Li Tong told all the prophecies, and Guangwu started to have a big surprise, saying that he didn't dare to take it seriously.
At this time, Li Shou was in Chang'an. Guangwu looked at Li Tong secretly and said, "In this case, what should your father do?" Li Tong said: I already have a solution. So he stated his plan in detail to Guangwu.
Since Guangwu was well aware of Li Tong's intentions, he made an agreement with Li Tong and made a plan to take advantage of the capital's knight test on the first day of autumn to kidnap Zhen Fu, a senior official in the front team, and Qiuci, a subordinate of Zhengliang, so he ordered the public to declare an uprising.
He sent Guangwu and Li Yi back to Chongling and raised their troops accordingly.
He sent his cousin's son Li Ji to Chang'an to tell Li Shou the plan.
Li Ji died of illness on the road. Li Shou knew the secret and wanted to flee back.
Li Shousu was friendly with Huang Xian, a fellow villager. Huang Xian was then the Zhonglang General. When he heard the news, he said to Li Shou: "The gates are now tightly guarded. Your appearance is special. Where will you go?"
It is better to go to the court and ask for your return.
Things haven't happened yet, as long as we can get away, we can avoid disaster. After Li Shou heard what he said, he wrote a letter asking for death. The memorial was not submitted in time, so he stayed in the palace.
At this time, the matter was discovered and Li Tong was able to escape. When Wang Mang found out, he arrested Li Shou and imprisoned him.
Huang Xian interceded for Li Shou and said: Li Shou heard that his son had committed a serious crime and did not dare to flee back. He obeyed his righteousness and returned to you.
I, Huang Xian, would rather take Li Shou to the east and inform his son.
If his son really wants to rebel, I will order Li Shou to commit suicide to the north to thank him for his great kindness. Wang Mang agreed.
At this time, Zhen Fu from the front team wrote another letter stating the situation of Li Tong's army. Wang Mang was angry and prepared to kill Li Shou. Huang Xian argued for him, so Li Shou and Huang Xian were killed together, along with all Li Shou's family members in Chang'an.
Nanyang also killed Li Tong's brothers and sixty-four members of his clan, and burned their bodies in Wan City.
At this time, Han soldiers had also gathered in large numbers.
Li Tong met Guangwu and Li Yi in Jiyang, so they attacked the front line together and killed Zhen Fu and Liang Qiuci.
summary: Li Tong, courtesy name Ciyuan, was from Wan County, Nanyang. His family was renowned for business, and his father Li Shou was a tall, imposing man who served Wang Mang. Li Tong worked for General Wuwei and later became magistrate of Wu County, known for his competence. During Wang Mang's late reign, Li Tong heard his father's prophecy about the Liu family's revival with the Li family as assistants. Wealthy and disinclined to serve, he resigned and returned home. When rebellions erupted in Nanyang, Li Tong and his cousin Li Yi discussed joining Liu Boxheng (Liu Yan) and his brother Guangwu (Liu Xiu) to restore the Han. Li Tong sent Li Yi to greet Guangwu, and they formed a pact. They planned to kidnap officials Zhen Fu and Liang Qiuci to spark an uprising. Li Tong sent his cousin's son Li Ji to inform Li Shou in Chang'an, but Li Ji died en route. Li Shou, learning the secret, tried to flee but was advised by Huang Xian to request leave. The plot was discovered; Wang Mang arrested Li Shou and, despite Huang Xian's pleas, executed both and Li Shou's family in Chang'an. Nanyang also killed sixty-four of Li Tong's clan members. Li Tong joined Guangwu and Li Yi in Jiyang, attacking and killing Zhen Fu and Liang Qiuci. Under Gengshi, Li Tong became General of Zhuguo and later King of Xiping. He married Guangwu's sister, Princess Ningping. After Guangwu ascended, Li Tong served as Grand Minister of Agriculture, guarding the capital during campaigns. In Jianwu 5-6, he led troops against Hanzhong bandits and Gongsun Shu, defeating them. As peace prevailed, Li Tong sought to retire due to illness, but Guangwu refused. He became Grand Sikong but remained humble, often taking sick leave. Guangwu favored him, granting his son Li Xiong a marquisate. Li Tong died in Jianwu 18, posthumously titled Gonghou. His lineage continued, and he alone among his kin lived with honor.

translation:
Later, the emperor pointed to Wang Chang in the meeting and said to the officials: This family leads the generals from the lower reaches of the Yangtze River to support the Han Dynasty, and their hearts are like gold and stone. They are really loyal ministers! On this day, King Tianqian Chang was a loyal general of the Han Dynasty. He sent him south to attack Deng Feng and Dong Yijin, and ordered all the generals to belong to him.
He also ordered the king to attack Hejian and Yuyang from the north to pacify the settlements.
In the autumn of the fifth year of Jianwu, he captured Huling and met with the emperor in Rencheng, thus defeating Sumao and Pang Meng from the emperor.
During the attack on Xiapi, Wang Chang's troops fought at the city gate. On the first day, the thieves fled into the city. Wang Chang pursued and forced them. Arrows rained down on the city. The emperor watched from a high place in the south of the city with more than a hundred riders. Wang Chang fought bravely and sent Zhonghuangmenchi to issue an edict to lure the thieves back. The thieves surrendered.
He also led the cavalry captain Wang Ba to defeat the Peijun thieves.
In the spring of the sixth year of Jianwu, he returned to Luoyang and ordered his wife to welcome Wang Chang in Wuyang, return home and go to the tomb.
Xitun troops were stationed in Chang'an and rejected Wei Xiao.
In the seventh year of Jianwu's reign, Guangwu sent an envoy with a seal to worship Wang Chang as the General of Hengye, and his rank was distinguished from that of other generals.
Wang Changbie defeated Wei Xiao and general Gao Jun was in Chaona.
Kaixiao sent his generals to pass through Wushi County, and Wang Chang invited him to attack and defeat Kaixiao's tribe.
He also surrendered the walls of the Qiang camps and pacified them all.
In the ninth year of Jianwu's reign, he attacked the yellow thieves and defeated them.
Later, he went to Gu'an in Beitun and refused Lu Fang.
In the twelfth year of Jianwu's reign, he died in the garrison and was given the posthumous title of Jiehou.
His son Wang Guang succeeded to the throne.
In the 30th year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Shicheng.
In the 14th year of Yongping, the fiefdom was abolished due to his involvement in the rebellion of King Chu.
Deng Chen, whose courtesy name was Weiqing, was from Xinye County, Nanyang County.
Both his great-grandfather and grandfather served as governors and had an estate of 2,000 shi.
His father, Deng Hong, was the captain of Yuzhang.
Deng Chen initially married Guangwu's sister Liu Yuan.
At the end of Wang Mang's reign, Guangwu, his brothers Bosheng and Deng Chendu went to Wancheng and talked with Cai Shaogong, a Rang man.
The young master learned from the prophecies and said that Liu Xiu should be the emperor.
Some people said: Is it the Grand Master Liu Xiu? Guangwuxi replied: How do you know it's not me? Everyone sitting there laughed, and Deng Chen felt happy.
When Guangwu and his family took refuge in Xinye, they lived in Deng Chen's home and became very dear to each other.
Deng Chen therefore said to Guangwu: "Wang Mang is rebellious and violent, killing people in midsummer. This is the time for the death of Wang Mang."
Is it true that I met in Wancheng before? Guangwu smiled but didn't answer.
When the Han soldiers rose up, Deng Chen led his guests to meet in Jiyang.
The Han army was defeated in Xiaochang'an, and many generals lost their families. Guangwu fled alone, met his sister Boji, and rode with her.
summary: Wang Chang, courtesy name Yanqing, from Wuyang, Yingchuan, fled to Jiangxia after avenging his brother. He joined Wang Feng and Wang Kuang in the Lulin uprising, becoming a supporting general. After defeats, he regrouped in Ruoxi Valley and revived his forces, defeating Jingzhou Mu and reaching Nanyang. When Han forces were defeated at Xiaochang'an, Bosheng and Guangwu sought Wang Chang's alliance. Wang Chang, convinced of the Han's destiny, persuaded his reluctant generals Cheng Dan and Zhang to join, citing the people's longing for Han. They united, defeated Zhen Fu and Liang Qiuci, and supported Gengshi. Wang Chang became a court official and marquis, later serving as Nanyang prefect under Gengshi. After Gengshi's fall, he surrendered to Guangwu, who forgave him and appointed him Zuocao. Wang Chang campaigned against various rebels, including Deng Feng and Wei Xiao, and pacified regions. He died in Jianwu 12, posthumously titled Jiehou. His son Wang Guang succeeded but lost the fief due to involvement in a rebellion. Deng Chen, courtesy name Weiqing, from Xinye, Nanyang, married Guangwu's sister Liu Yuan. During Wang Mang's reign, he heard a prophecy about Liu Xiu becoming emperor and bonded with Guangwu. When Han forces rose, Deng Chen joined Guangwu at Jiyang. After a defeat, Guangwu fled with his sister Boji, but Liu Yuan and her daughters were killed. Deng Chen's home was defiled, yet he remained loyal. Under Gengshi, he became a partial general, fighting alongside Guangwu. He served as Changshan governor, supporting Guangwu during Wang Lang's rebellion. After Guangwu's ascension, Deng Chen became a marquis. He governed Zhongshan and Runan, building irrigation systems that enriched the region. He died in Jianwu 25, posthumously titled Hui. His lineage continued until it ended without heirs.

translation:
After solid death, heir to the country.
If the country dies, the son will be blessed with heirs. If he dies in the first year of Yongjian's reign and has no children, the country will be eliminated.
Uncle Lai Shezi is from Xinye County, Nanyang.
My father came to Zhong. He was an admonishing official during the reign of Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty. He married Guangwu's aunt, and she was born. Lai She's sister was the wife of Liu Jia, the king of Hanzhong. Liu Jia sent people to greet Lai She, so he came south to Hanzhong.
After Emperor Gengshi failed, Lai She persuaded Liu Jia to join Emperor Guangwu, so he and Liu Jia went east to Luoyang.
After the rise of the Han army, Wang Mang imprisoned She since she was a relative of the Liu family, and the guests jointly used force to seize it, so they were spared.
After Gengshi came to the throne, Yishe became an official and followed him into the pass.
Several suggestions were not adopted and he left due to illness.
Lai She's sister was the wife of Liu Jia, the king of Hanzhong. Liu Jia sent people to welcome Lai She, so she went south to Hanzhong.
When Gengshi was defeated, Lai She persuaded Liu Jia to surrender to Guangwu, so he and Liu Jiadong went to Luoyang.
Emperor Guangwu was very happy to see Lai She. He immediately took off his own clothes and put them on Lai She, and appointed him as Taizhong doctor.
At this time, Emperor Wu was worried about Long and Shu, so Lai She took the initiative to ask for help and said: I once met Wei Xiao in Chang'an.
When that man first started his army, he was in the name of reviving the Han Dynasty. Now His Majesty's holy virtue is majestic. I hope that I can follow your orders and enlighten him with unchanging integrity. Wei Xiao will definitely surrender without restraint. Then Gongsun Shu will be destroyed, so there is no need to worry.
Emperor Guangwu thought he was right.
Emperor Guangwu thought he was right. In the third year of Jianwu's reign, Lai She was sent as an envoy to Kaixiao.
In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, Kai Xiao sent his son Kai Xun to follow Lai She and enter the court as a hostage.
At that time, Shandong was generally pacified. Emperor Guangwu planned to collect Wei Xiao's troops from the west and wanted to attack Shu with them. He also sent Lai She to inform Wei Xiao of his will.
Wei Xiao's subordinates persuaded him and raised many questions, which made him hesitate for a long time. Lai She had always been resolute, so he angrily questioned and blamed Kui Xiao, saying: The emperor thought that you knew good and evil, and the principles of rise and fall, so he wrote to you personally to express his feelings. You expressed your sincerity and sent your son Bochun as a hostage. This is the mutual trust between the emperor and his ministers.
Now, instead of listening to the words of a treacherous villain, making a plan to exterminate the family, betraying the monarch, and implicating his son, is this a violation of loyalty and integrity? The choice that determines good or bad luck is today.
Lai She wanted to step forward and assassinate Kai Xiao, but Wei Xiao got up and entered the inner room, deployed his soldiers, and wanted to kill Lai She. Lai She calmly walked to the car with the talisman, got in, and left.
Wei Xiao became even more angry, and Wang Yuan advised him to kill Lai She. Lai She was loyal and consistent in his words and deeds, which could be verified even when lobbying back and forth. The scholar-bureaucrats in Xizhou trusted and respected him, and many people interceded on his behalf, so Lai She was able to escape and return to the East to the Han Dynasty.
summary: Lai She, courtesy name Junshe, from Xinye, was the son of an admonishing official who married Guangwu's aunt. His sister married Liu Jia, King of Hanzhong. After Gengshi's fall, Lai She persuaded Liu Jia to join Guangwu, who appointed him Taizhong doctor. Lai She volunteered to negotiate with Wei Xiao, securing his son as hostage. When Wei Xiao hesitated to attack Shu, Lai She angrily confronted him, nearly assassinating him. Wei Xiao imprisoned him but released him due to his reputation. In Jianwu 8, Lai She attacked Lueyang, holding it against Wei Xiao's siege until Guangwu relieved him. He later campaigned against Gongsun Shu and Qiang tribes, pacifying Longxi. In Jianwu 11, he was assassinated by Shu agents. Before dying, he reprimanded General Gai Yan for weeping and dictated a memorial recommending Duan Xiang and pleading for his brother. Guangwu mourned deeply, granting him posthumous honors. His son Lai Xi succeeded, and his brother was made a marquis. The historian praised Lai She's integrity as an envoy, noting his sincerity earned trust without selfish ambition.

translation:
◆In the biography of Li Xun, Li Xun was born in Linjing, Anding.
He studied "Han Shi" at a young age and taught hundreds of students.
Li Hong, the prefect of Yingchuan, asked Li Xun to be appointed as a meritorious official. However, he failed to take up the post, and the prefecture called him to work.
When Li Hong died, Li Xun responded to the state's order and sent Li Hong back to his hometown for his funeral.
He has been buried, and the grave has been left to mourn for three years.
Later Li Xun was called into Situ Huanyu's mansion.
Later he was promoted to the imperial censor, and he went to Youzhou as an envoy to declare the emperor's favor and comfort Beidi. Wherever he went, he described the mountains and rivers, as well as the conditions of villages and settlements, etc., in more than a hundred volumes, all of which were sealed. Emperor Suzong commended him and appointed him as the governor of Yanzhou.
He set an example by keeping promises, often using sheepskin as a mat and a quilt as a cover.
He was promoted to the governor of Zhangye and gained a prestigious reputation.
At that time, General Dou Xian and his soldiers were stationed in Wuwei. No matter how far or near the country was, no one in the country did not practice rituals and gifts of property. Li Xun was not loyal to his duty and was dismissed by Dou Xian.
Later, he was recruited as a visitor and made Chijie the captain of the Western Regions.
The Western Region was rich and rich, and there were many treasures. The servants and envoys of various countries and merchants from Hu Dynasty gave Li Xun many things such as slaves, horses, gold, silver, and fragrant yokes, but Li Xun refused to accept any of them.
The Northern Xiongnu cut off Cheshi and Yiwu in the Western Regions several times, and missions in the area west of Longsha were blocked. Li Xun offered a reward, so he beheaded the commander and hung his head at the military gate.
From then on, the road was clear and smooth, and kindness and power flowed side by side.
Later he moved to Wuwei to be the prefect.
He was dismissed from his post for some reason and walked back to his hometown. He lived in seclusion in the mountains and swamps, making a hut from grass and weaving mats with other people to support himself.
When the Xiqiang rebelled, Li Xun went to the farm and was captured by the Qiang people.
The Qiang people always heard Xun's name and sent him away.
Xun went to Luoyang to express his gratitude.
At that time, there was a famine. Sikong Zhang Min, Situ Lu Gong and other sons sent grain to Xun, but Xun did not accept it.
He moved to Xin'an Pass and picked up acorns to fill his stomach.
Died at the age of ninety-six.
◆Chen Chan's biography, Chen Chan's courtesy name is Jishan, and he was a native of Anhan, Ba County.
He was a meritorious officer in the county, doing good and punishing evil, and was feared by the people in the country.
He was inspected for being filial and honest, and he was appointed in the state to be engaged in governance.
At that time, the governor was accused of accepting bribes, and Chen Chan should be arrested and investigated. He had no property, just some funeral utensils.
After arriving, the plunder was in vain, all the five poisons were used, the Zen mind was at ease, the confession remained unchanged, and the case was solved.
Deng Zhi, the general of chariots and cavalry, heard about his reputation and summoned him, making him a talented person.
summary: Li Xun was born in Linjing, Anding, and studied "Han Shi" from a young age, teaching hundreds of students. He was appointed as a meritorious official by Prefect Li Hong of Yingchuan but failed to take up the post initially. After Li Hong's death, Li Xun served three years of mourning at his grave. He later served in Situ Huanyu's mansion and was promoted to imperial censor, traveling to Youzhou and Beidi to declare the emperor's favor. He documented mountains, rivers, and villages in over a hundred volumes. Emperor Suzong appointed him governor of Yanzhou, where he lived frugally with sheepskin mats and quilts. He was later promoted to governor of Zhangye with a prestigious reputation. When General Dou Xian stationed troops in Wuwei, Li Xun refused to participate in corrupt gift-giving practices and was dismissed. He was later recruited as a visitor and made captain of the Western Regions. Despite receiving many valuable gifts from foreign envoys and merchants, he refused all of them. People in the Western Regions, Bingzhou, and Liangzhou mourned him. Qiao Xuan was from Suiyang, Liang State. His ancestor Qiao Ren wrote forty-nine chapters of the "Book of Rites." When Governor Zhou Jing visited Liang State, Qiao Xuan accused Chen Xiang Yangchang of crimes and investigated thoroughly despite Yangchang's friendship with General Liang Ji. summary: **Du Gen** (courtesy name Bojian) was from Dingling County, Yingchuan. His father Du An was known for his integrity, entering Imperial College at thirteen and gaining fame as "Qitong." summary: **Luan Ba** (courtesy name Shuyuan) was from Huang County, Wei County, and practiced Taoism. During Emperor Shun's reign, he served as a eunuch in Yeting against his wishes. He established marriage and funeral rites, built schools, and promoted officials based on ability. After seven years, he resigned due to illness. He later became governor of Yuzhang, where he used Taoist skills to destroy demonic sacrifices and eliminate monsters. When Emperor Shun died, Luan Ba remonstrated against destroying small tombs near the imperial mausoleum. Empress Dowager Liang interrogated him, convicted him, and sent him home. Over twenty years later, Emperor Ling ascended, and Luan Ba was recruited as Yilang. When Chen Fan and Dou Wu were killed, Luan Ba was relegated to Yongchang Prefect. He wrote an extreme remonstrance about their unjust case, and the emperor ordered his arrest. Luan Ba committed suicide.

We should think of a strategy of gradual elimination, not hasty and extravagant hopes.
Han Zhuo argued repeatedly with Ying Shao.
So the imperial court ordered all officials to gather in the court hall, and they all agreed with Ying Shao's view.
In the third year, Ying Shao was promoted to a high rank and promoted again. In the sixth year, he became the prefect of Taishan.
In the second year of Chuping, 300,000 people including Huangjin entered the county.
Ying Shaojiu led the civil and military forces to fight against the thieves continuously, beheading thousands of people, and captured more than 10,000 old and weak people, carrying 2,000 taels of baggage. The thieves all retreated, and the county was at peace.
In the first year of Xingping, the former Taiwei Cao Song and his son Cao De entered Taishan from Langfu. Yingshao sent troops to meet him, but they did not arrive. Tao Qian, the shepherd of Xuzhou, resented Cao Song's son Cao Cao for attacking them several times, so he sent Qingqi to pursue Cao Song and his son and kill them in the county.
Ying Shao was afraid that Cao Cao would kill him, so he abandoned the county and went to Jizhou to pastor Yuan Shao.
At first, during the reign of Emperor An, Yin Ci from Hejian and Shi Yu from Yingchuan were both guilty of murder and should be executed. Yin Ci's brother Yin Chu and Shi Yu's mother went to Guan Cao to ask for compensation for their lives, but they died by hanging.
Chen Zhong, the minister, believed that the crime should be given a lighter sentence and suggested that Yin Ci and Shi Yu should be expelled.
Ying Shao later refuted it, saying that according to the canonical punishment, some people could survive.
His opinion said: "Shangshu" says: The order of heaven is polite, and there are five orders and five chapters.
God punishes the guilty, and the five punishments are five uses.
And Sun Qing also said: The foundation of any punishment system is to prohibit violence and evil and punish the worst. All titles, official ranks, rewards and punishments, and punishments are all based on the same kind, so that they should be regarded as true.
If the virtue is not in line with the position, the ability is not in line with the official, the reward is not for the meritorious, and the punishment is not for the guilty, then there is no greater misfortune.
Murder is punishable by death, and those who injure others are sentenced to death. This is a system established by the Hundred Kings, and it is documented and verified by law.
When Emperor Gaozu entered the Pass, he made a three-part agreement, but the death penalty for murder was not reduced.
When there is change, the punishment is severe; when there is chaos, the punishment is light.
"Shu Jing" says: Punishment is sometimes light and sometimes heavy. This is how it is said.
In this Yin period, Shi Yu relieved his private regrets and relied on his troops to endure in peace. The court's grace was lenient, and he was fortunate enough to be imprisoned in winter. But at the beginning, the army was stupid and recklessly threw himself into death.
In the past, it was difficult for Zhao Hu to die in person, but Confucius said: He hanged himself in a ditch, and no one else knew about it.
The father of the Chao family could have killed himself without making mistakes. Ban Gu also said: It is not as good as Zhao Kuo's mother to preserve her clan.
"The Biography" says: The servants and concubines who died due to emotion did not show their bravery and carelessness.
Punishments, threats, and prisons are used to imitate heaven's glory and killing; gentleness, kindness, and kindness are used to imitate heaven's reproduction and growth. Therefore, when the grass dies in the spring, it is a disaster, and when the tree blooms in the autumn, it is a miracle.
Now, killing the innocent Chu and Jun, and rescuing the damned Ci and Yu, this is like a withered flower, isn't it normal?
Chen Zhong didn't know the basis of punishment, but believed in the benevolence of a moment, so he widely quoted the Eight Han Dynasty's tips for survival.
A relative, a virtuous person, a distinguished person, a distinguished guest, a diligent guest, how can it be considered a crime to be inferior or to treat jade as a crime?
If you think that small and large prisons must be based on emotion and original intention, this is a matter of survival, not that you can survive by dying.
If the law is corrupted and the government is corrupted, there will be no regrets.
summary: **Ying Shao** (courtesy name Zhongyuan), studious and well-read, served as a messenger under Emperor Ling. During border conflicts, he argued against recruiting Xianbei soldiers, citing their unreliability and past betrayals. His view prevailed. As prefect of Taishan, he defeated 300,000 Yellow Turban rebels. After failing to protect Cao Song, he fled to Yuan Shao. He wrote extensively on legal matters, compiling works like *Han Yi* and *Customs of Customs*. He refuted legal precedents, arguing that punishment should follow established principles. His writings totaled 136 works, and he interpreted the *Book of Han*. He died in Ye.

translation:
Is it possible to be impartial and impartial?
The generals of the Ming Dynasty have great virtues and high positions, and are unique among ministers. Their words and deeds can move heaven and earth, and their actions can move yin and yang. If they can be paid attention to and examined carefully, they will surely be blessed by the East China Sea. If you are harmonious and responsive, the world will be very lucky.
Liang Shang thought that Huo Chen was very talented and intellectual, so he immediately submitted a petition to pardon Song Guang's crime. From then on, Huo Chen's reputation became very prominent.
Huo Xu served as an official there, was promoted to Xiaolian, and later moved to the post of prefect of Jincheng.
Huo Xu has an upright and sincere character, and is able to seduce people from all walks of life with kindness and trust. He is highly respected by the Qiang and Hu people.
When my mother died, I wrote a letter and went home to hold a funeral.
After the mourning clothes were finished, he was summoned for public service, became the prime minister of Beihai, and entered the court as a minister.
At this time, the general Liang Ji and his relatives had exclusive power, and no one from the minister level dared to violate it.
Huo Xu and Shangshu ordered Yin Xun to report the matter several times, and they confessed their faults in person when they met.
After Liang Ji was killed, Emperor Huan commended him for his loyalty and granted him the title of Tinghou of Yedu.
He resolutely resigned and did not agree.
Later, he was promoted to Henan Yin, moved to Sili Xiaowei, and was transferred to Shaofu and Tingwei. Died in official position.
His son Huo Jun became the governor of Anding.
◆Yan Yan's biography, whose courtesy name is Ji Ping, is from Chen Liuwai Huang.
He comes from a poor family, is very studious, and can teach apprentices well.
His temperament is simple and sincere, and he seldom talks.
The county magistrate Longxi Niu Shu was a good scholar and knew people, so he politely asked Yuan Yan to be the court official, Fan Dan to be the meritorious official, and Puyang Qian to be the chief bookkeeper. They often talked together.
Later, Shi Zhao was ordered to use him as a village miser, and benevolent government and education became popular. People only heard of the miser's name and did not know who the county was.
After two years in office, the state government politely invited me, but I didn't go.
When Emperor Huan recruited doctors, Taiwei Yang Bing and others promoted him to be virtuous and upright, and Yuan Yan was promoted to the rank of Attendant.
The emperor swam to Linyuan and asked Yuanyan calmly: What kind of monarch am I?
He replied: Your Majesty is the Lord of Hanzhong.
Emperor asked: How?
Correspondence: Shangshu ordered Chen Fan to handle matters successfully, and the minister Huangmen intervened in the government affairs to prevent chaos. Therefore, he knew that your majesty can be kind to others, and he can also be wrong with others.
The emperor said: In the past, Zhu Yun's admonition to the emperor caused the court to break down the railings, but now the servants call me "disobedient" and are respectfully heard in the court.
So he worshiped Yuanyan as a general of the rank and file of the five sense organs, then a lieutenant of Changshui, then a prefect of Wei County, and was conscripted into the rank of Dahonglu.
The emperor often treated Confucian scholars with special banquets.
At that time, Taishi Ling came forward to persuade the guest star to pass through the emperor's throne, and the emperor asked Yan secretly.
Yuan Yan then wrote a letter saying: I have heard that the Son of Heaven is supreme, so God regards him as his son. He is above the subjects and his prestige is more important than anything in the world.
summary: **Huo Chen** (courtesy name Shuzhi), from Ye, Wei County, was a young scholar. When his uncle Song Guang was falsely accused and imprisoned, fifteen-year-old Huo Chen wrote to General Liang Shang, arguing for leniency based on the *Spring and Autumn Annals* principle of judging intent. Liang Shang pardoned Song Guang, and Huo Chen became famous. He served as prefect of Jincheng, respected by the Qiang and Hu. After his mother's death, he resigned for mourning. He later served as prime minister of Beihai and minister, courageously opposing Liang Ji's power. After Liang Ji's death, Emperor Huan honored him. He died in office. **Yuan Yan** (courtesy name Jiping), from Chenliu, was poor but studious. He served as a village official, known for benevolent governance. When Emperor Huan asked what kind of ruler he was, Yuan Yan replied he was a "Lord of Hanzhong," explaining that while Chen Fan handled affairs well, eunuchs interfered. The emperor appointed him to various positions. Yuan Yan warned against favoring unworthy associates, citing historical disasters from such practices. He urged the emperor to distance himself from flatterers and eunuchs. He later retired due to illness and died.

translation:
The Empress Dowager was angry and quickly summoned Zhang Zhong as the Sili Xiaowei to attack with power.
After Xu Chu arrived in the state, he reported the case to Zhang Zhong and Zang Yu 100 million, and sent Champion County Supervisor to Da Si Nong to expose the matter.
He also reported to the governors of the five counties and the subordinate counties that there were corrupt thieves, and they were all brought to justice.
In the first year of Zhongping, he and Zhonglang general Zhu Jun attacked the Yellow Turban bandits in Wan County and defeated them.
Zhang Zhong hated Xu Chu and fabricated unfounded crimes with other eunuchs. Xu Chu was recalled because of the crime.
Because he succeeded in defeating the thief, he was exempted from official duties and returned home.
Later, he was recruited again and moved to Runan to be the governor, and then to be the prime minister of the East China Sea. The place where he lived was very popular.
Emperor Xian moved the capital to Xuchang, and Xu Chu was recruited as a court lieutenant to serve in the capital. However, he was kidnapped by Yuan Shu on the way and was granted the title of Grand Duke.
Xu Chu sighed and said, "What kind of people are Gong Sheng and Bao Xuan?"
If you defend it, you will die!
Yuan Shu did not dare to force him.
After Yuan Shu died and the army was defeated, Xu Chu obtained the imperial seal stolen by Yuan. When he arrived in Xuchang, he handed it over to the emperor and gave it to the seals and ribbons of Runan and Donghai counties.
Situ Zhao Wen said to Xu Chu: "You were in great danger, did you still keep this?"
Xu Chu said: In the past, when Su Wu was trapped by the Xiongnu, he did not lose the seven-foot seal, so how about this square-inch seal?
Later, he was worshiped as Taichang, and he was sent to worship Cao Cao as the prime minister.
Cao Cao gave the opportunity to Xu Chu, but Chu did not dare to accept the offer.
Died in official position.
summary: **Xu Chu** (courtesy name Mengyu), from Guangling, was learned and served as governor of Jingzhou. He prosecuted corrupt officials, including Zhang Zhong, despite pressure from the Empress Dowager. He defeated Yellow Turban rebels but was falsely accused by eunuchs and dismissed. He later served as prime minister of Donghai. When Emperor Xian moved the capital, Xu Chu was kidnapped by Yuan Shu but refused to serve him. After Yuan Shu's defeat, Xu Chu recovered the imperial seal and returned it. He served as Taichang and died in office.

translation:
◆The biography of Yang Zhen, named Boqi, was from Hongnong Huayin. Yang happy, the eighth generation ancestor, was granted the title of Marquis of Chiquan due to his merit during the reign of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
His father, Yang Bao, studied Ouyang Shangshu. During the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, he did not care about worldly affairs and taught in seclusion.
In the second year of residence, he was drafted together with Gong Sheng, Gong She and Jiang Xu. However, he refused and ran away without knowing where he was.
Emperor Guangwu admired his integrity very much.
During the Jianwu period, he was specially recruited on the bus, but he died at home because he was old and sick.
Yang Zhen loved learning when he was young. He studied "Ouyang Shangshu" from Taichang Huanyu. He was proficient in classics, read a lot of books, and devoted himself to research.
At that time, Confucian scholars said: Confucius Yang Boqi in Kansai.
He lives in Hucheng and has not accepted invitations from prefectures and counties for decades. Many people said that he was old and should go out to become an official. Yang Zhen's determination not to be an official became even more determined.
Later, a crested sparrow took three fishes and flew in front of the lecture hall. The lecturer held the fish and said: Snakes are the symbol of Doctor Qing's clothes.
Three means three stations, and Mr. will be promoted from now on.
He became a state and county official only when he was fifty years old.
General Deng Zhi heard that Yang Zhen was a talented person and promoted him to Maocai. He was promoted four times to the governor of Jingzhou and the governor of Donglai.
When he went to the county and passed through Changyi, Wang Mi, the most talented person in Jingzhou whom he had recommended in the past, was serving as the county magistrate of Changyi. He went to see Yang Zhen and gave him ten pounds of gold in the evening.
Yang Zhen said: Old friends know you, why don’t you know old friends?
Wang Mi said: No one knows at night.
Yang Zhen said: God knows, God knows, I know, you know, how can you say no one knows.
Wang Mi left in shame.
Later he became the prefect of Zhuo County.
Be fair and honest, and do not accept personal requests.
His descendants lived a vegetarian diet and lived a simple life. Some of his old friends or elders wanted him to buy property for his descendants. He said: Wouldn't it be nice to let future generations call them the descendants of innocent officials? In the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, he was recruited as a servant and promoted to Taichang.
Most of the previous doctorate elections were not worthy of their name. Yang Zhen recommended Chen Liu, Yang Lun and other famous scholars who were proficient in Confucian classics to teach their studies, which was praised by Confucian scholars.
In the first year of Yongning, he replaced Liu Kai as Situ.
The following year, Empress Dowager Deng passed away, and some of the concubines that Emperor An liked became arrogant.
Emperor An's nanny, Wang Sheng, was responsible for raising Emperor An. She relied on the emperor's favor and was lawless. Wang Sheng's daughter Bo Rong went in and out of the palace, taking bribes and perverting the law.
Yang Zhen went to Shu.
Said: I heard that politics relies on talents, and those pests must be removed to govern the country.
Therefore, in the era of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, when outstanding talents were in power, the four bad guys Hundun, Qiongqi, Tao, and Taotie were all exiled to remote places. Everyone was convinced and the country was at peace. Morals were depraved, and the court was filled with despicable and sycophantic people. Wang Sheng came from a humble background and met with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to raise Sheng Gong. Although she had some merit, the reward she received far exceeded her hard work. And she was greedy to no end. Asking for help outside, disturbing the world, harming the court, and bringing discredit on the emperor's face.
summary: Yang Zhen, styled Boqi, was from Hongnong Huayin. His eighth-generation ancestor Yang Hou was granted the title of Marquis of Chiquan under Emperor Gaozu of Han. His father Yang Bao studied Ouyang Shangshu, lived in seclusion during the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping, and refused official appointments, disappearing. Emperor Guangwu admired his integrity but he died at home due to old age and illness. Yang Zhen loved learning, studied Ouyang Shangshu under Taichang Huanyu, and became a renowned scholar, called "Confucius of Kansai." He lived in Hucheng, declining official invitations for decades. At age fifty, he became a state and county official after a crested sparrow brought three fish, interpreted as a sign of promotion. General Deng Zhi recommended him, and he rose to Governor of Jingzhou and Donglai. Passing through Changyi, Wang Mi, a former subordinate, offered him ten pounds of gold at night, saying no one would know. Yang Zhen replied, "Heaven knows, earth knows, I know, you know—how can you say no one knows?" Wang Mi left in shame. As Prefect of Zhuo County, he was honest and refused personal requests, leaving his descendants a legacy of being "descendants of an innocent official." In the fourth year of Yuanchu, he became a servant and Taichang, reforming doctorate elections by recommending worthy scholars. In Yongning's first year, he became Situ. When Empress Dowager Deng died, Emperor An's nurse Wang Sheng and her daughter Bo Rong became corrupt. Yang Zhen memorialized, citing historical examples to warn against women and villains in politics, urging their removal. Emperor An showed the memorial to Wang Sheng, who held a grudge. Bo Rong's arrogance grew; she married Liu Gui, who took a title. Yang Zhen protested this breach of protocol, but the emperor ignored him.

translation:
"Shangshu" says: If you arrogate the sun, the minister has no authority and becomes the Duke of Fuyu.
That is to say: only the king can enjoy special blessings and delicacies. Your Majesty, please carry forward a strong and upright spirit, abandon those arrogant and extravagant people, ignore the source of the evil talk, adhere to the warning of the Emperor, and do not let your majesty and power be left behind for a long time.
Yang Zhen came forward and spoke passionately, and the emperor was already displeased with him, while Fan Feng and others looked sideways and resented him, but because he was a Confucian, they did not dare to harm him.
Soon, a man from Hejian went to the court to write a letter, describing the gains and losses of the government.
The emperor was angry and ordered his arrest and imprisonment, which was deemed as bullying and immorality.
Yang Zhen went to Shu to rescue him again and said: I heard that during the time of Yao and Shun, he was admonishing drums and slandering trees and standing in the court; the masters of sages of Shang and Zhou dynasties complained about villains, but they also checked themselves and encouraged themselves.
This is to open up channels of speech, brainstorm ideas, and make people feel better.
Now that Zhao Teng has been convicted of attacking and slandering, which is different from the crime of murder, I ask the emperor to reduce the crime, save Teng's life, and inspire the people to dare to speak. The emperor ignored him and Zhao Teng was killed. In the spring of the third year, the emperor ascended Mount Tai, and Fan Feng and others took the opportunity to compete for house repairs. Yang Zhen sent Gao Shu to summon the master craftsman Shi Shi to investigate the matter. After obtaining the false edict from Zhao Feng and others, he wrote a memorial and wanted to wait for the emperor to return before delivering it.
When Fan Feng and others heard about it, they were terrified. It happened that Taishi said that Xingbian was rebellious, so he framed Yang Zhen together and said: Since Zhao Teng's death, Yang Zhen has been deeply resentful. And he held a grudge against Deng Zhi's old subordinates.
When the emperor returned, he waited in Taixue for an auspicious day to enter the palace. In the evening, he sent an envoy with an order to collect Taiwei Yang Zhen's seal and ribbon. Yang Zhen then closed the door to exclude guests.
Fan Feng and others still hated him, so they asked General Geng Bao to report that Minister Yang Zhen refused to plead guilty and was resentful, and ordered him to be sent back to his hometown.
Yang Zhen walked to Jiyang Pavilion in the west of the city and said generously to his son and student: Death is inevitable for a person.
I am favored and occupy the position, but I hate the traitorous ministers who are cunning but cannot be punished, and the evil mistresses who are causing chaos but cannot be restrained. How can I show my face to the world?
On the day of death, a coffin of mixed wood is used, and the body is only covered with a sheet. There is no burial place or a shrine.
So he took poison and died at the age of seventy.
In response to the orders of Fan Feng and others, the prefect of Hongnong moved to Liang and sent officials to stay at Yang Zhen's funeral in Shaanxi County. They exposed the coffin beside the road and ordered Yang Zhen's disciples to post and write letters on their behalf. Everyone on the road shed tears for it.
When Emperor Shun was over, Fan Feng, Zhou Guang and others were put to death. Yang Zhen was a student of Yu Fang, and Chen Yi went to the court to complain about Yang Zhen.
summary: In Yanguang's second year, Yang Zhen became Taiwei. He refused to recommend Li Gui's brother at Geng Bao's request and rejected Yan Xian's recommendation of relatives, causing resentment. When an edict ordered building a house for the queen mother, Yang Zhen criticized the extravagance during disasters and border unrest, but Fan Feng and others continued unchecked. After an earthquake, Yang Zhen attributed it to excessive yin from corrupt officials, urging the emperor to abandon the arrogant. The emperor was displeased, and Fan Feng resented him but dared not harm him due to his reputation. When Zhao Teng was arrested for criticizing the government, Yang Zhen pleaded for leniency, but the emperor ignored him, and Zhao Teng was killed. In the third year, Fan Feng framed Yang Zhen for resentment after Zhao Teng's death. The emperor stripped Yang Zhen of his position and ordered him home. At Jiyang Pavilion, Yang Zhen declared he could not face the world with traitors unpunished, took poison, and died at seventy. His coffin was exposed by the roadside. After Emperor Shun ascended, Fan Feng was executed. Yang Zhen's students petitioned, and the emperor posthumously honored him, granting titles and money, and buried him with ceremony. A large bird mourned at his funeral, and a stone bird was erected in his memory. His son Yang Mu became Prime Minister of Fubo.

translation:
◆Huan Rong's biography, Huan Rong's courtesy name is Chunqing, and he was a native of Longkang, Pei County.
When he was young, he studied "Ouyang Shangshu" in Chang'an, with Jiujiang Zhu Pu as his teacher. His family was poor and he often relied on servants to support himself. He was energetic and tireless. He did not go home to visit for fifteen years and did not return until Wang Mang usurped the throne.
When his teacher Zhu Pu passed away, Huan Rong went to Jiujiang to attend the funeral. He carried the soil to build his teacher's grave, so he stayed to teach and had hundreds of disciples.
Wang Mang failed and the world was in chaos. Huan Rong took the scriptures and fled into the valley with his students. Although he was often hungry, he continued to lecture on scriptures and treatises. Later, he taught in the Jianghuai area.
In the 19th year of Jianwu's reign, when Huan Rong was over sixty years old, he was awarded the post of Grand Situ.
At that time, Xianzong had just been established as the crown prince, and he chose to seek Ming scriptures. He promoted Huan Rong's student Yuzhang Hetang to be the general of Huben Zhonglang, and taught the prince in the Book of Documents.
Shizu calmly asked He Tang who his master was, and He Tang replied: Huan Rong of Pei State.
The emperor immediately summoned Huan Rong and ordered him to explain "Shang Shu". He thought it was very good.
He worshiped Huan Rong as Yilang, gave him one hundred thousand yuan, and allowed him to enter the palace and teach the prince.
At every court meeting, Huan Rong was often asked to explain the scriptures in front of the ministers.
The emperor praised: It's too late to get Mr.
It happened that Dr. Ouyang was vacant, and the emperor wanted to use Rong.
Rong kowtowed and said in resignation: "I am not as good at Confucian classics as my fellow disciples Peng Hong and Yangzhou engaged in Gaohong."
The emperor said: OK, go ahead, you can do the job.
So he worshiped Huan Rong as a doctor, and recommended Peng Hong and Gao Hong as doctors.
The emperor drove to the university, and just as the doctors were discussing issues, Huan Rong was dressed in Confucian clothes. He was gentle and respectful, broad and erudite. He argued clearly about the classics and the meaning of the scriptures. He always showed courtesy and submission, and did not use words to win over others. None of the Confucian scholars could compare with him, so the emperor specially rewarded him.
The emperor also ordered all the students to play the chime, which lasted all day.
Later, when Huan Rong entered the court, the emperor gave him a strange fruit. The recipients all took it into their arms. Huan Rong raised his hand and held the fruit in his hands to thank him.
The emperor smiled and pointed at him and said, "This man is really a Confucian scholar!"
From then on, he became more respected and was often asked to stay in the palace of the Crown Prince.
Five years later, Huan Rong recommended his disciple Hu Xian from Jiujiang to serve as a lecturer. He just listened and went to the palace once every morning.
Huan Rong was once ill. The prince sent his master to inquire about his illness in the morning and evening. He gave him delicacies, curtains, slaves, etc., and said: "If there is any problem, don't worry about the family."
Later, he recovered from his illness and went to the palace to give lectures.
In the twenty-eighth year, there was a meeting of hundreds of officials in the DPRK, and the emperor asked who could be the prince's master? The ministers observed the idea and all said that the prince's uncle could hold Jinwu's original deerhou Yinshi.
Doctor Zhang Yi said seriously: "Your Majesty, when you appoint a prince, is it for the Yin clan or for the world?"
If it is the Yin family, then Yinhou can do it; if it is the world, then the talents of the world can be used.
The emperor thought it was a good statement and said: I want to set up the Taifu to assist the prince.
Now the doctor can't help me, let alone the prince?
So he worshiped Zhang Yi as the crown prince and tutor, and Huan Rong as the young tutor, and gave him carriages and horses.
Huanrong gathered all the students, displayed the chariots and horses, seals and ribbons and said: "Today I am given a gift from the emperor. This is the power of archaeological records. Can't you encourage me?"
Huan Rong thought that the prince's study of the Confucian classics had been completed, so he thanked him and said: "I am fortunate enough to have been able to lecture on the Confucian classics for several years. However, my knowledge is shallow and short-lived, and it cannot be of great benefit."
Now the crown prince relies on his intelligence and aptitude for understanding the classics and understanding ancient and modern times. No other prince can be as knowledgeable as this.
summary: Huan Rong, courtesy name Chunqing, was a native of Longkang, Pei County. He studied the "Ouyang Shangshu" under Zhu Pu in Chang'an, supporting himself through servant labor. He did not return home for fifteen years, only returning after Wang Mang's usurpation. After Zhu Pu's death, Huan Rong built his grave and stayed to teach, amassing hundreds of disciples. During the chaos following Wang Mang's fall, he fled into the valleys with his students, continuing to lecture despite hunger. Later, he taught in the Jianghuai region. In the 19th year of Jianwu, over sixty, Huan Rong was appointed Grand Situ. When Xianzong became crown prince, Huan Rong's student He Tang was chosen to teach him the "Book of Documents." The emperor summoned Huan Rong, was impressed by his explanation of "Shang Shu," and appointed him Yilang, allowing him to teach the prince. Huan Rong declined a promotion to Dr. Ouyang, recommending his disciples Peng Hong and Gao Hong instead. He was later made a doctor. The emperor praised his gentle, erudite manner and rewarded him. Huan Rong served as the prince's young tutor, and after the prince's studies were complete, he requested retirement but was persuaded to stay. He was later appointed Taichang. When Xianzong ascended the throne, Huan Rong was honored as a master of etiquette. He repeatedly requested retirement due to old age, receiving additional rewards each time. The emperor visited him, showing great respect. Huan Rong died after a long illness, and the emperor personally attended his funeral and granted him a tomb.
