translation:
His father, Ding Linlin, whose courtesy name was Youchun, served as the Yingyang Wei in the last years of Wang Mang's life.
Shizu occupied Yingyang, but Yingyang city could not be defended. Ding Linlin persuaded the county magistrate and surrendered with him. The ancestors were overjoyed and rewarded them greatly. He used Ding Jinlin to lead the soldiers to cross the river first, send a message to the prefecture and the country, attack the camp and seize the territory, and captured 21 counties in Henan, Chenliu and Sichuan.
In the first year of Jianwu, Ding Linlin was worshiped as the governor of Henan.
When it came time to award the meritorious officials, the emperor asked everyone to do what they wanted. All the generals occupied Fengyi Mei County, but Ding Linlin was the only one willing to grant the title to his hometown.
Someone said to Ding Jinlin: Everyone wants to occupy the county, but you only want the hometown. Why is this?
Ding Jinlin said: In the past, Sun Shuao told his son that when he was granted a title, he must seek a barren land. Now that I can do a small job, it will be great to get a rural pavilion.
The emperor obeyed and named him Marquis of Xin'an Township, Dingling, with a settlement of 5,000 households. Later, he was renamed Marquis of Lingyang.
When Ding Hongnian was 13 years old, he studied "Ouyang Shangshu" from Huan Rong. In three years, he understood the chapters and sentences, could debate and speak for everyone, so he determined to further his studies, put on civilian clothes, carried his luggage, and traveled thousands of miles to study.
At first, Ding Jinlin followed Shizu in the expedition, and Ding Hong lived with his younger brother Ding Sheng. They loved Ding Sheng when he was young and lived a poor life together.
After Ding Jinlin's death, Ding Hong was granted the hereditary title and wrote a letter to transfer the country to Ding Sheng, but received no reply.
His father had been buried, so he hung mourning clothes in the tomb and slipped away, leaving a message to Ding Sheng: "Hong was greedy for scriptures. He ignored his kindness and righteousness. He studied with his teacher when he was young. He did not support his parents during his life. He could not fulfill his filial piety until his death. The ancestors of the emperor and heaven did not bless and help him. He was seriously ill and could not bear the soil."
The last time I wrote a letter stating my illness, I was willing to resign my title to my younger brother, but the memorial was shelved without a reply, and the time was approaching for me to be granted a title.
I would like to give up the title and seek good doctors abroad.
If the disease cannot be cured, forget about dying in a ravine.
Ding Hong initially became a student with Huan Rong, a colleague of Bao Jun from Jiujiang, and the two had a close friendship. Later, Ding Hong escaped from the throne and met Bao Jun in the East China Sea. Ding Hong pretended not to know Bao Jun.
Bao Jun took Ding Hong's arm and scolded him: "In the past, Boyi and Wu Jizha were in troubled times, so they had to express their ambition to surrender the country."
The great righteousness of "Spring and Autumn" is not to waste the king's affairs because of family affairs. Now you are using your brother's affair to cut off your father's immortal inheritance. Can you say it is smart?
Ding Hong was very moved and sighed in tears, so he returned to his country and taught apprentices.
Bao Jun also wrote a letter saying that Ding Hong was a good scholar and practiced the classics, and Xianzong appreciated him very much.
In the 10th year of Yongping, the emperor issued an edict to recruit talents. Ding Hong was summoned when he arrived and told the story of "The Order of Marquis Wen". The emperor bestowed royal robes and ribbons, food and carriage, and received the same courtesy as a doctor.
summary: Ding Hong, courtesy name Xiaogong, was a native of Dingling, Yingchuan. His father, Ding Lin, surrendered Yingyang to Shizu and was rewarded, later becoming Governor of Henan. Ding Lin chose to be enfeoffed in his hometown, becoming Marquis of Xin'an Township. Ding Hong studied "Ouyang Shangshu" under Huan Rong at thirteen, mastering it in three years. After his father's death, he attempted to cede his title to his younger brother Ding Sheng but fled when his request was ignored. His friend Bao Jun persuaded him to return, citing the importance of upholding his father's legacy. Ding Hong returned, taught disciples, and was later summoned by Emperor Xianzong, becoming a servant and then Captain of Shesheng. He participated in the White Tiger Temple discussions on the Five Classics, where his eloquence was praised. He was promoted to Shaofu and later Taichang. During Empress Dowager Dou's regency, Ding Hong submitted a memorial warning against the Dou family's power, citing solar eclipses as divine warnings. His advice led to the confiscation of Dou Xian's seal and the suicides of Dou Xian and his brothers. Ding Hong also reformed the system for recommending filial and incorrupt candidates. He died in the sixth year of Yongyuan.

translation:
◆The Legend of Huan Tan
Huan Tan, whose courtesy name is Junshan, was born in Xiangxian County, Peiguo County.
His father was Tai Leling when he became emperor.
Huan Tan was appointed as a minister due to his father's relationship, so he loved music and was good at drums and harp.
He is very knowledgeable, has read all the Five Classics, and can explain the great meanings of ancient books. Distinguish sentences without leaving chapters.
He wrote good articles, and especially loved ancient learning. He repeatedly analyzed difficult and different meanings through debates between Liu Xin and Yang Xiong. He also loved miscellaneous dramas. He was a simple man and did not put on official airs. He liked to slander secular Confucian scholars, so he was often ostracized and attacked.
During the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, his status was only that of a man.
Queen Fu's father, Fu Yan, the Marquis of Kongxiang, thought highly of Huan Tan.
At that time, Gao'an Hou Dong Xian was favored by the emperor, and his sister was named Zhaoyi. The emperor became increasingly alienated from Empress Fu, and Fu Yan was silently dissatisfied.
Huan Tan said to Fu Yan: In the past, Emperor Wu wanted to appoint Wei Zifu, and secretly collected Empress Chen's faults. Empress Chen was finally deposed, and Wei Zifu was actually appointed.
Now Dong Xian is favored and his sister is especially favored. There may be another change of "Wei Zihu". Don't you worry?
Fu Yan was alarmed and said: Yes, what should we do?
Huan Tan said: Punishment cannot be imposed on innocent people, and evil spirits cannot defeat righteous people in vain.
A scholar serves his master with his intelligence, and a woman seeks his master with a charming way.
The queen is young and has not experienced many hardships. There are people who are driving witch doctors inside, seeking magic skills outside, and practicing evil ways. We must be on guard against these.
Moreover, because the king is respected as the father of the queen, he communicates with the guests. The guests will definitely use this to enhance their power, which will attract people's ridicule.
Why don't you thank the guests and send the disciples away? You must be humble and cautious. This is the way to cultivate yourself and your family to avoid disaster.
Fu Yan said: OK.
So he dismissed the guests and went to the palace to tell the queen, just as Huan Tan said.
Later, Dong Xian indeed hinted to the imperial physician Ling Zhenqin to collect the Fu family's crimes and arrest Fu Xi, Empress Fu's younger brother. During the interrogation, no evidence of guilt was found, and the case was eliminated, so the Fu family was finally saved during the reign of Emperor Ai.
Later, Dong Xian became the Grand Sima. Hearing about Huan Tan's reputation, he wanted to make friends with him.
Huan Tan first wrote to Dong Xian, saying that Dong Xian could not use the method of assisting the country and protecting himself, so Huan Tan would not have any contact with him.
When Wang Mang was regent and usurped Emperor Ping, the intellectuals at that time all praised Wang Mang. Or they described auspicious signs to create public opinion to please Wang Mang, but Huan Tan kept his innocence and remained silent.
During the reign of Wang Mang, he was the official in charge of music. After Gengshili, he became the official of Taizhong.
When Shizu ascended the throne, he was summoned to wait for the imperial edict. Huan Tan wrote a letter and said something that was inconsistent with Shizu's will, so he did not adopt it.
Later, Song Hong, the Grand Sikong, recommended Huan Tan and paid homage to Yilang, so he wrote a letter stating the matters that should be paid attention to in political affairs at that time, saying: I heard that the failure of a country depends on political affairs; and the gains and losses of political affairs depend on whether the assistants are recruited.
summary: Huan Tan, courtesy name Junshan, was from Xiangxian County, Peiguo. He was appointed as a minister through his father's connections. He was knowledgeable in the Five Classics, wrote excellent essays, and favored ancient learning. He debated with Liu Xin and Yang Xiong, and enjoyed criticizing secular Confucian scholars, which led to his ostracism. During the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, his status remained low. Fu Yan, Marquis of Kongxiang, valued Huan Tan. When Emperor Ai favored Dong Xian and his sister Zhaoyi over Empress Fu, Huan Tan warned Fu Yan of potential danger, advising him to dismiss guests and remain humble. Fu Yan followed this advice, and when Dong Xian later attempted to incriminate the Fu family, no evidence was found, saving them. Dong Xian later sought Huan Tan's friendship, but Huan Tan refused, criticizing Dong Xian's inability to protect himself through proper governance. During Wang Mang's usurpation, Huan Tan remained silent while others praised Wang Mang. After Emperor Guangwu (Shizu) ascended, Huan Tan served as a郎官. He submitted memorials on governance, emphasizing the importance of wise advisors, harmony between ruler and ministers, and adapting policies to circumstances. He criticized harsh laws, private revenge killings, usury by merchants, and inconsistent legal punishments. He advocated for unified laws, agricultural development, and suppressing commerce. His proposals were not accepted.

translation:
I, Huan Tan, have observed your Majesty's use of troops, and found that for those who surrendered, there were no heavy rewards to induce kindness, and some even plundered their property. Therefore, the generals, large and small, were suspicious and colluded with each other, and could not solve the problem after many years.
The ancients said: Everyone in the world knows that taking is taking, but they don’t know that giving is also taking.
If Your Majesty can be more considerate than the official title but more important than the reward, and share it with the soldiers, then who will be unable to recruit, and who will not be able to explain it? Where does it point and where does it not open? Conquer the enemy, which enemy cannot be conquered!
In this way, narrowness can be used as broadness, delay can be used as speed, death can be reborn, and loss can be gained again.
The emperor was even more unhappy after reading the memorial.
Later, there was an edict to convene ministers to discuss the location of the spiritual platform. The emperor said to Huan Tan: I want to use prophecies to decide, how about it?
Huan Tan was silent for a long time and said: I don't read prophecies.
The emperor asked the reason, and Huan Tan once again argued that the prophecy was grotesque and unreasonable.
The emperor was furious and said: "Huan Tan is not a saint, so he should be taken down and beheaded."
Huan Tan kowtowed and the bleeding lasted for a long time.
Transferred to Liu'an County Cheng. Huan Tan was in a bad mood and died of illness on the road. He was over seventy years old.
At first, Huan Tan wrote twenty-nine articles on how to deal with the current situation, named it "New Treatise", and presented it to the imperial court, which was praised by his ancestors.
One chapter of "Qin Dao" was not completed, so Suzong ordered Ban Gu to continue completing it.
He wrote a total of twenty-six poems, admonitions, books and memorials.
During the Yuan Dynasty, Suzong went on a hunting tour to the east. When he arrived at Pei, he sent envoys to pay homage to Huan Tan's tomb, which made the village proud.
◆Feng Yan's biography: Feng Yan, courtesy name Jingtong, was from Duling, Jingzhao.
The ancestor Feng Yewang was Dahonglu during the Yuan Dynasty.
Feng Yan was a genius when he was young. He was able to recite "Poetry" at the age of nine. By the time he was twenty, he was well versed in many books.
During Wang Mang's reign, many people recommended him to be an official, but Feng Yan declined.
At this time, the army was rising, and Wang Mang sent Gengshi General Lian Dan to attack Shandong.
Lian Dan recruited Feng Yanshou as an official and went to Dingtao with him.
Wang Mang issued an edict to Lian Dan, saying: "The food in the warehouse has been exhausted, and the money in the treasury is empty. It's time to get angry and fight."
A general has a heavy responsibility for his country, and he cannot repay his kindness without sacrificing his life in the wilderness.
Lian Dan was frightened and summoned Feng Yan at night to read him the edict.
Feng Yan then said to Lian Dan: I heard that those who follow the right path are the greatest; those who go against the right path but can succeed, this should be taken seriously when weighing.
Therefore, if you hope to achieve success, don't ask about the reasons; if the principles are consistent with the general principles, don't stick to the details.
In the past, Feng Chou's father asked the Marquis of Qi to pretend to be a charioteer and go to Huaquan to drink, thus saving the Marquis of Qi from disaster, and was praised by the princes. Zheng Zhong's Ji Zhong succumbed to the intimidation of the Song Dynasty and made the prince Hu finally return to his throne, which was praised in the "Spring and Autumn Annals".
summary: The emperor believed in prophecies. Huan Tan submitted another memorial denouncing prophecies as absurd, urging the emperor to follow the Five Classics instead. He also criticized inadequate rewards for surrendered rebels, which prolonged military campaigns. The emperor became displeased. When later asked about using prophecies to decide the location of the Lingtai, Huan Tan refused, arguing prophecies were irrational. The emperor ordered his execution, but Huan Tan kowtowed until bleeding and was instead demoted to Liu'an County Magistrate. He died en route, over seventy years old. He wrote the "New Treatise" in twenty-nine chapters and other works. Feng Yan, courtesy name Jingtong, was from Duling, Jingzhao. A prodigy, he could recite the "Book of Songs" at nine and was well-read by twenty. During Wang Mang's reign, he declined official recommendations. He served under Lian Dan, advising him to garrison troops and wait for opportunities rather than fight recklessly. Lian Dan refused and died in battle. Feng Yan later served Bao Yong, advising him to prepare defenses in Bingzhou, cultivate virtue, and select talented officers.

translation:
Bao Yong sent his younger brother Bao Sheng and son-in-law Zhang Shu to lure him back to Niecheng County. Zhang Shu's family was in Shangdang, and his family was imprisoned in Tianyi.
He also wrote a letter to persuade Bao Yong to surrender, but Bao Yong never responded. From then on, Bao Yong and Tianyi had a grudge.
Tianyi, named Boyu, was born in Feng Yi, and later served as the prefect of Yuyang.
Bao Yong and Feng Yan knew for sure that Gengshi was dead, so they jointly stopped their troops and surrendered to Hanoi without any hats.
The emperor complained that Feng Yan was unwilling to surrender. Bao Yong was able to atone for his sins by performing meritorious service, so he was appointed, while Feng Yan was dismissed.
Bao Yong said to Feng Yan: In the past, Emperor Gaozu pardoned Ji Bu's sins and killed Ding Gu, who had contributed to him.
Now that I have met the Ming Lord, what else do I have to worry about?
Feng Yan said: I remember "Warring States Policy" tells about a man who teased his neighbor's wife and teased his eldest wife. The eldest wife cursed him and teased his younger wife, and the younger wife agreed. Later, when his neighbor died, he married his eldest wife.
Someone asked him: Didn’t the eldest wife scold you?
One person said: When I'm at someone else's house, I want her to agree to my flirting, but when I'm at my house, I want her to scold the person who teases and seduces her.
Destiny is hard to know, but the way of humanity is easy to follow. Are ministers who keep the way still afraid of death?
Soon, the emperor appointed Feng Yan as the Quyang Order, killed the big thief Guo Sheng and others, and surrendered more than 5,000 of them. They were awarded officials and titles based on merit. However, they were slandered and slandered, so the rewards were not implemented.
There was a solar eclipse in the sixth year of Jianwu, and Feng Yan wrote a petition asking for eight things: first, to show literary virtue, second, to praise military heroes, third, to repair old merits, fourth, to recruit heroes, fifth, to clarify likes and dislikes, sixth, to simplify laws, seventh, to improve rank and salary, and eighth, to care for borders.
After the book was written, Emperor Guangwu prepared to summon him.
At first, when Feng Yan was the magistrate of Langmeng County, he punished Linghu Luo for his crimes. At this time, Linghu Luo became the chief minister of Sikong, and said to Shangshu Ling Wang Hu and Shangshu Zhou Shengfeng: Feng Yan asked for help because he wanted to slander you.
Wang Hu and others were afraid, so they united to exclude Feng Yan. Therefore, Feng Yan could not be received by Guangwu.
Later, Weiwei Yinxing and Xinyang Houyin became rich and distinguished because of their relatives, and they deeply respected Feng Yan. Feng Yan made friends with them and was hired by the kings. Soon he became a minister.
Later, Guangwu punished his relatives and guests in Xijing, and most of them were brought to justice. The most serious ones were even put to death and relocated, while the rest were demoted.
Feng Yan was offended by this. He went to prison to plead guilty, but was pardoned by an imperial edict.
Feng Yan then returned to his hometown in the west and closed the door to protect himself. He did not dare to interact with his relatives and old friends again.
summary: After Emperor Guangwu's ascension, Feng Yan wrote to Tian Yi, urging him to remain loyal to the Gengshi regime. Tian Yi responded defiantly, criticizing Bao Yong and Feng Yan for their failures. Feng Yan and Bao Yong eventually surrendered. The emperor initially dismissed Feng Yan for his late surrender, but Bao Yong's intercession led to Feng Yan's appointment as Quyang Magistrate, where he suppressed bandits. Feng Yan later submitted a memorial on eight matters during a solar eclipse. However, former enemies slandered him, preventing imperial audience. He befriended influential relatives but was implicated when the emperor punished their associates. Feng Yan confessed and was pardoned, then returned home, isolating himself from former acquaintances.

translation:
In the last years of Jianwu, Feng Yan Shangshu said to himself: I think of Gaozu's talents and strategies and Chen Ping's wisdom. If I listen to slander, Chen Ping will be alienated. If I listen to praise, Chen Ping will be close to Gaozu.
With Emperor Wen's wisdom and Wei Shang's loyalty, those who are brought to justice will become criminals, and those who are treated with virtue will become heroes.
In his later life, Dong Zhongshu emphasized morality and was jealous of Gongsun Hong; Li Guang fought hard to fight against the Huns, but was rejected by Wei Qing. These are all tragedies for which loyal officials often cried bitterly.
I, Feng Yan, think to myself that I am just a humble minister. I don’t have the recommendation of Wei Wuwu above, the persuasion of Feng Tang below, the talent and learning of Dong Zhongshu, and the momentum of Li Guang. Isn’t it difficult to avoid slander and avoid resentment?
Feng Shen, the ancestor of Chen Feng Yan, was so loyal and unyielding that he actually caused trouble in his private family.
And when the minister Feng Yan encountered disturbances and revolutions, he did not dare to seek the benefits of the times. His servants had no evil plans, and the generals had no plans to plunder.
Wei Wei is Yinxing, respectful and careful, can cultivate himself internally, and avoid suspicion externally, so I dare to associate with him.
Yin Xing knew that I was poor and wanted to leave money to establish my basic livelihood several times.
I think to myself that my talent is of no use to the three friends, and I dare not be in a position where it will harm the three friends, and I resolutely refuse to accept it. In the past, during the Gengshi period, the troops stationed in Taiyuan held the power of goods and property, living in a hurry, and held the position for more than 20 years. However, the property was decreasing year by year, and the days were becoming poorer day by day. There was no savings of cloth and silk at home, and there was no decoration for horses when going out.
Now we are facing the period of Qingming, a time when we are reorganizing ourselves and striving to do good deeds, but resentments are rising and ridicule is flowing across the world.
It is true that it is easy to do good things if you are rich, but it is difficult to do good things if you are poor or lowly.
I am a minister who is alienated from my mother-in-law and has no hope of serving in the imperial court. I am just afraid to confess my sins in order to save myself from my sins.
After the book was submitted, it was still not used due to previous mistakes.
Feng Yan was dissatisfied and retired to write poems. He commented to himself: Feng Zi believed that a person's virtue is neither like the mediocre appearance of jade nor the falling shape of stone.
Storms and clouds arise, dragons and snakes soar together with the Tao, and change with the times. How can they stick to one law?
If you use it, it will become popular; if you abandon it, you will avoid it. There will be no master in advancing or retreating, and it will be impermanent.
Therefore, it is said: The laws and regulations, right and wrong, all follow the customs. Where things go, the laws follow; when things go, the laws violate them.
Always pursue the truth of morality instead of pursuing fame in the world, get rid of small etiquette, and indulge in human affairs.
Cultivate yourself and follow the right path, be at ease and indulge yourself as much as you want.
I used to like excellent strategies, but in this era, strategies cannot be used. I sighed and lamented that I didn't meet them.
summary: In the final years of the Jianwu era, Feng Yan submitted a memorial reflecting on historical figures. He compared Gaozu’s talents and Chen Ping’s wisdom, noting how slander could alienate Chen Ping while praise could draw him closer. He also referenced Emperor Wen’s wisdom and Wei Shang’s loyalty, observing that justice could turn people into criminals while virtue could make them heroes. Feng Yan lamented the tragedies of loyal officials like Dong Zhongshu, who was jealous of Gongsun Hong, and Li Guang, who was rejected by Wei Qing despite his efforts against the Huns. Feng Yan considered himself a humble minister without the recommendations of Wei Wuwu or Feng Tang, nor the talents of Dong Zhongshu or Li Guang, making it difficult to avoid slander and resentment. Feng Yan recounted his ancestor Feng Shen’s loyalty and the troubles it caused. During disturbances, Feng Yan avoided seeking personal gain, and his servants and generals had no evil plans. He associated with Wei Wei Yinxing, who was respectful and cautious, and who offered money to help Feng Yan establish a livelihood, but Feng Yan refused, believing his talents were insufficient. He noted that during the Gengshi period, he held a position for over twenty years but his property decreased, leaving him poor. In the Qingming period, he faced resentment and ridicule, acknowledging that it is easier for the rich to do good than the poor.

translation:
For a long time, he has lived behind a small official and cannot show his arms.
Suppress one's mood and submit to others, one's mood is desolate and the mood is sad.
The families of high-ranking officials and well-paid people do not seek small profits; the ministers of accumulation do not care about the interests of merchants.
What's more, he has been in office for more than 20 years, but his property has become less and less, and his life has become increasingly poor.
This is when a gentleman is in power and follows his own path.
Those who plan current affairs cannot flourish their virtues, and those who seek personal gain cannot achieve their merits. After leaving and returning home, he wandered and sojourned in prefectures and counties. He became more dependent on his work and his family became even poorer. As a result, he suffered from hunger and cold, and even lost his eldest son.
The former general Feng Fengshi was buried in Weiling. After the death of Emperor Ai, he was included in the tomb of Emperor Ai.
So to the east of Xinfeng, above Hongmen, in the middle of Shouan, the terrain is high and spacious, connected to the vastness on all sides, looking to the south of Mount Li, to the north of Jingwei, to the east of Hehua, to the south of Longmen, the road to the Three Jin Dynasties, to the west of Fenggao'an, the earth mountains of the Zhou and Qin Dynasties, the ruins of palaces and temples, with a broad field of vision, and the old capital can be seen, so it was designated as a cemetery.
Retreat and live in seclusion.
Loyal ministers will lament when passing by the old ruins, and filial sons will sigh with sadness when entering the old chamber.
Every time I remember my ancestors, I established great virtues in front of me and passed down my great achievements to future generations. However, I suffer from the disasters of the current situation, the tombs are dirty, the spring and Autumn sacrifices are arranged in disorder, and the arrangement of father south and son north is disordered. At the end of the year, mourning the failure of their achievements, they will go to the fertile and fertile fields to the west to graze, breed and produce, repair filial piety, run the ancestral temple, and conduct sacrifices.
Then close the door to lecture on morality, watch the remarks of Confucius and Laozi, and maybe enjoy the blessings of red pine nuts and Wang Ziqiao. Climb to Longban, climb to Gaogang, wander around the universe, and see beyond the world.
Take a closer look at the landscape of Jiuzhou's mountains and rivers, and trace the ethos of gain and loss in ancient times.
Anyone who sees its end must examine its origin, so we should preserve its people and chant their ways.
Situated in the wilderness of Kyushu, and connected to the Five Mountains, there is a vague artistic conception that transcends the clouds. So I wrote a poem to express my self-reliance, and named its chapter "Xian Zhi". Xian Zhi means to express the bright and weathered feelings and reveal the mysterious thoughts. After Xianzong ascended the throne, many people said that Feng Yanwen was exaggerating, so he was abandoned at home.
Feng Yan married a daughter of Ren's family in the North. He was jealous and did not allow Feng Yan to raise a young wife. His children often fetched water and pounded rice to take care of the housework. When they got old, they expelled her, so she was miserable and impoverished for a while.
However, if you have great ambitions, you will not worry about poverty.
summary: After his memorial was ignored due to past mistakes, Feng Yan retired to write poems. He reflected on virtue, comparing it to jade or stone, and emphasized adapting to changing times. He criticized rigid adherence to laws and customs, advocating for moral truth over worldly fame. He lamented that his strategies were unused and that he remained a minor official for years, unable to display his abilities. His property diminished over twenty years, and he suffered hunger and cold, even losing his eldest son. Feng Yan chose a cemetery east of Xinfeng, on high ground with broad views, and retreated into seclusion. He mourned his ancestors’ virtues and the disorder of their tombs, planning to repair them and conduct sacrifices. He closed his door to lecture on morality, studying Confucius and Laozi, and sought spiritual blessings. He wrote a poem titled "Xian Zhi" to express his feelings, but after Xianzong ascended the throne, he was accused of exaggeration and abandoned. Feng Yan married a jealous woman who prevented him from raising a young wife, leaving him impoverished in old age. Despite this, he maintained his ambitions, refusing to seek high status or wealth. He died poor and old, leaving behind fifty works valued by Suzong. His son was Feng Bao.

translation:
◆Liang Tongchuan, Liang Tong, courtesy name Zhongning, was a native of Anding Wushi.
His ancestor was Liang Yi'er, a doctor of the Jin Dynasty. Liang Tong's grandfather was named Zidu, who moved from Hedong to the north. Zidu's son Liangqiao moved to Maoling with tens of millions of family assets, and returned to Anding in the last years of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping.
Liang Tong had a resolute character and loved the law.
Started to serve as an official in the state and county.
In the second year of Gengshi's reign, he summoned the general Zhonglang and sent him to Hujing Prefecture to be appointed the governor of Jiuquan.
After the failure of the reform, the Red Eyebrow Army entered Chang'an. Liang Tong, Dou Rong and the governors of various counties raised troops to defend their territory. They all discussed how to establish a commander-in-chief.
They began to rank in order, and everyone recommended Liang Tong. Liang Tong firmly declined and said: In the past, Chen Ying refused to be king because his mother was still alive.
Now I have respect for my relatives, but I have little virtue and little ability, so I am really not qualified for the job.
So everyone elected Dou Rong to be the general of Hexi and the governor of Wuwei.
Liang Tong's political views were strict and his prestige reached neighboring counties.
In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, Liang Tong and other envoys sent to the imperial court with Dou Rong's chief minister Liu Jun to pay tribute, hoping to reach the emperor's temporary residence. The emperor issued an edict and conferred the title of General Xuande on Liang Tong.
In the summer of the eighth year, Emperor Guangwu personally conquered Kaixiao. Liang Tong, Dou Rong and others led their soldiers to join Guangwu.
After the defeat of Wei Xiao, Guangwu granted Liang Tong the title of Marquis of Chengyi, and Tong's brother Liang Xun and cousin Liang Teng were also granted the title of Marquis of Guannei. Liang Teng was made the captain of Diannong in Jiuquan, and all of them were sent back to Hexi.
In the twelfth year, Liang Tong, Dou Rong and others came to the capital and went to the court as marquises. They were also granted the title of Gaoshan Marquis, paid homage to the Taizhong doctor, and named their four sons as Lang Lang.
When Liang Tong was in the court, he repeatedly reported things that were beneficial to the country.
He believes that if the law is too light, bad guys will increase, and the punishment should be increased and things should be done in accordance with the old laws.
So Shangshu said: I have seen that Emperors Yuan and Ai gave special punishments lightly and dealt with one hundred and twenty-three things. Those who killed people with their own hands were reduced to one level of death penalty. From then on, the standard was set, so people easily broke the law and officials killed people at will. The ministers heard that the principle of establishing a king should be based on benevolence and righteousness. Only the benevolent can love the people, and the righteous can govern the government. If you love the people, you should eliminate cruelty, and if you regulate politics, you should eliminate rebellion.
Punishment should be moderate and not too light. Therefore, the Five Emperors had methods such as exile, execution, release, and killing, and the Three Kings had methods such as large openings and skin carvings.
Confucius said: A benevolent person must be brave. He also said: The right words for financial management, and the wrong words for banning people are called righteousness.
Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty was ordered by heaven to punish the Qin Dynasty and pacify the world. He made a three-chapter agreement, which is indeed very appropriate.
summary: Liang Tong, courtesy name Zhongning, was from Anding Wushi. His ancestor Liang Yi'er was a Jin Dynasty doctor. His grandfather Zidu moved from Hedong northward, and his son Liangqiao relocated to Maoling with great wealth, returning to Anding during the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping. Liang Tong had a resolute character and loved law. He began his official career in state and county posts. In the second year of Gengshi's reign, he was summoned as General Zhonglang and appointed Governor of Jiuquan. After the reform failed, the Red Eyebrow Army entered Chang'an. Liang Tong, Dou Rong, and other governors raised troops to defend their territory. When they discussed establishing a commander-in-chief, all recommended Liang Tong, but he firmly declined, citing his lack of virtue and ability. Thus, Dou Rong was elected General of Hexi and Governor of Wuwei. Liang Tong's strict political views earned him prestige in neighboring counties. In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, Liang Tong and others sent envoys to the imperial court with Dou Rong's chief minister Liu Jun to pay tribute. The emperor conferred on Liang Tong the title of General Xuande. In the eighth year, Emperor Guangwu personally conquered Kui Xiao, and Liang Tong and Dou Rong led soldiers to join him. After Kui Xiao's defeat, Guangwu granted Liang Tong the title of Marquis of Chengyi, and his brother Liang Xun and cousin Liang Teng were also made marquises. In the twelfth year, Liang Tong and Dou Rong came to the capital as marquises. Liang Tong was granted the title of Gaoshan Marquis, appointed Taizhong大夫, and his four sons were named Lang. While in court, Liang Tong repeatedly reported beneficial matters. He believed the law was too light, increasing crime, and advocated for stricter punishments according to old laws. He submitted a memorial arguing that lenient punishments under Emperors Yuan and Ai had led to lawlessness and increased crime. He cited historical precedents from the Five Emperors, Three Kings, and Han emperors, urging the adoption of stricter measures. However, the matter was referred to the Sangong and Tingwei, who deemed harsh punishments unnecessary and refused to change the old law. Liang Tong wrote again, clarifying he did not seek severe punishment but adherence to old rules. He argued that mitigating punishment had caused rampant theft and rebellion, citing recent outbreaks of banditry. His memorial was sent but not reported. Later, Liang Tong served as Prefect of Jiujiang and was granted the title of Marquis of Lingxiang. He achieved great governance in the county, earning the fear and love of officials and people, and died in office.

The memorial was sent, but he was taken away without reporting.

Later died in official position.
◆In the biography of Liang Ji, Liang Ji's courtesy name is Bozhuo.
His shoulders were hunched like an eagle's wings, and his eyes were upright like a jackal. He looked straight at people with no expression on his face and his speech was slurred.
Learning can only be done by copying and writing and keeping accounts.
He has been a noble royal relative since he was a child, idle and unruly. He is fond of drinking and drinking, and is good at archery, playing chess, five grids, six gambling, playing ball, and playing with money. He also likes to drive hawks and dogs, and race horses and fight cocks. At first, he served as the Minister of Huangmen, and was promoted to the official positions of Shizhong, Huben Zhonglangjiang, Yueqi, Infantry Colonel, and Zhijinwu.
In the first year of Emperor Shun Yonghe's reign, Liang Ji was appointed Yin of Henan. During his tenure, he was brutal and cruel and did many illegal things.
His father, Liang Shang, had a close friend, Lu Fang, the commander of Luoyang, who discussed many of Liang Ji's shortcomings with Liang, and Liang Shang blamed Liang Ji for this.
Liang Ji had a grudge, so he sent someone to assassinate Lu Fang on the road. He was afraid that Liang Shang would find out, so he put the suspicion of assassinating Lu Fang on Lu Fang's enemies. He also asked Lu Fang's younger brother Lu Yu to be the order of Luoyang, asking him to capture the enemies who killed Lu Fang.
As a result, more than 100 members of Lu Fang's enemy's clan, relatives, and guests were killed. When Liang Shang died and was not buried, Emperor Shun appointed Liang Ji as the general and Liang Ji's younger brother, Shizhong Liang Buyi, as the Yin of Henan. When Emperor Shun of the Han Dynasty died, Emperor Chong of the Han Dynasty was only two years old and still in his infancy. The Queen Mother took charge of the court and ordered Liang Ji, Taifu Zhao Jun, and Taiwei Li Gu to participate in Shangshu affairs and take charge of the government.
Although Liang Ji refused to take responsibility, he was even more extravagant and cruel.
Soon, Emperor Chong of the Han Dynasty died again, and Liang Ji welcomed Emperor Zhi.
Emperor Zhi is young but very smart. He knew that Liang Ji was arrogant. When he met with the ministers in court, he looked at Liang Ji and said: This is a domineering general.
summary: Liang Ji, courtesy name Bozhuo, had a hunched back like an eagle's wings and upright eyes like a jackal. He was idle and unruly from childhood, fond of drinking, archery, gambling, and racing. He began as Minister of Huangmen and rose to various military and police posts. In the first year of Emperor Shun's Yonghe reign, he was appointed Yin of Henan, where he was brutal and illegal. His father Liang Shang's friend, Lu Fang, criticized Liang Ji, leading Liang Ji to have Lu Fang assassinated. He then framed Lu Fang's enemies and had Lu Fang's brother capture them, killing over a hundred people. After Liang Shang's death, Emperor Shun appointed Liang Ji as General and his brother Liang Buyi as Yin of Henan. When Emperor Shun died, the Queen Mother ordered Liang Ji, Taifu Zhao Jun, and Taiwei Li Gu to manage government affairs. Liang Ji became more extravagant and cruel. After Emperor Chong died, Liang Ji welcomed Emperor Zhi, who was young and intelligent. When Emperor Zhi called Liang Ji a "domineering general," Liang Ji poisoned him. He then welcomed Emperor Huan and framed Li Gu and Du Qiao.

translation:
Liang Ji was very angry after hearing this, and ordered his cronies to put poison into soup cakes and give them to Emperor Zhi. Emperor Zhi died that day. After the death of Emperor Zhi, Liang Ji ushered in Emperor Huan and framed Li Gu and former Taiwei Du Qiao. Everyone in the country sighed and felt in danger. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of Li Gu".
In the first year of the founding of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Huan of the Han Dynasty granted 13,000 households in Liangji food towns, and increased the number of people recommended by the General's Palace for outstanding candidates and the number of talented people. The number of officials in the General's Palace was twice that of Taiwei, Situ, and Sikong.
Liang Buyi was also granted the title of Marquis of Yingyin, Liang Buyi's younger brother Liang Meng was granted the title of Marquis of Xiping, and Liang Ji's son Liang Yin was granted the title of Marquis of Xiangyi, each with a settlement of 10,000 households.
In the first year of peace, Emperor Huan of the Han Dynasty granted another 10,000 households in Liangji and Hebei provinces, adding to the previous 30,000 households. Zaixuan, a native of Hongnong, had a treacherous and evil nature and wanted to please Liang Ji, so he wrote to the emperor saying that Liang Ji had the meritorious service of Zhou Gong and became king. Now that his son has been enfeoffed, his wife should also be enfeoffed as the king of the city.
Emperor Huan then granted Liang Ji's wife Sun Shou the title of Lord of Xiangcheng. In addition to the tax from Xiangcheng, he also enjoys the tax from Yangzhai County. The annual income is 50 million, and he is given a red seal ribbon, which is equal to the eldest princess.
Sun Shou was very beautiful, and was good at pretending to be demonic. He painted his eyebrows flat and thin, wore pink makeup that looked like tear stains on his cheeks, his bun was on the side, twisted his waist, and his feet seemed unable to support his weight. He put on a clever smile to seduce Liang Ji.
Liang Ji also changed the style of carriages and carriages, creating flat-top curtain carriages, piqus, narrow crowns, folded scarves, body-hugging fans, and foxtail singles. Sun Shouxing was jealous because she was able to subdue Liang Ji. Liang Ji doted on her very much and was also afraid of her. In the past, Liang Ji's father Liang Shang gave the beauty Youtongqi to Emperor Shun of the Han Dynasty.
You Tongqi made a small mistake, so Emperor Shun returned her to Liang Shang. Liang Shang did not dare to keep her and married her off.
Liang Ji sent someone to snatch her back. When Liang Shang passed away, Liang Ji secretly lived with You Tongqi in the west of the city.
Sun Shou found out that Liang Ji was out, so he brought many slaves with him, snatched You Tongqi home, cut off his hair, slashed his face, beat him severely, and wanted to write a letter to the emperor to report the matter.
Liang Ji was very frightened and kowtowed to Sun Shou's mother, asking her not to do this. Sun Shou also gave up because he had no choice but to do so. However, Liang Ji still had an affair with You Tongqi and gave birth to a son named Boyu. He hid him and did not dare to let him out.
Soon, Sun Shou still found out and taught her son Liang Yin to kill Youtongqi's family.
Liang Ji was afraid that Sun Shou would kill Boyu, so he often hid him in the wall.
Liang Ji favored a servant named Qin Gong, who became the Taicang Order and had access to Sun Shou's residence.
When Sun Shou met the Qin Palace, he often sent away the slaves who served her, pretending to have something to discuss, so she had an affair with him.
The Qin Palace favored Liang Ji externally and Sun Shou internally. It was so powerful that the governor and county governor went to see him and bid farewell to him when they were appointed.
Liang Ji listened to Sun Shou's words and dismissed many people in power in the Liang family. On the surface, he was showing humility, but in fact, he was raising the status of the Sun family and relatives.
As many as ten people from the Sun family became servants, ministers, captains, county guards, and chief officials under their false names. These people are greedy, violent and dissolute.
They each sent their cronies to record the wealthy households in the counties under their jurisdiction, added other charges, imprisoned them, tortured them, and asked them to pay for their sins. Those who contributed less money were often executed or exiled.
There was a Fufeng man named Shisun Fen who was very rich but stingy by nature.
Liang Ji gave him a carriage and horses, and borrowed 50 million yuan from him. Scholar Sun Fen gave him thirty million.
Liang Ji was furious and informed the county officials, falsely accusing Shi Sun Fen's mother of being a slave in charge of his family's property, saying that she had stolen ten husks of white pearls and a thousand pounds of purple gold and escaped. So the scholar Sun Fen brother was imprisoned, tortured, and killed in prison, and all his family's money of more than 170 million was confiscated.
The property collected from various parties, as well as the tribute items throughout the year, had to be given to Liang Ji first, while the emperor received the inferior ones.
There was an endless stream of officials and common people bringing property to the Liang family to plead guilty. Liang Ji also sent people out to the fortress to contact foreign countries and conduct extensive searches for rare treasures. Taking advantage of the opportunity to travel, they asked for singers and servants from various places, and the people they sent relied on their power and acted tyrannically, robbing and humiliating women of the people, and beating officials and soldiers. Everyone hated them wherever they went. Liang Ji then built a large mansion, while Sun Shou also built a courtyard across the street, maximizing civil engineering to show off and compete with each other. There are deep and dense rooms where guests are received and where they sleep every day. The houses are connected and the doors are connected. The pillars and walls of the courtyard are carved with patterns and painted with gold paint.
summary: Emperor Huan granted Liang Ji 13,000 households and increased his staff. Liang Buyi and others were also enfeoffed. In the first year of peace, Liang Ji received another 10,000 households, totaling 30,000. His wife Sun Shou was granted the title of Lord of Xiangcheng. Sun Shou was beautiful and seductive, and Liang Ji doted on and feared her. Liang Ji had an affair with You Tongqi, a former concubine of his father, and she bore him a son. Sun Shou killed You Tongqi's family, and Liang Ji hid the child. Liang Ji also favored a servant named Qin Gong, who had an affair with Sun Shou. Liang Ji and Sun Shou amassed immense wealth through extortion and bribery, confiscating property from wealthy families. They built grand mansions with lavish decorations, gardens, and rare animals. Liang Ji's power grew unchecked, with all court matters decided by him. He killed officials who opposed him, including Wu Shu and Hou Meng. A young doctor named Yuan Zhu wrote to the emperor criticizing Liang Ji's power, but Liang Ji had him beaten to death. Liang Ji also killed many others, including Hao Xie and Hu Wu's families. Liang Buyi, who loved scriptures and treated others well, was estranged by Liang Ji and resigned. Liang Ji's family included seven marquises, three queens, six nobles, two generals, and many other officials. Liang Ji held power for over 20 years, dominating the court. Emperor Huan, angered by Liang Ji's arrogance, plotted with eunuchs to kill him. In the first year of Yanxi, after a series of events, Emperor Huan ordered the arrest of Liang Ji. Liang Ji and Sun Shou committed suicide. Over 300 of his officials and guests were dismissed. His property, worth over three billion, was confiscated and used to reduce taxes. His gardens were given to the poor.

◆Biography of Fan Hong, named Mi Qing, a native of Huyang, Nanyang County, and the uncle of Shizu.
His ancestor, Zhou Zhongshanfu, was granted the title of Fan, and because of this, he became a prominent surname in the village.
His father, Fan Zhong, whose courtesy name was Junyun, was good at farming and breeding goods.
Fan Zhong was kind-hearted and law-abiding. He lived together for three generations, and his descendants respected him day and night, always like a public servant.
In his business operation, he threw away nothing, taught children, slaves, and slaves, and everyone found his own suitability. Therefore, he was able to work together, and his financial profits doubled every year, so he opened more than 300 hectares of land.
The cottages they built all had high halls and pavilions, and were filled with ponds and canals.
There are also fish and livestock in the pond, and everything you ask for will be given.
He once wanted to make utensils, so he first planted Ziqi lacquer, which was ridiculed by people at that time. However, over time, it was put to good use, and people who had ridiculed him in the past borrowed it from him.
With a huge capital of tens of thousands, he provided relief to support the clan and enga the village.
Fan Zhong, his grandson and his brothers, fought over property. Fan Zhong felt ashamed and settled their grievances with two hectares of land.
The county praised him and recommended him as the third elder.
He died at the age of eighty.
The people who borrowed money from him accumulated millions in debt, and Fan Chong ordered the deeds to be burned.
The debtors were very ashamed when they heard about it and tried to repay their debts, but the sons obeyed their father's orders and refused to accept.
Fan Hong rarely has ambitions.
In the last years of Wang Mang's reign, rebels rose up. Liu Boxheng and his clan brother Liu Ci both led their troops to attack Huyang, but failed to capture it.
Liu Ci's sister was Fan Hong's wife, so Huyang arrested Fan Hong's wife and ordered her to tell Bo Sheng, but Fan Hong stayed behind and refused to return.
The military commander of Huyang wanted to kill his wife, and the chief officials said the following: Fan Zhong and his son lived in the countryside with courtesy, justice, and kindness. Although they are guilty, we will talk about it later.
Just when the Han soldiers arrived, the Yang army was frightened and anxious and did not dare to kill Fan's wife, so they were able to escape from danger.
When Gengshi was appointed, he wanted to make Fan Hong his general, but Fan Hong kowtowed and declined, saying: Scholars don't understand military affairs.
Unexpectedly, he was exempted from returning and built a camp with relatives of the clan to defend himself. More than a thousand people, old and weak, followed him.
At that time, the Red Eyebrow bandits plundered Tangzi Township and killed many people. They also wanted to attack Fan Hong's camp. Fan Hong sent people to bring cattle, wine, rice and grain to the Red Eyebrows.
The red eyebrow elders first heard about Fan Hong's benevolence and said: "Fan Jun has always been kind, and now he treats us so favorably, why attack him."
So he led his troops away, and Fan Hong was spared.
When Shizu ascended the throne, he paid homage to Dr. Guanglu and was promoted to the throne, second only to the Three Dukes.
In the fifth year of Jianwu, he was granted the title of Changluohou.
In the thirteenth year, he named his younger brother Fan Dan the Marquis of Sheyang, his brother Xun as the Marquis of Xuanxiang, and his elder brother Fan Zhong as the Marquis of Gengfu.
In the fifteenth year, Fan Hong was granted the title of Hou Zhang.
In the 18th year, the Emperor's South Temple Zhangling offered sacrifices, and he passed through Huyang to pay homage to Fan Zhong's tomb. He posthumously named Fan Zhong the longevity Zhang Jinghou, and built a temple in Huyang. Every time the emperor visited the south, he often worshiped his tomb and held reward meetings.
Fan Hong is modest and cautious, and does not seek luck.
Chang warned his son: If you are too wealthy, you will never have a happy ending.
summary: The biographies of Fan Hong and Yin Shi, two figures from the early Eastern Han dynasty. Fan Hong, a native of Huyang, Nanyang, was the uncle of Emperor Guangwu (Shizu). His ancestor was granted the title of Fan. His father, Fan Zhong, was a kind, law-abiding farmer and businessman who expanded the family's wealth to over 300 hectares of land, building grand estates with ponds and canals. He provided relief to his clan and village, and once settled a property dispute among his grandsons by giving them two hectares of land. Upon his death at eighty, his son Fan Hong burned the deeds of debtors, refusing repayment. During Wang Mang's reign, rebels attacked Huyang, and Fan Hong's wife was captured, but she was spared due to the family's reputation for kindness. Fan Hong declined a generalship under Gengshi, instead building a defensive camp that sheltered over a thousand people. When Red Eyebrow bandits threatened, he sent them gifts, and they spared him due to his benevolence. Under Emperor Guangwu, he became a high-ranking official, was enfeoffed as Changluohou, and later as Hou Zhang. He was known for his modesty, caution, and advice to his son against excessive wealth. He often arrived early at court and destroyed drafts of his memorials. On his deathbed, he requested a simple burial, which the emperor honored, granting him the posthumous title of Marquis Gong.

In the second year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted additional titles based on his military exploits. I entrusted my relatives to the nobles of Yin, and they still added titles. They cannot be made public to the world."
The emperor praised him very much and made him the captain of Guandu to guard Hangu.
Later, he moved to serve as a servant and returned home in the name of his mother's death.
In the fifteenth year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Luhou.
After Xianzong was established as the crown prince, he used his Yin consciousness to guard King Wu and guide the East Palace.
Every time the emperor visited the prefectures and counties, Yinshi always stayed to guard the capital and entrusted him with the ban of troops.
Although he spoke very seriously when he entered the palace, when he spoke to the guests, he did not mention state affairs.
The emperor respected him and often pointed to his yin consciousness to warn his relatives and encourage his surroundings.
The scribes used by Yinshi are all concise and virtuous people, such as Yu Ting, Fu Kuan, Xue Yanyin, etc., most of whom were public officials and lieutenants.
When Xianzong ascended the throne, he was worshiped as Zhijinwu, and his position was particularly advanced.
In the second year of Yongping, he passed away. He was given the official seal and ribbon as a gift and was given the posthumous title of Zhenhou.
summary: Yin Shi, a native of Xinye, Nanyang, was the brother of Empress Guanglie. His ancestor was Guan Zhong, whose descendant changed his surname to Yin. During Liu Bo's uprising, Yin Shi abandoned his studies in Chang'an to join him, leading over a thousand followers. He became a captain and later a general under Gengshi, conquering five counties. Under Emperor Guangwu, he was made a Cavalry Captain and Marquis of Yin Township. He humbly declined additional titles, stating the world was newly settled. He served as a captain and later returned home for his mother's funeral. He was enfeoffed as Luhou and served as a guardian to the crown prince, often staying to guard the capital during the emperor's travels. He was discreet about state affairs and employed virtuous scribes. Upon Emperor Ming's ascension, he became Zhijinwu. He died in the second year of Yongping, receiving the posthumous title of Zhenhou.

◆The biography of Qiao Xuan, whose courtesy name is Jun Huang, was born in Langzhong, Ba County.
When he was young, he was easy to learn and could speak "Yi" and "Spring and Autumn".
He was appointed as an official in the state and county.
In the second year of Emperor Yongshi's reign, there was a solar eclipse, and the imperial court issued an edict to appoint one person each to be honest, humble, and righteous.
The state held the title of Qiao Xuan, went to the bus, answered policy questions, got a high rank, and was awarded the title of Consultant.
Emperor Cheng began to hold regular meetings and went out casually many times.
Zhao Feiyan was made queen, but Zhao Feiyan was jealous of her and many of her princes were killed.
Qiao Xuan wrote: I heard that the emperor upholds the destiny to inherit the clan, protect the great cause of the ancestors, and continue the emperor's throne. The most important thing is to have successors. Therefore, "Yi" has the meaning of "Qian Gu", and "Poetry" praises many blessings.
It means being able to inherit the past, being capable in dealing with things, and correcting the mistakes of parents. It means having many children and grandchildren is a blessing to the family and the country. Now the emperor's successor has not been established, and everyone in the world is looking forward to it. However, the emperor does not care about the country's big plans, and only engages in trivial matters. He is seduced by women and devotes his attention to non-serious things.
When I heard that the harem prince had given birth to many children and could not survive, I felt extremely sad and worried, and I will not forget it for a moment.
If the guards are unprepared, disasters often occur and unexpected events occur.
Suddenly there are drunken and crazy husbands, fighting on the road, no dignity of honor, who knows the difference between up and down.
This is why tigers start under your vehicles and thieves appear around you.
I hope that the emperor will think of the great things in the world, cherish his golden body, and benefit from the blessings of the nine daughters, so as to preserve endless blessings. The world will be fine.
At this time, disasters occurred frequently, and Qiao Xuan stated the reasons for them.
summary: It suggests that this is an imperfect approach, as people's temperaments differ, and what they do or refrain from doing is appropriate for each individual. In times of peace, many who deviate from the norm can become famous and upright, with ambitions as strong as gold or integrity as severe as winter frost. Some make friends willing to live and die together, risking their lives for justice. Though not perfect, these deeds are memorable, though their complexities make them hard to categorize. The text states that such exceptional conduct is recorded in the "Ding Xing Pian" to fill gaps in history.

If the emperor does not adopt it, he will remain in the Langguan position for a long time and will not be promoted.
Later, he was promoted to Taichang Cheng and resigned due to the death of his younger brother.
In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty of Emperor Ping, there was a solar eclipse, and he ordered the ministers to promote honest and outspoken people.
Da Honglu and Zuo Xian raised Qiao Xuan to the bus to answer the emperor's policy questions. He was also awarded the title of Yi Lang and was promoted to Zhongsan Dafu.
For four years, eight people who are wise in politics and able to change customs are selected.
At that time, everyone held the title of Qiao Xuan and was appointed as an envoy of embroidered clothes. They uphold integrity and traveled all over the country with the imperial servant Wang Yun and others to observe the customs. Wherever they went, they specialized in killing bad people and rewarding good people.
Before the matter was completed, Wang Mang took charge of the emperor's affairs, so Qiao Xuan threw away the embroidered messenger's car, changed his name, ran back home privately, and hid himself.
Later, Gongsun Shu claimed that he had a false name in Shu and hired him many times, but he refused to go.
Gongsun Shu then sent an envoy to summon him with gifts; if Qiao Xuan refused to go, he would be given poison.
The prefect himself sent the seal to Qiao Xuan's home, saying: "You are already famous for your high integrity, and the court intends to use you. You should not resign, or you will bring disaster."
Qiao Xuan looked up to the sky and sighed: "For a great sage like Tang Yao, Xu You was ashamed to be his minister. For someone as virtuous as King Wu of Zhou, Boyi would rather starve to death than eat his corn."
Who is Gongsun Shu and who am I?
Keep your ambitions high, live a good life, and die without regrets!
For receiving poison.
Qiao Xuan's son Qiao Wangying kowtowed in tears and said to the eunuch: "There is a big enemy in the east now. The army is attacking. The country is spending a lot of money, there are a lot of military supplies, and the country's treasury is insufficient. I am willing to spend tens of millions of my family's money to atone for my father's death."
The prefect made a request for him, and Gongsun Shu agreed.
Qiao Xuan therefore hid in the fields until Gongsun Shu's death.
At this time, wars continued for many years, and no one could talk about his studies. Qiao Xuan alone taught his disciples to study the classics diligently.
He died in the eleventh year of Jianwu.
The next year, when the world was at peace, Qiao Xuan's younger brother went to the capital to report Qiao Xuan's deeds to the emperor. Guangwu praised Qiao Xuan's deeds, ordered the county to sacrifice him in a prison, and ordered the locality to return Qiao Xuan's family money.
At that time, there was a Jian named Fei Yi, who refused to accept Gongsun Shu's fake post, so he painted his body with paint to act as a ghost, pretended to be crazy and escaped, and lived in the Tibetan mountains for more than ten years.
After Gongsun Shu was eliminated, he became the prefect of Hepu.
King Qiao Ying was good at explaining the Book of Changes and used it to teach Xianzong, and he was appointed as the guard order of Beigong.
◆The biography of Li Ye, whose courtesy name is Juyou, was born in Zitong, Guanghan.
When he was young, he was ambitious and upright, admiring himself and not following the popular customs.
He studied "Lu Shi" with Dr. Xu Huang as his teacher.
In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, he cited the Ming Sutra and was awarded the title of Lang.
When Wang Mang came to power on behalf of the emperor, Li Ye resigned due to illness and refused to be appointed by the state and county.
The prefect Liu Xian forced him to come out. Li Ye had no choice but to go to Liu Xian when he was ill. Liu Xian got angry and came out to teach him a lesson: A wise man does not avoid disaster. This is like a sword and crossbow shooting into a busy city. The less fortunate will die first.
summary: The biography of Qiao Xuan follows. Born in Ba County, he was learned in the "Yi" and "Spring and Autumn." He became an official and was recommended for his integrity during a solar eclipse in Emperor Yongshi's reign. He criticized Emperor Cheng for neglecting state affairs and focusing on trivial matters, warning of dangers from unpreparedness. Despite frequent disasters, his advice was ignored, and he remained in a low position. He later resigned after his brother's death. During Wang Mang's usurpation, Qiao Xuan abandoned his post and hid. Gongsun Shu tried to recruit him with threats of poison, but Qiao Xuan refused, citing historical examples of integrity. His son offered money to spare his life, and Qiao Xuan hid until Gongsun Shu's death. He died in the eleventh year of Jianwu, and Guangwu later honored him.

A guest said to Liu Xian: Zhao Jianzi killed Dou Mingdu, and Confucius refused to cross the river.
