Liu Xiancai released Li Ye and promoted him as Founder.
Wang Mang appointed Li Ye as a bartender, but he refused to leave due to illness, so he hid in the valley and lost his name until Wang Mang's death.
Gongsun Shu set up a false name. He often heard people say that Li Ye was talented, so he recruited him and wanted to use him as a doctor. Li Ye insisted that he could not afford to be ill.
A few years later, Gongsun Shu thought he had lost face because he did not summon Li Ye, so he sent Dahong Yinrong to threaten Li Ye with poison and an edict: if he obeyed the order, he would give the Duke the throne; if he did not, he would give poison.
Yin Rong persuaded Li Yedao: Today the world is falling apart, no one knows who is right and who is wrong.
Why try the unpredictable abyss with your small body?
The imperial court admires your reputation and morality, and has kept your official position and position vacant for seven years now. It has cherished you all the time and will not forget you.
Isn't it good to serve your close friends at the top and consider your children and grandchildren at the bottom?
If you don't go there for a few years now, if you are suspected of being hostile, disaster may befall you immediately. This is not an option.
Li Ye had no choice but to sigh and said: "You can't enter a country that is in danger, and you can't live in a country that is in chaos."
Doing evil deeds personally is not allowed by righteousness.
When a gentleman sees danger and gives orders, how can he be lured with heavy bait from a high position?
Seeing that Li Yezhi couldn't give in, Yin Rong said again: "You should call your wife, children and children to discuss it."
Li Ye said: It took me a long time to make up my mind. Why did I ask my wife?
He drank poison and died.
Gongsun Shu was shocked when he heard that Li Ye was dead. He felt it was shameful to carry the name of killing a wise man, so he sent envoys to pay homage to Li Ye and perform hundreds of funeral rites.
Li Ye's son Li Fu resigned and refused to accept it.
After Gongsun Shu's puppet Shu was pacified, Guangwu issued an edict to show Li Ye's inner circle. "Yi Bu Ji" records Li Ye's high integrity and paints his image.
At first, during the reign of Emperor Ping, Wang Hao of Shu County was appointed as the Order of Meiyang, and Wang Jia was appointed as Lang.
Wang Mang usurped the throne of the Han Dynasty, and they all abandoned their official positions and returned to the west.
When Gongsun Shu proclaimed himself emperor, he sent envoys to recruit Wang Hao and Wang Jia. He was worried that they would not go, so he captured their wives first.
The messenger said to Wang Jia: Let's go on the road quickly, my wife can be saved.
Wang Jia replied: Dogs and horses know their owners, let alone humans?
Wang Hao committed suicide first and gave his head to the messenger.
Gongsun Shu was furious and killed Wang Hao's family members.
When Wang Jia heard about it, he sighed and said, "I'm a step too late!"
summary: Li Ye, from Guanghan, was ambitious and upright, studying the "Lu Shi." He refused to serve under Wang Mang, feigning illness. Forced by Prefect Liu Xian, he was imprisoned but released after a guest intervened. He later hid in the valley. Gongsun Shu tried to recruit him with threats of poison, but Li Ye refused, stating that a gentleman should not enter a chaotic state. He drank poison and died. Gongsun Shu, ashamed, held a funeral. After Shu was pacified, Guangwu honored Li Ye. Others like Wang Hao and Wang Jia also refused to serve Gongsun Shu, choosing death over submission.

translation:
He bent his sword against the messenger and died.
At this time, Ren Yong from Jianwei and Feng Xin from the same county as Li Ye were both eager to learn and knowledgeable about the present and the past.
Gongsun Shu was recruited many times and promised high officials and generous salaries, but he used glaucoma to escape the world's difficulties.
Ren Yong's wife had committed adultery before and kept it secret. She watched her son fall into a well and did nothing to save her.
Feng Xin's maid also committed adultery with Feng Xin.
When they heard that Gongsun Shu had been executed, Ren Yong and Feng Xin both washed their faces and looked at each other and said: "The world is at peace and our eyes are clear."
Those who commit adultery and adultery commit suicide.
After Guangwu heard about it, he recruited them, but they all happened to die of illness at home.
◆The biography of Liu Mao, whose courtesy name is Ziwei, was born in Jinyang, Taiyuan.
Lost his father when he was young.
A person lives with his mother. His family was poor and he relied on his labor income to support his mother. His filial piety was praised by the villagers.
When he grows up, he can study the Book of Rites and teach hundreds of students.
During the reign of Emperor Ai, he promoted filial piety and integrity and was promoted to five former princes of the country. However, his mother died and he was dismissed.
When the mourning period expires, he will be appointed Juyang Order.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne of the Han Dynasty, Liu Mao abandoned his official position and hid in Hongnong Mountain to teach his students.
In the second year of Jianwu, he came back from Hongnong Mountain and served as a subordinate of the county.
At this time, more than 200,000 people from Chimei came to attack the county and killed the chief officials and government officials.
Liu Mao carried the prefect Sun Fu on his back, climbed the wall and hid in a hollow, and narrowly escaped death.
That night, the two people fled to Yu County.
They hide during the day and come out to find food at night.
In this way, it took more than a hundred days before the red-browed thief left and was able to return to the county.
In the second year, the imperial edict was issued to visit the righteous people in the world.
Sun Fu said to Liu Mao: I was attacked by Red Eyebrows in front of me. The officials and the people were in chaos and fled up the mountain. I was surrounded by thieves and my life was tied to my hair. Fortunately, you carried me on my back to climb the city and get out of Baoyu County.
You and your brother risked their lives to find food in the mountains, and my wife and I were able to save our lives. This is a very high moral integrity.
We should praise and promote righteous people.
The imperial edict immediately conscripted Liu Mao as Yilang and promoted him to Zong Zhengcheng.
Later, he was awarded the title of Shizhong and died in office.
In Yanping, hundreds of people from Xianbei invaded Yuyang. The eunuch Zhang Xian led his officials to chase them out of the fortress. Looking at the fireworks of the prison camp in the distance, they followed closely.
Yan Shuo, who was carrying soldiers and horses, was worried about an ambush and tried hard to persuade him not to pursue him, but Zhang Xian, the prefect, refused to listen to him.
Zhang Xian still forced his way forward, but Yan Shui had no choice but to advance forward to fight. Sure enough, the Xianbei soldiers who were ambushing him suddenly attacked and Yan Shui was wounded ten times and died on the battlefield.
summary: Liu Mao, from Taiyuan, was known for filial piety. He studied the "Book of Rites" and taught students. He abandoned his post during Wang Mang's usurpation and hid in Hongnong Mountain. During a Red Eyebrow attack, he carried the prefect Sun Fu to safety, hiding and foraging for food for over a hundred days. Sun Fu praised his integrity, and Liu Mao was appointed Yilang. He later died in office. Other accounts describe Yan Shuo, who died fighting Xianbei invaders, and Suo Fu, who died saving a magistrate from thieves.

translation:
Zhang Xian drew his sword and chased the scattered soldiers, but was unable to stop them. The enemy captured Zhang Xian and shot him. Chief Wei Fu and meritorious officer Xu Xian quickly went to rescue Zhang Xian. Zhang Xian fell under his horse. Wei Fu covered Zhang Xian with his body, and the enemy captured them all.
The imperial court took pity on Yan Shu and other righteous martyrs, issued an edict to praise them, and gave them great rewards. Each of his sons was appointed a doctor.
In the second year of Yongchu, the big thief Bi Hao and others entered the territory of Pingyuan, and the county magistrate Liu Xiong led his officials to chase them by boat.
When he arrived at the Yanci River, he fought with the thieves. Liu Xiong was defeated and captured, and the thieves stabbed him with a spear.
At this time, the assistant of the minor official came forward to kowtow and beg for mercy, and was willing to die in Liu Xiong's place.
Bi Hao and others let Liu Xiong go to stab Suo Fu. The spear penetrated his heart and back, killing him immediately.
The prefect of Dongjun captured Bi Hao and others and reported the situation to the court.
The edict commemorated the mourning, granted two hundred thousand yuan in money, and appointed the doctor who was appointed by his father as his assistant.
◆Biography of Wen Xu, courtesy name Cifang, a native of Qi County, Taiyuan.
He became an official in the state.
In the second year of Jianwu, the cavalry captain Gongli Shu led his troops to pacify Beizhou and arrived in Taiyuan. He visited handsome people and asked them for their plans.
Gongli garrison met Wen Xu and thought he was a genius. He recommended Wen Xu to the emperor, so the imperial court recruited him to serve as a censor. He was promoted to captain of Wuling, but he resigned due to illness.
In the sixth year, Wen Xu was granted the title of Visitor and promoted to the Colonel of the Qiang Protector.
Wen Xu went to Xiangwu to inspect his subordinates and inspect the criminal administration, but he was arrested by Gou Yu, the general of Nang Guixiao.
Gou Yu said to Wen Xu: If you cooperate with me, the world can win.
Wen Xu said: "If you accept the heavy responsibility of the country, you can only put your life on the line. For the sake of righteousness, you must not be afraid of death and betray the kindness of the court."
Gou Yu and others persuaded him again and again.
Wen Xu, who was already strong, was furious and scolded Gou Yu and others: "How dare the ugly prisoners threaten the Han generals!"
He killed a few people with his sword.
There were many thieves and they were vying to kill Wen Xu. Gou Yu stopped them and said, "This is the day for the death of a righteous man. You can give him a sword."
Wen Xu took the sword, put his beard in his mouth, looked around at the people around him and said, "I have been forced to kill by thieves, so don't let your beard be stained by dirt again."
He fell on his sword and died.
Wen Xu was in charge of registering Han Zun, and Wang Zhong was responsible for collecting the corpse and burying it.
Guangwu felt sorry for him when he heard about it, and ordered Wang Zhong to send the funeral to Luoyang. He gave Wen Xu a cemetery next to the city, sent him a thousand dendrobiums and five hundred pieces of silk, and appointed his three sons as doctors.
The eldest son, Wenshou, was appointed Houxiang of Zouping after his mourning period expired.
In his dream, Wen Xu told him: I have been a guest away for a long time and miss my hometown.
Wen Shou abandoned his official position and wrote a letter asking to go home and bury his father.
The emperor approved his request and sent his father's coffin back to the old cemetery in his hometown.
◆Peng Xiu's biography, Peng Xiu's courtesy name is Ziyang, and he was from Piling, Kuaiji.
summary: Wen Xu, from Taiyuan, was recommended as a talent and became a censor. He was captured by Gou Yu, who tried to persuade him to join a rebellion. Wen Xu refused, scolding the rebels and killing several before falling on his sword. Guangwu honored him with a grand funeral and appointed his sons as doctors. Peng Xiu, from Kuaiji, defended his father from robbers at age fifteen, gaining fame. As an official, he saved a chief clerk from execution by reasoning with the prefect. He later died shielding the prefect from thieves' arrows.

translation:
In the last years of Jianwu, when he could no longer be recruited, Guangwu sent someone to carry him to the capital in a sedan chair. He was summoned at Yuntai, Nangong, and given two thousand dendrobiums of grain, he was sent home and his son was consecrated as the prince's concubine.
Die at home.
◆Zhou Jiachuan, courtesy name Huiwen, was from Ancheng, Runan.
My great-great-great-grandfather Zhou Yan was a county general Cao Cao during the reign of Emperor Xuan.
The eunuch wanted to kill someone unjustly, but Zhou Yan refused to listen to his advice, so he killed the prisoner and deposed Zhou Yan at the same time.
The prisoner's family stood guard at the palace gate, crying out for injustice and ordering a reexamination. Zhou Yan met the prefect and said, "I hope you will write the documents carefully, with my name written on them. The prince only said that you were ill at that time."
When he came out of the prefect's office, he said to the governor: "When you are questioned, just blame me, Zhou Yan."
If you say something to Fu Jun, I, Zhou Yan, will use my swords in my hands.
The envoy then arrested Zhou Yan and imprisoned him.
He was tortured many times and refused to tell the truth.
According to the crime, he should be thrown into the Jamshi room, so he sighed and said: I am a descendant of King Ping and the great-great-grandson of Zhenggong. How can I go to see the late king without cutting off the sword?
He went on a hunger strike and died.
Zhou Yan had five sons, all of whom were governors and prefects.
Zhou Jia became an official and became the governor of the county.
In the last years of Wang Mang, a group of thieves entered Ruyang City. Zhou Jia followed the prefect He Chang to attack the thieves. He Chang was hit by a stray arrow. The county soldiers fled one after another. The thieves surrounded him for dozens of miles and fought with swords. Zhou Jia supported He Chang and defended He Chang with his own body.
Because he scolded the thieves and said: You are all slaves of others. Being thieves is already treason. Is there anyone who kills his own superiors?
I, Zhou Jiaqing, sacrificed my life to redeem the officer's life.
Because he looked up to the sky and cried.
The thieves looked at each other and said, "This is a righteous man!" He returned his carriage and horses and sent him away.
Later, the prefect Kou Xun promoted Zhou Jia to the title of Xiaolian and the minister of minister.
Guangwu summoned him and asked him about Zhou Jia's death.
Zhou Jia replied: The governor is injured and his life is in the hands of thieves. I am too stupid and coward to die.
The emperor said: This is the elder.
The imperial edict ordered Zhou Jia to marry the princess, but Zhou Jia said that he was seriously ill and did not dare to marry the princess.
He was promoted to the prefect of Lingling and served for seven years before passing away.
Lingling praised his legacy, and officials and people built a shrine in his honor.
Zhou Jia's uncle and brother Zhou Chang, named Bochi, was kind-hearted and served as Yin of Henan.
In the second year of Yongchu, there was a severe drought in the summer, and there was no rain after long prayers. Zhou Chang collected and buried the bones of more than 10,000 people who died in Luoyang, and a sweet rain fell at the right time, and this year he had a good harvest.
The position reaches Guang Luxun.
◆The biography of Shishi, whose courtesy name is Juqing, was born in Jinxiang, Shanyang, and his last name was Si.
When he was young, he entered the Imperial Academy and became a student, and became friends with Zhang Shao of Runan.
Zhang Shao was named Yuan Bo.
summary: Suo Lufang, from Dongjun, taught the "Shang Shu" and served as a county magistrate. During the Gengshi period, he offered to die in place of a prefect condemned by an envoy, who pardoned them. He later became Luoyang Order, known for his ability. In his old age, Guangwu summoned him to the capital and honored him. Zhou Jia, from Runan, followed a prefect into battle against thieves. When the prefect was wounded, Zhou Jia shielded him and scolded the thieves, who released them. He later refused to marry a princess and died as prefect of Lingling.

translation:
The two took leave and returned home.
Shi Shi said to Uncle Yuan: "I will come back in two years' time and come to your house to pay homage to Lord Zunlingtang and see your son."
So the two agreed on a date together.
Later, when the day came, Zhang Yuanbo told his mother all the details of the incident, and asked his mother to prepare wine and dinner to wait for Fan Shi's arrival.
His mother said: After two years apart, why do you take the words spoken thousands of miles away so seriously?
Answer: Fan Juqing is a very faithful person and will definitely not break the contract.
Mother said: In this case, I will prepare wine and food for you.
On that day, Fan Juqing really arrived, went to the hall to worship, and parted happily.
Shi Fan was appointed as the meritorious official of the county.
Later, Zhang Yuanbo fell seriously ill, and fellow county residents Zhi Junzhang and Yin Zizheng visited him day and night.
When Uncle Yuan was dying, he sighed: I regret not seeing my dead friend!
Yin Zizheng said: "Jun Zhang and I are wholeheartedly recruiting you. We are not dead friends. Where can you find a dead friend?"
Yuan Bo said: You two are my living friends, but Fan Juqing of Shanyang is my dead friend.
Soon, he passed away.
Shi Fan suddenly dreamed of Uncle Yuan's black crown hanging with tassels on his clothes and he shouted: "Ju Qing, I have died on a certain day. I should be buried on time and return to the underworld forever."
You have not forgotten my words. Can you be there for the burial?
Paradigm suddenly woke up, lamented and cried, reported to the prefect, and asked to be allowed to go to the funeral.
Although the prefect didn't believe it in his heart, he believed that Shi Shi's feelings were valuable, so he agreed to attend the funeral.
Paradigm dressed in his friend's mourning clothes and rode horseback on the day of burial.
Before the paradigm arrived, Yuan Bo's mourning had already begun. He arrived at Xiengjing and was about to lower the coffin. At this time, the coffin could not be lifted and refused to enter.
His mother patted the coffin and said: Uncle Yuan, is there still hope?
He stopped the coffin for a while and saw plain carriages and white horses coming wailing.
His mother took a look and said, "This must be Fan Juqing!"
When Juqing arrived, he kowtowed to the coffin and said, "I've gone to Uncle Yuan!"
Life and death are different paths, farewell forever.
More than a thousand people who attended the funeral shed tears.
The paradigm then held on to the silk ribbon as a guide, and the coffin moved forward.
Paradigm stayed next to the tomb, repaired the tomb tree, and then went back.
Later he arrived in the capital and studied at Taixue.
At this time, Zhu Changsha and Chen Pingzi were also at Taixue and did not know Shi Shi. Chen Pingzi was ill and was about to die. He said to his wife: I heard that Fan Juqing of Shanyang was a righteous man and could be trusted to die.
After I die, it will be fine if I just bury my body in front of Juqing's house.
So he tore off a piece of vegetarian food and wrote a letter to Ju Qing.
After his death, his wife followed Hirako's will.
At this time, Fan Shi just returned from an trip. He read Chen Pingzi's letter and his tomb. He was so sad that he bowed to the tomb and cried non-stop, thinking that he was his dead friend.
So he took care of Pingzi's wife and children and personally sent the funeral back to Linxiang.
At a place four or five miles away from Linxiang, he put the plain calligraphy on the coffin, cried goodbye and left.
summary: Shi Shi, from Shanyang, was known for his faithfulness. He promised to visit his friend Zhang Shao after two years and kept his word. When Zhang Shao died, Shi Shi dreamed of him and traveled to attend his funeral, where the coffin moved only after his arrival. He later cared for another friend's family after his death. As governor of Jingzhou, he recognized a poor friend working as a laborer and offered him a position, but the friend refused. Shi Shi died as prefect of Lujiang.

translation:
Pingzi's brother heard about it but couldn't find him.
Changsha sent a messenger to the capital to write a letter indicating Fan Shi's behavior. The three prefectures were all vying to recruit him, but they were not accepted.
The most talented person in Juzhou was promoted to the rank of governor of Jingzhou.
My friend Kong Song from Nanyang had a poor family and his parents were old, so he changed his name and was hired as a pawn on Ali Street in Xinye County.
Shishi inspected the new fields, and the county chose Kong Song as a guide to welcome Shishi.
Fan Shi knew him as Kong Song. He held Kong Song's arm and said, "Aren't you Kong Zhongshan?"
He sighed and talked about his life experiences, saying: "In the past, you and I both wore long robes and studied at the Imperial Academy. I was favored by the country and became the governor, but you actually concealed your identity and stayed in the army. What a pity!"
Kong Song said: Hou Ying has been a soldier of the Yi clan for a long time, guarding the city gate, and he is very happy.
Confucius wanted to live in Jiuyi, and he did not mind being humble.
Being poor is the duty of a scholar. Is this despicable?
Shifan ordered the county to replace Kong Song. Kong Song thought that he was hired first and the date of employment had not expired, so he refused to go.
When Kong Song was in Ali, he acted righteously and strictly, and all the children in the street obeyed his teachings.
So the government conscripted him.
On the way to the capital, they stayed in the pavilion. Thieves stole his horse. Soon after they learned that it was Kong Song's horse, they scolded each other: Kong Zhongshan is a good man, how can he invade it?
So the horse was returned to Kong Song.
Kong Song was appointed as the governor of Nanhai.
Shi Fan was later promoted to the prefect of Lujiang and became famous. He died in office.
◆Li Shanchuan, the second grandson of Li Shan, was born in Yuyang, Nanyang. He was originally a servant of Li Yuan from the same county.
An epidemic was prevalent in Jianwu, and Li Yuan's family members died of illness one after another. Only an orphan, Li Xu, was born. In just a few dozen days, the family had tens of thousands of dollars in wealth. The slaves discussed privately and wanted to kill Li Xu too, so that everyone could divide the property.
Li Shan pitied Li Shi, but was unable to stop him, so he secretly carried Li Xu and ran away, hiding in the Shanyang Xiaqiu world, feeding him himself, feeding him food and water, and his milk also produced milk, so as to avoid the heat and cold, and prepare for hardships.
Although Li Xu was in his arms, Li Shan treated him like an elder brother. If something happened, he would kneel down and ask for instructions before reporting.
The villagers were moved by his deeds and followed him in doing good deeds.
When Li Xu was ten years old, Li Shan took him back to the county to reorganize his old business.
He complained to the chief minister about the slaves, and he rounded them up and killed them all.
At this time, Zhong Liyi Ren Xia Qiu ordered him to write a letter recommending Li Shan's deeds.
Guangwu issued an edict to grant Li Shan and Li Xu both sacrifices for the prince.
Li Shan was recruited by the government during the reign of Emperor Xianzong. Because he could manage difficult places, he was promoted to the governor of Rinan.
On his way to his post in the capital, he passed by Xuyuyang and passed Li Yuan's tomb. A mile away, he took off his court clothes and started weeding with a hoe.
After paying homage to the tomb, he wept and grieved endlessly. He cooked rice with his own hands and held a tripod to offer sacrifices to Li Yuan.
summary: Li Shan, from Nanyang, saved an orphaned infant, Li Xu, from murderous slaves by fleeing and raising him. He treated Li Xu with respect and later returned to reclaim the family property, punishing the slaves. Guangwu honored them. Li Shan later became governor of Rinan, visiting Li Yuan's tomb with great reverence. He died en route to Jiujiang. Wang Yi, from Guanghan, buried a stranger who died in his care, using gold from the deceased. Later, a horse and embroidered quilt led him to the stranger's father, who recognized his son's belongings. Wang Yi also solved a ghostly murder case at an inn.

translation:
The woman then came to complain and said: "My husband is the magistrate of Fu County. When he became an official, he passed by this pavilion and stayed here. The director of the pavilion was a bad guy. He killed more than ten members of my family, buried them downstairs, and robbed all my family's belongings."
Wang Yi asked the pavilion chief who his last name was.
The woman said: This is the current Youyou under your sect.
Wang Yi said: Why did you kill passers-by many times?
The woman replied: I cannot complain to myself during the day and state my grievances at night. The passer-by often sleeps and does not respond. She is very angry, so she kills the passer-by to vent her hatred.
Wang Yi said: I will resolve this unjust case for you and never kill kind people again.
The woman took off her clothes, threw them on the ground, and suddenly disappeared. The next day Wang Yi called Youyou for interrogation and confessed all the crimes. He was immediately arrested and a dozen of his accomplices were executed.
They sent officials to take their mourning back to their hometowns, and Erting was at peace from then on.
◆Zhang Wu Chuan, Zhang Wu, was from Youquan County, Wu County.
My father, Zhang Ye, was a servant of the county. He sent the eunuch's wife back to his hometown and went to Hanoi Pavilion. She was robbed and robbed at night. Zhang Ye died fighting with the thieves, and his body was not found.
Zhang Wu was still young at the time and could not remember his father's face.
Later, Zhang Wu entered the Imperial College to study. On festival days, he often took his father's sword and went to the place where his father died in battle to pay homage and come back crying.
The Fifth Lun of the prefect commended Zhang Wu for his filial piety and commended him for his filial piety and integrity.
When his mother died, he grieved excessively. His father's soul did not return and he died of grief.
◆Lu Yu was passed down, with the courtesy name Zhi Chu, from Wuxian County, Kuaiji.
It has been the common surname in the county for generations.
His grandfather, Lu Hong, whose courtesy name was Zichun, was a minister in Jianwu.
He was a handsome man who liked to wear Yue cloth. Guangwu also liked this kind of Yue cloth when he saw it. From then on, he often ordered Kuaiji County to offer Yue cloth.
His father died one after another when he was young, and he became an official in the county.
At this time, the people were hungry, so the prefect Yin Xing sent gruel to the people in Duting one after another.
All the hungry people were called together one after another and their names were asked one by one.
When the matter was over, Yin Xing asked how many people had eaten the gruel?
One after another, they immediately replied that there were more than 600 people, and they also named each one, without any mistakes.
Yin Xing admired his talent very much.
The governor inspected his subordinates, inspected the criminal administration, summoned them one after another, and recruited them to work as other officers.
He resigned due to illness and returned to the county to serve as a servant.
At this time, Chu Wangying rebelled and secretly searched for talents from all over the world. Chu Wangying's rebellion was discovered, and Xianzong obtained the case record, which contained Yin Xing's name, so he conscripted Yin Xing to Tingwei Prison.
summary: Zhang Wu, from Wu County, mourned his father, who died fighting thieves. He often visited the site of his father's death with his sword. He was commended for filial piety but died of grief after his mother's death. Lu Yu, from Kuaiji, was known for his intelligence and loyalty. During a rebellion, he and others were tortured but refused to implicate the prefect. His mother's cooking helped identify her presence. He was pardoned and died of old age.

translation:
After the brothers got married, their wives asked for separation and they often quarreled.
Miao Xu was extremely angry and hit himself for closing the door. He said: "Miao Xu, you cultivate your moral character and learn the ways of saints because you want to straighten the customs. Why can't you straighten your own family?"
After hearing this, Miao Xu's younger brother and each of their wives kowtowed and apologized, and the family became a harmonious and moral family.
Miao Xu became an official in the county and was the chief bookkeeper.
At this time, the county magistrate was accused and put on trial. The officials were all afraid and confessed their innocence. Only Miao Xu was the only one to prove his innocence.
Liang Zhan, the prefect of Longxi, summoned Miao Xu to be the judge of Cao Shi.
In the early years of Emperor An's reign, Liang Zhan died in his official residence, and Miao Wei returned to Longxi in mourning.
At the beginning of the burial, when the Xiqiang rebelled, all Liang Zhan's wives fled to other counties to escape the rebellion. Miao Wei stayed there alone to build a tomb for Liang Zhan.
A secret room was built next to the well. He hid in it during the day and built a tomb with earth at night. When the Qiang thieves were put down, the tomb was also built.
Liang Zhan's wife thought Miao Xu was dead long ago. When she came back to see him, she was greatly surprised.
There is a legend in Guanxi that Miao Xu was given gifts of carriages, horses, clothes, and money, but Miao Xu refused to accept them and went home.
The government conscripted him, and he was promoted to Zhong Mou Ling.
The county was close to the capital, and there were many prominent and powerful people. When Miao Wei took office, he executed a group of traitors and more than a hundred people who had entrusted noble relatives and guests to death, which made him famous.
Die in office.
◆Chen Chongchuan, courtesy name Jinggong, was a native of Yichun County, Yuzhang County.
When he was young, he was friends with Lei Yi, who was from the same county, and they both studied "Lu Shi" and "Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals".
The prefect Zhang Yun promoted Chen Chong to Xiao Lian, and Chen Chong gave it to Lei Yi. He wrote more than ten letters successively, but Zhang Yun refused to obey him.
In the second year of Lei Yi's promotion of filial piety and integrity, Chen Chong and Lei Yi were both at the Lang Office.
There was a colleague who owed hundreds of thousands of dollars in interest. Creditors came every day to press for debts, so Chen Chong secretly paid the money back on his behalf.
The same official later found out and thanked him profusely.
Chen Zhongdao: I didn't return it on my behalf, it was probably someone with the same name as me who did it.
He never said that he paid the interest on his behalf.
Another fellow servant went home to visit his relatives and mistakenly took away a pair of trousers belonging to his neighbor.
The owner suspected that Chen Zhong had taken it, but Chen Zhong refused to tell him and bought a pair of pants to return to him.
Later, the person who returned home came back and returned the pants to the owner, and the matter became clear.
After Chen Chong and Lei Yi were both appointed ministers, Lei Yi suffered on behalf of his contemporaries and was deposed. When Chen Chong saw Lei Yi being deposed, he also resigned due to illness.
Later, he promoted outstanding talents and was awarded Xiyang Order.
He had special political achievements and extraordinary achievements. He was about to be promoted to the prefect of Kuaiji, but his sister mourned him and he resigned.
Later, he was recruited by Situ and appointed as a censor. He died.
◆Lei Yi Zhuan, whose courtesy name is Zhonggong, was born in Poyang County, Yuzhang County.
He first served as a meritorious officer, promoted good people, and did not take credit for himself.
Lei Yi once saved a man from death. The sinner later thanked him with two pounds of gold, but Lei Yi did not accept it.
When the gold owner saw that Lei Yi was not around, he quietly placed the gold on the tent on the hanging bed to catch the dust.
It was only after repairing the house and cleaning that I discovered it.
The gold owner was dead and could not be returned, so Lei Yi had no choice but to send the gold to the county.
Later, he was promoted to be Xiaolian and was appointed Minister of the Secretariat. His fellow minister committed a crime and should be punished. Lei Yi silently confessed his crime, so he was punished as a military officer and sent to the border to guard against the enemy.
Tongtai Lang found out about it, resigned from his position and asked for atonement for Lei Yi's crime.
Emperor Shun's edict removed all their punishments.
Lei Yi returned to the county and promoted his talents to Chen Chong, but the governor refused. Lei Yi pretended to be crazy and ran away with his hair scattered, not obeying his orders.
The villagers made a jingle and said: Glue paint is said to be strong, not as good as Lei and Chen.
The three governments recruited them at the same time.
Lei Yi was the agent of the envoy.
The envoy Chijie inspected the customs of the county and state, and a total of seventy people were convicted by the prefect.
Soon after, he was awarded the title of Imperial Censor and served as the Nandun Order. He died in office.
His son Lei Shou was promoted to the prefect of Cangwu.
summary: Dai Feng, from Jibei, was a devoted student who buried a classmate and returned his belongings. He once gave his remaining money to a thief, who returned his stolen goods. As a magistrate, locusts avoided his territory, and he prayed for rain by threatening self-immolation, which brought rain. He released prisoners to visit families, and all returned. He died in office. Li Chong, from Chenliu, was poor but refused to separate from his family. He expelled his wife for suggesting division. He later killed a tomb robber and refused official posts. He was respected by General Deng Zhi but criticized him openly. He died at eighty-eight. Miao Xu, from Runan, resolved family disputes by self-reflection. He defended a magistrate and built a tomb for a prefect during a rebellion. As magistrate, he executed corrupt officials and died in office. Chen Chong, from Yuzhang, was generous, paying a colleague's debts and taking blame for a missing pair of pants. He resigned when a friend was deposed and died as a censor. Lei Yi, from Yuzhang, refused gold and took blame for a colleague's crime. He later feigned madness to avoid office and died as Nandun Order. Fan Ran, from Chenliu, was a maverick who rejected世俗 norms. He refused to travel with a friend to avoid appearing sycophantic. He lived simply, selling divination and farming. During the party ban, he was imprisoned. He died at seventy-four, instructing a simple burial. Dai Jiu, from Kuaiji, endured brutal torture while refusing to falsely accuse a prefect. His resilience impressed the interrogator, who released him. He died of illness. Zhao Bao, from Ganling, was ashamed of his eunuch relative. As prefect, he fought Xianbei invaders who captured his mother. She urged him to fight, and he did, but she was killed. He died of grief. Xiang Xu, from Hanoi, was eccentric, wearing disheveled hair and shouting. He taught disciples and later became Prime Minister of Zhao, where he was solemn. He was executed for allegedly conspiring with Zhang Jiao. Lang Fu, from Guanghan, prayed for rain by threatening self-immolation, which brought rain.

translation:
Zhongfu from Henan came to the county and cited Liu Yi as a meritorious official. Liu Yi believed that Zhongfu was the son of a famous feudal lord and came to serve.
Zhong Fu believed that Liu Yi had chosen the right time to become an official and respected him very much.
Relying on Mrs. Cheng's power, Huang Gang of Yangzhai demanded that the mountains and swamps be occupied for planting.
Zhong Fu summoned Liu Yi and asked: "The Cheng family is Guisheng, and if he is not allowed to be around the emperor, he is afraid of causing resentment. If he gives it to him, it will usurp the interests of the people. What should we do?"
Liu Yi said: Famous mountains and great rivers are not for the sake of people, but for the common people.
If the prefect complies with his request, he will gain a reputation as a flatterer. If he gets into trouble as a result, his master, Shenfu, will not become an orphan.
Zhong Fu listened to Liu Yi's words and refused to give Huang Gang.
So Liu Yi was promoted to be filial and honest, but he refused.
Later, when the Yellow Turban bandits broke out and there was a famine in the counties, Liu Yi helped hundreds of hungry people.
For poor families in the countryside, the dead are helped to bury, and the widows and widowers are helped to marry.
Emperor Xian moved the capital to Xijing, and Liu Yi was appointed as the chief minister.
At this time, thieves were everywhere and the roads were blocked, making it very difficult to reach the post.
Liu Yi left at night and hid during the day before arriving in Chang'an.
The imperial edict commended his loyalty and diligence, and he was specially appointed as Yiyi Lang and promoted to Chenliu Grand Administrator.
Liu Yi lost all his treasures, leaving only his carriage and horses, and rode back eastward.
After leaving the customs for hundreds of miles, I saw a scholar-official died of illness on the roadside with no one to bury him, so he traded a horse for a coffin and took off his clothes for burial.
He met his old friends who were hungry on the road, and couldn't bear to abandon them, so he killed the ox driving them to help them.
Many people asked him not to do this. Liu Yi said: "You are not a person with lofty ideals if you don't save someone in the face of death."
Because they all starved to death.
◆Biography of Wang Lie, courtesy name Yanfang, a native of Taiyuan.
He studied under Chen Chen when he was young and was famous for his righteous deeds.
There was a cattle thief in the village. The owner of the cattle caught the thief. The thief apologized and said, "I am willing to accept the punishment. Please don't let Wang Yanfang know about it."
When Wang Lie heard about it, he sent someone to thank him and gave him six feet of cloth.
Someone asked him the reason for this, and Wang Lie said: The thief is afraid that I will know his sins, and he is ashamed.
Since he has a sense of shame, he must be able to change his evil ways and do good, so he is encouraged in this way.
Later, an old man lost his sword on the road. A passerby saw it and stood guard there. At night, the old man came back and found the sword. Strangely, he asked the man what his name was, but he didn't answer. So he told Wang Lie about this.
Wang Lie sent people to investigate and found out that it was the man who had stolen the cattle before.
When those who were arguing about the merits of the lawsuit were about to ask Wang Lie to judge the rights and wrongs, some walked back to the road, and some came back when they saw Wang Lie's house.
summary: Liu Yi, from Yingchuan, was generous, giving his car to a mourner and helping the poor. He refused office but later served as chief minister during Emperor Xian's reign. He sold his horse to bury a stranger and starved to death helping friends. Wang Lie, from Taiyuan, was known for his virtue, encouraging a thief to reform by giving him cloth. He fled to Liaodong during the Yellow Turban rebellion and died there.

translation:
◆Biography of Wang Chong, Wang Chong, courtesy name Zhongren, was from Shangyu, Kuaiji. His ancestors moved here from Yuancheng, Wei County.
Wang Chong's father died when he was young, and his fellow villagers praised him for his filial piety.
Later he went to the capital to study at Taixue, where he was taught by Ban Biao, a Fufeng native.
He is well-read and does not stick to chapters.
His family was poor and had no books, so he often went to Luoyang bookstore to read the books for sale, and he could memorize them after reading them once. So he understood the theories of various schools of thought.
Later, he returned to his hometown and lived in seclusion to teach.
He served as a meritorious official in the prefecture and county, but because he repeatedly advised the superiors, he left due to disagreements.
Wang Chong likes to make comments, which may sound weird at first, but if you think about it carefully, they are reasonable and well-founded.
He thought that those Confucian scholars with little knowledge clung to the chapters and sentences in the books and lost the essence and true meaning of the books. So I closed my door and thought deeply, and declined those social gatherings of congratulations and condolences. There were knives and pens placed on the door, windows and walls of his home. He wrote 85 chapters of "Lunheng", totaling more than 200,000 words, explaining the similarities and differences of objects and correcting people's doubts about certain things at that time.
Dong Qin, the governor, recruited him to work and was later transferred to Zhizhong. He resigned and returned home.
His friend Xie Yiwu from the same county wrote to the court recommending Wang Chong's talents. Suzong specially issued an edict to recruit him, but he was unable to make the trip due to illness.
When he was nearly seventy years old, his memory failed. Due to exhaustion of energy, he wrote sixteen chapters of "The Book of Cultivation of Nature", which discusses the principles of controlling cravings, maintaining the spirit, and guarding one's mind.
During the Yongyuan period, he died of illness at home.
◆Wang Fu Chuan, Wang Fu, Bye Xin, a native of Linjing, Anding.
When he was young, he was studious and ambitious, and was good friends with Ma Rong, Dou Zhang, Zhang Heng, Cui Yuan, etc.
The custom in Anping was to look down on the children of the younger wives, but Wang Fu did not have a maternal wife, so the village looked down upon him.
Since Emperor He and Emperor An, it was popular to serve as an official on the move, and powerful people recommended each other. However, Wang Fu was upright and unconventional, so he could not become an official.
But he felt very uncomfortable in his heart, so he lived in seclusion at home and wrote more than 30 books to satirize the political gains and losses at that time. He did not want his name to be known by others, so the book was called "The Theory of Qianfu".
The book denounces the shortcomings of the time and discusses customs and sentiments, from which the political fashion of the time can be seen. Here are five of them: 1. "Guizhong Pian" The emperor respects God the most, and God loves people the most.
Now that human ministers are entrusted by the king to govern the people whom God loves, how can they not allow them to be raised and relieved safely and smoothly?
Therefore, when a gentleman is in a position, he should think about how to benefit others, and those who are above should think about how to introduce wise people. Therefore, those who are in the upper position should not be resentful when they are below, and those who are in the front and behind will not be disobedient.
summary: Wang Chong, courtesy name Zhongren, was from Shangyu, Kuaiji, though his ancestors had moved from Yuancheng, Wei County. His father died when he was young, and he was praised for his filial piety. He studied at Taixue in the capital under Ban Biao of Fufeng. Despite his family's poverty and lack of books, he frequently visited Luoyang bookstores, memorizing texts after a single reading, which allowed him to master various schools of thought. He later returned home to teach and served as a meritorious official, but left due to disagreements with his superiors after repeatedly offering advice. Wang Chong criticized Confucian scholars for clinging to textual details while losing deeper meanings. He secluded himself, placing writing tools throughout his home, and composed 85 chapters of "Lunheng" (over 200,000 words) to explain phenomena and correct contemporary misconceptions. Governor Dong Qin recruited him, but he resigned. His friend Xie Yiwu recommended him to the court, and Emperor Suzong issued an edict for his service, but illness prevented him from traveling. Near age seventy, with failing memory, he wrote sixteen chapters of "The Book of Cultivation of Nature" on self-discipline and spiritual preservation. He died at home during the Yongyuan period. Wang Fu, courtesy name Xin, was from Linjing, Anding. Studious and ambitious, he befriended Ma Rong, Dou Zhang, Zhang Heng, and Cui Yuan. Because he was born to a secondary wife, his village looked down on him. During the reigns of Emperors He and An, when powerful families recommended each other for office, Wang Fu's uprightness prevented him from becoming an official. Distressed, he secluded himself and wrote over thirty books criticizing contemporary politics, calling his work "The Theory of Qianfu" to remain anonymous. His writings denounced societal ills. He argued that officials should govern justly, as heaven loves the people, and that stealing official positions for personal gain was worse than robbery. He criticized the neglect of agriculture, noting that in Luoyang, merchants outnumbered farmers tenfold, creating widespread poverty. He condemned extravagant dress, wasteful religious practices, and lavish funerals where families spent fortunes on coffins and burials while neglecting living parents. He advocated for proper talent selection, arguing that wise men existed but were improperly used, and criticized judicial corruption where the poor could not obtain justice against wealthy officials. He opposed frequent amnesties, which he believed emboldened criminals while harming the virtuous.

Why?
Anyone who dares to do bad things must have extraordinary abilities and be able to please their superiors.
For example, stuffing more ill-gotten gains and saying more things to please others to soften them up. If someone is not as honest and upright as the fifth ethical person, who wouldn't care about money?
Some people often say: If sins are not pardoned for a long time, bad people will flourish and officials will be unable to stop them. We should use various methods to enlighten them to break them up.
This is because we do not understand the fundamental source of political chaos and the causes of misfortunes and blessings.
Later, Huangfugui, the general who conquered the Liao Dynasty, was dismissed from his official post and returned to Anding. The people from the same town who used their goods and wealth to buy the governor of Yanmen also left their jobs and went home, and went to see Huangfugui with their business cards.
Huangfu Gui lay sleeping and did not come out to greet the man. After the man had already entered the door, he asked: "You used to eat wild goose meat in the county magistrate Renli. It tasted good, didn't it?"
Soon, someone reported that Wang Fu was at the door asking to see him.
Huangfu Gui had always heard of Wang Fu's reputation, so he got up quickly, with his clothes not tied yet, put on his shoes and went out to greet him. He held Wang Fu's hand and entered the room, sitting with him very happily.
People at that time said this: A governor with two thousand stones is not worth a common man.
That is to say, the moral character of scholars is noble.
Wang Fu finally stopped serving as an official and died at home.
◆Zhong Changtong, also known as Zhong Changtong, was born in Gaoping, Shanyang.
When he was young, he was studious, read extensively in books, and was good at diction.
When he was more than 20 years old, he studied in Qingzhou, Xuzhou, Bingzhou and Jizhou. Most of his friends thought he was different from ordinary people.
Gao Gan, the governor of Bingzhou, was Yuan Shao's nephew. He had always been noble and famous, attracting wanderers from all over, and many scholars attached themselves to him.
Zhong Changtong passed by Gao Gan, who entertained him well and asked about the major events at that time.
Changtong said to the senior officials: You have great ambitions but no great talents. You like to make friends with scholars but cannot choose talents. Therefore, I am worried about you. Please take this as a warning.
The senior cadre often felt that he was good. If he didn't accept his advice, Chang Tong would leave.
Not long after, the high officials rebelled against Bingzhou and were defeated.
The scholars of Bingzhou and Jizhou all differed in their ability to know people.
Zhong Changtong was a man of suave nature, who dared to speak out without caring about trivial matters, and who spoke impertinently in silence. Some people at that time called him Kuang Sheng.
Whenever summoned by the state or county, he often complained that he was ill and would not go away.
It is often thought that those who lobby the emperor just want to establish themselves and make a name for themselves, but fame does not last forever and life is easy to perish. They can enjoy themselves by wandering and admiring. They want to build a house and live in a clear land to satisfy their ambitions.
His argument is: Suppose you live in a large house with fertile land, with mountains on the back and water on the side, surrounded by ditches and ponds, surrounded by bamboos and trees, with a field in front and an orchard in the back.
summary: Wang Fu never served as an official and died at home. His contemporary Huangfu Gui famously demonstrated respect for him by rushing to greet him while ignoring a wealthy former governor, leading people to say that "a governor with two thousand stones is not worth a common man." Zhong Changtong was from Gaoping, Shanyang. Studious and well-read, he was considered extraordinary by his peers. When visiting Gao Gan, the governor of Bingzhou, he warned that Gao had great ambitions but insufficient talent and poor judgment in choosing associates. Gao ignored this advice and later rebelled and was defeated.

Boats and carts can replace the labor of traveling and wading, which is enough to relieve the four-body struggle.
Raising relatives has a delicious meal, and the wife does not have to work hard.
When good friends arrive, they will be entertained with wine and food, festive events, and pigs and sheep will be killed to honor them.
Take a walk in Qiyuan, play in the plain forest, wash your feet on the shore of clear water, enjoy the cool breeze, go fishing, and shoot birds.
Sing under the dancing beauties, chant in the high hall.
Relax in the boudoir, think about the mystery of Lao Tzu, breathe fresh air, and seek to be like a perfect person.
Talking about Taoism and writing with a few close friends, looking down at the sky and the earth, commenting on the rights and wrongs of people.
Play the "South Wind" harp and sing the wonderful music of Qing Dynasty and Shang Dynasty.
A carefree life, looking between heaven and earth.
He will not be blamed at that time, and his life will be preserved forever.
In this way, one can rise above the sky and be beyond the universe.
Are you still envious of entering the imperial family?
He also wrote two poems to express his ambition. The poem says: The flying birds leave their remains, the singing cicada sheds its body.
The flying snake abandons its scales and armor, and the divine dragon loses its head and horns.
A great person can change, a noble person can transcend vulgarity.
Riding on the clouds without a saddle or bridle, riding the wind with no satisfaction.
The hanging dew becomes a tent curtain, and the Zhang Xiao becomes a scarf.
Hangzhou serves as dinner, and Nine Suns replace candles.
The stars are as bright as pearls, and the morning glow is as smooth as jade.
Liuhe allows me to roam as much as I want.
People and things can be left behind, so why be cramped.
Although the road is flat, there are only a few people there.
There is no right or wrong in anything you want, and there is nothing wrong with what you want.
It has been a circuitous and complex process since ancient times.
No matter what I do, the most important thing is still with me.
Put your worries in heaven and bury them in the earth.
The rebellion was dispersed in the Five Classics, and Heaven abandoned the Wind and Ya.
Baijia is too messy, please use a fire.
The ambition to fight is in the mountains, and the heart is in the sea.
The vitality becomes a boat, and the breeze can be the rudder.
Ao Xiang is in Taiqing, Zongyi is in Rongye.
The minister ordered Xun to be surprised when he heard Zhong Changtong's name, so he appointed him as minister.
Later he participated in the military affairs of Prime Minister Cao Cao.
Whenever he talks about ancient and modern times and the customs and practices of that time, he often sighs with anger.
Because the treatise is called "Chang Yan", it has a total of thirty-four chapters and more than 100,000 words.
In the year when Emperor Xian abdicated, Zhong Changtong died at the age of forty-one.
summary: Zhong Changtong was unconventional and outspoken, earning the nickname "Kuang Sheng" (Mad Scholar). He frequently declined government summons by claiming illness. He valued personal freedom over official service, describing an ideal life of leisure with fertile land, comfortable housing, family, friends, entertainment, and philosophical contemplation. He wrote poems expressing his desire to transcend worldly concerns. Minister Xun Yu appointed him, and he later served under Prime Minister Cao Cao. He wrote "Chang Yan," consisting of 34 chapters and over 100,000 words, expressing his critical views on contemporary society. He died at age forty-one during the year Emperor Xian abdicated.

translation:
Wang Chang was a prince, a native of Handan, Zhao State.
He was originally a fortune-teller and fortune-teller, and he had some knowledge of astronomy and calculus. He often thought that Hebei had the aura of the Son of Heaven.
At this time, Liu Lin, the son of King Mu of Zhao, loved magic and practiced chivalry between Zhao and Wei. He had many connections with powerful and lawless people, and Wang Chang was friendly with him.
At first, when Wang Mang usurped the throne, there was a man in Chang'an who claimed to be Liu Ziyu, the son of Emperor Cheng, and Wang Mang killed him.
Wang Lang relied on this clue and falsely claimed that he was the true son of the emperor, saying: My mother was a singer who became the emperor. One time when she was going down to the palace, she suddenly collapsed.
When Ziyu was twelve years old, a doctor named Li Manqing took him to Shu. When he was seventeen, he arrived in Danyang. When he was twenty, he returned to Chang'an. He traveled between Zhongshan and Yanzhao, waiting for the arrival of the right time.
Liu Lin and others were even more confused, so they conspired with Li Yu, Zhang Shen and others to plan to support Wang Lang.
It happened that people said that Red Eyebrow was about to cross the Yellow River, so Liu Lin and others declared that Red Eyebrow was coming, and asked Liu Ziyu to see the reaction of the people, and many people believed it.
In December of the first year of Gengshi, Liu Lin and others led hundreds of chariots and riders, entered Handan City early in the morning, stopped at the palace, and made Wang Lang the emperor.
Liu Lin was the Prime Minister, Li Yu was the Grand Sima, and Zhang Shen was the General.
Send generals to capture Youzhou and Jizhou respectively.
Send the proclamation to the prefectures and counties and say: "I order the governors of each prefecture and the prefect of the prefecture: I am Liu Ziyu, the son of Emperor Xiaocheng."
In the past, I was harmed by the Zhao family. After Wang Mang usurped the Han Dynasty, he killed the fake Ziyu. Fortunately, someone who knew the destiny protected me, and I was able to escape from the riverside and disappear between Zhao and Wei.
Wang Mang's theft of the throne offended Heaven, and Heaven blessed us with the Han Dynasty, so we sent Zhai Yi, the governor of Dongjun, and Liu Xin, the Marquis of Yanxiang, to support the attack and go between the Hu people and the Han people.
Everyone in the world, on the shores of the earth, knows that I am hidden in the world.
The Liu brothers in Nanyue are all my pioneers.
I looked up at the astronomical sky and knew that God wanted me to rise here, so I ascended the throne of Zhao Palace on Renchen this month.
The auspicious atmosphere is fumigating, and the rain falls at the right time.
I heard that for a country's leader, the son inherits the throne from his father. This is a legal system that has not changed since ancient times.
Liu Shenggong didn't know I was there, so he temporarily became emperor.
They are all helping me by raising armies for justice, and they should allocate land so that their descendants can enjoy happiness.
I have ordered Duke Sheng and Prefect Zhai to hurry up and come to me with all the heroes.
Some people suspect that the governor and the two thousand stones were set up by the Holy Gong. They did not see my stagnation and suffering, and some did not know where to go. The strong relied on their own strength, and the weak were afraid and confused.
summary: Wang Chang, a prince from Handan in Zhao State, was originally a fortune-teller with knowledge of astronomy. He believed Hebei had the aura of a Son of Heaven. Liu Lin, son of King Mu of Zhao, was a chivalrous man with connections to powerful figures, and Wang Chang befriended him. After Wang Mang usurped the throne and killed a man claiming to be Liu Ziyu, son of Emperor Cheng, Wang Lang falsely claimed to be the true son. He fabricated a story about his mother, a singer who became the emperor's consort, and his escape with a doctor. Liu Lin and others, including Li Yu and Zhang Shen, conspired to support Wang Lang. In December of the first year of Gengshi, they entered Handan, made Wang Lang emperor, and appointed Liu Lin as Prime Minister, Li Yu as Grand Sima, and Zhang Shen as General. They sent proclamations to prefectures, declaring Wang Lang as Liu Ziyu and calling for support. Wang Lang's claims gained traction, and much of northern China submitted to him.

translation:
At first, Su Mao, a native of Chenliu, attacked the general for the purpose of reform and guarded Luoyang with Zhu Tuna and others.
After Zhu Jun surrendered to the Han Dynasty, Su Mao also returned to Guangwu. Guangwu sent Su Mao and Gai Yan to attack Liu Yong together. When there was disharmony among the troops, Su Mao rebelled, killed the governor of Huaiyang, plundered several counties, occupied Guangle and declared himself a vassal to Liu Yong.
Liu Yong took Su Mao as the Grand Sima and King of Huaiyang.
Gai Yan then besieged Suiyang for several months and captured Suiyang. Liu Yong and his family fled Yu County.
The Yu people rebelled and killed Liu Yong's mother, wife and children. Liu Yong and dozens of his men fled to Qiao County.
Su Mao, Jiaoqiang, and Zhou Jian joined forces to rescue Liu Yong, but were defeated by Gai Yan. Su Mao rushed back to Guangle, while Jiaoqiang and Zhou Jian followed Liu Yong to protect Huling.
In the spring of the third year of Jianwu, Liu Yong sent envoys to establish Zhang Bu as King of Qi and Dong Xian as King of Haixi.
Guangwu then sent Grand Sima Wu Han and others to surround Su Mao in Guangle. Zhou Jian led his troops to rescue Su Mao. Sum Mao and Zhou Jian were defeated, abandoned Guangle City and returned to Huling, while the Suiyang people in turn gathered the city to welcome Liu Yong.
Wu Han, Gai Yan and other combined forces surrounded Suiyang and the city ran out of food. Liu Yong, Su Mao and Zhou Jian fled to Zanhuang County.
The generals pursued him urgently. Liu Yong beheaded Qingwu and surrendered. Qingwu was granted the title of lord.
Su Mao and Zhou Jian fled to Chuihui and jointly established Liu Yong's son Liu Yu as King of Liang.
Jiaoqiang fled back to the west to defend himself.
In the autumn of the fourth year of Jianwu, Guangwu sent the captured general Ma Wu and the cavalry captain Wang Ba to surround Liu Yu and Zhou Jian in Chuihui. Su Mao led five soldiers to rescue them. Liu Yu and Zhou Jian also sent troops to fight Ma Wu and others, but they were defeated. However, Zhou Jian's nephew Zhou Song rebelled and closed the city gates to resist.
Su Mao, Zhou Jian, and Liu Yu all fled. Zhou Jian died on the road. Su Mao fled to Xiapi to join Dong Xian, and Liu Yu became the best.
In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, Guangwu sent General Du Mao to attack Jiaoqiang and defend against the west. Jiaoqiang and Liu Yu fled to Dong Xian.
At this time, General Pang Meng of Pingdi rebelled, so he conquered Gaiyan, led his troops to join forces with Dong Xian, named himself King Dongping, and stationed troops in the north of Taoxiang.
Pang Meng is from Shanyang.
At first, he died among the soldiers in Xiajiang.
Gengshi ascended the throne and appointed him as the shepherd of Jizhou, and ordered him to lead the army under the command of Shangshu Ling Xie Gong to defeat Wang Lang.
After Xie Gong failed, Pang Meng surrendered. Guangwu ascended the throne and made him his attendant.
Pang Meng was humble and docile, and was loved by Guangwu.
Guangwu often praised and said: "The person who can entrust an underage orphan with a mission is Pang Meng." He was worshiped as General Pingdi and jointly attacked Dong Xian with Gai Yan.
At this time, the edict was only issued to Gai Yan but not to Pang Meng. Pang Meng thought that Gai Yan had said bad things about him, so he became suspicious and rebelled.
After hearing this, Guangwu was furious and personally led his army to attack Pang Meng.
Guangwu wrote to the generals: I always thought that Pang Meng was a trustworthy and loyal minister. Wouldn't the generals laugh at my words?
Pang Meng, an old thief, should be exterminated.
You each have strong horses and strong troops, and join forces in Suiyang! When Dong Xian heard that Guangwu was attacking Pang Meng, he went to Xiapi with Liu Yu, Su Mao, and Jiaoqiang, and returned to Lanling. He asked Su Mao and Jiaoqiang to assist Pang Meng, and they combined 30,000 troops to besiege Taocheng.
summary: The next year, Guangwu attacked Wang Lang, besieging Julu and then Handan. Wang Lang sent Du Wei to negotiate, claiming to be the true son of Emperor Cheng, but Guangwu refused. After a 20-day siege, Li Li, Wang Lang's Shaofu, rebelled and opened the city gates. Wang Lang fled but was killed. Liu Yong, an eighth-generation grandson of King Xiao of Liang, was enfeoffed after Gengshi's ascension. He raised troops, captured 28 cities, and allied with Dong Xian and Zhang Bu. After Gengshi's failure, Liu Yong proclaimed himself emperor. Guangwu sent Gai Yan to attack Liu Yong. Su Mao, initially serving Gengshi, surrendered to Guangwu but later rebelled and joined Liu Yong. Gai Yan besieged Suiyang, capturing it, but Liu Yong fled. After several battles, Liu Yong was killed, and his son Liu Yu was briefly established as king before being defeated. Dong Xian and Pang Meng also rebelled but were eventually killed. Zhang Bu, from Langfu, gathered troops and declared himself General Wuwei. He allied with Liu Yong and later killed Fulong, Guangwu's envoy. Guangwu attacked Zhang Bu, who was defeated and surrendered, but later fled and was killed.

translation:
So he packed up his gold and jade clothes, packed them at Peng Chong's residence, prepared six horses, and asked his wife to sew two parcels.
After dark, he untied Peng Chong's hand and ordered him to tell the city gate general in his own handwriting: "I am sending Zi Mi to the residence of Lan Qing, the queen of the family. Open the door quickly and let them out. Don't stay." After writing, he beheaded Peng Chong and his wife, put them in a bag, and immediately left the city with the note to pay homage to Guangwu.
He was named Unjust Marquis.
Early the next morning, the door was tightly closed, and the officials climbed in through the wall. They were shocked and horrified when they saw Peng Chong's body.
His minister Han Li and others jointly established Peng Chong's son Peng Wu as king, and his son Lan Qing as general.
Han Li, the national counselor, beheaded Peng Wu's head and took him to the place where General Zhenglu was offering sacrifices to surrender.
Peng Chong's clan was wiped out.
Lu Fang, whose courtesy name was Junqi, was from Sanshui County, Anding County, and lived in Zuoguzhong.
During the reign of Wang Mang, everyone in the world missed Han De, so Lu Fang falsely claimed that she was Liu Wenbo, the great-grandson of Emperor Wu.
It is said that the sister of the great-grandmother Hunxie King of Xiongnu Guli was the Empress of Emperor Wu and gave birth to three sons.
During the Jiang Chong Rebellion, the prince was killed, the queen was convicted and died, the middle son Ciqing fled to Changling, and the boy Huiqing fled to Zuogu.
General Huo made him a second minister and welcomed him back.
Hui Qing could not leave, so he lived in Zuogu and gave birth to a son, Sun Qing, who had a son, Wen Bo.
Lu Fang often used these words to deceive and confuse Anding.
At the end of Wang Mang's reign, he started an army with the Qiang and Hu from the state of Sanshui.
Gengshi arrived in Chang'an and recruited Lu Fang as the cavalry captain to calm him and pacify the west of Anding.
After the failure of Gengshi, the heroes of Sanshui jointly decided that Lu Fang was a descendant of the Liu family and should inherit the ancestral temple. So they jointly appointed Lu Fang as the general and king of Xiping, and sent envoys to make peace with the Western Qiang and Xiongnu.
Shanyu said: The Xiongnu and the Han were originally brothers.
Later, when the Xiongnu weakened, Huhanxie Shanyu surrendered to the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty sent troops to protect him, and the Shanyu became a vassal for all generations.
Now that Han Zuo has been defeated, and the Liu family has returned to me, I should also establish him and let him respect me. So he sent King Julin to lead thousands of horses to meet Lu Fang. Lu Fang, his brother Lu Qin, and his brother Lu Cheng all went to the Xiongnu.
The Chanyu established Lu Fang as Emperor of the Han Dynasty.
With Lu Cheng as the Zhonglang general, he led the Huns cavalry back to Anding.
At first, Li Xing and Sui Yu from Wuyuan, Tian Sa from Shuofang, and Shi Tun and Min Kan from Daijun each raised their own troops and called themselves generals.
In the fourth year of Jianwu, Shanyu sent King Wulou Qiequ to Wuyuan fortress to make peace with Li Xing and others, and told Li Xing that he wanted to make Lu Fang return to the Han Dynasty and become the emperor of the Han Dynasty.
In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, Li Xing and Min Kan led troops to the Shanyu Courtyard to welcome Lu Fang, and they entered the fortress together and made Jiuyuan County their capital.
The five counties of Wuyuan, Shuofang, Yunzhong, Dingxiang and Yanmen were plundered. They all set up prefectures and magistrates, and fought with the Xiongnu. The northern frontier was invaded and suffered.
In the sixth year of Jianwu, Lu Fang's general Jia Lan led Hu Qi to kill Liu Xing, the prefect of Daijun.
Lu Fang later executed the brothers Li Xing, the prefect of Wuyuan, so that Tian Sa, the prefect of Shuofang, and Qiao Hu, the prefect of Yunzhong, were frightened, rebelled against Lu Fang, and surrendered with the whole county. Guangwu ordered them to remain the prefects of the original county as before.
Later, Grand Sima Wu Han and Hussar General Du Mao attacked Lu Fang several times, but failed to conquer it.
In the twelfth year of Jianwu's reign, Lu Fang and Jia Lan jointly attacked Yunzhong, but could not capture it for a long time. Their general Sui Yu stayed in Jiuyuan, hoping to force Lu Fang to surrender.
Lu Fang knew that his subordinates were affiliated with the Han Dynasty and that their confidants were rebelling from within, so he abandoned his baggage and fled to the Xiongnu with more than ten cavalry. All his subordinates joined Sui Yu.
Sui Yu then went to the capital with his envoy Cheng Xun. Emperor Guangwu worshiped Sui Yu as the governor of Wuyuan, granted him the title of Marquis of Hu, and followed his younger brother Sui Xian as the Marquis of Wujin.
In the 16th year of Jianwu's reign, Lu Fang returned to Gaoliu County and sent an envoy to Min Kan's brother Min Lin to request his surrender.
The emperor then appointed Lu Fang as the acting king, Min Kan as the acting prime minister, and Min Lin as the acting Taifu. He gave him 20,000 pieces of silk, so that he could live in peace with the Xiongnu.
Lu Fang Shangshu Xie En said: My minister Lu Fang entrusted me with the late emperor's body, which was abandoned at the border. The Han Dynasty Sheji was abolished by Wang Mang. This is the worry of the descendants of the Liu family. They should rise up and kill the national traitors together. Therefore, I am connected with the Qiang Rong in the west and the Xiongnu in the north.
The Shanyu does not forget his old virtues, and he has the right to appoint me to help him. At that time, there were wars and revolutions everywhere.
I dare not be greedy and covet, but only hope to flatter the ancestral temple and establish the state. Therefore, I have usurped the title of Han Emperor for more than ten years. This is a crime worthy of death.
summary: Li Xian, from Xuchang, declared himself King of Huainan and later emperor. Guangwu attacked and captured Shu County, leading to Li Xian's death. Peng Chong, from Wan County, served as a county official and later fled to Yuyang. He supported Guangwu but became resentful when his rewards were insufficient. He rebelled, attacked Zhufu, and allied with the Xiongnu. He declared himself King of Yan but was killed by his servants. Lu Fang, from Sanshui, falsely claimed to be Liu Wenbo, a descendant of Emperor Wu. He allied with the Xiongnu and declared himself emperor. He fought with Guangwu's forces but eventually surrendered, though he later rebelled again and died among the Xiongnu. The historian comments that the Liu family's legacy endured due to the deep kindness of Gaozu and Xiaowen, and that the rebels like Wang, Liu, Zhang, Li, Peng, and Lu merely took advantage of the situation without true foresight or strategy.

translation:
◆Ban Biao's biography, Ban Biao, courtesy name Shupi, was born in Anling, Fufeng.
His grandfather, Ban Kuang, served as a captain of the Yue Cavalry School when he became emperor.
His father, Ban Zhi, served as the prefect of Guangping during the reign of Emperor Ai.
Ban Biao has a serious personality and likes traditional culture.
When he was in his twenties, Gengshi was defeated and fled, and there was chaos near the capital.
At that time, Wei Xiao led everyone to revolt in Tianshui, and Ban Biao followed him to seek refuge.
Once, Wei Xiao asked Ban Biao: "In the past, the Zhou Dynasty was destroyed, the Warring States Period was full of disputes, and the world was torn apart. It took several generations to stabilize."
Will the combination of verticality and horizontality appear again today, or will it be a destiny for a certain person?
Please give me your opinion, sir. Ban Biao replied: The decline and prosperity of the Zhou Dynasty was different from that of the Han Dynasty.
In the past, the Zhou Dynasty was divided into five categories: Duke, Marquis, Uncle, Son, and Male. The princes controlled their own territories and governed their own affairs, just like a big tree, with weak roots and luxuriant branches and leaves. Therefore, later, when there were vertical and horizontal alliances, it was the situation that prompted it.
The Han Dynasty inherited the system of the Qin Dynasty and changed the feudal system into a system of prefectures and counties. The monarch had autocratic authority and his subordinates did not have the power to control the country for a hundred years.
When Emperor Cheng arrived, he used the power of his relatives to reign. Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping reigned for a short time. The three emperors had no children, so Wang Mang usurped the throne and stole the title of the country.
The danger comes from above, and the harm is not as bad as below. Therefore, after Wang Mang actually usurped the throne, everyone in the world stretched their necks and sighed.
For more than ten years, there have been disturbances at home and abroad, and actions have been taken by people near and far, each under the banner of the Liu family, and they have responded in unison.
Nowadays, the states and counties ruled by heroes and heroes do not have the traditional capital of the Seven Kingdoms, but the common people miss the kindness of the Han Dynasty with one voice. The development trend can be imagined. Wei Xiaodao: Sir, your analysis of the situation between the Zhou Dynasty and the Han Dynasty is correct; as for saying that the Han family will definitely revive because the stupid people are accustomed to the Liu surname, it is not necessarily true.
In the past, when the Qin Dynasty lost the world, it was like a deer running away. Liu Bang chased the deer and caught it. Who knew there was a Han Dynasty at that time?
On the one hand, Ban Biao hated Wei Xiao's arrogance, and on the other hand, he lamented the difficult situation, so he wrote an article "On the King's Mandate", believing that Han De succeeded Tang Yao, as evidenced by the efficacious king's talisman, and that the king ascended the throne, not by deception. He wanted to use this to impress Wei Xiao, but Wei Xiao never realized it, so he avoided Hexi.
Dou Rong, the general of Hexi Province, used him as an official, treated him with great respect, and treated him as a mentor and friend. Ban Biao made suggestions for Dou Rong, served the Han Dynasty, and led the Xihe area to resist Wei Xiao. Later, Dou Rong was ordered to return to the capital. Emperor Guangwu asked: Who was your adviser on the memorial you submitted? Dou Rong replied: It was all done by my colleague Ban Biao. The emperor had always heard that Ban Biao was very talented, so he summoned Ban Biao, promoted him to be the Secretary Maocai, and asked him to be the Order of Xuzhou. However, he was unable to take the post due to illness.
Later, he went several times in response to Sangong's orders.
summary: Ban Biao, courtesy name Shupi, was born in Anling, Fufeng. His grandfather Ban Kuang served as a captain of the Yue Cavalry School, and his father Ban Zhi was prefect of Guangping. Ban Biao had a serious personality and valued traditional culture. In his twenties, during the chaos following Gengshi's defeat, he followed Wei Xiao to Tianshui. When Wei Xiao asked whether the Warring States period's vertical and horizontal alliances would recur or if a single ruler would unify the realm, Ban Biao explained that the Zhou Dynasty's feudal system led to weak central control and allowed such alliances, while the Han Dynasty's prefecture and county system centralized power. He argued that the Han's decline stemmed from above, not below, and that after Wang Mang's usurpation, people longed for the Han, leading to widespread uprisings under the Liu family banner. Wei Xiao disagreed, citing the Qin collapse as an unpredictable event. Ban Biao, disturbed by Wei Xiao's arrogance, wrote "On the King's Mandate" to argue that Han virtue succeeded Tang Yao, but Wei Xiao remained unmoved, so Ban Biao fled to Hexi. There, Dou Rong employed him as an official, treating him with great respect. Ban Biao advised Dou Rong to serve the Han and resist Wei Xiao. When Dou Rong returned to the capital, Emperor Guangwu learned of Ban Biao's role and summoned him, promoting him to Secretary Maocai and appointing him as Order of Xuzhou, though illness prevented him from taking the post. Ban Biao later served under the Three Dukes.
