translation:
Ban Biao was both talented and good at writing, so he concentrated on historical records.
During the reign of Emperor Wu, Sima Qian wrote the "Historical Records". Since the Taichu period, there has been no writing. Later, some good people connected the deeds at that time, but the writing style is vulgar and is not worthy of being a follow-up to the "Historical Records".
Ban Biao then continued to collect the historical relics of the previous dynasty, and also read some anecdotes from the side, and wrote dozens of later biographies, commenting on the gains and losses with reference to the previous history.
The summary of the article reads: During the Tang and Yu dynasties, according to the records of "The Book of Songs" and "The Book of Books", each dynasty had historians to manage classic works. When it came to the vassal states, each country had its own history. Therefore, "Mencius" said that the history of Chu State is called "Mu Shou Chu", the history of Jin State is called "Cheng", and the history of Lu State is called "Spring and Autumn". Their records of history are all the same. In the era of Duke Dinggong and Duke Ai of Lu, Zuo Qiuming, a gentleman of the state of Lu, collected the history of that time and wrote thirty chapters of "The Biography of the Zuo Family", and based on various materials, he wrote twenty-one chapters of "Guoyu".
There is also a book that records the deeds of emperors, princes, princes, princes and officials from the time of the Yellow Emperor to the Spring and Autumn Period, called "Shiben", with a total of fifteen chapters.
After the Spring and Autumn Period, there were disputes among the seven kingdoms and the Qin State annexed the princes. Thirty-three chapters of "Warring States Policy" were published.
The rise of the Han Dynasty brought peace to the world. Lu Jia, a senior official in Taizhong, recorded the situation at that time and wrote nine chapters of Chu-Han Spring and Autumn Annals.
In the era of Emperor Xiaowu, Taishi ordered Sima Qian to collect "Zuo Shi" and "Guoyu", and delete "Shiben" and "Warring States Policy". According to the current affairs of the Chu and Han states, starting from the Yellow Emperor and going down to the second year of Taishi, he wrote a total of 130 chronicles, family biographies, books, and lists. Ten of them are missing. Sima Qian recorded that from the founding of the Han Dynasty to the last time of Emperor Wu, this is his contribution.
As for the collection of scriptures and biographies, materials scattered among hundreds of schools of thought are found in many rough and schematic parts, which are not as true and detailed as the original ones. It is known for being widely read and widely published, and its discussion is superficial but not solid.
When talking about academics, he praised Huangdi and Laozi and despised the Five Classics; when writing about goods and culture, he despised benevolence and righteousness and was ashamed of poverty; when writing about knight-errants, he despised those who were chaste and heroic and praised those who made meritorious deeds in the world. This is a serious problem, and it harms the righteousness, so it is the reason for being punished by corruption.
However, he is good at describing events, his writing style is fluent but not gorgeous, simple but not crude, his writing quality is commensurate, and he deserves to be regarded as a good historian.
If he were allowed to follow the etiquette and laws of the Five Classics and conform to the saint's standards of right and wrong, that would be enough. Those history books of hundreds of schools all have their merits.
For example, after reading "Zuo Shi", "Guoyu", "Shiben", "Warring States Policy", "Chu-Han Spring and Autumn", and "Tai Shi Gong Shu", people today can know ancient history, and people in future generations can know things of previous generations. It is really the eyes and ears of a saint.
Sima Qian's biography of the emperor is called Benji, his biography of dukes and princes is called his family, and his biography of officials and officials is called his biographies.
He included Xiang Yu and Chen She in this era and his family, while the King of Huainan and the King of Hengshan were demoted to biographies. He wrote them carefully, euphemistically and in a very orderly manner.
Sima Qian's works are based on anecdotes from ancient and modern times, and the historical materials throughout the classics are indeed very extensive.
With one person's energy, the content is complex and heavy, so his collection, deletions and clutter are not enough. There are some redundant words and it is not neat enough.
For example, when writing about Sima Xiangru, list the prefectures and counties and write down his names. As for Xiao He, Cao Shen, Chen Ping, and Dong Zhongshu's contemporaries, do not record their names. Some only write the counties but not the counties. Maybe they did not take it into account.
In the future, when writing history, we must strictly check the facts, modify the words, and unify the style. When writing about aristocratic families, only records and biographies are enough.
An ancient book says: Killing insects is the most important thing: these four words are difficult to understand. Killing people, writing "killing people" means "writing history". It can be used as a standard, translated as "history" is to make people see some standards.
summary: Ban Biao was talented in writing and focused on historical records. After Sima Qian's "Historical Records," no comprehensive history existed for the period after Taichu. Ban Biao collected historical materials and wrote dozens of later biographies, critiquing their merits and flaws. He noted that various states had their own histories, such as "Mu Shou Chu," "Cheng," and "Spring and Autumn." He praised Sima Qian's narrative skill but criticized his bias toward Huang-Lao thought, neglect of the Five Classics, and superficial discussions. Ban Biao emphasized the need for strict factual verification and stylistic consistency in history writing.

translation:
The explanation is barely provided for reference. Pleasure and uprightness are the original meaning of "Spring and Autumn".
Ban Biao was promoted to Situ Yukuang Mansion. At that time, the prince's East Palace had just been established, and various kingdoms were opened at the same time, but there were not enough officials and teachers and guards.
Ban Biao said again: Confucius said: People's natures are similar, but the influence of customs is very different.
Jia Yi believes: If you often deal with good people, you have to do good deeds, just like growing up in Qi, you have to speak Qi dialect. If you often come into contact with evil people, you have to do bad things, just like growing up in Chu country, you have to speak Chu language.
Therefore the sage strictly selects his neighbors, paying special attention to the influence of the environment. In the past, when King Cheng of Zhou was a child, he was assisted by Zhou Gong, Shao Gong, Taishi Yi and others when he was away from home; when he was at court, he was assisted by Dadian, Hongyao, Nangong Shi, San Yisheng and others. His left and right sides did not violate the meaning of etiquette. As soon as King Cheng ascended the throne, the world enjoyed unprecedented peace.
Therefore, "Spring and Autumn" states: If you love your son, you should educate him to follow the right path and not to follow evil ways.
Pride and luxury, lewdness and laziness are the root of evil ways.
"The Book of Songs" says: The good idea left to the grandson is the way of peace and respect.
It refers to the precious legacy left by King Wu of Zhou to King Cheng. After the rise of the Han Dynasty, Taizong sent Chao Cuo to use magic to educate the prince, and Jia Yi used "The Book of Songs" and "The Book of Books" to educate the king of Liang. When Zhongzong came, he also asked Liu Xiang, Wang Bao, Xiao Wangzhi, Zhou Kan and others to use articles and Confucianism to educate people below the East Palace, and they chose the right people to promote their moral character and talents.
Nowadays, although the princes and princes have been studying and practicing rituals and music since they were young, the tutors have not yet encountered talents, and the officials and their families are rarely familiar with the old scriptures.
We should widely select famous Confucian scholars with prestige and understanding of political affairs, and use them as princes and tutors. The officials and subordinates of the East Palace and other kingdoms should be fully matched.
According to the old regulations, the prince has ten counties as Tangmuyi, and has security personnel. He will meet once every five days, sit in the carriage, and check the food. It is not the day of the court, and the servants and Zhongyun will just greet him every day. This shows that he is not casual in his behavior and must pay attention to respect in everything.
After the book was submitted, the emperor accepted it.
Later, Situ Lian was selected as the commander of the capital, and he was loved by the officials and the people.
In the 30th year of Jianwu's reign, Ban Biao died in his official position at the age of 52.
He wrote a total of nine Fu, treatises, books, notes and memorials.
summary: Ban Biao also advised on the selection of tutors for princes, citing historical examples like King Cheng of Zhou and the Han's use of scholars like Chao Cuo and Jia Yi. He recommended choosing prestigious Confucian scholars as tutors and ensuring proper staffing for the Eastern Palace and other kingdoms. The emperor accepted his advice. Ban Biao later served as commander of the capital under Situ Lian, beloved by officials and people. He died in office at age 52, leaving nine works including fu, treatises, and memorials.

translation:
◆Ban Gu's biography, Ban Gu's courtesy name is Meng Jian. When he was nine years old, he could compose sentences and recite poems. When he grew up, he was familiar with classics and all the opinions of hundreds of schools of thought were discussed in depth.
He has no fixed teacher and does not work on the chapters and sentences, but only grasps the general principles. He has a generous and kind personality, is compatible with everyone, and does not think he is superior to others just because he is talented. Some Confucian scholars envy him for this.
In the early years of Yongping, King Cang of Dongping used his relatives to assist the Hussar General, opened the East Pavilion, and admitted the heroes. At this time, Ban Gu was only twenty years old. The former Duke of Zhou and the current generals, as recorded in "Poems" and "Books", are not like you three.
Ancient books say: There must be extraordinary people, and then there will be extraordinary things; there must be extraordinary things, and then there will be extraordinary achievements. Ban Gu was fortunate to be born in the Qingming era, and was at the end of his participation in the audio-visual world. With his smallness as a mole cricket, he privately viewed the greatness of the country's affairs. He really praised the general for having a thousand-year important responsibility, following the footsteps of the ancestors, and embodying the beautiful qualifications. Based on his high-level position, he widely picked up all kinds of things, followed the Six Classics, if white and black are different from each other, there is no end to the pursuit of goodness, he adopts the words of a madman, and does not go against the opinions of a salaryman.
I saw privately that the shogunate was newly opened, with handsome men and women from all over the country. They came forward enthusiastically, regardless of their clothes being turned upside down.
The general should carefully study the actions of Tang and Shang, and observe the recommendations of Yi Yin and Gaotao, so that there is no partiality from far and near, and talents in every corner can know. The purpose is to have an overview of talents, collect wise people, find capable people for the country, and bring peace to the dynasty.
Then the general will cultivate his ambition and spirit, travel in temples, spread his fame to the present, and leave his legacy to the endless generations. I saw that the old minister had long been known as a Confucian scholar. His moral character was the highest in the state. He followed his heart at the age of seventy and did not violate the rules. He was the glory of the Qing temple and a contemporary talent.
Jingzhao offered wine to Jin Feng. He cultivated his moral character at a young age. Even when his hair turned gray, he still kept his original intention. He loved ancient music and Taoism, and was silent and self-sufficient. The beautiful qualities of the ancients cannot be matched by contemporary people. Fufeng rafter Li Yu, Ming Dynasty scriptures, good conduct, taught hundreds of people, lived in Duling, in a thatched house with earthen steps.
Jingzhao and Fufeng counties both invited him, but because his family was poor, he resigned several times due to illness. Review the past and learn the new, be clear-headed in discussion, honest and upright in cultivation, and perfect in conduct. Although he was famous as a Confucian in his previous life, he was highly regarded by the country, Wei, Ping, Kong, and Zhai, and there is no better one.
Respondents evaluate performance and participate in everything. Guo Ji, the governor of Jingzhao, was well-known in the state for his filial piety. His Confucian studies were praised by his disciples, and his achievements in government affairs had special effects.
If you encounter the Ming Dynasty and work under the subordinates, you can advance like a bird and fly high, and retreat like Qiliang and die for your country.
Wang Yong, who was engaged in Jingzhou, had Bian Yan's integrity, coupled with his artistic writings, there was no leading figure in Jingzhou before Wang Yong. In ancient times, when the Duke of Zhou promoted the talents of one party, the other three parties complained, saying, "Why did you put me behind?"
The door of the house should be opened in time so that people far away can be comforted.
Yin Su, the envoy of Hongnong Gongcao, was well-educated, knowledgeable and talented. He could recite three hundred poems and could receive foreign guests.
These six people all have special character and talents, and their moral character is higher than that of the world. If they are accepted, they can assist Gao Ming. This is what Confucius sighed in the autumn of the mountains!
In the past, Bian He offered treasures and had his toes amputated, and Qu Yuan offered loyal advice and finally sank to Miluo. However, He's jade has retained its glory for thousands of years, and Qu Zi's legacy has been praised forever.
I hope that the general will be aware of everything, broaden his horizons, be less humble, and listen more to subordinates, so that there will never be any regrets from Jingshan and Miluo in the dust.
summary: Ban Gu, courtesy name Meng Jian, was a precocious scholar who could compose sentences and recite poems at age nine. As an adult, he mastered classical texts and philosophical schools without adhering to a single teacher, focusing on general principles rather than textual minutiae. He was generous and unassuming, earning admiration from fellow Confucians. During the early Yongping era, King Cang of Dongping, serving as a general, opened the East Pavilion to recruit talents. Twenty-year-old Ban Gu addressed him, praising his extraordinary achievements and urging him to emulate ancient sage-kings in selecting virtuous officials. Ban Gu recommended six exceptional individuals: a retired Confucian elder, Jingzhao wine-offerer Jin Feng, Fufeng scholar Li Yu, Jingzhao governor Guo Ji, Jingzhou officer Wang Yong, and Hongnong clerk Yin Su. He emphasized the importance of recognizing talent without bias, citing historical examples like Bian He and Qu Yuan to warn against neglecting worthy men. King Cang adopted his advice.

translation:
Wang Cang of Dongping adopted Ban Gu's opinion.
His father Ban Biao died and returned to his hometown. Ban Gu thought that the history written by Ban Biao was not detailed enough, so he studied in depth and wanted to complete his father's legacy.
Soon someone wrote a letter to Xian Zong, accusing Ban Gu of secretly changing the history of the country. The imperial court sent an edict to the county, imprisoned Ban Gu in Jingzhao Prison, and confiscated all his books.
First, Su Lang, a man from Fufeng, made false predictions and was imprisoned and died.
Ban Chao, Ban Gu's younger brother, was afraid that Ban Gu would be examined by the county and would not be able to distinguish right from wrong, so he went to the court and was summoned by the emperor to tell all the original meaning of Ban Gu's writings. Later, he was promoted to Lang and secretary of the school.
Ban Gu also wrote about the deeds of heroes, Ping Lin, Xinshi, Gongsun Shu and others, and wrote 28 biographies and records, which were reported to the emperor. The emperor also asked him to complete the history book he had written before.
Ban Gu believed that the Han Dynasty inherited the fate of Tang Yao and established the emperor's empire. As for the Six Dynasties, historians traced the merits and deeds, and privately wrote this chronicle, which was compiled at the end of the Hundred Kings and included in the Qin and Han Dynasties. After the beginning of the Tai Dynasty, it was missing and not recorded, so he explored the previous records, compiled what he heard, and wrote the "Book of Han". From the time of Emperor Gaozu to the death of Wang Mang of Xiaoping, there were ten or two generations, a total of two hundred and thirty years. Their actions were combined with the "Five Classics" and linked up and down, and a total of one hundred chapters of records, records, records and biographies were written in "Spring and Autumn".
Ban Gu began to receive the imperial edict in his middle age in Yongping. He racked his brains and pondered for more than 20 years before writing it in the early years of Jianchu.
Contemporary people attach great importance to his books, and there are many scholars who do not read them. Ban Gu later left his official position due to his mother's death.
In the early years of Yongyuan, General Dou Xian went out to conquer the Xiongnu, using Ban Gu as the central guard and counselor.
When Beidan heard that the Han army was coming out, he sent an envoy to Juyansai. He wanted to continue the Huhanxie story and meet with the emperor, so he asked for an envoy.
Dou Xian sent a letter to General Ban Guxing Zhonglang, leading hundreds of cavalry and captive envoys to come out from Juyan fortress to greet them.
Just as the Huns from the south were covering up the Beiting, Ban Gu arrived at Sequhai. When he heard about the chaos among the captives, he led his troops back.
When Dou Xian failed, Ban Gu was dismissed first.
Ban Gu did not educate his sons. Most of his sons did not abide by the laws, which made the officials very troubled.
At first, Luoyang ordered Zhong Jing to go out for inspection. Ban Gu's domestic slaves interfered with his riding, and the officials scolded him. The slaves cursed others when they were drunk. Zhong Jing was furious, afraid of Dou Xian and did not dare to vent, and he held a grudge in his heart.
When Dou's guests were all arrested and interrogated, Zhong Jing arrested Ban Gu and died in prison.
He was sixty-one years old.
The imperial court issued an edict condemning Zhong Jing and those who resisted the master as officials.
Ban Gu wrote "Dian Yin", "Bin Xi", "Ying Ji", poems, rhymes, inscriptions, edicts, odes, books, articles, notes, treatises, discussions and six words. There are a total of forty-one words in existence.
summary: After his father Ban Biao died, Ban Gu sought to complete his father's incomplete historical work. However, he was accused of secretly altering national history and imprisoned. His brother Ban Chao successfully petitioned the emperor, explaining Ban Gu's intentions. Ban Gu was subsequently promoted to court positions and tasked with writing about heroes and compiling historical records. He authored the *Book of Han*, covering 230 years from Emperor Gaozu to Wang Mang's death, completing it over twenty years. The work was highly regarded by contemporaries. Ban Gu later served under General Dou Xian during campaigns against the Xiongnu, acting as a counselor and envoy. After Dou Xian's downfall, Ban Gu was dismissed. He failed to discipline his sons, who often broke laws. A grudge held by Luoyang magistrate Zhong Jing, stemming from an incident with Ban Gu's drunken slaves, led to Ban Gu's arrest and death in prison at age sixty-one. The court later condemned Zhong Jing. Ban Gu's writings, including various literary forms, comprised forty-one works.

translation:
◆Ban Chao's biography, Ban Chao's courtesy name is Zhong Sheng, a native of Pingling County, Fufeng, and the youngest son of Ban Biao, the magistrate of Xu County.
He is ambitious and does not stick to trivial matters.
However, he is filial and respectful, diligent in housekeeping, and is not ashamed of hard work and humiliation.
He read widely and was very eloquent.
In the fifth year of Yongping, his elder brother Ban Gu was recruited as the school secretary. Ban Chao and his mother went to Luoyang together.
His family was very poor and he was often hired by officials to copy books and use his income to support his mother.
Therefore, he worked hard for a long time. He once put down his work and wrote and sighed: A man has no other great ambitions. He should follow the example of Fu Jiezi and Zhang Qian and make meritorious service in foreign lands to gain a title. How can he be engaged in the work of pen and inkstone for a long time?
Colleagues made fun of him.
Ban Chao said: How do boys know the ambition of a strong man?
Later, he went to the fortune teller to see the fortune teller. The fortune teller said: Sir, you are just a commoner, but in the future you will definitely become a prince thousands of miles away.
Banchao asked about his appearance, and the fortune teller said: "Your forehead is like a swallow, your neck is like a tiger, you fly and eat meat, this is the appearance of Wanli Hou."
After a long time, Xianzong asked Ban Gu: Where is your brother?
Ban Gu said to Xianzong: He is copying documents for the government and needs some money to support his old mother.
Emperor Xianzong appointed Ban Chao as the Lantai Lingshi.
Later, Ban Chao was dismissed from office due to his fault.
In the 16th year of Yongping, Dou Gu, the captain of Fengdong, attacked the Xiongnu. He appointed Ban Chao as a fake Sima and asked him to lead an army to attack Yiwu. They fought in Puleihai and returned with many enemy heads beheaded.
Dou Gu thought Ban Chao was very talented and sent him to follow Guo Xun on an envoy to the Western Regions.
When Ban Chao arrived in Shanshan, King Guang of Shanshan received him respectfully and politely, but then suddenly became cold.
Ban Chao said to his subordinates: Have you ever felt that King Guang of Shanshan's respect for us has diminished?
This must be because the Huns envoys came, and King Shanshan was hesitant and didn't know why.
Wise people can see things that are not yet apparent, let alone obvious facts.
So he called the barbarian who was waiting on him and threatened him by saying: "The Huns' envoys have been coming for several days." Where are you now?
The waiter was not frightened, so he revealed the whole situation.
Ban Chao locked up the waiter and gathered all thirty-six of his subordinates to drink together. When they were drunk happily, Ban Chao used words to irritate them and said: You and I are both in a very remote place, and we want to achieve great achievements in order to gain wealth.
It has only been a few days since the Huns envoy came, but King Guang of Shanshan has canceled the salute. If he captures us and gives them to the Huns, our bones will be fed to jackals forever. What do you think we should do?
All the subordinates said: We are now in a critical situation, and we must obey Sima's orders whether we live or die.
Ban Chao said: If you don't get into the tiger's cave, you won't be able to catch the little tiger.
summary: Ban Chao, courtesy name Zhong Sheng, was from Pingling County, Fufeng, and the youngest son of Ban Biao. Ambitious and diligent, he supported his mother by copying documents. In the fifth year of Yongping, he followed his brother Ban Gu to Luoyang. Dissatisfied with clerical work, he aspired to emulate Fu Jiezi and Zhang Qian in foreign exploits. A fortune-teller predicted he would become a marquis. Emperor Xianzong appointed him Lantai Lingshi, but he was later dismissed.

translation:
The best strategy now is to attack the Huns with fire when it is dark at night. They don't know how many of us there are, so they will be greatly frightened, and we can wipe them all out.
After destroying the Huns, King Shanshan will be frightened out of his wits. We are done and things are done.
The subordinates said: We should discuss this with the managers.
Ban Chao said angrily: "Whether it is good or bad depends on today."
If you are a vulgar civil servant, if you hear our plan, you will definitely leak the secret out of fear. He died unappreciated and was not a heroic and brave man. Everyone said: OK!
At the first watch, Ban Chao led his subordinates to the camp of the Huns envoys.
At this time, a strong wind was blowing. Ban Chao asked ten people to hold drums and hide behind the Xiongnu envoy's station, and made an agreement: When you see the fire attack, all of you will beat the drums and shout loudly.
The rest of the people were armed with bows and arrows and ambush on both sides of the door of the Huns envoy's residence.
Banchao set fire to the wind, beating drums and making noises in front and back, causing the Huns to panic and panic.
Ban Chao killed three people with his own hands, and his subordinates killed the Xiongnu envoy, and also killed more than 30 of the Xiongnu envoy's followers, and chopped off their heads. The remaining more than a hundred people were burned to death.
The next day, I went back and informed Guo Xun of the situation. Guo Xun was startled, and his expression changed after a while.
Ban Chao knew that he wanted to share the credit, so he raised his hand and said to Guo Xun: Although you didn't defeat the enemy together, how could I deliberately take the credit?
Only then did Guo Xun become happy.
Ban Chao then called King Guang of Shanshan and showed him the head of the Huns envoy. The whole country of Shanshan was shocked.
Ban Chao made the matter public and comforted him. So King Shanshan sent his son to the Han Dynasty as a hostage.
Ban Chao came back and reported the incident to Dou Gu. Dou Gu was overjoyed and reported Ban Chao's achievements to the emperor in detail, and asked to send another envoy to the Western Regions. Emperor Ming of the Han Dynasty praised Ban Chao's integrity and ordered Dou Gu: Why don't you choose an official like Ban Chao, but choose someone else?
Now Ban Chao is appointed as Army Sima and asked to complete his unfinished work.
Ban Chao was once again ordered to go on an envoy to the Western Regions. Dou Gu wanted to give more soldiers to Ban Chao, but Ban Chao said: I only want to give me the original thirty more soldiers.
If something unexpected happens, more people will be even more of a burden.
At this time, Yu Bin Wang Guangde had just conquered Shadong Kingdom and became the lord in the south of Tianshan Mountain. And the Xiongnu sent envoys to guard their country. When Banchao went to the Western Regions, he first arrived in the country of Ming. King Guangde was very cold to him and his etiquette was not very thoughtful.
Moreover, the customs of this country are based on witchcraft.
The wizard said: The god lost his temper, why did he want to get close to the Han Dynasty?
The envoy from the Han Dynasty had a bad horse, and he quickly brought it to me as a sacrifice.
King Guangde sent people to Ban Chao to ask for the horse.
Ban Chao secretly learned about this situation, so he agreed to give him the horse and asked the wizard to come and hold the horse himself.
After a while, the wizard came, and Ban Chao killed him, cut off his head and gave it to King Guangde, and reproached him with words.
summary: In the 16th year of Yongping, Ban Chao served as a fake Sima under Dou Gu, attacking the Xiongnu at Puleihai. Dou Gu then sent him as an envoy to the Western Regions. In Shanshan, Ban Chao deduced that the Huns had arrived when King Guang's hospitality waned. He interrogated a servant, confirmed his suspicion, and gathered his 36 men. At night, he led a fire attack on the Hun camp, killing the envoy and over 30 followers, with 100 burned to death. King Guang, impressed, sent his son as a hostage. Ban Chao reported to Dou Gu, who recommended him to Emperor Ming. Appointed Army Sima, Ban Chao refused extra troops, retaining only his original 36 men.

translation:
King Guangde had long heard about Ban Chao's destruction of the Huns' envoys in Shanshan, and was very frightened, so he killed the Huns' envoys and surrendered to Ban Chao.
Ban Chao rewarded King Guangde and his subordinates heavily, thus frightening and pacifying Yu Chong.
At that time, King Kui of Qiuci was supported by the Xiongnu. Relying on the power of the Xiongnu, he occupied the northern route of the Tianshan Mountains, attacked Shule, killed the king of Shule, and established a Qiuchi man as the king of Shule.
In the spring of the next year, Banchao took a small road to Shule, ninety miles away from Lucheng where Douti lived.
Ban Chao sent an official Tian Liu to Lucheng in advance to ask Dooti to surrender. He also told Tian Liu: "Dooti is not from Shule. The people of the country will definitely not listen to his orders. If he does not surrender, they will catch him."
When Tian Lu arrived at Lucheng, Douti saw that he was weak and had no intention of surrendering.
Tian Liu took advantage of him being unprepared and stepped forward to tie him up.
Douzi's entourage had an accident and all of them were scared away.
Tian Liu Pegasus informed Ban Chao. Banchao rushed to Lucheng, summoned all the Shule generals and officers, told them about Qiuci's rebellious behavior, and promoted their brother's son, named Zhong, to be king of Shule. The people of Shule were very happy.
Shule Wang Zhong and his subordinates all requested that Dooti be killed. Ban Chao disagreed and wanted to show his prestige, so he released Dooti.
Shule and Qiuci had enmity from then on.
In the 18th year of Yongping, Emperor Ming of the Han Dynasty died. Ma Qi attacked and killed the governor Chen Mu because there was a big funeral in China.
Banchao was isolated without foreign aid, and Kucha, Gumo and other countries sent troops to attack Shule many times.
Ban Chao guarded the city, forming a leading and trailing force with Shule Wang Zhong, and held on for more than a year with very few troops.
When Suzong first ascended the throne, because Chen Mugang had just been killed, he was afraid that Ban Chao's troops were too weak to protect himself, so he ordered Ban Chao to be summoned to return to the court.
Ban Chao was preparing to return home, and the whole country in Shule was worried and fearful.
Du Wei Li said: "The Han envoys have abandoned us, and we will definitely be destroyed by Qiuci again. I really can't bear to see the Han envoys leave."
So he drew his knife and committed suicide.
When Ban Chao returned to Yu Sheng, everyone in the state of Yu Sheng, from the prince to the prince, cried and said: "We rely on the Han envoys just like we rely on our parents. We really can't leave!"
So each other held Ban Chao's legs, making Ban Chao unable to walk.
Ban Chao was afraid that Yu Xing would never let him return eastward, and wanted to realize his original wish, so he returned to Shule.
There are two cities in Shule. Since Banchao left, they have been sent to Guibei and are in the same place as Weitou State Company.
Banchao hunted down the rebels, defeated Weitou, and killed more than 600 people. Shule was peaceful again.
In the third year of Jianchu's reign, Ban Chao led 10,000 troops from Shule, Kangju, Yuxing and Kumi to attack Gumo Stone City, captured the city and beheaded 700 people. Ban Chao wanted to take advantage of the victory to pacify the other countries, so he wrote to the emperor asking for more troops, saying: I secretly thought that the late emperor wanted to open up the Western Region, so I sent troops to the north to attack the Xiongnu, and sent envoys to the west to go to foreign countries. Shanshan and Yu Shen soon submitted to our court.
summary: In Yutian, Ban Chao killed a wizard who demanded his horse, shocking King Guangde into submitting. In Shule, he captured the usurper Douti, installed King Zhong, and released Douti to show prestige. After Emperor Ming's death, Ban Chao faced isolation but held Shule with minimal forces. Recalled by Emperor Suzong, he was persuaded by the people to stay, defeating rebels and stabilizing Shule. In the third year of Jianchu, he led 10,000 troops to capture Gumo, then petitioned for reinforcements to conquer Qiuci, proposing to use local forces and resources. The emperor approved, sending Xu Qian with 1,000 men. Ban Chao defeated Fan Chen, and later, despite slander from Li Yi, he remained loyal, leaving his wife to prove his commitment.

translation:
Ban Chao learned of their plot and pretended to accept surrender. King Zhong of Shule was overjoyed and immediately led his light cavalry to Banchao to feign surrender.
Ban Chao secretly ambush the soldiers, set up tents, arranged banquets and banquets, and waited for the arrival of Shule Wang Zhong.
King Zhong of Shule came. While drinking, Ban Chao ordered his soldiers to tie up King Zhong of Shule and kill him. So he took advantage of the victory and attacked his army, killing more than 700 people, and the southern road was opened.
The next year, Ban Chao led an army of 25,000 from the Yu Sheng Kingdom to attack Shadong again, while King Qiuci sent General Zuo to lead a total of 50,000 troops from Wensu, Gumo, Weitou and other countries to rescue Shadong.
Ban Chao summoned the generals to discuss with King Yu Shen and said: Now that we can't defeat the enemy with a small number of soldiers, the best strategy is to disperse.
Yu Xing walked eastward from here, and Chang Shi returned westward from here. Wait until you hear the sound of drums in the night before setting off.
Secretly relax the imprisonment of captured prisoners.
King Qiuci was very happy when he heard the news and led 10,000 cavalry to the west to stop Banchao; King Wensu led 8,000 cavalry to the east to intercept King Yu.
Ban Chao knew that two groups of enemy troops had set off, so he secretly ordered his troops to rush to the Shadong military camp when the rooster crows. The enemy was frightened and fled in a hurry. Banchao's army pursued the enemy, killed more than 5,000 enemy soldiers, and seized a large amount of property and horses.
Sha Dong surrendered. Kucha and other countries also retreated and dispersed. From then on, Ban Chao became famous in the Western Regions.
In the past, the Yuezhi helped the Han Dynasty attack the Cheshi Kingdom and made great contributions. This year, he contributed pearls, talismans, and lions to the Han Dynasty, and asked the Han Dynasty to marry him as a princess.
Ban Chao rejected the Yuezhi's request and sent back their envoy. From then on, the Yuezhi resented the Han Dynasty.
In the second year of Yongyuan, Yuezhi sent his deputy king Xie with 70,000 troops to attack Banchao.
Ban Chao had few soldiers and horses, and the sergeants were frightened.
Sergeant Ban Chao Xiaoyu said: Although there are many Yueshi soldiers, they have to travel thousands of miles and cross the green mountains to invade, and transportation is extremely inconvenient. What is there to worry about?
As long as the food is stored well and held tight, the enemy will surrender due to hunger. The enemy will be defeated in just a few dozen days.
Xie, the deputy king of the Yuezhi, led his army to attack Ban Chao, but could not win; he also looted and looted, but gained nothing.
Ban Chao estimated that the enemy troops would run out of food and would definitely ask for help from Qiuci. So hundreds of troops were sent to intercept on the east road.
Sure enough, Xie, the deputy king of Yuezhi, sent cavalry to bribe Qiuci with gold, silver, pearls and jade.
Ban Chao's ambush troops stepped out to intercept and kill all the enemies, and sent someone to show the deputy king Xie the head of the Yuezhi envoy.
Xie was shocked and immediately sent an envoy to Ban Chao to apologize, asking only for him to be allowed to go back alive.
Ban Chao then released Yuezhi Deputy Wang Xie and asked him to go back.
The Yueshi were greatly shaken from then on and paid tribute to the Han Dynasty every year. In the third year of Yongyuan, Qiuci, Gumo, and Wensu all surrendered. The imperial court appointed Ban Chao as the county protector, Xu Qian as the long history, Bai Ba as the king of Qiuci, and sent Sima Yao Guang to escort him.
Ban Chao and Yao Guang jointly coerced Qiuci to depose the original king Yuliduo and establish Baiba as king, and sent Yao Guang to return to the capital with Yuliduo.
Banchao was stationed in Tagancheng, Kucha, and Xu Gan was stationed in Shule.
Only Yanqi, Weixu, and Yuli in the Western Regions had killed Chen Mu, the guard of the Han Dynasty, but had second thoughts and did not dare to surrender. The rest of the countries in the Western Regions were pacified.
In the autumn of the sixth year of Yongyuan, Banchao mobilized a total of 70,000 troops from eight countries including Qiuci and Shanshan, and 1,400 officials and officials to attack Yanqi.
When the army arrived at the border of Yuli, they sent someone to tell Yanqi, Yuli and Weixu: "The governor came here this time just to stabilize and appease the three countries."
summary: Ban Chao conquered Shadong, killed the treacherous King Zhong, and opened the southern route. In a major battle, he feigned retreat, then attacked Shadong at dawn, killing 5,000 and securing surrender. Yuezhi attacked but were repelled due to supply issues. By the third year of Yongyuan, Qiuci, Gumo, and Wensu submitted. Ban Chao became Protector General, stationed in Tagancheng. In the sixth year, he led 70,000 troops to attack Yanqi, capturing and executing King Guang and others, pacifying over 50 states. He was granted the title Marquis of Dingyuan.

translation:
The nature of barbarians is to violate the right way and bully the elderly. Ban Chao will die sooner or later, and there will be no one to replace him for a long time. I am afraid that bad guys are waiting for the opportunity and have the intention of committing crimes. However, Dr. Qing is not willing to make any profound considerations.
If a riot suddenly breaks out and Ban Chao is unable to quell it, then the superior government will destroy the country's past achievements and the subordinate government will abandon all the efforts made by loyal ministers. That is really sad!
So it has been three years since Ban Chao, who was thousands of miles away, expressed his pain and anxiety with the sincerity of returning home, and craned his neck to look forward.
It has not yet been inspected by the emperor. I heard that in ancient times, people served at the age of fifteen and were exempted from service at the age of sixty. There were also people who took a break and did not serve.
Because Your Majesty governs the world with filial piety, he wins the favor of all nations and does not forget the ministers of small countries. What's more, Ban Chao was awarded the title of Marquis, so I dared to risk my life to plead for Ban Chao, begging him to live in peace for the rest of his life because of the country.
If Ban Chao can come back alive and see Gong Lique again, the country will never have to worry about labor expeditions, and there will be no worries about sudden uprisings in the Western Regions. Ban Chao will be able to long-term receive the kindness of the emperor for burying the bones like King Wen did, and the compassion for aging like Tian Zifang.
"The Book of Songs: Daya" says: Through labor, ordinary people can achieve a well-off life. First show favor to China, and then stabilize the four directions.
Ban Chao wrote to me to say goodbye before he died. I'm afraid I will never see him again.
I am indeed sad that Ban Chao devoted his loyalty and filial piety to the desert in his prime, but when he was old, he was abandoned and died in the desolate and empty wilderness. This is so sad and pitiful!
If Ban Chao does not receive the emperor's rescue and love, if Ban Chao changes in the future, I hope that Ban Chao's family can be forgiven by the emperor like Zhao's mother and Wei Ji, who were exempted from the crime of being implicated because they reported the matter in advance.
I am stupid and do not understand justice, and I have violated a taboo.
The memorial was sent up, and the emperor was moved by her words and recalled Ban Chao.
Ban Chao lived in the Western Regions for thirty-one years.
In August of the 14th year of Yongyuan, he returned to Luoyang and was appointed as the captain of Shesheng.
Ban Chao had a disease in his chest and ribs. After returning home, his condition worsened. The emperor sent Zhonghuangmen to check on him and gave him medicine.
He died in September of this year at the age of seventy-one.
The imperial court took pity on him and sent envoys to express condolences and offer him generous rewards.
Ban Chao's son Ban Xiong inherited his title.
Previously, when Ban Chao was summoned back, the imperial court appointed Wuji Colonel Ren Shang as the Protector. When handing over the work, Ren Shang said to Ban Chao: "The prince has been in a foreign country for more than thirty years, and I am ashamed to succeed you. I have great responsibilities and short wits. You should be able to teach me."
Ban Chao said: I am getting old and stupid. If you take up a big position, how can I, Ban Chao, compare with you?
As a last resort, I am willing to say a few words that are not very wise.
summary: Aged and homesick, Ban Chao petitioned to return, citing his long service. His sister Ban Zhao also pleaded. In the 14th year of Yongyuan, he returned to Luoyang, dying at 71. His son Ban Xiong inherited his title. Ban Chao's advice to successor Ren Shang—to be lenient—was ignored, leading to rebellion.

translation:
The officials and soldiers outside the Great Wall were not filial sons and grandsons in the first place. They were all moved to supplement the troops stationed on the frontier because of their sins.
The barbarians, on the other hand, have an animal heart, which makes them difficult to adopt and easy to do bad things.
Now you have a stern and somewhat impatient nature. If the water is clear, there will be no big fish. If supervision is strict, the people below will not be happy.
You should be tolerant and calm, act simply, deal with minor mistakes leniently, and just stick to the important links.
After Ban Chao left, Ren Shang said privately to his cronies: I thought Ban Chao had some clever ideas, but what he said now was just ordinary remarks.
A few years after Ren Shang took office, there was a rebellion in the Western Regions. Ren Shang was recalled because of his guilt, just as Ban Chao warned.
Ban Chao had three sons. The eldest son was named Ban Xiong, who was promoted to the rank of captain of the garrison.
When the Qiang invaded Sanfu, the emperor ordered Ban Xiong to lead five battalions of soldiers and horses to station in Chang'an and appointed him as Jing Zhaoyin.
After Ban Xiong died, his son Ban Shi inherited his position and married Princess Yincheng, the daughter of King Xiao of Qinghe.
Princess Yincheng is the aunt of Emperor Shun, who is arrogant and promiscuous. She was in the curtain with her beloved, and asked Ban Shi to go in and ask him to crawl under the bed.
Ban Shi could not hold back his anger. In the fifth year of Yongjian's reign, he drew his sword and killed the princess.
Emperor Shun was furious and had Ban Shi cut in half, and all his people were killed.
Ban Chao's youngest son is named Ban Yong.
◆Ban Yongzhuan, Ban Yong, courtesy name Yi Liao. When he was young, he had the general demeanor of his father, Ban Chao.
In the first year of Yongchu, the Western Regions rebelled against the Han Dynasty, and the imperial court sent Ban Yong to serve as an army commander.
Ban Yong and his brother Ban Xiong both sent troops from Dunhuang to welcome the return of the Duhu and the armored soldiers from the Western Regions.
So he dismissed the governor.
Later, there were no officials from the Han Dynasty in the Western Regions for more than ten years.
In the sixth year of the Yuan Dynasty, Shi Suoban, the governor of Dunhuang Cao Zong, led more than a thousand people to garrison in Yiwu. The former king of Cheshi and the king of Shanshan both surrendered here to Suoban.
A few months later, Bei Shanyu and the rear of the chariot division attacked Soban, drove away the former king, and occupied the road to the north.
King Shanshan became anxious and asked Cao Zong for help. Cao Zong therefore asked the court to send 5,000 troops to attack the Xiongnu to avenge Soban and recover the Western Regions.
Empress Dowager Deng summoned Ban Yong to the court to attend the meeting.
At first, most of the ministers advocated closing Yumen Pass, so they gave up the Western Region.
Ban Yong went to the memorial and said: In the past, Emperor Xiaowu was worried that the Huns would become powerful and become the commander-in-chief of hundreds of barbarians and force them to invade our borders, so he opened the Western Region to separate their comrades. Public opinion at the time believed that this was equivalent to seizing the Xiongnu's internal organs and cutting off his right arm.
Later, Wang Mang usurped the throne and demanded too much from the Western Regions. He was so greedy that Hu Yi was so angry that he betrayed the Han Dynasty.
After Emperor Guangwu was resurrected, he had no time to consider foreign affairs, so the Xiongnu relied on their own strength to drive away others and occupy other countries.
During the Yongping period, they attacked Dunhuang again, and all the counties in Hexi closed their city gates during the day.
Emperor Xiaoming considered the national plan and sent tiger generals to conquer the Western Regions. As a result, the Huns fled far away and the borders were peaceful.
By the Yongyuan period, all the places in the Western Regions had surrendered to the mainland.
Later, when the Qiang people were in rebellion and communication with the Western Regions was cut off, the Northern Xiongnu sent troops to supervise other small countries. Collect evaded rent and taxes, raise the value high, and strictly limit meetings.
Both Shanshan and Cheshi were resentful and wanted to get close to the Han Dynasty, but unfortunately they could not find a way.
It can be seen that there were rebellions in the previous period because the governance work was not appropriate enough, so the opposite effect occurred.
Now Cao Zong just felt the previous humiliation and wanted to retaliate against the Xiongnu to clear up the humiliation. He did not check the historical precedents of sending troops and did not consider the specific situation at that time.
summary: Ban Yong, Ban Chao's son, served as an army commander. In the first year of Yongchu, he helped withdraw Han forces from the Western Regions. Later, he advised against a costly campaign, recommending a modest garrison in Dunhuang. His strategy was adopted, stabilizing the region. In the second year of Yanguang, he led 500 soldiers to Liuzhong, securing Shanshan and Qiuci's submission. He defeated the Xiongnu and pacified Cheshi. In Yongjian's first year, he attacked Yanqi but was imprisoned for missing a rendezvous, later dying at home.

translation:
From then on, there was no trace of the Xiongnu in the chariot division, and the city was very stable.
Only Yuanmeng, the king of Yanqi, has not yet surrendered.
The next year, Ban Yong wrote a letter requesting to attack Yuan and Meng, so the imperial court sent Zhang Lang, the governor of Dunhuang, to lead 3,000 soldiers from Hexi County to cooperate with Ban Yong.
Ban Yong mobilized more than 40,000 soldiers from various countries and divided them into two groups to attack.
Ban Yong walked from the south road, Zhang Lang walked from the north road, and agreed to meet at Yanqi on a date.
However, Zhang Lang was guilty first and wanted to make atonement, so he rushed to Jue Liguan first. Sima was sent to lead troops to attack the front station and captured more than 2,000 enemy people.
Yuan Meng was afraid of beheading, so he sent an envoy to ask for surrender. Zhang Lang went directly to Yanqi and surrendered.
Yuan Meng actually refused to be tied up in person, and only sent his son to the court to pay tribute.
Zhang Lang was pardoned from the death penalty.
Because Ban Yong did not arrive as scheduled, he was convicted and imprisoned. He was pardoned soon after, and later died at home.
◆In the biography of Liang Jin, Liang Jin was named Bowei and was a native of Yiju in the north.
His father, Liang Xi, served successively as governor of the state.
In the first year of Yongyuan, Dou Xian, the general of chariots and cavalry, went to conquer the Xiongnu. Liang Xi was granted the title of Army Sima, and he was asked to bring gold and silk as an envoy to Bei Chanyu to promote the country's might and virtue. More than ten thousand people joined him.
Later, because he violated Dou Xian's will, he was exiled to Wuwei, and the prefect of Wuwei ordered to kill him.
After the Dou family was destroyed, Emperor He knew that Liang Xi had been unjustly killed by Dou Xian, so he summoned him as a doctor.
Liang Jin was courageous and generous in his fame.
At first, he was the Sima of Deng Hong, the chariot and cavalry general. He was promoted again and became the deputy captain of the Western Regions in the first year of Yanping.
When Liang Jin went to Hexi, he encountered the rebellion of various countries in the Western Regions. He attacked the capital and protected Shang Yu in Shule.
Ren Shang wrote a letter asking for help, and the court summoned Commander Liang Jin to lead five thousand Qiang and Hu cavalry from the four counties of Hexi to run to the rescue. However, Liang Jin did not arrive and Ren Shang had already rescued the siege.
Just when Ren Shang was called back, the imperial court appointed Duan Xi, the Cavalry Commander, as the Protector, and Zhao Bo, the chief historian of the Western Regions, as the Cavalry Commander.
Duan and Zhao guarded Qiancheng.
Qiancheng was very small, and Liang Jin thought it was not very strong, so he cunningly persuaded Bai Ba, the king of Qiuci, to come in and protect the city together. Bai Ba agreed.
The officials tried to dissuade him, but Bai Ba refused to listen. After Liang Jin entered the city, he sent generals to greet Duan Xi and Zhao Bo, with a total of eight or nine thousand sergeants.
The officials of Qiuci all rebelled against their king, and they rebelled with tens of thousands of soldiers from Wensu and Gumo, and together they surrounded the city.
Liang Jin and others came out to fight and defeated them.
summary: Liang Jin, a brave officer, served as Deputy Captain of the Western Regions. During a rebellion, he defended Qiuci with King Baiba, defeating tens of thousands of attackers. After the Western Regions were abandoned, he fought Qiang rebels, stabilizing Hexi. He later campaigned against the Xiongnu, accepting Chanyu's surrender. Appointed General Who Conquers the Liao, he died of illness while suppressing Qiang rebels.

translation:
◆The legend of Shentu Gang is that Shentu Gang was named Juqing and was a native of Maoling, Fufeng County. The seventh generation ancestor Shen Tujia was the prime minister during the reign of Emperor Wen. Shentu was upright and upright, and often envied the conduct of Chief Shi Yu and Ji An.
He became an official of the county meritorious service.
During the reign of Emperor Ping, Wang Mang was in dictatorship, and there were many suspicions in the court. Wang Mang isolated the Feng clan of Emperor Ping's grandmother from the mother Wei clan, and was not allowed to go to Beijing to interact and serve as an official. Shentu Gang always resented this.
Later, when he was praised as a virtuous and upright man, he wrote a countermeasure, saying: If I hear that the government is wrong, the gods of heaven and earth will be angry, and the treacherous and evil will cause trouble, so the yin and yang are wrong.
This is why God condemns and warns the emperor, hoping to teach the unjust monarch to suddenly wake up and make those ministers with evil intentions fear and correct themselves. Nowadays, the imperial court does not examine merits or compare virtues, but instead accepts false slander or praise. It has issued several edicts and set up strict laws to suppress slander and prohibit discussion. Those who commit serious crimes may even be cut in half.
This dampens the friendship of loyal ministers and dampens the spirit of loyal and upright people. It is contrary to the purpose of establishing banners to offer good words, hanging bells and drums for daring to give advice, opening up channels for words from all directions, and clearly observing the four directions so that the feelings of subordinates can be conveyed to superiors.
I heard that when King Cheng was young, the Duke of Zhou acted as regent. He listened to the opinions of others, treated the virtuous and corporal, shared rights and interests equally, spread favor widely, regardless of old or new, treated everyone with kindness, love and closeness, acted in accordance with heaven and earth, and did not violate the rules.
However, if you are close, Duke Zhao is unhappy, and if you are far, there are rumors about Cai, Shang, and the four kingdoms.
The relationship between mother and child is a close relative in heaven.
Your Majesty is young now, only nine years old. Since he came to the throne, his close relatives have been separated, his relatives are separated from each other, and his kindness is not as good as that of his uncle's family.
Moreover, although the Han Dynasty system employed heroes and virtuous men, it was still necessary to use in-laws. In this way, kinship and distance were intertwined, and gaps could be closed. This was a method used to install ancestral temples and restructure the country.
Now the Feng and Wei clans are innocent and have been deposed for a long time without being hired, or they are far away in remote and remote areas and are not as good as the common people. This is not the intention of loving, loyal and filial servants to the emperor.
Those who are human beings will naturally have justice. No matter whether they are the most noble or the most humble, their power will not disapprove of each other. Therefore, people are not wise and foolish, and everyone will resent them. Traitors and traitors can act very conveniently, and it is difficult to predict changes that are not hidden.
The guardian who tutors the sons of the emperor today is not the Duke of Zhou in ancient times.
The Duke of Zhou is the most holy person, yet he is still involved, let alone some things that are out of his original intention and inconsistent with Heaven's will?
In the past, the Duke of Zhou first sent Bo Qin to the state of Lu to maintain the title, in order to sever the relationship between father and son, and to cut off the favor with loyalty, so that his respect and favor would not be extended to future generations. Therefore, Lu thought that Duke Zhou was a descendant of the great sage, and worshiped him in the suburbs, just like the emperor's gift, for more than thirty generations.
Huo Guang was responsible for the affairs of the government, assisted the young Emperor Zhao, cultivated good government, and promoted talents. On the surface, he was very loyal. However, he relied on his clan, suppressed his relatives, and made friends with powerful people to monopolize the government. After Huo Guang's death, his son rebelled against the Huo family and was exterminated.
Today's masters all use the power of Yi Yin and Zhou Gong to hold the great responsibility of being virtuous and protecting the country, and they use this to think about education. So what can't they achieve?
summary: Shentu Gang, a native of Maoling, was an upright man who resented Wang Mang's isolation of Emperor Ping's maternal relatives. When recommended as a virtuous and upright man, he submitted a countermeasure criticizing the court for suppressing dissent and separating close relatives, arguing this violated the principles of good governance. He cited the examples of the Duke of Zhou and Huo Guang, warning that those with great power are often unsafe. He urged the emperor to welcome his grandmother and recall the Feng and Wei clans. Wang Mang had him dismissed from office. After Wang Mang usurped the throne, Shentu Gang fled. Later, when Wei Xiao considered betraying Han, Shentu Gang advised him to remain loyal to Emperor Guangwu, but Wei Xiao refused. In the seventh year of Jianwu, Shentu Gang was summoned. He again wrote to Wei Xiao, warning that isolation and refusal of advice lead to ruin, but Wei Xiao did not accept. Shentu Gang was appointed imperial censor and then ministerial order. He once stopped Emperor Guangwu from traveling by placing his head on the wheel. He repeatedly advised against the emperor's harsh treatment of officials and urged the appointment of virtuous guardians for the crown prince, but was not heeded. He was eventually released as the Pingyin Order, later recalled as Taizhong doctor, and died at home after resigning due to illness.

translation:
◆Bao Yongzhuan Bao Yong, courtesy name Junchang, was a native of Tunliu, Shangdang County.
His father, Bao Xuan, was the captain of Sili School at the time of Emperor Ai and was killed by Wang Mang.
When Bao Yong was young, he was ambitious and studied Ouyang's "Shang Shu".
He was very filial to his stepmother. His wife once scolded the dog in front of his stepmother, so Bao Yong divorced his wife immediately.
At first he was a county meritorious official.
Wang Mang thought that Bao Xuan would not join him and wanted to kill his descendants.
Duwei Luping followed Wang Mang's wishes and formulated a plan to kill Bao Yong.
The prefect Gou Jian protected him, called him an official, and allowed him to live in the mansion permanently. Therefore, Bao Yong repeatedly stated the strategy of reviving the Han Dynasty and cutting off the treason for Gou Jian.
Gou Jian repeatedly warned Bao Yong: If the ruler reveals the secret, the whole family will be killed.
Bao Yong was grateful for his persuasion.
After Gou Jian passed away, Bao Yong returned to Fufeng Luping to attend his funeral, so Bao Yong's younger brother Bao Sheng was put on trial.
When the new governor Zhao Xing arrived, he sighed after hearing these things: I accepted the grant from the Han Dynasty and could not establish a festival. Bao Xuan was killed, how could I frame his son?
The county magistrate was ordered to release Bao Sheng and restore Bao Yong to his position of meritorious service.
At that time, there was a person pretending to be Shizhong living in Chuanshe, and Zhao Xing wanted to pay him a visit.
Bao Yong suspected that he was lying and stopped Zhao Xing, but Zhao Xing refused to listen.
Zhao Xing drove there, and Bao Yong drew his sword and cut the horse in the chest before the carriage stopped. A few days later, Wang Mang issued an edict to search for those who pretended to be servants, and Bao Yong became famous. It is inappropriate to recommend him as a scholar. In the second year of Gengshi's reign, Bao Yong was recruited, and then moved to the post of Shangshu Pushe, acting as the general's military affairs. He commanded the troops with Fu Jie, and assembled the Hedong, Bingzhou, and Shuo tribes, and authorized him to appoint partial generals and exercise military law.
Bao Yong went to Hedong, led an army to attack Qingdu, and defeated him. He was granted the title of Marquis of Zhongyang.
Although Bao Yong was a general, his carriage and clothing were simple, and people on the road called him Bao Shangshu's soldiers and horses.
At this time, Chimei killed Gengshi, and the road to Sanfu was blocked.
When Guangwu came to the throne, he sent Uncle Chu, an official to advise him, and summoned Bao Yong to pay homage to him at his residence.
Bao Yongyou was suspicious of disobedience, so he imprisoned Uncle Chu and sent another envoy to Chang'an to inquire.
When he knew for sure that Gengshi was dead, he declared mourning, released Uncle Chu and others, and was awarded the title of general, Liehou Yinshou. He dismissed all the troops and arrived in Hanoi with the generals and more than a hundred fellow travelers without their heads.
The emperor saw Bao Yong and asked: "Where are your subordinates?"
Bao Yong left his seat and kowtowed and said: "I serve Gengshi, but I can't protect his safety. I am really ashamed to use my subordinates to invite wealth and honor, so they are all dismissed."
The emperor said: You are talking nonsense!
And feel unhappy inside.
At that time, Huai County could not be captured. The emperor said to Bao Yong: I have been attacking Huai County for three days but cannot capture it. Guandong fears and respects you. As an old friend, I can go to the city in person to inform him.
Then he worshiped Bao Yong as the admonishing doctor.
When Bao Yong arrived in Huai, he persuaded the governor of Gengshi Hanoi and surrendered to the city.
The emperor was overjoyed and rewarded Bao Yong with a residence in Shangshangli, Luoyang, but Bao Yong refused.
At this time, General Dong Xianpi stationed troops in Lu and invaded the people, so he worshiped Bao Yong as the governor of Lu County.
Bao Yong arrived, attacked and defeated them, and thousands of people surrendered.
But the other commanders, Peng Feng, Yu Xiu, and Pi Chang, each with more than a thousand men, claimed to be "generals" and refused to surrender.
Soon, the thorns in Confucius's palace were cleared for no reason, from the lecture hall to the inner gate.
Bao Yong felt strange and said to Fu Cheng and Lu Ling: "Now that the crisis is critical, the gate opens. Is this because Confucius wants me, the prefect, to salute and help me punish the unjust?"
So everyone gathered together to practice the ritual of local shooting. Please invite Peng Feng and others to watch and prepare to capture Peng Feng and others.
Peng Feng and others also wanted to murder Bao Yong, so they prepared cattle and wine for the feast, and secretly carried weapons.
Bao Yong found out and killed Peng Feng and others with his own hands, and captured his gang members.
The emperor praised his strategy, made him a Marquis of Guannei, and moved him to Yangzhou as a Mu.
At this time, there were still a lot of violent bandits in the southern land. After the officials and the people were injured, Bao Yong relaxed the law to control the movement of people. He issued notices only to punish the violent ones, and calmed and appeased the people who threatened them, so the people settled down.
When his mother passed away, he resigned and distributed all his property to his disciples.
In the 11th year of Jianwu's reign, he was appointed as Sili Xiaowei.
The emperor's uncle, King Liu Liang of Zhao, was a respected relative. Bao Yong's impeachment of Liu Liang was considered disrespectful, so the court was in awe of him and everyone was vigilant and cautious.
So Fufeng Bao Hui was recruited to serve as an official in the capital, but Hui resisted and did not avoid violence.
Emperor Chang said: Noble relatives should restrain themselves to avoid the second wave.
It's so terrifying.
Bao Yongxing County went to Baling, passing Gengshi Tomb, and drove to the Northeast Cemetery to persuade him not to go.
Bao Yong said: I once went to the north to serve Gengshi. How could I not not worship the tomb? Even though I was guilty of this, I did not avoid it.
summary: Bao Yong, a native of Tunliu, was the son of Bao Xuan, who was killed by Wang Mang. He was filial, once divorcing his wife for scolding a dog in front of his stepmother. Wang Mang sought to kill Bao Yong, but the prefect Gou Jian protected him. Bao Yong advised Gou Jian on reviving the Han. After Gou Jian's death, Bao Yong's brother was arrested, but the new prefect Zhao Xing released him. Bao Yong later exposed an impostor. During Gengshi's reign, he became a general and defeated Qingdu. After Gengshi's death, he submitted to Guangwu, dismissing his troops out of shame for serving Gengshi. He persuaded the governor of Huai County to surrender. As governor of Lu County, he killed the rebel generals Peng Feng and others. He later served as Yangzhou Mu, relaxing laws to pacify the people. As Sili Xiaowei, he impeached the emperor's uncle, King Liu Liang of Zhao, for disrespect, causing the court to be in awe. He wept at Gengshi's tomb, which initially displeased the emperor but was defended by a minister. He was later demoted for speaking out and then served as Yanzhou Mu until his death. The historian commented that Bao Yong's loyalty to his old master allowed him to serve a new one, and that upright words are difficult for people to understand. Zhi Yun, a native of Runan, was a scholar who, during Wang Mang's reign, observed astronomical signs and predicted the Han would be restored. He advised a local official to follow this destiny but refused a minor post, citing historical precedents. He then wrote to Wang Mang, urging him to return the throne to the Liu family, citing heavenly warnings. Wang Mang imprisoned him, but he was released. Later, he served under General Fu Jun, advising him to stop looting tombs and mistreating corpses, which the general did. Zhi Yun resigned, ashamed of gaining office through military merit. He avenged his friend Dong Zizhang by killing his enemy and then turned himself in, but the magistrate refused to imprison him. He later served as a meritorious officer under Prefect Ouyang She. At a feast, he publicly denounced another official, Yao Yan, as corrupt, causing the prefect shame. After a period of conflict, Zhi Yun left the prefect's service. He later became a marquis and gatekeeper, once refusing to let Emperor Guangwu enter the city at night. He remonstrated with the emperor about hunting and later advised the crown prince after Empress Guo was deposed. He served as governor of Changsha, where he praised a filial son, and later as magistrate of Mang County before retiring to teach. He wrote eight books and died of illness.

translation:
◆Huangfu Song's biography, Huangfu Song's character is Yizhen, he was the son of the brother of Huangfu Gui, the general who conquered Liao Dynasty.
Father Huangfu Festival, Yanmen Prefecture.
When Huangfu Song was young, he had ambitions of literary and martial arts. He was good at "Poems" and "Books", and learned to bow, sword and ride horses.
He began to be promoted as Xiaolian and Maocai.
Taiwei Chen Fan and General Dou Wu were summoned one after another, but neither of them went.
During the reign of Emperor Ling, he was promoted to Yilang by a public chariot and promoted to the governor of the North.
In the past, Julu Zhangjiao claimed to be a great teacher. He believed in the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi, adopted disciples, knelt down and stated his faults, and used talisman water to recite mantras to cure diseases. The patients were cured, and the people believed in him.
Therefore, Zhang Jiao sent eight of his disciples to all directions to educate the people of the world by doing good deeds and deceiving and confusing them.
Over the past ten years, hundreds of thousands of believers have contacted counties and counties, and no one from the eight prefectures of Qing, Xu, You, Ji, Jing, Yang, Yan, and He did not respond.
So thirty-six squares were set up.
Fang is equal to the title of general.
There are more than 10,000 people in Dafang and six or seven thousand in Xiaofang. Each party has a general.
Rumors were spread that: Cang Tian is dead, Huang Tian should be established, and the age of Jiazi will bring good luck to the world.
Written in white clay on temple gates in the capital and on state and county government offices, they are all marked with the character Jiazi.
In the first year of Zhongping, Dafang Ma Yuanyi and others first collected tens of thousands of people from Jing and Yang, and gathered at Ye regularly to set off.
Ma Yuanyi visited the capital many times, using Zhongchang Shifeng and Xu Feng as internal agents, and agreed to start an uprising both inside and outside the capital on March 5.
Before the rebellion broke out, Zhang Jiao's disciple Jinan Tang Zhou wrote a letter to report, so he drove Ma Yuanyi to Luoyang.
Emperor Ling used Zhou Zhang to issue orders to the three princes and officials, and ordered Zhou Bin to take the three government officials with him. He asked the palace guards and the people if they believed in Zhang Jiao, killed more than a thousand people, tracked down Jizhou, and arrested Zhang Jiao and others.
Zhang Jiao and others knew that the matter had been exposed, so they notified all parties day and night and started revolts at the same time.
They all wore yellow scarves as a symbol. At that time, they were called "yellow scarves" and also "moth thieves".
Kill people and sacrifice to heaven.
Zhang Jiao was called General Tiangong, Zhang Jiao's younger brother Zhang Bao was called General Digong, and Zhang Bao's younger brother Zhang Liang was called General Renggong.
Wherever he went, government offices were burned, villages and towns were robbed, states and counties lost their basis, and many officials fled.
Within ten days, the whole country responded and the capital was shaken.
The imperial court ordered the prefectures and counties to repair offensive and defensive positions, select and prepare ordnance, and set up captains at Hangu, Dagu, Guangcheng, Yique, Longyuan, Xuanmen, Mengjin, and Xiaopingjin passes.
Call the ministers to a meeting.
Huangfu Song believed that the ban on the party should be lifted, and he gave Zhongzang money and Xiyuan stable horses to the sergeants.
Emperor Ling adopted his opinion.
summary: Huangfu Song, styled Yizhen, was a nephew of the general Huangfu Gui. His father served as the Prefect of Yanmen. From a young age, Huangfu Song was learned in the *Classic of Poetry* and *Book of Documents*, and skilled in archery, swordsmanship, and horsemanship. He was recommended as a Xiaolian and Maocai, but declined summons from Grand Commandant Chen Fan and General Dou Wu. During Emperor Ling's reign, he was appointed Yilang and later Governor of Beidi. When Zhang Jiao founded the Way of Great Peace, claiming to cure illness through faith and talismanic water, he amassed hundreds of thousands of followers across eight provinces over a decade. He organized them into thirty-six "squares," each led by a general, and spread the prophecy: "The Azure Heaven is dead; the Yellow Heaven shall rise. In the year of Jiazi, the world will be blessed." In the first year of Zhongping (184 AD), his disciple Tang Zhou betrayed the planned uprising, leading to the execution of Ma Yuanyi and a crackdown in Luoyang. Zhang Jiao then launched a nationwide rebellion, with followers wearing yellow scarves—hence called the "Yellow Turbans"—burning government offices and terrorizing provinces.

translation:
So he recruited the best soldiers from all over the world. Generals were widely selected, and Huangfu Song was appointed as the left Zhonglang general. He held the talisman, and together with the right Zhonglang general Zhu Ai, they sent out five schools, Sanhe knights and recruited brave warriors, totaling more than 40,000 people. Huangfu Song and Zhu Ai unified their armies and joined forces to attack the Yingchuan Yellow Turbans.
Zhu Ji had previously fought against the thief Bo Cai and was defeated, so Huangfu Song marched to defend Changshe.
Bocai led a large army to besiege the city, but Huangfu Song had few soldiers. The army became frightened, so he summoned the military officers and said: "There is a strange change in the army, not because there are more soldiers than there are fewer soldiers."
Nowadays, thieves have camped on grass and are prone to catching fire due to the wind.
If you set fire to it at night, you must be frightened and dispersed. I will send troops to attack and surround it on all sides. Tian Dan and Jimo will use the fire ox to attack Yan and win.
That night, there was a strong wind, so Huangfu Song ordered his sergeants to tie up ropes and climb up the city. He sent elite and brave men to go out on the small road, lit fires and shouted, and the city raised torches in response. Huangfu Song beat drums and rushed to the enemy's position. The thieves fled in panic.
At this time, Emperor Ling sent Cao Cao, the cavalry captain, to arrive with his troops. Huangfu Song, Cao Cao and Zhu Ji joined forces to fight again. They defeated the rebel army, beheaded tens of thousands of people, and made Huangfu Song the Marquis of Duxiang.
Huangfu Song and Zhu Ji took advantage of their victory to attack Runan and Chen Guohuangjin, pursued Bo Cai in Yangdi, attacked Peng Tuo in Xihua, and defeated them all.
The remaining thieves either surrendered or fled, and the three counties were pacified.
They also attacked Dongjun Huangjin Buji in Cangting, captured Buji alive, and beheaded more than 7,000 people.
At that time, Lu Zhi, the general of Bei Zhonglang, and Dong Zhuo, the general of Dong Zhonglang, attacked Zhang Jiao, but they all failed, so they ordered Huangfu Song to lead troops to attack Zhang Jiao.
Huangfu Song fought against Zhang Jiao's younger brother Zhang Liang in Guangzong. Zhang Liang's troops were elite and brave, but Huangfu Song could not defeat him.
The next day, Huangfu Song closed the camp and allowed the soldiers to rest and observe the changes in the enemy's army.
Knowing that the thieves and sergeants had become lax, they quietly gathered their troops at night, waited until the rooster crow, launched a charge, and fought until dark. They defeated the enemy army, beheaded Zhang Liang, and won the 30,000-level leader. About 50,000 people went to the Yellow River and drowned. They burned more than 30,000 vehicles and equipment, captured all the enemy's wives, children, and arrested many.
Zhang Jiao died of illness first, so he opened his coffin, killed his body, and reported it to the capital.
Huangfu Song, together with Feng Yi and Guo Dian, the governors of Julu, attacked Zhang Jiao's younger brother Zhang Bao in Xiaquyang and killed him.
More than 100,000 people were captured, and their corpses were piled up and sealed with earth to build a palace in the south of the city.
Huangfu Song was appointed General of Zuo Chaoqi and Jizhou Mu, and was granted the title of Marquis of Huaili. He served in Huaili and Meiyang counties, totaling 8,000 households.
Because the Yellow Turbans had been pacified, the year was changed to Zhongping.
Huangfu Song petitioned to reduce one year's land rent in Jizhou to help the hungry people. Emperor Ling agreed.
The common people made a song: The world is in chaos, the city has turned into ruins, the mother cannot protect her son, the wife has lost her husband, help Huangfu to live in peace again.
Huangfu Song loved to nurse his soldiers and was very popular. Every time you take a break during the march, you have to wait for the military tent to be set up before entering your own tent.
The sergeants have all eaten, and then I eat.
Some officials accepted bribes for certain reasons, and Huangfu Song even gave them money and gifts. The officials were ashamed, and some even committed suicide.
Huangfu Song has eliminated the Yellow Turbans, and his fame shocked the world. However, the political affairs of the imperial court became more and more chaotic day by day, and the country was empty and troubled.
The previous letter made Hanyang Yan Zhong rashly say to Huangfu Song: What is rare and easy to lose is time. When the time comes, the opportunity also comes.
summary: The court appointed Huangfu Song as Left General of the Central Army, alongside Zhu Jun, to suppress the rebellion. After an initial defeat, Huangfu Song used a fire attack at Changshe, exploiting a strong wind to burn the enemy camp and rout Bo Cai's forces. Reinforced by Cao Cao, they defeated the rebels, beheading tens of thousands. Huangfu Song was made Marquis of Duxiang. They then pacified Runan and Chen, capturing Bo Cai and Peng Tuo. At Cangting, they captured Bu Ji, killing over 7,000. Huangfu Song was then ordered to attack Zhang Jiao. After initial setbacks against Zhang Liang at Guangzong, he feigned rest, then launched a surprise dawn assault, killing Zhang Liang and 30,000 rebels, with 50,000 drowning in the Yellow River. Zhang Jiao had died of illness, so Huangfu Song beheaded his corpse. He then killed Zhang Bao at Xiaquyang, capturing over 100,000. He was appointed General of the Left Chariot and Cavalry and Governor of Jizhou, with 8,000 households. He petitioned to reduce Jizhou's land rent, earning popular praise. Huangfu Song was a benevolent commander who shared hardships with his troops. After pacifying the Yellow Turbans, his fame grew, but court politics worsened. Advisor Yan Zhong urged him to seize power, but Huangfu Song refused, remaining loyal. Later, due to conflicts with eunuchs Zhao Zhong and Zhang Rang, he was demoted to Marquis of Duxiang with 2,000 households.
