translation:
Yan Zhong knew that the plan could not be adopted and ran away.
At the time when Bian Zhang and Han Sui were causing trouble in Longyou, in the spring of the next year Huangfu Song was ordered to return to Chang'an to defend the garden and mausoleum.
Bian Zhang and others invaded Sanfu again and sent Huangfu Song to attack them.
At first, when Huangfu Song was conquering Zhangjiao, he passed by Ye and saw that the building of Zhao Zhong's house exceeded the regulations, so he sent a memorial to confiscate his house.
Also, Chang's attendant Zhang asked a private person to ask for fifty million from him, but Huangfu Song refused to give it. Zhao and Zhang hated Huangfu Song because of this, and reported to Huangfu Song that the battle was fruitless and expensive.
In the autumn of this year, he was recalled and received the seal and ribbon of General Zuo Chaoqiu. He cut off 6,000 households and changed his title to Duxiang Hou, with 2,000 households.
In the fifth year, the Liangzhou bandit kingdom surrounded Chencang. Huangfu Song was appointed as the general of the left, and Dong Zhuo, the former general in charge, each led 20,000 people to resist.
Dong Zhuo wanted to go to Chencang soon, but Huangfu Song refused to listen.
Dong Zhuo said: A wise man never misses an opportunity, a brave man never hesitates.
If you save it quickly, the city will be saved; if you don't save it, the city will be destroyed. The situation of preservation or destruction was at this moment, Huangfu Song said: Not like this.
It is better to surrender the enemy's army without fighting than to win a hundred battles.
Therefore, you must first act like you are invincible and wait for the enemy to be able to defeat you.
The invincible lies with me, but the victorious lies with the enemy.
The enemy is hard to defend against, but I am very proactive in attacking, hitting wherever I want.
The ones that are more than enough seem to be moving above the Nine Heavens, and those that are not enough seem to be trapped under the Nine Earths.
Now, although Chencang is small, the fortifications that defend the city are strong and complete, and it is not a trap in the Nine Heavens. Although the kingdom is strong, if I can't save anything if I attack, it is not a situation above the Nine Heavens.
Without a situation above the Nine Heavens, those who attack will suffer. If you fall under the Nine Grounds, your defense will not be broken.
The kingdom is now in a vulnerable position, and Chen Cang can be guaranteed not to be breached. I can mobilize a large number of troops and receive a complete victory, so why should I save him?
He never listened to Dong Zhuo.
The kingdom surrounded Chencang. From winter to spring, for more than eighty days, the city was firmly defended, but it was not captured in the end.
The bandit troops were so exhausted that they had no choice but to rescue themselves.
Huangfu Song commanded the troops to attack.
Dong Zhuo said: No, the art of war says that the defeated enemy should not be pursued, and the retreating troops should not be forced.
Now, when we pursue the kingdom, we are forcing the retreating troops. We are pursuing the defeated enemy and the besieged beasts. They still have to struggle. The bees are poisonous, not to mention so many people!
Huangfu Song said: That's not the case.
In the past, when I did not attack, it was to avoid his fierceness. Now, when I attack, I wait until the enemy is weakened.
We attack the exhausted enemy, not the retreating troops.
The troops of the kingdom were ready to flee and had no fighting spirit.
Using a majestic formation to attack the defeated enemy is not called chasing the poor bandits.
summary: In 189 AD, when the Liangzhou rebel Kingdom besieged Chencang, Huangfu Song and Dong Zhuo led 20,000 men each. Dong Zhuo wanted to attack immediately, but Huangfu Song argued for a defensive strategy, waiting for the enemy to weaken. After 80 days, the rebels retreated, and Huangfu Song pursued, defeating them and beheading over 10,000. Dong Zhuo, humiliated, grew to hate him.

translation:
He led his troops to attack alone and made Dong Zhuo's rear. After a few battles, the kingdom was severely defeated and more than ten thousand people were beheaded.
The kingdom fled and died.
Dong Zhuo was ashamed and jealous. Therefore, he hated Huangfu Song.
The next year, Dong Zhuo was appointed as the shepherd of Bingzhou, and he was ordered to hand over his troops to Huangfu Song. Dong Zhuo did not obey the imperial order.
Huangfu Song's nephew Huangfu Li was in the army at this time and advised Huangfu Song: "This dynasty is in turmoil, political corruption, and the people are suffering terribly. The only ones who can save the crisis from overthrowing are your Excellency and Dong Zhuo."
Now the two have developed a grudge and are irreconcilable.
Dong Zhuo was ordered to deliver troops to you, but he refused to do so. This is a violation of the emperor's order.
He was delayed because of the chaos in the capital. This was treason.
He is violent and has no loyal people, and his soldiers will not follow him.
Your Excellency is now a marshal. You rely on the power of the country to defeat him. You have shown your loyalty to your superiors and eliminated evil for your subordinates. This is Huan Wen's career!
Huangfu Song said: Although Dong Zhuo is guilty of disobeying orders, I am also responsible for punishing him.
It is better to report it to the court openly and let the court handle it.
So he wrote to the court.
Emperor Ling blamed Dong Zhuo for something wrong. Dong Zhuo resented Huangfu Song even more.
When Dong Zhuo later came to power, in the first year of Chuping, he recruited Huangfu Song as the city gate captain and wanted to kill him.
Huangfu Song was about to go, but Liang Yan, the chief historian, persuaded him: The Han Dynasty was weak and the eunuchs were in chaos. Although Dong Zhuo killed the eunuchs, he could not be loyal to the country. He robbed the counties of the capital, deposed the emperor and established the emperor as he wished.
If you recruit a general today, you will not only suffer great disasters, but you will also suffer humiliation.
Now Dong Zhuo is in Luoyang, and the emperor comes to the west. He uses the general's troops, 30,000 elite soldiers, to welcome the emperor. He is ordered to attack the rebels. He issues orders to the sea, recruits troops, and gathers all the commanders. The Yuan family comes to attack him from the east, and the general goes to attack him from the west. It is not a problem to capture Dong Zhuo.
Huangfu Song refused, so he was called up.
The officials followed Dong Zhuo's order and told Huangfu Song to hand him over to the jailer, preparing to kill him.
Huangfu Song's son Jianshou had a good relationship with Dong Zhuo, so he rushed from Chang'an to Luoyang and defected to Dong Zhuo.
Dong Zhuo was preparing wine to welcome him. Jian Shou walked up to Dong Zhuo and questioned Dong Zhuo. He scolded Dong Zhuo out of righteousness and kowtowed with tears.
Everyone present was moved by this and stood up to ask Dong Zhuo not to kill Huangfu Song. Dong Zhuo got up and took Huangfu Jianshou to sit with him.
He sent someone to free Huangfu Song from prison, and then appointed Huangfu Song as Yilang and promoted to Yushi Zhongcheng.
When he arrived at Dong Zhuo and returned to Chang'an, he was greeted by the officials and ministers at the roadside.
Dong Zhuo hinted that all officials below Zhongcheng, the censor, must bow down and submit to Huangfu Song. After everything was done, he took Huangfu Song's hand and said, "Are you convinced by Yi Zhen?"
Huangfu Song smiled and apologized to him. Dong Zhuo finally relieved his hatred.
When Dong Zhuo was killed, Huangfu Song was appointed General of the Western Conquest and promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
summary: When Dong Zhuo later seized power, he tried to kill Huangfu Song, but his son Jian Shou pleaded successfully. Huangfu Song was eventually released and served as Yilang and Yushi Zhongcheng. After Dong Zhuo's death, he became Grand Commandant, but was dismissed due to a meteor omen. He later died of illness, posthumously honored as General of Hussars.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/皇甫嵩朱俊列传

translation:
In the autumn of this year, he was appointed as Taiwei. In winter, he was dismissed from office due to the appearance of meteors.
He was appointed as Guanglu doctor again and promoted to Taichang.
Not long after, Li Chu rebelled, and Huangfu Song also died of illness. He presented the seal and ribbon to General Hussar and appointed one of his family members as Lang.
Huangfu Song was a benevolent, prudent and diligent person. He wrote more than 500 things that would be beneficial to the country, and then destroyed the drafts and did not publicize them to the outside world.
He was also an open-minded corporal and tried his best to promote him. There was no guest in the house who stayed because he was not recommended.
At that time, people praised him and supported him.
Jianshou was also famous at that time. Later, he became a servant, but he could not resign and died of illness.
◆The biography of Zhu Jun, whose courtesy name is Gongwei, was from Shangyu County, Kuaiji County.
My father died when I was young, and my mother used to sell silk fabrics.
Zhu Jun was famous for being a filial piety to his mother, and he served as a secretary in the county. He loved justice more than wealth, and the villagers admired him very much.
At that time, Zhou Gui of the same county summoned the government, and when he set out on his journey, he borrowed a million dollars from the county treasury to pay for clothing. Later, the county urgently demanded payment, and Zhou Gui's family was too poor to pay back. Zhu Jun stole his mother's silk to prepare money for Zhou Gui to solve the problem.
As a result, his mother lost her inheritance and became furious and scolded him.
Zhu Jun said: A small loss will lead to a big benefit. It is inevitable to be poor first and then rich.
Yangdu Shang, the magistrate of Shangyu County, met Zhu Jun and thought he was not an ordinary person. He introduced him to Wei Yi, the prefect, and he took up some positions in the county. The succeeding prefect Yin Duan took Zhu Jun as his chief official.
In the second year of Xiping's reign, Yin Duan was impeached by the state because he failed to attack the traitor Xu Zhao. He was guilty of abandoning the city.
Zhu Jun wore rags, walked along the narrow road, brought hundreds of gold to the capital, and bribed the officials in charge of the memorial. Because he was able to change the memorial to Dingzhou, Yin Duan was sent to Zuo School for labor reform.
Yin Duan was very happy that he was exempted from the exemption, but he didn't know the reason, and Zhu Jun never said it.
Later, the prefect Xu Wanggui promoted Zhu Jun to be filial and honest, and was promoted to the Lanling Order. His political achievements were very good, and he was commended by the Prime Minister of the East China Sea.
At this time, a group of thieves broke out in Jiaozhi tribe, but Mu Shou was too weak to stop them.
He also handed over the rebels Liang Long and more than 10,000 people, who rebelled with Kong Zhi, the prefect of Nanhai, and conquered the counties.
In the first year of Guanghe, he appointed Zhu Jun as the governor of Jiaochengzhi. He ordered Zhu Jun to recruit 5,000 soldiers in the county plus the ones he had dispatched. They marched in two directions and arrived at the state border. He stopped advancing. He first sent envoys to the county to observe the strength of the thieves and publicize the power of the court to shake their hearts. Then he joined forces with the soldiers of the seven counties to force the thieves. He killed Liang Long and tens of thousands of people surrendered. They were all pacified within a month.
Zhu Jun was granted the title of Marquis of Tingting in the capital for his meritorious service, with 1,500 households, 50 jins of gold, and conscription as an admonishment official.
When the Yellow Turban bandits arose, many ministers recommended Zhu Jun as a talented man. He was appointed as the Right Zhonglang General, holding the emperor's festival, and he and the Zuo Zhonglang General Huangfu Song attacked the Yingchuan, Runan, and Chen Kingdom thieves, and they were all put down.
Huangfu Song went up to report on the situation of pacifying the thieves, and attributed the credit to Zhu Jun. Therefore, the Jin Dynasty granted Zhu Jun the title of Marquis of Xixiang, and promoted him to the rank of Lang General in the town of thieves.
At this time, Zhang Mancheng, a yellow turban in Nanyang, raised an army. He claimed to be the envoy of the gods and had tens of thousands of people. He killed Chu Gong, the governor of the county, and stayed in Wanxia for more than a hundred days.
summary: Zhu Jun, styled Gongwei, was from Shangyu, Kuaiji. Orphaned young, he was known for filial piety and generosity. He once stole his mother's silk to help a friend repay a debt. He served as a county official and later bribed officials to save Prefect Yin Duan from punishment. Recommended as Xiaolian, he became Magistrate of Lanling, earning commendation. When the Jiaozhi rebellion erupted, Zhu Jun was appointed Governor of Jiaozhi. He recruited 5,000 troops, pacified the rebels, killed Liang Long, and secured surrender. He was made a Marquis and later served as an admonishment official. During the Yellow Turban rebellion, Zhu Jun was appointed Right General of the Central Army, alongside Huangfu Song. They suppressed rebels in Yingchuan, Runan, and Chen. Huangfu Song credited Zhu Jun, who was made Marquis of Xixiang. Zhu Jun was appointed General of the Right Chariot and Cavalry, then served as Guanglu Doctor. After his mother's death, he returned to office as Master of Works, then Shaofu and Grand Servant. The historian comments that both Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun were talented generals who achieved fame but failed to seize the moment for greater change, adhering to minor loyalties. Huangfu Song's humility and refusal to claim credit preserved his family and wealth, earning praise.

translation:
Later, the prefect Qin Jie killed Zhang Mancheng, and the thieves appointed Zhao Hong as their commander. The army gradually grew to more than 100,000 people and occupied Wancheng.
Zhu Jun, Jingzhou governor Xu Chu and Qin Jie gathered 18,000 troops to surround Zhao Hong. From June to August, they could not capture Zhao Hong.
The manager wanted to recruit Zhu Jun.
Sikong Zhang Wen Shangshu said: In the past, the Qin State appointed Bai Qi, and the Yan State appointed Le Yi. It took many years before they could defeat the enemy.
Zhu Jun's crusade against the Yingchuan bandits has been successful. He has led his troops to the south. The plan has been made. Changing generals before the battle is taboo for military strategists. Zhu Jun should be given some time to win.
Therefore, Emperor Ling did not recruit Zhu Jun.
Zhu Jun therefore attacked Zhao Hong severely and finally killed him.
The remaining thief commander Han Zhong took Wan again to resist Zhu Jun.
The Jie soldiers were few and invincible, so they set up a siege and fortified the city. They raised earthen hills to serve as the inner city and beat drums to attack the southwestern side of the city. The thieves attacked with all their strength.
Zhu Jun himself led five thousand elite troops, assaulted the northeast of the city, and climbed into the city.
Han Zhong had no choice but to withdraw from the small town and asked to surrender in fear.
Sima Zhang Chao, Xu Chu and Qin Jie all wanted to accept Han Zhong's surrender.
Zhu Jun said: The military has the same physical appearance but different potential.
In the past, during the reign of Qin Xiang, the people had no fixed masters, so they rewarded those who came to join him to encourage those who had not yet returned.
Now that the country is unified, only the Yellow Turbans can cause chaos. Accepting surrender cannot encourage good people, and only crusade can punish evildoers.
Accepting surrender now will further encourage the idea of ​​​​causing chaos. If it is advantageous to the thieves, they will go to war. If it is not advantageous, they will beg for surrender. It is not a good idea to indulge the enemy and encourage the rebellion.
Due to the hasty attack, they were unable to win consecutive battles.
Zhu Gan climbed up Tushan Mountain to look around, then turned around and said to Zhang Chao: I understand!
The thieves' outer perimeter was strong, but the inner camp was pressed hard. They could neither surrender nor escape, so they fought to the death.
It’s not enough for ten thousand people to unite, let alone one hundred thousand!
The harm of a strong attack is too great.
It is better to remove the siege and gather the troops into the city.
When Han Zhong saw that the siege had been lifted, he would definitely come out on his own. When he came out, his thoughts would disperse. This is an easy way to break through.
After the siege was lifted, Han Zhong came out to ask for a battle, and Zhu Jun attacked and won a great victory. And they took advantage of the victory and pursued for dozens of miles, beheading more than 10,000 people.
Han Zhong and others surrendered.
But because Qin Jie hated Han Zhong and killed him, the remaining thieves were frightened and uneasy, so they still stationed themselves in Wanzhong with Sun Xia as their commander.
Zhu Jun rushed to attack, but Sun Xia escaped and chased him to Jingshan Mountain in western Hubei. He defeated him again and beheaded more than ten thousand people before the thieves were disbanded.
summary: Zhu Jun then besieged Nanyang Yellow Turban leader Zhao Hong at Wancheng for months. Despite advice to replace him, the court persisted. Zhu Jun killed Zhao Hong, then faced Han Zhong. Feigning weakness, he attacked the city's northeast, forcing Han Zhong to retreat. When Han Zhong sought surrender, Zhu Jun refused, arguing it would encourage rebellion. He lifted the siege, allowing Han Zhong to scatter, then defeated him, beheading over 10,000. After Han Zhong was killed by Prefect Qin Jie, Zhu Jun defeated Sun Xia, ending the rebellion.

translation:
In the spring of the next year, the imperial court sent an envoy to appoint Zhu Jun as the Right Cavalry General on the Emperor's Day. He returned to the capital in triumph and was appointed Guanglu Doctor.
He resigned from the official position due to the death of his mother, and later came out from home to serve as an official. He was appointed as a master craftsman, and transferred to the Shaofu and Tai servants.
Since the Yellow Turban rebellion, there have been countless followers from Heishan, Huanglong, Baibo, Zuoxiao, Guo Daxian, Yu Digen, Qingniujiao, Zhang Baiqi, Liu Shi, Zuo Zhuzhangba, Pinghan, Daji, Sili, Juzai, Lei Gong, Fuyun, Feiyan, Baique, Yangfeng, Yudu, Wulu, Li Damu, Bairao, Qigu, and Kuca, and they have appeared in the valley.
Among them, the loud one is called Lei Gong, the one riding a white horse is called Zhang Baiqi, the brisk one is called Feiyan, the one with many beards is called Yu Digen, and the one with big eyes is called Damu. Each of these titles has its own reasons.
The big one has 20,000 to 30,000 people, and the small one has 6,000 to 7,000 people.
Zhang Yan, a bandit commander from Changshan, was light, brave and good at walking, so he was called Feiyan in the army.
He was very loved by the soldiers, and interacted with bandits in Zhongshan, Changshan, Zhaojun, Shangdang, and Hanoi valleys. Their number reached one million, and they were called Black Mountain Bandits.
All counties and counties in Hebei suffered from them, and the imperial court could not attack them.
Zhang Yan sent an envoy to the capital to beg for surrender. The imperial court awarded Zhang Yan the rank of Lieutenant General in times of difficulty, allowing him to manage affairs in the valleys of Hebei. He could be promoted to filial piety, honesty, and planning officials every year.
Zhang Yan gradually invaded Hanoi and approached the capital, so he appointed Zhu Jun as the governor of Hanoi and led his troops to repel him.
After that, many of the thieves were put down by Yuan Shao, which was recorded in the "Biography of Yuan Shao". Zhu Jun was again appointed as the Guanglu doctor, and he was assigned to the garrison and cavalry. Soon, he was awarded the title of Chengmen Xiaowei and Henan Yin.
At this time, Dong Zhuo was in power and thought Zhu Jun was a veteran. On the surface, he pretended to trust him, but in his heart he was jealous of him.
When the Kwantung Army became powerful, Dong Zhuo was afraid. He convened many meetings with ministers and moved the capital to Chang'an, but Zhu Jun often stopped him.
Although Dong Zhuo hated Zhu Jun for opposing him, he wanted to take advantage of his fame, so he asked him to be promoted to Taiwen as his deputy.
The imperial envoy offered him an official position, but Zhu Junci refused to accept it.
He said: If the country's capital moves westward, it will definitely disappoint the hopes of the people of the world and become a disaster for Shandong. I don't see how it is right.
The messenger asked: I called you to worship, but you refused. I didn't ask you about moving the capital, but you talked about moving the capital. What's the reason?
Zhu Jun said: I am not qualified to be the deputy prime minister; moving the capital is not a top priority.
It is appropriate for me to resign those who are incompetent and say that those are not the urgent matters of the day.
The envoy said: I have never heard of the capital relocation, and the state has not announced it. How did you know about it?
Zhu Jun said: Prime Minister Dong Zhuo told me everything, so I know!
People could not submit to him, so he was not appointed as the deputy prime minister.
summary: Later, the Black Mountain bandits, led by Zhang Yan, emerged with over a million followers. Zhu Jun was appointed Governor of Henei to repel them. Under Dong Zhuo's rule, Zhu Jun opposed moving the capital to Chang'an. He later conspired with Shandong generals, fled to Jingzhou, then returned to Luoyang, garrisoning Zhongmou. He called for troops against Dong Zhuo, but was defeated by Li Jue and Guo Si.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/皇甫嵩朱俊列传

translation:
Dong Zhuo later entered the Pass and left Zhu Jun to guard Luoyang. Zhu Jun conspired with the Shandong generals to act as an internal agent.
Later, he was afraid of being attacked by Dong Zhuo, so he abandoned his official position and ran to Jingzhou.
Dong Zhuo appointed Hongnong Yang Yi as Henan Yin and guarded Luoyang.
Zhu Jun heard about it and marched into Luoyang again, but Yang Yi ran away.
Zhu Jun believed that Henan was in ruins and had nothing to rely on, so he went east to garrison Zhongmou and notified the prefectures and counties, asking them to send troops to attack Dong Zhuo.
Tao Qian, the governor of Xuzhou, sent out 3,000 elite soldiers, and other states and counties also gave some. Tao Qian wrote a letter to recommend Zhu Jun as a riding general.
Dong Zhuo found out and sent tens of thousands of his generals, including Li Chun and Guo Si, to Henan to resist Zhu Jun.
Zhu Jun attacked and was defeated by Li Chu and Guo Si.
Zhu Jun himself knew that he was invincible, so he stayed in Guanxia and did not dare to move forward.
After Dong Zhuo was executed, Li Ju and Guo Si rebelled, while Zhu Jun was still in Zhongmu.
Tao Qian believed that Zhu Jun was a famous official with many military exploits and could be appointed to great tasks, so he and other heroes recommended Zhu Jun as the grand master, notified the shepherds, and challenged Li Ju and others to welcome the emperor.
Because the memorial to Zhu Jun said: Tao Qian, the governor of Xuzhou, Zhou Qian, the former governor of Yangzhou, Yinde, the prime minister of Langfu, Liu Kui, the prime minister of the East China Sea, Ji Lian, the prime minister of Pengcheng, Kong Rong, the prime minister of Beihai, Yuan Zhong, the prime minister of Pei, Ying Shao, the prefect of Taishan, Xu Chu, the prefect of Runan, Fu Qian, the former prefect of Jiujiang, Dr. Zheng Xuan, etc., dared to speak out the driving general of Henan Yin Mufu : After the country suffered the disaster of Dong Zhuo, there was also the rebellion of Li Chu and Guo Si. The young master was kidnapped, Zhongliang was brutally killed, Chang'an was isolated, and it was unclear what the good or bad outcome would be.
Therefore, there is no scholar-bureaucrat who is not afraid of being an official and governing people. I think if there are not wise and wise people, how can we stop the chaos!
It has been three years since the army was launched. The states and counties watched each other and did not take credit for attacking. They only fought against each other for selfish reasons and did not trust each other.
The humility and others discussed together to eliminate the difficulties, and they all said: Generals and princes are civilized and military, and they are in line with the times. All upright people will not fail to look up.
Therefore, we encourage each other to select capable troops who can penetrate deep into the enemy's army and point directly at Xianyang. There is a lot of supplies and food, which can last for half a year. With one heart and one mind, we trust the marshal.
At that time, Li Chu used the strategy of Taiwei Zhou Zhong and Shangshu Jia Xu to recruit Zhu Jun to the court.
The military officials were afraid of entering the pass and wanted to respond to Tao Qian and others.
Zhu Jun said: "When summoning ministers with the emperor's order, you should go there without waiting for the carriage, let alone the emperor's edict?"
Moreover, Li Chu and Guo Si were treacherous villains, and Fan Chou was mediocre and useless. They had no other far-reaching plans, and since they were equal in power, trouble was bound to happen.
If I take advantage of their unpreparedness and act suddenly, great things can happen.
So he resigned from Tao Qian and went to Li Chu's recruitment. If he becomes a servant again, Tao Qian and others will have nothing to do.
In the fourth year of Chuping's reign, Zhu Jun replaced Zhou Zhong as Taiwei, and also served as minister of book affairs.
In the autumn of the next year, he was dismissed from his post due to the solar eclipse, and resumed his military duties as a hussar general, holding the Emperor's Festival to guard Kantung.
Before setting off, when Li Chu was about to kill Fan Chou, Guo Si became suspicious and started fighting with Li Chu. Chang'an was in chaos, so Zhu Jun did not go to guard Guandong and stayed in the court as the chief minister.
Emperor Xian ordered Zhu Jun, Taiwei Yang Biao and more than ten people to persuade Guo Si to reconcile with Li Chu.
Guo Si refused and detained Zhu Jun and others as hostages.
Zhu Jun, who always had a strong personality, fell ill and died that day.
Zhu Jun's son Zhu Hao was also talented and virtuous, and was promoted to the governor of Yuzhang.
The historian commented: Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun both received orders when the country was in chaos because of their talents as generals.
summary: After Dong Zhuo's death, Tao Qian and others recommended Zhu Jun as Grand Marshal, but Li Jue and Guo Si summoned him to court. Zhu Jun accepted, becoming Grand Commandant and Minister of Works. He was dismissed due to a solar eclipse, then served as General of Hussars. During Li Jue and Guo Si's conflict, he was taken hostage by Guo Si and died of illness.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/皇甫嵩朱俊列传

translation:
Huangfu Guizhuan, whose courtesy name was Weiming, was from that county in Anding County.
His grandfather Huangfuleng was a general of Liao Dynasty.
His father, Huangfu Banner, was the Commander-in-Chief of Fufeng.
In the sixth year of Yonghe, the Western Qiang invaded Chang'an and the nearby Guanzhong areas, and surrounded Anding. General Ma Xian, the general who conquered the West, led troops from various counties to attack the Qiang, but they failed to win.
Although Huangfu Gui was a civilian at this time, he found that Ma Xian was not worried about the war and judged that he was bound to fail, so he wrote to the court stating Ma Xian's situation and his own views.
Soon Ma Xian was defeated by the Xiqiang. The county governor knew Huangfu Gui's strategy of using soldiers, so he appointed him as a meritorious officer and sent him to lead 800 armed soldiers to fight with the Qiang people and kill several enemies, so the bandits retreated.
Then he recommended Huangfu Gui to the position of planner.
Later, Qiang soldiers gathered in large numbers to attack, burn, and plunder Longxi, and the court thought it was a disaster.
Huangfu went to the imperial court and asked to serve the country, saying: In recent years, I have stated many times the measures to deal with the Western Qiang.
The Qiang Rong had not yet moved, so I expected him to rebel. As soon as Ma Xian sent troops, I knew he would be defeated.
These words said by chance are supported by facts everywhere.
I often think that Ma Xian and others have been holding troops for four years without success. The cost of suspending the army is calculated in tens of billions. This money comes from the common people and falls into the pockets of traitors.
Therefore, the common people in the rivers and lakes gathered together as thieves, there was famine in Qingzhou and Xuzhou, and the old and the weak were scattered.
It turns out that the Qiang Rong rebelled, not when the world was at peace, because the border generals failed to appease and govern them.
They should be in peace, but they invade them. In order to obtain small benefits, they end up causing great harm. In order to prove that they won the battle, they often falsely reported the number of beheadings, and they kept it secret when they lost the battle.
The soldiers worked hard, were full of resentment, and were forced by the treacherous officials. They could not advance quickly to gain fame and retreat, and could not retreat to have enough food and clothing to survive. They starved to death in the ditch and left their corpses scattered everywhere. They saw the king's division send troops in vain, but did not see the king's division come back.
Weeping and weeping for God's sorrow, fearing that something might happen.
Therefore, the period of peace is very short, and once chaos breaks out, it lasts for many years.
This is what I sigh with clapping my hands and tapping my heart.
I hope to give me the strength of the two battalions of Ma Xian and Zhao Chong and the land of the two counties of Anding and Longxi. I will lead five thousand soldiers to sit down and eat. If there is an unexpected Qiang Rong incident, I will be responsible for the head and tail of Zhao Chong, the captain of the Qiang school.
The situation of the land and valleys is familiar to me; the military situation is convenient and I have rectified it.
You don't have to worry about using a square-inch seal to issue documents, and a foot of silk as a reward. High can eliminate worries, and low can accept surrender.
If it is said that I am young and have a low official rank, I cannot be used. Those generals who defeated the army are not high in official rank and young in age.
summary: Huangfu Gui, courtesy name Weiming, was from Anding County. His grandfather served as a Liao general and his father as Commander-in-Chief of Fufeng. During the sixth year of Yonghe, when Western Qiang forces invaded Chang'an and surrounded Anding, General Ma Xian failed to defeat them. Huangfu Gui, though a civilian, recognized Ma Xian's impending defeat and wrote to the court about it. After Ma Xian was defeated, the county governor appointed Huangfu Gui as a meritorious officer. He led 800 soldiers against the Qiang, killing several enemies and causing the bandits to retreat. He was subsequently recommended as a planner.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/皇甫张段列传

translation:
I grew up in a remote place and seldom came to the capital. I was so frightened that I did not speak out everything that was in my heart.
Liang Ji hated Huangfu Gui for mocking him, so he took Huangfu Gui as his subordinate and appointed him as a doctor.
Huangfu Gui excused himself from official duties and returned home due to illness. The prefectures and counties followed Liang Ji's will and almost framed him to death several times.
Huangfu taught more than 300 students using "Poetry" and "Yi" for a total of fourteen years.
Later, Liang Ji was killed. Within a month, the court summoned him five times with courtesy, but he failed.
At this time, the Taishan bandit uncle Sun Wuji invaded the counties, and Zhonglang conquered Zongzi without success.
The character of the bus was called Huangfu Gui, who was appointed as the prefect of Taishan.
Huangfu Gui took office and launched various conquest strategies, and all the bandits were pacified.
In the autumn of the fourth year of Yanxi, the rebellious Qiang Lingwu and others and the Xianling Qiang tribe invaded and plundered Guanzhong. Duan Zhen, the Qiang school captain, was found guilty and summoned.
Later, all kinds of things went rampant and destroyed the camp.
Huangfu Gui was usually familiar with Qiang affairs and was determined to work hard, so Shangshu said: Since my appointment, I have been dull in ambition. It is only thanks to the leadership of the Yanzhou governor that I am honest and brave, and the loyalty of Zhonglang Zongzi has allowed me to uphold the discipline. Fortunately, I don't have a bad reputation.
Now that the cunning Qiang thieves have been exterminated, and most of the Taishan bandits have been put down, it is also heard that the Qiang groups are revolting.
I am Changqi, now fifty-nine years old. I used to be a county official. After several Qiang rebellions, I planned in advance and often said the right things.
I have a stubborn illness and am afraid of dogs and horses. Once I die, I will not be able to repay the emperor's great kindness. Please allow me to serve as an official and prepare a bicycle to comfort the three assistants, promote the country's prestige and grace, and use the familiar terrain and military forces to help the armies.
I have been living in poverty, isolation and danger, watching the commander-in-chief for decades.
From Niao Mo to Dong Dai, it was because the governor did not appease the Qiang and led to rebellion. The cause of the disaster was the same. If you want brave generals, it is better to have a peaceful politics of the Qing Dynasty and to study the military techniques of Wu Qi and Sun Wu than to have a county guard follow the law so that they will not rebel.
The memories of the Qiang rebellion in the past are still fresh in my mind, and I am really worried about this.
Therefore, I went beyond my duties and submitted a letter to fulfill my only patriotic intention.
In winter, all the Qiang people gathered together and were ready to move, and the court felt worried.
Sangong promoted Huangfu Gui to the rank of Zhonglang General, held the emperor's talisman to supervise the Guanxi soldiers, conquered Lingwu and others, defeated them, and beheaded eight hundred people.
There were more than 100,000 Qiang people who envied Huangfu Gui's prestige and persuaded each other to surrender.
The next year, Huangfu Gui took the opportunity to mobilize his cavalry to jointly attack Longyou. However, the roads were blocked and an epidemic broke out in the army. Three or four out of ten people died of the disease.
Huangfu Gui personally entered the nunnery to express condolences to the soldiers. The three armies were grateful and happy.
Because the Eastern Qiang sent envoys to beg for surrender, Liangzhou was no longer blocked.
At that time, Sun Gen, the governor of Anding, was very serious about bribery and corruption. Li Xi, the captain of the country, and Zhang Xun, the governor's censor, killed and surrendered the Qiang. Guo Hong, the governor of Liangzhou, and Zhao Xi, the governor of Hanyang, were both old and weak and could not hold their posts. However, they relied on powerful relatives and did not abide by the laws of the country.
Huangfu Gui arrived at the state border and reported their crimes one by one. Some were removed from their official positions and some were sentenced to death.
After hearing this, the Qiang people quickly surrendered. More than 100,000 people including Dianchang and Xongtian, the great tycoons of the Shen family, surrendered to Huangfu Gui.
Huangfu Gui was born a few years ago and held the Emperor's Talisman as a general. He led the people to perform meritorious service and returned to supervise the countryside. He had no personal favors. On the contrary, he reported many bad people and bad deeds. He also hated eunuchs deeply and refused to associate with them. As a result, people inside and outside the court complained about him, and they all falsely accused Huangfu Gui of bribing the Qiang people and causing them to surrender.
The emperor issued edicts one after another.
Huangfu Gui was afraid that he would be killed, so he complained to Shangshu: In the autumn of the fourth year, Rong Chou made a fool of himself to cause chaos. From Xizhou to Jingyang, the old capital was frightened and the imperial court looked westward.
The imperial edict of the Ming Dynasty did not consider me a fool and ordered me to urgently lead the army on the road.
Thanks to the emperor's power, the country's fortunes were greatly boosted. Qiang and Rong, large and small, kowtowed and submitted. I immediately sent a letter to the military camp and the county guard to inquire how many they had killed and how many they had surrendered. This saved the cost, which was more than 100 million.
summary: When Qiang soldiers later gathered to attack Longxi, Huangfu Gui petitioned the emperor, explaining that the Qiang rebellion resulted from border generals failing to properly govern, instead invading peaceful territories for small gains, falsely reporting victories, and concealing defeats. He requested command of troops from two battalions and two counties to lead 5,000 soldiers against the Qiang, but the emperor did not use him at that time. During the reigns of Emperors Chong and Zhi, when Empress Dowager Liang held power, Huangfu Gui was praised as virtuous and upright. He criticized the court for allowing treacherous ministers to accumulate wealth, sell official positions, and disturb the world. He specifically condemned General Liang Ji and others for their misconduct, urging the dismissal of corrupt officials. Liang Ji hated Huangfu Gui for mocking him and appointed him as a doctor, but Huangfu Gui excused himself due to illness and returned home, teaching over 300 students for fourteen years. After Liang Ji was killed, the court summoned Huangfu Gui five times but he did not respond. He was later appointed as the prefect of Taishan to deal with bandit Sun Wuji, and he successfully pacified all the bandits. In the fourth year of Yanxi, when Qiang forces invaded Guanzhong, Huangfu Gui, familiar with Qiang affairs, petitioned to serve. He was promoted to Zhonglang General and defeated the Qiang, beheading 800 people. Over 100,000 Qiang people surrendered due to his prestige. However, Huangfu Gui reported the crimes of corrupt officials, including the governor of Anding and others, leading to their removal or execution. This made him enemies both inside and outside the court, who falsely accused him of bribing the Qiang. Huangfu Gui defended himself, explaining that his actions saved over 100 million in costs and that his expenditures were documented. Despite his merits, eunuchs Xu Huang and Zuo Xiang demanded bribes from him, and when he refused, they framed him. He was sentenced to hard labor but was released after an amnesty.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/皇甫张段列传

translation:
Zhang Huan, the commander-in-chief, is very talented and strategic. He should be appointed as the marshal in order to meet everyone's expectations.
If I can still serve in the military, I would like to be given a casual official position as Zhang Huan's assistant.
The imperial court approved his request, and Zhang Huan was appointed as the general to conquer the Liao Dynasty, and Huangfu Gui was appointed as the envoy to the Xiongnu Zhonglang General. Later, Zhang Huan was promoted to the chief minister of agriculture, and Huangfu Gui was appointed as the general to conquer the Liao Dynasty again.
Huangfu Gui was very scheming. He thought that he was still in the high position, and wanted to retire quickly and stop serving as an official. He wrote many times to complain about his illness, but no one listened.
When the coffin of his friend Wang, the governor of Shangjun, passed away and returned to his hometown, Huangfu Gui crossed the border in white plain clothes and went to the lower pavilion to welcome the funeral.
Yin Lingke secretly told Hu Fang, the governor of Bingzhou, that Huangfu Gui stayed away from the military camp without permission and blatantly violated the ban, so he should report it immediately.
Hu Fang said: Wei Ming wanted to return home and leave his official career, so he inspired me.
I should love talents for the imperial court, so how can I help him with his plans?
Ignore him.
Later, party affairs broke out, and many celebrities and sages in the world were implicated. Although Huangfu Gui was a famous general, he was not usually well-known.
He considered himself a hero of Xizhou, and thought it was shameful that he was not involved in party affairs, so he wrote to him first and said: I used to recommend Zhang Huan, the great minister of agriculture, but this was a sign of being a party member.
Also, when I was undergoing reform through labor at the Left School, Taipei student Zhang Feng and others wrote a letter to appeal on my behalf. This was a party member trying to win over me, and I should be held accountable.
The imperial court knew this but did not hold anyone accountable. People at that time thought Huangfu Gui was a wise man.
During the past few years, nothing happened on the northern border. In the first year of Yongkang, he was recruited as a minister. In the summer of that year, there was a solar eclipse. The emperor ordered the ministers to recommend virtuous and upright people and ask about political gains and losses.
Huangfu Gui replied: God treats a king just as a king treats his ministers, and a father treats his son. He warns him with disasters and monsters, so that he can achieve happiness and good fortune.
During the eight years of the emperor's reign, he cleared prisons three times, eliminated his internal concubines once, and then executed his foreign ministers.
However, there are still disasters and uneasy relationships, probably due to the appointment of wise and foolish people and the implementation of criminal laws, which are also unreasonable.
Former Taiwei Chen Fan and Liu Ju were loyal and outstanding, but were discarded; Liu, Feng Nui, Zhao Dian, and Yin Xun were upright and resentful, so they were exiled; Li Ying, Wang Chang, and Kong Yi were honest and law-abiding, and were never appointed as prime ministers.
As for the so-called party imprisonment, it is simply created out of nothing to torture good people and cause harm to many innocent people.
Nowadays, it is easy to do good and eliminate evil. The officials kept silent because they took the past events as a warning and looked at each other, not daring to tell the truth.
I only hope that the emperor will be wise and tolerate honest and honest advice, then the mistakes of the past can be eliminated, and future blessings will come.
The emperor ignored his words.
He transferred Huangfu to serve as the prefect of Hongnong, and granted him the title of Marquis of Ting, with 200 households in the city. Huangfu humbly refused to comply with the regulations.
summary: Huangfu Gui later recommended General Zhang Huan to replace him as commander. He was appointed as General Conquering Liao, but repeatedly requested retirement due to illness. When party affairs broke out, Huangfu Gui, considering himself a hero of Xizhou, felt ashamed not to be implicated and wrote to claim involvement, but the court did not hold him accountable. He died at age seventy-one, leaving twenty-seven written works. The historian commented that Huangfu Gui's words matched his actions, and he achieved success in military affairs without greed or arrogance.

translation:
He was then transferred to the rank of Colonel Protecting Qiang.
In the third year of Xiping's reign, he was recalled to the court due to illness, but he did not arrive and died in Yuncheng at the age of seventy-one.
He wrote a total of twenty-seven articles including poems, inscriptions, tablets, praises, prayers, condolences, chapters, orders, letters, epistles, and notes.
Historian's comment: Confucius said: If you speak well, you will not feel ashamed, but doing it is not easy.
After examining what Huangfu Gui said, he would not be ashamed in his heart!
Seeking an official position based on one's own talents, and giving the position to others when he sees someone smarter than himself; therefore, his seeking an official position is not considered greedy, and giving the position to others is not asking for concessions; he does not doubt his own talents, and does not brag, so that people have no fear.
Therefore, you can achieve success in the army and Di, and achieve good things for your family and country.
◆The biography of Zhang Huan, named Ranming, was from Yuanquan County, Dunhuang County.
His father, Zhang, was the governor of Hanyang.
When Zhang Huan was young, he traveled to study at Sanfu, where he studied "Ouyang Shangshu" with Taiwei Zhu Chong as his teacher.
At first, "Mou's Chapters" contained many redundant words and phrases, with more than 450,000 words, but Zhang Huan cut it down to 90,000 words.
Later, the general Liang Jifu was recruited, so he wrote to Emperor Huan and presented his "Zhangju" and ordered him to serve in Dongguan. He was dismissed from the official position due to illness, and was recommended as a virtuous person. When the emperor asked for advice, he answered first, and was promoted to Yilang.
In the first year of Yongshou, he was transferred to the capital of Anding.
Just after taking office, more than 7,000 people including Zuo Ge, Qiequ Bode and others from the Southern Xiongnu invaded Meiji. The Eastern Qiang responded to them all again. There were only 200 people in Zhang Huan's position. When he heard the alarm, he led his troops out.
The military officials believed that they were not as powerful as the enemy and kowtowed to stop them. Zhang Huan refused to listen. They stationed at the Great Wall, gathered soldiers, and sent general Wang Wei to lure the Eastern Qiang. They occupied Qiuci so that the Southern Huns could not communicate with the Eastern Qiang.
The leaders of various ministries made peace with Zhang Huan, and together they attacked the Gejian and other ministries. They defeated the Gejian and other ministries in several consecutive battles.
Byrd was frightened and led his men to surrender, and the county was at peace.
The Qiang marshal was grateful for Zhang Huan's kindness and presented him with twenty horses. Chief Xianling also presented eight gold taels. Zhang Huan accepted it, but called the chief clerk in front of each Qiang, poured wine over it and said: If the horse is like a sheep, it cannot be put into the stable; if the gold is like millet, it cannot be put into the bosom.
All the golden horses were returned to the marshal and chief.
The Qiang people are greedy in nature, but they respect honest officials the most. In the past, the eight captains were all fond of wealth and suffered from them.
Promoted to the Xiongnu Zhonglang General.
At this time, Xiutuge and Wuhuan of Shuofang rebelled at the same time. They burned the general gate of Duliao and stationed in Chinankang, facing each other with fireworks.
The army was frightened and wanted to escape.
summary: Zhang Huan, courtesy name Ranming, was from Dunhuang County. He studied at Sanfu and later reduced a lengthy text from over 450,000 words to 90,000 words. After serving as a gentleman, he was transferred to Anding. When Southern Xiongnu and Eastern Qiang forces invaded with 7,000 men, Zhang Huan led only 200 troops but stationed at the Great Wall, gathered soldiers, and lured the Eastern Qiang to make peace. Together they attacked and defeated the invaders. The Qiang marshal presented him with twenty horses and eight gold taels, but Zhang Huan returned them, saying gold and horses could not be kept. He was promoted to Xiongnu Zhonglang General. When Xiutuge and Wuhuan rebelled, Zhang Huan calmly sat in his tent while others panicked, secretly lured Wuhuan to make peace, and defeated the rebels. After Liang Ji was executed, Zhang Huan was dismissed as his subordinate. Huangfu Gui recommended him seven times. He later served as prefect of Wuwei, where he changed the custom of killing children born in certain months. He was appointed General of Liao Dynasty, and for several years the border was peaceful.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/皇甫张段列传

translation:
Zhang Huan sat safely in the curtain, talking and reciting to his disciples freely, and his subordinates finally settled down a little.
So he secretly lured Wuhuan to make peace with him, ordered the generals to behead Xiutu, and attacked them suddenly, defeating them, and all the Husbands surrendered.
In the first year of Yanxi, Xianbei invaded the border. Zhang Huan led Nan Shanyu to attack them and beheaded hundreds of them.
The next year, Liang Ji was executed. Zhang Huan was dismissed from office because he was a subordinate of Liang Ji, and was banned from serving as an official.
Zhang Huan and Huangfu Gui were good friends, but Zhang Huan had been imprisoned. None of his old friends and relatives dared to speak for Zhang Huan. Only Huangfu recommended Zhang Huan seven times.
After living at home for four years, he was appointed as the prefect of Wuwei.
Counties are best at balancing the burdens of the common people and leading and training the fleeing soldiers and civilians. Hexi was thus preserved.
There are many monsters and taboos in the customs of Hexi. All sons born in February and May, as well as those born in the same month as their parents, must be killed.
Zhang Huan taught him the responsibility of being a parent and set strict rewards and punishments. As a result, customs changed and the people built a shrine in his honor.
He was recommended by You Yi as the general of Liao Dynasty.
In the past few years, Youzhou and Bingzhou were quiet and peaceful.
In the spring of the ninth year, he was recruited and appointed as the chief agricultural officer.
When Xianbei heard about Zhang Huan's mobilization, that summer, he summoned the Southern Xiongnu and Wuhuan to invade the fortress in several groups. Some had five or six thousand cavalry, and some had three or four thousand cavalry. They invaded and plundered the nine surrounding counties, killing and plundering the people.
In autumn, Xianbei led eight or nine thousand cavalry to invade the fortress and lured the Dong Qiang to make an alliance with them.
So the Shen family of Shangjun, Anding Xianling and others invaded Wuwei and Zhangye together, causing great harm to the border area.
The court felt worried. Zhang Huan was then appointed as the Zhonglang General who protected the Xiongnu. According to the position of Jiuqing, he would oversee the three states of You, Bing, and Liang, as well as the two camps of Liao and Wuhuan. He also inspected the governor and inspected the competent and incompetent officials with two thousand stones. He was rewarded with many rewards.
When the Xiongnu and Wuhuan heard that Zhang Huan was coming, they led the Prime Minister back, and a total of 200,000 people surrendered.
Zhang Huan only killed the most guilty ones, and the rest of the people comforted and accepted them.
Only Xianbei went beyond the Great Wall.
In the spring of the first year of Yongkang, five or six thousand cavalry from Dong Qiang and Xian Ling invaded Guanzhong, surrounded 绻箳礻yu, and captured Yunyang.
In the summer, they attacked Yuying again and killed more than a thousand people.
In winter, Qiang Anwei, Mo Ni, etc., threatened the same species and robbed Sanfu again.
Zhang Huan sent Sima Yin Duan and Dong Zhuo to attack together. They defeated them completely, beheaded their leaders, captured more than 10,000 people, and pacified the three states.
In terms of merit, Zhang Huan should be ennobled, but Zhang Huan did not make friends with eunuchs, so the matter of ennobling him was not carried out. He only gave 200,000 yuan in money and appointed one of his family members as a man, but Zhang Huan did not accept it and asked to move to Huayin County, Hongnong.
Under the old system, people from the border were not allowed to move inward. Only Zhang Huan was allowed to move in because of his merit, so Zhang Huan became a Hongnong native.
In the first year of Jianning, he led his army back to the dynasty.
At this time, Empress Dowager Dou came to power. General Dou Wu and Tai Fu Chen Fan plotted to kill the eunuchs. The matter was leaked out, and Zhongchang Shi Cao Jie and others caused trouble. Because Zhang Huanxin was recruited, they did not know about the plan. Cao Jie and others pretended to entrust Zhang Huan to the imperial court, and Shaofu Zhou Jing led five battalions to surround Dou Wu. Dou Wu committed suicide, and Chen Fan was also killed.
Zhang Huan was promoted to the post of Shaofu and then to the post of Chief Agriculture Officer, and was granted the title of Marquis for his meritorious service.
Zhang Huan was devastated to be betrayed by Cao Jie, so he resolutely resigned in a letter and returned the seal and ribbon, but finally refused to accept it.
In the summer of the second year, a green snake was found in front of the imperial pavilion. There was also strong wind, rain, hail, and thunder uprooting trees, and the officials were ordered to report the unusual disaster.
Zhang Huan Shangshu said: I heard that wind is the command, animals are ventilated, wood is born from fire, and wind and fire interact to produce light.
summary: When Xianbei invaded, Zhang Huan was recalled to defend against them. Over 200,000 Xiongnu and Wuhuan surrendered. He was later deceived by eunuch Cao Jie into surrounding General Dou Wu, who committed suicide. Zhang Huan was devastated and refused the marquis title granted for this action. He later petitioned to rebury Dou Wu and Chen Fan and vindicate those imprisoned for their association, but eunuchs opposed this. Zhang Huan was eventually banned from office due to party crimes. He educated thousands of disciples and wrote over 300,000 words. He died at age seventy-eight, leaving instructions for a simple burial. His sons were famous for cursive calligraphy.

translation:
Because he was afraid that the thieves would flee in fear, he sent a post rider to pretend to deliver a seal to order Duan Jiong to retreat. Duan Jiong pretended to retreat on the road and set up an ambush on the retreating road.
Xianbei thought that Duan Jiong was really retreating and pursued Duan Jiong.
Duan Qiao then sent out a large number of troops, and all the Xianbei invaders were captured.
Duan Jong, however, deserved severe punishment for falsely claiming to be the official seal official. Because of his meritorious service, he was punished as a bandit and sent to the border to defend against enemies.
After serving his sentence, he was appointed as Yilang.
At this time, Taishan, Langfu bandits Dongguo Dou, Gongsun Ju and others gathered 30,000 people and destroyed the counties. The imperial court sent troops to suppress the rebellion, which could not be quelled for several years.
In the second year of Yongshou's reign, Emperor Huan ordered the ministers to elect those with all-round talents in both civil and military affairs as generals. Situ Yin Song recommended Duan Jiong, and Duan Jiong was awarded the title of Zhonglang General.
He conquered Dongguo Dou, Gongsun Ju and others and won a great victory. He killed Dongguo Dou and Gongsun Ju and gained more than 10,000 leaders. Some of the remaining party members fled and some surrendered.
He made Duanju a prince, rewarded him with 500,000 yuan, and appointed one of his sons as a doctor.
In the second year of Yanxi's reign, he was promoted to the rank of Colonel Protecting Qiang.
When eight kinds of Qiang including Shaodang, Shaohe, Dangjian and Lejie invaded the borders of Longxi and Jincheng, Duan Jun led his troops and 12,000 Huangzhong uprising Qiang cavalry out of Huanggu and defeated them.
Pursuing the remaining troops who fled south across the Yellow River, they sent military officials Tian Yan and Xia Yu to recruit warriors to ascend first and use ropes to pull them up. They then fought at Luoting and won a great victory. They killed 2,000 people under their leader and captured more than 10,000 people. The remaining captives fled.
In the spring of the second year, the remaining Qiang captives and Marshal Shao He invaded Zhangye, captured Juluwu, and killed the officials and people of the country. They also summoned more than a thousand tribesmen of their own kind and concentrated their forces to attack Duan Jiong's troops at dawn.
Duan Jiong dismounted and fought with them. The battle lasted until noon, when all the swords and arrows were broken and the prisoners retreated.
Duan Jiao pursued, fighting and walking at the same time, fighting day and night, cutting flesh and swallowing snow. After more than forty days, they arrived at Jishi Mountain, the source of the Yellow River, and traveled more than 2,000 miles beyond the Great Wall. They beheaded and burned Marshal He, and killed and captured more than 5,000 people.
They also divided their troops to attack the Shicheng Qiang and killed 1,600 people who drowned.
More than ninety people from Shaodangzhong surrendered to Duan Jiong.
When the Qiang hybrids were stationed in Baishi, Duan Jong sent troops to attack, beheading and capturing more than 3,000 people.
In winter, Le Jie and Ling Wuzhong surrounded Yunjie, killing and robbing officials and people. Duan Juan organized a rescue camp and captured hundreds of people.
In the winter of the fourth year, Shen Di, Longxi Laojie, and Wuwu Qiang from Shangjun jointly invaded the two prefectures of Bing and Liang. Duan Jun led the Qiang uprising in Huangzhong to conquer them.
Guo Hong, the governor of Liangzhou, shared the military exploits with Duan Jiong and delayed and stopped Duan Jiong's army from advancing.
The uprising Qiang had been fighting for too long and missed their hometown, so they all rebelled.
Guo Hong put the blame on Duan Jiong, who was therefore arrested and imprisoned and sentenced to hard labor.
The Qiang pirates became more rampant, captured camps, and colluded with each other to disrupt various counties. So thousands of officials and people stayed at the court to appeal to Duan Jiong.
The imperial court knew that Duan Jiong had been framed by Guo Hong, and the emperor issued an edict to inquire about Duan Jiong's situation.
Duan Jiong just apologized and did not dare to say that he had been wronged. The capital called Duan Jiong an elder.
He was transferred from among the criminals, appointed as Yilang, and promoted to governor of Bingzhou.
At that time, five or six thousand Qiang people from Dian and other tribes invaded Wuwei, Zhangye, and Jiuquan and burned people's houses.
In six years, the enemy forces became stronger and Liangzhou almost fell.
In the winter, Duan Ji was appointed as the captain of the Qiang Guard, and he rushed to his post by post.
In the spring of the next year, 355 Qiang marshals including Fengshuang, Liangduo, and Dianna led 3,000 tribesmen and surrendered in front of Duan Jiao's army.
Dangjian and Lejiezhong also gathered and stationed themselves.
In winter, Duan Juan defeated them with more than 10,000 people, beheaded their commander, and killed more than 4,000 prisoners.
In the spring of the eighth year, Duan Juan attacked Lejiezhong again, beheading more than 400 people and surrendering more than 2,000 people.
In the summer, they marched to attack Dang Jianzhong in Huangzhong. Duan Zhao's soldiers were defeated and were besieged for three days. He used the hermit Fan Zhi to devise a strategy and secretly sent out troops at night, beating drums to fight back. They defeated the rebel army and killed thousands of people.
Duan Jiong pursued them fiercely, moving through the valleys, fighting every day from spring to autumn. As a result, the enemy was hungry and sleepy, so they fled and went north to invade the Wuwei area.
Duan Juan defeated the Xiqiang, beheading 23,000 people in total, captured tens of thousands of people, and captured 8 million horses, cattle and sheep. More than 10,000 tribesmen surrendered.
He was granted the title of Marquis of Duanjudu Township, with a settlement of 500 households.
In the first year of Yongkang, Dangjian Zhuzhong rebelled and gathered more than 4,000 people to attack Wuwei. Duan Jiong pursued Luanniao and completely defeated them. He killed their leader and beheaded more than 3,000 people. The Xiqiang was pacified from then on.
Since the Eastern Qiang Xianling and others defeated the general Ma Xian who conquered the West, the imperial court was unable to conquer and often harassed the three assistants.
Later, the Liao generals Huangfu Gui and Zhonglang general Zhang Huan tried to surrender year after year, but they always surrendered and then rebelled.
Emperor Huan issued an edict and asked Duan Qiang: "Xian Ling Dong Qiang rebelled against evil, but Huangfu Gui and Zhang Huan each had elite troops and could not quell them on time."
summary: Duan Jiong, courtesy name Jiming, was from Wuwei County. He learned horse racing and archery as a youth but later turned to ancient learning. He served as a captain and used a clever ambush to capture Xianbei invaders. He was appointed Zhonglang General to suppress bandits in Taishan, killing their leaders and gaining over 10,000 heads. He was promoted to Colonel Protecting Qiang and fought numerous battles against various Qiang groups, killing thousands and capturing tens of thousands. He was imprisoned due to a governor's false accusations but was later released and appointed governor of Bingzhou. He was again appointed Colonel Protecting Qiang and defeated the Qiang, beheading 23,000 and capturing tens of thousands. He was granted a marquis title. When Emperor Huan asked about dealing with Eastern Qiang, Duan Jiong argued that the Qiang could not be won over with kindness and would rebel again after surrendering. He proposed using 5,000 cavalry, 10,000 infantry, and 3,000 chariots to completely defeat them in two or three years. The emperor agreed. Duan Jiong fought 180 battles, beheading over 38,600 enemies and capturing over 427,500 animals, at a cost of 4.4 billion. He was granted a county marquis title. He later relied on eunuchs and unjustly killed several people. He served as Taiwei but committed suicide in prison after being implicated in a murder. The three men were collectively known as "Liangzhou Sanming."
