translation:
◆Dou Wu's biography, Dou Wu's courtesy name is You Ping, a native of Pingling County, Fufeng County, and the great-great-grandson of Dai Hourong of Anfeng County.
His father, Dou Feng, was the prefect of Dingxiang.
When Dou Wu was young, he was famous for his virtues in Confucian classics. He once taught Osawa Zhong. He was not involved in current affairs, and his reputation was prominent in the Kansai area.
In the eighth year of Yanxi's reign, the eldest daughter was elected to the palace. Emperor Huan appointed her as a nobleman and appointed Dou Wu as the doctor.
In the winter of this year, the noble lady was made queen, Dou Wu was promoted to Yueqi Xiaowei, and was granted the title of Marquis of Huaili, with 5,000 households.
In the winter of the second year, he was awarded the title of captain of the city gate.
During his tenure, he recruited famous people, was honest and dedicated to the public affairs, deeply hated bad people and bad deeds, did not accept gifts or bribes, and his wife had only enough food and clothing for food and clothing.
At this time, the Qiang barbarians were in rebellion, the harvest was poor, and the people were hungry. General Dou gave all the rewards from the two palaces to the students of the Imperial Academy, and he also used carts to carry food and meals to the poor on the roads.
Dou Shao, the son of Dou Wu's brother, was appointed as Huben's lieutenant general and had a lazy and extravagant temperament.
Dou Wu often reprimanded him severely, but he still didn't realize it, so he wrote a letter requesting that Dou Shao be removed from his post. He also blamed himself for not being able to discipline Dou Shao well and that he should suffer first.
From then on, Dou Shao abided by restraint and did not dare to violate anything illegal, no matter how big or small.
At that time, there were many political mistakes in the country. The eunuchs had exclusive power. Li Ying, Du Mi and others were arrested and interrogated for party affairs.
In the first year of Yongkang, Dou Wu Shangshu said: I heard that a wise emperor is not afraid of people saying sarcastic words in order to understand some dark facts; loyal ministers are not afraid of causing harm by admonishing the emperor, in order to make everything smooth for the country.
Therefore, the harmony between the monarch and his ministers will be famous for centuries.
I was lucky enough to live in the prosperous Ming Dynasty and be enlightened by civil and military forces. How dare I protect the throne in order to escape crime and not be sincere and wise to the emperor?
The emperor first lived in a vassal state and later ascended to the throne. The whole world rejoiced and thought it was the rejuvenation of the country.
However, since taking office, no good political measures have been seen.
Although Liang Ji, Sun Shou, Kou Rong, and Deng Wandai were executed, the eunuchs who often served him continued to cause trouble, bully His Majesty, and engage in deceit. They created systems without authorization and gave officials and titles to bad people at will. The politics of the court became worse day by day, and the treacherous ministers became stronger day by day. I recall that the Western Han Dynasty indulged the Wang family and ruled with flattering ministers, and finally lost the world.
Ignore the lessons of previous failures and continue on the wrong track; I am afraid that the disaster of Hu Hai, the second emperor of the Qin Dynasty, will definitely happen again, and the chaos of Zhao Gao will come either in the morning or in the evening.
summary: Dou Wu, a native of Fufeng, was known for his virtue and Confucian scholarship. He entered officialdom after his daughter became Empress to Emperor Huan, rising to Colonel of the City Gates. He was known for his integrity, recruiting worthy men, and refusing bribes. During a famine, he distributed his own rewards to students and the poor. He strictly disciplined his extravagant nephew, Dou Shao, even requesting his dismissal. When eunuchs seized power and arrested scholars like Li Ying and Du Mi in a party affair, Dou Wu memorialized the emperor, criticizing the eunuchs' corruption and warning of historical disasters like the fall of the Qin dynasty. He defended the arrested scholars and recommended virtuous ministers. After Emperor Huan died without an heir, Dou Wu consulted with an official and installed Liu Hong as Emperor Ling. He was made a general and marquis.

translation:
Dou Wu did not listen to his opinions and ordered Shan Bing, Yin Xun, and Shi Yushi Zhu Wangjin to interrogate Zheng Sa in a chaotic manner. Sa's confession implicated Cao Jie and Wang Fu.
Yin Xun and Shan Bing petitioned to arrest Cao Jie and others, and asked Liu Yu to report to the Empress Dowager.
At this time, Dou Wu went out to stay and returned to his mansion. The person in charge of Zhongshu first reported him to Zhu Wangyu, the official historian of Changle.
Zhu Wangyu stole Dou Wu's memorial and read it, and cursed: Of course the eunuchs who indulge in illegal acts can be killed.
What sin do we people have, and why should we be exterminated together?
So he shouted: Chen Fan and Dou Wu asked the Queen Mother to depose the emperor. This is treason!
So in the evening, he summoned seventeen of his cronies, including the official Shi Gongpu and Zhang Liang from Changle, and made an alliance with livestock blood in their mouths to kill Dou Wu and others.
After hearing this, Cao Jie told the emperor in panic: "It's very tense outside. Please come out of Yu Deyang's front hall."
The emperor was so excited that he drew his sword, and asked the wet nurse Zhao Rao and others to support and protect the left and right, collect the entrance certificates, and close all the forbidden doors.
Summon the ministers and officials, threaten them with swords, and make them write edicts.
He appointed Wang Fu as the Huangmen Order and went to Beisi Prison to arrest Yin Xun and Shan Bing with the emperor's order.
Shan Bing was suspicious and refused to accept the edict, so Wang Fu killed him.
So Yin Xun was killed and Zheng Sa was released.
They came back together to kidnap the Queen Mother and seize the seal.
Those who are exhausted are ordered to guard the Nangong, close the door, and cut off any further path.
Zheng Sa and others were ordered by the emperor to arrest Dou Wu and others together with the imperial censor and the envoys.
Dou Wu refused to accept the order, ran into the barracks, and shot the envoy together with Dou Shao.
He summoned thousands of soldiers from the five Northern Army schools to station under the capital pavilion, and ordered the sergeants to say: The eunuchs in Huangmen have rebelled, and those who try their best to kill them will be rewarded heavily.
The imperial edict ordered Shaofu Zhou Jing to march and ride on General Zhang Huan to lead five battalions of soldiers to attack Dou Wu.
Late at night, Wang Fu led more than a thousand people including Hu Ben, Yu Lin, Mang Ma Cu, Du Hou, and Jian Zhuo Geshi to go out of Zhuqueye Gate to join Zhang Huan and other troops.
Early the next morning, the entire army was stationed under the palace gate to confront Dou Wu's troops.
Wang Fu's troops gradually increased, and he ordered the soldiers to shout to Dou Wu's army: "Dou Wu rebels, you are all forbidden soldiers. You should protect the palace and province. Why do you follow the rebels?"
The first to surrender will be rewarded!
The camp was usually afraid of subduing the eunuchs, so Dou Wu's army returned to Wang Fu.
From morning to lunch, Dou Wu's troops had almost surrendered.
Dou Wu and Dou Shao fled and were pursued and surrounded by Wang Fu's army. They both committed suicide and showed their heads to Luoyang Duting.
Their clansmen, guests, and in-laws were all captured and killed. Liu Yu and Feng Shu all annihilated their clans.
Moved Dou Wu's family to Rinan and moved the Queen Mother to Yuntai.
At this time, the vicious eunuch succeeded, and the upright people were discouraged and dared not say anything.
summary: Dou Wu, along with Grand Tutor Chen Fan, planned to eliminate the eunuchs. Chen Fan urged immediate action, citing a solar eclipse as an omen. Dou Wu proposed the plan to the Empress Dowager, but she hesitated, citing tradition. After executing some eunuchs, Dou Wu's plan to kill others like Cao Jie stalled. When an astrological omen appeared, Dou Wu and Chen Fan prepared to act. They appointed allies to key posts and arrested a eunuch, whose confession implicated Cao Jie and Wang Fu. However, a eunuch stole the memorial and alerted his colleagues. They falsely accused Dou Wu of treason to the young emperor, seized the Empress Dowager, and issued an edict for Dou Wu's arrest. Dou Wu refused to submit, rallied troops, but his soldiers were persuaded to defect by the imperial edict. Pursued, Dou Wu and his nephew committed suicide. Their clans were exterminated, and the Queen Mother was moved. Dou Wu's grandson, Dou Fu, was saved by a former student, Hu Teng, who hid him and later helped him establish a family.

translation:
In the past five years, the world has become more chaotic. The angry people think that there will be soldiers in the capital, and the two palaces will bleed. General Xu Liang and fake Sima Wudang said to He Jin: "Tai Gong's Six Tao" has the emperor's military affairs, which can control the four directions.
He Jin thought it was right and went to court to tell the emperor.
So he ordered He Jin to send out troops from all directions, hoping that the situation would be peaceful.
A large altar was built, with twelve layers of colorful canopies, ten feet high, built on it. A small altar was built in the northeast of the altar, and another nine layers of canopies, nine feet high, were built. Tens of thousands of infantry and knights were lined up in a camp. The emperor personally came out to review and stationed under the big canopy. How could he station under the small canopy?
After the ceremony, Emperor Ling, wearing armor and horse, called the "Supreme General" and circled the formation three times before returning.
He Jin was ordered to lead the entire army to watch.
At this time, eight captains of Xiyuan were set up, with Xiaohuangmen Jianshuo as the upper military captain, Huben Zhonglang Yuan Shao as the middle military captain, Tunqi Commander Bao Hong as the lower military captain, Yilang Cao Cao as the dian military captain, Zhao Rong as the assistant military captain, Chunyu Qiong as the assistant military captain, and the left and right captains.
Emperor Ling believed that Jian Shuo was strong and capable of military strategy. He trusted him especially and appointed him as a marshal, supervising and supervising the commanders and subordinates below the school captain. Even the generals were also under his leadership.
Although Jian Shuo was in charge of military power in the imperial court, he was still a little afraid of being jealous of He Jin, so he talked to Emperor Ling with his ministers and asked him to send He Jin to the west to attack Bian Zhang and Han Sui.
Emperor Ling listened to them and rewarded He Jin with hundreds of military chariots, tigers, sharp axes and axes.
He Jin secretly knew this was a conspiracy. So he submitted a petition to send Yuan Zhaodong to attack Xu and Yanzhou soldiers. He wanted to wait for Yuan Shao to return before sending troops to delay time.
At first, Queen He gave birth to Prince Bian, and Wang Gui gave birth to Prince Xie.
The ministers asked for a crown prince, but Emperor Ling thought that he was too frivolous and unworthy to be a king. However, the queen was favored by Emperor Ling, and He Jin held great power, so he hesitated to decide.
In the sixth year, Emperor Ling was seriously ill and asked Jian Shuo to assist Liu Xie.
Jian Shuo had received the imperial edict and had always looked down upon and envied brothers He Jin and He Miao. When Emperor Ling passed away, Jian Shuo was in the palace and wanted to kill He Jin first and establish Xie as emperor.
When He Jin came in from outside, Jian Shuo Sima Pan Yin and He Jin had known each other for a long time, and they welcomed He Jin with his eyes. He Jin was frightened and rode back to the camp from a shortcut, leading his troops to the Baijun Mansion, so he refused to go in because of illness.
Jian Shuo's plot did not come true, and Prince Bian became emperor. The Empress Dowager He came to the court to attend to the affairs of state, while He Jin and the Grand Tutor Yuan Kai assisted in the administration and also took charge of the affairs of the Secretariat.
He Jin had known for a long time that eunuchs were hated by everyone in the world, and he hated Jian Shuo for plotting to harm him and for taking over the power of the court, so he secretly arranged to kill the eunuchs.
Yuan Shao also had a plan for a long time, and asked He Jin's relative Zhang Jin to persuade He Jin: Huangmen Changshi has been in power for a long time, and he has committed adultery with the Empress Dowager Changle. The general should select virtuous talents to rectify the world and eliminate harm to the country.
He Jin thought it was right.
In addition, the Yuan family has been favored for many generations and is supported by people at home. Yuan Zhao was good at raising scholars, and the heroes were willing to be used by him. His younger brother Huben Zhonglang, General Yuan Shu, was also fond of chivalry, so they all accepted him favorably.
Therefore, more resourceful people such as Feng Ji, He, Xun You, etc. were recruited and became close friends with them.
Jian Shuo was suspicious and uneasy, so he wrote a letter to Zhao Zhong and others, saying: The generals and brothers are in power and are now plotting with the people of the world to kill those close to the late emperor and to eliminate us. It is only because I am in charge of the forbidden troops, so I am temporarily hesitant.
summary: He Jin, from Nanyang, rose to power after his half-sister became Empress to Emperor Ling. He was made a general to suppress the Yellow Turban rebellion and later a marquis. He and his brother He Miao defeated a rebellion of thieves. Emperor Ling established a new army with eight colonels, entrusting the eunuch Jian Shuo with overall command. Jian Shuo, fearing He Jin, plotted to send him away. When Emperor Ling died, Jian Shuo planned to kill He Jin and install Prince Xie as emperor, but He Jin was warned and avoided the trap. He Jin then made Prince Bian emperor, with the Empress Dowager as regent. He Jin, hating the eunuchs and Jian Shuo's plot, planned to eliminate them with Yuan Shao's support. However, the Empress Dowager refused, and He Jin's relatives, bribed by eunuchs, also opposed him.

translation:
Now we actually want to kill our race. Isn't it a bit excessive?
You say that the palace is filthy and filthy, but who is loyal and honest below the rank of minister?
So Shangfang's supervisor, Qu Mu, drew his sword and killed He Jin in front of the Jiade Hall.
Zhang Rang, Duan Wanggui and others issued an edict to appoint the former Taiwei Fan Ling as the Sili school attaché, and the Shaofu Prime Minister Xu as Henan Yin.
The minister received the edict, suspected it was false, and said: "Please invite the general to come out and discuss it together."
Zhonghuangmen threw He Jin's head to the minister and said: "He Jin has rebelled and has been killed."
He Jin's subordinate generals Wu Kuang and Zhang Zhang were He Jin's cronies. They heard that He Jin had been killed outside and wanted to lead troops into the palace. The palace was closed and no one was allowed to enter.
Yuan Shu and Wu Kuang worked together to cut and attack, while Zhonghuang Gate defended the pavilion with weapons.
At sunset, Yuan Shu set fire to the Nine Dragon Gate of Nangong and the East and West Palaces, and wanted to threaten Zhang Rang and others to come out.
Zhang Rang and others went in and told the Queen Mother that the general had rebelled, burned the palace, and attacked the Shangshu Gate, so he kidnapped the Queen Mother, the Emperor, and King Chenliu, and also robbed the palace officials and their families, and took the North Palace via Fudao.
Shangshu Lu Zhi held a sword under the window of the pavilion, raised his head and scolded Duan Wanggui.
Duan Wanggui was afraid and released the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother jumped from the pavilion and escaped without being robbed.
Yuan Shao and his uncle Yuan Wei falsely claimed that the emperor ordered Fan Ling and Xu Xiang to be killed.
He Miao and Yuan Shao then led troops to station under Zhuque Tower, arrested Zhao Zhong and others and killed them.
Wu Kuang waited for a long time and complained that He Miao was not of the same mind as He Jin. He also suspected that he was conspiring with the eunuchs, so he ordered the army to say: The one who killed the general was the chariot. Can you avenge the general?
He Jin was kind and kind to his subordinates, and all the soldiers cried and said: I am willing to die in repayment!
Wu Kuang led his troops and Dong Zhuo's younger brother, Fengche Duwei Dong, attacked and killed He Miao and dumped his body in the garden.
Yuan Shao closed the North Palace Gate and ordered his soldiers to capture the eunuchs. No matter how big or small, kill them all.
Some were mistakenly thought to be killed by eunuchs, while others exposed themselves and were spared from being killed.
More than two thousand people died.
Yuan Shaoyin marched into the palace, and some people from the upper gates attacked the palace.
Zhang Rang, Duan Wanggui and others could not escape the siege, so they kidnapped the emperor and dozens of King Chen Liu and fled to Xiaopingjin.
The ministers all came out from Pingtang, and no one ran with them. Only Lu Zhi, the minister, rode on horseback on the river at night. Wang Yun sent Minggong from central Henan to follow Lu Zhi.
Mingong arrived and killed several people with his sword, while the rest jumped into the river and died.
The next day, the ministers and officials welcomed the emperor back to the palace, appointed Min Gong as the doctor, and granted the title of Marquis of Ting.
Dong Zhuo then deposed Emperor Ling, forced the Queen Mother to be killed, and killed Lord Wuyang. The He family died, and the Han Dynasty also fell into chaos.
The historian commented: Dou Wu and He Jin, as uncles, held the power of assisting the government. Inside the palace, they relied on the power of the Queen Mother to listen to the government, and outside they had favorable conditions for heroes to ride on the wind. Finally, they were defeated by the eunuchs, died in power, and were lamented by the world. Is it possible that they lacked intelligence but had more power?
summary: He Jin hesitated, and Yuan Shao suggested summoning provincial generals like Dong Zhuo to threaten the court. Despite advice against this, He Jin agreed. The eunuchs, fearing for their lives, tricked their way back into the palace. When He Jin went to the palace to urge the Empress Dowager to act, the eunuchs ambushed and killed him. His subordinates then attacked the palace. Yuan Shao and others massacred the eunuchs, killing over two thousand. During the chaos, the eunuchs kidnapped the emperor and his brother, but were eventually killed. Dong Zhuo then deposed the emperor, killed the Empress Dowager, and the He family was destroyed, plunging the Han dynasty into chaos. The historian comments that both Dou Wu and He Jin, despite their power and favorable positions, were defeated by eunuchs due to a lack of wisdom and excessive reliance on power.

translation:
◆Dou Rong's Biography: Dou Rong's courtesy name was Duke of Zhou, and he was a native of Pingling County, Fufeng County.
Dou Guangguo, the seventh generation ancestor, was the younger brother of Queen Xiaowen and was named Zhang Wuhou.
His great-great-grandfather moved from Changshan with two thousand stones as an official during the reign of Emperor Xuan.
Dou Rong has been an orphan since he was a child.
During the reign of Wang Mang, he was the Sima of Wang Jun, the strong crossbow general. He attacked Zhaiyi in the east and Huaili. He was named Jianwu Nan for his military merits.
The younger sister is the younger wife of the great Sikong Wangyi.
He lived in Chang'an, visited noble families, made friends with local heroes, and was famous for his chivalry and righteousness. However, he served his mother and elder brother and raised his weak younger brother, practicing benevolence and righteousness.
In the last years of Wang Mang, bandits broke out in Qingzhou and Xuzhou. Wang Kuang, the Grand Master, asked Dou Rong to help the army and join him in the eastern expedition.
When the Han army rose, Dou Rong was defeated by Wang Yi at Kunyangxia and returned to Chang'an.
When the Han army commander entered the pass, Wang Yi recommended Dou Rong as General Bo Shui, rewarded him with a thousand catties of gold, and led his troops to Xinfeng.
When Wang Mang was defeated, Dou Rong led his army and surrendered to Zhao Meng, the commander-in-chief of Gengshi. Zhao Meng regarded Dou Rong as a school captain and thought highly of him. He recommended Dou Rong to be the prefect of Julu.
When Dou Rong saw the new establishment and the chaos in the east, he didn't want to leave the country. He remembered that his great-great-grandfather was the governor of Zhangye, his grandfather was the captain of the Qiang Guard, and his younger brother was the governor of Wuwei. They had been in Hexi for several generations and knew the local customs, so he said to his brothers alone: The safety of the world is still unknown. Hexi is rich and fertile, and the Yellow River is very strong. Zhangye's vassal state has thousands of elite soldiers and cavalry. In the event of an emergency, it will be enough to defend itself by eliminating the crossing of the Yellow River. This is a good place for us to leave to our descendants.
The brothers all agreed. Dou Rong asked to see Zhao Meng that day, resigned as Julu governor, and asked to go to Hexi.
Zhao Meng told Gengshi, and he became the captain of Zhangye's vassal state.
Dou Rong was so happy that he took his family to the northwest.
When he arrived in Zhangye, he made friends with local heroes and lived in harmony with the ethnic minorities. He was very popular with the people from all over the world, and Hexi quickly surrendered to him.
At this time, Liang Tong, the prefect of Jiuquan, Shejun, the prefect of Jincheng, Shi Bao, the captain of Zhangye, Zhu Zeng, the captain of Jiuquan, Xin Xu, the captain of Dunhuang, and all the heroes of the prefectures and counties, Dou Rong treated them kindly.
When Gengshi failed, Dou Rong and Liang Tong discussed the situation and said: "Today there is chaos in the world, I don't know what the outcome will be."
Hexi is in a dangerous position between Qiang and Hu. Without concerted efforts, we cannot defend ourselves. The power is generally great, and there is no leader.
One person should be elected as a general to ensure the security of the five counties and observe changes in the current situation. After deliberation, it was decided that Dou Rong should be the general of the five counties in Hexi.
At this time, Ma Qi, the governor of Wuwei, and Ren Zhong, the governor of Zhangye, were both isolated and had no party members, so they jointly informed them in letters, and they took off their seals and resigned.
So Liang Tong was appointed as the prefect of Wuwei, Shi Bao as the prefect of Zhangye, Zhu Zeng as the prefect of Jiuquan, Xin Xu as the prefect of Dunhuang, and Shengou as the prefect of Jincheng.
Dou Rong still lives in the vassal state, and his concurrent post as captain remains unchanged, and he is assigned to supervise the five counties.
The folk customs in Hexi are simple, and the politics of Dou Rong and others are also tolerant. They are friendly to each other, and they are safe and prosperous.
He repaired his troops and horses, practiced archery, and sounded the beacon fire alarm at the border. When Qiang and barbarians invaded the border fortress, Dou Rong often led his troops to rescue the troops together with the counties. He always arrived as scheduled and often defeated the invaders.
Later, the Huns also learned their lesson and rarely invaded again. The Qiang and Hu who were attached to the fortress were frightened by their relatives, and the homeless people who suffered from starvation in Anding, Beidi, Shangjun and other places came back in an endless stream.
When Dou Rong and others heard that Guangwu had ascended the throne, they wanted to go east to Luoyang, because the river and the west were far apart and could not be reached by themselves.
At this time, Wei Xiao first took the title of Jianwu, Dou Rong and others accepted Zhengshuo, and Wei Xiao all pretended to be his general's seal and ribbon.
Kuai Xiao looked obedient to others but harbored dissatisfaction inside. He sent the debater Yong Lian to lobby Hexi and said: Gengshi became emperor and soon fell into ruin. This is the result of a surname that cannot be revived.
summary: Dou Rong, courtesy name Duke of Zhou, was from Pingling County, Fufeng. His seventh-generation ancestor Dou Guangguo was the younger brother of Queen Xiaowen. Orphaned young, he served as Sima under Wang Jun during Wang Mang's reign, earning the title Jianwu Nan for military merit. He was known for chivalry and filial piety, caring for his mother, elder brother, and younger sibling. During the chaos at the end of Wang Mang's rule, Dou Rong initially served under Wang Yi but later surrendered to Gengshi's general Zhao Meng. Seeking stability, he requested and received the position of Captain of Zhangye's Vassal State, moving his family to Hexi. There, he befriended local heroes, harmonized with ethnic minorities, and gained widespread support. After Gengshi's fall, Dou Rong was elected General of the Five Counties in Hexi, overseeing a peaceful and prosperous region with tolerant governance and strong defenses against Qiang and Hu invasions. When Guangwu ascended the throne, Dou Rong considered allegiance but was courted by Wei Xiao, who urged independence. After consulting with local leaders, Dou Rong decided to support Guangwu, citing prophecies and the strength of Luoyang. He sent an envoy with gifts, and Guangwu responded by appointing him General of the Five Counties and later Liangzhou Mu. Dou Rong rebuffed Wei Xiao's attempts at alliance, writing letters to persuade him to submit, but Wei Xiao refused. Dou Rong then prepared for military action against Wei Xiao. Dou Rong joined Guangwu's campaign against Wei Xiao, leading troops from five counties. After Wei Xiao's defeat, Dou Rong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anfeng. Despite his high rank, he remained humble and repeatedly sought to resign, but Guangwu refused. His family became powerful, with multiple marriages to royalty, but later fell from grace due to misconduct. Dou Rong died at seventy-eight, posthumously honored as Marquis of Dai. His descendants continued, though some faced imprisonment and loss of titles. The historian comments that Dou Rong rose from obscurity to high office through merit, wisely yielding power when at his peak. While not a great strategist, his conduct in advancing and retreating was exemplary.

translation:
His father, Song Yang, was praised by the village for his respectfulness and filial piety, and he should not be drafted by the state or county.
Song Yang's aunt is the maternal grandmother of Empress Ma of Mingde.
After Ma heard that Song Yang's two daughters were both talented and beautiful, she took them to teach them a lesson.
At the end of Yongping, both daughters were selected into the prince's palace, and the prince liked them very much.
When Suzong came to the throne, they were all nobles.
In the third year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the great nobleman Liu Qing was born. In the second year, he was established as the crown prince, and Song Yang was recruited as Yilang. He was highly praised and rewarded.
The empress dowager liked her because she was a good person, dedicated to Changle Palace, and did the cooking work herself.
After the death of the Empress Dowager, Empress Dou was favored by Su Zong. Because both noble sisters were favored by the emperor, and Liu Qing was the prince, he was jealous of them and conspired with her mother Biyang Zhu to frame the Song family.
Outside, let her brothers collect her faults, even small ones; inside, let her attendants spy on her gains and losses.
Later, I intercepted a letter from the nobleman at Yeting Gate, saying: I want some raw dodder when I am sick, and I want my family to look for it. Therefore, he slandered her and said that she wanted to do magic tricks to pray for ghosts and gods to bring disaster on Queen Dou. She used dodder as a means of victory. She was slandered and framed day and night. The noble mother and son gradually became alienated from the emperor.
Liu Qing came to live in Chenglu Temple. A few months later, Queen Dou hinted that Ye Ting had ordered a noble man to survive and framed the noble man. Please test it and implement it.
In the seventh year, the emperor deposed the crown prince Liu Qing and established the crown prince Liu Zhao. Liu Zhao is the son of Liang Guiren.
So he issued an edict saying: The Crown Prince has a confusing and unpredictable nature, which started when he was a child and has become more obvious now. I'm afraid he inherited his mother's vicious style and cannot worship in the ancestral temple or be the master of the world.
Killing relatives for the sake of justice, let alone surrendering?
Now Prince Liu Qing is deposed as King Qinghe.
Crown Prince Liu Zhao was raised by the Queen and was educated by his mother when he was a child, which induced him to have a good character and he was expected to become a great person.
Most concubines have a loving mother as their mother and have a lifetime of kindness. How can it be compared with the righteousness of a direct descendant?
Now Zhao is the crown prince.
So the noble sister Ju Bing was sent to Cai Lun of Xiaohuangmen to conduct the examination and implementation. They all adhered to the above-mentioned will and attached it to the facts, so they were sent to the violent room.
The two noble men committed suicide by drinking medicine at the same time.
The emperor still mourned them and ordered Ye Ting to bury them in Fan Zhuoquan.
Song Yang was relieved of his official position and returned to the county.
The county arrested him again for the crime. Song Yang's friends Qianhuai County Magistrate Zhang Jun, Zuofeng Yipeiguo Liu Jun and others rushed to explain and were exempted from the crime.
Song Yang lost his ambition, became haggard and melancholy, and died at home.
summary: The lives and fates of Emperor Zhang's eight sons, focusing on the lineages of several kings. Liu Qing, King Xiao of Qinghe, was born to Noble Consort Song. His mother and aunt were favored by Emperor Zhang but were framed by Empress Dou after the death of Empress Dowager Ma, leading to their forced suicide. Liu Qing was deposed as crown prince in favor of his half-brother Liu Zhao (Emperor He). Despite this, Liu Qing maintained a close and respectful relationship with Emperor He, who treated him with great favor and trust. Liu Qing was known for his filial piety, caution, and grief over his mother's unjust death, often making private sacrifices. He died at age 29 and was buried in Guangqiu. His son Liu Hu succeeded him but died without heirs, leading to the appointment of Liu Yanping, son of Liu Chong, as King of Qinghe. Later, Liu Qing was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaode, and his mother as Empress Jingyin.

translation:
When the matter was discovered, Liu Wen and others kidnapped Qinghe Prime Minister Xie Fan and took him to Simamen of the palace. They said: The king should be made the emperor and Xie Fan the duke.
Xie Fan refused to listen to them and scolded them, so Liu Wen assassinated Xie Fan.
So Liu Wen and Liu Tuna were arrested and killed.
Officials impeached Liu Lian due to his impeachment, and he was demoted to the rank of Marquis of Wei clan. He moved to Guiyang and committed suicide.
After three years of establishment, the feudal state was abolished.
Liang Ji hated the name Qinghe and changed it to Ganling the next year.
The Empress Dowager Liang appointed Prince Jinghou Li of Anping Xiao as the King of Ganling, and served Emperor Xiaode to offer sacrifices, making him the King of Wei.
Liu Lili passed away in the twenty-fifth year, and Liu Ding, King Zizhen, succeeded to the throne.
Liu Dingli died in four years, and Prince Xian Liu Zhong succeeded to the throne.
The Yellow Turban bandits arose, and Liu Zhong was captured by the countrymen and released soon after.
Emperor Ling believed that one should kiss one's relatives, and it was most important to kiss one's relatives, so he ordered the restoration of Liu Zhong's feudal state.
Liu Zhongli died in the 13th year of his reign, and his son was killed by the Yellow Turban Army. In the 11th year of Jian'an, the feudal state was abolished because he had no heirs.
Liu Shou, King Hui of Jibei, and his mother Shen Guiren, were from Yingchuan. He has been an official for two thousand years.
When the noble was thirteen, he entered Yeting.
Liu Shou was named king in the second year of Yongyuan. Divide Taishan County into a country.
Emperor He abided by Suzong's old custom, and his brothers all stayed in the capital, and their love was extremely close.
The officials asked the kings to return to the feudal kingdom, but the emperor could not bear them leaving. He waited until the emperor died before returning to the feudal kingdom.
In the first year of Yongchu, Empress Dowager Deng granted Liu Shou's uncle Shen Zhuan the title of Marquis of Xinting.
Liu Shouli passed away in the 31st year of his reign. Since Yongchu, Rong and Di rebelled, and the country's finances were insufficient. When the newly crowned king passed away, the funeral expenses were reduced to tens of millions and ten thousand pieces of cloth. When the king who succeeded the throne died, the money was five million and five thousand pieces of cloth.
At this time, only Liu Shou respected his relatives the most, and specially sent him 30 million yuan for funeral expenses and 30,000 pieces of cloth.
Zijie King Liu ascended to the throne.
In the first year of Yongning, Liu Deng's five younger brothers were granted the title of Marquis of the Countryside, and all of them were taxed in Taishan.
Liu Dengli passed away in the fifteenth year, and Prince Ai Wang Liu Duo succeeded to the throne.
Liu Duoli died three years ago without any sons.
In the fourth year of Yonghe's reign, Liu Anguo, the marquis of Zhanxiang, was appointed King of Jibei, and was named King of Li.
Liu An passed away seven years after the founding of the People's Republic of China, and his son Xiao Wang Liu Ci succeeded to the throne.
In the first year of Benchu, Liu Meng, Liu Ci's younger brother, was granted the title of Tinghou.
Liu Ci lost his father when he was nine years old, and he has the most filial nature.
In the first year of Jianhe, the Empress Dowager of Liang issued an edict saying: King Liu Ci of Jibei spent his childhood guarding the vassal state and practicing filial piety. When his father died, he mourned excessively. He lived in a thatched hut, sitting and lying on earthen mats, never leaving his mourning stick, and his hair was not combed or washed, which resulted in sores and swelling on his body.
Since the beginning of mourning, in the 28th month of the twelfth month, since every feudal country has mourned, I have never heard of anyone like him.
summary: Liu Shou, King Hui of Jibei, was born to Noble Consort Shen. He was granted his kingdom in the second year of Yongyuan. Emperor He, following his father's customs, kept his brothers in the capital, and they were very close. Liu Shou died after 31 years as king. His descendants included Liu Deng, Liu Duo (who died without sons), and Liu Anguo, who was appointed king. Liu Ci, son of Liu Anguo, was noted for his extreme filial piety during his father's mourning, for which Empress Dowager Liang granted him an additional 5,000 households. The Jibei line ended when Liu Zheng died without sons in the eleventh year of Jian'an.

translation:
He was demoted to the title of Marquis of Duxiang and sent back to Hejian.
Liu Yi then declined the guests, refused to interact with them, and kept to himself.
In the fifth year of Yongjian's reign, his father Liu Kai wrote a letter requesting that Liwu County be divided and given the title of Liu Yi, and Emperor Shun agreed.
Liu Yi died and his son Liu Zhi succeeded him. He was established as Emperor Huan by General Liang Ji.
The Empress Dowager Liang honored King Xiao of Hejian as Emperor Xiaomu, and his wife Zhao as Empress Xiaomu. The temple was called Qingmiao and the mausoleum was Lecheng Ling.
They all set up orders and ministers to make the Situ hold the policy books and seals and ribbons in a strict manner, and the sacrifices were too tight.
In the second year of Jianhe's reign, Liu Shuo, the emperor's younger brother, the Marquis of Duxiang, was granted the title of King of Pingyuan. He stayed in Boling and served Liu Yi's descendants.
He respected Liu Yi's wife, Ma, as a noble of Xiao Chongbo Garden, and designated the three counties of Liangxiang and Gu'an in Zhuojun and Liwu in Hejian as Tangmuyi, and the income from the town was used for bathing.
Liu Shuo, the Marquis of Duxiang, was fond of drinking and made many mistakes. The emperor sent Ma Guiren to manage the king's household affairs.
In the eleventh year of Jian'an, the feudal state was abolished.
Liu Shu, the Marquis of Jiedu Ting, was granted the title of the son of King Xiao of Hejian.
Liu Shu died and was succeeded by his son Liu Chang.
Chang died and was succeeded by his son Liu Hong, who was made Lingdi by General Dou Wu.
In the first year of Jianning, Empress Dowager Dou issued an imperial edict to honor the imperial ancestor Liu Shu as Emperor Xiaoyuan. His wife, Xia, was named Empress Xiaoyuan, the mausoleum was called Dunling, and the temple was called Jingmiao.
They all set up ministers and ministers to make Situ Chijie serve policy books and seals in the river, and use Tailao to offer sacrifices. They often sent Zhongchang to serve in the river at the beginning of the year.
In the third year of Xiping, the envoy worshiped Liu Lizi, the king of Hejian An, as Liu Kang, the king of Jinan, and served Emperor Xiaoren to offer sacrifices.
Liu Kang passed away and was succeeded by his son Liu Binbei. In the twelfth year of Jian'an, he was killed by the Yellow Turban bandits.
His son Liu Kai succeeded him, and in the 13th year of his reign, Wei accepted the abdication of the Han Dynasty and made him the Marquis of Chongde.
Liu Shu, the Huaiwang of Chengyang, was divided into Jiyin and the country in the second year of Yongyuan. He died in the fifth year of Lili and was buried in the capital.
Having no children, the feudal state was removed and still merged into Jiyin.
Liu Wansui, the mourning king of Guangzong, was granted the title in the fifth year of Yongyuan, and he was divided into Julu as the country.
He died this year and was buried in the capital.
Having no children, the feudal state was removed. Still merged into Julu.
Liu Sheng, King Huai of Pingyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor He.
The mother's name is not recorded.
He had a difficult-to-treat disease when he was young, so he was granted the title in the first year of Yanping.
He died in the eighth year of his life and was buried in the capital.

Liu Yi, a son of Liu Kai, was initially favored by Empress Dowager Deng but was later framed and demoted. He eventually became the father of Emperor Huan, who honored Liu Kai as Emperor Xiaomu. Liu Shu, another son of Liu Kai, was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaoyuan by his son, Emperor Ling.

His ancestors had the surname Tian from Qi State. Later, many people with the surname Tian moved to Yuanling, so they used the order as their surname.
Fifth Lun was very upright and virtuous when he was young.
In the last years of Wang Mang's life, thieves and thieves appeared in droves, and people from the same clan and fellow villagers rushed to join him.
Fifth Lun then built a strong fortress based on the dangerous terrain. When thieves came, he mobilized all the villagers to defend themselves with strong crossbows. Dozens of generations like Bronze Horse and Red Eyebrow came to attack, but they could not capture it.
Wu Lun began to contact the county Yin Xianyu Bao as a battalion commander. When Xianyu Bao met him, he felt that he was different, so he used him as an official.

Wu Lun later became a stingy man in the village, collecting taxes fairly, sending out servants, and mediating civil disputes, and was very popular among the people.
He himself thought that he would not be able to be a high official for a long time, so he moved his family to Hedong, changed his name, and called himself Wang Boqi. He carried salt between Taiyuan and Shangdang, and the places he passed must be cleaned before leaving. The villagers called him a Taoist priest, and his relatives and friends did not know where he lived.
A few years later, Xian Yubao recommended Wu Lun to Jingzhao Yin Yanxing, and Yan Xing called Wu Lun to be the chief bookkeeper.
At that time, most of the people who minted coins in Chang'an resorted to fraud, so Yan Xing ordered Wu Lun to be the official who supervised the minting of coins and was in charge of the Chang'an market.
The fifth Lun rectified the substandard scales and buckets. From then on, there was fair trade in the market, there were no big scales and small buckets, and the people were convinced.
Every time Wu Lun read the edict, he often sighed: This is the wise emperor, and my fate will be decided by just meeting him. People of his generation laughed at him and said: "You can't convince the state generals, how can you move the Emperor Wancheng?" Lun said: "I haven't met a close friend, it's just because of different ways."
In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu's reign, Wu Lun was promoted to Xiaolian and promoted to the chief medical officer of Huaiyang State Medical University. He followed the king to Kyoto.
Emperor Guangwu felt strange after summoning him.
In the twenty-ninth year, he and the king had the opportunity to meet with the capital and accompanying officials. The emperor asked them about political affairs. Wu Lun took this opportunity to answer questions about the way to govern. The emperor was very happy to hear this.
The next day, he specially called in and Wu Lun to talk from day to night.
The emperor jokingly said to Fifth Lun: I heard that when you were an official, you beat your father-in-law and refused to feed your cousin. Is this true? The Fifth Lun replied: I have married three times, but my wives have no father.
I suffered from famine when I was young, so I really didn’t dare to invite anyone to eat. The emperor laughed.
After Wu Lun came out, there was an edict ordering him to be the governor of Fuyi. Before he arrived at the official office, he was chased and reassigned to be the governor of Kuaiji.
Although he made two thousand dan, he cut grass to feed the horses himself, and his wife cooked the food.
summary: Fifth Lun, courtesy name Boyu, was from Changling, Jingzhao, descended from the Tian clan of Qi. Upright from youth, he built fortresses during Wang Mang's era to defend against bandits like Bronze Horse and Red Eyebrow, successfully repelling attacks. He served under Yin Xianyu Bao, who recognized his talent, and later became a village official, gaining popularity through fair tax collection and dispute mediation. He moved to Hedong, changed his name to Wang Boqi, and worked as a salt carrier. Recommended by Xianyu Bao, he became chief bookkeeper under Jingzhao Yin Yanxing, where he rectified market scales and coins, earning public trust. Promoted to Xiaolian in 51 CE, he served as chief medical officer for Huaiyang State. Emperor Guangwu, impressed by his governance insights, appointed him governor of Fuyi, then Kuaiji. In Kuaiji, he banned superstitious cattle sacrifices and witch fraud, restoring order. Transferred in 62 CE for legal violations, he was pursued by weeping locals. After release, he farmed privately until appointed magistrate of Danqu County, then governor of Shu Commandery, where he dismissed corrupt officials and promoted virtuous ones, ending bribery. As Sikong under Suzong, he warned against the power of Empress Dowager Mingde's Ma relatives, citing their lavish gifts and potential corruption. He also opposed Ma Fang's Western Qiang campaign, fearing nepotism. Known for strictness but leniency, he criticized harsh governance, advocating for benevolent officials. He retired in 86 CE with honors and died over eighty, receiving imperial burial gifts.

Making people sick?

Construction should be stopped temporarily to comply with Tianxin.
I have the talents of an ordinary man, but no moral ability. I have been earning a lot of money for a long time, and I have been promoted to a close minister. I have received generous gifts. I am full of joy and fear. I am not full of stupid enthusiasm. I am guilty of death.

summary: Zhongli Yi, courtesy name Zi'a, from Shanyin, Kuaiji, began as a county governor. During a plague in 38 CE, he personally provided medicine to victims. Promoted to Xiaolian, he served under Grand Situ Hou Ba, showing compassion by arranging clothes for a sick disciple. As Xiaqiu magistrate, he privately forgave an official's theft, leading the thief's father to force his son's suicide. As Tangyi magistrate, he allowed a prisoner, Guang, to bury his mother, later securing his pardon. Under Xianzong, as minister, he refused tainted pearls from corrupt official Zhang Hui, earning imperial praise and a reward. He criticized the emperor's frequent hunts at Guangcheng Garden, urging frugality during a drought. He also defended a clerk's clerical error, taking blame himself. Known for bold remonstrance, he rescued ministers from punishment and advised leniency in governance. As prime minister of Lu for five years, he promoted moral education, dying in office. His final words urged gentle rule, and the emperor granted burial funds.

summary: Song Jun, courtesy name Shuxiang, from Nanyang, became a doctor at fifteen via his father's appointment. As minister, he defended his principles against imperial anger, earning praise for his integrity. As Hanoi governor, he was beloved by the people. He retired due to illness, receiving honors. summary: Han Lang, courtesy name Boqi, from Xue, Lu, survived abandonment as an infant during chaos. A Confucian scholar, he taught *Shang Shu* and served as imperial censor during Yongping. Geng Yan entered the bedroom and went to the bed to take advantage of Guangwu's free time, so he said: Today is the beginning of political chaos, the monarchs and ministers are promiscuous, the generals are arrogant and domineering in the capital, and the princes and nobles are tyrannical in the capital.

He argued that the Han dynasty, despite Wang Mang’s usurpation, was revived by Guangwu, and that celestial signs—such as irregular movements of Taibai and Yinghuo—foretold doom for rebels like Dong Xian and Peng Chong. He warned against following false prophecies and urged surrender, comparing Liu Gong’s potential choice to the virtuous actions of Duke Zhou’s uncle Kang and King Jibei Liu Zhi. Su Jing also wrote to Deng Zhongkuang, who eventually surrendered with Liu Gong. Su Jing died at home at age seventy, leaving writings like *Records of Teachings*.

Later, due to conflicts with eunuchs, he lived in seclusion for over ten years, writing books and becoming a great Confucian. After the party ban was lifted, he was recruited multiple times but refused. When Yuan Feng died, Xun Shuang mourned him for three years, setting a custom. He later served under General He Jin and then Dong Zhuo, rising to Sikong within ninety-five days. Seeing Dong Zhuo's cruelty, he conspired with Wang Yun but died of illness at sixty-three. He wrote numerous works, including "Li," "Yizhuan," and "Hanyu," totaling over a hundred chapters, many now lost. **Xun Yue (Zhongyu)** was the son of Xun Jian, who died early. At twelve, Xun Yue could explain "Spring and Autumn." Despite poverty and lack of books, he could recite most texts after reading them at others' homes. During Emperor Ling's reign, when eunuchs held power, he feigned illness and lived in seclusion. He later served under Cao Cao and became Minister of Huangmen. Emperor Xian, fond of literature, conversed with Xun Yue and Kong Rong daily. As political power shifted to Cao Cao, Xun Yue wrote five chapters of "Shenjian" on governance, emphasizing benevolence and righteousness. He identified four troubles—hypocrisy, selfishness, debauchery, and luxury—and five policies: promoting agriculture, distinguishing good from evil, spreading culture, establishing military force, and enforcing rewards and punishments. He also criticized the marriage system for placing women above men and advocated for historical recording. The emperor, finding Bangu's "Hanshu" too lengthy, ordered Xun Yue to write thirty chapters of "Han Ji" in the style of "Zuo Shi Zhuan." Xun Yue's work was concise yet detailed. He also wrote "Chongde" and "Zhenglun." He died in the fourteenth year of Jian'an at age sixty-two.

translation:
Han Shao felt sorry for them because they were hungry, so he opened a warehouse to help them. More than 10,000 families received food.
The county supervisors all argued that it couldn’t be done.
Han Shao said: If you save these people who will die in the ravine and are punished for it, you will be happy even if you die. The prefect knew Han Shao's character on weekdays and finally did not deal with him.
Died in office due to illness.
Li Ying, Chen Chen, Du Mi and Xun Shu from the same county erected monuments to praise him.
His son Han Rong has a long character.
When he was young, he was able to debate famous theories without writing poems. He became so famous that he was recruited by all the five prefectures.
In the early years of Emperor Xian's reign, he became a servant.
Died at the age of seventy.
◆Zhong Hao's biography, Zhong Hao's courtesy name was Ji Ming, and he was a native of Changshe County, Yingchuan County.
It is a common surname in the county and has been proficient in law for generations. When he was young, Zhong Hao was praised for his honesty and honesty, and was continuously recruited by the government. Because his second brother did not serve as an official, he lived in seclusion in the mountains and taught poetry and rhythm to more than a thousand students. Chen Chen from the same county was younger than Zhong Hao, so Zhong Hao became friends with him. Zhong Hao was appointed as the county's meritorious officer. When he was summoned to the Situ Mansion, before he left, the prefect asked him: Who can take your place? Zhong Hao said: If the prefect must find the right person, Chen Chen, the chief of the Ximen Pavilion, can do it. Chen Chen heard about it and said: "Zhong Jun doesn't seem to be carefully inspecting people. I don't know why he only looks at me?" Not long after, Zhong Hao resigned.
He was recruited by the government nine times, and he was promoted to Tingweizheng, doctor, and Lin Luchang, but he failed.
At that time, both Zhong Hao and Xun Shu were admired by the scholar-bureaucrats.
Li Ying once sighed and said: "It is difficult to compare Xunjun's clear knowledge with him, but Zhongjun's virtue can be his teacher's example."
The mother of Zhong Hao's nephew Zhong Jin is Li Ying's aunt.
Zhong Jin was eager to learn and admire ancient Taoism, and he was modest and conciliatory. He was the same age as Li Ying and both were famous.
Li Ying's grandfather, Taiwei Li Xiu, once said: Zhong Jin is like my family's temperament. If the country is righteous, he can make use of his talents, but if the country is ungrateful, he can avoid punishment. He also married Li Ying's sister to him.
Zhong Jin summoned the state capital and never gave in to his will.
Li Ying said to him: Mencius believed that if a person has no sense of right and wrong, he cannot be considered a human being.
Why don't you agree with what Meng Ke said? Zhong Jin once told Zhong Hao what Li Ying said.
Zhong Hao said: In the past, Guo Wuzi, a senior official in the state of Qi, liked to expose other people's sins, so as to attract resentment.
In the end, it is your humility that is more valuable than your own to protect your family. He realizes that the teachings of the ancients are not dogmatic, but seek to implement them appropriately.
This is often the case. He died at home at the age of sixty-nine.
Confucian scholars praised him: "Lin considers virtue and does not do anything inappropriate."
He loves poetry and books, and plays ancient music.
summary: **Han Shao (Zhonghuang)** was from Wuyang County, Yingchuan. He served as a county official and was recruited into the Situ Mansion. When Taishan bandit Gongsun Ju caused trouble, Han Shao was appointed county magistrate. The bandits, hearing of his reputation, avoided Ying County, but other counties suffered. Many fled to Ying County, and Han Shao opened granaries to feed over 10,000 families, despite objections from supervisors. He died in office. Li Ying, Chen Chen, Du Mi, and Xun Shu erected monuments praising him. His son Han Rong became a servant under Emperor Xian and died at seventy. **Zhong Hao (Ji Ming)** was from Changshe County, Yingchuan, from a family proficient in law. Praised for honesty, he lived in seclusion teaching poetry to over a thousand students. He befriended Chen Chen and served as the county's meritorious officer. Recruited nine times by the government, he never accepted. Both Zhong Hao and Xun Shu were admired by scholar-bureaucrats. Li Ying said Xun Shu's knowledge was hard to match, but Zhong Hao's virtue could be a teacher's example. Zhong Hao's nephew Zhong Jin married Li Ying's sister. Zhong Hao died at sixty-nine at home. Confucian scholars praised his virtue. His grandson Zhong Yao became Sili Xiaowei.

translation:
At that time, the official Zhang Rang was very powerful. When Zhang Rang's father died, he was sent back to Yingchuan for burial. Although everyone in the county went, none of the famous scholar-bureaucrats went. Zhang Rang felt that he had no face and was very ashamed, but Chen Chen went to mourn alone.
Later, the party members were killed again. Zhang Rang was grateful to Chen Chen for his condolences. Many people were forgiven and their wealth and lives were saved.
In the countryside, Chen Chen set an example by being fair.
If there is a dispute, he will seek correct judgment and the right and wrong will be explained clearly. After returning home, there will be no complaints.
Some even sighed and said: I would rather be punished than be told wrong by Chen Chen. At this time, there was a famine and the people were in poverty. A thief entered his room and stopped on the beam.
Chen Shi secretly saw it, so he got up, arranged the bedding, and cleaned the house. Then he called his descendants together and warned him sternly: "People must encourage themselves. Bad people are not necessarily inherently bad. Habits are caused by nature, leading to this point." Liang Shangjun is this kind of person!
The thief was shocked. He knelt on the ground and knelt down to apologize. Chen Chen slowly told him: "You don't look like a bad person. You should reflect deeply and become a good person."
However, this time it was probably because of poverty that he did this. He ordered his family to send him two pieces of silk.
Since then, there have been no burglaries in the county.
Every time Taiwei Yang Ci and Situ Chen Dan were appointed ministers, hundreds of officials came to congratulate them. Yang Ci and others often lamented that Chen Chen had not ascended to the big position, and they felt ashamed. When the party ban was lifted, Generals He Jin and Situ Yuan Wei sent people to persuade Chen Chen, hoping to make an exception and give Chen Chen a big position.
Chen Chen declined the envoy and said: I have not thought about the things in the world for a long time. I am just dressing up my clothes and waiting for death. At this time, every time the three princes were vacant, everyone thought of Chen Chen. He was called up many times and refused to go. He closed the door and hung up the car to rest and retire.
He died at home in the fourth year of Zhongping at the age of eighty-four.
He Jin sent envoys to offer condolences, and more than 30,000 people from all over the country came to express their condolences, hundreds of them wearing mourning clothes.
They jointly carved stones and erected monuments, and their posthumous title was Mr. Wen Fan.
He has six sons, among whom Chen Ji and Chen Chen are the best.
Chen Ji's character Yuan Fang was also praised by others for his virtuous conduct.
His brothers are filial, his women are harmonious, and the younger generations in the village are envious of his good family tradition.
Being imprisoned by the party, he worked hard to write a book of tens of thousands of words called "Chen Zi".
The ban on the party was lifted, and the four governments competed for appointments, but he was not accepted.
When his father passed away, he was extremely grieved. He often vomited blood and died. Although the period of mourning was over, he was still grieving so much that his body became emaciated, leaving only a few bones, and he became like a dead person.
The governor of Yuzhou believed that Chen Ji's excellence was extremely valuable, so he commissioned it as a minister, and all cities in Yuzhou painted images of Chen Ji and other figures to encourage customs.
summary: **Chen Chen (Zhonggong)** was from Xu County, Yingchuan, of humble origin. From childhood, he was respected by peers. He served as a county official and studied at Taixue. When falsely accused of murder, he was tortured but released. Later, as postal supervisor, he treated his accuser with courtesy, earning admiration. As a meritorious officer, he refused to appoint an unsuitable candidate recommended by eunuch Hou Lan, taking the blame himself. He served as Chief of Taiqiu, governing with virtue and quietness. During the party arrests, he willingly imprisoned himself. He mourned for Zhang Rang's father, later saving many lives during renewed party persecutions. In his village, he settled disputes fairly. When a thief entered his home, he admonished him and gave him silk, ending burglaries in the county. He repeatedly refused high positions, closing his door to retire. He died at eighty-four in the fourth year of Zhongping. Over 30,000 mourners attended his funeral. His posthumous title was Mr. Wen Fan. His sons Chen Ji and Chen Chen were also virtuous. Chen Ji served under Dong Zhuo but opposed moving the capital, warning of destruction. He later became Dahonglu and died at seventy-one. Historians praised Chen Chen's virtue, noting that while imperial teachings declined, integrity survived among the people.
