translation:
Dong Zhuo, courtesy name Zhongying, was from Lintao, Longxi.
He has a rough and scheming temperament.
When he was young, he traveled among the Qiang and tried his best to make friends with the leaders.
Later, when he returned home to farm, some of the leaders came to join him. Dong Zhuo slaughtered cattle for them and had banquets with them. The leaders thanked him for his kindness and collected the remaining heads of various livestock as gifts to him after returning. From then on, he became famous for his bravery and chivalry.
The soldiers and horses who were appointed as state guards once patrolled and guarded under the fortress.
Dong Zhuo has extraordinary physical strength. He wears two bow boxes and shoots them left and right. The Qiang and Hu people are afraid of him.
In the last years of Emperor Huan's reign, as a son of a good family in six counties, he was appointed Yulin Lang, and followed Zhang Huan, the general of Zhonglang, as a military commander. Together they went to attack the rebellious Qiang people in Hanyang. After defeating them, he was named Langzhong and was rewarded with nine thousand bundles of silk.
Dong Zhuo said: I am the one who records the merits, and the soldiers are the ones who make the merits.
So they were all distributed to the soldiers, leaving nothing behind.
He was gradually promoted to the rank of captain of Wuji School in the Western Regions, but was dismissed for some reasons.
Later he became the governor of Bingzhou and the governor of Hedong.
In the first year of Zhongping, he was appointed as Shu Zhonglang General. With integrity, he went to Xiaquyang to attack Zhangjiao on behalf of Lu Zhi. He was defeated and punished.
That winter, the Ling Qiang and Paohan Heguan bandits in the north rebelled, so they jointly supported Beigong Boyu and Li Wenhou, the Hu people who had surrendered to Huangzhong, as generals, and killed the Qiang captain Ling Zheng.
Boyu and others kidnapped Bian Zhang and Han Sui, who came to Jincheng, and made them specialize in military administration. Together they killed Jincheng prefect Chen Yi, attacked and burned the prefectures and counties.
In the spring of the next year, he led tens of thousands of cavalry to invade the Third Auxiliary and approached the royal cemetery, under the pretext of killing the eunuchs.
The imperial court issued an edict appointing Dong Zhuo as Zhonglang General and serving as the deputy of Zuo Chaoqi General Huangfu Song to conquer them.
Huangfu Song was dismissed and recalled due to ineffectiveness, while Bian Zhang, Han Sui and others became more powerful.
The imperial court also appointed Sikong Zhang Wen as the general of chariots and cavalry. During the holiday, Yuan Pang, the commander of Jinwu, was appointed as his deputy.
Dong Zhuo was appointed as the Polu General, and he and Zhou Shen, the Dangqi General, were under the command of Zhang Wen.
A total of more than 100,000 infantry and cavalrymen from all counties were combined and stationed at Meitun to protect the royal cemetery.
Bian Zhang and Han Sui also marched into Meiyang.
Zhang Wen and Dong Zhuo always lost when they fought with them.
In November, there was a shooting star like fire at night, with a light of more than ten feet long, shining in Bianzhang and Han Sui's camp. Donkeys and horses were braying together. The thieves thought it was unlucky and wanted to return to the Golden Globe. Emperor Dong was overjoyed when he heard about it. The next day, he joined forces with You Fufeng, Bao You and others to attack, defeating the enemy and beheading thousands of people.
Bian Zhang and Han Sui were defeated and fled to Yuzhong. Zhang Wen sent Zhou Shen with 30,000 people to pursue them.
summary: Dong Zhuo, a man of rough and scheming temperament from Lintao, Longxi, rose to prominence through his interactions with Qiang leaders, distributing rewards to soldiers and gaining a reputation for bravery. He served as a military commander under Zhang Huan, defeating rebellious Qiang forces, and was later appointed to various posts, including Governor of Bingzhou and Hedong. During the Zhongping era, he was tasked with suppressing rebellions, including those led by Bian Zhang and Han Sui, but faced defeats. Despite setbacks, he managed to preserve his army and was granted the title of Marquis of Lianxiang.

translation:
So he stationed troops in Hedong to observe changes in the situation. When Emperor Ling died, General He Jin and Sili Colonel Yuan Shao planned to kill the eunuchs, but the Queen Mother did not agree, so they privately summoned Dong Zhuo to lead troops into the court to intimidate the Queen Mother.
After Dong Zhuo was summoned, he set out on the road that day.
He also wrote a letter saying: Zhang Rang, the minister of the Central Committee, and others stole the favor and caused chaos in the world.
I have heard that raising the soup to stop it from boiling is not as good as drawing fuel from the bottom of the cauldron; although it hurts to break a malignant sore, it is worse than having it invade the inside.
In the past, I went to martingale to raise troops in Jinyang to drive away the evildoers around the monarch.
Now I am going to Luoyang with drums to arrest Zhang Rang and others in order to eliminate the evil and filth.
He Jin was defeated and died before Dong Zhuo arrived. Huben Zhonglang general Yuan Shu burned down the Nangong Palace to attack the eunuchs. Duan Gui, the general servant, and others kidnapped the young emperor and King Chenliu and fled to Xiaopingjin at night.
Dong Zhuo saw the fire from a distance and led his troops forward quickly. He arrived at the west of the city before dawn. He heard that the young emperor was in Beimang, so he went to greet him.
When the young emperor saw Dong Zhuo coming with his troops and horses, he was frightened and cried.
Dong Zhuo talked to him, but he couldn't answer; he talked to King Chenliu and found out the cause of the trouble.
Dong Zhuo believed that King Chenliu was wise and was born to the Empress Dowager Dong. Dong Zhuo believed that he was of the same clan as the Empress Dowager and had plans to dethrone the emperor.
When Dong Zhuo entered Beijing, he had only three infantry and cavalrymen. He felt that he had few troops and was afraid that he would not be subdued by people near and far. For about four or five days, he secretly separated his troops from the city at night and camped nearby. After dawn, he returned to the city with great fanfare, making people think that the army from the west had arrived again, and no one in Luoyang knew it.
Soon the troops previously led by He Jin and his brother He Miao all surrendered to Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo asked Lu Bu to kill Zhijin Wu Dingyuan and annex his tribe. Dong Zhuo's army greatly increased.
So he signaled the court to remove Sikong Liu Hong and replace him himself.
Then he summoned the courtiers to discuss deposing the emperor.
All the officials gathered together, and Dong Zhuo held his head high and said: The greatest relationship is the relationship between heaven and earth, and the second is the relationship between monarch and ministers. This is the foundation of government.
The emperor is ignorant and cowardly, unable to serve the ancestral temple and be the monarch of the world.
Now I want to follow the old rules of Yi Yin and Huo Guang and establish King Chenliu instead. How about that?
No one below the rank of Duke dares to speak.
Dong Zhuo said loudly: "In the past, Huo Guang made decisions and Tian Yannian supervised them with his sword. Anyone who dared to hinder the policies and plans would be dealt with according to military law."
Everyone present was shocked.
Only Shangshu Lu Zhi said: In the past, after Taijia came to the throne, King Lu Yi had more than a thousand sins, so there was something about abolishing the throne.
The current emperor is still young and his behavior is not inappropriate and cannot be compared with previous cases.
Dong Zhuo was furious and left the table.
The next day, he summoned all the officials in the front hall of Chongde, and then threatened the Queen Mother, asking her to issue an edict to depose the young emperor.
Said: During the period of mourning for the late emperor, the emperor did not have the mentality of a son, and did not behave like a monarch. Now he is deposed as King Hongnong.
So he established King Chenliu and created Emperor Xian.
He also pointed out that the Queen Mother persecuted the Queen Mother Yongle, causing her to die of depression. She violated the etiquette of mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, and had no filial qualities. She moved her to Yong'an Palace, where she was subsequently murdered and died.
Dong Zhuo was promoted to Taiwei, acting as the agent for the affairs of the former general. He added the certificate of carriage and horse riding at the post station during the Xijie Festival and the warriors with axes and iron tigers, and was granted the title of County Lord.
Dong Zhuo, together with Situ Huang Wan and Sikong Yang Biao, all brought Zhuan to the court and wrote to the court, demanding that Chen Fan, Baowu and other party members be traced in order to comply with people's wishes.
So the titles of Chen Fan and others were completely restored, and their descendants were promoted and appointed.
Soon after, Dong Zhuo was granted the title of Prime Minister, and he could enter the court without any hesitation, and go to the palace with a sword and shoes.
He named his mother Chiyangjun and appointed Lingcheng and other officials for her.
At that time, the residences of the emperor's relatives in Luoyang City were connected, and every family had a lot of gold and silk property.
summary: After Emperor Ling's death, Dong Zhuo was summoned to the capital by He Jin and Yuan Shao to intimidate the Empress Dowager. He entered Luoyang with a small force but cleverly expanded his army by integrating defectors, including troops from He Jin and He Miao. He deposed the young emperor, established Emperor Xian, and assumed the role of Prime Minister, wielding immense power. His rule was marked by brutality, including the massacre of civilians, looting, and the destruction of the economy through coinage reforms. He also moved the capital to Chang'an, forcing millions to relocate, causing widespread death and destruction.

translation:
Hundreds of officials were hungry, so Zhang Yang, the governor of Hanoi, sent thousands of people to carry rice as tribute and pay.
The emperor then rode in an ox cart and decided to make his capital in Anyi.
Wang Yi, the governor of Hedong Province, donated cloth and silk, and all of them were given to the officials below.
The king was granted the title of lord, Hu Cai was appointed as the General of the Eastern Conquest, and Zhang Yang was appointed as the General of Anguo. They all celebrated holidays and opened mansions.
Other villains who led soldiers rushed to beg for official status, and they couldn't make the seal in time, so they carved it with an awl.
Someone brought wine and meat to the emperor's palace to eat and drink.
The emperor also sent his servant Han Rong to Hongnong to make peace with Li Cui, Guo Si and others.
Li Jiu then returned the palace to the palace, and also returned some of the maids' family members, as well as the emperor's vehicles, utensils and clothing.
When the emperor first entered the Pass, there were still hundreds of thousands of households in Sanfu. After Li Cui and Guo Si attacked each other and the emperor returned, Chang'an became an empty city for more than forty days. The strong ones fled everywhere, and the weak ones were eaten. Within two or three years, there was no one in Guanzhong anymore.
In the spring of the first year of Jian'an, the generals fought for power. Han Xian attacked Dong Cheng. Dong Cheng defected to Zhang Yang, who asked Dong Cheng to repair the palace in Luoyang first.
In July, the emperor returned to Luoyang and entered Yang'an Palace.
Zhang Yang regarded this as his own contribution, so he named the palace after "Yang".
He said to the generals: The emperor should be the emperor of all people in the world. Everyone has the responsibility to protect him. The imperial court has its own ministers. I should go out to defend against foreign invasion. What am I doing in the capital?
Then he returned to Wild King.
Yang Feng also left the capital and stationed in Liang.
So the imperial court appointed Zhang Yang as Grand Sima, Yang Feng as Chariot and Cavalry General, Han Xian as Grand General, and concurrently as Sili Xiaowei, and they were all awarded with talisman axes and cymbals.
Han Xian and Dong Cheng both stayed in Beijing to guard the palace.
Han Xian was arrogant and did whatever he wanted, disrupting political affairs. Dong Cheng was worried and secretly summoned Cao Cao, the governor of Yanzhou.
Cao Cao then went to the court to pay tribute and presented it to hundreds of officials below the Duke, taking the opportunity to report the sins of Han Xian and Zhang Yang.
Han Xian was afraid of being killed, so he went to Yang Feng alone.
Because of Han Xian and Zhang Yang's role in protecting them, the emperor issued an edict saying that no further questions would be asked.
So Dong Cheng, the general of the guard, Fu Wan, the general of the auxiliary state, and more than ten people were conferred as marquises, and Juju was posthumously given the title of prefect of Hongchen.
Youcao moved the emperor to Xu on the grounds that Luoyang was in ruins.
Yang Feng and Han Xian tried to stop the carriage, but failed to catch up. Cao Cao attacked them. Yang Feng and Han Xian defected to Yuan Shu, and they committed wanton evil in the Yangzhou and Xuzhou areas.
The next year, Liu Bei, the general of the left, trapped Yang Feng and killed him.
Han Xian was frightened and fled back to Bingzhou, but was killed on the way.
Hu Cai and Li Le stayed in Hedong. Hu Cai was killed by his enemies and Li Le died of illness.
Zhang Jijun had no food, so he left his territory and went to Nanyang, where he attacked and died in battle.
Guo Si was killed by his general Wu Xi.
In the third year of Jian'an, the imperial court sent Pei Mao, a servant of the imperial court, to take Shao Shu and order Duan Xuan, the general in Guanzhong, and others to attack Li Cui. Destroy the three tribes.
Duan Xuan was appointed General Annan and granted the title of Marquis of Minxiang.
In the fourth year of Jian'an, Zhang Yang was killed by his general Yang Chou.
Dong Cheng was appointed as general of chariots and cavalry and opened the government.
Since moving the capital to Xu, Cao Cao has been in power, the emperor has no time to take care of himself, and all the officials are just filling in.
Emperor Xian hated Cao Cao's power and oppression, so he secretly issued an edict to Dong Cheng, asking him to make friends with righteous people from all over the world to get rid of Cao Cao.
Dong Cheng planned with Liu Bei. Before he could take action, Liu Bei went on an expedition. Dong Cheng also conspired with the general Wang Fu, Changshui captain Zhong Ji, and Yilang Wu Shuo.
When the incident was revealed, Dong Cheng, Wang Fu, Zhong Ji, and Wu Shuo were all killed by Cao Cao.
Since Han Sui and Ma Teng returned to Liangzhou, the war continued, and they captured Longdi and occupied Guanzhong.
Cao Cao was dealing with Hebei at that time, and he was afraid that they would take the opportunity to cause rebellion. In the seventh year of Jian'an, he asked the court to confer the title of General Ma Teng to conquer the south, and the title of General Han Sui to conquer the west, and both opened their offices.
Later, Duan Yan was recruited as Dahonglu, but Duan Yan died of illness.
Ma Teng was also recruited as a guard and given the title of Marquis of Huaili.
Ma Teng responded, leaving his son Ma Chao to lead his troops.
In the 16th year of Jian'an, Ma Chao and Han Sui rebelled against Cao Cao in the Guanzhong area. Cao Cao defeated them, Han Sui and Ma Chao fled, and Ma Teng was reduced to three clans.
Ma Chao attacked and killed Wei Kang, the governor of Liangzhou, and occupied Longyou again.
In the 19th year of Jian'an, Yang Fu from Tianshui defeated Ma Chao. Ma Chao fled to Hanzhong and surrendered to Liu Bei.
Han Sui ran to Jincheng Qiang land and was killed by his men.
At the beginning, a native of Longxi established his clan in Baohan, claiming to be the "King of the Han Dynasty at the head of the river" and entrusting hundreds of officials for more than thirty years.
Cao Cao sent Xia Houyuan to attack Zong Jian and behead him, and Liangzhou was pacified.
The argument goes: Dong Zhuo was originally a fierce and powerful person, but because he caught up with the turmoil in the world, he was able to trample on common sense and harm the world. With his cruel temperament, which was like cutting open the abdomen, taking out the liver and cutting off the feet of people, killing all the people in the world would not satisfy his satisfaction. However, he was still able to treat officials and gentlemen with humility, and was not determined to bully and usurp the royal family. He was still a thief.
summary: Dong Zhuo's tyranny led to a coalition of regional governors, including Yuan Shao and Sun Jian, rising against him. He was eventually assassinated in a plot by Wang Yun and Lü Bu in 192 AD. His death was followed by chaos, as his former subordinates Li Jue and Guo Si seized control of Chang'an, leading to further violence and famine. The capital was devastated, with widespread cannibalism and depopulation.

translation:
Dong Zhuo indulged his soldiers, rushed into their homes, raped and robbed women, and robbed their property. He called this "prison raids."
He also raped and harassed the princess, occupied and robbed the palace maids, and indiscriminately inflicted cruel punishments. Anyone with a little hatred would be killed. No one in the palace or outside the palace could protect himself.
Dong Zhuo once sent troops to Yangcheng. At that time, people were gathering in front of the Tutu Temple. Dong Zhuo ordered them to go forward and kill all the people, take away the belongings on the carts, load the robbed women, tie their heads to the shafts of the carts, and return to the capital singing and shouting.
They also destroyed the five-baht coins and cast them into small coins. They also collected all the bronze men, Zhongxu, Feilian, bronze horses and so on from Luoyang and Chang'an to use as materials for coining coins.
Therefore, money is cheap and goods are expensive, and a stone of millet is worth tens of thousands.
In addition, the money he cast had no outline patterns, making it inconvenient for people to use.
At that time, people thought that Qin Shihuang saw a long man in Lintao, so he cast a bronze man.
Dong Zhuo, a native of Lintao, has now destroyed it.
Although the casting and melting are different, the violence is similar.
Dong Zhuo had always heard that people all over the world hated the eunuchs who killed Zhongliang. When he took control of the government, although he did not follow the right path, he still pretended to be temperamental and promoted and appointed many scholars, such as the Secretary of the Ministry of Personnel, Secretary of Hanyang Zhou, Shizhong Runan Wu Qiong, Minister Zheng Gongye, and Chang Shi He Xian, etc.
Xun Shuang, a scholar without an official position, was appointed as Sikong.
Chen Ji, Han Rong and others who were implicated by the party all became ministers.
Those who sink and are buried are often promoted.
Appoint Shangshu Han Fu as the governor of Jizhou, Shizhong Liu Dai as the governor of Yanzhou, Chen Liu and Kong Dian as the governor of Yuzhou, and Yingchuan Zhang Zi as the governor of Nanyang.
Dong Zhuo's cronies were not in prominent positions, they were just generals.
In the first year of Chuping, when Han Fu took office, he and Yuan Shao and more than ten others formed an alliance to attack Dong Zhuo, while Wu Qiong and Zhou secretly acted as internal correspondents.
At the beginning, in the last years of Emperor Ling's reign, the Yellow Turban remnant party Guo Tai and others started an uprising in the Baibo Valley of Xihe River, and invaded Taiyuan, and then conquered Hedong. The people fled to Sanfu and called them "Baibo Bandits", with more than 100,000 people.
Dong Zhuo sent Zhonglang General Niu Fu to attack them, but they could not retreat.
When Dong Zhuo heard about the rise of troops from the east to attack Dong Zhuo, he was frightened and poisoned King Hongnong with poisonous wine and wanted to move the capital to Chang'an.
The ministers were summoned to discuss the matter, but Huang Wan, the Taiwei, and Yang Biao, the Situ, tried their best to dissuade him. Wu Qiong and Zhou Shai tried their best to dissuade him.
Dong Zhuo then became furious and said: When I first entered the court, these two men advised me to use virtuous people, so they obeyed. However, after you took office, you raised troops to attack me.
These two betrayed me, how can I feel sorry for them!
So Wu Qiong and Zhou Suo were killed.
summary: The aftermath saw continued infighting among Dong Zhuo's former allies and the rise of Cao Cao, who eventually took control of the imperial court. The text concludes with a critical assessment of Dong Zhuo as a ruthless and destructive figure whose actions plunged the empire into turmoil, leading to the collapse of central authority and widespread suffering.

translation:
◆Cai Yong's biography, Cai Yong's courtesy name was Bo Zhe, and he was a native of Chenliuyu County.
Cai Xun, the sixth generation ancestor, was a master of the skills of Huang Emperor and Lao Tzu. He was the magistrate of Meichan County during the reign of Emperor Ping.
In the early years of Wang Mang's usurpation of the throne, he was appointed as the commander of the Yanrong Company.
Cai Xun looked up at the official seal and sighed and said: I am an official of the Han Dynasty, and I will not deviate from the right path even if I die.
In the past, Zengzi would not accept anything from Jisun, let alone serving someone with a second surname! So he took his family and fled into the mountains, where he, Bao Xuan, Zhuo Mao and others did not serve as Wang Mang's officials.
His father, Cai Leng, also had a clean conduct and was named Duke Zhending after his death.
Cai Yong was a filial person, and his mother was ill for three years. No matter whether it was midsummer, severe winter, or the weather changed, she never untied her clothes and didn't sleep for seventy days.
When my mother died, a house was built next to the tomb to live in and guard her. Every movement and silence was observed in accordance with the etiquette.
A rabbit jumped docilely next to his house, and there were trees and branches. People from far and near found it strange, and many people came to see it.
He lived with his uncle and his brothers, and the family was not separated for three generations. People in the village praised him for his good conduct.
He was erudite when he was young and learned from Taifu Hu Guang.
He likes literature, mathematics, astronomy, and is also good at music.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, Xu Huang, Zuo and other five princes, who were often ministers in the imperial court, were masters of power and lawlessness. Hearing that Cai Yong was good at playing the piano and drums, he informed the emperor and ordered the prefect Chenliu to supervise the departure.
Cai Yong had no choice but to go to Yanshi, pretended to be ill, and returned home.
Nothing to do, just playing with antiques at home and not interacting with ordinary people nowadays.
Inspired by Dongfang Shuo's "The Guest" and Yang Xiong, Ban Gu, and Cui Xi's self-examination of doubts, I learned from hundreds of schools of thought, affirmed what was correct and corrected what was incorrect, and wrote "Explanation" to alert and encourage myself.
In the third year of Jianning, he was recruited to Situ Qiaoxuan's mansion. Qiaoxuan treated him very well.
The river is flat and long.
He summoned the doctor to pay homage and read the book to the east.
Promoted to Yilang. Cai Yong believed that the classics were written by saints a long time ago, and there were many textual errors, which were far-fetched by vulgar Confucianism, which was a nuisance to students. In the fourth year of Xiping, together with Wu Guan Zhonglang Xi Gudian, Guanglu doctor Yang Ci, admonishment doctor Ma Rishidan, Yilang Zhang Xun, Han Shuo, Taishi Lingdan, etc., he petitioned for the correct text of the Six Classics.
Emperor Ling approved it, and Cai Yong wrote it on the stele himself with a red pen, and asked the workers to carve it and set it up outside the gate of Taixue. Later Confucian students took this as their standard scripture. When the monument was newly erected, more than a thousand cars came to see and copy it in one day, and the streets were blocked.
summary: Cai Yong, courtesy name Bo Zhe, was a native of Chenliuyu County. His sixth-generation ancestor Cai Xun served under Emperor Ping but refused to serve Wang Mang, fleeing into the mountains with his family to maintain loyalty to Han. Cai Yong's father, Cai Leng, was known for his integrity. Cai Yong himself was filial, tending to his ill mother for three years without rest, and after her death, he built a hut by her tomb and observed strict mourning rituals. He lived harmoniously with his uncle and brothers for three generations, earning local praise. Erudite from youth, he studied under Hu Guang and excelled in literature, mathematics, astronomy, and music. During Emperor Huan's reign, eunuchs like Xu Huang and Zuo Guan summoned Cai Yong to play the qin, but he feigned illness and returned home. He wrote "Explanation" to encourage himself, inspired by Dongfang Shuo and others. In the third year of Jianning, he served under Situ Qiaoxuan. Later, as Yilang, he noted errors in the classics and, in the fourth year of Xiping, petitioned Emperor Ling to correct the Six Classics. He personally wrote the text on steles, which were set up outside Taixue, attracting over a thousand visitors daily.

translation:
How dare you violate the taboo and write the correct answer in handwriting. If the king and his ministers are not intimate, and the king must be wary of leaking secrets, the ministers will always be in danger of losing their virginity.
Please keep your official records well, so that your loyal and upright ministers will not be resented by bad people. When the music was played, the emperor sighed after watching it.
Because he went out to use the toilet, Cao Jie peeked in from behind, so he told everyone around him, causing the matter to leak out.
Those who should be deposed by Cai Yong hated him and tried to retaliate.
In the past, Cai Yong was at odds with Situ Liu, and his uncle, Weiwei Cai Zhi, had an issue with Yang Qiu, the general's great craftsman. Yang Qiu was the son-in-law of Zhongchang Shi Cheng Huang. Cheng Huang sent someone to write an anonymous report, falsely accusing Cai Yong and Cai Zhi of asking Liu for personal matters several times, but Liu did not agree to him, so Cai Yong held a grudge, and so on.
Determined to frame Cai Yong.
Therefore, an edict was issued to the minister and Cai Yong was summoned to question him.
Cai Yong wrote a letter to complain: I was summoned and asked about: Dahonglu and Liu Qian were the governor of Jiyin, and my subordinate Zhang Wan took a long rest for a hundred days; Liu was the secretary, and he asked Li Qi, the official of Hanoi County, to be the state secretary; and Liu did not do anything to make me feel resentful about Yin Yangzhi of Henan before the camp, and Hu Muban, the imperial censor. I am horrified, my heart is broken, and I have no place to bury myself.
I think the matter belongs to Zhang Wan and Li Qi and has nothing to do with Yangzhi and Hu Muban.
Generally speaking, petty officials are on vacation, which is not the basis for hatred.
He is a relative of Yangzhi, how dare he help a private party?
If we, father and son, want to frame him, we should file a lawsuit with the government and explain in detail why we hate him. There is nothing wrong inside, but the slanderous book has been published. I am willing to face Liu to prove it.
I was specially rewarded for my knowledge. Working in the secret hall, running in front of the emperor, the emperor knew his name and appearance.
In July this year, I summoned Jin Shangmen and asked me the reason for the disaster. Hold the imperial edict and apply for the purpose, and inspire again and again.
I am really stupid, I only know how to be loyal and have no thought of the consequences.
Then he ridiculed the ministers and favored ministers. I want to ask the Emperor's question, eliminate the disaster, and then build a peaceful and prosperous age for the Emperor. The emperor did not expect that the loyal minister should keep it secret. Then the false accusation came suddenly, which aroused suspicion.
How can we tolerate officials who are dedicated to harming others?
The imperial edict was issued, requiring all officials to submit secret reports, hoping to change the course and eliminate evil and bring good fortune. Not only was the person who made the suggestion not rewarded, but in the blink of an eye, he was framed. Now they are all dumbfounded and take me as a warning. Who dares to be loyal and filial to the emperor?
My uncle Cai Zhi was promoted to a very high position one after another; I was deeply favored and visited him several times.
The person who wrote the anonymous report wanted to frame our father and son and destroy my family. He did not want to expose traitors and benefit the country!
I am forty-six years old and alone. Fortunately, I am ranked as a loyal minister and will die with honor.
I'm afraid the emperor will never hear good advice again! I was ignorant and deserved my punishment. But my uncle Cai Zhi didn’t know the correct answers before. I am gray-haired and senile for more than a year. I was arrested. I suffered along with me and was framed together. What an injustice! What a pain!
As soon as I was imprisoned, I was forced by pain and urged to report anonymously. How could the emperor know about my situation? The day of death is coming soon, and he is reckless and self-proclaimed. He is willing to be executed himself. Then, the day I die will be the day I am reborn!
Long live health! Love yourself for the people.
summary: Cai Yong submitted a memorial criticizing the "three mutual laws" that prevented officials from serving in related regions, arguing they hindered governance in You and Ji provinces. He urged their abolition to select talented officials promptly, but his advice was not adopted. He also addressed disasters and Xianbei invasions, proposing seven reforms: proper imperial sacrifices, recruiting virtuous scholars, rewarding loyal officials like Zhang Wen, empowering honest governors, and ending corrupt recruitment practices. His memorial was leaked by Cao Jie, leading to false accusations from enemies like Yang Qiu. Cai Yong was imprisoned and sentenced to death, but Lu Qiang interceded, and his sentence was commuted to exile in Shuofang. Despite assassination attempts by Yang Qiu, he survived.

translation:
So Cai Yong and Cai Zhi were sent to Luoyang Prison, where they were sentenced to serving the public with hatred, murdering ministers, being disrespectful, and abandoning the market.
After the incident was reported, Lu Qiang, the constant servant, took pity on Cai Yong's innocence and asked the emperor. The emperor thought again about what Feizhang said and issued an edict to reduce the death penalty. He shaved his head, tied his neck with an iron ring, and moved to Shuofang with his family. He was not exempted from the pardon order.
Yang Qiu sent assassins to chase and assassinate Cai Yong. The assassins were moved by Cai Yong's justice and were not used by Yang Qiu.
Yang Qiu bribed his tribe leader to poison Cai Yong, but the bribed person told Cai Yong the news and asked him to be more vigilant.
So he was not killed. Lives in Anyang County, Wuyuan.
Cai Yongqian was in Dongguan, where he, Lu Zhi, Han Shuo and others wrote a supplement to the "Records of the Later Han Dynasty", but he was in exile and did not have time to complete it. Therefore, the ten ideas written in the letter are divided into headings and appended to the end of the book.
The emperor loved Cai Yong because of his talent, so the country held a general amnesty the following year, so he pardoned Cai Yong's crime and allowed him to return to his hometown. Cai Yong was exiled for nine months until he returned home.
When he was about to return to the county, Wang Zhi, the governor of Wuyuan, saw him off.
After drinking enough, Wang Zhi danced to persuade Cai Yong, but Cai Yong ignored him.
Wang Zhi was the younger brother of Wang Fu, a regular servant. He was originally very arrogant, but he lost face and was laughed at by the guests, so he cursed Cai Yong and said: "The criminal dares to insult me!" Cai Yong shook up his clothes and left.
Wang Zhi hated him and reported that Cai Yong had a grudge against him and slandered the court.
The emperor's favored people also hated him.
Cai Yong thought that he would be killed in the end, so he fled across the rivers and seas and went to Wuhui. He relied on the Taiyang clan for his travels and stayed in Wu for twelve years.
When the people of Wu were burning tung trees for cooking, Cai Yong heard the sound of the fire and knew that tung trees were a good wood, so he asked him to make a qin. Sure enough, the sound was great, but the tail of the qin was burnt. At that time, it was called "Jiaowei Qin".
Once upon a time, Cai Yong was in Chenliu. A neighbor invited Cai Yong to dinner, but by the time he left, he had already finished the wine.
There was a guest playing the piano behind the screen. Cai Yong went to the door and listened quietly and said: Oh!
You call me happy but you have murderous intention. Why?
Just went back on his own. Cai Yongsu was respected by the villagers. His master immediately chased him and asked him what was the reason. Cai Yongsu told him the whole story, and everyone was surprised. The man playing the harp said: I was playing the strings in front of me and saw a mantis facing the cicada. The cicada was about to leave but before it took off, the mantis suddenly moved forward and then retreated.
I was terrified, fearing that the mantis would not be able to catch the cicada.
Is this what is called killing the heart shaped by the sound? Cai Yong smiled and said: That's true.
In the sixth year of Zhongping, Emperor Ling died and Dong Zhuo became Sikong. Hearing that Cai Yong was famous, he recruited him, but Cai Yong said he was ill and could not go.
summary: After nine months, a general amnesty allowed his return, but he fled to Wuhui after offending Wang Zhi. He lived in Wu for twelve years, once crafting a famous "Jiaowei Qin" from a burnt tung tree. In the sixth year of Zhongping, Dong Zhuo forced him into service, promoting him rapidly. Cai Yong advised Dong Zhuo against excessive honors but grew disillusioned with his tyranny. After Dong Zhuo's execution, Cai Yong expressed regret, angering Wang Yun, who imprisoned him. Despite pleas from scholars like Ma Rishidan, Wang Yun executed him, fearing his historical writings would slander the court. Cai Yong died at sixty-one, mourned by many. His works included poems, inscriptions, and 104 other pieces, though much was lost in chaos. The historian noted his tragic fate, bound by loyalty and circumstance.

translation:
◆The biography of Yu Xu, whose courtesy name was Shengqing, was from Wuping in the state of Chen.
My grandfather, Yu Jing, was a county prison officer. He handled cases impartially, was generous, and respected himself and others. Every winter month, the case is reported, and I often shed tears over it.
He once said: In the East China Sea, a gate was built at the Duke's height, and the horses and chariots were made high, thinking that some of their descendants would become high officials. And his son Dingguo finally became prime minister.
I have been in prison for sixty years. Although I am not as good as Yu Gong, maybe it is about the same. My descendants may not become Jiuqing.
Therefore, Yu Xu was given the title "Qing".
Yu Xu was twelve years old and could read Shangshu.
Is an orphan. Take care of your grandmother.
The county elected him as his grandson, and the prime minister admired him very much and wanted him to be an official.
Yu Xu declined and said: "Grandma is ninety years old. Without me, there is no one to take care of her."
The Prime Minister didn't ask him to go.
After his grandmother passed away and the period of mourning expired, he was recruited into Taiwei Li's Mansion and was awarded the title of doctor.
In the fourth year of Yongchu, the Qiang rebelled and ravaged Bing and Liang. The general Deng Zhi thought that the military situation was tense and could not take care of both. He wanted to abandon Liangzhou and concentrate his forces on the north.
So he summoned the ministers for a meeting, and Deng Zhi said: For example, if your clothes are broken, if you repair one broken piece and repair another, one piece will still be intact.
If not, there will be no protection.
Everyone at the meeting agreed. After hearing this, Yu Xu said to Li: "It is said that Gongqing decided to abandon Liangzhou. In my opinion, it is inappropriate." The late emperor worked hard to open up the territory, but now he was afraid of the trouble and threw it away.
Since Liangzhou is lost, then the Third Assistant is regarded as a frontier fortress. If the Third Assistant is a frontier fortress, then the ancestral garden tombs are outside the boundary. This is absolutely unacceptable. As the saying goes: Guanxi produces prime ministers, Guandong produces generals, Liangzhou trains troops and trains bravery, surpassing other states.
Now the Qiang and Hu dare not invade Sanfu because Liangzhou is behind him and is his thorn in the side!
The people of Liangzhou took up arms to defend Liangzhou without any hesitation, because Liangzhou belonged to the Han Dynasty!
If you abandon it and move the people away, and the people are content with their homeland and are unwilling to move, something will happen.
Suppose the heroes gather together and take advantage of the situation to come eastward. Even though there are warriors like Ben and Yu and generals like Taigong, they may not be able to withstand it.
The speaker used the analogy of mending clothes that has yet to be completed. I see it as a ulcer that gets wider and wider and never stops.
Abandoning Liangzhou is not a strategy.
Li said: I didn't expect that.
It’s not like you said that it almost failed in national affairs.
So, what’s a good strategy?
Yu Xu said: There is a commotion in Liangzhou today, and people are uneasy. I am worried that something unexpected will happen.
The nine ministers of the four prefectures should be ordered to recommend several people from their respective states, and all the eldest sons of the Mu Shou Ling should be given official positions. On the surface, it is to reward their merits, but in fact, it is to monitor them and prevent them from causing trouble.
Li thought he was right, and even extended the four prefectures to follow Yu Xu's plan.
So he recruited the heroes of the two states as vassals, and appointed the sons of the shepherds and guardians as ministers to comfort them.
The Deng Zhi brothers were dissatisfied because Yu Xu opposed Deng Zhi's opinions. He wanted to use the official law to frame Yu Xu.
summary: Yu Xu, from Wuping in Chen, was known for his integrity. His grandfather, a prison officer, handled cases with compassion. Yu Xu was orphaned young and cared for his grandmother, refusing an official post until after her death. He later served as a doctor. When General Deng Zhi proposed abandoning Liangzhou due to Qiang rebellions, Yu Xu argued against it, stating it would expose the imperial tombs and that Liangzhou's people were a vital defense. He suggested controlling local leaders by giving their sons official posts to prevent rebellion. Deng Zhi, resentful of Yu Xu's opposition, sent him to govern Chaoge, a bandit-ridden area. Yu Xu used deception, recruiting former bandits to ambush others and marking thieves' clothes with silk threads, leading to their dispersal. Promoted to Wudu's prefect, he again used deception against the Qiang, increasing his campfires to feign strength and marching rapidly. He then used a strategy of weak arrows to lure the Qiang into range of his strong crossbows, defeating them. He improved the county by building fortifications, opening waterways for transport, and increasing the population. As Sili Xiaowei, he impeached powerful officials, earning their hatred. He was framed and sentenced to hard labor, but eunuch Sun Cheng defended him, leading to his release and promotion. He later abolished the practice of "righteous money" and argued for fair treatment of petitioners. He remained upright despite nine reprimands and three punishments, dying as Shangshu Ling. On his deathbed, he regretted killing many bandits at Chaoge, believing it brought divine punishment.

translation:
Soon, Zhao Zhong became the general of chariots and cavalry, and ordered Zhao Zhong to discuss his merits in the crusade against the Yellow Turbans. Zhijinwu Zhenju and others said to Zhao Zhong: Fu Nanrong was in the Eastern Army before. He had merits but was not granted a title. Everyone in the world was disappointed.
Now the general has the important task of advancing the wise and redressing grievances in order to conform to everyone's wishes.
Zhao Zhong accepted his words. He sent his younger brother Chengmen School Captain Zhao Yan to express his yearning.
Zhao Yan said to Fu Xie: "Nan Rong is a little bit polite and I am a regular servant, but Wanhu Hou is not enough for you!"
Fu Xie refused sternly and said: Whether a person succeeds or fails is determined by fate; merit without reward is caused by the times.
Do I, Fu Xie, still want a private reward?
Zhao Zhong was even more resentful, but he was too famous to dare to harm him.
There are also many powerful people who are jealous of him, so they are not allowed to stay in the court and become the governor of Hanyang.
At first, Fan Jin, the general of the county, had the knack of knowing people and promoted Fu Xie as Xiaolian.
Later, Fan Jin was appointed as the prefect of Hanyang. When Fu Xie left, Fan Jin went through the handover procedures with him. After passing the verification, he left. The country and the country were proud of them.
Fan Jin, courtesy name Wenyuan, was from Nanyang.
Fu Xie was good at sympathizing with people, and the rebellious Qiang people were moved by his kindness and enlightenment, and they all surrendered. He cleared the land and cultivated fields and set up more than forty camps to accommodate them.
At this time, the governor Geng Bi appointed Cheng Qiu to be in charge. Cheng Qiu sought personal gain for him and associated with traitors, and the soldiers hated him.
In the fourth year of Zhongping, Geng Bi led soldiers from six counties to conquer the Kingdom of Jincheng, Han Sui and others.
Fu Xie knew that Geng Bi had broken people's trust and must fail.
The admonishment said: The emperor has not been in power for a long time, and the people do not know how to educate him.
Confucius said: To make people fight without first teaching them is to abandon them.
Now he leads untrained men across the dangers of Dalong. There will be ten dangers and ten dangers. When the thieves hear that the army is coming, they will surely unite as one.
The border soldiers are brave and difficult to resist; the newly organized troops are not harmonious among the officers and soldiers. If internal changes occur, it will be too late to regret it.
It is better to let the army rest for a period of time, improve discipline, and strictly enforce rewards and punishments.
When the thieves learn that our army is lax, they must think that our army is cowardly, and they will surely fall apart due to their internal struggle for power.
Then lead the trained troops to defeat the disintegrating thieves, and then sit back and wait for victory to come.
Now if you don't seek to be foolproof and take a path that is bound to fail, I won't do it for you.
Geng Bi refused to listen.
When the troops arrived at Didao, there were indeed rebels. They killed Cheng Qiu first and then Geng Bi. The thieves then surrounded Hanyang. There were few soldiers in the city and no food, but Fu Xie still held on.
At this time, thousands of Hu cavalry from the north followed the bandits to attack Hanyang County. They all cherished Fu Xie's kindness for a long time. They kowtowed outside the city and asked to send Fu Xie back to his hometown.
summary: Fu Xie, from Lingzhou, was known for his caution in speech and action. He served as Sima under Huangfu Song against Zhang Jiao's Yellow Turbans. Before the campaign, he warned the emperor that the real threat was internal, from eunuchs like Zhao Zhong, and that evil and good cannot coexist. Despite his merits, Zhao Zhong framed him, but the emperor spared him. Later, when Situ Cui Lie proposed abandoning Liangzhou during a Xiqiang rebellion, Fu Xie vehemently opposed him, arguing that Liangzhou was the empire's shield and that abandoning it would empower the barbarians. The emperor agreed. Fu Xie refused to curry favor with the powerful eunuch Zhao Zhong, even when offered a marquisate. As Hanyang's governor, he pacified the Qiang. He warned Governor Geng Bi against attacking Han Sui with untrained troops, predicting disaster. Geng Bi ignored him and was killed. When Hanyang was besieged, Fu Xie refused to abandon the city despite his son's pleas and the offer of safe passage from grateful Hu cavalry. He chose to die in battle, cursing a defecting official. His posthumous title was Zhuangjiehou.

translation:
In the sentence, I planted Qiang Dianwu. I had received Gai Xun's kindness on weekdays, so I stopped everyone with weapons and said: Gai Changshi is a wise man. Killing him is called deceiving the sky.
Gai Xun raised his head and cursed: "You are a rebel, what do you know?" Come and kill me!
The soldiers looked at me and I looked at you, shocked.
Dian Wu jumped off his horse and asked Gai Xun to mount his horse. Gai Xun refused and was captured by the bandit soldiers.
Qiang Rong admired Gai Xun's righteousness. He was brave enough to conquer the three armies and did not dare to harm him, so he was sent back to Hanyang.
Later, the governor Yang Yong recommended Gai Xun to concurrently serve as the prefect of Hanyang.
At that time, there was a famine and people were cannibalizing. Gai Xun allocated food to relieve the famine. He first took out his own food to set an example and saved more than a thousand hungry people.
Later, he resigned from the official position and was conscripted as the captain of the school to fight against the captives.
Emperor Ling summoned him and asked: Why is the world so rebellious?
Gai Xun said: It was caused by the eunuch's children.
At this time, Jian Shuo, the eunuch and commander of the military academy, was standing by. Emperor Ling turned back to Jian Shuo. Jian Shuo was afraid and didn't know how to persuade Gai Xun, so he hated Gai Xun.
Emperor Ling said to Gai Xun again: "I have concentrated the troops in Pingtang. How about taking out more of the hidden treasures and giving them to the soldiers?"
Gai Xun said: I heard that the late king Mingde did not show troops.
Now the enemy is far away and arrayed nearby. This is not enough to show the country's courage and determination. It is just a waste of force. Emperor Ling said: Very good.
It's a pity that it's too late to see you. My ministers have never said such things!
At that time, Gai Xun, Zong Zheng, Liu Yu, and Assistant Military Colonel Yuan Shao were in charge of the emperor's security forces.
Gai Xun said to Liu Yu and Yuan Shao: I have seen the emperor many times. The emperor is very smart, but he is just deceived by the left and right.
If everyone worked together to kill the eunuchs, recruit and select handsome talents, revive the Han Dynasty, and retire with great success, wouldn't it be a great thing?
Liu Yu and Yuan Shao had also discussed this matter on weekdays, so they contacted each other. Before they could take action, Sili Colonel Zhang Wen recommended Gai Xun to serve as Jing Zhaoyin.
Emperor Ling still wanted to receive him. Jian Shuo and others were afraid of Gai Xun, so they all persuaded the emperor to approve Zhang Wen's memorial, so Gai Xun was appointed as Jing Zhaoyin.
At that time, Chang'an ordered Yang Dang, whose father was a regular servant. Relying on his father's power, he engaged in corruption and misbehavior. Gai Xun found out that Yang Dang had embezzled more than tens of millions.
The noble relatives all interceded for him, but Gai Xun refused to listen. He reported all the facts to the emperor, and involved Yang Dang's father. He ordered strict execution, and Gai Xun was powerful in the capital.
At that time, Xiaohuangmen Jingzhao was highly regarded as the Shang Pharmacy Supervisor and was favored by the crown prince. Because of Jian Shuo's request, the crown prince asked Gai Xun to promote Gao Xun's highly respected son Gao Jin as Xiaolian, but Gai Xun refused.
Some people say: The Crown Prince is the deputy lord and the heir to the throne, Gao Wang is the Crown Prince's favorite, and Jian Shuo is the Emperor's favorite, but you are unwilling to do this good thing. As the saying goes, "Three grudges make a house." Three grudges gather together. Aren't you afraid?
Gai Xun said: "Electing worthy people to be filial and honest is to serve the country. If you are not a worthy person, even if you don't elect them, you will not regret it even if you die!"
Although Gai Xun was a local official and had military and state secrets, Emperor Ling often issued edicts to ask him.
He received many rewards and trusted him very much. No other minister in the court could compare with him.
summary: Gai Xun, from Dunhuang, was a Xiaolian and Hanyang's chief historian. He refused to take revenge on an enemy, Su Zhenghe, when the governor wanted to kill him to cover for a corrupt prefect, arguing it was wrong to kill a good man. He later remonstrated with Governor Zuo Chang for embezzling funds, but Zuo Chang sent him to a dangerous post. Gai Xun survived and later rescued Zuo Chang from a siege by Bian Zhang. He criticized Governor Song Xiao's plan to teach the *Classic of Filial Piety* to pacify the border, calling it impractical. During a battle against Qiang rebels, he was wounded but refused to flee, cursing his captors. The Qiang, respecting his courage, released him. As a famine relief official, he used his own grain to save over a thousand people. Summoned by Emperor Ling, he blamed eunuchs for the world's chaos. He planned with Liu Yu and Yuan Shao to kill the eunuchs, but was made Jing Zhaoyin instead. There, he prosecuted a corrupt official despite pleas from nobles. After Emperor Ling's death, he wrote to Dong Zhuo, criticizing his deposition of the young emperor. He openly defied Dong Zhuo in court, refusing to bow. He died of illness at 51, refusing Dong Zhuo's funeral gifts.
