translation:
Now that the county is still intact and the people are prosperous, if the war drums sound, we can gather 20,000 people and lead them to kill the national traitors and hold high the flag of righteousness for the world. Wouldn't it be great?
Zhang Chao agreed with his opinion and went to Chenliu with Zang Hongxi to discuss with his brother Zhang Miao.
Zhang Miao first said to Zhang Chao: I heard that you are a prefect and leave government affairs to Zang Hong. What kind of person is Zang Hong?
Zhang Chao said: Zang Hong is a strange man in the country. He is more talented and resourceful than me.
Zhang Miao immediately talked to Zang Hong and greatly appreciated him.
He sent Zang Hong to see Liu Dai, the governor of Yanzhou, and Kong Danyou, the governor of Yuzhou, and they both became close friends with each other.
Zhang Miao originally had an agreement. When Zhang Chao arrived, he made the decision, so he held a meeting with the herdsmen in Suanzao.
They set up a altar and prepared to make an alliance, but they gave in to each other. No one dared to go first, and everyone recommended Zang Hong.
Zang Hong then raised his clothes to the altar, expressed his blood and made an alliance, saying: The Han Dynasty was unlucky, and the rules and regulations of the court were in chaos. The traitor Dong Zhuo took the opportunity to cause harm, and the disaster fell on the emperor and poisoned the people.
The most terrifying thing is that the Han Dynasty fell and the country was ruined.
Liu Dai, the governor of Yanzhou, Kong Qianyou, the governor of Yuzhou, Zhang Miao, the governor of Chenliu, Qiao Mao, the governor of Dongjun, Zhang Chao, the governor of Guangling, etc., gathered volunteers to fight against the national calamity.
All those who are in our alliance will work together to fulfill the loyalty of our ministers and kill their heads as they please without any second thought.
If he violates the oath, he will die and die without any descendants.
The emperor, the queen, the earth, the ancestors and the gods all learn from each other.
Zang Hong's poems were so passionate that everyone who listened to them got excited.
From then on, each army hesitated, and no one dared to go first, resulting in insufficient military supplies and the disintegration of the soldiers.
At this time, Gongsun Zan, the commander-in-chief of the imperial army, had a disagreement with Liu Yu, the commander-in-chief. Zhang Chao sent Zang Hong to find Liu Yu to discuss the plan to defeat the bandits. When they walked to the river, they encountered a war between You and Ji, and the road was blocked, so they went to Yuan Shao's place.
Yuan Shao met Zang Hong and admired his talent. He became friends with Zang Hong and asked Zang Hong to act as the governor of Qingzhou.
The former governor, Jiao He, had a false reputation and was a master of empty words.
At this time, yellow scarf thieves were scurrying everywhere, and the people in Qingzhou were rich and had many troops and equipment.
Jiao He wanted to go to the capital with various allies, but before he left, the Yellow Turban thieves had already arrived, conquered the city and massacred the people.
Jiao He didn't know anything about military affairs, so he just invited the witch Zhu Shi to his house to pray for God's blessing.
He was also afraid that yellow turban thieves would cross the river during the freezing period, so he ordered many ice-trap pills to be made and placed in the river.
His tribe was disbanded and Jiao He also died of illness.
Zang Hong gathered together to comfort the scattered tribes, and the people were at peace.
In the second year of his reign, Yuan Shao was afraid of his incompetence and appointed him as the prefect of Dongjun, with his capital in Dongwuyang.
At this time, Cao Cao surrounded Zhang Chao in Yongqiu, and the situation was very dangerous.
Zhang Chao said to the soldiers: Zang Hong is the only one who will come to save me today.
Some people say: Yuan Shao and Cao Cao are getting along well, and Zang Hong is Yuan Shao's man. I'm afraid Zang Hong will not come far away, and he will bring disaster instead of good fortune.
Zhang Chao said: Ziyuan is a righteous man in the world and will never deviate from his original aspirations. He may be held hostage by force, but there is nothing we can do!
Zang Hong began to hear that Zhang Chao was surrounded, cried barefoot, and prepared his troops to rescue Zhang Chao.
Thinking that his troops were too weak, he asked Yuan Shao for troops, but Yuan Shao refused. Zhang Chao's defense was breached and Zhang Chao's entire clan was killed.
Zang Hong resented Yuan Shao and severed ties with him.
Yuan Shao sent troops to surround Zang Hong, but could not capture it after many years. Yuan Shao sent Zang Hong to write a letter to Zang Hong from Chen Lin, a county resident, explaining the blessings and misfortunes to Zang Hong, and blaming each other with personal kindness and national justice.
Zang Hong replied: Missing each other after farewell often occurs when we are asleep.
We are not far apart, but each of us has taken a different path, and each of us has a different mood. How can we describe it in just one or two sentences?
summary: Zang Hong, from Guangling, was made a Dong Zilang due to his father's military merits. After Dong Zhuo killed the emperor, Zang Hong urged Prefect Zhang Chao to raise an army. He helped organize an alliance at Suanzao, where he gave a passionate oath, calling for the destruction of Dong Zhuo. The alliance, however, failed to act decisively. Later, Zang Hong served Yuan Shao as Qingzhou's governor, pacifying the region. When Cao Cao besieged Zhang Chao, Zang Hong begged Yuan Shao for troops to rescue him, but Yuan Shao refused. Zhang Chao was killed. Enraged, Zang Hong broke with Yuan Shao, who then besieged him. Despite a letter from Chen Lin urging surrender, Zang Hong refused, accusing Yuan Shao of betraying allies and killing loyal men. He stated he would rather die for righteousness. During the siege, he shared his last food with his soldiers and even killed his concubine to feed them. The city fell, and Zang Hong was captured. He defiantly cursed Yuan Shao for his treachery and was executed. His subordinate Chen Rong also chose to die with him.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/虞傅盖臧列传

translation:
◆Biography of Yuan An, Yuan An, courtesy name Shaogong, was born in Ruyang County, Runan County.
Grandfather Yuan Liang studied "Mencius' Book of Changes". During the reign of Emperor Ping of the Han Dynasty, he was recommended for his Ming Dynasty and became the crown prince. In the early years of Jianwu, he became the magistrate of Chengwu County.
Yuan An inherited the knowledge of his grandfather Yuan Liang when he was young.
He is a very dignified man, has authority, and is respected by people in the state.
He started to work as a county magistrate. Once, he went to the prefecture with a letter to do some work. He asked Yuan An to send a letter to the county magistrate. Yuan An said: "You are doing official business, and you have a post to deliver it for you. If it is a private matter, you should not ask me for merit."
He declined to accept the letter, and the person in charge was a little scared, so he stopped entrusting him.
Later, he was recommended as Xiaolian and became the magistrate of Yinping County and Rencheng County successively. Wherever he worked, officials and people respected and loved him.
In the twelfth year of Yongping, King Liu Ying of Chu conspired to rebel against the imperial court, and the case was submitted to the county for verification.
The next year, the three government offices recommended Yuan An to handle cases, believing that he could handle complex cases. The emperor appointed him as the prefect of Chu County.
At this time, thousands of people were imprisoned due to the confession of Chu King Liu Ying. Xianzong lost his temper, and the investigators were eager to finalize the case. They tortured many people to force them to confess, and many of them were sentenced to death.
After Yuan An arrived at the county, he went to the prison instead of entering the yamen, tried those who had no obvious evidence, reported them one by one, and let them be released from prison.
The officials and officials of the government all kowtowed to Yuan An and argued that anyone who agreed with Liu Ying, the king of Chu, would be guilty of the same crime as Liu Ying according to the law. Yuan An disagreed.
Yuan An said: If there is any violation of the regulations, I will bear full responsibility and will not harm you.
So they were reported one by one.
The emperor was moved to consciousness and immediately agreed, and more than 400 families were released from prison.
A year later, Yuan An was conscripted into Henan Yin.
The government's orders were very strict, but no one was ever tried for bribery.
He often said: Anyone who is an official hopes to be a prime minister at the highest level, and a prefect at the lowest level. To imprison talents in the age of sage is something I cannot bear to do.
Those who heard this were very moved and encouraged themselves to be honest and honest.
Yuan An had been in office for ten years, and the political discipline in the capital was very orderly, and his reputation was highly valued by the court.
In the eighth year of Jianchu's reign, he was promoted to imperial servant.
In the second year of Yuanhe, Meng Yun, the governor of Wuwei, wrote: The Northern Huns had already made peace, but the Southern Huns went to rob them again. The Northern Chanyu said that the Han Dynasty deceived them and wanted to invade the border.
The prisoners should be returned to comfort them.
The emperor issued an edict to summon hundreds of officials to the court for discussion. The ministers all thought that the Yi Di were cunning and greedy. After being captured, they would exaggerate and exaggerate. This should not be the case.
summary: Yuan An, courtesy name Shaogong, was from Ruyang County in Runan. He inherited his grandfather Yuan Liang's knowledge of the *Book of Changes*. A dignified and authoritative man respected by his state, he began his career as a county magistrate. When a superior asked him to deliver a private letter, Yuan An refused, stating that official business should use official channels and private matters should not seek merit through him. He was later recommended as Xiaolian and served as magistrate of Yinping and Rencheng counties, where officials and people respected him. In the twelfth year of Yongping, when King Liu Ying of Chu conspired to rebel, Yuan An was appointed prefect of Chu County to handle the case. Thousands were imprisoned due to confessions, and investigators tortured many to death. Yuan An went directly to the prison, tried those without clear evidence, and reported them for release. Despite officials arguing that associates of Liu Ying were equally guilty, Yuan An took full responsibility. The emperor agreed, and over 400 families were freed.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁张韩周列传

translation:
Yuan An said: The Northern Huns sent envoys to pay tribute and request peace, and also returned the captives to the Han Dynasty. This shows that they were afraid of the prestige of the Han Dynasty, and did not violate the treaty first.
Meng Yun, as a minister, guards the border and should not be dishonest to the Yi and Di. Letting the prisoners go back is enough to show China's lenience towards them, and it is great to bring peace to the people on the border.
Situ Huanyu changed his mind and obeyed Yuan An.
Taiwei Zheng Hong, Sikong Wulun and others all hated Yuan An.
Zheng Hong also loudly angered Huan Yu and said: Anyone who advocates the release of prisoners is disloyal to the emperor.
Huan Yu scolded him on the spot. Wu Lun and Dahonglu Wei Biao were so angry that their faces changed color. Sili Xiaowei reported the whole situation to the emperor, and Yuan An and others handed over their seals and ribbons to the emperor to plead guilty.
Suzong issued an edict saying: The long time to discuss politics shows that everyone has different opinions.
Important matters in the court should be discussed more frequently, and strategies should be decided upon by everyone. It is good to have an upright and polite attitude when speaking, but it is not a blessing for the court to dare to say anything when trouble occurs. What faults do you have that you should blame yourself for?
It’s better to put on your hat and put on your shoes!
In the end, the emperor followed Yuan An's suggestion.
The next year, Yuan An replaced Wu Lun as Sikong.
In the first year of Zhanghe, he replaced Huan Yu as Situ.
When Emperor He came to the throne, due to his young age, the Queen Mother Dou came to the court to listen to the government. The Queen Mother's brother, the cavalry general Dou Xian, went north to attack the Xiongnu. Yuan An, together with the Taiwei Song You, Sikong Renkai and Jiu Qing, went to the court to dissuade them. They believed that the Xiongnu did not invade the frontier and sent troops for no reason. It cost the country money and claimed credit from thousands of miles away. This was not a proper national policy.
Even the last few letters were withheld and not reported.
Song You was a little frightened and did not dare to submit a letter by his name, and the ministers gradually became silent.
Only Yuan An and Ren Wei still insisted on the right path and did not give in. They even took off their hats and went to the court to fight for more than ten times.
The Queen Mother still refused to listen, and everyone was worried about Yuan An, but Yuan An remained calm and composed.
Dou Xian had already sent troops to fight. His younger brothers, Weiwei Dou Du and Zhijinwu Dou Jing, each relied on their own power and openly allowed their minions to block roads and rob property in the capital.
Dou Jing also sent people to distribute messages to the border counties without authorization, mobilized cavalry commandos and capable shooters, and ordered officials from Yuyang, Yanmen, and Shanggu counties to send them to Dou Jing's residence.
The officials concerned were afraid and did not dare to say no.
Yuan An impeached Dou Jing for mobilizing border guards without authorization and disturbing the officials and the people. The governor did not wait for Fu Xin but followed Dou Jing's arrangements. He should be beheaded in public.
He also reported to Si Lixiaowei and Henan Yin to please their dependent relatives and failed to uphold justice. They requested that they be removed from their official positions and punished according to law.
These memorials were withheld and not reported.
Dou Xian and Dou Jing were even more tyrannical. They deployed their cronies in various cities and towns to collect taxes and bribes from officials and people, and other states and counties followed suit.
Yuan An and Ren Wei jointly reported the two thousand stone governors, and more than 40 people who were implicated in being demoted and dismissed from office. The Dou family held a grudge.
But Yuan An and Ren Wei have always been of noble character, and there is no way to harm them.
At that time, Dou Xian sent troops to Wuwei.
In the second year, Bei Shanyu was defeated by Geng Kui and fled to Wuhuan. There was no one in control of Beikong, and it was unknown who was in charge of the remaining Huns.
Dou Xian boasted about his achievements every day and wanted to use his favor to build a good relationship with the remaining Northern Huns, so he wrote a letter to appoint A Tong, the surrendered King of Zuoluli, as the Northern Chanyu, with General Zhonglang as his guardian, just like he had done in the past to establish the Southern Chanyu.
The emperor handed over the matter to the ministers for discussion. Ten people including Taiwei Song You, Taichang Dinghong, Guangluxun Geng Bing and others thought that this could be done.
Yuan An and Ren Wei reported that Emperor Guangwu's recruitment of the southern Xiongnu was not to allow him to settle in the interior forever, but was a temporary measure because he wanted them to resist the northern Xiongnu.
summary: Yuan An later served as Henan Yin for ten years, maintaining strict but fair governance with no bribery cases. He believed officials should aspire to be prime ministers or prefects, not imprison talented people. He was promoted to imperial servant, then to Sikong and later Situ. When Emperor He ascended as a child, Empress Dowager Dou ruled. Her brother Dou Xian attacked the Xiongnu without provocation. Yuan An and others repeatedly advised against this costly policy, but their memorials were withheld. Yuan An also impeached Dou Jing for illegally mobilizing border troops. When Dou Xian wanted to appoint a surrendered Xiongnu king as Northern Chanyu, Yuan An argued against it, warning it would empty the treasury and break faith with the Southern Chanyu. Dou Xian proceeded anyway, but the appointee soon rebelled as Yuan An predicted. Yuan An died in the spring of four years, deeply mourned by court officials.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁张韩周列传

translation:
Dou Xian relied on his own power insidiously, spoke proudly, exposed others' shortcomings, and even scolded Yuan An. He also brought up the example of Emperor Guangwu killing Han Xin and Dai She to intimidate Yuan An, but Yuan An never gave in.
In the end, Dou Xian still appointed the Xiongnu surrender general You Luli and King Yu Zhijian as a chanyu, but he soon rebelled, just as Yuan An expected.
Yuan An believed that the emperor was young and weak, and his relatives were in power. Every time he went to court and talked about national affairs with the ministers, he would cry bitterly.
From the emperor to the ministers, everyone relied on him.
In the spring of four years, Yuan An died, and the court officials were very sad.
A few months later, the Dou family collapsed, and the emperor began to rule in person. Recalling the situation between the pros and cons that discussed state affairs in the past, he named Yuan An's son Yuan Shang as a man.
He dismissed Song You, appointed Yin Mu as Taiwei, and Liu Fang as Sikong. Yin Mu, a native of Henan, died in office.
Liu Fang, a native of Pingyuan, later committed a crime, was dismissed from his post, returned home, and committed suicide. ◆Biography of Zhang Youfu, named Menghou, a native of Xiyang, Runan, and a descendant of Zhao Wang Zhang Ao.
Zhang Ao's son Zhang Shou was granted the title of Chiyang Township in Xiyang. He was later deposed and settled here.
Zhang Youfu learned Shangshu from his grandfather Zhang Chong when he was young and was able to inherit his studies. He also served Taichang Huanrong.
He was diligent and never slacked off, gathering hundreds of followers.
In the ninth year of Yongping, Xianzong opened a school for Xiaohou of the fourth surname in Nangong and set up a "Five Classics" teacher.
Zhang Youfu taught his disciples using "Shang Shu" and gave lectures in front of the emperor several times. Because the discussion was difficult to meet the monarch's wishes, he was appointed as a minister, given carriages, horses and clothes, and was asked to enter the palace and be crowned the crown prince.
Zhang Youfu was a simple and upright man who abided by the scriptures. Every time he gave lectures, he would often correct his mistakes, because seriousness made people afraid.
When Suzong came to the throne, Zhang Youfu was promoted to the position of Shizhong and Huben Zhonglang.
A few months later, he became the governor of Dongjun.
Zhang Youfu thought he had been close to the emperor, but he didn't realize it, so he felt a little dissatisfied. So Shangshu Ci said: "I am a fool who relies on Confucian classics to influence me. I don't change my position when I am young. I don't know grammar. I should criticize Fudian County. I have a long-term leadership. I must be guilty of being unfaithful and humiliating my position."
The minister was thinking about himself in private, and did not consider leaving the city. He hoped to retain his favor and support redundant officials. The officials were uneasy and did not dare to avoid being ugly after hearing and seeing.
The imperial edict reported: The scriptures say: Although I am outside my body, my heart never leaves the royal family.
Diancheng is close to the people, and it is extremely effective. The good and the ugly will go up, no matter how far or near.
I will give you 300,000 yuan now, so hurry up and take office.
Although Zhang Youfu was a Confucian scholar, he had a strong character.
After taking office, he promoted volunteers and bravery to fight against powerful men.
summary: Zhang Youfu, courtesy name Menghou, was from Xiyang, Runan, a descendant of Zhao King Zhang Ao. He studied *Shangshu* from his grandfather and later served Taichang Huanrong, gathering hundreds of followers. During Yongping, he taught *Shangshu* at the imperial school and lectured before the emperor, who appointed him as a minister and tutor to the crown prince. A simple, upright man who strictly adhered to the classics, he was promoted to governor of Dongjun under Suzong. Though a Confucian scholar, he had a strong character and fought against powerful men. He promoted Wang Qing, whose family had shown three generations of loyalty, to a high position.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁张韩周列传

translation:
If an official kills a thief, Zhang Youfu investigates and punishes him. He thinks that if the official receives the stolen goods, it is not a death penalty. The thieves are all hungry and cold people, so how can they exhaust their methods?
Wang Qing, a county official, and his grandfather Wang Weng, together with the former prefect Zhai Yi, raised an army to attack Wang Mang. When Zhai Yi failed and all the remaining people surrendered, Wang Weng fought alone, and Wang Mang burned him.
His father, Wang Long, served as the captain of the imperial court in the early years of Jianwu, and Wang Qing served as a minor historian.
When he and his father were traveling to the county with the captain, they encountered thieves on the road. Wang Long defended the captain with his body and died in the accident. Wang Ben was also shot in the throat by an arrow, making his voice hoarse.
The former county guard believed that Wang Qing was completely injured and could not lift.
Zhang Youfu saw this and sighed: Is there a loyal family that cannot be rewarded by a noble?
So he was promoted to the position of extreme right-wing Cao Cao, and he was also recommended to the emperor for the death of three generations of Wang Qing's family, so he should receive a remarkable gift.
The memorial was sent to Sangong, and he was appointed by Sikong.
After Zhang Youfu went out, whenever he saw the king's masters, the emperor often said: When Zhang Youfu was a minister in the past, he often gave correct advice, and his words were honest and sincere, out of sincerity. It can be said that he has the demeanor of Shiyu.
In the second year of Yuanhe, the emperor went on a hunting tour to the East and visited Dongjun. He invited Zhang Youfu and his disciples and the officials of the counties and counties to gather in the court. The emperor first prepared the disciples' rituals, asked Zhang Youfu to lecture on "Shangshu", and then repaired the rituals of the monarch and his ministers.
The rewards are special and nothing is inappropriate.
Zhang Youfu served as an official for fifteen years, and in the early years of Emperor He's reign, he was promoted to the prefect of Wei County.
Zheng Ju, a native of the county, was serving as the Sili Xiaowei at that time, and he was dismissed from the post of Jin Wu Dou Jing.
Dou Jing was later restored to power, and sent Xia Meng to personally thank Youfu, saying: "Zheng Ju is a villain, and I was wronged by him."
I heard that his son was an official and indulged in disorder.
Take this Cao Zi alone to serve as a warning to others.
Zhang Youfu was furious and immediately put Xia Meng in prison. He made a speech to Jinwu Mansion. He suspected that Xia Meng was not equal to Zheng Ju's son, so he pretended to express your opinion in order to avenge himself.
Xia Meng was released from prison when he was ordered to atone.
Soon, he was conquered as Henan Yin.
Dou Jing's family also wounded the city's soldiers, and the officials captured them. Dou Jing was angry and sent Tiqi Hou Hai and other 500 people to beat and injure the city's chief.
Zhang Youfu's subordinates Yang Zhang and others investigated thoroughly and found out that Zhenghou Hai was guilty of the crime and had his army exiled to Shuofang.
Dou Jing was furious, so he wrote a letter mentioning Yang Zhang and six others as Jinwu officials, hoping to take revenge on them.
Yang Zhang and others were frightened and reported to Zhang Youfu that they were willing to incriminate Zang themselves in exchange for Ci Jing's fate.
Zhang Youfu immediately wrote a letter explaining his situation.
Empress Dowager Dou issued an edict saying: From now on, I will appoint officials in charge of the Jin Dynasty and do not send them away.
When Dou failed, Zhang Youfu went to court and said: I am really stupid and inferior to the general rule. I thought that although Dou was convicted, his crime was not exposed. Later generations did not see his crime and only heard that he was killed. This was not a sign of national canon and left to the future.
summary: When the emperor toured Dongjun, he invited Zhang Youfu and his disciples to lecture on *Shangshu*. After fifteen years of service, Zhang Youfu became prefect of Wei County. When Dou Jing sought revenge against Zheng Ju through Zhang Youfu, Zhang Youfu imprisoned Dou Jing's messenger instead. Later, as Henan Yin, he investigated Dou Jing's men who had injured city soldiers and exiled them. After Dou Xian's fall, Zhang Youfu argued that Dou's crimes should be publicly examined rather than secretly punished. He was promoted to Taiwei but repeatedly requested retirement due to illness. The emperor refused, sending gifts and urging him to remain in service.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁张韩周列传

translation:
It should be handed down to the magistrates so that everyone in the world can comment together.
When Dou Xian and others favored the nobles, the ministers were afraid that it would be too late to please them. They all said that Dou Xian was entrusted by Gu Ming and had the loyalty of Yi Yin and Lu Shang. They even compared Mrs. Deng to the wife of King Wen.
Nowadays, when people are strict and majestic, they all say that they should be punished by death. We no longer care about the before and after, and analyze the reasons behind it.
When I see Xia Yanghou, I always have a loyal and kind heart. I told you last time that I always have a sense of integrity, check the guests, and never break the law.
I heard that the punishment of flesh and blood has three meanings: too thick but not too thin.
The current deputies believe that a strict and capable prime minister should be selected, fearing that he will be forced to do so, and he will not be completely removed. The loan should be reduced and extended to uphold virtue.
Emperor He was moved by Zhang Youfu's words, changed his title, and returned to his fiefdom.
In the fifth year of Yongyuan, Zhang Youfu was promoted to imperial servant.
A few months later, Dai Yinmu was promoted to Taiwei.
Several times Shangshu asked to retire due to illness and recommended Xu Fang, the prefect of Wei County, to replace him.
The emperor did not allow it, so he asked Zhonghuangmen to inquire about his illness, and he also gave him delicacies and 300,000 yuan.
Zhang Youfu's illness became more serious.
At that time, his son Zhang Fan was serving as minister, so the emperor sent Xiaohuangmen to restrain Lifan and said: "Yin and Yang are at odds, tens of thousands of people have been displaced. The imperial court hopes that the public will consider the gains and losses, be of one mind with the country, and purify oneself because of illness, and ask for removal of important responsibilities. Who will share the responsibility with me?"
There is no hope of being of one heart and one mind.
Situ Liu Fang is suffering from a serious illness, and Sikong Zhang Fen is old. He hopes that his father will obey his orders and not show his restraint.
Zhang Youfu was afraid of going to the court to apologize and returned to his original post.
Although Zhang Youfu was in the official position, his father often lived in the fields. Zhang Youfu would go to the capital once every time his position changed.
People who admired Zhang Youfu would come to Zhang Youfu's house every New Year's Eve to drink wine and celebrate his birthday. They had a great time and everyone was envious of him.
When his father died and was buried, the imperial edict sent an envoy with cattle and wine to remove his mourning clothes.
Later, Zhang Youfu met Yan Cheng, the captain of the Sili School, in the court hall due to business. Zhang Youfu calmly said to Yan Cheng: Most of the officials recruited by the three prefectures were not employed properly.
After Yan returned home, he immediately ordered the three prefectures to verify their official history.
Zhang Youfu was originally having a private conversation, but he didn't expect that Yan would report it at the meeting, and he was very resentful.
Encountering another thank you, Zhang Youfu scolded Yan Cheng. Yan Cheng's words didn't go well with him, and Zhang Youfu got angry, so he scolded him in court. Yan Cheng impeached Zhang Youfu for complaining.
Because Zhang Youfu was the teacher of the late emperor, the emperor ordered a meeting with ministers, doctors, and courtiers.
Situ Lugai reported that Zhang Youfu was in the third division. He knew that there was etiquette in public affairs. He did not hold his breath and bow in response to the edict. Instead, he made eloquent remarks, resented and blamed the envoys. He could not set an example for Siyuan.
So he was dismissed from his post.
Zhang Youfu returned to his residence, thanked all the students, and closed the door without interacting with the guests.
Zuo Zhonglang, He Chang, and most of the speakers praised Zhang Youfu for his loyalty, and the emperor also respected him.
summary: Zhang Youfu's father lived in the countryside, and Zhang Youfu visited him whenever his position changed. After his father's death, Zhang Youfu was dismissed for scolding an official in court. He returned home, closed his doors, and refused visitors. Later reinstated as Guang Luxun and then Situ, he died soon after. Before death, he instructed his son to bury him simply without an ancestral hall, using only a straw shelter for offerings.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁张韩周列传

translation:
In the fifteenth year, he was worshiped as Guang Luxun.
After a few months, Lu Gong became Situ.
Yu Yu died.
The ministers of the imperial court sat in plain carriages to pay their respects to him, and gave him a place for his tomb, but the grace he gave him was different from his appearance.
When Youfu was about to become ill, he told his son: "I wanted to set a model of frugality for the world by dew offering sacrifices on the ground in Xianjie Mausoleum."
Since I, as the Three Officials, cannot promote the king's behavior and make the officials do things according to the rules, how can I not be economical? After death, there is no need to build an ancestral hall. You can just build a house with straw and offer sacrifices underneath. ◆Han Lengzhuan, Han Lengzi Bo Shi, a native of Wuyang, Yingchuan, and a descendant of Gonggaohou Xiuguidang.
Generations is a famous surname in the township.
His father, Han Xun, served as the governor of Longxi during the Jianwu period.
Han Leng lost his father when he was four years old, and his adoptive mother and brother were known as filial friends.
When he reached his prime, he gave away millions of his father's remaining wealth to his cousins, and the villagers praised him for his high style.
When he began to serve as a meritorious official in the county, the prefect Ge Xing suffered from a stroke and was unable to handle government affairs. Han Leng secretly handled official affairs on behalf of Ge Xing. He stayed in and out for two years without disobeying orders.
Ge Xing's son once wanted to be an official, but Han Leng refused, so he ordered those who complained to report him.
The official document was handed over for inspection. The officials believed that Han Leng was covering up Ge Xing's illness and taking charge of the county guard's duties without authorization, so they locked up Han Leng.
Xianzong knew Han Leng's loyalty and later issued an edict to forgive him.
From then on, he was recruited into the court and promoted to Shangshu Ling five times. Together with Pu She Zhi Shou and Shangshu Chen Chong, they were all famous for their talents.
Suzong once gave swords to various ministers, but only these three people wrote their names on the swords: Han Leng, Chu Longyuan, Zhi Shou, Shu Hanwen, Chen Chong, Jinan Zhicheng.
Commentators at the time explained it: Han Lengyuan had profound strategies, so he won Longyuan; Zhi Shouming had great articles, so he won Hanwen; Chen Chong was honest and simple, and his beauty was not expressed externally, so he won Zicheng.
When Emperor He came to the throne, his servant Dou Xian sent people to assassinate Liu Chang, the Duxiang Marquis, the son of King Shang of Qi, at the Shangdong Gate. Some officials were afraid of Dou Xian and deliberately suspected Liu Chang's brother.
The emperor ordered the censor to go to Qi to investigate the matter.
Han Leng Shangshu believed that thieves were in the capital, and they should not abandon the near and ask for the distant ones, for fear of being laughed at by the traitorous ministers.
Queen Mother Dou was angry and blamed Han Leng, but Han Leng insisted on his opinion.
When the incident was revealed, it turned out to be exactly what he said.
Dou Xian was very frightened and asked the Queen Mother to attack the Huns to atone for his sins.
Han Leng went to Shu to remonstrate with him again, but the Queen Mother did not listen.
When Dou Xian achieved meritorious service and returned as a general, his fame shocked the world, and he sent troops to station in Wuwei.
Encountering the emperor's mausoleum in the West Ancestral Temple, he ordered Dou Xian to meet Chao Jia in Chang'an.
When Dou Xian arrived and the officials below Shangshu discussed wanting to worship Dou Xian, they fell to the ground and said long live him.
Han Leng said sternly: Don't be flattering to superiors, don't be slanderous to inferiors, and be polite to no one.
Those who discussed it were ashamed to give up their opinions.
summary: Han Leng, courtesy name Bo Shi, was from Wuyang, Yingchuan, a descendant of Marquis Xiugui. Orphaned at four, he was known for filial piety and gave away his father's wealth to cousins. As a county official, he secretly handled affairs for a paralyzed prefect for two years. Though imprisoned for this, Emperor Xianzong pardoned him. He was promoted to Shangshu Ling and was known for his talent. Emperor Suzong once gave swords inscribed with names to three ministers, including Han Leng, whose sword was inscribed "Longyuan" for his profound strategies.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁张韩周列传

translation:
Wang Long, the minister Zuocheng, secretly wrote a memorial to give Dou Xian some beef and wine. Han Leng gave the memorial to Long and sentenced him to the crime of Cheng Dan.
Han Leng recommended several good officials to the court, including Ying Shun, Lu Zhang, and Zhou Yu, all of whom were famous at that time.
When the Dou family failed, Han Leng took charge of investigating the case and went after his accomplices, not taking a break or bathing for several months.
The emperor thought that Han Leng was worried about his country and had forgotten his home, so he gave him three hundred pieces of cloth.
Han Leng was promoted to the governor of Nanyang. The court specially allowed Han Leng to go home and visit his ancestors' graves, which was considered an honor by the villagers.
Han Leng exposed the thieves and villains, and the villains in the county were all afraid. The political slogan was strict fairness.
A few years later, he was called into the imperial court as a servant.
In the winter of the ninth year, he served as Sikong on behalf of Zhang Fen.
He died the next year. His son Han Fu became the prime minister of Zhao Wangliang's grandson Liu Shang during the reign of Emperor An.
◆Zhou Rongzhuan, named Pingsun Zhou, was born in Shu, Lujiang.
During the reign of Emperor Suzong, he was summoned to Situ Yuan'an's house as an official by holding the Ming Dynasty Classics.
Yuan An discussed with Zhou Rong several times and thought highly of him.
When Yuan An raised the issue of Dou Xian and Dou Jing argued for the establishment of Beidan, it was Zhou Rong who drafted it.
Dou's guest Taiwei Xu Zhiqi disliked him very much and threatened Zhou Rong, saying: "You are Yuan Gong's confidant. I'm going to tell you that Dou's thugs and assassins are all over the city. Be careful!"
Zhou Rong said: I am the only son of Jianghuai. Thanks to the kindness of the late emperor, I have been the master of two cities.
Now that he can be promoted to Situ Mansion, he is very willing to be harmed by the Dou family.
Therefore, I often warn my wife not to rush into the funeral if a disaster suddenly strikes her, hoping to make the court wake up with a mere corruption.
When the Dou family failed, Zhou Rong became famous.
From Li Lingti to Shangshu Ling.
When he was the prefect of Yingchuan, he violated the law and was imprisoned. Emperor He thought of Zhou Rongzhong Festival and was demoted to the county magistrate of Gongxian County.
For more than a year, he was appointed as the governor of Shanyang.
The counties he passed through were praised.
Due to old age and illness, he requested to retire and died at home. The imperial edict granted him 200,000 yuan, and appointed his son Zhou Xing as the doctor.
Zhou Xing was famous when he was young. During the Yongning period, Chen Zhong, the minister, recommended Zhou Xingdao: I remember that the ancient emperors had orders, and their words must be grand and elegant, and their rhetoric must be gentle and graceful. They must be handed down to future generations and listed in the classics.
Therefore, Zhongni praised Tang Yu's articles and followed the elegance of Zhou Dynasty.
I saw Guanglu Lang Zhou Xing privately, and his filial friend's trip was recorded in his boudoir, and his clear and serious ambitions were heard in the state.
Study ancient and modern times and learn a lot about history. The chapters of "Three Tombs" and the strategies of "Five Codes" should be read.
Writing an article is very impressive.
The Minister of Finance accepts the emperor's orders and serves as the king's mouthpiece.
The ministers are stupid and dark, and the ministers are mostly literary and vulgar officials, with few elegant talents. Every time they draft edicts, declare internal and external affairs, and turn to each other for petitions, some of them are incompetent and focus on their own freedom, and their words are often vulgar and crude.
summary: When Dou Xian assassinated a marquis, Han Leng insisted the thieves were in the capital, not elsewhere. Though the Empress Dowager was angry, the truth proved him correct. When officials wanted to bow to Dou Xian and shout "long live," Han Leng sternly rebuked them. After the Dou family fell, Han Leng investigated their accomplices tirelessly, and the emperor rewarded him with cloth. He became governor of Nanyang, where he exposed villains and maintained strict fairness. Later recalled as a servant, he served as Sikong but died the following year. Zhou Rong, courtesy name Pingsun, was from Shu, Lujiang. During Suzong's reign, he served as an official in Situ Yuan An's house. Yuan An valued him highly, and Zhou Rong drafted Yuan An's arguments against Dou Xian regarding the Northern Chanyu. When Dou Xian's guest threatened Zhou Rong with assassins, Zhou Rong declared he was willing to be harmed to awaken the court. After the Dou family fell, Zhou Rong became famous and rose to Shangshu Ling. As governor of Yingchuan, he violated the law but was demoted rather than imprisoned due to his loyalty. He later served as governor of Shanyang with praise, then retired due to illness and died at home. His son Zhou Xing was recommended for his literary talent and served as Shangshu Lang before dying.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁张韩周列传

translation:
◆Yuan Shao Zhuan, Yuan Shao, courtesy name Benchu, was born in Ruyang, Runan, and was the grandson of Situ Yuan Tang.
Yuan Shao's father, Yuan Cheng, had served as a lieutenant general with five senses. He was physically strong and liked to make friends. From the time of the great general Liang Ji, he was always friends with him.
Yuan Shao served as a Langguan when he was young, and was later appointed as the Chief of Puyang. When his mother died, he resigned from the official position.
After serving three years of funeral service, Yuan Shao recalled and lamented that he had lost his father since childhood and had to attend the funeral service for his father.
After the mourning period expired, he moved to Luoyang.
Yuan Shao was elegant, beautiful, kind to others, and focused on reputation.
Yuan Shao's ancestors had served as three ministers for generations, and the guests came to join him. In addition, Yuan Shao lowered his status to befriend him, so all the scholars rushed to join him. Regardless of whether the scholars who came were high or low, Yuan Shaoyu and others were equal in etiquette. Various vehicles of visiting guests crowded the streets and alleys.
The courtiers around the emperor were disgusted with him.
Zhongchang Shi Zaozhong said in the ban: Yuan Benchu ​​does things to enhance his reputation and value, and likes to raise people who are not afraid of death. I don't know what this kid wants to do!
After hearing this, Yuan Shao's uncle Taifu Yuan Wei called Yuan Shao and reprimanded him with the words of Zhong Zhong, but Yuan Shao never changed.
Later, Yuan Shao was summoned by General He Jin as a subordinate officer and served as Shi Yushi and Huben Zhonglang General.
In the fifth year of Zhongping, the imperial court began to set up eight Xiyuan captains and appointed Yuan Shao as the assistant military captain.
When Emperor Ling died, Yuan Shao persuaded He Jin to recruit Dong Zhuo and other troops and coerced the Queen Mother to kill all the eunuchs. He Jin transferred Yuan Shao to serve as the captain of the Sili school.
The incident has been recorded in "The Biography of He Jin".
When Dong Zhuo led his army to the capital, Bao Xin, the cavalry captain from Taishan, persuaded Yuan Shao: If Dong Zhuo controls a powerful army, he will have the intention of rebelling. If we don't deal with it early, we will definitely be controlled by Dong Zhuo.
When Dong Zhuo had just arrived and the soldiers were tired, they attacked Dong Zhuo and captured him.
Yuan Shao was afraid of Dong Zhuo and did not dare to send troops.
Soon, Dong Zhuo discussed deposing the emperor and establishing a new emperor. He said to Yuan Shao: The monarch who rules the world should find a wise person. Every time I think of Emperor Ling, it makes me angry.
Marquis Dong seems to be okay, and he should be made emperor now.
Yuan Shao said: "The emperor is young now and has done nothing wrong to spread the news to the world. If you ignore etiquette and follow your own desires, abolish your legitimate heir and establish your concubine as emperor, I am afraid that everyone will not think it is appropriate."
Dong Zhuo put his sword in his hand and scolded Yuan Shao angrily, saying: How dare you talk like this!
Don’t I have the final say in everything in the world?
I want to do this, who dares to disobey!
Yuan Shao replied wittily: This is a national matter. Please go outside to discuss it with the Taifu.
Dong Zhuo also said: There are not enough descendants of the Liu family to keep.
Yuan Shao was furious and said: "You are the only one who is tyrannical in the world, Dong Gong!"
He laid out his sword, bowed to the end, and walked out.
summary: Yuan Shao, courtesy name Benchu, was from Ruyang, Runan, and the grandson of Situ Yuan Tang. His father Yuan Cheng served as a lieutenant general. Yuan Shao began his career as a Langguan and later became Chief of Puyang. After his mother's death, he resigned to observe mourning, and later also mourned his father. He then moved to Luoyang, where his elegant demeanor and generosity attracted many scholars, leading to resentment from court eunuchs. His uncle Yuan Wei reprimanded him, but Yuan Shao did not change his ways. Yuan Shao served under General He Jin as a subordinate officer and later as Colonel of the Eight Xiuyuan. After Emperor Ling's death, he advised He Jin to eliminate the eunuchs, but He Jin was killed. When Dong Zhuo arrived, Yuan Shao opposed his plan to depose the young emperor. After a heated argument, Yuan Shao fled to Jizhou. Dong Zhuo initially offered a reward for his capture but later pardoned him and appointed him Governor of Bohai and Marquis of Yunxiang.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上

translation:
He hung the talisman on the upper door and fled to Jizhou.
Dong Zhuo offered a reward for Yuan Shao's capture.
At that time, Secretary Zhou and Wu Qiong, the captain of the city gate school, were trusted by Dong Zhuo. Wu Qiong and others secretly interceded for Yuan Shao and persuaded Dong Zhuo: The important matter of deposing and establishing the emperor is not something ordinary people can participate in.
Yuan Shao didn't understand the overall situation and ran away in fear, not because he had other ideas.
Now the rush to put a reward on him will inevitably lead to sudden changes.
The four generations of the Yuan family have been generous and generous, and their disciples and former subordinates are all over the world. Once you recruit heroes, gather soldiers, and heroes rise, I am afraid that Taihang Shandong will no longer belong to you.
It is better to pardon Yuan Shao and make him a county guard. Yuan Shao will be happy to see that he is exempted from guilt, and there will be no disaster.
Dong Zhuo thought it was reasonable, so he sent someone to grant Yuan Shao the position of governor of Bohai and named him Marquis of Yunxiang.
In name, Yuan Shao also served as Sili Xiaowei.
In the first year of Chuping, Yuan Shao finally raised troops in Bohai. He and his cousin General Yuan Shu, Jizhou Mu Han Fu, Yuzhou Governor Kong Dian, Yanzhou Governor Liu Dai, Chenliu Governor Zhang Miao, Guangling Governor The governor Zhang Chao, the governor of Hanoi Wang Kuang, the governor of Shanyang Yuan Qian, the governor of Dongjun Qiao Mao, the prime minister of Jibei Bao Xin and others raised troops at the same time, with tens of thousands of troops each, under the banner of crusade against Dong Zhuo.
Yuan Shao and Wang Kuang were stationed in Hanoi, Kong Dian was stationed in Yingchuan, Han Fu was stationed in Ye County, and other armies were stationed in Suanzao, and they agreed to form an alliance, nominally recommending Yuan Shao as the leader of the alliance.
Yuan Shao claimed to be a general of chariots and cavalry, and was the commander of the Sili school.
When Dong Zhuo learned that Yuan Shao had raised troops in Shandong, he killed Yuan Shao's uncle Yuan Wei and all the Yuan clan in the capital.
Dong Zhuo then sent Da Honglu Han Rong, Shaofu Yin Xun, Zhi Jin Wu Hu Muban, General Wu Xun, the great craftsman, and Yue Qi Xiaowei Wang Quan to advise Yuan Shao and other armies.
Yuan Shao assigned Wang Kuang to kill Hu Muban, Wang Quan, Wu Xun and others. Yuan Shu also hunted and killed Yin Xun, but Han Rong was spared because of his high moral character and prestige.
When he was dispatched, most of the heroes joined Yuan Shao, and because his family was moved by the suffering, everyone wanted to avenge him, so troops from all prefectures and counties swarmed up, all under the banner of the Yuan family.
When Han Fu saw that people were turning to Yuan Shao, he was jealous of Yuan Shao's support and was afraid that he would use it against him. He often sent officers to guard Yuan Shao's gates to prevent him from sending troops.
Qiao Mao then pretended to be the Third Duke and sent documents to the prefectures and counties through the post, telling Dong Zhuo's crimes. The emperor was threatened and was in danger. He stood on tiptoe and hoped that the volunteers would eliminate the national disaster.
Han Fu then agreed with Yuan Shao to send troops.
Then Han Fu discussed with everyone and said: Are you helping the Yuan family?
Or help Dong?
During the war, Liu Hui said angrily: "The troops are sent for the sake of the country, so why should we take care of the Yuan family and the Dong family?"
However, Han Fu was still suspicious of Yuan Shao and often reduced military rations in an attempt to shake the morale of the army.
The next year, Han Fu's general Qu Yi rebelled. Han Fu fought with Qu Yi and lost.
Since Yuan Shao resented Han Fu, he befriended Qu Yi.
Yuan Shao's guests said to Yuan Shao at the right time: If you do a big business and don't occupy a state, you won't be able to gain a foothold.
summary: In the first year of Chuping, Yuan Shao raised troops in Bohai, joining forces with Yuan Shu, Han Fu, and others to crusade against Dong Zhuo. They formed an alliance with Yuan Shao as leader. Dong Zhuo killed Yuan Shao's uncle and clan members in the capital. Yuan Shao then took control of Jizhou from Han Fu through a combination of military pressure and persuasion, becoming its governor. He appointed Ju Shou as his advisor and expanded his territory.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上

translation:
Yuan Shao took off his helmet and threw it to the ground, saying: "A real man should go forward and die in battle, why do you run into the wall and wrap your face instead?"
He urged the archers to shoot arrows and injured many of Gongsun Zan's cavalry.
Gongsun Zan's men didn't know it was Yuan Shao, so many of them gradually retreated.
Just as Qu Yi came to greet Yuan Shao, Gongsun Zan's cavalry retreated.
Three years later, Gongsun Zan sent troops to challenge Longcuo again, and Yuan Shao defeated Gongsun Zan again.
Gongsun Zan then returned to Youzhou and did not dare to come out again.
At the beginning of the fourth year, the emperor sent his servant Zhao Qi to mediate the Kanto troops and asked them to stop their troops.
Gongsun Zan took this opportunity to write a letter to Yuan Shao, saying: The servant has the virtue and prestige of Zhou Gong and Shao Gong. He has been commissioned to come quickly to spread the grace of the imperial court. He wants us to live in harmony and be as bright as the sun after setting aside the dark clouds. What could be more gratifying than this?
In the past, Jia Fu and Kou Xun were quarreling to harm each other. When Shizu mediated the dispute, they finally came out in the same car. After the rift and hatred were eliminated, people at that time praised them.
I consider that I am a remote and humble person, and I can be friendly with the general. This is indeed humiliating to the general, but it is my wish.
Yuan Shao led his army back south.
On the first day of March, Yuan Shao gathered his guests and subordinates at Boluojin.
When they learned that the soldiers of Wei County had rebelled and that they, together with the Black Mountain bandit Kou Yudu and tens of thousands of others, captured Ye City and killed the county guard, all the guests who lived in Ye County were worried and frightened. Some stood up and cried. However, Yuan Shao's face did not change, as if nothing had happened, and he did not lose his usual demeanor.
There was a thief named Tao Sheng, who called himself "General Pinghan" and rebelled against other thieves alone. He led his troops over the city wall from the west and entered the city, sealed off the county government, loaded the baggage into the car, and used the car to personally escort Yuan Shao's family and the families of other officials who lived in Jizhou City to Cuiqiu.
After Yuan Shao returned, he stationed himself at Cuiqiu and appointed Tao Sheng as the general of Jianyi Zhonglang.
In June, Yuan Shao then sent troops into the entrance of Cangyan Valley in Luchang Mountain, Chaoge, to attack Yu Du.
After a five-day siege, Yu Du was defeated and more than 10,000 Yu Du and his followers were killed.
Then Yuan Shao went north along Luchang Mountain to attack Zuo Zhuozhangba and other thieves, and wiped them all out. He also attacked Liu Shi, Qing Niujiao, Huang Long, Zuo Xiao, Guo Daxian, Li Damu, Yu Digen and others, killing tens of thousands again and destroying all their fortresses.
Then he fought with Zhang Yan, the Black Mountain bandit, the fourth battalion of the Xiongnu Tu various tribes, and Wuhuan of Yanmen in Changshan.
Zhang Yan had tens of thousands of elite soldiers and thousands of cavalry. The two sides fought continuously for more than ten days. Although Zhang Yan's army suffered many casualties, Yuan Shao's army was also exhausted, so they retreated.
Qu Yi relied on his military exploits, pride and indulgence, and disobedience to the law. Yuan Shao summoned him, killed him, and merged his troops.
In the second year of Xingping, the emperor appointed Yuan Shao as the right general.
In the winter of this year, the emperor was pursued by Li Ji and others in Caoyang. Jushou persuaded Yuan Shao: "The general has served as the prime minister of the court for generations, and has assisted the country with loyalty throughout the ages."
summary: Yuan Shao defeated Gongsun Zan in battle, killing Yan Gang and pursuing him to the boundary bridge. Despite a near-capture by Gongsun Zan's cavalry, Yuan Shao's forces prevailed. He later suppressed rebellions in Wei County and defeated the Black Mountain bandits, killing tens of thousands. Yuan Shao also killed his general Qu Yi for insubordination.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上

translation:
Now the emperor is wandering around and the ancestral temple is destroyed, but if you look at the states and counties, although they appear to be volunteers on the outside, they are actually thinking about each other in their hearts, and they have no worries about the country and the interests of the people.
Moreover, the city of Jizhou was generally pacified, the army was strong, and the scholars returned, went west to meet the emperor, used Ye County as the imperial palace, held the emperor hostage and ordered the princes, raised troops and horses to attack those who did not worship the royal court, who could resist?
Yuan Shao was ready to follow Ju Shou's plan.
The wise men Guo Tu and Chunyu Qiong said: The royal family of the Han Dynasty declined for a long time. Isn’t it too difficult to revitalize the royal family now?
Besides, heroes rise up at the same time, occupy states and counties separately, and unite to gather followers, often tens of thousands of them. This is just like the Qin Dynasty who lost the throne and the person who got it first became the emperor.
Now that the emperor has been brought in, he has to write to the emperor at every turn. If you obey, you will have too little power. If you don't obey, you will be disobeying the emperor's order. This is not a good approach.
Jushu said: It is morally reasonable and the timing is appropriate to bring the emperor in now.
If you don't decide early, someone else will be there to greet you first.
Don't lose the opportunity to make a contingency, and don't be too quick to succeed. I hope you will consider it.
The emperor's ascension was not in line with Yuan Shao's wishes, so Yuan Shao did not accept it.
Yuan Shao had three sons: Shei Tan, whose courtesy name was Xiansi, Yuan Xi, whose courtesy name was Xian Yong, and Yuan Shang, whose courtesy name was Xianfu.
Yuan Tan is older and wiser, while Yuan Shang is younger but more beautiful.
Sai Niu's step-wife type overwhelms Zhi Cheng and dotes on her. She prefers Tong Yao and praises him many times in front of Zhi Cheng. Sai Niu is also amazed by Zhi Cheng's appearance and wants him to succeed him.
So Yuan Shao adopted Yuan Tan as his brother's descendant and sent him to be the governor of Qingzhou.
Jushou dissuaded him and said: "It has always been said that if ten thousand people chase a rabbit, one person will get the rabbit, and all the others who want to get it will give up. This is because their status has been determined."
Besides, if they are similar in age, it depends on who is talented and virtuous, and if they are similar in moral character, it depends on the results of divination. This is an ancient system.
I hope you will consider the warnings of the successes and failures of previous generations on a large scale, and consider the principles of chasing rabbits and determining one's status on a small scale.
If you don't change it, this is where the disaster begins.
Yuan Shao said: I want the children to govern a state each so that their talents can be seen.
So: Chu appointed his second son Zhisai as the governor of Youye, and his nephew Zhibi as the governor of Bingzhou.
In the first year of Jian'an, Cao Cao welcomed the emperor and established his capital in Xu County. He then issued an edict to Yuan Shao, blaming him for having a vast land and a large army, and for always forming cliques for himself. He had never heard of sending troops to rescue the emperor, but he attacked others without permission.
summary: When Emperor Xian was in danger, Ju Shou advised Yuan Shao to welcome the emperor, but Yuan Shao hesitated due to advice from Guo Tu and Chunyu Qiong. He eventually declined. Yuan Shao had three sons: Yuan Tan, Yuan Xi, and Yuan Shang. He favored Yuan Shang due to his wife's influence, adopting Yuan Tan as his brother's heir and sending him to Qingzhou, against Ju Shou's warnings.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上

translation:
The minister's title is Chehou, and his salary is two thousand dan.
I have already been greedy for special favors and rich reputation. Do you dare to covet the court's gifts and hope to get Tong Gong's orders?
It really hurts that the hard work of the general and colonel was not recorded, and it turned out to be a great sin to be loyal to the country.
This is the reason why Meng Tian cried bitterly in the border prison and Bai Qi lamented and shed tears in Du You.
Taifu Ma Ribei was the official guardian and was responsible for the Eastern Expedition. However, he disrupted the emperor's mission. The people he favored and appointed were all unqualified. All the people he selected and appointed were abandoned by everyone.
However, he adopted the strategies of these people and used them as his masterminds, turning his brothers and sisters into enemies, causing swordsmen to fight against each other, and the disasters caused became more and more serious.
Although I want to take off my armor and throw away my spear, the matter cannot end.
I am indeed worried that your majesty’s radiance, which is as bright as the sun and the moon, may not shine in some places; your majesty’s ears may hear the clear observations from all directions, but there may be situations where you cannot hear them. I request your majesty to send the memorial to the ministers, ask all the wise ministers about the situation, and let the three ministers and nine ministers discuss the crimes committed by the ministers.
If it were regarded as a crime for ministers to change their authority, then Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin should be sentenced to death; if it was regarded as virtuous that everyone did not attack the bandits, then there would be no need to write the derogatory word "regicide" on the shield.
Although I am an ordinary person, I am determined to maintain integrity.
If you can make your ministers express their sincerity and be worthy of the late emperor, then even if they lower their heads to use the torture knife or lift their clothes to use the soup pot, they will be willing to do so.
Your Majesty, please pay attention to the meaning of equality in "Corpse Dove", avoid flattery remarks, and do not make your ministers resentful.
So the imperial court appointed Yuan Shao as Taiwei and granted him the title of Marquis of Ye.
At that time, Cao Cao himself served as the general. Yuan Shao felt ashamed of being under Cao Cao and deliberately wrote a letter of resignation to the emperor and refused to accept it.
Cao Cao was very scared and gave up the position of general to Yuan Shao.
In the second year of Jian'an, the emperor sent the great craftsman Kong Rong to hold the emperor's talisman to grant Yuan Shao the position of general. He also gave him bows and arrows, talismans, axes and irons, and a hundred tigers and swords. He was asked to take charge of the four states of Jizhou, Qingzhou, Youzhou and Bingzhou. Yuan Shao accepted the appointment.
Every time Yuan Shao received an imperial edict, he was always worried that it would be detrimental to him, so he wanted the emperor to move closer to him. He sent people to tell Cao Cao that Xu County was low-lying and humid, and Luoyang was incomplete and ruined. The capital should be moved to Zhencheng to be close to a complete and abundant area.
Cao Cao refused.
Tian Feng said to Yuan Shao: Since the strategy of moving the capital has not been adopted, it is best to seize Xu County as soon as possible, bring the emperor over, and often issue orders to the whole country under the pretense of the emperor Shao Ling. This is the best way.
If you don't do this, you will eventually be controlled by others, and then even regret will have no effect.
Yuan Shao did not adopt it.
summary: In the first year of Jian'an, Cao Cao welcomed the emperor to Xu County and blamed Yuan Shao for not aiding the emperor. Yuan Shao responded with a lengthy letter defending his actions, citing his loyalty and efforts against Dong Zhuo and others. The court appointed him Taiwei and Marquis of Ye, but he refused until Cao Cao yielded the position of General. Later, he was granted command of four provinces.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上

translation:
In the spring of the fourth year, Yuan Shao attacked Gongsun Zan and pacified the Youzhou area. The incident is recorded in "The Biography of Gongsun Zan".
Since Yuan Shao annexed the territory of four states and had hundreds of thousands of troops, his pride became strong, and the tribute to the emperor was sparse and simple.
Geng Bao, the chief registrar, secretly wrote to Yuan Shao, saying: The Red Virtue of the Han Dynasty is about to decline. The Yuan family is the descendant of Yu Shun and Huang De, and they should comply with the will of God and the wishes of the people.
Yuan Shao showed Geng Bao's petition to his staff. Everyone believed that Geng Bao was deceitful and should be beheaded.
Yuan Shao knew that everyone disagreed, so he had no choice but to kill Geng Bao to cover up his feelings.
So Yuan Shao selected 100,000 elite soldiers and 10,000 cavalry to attack Xu County. He was responsible for supervising military affairs and observing discipline. Tian Feng, Xun Chen and Xu You from Nanyang were the main advisers, and Yan Liang and Wen Chou were the generals.
Jushou stepped forward and said: "The recent attack on Gongsun Zan lasted for a year. The people are exhausted and impoverished, there is no surplus in the warehouses, and there are too many taxes and labor. This is a matter of great concern to the country."
It is best to send envoys to present prisoners and spoils of war to the emperor first, and devote themselves to farming so that the troops and horses can rest.
If I can't reach the Emperor, I will report that Cao Cao has blocked my path to the Emperor, and then I will march troops to garrison Liyang, and gradually develop operations south of the Yellow River, build more ships, renovate equipment, dispatch excellent cavalry, and plunder the opponent's border areas, so that they will not have peace, but I will have peace of mind.
In this way, you can sit back and control the world.
Guo Tu and Shen Pei said: The method in the military book is to surround the enemy when the enemy is ten times more numerous, attack the enemy when the enemy is five times more numerous, and engage in battle when the strength is equal.
At present, with the help of Ming Gong's divine power and the powerful army in Heshuo area, it is easy to defeat Cao Cao.
If we don't capture it in time now, it will be difficult to deal with it in the future.
Jushu said: An army that eliminates chaos and violence is a moral army; an army that relies on large numbers and strength is called a proud army.
The army of benevolence and righteousness has no rival, but the army of pride will perish first.
Cao Cao supported and welcomed the emperor and built a palace in Xudu.
Now mobilizing all the troops to attack Cao Cao in the south would be contrary to righteousness.
Moreover, defeating the enemy depends on strategy, not strength. Cao Cao's decree has been implemented, and the soldiers are strong and capable, not the kind of people like Gongsun Zan who are waiting to be surrounded.
Now that you are abandoning perfectly safe strategies and launching armies without justifiable reasons, I am secretly afraid for you.
Guo Tu and others said: It is not unjust for King Wu of Zhou to attack Shang Zhou; besides, sending troops to attack Cao Cao is afraid that there will be no reason!
Besides, the lord's troops are strong and brave, and the generals and soldiers are all thinking of working hard. If you don't seize the opportunity to decide the great cause early, it will become what people say, God gives you a gift but does not take it, but you will be condemned by God. This is the reason why the Yue Kingdom dominates and the Wu Kingdom is destroyed.
The method of supervising the army lies in adhering to stability, rather than using expedient measures to seize opportunities according to the situation.
summary: Yuan Shao attacked Gongsun Zan again, pacifying Youzhou. With control of four provinces and hundreds of thousands of troops, he grew arrogant. He planned to attack Xu County, ignoring Ju Shou's advice to rest and farm. Instead, he followed Guo Tu and Shen Pei's counsel to attack immediately. Tian Feng's warnings led to his imprisonment.

translation:
Ju Shou also advised Yuan Shao: Although the northern army has more people, it is not as strong and decisive as the southern army; the southern army has less food and its reserves are not as good as the northern army.
The Southern Army wanted a quick victory, while the Northern Army had the advantage of advancing slowly.
It is best to use a slow and long-lasting method to delay time.
Yuan Shao didn't listen.
Yuan Shao connected the camps and gradually advanced, slowly approaching Guandu. The two sides fought. As a result, Cao's army was defeated and retreated to the camp to hold on.
Yuan Shao built a tall watchtower and piled it into a mountain of earth, and fired arrows at Cao Cao's camp. The soldiers in the camp walked with shields on their heads.
So Cao Cao used a stone chariot to fire stones and destroyed all Yuan Shao's watchtowers. The soldiers in the army called them "Thunderbolt Chariots".
Yuan Shao dug tunnels to attack Cao Cao. Cao Cao immediately dug a long trench in the camp to stop Yuan Shao, and sent a surprise attack on Yuan's army's grain truck, burning all the grain.
The two sides fought for more than a hundred days, and the people south of the Yellow River were exhausted. Many people betrayed Cao Cao and joined Yuan Shao.
Yuan Shao sent Chunyu Qiong and others to lead more than 10,000 soldiers north to meet the troops transporting grain.
Jushu persuaded Yuan Shao to send Jiang Qi to lead another army as foreign aid to cut off Cao Cao's looting.
Yuan Shao disagreed.
Xu You offered advice and said: Cao Cao has few soldiers and all his troops are used to resist our army. The remaining defense force in Xu County must be empty and weak.
If another lightly-armed force is sent to attack day and night and capture Xu County, Cao Cao will naturally be captured.
Even if Cao Cao's army is not defeated, they can be forced to run from both ends and they will definitely defeat Cao Cao.
Yuan Shao couldn't accept it.
It happened that someone in Xu You's family broke the law and was imprisoned. Xu You felt frustrated, so he defected to Cao Cao and suggested that Cao Cao sneak attack Chunyu Qiong and others.
Chunyu Qiong and others were staying overnight at the Bird's Nest, which was forty miles away from Yuan Shao's troops.
Cao Cao personally led five thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Chunyu Qiong and others overnight and wiped them out.
Yuan Shao first learned that Cao Cao was attacking Chunyu Qiong, and said to his eldest son Yuan Tan: Even if Cao Cao defeats Chun Yuqiong and I capture Cao Cao's military camp, he will definitely have nowhere to return.
So he sent Gao Lan, Zhang He and others to attack Cao Cao's camp, but they couldn't capture it.
When the second general heard that Chunyu Qiong and others were defeated, he defected to Cao Cao.
At this time, Yuan Shao's army panicked and was completely defeated.
Yuan Shao, Yuan Tan and others, wearing turbans and riding horses, crossed the Yellow River with 800 cavalry, arrived at Liyang on the north bank, and entered the military camp of their general Jiang Yiqu.
When they arrived at Jiang Yiqu's tent, Yuan Shao took his hand and said, "I entrust my life to you."
Yiqu gave up his camp to Yuan Shao and asked him to issue orders.
Yuan Shao's tribe heard that Yuan Shao was alive, and gradually gathered together again.
The remaining tribesmen pretended to surrender, and Cao Cao buried them all alive. Eighty thousand people were killed one after another.
Jushou was captured by Cao Cao's army. He shouted loudly: I will not surrender, I am just captured.
Cao Cao saw Jushu and said to him: "We are not in the same place, so we are isolated from each other. I didn't expect to get you today."
summary: In the fifth year of Jian'an, Yuan Shao marched south after Liu Bei's defection. He issued a proclamation condemning Cao Cao's crimes. His forces initially succeeded but were defeated at Guandu after Xu You defected and revealed the location of Yuan Shao's grain supplies at Wuchao. Cao Cao attacked and destroyed the supplies, leading to Yuan Shao's defeat. Yuan Shao fled with 800 cavalry, while many of his troops were killed or surrendered. Ju Shou was captured and executed after attempting to return to Yuan Shao.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/袁绍刘表列传上

translation:
Jushu replied: Yuan Jizhou made a mistake in his strategy and caused his own defeat.
My intelligence and ability are limited, so I was naturally caught.
Cao Cao said: Yuan Benchu ​​has no strategy and cannot adopt your strategy.
Now the country has been in chaos for more than 12 years, and it still cannot be pacified. We are preparing to work with you to find a solution.
Jushu said: The lives of my uncle, mother, and brother hang in Yuan's hands. If you please allow me to die quickly, it will be my blessing.
Cao Cao sighed and said: If I had gotten you earlier, the world wouldn't have cared enough about you.
So he pardoned Ju and treated him favorably.
Soon Jushu tried to return to the Yuan family, and Cao Cao killed him.
Yuan Shao appears to be generous, elegant and considerate, and does not show sorrow or joy on his face. However, he is proud and arrogant by nature and cannot listen to correct opinions, which leads to failure.
When Yuan Shao's army returned, someone said to Tian Feng: You will definitely be used in important ways.
Tian Feng said: Mr. Yuan is generous on the surface but jealous in his heart. He does not believe in my loyalty, and I have offended him many times by telling the truth.
If he wins, he will definitely forgive me when he is happy; if he loses the battle, he will be resentful and jealous in his heart.
If I had been victorious, I would have been saved. Now that I have been defeated, I have no hope of surviving.
After Yuan Shao came back, he said: I didn't adopt Tian Feng's advice, and he really laughed at me.
So Tian Feng was killed.
Guan Du was defeated and Shen Pei's two sons were captured alive by Cao Cao. Meng Dai had a conflict with Shenpei, so he told Yuan Shao through Jiang Qi: Shenpei has monopolized power in office, has a large clan, strong military strength, and his two sons are in the south. He must want to rebel.
Guo Tu and Xin Ping also thought so.
Yuan Shao then appointed Meng Dai as the supervisor of the army to guard Ye County instead of Shen Pei.
The guard Feng Ji and his colleagues tried to find out whether they were in harmony with each other. Yuan Shao asked Feng Ji about the incident. Feng Ji replied: "Shen Pei is strong and straightforward by nature. Every time he says something or does something, he admires the integrity of the ancients. He will not do anything unjust because his two sons are in the south. Don't doubt him."
Yuan Shao said: Don't you hate him?
Feng Ji said: In the past, the disputes were personal matters, but now we are talking about national affairs.
Yuan Shao said: That's so right.
So the judge was not dismissed. Since then, the relationship between Shen Pei and Feng Ji has become more harmonious.
Many cities in Jizhou rebelled against Yuan Shao, and Yuan Shao was busy attacking and pacifying these cities.
Yuan Shao became ill after his defeat. In the summer of the seventh year of Jian'an, Yuan Shao died.
Yuan Shao had not had time to determine his successor. Fengji and Shenpei had always disgusted Yuan Tan because of their pride and luxury. Xin Ping and Guo Tu were both close to Yuan Tan and had conflicts with Shenpei and Fengji.
Everyone thinks that Yuan Tan is older and wants to establish Yuan Tan.
Shen Pei and others were afraid that Xin Ping and others would harm them after Yuan Tan came to the throne, so they pretended to be sent by Yuan Shao and supported Yuan Shang as their successor.
summary: Yuan Shao appeared generous but was proud and unable to accept advice, leading to his downfall. After his defeat, he killed Tian Feng. He fell ill and died in the seventh year of Jian'an. His succession was disputed: Shen Pei and Feng Ji supported Yuan Shang, while others favored Yuan Tan, leading to internal conflict.

translation:
Liu Biao, courtesy name Jingsheng, was born in Gaoping, Shanyang, and was a descendant of King Lu Gong.
Liu Biao was more than eight feet tall, with a gentle appearance and a burly build.
Together with Zhang Jian and others from the same county, he was slandered and discussed as "Ba Gu". The emperor issued an edict to arrest the party members and punish them, but Liu Biao escaped without being caught.
After the party ban was lifted, Liu Biao was summoned by General He Jin as an assistant.
In the first year of Chuping, Sun Jian, the governor of Changsha, killed Wang Xu, the governor of Jingzhou, and issued an edict appointing Liu Biao as the governor of Jingzhou.
At that time, there were many bandits of the same clan in the south of the Yangtze River, and Yuan Shu's troops were stationed in Luyang to block the road. Liu Biao could not reach Jingzhou, so he rode into Yicheng alone and invited Kuai Yue from Nanjun and Cai Mao from Xiangyang to discuss countermeasures.
Liu Biao said to Kuai Yue: Although there are many thieves in the same clan, no one will join them. If Yuan Jie takes advantage of them, disaster will inevitably come.
I want to recruit troops, but I'm worried that I can't combine them. What strategy should I use?
Kuai Yue replied: When governing peace, benevolence and righteousness should be the first priority; when governing war, the first priority should be to use contingency strategies.
The army does not have a large number of people, the important thing is to get the right talents.
Yuan Shu was proud and had no strategy, and most of the thieves gathered from his own clan were greedy and cruel.
Among them are people who I usually support. If I send someone to tell them the benefits, they will definitely lead their troops over.
You kill the cruel ones among them and appoint the talented ones among them. Once your prestige and kindness are established, people will come to you carrying their children in swaddling clothes.
The soldiers gathered and the people surrendered. Jiangling was captured in the south and Xiangyang was defended in the north. The eight counties under Jingzhou's jurisdiction could be pacified with a single proclamation.
Even if Yuan Gongli arrives, there is nothing he can do.
Liu Biao said: Yes.
So he asked Kuai Yue to send people to lure the leaders of thieves from his own tribe. Fifteen people came, killed them all and captured their tribes by surprise.
Only when the Jiangxia thieves Zhang Hu and Chen Li gathered their troops to occupy Xiangyang City, and Liu Biao sent Kuai Yue and Pang Ji to inform them, did they surrender.
Everything south of the Yangtze River was pacified.
Many prefects and county magistrates heard about Liu Biao's reputation, and many of them took off their seals and ribbons and left.
Liu Hu then organized his troops in the fortress area to observe changes in the current situation.
There was a gap between Yuan Shu and his cousin Yuan Shao, and Yuan Shao was friends with Liu Biao, so Yuan Shu and Sun Jian jointly attacked Liu Biao from the north and south.
Liu Biao was defeated, and Sun Jian then surrounded Xiangyang.
Just as Liu Biao's general Huang Zu came to rescue him, Sun Jian was shot by a stray arrow and died, and the rest of the people retreated.
When Li Cui and others entered Chang'an, in winter, Liu Biao sent envoys to pay tribute to the emperor.
Li Ji appointed Liu Biao as the General of Zhennan and the Shepherd of Jingzhou, and made him a Marquis of Wu, holding the Emperor's Talisman as his aid.
In the first year of Jian'an, the hussar general Zhang Ji fled from Guanzhong to Nanyang, attacked Lucheng along the way, and was shot to death by a flying arrow.
summary: Liu Biao, courtesy name Jingsheng, was a descendant of King Lu Gong from Gaoping, Shanyang. Over eight feet tall with a gentle appearance and burly build, he was implicated in the "Ba Gu" party affair and escaped arrest. After the party ban was lifted, he served as an assistant to General He Jin. In the first year of Chuping, he was appointed Governor of Jingzhou following Sun Jian's murder of Governor Wang Xu. Unable to reach Jingzhou due to bandits and Yuan Shu's troops blocking the road, Liu Biao rode alone to Yicheng and consulted Kuai Yue and Cai Mao. Following Kuai Yue's advice, he lured and killed fifteen clan bandit leaders, then pacified their tribes. The Jiangxia thieves Zhang Hu and Chen Li surrendered after negotiations, and the region south of the Yangtze River was subdued. Liu Biao organized troops to observe the situation. Yuan Shu and Sun Jian attacked Liu Biao, but Sun Jian was killed by a stray arrow during the siege of Xiangyang. Liu Biao sent tribute to Emperor Xian and was appointed General of Zhennan, Shepherd of Jingzhou, and Marquis of Wu. When Zhang Ji attacked Lucheng and was killed, Liu Biao accepted condolences and recruited Zhang Ji's troops. He suppressed rebellions by Zhang Xian and others, expanding his territory to connect with Wuling in the south and Han in the north, commanding over 100,000 armored warriors. Liu Biao pacified bandits, supported scholars, established schools, and commissioned commentaries on the Five Classics.
