translation:
Liu Biao thought that he was afraid of sending an envoy and forced him to go.
After arriving in Xu County, the emperor appointed Han Song as his minister and prefect of Lingling.
After returning, Han Song strongly praised the kindness of the emperor and Cao Cao, and persuaded Liu Biao to send his son to serve.
Liu Biao was furious, thinking that Han Song had double-minded intentions, so he displayed his troops, insulted Han Song, and prepared to kill him.
Han Song's expression remained unchanged as he slowly recounted what he had said before leaving.
Liu Biao's wife Cai knew Han Song's virtues and dissuaded Liu Biao.
Liu Biao was still furious, so he tortured and killed Han Song's entourage.
Liu Biao learned that Han Song had no other intention but to imprison him.
In the sixth year, Liu Bei came from Yuan Shao and defected to Jingzhou. Liu Biao treated Liu Bei favorably and made friends with him, but he could not use him.
In the thirteenth year, Cao Cao personally led an army to conquer Liu Biao but did not reach Jingzhou.
In August, Liu Biao died of malignant sores on his back.
Liu Biao had been in Jingzhou for nearly twenty years, and his family had no extra savings.
Liu Biao had two sons: Liu Qi and Liu Cong.
At first, Liu Biao thought Liu Qi looked like him and liked him very much. Later, he married Liu Cong's niece, Cai's niece. Cai then liked Liu Cong and hated Liu Qi. Liu Biao heard words slandering Liu Qi and praising Liu Cong every day.
Liu Biao loved his second wife deeply, so he believed and accepted these words every time.
In addition, Liu Biao's brother-in-law Cai Mao and nephew Zhang Yun were both placed in important positions by Liu Biao, and they were also close friends with Liu Cong.
Liu Qi felt that he was not safe and once discussed with Zhuge Liang, a man from Langxie, how to protect himself.
Zhuge Liang didn't answer at first.
Later, the two climbed up the tall building together, and then Liu Qi asked someone to take away the ladder. He said to Zhuge Liang: Today, the sky can't be seen from the top, and the ground can't be seen from the bottom. The words that came out of your mouth reached my ears. Can you speak?
Zhuge Liang said: "Don't you see that Shen Sheng is in danger at home and Chong'er is safe when he lives abroad?"
Liu Qi realized in his heart and secretly planned a way out. It happened that Huang Zu, the governor of Jiangxia under Liu Biao, was killed by Sun Quan, so Liu Qi asked to take over the position.
When Liu Biao was seriously ill, Liu Qi came back to visit him. Because Liu Qi was kind and filial by nature, Zhang Yun and others were afraid that they would have a father-son relationship after seeing Liu Biao. Liu Biao once again wanted to let him succeed, so he said to Liu Qi: The general has ordered you to govern Jiangxia. This responsibility is of great importance.
If you leave your subordinates and come here without permission, you will definitely be scolded.
It is not filial piety to ruin your father's interest and aggravate his illness.
So he blocked the door and prevented him from seeing Liu Biao.
Liu Qi left in tears, and many people sighed after hearing this.
In this way, Liu Cong succeeded to the throne.
Liu Cong awarded Liu Qi the seal of the feudal lords. Liu Qi became angry and threw the seal to the ground, preparing to take advantage of the funeral to make trouble.
Just as Cao Cao's army arrived in Xinye, Liu Qi fled to the south of the Yangtze River.
Kuai Yue, Han Song and Dong Cao's Fu Xun persuaded Liu Cong to surrender to Cao Cao.
Liu Cong said: Now that I have the entire territory of Chu State with you, I can preserve the career of the late emperor and use it to observe the situation in the world. Why not?
summary: During Cao Cao and Yuan Shao's conflict at Guandu, Liu Biao remained neutral despite advice from Han Song and Kuai Yue to submit to Cao Cao. He sent Han Song to observe Cao Cao, but after Han Song praised Cao Cao and urged submission, Liu Biao imprisoned him. Liu Bei defected to Jingzhou in the sixth year of Jian'an, but Liu Biao did not utilize him. In the thirteenth year, Cao Cao marched south, and Liu Biao died of illness in August after nearly twenty years in Jingzhou. Liu Biao favored his son Liu Qi initially but later favored Liu Cong due to his wife Cai's influence. Liu Qi, feeling unsafe, sought advice from Zhuge Liang and requested to govern Jiangxia. When Liu Biao fell ill, Liu Qi was prevented from visiting him, and Liu Cong succeeded. Liu Cong surrendered Jingzhou to Cao Cao, who appointed him Governor of Qingzhou and granted marquisates to others. Cao Cao later released Han Song and appointed him Da Honglu. Liu Biao's alliance with Yuan Shao was criticized by Deng Yi, who resigned. Cao Cao was defeated at Chibi, and Liu Bei recommended Liu Qi as Jingzhou's historian; Liu Qi died the following year. The text concludes that Liu Biao's indecision and favoritism led to his downfall.

translation:
Xiqiang originally came from Sanmiao, another branch of the Jiang surname.
The Western Qiang Kingdom is close to Nanyue.
When Shun exiled four stubborn people, he exiled them to Sanwei, which is the Qiang area southwest of Heguan. This area is wrapped around the Cizhi River and stretches for thousands of miles to the head of Cizhi River.
The gift branch is the analysis branch mentioned in "Yu Gong".
This area borders the barbarians outside the borders of Shu and Han to the south, and borders Shanshan, Cheshi and other countries to the northwest.
The Xiqiang people do not have fixed residences. They migrate with water and grass.
Grains are rarely grown on this land, and they mainly rely on livestock raising.
The custom of Xiqiang is that clans are not fixed. Some clans use the father's name and the mother's surname as the title of their tribe.
After the twelfth generation, clans intermarry with each other. After the father dies, he marries his stepmother, and after his elder brother dies, he marries his widower. Therefore, there are no widowers or widows in the Xiqiang country, and the population reproduces quickly.
Xiqiang does not have a king or ministers, and no one is its leader. If the power is strong, they will separate into races and become chiefs. If the power is weak, they will become subordinate tribes of others. They plundered and invaded each other, ruling the roost with violence.
Kill for life, there is no other prohibition.
The soldiers of Xiqiang are good at fighting in the valleys, but not on the plains; they cannot fight for a long time, but they dare to charge into battle; they regard death in battle as auspicious, while death from illness is considered unlucky.
The Xiqiang people can endure cold and hardship just like animals.
Even when women give birth to children, they do not hide from the wind and snow.
The Xiqiang people are strong and brave in fighting for the land, and they have accepted the energy of the metal element in the five elements and the west.
If the emperor's government is clear and clear, the barbarians will surrender; if the emperor loses virtue and education, the barbarians will invade and cause chaos.
In the past, Taikang, the king of the Xia Dynasty, lost the world and all the barbarians rebelled.
When the later prime minister came to the throne, he conquered the Yiyi. Seven years later, the Yiyi came to submit.
After Houxie, the title of nobility was added to Ruyi, and Ruyi obeyed the Xia Dynasty from then on.
When Hou Jie was in turmoil, the Yi people came to live in the Linqi area. After the rise of Chengtang, he conquered the Yiyi and made them retreat.
When the Yin Dynasty weakened in the middle period, all barbarians rebelled.
When Wuding arrived, he conquered Xirong and Guifang, and it took three years to conquer them.
So the poem says: Since the time of Di Qiang, no one has dared not to come to pay homage to the Emperor.
When Wu Yi was brutal and cruel, and the dog soldiers invaded the border, Zhou Gugong Yi's father crossed Liangshan and took refuge at the foot of Qishan Mountain.
At the time of his son Ji Li, he conquered the Xiluo Guirong.
During the reign of Taiding, Ji Li attacked the Rong tribe in Yanjing, and the Rong tribe defeated Zhou's army.
Two years later, when Zhou's troops defeated Yu Wu's Rong tribe, Taiding appointed Ji Li as priest.
From then on, Ji Li attacked the Rong tribe of Shihu and Yitu, and won both of them.
summary: The Xiqiang people, originally from Sanmiao, a branch of the Jiang surname, lived in a region near Nanyue, stretching from the Cizhi River to the borders of Shu and Han in the south and Shanshan and Cheshi in the northwest. They were nomadic, migrating with water and grass, relying primarily on livestock rather than grain. Their society lacked fixed clans, with tribes named after paternal or maternal lines. After twelve generations, intermarriage occurred, and customs included marrying stepmothers after a father's death and widows after an elder brother's death, leading to rapid population growth. They had no central ruler; power determined leadership, with violence and plunder common. Their soldiers excelled in valley combat but not on plains, valued death in battle over illness, and endured harsh conditions.

translation:
When King Wen was appointed as the Western Bodhisattva, there were Kun barbarians to the west of the Zhou Dynasty, and there were dangers to the north from the Ming dynasties. So King Wen repulsed the Rong and Di and garrisoned troops there, and all of the Rong and Di surrendered.
King Wen then commanded the Xirong and conquered the countries that had betrayed the Yin and Shang dynasties to serve King Zhou.
When King Wu attacked Shang, the Qiang people and Zhang Ren led their troops to meet in Muye.
At the time of King Mu, the Rongdi did not pay tribute to the Zhou Dynasty. King Mu then marched westward against the Quanrong, captured the five kings of the Quanrong, and obtained four white deer and four white wolves. King Mu then moved the Rong people to Taiyuan.
During the reign of King Yi, the Zhou Dynasty was weak and the Rong people from the outlying areas did not come to worship. The emperor ordered Duke Guo to lead a division of six armies to attack the Rong people in Taiyuan as far as Yuquan and obtained a thousand horses.
King Li was cruel, and the Rong and Di invaded and plundered. He even entered Quanqiu and killed Qin Zhong's family. The emperor ordered to conquer the Rong people, but they could not win.
In the fourth year after King Xuan succeeded to the throne, he sent Qin Zhong to attack the Rong people, but Qin Zhong was killed by the Rong people.
The emperor then summoned Duke Zhuang, son of Qin Zhong, and gave him seven thousand troops to conquer the Rong people. He defeated the Rong people, and the Rong people retreated slightly.
Twenty-seven years later, the emperor sent an army to attack the Rong people in Taiyuan, but could not win.
Five years later, the emperor conquered Tiao Rong and Ben Rong, and the emperor's army was defeated by the Rong people.
Two years later, the Jin people defeated the Beirong at Xiaxi by the Fen River. The Rong people also destroyed Jianghou's fiefdom.
The next year, the emperor conquered Shen Rong and defeated him.
Ten years later, King You ordered Bo Shi to conquer the Rong people in Liuji. As a result, the army was defeated and Bo Shi died there.
This year, the Rong people surrounded Quanqiu and captured Qin Xianggong's brother and uncle.
At that time, King You was fatuous and cruel, and barbarians from all directions invaded alternately. As a result, King You deposed Queen Shen and made Bao Si the queen.
The Marquis of Shen was angry, so he invaded the Zhou Dynasty with his troops and killed King You in Mount Li. Zhou then moved eastward to Luoyi, and Qin Xianggong attacked the Rong people to rescue the Zhou Dynasty.
Two years later, Xinghou defeated Beirong.
By the end of King Ping's reign, the Zhou Dynasty finally weakened. The Rong people are approaching the Central Plains, and there are Rong people everywhere from Longshan to the east to Yishui and Luoshui.
At this time, there were the armies of Di, Xi, Bang, and Ji in the upper reaches of the Wei River, the Rong of Yiqu in the north of the Jing River, the Rong of Dali in the Luo River, the Li Rong in the south bank of the Wei River, the Rong of Yang Ju and Quan Gao in the upper reaches of the Yishui River, and the Rong of Manshi in the west of the upper reaches of the Ying River.
During the Spring and Autumn Period, Rong people occasionally entered the Central Plains and participated in alliances with various Chinese countries.
Duke Zhuang of Lu attacked Qin and captured the state and the army of Ji.
More than ten years later, Jin lost Li Rong. At this time, Yi and Luo Zhirong became stronger and invaded Cao and Lu eastward. Nineteen years later, they finally entered the capital of the emperor. So Qin and Jin attacked the Rong people to rescue the emperor of Zhou.
Two years later, the Rong invaded the capital again. Duke Huan of Qi fine-tuned the troops of the princely states to garrison in Zhou.
Nine years later, Lu Hunrong moved from Guazhou to Yichuan, and Yunrong moved to the Weishui and Youshui areas, and he arrived in Nanyuan with his face tied.
Those south of the Yellow River and north of the mountains are called Yinrong, and the Yinrong race multiplies more and more.
Duke Wen of Jin wanted to establish his hegemony, so he bribed Rong Di and asked them to open a road to assist the emperor of Zhou.
Duke Mugong of Qin got the rest of the Rong people and finally dominated Xirong and opened up thousands of miles of land.
At the time of Duke Mourning of the Jin Dynasty, Wei Jiang was sent to make peace with the Rong and once again established his hegemony.
At this time, Chu and Jin were very powerful and used their power to make the Rong obey. Lu Hun, Yi, Luo, and Yin Rong served Jin, but the Man clan followed Chu.
Later, Lu Hun betrayed the Jin State, and the Jin State sent Xun Wu to eliminate Lu Hun.
summary: Historically, the Xiqiang's relationship with Chinese dynasties fluctuated. During the Xia Dynasty, Taikang's loss of control led to barbarian rebellion, but later rulers like Houxiang and Houxie subdued them. Under the Yin Dynasty, Wuding conquered Xirong and Guifang, but Wu Yi's brutality provoked Dog Soldier invasions. The Zhou Dynasty saw King Wen and King Wu command Xirong, while King Mu campaigned against Quanrong. As Zhou weakened, Rong tribes invaded, leading to conflicts with Qin and Jin. During the Spring and Autumn period, Rong groups like Yiqu and Dali grew powerful, building cities and claiming kingship. Qin gradually absorbed them, with King Zhao of Qin destroying Yiqu in the 4th century BCE.

translation:
Ten years later, the chiefs of Xianling colluded with the Qiang people of other tribes and invaded Jincheng and Longxi again. The imperial court sent Zhonglang Lai She and others to attack the invading Qiang people, and defeated the Qiang people. The incident has been recorded in the "Biography of Lai She".
In the summer of the eleventh year, Xian Lingzhong invaded Lintao again. Ma Yuan, the prefect of Longxi, defeated Xian Lingzhong and made them surrender.
Later, all the Qiang people surrendered, and the imperial court moved the Qiang people to Tianshui, Longxi, and Fufeng counties.
The next year, the Shenlang Qiang in Wudu rebelled, and Ma Yuan defeated the Shenlang Qiang and made them surrender.
The incident has been recorded in "The Biography of Ma Yuan".
From Shaodang to Dianliang, they lived in the Dayun Valley north of the Yellow River for generations. The tribe was small and the people were poor.
However, Xianling and Beinan were powerful and wealthy, and invaded Yunnan Liang many times.
Dian Liang and his son had been bullied and slighted for a long time, and they were very angry. Moreover, they usually had kindness and loyalty in the tribe, so Dian Liang joined the affiliated tribes and other mixed tribes, marched from Dayu Valley, and suddenly attacked Xianling and Bei'an. They defeated Xianling and Bei'an. They killed 3,000 people, plundered property and livestock, and seized the central area of ​​Dayu Valley as their residence. From then on, they became powerful.
Dian Liang's son Dian Wu succeeded to the throne.
In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, the Shenlang Qiang in Wudu rebelled, killing and plundering officials and people. The prefect fought with the Shenlang Qiang, but failed to win. The Longxi prefect Liu Xu sent Li Bao, an officer from Xindu and the supervisor of the army, to lead five thousand people to Wudu and fight against the Qiang. They killed the Qiang leader and killed and captured more than a thousand Qiang people.
At this time, Wudu's army also defeated the Qiang people, killing more than a thousand people, and the rest of the Qiang people surrendered.
At that time, Dianwu's subordinate tribes became powerful and often dominated the Qiang tribes. Anyone who wanted to invade the border, Dianwu taught them strategies and became their big leader.
In the autumn of the second year, Shaodang Qiang Dianwu and his younger brother Dian'an led 5,000 infantry and cavalry to invade the Longxi border fortress. Liu Xu sent troops to attack Dianwu in Paohan, but could not win. They fought again in Yunjie and were defeated by the Qiang. More than 500 people were killed.
At this time, the Qiang people of various tribes who guarded the fortress followed and invaded the border one after another.
The imperial court sent envoy Zhang Hong to lead the troops from various counties to attack the Qiang people. They fought at Yunwu and Tanggu, but were defeated. Zhang Hong and Longxi Chief Shi Tiansa both died.
Tianshui's army was defeated by Lao Jiezhong at Baishi, and more than a thousand people died.
At that time, among the leaders of Shaohe, there was a woman named Bi Tongqi, who was more than a hundred years old and very resourceful. She was trusted and respected by the people in the tribe, and everyone listened to her for advice.
Bitongqiu was attacked by Lu Shuihu, so she led her troops to defect to the county.
Many people in the tribe broke the law, so the chief of Linqiang arrested and imprisoned Bitongqi, and killed six to seven hundred people from the Bitongqi tribe.
Emperor Xianzong sympathized with her and issued an edict saying: In the past, Duke Huan of Qi conquered the Rong people without kindness and kindness, so the Spring and Autumn Annals derogatoryly called Duke Huan of Qi "people of Qi".
Today's country lacks benevolence, and the kindness cannot reach far away. What sin does the old and the weak have? Instead, they lose their lives together!
summary: Under the Han Dynasty, the Xiqiang faced expulsion and relocation. Emperor Wu expanded borders, building fortresses and separating Qiang from Xiongnu. In 42 BCE, Xianling Qiang allied with Xiongnu, attacking Lingju and Paohan, but were suppressed by General Li Xi. Later, Zhao Chongguo defeated them in 60 BCE. During Wang Mang's reign, Qiang lands were seized, but after his fall, they rebelled. In 25 CE, Guangwu restored the Qiang Protectorate, but conflicts persisted. Ma Yuan defeated Qiang rebellions in 35 CE, moving them to Tianshui and Longxi. By 58 CE, Dianwu's rebellion was crushed, and Qiang were resettled in Sanfu.

translation:
Suzong issued an edict to commemorate and praise Fu Yu, and named his son Fu Yi the Marquis of Ming Dynasty, granting him a fief of 700 households.
Zhang Yu, the governor of Longxi, was appointed to succeed the captain and led 10,000 people to garrison Linqiang.
Miwu has already killed Fu Yu and is used to getting benefits at the border.
In the first year of Zhanghe, Miwu and seven thousand infantry and cavalry from various tribes entered the Jincheng border fortress.
Zhang Yu sent Sima Fang to lead more than a thousand cavalry and Jincheng's troops to fight Miwu in Mucheng Valley. Miwu's army was defeated and fled. Miwu planned to surrender through an interpreter, and Zhang Yu agreed.
Miwu then led people from the same tribe to Linqiang County. Zhang Yu deployed his troops, held a meeting, and put poison in the wine. After the Qiang people got drunk, Zhang Yu took the opportunity to take action himself, ambushed all four, and killed more than 800 Qiang leaders.
Zhang Yu cut off the heads of Miwu and five other people and used them to pay homage to Fu Yu's grave.
He also allowed his troops to attack the Qiang people in the valley, killing more than 400 people and capturing more than 2,000 people alive.
Miwu's son Mitang and the people of his tribe cried towards the frontier fortress. They colluded with the Shaohe, Dangjian, Dangtian and other tribes, and used their children and gold and silver to recruit and accept the Qiang people of each tribe to resolve hatred and exchange hostages. Mi Tang led 5,000 troops to invade the Longxi frontier fortress. The prefect Kou Xu fought with Mi Tang at Baishi. The situation was unfavorable for Mi Tang, so he led his troops back to the Big and Small Yu Valleys, summoned various Hu tribes in the north, and joined the affiliated tribes. The races and tribes were very strong, and Zhang Yu was unable to conquer Mi Tang.
In the first year of Yongyuan, Zhang Yu was requisitioned for committing a crime. The imperial court appointed Deng Xun, the governor of Zhangye, as the school captain. Deng Xun gradually used rewards and bribes to alienate the Qiang people, and these tribes gradually collapsed.
Dongwu's son Camhao succeeded to the throne.
I was sent to lead my tribe to surrender.
The school captain Deng Xun sent troops to attack Mi Tang, who left Xiaoyu Valley and moved to Poyan Valley.
In the fourth year of Emperor Yongyuan's reign, Deng Xun died of illness, and Nie Shang, the governor of Shu County, took over as the school captain.
Nie Shang saw that the people in front of him could not conquer it after repeated attacks, and wanted to win them over with virtue, so he sent a messenger with an interpreter to call Mi Tang and let him return to live in Xiaoyu Valley.
After Mi Tang came back, he sent his grandmother Bei Que to Nie Shang. Nie Shang personally sent Bei Que to the border gate, offered sacrifices to the road gods and held a banquet to see her off. He also sent translator Tian Si and five other people to escort her to the tribe.
Mi Tang took this opportunity to rebel, and together with other tribes, they dismembered Tian Si and others alive, and used their blood oath to invade the Jincheng frontier again.
In the fifth year, Nie Shang was expelled from his post, and Juyan Duwei Guanyou took over as the school captain.
Because Guanyou was obsessed with the Tang Dynasty, it was difficult to be influenced by morality, and eventually rebelled. He sent messengers to instigate discord among the various Qiang tribes and lured them with property. Since then, the Qiang people have been divided and disintegrated.
Guanyou then sent troops out of the fortress to attack the Midang in the Xiaoyu Valley, killing and capturing more than 800 Qiang people, and harvesting tens of thousands of dendrobiums of wheat. He then built a castle on both sides of the Fengliu River, built large ships, and built a bridge over the Yellow River, intending to send his troops across the river to attack the Midang.
summary: The Qiang continued to resist Han rule. In 77 CE, Miwu led a revolt, defeating Han forces. Fu Yu, the Qiang Protector, was killed in 87 CE. Zhang Yu retaliated by poisoning Qiang leaders, but Miwu's son Mitang continued raids. Deng Xun and later officials used bribery to divide the Qiang, but conflicts resumed. In 107 CE, the Qiang rebellion under Dianling and others devastated border regions, costing billions and causing massive displacement. Ren Shang and Deng Zun campaigned against them, but corruption and mismanagement plagued efforts. By 118 CE, the Qiang were largely subdued, though sporadic revolts occurred.

translation:
In the first year of Xingnuo, the Qiang people who surrendered under Feng Xiang rebelled and invaded various counties. Guo Bang and Fan Chou defeated them and killed thousands of Qiang people.
Since Yuan Ren, his descendants have divided into a total of 150 tribes.
Among them, nine tribes are located west of the head of the Cizhi River and north of the border between Shu and Han. Their population numbers are not recorded in previous history books.
Only Shenlang Qiang is in Wudu and has thousands of men capable of fighting.
There are fifty-two tribes that are weak and have few people and cannot be independent. They are scattered into subordinate tribes. Some of them have completely declined and have no descendants, and some have moved away.
Among its eighty-nine tribes, only Zhong Qiang is the most powerful, with more than 100,000 people capable of fighting.
Other tribes range in size from tens of thousands to thousands. They plunder and invade each other, and their strength and decline are ever-changing. During the reign of Emperor Shun, the total number of Qiang people capable of fighting was approximately 200,000.
The Faqiang, Tangyan and other tribes were very far away and had no contact with them.
The names of the tribes of Li Niu and Baima Qiang in Shu and Han cannot be known or recorded.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, Lou Deng, leader of the Baima Qiang outside the Great Wall of Guanghan, and others led more than 5,000 Qiang households of his tribe to surrender to the imperial court. Guangwu granted Lou Deng the title of Lord Commander of Guiyi.
In the fifth and sixth year of Emperor He's reign, Zaotou and others, a fat Yi Qiang leader outside the borders of Shu County, led more than 500,000 people of the same tribe to surrender to the imperial court. Emperor He appointed Zaotou as the chief of the city and gave him a seal.
By the first year of Yongchu reign of Emperor An, 17,280 people from six tribes including Longqiao and other Qiang tribes outside the borders of Shushu had surrendered to the imperial court.
The next year, 36,900 people from eight tribes including the Qiang Bo Shen outside the borders of Shu County surrendered the entire area to the imperial court.
In winter, 2,400 Qiang people from the Shenlang tribe outside the Guanghan border came to submit to the imperial court.
In the second year of Emperor Huan's establishment of peace, more than a thousand Baima Qiang invaded the Guanghan vassal state and killed county officials. The Yizhou governor led the Banchu barbarians to defeat the invading Baima Qiang.
The Yuezhi Hu in Huangzhong was originally another branch of the Da Yuezhi. Was it retreating in the past? Leg area resides.
King Yuezhi was killed by Bao Shuandun, and the remaining tribes dispersed and crossed Congling to the west.
Among them, the weak ones went south into the mountains, lived among the Qiang tribes, and intermarried with the Qiang people.
When Husband General Huo Qubing defeated the Xiongnu, captured the Xihe area, and opened up Huangzhong, the Yuezhi came to surrender and lived mixed with the Han people.
Although they relied on the imperial court, they hesitated to wait and see. They followed the Han army to fight, and their fighting intensity also changed with the strength of the Han army's situation.
Their clothing, food, and language are roughly the same as those of the Qiang people, and they also use their father's name and mother's surname as tribal titles.
There are seven large tribes, and the total number of those who can fight is more than 9,000, distributed in Huangzhong and Lingju.
There are still hundreds of households in Zhangye, called Yiconghu.
In the first year of Zhongping, they rebelled with Beigong Boyu and others, killing Ling Zheng, the captain of the Qiang Protector, and Chen Yi, the prefect of Jincheng, and then invaded Longyou to cause chaos.
On Japan: The Qiang and Rong have been causing harm for a long time since the third generation.
During the Han Dynasty, they were quite weak compared to the Xiongnu, but after the Guangwu Zhongxing, their harm to the border gradually became serious.
The imperial court made mistakes in appeasing, governing and harmonizing the Qiang and Rong, and the army generals also violated their promises and trustworthiness.
Some of the Qiang people who surrendered to the imperial court fell into poverty and embarrassment in the hands of the powerful, and some were forced to work as slaves and do manual labor.
summary: In later years, the Qiang faced further suppression. Ma Xian defeated them in 141 CE, but his death in battle in 144 CE led to renewed chaos. Zhao Chong and others campaigned, but the Qiang declined by the 2nd century CE. During the Han dynasty's decline, Qiang allied with Yellow Turban rebels in 184 CE. By the 3rd century CE, the Qiang had fragmented into 150 tribes, with the Zhong Qiang being the most powerful, fielding over 100,000 warriors. The Yuezhi Hu, a related group, intermarried with Qiang and lived in Huangzhong. The text concludes that the Qiang's persistent harm stemmed from Han mismanagement, including broken promises and exploitation. The Yongchu period saw widespread rebellion, with Qiang plundering Sanfu and cutting off Longxi. Despite costly campaigns by generals like Deng Lu and Ren Shang, the Han failed to achieve lasting peace. The author criticizes the policy of relocating Qiang into Han territory, which exacerbated conflicts. Ultimately, the Qiang were suppressed by Duan Yi, but the Han dynasty's decline followed. The narrative emphasizes the cyclical nature of Qiang-Han relations, marked by rebellion, suppression, and eventual fragmentation.

translation:
Preface to the biographies of Yimin. "The Book of Changes" says: The meaning of Dun Gua is very great!
He also said: Don't serve princes and nobles, keep your noble reputation. Therefore, Emperor Yao took heaven as the law and could not make Chao Fu and Xu You accept his throne; King Wu of Zhou was a perfect man, and in the end he could only fulfill the innocent reputation of Boyi and Shuqi, the two sons of Lord Guzhu, for not eating Zhou Su.
Since then, the trend of seclusion has become more popular. Most people's deeds are roughly the same, but their motivations for seclusion are very different.
Some live in seclusion to satisfy their ambitions; some avoid the entanglements of big men to perfect their moral character; some seek a quiet environment to suppress impatience; some avoid dangerous disputes to seek temporary safety; some are cynical to establish their integrity; some despise wealth and honor to preserve their innocence.
However, seeing that they are willing to work in the fields and fish in the rivers and seas, must they be so interested in fish, birds, forests and grass?
But everyone has different personalities.
Therefore, even though Liu Xiahui suffered humiliation and was dismissed three times, he still refused to leave Qi. Lu Zhonglian would rather jump into the sea and die than respect Qin as emperor. Even his status as the king of a thousand-year-old country could not tempt him.
If they were put in another position, they wouldn't act the same way. Their stubbornness does have the appearance of seeking fame and fame, but they are like cicadas shed in the dust, jumping out of this filthy environment, far behind those who sharpen their heads to pursue fame and fortune.
Xunzi said it well: If you have high ambitions, you will look down on wealth; if you are moral, you will look down on princes.
The middle path of the Han Dynasty declined and Wang Mang usurped the throne. People with lofty ideals had strong indignation.
At that time, I don’t know how many people threw away their black gauze hats and left their official positions.
Yang Xiong said: The swan geese flew so high that the hunter’s arrow missed.
It is a metaphor for those who have traveled far away.
Emperor Guangwu came to the throne and sat sideways waiting for the wise men. He was hungry and thirsty. He sent people to recruit people from Qiuyuan with banners, silk and push carts. There was an endless stream of messengers on the rugged mountain roads.
For example, Xue Fang, Feng Meng and others invited him but refused to come out. Yan Guang, Zhou Dang, Wang Ba and others came out but refused to take their seats.
At that time, all conditions were in place, and people with lofty ideals were also thinking about the sage emperor. Isn't this a great opportunity to promote the free people and make the people of the world surrender?
Emperor Suzong also paid courtesy to Zheng Jun and hired Gao Feng to complete their honor.
Since then, the emperor's virtue has gradually declined, and villains have taken over. The hermits are wary and feel that it is shameful to stand with those ministers. They even walk away, losing the way of neutrality. Now record those who lived in seclusion, and those who returned to seclusion one after another after coming out, are listed in this article. Xiang Changchuan, whose courtesy name is Ziping, was born in Chaoge, Hanoi. He lives in seclusion and does not serve as an official. He has a moderate personality and is proficient in Laozi and the Book of Changes.
He was poor and had no resources for food. If a good person gave him some food, he would accept part of it and return the rest.
summary: The preface explains that seclusion has been a respected tradition since ancient times, as seen in figures like Chao Fu and Xu You, who refused Yao’s throne, and Boyi and Shuqi, who rejected Zhou’s rule. The motivations for seclusion vary: some seek to fulfill ambitions, perfect moral character, suppress impatience, avoid danger, establish integrity, or preserve innocence. While some criticize such acts as seeking fame, the preface argues that true hermits transcend worldly pursuits, as Xunzi noted: high ambitions despise wealth, and strong morals disdain princes. During Wang Mang’s usurpation, many abandoned office, and under Emperor Guangwu, hermits like Yan Guang and Zhou Dang were recruited but often refused to serve. The text records those who lived in seclusion or withdrew after serving.

translation:
Wang Mang's chief minister, Wang Yi, summoned him, but it took several years for him to arrive. He wanted to recommend him to Wang Mang, but Xiang Chang resolutely refused.
Hidden at home.
After reading the "Book of Changes" to the two hexagrams "Loss" and "Benefit", I sighed deeply and said: I already know that wealth is worse than poverty, and nobleness is worse than lowliness, but I don't know how death is worse than life.
During the Jianwu period, after his son and girl got married, he severed ties with his family and said, "Just think of me as dead."
So he acted randomly and traveled to the famous Five Mountains with his friend Beihai Qinqing, but in the end he didn't know where he ended up.
Feng Meng's biography, Feng Meng's courtesy name is Zikang, and he was born in Duchang, Beihai.
His family was poor and he worked as a pavilion chief in the county.
At that time, the county captain passed by the pavilion, and Peng Meng was waiting to greet him. He dropped his wooden shield and sighed, "How can a man serve as a servant for others?"
So he went to Chang'an to study and became proficient in the Spring and Autumn Classic.
At this time, Wang Mang killed his son Yu. Pengmeng said to his friends: The three cardinal principles are severed!
If you don't leave, disaster will bring harm to others.
He immediately took off his hat and hung it on the gate of Dongdu City. After returning, he moved his family to the seaside and lived in Liaodong.
Fengmeng had always understood the art of yin and yang, and knew that Wang Mang would be defeated soon, so he put a clay basin on his head and cried in the market: "New! New!"
So he hid.
When Guangwu came to the throne, he went to Langfu Mountain to cultivate his aspirations and practice Taoism. Everyone was influenced by his virtues.
The governor of Beihai heard about his noble character and sent officials to pay homage to him, but he did not respond to his courtesy.
The prefect held a grudge and sent people to arrest him.
The official kowtowed and said: "Zikang is a great sage and is famous all over the world. Wherever he is, people respect him like a father. If you go, you will definitely not be able to catch him. You will only bring humiliation to yourself."
The eunuch became angry, imprisoned the officials, and sent others to go.
When the man walked to Laoshan, people united to defend him with crossbows. The officials were wounded and bleeding and ran back.
Later, the imperial court summoned Fengmeng with an edict. Meng told the envoy that he was too old and had lost his way to the east-west direction, and said to the envoy: "The reason why the imperial court summoned me is because it thought I would be beneficial to politics. I don't even know the direction. How can I help the time?"
Hitched home immediately.
If you don't come out for continuous recruitment, you will die.
At first, Fengmeng was good friends with Xu Fang, Pingyuan Li Ziyun, and Wang Jungong from the same county. They all knew the theory of yin and yang and harbored virtuous behavior.
Xu Fang and Ziyun each raised thousands of apprentices. When the emperor was in trouble, he would not leave alone, but he worked as a cattle broker and secluded himself.
People at that time commented: "The King of the East Wall is a refuge from the world."
Biography of Zhou Dang, named Bo Kuang, a native of Guangwu, Taiyuan.
The family fortune is thousands of gold.
His father died when he was young and he was raised by his tribe. However, he was not treated politely and when he grew up, his property was not returned.
summary: Xiang Changchuan, a hermit from Hanoi, refused Wang Mang’s summons, studied the *Book of Changes*, and after his children married, he severed ties with his family and disappeared into the Five Mountains. Feng Meng, from Beihai, left his post as a pavilion chief, studied the *Spring and Autumn Annals*, and fled to Liaodong after Wang Mang killed his son. He later refused Guangwu’s summons, claiming old age and disorientation, and died in seclusion. Zhou Dang, a wealthy man from Taiyuan, studied in Chang’an, fought a duel over an old insult, and later refused to serve Wang Mang. Under Guangwu, he was summoned but declined, and the emperor defended his choice, granting him silk. Zhou Dang wrote books and died in Mianchi.

translation:
Someone asked him why.
Ba said: The emperor has dissatisfaction with his subjects, and the princes have dissatisfaction with others.
Situ Houba gave way to Wang Ba.
Yan Yang ruined the king's domineering ways: Wang Ruzhong, a secular party in Taiyuan, had this kind of trend.
So it was stopped.
Returned home due to illness. Live in seclusion and keep your ambitions, with a thatched hut.
After failing to call for several times, he died.
Yan Guangzhuan, Yan Guang, courtesy name Ziling, also known as Zun, was born in Yuyao, Kuaiji.
He became famous at a young age and traveled and studied with Emperor Guangwu.
When Guangwu became emperor, Yan Guang changed his name and lived in seclusion.
The emperor missed his talent, so he sent someone with the image to find it.
Later, someone from Qi State reported that there was a man wearing a sheep fur fishing in the lake.
The emperor suspected that it was Yan Guang, so he prepared a carriage and black silk and sent someone to invite him.
It took three times to come out.
Let him live in the military camp, make a bed, and have meals delivered by the eunuch in the morning and evening.
Situ Houba and Yan Guang were old friends and sent someone to deliver the letter.
The messenger said by the way: When Mr. Hou heard that your husband had arrived, he wanted to see you immediately, but he was busy with official duties, so he did not come.
I hope you will go to him at dusk and talk.
Yan Guang didn't answer, so he gave the visitor a pen and paper, and said to himself: "Mr. Junfang, it's very good to be a third official."
I hope you can have a kind heart, supplemented by morality, and make the world happy. If you flatter and follow the will, you will be killed.
Hou Ba read the letter, sealed it and sent it to the emperor. The emperor smiled and said: "What a crazy slave."
So I drove to the hotel immediately.
At this time, Yan Guang was still sleeping and had not gotten up. The emperor walked to the bedside. Touching his belly and saying: Oh! Ziling, can't you help me govern the country?
Yan Guang still slept silently. After a long time, he opened his eyes and stared at the emperor and said: In ancient times, Tang Yao was very virtuous and wanted to give up the throne to Father Chao. Father Chao washed his ears after hearing this.
Scholars all have their own ambitions, so why force others?
The emperor then said: Ziling, how can I not make you submit?
So he got in the car and left with a sigh.
Another time, the emperor invited Yan Guang in and talked with him about the past. The two talked to each other for several days.
The emperor calmly said to Yan Guang: How am I better than before?
Answer: You are a little fatter than before.
So they slept together, Yan Guang put his feet on Guangwu's belly.
The next day, Taishi reported that there was a guest star in the sky invading the throne of the emperor, and the situation was urgent.
The emperor smiled and said: I am sleeping with my old friend Yan Ziling!
Emperor Guangwu worshiped Yan Guang as an admonishment official, but Yan Guang refused to do so, so he farmed in Fuchun Mountain. Later generations called the place where Yan Guang fished Yan Linglai.
In the seventeenth year of Jianwu's reign, he sent someone to invite Yan Guang, but he still refused to come out.
Yan Guang lived to the age of eighty and died at home.
The biography of Jing Dan, named Dachun, was born in Fufeng.
summary: Wang Ba, also from Taiyuan, abandoned his official post during Wang Mang’s reign and refused to serve Guangwu, citing the emperor’s lack of respect for his subjects. Yan Guang, a childhood friend of Guangwu, changed his name and fished in seclusion. The emperor found him, but Yan Guang refused to serve, famously putting his feet on Guangwu’s belly while sleeping. He later farmed in Fuchun Mountain and died at home. Jing Dan, a scholar from Fufeng, was known for his pride and refused invitations from princes. When tricked into a banquet by a relative of the empress, he criticized the host’s meager food and left, living in seclusion thereafter.

translation:
Later, he fell ill and felt very sleepy, so he told his master: "In the past, Yanling Jizi buried his son between Yingbo and did not go to the countryside. After I die, please don't let my son carry the coffin back."
After Liang Hong died, Bo Tong and others buried him next to Yaoli's grave in the state of Wu. They all said: Yaoli was a martyr, and Liang Boluan was very noble, which allowed them to get close.
After the burial, the wife returned to Fufeng.
At first, Liang Hong's friend Gao Hui from Jingzhao liked to read "Laozi" when he was young and lived in seclusion in Huayin Mountain.
When Liang Hong traveled east, he thought of Gao Hui and wrote a poem: Birds are chirping looking for friends, and I also think of Gao Hui, hoping he can come here. The two never met again.
Gao Hui was also a proud man and had never been an official in his life.
Gao Fengzhuan, Gao Feng, courtesy name Wentong, was born in Nanyang Ye.
When he was young, he was a student, and his family was engaged in farming. However, Gao Feng specialized in reading and never rested day and night.
My wife once went to work in the fields and dried the wheat in the courtyard, calling Gao Feng to protect the chickens.
At this time, it was raining heavily, but Gao Feng was holding a bamboo pole and chanting scriptures. Unconsciously, the rainwater flowed into the wheat.
When his wife came back, she felt strange and asked him, and he realized it.
Later he became a famous Confucian and taught his disciples in the Western Tang Mountains.
Neighbors who were fighting over property were fighting with weapons. Gao Feng went to try to persuade him. As a last resort, he took off his turban, knelt, and resolutely requested: "Why have you forgotten all about benevolence, righteousness, and humiliation?"
The combatants were moved and put down their weapons to apologize to him.
Gao Feng was old, but he persisted in his ambitions tirelessly, and his reputation spread far and wide.
The eunuch continued to summon him, but Gao Feng was afraid that he would not be able to avoid it. He claimed that he was from the Wu family and should not be an official. He also pretended to have a lawsuit with his widowed sister-in-law over property, so he did not go out to serve as an official.
He fished invisibly and died at home. Tai Tong's biography, Tai Tong's courtesy name is Xiaowei, and he was born in Ye, Wei County. He lives in seclusion in Wu'an Mountain, digging caves as his residence and collecting medicine as his occupation.
During the early years of Jian's reign, he was not summoned by the state.
When the governor arrived at Ye, he sent an official to visit Tai Tong.
Tong Zaibing went to express his thanks.
The governor took the meeting gift and asked Tong: "It's very hard for Xiaowei to live like this. What should I do?"
Tong said: Fortunately, I was able to save my life and maintain my peace.
Isn't it like having an envoy read out the imperial edict in the morning and working hard at night? Isn't it not painful?
So he left, secluded himself, and never disappeared.
According to the biography of Han Kang, Han Kang's courtesy name was Boxiu, also known as Tianxiu, and he was a native of Baling, Jingzhao.
The family background is very famous.
He often went to famous mountains to collect medicinal herbs and sold them in Chang'an market. The price was always the same for more than thirty years.
At that time, a girl asked Han Kang to buy medicine, but Kang insisted that the original price should remain unchanged.
summary: Liang Hong, from Fufeng, studied in Taixue, worked as a pig herder, and compensated a neighbor for a fire by labor. He married Meng Guang, who dressed simply and shared his life of seclusion. They fled to Baling Mountain, then to Wu, where Liang Hong worked as a rice pounder. His wife served him with respect, raising the tray to her eyebrows. Liang Hong died in Wu and was buried near the martyr Yaoli. Gao Feng, a scholar from Nanyang, was so absorbed in reading that he let rain ruin his wheat. He mediated disputes and refused official summons, pretending to have a lawsuit to avoid service. Tai Tong, from Wei County, lived in a cave, collected herbs, and refused summons, stating his life was peaceful compared to officials’ toil.

translation:
The girl lost her temper and said: Are you Han Boxiu?
Aren't they sold at two prices?
Han Kang sighed and said: "I originally wanted to keep my name from others, but now the little girl knows my name, why are I selling medicine?"
So he fled to Baling Mountain.
The doctor invited Han Kang several times on his bus, but Han Kang never came.
Emperor Huan prepared a black silk curtain as a gift and used a carriage to hire him.
The envoy went to Han Kang's home with the emperor's edict, but Han Kang had no choice but to agree.
But instead of taking an An chariot, he took a diesel chariot and set off early in the morning before the messenger set off.
When they arrived at the pavilion, the pavilion chief knew that Han Zhengjun would pass by, so he sent someone to repair the road and bridge with a cow.
Suddenly, he saw Han Kang arriving in a chariot and wearing a scarf. Thinking that he was an old man farming, he asked someone to take the cow away.
Han Kang untied the cow in front of the car and gave it to him.
Soon after, the official arrived and found that the old man who had the cow taken away was Zheng Jun.
The envoy wanted to tell the emperor to kill the pavilion chief.
Han Kang said, "I gave him this cow myself. What's the crime of the pavilion chief?"
The messenger gave up.
Han Kang fled halfway, and later died of a long life without any illness.
Jiao Shen's biography, whose courtesy name is Zhongyan, was born in Maoling, Fufeng.
When I was young, I loved the learning of Huangdi and Laozi. I lived in seclusion in the valley, built a house in a cave, and admired the skills of pine and Qiao Daoyin.
When they merged with Ma Rong and Su Zhang in the countryside, Ma Rong was famous for his talent and erudition, and Su Zhang was famous for his honesty, but they both put caution before Jiao Shen.
Wu Cang of Runan valued him very much. So he sent a letter to observe his ambition and path: Zhong Yan's feet: Qin's place is vague. Although he rides on the clouds and walks on the mud, his habitat is different. Every time the west wind blows, why don't he sigh!
I heard that Huang and Lao said that they took advantage of the void and entered the underworld, hid themselves and escaped, and also managed the country and nourished the people, and made achievements in politics.
It's like climbing a mountain to the point where it becomes extinct, God doesn't see its proof, and people don't see its effect.
I think what do you think of it, sir?
In the past, Yi Yin did not have the right to treat the kings of Yao and Shun.
In today's Ming Dynasty, the world has opened up. Chao and Xu Wuwei are in Jishan, while Yi and Qihui are in Shouyang Mountain.
Being able to ride a dragon or a phoenix or fly among the clouds with one single step is beyond the imagination of a fox, rabbit or sparrow.
Jiao Shen didn't answer.
When he was more than seventy years old, he refused to marry. Later, he suddenly returned home and told himself the day when he was going to die, and he died on time.
Later, someone saw Jiao Shen in Dunhuang, so he was different from his previous life. Some people said that he was an immortal.
Ma Yao, a native of the same county as Jiao Shen, lives in seclusion in the mountains and makes a living by catching rabbits.
The place where he lived was secularized, and the people praised him and called him Mr. Ma Mu.
summary: Han Kang, from Jingzhao, sold herbs at a fixed price for thirty years. When a girl recognized him, he fled to Baling Mountain and refused Emperor Huan’s summons, escaping halfway. Jiao Shen, from Fufeng, studied Huang-Lao, lived in a cave, and refused to marry. He predicted his death and later was seen in Dunhuang, rumored to be immortal. Dai Liang, from Runan, imitated his mother’s braying for fun, and after her death, he ate meat while mourning, arguing that rituals should not suppress genuine emotion. He refused office and fled to Jiangxia, marrying off his five daughters with simple dowries.

translation:
Emperor Xu wanted to invite him, so he called him four times.
Fazhen said: Since I can't escape from this world, how can I drink the water that Xuyou washes my ears with?
So he lived in seclusion.
My friend Guo Zhengcheng said: Fazhen's name can be heard, but his body is rare. If he runs away from his name but his name follows me, he avoids his name but his name follows me. He can be regarded as a master of all generations.
So they published a book praising him and called him Mr. Xuande.
He died at the age of eighty-nine, five years after his death.
The biography of Hanyin Laofu, Hanyin Laofu, I don’t know who he is.
During the Yanxi period of Emperor Huan, the emperor was lucky enough to visit the mausoleum, pass by Yunmeng, and visit the Mianshui River. The common people all went to see it, and there was an old man who continued to farm alone.
Zhang Wen, the minister of Nanyang, felt strange and sent someone to ask: "People are coming to watch, but my father keeps plowing alone. Why?"
The old man smiled but did not answer.
Zhang Wen came down and walked a hundred steps to talk to his father in person.
The old father said: I am a savage and I don’t understand this.
May I ask why the emperor was established because of chaos in the world?
Or is it to establish the emperor because of governance?
Is the purpose of establishing the Son of Heaven to be the father of all people in the world?
Or enslave the common people to support the emperor?
In the past, the sage kings ruled the world, raised rafters and raised rafters, and all surnames were peaceful.
Today, your king works hard for the people but indulges himself and enjoys leisurely life without restraint.
I'm ashamed of you. How can you bear to let others watch?
Zhang Wen was greatly ashamed after hearing this.
Ask him his name and leave without telling him.
The biography of Chen Liu's father, Chen Liu's father, I don't know who he is.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, the party's insurrection broke out, and Huang Shuwai ordered Zhang Sheng, a native of Chenliu, to leave his official position and return to his hometown. Meeting friends on the road, we spread the grass together and sat on the ground to talk.
Zhang Sheng said: I heard that the people of Zhao killed Mingdu, and Confucius went to the riverside and returned;
Today there is chaos in the officialdom and the slander of loyal and good people. Will the virtuous and gentlemen leave the court?
If virtue is not established and people are helpless, their lives will be inevitable in the future. What should we do?
So they hugged each other and cried.
The old father walked past in a hurry, leaning on his staff and sighing: Oh, why is the second doctor crying so sadly?
The dragon does not hide its scales, the phoenix does not hide its feathers, the snare is hung high, no matter where it goes, what is the use of crying?
The two wanted to talk to him, but left without knowing where they ended up.
The biography of Pang Gong, Pang Gong, was from Xiangyang, Nanjun.
They live in the south of Xian Mountain and have never been to the city. The husband and wife treat each other as if they were guests.
Liu Biao, the governor of Jingzhou, invited him several times but could not give in, so he went to visit him.
He said to him: If you can protect yourself, how can you protect the world?
summary: Fa Zhen, a great Confucian from Fufeng, refused a prefect’s offer of office, saying he would rather be north of Beishan or south of Nanshan. He was recommended to Emperor Shun but declined, living in seclusion and earning the title Mr. Xuande. The Hanyin Old Man, during Emperor Huan’s visit, continued plowing and criticized the emperor for indulging in leisure while the people suffered. The Chenliu Old Man, during the party insurrection, told weeping officials that crying was useless, as the world’s traps were everywhere. Pang Gong, from Xiangyang, refused Liu Biao’s summons, saying he left peace to his descendants, not danger. He and his wife later retreated to Lumen Mountain.

translation:
Deng Yu, courtesy name Zhonghua, was a native of Xinye County, Nanyang County.
At the age of thirteen, he was able to recite poems and studied under a teacher in Chang'an. At that time, Guangwu was also traveling to the capital to study. Although Deng Yu was young, when he saw Guangwu, he knew that he was not an ordinary person, so he got close to him.
Return home after a few years.
When the Han army rose up and Gengshi came to the throne, many heroes recommended Deng Yu, but Deng Yu refused to comply.
Guangwu said: Even so, what do you want to do? Deng Yu said: I hope that Duke Ming's majesty will spread throughout the world, and I will be able to do my best for Duke Ming and go down in history.
Guangwu laughed and left him to sleep and chat.
Deng Yujin said: Although Guanxi was the capital of Gengshi, there is no stability in Shandong now. The likes of Red Eyebrow and Qingdu are often robbed by tens of thousands, and people in Sanfu area often gather in groups under the guise of names.
Gengshi did not defeat them, and they did not listen to the command and ruling. The generals were all mediocre people who wanted to get rich, compete for power, and be happy sooner or later. They were not loyal, wise, foresighted, and really wanted to respect the Lord and appease the people.
The four parties are falling apart and the situation is clearly visible.
Although Ming Gong has established a meritorious service in assisting the royal family, he may not be able to achieve great success.
For the current plan, it is better to recruit heroes from all over the world, make sure to please the people, build the great cause of the great ancestor, and save the lives of the people.
It is enough to pacify the world with public virtue and talent. Emperor Guangwu was so pleased that he ordered everyone around him to call Deng Yu General Deng.
Let him stay in the tent and discuss strategic plans together.
When Wang Lang raised his army, Guangwu went from Ji to Xindu and sent Deng Yu to recruit "quick troops" from various counties. He got thousands of people and ordered him to personally lead them to attack Leyang County.
Deng Yu said: Now there is chaos in the sea, and people miss Ming Jun like a baby longing for its loving mother. In ancient times, it was the strength of virtue, not the size of the land, that made great achievements and conquered the world. Guangwu is happy.
When appointing generals at that time, they often visited Deng Yu. The talents recommended by Deng Yu were all worthy of their positions. Guangwu believed that Deng Yu knew people.
He was sent to lead another cavalry team with Gai Yan and others to attack the bronze horses in Qingyang.
Gai Yan and others arrived first, but lost the battle and retreated to protect the city. They were trapped by the thieves. Deng Yu advanced to fight with the thieves, defeated the thieves and captured their general alive.
From Guangwu chasing the thieves to Puyang, they won consecutive battles and Beizhou was generally pacified.
When Chimei entered the pass in the west, Gengshi sent Duke Kuang of Dingguo, Chengdan of Xiangyi, General Liu Jun of Anti-Wei and other generals to guard Hedong and Hongnong counties respectively to resist.
The Red Eyebrow tribe gathered in large numbers, and Wang Kuang and others could not resist it. Guangwu expected that the Red Eyebrow Army would break through Chang'an and wanted to take advantage of the opportunity to annex Guanzhong. However, he was busy with Shandong and did not know who to entrust with the Western Expedition. Since Deng Yu had the demeanor of a general, he gave him the strategy of Western Expedition.
summary: Deng Yu, courtesy name Zhonghua, was from Xinye County, Nanyang. At thirteen, he could recite poems and studied in Chang'an, where he befriended Guangwu, recognizing his extraordinary nature. After returning home, he refused offers from other heroes when the Han army rose. He told Guangwu he wished to serve him and achieve lasting fame. Guangwu kept him close, and Deng Yu advised that while Gengshi held Guanxi, instability in Shandong and bandit groups like the Red Eyebrows threatened order. He urged Guangwu to recruit heroes, win over the people, and build a great cause. Guangwu appointed him General Deng and consulted him on strategies.

translation:
He worshiped Deng Yu as the former general and divided his 20,000 elite troops equally. He sent him to the west and ordered Deng Yu to select the generals and subordinates who could join him in the western expedition.
So Han Xin was appointed as the military advisor, Li Wen, Li Chun, and Cheng Liu were used as sacrificial wines, Feng Yiyin was appointed as General Jinu, Fan Chong was appointed General Xiaoqi, Zong Xin was appointed General Chariot, Deng Xun was appointed General Jianwei, Geng Jinjin was appointed General Red Eyebrow, and Zuo Yu was appointed General Advisor, and they led the army westward.
In the first month of the first year of Jianwu, Deng Yu entered Hedong County from Jiguan. The captain of Hedong County guarded the pass and refused to open it. Deng Yu attacked for ten days and broke through the pass, seizing more than a thousand vehicles with baggage.
He entered Anyi and was unable to capture it for several months.
Gengshi General Fan Shen led tens of thousands of people and crossed Dayang to attack Deng Yu. Deng Yu sent his generals to attack south of Jie County, defeated Fan Shen's army and beheaded Fan Shen.
So Wang Kuang, Cheng Dan, Liu Jun and others combined an army of more than 100,000 to attack Deng Yu. Deng Yu's army was disadvantaged and Fan Chong died in the battle.
It was sunset and the fighting was over. Seeing that the army was in ruins, military advisor Han Xin and other generals advised Deng Yu to leave at night, but Deng Yu refused to listen.
On the second day of Guihai, Wang Kuang and others believed that Guihai was an unlucky day in Liujia and no troops were sent out all day, so Deng Yu was able to stop his weapons and readjust his troops.
The next morning, Kuang's entire army went out to attack Deng Yu. Deng Yu ordered his troops not to move rashly. When Wang Kuang's army arrived at the camp, Deng Yu sent an order to the generals to march forward with great noise and defeat Wang Kuang's army.
Wang Kuang and others abandoned their troops and fled, but Deng Yu led his light cavalry in pursuit. He captured Liu Jun, Hedong Governor Yang Bao, and Chijie Zhonglang General Mi Xi. He killed them all, confiscated six talismans, five hundred seals and ribbons, and countless weapons, and Hedong County was pacified.
In the same month, Guangwu ascended the throne in Gaohuang and sent envoys to worship Deng Yu as the chief minister.
The order of the official appointment said: The former general Deng Yu is ordered to: Adhere to loyalty and filial piety, and plan strategies with me to win a decisive victory thousands of miles away.
Confucius said: Since I had Yan Hui, my disciples have become increasingly close.
He beheaded the generals and defeated the army, and pacified Shanxi, which was a particularly outstanding achievement.
If the people are not close to each other and lack the teachings of the Wuchang, you, as a Situ, should give the people the teachings of the Wuchang. The teachings of the Wuchang lie in generosity.
Now I am sending you Captain Fengche to grant you the seal and ribbon, and you will be granted the title of Marquis of Zan, and you will be able to live in the city for ten thousand households.
Deng Yu was only twenty-four years old at this time. So Deng Yu crossed the Fenyin River and entered Xiayang County.
Gengshi Zhonglang sent Zuo Fuduweigong to She, leading his troops of 100,000, and together with Zuo Fengyi's soldiers, they resisted Deng Yu in Yaxian County. Deng Yu again broke through and drove them away, and the red eyebrow army entered Chang'an.
summary: Deng Yu recruited troops for Guangwu, defeating enemies like the bronze horses in Qingyang. When the Red Eyebrows threatened, Guangwu entrusted Deng Yu with the Western Expedition, appointing him Former General with 20,000 elite troops. In the first year of Jianwu, Deng Yu entered Hedong, defeating Gengshi generals and pacifying the region. Guangwu ascended the throne and made Deng Yu Chief Minister, praising his loyalty and achievements. At twenty-four, Deng Yu crossed into Xiayang, defeating more enemies as the Red Eyebrows entered Chang'an. His disciplined troops attracted many followers, and he became famous in Guanxi.

translation:
At this time, Sanfu's armies were defeated one after another. The Red Eyebrow Army brutally plundered wherever they passed, and the people did not know where they were going.
I heard that Deng Yu always took advantage of victory and his troops were well-disciplined, so they all came to welcome Deng Yu's army with their young and old. Thousands of people returned every day, and the crowd was said to be millions.
Wherever Deng Yu went, he often stopped to pay his respects and express his condolences. Fathers and children, with their white hair hanging in buns, crowded under his car. They were all grateful and happy, so Deng Yu became famous in Guanxi.
The emperor praised him and wrote several letters praising him.
All the generals and heroes advised Deng Yu to attack Chang'an directly.
Deng Yu said: Otherwise, although we have many troops now, there are few who can fight. There will be no savings to rely on in the front, and there will be no resources for transfer behind.
The Red Eyebrow Army had just captured Chang'an, with abundant wealth and unstoppable morale.
However, thieves live in groups and have no plan for the whole day. Although there is a lot of wealth, there are many changes, how can they hold on?
The three counties of Shangjun, Beidi, and Anding are vast, sparsely populated, and plentiful in grain, rice, and livestock. We are temporarily reorganizing the army in the north, providing food and nourishing the soldiers, so as to observe the weaknesses of the Red Eyebrow Army, and then try to attack them! So he led his army north to Yuyi County.
Wherever Deng Yu went, he defeated the Red Eyebrow Army's various camps and defenses, and all counties and counties opened their doors and surrendered.
Zongyu, the prefect of Xihe, sent his son to surrender with Deng Yu's documents from various places in hand, and Deng Yu sent him to the capital.
The emperor thought that Guanzhong was not yet settled and Deng Yu had not advanced for a long time, so he issued an order: "Situ is Yao; the traitor is Jie."
The officials and people in Chang'an were in panic and had nowhere to turn.
We should seize the opportunity to attack and calm Xijing to maintain the hearts of the people. Deng Yu still insisted on his previous opinions and sent his generals to attack the counties in Shangjun separately. He also recruited troops to bring in grain and returned to Dayao County.
Feng Huanyin and Zong Xin were sent to guard Yuyi.
The two fought for power and attacked each other. Feng Yiyin killed Zong Xin and counterattacked Deng Yu. Deng Yu sent an envoy to report to Emperor Guangwu.
The emperor asked the envoy: Who is the dearest to you? The messenger said: This is Huang Fang, the protector of the army. The emperor guessed that Feng Yiyin and Huang Fang could not reconcile for a long time and would inevitably have a confrontation. Therefore, he told Deng Yu: The person who arrested Feng Yanyin must be Huang Fang. So he sent Shangshu Zongguang to take the talisman to recruit Huang Fang to surrender.
More than a month later, Huang Fang indeed arrested Feng Yanyin and led his troops to accuse him.
Gengshi generals Wang Kuang, Hu Yin and others surrendered to Zong Guang and returned east together with Zong Guang.
When they arrived at Anyi, Wang Kuang and others tried to escape on the way, but Zong Guang killed them all.
Feng Yiyin went to Luoyang and was pardoned but not killed.
In the spring of the second year of Jianwu, he sent envoys to change the title of Deng Yu to the title of Marquis of Liang, and granted him four counties in the city.
At this time, the Red Eyebrow Army marched west to Fufeng, and Deng Yu then went south to Chang'an, where he garrisoned at Kunming Pool and feasted the soldiers with wine and food.
He led the generals to bathe, change clothes, fast, choose auspicious days, practice etiquette and worship in the Gaozu Temple, accept the god of the eleven emperors, and send envoys to Luoyang to visit the garden and mausoleum, and specially arranged officials and soldiers to worship and guard the mausoleum.
Deng Yu led his troops to fight with Yan Cen in Lantian, but failed, so he went to Yunyang.
Liu Jia, the king of Hanzhong, surrendered to Deng Yu.
Liu Jiaxian Li Bao was arrogant and rude, so Deng Yu killed him.
Li Bao's younger brother gathered Li Bao's troops to attack Deng Yu and killed the general Geng Jinjin.
Since Feng Yiyin rebelled against Deng Yu, Deng Yu's prestige was damaged. At this time, the Red Eyebrow Army returned to Chang'an again. Deng Yu fought with it and was defeated. When they arrived at Gaoling, the soldiers were hungry and ate jujube vegetables to survive.
The emperor then summoned Deng Yu back and issued an edict: "Chimei is short of food, so he will naturally come eastward. I only need to break the horse's staff and whip him to defeat him." The generals are not something to worry about, so don't rush into the army rashly.
Deng Yu felt ashamed that he had not accomplished anything since he had been appointed. He sent hungry soldiers to fight several times, but was often unfavorable.
In the spring of the third year, he attacked Chimei with Deng Hong, the chariot and cavalry general, but was defeated by Chimei. All his troops died and dispersed. He returned to Yiyang alone with twenty-four cavalry, and returned the seal to Da Situ and Liang Hou as apology.
The imperial edict was returned to Hou Yinshou.
After a few months, I paid homage to the right general.
Since Yancen was defeated in Dongyang, he cooperated with Qin Feng.
In the spring of the fourth year, they invaded the Shunyang area again.
He sent Deng Yu to protect General Deng Ye of the Fu Han Dynasty and General Yu Kuang of the Fu Han Dynasty, and defeated Yan Cen against Deng. He pursued them to Wudang and defeated Yan Cen again.
Cen fled to Hanzhong, and the rest of the party surrendered.
In the 13th year of Jianwu's reign, the world was peaceful, and all the meritorious officials increased their households. They appointed Deng Yu as the Marquis of Gaomi and received the taxes from the four counties of Gaomi, Chang'an, Yi'an, and Chunyu.
The emperor considered Deng Yu's meritorious service and made Deng Yu's younger brother Deng Kuan the prince of the Ming Dynasty.
Later, the titles of left and right generals were revoked, and they were granted special access to the court to see the emperor.
Deng Yu was civilized at heart, honest, honest and considerate in his behavior, and he served his mother very filially.
The world has been peaceful, and people often want to distance themselves from fame and power.
summary: Deng Yu advised against directly attacking Chang'an, citing the Red Eyebrows' strength and advocating a strategy of gathering resources in the north to observe their weaknesses. He led his army north, defeating Red Eyebrow camps and gaining surrenders. However, internal conflicts among his generals led to setbacks. In the second year of Jianwu, Deng Yu was made Marquis of Liang. He fought the Red Eyebrows but faced defeats, and Guangwu recalled him, advising caution. Deng Yu, ashamed, continued fighting but was ultimately defeated in the third year, returning to Yiyang with few men and resigning his posts. He was later reinstated as Right General and achieved victories against Yan Cen.

translation:
He had thirteen children, and each of them mastered a skill.
By regulating family rules and educating children and grandchildren, you can become a model for future generations.
All expenses are derived from fiefdom taxes, and no private property is repaired or private gain is sought. Therefore the emperor respects him more.
In the first year of the Zhongyuan Dynasty, he acted as Situ again.
From the emperor's tour of Shandong, he went to Mount Tai to build an altar to worship heaven.
When Xianzong came to the throne, because Deng Yu was the late emperor, he was worshiped as Taifu. When he came to court, he was ordered to stand facing east and treated like a guest, and he was very respected and favored. In the first year of Yongping, Deng Yu died at the age of fifty-seven. His posthumous title is Yuan Hou.
The emperor divided Yu into three kingdoms: Zhen, the eldest son, was the Marquis of Gaomi, Xi was the Marquis of Chang'an, and Zhen was the Marquis of Yi'an.
Yu's young son, Zihong, was good at making plans.
In Yongpingzhong, I thought I was Xiaohou.
Introducing and discussing border affairs, the emperor thought he could, worshiped the general and commander Shi, and led five battalions of soldiers to garrison Yanmen.
During the reign of Emperor Suzong, he was the general of Du Liao.
In the Yongyuan period, he and the general Dou Xian jointly attacked the Huns and achieved great success, conquering the chariot and cavalry generals.
He went out of the fortress to pursue Hu Fenghou, stayed there, and was thrown into prison to die.
Gaomi Hou Zhen died and was succeeded by his son.
Princess Qinshui, the daughter of Emperor Qian Shangxian.
In the fourteenth year of Yongyuan, the Yin Queen's witchcraft incident occurred. Qian Cong's brother Feng Hou's uncle was executed, Qian Cong was seated, and the country was eliminated.
In the first year of Yuanxing, Emperor He was granted the title of Qian and served as his minister.
When the emperor dies, the son becomes an heir.
After death, the son praises the heir.
Princess Wuyin, the sister of Emperor Shang An, was the Shaofu during the reign of Emperor Huan.
Praise for death, the eldest son of a certain heir.
The youngest son Chang took the title of Marquis of Wuyin from his mother-in-law and worshiped Huangmen as his minister.
The Marquis of Chang'an succeeded to the vassal vassal, and the eldest daughter of the clan, Princess Pinggao, served as an attendant during the reign of Emperor He.
The Marquis of Yi'an, Zhen Zikang, had little conduct.
Brother Liang attacked and had no heirs. In the sixth year of Yongchu, Shao granted Kang Kang the title of Marquis of Yi'an.
At that time, all those who were granted the title of Shao lived half of the rent from their homeland. Kang, who was a relative of the empress dowager, only had three to two of his own, and served as the auxiliary of the Yue Cavalry School.
The Empress Dowager Kang Yi had been in the government for a long time, and the clan was full of people. She wrote several letters to Changle Palace to advise against the disputes. She should worship the public office at the expense of her private rights.
The Queen Mother refused.
Kang was afraid, so in the first year of Yongning, he declined due to illness.
The Queen Mother asked her servants to ask.
At that time, the people in the palace came and went, and many of them could be criticized or praised. Among them, the elders were all called Zhongdaren.
The envoy was the maidservant of the Kang family, who was also from Tongzhong.
When Kang heard about it, he criticized him and said: "How dare you come from my family?" The maid was resentful and said that it was not good for Kang to pretend to be ill.
The Queen Mother was furious, so she dismissed Kang as an official and sent him back to his country without any official status.
After his brother was executed, Emperor An of Zhengkang became his minister.
After Emperor Shun was established, he was appointed as a servant. He had the title of Fangzheng and was well-known in the court.
Avoid illness and get special promotion.
He died in the third year of Yangjia, and his posthumous title was Hou Yi.
summary: In the 13th year of Jianwu, Deng Yu was made Marquis of Gaomi. He was known for his filial piety, modesty, and avoidance of fame and power. He had thirteen children, each skilled in a craft, and lived frugally on his fiefdom taxes. He served as Acting Situ again and accompanied the emperor to Mount Tai. Under Xianzong, he was made Grand Tutor and treated with great respect. He died at fifty-seven in the first year of Yongping, posthumously titled Yuan Hou. His sons inherited his titles, and his descendants continued in service, though some faced downfall due to political incidents.

translation:
The historian commented: In the era of change, kings and ministers choose each other, which is the key to the initial planning of things.
Deng Gong carried food on foot and ran alone in the chaos. It can be said that he knew where he was going and what he would do. He divided half of the army to attack the gap in Shanxi, so that the east of the river and the west of Guanxi were shaken. Those who defected to his command felt as if they had returned home.
Although the achievements were not completed, the moral virtues were promoted.
Later, although the power of the city was lost, the troops dispersed in Yiyang, and Situ's seal and ribbon were handed over, the marquis still died in his years, glorious and haggard, but his subordinates were always the same. He was promoted to an official, and he returned to the court in frustration. Guangwu never doubted him, so that future generations would not see any flaws or barriers in the beauty of the monarch and his ministers. Isn't this the most perfect act of a benevolent gentleman?
Kou Xun, courtesy name Ziyi, was from Changping County, Shanggu County, and his surname has been prominent for generations.
Kou Xun was initially a meritorious officer of the county, and the prefect Geng Kuang thought highly of him.
When Wang Mang failed, Gengshi ascended the throne and sent envoys to declare to the various counties that those who surrendered first would have their titles restored.
Kou Xun followed Geng Kuang to greet the envoy at the border. Geng Kuang presented the seal and ribbon. The envoy accepted it and had no intention of returning it all night.
Kou Xun brought weapons to see the envoy. Please return the seal and ribbon.
The messenger refused to give it and said: I am the messenger of the King of Heaven. Does the master want to coerce me? Kou Xun said: "It's not that I dare to coerce you, but privately I feel sad for your poor plan."
Now that the world has been settled, the country's credibility has not been declared, so the king can establish a talisman to carry out missions to all directions. Everyone in the county and country stretches their necks and tilts their ears, watching for the wind and returning to their fate.
Now that you first arrived in Shanggu, you destroyed Daxin, discouraged the whole county's desire to return to Hue, and created a gap for centrifugal betrayal. How will you command other counties?
Moreover, Lord Geng was in Shanggu and had been trusted by the officials and the people for a long time. Now if he is replaced, if he is succeeded by a virtuous man, Geng will be uneasy, and if he is an unworthy person, he will be reborn in chaos.
In order to make your plans better, there is no better way to restore Geng Kuang's position as governor to bring peace to the people. The envoy did not agree, and Kou Xun angrily scolded the people around him to summon Geng Kuang according to the envoy's order. When Geng Kuang arrived, Kou Xun gave the seal and ribbon to Geng Kuang.
The envoy had no choice but to reinstate Geng Kuang in accordance with the emperor's will. Geng Kuang returned from his post.
When Wang Lang raised his troops, he sent generals to attack Shanggu and urgently ordered Geng Kuang to send troops.
Kou Xun and his disciple Yu Minye jointly said to Geng Kuang: Handan has suddenly risen, and it is difficult to trust and return.
In the past, when Wang Mang was king, only Liu Boxheng was the most rare.
summary: Kou Xun, courtesy name Ziyi, was from Changping, Shanggu, from a prominent family. He served as a county officer under Prefect Geng Kuang. When Gengshi sent envoys, Kou Xun ensured Geng Kuang retained his position by persuading an envoy to return the seal. When Wang Lang rose, Kou Xun advised Geng Kuang to ally with Guangwu, citing his virtue. He attacked Handan's envoys and joined Guangwu, who made him a partial general. Deng Yu admired him, and Guangwu entrusted him with guarding Hanoi, comparing him to Xiao He.

translation:
Kou Xun then ordered his soldiers to ride in the city and beat drums, shouting: "Liu Gong's soldiers are here!" When Su Mao's army heard that the formation was loose, Kou Xun led his army to attack, defeated Su Mao's army, chased him to Luoyang, and beheaded Jia Qiang.
Thousands of Sumao soldiers themselves threw themselves into the Yellow River and died, while more than ten thousand were captured alive.
Kou Xun and Feng Yi crossed the Yellow River and returned.
