From then on, Luoyang was shaken and frightened, and the city gates were closed during the day.
At this time, Guangwu heard that Zhu Jun had defeated Hanoi. Soon Kou Xun's letter arrived. Guangwu was overjoyed and said: I know Kou Ziyi is capable of the job! The generals celebrated and gave Guangwu a title, and Guangwu ascended the throne.
At that time, there was an urgent shortage of military rations. Kou Xun used rickshaws and horse-drawn carriages to transport the rations continuously. The minister only sent the amount of rations to the officials.
Emperor Guangwu comforted Kou Xun several times with simple policy letters. Dong Chong, a fellow student from Maoling, said to Kou Xun: The emperor has newly ascended the throne, and the four parties have not yet been settled. At this time, the princes occupy the major counties, win the hearts of the people internally, destroy Sumao externally, intimidate the neighboring enemies, and have great fame. This is the time for treacherous people to look at and cause resentment!
In the past, when Xiao He was guarding the pass, Mingwu adopted Bao Sheng's suggestion and Gao Zu was overjoyed.
The people you are leading now are all Kun brothers of the Liu clan. I'm afraid you want to serve as a warning to those who came before you! Kou Xun thought it was true and pretended to be sick.
The emperor's general attacked Luoyang and went to Hanoi first. Kou Xun asked to join the army.
The emperor said: Hanoi cannot leave you! The emperor refused to listen to his repeated requests, so he sent his brother's son Kou Zhang and sister's son Gu Chong to lead a commando team willing to be the vanguard of the army.
The emperor praised him, but everyone thought he was partial to the general.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, Kou Xun was dismissed from his post because he was involved in the case of investigating the petition.
At this time, Yan Zhong and Zhao Dun from Yingchuan gathered more than 10,000 people in their tribe and joined forces with the secret man Jia Qi to become bandits.
Kou Xun was dismissed from office for several months, and was worshiped as the prefect of Yingchuan. He jointly attacked with Hou Jin, the traitor general.
Within a few months, Jia Qi's head was beheaded, and Yingchuan County was all pacified.
He was granted the title of Kou Xun Yong Nuhou, and he was able to feed thousands of households in the city.
When Zhijinwu Jiafu was in Runan, his generals killed someone in Yingchuan, and Kou Xun arrested him and imprisoned him.
At that time, the legal system was in its infancy, and those who broke the law in the military camp were mostly tolerated and tolerated, but Kou Xun beheaded him in the city.
Jia Fu sighed in shame.
He passed by Yingchuan on his return and said to his surroundings: "I am the same general as Kou Xun, and now I have been framed by him. How can a man refuse to fight despite being attacked?"
When I see Kou Xun now, I will kill him with my own hands! Kou Xun knew his plan and did not want to meet him.
summary: Kou Xun fortified Hanoi, supplying Guangwu's army with arrows, horses, and grain. When Zhu Tuna attacked Wen, Kou Xun led a swift defense, defeating Su Mao and Jia Qiang with reinforcements. Guangwu praised him and ascended the throne. Kou Xun continued supplying the army, but heeded advice to feign illness to avoid suspicion. He later served as Prefect of Yingchuan, suppressing bandits, and was made Marquis of Yongnu. He avoided conflict with General Jia Fu, reconciling with him for the nation's sake.

translation:
General Geng of Jianwei led Dou Shi, the senior official of Taizhong, Liang Tong, the prefect of Wuwei, and others to besiege Gaoping, but they could not capture it for a year.
In the tenth year of Jianwu's reign, the emperor entered the pass and prepared to conquer it personally. Kou Xun followed Guangwu at that time and advised: "Chang'an is located between Luoyang and Gaoping, so it is convenient to connect. Anding and Longxi will definitely feel shaken and fearful. This is because being comfortable in one place can subdue the four directions."
Now that the soldiers and horses are tired and have just come out of danger, this is not a good strategy for His Majesty to secure the country. The historical events that happened in Yingchuan the year before last can serve as a warning. The emperor did not listen.
After marching to the county, Gao Jun still could not be captured. The emperor discussed sending an envoy to persuade Gao Jun to surrender, and said to Kou Xun: "You stopped my action before, now go for me."
If Gao Jun does not surrender immediately, I will lead Geng and other five battalions to attack. When Kou Xun came to the first city with the seal, Gao Jun sent military advisor Huangfu Wen to pay an audience, but he refused to obey any words or etiquette.
Kou Xun was angry and prepared to kill Huangfu Wen.
The generals remonstrated and said: "We have ten thousand elite soldiers with many powerful crossbows. They have blocked the Long Road in the west and have not been able to capture it for years."
I'm afraid it's not possible to ask him to surrender and kill his envoy now, right? Kou Xun refused and killed Huangfu Wen.
Let his deputy go back and tell Gao Jun: "The military advisor was rude and has been killed."
If you want to surrender, hurry up; if you don't want to surrender, just hold on. Gao Jun was frightened and immediately opened the city gate and surrendered.
All the generals celebrated and said: "Excuse me, I killed his envoy and Gao Jun surrendered the whole city. What is the reason for this?" Kou Xun said: Huangfu Wen is Gao Jun's confidant, and Gao Jun draws all his strategies from him.
Now that he is here, his words are unyielding and he will have no intention of surrender.
If you let him go, Gao Jun will succeed in his plan; if you kill him, Gao Jun will be frightened and surrender. All the generals said: We didn't expect it. So Gao Jun was arrested and returned to Luoyang.
Kou Xun was proficient in classics and cultivated virtues, and his reputation was more important than that of the court. He used all his salary and salary to give generously to his friends, old friends, and officials who followed him.
Often said: I relied on the help of scholar-bureaucrats to get where I am today. How can I enjoy wealth alone? People at that time regarded him as an elder and thought he had the talents of a prime minister.
He died in the twelfth year of Jianwu and was given the posthumous title of Weihou.
Zi Kou lost his heirship.
Kou Xun's brother from the same mother, his brother's son, and sister's son were named marquises for their military merits, a total of eight people. They were all marquises for life but were not passed down to future generations.
At first, Min Ye was planning affairs with Kou Xun. Kou Xun explained his loyalty to the emperor many times, and the emperor conferred on him the title of Marquis of Guannei and the post of governor of western Liaoning.
In the 13th year of Jianwu's reign, he again granted the title of Marquis of Jiujiao to his brother Shou, who had lost his concubine.
Later, he was granted the title of Marquis of Jieliu by Kou Shan.
After Kou Xi's death, his son Kou Li succeeded to the throne and was granted the title of Marquis of Shangxiang.
After Kou Li died, Zi Kou succeeded to the throne.
Kou Xun's granddaughter was the wife of General Deng Zhao, so the Kou family was very successful during the Yongchu period of Emperor An.
Kou Xun's great-grandson Kou Rong.
summary: Kou Xun governed Runan, building schools and teaching the Spring and Autumn Annals. He pacified Yingchuan again when bandits rose, and the people begged for his continued service. He advised Guangwu against personally attacking Gaoping, but when the campaign stalled, he persuaded Gao Jun to surrender by executing his advisor. Kou Xun was known for his virtue, generosity, and learning, and was considered prime minister material. He died in the 12th year of Jianwu, posthumously titled Wei Hou. His descendants continued his legacy, and his family remained influential. The historian praised his ability to control his emotions and avoid grudges, likening him to Boyi and Shuqi.

translation:
◆Deng Biao's biography, Deng Biao's courtesy name was Zhibo, a native of Nanyang, the same clan as Taifu Deng Yuzhi, his father was Deng Han. In the early days of the Zhongxing Dynasty, he was granted the title of Marquis of Monument due to his meritorious service, and his official position was the Prefect of Bohai Sea.
When Deng Biao was young, he focused on inspiration and practicing filial piety.
After his father died, he left the country to his half-brother Jing Feng. Emperor Xianzong believed that his character was noble and he issued an edict to agree to it.
Deng Biao later served as an official in prefectures and counties, was promoted to the government, and moved to Guiyang for five years.
In the 17th year of Yongping's reign, he was recruited as a servant.
A few years later, his stepmother died and she left home due to illness. The imperial edict granted him the service of Guanglu Dafu. After completing his service, he was worshiped as the Captain of Fengche and promoted to Dasi Nong.
A few months later, he replaced Bao Yu as Taiwei.
When Deng Biao was in power, he was very clean and set an example for all officials.
After serving as an official for four years, he resigned due to illness.
In the first year of Yuanhe, he was dismissed from office, given 300,000 yuan as a gift, and lived with a salary of 2,000 dan for the rest of his life.
He also ordered Taichang to send the sacrificial meat from the ancestral temple in all seasons. The Cheng Cunwen of Yinpai County in Henan often sent sheep wine and other items on the first day of the eighth month.
Emperor He ascended the throne, appointed Deng Biao as Taifu, recorded the ministerial affairs, and granted him the title of Marquis of Guannei.
In the early years of Yongyuan, the Dou family was autocratic, arrogant and indulgent, and many people in the court criticized and disputed it. However, Deng Biao only cultivated himself in office and could not make any corrections.
He also once submitted a memorial to remove the censor Zhongcheng Zhou Yu. Zhou Yu failed to do so, so some people ridiculed him for this, but people at that time respected his courtesy.
When Dou was killed, Deng Biao returned to the cardinal position due to his old age and illness, and he was given permission to raise cattle and wine.
In the spring of the fifth year, he died in office, and the emperor came to his home to pay his respects.
◆Zhang Yu's biography, Zhang Yu's courtesy name was Boda, and he was a native of Zhao Guoxiang.
Grandfather Zhang Kuang's clan sister was the wife of Emperor Zukao. She traveled to Nanton many times and met Emperor Guangwu.
Guangwu was the Grand Sima and passed through Handan. Zhang Kuang was a county official and paid an audience with Guangwu.
Guangwu said happily: Now I have found my uncle!
So we went north together to Gaoyi, and used Kuang as the Yuan family order.
He was promoted to the governor of Zhuo County.
He also became the chief of Changshan Pass.
Just as the Red Eyebrow Army was attacking Guancheng, Zhang Kuang was killed.
His father, Zhang Xin, first fled for revenge. Later he became the Prime Minister of Huaiyang and died in the post of magistrate of Ji County.
Zhang Yu was honest and thrifty.
After his father's death, the officials in Ji County offered him millions in donations, but none of them were accepted.
He also gave the land and house to his uncle and stayed there by himself.
In the eighth year of Yongping, he was promoted to Xiaolian and promoted slightly. In the early years of Jianchu, he was appointed the governor of Yangzhou.
summary: **Deng Biao** (courtesy name Zhibo), a native of Nanyang and of the same clan as Taifu Deng Yuzhi, was the son of Deng Han. In the early Zhongxing Dynasty, he was made Marquis of Monument for his service and served as Prefect of Bohai Sea. Known for filial piety, he ceded his inheritance to his half-brother Jing Feng after his father's death, a decision Emperor Xianzong approved. He held various official posts, including Guiyang magistrate, and was recruited as a servant in Yongping's 17th year. After his stepmother's death, he served as Guanglu Dafu, then Fengche Captain and Dasi Nong, eventually replacing Bao Yu as Taiwei. Known for his integrity, he resigned due to illness after four years. In Yuanhe's first year, he was dismissed with a gift of 300,000 yuan and a lifelong salary of 2,000 dan. Emperor He later appointed him Taifu and Marquis of Guannei. During the Dou family's autocracy, he remained self-cultivating but made no corrections. He died in office in the spring of the fifth year, and the emperor visited his home. **Zhang Yu** (courtesy name Boda), from Zhao Guoxiang, was the grandson of Zhang Kuang, whose clan sister married Emperor Zukao. Zhang Kuang met Emperor Guangwu and served as Yuan family order, Zhuo County governor, and Changshan Pass chief, dying in battle against the Red Eyebrow Army. Zhang Yu's father, Zhang Xin, sought revenge and later became Prime Minister of Huaiyang. Zhang Yu was honest and thrifty, refusing donations after his father's death and giving his land to his uncle. Promoted to Xiaolian in Yongping's 8th year, he became Yangzhou governor in Jianchu's early years. He famously crossed the river despite fears of the god Zixu, personally interrogating prisoners and resolving cases. As Yanzhou governor, he gained a reputation for fairness. As Xiapi Prime Minister, he irrigated Puyangpo, reclaiming hundreds of hectares and attracting over a thousand poor households. He punished the powerful official Shi Dairun, earning respect. In Yongyuan's 6th year, he became Grand Sima and Taiwei, advising Emperor He against risky travel. Promoted to Taifu in Yanping's 1st year, he lived in the palace under Empress Dowager Deng's orders, advocating for allocating open lands to the poor. He served Emperor An, resigning several times but receiving gifts. He was made Marquis of Anxiang in Yongchu's 1st year. He advised the Empress Dowager to return to the palace during her mother's illness. After years of famine, he requested tax collection for relief. He was dismissed in the 5th year due to yin-yang disharmony and died at home seven years later.

translation:
In the first year of Yongchu, Zhang Yu was granted the title of Marquis of Anxiang due to his merits in making decisions, with a settlement of 1,200 households. He was granted the title on the same day as Taiwei Xu Fang and Sikong Yinqin.
In the autumn of this year, Xu Fang and Yin Qin were dismissed from their posts due to water and rain disasters by bandits. Zhang Yu felt uneasy and wrote a letter requesting to resign and be promoted to Taiwei.
Four years later, Queen Mother Deng's mother, Yinshi, fell ill, and the Queen Mother drove to her residence.
Zhang Yu, Situ Xiaqin, and Sikong Zhang Min all came forward and said: Mr. Xinye was uneasy and drove his car to stay at her place for several days. The ministers and others were very frightened.
I heard that when the king goes out, he must make arrangements first, and when he stays, he must be protected by the men of Drogo. He clears the road and then walks, cleans the house and then stays, and leaves the palace without staying overnight. In order to pay attention to the protection.
Your Majesty has a filial piety, and his kindness comes from the heart. When he is away for a long time, all the officials are exposed, and the deputies feel uneasy.
You should return to the palace temporarily, for the sake of the ancestral temple and the country at the top, and for the people of all nations at the bottom.
After three consecutive performances, he returned to the palace after struggling.
Later, there were successive years of famine and the government was empty. Zhang Yu asked to collect taxes for three years to help the county with food and loans.
The imperial edict allowed it.
Five years later, he was dismissed because of the disharmony between yin and yang.
Seven years later, he died at home.
The imperial court sent envoys to pay tribute.
In addition to his youngest son Zhang Yao, he was the doctor.
The eldest son Zhang Sheng was the heir.
◆Xu Fang's biography, Xu Fang's courtesy name is Ye Qing, and he is the best person in the state of Pei.
My grandfather Xu Xuan was a lecturer and taught Wang Mang the Book of Changes.
His father Xu Xian also taught Xu Xuan his career.
Xu Fang learned from his father and grandfather when he was young. During the Yongping period, he was promoted to Xiaolian and was promoted to Lang.
Xu Fang's physical appearance was reserved and serious, and his appearance was impressive. Xianzong thought it was very strange, and specially appointed him as Shangshulang.
The duty is to be in charge of secrets, to be carried out with thoroughness and prudence, to serve the two emperors without any fault.
During the reign of Emperor He, he was promoted to Sili Xiaowei and became the prefect of Wei County.
In the tenth year of Yongyuan's reign, he was promoted to Shaofu and DaSinong.
Xu Fang is diligent in political affairs and has made achievements in every position.
In the fourteenth year, he became Sikong.
Xu Fang believed that the "Five Classics" were ancient and difficult to understand the sacred meaning. Some explanations should be given to make it easier for future students to learn.
Shangshu Dao: I heard that "Poems", "Books", "Rites", and "Music" are all derived from Confucius, and the invention of chapters and sentences began with Zixia.
In the future, each analysis will give different opinions.
After the Han Dynasty succeeded the Qin Dynasty, the classics have been abolished. Only a few chapters of this text remain, and some have no chapters or sentences.
He sorted out the missing things, established the Ming Dynasty, studied Confucianism, and established the Imperial Academy.
summary: **Xu Fang** (courtesy name Yeqing), from Pei, learned from his father and grandfather, who taught Wang Mang the Book of Changes. Promoted to Xiaolian during Yongping, he became Shangshulang, serving two emperors without fault. Under Emperor He, he served as Sili Xiaowei, Wei County prefect, Shaofu, and DaSinong. In Yongyuan's 14th year, he became Sikong. He proposed reforming the examination system for doctors, advocating for testing based on famous scholars' chapters and verses to prevent private interests and disputes. His suggestions were followed. In the 16th year, he became Situ, then Taiwei in Yanping's 1st year, participating in Shangshu affairs with Taifu Zhang Yu. Emperor An made him Marquis of Longxiang. He was dismissed due to disasters and bandits, the first of the three ministers to be exempted. After his death, his son Xu Heng inherited, later passing the title to his brother Xu Chong.

translation:
Zhang Min went to Shudao again and said: "I have been favored and specially promoted. My foolish heart does not understand, my confusion does not understand, and I do not dare to agree with others' opinions casually."
I want to see Confucius hanging down the classics and Gao Tao making laws, and I can deduce that their original intention is to prevent the people from doing bad things.
Wonder what the "Insult" law would be used to prohibit?
It will definitely not make people not treat each other with contempt, but open the way to kill each other, and the officials who enforce the law will allow them to be treacherous.
Some commentators say: The common law should be discussed first.
I foolishly believe that in the nature of heaven and earth, only human beings are the most precious, and killing someone is punishable by death. This is the rule of the Three Generations.
Now I want to live, but instead open the way to death. If a person breaks the law and does not die, the whole world will suffer from him.
Ancient records say: One benefit can bring a hundred harms, so people go to the city walls.
Spring brings birth and autumn kills, the routine of heaven.
If something dies in spring, it is a disaster; if something blooms in autumn, it is a miracle.
The king inherits the heaven and the earth, follows the four seasons, takes the sages as the law, and takes the scriptures as the basis.
May your Majesty pay attention to the people below, consider the pros and cons, and let everyone comment on it, and the world will be very lucky.
He Di obeyed.
In the ninth year, Zhang Min was appointed as Sili Xiaowei.
Two years after taking office, he was promoted to the prefect of Runan.
Keep covenants clean and uncomplicated, use punishments fairly and upright, and be reasonable and reputable.
Later he was dismissed due to circumstances.
In the first year of Yanping, he was promoted to Yilang and then to the prefect of Yingchuan.
In the first year of Yongchu, he was recruited as Sikong, and he only served in accordance with the law.
After three years of service, he requested to retire due to illness. The emperor didn't listen.
In the spring of the sixth year, during the grand shooting ceremony, his companion suddenly fell down, and Cai Ce was dismissed.
He died at home due to serious illness.
◆Hu Guangchuan, courtesy name Boshi, was a native of Huarong, Nanjun.
Hu Gang, the sixth generation ancestor, was a man of high moral integrity and integrity.
During the reign of Emperor Ping, he was selected by the Great Situ Ma Palace.
When Wang Mang was regent, Hu Gang took off his clothes and hung up the door of the palace. Then he fled to Jiaochang and hid among the slaughterhouses.
Later, Wang Mang failed and returned to his hometown.
His father, Hu Gong, served as the commander-in-chief of Jiaozhi.
Hu Guang was lonely and poor when he was young and did housework by himself.
When he grew up, he followed his elders and joined the county as a casual official.
Fazhen, the son of the prefect Faxiong, came from home to visit his father.
The truth of the law is quite knowledgeable.
Faxiong ordered Fazhen to help him select talents when he was due to take the year-end exam.
Faxiong then held a meeting with all the officials, and Fazhen himself observed from the window, so he pointed Hu Guang to warn Faxiong and inspected his filial piety and integrity.
After arriving in the capital, he was tested by Zhang Zhi. Emperor An regarded Hu Guang as the best in the world.
In the tenth month, he was promoted to Shangshulang and was promoted to Shangshu Pushe five times.
summary: **Zhang Min** (courtesy name Boda), from Molan, Hejian, was promoted to Xiaolian in Jianchu's 2nd year. He opposed the "Insult Law," arguing it opened the way to killing and promoted sin. He cited Confucius and the Spring and Autumn Annals, advocating for removing complicated laws. Emperor He agreed. In the 9th year, he became Sili Xiaowei, then Runan prefect, known for fairness. After dismissal, he became Yilang and Yingchuan prefect in Yanping's 1st year. In Yongchu's 1st year, he was recruited as Sikong, serving according to law. He requested retirement due to illness but was refused. In the spring of the 6th year, he fell during a grand shooting ceremony and was dismissed, dying at home.

translation:
It is the most important thing to correct the situation, not to visit the Taiwan Affairs Bureau, and not to seek help from the ministers.
If the document is issued and the discussants have different views and disagree, it will be inconvenient for the court to exercise it. If they agree, the king's words have been fulfilled.
Chen Yu thought that we could declare hundreds of officials, refer to their similarities and differences, and then decide whether they would win or not, and take a detailed look at their core parts.
If you dare to tell nonsense and violate the heavenly prohibition, I hope your majesty will accept it.
The emperor did not listen.
At that time, Chenliu County was vacant, so Shangshu Shichang and others recommended Hu Guang.
The memorial said: I have heard that virtuous people are recognized by virtue, noble titles are used to build things, and outstanding trials are recognized by merit. It is praised in "Dian Mo" and has five chapters in five chapters. It is written by Tianzhi. Therefore, I will do my best to be loyal, the king will favor him, my actions will not lose virtue, and I will forget about his death.
Privately, I saw Hu Guang, the minister of public affairs, be true to the rules, modest and elegant, well-versed in knowledge, and thoroughly studied its principles. He read everything in the Six Classics and the old constitutions.
Be gentle but not guilty of injustice, be civilized and polite, be loyal, and worry about public affairs as well as home.
Don't praise your abilities, don't undervalue your efforts, be cautious and thoughtful, and behave without mistakes.
I have worked hard morning and night, for more than ten years, without caring about anything else, and with an unswerving ambition.
The ministers believed that Hu Guang worked hard for a long time in the position of minister. Later, when his mother was old, he was taken care of by Jianzhao.
Chen Liu was close to the county, and now the prefect is in vacancy.
Hu Guang has profound talents and is able to get rid of troubles. He is willing to participate in the election to correct the decadent customs, make people practice good and encourage them.
Hu Guang stayed in power for ten years and became the prefect of Jiyin. He was dismissed for making false promises in appointing officials.
He also became the prefect of Runan and went to worship Da Sinong.
In the first year of Han'an, he was promoted to Situ.
After the death of Emperor Zhi, he took Li Gu's place as Taiwei and recorded the affairs of the minister.
Because of his decision, he established Emperor Huan and was granted the title of Marquis of Yuyang Anle Township.
Abdicated due to illness.
He paid homage to Sikong and returned home.
Soon after, he summoned Taichang to pay homage to Taichang and was promoted to Taiwei. He was dismissed due to the solar eclipse.
Return to Tai Chang and pay homage to the Taiwei.
In the second year of Yanxi, General Liang Ji was killed. Hu Guang, Situ Han Jinyin, and Sikong Sunlang committed the crime of not guarding the palace. They were all reduced to one level of death, seized the title, and were dismissed as commoners.
Later, he paid homage to Taizhong Dafu and Taichang.
In the ninth year, he worshiped Situ again.
Emperor Ling came to the throne, and together with Taifu Chen Fan, he recorded the affairs of the ministers and restored the title of his homeland.
Requested to retire due to illness.
When Chen Fan was killed, he took over as Taifu, and the general record remained the same.
summary: **Hu Guang** (courtesy name Boshi), from Huarong, Nanjun, was a descendant of the virtuous Hu Gang. Orphaned and poor, he worked as a casual official. Recommended by Fazhen, he was tested by Zhang Zhi and deemed the best in the world by Emperor An. He became Shangshulang and Shangshu Pushe. He advised Emperor Shun against drawing lots to choose a queen, advocating for selecting based on virtue, age, and appearance. He opposed Zuo Xiong's proposal to set a minimum age of 40 for officials, arguing for flexibility based on talent. He served as Chenliu prefect, Jiyin prefect, Runan prefect, and Da Sinong. In Han'an's 1st year, he became Situ, then Taiwei, establishing Emperor Huan and becoming Marquis of Yuyang Anle Township. He served multiple terms, including as Sikong and Taiwei, but was dismissed after Liang Ji's death. He later served under Emperor Ling as Taifu. Known for his gentle and discreet nature, he mastered court rules and was praised in the capital: "Ignore everything and ask Bo Shi, there is only Hu Gong among the mediocre." He served six emperors for over 30 years, holding high offices repeatedly. He died at 82 in Xiping's 1st year, receiving grand honors. He also compiled the "Baiguan Zhen" and other works. Emperor Ling later had his portrait painted in the province.

translation:
◆The Legend of Lang Yi
Lang Yi, courtesy name Yaguang, was born in Anqiu, Beihai.
His father, Langzong, whose courtesy name was Zhongsui, studied "Jing's Book of Changes" and was good at wind angle, astrology, and six-day and seven-minute calculations. He could tell the weather about good and bad luck, and he often sold divination to support himself.
Emperor An summoned him, and his countermeasures set an example for other Confucian scholars. Later, he became the magistrate of Wu County.
At this time, there was a sudden storm, and Lang Zong learned from divination that there was going to be a fire in the capital. He noted the time and sent someone to inquire, and it was indeed as he said.
After hearing this, all the princes went up to the table to hear the news, and the imperial court summoned him with a doctor.
Lang Zong thought it was shameful to be known for his fortune-telling. When he heard that the summons had arrived, he hung his seal and ribbon in the county court at night and fled, so he never served as an official for the rest of his life.
When he was young, Lang Yi passed on his father's studies and learned the classics. He lived in seclusion by the sea and often taught hundreds of disciples.
During the day, he studies the essence and at night, he divines the images. He meditates diligently and is tireless in the morning and evening.
The prefectures and counties appointed him to be a man of integrity and uprightness, but he did not go to the post.
During the reign of Emperor Shun, disasters occurred many times. In the first month of the second year of Yangjia, when public transport was called for, Lang Yi went to the court to pay homage and wrote a memorial: I heard that monsters descended from the sky and disaster talismans appeared on the earth, in order to condemn the masters, to punish the people, to cultivate virtues, to balance the good opportunities, and to promote the government.
"Yi Neizhuan" says: All disasters and disasters are caused by different things, and everyone has their own governance.
Change it and eliminate it, eliminate it and eliminate it.
Thinking of His Majesty personally attending to the affairs of state every day, I should review Zengzi's three self-examinations, reflect on my faults and blame, and make sure to eliminate my great regrets.
The current custom is one of luxury and licentiousness, and shallow kindness and righteousness.
To save extravagance, one must be frugal. To save the poor, it is better to be generous. To appease the superiors and straighten the people, there is nothing better than using propriety.
When it comes to cultivating etiquette and abiding by promises, only the top takes the lead; changing the rules does not matter to the bottom.
Therefore, the virtues of "Zhou Nan" and "Guan Sui" are the foundation of politics.
The root is rooted in the Tao, and when the wind moves, the grass will follow. If the source of water is clarified, the running water will be clear. If the root is muddied, the end will be turbid.
The way of heaven and earth is similar to that of drums and drums. It takes emptiness as its virtue and moves from near to far.
I have seen that in the past few years, disasters have occurred in the garden and mausoleum several times, and the fire has been very strong, alarming the gods.
"Yi Tianren Ying" said: A gentleman does not think about following the interests, so he is said to be without benefits, and his palace will be burned down by evil.
He also said: In Jun Gaotai Mansion, Yin invades Yang and causes fire.
He also said: If you are not frugal at the top and unscrupulous at the bottom, the fire will burn down your house.
Recently, Xiyuan has been managed, the Imperial College has been restored, many palaces and government buildings have been built.
In the past, Pan Geng moved to Yin to avoid luxury, that is, to be frugal. After Xia, he humbled his family and tried his best to achieve beauty.
Also, when the people of Lu were the governor, Min Ziqian said: "It's still the same, so why change it?"
I think these repairs can be done with frugality, and the warehouses can be used to help the poor, orphans and widows. This is God's will, people's happiness, the foundation of benevolence, and the essence of frugality.
How can anyone support people according to nature, be benevolent and frugal, and not bless them?
summary: Lang Yi, courtesy name Yaguang, was born in Anqiu, Beihai. His father, Lang Zong, studied the "Jing's Book of Changes," excelled in divination and astrology, and supported himself by fortune-telling. Emperor An summoned him, and his responses set a standard for Confucian scholars. He later became magistrate of Wu County, where he accurately predicted a fire in the capital through divination. The imperial court summoned him with a doctor's title, but Lang Zong, ashamed of being known for fortune-telling, fled by night, hanging his seal in the county court, and never served as an official again. Lang Yi inherited his father's studies, lived in seclusion by the sea, and taught hundreds of disciples. During Emperor Shun's reign, disasters occurred frequently. In the first month of the second year of Yangjia, Lang Yi was summoned to court. He submitted a memorial attributing disasters to the ruler's governance, urging the emperor to practice frugality, reflect on faults, and reform policies. He warned that luxury, excessive construction, and harsh punishments caused celestial anomalies like prolonged cloudiness, cold spells, and fires. He cited classical texts to argue that the emperor should reduce palace expenditures, release palace maids to restore harmony, and dismiss incompetent officials. He also predicted earthquakes, floods, and invasions if reforms were not enacted.

translation:
The king follows the will of God, which is like changing his color from blue to red from spring to summer.
It has been exactly three hundred years since Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty reduced corporal punishment, and minor prohibitions have gradually accumulated.
The king's law is like a river, which should be easy for people to avoid but difficult to violate.
Therefore, the "Book of Changes" says: If it is easy, it is easy to know; if it is simple, it is easy to follow; if it is simple, it is easy to understand the principles of the world.
Now let go of extravagance, start being frugal, be the first in the world, change your name, and use whatever you call me.
"The Book of Changes" says: "The way of a gentleman may come from another place, return to the same place by different paths, and have the same purpose."
This means knowing that changing from normal to good can eliminate disasters, and changing from normal to evil will inevitably lead to disaster.
This year is in the middle of the year, next year the season is in the middle, and the season is in the middle of the end. The calendar fortune has changed, so the yuan can be changed. This is the way of heaven.
I am too ignorant to answer the sage question.
Lang Yi also wrote a letter recommending Huang Qiong and Li Gu, and stated the methods to eliminate disasters: The seven things I answered correctly before are all urgent political matters, meet the current needs, and should be implemented.
Indeed, I knew that I had a foolish and shallow view, which was not in line with the emperor's holy hearing. I was a mean person and should be punished for my bad words. I was very frightened and did not know where to put my body. I heard that the purpose of carving boats and oars is to cross the rivers and seas, and to recruit talents and assistants to stabilize the world.
In ancient times, when Yao of the Tang Dynasty was in power, his ministers worked for him and cultivated virtues in civil and military affairs. The Duke of Zhou and Duke of Zhao served as assistants. Therefore, they were able to build the heaven and earth and increase the brilliance of the sun and the moon.
"The Book of Songs" says: Zhongshan is the one who will lead the illustrious king's order. If the country is not good, Zhongshan will be the one who makes it clear.
King Xuan of Zhou relied on Zhongshanfu, which led to a harmonious situation.
Since your Majesty came to the throne, you have been diligent in the administration of common people, but the positions of the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers have not been seen. Therefore, disasters have occurred one after another, and the countries in the four directions have no peace.
I have examined the canons of the country and verified what I have seen and heard. It is found that if you gain wise men, you will achieve meritorious service, and if you lose wise men, you will fail.
Moreover, whether a wise man comes out or not, he flies like a bird and then gathers, and he is given a title according to virtue, so he is unscrupulous, and then makes the gentleman feel ashamed of poverty and lowliness, but takes pleasure in wealth.
If one's virtues are not rewarded, if one's words are not rewarded, if one comes and there is no reward, and if one enters and there is no hope, then all the wise men will return to the swamp and cultivate their old ambitions.
Those who seek virtue should adhere to God's will at the top, and obey the human heart at the bottom.
Not using it would be against heaven's order and contrary to human expectations.
If it goes against the order of heaven, disaster will happen; if it goes against the wishes of others, it will be ruined.
When a disaster comes, the people below will cry out with resentment. If the weather is not good enough, the ruler will suffer losses.
The "Four Beginnings" in the "Book of Songs" were depleted and the "Five Worlds" were devastated. This is where the fault lies.
Isn’t it possible to be strong and solid, cautious and cautious, and to abide by the great cause of heavenly merit and virtue? The ministers saw Jiangxia Huangqiong, the Guanglu doctor, who was deeply in love with Taoism. He advocated purity and naturalness. He was dressed in coarse cloth and carried precious jade. He had a deep understanding of the classics, was bold in politics, and knew the art of eliminating variation and recovery.
summary: In a dialogue with the minister, Lang Yi elaborated on seven urgent matters: cemetery fires due to extravagance, hypocritical officials causing yin-yang imbalances, impending droughts and floods, the need to establish an heir, white rainbow portending coups, and the necessity to change the calendar and official titles. He recommended recruiting virtuous men like Huang Qiong and Li Gu to stabilize the state. Despite his detailed warnings, Lang Yi resigned from his appointed doctor position and returned home. His predictions of earthquakes, droughts, and barbarian invasions later proved accurate. He was eventually killed by a local knight-errant, Sun Li.

translation:
Your Majesty should review the situation of the Mingtang administration in detail, and then the evil will be eliminated, and the five latitudes will be able to operate in order. The fourth thing: "Yi Zhuan" says: If Yang has no virtue, there will be drought, and if Yin submerges Yang, there will be drought.
Yang has no virtue, which means that the king's kindness is not extended to the people.
The yin subsides and the yang lurks, and the salary goes to the public office, which means that the subordinates have exclusive power.
From winter to spring, there has been no Jiaze, and there have been several westerly winds, which violates the seasonal regulations.
The court worked hard, prayed widely, paid homage to the mountains and rivers, and the dragon moved to the city.
I have heard that the emperor and heaven move all things, and do not act in vain. Catastrophes respond to people. The important thing is to blame yourself.
If the rain can fall and the water can stop, then the years will not be separated and the year of peace can wait and come.
However, the disaster does not stop, it can be seen that the problem is not here.
Since the beginning of spring, I have not seen the imperial court appreciating meritorious people, commending virtuous people, caring for orphans and widows, or providing relief to the poor and weak. I have only seen Luoyang officials rushing from east to west, collecting minor crimes, and filling the prisons with prisoners.
I heard that the fire in Gongling continued to shine, indicating that it was a natural disaster and not a human fault.
Ding Chou sent out a strong wind, covering the heaven and earth.
The wind is a command, and the expression of heaven's majesty and anger is used to inspire people to be loyal and honest.
Another month without rain will harm Sumai. If there is no harvest, then three or four out of ten people will be hungry. Your Majesty should indeed be favored widely in response to your heavenly merit. If the minister's words are not adopted and the government is not reformed, there will be some rain after the beginning of summer, and there will be no hope now.
If the government is reformed but it still does not rain, then the minister is falsely accused, stupid and ignorant of his weight, and should be punished.
The book was sent up, and he was specially ordered to be appointed as a doctor. Lang Yi resigned from his illness and refused to take up his post, so he went home immediately.
In April, there was an earthquake in the capital and it fell.
There was a severe drought this summer.
In autumn, the Xianbei people invaded Mayi City and defeated the troops of Dai County.
The next year, the Western Qiang invaded Longyou.
It's all roughly as Lang Yi said.
Later, the court officials summoned him in a bus, but he refused to come out.
Sun Li, a native of the same county, was evil and violent, and liked knight-errants. People in his hometown often envied Lang Yi's reputation and wanted to be friendly with him.
Lang Yi ignored them and became enemies, so Lang Yi was killed by Sun Li.
◆Xiangkai Chuan Xiangkai was named Gongju and was from Xiyin, Pingyuan.
He is good at learning, has extensive knowledge of ancient books, and knows the art of astronomy and yin and yang.
During the reign of Emperor Huan, the eunuchs monopolized the affairs of the state, and brutal punishments were rampant. Princes also died one after another, and disasters were particularly common.
In the ninth year of Yanxi's reign, Xiangkai left home and went to the court to preach: I heard that the emperor did not speak, so he used astronomical pictograms to teach.
summary: Xiang Kai, courtesy name Gongju, was from Xiyin, Pingyuan. During Emperor Huan's reign, eunuchs dominated, punishments were brutal, and disasters were frequent. In the ninth year of Yanxi, Xiang Kai submitted a memorial citing astronomical anomalies—Mars and Venus invading key stars—as warnings against harsh rule and unjust executions. He criticized the killing of loyal officials like Li Yun and Du Zhong, the neglect of heirs due to excessive palace maids, and the decline of education. He noted omens like a dead dragon and falling stars, linking them to past dynastic collapses. He urged the emperor to reform punishments, release prisoners, and promote virtue.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/郎顗襄楷列传下

translation:
Xiangkai is not correct in his rhetoric, pointing out the important affairs of the country, but breaking the law with analysis, violating the classics and art, using the stars and gods, falsely entrusting gods, creating personal agendas, and slandering the Holy One for neglecting state affairs. Please hand it over to Sili, and he will be imprisoned in Luoyang Prison for the crime of Zhengkai.
The emperor believed that although Xiangkai's words were passionate, they were all astronomical and constant phenomena, so he was not killed, but was handed over to the commander of the army for deliberation.
At the beginning, during the reign of Emperor Shun, Langfu Palace Chong came to the court and presented one hundred and seventy volumes of sacred books that his master Ganji had obtained in the Quyang Spring. They were all written in white, with Zhu Jieqing's head and eyes, and they were called "Taiping Qingling Shu".
His language is based on yin and yang and the five elements, and is mostly based on shamanism and miscellaneous language.
One official reported that the book written by Gong Chong was monstrous and unreliable, so he kept it.
Later Zhang Jiao had his own writings.
When Emperor Ling came to the throne, he believed that Xiangkai's book was correct.
Grand Tutor Chen Fan appointed him as Founder, but he did not take up the post.
Whenever the governor of the village comes to take office, he always greets him with courtesy.
During the Zhongping period, both Xun Shuang and Zheng Xuan were recruited as doctors, but they did not go and died at home.
summary: Emperor Huan initially ignored Xiang Kai's reports. When summoned, Xiang Kai condemned eunuchs, stating their proliferation caused the lack of an heir. The minister of corrections accused him of slander, but the emperor spared him, citing the astronomical basis of his words. Xiang Kai later refused official posts, including one offered by Grand Tutor Chen Fan, and died at home during the Zhongping period.

translation:
◆Zheng Taichuan, also named Gongye, was born in Kaifeng, Henan. The great-grandson of Sinong Zheng Zhong.
He was talented when he was young. In the last years of Emperor Ling's reign, Mrs. Zheng knew that the world would be in chaos, so she secretly made friends with heroes.
His family was very wealthy, with 400 hectares of land, but he often had no food to eat. He was very famous, and everyone in Shandong knew about him.
At the beginning, he was promoted to Xiaolian, and he was recruited from the three government offices and buses, but he was not accepted.
After the general He Jin assisted in the administration, he recruited famous people and appointed Zheng Gongye as the Minister of the Secretariat and promoted to the Censor.
He Jin was preparing to kill the eunuchs and wanted to recruit Dong Zhuo, the governor of Bingzhou, as his assistant.
Zheng Gongye said to He Jin: Dong Zhuo is violent, cruel, unloyal, and very ambitious.
If you lend him the government affairs and grant him important tasks, you will be able to fulfill your evil desires and endanger the court.
With your important position as a pro-German, you have the authority to guide the emperor and preside over state affairs. Chengyi is arbitrary and punishes the guilty, so he really shouldn't use Dong Zhuo's power as a back-up.
And things change over time, and lessons are never far away.
Why enter Chen's top priority?
He Jin couldn't use it, so he abandoned his official position and left.
He said to Xun You, a native of Yingchuan: Mr. He is not easy to help.
He Jin was soon killed, and Dong Zhuo indeed rebelled.
Zheng Gongye and others, together with his servant Wu Qiong and Dong Zhuo's chief historian He, jointly talked about Dong Zhuo and appointed Yuan Shao as the prefect of Bohai to carry out Shandong's plan.
When the rebels arose, Dong Zhuo convened a discussion with the ministers and sent out a large army to attack the rebels. All the officials did not dare to violate Dong Zhuo's will.
Zheng Gongye was worried that if Dong Zhuo had more soldiers, he would become more arrogant and vicious and difficult to control. He said: "Ruling a country depends on virtue, not on having many soldiers."
Dong Zhuo was unhappy and said: According to what you say, soldiers are useless?
Zheng Gongye became frightened, so he made up a lie and said to Dong Zhuo: "I'm not saying that soldiers are useless, I just mean that Shandong doesn't have enough soldiers."
If you don't believe it, I can give you a rough idea.
Now Shandong is colluding, the states and counties are connected, and the people are united, it cannot be said that it is not strong. However, since Guangwu, the country has been safe and sound, the people have lived a prosperous life, and have long forgotten about the war.
Confucius said: To teach the people to fight without educating them is to abandon the people.
Therefore, although there are many of them, they are not enough to cause harm. This is one thing.
You were born in Xizhou and became a general of the country at a young age. You are familiar with military affairs and have participated in many battles. You are famous in the world. Everyone is afraid of you and obeys you. These are two.
Zhang Mengzhuo is a loyal elder in Dongping, and he doesn't look around.
Kong Gongxu was a clear talker, impartial and impartial.
These people have no military talent or experience in fighting. They are not your opponents in a decisive battle. This is three.
Talents in Shandong are never brave.
We don't have the bravery of Meng Ben, the agility of Qingji, the solid defense of Liaocheng, or the strategies of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping.
summary: **Zheng Taichuan (Zheng Gongye)** was born in Kaifeng, Henan, as the great-grandson of Sinong Zheng Zhong. Talented from youth, his mother foresaw chaos in the final years of Emperor Ling's reign and secretly befriended heroes. Despite owning 400 hectares of land, he often lacked food. He was renowned throughout Shandong. Initially recommended for office, he declined multiple appointments. When General He Jin recruited him as Minister of the Secretariat and Censor, Zheng warned against recruiting Dong Zhuo, predicting his violent ambition would endanger the court. He Jin ignored this advice, so Zheng resigned. After He Jin was killed and Dong Zhuo rebelled, Zheng conspired with others to oppose Dong Zhuo. When Dong Zhuo wanted to attack the rebels, Zheng argued that governing depends on virtue, not military might. Fearing Dong Zhuo's anger, he fabricated a flattering analysis listing ten reasons why Dong Zhuo would defeat the rebels. Dong Zhuo appointed him general, but others warned of Zheng's cunning, so Dong Zhuo revoked the command. Zheng later plotted to kill Dong Zhuo, but the plan leaked. He escaped to Yuan Shu, who appointed him Governor of Yangzhou, but he died en route at age forty-one.
rel_path: 后汉书/列传/郑孔荀列传

translation:
When He Jin, Yin of Henan Province, was to be promoted to general, Yang Ci sent Kong Rong to congratulate He Jin with his business card. However, without informing him in time, Kong Rong took the invitation back to the palace and went back home, blaming himself.
The officials of Henan Yin thought they had lost face and sent private swordsmen to hunt down Kong Rong. A visitor said to He Jin: Kong Wenju has a great reputation. If the general has a grudge with him, people from all over the world will follow him and flee.
It is better to treat him with courtesy and let everyone in the world know that the general has a broad mind.
He Jin thought it was right, and after being appointed as a general, he conquered Kong Rong, promoted him to a high rank, and became the imperial censor.
Because he was at odds with Zhongcheng Zhao She, he returned home due to illness.
Later he was conscripted as Sikong Peng and awarded the title of Military Marquis.
After three days in office, he was promoted to General of Tiger and Lieutenant Commander.
When Dong Zhuo deposed the Young Emperor and established the Xian Emperor, Kong Rong often corrected his mistakes when answering questions. Therefore, he violated Dong Zhuo's wishes and was transferred to Yilang.
At that time, the Yellow Turbans invaded several states, and Beihai was the place where thieves attacked the most. Dong Zhuo then signaled the three governments to jointly appoint Kong Rong as the Prime Minister of Beihai.
Kong Rong went to the county, summoned the soldiers and people, raised troops and taught martial arts. He not only issued proclamations, but also wrote letters himself, communicating with the prefectures and counties, and planning together.
The thief Zhang Rao and other 200,000 people returned from Jizhou. Kong Rong faced him and was defeated by Zhang Rao. So he gathered scattered soldiers to defend Zhuxu County.
Then he slowly gathered more than 40,000 officials and people, men and women who had been misled by the Yellow Turban, and built cities and schools, praised Confucianism, and recommended virtuous people such as Zheng Xuan, Peng Chu, and Bing Yuan.
Zhen Ziran, a county native, was famous in Linxiaocun. He died young. Kong Rong regretted not seeing him. Ordered to distribute food to the county society.
Even if the others have only a small amount of good deeds, they will not be treated with courtesy.
County residents who had no descendants and travelers from all over the country who died were buried in coffins.
At this time, the Yellow Turbans invaded again. Kong Rong then went to Duchang County and was surrounded by the thief Guan Hai.
Kong Rong was in great danger and sent Donglai Taishi Ci to ask for help from Pingyuan Prime Minister Liu Bei.
Liu Bei said in surprise: Kong Beihai actually knew that there was another Liu Bei in the world.
Three thousand soldiers were immediately sent to rescue him, but the thief escaped because he was scattered.
At that time, Yuan Shao and Cao Cao were very powerful, and Kong Rong did not rely on anyone.
Zuo Chengzu was rich in strategy and advised Kong Rong to join forces with Cao Cao and Yuan Shao.
Kong Rong knew that Yuan Shao and Cao Cao were ultimately trying to usurp the Han Dynasty, and he didn't want to get involved with them, so he killed Zuo Chengzu in a rage.
Kong Rong himself thought that he had a noble spirit and was determined to quell the country's crisis, but he failed because of his limited talents and empty ideas.
After six years in the county, Liu Bei recommended him to concurrently serve as the governor of Qingzhou.
In the first year of Jian'an, he was attacked by Yuan Tan. From spring to summer, there were only a few hundred soldiers left. Arrows came like rain, and the city was already in close combat.
Kong Rong could read a few books and talk and laugh freely.
The city fell at night and he fled to Shandong. His wife was captured by Yuan Tan.
When Emperor Xian arrived, he made Xuchang his capital and recruited Kong Rong as a general to be a great craftsman and promoted to Shaofu.
Every time the emperor visited and summoned his ministers, Kong Rong often made decisions, and the ministers and officials were just in name. In the past, Taifu Ma Rishi was sent to Shandong as an envoy to Huainan. He was dissatisfied with Yuan Shu many times. Yuan Shu despised him, insulted him, and took away his talisman. Ma Rishidan was so worried and angry that he vomited blood and died. Ma Rishidan's funeral was returned to the capital, and the court wanted to arrange a funeral ceremony. Kong Rong said: Ma Rishidan was ordered to handle local affairs directly by relying on his noble status as a prince and the integrity of the emperor. He calmed down Dongxia and even flattered a traitor. He was instigated by him. Ma Rishidan was the first to sign and sign the articles. Relying on subordinates, deceiving the court, and serving the emperor treacherously.
In the past, the state assisted the enemy Jin army and was not convinced. Yi Liao's expression did not change in front of the shining white sword.
summary: **Kong Rong**, a descendant of Confucius, showed exceptional intelligence as a child. At ten, he cleverly gained an audience with Li Ying by claiming family friendship through Confucius and Laozi. When Chen Wei dismissed him, Kong retorted sharply. At thirteen, his father's death caused such grief he needed support to stand. At sixteen, he sheltered the fugitive Zhang Jian, leading to his brother's execution when the family competed to take blame. Kong Rong became famous and was recruited as an official. He criticized corrupt eunuch relatives, offended He Jin, and later opposed Dong Zhuo's deposition of the Young Emperor. Dong Zhuo sent him to troubled Beihai as punishment. There, Kong Rong built cities, schools, promoted Confucianism, and recommended worthy men. When surrounded by Yellow Turban rebels, Liu Bei rescued him, amazed that Kong Rong knew of him. Kong Rong refused to ally with Yuan Shao or Cao Cao, knowing they would usurp the Han. After six years, Liu Bei recommended him as Qingzhou governor. Yuan Tan attacked; though outnumbered, Kong Rong remained calm, reading and laughing until the city fell. He fled, but his wife was captured. Later serving Emperor Xian, Kong Rong often made court decisions. He opposed corporal punishment, argued against publicizing Liu Biao's treason, and criticized Cao Cao's massacre of Yecheng and his son's marriage to Yuan Xi's wife. He mocked Cao Cao's campaigns and opposed his alcohol ban. Cao Cao, though outwardly tolerant, grew jealous. Eventually, Cao Cao had Kong Rong executed for treason at fifty-six. His children were also killed; his seven-year-old daughter and nine-year-old son calmly accepted death, saying a destroyed nest cannot have unbroken eggs.

translation:
As for Kong Wenju's noble aspirations and frank feelings, they can definitely inspire loyalty and resist the treacherous heart.
Therefore, when Cao Cao was alive, he did not dare to usurp the Han Dynasty, but it was Cao Pi who succeeded the Han Dynasty after his death.
Strict qi and righteousness are nothing more than overturning and destroying.
Is it possible to live a life of humiliation and compromise? Strict and neat, bright and white, Kong Rong's quality can be compared with that of white jade and autumn frost!
◆Xun Yu's biography, Xun Yu's courtesy name Wenruo, was born in Yingyin, Yingchuan, and was the grandson of Xun Shu, the magistrate of Langling County.
His father, Xun Nu, served as Prime Minister of Jinan.
Xun Yu was afraid of eunuchs, so he married Xun Yu's daughter to Tang Heng, the official minister of the imperial court.
Xun Yu was saved from being ridiculed because he was famous for his talent at a young age.
He Yong from Nanyang claimed to be able to understand people. When he saw Xun Yu, he thought he was extraordinary and said: "This is the talent of the emperor's assistant."
In the sixth year of Zhongping, he was recommended as Xiaolian and appointed as the magistrate of Kangfu County.
When Dong Zhuo rebelled, he abandoned his official position and returned to his hometown.
Han Rong from the same county took more than a thousand members of his clan to escape the chaos in the western mountains of Mi County.
Xun Yu said to his elders: Yingchuan is a place where war must pass.
When the world changes, it is often the place where troops are needed.
Although Mi County is somewhat safe, it is not enough to withstand a major disaster. You should leave here as soon as possible.
Most of the fellow countrymen are nostalgic for their homeland and are unwilling to leave.
When Han Fu, a fellow herdsman from Jizhou, sent cavalry to pick them up, Xun Yu led his clan to follow Han Fu. Most of the people he left behind were later killed and robbed by Dong Zhuo's general Li Jue.
By the time Xun Yu arrived in Jizhou, Yuan Shao had already usurped Han Fu's position. Yuan Shao treated Xun Yu like a distinguished guest.
Xun Yu was a well-informed person. Seeing the chaos in the Han Dynasty, he always wanted to correct things.
At that time, Cao Cao was in Dongjun. Xun Yu heard that Cao Cao was talented and strategist, but he estimated that Yuan Shao would not be able to achieve great things in the end.
In the second year of Chuping, he left Yuan Shao and went to Cao Cao.
Cao Cao was overjoyed after talking to him and said: "This is my Zhang Liang."
He was appointed Fenwu Sima when he was twenty-nine years old.
The next year, he was appointed Sima of Zhendong.
In the first year of Xingping, Cao Cao attacked Tao Qian in the east and sent Xun Yu to guard Zhen City to take charge of the affairs left behind.
He caught up with Zhang Miao and Chen Gong and took Yanzhou to rebel against Cao Cao, and secretly welcomed Lu Bu.
After Lu Bu arrived, all cities responded.
Zhang Miao sent someone to deceive Xun Yu and said: General Lu came to help Cao Shijun defeat Tao Qian, so we should quickly supply him with military supplies.
Xun Yu knew that Zhang Miao had changed, so he deployed troops to fortify Zhang Miao's plan. Therefore, Zhang Miao's plan could not succeed.
Guo Gong, the governor of Yuzhou, led tens of thousands of troops to the city and asked to see Xun Yu.
Xun Yu was about to go, but Xiahou Dun, the prefect of Dongjun, and others stopped him, saying: "How do you know that Guo Gong is not conspiring with Lu Bu and meets him rashly?"
summary: **Xun Yu**, grandson of Magistrate Xun Shu, was recognized as extraordinary by He Yong. Recommended as Xiaolian, he abandoned office when Dong Zhuo rebelled. He warned his clan to flee Yingchuan, predicting war; those who stayed were later killed. He joined Yuan Shao but, seeing the Han's chaos, left for Cao Cao, who called him "my Zhang Liang." When Zhang Miao and Chen Gong rebelled, Xun Yu defended Zhen City, outsmarting their deception and personally meeting Guo Gong to prevent his alliance with rebels. He secured three cities for Cao Cao's return. Xun Yu advised Cao Cao to stabilize Yanzhou before attacking Xuzhou, leading to Lu Bu's defeat. He urged Cao Cao to welcome Emperor Xian to Xuchang, arguing this would bring legitimacy. Xun Yu recommended talented men like Xun You, Zhong Yao, and Guo Jia. He predicted Yuan Shao's defeat despite his strength, correctly assessing his generals' weaknesses. During the Guandu stalemate, when Cao Cao wanted to retreat, Xun Yu insisted on holding position, leading to Yuan Shao's defeat. He advised against attacking Liu Biao before pacifying Yuan Shao's remnants. When Cao Cao wanted to restore the ancient Jiuzhou system, Xun Yu warned it would cause panic, and Cao Cao abandoned the plan. Cao Cao praised Xun Yu's strategies as turning defeat into victory. When Dong Zhao proposed making Cao Cao Duke of Jin, Xun Yu opposed it, saying Cao Cao should remain loyal to Han. Cao Cao grew resentful. During a southern campaign, Cao Cao kept Xun Yu at his camp, then sent him an empty food box. Xun Yu took poison and died at fifty. The next year, Cao Cao declared himself Duke of Wei.

translation:
◆Zheng Xingzhuan, Zheng Xing, courtesy name Shaogan, was born in Kaifeng, Henan.
He studied "Gongyang Chunqiu" when he was young, and "Zuo Shi Zhuan" in his later years. He accumulated knowledge, thought deeply, and understood the gist of the book. All his classmates regarded Zheng as their teacher.
During the Tianfeng period, he led his students to teach Liu Xin the meaning of "Zuo Shi Zhuan". Liu Xin praised Zheng Xing's talent and asked Zheng Xing to write regulations, chapters, exegesis, and correct "Santong Li".
When Gengshi came to the throne, he appointed Si Zhi Li Song as acting prime minister and entered Chang'an first. Li Song appointed Zheng Xing as chief historian and sent him back to pick up the emperor and move the capital.
Some of the generals in Gengshi were from Shandong, and they all advised him to stay in Luoyang.
Zheng Xing advised the emperor: Your Majesty raised troops from Jingchu, and the government had not yet been implemented. Once the country was established, the heroes of Shanxi were vying to kill Wang Mang, and opened the door to welcome Your Majesty in the suburbs. What was the purpose?
This is because the people of the world were suffering from Wang Mang's tyranny and missed the old virtues of Han Emperor Gaozu.
If you don't appease the people for a long time now, I'm afraid that the people will be alienated and thieves will rise again.
"Spring and Autumn" records that Duke Huan of Qi ascended the throne as "Qi Xiaobai enters Qi", but is not called Qi Hou because he has not yet gone to the temple to worship his ancestors.
Those who are discussing now want to pacify Chimei first and then enter the pass. They do not know the root and fight for the ends. I am afraid that the country's guards will be transferred to Hangu Pass. Even if they sleep in Luoyang, how can they be content with pillow mats?
Emperor Gengshi said: I have made up my mind to go west.
He worshiped Zheng Xing as an admonishment official and sent him to gather in Guanxi, Shuofang, Liangzhou and Yizhou. After returning, he worshiped him as the governor of Liangzhou.
It happened that someone rebelled in Tianshui and attacked and killed the county guard. Zheng Xing was dismissed from his post.
At that time, Chimei entered the pass and the road to the east was blocked, so Zheng Xing went west to join Kaixiao. Weixiao humbly invited Zheng with courtesy, but Zheng Xing felt aggrieved and said he could not afford to be ill.
Wei Xiao boasted about himself and often compared himself to King Wen of Zhou, so he discussed with the generals and established himself as king.
When Zheng Xing heard about it, he dissuaded Wei Xiao and said: "Spring and Autumn" legend: It is called deafness if the mouth does not speak the words of loyalty, and the ear does not hear the sum of the five tones.

Others with professional expertise were promoted and hired.

At first, Zhang Ba thought that Fan Min had deleted and edited "Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals" and there were many complicated words, so he reduced it to 200,000 words and changed its name to "Zhang's Studies".
Zhang Ba began to go to Vietnam, but the thieves had not been eliminated and the county was uneasy, so Zhang Ba issued an official document offering a reward. If he used it faithfully, the thieves would surrender without bothering the soldiers.
The nursery rhyme goes: Abandon me Drogo, donate my spear, all thieves will be gone, all officials will be put to rest.
In the third year of his service, Zhang told the official: "The prefect was born as an orphan and became a county governor."
Generally, when the sun is in the middle, it will be tilted, and when the moon is full, there will be losses.
Lao Tzu has a saying: Contentment is not humiliating.

summary: Zhang Ba, courtesy name Bo Rao, was from Chengdu, Shu County. Known for filial piety and humility from childhood, he was called Zhang Zengzi by villagers. He studied "Yanshi Gongyang Chunqiu" and extensively read the "Five Classics." During Yongyuan, he became prefect of Kuaiji, where he promoted talented individuals and encouraged moral cultivation, leading thousands to study scriptures. Zhang Ba simplified Fan Min's edition of "Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals" to 200,000 words, calling it "Zhang's Studies." He pacified thieves through rewards without military force. After three years, he requested sick leave, citing the principle that fullness leads to decline. Later promoted to Attendant, he declined friendship with the powerful Deng Zhi. He died at seventy, instructing his sons to bury him simply where he died rather than transport his body home. His disciples posthumously titled him Xianwen.

◆The biography of Guo Ji, named Xihou, was born in Maoling, Fufeng.
Great-great-grandfather Guo Xie was famous as a knight during the reign of Emperor Wu.
His father, Guo Fan, was the prefect of Shu County.
Guo Ji had ambitions when he was young. During the reign of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, he was recruited into the Da Sikong Mansion and moved to Yuyang Duwei three times.
At the time of Wang Mang, he was the Great Yin of Shanggu and moved to merge with the prefecture for animal husbandry.
In the new era of Gengshi, the three auxiliaries were invaded by soldiers one after another. The people were shocked, and the powerful clans and surnames supported each other to defend their camps and refused to surrender first.
When Gengshi Su heard of Guo Ji's name, he worshiped him as Zuo Fengyi and sent him to guard and appease the people.
When Shizu ascended the throne, he paid homage to Yongzhou's pastor, and then became a minister, offering loyal advice several times.
In the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, he became the prefect of Zhongshan.
The next year, Peng Chong was eliminated and became the governor of Yuyang.
Yuyang suffered both from Wang Mang's rebellion and from Peng Chong's defeat. The people were cunning and evil, and there were many thieves.
After Guo Ji arrived, he showed his loyalty with punishment and reward, and killed the bandits and commanders, and the thieves disappeared.
At that time, the Xiongnu harassed the county borders many times, and the border people suffered greatly.
Guo Ji organized his troops and horses and set up offensive and defensive strategies. The Huns were afraid to stay away and did not dare to enter the border fortress again, so the border people were able to live and work in peace and contentment.
After five years of working, the household registration will double.
Later, a group of bandits emerged in Yingchuan. In the ninth year, Guo Ji was conquered and worshiped as the prefect of Yingchuan.
When he was summoned to say farewell, the emperor expressed his condolences and said: "A virtuous prefect, I am not far from the imperial city. The river runs for nine miles. I hope that the capital will also be blessed."
Although you are good at hunting, the mountain roads are dangerous and dangerous. In battle, you are just like a soldier, so you must be cautious.
When Guo Ji arrived at the county, he recruited hundreds of bandits from Yangxia, Zhao Hong, and Xiangcheng Zhao Wu. They all surrendered to Guo Ji with their bare hands. Guo Ji dismissed them and returned to the countryside.
Because he repented and let the thieves go without permission, the emperor praised him for his good approach and did not blame him for his mistakes.
Later, when Zhao Hong, Zhao Wu and other party members heard about Guo Ji's prestige, they came from far away from the south of the Yangtze River, or from Youzhou, Jizhou and other places to surrender to him unexpectedly.
In the eleventh year, the provincial governor of Shuofang belonged to Bingzhou.
The emperor used Lu Fang to occupy the northern territory, and transferred Guo Ji to be the pastor of Bingzhou.
Guo Ji went to the capital to express his gratitude, and the emperor immediately introduced him. He summoned the crown prince and other kings to a banquet all day long, and rewarded him with carriages, horses, clothing and other items.
Guo Ji therefore said that when selecting and filling various positions, one should choose from among the wise and talented people in the world, and it is not appropriate to exclusively use people from Nanyang.
The emperor accepted it.
Guo Jiqian was in Bingzhou, and he had always been kind and kind. When he later entered the border, when he went to the county, old and young came together to greet him on the road.
summary: Guo Ji, from Maoling, Fufeng, was born into a family with a knightly ancestor and a prefect father. During the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, he served in the Da Sikong Mansion and became Yuyang Duwei. Under Wang Mang, he was Great Yin of Shanggu. During the Gengshi era, when the three auxiliaries were invaded, Gengshi appointed him Zuo Fengyi to pacify the people. After Shizu ascended, Guo Ji became Yongzhou's pastor and later a minister offering loyal advice. In the fourth year of Jianwu, he became prefect of Zhongshan, then governor of Yuyang after Peng Chong's defeat. There, he eliminated bandits through punishment and reward, and organized defenses against the Xiongnu, who ceased border incursions. After five years, household registrations doubled. In the ninth year, he became prefect of Yingchuan to suppress bandits, successfully recruiting Zhao Hong and Zhao Wu to surrender. Later appointed Bingzhou pastor, he advised selecting officials from worthy candidates nationwide rather than exclusively from Nanyang. He was known for keeping promises to children who welcomed him on horseback. He served long in Bingzhou due to Lu Fang's troubles, eventually forcing Lu Fang to flee to the Xiongnu. He resigned due to age and illness, became Taizhong doctor, distributed his wealth among his clan, and died at eighty-six.

◆The biography of Du Shi, whose courtesy name is Jun Gong, was born in Ji County, Hanoi County.
Talented at a young age. As a county meritorious official, he has the reputation of being fair and honest.
At the beginning of the revolution, he was recruited to the Da Sima Mansion.
In the first year of Jianwu, he was promoted to Shi Yushi three times a year, responsible for settling the people who were recalled to Luoyang.
At this time, the general Xiao Guang indulged his soldiers and committed violence among the people. The people were frightened and uneasy. Du Shi's orders to Xiao Yu were ineffective, so he killed Xiao Guang and reported the truth to Liu Xiu after he returned.
Liu Xiu summoned him and presented Du Shi with a set of ceremonial halberds. Then he was sent to Hedong to kill and surrender the traitor Yang Yi and others.
When Du Shi arrived in Dayang, he heard that the thief Yang Yi and others were waiting for an opportunity to cross the Yellow River north, so he and Chang Shi quickly burned Yang Yi's ships, led the county soldiers, and led the cavalry commando to attack the rebels and kill Yang Yi and others. The rebels were all wiped out.
He was appointed magistrate of Chenggao County and served for three years with excellent political performance.
He was then moved to the rank of Captain of Pei County, and then transferred to the rank of Captain of Runan. He managed well wherever he went.
In the seventh year of Jianwu's reign, Du Shi was promoted to Nanyang Prefect.
Du Shi was frugal and frugal by nature, and he was honest in politics. He established prestige among the people by killing and raping people. He was good at making suggestions and cherishing the people's labor.
Make a machine that uses water to push a piston to blow air. It is used to smelt iron and cast it into agricultural machinery. It requires less labor and is more effective. People think it is very convenient.
He also repaired sloping ponds and expanded the area of ​​cultivated land. Every household in Nanyang County became rich and prosperous.
People at that time compared him with the former prefect Zhao Xinchen. Some people in Nanyang praised him and said: There was Zhao Fu before him and Du Mu behind him.
Du Shi thought he had little merit, and felt uneasy after living in a large county for a long time. He asked to be demoted to a small county to avoid meritorious officials, so he went to Shudao: "Your Majesty has achieved great achievements in heaven, and has been able to complete the great cause of prospering the Han Dynasty. He has suppressed his troops and cultivated civilized governance. The generals have all returned to the court. There is peace in the country, blessings for all generations, and the world is lucky."
Only the Xiongnu, who do not know their virtues, are still causing trouble in the northwest frontier, tyrannizing China, and the people on the border are wasted and unable to defend themselves. I am worried that although the brave generals try their best to defend the border, they still cannot stop fighting.
summary: Du Shi, from Ji County, Hanoi, was talented from youth. He served as a county meritorious official, then joined the Da Sima Mansion. In the first year of Jianwu, he became Shi Yushi and executed the violent General Xiao Guang, receiving ceremonial halberds from Liu Xiu. He later killed the traitor Yang Yi and others. As magistrate of Chenggao, then captain of Pei and Runan, he governed well. In the seventh year, he became Nanyang Prefect, known for frugality and honesty. He invented a water-powered piston bellows for iron smelting, making agricultural tools more efficiently. He repaired ponds and expanded farmland, enriching the county. People compared him to former prefect Zhao Xinchen. Feeling uneasy about his merit, he requested demotion, arguing that troops needed rest and that meritorious generals should be rewarded with county positions. The emperor refused. Du Shi recommended talented people and proposed using tiger talismans for troop mobilization to prevent forgery, which the emperor accepted. After seven years, he was recalled due to a case involving his brother's revenge. He died poor without land or house; the emperor provided funeral expenses.

◆Kong Fenchuan, whose courtesy name is Junyu, was born in Maoling, Fufeng.

summary: Kong Fen, from Maoling, Fufeng, studied the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals under Liu Xin. During Wang Mang's rebellion, he fled to Hexi with his mother and brother. In the fifth year of Jianwu, Dou Rong appointed him as chief aunt. He became Marquis of Guannei. Despite Guzang's wealth, Kong Fen's property did not increase in four years. He served his mother filially, eating vegetables with his wife while others laughed at his frugality. summary: Zhang Kan, from Wan, Nanyang, was orphaned early and shared his father's wealth with his brother and son. At sixteen, he studied in Chang'an, where classmates called him "Holy Boy." After capturing Chengdu, Zhang Kan inspected the treasury without taking anything. He comforted the people, who were delighted. summary: Lian Fan, from Duling, was a descendant of Zhao general Lian Po. His family had served as frontier county guards for generations. After his father died in Shu Han, fifteen-year-old Lian Fan went to retrieve his body. The prefect offered money, which he refused. When the coffin boat sank, Lian Fan clung to it and was rescued. He studied under Dr. Xue Han. When Xue Han was killed for involvement in King Chu Ying's rebellion, Lian Fan alone collected his body. The emperor questioned him but pardoned him for his courage. As governor of Yunzhong, when the Huns invaded with overwhelming numbers, Lian Fan ordered soldiers to light multiple torches, making the enemy think reinforcements had arrived. He pursued at dawn, killing hundreds. The Huns never attacked Yunzhong again. As prefect of Shu County, he discouraged frivolous debate and abolished night work restrictions, instead requiring water storage for fire prevention. The people sang his praises.
