translation:
Yang Xu was regarded as a descendant of a loyal minister and was worshiped as a doctor. After he resigned from the official position, he was conscripted into the mansion of General Dou Wu.
After Dou Wu failed, he was imprisoned for more than ten years due to party affiliation and lived in seclusion.
When the party ban was lifted, he was conscripted into the Taiwei Mansion and moved to Lujiang Prefecture.
Later, the Yellow Turban bandits in Yangzhou attacked Shu and burned the city walls. Yangxu recruited all the men in the county who were over twenty years old. They all held troops and put out the fire. The weak ones participated in fetching water to put out the fire. They gathered tens of thousands of people and fought hard. They defeated the Yellow Turban bandits and the county boundaries were pacified.
Later, the Anfeng thief Dai Feng and others caused trouble, and Yangxu defeated them again, beheaded more than 3,000 people, and captured their commander alive. The rest of the party were civilians, and they were given farming tools so that they could engage in legitimate agricultural production.
In the third year of Zhongping, Zhao Ci, a soldier of Jiangxia, rebelled, killed Qin Jie, the prefect of Nanyang, captured six counties, and worshiped Yang as the prefect of Nanyang.
When he entered the county, he would patrol incognito and take a boy with him to inspect the county and collect rumors before entering.
Some commanders were greedy and officials and people were cunning, but he knew the situation, and everyone in the county was frightened and frightened.
So he sent troops and Wang Min, the governor of Jingzhou, to attack Zhao Ci and beheaded him. He was killed by more than 5,000 people. The remaining thieves in the county came to surrender to Yangxu, and Yangxu appealed to them to pardon the remaining gang members.
After the thieves were put down, political decrees were issued to meet the urgent needs of the people, and the people were happy and admired.
At that time, many powerful families were extravagant, and Yang Xu was very ill. He often had poor food and clothing, and drove an old horse and a broken carriage.
Fu Cheng once offered him raw fish, and Yang Xu accepted it and hung it in the court. Fu Cheng later offered it to him, and Yang Xu showed him the raw fish hanging in the court to stop him from offering fish.
Later, Yangxu's wife and son Yangmi arrived at the county house, but Yangxu refused to accept them. His wife took Yangmi away with only cloth quilts, rags, salt, and a few bushels of wheat. She turned around and said to Yangmi: How can I support your mother and son if I treat myself so poorly?
Let both mother and son go home.
Six years later, Emperor Ling wanted to make Yangxu the Taiwei.
At that time, those who worshiped the Three Dukes would give tens of millions of gifts to Dongyuan and order the envoys and governors to pay the money, which was named "Zuozou".
Wherever he went, he was often greeted with salutes and generous bribes.
Yangxu sat on the single table, held up his old cotton robe to show it off, and said, "This is all my property."
The emperor was displeased with Zuo Zou's report, so Yang Xu failed to ascend to the throne.
However, he was drafted too often and died of illness at the age of forty-eight before he could set out.
The deceased will be buried with a thin will and no legacy will be accepted.
According to the old system, after the death of an official with two thousand dan, he would be paid a million yuan. Jiao Jian, the prime minister of the government, followed Yang Xu's will during his lifetime and received nothing.
The emperor praised Yangxu with an edict and ordered the Taishan prefect to give Yangxu money from the government to support his family.
summary: Yang Xu, from Pingyang, Taishan, was a descendant of officials. He served as a doctor and joined General Dou Wu's mansion. After Dou Wu's failure, he was imprisoned for over ten years due to party affiliation. When the ban was lifted, he served in the Taiwei Mansion and became prefect of Lujiang. When Yellow Turban bandits attacked Shu, Yang Xu mobilized all men over twenty to fight, defeating the bandits. He later defeated the Anfeng thief Dai Feng, beheading over 3,000 and giving farming tools to the rest. As prefect of Nanyang, he traveled incognito to gather information, then attacked and killed the rebel Zhao Ci. He lived frugally, driving an old horse and broken carriage. When offered fish, he hung it in the court to discourage further gifts. He refused to let his wife and son stay with him, sending them home with only basic necessities. He was nominated for Taiwei but failed due to refusing bribes. He died at forty-eight, requesting a simple burial.

translation:
◆Zongzhuan of King Jia, named Meng Jian, a native of Liaocheng, Dongjun.
He was promoted to Xiaolian, then moved to the capital, and had political achievements.
There are many precious products in the old Jiaozhi soil. Mingji, green feather, rhinoceros, elephant, tortoise shell, exotic fragrant and beautiful trees all come from Jiaozhi.
Most of the former and later governors were corrupt and perverted the law. They flattered the powerful at the top and accumulated private bribes at the bottom. They often used this to seek promotion, so the officials and the people resented betrayal.
In the first year of Zhongping, Jiaozhi stationed troops and served as governor and governor of Hepu. He called himself "General Zhutian".
Emperor Ling specially ordered the three palaces to select capable officials, and one official recommended Jia Cong to be the governor of Jiaozhi.
Jia Cong went to the ministry and interrogated his counter-claims. They all said that the people gathered together as thieves because the taxes were too heavy, the people were poor and empty, the capital was far away, there was nothing to complain about, and the people had no life.
Jia Wangzong immediately sent a letter to inform the people, so that the people could settle down in their own affairs, recruit people who had fled the famine, exempt them from corvee service, execute the generals who caused harm, and select good officials to try to guard the counties. Within a year, the whole territory was settled, and the people were in peace.
There is a song in the lane: "Jia's father came late, so I rebelled first; now that there is peace, the officials dare not eat."
After three years of service, he became the best among the thirteen states and was worshiped as Yilang.
At that time, the Yellow Turbans had just been defeated. After the brutal war, the counties and counties imposed excessive taxes and levies, which led to adultery.
The imperial edict sent Sha to eliminate the governor and two thousand stones, and to select honest and capable officials, so Jia Wangzong was appointed as the governor of Jizhou.
According to the old system, a post car is used to accompany the driver, and red curtains are hung to greet the state border.
When Jia Wangzong arrived, he Shengcha said: "The governor should watch from a distance and listen widely, correct and examine the good and evil. How about those who hang up curtains to cover themselves up?"
So he ordered the driver to take off the curtains.
People everywhere were naturally shocked when they heard the news.
Those officials who had made mistakes were sent away by looking at the wind to remove their seals and ribbons. Only Dong Zhao, the chief of Yingtao, Jiyin, and Liang Guohuang, the chief of Guanjin, served as officials and waited for Jia Wangzong, so the state boundaries became peaceful and smooth.
Emperor Ling died, and the general He Jin recommended Jia Wangzong as the general of Liao Dynasty. He died in the official position.

Grandfather successively, in "The Biography of Du Xing".

Jiaozhi was rich in precious products, but corrupt governors exploited the people, causing rebellion. In the first year of Zhongping, Emperor Ling sent Jia Wangzong as governor of Jiaozhi. translation:
When Lu Kang arrived, no one was sent, and the people were very happy.
Lu Kang governed with kindness and trust, and the bandits and bandits were gone, and the states and counties reported their results.
In the first year of Guanghe, he moved to the post of Wuling Prefect and then became the Prefect of Guiyang and Le'an counties. The county where he lived praised him.
At that time, Emperor Ling wanted to cast bronze figures, but the court's resources were insufficient, so he issued an edict to transfer people's land and charge ten yuan per mu.
At that time, floods and droughts damaged farmers and made the people poor.
Lu Kang came up and remonstrated: I heard that the former kings governed the country by caring for the people.
Eliminate corvee, lighten taxes, and reduce taxes, so as to bring peace to the world, eliminate troubles and become simple, and worship simplicity. Therefore, all surnames obey the teachings, and all kinds of spiritual creatures sense kindness.
The Lord of Decline in the last days is extremely extravagant and unprovoked, and has developed all kinds of new methods to work hard and exploit the people below to satisfy his own meager needs. Therefore, the people lament and Yin and Yang are moved.
His Majesty's holy virtues should be promoted and enlightened, but he actually issued an edict to collect land money for each acre and cast them into bronze figures. I read the edict with melancholy and worried that this was a mistake.
The tax on the eleventh day was called "Che" in the Zhou Dynasty, and "Che" means "tong", which means that this kind of law can be implemented throughout the ages.
Therefore, Duke Xuan of Lu changed the old system of public land and implemented a tax on acres, but the insect plague occurred naturally; Duke Ai of Lu increased taxes, which Confucius thought was wrong.
Is there anyone who seizes the people's belongings to build useless bronze figures, abandons the admonitions of the saints, and follows the same path as the fallen master?
It is said in the legend: What you do must be recorded in a book. If the book fails to follow the law, what will future generations say?
Your Majesty should be careful and reflect on your behavior, and try to change your ways for good, so as to eliminate the resentment of the people.
When the book was circulated, the concubines falsely accused Lu Kang of quoting the subjugation of the country as a metaphor for a saint, which was disrespectful, and sent him to the imperial court in a prison car.
Liu Dai, the imperial censor, examined the matter. Liu Dai gave an explanation, dismissed him, and returned him to the fields.
Later he was worshiped as Yilang.
By chance, Lujiang thief Huang Rang and others joined forces with Jiangxia barbarians with more than 100,000 people, captured four counties, and worshiped Lu Kang as the governor of Lujiang.
Lu Kang declared rewards and punishments, defeated Huang Rang and others, and the rest of the party surrendered.
The emperor commended him for his contribution and appointed Lu Kangsun and Lu Shang as his doctor.
When Emperor Xian came to the throne, the world was in chaos. Lu Kang risked his life and sent filial and honest officials to pay tribute to the imperial court.
At that time, Yuan Shu was stationed in Shouchun, but his troops were hungry, so he sent an envoy to ask Lu Kang to transport soldiers and armor.
Lu Kang believed that Yuan Shu was rebellious and closed himself off to others. He practiced war preparations internally and prepared to resist.
Yuan Shu was furious and sent his general Sun Ce to attack Lu Kang and besieged the city several times.
Lu Kang stood firm, and some of the officials and soldiers were already on vacation. They all returned from hiding and entered the city at night.
summary: Lu Kang, from Wu County, was known for righteousness. As magistrate of Gaocheng County, he governed with kindness and trust, eliminating bandits. As prefect of Guiyang and Le'an, he was praised. When Emperor Ling wanted to cast bronze figures and tax land ten yuan per mu during floods and droughts, Lu Kang remonstrated, citing historical examples of how excessive taxes caused disasters. Concubines falsely accused him of disrespect, and he was sent to court in a prison cart. He was dismissed but later became Yilang. When the Lujiang thief Huang Rang gathered over 100,000 people, Lu Kang became prefect of Lujiang, defeated them, and the rest surrendered. During Emperor Xian's reign, he sent tribute to court despite chaos. When Yuan Shu demanded soldiers and armor, Lu Kang refused, preparing defenses. Yuan Shu sent Sun Ce to attack; Lu Kang held out for two years before the city fell. He died a month later at seventy. His youngest son Lu Ji served Wu as governor of Yulin and was known for filial piety, once taking oranges from Yuan Shu's table for his mother.

Just quit.

Situ Huang Qiong recruited him, and Taichang Zhao Dianju was wise.

So, he didn't respond.
He is talented in understanding people and likes to reward and educate scholars.
He is eight feet long, has a tall and majestic appearance, wears loose clothes and wears a large belt, and travels around the country.

Although Guo Linzong was good at identifying and criticizing people, he did not make passionate and profound discussions, so the eunuch dictatorship could not harm him.

So he taught behind closed doors and had thousands of students.
In the first year of Jianning, Taifu Chen Fan and General Dou Wu were killed by eunuchs. Guo Linzong cried in the wild and was extremely sad.
Because he sighed and said: When people die, the country is also in danger.  The crow landed on that person's house.
In the spring of the next year, he died at home at the age of forty-two.
More than a thousand people from all over the world came to pay their respects to the funeral.
The comrades then carved a stone and erected a stele together, and Cai Yong wrote the inscription. When it was completed, he said to Lu Zhi of Zhuojun: I have written many inscriptions! Everyone felt a little ashamed, but Guo Youdao was the only one who didn't feel ashamed.
The scholars rewarded and selected by Guo Linzong were all as he appraised.
He speaks first and then proves it, and everyone admires him. Later, those who liked to appreciate characters might add exaggerations, so there were some flashy and grotesque words added, just like a book of divination.
Now I record the facts that clearly show effect and write them at the end of the article.
Zuo Yuan, Chen Liuren. As a county student, he broke the law and was expelled.
summary: Guo Taichuan, also known as Lin Zong, was born into a poor family in Jiexiu, Taiyuan. After his father's early death, he refused his mother's suggestion to work in the county, instead studying under Chenggao Qu Boyan. He became well-versed in many books, eloquent, and renowned for his loud voice. While traveling in Luoyang, he befriended Li Ying of Henan, gaining fame in the capital. Returning home, he crossed the river alone with Li Ying, impressing onlookers. Despite recruitment offers from officials like Situ Huang Qiong, he declined, citing his observations of heaven and society. He was known for his tall, majestic appearance and his habit of folding a corner of his towel, which others imitated as "Lin Zongjin." Fan Pang praised him as a man who could not be treated as a subject or friend. After his mother's death, he was known for extreme filial piety. During the party disaster, he avoided harm by refraining from passionate discussions, teaching behind closed doors with thousands of students. In the first year of Jianning, he mourned the deaths of Chen Fan and Dou Wu, predicting the country's danger. He died at home at forty-two, with over a thousand mourners. Cai Yong wrote his epitaph, feeling no shame in doing so.

Li Ying had a noble and pure temperament. Every time he met with Fulong, he often declined other guests and listened to Fulong's words.
Fulong waved his sleeves and talked fluently, while Li Ying often held his hands and sighed.
Guo Linzong began to go to the capital, and he didn't know each other at the time. Fulong admired him when he met him, and introduced him to Li Ying. Guo Linzong became famous all over the world.
At that time, Wenjing of Jin Dynasty in Hanzhong and Huang Ziai of Liang Dynasty all relied on their talents to show off to the capital, and excused themselves to stay home due to illness and did not receive guests.
summary: Guo Linzong was skilled in identifying and rewarding scholars. He advised Zuo Yuan, a disgraced county student, to reform, citing historical examples. He reformed Song Guo, a vengeful man, into an upright official. He accepted Jia Shu, a sinister man, after his mother's death, leading to Jia's transformation. He noted Xie Zhen and Bian Rang's talents but lack of Taoism, leading to their downfalls. He correctly predicted Wang Rou and Wang Ze's career paths. He also discovered talents among commoners, such as Zhang Xiaozhong and Fan Tezu.

Said: In ancient times, dead people were thrown into the wild.
Only my wife can carry out my will, so let me bury her in the ground.
Tian Sheng, whose courtesy name was Zhongxiang, was from the same county as Fulong. He was close to Guo Linzong and had a good understanding of people. He did not hold an official position and was carefree and died at home.
◆The biography of Xu Shao, named Zijiang, was from Pingyu County, Runan County.
When he was young, he established a reputation, was morally responsible, liked to talk about people, and was appreciated by many people.
For example, Fan Zizhao and He Yangshi were all famous at that time.
He began to serve as a meritorious officer in the county, and the prefect Xu Chu respected him very much.
When I heard that my son was going to be an official, there was no one in the government who would not change his conduct and be careful about his words and deeds.
Yuan Shao, a member of the same county, was a noble knight. He left the Puyang Order and returned home with a large number of carriages and horses. He was very luxurious. When he was about to enter the county, he sent away the guests and others and said, "Can Xu Zijian see my carriage and horse attire like this?"
So I just took a car back home.
Xu Shao once went to Yingchuan, and the people who traveled with him were some moral and knowledgeable elders. He did not visit Chen Chen alone.
Chen Fan's wife died and she returned to her hometown for burial. Everyone in the village went to attend the funeral, but Xu Shao did not go.
Someone asked him why, and Xu Shao said: Taiqiu's Taoism is too broad, and it is hard to be thorough in wideness; Zhongju has a severe temperament, and he cannot be thorough in Jun.
So I won't go.
Most of his comments on people are like this.
When Cao Cao didn't want to make a name for himself, he once made generous gifts and humbly asked Xu Shao to talk to him.
summary: Fulong, from Chenliu, abandoned his post as a capital official and studied under Li Ying. He introduced Guo Linzong to Li Ying, making him famous. Fulong exposed the false reputations of Wenjing and Huang Ziai, causing their decline. He refused official posts and buried his wife simply. Tian Sheng, his close friend, was also skilled in understanding people.

translation:
Xu Shao looked down on him and refused to speak, so Cao Cao found an opportunity to threaten Xu Shao. Xu Shao had no choice but to say, "You are a traitor in a time of peace and a hero in a time of trouble."
Cao Cao left very happily.
Xu Shao's uncle Xu Jing, Xu Jing's son Xu Xun, and Xu Xiang were all ministers of the Three Dukes. Because Xu Xiang flattered the eunuchs, he went to Taisi to grant him the title of Marquis. He sent people to invite Xu Shao many times. Xu Shao thought that Xu Xiang had no virtue and behaved abominably, so he never visited him.
Li Kui, a native of the same county as Xu Shao, was upright and had noble ambitions. Xu Shao began to be friendly with him, but later they had conflicts and discord with his brother Xu Jing. Public opinion at that time was dissatisfied with him.
At first, Xu Shao and Xu Jing were both well-known and liked to comment on township party figures. They changed the topic every month, so there was a custom of commenting on the first day of the month in Runan.
When Sikong Yang Biao summoned Xu Shao, he promoted him as upright, upright, and honest, but he failed to respond.
Someone advised Xu Shao to become an official. He replied: "Now that the villain has succeeded, the royal family will be in chaos. I want to go to Huaihai to escape to save the children and the elderly."
So we went south to Guangling.
Tao Qian, the governor of Xuzhou, treated each other with courtesy and was extremely considerate.
Xu Shao felt uneasy and told his disciples: "Tao Gongzu has a good reputation on the surface, but he is not true in his heart."
Although it is very kind to me, this situation cannot last long, so it is better to leave.
So he went to Qu'a to join Liu Yao, the governor of Yangzhou.
Later, Tao Qian indeed captured the guests who were staying with him. After Sun Ce pacified Wu, Xu Shao and Liu Yaonan fled Yuzhang and died there at the age of forty-six.
Xu Shao's brother Xu Qian was also famous. People in Runan said Pingyu had two dragons.
summary: Xu Shao, from Runan, was known for moral responsibility and commenting on people. He influenced Yuan Shao to reduce his luxury. He avoided visiting Chen Chen and Chen Fan, citing their flaws. He famously called Cao Cao a "traitor in peace, hero in trouble." He refused to visit his uncle Xu Xiang due to his flattery of eunuchs. He and his brother Xu Jing held monthly critiques in Runan. He declined official posts, fleeing to Guangling and later to Qu'a to join Liu Yao. He died in Yuzhang at forty-six. His brother Xu Qian was also famous, known as the "two dragons of Pingyu."

translation:
◆The biography of Guo Gong, named Zhongsun, was born in Yangzhai, Yingchuan. The family has been officials for generations.
His father, Guo Hong, studied "Xiao Du Lv" and the prefect Kou Xun used Guo Hong to make judgments on Cao Cao. He stayed in prison for thirty years and his methods were fair.
In all cases judged by Guo Hong, there is no resentment when he retreats. The county will compare Hong to Donghai Yugong.
Guo Hong died at the age of ninety-five.
Guo Gong inherited his father's business when he was young and taught hundreds of disciples.
Later he became a county official and was called into the government.
During the Yongping period, Dou Gu, the captain of Fengche, sent troops to fight against the Huns, and Qin Peng, the captain of cavalry, served as deputy commander.
Qin Peng was stationed elsewhere and often killed people according to the law. Dou Gu reported that Qin Peng had exclusive power and requested that he be killed.
Xianzong then cited officials and ministers to assess Qin Peng's crime.
Because Guo Gong understood the law, he was summoned to the court to participate in the review.
Everyone who discussed it agreed with what Dou Gu said, but Guo Gong said alone: ​​According to the law, Peng should be beheaded.
The emperor said: When the army goes out for battle, the captain is unified under the governor.
Since Peng has no axe, can he have the power to kill people?
Guo Gong replied: "Unifying under the governor is a matter of trilogy." Today's special general Peng Zhuan is a little different from this.
Military affairs are as urgent as human breathing, and the commander is not allowed to be notified in advance.
Moreover, under the system of the Han Dynasty, Zhuoge was the same as Wu, and he was not considered guilty legally.
The emperor listened to Guo Gong's opinion.
There are also brothers who commit murder together, and it is hard to pin the blame on whom.
The emperor believed that the elder brother should not discipline his younger brother, so he reported that the elder brother should be sentenced severely and the younger brother should be commuted to death.
The imperial edict was read out by Sun Zhang, who made a mistake and was punished twice. The minister reported that Sun Zhang had falsely conveyed the imperial edict and should be cut in half for his crime.
The emperor called Guo Gong to ask again, and Guo Gong replied: Sun Zhang should be fined.
The emperor said: Sun Zhang falsely issued an imperial edict to kill people, how can he say that he was only fined?
Guo Gong said: In law, there is a distinction between intentional homicide and manslaughter. Sun Zhang's mistake in conveying the order is considered manslaughter, and manslaughter is lighter in terms of regulations.
The emperor said: Sun Zhang lives in the same county as the prisoner, so I suspect he did it on purpose.
Guo Gong said: The road is as flat as a hammer, and as straight as an arrow. A gentleman will not cheat and deceive. The king regards heaven as the law, and punishment should not be compromised.
The emperor said: OK.
He was awarded the title of Tingweizheng, but was later dismissed for breaking the law.
Later, he was promoted three times, and in the third year of Yuanhe, he was promoted to Tingwei.
Guo Gong's family has been in charge of law for generations, and their affairs are in Kuanping. When he was a magistrate, he decided on prisons and sentences, and mostly acted on the principle of mercy. Therefore, he reported to the emperor the forty-one things that meant severe punishment could be mitigated, and everything was implemented according to the law. In the first year of Zhanghe, the prisoners in the world were pardoned before Bingzi in April, and their death penalty was reduced to one level, without being flogged, and they were sent to Jincheng. However, the article did not mention those who escaped unnoticed.
Guo Gong went to Fengshi and said: The reason why the holy grace reduces the death penalty and makes the border guards more important is that human life is the most important thing.
There are probably tens of thousands of people on death row today, and since the pardon, many criminals have been arrested. Even if the edict does not involve them, they should all be punished with serious crimes.
summary: The biography of Guo Gong, styled Zhongsun, was from Yangzhai, Yingchuan, in a family of officials for generations. His father, Guo Hong, studied "Xiao Du Lv" and served as a judge for Prefect Kou Xun, handling cases for Cao Cao. Guo Hong worked in prison for thirty years with fair methods, and those he judged felt no resentment, earning comparisons to Donghai Yugong. He died at ninety-five. Guo Gong inherited his father's work, teaching hundreds of disciples, then became a county official. During the Yongping period, he was summoned to court to review a case involving Dou Gu and Qin Peng. While others agreed with Dou Gu, Guo Gong argued that Qin Peng should be beheaded according to law, citing military urgency and Han system precedents. The emperor accepted his view. In another case of brothers committing murder, the emperor initially ruled the elder brother be severely sentenced, but Guo Gong advised leniency for a clerk, Sun Zhang, who mistakenly conveyed an imperial edict, distinguishing between intentional homicide and manslaughter. The emperor agreed. Guo Gong became Tingweizheng but was later dismissed for breaking the law. Promoted three times, he became Tingwei in the third year of Yuanhe. He advocated mercy in sentencing, reporting forty-one cases for mitigation, all implemented. In the first year of Zhanghe, he successfully petitioned to extend a pardon to escaped criminals, saving many lives. He died in the sixth year of Yongyuan. His son, Guo Rizhi, also understood law and served as Nanyang prefect.

translation:
Thinking of God's kindness, all those who were convicted of capital crimes were reborn, but those who were arrested after escaping did not benefit from the kindness.
I think that those who have committed capital crimes before and are imprisoned after the pardon may not be flogged to Jincheng, so as to save lives and benefit the frontier.
Suzong thought it was very good and immediately issued an edict to pardon him.
Guo Gong reported on the legal system, and many people saved their lives.
In the sixth year of Yongyuan, he died in the official government. The middle son, Guo Rizhi, also understood the law. His official position was the prefect of Nanyang, and he was famous in politics.
◆Chen Chong's biography, Chen Chong's courtesy name is Zhaogong, and he was a member of the Pei Kingdom.
My great-grandfather, Chen Xian, served as Minister of Law and Order during the reigns of Emperor Cheng and Emperor Ai.
During the reign of Emperor Ping, Wang Mang assisted the government and made many changes to the Han Dynasty system, which made Chen Xian dissatisfied.
When Wang Mang killed He Wu, Bao Xuan and others who were not attached to him because of Lu Kuan's affairs, Chen Xian sighed: "The Book of Changes" says: "A gentleman acts when the opportunity arises. If I don't wait until the end of the day, I can pass away!"
Immediately asked to resign and left.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he summoned Chen Xian to serve as the chief bandit officer, but Chen refused to take up the post on the grounds of illness.
At this time, the three sons Shen, Feng, and Qin were all in official positions, so they were all dismissed from their positions. The father and son returned to their hometown together, staying behind closed doors. They still held sacrifices in the twelfth lunar month according to the custom of the Han family.
When people asked him why, Chen Xian said: Do my ancestors know about Wang's wax sacrifice?
Later, Wang Mang summoned Chen Xian and said that he was seriously ill, so he collected all the laws and regulations at home and hid them in the walls.
Chen Xian had a kind and tolerant character, and often warned his descendants: When negotiating for others, you should rely on lightness. Even if you have the benefit of a hundred gold, never compare yourself with others.
In the early years of Jianwu's reign, Chen Qinzi and Chen Gong served as the left prisoner of the Tingwei and died early.
Chen Gong gave birth to Chen Chong, who learned about the family business. When he was young, Chong served as a state and county official and was called to Situ Baoyu's mansion.
At this time, the three houses were very friendly, and it was considered noble to refuse to do anything.
Chen Chongchang disagreed and worked hard alone, explaining contemporary politics to Bao Yu several times.
Bao Yu was convinced of his ability to favor, so he resigned from Cao Cao and took charge of the world's lawsuits.
His judgment was fair and did not fail to satisfy everyone's wishes.
At that time, Situ's lawsuits were delayed for decades. The matters were complicated and easy to judge, and bad officials had to rely on them to make a difference.
Chen Chong wrote seven volumes of "Resignation and Litigation Bi" for Bao Yu. The rules for dealing with the case were all in accordance with the categories of things.
Bao Yu played this, and later the government took it as an example.
After being promoted three times, in the early years of Emperor Suzong's reign, he became minister.
At this time, the old practices of the Yongping period were inherited. The official administration advocated strictness, and the ministers generally tended to impose heavy sentences in handling cases. Chen Chong believed that the emperor had just ascended the throne and the harsh politics of the previous generation should be changed.
So Shangshu said: I have heard that in the previous king's government, rewards were not excessive and punishments were not excessive. Rather than being forced to do so, I would rather be excessive than excessive.
Therefore, Tang Yao wrote the "Yao Canon", which advocated "forgiveness of disasters". The Duke of Zhou gave a precept, not to miss the rules of Boyi in prison, but to respect the five punishments in order to achieve the three virtues.
summary: Chen Chong, styled Zhaogong, was from Pei Kingdom. His great-grandfather, Chen Xian, served as Minister of Law under Emperors Cheng and Ai but resigned during Wang Mang's usurpation, hiding legal texts in walls. Chen Chong learned family law, served as a county official, and later worked for Situ Bao Yu, writing seven volumes of "Resignation and Litigation Bi" to handle lawsuits fairly. Promoted three times, he became minister under Emperor Suzong. He advocated leniency, arguing against harsh punishments in a memorial, and the emperor adopted his views, abolishing cruel punishments and fixing over fifty legal items. Chen Chong also debated the timing of executions, supporting winter executions based on classical texts, and the emperor accepted his reasoning. He served as prefect of Taishan and Guanghan, where he appointed good officials, reduced lawsuits, and investigated mysterious cries, burying unburied bones to stop them. He refused to flatter Dou Xian, later becoming Tingwei in the sixth year of Yongyuan. He cleaned up laws, proposing to reduce death sentences to 200 and total punishments to 3,000, but this was not implemented. He served as Sikong and died after three years.

translation:
◆Preface to the biographies of ruthless officials. The Han Dynasty inherited the turbulent and uneasy era of the Warring States Period, which affected many people, including those who were arrogant and cunning.
Those who use the big to swallow up the small, cross the country and the city, and those who are strong and unruly become the kings and hegemons in the countryside. The prefectures and counties govern vast areas and have many household registrations.
Therefore, officials can act arbitrarily and arbitrarily, and the traitors should be killed first and then punished.
Show off his staunch spirit and achieve his unyielding power.
He stood up to others and used his own opinions to reveal his unpredictable wisdom.
As for the intricacies of the text, the indiscriminate accusations, and the infuriating of people, they are countless.
Some pits were even filled with corpses, bleeding for miles.
So Wang Wenshu has the reputation of a tiger-crowned official, and Yan Yannian has the reputation of being a butcher. Is this false?
However, those among them who suppressed the strong and suppressed the ministers to the point of breaking their minds and ignoring them can be considered very heroic.
Since the ZTE, the laws have gradually become stricter, and fewer officials and common people break the law than in previous lives.
But eunuchs and relatives harm the world.
They even ordered Yang Qiu to dig up Wang Fu's body and Zhang Jian to dissect Cao Jie's tomb.
Such and such, although it vents public anger and is pleasing to everyone, it can also be said to be too cruel.
Zhang Jian is a well-known figure, so he is included in the "Party Man Chapter".
◆Dong Xuan, courtesy name Shaoping, was a native of Yuxian County, Chenliu County.
At first he was recruited by Situ Houba and recommended as a person with excellent performance. He was gradually promoted to the state minister of Beihai County.
When he arrived, he appointed Gongsun Dan as the chief minister of the five sense organs.
When Gongsun Dan built a new house, the fortune teller believed that someone would definitely die, so Gongsun Dan asked his son to kill passers-by and put the corpses in the house to ward off his disaster.
When Dong Xuan found out, he arrested and killed Gongsun Danzi.
More than thirty people from Gongsun Dan's clan and close associates came to Dong Xuan's government with weapons and complained about their injustice. Dong Xuan believed that Gongsun Dan had taken refuge with Wang Mang before, and was worried that they had colluded with pirates, so he arrested them all and imprisoned them in Jixian Prison. He sent his subordinate Zuo Shuiqiu Cen to kill them all.
The governor of Qingzhou thought that he had killed too many people, so he wrote to the emperor to report Dong Xuan and examine his charges. Dong Xuan was found guilty and recruited into the imperial court.
Dong Xuan was in prison, reciting poems and poems morning and night, without any worries.
When it was time for him to be released from prison and sentenced, the officials and his family prepared a meal for him. Dong Xuan said sternly: "I, Dong Xuan, have never eaten other people's food in my life, let alone when I die?"
Get in the car and drive away.
Among the nine people who were tortured together at that time, it was Dong Xuan's turn. Emperor Guangwu hurriedly sent his attendant knights to rush over. He only pardoned Dong Xuan's death penalty and ordered him to return to prison.
summary: The Han Dynasty inherited the turbulent Warring States period, fostering arrogant and cunning individuals who used power to dominate regions. Officials acted arbitrarily, killing traitors before reporting, displaying staunch spirit and unyielding power. Countless injustices occurred, with corpses filling pits and blood flowing for miles. Figures like Wang Wenshu and Yan Yannian gained reputations as tiger-crowned officials and butchers. After the Zhongxing period, laws tightened, but eunuchs and relatives harmed the world, leading to excessive acts like Yang Qiu digging up Wang Fu's body and Zhang Jian dissecting Cao Jie's tomb, which vented public anger but were deemed too cruel. Dong Xuan, from Chenliu, was recommended as a person of excellent performance and became state minister of Beihai. He killed Gongsun Danzi for murdering a passerby to ward off disaster, then arrested and executed over thirty of Gongsun Dan's clan. The governor of Qingzhou reported him, and Dong Xuan was imprisoned but remained calm. Emperor Guangwu pardoned him, demoting him to county magistrate of Huai. Later, as governor of Jiangxia, he intimidated the giant thief Xia happy into surrendering. As magistrate of Luoyang, he killed Princess Huyang's murderous slave, defying the emperor's order to apologize. He died in office at 74, leaving a poor household, and was honored posthumously.

translation:
He had a good relationship with Guangwu when he was young.
At the beginning of Jianwu's reign, he was recruited to serve as a censor, promoted to captain of Hedong, and introduced in Yuntai.
At first, when Guangwu was poor and humble, he was detained in Xinye for some reason. Fan Ye was appointed as a city official and sent a box of dry food to Guangwu. Guangwu was grateful for his kindness and did not forget it. He invited Fan Ye to eat many times and provided clothes for his carriage and horse.
Because he joked: How about becoming a captain with a box of dry food?
Fan Ye kowtowed in thanks.
After arriving at the county, he punished Ma Shikuang and others. The thieves were eliminated, and the officials and the people were afraid of him.
A few years later, he was promoted to the post of state animal husbandry and taught the people how to farm, plant trees and manage their families.
After serving for more than ten years, he was demoted to Zhi County Magistrate for breaking the law.
After Wei Xiao was eliminated, Longyou was uneasy, so he appointed Fan Ye as the prefect of Tianshui.
He is strict and fierce in politics, likes to apply the law not to harm Han Fei, and makes quick decisions about good and evil.
Anyone who violates his prohibition will never get out of prison alive. Officials, people, Qiang and Hu are all afraid of him.
If something is lost on the road, no one will pick it up.
At night, the traveler left his clothes and luggage by the roadside and said, "I have entrusted it to Duke Fan."
Liangzhou people made a song saying: Wanderers are often poor, but hardworking people are naturally rich.
I would rather see Ruhu's cave than enter Tianshui Temple.
When you laugh, you will surely die; when you are angry, you may live.
well! My Mr. Fan Mansion, where can I meet him again?
He served for fourteen years and died in office.
In Yongping, Xianzong recalled Fan Ye's political achievements when he was in Tianshui and believed that no future generation could catch up with him, so he ordered his family to be given millions of dollars.
Zifan Rong was a talented man who liked the skills of Huangdi and Laozi, but he was unwilling to serve as an official.
◆The biography of Li Zhang, whose courtesy name was Di Gong, was from Huai County, Hanoi County.
The five generations of my family have had two thousand stones.
Li Zhang studied "Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals". After the Ming Dynasty, he taught various students and served as state and county officials.
Guangwu became the Grand Sima, and he pacified Hebei. He summoned Li Zhang to establish Dong Cao's vassal, and he led many expeditions from Guangwu.
Guangwu became emperor and granted Li Zhang the title of Yangping Order.
At this time, Zhao and Wei powerful men gathered together, and Zhao Gang, a surname of Qinghe, built dock walls at the county boundary, built weapons, and harmed the place.
When Li Zhang arrived, he held a banquet and invited Zhao Gang to meet with him.
Zhao Gang came with a sword and feathers and more than a hundred guards.
Li Zhang drank with him, and after a while, Li Zhang killed Zhao Gang with his sword. The soldiers who had been ambushing him also came out and killed all Zhao Gang's guards. Then they ran to the wall of the dock and broke through it with a surprise attack. The officials and the people were in peace.
The prefect of Shengqiancheng, because he was too indiscriminate in killing thieves, was conscripted into prison and relieved of the post of prefect.
summary: Fan Ye, from Nanyang, was a friend of Guangwu from youth. He served as censor and captain of Hedong, punishing Ma Shikuang and eliminating thieves. As state animal husbandry, he taught farming and management. After Wei Xiao's elimination, he became prefect of Tianshui, applying strict laws like Han Fei. His harsh rule made the road safe at night, and Liangzhou people sang of his severity. He died in office after 14 years, and Emperor Xianzong later granted his family millions. Li Zhang, from Huai, studied Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals and served under Guangwu. As Yangping Order, he killed the powerful Zhao Gang at a banquet and pacified the area. As prefect of Langxie, he attacked rebels imprisoning the prefect, killing leader Xia Changsi. He was later conscripted for land measurement issues but released due to merit, dying of illness.

translation:
Half a year later, he was awarded the title of Censor and served as the prefect of Langxie.
At this time, Xia Changsi and others from Anqiu, Beihai, rebelled, imprisoned the prefect Chu Xing, and occupied Yingling City.
When Li Zhang got the news, he immediately sent thousands of troops to attack.
Li Shi stopped Li Zhang and said: "Two thousand stones cannot go to the county, and the troops cannot be sent without permission."
Li Zhang pressed his sword and became angry and said: The rebels are so bold that they imprison and rob the county guard. How can this be tolerated!
If I die because of begging a thief, I will have no regrets!
So he led his troops to Anqiu City, recruited some brave men to burn the city gate, fought with Changsi, killed Changsi, and returned with more than 300 heads and more than 500 oxen and horses.
Chu Xing returned to the county, reported the incident to the emperor, and gave all the proceeds to the officials to comfort them.
Later, because the land he measured was not real, he was conscripted. Because of Li Zhang's meritorious service, he was only served as a military commander and punished by sent to the border to guard against the enemy.
He was released from prison more than a month later.
He was drafted again and died of illness.
◆Zhuan was passed down by Zhou Jin, whose courtesy name was Wentong. He was a native of Pixu.
He is a man who carves out Shao En and likes Han Fei's magic.
When he was young, he served as Tingwei Shi.
In Yongpingzhong, he supplemented the southward line and headed the Tang Dynasty.
After arriving in office, he told the officials: The court does not consider me unworthy and wants me to govern the people. I hate cunning officials by nature and am determined to get rid of the tyrants. Don't test the law by yourself!
Because he killed dozens of particularly powerful bad guys in the county, the officials and the people were shocked.
Promoted to Bo Ping Ling.
No one can come out of prison alive when they hunt down hidden traitors.
Because of his prestige, he was promoted to Qi Xiang, and he was also very strict. He specialized in the rule of law and was good at writing documents and regulations, which were the laws of the state.
Later, because he killed an innocent person, he was demoted to Bo Ping Order again.
He built a junior high school and served as the prefect of Bohai.
Whenever the imperial court's pardon order came to the county, it was often kept secret and not announced. People were first sent to the subordinates to execute the criminals before the edict was announced.
After being convicted, he was conscripted to the imperial court, dismissed from office and returned home.
Zhou Jin was honest and had no property, so he often lived a brick-and-mortar life. Suzong heard about it, took pity on him, made him a man, and promoted him to the Prime Minister of Zhaoling.
Ting Yu was afraid that Zhou Jin would be defeated by Yan Ming and wanted to frustrate his power, so he took a dead man early in the morning, cut off his limbs, and built a temple gate.
Zhou Jinkui found out, so he walked to the dead man and pretended to talk to him.
He secretly observed that there were rice awns in his mouth and eyes, so he secretly asked the gatekeeper: "Do you know who is carrying the rice draft into the city?"
The gatekeeper replied: There is only Ting Yu.
He also asked his disciples: Is there anyone outside who suspects that I am talking to the dead?
He replied: Tingpu doubts you.
So he arrested Ting Yu and tortured him, and he admitted: "If you don't kill people, you will kill people along the way."
summary: Zhou Jin, from Pixu, liked Han Fei's methods. As a county official, he killed dozens of powerful bad guys. As Bo Ping Ling, no one left prison alive. He hid pardon orders to execute criminals first. He was dismissed for killing innocents but later promoted to Zhaoling Prime Minister. He exposed Ting Yu's deception and, as Luoyang Order, intimidated nobles. He clashed with Huangmenlang Dou Du, was imprisoned, pardoned, and later dismissed for harshness. He returned as Yushi Zhongcheng, but was removed again. He later impeached Xia Yanghou, becoming Sili Xiaowei, and died in office.

translation:
◆Huang Changzhuan, Huang Chang, courtesy name Shengzhen, was a native of Yuyao County, Kuaiji County.
He was born into a humble and lonely family.
Living near the school officials, I often saw students learning the etiquette of the school, so I loved learning, so I studied Confucian classics, scribes and laws, and served as a judge in the county.
The governor went on a tour and saw Huang Chang, praised him and recommended him to work.
Later, he served as magistrate of Wan County. He was strict and fierce in politics and liked to expose those hidden evildoers.
Someone stole the hood of his car. Huang Chang didn't say anything at first. Later, he secretly sent relatives to the house of the person in charge of the thief. He caught him unawares and used lightning-fast means to catch him. He also arrested and killed his family members.
All the noble families were afraid of him and called him a god.
The imperial court elected talented people, and Huang Chang was promoted to the governor of Shu County.
The former governor was old and his administration was chaotic, and the people suffered injustice.
When Huang Chang took office, more than 700 people were sued by officials and people, and all of them were clearly dealt with, and none of them were handled improperly.
A bandit leader was secretly arrested and forced to write down the names and addresses of the rapists in each county one by one. Then he sent people to arrest or attack them respectively, but no one escaped or ran away.
Those big bad guys who were full of evil have gone to other counties.
Previously, when Huang Chang was the secretary of the state, his wife returned to her parents' home. She was caught by a thief on the road, so she fled to Sichuan and got married.
Her son committed a crime and had to go to Huang Chang to sue.
Huang Chang suspected that his mother was not from Sichuan, so when he asked her about her situation, she replied: "I am the daughter of Dai Cigong of Yuyao, Kuaiji County, and the wife of Huang Chang, the secretary of the state."
On the way home, he was captured by thieves and that's why he got here.
Huang Chang was surprised and called her to him and said: How do you identify Huang Chang?
She replied: Huang Chang has a sunspot on the center of his left foot. He once said that he would be an official with two thousand stones.
Huang Chang then stretched out his left foot for her to see.
So they hugged each other, wept, and became husband and wife again.
After serving for four years, he was recruited by the imperial court and promoted to Chen Xiang.
Peng, a native of the county, was an old powerful man. He built a very large house and the high-rise building was right next to the road.
Whenever Huang Chang went out to inspect his work, Mrs. Peng would climb up to a high building to watch him.
Huang Chang was unhappy and ordered her to be arrested, thrown into prison, interrogated and executed.
He was promoted to the prefect of Hanoi, and then to the prefect of Yingchuan.
In the fifth year of Yonghe's reign, he was recruited as a general and a master craftsman.
In the first year of Han'an, Si Nong, the chief minister of tonics, was demoted to Taizhong doctor and died in office.
◆Yang Qiu Chuan, whose courtesy name is Fangzheng, is from Quanzhou County, Yuyang County.
It has been a family of surnames and bureaucrats for generations.
He can fence and learn to ride and shoot.
He is strict by nature and likes the teachings of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.
A county official insulted his mother. Yang Qiu gathered dozens of young people to kill the official and his whole family, and he became famous.
Initially, he was promoted to Xiaolian and served as Minister of the Secretariat. Yang Qiu is familiar with history, and his chapters and handling of matters are often praised and trusted by ministers.
When he served as the magistrate of Gaotang County, he was arrested and punished by the county magistrate because of his harshness and harshness, and he happened to be pardoned.
Zhengpi was appointed to Situ Liu Chong's Mansion and was rated as outstanding upon assessment.
The thieves in the mountains of Jiujiang County were causing chaos, which has not subsided for several months.
The three mansions of Taiwei, Situ and Sikong reported that Yang Qiu had the ability to deal with traitors and appointed him as the prefect of Jiujiang.
When Yang Qiu took office, he devised a plan to eliminate the thieves, and arrested and executed all the officials who committed crimes in the county.
summary: Huang Chang, from Kuaiji, studied Confucian classics and served as a judge. As magistrate of Wan, he exposed hidden evildoers, catching a thief who stole his hood. As governor of Shu, he handled over 700 lawsuits and arrested bandits. He reunited with his long-lost wife, captured by thieves. He executed Mrs. Peng for watching him from a high building. He served as prefect of Yingchuan and died as Taizhong doctor. Yang Qiu, from Yuyang, was strict and liked Shen Buhai and Han Fei. He killed a county official who insulted his mother. As prefect of Jiujiang, he eliminated thieves and executed corrupt officials. He was dismissed for cruelty but later promoted to Yilang. As Sili Xiaowei, he arrested and tortured Wang Fu and his son, tearing Wang Fu's body apart. He attempted to impeach Cao Jie but was demoted to Weiwei. He was later executed for plotting against eunuchs.

translation:
Wang Fu was on vacation at home, and Yang Qiu went to the palace to express his gratitude to Emperor Shun. He petitioned Wang Fu and the eunuchs Chun Yudeng, Yuan She, Feng Yueyu and other flattering eunuchs to be arrested and executed together. So Wang Fu, Duan Zhen, Wang Fu's son Yongle Shaofu Wang Meng, and Pei Guo Xiang Wang Ji were arrested and escorted to Luoyang Prison.
Yang Qiu personally interrogated, using all five torture instruments including whip, beating, burning, Hui, and ink to the extreme.
Wang Meng said to Yang Qiu: Since my father and son deserve to die, please be kind to me and use less physical punishment.
Yang Qiu said: You have committed a heinous crime and deserved to die. Do you still want to be treated leniently?
Then Wang Meng cursed: "You used to serve our father and son like slaves. How dare a slave oppose his master?"
Torture me today, it will be your turn soon!
Yang Qiu ordered people to block Wang Meng's mouth with soil and hit him with sticks. Both father and son died under the sticks.
Duan Yu also committed suicide.
So Yang Qiu tore Wang Fu's body apart at the gate of Xia City and wrote "The Thief Wang Fu" on the list.
All Wang Fu's property was confiscated, and his wife and children all moved to Bijing County.
After Yang Qiu killed Wang Fu, he still wanted to impeach Cao Jie and others one by one, so he ordered Zhongdu officials to engage in the investigation and said: "We will get rid of the big bullies first, and the next step is to interrogate the powerful ones."
After hearing this, no one from the wealthy family dared to say a word.
All kinds of luxurious and gorgeous things were sealed and collected, and they did not dare to be displayed again. The capital was afraid of being shocked.
At that time, Emperor Shun's nobleman Yu was buried, and all the officials returned to the city after attending the funeral. When Cao Jie saw Wang Fu's broken body on the roadside, he sadly wiped his tears and said: We can eat each other ourselves, how can we let dogs lick his blood?
Tell all the attendants to go back to the palace for the time being and not to go back home.
Cao Jie went straight to the palace and reported to Emperor Ling: Yang Qiu was originally a cruel official. He should be removed from office after being impeached by the previous three divisions. Because of Jiujiang's small contribution, he was promoted and used.
Sinful people often act recklessly and are not suitable to serve as Sili Xiaowei, which allows him to be cruel and tyrannical.
So Emperor Ling demoted Yang Qiu to Weiwei.
At this time, Yang Qiu was going out to visit the emperor's mausoleum. Cao Jie instructed Shangshu to recall him for official appointment and not to delay the issuance of the edict.
Yang Qiu was urgently recalled and asked to see Emperor Ling. He kowtowed to Emperor Ling and said, "I have no high moral character and was entrusted with the important task of fighting evil. Although I had killed Wang Fu and Duan Zhen before, I had left out foxes like Cao Jie, which was not enough to show the sage of the court to the world."
Please give me one month, and I will make sure that all the wolves, owls, and owls plead guilty.
Yang Qiu kowtows and bleeds, and the palace yells: Weiwei Yang Qiu resists the imperial edict?
After repeated scoldings, Yang Qiu accepted the appointment as a guard.
In the winter of this year, Situ Liu and Yang Qiu discussed arresting Zhang Rang and Cao Jie. Cao Jie and others found out about it and jointly framed Liu and others.
This matter has been seen in "The Biography of Chen Qiu".
So Yang Qiu was arrested and sent to Luoyang prison and executed. His wife and children were exiled to the frontier.
◆Biography of Wang Ji, Wang Ji was born in Junyi County, Chenliu County, and was the adopted son of Wang Fu, a regular servant.
Wang Fu in "Eunuch Biography".
When Wang Ji was young, he liked to read biographies and gained a good reputation, but his temperament was very cruel.
Because his father was powerful and favored by the emperor, he was appointed Prime Minister Pei when he was in his twenties.
summary: Wang Ji, adopted son of Wang Fu, was cruel as Prime Minister Pei. He killed over 10,000 people in five years, using harsh methods like killing parents who didn't raise children. He was detained and died in Luoyang prison when Yang Qiu impeached Wang Fu.

translation:
He is well versed in political affairs, can judge and investigate difficult cases, and expose evil and hidden villains. He is smarter than ordinary people.
The county was ordered to arrest traitors and powerful people, and there were often those who had stolen wine and meat as stolen goods. Even though they happened decades ago, they were derogated and their names were cancelled.
A group of tough officials are specially selected to fight against illegal activities.
If a child is born and cannot be raised, the parents are killed and buried in earth.
Anyone who kills someone will put his body in a car, announce his crime, and declare that he belongs to the county.
In the summer months, when the weather was hot and the corpses were rotting, they tied the bones together with ropes and traveled all over the county. Everyone who saw them was frightened.
During his five years in office, he killed more than 10,000 people.
There are countless other cruel and cruel things.
The county is fearful, everyone is in danger and dare not protect themselves.
When Yang Qiu impeached Wang Fu, he was detained and died in Luoyang prison.
The historian commented: People in ancient times were generous and could easily distinguish between good and evil.
If you commit a crime, if you dress in a different color, you will not dare to commit a crime.
In the last days, customs have become weak, superiors and inferiors are bullying each other, morality and justice cannot make people live in harmony, and transformation is not enough to punish evil, so they use severe torture and killing, and deal with them at any time, which leads to profound officials to rape according to violence and justice, relying on their impartiality to hate evil and evil, and encourage cruel cruelty.
There were quite a few capable people in the Han Dynasty.
It's all because of his courage to defend, his dexterity, his skill in grammar, his resolute actions, and his reputation.
Why is there such a big difference between the good and bad of officials who are dedicated to keeping the law?
Therefore, Yan Yannian sneered at Huang Ba's treatment of forgiveness, and people in Mi County laughed at Shan Mao's extreme measures, which could not cure him.
However, Zhu Yi did not use flogging to humiliate people, and Yuan An did not use Zang to accuse people, but cunning and evil were naturally prohibited, and people did not dare to bully them.
Why is this?
Because the power and punishment have been used, sloppy behavior has arisen, and the way of benevolence and faith has been felt by people.
For those who are lucky enough, their evil intentions will arise again in the gap of power; for those who are inspired, their thoughts will remain even though they are gone.
From one state to the whole world, we can know the gains and losses of numerous punishments and lawsuits.
summary: The historian commented that ancient people were generous, but in later times, severe torture and killing led to cruel officials. Some were brave and skilled, but their methods varied. Power and punishment caused sloppy behavior, while benevolence and faith could prevent evil. The gains and losses of numerous punishments and lawsuits could be understood from one state to the whole world.

translation:
Yao Qi, whose courtesy name is Ci Kuang, was born in Jiaxian County, Yingchuan County.
He is eight feet two inches long, has a very strange appearance, is solemn and majestic.
His father, Yao Meng, was the governor of Guiyang. After his death, Yao spent three years in mourning for him, and everyone in the village praised him.
Guangwu raided Yingchuan. Hearing that Yao Qi was very ambitious, he summoned the thief Cao Yu to follow him and attack Ji.
At that time Wang Lang sent a message to Ji, and Ji Zhong raised troops to respond to Wang Lang.
Guangwu's chariots drove out, and the people gathered to watch. The roads were crowded with noise and chariots could not pass. Yaoqi rode on horseback and raised his halberd, glaring angrily and shouting "guards" to the left and right, and the spectators retreated one after another.
When they arrived at the city gate, the gate was closed, so they broke through the city gate and left.
When he arrived at Xindu, he took Zhao Qi as his assistant general. He, Fu Kuan and Lu Yan all belonged to Deng Yu.
After attacking a nearby county, he also sent out soldiers. Deng Yu thought that Yao Qi was capable, so he paid homage to the partial generals alone and awarded him 2,000 soldiers, including several hundred soldiers each to Fu Kuan and Lu Yan.
After returning, he reported the situation to Guangwu, who was very complimentary.
He sent Yaoqi to attack Zhending Songzi and captured the counties of Leyang, Gaohe and Fei.
Following Deng Yu, he attacked Wang Lang's generals Erhong and Liu Feng under a huge deer. Yaoqi took the lead and captured the enemy's formation. He killed more than fifty people with his own hands and was wounded in the forehead. He tied the wound with a turban and fought again, thus defeating the enemy.
After Wang Lang was killed, he worshiped Yao Qi as General Huya.
So he took the opportunity and said to Guangwu: "In the land of Hebei, which borders the border fortress, people practice military warfare and are known as elite and brave people."
Now that the reform has failed, the unification of the Han Dynasty is in crisis, and there is no way to return to the country.
The Ming Dynasty took control of the mountains and rivers of Hebei, supported the elite people, and obeyed the hearts of thousands of people who longed for the Han Dynasty. Who in the world would dare not to obey? Guangwu smiled and said: Do you want to call the police like before? At that time, hundreds of thousands of bronze horses entered Qingyang and Boping. Yaoqi and his generals attacked them. The battle was unfavorable. Yaoqi fought against the water even more, killing many enemies.
It happened that Guangwu's reinforcements arrived, so they defeated the enemy and chased them to Guantao, where all the bronze horses surrendered.
Following Ji Qing Du and Chi Mei Yu She Dog, the bandits attacked Yao Qi's baggage. Yao Qi fought back, killing dozens of people with his own hands and being wounded in three places on his body. However, he continued to fight hard, defeated the enemy and drove them away.
Guangwu ascended the throne and was granted the title of Marquis of Ancheng, with a settlement of 5,000 households.
At that time, Tanxiang and Wulou thieves entered Fanyang, Neihuang, and the Wei capital several times, and Gengshi general Zhuo Jing was planning to lead a rebellion in Yecheng. The emperor appointed Yaoqi as the prefect of Wei County to perform the affairs of the general.
Yao Qi sent county soldiers to attack Zhuo Jing, defeated him, and beheaded more than 600 people.
Zhuo Jing rushed to the mountains, and Yao Qi chased and killed dozens of his generals and captured Zhuo Jing's wife and children.
They also attacked Fanyang and Neihuang, and beheaded hundreds of people, and the county boundaries were peaceful.
The thief Li Xiong is a strong man in Ye. Li Xiong's younger brother Li Lu wants to plot a rebellion in the city to welcome Tanxiang.
Some people reported to Yaoqi, but Yaoqi did not respond. They complained three or four times, and Yaoqi summoned Li Xiong for questioning.
Li Xiong kowtowed and surrendered, willing to die with his mother.
Yao Qi said: If being an official is not as happy as being a thief, you can go back to Li Lu's place with your mother. Send officials to escort him out of the city.
Li Xiong left to see Li Lu and was about to arrive at the west gate of Yecheng.
Li Lu was so ashamed and grateful that he committed suicide to thank Yaoqi.
Yaoqi sighed, buried him with ceremony, and restored Li Xiong to his original position.
So everyone in Weijun was convinced of his authority.
In the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, Guangwu traveled to Wei County and appointed Yaoqi as Taizhong doctor.
He followed Guangwu back to Luoyang and paid homage to the Weiwei.
Yaoqi is more important than faith. Since he became a general, he often sent troops to the city, but he never captured the people.
Serving in the imperial court, caring about the country and loving the Lord, and if there is anything that has to be remonstrated, it must be a crime to remonstrate.
The emperor once made light of himself to go in and out of Qi's gate. Yao Qi kowtowed in front of his chariot and said: I have heard the warnings of ancient and modern times, things often happen unexpectedly, and I really don't want your Majesty to reveal them in detail. The emperor returned the car for him.
In the tenth year of Jianwu's death, the emperor came in person to present the deceased with clothes, as well as the seals and ribbons of Weiwei and Anchenghou, and was given the posthumous title of Zhonghou.
Zi Yaodan succeeded to the throne.
He also granted the title of Marquis of Jianping to his brother Yaotong.
Later, Yao Dan was granted the title of Marquis of Ge Ling.
Yao Dan passed away, and his son Yao Shu succeeded him.
Yaoshu passed away and was succeeded by his son Yaoyu.
Yao Yu passed away and was succeeded by his son Yao Cai Si.
summary: **Yao Qi** (courtesy name Ci Kuang) was born in Jiaxian County, Yingchuan. Standing eight feet two inches tall with a striking appearance, he was known for solemnity and majesty. After his father Yao Meng, Governor of Guiyang, died, Yao Qi observed three years of mourning, earning village praise. When Guangwu raided Yingchuan, he recruited Yao Qi to attack Ji. During Wang Lang's rebellion, Yao Qi cleared crowded roads by brandishing his halberd and shouting, broke through a closed city gate, and later served under Deng Yu. Deng Yu recognized Yao Qi's capability, making him a partial general with 2,000 soldiers. Yao Qi captured several counties, fought bravely against Wang Lang's forces—killing over fifty enemies despite a forehead wound—and was appointed General Huya after Wang Lang's death. He advised Guangwu to consolidate Hebei's elite forces, and Guangwu smiled at his boldness. Yao Qi fought the Bronze Horse rebels, killing many despite initial setbacks, and later defeated bandits attacking his baggage, sustaining three wounds. After Guangwu ascended the throne, Yao Qi became Marquis of Ancheng with 5,000 households. As Prefect of Wei County, he suppressed Zhuo Jing's rebellion, beheading over 600, and pacified the region. When Li Lu plotted rebellion, Yao Qi showed mercy to Li Xiong, leading Li Lu to suicide from shame. Yao Qi served as Taizhong大夫 and Weiwei, known for integrity and remonstrating with the emperor, once stopping Guangwu from careless travel. He died in the tenth year of Jianwu, receiving posthumous honors as Marquis Zhong.

translation:
When Guangwu came to the throne, he believed that the king knew military affairs, loved the soldiers, and could serve alone, so he was worshiped as a partial general and led the troops of Zang Gong and Chen Jun, while Zang Gong and Chen Jun were appointed as cavalry captains.
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, Wang Ba was granted the title Fubohou.
In the autumn of the fourth year of Jianwu, Guangwu drove Qiao, and Wang Ba and the captured general Ma Wudong discussed Zhou Jianyu Chuihui.
Su Mao led more than 4,000 soldiers from five schools to rescue Zhou Jian, and first sent elite cavalry to cover Ma Wu's supplies, and Ma Wu went to rescue him.
Zhou Jian sent troops from the city to attack Ma Wu. Ma Wu relied on Wang Ba's assistance and did not make much effort in the battle. He was defeated by Su Mao and Zhou Jian.
Ma Wujun ran through Wangba's camp and shouted for help.
Wang Ba said: The thieves are strong, and they will lose both sides in battle. Just work hard. So he closed the camp gate and stood firm.
All the soldiers rushed to fight.
Wang Ba said: "Su Mao's soldiers are elite and numerous. Our officers and soldiers are afraid. However, the captive general and our army rely on each other. The two armies are inconsistent. This is a path to failure."
Now that the camp is closed and the enemy is not willing to come to rescue, the traitors will surely take advantage of the victory and advance easily. The captor general will fight harder when he sees that there is no rescue.
In this way, when the troops of Sumao and Mao are tired, we can defeat them by attacking their fatigue. Sure enough, Su Mao and Zhou Jian concentrated their forces to attack Ma Wu, and the battle lasted for a long time. Dozens of people including Lu Run, a strong man in Wang Ba's army, cut off their hair to invite the battle.
Wang Ba knew that his soldiers were eager, so he opened the back door of the camp and sent out his elite cavalry to attack behind them.
Su Mao and Zhou Jian were attacked successively and fled in panic. Wang Ba and Ma Wu each returned to their camps.
The thieves gathered again to challenge him, but Wang Ba was unable to get out of the wall and was enjoying a song and dance party with his soldiers.
Su Mao fired arrows like raindrops into the camp, hitting the wine bottle in front of Wang Ba. Wang Ba sat still.
The soldiers all said: Sumao was defeated the day before yesterday, but now it is easy to defeat him.
Wang Ba said: Otherwise, Su Mao's soldiers came from far away and there was insufficient food, so he challenged him several times in order to win by chance.
I am closing the camp and resting my soldiers. As the saying goes, it is to conquer the enemy without fighting. This is the best tactic. Su Mao and Zhou Jian were unable to fight, so they led their troops back to camp.
That night, Zhou Jian's nephew Zhou Songzao closed the city gates and resisted. Su Mao and Zhou Jian fled, and Zhou Song surrendered to the king.
In the spring of the fifth year of Jianwu's reign, the emperor sent Taizhong, a senior official, to hold a talisman to worship Wang Ba as a general against captives.
In the sixth year of Jianwu, Xin'an was established.
In the eighth year of Jianwu's reign, he stationed at Hangu Pass and defeated the bandits in Xingyang and Zhongmou.
In the ninth year of Jianwu, more than 50,000 people including Wang Ba, Wu Han, Hengye general Wang Chang, Jianyi general Zhu You, and traitor-breaking general Hou Jin attacked Lu Fang generals Jia Lan and Min Kan at Gaoliu.
The Xiongnu sent cavalry to assist Lu Fang, but the Han army encountered rain and the battle was at a disadvantage.
Wu Han returned to Luoyang and ordered Zhu You to garrison Changshan, Wang Chang to garrison Zhuojun, and Hou Jin to garrison Yuyang.
Xishu worshiped Wang Ba as the prefect of Shanggu, and led the troops as in the past, hunting barbarians without being restricted by county boundaries.
The next year, Wang Ba and Wu Han and other four generals sent out 60,000 men to Gaoliu to attack Jia Lan. Wang Ba and Yuyang Governor Chen Yujin were ordered to lead the army as the vanguard.
General Zuonan of the Xiongnu led thousands of cavalry to rescue Jia Lan. Wang Ba and others fought with him at the foot of Pingcheng, defeated the enemy troops, pursued him out of the fortress, and beheaded hundreds of people.
Wang Ba and other generals returned to Yanmen and joined forces with General Du Mao to attack Lu Fang General Yin Yuguo County and Fan County, but failed to win.
In the thirteenth year of Jianwu's reign, the number of households in the city was increased, and Wang Ba was granted the title of Xianghou.
At this time, Lu Fang, together with the Xiongnu and Wuhuan soldiers, invaded and plundered more frequently, making the borderland miserable.
Wang Ba was ordered to lead more than 6,000 prisoners who were freed from their shackles, and he and Du Mao managed Feigu Road, piled stones and earth, built pavilions and barriers, and traveled more than 300 miles to Pingcheng.
Wang Ba fought hundreds of battles with the Xiongnu and Wuhuan, large and small, and was well versed in border defense affairs. He wrote several times that it was advisable to make peace with the Xiongnu, and also suggested that transportation could be carried out by warm water canal to save the labor of land transportation. These were all accepted.
Later Nan Danyu and Wuhuan surrendered. The north side is quiet and uneventful.
Wang Ba has been in Shanggu for more than 20 years.
In the 30th year of Jianwu's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Huailing.
summary: **Wang Ba** (courtesy name Yuan Bo) was from Yingyang, Yingchuan. His family valued legal traditions, and he worked as a jailer before studying in Chang'an. When Guangwu passed through Yingyang, Wang Ba joined his army, fighting at Kunyang. Despite others leaving, Wang Ba remained loyal; Guangwu praised him, saying "The strong wind knows the strong grass." During Wang Lang's rebellion, Wang Ba falsely claimed the Hutuo River was frozen to calm frightened troops, and the ice miraculously formed, allowing crossing. He became a military commander and Marquis of Guan Nei, later capturing Wang Lang's seal. Known for comforting soldiers, he was made a partial general after Guangwu's ascension. In the fourth year of Jianwu, Wang Ba employed strategic patience against Su Mao, closing his camp and refusing battle until the enemy tired, then launching a surprise attack that routed them. He served as General Against Captives, fought Xiongnu forces at Gaoliu, and became Prefect of Shanggu. For over twenty years, he managed border defenses, built roads and barriers, and advocated peace with the Xiongnu. He died in the second year of Yongping, having been granted Marquis of Huailing.

translation:
Ji Zun's soldiers arrived first and attacked Zhang Feng in a hurry. Zhang Feng's hero Cao Meng captured Zhang Feng and surrendered.
At first, Zhang Feng was fond of alchemy. A Taoist priest said that Zhang Feng was regarded as the emperor. He wrapped a stone in a colorful bag and tied it to Zhang Feng's elbow, saying that there was a jade seal in the stone.
Zhang Feng believed it and rebelled.
After being caught and beheaded, he also said: There is a jade seal on his elbow. Ji Zun broke his stone vertebrae, and Zhang Feng realized that he had been deceived by the Taoist priest. He looked up to the sky and sighed: "I will die without regrets!" All the generals were led back, and Ji Zun was ordered to stay in Liangxiang to resist Peng Chong.
Therefore, he sent the guard Fu Xuan to attack Peng Chong's general Li Hao and Yu Lu, and defeated his army, beheading more than a thousand people.
They resisted each other for more than a year and were defeated several times. Many of Peng Chong's followers surrendered.
When Peng Chong died, Ji Zun marched to pacify his territory.
In the spring of the sixth year of Jianwu, he ordered Ji Zun and Jianwei General Geng Yan, Huya General Gai Yan, Han Zhong General Wang Chang, Capture General Ma Wu, Xiaoqi General Liu Xin, Wuwei General Liu Shang and others to attack Gongsun Shu from Tianshui.
The army stopped in Chang'an, and Guangwu's chariots also arrived, but Kaixiao did not want the Han soldiers to go to Long, so he excused himself.
Guangwu summoned the generals to discuss. They all say: You can temporarily delay the period of the sun and the moon of Wei Xiao, and add titles to his generals to promote their dispersion and disintegration. Ji Zun said: Kui Xiao has been plotting for a long time.
If he stands still and procrastinates for a while now, it will prompt him to deepen his deception and make Gongsun Shu increase his security, so it is better to march directly. Guangwu obeyed and sent Ji Zun as the vanguard.
Kaixiao sent his general Wang Yuan to stay at Longdi, and Ji Zun attacked, defeated Wang Yuan's army, and pursued him to Xinguan.
When the generals arrived, they fought with Kai Xiao but failed, so they retreated to Long.
Guangwu ordered Ji Zun to garrison troops in Qi, ordered Geng Yan to garrison troops in Qi, ordered General Feng Yi to garrison troops in the city, and ordered Grand Sima Wu Han and others to return to Chang'an.
Since then, Ji Zun has defeated Kuai Xiao several times.
See "Feng Yi Zhuan" for details.
In the autumn of the eighth year of Jianwu, he went up to Long from Guangwu.
When Kuai Xiao was destroyed, Guang Wu returned eastward and passed through Qian. He went to the Ji Zun military camp, comforted and fed the soldiers, and performed Huangmen martial arts, which stopped late at night.
At this time, Ji Zun was ill and was given a thick mattress to sit on, which was covered with the emperor's royal canopy.
Then let him march to Longxia.
When Gongsun Shu sent troops to rescue Wei Xiao, Wu Han, Geng Yan and others all fled back, except for Ji Zun who remained.
In the spring of the ninth year of Jianwu, he died in the army.
Ji Zun was an honest, conscientious, careful, self-denial, and dedicated to the public service. He always gave all the rewards he received to his soldiers. He had no private property at home. He wore a Wei belt, a quilt, and a quilt, and his wife's clothes were not colorful. Therefore, the emperor valued him.
After his death, sympathy and mourning were especially intense.
When the coffin arrived in Henan County, the emperor sent hundreds of officials to gather at the funeral site. Guangwu came in white mourning clothes and looked at the coffin in mourning.
summary: **Ji Zun** (younger brother's grandson) was from Yingyang, Yingchuan. Though wealthy, he was respectful and frugal. After killing a bullying government official, he joined Guangwu. As a military commander, he executed Guangwu's own son for breaking the law, earning Guangwu's respect. He became a partial general and Marquis of Yingyang. Ji Zun fought bravely despite arrow wounds, defeated Zhang Man by cutting his food supply, and captured him alive. He attacked Zhang Feng, whose rebellion stemmed from a Taoist priest's deception about a jade seal. Ji Zun resisted Peng Chong for over a year, and after Peng's death, pacified his territory. In the sixth year of Jianwu, he argued for direct attack against Kui Xiao, serving as vanguard. He remained steadfast when others retreated, dying in the army in the ninth year of Jianwu. Ji Zun was known for self-denial, giving rewards to soldiers, owning no private property, and wearing plain clothes. Guangwu mourned deeply, personally attending his funeral. Posthumously named Marquis Cheng, Ji Zun was praised for his purity, loyalty, and Confucian conduct—selecting talents by Confucian standards, reciting poetry, and establishing a Confucian temple. He had no children, so his title was abolished.
