translation:
I think that although there is a locust plague now, the timely rains and dews since May this year are a good sign.
Entering the winter festival, during the break from farming, one should go to Guangcheng to observe the plains of Sichuan, see wheat fields, and reward collections, so as to teach martial arts and hunting, so that officials and people can see the beauty of flags and flags, hear the sound of bells and drums, rejoice and be encouraged in the fields, welcome harmony, and call for holiday celebrations.
You little ant, I miss you endlessly. The book written by Zhi Zhi is based on an old article and tells the story of hunting in the field. Wrote "Ode to Guangcheng" as a satire. "Ode" was sent to him, which offended Deng, so he stayed in Dongguan and was not allowed to be promoted for ten years.
Because my brother's son died, I apologized and returned home.
When the Queen Mother heard about it, she was furious and said that Ma Rong did not respect the court's orders and wanted to be an official in the prefecture and county. So he ordered Ma Rong to be prohibited from becoming an official.
After the death of the Empress Dowager, Emperor An took charge of the government, recalled the Lang Office, and returned to the Lecture Department.
He was born as the chief of the stables of the King of Hejian.
At this time, the emperor visited Mount Tai in the east, and Ma Rong wrote "Ode to the Eastern Tour". The emperor appreciated his article and summoned the doctor to pay homage to him.
When the Marquis of Beixiang came to the throne, Rong wrote a book called Bing, Li Langzhong, and became the county's meritorious official.
In the second year of Yangjia, the imperial court recommended honest and simple people. Cen, the captain of the city gate school, raised Ma Rong and was called to the public carriage. After passing the examination, he paid homage to Yilang. The general Liang Shang recommended him as a Zhonglang and was promoted to the governor of Wudu.
At this time, the Xiqiang rebelled, and the general Ma Xian and the captain Hu Chou who protected the Qiang in the west launched a campaign, but the advance was delayed.
Ma Rong knew that he was going to be defeated, and Shangshu asked for his service: Now the bastards and Qiang are stealing everywhere, and we should quickly send troops deep into the army to eliminate his gang members before he can concentrate, while Ma Xian and others are stranded everywhere.
The Qiang and Hu are well-informed and well-informed. Although they are hiding and avoiding things now, once they take advantage of the situation, they will definitely invade and plunder the three assistants and cause great harm to the people.
I would like to ask the five thousand Kwantung soldiers who are not available to Ma Xian. Under the guise of the army's order, I will try my best to lead the troops and take the lead. Within thirty days, we will definitely defeat the Qiang and Hu.
I studied arts and literature when I was young, but I don’t understand military affairs. I made presumptuous remarks and made false statements. I should be held accountable.
In the past Mao Sui was a lowly person and everyone laughed at him. Finally, with one sentence, Chu and Zhao agreed to form an alliance.
I'm afraid that Ma Xian and others are only guarding one city and want to attack the west. If the Qiang appears in the east, their soldiers will inevitably be defeated and defect like Gao Ke.
The court cannot use it.
Shangshu also said: Can and Bi change color, Can and Bi are the places to stay in the west, Bi are the frontier soldiers, and as for dividing fields, Can and Bi are the places where Jin divides and merges states.
Xirong and Beidi may come to invade, so we should be prepared.
Soon, the Qiang rebels in Longxi and Wuhuan invaded and plundered Shangjun, just as Ma Rong said.
After three official transfers, he was the prefect of Nanjun during the reign of Emperor Huan.
First, something happened to Ma Rong that violated the will of the general Liang Ji. Liang Ji hinted that the officials would accuse Ma Rong of corruption in the county, dismissed him from office, shaved off his hair, and moved to Shuofang.
If you commit suicide but do not die, you will be exempted from guilt. I paid homage to Yilang again and wrote in Dongguan. Resigned due to illness.
summary: During Empress Dowager Deng's regency, Confucian scholars advocated abolishing martial arts, leading to widespread banditry. Ma Rong disapproved, arguing that civil and military affairs were both essential. In the second year of Yuanchu, he wrote "Guangcheng Ode" to satirize this policy, suggesting that the emperor should engage in hunting and martial training to promote harmony. This offended Deng, and he was confined to Dongguan for ten years without promotion. After his nephew's death, he resigned and returned home, angering the Empress Dowager, who banned him from office. After her death, Emperor An recalled him, and he served as chief of the stables for the King of Hejian. He wrote "Ode to the Eastern Tour" for the emperor's pilgrimage to Mount Tai, earning a promotion to doctor. Later, as governor of Wudu during a Xiqiang rebellion, Ma Rong proposed a swift military campaign to defeat the rebels, but his advice was ignored. He accurately predicted the subsequent invasions. Under Emperor Huan, he became prefect of Nanjun but was framed by General Liang Ji, exiled to Shuofang, and later pardoned. He returned to writing at Dongguan before retiring due to illness.

translation:
Ma Rong was a man of great talent and profound knowledge, and was a general expert in the world. Professors tutor students, often by the thousands.
Lu Zhi of Zhuojun and Zheng Xuan of Beihai were both his students.
He knows how to play the drums and harp, and is good at playing the flute. Be free and willful and not be bound by the small details of Confucianism. The house is furnished with clothes, advocating luxury, and often sits in a high hall with a red gauze hanging. There are students in front of the teacher and female musicians in the back. The disciples taught the teachings one by one, and few entered the room.
I once wanted to annotate "Zuo Shi Chun Qiu". When I saw the annotations by Jia Kui and Zheng Zhong, I said: Jia Jun is good but not knowledgeable, and Zheng Jun is good but not good.
You are knowledgeable and knowledgeable, I have nothing more to say. He only wrote "The Theory of Similarities and Differences in Three Biographies".
Annotated "The Classic of Filial Piety", "The Analects of Confucius", "Poetry", "Yi", "Three Rites", "Shangshu", "Biography of Lienu", "Laozi", "Huainanzi", "Li Sao", and wrote a total of twenty-one poems, odes, stele, memorials, books, notes, tables, memorials, seven-character poems, zither songs, countermeasures and testaments.
At first, Ma Rong was punished by Deng, and he did not dare to offend the powerful family again. He drafted a memorial for Liang Ji to frame Li Gu, and wrote the general "Ode to the West". Therefore, he is quite ridiculed by ordinary honest people.
He died at home in the 88th year of Yanxi's reign.
The will was buried poorly.
The grandson of the clan, Ma Ri Shi Dan, was promoted to Taifu when he was presented to the emperor.
The historian commented: Ma Rong resigned from Deng's order and wandered between Long and Han, perhaps because he was demanding that his words and deeds should be consistent.
However, he soon became ashamed of the formal details of the country folk and cherished his rich body. Finally, he was ridiculed for his extravagant and lewd pleasures. There are too few people who are intellectually correct!
When the work is hard, the feeling of cherishing and preserving becomes thinner. Life is precious, so the thoughts of safety and survival are more numerous.
Those who are not afraid of climbing high are those who are being punished because they have no regard for life or death.
If you don't sit under the eaves for fear of the tiles falling down and hitting you, you are the son of a rich man!
Examine the main reasons and seek peace of mind.
We have different views on things, and we can't help but laugh at each other.
summary: Ma Rong was a renowned scholar with thousands of students, including Lu Zhi and Zheng Xuan. He was skilled in music, lived luxuriously, and taught with a red gauze curtain, separating male and female students. He annotated many classics, including the "Classic of Filial Piety," "Analects," and "Book of Songs." However, he was criticized for drafting a memorial for Liang Ji to frame Li Gu. He died at home at age 88, with a simple burial. The historian noted his initial integrity but later indulgence in luxury, reflecting the tension between valuing life and maintaining moral principles.

translation:
The founder of the Eastern Han Dynasty, Emperor Guangwu Liu Xiu, whose courtesy name was Uncle Wen, was born in Caiyang, Nanyang. He was the ninth-generation grandson of Liu Bang, the great ancestor of the Han Dynasty. It comes from Liu Fa, the king of Shading who was born under Emperor Jing.
Liu gave birth to Liu Mai, the Marquis of Chung Ling Festival, Liu Mai gave birth to Liu Wai, the governor of Yulin, Liu Hui, the captain of Julu, was born to Liu Wai, Liu Qin was born to Liu Qin, the Nandun order, and Liu Qin was born to Guangwu.
Guangwu lost his father at the age of nine and was raised by his uncle Liu Liang.
He is seven feet three inches tall, has thick eyebrows, a wide mouth, a protruding nose, and a full forehead.
He is industrious by nature and enjoys farming. His elder brother Bo Sheng was fond of chivalry and raising people. He often ridiculed Guang Wu for only working in the fields and compared him with Liu Bang's second brother Liu Zhong.
It was not until the reign of Wang Mang and Tianfeng that Guangwu came to Chang'an to study "Shang Shu" as a disciple and roughly understand the gist of the book.
In Wang Mang's last years, there were successive locust plagues in the country, and bandits and bandits were raging.
In the third year of Emperor Di Huang's reign, there was a serious famine in Nanyang, and most of the family's guests went out to rob and steal.
In order to avoid the government, Guangwu fled to Xinye County and transported the harvested grain to Wancheng to sell.
Li Tong and others from Wan used prophecies and talismans to tell Guangwu: The Liu family has risen again, and the Li family will be the assistant. Guangwu didn't dare to act rashly at first, but then he thought that his brother Bo Sheng would do great things by making friends with diners. Moreover, Wang Mang's regime showed signs of decline and destruction, and the world was in turmoil, so he planned with the Li family and decided to raise an army, so he began to purchase various weapons.
In October, he and Li Tong's cousin Li Yi and others raised troops in Wancheng. He was 28 years old at the time.
In November, the comet appeared in Zhangsu in the south.
Guangwu then led his retainers back to Chongling.
At this time, Bo Sheng had gathered the people to raise troops.
At first, the children of each family were very frightened. They ran and hid, saying: "Bosheng wants to kill us!"
When they saw Guangwu in crimson robes and crowns, they were all surprised and said: "Uncle Wen, who is cautious and kind, has also raised an army!"
Only then did everyone settle down. Bo Sheng then recruited troops from Xinshi and Pinglin, and together with his leaders Wang Feng and Chen Mu, went west to attack Changju.
Guangwu first rode the bull, and then he was able to ride the horse after killing Xin Yewei.
He entered Tu Tangzi Township and killed the Huyang county captain.
The wealth obtained by the army was unevenly distributed, and everyone was angry. The soldiers wanted to counterattack the Liu family.
Guangwu then collected all the property from his clan and gave it all to the soldiers. Only then did everyone feel satisfied.
He then attacked and captured Jiyang, and fought with Wang Mang's former commander Zhen Fu and Zhengliangqiu in Xiaochang'an. As a result, the Han army was defeated and had to retreat to Jiyang.
On the first day of the first lunar month of the first year of Gengshi, the Han army fought against Zhenfu and Liangqiuci in the west of Xianshui River. They defeated the enemy and killed Zhenfu and Liangqiuci.
Bo Sheng defeated Wang Mang's general Yan You and Zhizong's general Chen Mao in Huoyang, and then besieged Wancheng.
On the first day of February, Liu Xuan was proclaimed emperor. Liu Xuan appointed Bo Sheng as the Great Situ and Guang Wu as the Taichang Commander.
summary: Emperor Guangwu Liu Xiu, courtesy name Uncle Wen, was born in Caiyang, Nanyang, as the ninth-generation grandson of Liu Bang. He lost his father at age nine and was raised by his uncle Liu Liang. Described as tall with distinctive features, he was industrious and enjoyed farming, unlike his elder brother Bo Sheng who favored chivalry. During Wang Mang's reign, Liu Xiu studied the "Shang Shu" in Chang'an. When locust plagues and famine struck, Liu Xiu fled to Xinye County to avoid government persecution. After receiving prophecies about the Liu family's revival, he initially hesitated but eventually planned with the Li family to raise an army. In October, at age 28, he raised troops in Wancheng. When local families saw the cautious Liu Xiu had joined the uprising, they stopped hiding. After initial victories and defeats, the Han army captured several cities.

translation:
At this time, it happened that Geng Kuang, the governor of Shanggu, and Peng Chong, the governor of Yuyang, respectively sent generals such as Wu Han and Kou Xun to lead elite cavalry to assist in attacking Wang Lang. Emperor Gengshi also sent Shangshu servant She Xie Gong to attack Wang Lang. Guangwu rewarded the soldiers well, and then marched eastward and surrounded Julu City.
Wang Lang's general Wang Rao defended the city, and Guangwu failed to capture it for more than a month.
Wang Lang also sent Ni Hong and Liu Feng to lead tens of thousands of troops to rescue Julu. Guangwu went to Nanxian to attack them head-on, killing thousands of enemy troops.
In April, he marched again and besieged Handan, winning consecutive battles.
On the day of Jiachen in the fifth month, Handan was captured and Wang Lang was killed.
The documents were seized and it was discovered that the Han military officials had colluded with Wang Lang to slander Guangwu's letter, which was called Qianzhang.
Without even looking at it, Guangwu summoned the generals to burn them, saying: "Let those who are tossing and turning calm down."
Emperor Gengshi sent his censor, Shi Zhifujie, to make Guangwu the King of Xiao, asking him to cease the war and return to the seat of Emperor Gengshi.
Guangwu declined, saying that Hebei had not yet been pacified and would not accept the order.
From then on, Guangwu began to have second thoughts about Emperor Gengshi.
At that time, the political situation in Chang'an was in chaos, and all parties rebelled against Gengshi Emperor.
Liu Yong, the king of Liang, acted exclusively in Suiyang County, Gongsun Shu proclaimed himself king in Bashu, Li Xian established himself as the king of Huainan, Qin Feng claimed to be the king of Chuli, Zhang Bu raised troops in Langxie, Dong Xian raised troops in Donghai, Yancen raised troops in Hanzhong, and Tian Rong raised troops in Yiling. They all appointed generals and invaded various counties.
There were also bandits from various places with nicknames such as Tongma, Daxi, Gaohu, Chonglian, Tieshan, Dajiao, Youlai, Shangjiang, Qingdu, Wuxiao, Tanxiang, Wufan, Wulou, Fuping, Huosuo, etc. Each led his troops, totaling millions of people, to plunder in their respective counties.
Guangwu was preparing to attack these thieves, so he first sent Wu Han to recruit soldiers and horses from ten counties to march north.
When Miao Zeng, the governor of Youzhou, refused to obey, Wu Han killed him and mobilized his troops.
In autumn, Guangwu attacked the Bronze Horse Army in the county. Wu Han led the elite cavalry to Qingyang County to join Guangwu.
The Bronze Horse Army repeatedly challenged them, but Guangwu stood firm in the barracks and refused to fight back. Once someone from the Bronze Horse Army went out to rob property, Guangwu sent people to intercept them and cut off the Bronze Horse Army's food and grass channels.
After more than a month of this, the Bronze Horse Army ran out of food and fled in the middle of the night. Guangwu led his army to pursue them to Guantao County and defeated the Bronze Horse Army.
Before all the Bronze Horse Army surrendered, Gaohu and Chonglian came from the southeast to join the remaining Bronze Horse Army. Guangwu then fought fiercely with them in Puyang, defeated the enemy forces across the board and made them surrender, and named their generals as marquises.
The surrendered generals still felt uneasy. Guangwu knew their doubts and asked them to return to their respective armies to manage the soldiers, and then he leisurely rode on horseback to inspect each battalion.
The surrendered people talked among themselves and said: King Xiao confides in us, how can we not retaliate with death? From then on they were all convinced.
Guangwu distributed all the surrendered troops to the generals, and his troops expanded to hundreds of thousands. The people in Kansai therefore called Guangwu the "Bronze Horse Emperor".
The generals of other branches of the Red Eyebrow Army and more than 100,000 horses from Daxu and Qingdu gathered at Shedog. Guangwu led his troops to attack and defeated the Red Eyebrow Army. All the troops fled.
Guangwu sent Wu Han and Cen Peng to attack Yecheng and killed Xie Gong.
Qingdu and Chimei troops entered Hangu Pass and attacked Emperor Gengshi.
Guangwu then sent Deng Yu to lead his six lieutenants to march westward to take advantage of the war between Emperor Gengshi and Chimei.
At this time, Emperor Gengshi sent Grand Sima Zhu Tuna, Wuyin King Li Yi and others to garrison in Luoyang. Guangwu also ordered Feng Yi to defend Mengjin against them.
In the first month of the spring of the first year of Jianwu, Fang Wang, a native of Pingling, made Liu Ying, a young boy of the former Han Dynasty, the emperor. Gengshi sent Prime Minister Li Song to attack him and kill Liu Ying.
Guangwu attacked Youlai, Daqiang, and Wuban Yuyuan in the north, and pursued them to Youbeiping, winning successive victories.
They also fought in the north along the river, taking advantage of the victory to easily advance, but were defeated.
The thieves followed closely, and Guangwu jumped to the high bank, where he met Wang Feng, a sudden rider. Wang Feng dismounted and gave his horse to Guangwu. Guangwu pressed Wang Feng's shoulders and mounted, turned around and smiled at Geng Yan and said: "I almost made the bandits laugh!"
Geng Yan shot repeatedly to drive back the enemy and avoid suffering. Thousands of soldiers died, and the remaining troops retreated to Fan Yang.
The troops could not see Guangwu. Some people said that Guangwu was dead, and the generals did not know what to do.
Wu Han said: "Everyone, please work hard. Brother Xiao Wang's son is in Nanyang. Why worry about having no owner!" Everyone was in panic and fear, and it took several days to calm down.
Although the thieves won the battle, they were always afraid of the glory of military power and did not understand each other's situation, so they led their troops away at night.
Guangwu marched to Anci again, fought with the enemy, defeated the enemy, and killed more than 3,000 people.
When the enemy retreated into Yuyang, Guangwu sent Wu Han commander Geng Yan, Chen Jun, Ma Wu and other twelve generals to pursue the enemy east of Lucheng and as far as Pinggu, where they destroyed Youlai and other tribes.
Zhu Tun sent the general Su Mao to attack Wencheng. Feng Yi and Kou Xun fought against him, defeated Su Mao's army and killed Su Mao's general Jia Qiang.
So the generals began to discuss the matter of Guangwu proclaiming himself emperor.
summary: Wang Mang sent Grand Situ Wang Xun and Grand Sikong Wang Yi with a massive army. Liu Xiu advised unity against the enemy, though generals initially resisted. With only 8,000-9,000 troops in Kunyang, Liu Xiu organized defenses and gathered reinforcements. Wang Mang's forces surrounded Kunyang with overwhelming numbers, using siege towers and tunnels. Despite the enemy's strength, Liu Xiu led a daring counterattack with 3,000 elite troops, breaking the enemy formation and killing Wang Xun. A storm aided the Han forces, causing panic and massive casualties among Wang Mang's army. When Wang Lang proclaimed himself emperor in Handan, Liu Xiu faced numerous hardships, including food shortages and dangerous river crossings. After gathering forces, he captured Handan and killed Wang Lang. He burned documents revealing officials' collaboration with Wang Lang, saying this would calm those who were anxious. As chaos spread across the empire, Liu Xiu pacified various rebel groups including the Bronze Horse Army. He won over surrendered troops by personally inspecting their camps, earning their loyalty. His forces grew to hundreds of thousands.

translation:
Guangwu took advantage of the situation and captured Yingyang County.
At this time, Liu Boxheng was killed by Liu Xuan, the Gengshi Emperor. Guangwu immediately rushed from his father city to Wancheng to apologize.
The officials of the Situ Mansion all came to express their condolences to Guangwu. Guangwu was not in a position to discuss anything with them in private, but he only blamed himself deeply.
He never boasted about his achievements in the Battle of Kunyang, nor did he dare to mourn for Bo Sheng. He ate, talked and laughed as naturally as usual.
Emperor Gengshi felt guilty about this, so he worshiped Guangwu as the general of Polu and named him Marquis of Wuxin.
On the third day of September, the three auxiliary heroes of Chang'an worked together to kill Wang Mang and sent his head to Wancheng.
Emperor Gengshi was about to go north to make his capital Luoyang, so he asked Guangwu to act as Sili Xiaowei and asked him to go to Luoyang first to repair the palace and government offices.
Guangwu then set up subordinate officials to draft official documents to conduct historical inspections and illegal affairs, and everything was handled according to the old system of the Han Dynasty.
At this time, the three auxiliary officials went east to welcome Emperor Gengshi. When they saw the generals passing by, they all wore civilian headscarves, women's clothes, large tie-ups and embroidered half-armor, and everyone laughed at them.
Some even run away in fear of disaster because of the ominous things they are convinced of. When they saw Guangwu's staff, they were all overjoyed.
Some old officials shed tears and said: "I didn't expect to see the majesty and grace of my Han officials again today!" From then on, all knowledgeable people turned to Guangwu.
When Gengshi arrived in Luoyang, he appointed Guangwu as General Polu to act as Grand Sima.
In October, Guangwu took the talisman and crossed the Yellow River to the north to calm the officials and people of the prefecture and county.
When arriving at a county, he would meet with the county governor, chief officials, three elders, officials, and officials, down to the assistant historian, to inspect promotion matters, just like a state herdsman inspecting the county to handle affairs.
He vindicated wrongful cases, released prisoners, got rid of Wang Mang's harsh rule, and restored the official title of the Han Dynasty. The officials and the people were happy, and they rushed to greet them with cattle and wine.
When they arrived at Handan, Liu Lin, the son of the late King Mu of Zhao, offered advice to Guangwu: The Red Eyebrow Army is now in the east of the river. As long as the Yellow River is opened to flood them, the Red Eyebrow Army of millions will become fish and shrimps in an instant. Guangwu didn't answer and left Handan for Zhending.
Zhao Lin asked Wang Lang, who was engaged in divination, to pretend to be Liu Ziyu, the son of the emperor. In December, he proclaimed Wang Lang the emperor, made Handan his capital, and sent envoys to persuade the counties to surrender.
In the first month of the second year of Gengshi, Guangwu went north to inspect Jidi because of Wang Lang's new rise.
Wang Lang issued a proclamation, promising to kill those who captured Guangwu and grant him the title of 100,000 households. Liu Jie, the son of the late King Liu Jia of Guangyang, raised an army in Jizhong to support the king. The city of Jicheng was disrupted and the people were frightened. It was also said that an envoy from Handan had just arrived, and officials with a weight of less than two thousand stones went out to welcome him.
summary: After Bo Sheng was killed by Emperor Gengshi, Liu Xiu rushed to apologize without boasting of his achievements. Emperor Gengshi appointed him General Polu and Marquis of Wuxin. When sent to Luoyang, Liu Xiu restored Han dynasty administrative practices, winning popular support. He crossed the Yellow River to pacify northern regions, releasing prisoners and abolishing Wang Mang's harsh policies.

In 213, Cao Cao became Duke of Wei. In 214, Cao Cao killed Empress Fu. In 215, Cao Cao captured Hanzhong. In 216, Cao Cao became King of Wei. In 220, Cao Cao died, and his son Cao Pi succeeded. God's law is trustworthy, and your family will definitely receive blessings. In the past, Taifu Deng Yu once said with emotion: I command millions of people and have never killed anyone indiscriminately. Some of my descendants will be prosperous.
In the seventh year of Emperor Yongyuan's reign, Deng Sui was selected into the palace together with the women of various families.
She was seven feet two inches tall, very beautiful and outstanding, and everyone was surprised.
In the winter of the eighth year of Yongyuan, he entered Yeting as a nobleman at the age of sixteen.
summary: Queen Yin, great-niece of Queen Guanglie, was deposed for witchcraft and died in sorrow. Queen Hexi Deng, granddaughter of Tai Fu Deng Yu, was known for her intelligence and virtue. She entered the palace at sixteen, serving Queen Yin humbly. After Yin's deposition, she became queen, banning luxury and refusing to ennoble her family. As empress dowager, she ruled during crises, reducing expenses, pardoning exiles, and promoting education. She died at forty-one, buried with Emperor He. Historians criticize her for holding power too long, leading to resentment, but acknowledge her efforts to stabilize the state.

translation:
An Si Yan Queen Yan Ji was born in Xingyang, Henan.
Grandfather Yan Zhang was the minister in Yongpingzhong, and his second sister was a nobleman.
Yan Zhang was proficient in the old canons and had not been promoted to an important position for a long time. He should have been promoted to an important position. However, Emperor Xianzong and Ming Emperor considered him a relative of the harem, so he did not use it and became an infantry captain.
Yan Zhang gave birth to Yan Chang, and Yan Chang gave birth to Queen Yan Ji.
Yan Ji has talent and beautiful appearance.
In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty of Emperor An, he was selected to join Ye Ting, where he was favored and considered a noble person.
In the second year of Yuan Dynasty, she was established as queen.
Queen Yan wanted to monopolize Emperor An's special favor and was deeply jealous. Emperor An favored the Li family in the palace and gave birth to the prince Liu Bao, so Queen Yan poisoned Li family.
In the third year of the Yuan Dynasty, he appointed Yan Chang, Queen Yan's father, as the Shizhong of Changshui. He was granted the title of Marquis of Northern Yichun and had a settlement of 5,000 households.
In the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, Yan Chang died. His posthumous title was Wenhou, and he was succeeded by his son Yan Xian.
In the first year of Emperor An's reign, Empress Dowager Deng passed away, and Emperor An began to take charge of political affairs.
Yan Xian and his younger brothers Yan Jing, Yan Yao and Yan Yan were all in charge of the Imperial Guards.
In the first year of Emperor An's reign of Yanguang, Yan Xian was granted the title of Marquis of Changshe, with a settlement of 13,500 households, and the title of Queen Yan's mother was the Lord of Xingyang.
The sons of Yan Xian and Yan Jing were only eight years old, and they were appointed as ministers of Huangmen.
Queen Yan was particularly favored by Emperor An, and her brothers also participated in the government. However, Queen Yan still worked with Dachangqiu Jiang Jing, Zhongchang Shi Fan Feng and others to slander the crown prince Liu Bao and deposed him as King Jiyin.
In the spring of the fourth year of Emperor An's reign, Queen Yan followed Emperor An to Zhangling. Emperor An fell ill on the way and died in Ye County.
Queen Yan, brothers Yan Xian, Jiang Jing, Fan Feng and others planned and said: Now that the emperor has died on the journey, King Jiyin is in the capital, and the ministers meet unexpectedly and make him emperor. Wouldn't it be a big disaster?
So he lied that Emperor An was seriously ill and carried him to the sleeping car. After walking for four days, the carriages and horses were hauled back to Beijing in a hurry.
The next day, he sent Situ Liu Xi to the suburban temple Sheji to appeal to heaven for orders.
This evening, there was a funeral for Emperor An.
The empress dowager Yan was respected as the empress dowager. When the empress dowager came to the court, Yan Xian was appointed as the chariot and cavalry general. The ritual system was the same as that of the three princes.
The Empress Dowager Yan wanted to exclusively take charge of the country's affairs for a long time, so she was greedy for the throne at a young age. She made a plan with Yan Xian and others to ban her. She welcomed Liu Yi, the Marquis of Beixiang, Prince Hui of Jibei, and was established as emperor.
Yan Xian and others were afraid that General Geng Bao would be respected in his position and be powerful in the An Dynasty, so he quietly signaled the officials to join Geng Bao and his party, Chang Shi Fan Feng, Huben Zhonglang General Xie Yun, Yun's brother Shi Zhong Xie Du, and General Dudi General Shi. Xie Mi, the minister Zhou Guang, the emperor's wet nurse Yewang Wang Sheng, Wang Shengnu Yong, Yong's son-in-law Huangmen's minister Fan Yan, etc., have personal favors with each other, form cliques for personal gain, dominate each other, spy on forbidden secrets, echo and sing, and are treasonous.
Fan Feng, Xie Yun, and Zhou Guang were all imprisoned and died, and their families were exiled to Bijing; Xie Mi and Fan Yan were punished with the penalty of having their hair shaved off and having their necks tied with iron rings; Geng Bao was demoted to the rank of Zetinghou, and was sent to the country to be enfeoffed, forcing Geng Bao to commit suicide; Wang Shengsheng and his son were exiled to Yanmen.
So Yan Jing was appointed as the guard, Yan Yao was appointed as the city gate captain, and Yan Yan was appointed as the commander Jinwu. The brothers were all in positions of authority, dominating and enjoying freedom.
More than two hundred days after Beixiang Hou Liu Yi became emperor, he became seriously ill. Yan Xian brothers, Jiang Jing and others were all around him.
Jiang Jing took Yan Xian to avoid people and said: "The Marquis of Beixiang's illness will not be cured, and who will succeed the throne should be decided as soon as possible."
He did not establish King Jiyin before, but if he is established as emperor now, he will definitely hold a grudge in the future. Why not quickly recruit many princes to select a suitable one who can inherit the throne?
After hearing this, Yan Xian felt that he was right. When the young emperor Beixiang Hou died, Jiang Jing told Queen Mother Yan to recruit the princes of Jibei and Hejian.
But before they could reach the capital, Sun Cheng and others from Zhonghuang Gate conspired to murder Jiang Jing and others, and established King Jiyin as Emperor Shun.
Yan Xian, Yan Jing, Yan Yan and their accomplices were executed. The Queen Mother Yan moved to the palace and her family members were exiled to Bijing.
The following year, Queen Mother Yan died. After reigning for 12 years, she was buried in Gongling Mausoleum with Emperor An.
Emperor Shun Liu Bao's mother, Li, was buried in the north of Luoyang City. Emperor Shun didn't know about it, and no one dared to tell him.
When Empress Dowager Yan passed away, people around her told him that Emperor Shun was awakened and felt sad, so he went to the burial site in person and held the funeral ceremony again. She was posthumously named Empress Gongmin and was buried in Gongbeiling. A golden cabinet for policy books was hidden in the Shizu Temple.
summary: An Si Yan, Queen Yan Ji, was born in Xingyang, Henan. Her grandfather Yan Zhang served as a minister but was never promoted to an important position because Emperor Xianzong considered him a relative of the harem. Yan Ji possessed talent and beauty, and was selected to enter the palace in the first year of Emperor An's Yuan Dynasty. She became empress in the second year. Queen Yan monopolized Emperor An's favor and poisoned the Li family, who had given birth to Prince Liu Bao. After Emperor An's death, Queen Yan and her brothers conspired to conceal his death, then established Liu Yi, the Marquis of Beixiang, as emperor. When the young emperor died, Sun Cheng and others conspired to establish Prince Liu Bao as Emperor Shun. Yan Xian and his accomplices were executed, and Queen Yan was moved to another palace, dying the following year after reigning for twelve years.

translation:
At this time, bandits from Yangzhou and Xu Feng from Jiujiang were invading the prefectures and counties. Barbarians from Xiqiang, Xianbei and Rinan attacked the city and looted the city. There were many types of land taxes and taxes. The officials and the people were in poverty.
The Empress Dowager Liang worked hard day and night, treated people with sincerity, trusted the wise men in their elder years, and appointed Lieutenant Li Gu to select loyal and virtuous people, and she must practice frugality.
The scum who are greedy for money and treacherous are often killed or dismissed.
There were bandits who gathered to make trouble and divided their troops to fight against them, but they were all eliminated and put down.
Therefore, the world is at peace, and the ancestral temple and the country are at peace.
However, the Empress Dowager Liang's brother, General Liang Ji, actually poisoned Emperor Zhi and killed Emperor Zhi. He was dictatorial and tyrannical, and hated Zhongliang.
The Empress Dowager Liang also doted on the eunuchs and granted them titles and titles. As a result, the world was disappointed and unpopular.
In the spring of the first year of Heping, the Empress Dowager Liang returned to power under Emperor Huan. Due to her serious illness, she took a chariot to the Xuande Hall and summoned the ministers, Zhongshu and other officials in the palace as well as the Liang brothers.
The edict was issued saying: I have an old ailment of qi in my heart, which has recently become swollen, and I don't like to eat. I am becoming more and more heavy and sleepy, which makes me both inside and outside pray for me.
After thinking about it, I feel that I am weak day and night, and I am afraid that I will no longer be able to meet the princes and ministers.
A wise emperor has been established to inherit the great rule. I only regret that I cannot educate him for a long time, so I can see his present and future.
Today, the emperor and the general brothers have entrusted the ministers to encourage each other. Two days later, Empress Dowager Liang died.
He reigned for nineteen years and died at the age of forty-five.
Buried in Xianling Mausoleum with Emperor Shun.
The poppy was selected into Yeting at the age of thirteen as a girl from a good family, and she gave birth to Emperor Chong and another daughter, Princess Wuyang.
Since the founding of the Han Dynasty, the mother family has always respected and favored her.
Emperor Shun did not add the title of Meiren, and Emperor Chong died young. The general Liang Ji took over as regent, and was afraid of other noble families. Therefore, the Yu family was suppressed and could not be promoted, but was called "everyone".
Mrs. Chen was born in Wei County. When she was young, she entered the Palace of Xiao Wang Liu Hong as a vocal performer. She was favored and became Emperor Zhi.
Also because of the Liang family, he could not get honor and favor.
In the fourth year of Xiping reign of Emperor Ling, Zhao You of Xiaohuangmen wrote a letter to Yilang Beizheng, saying: The meaning of "Spring and Autumn" is that mother is more valuable than son.
During the grand ceremony of the Long Han Dynasty, the mother's family was respected, and all relatives were given honors and favors.
Jin Chong Emperor's mother, Yu Jiajia, and Zhi Emperor's mother, Mrs. Chen, both gave birth to holy emperors, but did not have titles.
summary: Empress Shunlie Liang was the daughter of Liang Shang. From a young age, she was intelligent, well-read in historical records and classics, and kept pictures of virtuous women for self-reflection. At thirteen, she was selected to enter the palace. Emperor Shun made her a noble and later established her as empress. Empress Liang was humble and cautious, declining to monopolize the emperor's favor. After Emperor Shun's death, she became empress dowager and governed during the reigns of Emperors Chong and Zhi. She worked diligently, appointed worthy officials, and suppressed bandit uprisings, bringing peace to the realm. However, her brother Liang Ji poisoned Emperor Zhi and became tyrannical. Empress Dowager Liang also favored eunuchs excessively, causing public disappointment. She died after nineteen years of reign at age forty-five.

translation:
In June of the first year of Jianhe, Liang Nuying entered Yeting and was established as queen in August.
At that time, the Empress Dowager Liang was in charge of the government, and Liang Ji was in power. Therefore, the Empress Dowager Liang was the only one favored, and no one from the concubines down could share the emperor's favor.
Relying on the shelter and influence of her elder sisters and brothers, Empress Liang indulged in extravagance. The palaces were decorated with colorful decorations, the curtains were gorgeous, the clothes were precious, and the utensils were luxurious, doubling the previous ones.
After the death of Empress Dowager Liang, Emperor Huan's love for her gradually declined.
Empress Liang had no sons of her own, and she harbored secret resentment and jealousy. The palace concubines gave birth to sons, but few were able to survive.
Although Emperor Huan was persecuted and feared Liang Ji, he did not dare to criticize and anger Empress Liang. However, he was fortunate to see Liang Empress rarely in person.
In the second year of Yanxi, Empress Liang died of sorrow and hatred. After reigning for thirteen years, she was buried in Yiling.
In this year, Liang Ji was executed and Yiling was abandoned as a tomb for nobles.
Deng Meng's daughter, Empress Huan Deng, was the daughter of Deng Xiang, cousin of Empress He Xi.
Her mother's name is Xuan. She married Deng Xiang first and gave birth to a fierce daughter.
Remarried Liang Ji, who was the uncle of Sun Shou, the wife of General Liang Ji.
Deng Meng's daughter lost her father when she was young. She followed her mother to live in Liang Ji's house, so she assumed the surname Liang.
Sun Shou, the wife of Liang Ji, saw that Deng Meng's daughter was beautiful. Emperor Huan entered Yeting in Yongxing and became a prostitute. She was extremely favored by Emperor Huan.
In the second year, Deng Yan, Deng Meng's daughter brother, was granted the title of Marquis of Nanton, a special advancement.
Deng Yan died and was succeeded by his son Deng Kang.
When Queen Liang Nuying of Yixian Liang passed away, Liang Ji was executed, and Deng Mengnu was established as queen.
Emperor Huan hated the Liang family so much that he changed the queen's surname to Bo and granted the title of Queen of Chang'an to the mother of Queen Deng.
In the fourth year, the steward told Queen Deng that it was not appropriate to change her surname to the daughter of Deng Xiang, one of Queen Deng's doctors, so the surname was restored to Deng.
Deng Xiang's chariot and cavalry general Anyang Hou Yinshou was posthumously granted the title, and his mother Xuan and nephew Deng Kang were granted the title of Grand County.
Announcement of death, carriages, horses, money, and funerals were all carried out according to the Queen's mother's funeral arrangements.
Deng Kang's younger brother Deng Tong was granted the title of Marquis of Kunyang, with the title of Shizhong; Deng Tong's cousin Deng Hui was granted the title of Marquis of Anyang, and he was granted the title of Huben Zhonglang General; Deng Tong's younger brother Deng Bing was also granted the title of Marquis of Yuyang.
The Deng clan is ranked among the top schools and generals.
Emperor Huan was favored by many, and he had as many as five or six thousand maids in his palace, and many times as many as he commanded and followed.
Empress Deng relied on her high position to be arrogant and jealous, and framed and accused each other with Guo Guiren, who was favored by Emperor Huan.
In the eighth year of Yanxi's reign, after Emperor Huan's edict was abolished, he was sent to Ye Ting to be raped and died of melancholy.
summary: Empress Huan Yi Xian Liang, sister of Empress Shunlie, was married to Emperor Huan while Empress Dowager Liang governed. She relied on her sister's influence, indulged in extravagance, and was jealous of concubines who bore sons. After Empress Dowager Liang's death, Emperor Huan's favor diminished, and she died of sorrow after thirteen years. Empress Huan Deng, daughter of Deng Xiang, was raised in Liang Ji's household. She entered the palace and was greatly favored. After Queen Liang's death, she became empress. Emperor Huan later hated the Liang family and changed her surname to Bo, but later restored it to Deng. She was arrogant and jealous, and was deposed after seven years, dying in confinement.

translation:
Became queen for seven years.
Buried in Beimang.
Empress Deng's uncles, Henan Yin Deng Wanshi and Huben Zhonglang, imprisoned Deng Hui and died.
Deng Tong was also detained in the violent chamber, removed from the title of Marquis of Kunyang and the official position of Shizhong, and was sent back to his own county. His property was confiscated.
Queen Huansi Dou Miao, the granddaughter of Queen Zhangde's ancestral brother, and her father Dou Wu.
In the eighth year of Yanxi reign of Emperor Huan, Empress Deng and Deng Meng were deposed, and Dou Miao was elected to Yeting as a noble. In the winter of that year, she was established as a queen. Emperor Huan seldom favored her. The most favored by Emperor Huan were Cai Nv Tian Sheng and others.
Emperor Huan died without heirs, and Empress Dou became the empress dowager.
The Queen Mother made a decision before the court and appointed Liu Hong, Marquis of Jieduting, as the Ling Emperor.
Empress Dowager Dou was jealous and cruel by nature, and she was angry with Tian Sheng and others. When Emperor Huan's coffin was still in the front hall, she killed Tian Sheng.
He also wanted to kill all the nobles, but the ministers Guan Ba ​​and Su Kang tried hard to persuade him, so he did not take action.
At this time, Dou Wu, Empress Dowager Dou's father, conspired to kill the eunuchs. However, Cao Jie and others falsely claimed that Emperor Ling's edict had been issued to kill Dou Wu. Empress Dowager Dou was moved to Nangong Yuntai, and her family was exiled to Bijing.
Although Dou Wu was executed, Emperor Ling still remembered Empress Dowager Dou's contribution to establishing him as emperor. On the first day of October in the fourth year of Jianning, he led his ministers to go to the Nangong Palace to congratulate the Empress Dowager on her birthday.
Huangmen ordered Dong Meng to express his grievances to the Queen Mother many times. Emperor Ling accepted them one by one, and the support and funds were increased than before.
The ministers Cao Jie and Wang Fuji hated Dong Meng for helping Empress Dowager Dou, so they framed him for slandering the Yongle Palace where Emperor Ling's mother lived. Dong Meng was imprisoned and died for his crime.
In the first year of Xiping, Queen Mother Dou's mother died in Bijing, and the Queen Mother died of illness.
Stand for seven years.
Buried in Xuanling together with Emperor Huan.
Empress Xiaoren Dong was from Hejian.
To Mrs. Chang, the Marquis of Jieduting, she gave birth to Emperor Ling.
In the first year of Jianning, Emperor Ling came to the throne and honored Chang as Emperor Xiaoren. The mausoleum was named Shenling. Later, he was named Shenyuan nobleman until Dou Wu was executed. In the second year, Emperor Ling sent Zhong Changshi to welcome the nobleman and recruited Dong Chong, the nobleman's brother, to the capital. He was named Empress Xiaoren and lived in the Jiade Hall of Nangong. The palace was called Yongle.
He worshiped Dong Chong as his successor King Wu.
Later, he falsely claimed that he was a subordinate of Yongle Empress, and died after being imprisoned.
After the death of Empress Dowager Dou, Empress Xiaoren participated in the affairs of the court, causing the emperor to sell his officials to obtain property, and to collect money from himself, the palace was full.
In the fifth year of Emperor Zhongping's reign, Empress Xiaoren's brother, Weiwei Xiuhou Dong Chong, was appointed as the hussar general, leading more than a thousand troops.
At first, Empress Xiaoren raised her own prince Liu Xie and repeatedly urged the emperor to establish him as the crown prince. However, Empress He was resentful and Emperor Ling died before the agreement was reached.
When Empress Dowager He came to the court, Dong Chong was in conflict with the power of General He Jin, Empress Dowager He's brother. Every time Empress Xiaoren wanted to interfere in political affairs, Empress Dowager He forbade her to stop him.
Queen Xiaoren cursed angrily: Are you so domineering now, relying on your brother's power?
summary: Empress Huansi Dou Miao, granddaughter of Queen Zhangde's brother, was established as empress in the eighth year of Yanxi. Emperor Huan rarely favored her. After Emperor Huan's death, she became empress dowager and established Emperor Ling. She was jealous and cruel, killing favored concubines. Her father Dou Wu conspired to kill eunuchs but was executed. Empress Dowager Dou was moved to Nangong and died after seven years. Empress Xiaoren Dong gave birth to Emperor Ling and was honored as empress dowager. She participated in court affairs, sold offices, and collected wealth. She favored Prince Liu Xie and urged Emperor Ling to make him crown prince, causing conflict with Empress He. After Empress Dowager He came to court, Dong was worried and fell ill, dying after twenty-two years.

translation:
Liu Kui, King of Bohai, was the younger brother of Emperor Huan's mother. He had never made any mistakes in handling the affairs of the feudal state and serving the court as a vassal. However, His Majesty had him convicted and executed without verification and scrutiny.
In the past, the Marquis of Jin dreamed of a big fierce ghost with long hair that reached the ground. It was because the Marquis of Jin had killed the ancestors of the fierce ghosts.
The moral principles between heaven and earth are clear, and it is difficult for ghosts and gods to deceive them.
They should be reburied together so that the innocent souls can rest in peace. Let Queen Song's exiled relatives return to their place of origin and restore the title of King Bohai, in order to eliminate the blame caused by this. Emperor Ling did not listen to Xu Yong's advice, and Emperor Ling died soon after.
Queen Lingsi He was from Wancheng, Nanyang.
The family was originally a butcher of pigs, so he was selected to join Yeting with bribes of gold and silk.
Seven feet and one inch long, he gave birth to the prince Liu Bian. He was raised in a Shidao family and was named Shihou.
Therefore, he became a nobleman and was favored by Emperor Ling.
She has a strong and fierce personality, and all the concubines in the harem are afraid of her.
In the third year of Guanghe's reign, she was established as queen.
The next year, her father He Zhen was granted the title of Chariot and Cavalry General and Wuyang Xuandehou, and her mother Xing was granted the title of Wuyang Lord.
At this time, Wang Meiren was pregnant and was afraid of Queen He's murder, so she took abortion pills in an attempt to abort the fetus, but the fetus was safe and motionless. She also dreamed of walking with the sun on her back many times.
In the fourth year of Guanghe's reign, the prince Liu Xie was born, and Queen He poisoned Wang Meiren to death.
The Ling Emperor was furious and wanted to depose Queen He, but the eunuchs repeatedly begged the Ling Emperor for mercy.
Empress Dowager Dong personally raised Liu Xie and named him Hou Dong.
Wang Meiren, a native of Zhao.
Grandfather Wang Bao, a general with great facial features.
Wang Meiren is beautiful, smart, talented, and can write and do calculations. She is a good family member who conforms to the law and is selected into Yeting.
Emperor Ling felt sorry for Liu Xie's early loss of his mother, and missed Wang Meiren in his heart. He wrote "Ode to Pursuing De" and "Ode to Lingyi" to express his grief.
In the sixth year of Zhongping, Emperor Ling died, and Prince Liu Bian came to the throne, respecting Queen He as the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother comes to court.
The Queen Mother's brother, General He Jin, tried to kill the eunuchs, but He Jin was killed by the eunuchs. He's mother, Wuyang Jun, was also killed by the rebels.
Bingzhou Mu Dong Zhuo was recruited, led troops into Luoyang, ravaged the court, deposed the young emperor Liu Bian as the Hongnong King, and established Liu Xie as Emperor Xian.
Dong Zhuo helped King Hongnong go down to the palace and became a minister in the north.
Empress Dowager He choked with tears, and the ministers were sad and did not dare to say a word.
Dong Zhuo also criticized the Empress Dowager He for forcing Xiaoren Empress Dong to live in Yongle Palace, causing her to die of grief and anger, violating the filial piety that a daughter-in-law should have to her aunt, so he moved the Empress Dowager He to the Yong'an Palace and killed her with poison. She reigned for ten years.
Dong Zhuo called Emperor Xian to mourn at Fengchang Pavilion. All the ministers came to court in plain clothes. Without a funeral letter, it would not be a funeral.
summary: Empress Ling Song was established as empress in the third year of Jianning but was not favored. She was falsely accused of witchcraft and died in confinement after eight years. Her father and brothers were killed. Emperor Ling later dreamed of Emperor Huan rebuking him for this injustice. Empress Lingsi He, from a butcher family, entered the palace through bribery. She gave birth to Prince Liu Bian and became empress. She was strong and fierce, poisoning Wang Meiren who gave birth to Prince Liu Xie. After Emperor Ling's death, Prince Liu Bian succeeded, and Queen He became empress dowager. Her brother He Jin was killed by eunuchs. Dong Zhuo entered Luoyang, deposed the young emperor, established Emperor Xian, and poisoned Empress Dowager He after ten years of reign.

translation:
Queen Fu saw this situation and felt fear from then on. So she wrote a letter to her father, telling her about Cao Cao's brutal persecution and asking her father to make a secret plan to eradicate Cao Cao.
Fu Wan didn't dare to take action. By the 19th year, the secret was revealed.
Cao Cao was furious after the investigation, so he forced Emperor Xian to depose Empress Fu, and wrote a fake policy saying: Empress Fu Shou entered the palace from a humble position, and even ascended to the throne of empress and became prominent. It has been twenty-four years now.
She does not have the beauty of Huiyin like Queen Mother Wen and Queen Mother Wu, and lacks the blessings of careful self-cultivation and comfort. However, she harbors jealousy and harbors evil intentions insidiously, and cannot fulfill the destiny and worship the ancestors.
Now, Xi Lu, the imperial censor, is sent to hold Fu Jie Ce and write an edict, hand over the queen's seal and ribbon, retreat to the central palace, and move to other buildings. Alas!
How sad!
I took the blame for my life on my own and was not put on trial. I'm so lucky! He also appointed Shangshu Ling Hua Xin as hope Zanli's deputy and led his troops into the palace to arrest the ambush queen.
Fu Hou closed the door and hid in the wall. Hua Xin stretched out his hand to pull Fu Hou out.
At that time, Emperor Xian was in the outer hall and led Xi Cun to his seat.
After lying down and walking barefoot on foot, he passed by Emperor Xian and cried, saying goodbye and saying: "Can't you let me live anymore?"
Emperor Xian said: I don’t know how long my life can last! Looking back at Xi Lu, he said: Mr. Xi!
Is there such a thing in the world? So Cao Cao buried his queen in a violent chamber in Yeting, where he died under house arrest. The two princes he gave birth to were both poisoned and killed. Fu Hou reigned for twenty years, and more than a hundred of her brothers and clan members died. Nineteen of her mother and others were exiled to Zhuojun.
Cao Jie, Queen of Xianmu Cao, was the middle daughter of Duke Cao Cao of Wei.
In the 18th year of Jian'an, Cao Cao adopted three daughters, Cao Xian, Cao Jie, and Cao Huahua, as wives, and hired them to make 50,000 pieces of silk, Xuanjin and fumigation. The younger ones stayed in the country to wait until they were older.
In the 19th year of Jian'an, we worshiped each other as nobles.
When Queen Fu was killed, the next year, Cao Jie was made queen.
When Wei accepted the throne of Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty, he sent an envoy to ask for the seal and ribbon, but Queen Cao Jie was angry and refused to give it.
After chasing the seal for several times, Empress Cao called the envoy in, scolded her personally, and threw the seal under the pavilion, crying and saying: God will not let you last long! Everyone present could not bear to look up at Queen Cao.
Queen Cao reigned for seven years.
After Cao Wei won the throne, he made Queen Cao the Duke of Shanyang.
Forty-one years later, Wei Jingyuan died in the first year of his life and was buried in the Zen Mausoleum together with Emperor Xian. The carriages, clothing, and etiquette were all based on the Han system.
Historians commented: The queens of the Han Dynasty did not have posthumous titles, and they were all given titles based on the emperor's posthumous title.
Although Emperor Gaozu and Empress Lu were in dictatorship, Emperor Zhao, Shangguan and Empress came to the court and had no special titles.
After Guangwu Zhongxing and Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne, he established the title of Guanglie for his mother, Queen Guangwuyin, and called her Queen Guanglieyin. Since then, virtue has been used as a match. As for the good and the foolish, the confusion has always been like this. Therefore, Empress Ma of Emperor Ming was called Empress Ma of Mingde; Empress Zhang of Emperor Dou was called Empress Zhang Dedou. They were all named after virtue.
The rest were only the emperor's concubine's mother and the Tibetan king Chengtong, who valued honor and had unique titles. For example, the emperor's mother, Zhang Diliang, was honored as empress Gonghuai and Xiaojing; the emperor Huan's mother, Liwuhou Liu Ji's concubine Ming, was honored as empress Xiaochong.
During the reign of Emperor Xian, Cai Yong began to pursue the posthumous title of Empress Deng Sui of Emperor Zhenghe as Empress Hexi Deng. From then on, empress Yanji of Emperor An was empress An Siyan, and empress Shun Di Liang's wife was empress Shunlie Liang. They were all given posthumous titles accordingly.
Historians praised: Kun is the earth, and its valuable thing is that it is heavy; Yin refers to women, and her responsibility is to be in the inner position. The "Book of Songs" says that the concubine is the wife of a gentleman because of her virtues;
Many concubines were married to the emperor to show their loyalty and virtuousness.
summary: Empress Xian Fu Shou entered the palace as a noble and became empress in the second year of Xingping. She witnessed Cao Cao's brutality and wrote to her father asking him to eliminate Cao Cao. The secret was revealed after nineteen years. Cao Cao forced Emperor Xian to depose her, and she died in confinement. Her two sons were poisoned, and over a hundred of her relatives died. Empress Xianmu Cao, daughter of Cao Cao, became empress after Fu Shou's death. When Wei accepted the Han throne, she angrily refused to give up the seal and threw it under the pavilion. She reigned for seven years and was later made Duchess of Shanyang, dying forty-one years later.

translation:

summary: A cattle plague and severe drought struck the capital and three prefectures, leading to exemptions from land rent and aid for the poor.
