Queen Huijia was named Nanfeng, a native of Pingyang, and her nickname was Qing. There is another biography about his father, Jia Chong.
At first, Emperor Wu wanted to marry Wei Xuan's daughter for the crown prince. Empress Yuan listened to the persuasion of Mai and Guo's cronies and wanted to marry Mai.
Emperor Wu said: There are five things that are desirable about the daughter of Duke Wei, and there are five things that are undesirable about the daughter of Duke Jia.
The descendants of the Wei family are virtuous and have many children, and are beautiful in appearance and slender in stature.
Empress Yuan insisted on her request, and both Xunja and Xunxu praised Jia Chong's daughter for being virtuous, so they made an engagement.
At first, he wanted to marry Jia Wu, Empress Jia's sister. Jia Wu was twelve years old at the time, one year younger than the prince, and was too short to wear adult clothes.
So she married Nan Feng, who was fifteen years old at the time and two years older than the prince.
In the second month of the eighth year of Taishi (Xinmao), she was granted the title of Crown Princess.
She was jealous and cunning by nature, and the prince was both afraid of and beguiled by her. Few of the concubines were favored by the prince.
Emperor Wu often suspected that the prince was not smart, and officials in the court and Wei and others also made Zao a topic many times, so he wanted to test him.
All the officials from Shu Palace were summoned, a banquet was arranged, and a difficult matter was sealed, allowing the prince to make a decision, and the messenger stopped to wait for an answer.
Concubine Jia was very panicked and asked an outsider to answer for her.
Most of the people who responded quoted ancient meanings.
Zhang Hong, the envoy, said: The prince is not a good learner, but he can quote ancient meanings when answering Shao Shu. The Holy Emperor will definitely track down the person who answered on his behalf, and the punishment will be even more serious.
It's better to answer directly based on the meaning.
Concubine Jia was very happy and said to Zhang Hong: "Answer me well immediately. If I get rich in the future, I will share it with you."
Zhang Hong, who had always been a little talented, drew up a draft and asked the prince to copy it by himself.
Emperor Wu was very happy after seeing it.
First, he showed it to the prince's young master, Wei Cui. Wei Xuan was very uneasy. Only then did everyone realize that Wei Cui had said something dissatisfied with the prince before, and everyone in the palace shouted long live.
Jia Chong secretly sent someone to tell Concubine Jia: "This old guy Wei Cui almost destroyed our family."
Concubine Mai was very cruel by nature and had killed several people with her own hands.
summary: Queen Huijia, named Nanfeng, was married to the crown prince despite Emperor Wu's reservations. She was jealous and cruel, killing several people with her own hands and causing a pregnant concubine to miscarry. After becoming empress, she grew increasingly dissolute, engaging in affairs with physicians and luring young men into the palace. She conspired against the crown prince and was eventually deposed and forced to commit suicide by King Zhao Sima Lun.

translation:
I hope that your majesty will have a detailed review with Dazai again, so as not to cause doubts among people near and far and cause resentment in the world.
Sima Yi was very angry after seeing the memorial, so he sent Chen Yan and Lu Langdong to arrest Liu Tun.
Liu Tun fled to Qingzhou, and Queen Yang was able to avoid death. Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang, welcomed back the sheep, and resumed his post.
Later, Luoyang ordered He Qiao to depose the Sheep Queen.
On the day Zhang Fang's head was delivered, she was restored to the position of queen.
When Emperor Hui died, the queen was worried that her brother-in-law would become uncle and sister-in-law after succeeding to the throne, and she would not be able to be called the queen mother, so she urged the former prince Sima Tan, King of Qinghe, to enter the capital and prepare to establish himself as emperor, but failed.
After Emperor Huai ascended the throne, he honored Queen Sheep as Queen Hui and let her live in Hongxun Palace.
Luoyang was defeated and the queen fell into Liu Yao's hands.
Liu Yao arrogantly proclaimed himself emperor and made the Sheep Queen his queen.
He once asked: How am I compared to the boys from the Sima family?
The queen said: How can they be compared?
Your Majesty is the holy master who founded the business, but he is a foolish man who has subjugated his country. He only has a wife, a son and himself, and he cannot protect him. I was honored as an emperor, but my wife and children were humiliated at the hands of ordinary people. I really didn't want to live anymore at that time, and I never imagined that I would still be here today.
I was born into a noble family and often thought that all men in the world were like that.
Since I became your wife, I have known that there are men in the world.
Liu Yao doted on her very much. After giving birth to Liu Yao's two sons, she died and Mi was made Queen Xianwen.
Mrs. Xie’s name is Xie Jiu.
The family was originally very poor, and his father made a living by killing sheep. Xie Jiu is pure, virtuous, upright and beautiful, and was selected into the harem as a talented person.
When Emperor Hui was in the Cambodian palace, he was preparing to accept a concubine.
Emperor Wu was worried that the prince was young and did not understand the affairs of the boudoir, so he sent Xie Jiu to serve in Shu Palace, and she was lucky to be pregnant.
After buying her, Xie Jiu was jealous of her and asked to return to the West Palace. She gave birth to Prince Minhuai, who was three or four years old, but Emperor Hui didn't know it yet.
When he entered the court, he saw Minhuai playing with the princes and took his hand. Emperor Wu said: "This is your son."
After being established as the prince, Xie Jiu was granted the title Shuyuan.
Empress Jia did not allow the prince to see Xie Jiu and kept her alone in a room.
Feeling sorry for the misfortune of the prince. Xie Jiu was also killed.
In the early years of Yongkang, an edict was issued to rebury the prince, so he posthumously presented Mrs. Xie Jiu with a seal ribbon and buried him in the Xianping Mausoleum.
The Empress Dowager of King Huai was named Xie Tan, but her life experience was unknown.
He was selected into Emperor Wu's harem as a talented person and died very young.
After Emperor Huai ascended the throne, he was posthumously named the Empress Dowager.
summary: Queen Huiyang, named Xianrong, was established as queen in the first year of Tai'an but was deposed and restored multiple times amid political turmoil. After Emperor Hui's death, she attempted to install a different successor but failed. When Luoyang fell, she was taken by Liu Yao, who made her his queen. Mrs. Xie, named Xie Jiu, from a poor family, was selected as a talented person and sent to serve the prince, bearing Prince Minhuai. Empress Jia kept her isolated, and she was eventually killed. The text concludes with brief accounts of Empress Dowager Huai, named Xie Tan, who died young and was posthumously honored, and the concubine of Marquis Yuanxia, named Guangji, who married into the Langye royal family and bore Emperor Yuan.

translation:
◎Clan Anping Xian Wang Fu Pengcheng Mu Wang Quan Gaoden Documents Wang Tai Jinan King Hui Sui Qiao Gang Wang Xun
Anping Xianwang Sima Fu, courtesy name Shuda, was the second brother of Emperor Xuan.
At the beginning, Sima Fu's eldest brother Sima Lang was known as Boda, Emperor Xuan was known as Zhongda, Sima Fu's younger brother Sima Kui was known as Jida, Sima Xun was known as Xianda, Sima Jin was known as Huida, Sima Tong was known as Yada, and Sima Min was known as Youda. They were all famous, so they were known as Bada at that time.
Sima Fu was gentle, honest, upright and modest, and read widely classic historical books.
In the last years of the Han Dynasty, there was death and turmoil, and he and his brothers were in danger. They had only a simple diet, but read tirelessly.
He has an open-minded and tolerant personality, takes chastity and innocence as the foundation of his life, and has never had any grudges with others.
Yin Wu, a native of Chenliu, was well-known in the country and had been punished. Sima Fu went to visit him, so he ate and lived with him. People who talked about it praised him.
Cao Zhi, the king of Chensi in Wei Dynasty, had superhuman talents. He selected his officials and appointed Sima Fu as literary director.
Cao Zhi relied on his talent to dominate others, and Sima Fu often gave sincere advice. At first, he did not agree with Cao Zhi, but later he admitted his mistakes.
He was moved to the position of concubine among the crown princes.
When Emperor Wu of Wei passed away, the prince cried too much. Sima Fu advised him: "The emperor has passed away, and the world relies on you, Your Highness, to issue orders."
It should be for the ancestral temple at the top and for the various feudal states at the bottom. Why should we imitate the filial piety of the common people!
It took the prince a while to stop crying and said: You are right.
At that time, the ministers had just heard that the emperor had died, and they gathered together to weep and no longer formed a procession.
Sima Fu said sternly at the court: Now that the emperor has passed away and the world is in shock, we should pay homage to the successor as soon as possible and come to control the country. Is it enough to just cry?
Sima Fu made peace with the minister, dismissed the ministers, set up imperial guards, completed the funeral, and supported the crown prince to ascend the throne, that is, Emperor Wen.
At that time, the selection of officials such as servants and permanent servants was being carried out. From time to time, the old people around the prince hinted that the people in charge planned to appoint themselves and not recruit anyone else.
Sima Fu said: Although there were Yao and Shun, Ji Qi was still indispensable.
Now that the new king has just ascended the throne, he should recruit the talents and wise men at home. If he is still afraid of not getting them, how can he take advantage of the opportunity to recommend them to his ministers? Being an official is incompetent, and getting an official position is not enough to be respected.
So another recommendation was made.
He was transferred to Sima Fu as Zhongshulang and Changshishi, and he stayed in the official office. He was also appointed as Huangmen Shilang and Cavalry Captain.
At that time, Sun Quan claimed to be a vassal of Wei and asked for hostages to be sent to Wei. Wei's former general Yu Jin should be sent back to Wei, but it took a long time for them to arrive.
summary: Sima Fu, courtesy name Shuda, was Emperor Xuan's second brother. He was one of the "Bada" (Eight Talents) along with his brothers, known for their fame. Sima Fu was gentle, honest, upright, and widely read in classics. During the late Han Dynasty's turmoil, he maintained simple living while studying tirelessly. He was open-minded, tolerant, and held no grudges. When Yin Wu of Chenliu, a nationally known figure who had been punished, was visited by Sima Fu, they ate and lived together, earning praise. Sima Fu served as literary director under Cao Zhi, King of Chensi, offering sincere advice that Cao Zhi eventually accepted. After Emperor Wu of Wei died, Sima Fu advised the crown prince against excessive mourning, emphasizing his responsibilities to the ancestral temple and feudal states. When ministers gathered weeping without forming a procession, Sima Fu sternly organized them, completed funeral arrangements, and supported the crown prince's ascension as Emperor Wen. During official selections, Sima Fu opposed nepotism, advocating for recruiting talented individuals nationwide.

translation:
The emperor asked Sima Fu about this, and Sima Fu said: The former king set up the system of nine services because he sincerely used his benevolence to request remote areas, instead of using the etiquette of the Central Plains to demand requests.
Your Majesty inherits the throne, and people from far away obey and pay tribute.
Although Sun Quan did not send any hostages and Yu Jin did not come back, they should still be treated leniently. Accumulate soldiers and horses and observe changes in the situation.
You can't blame someone just because of suspicion, as that might hurt the righteousness of people far away.
From Sun Ce to Sun Quan, successive generations have succeeded each other, and the strength of the people is not due to one Yu Jin. There must be other reasons why the ban did not arrive.
Later Yu Jin returned to Wei. Sure enough, he was detained because of illness, but the hostages were never delivered.
The army marched to the river and blamed Wu for breaking his promise, so Wu broke off relations and stopped contributing.
After that, he served as a dianong in Hanoi, was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, and was transferred to the prefect of Qinghe.
At the beginning, Emperor Wen of Wei established Duzhi Shangshu, who was specifically in charge of the military and state's expenditure plan. The court's discussion believed that the conquests had not subsided, and measures must be economized.
When Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne and planned to appoint Sima Fu, he asked those around him: "Does he have the demeanor of his elder brother?"
He replied: Like his brother.
The emperor said: I have got two Sima Yis, so what else do I have to worry about?
Sima Fu was transferred to Duzhi Shangshu.
Sima Fu believed that to capture the enemy and win, one should be prepared.
Every time Zhuge Liang invaded Guanzhong, the troops at the border could not stop the enemy, and the rear troops rushed to the border and would not be able to catch up with the fighters. Twenty thousand infantry and cavalry should be selected in advance and divided into two parts as a reserve force to attack the enemy.
Sima Fu also believed that Guanzhong suffered continuous enemy attacks and there was insufficient grain and cloth, so he sent 5,000 farmers from Jizhou to station in Shangying to practice battle formations in autumn and winter, and to manage fields and mulberry gardens in spring and summer.
From then on, the Guanzhong army and the country had a surplus and were prepared to prevent invasion.
After that, he was appointed as Shangshu Youpu She, was granted the title of Marquis of Changping Ting, and was moved to Shangshu Ling.
When General Cao Shuang took over power and Li Sheng, He Yan, Deng Yang and others made political chaos, Sima Fu did not care about daily political affairs, but just rectified himself and stayed away from harm.
When Emperor Xuan executed Cao Shuang, Sima Fu and Emperor Jing were stationed at Simamen. Because of their meritorious service, they were granted the title of Marquis of Changshe County and were appointed as ministers.
At that time, Wu general Zhuge Ke surrounded the new city and appointed Sima Fu to command 200,000 troops to defend the enemy.
Sima Fu was stationed in Shouchun and sent his mother Qiu Jian, Wen Qin and others to attack.
The generals wanted to attack quickly, but Sima Fu said: To attack, you must rely on the opponent's strength to succeed, and you must be cunning and ingenious, without being able to fight.
Deliberately staying for more than a month before advancing, the Wu army fled.
summary: When Sun Quan claimed vassalage to Wei but delayed sending hostages and returning Yu Jin, Sima Fu advised leniency, suggesting military preparation while observing developments. Yu Jin eventually returned, detained due to illness, but hostages never arrived. Sima Fu later served as Diannong in Hanoi, Marquis of Guannei, and Prefect of Qinghe. Emperor Ming appointed him Duzhi Shangshu, remarking he had "two Sima Yis." Sima Fu proposed preparing 20,000 infantry and cavalry as reserves against Zhuge Liang's invasions and stationed 5,000 farmers in Shangying for agricultural-military training, ensuring Guanzhong's surplus and defense readiness. During Cao Shuang's corrupt regime, Sima Fu maintained rectitude and avoided harm. After Emperor Xuan executed Cao Shuang, Sima Fu was granted the title of Marquis of Changshe County and appointed Minister. When Wu general Zhuge Ke besieged Xincheng, Sima Fu commanded 200,000 troops, deliberately delaying before advancing, causing the Wu army to flee. Regarding funeral flags for Wei Ming's mourning, Sima Fu argued against writing "Wei" or surnames, citing classical precedents, and his view prevailed.

translation:
When Wei Ming passed away after mourning, they discussed how to write the flags in front of the coffin. Some people planned to remove the surname and write Wei, while others planned to write both the surname and Wei. Sima Fu believed: According to classical justice, neither should be written.
All emperors named the world based on the name of their own country, so as to distinguish themselves from previous generations, not to choose a good name to glorify themselves.
The sky is called Huangtian, and the emperor is called the emperor; the earth is called the queen earth, and the queen is called the queen.
Creation is the same as the name of heaven and earth. There is no second noble name in the world. There is no need to use the name of the country to express yourself, and there is no need to use the name of the clan to show off.
Therefore, the "Jing" in the third year of Yin Gong's "Spring and Autumn" says that in the third month of the third month, King Gengxu died. He respected him and called him Heaven, not King of Zhou, in order to distinguish him from the kings of other countries. In August Gengchen, Song Gonghe died. He wrote the name of the country and the person in order to distinguish him from the king of heaven.
The "Jing" written in the fifteenth year of Duke Xiang said that Liu Xia welcomed the queen in Qi, not to mention the queen Jiang of Zhou, in order to distinguish herself from the ladies of other countries.
As for the countries, it is said that Mrs. Jiang came from Qi, and it is also said that Ji Boji passed away. The name of the country is used to refer to the surname, in order to distinguish it from the Queen of Heaven.
From this research, it can be seen that the title of emperor is unparalleled, so why is it necessary to write Wei?
When we honor the queen and use the title "Mi" to make it clear, why is it necessary to write down the surname?
Those who wanted to write "Wei" among the commentators thought they showed the dignity of the emperor, but in fact they were equal to the kings of ancient countries.
People who wanted to write their last names thought they were showing that they were the emperor's concubines, but they were actually the same as ancient ladies.
It violates the principles of the classics and is different from the clear system of the saints. It cannot leave a lasting lesson for the future and cannot become an unchanging formula for all ages.
So he followed Sima Fu's argument.
Moved to Sikong.
He was appointed Taiwei instead of Wang Jun.
When Shu general Jiang Wei invaded Longyou, Wang Jing, the governor of Yongzhou, was defeated and sent Sima Fu to the west to guard Guanzhong and command the troops.
Chen Tai, general of the expedition to the west, and Deng Ai, general of Anxi, marched to attack Jiang Wei, but Jiang Wei withdrew.
Sima Fu returned to the capital and was transferred to Taifu.
When Lord Gao Gui was killed, no one from the officials dared to express condolences. Sima Fu lay on the body and cried very sadly, saying: "It is my crime to kill your majesty."
Invite the person who investigated the mastermind.
When the Queen Mother ordered him to be buried with common people's rites, Sima Fu and the Dukes went to court and requested that he be buried with royal rites, and they complied.
Sima Fu is very cautious by nature.
When Emperor Xuan was in power, Sima Fu often gave in and remained humble.
Later, during the period when the monarch was abolished and established, he did not participate in the planning.
The emperors of Jing and Wen dynasties did not dare to force Sima Fu because of his high status.
Later he was granted the title of Duke of Changle.
summary: Sima Fu served as Sikong, then Taiwei. When Shu general Jiang Wei invaded Longyou, Sima Fu guarded Guanzhong, and Jiang Wei withdrew. After Lord Gao Gui was killed, Sima Fu alone wept over his body, requesting investigation of the mastermind. He petitioned for royal burial rites, which were granted. Sima Fu was cautious, humble during Emperor Xuan's time, and uninvolved in monarch depositions. He was granted the title of Duke of Changle. When Emperor Wu accepted abdication and King Chenliu departed, Sima Fu bid farewell tearfully, vowing lifelong loyalty to Wei. He was made King of Anping with 40,000 households, later promoted to Dazai and Commander-in-Chief. Despite honors, Sima Fu remained unassuming and often sorrowful. Before death at age ninety-three, he ordered simple burial in ordinary clothes. The emperor mourned three days and provided lavish funeral gifts, though Sima Fu's family followed his wishes and used none.

translation:
Dan Mafu had nine sons: Sima Yong, Sima Wang, Sima Fu, Sima Yi, Sima Huang, Sima Quan, Sima Gui, Sima Heng, and Sima Jing.
Sima Yong's courtesy name is Zikui.
When he first became the heir to the throne, he was appointed as an infantry captain and a lieutenant.
He died before Sima Fu, and was given a posthumous gift to the general of the auxiliary state, with the nickname Zhen.
Sima Yong's son Sima Chong was a grandson and died early.
In the ninth year of Taishi, Sima Long, the younger brother of Sima Chong, was made King of Anping.
Four years later, he died in the second year of Xianning. His nickname was Mu. Without a son, the feudal state was cut off.
Sima Wang, the king of Yiyang, whose courtesy name was Zichu, was adopted by his uncle Sima Lang. He was generous and like his father.
He served as a senior planner in the county. He was recommended as Xiaolian and appointed as Situ Tu. He successively served as the prefect of Pingyang and the general of Luoyang Diannong.
He followed Emperor Xuan to attack Wang Bo and was named Yong'an Tinghou for his meritorious service.
He was moved to the position of general of the army guard, changed to the title of Marquis of Anle Township, and was appointed as the regular servant of Sanqi.
At that time, the Duke of Wei Gaogui was a man of talents and loved scholars. Sima Wang, Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, and Zhong Hui were all treated very well and served at banquets many times.
The Duke is impatient. Pei Xiu and others are serving in the palace and will be there immediately if there is an emergency call.
Because Sima Wang was in a foreign position, he was specially given a chariot with five warriors.
At that time, Emperor Jing and Emperor Wen successively assisted in the affairs of the court without meeting the court, and the power belonged to the Jin Dynasty.
Although Sima Wang was favored, he often felt uneasy, so he asked to leave the capital and be appointed as the general of Zhengxi, Chijie, and the commander-in-chief of the military affairs of Yongliang and Liangzhou.
During his eight years in office, he was dignified, educated, and purified.
In the past, Shu general Jiang Wei invaded Guanzhong many times. When Sima Wang took office, he made extensive plans. Jiang Wei was unable to invade, and Guanzhong relied on him.
He was granted the title of Marquis of Shunyang.
He was appointed as General of the Guard, concurrently as the leader of the Central Army, and in charge of the forbidden troops.
Soon he was promoted to General of Hussars and opened a government office.
Soon, he replaced He Zeng as Situ.
Emperor Wu accepted the concession and granted Sima Wang the title of King of Yiyang, with a fief of 10,000 households and 2,000 soldiers.
In the third year of his reign, the edict stated: Advocate the virtuous and appoint meritorious officials, respect the prosperous relatives of the clan, use this to govern the country, promote education, and set an example for all officials to see.
Besides, the importance of Taisi lies in the Heavenly Officials. Therefore, the Zhou Dynasty established six official positions: government, punishment, affairs, governance, education, and etiquette. The regulations for governing the country were the most important.
Situ, the leader of the army, Sima Wang, was a member of the imperial family because of his good virtues, and the world benefited from his virtues. His ancestors started a business, assisted the destiny, came out of the capital to take charge of important tasks, and entered the court to assist in court politics. He had both obvious literary virtues and provocative martial arts.
When I succeed to the throne, I will be a wise minister and should ascend to the position of Taiwei. I will also be in charge of military affairs, assist the royal family internally, and enhance the authority of the monarch externally. He was promoted to Taiwei, and the leader of the army remained the same.
summary: Sima Fu had nine sons: Sima Yong, Sima Wang, Sima Fu, Sima Yi, Sima Huang, Sima Quan, Sima Gui, Sima Heng, and Sima Jing. Sima Yong died before his father. Sima Wang, adopted by his uncle Sima Lang, served as Prefect of Pingyang and Luoyang Diannong, followed Emperor Xuan against Wang Bo, and was named Yong'an Tinghou. He later served as General of Hussars and Situ. Emperor Wu made him King of Yiyang with 10,000 households. He was promoted to Taiwei, commanding troops against Wu invasions. He died at sixty-seven, known for frugality and money accumulation, leaving four sons.

translation:
There will be one Taiwei officer, six military officers, and five cavalry officers.
Ten more officers and cavalry were added, adding to the previous thirty people, false Yu Bao advocated.
Wu State general Shi Ji invaded Jiangxia, causing commotion on the border.
Sima Wang was appointed to command 20,000 infantry and cavalrymen of the Chinese army and stationed at Longpi, forming an important town on both sides. During the holidays, he was appointed as the governor to supervise all military affairs.
It happened that Hu Lie, the governor of Jingzhou, resisted Shi Ji and defeated the enemy army, so Sima Wang withdrew his troops and returned to the court.
Soon Ding Feng, the general of Wu State, invaded Shaopi. Sima Wang led his troops to the front line, but retreated before Ding Feng could reach him.
Become the Great Sima.
Sun Hao led his army to invade Shouchun. Shaoshu ordered Sima Wang to command 20,000 Chinese troops and 3,000 cavalry to occupy Huaibei.
Sun Hao retreated and the Jin army gave up.
In the seventh year of Taishi's reign, he passed away at the age of sixty-seven. The funeral gifts exceeded the usual rites. Sima Wang was frugal and stingy by nature and liked to accumulate money. After his death, he was full of gold and silk, so he was ridiculed.
He has four sons: Sima Yi, Sima Hong, Sima Zheng and Sima Pin.
Sima Yiguan went to Huangmenlang and died before Sima Wang.
Sima Zheng also died early.
Let Sima Yi's son Sima Qi inherit the title.
Sima Qi also liked to accumulate money without any limit. He sent three envoys to Jiaoguang to do business, which was reported by the relevant officials. In the ninth year of Taikang, Shaoshu demoted Sima Qi to the title of Sanzongtinghou.
Instead, King Zhangwu Sima Wei was appointed as Sima Wang's successor.
Later, Sima Wei was killed, and Sima Qi was appointed King Jiyang to succeed Sima Wang.
Sima Hong, the king of Ping in Hejian, whose courtesy name was Kongye, was adopted by his uncle, Sima Qian, the Marquis of Changwuting.
Serving as an official in Wei, he served successively as Dian Nong Zhonglang Jiang and Yuan Wu Taishou, and was granted the title of Xiang Bennan.
Emperor Wu accepted the abdication and made him King of Hejian.
Twelve years later, Xianning died in the second year of his life.
He has two sons: Sima Wei and Sima Hun.
Sima Wei inherited the title and was transferred to Zhang Wu.
Later, Sima Wei succeeded Sima Wang, King of Yiyang, and appointed Sima Hun as the successor of Sima Hong.
Sima Hun served as the regular attendant of Sanqi until his death.
When Luoyang fell, several of Sima Hun's sons were captured by the Hu people.
The youngest son Sima Tao had just succeeded Sima Que, the new king of Cai, and was also captured together with his elder brother.
Later, he was able to return to the south and had a falling out with Concubine Xincai.
In the second year of Taixing, he thought that since his brothers had been taken captive to Liaodong and Zhang Wu's feudal kingdom had been cut off, he should return to the place of his birth.
The concubine argued about this and left the matter to Taichang.
Taichang He Xun commented: Zhang Wu and Xincai both flattered a system in which feudal states should not be exterminated. According to morality, they could not abandon their own clans and become descendants of side relatives first.
Investigation: Sima Tao has been designated as someone else's heir. He must no longer have any brothers, and his country will never have any descendants, so that he can return to his birthplace.
Now my brother is far away. It cannot be said that he is not there. Although the road is blocked, it is not an extremely far place.
summary: Sima Hong, King of Hejian, was adopted by his uncle Sima Qian. He served as Diannong Zhonglang Jiang and Yuanwu Taishou, was made King of Hejian by Emperor Wu, and died after twelve years. Sima Wei, his son, succeeded but was later transferred to Zhangwu. Sima Wei flattered Sima Lun, king of Zhao, and served as Zhongshu Ling during Sima Lun's usurpation. After Sima Lun's failure, Emperor Hui ordered his execution. Sima Zheng died before his father Sima Wang and was posthumously named King of Sui County.

translation:
Sima Liang dismissed Sima Yao, Sima Pin and others from their official positions on the grounds that Sima Yao was not resolute in his crusade against Yang Jun, and sent Sima Suan to the feudal country.
Sima Suan then managed goods, and his luxury exceeded the system.
King Zhao Sima Lun usurped the throne and recalled Sima Cun.
When the rebels rose up, Sima Lun appointed Sima Pin as general of the guard and commander of all military affairs.
Sima Lun failed and Sima Cun was dismissed from office.
Sima Tong, King of Qi, assisted in the government affairs, and Sima Yao was appointed as a servant. Sima Liu was elected as General Pingdong and Commander-in-Chief of Xuzhou's military forces to guard Xiapi.
Sima Ying, king of Chengdu, assisted in government affairs and promoted Sima Pin to General Wei.
When Emperor Hui was on his way to the north, he appointed Sima Suan as the general of chariots and cavalry. His duties as governor remained unchanged and he was sent to lead the army to Ye.
During the Battle of Dangyin, Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, ran to Xiapi, but Sima Cun refused to accept him, so Sima Yue returned to his own kingdom.
After the emperor visited the west, Sima Yue gathered troops to prepare to meet the emperor. Sima Cun was very frightened.
Wang Xiu, the chief historian, said: "The king of Donghai has an important position in the clan. Now he is about to perform a righteous deed. The Duke should grant Xuzhou to him. This is a beautiful thing of restraint and humility."
Sima Bang obeyed him, so he considered himself to be adhering to the emperor's will, commanding the governor of Yanzhou and the general of chariots and cavalry, and reported to the emperor.
The emperor was in Chang'an at that time and sent the envoy Liu Qian to confer the post.

He was moved to the post of General Zhendong and guarded Xuchang.
He was promoted to the title of King of Nanyang.
In the early years of Yongjia, he was transferred to General Zhengxi, Kaifu, and Commander-in-Chief of Qin Yong and Liang Yi Zhu, replacing Wang Yong of Hejian to guard Guanzhong.
Sima Mo was grateful for Ding Shao's kindness and ordered his countrymen to erect a monument for Gong Shao during his lifetime.
At that time, there was a famine in Guanzhong, the people were eating each other, and there were diseases and plagues, and thieves openly committed evil.
summary: Sima Teng, King of Xincai, served as Prefect of Nanyang and Wei, competent in office. He was recruited as Zongzheng, moved to Taichang, then served as General Ningbei and Governor of Bingzhou. When Emperor Hui attacked Sima Ying, Sima Teng and Wang Jun defeated Sima Ying's forces. Sima Ying fled with the emperor to Luoyang. Sima Teng was promoted to General Anbei, later General of Chariots and Cavalry. He was renamed King Xincai. When Ji Sang and others rebelled, Sima Teng dismissed them as insignificant but was killed by Li Feng. Sima Teng had four sons: Sima Yu, Sima Jiao, Sima Shao, and Sima Que. Sima Teng was frugal and stingy, not giving relief to people, leading to disaster. His bones were not recovered. Sima Que succeeded him, served as General Dongzhonglang, guarded Xuchang, and was killed by Shi Le. He had no sons, so Sima Tao, son of Sima Hun, was asked to worship Sima Que, later Sima Bi, son of Sima Ku, succeeded. Sima Bi died without sons, succeeded by his brother Sima Miao. After his death, his son Sima Huang succeeded, but Huan Wen deposed him. Emperor Xiaowu established Sima Chong as heir. Song accepted abdication and the feudal state was cancelled.

translation:
Sima Mo couldn't control his power, so he cast bronze human bells and tripods into cooking utensils in exchange for food. The commentators rejected this approach.
Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, summoned Sima Mo as Sikong and sent Fu Zhi, the supervisor of Zhongshu, to replace Sima Mo.
Sima Mo's adviser Chun Yuding persuaded Sima Mo: Guanzhong is the land of abundance and the overlord's territory.
If he returns to the court because he cannot be appeased, it will already damage his reputation. Besides, the Duke's brothers advocate important things, and both of them are in the court. If you are strong, you will be accused of being authoritarian, and if you are weak, you will be controlled by others. Returning to the court will not be beneficial to you.
Sima Mo accepted his words and refused to go to the conscription.
The emperor sent his eldest son, Sima Bao, to serve as General of the West Zhonglang and Colonel of the East Qiang to guard Shangying. Pei Bao, the governor of Qinzhou, rejected Sima Bao.
Sima Mo sent his captain Chen An to lead his troops to attack Pei Bao, but Pei Bao ran to Anding.
The prefect Mai Tzu led the county people to welcome Pei Bao, and Sima Mo sent military commander Xie Ban to attack Jia Tzu, who fled to Lu River.
This year, he was promoted to Taiwei and Grand Governor.
Luo Jing was overthrown, and Sima Mo sent Yamen Zhao Ran to guard Pu Ban. Za Ran asked Prefect Feng Yi for help but failed, so he got angry and led everyone to surrender to Liu Cong.
Liu Cong sent his sons Liu Can and Chan Ran to attack Chang'an. Sima Mo sent Chunyu Ding to resist, but was defeated by Chan Yuan.
Everyone betrayed and fled, and the warehouse was empty. The army offered wine to Wei Fu and said: "The matter is urgent. Surrender early to avoid disaster."
Sima Mo obeyed him and surrendered to Zhao Ran.
Zhao Ran sat with his feet forward, rolled up his sleeves, recited Sima Mo's crimes, and sent them to Liu Can.
Liu Can killed Sima Mo and gave Sima Mo's concubine Liu to the Hu man Zhang Ben as his wife.
Sima Mo's son Sima Bao succeeded him.
Sima Bao, whose courtesy name is Jingdu, was talented in literature when he was young and loved writing.
At first he was named the Crown Prince of Nanyang Kingdom.
When Sima Mo was killed, Sima Bao was in Shangying.
Later, when Mai Bao died and Pei Bao was killed by Zhang Gui, Sima Bao completely controlled the territory of Qinzhou. He was known as the Great Sima and appointed hundreds of officials according to his will.
All the Di and Qiang people in Longyou obeyed him, and Zhang Ku, the governor of Liangzhou, sent envoys to contribute.
When Emperor Min came to the throne, he appointed Sima Bao as the right prime minister, and was appointed as the minister in charge and the commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Shaanxi.
Soon he became the prime minister.
After Sima Mo's defeat, Captain Chen An defected to Sima Bao. Sima Bao ordered him to lead more than a thousand elite warriors to attack the Qiang, and treated Chen An well.
Sima Bao's general Zhang Chun and others were jealous, falsely accused Chen An of having second thoughts, and requested to get rid of him, but Sima Bao did not agree.
Zhang Chun and others ambush assassins to assassinate Chen An. Chen An was injured and ran back to Longcheng. He sent envoys to Sima Bao and paid tribute continuously.
After Emperor Min suffered humiliation, Sima Bao claimed to be King of Jin.
At that time, there was a serious famine in Shangbang and the officers and soldiers were in embarrassment. Zhang Chun escorted Sima Bao to Nan'an.
Chen An himself was appointed governor of Qinzhou and claimed to belong to Liu Yao.
Zhang Chun escorted Sima Bao to Sangcheng, and was about to join Zhang Fu.
Zhang Gong sent troops to meet Sima Bao, which was actually to guard against him.
summary: Sima Mo, King of Nanyang, was eager to learn young, famous with Emperor Yuan and Sima You. He was initially named Pingchang Gong. He served as Crown Prince's Concubine and Official Attendant. Sima Yue appointed him Beizhonglang General to guard Ye. He was promoted to King of Nanyang. During famine in Guanzhong, Sima Mo cast bronze vessels into cooking utensils for food, criticized by commentators. Sima Yue summoned him as Sikong, but Sima Mo refused, persuaded by Chun Yuding. He was promoted to Taiwei and Grand Governor. When Luo Jing fell, Sima Mo surrendered to Zhao Ran, who recited his crimes and sent him to Liu Can, who killed him. Sima Mo's son Sima Bao succeeded him. Sima Bao, courtesy name Jingdu, was talented in literature. When Sima Mo was killed, Sima Bao was in Shangying. He controlled Qinzhou, appointed officials, and Di and Qiang people obeyed him. Emperor Min appointed him Right Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief. After Emperor Min's humiliation, Sima Bao claimed to be King of Jin. Famine struck Shangbang, and Zhang Chun escorted Sima Bao to Nan'an. Sima Bao died of illness at twenty-seven. He was tall, fat, weighed 800 jin, slept well but was impotent. Having no sons, Zhang Chun established Sima Zhan as successor. Chen An attacked Zhang Chun, Sima Zhan surrendered to Chen An, who sent him to Liu Yao, who killed him. Chen An buried Sima Bao with emperor's rites, posthumous title Yuan.

translation:
So Sima Cheng took the lead in moving everyone from Xu to Rongyang to garrison.
Coinciding with Emperor Hui's westward move, Sima Cheng formed an alliance with his cousin Ma Mo of Pingchang Company, Chief Shi Feng Song and others, and elected Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, as the leader of the alliance.
Liu Qiao refused to accept the restraint of Sima Yue and others and took advantage of the opportunity to attack Xu.
Sima Cheng moved to cross the Yellow River on his own, and Wang Jun asked Sima Ji to serve as the governor of Jizhou to support his troops.
Sima Yan entered Jizhou to mobilize his troops, then crossed the Yellow River south and defeated Liu Qiao and others.
When Sima Ji, the king of Hejian, heard that Liu Qiao was defeated, he killed Zhang Fang and sent his head to Sima Yue.
Sima Yue and Sima Jin went west to meet the emperor, while Sima Ke fled.
So he escorted the emperor back to the capital and worshiped Sima Ji as Situ.
In the third year of Yongxing's reign, he fell seriously ill and died at the age of thirty-seven.
He had no son, so he adopted Sima Mo's son Sima Li Jisi. Sima Li followed Sima Mo to his own kingdom and was killed in Chang'an.
Sima Sui, King Hui of Jinan, also known as Zibo, was the son of Wei Honglu, Sima Xun, the younger brother of Emperor Xuan.
He was appointed as the Marquis of Guannei in Wei, was promoted to the Marquis of Qianchang Ting, and successively served as Dianjunlang.
In the second year of Jingyuan, he was granted the title of Rural Marquis of Wucheng, the governor of Yecheng and the general of Beizhonglang.
The fifth-class title was established, and he was named Zhu Abo, and gradually moved to the title of champion general.
Emperor Wu accepted the abdication and named him King of Jinan.
He died in the second year of Taishi.
He has two sons: Sima Dan and Sima Ji.
Sima Dan succeeded him and was renamed King of Zhongshan in the third year of Xianning.
He died that year without any sons, and Sima Ji succeeded him.
When the day was prosperous, Sima Ying appointed Sima Ji as General Jianwei. He, Hu Ju and others led the army to resist Wang Chuang, but fell into the battle formation and died.
Without a son, the feudal state was cancelled.
Later, Sima Sui's great-grandson Sima Xun, named Wei Chang, was more than ten years old. At the end of Emperor Min's reign, Chang'an fell, and Liu Yao's general Linghu Ni adopted Sima Xun as his son.
When he reaches adulthood, he will be familiar with archery, horseback riding, and can shoot the bow left and right. In the sixth year of Xianhe, he came back from Guanyou and claimed to be the great-great-grandson of Sima Xun of Great Changqiu, the great-grandson of the champion general Sima Sui, King Hui of Jinan, and the son of Sima Can, the prefect of Lueyang. He therefore paid homage to Pu She, who was famous for his bravery.
When Yu Yi was guarding Xiangyang, because Huan Xuan, the governor of Liangzhou, died, he asked Sima Xun to take his place.
Initially stationed in Xicheng, he retreated to Wudang.
At that time, Shi Jilong died and the Central Plains was in turmoil. The powerful generals in Yongzhou quickly reported to Sima Xun.
Sima Xun led his army out of Luo Valley and camped at Hangou, two hundred miles away from Chang'an. He dispatched general Liu Huan to attack Chang'an and capture Hecheng.
So Guanzhong all responded to Sima Xun by killing Ji Long's prefect commander.
Sima Xun had few soldiers and could not stabilize himself, so he retreated to Liangzhou.
During the Yonghe period, Zhang Ju occupied Longsu and sent an envoy to summon Sima Xun, who then entered Chang'an.
At first, Du Hong, a native of Jingzhao, was superior to Zhang Ju because he was a wealthy man. Zhang Ju humiliated Du Hong because of his bravery. Du Hong knew that Sima Xun was afraid that Zhang Ju would strengthen his army, so he persuaded Sima Xun: If Zhang Ju is not killed, Guanzhong will not be owned by the country.
Sima Xun then pretended to invite Zhang Ju and killed him on the spot.
Zhang Ju's younger brother ran to Chiyang and gathered his troops to attack Sima Xun. After repeated defeats, he sued for peace and returned to Liangzhou.
Later, Huan Wen attacked Guanzhong and ordered Sima Xun to send troops to Ziwu Road, but he was defeated by Fu Xiong; he withdrew his troops and stationed himself at Nuwa Fort.
Soon he was promoted to the general who conquered the captives, supervising the military affairs in Guanzhong, and also the captain of the Xirong school. He was given the title of Marquis of Tongjiting.
summary: Sima Sui, King of Fanyang, was younger brother of Sima Quan, King of Pengcheng. He was initially an Admonishment Official, granted title in the first year of Taishi, reigned fifteen years, died in the fifth year of Xianning, succeeded by his son Sima Gai. Sima Gai was famous for studiousness, studied classics, good at speaking. He served as Sanqi Changshi, Minister, General Annan, guarding Xuchang, promoted to General Conquering the South. Sima Yong proposed appointing Wang Siyan. Sima Gai, Sima Liu, and Zhou Fu reported to the emperor about Sima Ying's failures and recommended Zhang Fang. They urged the emperor to give Guan You to Dazai and send Zhang Fang back to the county. Sima Gai led everyone from Xu to Rongyang to garrison. When Emperor Hui moved west, Sima Gai formed an alliance with Sima Mo and elected Sima Yue as leader. Liu Qiao attacked Xu, Sima Gai crossed the Yellow River, defeated Liu Qiao. Sima Ji killed Zhang Fang and sent his head to Sima Yue. Sima Gai escorted the emperor back to the capital, worshiped as Situ. He died at thirty-seven, no sons, adopted Sima Mo's son Sima Li, who was killed in Chang'an. Sima Sui, King Hui of Jinan, was son of Sima Xun, younger brother of Emperor Xuan. He was Marquis of Guannei in Wei, promoted to Marquis of Qianchang Ting, served as Dianjunlang. In the second year of Jingyuan, he was granted title of Rural Marquis of Wucheng, Governor of Yecheng and General Beizhonglang. He was named Zhu Abo, moved to Champion General. Emperor Wu made him King of Jinan. He died in the second year of Taishi. He had two sons: Sima Dan and Sima Ji. Sima Dan succeeded, renamed King of Zhongshan, died without sons, Sima Ji succeeded. Sima Ji served as General Jianwei, fought against Wang Chuang, died in battle. Without sons, the feudal state was cancelled. Later, Sima Sui's great-grandson Sima Xun, named Wei Chang, was adopted by Liu Yao's general Linghu Ni. He returned from Guanyou in the sixth year of Xianhe, claimed to be Sima Xun's descendant, paid homage to Pu She. He served as Governor of Liangzhou, attacked Chang'an, captured Hecheng. Guanzhong responded to him. During the Yonghe period, he entered Chang'an, killed Zhang Ju, but was defeated by Fu Xiong. He was promoted to General Conquering the Captives, Marquis of Tongjiting. He was tyrannical, killing wealthy families who disagreed with him. He planned to occupy Shu territory. Huan Wen sent troops to attack him, Sima Xun was captured and killed.

translation:
He was tyrannical and cruel in politics. As for the wealthy families under his jurisdiction and the state, if his words did not agree with him, he would kill them on their seats, or shoot them themselves with bows.
The West is worried about his cruelty.
In the state, he often wanted to occupy the Shu territory and had the intention of separatizing the Baifeng Dynasty.
After Huan Wen heard about it, he devoted himself to appeasement and care and made his son Sima Kang the governor of Hanzhong.
Sima Xun's rebellious plan was completed, but he did not take action because he was afraid of Zhou Fu, the governor of Yizhou.
When Zhou Fu died, he gathered his troops into the sword pavilion.
Liangzhou Biejia Yongduan and Xirong Sima Kaicui earnestly advised him, but they were both killed by Sima Xun. He claimed to be the shepherd of the two states of Liangyi and the king of Chengdu.
Huan Wen sent Zhuzhuang to attack Sima Xun. Sima Xun's army was defeated and he was captured by Saizhuang. He and his son Long Wang, Chang Shisu, Sima Jintong and others were escorted to Danzhou Nahuo. They were all killed and their heads were sent to the capital.
Sima Xun, the king of Qiao Gang, whose courtesy name was Zi Ti, was the son of Sima Jin, the younger brother of Emperor Xuan, Wei Zhonglang.
He was appointed Marquis of Wei Guannei and was granted the title of Marquis of Yangting of Chengcheng. He participated in the military affairs and was worshiped as General Qingche and Zuojian Yulin.
The fifth-class title was established and the title was changed to Jingyang Nan.
Emperor Wu accepted the concession and named him King Qiao, granting him a fief of 4,400 households.
He died in the second year of Taishi.
He has two sons: Sima Sui and Sima Cheng.
King Ding Sima succeeded him.
After his death, his son Sima Sui succeeded him. He died in Shile. Emperor Yuan asked Sima to succeed him and his successor Sima Xun.
King Min Sima Cheng was named Jingcai. He was loyal, ambitious and virtuous when he was young.
At the invitation of the imperial court, he was promoted to General of Guangwei and Protector of Anyi to guard An'ding.
He returned to Luoyang with Emperor Hui and became a guerrilla general.
During the Yongjia period, the world gradually became chaotic, and they secretly attached themselves to Shan Jian, the general who conquered the south. When Shan Jian died, he entered Wuchang.
When Emperor Yuan began to guard Yangzhou, Sima Cheng returned to Jiankang and took up the post of military counselor and wine worshiper.
Emperor Min summoned him as General Longxiang, but he refused to take up the post.
Emperor Yuan became the King of Jin, and according to the decree, he changed the title of Sima Cheng to King Qiao.
In the early years of Taixing, he was appointed as the captain of the Tunqi School, and was appointed as the general of the auxiliary state and the general of the left army.
Sima Cheng was frugal as an official and did not take concubines.
Soon after, he was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi, and his positions of auxiliary to the country and left army remained.
Wang Dun was disloyal to the king, and the memorial was arrogant.
The emperor summoned Sima Cheng at night, showed him Wang Dun's watch, and said, "Wang Dun has gained a high position in power in recent years, and there is no limit to what he wants. What should we do with him?"
Sima Cheng said: If your Majesty does not rule on this matter early, disaster will happen.
The emperor wanted to build a barrier, but when Wang Dun petitioned Shen, the inner historian of Xuancheng, to serve as the governor of Xiangzhou, the emperor said to Sima Cheng: The southern Chu territory of Xiangzhou must be fortified. It is in a strategic position on the upper reaches and controls the intersection of the three states. It is a fiefdom that can be used with troops.
What if I let my uncle guard it?
summary: Sima Xun, King of Qiao Gang, was son of Sima Jin, younger brother of Emperor Xuan. He was Marquis of Wei Guannei, granted title of Marquis of Yangting of Chengcheng, served as General Qingche and Zuojian Yulin. He was named Jingyang Nan. Emperor Wu made him King Qiao with 4,400 households. He died in the second year of Taishi. He had two sons: Sima Sui and Sima Cheng. Sima Sui succeeded, died in Shile. Emperor Yuan asked Sima to succeed him. Sima Cheng, King Min, was loyal and virtuous young. He served as General Guangwei and Protector of Anyi. He returned to Luoyang with Emperor Hui, became Guerrilla General. During Yongjia period, he secretly attached himself to Shan Jian. When Shan Jian died, he entered Wuchang. When Emperor Yuan guarded Yangzhou, Sima Cheng returned to Jiankang, served as Military Counselor and Wine Worshiper. Emperor Yuan changed his title to King Qiao. He served as Captain of Tunqi School, General of the Auxiliary State and Left Army. He was frugal, did not take concubines. When Wang Dun was disloyal, the emperor summoned Sima Cheng at night, showed him Wang Dun's memorial. Sima Cheng advised early action. The emperor appointed him to guard Xiangzhou. Sima Cheng traveled to Wuchang, saw Wang Dun unarmed. Wang Dun tested him but let him go to his post. Sima Cheng was frugal, rode a reed cart, comforted people, earned good reputation. Wang Dun feared him, requisitioned his ships. When Wang Dun rebelled, Sima Cheng raised righteous deeds, but the city fell after more than a hundred days. Wei Yi sent him to Jingzhou, where Wang Yu killed him on the way at fifty-nine. After Wang Dun was pacified, Sima Cheng was posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry. His son Wuji succeeded him.

translation:
Ji Si takes a step forward and works hard!
Letters cannot fully express my feelings, they are just my suicide notes.
Ganzhuo's army was stationed at Gankou. Hearing that King Qiao's army had been defeated, the army stopped advancing. Wei Yi and others were fighting fiercely day by day. Wang Dun also sent the notes he had obtained from people in Taiwan Province and ordered Wei Yi to shoot them to Sima Cheng.
Everyone in the city felt sad and regretful when they learned that the imperial court could no longer defend it.
Liu Yi died in battle, and the stalemate lasted for more than a hundred days, and the city fell.
Wei Yi sent Sima Cheng to Jingzhou in a carriage. The governor Wang Yu killed him on the way according to Wang Dun's wishes. He was fifty-nine years old at the time.
Wang Dun was pacified, and Xia Shao posthumously awarded Sima Cheng the title of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
His son Wuji succeeded him.
Lie Wang Wuji was named Gongshou. When Sima Cheng was in trouble, he escaped because of his young age.
During the Xianhe period, he was promoted to the rank of Sanqi Shilang, and gradually moved to Tunqi Xiaowei, Zhongshu, and Huangmen Shilang.
Chu Pei, the governor of Jiangzhou, was going to the border town. Wuji, Dan Yang, Yin Huanjing and others paid him a farewell farewell at Banqiao.
At that time, Wang Yu's son Danyang Cheng Qizhi was present. Wuji was determined to take revenge and drew his sword to kill Qizhi himself. Chu Pei and Huan Jing ordered the guards to protect Qizhi before he was spared.
The imperial censor Zhongcheng Che recorded a report saying that Wuji wanted to kill someone on his own initiative and handed it over to Tingwei for punishment.
Emperor Cheng issued an edict saying: Wang Dun caused a rebellion, and King Min was in trouble. Let's explore the origin of the matter. What is the fault of this king?
However, the public and private legal system has also been decided. The king should focus on governing the country. How can he deduce the root cause and mess up the court laws.
Those in charge should state the law, and from now on, those who violate it will be punished.
So he was allowed to be treated as atonement.
In the early years of the founding of the Yuan Dynasty, he moved to the position of regular attendant of Sanqi, then to the position of censor Zhongcheng. He left the capital to serve as the general of the auxiliary state, the prime minister of Changsha, and also the prime minister of Jiangxia. Soon he was transferred to the post of prefect of Nanjun and Hedong counties, and the position of general remained the same.
He followed Dandan in the expedition against Shu, and because of his meritorious service, his youngest son Mo Qing was given the title of Duke Guangzhi, and was given the title of former general. Cheng Mian died in the sixth year and was given posthumously to General Wei.
He has two sons: Sima Tian and Sima Qing.
Sima Tian succeeded.
King Jing Sima Tian was named Yuan Yu. When he was young, he became an official of Sanqi Shilang, and gradually rose to the rank of Sanqi Changshi, Huangmenlang, and Yushi Zhongcheng.
At that time, Duke Haixi was deposed and Emperor Jian Wen ascended the throne. The martial law had not yet been lifted. Grand Sima Xun gathered in the middle hall and blew the police horn. Sima Tian presented an impeachment report but Zhou was disrespectful and asked to convict him.
Dan Wen looked at the memorial and sighed: "Young people from Japan dare to impeach me. It's really awe-inspiring."
Sima Tian was loyal, upright and talented, and the officials in the court were afraid of him.
summary: Sima Wuji, King Lie, escaped when young during Sima Cheng's trouble. He served as Sanqi Shilang, moved to Tunqi Xiaowei and Zhongshu. He tried to kill Wang Yu's son Qizhi for revenge but was stopped. The emperor pardoned him. He served as Sanqi Changshi and Censor Zhongcheng, then General of the Auxiliary State and Prime Minister of Changsha. He followed Dandan in expedition against Shu, given title of Duke Guangzhi. He died in the sixth year of Cheng Mian, posthumously awarded General Wei. He had two sons: Sima Tian and Sima Qing. Sima Tian succeeded him.

translation:
He was moved to the post of General of the Right Guard, Si Yong, Grand Zhongzheng of the four states of Qin and Liang, paid homage to Shangshu, transferred to the post of Shizhong, and concurrently served as General of the Left Guard. He was appointed as the domestic history of Wu, and concurrently served as the Prince Zhanshi.
Sima Tian had a high reputation and talent in the clan. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu, he relied heavily on him and appointed him as the military governor of Yan, Qing, Ji, You, Jinling in Yangzhou, and the north and south counties of Xuzhou. He was also the general of Zhenbei, the governor of Yanqing and Jiejie.
When he died in the fifteenth year of Taiyuan, he was given posthumously as a general of chariots and cavalry.
He has four sons: Shangzhi, Huizhi, Yunzhi and Xiuzhi.
Shang's heir.
Zhongwang Shangzhi's courtesy name was Bodao. He initially became a secretary-general and then moved to the rank of Sanqi-shilang.
Sima Tian guarded Jingkou and served as General Zhenwei and Prime Minister Guangling. He resigned when his father died.
After the mourning was over, he was appointed as a hussar to consult and join the army.
Within the clan, there have been outstanding figures from generation to generation.
When Wang Guobao was executed, Sanqi Changshi Liu Zhenzhi, Pengcheng Neishi Liu Juanzi, and Xuzhou Biejia Xu Fang were all arrested according to their accomplices and will be sentenced to death.
Shang Zhi said to King Daozi of Kuaiji: The punishment should not be too extensive, Zhenzhi and others should be let go.
Daozi obeyed him because all of Shang's brothers were serving in the court and relied on him whenever something happened.
Wang Gong, the governor of Yanzhou, was jealous of Shang's growing power. He and Yu Kai, the governor of Yuzhou, raised troops to attack Shangzhi and went south to join forces with Yin Zhongkan, the governor of Jingzhou, Huanxuan, the Duke of Nanjun, and others.
Daozi ordered the former general Wang Shi and the right general Xie Yan to attack Wang Gong, and Shangzhi to resist Yu Kai.
Yun Zhi fought with Yu Kai's son Yu Hong in Dangli. Yu Hong was defeated and fled, killing Yu Kai's general Duan Fang. Yu Kai fled to Huan Xuan alone on horseback.
Daozi appointed Shang Zhi as General Jianwei, Governor of Yuzhou, and Jiajie, all in accordance with Yu Kai's original positions, and soon he was promoted to General Former; he was allowed to be appointed as the domestic history of Wu; he was appointed as Hushi Sima and Danyang Yin; he was appointed as the prefect of Xiangcheng.
Each is in charge of troops and horses, and his power surpasses others in the court.
Later general Yuan Xian came to power and also relied on him as a back-up.
Yuan Xian favored Zhang Fashun, and there was no difference between sitting up and sitting down during banquets.
Shang Zhi entered the court and said to Yuan Xian with a serious face: Zhang Fashun is just an errand boy. If he has any outstanding talents, he will be promoted quickly.
In today's holy world, this shouldn't be the case.
Yuan Xian remained silent.
Shang Zhi added: Although there are many people in the clan, there are few people who can correct and advise. The emperor still accepts the opinions of the people in the grassland. What's more, I have a close blood relationship with the chief. I have been favored for several generations. How can I sit back and watch the gains and losses without speaking out.
So he scolded Bo Shu and ordered him to retreat.
Everyone in the room was surprised. Shang Zhi talked and laughed freely, but Yuan Xian held a deep grudge.
Later, Xiangfu issued a talisman and ordered two thousand warriors to be dispatched.
summary: Sima Tian, King Jing, served as Sanqi Shilang, Sanqi Changshi, Huangmenlang, and Yushi Zhongcheng. When Duke Haixi was deposed, Sima Tian impeached Grand Sima Xun for disrespect. The emperor sighed at his courage. Sima Tian was loyal, upright, talented, feared by officials. He served as General of the Right Guard, Shangshu, Shizhong, and General of the Left Guard. He was appointed Domestic History of Wu and Prince Zhanshi. Emperor Xiaowu relied on him heavily, appointed him Military Governor of several states and General of Zhenbei. He died in the fifteenth year of Taiyuan, posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry. He had four sons: Shangzhi, Huizhi, Yunzhi, and Xiuzhi. Shangzhi succeeded him. Sima Shangzhi, King Zhong, served as Secretary-General and Sanqi Shilang. He guarded Jingkou as General Zhenwei and Prime Minister Guangling. After his father's death, he served as Hussar Consultant. Within the clan, outstanding figures appeared generation after generation. When Wang Guobao was executed, Shangzhi advised King Daozi of Kuaiji to release Liu Zhenzhi and others. Daozi obeyed. Wang Gong, Governor of Yanzhou, jealous of Shangzhi's power, raised troops with Yu Kai and others. Daozi ordered Shangzhi to resist Yu Kai. Shangzhi defeated Yu Kai's forces. Daozi appointed Shangzhi as General Jianwei and Governor of Yuzhou. Shangzhi's power surpassed others. Later, Yuan Xian came to power and relied on him. Shangzhi scolded Yuan Xian's favorite Zhang Fashun, earning Yuan Xian's resentment. When Yuan Xian attacked Huan Xuan, Shangzhi was ordered to be vanguard. Huan Xuan attacked, Shangzhi's army collapsed, and Huan Xuan had Shangzhi killed. The emperor posthumously awarded General Wei to Shangzhi. His cousin Kangzhi was renamed King of Qiao County. Later, Wensi, Xiuzhi's eldest son, succeeded Shangzhi but was cruel and rebellious. Liu Yu killed him, and the feudal state was cancelled.

translation:
He refused and said: Western Fan is connected to a remote area, where enemy invaders appear and disappear, but the number of troops is only a few thousand, which is not enough to defend it, and there are no more people to send out.
Yuan Xian was particularly angry. It happened to be that he was about to attack Huan Xuan, so he did not cause any harm.

summary: Wang Xiang, courtesy name Xiuzheng, was from Linyi, Langye, a descendant of Han official Wang Ji. His grandfather Wang Ren served as Qingzhou governor, while his father Wang Rong refused government service. Wang Xiang was exceptionally filial. Despite being ordered to clean cattle pens, Wang Xiang remained respectful. When his parents fell ill, he personally tasted their medicine. During freezing weather, his stepmother desired live fish; Wang Xiang removed his clothes to break ice, and two carps leaped out spontaneously. When she wanted roasted oriole, dozens flew into his tent. Villagers attributed these events to his filial piety. During late Han warfare, he supported his mother and younger brother Wang Lan while hiding in Lujiang for over twenty years, refusing official appointments. After his mother's death, he became ill from grief. At nearly sixty, he initially refused Governor Lu Qian's invitation but eventually accepted after Wang Lan's persuasion. He defeated bandits, brought peace to the state, and was praised in song. Wang Xiang held various official positions including Wen Ling, Da Sinong, and was named Guannei Marquis. He served as Sili Xiaowei, Taichang, and Marquis of Wansui Ting. The emperor appointed him as third elder at the Imperial Academy, where he taught political education. He was promoted to Sikong, Taiwei, and Shizhong, eventually becoming Suiling Marquis with 1,600 households. When Emperor Wen became King of Jin, Wang Xiang refused to kneel, stating that as a Wei official, he would not bow to others. Emperor Wu appointed him Taibao and promoted him to Duke. Despite repeated retirement requests due to age, the emperor refused, granting him privileges including exemption from court attendance. Upon critical illness, Wang Xiang instructed his descendants on simple burial, forbidding elaborate ceremonies and expensive items. He died in the fourth year of Taishi at age eighty-five. His sons included Wang Zhao, Wang Xia, Wang Fu, Wang Lie, and Wang Fen.
