Emperor Wu ascended the throne, appointed him as Taifu, and promoted him to Duke.
Soon, Si Li Yi and Zhong Cheng Hou Shi Guang wrote a letter saying that Zheng Chong, He Zeng, Xun Hao and others should be relieved of their official positions due to illness.
summary: Zheng Chong, courtesy name Wenhe, was from Kaifeng, Rongyang. Born poor, he established moral integrity, was quiet with few desires, and extensively studied Confucian classics. He followed etiquette strictly and did not seek local fame. Emperor Wen of Wei appointed him literary minister, later promoting him to Shangshulang and Chenliu prefect. He valued elegance over wealth, earning respect. Cao Shuang recommended him as lieutenant, then Sanqi Changshi and Guang Luxun. In Jiaping's third year, he became Sikong, later Situ. He was appointed Taibao and named Shouguang Hou. Though holding prime ministerial rank, he avoided worldly affairs. When Emperor Wei abdicated, Zheng Chong presented the policy letter. Emperor Wu appointed him Taifu and promoted him to Duke. Despite illness-related requests for removal, the emperor refused. In the sixth year of Taishi, the emperor praised Zheng Chong, He Zeng, and Xun Hao for their virtue and service. Zheng Chong repeatedly resigned, and the emperor eventually allowed him to return to his mansion as Duke Shouguang with full privileges. He died the following year, receiving posthumous honors. Zheng Chong compiled "Collected Commentary of the Analects of Confucius" with others. Having no sons, his nephew Zheng Hui inherited his title.

translation:
In the past, Yang Wangsun rectified the current situation by burying him naked. His sons followed their father's orders, and a gentleman would not ridicule them, not to mention those who conformed to the etiquette and codes. The sons all obeyed the orders, and refused to offer sacrifices to relatives or former subordinates.
Shi Bao had six sons: Shi Yue, Shi Qiao, Shi Tong, Shi Jun, Shi Jun, and Shi Chong.
Shi Tong inherited the title.
Shi Tong, whose courtesy name was Hongxu, served successively as the captain of Shesheng and Dahonglu.
His son Shi Shun was appointed Shangshu Lang.
Shi Yue, whose courtesy name was Honglun, died early.
Shi Qiao, whose courtesy name was Hongzu, served successively as Shangshu Lang and Sanqi Shilang.
Since Emperor Wu could not summon Shi Qiao, he suspected Shi Bao of rebellion.
When Shi Bao arrived, Emperor Wu looked ashamed and said to him: Your son almost destroyed your family.
Shi Bao then deposed him and refused to let him serve as an official for the rest of his life.
Because of his dirty behavior, he was exiled to Dunqiu and was killed together with his younger brother Shi Chong.
His two sons, Shi Chao and Shi Xi, escaped and were not killed.
When King Sima Ying of Chengdu raised an army, he appointed Shi Chao as General Zhechong to attack Sun Xiu. He was granted the title of Marquis for his meritorious service.
He was also appointed General Zhenwu to conquer the Jingzhou bandits and bandits who were fighting for the house.
Sima Ying and Sima Yi, king of Kensha, attacked each other. Shi Chao served as the vanguard and was promoted to the central guard.
Chen Zhen and others kidnapped Emperor Hui for the Northern Expedition, and Shi Chao returned to Ye.
Sima Ying sent Shi Chao to resist the emperor in Dangyin. The emperor's army was defeated, and Shi Chao forced the emperor to visit Ye Palace.
When Wang Jun attacked Sima Ying in Ye, Sima Ying appointed Shi Chao as the right general to resist Wang Jun, but he returned with a disastrous defeat.
Follow the emperor to Luoyang and move west to Chang'an.
Sima Ji, the king of Hejian, appointed Shi Chao and General Beizhonglang, and sent him and Sima Ying to jointly resist Sima Yue, the king of the East China Sea.
Shi Chao recruited troops in Rongyang. Wang Chan, the right general, and Zhao Ze, the commander of the Dian soldiers, were both under Shi Chao's command and served as backup for Liu Qiao, the governor of Yuzhou.
Fanyang King Sima Chengcheng attacked and killed Shi Chao, but Shi Xi was able to escape and avoid death.
In the reign of Yongjia, Sima Yue was appointed as Taifu and joined the army.
Shi Jun, whose courtesy name is Jinglun, is honest, frugal, knowledgeable, and respectful.
He was a well-known scholar at the time when he reached the rank of Huangmen Shilang. He died early.
Shi Jun, courtesy name Yanlun, was famous when he was young. People who commented on him said that he was an outstanding talent.
When he reached Yangping Prefecture, he died early.
Shi Chong, whose courtesy name was Jilun, was born in Qingzhou, so his nickname was Qinu.
When he was young, he was smart, brave and resourceful.
When Shi Bao died, he divided his property among his sons, but not Shi Chong.
Shi Chong's mother spoke for Shi Chong, and Shi Bao said: Although this son is young, he can get it later.
In his twenties, he was practicing martial arts and had a reputation for being capable.
He entered the court as a Sanqi Lang and was promoted to the prefect of Chengyang.
For his meritorious service in the crusade against Wu, he was granted the title of Anyang Marquis.
Although he had a position in the county, he was eager to learn and asked to be dismissed due to illness.
Soon, he was awarded the title of Huang Menlang.
Brother Shi Tong offended Sima Jun, King of Fufeng. Officials accepted the decree and impeached Shi Tong, who was about to be severely punished, but he was later forgiven.
Because Shi Chong did not go to the palace to thank him, the officials wanted to accuse Shi of ruling again.
Shi Chong himself said in the letter: With the grace of his late father, my brother Shi Tong received favorable treatment early on. His official position is clean and he works hard in office.
I guessed the emperor's heart and was aware of this.
Recently, he was slandered and slandered by King Sima Jun of Fufeng. Sili Zhongcheng and others used words to emphasize the memorial, and the impeachment memorial quoted the law and fabricated charges to cover up the emperor's hearing.
summary: He Zeng, courtesy name Yingkao, was from Yangxia, Chen State. His father He Kui was Taipu of Wei. He Zeng inherited his title young, was eager to learn, and gained reputation. He served as Sanqi Changshi, Diannong General, and Huangmen Shilang. He submitted memorials advising careful selection of county governors. He served as governor of Hanoi with majestic reputation. As Sili Xiaowei, he impeached the favored official Yin Mo. He criticized Ruan Ji's dissolute behavior during mourning. He held various positions including Zhenbei General and was granted Marquis of Yingchang Township. Emperor Wu appointed him Taibao and later Taifu. He was known for filial piety, treating his wife with formal respect. However, he was extremely extravagant, spending ten thousand on daily meals, with luxurious carriages and clothing exceeding imperial standards. He died at age eighty, receiving the posthumous name Xiao. His sons He Zun and He Shao inherited his wealth. He Shao served as prince's grand master and Situ, maintaining similar extravagance. Shi Bao, courtesy name Zhongrong, was from Nanpi, Bohai. Known for beauty and intelligence, he was discovered by Guo Xuanxin who predicted his future as minister. He served as Sima of Emperor Jing's Imperial Guard. Despite concerns about his character, Emperor Jing defended him, comparing him to Guan Zhong and Chen Ping. He served as Ye Diannong Zhonglang Jiang, governor of Donglai and Langye, and Xuzhou governor. During Zhuge Dan's rebellion, Shi Bao led troops and defeated Wu forces. He was granted Marquis of Shuguang and later promoted to Grand Sima and Duke of Leling County. Suspected of rebellion due to rumors, he was dismissed but later reinstated as Situ. He focused on agricultural policies and died in the eighth year of Taishi. His sons included Shi Yue, Shi Qiao, Shi Tong, Shi Jun, Shi Jun, and Shi Chong. Shi Chong, known for wealth and extravagance, competed with royal relatives in luxury, owning numerous slaves and treasures. He was executed at age fifty-two during political conflicts, with his entire family killed.

translation:
Wang Chen, courtesy name Chudao, was born in Jinyang, Taiyuan.
His grandfather, Wang Rou, was a lieutenant general of the Huns in the Han Dynasty.
His father, Wang Ji, was the prefect of Wei Dong County.
When Wang Chen lost his father when he was young, he was adopted by his cousin Sikong Wang Chang. He served Wang Chang as if he were his biological father, and he was famous for his filial piety in serving his stepmother and widowed sister-in-law.
Good at reading and good at writing articles.
General Cao Shuang recruited him as a subordinate officer, and gradually moved to the position of minister under Zhongshu's family.
When Cao Shuang was executed, he was dismissed because of his status as an old official.
Later, he was appointed as the censor of the book administration department and transferred to the position of secretary supervisor.
During the Zhengyuan period, he was promoted to the rank of Sanqi Changshi and Shizhong, and was in charge of writings.
Together with Xunjie and Ruan Ji, he wrote the "Book of Wei". He often had hidden taboos and did not record it as truthfully as Chen Shou did.
At that time, Duke Gaogui of Wei was eager to learn and have literary talents. He invited Wang Chen and Pei Xiu to give lectures, banquets and write articles in Shutang many times.
Duke Gaogui was about to attack Emperor Wen, so he summoned Wang Shen and Wang Ye to tell them. Wang Chen and Wang Ye quickly reported to Emperor Wen, and they were granted the title of Marquis of Anping for their meritorious service. There are two thousand households in the city.
Because Wang Chen was disloyal to his master, he was criticized by public opinion.
Soon he was promoted to minister, and went out of the capital to supervise the military affairs of Yuzhou, General Fenwu, and governor of Yuzhou.
When he arrived at his post, he taught: The ancient sages like to listen to criticism and listen to the opinions of their servants. Those who cut grass and chop wood can also record things, and those who carry firewood can tell the affairs of the court.
Since the day I arrived at my post, I haven't heard anything offensive. Is it because I didn't show my humility and made people suspicious?
Notify the city and the people of the city that if you can recommend reclusive talents from among the people, depose treacherous officials in the state, state the good and bad of officials, tell the people's worries, promote benefits and eliminate harm, and if the effect is remarkable, you will be given five hundred dendrobium of grain.
If it is a wise saying, commenting on the gains and losses of the governor, the leniency and strictness of the government, and the appropriateness of firmness and softness, a thousand dendrobium of grain will be given as a gift.
Don't say I'm dishonest, my integrity is like the bright sun.
Chen Chang and Chu Bi, the chief registrars, said: Reading the decree while holding the bundle in hand makes us sigh.
I am tired and humble from morning to night, and I still want to hear criticism.
We believe that what is good for the people above should be followed by the people below.
However, there are no people trying to persuade me around me, and there are no words of advice from far away. This is because there are almost no things related to gains and losses.
Now that the decree is promulgated, it means that there will be rewards and encouragement. I am afraid that some honest and self-restrained people will be afraid of the rewards and will not speak up; those who are greedy for money will make random reports for the sake of profit.
summary: Wang Chen, courtesy name Chudao, was born in Jinyang, Taiyuan. His grandfather Wang Rou served as a lieutenant general of the Huns in the Han Dynasty, and his father Wang Ji was the prefect of Wei Dong County. Orphaned young, Wang Chen was adopted by his cousin Sikong Wang Chang, whom he served as a biological father, gaining fame for his filial piety toward his stepmother and widowed sister-in-law. He was well-read and skilled in writing. General Cao Shuang recruited him as a subordinate officer, and he gradually rose to minister under Zhongshu's family. After Cao Shuang's execution, Wang Chen was dismissed as an old official but later reappointed as censor of the book administration department and transferred to secretary supervisor. During the Zhengyuan period, he was promoted to Sanqi Changshi and Shizhong, overseeing writings. Together with Xunjie and Ruan Ji, he compiled the "Book of Wei," though he often concealed taboos and did not record events as truthfully as Chen Shou. Duke Gaogui of Wei, eager to learn and talented, frequently invited Wang Chen and Pei Xiu to lectures and banquets in Shutang. When the Duke planned to attack Emperor Wen, he summoned Wang Chen and Wang Ye to inform them, but Wang Chen and Wang Ye quickly reported to Emperor Wen. For this, they were granted the title of Marquis of Anping with two thousand households. Wang Chen's disloyalty to his master drew public criticism. He was soon promoted to minister and sent to supervise military affairs in Yuzhou as General Fenwu and governor. Upon arrival, he issued a decree encouraging criticism and recommendations, offering rewards of grain for those who exposed corruption or proposed beneficial policies. His chief registrars, Chen Chang and Chu Bi, advised caution, fearing that rewards might deter honest people or attract greedy ones. Wang Chen initially insisted on his sincerity but eventually relented, following Chu Bi's advice. He then focused on good governance, implementing legal prohibitions established since Jia Kui and promoting education to reform declining customs.

translation:
Wang Chen was famous for his talents and fame at that time. Therefore, Yang Hu, Xun Xu, Pei Xiu, Jia Chong and others all discussed with Wang Chen about starting a business.
When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, because of his merits in assisting the emperor, he was transferred to the general of hussars, the secretary of green, and the regular attendant of casual cavalry to control the military outside the city.
He was granted the title of Duke of Boling County, but he resolutely refused to accept it, so he was promoted to the title of County Duke and granted the title of 1,800 households.
The emperor was about to appoint him as a minister in power, but he died in the second year of Taishi.
The emperor wore plain clothes to express his condolences, and gave the coffin a set of court clothes, a set of clothes, 300,000 yuan, 100 pieces of cloth, and a hectare of land for burial, with the title of Yuan.
The next year, the emperor recalled Wang Shen's achievements and issued an edict: "To praise the past merits is to respect the virtuous and spread the ancient teachings, to pay careful attention to the dead and commemorate the ancestors, to promote morality and promote religion."
The late Sanqi Changshi, Hussar General, and Prince Boling Yuangong Wang Shen followed etiquette and lived in the right path. He was loyal, honest and pure. He studied ancient books carefully and was knowledgeable.
He held the official position of Chang Bonayan successively in the imperial court, taking on the important task of governing a party when going abroad, making plans internally, and showing his power and strategies externally.
When establishing a country and setting up official positions, he first ascends to the position of three ministers and assistant ministers, and is also responsible for the internal affairs of the court and issuing the emperor's orders. This is indeed a meritorious service to assist the country.
He gave it to Wang Shen Sikong Gong posthumously to express his favor to the past and make him immortal after death.
In addition, because of his assistant's meritorious service, he should have been knighted by the Duke, but he firmly refused, praising his modest character and not changing his ambition.
The officials of the county can be allowed to attend the funeral.
Wang Chen was always honest and frugal, and did not own any property.
He sent the soldiers he led to build fifty houses.
He was succeeded by his son Wang Jun.
Later, Wang Shen's wife Xun passed away and they were to be buried together. Wang Shen's coffin had decayed, so they were given a new coffin for the nobles.
During the Xianning period, Wang Shen was granted the title of Duke.
Wang Jun's courtesy name is Peng Zu.
The mother's surname was Tang, and she was the daughter of an innocent family. Her family was poor. She went to Wang Shen's house, so she gave birth to Wang Jun. Wang Chen despised him at first.
When Wang Jun was fifteen years old, Wang Chen passed away without a son. His relatives jointly made Wang Jun his heir, and he was worshiped as Prince Consort.
In the early years of Taikang, he and all the princes went to the feudal country.
Three years later, he returned to Beijing to see him and was appointed as the minister of foreign cavalry.
In the early years of Yuankang, he was transferred to Yuanwai Changshi, and was promoted to Yue Cavalry School Lieutenant and General of the Right Army.
He left the capital to serve as the governor of Hanoi, but because the county prince could not be appointed as the governor, he was transferred to General Dong Zhonglang to guard Xuchang.
When Prince Minhuai was imprisoned in Xuchang, Wang Jun followed Empress Jia's will and killed the prince together with Sun Lu of Huangmen.
He was promoted to general of Ningbei and governor of Qingzhou.
Soon he was appointed as General Ningshuo, Chijie, and Commander-in-Chief of Youzhou's military affairs.
summary: Wang Chen was promoted to General Zhenglu and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs north of the Yangtze River. When the fifth-class title system was established, he was granted the title of Marquis of Boling. During the pacification of Shu, Wu forces threatened the border, but Wang Chen defended well, causing the enemy to retreat. He was later transferred to General Zhennan. After Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Wang Chen became imperial censor and abided by the Shangshu order. Known for his talent and fame, he consulted with Yang Hu, Xun Xu, Pei Xiu, and Jia Chong on state affairs. For his role in the abdication, he was promoted to general of hussars and granted the title of Duke of Boling County, which he initially refused but later accepted with 1,800 households. He died in the second year of Taishi, and the emperor mourned him with lavish gifts. Posthumously, he was given the title of Sikong Gong. Wang Chen was always honest and frugal, leaving no property. His son Wang Jun succeeded him.

translation:
At that time, the court was in chaos and thieves were emerging. For his own safety, Wang Jun made friends with Yi Di and married one of his daughters to Xianbei Wu Wuchen and the other to Su Shuyan.
After King Sima Lun of Zhao usurped the throne, the three kings raised troops to protest. Wang Jun led the troops to wait and see, preventing the message from being passed on, so that the people in his territory could not join the rebel army. King Sima Ying of Chengdu wanted to attack Wang Jun but had no time.
King Zhao Sima Lun was executed, and Wang Junjin was named General Anbei.
When Sima Yi, king of Hejian, and Sima Ying, king of Chengdu, attacked Luoyang and killed Sima Yi, king of Changsha, Wang Jun felt indignant.
Sima Ying petitioned Youzhou Governor Shi Kan to serve as You Sima, replaced Shi Kan with You Sima He Yan, and secretly ordered He Yan to kill Wang Jun and annex Wang Jun's army.
Heyan and Wuwan Shanyu Shendeng planned this matter, so they agreed with Wang Jun to go to the clear spring in the south of Jicheng to play.
There are two roads going west in Jicheng, one for He Yan and one for Wang Jun.
He Yan prepared to take the opportunity to strike when he met Wang Jun with the honor guard.
It was raining heavily and all the weapons were wet, so they returned without being able to realize their plan.
Shan Yu therefore plotted with his fellow tribesmen and said: He Yan planned to kill Wang Jun, but when he was about to succeed, it rained and the plan failed to come true. This is God's help to Wang Jun.
Going against God's will is unlucky, and I cannot be complicit with He Yan for a long time.
So he told Wang Jun his plan.
Wang Jun secretly ordered the army to impose martial law, and He Chanyu surrounded He Yan.
He Yan took the white banner and went to Wang Jun's place to surrender, so He Yan was killed and Wang Jun occupied Youzhou himself.
He built equipment on a large scale, summoned Wuchen, and led a total of 20,000 Hu and Jin people to march against Sima Ying.
With Chief Qi Hong as the vanguard, he encountered Sima Ying's general Shi Chao in Pingji and defeated Shi Chao.
Wang Jun took advantage of the victory and captured Yecheng. The soldiers looted and looted brutally, and many people died.
The Xianbei people plundered women wantonly. Wang Jun ordered the beheading of women who dared to hide them, so eight thousand people were thrown into the Yishui River.
The disaster for the people began at this time.
Wang Jun returned to Ji, and his reputation and strength became even stronger.
Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, will welcome the emperor, and Wang Jun sends Qi Hong to lead Karasuma's cavalry as the vanguard.
Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang, and Wang Jun was transferred to General Hussar, Commander-in-Chief of Shu Yi and Hebei military forces, and governor of Youzhou, using the Yan Kingdom to increase the fiefdom of Boling.
Emperor Huai ascended the throne and appointed Wang Jun as Sikong and Wuwan Xiaowei, and Wu Wuchen as the Great Chanyu.
Wang Jun also petitioned to grant Wu Wuchen the title of Duke of Western Liaoning, and his subordinate Da Piaohua and his younger brother Kemo's subordinate Datu Weng and others as pro-Jin kings.
During the Yongjia period, Shi Le invaded Jizhou. Wang Jun sent the Xianbei people Wenyang to conquer Shi Le, but Shi Le fled to Nanyang.
The next year, Shi Le invaded Jizhou again, and the governor Wang Bin was killed by Shile. Wang Jun also took charge of Jizhou.
summary: Wang Jun, courtesy name Peng Zu, was born to a poor mother from a common family. Initially despised by his father, he became heir at fifteen after Wang Chen's death. He served as Prince Consort and later held various military and civil posts. During the chaos of the court, he allied with Yi Di, marrying his daughters to Xianbei leaders for safety. After King Sima Lun of Zhao usurped the throne, Wang Jun led troops to wait and see. He later killed He Yan, who plotted against him, and occupied Youzhou. He built equipment and led 20,000 Hu and Jin troops against Sima Ying, defeating his general and capturing Yecheng, where his soldiers looted brutally. Wang Jun's power grew, and he was promoted to General Hussar and Commander-in-Chief of Hebei. During the Yongjia period, he fought Shi Le and Liu Kun, but his harsh rule led to defections. He planned to become emperor based on prophecies, killing those who advised against it. Shi Le pretended to surrender, and Wang Jun, trusting him, was captured and killed. Wang Jun had no sons, and his title passed to his nephew Daosu.

translation:
When he was young, he was appreciated by his brother-in-law Chen Qun.
He was extremely filial by nature, and was famous at an early age, with extensive knowledge and thoughtful thinking.
Wei Shi was appointed Zhonglang because of his father's meritorious service.
Emperor Xuan assisted in the government affairs and was surprised to see Xun Hao and said, "He is really Xun Lingjun's son."
He was promoted to the rank of Sanqi Shilang, and then promoted to the rank of Shizhong.
He taught classics to the young emperor of Wei. He was worshiped as a cavalry captain and given the title of Marquis of Guannei.
He criticized Zhong Huizhi for not being consistent in the Book of Changes, and he discussed with Sima Jun, the king of Fufeng, about who should be the leader in benevolence and filial piety, which was praised by the world.
At that time, Cao Shuang had sole power. He Yan and others wanted to harm Taichang Fu Gu, but Xun Hao rescued him and saved him from danger.
When Gao Guixiang Gong came to the throne, Xunjie said to Emperor Jing: Now that the emperor has ascended the throne, the way to obtain the monarchy is unusual. We should quickly send people to various places to declare benevolence and observe the trends in the outside world.
His mothers Qiu Jian and Wen Qin were indeed dissatisfied and sent troops to rebel.
Xunjie participated in the expedition against Ceqiu Jian and others and made meritorious service. He was promoted to the title of Marquis of Wansuiting and was granted the title of 400 households.
When Emperor Wen assisted in government affairs, he was promoted to Shangshu.
Emperor Wen conquered Zhuge Dan and left Xunjie to guard him.
Xunjie's nephew Chen Tai died. Xunjie replaced Chen Tai as a servant and was also in charge of the staff. He resigned four times and then took office.
Xun Hao succeeded Chen Tai and became more respectful and prudent, comprehensively assessed reputation and reality, and clarified customs.
During the reign of Xianxi, he was promoted to Sikong and became a rural marquis.
Xunjie was over sixty years old. He was filial and devoted. He resigned from his post because of his mother's funeral. He was so sad that he almost lost his mind. He was praised throughout the country.
Emperor Wen ordered that Sikong should be given a funeral ceremonial entourage in accordance with the precedent of the Han Dynasty Fu Guang's funeral for his mother.
After Shu was pacified, five levels of nobility were established, and Xun Zhuan was ordered to formulate etiquette.
Xun Yun Shangshu asked Yang Hu, Ren Kai, Yu Jun, Ying Zhen, and Kong Hao to jointly delete the old regulations and compile the Jin etiquette.
In the early years of Xianxi's reign, he was granted the title of Marquis of Linhuai.
Emperor Wu ascended the throne, was promoted to the title of Duke, and had 1,800 households living in the city.
He also went to Shao and said: In the past, Yu appointed nine officials to carry out the five religions, to uphold the king's teachings and show the laws and etiquette.
I accepted the great cause, but I was ignorant of the Dao. I wanted to teach the people the five ethics to make the world peaceful.
Attendant and Sikong Xunzhuan, fair, honest and ambitious, assisted the late emperor and me. He really has the merit of assisting and tutoring the emperor.
He should be in charge of enlightenment rituals to make the world more stable and peaceful.
Xunjie was appointed Situ.
Soon he was appointed as a sergeant, and was promoted to Taiwei and Commander-in-Chief of all the military affairs in Yamen outside the city. He was assigned a hundred personal soldiers of Sima.
Soon after, another edict was issued saying: "Shi Zhong, Taiwei Xun Pin, is gentle, respectful, loyal and fair, has pure conduct, is knowledgeable about ancient affairs and is knowledgeable, and is not slacking off despite his advanced age."
Let him act as the Crown Prince and Tutor, and his official positions of Shizhong and Taiwei will remain.
At that time, because the elegant songs in "Zhengde" and "Dayu" did not match, Xunhao was ordered to settle the music.
Before the matter was over, he died in the tenth year of Taishi.
The emperor mourned for him, the crown prince attended the funeral in person, and the emperor and empress presented items for the funeral furnace. The etiquette level exceeded the norm.
The edict said: "Servants, Taiwei, Princes and Tutors, Linhuai Gong Xun Chan, have pure conduct and follow morality, are honest and fair in government, hold various internal and external official positions, have outstanding achievements, teach the prince, and promote good and beautiful ways. They can be said to be people with perfect behavior, beginning and ending."
summary: Xunjie, courtesy name Jingqian, was from Yingchuan and the sixth son of Wei Taiwei Xun You. Known for filial piety and extensive knowledge, he served as Zhonglang and later Sanqi Shilang. He taught the young emperor of Wei and was granted the title of Marquis of Guannei. He rescued Fu Gu from Cao Shuang's harm and advised Emperor Jing to declare benevolence after Gao Guixiang Gong's ascension. He participated in suppressing rebellions and was promoted to Marquis of Wansuiting. Under Emperor Wen, he became Shangshu and later Sikong. He was filial, resigning for his mother's funeral, and was praised nationwide. He formulated Jin etiquette and was promoted to Duke of Linhuai. He served as Crown Prince Tutor and Taiwei, settling music before dying in the tenth year of Taishi. The emperor mourned him greatly. Xunjie understood the "Three Rites" but lacked upright moral integrity, catering to Xun Xu and Jia Chong. He had no sons, and his title passed to his grandnephew Xun Hui.

translation:
At that time, the official cavalry sent a request to enter the Shu Kingdom as an assassin. Gou Xu said to Emperor Wen: Duke Ming rules the world by justice, and he should rely on justice to defeat disobedience.
If you rely on assassins to eliminate enemies, you will not be the so-called model of the world. Relying on virtue to make distant people surrender.
Emperor Wen thought it was right.
When Zhong Hui rebelled, the details had not yet been discovered, and outsiders came to report first.
Emperor Wen had always been kind to Zhong Hui and did not believe that he would rebel.
Xun Xu said: Although Zhong Hui was favored, he was not necessarily loyal by nature, so he had to take precautions.
Emperor Wen immediately went out to guard Chang'an. Guo Yi, the chief secretary, and Wang Shen, who joined the army, persuaded Emperor Wen to repel Xun Xu because he was Zhong Hui's nephew and uncle. He grew up in his uncle's family when he was young.
Emperor Wen did not accept it, but asked Xun Xu to accompany him and treated him as before.
Before this, Xun Xu stated that in order to conquer Shu, Wei Xuan should be appointed as the supervisor of the army.
When the war broke out in Shu, it was all up to Wei Xuan to maintain it.
After the Zhonghui rebellion was put down, he returned to Luoyang and took charge of important departments together with Pei Xiu and Yang Rong.
At that time, an envoy was sent to visit the State of Wu, and the literati at that time were asked to write documents to Sun Hao. Emperor Wen chose the document written by Xun Xu.
Sun Hao replied that he agreed to the marriage, and Emperor Wen said to Xun Xu: The documents you wrote before made Wu Guo want to submit, which is better than a hundred thousand troops.
Emperor Wen ascended the throne of Jin and appointed Xunxu as his minister. He was granted the title of Anyangzi and was granted a settlement of 1,000 households.
Emperor Wu accepted the abdication and was granted the title of Duke of Jibei County.
Xun Xu resolutely refused and became a marquis because of Yang Hu's modesty.
The official worship was Zhongshu Supervisor, and he was added as a servant. He was also in charge of writings and jointly formulated laws and regulations with Jia Chong.
Jia Chong was about to guard Guanyou, and Xun Xu said to Feng Shou: "If you buy a public servant, you will be sent far away, and we will lose our power."
The prince's marriage has not yet been decided. If Maichong's daughter is made the concubine, Jia Chong will not be able to leave without having to persuade her to stay.
Xun Xu and Feng You both said when the emperor was free that Maichong's daughter would have unparalleled beauty. If she married into the East Palace, she would be able to assist the prince and have the virtues of the concubine in "Guan Ju".
So they got married.
At that time, he was very disgusted by honest people and was ridiculed as flattery.
After a long time, he was promoted to Doctor Guanglu.
After taking charge of rituals and music, he also revised the music rhythm, which became popular in the world.
At first, Gou Xu heard the cow bell from Merchant Zhao on the road. Memorized the sound.
When he was in charge of ritual music and the music was not harmonious, he said: "It will be harmonious if I get Zhao's cowbell."
So he ordered all counties and counties to send cow bells, and the music was indeed harmonious.
He once had a meal in front of the emperor's throne and said to the people present: "This meal is cooked with the feet of a cart."
Don't believe what he said.
The emperor sent a human chef, who replied: "It is indeed an old cart wheel."
Everyone admired his clarity.
Soon he also served as secretary-supervisor, and together with Zhongshu ordered Zhang Hua to compile bookkeeping classics according to Liu Xiang's "Bielu".
He also established a doctor of books and arranged for his disciples to teach and study, following the example of Zhong Yao and Hu Zhao.
In the early years of Xianning, he, together with Shi Bao and others, were among the auxiliary officials who carved stones.
When Wang Jun petitioned to attack Wu, Xunxu and Jia Chong resolutely dissuaded him, but the emperor did not listen, and the kingdom of Wu was indeed reduced.
Because Xun Xu was in charge of edicts, he made one of his sons the Marquis of Ting based on his merits, gave him a thousand households in the city, and granted him a thousand bolts of silk.
He also named his grandson Xunxian the Marquis of Yingyang Ting.
After obtaining the ancient asparagus script from Jijun's tomb, he issued an order to Xunxu to compile it as the "Zhongjing" and include it in the palace collection.
At that time, there was a discussion about sending princes to enfeoff the country. The emperor asked Xun Xu, and Xun Xu replied: All the princes are already governors, and if they are allowed to enfeoff the country, they will abandon the post of local governor.
summary: Xun Xu, courtesy name Gongzeng, was from Yingyin, Yingchuan, and the great-grandson of Han Sikong Xun Shuang. Orphaned young, he was raised by his uncle. He was intelligent and wrote articles in his teens. He served under Cao Shuang and later became Zhongshu Tongshilang. After Cao Shuang's death, he alone attended the funeral, earning respect. He served as Anyang Order and later Tingweizheng, participating in Emperor Wen's military affairs. He advised against assassins and warned of Zhong Hui's rebellion. He wrote documents to Sun Hao of Wu, which were praised as better than a hundred thousand troops. After Emperor Wu's abdication, he was granted the title of Duke of Jibei County but refused, becoming a marquis. He served as Zhongshu Supervisor and jointly formulated laws with Jia Chong. He helped secure Jia Chong's daughter as crown prince's concubine, drawing criticism. He revised music rhythms and compiled classics. He opposed the attack on Wu but was overruled. He advised against sending princes to feudal states and discussed reducing officials. He praised the prince's character, leading to respect for He Jiao and disdain for him. He died in the tenth year of Taikang, with ten sons, including Xun Ji, Xun Fan, and Xun Zu. Xun Xu's descendants continued his legacy, with Xun Sui and Xun He crossing the river eastward during the chaos.

If it is a court meeting on other days, you can naturally be polite.

Xia Shao obeyed him.
When Xianhe died in the seventh year, he was given a posthumous gift to the imperial servant, and his name was Mi.
Feng Squid, courtesy name Shaozhou, was born in Anping.
His grandfather, Feng Fu, was the school captain of Wei Sili.
His father, Feng Yuan, was the prefect of Ji County.
Feng You read a lot of classics and history books when he was young, and he was smart and eloquent.
He successively served as the prefect of Wei County, transferred to the infantry school captain, and was transferred to Yueqi.
He was highly regarded by Emperor Wu and was soon promoted to General Zuowei.
He was able to please the emperor obediently and favored him greatly. Both Jia Chong and Xun Xu were friendly to him.
Jia Chong's daughter became the dowager, and Feng Shou helped in this matter.
When Concubine Jia was about to be deposed, Feng Shou and Xun Xu tried their best to save her, so she was not deposed.
During the battle against Wu, Feng You, who was also the prefect of Runan, led the county soldiers to follow Wang Jun into Moling.
He was promoted to censor Zhongcheng and transferred to Shizhong.
After the emperor recovered from a serious illness, Feng You and Xun Xu's desire to see each other inside and outside the court rested on Qi King Sima You. Sima You had always looked down on Xun Xu.
Because the prince was stupid, Xun Xu was afraid that Sima You would succeed to the throne, which would be harmful to him, so he asked Feng Shou to tell the emperor: If your majesty has not recovered from his illness some time ago, the prince may be deposed.
summary: Feng You, courtesy name Shaozhou, was from Anping. He read extensively and was eloquent. He served as prefect of Wei County and later General Zuowei, favored by Emperor Wu. He befriended Jia Chong and Xun Xu, helping Jia Chong's daughter become dowager. He opposed the attack on Wu but later followed Wang Jun into Moling. He advised the emperor to send Qi King Sima You to his feudal state, leading to Sima You's death. He hated Zhang Hua and prevented his promotion. He died in the seventh year of Taikang, leaving two sons, Feng Bo and Feng Xiong. The historian comments that Wang Chen's disloyalty and Wang Jun's violence brought disaster, while Xunjie and Xun Xu, despite their talents, contributed to court strife. Feng You's flattery led to Sima You's death and Jia's rise, causing endless civil unrest.

Empress Xia Yuan Jing Yu, Yu Zhang Jun Ming, Empress Mu Yu became Gong Du Empress

Queen Yuan Jingyu's name was Meng Mu, a native of Jiyang Waihuang.
His father's name is Yu Yu, and his deeds can be found in "The Biography of Foreign Relatives".
When Emperor Yuan was King Langxie, he married the queen as his concubine and had no sons.
He died in the sixth year of Yongjia at the age of thirty-five.

During the Taining period, Emperor Ming commemorated his mother's kindness in raising her and gave Yuzhang's wife Wang as the queen of Qiuyang County. His aunt Sanqi often served as the wife of Sima Han, the king of Xinye, as the queen of Pingyang Township.
The Xun family of Yuzhang Jun was a palace member of Emperor Yuan.
After being favored at first, she gave birth to Emperor Ming and King Langxie Sima Sui, so she was hated by Empress Yu.
Because of his low status and constant resentment, he was condemned by Emperor Yuan and gradually became alienated and neglected.
When Emperor Ming came to the throne, he was granted the title of Jianxuanzhou and built another residence.
In the first year of Zuo Zhen's reign, Dandao welcomed her back to the palace and provided her with grand and generous supplies.
When Emperor Cheng came to the throne, he treated her with the same respect as the Queen Mother.
He died in the first year of Xiankang.
Shao Shu said: I suffered misfortune when I was young, but it was Jian Sairi who taught me lovingly and worked hard to raise me.
Once I pass away, I really want to repay the favor and will always miss the past and be sentimental and sad.
He was given the title of Yuzhang County Lord and built another temple in Kyoto.
Empress Muyu of the Ming Dynasty was named Wenjun and was a native of Yanling, Yingchuan. His father Yu Bi's deeds can be found in "The Biography of Foreign Relatives".
The queen has a kind temperament and beautiful appearance.
After Emperor Yuan heard about it, he appointed her as the crown princess, and she was respected for her good virtues.
Emperor Ming ascended the throne and became queen.
The book says: Concubine Yu previously followed the Holy Order and served as a concubine in the East Palace. She was respectful of women, loving and courteous.
summary: A detailed account of the empresses, consorts, and dowagers of the Jin Dynasty, chronicling their lives, titles, deaths, and roles in court politics. Empress Xia Yuan Jing Yu, who died young before her husband became emperor, and was later posthumously honored. Her rival, Concubine Zhang, bore Emperor Ming but was hated by Empress Yu and neglected by Emperor Yuan; she was later honored by her son. Empress Ming Mu Yu, known for her virtue, served as regent for her young son, Emperor Cheng, during a rebellion, and died in distress. translation:
This is a clear precedent that I should follow.
Queen Mingmu did not force him to change his mind, so she appointed King Langxie as King of Kuaiji and posthumously named the Queen as Princess of Kuaiji.
Emperor Jian Wen ascended the throne and would have time to add titles in the future.

In the 19th year of Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict saying: Concubine Kuaiji is the mother of virtue and virtue, with a harmonious sound of virtue, full of sage wisdom, and illumination of the Jin Dynasty.
The late emperor gave the wise and kind-hearted concubine Kuaiji an additional honorary title. The court's opinions were inconsistent, and the Tao was suspected of being distorted.
I stated that I would follow the late Emperor's ambition and always warned him in my heart.
Today, in accordance with the "Spring and Autumn Annals", the Han Dynasty and the past practices of Emperor Xiaohuai, the concubine is given the title of Empress Dowager Jian Wenxuan.

Respect has reached the extreme. Because of the ministers, she can be called the Queen Mother, and the ceremony of the mausoleum and temple is complete.
If they are buried together and sacrificed, it is not allowed by the righteousness and etiquette.
Complied with him.
Queen Jian Wenshun's name is Jian Ji, a native of Jinyang, Taiyuan. His father Wang Xia's deeds can be found in "Biography of Foreign Relatives".
Because the queen came from a distinguished family, she was originally the princess of Kuaiji. She gave birth to a son, Daosheng, who was established as the prince.
In the fourth year of Yonghe, both mother and son lost the emperor's favor and were both imprisoned and deposed. The queen died of depression.
In the second year of Xian'an, Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne and was given the additional honorary title of Queen Shun. They were buried together in Gaoping Mausoleum. At first Emperor Jian Wen was the king of Kuaiji and had three sons, all of whom died in infancy.

The emperor ordered the soothsayer Hu Qian to divine for this purpose. Hu Qian said: There is a woman in the back room who will be able to give birth to two rich boys, one of whom will eventually prosper and advance to the imperial family.

Emperor Xiaowu had just ascended the throne and respected her as Concubine Shu.
In the third year of Taiyuan, he was promoted to a nobleman. In the ninth year, she was promoted to wife.
In the twelfth year, she became the imperial concubine, and the ceremonial dress was exactly the same as that of the empress dowager.
In the 19th year, King Daozi of Kuaiji declared: "Mothers value their sons, and they are rich in blessings and gifts."
I believe that the virtue of the Crown Princess shines everywhere, and the blessing of her virtue has been gathered for a long time. She has begun to have good fortune in the holy light, and has inherited the sound of virtue from her ancestors.
Although subtle or prominent are based on the same consideration, the title is not respectful to the extreme and cannot express respect for the Sacred Heart. Unable to answer the gods.

summary: The text concludes with a historian's commentary, praising virtuous empresses who aided the dynasty's rise, while condemning those like Empress Jia Nanfeng for causing decline. translation:
Chen Qian’s son, Pei Xiuzi, and his younger brother Kaikai Zixian
Chen Qian was a native of Shuyang, Linhuai.
His father, Chen Jiao, was a Situ of Wei.
Chen Jiao was originally from the Liu family in Guangling, and was raised by his maternal grandfather Chen, so he changed his surname.
Chen Qian is deep and resourceful.
At the beginning, Chen Jiao was appointed as Shangshu Ling, and his attendant Liu Ye was favored by Emperor Wei Ming, who falsely accused Chen Jiao of monopolizing power.
Chen Jiao was worried and fearful, so he asked Chen Qian.
Chen Qian said: The emperor is wise and his father is a minister. If things don't go as planned, it's just not doing justice.
Later, the emperor's doubts were indeed eliminated. When Chen Qian was a boy, he was insulted by Xia Houxuan, but he looked calm, so Xia Houxuan thought he was unusual.
He initially served as an official as Shangshu Lang, and later became the Grand Administrator of Zhongshan and Anping, both of which had remarkable achievements.
He was promoted to Sima, Changshi, and Yushi Zhongcheng of the Prime Minister. He was promoted to Shangshu and was granted the title of Tinghou of Anguo.
When the Shu Kingdom invaded Longyou, Chen Qian used the title of Shangshu Zhijie and conquered the Shu generals on his behalf, defeated the enemy and returned to the dynasty.
Coinciding with the Zhuge Dan Rebellion, he also acted as Minister of General Anshu.
Shouchun was pacified, and he paid homage to the envoy Chijie, the commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Huaibei, and the general Andong, and his title was promoted to Marquis of Guangling.
He was transferred to the governorship of Yuzhou's military affairs and the governor of Yuzhou, but his positions of Chijie and general remained.
He was also transferred to be the Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs in the south of the Yangtze River, the Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs in Jingzhou, the General of the Conquest of the South, and was granted the title of Marquis of Tan.
Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, and Chen Qian was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry for his merits in assisting Tianming. He was granted the title of Duke of Gaoping County, promoted to the rank of Shizhong, Grand General, and served as the Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou's military affairs. The rest of his official positions remained the same, with the fake Huangyue.
He captured the city of Zhili in the state of Wu, defeated Tu Zhong's troops, and granted Chen Qian's brother's son, Chen Kui, the title of Marquis of Guanzhong.
In the early years of Xianning, he was promoted to Taiwei and transferred to Grand Sima.
Chen Qian took the opportunity to enter the court and said to the emperor: Hu Lie and Qian Hong are both brave and overconfident. They are not capable of stabilizing border defense and will bring shame to the country.
I hope your Majesty will take a closer look.
At that time, Qian Hong was appointed governor of Yangzhou and did not obey Chen Qian's orders.
The emperor thought that the two men were at odds with each other, so he recruited Qian Hong. After his arrival, he soon became the governor of Liangzhou.
Chen Qian sighed privately, thinking that this move would definitely lead to failure.
The two men later lost their peace with the Qiang Rong, and both died at the hands of enemy invaders. After years of conquests, they could only achieve peace, and the emperor regretted it very much.
Chen Qian was magnanimous, tolerant and generous when he was young, and had achievements in any position.
He, Maichong, Shi Bao, Pei Xiu and others were all assistant ministers, but Chen Qian was superior to them in resourcefulness, and Maichong and others thought they were not as good as him.
summary: Chen Qian, a native of Shuyang, Linhuai, was the son of Chen Jiao, a Situ of Wei. Chen Jiao, originally from the Liu family, was raised by his maternal grandfather and changed his surname. Chen Qian was known for his depth and resourcefulness. Early in his career, he advised his father during a false accusation by Liu Ye, which was later resolved. As a youth, he remained calm when insulted by Xia Houxuan, impressing him. He served as Shangshu Lang, Grand Administrator of Zhongshan and Anping, achieving remarkable success. He rose to Sima, Changshi, and Yushi Zhongcheng, then Shangshu, and was granted the title of Tinghou of Anguo. During the Shu invasion of Longyou, he led forces to victory. He also acted against the Zhuge Dan rebellion. After pacifying Shouchun, he was appointed envoy Chijie, commander of Huaibei military affairs, and General Andong, with his title promoted to Marquis of Guangling. He later governed Yuzhou and was transferred to command military affairs south of the Yangtze and in Jingzhou, becoming General of the Conquest of the South and Marquis of Tan. When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, Chen Qian was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry for his merits, granted the title of Duke of Gaoping County, and served as Shizhong, Grand General, and commander of Yangzhou military affairs. He captured Zhili in Wu and defeated Tu Zhong's forces. In the early Xianning years, he was promoted to Taiwei and then Grand Sima. He warned the emperor about Hu Lie and Qian Hong's overconfidence, but the emperor dismissed his concerns. Both later died in conflict with the Qiang Rong, leading the emperor to regret his decision. Chen Qian was magnanimous and achieved success in all positions. He surpassed colleagues like Maichong, Shi Bao, and Pei Xiu in resourcefulness. He held high office beyond retirement age and eventually retired, receiving honors and gifts from the emperor. He died at eighty-one, with the emperor attending his funeral.

Zhuge Dan was pacified, transferred to the position of Minister, and granted the title of Marquis of Luyang Township, adding a thousand households to the city.
Changdao Township Duke succeeded to the throne. Because of his participation in the establishment of the throne, Pei Xiu was promoted to the title of County Marquis, increased the number of households by 700, and was promoted to the position of Minister of Public Affairs.
In the early years of Wei Xianxi's reign, the Xiansi was reformed.
At that time, Xun Zhuan revised the etiquette, Mai Chong revised the law, and Pei Xiu changed the official system.
Pei Xiu proposed the fifth-class title, and more than 600 people from the riding governor level and above were awarded the title.
So Pei Xiu was granted the title of Marquis of Jichuan, with a land area of ​​60 miles, a settlement of 1,400 households, and the Jichuan Ruins of Gaoyuan County as the marquis state.
At the beginning, Emperor Wen had not yet determined his successor, but he intended to establish Sima You, Marquis of Wuyang.
Emperor Wu was afraid that he would not be able to establish himself, so he asked Pei Xiu: Is there any theory of appearance?
So he said that he looked strange.
Pei Xiu later told Emperor Wen: "The Zhongfu Army has a high reputation and has the appearance of an emperor. It is definitely not the appearance of a minister."
This determines the heir apparent.
After Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Pei Xiuguan paid homage to Shangshu Ling and Dr. You Guanglu, as well as Dr. Wang Shen, the imperial censor, and General Jia Chong of the Wei Dynasty.
Emperor Wu accepted the abdication and granted him the title of Doctor Zuo Guanglu, the title of Duke of Julu County, and the title of 3,000 households in the city.
At that time, Anyuan Guardsman Hao Xiang wrote to a friend: I and Shangshu Ling Pei Xiu knew each other well, and I saw him seeking personal gain.
Regarding the officials' petition to remove Pei Xiu from his official position, the emperor wrote to Shao: "It is impossible to prevent and avoid adding sinners. This is difficult for the ancients."
Collusion is Hao Xiang's crime. Isn't it something that Shangshu Ling can prevent!
Don't ask about it.
Li Yi, the captain of the Sili school, said again that Liu Shang, the captain of the cavalry, ordered Pei Xiu to invade the public rice fields and requested to restrict Pei Xiu's freedom of movement.
The edict also said that Pei Xiu assisted in government affairs and had meritorious service to the royal family. Small shortcomings could not cover up his great virtues. He sent people to investigate Liu Shang's guilt and lifted the restrictions on Pei Xiu.
A long time later, the emperor issued an edict saying: The responsibility of the three divisions is to assist the royal family and assist in royal affairs.
summary: Pei Xiu, courtesy name Ji Yan, was from Wenxi, Hedong. His grandfather Pei Mao and father Pei Qian were ministers. Pei Xiu was eager to learn and wrote articles at eight. His uncle Pei Hui had many guests, and Pei Xiu's mother was once humiliated by her aunt, but Pei Xiu's reputation grew. He was recommended to Cao Shuang, who recruited him. After Cao Shuang's death, he was dismissed but later served as Tingweizheng and Wei Sima, with his policies adopted. He participated in the campaign against Zhuge Dan and was promoted to Minister and Marquis of Luyang Township. He helped establish the throne and was promoted to County Marquis. In the Xianxi era, he reformed the official system, proposing the fifth-class title. He was granted the title of Marquis of Jichuan. He advised Emperor Wen on the heir, supporting Emperor Wu. After Emperor Wu's ascension, he became Shangshu Ling and Duke of Julu County. He faced accusations but was defended by the emperor. He was later made Sikong.

translation:
Pei Xiu founded and formulated court etiquette and extensively stated criminal laws and decrees, which were mostly followed and adopted by the court as precedents.
He reigned for four years and was a famous minister at that time.
Pei Xiu was poorly dressed and did not eat on time. He drank cold wine when he should drink hot wine. He died in the seventh year of Taishi at the age of forty-eight.
The edict said: Sikong was wise, virtuous, and behaved elegantly. He assisted the emperor and supported the dynasty, and his merits and deeds were great.
Just when I was about to make a difference to amend the country's legal system, as a great master and model in the world, he unfortunately passed away. I was very sad.
Give him a noble coffin, a set of court robes, a piece of clothing, three hundred thousand dollars, and a hundred pieces of cloth.
Mi Hao Yuan.
At the beginning, Pei Xiu believed that the management of the thirty-six departments of Shangshu was not clear and that ministers should be allowed to serve. He would die before he could submit a memorial in the future.
His friend sorted out his manuscripts and found the draft above, which discussed the pacification of Wu. It said: Sun Hao is cruel and tyrannical. If he does not take advantage of the wise king to rule the country, he annexes the weak and attacks the ignorant, and leaves it to his descendants. He will not be able to make the enemy surrender. There are good and bad times in the world, and it is not always smooth.
Although I have said it many times, I have not written it into a memorial.
Now that I am seriously ill, I respectfully state it again.
May your Majesty implement it in due course.
Then he sealed the table and played it.
The edict replied: Sikong passed away, and the deep sorrow cannot be erased from my heart.
I also got the draft of the memorial. Although I was seriously ill, I did not forget the royal family and served the country with all my heart.
The more I read, the sadder I became, so I discussed it with all the wise ministers.
In the early years of Xianning, Shi Bao and others were princes and worthy of enjoying the imperial temple.
He has two sons: Pei Jun and Pei Po.
Pei Jun was the heir, and he often served as an official, but he died early.
Pei Jun's concubine Pei Jing was not smart, so he was granted the title of Marquis of Gaoyang Ting, and Pei Jun's younger brother Pei Dian succeeded him.
Pei Yuan's courtesy name is Yimin.
He is very elegant and far-sighted, has extensive knowledge and studied ancient affairs, and has been famous since he was a child.
Zhou Bi, the censor Zhongcheng, saw him and said with emotion: Pei Po is like an arsenal with all kinds of weapons. He is a hero for a while.
Jia Chong is the husband of Pei Dian's aunt. The above table says that Pei Xiu had the merits of assisting the emperor. Unfortunately, his eldest son died, leaving him orphaned and weak.
Pei Po has both talent and virtue, enough to be prosperous and granted a title.
Xia Shao asked Pei Po to inherit the title, but Pei Dian firmly refused, but the emperor refused.
In the second year of Taikang's reign, Pei Dian was conscripted as the crown prince's concubine and promoted to the rank of regular attendant of Sanqi.
Emperor Hui ascended the throne and was transferred to the post of Guozi Jijiu and general of the right army.
summary: Pei Xiu was knowledgeable and compiled the "Yugong Regional Circle," a map with six principles: ratio, accurate observation, road, high-low, fangxie, and roundabout. He established court礼仪 and criminal laws. He died at forty-eight, and the emperor mourned deeply. His son Pei Jun died early, and his younger son Pei Dian succeeded him. Pei Dian, courtesy name Yimin, was elegant and knowledgeable. He served as crown prince's concubine and Sanqi Changshi. He advised against Yang Jun's rebellion and was promoted. He discussed the prince's education and medical standards. He wrote the "Chongyou Lun" against nihilism, arguing for the importance of existence and ritual. He was killed by Sima Lun at thirty-four. His sons Pei Song and Pei Gai were exiled but later restored.

translation:
Wang Hun pleads for Pei Kai, saying: Pei Kai was favored by the promotion of the previous emperor, and was favored by your majesty. It was the autumn of his utmost loyalty.
However, Pei Kai was not good at competition by nature. He used to be a regular servant and asked to be appointed as the governor of Hanoi. Later he was appointed as the servant and asked to be appointed as the Yin of Henan. He had a disagreement with Yang Jun and asked to be appointed as a guard. When he was transferred to Shu Palace, his position was lower than that of his peers at that time. However, he was content to retire indifferently. People with knowledge can see his thoughts.
I am deeply worried that Pei Kai is not cheering up now.
Guang Luxun is short of personnel, I think he can be appointed.
Now that Zhang Hua is in Zhongshu and Wang Rong is in Shangshu, they are enough to control the documents. There is no need for Pei Kai to intervene. There are not many famous officials, so they should be supported and not go against their wishes for long-term benefits.
If he is not accepted, he will be appointed as Guanglu Doctor and Kaifu Yitong.
When he became seriously ill, he issued an edict to send Huangmenlang Wang Yan to visit him. Pei Kai looked back at him and said, "I have never seen him before."
Wang Yan was deeply impressed by his superior intelligence.
Pei Kai was good at identifying talents. At first in Henan, Yue Guang was living in the county and had no reputation. When Pei Kai saw him, he thought he was a strange person and introduced him to the Zaifu.
I once read Xia Houxuan's words: "It's like walking into the ancestral temple respectfully, only seeing the ritual instruments; seeing Zhong Hui said, it's like seeing an armory, only seeing the spears and halberds in front of me; seeing Fu Gu, saying that the ocean is omnipresent; seeing the mountain waves, it's like looking down from a mountain, deep and quiet."
At first, when Pei Kai's family was cooking, some of the yellow rice in the pot became like fists, some like blood, and some like turnip seeds.
Pei Kai died in the year of Zao, at the age of fifty-five, and his title was Yuan.
He has five sons: Pei Yu, Pei Zan, Pei Xian, Pei Li, and Pei Xun.
Pei Yu's courtesy name was Zuming.
He inherited his father's title when he was young, and he rose to the rank of Sanqi Shilang. After his death, he was given the nickname Mi Jian.
Pei Zan, also known as National Treasure, served as Zhongshu Lang. He was very talented and respected by everyone who saw him.
He was especially valued by Wang Sui and often traveled with him.
Wang Sui's father Wang Rong said to him: The national treasure didn't come at first, but you went to him many times. Why?
He replied: Although the national treasure does not understand Wang Sui, Wang Sui himself understands the national treasure.
During the Yang Jun Rebellion, he was killed by the rebels.
Pei Xian's courtesy name is Jingsi.
Young and smart, he likes to make friends.
When he was twenty years old, he completely changed his daily ambitions and advocated Confucianism. He was unable to produce anything for several years.
Xie Kun of Chen County and Yu Gu of Yingchuan were both talented people. They were surprised to see Pei Xian and said to each other: Pei Xian is upright and open-minded. He knows the situation well and is better than his father. As for his deep innocence and not bothering himself with worldly things, he is probably better than his father.
At first, he served as a minister in the East Palace, and successively served as a minister and minister in Huangmen.
Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, appointed him as the governor of Yuzhou, the general of Beizhong Lang, and the governor of Jiajie.
Wang Jun took power and appointed Pei Xian as minister.
In the last years of Yongjia, Wang Jun was defeated by Shi Le. Zaosong and others all went to the military gate to apologize. People who paid tribute and bribed people came and went, but only Hu and Bao Wei stayed at home safely.
summary: Pei Kai, courtesy name Shuze, was Pei Hui's son. He was intelligent and famous young, proficient in "Laozi" and "Yijing." He served as Shangshu Lang and Ding Kelang. He was known as the "Jade Man" for his elegance. He advised Emperor Wu during a divination, calming him. He served as Sanqi Minister and other posts. He was generous, giving away possessions. He criticized Jia Chong's presence in court. He survived the Yang Jun rebellion by hiding. He later served as Zhongshu Ling. He died at fifty-five. His sons included Pei Yu, Pei Zan, Pei Xian, Pei Li, and Pei Xun. Pei Xian, courtesy name Jingsi, was upright and served as Yuzhou governor. He was captured by Shi Le but praised for his integrity. He later served under Shi Le and Jilong, but his sons were killed, and he was dismissed. He died in the Shi family's hands.

translation:
Sima Ao advised Pei Dun to use punishment and execution to establish his prestige, recruit civilians as soldiers on a large scale, and sentence those who did not abide by the law to death.
After three years in office, the people were resentful.
Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, was Pei Dun's brother-in-law.
After Sima Yue died, Riding Governor Man Heng led the civilians he had collected to return him.
Soon Liu Yuanhai sent generals Wang Sang and Tang Gu to send troops to Pengcheng. The vanguard arrived at Xiapi. The civil and military officials could not stand the harsh rule and all fled. Pei Dun and Sima Ao fled to Huaiyin, but their wives and children were captured by bandits.
Sima Ao also persuaded Pei Dun to surrender to Zhao Gu.
Zhao Gu's wife was Pei Dun's daughter and she was favored. Pei Dun cried to her daughter, so Zhao Gu killed Pei Dun.
Pei Dun's younger brother Pei Shao, named Daoqi.
When Emperor Yuan was General Anton, he appointed Pei Shao as the chief historian and Wang Dao as the Sima. The two had a close friendship.
Pei Shao was conscripted as the concubine of the crown prince, and was transferred to the rank of regular servant of Sanqi. He envoy Chijie, the governor of Yangzhou, Jiangxi and Huaibei military affairs, and Shuzhonglang general, followed Sima Yue to Xiangxiang, and died in the army.
When Director Wang became Sikong and took office, he sighed and said: "If Pei Daoqi and Liu Wangqiao are here, I can't hold this official position alone."
Director Wang's son Zhongyu had the same name as Pei Kang. Director Wang missed his old friend, so he changed his name to Jingyu.
Pei Kai's younger brother Pei Chuo, also known as Ji Shu, had a broad mind and served as the Minister of Huangmen and the Captain of Changshui.
Pei Chuo's son Pei Xia was good at talking about mysteries, his words were fluent, and he was as clear as the harp.
I once discussed it with Guo Xiang of Henan, and everyone in the room admired him.
He also played Go with others at Pingshu General Zhou Fu's place.
Zhou Fu's Sima persuaded Pei Xia to drink wine, but Pei Xia did not drink immediately. Sima got drunk and became angry, so he pulled Pei Xia to the ground.
Pei Xia slowly got up and returned to his seat, his expression unchanged, playing chess as before.
His character is so modest and peaceful.
Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, asked him to be the chief registrar, but he was later killed by Sima Yue's son Sima Bi.
At that time, the two families of Pei and Wang were very prosperous in the Wei and Jin Dynasties. People at that time believed that the eight surnames Pei were just like the eight surnames Wang: Pei Hui was better than Wang Xiang, Pei Kai was better than Wang Yan, Pei Kang was better than Wang Sui, Pei Chuo was better than Wang Cheng, Pei Zan was better than Wang Dun, Pei Xia was better than Wang Dao, Pei Yuan was better than Wang Rong, and Pei Miao was better than Wang Xuan.
Shi Chen said: The Zhou Dynasty was considered to have many scholars, and the Han Dynasty was said to have gained sages. They used the astrological analogy to correspond to the destiny.
There was a lack of celebrities at that time, and most people used the term "backbone" to praise him. His family was shining brightly on the country. Could it be that he was talking about Chen Qian?
Pei Xiu's reputation surpassed that of his colleagues and he was called a leader.
When he was young, Pei Kai was very resourceful and knowledgeable.
They are all famous officials of the Jin Dynasty, it is true!
summary: The Pei family was prominent in Wei and Jin, with eight members compared to the eight Wangs. The text praises Chen Qian and Pei Xiu as famous officials of the Jin Dynasty.

translation:
Emperor Xuan had nine sons. Queen Mu Zhang gave birth to Emperor Jing, Emperor Wen, and Sima Wangqian of Pingyuan. Mrs. Fu gave birth to Sima Liang, king of Wencheng in Runan, Sima Nian, king of Langye Wu, Sima Jing, Hou Huiting of Qing Dynasty, and Sima Jun, king of Fufeng Wu. Mrs. Zhang gave birth to Sima Xu, king of Liang, and Sima Lun, king of Zhao, was born to Mrs. Bai.
Sima Liang and Sima Lun have other biographies.
Sima Qian, king of Pingyuan, was named Ziliang.
When he was young, he was granted the title of Marquis of Anyang Ting in the Wei Dynasty as a young master. He gradually moved to the rank of Zhonglang General of the Fu Army and became the Marquis of Pingyang Township.
The fifth-class title was established and the title was changed to Tao Bo.
Emperor Wu ascended the throne and made him the King of Pingyuan. He was granted the title of 11,300 households, two horses for preaching and driving, and the clothes of the attendants.
In the early years of Xianning, kings were sent to feudal states. Sima Qian was seriously ill and could not maintain his rationality. He also liked peace and quiet and had little desire to compromise, so he specially wrote a Shao letter to keep him.
In the last years of Taikang, the official worshiped Dr. Guanglu and was appointed as a servant. He was specially given a gold seal and a purple ribbon, and his rank was the same as that of the three divisions.
Emperor Hui ascended the throne and was promoted to Dr. Zuo Guanglu. His position as a servant remained the same. He wore a sword and wore shoes when going to the palace. There was no need to walk in small steps when entering the court.
Although Sima Qian was the king of a great feudal state and did not take care of government affairs, if he was transferred or replaced, it would be based on his ability.
Although he has a title and salary, it seems that he does not have it with him. The salary, cloth and silk are all piled up in the open air to rot.
On cloudy and rainy days, the bullock carts are driven out and the carts without curtains are put into the warehouse. Someone asked why, and the answer was: carts without curtains are suitable for storage.
When a court official visited him, even though his name was announced, the visitor's carriage and horses would be parked outside the door, and he might not be seen for a whole day.
I was able to visit him sometimes and socialize with others. He was very respectful and humble, and there were no mistakes at first.
Before and after my concubine died and was buried, the coffin was always left unnailed in an empty room at the back. I opened it every few days to look at it, maybe did some obscene things, and waited until the body rotted before burying it.
King Zhao Sima Lun assisted in the government affairs and appointed Sima Qian as General Wei.
Emperor Hui was deposed and re-established. Sima Qian wrote poems and was appointed Taibao.
When King Sima Tong of Qi pacified King Sima Lun of Zhao, the members of the royal family and the officials in the court all comforted Sima Tong with cow wine. Only Sima Qian had a hundred coins in his pocket. When he saw Sima Tong take it out, he said: King Zhao rebelled and rebelled. It is your credit for your righteous deeds. Now I use a hundred coins to congratulate you.
Even so, it is difficult for you to take advantage of the general trend, so you must be cautious.
After Sima Jian assisted in the government affairs, Sima Qian went to visit him, and Sima Tong came out to greet him.
summary: Emperor Xuan had nine sons from various consorts. Queen Mu Zhang bore Emperor Jing, Emperor Wen, and Sima Qian (King of Pingyuan). Mrs. Fu gave birth to Sima Liang (King of Wencheng in Runan), Sima Nian (King of Langye Wu), Sima Jing (Marquis of Huiting in Qing Dynasty), and Sima Jun (King of Fufeng Wu). Mrs. Zhang bore Sima Xu (King of Liang), while Mrs. Bai bore Sima Lun (King of Zhao). Sima Qian, King of Pingyuan, was granted the title of Anyang Tinghou in the Wei Dynasty and later became King of Pingyuan under Emperor Wu with 11,300 households. He suffered from severe illness and was allowed to remain in the capital rather than go to his feudal state. He held various official positions including Guanglu大夫 and served as a servant. Although a great feudal lord, he did not care for government affairs. His salary and goods were left to rot in the open air. He was known for eccentric behavior, such as keeping his concubines' coffins unsealed in empty rooms and opening them to look at them periodically. During the rebellion of King Zhao Sima Lun, Sima Qian was appointed as General Wei and later Taibao. When Sima Tong of Qi pacified Sima Lun, Sima Qian congratulated him with a hundred coins. He died in the fifth year of Yongjia at age eighty.

translation:
After Sima Qian entered the house, he squatted on Sima Gang's bed and refused to let Sima Tong sit down. He said to him: "Don't imitate women." This word means Sima Lun.
When Sima Tong was killed, Sima Qian cried very sadly and said to the people around him: "The clan is gradually declining, and only this son is the best. If you kill him, you will be in danger from now on!"
Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, acted righteously and arrived in Luoyang to visit Sima Qian, but Sima Qian stayed behind closed doors.
Sima Yue's car stayed for a long time before Sima Qian sent someone to see the guest off, while he peeped through the crack in the door.
At that time, no one could fathom his intentions. Some said he was ill, while others thought he was doing something cryptic.
Yongjia died in the fifth year of his reign at the age of eighty.
It happened that Liu Cong invaded Luoyang and had no time to give him the nickname "Mi". He has two sons. The eldest son, Sima Guang, died young. The second son, Sima Yong, was named the Duke of Ande County in the Taixi year and served as a regular attendant. They are both good people.
In trouble, the whole family will be exterminated.
Sima Dian, the king of Langye Wu, was given the title Zijiang in the early years of his reign and was named Nan'antinghou.
He was talented and famous very early. He initially served as General Ningshuo and guarded Yecheng. He had a reputation for being good at appeasing people and making them obey.
Gradually he was moved to serve as a regular servant of Sanqi. In the Jin Dynasty, he was granted the title of Marquis of Shuwu Township. He was appointed as the Right General, supervised the military affairs of Yanzhou, and was the governor of Yanzhou.
The fifth-class title was established and he was named Nanpi Bo.
He was transferred to the post of General Zhenglu, Jiajie. Emperor Wu ascended the throne and granted him the title of Prince of Dongguan County, granting him a fief of 10,600 households.
When the second ministers were first established, a special edict was issued to let the kings choose their own commanders.
Sima Dian asked for permission, but the emperor refused.
After entering the imperial court, he served as Shangshu Youpushe and Fujun General. He was appointed as General Zhenshu, Jiajie, and Commander-in-Chief of Xuzhou's military affairs. He replaced Wei Cui to guard Xiapi.
Sima Dian defended the enemy well, and the soldiers were willing to die to serve him. The people of Wu were afraid of him.
He was granted the title of Kaifu Yitong and the Third Division, and was granted the title of King Langxie, using Dongguan to expand his feudal kingdom.
In the battle of Pingding County, Sun Hao led tens of thousands of troops from Tusheng. Sun Hao sent a letter and seal to Sima Dian to ask for surrender. Shaoshu says: Sima Bodu, King of Langxie, led the troops under his command to occupy Tuzhong one after another, making it impossible for the enemy to save each other.
He also sent the fallen evil minister Liu Hong and others to march towards the Yangtze River. The enemy was shocked and frightened, and sent an envoy to present the fake seal and ribbon.
Sima Dian then sent Chief Shi Wangheng to lead his troops to cross the Yangtze River, break through the enemy's border defenses, capture Lan Bian, the governor, beheaded and surrendered 50,000 to 60,000 people, and condemned Jiang Dan, Yu Sai and others to surrender and plead guilty. Sima Dian's meritorious service was outstanding, and his two sons were granted the title of Marquis of Ting, each with a title of 3,000 households and 6,000 pieces of silk.
Soon, he also supervised all the military affairs in Qingzhou and added the clothing of the servants.
He was promoted to General, Kaifu Yitong and the Third Division.
Sima Dian not only had a distinguished status because he was a relative of the emperor, but also contributed to the pacification of Wu. He restrained himself from being respectful and indulgent, and did not appear to be complacent about his achievements. His staff did their best, and the people were inspired and attached to him.
When he was seriously ill, he was given bed tents, clothes, money, silk, rice and other items, and his servants were sent to greet him.
summary: Sima Dian, King of Langye Wu, was talented and famous from an early age. He served as General Ningshuo guarding Yecheng and later as General Zhenshu guarding Xiapi, where he defended well against the Wu people. During the pacification of Wu, Sun Hao surrendered to Sima Dian, who sent troops across the Yangtze River, capturing enemy officials and securing the surrender of 50,000 to 60,000 people. His two sons were made marquises. He died in the fourth year of Taikang at age fifty-seven. His descendants included Sima Rui, who later became Emperor Yuan, and several others who successively held the title of King of Langye.

translation:
Taikang died in the fourth year of his reign at the age of fifty-seven.
On his deathbed, he petitioned to be buried next to his mother's mausoleum and to divide his kingdom among his four sons. The emperor agreed.
His son, Prince Gong, Sima Su, succeeded to the throne.
He also named his second son, Mo Shan, King of Juni, Sima Yao as King of Dong'an, and Sima Huai as King of Huailing.
Sima Jin's name is Sizu, and he has many officials and servants.
Taixi died in the first year of his reign at the age of thirty-five.
His son Sima Rui succeeded to the throne, also known as Wu Tong.
At the beginning of the restoration of the emperor's empire, the prince Sima Cao was made the king of falling mo and offered sacrifices to Prince Gong.
Sima Pei died early and made his prince Sima Huan the king of Langxie.
He died that day and took the title of Prince Sima Yu as King Langxie.
In the early years of Xianhe, after Sima Yu was transferred to Kuaiji, Emperor Cheng made Emperor Kang the king of Langxie. Emperor Kang ascended the throne and named Emperor Cheng's eldest son Ai Emperor as King Langxie.
Emperor Ai ascended the throne and made the deposed Emperor the king of Langxie.
After the deposed emperor ascended the throne, King Kuaiji acted as the minister of sacrifice for the Langye Kingdom.
Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne, and King Langxie had no successor.
When the emperor was dying, he named his youngest son Daozi King Langxie.
Daozi later became King of Kuaiji, and Emperor Gong was appointed King of Langxie.
After Emperor Gong ascended the throne, Langye Kingdom was abolished.
Sima Dan, the king of Wulingzhuang, was named Sihong.
At first he served as a servant, and later he was granted the title of Duke of Dongwu, with a fief of 5,200 households.
Transferred to the post of former general and central protector.
He is jealous and harmful by nature and has no filial and friendly character.
His younger brother Sima Yao, king of Dong'an, had a good reputation and was loved by his parents. Sima Dan hated him as an enemy, so he spoke ill of Sima Yao to Sima Liang, king of Runan. Sima Liang had always had conflicts with Sima Yao, so he petitioned to abolish him and move him.
King Zhao Sima Lun rebelled and appointed Sima Dan as the leading general.
Sima Dan has always been friendly with Guo Chu in Hanoi and Sima Chu's younger brother.
When the wine was in full swing, He Ye and others talked about the grievances of Tui Gan. Sima Dan was a drunkard by nature, so he killed both of them and gave their heads to Sima Lun. He stopped drinking and went on a violent rampage.
Sima Dan's wife, Su Di, was the queen's sister-in-law.
At first, relying on his family status, he was rude to Sima Dan's mother.
King Sima Tong of Qi was assisting in government affairs. Sima Dan's mother, Princess Zhuge, complained that Sima Dan was unfilial and begged to be let back. Therefore, Sima Dan, his wife and children moved to Liaosai.
His son Sima Xi, who was five years old, refused to go with him, saying: "We should ask to come back for our father, and we should not move together."
After complaining for many years, the concubine passed away, Sima Yao was killed, and then he was able to return to the court.
The official title was Guanglu Dafu, Shangshu, Prince Taifu, and was renamed King Wuling.
In the last years of Yongjia, he was killed by Shi Le, and his son Sima Zhe, King of Ai, succeeded him.
summary: Sima Dan, King of Wulingzhuang, was jealous and harmful by nature with no filial character. He hated his brother Sima Yao and spoke ill of him to Sima Liang. During Sima Lun's rebellion, Sima Dan served as leading general. He killed two men while drunk and gave their heads to Sima Lun. His mother complained of his unfilial behavior, and he was moved to Liaosai with his family. He was later killed by Shi Le in the late Yongjia period.

translation:
