Sima Zhe, whose courtesy name was Jinglin, was a regular servant of Sanqi. He was also killed by Shi Le.
He had no son, so Emperor Yuan later appointed his prince Sima Xi as King of Wuling to offer sacrifices to Sima Dan.
Sima Yao, King of Dong'an, had the courtesy name Si Xuan.
At first, he was the Duke of Dong'an, and he successively served as the minister of Huangmen of Sanqi, and then moved to the position of regular servant of Sanqi.
A person with a beautiful beard, resolute temperament, authority, erudition, filial piety in serving relatives, and exhaustive etiquette in mourning.
When Yang Jun was executed, Sima Yao stationed troops in Yunlong and commanded all the troops. Because of his meritorious service, he was worshiped as the General of the Right Guard and the Colonel of Shesheng. He was granted the title of Prince of the County in the Jin Dynasty and was granted the title of 20,000 households. He was also appointed as the Shizhong and the General of the Dian Army. He also served as the General of the Right Guard.
He was moved to the right servant of Shangshu and appointed as the regular servant of Sanqi.
On this day, more than three hundred people were punished and rewarded, and the orders were all issued from Sima Yao.
The father of Shuyi captain Wen Fang, Sai Leng, was killed by Danwudeng's grandfather, Zhu Jiang Dan. Danwu Xun was worried that Sai Tan was a nuisance to his uncle's family, so Zaotian killed Wen because he was not guilty.
Sima Yao's brother Sima Dan repeatedly accused Sima Liang of being accused by King Sima Liang of Runan, but Sima Liang refused to listen.
At this time, because Sima Yao was arbitrary in punishments and rewards, Sima Dan took the opportunity to speak ill of Sima Yao. Sima Liang was deceived by Sizhui's rhetoric, so he dismissed Yao Sheng from his official position and returned to his mansion as a public servant. He was convicted of rebellious remarks and moved to Daifang.
In the early years of Yongkang, Sima Yao was recruited and his title was restored. His official title was Zong Zhengqing, and he was moved to the post of Shangshu and Zuopushe.
When Emperor Hui was attacking Sima Ying, the king of Chengdu, Sima Yao was holding a funeral for his mother in Ye, and he persuaded Sima Ying to lay down his weapons and surrender.
When the emperor's army was defeated, Sima Ying resented Sima Yao and killed him.
Later, Sima Hun, the Marquis of Changleting, son of Sima Jin, the king of Langxie, was appointed king of Shu'an to offer sacrifices to Sima Yao.
He died soon after and the feudal state was lifted.
Sima Huai, king of Yuan Dynasty in Huailing, was named Sichong.
At first he was granted the title of Duke of Guangling, with a fief of 2,900 households.
He successively served as general of the left and regular attendant of Sanqi.
When King Sima Lun of Zhao usurped the throne, the three kings rebelled. Sima Guan and Zuowei General Wang Yu attacked and killed Sun Xiu, thus deposing Sima Lun.
Because of his meritorious service, he ascended the throne and became the King of Huai Ling. He entered the court and was appointed as the Minister, and was also appointed as the Minister, and was transferred to Zong Zheng and Guang Lu.
After his death, his son Zhenwang Sima Rong succeeded him.
He died without a son. During the reign of Emperor An, he appointed Sima Yun, the grandson of King Wulingwei, as King of Huailing to offer sacrifices to King Yuan.
He died without a son, Yilin! Wang Sima Bao's son Anzhi succeeded him.
Song accepted the abdication and the feudal state was cancelled.
Sima Jing, the Marquis of Huiting in the Qing Dynasty, was given the title Zizuo as a prince in the late Wei Dynasty.
When he died at the age of twenty-four, he was given posthumously as Captain Shesheng, and was succeeded by Emperor Wen's son Sima Ji, courtesy name Taixuan.
In the first year of Taishi, he was granted the title of King of Yan and granted 6,663 towns.
Sima Ji went to the feudal state. In the early years of Xianning, he was recruited as an infantry captain. He used Yuyang County to expand his feudal state and add clothes to his servants.
The official paid homage to the governor of Qingzhou and the general of Zhenshu. During the holidays, he used 10,337 households in Beiping, Shanggu and Guangmi counties to increase the number of Yan Kingdom to 20,000.
He died without a son, so King Sima Jian of Qi asked his son Sima Ji to succeed him.
Later, Sima Tong failed and the feudal state was cancelled.
Sima Jun, the King of Wu in Fufeng, was given the courtesy name Zizang.
He was clever when he was young, and when he was five or six years old, he could write memorials and recite scriptures, and people who saw him were amazed.
When he grows up, he will be quiet, upright and upright, and he will have the best reputation in the clan. In the middle of Wei Jingchu's reign, he was named Pingyang Tinghou.
King Cao Fang of Qi came to the throne. Sima Jun was eight years old and became a regular attendant of Sanqi.
summary: Sima Yao, King of Dong'an, was resolute, authoritative, and learned, with filial piety in serving relatives. He was granted 20,000 households and held various positions. He was arbitrary in punishments and rewards, leading to his dismissal and exile to Daifang. He was later restored but killed by Sima Ying after the emperor's army was defeated. Sima Jun, King of Fufeng Wu, was clever from childhood, able to write memorials and recite scriptures at age five or six. He was quiet, upright, and had the best reputation in the clan. He served as General of Zhenxi, guarding Guanzhong, and was skilled at appeasing rulers. He promoted agriculture and shared labor with soldiers. He suppressed Qiang rebellions and received surrenders from various tribes. He was filial to his mother and eager to learn, writing treatises on benevolence and filial piety. When he died, people wept for him and erected monuments.

translation:
The Duke is responsible for the royal family's barrier and is in an important position to assist the court. He can act as soon as he submits the seal. What's wrong with that?
If evil and evil grow and spread, and disasters are difficult to predict, can this be called supporting the royal family to pacify the Central Plains?
Sima Xin was about to send troops, and Wang Sui said again: "Zhang Chang and other small bandits can be subdued by his own generals. There is no need to disobey the emperor's orders and go to the battlefield in person!"
So he withdrew his troops.
When Zhang Chang arrived at Fancheng, Sima Xin sent troops to resist him. The army was defeated and Zhang Chang killed him.
Posthumously awarded the title of General of Hussars.
He had no sons, so his elder brother's son Sima Shao was his heir. Yongjia died in Shile in the last years of his life.
Liang Xiaowang Sima Xu was named Zihui. He practiced Qingjing, was respectful and prudent, and had no other talents. As a young master, he was named Pingletinghou.
When the fifth-class title was established, he was renamed Kaipingzi.
Emperor Wu ascended the throne and named him King of Liang, granting him 5,358 households.
When he left the enfeoffed country, he was moved to the position of Beizhonglang General and supervised the defense of Yecheng.
At that time, the kings selected their own officials and subordinates, and Sima Shu selected Zhang Fan, the chief official of Ruyin, as the middle official.
Zhang Fan has never been of good character. His real name is Xiong, and his wife Liu knows music and teaches singing to Cao Shuang. Zhang Fan visited He Yan again and committed adultery as he pleased.
He Yan was killed and moved to Hejian, so he changed his name and took the initiative to befriend Sima Xu.
After being reported by relevant officials, Sima Xu was reduced to one county in Xia Shao.
During the Xianning period, Chen Guo and Runan Nandun were added as vassal states.
During the Taikang period, he replaced Kong Xun in supervising the military affairs of Yuzhou, and was appointed General Pingdong to guard Xu Lu.
Soon, he replaced Sima Huang, King of Xiapi, in his original position as supervising the military affairs of Qingzhou and Xuzhou, and was promoted to General Anton.
In the early years of Yuankang, he was transferred to the general of Zhengxi, replacing the Qin King Sima Sai to supervise the military affairs in Guanzhong, and also served as the captain of the Xirong Guards.
He was appointed as a minister and promoted to supervise Liangzhou.
Soon after, he was appointed as General of the Guard, recorded as a minister, acted as the crown prince's Taibao, and was given the title of one thousand soldiers and one hundred horses.
Much later, he was appointed as the General of the Expedition to the West, replacing King Sima Lun of Zhao to guard Guanzhong. He was also the commander-in-chief of the military affairs of Liang and Yong, and appointed the left and right Chang Shi and Sima.
He also served as the captain of the Xirong School, stationed troops in Haozhi, and supervised General Jianwei Qiechu, Zhenwei General Lu Zhong and others in Liumo against the Di enemy bandit Cha Wannian.
There was a conflict between Sima Xu and Dan, who urged him to march and cut off his support. Lu Bo did not save him, so Zhou Chu was killed.
The court accused Sima Xu.
Soon he was recruited as a general, a minister, a leading general, and a minister.
Sima Xu once held a gathering of guests and said to the army workers: My cousin is serving as a minister and cannot swallow his power.
Rights are hard to come by.
summary: Sima Xu, King of Liang, practiced quietness and was respectful and prudent. He served as General of Zhengxi guarding Guanzhong and later as Grand Administrator and Situ. During Sima Lun's usurpation, he served as prime minister. After his death, there was debate over his posthumous name, with some criticizing him for failing to take a stand during crises. He had no sons, and his title passed through various relatives.

translation:
When he grows up, he will be calm, kind and fair, be close to wise people, like charity, like classic books, be able to write articles, be good at letters, and be imitated by the world.
His talent and reputation were greater than those of Emperor Wu, and Emperor Xuan often valued him.
Emperor Jing had no sons, so he made Sima You his heir.
He followed Wang Jun in his campaign and was named the Marquis of Changle Pavilion.
When Emperor Jing died, Sima You was only ten years old. His sorrow moved the people around him and he was praised and praised.
Inherited the title of Wuyang Hou.
After serving Jing Xian Yang in another mansion, he became famous for his filial piety when serving the queen.
He also served as a regular servant of the cavalry and an infantry captain. He was 18 years old at the time. He appeased the subordinates in the military camp and was very majestic and gracious.
The fifth-level title was established, and he was renamed Anchanghou and moved to General Wei.
In mourning for Emperor Wen, he was so disfigured that he could only stand up with a wooden stick.
His subordinates made rice balls into balls for him to eat, but Sima You cried and refused to accept them.
The Queen Mother personally went to enlighten him and said: What should I do if I get other diseases?
You should think long-term and not stick to one idea.
He often sent people to force Sima You to eat, but Sima Jixi remonstrated and said: "Be sad without losing your temper. This is the teaching of a saint."
Moreover, the king is a close relative of the clan and has the important task of assisting in government affairs.
Ordinary people still cherish their lives for the sake of their ancestors, not to mention that you are responsible for the great cause of the world and the important task of assisting the royal family. How can you express your boundless sorrow and compete with Yan Yuan and Min Sun for filial piety!
Don't let wise people laugh at you and fools rejoice.
Ji happy personally served food and drinks, but Sima You had no choice but to eat.
After Ji Xi withdrew, Sima You said to the people around him: "Ji Sima will make me remember the etiquette of mourning and preserve my small body."
Emperor Wu ascended the throne and named Sima You King of Qi. At that time, the imperial court had just been established, and Sima You was in charge of the military affairs. He was responsible for the control of Anning both inside and outside.
Shao Shu discussed how the vassal king asked them to choose the senior officials in the country. Sima You reported: In the past, the sage kings established feudal kingdoms to get close to the princes. The rules were passed down from generation to generation and no one could change them.
The truth is that if the king is not passed down from generation to generation, people will be left to chance; if people do not have stable masters, their customs will be hypocritical and honest.
Therefore, the late emperor deeply studied the orthodoxy that governs all ages, and considered restoring the rules of the ancient sages, dividing land boundaries, and establishing five levels of nobility, either to promote virtue or to reward meritorious officials.
I thought that Your Majesty was following the will of God to establish a great cause, establish feudal relatives, and let the vassal state appoint senior officials on its own.
However, the great cause is now being established and the system has just been established. Although Yongshu is obedient, Wu has not yet surrendered. We should wait until the Qing Dynasty is peaceful before discussing the restoration of the ancient system.
The memorial was sent three times in succession, and they all responded that they disagreed.
summary: Sima You, King of Qi Xian, was wise from youth, calm, kind, and fond of classical books. He was made heir to Emperor Jing and inherited the title of Wuyang Hou. Under Emperor Wu, he was made King of Qi and managed military affairs. He was known for his filial piety and moral conduct. He advised on agricultural policies and government administration. He was especially favored by Emperor Wen, who nearly made him crown prince. However, due to the machinations of Xun Xu and Feng Shou, Emperor Wu sent him to his feudal state. Sima You became ill from resentment and died at age thirty-six while traveling. His son Sima Tong succeeded him.

translation:
Wei Guan, courtesy name Boyu, was born in Anyi, Hedong Province.
During the reign of Emperor Ming of the Han Dynasty, the great ancestor Wei Hao was recruited by the imperial court from Dai County for his proficiency in Confucianism. He went to Anyi, Hedong, and died. The land where he died was given to him for burial, and his descendants settled there.
His father, Wei Jian, was the Minister of Wei.
Wei Guan's father passed away when he was ten years old, and his extreme filial piety exceeded that of ordinary people.
He has a quiet temperament and is good at distinguishing right from wrong, and is known for being knowledgeable and fair.
Inherited his father's title of Marquis of Yuexiang.
At the age of twenty, he became the minister of Wei.
At that time, Wei's laws were strict and detailed, and his mother Chen was worried. Wei Guan asked to be transferred to Tongshilang, and was later transferred to Zhongshulang.
At that time, the court officials were in exclusive power, and Wei Guan was among them. He had no distinction between those who were in power and those who were in power. He was highly regarded by Fu Gu, who called him Ning!
After ten years in the official position, he was known for his competence and was gradually promoted to the rank of regular attendant.
When King Chenliu came to the throne, he paid homage to his ministers and went to Hebei to express his condolences.
Because of the merits of agreeing on major events, the number of households in the fief was increased.
A few years later, he was transferred to Tingweiqing.
Wei Guan is well versed in legal principles, and every time he judges a case, he bases his judgment on reason, no matter how big or small the case is.
When Deng Ai and Zhong Hui conquered Shu, Wei Gan used his former official position to supervise the military affairs of Deng Ai and Zhong Hui, and also served as the Zhenxi Military Division, with a thousand soldiers.
After the Shu Kingdom was pacified, Deng Ai was granted the title in accordance with the emperor's will.
Zhong Hui secretly harbored rebellious intentions because Deng Ai was dictatorial and arbitrary, so he secretly reported the situation with Wei Guan.
The emperor issued an edict to send a guard to arrest Deng Ai, and Zhong Hui sent a guard to arrest Deng Ai first.
Zhong Hui believed that Deng Ai had few soldiers and wanted Deng Ai to kill Wei Guan in order to aggravate Deng Ai's crime.
Wei Guan knew that Zhong Hui wanted to harm him, but he could not refuse, so he arrived in Chengdu at night and sent a message to the generals led by Deng Ai, claiming that he had issued an imperial edict to arrest Deng Ai, and the others ignored him.
If you come to join the army, you will still be rewarded with titles; if you dare not come and join the army, the three clans will be killed.
When the cries of war broke out, they all came to defend Wei Guan. Only Deng Ai's entourage was still there.
When the doors opened at dawn, Wei Guan took the messenger's vehicle and went directly to the Chengdu Palace.
Deng Ai fell asleep before he got up, and both his father and son were captured.
Several generals under Deng Ai planned to kidnap Deng Ai back and went straight to Wei Guan's camp with weapons.
Wei Guan came out of the camp to meet them. He pretended to write a draft of the above table and was going to explain Deng Ai's affairs. The generals believed him and gave up.
As soon as Zhong Hui arrived, he invited all the generals Hu Lie and others, took the opportunity to capture them, imprisoned them in Yizhou Prison, and then sent troops to rebel.
As a result, the soldiers were worried about returning home, there was turmoil inside and outside, and people were worried and fearful.
summary: Wei Guan, courtesy name Boyu, was from Anyi, Hedong. His ancestor Wei Hao was recruited for his Confucian learning during the Han Dynasty, and his father Wei Jian served as a minister. Orphaned at ten, Wei Guan was known for his filial piety, quiet temperament, and fairness. He inherited his father's marquis title and began his official career at twenty. He served in various positions, including as a regular attendant, and was known for his competence and legal expertise, judging cases based on reason.

translation:
Zhong Hui left Wei Guan to plan and discuss, and wrote on his hand that he planned to kill Hu Lie and others. He raised his hand to show Wei Guan, but Wei Guan refused, so they became suspicious of each other.
Wei Guan went to the toilet and saw Hu Lie's former entourage, and asked him to inform the three armies that Zhong Hui would rebel.
Zhong Hui forced Wei Guan to make a decision and stayed up all night, each holding a knife across his knees.
The armies outside had secretly planned to attack Zhonghui, but because Wei Guan had not come out, they did not dare to take action first.
Zhong will ask Wei Guan to comfort the troops.
Wei Guan wanted to leave, so he tried to keep Zhong Hui from changing his mind, saying: "You are the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, so you should go in person."
Zhong Hui said: You are the supervisor, you go first, and I will go later.
Wei Guan went down to the palace.
Zhong Hui regretted sending Wei Guan and asked someone to recall Wei Guan.
Wei Guan refused on the grounds of dizziness and pretended to fall to the ground.
When he got out, dozens of messengers chased him.
Wei Guan went outside, drank salt soup, and vomited violently.
Wei Guanzi was weak, so he appeared to be seriously ill.
Zhong Hui sent his cronies and doctors to visit him, but they all said that he could not get out of bed, so Zhong Hui was unscrupulous.
Waiting until sunset, the city gates were closed, and Wei Cui wrote a message to inform all the armies.
All armies responded to the righteous deed and attacked Zhonghui together at dawn.
Zhong Hui led the resistance from the left and right, and the generals defeated him. Only a few hundred people in his tent followed Zhong Hui and fled around the palace, but they were all killed.
Wei Quan deployed the generals and the morale of the army was in order.
The soldiers from Deng Ai's headquarters caught up with the broken carriage, rescued Deng Ai, and returned to Chengdu.
Wei Gan thought he was working with Zhong Hui to capture Deng Ai. He was afraid of an incident and wanted to take all the credit for killing Zhong Hui, so he sent his army guard Tian Xu to Mianzhu to attack Deng Ai at night in Sanzaoting, killing Deng Ai and his son Deng Zhong.
When Deng Ai entered Jiangyou, he was about to kill Tian Xu because he refused to join him, but later pardoned him.
When Wei Cui sent Tian Xu, he said to him: You can avenge Jiang You's humiliation.
After the matter was settled, the court discussed granting Wei Guan the title.
Wei Guan believed that the conquest of Shu was due to the strength of the generals. Generals Zhong Hui and Deng Ai were domineering and brought their own destruction. Although he used his resourcefulness, he did not take the credit for taking down the enemy flag, so he resolutely refused to accept it.
Wei Cui was granted the title of Envoy Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Guanzhong, and General of Zhenxi. Soon he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Guanzhong, and General of Zhendong. He was granted the title of Marquis of Miaoyang, and the remaining titles were given to his younger brother Wei Shi as Marquis of Kaiyangting.
In the early years of Taishi, he was transferred to the post of General Zhengshu, and his title was promoted to Duke. He was in charge of all military affairs in Qingzhou and the governor of Qingzhou. He was also awarded the title of General Zhengshu and Qingzhou Mu.
There are political achievements wherever he works.
He was awarded the title of General of Peking University, Commander-in-Chief of Youzhou's military affairs, Youzhou's governor, and Wuhuan's captain.
When you arrive at your post, please set up Pingzhou, and then take charge of Pingzhou.
At that time, Youzhou Bingzhou had Wuhuan in the east and Weiwei in the west, which was a scourge on the border.
Wei Guan alienated the two of them, causing them to become suspicious and enmity. Wu Huan surrendered and Li Wei died of sorrow and anger.
The imperial court commended Wei Guan for his achievements and gave him a son as Tinghou.
Wei Guan asked for the title of his younger brother, but he died before he could be granted the title. His son Wei Mi was granted the title of Marquis of Ting.
Wei Guan's six sons did not have titles, so they were all given to his two younger brothers. This was praised by people near and far.
He repeatedly requested to enter the court. After entering the court, Emperor Wu treated him well and soon allowed him to return to guard.
In the early years of Xianning, he was recruited to serve as Shangshu Ling and serve as a minister.
summary: During the conquest of Shu, Wei Guan supervised the armies of Deng Ai and Zhong Hui. Zhong Hui, harboring rebellious intentions, plotted to have Deng Ai kill Wei Guan. Wei Guan, aware of the danger, arrested Deng Ai at night by issuing a false imperial edict. After Zhong Hui rebelled and was killed, Wei Guan, fearing repercussions from his involvement with Zhong Hui, ordered the assassination of Deng Ai and his son. Despite his role, Wei Guan refused credit for the conquest, attributing it to the generals. He was later appointed to high military positions, including General of Zhenxi and Governor of Qingzhou, where he achieved political successes and pacified border tribes like the Wuhuan.

translation:
He is strict by nature and manages his subordinates according to the law. He regards the minister as an assistant and the minister as a subordinate official.
Wei Gan had profound knowledge and was familiar with literature and art. He was good at cursive calligraphy along with Suo Jing of Dunhuang. People at that time said that "one minister can save two masters".
Zhang Zhi was also good at cursive calligraphy in the late Han Dynasty. Commentators said that Wei Quan got the strength of Boying's calligraphy, and Suo Jing got the flesh of Boying's calligraphy.
In the early years of Taikang, he was promoted to Sikong, but his positions of Shizhong and Shangshuling remained.
His honest and concise administration was highly praised both inside and outside the court.
Emperor Wu arranged for Wei Xuan, Wei Gan's fourth son, to marry Princess Fanchang.
Wei Gan believed that he was a descendant of a Confucian disciple, and his marriage was not a prominent one. He refused outright, but the emperor did not allow it.
He also served as the prince's young master, and was awarded the title of a mansion with thousands of soldiers and hundreds of cavalry.
Because of the solar eclipse, Wei Gan and Taiwei Runan Wang Sima Liang and Situ Wei Shu all requested to give up their official positions, but the emperor refused.
Wei Guan believed that the nine-level Zhongzheng system established by Wei was a temporary system, not a long-term solution, and the ancient rural selection and recommendation system should be restored.
He and Taiwei Sima Liang and others wrote in Shangshu: In the past, sage kings respected wise men and recommended talented people for education, so that the court would be benevolent, virtuous and modest, and there would be no evil behavior outside the court.
It is indeed because the politics of the people in the village are enough to supervise each other, consult on things and evaluate opinions, and there will definitely be wise men among them. People's reputation cannot be obtained out of thin air, but should be cultivated themselves.
Therefore, when the virtuous are revered, the customs become more solemn, and when the wicked are deposed, the behavior of the people becomes more sincere.
Therefore, the selection and recommendation by the township is a beautiful example of the late king.
Since then, the approach has fallen into decline.
Wei inherited a subversive national destiny. It arose after death and war. People were displaced and moved, and there was no fixed place for detailed assessment. Therefore, the system of nine grades was established as a temporary basis for selecting talents.
When this system was first established, the rural appraisals were not limited to titles. The praise and criticism of people were enough to encourage and inspire, and there was also the spirit of rural commentary.
The middle gradually became polluted, so seniority was used to determine grades, making people in the world believe that only high positions are noble. People abandoned virtue and ignored morality, fought for small gains, and violated morals. The disadvantages are not small.
Now that the world is unified and enlightenment is beginning, we believe that all those bad laws and regulations should be eliminated and based entirely on the ancient system, judging by the place of residence, it is stipulated that from the public minister down, all officials from the place of residence will be appointed, and no more guests or people from other places will be appointed.
In this way, all neighbors from the same township are from the same town. Officials in counties and counties will appoint elders from the township. The system of Zhongzheng Jiupin will be completely abolished, so that the recommendation of talents will be determined by the township.
In this way, the subordinates will respect the superior, the people will be content with education, customs and politics will be clear, and education and laws will be successful.
People know that the education of good and bad does not lie in communication. In this way, the flashy competition will naturally stop, and people will demand themselves.
If the Nine Ranks are abolished, the ancient system should be used as the standard, allowing courtiers to recommend and appoint each other, creating a way to appoint talents, inspiring the public spirit of recommending talents, and assessing the political performance of those in office. This is indeed a good system.
summary: Wei Guan was a strict administrator and a scholar, skilled in cursive calligraphy alongside Suo Jing. He advocated for the abolition of the nine-rank system in favor of ancient rural selection, but his proposal was not implemented. He also attempted to advise Emperor Wu against appointing the simple-minded Crown Prince, but his hints were dismissed. This led to resentment from Empress Jia. Later, due to his son's marital issues and political conflicts, Wei Guan requested retirement and was granted the title of Taibao.

translation:
It's not too late to wait until you get a reply from the list before going to be punished.
Wei Cui refused to listen, so he was killed together with nine other people, including his sons Wei Heng, Wei Yue, Wei Yi and his grandson. He was seventy-two years old at the time.
Wei Heng's two sons, Wei Cao and Wei Jie, were able to escape the disaster at the time.
When Du Yu heard that Wei Guan had killed Deng Ai, he said to everyone: Boyu may not be immune to the disaster!
As a celebrity, in the position of commander-in-chief, without a good reputation, and without the right way to manage his subordinates, this is a villain taking advantage of the generosity of a gentleman. How should he bear the blame of others?
After Wei Guan heard about it, he couldn't wait to drive and went to apologize.
In the end, it was as predicted by Du Yu.
At first, Wei Guan's family was cooking, and when it fell on the ground, it turned into snails, and he died more than a year later.
Taibao Chief Secretary Liu Yao and others risked their lives to collect and bury Wei Cui's body.
At first, Wei Guan was appointed Sikong. At that time, the governor Ronghui was guilty, so Wei Guan rebuked him and expelled him.
When a disaster occurred, he followed the army to conquer Wei Guan, so his descendants were affected by the disaster.
After Sima Zhang, the king of Chu, was executed, Wei Guan's daughter wrote to the ministers: My late grandfather has not yet received his name and title, and he is no different from ordinary people. I often blame the people in the country for not speaking up for him.
Where does the blame for the mistakes of "Spring and Autumn" lie?
Feeling sad and angry, I wrote a letter to express my gratitude.
So Liu Yao and others held Huang Yao in their hands, beat the Dengwen drum, and told the emperor: When the person who falsely claimed the imperial edict arrived, the Duke received Shao Shu and said he should be dismissed. He immediately gave him a seal and ribbon. Although he had weapons, he did not move a sword or a gun. He also ordered the Duke to leave the house and ride a bicycle to obey the orders.
According to the false edict, they only removed the duke from his official position. The right army and others followed the false edict and violated the original text and killed the prime ministers and assistants. Instead of going to court, they arbitrarily captured the duke's descendants and killed them, killing nine ministers, father and son.
We saw that the edict stated that those who were deceived by the King of Chu were not the original conspirators and were given leniency.
According to the purpose of the edict, it refers to people in private houses who are driven and persecuted and kill people with sticks.
The law stipulates that those who are ordered to kill cannot be exempted from the death penalty.
What's more, if you kill heroes and harm loyal people with your own hands, although you are not an accomplice, you cannot be forgiven.
Although the chief culprit has been killed, the murderer is still there.
We are afraid that the relevant officials are not clear about the facts, or have indulged in omissions, and have not eliminated the evil, so that the enemies of the father and son will not be eliminated, and the souls of the grievances will hold a grudge for a long time and complain to the sky. The extremely painful ministers will be sad in the clear world.
Those of us who have suffered physical trauma need to complete the funeral arrangements.
He solemnly stated to the emperor that when Wei Guan was Sikong, his attendant Rong Hui was dismissed for being dishonest. He knew the number of Wei Guan's family members and the names of his descendants.
Rong Hui later transferred to the Youjun Army. That night Rong Hui shouted loudly outside the door, announcing that Shao Shu had dismissed the Duke and returned home to serve the people.
When the door opened, Rong Hui entered the middle door, read out the false edict again, took the duke's official seal, ribbon and crown, and urged the duke to leave the house.
Rong Hui registered the population and descendants of Wei Gan's family in order, escorted them with weapons, and formed a circle to the north of Dongting Road to guard them. In a short time, they were all killed.
The reason for killing the Duke's descendants is really because of honor and disgrace.
As for instigating people to rob and steal the treasury, it was Rong Hui who did it.
Examine Rong Chabo, and all evil deeds come from him.
Request to verify the authenticity and impose the punishment of clan execution on him.
The edict complied with the memorial.
Because Wei Guan's family suffered an innocent disaster, the imperial court remembered Guan's achievements in conquering Shu and made him the Duke of Junjian.
summary: After Emperor Hui ascended, Wei Guan was restored to power but clashed with Prince Sima Zhang of Chu. Empress Jia, resenting Wei Guan's integrity, falsely accused him of plotting rebellion. Sima Zhang arrested Wei Guan and his family, executing them despite his subordinates' advice to resist. Wei Guan was 72. His grandsons Wei Cao and Wei Jie escaped. Du Yu had predicted Wei Guan's downfall due to his role in Deng Ai's death. Wei Guan's son Wei Heng, a calligrapher, wrote extensively on the history of Chinese scripts, from ancient characters to seal, clerical, and cursive styles. He was also killed in the purge. Wei Guan's other son Wei Zhan served as an official and petitioned to abolish cruel interrogation methods. Wei Jie, Wei Guan's grandson, was a renowned beauty and philosopher, known for his eloquence and admired by contemporaries. He died young at 27.

translation:
Later, Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, used Lanling to expand his feudal kingdom and changed it to Jiangxia County Duke, with a settlement of 8,500 households.
Emperor Huai ascended the throne and was appointed Minister of Sanqi.
In the fifth year of Yongjia, he died at the hands of Liu Cong.
Emperor Yuan gave Wei Guan successive heirs.
Wang Jie's courtesy name is Shubao. When he was five years old, his demeanor was different from ordinary people.
Grandfather Wei Guan said: This child is different, but I am too old to see him grow up!
When he was young, he rode a sheep cart to the market. Everyone who saw him thought he was a beauty, and people went to watch him.
General Wang Ji, Wei Jie's uncle, was handsome, forthright and graceful. Every time he saw Wei Jie, he would sigh and say, "I feel ugly when I have pearls and jade around me."
He once said to others: Traveling with Wei Gecko is like having bright beads beside you, shining brightly.
When I grow up, I like to talk about mysteries.
Later, he became sick and weak, and his mother often didn't let him talk much.
On a good day, relatives and friends would sometimes ask him to say a few words, and everyone would praise him, thinking that he had touched on the subtleties of what he said.
Langxie Wang Cheng was famous and rarely praised others. Whenever he heard Wei Gecko's remarks, he would sigh and fall in love.
For this reason, people at that time said: Wei Gecko talks about Tao, and Pingzi falls over.
Wang Cheng, Wang Xuan, and Wang Ji are all famous, and they are all inferior to Wei Gecko. People say that the three sons of the Wang family are not as good as the one son of the Wei family.
Wei Jie's father-in-law Yue Guang is famous throughout the country. Commentators believe that his father-in-law is as clear as ice and his son-in-law is as smooth as jade.
The recruitment order came many times, but he never showed up.
A long time later, Taifu Ren Xihe offered wine and washed the prince's horse.
Wei Duo served as Sanqi Shilang and served Emperor Huai in the palace.
Wei Gecko planned to move to the south because of the chaos in the world.
Mother said: I can't leave Zhongbao behind.
Wei Jie explained the truth thoroughly, and for the sake of the family plan, my mother agreed to him with tears.
Before leaving, Wei Gecko said to his brother: The morality of respecting father, teacher and king is what people value.
Now it can be said that I am dedicated to serving the king, and my brother encourages himself.
So he escorted his mother to Jiangxia.
Wei Gecko's wife died first.
When Shan Jian, the general who conquered the south, saw Wei Chan, he admired him very much.
The mountain slips say: In the past, Dai Shuluan only married virtuous men, regardless of their status, not to mention that the Wei family was from a powerful and famous family!
So she married her daughter to him.
Then enter Yuzhang. At that time, the general Wang Dun was guarding Yuzhang, and the chief minister Xie Wan had always respected Wei Gecko before. He was very happy to meet him and talked with him for a whole day.
Wang Dun said to Xie Wan: In the past, Wang Fusi's speech in China and North Korea was like the sound of gold, and this person's speech in Jiangbiao was like the vibration of jade. His subtle speech was interrupted and continued.
Unexpectedly, in the last years of Yongjia, I heard Zhengshi's voice again. If Uncle He Ping was still here, he would definitely fall in love.
Wei Jie often believes that no one is perfect and can be forgiven; if the offense is not intentional, it can be dealt with according to reason, so he will never see his happy and angry face throughout his life.
Because Wang Dun was bold and unsociable, he liked to live among others, and he was probably not a loyal minister of the country. He took concrete and planned to build Ye.
People in the capital heard about the appearance of Basket Gecko, and those who watched him crowded into a wall.
Wei Jie's illness worsened due to overwork. He died in the sixth year of Yongjia at the age of twenty-seven. People at the time said that Wei Jie was expected to die.
Buried in Nanchang.
Xie Wan cried and he was very sad. Someone asked him: Why are you so sad?
The answer is: The pillars are broken, so I am sad.
In Xianhe, he was buried in Jiangning.
Prime Minister Wang Dao said: Wei Xima should indeed be reburied.
This person is a romantic and famous person who is looked up to by people from all over the world. He can prepare a small sacrifice to encourage his old friends.
Later, Liu Hui and Xie Shang discussed Chinese and Korean people together. Someone asked: Can Du Yi be compared with Wei Xima?
Xie Shang said: How can they be compared? The gap between them can accommodate several people.
Liu Hui added: Du You is pure in appearance, and Shu Ben is pure in spirit.
This is how Wei Gecko is highly regarded by knowledgeable people.
At that time, among the celebrities of ZTE, Wang Chenghe and Wei Jie were the number one at that time.
Wei Heng's younger brother Wei Zhan, named Daoshu, served successively as Shangshu Lang and Nanyang Prefect.
During the Yongjia period, he served as the governor of Jiangzhou and was gradually promoted to Dali, King of Jin Dynasty.
There are provisions in the Shao book about torture of sons to prove their father's sins, or whipping parents to ask where their sons are. Wei Zhan thought that this might harm the political religion, so he petitioned to abolish it.
During the Zhongxing Dynasty, he was appointed Tingwei. Shangshu said that corporal punishment should be restored. The matter was recorded in the book "Criminal Law Chronicles".
After his death, he was given posthumously to Dr. Guanglu.
Zhang Hua, courtesy name Maoxian, was born in Fangcheng, Fanyang.
His father, Zhang Ping, was the governor of Yuyang County in Wei.
When Zhang Hua was young, he was lonely and poor, tending sheep by himself. Lu Qin from the same county discovered him and valued him.
Liu Fang, a fellow countryman, also valued his talent and married his daughter to him.
Zhang Hua's studies are profound and extensive, his vocabulary is gorgeous, he is smart and erudite, and there is no book like Yuanwei Fanggui that he does not read carefully.
When he was young, he cultivated himself carefully and acted according to etiquette.
summary: Zhang Hua, courtesy name Maoxian, was from Fangcheng. Orphaned and poor, he herded sheep but was recognized for his talent. He was learned and wrote the "Ode to the Quail," which gained him fame. He served as a key advisor to Emperor Wu, supporting the conquest of Wu and overseeing logistics. After Wu's fall, he was rewarded but later fell out of favor due to his support for Prince Sima You. He was sent to Youzhou, where he pacified border tribes and received tribute from distant states. Zhang Hua's son Zhang Yi was also killed. His grandson Zhang Yu survived. Liu Bian, a loyal official, warned Zhang Hua of Empress Jia's plots but was not heeded. He later died by poison to avoid execution. The text concludes with a lament for Wei Guan and Zhang Hua, praising their loyalty but noting their tragic ends in a time of chaos.

translation:
King Sima Zhang of Chu accepted a secret edict to kill Sima Liang, King of Runan, and Guan, the chief minister. The internal and external armies were in chaos, and the court was in panic and could do nothing.
Zhang Hua told the emperor: Sima Zhang forged an edict and killed the second prince without permission. In a hurry, the soldiers thought it was the will of the country and followed him.
Now we can send people to carry Yuyu banners to relieve the peripheral troops from alerting them. Logically, they will follow the wind.
The emperor obeyed him, and Chu King Sima Zhang's rebellion failed.
When Sima Zhang was killed, Qiang Jie was awarded the title of Doctor Youguanglu, Kaifu Yitong Sansi, Shizhong, Zhongshujian, with a gold seal and purple ribbon because he was the first to make a plan.
Resolutely refuse to open the government.
Jia Mi conspired with the queen and believed that Zhang Hua was from a commoner family, elegant and strategic, and was not suspected of intimidating the emperor when he advanced, but would be favored by the public when he retreated. He planned to rely on him to govern the court and consult on political affairs.
Undecided, he went to ask Pei Yuan. Pei Yuan had always respected Zhang Hua and fully agreed with this matter.
Zhang Hua then tried his best to help and correct mistakes. Although the fatuous emperor was tyrannizing the queen, the country was stable. This was Zhang Hua's credit.
Zhang Hua was afraid that the queen's family would become powerful, so he wrote "Proverbs for Women's History" as a satire.
Although Empress Jia was fierce and jealous, she knew how to respect Chui Long.
After a period of time, people discussed Cheng Chu's outstanding achievements and made him the Duke of Zhuangwu.
Zhang Hua gave in more than ten times, and the emperor issued an edict to urge him to enlighten him, and then he accepted it.
A few years later, he replaced Sima Huang, the king of Xiapi, as Sikong and concurrently as the author.
When Empress Jia planned to depose the prince, Zuo Wei led Liu Bian, who was trusted by the prince. Liu Bian would definitely attend every gathering and banquet.
The prince resented Buying Pride when he saw him many times, and it showed in his words and expressions, and Buying was not convinced.
Liu Bian asked Zhang Ge about Empress Jia's plan, Qiang Long said, "I haven't heard of it."
Suzhuang said: Suzhuang was born in poverty. He was promoted from a small official in Xuchang to his current status.
The scholar was grateful to his confidant, so he told me everything, but the gentleman had doubts about me!
Zhang Hua said: If there is something like you said, what do you want to do?
Liu Bian said: The heroes of the East Palace cannot be deployed clearly, and there are ten thousand elite soldiers in the four ranks.
The Duke is in the important position of presiding over the state affairs. If he gets the order from the Duke and the crown prince enters the court and serves as the minister, after the purchase of Jinyong City is abolished, the power of the two Huangmen will be enough.
Zhang Hua said: Now that the emperor has ascended the throne, the prince is the emperor's son. I did not accept the order and suddenly participated in such a thing. I have no regard for the emperor and my father, and I show my unfilial piety to the world.
Even if they succeed, they still cannot be exempted from the crime. What's more, the dynasty is full of powerful officials and nobles, and the authority is not on one side. How can this be stable?
When the emperor gathered the ministers in Shiqian Hall and showed the prince's handwriting to the ministers, no one dared to speak.
summary: Recalled to court, Zhang Hua became a central figure under Emperor Hui, stabilizing the government despite Empress Jia's tyranny. He opposed the deposition of the crown prince, arguing for caution, but was overruled. He also thwarted a coup by Prince Sima Zhang of Chu. However, his refusal to join Prince Sima Lun of Zhao's rebellion led to his arrest and execution at 69, along with his family. He was known for his vast knowledge, collecting rare books, and his expertise in astronomy and strange phenomena, such as identifying dragon meat and predicting chaos from a bird feather.

translation:
Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was born in Renchengfan.
His father died when he was young and he was adopted by his maternal grandfather's Ning family.
When Mr. Ning built a house, the person who looked at the feng shui of the house said: "A noble nephew will be born."
Because her grandson Wei was young and smart, my grandmother thought that he had followed the Feng Shui master's words.
Wei Shu said: I should prove the auspiciousness of this house for my grandfather's family.
It took a long time before I moved to another place.
He is eight feet two inches tall, has a beautiful body and a majestic appearance, and can drink more than a stone of wine. However, he is slow and simple, and is not valued by the villagers.
Wei Heng, the official uncle of the hall, was well-known in the world but didn't know him well. He asked him to guard the water-powered rice pounding facility. He often sighed and said: "Wei Shu can be the head of a hundred households, so I will be satisfied!"
Wei Shu didn't take this to heart either.
Don't pay attention to ordinary people's moral integrity, don't do things that are reserved and arrogant, and always want to be tolerant in order to respect people. Never reveal the shortcomings of others.
By nature, he likes to ride horses and shoot arrows. He wears reed clothes and goes into the mountains and rivers to fish and hunt.
Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Wei Shu: You will eventually become prime minister, but now you cannot protect your wife and children from hunger and cold. I should help you make a living.
He often offered relief to Wei Shu for his shortcomings, but Wei Shu accepted it without refusing.
Wei Shu once went to Yewang. The wife of the owner of the house was giving birth to a baby at night. After a while, he heard the sound of carriages and horses. The people in the carriages asked each other: "Is it a boy or a girl?"
Answered: Boy, write it down, died by a sharp weapon at the age of fifteen.
Asked again: Who is sleeping in the room?
He replied: Wei Gong Wei Shu.
Fifteen years later, he went to the house owner again and asked where his son was. He was told that he died because he was injured by an ax while cutting mulberry branches.
Wei Shu himself knew that he would become a public servant.
When he was in his forties, the county's planner visited Xiaolian.
The clan believed that Wei Zhong had no academic skills and advised him not to take the exam as this would show his noble character.
Wei Shu said: If I go to the exam and fail, the responsibility lies with me. How can I take the honor of not going to the exam and stealing the false name of Gao Jie as my own glory?
So he studied his own homework and studied a "Sutra" for a hundred days, so he answered the policy questions and passed the exam.
He was granted the title of Chief of Mianchi, moved to the post of Jun Yi Ling, and entered the court as Shangshu Lang.
At that time, Lang officials were selected and eliminated, and those who were incompetent were dismissed.
Wei Shu said: I am the one who should be eliminated.
Roll up the quilt and leave.
Those among his colleagues who had never spoken highly felt ashamed, while those who discussed the matter praised Wei Shu.
After gradually moving to the post of general Zhong Yu, Zhong Yu often shot arrows with his subordinates, and Wei Shu often planned for him.
Later, when he encountered a shortage of friends, he asked Wei Shu to make up the number.
Zhong Yu didn't know Wei Shu was good at archery at first.
Wei Shu's shooting posture was elegant and he never failed to hit the mark. Everyone in the audience was amazed. No one could compare with him.
Zhong Yu sighed and apologized: I didn't give full play to your talent. With such a good archery skill, shouldn't it be limited to archery?
summary: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was born in Renchengfan. Orphaned young, he was raised by his maternal grandfather’s Ning family. A feng shui master predicted a noble nephew would be born, and Wei Shu’s intelligence led his grandmother to believe he fulfilled this prophecy. Tall and majestic, he was slow and simple, not valued by villagers. His uncle Wei Heng underestimated him, but Wei Shu remained unbothered. He enjoyed riding, archery, and hunting. Wang Yi of Taiyuan predicted he would become prime minister and supported him. Wei Shu once witnessed a prophecy about a boy who died at fifteen from an ax wound, which later came true. At forty, he studied for a hundred days, passed exams, and became Chief of Mianchi. He later served as Shangshu Lang, where he voluntarily resigned when incompetent officials were dismissed. He excelled in archery, surprising his superior Zhong Yu. As Prime Minister’s aide, he planned wisely on major issues. Emperor Wen valued him, and he governed Yiyang and Rongyang with a good reputation. He served as governor of Jizhou for three years, known for simplicity and benevolence. Emperor Wu rewarded him for honesty. He married three times, all wives predeceased him. In the Taikang era, he advocated for the Fengshan ceremony but was refused. He served as Zuopushe and managed the official department, proposing reforms for imperial marriage gifts. He became Situ and was known for distributing his salary to relatives, leaving no surplus. He appointed Zhou Zhen, who had been avoided due to a superstitious nickname, without disaster. He repeatedly resigned due to illness, eventually being allowed to retire as Juyangzi with honors. He died at eighty-two, posthumously named Kang. His son Wei Hun died young, and his great-nephew Wei Huang succeeded him.

translation:
When Emperor Jing was assisting the government, he appointed Kuitai as the general to serve as a lieutenant. When Li Xi arrived, he was introduced. Emperor Jing said to Li Xi: In the past, my father-in-law recruited you and you didn't agree. Now that I have appointed you, you are here. Why?
Li Xi replied: Your ancestors treated me with courtesy, and I was able to decide whether to enter an official position or retire according to the courtesy.
Ming Gong uses the law to restrain me, and I am afraid of the law.
Emperor Jing thought highly of him.
He was transferred to Sima, and soon he became the right chief historian.
Following the expedition against Qiu Jian, he returned to the imperial court and moved to the post of censor Zhongcheng.
The official is upright and not afraid of violence and power, and all the officials are shocked by this.
Sun Pu, a native of Le'an, was recommended. He was also famous for his morality. People at the time praised him for his ability to identify talents.
Soon he was moved to the post of Grand Sima, but was dismissed due to official duties.
Sima Bo was appointed as the general of Ningbei and guarded Ye, with Li Fu as the military commander.
Soon after, Li Cong was appointed as the governor of Liangzhou, and he was also appointed as General Yangwei, Jiajie, and Protector of Qiang. He stabilized China and resisted the barbarians, which was a very prestigious achievement.
When the Qiang people invaded the frontier, Li Fu took advantage of the opportunity without having time to report, so he sent troops to penetrate deeply at the right time. He won a great victory and was not condemned because of his great achievements. People at the time compared him to Dun Kuishi and Gan Yanshou of the Han Dynasty.
So he asked to go back to Beijing and agreed to him.
After living at home for more than a month, he became the governor of Jizhou and was gradually promoted to the rank of Sili Xiaowei.
When the Wei Emperor surrendered to the Jin Dynasty, Li Cuo assumed the position of Situ as his own official, and served as Taiwei Zheng Chong's deputy to hold the policy document.
In the early years of Taishi, he was granted the title of Marquis of Qi.
Li Xishangshu said: The former Li Jinling Liu You, the former Shan Tao, the Zhongshan King Sima Mu, and the late Shangshu Pushe Wu Bei each occupied the public rice fields at three o'clock, and requested that Shan Tao, Sima Mu and others be removed from their official positions.
Wu Ye is already dead, so I request that his nickname be derogated.
Shao Shu said: The world takes the law as the criterion and does not shun the royal family and nobles. It can only be implemented after the law. How can I indulge in evil and wasteful things!
However, the investigation was all done by Liu You, who violated and exploited the people and confused the court officials.
The traitor actually dared to do such a thing, so Liu You was tortured to punish the evil traitor.
If Shan Tao and others make no more mistakes, they will no longer be held accountable.
The Book of Changes says that kings and ministers are loyal because they have no selfish motives.
Nowadays, Li Fu persists in his ambition to serve the public affairs and acts in accordance with his responsibilities. He can be said to be the director of the country.
Emperor Guangwu said that the emperor's relatives restrained themselves to avoid Erbao. Is this the case?
All officials are warned to treat their duties with caution. The grace of leniency and forgiveness will not be encountered many times.
Li Yi served as a minister for two generations, and he was praised both inside and outside the court.
Dismissed from office due to official duties.
summary: Li Xi, courtesy name Jihe, was from Shangdang Tongtian. He had good conduct, studied widely, and refused recruitment by Guan Ning and others. Emperor Xuan summoned him, but he declined due to his mother’s illness. He later served as a special chariot in Bingzhou, advising Bi Gui against improper conduct. Emperor Jing appointed him as a lieutenant; when asked why he accepted, Li Xi replied he feared the law. He became censor Zhongcheng, feared for his uprightness. He recommended Sun Pu, praised for identifying talent. He was dismissed as Grand Sima but later served as governor of Liangzhou, stabilizing the region and defeating Qiang invaders without prior approval, compared to Han generals. He returned to Beijing, then governed Jizhou and became Sili Xiaowei. When Wei surrendered to Jin, he assisted in ceremonies. He was made Marquis of Qi and accused officials of occupying public rice fields, leading to punishment for Liu You. He served as crown prince’s tutor, teaching diligently. He resigned due to old age, receiving honors. He advocated attacking Liangzhou invaders but was overruled, leading to Liangzhou’s destruction. He was honest and frugal, sharing with relatives. He died, posthumously named Taibao. His son Li Zan succeeded him.

translation:
That year, the crown prince was established and Li Fan was appointed crown prince and tutor.
Since Emperor Wei Ming, Shu Palace has been empty for a long time, the system is desolate and defective, and the officials are incomplete. There are no official positions such as Zhan Shi, Zuo Sui, Shuzi, Zhong Sheren, etc., only Wei Sui is set up to be in charge of the army, and the Taifu and Shaofu jointly act as agents.
Li Yi has been in office for many years, teaching Daoyi and planning with all his heart.
He was moved to the post of Minister Pushe, and was awarded the title of Tejin and Guanglu. He abdicated due to old age.
Shao Shu said: Dr. Guanglu, Tejin Li Yi, relied on virtue to promote morality, and should be an official in Taisi to assist the Guangda royal family. However, he resigned from his official position because of his old age.
Although leisurely and inactive can rest your mind, how can you not be moved by your humility and fame?
Following the title of Guanglu, he was instead awarded fake gold and purple, appointed ten officers and cavalry, and was given five hundred thousand in money. The salary and rewards were graded and etiquette. They were the same as those of the three divisions. A wooden gate with antlers was set up in front of the door.
At the beginning, when Li Gu was serving as Pushe, enemies from Liangzhou invaded the border, and Li Yi advocated raising troops to attack them.
Imperial officials believed that it was not easy to send troops and that the enemy was not enough to cause disaster, so they ultimately refused to listen to Li's wishes.
Later, the enemy turned out to be extremely reckless and Liangzhou was destroyed. The court deeply regretted it.
Because Li Fan was honest, simple and frugal, he was given a hundred pieces of silk.
When Sima You, the king of Qi, went out to guard, Li De was very sincere in admonishing Jing.
Since Li Yi became an official, although he was not unusually clean, his family had no savings and he even shared food and clothing with his relatives and friends. He never used his status as a court official for personal gain.
After his death, he gave posthumous gifts to the Taibao, and the title of Mi was established.
He was succeeded by his son Li Zan.
The youngest son Li Jian, also known as Zhongyue, served successively as General Zuo Jinu and Tunqi Colonel.
Li Jian's son, Li Hong, also known as Shiyan, had an upright character when he was young. In the last years of Yongjia, he served successively as the minister of Huangmen and the regular minister of Sanqi.
Liu Zizhen was born in Gaotang, Pingyuan.
He is a descendant of Liu Shou, King Hui of Jibei in the Han Dynasty. His father, Liu Guang, was Kuqiu Ling.
Liu Yi was poor when he was young and relied on selling cow clothes to support himself.
However, he is eager to learn, his hands are wrapped with ropes, and he is reciting poems and books. He is knowledgeable about ancient and modern times.
His own moral character is clean and his conduct is flawless.
The county officials visited Xiaolian, and the prefectures recommended scholars, but they didn't go.
He entered Luoyang as an accounting official, was transferred to Yin Cheng of Henan, and was transferred to Shangshu Lang and Ting Weizheng.
Later, he successively served as a minister of official affairs, participated in the military affairs of Emperor Wen's prime minister, and was named Xunyangzi.
When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai were attacking Shu, a guest asked Liu Gong: Can these two generals pacify Shu?
Liu Gong said: We will definitely defeat Shu, but we will not be able to come back.
When the guest asked the reason, he smiled and said nothing, and the outcome was just as Liu Xi said.
Liu Ku's foresight is similar to this.
Because there is too much enterprising and competition in the world, and the moral character of integrity and humility is defective, he wrote "On Chong Rang Lun" to correct the world's customs.
summary: Liu Yi, courtesy name Zizhen, was from Gaotang, Pingyuan. Poor in youth, he sold cow clothes but studied diligently. He was recommended as Xiaolian but refused. He served as Shangshu Lang and Tingweizheng. He predicted Zhong Hui and Deng Ai would conquer Shu but not return, which came true. He wrote “On Chong Rang Lun” advocating humility to correct worldly competition. He argued that humility reveals talent, reduces slander, and stabilizes governance. He criticized the lack of humility in official appointments, leading to mediocrity and corruption. He proposed that officials should recommend the worthy, with selection based on collective recommendations rather than seniority. He served as Taichang and Shangshu. His son Liu Xia’s bribery led to his dismissal. He later served as crown prince’s mentor and Taibao. He resigned at ninety-one, dying soon after. He was frugal, once mistaking Shi Chong’s luxurious toilet for a bedroom. He studied the “Three Biographies” and wrote “Spring and Autumn Regulations.” His sons Liu Ji and Liu Xia were noted, with Liu Xia disgraced for corruption.

translation:
At that time, King Zhao Sima Lun usurped power and rebelled. During that time, Gao Guang stayed true to the right path and maintained his integrity.
After Sima Lun was sentenced to death, King Sima Tong of Qi assisted in the government affairs. He also appointed Gao Guang as Tingwei, moved to Shangshu, and was appointed as Fengche Duwei.
Later, he followed the emperor to defeat Sima Ying, the king of Chengdu, and was granted the title of Duke of Yanling County, granting 1,800 households.
At that time, the imperial court praised Gao Guang for being good at using law, so he served as a legal official many times.
Emperor Hui was forced by Zhang Fang to go to Chang'an. The ministers of the court were scattered and had no followers. Only Gao Guang served the emperor on his journey westward.
He was moved to the post of Minister Zuopushe and appointed as the regular attendant of Sanqi.
Gao Guang's elder brother Gao Dan was appointed by Shangguan Si and others, and served as governor of Tu and Yu prefectures.
His direct sexual indulgence has no rules, but his decisiveness and firmness are beyond ordinary people, which is different from Gao Guang's character.
Gao Dan often said that Zhi Guang was stuck in small details and always bullied him. Gao Guang treated Gao Dan more respectfully.
After the emperor returned to the stolen house, the emperor's younger brother had just been established. He carefully selected assistant talents, appointed Gao Guang as the young master, and appointed him as the doctor Guanglu. The position of permanent attendant remained the same.
When Emperor Huai came to the throne, he was awarded the gold medal and purple ribbon by Dr. Guanglu, and he was highly praised together with Fu Zhi.
Soon he was appointed minister, and his original official position remained.
He died of illness and was given posthumously to Sikong and Shizhong.
When Sero was overthrown, he was not given the title of Mi.
Zitao, whose courtesy name is Ziyuan, is indulgent and indiscreet.
When Zhili was appointed as Tingwei, Tao accepted bribes. The relevant officials reported this matter, but Gao Guang did not know about it.
Although people at the time criticized Gao Guang for not being able to guard against his son, because he was always attentive, he did not bother Gao Guang by doing anything.
At first, Gao Guang stayed in the government office in Chang'an and asked Gao Tao to serve as the right guard general.
Gao Tao colluded with the villains in the residence of the emperor and the ministers. When Gao Guang died, he was still in mourning and kept coming and going.
At that time, Sima Yue, King of Shuhai, assisted in government affairs and did not meet the emperor.
Gao Tao knew that people were complaining, so he secretly planned a crusade against Sima Yue with Taifu Jiang Ji, Jingzhao Du Ao and others. When the incident was revealed, he was killed.
Shi Chen said: It is better for people with lower talents to compete and have literary talents, and for people with medium talents to be quiet and simple.
Wei Shu and Liu Shi had the essence of their thinking. If they became officials, they would achieve great things.
Ji Su asked questions sincerely and answered truthfully, acting with dignity as an official.
Could it be that the "greedy and scumbag" in the poem is Liu Xia?
Praise said: Wei Shu's words are not arrogant, and Li Fu dares to go against the prince.
Zizhen and Xuanmao have noble aspirations and are difficult to bully.
Able to promote loyalty and good deeds, and to promote retreat.
The bright coral vessel shines like a jade rope star.
summary: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuan Mao, was from Chenliu. He knew law from youth, serving as Shangshu Lang and governor of Youzhou and Yingchuan. He was appointed Huangsha Yushi for legal expertise. During Sima Lun’s rebellion, he stayed loyal. He served as Tingwei and Shangshu, later following Emperor Hui to Chang'an when others fled. He became Zuopushe and young master. He died of illness, posthumously named Sikong. His son Gao Tao was corrupt and plotted against Sima Yue, leading to his execution. The historian praised Wei Shu and Liu Yi for their wisdom, Li Xi for his boldness, and Gao Guang for his integrity, noting Liu Xia’s corruption as a flaw.

translation:
Fu Xuan, whose courtesy name was Xiu Yi, was from Niyang in the north.
His grandfather Fu Xie was the prefect of Hanyang in the Han Dynasty.
His father, Fu Qian, was the governor of Fufeng in the Wei state.
Fu Xuan was lonely and poor when he was young. He was erudite, good at writing articles, and knew the rhythm of music.
He has a strong and upright character and cannot tolerate the shortcomings of others.
He was appointed as a planner in the county, and he was recommended as Xiaolian twice. He was also recruited by the Taiwei, but he did not take up the post.
He took the state examination and passed the scholar examination, and was appointed as a doctor. Due to their reputation at that time, he and Donghai Mushi were selected as writers and compiled Wei books.
Later, he learned about the military affairs of Anton and Weijun. He was transferred to the county magistrate of Wen County and promoted to the prefect of Hongnong. In charge of the post of captain of Diannong School.
He was a competent official, wrote many petitions and made many corrections.
After the establishment of the fifth-grade system, he was granted the title of Baron Quail.
When Emperor Wu Sima Yan was the king of Jin Dynasty, he appointed him as a regular attendant of Sanqi.
When Emperor Wu succeeded to the throne, he was promoted to viscount and promoted to Prince Consort and Commander-in-Chief.
As soon as Emperor Wu came to the throne, he widely adopted outspoken speech and opened up a way of speaking without taboos. Fu Xuan and Huangfu Tao, the regular servant of Sanqi, jointly took charge of the post of admonishment officer.
Fu Xuan Shangshu said: I have heard that the former king came to the world, proclaimed the great teachings, and increased etiquette, righteousness, and moral integrity. The teachings flourished in the court, public opinions became popular below, and everyone followed them together, and everyone had a heart of benevolence and righteousness.
The perished Qin Dynasty destroyed the laws of the ancestors and ruled with harsh laws, and the heart of benevolence and righteousness declined.
In modern times, Emperor Wu of the Wei Dynasty Cao Cao liked magic, so the world valued punishments; Emperor Wen of the Wei Dynasty Cao Pi admired those who knew the truth, so the world despised keeping integrity.
From then on, the imperial court was unable to govern, so empty, useless, and uninhibited discussions flooded the government and the public, so that there was no longer any fair discussion in the world, and the ills of the Qin Dynasty's demise recurred today.
His Majesty's morality is supreme, the dynasty has risen, he has inherited the throne, he has carried forward the teachings of Yao and Shun, he has opened up the path of righteous advice, he has experienced the frugality of Xia and Yu, and after considering the laws and essays of the Shang and Zhou dynasties, I can only sigh, what else am I going to say!
It's just that I didn't recommend courteous ministers with lofty ideals to uphold moral integrity; I didn't remove hypocritical and despicable villains to punish disrespectful ministers, so I still dare to say something.
The edict replied: Recommending ministers with high aspirations and etiquette is an especially important thing today.
So Fu Xuan was asked to draft an edict and present it to him.
Fu Xuan wrote again:
I heard that Shun recommended five ministers and governed without doing anything. This was because he had found the essentials in employing people.
Because there are so many official positions in the world, it is necessary to examine and find the right person.
summary: Fu Xuan, courtesy name Xiu Yi, was from Niyang in the north. His grandfather Fu Xie was a Han prefect, and his father Fu Qian was a Wei governor. Orphaned and poor in youth, Fu Xuan was erudite, skilled in writing, and knowledgeable in music. He had a strong, upright character and could not tolerate others' faults. He was appointed as a county planner, recommended as Xiaolian twice, and recruited by the Taiwei, but did not take the post. He passed the scholar examination, became a doctor, and was selected with Donghai Mushi to compile Wei books. He later held various military and civil posts, including prefect of Hongnong and captain of Diannong School, and was known for his competent governance and many petitions. After the fifth-grade system was established, he was granted the title of Baron Quail. Under Emperor Wu of Jin, he was promoted to viscount and Prince Consort and Commander-in-Chief.

translation:
If you don't find the right person, you will waste a lot of money in one day, not to mention the accumulated time?
"Shangshu Gao Tao Mo" said: Do not leave hundreds of officials vacant, which means that the positions cannot be abandoned for a long time.
Those who have been ill for a hundred days and have not recovered should be allowed to leave their jobs and be given generous courtesy and salary until they recover.
The ministers will not give up their positions in the government, and the country will not be burdened by idle officials. This is the top priority of the king's government.
I heard that the previous emperors managed state affairs according to the division of labor between scholars, farmers, industry and commerce. Each had its own industry and different affairs.
For the children of scholars and above, the Imperial Academy was established for them to educate them, sage teachers were selected to teach them, and they were appointed according to their respective talents.
Agriculture must ensure a bumper harvest, industry must provide sufficient equipment, and merchants must ensure the circulation of goods.
Therefore, the world is huge and there are many people, and no one is empty-handed.
The division of labor is so thorough and complete.
However, there was no fixed division of labor in the Han Dynasty and the Wei Dynasty. The children of hundreds of officials did not learn the Five Classics and Six Arts but engaged in socializing and enjoyed the imperial salary before they knew how to do things. Agricultural and industrial industries were mostly abandoned, and some left their business in pursuit of huge profits. They were in the Imperial Academy in vain, but they did not hear the teachings of the previous kings.
Now that Shengming's politics has begun, the mistakes of the Han and Wei dynasties have not changed. There are many informal officials but no schools. There are many people who are not doing their jobs but few people who are engaged in agriculture. Industrial utensils are not suitable for use.
I think it is urgent to formulate a system to uniformly plan how many people in the world will be scholars, so that they can serve as various officials; how many people will be farmers, so that they can have a year's worth of grain reserves after working for three years; how many people will be workers, so that all kinds of utensils are sufficient; how many people will be engaged in business, so that they can circulate goods.
Respecting Confucianism and Taoism and advocating academics, agriculture as the most noble, and commerce as the lowest, these are all important matters in national affairs.
Previously, Huangfu Tao made a memorial requesting that the appointment of casual officials should be reviewed and let them personally cultivate the land so that the world could enjoy the benefits of sufficient food.
Xia Yu Houji personally engaged in farming, and his blessings were passed down to later generations. Therefore, the "Mingtang" and "Yueling" chapters in the "Book of Rites" record the system of the emperor's land registration.
Yi Yin was a famous official in ancient times and farmed in Youxin; Yan Ying was a senior official in Qi State who also went to the seaside to farm in order to avoid the disaster of Duke Zhuang of Qi.
In the past, sage emperors and capable men were all engaged in agricultural production.
The emperor conferred official positions, and if those officials who were superfluous, idle and had nothing to do were urged to study, they should be allowed to farm. There was no reason to let them sit back and eat the people's food.
Nowadays, there are many civil and military officials, but there are still more who do not serve in their posts. In addition, they serve as soldiers and cannot grow crops, and they are half the number of farmers. In this way, the number of people sitting facing south and receiving salary is three times that of the previous dynasty.
Let the idle and redundant officials work on the farm and collect their taxes, and private individuals will also gain substantial benefits, and the world will not be short of food.
Every family has enough food. A son should be filial, a father should be loving, an elder brother should be friendly, and a younger brother should be filial.
If the world has enough food and clothing, then the teachings of benevolence and righteousness will be implemented without orders.
The key to government is to set up officials according to the total number of people, divide labor until people are assigned their duties, and the division of labor between scholars, farmers, industry and commerce cannot be abandoned at all times.
summary: As an admonishment officer, Fu Xuan submitted a memorial criticizing the decline of benevolence and righteousness since the Qin and Wei dynasties, praising Emperor Wu's virtue, and urging the recommendation of courteous ministers and removal of hypocritical ones. The emperor agreed and asked him to draft an edict. Fu Xuan further wrote on the importance of proper official appointments, advocating for long-term positions and the division of labor among scholars, farmers, workers, and merchants. He stressed the need for a system to plan the number of people in each class, emphasizing agriculture and Confucian education. He also proposed that idle officials should farm, and that the government should evaluate officials every three years, with promotions after nine years. The emperor praised his sincerity and ordered further study of his proposals.

translation:
The fifth thing is: I think the Hu Yi tribe has a human face and a beast heart. They are not the same as the Chinese. The Xianbei tribe is the most powerful.
At the beginning, Deng Ai only wanted to obtain temporary benefits and did not consider the future troubles. He caused tens of thousands of Xianbei people to live scattered among the people, which would inevitably lead to disaster.
Hu Lie, the governor of Qinzhou, has always been kind to the west. Now that Hu Lie has gone, although all kinds of barbarians have stopped causing trouble and will be eliminated, their beastly hearts cannot be kept alive, and long-term peace and stability may not be possible.
If there are signs of unrest in the future, Hu Lie's strategy can subdue them.
I am just worried that the Hulu will flee eastward to Anding and westward to Wuwei just after being trapped by the conquest. They will appear to surrender, but they will still riot when they can.
These two counties are not under the control of Hu Lie, and the vicious Hu people have caves and caves to buffer and roam, so there is no way to prevent future disasters.
Another county should be established in Gaopingchuan, so that the captain of Anxizhou can recruit people who are willing to migrate, supplement them with a large number of people exempted from corvee, open up the northbound road, and gradually enrich the border.
It is best to consider that these two counties and the established counties belong to Qinzhou, so that Hu Lie can take charge of border affairs.
The edict said: "To obtain the things that should be done as stated in the report, including the gains and losses of farming, the rise and fall of water conservancy officials, as well as the security of the border to resist the barbarians and the severity of the political affairs, are described in detail and complete. This is indeed a fundamental matter of governing the country and an urgent task today."
The discussion is correct. Knowing that you are loyal to the royal family, you should think more broadly about what should be done and tell me the situation.
In the fifth year of Taishi's reign, he was appointed as a servant.
At that time, the grain harvest had not been harvested for several years, and the Western Qiang and Hu people were harassing the border. The emperor issued an edict for the ministers to discuss.
Fu Xuan responded to the emperor's questions and stated his reasons sincerely and straightforwardly. Although he did not implement everything, he was often tolerated.
Transferred to the post of Sili Xiaowei.
Queen Xian passed away in Hongxun Palace, and a place of mourning was set up.
According to the old system, the minister should sit outside Duanmen, sitting alone above the other ministers.
Entering the palace, according to the official rank of this product, under the ministers, sit in order and sit at the same table with others.
The visitors believed that Hongxun Palace was within the palace, and placed Fu Xuan's position under the position of Qing.
Fu Xuan was furious and shouted at the visitors.
The visitor pretended that it was arranged by the Minister, and Fu Xuan cursed the Minister in front of all the officials and left the table.
Yu Chun, the imperial censor, reported to Fu Xuan how disrespectful he was, but Fu Xuan's report was inconsistent with the facts, so he was dismissed from office.
However, Fu Xuan was by nature severe and impatient, and could not be tolerant when things happened. Every time there was a memorial to report, or when it was late, he would hold the memorial in his hand, straighten his crown and belt, and restlessly not sleep, but sit and wait for dawn.
As a result, those princes and nobles without official positions were afraid to surrender, and the minister suddenly gained prestige.
