summary: In the fourth year of Taishi, Fu Xuan became Yushi Zhongcheng. During floods and droughts, he submitted five proposals: adjusting the share of harvest for soldiers using government cattle; enforcing Han-era laws to punish negligent officials; improving water conservancy by dividing responsibilities; reforming land tax to rest labor; and establishing a new county in Gaopingchuan to manage the Xianbei tribe and prevent border unrest. The emperor approved these as fundamental to governance. In the fifth year of Taishi, Fu Xuan became a servant. Despite grain shortages and border troubles, his sincere advice was often tolerated. He later became Sili Xiaowei, but was dismissed after a dispute over seating at a mourning ceremony. He died at home at age sixty-two, posthumously titled Gang.

translation:
Soon he died at home at the age of sixty-two. His posthumous title was Gang.
Fu Xuan took refuge in Hanoi when he was young and concentrated on reading. Although he became rich and powerful, his writings were not neglected.
He wrote a book that commented on the three religions and nine streams of governing the country and the three historical events, and judged the pros and cons, each with regulations. The book is called "Fu Zi", which is divided into three chapters: internal, external and middle. It has four parts and six records, with a total of 140 poems and hundreds of thousands of words. It has been popular in the world together with more than 100 volumes of collected works.
Fu Xuan originally wrote the internal chapter, and his son Fu Xian gave it to Sikong Wang Shen to read.
Wang Chen wrote to Fu Xuan: I saw your book, which contains grand words and well-equipped principles, plans for governing the country, and attaches great importance to Confucian education and morality. It is enough to block the debauchery of Yang Zhu and Mo Zhai's teachings, and can be compared with Xun Kuang and Meng Ke in ancient times.
Every time I open the book, I sigh with emotion. Without seeing Jia Yi, I thought I was better than him, but now I know I can't compare to him.
That’s so true! Later, he was granted the title of Marquis of Qingquan, and his son Fu Xian inherited the title.
Fu Xian's character is "Yu", and he has a strong sense of uprightness.
He has a strict demeanor and conduct, is well-informed, intelligent and wise, hates evil as much as his enemies, recommends talents, is willing to do good, and often looks up to the ambitions of Ji Wenzi and Zhongshanfu.
I like to write literary essays. Although my literary talent is not brilliant, my remarks can serve as a warning.
Yu Chun of Yingchuan often lamented: Fu Changyu's articles are close to the poet's creation.
In the early years of Xianning, he inherited his father's title and worshiped him as Prince Xima. He moved to Shangshu Youcheng and went to court to serve as the governor of Jizhou. His stepmother Du refused to go with Fu Xian, so Fu Xian petitioned to be dismissed.
Thirty years later, he was appointed Situ Zuo Changshi.
At that time, Emperor Wu paid attention to political affairs and issued an edict to visit courtiers to inquire about political affairs.
Fu Xian wrote a letter saying: Your Majesty is in the most distinguished position, but you do what commoners do, take care of everything yourself, and work hard until the sun is in the west.
The emperors of the past, even if they personally did small things to benefit the world, they would not surpass His Majesty.
However, it has been fifteen years since the founding of Thailand, but the army and the country are not strong enough, and the people are not rich enough. When a year is not good, famine will occur. It is indeed because there are too many official positions and complicated affairs, and there are too many people who are exempted from corvee. There are many people who cannibalize and few people who work in agriculture.
Because of my ignorance and carelessness, I am ashamed of my position. Every time I see the edicts worrying about the people's famine in the years and being unable to help, I feel extremely ashamed. How dare I not use all my stupidity to answer the emperor's inquiries?
There used to be four governors, but now including the supervisors, there are more than ten.
Xia Yu divided the land into nine states. The current number of governors is almost doubled, the household population is only one-tenth that of the Han Dynasty, and there are even more counties and counties.
The empty gate of the captain's teeth is of no use to the palace guards, but military mansions are set up out of thin air, and there are often hundreds of them.
The fifth-level princes also set up official subordinates.
summary: Fu Xuan wrote "Fu Zi," a book on governance and the three religions, divided into internal, external, and middle chapters, with over 100 volumes. His son Fu Xian inherited his title. Fu Xian, courtesy name Yu, was upright, strict, and hated evil. He served as Prince Xima, Shangshu Youcheng, and governor of Jizhou, but resigned when his stepmother refused to accompany him. Later, as Situ Zuo Changshi, he criticized the emperor for overworking himself and proposed consolidating official positions, simplifying affairs, and promoting agriculture. He also petitioned against extravagance, citing ancient frugality. During Emperor Hui's reign, he advised Yang Jun on regency matters and later criticized Sima Liang for excessive rewards. Fu Xian was known for his fearless impeachments, including against Wang Rong, and his advocacy for long-term official tenures. He died in office at age fifty-six, posthumously titled Zhen. He had three sons: Fu Fu, Fu Rixi, and Fu Zuan.

translation:
Shantao is named Juyuan, and Hanoi embraces people.
Father Shan Yao is Wanjuling.
Shantao lost his father in his early years and his family was poor. When he was young, he was thoughtful and unique.
He likes "Zhuangzi" and "Laozi" and often hides himself without showing his talents.
He had friendship with Ji Kang and Lu An, and later met Ruan Ji, and established a friendship in the bamboo forest and became the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Forest. They had a tacit understanding of understanding each other without having to speak. Ji Kang was later convicted. Before his execution, he said to his son Ji Shao: With Juyuan here, you are no longer an orphan.
Shan Tao was forty years old, and he was initially appointed as the princess's administrator, meritorious officer, and chief planner.
He was elected Xiaolian, and the state called him to serve in the Ministry of Henan.
Living with Shi Jian, Shan Tao wrapped himself up at night and pushed Shi Jian awake and said: "When are you still sleeping now?"
Do you know what Tai Tu meant by calling him sick?
Shi Jian said: "The prime minister failed to come to court three times, so I issued an edict to let him go home. What are you worried about?"
Shan Tao said: Alas, Mr. Shi will not be in danger during the war!
He threw down the talisman and left.
Within two years, Cao Shuang changed his mind and he became invisible and no longer participated in world affairs.
After Yu Xuanmu was a middle cousin, he met Emperor Jing.
Emperor Jing said: "Does Lu Wang want to be an official?"
He was ordered to recommend him as a scholar and a doctor.
He was transferred to General Wang Chang and served as a lieutenant.
After a long time, he paid homage to Zhao Guoxiang. He was promoted to minister of official affairs.
Emperor Wen wrote to Shan Tao: You are honest and smart in doing things, and your elegant conduct is beyond the world.
Considering your shortage of various supplies, I will send you 200,000 yuan of money and 200 dendrobium of grain today.
Emperor Wei once gave spring clothes to Emperor Jing, who in turn gave them to Shan Tao.
And because his mother was old, she also gave him a quinoa staff.
In his later years, he interacted with Shangshu Hekui and treated Zhong Hui and Pei Xiu sincerely and intimately.
Since they were high-ranking officials and competed for power, Shantao lived peacefully among them, each getting what he wanted without any regrets.
He was promoted to general and became a lieutenant.
The bell box is causing chaos in Shu, and Sai Tong will march westward.
At that time, all the princes of the Wei family were in Ye, and Emperor Wen said to Shan Tao: I will handle the affairs in the west by myself, and I will entrust you with everything in the rear.
I appointed my officer as an agent for the marching Sima, and assigned 500 personal soldiers to guard Ye.
In the early years of Xianxi's reign, he was named Xin Da Zi.
He was transferred to the post of Prime Minister Zuo Changshi and took charge of other camps.
At that time, the emperor ordered the prince to pay homage to Shan Tao because he was famous in the countryside.
The emperor succeeded King Jing with Sima You, King of Qi, and he always thought highly of Sima You. He once asked Pei Xiu: "The general failed to achieve his great cause, so I only inherited what he did after his death."
Therefore, the appointment of Sima You will be attributed to his brother, is that okay?
Pei Zhou thought it was impossible and asked Shan Tao about this matter.
Shan Tao replied: It is against etiquette and ominous to abolish the elder and establish the younger.
summary: Shantao, also known as Juyuan, was a man of Hanoi who lost his father early and grew up in poverty. He was thoughtful from a young age, favored the works of Zhuangzi and Laozi, and often concealed his talents. He formed deep friendships with Ji Kang, Lu An, and later Ruan Ji, becoming one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Forest. At forty, he began his official career, serving in various roles such as the princess's administrator and chief planner. He was known for his integrity and wisdom, once warning Shi Jian about the dangers of Cao Shuang's rebellion. After Cao Shuang's downfall, Shantao withdrew from public life for a time. Shantao later served under Emperor Jing and Emperor Wen, holding positions such as Zhao Guoxiang and minister of official affairs. He was praised for his honesty and intelligence, receiving generous gifts from the emperor. In his later years, he interacted with high-ranking officials like Zhong Hui and Pei Xiu, maintaining harmony among them. He was promoted to general and lieutenant, and during the campaign against Shu, he was entrusted with guarding Ye. In the early years of Xianxi, he was named Xin Da Zi and later served as Prime Minister Zuo Changshi.

translation:
The safety of the country often arises from this.
The candidate for the crown prince was then determined.
The prince personally thanked Shan Tao.
After Emperor Wu accepted the concession, he asked Shantao to guard Dahonglu and escort King Chenliu to Ye.
In the early years of Taishi, he was awarded the title of Captain of Fengche and was promoted to the title of Xin Da Po.
When Yang Hu was in power, people at that time wanted to exclude Tomb Chui, but Shan Tao protected him sternly.
Therefore, against the wishes of his powerful ministers, he left the capital to serve as the governor of Jizhou and became the general of Ningyuan.
The customs in Jizhou are despicable and they do not recommend each other.
He screened and selected hermits and aggrieved people on the mountainside, searched for and visited talented people, and commended and recruited more than 30 people. He was famous at that time.
People began to respect the worthy, and customs changed.
He was transferred to Beizhonglang General to supervise the defense of Yecheng.
After entering the dynasty, he was appointed as a minister and later as a minister.
Because his mother resigned in old age, Shao Shu said: Although you put your mind on filial piety, your duties are divided into upper and lower positions, and you have to take care of yourself sooner or later. You should let go of family ties so that the spirit of serving the public can flourish.
Shan Tao wholeheartedly requested to resign and submitted it dozens of times. It took a long time for his resignation to be accepted.
He was awarded the title of Yilang. Because the mountainside was honest and frugal and it was difficult to provide for him, the emperor specially gave him a certificate of daily supply and a bed, tent and mattress.
The courtesy salary was high and heavy, and no one could compare with it at that time.
Later, he was appointed Taichang Qing, but he did not go to his post because of illness.
My mother passed away and I returned to my hometown.
Xiying was over sixty years old and went beyond the formal mourning standards. She carried earth on her back to build a grave and planted pines and cypresses with her own hands.
Shao Shu said: The person who completes the education together with me is the official position of ruling everyone.
Nowadays, customs are declining and people's hearts are in turmoil. We should declare our likes and dislikes. How can we suppress ourselves by giving in?
Although Shan Taichang is still in mourning and it is difficult to violate human feelings, but there are many things going on now, how can he fulfill his wish?
Shanmai was appointed Shangshu of the Ministry of Personnel.
Shan Tao declined on the grounds of mourning and illness, and expressed his sincerity.
After the death of Queen Yuan, she returned to Luoyang by car.
Because of Shao Ling's persecution, he took office.
Officials were selected one after another, both inside and outside the court, and talented people were appointed.
In the early years of Xianning, he was transferred to the position of Shaofu of the Crown Prince, and was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi.
He refused firmly on the grounds of old age and illness, and stated his condition in the table above.
I have been listed dozens of times, but I have not been in office for a long time, and I was impeached by Zuo Cheng Bai.
The emperor said: Shan Tao said that he was sick, but I didn't listen to him.
Just let Shan Tao sit and be in charge of the official selection. Why care about the superiors and subordinates? Don't ask for guilt.
Shantao felt uneasy, so he apologized and said: In ancient times, the king's way was about integrity.
Your Majesty cannot be partial because of an old minister, so why should I feel like facing the sun and the moon again and again?
Please follow the above table to clarify the laws and regulations.
summary: When Emperor Wu succeeded, Shantao advised against appointing Sima You, citing the importance of proper succession. He served as Dahonglu and later as Fengche Captain. As governor of Jizhou, he reformed local customs by recommending talented individuals. He resigned multiple times due to his mother's age, but was eventually persuaded to return to office. He served as Shangshu of the Ministry of Personnel, selecting officials based on merit. Despite facing criticism, he continued his work, earning the title "Monkey Announcement" for his screening methods.

translation:
The person in charge did not understand the purpose of Shaoshu, but instead slandered me deeply, damaging the culture of respecting sages and worsening my reputation for being unvirtuous. How can I set an example to far and near!
Shan Tao had no choice but to take up the post of director again.
In the early years of Taikang, he was promoted to Youpuse and became a Guanglu doctor, but his positions of serving in the palace and in charge of the election remained the same.
Shan Tao resolutely refused because of his old age and illness. The emperor said to Shao: "You have become a role model for the world with your morality. Moreover, I have admired your lofty ambitions since the late emperor."
I will rely on you to make customs clear. Why do you want to stay away from the government and just make your own ambitions noble? Isn't my sincerity enough to make you understand? Why do you still refuse?
We should work hard in time to meet expectations.
If you don't take back your refusal, I can't sleep peacefully.
Shantao went to the table again and firmly declined, refusing to allow it.
After Wu was pacified, the emperor issued an edict to stop military service to show peace in the world. All prefectures and counties withdrew their troops. One hundred military officials were appointed in large counties and fifty in small counties.
The emperor once gave a martial arts lecture at the Xuanwu Field. Shan Tao was ill at the time, so he sent a letter to Shao to let him follow him in a sedan chair.
So he discussed the use of troops with Lu Qin and believed that the armaments of prefectures and counties should not be withdrawn. His remarks were very accurate.
At that time, it was believed that Shanliao did not follow the example of strong tyrants and ridges, but secretly cooperated with them.
The emperor praised him and said: This is a famous saying in the world.
However it was not accepted.
After the death of the Prime Minister, there were many wars and bandits. The counties and counties were unable to resist because they were unarmed, and the world was in chaos, just as Shan Tao said.
Later, when he was appointed Situ, Liangzhan resolutely declined.
The edict said: You have high moral character and high prestige, and you are a famous elder in the court. Therefore, you were granted the high position of prime minister, but you gave in too much and repeated it many times. It is really sad.
You should always serve the government and assist me.
Shan Tao went on to say: I have served this dynasty for more than thirty years, but in the end I failed to make the slightest contribution to the advancement of education.
His Majesty favored me infinitely and granted me the position of the Third Division.
I have heard that a person with poor moral character and a high official but little ability to shoulder heavy responsibilities is in danger of ruining state affairs due to his incompetence and bringing disaster to his family. May your Majesty grant me generations of grace, and beg me to retire and return to my hometown.
The edict said: I rely on your merits in assisting the government, stabilizing the royal family, and supporting the emperor.
The position of Situ is actually in charge of national education, so I respectfully grant it to you to meet everyone's expectations.
How can you suppress and degrade yourself by giving in?
After ordering him no longer to submit memorials, he sent someone to add a seal and ribbon to Shan Tao's bed.
Shan Tao said: How can a dying person defile the government?
Riding home sick.
summary: In his later years, Shantao faced the dictatorship of the Hou party and advised the emperor without success. He resigned due to old age and illness, but was repeatedly called back to service. He was promoted to Youpuse and Guanglu doctor, but continued to decline due to health. After Wu was pacified, he advised against withdrawing military forces, a warning that proved prescient during later chaos. He was appointed Situ but refused, eventually dying at seventy-nine. He was given posthumous honors and his family was provided for by the emperor.

translation:
He died in the fourth year of Taikang at the age of seventy-nine. Xia Shao gave him a noble coffin, a set of court robes, a set of clothes, 500,000 yuan in money, and a hundred bolts of cloth for funeral purposes. He was forced to serve as a Situ through a policy letter, and was given a purple ribbon with a honey seal to serve as Diao Chan.
When he was about to be buried, he was given 400,000 pieces of money and a hundred pieces of cloth.
Zuo Changshi Fan Di and others said to the emperor: Shantao's old house has ten rooms, and his descendants cannot live in it.
The emperor built houses for it.
At first, Shantao was a commoner and his family was poor. He said to his wife Han Di: "Bear the hunger and cold. I will be the third father-in-law in the future. I wonder if you can be the father-in-law's wife!"
After becoming prosperous and wealthy, he was loyal, prudent and frugal. Although his title was like that of a prince, he did not take concubines.
Salaries and rewards were distributed to relatives and friends.
At first, Yuan Yi, a native of Chen County, served as a minister. He corrupted and bribed officials to gain fame. He also gave Shan Tao a hundred catties of silk. Shan Tao did not want to be different from others at that time, so he accepted the silk and kept it in the attic.
Later, Yuan Yi's affairs were exposed and he was put into a carriage and handed over to Tingwei. Anyone who accepted a bribe would be held accountable.
Shan Tao took out the silk and gave it to the officials. After years of dust accumulation, the seal was not opened.
Shan Tao drank until he was drunk until he was drunk. The emperor wanted to test him, so he prepared eight measures of wine for him to drink, and secretly added more wine for him. Shan Tao drank to his limit and stopped drinking.
He has five sons: Shan Gai, Shan Chun, Shan Yun, Shan Mo, and Shan Jian.
Shan Gai, whose courtesy name was Bolun, inherited his father's title. He became governor of Bingzhou and crown prince Zuo Li, and was posthumously awarded the title of Captain of Changshui.
Shan Gai's son Shan Zhang was named Yanzu and served as a lieutenant in the Yi Army.
The second son returned to Shanshi and served as a official official and a regular attendant on Sanqi.
Shan Chun, whose courtesy name was Zixuan, was not an official, while Shan Yun, whose courtesy name was Shuzhen, was appointed as the captain of Fengche. Both of them had a hunchback and were short in stature, but they were extremely intelligent.
After Emperor Wu heard about it, he wanted to see them. Shan Tao did not dare to refuse, so he went to ask Shan Yun.
Shan Yun thought he was short with a hunchback and refused to go.
Shan Tao thought that they were better than him, so he wrote: My two sons are weak and sick, do not interact with others, and dare not accept orders.
Shan Mo, whose courtesy name is Ji Chang, is intelligent and talented, and his official position reaches the rank of Sikong Tu.
Shan Jian's courtesy name is Ji Lun.
He has a gentle temperament and a fatherly demeanor. He is in his twenties and Shantao doesn't understand him.
The mountain slip sighed and said: I am almost thirty years old and my father does not understand me!
Later, he became famous with Ji Shao from Qiao, Liu Mo from Peijun, and Yang Zhun from Hongnong.
At first, he was appointed as Prince Sheren, and was promoted several times to Prince Concubine, Huang Menlang, and the governor of Qingzhou.
summary: Shantao was known for his frugality and loyalty, never taking concubines despite his high status. He distributed his salary to relatives and friends. He once accepted silk from a corrupt official but kept it sealed, later returning it when the official's crimes were exposed. He had five sons: Shan Gai, Shan Chun, Shan Yun, Shan Mo, and Shan Jian. Shan Gai inherited his title and served as governor of Bingzhou. Shan Jian, known for his gentle temperament, became a prominent official, serving as minister and governor of various regions.

translation:
Wang Rong was good at identifying talents. He once regarded Shan Tao as uncarved jade and uncut gold. People respected him for his preciousness, but they didn't know how to describe his talent. Wang Yan's charm and appearance were elegant and pure, like a beautiful Yao Lin tree, so he was naturally a figure outside the world.
It is said that Pei Fan was not good at utilizing his strengths, while Xun Xu was good at making up for his shortcomings, and Chen Daoning was as tall and straight as a long pole.
His younger brother Wang Dun was famous, but Wang Rong hated him.
Every time Wang Dun waited to see Wang Rong, Wang Rong would excuse himself because he was ill.
Wang Dun later turned out to be rebellious and rebellious.
Wang Rong's discernment and foresight are like this.
I once passed Huang Gong's wine stove and turned around and said to the guests in the car behind me: I used to have a drink here with Ji Shuye and Ruan Sizong, and I also participated in the bamboo forest tour.
Ever since Ji and Ruan passed away, I have been bound by current events.
Today I see all this so close to my eyes, but it seems so far away!
At the beginning, Sun Xiu was appointed as an official in Langye County and asked the township officials to make comments.
Wang Rong's cousin Wang Yan planned not to agree, but Wang Rong persuaded him to criticize Sun Xiu.
After Sun Xiu succeeded, all the officials in the court who had a grudge against him were killed, but Wang Rong and Wang Yan benefited from Sun Xiu.
His son Wang Wan has a good reputation.
He was young and obese. Wang Rong made him eat chaff and he became even more obese.
Died at the age of nineteen.
There was a concubine named Wang Xing, and Wang Rong looked down upon him.
Let the son of his cousin Wang Qing, the prefect of Yangping, succeed him.
Wang Yan, whose courtesy name is Yifu, has a clear and beautiful expression, tranquility and elegance.
When I was a child, I visited Shan Tao. Shan Tao sighed for a long time. Wang Yan left. Shan Tao looked at him and said: What an old woman, she gave birth to such a son!
The person who delays the people of the world may not be this person.
His father, Wang Yi, was a general in Qianbei Province. He often had official matters and sent people to list them and report them from time to time.
Wang Yan was fourteen years old. He was in the capital at that time. He went to the servant She Yangkun to explain the matter. His words were very clear and eloquent.
Yang Hu had a reputation for being very virtuous, but although Wang Yan was young, he did not appear to be aggrieved by others. Everyone was surprised.
Yang Jun wanted to marry his daughter to him, but Wang Yan was ashamed of this and pretended to be crazy to avoid the matter.
Emperor Wu heard about his reputation and asked Wang Rong: Who can Yifu be compared with in this world?
Wang Rong said: If you don't see anyone who can compare with him, you should look for it from the ancients.
In the eighth year of Taishi, Xia Shao asked him to recommend people with talents who could stabilize the border. Wang Jie initially liked to talk about Zongheng, so Lu Lian, the minister, recommended him as the governor of Liaosai.
I didn't go to my post, so I didn't talk about worldly affairs. I just wrote poems and talked about it.
Once, because of a banquet, the tribesmen were angry and threw a wooden plate into his face.
Wang Yan didn't say anything at first and asked Wang Zun to get in the car and leave.
However, I felt dissatisfied. I picked up the mirror in the car and looked at myself, and said to Director Wang: You are looking at me on the back of the cow.
His father died in Peiping, and he gave many gifts at his funeral. His relatives and friends borrowed money from him and gave it to them.
Within a few years, his family property was exhausted and he went to live in the countryside west of Luocheng. Later, he was appointed Prince Sheren and promoted to Shangshu Lang.
summary: Wang Rong, courtesy name Junchong, was from Linyi. He was known for his intelligence and calmness from a young age, once standing unafraid during a tiger's roar. He was friends with Ruan Ji and others, and was known for his insight. He served in various official roles, including governor of Jingzhou and Yuzhou, and was involved in the conquest of Wu. He was known for his filial piety, though he did not strictly adhere to rituals. He was criticized for his greed and stinginess, often calculating his wealth day and night. He died at seventy-two, posthumously named Yuan.

translation:
When Prince Minhuai was deposed, the old officials were ordered not to say goodbye. The officials were very angry and even braved the ban to say goodbye.
Sili Colonel Man Fen ordered the people who were seeing them off in central Henan to be captured and sent to prison, but Yue Guang let them go.
Everyone was worried about Le Guang.
Sun Yan advised Jia Mi: "In the past, the prince was deposed because of his sins. His ministers were not afraid of severe prohibitions and took the risk to see him off."
If arresting them would only promote the prince's interests, it would be better to let them go.
Mai Mi thought he was right, and Yue Guang was not convicted.
He was promoted to Zuopushe, the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel. Later, Sima Yao, King of Shu'an, was supposed to be the Pushe. He was appointed as Youpushe to Yue Guang, leading the Ministry of Personnel, and acting as the Shangshuling on behalf of Wang Rong. At first Wang Rong recommended Yue Guang, but eventually he took his place. People at the time praised Yue Guang.
Sima Ying, the king of Chengdu, was Le Guang's son-in-law. When Sima Yi, the king of Changsha, launched an attack, Le Guang was already in an important position in the court, and some villains slandered him.
Sima Yi asked Le Guang about this matter. Le Guang's expression remained unchanged and he slowly replied: "How can I exchange five men for one woman?"
Sima Yi still had doubts, and Le Guang eventually died of worry.
When Xun Fan heard that Yue Guang had not been able to escape the disaster, he shed tears for him.
He has three sons: Le Kai, Le Zhao and Le Chen.
Le Kai, whose courtesy name was Hongxu, was appointed as the commander-in-chief of the King of Qi, and participated in the Hussar Army.
Yue Zhao, whose courtesy name was Hongmao, was appointed as Taifu Shuhaiwangju.
Luoyang fell, and the brothers crossed the Yangtze River south together.
Lemo's courtesy name was Hongfan, and he served as General Zhenglu and Internal Secretary of Wu County.
Shi Chen said: The Han prime minister was quiet and governed by doing nothing; the Zhou prime minister was pure and empty, receiving salary and not doing political affairs.
Is the appointment of the three prime ministers different from that of ordinary officials?
Junchong is good at talking, Yifu advocates Taoism, ascends to the prominent position of Sangong, learns from Laozi and Zhuangzhuang and is lofty.
They believe in nothingness and chaos.
Wang Rong pleases others to seek shelter and accumulate wealth; Wang Yan protects himself, how can he still take care of the country?
There was a war between the three parties, foreign tribes intervened, Qiang and Di people and horses, and weapons like clouds.
A villain who flatters and flatters evil people in order to seek tolerance. Pushing a wall and crushing him to death is considered a courtesy.
Pingzi indulged in arrogance and could not bear the good reputation, so he finally lost his life and committed suicide.
Clothes decorate the appearance, Guizhang standardizes morals, the voice and rhyme conform to rituals and music, the spirit reflects the beauty of the mountains, the martial arts are justified, and the words are established as training.
Wang Cheng's arrogance is too much.
If you take off your clothes and climb trees, catch magpies naked, and take this as a way of understanding and think it is an elegant taste, then frivolous people will follow suit and violate morals.
His moral corruption was so extreme that he did strange things one after another. He went alone and ruined his life.
In the past, Yan Ying lay down and cried bitterly for Duke Zhuang, but now he is ordering to release his mournful followers. It must be because of Boyi's influence. Weak people can also be determined.
It is said in praise: The Jin Dynasty visited wise men and hermits, built a fairy platform, so high that it reached the sky, and the mountain emperor knew the talents.
Wang Jun is in a high position and likes to talk rather than be pragmatic.
summary: Wang Yan, courtesy name Yifu, was known for his clear expression and elegance. He was a leading figure in the Qingtan movement, advocating the philosophy of nothingness. He held high positions but was criticized for his lack of integrity and self-preservation. During the chaos of the Jin dynasty, he advised his brothers to take up posts in strategic regions, a plan known as the "cunning rabbit's three burrows." He was captured by Shi Le and killed after refusing to take responsibility for the dynasty's fall. He was fifty-six at his death. Le Guang, courtesy name Yanfu, was known for his calm and far-sighted nature. He was skilled in conversation and used simple words to explain profound truths. He served as Henan Yin and was known for his ability to resolve disputes. He once cured a guest's illness by explaining the illusion of a snake in a cup. He was praised for his integrity and adherence to ritual, even during times of chaos. He died of worry after being slandered. He had three sons: Le Kai, Le Zhao, and Le Chen.

translation:
Wang Hun, courtesy name Xuanchong, was born in Jinyang, Taiyuan.
His father, Wang Chang, was Wei Sikong.
Wang Hun is deep, elegant and thoughtful.
Inheriting his father's title of Marquis of Jingling, he was recruited as a subordinate officer of General Cao Shuang.
Cao Shuang was executed and dismissed from office as usual.
He was promoted to Huailing, and was promoted to serve as the minister of Huangmen of Sanqi and the regular servant of Sanqi.
During the Xianxi period, he was appointed as the captain of the Yue Cavalry School.
Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, granted Wang Hun the title of General Yanglie, and moved him to the post of governor of Xuzhou.
When there was famine and famine at that time, Wang Hun opened a warehouse to provide relief, and the people relied on him.
In the early years of Taishi, 1,800 households were added to the fiefdom.
After a period of time, he was transferred to General Dongzhonglang to supervise the military affairs in Huaibei and guard Zhuchang.
He stated the strategy of governing the country many times and was mostly adopted.
He was transferred to the post of general of conquering captives, supervising the military affairs of Yuzhou, and serving as the governor of Yuzhou.
Xinggeng's jurisdiction was connected to the county border. He declared his prestige, and many people surrendered and attached themselves to him.
The armies of Wu generals Xue Ying and Lu Shu were said to be one hundred thousand. Lu Shu's army went to Yiyang, and Xue Ying's army went to the new emperor.
At that time, all the soldiers in the state were on holiday, and there was only one traveler in the army. Wang Hun used a boat to cross the border quietly, but by surprise, Ying and others did not expect the arrival of Zhijun.
Wang Hun defeated them and made Wang Hun's second son Wang Shang the Marquis of Guannei due to his meritorious service.
He was moved to the post of General Andong, Commander-in-Chief of the Yangzhou military forces, and guarded Shouchun.
The Wu people settled in Wancheng on a large scale and planned to cause harm on the border.
Wang Hun sent the governor of Yangzhou, Ying Chuo, to lead all the armies in the south to defeat them. He also defeated some other military camps and burned more than 1.8 million hu of grain, more than 4,000 hectares of rice seedlings, and more than 600 ships that the Wu people had accumulated.
Wang Yun then deployed his troops on the eastern border to understand the dangers of the terrain, watched the enemy cities one by one, and inspected the situation of the attack.
After a large-scale crusade against Wu, Wang Hun led his troops from Hengjiang and sent soldiers Chen Shen and captain Zhang Qiao to attack Xunyangse Township. He also attacked Wuya gate general Kong Zhong and defeated them all, capturing Wu general Zhou Xing and five others.
He also sent Li Chun, the protector of Wu, to occupy Gaowang City and attack Wu general Yu Gong. He defeated him, killed many of them and captured many.
Wu Liwu's general Chen Dai and Pinglu general Zhu Ming came to surrender out of fear.
Wu Prime Minister Zhang Ti, General Sun Zhen and others led tens of thousands of troops towards Chengyang. Wang Hun sent Sima Sunchou and Yangzhou Governor Zhou Jun to defeat them. They killed two generals in front of the battle and beheaded 7,800 people. The Wu people were very frightened.
Sun Hao's Situ He Zhi and Jianwei General Sun Yan sent Guanyin Fujie to Wang Hun to surrender.
Later, Wang Jun broke through the stone and made Sun Hao surrender, gaining even greater prestige and fame.
The next day, Wang Hunchai crossed the river and boarded Jianye Palace to hold a banquet.
Thinking that he would occupy the river first and defeat Sun Hao's central army, he stood still and fell behind Wang Jun.
He felt very ashamed and jealous, and seemed unconvinced. He reported Wang Jun's crimes many times, and the people at the time ridiculed him.
The emperor issued an edict saying: The envoy Chijie, the governor of Yangzhou's military forces, General Andong, and the Marquis of Jingling Wang Hun led his army to advance to Moling, which made the enemy Sun Hao save his own life and defend himself, and was unable to divide his troops and rush upstream, thus achieving the success of the Western Army. He also destroyed the enemy and captured Zhang Ti, leaving Sun Hao with no choice but to tie himself up and beg to surrender.
So he pacified Moling and made outstanding achievements.
Eight more households were added to the fiefdom, he was promoted to the title of Duke, his son Wang Cheng was made Tinghou, his younger brother Wang Zhan was Guanneihou, and he was given eight thousand pieces of silk.
He was transferred to General Zhengshu and guarded Shouyang.
Wang Hun does not believe in criminal status and is fair and decisive in dealing with matters.
At that time, the Wu people had just surrendered and were very fearful.
Wang Hun comforted the strangers and sincerely comforted and accepted them. There were no empty seats in the seats and no guests lingering in front of the door.
Therefore, there are no people in Jiang Shu who are not happy to rely on him.
He was conscripted and appointed as Shangshu Zuopushe, and he was appointed as a regular attendant of Sanqi.
It happened that the courtiers were discussing that King Sima You of Qi should go to the vassal state. Wang Hun wrote a letter to advise: Accept the edict respectfully, follow the ancient laws, promote King Sima You of Qi to the rank of superior, uphold the etiquette towards him, and send Sima You to the vassal state.
In the past, when the Zhou family founded the country, they granted the surname Ji to shield the royal family, and they followed suit from generation to generation.
As for Gong Dan, he was the younger brother of King Yuan. He was in charge of the king's affairs and assisted in the great cause, and he was not allowed to go to the vassal state.
summary: Wang Hun, courtesy name Xuanchong, was from Jinyang, Taiyuan, and inherited his father Wang Chang's title of Marquis of Jingling. He served under Cao Shuang but was dismissed after Shuang's execution. Later, he held various posts, including Governor of Xuzhou, where he opened granaries to relieve famine. During the Taishi era, he was transferred to guard Zhuchang and frequently submitted governance strategies that were often adopted. As General of Conquering Captives in Yuzhou, he attracted many surrenders. He defeated Wu generals Xue Ying and Lu Shu, earning his son Wang Shang the title of Marquis of Guannei. As General Andong in Yangzhou, he repelled Wu forces, burning their grain and ships. During the major campaign against Wu, Wang Hun led troops from Hengjiang, capturing Wu generals and receiving surrenders from Chen Dai and Zhu Ming. He defeated Wu Prime Minister Zhang Ti, killing 7,800, leading to Sun Hao's surrender via He Zhi and Sun Yan. However, Wang Jun later took Sun Hao's surrender, causing Wang Hun shame and jealousy. He reported Wang Jun's crimes, drawing public ridicule. The emperor praised Wang Hun's role in pacifying Moling, adding fiefs and promoting him to Duke. He was later transferred to General Zhengshu, where he comforted surrendered Wu people. As Shangshu Zuopushe, he advised against sending Prince Sima You to a vassal state, citing historical precedents and urging retention for state security, but the emperor did not accept. In the Taixi era, he became Situ. Under Emperor Hui, he was given military command but insisted on wearing black robes to avoid impropriety, earning praise. When Prince Sima Zhang of Chu sought to kill Sima Liang, Wang Hun feigned illness and resisted with soldiers, and Sima Zhang was later killed. The emperor consulted Wang Hun on customs inquiries; Wang Hun proposed detailed questioning of local planners, which was approved. He died at seventy-five, posthumously named Yuan.

translation:
The eldest son Wang Shang died early, and the second son Wang Ji succeeded him.
Wang Ji, courtesy name Wuzi.
When he was young, he had superhuman talents, was handsome and bold, and his spirit was beyond compare. He likes to bow and arrow and ride horses. His bravery is unmatched. He is good at "Yi", "Zhuang" and "Lao". His writing is beautiful and his skills are superhuman. He is famous in the world, and he is as famous as his brother-in-law He Wei and Pei Kai.
Married Princess Changshan.
At the age of twenty, he was called away from home to serve as Zhongshu Lang and resigned in mourning for his mother.
He was appointed as a general of valiant cavalry, and was gradually promoted to the rank of servant. He was in the same official rank as the servants Kong Xun, Wang Xun and Yang Ji, and became a hero of his time.
Emperor Wu once met with ministers and local governors in the Shiqian Hall. Looking at Erji and Erxun, he said to the ministers: My right and left servants can be said to be docile and respectful.
Every time the servants come to see him, they always discuss the gains and losses of people and various things.
Wang Nai was good at talking, eloquent, and sarcastic. No courtier could surpass him, and the emperor valued him more closely.
Although he was promoted quickly, those who commented did not think it was because of Weng's son-in-law. They all said that he was achieved through talent.
However, although he looks magnanimous and elegant on the outside, he is very jealous and harsh on the inside and likes to hurt others with words, so people around him despise him.
Because of his father, Wang Jun was often excluded, and the discussions at that time ridiculed him.
King Sima You of Qi was about to go to the vassal state. After Wang Ji stated his request, he repeatedly asked the princess to enter the palace with Princess Changguang, Zhen De's wife, and kowtowed and cried, begging the emperor to keep Sima You.
The emperor angrily said to his attendant Wang Rong: "Brothers have the closest relationship. Now sending the King of Qi is naturally a matter for my family." And Zhen De and Wang Ji sent women one after another to cry to death!
Due to his disobedience to the imperial edict, he was demoted to the post of Prince of the State to offer wine, but his position as a regular attendant remained unchanged.
A few years later, he entered the palace and served as a servant.
At that time, Wang Hun was a servant, and his boss sometimes handled things improperly. Wang Ji was strict by nature and punished him according to law.
Wang Jiping had always been at odds with his cousin Wang You. Wang You's party members believed that Wang Liao did not care about his father too much, so they encouraged different opinions.
He took up the post of Henan Yin, but before he took office, he was found guilty of whipping an auxiliary official in the palace and was dismissed from office. Wang Youzheng was appointed.
Shan Shan was dismissed from the court, so Wang Ji moved his family to the foot of Beimang Mountain.
Wang Ji was extravagant by nature and was very particular about food and clothing.
At that time, the land price in Luojing was very high. Wang Ji bought the land and used it as a riding and shooting track. He put the money together to pave the track. People at the time called it "Jingou".
Because Wang Kai was the emperor's uncle, he was extravagant and luxurious. He had a cow named "Eight Hundred Miles Pier", and the horns of the cow's hooves were often decorated.
Wang Ji proposed to use 10 million yuan as a bet and a cow to compete in archery.
Wang Kai thought he was capable and asked Wang Ji to shoot first.
As soon as Wang Ji hit the target, he sat on the throne and yelled at everyone to quickly get the heart of the cow. In a blink of an eye, he arrived, cut it off with a knife, and left.
He Wei was very frugal by nature and had a good plum tree at home. The emperor asked for it but only gave him dozens of it.
While Wang Ji was on duty with Wei, he led the young man to the orchard, ate together, and cut down the plum tree before leaving.
The emperor once visited Wang Ji's residence and served him a sumptuous meal, all of which was served in glassware.
Steamed gizzards tasted very good. When the emperor asked why, he replied: Steamed with human milk.
The emperor looked very unhappy and left before finishing his meal.
Wang Ji knew the temperament of horses very well. He once rode a horse that was covered with dry mud. There was water in front of it, but the horse refused to cross.
Wang Zha said: This must be because he is reluctant to give up the clay.
He was asked to let go, and the horse crossed the water.
Therefore, Du Yu said that Wang Ji had a hobby of loving horses.
The emperor once said to Qi Ku: I want to scold Wang Liao and then give him an official title. How about that?
He Wei said: Wang Ji is generous and generous, I'm afraid I can't wrong him.
The emperor then summoned Wang Ji, scolded him deeply, and then said: Do you know how ashamed you are?
Wang Ji replied: Brothers are incompatible. I am always ashamed of your majesty.
Others can alienate their relatives, but I cannot let my relatives get close. I am ashamed of Your Majesty for this.
The emperor remained silent.
The emperor once played chess with Wang Ji, and Sun Hao was beside him. The emperor said to Zhubi: Why do you like to skin people?
Sun Hao said: If you see someone who is rude to the king, skin him.
Wang Ji put his feet under the chessboard, so Sun Hao ridiculed Wang Ji.
Soon he was made a civilian and served as a servant.
summary: Wang Ji, courtesy name Wuzi, was Wang Hun's son. He was exceptionally talented, skilled in archery and the "Yi," "Zhuang," and "Lao" texts, and married Princess Changshan. He served as Zhongshu Lang and later as a servant, known for his eloquence and favored by Emperor Wu. However, he was inwardly jealous and harsh with words. He opposed sending Prince Sima You away, crying with the princess, which angered the emperor and led to demotion. As Henan Yin, he was dismissed for whipping an official. He was extravagant, paving a riding track with money and betting a prized cow with Wang Kai, cutting it up after winning. He once served human-milk-steamed food to the emperor, who left displeased. He understood horses, once recognizing a horse's reluctance to cross mud. He died at forty-six, posthumously named General of Hussars. At his funeral, Sun Chu brayed like a donkey in tribute, making guests laugh. He married a blind, jealous princess and had two sons by a concubine.

translation:
At the age of forty-six, he died before Wang Yun, and was posthumously awarded the title of General of Hussars.
When it was about to be buried, all the wise men of that time came.
Sun Chu respected Wang Ji very much. He came late and cried very sadly. All the guests shed tears.
After crying, he said to the coffin: You often like me to bray like a donkey, so I will bray for you.
I learned that the shape is similar and the voice is lifelike, and the guests all laughed.
Yaochu looked back at them and said: You didn't die, but Wang Zha died!
At the beginning, Wang Ji married a princess. The princess was blind and very jealous. However, she never had children. She had two sons by his concubine.
The king, named Seixuan, inherited the title of Yuyun and paid homage to Shizhong.
The second son, Wang Lou, whose courtesy name was Jianxuan, succeeded the princess and was given the title of Qian Dancai.
Wang Zha has two younger brothers, Wang Tuo, whose courtesy name is Su, and Wang, who has a short stem. They are both good at talking, intelligent and literary, and both have held high and noble positions.
Wang Jun, courtesy name Shizhi, was from Hongnong Lake.
Someone in the family has been a prefect.
Wang Jun was well-read in ancient books and had a handsome appearance. He did not pay attention to reputation and conduct, and was not praised by the villagers.
Later, I changed my moral integrity, became open-minded and had great ambitions.
Once a house was built, dozens of steps were left in front of the door.
Someone asked him why he left too much space. Wang Jun said: I want to allow halberds and flags to be accommodated in front of the door.
Everyone laughed at him, and Wang Jun said: "Chen Sheng once said, how can the sparrow know the ambition of the swan?"
The state and county recruited him to work in Hedong.
Those who were dishonest among the officials all left on their own after hearing the news.
Xu Miao, a native of the state of Yan, the governor, had a daughter, Shu Xian, who was talented and unmarried.
Xu Miao gathered his subordinate officials in a grand ceremony and asked his daughter to watch them in their buns.
The daughter pointed at Wang Jun and told her mother, so Xu Miao married her daughter to him.
Later, when he participated in the Southern Military Campaign, Yang Hu understood and treated him favorably.
Yang Ji, the son of Yang Hu's elder brother, said to Yang Hu: Wang Jun's ambitions as a man are too excessive, his extravagance is intemperate, and he cannot be trusted too much. He should be restricted.
Yang Hu said: Wang Jun has a great talent. I will help him realize his wish and I will definitely use him.
He was transferred to the position of charioteer and knight, and knowledgeable people said that Yang Hu could recommend talented people.
He was appointed as the governor of Bajun.
Bajun is adjacent to the border with Wu State. The soldiers are hard at work and most of the boys are not supported.
Wang Jun then made the regulations strict and the corvee loose. Those who gave birth were allowed to rest and exempted from the corvee. Thousands of people survived in this way.
He was transferred to the post of governor of Guanghan and implemented benevolent and benevolent policies, and the people relied on him.
Wang Jun dreamed of three knives hanging on the beam in his bedroom at night, and then another knife was added. Wang Jun woke up with a start, hating this dream in his heart.
Li Yi, the chief registrar, paid two obeisances to congratulate him and said: "The three knives are the characters for state. One more sword has been added. I'm afraid you are going to Yizhou?"
When the thief Zhang Hong killed Huangfu Yan, the governor of Yizhou, he transferred Wang Jun to be the governor of Yizhou.
Wang Jun planned to kill Zhang Hong and others, and was named a Marquis of Guannei for their meritorious services.
summary: Wang Jun, courtesy name Shizhi, was from Hongnong Lake. He was well-read and handsome, initially lacking reputation but later changed his ways. He built a house with a wide gate, saying it would accommodate halberds and flags. He married Xu Miao's daughter after she saw him at a gathering. Yang Hu recognized his talent and helped him. As Governor of Bajun, he eased corvée for newborns, saving thousands. As Governor of Guanghan, he was benevolent. He dreamed of knives, interpreted as a sign he would govern Yizhou, and became its governor, pacifying rebels. He built large ships for attacking Wu, with iron cones and locks countered by rafts and torches. He captured Wu territories, and Sun Hao surrendered. Wang Jun entered Shitou, accepting Sun Hao's surrender. He was promoted but conflicted with Wang Hun, who accused him of violating orders. Wang Jun defended himself, citing edicts and circumstances. He was made General of the Auxiliary State but felt under-rewarded, often complaining. He died at eighty, posthumously named Wu. His descendants later fell into poverty, prompting Huan Wen to request restoration of their title.

translation:
In the early years of Taishi's reign, he was given the title of Marquis of Guannei.
Ye Ling was left alone, Tang Bin's morals were in line with etiquette, and his education was completed in one year.
He was moved to the post of governor of Yiyang, and public bans were established to prevent it, and the people became stable.
He resigned from the palace because of his mother's funeral.
Yizhou was adjacent to the enemy invaders in Chengli, and there was a shortage of personnel for the position of military supervisor. The court discussed appointing Wuling prefects Yang Zong and Tang Bin.
Emperor Wu asked Wen Li, the regular attendant of Sanqi, about this incident. Wen Li said: "Neither Yang Zong nor Tang Bin should be lost."
However, Tang Bin has a strong desire for wealth and Yang Zong is a drunkard. Please ask your Majesty to rule.
Emperor Wu said: The desire for money can be satisfied, but it is difficult for people who are greedy to change.
So Tang Bin was appointed.
Soon after, Tang Bin was ordered to supervise the military affairs in Badong and was awarded the title of General Guangwu.
Shangshu discussed the strategy of conquering Wu, which was very much in line with the emperor's wishes.

translation:
Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, was born in Guangling and was a descendant of Liu Xu, King Li of Guangling in the Han Dynasty.

During the Xianning period, Liu Song and Sanqi Lang Bai Bao were ordered to inspect the Jingyang area. Because the envoys were in compliance with the decree, they were transferred to Huang Menlang.

The emperor thought that Liu Song was unreasonable in enforcing the law, so he was demoted to the prefect of Jingzhao. Before taking up the post, he was transferred to Hanoi.

After the mourning period expired, he was appointed Prime Minister of Huainan.
During his tenure, he was serious and organized and had great political achievements.
In the past, the construction of Shaopi required tens of thousands of labors a year. The powerful took advantage of the opportunity to annex the land, and the weak and poor people lost their fields. Liu Song asked the old and young to work together, and the value was calculated according to the amount of repairs. The people praised him for his fair administration and benefiting the people.
Liu Song wrote in the county:
I used to serve in Hanoi. When I was leaving, I received an edict and said: "What you talked about are all very important things. After taking office, you should report all the big and small things."
I usually have a lot to do, so I may not be able to give you all the answers, so please don’t doubt me because of this.
On the day when the minister accepted the edict, he was filled with joy and fear, and he was even more thoughtful about doing his best to be loyal. Therefore, he forgot his own contempt and was willing to use a small candlelight to increase the glory of the emperor.
summary: Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, was born in Guangling and descended from Liu Xu, King Li of Guangling in the Han Dynasty. His family had been prestigious for generations, belonging to a group of four surnames—Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu—all originating from the Liu surname. His father, Liu Guan, served as the prefect of Pingyang. Liu Song demonstrated analytical abilities from childhood and was praised by contemporaries. Though recommended as a filial and honest scholar, he declined the position. Emperor Wen summoned him to serve in the Prime Minister's Mansion and sent him as an envoy to Shu, which had just been pacified. Finding the people hungry and the land desolate, Liu Song petitioned for relief but granted aid without waiting for approval, resulting in his removal from office. When Emperor Wu of the Jin Dynasty ascended, Liu Song was appointed Shangshu Sangonglang, presiding over laws and redressing injustices. He gradually rose to Vice Minister of Zhongshu. During the Xianning period, he inspected Jingyang with Sanqi Lang Bai Bao and was transferred to Huang Menlang, then to Yilang and acting Tingwei. He reviewed the case of Shi Huyin, who was imprisoned without guilt, and proved his innocence, earning comparison to Zhang Shizhi. After six years in office, he was known for thoroughness and fairness. When Wu was conquered and generals competed for merit, Liu Song investigated and determined Wang Hun had highest merit and Wang Jun middle merit. The emperor considered this unreasonable and demoted Liu Song to prefect of Jingzhao, then transferred him to Hanoi. Before departing, he reported matters benefiting the country, petitioning to demolish water dams that caused disasters, bringing convenience to the people. After his mother's death, Liu Song left office. Following the mourning period, he became Prime Minister of Huainan, where he was serious and organized with great political achievements. He reformed the construction of Shaopi, which previously required tens of thousands of laborers annually, by having the old and young work together with compensation based on repairs, earning praise for fair administration. Liu Song submitted a lengthy memorial discussing various state affairs, including the establishment of feudal states, the importance of enfeoffing princes to create stable foundations, and the dangers of relying solely on county systems. He argued that enfeoffment would ensure long-term stability, drawing comparisons between the Zhou Dynasty's long duration due to feudal systems and the Qin Dynasty's rapid collapse after abolishing them.

Expedient systems cannot be used for a long time, and perverse government affairs cannot be used to ensure security. This means that the methods of attack and defense are different.
Although the people are ignorant, their wishes will not arise out of thin air. They must arise at the right time.
If there is a reason for it, then this desire cannot be taken away; until things change, the opportunity cannot be defied.
The sage's way of governing is to deal with things quickly and not wait to get off the bus, so every move can be timely and win the hearts of the people.
In the past, Emperor Wu of Wei divided the country and ordered people to serve and live in one place. This was necessary for the situation, but it was also unsatisfactory. The power was only used for a while to deal with urgent matters, which was not a regular rule.
But it has been used to this day and has not been changed for many years. Although the people are suffering hardships, they do not have any personal grudges. This is really because they understand that the three parties have not yet settled and unified, and they know that peace cannot be achieved for the time being.
summary: Liu Song also discussed the need for proper official evaluation, reducing labor burdens, developing agriculture, and maintaining grain prices. He criticized current governance for focusing on minor faults while ignoring major crimes, comparing this to leaving dangerous beasts on the road while strictly prohibiting mice. He advocated for simpler governance, long-term official appointments, and proper assessment of achievements. The imperial edict replied acknowledging his loyal service and requesting continued reports.

translation:
When Sima Lun's party member Zhang Lin heard about this, he was furious, but he was afraid that Sheng Feng was an upright person and could not assassinate him.
Sun Xiu and others praised Sima Lun's achievements and believed that Jiuxi should be added, and the officials did not dare to raise objections.
Only Xing Zuo said: In the past, nine tins were added to the droppings and nine tins were added to the cushions. They were only used temporarily and cannot be implemented as regular rituals.
Now that the ancestral temple is safe, even if the queen is deposed and the traitorous ministers who are in power are executed, in the past Zhou Bo killed Zhu Lu and honored Xiaowen, and Huo Guang abolished Changyi and honored Xiaowen, but they did not give Jiuxi his life.
It is not the system of the previous emperors to violate the old regulations and follow the system of the moment.
Please don’t implement Jiuxi’s suggestion.
Zhang Bing was very angry about this and believed that Liu Song was a member of Zhang Hua's party and was going to kill him.
Sun Xiu said: Killing Zhang Hua and Pei Ban has already hurt people's popularity, so we can't kill Liu Song again.
Zhang Lin gave up.
Then he appointed Luluo as the official Guanglu, and set up a horse parade in front of his official office.
Soon after he died of illness, the emperor sent someone to offer condolences and offered him 200,000 yuan and a court dress.
Liu Chen, the assistant minister of Zhongshu, reported that Liu Tan was the junior at that time and should be given as a gift to open the mansion.
Sun Xiuping always hated him and did not allow him.
Song had no children, and his son Liu Yong, who raised his younger brother Liu He, died early, and Xingli, the son of Liu Yong's younger brother Xingyi, was his legitimate grandson and inherited the title.
In the first year of Yongkang, an edict was issued to Liu Song for his meritorious service in taking charge of Pepsi when he killed Jia Mi. He was posthumously granted the title of Marquis of Liangzo County. Liu Biao, Liu Song's younger brother, who lived in the 1,500 households in the city, was given the courtesy name Zhongya to participate in the Andong military.
During the expedition to the county, Zhang Ti was captured and promoted to General Jinu many times.
When a fire broke out in the arsenal, Liu Biao came up with the idea to demolish the houses connected to the fire place and rescued many jewelry items.
He successively served as the governor of Jingzhou.
Liu Song's second brother Liu Zhong, also known as Shihun, served successively as Huang Menlang and Rongyang Prefect, but he died before taking office.
At first, Liu Song married his daughter to Chen Jiao from Linhuai. Chen Jiao was originally a descendant of the Liu family and was a close relative of Liu Song. She was adopted by his aunt's family and changed her surname to Chen.
Zhongzheng Liu You advised him on this matter. Liu Song said: After Shun, the surnames of Yao Yu, Chen Tian and others were originally from the same family, but intermarriage was inevitable for generations.
The same thing applies to my family now, intermarriage is allowed.
Liu Youzheng is thinking of writing a memorial. Stopped by sketch and therefore not impeached.
Liu Song asked Ming Fa, Chen Fu and Ji Zang, and said: "Who among the villagers is the most aggrieved?"
Both of them said: Liu You feels wronged.
He changed his temper and scolded them. Jiantang argued: Liu You was wrong to offend the Ming Dynasty because of his private discussion, but the public opinion of the villagers said that he was wronged.
Liu You was successively recruited into the positions of Duke Fu, Shangshu Lang, and Huangsha Yushi.
Li Chong, courtesy name Maozeng, was born in Zhongwu, Jiangxia.
His father, Li Jing, was the governor of Qinzhou and the Marquis of Dutingding.
Kui Zhong was studious and talented since childhood. He became an orphan in his early years and lived with his younger brothers. He was known for his friendship.
When he was twenty years old, he was appointed as the leader of the country. He was too humble to give in and refused to take office.
Later, in the literature of King Sisu, Shangshu stated that Jiupin said: The previous emperors established systems and changed them at any time. The reason for change is to make them suitable for the national conditions.
summary: In the early Yuankang period, Liu Song followed Sima Yun into court. When Yang Jun was executed, Liu Song guarded the palace and was appointed Minister of the Three Lords. He later transferred to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, establishing a nine-class system to reduce official turnover, but Jia Guo's specialized government prevented implementation. When Sima Lun killed Zhang Hua, Liu Song wept bitterly and rejoiced upon learning Zhang Hua's son had escaped. When Sun Xiu and others praised Sima Lun's achievements and proposed adding Jiuxi, Liu Song opposed it, citing historical precedents. Zhang Lin was furious but spared Liu Song due to Sun Xiu's advice. Liu Song soon died of illness, receiving imperial condolences and gifts.

translation:
Li Chong and Li Yi were both ministers. At that time, Wang Rong was appointed minister. Li Chong was praised for his integrity and uprightness. Li Yi Botong was wise and talented. Although they had different moral integrity, they both held important positions. Wang Rong treated them as close friends and each benefited from their own strengths.
Li Yi's courtesy name is Maoyan, and his deeds are not recorded in history books.
At that time, internal officials had more power and external officials had less power. In addition, there were many official ranks. Li Duan discussed this disadvantage and found it in "Hundred Officials".
Another Shangshu said: Although all those who escape favor in the mountains and forests are against the current world and have different origins, the reason why the late king praised them is to praise their noble sentiments.
In the past, the late emperor was worried about the disadvantages of luxurious customs and wanted to return to simplicity, so he consulted the officials at court and searched for reclusive people.
In the second year of Xianning, Huang Fumi of Anding was conscripted as the concubine of the crown prince. In the fourth year, Zhu Chong of Nan'an was conferred as the doctor. In the first year of Taikang, Zhu Chong was conscripted as the concubine of the crown prince. Although they all claimed to be ill and did not take office, both the government and the public expressed their joy and sincere submission.
Now Your Majesty is carrying forward the purpose of honoring the late emperor and respecting the virtuous. I visited Zhu Chong's hometown. I said that although he was very old, he still had great ambitions. He studied Confucianism and Taoism carefully, and his virtues were renewed as he grew older. His morals were pure, and everyone in the place was taught by him. He was indeed a virtuous man who lived in seclusion in the mountains, and he could serve as an example to keep the customs honest.
I think we should declare divine grace and give him a gift of recognition before he dies.
The government was in chaos at the time and ultimately failed to obey.
Li Chong served as the Protector of the Expeditions and the Prefect of Pingyang. He respected moral education, built schools, commended those who were loyal, and promoted talents. He was honest, frugal and without desires. He set an example for his subordinates. During his three years in office, he impeached and removed officials from four counties.
After the death of his younger brother Li Yi, he resigned from his official post.
In the early years of Yongkang, King Sima Lun of Zhao appointed Li Chong as Prime Minister Zuo Sima. He died of illness at the age of forty-eight due to worry.
The family is poor, the house is small, and there is no place to collect the coffin. In the afternoon, the funeral is held at the Dianke Office.
As a posthumous gift, he became a regular attendant of Sanqi, and his name was Mi.
His son's name was Li Shi, who had a good reputation. He reached the rank of servant and died in the early years of Xianhe.
Shi Chen said: Ziya served as an official in the court when he was young. He devoted his loyalty and efforts to serving the country. He extensively discussed the establishment of feudal states, which was in line with the times. He discussed the names of punishments in detail, and everything he discussed was suitable for the political system.
Although the words are not gorgeous and graceful, they must be reasonable.
Compared with the people of the Xijing era, he was not far away from Maiyi; compared with the people of Shu State, he surpassed Lang Chan.
During the period of Yuankang, the rebellious ministers and thieves were busy with the affairs of the court. The whole court was shocked and everyone was in peace. At this time, Liu Song was still loyal and unyielding. He cried bitterly for Zhang Gong's innocence and refused to make extravagances to the king of Zhao. Even the upright and famous officials in ancient times could not do this.
summary: Li Chong, courtesy name Maozeng, was born in Zhongwu, Jiangxia. His father, Li Jing, was governor of Qinzhou. Li Chong was studious and talented, becoming orphaned early and living with his younger brothers, known for his friendship. He discussed the nine-grade system, arguing it was a temporary military measure, not a long-term governance method. He advocated for simpler systems with fewer grades and long-term official positions. He opposed limiting slaves and property, arguing that without restoring the well-field system, such restrictions were impractical. He recommended promoting reclusive talents like Huo Yuan, emphasizing the importance of selecting virtuous people regardless of background. Li Chong served as Protector of Expeditions and Prefect of Pingyang, respecting moral education and promoting talents. After his brother's death, he resigned. He died of illness at age forty-eight, leaving his family poor with no place for his coffin. The historical commentary praised Liu Song for his loyalty, extensive discussions on feudal states, and refusal to compromise with the king of Zhao. Li Chong was commended for his integrity, uprightness, and recommendation of virtuous recluses. Both were considered cornerstones of the country.

translation:
Zheng Miao, courtesy name Uncle Lin, was a native of Kaifeng, Xingyang.
The great ancestor Zheng Zhong was the chief agricultural officer during the Han Dynasty.
His father, Zheng Tai, was the governor of Yangzhou during the Han Dynasty and had a good reputation.
Zheng Miao lost his father when he was young, and he was insightful and able to identify talents very early.
Xun You saw him and said, "Zheng Gongye seems to be still alive."
Zheng Miao fled to Jiangdong with his uncle Zheng Hun.
At that time, Hua Xin was the governor of Yuzhang, and Zheng Hun went to join him. Hua Xin had always been friendly with Zheng Tai and raised Zheng Miao as his own son.
Zheng Miao did not return to his hometown until he was seventeen years old.
Be an upright person.
At that time, Wei Xie, a native of Jiyin, was appointed as the prime minister of the country and was very famous. Ren Lan, who was in the same county as Zheng Yu, made friends with him.
Zheng Miao believed that Wei Xi was a traitor who would eventually cause disaster, and advised Ren Lan to stay away from him.
When Wei Xi was defeated, everyone who discussed it praised Zheng Mao.
When Emperor Wu of Wei first made his sons princes, he carefully selected their retainers and friends. Zheng Miao and Xu Qian both served as Marquis of Linzi, and later became Sili Gongcao.
Wang Lang of Sikong invited him to serve as subordinate officials. Zheng Mian recommended Xu Yun from Gaoyang, Lu Zhi from Fufeng, and Wang Ji from Donglai. Wang Lang appointed them all. Later, they all became high-ranking officials with high reputations.
Zheng Miao was promoted to Shangshu Lang.
Later, he was appointed as Li Yangling, and his subordinates and people were sincerely convinced.
The prefect evaluated subordinate officials. After screening, Zheng Miao stood out and was ranked first among the county magistrates.
He was promoted to Minister Youcheng.
He was appointed as the prefect of Jiyin. When he took office, he praised the filial and brotherly people, respected the talented and talented people, and established schools to educate the younger generations.
He was transferred to the rank of general to serve as a lieutenant and a regular attendant on the casual cavalry.
When there was a vacancy for the governor of Guangping, Emperor Xuan said to Zheng Miao: Your uncle will be a great craftsman. Zheng Hun will have a good reputation in Yangping and Wei counties, and the people will be favored and influenced.
Moreover, Lu Zisai and Wang Ziyong continued to manage this county, so that there was no shortage of virtuous people from generation to generation, so I asked you to serve again.
When Zheng Miao was in Guangping, he put education first and was good at using laws and regulations to manage people. The people loved him.
He was recruited as a servant, and the people respected him and were reluctant to let him go. They cried and saw him off by the roadside.
Promoted to Shaofu.
When Gaogui Xianggong came to the throne, Zheng Miao and his mother Yin Wangsheng prepared chariots and horses to greet him in Yuanqiu, and granted him the title of Marquis of Ludantai.
He was appointed Guang Luxun and led Zongzheng.
Guanqiu Jian made a rebellion, and Emperor Jing personally conquered it. Hundreds of officials gathered in the city to offer sacrifices to him as a road god to see him off. Zheng Miao was ill and could not arrive.
Emperor Jing said to Wang Su, the leader of the army: It's just a pity that I didn't see Yinmao.
Wang Su told Zheng Miao, and Zheng Miao personally drove the car to chase Emperor Jing and caught up with him not far away.
Emperor Jing smiled and said: I knew you would definitely come like Hou Sheng.
So he and Zheng Miao rode in the car together and asked him: What strategy should I use first?
Zheng Miao replied: Li Qiujian and I were both ministers in the past, so I knew him very well.
This person likes strategies but does not know the truth. Since his past achievements in Youzhou, his ambitions and desires are unlimited.
Wen Qin is brave but has no plans.
Now the king's army was surprised, and the Jiang and Huai soldiers were energetic but unable to hold on. We dug deep ditches and built high fortresses to dampen their enthusiasm. This is what Yafuqu is best at.
Emperor Jing agreed.
summary: Zheng Miao, a native of Kaifeng, lost his father young and was raised by his uncle Zheng Hun. Known for his insight, he warned Ren Lan to avoid Wei Xie, who later caused disaster. He served as an official under Emperor Wu of Wei, recommended talents like Xu Yun, and governed with education and law, earning the people's love. During Guanqiu Jian's rebellion, he advised Emperor Jing to use defensive tactics. He declined high positions multiple times, eventually becoming Sikong, and died at eighty-five. His son Zheng Mo served as Tingwei, known for integrity and opening granaries during famine, and was posthumously honored.

translation:
Your Majesty is a wise man who manages all matters day by day, issues many edicts, and follows ancient laws. Even though Tang and Yu visited and asked for help, Zhou's writings were rigorous, but he could not catch up.
From now on, when there are important matters in the country, you can personally summon the princes to ask for the correct advice.
When encountering difficulties, it can be extended to Taiwan Province and let the ministers and ministers express their opinions.
If you are ill and do not come, you can temporarily send a close minister to inquire. The emperor issued an edict and agreed.
He was promoted to the position of Pushe, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and soon he was promoted to Prince Shaofu.
Because of his high integrity, he was appointed as the captain of Sili School.
Li Yin repeatedly stated that he was worthy of being the prince's master and was not suitable to serve as a supervisor.
Emperor Wu believed that those holding these two positions must be loyal and wise, so he disagreed every time.
In the early years of Xianning, the crown prince came to live in the East Palace. Emperor Wu thought that the affairs of the Sili school captain were heavy, and the young master had to tutor the crown prince in the morning and evening. Li Yin had always been in weak health and should not be tired for a long time, so he was changed to serve in the imperial palace and was promoted to special rank.
Soon he was appointed as the Minister of Secretariat, and Shizhong and Tejin remained as before.
Although Li Yin had held official positions inside and outside the court, his family was very poor and frugal. His son was sick and had no money to buy medicine.
When Emperor Wu heard about it, he rewarded him with a hundred thousand yuan.
Later, Emperor Wu believed that there was a Situ in the position of prime minister in the past, and Li Yin was appointed Situ in Xia Shao.
He has been in office for five years, and he is quiet, prudent and very competent.
On the grounds that Wu Hui had just been pacified and many ministers had meritorious service and should be promoted, Shangshu requested to resign.
Emperor Wu refused to listen and sent his servants to announce the decree. He refused to go to the throne and issued a thick edict to urge him.
Li Yin had no choice but to come out to deal with political affairs.
When Taikang passed away in the third year of his life, Emperor Wu issued an edict to send censors to monitor the funeral procession and mourn him, and the title of Mi was established.
The crown prince asked Wang Zan, the prince of the family, to write a condolence article. The writing style and content were very beautiful.
Emperor Wu later remembered Li Yin's noble integrity and told Shao: The late Situ Li Yin, Taichang Peng Guan, was loyal, noble and frugal. After his death, his family had no money left. He rewarded Li Yin's family with two million yuan and one thousand dendrobiums of grain, while Peng Guan's family was given half of it.
Three sons: Li Gu, Li Zhenchang, and Li Xiu.
Li Gu, whose courtesy name was Wanji, served as a Sanqi Lang. He died before Li Yin, and his son Li Zhi inherited the title.
Li Zhi, whose courtesy name was Yandao, served successively as Minister of Sanqi, General Jianwei, and Grand Administrator of Yangping.
Chief Li Zhen arrives at Taipuqing.
Li Xiu was appointed as Huangmen's minister and his concubine.
Lu Qin, named Ziruo, was from Fanyang Zhuo.
His grandfather Lu Zhi was a minister during the Han Dynasty.
His father, Lu Yu, served as Sikong during the Wei Dynasty.
Confucianism has been prominent for generations.
summary: Li Yin, from Liaodong, was famed for filial piety, mourning his lost grandfather and father. He served as a fair official, enforcing laws strictly, and was appointed Situ. Despite poverty, he refused gifts, and after his death, his family had no savings. His son Li Gu died early, and his grandson Li Zhi inherited the title.

translation:
Lu Qin was indifferent and far-sighted, specializing in classics and history. He was promoted as a filial and honest man. However, if he did not leave, Cao Shuang, the general of Wei, recruited him as a subordinate official.
Cao Shuang's younger brother once had some instructions. Lu Qin told them that they should act in accordance with the law. Cao Shuang strongly agreed and punished his younger brother.
Served as Shangshu Lang.
Cao Shuang was killed and Lu Qin was dismissed from office.
Later, he became a censor, inherited his father's title of Marquis of Daliting, and was promoted to the prefect of Langxie many times.
When Emperor Xuan was appointed as Taifu, he was recruited as a Zhonglang and was appointed as Yangping Prefect. He was promoted to the governor of Huaibei and the general of Fubo. He had great political achievements.
He was recruited as a regular servant of Sanqi and a great minister of agriculture. He was promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and was granted the title of Marquis of Liang Dynasty.
