Emperor Wu accepted the concession and appointed Lu Qin as the commander-in-chief of all the military forces in Mianbei, General Pingnan, and Jiejie. He also gave Zhuifeng Tao a sleeping chariot each, two horses for the second son-in-law, riding equipment, knives, mirrors and armor for the imperial men, horses, etc., as well as 300,000 yuan in money.
Lu Qin was generous and fierce in the military town, and the border areas were safe and sound.
He was summoned to serve as a servant of the minister, a servant, a captain of the chariot, and the leader of the official department.
Because he was poor, he was given a hundred pieces of silk.
Lu Qin is a talented person and enjoys the reputation of being honest and fair.
Xianning died in the fourth year. The edict said: Lu Qin followed the right path and was honest and upright.
Excellent in both civil and military affairs, he is famous in China.
Keep secrets in hand and be fair in dealing with matters.
Work diligently both internally and externally, and do your best.
I am devastated by his tragic passing.
As a posthumous gift to General Wei and the three divisions of Kaifu Yitong, he was given a coffin, a set of court clothes, a piece of regular clothes, 50 pieces of cloth, and 300,000 yuan in money.
Mi Hao Yuan.
Because Lu Qin was loyal and noble, and did not run any property. After his death, his family had no real estate, so he was given a special reward of 500,000 yuan to build a house.
He also issued an edict saying: The late King Ji of Sikong, General Lu Qin of the Wei Army, and Yang Xiao, the general of the Lingdian Army, have always been poor. After their deaths, their families had no money left.
There has been a famine in Zha recently, and I heard that these families were particularly in need, so each of them was given three hundred dendrobiums of grain.
Lu Qin served as a local official successively, not advocating fame, but only aiming at fair governance.
The salary is distributed to relatives and old friends, and the family property is not managed.
According to the etiquette and regulations, the wife passed away, built a shabby house, and completed the mourning outside.
He has written dozens of poems, poems and essays, and the title of the book is "Xiao Dao".
Heir to son Louvre.
Lufu, whose courtesy name is Ziyun, first gave up his life to the prince.
A poisonous sore on his hand was amputated, leaving him disabled.
But the imperial court valued him very much and asked him to serve as a doctor of the imperial family, a wine minister, and a secretary-supervisor, but he refused.
Lu Qin's younger brother Lu Jue, also known as Zihu, was appointed as Weiweiqing.
Lu Jin, the son of Lu Cui.
Lu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Zidao, was initially recruited as a public official and a minister, and later served as Yeling.
summary: Lu Qin, from Fanyang, was a Confucian scholar who served as a local official, focusing on fair governance and not managing property. He was appointed General Pingnan, securing borders, and died in Xianning. His family was so poor that the emperor granted funds for a house. His son Lu Fu declined high offices due to disability.

translation:
When they arrived in Luoyang, they encountered Pingchang Company Ma Mo sent forward to protect Feng Song to resist Sima Ying.
Sima Ying returned to Chang'an. Before she arrived, she heard that Sima Ji had killed Zhang Fang and asked Sima Yue for peace.
Sima Ying lived in Huayin. Lu Zhi arrived in Chang'an, entered the palace to apologize, and immediately went to Wuguan to meet Sima Ying.
He fled to Nanyang, but was driven back to Hebei by Liu Tao.
When Sima Ying died, the officials and his family fled, and only Lu Zhi personally attended the funeral. People at that time praised him.
Sima Yue appointed Lu Zhi as a military counselor and offered wine, and was promoted to Weiwei. In the last years of Yongjia, he was appointed minister.
Luoyang fell, and Lu Zhi led his wife and children to the north to join Liu Kun, the governor of Bingzhou.
When he arrived in Yangyi, he was captured by Liu Can and killed in Pingyang together with his second sons Lu Mi and Lu Jiu.
The eldest son Lu Chen.
Lu Chen, whose courtesy name is Ziliang, has a clear mind, quick wit and insights. He likes "Lao" and "Zhuang" and is good at writing articles.
He married Princess Rongyang, the daughter of Emperor Wu, and served as Prince Consort, but the princess died before the marriage was consummated.
Later, he was promoted to scholar in the state and conscripted into Taiwei.
When Luoyang fell, he followed Lu Zhi to the north and attached himself to Liu Kun. He and Lu Zhi were captured by Liu Can.
Liu Can occupied Jinyang and left Lu Chen to join the army.
Liu Kun gathered some scattered troops and led Yi Lu's cavalry to attack Liu Can.
Liu Can was defeated and Lu Chen was able to return to Liu Kun. His parents and brothers who were in Pingyang were all killed by Liu Cong.
Liu Kun was appointed Sikong, with Lu Chen as chief clerk, and was appointed as Zhonglang.
Liu Kun's wife was Lu Chen's aunt. She loved him and valued his talents and family status.
In the last years of Jianxing, he followed Liu Kun to Duan Pichan.
Duan Pichen occupied Youzhou exclusively, with Lu Chen as his chariot.
Duan Pi Tan was defeated soon after he killed Liu Kun.
At that time, the road to the south was blocked, Duan Mobo was in western Liaoning, and Lu Chen went to join him.
In the early years of the Yuan Dynasty, Duan Mobo exchanged envoys with the Jin Dynasty. Lu Chen's envoy petitioned for Liu Kun, and the text was profound, so the court offered condolences and sacrifices.
Lu Chen was recruited many times as the Minister of Sanqi Zhongshu, but was retained by Duan Mobo and was not allowed to cross south.
Duan Mobo died and his younger brother Duan Liao succeeded to the throne. Lu Chen lived in a foreign country for nearly twenty years.
Shi Jilong conquered Liaoxi, and Lu Chen was captured by Shi Jilong. He was appointed as the minister of Zhongshu, the prince of the state, the minister of Zhongshu, and the supervisor of Zhongshu.
Ran Min killed Shi, and Lu Chen followed Ran Min's army and was killed in Xiangguo. He was sixty-seven years old. That was the sixth year of Yonghe.
Lu Chen was the son of a famous family. He had long had a reputation for his high talents and cleanliness, and was highly respected by people at the time.
At the time of the war in the Central Plains, Cui Yue from Qinghe, Xun Chuo from Jiechuan, Pei Xian from Hedong, and Fu Chang from Beidi were all trapped in foreign countries. Although they were very prominent in the later Zhao Dynasty, they were always ashamed of it.
President Lu Chen said to his sons: After my death, I will only be called Sikong Zhonglang of Jin Dynasty.
He wrote "Sacrifice", commented on "Zhuangzi", and collected essays, all of which have been passed down to the world.
Cui Yue, courtesy name Taoist, was the great-grandson of Wei Sikong Cui Ta and Liu Kun's nephew.
Together with Lu Chen, he worked as a lieutenant in Xingxi Sikong, and later served as Kengui Zhezuo Shi.
summary: Lu Zhi, Lu Qin's nephew, served as a strategist for Sima Ying, advising against rebellion and later escorting the emperor to Luoyang. He was captured and killed by Liu Can. His son Lu Chen, a talented writer, was captured by Shi Jilong and died in Xiangguo, leaving works like "Sacrifice" and commentaries.

translation:
If you fall into Pengzhao, you will also become a high official.
There are other biographies in the books of Baozhong, Xian and Chang.
Huabiao, whose courtesy name is Weirong, was from Gaotang, Pingyuan. His father, Hua Xin, was of noble character and served as Wei Taiwei.
When Huabiao was twenty years old, he was appointed as a Sanqi Huangmenlang and was promoted to the rank of Attendant several times.
In the early years of the Zhengyuan Dynasty, Shi Bao came to the court and praised Gaogui Xiang Gong, thinking that Wei Wu was reborn.
Everyone present was sweating profusely at that time. Hua Biao was afraid of the impending disaster and repeatedly said that he had to go home because he was ill, so he was spared the disaster.
Later he was promoted to minister.
He was given a fifth-class title and named Guanyang Bo.
Because the supplies for the funeral were not complete, he was dismissed from office.
During the Taishi period, he was appointed Prince Shaofu, changed his post to Guang Luxun, and was promoted to Taichang Qing.
A few years later, he requested to retire due to old age and illness.
The edict said: He is pure and upright, has good conduct, and has the beauty of maturity. He has handled government affairs for many years and dare not slack off.
He requested to retire due to serious illness and his attitude was sincere.
Now let him grant what he asked for, and he will be rewarded with a reward of 200,000 yuan by the Taizhong doctor. The bed, tent, mat, and seat will be the same as those of Jiuqing, and a wooden fence will be set up in front of the door to block the passage of people and horses.
Known for his unswerving determination, Situ Li Yin, Sili Wang Hong and others all lamented the indifference and tranquility of Jianzhi, and believed that distance should not be determined by high or low.
He died in August of the first year of Xianning at the age of seventy-two. Mi was named Chen and was given imperial robes by imperial edict.
He has six sons: Hua Du, Hua Cen, Hua Wei, Hua Jian, Hua Dan and Hua Jian.
Hua Hao, whose courtesy name is Changjun, has a quick mind.
Father-in-law Lu Yu presided over the election and did not mention in-laws, so Hua Yu was not allowed to be an official at the age of thirty-five, and was appointed Zhongshu Tongshilang very late.
In the early years of Taishi's reign, he was promoted to redong servant servant.
He was treated politely by Genduo when he was young, and served successively as Huangmen Shilang, Sanqi Changshi, Qianjun General, Shizhong, Nanzhonglang General, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Hebei.
When his father was seriously ill, he returned home and died of illness. According to the old rule, one must return to one's post after the burial, but Jianxiang refused to return, violating the emperor's will.
At first, there were three guests in the district, so Hua Hao was sent to the county magistrate Yuan Yi to register his name, and the three guests were all used as slaves.
When Yuan Yi was convicted of bribery, the verdict document was confusing and absurd. It no longer stated that slaves were used as guests, but directly said that three slaves were sent to Jiyu, and Yuan Yi was also the son-in-law of the Lu family.
Furthermore, Zhongshu Jian Baoxi once asked Hua Fu to marry his daughter on behalf of his son. Because he did not agree, he held a grudge, so he secretly reported to the emperor that there were too many people who had given bribes and they could not all be punished. The closest person should be punished, so he suggested that Hua Yu would be suitable.
summary: Hua Biao, from Gaotang, served as Taichang Qing, retiring due to illness. His son Hua Yu was dismissed for violating mourning rules but later restored. Hua Heng, Hua Yu's son, served as Taichang, establishing ritual systems after wars, and died in poverty with only books.

translation:
In previous generations, banquets were held to show the importance of the three princes when they were enthroned.
Since the end of the Wei Dynasty, it has no longer been implemented.
By the time of Shijian, Shao Ling was restored and became a system.
In the last years of Taikang, he was appointed Sikong and served as the crown prince and tutor.
When Emperor Wu died, Shi Jian and Zhang Shao, the Central Guardsman, supervised the tomb.
At that time, Grand Sima and Runan King Sima Liang were suspected by Taifu Yang Jun and did not dare to go to express condolences and stationed outside the city.
At this time, someone reported that Sima Liang wanted to send troops to attack Yang Jun. Yang Jun was very frightened and asked the Queen Mother to order the emperor to write the Shao Shu personally, and ordered Shi Jian and Zhang Shao to lead the soldiers guarding the mausoleum to attack Sima Liang.
Zhang Shao was Yang Jun's nephew, so he led his troops to urge Shi Jian to send troops quickly. Shi Jian thought that this would not be the case, so he held his troops back and sent someone to spy on Sima Liang. Sima Liang had returned to Xuchang by another way, so Yang Jun stopped his action, and everyone who discussed it praised Shi Jian.
After guarding the mausoleum, he was granted the title of Marquis of Chang'an County.
In the early years of Yuankang, he was appointed Taiwei.
In his eighties, impassioned, he thought of himself as a teenager: people praised him.
He died soon after and was named Yuan.
His son, Shi Chou, had a lowly character, inherited the title, and served as the captain of the Tunqi School.
Wen Xian, also known as Changqing, was a native of Qi, Taiyuan, and a descendant of Wen Xu, the captain of the Han Qiang School.
His grandfather Wen Hui was the governor of Yangzhou during the Wei Dynasty.
His father Wen Gong served as the prefect of Jinan.
The six brothers are famous all over the world and are known as the "Six Dragons".
Wen Xian was famous for his intelligence when he was young. King Sima You of Qi recruited him as a subordinate official and was promoted to Shangshu Lang.
Emperor Hui ascended the throne and was appointed governor of Yuzhou. He was recruited as a regular servant of Sanqi and was promoted to minister several times.
When Sima Jian, King of Qi, assisted in the administration, because Wen Xian was Sima You's old subordinate and was particularly close to him, he was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
It turned out that Zhang Hua was killed, and Ji suggested that his title be reinstated.
Someone raised an objection, and Shi Xian retorted: From the time of the Emperor of Heaven onwards, the admonishment officials all have their faults, and they cannot be blamed on one person.
Therefore King Lei said: If someone is not close to him, who can bear it if he dies for himself?
Rick killed the two concubines, Chen Qi established Yangsheng, and the Han Dynasty killed the Lu family, but it took many years for them to establish their affairs.
No one can do whatever they want within a few months while the victim is still alive.
At the meeting in Shiqian Hall, Zhang Hua was the only one to give advice.
The prime ministers are at odds and cannot take advantage of the situation to promote good deeds. Isn't it difficult to expect Zhang Hua to command them to follow closely?
Moreover, now the queen only framed the prince and did not take part in the internal trouble, so she was ignorant of etiquette.
Moreover, the queen and the emperor are one and the same, and they respect the same emperor. Her crime is to frame the prince, which is not considered treason, and according to etiquette, she should not be attacked.
Now it is unreasonable to equate Zhang Hua's failure to depose the queen who framed the prince with Zhao Dun's failure to attack the thief who killed the king, and to belittle and condemn him.
Zhang Hua was eventually able to regain his title.
Later, he served as a servant in the campaign against Sima Ying, the king of Chengdu, and was granted the title of Duke of Daling County, with a settlement of 1,800 households.
He was appointed as the governor of Jizhou and later became a general. Fanyang King Sima Rao defeated Xuchang and took charge of Jizhou himself, but Wen Xian avoided him.
When Emperor Hui went to Chang'an, he appointed Wen Xian as his official secretary, but he refused to go.
When Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang, he was recruited as the supervisor of the Zhongshu, and he was appointed as a regular attendant on casual cavalry.
Before the appointment, Emperor Hui died and Emperor Huai ascended the throne. He was appointed doctor Zuo Guanglu, opened the mansion, and led the Situ. People commented that he was promoted too quickly.
He died of illness shortly after taking office and was given to Situ as a gift. Mi was given the title Yuan.
He has three sons: Wen Zhi, Wen Yun and Wen Yu.
Shizhi was named Jingqi and was appointed as Taifu Xicao.
Shiyun's courtesy name was Jingxian, and he was appointed as the prince's wife.
Shiyu, courtesy name Jingsi, married the eldest princess of Wu'an and became the official of Zuo Guanglu.
Shi Chen said: In the middle of the Jin Dynasty, the achievements of several generations were inherited, the great cause of unification was established, and there were many talents and wise men.
These few people either live in Taiwan Province because of their reputation, or they become the prince's master because of their high reputation. They are not talents for a while, so how can they be like this.
summary: Shi Jian, from Leling, was a fair official who corrected abuses. He was dismissed for false reports but later restored as Sikong. During Yang Jun's crisis, he refused to attack Sima Liang, earning praise. He died as Taiwei. Wen Xian, from Taiyuan, was known for intelligence, serving as Minister of Personnel. He defended Zhang Hua's title after his death, arguing against unfair condemnation. He died as Zuo Guanglu Doctor, leaving three sons.

translation:
Jia Chong, whose courtesy name was Gonglu, was from Xiangling, Pingyang.
His father, Jia Kui, was the governor of Yuzhou in Wei and the Marquis of Yangliting.
Jia Kui gave birth to Jia Chong in his later years. He said that in the future there would be joyful celebrations filling the streets, so he named Jia Chong and Jia Chong.
Jia Chong lost his father when he was young, and he was famous for his filial piety in mourning.
The Marquis who succeeded his father.
The official paid homage to Shangshu Lang, who presided over the assignment of imperial orders and held examination classes at the same time.
Analyze the rules and regulations of the classics and chapters, and apply them in work.
After his meritorious service, he was moved to serve as Huangmen Shilang and Jijun Diannong Zhonglang.
He participated in the general's military affairs and followed Emperor Jing in the campaign against his mothers Qiu Jian and Wen Qin in Lejia.
The emperor was seriously ill and returned to Xuchang, leaving Jia Chong to supervise the military affairs. Because of his meritorious service, 350 additional households were granted fiefs.
Later he was appointed Sima, the general of Emperor Wen, and was transferred to You Changshi.
Emperor Wen had just taken over the power of the imperial court. He was afraid that there would be objections from the border towns in the four directions, so he sent his aides to Zhuge Dan to discuss preparations for the attack on Wu and secretly observe the changes.
After Jia Chonglun talked about the current situation, he took advantage of the situation and said to Zhuge Xi: "Everyone in the world hopes to take over the throne. What do you think?"
Zhuge Dan said sternly: "Aren't you the son of Jia Yuzhou? You have been favored by Wei for generations, how can you want to hand over the country to others!"
If there is trouble in Luoyang City, I will die for Wei.
Maichong remained silent.
When he returned to Beijing, he told Emperor Wen: "Zhuge Dan has been stationed in Yangzhou twice. His majesty and reputation have always been outstanding, and he can win the desperate service of others."
Observing his planning and strategy, it is certain to rebel.
If he is drafted, it will prompt him to rebel with little harm; if he is not drafted, the rebellion will be delayed but the harm will be great.
Emperor Wen then recruited Zhuge Dan to serve as Sikong, but Zhuge Dan rebelled.
Maichong followed Zhuge Dan in the expedition and offered a plan: Chu soldiers are lightly armed but sharp. If they dig deep ditches and build high forts to approach the rebel city, they can win without a fight.
Emperor Wen obeyed him.
After conquering the city, Emperor Wen ascended the fortress to comfort Jia Chong.
Emperor Wen first returned to Luoyang and sent Jia Chong to take charge of the funeral affairs. He was promoted to the title of Marquis of Xuanyang Township, and a thousand households were added to the fiefdom.
After being moved to the post of Tingwei, Jia Chong was very good at jurisprudence and had a reputation for correcting wrong cases.
After he was transferred to the Central Guards Army, when Gaogui Xianggong attacked the Prime Minister's Mansion, Jia Chong led the people to fight at Nanque.
The army was about to be defeated. Prince Sheren Chengji, the younger brother of Cavalry Governor Cheng Chou, said to Maichong: What should we do today?
Maichong said: I have raised you people just for today, so what is there to worry about?
Cheng Ji then drew his gun and attacked Gao Gui's carriage.
When the Duke of Changdao came to the throne, he was granted the title of Marquis of Anyang Township. He was granted an additional 1,200 households, commanded the armies outside the city, and was appointed as a regular attendant on casual cavalry.
Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu. Emperor Wen ordered Jia Chongzhijie to supervise the military affairs of Guanzhong and Longyou as his own officer, and moved westward to occupy Hanzhong. Zhong Hui died before he could reach him.
At that time, the army and the country were troubled, and Jia Chong was involved in the planning of the court's secrets.
Emperor Wen trusted and valued Jia Chong very much, and together with Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, Yang Ku, and Xun Xu, he accepted the important tasks of his confidants.
Emperor Wen also ordered Jia Chong to revise the law.
summary: Jia Chong, courtesy name Gonglu, was from Xiangling, Pingyang. His father, Jia Kui, served as Governor of Yuzhou under Wei and was the Marquis of Yangliting. Jia Kui fathered Jia Chong in his later years, naming him "Chong" (meaning "fill") in anticipation of future joyful celebrations filling the streets. Jia Chong lost his father young and was renowned for his filial piety in mourning. He succeeded his father's marquisate and began his official career as Shangshu Lang, where he analyzed classical rules and regulations for his work. He later held positions including Huangmen Shilang and Jijun Diannong Zhonglang. Jia Chong participated in military campaigns under Emperor Jing against Qiu Jian and Wen Qin at Lejia. When the emperor fell ill and returned to Xuchang, Jia Chong was left to supervise military affairs, earning an additional 350 households in his fief. He later served as Sima under Emperor Wen and was transferred to You Changshi. Emperor Wen, newly in power, sent Jia Chong to Zhuge Dan under the pretext of discussing plans to attack Wu, but actually to observe his intentions. During their conversation, Jia Chong hinted at the possibility of a dynastic change, but Zhuge Dan sternly rebuked him, declaring his loyalty to Wei. Jia Chong reported to Emperor Wen that Zhuge Dan would surely rebel, advising that summoning him would trigger a minor rebellion, while delay would cause greater harm. Emperor Wen summoned Zhuge Dan as Sikong, and Zhuge Dan indeed rebelled. Jia Chong accompanied the expedition and proposed a strategy of digging deep moats and building high forts to besiege the rebels without battle, which succeeded. After the city fell, Jia Chong was promoted to Marquis of Xuanyang Township with an additional 1,000 households. He became Tingwei, known for correcting wrongful cases, then Central Guards Army commander. When Gaogui Xianggong attacked the Prime Minister's Mansion, Jia Chong led troops at Nanque. As his forces faltered, Cheng Ji asked what to do, and Jia Chong replied, "I have raised you for just this day." Cheng Ji then killed Gaogui Xianggong. Under the new emperor, Jia Chong was made Marquis of Anyang Township with 1,200 additional households, commanding城外 armies. When Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu, Jia Chong was sent to supervise Guanzhong and Longyou, but Zhong Hui died before his arrival.

translation:
Use the gold medal to get the first high-class house.
The fifth-class title was just established and he was named Marquis of Linyi. As a person with great meritorious service in the Jin Dynasty, he was deeply favored and treated with special treatment. His salary and rewards were often better than those of other officials.
Jia Chong had the talent of writing and writing, and could observe the will from above.
At the beginning, Emperor Wen used Emperor Jing Hongda to assist the king and was about to pass the throne to Wuyang Hou Sima You.
Maichong praised Emperor Wu for being generous and kind, and as the eldest son, he had the virtues to be a king and should inherit the throne.
When Emperor Wen was ill and lying in bed, Emperor Wu asked about his funeral.
Emperor Wen said: It is Jia Gonglu who understands you.
Emperor Wu succeeded to the throne and worshiped Jia Chong as General of the Guards of the Jin Dynasty, the Third Division of Yitong, and the title of Marquis of Linying.
After accepting the transfer, Jia Chong was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Regular Attendant of Disciplined Cavalry, and Minister of Public Affairs because of his participation in establishing the destiny of a prosperous country.
After the promulgation of the new law on buying and selling, people felt convenient.
The edict said: Since the Han Dynasty, the laws have been strict.
Therefore, from the time of Emperor Moyuan and Emperor Cheng of Han Dynasty to Jian'an and Jiaping, everyone wanted to analyze the old laws and regulations, delete and reform the criminal law.
Due to the grand scale of the work, it took many years without success.
The late emperor took pity on the kind-hearted people trapped in the fine legal net, and personally spoke out the voice of benevolence and corrected the name and reality.
The generals of chariots and cavalry buy and charge, assist in spreading the holy will, and consult the good way.
Taifu Zheng Chong, together with Sikong Xunhao, Zhongshu Supervisor Xunxu, Central Army General Yang Ku, Central Guardsman Wang Ye, Tingwei Du You, Henan Guard Yin Duyu, Sanqi Minister Pei Kai, Ying! Prefect Zhou Xiong, Qi Prime Minister Guo Qi, Cavalry Commander Chenggong Sui Xunhui, Shangshu Lang Liugui, etc. presided over this matter.
Every time I see their hard work, I always praise them with emotion.
Now that the law has been completed and has begun to be promulgated throughout the world, the penalties are relaxed and the prohibitions are simplified, which is enough to comply with the original decree.
In the past, Xiao He was granted a title for revising laws, and Shusun Tong was appointed as a regular official for formulating etiquette. He was given five hundred catties of gold, and his disciples were all Langguan.
Establishing meritorious deeds and completing careers was valued in ancient times.
Taifu Bai, Chaqiu and below are all rewarded with salary and salary, and the detailed procedures are in accordance with the old regulations.
So one of Jia Chong's children was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and five hundred pieces of silk.
Jia Chong firmly refused, but the emperor refused.
Later, he replaced Pei Xiu as Shangshu Ling, and his positions as regular attendant and general of chariots and cavalry remained.
Soon he was changed from regular servant to servant, and was given 700 pieces of silk.
He left his job due to his mother's death, and Shaoshu sent Huangmen Shilang to express his condolences.
Because there was something going on in the southeast, he sent General Yang Xiao of the Dian Army to read out the decree and asked Maichong to return to the court after sixty days.
summary: Jia Chong was deeply trusted by Emperor Wen, revising laws alongside Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, Yang Ku, and Xun Xu. He received the highest-class house and was named Marquis of Linyi. Initially, Emperor Wen considered passing the throne to Wuyang Hou Sima You, but Jia Chong praised Emperor Wu's virtues as the eldest son, convincing him to choose Emperor Wu. Upon Emperor Wu's succession, Jia Chong became General of the Guards of Jin, Yitong Sansi, and Marquis of Linying. He was later promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Regular Attendant, and Minister of Public Affairs for his role in establishing the dynasty. Jia Chong oversaw the revision of laws, which were praised for their leniency and simplicity. The emperor rewarded him with a marquisate for one of his children and 500 bolts of silk, which Jia Chong declined but was overruled. He succeeded Pei Xiu as Shangshu Ling while retaining his other posts. After his mother's death, he was recalled from mourning after 60 days due to affairs in the southeast. He devoted himself to agricultural savings and streamlining officials, earning imperial praise. Jia Chong recommended talents and treated others with sincerity, though he lacked integrity and relied on flattery, earning hatred from upright officials like Ren Kai and Yu Chun.

translation:
He was fully in power, devoted himself to saving money in agriculture, merged officials and reduced provincial positions, and the emperor praised him. And because civil and military forces have their own specialties, he requested that the soldiers under his command be dismissed.
When Yang Hu and others went out to guard the area, the imperial seal office came forward to perform meritorious service on the border, but the emperor did not agree.
He takes office calmly, praises and blames himself, and likes to recommend talents. Whenever he is recommended, he will make arrangements from beginning to end, so many scholars attach themselves to him.
The emperor's uncle Wang Xun had slandered Jia Chong, and Zhi Li promoted him to Wang Gu.
Sometimes there are people who play tricks on powerful people behind Maili's back, but Jia Chong treats them with sincerity on the surface.
However, Jia Chong did not have integrity and impartiality, could not correct himself and set an example for his subordinates, and relied exclusively on flattery to please others.
Ren Kai, the servant, Yu Chun, the secretary, and others were upright and upright, and they all hated him.
And because Ma Chong's daughter became Princess Qi, she may become even more powerful in the future.
When the Di and Qiang rebelled, the emperor was very worried about this, so he made a request to send Maichong to guard Guanzhong.
So he issued an edict saying: The two borders of Qin and Liang have suffered repeated defeats in successive years. The barbarians indulged in atrocities and the people suffered.
As a result, foreigners were encouraged and disasters spread to the Central Plains.
Even the invasion by Wu and Shu did not reach this extent.
It is really because the officials in office are not enough to appease the Yixia internally and suppress the rebellion externally. They use troops rashly and cannot fully exert their strength.
If we don't appoint our trusted ministers, entrust them with important responsibilities to achieve success, and completely correct the original shortcomings, I'm afraid there will be no end to the disaster.
Whenever I think of the disaster at the border, I forget to eat or sleep.
He is a servant, a guardian of the ministerial order, a general of chariots and cavalry. He has extraordinary magnanimity and far-reaching knowledge. His martial arts have the majesty of repelling the enemy. His literature has the wisdom to govern the country. His integrity can unite people's hearts. His reputation is powerful abroad.
Assign him to shoulder the important task of commanding one side and stabilizing Xixia. Then I will not have to worry about the worries of the west, and everyone near and far will be safe.
Jia Chong was appointed as envoy Chijie and commander-in-chief of the military affairs of the two states of Qin and Liang. His positions as servant and general of chariots and cavalry remained unchanged, and he was given Yu Bao, Guang Zhang, and the first prince consort.
The virtuous people in the court who wanted to be loyal, admonishing, and speaking out were all grateful for Jia Chong's transfer and looked forward to the great enlightenment.
Since Jia Chong was sent out to serve, he felt that he had neglected his duties. He deeply resented Ren Kai and had nothing to do.
When he was about to go to the border town, hundreds of officials bid farewell to him at the Sunset Pavilion, and Xun Xu had a private conversation with him.
Jia Chong told him his worries, and Xun Xu said: "My lord, he is the prime minister of the country, but he is restrained by one person. Isn't it too contemptuous of others!"
However, this time out, it was too difficult to say no. As long as you marry the prince, you can stay without any trouble.
Jia Chong said: That's right.
summary: When Di and Qiang rebelled, Jia Chong was sent to guard Guanzhong as commander of Qin and Liang provinces. However, through Xun Xu's influence, his daughter was married to the crown prince, allowing him to remain in the capital. During the campaign to conquer Wu, Jia Chong was appointed supreme commander but was reluctant, fearing failure. He repeatedly advised against the campaign, but the emperor insisted. After Wu's surrender, Jia Chong was heavily rewarded but felt ashamed of his lack of strategy. He died in the third year of Taikang at age 66, receiving grand posthumous honors.

translation:
The funeral followed the precedents of Huo Guang and Anping King Xian, and an area of ​​​​area was given to the cemetery.
He, Shi Bao and others were enshrined in the royal ancestral temple for their meritorious service in assisting the emperor. Their nickname was Wu.
He gave a posthumous gift to Maichong's son Li Min, who was named Duke Shang of Lu.
Jia Chong's wife, Guo Huai, the king of Guangcheng, was jealous by nature.
Back then, when Li Min was three years old, his wet nurse was holding him in front of the door.
When Li Min saw Maichong coming in, he smiled happily, and Jia Chong went over to caress him.
Guo Huai saw it and said that the wet nurse who bought Chongyu was having an affair, so he whipped the wet nurse to death.
The people missed their wet nurse and she fell ill and died.
Later, Guo Huai gave birth to another boy. When he was over one year old, he was held by the wet nurse again, and she touched the child's head with her hands.
Guo suspected the wet nurse and killed her again. Her son also died because he missed her.
Maichong therefore had no descendants.
After Jia Chong's death, Guo Huai made his grandson Han Mi the son of a commoner and continued to buy and charge.
The doctor ordered Han Xian and the lieutenant Cao Zhen to advise Guo Sou: According to the etiquette system, the authentic sect has no descendants, and the sons of the branches of the side sects are used as descendants. There is no provision for allowing descendants with different surnames.
Don't let the virtues of our late grandfather go underground, but let good historians record his faults. Wouldn't it be sad?
Guo Huai refused to obey.
Han Xian and others wrote a letter requesting a new heir, but the matter was suppressed and not reported.
Qianlu then stated in the table that it was Yishi's last wish to erect a fallen chariot.
The emperor went down to Shao and said: Dazai and Lu Gong Jia Chong, who upheld great virtues and established meritorious deeds, worked diligently to assist the destiny, passed away, and I always mourn them.
Besides, the heir died early and the descendants have not yet been established.
In ancient times, countries had no heirs and were succeeded by the branch of the person who initiated the title. However, in modern times, the feudal country was abolished.
As for Gong Dan in the Zhou Dynasty and Xiao He in the Han Dynasty, they either predetermined the eldest son or conferred a title on the Yuan concubine, which was a sign of respect for their merits, which was different from the norm.
Dazai always chose his grandson Han Mi as the descendant of his eldest son Li Min.
I have been thinking about it privately. My grandson is very close to me by flesh and blood, and it is in line with people's hearts to think about kindness.
Let Han Mi be the grandson of Lu Gong and inherit his feudal kingdom.
If the meritorious service is not the same as that of Dazai, and Shifeng has no descendants who are the same as Dazai, the descendants he chooses must be chosen by his own will, and may not be as good as Dazai. This example cannot be compared.
When the ceremonial officials agreed on Jia Chong's chanting, Dr. Qin Xiu suggested that Jia Chong be called Huang, but the emperor did not accept it.
Dr. Duan Chang catered to the emperor's wishes and suggested that Mi Haowao should be called Wu, and the emperor agreed.
From the time of Jia Chong's death to his burial, the funeral reward amounted to 20 million.
Emperor Hui ascended the throne, bought the throne and took exclusive power. He also gave Jia Chong the ancestral temple to have a band of six hundred people, and his mother Guo was the king of Yicheng.
After Guo's death, Mi's name was changed to Xuan, and special etiquette was specially added.
summary: Jia Chong's wife, Guo Huai, was extremely jealous, causing the deaths of two sons by killing their wet nurses. After Jia Chong's death, his grandson Han Mi was made heir. His daughter Jia Wu secretly married Han Shou after an affair, which Jia Chong discovered but concealed. Jia Chong's descendants, including Jia Mi, became powerful but were eventually killed during political turmoil. The text concludes with commentary on Jia Chong's flattery and lack of virtue, contrasting him with his brother Yang Yao, who foresaw disaster but could not avoid it.

translation:
Yang Hu Du Yu
Uncle Yang Hu was born in Nancheng, Mount Tai.
He has been an official of two thousand shi for generations, and he has been in Yanghu for nine generations. They are all famous for their integrity and virtue.
His grandfather, Yangxu, served as the prefect of Nanyang in Han Dynasty.
His father, Yang Gou, was appointed as the prefect of Shangdang.
Yang Hu is the grandson of Cai Yong and the younger brother of Queen Jingxian.
Yang Hu's father passed away when he was twelve years old. He obeyed filial piety more than etiquette and served his uncle Yang Dan with great respect.
Once when he was playing by the Wenshui River, he met an old man who said to him: This boy has good looks and is less than sixty years old. He will definitely make great achievements in the world.
After he left, no one knew where he was.
When he grew up, he was erudite and could write articles, and he was seven feet three inches tall. The man is handsome and good at talking.
Xiahou Wei, the general of the county, thought he was unusual and married his brother Xiahou Ba's daughter to him.
He was recommended as a planner, and he was called up four times to serve as an official or scholar in the state. He refused to take up the post in any of the five prefectures.
Guo Yi from Taiyuan saw him and said: This is Yan Hui today.
Both Wang Chen and Wang Chen were recruited by Cao Shuang.
Wang Chen persuaded him to apply, but Yang Hu said: It is not easy to entrust yourself to others to do things for others.
When Cao Shuang failed, Wang Chen survived as an old official, so he said to Yang Ku: "Always remember what you said before."
Yang Ku said: "It was not what I considered at the beginning."
He was so prescient and boastful.
Xiahou Ba surrendered to Shu, and his in-laws broke off all relations with him. Only Yang Hu got along with his wife calmly, and was more loving and courteous.
Soon his mother passed away, and his eldest brother Yangfa died again. He lived in mourning for more than ten years. He regarded himself as honest and honest, like a Confucian scholar.
Emperor Wen appointed him as a general and summoned Yang Hu, but he did not go. Instead, he was appointed as the Minister of Zhongshu in a public car, and soon he was promoted to Shizhong and Huangmenlang.
At that time, the prince of Gaogui County was fond of writing articles, and those in official positions often contributed poems and poems. Runan and Di were reprimanded for violating the emperor's wishes.
King Chenliu ascended the throne and granted him the title of Marquis of Guanzhong and the title of 100 households.
Because the young emperor was unwilling to serve as a minister, Yang Hu asked to leave the palace to find a position to fill the vacancy, and was appointed secretary supervisor instead.
When the fifth-level title was established, he was granted the title of Jupingzi and was granted the title of 600 households.
Zhong Hui is favored and jealous, and Yang Ku is also afraid of him.
Zhong Hui was executed and appointed as the Prime Minister of the country, Zhonglang, and jointly took charge of Zhongshu affairs with Xun Xu.
He was promoted to the leader of the central army, and all the guards were under his command. He was on duty in the palace, in charge of the imperial army, and took care of both inside and outside the palace.
Emperor Wu accepted the concession, and because of his assistance, Yang Hu was promoted to the rank of general of the central army. He was given the rank of casual cavalry and permanent attendants, and was granted the title of county prince, with a settlement of 3,000 households.
summary: Yang Hu, a native of Mount Tai, came from a lineage of high-ranking officials renowned for integrity. Orphaned at twelve, he was known for his filial piety and erudition, standing seven feet three inches tall with a handsome appearance and eloquence. He repeatedly declined official appointments, demonstrating foresight by avoiding service under Cao Shuang, whose subsequent downfall vindicated his caution. After his mother and brother died, he observed mourning for over a decade. He later served Emperor Wen as a palace attendant and was enfeoffed as a marquis. Fearing the favored Zhong Hui, he was relieved when Zhong was executed. Under Emperor Wu, he rose to general and marquis, but humbly declined higher titles. As commander in Jingzhou, he reduced border troops, opened schools, and won the loyalty of the people through sincerity and leniency toward defectors. He implemented agricultural policies that amassed a decade’s worth of grain reserves. Despite his relaxed demeanor, a military officer once blocked his unauthorized night outing, and Yang Hu accepted the reprimand. He repeatedly refused promotions, citing his lack of merit and fear of disgrace. His campaign to support Wu defector Bu Chan failed due to slow mobilization, leading to his demotion. He later built strategic cities, expanded farmland, and treated Wu soldiers with humanity, returning captives and compensating for requisitioned crops. His virtuous conduct so impressed Wu general Lu Kang that they exchanged envoys and medicine without suspicion. Yang Hu hated sycophants like Xun Xu and Feng Tong, and predicted that his nephew Wang Yan would corrupt morals. He advocated for conquering Wu, arguing that Sun Hao’s tyranny and Wu’s internal discord made victory certain. Despite opposition, he persisted, but died at fifty-eight before the campaign succeeded. His death caused widespread mourning, even among Wu soldiers. He was buried with honors, and his posthumous title reflected his humility. Two years later, Wu was pacified, and the emperor credited Yang Hu’s plans.

translation:
The late Grand Tutor and Marquis of Juping, Yang Hu, was of perfect virtue and virtuous. He was a person respected by the country. He had the merits of assisting the destiny of heaven and plotting to pacify Wu. However, he had no heirs and no sustenance for sacrifices.
Because Xiao He had great achievements in the Han Dynasty, he did not have any successors. I think the title of Marquis Juping should be the same as that of Deng Guo.
The late Taiwei Guangling Gongzhun favored the traitor Lun and caused harm to Huainan, because rebellion actually benefited him and he occupied a large fiefdom.
The laws and regulations of the Western Dynasty at that time were unfair, and the fiefdoms were not recovered after the ZTE.
Nowadays, the royal way is reforming, how can we not distinguish right from wrong. I think Guangling Kingdom should be eliminated.
The late Taibao Qianxing's title was originally the Duke of Miaoyang County. After the persecution, he was promoted to the title. He was first given Lanling as a gift, and then transferred to Jiangxia.
Many famous ministers in China and Korea were given unjustified gifts. Wei Guan's merits were not outstanding, but he only received great rewards. I think his fief should be recovered and restored to Leiyang. This would make the donation and withdrawal fair and distinguish between good and evil.
In the end there was no result.
Yang Hu's first mother was the daughter of Kong Rong, and she gave birth to her eldest brother Yang Shu, who became the governor of the Northern Guards.
At first, both Fu Deng and Guigu's half-brother Yu Cheng were ill. Yu La's mother considered that she could not take care of two people at the same time, so she concentrated on taking care of Yang Fa, and Yang Fa survived. And Yang Cheng finally died.
Yangfa's eldest son, Yanglun, has Gaoyang aspect.
Yang Lun's younger brother Yang Ji was the prefect of Kengai.
Yuji's younger brother, Shengyi, was initially a subordinate officer of the chariots and cavalry. Later, he served successively as General Pingnan, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Jiangbei, and guarded Wan. He was killed by Zhang Dan and posthumously promoted to General Zhennan.
Yang Nian's uncle, Feng Dian, was appointed as the prefect of Zhili.
His son Feng Cha is the prefect of the Silk School.
Yuncong's grandson is in charge, named Danxuan. He is talented and resourceful.
When someone interacts with him, he must pretend to be very warm and frank. People think they understand his heart, but this is not true at all.
At first, Taifu Yang Jun joined the army. At that time, there were many thefts in Jingzhao.
Zhihui planned to aggravate the criminal law. He would be sentenced to death for stealing a hundred coins, and asked the officials and family to discuss it together. Yang Liang said: In the past, Chu Jiang Yi's mother lost her cloth and thought that the theft was due to Ling Yin.
If the public has no selfish desires, thefts should naturally stop. Why should the criminal law be aggravated?
Yang Jun was ashamed and gave up.
Jiuliang was gradually promoted to Dahonglu.
At that time, Emperor Hui was in Tongdie. Locust and Gill Shu conspired. He felt uneasy and ran to Chaiye, where he was killed by Liu Yuanhai.
Jianhao's younger brother Fuidi was the governor of Tuzhou.
Du Yu, courtesy name Yuan Kai, was born in Duling, Jingzhao.
His grandfather, Du Ji, was the official secretary of the Wei Dynasty.
His father, Du Shu, was the governor of Youzhou.
Du Yu had extensive knowledge and was familiar with the rise and fall of a country. He often said: Virtue cannot be expected to be achieved, but it is still possible to make meritorious deeds.
At first, his father and Emperor Xuan did not get along with each other, so he was removed from office and died in confinement. Therefore, Du Yu could not be called upon for a long time.
When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Du Yu married the emperor's sister, Princess Gaolu, and initially served as Shangshulang, inheriting the ancestral title of Fengletinghou.
After four years in office, he was transferred to the Military Affairs Council of the Prime Minister's Office.
Zhong Hui attacked Shu and appointed Du Yu as the chief historian of Zhenxi.
Zhong Hui rebelled, and all his staff and assistants were killed. Only Du Yu escaped the disaster with his wisdom and increased the number of households by 1,150 households.
He drafted laws and regulations with Chariot General Maichong and others. After they were completed, Du Yu annotated the laws and regulations, and then reported: "The law is a decision-making regulation like a pencil ink stick, not a book that exhausts rationality."
summary: Du Yu, from Duling, was knowledgeable and pragmatic, believing virtue could not be forced but deeds could be achieved. His father’s conflict with Emperor Xuan delayed his career, but he married a princess and served as a minister. He survived Zhong Hui’s rebellion through wisdom. He codified laws, emphasizing simplicity and clarity to prevent violations. As Henan Yin, he advocated for straightforward official assessments, arguing that overly detailed regulations bred hypocrisy. He was dismissed after a conflict with Shi Jian but later served as a military commander, correctly predicting the enemy’s actions. He proposed numerous reforms, including new tools, granaries, and tax regulations. He built a bridge at Fupingjin despite skepticism, and crafted a water clock. Appointed to replace Yang Hu in Jingzhou, he repaired weapons, trained troops, and defeated Wu general Zhang Zheng, then alienated Wu by returning captives. He urged immediate conquest of Wu, countering objections about summer rains by citing overwhelming momentum. His forces captured Jiangling and other cities, leading to Wu’s surrender. He was enfeoffed as a marquis. After the war, he focused on education, irrigation, and stabilizing the region, earning the people’s trust. He carved stone tablets to record his achievements, predicting geological changes. Though not a horseman or archer, he led effectively and was known for his humility and dedication to the *Zuo Zhuan*, which he annotated extensively. He died at sixty-three while traveling, leaving instructions for a simple burial. His son Du Xi served as a crown prince’s tutor, known for his integrity, and survived political turmoil. The chroniclers praised Yang Hu’s strategic vision and Du Yu’s multifaceted talents, noting their contributions to unifying the realm.

translation:
Emperor Xuan's name was Yi, whose courtesy name was Zhongda. He was from Xiaojingli, Wen County, Henan, and his surname was Sima.
His ancestors were descendants of Chongli, the son of Emperor Gaoyang, namely Xia Guan Zhurong. After experiencing the Tang, Yu, Xia and Shang dynasties, he inherited this official position.
During the reign of King Xuan of Zhou Dynasty, the person who served as Sima of the Xia Dynasty was a man named Cheng Baixiu's father. Because he conquered and pacified Xu Fang as a world official, he was given the family name of Sima.
Therefore, Longmo became their last name. During the Chu and Han Dynasties, Sima Yan was a general who joined the army of the princes in conquering the Se country.
After the fall of the Qin State, it was established as: Mudou, and the king's capital was established in Chi.
He designated the land as a county, and his descendants lived here permanently.
From Sima, the eighth generation descendant, Sima Gou, the general of the Western Conquest, named Shuping.
Sima Gou Sheng invited Tong Taishou to cultivate the land, named Gong Ji.
Dandan was born in Yuanbei, Dankentan, the prefect of Yuanbei, with the courtesy name Wuken.
When Siya was born and fled, Siken fell to Yin, whose name was Jiangong.
Emperor Xuan was Si Yaduo's second son.
Emperor Xuan had extraordinary integrity when he was young. He was smart, bold and had lofty ambitions. He was erudite and devoted to Confucianism.
At the end of the Han Dynasty, the world was in chaos, and Emperor Xuan often lamented and worried about the world.
Nanyang Prefect Dangyu, who was from the same county and was known for being good at identifying talents, met Emperor Xuan, who was underage at the time. He thought Emperor Xuan was an unusually talented person.
Cui Yanyu, a native of Qinghe who served as minister, was a friend of Emperor Xuan's brother Sima Lang. He once said to Sima Lang: Your brother is smart, wise and honest, and his decisive ability is outstanding. He is not comparable to ordinary people.
Six years after the founding of the Imperial Household, the county recommended candidates for the imperial office.
At that time, Yan Gen Zaoxuan invited Sikong to serve. After hearing about Emperor Xuan's reputation, he recruited him.
Emperor Xuan understood that Yi's fortune was declining, and he was unwilling to lose his integrity and succumb to Tadang, so he declined on the grounds that he had wind paralysis and was unable to eat and live normally.
Wei Genzuo sent a secret agent at night to spy on the situation, but Emperor Xuan lay motionless on the bed.
When Emperor Wu of Wei was appointed prime minister, he summoned Emperor Xuan to be a literary advisor and ordered the people sent there: If he makes excuses again, he will be imprisoned.
Emperor Xuan was afraid and took office.
From then on, Emperor Wu of Wei ordered Emperor Xuan to accompany the prince at all times. He was promoted to the position of Huangmen Shilang, then Yilang, Prime Minister Shu Cao's family, and soon he was transferred to the chief secretary.
Emperor Xuan followed Cao Cao to attack Zhang Lu and advised Emperor Wu of Wei: Liu Bei captured Liu Zhang through deception and force. The Shu people sent troops to fight for Jiangling before they surrendered. This opportunity cannot be missed.
Now if we go to Hanzhong to display our troops and show off our power, Yizhou will panic and seize the opportunity to march and attack the city, which will inevitably lead to collapse.
With this momentum, it is easy to establish achievements.
A saint cannot go against heaven's timing, nor can he lose his opportunity.
summary: Emperor Xuan, named Sima Yi with the courtesy name Zhongda, was from Wen County, Henan. His ancestors traced back to Chongli, a descendant of Emperor Gaoyang, who served as Xia Guan Zhurong. During the Zhou Dynasty, a descendant named Cheng Baixiu's father was granted the surname Sima for pacifying Xu Fang. In the Chu-Han period, Sima Yan was a general. By the eighth generation, Sima Gou emerged, and Emperor Xuan was the second son of Si Yaduo. From a young age, Emperor Xuan displayed extraordinary integrity, intelligence, and lofty ambitions, being erudite in Confucianism. During the late Han Dynasty's chaos, he lamented the state of the world. Nanyang Prefect Dangyu recognized his talent early on, and Cui Yanyu praised his wisdom and decisiveness. In the sixth year of the founding, he was recommended for office but initially declined due to illness, fearing the declining fortunes of the Han. When Emperor Wu of Wei (Cao Cao) summoned him as a literary advisor, he was threatened with imprisonment and reluctantly took the post. He served as Huangmen Shilang, Yilang, and Prime Minister Shu Cao's family, eventually becoming chief secretary.

translation:
Emperor Wu of Wei said: People are suffering from lack of satisfaction. They have captured Longxi and still want to capture Shu!
In the end, he did not listen to Emperor Xuan's opinion.
Soon Emperor Xuan followed Cao Cao to conquer Sun Quan and defeated Sun Quan's army.
After the army triumphantly returned, Sun Quan sent an envoy to beg for surrender, presented a memorial to him, and stated that this was his destiny.
Emperor Wu of Wei said: This boy wants to roast me on the fire!
Emperor Xuan replied: The fate of the Han Dynasty is coming to an end, and the prime minister owns nine-tenths of the world, and serves the emperor accordingly.
Sun Quan became a minister, which was the common wish of heaven and man.
The reason why the Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou dynasties refused to give in and refuse was precisely because they feared God and knew God's will.
After the establishment of the Wei Kingdom, Emperor Xuan was promoted to the crown prince and concubine.
Whenever he participates in major decisions, he always has a good plan and wins the trust and respect of the prince. He is known as the four friends with Chen Qun, Wu Zhi and Zhu Shuo.
Emperor Xuan was promoted to Army Sima and told Emperor Wu of Wei: In ancient times, Jizi discussed the strategy of governing the country and proposed that food is the first priority for the people.
At present, there are about 200,000 people in the country who are not engaged in agricultural production. This is not a long-term solution for running the country.
Although the war has not subsided, we should still cultivate the land and defend at the same time.
Emperor Wu of Wei adopted this opinion and devoted himself to farming to accumulate grain. The country's property was rich and sufficient.
Emperor Xuan also issued a memorial stating that Hu Xiu, the governor of Jingzhou, was cruel to the people, and Fu Fang, the governor of Nanxiang, was arrogant and extravagant, and neither of them should be appointed officials to serve as border guards.
Emperor Wu of Wei did not investigate or deal with them.
When Shu general Guan Yu besieged Cao Ren in Fan, Yu Jin and other seven armies were completely wiped out. Hu Xiu and Fu Fang surrendered to Guan Yu, making Cao Ren's siege even more critical.
At this time, Emperor Han made Xuchang his capital. Emperor Wu of Wei thought that Xuchang was too close to the enemy and wanted to move to the north of the Yellow River.
Emperor Xuan advised: "The defeat of Yu Jin and other troops by the water was not due to a blunder in combat and defense. The relocation did not harm the overall situation of the country. Moving the capital rashly not only showed our weakness to the enemy, but also caused extreme unrest among the soldiers and civilians in the Huaihe and Mianshui areas."
Sun Quan and Liu Bei were close on the outside but distant on the inside. Guan Yu's victory was exactly what Sun Quan did not want.
You can explain to Sun Quan and let him contain Guan Yu's rear, then the siege of Fandi will naturally be lifted.
Emperor Wu of Wei followed this opinion.
Sure enough, Sun Quan sent general Lu Meng to the west to attack Gong'an. After capturing Gong'an, Guan Yu was finally killed by Lu Meng.
Emperor Wu of Wei believed that the repatriated people in Jingzhou and the people stationed in Yingchuan to guard the border were too close to the southern enemy, and wanted to move them all away.
Emperor Xuan said: The people of Jingchu are imprudent, easily agitated and difficult to appease.
Guan Yu had just been defeated, and all kinds of evildoers hid and fled to watch.
Now ordering those good people to migrate will not only hurt their feelings, but will also make those who have fled dare not return to their hometowns.
Emperor Wu of Wei followed this opinion.
After that, the exiles all returned to their hometowns to engage in their own professions.
When Emperor Wu of Wei died in Luoyang, the government and the public were frightened.
summary: Emperor Xuan accompanied Cao Cao on campaigns, advising against missing opportunities to attack Shu after capturing Hanzhong, but Cao Cao refused. He later followed Cao Cao to defeat Sun Quan. After Sun Quan's surrender, Emperor Xuan argued that the Han dynasty's fate was ending and Cao Cao should accept heaven's will. In the Wei Kingdom, he became crown prince and concubine, trusted by the prince, and was known as one of the four friends with Chen Qun, Wu Zhi, and Zhu Shuo. As Army Sima, he advocated for agricultural cultivation to support the military, which Cao Cao adopted, enriching the state. He also criticized corrupt officials Hu Xiu and Fu Fang, but Cao Cao ignored him; they later surrendered to Guan Yu, worsening Cao Ren's siege. Emperor Xuan advised against moving the capital, suggesting instead to ally with Sun Quan against Guan Yu, which led to Guan Yu's death. He also opposed relocating people from Jingzhou, allowing exiles to return home.

translation:
Emperor Xuan presided over the funeral and kept order inside and outside the court.
Then he personally carried the coffin back to Ye.
After Emperor Wen of Wei came to the throne, he granted Emperor Xuan the title of Marquis of Hejin Ting, and then the title of Prime Minister Chang Shi.
At the same time, Sun Quan led his troops to march westward. The imperial court considered that Fan and Xiangyang did not have enough food reserves to defend themselves against the enemy.
At that time, Cao Ren was guarding Xiangyang, hoping to recall Cao Ren to Wandi.
Emperor Xuan said: Sun Quan recently defeated Guan Yu. This is the time when he wants to take the initiative to make friends, so he must not dare to invade.
襄阳是水陆交通的要道，抵御敌人的要害之地，不能放弃。
最终没听从。
So Cao Ren burned and abandoned the two cities. As expected, Sun Quan did not invade. Emperor Wei Wen regretted it very much.
After accepting the abdication of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Xuan was appointed Shangshu.
Soon, he was appointed as military governor and censor Zhongcheng, and was granted the title of Marquis of Anguo Township.
In the second year of Jianchi's reign, he was dismissed from the post of military governor and promoted to Shizhong and Shangshu Youpushe.
In the fifth year, the emperor visited the south and reviewed the army at the border of Wu.
Emperor Xuan stayed to guard Xidan, and renamed it Xuesu Castle. He was granted the title of Fujun and Jiajie, commanding five thousand soldiers, and was given the title of Shizhong and Lu Shangshushi.
Emperor Xuan firmly refused.
The Emperor said: Because of many trivial matters, I work day and night without a moment of peace and rest.
This is not an honor, it is just to share my worries.
In the sixth year, the emperor mobilized a large naval army to conquer the state of Wu, and ordered Emperor Xuan to stay behind to appease the people internally and provide military supplies externally.
Before setting off, he issued an edict saying: I am deeply worried about the rear affairs, so I entrust it to you.
Although Cao Shen had military exploits, Xiao He was more important.
Wouldn't it be great if I don't have to worry about anything?
The emperor returned to Luoyang from Guangling and ordered Emperor Xuan: "I am in the east, you should be in charge of the affairs in the west; I am in the west, you should be in charge of the affairs in the east."
So Emperor Xuan stayed to guard Xuchang.
The emperor was seriously ill, and Emperor Xuan, Cao Zhen, Chen Qun and others paid homage to the emperor in the South Hall of Chonghua Hall, and together they accepted his deathbed orders to assist the government.
The prince was ordered to say: If there is a estrangement between the three adults, do not be suspicious.
After Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he changed the title of Emperor Xuan to Wuyang Marquis.
Sun Quan besieged Jiangxia and sent generals Zhuge Jin and Zhang Ba to attack Xiangyang. Emperor Xuan led all armies to attack Sun Quan and drove back the Wu army.
He marched in pursuit, defeated Zhuge Jin, killed Zhang Ba, and killed more than a thousand enemy soldiers in total.
Emperor Xuan was promoted to General of Hussars.
In June of the first year of Taihe, the emperor ordered Emperor Xuan to garrison in Wandi and add the military governor of Jingzhou and Yuzhou to the army.
When Shu general Meng Da surrendered, the Wei Dynasty treated him very well.
Emperor Xuan believed that Mengda's words and deeds were cunning and untrustworthy, and his repeated remonstrances were not accepted, so he appointed Mengda as the prefect of Xincheng, granted him the title of marquis, and gave him the title of holiday.
summary: After Cao Cao's death, Emperor Xuan managed the funeral and escorted the coffin to Ye. Under Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi), he was made Marquis of Hejin Ting and Prime Minister Chang Shi. When Sun Quan attacked, he advised against recalling Cao Ren from Xiangyang, but was ignored; Cao Ren burned the city, and Sun Quan did not invade, causing regret. After the Han abdication, Emperor Xuan served as Shangshu, then military governor and censor Zhongcheng, later becoming Shizhong and Shangshu Youpushe. He guarded Xuchang and was granted titles, though he refused honors. During campaigns against Wu, he stayed behind to manage affairs. On his deathbed, Emperor Wen entrusted him, Cao Zhen, and Chen Qun with assisting the government.

translation:
Shu generals Yao Jing, Zheng Ta and others led more than 7,000 men to surrender.
At that time, the border counties had just surrendered, and most of them did not have household registration books. The Wei Dynasty wanted to verify it and asked Emperor Xuan to come to the capital for an audience.
The emperor asked Emperor Xuan, who replied: The enemy used strict laws to rule the people, so the people turned their backs on him.
They should be treated leniently according to Dafa, and they can naturally live and work in peace and contentment.
He also asked, “Which country should be conquered first?”
He replied: The State of Wu thinks that the people in the Central Plains are not accustomed to water warfare, so they dare to live in Shuguan.
Whenever you attack an enemy, you must choke his throat and pound his heart.
Xiakou and Shuguan are the heart and throat of Wu.
If we send an army to march to Wancheng, lure Sun Quan to his side, and then send a navy army to march to Xia, and take advantage of the opportunity to attack them, it will be like magic soldiers falling from the sky, and we will definitely defeat them.
The emperor thought it was reasonable, and ordered Emperor Xuan to station troops in Wan.
In the fourth year, he was promoted to general, increased to governor, fake Huang Bo, and joined Cao Zhen in the crusade against Xili.
Emperor Xuan split the mountains from Youyue to clear a road, and the land and water armies advanced side by side, up the Mian River to Quji, and captured Xinfeng County.
The troops were stationed in Dankou. They encountered heavy rain and returned to the army.
The next year, Zhuge Liang invaded Tianshui and besieged generals Jia Si and Wei Ping in Qishan.
The Emperor said: There is a war in the West, and there is no one who can be trusted except you.
So Emperor Xuan was sent to the west to garrison Chang'an, and he commanded the military forces of Yongzhou and Liangzhou. He led the cavalry general Zhang He, the rear general Fei Yao, the army conquering Shu Dai Jun, the Yongzhou governor Guo Huai and others to attack Zhuge Liang.
Zhang He advised Emperor Xuan to divide his army and garrison it in Yong and Commandery to command from behind. Emperor Xuan said: If you know that the front army can resist the enemy on its own, your opinion is right, general.
If it cannot resist and the troops are divided into two parts, the Chu army will be destroyed by Yingbu.
So he marched to Yumi.
When Zhuge Liang heard that the army was coming, he personally led his soldiers to harvest the wheat in the upper state.
All the generals were very scared. Emperor Xuan said: Zhuge Liang is more worried and less decisive. He will definitely camp and defend himself, and then cut the wheat. We have two days to travel day and night. It is enough.
So he marched lightly and day and night, but Zhuge Liang fled.
Emperor Xuan said: We are very tired from marching all the way, which is what those who know military knowledge hope.
Lijiangtai did not dare to occupy Jusai, which was easy to deal with.
He marched and stationed in Hanyang, met Zhuge Liang, and Emperor Xuan formed a formation to face the Shu army.
He sent general Niu Jin to lure the Shu army with light cavalry. As soon as the two armies engaged, Zhuge Kui retreated and pursued him to Kongshan.
He condemned Jiangtai and stationed troops at Lu Su, occupying the two mountains in the north and south, and cut off the water sources to create a circle of encirclement.
summary: Under Emperor Ming, Emperor Xuan became Wuyang Marquis. He repelled Sun Quan's forces, killing Zhang Ba. He was promoted to General of Hussars and garrisoned in Wan. When Shu general Meng Da rebelled, Emperor Xuan suspected his cunning and, despite warnings, marched swiftly, capturing and executing Meng Da in sixteen days. He then dealt with Shen Yi, who had forged edicts, and exiled Meng Da's followers. He advised leniency for surrendered border counties and proposed attacking Wu via Xiakou and Shuguan. He was promoted to general and joined Cao Zhen against Shu, but heavy rain forced a retreat.

translation:
Emperor Xuan attacked and broke through his encirclement. Zhuge Liang escaped at night, pursued and defeated him, captured and killed more than 10,000 people.
The emperor sent people to comfort the army and increase the number of fiefs.
At that time, military advisor Du Xi and military governor Xue Ti both said that when the wheat was ripe next year, the tomb robbers would definitely attack. There was no food in Luxi and it should be transported in advance in winter.
Emperor Xuan said: Zhuge Liang came out of Qishan again, attacked Chenhe, was defeated and returned.
Even if he comes again in the future, he will not attack the city. He will definitely hope to fight in the field, and it will definitely be in Longshu, not in the west.
Zhuge Liang is often helpless due to lack of food. He will definitely accumulate food after returning. According to my speculation, he will not take action until three years have passed.
So Shangzou moved the farmers from Jizhou to Shangbang and strengthened the supervision and management of Jingzhao, Tianshui and Nan'an.
In the first year of the year, the Chengguo Canal was dug, a submerged pressure was built, thousands of hectares of land were irrigated, and the national treasury was enriched.
In the second year, Zhuge Liang led more than 100,000 troops out of Xiegu and stationed troops in the plain south of the Wei River in Yongdi.
The emperor was very worried and sent Qin Lang, the guard of Shu, to lead 20,000 infantry and cavalry to accept the command of Emperor Xuan.
The generals wanted to fight in Weibei, but Emperor Xuan said: "The people are gathering in Mengnan. This is a battleground."
So he led his army across the water and made a camp with his back to the water.
Then he said to the generals: If Zhuge Liang is a brave man, he should start from martial arts and march eastward along the mountain. If you go west to Wuzhangyuan, then all armies and horses will be safe.
As expected, Zhuge Liang went to the plain and prepared to cross the Wei River north. Emperor Xuan sent General Zhou Dang to lure the Shu army in Yangsu.
For several days, Zhuge Liang remained silent.
Emperor Xuan said: Zhuge Liang wanted to seize the plains instead of going to Yangsui. We can know his intentions.
He sent general Hu Zun and Yongzhou governor Guo Huai to jointly guard Yang Sui, and met Zhuge Liang at Jishi. When the battle began near the plain, Zhuge Liang was unable to advance and returned to Wuzhangyuan.
When a comet crashed into Zhuge Liang's camp, Emperor Xuan knew that Zhuge Liang would definitely fail, so he sent a surprise force to contain Zhuge Liang's rear, killing more than 500 people, capturing more than 1,000 alive, and more than 600 surrendered.
At that time, the imperial court believed that Zhuge Liang was a distant enemy living in the south of the Yangtze River and was conducive to a quick victory. Emperor Xuan was often ordered to be cautious and wait for his changes.
Zhuge Liang challenged Emperor Xuan many times, but Emperor Xuan refused to fight, so Zhuge Liang gave Emperor Yi women's clothes.
Emperor Xuan was furious and petitioned for a decisive battle. The emperor disagreed and sent an upright minister, Wei Wei Xinpi, holding a talisman as a military advisor to stop Emperor Xuan.
Later, Zhuge Liang came to challenge again. Emperor Xuan was preparing to send troops to fight. Xinpi stood at the military gate holding a talisman, and Emperor Xuan gave up.
At the beginning, Shu general Jiang Wei heard that Xinpi was coming and said to Zhuge Liang: If Xinpi comes to hold the festival, the enemy will not fight again.
Zhuge Liang said: He had no intention of going to war in the first place, so the reason why he insisted on asking for a fight was just to show his bravery in front of his soldiers.
When a general is in the army, you don't have to accept your orders. If you can really deal with me, why bother asking for a battle thousands of miles away?
Emperor Xuan's younger brother Sima Fu wrote to ask for military advice. Emperor Xuan replied: Zhuge Liang has great ambitions but no opportunities. He is more resourceful and less decisive. He likes to use troops but has no power. Although he leads a hundred thousand soldiers, he has fallen into my trap. Defeating them is certain.
The confrontation with Zhuge Liang lasted for more than a hundred days. When Zhuge Liang fell ill and died, the generals burned their camps and fled quietly. The people rushed to tell each other, and Emperor Xuan sent troops to pursue him.
Zhuge Liang's chief commander, Yang Yi, turned around and marched with drums and flags, as if he was going to fight Emperor Xuan.
Emperor Xuan thought that it was not appropriate to pursue poor bandits, so Yang Yi formed a formation and left.
After a few days of encounter, Emperor Xuan came to Zhuge Liang's camp, inspected the things they sent, and seized many books, grain and grass. Emperor Xuan was sure that Zhuge Liang was dead and said: "He is really a genius in the world."
Xinpi thinks it’s not certain yet.
Emperor Xuan said: What the military attaches great importance to are military documents and secrets, as well as food and fodder for soldiers, horses, and horses. Now that they have been thrown away, is there anyone who can still live after throwing away his own five internal organs?
summary: When Zhuge Liang invaded, Emperor Xuan was sent west to command forces. He marched to Yumi, forcing Zhuge Liang to flee. He defeated Shu forces at Kongshan, capturing thousands. He predicted Zhuge Liang would not attack for three years due to food shortages, so he moved farmers and dug canals to enrich the state. In the second year, Zhuge Liang led 100,000 troops to Wuzhangyuan. Emperor Xuan avoided battle, despite Zhuge Liang sending women's clothes to provoke him. He petitioned for a decisive battle but was stopped by Xinpi. Zhuge Liang died, and Emperor Xuan pursued, confirming his death. He later learned Zhuge Liang ate little and handled all affairs, predicting his early death. He defeated Shu general Ma Dai and accepted surrenders from Di kings.

translation:
However, from the north of the Yellow River, the people are poor and distressed, and they are working hard both inside and outside. The forces cannot be developed at the same time, and construction should be temporarily stopped to relieve temporary emergencies.
In the second year of Jingchu, Emperor Xuan led Niu Jin, Hu Zun and other 40,000 infantry and cavalry troops to set out from Kyoto.
The emperor sent him out of Ximing Gate, and his brother Sima Fu and his son Sima Shi sent him warm water and gave him grain, silk, cattle and wine. He ordered the county governor, Dian Nong, and all the officials below to pay homage to Emperor Xuan.
Emperor Xuan met with his father and old friends and had a banquet for several days.
Emperor Xuan sighed deeply and felt sad. He chanted a poem and said: The sky and the earth are created, and the sun and the moon shine again.
At the right time, we went on an expedition with all our strength.
He will sweep away the enemies and return to the army to cross the countryside.
Clear away thousands of miles and unify the four directions.
Retire after success, and wait for sin to dance in the sun.
So he marched, passed Guzhu, crossed Jieshi, and stationed troops in Liao River.
As expected, Wen Yi sent tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to block the Liao Tunnel and defend the walls sixty or seventy miles from north to south to resist Emperor Xuan.
Emperor Xuan sent out heavy troops to the south with great fanfare, and the bandits gathered their elite troops to fight.
Emperor Xuan used boats to secretly cross the army to attack the north, close to the bandits' camp, sank the boats and burned the bridges, built a long siege along the wall of water, abandoned the enemy troops and marched towards Xiangping.
The generals said: Setting up a siege instead of attacking the rebel army is not a good way to inform the army.
Emperor Xuan said: The bandits have strengthened the fortress in order to tire out our army.
Attacking them fell into their trap, which was why Wang Yi was ashamed of Guo Kunyang.
The ancients said that the reason why the enemy has to fight us despite building high barriers is because we attack the place they must rescue.
When the army of thieves and bandits gathers here, their lair will be empty.
If we attack Xiangping directly, the enemy will be fearful and seek battle in fear, and we will definitely defeat them.
So the whole column marched away.
When the rebels saw our troops appearing behind them, they actually intercepted them.
Emperor Xuan said to the generals: "That's why I didn't attack their camp because I was hoping to create this situation. This opportunity should not be missed."
So he sent his troops to fight back and defeated the enemy. After three battles and three victories, the rebels retreated to Xiangping, and Emperor Xuan marched to surround Xiangping.
When Wenyi heard the news of Wei Jun's departure, he asked Sun Jie for help.
Jieqie also sent troops to support him from a distance, and wrote to Wen Yi: "Sima Gong is good at using troops, his transformation is like a god, and he is invincible. I am deeply worried about you."
It happened to be a continuous heavy rain and several feet of water accumulated on the flat ground. The soldiers of the three armies panicked and wanted to move the camp.
Emperor Xuan ordered that anyone in the army who dared to speak of migration be beheaded.
The commander-in-chief Shi Zhangjing violated military orders and was beheaded, and the morale of the army stabilized.
Relying on the strength of the water, the bandit army was able to cut firewood and graze their cattle in peace and contentment.
The generals wanted to capture them, but Emperor Xuan did not agree.
Sima Chen Gui said: In the previous attack on Shangyong, eight troops marched at the same time, day and night, so they were able to capture the fortified city and kill Mengda in five or six days.
Now I feel more peaceful and relaxed when I come from afar. I don't understand it.
Emperor Xuan said: Meng Da has a small number of soldiers but enough food to last a year. Our soldiers are four times as many as Meng Da but have less than a month's food. If we use troops that can last for one month against those that can last for a year, how can we not fight quickly?
With four against one, this should be done even if split in half.
Therefore, regardless of the number of casualties, we are competing with food.
Now that the enemy is outnumbered and we are outnumbered, the thieves are hungry and we are full, and the rain is falling like this, the effect cannot be exerted. Although it should be accelerated, what can be done.
Since setting off from the capital, I have not been worried about the rebels attacking, but I am worried about the rebels escaping.
Now the bandits' army is about to run out of food and grass, but our army has not yet encircled them. We have robbed their cattle and horses and confiscated their firewood, in order to deliberately drive them away.
The use of soldiers pays attention to the art of deception and is good at changing at any time.
The thieves relied on large numbers of people and heavy rain, so even though they were hungry and sleepy, they refused to surrender. We should show our incompetence to reassure them.
It's not a good idea to alarm them by seeking small profits.
When the court heard that the army had encountered heavy rain, they sent a letter to summon them back.
The Emperor said: If Sima Gong can respond to danger, he will soon be able to capture the bandits.
Soon the rain stopped and they were surrounded.
