They built earthen mountain tunnels, prepared shields, oars, hooks and carts, and attacked day and night with arrows and stones raining down on them.
summary: When Gongsun Wenyi rebelled in Liaodong, Emperor Xuan predicted he would hold the Liao River and estimated a year for the campaign. He advised halting palace construction to relieve the people. In the second year of Jingchu, he led 40,000 troops, crossing the Liao River and feinting south while crossing north. He besieged Xiangping, ignoring calls to attack the enemy camp, and defeated Wenyi after three battles. Despite heavy rain, he forbade moving camp, beheading a violator. He rejected surrenders, executed Wenyi, and killed 7,000 men over fifteen, plus 2,000 officials. He released Gongsun Gong and honored loyalists. He refused to give short coats to soldiers, citing public property. He dismissed elderly soldiers and mourned the dead.

translation:
Emperor Xuan was so panicked that he took a light post car and traveled day and night. He traveled more than four hundred miles from Baiwu and arrived there in one day.
Enter the Jiafu Palace bedroom and walk to the imperial bed.
Emperor Xuan asked about his condition with tears in his eyes. The emperor took Emperor Xuan's hand, looked at King Qi and said, "I will entrust you with the funeral affairs."
Death can actually be controlled. I waited patiently for you until we met, and there was no regrets left.
Cao Shuang, the general of Emperor Xuan, accepted the imperial edict to assist the young master.
After the King of Qi succeeded to the throne, Emperor Xuan was promoted to Shizhong, Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese and foreign armies, and Secretary-General. He and Cao Shuang each commanded three thousand troops, and jointly took charge of the government affairs. They took turns to be on duty in the palace, and could sit in the palace as a public servant.
Cao Shuang wanted the affairs to be reported to the minister to go through him first, so he proposed to the emperor and appointed Emperor Xuan as the chief minister.
After deliberation, the imperial court concluded that all the great ministers before and after had died in their positions, so they appointed Emperor Xuan as Taifu. He did not need to walk quickly when entering the palace, did not need to state his name when meeting the emperor, and was allowed to wear swords and shoes when entering the palace. Everything was just like the old practice of Xiao He of the Han Dynasty.
All wedding and funeral expenses for Emperor Xuan's family were provided by the government. His eldest son, Sima Shi, was appointed as the regular attendant of the cavalry, three of his children were appointed as lieutenants, and four were appointed as cavalry captains.
Emperor Xuan resolutely resigned and refused to accept the official titles of his disciples.
In the first month of the spring of the first year of the Zhengshi period, envoys from the Eastern Japan came to pay tribute. The kings of the Yanqi, Weixu, and Xianbei people south of Weishui all sent envoys to pay tribute.
The emperor attributed the credit to the prime minister and increased Emperor Xuan's fiefdom.
At first, Emperor Wei Ming liked to build palaces, which were luxurious and magnificent in scale, which made the people feel miserable.
When Emperor Xuan returned from Liaodong, there were still more than 10,000 people serving as laborers, and there were often thousands of prize items.
At this time, everyone petitioned to stop, and those who saved money went back to farming, and the world was happy and looked up to it.
In the summer and May of the second year of Zhengshi, the Wu general Quan Cong invaded Shaopi. Zhu Pan and Jianjian besieged! Bi. Zhuge Jin and Chu Ju were plundering Dan Shi. Emperor Xuan requested to attack personally.
Commentators all said that the bandits came from afar to besiege Sanzhiqiu, and it was impossible to capture the city quickly.
If they are frustrated under the city, they will have the tendency to self-destruct, and they can use good strategies to resist.
Emperor Xuan said: If the border town is invaded but sits on top of the imperial court, if the border is not stable, doubts will arise in the hearts of the people. This is a great worry for the country.
In June, he led various armies to march south, and the emperor sent out the Jinyang League.
Emperor Xuan ordered the light cavalry to challenge because the weather in the south was hot and humid and could not last long. Zhu Ran did not dare to attack rashly.
summary: Returning, he was granted more fiefs. When Emperor Ming was dying, he entrusted Emperor Xuan with the young King Qi, alongside Cao Shuang. Emperor Xuan became Taifu with high honors. He refused titles for his sons. Under King Qi, he repelled Wu attacks, digging canals for farming. He advised against Cao Shuang's Shu campaign, which failed. When Cao Shuang moved the Empress Dowager and controlled the government, Emperor Xuan feigned illness. He tricked Li Sheng into thinking he was dying, so Cao Shuang relaxed. In the first year of Jiaping, he deposed Cao Shuang during an imperial visit, executing him and his party. He refused the prime minister position and Jiuxi honors.

translation:
Wang Jun had no choice, so he went to Wuqiu to greet him, tied himself by the water, and said: "If Wang Jun is guilty, you should break the slip and call me in letter. Why bother to come in person?"
Emperor Xuan said: Because you are not a person who can turn your abbreviation into a letter.
He took Wang Jun back to the capital with him.
Passing the Maikui Temple on the way, Wang Jun shouted: "Maikui Road!"
Wang Jun was a loyal minister of the Wei Dynasty, and only the gods understood this.
When he reached Xiang, he took poison and died.
The remaining party members who arrested him killed all three tribes and beheaded Cao Biao.
Gather all the princes of the Wei family in Ye and order the relevant departments to keep them under guard and not to allow them to come in casually.
The emperor sent his servant Wei Dan to hold the talisman festival in Wuchi to comfort the army.
After Emperor Xuan arrived from Gancheng, the emperor ordered Da Honglu and his imperial servant Yu Yi to hold the talisman, and ordered Emperor Xuan to be the prime minister of the country, and to make Anping County Duke. Each of his grandson and his brother's son was made a marquis, and 50,000 households were granted successively. There were 19 people in the clan who were marquises.
Emperor Xuan resolutely dismissed the Prime Minister and the Duke but did not accept it.
In June, Emperor Xuan was bedridden. He dreamed that Mai Kui and Wang Jun were causing trouble, and he was very disgusted.
Wuyin died in the capital in the eighth month of autumn at the age of seventy-three.
The emperor came to express his condolences in person wearing plain clothes. The funeral specifications were modeled on the old system of Huo Guang of the Han Dynasty, and he was given posthumously to the prime minister and the county governor.
His younger brother, Sima Fu, went to court to state Emperor Xuan's wishes during his lifetime and to reject the Duke and Yun Cheng.
In September, Geng Shen was buried in Heyin. Mi Hao Wen was later changed to Xuan Sai.
Before that, Xuanhu had given instructions in advance that he would be buried in Juyang Mountain without building a grave or erecting a monument; he would write three chapters of "Gu Ming" and bury him in the clothes of the time, without any funeral objects, and those who died later could not be buried together.
Everything is according to his orders.
When the Jin Kingdom was first established, Emperor Xuan was honored as King Xuan.
After the master boy accepted the abdication, he was honored as Emperor Xuan, his mausoleum was named Plateau, and his temple was named Gaozu.
Xuanhu was jealous in his heart but generous in appearance, suspicious and manipulative.
Emperor Sewu noticed that Emperor Xuan was ambitious. He heard that he could look back at people like a wolf and wanted to test it.
He called him forward and asked him to look back. Emperor Xuan's face was facing backward but his body was not moving.
Emperor Wu once dreamed that three horses were eating in the same manger, and he was very disgusted.
He told Prince Cao Pi: Sima Yi is not a willing minister and will definitely interfere in national affairs.
The prince had always been very good with Emperor Xuan and always protected him, so he was spared.
Emperor Xuan was very diligent in his position, working around the clock, personally taking care of everything from cutting grass to grazing, so Emperor Wu of Wei was relieved.
When Gongsun Wenyi was pacified, they massacred them wantonly.
When Cao Shuang was killed, all his party members were killed by the Yi clan, regardless of gender, old or young. Even his married sisters and so on were all killed, and then he finally usurped the power of Wei.
During the reign of Emperor Ming of Jin Dynasty, Director Wang was sitting beside him.
When Emperor Ming asked about how he had conquered the world in his previous life, Wang Dao recounted what happened when Emperor Xuan started his business and what happened to the noble countryman in the last years of Emperor Wen.
Emperor Ming put his face on the bed and said: If it is really like what you said, how can the Jin Dynasty last long?
summary: Later, he suppressed rebellions by Ling Huyu and Wang Leng, executing them and Cao Biao. He confined Wei princes. He refused further honors. He died at seventy-three, buried simply as per his wishes. Posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan of Jin, his temple name was Gaozu. He was described as jealous but generous, suspicious and manipulative. Cao Cao warned about his ambition, but Cao Pi protected him. He massacred after victories and usurped Wei power. His cruelty was noted, and Emperor Ming of Jin lamented the dynasty's foundation. His strategies were praised but his loyalty questioned, as he betrayed trust and killed rivals, leading to later ridicule.

translation:
Emperor Cheng's name was Sima Yan, whose courtesy name was Shigen. He was the eldest son of Emperor Ming Sima Shao.
On the second day of March in the third year of Taining, he was established as the crown prince.
On the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month, Emperor Ming died.
On the 26th, the prince became emperor, granted a general amnesty to the world, increased the title of civil and military officials to the second level, gave widows, widowers, orphans and old people two pieces of cloth each, and honored the queen Yu as the empress dowager.
On the ninth day of September, the Empress Dowager came to the court to act as the emperor.
Situ Wang directed the affairs of the ministers and participated in the affairs of the court together with Zhongshu Ling Yu Liang.
He appointed Sima Zong, the general of the Fu army and King of Nanton, as the hussar general, and the leading general, Sima Wei, the king of Runan.
On the 11th, Emperor Ming was buried in Wuping Mausoleum.
On the first day of November, there is a solar eclipse. Cao Hun, the prime minister of Guangling, was guilty and was imprisoned and died.
On the twenty-seventh day of the second month of the second month in the first year of Xianhe, a general amnesty was granted to the whole country, and the new year's title was adopted. A banquet was held for five days. The widows, widows and orphans were given old rice and grain, two huks per person, and the corvée tax was exempted for one year within a hundred miles of the capital.
In April, Shi Le sent his general Shi Sheng to invade Runan, and the Runan people seized Neishi Zuji and rebelled.
On the fifth day of the lunar month, Shangshu Zuopu shot Deng You to death.
In May, there was a flood.
On the fifth day of the sixth lunar month, Liu Xia, the envoy Chijie, Sanqi Changshi, supervisor of Huaibei military affairs, Beizhong Langjiang, Xuzhou governor, and Quanling Gong Liu Xia died.
On the 15th, Xi Jian, the chariot and cavalry general, led the governor of Xuzhou, and Guo Mo, the conscript general, was appointed as Beizhonglang general to supervise all the armies in Huaibei.
Liu Xia's generals Li Long and Shi Die supported Liu Xia's son Liu Zhao to replace Liu Xia in order to resist Guo Mo. Liu Jiao, the prefect of Linhuai, defeated them, beheaded Li Long, and sent his head to the capital.
On July 25th, the envoy Chijie, the military commander of Jiangzhou, the governor of Jiangzhou, General Pingnan, and the Marquis of Guanyang County Yingzhan died.
In August, Yi Shizhong, the former general, Danyang Yin Wenqiao was appointed as the general of Pingnan, the governor of Jijie, and the governor of Jiangzhou.
September, severe drought.
Li Xiong's general Zhang Long invaded Fuling and captured the prefect Xie Jun.
In October, Cao Mai, the great-great-grandson of Emperor Wu of Wei, was granted the title of King Chenliu to inherit the Wei state.
On the tenth day of the lunar month, General Wei and King Sima of Runan died.
On the 13th, Sima Yue, the emperor's younger brother, was granted the title of King of Wu.
Sima Zong, the cavalry general and king of Nanton, was found guilty and executed. His family was demoted to the Ma family.
He deposed Dazai and Sima, King of Xiyang, and demoted him to King of Yiyang County.
24. Amnesty for those sentenced to imprisonment of not more than five years within a hundred miles of the capital.
This month, Liu Yao's generals Huang Xiu and Bo Cheng invaded the Zanli territory, and Pingbei general Wei Gai led his troops to Xiangyang.
summary: Emperor Cheng, named Sima Yan (courtesy name Shigen), was the eldest son of Emperor Ming. He was established as crown prince in the third year of Taining and became emperor following his father's death. He honored Queen Yu as Empress Dowager, who acted as regent. Situ Wang directed ministers' affairs alongside Zhongshu Ling Yu Liang. During his reign, the empire faced numerous challenges including solar eclipses, floods, droughts, famines, and rebellions. The Xianhe era began with a general amnesty and tax exemptions. Shi Le's forces repeatedly invaded, with generals like Shi Sheng attacking Runan. Internal rebellions erupted, including Liu Xia's generals supporting his son Liu Zhao to resist Guo Mo. Various military officials died or were appointed to new positions. The period saw severe droughts, earthquakes, and the execution of Sima Zong, King of Nanton, for guilt. Liu Yao's generals invaded Zanli territory, while Shi Le's general Shi Cong attacked Shouyang unsuccessfully.

translation:
The imperial court appointed the leading general Sima You, King of Runan, as the general of the guard. Bian Hujie led the six armies and fought with Su Jun in Xiling. The king's army was defeated.
On the seventh day of the lunar month, Su Jun attacked Qingxizha and set fire to it. Wang's army was defeated again.
Bian Hu, the leading general of Shangshu Ling, Yin Yangman of Danyang, Zhou Dao, the minister of Huangmen, and Tao Zhan, the prefect of Lujiang, were all killed. Thousands of people died.
Yu Liang failed again at Xuanyang Gate, so he took his younger brother, Guo Mo, and Zhao Yin and fled to Xunyang.
So Situ Wangdao, Youguanglu doctor Lu Ye, Xun Song and others guarded the emperor in the Taiji Hall, and the prefect Kong Yu guarded the ancestral temple.
Taking advantage of the victory, Su Jun and other thieves approached the imperial palace and broke into the Queen Mother's harem. All the attendants on the left and right were plundered.
At this time, the eunuch could only use the remaining few stones of rice to cook rice for the royal family.
The people howled and cried, and the sound shook the city.
On the eighth day of the lunar month, Su Jun falsely issued an edict of amnesty to the world, and appointed his ancestors as Shizhong, Taiwei, and Shangshu Ling. He appointed himself General of Hussars and recorded Shangshu affairs.
Yu Bing, the governor of Wu County, fled to Kuaiji.
On March 22, Empress Dowager Yu passed away.
In April, Shi Le attacked Wandi, and the Nanyang Prefecture Kingdom rebelled and surrendered to Shi Le.
On the 24th, Queen Mingmu was buried in Wuping Mausoleum.
On May 18th, Su Jun threatened the emperor to move to Stone City. The emperor got into the car and cried sadly, and the palace was wailing.
Su Jun used the warehouse as his palace, and sent Guan Shang, Zhang Jian, and Hong Hui to invade Jinling, and Han Huang invaded Yixing.
Yu Tan, the governor of Wuxing, Yu Bing, Wang Shu and others launched a rebellion in Sanwu.
On the 29th, Tao Kan, the general who conquered the west, Wen Qiao, the general of Pingnan, Yu Liang, the general of the army guard, and Wei Gai, the general of Pingbei, led 40,000 naval troops and stationed themselves in Caizhou.
In June, Han Huang attacked Xuancheng, and Neishi Huanyi fought hard and died.
On the 15th, General Pingbei and Governor of Yongzhou Wei died in the army.
Mao Bao, the governor of Lujiang, attacked the thieves garrisoning Hefei and captured Hefei.
In the seventh month, Zuyue was attacked by Shi Le's general Shi Cong, and his troops dispersed and fled to Liyang.
Shi Le's general Shi Jilong attacked Liu Yao in Puban.
In August, Liu Yao and Shi Jilong fought in Gaohou, and Shi Jilong was defeated. Liu Yao then besieged Shi Sheng in Luoyang.
On the third day of September, Director Situ Wang fled to Baishi.
On the 25th, Tao Kan asked the governor Yang Qian to attack Su Jun who was defending Stone City.
Wen Qiao and Yu Liang formed a formation at Baishi, and Li Yang, the prefect of Jingling, resisted the bandits' southward division.
Su Jun led his light cavalry into battle, fell off his horse and was beheaded, causing his troops to disperse.
The bandits appointed Su Jun's younger brother Su Yi as their leader.
Zhang Lian, the former governor of Jiaozhou, occupied Shixing and rebelled, attacking Guangzhou. Zhennan Sima Zeng Xie and others defeated him.
In October, Li Xiong's general Zhang Long invaded Fuling, and the prefect Zhao Bi was killed by the thieves.
On December 21, Shi Le defeated Liu Yao in Luoyang and captured him alive.
This year, Shi Le's general Shi Jilong attacked the Di leader Pu Hong in Longshan, and Pu Hong surrendered.
In the first month of the fourth year of Xianhe's reign, the emperor was in Shitucheng. The bandit general Kuangshu surrendered to Xianyuan City, and all the officials rushed there.
Attendant Zhong Ya and right guard general Liu Chao planned to leave the city for the emperor, but were killed by thieves.
On the 25th, the champion general Zhao Yin sent Gan Miao to Liyang to conquer Zu Yue and defeated Zu Yue. Zu Yue defected to Shi Le, and his general Tian Teng surrendered with his troops.
Su Jun's son Su Shuo attacked Taicheng and burned the East Hall and Secret Pavilion of Tai Chi Hall, turning them all into ashes.
There was a great famine in the city, and a bushel of rice was worth ten thousand yuan.
summary: The rebellion of Zu Yue and Su Jun in the second year of Xianhe proved devastating. Su Jun's forces massacred Yuhu, and multiple kings defected to him. The capital was placed under martial law. Yu Liang and others fought Su Jun at Cihu, suffering defeat. The following year, Su Jun crossed the Hengjiang River, attacked the capital, and burned Qingxizha. Many officials were killed, and Yu Liang fled to Xunyang. Su Jun forced the emperor to move to Stone City, causing great suffering. Empress Dowager Yu died during this turmoil. The rebellion was eventually suppressed. Various armies attacked Shitou, and Su Jun was beheaded after falling from his horse. His brother Su Yi became the new rebel leader but was later captured. The palace was reduced to ashes, and Jianpingyuan was used as the imperial residence. Liu Yao was captured alive by Shi Le. The empire continued facing challenges including Shi Jilong's attacks, Li Xiong's invasions, and natural disasters like floods and comets.

translation:
He failed to establish a harmonious political system and eliminate disasters. He was wary day and night and had no time to live in peace.
Now that I am suffering from an illness, I may not be able to recover, so I am very frightened and sad.
A thousand years is so far away that I cannot bear its hardships.
Situ, King Langya and King Sima Yue were brothers from the same mother according to their close relationship. They were benevolent and virtuous, and they had the style of a human king and enjoyed great prestige at that time.
All you princes and ministers, please assist him!
In order to worship the ancestors, both inside and outside the Xiehe court, his words and deeds are in line with the principles of justice.
well! Be respectful!
Don't destroy the beautiful order of your ancestors.
On the sixth day of the lunar month, Sima Xi, the king of Wuling, Sima Yu, the king of Kuaiji, Yu Bing, the eunuch of the Zhongshu, He Chong, the Ling of the Zhongshu, and Zhuge Hui, the minister of the Shangshu, all accepted the decree.
On the seventh day of the lunar month, the emperor died in the West Hall at the age of twenty-two. He was buried in the Xingping Mausoleum, and the temple name was pronounced.
Emperor Cheng was smart when he was young and had the capacity of an adult.
When Sima Zong, the king of Nanton, was executed, Emperor Cheng didn't know. After Su Jun's rebellion subsided, Emperor Cheng asked Yu Liang: Where is the old white-headed man?
Yu Liang replied that he was killed for treason. Emperor Cheng cried to Yu Liang and said: If my uncle accuses someone of being a thief, he will kill him. What should he do if someone else accuses him of being a thief?
Yu Liang was so scared that his face changed color.
Yu Yi once sent wine to Wang Yunzhi, the governor of Jiangzhou, and allowed him to feed a dog. The dog was poisoned to death, and his fear was expressed on the ground.
Emperor Cheng said angrily: "My uncle has brought trouble to the world, what about my younger uncle?"
After hearing this, Yu Yi drank the medicine and died.
However, he was restricted by his uncle when he was young and could not personally handle various political affairs.
When I got older, I paid close attention to national affairs and strived to be simple. I once wanted to build a shooting hall in the back garden. I calculated that it would cost forty gold, but I stopped because it was a waste of money.
Although Emperor Cheng's majestic and mighty weapons were not as good as those of previous emperors, his virtues of respect and frugality were enough to track the heroes of previous generations.
Emperor Kang, whose name was Sima Yue and whose courtesy name was Shitong, was the younger brother of Emperor Cheng.
In the first year of Xianhe, he was granted the title of King of Wu, and in the second year of his reign, he was posthumously named King of Langxie; Jiuwei was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi, plus a general of Hussar; in the fifth year of Xiankang, he was promoted to Shizhong and Situ.
In the sixth month of the eighth year of Geng Yin, Emperor Cheng became unwell and issued an edict to name King Langxie as his successor.
Guiji, Emperor Cheng died.
In the Jiawu period, Emperor Kang ascended the throne and ruled the world.
Fangwu generals and local county governors stationed in various places are not allowed to leave their posts without authorization and come to attend the funeral.
summary: Emperor Cheng died at age twenty-two. He was described as intelligent in youth but restricted by his uncle's influence. He showed concern for frugality, once stopping construction of a shooting hall due to cost. Emperor Kang, named Sima Yue (courtesy name Shitong), was Emperor Cheng's younger brother. He was initially made King of Wu, then King of Langxie, and served as Situ before being named successor. He ascended the throne after Emperor Cheng's death, entrusting Yu Bing and He Chong with government affairs. His reign saw continued conflicts with Shi Jilong and Li Shou, as well as military campaigns by various generals. Emperor Kang died at age twenty-three and was buried in Chongping Mausoleum.

translation:
Emperor Wu's name was Yan and his courtesy name was Anshi. He was the eldest son of Emperor Wen of Jin Dynasty.
He is tolerant and kind, deep and magnanimous.
During the Jiaping period of Wei Dynasty, he was granted the title of Tinghou of Beiping, and successively served as the commander of the army, the commander of the army, the general of the base, the general of the cavalry, the general of the cavalry, and the title of the protector of the army and the holiday.
He went to Wuyang in the east to welcome Changdao Xianggong to the throne, moved to Zhongfujun, and was granted the title of Xinchang Xianghou in Jin Dynasty.
When the Jin State was established, he was established as the heir apparent and granted the title of General of Fujun, Kaifu, and Deputy Second Prime Minister.
At the beginning, because Emperor Jing was the heir of Emperor Xuan and died early without any heirs, Emperor Wen regarded Emperor Wu's younger brother Sima You as a heir of Emperor Jing. He took special care of him, thinking that he would be the prime minister and should pass on his great legacy to Sima You after his death.
Chang said: This is King Jing's world, and I will not get involved.
When it was time to decide on the crown prince, Emperor Wen wanted to appoint Sima You.
He Zeng and others persisted in their dissent and said: The Zhongfu Army is smart and martial, with extraordinary talents.
The hair is on the floor and the arms are above the knees. This is not the appearance of a minister!
It’s been settled ever since.
In May of the second year of Emperor Xianxi of Wei Yuan Dynasty, he was established as the crown prince of Jin Dynasty.
On the ninth day of August, Emperor Wen died, and the prince inherited the titles of the Prime Minister and the King of Jin.
Orders were given to relax punishments, pardon sinners, appease the people, reduce corvee service, and observe three days of mourning in the country.
This month, a tall man appeared in Xiangwu, three feet tall, and said to the local Wang Shi: Now is the time of peace and prosperity.
On the seventh day of the ninth lunar month, Wei Situ He Zeng became prime minister, Zhennan General Wang Shen became Yushi Dafu, Central Guards Jia Chong became Guard General, Yi Lang Pei Xiu became Shangshu Ling and Guanglu Dafu. These people can open offices and set up staff.
In November, the Fourth Guard Army was set up for the first time to command the armies outside the city.
On the 15th, he ordered the officials of all counties to recommend talents among the people according to six standards: the first one is loyalty, respect, diligence and self-restraint, the second one is filial piety, the third one is brotherhood and friendliness, the fourth one is self-discipline, hard work and humility, the fifth one is to strictly keep faith and words and deeds can be verified, and the sixth one is to study hard to cultivate oneself.
At this time, the virtues of the King of Jin were spread all over the world, and the whole world returned to his heart.
So the emperor knew that the movement of heaven would be transferred to Jin, so he sent the Taibao Zheng Chongfeng to read the policy book and said: Inform the king of Jin that my imperial ancestor has the Yu family. In response to the order of heaven, he received the Zen of Tao and Tang and became the throne. He also gave the world to Youxia.
Only Xia Yu, Shang Tang, and Zhou Wen were able to match the sky, all because their holy virtues were like the sun and moon shining brightly.
summary: Emperor Wu, named Sima Yan with the courtesy name Anshi, was the eldest son of Emperor Wen of Jin. He was known for his tolerance, kindness, and magnanimity. During the Jiaping period of Wei, he was granted the title of Tinghou of Beiping and held various military positions. He welcomed Changdao Xianggong to the throne in Wuyang, became Zhongfujun, and was granted the title of Xinchang Xianghou in Jin. When the Jin state was established, he was made heir apparent and given the title of General of Fujun. Emperor Wen initially intended to pass the legacy to Sima You, but after opposition from He Zeng and others, Sima Yan was established as crown prince in May of the second year of Xianxi. Upon Emperor Wen's death in August, he inherited the titles of Prime Minister and King of Jin, implementing policies to relax punishments, pardon sinners, and reduce corvée.

translation:
Although Deng Ai was proud of his merits and betrayed his integrity, he still folded his hands and confessed.
Today, the two families are granted amnesty and they can return to their hometown to raise heirs.
Reviving what was destroyed, continuing what was destroyed, simplifying the law and saving punishment.
The confinement of the Wei clan was lifted.
All generals, non-commissioned officers and officials who have been mourned for three years will be sent back to mourn for three years.
People who have been mourning for three years are exempted from corvee during the period of mourning.
It exempts generals and officials below from using their families as hostages, saves the supplies that counties and states transport to the capital, prohibits Yuefu, extravagant opera skills and ornately carved hunting equipment, opens the door to public opinion, and sets up admonishers to take charge of this matter.
During this month, six phoenixes, three blue dragons, two white dragons, and one unicorn appeared in each county.
On the seventh day of the first lunar month of the second year, Shi Guang and others were sent to all parts of the country to inspect the customs and eliminate the sacrifices that were not included in the ceremony.
On the eighth day of the lunar month, a minister requested the construction of seven temples. Emperor Wu thought that the corvee was too heavy and would not allow it.
On the eleventh day, those who sang rooster songs stopped.
On the 22nd, Emperor Zunjing's wife Yang Shi became Queen Jing, and the palace she lived in was called Hongxun Palace.
On the 27th, Queen Yang was established.
In February, the confinement of the Han clan was lifted.
On the eleventh day, Sima Heng, the king of Changshan, died.
The emperor issued an edict saying: The five titles of nobility are reserved for the heroes of the past.
If a person was originally a county marquis, his second son would be granted the title of Tinghou when he ascended the title; if he was originally a township marquis, his second son would be a Guannei marquis; if he was originally a Tinghou, his second son would be a Guanzhong marquis, and they would all receive one-tenth of the title of the title.
On the 29th, Emperor Xuan was worshiped in the suburbs to be worthy of heaven, and Emperor Wen was worshiped in Mingtang to be worthy of heaven.
The edict issued on the 22nd said: In ancient times, hundreds of officials were set up to admonish the king for his mistakes. However, Bao's officials have a special job of admonishing. Today's Shizhong and Changshi are actually in this position.
Choose those who can correct violations and rescue deficiencies to take on this position.
On March 20th, people from Wu came to offer condolences, and a superior responded with an edict.
Emperor Wu said: In the past, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty recruited Wei Ta, and Emperor Guangwu recruited Gongsun Shu, but they did not follow the etiquette of a monarch towards his ministers. This was to win over those who did not surrender.
When Sun Hao began to send envoys, he did not know that Jin had established a country and established an emperor, so he only thanked him in letters.
On Wuchen day of the fifth month of Xia Dynasty, an edict was issued saying: King Chenliu has a humble character and always has to go to court for everything. This is not my request for preferential treatment and respect for him.
The person in charge of the matter explained to him that as long as it was not a major matter, it would be enough to let King Chenliu's officials come to the table.
On the day of Renzi, the hussar general Prince Boling died.
On June 25th, King Sima of Jinan died.
summary: In December of the first year of Taishi, Sima Yan ascended the throne as emperor after a formal ceremony in the southern suburbs, attended by numerous ethnic minorities. He issued an edict of general amnesty, changed the reign name, and granted various titles and rewards. He honored his ancestors with posthumous titles and established many kings and dukes. He promoted frugality, distributed palace treasures, and reformed the calendar. He also issued edicts to simplify laws, lift restrictions on certain clans, and allow officials to observe mourning periods. Throughout his reign, he conducted inspections, established institutions, and responded to natural disasters with relief efforts.

translation:
In November, they launched a large-scale attack on Wu. They sent General Zhenjun and King Yawang of Lang, Sima Qianyou to send troops to Tuzhong, General Andong Wang Hun to Jiangxi, General Jianwei Wang Rong to send troops to Wuchang, General Pingnan Hu Fen to send troops to Xiakou, General Zhennan Du Yu to send troops to Jiangling, General Longxiang Wang Jun and General Guangwu Tang Bin led the Bashu army to float down the river, with a total of more than 200,000 troops from the east and west.
Taiwei Jia Chong was appointed as the chief governor, and General Yang Ji, the champion of the line, was appointed as his deputy, with overall command of the army.
In the twelfth month, Ma Long attacked the traitor Shu Jie Feng, defeated the rebel army, killed Shu Jie Feng, Liangzhou was pacified, and Su Shen came to offer wood, bitter arrows and stone valerians.
On the first day of spring in the first year of Taikang, there were five-colored clouds surrounding the sun.
On the 25th, Wang Hun captured the cities in Laixiang, Wu Xunyang, and captured Wu Wuwei general Zhou Xing.
On the first day of February, Wang Jun, Tang Bin and others captured Danyang City.
On the third day of the lunar month, they captured Xiling again and killed the governor of Xiling, the general of the town army Liu Xian, the general of the southern expedition Cheng Xu, and the supervisor of Xiling Zheng Guang.
On the fifth day of the lunar month, Wang Jun captured the Lexiang City of Yi Dao and killed Lu Yan, the eunuch of Yi Dao, and Lu Jing, the commander of the navy.
On the 17th, Du Yu captured Jiangling and killed Wu Yan, the governor of Jiangling. Pingnan general Hu Fen captured Jiang'an.
So all the armies advanced together, and the Wu garrison garrison in Lexiang, Jingmen and other places surrendered one after another.
On the 18th, Wang Jun was appointed as the commander-in-chief of the military forces in Yi and Liang prefectures, and an edict was issued: Wang Jun and Kang Bin went eastward, wiped out the Wu army in Baqiu, and together with Hu Fen and Wang Rong, pacified Xiakou and Wuchang.
Du Yu should pacify the Lingling and Guilin areas and recruit the soldiers and civilians of Hengyang.
After the soldiers passed, the southern part of Jingzhou could be pacified with a single message. Du Yu should allocate 10,000 people to Wang Jun and 7,000 people to Tang Bin.
After Xiakou was pacified, Hu Fenying distributed 7,000 men to Wang Jun.
After Wuchang was pacified, Wang Rongying divided 6,000 men into Tang Bin.
Taiwei Jia Chong moved to Xiang, and the governor had various troops.
Wang Jun conquered Xiakou and Wuchang, and then sailed eastward. Wherever he went, he immediately pacified them.
Wang Hun and Zhou Jun fought with Wu Prime Minister Zhang Ti at Banqiao and defeated the Wu army. Zhang Ti and his generals Sun Zhen and Shen Ying were beheaded, and their heads were sent to Luoyang.
Sun Hao was at the end of his rope and asked for surrender. He gave the seal to King Langya and King Sima Qinyou.
On March 15, Wang Jun led his navy to the Stone City near Jianye, the capital of Wu. Sun Hao was so frightened that he bound his hands, carried the coffin, and surrendered in front of the military gate.
Wang Jun held the emperor's talisman, untied Sun Hao, burned the coffin, and sent it to the capital.
After collecting Wu's books and records, we found that in this battle against Wu, a total of four states, 43 counties, 313 counties, 523,000 households, 32,000 officials, 230,000 soldiers, and a population of 2.3 million men and women were captured.
Officials below the county governor level remained in their original positions. Wu's harsh rule was removed and simple laws and regulations were implemented. The people of Wu were very happy.
summary: Emperor Wu's reign saw numerous military campaigns, including conflicts with Wu and various barbarian tribes. He expanded the empire, eventually conquering Wu in the first year of Taikang, capturing Sun Hao and unifying the realm. He implemented policies to stabilize the newly conquered territories, granted amnesty, and rewarded officials. He also faced internal challenges, such as rebellions and natural disasters, which he addressed through edicts and relief measures.

translation:
After the extravagant and harsh government in the late Wei Dynasty, the people longed for the simplicity of ancient times, so they encouraged respect and simplicity, and urged honesty and lack of desire. A minister once reported that the green silk rope used to guard the cattle was broken, and he issued an edict to replace it with green hemp. He was to be lenient and graceful in his dealings with the court, and his laws were consistent. After the Ping Wu Dynasty, the world was stable, so he neglected political affairs, indulged in banquets, doted on the queen's family, relatives and nobles were in power, old ministers were not allowed to hold full-time posts, and the laws and regulations were disordered or abandoned. Please ask for bribes.
In his later years, he knew clearly that Emperor Hui could not shoulder the important responsibilities of the country, but relied on the wisdom of the emperor and his grandson and did not make up his mind to depose the prince.
He was also worried that the emperor's grandson was not born to Empress Jia and would eventually be in danger, so he plotted with his confidants about the future affairs. The planners came out one after another, and the decision was still pending for a long time. Finally, using Wang You's plan, he sent the prince's brother Qin Wang Sima Cambodia to supervise Guanzhong. Chu Wang Sima Wei and Huainan Wang Sima Yun guarded the key points to strengthen the imperial family.
Fearing the threat of the Yang family in the rear party, Wang You was appointed as the Marquis of the Northern Army to lead the imperial army.
Later, the illness worsened, and all the founding fathers of the country died. The ministers were panicked, doubtful, and at a loss. After Emperor Wu recovered from his illness, he issued an edict to let Sima Liang, king of Runan, assist in the government. He also wanted to ask several young and famous courtiers to assist him, so Yang Jun hid the edict secretly and did not publish it.
Emperor Wu soon fell into a coma again, and Empress Yang actually issued an edict to make Sima Jun assist the government and urge Sima Liang to advance.
Emperor Wu's illness improved slightly and he asked King Runan if he had come. He wanted to meet with King Runan and entrust him with something, but when no reply came, Emperor Wu changed the story. The chaos in the late Western Jin Dynasty actually started at this time.
Zhi said: Emperor Wu inherited the great cause, in fact, he complied with the destiny, controlled the world, universally educated the people, replaced labor with ease, and replaced chaos with rule.
No longer allow the four parties to pay tribute with fine silk fabrics, strive to get rid of carved decorations, suppress the trend of luxury and turn to frugality, stop frivolity and superficiality and return to simplicity.
They like to be outspoken and reverent, and carefully select talents. Plastic tunnel and tomb bumper are trusted because of their simplicity and integrity. Although haze crocodile and injection boy are enemies, they are not abandoned.
Rule the world with benevolence and righteousness, win the hearts of the people because of tolerance, be majestic and generous, and have the grace of an emperor.
At that time, the people were harmonious, their customs were peaceful, and their families were prosperous. Then they managed the army, practiced martial arts, and planned to expand the territory.
God's clever calculations and grand plans. Ma Long's expedition to the west and Wang Jun's expedition to the south did not delay the opportunity. The bandits disappeared, the blades were not stained with blood, and Yang Yue was reduced to ruins.
Communicate in places that were inaccessible in previous generations, and conquer countries that were not subject to previous kings.
summary: In his later years, Emperor Wu became neglectful of political affairs, indulging in banquets and favoring the queen's family, leading to the rise of relatives and nobles in power. He failed to depose the incapable crown prince, leading to chaos after his death. Despite his initial successes, his reign ended with turmoil, as the Western Jin dynasty eventually collapsed due to his lack of foresight and poor decisions. Historians note that while he had a good beginning, his later years were marked by decline and disaster.

translation:
Emperor Jianwen's name was Yu, with the courtesy name Daowan, and he was the youngest son of Emperor Yuan.
He was very smart when he was young and was loved by Emperor Yuan.
When Guo Pu saw him, he said to people: This person must be the one who revitalizes the Jin Dynasty.
When Sima Yu grew up, he was pure and had few desires, and was especially good at talking about mysteries.
In the first year of Yongchang, Emperor Yuan issued an edict saying: King Wu Xiangong and King Xiankao Gong ruled Langye.
Father and son have been passed down from generation to generation, but the current heir has not set up a ceremony or presided over the ceremony. I am often sad about this.
His son Sima Yu is kind, wise, resourceful and generous, and can serve his ancestors respectfully to comfort his endless kindness.
Sima Yu was granted the title of King of Langxie, and his official residences were still Kuaiji and Xuancheng.
In the first year of Xianhe, Sima Yu's biological mother, Mrs. Zheng, passed away.
Emperor Jian Wen was only seven years old at the time. He cried blood when he cried to offer sacrifices to his biological mother, and insisted on wearing mourning clothes.
Emperor Cheng took pity on him and agreed to his request, so he changed his title to King of Kuaiji and assisted Sanqi as a regular attendant.
In the ninth year, he was promoted to general on the right and was awarded the title of Shizhong.
In the sixth year of Xiankang's reign, he was promoted to general of the Fu army and concurrently served as secretary and supervisor.
In the fifth month of Guichou in the summer of the first year of Jianyuan, Emperor Kang issued an edict saying: Taichang felt that the responsibility of worshiping heaven and earth and taking care of the ancestral temple can be said to be very great.
Therefore, in selecting roles throughout the ages, people who are both prestigious and knowledgeable have been chosen.
The King of Kuaiji advocated purity, worked tirelessly to pursue the Tao, took his time in high-ranking positions, and satirized the government and the public, so he allowed the King of Kuaiji to concurrently lead Taichang, and his original official position remained unchanged.
In the first year of Yonghe, Empress Dowager Chongde came to the court, and Sima Yujin was promoted to the general of the Fu army and recorded six things in Shangshu.
In the second year, the knight He Chong died, and Empress Dowager Chongde issued an edict to let Emperor Jianwen handle state affairs exclusively.
In eight years, he was promoted to Situ, but Sima Yu firmly refused.
When Emperor Mu began to perform the crowning ceremony, Emperor Jianwen asked for the return of state affairs, but Emperor Mu refused.
After the deposed emperor came to the throne, because King Langxie had no heir, he changed the title of Emperor Jianwen to King Langxie and made his son Sima Ming King of Kuaiji.
Emperor Jianwen tried his best to refuse, so although he was granted the title of King Langxie, he did not remove the title of King of Kuaiji.
In the first year of Taihe, when he was promoted to prime minister and recorded ministerial affairs, he did not need to step forward when entering the court, and did not need to say his name when paying homage. He could wear a sword and wear shoes when going to the palace. He was provided with an honor guard of sixty Yu Bao's advocating classes and swords. Emperor Jian Wen strongly recommended it.
After the deposed emperor was deposed, the empress dowager issued an edict saying: The prime minister, Lu Shangshu, and King Kuaiji are the descendants of Zhongzong. They have good virtues, noble empresses, and empresses advocate purity and emptiness, and their magic is manifested in their conduct.
Because of his position as an assistant to important ministers, he guided three generations of emperors to preside over state affairs.
summary: Emperor Jianwen, named Sima Yu with the courtesy name Daowan, was the youngest son of Emperor Yuan. He was exceptionally intelligent as a child and beloved by his father. The diviner Guo Pu predicted he would revitalize the Jin Dynasty. Sima Yu grew to be pure-hearted with few desires, particularly skilled in discussing metaphysical matters. He was granted the title of King of Langxie in the first year of Yongchang, and later became King of Kuaiji. Throughout his career, he held various high-ranking positions including General of the Right, General of the Fu Army, and concurrently served as Secretary and Supervisor.

translation:
It has been a long time since moral education spread and everyone expected it to return.
We should obey the will of God and the will of the people and ascend to the throne.
The people in charge clearly followed the regulations at that time and implemented them on time. So Grand Sima Huanwen led all the officials into the Taiji front hall, prepared the emperor's car, and went to the palace of King Kuaiji to greet Emperor Jian Wen. He changed his clothes in the court hall, wearing a plain scarf and single clothes, and bowed to the east to accept the seal ribbon.
In the eleventh month of the winter of the first year of Xian'an, Sima Yu ascended the throne as emperor.
Huan Wen left the palace and stayed in the middle hall, ordering the troops to garrison. On Yi Mao, Wen sent a petition to the emperor to depose Sima Xi, the Grand Prime Minister and King of Wuling, and his son, General Sima.
The emperor ordered Marshal Mao An, the prefect of Wei County, to lead his troops to guard the palace and change the name to Xian'an.
On the day of Xinhai, Huan Wen sent his younger brother Huan Mi to force Xincai King Sima Huang to go to the West Hall, forcing him to tell Dazai, Wuling King Sima Xi and others that he was conspiring against him. The emperor shed tears towards Sima Huang, and Huan Wen arrested Sima Huang and others and handed them over to the Tingwei.
On Guichou day, he killed the two sons of King Donghai and their mother.
At the beginning, the emperor was indifferent, pure, simple, arrogant and noble. He served as prime minister for three dynasties. Huan Wen always respected and feared him.
When the emperor received Huan Wen, he cried sadly to him. Huan Wen was so scared that he could not speak.
At this time, some officials adhered to Huan Wen's will and petitioned to kill Sima Xi, the king of Wuling, but the emperor refused.
Huan Wen insisted again and again, and the emperor personally issued an edict in reply: If the Jin Dynasty lasts for a long time, Ming Gong should implement the previous edict.
If the great fortune of the Jin Dynasty is over, then please let me make way for the sages.
Huan Wen looked at it and was so frightened that he broke into a cold sweat, his face changed, and he stopped talking.
On Yimao day, Sima Xi and his three sons were deposed and exiled to Xin'an.
On Bingchen day, Sima Chao, the new king of Cai, was exiled to Hengyang.
On Wuwu Day, an edict was issued saying: The royal family is in trouble. Emperors Mu and Ai passed away prematurely, the imperial line has long been changed, and the throne has no owner.
The King of the East China Sea is a close relative of the emperor's mother and brother. He has inherited the throne after entering the dynasty. He has been in charge for many years. He has traveled far and wide, disrupting the dynasty's agenda. Human relations have been corrupted. A great disaster is about to come. I don't know where to place the gods of my ancestors.
The Empress Dowager was deeply worried about the royal family's foundation and made a big plan in time.
Da Sima followed the will of heaven and man, coordinated with the gods' general strategy, personally led the princes, and respectfully accepted the orders of the saints.
Now that the clouds and mist have been cleared away and the royal family is clear, they will take care of me and inherit the great achievements.
Even if Yi Yin stabilized the Yin Dynasty and Bo Lu stabilized the Han Dynasty, they could not surpass them.
Because of my meager virtues, I temporarily occupy the throne. I am really worried that my vision is narrow and I will not be able to shoulder the important responsibilities. I am trembling and trembling, not knowing how to succeed.
summary: After the deposed emperor was removed, the Empress Dowager issued an edict declaring Sima Yu the rightful heir to the throne. In the eleventh month of the first year of Xian'an, he ascended as emperor. Huan Wen, who had previously deposed the former emperor, maintained significant power. When Huan Wen insisted on executing Sima Xi, the King of Wuling, Emperor Jianwen personally issued an edict refusing, stating that if the Jin Dynasty was destined to continue, Huan Wen should follow his previous edict, but if the dynasty's fortune was exhausted, he would make way for worthier men. Huan Wen was so frightened by this response that he broke into a cold sweat and abandoned the matter.

translation:
Monsters appear in Yuzhang.
In April of summer, Duke Haixi was transferred to Xichaili, Wu County.
After Yu was demoted, she was said to be his wife.
In June, an envoy was sent to consecrate King Yugou of Baekje as General of Zhendong and also as governor of Lelang.
On the day of Wuzi, the former guard general Geng hope led his troops to rebel and entered Jingkou from Hailing. Bian Wan, the prefect of Jinling, fled to Qu'a.
In the seventh month of Autumn, at Renchen, Huan Wen sent Zhou Shaosun, the internal historian of the East China Sea, to attack Geng hope, captured him, and killed him in the bustling city of Jiankang.
At the end of the year, Sima Changming, the king of Kuaiji, was made the crown prince, and the prince Sima Daozi was made king Langxie, and he also took charge of the internal history of Kuaiji.
On the same day, the emperor died in the East Hall at the age of fifty-three.
He was buried in Gaoping Mausoleum, with the temple name Taizong.
The posthumous edict asked Huan Wen to assist in state affairs, according to the story of Zhuge Liang and Wang Dao.
When Emperor Jian Wen was young, he was graceful and well behaved. He paid attention to the classics and did not care about his living environment. Even though his seat was covered with dust, he was still happy.
Once while visiting Banqiao with Huan Wen and Sima Xi, King of Wuling, Huan Wen suddenly ordered the drums to be beaten and the horns to be blown, and the carriages and horses suddenly galloped quickly, wanting to see how the two of them performed.
Sima Xi was very frightened and asked to get out of the car, but Emperor Jian Wen looked calm and did not panic at all. Heng Wen was therefore in awe of him.
Huan Wen relied on his civil and military positions to achieve great achievements many times. In addition, he abolished the old emperor and established a new emperor, which made him powerful both inside and outside the court.
Although Emperor Jian Wen was on the throne, he could only do nothing and stick to the normal way. He was often afraid of being deposed.
Previously, the disaster star entered Taiwei, and soon Haixi Gong was deposed.
When Emperor Jian Wen ascended the throne, the disaster star entered Taiwei again, which Emperor Jian Wen hated very much.
At that time, Zhongshu Lang Xichao was on duty, so the emperor called him in and told him that the length of life is of course not considered, so there should be no more abolishment of the establishment of the previous days!
Xi Chao said: Grand Sima Huanwen is consolidating the country internally and planning extraordinary things externally, and I will use my whole family to guarantee it.
When Xi Chao asked for a quick visit to his father, the emperor said to him: Please convey my greetings to your father, the country's affairs have reached this point!
Because I cannot use the right way to rectify the country, I am so ashamed that words cannot express it.
So he chanted Yu Chan's poems. The patriots were saddened by the crisis of the court, and the loyal ministers were saddened by the humiliation of the monarch. In the end, they wet their clothes with tears.
Although Emperor Jian Wen was knowledgeable, he had no grand strategy to save the world, so Xie An called him someone like Emperor Hui, who was just a bit better at talking.
The monk Zhi Daolin once said that the King of Kuaiji had a lofty appearance but no lofty spirit.
Xie Lingyun traced his actions and believed that he was a figure like King Nan of Zhou and King Xian of Zhou.
Emperor Xiaowu's name was Yao and his courtesy name was Changming. He was the third son of Emperor Jianwen Sima Yu.
On June 12, the third year of Xingning, he was granted the title of King of Kuaiji.
On July 28, the second autumn of the second year of Xian'an, he was established as the crown prince.
On this day, Emperor Jianwen died, and the prince became emperor.
The edict was issued saying: Due to my misfortune, I suddenly encountered a funeral and cried out to heaven and earth, not knowing what to complain about.
He was young and weak, and the country was in danger. He deeply felt the importance of the country and worried that he would not be able to shoulder the important responsibilities.
Relying on the ancestors to show their spirits, accumulate virtues and enjoy sacrifices, the customs of the late emperors are honest and simple, and the moral teachings of the saints are spread among the people.
summary: Emperor Jianwen was known for his graceful demeanor and disregard for material circumstances. He could remain calm even when Huan Wen deliberately created chaotic situations to test him. Despite his knowledge, he lacked grand strategies for saving the world. He was often afraid of being deposed, especially when the disaster star entered Taiwei after his ascension. He died at age fifty-three in the East Hall and was buried in Gaoping Mausoleum with the temple name Taizong.

translation:
In August, Fu Jian led his troops to cross the Huaihe River. The imperial court sent the expedition commander Xie Shi, the champion general Xie Xuan, the auxiliary general Xie Yan, and the Xizhonglang general Huan Yi to resist.
In September, an edict was issued to ask Situ and Sima Daozi, King of Ya and King of Lang, to record six items in the Secretariat.
In October, Fu Jian's younger brother Fu Rong captured Shouchun.
On the 20th, the generals fought with Fu Jian at Fei River and defeated the enemy. They captured and beheaded tens of thousands of people and captured Fu Jian's chariot and mica chariot.
On a certain day in November, General Xie An of the Imperial Guard was in Jincheng to greet the victorious troops.
On the 27th, Cao Lingdan, the eldest son of King Chenliu, was made King Chenliu.
On December 15th, because the enemy invaders had just been pacified, a general amnesty was granted to the whole country.
Xie Shi, the general of the Chinese army, was appointed as Shangshu Ling.
Lift Prohibition.
And began to increase the tax rice from the people, five stones per person.
In the past, Zhai Liao, the king of Juding, betrayed Fu Jian and raised troops in Henan. Murong Chui joined Zhai Liao from Ye and attacked Fu Jian's son Fu Hui in Luoyang.
Yang Shi, Duke of Qiuchi, fled back to Longyou and sent envoys to proclaim him his ministers.
On the 16th day of the first month of the ninth year of Taiyuan, Sima Bao, the grandson of King Wuling, was granted the title of King of Linchuan.
On the fourth day of February, Sima Zun, the son of King Sima of Xinning, was made King of Xinning.
On the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month, the emperor paid homage to the four tombs of Jianping.
Longxiang General Liu Laozhi captured Qiaocheng.
Guo Bao, the chariot general and governor Huan Chong's subordinate, attacked Xincheng, Wei Xing and Shangyong counties and surrendered them.
On February 27th, the envoy Chijie, the commander-in-chief of Jingzhou, Jiang, Liang, Ning, Yi, Jiao, and Guangzhou, and the generals of chariots and cavalry, and the governor of Jingzhou Huan Chong died.
Murong Chui joined forces with Zhai Liao from Luoyang to attack Fu Jian's son Fu Pi in Yedi.
In March, General Xie An of the Guard was appointed as the chief security officer.
Fu Jian's northern governor Shi Muronghong and Pingyang governor Murong Chong both rebelled against Fu Jian.
On April 26, 100 Tai students were added.
Zhang Tianxi was granted the title of Duke of Xiping.
He sent Zhao Tong, the governor of Jingling, to attack Xiangyang and captured it.
Fu Jian's general Yao Chang betrayed Fu Jian, raised troops in the north, and proclaimed himself king. His country was named Qin.
On the first day of June, Empress Dowager Chu of Chongde died of illness.
Murong Hong was killed by his uncle Murong Chong, who called himself the emperor's younger brother.
On July 17, he sent Sikong Sikong and Sima Chunzhi, King of Gaomi, to repair and worship Luoyang and other Five Tombs.
On the 28th, Queen Kang Xian was buried in Chongping Mausoleum.
Baekje sent envoys to pay tribute to local products.
Fu Jian and Murong Chong fought in Zhengxi, and Fu Jian's army failed.
On August 27, Sikong Xiyin died.
On September 11, the forward commander Xie Xuan attacked Fu Jian's general Yanzhou governor Zhang Chong in Juancheng and defeated him.
On the 14th, Taibao Xie'an was granted the title of Grand Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the fifteen prefectures of Yang, Jiang, Jing, Si, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, You, Bing, Liang, Yi, Yong, and Liang.
On the first day of October, there is a solar eclipse. On the seventh day of the lunar month, Sima Tan, the king of Hejian, died.
summary: Emperor Xiaowu, named Sima Yao with the courtesy name Changming, was Emperor Jianwen's third son. He was initially made King of Kuaiji, then Crown Prince, and ascended the throne upon his father's death. His reign saw significant events including the death of Huan Wen, after which the Empress Dowager briefly returned to court. The famous Battle of Fei River occurred during his reign, where Jin forces defeated Fu Jian's massive army, capturing tens of thousands of enemy soldiers.

translation:
This year, it doesn't rain from autumn until winter.
On the first day of the first lunar month in the eighteenth year of Taiyuan, an earthquake occurred.
On the fourth day of February, another earthquake occurred.
In March, Zhai Zhao invaded Henan.
On the ninth day of the sixth lunar month, floods broke out in Shixing, Nankang, and Luling, and the water was five feet deep.
In July, there was a severe drought.
In the seventh month, the traitor Sima Hui gathered his followers in Ma Tou Mountain, and Liu Laozhi sent his troops to put him down.
On August 28, Longxiang general Yang Quanqi attacked Di commander Yang Fosong in Tonggu and defeated him.
In December, Yao Chang died, and his son Yao Xing inherited the pseudo-throne.
In June of the 19th year of Taiyuan, the Queen Mother Zheng of Kuaiji was honored as Queen Mother Jian Wenxuan.
In July, floods occurred in Jing and Xuzhou, destroying the autumn crops. The imperial court sent envoys to provide relief and compensation.
On August 16, the imperial concubine Li was honored as the empress dowager, and the palace where she lived was called Chongxun Palace.
Murong Chui's eldest son attacked Murong Yong and beheaded him.
In October, Murong Chui sent his son Ernu to invade Linqiu. Wei Jian, the prefect of Dongping, fought with Murong Chui's general Yin Guo in Pinglu, and Wei Jian died in the battle.
In this year, Fu Deng was killed by Yao Xing. Fu Deng's prince Fu Chong fled to Huangzhong and assumed the throne as emperor.
In February of the 20th year of Taiyuan, the Temple of Queen Mother Xuan was built.
On the fourth day of the lunar month, Sanqi Changshi, Guanglu Dafu, Kaifu Yitong, and Shangshu ordered Lu Na to die.
On the first day of March, there is a solar eclipse. In June, there were floods in Jingzhou and Xuzhou.
In November, King Tuoba Wang Gui of Wei attacked Murong Chui's son Murong Bao in Shui Valley and defeated him.
In the first month of the 21st year of Taiyuan, the Qingshu Palace was built. In March, Murong Chui captured Pingcheng. In April, the new Yong'an Palace was built.
On the 14th, there was hail.
Murong was dying, and his son Murong Bao succeeded him to the throne.
On May 15th, Wang Cai Gong Xie Yan was appointed as Shangshu Zuopushe.
Flood.
In June, Lu Guang usurped the throne and became the emperor.
On September 20, the emperor died in Qingshu Palace at the age of thirty-five.
Buried in Longping Mausoleum.
Emperor Xiaowu was known for his intelligence and enlightenment when he was young.
When Emperor Jian Wen died, he was only ten years old. He did not attend the funeral in the evening, but came to give advice. He replied: "Weep when you are sad. What is the rule?"
Xie An once lamented that Emperor Xiaowu was as good at affairs as the previous emperor.
After the authority was established, some people were magnanimous and soon indulged in wine and sex, drinking almost all night long.
When the comet appeared at the end of the year, the emperor was very disgusted in his heart. He raised a glass of wine in Hualin Garden and prayed: Comet, I advise you to drink a glass of wine. Since ancient times, where has the emperor lived for ten thousand years?
The Taibai Star appears in the daytime year after year, and earthquakes, floods and droughts occur one after another.
Days of sobriety are rare. And since there are no upright people around him, he cannot change in the end.
summary: Emperor Xiaowu was known for his intelligence and enlightenment in youth. After establishing his authority, however, he became indulgent in wine and sensual pleasures, often drinking through entire nights. He showed little concern for celestial omens, once toasting a comet and declaring that no emperor had ever lived ten thousand years. His reign was marked by natural disasters including earthquakes, floods, and droughts. He died suddenly at age thirty-five after drunkenly teasing his favored consort Zhang Guiren about her age, which led to her killing him in anger. He was buried in Longping Mausoleum.

translation:
At that time, Zhang Guiren was favored and she was nearly thirty years old. The emperor teased her and said: "You should be abandoned according to your age."
Zhang Guiren was secretly angry. At night, the emperor got drunk and died suddenly.
At that time, Sima Daozi was fatuous and confused, and Sima Yuan showed his power and did not even pursue the criminals.
At the beginning, Emperor Jian Wen saw the text predicting good and bad luck and said: The national destiny of the Jin Dynasty failed in the hands of Changming.
When Emperor Xiaowu was still a fetus, Empress Dowager Li dreamed that the man of God said to her: If you give birth to a boy, the character will be "Changming".
When he was born, it was bright in the east, so he took the word "Changming" as his character.
Emperor Jian Wen later understood and burst into tears.
When the Qingshu Palace was built, knowledgeable people believed that the sound of "Qingshu" was the sound of "Chu", which meant a sign of sadness and sadness.
Soon after the emperor died, the fortune of the Jin Dynasty collapsed.
Shi Chen said: The historical books in the past said: "How can a king rise without being deposed? If he is as outstanding as a god, he will inherit the throne with glory, cross the thick clouds with high head, and cross the river with leaps."
Shaokang only had one brigade of troops, so he won the throne of the Xia king; Chengtang only had seventy lands, but he revitalized the emperor's great cause; he was able to manage the rivers and seas after they broke out, and he was able to remedy the chaos in the sky; things are different from this, so the reasons are also different.
Emperor Jian Wen was in a difficult time because of his innocuous nature. Government orders were issued by the Huan family, and people of his own clan had no power.
After Taizong's death, Ningkang inherited the great cause. God was moved by his loyalty, and the treacherous officials perished on their own.
So in the west, we surpassed Jianxiu and crossed Lingshan Mountain, and in the north, we crossed the Yellow River and reached the clear Luoshui River. The warriors of Jing and Wu became powerful, famous virtuous ministers appeared one after another, and the virtuous elders were still there. Xie An can lead elegant and popular people, Wang Biaozhi can regulate discipline, Huan Chong works hard all day long, and Xie Xuan is good at military affairs.
At that time, God favored him, and the powerful Di people disappeared.
The five-foot-old boy waved his sleeves to the Yangtze River, hoping to let the flag fly to the Tianshan Mountains and guard the Xiongguan in Han Valley; but the laws and regulations were not spread, the majesty and kindness were rarely achieved, Sima Daozi was idle in the government, the national treasure gathered villains, the honor of being awarded an official title was not originally God's will, the goods obtained through corruption in prison entered the homes of the powerful, exorbitant taxes and miscellaneous taxes increased year by year, and the number of poor people increased year by year.
So Wen Ren and Xu Rong wrote to the emperor, and Lie Zong knew that they were frank and honest, but they hated hearing unfavorable advice, so they drank as much as they wanted in the morning and toasted frequently at night.
Although there are dreams of prosperity, where can I hear the words of the gods?
It can be seen that the decline of the Jin Dynasty was also man-made. As the saying goes, the political affairs of big countries have not yet declined, but the chaos of small countries has brought the country to its knees.
It happened that Fu Jian was at the moment when his misfortune was approaching. Isn't it funny to abandon his defeated troops and call Mi Mi the "Wu"?
Praise says: A king is like a crown, his fortune is not always good.
Emperor Jian was quiet and inactive, leaving no disaster behind.
When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, the traitor disappeared naturally.
Yan Zhizhi fought for the road, and Uncle Zheng parted ways.
The sponsors came to the emperor's banquet, and the beautiful women persuaded them to drink wine.
The autumn wind is sluggish, and human affairs are the first to decline.
summary: The historical commentary notes that Emperor Jianwen governed during difficult times with Huan family controlling government orders. After Emperor Xiaowu's ascension, treacherous officials perished naturally, and capable ministers like Xie An, Wang Biaozhi, Huan Chong, and Xie Xuan emerged. However, the decline of the Jin Dynasty was ultimately attributed to human failings rather than divine will.

translation:
Emperor Jing's famous teacher, named Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan.
Elegant and charming, calm and perseverant, with far-reaching strategies.
When he was young, he had a good reputation and was as famous as Xia Houxuan and He Yan.
He Yan often said: Sima Ziyuan is the one who can achieve great things in the world.
During the early years of Wei Jingchu, he served as a regular servant of Sanqi and was promoted to the rank of Central Protector for many times.
Formulate methods for selecting talents, promote people without exceeding their merits, and officials have no selfish feelings.
When Queen Xuanmu passed away, Emperor Jing was famous for his extreme filial piety in mourning.
When Emperor Xuan was about to kill Cao Shuang, he planned carefully and secretly with Emperor Jing alone. Emperor Wen didn't know what was going on and only told him the night before he was about to take action.
Afterwards, someone was sent to spy on him. Emperor Jing fell asleep as usual, but Emperor Wen could not sleep peacefully.
In the early morning, the troops gathered at Simamen. Emperor Jing was calm both inside and outside, and the arrangements were very strict.
Emperor Xuan said: This son is really good after all.
At the beginning, Emperor Jing secretly took in three thousand scholars who were not afraid of death and scattered them among the people. When they arrived, they gathered them together in one morning. No one knew where these people came from.
After the incident subsided, because of his meritorious service, he was granted the title of Marquis of Changping Township, with a population of 1,000 households, and was later granted the title of General of Wei.
When Emperor Xuan died, people who discussed politics said: Yi Yin is dead, and Yi Zhi will inherit the business. The emperor appointed Emperor Jing as the general of the Fu army to assist in government affairs.
In the spring and first month of the fourth year of Wei Jiaping's reign, he was promoted to general and granted the title of Shizhong. He held the title of Commander-in-Chief, commanded all the Chinese and foreign armies, and recorded affairs of the Shangshu.
Order the officials to recommend talents, clarify the hierarchy between the young and the elderly, sympathize with the poor and lonely, and clean up those who have been abandoned.
Zhuge Dan, Mu Qiujian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun were appointed governors of the four directions; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao were in charge of the prefectures and counties; Lu Yu and Li Feng were in charge of elections; Fu Gu and Yu Song participated in making plans; Zhong Hui, Xia Houxuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Tan Feng, and Zhang Ji participated in the court meetings. They were admired by all the people and respected inside and outside the court.
Occasionally, there were people who asked for changes in the system. Emperor Jing said: "As if you don't know anything, you obey the laws of God and do it. This is what the poet praises."
The rules and regulations of three generations of ancestors should be observed; unless there is a war, they cannot be changed at will.
In the summer and May of the fifth year, Zhuge Ke, the Taifu of Wu State, besieged Xincheng. The court was worried that he would divide his troops to invade Huaisi and planned to guard various waterway ports.
Emperor Jing said: Zhuge Ke had recently gained power in Wu State, and wanted to seek temporary benefits. He gathered his troops in Hefei, hoping that he would succeed by luck and had no energy to cause trouble in Qingxu.
Besides, there is not one waterway port. If there are more guards, more troops will be needed. If there are fewer guards, it will not be enough to defend against the enemy.
summary: Emperor Jing, named Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan. He was elegant, calm, and strategic, renowned from youth alongside Xia Houxuan and He Yan. He Yan once said he would achieve great things. Serving as a regular servant of Sanqi in the early Wei Jingchu period, he was promoted to Central Protector, where he formulated talent selection methods without bias. After Queen Xuanmu's death, he showed extreme filial piety. When Emperor Xuan planned to kill Cao Shuang, he secretly strategized with Emperor Jing alone, keeping Emperor Wen unaware until the night before action. A spy found Emperor Jing sleeping calmly, while Emperor Wen could not rest. At dawn, troops gathered at Simamen, and Emperor Jing's calm arrangements impressed Emperor Xuan, who praised him. He had secretly gathered three thousand fearless scholars, who assembled unnoticed. After the incident, he was made Marquis of Changping Township with 1,000 households and later General of Wei. Upon Emperor Xuan's death, he became General of the Fu army to assist in governance. In the fourth year of Wei Jiaping, he was promoted to general and Shizhong, commanding all armies and recording affairs of the Shangshu. He ordered officials to recommend talents, clarify hierarchies, and aid the poor. He appointed governors like Zhuge Dan and Mu Qiujian, and officials like Wang Ji and Deng Ai, earning admiration. When asked about system changes, he advocated following ancestral laws unless war necessitated change. In the fifth year, Wu's Zhuge Ke besieged Xincheng. Emperor Jing predicted he would concentrate forces in Hefei, not trouble Qingxu, and advised against excessive guards. He sent General Guanqiu Jian and others to resist, ordering high forts for defense. After months, Zhuge Ke's forces were exhausted, and Emperor Jing's counterattack killed over 10,000 enemies.

translation:
Zhuge Ke indeed concentrated his troops in Hefei, just as Emperor Jing had speculated.
Emperor Jing sent General Guanqiu Jian, the general of Zhendong, Sai Zhen, the governor of Nuosu, and others to resist the enemy.
Dan Qiu Jian and Sai Zhen requested to go out to fight. Emperor Jing said: Zhuge Ke went all out to penetrate our side and put the army in danger. Their sharp edge was difficult to withstand.
Besides, the new city is small and strong, making it difficult for enemy troops to attack.
So he ordered the generals to build high forts to defend.
After several months of stalemate, Zhuge Ke's siege force was exhausted, and more than half of his troops were killed or injured.
Emperor Jing ordered Governor Wen Lian to lead his elite troops to Heyu to intercept the enemy's retreat, and Wu Danjun led the generals as his successors.
Jiang prisoner fled out of fear. Sai Xun went up to attack and defeated the enemy army, killing more than 10,000 enemies.
In the spring and first month of the first year of the fifth year, the emperor and Zhongshu Ling Li Feng, the Queen's father Guanglu doctor Zhang Ji, Huangmen Supervisor Su Shuo, Yongning Department Ling Leqian, red servant Liu Zhili and others planned to use Taichang Xing Lou Sai to replace Emperor Jing to assist the government.
Emperor Jing secretly knew about this and sent Wang Xian, his minister, to greet Kuifeng in his car.
Kuifeng was forced to follow Wang Dong to see Ji Tong, who listed his sins.
Kuifeng knew that disaster was coming, so he insulted him wantonly.
Emperor Jing was angry and sent warriors to beat him to death with sword-tipped darts.
The arrest of Xia Houxuan, Zhang Ji and others reduced the number of three clans.
In March, he politely advised the emperor to depose Queen Zhang. The emperor then issued an edict saying: The treacherous official Li Feng and others are accustomed to listening to slander, using evil and evil, and secretly plotting evil.
The general inspector worshiped the laws of heaven and put them under the criminal law.
Zhou Bo surrendered to the Lu family, and Huo Guang captured Shangxuan's achievements, which are difficult to surpass.
9,000 additional households were added to the general's food estates, adding to the previous total of 40,000 households.
Emperor Jing declined and refused to accept.
The emperor felt deeply unsafe because Xia Houxuan and Zhang Ji were executed.
Liangcha was also worried about causing disaster and secretly planned to depose and re-establish the emperor, so he secretly advised the Empress Dowager Wei Yongning in a polite way.
In Jiaxu, the ninth month of autumn, the Empress Dowager issued an order: The emperor was too old to manage the complicated government affairs himself. He indulged in favors from the inner palace, indulged in lewdness, approached actors and actresses every day, indulged their ugly behavior, welcomed the concubine's family to stay in the inner palace, destroyed the morality between people, and disturbed the moral integrity of men and women.
He was coerced by a group of villains and was about to endanger the country, so he could not continue to worship the ancestral temple.
Emperor Jing convened a gathering of ministers for discussion, and said with tears: "The Queen Mother's order is this, what should we do with the royal family?"
The ministers all said: Yi Yin exiled Taijia to bring peace to Yin, Huo Guang deposed the king of Changyi to bring peace to Mo, weighed the priorities, stabilized the country, and brought peace to the world.
The Yin and Han dynasties did this in ancient times, and Ming Gong should do the same today. All matters today must be obeyed by Ming Gong's orders.
summary: In the first year of the fifth year, Li Feng, Zhang Ji, and others plotted to replace Emperor Jing. He secretly knew, forced Li Feng to confess, and had him beaten to death. Xia Houxuan and Zhang Ji were arrested, and their three clans were reduced. He advised deposing Queen Zhang, and the emperor added 9,000 households to his estate, totaling 40,000, but he declined. After Xia Houxuan's execution, the emperor felt unsafe. Emperor Jing, fearing disaster, secretly advised the Empress Dowager to depose the emperor. In autumn, the Empress Dowager issued an order citing the emperor's misconduct. Emperor Jing convened ministers, who supported deposition. He deposed the emperor as King of Qi, killing his associates. He proposed King Pengcheng as successor, but the Empress Dowager chose Cao Mao, Duke of Gaogui Township. Emperor Jing reluctantly agreed, but worried when the new emperor showed laziness. He advised the emperor on proper conduct.

translation:
At first, Emperor Jing had a tumor on his eye and asked the doctor to remove it.
When Saizu attacked, Liangtong's eyes went in and out due to fright.
Afraid that the Sixth Army would panic, they covered their heads with a quilt. The pain was so unbearable that they bit the quilt to pieces, but no one around them knew about it.
In the leap month, the illness worsened, and Saitong was asked to take charge of the army.
He died in Xuchang in Xinhai at the age of forty-eight.
In February, Jitong's funeral carriage arrived in Kyoto from Zhudan. The emperor came to mourn in person in plain clothes.
Order the ministers to discuss the funeral arrangements.
Relevant officials discussed that Emperor Jing's loyalty had stabilized the country and his achievements had saved the world, so Huo Guang's precedent should be followed. The title of Grand Sima was added in front of the General, and fifty thousand households were added to the city, and Mi was given the title of Duke Wu.
Emperor Wen expressed his resignation and said: My late father did not dare to accept the courtesy of Prime Minister Xiang Guo Jiu Ming, and my late brother did not dare to accept the high position of Xiang Guo, all because Taizu once served as prime minister.
Now that the title of Mi is the same as that of Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen, it must be frightening.
