In the past, Xiao He, Zhang Liang, and Huo Guang all contributed to saving the situation and assisting the monarch. Xiao He's nickname was Wen Zhong, Zhang Liang's nickname was Wencheng, and Huo Guang's nickname was Xuancheng. If you must use Wenwu as your nickname, please follow the precedents of Xiao He and others when adding gifts.
The emperor agreed to the edict and named Mi Zhongwu.
After the establishment of Jin State. The additional honorary title is King Jing.
Emperor Wu accepted the concession and was honored as Emperor Jing, the mountain mausoleum was called Junping, and the ancestral temple was called Shizong.
Emperor Wen, whose name is Zishang, is the half-brother of Emperor Jing.
In the second year of Wei Jingchu's reign, he was granted the title of Xincheng Rural Marquis.
In the early years of Zhengshi, he was appointed as the lieutenant general of Diannong in Luoyang.
It was the late period of Emperor Wei Ming's extravagant style. Emperor Wen exempted him from harsh and cumbersome conditions and did not take up farming time. The people were very happy.
He was transferred to serve as a regular attendant of Sanqi.
When the general Cao Shuang was conquering Shu, he appointed Emperor Wen as the general to conquer Shu. As Xia Houxuan's deputy, he sent troops to Luo Valley and stationed himself in Xingshi.
Shu general Wang Lin attacked Emperor Wen's camp at night, but Emperor Wen lay motionless.
Wang Lin retreated, and Emperor Wen said to Xia Houxuan: Fei Zhang occupied a dangerous position to resist and hold on. We can't fight if we advance, and we can't attack by force. We should return to the army as soon as possible and think about it later.
Cao Shuang and others led their troops to retreat, and as expected, Fei Zhang led his troops to pursue them straight to the Three Ridges. After a battle and many obstacles, the Wei army was able to pass.
So he returned to the court and paid homage to Yilang.
When Cao Shuang was executed, he led the people to defend the second palace. Due to his meritorious service, he gained an additional 1,000 households.
When Shu general Jiang Wei invaded Longxi, General Guo Huai sent troops from Chang'an to defend against the enemy.
Emperor Wen was promoted to the general of Anxi and held a festival, and he stationed troops in Guanzhong to control the military affairs.
Guo Huai attacked Jiang Wei's deputy general Ju'an in Qudi, and the outcome was indecisive for a long time.
summary: The emperor later issued an edict praising Emperor Jing's virtues and granting him the title of Prime Minister, adding 9,000 households, totaling 40,000, with honors like wearing swords in court. Emperor Jing resigned from the prime ministership and advised the emperor to study and be simple. The emperor accepted. In the second year, Mu Qiujian and Wen Qin rebelled, crossing the Huaihe River with 60,000 troops. Emperor Jing led over 100,000 troops to conquer, using strategy to avoid direct conflict. He sent generals to cut off retreat, and the rebels were defeated. Wen Qin fled, and Mu Qiujian was killed. Emperor Jing, suffering from an eye tumor, endured pain during the campaign, hiding it from his troops. He died in Xuchang at age 48. His funeral followed Huo Guang's precedent, and he was posthumously named Duke Wu, later Emperor Jing. Emperor Wen, named Zishang, was Emperor Jing's half-brother. He served as a lieutenant general in Luoyang, exempting harsh taxes and pleasing the people. During Cao Shuang's campaign against Shu, he advised retreat, which proved correct. After Cao Shuang's execution, he gained 1,000 households. He defended against Shu's Jiang Wei, using strategy to force his retreat. He later led campaigns against Wu, but was defeated and lost his marquis title. He again faced Jiang Wei, predicting his tactics and defeating him. He suppressed a rebellion in Xinping, regaining his title. When Gaogui Township became king, he was made Gaodu Marquis. During Mu Qiujian's rebellion, he stayed in Luoyang. After Emperor Jing's death, he became General of the Guard, then general and Shizhong, commanding all armies. He refused high honors but was eventually made Duke of Gaodu with nine tins.

translation:
In the past, Yi Yin was a domestic slave of the Xin family. Once Sasuke made soup, he had the title of A Heng.
Relying on the established national power and the already stable foundation, Duke Zhou built his glorious mansion in Qufu and covered Guimeng.
Lu Shang was a fisherman from Pixi River. As soon as he waved his flag, he sealed the land in Yingqiu.
Since then, the situation of meager achievements and generous rewards has been unbearable. However, sages still regard this as a good talk.
Moreover, since he was the Prime Minister of the previous dynasty, he has been virtuous from generation to generation, assisting the Wei royal family and bringing peace to the world. There is no malpractice in the government and no complaints from people.
In the past, Ming Gong conquered Lingzhou in the west, bordering the desert to the north and west of Yuzhong. When he heard the news, he was frightened and obeyed.
He captured the generals of Hejian and captured tens of thousands of elite soldiers. His majesty covered the South China Sea, and his reputation shocked Mitsukoshi. The world was healthy and peaceful, and evil spirits were suppressed.
Therefore, the customs of the time were awe-inspiring, and the barbarians presented dance and music.
So the Holy Master read the old rituals from ancient times and built a glorious mansion for the public feudal state, which was prominent in Taiyuan.
Ming Gong should obey the imperial edict and accept this great blessing so that the relationship between heaven and man can be harmonious.
The first meritorious service is as glorious as that; the land's blessings are as grand as this.
Rewards are consistent with merit, and there is no excess or violation.
From then on, in the expedition, we could cross the Yangtze River in court clothes, sweep away Wu Hui, and use the source of the Yangtze River as a frontier to the west to offer sacrifices to Minshan Mountain in the distance.
Return to the army and gather your troops to command the world. There will be no one who is disobedient in the distance and no one who is not in order nearby.
Let the virtues of the Wei Dynasty shine in the Jin Dynasty; the Ming Gong's greatest achievements surpass those of Qi Huan and Jin Wen.
Facing the sea to express gratitude to Wen Bo, and climbing Jishan Mountain to salute Xu You, isn't it a grand event?
It's very fair. Who can compare with me, so why should I be humble?
Only then did Emperor Wen accept the emperor's gift.
In November, Deng Ai led more than 10,000 people from Yinping to Jiangyou, where he defeated Shu general Zhuge Zhan in Mianzhu, killed Zhuge Zhan, and had his head revealed to the public.
Marching into Luoxian County, Liu Chan surrendered.
The emperor ordered the Duke of Jin to take charge of everything as the prime minister, so Emperor Wen sent a decree to remove himself from the titles of Shizhong, Grand Governor, and Lu Shangshu.
Please appoint Deng Ai as Taiwei and Zhong Hui as Situ.
Zhong Hui conspired to rebel, so he secretly sent people to speak ill of Deng Ai.
In the first month of spring of the first year of Xianxi, a chariot was sent to arrest Deng Ai.
In Yichou, Emperor Wen and the Emperor marched westward and were stationed in Chang'an.
At that time, all the princes were in Yecheng. They ordered Zhonglang to be the military officer of Shantao March and guard in Ye. He sent the guard Jia Chongzhijie to supervise the troops and guard Hanzhong.
Zhong Hui then rebelled in Shu. The supervisor Wei Gan and the right general Hu Lie attacked Zhong Hui and killed him.
At the beginning, when Zhong Hui was attacking Shu, Shao Ti, a subordinate of Xicao, told Emperor Wen: Zhong Hui is difficult to trust and cannot be ordered to send troops.
Emperor Wen smiled and said: "We are in control of conquering Shu, but everyone says no, only Zhong Hui agrees with me."
After the reduction of Shu, the soldiers in the Central Plains missed their homeland. The people left behind in Shu were still shocked and fearful. Even if they had the intention to rebel, they were powerless.
summary: In the second year, Zhuge Dan rebelled, seeking Wu aid. Emperor Wen led 500,000 troops, using strategy to besiege Shouchun. He defeated Wu reinforcements, and after a long siege, Zhuge Dan was killed. He was made Duke of Jin with nine tins, but resigned nine times. He later planned to attack Shu, building warships and training troops. In the fourth year, he attacked Shu, sending Deng Ai and Zhong Hui. Deng Ai defeated Shu, and Liu Chan surrendered. Zhong Hui rebelled but was killed. Emperor Wen was made King of Jin, with twenty counties. He established five-class titles and sent envoys to Wu. He died at age 55, posthumously named King Wen, later Emperor Wen. His achievements included pacifying rebellions, conquering Shu, and stabilizing the realm, though he was criticized for regicide.

translation:
Emperor Xiaohuai, whose name was Chi and whose courtesy name was Fengdu, was the twenty-fifth son of Emperor Wu.
In the first year of Taixi's reign, he was granted the title of Prince of Yuzhang County.
When Emperor Hui was on the throne, members of the royal family were in chaos. The emperor was peaceful and self-restrained, thanked guests behind closed doors, paid no attention to worldly affairs, and concentrated on studying historical classics. He was very prestigious at that time.
At first he served as a regular servant of Sanqi, but when King Zhao Sima Jian usurped the throne, he was imprisoned.
After Sima Lun failed, he served as the captain of Shesheng.
Gradually he was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry, and commander of all military forces in Qingzhou, but he did not go to the town.
In the first year of Chenglei's reign, he was appointed as the general of Zhenbei and the governor of Yecheng garrison.
In December Dinghai, he was established as the emperor's younger brother.
The emperor believed that Sima Tan, the king of Qinghe, was the prince, so he was afraid and did not dare to take the responsibility.
Kaisheng, a doctor in Lu, said: The two prime ministers manage royal affairs with the aim of stabilizing the country. The crown prince has an important position and should be carried out by someone who is favored by the public. To recommend worthy people, who else but the king can do it?
King Qinghe was young and weak, and was not popular with everyone, so he entered the East Palace and returned to the feudal kingdom as King Qinghe.
Nowadays, the emperor is homeless, and the second palace has been empty for a long time. He is often worried that the Di and Qiang people will attack him, and the enemies like ants will come to the shore of the river to show off their power.
He should take advantage of the auspicious time and ascend to the position of crown prince in time, so that he can assist the emperor and pacify the house of Sesai as soon as possible, and satisfy the people's sincere and urgent wishes. Emperor Huai said: You are really my Song Ken.
So he followed Xiu Su's advice.
In the eleventh month of the first year of Guangya, Chu Zhao passed away.
Queen Jian thought that she was just a sister-in-law to the crown prince and could not be the queen mother, so she urged Qinghe King Sima Tan to enter the palace. She had already arrived at Shangshuhe, and Shi Zhonghuahun and others hurriedly summoned the crown prince.
Guiyou, that is, the emperor, granted amnesty to the world, honored Queen Yang as Queen Hui, and allowed her to live in Hongxun Palace. After honoring her biological mother, Princess Wang, as the Empress Dowager, she established the concubine as the Queen.
On the first day of Renwu, there will be a solar eclipse.
In Jihai, Sima Rong, the son of Dan Zhouchui, the king of Yue, was granted the title of King of Lecheng County.
Sima Mo, who pressed his eyes directly, killed Sima Yi, the king of Hejian, in Yongzhao.
Xin Chou appointed Zhongshu Jian as Situ, and Shangshu Zuopushe Wang Qu as Sikong.
Jiyou buried Emperor Xiaohui in Zhukenqiu.
Kui Bao's general Kui Zheng invaded Luan Ye.
On the first day of spring in the first year of Yongjia, on the first day of the first lunar month, Guichou Shuo, a general amnesty was granted to the whole country, the reign name was changed, and the punishment of the three clans of Lian was abolished.
He asked Taifu and Shuhai King Sima Yue to assist the government and killed Zhuge Mei, the censor Zhongcheng.
summary: Emperor Xiaohuai, named Sima Chi, was the twenty-fifth son of Emperor Wu. He was made Prince of Yuzhang in the first year of Taixi. During Emperor Hui's reign, amid royal chaos, he remained peaceful and reclusive, studying classics and gaining prestige. He served as a regular attendant but was imprisoned when Sima Jian usurped the throne. After Sima Lun's failure, he held various military posts, including general of chariots and cavalry. In the first year of Chenglei, he became general of Zhenbei and governor of Yecheng. In December, he was made emperor's younger brother but feared taking responsibility due to Sima Tan being prince. Doctor Kaisheng advised him to accept the crown prince role to stabilize the state, and he eventually ascended.

translation:
In the second month of Xinsi, Wang Mi from Donglai rebelled and invaded Qingzhou and Xuzhou. Song Ba, the governor of Changguang, and Pang and his wife, the governor of Dongmou, were both killed.
On the first day of the third month, Pingshu General Zhou Fu beheaded Chen Min and sent him to him.
Ding Mao reburied Empress Wu and Yang.
In Gengwu, Sima Quan, the king of Yuzhang, was made the crown prince.
Xin Wei, grant amnesty to the world.

Ding Chou, grant amnesty to the world.
Yang Wu looted the Hanzhong area and then defected to Li Xiong.
In the second month of Renyin, Wang Jun of Sikong was appointed as Grand Sima, General Xun Zu of Wei was appointed as Sikong, Zhang Gui, the governor of Liangzhou, was made Taiwei, Zhang Gui was made the Duke of Xiping County, and Liu Kun, the governor of Bingzhou, was appointed as the general.
In the third month of Guiyou, Shi Le captured Youzhou and killed Shi Zhong, Da Sima, Youzhou Mu, and Prince Boling. He set fire to the houses in the city and killed more than 10,000 people.
Du Sou's deputy commander Wang Zhen attacked Tao Kan, the governor of Jingzhou, in Lin Zhang, and Tao Kan fled to Tianzhong.
On the first day of April in summer, there was an earthquake.
In the fifth month of Renchen, Zhang Gui, the Taiwei, the captain who led the Qiang army, the governor of Liangzhou, and the Duke of Xiping died.
In June, Liu Yao and Tran Ran invaded Xinfeng counties, and Anton general Suo Sui attacked and defeated them.
In the seventh month of autumn, Liu Yao, Zhao Ran and others invaded Kyoto again. The leading general Qu Yun attacked and defeated them. Zhao Ran was killed by an arrow.
In September, Beizhonglang general Liu Yan captured Dunqiu and beheaded Bingxu, Shao Pan, the prefect appointed by Shi Le. Qilin appeared in Xiangping.
Shanyu sent an envoy to offer horses on behalf of Duke Yilu.
Puzi's horse gave birth to a human being.
In the first month of spring of the third year, thieves killed Zhao Pei, the prefect of Jinchang.
Xu Fu, a native of Wuxing, killed the prefect Yuan You.
Song Zhe, the servant in charge, was appointed as General Pingdong and stationed in Huayin.
On the second day of the second month, Sima Rui, the prime minister of the left and the king of Langxie, was promoted to the general governor, supervising all the Chinese and foreign military affairs. The prime minister on the right and the king of Nanyang, Sima Bao, was promoted to the prime minister.
Jin made Dai Gong Yilu the acting king.
Tao Kan, the governor of Jingzhou, defeated Wang Zhen in Baling.
Du Hong and Zhang Yan, Du Sou's generals, fought with Linchuan Nei Shi Xie in Haihun. Xie Zie failed and died in the battle.
In March, Zhou Fang, the internal historian of Yuzhang, attacked Du Hong, drove him away, and beheaded Zhang Yan in the battle.
In the fourth month of summer, there is a general amnesty for the whole world.
In May Liu Cong invaded Bingzhou.
summary: In the second year, black fog and three suns appeared. A general amnesty was declared. Yang Wu defected to Li Xiong. Wang Jun was promoted. Shi Le captured Youzhou, killing many. Du Sou's deputy attacked Tao Kan. Earthquakes occurred. Zhang Gui died. Liu Yao invaded but was defeated. Liu Yao invaded again but was defeated. Liu Yan captured Dunqiu. Qilin appeared. Yilu offered horses. A horse gave birth to a human. In the third year, thieves killed officials. Xu Fu killed the prefect. Song Zhe was stationed in Huayin. Sima Rui was promoted. Yilu was made king. Tao Kan defeated Wang Zhen. Du Hong and Zhang Yan were defeated. Zhou Fang killed Zhang Yan. A general amnesty was declared. Liu Cong invaded Bingzhou. Tombs were robbed. The emperor ordered burial of dead bones. Shi Le captured Puyang. Liu Cong invaded Shangdang. Tao Kan pacified Xiangzhou. Liu Yao invaded the north. Qu Yun attacked Qingbaicheng. Suo Sui was appointed. Liu Cong captured Feng Yi. Zhang Xuan sent the imperial seal. Thieves killed Zhao Ban.

translation:
The ministers cried and clung to the car, holding the emperor's hand tightly. The emperor could not help himself in grief.
Yushi Zhongcheng Jilang committed suicide.
Liu Yao burned the coffin, accepted the jade, and asked Song Chang to serve the emperor and return to the palace.
At the beginning, there was a nursery rhyme that said: Why is the emperor wrapped in a bean field?
At that time, Wang Jun was in Youzhou. He thought that the bean leaf was called Huo, so he killed the hermit Huo Yuan to make the nursery rhyme come true.
When the emperor went to Liu Yao's military camp, the military camp was on the wall of the bean field near the city.
Xin Chou, the emperor was taken to Pingyang and imprisoned, and Qu Yun and other officials accompanied him.
Liu Cong asked the emperor to temporarily serve as Doctor Guanglu and Marquis Huai'an.
In Renyin, Liu Cong went to the palace, and the emperor kowtowed in front of him. Qu Yun fell on the ground and cried bitterly, and then committed suicide.
Shangshu Liang Yun, Shizhong Liang Jun, Sanqi Changshi Yan Dun, Zuo Cheng Zang Zhen, Huangmen Shilang Ren Bo, Zhang Wei, Du Man and the prefects of various counties were all killed by Liu Yao, and Hua Ji fled to Nanshan.
Shi Le besieged Leping, and Sikong Liu Kun sent troops to rescue him. Shi Le was defeated, and Han Ju, the governor of Leping, fled.
Sikong Chief Shi Li Hong betrayed Bingzhou and surrendered to Shi Le.
There is a solar eclipse on the first day of December, Yi Mao.
Before long, Liu Kun fled to Ji and attached himself to Duan Pichen.
In the first month of spring of the fifth year, the emperor was in Pingyang.
Gengzi, the sky is full of rainbows, and three suns are shining at the same time.
Pingdong General Song Zhe fled to Jiangzuo.
Li Xiong sent his generals Li Gong and Luo Yin to invade Ba Shu.
In February, Liu Cong sent his general Liu Chang to attack Rongyang, and the prefect Li Ju defeated him.
In March, Langye King Sima Rui followed the emperor's will and changed his reign title, calling himself King Jin in Jiankang.
In the fifth month of summer, there is a solar eclipse.
In autumn and July, there is a severe drought, and there are locusts in Si, Ji, Qing, and Yong prefectures.
Shi Le also rushed to collect the crops of the people. At that time, people called them "Hu locusts".
In August, Liu Cong sent Zhao Gu to attack General Hua Lei in Linying and killed him.
In the tenth month of winter, there is a solar eclipse.
Liu Cong went out hunting and ordered the emperor to act as a general of chariots and cavalry, wearing a military uniform and holding a halberd as a leader. The people gathered to watch him. Some of the old ministers cried and shed tears. Liu Cong was disgusted after hearing this.
Later, at the banquet, Liu Cong asked the emperor to drink wine and rinse the wine master. When he went to the toilet, he asked the emperor to hold the toilet lid. Many of the old officials of the Jin Dynasty present here burst into tears. Shangshulang Xinbin held the emperor in his arms and cried bitterly, and was killed by Liu Cong.
In December of 1898, the emperor was killed and Zai Huyang passed away at the age of eighteen.
When the emperor inherited the throne, the Yongjia Rebellion was happening, and the world was falling apart. There were less than a hundred households in the city of Chang'an, the walls and palaces were in ruins, and forests of wormwood and thorns had grown.
summary: In the fourth year, Yilu died. Liu Yao invaded Shangjun. Zhang Shi sent troops. Shi Le captured Linqiu. Lei Zhao rebelled. A solar eclipse and locusts occurred. Liu Yao attacked the north. Qu Yun's army collapsed. Liu Yao entered Jingyang. The capital was cut off. Qu Yun defended Chang'an. Famine struck. The emperor surrendered. Liu Yao accepted the surrender. The emperor was taken to Pingyang. Qu Yun committed suicide. Many officials were killed. Shi Le besieged Leping. Liu Kun fled. In the fifth year, the emperor was in Pingyang. Rainbows and three suns appeared. Song Zhe fled. Li Xiong invaded Ba Shu. Liu Chang attacked Rongyang. Sima Rui changed the reign title. A solar eclipse occurred. Drought and locusts infested. Shi Le collected crops. Zhao Gu killed Hua Lei. A solar eclipse occurred. Liu Cong humiliated the emperor. The emperor was killed at age 18. The Yongjia Rebellion caused chaos. Chang'an was in ruins. The court lacked resources. The emperor was forced to surrender. Historians commented on the decline of the Jin dynasty, blaming weak governance, corrupt officials, and moral decay. The emperors were unable to restore order, leading to their capture and death.

translation:
Zhu Xu attacked Sima Xun in Chengdu. Sima Xun's army was defeated. Zhu Xu captured Sima Xun and killed him.
In the seventh month of autumn, Guiyou, Empress Xiao was buried in Jingping Mausoleum.
In September, during the Sino-Japanese War, Liang and Yizhou were granted amnesty.
In Xinchou, the tenth month of winter, Fu Jian's generals Wang Meng and Yang An attacked Nanxiang. Huan Huo, the governor of Jingzhou, went to rescue them. The army was stationed in Xinye, while Wang Meng and Yang An retreated.
Appointed King Sima Yu of Kuaiji as prime minister.
In December, Nanyang natives Zhao Hong, Zhao Yi and others rebelled against Wancheng, and the prefect Huan Dan fled to Xinye to defend it.
Murong Wei's general Murong Li captured Lu County and Gaoping.
In the spring of the second year of the lunar month, Yu hope, the general of Beizhonglang, committed a crime and fled to the sea.
In April of summer, Murong Wei's general Murong Chen invaded Jingling, and the prefect Luo Chong defeated them.
Fu Jian's general Wang Meng invaded Kou Liangzhou, Zhang Tianxi attacked them, and Wang Meng's army was severely defeated.
In May, the right general Huanhuo attacked Zhao Yi, but Zhao Yi escaped. Henghuo attacked, captured Murong Wei's general Zhao Pan, and escorted him to the capital.
In the ninth month of autumn, Xi Min, the internal historian of Kuaiji, was appointed as the commander-in-chief of Xu Yanqingyou's military affairs in the four states, the general of Pingbei, and the governor of Xuzhou.
In the tenth month of winter, Sima Xuan, king of Pengcheng, passed away.
In the spring of the third year, on the first day of the third lunar month, there was a solar eclipse. On Guihai day, there is a general amnesty.
In the summer of April, there are hail and tornadoes.
In the eighth month of autumn, Renyin, Shangshu Ling, General Wei, and Lantianhou Wangshu passed away.
In the fourth summer and April of Gengxu, Grand Sima Huanwen led an army to attack Murong Wei.
In the seventh month of autumn, at Xin Mao, Murong Wei's general Murong Chui led his army to resist Ju Wen, but Huan Wen defeated them.
In the ninth month of Wuyin, Huan Wen's generals Deng Xia and Zhu Xu met Murong Wei's general Fu Mobo in Linzhu, and defeated them again.
On Wuzi day, Huan Wen arrived at Fangtou.
On Bingshen day, because the grain and grass transportation could not be picked up, they burned the boats and returned.
On Xinchou day, Murong Chui caught up with and defeated Huan Wen's rear army in Xiangyi.
In October in winter, a comet flies down to the west with a thunderous sound.
On the day of Ji Si, Huan Wen gathered scattered troops and stationed them in Shanyang.
Yuzhou governor Yuan Zhen led Shouyang to rebel.
On Xinchou Day in November, Huan Wen went from Shanyang to Tuzhong to meet with King Sima Yu of Kuaiji to plan future actions.
In December, he settled in Guangling.
In the spring of the fifth year of the first lunar month of Jihai, Yuan Zhen's sons Yuan Shuangzhi and Yuan Aizhi killed Zhu Xian, the internal history of Liang, and Zhu Bin, the internal history of Runan.
In February Guiyou, Yuan Yuanzhen died. Zhu Fu, the governor of Chen County, appointed Yuan Zhen's son Yuan Jin as his heir and asked Murong Wei for help.
At the end of the fourth month of summer, Huan Wen's general Zhu Yao defeated Yuan Jin in Wuqiu.
On the first day of the seventh lunar month in autumn, there is a solar eclipse. In August Guichou, Huan Wen defeated Yuan Jin in Shouyang. In September, Fu Jian's general Wang Meng attacked Murong Wei and captured Shangdang.
The demon thief Li Hong of Guanghan and Li Jingen, the demon thief of Yizhou, gathered people and horses to make a rebellion. Li Hong claimed to be the holy king and had more than 10,000 people. Zhou Gai, the prefect of Zitong, attacked and pacified them.
In the tenth month of winter, Wang Meng defeated Murong Wei's general Murong Ping in Luchuan.
In November, Wang Meng conquered Ye, captured Murong Wei, and occupied all of his territory.
In the spring and first month of the sixth year, Fu Jian sent general Wang Jian to rescue Yuan Jin. General Huan Yi attacked and defeated Wang Jian.
On Dinghai day, Huan Wen captured Shouyang and killed Yuan Jin.
On Renchen in the third month, Zhou Chu, who oversaw the military affairs of the two states of Yining, the champion general, the governor of Yizhou, and the founding father of the city, died.
On the fifth day of the fourth month of the summer, there is a general amnesty, and food is given to the poor and the elderly and childless, with each person receiving five huks of dendrobium.
Fu Jian's general Fu Ya attacked Qiu Chi, and Qiu Chi Duke Yang Zuan surrendered.
In June, there are floods in Kyoto, Danyang, Jinling, Wujun, Wuxing, and Linhai.
In autumn and August, Zhou Shisun, the former governor of Ningzhou, was appointed as the governor of Jiajie, supervising the military affairs of the two states of Yiliang and the governor of Yizhou.
In the tenth month of winter, Sima Jun, king of Gaomi, passed away.
In the eleventh month of Guimao, Huan Wen went from Guangling to station in Baishi.
On Ding Wei day, he planned to depose the current emperor and install a new emperor. He spread rumors that the emperor had suffered from impotence when he was feuding. His favorites Xianglong, Jihao, Zhu Lingbao and others were involved in the affairs of the inner chamber, which made his two beauties Tian and Meng give birth to three sick sons. They wanted to be enfeoffed and enthroned. People were confused at that time, so Huan Wen used the deeds of Yi Yin and Huo Guang to tactfully persuade the Queen Mother.
On Jiyou day, hundreds of officials gathered in the court hall and announced the order of Empress Dowager Chongde: The royal family is in a difficult situation. Emperor Mu and Emperor Ai's fortunes were short-lived and they did not have time to raise offspring and could not establish a prince.
Langxie King Sima Yi was the emperor's half-brother according to relatives, so he was allowed to succeed the throne.
summary: Emperor Mu, named Sima Dan, became emperor at age two after his father Emperor Kang's death. His mother, the Empress Dowager, served as regent. During his reign, there were numerous military campaigns, rebellions, and natural disasters. Key events included Huan Wen's successful attack on Shu, the rebellion of Fan Wen, and the deaths of various generals and officials. The state of Zhao under Shi Jilong and later his sons experienced internal turmoil, while Murong Huang and his son Murong Jun established the state of Yan. There were also conflicts with Fu Jian, who later proclaimed himself emperor of Qin. The text records a series of battles, surrenders, and changes in leadership across various regions, including Liangzhou and Yizhou. Emperor Mu died at age nineteen and was buried in Yongping Mausoleum.

translation:
In the fifth year of spring and the first month of the year, there was a general amnesty, and five dendrobiums of rice were given to each of the widowers, widowers, and lonely people who had no means of living.
General Beizhong Lang, Commander-in-Chief Xu Yanqing, the military commanders of the five prefectures of Hebei You, and Xi Tan, the governor of Xu Yan and the second prefecture, passed away.
In February, Fan Wang, the general of the town army, was appointed as the commander-in-chief of Xu Yanqing, the military commander of the five states of Hebei You, the general of Anbei, and the governor of Xu Yan's two states.
General Pingnan, governor of Guangzhou, and Marquis of Yangxia Tenghan passed away.
In April in summer, there are floods.
Taiwei Huanwen guarded Wancheng and sent his younger brother Huanhuo to lead troops to attack Xuchang.
Fenghuang appeared in Mianbei.
In May of Dingsi, Emperor Mu died in Xianyang Hall at the age of nineteen.
He was buried in Yongping Mausoleum, with the temple name Xiaozong.
Emperor Ai's name was Sima Pi, whose courtesy name was Qianling, and he was the eldest son of Emperor Cheng.
In the eighth year of Xiankang's reign, he was granted the title of King Langxie.
In the first year of Yonghe's reign, he was appointed as a regular servant of the scattered cavalry. In the twelfth year, he was awarded the title of general of the Chinese army. In the third year of Shengping, he was promoted to the general of hussar cavalry.
In May of the fifth year of Shengping, Emperor Mu passed away.
The Empress Dowager ordered: Emperor Mu suddenly fell ill and could not be cured, and there was no successor. King Sima Pi of Langxie was an orthodox and virtuous descendant of the Zhongxing royal family.
In the past when he was in Xiankang, he should have been the crown prince.
Because he was too young to bear the national calamity, Emperor Xianzong abdicated his throne to Emperor Kang.
Now there is no one who can compare with him in terms of family ties, fame and status, so King Langxie can inherit the imperial throne.
So the officials prepared their carriages and went to King Langxie's mansion to greet him.
On the Gengshen day, King Langxie ascended to the throne of emperor and granted amnesty to the whole world.
On the day of Renxu, an edict was issued saying: I was able to accept the order of the Holy Ming and enter the court to accept the throne.
Thinking of the ancestral temple of the former kings, where the sacrifices had no owner, and the palace where the concubine mourned was empty and there was no place to stay, I felt very sad in my heart, and the five internal organs were as painful as being cut.
What the clan respects, love and etiquette are equally valued. The importance of descendants and heirs is no different from love and righteousness.
Sima Yi, the king of the East China Sea, is a close relative. He should respect the lineage of his clan and regard Sima Yi as the king of Langxie.
On the fifth day of the seventh month of autumn, Emperor Mu was buried in Yongping Mausoleum.
Murong Ke captured Ye Wang, and the guard general Lu Hu retreated to protect Xingyang.
On the night of Ji Mao in August, there was a crack in the sky, several feet wide, and there was a thunder-like sound.
In the ninth month of Wushen, Queen Wang was established.
Emperor Mu's wife, He, was called Yong'an Palace.
Lu Hu rebelled and defected to Morongwei.
In the tenth month of winter, General Fan Wang of Anbei committed a crime and was deposed as a commoner.
On Bingchen in November, an edict was issued saying: Emperor Xianzong Cheng left a legacy when he was dying. Because the current situation was difficult, he wanted to promote the customs of the high world and establish morality and justice to gain prestige, so as to revitalize the country.
However, national calamities continued. Emperor Kangdi and Emperor Mu passed away prematurely, and the continued national destiny was not prosperous.
With my meager virtues, I have inherited the legacy of the late king. I have longed for you in my heart, and my heart is broken by grief.
The righteousness of the two emperors Zhao and Mu should have been obeyed by God.
Inheriting the great cause of the country is a common practice in ancient and modern times.
It should be followed by the Xianzong to extend the lineage of the clan.
In December, Zhang Xuanliang, the governor of Jialiang Prefecture, was appointed as the military commander of Longyou, the military commander of Qiang, and the Duke of Xiping.
In the spring and first month of the first year of Longhe, Renzi received a general amnesty and changed his reign name.
summary: Emperor Ai, named Sima Pi, succeeded Emperor Mu. He was the eldest son of Emperor Cheng. The Empress Dowager declared him the rightful heir due to Emperor Mu's lack of an heir. His reign was marked by continued conflicts with Murong Wei's forces, who captured Luoyang, and the ongoing influence of Huan Wen. Emperor Ai was known for his interest in immortality, consuming elixirs that poisoned him and rendered him unable to govern, leading the Empress Dowager to resume regency. He died at age twenty-five and was buried in Anping Mausoleum.

translation:
Unexpectedly, he did not establish his moral character and would reach such a state of ignorance and disorder, violating etiquette and law.
I don’t know whose son these three evil obstacles are.
Human ethics are lost, and the reputation of ugliness spreads far and wide.
Sima Yi could not uphold the country and respect his ancestors, but he was also extremely confused and rebellious, yet he wanted to make a prince a vassal king.
It is intolerable to deceive the ancestors and shake the foundation of the royal family, but what is intolerable!
Now Sima Yi is deposed as the King of Donghai, and he returns to the mansion as the King of Donghai. The standards for enshrining and guarding are the same as those of the King of Changyi in the Han Dynasty.
It is my misfortune that I have encountered so many sorrows. Thinking of the living and the dead makes my heart feel like a knife.
The great plan of the country, the great righteousness has not been carried out.
How could I still speak when I was so sad in front of the paper?
So all the officials entered the front hall of Taiji, and that day Huan Wen asked Liu Xiang, the minister of Sanqi, to take back the emperor's seal and ribbon.
The emperor, wearing a white silk hat and single clothes, walked down the west hall and drove out of the Divine Beast Gate in an ox cart.
The ministers bid farewell respectfully, all looking at him and sighing.
The censor and eunuch led a hundred soldiers to escort him to Donghai Mansion.
At first, Huan Wen had the ambition to seize the throne and planned to perform meritorious service in Heshuo first to gain the attention and reputation of the world.
After Fangtou failed, his prestige was suddenly damaged, so he secretly planned to abolish the emperor and establish a new emperor in order to increase his power.
But he was also afraid that the emperor would stick to the right path and worry that doing so would attract criticism.
Because the affairs in the boudoir were secretive and the affairs in the bed were easy to be falsely accused, Gong Chan spread the word that the emperor was a man without sexual ability. So it was deposed.
At first, the emperor was often worried about Huan Wen. He once summoned the sorcerer Hu Qian to lower his banquet. After the hexagrams came out, Hu Qian said: The Jin royal family is as stable as a rock. Your Majesty has the slightest sign of leaving the palace.
The result turned out to be the same as Hu Qian said.
In the first month of the second year of Xian'an, the emperor was granted the title of Duke of Haixi County.
In April, he moved to Wu County. He ordered Wu Domestic Shi Diao Yi to defend himself, and sent Yu Shi Gu Yun to supervise.
In November, the demon thief Lu Ju sent his disciple Xu Long to the gate of Haixi County Duke early in the morning. He said that there was a secret edict from the Queen Mother to welcome Haixi County Duke back to restore the throne.
The emperor initially wanted to obey Xu Long, but gave up after listening to the centralized and unified advice.
Xu Long said: "The big thing is about to succeed, why do you still listen to women?"
The emperor said: I committed such a crime, but fortunately I was forgiven. How dare I act rashly!
And if the Queen Mother has an edict, she should send her confidants. Why should it be you?
You must be causing trouble.
He shouted to his attendants to tie him up, and Xu Long fled in panic.
summary: The Deposed Emperor, Sima Yi, was the half-brother of Emperor Ai. He ascended the throne after Emperor Ai's death without an heir, as decreed by the Empress Dowager. His reign saw further wars with Murong Wei and Fu Jian. Huan Wen, seeking to increase his power after a failed military campaign, deposed the emperor. Huan Wen spread rumors about the emperor's impotence and illicit affairs to justify the deposition. The emperor was deposed as the King of Donghai and later granted the title of Duke of Haixi County. He was moved to Wu County, where he lived in fear, avoiding political involvement and indulging in pleasure to preserve his life. He died at age forty-five. The text concludes with a historical commentary praising Emperor Mu's stable early reign, Emperor Ai's generosity, and the deposed emperor's wisdom in refusing a plot to restore him to the throne.

translation:
Emperor Yuan, whose name was Rui and whose courtesy name was Jingwen, was the great-grandson of Sima Yi, Emperor Xuan, and the son of Sima Jin, Prince Yagong of Lang.
He was born in Luoyang in the second year of Xianning. When he was born, there was a strange divine light, which illuminated the whole room. The manuscript on which he was placed looked like freshly cut grass.
When he grows up, he will have white hair on the left side of his forehead, a high bridge of nose, protruding brows, and bright eyes.
At the age of fifteen, he succeeded to the throne as King Langya.
A young man has a good reputation.
During the reign of Emperor Hui, the royal family was troubled. Emperor Yuan often maintained a thrifty and conciliatory attitude, thus avoiding disaster.
He is usually calm, smart and thoughtful, and does not show his talents easily, so he has not been recognized by people at the time.
Only the servant Ji Shao thought that he was an extraordinary person. He once told people: King Lang Yawang's hair and bones are different from ordinary people, so he is not a minister.
In the second year of Yuankang, he was appointed as a regular attendant of Yuanwai Sanqi.
Promoted to General Zuo, he participated in the crusade against Sima Ying, king of Chengdu. The king's division failed in the Battle of Dangyin, and Emperor Yuan's uncle, Sima Yao, king of Dong'an, was killed by Sima Ying.
Emperor Yuan was afraid of the impending disaster and wanted to flee elsewhere.
That night the moonlight was bright and the security was tight. Emperor Yuan was unable to escape and was in a difficult situation.
After a while, dark clouds covered the sky and thunderstorms broke out. The patrols relaxed and they were able to escape secretly.
Previously, Sima Ying ordered all the passes to prevent nobles from passing through. When Emperor Yuan arrived in Heyang, he was blocked by officials at the ferry.
Attendant Song Dian came from behind, hit Emperor Yuan's horse with a whip and said with a smile: Chief of the House!
The government prohibits noble people from passing through. Are you also being detained?
The officials then let Emperor Yuan pass.
Arriving in Luoyang, he welcomed the concubine back to the feudal country.
When Sima Yue, King of the East China Sea, gathered troops in Xiapi and prepared to march westward, he gave Emperor Yuan the title of General of the Auxiliary State.
Soon he added General Pingdong and the military supervisors in Xuzhou to guard Xiapi.
Soon he was promoted to General Anton and Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou's military affairs.
Sima Yue went west to meet the emperor, leaving Emperor Yuan to stay in the east.
In the early years of Yongjia, Wang Dao's strategy was adopted and he began to guard Jianye, with Gu Rong as the military commander and He Xun as the counselor. Wang Dun, Wang Dao, Zhou Qiye, and Diao Xie were all loyal ministers who respected famous people and inspected the people's sentiments. All the scholars and people in Jiangdong were sincerely convinced.
When the concubine died in the feudal country, she went to the funeral. After the burial, she returned to Jianye and added 20,000 households to Xuancheng County's fiefdom, and added the titles of General Zhendong and Kaifu Yitong.
Under the instruction of Sima Yue, he attacked Zhou Fu, the general who conquered the east, and drove Zhou Fu away.
When Emperor Huai was kidnapped and taken to Pingyang, Sikong Xunfan and others issued a proclamation to the world, recommending Emperor Yuan as the leader of the alliance.
Hua Yi, the governor of Jiangzhou, refused to obey. Xun Fan sent Zhou Guang, the internal historian of Yuzhang, and Wei Zhan, the former governor of Jiangzhou, to attack and capture him.
After Emperor Min ascended the throne, he was given the post of Prime Minister Zuo.
More than a year later, he ascended the throne as prime minister and governor, overseeing all domestic and foreign military affairs.
summary: Emperor Yuan, named Sima Rui, was born in Luoyang in 276 CE with auspicious signs. He succeeded as King of Langya at fifteen and maintained a cautious, thrifty demeanor during the political turmoil of Emperor Hui's reign, avoiding disaster. Initially unrecognized for his talents, only servant Ji Shao perceived his extraordinary nature. He held various military posts, including General of the Left and General of the Auxiliary State, and participated in campaigns against Sima Ying. After a failed battle, he narrowly escaped capture during a thunderstorm. Following Sima Yue's westward march, Emperor Yuan adopted Wang Dao's strategy and established his base in Jianye, winning the loyalty of Jiangdong's elite through respectful governance. Emperor Yuan's reign faced challenges from Shi Le's invasions, repelled by General Zu Ti. He issued proclamations offering rewards for Shi Jilong's head. He mourned ministers Zhu Song and Gu Qiu despite protocol, emphasizing the need for special rites during national decline. In 319 CE, after Emperor Min's death, he assumed the imperial title, issuing edicts on governance, frugality, and moral conduct. He banned extravagant gifts and promoted merit-based evaluations. Natural disasters like droughts and earthquakes prompted personal prayers and relief efforts. He dealt with rebellions, including those by Zhou Fu and Xu Gong, and faced military defeats against Shi Le's forces.

translation:
He sent various generals to pacify Jiangdong respectively, beheaded the rebel general Sun Bi in Xuancheng, pacified Du in Xiangzhou, and implemented amnesty in Jingyang and Yangzhou according to the emperor's decree.
When the western capital of Chang'an fell, Emperor Yuan went on an expedition. He personally wore armor and sent messages to all directions, recruiting soldiers and horses from all over the world, and marched on an appointment date.
At this time, a jade album was discovered in Lin'an, and a white jade divine seal engraved with a unicorn was found in Jiangning. The text engraved on the seal was "Longevity for Ten Thousand Years". The sun appeared with two haloes. Everyone thought this was a sign that the country would be rejuvenated.
On February 28, the first year of Emperor Jianwu's reign in the Yuan Dynasty, Pingdong General Song Zhe came to Jiankang and read out an imperial edict from Emperor Min, saying: Facing difficult times, the royal family's political order has declined.
Because of my lack of virtue and hope, after inheriting the great cause, I could not ask God to protect the Jin Dynasty forever and revive the royal industry, so that the ferocious Hu people dared to lead their dogs and sheep to persecute the royal family in the capital.
I am now imprisoned in a poor frontier city, worried about everything, and my life is hanging by a thread.
Qing met with the Prime Minister and announced my intention to have the Prime Minister take charge of the government, restore the old capital as soon as possible, repair the ancestral temple and mausoleum, and avoid the great shame of the country.
In March, Emperor Yuan wore white clothes and went to the countryside to mourn for three days.

Emperor Hui Ji, Emperor Xiaohui's name is Zhong, and his courtesy name is Zhengdu. He is the second son of Emperor Wu.
In the third year of Taishi's reign, he was established as the crown prince. He was nine years old at the time.
On April 20, the first year of Taixi, Emperor Wu died. On that day, the crown prince ascended the throne as emperor. He granted a general amnesty to sinners, changed the reign name to Yongxi, honored the empress Yang as the empress dowager, and established the crown prince Jia as the empress.
On the 13th day of the fifth lunar month, Emperor Wu was buried in Junyang Mausoleum.
On the 18th, the official rank in the world was increased to one level, and those who participated in the funeral of Emperor Wu were increased to the second level. People were exempted from taxes for one year, and officials with more than 2,000 shi were granted the title of Guanzhong Marquis.
Taiwei Yang Jun was appointed as Taifu to assist in government affairs.
On the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month in autumn, Sima Wei, the king of Guangling, was established as the crown prince, He Shao, the eunuch of the Zhongshu, as the crown prince's chief tutor, Wang Rong, the official secretary of the Ministry of Personnel, as the crown prince's Taifu, and General Yang Ji of the Wei as the crown prince's Taibao.
Nan Zhonglang General Shi Chong, Shesheng Colonel Hu Yi, Changshui Colonel Zhao Jun, and Yang Lie General Zhao Huan were sent to lead their troops to garrison in all directions. On the sixth day of the tenth lunar month in winter, Sikong Shijian was appointed as Taiwei, and Sima Tai, the former general of Zhenxi and King of Longxi, was appointed as Sikong. On the first day of spring in the first year of Yongping, Emperor Hui came to the court to celebrate, but there was no music. The edict said: I have suffered misfortune early on and have endured hardships for a long time. It is only because of the spirit of my ancestors and the loyalty and virtuousness of my ministers and ministers that I am able to entrust my small body to the princes and ministers. I don't know the great road and ancient precepts, so I am trembling with fear, day and night. The three ministers attached great importance to the country, abided by the old regulations in the palace, and always followed the system of the previous emperor, so they changed the reign name to Yongxi. However, as time passed, the new year has entered, and the new era has changed, but the old rituals are still the same.
The second year of Yongxi is now changed to the first year of Yongping.
He also issued an edict that his children and officials were not allowed to visit the mausoleum.
On the 22nd, the crown prince came of age and was crowned. On the 23rd, he went to the Ancestral Temple to pay his respects.
On the first day of the second lunar month, the following silks were given to the prince.
On the 20th, Sima Wei, the general of Zhennan and the king of Chu, and Sima Yun, the general of Zhendong and the king of Huainan, came to see him.
On the 25th, he resumed his position as secretary and supervisor.
On the eighth day of March, they killed Grand Tutor Yang Jun, Yang Jun's brother Wei General Yang Jue, Prince Taibao Yang Ji, Central Guard Zhang Shao, Sanqi Changshi Duan Guang and Yang Miao, Zuo General Liu Yu, Henan Yin Li Bin, Zhongshu Ling Jiang Jun, Dongyi school captain Wen Shu, Shangshu Wu Mao, all three tribes were wiped out.
On the ninth day of the lunar month, sinners are pardoned and the year is changed.
summary: Emperor Hui Ji, named Zhong and styled Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu. He was made crown prince at age nine in the third year of Taishi and ascended the throne on April 20, the first year of Taixi, upon Emperor Wu's death. He granted amnesty, changed the reign name to Yongxi, honored Empress Yang as empress dowager, and established Crown Prince Jia as empress. Emperor Wu was buried in Junyang Mausoleum on May 13. Officials and participants in the funeral received rank promotions, taxes were exempted for a year, and high-ranking officials were granted titles. Taiwei Yang Jun was appointed Taifu to assist in governance. In the eighth month, Sima Wei, King of Guangling, was made crown prince, with He Shao, Wang Rong, and Yang Ji as his tutors. Generals were sent to garrison various regions. In winter, Sikong Shijian became Taiwei, and Sima Tai, King of Longxi, became Sikong. In the first year of Yongping, Emperor Hui issued an edict expressing his humility and fear, changing the reign name from Yongxi to Yongping. He forbade officials from visiting the mausoleum, and the crown prince came of age and was crowned. In the second month, silks were given to the prince, and Sima Wei and Sima Yun visited. In the third month, Grand Tutor Yang Jun and others were killed, and their clans were exterminated. Empress Jia deposed the empress dowager and killed her mother. Sima Liang, King of Runan, was made Dazai to assist in government, and other nobles received appointments. Over a thousand people were ennobled, but Sima Yao and Sima Mao were later dismissed.

In the sixth month, Empress Jia used the emperor's edict to send King Sima Wei of Chu to kill Dazai, King Sima Liang of Runan, and Taibao Sima Wei.

Amnesty for prisoners in Luoyang.

King Sima Kui moved to Changsha and became the King of Changshan.

On the 20th, Sima Yue, the eldest son of Longxi King Sima Tai, was made King of East China Sea.
On September 14th, the general Qin Wang Sima Jian died.
On the 21st, Sima Xu, the general of the expedition to the west and the king of Liang, was recruited as the general of the guard and the official secretary. Sima Lun, the king of Zhao, was recruited as the general of the expedition to the west and the governor of Yong and Liang states.
On December 12th in winter, there was an earthquake in the capital.
In this year, the seventeen countries of Dongyi and the twenty-four tribes of Nanyi went to the school captain who had jurisdiction over the barbarians to contact them.
In the spring of the second year, on the first day of February, Empress Jia killed the Empress Dowager in Jinyong City.

In the fifth month, Sima Gui, King of Piling, died, and taxes were exempted for the elderly and widowed. In the sixth month, Empress Jia ordered Sima Wei to kill Sima Liang and Sima Wei, then executed Sima Wei for unauthorized killings. In the seventh month, ten counties were divided into Jiangzhou. In the eighth month, Sima Lun, King of Zhao, and Sima Yong, King of Hejian, received military commands. Sima Kui moved to Changshan, and Ma Fan and Sima Yue were made kings. During the Sino-Japanese War of the Sino-Japanese War, big meteors started from the northeast and crossed the sky.

Danyang hails.

summary: In the second year, Empress Jia killed the empress dowager. In the eighth month, a general amnesty was declared. In the ninth month, Sima Dan, King of Zhongshan, died. In the eleventh month, a great plague occurred. Hail destroyed crops in Pei. In the third year, hail fell in Xingyang and Hongnong. translation:
In March, General Pingdong and King of Qi Sima Wei raised troops to attack Sima Lun. The message was spread to various states and counties, and the army was stationed in Yangzhai.
General Zhengbei, Sima Ying, King of Chengdu, General Zhengxi, Sima Yong, King of Hejian, Sima Qi, King of Changshan, Li Yi, the governor of Yuzhou, Wang Yan, the governor of Yanzhou, General Lang of Nanzhong, and Ma Xin of the Xinye Company all raised their troops to respond to King Sima Wei of Qi, with a total of hundreds of thousands of troops from each route.
Sima Lun sent his generals Lu He to send troops to Yique, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu sent troops to Ban to fight against Sima Wei. Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao sent troops to Huangqiao to resist Sima Ying. They fought with Sima Ying's generals Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao at Bromishui. Sun Hui and others were defeated and fled.
On the first day of March, there is a solar eclipse. In April of summer, the year star appears during the day.
Sima Cheng's generals He Xu and Lu Bo defeated Zhang Hong's army in Yangzhai and killed Sun Fu and others.
On the seventh day of the lunar month, Zuo Wei General Wang Yu and Shangshu Huailing King Sima Xucui led their troops into the palace and captured Sima Lun's party members Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, etc., and they were all beheaded.
Drive Sima Lun back to his mansion. Emperor Hui took the throne anyway that day.
The ministers kowtowed and apologized. Emperor Hui said, "This is not your fault."
On the ninth day of the lunar month, Emperor Hui issued an edict saying: As an immoral person, I inherited the throne, far from being able to prosper the great cause and appease the four sides, and far from being able to impose strict punishments and prohibit traitors. As a result, Sun Xiu, the rebellious minister, committed evil wantonly and waited for an opportunity to alienate the royal family, so he stole the throne from King Zhao Sima Lun.
General Zhendong and King Cong of Qi, General Zhengbei and Wang Ying of Chengdu, General Zhengxi and King Sima Yong of Hejian, all have good virtues and are members of the royal family. They are loyal to the country and behave appropriately. They are the first to oppose the great plan and save the country.
Shangshu Xu Cui participated in the plan, and the left guard general Wang Yu and the public officials and officials coordinated the plan and personally commanded the soldiers of the camp to kill Sun Xiu and his two sons.
The former King of Zhao Sima Lun was mistaken by Sun Xiu, and he and his sons have come to Jinyong You Palace to welcome me back to the throne. I am not the only one who deserves to be lucky, but the ancestral temple and the country also depend on it.
So a general amnesty was implemented, the year name was changed, the orphans and the helpless were each given grain and five dendrobiums, and a banquet among the people was allowed for five days.
Killed Zhao Wang Sima Lun, Yiyang King Sima Wei, Jiumen Hou Zhi, etc., as well as Sima Lun's party members.
In May, Sima Shang, king of Xiangyang, was made the grandson of the emperor.
On June 15, sinners were pardoned, officials were promoted to the second level, and the guest king Sima Yan was restored to the title of King of Wu.
On the 17th, King Sima Rui of Donglai and General Wang Yu of Zuowei plotted to depose King Sima Wei of Qi. The plot was leaked, Sima Rui was deposed as a commoner, Wang Yu was executed, and the three tribes were wiped out.
On the 21st, Sima Wei, the king of Qi, was appointed as the chief commander and the commander-in-chief of the Chinese and foreign military affairs. Sima Ying, the king of Chengdu, was appointed as the general and the official secretary. Sima Yong, the king of Hejian, was appointed as the Taiwei.
The prime minister was dismissed and the Situ official was reinstated.
On the 26th, Sima Xu, the king of Liang, was appointed as the Grand Prime Minister and also held the post of Situ.
Ge Qi, the hero of King Sima Wei of Qi, was granted the title of Duke Mouping, Lu Ji was granted the title of Xiaohuang Gong, Wei Yi was granted the title of Pingyin Gong, Liu Zhen was granted the title of Anxiang Gong, and Han Tai was granted the title of Qiu Gong.
On the eleventh day of the seventh month in autumn, the son of Sima Yan, king of Wu, was made king of Han, and Sima Xi, king of Changshan, was restored to be king of Changsha.
In August, a general amnesty was implemented.
On the 16th, the people who moved to the border were exempted.
Luo Shang, the governor of Yizhou, attacked and defeated the Qiang people. On the 17th, Sima Xiang, the king of Nanping, became the king of Yidu.
summary: In the first year of Yongkang, amnesty was declared, and the reign name changed. Solar eclipses, strong winds, and blood rain occurred. Empress Jia killed the deposed prince. Sima Lun and Sima Xu deposed Empress Jia, killed Zhang Hua and others, and Sima Lun became prime minister. Sima Xu became chief minister. Sima Lun killed the deposed empress. The emperor’s grandson Sima Zang was made heir. Sima Yun attacked Sima Lun but failed and was killed. Sima Lun usurped the throne in the first year of Yongning, moving Emperor Hui to Jinyong City. Sima Wei, King of Qi, raised troops against Sima Lun, joined by Sima Ying, Sima Yong, and others. Sima Lun’s forces were defeated, and Emperor Hui was restored. Sima Lun and his party were killed. Sima Wei became chief commander, and Sima Ying and Sima Yong received high offices. In the second year of Tai’an, Sima Xu died, and Li Te rebelled in Shu. Sima Yong and Sima Ying attacked Sima Xi, King of Changsha. Emperor Hui personally led troops but was defeated. Zhang Fang entered the capital, causing destruction and famine. Sima Yue arrested Sima Xi, who was killed. Li Xiong occupied Shu. In the first year of Yongxing, Sima Ying became crown prince, but was later deposed. Emperor Hui was kidnapped to Chang’an by Zhang Fang. Sima Yong controlled the government. In the second year, Sima Yue marched west to rescue the emperor. After battles, Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang. In the first year of Guangxi, Sima Yong killed Zhang Fang. Sima Yue’s forces escorted Emperor Hui back. Emperor Hui died in Xianyang Hall at age 48, possibly poisoned by Sima Yue.

translation:

Visit the Ancestral Temple.

In August, Sima Yue, the Grand Tutor of the East China Sea, was appointed Minister, and Sima Jiuhu, the General of the Hussars and Fanyang, was appointed Sikong.
In September, Feng Song, the governor of Dunqiu, arrested Sima Ying, king of Chengdu, and escorted him to Yecheng.
Ma Teng of Dongying Company was promoted to King of Dongyan, and Ma Mo of Pingchang Company was promoted to King of Nanyang.
In the tenth month of winter, Sima Jiuhu, the king of Sikong Fanyang, died.
Liu Yu, the chief historian of Sima Jiuhu, killed Sima Ying, the king of Chengdu.

When Emperor Hui was the crown prince, all the ministers in the court knew that he was not qualified for world affairs, and Emperor Wu also had doubts about him.
Once, the officials of the East Palace were gathered together and asked the prince to decide on the government affairs of the minister, but the prince could not answer.
Concubine Jia sent her trusted aide to answer the question on the prince's behalf, quoting many scriptures.
Zhang Hong said to Concubine Jia: Your Majesty knows that the prince does not like to study. Today, you should answer questions based on the facts and do not quote ancient books.
Concubine Jia agreed with this opinion.
So Zhang Hong was asked to draft an answer sheet and the prince copied it and submitted it.
Emperor Wu was overjoyed after seeing it, and the prince's status was stabilized.
After he came to the throne, all major affairs of the state were in the hands of ministers, discipline was corrupted, bribery was common, powerful families used their nobles to dominate others, the path of loyalty and virtue was cut off, those who slandered and evil succeeded, and those who succeeded were recommended to each other. People all over the world called it "mutual market".
Wang Chen from Gaoping wrote "Shi Shi Lun", Lu Bao from Nanyang wrote "Qian Shen Lun", and Du Song from Lujiang wrote "Ren Zi Chun Qiu", all of which are cynical works.
Emperor Hui once visited Hualin Garden and heard the croaking of frogs. He asked his attendants, "Are they croaking like this for official business or for private matters?"
Someone answered: In public it is for business, in private it is private.
Later, there was war and famine in the world, and many people starved to death. Emperor Hui said: They have no food, why don't they eat meat?
Emperor Hui was confused and mostly like this.
Emperor Hui died of poisoning from eating pancakes. Some people say it was Sima Yue who poisoned him.
Shi Chen said: When an unworthy son ascends to the throne, the imperial power falls away, and those in power become close to villains.
Bao Si and his uncle had the same fortune, and Empress Xiang and Quan Rong had the same fortune.
summary: Emperor Hui was deemed unfit for rule, and his reign saw corruption and chaos. He once asked if frogs croaked for public or private reasons and suggested starving people eat meat. His death ended a tumultuous period marked by civil war and decline.

translation:
In the past, Ma Xi observed the phenomena and laws of nature with the purpose of understanding the virtues of Heaven and comprehending the true feelings between Heaven and Earth. From this, he could review the past, predict the future, reveal the truth of things, and make people and things suit their needs.
Therefore, the Book of Changes says: The heavens reveal celestial phenomena and show signs of good and bad luck, and the sages imitate these.
This is to observe the distribution and movement of the sun, moon and stars to show changes.
"Shangshu" says: The wisdom and understanding of heaven comes from the wisdom and understanding of our people.
This is to observe human ethics and culture to achieve enlightenment.
Therefore, the subtle signs of the quality of politics and religion lie in whether the people's sentiments are harmonious, changes in good and bad fortunes are in harmony with the celestial bodies and the universe, and although the gains and losses are very small, they are not unobvious.
Therefore, the three emperors were diligent and diligent, and the sun, moon and five stars followed their orbits. The sun and moon did not have the mutation of guest stars approaching thin eclipses, and the stars did not have strange phenomena of disordered movement.
Huangdi first studied the "River Map" and began to understand good and bad luck, good and evil, so his "Star Biography" is still preserved.
Later, in the Gaoyang period, Nan Zhengzhong was appointed to be in charge of astronomy, and Bei Zhengli was appointed to be in charge of geography.
When Emperor Ku was in power, he still observed the order of the sun, moon and stars.
In the Tang and Yu eras, it was the Xi family and the He family who inherited his rules, and in the Youxia era, it was Kunwu who inherited the previous rules.
However, it has been a long time and the literature and classics have not been handed down.
As for Wu Xian of the Yin Shang Dynasty and Shi Yi of the Zhou Dynasty, the historians of the vassal states, such as Zi Shen of Lu, Bu Yan of Jin, Bi Zao of Zheng, Zi Wei of Song, Gan De of Qi, Tang Mei of Chu, Yin Gao of Zhao, and Shi Shenfu of Wei, all were in charge of astronomical signs, and each discussed the fulfillment of the images.
Among them, the theories of Wu Xian, Gan De and Shi Shen Fuzhi were respected by future generations.
The tyrannical Qin Shihuang burned books, and the Six Classics were either damaged or reduced, but all the books on astronomy and stars were preserved and not destroyed.
Until the time of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty and Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Sima Tan and his son successively served as Taishi Ling and wrote the "Book of Heavenly Officials" to clarify the laws between heaven and man.
After that, Liu Xiang, the lieutenant of the Central Base, expanded the records of disaster laws in "Hong Fan" and compiled "Huang Ji Lun" to refer to past events.
When Ban Gu wrote the "Book of Han", Ma Xu wrote "Tianwen", Cai Yong, Qiao Zhou and others also wrote their own records. Sima Biao used the writings of these people to continue various previous records.
Now I have recorded everyone’s teachings in detail and written the following article.
In ancient times, there were three relevant theories proposed. One advocated the Gaitian theory, the other advocated the Xuanye theory, and the other advocated the Huntian theory.
During the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han Dynasty, Cai Yong wrote a letter to Shuofang, saying in the book: Xuan Ye's theory has no basis for learning.
All the mathematical arguments in "Zhou Bi" have been preserved, and there are many things that violate the facts when examining and testing the conditions of celestial bodies.
summary: This allowed sages to review the past, predict the future, and align human affairs with natural laws. The *Book of Changes* states that Heaven reveals signs of good and bad luck through celestial phenomena, which sages imitate. Similarly, the *Shangshu* emphasizes that Heaven's wisdom is reflected in the people's understanding. The quality of governance is linked to the harmony of people's sentiments and celestial movements. The three emperors were diligent, and as a result, the sun, moon, and stars followed their proper courses without anomalies. Huangdi studied the "River Map" to understand good and bad luck, and his "Star Biography" survives. Later rulers appointed officials to oversee astronomy and geography, but many ancient texts were lost over time. During the Yin Shang and Zhou dynasties, various historians and astronomers, such as Wu Xian, Shi Yi, and others from different states, were responsible for interpreting celestial signs. Their theories, particularly those of Wu Xian, Gan De, and Shi Shenfu, were highly regarded. Despite Qin Shihuang's book burning, astronomical texts were preserved. During the Han Dynasty, Sima Tan and his son wrote the "Book of Heavenly Officials," and later scholars like Liu Xiang, Ban Gu, Ma Xu, Cai Yong, and Qiao Zhou expanded on these records. The text then introduces three ancient cosmological theories: the Gaitian (hemispherical sky) theory, the Xuanye (infinite void) theory, and the Huntian (celestial sphere) theory. Cai Yong favored the Huntian theory, which was used in the armillary sphere observatory. The Gaitian theory, described in the "Zhou Bi," posits a round sky like an umbrella and a square earth like a chessboard, with the sun and moon moving in relation to the celestial body. The Xuanye theory, promoted by Ximeng, suggests the sky is a boundless void with stars floating freely, their movements governed by atmospheric forces.

translation:
All the books promoting Xuan Ye's theory have been lost. Only Han secretary Lang Ximeng recorded the legend of the late master: The sky has no texture at all. Looking up at it, it is so high and high that there is no limit. It is dazzling and full of energy, so it looks like a vast expanse.
For example, the loess mountains in the distance all appear cyan, while overlooking the thousand-foot-deep valley, they all appear dark. The green color is not the original color; the black color is not because of something.
The sun, moon and stars naturally float in the void, and their movements and stops all depend on the atmosphere.
Therefore, the seven stars sometimes disappear and sometimes appear, sometimes move forward and sometimes retrograde. There are no party rules for hiding and appearing, and their advancement and regression are also different. This is because they have no foundation to tie them together, so each one is different.

translation:
Human beings contain the spiritual energy between yin and yang of heaven and earth, and have emotions of sadness, joy, joy and anger.

"Biography" says: For one day, if one restrains oneself and returns to ritual, the world will return to benevolence.
Since the beginning of the world, the Sui people have drilled wood to make fire. Their ambitions have been modesty and frugality. Their feelings do not care about jade and silk. Instead, they drink the clear water on the banks of streams in spring, and set fires near forests in autumn to drive away hogs. There is nothing imperfect about it.
Xuanyuan and Zhuanxu obeyed the gods, and Yao and Yushun of Tang Dynasty investigated the archaeological system. It was passed to the prosperous Zhou Dynasty, and the regulations and systems were greatly completed.
It not only left an example of setting up hundreds of officials and formulated unchangeable laws and regulations; it also had 300 rules on etiquette and 3,000 kinds of rituals, all of which were used to promote and spread the will of God and adjust and standardize human behavior.
At the end of the Zhou Dynasty, the world's social customs changed, the king's rule declined, things went against the traditions of a beautiful country, and even the way of running a family in etiquette was lost.
Chang Jianzi asked Taishu about the etiquette of yielding and dealing with others, and he replied: "That can only be called a ceremony but not a true etiquette."
The truth that is a matter of course has been ignored ever since.
In the eleventh year of Duke Ai, Confucius returned to Lu from Wei, studied the models of the three generations, and wrote down the lessons of hundreds of kings. At that time, there was no wise king, so his ideas could not be implemented.
If sentiment is allowed to develop, benevolence will inevitably be thrown aside; if heresy is allowed to cause trouble, the style of Confucianism may be excluded.
Therefore, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty abolished the two-year mourning system, and Emperor Guangwu combined the suburban sacrifices into one.
This practice of catering to the current customs is not worthy of recognition. However, during the Yuanding period of the Western Han Dynasty and the Yongping era of the Shu Han Dynasty, they promoted education and respected the gentry, advocated Confucianism and appointed Confucian scholars. The prosperity of the two deserts era was the most beautiful in the Zao period.
Later, the small fish in the mountains became offerings in temples, and the wild boars in the swamp also went against the norm. The ritual and music system was abandoned for a long time, and the world advocated glitz, but the sacrificial etiquette was generally preserved.
During the Cao and Wei Dynasties, the rules and regulations were very good.
Wang Sheng, Gao Tanglong and others were erudite and well versed in the records of their predecessors, such as the three thousand articles of "Zhou Rites" and the seventeen articles of etiquette.
People hoped for great governance in the world, but what they caught up with at that time was not good governance. If the laws passed down from the Zhou Dynasty were used too much, they would violate the customs of the time, but the remaining chapters and books still have something for reference.

Humans possess spiritual energy and emotions, and sages established rituals to control arrogance, worship heaven and earth, and define social hierarchies, thereby ensuring good governance. The text references the concept that self-restraint and a return to ritual can lead to universal benevolence. Historically, early practices were simple, with modest ambitions and frugal customs. Over time, rulers like Xuanyuan, Zhuanxu, Yao, and Shun developed systems, which were perfected during the Zhou dynasty with detailed regulations and rituals. However, by the end of the Zhou, social customs declined, and the king's rule weakened, leading to a loss of proper etiquette. Confucius later studied ancient models but could not implement his ideas due to a lack of a wise ruler. The text then discusses the Han dynasty's efforts to revive rituals, noting that Emperor Wen abolished the two-year mourning period, and Emperor Guangwu combined suburban sacrifices. During the Yuanding and Yongping eras, education and Confucianism were promoted. However, later periods saw a decline in ritual and music systems, with a focus on glitz, though sacrificial rites were generally preserved. The Cao and Wei dynasties saw improvements, with scholars like Wang Sheng and Gao Tanglong studying ancient texts.

translation:

Therefore, the volume of "Mourning Clothes" is less than one volume, but there are many arguments and explanations.
For the three-year mourning period, Zheng Xuan said it was twenty-seven months, and Wang Su said it was twenty-five months.
Zheng Xuan said that the mourning clothes should be worn for three months after the burial, while Wang Su said that they would not be worn as soon as the funeral was over.
After the remarried stepmother passed away, Zheng Xuan said that she should be mourned, while Wang Su said that he should live with his stepmother in other people's homes and be raised before mourning for her.
For children who died under the age of eight, Zheng Xuan said that after the child was born for a month, he would cry for a day, and Wang Lu said that the day of crying should be changed to mourning for a month.
There are many situations like this.
The text of "Mourning Clothes" is very brief, and annotations are needed to understand its content. Later generations' explanations are not detailed, and the world thinks it was written by Zixia.

We can make the regulations clear according to the "Mourning Clothes Change" written by Wang Xingbao, so as to eradicate doubts and disputes, and then make the system have no two forms, all based on the same regulations.
In addition, the etiquette of dispatching the Ministry must be promulgated throughout the world, so it should not be too complicated.
The title is set at 165 articles, each of which is a volume, with a total of more than 150,000 words. I still think that the volumes are full of complicated words and most of them are repetitive.
summary: The text delves into specific debates, such as the correct duration of mourning (twenty-seven months according to Zheng Xuan, twenty-five according to Wang Su) and the proper rituals for mourning different relatives. Dali's opinions should be discussed in the court, and those in the imperial edict that cannot be implemented should be deleted. This is what Gu desires.

The population is now sparse, with less than one household left in a hundred, but the criminal law is very severe, which is not in line with Gou Jian's idea of ​​​​nurturing the people.
I believe that ancient corporal punishment should be restored to promote enlightenment in the peaceful and prosperous age.
The emperor ordered discussions both inside and outside the court.
So the hussar generals Wang Dao, Taichang He Xun, Shizhong Ji Zhan, Zhongshu Lang Yu Liang, the generals consulted the army Mei Tao, Sanqi Lang Zhang Yi and others discussed, and they believed: The system of corporal punishment has a long history.

How could an ordinary monarch like Emperor Wen of Han change it?
At that time, Xiao He and Cao Shen had passed away, and people like Zhou Bo and Guan Ying could not uphold justice.
summary: A comprehensive historical overview of the evolution of criminal law and punishment in ancient China, emphasizing the tension between benevolent governance and strict legal enforcement. It begins by contrasting ideal governance through etiquette, which fosters integrity, with reliance on criminal law, suggesting that the era of Emperor Wu was inferior to the Fuxi clan's time. The narrative underscores that natural principles govern human emotions and actions, and that benevolent policies, like those of Yao and Shun, should precede punishment to maintain harmony.
