The etiquette of the banquet is that within seven quarters of the night, congratulations and gifts are received. The princes present jade, two thousand stones for lambs, two thousand stones for geese, and four hundred stones or less for wild geese.
The third prince went up to the palace with the jade in his hands and went to the throne, facing north.
Taichang announced that the emperor stood up for the three princes.
The third prince fell to his knees.
The emperor sat down and stepped forward to offer the jade.
All the officials congratulated him, and more than two thousand stones went to the palace to shout long live and raise their glasses. When the meal is served, the apprentice holds the soup, and the big farmer holds the rice, and plays music to serve the meal.
The officials accepted the rewards, the banquet began, and music was played loudly, just like the ceremony on the first day of the first lunar month.
Wei and Jin received congratulations from the four princes and officials at all levels on the winter solstice, and held small court gatherings.
The scale of court etiquette is second only to New Year's Day.
In ancient times, there were no emperors who did not patrol the territory.
During the reign of Emperor Wei Wen, the world was divided into three parts, and border wars were frequent. The emperor's chariots were frequently dispatched, and no year was peaceful. They were probably dealing with immediate events, and were not based on the laws of the previous dynasties.
Emperor Ming visited the east three times in total. He visited the old people and provided relief to the poor in the places he passed. Sometimes he gave grain and silk as rewards, just like the ancient emperors during their inspection tours.
In the first year of his reign, Man Gong visited Luoyang County and gave different rewards to the elderly and local farm officials.
In the fourth year of Emperor Wu's reign, he issued an edict to the two thousand chief officials of the governor, saying: In ancient times, emperors inspected the mountains in all directions every year, and then the leaders of the two princes in the east and west reported their duties, or else they sent envoys to inspect.
summary: The Yangtze River region was unsettled, so morning greetings ceased. The crown prince met with descendants of previous dynasties and nobles. During New Year's gatherings, a white tiger bottle was set up for those who dared to speak out. Under the Wei Dynasty, vassal kings could not meet the emperor, except during Emperor Wei Ming's reign. During the Taishi period, officials reported that princes and nobles should pay court visits every three years, with temporary meetings allowed. The etiquette for court meetings involved holding jade, similar to the old system. In years without court visits, ministers were sent to pay respects. The emperor approved this. However, princes east of the Yangtze River did not return to their own countries, and some accepted appointments elsewhere, rendering this etiquette invalid. In the Han Dynasty, October was tentatively set as the beginning of the year due to Emperor Gao's pacification of Qin. Emperor Wu later adopted the first month as the beginning of the year but still held banquets on the first day of October and the first day of each month. The banquet etiquette involved receiving congratulations and gifts at night, with princes presenting jade and officials presenting animals. The third prince offered jade to the throne, and the emperor stood for them. Officials congratulated, and those with high salaries shouted long live and raised glasses. Music played during meals, similar to the first day of the first lunar month. Wei and Jin held small court gatherings on the winter solstice, second in scale to New Year's Day. Ancient emperors patrolled their territories, but during Emperor Wei Wen's reign, border wars prevented this. Emperor Ming visited the east three times, providing relief to the poor and rewarding the elderly. In the first year of his reign, he visited Luoyang County and gave rewards. In the fourth year of Emperor Wu's reign, he issued an edict to officials, emphasizing the importance of inspections and sending envoys to investigate political affairs and the people's sufferings. The new etiquette for patrolling mountains, offering sacrifices, and reporting on palace construction remained the same as in the past. When princes met the emperor, they set up flags to distinguish their ranks, as per the ancient ritual. However, this etiquette was not implemented until the end of the Jin Dynasty.

translation:
Does it mean that there is no such thing in the world, but I have the ambition to climb Tongshan Mountain!
I dare not deceive God.
What Jiang Ji said is beautiful, but it doesn't help me.
It is enough for the Minister of Public Affairs, Chang Shu, to read it. There is no need to discuss the matter any more, and there is no need to reply to this edict.
Although the emperor rejected Jiang Ji's memorial, he actually sent Zhitanglong to draft the etiquette of the sealing ceremony. Since the world was not unified, he did not want to hold a grand ceremony soon. When Gao Tanglong died, the matter was dropped.
When Emperor Wu pacified Wu and unified the country, in the ninth month of the first year of Taikang, Shangshu ordered Wei Xuan, Shangshu Zuopushe Shantao, Shangshu Youpushe Wei Shu, Shangshu Liu Sai, Sikong Zhanghua and others to report: We heard that since the beginning of mankind, there have been princes, but the number of years cannot be recorded.
To establish virtue, save the world, and promote benevolence and righteousness, there are seventy-four families who have climbed Mount Tai for this purpose, and there are fourteen people who know their names.
Their names and deeds were lost, and there were too many to remember without leaving any reputation.
The virtues of the Jin Dynasty began with Chong Li, who assisted Zhuan Xu, and by the Xia and Shang Dynasties, a system of inheritance from generation to generation was established in heaven and earth.
In the Zhou Dynasty, there was no stopping building meritorious deeds.
Jin's virtue increased, and the people in the world helped the Mingsheng, and the Shu Han was pacified externally. Within the four seas, people's hearts turned to Jin, and military victory actually relied on virtue.
When he arrived at your majesty, he was appointed by fate to receive the throne and expand his great cause. The people admired and followed him.
Only along the Yangtze River, Dongting Lake, Yuan River, and Xiang River, there are thugs who have relied on natural dangers and have been disobedient for generations.
His Majesty's miraculous strategic judgment ordered the army to go out for a crusade. As soon as the army showed its power, it was wiped out and pacified in dozens of days.
Binding evil people and pardoning their transgressions, clouds flowing, rain spreading, gathering around us from all directions, the influence of reputation and education reaches all parts of the world.
Even Huang Xuan's conquests, Yu the Great's far-reaching strategies, and the prosperity of the Zhou Dynasty could not exceed today's!
As for the writings on stone tablets that promote the way of saints, they are famous for their records in previous generations. They use numbers to represent objects and events to illustrate speeches. Even the ancient Hetu Luoshu does not show any signs beyond this.
We should hold grand ceremonies, salute at Zhongyue, sacrifice to heaven and earth at Mount Tai and Liangfu, issue orders to promote virtue, clarify the most noble position, enjoy blessings from heaven, treat the people sincerely, carve a mark for thousands of years, and spread a reputation that will be passed down to future generations, so that no one will not be inspired by it for a hundred generations.
This is the grand cause of the emperor and the greatest wish of God and man.
The edict said: Although the fleeing enemy invaders have been eliminated, there is still an alarm for the external blockage, and the people inside are still uneasy. There should be no discussion about the deeds of great virtue.
Wei Cui and others reported again: "Now it reaches the sea and the desert in the west. In the north of the desert, there is no one in the north and south who does not come to submit. The vast territory of Dayu's time has indeed been passed."
summary: The ritual system included sacrifices to heaven and earth. The emperor patrolled famous mountains, burned firewood to worship heaven, and reported success. During the Taihe period of Emperor Wei Ming, Jiang Ji reported that the emperor's grand ceremonies prioritized patrols and sacrifices. He argued that since ancient times, dynastic changes involved climbing Mount Tai and writing down names. He urged the emperor to perform the sealing ceremony, but the emperor declined, citing humility and the need to unify the world. Later, Emperor Wu pacified Wu and unified the country. Officials urged him to perform the sealing ceremony, but he repeatedly declined, citing the need for peace and stability. After several memorials, the emperor finally refused, stating that the time was not right.

translation:
Therefore, King Wu admired and pursued the achievements of previous generations, so according to the destiny, he added a king's title to respect his ancestors, indicating that it was not because of the son's honor that it affected the parents.
According to "Li", the young cannot give eulogies to praise the elders, the lowly ones cannot make eulogies to praise the noble ones, and the young and lowly people cannot commend the older and noble ones, so how dare they give them honorary titles!
Mozu revered the Grand Duke because he understood the words in the family motto. Xun Yue believed that there was no greater filial piety than respecting the father, so he applied the son's noble status to his parents. The words in the family motto were wrong.
As for the filial piety chapter, you don't need to buy a noble person with a distinguished title, but give more gold, silver, coins, silk and silk. It's not that a son fails to fulfill his filial piety, it's because the saint's code cannot be exceeded.
In the Spring and Autumn Period, when a concubine inherited the throne, his mother could be called Madam.
Is it possible that we should not be cautious when conferring titles on mothers because of our sons? Should we report to the ancestors of the ancestral temple and grant titles based on the orders of the previous monarchs?
I think the edict should go to court and confer the honorable lady as the Crown Princess.
Nowadays, when the emperor orders nobles to be conferred titles, it means that the son is conferring titles on his mother.
If a nobleman faces north and kneels before receiving a title, it means that the mother has become her son's minister.
Heaven is superior and earth is inferior, this is stipulated by fame and position, mother is noble and son is humble, this is the order of human relations.
Although it is intended to make the noble status higher, it actually makes her lower; although the national code is clarified, it is actually abolished.
Moreover, every move of the king must be recorded by the historian.
If the recorded policies and strategies were shown to future generations, it would probably not go well!
I think it should be reported to the temple of Sutra, saying that noble people are extremely benevolent and virtuous, and should use special etiquette to repay the kindness of upbringing.
According to the order of the ancestor's spirit, the matter does not depend on oneself.
Although the concubine and empress are the names of the monarch's spouses, there are wives and nine concubines starting from the empress, and none of them are called concubines.
It is not unfair for Duke Huan to say that the title should be promoted to Tai Fu.
If you think the title of Madam is not enough, you can call her the Crown Princess.
Huang means the king, and the king and his wife both make sense in terms of name and etiquette.
The emperor specially sent a letter to Shao to worship the imperial concubine.
On Bingchen in March, Wang Tian, ​​the eunuch and Taibao, was awarded the jade seal ribbon and ceremonial clothes, which were exactly the same as those of the Queen Mother.
He also issued an edict saying: The court minister did not show respect to the concubine. Is this in line with etiquette?
Taichang Jiang Di commented: If the status and title are not the highest, the greatest respect should not be paid.
Emperor Xiaowu posthumously awarded Concubine Zheng of Kuaiji the title of Empress Dowager Jianwen to show his respect, and issued an edict asking whether a tomb should be established.
Wang Shi replied: According to the three generations of ancestors who followed Zhongzong Jing, no tombs were opened, so we just need to change the cemetery system.
summary: Emperor Ai wanted to honor Princess Zhang, but officials debated the etiquette. Some argued that a son should not knight his father, while others cited historical precedents. The discussion concluded that the emperor should not confer titles on his mother, as it would violate the order of human relations. The emperor eventually issued an edict to worship the imperial concubine, granting her the same status as the Queen Mother. Further debates arose about the etiquette for the crown prince, with some arguing that he should call himself a minister, while others disagreed. The emperor ultimately decided to follow the old system.

translation:
The ceremony was that the emperor drove a military chariot with a white horse and red hyenas, and personally held a crossbow to shoot the sacrifices, and the sacrifices were young deer.
The Dazai Ling and the visitor each loaded the deer into the car and quickly took it to the mausoleum and the ancestral temple.
Returning to the palace, he sent envoys to deliver silk and silk rewards to the military attachés.
The ceremony of military attaches training and practicing battle formations.
The etiquette of beheading sacrifices is called Chu Liu.
The officers and soldiers all practiced the sixty-four formations of Sun Wu's Art of War.
After the troops were withdrawn, the officials below the duke lined up in Luoyang's front street. The emperor arrived. The officials below the duke bowed down and bowed. The emperor got off the car. The duke saw the emperor's face and then returned to the palace.
There is a saying in ancient times that says to get off the car, so it is only implemented at this time.
This was probably a common ritual in the Han Dynasty.
In the 21st year of Emperor Xian's reign, Wei officials reported: In ancient times, martial arts were practiced throughout the four seasons during the breaks in farming.
Modai Xijing inherited the system of the Qin Dynasty. There were no martial arts exercises in three seasons, and there was only a martial arts examination in October.
Nowadays, the war has not subsided, and the soldiers and civilians are familiar with military affairs, so there is no need for drills in all seasons.
However, an auspicious day was chosen at the beginning of autumn to review the carriages and soldiers on a large scale. It was called a military parade. On the one hand, it conformed to the etiquette name, and on the other hand, it inherited the system of the Han Dynasty.
The memorial was approved.
This winter, during the military parade, the King of Wei personally mastered the golden button war drum to direct the advance and retreat.
In the first year of Yankang, Emperor Wen of Wei became King of Wei.
At the beginning of autumn in the sixth month of the year of sending, there was a military parade in the suburbs of Shu. The ministers presided over the ceremony and praised it. The king of Wei used a canopy for his chariot and personally directed the rhythm of the golden war drum.
In October of the first year of Taihe, Emperor Wei Ming, there was another military parade.
In September of the fourth year of Taishi, the first year of Xianning, the fourth year of Taikang, and the winter of the sixth year, Emperor Wu visited Xuanwu Temple in person and reviewed the troops on a large scale, but did not personally direct the advance or retreat.
After Emperor Hui, this etiquette was abandoned.
In the fourth year of Wutong Youxing, Shaoshu ordered the left and right guards and various military camps to practice and make wild goose feather battles according to the ceremony of Da Xi.
During the Xianhe reign of Emperor Cheng, Shaoshu ordered all internal and external armies to compete in an open field in the southern suburbs, so that place was called the fighting field.
From then on, the local governors Huan, Yu and other leaders often conducted military parades and drills, but the imperial court no longer had such things.
The precedent of the Han and Wei Dynasties is that when generals are sent out to fight, Fu Jielang will confer Fu Jie and ax iron in the court hall.
Later, the new etiquette formulated by Xunjie and others was to send generals, the emperor personally visited the palace, and the minister awarded the talisman, ax and cymbal. This was based on the ancient military book where the emperor appointed generals and had to kneel and push carts for them as a grand courtesy.
summary: The fourth type of etiquette is military, used to achieve peace abroad and tranquility at home. In the Han Dynasty, military exercises were held on the day of the Beginning of Autumn, with the emperor personally shooting sacrifices. The ceremony included training in battle formations and beheading sacrifices. In the 21st year of Emperor Xian's reign, Wei officials proposed a military parade in autumn, which was approved. During the Wei Dynasty, military parades were held, but after Emperor Hui, this etiquette was abandoned. Later, local governors conducted military parades, but the imperial court no longer did so.

translation:
When Emperor Mu and Emperor Xiaowu were about to perform the crowning ceremony, they would first offer silk to the ancestral temple, and then pay homage to the ancestral temple again after the crowning ceremony.
When Emperor Hui became the crown prince, the crowning ceremony was to be held. Emperor Wu came to the palace in person and sent Sima Gui, the Prince of Gaoyang, who was also the situ, to crown the crown prince. Hua Yu, the captain of the Tunqi School, who was also the Guanglu doctor, was the master of ceremonies for the crowning ceremony.
Several emperors from Jiang Shu will perform the crowning ceremony, with musical instruments set up in advance and hundreds of officials accompanying them.
A big bed was laid in the palace in advance, and the royal order handed the crown, turban, hairpin, and uniform to the attendants. The Taiwei was responsible for tying the turban, and the Taibao crowned the king.
When the coronation was about to take place, the Taiwei knelt down and read the congratulations: "It's an auspicious month and auspicious day, the coronation begins."
The emperor respectfully thought about the great imperial cause.
Respect Wu Tian and imitate the four directions of heaven and earth.
Everything follows the ancestors and there is no end.
May you live a long and prosperous life, may Sasuke be blessed.
After the coronation, the attendant wore a black hatband. The attendant took off the emperor's crimson gauze clothes and put on the royal robes and crown.
When the matter was over, the Taibao led the ministers to toast the birthday, and everyone below the princes shouted long live three times before retreating.
According to the "Etiquette Notes", it is just a turban and crown added once.
In the tenth year of Taishi, Sima Cheng, the king of Nangong, was fifteen years old. According to the old etiquette, he should be crowned.
The officials discussed and reported: "Li, you enter youth at the age of fifteen, and the king gives birth to a son at the age of fifteen, which illustrates the appropriate time for crowning."
In addition, Han and Wei sent envoys to crown kings, which was not an ancient system.
So it was decided that all kings would be crowned at the age of fifteen and no more envoys would be sent.
Wang Biaozhi said that "Li" and "Zhuan" record that the crowning ceremony took place in the ancestral temple.
After he was crowned emperor, he went out by car to the Ancestral Temple to salute and report the success.
This is probably also imitating the ceremony in the ancestral temple.
In the fourth year of the reign of King Zhengshi of Wei Qi, he established the Queen Zhen family. The ceremony of that time has not been preserved.
In the second year of Xianning reign of Emperor Wu, the emperor came to the palace in person and sent a Taiwei to purchase the title of Empress Yang and marry her into the mourning queen.
For this reason, there was an amnesty, and there were different rewards for the princes and below, and all officials gave gifts.
In the eighth year of Taikang's reign, officials reported: As a wedding gift, the emperor's wedding used black coins, silk, and eight horses.
The princes used black coins and silk, plus bi and four horses.
The doctor used black coins and silk and added sheep.
In the Zhan Dynasty, fur horses were displayed in the atrium as gifts. The emperor added grain and the princes added Zhang. According to the etiquette of the Zhou Dynasty, the use of bi was changed to the use of Zhang. Others, such as sheep, wild goose, wine, rice, silk and silk, remained the same.
For the weddings of princes, five pieces of coins and silk were added to the betrothal gifts, wedding gifts, and wedding gifts. The husband's family had to prepare all four horses for the wedding ceremony.
summary: The fifth type of etiquette is Jia, covering banquets, crown ceremonies, and weddings. At the end of the Zhou Dynasty, these rituals were rarely practiced. The crown ceremony for emperors was not recorded in the "Zhou Rites," but it was performed for princes. The emperor's crown ceremony involved three crowns, while the crown prince was crowned twice. The ceremony was held in the ancestral temple, and the emperor personally attended. The wedding etiquette for emperors included gifts of black coins, silk, and horses. The ceremony involved sending envoys to marry the queen, with various rituals such as asking for names, accepting gifts, and personal greetings. The emperor's wedding did not include music or congratulations, as per the rites. The crown prince's wedding also followed specific protocols, with gifts and ceremonies similar to those of the emperor.

translation:
The emperor must have virtue that matches heaven and earth, harmonizes with yin and yang, gives orders, and acts in a state of trance. Signs of disaster and auspiciousness will appear due to induction. Therefore, "Shangshu" says: The way of benevolence and love is auspicious, and the indulgence of evil is unlucky, just like a shadow echoing the sound.
In the past, the Fuyi family inherited the destiny of being king, accepted the "River Map", and drew circles based on it, creating the Bagua.
When Yu controlled the flood, he was given "Luo Shu". According to its description, this is "Hong Fan".
A sage who follows his path takes truth as his treasure and is blessed by God with good fortune and no disadvantage.
Since the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, officials have been in charge of each.
Until the Yin Dynasty, Jizi occupied the position of his father's teacher and followed the example of sending great disciples.
After the Zhou Dynasty replaced the Yin Dynasty, Jizi was brought back, and King Wu humbly asked him for advice.
Jizi responded with the "Luoshu" that Yu had obtained, taught him and left instructions.
In this way, "He Yuan" and "Luo Shu" are the longitude and latitude of each other, and the Bagua and Jiu Zhang are the surface wrappers of each other.
The Taoism of the Yin Dynasty was cut off, and King Wen deduced the Book of Changes; the Taoism of the Zhou Dynasty declined, and Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Respect the yin and yang of the universe, and imitate the disasters and auspiciousness of Hong Fan, and the way of correspondence between heaven and man will be clear.
The rise of the Han Dynasty continued after the extinction of scholarship in the Qin Dynasty. During the reign of Emperor Wen, Liu Sheng created the "Da Zhuan", in which the various signs of the five elements were fully discussed.
Later, during the reigns of Emperor Jing and Emperor Wu, Dong Zhongshu studied "Gongyang Chunqiu" and began to deduce Yin and Yang, becoming the master of Confucianism.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan and Yuan Hu, Liu Xue studied "Gu Liang Chun Qiu", calculated its blessings and misfortunes, and wrote annotations for "Hong Fan", which was very different from Dong Zhongshu.
When Xingyi's son Su Ta studied the "Zuo Shi Zhuan", he discussed the "Spring and Autumn" and the Five Elements, but there were many differences and errors.
Based on the "Da Zhuan", Ban Gu adopted the comments of Dong Zhongshu, Liu Xiang, and Liu Xin in the "Five Elements Chronicles", and recorded the comments and deeds of Suimeng, Xia Housheng, Jingfang, Gu Yong, Kuiman, etc., ending with Wang Mang, and Botong auspicious variations to provide evidence for the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Generally speaking, there are three methods.
First, if the king governs according to the Tao, and his ministers assist and are loyal, and all things follow their nature, then there will be harmony, auspicious signs will appear, and the country will be peaceful.
Secondly, if the king disobeys his way, if a villain is in power, and all people lose their way, ominous omens will come true, signs of disaster will appear, and the country will perish.
Third, when emperors and ministers see disasters, they retreat and reflect on themselves, review their own moral character, and work together to make up for their mistakes. Then the disasters will be eliminated and good fortune will come.
This is roughly it.
Just give examples in this regard, interweave and review the changes at that time, and form a mixed chapter, which is worthy of reference.
When Sima Biao compiled the events after Emperor Guangwu to deduce the affairs of the Han Dynasty, the theory of disaster did not go beyond previous rules.
Now we select the things that Huang Chu mentioned about auspicious disasters and strange things after that, and write them in the scroll.
summary: The emperor's virtue must align with heaven and earth, harmonizing yin and yang, as signs of disaster or auspiciousness appear through induction. The "Shangshu" states that benevolence brings good fortune, while evil brings misfortune, like a shadow following form. In antiquity, the Fuyi family received the "River Map" to create the Bagua, and Yu was given the "Luo Shu" during flood control, forming the "Hong Fan." Sages who follow this path are blessed by God. From the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors onward, officials managed affairs. In the Yin Dynasty, Jizi served as a teacher, and after the Zhou replaced Yin, King Wu consulted Jizi, who taught him from the "Luoshu." Thus, the "He Yuan" and "Luo Shu" are intertwined, as are the Bagua and Jiu Zhang. When Yin's Taoism declined, King Wen deduced the Book of Changes; when Zhou's Taoism waned, Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals. By respecting yin and yang and imitating Hong Fan's disasters and auspiciousness, the correspondence between heaven and man becomes clear. The Han Dynasty revived scholarship after the Qin. Under Emperor Wen, Liu Sheng created the "Da Zhuan," discussing the five elements. Later, Dong Zhongshu studied "Gongyang Chunqiu," deducing yin and yang, becoming a Confucian master. During Emperor Xuan and Yuan's reigns, Liu Xue studied "Gu Liang Chun Qiu," calculating fortunes and writing annotations for "Hong Fan," differing from Dong Zhongshu. Su Ta studied "Zuo Shi Zhuan," discussing the "Spring and Autumn" and Five Elements, but with errors. Ban Gu compiled the "Five Elements Chronicles," incorporating comments from Dong Zhongshu, Liu Xiang, and Liu Xin, along with records from others, ending with Wang Mang, to provide evidence for the Spring and Autumn Annals. Generally, there are three methods: if the king governs according to the Tao, harmony and auspicious signs appear; if he disobeys, ominous omens and disasters occur; when emperors and ministers see disasters and reflect, disasters can be eliminated. Sima Biao compiled events after Emperor Guangwu, and now we select auspicious and strange occurrences from Huang Chu onward.

translation:
"Jing" says: Five elements: one is water, the second is fire, the third is wood, the fourth is metal, and the fifth is earth.
Water refers to moistening the lower part, fire refers to the flaming upper part, wood refers to straightness, gold refers to leather, and earth refers to crops.
The "Biography" says: If one does not return from the field to rest on time, does not eat and drink according to the gifts offered, does not go in and out according to the regulations, violates the farming season, and has evil plans, the tree will not be upright.
Commentary: Wood is the east.
In "Yi", the tree on the ground is "Guan".
In kingly affairs, one's majesty and appearance are impressive.
Therefore, there is a system for wearing jade when walking, there are festivals for hanging luan bells when boarding, there are regulations for three drives in the field, and there are etiquette for eating and drinking. There are regulations for going in and out, advising the people according to the seasons, encouraging farming and mulberry planting, planning and stabilizing the people. If you do this, the wood will get its nature.
If you go hunting in the fields without returning to the palace; if you indulge in food and drink without regard to the laws; if you engage in corvee work at will and violate the farming season; if you are hypocritical, evil and deceitful and harm the people's property, you will lose your nature.
The craftsmen who make chariots, bows and arrows are often in danger, and the Trojan spirit becomes strange and the creation is not straight.
In the first month of the sixth year of Huangchu, Emperor Wen of Wei, it rained and the trees froze.
Liu Xin said that there is yang above but not below, and there is yin below but no upwards, so it rains and the trees freeze because of it. This is because the evil energy is cold and the trees are not straight.
Liu Xiang said that ice represents the prosperity of yin and wood represents shaoyang, which is a symbol of noble ministers and officials.
This person will be hurt, and the yin energy will invade the wood. The wood will be cold first, so it will freeze when it rains.
In June of this year, Cai Fang and others, a soldier from Licheng County, killed the prefect Xu Zhi and occupied the county to rebel.
The prefect is like the princes in ancient times. This is the fulfillment of the harm to noble ministers.
One theory is that the frozen wood is wood, and the wood is a symbol of armor and soldiers.
That year, after the crusade against Cai Fang, and in August, the emperor himself led a navy to conquer the state of Wu, with more than 100,000 soldiers and banners stretching for hundreds of miles. He went to the Yangtze River to inspect the army, and it was Chang Yu.
In the second month of the third year of Emperor Taixing's reign, it rained and the trees froze.
In the next two years, Zhou Wei and others were killed. This was because the Yang Qi was not in harmony with the lower levels.
On Yisi, the first month of the eighth year of Emperor Mu's Yonghe reign, it rained and the trees froze.
Yin Hao was sent to the Northern Expedition in the first year, but was defeated in the second year, and Yonghe was deposed in the tenth year.
He also said that Xun Xian and Yin Hao's Northern Expedition was a sign of Huan Wen joining the alliance.
In the twelfth month of the 54th year of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, it rained and the trees froze.
summary: The "Jing" says the five elements are water, fire, wood, metal, and earth, each with specific properties. The "Biography" states that if one violates farming seasons and has evil plans, trees will not be upright. Wood represents the east, and in "Yi," it is "Guan." In kingly affairs, majesty and appearance are important, with systems for walking, boarding, hunting, and eating. If these are followed, wood gains its nature; if violated, it loses it. In the sixth year of Huangchu, rain froze trees, interpreted as yin energy harming wood. This led to rebellions and military campaigns. Similar events occurred in later reigns, such as in the third year of Taixing and the eighth year of Yonghe, where frozen trees presaged conflicts and deaths. In the second year of Wu Sunliang, beams broke due to Zhuge Ke's violations, leading to his execution. In the fifth year of Taikang, temple beams broke, foretelling Emperor Wu's death and royal chaos. In the second year of Emperor Hui, a flagpole broke during a campaign, leading to defeat. In the fourth year of Taixing, a bell guard sprouted flowers, which withered, presaging Wang Dun's rebellion and execution.

translation:
In the first month of the first year of Emperor Taining's reign, a fire broke out in Kyoto.
At this time, Wang Dun invaded and insulted the imperial court, and most of his actions were very rude. All the ministers inside and outside the imperial court were resentful and angry, which was extremely yin and yang.
In May of the second year of Emperor Xianhe's reign, the capital caught fire.
In July of the first year of Emperor Kangxi's founding, there was a fire in Wujun.
In June of the fifth year of Yonghe reign of Emperor Mu, an earthquake and fire destroyed Dongzhuzhan Hall and the end gates of the two temples.
It took more than a month for the earthquake and fire to be extinguished, and all the gold and stone were burned down.
This year Shi Jilong died, and there was great chaos and soon perished.
During the reign of Haixi Gongtaihe, Xi Min was appointed as the prefect of Kuaiji.

summary: A detailed historical account of chariots, clothing, and ceremonial regalia from ancient times through the Jin Dynasty, emphasizing their symbolic and functional roles in governance, ritual, and social hierarchy. Since antiquity, gods and ancestors used specific vehicles and attire, such as the Yellow Emperor’s black top and light red lower clothes, and Fang Xun’s vermilion chariot with white horses, aligning with calendrical systems. The "Moon Order" describes women dyeing satin in regulated shades, while flags bearing sun and moon images and jade-adorned garments were meant to inspire awe and suppress evil. translation:
Pei Ziye, whose courtesy name was Jiyuan, was a native of Wenxi, Hedong, and the eighth-generation grandson of Pei Kang, Prince Zuo of the Jin Dynasty.
His elder brother Pei Li and his younger brothers Pei Kai and Pei Chuo were all famous and were called the Four Peis.
Great-grandfather Pei Songzhi was a Taizhong doctor in the Song Dynasty.
His grandfather Pei Si was a foreign soldier of Nan Zhonglang and joined the army.
My father Zhaoming is a regular attendant of Tongzhi Sanqi.
His mother died after Ziye was born. He was raised by his grandmother. When he was nine years old, his grandmother passed away. He burst into tears and his family was surprised.
When he was young, he was studious and good at writing articles.
He started his career and entered the court as Zuo Changshi of the Wuling Kingdom of Qi. He joined the army as the King of Jiangxia on the right and resigned due to his father's death.
His behavior during the period of mourning was completely in line with etiquette. Every time he went to the tomb, the grass withered for him when he was crying, and a white rabbit crouched beside him.
In the early years of Tianjian, Shangshu Pushe Fan Yun praised his conduct and was about to report it to the emperor. However, due to Fan Yun's death, the matter was not completed.
Ren Fang, a Le'an native, had a good reputation and was admired by his descendants. Anyone who studied under him would be recommended by Ren Fang.
Ziye is Ren Fang's cousin, but he doesn't go to see him, and Ren Fang resents him.
After a long time, in addition to being granted the title of King Ancheng of the Right Army to join the army, he was immediately moved to the post of concurrently serving as Wei Zheng.
At that time, criminal judgment documents were jointly signed by officials from the three parties. Once when Ziye was absent, his colleagues signed his name. The memorial was not approved, and Ziye was implicated and was dismissed.
Someone advised him to explain the facts to Yusi, and he would be clear of fault.
Ziye smiled and replied: "Although I feel ashamed that I don't have Liu Ji's conduct, I can't get a job by litigating."
He has been deposed for a long time since then and has no hatred at all.
In the second year, Xiao Jing, Marquis of Wu Ping, was appointed as the governor of Southern Yanzhou. He was introduced to serve as the champion. After Xiao Jing was transferred, he was dismissed.
At that time, Zhongshu Fan Zhen had no contact with Ziye, but he praised him when he heard that he had good character and industry achievements.
Fan Zhenqian was appointed as the doctor of Guozi, and he immediately recommended Ziye, saying: I heard that Pei Ziye, the former secretary of the Champion Mansion, joined the army in Hedong. He was forty years old and had a few words. He was endowed with superhuman conduct when he was young. When he grew up, he developed excellent moral integrity. He followed etiquette during mourning. Grief was almost life-threatening. After the mourning period was over, he still had no food.
He was in a lower position, with a humble body and a low reputation, but his temperament was not greedy and he did not deceive his spouse. Therefore, knowledgeable people respected him and people in his hometown admired him.
Moreover, his family knowledge has been passed down from generation to generation, he has studied Confucianism and history, read a lot of books, and devoted himself to research and writing in his daily life and actions.
He is the author of twenty volumes of "Song Lue", which runs through the beginning and end, writing the history of a dynasty and writing articles and records, which are worth watching.
Moreover, the analysis of chapters and sentences is accurate and detailed, and the explanations of words can be handed down from generation to generation. If he is allowed to serve in the school, it will be a great reward for future generations, and the debate on misinformation issues such as Yikui can be found.
summary: Pei Ziye, courtesy name Jiyuan, was from Wenxi, Hedong, and a descendant of Jin Dynasty royalty. He was raised by his grandmother after his mother died at his birth, and showed deep filial piety when she passed when he was nine. Known for his studiousness and literary skill, he began his official career as Zuo Changshi of the Wuling Kingdom of Qi. His mourning period for his father was so exemplary that withered grass and a white rabbit appeared at his father's tomb. Fan Yun praised his conduct but died before reporting it to the emperor. Ren Fang, a famous scholar, resented Ziye for not visiting him, despite being a cousin. Ziye later served as a military advisor but was dismissed when a document was signed in his absence without his knowledge. He refused to litigate to clear his name, accepting the dismissal without resentment.

translation:

Immediately, he was ordered to draft an edict to Wei Xiangyuan. After accepting the edict that night, Ziye thought that it could be submitted tomorrow, so he did not start writing. When asked about the reason why he wrote quickly, Ziye replied: "People's articles are written by hand, and I wrote them with my heart alone. Although there are differences that I can see and cannot see, the modifications are the same."
Soon he was moved to the post of Vice Minister of Zhongshu, and the other posts remained as before.
In the first year of Datong, he was transferred to Hongluqing, and then concurrently served as the infantry captain.

There was no residence, so we borrowed two acres of official land and built several thatched houses.
His wife and children often suffered from hunger and cold, but he only focused on teaching. His children and nephews respected him as they served their father.
In his later years, he believed deeply in Buddhism, strictly abided by religious rules, and only ate vegetarian food throughout his life.
In the second year of Zhongdatong, he died in office at the age of sixty-two.
First, Ziye himself estimated that his death date would not be past the Gengxu year.

We must be frugal and moderate in dispatching and funeral arrangements.

Sudden loss makes people sad and missed.
He can be given as a posthumous gift to the regular attendants of Sanqi, 50,000 yuan for the funeral, and 50 pieces of cloth, and he will be buried in the near future.

Shaoling also compiled twenty volumes of "Biography of Gan Seng", two volumes of "Hundred Officials and Nine Ranks", one volume of "Fu Yi Mi Fa", one volume of "Pictures of Fang Guo Envoy", and twenty volumes of collected works, all of which have been circulated in the world.
He also wanted to compile "Qi Liang Chun Qiu" and had started drafting it, but he died before it could be completed.
His son Pei Jian was promoted to Tongzhilang.

summary: Fan Zhen later recommended Ziye, praising his moral integrity, filial piety, and scholarly achievements, including his twenty-volume "Song Lue." Despite some officials objecting to his qualifications, Ziye was appointed as Minister Bibu Lang and later as a county magistrate, where he resolved disputes through reasoning, eliminating lawsuits. He completed his great-grandfather's unfinished history, earning praise from Shen Yue and others. He was then appointed as a historian and editor, known for his broad knowledge, such as identifying the origins of envoys from the Baiti and Hua kingdoms. He served in the palace for over a decade, living frugally, giving his salary to poor relatives, and supporting his family on borrowed land. He was a devout Buddhist vegetarian in his later years. He died at sixty-two, and the emperor mourned him, granting posthumous honors and a burial. His works include "Collection of Mourning Clothes," "Continued Biography of the Pei Family," and others.

translation:
He died in the eighth year of his reign at the age of seventy-three.
Emperor Gaozu mourned and remembered him, and wrote a letter from Shao: "I was a member of the imperial family, a regular servant of Sanqi, a minister of Honglu, and a general secretary of Zhongshu. I was honest and self-respected. I never faded even when I was old. I stayed in the palace for a long time and was praised by people both inside and outside for my good deeds."
Passed away suddenly, sadly missed. Can't stop.
He has no close relatives, which makes people even more sad.
After getting dressed and putting the coffin in, he immediately sent the coffin back to his hometown, built a cemetery coffin and paid for it, and tried his best to get everything done.
You can posthumously give him a casual knight as a permanent attendant, so that he can express his condolences.
Mi's nickname is Wen Zi.
When Gu Xie was young, he was upright, upright and ambitious.
When he first took office as Tingweizheng, his clothes were thin in winter. Ji Fadu, the minister of the temple, said to people: I would like to give the short coat I am wearing to Shou Lang. I am afraid that Shou Lang will not be able to accept the food and clothing given by others.
I didn't dare to give him the short coat.
When he took office, his fellow officials all decorated their houses. Gu Xie stayed in the official office for sixteen years, providing food and clothing and did not change the previous situation.
The disciple came to see Gu Xie for something. Knowing that he was honest, he did not dare to give him a generous gift. He only gave him 2,000 yuan. Gu Xie became angry. He was beaten twenty times with a rod. From then on, anyone who came to him for trouble would never give him a gift.
Since the death of his parents, he has been a vegetarian all his life.
When he was young, he was engaged to his uncle's daughter. Before they got married, Gu Xie's mother died and he did not marry her after the mourning period expired.
When she was more than sixty years old, the girl did not remarry. Gu Xie married her because of her affection.
Although he got married in his later years, he had no children.
Gu Xie is well-read and knows more about writing, animals, and plants.
He compiled five volumes of "Yi Xing Yuan" and ten volumes of "Suo Yu", both of which have been circulated in the world.
Xu Zhai, courtesy name Shixiu, was from Tan, Donghai.
My grandfather Pingdao was the prefect of Hailing in the Song Dynasty.
His father surpassed him. In the early years of Tianjian, he often served as an official on horseback.
Xu Gan was young and eager to learn. When he grew up, he read books on classics and history.
The writing is so new and varied, and doesn't stick to the old style.
He started as a doctor of Taixue and moved to Sima Zuowei.
At this time, King Gang of Jin'an went out to garrison the stone. Emperor Gaozu said to Zhou She: I am looking for a person for me who is good at literature and has good character. I want him to associate with Jin'an and accompany him.
Zhou She said: My cousin Xu Go is humble in appearance and may not be able to wear more clothes, but he is capable of doing this job.
Emperor Gaozu said: If Wang Can had talent, there would be no need to pick on his appearance.
Let Xu Zhi serve as an attendant.
Later, when the King of Jin'an left Zhenjiang Prefecture, he appointed Xu Gao as the Record Office of Yunhui Prefecture to join the army, and then he was transferred to the Record Office of Pingxi Prefecture.
summary: Gu Xie, courtesy name Zhengli, from Wu County, lost his father young and was raised by his grandfather. As a child, he expressed a desire for seclusion, impressing his maternal grandfather. He was studious and praised for his concentration. He began his career as a historian in Yangzhou and later as a Taixue doctor. Minister Shen Yue praised his policy essay as unmatched since the Eastern Jin. He served in various roles, including as a magistrate and military advisor. At sixty, he was recommended for his conduct and knowledge, though he remained indifferent to fame. He was appointed as a minister and died at seventy-three. The emperor mourned him, noting his honesty and lack of close relatives. Gu Xie was known for his integrity, refusing gifts and living frugally. He married his uncle's daughter in his sixties, having no children. He was well-read and compiled works like "Yi Xing Yuan" and "Suo Yu."

translation:
Taizong listened to his advice.
Later, he was awarded the title of Prince Zuowei.
In the third year of Taiqing, Hou Jing captured Taicheng and sent Taizong to live in Yongfu Province. The thieves rushed in and raised their troops to the palace. The palace guards fled and no one was willing to stay.
Xu Zhai stood alone and solemnly without moving, and slowly said to Hou Jing: "The Duke of Hou is supposed to bow before you, how can you do this?"
Hou Jing was impressed by his fierceness.
Hou Jing then paid homage to him, and from then on he was often afraid of Xu Gao.
Taizong succeeded to the throne and was awarded the title of General Zuowei, but Xu Gao refused to accept the title.
Later, Taizong was imprisoned, and Xu Zhai could not go to court. He died of a gas disease at the age of seventy-eight.
The eldest son, Xu Ling, is the most famous.
Bao Quan, whose courtesy name is Runyue, is from Donghai.
His father, Bao Ji, was consulted by the king of eastern Hunan to join the army.
Bao Quan was well-read in historical and biographical books and was good at writing both rhymed and non-rhymed articles.
He served Emperor Yuan when he was young and was promoted and appointed very early.
After Emperor Yuan inherited the throne, Lei moved to Xinzhou as governor.
In the third year of Taiqing, Emperor Yuan ordered Bao Quan to go to Xiangzhou to conquer Xiao Yu, the king of Hedong. Bao Quan went to Changsha and deployed neighboring cities to force Xiao Yu. Xiao Yu led his troops to attack Bao Quan. Bao Quan held on to the fence, but Xiao Yu could not conquer it.
Bao Quan took advantage of his fatigue to attack again, and Xiao Yu was defeated. Bao Quan captured many of his soldiers and surrounded the city, but could not capture it for a long time.
The emperor Shizu denounced Bao Quan's crimes and sent Pingnan General Wang Sengbian to replace Bao Quan as governor.
When the monk argued with the army, Bao Quan was very surprised and said to the people around him: "With Wang Jingling's help in my strategy, I can pacify the bandits without any effort."
Monk Bian entered the room, sat with his back to Bao Quan, and said, "Bao Lang is guilty, and I have ordered you to be imprisoned. Please don't have any hope based on the feelings of an old friend."
So he showed Bao Quan the edict and locked him under the bed.
Bao Quan said: "I am willing to plead guilty for delaying the attack of the king's army, but I am afraid that people in the future will think more of Quan's confusion."
So Seng Bian petitioned to forgive Bao Quan for his delay in using the army.
Shizu soon resumed his position and ordered him, Seng Bian and others to lead a fleet of boats from Yingzhou in the east to attack King Shaoling.
After pacifying Yingzhou, Emperor Yuan appointed his eldest son Fang Zhu as governor and Bao Quan as chief historian to handle the affairs of the prefecture.
Hou Jingmi sent generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to attack Yingzhou with fine cavalry. Fang Zhuyu Bao Quan did not consider military affairs, but only gambled and drunkenly enjoyed himself. When thieves and cavalry arrived, the people rushed to report. Fang Zhuyu Bao Quan was playing games and did not believe it. He said: "Xu Wensheng's army is guarding Shumian, how can the thieves come?"
Then many people were informed, so the city gates were closed. The thieves set fire to the city. No one dared to resist. The thieves' cavalry were able to enter the city and the city fell.
The arrests of Fang Zhu and Bao Quan were sent to Hou Jing's office.
Later, Hou Jing attacked Wang Sengbian in Baling, but failed to capture him. He returned after failure, so he killed Bao Quan in Jiangxia and sunk his body in Huanghuji.
summary: Xu Zhai, courtesy name Shixiu, from Donghai, was studious and known for his innovative writing. He served as a Taixue doctor and was recommended by Zhou She to accompany Prince Jin'an, despite his plain appearance. He held various posts, including as a magistrate and military advisor. His writing style, known as "gong style," was imitated in the palace, initially angering Emperor Gaozu but later earning his favor. Zhu Yi, feeling threatened, had Xu Zhai appointed as prefect of Xin'an, where he governed fairly and improved customs. He later served as a general and advisor on marriage rituals, advising the emperor on proper etiquette. During Hou Jing's rebellion, Xu Zhai stood firm, impressing Hou Jing with his fierceness. He died at seventy-eight after refusing a general title. His eldest son, Xu Ling, was famous. Bao Quan, courtesy name Runyue, from Donghai, was well-read and skilled in writing. He served Emperor Yuan and was appointed governor of Xinzhou. He defeated Xiao Yu but was later accused of delaying the king's army and imprisoned by Wang Sengbian. He was forgiven and later served as chief historian in Yingzhou. The city fell due to neglect by Fang Zhu and Bao Quan, who were captured by Hou Jing. Bao Quan was killed in Jiangxia. He had prophetic dreams about his fate. He was an expert on "Ritual" and compiled forty volumes of "Xinyi."

translation:
When Bao Quan went to serve as the governor of Nanchao, his friend dreamed that Bao Quan had offended Shizu and told Bao Quan when he woke up.
Within ten days, Bao Quan was indeed arrested.
Soon, he dreamed of Bao Quan walking on the water wearing a red official uniform, and told Bao Quan: "Don't worry, you will be exempted from guilt soon."
He told the dream to Bao Quan. Bao Quan kept a secret record of the matter and was appointed again soon, and he fulfilled what was said in the dream.
Bao Quan knew "Ritual" best and compiled forty volumes of "Xinyi", which was circulated in the world.
Yao Cha, the official secretary of the Chen Dynasty, said: Ruan Xiaoxu often said: Zhongni discusses four subjects, starting with virtue and ending with literature.
Most virtuous people advocate simplicity, while most literary people do not abide by the rules. Therefore, Wei Wan and Shi Fen have nothing to spread, and Qu Yuan and Jia Yi have no reputation for virtue.
Like following Ziyou and Zixia, imitating Yan Hui and Ziqian, virtue and literature coexist, which can be seen in Pei Jiyuan.
summary: Yao Cha noted that Ruan Xiaoxu observed that virtue and literature rarely coexist, but Pei Ziye exemplified both, combining the qualities of Ziyou, Zixia, Yan Hui, and Ziqian.

translation:
Yuan Ang, whose courtesy name was Qianli, was from Yangxia, Chen County.
His grandfather, Yuan Xun, was a general who conquered captives and a prefect of Wu County in the Song Dynasty. His father, Yuan Hao, was a champion general and the governor of Yongzhou. In the early years of Taishi, he raised troops to support Prince Xun of Jin'an, but was defeated and killed.
When Yuan Ang was five years old, his wet nurse hid him in Lushan Mountain. He left the mountain only when he was pardoned and moved to Jin'an. During the Yuanhui period, he was allowed to return to his hometown when he was fifteen years old.
At the beginning, Yuan Pinqi was defeated and his head was sent to the capital and hidden in the arsenal. It was only now sent back.
Yuan Ang cried and vomited blood and came back to life. His brother Yuan Yuzeng raised and educated him. Yuan Ang put on mourning clothes and built a house in the cemetery to live.
Later, he and Yuan Tuan went to visit his uncle, Situ Yuan Can. Yuan Can said to Yuan Tuan: "He can behave like this because he is young and alone, so he knows that his title and title have their own place."
In the early years of the Qi Dynasty, Wang Xing, the first champion of Ancheng, joined the army and moved to the post of chief warden, prince Sheren, and Wang Jianzhen, the military official's meritorious official.
Wang Jian was the Yin of Beijing at that time. He once introduced Yuan Ang alone in the back hall, pointed to the north hall and said to Yuan Ang: Your Majesty will definitely live here.
Lei moved to serve as Secretary Cheng and Huangmen Shilang.
Yuan Ang's real name was Qianli. During the Yongming Dynasty of the Qi Dynasty, Emperor Wu said to him: Angang, the horse of a thousand miles, your name contains this meaning. Now I will change your name to Yuan Ang, using the character Qianli.
He served as the chief historian of Poyang in Annan and the Duke of Xunyang.
He was also appointed as the grandson's concubine and the chief historian of Wuling King of the Guards.
When the mother dies, mourning is carried out according to etiquette.
Before he was discharged from the service, his cousin Yuan Tuan passed away.
Yuan Ang's father died when he was young and he was raised by Jiang Yu, so he served as a uniform.
Someone asked him about something strange, and Yuan Ang wrote to him and said: I heard that the degree of etiquette is determined by the distance between relatives, and mourning is to express grief. Therefore, if you make a small contribution to another country, you can add a higher level. Relatives who live and eat together have to take gills. It is clearly recorded in the classics.
In the past, I was not protected by God. I lost my father's protection when I was young. I failed to respect my father and accepted my father's teachings. I was still young and failed to achieve great success.
My cousin supported me and taught me the right way to behave and do things. There is indeed a reason for me to use his comments and comments to falsely gain his reputation and reach the crowd.
He also expanded my house for me and lived in a gorgeous, spacious and bright house. He shared the money and allowed me to ask for what I needed. Since then, for more than thirty years, he has shown me the utmost love and affection.
Sisters and nephews, they have made a whole generation whole. They sincerely missed him deeply and it became even stronger when he was dying. This kindness and love will never be regretted for the rest of his life.
Since emotions are like one's own life, and mourning is the same as that of his peers, it is really unbearable to pour out your heart and face the things in front of you.
In the past, Maleng and his younger brother Ma Yi lived together. When Ma Yi died, Maleng mourned for him for three years.
Zhong Yu also did not mourn when the time was due, and it was also due to love. Although my knowledge is not as good as that of the ancients, I sincerely express my gratitude and admiration to them.
Chang is willing to serve his brother since his death. Unexpectedly, when the family declined and misfortune occurred, the grief of his mother's death had not subsided, and he encountered today's cruelty, and then he fainted from grief, which became more and more severe.
summary: Yuan Ang, courtesy name Qianli, was from Yangxia, Chen County. His grandfather and father were military officials in the Song Dynasty; his father was killed after supporting Prince Xun of Jin'an. At age five, Yuan Ang was hidden in Lushan by his wet nurse, returning home at fifteen after a pardon. He mourned his father deeply, vomiting blood and building a hut by the grave. Raised by his brother Yuan Yuzeng, he later served in various official posts under the Qi Dynasty, including Secretary Cheng and Huangmen Shilang. Emperor Wu of Qi renamed him Yuan Ang, using his courtesy name Qianli. The historical commentary praises Yuan Ang for his unwavering loyalty and integrity, comparing him to the virtuous Boyi and Shuqi, and noting his role in supporting the Liang dynasty.

translation:
Now, with the rest of my life, I want to fulfill my usual aspirations, place my heart in the pain of endless longing, and stretch out my endless affection.
Although there is no clear evidence for etiquette, there is a precedent, and if you are addicted to it, you will definitely want to follow it.
You asked about the basis of etiquette, and I would like to report it here.
Facing the letter paper, I was crying and choking, and my words were incoherent.
When the mourning period expired, in addition to being awarded the title of Chief of History to the Right Army King Shaoling, he was immediately moved to the post of Censor Zhongcheng.
At that time, Wang Yan's younger brother Wang Xiang was appointed as the governor of Guangzhou, and he accepted bribes from many parties. Yuan Ang reported him to the emperor according to the matter, and was not afraid of the rich and powerful. People at the time praised him for his integrity.
When he served as the internal history of Yuzhang, he resigned when his biological mother died. He returned to his hometown for the funeral. The Yangtze River was violently stormy. Yuan Ang tied himself to the coffin with his clothes and vowed to sink with the coffin.
When the wind stopped, all the other boats were submerged in the river. Only Yuan Ang's boat was safe, and it was said that it was due to his sincerity.
After the burial, he was appointed as General Jianwu and Prefect of Wuxing.
At the end of Yongyuan, when the righteous army arrived in the capital, all the prefectures, pastoral and county guards obeyed and surrendered. Yuan Ang defended his territory and resisted without orders.
Emperor Gaozu wrote a letter in his own hand telling him: There is no fixed destiny for misfortunes and blessings, they are all brought about by people. The rise and fall of a country is determined. If God abandons him, who can restore him?
If the opportunity never comes again, you should plan early.
Recently, people have heard that you want to occupy a corner like a wolf. Since I don’t know your intentions, let me state my consistent opinion.
Dufu is arrogant and rampant. I have never heard anyone like him in the past. He is extremely cruel and cruel. As time goes by, he becomes more powerful.
The heavens will not diminish, the sage will open up the destiny of the world, the people will have dependence, and the people will be resurrected from the hardships.
I served as the vanguard, swept away the capital, brought order to chaos, attacked criminals and saved the people. Since I was sent, there has been no blocking position in front of me.
Today, the imperial power is everywhere, the long circle has been closed, the people from far and near have gathered together, and they are fighting together in a state of trance.
With tens of thousands of elite soldiers and thousands of cavalry, if you attack with this, you will never be victorious.
What's more, Jianye has become an isolated city. Everyone wants to leave the dangerous place. People who surrender to the military gates come one after another day and night. The date when they flee for fear of execution cannot be too far away.
In addition, Mars appears in Duanmen, and Taibai appears in Dishi. The upper part is in astronomy, and the lower part is in line with human affairs. They coincidentally coincide with each other at this moment.
Moreover, Fan Xiu and Shen Zhou expressed their sincere submission a long time ago, and each led the relevant officials, but they still divided their troops to contain the enemy; Shen Fama, Sun Zhuang, and Zhu Duan had first eliminated Wu and Hui, and then they wanted to use a mere county to resist the powerful army. The roots of the tree have fallen, but the branches and leaves are attached?
summary: During the Liang Dynasty, Yuan Ang held numerous high-ranking positions, such as Censor Zhongcheng, Prefect of Wuxing, and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel. He was known for his integrity, once impeaching a corrupt official despite the latter's powerful connections. When his mother died, he tied himself to her coffin during a storm, vowing to sink with it; the storm ceased, and his boat alone survived.

translation:
I am a lowly man from the Eastern Kingdom. I have no merit in learning and practice. Since I am different from Mingyan and Naoki, I have not become an official. It is in vain to rely on my auxiliary wings to change from farming to being an official.
In previous years, he was incompetent and ranked in his position. He was guarding his salary in the east corner. People looked up to him and followed him, and the wind drove and lightning covered him.
At that time, people holding important national utensils arrived, and people holding jade silk saw each other.
I am a foolish minister, confused by righteousness, martyred by the lightness of a feather, forgetting the importance of common virtue.
However, the terrain of Sanwu was dangerous and poor, and the transportation of Wuhu and the frequent changes in Tiandan's order to make him king. He was often afraid of the troubles caused by Yin Tong's death. He only admired Junyu to defend the territory, so he lost the loyalty of Shi Juan.
Those who later surrendered were killed, and I was willing to be killed.
Public punishment shows everyone that it shouldn't be this way.
The great fortune of the stipulation, thanks to benevolence and pardon, was reduced to one level of ghost punishment, and he was immediately released from the torture of ocher.
Gathering the bones and blowing away the soul, he was reorganized among the common people to cleanse his faults and cleanse his filth. He entered the Chu Kingdom and traveled to the Chen Kingdom. The emperor's favor was washed away and cloud oil suddenly washed over him.
There is an ancient saying: It is not difficult to die, but it is difficult to live together until death. The favors I received have not been recorded in the past; the place where I died is unknown.
Emperor Gaozu replied: I am sending you a shooting hook, please do not think of yourself as an outsider.
Soon he was awarded the title of Minister of Huangmen.
This year he was moved to the post of Shizhong.
In the second year, he served as the prefect of Xunyang and conducted affairs in Jiangzhou.
In the sixth year, he was recruited as the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel. He resigned many times and was transferred to the position of Minister of the Zuo Min and concurrently as the Minister of the Right.
In the seventh year, in addition to being granted the imperial title of offering wine to the prince, he also served as a servant as usual and led the great Zhongzheng of Yuzhou.
In the eighth year, he served as General Renwei and Governor of Wu County.
In the eleventh year, he was appointed as the Minister of the Five Arms, and then served as the Right Servant. He was not granted the title, but was replaced by an imperial edict.
Then he took over the position of Minister of the Ministry of Finance and was appointed as a minister.
In the fourteenth year, Ma Xianbei defeated the Wei army in Qushan and ordered Yuan Ang to temporarily act as Chijie and go to labor the army.
In the fifteenth year, he was moved to Zuopushe, and then appointed as Shangshu Ling and General Xuanhui.
In ordinary three years, he served as Zhongshu Supervisor and Danyang Yin.
In the year of Han, he was promoted to the rank of General of Zhongwei, and then appointed as Shangshu Ling, that is, his title was Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
In the first year of Datong, he was appointed Zhongshu Supervisor and given thirty guards.
Not long after, the sacrificial wine was lifted, he was promoted to the rank of General of the Fu Army, and moved to Sikong, Shizhong, and Shangshuling. His confidants and advocates remained the same as before.
In the fifth year, Dr. Jia Tejin and Dr. Zuo Guanglu were added, and the number of confidants increased to eighty.
Zuo Hui six years later, he died at the age of eighty.
Shaoling said: Shi Zhong, Te Jin, Dr. Zuo Guanglu, and Sikong Yuan Ang died suddenly, and their hearts were filled with sadness.
summary: At the end of the Yongyuan period, when the righteous army arrived, Yuan Ang initially resisted but later surrendered after Emperor Gaozu wrote him a letter. He was pardoned and continued to serve, eventually becoming Sikong, Shizhong, and Shangshuling. He died at age eighty, posthumously titled Muzheng Gong. In his final words, he refused posthumous honors, citing his humble origins and gratitude for imperial grace. His son, Zijun, also served in official posts but died of illness after Hou Jing's rebellion.

translation:
Xie Ju, whose courtesy name is Yan Yang, is the younger brother of Xie Lan, who was ordered by Zhongshu Ling.
He was eager to learn when he was young, could talk about mystical principles, and was as famous as Xie Li.
When Xie Gao was fourteen years old, he once presented a selected five-character poem, which was praised by the composer.
People in the world therefore say: The person named Wang has Yang and Ju, and the person named Xie has Lan and Ju.
Yang and Ju are the nicknames of Wang Yun and Wang Tai.
Xie Ju first served as Secretary Lang, and later moved to Prince Sheren. He was Cao Shi of Qingchao Gong, Secretary Cheng, Sikong Zhonglang, Prince's concubine, family order, and in charge of the management of the East Palace. He was deeply appreciated by Prince Zhaoming.
When Ren Fang, the secretary supervisor, took office as the prefect of Xin'an County, he bid farewell to Xie Ju with a poem and said: If you miss the elderly, remember my sustenance deeply.
He was valued like this.
Once at a banquet, Emperor Gaozu asked Xie Ju for advice. Xie Ju replied: "My knowledge and skills are far superior to those of my ministers, but I am not as good as my ministers in drinking."
Emperor Gaozu was very happy.
He was transferred to the position of concubine among the crown princes and was still in charge of the records.
In the eleventh year of Tianjian, he moved to serve in the middle school.
In the fourteenth year, he served as General Ningyuan and Internal History of Yuzhang. His administration was tolerant and gentle, which won the hearts of the people.
In the 18th year, he entered the imperial court and served as a servant and an infantry captain.
In the first year of Pongyong, he served as General Zhenyi and Taiwei Wang Changshi of Linchuan.
Four years later, he entered the court and was appointed Minister of Zuo Min.
In the same year, he was moved to the post of Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, but was soon dismissed due to official business.
In the fifth year, he was appointed as the prince's concubine and led the right army general.
In the sixth year, he was again appointed Minister of Zuo Min and led the infantry school captain.
Soon he was moved to the post of Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and then he was added to the post of Shizhong.
He served as General Renwei and Governor of Jinling.
In the county government, the people were influenced by their virtues and their policies, and the territory was awe-inspiring.
After the dismissed governor returned to the capital, officials and people went to the court to request that a monument be erected for him, and Xia Shao agreed.
In the second year of Taibi's reign, he was appointed as Shizhong and Shangshu of the Five Arms. Before taking office, he was moved to the position of Shangshu of the Ministry of Personnel, and Shizhong remained as before.
Xie Ju's grandfather, Xie Zhuang, was in charge of the election of officials twice in Fengfa, and Xie Ju held this position three times. This was not done in previous generations.
Xie Ju read a lot of books when he was young and was able to understand them all. He was especially good at Lao, Zhuang, Xuanli and Buddhist philosophy.
When he was appointed as the prefect of Jinling County, monk Chang Yuyi took turns explaining Buddhist scriptures, and the conscript He Yin came from Huqiu Mountain to listen to the lectures.
Such a grand occasion.
Before that, Lu Guang, who came from across the Yangtze River, was proficient in Confucianism and was a doctor of the Imperial Academy. When he explained the Confucian classics, everyone under Xu Mian went to listen.
Xie Ju sat on the floor and pointed out Lu Guang's mistakes many times, and his rhetoric was beyond the ordinary. Lu Guang was so impressed that he gave him the pawn tail he held and gave him a precious seat.
summary: Xie Ju, courtesy name Yan Yang, was the younger brother of Xie Lan. He was an eager learner from a young age, skilled in discussing mystical principles, and shared fame with Xie Li. He began his career as Secretary Lang and later held various positions, including Prince Sheren and Cao Shi of Qingchao Gong. He was deeply appreciated by Prince Zhaoming. Emperor Gaozu once asked Xie Ju for advice, and Xie Ju humbly replied that his knowledge was far superior but he was not as good in drinking, which pleased the emperor. He served as General Ningyuan and Internal History of Yuzhang, where his tolerant administration won the people's hearts. He later held several high-ranking positions, including Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and Shizhong. Xie Ju was well-read, especially in Laozi, Zhuangzi, and Buddhist philosophy. He once corrected Lu Guang's errors during a lecture, earning Lu's respect. He died in the besieged capital during Hou Jing's invasion. His works were lost in the war.

translation:
In four years, he was appointed as a minister.
In the fifth year, he was appointed as the right servant of Shangshu, and he continued to serve as the minister.
In the third year of Datong, Chen resigned due to illness and was transferred to Dr. Youguanglu, giving 20 close followers.
That year, he served as General Yunhui and Grand Administrator of Wu County.
Previously, He Jinrong served as the county governor and performed in politics, and was known as "He Wujun". He was in power with Xie Ju, and his reputation was roughly the same.
In the sixth year, he was appointed as Shizhong and Zhongshu Supervisor. Before taking office, he was moved to Prince Zhan Shi and General Yizuo, and Shizhong remained as usual.
Xie Ju's father, Xie Man, ended up in this position in the Qi Dynasty. Xie Ju went to the court many times to beg for a new appointment, but was not allowed to do so. It took a long time before he could take up the post.
In the ninth year, he was moved to the post of Minister Pushe, but Shishen and General remained as before.
Although Xie Ju held the position of prime minister, he was unwilling to participate in current affairs and requested to be dismissed many times due to illness. The emperor granted him leave, wrote prescriptions in his own hand, and gave the emperor medicine.
He was so favored by the emperor.
In the year of dispatch, I used my official position to participate in the election.
In the second year of Taiqing's reign, he was moved to the post of Shangshu Ling, but the ministers and generals remained as before.
This year, Hou Jing invaded the capital, and Xie Ju died in the besieged city.
Shao Ling posthumously presented Shizhong, Zhongwei General, and Kaifu Yitong to the three divisions, while Shizhong and Shangshu Ling remained as before.
The collected works were all lost during the war.
The two sons, Xie Xi and Xie Gu, both became famous at a young age.
Xie Gu, during the Taiqing period, served successively as the concubine among the crown princes and as the prefect who built the house.
He Jinrong, courtesy name Guoli, was born in Lujiang.
His grandfather Youzhi served as Taichang Qing of the Song Dynasty; his father Chang Jue served as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel of the Qi Dynasty: both were well-known at that time.
He Jinrong came from a well-known family, and when he came of age, he married Princess Changcheng, the daughter of Emperor Wu of Shang Qi, and was awarded the title of Prince Consort.
In the early years of Tianjian, he served as Secretary Lang, and successively served as Prince Sheren, Zhonglang of Shangshu Palace, Prince Xima, Zhongshu Sheren, Secretary Cheng, and moved to Yangzhou to rule the country.
