The monks were afraid, so they sent envoys to express their submission to the Liang Dynasty and asked him to become a vassal of the Liang Dynasty. Emperor Gaozu agreed and appointed him Shizhong and Sikong.
When the Northern Wei army approached him, Fa Seng asked to return to the Liang Dynasty, and Emperor Gaozu sent Zhu Yi, a member of Zhongshushe, to greet him.
When he came to Liang Dynasty, he was extremely favored.
At that time, he was attracting people who had returned, and he was friendly to those who surrendered. He also gave the Dharma monk a house, female music, and gold and silk.
When Fa Seng was in the Northern Wei Dynasty, he had been a border guard official for a long time. Every time he invaded and plundered, he killed many people. He asked for troops to be sent for self-defense. Shao ordered him to have hundreds of guards wearing armor and weapons, and they were prohibited from entering and leaving the palace.
In the second year of Datong, he was appointed as the champion general.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, he was transferred to the general of chariots and cavalry.
In four years, he was promoted to Taiwei and received gold and purple light.
At that time, he was established as the lord of the Eastern Wei Dynasty, but he did not return to the Wei Dynasty. He was appointed as envoy Chijie, regular attendant of Sanqi, general of Hussar, Kaifu Tongsansi Zhiyi, and governor of Yingzhou.
In the second year of Datong, he was recruited as Shizhong, Taiwei, and general of the army division. He died at the age of eighty-three.
The two sons, named Jinglong and Jingzhong, followed Fa Seng into the Liang Dynasty during the ordinary years.
Jinglong was granted the title of Duke of Chuanyang County, with a settlement of thousands of households, and served as Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of Guangyue, Jiaogui and other thirteen states' military affairs, General Pingnan, General Lang of Huyue Zhonglang, and Governor of Guangzhou.
In the third year of Zhongdatong, he was recruited as Shizhong and General Anyou.
In the fourth year, he was appointed as the General of Zhengbei and the Governor of Xuzhou, and was granted the title of King of Pengcheng.
In the early years of the Taiqing Dynasty, he also served as envoy Chijie, governor of Guangyue Jiaogui and other military forces in thirteen states, general of the southern expedition, general of Pingyue Zhonglang, and governor of Guangzhou. He traveled to Leishou and died of illness at the age of fifty-eight.
Jing Zhong was granted the title of Duke of Zhijiang County, with thousands of households living in the city, and was appointed as Shizhong and Right Guard General.
In the third year of Datong, the number of new towns was increased to 2,000 households, and a female musical instrument was also given.
summary: The lives of several individuals from the Northern Wei Dynasty who later served the Liang Dynasty, focusing on their careers, military actions, and fates. Yuan Faseng, a relative of the Northern Wei imperial family, served as an official and later declared himself emperor during a period of chaos. He submitted to the Liang Dynasty and was granted high titles. He died at age 83, and his sons, Jinglong and Jingzhong, also served the Liang. Jingzhong later rebelled with Hou Jing but was defeated and hanged himself. Yuanshu, another Northern Wei relative, served as an official and later defected to the Liang. He was appointed to military and civil posts, captured a city, but was eventually captured and died in the Northern Wei at age 48.

translation:
He served as Chijie, governor of Guangyue and other thirteen states' military affairs, general Xuanhui, general Pingyue Zhonglang, and governor of Guangzhou.
During the Zuohui period, he was recruited as Shizhong and Zuowei General.
His elder brother Keelung also served as governor of Guangzhou.
Hou Jing started a rebellion. He thought Jing Zhong was a member of the Yuan family, so he sent an envoy to persuade him and promised to make him the leader of the country.
Jing Zhong then raised his troops to respond to Hou Jing.
At that time, Chen Baxian, the governor of Xijiang, and Wang Huaiming, the governor of Chengzhou, and others launched an army to attack Jingzhong. Baxian announced to Jingzhong's soldiers: Because the traitors of Yuan Jingzhong and Yuan have united from the north to the south and are plotting to harm the country, the imperial court has sent Xiao Bo, Duke of Qujiang, as the governor to control this state.
After hearing this, everyone abandoned their armor and dispersed. Jing Zhong hanged himself and died.
Yuanshu, whose courtesy name was Junli, was also a close relative of the Northern Wei Dynasty.
His grandfather was Emperor Xianwen.
His father Yuan Xi was granted the title of King of Xianyang.
Yuan Shu served as an official in the Wei Dynasty and served as Zong Zhengqing. At the time when Erzhu Rong was in rebellion, Yuan Shu returned to the country in the eighth year of Tianjian.
In the sixth year of ordinary life, when the Yuan Dynasty monk returned to the court, he was transferred to the envoy Chijie, the governor of Ying, Si, and Huo, the three states of military affairs, the general of Yunhui, and the governor of Ying state.
After conquering the Southern Barbarians and pacifying them, he was appointed as a regular servant of the Sanqi and General of Anxi, and granted 500 additional households.
In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was recruited as Shizhong and Zhenyou General.
In the fourth year, he was appointed as envoy Chijie, general of Zhenbei, and governor of Beichai military affairs, and he also added a department of advocacy. Let him attack Jiu Wei and capture Zhong Ji in Tanjian.
Dugu, the general who sent Jiuqiao at that time, came to help as he wished, so he surrounded Yuanli. The city was captured and he was arrested. He died angrily in the Northern Wei Dynasty at the age of forty-eight.
During the Datong period, Zi Yuanzhen requested to follow Cui Changqian, the Wei envoy, to Ye to bury his father. After returning, he was appointed Prince Sheren.
In the early years of Zuo Zha's reign, Baoliang surrendered and invited his relatives from far away to be the king of the country. Shao Ling made Zhen the king of Xianyang and sent him back to the north with the etiquette of the emperor. At that time, Hou Jing failed and returned.
Yuan Yuanda was also a branch of Wei Shu.
His grandfather was Emperor Ming Yuan.
His father was named King Leqian.
Yuanda served as an official in the Northern Wei Dynasty, serving as Zhongshu Ling and the governor of Ying Zhao.
In ordinary years, the army went north to attack Yiyang, hoping to reach the territory of Xianzhou and submit it. He was granted the title of Duke of Leping, with a settlement of thousands of households, and was given the mansions of wealthy nobles and female musicians.
Later, he served as envoy Chijie, regular attendant of Sanqi, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Xiangzhou, general Pingnan, and governor of Xiangzhou.
In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was recruited as Shizhong, Taizhong doctor, and Yizuo general.
In the third year of Datong, he died at the age of fifty-seven.
Wang Shennian was from Qi, Taiyuan.
When he was young, he was fond of Confucianism, especially Buddhist scriptures.
He started as an official in the Northern Wei Dynasty and served as the governor of the state. Soon he was promoted to the prefect of Yingchuan, and he took over the county and returned the money.
When the Wei army arrived, he crossed the river with his family and was granted the title of Marquis of Nancheng County, with a settlement of 500 households.
Soon after, he was appointed as the internal history of Ancheng, and successively as the internal history of Wuyang and Xuancheng, all of whom made remarkable achievements in politics.
He returned to the capital and was appointed Taipuqing.
He served as Chijie, governor of the military affairs of Qing and Ji states, general Xinwu, and governor of Qing and Ji states.
Wang Shennian has an upright temperament, and the prefectures and counties he has visited will prohibit unnecessary temples.
At that time, there was Shilu Mountain near the sea in the northeast of Qing and Jizhou. There used to be a temple. The witch deceived the people. People from far and near came to pray. There was a lot of waste. When the money came to send parcels, they ordered the temple to be demolished, and the customs changed.
summary: Yuan Yuanda, a branch of the Wei family, served in the Northern Wei and later submitted to the Liang, receiving titles and positions. He died at age 57.

translation:
In ordinary years, he launched a large-scale Northern Expedition and was recruited as a right-guard general.
In the sixth year, he was transferred to envoy Chijie, Sanqi Changshi, and minions general, but the right guard remained as before.
He fell ill and died at the age of seventy-five.
Shaoling gave posthumously to his own official, the governor of Hengzhou, and also gave a piece of propaganda.
Mi's name is Zhuang.
Wang Shennian was good at riding and shooting when he was young, and he never failed in his old age. He once held two swords and shields in front of Emperor Gaozu, passed them from left to right, galloped back and forth, and his martial arts skills overwhelmed the crowd.
At that time, there was Yang Hua, who was able to shock the army and cavalry. It was a moment of great success. Emperor Gaozu deeply admired them.
The son respects his career, and his official position reaches the rank of Imperial Servant.
After his death, he posthumously awarded General Xinwei, governor of Qingzhou and Jizhou, and a volume of advocacy.
The second son, Seng Bian, has another biography.
Yang Hua was from Qiuchi, Wudu.
His father, Big Eyes, was a famous general in the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Yang Hua was brave and handsome when he was young. Empress Dowager Hu of the Northern Wei Dynasty forced him to commit adultery. Yang Hua was afraid of disaster, so he led his troops to surrender.
Empress Dowager Hu recalled that he could not control him, so she composed "Yang Baihua's Song" for him, and asked the palace people to sing with arms and legs all day and night. The song was extremely sad.
After Yang Hua participated in many expeditions and had military exploits, he served as a taipuqing, led by the prince Zuowei, and was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang County.
During the Taiqing period, Hou Jing rebelled, and Yang Hua wanted to establish a moral integrity. However, his wife and children were captured by thieves, so he surrendered and died in the thieves' territory.
Yangkan, named Zuxin, was a descendant of Liangfu in Mount Tai and a descendant of Yangxu, the prefect of Nanyang in the Han Dynasty.
Grandfather Yang Gui, when Emperor Wu of the Song Dynasty was appointed as the governor of Xuzhou, he was recruited to serve as a wine minister and a great official.
It happened that Xue Andu surrendered to Jiugui with the cutting ball, and Jiugui was trapped in the ravine. Jiuwei awarded him the title of General of Wei and Governor of Yingzhou.
His father, Yang Zhi, served as a servant in the Northern Wei Dynasty and was a doctor named Jin Ziguanglu.
When Yang Kan was young, he was tall and handsome, seven feet eight inches tall. He was very fond of literature and history, and was well versed in books and memorials. He was especially fond of Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals and Sun Wu's Art of War.
When he was twenty years old, he followed his father to make military exploits in Liang Cong.
Tanji teased Li Nianwen and was gradually promoted to a special general.
At that time, Mo Zhe Niansheng, a Qiang people in Qinzhou, occupied the state and rebelled, proclaiming himself the emperor. He sent his younger brother Tiansheng to lead his troops to capture Qizhou, and then invaded Yongzhou.
Yang Yi was appointed as a partial general, and he went to fight under Lu Xuanyu. He was patrolling in the ditch and waiting for an opportunity to shoot Tiantian. Tiantian was shot and fell down, and his soldiers immediately dispersed.
Due to his merit, he was promoted to envoy Chijie, Zhengshu general, Shudaoxingtai, Taishan prefect, and was promoted to the title of Jupinghou.
summary: Wang Shennian, from Qi, was a Confucian scholar who served as a prefect in the Northern Wei and later defected to the Liang. He was known for his uprightness, destroying a fraudulent temple. He died at age 75, and his son also served as an official. Yang Hua, from Qiuchi, was a brave general forced into adultery by Empress Dowager Hu. He defected to the Liang, served in expeditions, and later surrendered to Hou Jing, dying in the rebel territory. Yang Kan, from Tai Shan, was a tall and learned man who followed his father in military service. He shot a rebel leader, was promoted, and later defected to the Liang with his family. He was besieged by Wei forces but broke out, arriving in the Liang capital. He served in various military posts, advised against attacking Hou Jing prematurely, and defended the capital during Hou Jing's rebellion. He refused bribes, used tactics to counter siege engines, and remained loyal despite his son being captured. He died of illness at age 54, known for his bravery, strength, and luxurious lifestyle. The text concludes with a commentary praising the loyalty of Yang Kan and Yang Yaren during the Taiqing period, comparing their steadfastness to ancient martyrs.

translation:
He conquered the fallen uranium and was appointed as a regular servant of the Sanqi.
After pacifying Xia Sheng, he was appointed governor of Western Jinzhou.
Defeated Guo Yuanjian in Dongguan and moved him to the post of envoy Chijie, general Xinwu, and governor of Eastern Jinzhou.
In the third year of Chengsheng's reign, the Western Wei Dynasty besieged Jiangzuo, but Fuou failed to arrive when he came to help. He followed Wang Tanqi to conquer Xiao Bo in Lingtong. When he learned that Taiwei Sengbian was defeated, he returned, was defeated by Hou Tian, ​​and was killed in Yuzhang. He was twenty-eight years old.
Yang Yaren, whose courtesy name is Xiaomu, is from Juping, Taishan.
When he was young, he was brave, resolute and courageous, and served as an official in the county.
During the ordinary years, he led his brothers to join Liangqu from Cunxu and was granted the title of Marquis of Guangjin County.
After conquering the Qing and Qi areas, he made great achievements. He was later appointed as a member of the Standing Committee of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Grand Administrator of Liyang.
In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, he served as Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs, General Xinwei, and governor of Qiaozhou.
In the seventh year of Datong, he was appointed as the prince Zuowei Lian, and served as Chijie, governor of the Southern and Northern Divisions of the four states of Henan and Chu, general of Qingchao, and governor of Beisi Prefecture.
Hou Jing surrendered, and ordered Ya Rendu to lead 30,000 elite troops including Huan Hezhi, the governor of Tuzhou, and Zhan Haizhen, the governor of Renzhou, to go to Xuanhu to pick up Hou Jing. He was also appointed as the commander-in-chief of the military affairs of the seven prefectures including Yusi, Huaiji, Yinying, and Xiyu, and the governor of the two prefectures of Yu, to guard Xuanhu.
At this time, Hou Jing was defeated in Guoyang, and the Eastern Wei army gradually approached. Crow Ren was afraid that the food shipment would not be able to catch up, so he returned to the Northern Division and apologized. Emperor Gaozu was furious and blamed him. Crow Ren was afraid, so he stationed troops in Huaishang again.
When Hou Jing rebelled, Yaren led his troops to aid the court.
In the second year of Taiqing, after Hou Jing betrayed the alliance, Yaren, Tang Bochao and Nankang Wang Huili jointly attacked the thieves in Shufu City, but were defeated by the thieves.
When Taicheng fell, Yaren met Hou Jing and was left by Hou Jing to serve as Minister of the Five Arms.
Yaren often wanted to cheer up, and said to those close to him: As a mediocre person, I have been favored by the court, but I have not yet repaid the favor.
The country was overthrown, but I couldn't die, so I was living an ignoble existence until now.
If I die now, I have no regrets.
As he spoke, he wept, and everyone who saw him was grieved for him.
Three years later, he fled Jiangxi. His original tribe was filled with hundreds of people to welcome him. He was about to go to Jiangling and then to Dongguan, where he was killed by Xun Bodao, the former governor of Xuzhou in the north.
Shi Chen said: Emperor Gaozu carried out reforms in response to the destiny of heaven, inherited the throne, and hoped for a great destiny for the country. He was infiltrated by might and virtue, and all of them were attracted. They all sacrificed their lives for the country and went on to succeed him.
summary: Yang Yaren, also from Tai Shan, was brave and served as an official. He defected to the Liang, was granted a marquisate, and held military commands. He was sent to pick up Hou Jing but later feared punishment. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he aided the court but was defeated. After the capital fell, he served Hou Jing but planned to flee, eventually being killed.

translation:
Chen Qingzhi, whose courtesy name is Ziyun, is from Yixingguoshan. He followed Gaozu since he was young.
Emperor Gaozu loved to play chess. Every time he played chess, he would play chess all the time without stopping. All his peers were tired and went to bed. Only Qingzhi did not sleep, and he would come as soon as he was called. He was highly appreciated by his close followers.
Following Emperor Gaozu, he put down Jianye and later served as chief secretary. He dispersed money to recruit soldiers, and Chang Si played a role.
Granted the imperial invitation.
In the ordinary years, Yuan Faseng, the governor of Xuzhou in Wei Dynasty, requested to be attached to Pengcheng. He was appointed as a powerful general in order to celebrate him, and he, together with Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun, led other armies to pick him up.
After returning to the army, he was appointed General Xuanmeng and Commander Wende. He still led an army of two thousand and sent Xiao Zong, the king of Yuzhang, to guard Xuzhou.
Wei sent Prince Yanming of Anfeng and Prince Yuan of Linhuai with 20,000 troops to resist and garrisoned at Zhikou.
Yanming first sent another general, Qiu Dagan, to build a fort in Xunliang and show his strength at the border.
Qingzhi advanced on his earthen fortress and was defeated in a single battle.
Later, King Yuzhang abandoned his army and fled to Wei. Everyone was routed and the generals could not stop him, so Qingzhi cut off the bolts and breached the city. He retreated at night and the sergeants were saved.
In the seventh year of the Ordinary Year, General Yuan Shu of Anxi went to Shouchun to confer the holiday of celebration and general military affairs.
Li Xian, the governor of Yuzhou in Wei, sent his son Chang Gou to build two more forts to resist him. Qingzhi attacked him, but Li Xian was exhausted and surrendered, and Qingzhi entered and occupied the city.
He was transferred to Donggong Zhihe and given the title of Marquis of Guanzhong.
In the first year of Datong, the subordinate leader Xuan lived in the fortress and conquered Yan.
Gong sent General Changshan Wang Yuanzhao and others to come to the rescue with 150,000 cavalry and infantry. The front army reached Tuojian, forty miles away from Guoyang.
Qingzhi wanted to fight, but Tong Zhen believed that the thieves' vanguard must be light and agile. If we win the battle, it will not be enough. If the battle is unfavorable, our military strength will be destroyed. The art of war says that we should wait for the work in leisure, rather than not attacking.
Qingzhi said: The Wei people came from afar and are already tired. Since they are far away from our army, they will not be suspected. Before they gather, we must frustrate their energy and take them by surprise. There must be no reason to be invincible.
I also heard that the enemy's camp was heavily wooded and they would not go out at night.
If you have any doubts, please Qingzhi and attack him alone.
So Yu's 200 cavalrymen rushed towards the Wei army and defeated their front army. The Wei people were horrified.
Qingzhi then returned the army and the generals to attack together, occupy Woyang City, and confront the Wei army.
From spring to winter, hundreds of battles were fought. The army was exhausted and morale gradually declined. Wei's reinforcements wanted to build forts behind Qing's army. Zhongzong and others were afraid of being attacked from both sides, so they planned to retreat.
Qingzhi held a banner in front of the army gate and said: "We have been here for a year and have wasted a lot of food and weapons. The armies have no fighting spirit and are planning to retreat. They are not trying to gain fame. They are simply joining the camp for robbery."
I heard that if a soldier is put to death, he can be left to fight for his life. The enemy must gather in a large gathering and then fight with him.
If you really want to be a teacher, you will have a secret order to celebrate. If you violate it now, you will act according to Ming Shao.
Zhongzong admired his strategy and obeyed him.
In order to contain the troops, the Wei people built thirteen fortifications. Qingzhi held the coins horizontally in his mouth. He went out of the city at night and captured four of the enemy's fortifications. Wang Wei, the lord of Woyang City, begged to surrender.
summary: Chen Qingzhi, courtesy name Ziyun, from Yixingguoshan, served Emperor Gaozu from youth. Gaozu loved chess, playing tirelessly; while others tired and slept, Qingzhi remained alert and responsive, earning high regard. He followed Gaozu to pacify Jianye, served as chief secretary, and recruited soldiers with dispersed funds. He was granted an imperial invitation. In the ordinary years, Wei's Xuzhou governor Yuan Faseng sought attachment to Pengcheng. Qingzhi, as a powerful general, led Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun to escort him. After returning, he became General Xuanmeng and Commander Wende, leading 2,000 troops to guard Xuzhou with Xiao Zong. Wei sent Prince Yanming of Anfeng and Prince Yuan of Linhuai with 20,000 troops to resist at Zhikou. Yanming's general Qiu Dagan built a fort at Xunliang; Qingzhi defeated him in a single battle. Later, King Yuzhang fled to Wei, causing a rout. Qingzhi cut bolts, breached the city, and retreated at night, saving his sergeants. In the seventh ordinary year, General Yuan Shu of Anxi went to Shouchun. Wei's Yuzhou governor Li Xian sent his son to build forts; Qingzhi attacked, Li Xian surrendered, and Qingzhi occupied the city. He was transferred to Donggong Zhihe and titled Marquis of Guanzhong. In Datong's first year, a subordinate leader fortified and conquered Yan. General Changshan Wang Yuanzhao led 150,000 cavalry and infantry to rescue, reaching Tuojian, 40 miles from Guoyang. Qingzhi wanted to fight, but Tong Zhen advised caution. Qingzhi argued the Wei were tired and unsuspecting; he led 200 cavalry to defeat their front army. The Wei were horrified. Qingzhi then returned, and the generals attacked together, occupying Woyang City. From spring to winter, hundreds of battles ensued. The army grew exhausted, and Wei reinforcements threatened. Zhongzong and others planned retreat, but Qingzhi insisted on fighting, capturing four of thirteen Wei fortifications. Wang Wei of Woyang surrendered. Qingzhi displayed captured ears, beat drums, and attacked, causing the enemy to collapse. Over 30,000 men and women were captured. West Xuzhou was established on Guoyang's land. Emperor Gaozu praised Qingzhi in a personal letter.

translation:
The remaining nine city forts, whose military strength was still strong, displayed the left ears of the captured and slain enemies, beat drums and shouted to attack the enemies. The enemy then collapsed, captured a small amount of them, the vortex was filled, and more than 30,000 men and women in the city were captured.
Shao established West Xuzhou on the land of Guoyang.
Taking advantage of the victory, all the troops moved forward and stationed themselves in Chengfu.
Emperor Gaozu praised him and gave Qingzhi a Shao Shu written by him, saying: He is not a descendant of a general, nor is he a member of a wealthy family. He is dissatisfied with the current situation, which leads to this.
You can think deeply about the strategy and start well and end well.
Isn't it a true man to open the royal door to receive guests and spread the word of fame in books?
In the early years of Datong, Wang Yuanhao of Wei Beihai took the initiative to get out of trouble and surrendered because of the chaos in his dynasty, and asked to make him the lord of Wei.
Emperor Gaozu accepted him, appointed him Qingzhi Jiejie and Biaoyong General, and sent Yuan Hao back to the north.
Yuan Hao took the title of Emperor of Wei at Huanshui. He was awarded the title of Chijie, the envoy of Qing, general of Zhenbei, guard of the army, and commander of the front army. He set out from Liao County, advanced to Rongcheng, and then arrived in Suiyang.
Wei general Qiu Dagan had 70,000 troops and built nine forts to resist.
Qingzhi attacked him, and from dawn to afternoon, three city fortresses were captured, and Daqian surrendered.
At that time, General Wei Zhengshu, Jiyin Wang Yuanhuiye, led the Royal Guards and 20,000 noble servicemen to rescue Zhe and Si, and stationed in Huaqiu. The city was surrounded by water and was tightly guarded.
Qing ordered him to build a fortress on the water, capture the city, capture Zhuang Tomb alive, and seize 7,800 vehicles for transporting taxes.
Then they headed straight towards Dafun. The enemy looked at the flag and surrendered.
The five titles include the general of the guard of Shengqing, the governor of Lansu, and the arrest of Duke He.
So he led the people to the west.
Wei Zuopu shot Yang Yu, Xi'a Wang Yuanqing, and Fujun general Yuan Xianggong led the emperor's guard, royal family members, and nobles with a total of 70,000 soldiers, and occupied Rongyang to resist Yuan Hao.
The soldiers were strong and the city was dangerous, but Qingzhu failed to capture the city.
Wei general Yuan Tianmu's army was approaching again. He first sent his hussar general Erzhu Tumel to lead 5,000 Hu cavalry, and cavalry general Lu An to lead 9,000 Xiazhou infantry to assist Yang Dan. He also sent his right servant She'er Zhu Shilong and West Jingzhou governor Wang Zhuan's 10,000 cavalry to guard Hulao.
Tianmu and Tumeier arrived one after another, facing each other.
At that time, the stem salt had not been pulled out, and the soldiers were all frightened. Qingzhi took off his saddle and fed the war horses, and announced to everyone: Since I arrived here, I have broken down the city, killed people, and invaded a lot of land. You have killed fathers and brothers, and plundered people's children, which is incalculable.
Everyone in Tianmu is an enemy.
We only have 7,000 people and more than 300,000 captives. What happened today is that we are not seeking survival.
I and the captives cannot compete with each other in strength on the plains. Before he arrives, his fortress must be pacified. Don't be suspicious, sir. This will cause delays in having others slaughtered and cut into pieces.
So they all climbed up the city in one go. The strong men Shuyang Rensaixingti and Zhanzhao Mermaid Tianmin jumped over the low wall of the city and entered, thus conquering the city fortress.
summary: In early Datong, Wei's Wang Yuanhao surrendered due to internal chaos, seeking to become lord of Wei. Emperor Gaozu appointed Qingzhi as Jiejie and Biaoyong General, sending Yuan Hao north. Yuan Hao declared himself Emperor of Wei at Huanshui. Qingzhi, as Chijie and commander, advanced from Liao County to Suiyang. Wei general Qiu Dagan had 70,000 troops in nine forts; Qingzhi captured three by afternoon, and Daqian surrendered. Wei's Jiyin Wang Yuanhuiye led 20,000 troops to rescue; Qingzhi built a fortress on water, captured the city, and seized 7,800 tax vehicles. Heading to Dafun, enemies surrendered at the sight of his flag. Qingzhi became General of the Guard and Governor of Lansu. He led forces west. Wei's Yang Yu, Xi'a Wang Yuanqing, and Yuan Xianggong led 70,000 troops to hold Rongyang. Qingzhi failed to capture it. Wei general Yuan Tianmu's army approached; Qingzhi, with only 7,000 troops against 300,000 captives, rallied his men, conquered Rongyang, and defeated Tianmu's army. He entered Hulao, and Zhu Shichen fled. Yuan Ziyou fled, and Yuan Hao entered Luoyang Palace, ascending the throne. Qingzhi was appointed servant and general, with increased households. Wei generals led 40,000 troops to capture Daliang; Qingzhi's white-robed subordinates were invincible. A Luoyang nursery rhyme warned: "Thousands of troops should avoid white robes." From Zhixian to Luoyang, in 140 days, Qingzhi leveled 32 fortresses and fought 47 battles, unstoppable.

translation:
Emperor Gaozu then went down to Shao and stationed all his troops at the front edge of the border.
There are less than 10,000 Nan people in Luoxia, and the number of Qiang and barbarians is ten times that of them. The deputy commander of the army, Ma Fo Nian, said to Qingzhi: If there is no reward for great achievements, it will be dangerous for the monarch to be afraid. These two things have already happened. Is the general unconcerned?
Since ancient times, the emperor has been dethroned and the wise king has been established to help the crisis and resolve the difficulties. Very few people have a good death.
Today, the general's power has shaken the Central Plains and moved the rivers. It is a rare opportunity to kill Yuan Hao and defend Luoyang.
Qingzhi didn't listen.
Yuan Hao had appointed Ren Qingzhi as the governor of Xuzhou, so Qingzhi insisted on guarding it.
Yuan Hao was afraid of him, so he didn't send him.
Then he said: Your Majesty has entrusted the whole land of Luoyang to you. Suddenly I heard the decision to leave the imperial court. I want to go to Pengcheng. I will say that you will soon become rich and noble, and you will no longer plan for the country. The edicts are coming one after another. I am afraid it will become my responsibility to keep you.
Qingzhi did not dare to say anything more.
Wei Tianzhu's general Ji Zhufu, his right servant Sheqi Sai Shilong, the chief governor Wu Yulong, the hussar general Ji Zhu Tumu'er, Ji Zhurong's chief ministers Gao Huan, Xianbei and Ruirui, all claiming to have millions, took the Wei lord Yuan Ziyou and attacked Yuan Hao. Diligent in study, he began writing at twenty. Quiet and reluctant to serve, he was recruited as a secretary at thirty. He held posts including Prince Sheren, Beizhong Lang, and Danyang Yin Cheng. King Shu of Xiang appreciated him. He later served as Huang Menlang, General Qingche, and Minister of Civil Affairs. In the first year of Zhongdatong, he became Taifuqing, then General Zhenwei and Internal History of Linchuan. He returned as Regular Attendant of Sanqi and Minister of State. He proposed revising sacrificial music lyrics, replacing Shen Yue's works with classical references. Skilled in cursive calligraphy, he imitated Zhong Yao and Wang Xizhi, earning Emperor Gaozu's praise. In the seventh year, he served as General Renwei and Prefect of Shuyang. In the first year of Taiqing, he became Shizhong and Guozi Jijiu. In the second year, Hou Jing invaded, and Ziyun fled, dying of starvation at sixty-three in 549. His works include "Book of Jin" and "New Records of the East Palace." His son Xiao Te, skilled in calligraphy, died at twenty-five.

translation:
Ziyun was good at writing cursive official script and was regarded as a model by the world. He said that he was good at imitating Zhong Yao and Wang Xizhi and slightly changing his handwriting.
In reply to the edict: I used to have no ability to appreciate, so I decided it was precious according to the opinions of the world, so I imitated Wang Xianzhi's calligraphy for many years.
When he was twenty-six years old, he compiled the "Book of Jin" and wrote "The Biography of Two Kings". He wanted to write a comment on the writing style of cursive script, but it was not satisfactory and he failed to write it. He only briefly commented on Feibai style writing style.
It has been more than ten years since I first saw the imperial edict "On Calligraphy", a volume in which I commented on the calligraphy style and thoroughly understood the shape of the characters; I also thought that Wang Xizhi was inferior to Zhong Yao, just like Wang Xianzhi was inferior to Wang Xizhi.
After thinking about it, I realized that the rules of official script were first changed by Wang Xianzhi, and Zhong Yao was the one who standardized everything.
Since then, I feel that my writing skills have improved.
His calligraphy was highly praised by Emperor Gaozu. He once commented on Ziyun's calligraphy: "The pen is strong and straight, the heart and hand are in harmony, the skill is beyond Du Du, and the physical beauty is better than Cui Wei. He should compete with Zhong Yao."
He was appreciated like this.
In the seventh year, he served as General Renwei and Grand Administrator of Shuyang.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, he returned to the capital and was awarded Zong Zhengqing.
In the first year of Taiqing, he was again appointed as Shizhong and Guozi Jijiu, and led the Dazhongzheng of Xuzhou in the south.
In the second year, Hou Jing invaded the palace city, and Ziyun fled to the people.
In March of the third year, the palace city was lost. He fled eastward to Jinling and died of starvation in the monk's room of Xianling Temple. He was sixty-three years old.
His works include 110 volumes of "Book of Jin" and 20 volumes of "New Records of the East Palace".
The second son Xiaote was named Shida.
He became famous very early and was good at cursive calligraphy.
Emperor Gaozu once said to Xiao Te: Zijing's calligraphy is not as good as Wang Baozhi's.
Seeing Xiao Yi's handwriting recently made Qing feel threatened.
His official titles include Zuolang, Prince Sheren, Xuanhui, and the Zhongjun Records Office.
He took up the post of Haiyan Order, but was dismissed for some reasons.
At the age of twenty-five, he died in front of Wang Yun.
Zihui, whose courtesy name is Jingguang, is Ziyun's younger brother.
When he was young, he dabbled in book history and was also talented in literature.
He started as a member of the imperial family and served as a minister of Sanqi, and moved to the office of Nanzhonglang.
Served as Lin'an Order.
He has a quiet temperament and few hobbies. He once participated in the Chongyun Hall to listen to the "Three Wisdom Sutra" lectures, and came back to write "Lectures on Fu" as a memorial, which was highly praised.
He moved to Anxi to serve as a consultant to King Wuling of Anxi Province, and brought in new orders. He was transferred to Yitong to serve as a member of the imperial family, and to serve as the chief historian of Hussar. He died.
summary: Zihui, Ziyun's younger brother, was talented in literature. He started as a member of the imperial family and served as Sanqi Minister and Lin'an Order. Quiet and reserved, he wrote "Lectures on Fu" after attending a lecture. He later served as Consultant to King Wuling and Chief Historian of Hussar, dying in office. Chen Libu Shangshu Yao Chari noted that the Liang Dynasty, unlike previous dynasties, did not suppress former clans, allowing Zike's brothers to hold positions, reflecting Emperor Gaozu's magnanimity.

translation:
Zhu Yi, whose courtesy name was Yanhe, was from Qiantang, Wu County.
His father, Zhu Xun, was well-known for his loyalty and righteousness. He served as an official in the Qi Dynasty until the king of Jiangxia joined the army and was ordered by Wu Ping.
When Zhu Yi was old, his grandfather stroked Zhu Yi's head happily and said to his grandfather Zhaozhi: "This son is not an ordinary person. He will become your family."
He is more than ten years old. He likes to gamble in groups and is extremely hated by the township party.
When he grew up, he forced himself to change his bad habits and studied as a teacher. He studied the Five Classics, especially "Li" and "Yi", dabbled in literature and history, and was proficient in miscellaneous arts. He was good at gambling, go, calligraphy, and arithmetic.
When he was twenty years old, he arrived in the capital. The Minister ordered Shen to interview him, so he joked with him: "You are young, why are you not honest?"
Zhu Yi hesitated and did not understand the meaning of these words.
Shen Yue then said: "The only skills in the world are literature, history, classics, Yi, chess, calligraphy and so on. If you take them all at once, you can call them dishonest."
In this year, a letter was written stating that it was appropriate for Jiankang to set up a prison department, and Yu Tingwei was of the same rank. The edict was submitted to Yu Shangshu for detailed discussion, and he agreed with his opinion.
Under the old system, one could only become an official at the age of twenty-five.
At this time, Zhu Yi was twenty-one years old, and the imperial court made an exception and ordered him to be promoted to the post of Yangzhou Councilor to engage in history.
Not long ago, Shaoling was looking for people with special talents. Doctor Mingshan of the Five Classics recommended Zhu Yi and said: I met Zhu Yi, a native of Qiantang. He was still young, but he had perfect moral character, was shrewd and sophisticated in his work, had no thoughts of distraction when he was alone, and when no one saw him, he still looked respectful as if he were facing guests. His mind was broad and deep, and his demeanor was extraordinary.
For example, a famous mountain is so high that it is difficult to climb to the top; a blue sea is so deep that it is difficult to peer into its depths.
Another example is that Guizhang has just been carved, and the brocade group he is wearing begins to weave. When touched, it will make a loud sound, and the decoration will appear in the world.
Observe his honest character, which is not only rare among ten families. If he is allowed to carry a heavy load and gallop on a long distance, he will definitely have the function of a thousand-mile horse.
Emperor Gaozu summoned him and asked him to explain the principles of "The Book of Filial Piety" and "The Book of Changes". He was very happy after hearing this and said to the people around him: "Zhu Yi is indeed special."
Later I met Ming Shanbin and said to him: The person you recommended is indeed a very qualified person.
So he called Zhu Yi to be on duty in the Western Province, and soon he became a doctor of Imperial College.
This year, Emperor Gaozu personally explained the "Book of Filial Piety" and asked Zhu Yi to read it.
He was moved to the post of Minister Yi Cao Lang, and concurrently served as Zhongshu Tongshi Shiren. After repeated promotions, he was promoted to Hongluqing, the prince's right guard, and soon he was appointed as a member of the imperial family.
summary: Zhu Yi, courtesy name Yanhe, was from Qiantang, Wu County. His father, Zhu Xun, served as an official in the Qi Dynasty. As a child, Zhu Yi was fond of gambling and was disliked by his community. In his youth, he reformed his habits, studied the Five Classics—especially the "Li" and "Yi"—and became skilled in literature, history, chess, calligraphy, and arithmetic. At age twenty, he went to the capital, where Shen Yue interviewed him and remarked on his diverse talents. Despite the rule that officials must be at least twenty-five, Zhu Yi was appointed at twenty-one as Yangzhou Councilor due to an imperial exception. Doctor Mingshan of the Five Classics recommended him, praising his moral character and intellect. Emperor Gaozu summoned Zhu Yi to explain the "Book of Filial Piety" and the "Book of Changes," was pleased, and appointed him to the Western Province and later as a doctor of Imperial College. He rose through various posts, including Hongluqing and prince's right guard.

translation:
In the fifth year of the Ordinary Period, a large-scale Northern Expedition was launched. Yuan Faseng, the governor of Xuzhou in the Northern Wei Dynasty, sent an envoy to ask for the surrender of the land and the people. Shao ordered a minister to discuss the truth of the matter.
Zhu Yi said: Since the king's army marched north and continued to win, the local forces in Xuzhou have weakened, and they all want to blame Fa Monk. Fa Monk is afraid of the impending disaster, so his surrender will not be false.
Emperor Gaozu sent Zhu Yi to report to the Dharma monk and ordered all the troops to respond, all under Zhu Yi's command.
After arriving, the monk followed the imperial decree, just as Zhu Yi predicted.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, he moved to serve as a regular attendant of Sanqi.
Since Zhou She's death, Zhu Yi took his place in charge of the court's affairs, the replacement of military commanders, court rituals and state codes, and the drafting of Shao's imperial edicts.
Whenever people from all over the world come in to submit their reports, the official records and detailed consultations are all piled up in front of him. Zhu Yi writes with his pen and makes decisions. He is talented and smart. He keeps writing in his hand, and everything is done in an instant.
In the fourth year of Datong, he was promoted to General Youwei.
In the sixth year, Zhu Yishou told the "Lao Zi Yi" written by Chan Dan in Jinshu Hall, and the imperial order allowed it.
When he sat down to speak, there were more than a thousand people from the imperial court and Taoists and laymen listening, which became a grand event at that time.
At that time, the Shilin Museum was opened in the west of the city to introduce scholars. Zhu Yiyu and Zuo Cheng He Chen took turns lecturing on the "Book of Rites" written by Gao Zu, and the crown prince summoned Zhu Yi to lect on "Yi" in Xuanpu.
In the eighth year, he was appointed as a servant.
In the first year of Taiqing, he was moved to the position of general of Zuowei and led the infantry.
In the second year, he was moved to the position of leader, but his family remained as usual.
Emperor Gaozu dreamed that he had pacified the Central Plains, and he praised and celebrated it. The next morning, he told Zhu Yi the dream, and Zhu Yi replied: This is a sign of the unification of the four directions in the universe.
When Hou Jing returned and surrendered, he summoned the ministers to discuss it. Shangshu Pu She Xie Li and others thought it was unacceptable to accept it. Emperor Gaozu wanted to take Zhu Yi over, but the matter was pending. Zeng came to Wu Shanyu at dawn and said to himself: Our country is so peaceful that I will accept the land now. If doing so will cause chaos to the country, it will be too late to regret it.
Zhu Yi sensed Gaozu's hidden thoughts and responded: The wise emperor rules the world and obeys the will of heaven. The people of the subjugated north do not admire you because they have no chance to express their wishes.
Now Hou Jing divides most of the land of Wei State, sincerely expresses his submission, and comes from afar to join the Holy Dynasty. Isn't it true that God enlightens his heart and everyone helps him realize his plan?
After deducing Hou Jing's original intention and examining this matter, it is highly commendable.
If we don't accept him today, I'm afraid it will make those who come after us despair.
This is obvious, may your Majesty have no doubts.
Emperor Gaozu wanted to adopt Zhu Yi's advice, but he thought of his previous dream, so he accepted Hou Jing's surrender.
The Marquis of Zhenyang was defeated and captured, and an envoy was sent back from Wei to tell him that Gao Cheng, the prime minister of Wei, wanted to live in harmony with the Liang Dynasty again.
In June of that year, Jiankang Ling Xie Ting and Tongzhi Lang Xu Ling were sent as envoys to Tonghao in the north.
At that time, Hou Jing was guarding Shouchun. He repeatedly warned Gaozu to sever peace with Wei and asked for the envoy to be recovered.
He also wrote to Zhu Yi with sincere words, but Zhu Yi just relayed the imperial edict in reply.
In August, Hou Jing raised his troops to rebel in the name of condemning Zhu Yi.
Zhu Yi recruited 3,000 troops. Hou Jing marched to Beijing and used these people to guard Da Sima Gate.
At the beginning, Hou Jing conspired to rebel, and the governor of Hezhou, Xiao Fan, the king of Poyang, and the governor of Sizhou, Yang Yaren, reported many times. Zhu Yi thought that Hou Jing would not do that if he was sent to the Liang Dynasty alone, so he said to the envoy: The king of Poyang does not allow the country to have a guest!
He also suppressed the report and did not report it, so the court did not take precautions against this matter.
When Hou Jing came to invade, the civil and military officials in the city blamed him.
The crown prince also wrote "Ode to the Siege of the City", the last chapter of which says: Wearing a high crown and thick-soled shoes, he sat on a fat horse, climbed to the palace where the emperor lived, opened the golden gate of the royal family, stated strategies to assist the king, and announced the power of political punishments. Many fortifications were built in the surrounding suburbs, and all nations were unrest.
summary: In the fifth year of the Ordinary Period, during a northern expedition, Yuan Faseng of the Northern Wei sought to surrender. Zhu Yi confirmed the sincerity of the surrender, and Emperor Gaozu placed him in command. After Zhou She's death, Zhu Yi managed court affairs, military appointments, and imperial edicts. He was known for his efficiency in handling documents. In the sixth year of Datong, he lectured on the "Laozi Yi" to over a thousand listeners. He later served as a servant and general. When Hou Jing surrendered, Zhu Yi advised Emperor Gaozu to accept him, citing a dream of unification. Despite warnings from officials like Xie Li, the emperor followed Zhu Yi's advice. Hou Jing later rebelled, blaming Zhu Yi, who raised troops to defend the capital. Zhu Yi had suppressed earlier reports of Hou Jing's conspiracy, leading to the city's siege. The crown prince's poem criticized Zhu Yi, who fell ill and died at sixty-seven. Emperor Gaozu mourned him deeply and granted posthumous honors. Zhu Yi held power for over thirty years, was skilled at flattering the emperor, and amassed wealth through gifts. He was stingy, never sharing with others, and wrote over 100 works, many lost in war.

translation:
May I ask the jackal who he is?
May I ask the gizzard who he is for?
This refers to Zhu Yi.
Zhu Yi was so angry that he fell ill and died at the age of sixty-seven.
Shaoling said: Zhu Yi, the leader of the old army, has a broad mind and outstanding talents. He has been discussing and planning strategies in the court for many years. I was supposed to be assisting the imperial government in its administration, and I had entrusted him with important responsibilities for a long time. He died suddenly, and my heart was filled with sadness.
You can posthumously give him a coffin as a posthumous gift from his attendant and minister, Youpu She.
The money needed for the funeral can be provided at will.
In the past, when ministers died, they did not give posthumous gifts to the chancellor. When Zhu Yi passed away, Emperor Gaozu felt sorry for him. When discussing the matter of posthumous gifts, some people who were friendly to Zhu Yi began to report: Although Zhu Yi held many officials, what he hoped for in his life was to be a law enforcement official.
According to his long-cherished ambition, Emperor Gaozu made this posthumous gift.
Zhu Yi had been in power for more than thirty years. He was good at peering into the innermost intentions of his lord, and he was able to flatter and obey the emperor's orders, so he was particularly favored.
Officials in the officialdom often serve from outside to the middle. All these four positions can wear mink tails on their hats, and lead from the right guard to the leader. These four positions all have retinues and honor guards when they travel. There has never been such a thing in modern times.
Zhu Yi and his disciples built houses from Chaogou all the way to Qingxi. The house was surrounded by terraces and ponds, where they could play with guests every spare time.
Gifts from all parties and wealth accumulated.
He has a stingy temperament and has never given anything to others.
The delicacies in the kitchen were delicious and rotten, and more than ten carts of them were often thrown away every month, even though his sons and relatives did not give them away.
He wrote more than 100 expositions, notes on rituals, and essays on "Li" and "Yi", many of which were lost during the war.
The eldest son was named Su, and he was a doctor of state; the second son was named Run, and he was appointed as Situ Tuo.
Both died in the war.
He Chen, named Guobao, was from Shanyin in Kuaiji.
His uncle He Chang was appointed as an infantry captain and was a great Confucianist of the time.
When He Chen was young, He Chang taught him Confucian classics, and he could understand the principles as soon as he listened.
He Yi felt very strange and often said: "This son should be distinguished by his understanding of the meaning of the scriptures."
After He Chang's death, He Chen's family was poor and he often traveled to and from Zhuji, selling millet to support himself.
In his spare time, he studied economics and was especially proficient in the "Three Rites".
At first, He Jiang gathered his disciples in the countryside to teach economics, but now they started to learn economics from He Chen.
In ordinary years, the governor of Linchuan called him to serve as a wine minister and engage in history.
He Ge began to show his talents in the capital. When Emperor Gaozu learned that he had knowledge, he summoned him in the Wende Hall and talked happily with him. He told Xu Mian, a servant of Xu Mian: "He Ge indeed has a scholarship that has been handed down from generation to generation."
So he was appointed as the minister of the kingdom, and soon he was concurrently appointed as the doctor of Taixue. Then he was moved to the position of Zhongwei to participate in military affairs, Shangshu general, Shiren, and ceremonial affairs.
After many years of promotion, he was promoted to Tongzhi Zhengyuanlang, but he remained the same.
He was also appointed to record the affairs of the king of Poyang in the west, and concurrently served as minister Zuo Cheng. Upon completion of his term, he was actually granted the title.
He Chen was ordered to compile the "New Mi Law", which is still in use today.
summary: He Chen, courtesy name Guobao, was from Shanyin. His uncle He Chang taught him Confucian classics, and he excelled in the "Three Rites." After He Chang's death, He Chen sold millet to support himself. He later taught economics and was summoned by the governor of Linchuan. Emperor Gaozu appointed him as a minister and doctor of Taixue. He Chen compiled the "New Mi Law" and debated ritual matters, such as whether one could marry during mourning. He argued that rituals should not interfere with mourning, and his views were accepted. He served as a regular attendant and censor, but was dismissed for buying the princess's house. He later held various posts, including Huangmen minister and Guozi doctor. He Chen was known for his elegant demeanor and was called "He Ya" in the palace. He submitted a sealed memorial criticizing current affairs, including the decline in household registrations due to corrupt officials, extravagant feasts and entertainments, and the need for frugality. He also criticized the emperor's reliance on flattering officials and the waste of resources. Emperor Gaozu responded angrily, defending his own frugality and questioning He Chen's claims. He Chen apologized and did not criticize again. He later served as Taifuqing and general. During Hou Jing's rebellion, He Chen was captured and forced to persuade officials to surrender. He fled home after Taicheng fell but was recaptured and appointed as Doctor Jin Ziguanglu. He died at sixty-nine, leaving over 100 chapters of works.

translation:
After receiving the order, He Chen could only admit his mistake and did not dare to criticize him again.
A long time later, he was moved to the post of Taifuqing.
In the second year of Taiqing, he was moved to the post of General Yunqi and Changshi of Xuancheng King of the Chinese Army.
Hou Jinggao's troops attacked the capital, and the king moved to Taiwan, leaving He Chen and Sima Yang Ao to guard the East Mansion.
The thieves soon captured the capital and allowed the soldiers to slaughter him. He Chen was shot but was still alive. The thieves found him and drove him to the palace in a car. They asked him to see Wang Ke, the servant, and Zhu Yi, the leader, and persuaded them to open the city gate and let the thieves in.
Wang Ke and others blamed him, but he stopped crying. The thief drove him to Zhuangyan Temple in a car for treatment of his wounds.
The next year, Taicheng fell and He Chen fled back to his hometown.
In the winter of that year, thieves invaded Kuaiji, arrested He Chen again, sent him out of the capital, and appointed him as Doctor Jin Ziguanglu.
He later became ill and died at the age of sixty-nine.
He Chen compiled more than 100 chapters in total such as "The Book of Rites", "The Five Classics' Zhiyi" and various rites and methods.
His son Xu Mian, in the early years of the Taiqing Dynasty, served as the prefect of Bashan together with the Marquis of Xichang. He died in chaos in the county.
Yao Cha, the official secretary of the Chen Dynasty, said: Xia Housheng once said: The worry of a scholar is that he is not proficient in Confucian classics; if he is proficient in Confucian classics, he will be able to obtain high officials and titles as easily as picking up mustard greens on the ground.
Zhu Yi and He Chen were both from humble backgrounds. They relied on their knowledge of Confucian classics to gain eminence when they had the opportunity, which is in line with Xia Housheng's remarks.
However, after Zhu Yi received the emperor's favor and assumed power, he could not assist the emperor in the right way, but was aggressive and flattering.
It was Zhu Yi's responsibility to lead the enemy to defeat the country.
The disaster caused was obvious, but his guilt was not shown. After his death, he was still treated with special favors.
If there is no punishment for the guilty, and the rewards are so false and unrealistic, and there is no reason to persuade them to stop them, how can we govern the country?
Gentleman, the reason why you know about the troubles in the Taiqing period is that it has something to do with Zaodian.
summary: Yao Cha commented that Zhu Yi and He Chen rose from humble backgrounds through their knowledge of Confucian classics. However, Zhu Yi's flattery and failure to assist the emperor properly led to national disaster. Despite his guilt, he received special favors after death, which Yao Cha criticized as unjust governance.

translation:
Kong Xiuyuan, courtesy name Qingxu, was a native of Shanyin, Kuaiji.
The eighth grandson of Kong Chong, the prefect of Danyang in Jin Dynasty.
His great-grandfather Kong Yaozhi served as Minister of the Ministry of Water of the Song Dynasty.
His father, Wang Er, died early when he was appointed to Chalu and fell into the Wangji family to join the army.
Xiuyuan lost his father when he was eleven years old. The mourning period was completely in accordance with etiquette. Every time he saw his father's handwriting, he would burst into tears and couldn't help himself. Everyone who saw it would not shed tears for him.
Later, he went to Wuxing to study under Xuan Diezao, and he was familiar with the principles of Confucian classics.
In the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, the prefecture held a ceremony for scholars. Taiwei Tu Cunqi read his policies and articles and admired them very much. He said to the people sitting with him: "Why are Dong Zhongshu and Hua Lingsi better than him? They can be called models for future generations."
Looking at his policy article, it can be said that he has the talent of a king.
Wang Rong, a native of Longxie, was very friendly with him, so he recommended Kong Shunuo to King Situ Jingling as a bachelor of Xili.
The chisel sculpture was built, and Lu Li and the humanoid master were both doctors of Taixue. People at the time thought it was a beauty.
Xiuyuan came to Beijing for the first time and stayed in the house of Kong Deng, the minister of the clan's Shaofu. He once went to the temple for sacrifices. Fan Yun, the attendant, met him for the first time and praised him very much. He said: "I met you unexpectedly, and my stingy heart disappeared. Unexpectedly, I parted the clouds and saw the blue sky today."
Later in the day, he drove to the Shaofu Gate. Renzhao prepared the banquet, thinking that he must be visiting him. However, he visited Xiuyuan alone, talked for the whole day, and drove back together. Kong Deng felt deeply ashamed.
Shangshu ordered Shen Yue to be a noble person in the court, and the door was full of carriages and horses. Xiu Yuan would arrive later, and he would receive him humbly and let him sit on the right side to discuss literature and meaning.
He was held in high esteem by learned men as such.
Soon he was granted the title of Prince of Linchuan to join the army.
Xu Mian, the Minister of Civil Affairs during the Great Ancestor's reign: Now that the emperor's career has been decided, he needs someone who is knowledgeable and understands the etiquette of the court to be appointed as Minister Cao Lang.
Think about me, who can do the job.
Xu Mian replied: Kong Xiuyuan has clear knowledge and is familiar with the past. He is familiar with the "Daily Notes" of the Jin Dynasty and Song Dynasty.
Emperor Gaozu had always heard about it, so he was awarded the title of Doctor Cao, who was also the Minister of Book Yi.
At that time, there were many changes in the court rituals. Whenever he was asked about the past, Xiuyuan immediately made random decisions based on his memory without hesitation.
Renfang, the official of the official department, often called him "Kong Dusong".
He moved to Kangyuanzheng, where he tried cases and seldom wronged anyone.
Later, some people were selected to serve as prison chiefs, and Emperor Gaozu encouraged them by citing Xiu Yuan's deeds.
He was granted the title of Zhongshu Sheren, and Situ joined the army in the palace's record office. He moved to Zuocheng, Shangshu, and rectified the Shangshu Province, living up to the expectations of the court.
At that time, Prince Zhan Shizhou She compiled "The Book of Rites", which included relevant historical materials from Han and Wei to Qi and Liang, and all Xiuyuan's memorials were selected for inclusion.
summary: Kong Xiuyuan, courtesy name Qingxu, was from Shanyin, Kuaiji, and a descendant of Jin Dynasty official Kong Chong. Orphaned at eleven, he strictly observed mourning rites and was deeply moved by his father's handwriting. He studied Confucian classics under Xuan Diezao in Wuxing. In the fourth year of Jianwu, his policy essays impressed Taiwei Tu Cunqi, who compared him favorably to Dong Zhongshu and Hua Lingsi. Wang Rong of Longxie recommended him as a bachelor of Xili to King Situ Jingling. Upon arriving in the capital, he stayed with Minister Kong Deng, where Attendant Fan Yun praised him highly. Later, when Renzhao prepared a banquet expecting many guests, he visited only Xiuyuan, causing Kong Deng shame. Shangshu Ling Shen Yue, a powerful court figure, received Xiuyuan humbly and seated him at his right to discuss literature. Xiuyuan was appointed Prince of Linchuan's army adjutant. During Emperor Gaozu's reign, Xu Mian recommended him as Minister Cao Lang for his knowledge of Jin and Song court rituals. He served as Doctor Cao and Minister of Book Yi, answering historical questions from memory without hesitation. Renfang, an official, called him "Kong Dusong." He moved to Kangyuanzheng, where he judged cases fairly. Later, as Zhongshu Sheren and Zuocheng, he rectified the Shangshu Province. He compiled "The Book of Rites" with Prince Zhan Shizhou She, including his own memorials. As Shilang of Huangmen and Censor Zhongcheng, he enforced laws strictly, intimidating officials. He served as Shaofu Qing and Danyang Yin, then as chief historian of Xuanhui Jin'an Palace and Prefect of Nanjun, overseeing Jingzhou. Emperor Gaozu entrusted his young son to him, comparing him to Zhou Chang. Xiuyuan served with distinction, rejecting favor-seeking. He later held posts including Standing Attendant, Yulin Supervisor, and Secretary Supervisor. King Jin'an reserved a special seat for him. In the seventh year of the ordinary year, he became Governor of Yangzhou after Wang Hong's death, praised for his talent and knowledge. In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was awarded Doctor Jin Ziguanglu. He died in May at sixty-four, mourned by Emperor Gaozu, who granted posthumous honors and a frugal burial. His collection included over 7,000 volumes and fifteen volumes of impeachment proceedings.

translation:
After the period of mourning expired, he and Jiang Su went to Taixue together to become a national student and achieved the best results.
Wang Rong, the scribe of Qi Quzhong, and Xie Chui, the official secretary, respected them very much.
Jiji once served as a guard in the palace. On his way back, he went to visit Jiang Ge. It was snowing heavily. He saw that Jiang Ge was single-seating in ragged clothes, but he was concentrating on studying without getting tired. After sighing for a long time, he took off his clothes, cut off half of the felt with his own hands and used it as a bedding for Jiang Jin.
When King Situ Jingling heard of his name, he introduced him as a bachelor of Nuoying.
At the age of twenty, he was elected as a scholar in Xuzhou.
At that time, Hu Xiezhi, a native of Yuzhang, was handling state affairs. Wang Rong wrote to him and asked him to recommend Jiang Ge.
Xie Zhi was about to recommend Langxie Wang Fan, so he replaced him with Jiang Ge.
He became an official at the invitation of the imperial court.
Pu She Jiang Zhe tried his best to introduce him. Jiang Zhe was appointed Prince Zhan Shi, and Qi Zuo Hong Jin was appointed as Fu Cheng.
At that time, he was very powerful, and he believed that Wuxing had the talent to manage the country, so he was asked to take charge of secrets, and he was entrusted with all the imperial edicts and documents.
Jiang Ge kept his identity secret, and the matter was not known to outsiders.
Liao Tuo was killed, and all his guests were implicated, but Jiang Jin was able to avoid it only by her cleverness.
He was awarded the title of Minister Jiabu Lang.
In the first year of the Zhongxing Dynasty, Emperor Gaozu marched into Shitou. At that time, Yuan Ang, the prefect of Wuxing, occupied the county and resisted. Emperor Gaozu asked Jiang Ge to write a letter to Ang. He wrote it impromptu. The words were elegant and concise. Emperor Gaozu greatly appreciated it, so he made him and Xu Mian share the post of secretary.
The King of Jian'an was appointed as the governor of Yongzhou, and asked to be in charge of the administration. He appointed Jiang Ge as the Zhengbei Records Office to join the army, and led the Zhonglu Order.
He and his younger brother Jiang Guan had never been separated, and they couldn't bear to be separated, so they begged to accompany him, so he appointed Jiang Guan to join the army for the expedition to the north and also served as a recorder.
At that time, Shen Yue, a native of Wuxing, and Ren La, a native of Le'an, both respected him. Ren Fang wrote to Jiang Ge saying: This time Yong Mansion has made a wonderful selection of talents, and all the positions of the study are held by brothers Qing. It can be said that they can control two dragons for long distances and gallop for thousands of miles.
When he arrived in Jiangxia, Jiang Guan fell ill and died.
Jiang Ge was in Yongzhou at that time and received courtesy from the prince, as if he were a friend of common people.
The king was conquered as Danyang Yin, appointed Jiang Ge as the recorder, led the five officials, and was awarded Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi, Jiankangzheng.
He frequently moved to Moling and Jiankang orders, and his administration was clear and strict, and the powerful were afraid of him.
He was appointed as Zhongshu Sheren, Shangshu Zuocheng, Sinong Qing, and then served as Yunhui Jin'an Wang Changshi, Xunyang Prefect, and handled Jiangzhou Prefecture affairs.
He moved to Renwei and became the chief historian of Luling. The governor continued to act as usual, and his purity and strictness made officials in hundreds of cities fear him.
At that time, the young king mostly listened to the opinions of the commander-in-chief when doing things. Jiang Ge regarded himself as upright and would not sit with the commander-in-chief and others.
Soon he was moved to the post of Dr. Zuo Guanglu, Nanping Wang Changshi, and Yushi Zhongcheng. He impeached the powerful and was fearless.
He was awarded the rank of Shaofu Qing, and was appointed as General Zhenwei, Beizhonglang, Prince Changshi of Nankang, and Grand Administrator of Guangling. He was then granted the title of Chief Secretary of the Prince of Zhenbei Yuzhang, and the general and governor remained the same.
At that time, Yuan Faseng, the governor of Xuzhou in the Wei Dynasty, surrendered, and Jiang Ge was ordered to guard Pengcheng with the king.
When the city was lost, Jiang Ge never rode a horse, so he returned by boat. Passing by Xiapi, he was captured by the Wei people.
Yuan Yanming, the governor of Xuzhou in the Wei Dynasty, had known Jiang Ge's talents and received him ceremoniously. Jiang Ge refused to pay homage because he had a foot disease. Yanming was going to harm him. Seeing Jiang Jin's serious words, he respected him even more.
At that time, Zu Qu was detained, and Xingdan surrendered! He argued about writing "Qi Qi" and "Leu Engraving Inscription". Liao Jian scolded Zu Qu and said: You have received great kindness from the country and have not repaid it. Now you have written an inscription for the enemy and you have failed the court.
When Yanming heard this, he asked Jiang Ge to write a stele for Zhangcong Temple and a memorial to Peng Zu. Jiang Ge declined on the grounds that he had been imprisoned for a long time and would no longer have the desire to do so.
Yanming forced him very hard and was about to punish him with a beating.
Jiang Ge said sternly: "Jiang Ge is sixty years old and cannot serve the emperor. He is lucky to die today. I swear not to write for others."
Yanming knew he couldn't make him surrender, so he stopped forcing him.
summary: Jiang Ge, courtesy name Xiuying, was from Kaocheng, Jiyang. His father died when he was nine, and his mother when he was sixteen, after which he and his brother Jiang Guan studied at Taixue, excelling. Wang Rong and Xie Chui respected them. Once, Ji Ji saw Jiang Ge studying in ragged clothes during a snowstorm and gave him half a felt. King Situ Jingling made him a bachelor. At twenty, he was elected a scholar in Xuzhou. He served as an official, with Pu She Jiang Zhe introducing him. He kept his role in handling imperial edicts secret, avoiding implication in Liao Tuo's death. In the first year of Zhongxing, Emperor Gaozu appreciated his impromptu letter to Yuan Ang. He served under King Jian'an in Yongzhou, but his brother Jiang Guan died en route. He held various posts, including Zhongshu Sheren and Yushi Zhongcheng, impeaching the powerful. During a Wei invasion, he was captured but refused to write inscriptions for the enemy, even under threat of beating. He was given three liters of millet daily. Emperor Gaozu later praised his integrity and appointed him to high offices. As governor of Dongzhou, he refused gifts, handled cases efficiently, and punished corruption. He left office with only a small boat, using stones for ballast. In Wu County, he quelled thieves through kindness. He served as Minister of Ren Duzhi, supporting commoners and juniors. He died in February of the first year of Datong, leaving a collection of twenty volumes. He served eight palaces and four kings without acquiring concubines, living frugally. His sons Xingmin and Cong Jian died early, the latter killed by Hou Jing's rebels. The historian noted that Emperor Gaozu valued Kong Xiuyuan's insights, while Jiang Ge was known for his intelligence and straightforwardness.

translation:
Zhang Mian, also known as Yuan Chang, was the son of the chariot and cavalry general Hong Ce.
When he was only a few years old, his maternal grandfather Liu Zhongde, who was from Zhongshan, thought he was very special. He once said: This son is not an ordinary person, he is the noble person of the Zhang family.
At the end of the Yongyuan period of the Qi Dynasty, the righteous army rose up. Hongce followed Gaozu to Beijing to crusade, leaving Zhang Mian in Xiangyang. He was just ten years old. Every time he heard about the victory or defeat of the army, his face showed sorrow and joy.
In the first year of Tianjian, Hong Ce was appointed Wei Qing and was killed by demon thieves. Zhang Mian grieved that his father died tragically and went beyond the usual mourning rituals. He sent people to warn and advise.
When the period of mourning is over, the mourning period is over, he inherits the title of Marquis of Taoyang County, and summons the descendants of the country.
He was recruited from his family as secretary Lang and appointed as the governor of Huainan at the age of eighteen.
Concerned that he was young and not familiar with official affairs, he sent his master to write a letter to obtain the copy of the county magistrate. When he saw that his decision was appropriate, he highly praised him.
After returning to the capital, he was appointed Prince Sheren, and Yun Hui served as a foreign soldier to join the army.
Zhang Mian studied diligently when he was young, completed the required reading by himself, kept writing, and was very clear about selecting and criticizing various academic schools.
When a guest holds a scroll and asks for advice, he answers his questions without missing anything.
There was a vacancy in the palace, and the chief minister said to Tu Tian: "This position has traditionally been for appointing people with literary talent, and it is at the head of the court. The person appointed should be carefully selected."
Zhang Mian was recommended for selection.
Soon after, he was appointed as the prefect of Wuling, and was appointed Prince Xima and Zhongsheren in the capital.
Zhang Mian's mother Liu Ya, because Zhang Mian's father died in a poor family and the burial etiquette was not thorough, so she never lived as the main wife or lived with her son in the official residence.
Qiang Mian did not dare to use the salary he earned in the county, and even his wife and children did not wear new clothes. When he returned to the capital, he gave it all to his mother to support his relatives. Although it was all his savings for many years, it was all used up in a short time. Zhang Mian's private room was often empty, like an ordinary poor family.
After repeated promotions, he was appointed as Beizhonglang and consulted to join the army. He was willing to have a long history.
He served as the internal history of Yuzhang.
Zhang Mian used favors for the government and did not investigate repeatedly because of suspicion. Officials and people were inspired by his virtues and did not dare to commit fraud. Therefore, the old people said: There has been no such person in decades.
In the first year of Datong, he was conscripted into the post of Situ Zuo Changshi. Due to illness, he was not accepted. He was appointed as the prince's concubine and led the Yulin Supervisor.
Soon he was moved to the post of Yushi Zhongcheng. He was convicted of arresting people and fighting with foreign envoys. He was demoted to Huangmenlang, which also took the lead in his previous post. Soon he was changed to a real professor.
Zhang Mian served as the imperial censor. He was fearless and hesitant in handling matters according to the law, and was known to be upright. Emperor Gaozu sent a painter to paint a portrait of him and place it in the official office of the minister to encourage officials.
In the third year of Zhongdatong, he was moved to serve as a minister, but he was not accepted and died at the age of forty-two.
Shaoling gave him posthumous gifts to his servants and added him to General Zhenwei, but the marquis remained the same.
summary: Zhang Mian, also known as Yuan Chang, was the son of General Hong Ce. As a child, his maternal grandfather Liu Zhongde recognized his exceptional nature, declaring him a noble person of the Zhang family. During the Qi Dynasty's Yongyuan period, when his father followed Gaozu to war, ten-year-old Zhang Mian was left in Xiangyang, where his emotions mirrored the army's victories and defeats. After his father was killed by demon thieves in the first year of Tianjian, Zhang Mian mourned excessively, beyond normal rituals. Upon completing mourning, he inherited the title of Marquis of Taoyang County. At eighteen, he was appointed governor of Huainan. Concerned about his youth, his superior sent a master to evaluate him but was impressed by his appropriate decisions. Returning to the capital, he served as Prince Sheren and later as a foreign soldier joining the army. Zhang Mian studied diligently, mastered required readings, and wrote extensively, clearly critiquing various academic schools. He answered guests' questions without omission. When a palace position became vacant, the chief minister recommended Zhang Mian for his literary talent. He later served as prefect of Wuling and Prince Xima. His mother Liu Ya, due to his father's poor burial, never lived as the main wife or in official residences. Zhang Mian did not use his salary for personal gain, giving it all to his mother, leaving his household as frugal as a poor family. He was promoted to Beizhonglang and served as internal history of Yuzhang, governing with favor and without suspicion, inspiring officials and people not to commit fraud. Elders noted no such governance in decades. In the first year of Datong, he was summoned as Situ Zuo Changshi but declined due to illness, later becoming the prince's concubine and Yulin Supervisor. He was moved to Yushi Zhongcheng but demoted for arresting people and fighting with foreign envoys. As imperial censor, he was fearless and upright, prompting Gaozu to have his portrait painted to encourage officials. In the third year of Zhongdatong, he was moved to serve as a minister but died at forty-two. Gaozu wept bitterly, and Prince Zhaoming mourned, praising Zhang Mian's knowledge and official skills in a letter to his brother. Zhang Mian loved classical books, collecting over 10,000 volumes, and compiled "Hou Han Ji" and "Jin Chao" along with "Jiangzuo Collection," though unfinished. His son Fu inherited his title.

translation:
Pei Ziye, a native of Hedong, said: Zhang Libu has been appointed as the mouthpiece, but it is a pity that he was appointed late.
Ziye has an open-minded temperament and says to himself: When he is over thirty years old, he no longer visits people.
He had not met Zhang Lan at first, so he humbly respected him, and thus they became a close friend.
In the first year of Datong, he served as the official historian of Ningyuan Huarong, and also took photos of the state affairs of Langye and Pengcheng counties.
In the second year, he was moved to the post of Huarong Gongbeizhonglang Changshi and Mu Lanling prefect, and was awarded the title of General Zhenwei to handle the affairs of the prefecture.
In the third year, he entered the imperial court and was appointed as the minister of the branch. When his mother died, he resigned.
After the period of mourning was over, he was relieved of his duties and became the prefect of Wuxing.
Zhang Zuan managed the county affairs, eliminating the cumbersome affairs, making the administration clear and simple, and the people all found it convenient.
In the second year of Datong, he was recruited as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
Zhang Zan served as the official of selection, and the people who came to his back door were all from humble backgrounds. The upright people were promoted, and they did not change their opinions for the important people. The scholars unanimously praised him.
In the fifth year of Datong, Emperor Gaozu wrote a Shao Shu book and said: Zhang Zuan is the Yinghua of his grandfather's family and the leader of the imperial court. After Sikong Zhang Mian, his reputation is the first in Fan Yang.
You can let him serve as a servant of the minister.
At first, Zhang Zan and his minister He Jingrong were not in harmony. Jingrong was the prime minister and guests gathered. When his guests passed by to visit Zhang Zan, he always refused to come, saying: I can't treat He Jingrong's disabled guests.
When he was transferred this time, he wrote: "Since I have been appointed as a minister to assist the monarch, and have been in charge of selecting talents, I can raise my head and raise my eyebrows to judge right and wrong."
However, he was hindered by his narrow mind and his ears and eyes were blocked. Deep and shallow, clear and muddy, how could he have the ability to intervene.
In addition, it is impossible to prevent him from concealing his feelings, and he does not like to work with extremely restless vulgar people.
This statement refers to captivity.
When Zhang Lian was in office, he proposed that the emperor should be enshrined in a car without decorations in the southern suburbs, which was suitable for ancient and modern times. He also proposed that court uniforms should be prepared for the Yinshou Palace, and that they should all be printed with ribbons, which was implemented at that time.
In the ninth year, he was transferred to the posts of General Xuanhui and Danyang Yin. When he was not appointed, he was appointed as envoy Chijie and governor Yu Guasai. He was the military and fishery governor of the three prefectures. On the way to take office, he wrote "Ode to the Southern Expedition".
Its words say:
The star of the year is in Kunzi, and the time is April. I have an audience with the emperor in the Chengming Hall, and I am about to take office and go to Nanchu.
Suddenly I came to Zhongchuan and looked back, missing my old hometown and stopping in my tracks; the road was long and endless, and there was no one to express my feelings.
summary: Zhang Zan, courtesy name Boxu, was Zhang Mian's third brother, adopted by his uncle Hong Ji. At eleven, he married Princess Fuyang, Emperor Gaozu's fourth daughter, becoming Prince Consort Duwei. At seventeen, he was recruited as a secretary. Standing seven feet four inches tall with handsome features, Gaozu found him remarkable. Zhang Zan was eager to learn, reading his brother's vast collection day and night. As one of four Secretary Langs, he firmly requested not to move positions to read all books in the pavilion. He was later moved to Prince Sheren and then Xima and Zhongsheren, managing records. He was as famous as Wang Xi. In the early Tongren years, Northern Wei's Liu Shanming admired him greatly.
