Zhang Zan was promoted to Taiwei and Minister of Libu Lang, becoming commander and minister at a young age. Pei Ziye praised him as a mouthpiece but regretted his late appointment. In the first year of Datong, he served as official historian of Ningyuan Huarong and managed Langye and Pengcheng counties. He later became Huarong Gongbeizhonglang Changshi and Mu Lanling prefect. In the third year, he entered the court as minister of the branch but resigned when his mother died. After mourning, he became prefect of Wuxing, simplifying administration for the people's convenience. In the second year of Datong, he was recruited as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, promoting upright people without changing for the powerful. In the fifth year, Gaozu praised him as the leader of the imperial court. Zhang Zan had conflicts with He Jingrong, refusing to treat his guests. In office, he proposed suitable ancient and modern reforms for court uniforms. In the ninth year, he was transferred to General Xuanhui and Danyang Yin but was appointed as envoy Chijie and governor Yu Guasai. On his way, he wrote "Ode to the Southern Expedition," reflecting on his journey, governance, and historical reflections. He managed Xiangzhou effectively, increasing household registration by over 100,000 and bringing peace. In the second year of Taiqing, he was recruited as leader and later as governor of multiple regions. He had conflicts with Xiao Shu and Xiao Yu, leading to his arrest and forced shaving as a Taoist priest. He was killed at fifty-one. Emperor Yuan posthumously honored him as Jian Xian Gong. Zhang Zan wrote one hundred volumes of "Hongbao" and twenty volumes of collected works. His son Zhang Wang married Princess Haiyan.

translation:
During the Han Dynasty, Xiao Yuanzao, the Marquis of Xichang in Danyang Yin, was unable to take up his post due to a long illness. He ordered Zhang Wanquan to know about Yin's affairs and move him to the post of Changshi, King of Xuancheng of the Chinese Army.
Not long after he moved to Zhongcheng, the imperial censor, Emperor Gaozu sent Zhang Wan's younger brother, Zhang Xuan, from Zhongshushe, to announce an imperial edict: "The most urgent task in governing the country is that those who implement the laws must be as upright as ropes of ink. There should be no restrictions on promotion or demotion of personnel."
During the Jin and Song dynasties, Zhou Min and Cai Kuo were appointed as Shizhong and Yushi Zhongcheng. Please do not doubt that this is a demotion.
At that time, Xuancheng Palace was very famous, so there was this imperial edict.
In the fourth year of Datong, under the old system of servants, the two posts of servants were of equal rank in the east and west. Zhang Wan's brother Zhang Zan was sent to serve as servant. When the hundred ministers lined up, each brother led the queue and walked quickly to the steps on both sides. This situation was unprecedented in the previous generation and was praised by people at the time.
More than a year later, he was appointed as the internal history of Yuzhang.
When Zhang Wan was in the county, he lectured on the principles of "The Right Statement of the Book of Rites", and there were often hundreds of people listening to the lectures, including nobles, officials, gentry, and scholars taking exams.
In the eighth year of An's reign, Liu Jinggong held Ao Dao hostage, and gathered his comrades to attack the county. Xiao Yue, the internal historian, abandoned the city and fled.
The thieves then invaded Muchen and Luling, conquered the counties and towns, and numbered ten thousand people. They also invaded Xingan County in Yuzhang.
The south has not been accustomed to war for a long time, and the officials and people are afraid and scattered.
Some people advised Zhang Wan to avoid the sharp attack of the thieves, but Zhang Wan did not listen. He still built trenches, set up war preparations, recruited brave people, and received more than ten thousand.
The governor of Xiangdong, King Xiangdong, sent Sima Wang Sengbian to lead his troops to fight against the thieves, and accepted Zhang Wan's command. Within a month, all the thieves were pacified.
Ten years later, he was again appointed as the censor Zhongcheng, and was appointed as the regular attendant of Tongzhi Sanqi.
Zhang Wan once again served as the censor. He was unstoppable and powerful people were afraid of him.
When he was sent, a scholar's hall was opened in the west of the city to gather people who wanted to study. Zhang Wan, his right guard Zhu Yi, and Taifu Qing He Chen passed on the teachings and principles to each other.
In the second year of Taiqing's reign, he was promoted to Zuowei General.
When Hou Jing invaded the capital, Zhang Wan went to guard Shuye Gate.
Three years later, he was moved to the post of Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
When the palace fell, Zhang Wan fled out of the city and turned to Jiangling. King Xiangshu followed the emperor's will and granted Zhang Wan the title of Shizhong, Zuowei General, and Prime Minister. The Shizhong remained as usual.
He served as Chijie, General Yunhui, and Internal History of Eastern Hunan.
In the second year of Chengsheng's reign, he was recruited as Minister Youpushe, and soon he was appointed as Shizhong.
summary: Zhang Wan, courtesy name Xiaoqing, was Zhang Zan's fourth brother. Excelling in shooting as a first-year student, he was recruited as chief and secretary, later moving to Prince Sheren and other roles. He was promoted to Zhongshu Lang and Doctor of Guozi, serving as Lang Changshi of Beizhong and Grand Administrator of Lanling. During the Han Dynasty, he managed Danyang Yin's affairs due to Xiao Yuanzao's illness. He moved to Zhongcheng, where Gaozu praised his legal uprightness. In the fourth year of Datong, he and his brother Zhang Zan served as servants, an unprecedented situation praised by contemporaries. He became internal history of Yuzhang, lecturing on "The Right Statement of the Book of Rites" to hundreds. In the eighth year, when Liu Jinggong held Ao Dao hostage, Zhang Wan ignored advice to flee, built defenses, recruited over 10,000 brave men, and pacified the thieves with Wang Sengbian's help. Ten years later, he again served as censor Zhongcheng, unstoppable and feared by the powerful. He opened a scholar's hall in the city. In the second year of Taiqing, he was promoted to Zuowei General, guarding Shuye Gate during Hou Jing's invasion. Three years later, he became Minister of the Ministry of Personnel. After the palace fell, he fled to Jiangling, where King Xiangshu granted him titles. He served as Chijie and Internal History of Eastern Hunan. In the second year of Chengsheng, he was recruited as Minister Youpushe and later Shizhong. When Jiangling fell, he survived due to illness and died at sixty-three. His son Zhang Jiao married Princess Anyang. Yao Cha commented that during the Taiqing period, Zhang Zan's personal grudges led to discord among kings, contributing to the Liang Dynasty's chaos.

translation:
Wang Mao, whose courtesy name is Xiuyuan, was born in Qi, Taiyuan.
Grandfather Wang Shen, Beizhonglang Sima.
His father was born in Tianjin. He served as a general in the late Song Dynasty. He defeated Situ Yuancan at Shitou. He became an official with military merit and became the prefect of Brazil and Zitong counties. He was a man in Huang County.
When Wang Mao was a few years old, he was valued by his grandfather Wang Shen. He often said to relatives and friends: This child is the horse of my family, and he must be the one who establishes the family.
When he grew up, he liked to read military books and explore the main ideas in them in general and brief terms.
She is calm and reserved by nature, not sociable, eight feet tall, and has a white and beautiful face.
When Emperor Wu of Qi was still a commoner, he sighed when he saw him: "Wang Mao is young and looks so majestic. He will definitely become a talent to assist the emperor."
At the end of the Song Dynasty and the Ming Dynasty, Wang Maoren was appointed from home to serve in the imperial court. He served successively as Houjunxing, Sikong Cavalry, and Taiwei Zhongbing.
Wei general Li Wunu invaded the desert, and Wang Mao was ordered by the emperor to march westward.
After the Wei army retreated, he returned and served as Sima of Zhennan, leading the Linxiang order.
He entered Beijing and served as the captain of the Yue Cavalry School.
When the Wei army invaded Yanzhou, Wang Mao was serving as General Shi of Ningshuo to guard and reinforce the northern border. He was transferred back to serve as the former general of Jiangxia, Wang Sima of Jiangxia.
He was also promoted to General Ningshuo and Internal History of Jiangxia.
In the early years of Jianwu's reign, the Wei army besieged Sizhou, and Wang Mao led the Yingzhou army to rescue him.
Gaozu led his troops to climb Xianshou Mountain first, and Wei generals Wang Su and Liu Chang came to fight. Wang Mao followed Gaozu to resist the enemy and defeated Wang Chong and others' army.
After the Wei army retreated, Wang Mao returned to Yingzhou and served as the chief minister of the auxiliary state and the governor of Xiangyang.
When Emperor Gaozu raised a righteous army, Wang Mao consulted privately with Zhang Hongce and persuaded Emperor Gaozu to welcome Emperor He, but Emperor Gaozu did not agree to do so. These words are recorded in "Gaozu Ji".
Emperor Gaozu sent the Yong army to advance, often sending Wang Mao as the vanguard.
The army was temporarily stationed in Yingcheng. Wang Mao attacked and pacified Jiahu, defeated Guangzijin, Wu Ziyang and others, beheaded and cut off the ears of tens of thousands of people, and returned to Hanchuan to report his victory.
After Ying and Lu were pacified, he followed the emperor's troops and became the vanguard of the army.
The army was stationed in Moling. Shuhunhou sent General Wang Zhenguo to assemble the army at Zhuque Gate. The number of soldiers was said to be 200,000, and they crossed the sea to fight.
Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong and others went to attack together and defeated the enemy.
The army was allowed to pursue the fleeing enemies, and the corpses of the enemy soldiers were piled up to the height of the fence. Those who died by jumping into the Huai River were incalculable.
Chase them all the way to Xuanyang Gate.
After Jiankang City was pacified, Wang Mao was appointed as the general guarding the army, and was soon promoted to the rank of Shizhong and leading general.
The thieves set fire to Shenhu Gate. Wang Mao led his army to Dongye Gate to respond to the rescue. The thieves fired arrows at them. Wang Mao whipped his horse and advanced, while the thieves fled back.
Wang Mao believed that he had failed to control the traitors, so he petitioned to be relieved of his duties, but the emperor's generous Shao Ling did not agree.
He was also given the title of general of the town army, and was granted the title of Duke of Wangcai County, with a settlement of 2,300 households.
In the first year of the Han Dynasty, Chen Bozhi, the governor of Jiangzhou, rebelled. Wang Mao was appointed as envoy Chijie, regular servant of Sanqi, governor of Jiangzhou's military affairs, general in the southern expedition, and governor of Jiangzhou. He was given a set of drums and drums and went to conquer Chen Bozhi in the south.
Bozhi defected to Wei.
At that time, Jiujiang had just suffered from military turmoil, and the people wanted to return to farming. Wang Mao focused on farming to reduce civil service, so the people were content with agricultural production.
In the fourth year, Wei invaded Mozhong again. Wang Mao was ordered by Emperor Shao to march westward, and Wei retreated.
In the sixth year, he was promoted to the right servant of Shangshu, and he still served as a regular attendant.
However, he refused to resign and took up the post, so he was appointed as a minister in charge and a general in charge of the Central Guards, leading Prince Zhan to serve.
In the seventh year, he was appointed as a general of chariots and cavalry, and he was still appointed as Prince Zhan Shi.
In the eighth year, he took his title as Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Danyang Yin, and continued to write poems.
At that time, the world was peaceful and Emperor Gaozu was trusting gentle people. Wang Mao was in a bad mood. After drinking and drinking with the emperor, it often showed in his words and expressions. Emperor Gaozu often forgave him but did not blame him.
In the eleventh year, he was promoted to Sikong, but the positions of Shizhong and Yin remained the same.
Wang Mao resigned from Beijing and became General Zhongquan.
Wang Mao has a generous temperament. Although he does not have a great reputation as an official, he still manages to calm down the lower-level officials and the people.
summary: Wang Mao, courtesy name Xiuyuan, was born in Qi, Taiyuan. His grandfather Wang Shen served as Beizhonglang Sima, and his father served as a general in the late Song Dynasty, defeating Situ Yuancan at Shitou and becoming prefect of Brazil and Zitong counties. As a child, Wang Mao was valued by his grandfather, who predicted he would establish the family. He grew to eight feet tall with a white and beautiful face, calm and reserved by nature, and fond of military books. During the late Song and Ming Dynasties, Wang Mao served in various military positions. When Wei general Li Wunu invaded, Wang Mao marched westward. After the Wei army retreated, he served as Sima of Zhennan and later as Yue Cavalry School captain. When Wei invaded Yanzhou, he served as General Shi of Ningshuo. In the early Jianwu years, he rescued Sizhou from Wei siege and followed Gaozu to defeat Wei generals. After the Wei retreat, he became chief minister of the auxiliary state and governor of Xiangyang. When Emperor Gaozu raised a righteous army, Wang Mao consulted with Zhang Hongce about welcoming Emperor He, but Gaozu disagreed. Wang Mao served as vanguard, pacifying Jiahu and defeating Guangzijin and Wu Ziyang, beheading tens of thousands. After Jiankang City was pacified, he became general guarding the army, then Shizhong and leading general. He was granted the title of Duke of Wangcai County with 2,300 households. In the first year of the Han Dynasty, he conquered the rebellious Chen Bozhi. He later served as right servant of Shangshu, general of chariots and cavalry, and Kaifu Yitong Sansi. He died at sixty, receiving posthumous honors and the title Zhonglie.

translation:
When he was just twenty years old, Cao Xinzhi sent Cao Jingzong out of the state to handle affairs in Xinye. He was alone and had only a few followers. On the way, he was unexpectedly surrounded by hundreds of barbarians.
Cao Jingzong brought more than a hundred arrows and galloped around to shoot arrows in all directions. Every time he fired an arrow, he killed a barbarian. The barbarians fled in all directions, so he gained fame for his courage and courage.
He loved reading history books. Every time he read "Rang Ju" and "The Biography of Le Yi", he put down the book and exclaimed: A man should be such a person!
He was recruited to serve as an official in Xicao, but he did not accept the appointment.
During the reign of Emperor Yuanhui of the Song Dynasty, he left the state with his father and went to the capital to Jiankang. He served as Feng Chao, Yuan Wai Lang, and was transferred to Shangshu Zuo Minlang.
Soon after his father passed away, he left his job and returned to his hometown.
After the mourning period expired, the governor Xiao Chiaxu appointed him as a champion soldier to join the army and concurrently as the prefect of Tianshui.
In the early years of the founding of the Southern Qi Dynasty, the barbarians gathered in crowds to riot. Cao Jingzong marched east and west, capturing thieves and defeating the enemy many times during the battle.
Xiao Qiang, the king of Poyang in the Qi Dynasty, served as the governor of Yongzhou, and he was also used as a conscript soldier to join the army. He also served as the prefect of Feng Yi, supervising the military affairs in Xiannan, and was appointed as the captain of the garrison and cavalry school.
When he was young, he had a close friendship with fellow countryman Zhang Daomen.
Zhang Daomen was the youngest son of Zhang Jing'er, the Southern Qi cavalry general, and served as the prefect of Wuling.
Zhang Jing'er was killed, and Zhang Daomen was also implicated and executed in the county. His relatives and old officials did not dare to come to collect the body. Cao Jingzong sent people and ships from Xiangyang to Wuling to collect Zhang Daomen's body and bring it back for burial. The people in the village thought that Cao Jingzong was loyal.
In the second year of Jianwu reign of Emperor Ming of the Southern Qi Dynasty, Tuoba Hong, the leader of the Northern Wei Dynasty, attacked Zheyang, and Cao Jingzong was appointed as a partial general. Every time he attacked a strong enemy and captured the enemy's formation, he always killed someone and captured him. Because of his meritorious service, he was awarded the rank of guerrilla general.
In the fourth year, Taiwei Chen Xianda led the troops north to besiege Maquan. Cao Jingzong accompanied the army and led 2,000 soldiers to set up an ambush and defeated the 40,000 reinforcements led by Tuoba Ying of the Northern Wei Dynasty.
After conquering the horse circle, Chen Xianda rewarded Cao Jingzong for his merits and ranked him last. Cao Jingzong retreated without any complaints.
The leader of the Northern Wei Dynasty led an army to attack again. Chen Xianda escaped at night. Cao Jingzong guided him into the mountain road, so Chen Xianda and his son were able to escape safely.
In the fifth year, Xiao Yan, Emperor Wu of Liang Dynasty, became the governor of Yongzhou. Cao Jingzong became deeply friends with him and invited him to his home many times.
At that time, the world was in turmoil, and Emperor Wu of Liang also wanted to pay attention to Cao Jingzong.
In the early years of the Yongyuan reign of Donghun Hou of the Southern Qi Dynasty, Emperor Wu of Liang asked Cao Jingzong to be appointed as the champion general and the prefect of Jingling.
summary: Cao Jingzong, courtesy name Zizhen, was a new savage. His father Cao Xinzhi was a military general in the Song Dynasty. Young Cao Jingzong excelled at horseback archery and hunting. At twenty, while traveling alone with few followers, he was surrounded by hundreds of barbarians but fought them off with arrows, gaining fame for courage. He loved reading history books, particularly admiring Rang Ju and Le Yi. During the Southern Qi Dynasty, Cao Jingzong served as prefect of Tianshui and fought against barbarian uprisings. He showed loyalty by retrieving the body of his friend Zhang Daomen after Zhang's father was killed. In the Jianwu years, he fought against Northern Wei invasions, defeating Tuoba Ying's 40,000 reinforcements with 2,000 ambush soldiers. He became close friends with Xiao Yan (Emperor Wu of Liang) when Xiao served as governor of Yongzhou.

translation:
When Emperor Wu of Liang raised his troops to the east, Cao Jingzong gathered his troops and sent his confidant Du Sichong to persuade Emperor Wu of Liang to first welcome Xiao Wei, King of Nankang, to ascend the throne in Xiangyang, and then send troops. This was a sound strategy.
Emperor Wu of Liang did not adopt this opinion, and the matter was recorded in "Gaozu Ji".
Emperor Wu of Liang led his troops to Jingling and sent Cao Jingzong and champion general Wang Mao across the Yangtze River to besiege Yingcheng. From February to July, the Yingcheng defenders surrendered.
He also led the troops as the vanguard to advance to Nanzhou, and led the horse infantry to advance towards Jiankang.
On the way, the army was stationed in Jiangning. Donghun Hou's general Li Jushi led a heavy army and was stationed in Xinting. On this day, a thousand elite cavalry were selected to temporarily station in Jiangning. Cao Jingzong's troops had just arrived and the fortress had not yet been built. Moreover, the troops had been marching for a long time, and their weapons and armor were damaged and leaked. Seeing the situation of Cao Jingzong's troops, Li Jushi underestimated the enemy's carelessness, so he took advantage of the situation and beat the drums and shouted to attack Cao Jingzong.
Cao Jingzong put on his armor and mounted his horse to fight. As soon as they engaged, Li Jingzong abandoned his armor and fled. Cao Jingzong captured all Li Jingshi's soldiers and horses, and took advantage of the victory to chase the enemy with drums. They advanced to Zaoying Bridge and built a fortress. Cao Jingzong, Wang Mao and Lu Sengzhen divided their forces to attack together, and defeated Wang Guozhen at Dahang.
Wang Mao attacked Wang Guozhen's main force and immediately overwhelmed the enemy formation. Cao Jingzong took advantage of the situation and launched an attack.
The sergeants in Cao Jingzong's army were all fierce and cunning scoundrels, and the residents on both sides of the imperial street were all from wealthy families. The sergeants robbed property and plundered their children, and Cao Jingzong could not stop them.
When Emperor Wu of Liang entered the new city and solemnly declared military discipline, the plundering incidents subsided slightly.
Cao Jingzong and other military commanders besieged the six gates.
After the city was broken, he was appointed as a regular servant of the scattered cavalry and a general of the right guard. He was granted the title of Marquis of Xiangxi County and was granted the title of 1,600 households.
So he moved to Chijie, the governor of Ying, the military commander of the two states, the general of Zuo, and the governor of Ying state.
In the first year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu of Liang Dynasty, he was promoted to General Pingxi and changed to Marquis of Jingling County.
Cao Jingzong was in Yingzhou, buying and selling goods to accumulate money, and built residences in the south of the city. He opened streets from the east of the Changdi to the north of Xiakou, several miles long from east to west, and the people were extremely disgusted by the brutality of his troops.
In October of the second year of Tianjian, the Northern Wei Dynasty invaded Sizhou and surrounded Cai Daogong, the governor.
At that time, the offensive of the Northern Wei Dynasty was becoming more and more serious day by day. People in the city had to carry door panels on their backs to guard against arrows to collect water. However, Cao Jingzong sat at home and watched without sending troops to rescue. He only went out to hunt in a show of force.
After Sizhou City was captured, Cao Jingzong was impeached by the Japanese imperial censor Zhongcheng. Because Cao Jingzong was a hero, Emperor Wu suppressed the matter and did not sanction it. Instead, he recalled Cao Jingzong to serve as a guard.
After Cao Jingzong arrived in Beijing, he was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi and a general of right guard.
In the fifth year, Tuoba Ying of the Northern Wei Dynasty invaded Zhongli and besieged Chang Yizhi, the governor of Xuzhou. Emperor Wu issued an edict and ordered Cao Jingzong to lead the army to rescue Chang Yizhi. Wei Rui, the governor of Yuzhou, also participated in this military operation and was controlled by Cao Jingzong.
The imperial edict ordered Cao Jingzong to station himself at Daoren Island and wait for all the armies to gather before marching together.
Cao Jingzong repeatedly requested that his troops be allowed to occupy the end of Shaoyang Island first, but Emperor Wu refused.
Cao Jingzong planned to win this battle alone, so he defied the imperial edict and marched forward. A sudden storm blew up, and many soldiers fell into the water and drowned. He had no choice but to return to defend the previous station.
After Emperor Gaozu learned about the news, he said: This is the condition for being able to defeat the thief. Cao Jingzong cannot move forward. It turns out to be God's arrangement!
If Cao Jingzong went alone and the fortress could not be built in time, he would definitely suffer an embarrassing defeat.
summary: When Emperor Wu raised troops, Cao Jingzong gathered his forces and served as vanguard, besieging Yingcheng for months until surrender. He advanced toward Jiankang, defeating Li Jushi at Jiangning despite his troops' worn equipment. After the city fell, he was made Marquis of Xiangxi County with 1,600 households. In the Tianjian years, he was promoted to General Pingxi and Marquis of Jingling County. During the Northern Wei invasion of Sizhou, he was impeached for not sending timely rescue but was protected by Emperor Wu.

translation:
Now we can wait for all the armies to advance at the same time, so that we can achieve a complete victory.
When Wei Rui arrived, he and Cao Jingzong advanced to station troops in Shaoyangzhou and built a fortress more than a hundred steps away from Wei City.
The Wei army fought one after another and was unable to repel the Southern army. Two or three-tenths of the people were killed and wounded. From then on, the Wei army did not dare to approach the Southern army to fight.
The weapons and armor of Cao Jingzong and other parts of the army were exquisite and beautiful, and their military appearance was grand. The Wei army was discouraged when they saw it.
Yang Dayan, the general of Wei, built a city on the north bank facing the bridge to make the road for transporting grain smooth. Whenever herdsmen from the south came across the bank to gather livestock, they were all captured by Yang Dayan.
Cao Jingzong then recruited more than a thousand brave soldiers and crossed the river to build a fortress a few miles south of Yang Dayan City. Cao Jingzong personally built and rammed it.
Yang Dayan led his troops to attack, and Cao Jingzong fought and defeated him, so he was able to build a fortress.
Cao Jingzong sent general Zhao Cao to guard the new base, so he called this military base Zhao Cao City. From then on, herders could graze their cattle here at will.
Yang Dayan sent troops to plunder from time to time, but was often captured by Zhao Cao.
Prior to this, Emperor Wu had ordered Cao Jingzong and others to build tall warships in advance, so that the tall buildings on the ship would be as high as the bridge, in order to implement the fire attack plan.
Order Cao Jingzong and Wei Rui to attack an enemy bridge each, Wei Rui to attack the Wei army's south bridge, and Cao Jingzong to attack the north bridge.
In March of the sixth year, the spring water rose, and the water in the Huaihe River surged six or seven feet high.
Wei Rui sent generals Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji and others under his command to land on warships, attack the Northern Wei garrison on the shore and annihilate them all.
Cao Jingzong took the opportunity to order all the troops to beat drums and shout together. In the chaos, they boarded the Wei army's camp. The sound of killing shook the world. Yang Dayan burned the camp on the west bank, and Tuoba Ying abandoned the city on the east bank and fled.
The various camps of the Wei army collapsed one after another, and they all abandoned their weapons and armor and jumped into the river to drown. The Huai River was blocked and could not flow.
Cao Jingzong ordered the army commander Ma Guang to follow Yang Dayan to the shore of Xuisui River. During the more than 40 miles of the road, the corpses of the fallen enemies were piled on top of each other.
Chang Yizhi sent troops to pursue Tuobaying to Luokou, but Tuobaying fled into Liangcheng alone.
Along the Huaihe River for more than a hundred miles, there were piles of dead bodies everywhere, more than 50,000 Wei soldiers were captured alive, and the food and equipment of the Wei army were seized, which were piled up like mountains, including countless cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules.
Cao Jingzong then collected more than 10,000 prisoners alive and thousands of horses, and sent people to escort them to the capital to offer victory. Emperor Gaozu issued an edict and ordered Cao Jingzong to return to his own army. Cao Jingzong's troops lined up in victory and returned to the court. They were granted an additional 400 households. Together with the previous grants, the total was 2,000 households. They were promoted to Dukes.
The imperial edict ordered the officials to be worshiped as ministers and leading generals, and an agitating band was given to them.
Cao Jingzong was a self-reliant man who relied on his merits and success. Every time he wrote a letter, he would not ask others if there were words he could not write, but would write them according to his own imagination.
Even when dealing with high-ranking officials, he was never polite and modest; only Wei Rui was older than him and was a famous figure in the same state. Cao Jingzong showed great respect to him and attended the imperial banquet with him. Cao Jingzong was also polite and humble, and Emperor Wu praised him for it.
Cao Jingzong was a womanizer. He had hundreds of singing prostitutes, wives and concubines at home, all of whom were dressed in extremely luxurious brocade.
summary: In the fifth year, when Tuoba Ying invaded Zhongli, Cao Jingzong led rescue forces. Despite imperial orders to wait, he attempted to advance alone but was turned back by storms. He eventually joined Wei Rui at Shaoyangzhou, building fortresses near Wei positions. In the sixth year, during spring floods, they launched a coordinated attack, burning Wei camps and causing massive casualties. Over 50,000 Wei soldiers were captured alive, with countless supplies seized. Cao Jingzong was promoted to Duke with 2,000 households.

translation:
He has an impatient and restless personality and cannot be silent. Whenever he goes out, he always wants to pick up the curtains on the car and look out. People around him always use his status and prestige to advise him, saying that it is inappropriate for everyone to see him.
Cao Jingzong said to those close to him: I used to ride a fast horse like a dragon in the countryside. I would join dozens of riders with my young friends. The bow strings would make a sound like thunder, and the sharp arrows would scream like a hungry eagle.
Chase the deer in the plains and swamps, count its ribs and shoot at it. Drink its blood when you are thirsty and eat its meat when you are hungry. The taste is as sweet as nectar.
I just feel the wind behind my ears and the fire in my nose. Such happiness makes people not aware that they will die, let alone that old age will come.
Now that I have come to Yangzhou and become a nobleman, I cannot move freely. When I open the car curtain while walking on the road, the villain will say no.
Sitting in the car suffocating, she was like a new daughter-in-law who was not allowed to see anyone for three days.
It's frustrating to be depressed like this.
Cao Jingzong was fond of drinking and having fun. During the twelfth lunar month, he had people shouting in his house to drive away diseases and ghosts, and he also went to all the houses to beg for food and wine.
Originally he did this for fun, but most of his subordinates were tough and frivolous, so they took the opportunity to tease other people's women and rob other people's treasures.
Emperor Wu was very aware of these situations, and Cao Jingzong stopped having fun after learning about it.
Emperor Gaozu held many banquets to meet with heroes and talk about their old friendships. When Cao Jingzong was drunk, he would always tell lies, or sometimes mistakenly call himself a subordinate to the emperor. Emperor Gaozu also deliberately let him do this to make fun of him.
In the seventh year, Cao Jingzong was transferred to Shizhong, General of Zhongwei, and Governor of Jiangzhou.
He died on the road when he went to take office at the age of fifty-two.
The emperor issued an edict granting him funeral money of 200,000 yuan and 300 bolts of cloth. He was also given the posthumous title of General Zhengbei, Yongzhou Governor, and Kaifu Yitong. His posthumous title was Zhuang.
Cao Jiao, Cao Jingzong's son, succeeded his father's title.
Liu Qingyuan was named Wenhe and was born in Hedong Jie.
Uncle Yuan Jing was a Taiwei of the Song Dynasty.
Qingyuan was appointed from home as the chief administrator of Yingzhou. In the early years of Qi, he was appointed as Shangshu Duguanlang, Da Sima Zhongbing joined the army, General Jianwu, and Prefect of Wei Xing.
The county suffered a flood and the residents were washed away by drifting water. The lower-level officials requested that the people be moved to the city to offer sacrifices.
Qingyuan said: How can the city predict the rainfall from the sky?
I heard that the rivers will only rise for three days, so there is nothing to worry about.
He merely orders the earth to be pounded to make it solid.
Soon the flood passed and the people admired him.
He went to Beijing and served as the captain of Changshui School, and also served as Pingbei Green Affairs Joining the Army and Xiangyang Order.
Emperor Gaozu went to Yongzhou and asked Du Zang, a native of Jingzhao, about finding an official who could serve as the head of the state. Du Zan recommended Qingyuan.
summary: Cao Jingzong was self-reliant and proud, showing respect only to Wei Rui. He was a womanizer with hundreds of concubines, impatient and restless, fond of drinking and hunting. He died at fifty-two while traveling to assume the governorship of Jiangzhou.

translation:
Emperor Gaozu said: Wen He and I already know him, but I am asking about other people whom I don't know well.
So he was recruited to work as a historian.
At this time, Qi Zheng was in a lot of trouble. Qingyuan said to those close to him: If the world is going to be in chaos, heroes will definitely rise. The person who protects the people and establishes hegemony is probably our monarch, right?
Therefore, he tried his best to assist Gaozu loyally.
When Gaozu's rebellion rose, Qingyuan often strategized and became the mastermind.
In the first year of the Zhongxing Dynasty, Xi Tai selected him as Huang Menlang and was promoted to champion general and a long history of the Eastern Campaign.
He followed the army eastward and took the lead in fighting.
When Emperor Gaozu was walking among the forts and saw the neat buildings where he stayed in Qingyuan, he often sighed and said: If everyone is like him, what do I have to worry about?
After the city of Jiankang was pacified, he went to Beijing and served as a minister, leading the general of the front army and the prefect of Huailing and Qichang counties.
There was a fire in the city at night, and the palace was panicked. At that time, Gaozu was living in the palace, collected all the keys, and asked everyone where Liu Shizhong was. When Qingyuan came, he handed all the keys to him.
This is how he was trusted by Emperor Gaozu.
After the establishment of Gaozu's Bafu, he was appointed as Taiwei and Zhonglang.
Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication and ascended the throne. He was promoted to the rank of regular attendant of Sanqi, general of right guard, general of conquering captives, and the title of Marquis of Chong'an, with a land of 1,000 households.
He resigned due to the death of his mother. Later, he was appointed to his original official position, but he insisted on refusing to take office.
In the second year of Tianjian, he was promoted to the leader of the Central Military Commission and changed his title to Yun Duhou.
In four years, he served as the envoy Chijie, the governor of the military affairs of the four states of Liang, Southern and Northern Qin, the general who conquered the captives, the captain of Ningman, and the governor of Yongzhou.
Emperor Gaozu held a banquet in the new pavilion to see him off, and said to him: "You have returned home in fine clothes, and I no longer have the worries of looking westward."
In the seventh year, he was recruited as a general to protect the army and led the prince's concubine.
He did not take up any post, but was promoted to the rank of regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi, general of Youwei, and general of Xiaoqi of the right.
When he arrived in Kyoto, it was when Wei Su asked for surrender in advance of the city. He was ordered by the emperor to provide assistance, so he guarded Huaiyin with integrity.
The Wei army retreated.
In the eighth year, he returned to Kyoto and was promoted to Sanqi Changshi, Prince Zhanshi, and Yongzhou Dazhongzheng.
In ten years, he was promoted to the rank of servant and general, and was given support and a set of drums and instruments.
In the twelfth year, he was promoted to general Anbei, captain of Ningman, and governor of Yongzhou.
Qingyuan served in Honshu again. He further improved his integrity and the hearts of scholars and common people all attached to him.
He died in the spring of the next year at the age of fifty-seven.
The imperial edict stated: "Remembering those who were loyal until the end of their lives is a legal system that existed during the time of the previous kings; it is a common practice for emperors to ceremoniously treat their subordinates with courteous treatment in all dynasties."
Envoy Chijie, the commander-in-chief of the four prefectures of Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, as well as the military forces of Jingling in Yingzhou and Suijun in Sizhou, general Anbei, captain of Ningman, governor of Yongzhou, and Liu Qingyuan, the founder of Yundu County, are profound and knowledgeable, and their thoughts are smooth and elegant.
From the earliest days of creation, he has participated in and followed the planning and management of national affairs; as far back as the peace of the world, he has worked hard in forbidden travel.
summary: Liu Qingyuan, named Wenhe, was born in Hedong Jie. He served as chief administrator of Yingzhou and prefect of Wei Xing, where he handled a flood wisely. Emperor Gaozu recruited him as a historian, and Qingyuan became a loyal strategist during Gaozu's rebellion. After Jiankang was pacified, he served as minister and was deeply trusted by Gaozu, who entrusted him with palace keys during a fire. After Gaozu ascended the throne, Qingyuan became Marquis of Chong'an with 1,000 households. He served as governor of Yongzhou, where Emperor Gaozu praised him for eliminating western concerns. He later returned to Kyoto and served in various high positions. He died at fifty-seven while serving as governor of Yongzhou again, receiving posthumous honors and the title Zhonghui.

translation:
Now that I have returned to rule Xifan, I was just about to carry forward my political ideas, but suddenly passed away, which makes me extremely sad.
An honorable appointment should be added to him in recognition of his great merits.
He can be posthumously granted the titles of Shizhong, General of the Central Army, and the Third Division of Kaifu Yitong. The rituals of Drum Music and Marquis are the same as those originally conferred.
The nickname is Zhonghui.
Two hundred thousand coins and two hundred pieces of cloth were given for the funeral.
After the body of the deceased was transported back to Kyoto, Gao Zu came out of the palace to mourn.
His son Liu Jin succeeded him.
At the beginning, Qingyuan's cousin, General Wei Shilong, once said to Qingyuan: I once dreamed that the Taiwei gave me a mattress, and my status was second only to that of Taisi. Later, I happened to dream of giving my mattress to you. It seems that you will definitely honor your ancestors.
By this time, Qingyuan had inherited the honor held by Shilong.
Yao Cha, Chen's official minister, said: Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong: Although Liu Qingyuan has been a military leader for generations, they have not shown outstanding integrity.
When the Liang Dynasty rose, they relied on the last light of the sun and the moon to realize their personal ambitions. Pei left relics in Fang, Shao and other places, and recorded their achievements on bells and tripods. How great!
In the past, Emperor Guangwu of the Han Dynasty protected and cared for meritorious officials, but only awarded official positions such as court invitations and special promotions. Kou, Deng, Geng, and Mai could not fully display their talents.
However, Wang Mao and others were able to take turns serving as local governors, and their official positions were finally generals. The relationship between the monarch and his ministers was better than that of the previous generation.
summary: Yao Cha commented that Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and Liu Qingyuan, though military leaders, achieved great success during the Liang Dynasty's rise, with their accomplishments recorded on bells and tripods. Unlike Emperor Guangwu of Han who limited his officials, these men were able to serve as local governors and reach high military positions, demonstrating superior monarch-minister relations.

translation:
Liu Ji, whose alias is Huixu, is from Pengcheng.
His father, Liu Sisi, became prominent in the Song Dynasty because he was a younger brother of Emperor Gaozu of the Song Dynasty, reaching the rank of Jin Ziguanglu. Liu Jilian had a very good reputation and had served as an upright official very early on.
After Emperor Qi Gao accepted the abdication and ascended the throne of the emperor, he killed all the close relatives of the Song Dynasty. When he was about to kill Liu Jilian and others, Ji Lian was saved from death because the Grand Prime Minister Chu Yuan had always been very good with Zhilian. With his firm plea, Ji Lian was saved.
During the Jianyuan period, Liu Ji was re-elected as Minister Zuocheng.
In the early years of the Yongming Dynasty, Liu Weilian served as the internal history of Jiangxia County, and was promoted many times to the internal history of Pingnan Changsha County, the champion chief historian, the prefect of Guangling County, and was in charge of the affairs of the prefecture.
Later, he was called to serve as the minister of Huangmen, and was transferred to the prince's concubine.
During the Jianwu period, Liu Jilian served as the long history of Xiao Yaoxin in Pingxi and the prefect of Lu Su.
At that time, Dancha's sons were still young, so the relatives relied on the brothers Xiao Yaoxin, and the relatives relied on the queen's younger brother Liu Xuan and brother-in-law Jiang Zhe.
When Xiao Yaoxin was guarding Jiangling, Emperor Ming had great hopes for him; however, when Yaoxin arrived in Zhoubao, he invited guests and privately gave him large rewards, which Emperor Ming was very disgusted with.
Liu Erlian's nephew, Ji Xing Artificial Hehe, was consulted by Luwei to join the army. Wanghe was handsome, talented and eloquent, and Luwei valued him very much.
Wang Hui was so arrogant that he even argued with Xiao Yaoxin to insult Liu Jilian in front of everyone. Liu Jilian was very unhappy about this. He secretly reported to Emperor Ming that Xiao Yaoxin had abnormal signs. Emperor Ming accepted his opinion and appointed Xiao Yaoxin as the governor of Yongzhou.
Emperor Ming was deeply grateful to Ji Lian. Four years later, he appointed Liu Jilian as an auxiliary general and the governor of Yizhou, and ordered him to guard the upper reaches of Xiao Yaoxin.
When Liu Jilian's father was the governor of Dong in Saiqu, he was greedy and despicable and had no political achievements. However, the people of Yizhou still valued justice and treated Jilian very well.
After Liu Jilian got off the bus and took office, he expressed condolences to old and old officials, comforted and made new and old friends. When he saw his father's old officials, they all shed tears in front of them.
Liu Jilian appointed Gong Sui, a native of Suining, as the chief administrator of the prefecture.
Gong Rui is the grandson of Gong Ying. His family has been educated and virtuous for generations, so he was recommended to be an official.
When Donghunhou came to the throne, in the first year of Yongyuan, Liu Jilian was recruited as the right guard general, but he did not take office because of the road blockage.
Liu Jilian heard that Marquis Shuhun had lost his moral character and that there were many changes in the capital, so he became proud and reserved.
Liu Jilian was originally known as a civil servant with a jealous and intolerant temperament. Now he has become more cruel, cruel and self-willed. The local people began to feel resentment and disappointment towards him.
In September of the first year of the Han Dynasty, Liu Jilian gathered five thousand people, claiming to be practicing martial arts, but in fact he sent Chinese soldiers to join the army. Song Mai led these people to attack Zhongshui.
summary: Liu Ji, also known as Huixu, was from Pengcheng. His father, Liu Sisi, rose to prominence in the Song Dynasty as a younger brother of Emperor Gaozu, reaching the rank of Jin Ziguanglu. Liu Ji had a strong reputation and served as an upright official early on. After Emperor Qi Gao ascended the throne, he killed many Song relatives, but Liu Ji was spared due to the intervention of Grand Prime Minister Chu Yuan. During the Jianyuan period, Liu Ji became Minister Zuocheng. In the Yongming era, he held various posts, including internal history of Jiangxia and Guangling counties. Later, he served as Huangmen minister and prince's concubine. During the Jianwu period, he was long history of Xiao Yaoxin and prefect of Lu Su. Liu Ji's nephew, Ji Xing, was handsome and eloquent, valued by Luwei, but his arrogance led to conflict with Xiao Yaoxin. Liu Ji secretly reported Xiao Yaoxin to Emperor Ming, who then appointed Xiao Yaoxin as governor of Yongzhou. Grateful, Emperor Ming made Liu Ji auxiliary general and governor of Yizhou. Liu Ji's father had been a greedy governor in Yizhou, but the people treated Liu Ji well. Upon taking office, Liu Ji comforted old officials and wept with them. He appointed Gong Sui as chief administrator.

translation:
Li Tuo, a native of Zhenxian County, knew about this in advance and deployed defensive forces to guard the dangerous places. The battle between Songmai and Li Tuo was unfavorable. When they returned to the state, many counties and counties rebelled.
In the same month, Pang Xubo, a native of Xincheng, killed the county magistrate of Wucheng and drove away the prefect of Shiping County.
In October, Le Shichun and Li Nandang, who were natives of the Jin Dynasty, killed the governor of their county. Le Shichun named himself the governor of Nan Qinzhou and Li Nandang the governor of Yizhou.
In December, Liu Jilian sent Cui Maozu, who joined the army, to lead 2,000 soldiers to conquer, bringing only three days of food.
It was the coldest season of the year. A group of thieves gathered together to cut down trees and block the roads. The soldiers were unable to get water and fire to quench their thirst and keep out the cold. As a result, they returned in a great defeat, with seven to eight tenths of them dead.
In the first month of the second year, Bo Yang, a native of Xincheng, expelled Qiao Xiyuan, the prefect of Suining County.
In March, Yong Daoxi, a native of Brazil County, led a group of more than 10,000 thieves to invade Brazil County. They were still several miles away from the county. Yong Daoxi claimed to be General Zhenxi and was given the title Jianyi.
Lu Xiulie, the governor of Brazil County, and Kui Lu, the magistrate of Qianxian County, surrounded the city to defend themselves. Liu Chuilian sent Chinese soldiers to join the army, Li Fengbo, and led 5,000 soldiers to rescue.
After Kui Guibo arrived, he and the soldiers from the county defeated and captured Yong Daoxi alive, and beheaded Daoxi in the market of Fujian County.
Taking advantage of the victory, Li Fengbo wanted to go alone to Shuxiang in Bayou Valley to pursue the remaining thieves.
Kui Ying dissuaded him and said: Now the soldiers are slack and the generals are arrogant. It is not a good strategy to take advantage of victory and go into danger.
It's better to slow down for a while and think of other ways.
Li Fengbo did not take his advice and led all the army into the mountains. As a result, they were defeated and fled back to Zhouxiang.
In June, Cheng Yanyan, a native of Jiangyang, rebelled and killed the prefect He Fazang.
Lu Baolie was afraid that he would not be able to protect himself, so he went to Basu County Prime Minister Xiao Huixun.
In October, Zhao Xubo, a native of Brazil County, rebelled again. With 20,000 people, he set out from Guanglian, took a Buddhist chariot, wrapped blue stones with colorful cloth, and deceived the people, saying: God has given me the jade seal, and I should be the king of Shu.
Many people foolishly followed him.
Liu Jilian marched against Zhao Xubo and others, and sent Chief Shi Zhao Yuetang as the vanguard.
After being defeated, Liu Chonglian sent Li Fengbo to attack from Fu County.
Another army of Li Fengbo joined the army from Shihuang in front of the city and attacked Zhao Xubo's camp gate, resulting in a major defeat of the Zhao army.
At that time, there was a man named Shi Wen'an from Kuaiji who lived in seclusion in the countryside and practiced courtesy. He was re-elected as Shangshu Zuocheng instead of Liu Ji and served as the internal history of Jiangxia County. He was also called to serve as Yushi Zhongcheng instead of Ji Lian. He and Ji Lian were very close.
summary: In the first year of Yongyuan, Liu Ji was recruited as right guard general but did not take office due to road blockages. Hearing of Marquis Shuhun's moral decay, Liu Ji became proud and cruel, causing local resentment. In September, he gathered 5,000 men, claiming to practice martial arts, but sent them to attack Zhongshui. The battle was unfavorable, and many counties rebelled. In October, Le Shichun and Li Nandang killed their governor, with Le Shichun naming himself governor of Nan Qinzhou and Li Nandang governor of Yizhou. In December, Liu Ji sent Cui Maozu with 2,000 soldiers, but they were defeated due to cold and blocked roads, with seven to eight tenths dead. In the second year, further rebellions occurred. Yong Daoxi led 10,000 thieves to invade Brazil County, but was captured and beheaded by Lu Xiulie and Kui Lu. Li Fengbo pursued remaining thieves against advice and was defeated. In June, Cheng Yanyan rebelled and killed the prefect. In October, Zhao Xubo rebelled with 20,000 people, claiming divine mandate. Liu Ji defeated him with Zhao Yuetang and Li Fengbo. Later, Liu Ji's son, Liu Zhongse, responded to the Zhidan uprising.

translation:
Liu Jilian's son was named Liu Zhongse, also named Fuli. When he heard about the Zhidan uprising, he led his fellow villagers to respond to Zhidan.
In the early years, Liu Jian took the title of worship official as Shu Miao Farewell, and followed Gaozu to pacify the capital.
In the spring of the next year, the emperor sent his right-hand man Chen Jiansun to escort Liu Jilian's younger brother, Tongzhilangxing Wang Zhao, and Zhilian's two sons to Dan Deng as envoys, announcing the emperor's intention to express his condolences.
After receiving the order, Liu Jilian packed his bags and prepared to return home.
Emperor Gaozu appointed Xitai general Deng Yuanqi as the governor of Yiye.
Deng Wujie was from Luxuan.
When Liu Chonglian was an official at Zhi Deng, he always treated Jian Wuqi very badly.
Zhu Daochen, the signature officer, once met Liu Jilian in Dulu, the capital of the state. He was a scoundrel. Liu Jilian wanted to kill him because he was guilty, but he escaped and escaped death.
Now he advised Deng Wu tomb: "The situation in Yiye has been in chaos for a long time. The losses in public and private treasuries must be great. How can Liu Yizhou transport supplies over a long distance when he comes to an empty city."
Daochen asked me to check first and welcome him along the way; otherwise, it would not be easy to get the supplies transported thousands of miles away.
Deng Yuanqi agreed to his request.
When Sai Dao arrived at Yiye, his words were very disrespectful. He went to the houses of officials in various prefectures one by one and snatched away utensils and property whenever he saw them. When he met someone who refused to give it to him, he said: "Sooner or later, things will belong to others, so why bother to cherish them."
So everyone in the military government was very panicked, thinking that Deng Wu would definitely kill Liu Jilian when he arrived here, and would also implicate his subordinates, so they all went to Ji Lian's house to complain.
Liu Jilian thought so too; he was also jealous of his disrespect to Sha Gendan in the past, so he felt even more angry.
Sima Zhujian persuaded Liu Chonglian and asked him to serve as the governor of Danxi County and leave his three sons as hostages. Liu Jilian agreed.
Soon, Liu Shenglian summoned the assistant historian and lied that Queen Xuande of Qi Dynasty had an order to gather troops to rebel again. He captured Zhu Daochen and killed him.
He also wrote a letter to inform Zhu Shilue and summoned Li Ying back.
Neither Li Ying nor Zhu Shilue accepted his mission.
After the envoy returned, Deng Yuanqi gathered his troops and waited for an opportunity in Brazil County. Liu Jilian killed Zhu Shiluo's three sons.
In June of the first year of Tianjian, Deng Yuanqi arrived in Brazil County, and Liu Jilian sent general Li Fengbo and others to resist the attack.
The two armies fought, each gaining and losing. As time passed, Li Fengbo was defeated and retreated to Chengdu.
Liu Jilian drove the residents out, then closed the city gates and stood firm.
Deng Yuanqi quietly marched and surrounded the city of Chengdu.
In the winter of that year, Liu Jilian's city bureau chief Jiang Xizhi and others plotted to surrender the city, but failed, so Liu Jilian killed them.
Sichuan has been suffering from chaos for two years. The food in the city has been exhausted, and a liter of rice cannot be bought for three thousand yuan. People who have died of starvation are piled up together to sleep on each other.
Those who had no relatives or friends killed others to eat.
summary: In the spring of the next year, the emperor sent Chen Jiansun to escort Liu Ji's brother and sons, announcing the emperor's intent. Liu Ji prepared to return home. Emperor Gaozu appointed Deng Yuanqi as governor of Yiye. Deng Yuanqi, previously mistreated by Liu Ji, was advised by Zhu Daochen to check supplies first. Deng agreed. When Sai Dao arrived, he was disrespectful, causing panic. Liu Ji, fearing Deng would kill him, gathered troops again, killed Zhu Daochen, and summoned Li Ying and Zhu Shilue, who refused. Liu Ji killed Zhu Shilue's three sons.

translation:
Liu Ji drank gruel for several months. He was hungry and distressed and had no idea what to do.
In the first month of the second year, Emperor Gaozu sent his chief secretary Zhao Jingyue to announce the order for Liu Jilian to surrender. Liu Jilian took off his shirt and exposed his chest to plead guilty.
Deng Yuanqi moved Liu Jilian outside the city, and soon visited him and treated him with courtesy.
Liu Jilian thanked him and said, "If I had known this, how could it have happened before?"
Deng Yuanqi killed Li Fengbo and other generals, and sent Liu Jilian back to the capital.
Before Liu Jilian left, no one came to see him, only Gong Rui came to see him off.
At the beginning, when Deng Yuanqi was on the road, he was afraid that the matter would not be successful, and there would be nothing to reward the soldiers, so as long as there were people who came to serve as soldiers, they all promised to appoint them. Therefore, there were nearly two thousand people who accepted the duties of the governor.
After Liu Jilian arrived in the capital, he came to the palace to apologize, and Gao Zu received him.
Liu Jilian came in from Dongye Gate, walked a few steps, kowtowed, and came to the Emperor Gaozu.
Gaozu smiled and said to him: "You want to learn from Liu Bei but you can't even learn from Gongsun Shu. Is it because you don't have ministers like Wo Long?"
Liu Jilian kowtowed again to apologize.
Liu Jilian was pardoned and demoted to a civilian.
In the first month of the fourth year, Ji Lian was killed by Lin Daogong, a Shu native, when he was leaving Jianyang Gate.
When Liu Jilian was in Shu, he killed Dao Gong's father, but Dao Gong fled. Now he has taken revenge on him.
Chen Bozhi is the successor of Jiyin County. He had physical strength when he was young.
When he was thirteen or fourteen years old, he liked to wear an otter-skin hat and a bayonet. When the rice in the neighborhood was ripe, he would secretly cut it.
Once when the landowner saw him, he stopped him and said: "You bitch, don't move!"
Chen Bozhi said to the landowner: Fortunately, you still have a lot of rice. What does it matter if you have less rice?
The landlord wanted to arrest him and take him away, so Chen Bozhi came in with a knife. When he was about to stab the landlord, he said: What will happen to this little bitch!
The landowner quickly fled back, but Chen Bozhi calmly picked up the rice and went home.
When Chen Bozhi grew up, he often worked as a robber in the Zhongli area. Once, he showed his face and peeked at other people's boats. The boatman slashed him with a knife and cut off his left ear.
Later, he followed his fellow countryman Wang Guangzhi, a chariot and cavalry general. Wang Guangzhi loved his bravery and let him sleep on his bed every night, and often let him accompany him during expeditions.
When Xiao Zijing, King of Lu Qi'an Lu, was an official in Nan Yanzhou, he had a lot of troops to defend himself.
Emperor Ming sent Wang Guangzhi to attack Zijing. Wang Guangzhi arrived at Guowu and sent Chen Bozhi as the vanguard. With the city gate opened, Jianwang entered the city alone and killed Lu Wangman.
Later, he made many military exploits. Due to his meritorious service, Chen Bozhi was promoted to champion general and hussar commander many times. He was named the uncle of Yufu County and was granted a settlement of 500 households.
After the rise of the righteous army, Saidiebao was appointed as Jijie, supervising the military affairs in advance, and governor of Yuzhou. His duties as a general remained as before.
Soon, Chen Bozhi was transferred to Xingtu and occupied Manmo City to resist the rebels.
Jiansha was pacified, and Zhidan captured the leader of the palace, Lan Jianzhi, and sent him to persuade Danzhi to surrender. He was immediately appointed General Anton and Governor of Liaoye.
Although Su Zuzhi accepted the appointment of direct responsibility, he still had a wait-and-see mentality and lied that the army would come down and surrender soon.
Zhidan said to the generals: This worthy answer shows that his mind has not yet been settled and he is still hesitating. He should be forced to do so.
So the army was stationed in Mandang, and they quickly returned to their mother's invitation before returning to Zhidan.
The number of the rapid advance is Zhennan General, and he advances with the army.
Chen Bozhi garrisoned troops at Zhuoqie, and soon entered the Youdan siege.
summary: In June of the first year of Tianjian, Deng Yuanqi arrived in Brazil County. Liu Ji sent Li Fengbo to resist, but after a prolonged battle, Li Fengbo retreated to Chengdu. Deng Yuanqi surrounded the city. In winter, a plot to surrender failed, and Liu Ji killed the conspirators. After two years of chaos, food ran out, and people starved or resorted to cannibalism. Liu Ji drank gruel for months. In the first month of the second year, Emperor Gaozu sent Zhao Jingyue to order Liu Ji's surrender. Liu Ji surrendered, and Deng Yuanqi treated him with courtesy. Liu Ji was pardoned but demoted to civilian. In the first month of the fourth year, he was killed by Lin Daogong, whose father he had killed in Shu.

translation:
Wang Zhan, courtesy name Sifan, was born in Linyi, Langye, and was the grandson of Wang Hong, the Taibao of the Song Dynasty.
His grandfather, Wang Liu, served as the official of Guanglu and the Marquis of Dongting.
His father, Wang You, served as Tingweiqing.
When Wang Zhan was a few years old, he studied with a teacher. At that time, an artist passed by the door, and his classmates all went out to watch, but Wang Zhan did not watch, and continued to review and recite as before.
After hearing about this, his uncle, Pushe Sengda, the Minister of Public Affairs, looked at Wang Zhan in a different light and said to Wang Zhan's father: Our family's hope for survival rests on this child.
Wang Zhan was twelve years old and was in mourning for his father. He was famous for his filial piety.
When the mourning period expires, he will inherit the title of Marquis of Shuting.
When Wang Zhan was young, he was frivolous and mean, and liked to indulge in fun activities, which was hated by the villagers.
When he reaches adulthood, he will exercise self-restraint and have the ethics of a scholar. He will read a lot of books and be particularly good at chess and archery.
He became an official as Zuo Lang, and was repeatedly promoted to Prince Sheren, Taiwei Chief Secretary, and Prince Xima.
Soon after, he went out to serve as the internal history of Poyang. When his term of office expired, he was appointed Prince Zhongsheren.
He was also appointed as the friend of the king of Qin Nanhai, and soon he was appointed as the king of Situ Jingling to serve as a lieutenant. King Jingling respected him very much.
The King of Nanhai served as the general protecting the army, and Wang Zhan served as the chief history officer.
He also went out to serve as Xuzhou Biejia to engage in history, and was transferred to the hussar general Wang Yan's long history.
Wang Yan was killed, and Wang Zhan was appointed as the prefect of Jinling.
Wang Zhan's administration was honest, and his wife and children were not exempt from hunger and cold.
At that time, the Grand Sima Wang Jingze raised an army to cause rebellion. When passing through Jinling, many people in the county relied on Jingze. Later, the army failed and the imperial army wanted to attack the bandits. Wang Zhan reported to the imperial court and said: Stupid people are prone to riots and are not worthy of tracing the source and punishing them.
Emperor Ming agreed with his opinion and saved tens of thousands of people.
Wang Zhan was recruited and appointed as the Minister of Huangmen, Fujun Jian'an Wang Changshi, and Yushi Zhongcheng.
The vassal prince's palace was established, and Wang Zhan was appointed as the Grand Sima Xiangguo to consult and join the army, and also to record affairs and join the army.
In the Liang Dynasty, Tai Pavilion was established, and Wang Zhan was appointed as Shizhong. He was transferred to Zuo Min Shangshu, and soon he was changed to Libu Shangshu.
Wang Tuo has a straightforward personality, and he is in the department where officials are appointed and dismissed. Most of his recommendations are based on his own wishes.
I like to drink very much, and I often drink all day long, and my energy becomes more cheerful and full, and I don't delay paperwork.
Emperor Gaozu often said that Wang Dui had three skills, namely shooting, playing chess, and drinking.
Soon after, he was awarded the title of General of the Zuo Army. However, he did not take up the post due to illness. He continued to serve as a servant and also as a general of cavalry. However, he did not take office and died at the age of forty-nine.
Mi is called Dust Castle.
His son was born in the same family and served as Zuo Lang. He died early.
Wang Jin's courtesy name is silver carp, and his style is like a human being.
His grandfather, Tanzhi, was the official Guanglu of Sezuo and Wenhou of Yuning; his father was Lu, and he was Cha Sikong and Jian Mugong, both of whom were famous.
When Wang Jin was nine years old, he was in mourning for his biological mother. His face was sad and his body was thin, which astonished his brothers and sisters.
After becoming an adult, he was selected to marry Princess Angu, the daughter of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song Dynasty, and was appointed Prince Consort and Secretary Lang.
After being promoted many times, he was appointed as Taiwei to join the army, the prince sacrificed his life, and the martial arts doctor Wang Wenxue.
summary: Wang Zhan, courtesy name Sifan, was from Linyi, Langye, and was the grandson of Wang Hong. His grandfather, Wang Liu, served as Guanglu and the Marquis of Dongting. His father, Wang You, served as Tingweiqing. As a child, Wang Zhan was studious and did not go out to watch an artist pass by, which impressed his uncle. He was known for filial piety after his father's death at age twelve. As a young man, he was frivolous but later exercised self-restraint, becoming well-read and skilled in chess and archery. He held various official positions, including Zuo Lang, Prince Sheren, and internal history of Poyang. He served as a lieutenant for King Jingling, who respected him greatly. As prefect of Jinling, his administration was honest, and his family suffered from hunger and cold. When Wang Jingze rebelled, Wang Zhan advised Emperor Ming against punishing the many people who had followed him, saving tens of thousands. He later served as Minister of Huangmen and Libu Shangshu. He was straightforward in his recommendations and enjoyed drinking, which did not delay his work. Emperor Gaozu noted his three skills: shooting, chess, and drinking. He died at age forty-nine.

translation:
He served as Situ and appointed Wang Zhi as chief clerk.
Chu Zhao said to Denghulu: The court's grace is special and worthy of honor, but it has wronged the virtuous young master.
Wang Zhi was promoted many times and served as the two prince friends of Zhenbeitong, Cao Shi, Chubi and Zhijun.
He went to Beijing and served as the Vice Minister of Zhongshu.
Soon he was appointed as the internal history of Xuanyue. He was honest, cautious and kind.
The people of the county, Zhang Tan and Yu Qing, fought for land, but could not reach a verdict for many years.
After Wang Ji took office, the fathers and elders said to each other: Wang Fujun implements virtuous government, but there is such competition in our village.
Zhang Ni and Wu Qing then went together to plead guilty, and the land in dispute became wasteland.
The conscript Wang Jin was appointed as the Minister of Huangmen, and soon he was transferred to the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
When he went out, he served as general Ningshuo and prefect of Saichui.
There were more than ten serious criminals in the county jail. They were all released on the day of the winter solstice and returned after the festival. Only one of them was delayed. Prison officials reported this incident.
Wang Jin said: "This is naturally the responsibility of the prefect. The officials in charge should not worry."
The next morning, the man went to the prison by himself and said that it was because his wife was pregnant. The officials and the people admired Wang Jin even more.
After serving for three years and Man Chengpeng's second year, he entered the capital as a minister. Before taking office, he was appointed as the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel. He was praised for his peace and reasonableness in the selection of officials.
After Cui Chazhanji was pacified, Wang Jin was awarded the title of General of the Right Army in accordance with the regulations and sealed the fortress. Wang Cha firmly refused and refused to accept it, and was promoted to General of the Right Guard.
When the rebel army arrived, the people in the city killed Donghunhou, and hundreds of officials signed and presented Donghunhou's head.
When Wang Zhi heard about it, he sighed and said: Although the hat is broken, can it be worn on the feet?
So he rubbed leaves from the garden and swallowed them, pretending to be short of breath and not signing his name.
When Emperor Gaozu read the document and saw that there was no signature from Wang Zhi, he praised him in his heart and did not criticize him.
The vassal prince's palace was established, and Wang Zhi was appointed as the general of the right army and the general of the hussars.
In the Liang Dynasty, Tai Pavilion was established, and Wang Zhi was transferred to Sanqi Changshi and Zhongshu Ling.
In the first year of Tianjian, he concurrently served as general of the former army with his original official position.
This year, he was transferred to the title of champion general, Danyang Yin.
The administration should be simple and simple, and should be governed by inaction, without cumbersome and harsh government decrees.
There was a widow in the capital who had no son. After her mother-in-law died, she borrowed money to pay for her burial. After the burial, she was unable to repay the money. Wang Zhi sympathized with her morality and used his salary to repay her.
There was a famine that year, and porridge was placed in front of the county government office every morning to give alms to the people. The people praised Wang Zhi endlessly.
For three years, he served as a regular attendant of Sanqi, Zhongshu Ling, and guerrilla general.
Wang Zhi served as Zhongshu Ling and served as the governor of the capital, so he felt satisfied.
summary: Wang Jin, courtesy name silver carp, was the grandson of Tanzhi and son of Lu. At age nine, he mourned his biological mother with great sorrow. He married Princess Angu, daughter of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song Dynasty. He held various posts, including Prince Consort and Secretary Lang. As internal history of Xuanyue, he was honest and kind. When two men, Zhang Tan and Yu Qing, could not settle a land dispute for years, the elders shamed them into pleading guilty, and the land became wasteland. As prefect of Saichui, he released serious criminals on the winter solstice, and all but one returned. The man explained his delay was due to his wife's pregnancy, which increased the people's admiration. He was praised for his fairness in selecting officials. When the rebel army arrived and Donghunhou was killed, Wang Jin refused to sign the document presenting his head, saying a broken hat could not be worn on the feet. Emperor Gaozu praised him for this. He served as Danyang Yin, governing simply and without harsh decrees. He used his salary to repay a widow's debt for her mother-in-law's burial and gave porridge to the people during a famine. He was content as Zhongshu Ling and often complained of illness. He died at age fifty-four. He was skilled in cursive official script and was called the "Sage of Calligraphy" by Xu Xixiu. He was honest and kind, never impeaching others. When a guest stole his vehicle's curtains, he did not pursue the matter. He had five sons.

translation:
I often say to my nephews: When Xie Zhuang was Emperor Xiaowu of the Song Dynasty, his status was only Zhongshu Ling, and I thought I could not surpass him.
So he complained of illness many times and rarely interacted with guests.
Transferred to former general and Taichang Qing.
In the sixth year, he went out to serve as General Yunhui, Changshi of the Shixing King of Anxi, and Grand Administrator of Nanjun.
The following year, he was transferred to the post of Military Advisor General, Pingxi Poyang County Prince Changshi, and Jiangxia Prefecture, all of whom were awarded the rank of two thousand stones.
In the ninth year, he was transferred to Sanqi Changshi and Jin Ziguanglu, doctor.
Twelve years later, he died at the age of fifty-four.
Wang Zhi was good at cursive official script and served as a model at the time.
Xu Xixiu, a guerrilla general of the Qi Dynasty, also claimed to be able to write and often called Wang Zhi the "Sage of Calligraphy".
Wang Zhi's family has lived in Mayan Lane, Jinzhongli, Jiankang for generations. Since his father, Sengqian, the family tradition has been tolerant, and Wang Zhi is especially honest and kind.
In all the positions he has held, he has never impeached others for their crimes.
A guest once stole the curtains from Wang Zhi's vehicle and sold them. After Wang Zhi found out, he didn't pursue the matter and treated the person as he did then.
When guests visited his home, he would cover up their faults and praise their good deeds.
The brothers, nephews, and nephews were all honest, humble, and obedient. At that time, people said that the Ma Fan and Wang families had the demeanor of elders.
Four years later, Wang Zhi was reburied. Emperor Gaozu generously presented him with rewards and added the title Mi to An.
Wang Zhi had five sons, named Wang Ji, Wang Xiu, Wang Chui, Wang Cao and Wang Sai, all of whom were famous.
The stems of some of Wang's characters are far away, and the king is trapped and falls into witchcraft.
My great-grandfather, Jing Cong, was famous in Sequ, and his official position was as high as Dr. Zuo Guanglu and Kaifu Yitong.
Grandfather Zanzhi's official position reached the rank of Jin Zi Guang Lu.
His father showed him off, and his official position was as high as the prefect of Wuxing.
When the king was young, he was graceful and well behaved.
He started his official career as Zuo Lang, but did not take up the post. He was promoted many times and became the king of Luling in the Chinese army.
The master of the palace, Wang Ken, the king of Jingling, appreciated him very much and treated him favorably.
He was promoted to Chief Situ, but resigned due to his father's death.
After the period of mourning was over, he was appointed the prince to wash horses and the king of Jian'an.
When he went out, he served as general Ningyuan and internal history of Guiyang.
When the rebels rose, many counties upstream were in panic and commotion. Wang Jun closed the door and sat in meditation. The county was stable and the people relied on him.
In the early years of Jade Prison, he returned to Beijing and was appointed as the Minister of Zhongshu.
Emperor Gaozu liked his demeanor very much, and he was appreciated and promoted together with Sudeng Renping.
Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, but he was incompetent and was appointed as Changshi, King of Zhenglu Ancheng. He also served as the crown prince's concubine and a guerrilla general.
When he went out to serve as the prefect of Xuancheng, the administration was clean and peaceful, and the officials and the people were stable.
After serving for three years, he was conscripted to Beijing and appointed as a minister, and was transferred to Duzhi Shangshu.
He also used his original official position to concurrently serve as Minister of the Ministry of Finance and supervised the construction of Tai Chi Hall.
After the incident was over, he went out to serve as general of Zhengyuan, chief historian of Pingxi, and prefect of Nanjun.
Soon he served as general Zhiwu, chief historian of Zhenxi, and prefect of Shu County.
He returned to Beijing and served as Zuo Min Shangshu and infantry captain.
He was transferred to the Ministry of Civil Affairs and was highly praised for his role in selecting officials.
summary: Wang Jun, whose courtesy name is far away, was the grandson of Jing Cong. His grandfather was Zanzhi, and his father was Xianhui. He was graceful and well-behaved as a child. He started his career as Zuo Lang and was appreciated by Wang Ken, the king of Jingling. As internal history of Guiyang, he closed the city gates and meditated during a rebellion, stabilizing the county. Emperor Gaozu liked his demeanor. He served as prefect of Xuancheng, where his administration was clean and peaceful. He had a calm and elegant temperament and no desire to compete. He once agreed with Xie Yu to stop seeking promotion upon reaching the position of servant. After becoming a servant, his conduct was indifferent. He died at age fifty-six.

translation:
Not only could Xun Ling hope that Duke Li would not die!
He is really the secret treasure of the school and an outstanding talent who governs the country.
Wang Wei was appointed as a hussar and a lieutenant.
The vassal prince's palace was established, and Wang Wei was appointed as Hu Cao's vassal, and was promoted to Situ Zuo Changshi.
In the first year of Tianjian, he was appointed as the crown prince's concubine, and also as a general of heroic cavalry, and was appointed as a servant in the palace.
When he went out, he served as General Ningshuo and Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese Army.
He also served as the Shizhong and the Shesheng Xiaowei. He was transferred to the rank of Minister of the Five Soldiers and was granted the title of Shizhong. He went out to serve as the prefect of Jinling.
He was recruited to serve as Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, and soon he also served as the prince of the country to offer wine.
Wang Chen was the son of a famous official. He had a good reputation when he was young. When he was in the department of selecting officials, his responsibilities and affairs were well organized. However, he had been distinguished and distinguished for generations, and he was often separated from others. He could not pay attention to people of low origin. Everyone thought that he was cold and ruthless.
He was promoted to the right servant of Shangshu, and soon he was awarded the title of Attendant.
He was promoted to Zuopushe and resigned due to the death of his mother.
After his comeback, he served as General Yunhui and Grand Administrator of Wu County.
Returning to the capital, he served as a minister, minister Zuopushe, and concurrently as the son of the state offering wine.
In the winter of the fourth year of his reign, he died of a sudden illness at the age of forty-seven.
Shaoling gave posthumous gifts to Shizhong, Zhongshu Ling, and the general of the Chinese army, including a coffin, a set of formal attire, a set of clothes, one hundred thousand money, and one hundred pieces of cloth.
The name of Mi is Jing.
He has four sons, named Wang Xun, Wang Cheng, Wang Li, and Wang Gan, all of whom have successful and prominent official careers.
Jade was named Huai Zheng, and he was smart, alert, insightful and thoughtful when he was young. The hermit Tanhuang saw him and thought he was strange.
When he was thirteen years old, Wang Chen died and he became so sad and emaciated that his family could not recognize him.
At the age of sixteen, he was summoned in Selonggai, and he responded cheerfully and thoroughly.
The emperor watched him go out for a long time, then turned back and said to Zhu Yi: It can be said that there is a prime minister in the prime minister's house.
He was added as a student of the country, passed the examination as a top grade, was appointed Secretary Lang, and was transferred to Prince Sheren and Secretary Cheng.
He was appointed as the concubine of Xuancheng Wang Wenxue, You and the Crown Prince, and was in charge of records.
Soon he was promoted to the rank of servant. After being appointed, he went to the palace to see him. He asked Bao Yizuo calmly, "How old will Chu Yan be when he becomes prime minister?"
Jianchui replied: I just met thirty years old.
The emperor said: The current Wang Xun is no worse than Yan Hui.
He has beautiful appearance and grace, is good at advancing and retreating, writes well, and is a leader among the younger generations.
He was especially favored and honored in the palace of the Crown Prince.
He died of illness while serving as a servant at the age of twenty-six.
Posthumously give him his official position.
Mi's nickname is Wenzi.
summary: Wang Chen, courtesy name Sihui, was the son of Wang Jian. As a child, he had an outstanding demeanor. He married the eldest princess of Huainan. He was recommended by Wang Gui Yaoguang, who praised his talents and character. He was the son of a famous official and had a good reputation.
