As Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, his affairs were well-organized, but he was considered cold and ruthless for not paying attention to people of low origin. He died suddenly at age forty-seven. He had four sons. Wang Xun, courtesy name Huai Zheng, was Wang Chen's son. He was smart and thoughtful as a child. At thirteen, he mourned his father with great sadness. At sixteen, he responded cheerfully to the emperor's summons. The emperor remarked that there was a prime minister in the prime minister's house. He had a beautiful appearance and was a leader among the younger generation. He died of illness at age twenty-six.

translation:
Yutai, whose courtesy name is Zhubi, is the son of Wang Jin's eldest brother Yuci.
Wang Jie served successively as a minister and prefect of the county during the Yiqiao period, and his reputation was higher than that of Wang Zhi.
Wang Tai was smart and savvy when he was young. When he was a few years old, his grandmother gathered all her grandchildren and nephews and scattered dates and chestnuts on the bed. The children all rushed to get them, except the jade pot.
Asked the reason, he replied: If you don't take it, you will naturally be rewarded.
Therefore, his brothers and sisters in the same server looked at him differently.
As an adult, he becomes peaceful, gentle and elegant. People can't see his happy and angry expression.
He became an official as a writer, but he was not appointed as a secretary. He was transferred to the former general Facao Xing to join the army, Situ Shuhe, the winemaker, and the chariot and cavalry chief.
Gaozu's vassal palace was established, and Wang Tai was appointed as the hussar and cavalry officer.
In the first year of Tianjian, he was transferred to Secretary Cheng.
In the last years of Qi Yongyuan, a fire broke out in the harem, which spread and burned the books in the palace. Almost all the books were scattered and scattered.
Wang Tai was appointed secretary-general, and he submitted a memorial requesting that it be revised and written. Emperor Gaozu followed his advice.
Soon, he was transferred to the position of Minister of Zhongshu.
When he went out to serve as his mother in Xuzhou, Biejia was engaged in history and had a reputation for being capable in his post.
He was also recruited as the minister of Zhongshu and ordered to take charge of the affairs of the official department.
He was repeatedly promoted and appointed as the Minister of Huangmen, and the regular servant of Sanqi outside the Yuanwai. He was still in charge of the affairs of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, and soon he officially took up the post.
Since crossing the Yangtze River, Libulang is no longer in charge of the selection of high-ranking officials. In the history of the order, villains have been vying for one after another, and few people have been qualified.
After taking charge of the throne, he did not make any connections or ask for favors. The officials who came first were appointed. He did not change his opinion because of anyone's request for intercession. The whole world praised him for his fairness.
He was promoted to Tingwei many times and became Situ Zuo's chief historian.
He served as general Mingwei and prefect of Saitong when he was abroad, and his peaceful administration in the county won the hearts of the people.
He was recruited as General Ningyuan, An Youzhangshi, and was soon promoted to Shizhong.
Subsequently, he served as the prince's concubine, concurrently as an infantry captain, and as a lieutenant.
Soon he was transferred to Renwei Changshi and Nanlanling Prefecture to act as agent for the Nankang palace, state and feudal affairs.
King Taikang was transferred to another position, and Wang Tai served as Beizhong Lang Changshi, acting as the agent for Yuzhang's palace, state, and feudal affairs. The position of prefect remained as before.
He entered Beijing and served as the official minister of the capital.
Wang Tai was able to accept people. Scholars often missed Wang Tai and often hoped that he would be in the position of selecting officials.
Soon, Wang Tai was appointed as the Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, and high-ranking families placed their hopes on him. Before he could appoint officials, Wang Tai fell ill and was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi and a general of Zuo Xiaoqi. He died before taking office at the age of forty-five.
summary: Wang Tai, courtesy name Zhubi, was the son of Wang Jin's eldest brother. As a child, he did not grab dates and chestnuts scattered by his grandmother, saying he would be rewarded without taking them. He was peaceful and gentle as an adult. As Secretary Cheng, he requested to revise and write books after a fire burned the palace books. As Libulang in charge of selection, he did not change his opinion due to requests for intercession, and the world praised his fairness. He was able to accept people, and scholars often hoped he would be in the position of selecting officials. He died before taking office as Zuo Xiaoqi General at age forty-five.

translation:
Mi's nickname is Yizi. At first Wangtai had no sons, but his adopted brother's son Wang Qi gave birth to his son Wang Kuo a long time later. Yanzifu is a Qu person.
Grandfather Chi is the Duke of Yi and Cheng of Kaifu in Sai. His father, Wang Kong, was the minister of Huangmen.
Xingshu lost his parents at the age of fourteen and became a charioteer.
When he went out, he served as General Ningyuan and Tongtong Neishi.
Jinsai was killed, and no relatives or friends dared to see him. Wang Jian went alone to express his condolences, and he became famous for this.
He was transferred to the position of Prince Zhongsheren and Taiwei's vassal.
When you go out, you will leave the history inside.
He was promoted several times to the post of Assistant Minister of Zhongshu, and then to the post of Chief Secretary of Agriculture.
Wang Fen's brother Wang Huan was killed in Yongzhou, and Wang Huan's son Wang Su fled to Wei. Wang Fen imprisoned himself and asked for punishment. Qi Shizu knew his sincerity, enlightened him and let him go.
When Wang Su led Wei troops to invade the border one after another, he took advantage of Wang Feng's company and calmly asked Wang Feng: "Is there any news from the north recently?"
Wang Feng replied solemnly: "Since Wang Su has forgotten his family recently, how can he remember his subordinates?"
The emperor also trusted the king's identity.
Soon he was appointed General Ningshuo and Internal History of Lingling.
He was recruited to serve as Huangmen Shilang. Because his father died in this position, he resolutely refused to take up the post and was transferred to Secretary Supervisor.
In the early years of Tianjian's reign, he was appointed as a regular servant of the cavalry, a captain of the infantry, and a minister of the ministry.
Emperor Gaozu once asked the officials at a banquet: Am I doing something or inaction?
Wang Feng replied: Your Majesty, the way to comply with all things is action, and to realize the highest state is inaction.
Gaozu praised the answer well.
When he went out to serve as the prefect of Xuancheng, he was changed to the prefect of Wu County. He was transferred to General Ningshuo, Beizhong Lang, Wang Changshi of Yuzhang, and the prefect of Lanling to act as agent for the affairs of Kongxu Prefecture.
He was transferred to Taichang Qing, Prince Youli, and Sanqi Changshi to serve in Shu Palace, and was appointed Jin Ziguanglu doctor.
He also served as General Zhiwu and Changshi of Nankang King, with a rank of Zhong 2,000 stones.
Then he went to Beijing and served as a regular servant of Sanqi, a doctor of Jin Ziguanglu, and a great Zhongzheng of Nanxuzhou. He was awarded to twenty close followers.
He was promoted to Shangshu Zuopushe, and soon he was given the title of Attendant.
At that time, the altars in the northern and southern suburbs were built. Wang Feng concurrently served as the chief craftsman in his own position. He was appointed as a regular attendant of Sanqi and doctor Youguanglu, and he was awarded close associates, a total of forty people.
He was promoted to Shizhong, Tejin, and Zuo Guanglu doctors, and also served as Danyang Yin with his own position.
He died in March of the fifth year of his life at the age of seventy-nine.
The imperial edict ordered him to posthumously grant his original position, 400,000 yuan in money, 400 bolts of cloth, 400 pounds of wax, a coffin, a set of formal attire, and a set of clothes.
Mi's nickname is Beard.
The eldest son, Wang Bi, whose courtesy name was Chudui, was elected as a scholar in the Zhitu industry. He served as an official to conquer the captives and build the fortress, King Facao, joined the army, Situ Shuhe offered wine, and the king of Chenli wrote literature.
Married Princess Yixing and was appointed Prince Consort Captain.
He was repeatedly promoted to the position of Minister of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China.
When he went out, he served as General Mingwei and Prefect of Saiyan, and he was recruited as Situ Zuo Changshi.
Wang Xi, whose courtesy name is Gonggu, is Wang Lin's second son.
summary: Wang Fen, courtesy name Xingshu, lost his parents at fourteen. He went alone to express condolences when Jinsai was killed, becoming famous for this. When his brother Wang Huan was killed and his son Wang Su fled to Wei, Wang Fen imprisoned himself. When Wang Su led Wei troops to invade, Wang Fen said he could not remember his subordinates since Wang Su had forgotten his family. He refused to take the post of Huangmen Shilang because his father died in that position. He answered Emperor Gaozu's question about action and inaction well. He died at age seventy-nine.

translation:
When he was young, he was alert and savvy. He studied with his brothers, but when it was time to take a break, he was often left alone without getting up.
When he was seven or eight years old, he followed the princess into the palace. Emperor Gaozu praised him for his intelligence and agility, and often talked about him to officials in the court.
Wang Xi used all his energy to study regardless of his fatigue, which resulted in damage to his right eye.
The princess often restricted his studies and decorated his house for him.
Although he was a child, he had no other hobbies.
At the age of twelve, he became a son of the country.
At the age of fourteen, he was elected as a scholar and appointed Secretary Lang. He was as famous as Zhang Boxu, a native of Fanyang, and both served as the crown prince's minister.
When your father dies, mourn with all etiquette.
After the period of mourning was over, he was appointed the prince to wash horses.
At that time, Prince Zhaoming was still young and did not interact with his subordinates.
Emperor Gaozu ordered: Prince Xima Wang Xi and secretary Lang Zhang Lan are elites among relatives and talented people in the court. They can be respected as teachers and friends.
Because he was a relative, he was granted the title of Marquis of Yong'an and was appointed King of Jin'an. However, he refused to go to the post because he was ill, so he was ordered to accept Shao's order and stay in the capital.
When King Jin'an held the coronation ceremony, Wang Xi took charge of affairs as a member of the palace.
In the early years of the Pong Dynasty, the Wei State began to contact and sue for peace, and sent Liu Shanming to inquire about the reconciliation. Emperor Gaozu ordered Zhu Yi, a scholar from Zhongshushe, to receive him. All those who participated in the banquet were northerners who had surrendered.
Shanming relied on his talent and said to Zhu Yi after drinking to his heart's content: How many people in the southern countries are as eloquent and knowledgeable as you are from Zhongshushe?
Zhu Yi replied: The reason why I am able to receive guests is to fulfill my duties.
In the peaceful exchanges between the two countries, what is valued is closeness and friendship; if one is to be praised based on talent and debate, I should not be appointed.
Shanming then said: Wang Wang and Tuitang have been heard in the north. How can we see them?
Sai Yu started the memorial in detail, and Shandan ordered a banquet to be held immediately in Luyuan. There were only four people, Wang Xi, Zhang Zuan and Zhu Yi.
When Shanming came to the table, he discussed the classics and history books, and at the same time ridiculed and teased him. Wang Xi and Zhang Lan responded according to his discussion, without stopping to ask questions or asking each other about anything. Shanming admired each other very much.
Another day he said to Zhu Yi: "I met two wise men in one day, which really satisfied my expectations. How can a country become a country without gentlemen!"
He was renamed Zhongshu Lang and transferred to Shihuangmen Shilang and Shangshu Libu Langzhong. He was twenty-four years old this year.
Wang Xi said to his relatives and friends: Because I am a relative, I have been favored by the current emperor and received a title. This is not my ambition. In addition, I have been weak and sick recently, and all kinds of affairs are unbearable. How can I give up my hobbies and do things that I cannot do?
So he claimed to be ill and refused to take office.
Then he sent the servants back, declined the guests, closed the door and thought deeply, leaving the room lonely.
summary: Wang Xi, courtesy name Gonggu, was Wang Lin's second son. He was alert and savvy as a child, studying tirelessly even when his brothers took breaks, which damaged his right eye. At twelve, he became a son of the country. He was appointed Prince Xima. Emperor Gaozu ordered that he and Zhang Lan be respected as teachers and friends for the young Prince Zhaoming. He received Liu Shanming, a Wei envoy, and debated with him, impressing Shanming. He later claimed illness and refused to take office, closing his door and thinking deeply. He died at age thirty-six.

translation:
He died in the first month of the sixth year of Zhongdatong at the age of thirty-six.
As a posthumous gift to the attendants, he was given a coffin, a set of formal attire, and a set of clothes.
Mi was given the posthumous nickname Sadako.
He has sons Wang Fan and Wang Bao.
Wang Yu, named Guild, is Wang Xi's fifth younger brother.
When I was eight years old, my father died. I was so sad and thin that I became more and more emaciated.
When the mourning period expired, he was recruited to serve as the son of the country. Yuan Ang offered wine and praised him for his understanding of affairs.
He ranked high in the examination and was awarded the title of Chief and Secretary Langzhong. He successively served as Zhonglang of Shangshu Palace, Prince Zhongsheren, and Lu Xiang, a native of Wujun, took turns in charge of Shugong's official documents.
He went out to serve as the prefect of Jian'an.
The leaders of the mountain people, Fang Shan and Xie Xi, gathered their tribesmen to rely on dangerous positions. They repeatedly robbed and became a scourge for the people. Wang Lun secretly devised a plan and led the army to pacify them. Shao Ling praised the king even more and promulgated it to the prefectures and counties.
He was appointed General of Wuwei and Shixing Internal History, but when his biological mother died, he resolutely refused to take up the post.
He was also appointed General Ningyuan and Internal Secretary of Nankang. When Xunxu caused chaos, he appointed Wang Yu as Internal Secretary of Ancheng to calm them down.
He returned and was appointed Huangmen Shilang, and soon served as the chief historian of Wuling King in Anxi and the prefect of Shu County.
Wang Cang was afraid of the danger and resolutely refused because of his illness. The court dismissed him because of this.
Much later, he was appointed General Rongzhao and Minister Zuocheng, and was appointed Minister of Huangmen. He was transferred to the crown prince's concubine and was in charge of the documents of the East Palace.
He died in December of the second year of Taiqian's reign at the age of forty-five.
As a posthumous gift to the attendants, he was given a coffin, a set of formal attire, and a set of clothes.
In the third year of Chengsheng's reign, Shizu issued an additional edict: "A wise man without boasting is called Gong. King Yu Mi is named Gongzi."
The character of Tuili is Genwa, a native of Yudeng.
His father, Zhang Zhong, was a Mansu Tejin and Jin Ziguanglu doctor who was famous in the previous dynasty.
When Zhang Chong was young, he did not uphold moral integrity and liked to have fun and relax.
Zhang Xu once asked for leave and returned to Yusu. As soon as he entered Xicheng, he met Zhang Chong who was out hunting. He was holding an eagle in his left hand and leading a dog in his right hand. When Zhang Zhong's boat arrived, Zhang Chong put down the rope, untied his sleeves, and knelt down by the water.
Zhang Xu said: Isn’t it too tiring for one person to do two things?
Zhang Chong knelt down and replied: "I heard that you can be independent at the age of thirty. Now I am twenty-nine. Please wait until next year before respectfully changing."
Zhang Xu said: The Yan family has this virtue of being able to correct mistakes.
By the next year, he would cultivate himself and change his moral integrity.
He studied for less than a year and read a variety of books, especially "Laozi" and "Book of Changes". He could talk about philosophy elegantly and had a good reputation with his uncle Zhang Ji.
He served as an official in Fujun and joined the army. He was transferred to the position of Prince Sheren, Minister of the Palace of Secretaries, and Prince Wuling of Wuling.
At that time, Wang Jian was appointed as the official director of the imperial court, and all matters of Emperor Wu depended on his opinion.
Emperor Wu once wanted to appoint Zhang Chong's father, Zhang Xu, as a minister, and asked Wang Jian for his opinion. Wang Jian replied: Zhang Xu had a high reputation when he was young, so he is indeed a good candidate. However, the scholars in the East have not adhered to ethics recently, and Zhang Xu's sons often behaved frivolously. The ministers thought that the affairs should be carefully selected.
The emperor then gave up.
Before being sent away, Zhang Chong's brothers were both frivolous and arrogant. When Zhang Chong was young, he didn't care about trivial matters, so Wang Jian said that.
Zhang Chong was angry when he heard about it, so he wrote to Wang Jian: Zhang Chong, a citizen of the state of Wu, wrote to the king of Langxie: The journey has been long recently, the rain has been dark for a long time, and the heat and coolness are uneven. I think there will be no loss of food and supplies.
summary: Wang Yu, courtesy name Guild, was Wang Xi's fifth younger brother. He mourned his father with great sadness at age eight. As prefect of Jian'an, he pacified the mountain people leaders Fang Shan and Xie Xi. He refused the post of Shixing Internal History due to his mother's death. He died at age forty-five.

translation:
The talents in Maoling looked at the carriages and their clothes and thought about them for a long time; the common people in Bashan stopped their carriages and shrugged their shoulders and sighed.
Is it not a pity?
As for controlling swans and riding yellow cranes in the sky, the riverbanks will remain dry and the mountains and fields will be nourished.
Some exotic birds came to greet them on the edge of the rocks; a slight smoke suddenly appeared in the forest and steamed up.
Even if a bundle is not worth cherishing, how can Nanshan be considered valuable?
I am a commoner from the west of Kunshan, a commoner outside Daishan.
Raising silkworms for clothing, cultivating for food, not serving princes, looking for confidants, visiting contemporary officials, running fast and lobbying, walking around among butchers and gamblers with disheveled hair, and being extremely happy.
Man, you met Chenghua earlier and then Chongli.
Your unparalleled respect made you famous in your early years; the remarks of country people were made in haste and fallacy.
However, people all my life say that I am crazy, so how can I discuss it with you gentlemen?
Therefore, I disclose my knowledge, open my mind, narrate my life, talk about my source, communicate my dreams and souls, and express my sincerity, just because of you.
The mountain road at Guankou is blocked, so I can't deliver it after I finish writing it. If I meet someone collecting firewood, I hope to deliver it to the person in charge.
Wang Jian reported to the emperor, removed him from the vertical official position, and was deposed for a long time.
Later, he served as Situ's advisor and joined the army. Wang Modou, a native of Langxie, and Lu Huixiao, a native of the same county, were all guests of Situ Zhidou.
He entered Beijing and served as the Minister of Zhongshu, and soon he was appointed as the Minister of Huangmen.
Emperor Ming became prime minister and appointed Zhang Chong as the commander of the town army.
When he went out to serve as the prefect of Xianxing, his administration was clear and clear, and he followed the rule of inaction, which made it convenient for the people and officials.
Soon after his mother passed away, he left his post. After the mourning period expired, he was appointed the crown prince's concubine and promoted to the imperial court.
When the rebel army was stationed near the capital, Marquis Shuhun summoned hundreds of officials to enter the palace province. The court officials were worried about the disaster, and some came and went to drink and feast. Ji Tong lived alone in Shizhong Province and did not leave the gate.
Hou Shuhun was killed in the city, and all the officials gathered under the west bell to summon Zhang Chong but he did not show up.
The direct vassal prince's palace was established, and Zhang Chong was appointed as Grand Sima to consult and join the army. He was transferred to Yanguo Langzhongling, Ancestral Department Shangshu, and Tunqi Xiaowei, and was changed to Champion General and Situ Zuo Changshi.
In the early years of Tianjian, he was appointed Taichang Qing.
Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and he was given a fair reputation in the department of selecting officials.
Soon he served as the regular attendant of Sanqi and the general of Yunqi.
Then he was appointed as the prefect of Zhiluo, with a rank of two thousand stones.
He was recruited to serve as a regular attendant of Sanqi and a prince of the state to offer wine.
Zhang Chong was good at righteousness and lectured in lectures, and everyone from the crown prince on down came.
At that time, many princes were in the school, holding scriptures in their hands and prostrating. Zhang Chong stood in official uniform and did not dare to accept it.
summary: Zhang Chong, courtesy name Genwa, was the son of Zhang Xu. As a young man, he liked to have fun. His father saw him hunting and rebuked him. Zhang Chong promised to change the next year, and he did, studying various books. He wrote a letter to Wang Jian, explaining his character and lifestyle. Wang Jian reported to the emperor, and Zhang Chong was deposed for a long time. He later served as prefect of Xianxing, governing with inaction. When the rebel army was near the capital, he stayed alone in Shizhong Province. He was good at righteousness and lectured, with the crown prince and others attending. He died at age sixty-six.

translation:
He was appointed as General Zuowei, and the wine ceremony continued as before.
He was summoned to serve as Minister of Public Affairs, and soon he was appointed General Yunhui and Grand Administrator of Wu County.
When he took office, he would provide support to the poor and elderly people, and all his old friends would be happy.
Due to illness, he stated his request and was recruited as a regular attendant of Sanqi. Doctor Jin Ziguanglu did not have time to return to the court. He died in Wu County in the thirteenth year of Tianjian at the age of sixty-six.
The imperial edict issued a posthumous gift to the ministers and generals protecting the army.
Mi's nickname is Mu Zi.
His son Zhang Zui is the heir.
The main character of Guiyu is locust, and he is from Lixun. When he was young, he had ambition and integrity, loved learning, and was good at writing documents.
Living next to the people of Jianjun County, he was deeply friendly to him.
At the beginning, there were Ji Yuanrong and Gui Gai in the world, both of whom were good at playing the piano. They said they inherited the teachings of Dai Andao. He Xiu learned from them since he was a child, and he enjoyed playing the piano to the fullest.
After hearing about it, King Manjingling summoned him and appointed him as Fa Caoxing to join the army. Quanyu was highly appreciated and close to him.
King Jingling once held a banquet in the back garden. He placed a qin played by Xie Gui, the prime minister of the court, next to it and presented it to Liu Tan. Liu Tan played elegant tunes.
Ziliang said: Your exquisiteness surpasses Ji Yuanrong's heart, your mystery reaches the French style of Yang Gai, your excellent texture and wonderful techniques are indeed all present today.
It's not just contemporary that it can be called strange, it's enough to track ancient celebrities.
After being promoted to Prince Xi Ma many times, he resigned due to his father's death.
After the mourning period was over, he was tried to be appointed as the prime minister of Poyang. He allowed the officials to serve the three years of mourning and take charge of local cultural and educational matters, which was praised by the people.
After returning to Beijing, he was appointed as a hussar and a lieutenant.
When Emperor Gaozu arrived in the capital, Liu Pang went to Stone City to greet him and was appointed champion general and Sima of Zhengdong Prefecture.
At that time, Donghun Hou had not yet been pacified, and the soldiers were still fighting hard. Liu Pang wrote a letter stating what should be done, asking for books and documents to be collected before the city was pacified, and to follow Mo Gaozu's principles of magnanimity and caring for the people. Gaozu followed his advice.
When Xiao Yingzhou died in Jiangling, Liu Jin was sent west to greet Emperor He. He was then appointed as the Minister of Huangmen and the captain of the infantry school, and was transferred to the right Sima of the Prime Minister.
In the first year of Tianjian, he was appointed as the chief minister and the minister, and he worked with Pushe Shen Yue and others to formulate new laws.
Liu Pang was chaste and simple in character. He had a good reputation among the sons of your noble lord for a long time. He was devoted to poetry and poetry when he was young.
He began to write a poem and said: Under the leaves of trees in rivers, lakes and swamps, autumn clouds fly at the head of Longshan Mountain.
When Wang Yuanchang from Langxie saw it, he sighed and admired it, so he wrote it on the wall of the study.
Now that he participates in music banquets, Liu Pang will be ordered to compose poems.
The middle chapter of "Deng Jingyang Tower" written by Emperor Gaozu once was ordered to say: The waves are rising from the vast liquid, and the tall poplars and tall trees have already seen autumn.
summary: Liu Pang, courtesy name Guiyu, was from Lixun. He was good at playing the qin and was appreciated by King Jingling. He wrote a letter to Emperor Gaozu asking for books to be collected before the city was pacified. He was chaste and simple, devoted to poetry. His poem "Deng Jingyang Tower" was deeply praised by Emperor Gaozu. He was good at chess. As prefect of Wuxing, his administration was clear, and the people missed him. He died at age fifty-three.

translation:
In the ninth year of Yujian, Xuancheng County official Wu Chengbo relied on the evil way to gather his disciples to attack Xuancheng and killed the prefect Zhu Sengyong. Then he massacred the surrounding counties, crossed the mountains and invaded Wuxing, destroying everything he passed. The army numbered 20,000, and attacked the county town.
People in the East were not familiar with war, and the officials and the people were afraid of the disturbance and fled in all directions. They all asked Cai Lu to take shelter.
Cai Lu resolutely defended the city and recruited brave people to strengthen the county.
Cheng Bo used all his elite soldiers to attack Cai Lu. Cai Lu ordered his troops to go out of the city to resist, and fought at the city gate. He defeated Cheng Bo in the first confrontation, beheaded Cheng Bo in the military formation, and pacified all the remaining party members.
He was awarded the title of General Wu.
Recruited Ren Duzhi Shangshu and transferred him to Zhongshu Ling.
He also served as General Xinwu and Governor of Jinling.
Returning to the imperial court, he was appointed as a regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi and a minister of state.
He was transferred to the position of Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs and served in the department of selecting officials. He was famous for his magnanimity and simplicity.
He also served as a servant and secretary-supervisor. He was changed to Zhongshuling, and the servant remained the same.
In the second year of ordinary life, he went out to serve as general Xuan Yi and prefect of Wu County.
Four years later, he died at the age of fifty-seven.
Posthumous gifts include Shizhong, Doctor Jin Ziguanglu, and General Xuan Hui.
Mi's nickname is King of Dust.
His son Yanxi successively served as Zhongshu Lang and announced the city's internal history.
Jiang Bei, courtesy name Yanbiao, was born in Kaocheng, Jiyang.
His great-grandfather Jiang Zhan was a doctor of Zuo Guanglu and Kaifu Yitong in the Song Dynasty; his father Jiang Wei was Taichang Qing of the Qi Dynasty: all of them had great reputations in previous generations.
Jiang Bei was smart and alert when she was young. She could recite a book after reading it once.
He was selected as a student of the Imperial College. He was proficient in Shangshu and passed the examination at the top level.
He became an official as Secretary Lang, and was promoted many times to Situ Donghe Jijiu and the Chief Registrar of the King of Luling.
He was known for his filial piety when he mourned his father and built a shed next to the tomb to live in. Emperor Ming ordered twenty warriors to be sent to guard the tomb.
After the period of mourning was over, he was appointed Prince Xi Ma. He was repeatedly promoted to Situ Zuoxi, Prince Zhongsheren, and Secretary Cheng.
He went out to serve as the internal history of Jian'an and served for one year. The rebel army was stationed in Jiangzhou and Ningshuo general Liu Canzhi was sent as the county guard. Jiang Bei led the officials and people to occupy the county and resist him.
When Jiankang City was pacified, Jiang Bei was convicted and could not hold an official position. He was soon pardoned and appointed as a foreign soldier to the rear army of Linchuan King.
He was repeatedly promoted to Prince You of Linchuan, Minister of Zhongshu, Prince's family minister, Minister of Huangmen, and Dazhongzheng of Nanyanzhou.
He was transferred to the position of concubine among the princes, and the Zhongzheng remained the same.
He was changed to Zhongquan Shixing Wang Changshi.
When he went out, he served as General Fubo and Internal History of Jin'an.
During his tenure, he was honest and frugal, dedicated to being generous and generous, making it convenient for his subordinate officials and the people.
Shao Ling recruited him as General Ningshuo and King Changshi of Nankang to act as agent for the affairs of the government, state and feudal country.
Soon after, he was transferred to Taiwei, Prince Changshi of Linchuan, and was appointed Shangshu Libulang, General on the Right.
Jiang Bei is upright, elegant and has character.
Pushe Xu Mian was proud of his power, and everyone in power respected him as a senior. Only Jiang Bei and Wang Gui treated him with equal courtesy and did not condescend to him.
summary: Cai Lu, courtesy name Jingjie, was the son of Xingzong. He was upright and modest. He built a shed next to his mother's tomb to live in mourning. As prefect of Wuxing, he defeated the rebel Wu Chengbo, who had an army of 20,000, beheading him in battle. He was famous for his magnanimity and simplicity in the department of selecting officials. He died at age fifty-seven.

translation:
Xu Mian asked for the marriage of his seventh son Xu Yao to Jiang Hao's daughter through Zhai Jing, Jiang He's retainer. Jiang Hao refused. Zhai Jing mentioned the matter for the second time, so Jiang Bei beat Zhai Jing with forty sticks, thus causing a conflict with Xu Mian.
He was appointed as a regular attendant on casual riding, but he did not take up the post.

He studied diligently from youth, building a two-story thatched house where he isolated himself for years of study. translation:
My grandfather, Zhongdu, was a hussar and a lieutenant of the King of Jiangxia.
When his father arrived in Tan, he was the official official of the Qi Dynasty.
When Qia was eighteen years old, he was in charge of welcoming west Cao in South Xuzhou.
When he was young, he was well-known, high-minded, alert, talented and moral.
Xie Tiao's articles were very famous at that time. When he met Dao Qia, he was very friendly and appreciative of them, and invited him to discuss them with him every day.
I often say to Dao Qia: You are not only a celebrity, but also have both civil and military talents.
Xie Tiao later served as the official of the Ministry of Civil Affairs and resigned when he arrived at Qia. Xie Peng wanted to recommend him, but he refused after observing that the world would be in chaos.
He was appointed as the Zuo Changshi of the Kingdom of Jin'an, but he refused to take up the post, so he built a house on the side of a mountain rock and lived in seclusion for several years.
Ren Fang, a Le'an native, has the ability to understand others, and is friendly with his brother Daoqi, both in the marsh and the irrigated area.
I once visited Qia in a farm house. After seeing him, I admired him and said: This man is unparalleled in the world.
So I used the etiquette of meeting a friend's parents.
In the early years of Tianjian, both Dao Zhou and Dao Gai were promoted, and Dao Qia was especially appreciated by Zhiyu. His cousin Dao Hang also had the same reputation as him.
Emperor Gaozu asked Qiu Chi, who was waiting for the imperial edict, and said: How does Daoqia compare with Daohang and Daoji?
Qiu Chi replied: He is more upright and honest than Dao Hang, and his articles are not inferior to Dao Gai's; plus he can talk clearly, it is difficult for the two of them to compare with Dao Qia.
He was immediately recruited to Qia to serve as the prince's sacrificer.
When Emperor Gaozu went to the Huaguang Hall, Shao Ling went to Xia, and Dao Hang, Xiao Chen, and Ren Fang served him at a banquet. He composed twenty poems in rhyme, and the diction of Dao Qia was the most skillful. He also gave him twenty pieces of silk.
Emperor Gaozu said to Ren Fang: The Dao brothers can be called talented men.
Ren Fang replied: "My ministers often discuss privately that Song Dynasty will get military generals and Liang Liang will get literati."
In the second year, he was transferred to Chief Situ and was on duty in Shao Province. Shao ordered him to copy the scriptures.
In the fifth year, he was transferred to the position of Zhonglang in Shangshu Palace.
The uncles and brothers who came together occupied this position one after another, and people at that time thought they were very honored.
In the seventh year, he was transferred to the crown prince Zhongsheren, and he and his concubine Lu Chui were in charge of the records of the East Palace respectively.
Soon he served as an attendant, and the province soon appointed two bachelors, who came to serve as candidates.
In the ninth year, he was transferred to Dr. Guozi and was ordered to write the "Taixue Monument".
In the twelfth year, he went out to serve as the internal history of Linchuan and became a competent official in the county.
In the fourteenth year, he came to Beijing and served as the prince's family minister. He was transferred to serve as the minister of Huangmen and as a doctor of Guozi.
In the 16th year, he was transferred to the crown prince's concubine.
In the first year of ordinary life, he served as a doctor concurrently with his official position.
Not long after, when he joined the Ministry of Finance and served as a minister, he found it impossible to entrust him with anything.
Soon he was transferred to Yuanwai Sanqi Changshi, and also served as a doctor. He resigned due to the death of his mother.
In the fifth year, he served as the concubine of the crown prince and concurrently as the captain of the infantry school. Before taking office, he was subsequently transferred to serve as the Minister of Huangmen and concurrently as Zuocheng of the Minister. He never avoided noble relatives in his corrections, and bribery to the Minister of Ministers was not feasible.
At that time, the emperor wanted to go on an expedition in person, and the etiquette of the army and the country was mostly formulated through consultation.
In the sixth year, he was transferred to the position of censor Zhongcheng. He had no scruples in impeachment and picketing, and was known as strong and upright. He was punished at that time.
Demoted due to official duties, but still in his position.
According to the old system, Zhongcheng could not enter the Shangshu's residence. Daoqia's elder brother Guiji served as Zuomin Shangshu. Daoqia cited the clause that relatives should not interfere and sent it to the Shangshu Province for a detailed decision.
Zuo Cheng Xiao Ziyun suggested that he should be allowed to enter Gai's official office because their brothers had always been loyal and did not distinguish between them.
In the seventh year, he went out to serve as General Zhenwei, Yunhui Chief Shi, and Xunyang Prefect.
In the first year of Datong, he died in the county at the age of fifty-one.
A posthumous gift to the attendant.
Mi's nickname is Li Zi.
summary: Dao Qia, styled Maoyi, was from Pengcheng. At eighteen, he began his official career. Known for his talent and moral character, he impressed Xie Tiao, who praised his civil and military abilities. When offered a position by Xie Peng, he declined, foreseeing chaos in the realm, and built a secluded mountain dwelling. Emperor Gaozu recognized his talents, and he held numerous positions including prince's sacrificer, chief of staff, and censor Zhongcheng. He was known for his integrity, refusing bribes and correcting wrongs without fear of nobles. He died at fifty-one while serving as Xunyang Prefect.

translation:
In the fifteenth year of Tianjian, he went out to serve as Chijie, supervising the military affairs of Huaihe River, general of expedition, and governor of Northern Yanzhou.
In the second year of the ordinary year, he was recruited to serve as the crown prince's right guard, and was granted the title of Shizhong, and was transferred to the post of censor Zhongcheng.
Due to official duties, he was demoted to Huangmen Shilang and Sinongqing.
In the fourth year, he was transferred to the rank of regular servant of Sanqi, and concurrently served as the chief minister of Qingzhou and Jizhou.
A new bachelor was established in Shu Palace, and Shan Bin was appointed to take charge of it. Soon, he also served as the emperor's wine minister with his own position.
At first, Shanbin was in the prefecture, and the Pinglu County under his jurisdiction had a bad harvest. Yebin started to release grain from the warehouse to help the people. Later, the governor inspected the official office of the prefecture and lost the account books. He thought it was due to Shanbin's losses and omissions. The relevant departments investigated the responsibility and confiscated Shanbin's house and transferred it to the government. Shanbin remained silent and did not appeal for himself, and bought another land to build a house.
Prince Zhaoming heard that Shanbin could not complete the house, so he ordered: Although Ming Jijiu went out to control Dazhou, he held great power to help people achieve things, inserted gold ornaments and pulled purple ribbons, but his hands were always empty.
I heard that the construction of the house has not been completed, so I am offering a meager subsidy.
He also sent a poem saying: Ping Zhong has been called Qiqi since ancient times, and Yi Wu used to be good at good names.
Beautiful laws establish wise people, and the Eastern Qin Dynasty originally had many scholars.
The houses are not built next to the road, but the houses are placed in Quy Nhon.
Geng Sang has a successor, and it is easy to compare with him today.
Those who will come to live in seclusion in the countryside will attract scholars from the Five Classics.
Shanbin has a loyal and honest character. His family once lacked funds and sold the cow he rode.
After withdrawing the money after the sale, he said to the buyer: The cow had suffered from leaky hoof, and it has been cured for a long time after treatment. I am afraid that if it relapses in the future, I will have to tell him.
The buyer immediately recovered the money Shanbin had withdrawn.
After the hermit Ruan Xiaoxu heard about it, he sighed and said: This passage is enough to make people return to simplicity and curb the superficial trend.
Five years later, he served as Doctor of the Imperial College again, and continued to serve as a regular minister and Zhongzheng.
In the year of 1999, he was appointed as a leaver in his own capacity and temporarily acted as an agent for the affairs of Northern Yanzhou.
He died in the first year of La Datong at the age of eighty-five.
Shao Ling gave posthumously to Shi Zhong and General Xinwei.
The name is proton.
Prince Zhaoming held a funeral for him, donated 100,000 yuan in money and 100 bolts of cloth, and sent Wang Yi, the funeral director, to supervise the arrangements for the funeral.
He also gave an order to Yin Yun, the former Situ Zuochang, saying: The envoy from Northern Yanzhou arrived and Lang Jubi passed away suddenly. I felt sad when I heard about it.
This wise man was well versed in Confucianism and determined to investigate ancient affairs. He was meek, loyal, honest, peaceful, elegant and broad.
It has been more than twenty years since he taught the scriptures.
summary: Mingshan Bin, styled Xiaoruo, was from Pingyuan. His father lived in seclusion. From age seven, Shan Bin could discuss right and wrong, and by thirteen mastered classical texts. He held various academic and official positions, including the first Doctor of the Five Classics. As governor, he once released grain to aid famine victims without proper documentation, losing his house when audited, yet he did not appeal. Prince Zhaoming praised his virtue and provided assistance. He authored 224 volumes of "Notes on Ji Li" and other works, dying at eighty-five.

translation:
As for the fact that he does not flatter people in his dealings with those in high positions, he advises loyally and does not show outward signs, it comes from his heart, and he probably has a deep foundation.
He took charge of the post of governor, and his actions were appropriate and his words had the purpose. Unexpectedly, he passed away for a long time, which was far from the past.
Reminiscing about his conversation becomes a thread of sadness, how can it be calmed down?
The relationship between the past and the past should be sour and sad.
Ye Xuan has been an academic official for a long time and is very helpful in teaching. However, he has a thorough personality, welcomes students, and gets close to them. Everyone likes him.
He wrote 224 volumes of "Notes on Ji Li", 20 volumes of "Etiquette", and 15 volumes of "The Classic of Filial Piety and Funeral Dress".
His son Zhen, also named Xingdao, also inherited his father's studies.
He successively served as a doctor of Taixue, Prince Sheren, Shangshu Ancestral Minister, and Yuyao Ling.
Yin Jun, whose courtesy name was Jihe, was from Changping, County Chen.
He is the eighth generation grandson of Jin Qiao Taichang Chenlie.
His father, Yin He, was talented and eloquent. He was famous throughout the world and served successively as Situ and Zhonglang.
Yin Shu married Wang Huan's daughter.
Wang Lei served as the governor of Zhenbei and the general of Zhenbei, so he reported to the court and appointed Zhou Yao as the chief historian of Zhenbei and the governor of Henan.
Wang Huan was killed, and Wu Yao was killed together.
Wu Man was nine years old at the time and was known for his filial piety.
When he grows up, he will be indifferent and leisurely and rarely socialize. He likes to study and is intellectually interested.
He was good at official calligraphy and became a role model at that time. Fan Nuo from Nanxiang and Renmao from Luandong all praised him and knew him.
Emperor Gaozu and Yin Chang were friends when they were young, and they married their daughter to Yin Gou, who became Princess Yongxing.
In the early years of Tianjian, he was appointed as the Commander-in-Chief of the Prince Consort, and served as Secretary Lang, Prince Sheren, Situ Chief Secretary, and Secretary Cheng.
When Yin Gou was in office, he began to compile the four books of Mi Ge and compiled a separate catalogue.
Shao also searched for calligraphy monuments in Western Province and compiled a detailed list of grades.
He was transferred to Qiaoqi to serve as Zhonglang, Zhongshulang, Prince's family order, and in charge of the palace documents and records.
Soon after, he was transferred to serve as the Minister of Huangmen, the concubine in the middle, the Minister of Libu, Situ Zuo, Changshi, and the minister.
A bachelor was appointed in the East Palace, and Yin Gou was appointed as the official.
Removal from office on official business.
He also served as the concubine, doctor of the state, and general Zuo Xiaoqi. The title of doctor remained the same.
When he went out, he served as General Mingwei and Internal History of Linchuan.
Yin Gou was weak and sick, so he closed his door and treated him in bed. However, the people were inspired by his virtues, and all the thieves fled the country.
Yin Gou once captured the leader of a robbery, but instead of torturing him, he just scolded him in a pleasant manner.
The robber leader kowtowed and begged to change, and Yin Gou ordered him to be released. Later, the man became a good person.
There was a lot of malaria in the county in the past, and it would definitely break out in summer. Since Yin Jun took office, there is no more malaria in the county.
summary: Yin Jun, styled Jihe, was from Changping. His father was killed alongside his father-in-law Wang Huan. Orphaned at nine, Yin Jun was known for filial piety. He married Princess Yongxing and held various positions including Secretary Lang and Prince Sheren. He compiled the four books of Mi Ge and catalogued calligraphy monuments. As Linchuan Internal History, he governed with virtue, causing thieves to flee. He once captured a robber leader but released him after a gentle scolding, and the man reformed. He died at forty-nine. The historian Yao Cha commented that these men, despite different positions and salaries, were all listed among famous ministers for their learning, loyalty, integrity, and filial piety.

translation:
When Prince Zhaoming heard about Lu Xiang's academic conduct, he asked his great ancestor to invite him to travel with him. He appointed the prince to wash horses, transfer him to Zhongshe, and take charge of document records.
When Lu Xiang was out to serve as governor of Yangzhou, Lu Xiang's father died while taking this position. He resolutely refused, but Emperor Gaozu did not allow it and allowed the Sima of the government to exchange official residences.
Prince Zhaoming respected the elderly. Lu Xiang's mother was nearly eighty years old. He, Xiao Chen, Fu Zhao and Lu Dai sent people to visit her every month and gave her good food and clothes.
Lu Sai's mother suddenly suffered from angina pectoris, and the prescription required three liters of corn syrup. It was the winter moon, and it was close to dusk. There was no place to search. Suddenly, an old man came to the door to sell corn syrup, and the quantity was just as prescribed. When he was about to pay, the man disappeared somewhere. At that time, he thought it was because Lu Sai's filial piety moved God.
He was repeatedly promoted to doctor of the state, crown prince's family order, and in charge of document records. He resigned due to the death of his mother.
Lu Xiang was already fifty years old, and he was sad and thin beyond etiquette. The prince was worried about him and sent messengers every day to warn and enlighten him.
When the period of mourning was over, he was appointed as the crown prince's concubine, and was also in charge of document records.
In the third year of Zhongdatong, Prince Zhaoming passed away and his officials were dismissed. The concubine Cai lived in Jinhua Palace. Lu Xiang was appointed Zhongsan doctor, infantry captain, family magistrate of Jinhua Palace, and informed of Jinhua Palace affairs.
In the sixth year, he went out to serve as the internal history of Poyang.
Before this, the people in the county used elixirs to cultivate Taoism. They once went into the mountains to collect medicines, picked up flags of five colors, and found stone seals in the ground. They felt strange in private.
Xian Yuchen and his wife didn't live in the same room before, but there were always strange weather in the place where Xian Yuchen lived, which made him feel even more magical.
In the first year of Datong, he gathered his disciples and killed Wang Jun, the magistrate of Guangjin. He claimed that he changed his reign to the first year of Shangyuan, set up officials and subordinates, and his followers deceived and tempted him. He had more than 10,000 followers.
When troops were about to be sent to attack the county town, Lu Xiang first led the people and officials to build the city and take precautions. When the bandits arrived, he defeated them in successive battles and captured Xian Yugan alive, while the rest fled and dispersed.
At that time, the magistrates of the neighboring counties of Yuzhang, Ancheng and other counties interrogated the party members who were detained in Xianyuchen, and took advantage of the opportunity to obtain property, but they could not get the truth. Some good people and their whole families were in trouble, but the upright people in Lu Xiang's county were not harmed innocently.
The people composed a ballad and said: After Xianyu was pacified, good and evil were clearly distinguished, and no one died unjustly, all because of Mr. Lu.
There were also two families, the Peng family and the Li family, who had been angry and fighting before, so they falsely accused each other. Lu Xiang called them into the inner room and did not scold them. He only persuaded and guided them with kind words. The two were grateful for the kindness and deeply regretted their mistakes. Lu Xiang then held a banquet for them and let them drink to their heart's content. After the banquet, the two returned in the same car, and they treated each other favorably.
summary: Lu Xiang, styled Shiqing, was from Wu County. His father and brother were killed during a rebellion, and he mourned beyond ritual requirements. He held positions including Yongning magistrate and served Prince Zhaoming. When his mother fell ill requiring corn syrup in winter, an old man appeared selling exactly the needed amount, then vanished—considered divine intervention. As Poyang Internal History, he suppressed a rebellion led by Xian Yu Chen, capturing him alive while protecting innocent people from false accusations. He reconciled feuding families through gentle persuasion. During Hou Jing's rebellion, the city fell and Lu Xiang fled, later dying of grief at seventy. He lived simply, avoiding music and discussions of killing for fifty years.

translation:
Changsha's successor Xiao Ye, whose courtesy name was Jingkuang, was the son of Gaozu's eldest brother Xiao Yi.
Xiao Yi was named Yuanda and had a good reputation when he was young.
He became an official and joined the army under the command of Prince Shaoling of Annan. He inherited the title of Duoxiang County Fort.
He was also moved to Prince Sheren, Xima, and King You of Jian'an.
After taking office as the Medical Administrator of Jin, within a month, the lawsuits were sorted out, everyone was calm, and he was called good governance.
Later, he was called to serve as the Minister of Zhongshu.
During the next year of Cheng's reign, Xiao Yi was awarded the title of Chijie, the governor of Liangzhou, Southern Qinzhou, Northern Qinzhou, and the military affairs of the four prefectures, the captain of Xirong, the governor of Zhuzhou and Nanqinzhou, and the champion general.
This year, the Wei army invaded Hanzhong and then surrounded Nanzheng.
Xiao Yi responded accordingly, blocked the Wei army, and killed many enemies. The Wei army then dispersed the encirclement and quietly withdrew.
Xiao Yi then sent the Di commander Yang Yuanxiu to attack Wei Chao's six garrison posts, including Licheng, Gaolan, Luogu, and Kengchi, and captured these garrison posts. The Wei people were shocked and frightened, and the border was peaceful.
Xiao Yi was promoted to the title of General of the Conqueror, granted 300 additional households in the city, and moved to the military governorship of Yizhou and Ningzhou, and the governor of Yizhou.
He was also summoned to serve as the crown prince's right guard leader, minister of official affairs, and Weiweiqing.
In the second year of Yongyuan, Uncle Pei occupied Yuzhou and rebelled. Xiao Yi was awarded the title of Chijie, general of conquering captives, supervising the military affairs of Yuzhou, governor of Yuzhou, and concurrently serving as the governor of Libao and Luzhan counties.
Soon, Pingxi General Cui Huijing invaded the capital and followed Jiangxia King Xiao Yinxuan to surround Taicheng. The Qi Dynasty was in chaos, and the emperor ordered to summon Xiao Yi.
Xiao Yi was eating at the time. When he received the order, he immediately threw away his chopsticks, stood up, and led 3,000 elite soldiers to rescue the capital.
Cui Huijing sent his son Cui Jue to resist Lu Mo. Lu Kui led his army to attack and defeated Ju Jue, and Cui Jue escaped on horseback alone.
Xiao Han's army took advantage of the victory and pursued Cui Huijing's army. Xiao Yi caught up with Cui Huijing and killed him.
Xiao Yi was awarded the title of Shizhong and Shangshu Right Servant. Before he could become an official, he was moved to Shangshu Ling and Commander-in-Chief to conquer all land and water armies. He still held the post of Chief Officer and General, and added 2,500 households in the city.
At that time, Marquis Shuhun was in court, and he was brutal and indulgent. Ru Fazhen, Wang Xinzhi and others were in charge of the government. The old ministers and generals of the previous dynasty were killed one by one by the Yi tribe. After Xiao Yi established his merits, he alone occupied a high position in the court. Deeply feared by Ru Fazhen and others, they advised Donghunhou: Xiao Yi will repeat the story of the Longchang period, and your Majesty's life is in danger.
Marquis Shuhun believed their words and wanted to kill Xiao Yi. When people close to Xiao Yi learned about this plan, they secretly prepared a boat and placed it on the riverside, and persuaded Xiao Yi to escape westward by boat.
Xiao Zhu said: Since ancient times, there has been a matter of death festival. Is there anyone who has ordered the minister to defect?
So Xiao Yi was killed.
In the first year of Qi Zhongxing's reign, he was posthumously given the titles of Shizhong, Zhongshujian and Situ.
When the Empress Dowager Xuande came to power, she gave Xiao Yi the title of Taifu.
In the first year of Tianjian, Xiao Yi was promoted as prime minister, and he was granted the title of Prince of Changsha, with the title of Xuanwu.
Presented to the Jiuqi Banner, the Emperor Luan's car, the funeral car of Yunjing, the huangzhen car cover and the flag hanging on the left side of the car scale, Yubao drums at the front and rear, two elegy parts, and a hundred swordsmen with tiger swords. The funeral was carried out completely in accordance with the style of King Anping of Jin Dynasty.
Xiao Ye was smart and alert at a young age, and his knowledge and tolerance exceeded ordinary people.
He entered the Qi Dynasty as an official and served as a scholar and prince.
After the Xuanwu Incident, he fled and hid with his two younger brothers, Xiao Zao and Xiao Xiang.
After Gaozu arrived, he joined Gaozu's army, and Gaozu appointed Lu Tomb as General Ningshuo.
In the second year of Zhongxing Dynasty, Xiao Ye was appointed as the general of Fuguo and the prefect of Nanlangxie and Qinghe counties.
In the second year of Tianjian, he attacked the king of Changsha and was called to serve as the champion general.
summary: The lives and careers of several members of the Xiao family, descendants of Gaozu, focusing on their official positions, military campaigns, and personal virtues. Xiao Yi, son of Gaozu's eldest brother, held various military and civil posts, including governor of Liangzhou. He governed various regions, focusing on recruiting people, providing relief during famines, and building schools. He recruited hermits and scholars, and when floods destroyed crops, he distributed grain for relief. He died at age forty-four, and people from four states mourned him. He was known for his kind and forgiving nature, never showing anger. He collected scriptures and employed scholars to compile works.

Zhou She was smart when he was young. Zhou Yi thought he was very strange. Before he died, he said to him: "You don't have to worry about not being rich, you just should uphold morality."
When he grew up, he was erudite and proficient in doctrine. He was good at reading books aloud, reciting articles and making arguments, with a clear tone and eloquence.
He became an official and became a doctor of Taixue in the Qi Dynasty. He was transferred to the rear army and joined the army.
During the Jianwu period, Wu Bao, a native of Wei State, returned to the south and had Confucianism. Shangshu Pushe Jiang Zhe recruited Wu Bao to teach. Zhou She visited and sat down. He was impressed by Wu Bao many times. He was strong and elegant in arts and science, so he was known as eloquent.

Transferred to Taichang Cheng.

They valued Zhou She's talent and reported it to Emperor Gaozu, recruiting Zhou Chuang and appointing him as Shangshu Temple Minister.
At that time, the country was founded, and most of the additions and subtractions of etiquette came from Zhou She.
Soon he served as a member of the Hou Army Records Office and the Moling Order.
He entered the court as Zhongshu Tongshiren, and was promoted many times to the crown prince Xi Ma, Sanqi Changshi, Zhongshu Shilang, and Hongshanqing.
At that time, Wang Liang returned home after committing a crime and no friends came to see him. Zhou She valued the old favor alone. When Wang Liang died, he personally arranged the funeral and burial for him. People at that time praised him.
He was transferred to Shangshu Libu Lang, Prince Right Guard, and Right Guard General. Although his positions were changed many times, he often stayed in the official office and rarely went home for rest. He was in charge of national history, Shaogao, etiquette, law, and military strategy.
He served the emperor at night, participated in confidential affairs, and never left his side for more than twenty years.
Zhou She has always been eloquent, talking and joking with others all day long, but he never leaked secrets in a single word. Everyone admired and admired him.
His character is frugal and simple, and his clothes, utensils, and beds are just like those of the poor among the common people.
Every time I enter the palace, even if it is a tall and gorgeous building with layers of inner rooms, the houses are full of dust after living there.
Use Ogweed as a cover and don't dispose of it if it breaks.

After the mourning period expired, he was appointed as a sergeant and an infantry captain. However, he did not take up the post. He was also transferred to the rank of standing servant and the prince's left guard.
Soon after, he was awarded the title of Regular Attendant of Sanqi and Dazhongzheng of the state, and was transferred to Prince Zhan Shi.

summary: Zhou She, courtesy name Shengyi, was from Runan'an and a descendant of Jin official Zhou Chan. His father Zhou Yi served as Vice Minister of Zhongshu in the Qi Dynasty. Zhou She was intelligent from youth, and his father advised him to uphold morality rather than worry about wealth. He grew up erudite, eloquent, and skilled in recitation and debate. He began his official career as a Doctor of Taixue in the Qi Dynasty and later held various posts. During the Jianwu period, he impressed Confucian scholar Wu Bao with his knowledge, gaining a reputation for eloquence. Wang Liang appointed him chief administrator, entrusting him with political affairs. In the Liang Dynasty, Fan Yun recommended him to Emperor Gaozu, who appointed him Shangshu Temple Minister. Zhou She contributed to the establishment of state rituals and held numerous positions, including Zhongshu Shilang and Hongshanqing. He remained loyal to Wang Liang even after Wang Liang's disgrace, personally arranging his funeral. Despite frequent role changes, he rarely rested, overseeing national history, rituals, laws, and military strategy. He served the emperor in confidential matters for over twenty years, never leaking secrets. He lived frugally, with simple clothing and dusty homes. After his mother's death, he resigned but later returned to service. In the seventh year of the Putong era, he was implicated in a letter from Wuling Prefect Bai Guo offering him a bribe and was dismissed. He died that year at age fifty-six. The emperor mourned him, granting posthumous honors and praising his integrity, knowledge, and loyalty. Zhou She left two sons, Hongyi and Hongxin.

Xu Mian, whose courtesy name was Xiuren, was a native of Tan, East China Sea.
Grandfather Changzong served as the commander of the residence of the feudal prince of the Song Dynasty and joined the army.
His father, Xu Rong, served as the Prime Minister of Nanchang.

summary: Xu Mian, courtesy name Xiuren, was from Tan, East China Sea. His father Xu Rong served as Prime Minister of Nanchang. Orphaned young, Xu Mian cultivated moral integrity early. At six, he wrote a prayer during a rainstorm, praised by elders. He grew up diligent in learning, starting as a son of the state. Wang Jian, the wine minister, praised his prime ministerial demeanor. He ranked first in exams and held various posts, including Doctor of Taixue and Shangshu Palace lieutenant. He was dismissed due to official business but later reinstated. Wang Yuanchang sought his acquaintance, but Xu Mian declined, foreseeing Wang's trouble, earning admiration for his insight. He befriended King Xuanwu of Changsha and met Emperor Gaozu in Xinlin, who valued him. After Gaozu's accession, Xu Mian served as Minister of Zhongshu and other roles, known for effective law enforcement and impeachments. In the second year of Tianjian, he became Minister of Huangmen and Libu, participating in talent selection. During a northern campaign, he worked tirelessly on military documents, often not returning home for days. In the sixth year, he became Minister of Shizhong and later Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, managing selections efficiently. He avoided discussing official matters at social gatherings, earning respect for his lack of selfishness. He served as Prince Zhan Shi and taught the "Book of Filial Piety" to Prince Zhaoming. Xu Mian reformed funeral customs, advocating for three-day burials per ancient rites, which the emperor approved. He rose to Shangshu Pushe and Zhongwei General, serving the emperor wholeheartedly. He participated in revising the Five Rites, submitting a detailed memorial in the sixth year of the Putong era, compiling 1,176 volumes of rituals. He left his descendants integrity rather than wealth, as expressed in a letter to his son Xu Song. He built a small garden for leisure, not profit. After his son Xu Qiu's death, he wrote "Reply to Guests" to express his grief. In the third year of Zhongdatong, he retired due to illness, receiving honors. He died in the first year of Datong at age seventy. The emperor mourned deeply, granting posthumous titles and gifts. Xu Mian was a prolific writer, compiling works like "Notes on Living Things" and "Huilin." His son Xu Qiu was also talented, serving as Prince Sheren and Jin'an internal history. Chen Libu Shangshu praised Xu Mian as a respected minister of the Liang Dynasty.

After Pei Sui passed the examination as a scholar, he ranked first in high school in the imperial examination and was appointed as a minister.
After Donghunhou came to the throne, Xiao Yaoguang, the king of Shi'an, was appointed as the general of Fujun and the governor of Yangzhou. He recommended Pei Sui to join the army.
Later, when Xiao Yaoguang was defeated, Pei Sui returned to Shouyang, and met the governor Pei Shuye who offered Shouyang to surrender to the Wei State. All the noble families in Yuzhou were expelled and plundered, so Pei Sui followed everyone and moved north.
