The State of Wei sent Wang Su to guard Shouyang. Pei Sui firmly requested to follow Wang Su and secretly planned to return to the south.
In the early years of Tianjian, Pei Sui escaped from Wei and returned to the Southern Dynasty. He was appointed as a consultant to the rear army and joined the army.
Pei Sui himself asked to serve on the border, so he was appointed as the general of the auxiliary country and the governor of Lujiang County.
At that time, the Wei general Lu Po led an army of 50,000 troops to suddenly attack Lujiang County. Pei Sui led his men to resist and defeated the Wei army. Pei Sui was appointed as the general of the right army.
In the fifth year, during the expedition to Shaoyangzhou, the Wei army built a long bridge across the Huaihe River to meet the river.
Pei Sui built a fortress and pushed towards Long Bridge, winning every battle. Therefore, he secretly helped build ships without chimneys.
It was raining heavily and the water level of the Huaihe River surged. Pei Sui and his men took a ship and went straight to the long bridge. The Wei army was shocked and defeated. Pei Sui and others took advantage of the victory to pursue and defeated the Wei army.
Pei Sui then conquered Yangshi City and killed the city lord Yuan Kang.
He also captured Huoqiu City and beheaded the city lord Ning Yongren.
After that, Xiaoxian was pacified and Hefei was captured.
Pei Sui was granted the title of Son of Yiling County due to his meritorious service, and was granted the title of 300 households in the town.
He was moved to the post of Champion Changshi and Grand Administrator of Guangling County.
Pei Sui and his fellow villagers entered Wei Wu Temple and discussed the emperor's achievements.
His wife's nephew Wang Zhuanzhi secretly reported to Emperor Gaozu that Pei Sui had told many lies and showed signs of being disloyal to the monarch.
Therefore, Pei Sui was demoted and appointed as the governor of Shi'an County.
Pei Sui was determined to make meritorious service on the border and was unwilling to go to a place that was too quiet, so he wrote a letter to Lu Sengzhen saying: In the past, Ruan Xian and Yan Yan had the sigh of "Two Shi". My talents are not as good as those of the ancients. Now it is "Third Shi". This is not my wish. What should I do?
Before reaching Shi'an County, the Wei army happened to attack Suyu, and Emperor Shao ordered Pei Sui to go and resist the Wei army.
Pei Sui marched to Zhidu, and the Wei army retreated.
Pei Sui moved to the right army to consult and join the army, and was the Sima of Yunhui Mansion of King Yuzhang, and led his troops to help guard Stone City.
Later, he served as the governor of Tongling County. He cultivated and farmed fields, which was convenient for both the public and private parties.
He was also moved to the post of guerrilla general Zhu Yi Zhihe and was on duty in the palace province.
Soon, he was moved to the post of General Jiajie, Mingwei General, Xirong Xiaowei, and governor of Beiliang Prefecture and Qinzhou Prefecture.
He also created thousands of hectares of farmland and filled granaries with grain, which made it possible to save or stop transportation to the border, and both the army and the people were able to stabilize. So they sent more than a thousand pieces of silk one after another, and Pei Sui calmly said: "You shouldn't be like this, but I can't go against your wishes."
So, he only symbolically accepted two pieces of silk.
After returning to the court, he was appointed to Shizhong, General Yunqi, and General Zhu Yizhihe, and was moved to the rank of Great Craftsman.
In the second year of ordinary life, Yizhou governor Wen Seng Mingxian rebelled against Yizhou and defected to Wei, and the Wei army came to support him.
The emperor appointed Pei Sui as General Jiajie and Xinwu to lead the army to attack the Wei army.
Pei Sui penetrated deep into the territory of the Wei State and borrowed roads from the border towns to catch him by surprise. The Yizhou Governor Qian Zhou deployed by the Wei State occupied Shanggong Maggot. He defeated Lao Hua and then surrounded Fucheng. Feng Shou tied his hands behind his back and asked for surrender, and Yizhou was pacified.
Pei Sui was awarded the title of Controller, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Northern Xuzhou, General Xinwu, and Governor of Northern Xuzhou. Before he could take office, he was moved to Governor of Military Affairs of Yuzhou, Northern Yuzhou, and Huozhou, and Governor of Yuzhou, and was based in Hefei.
Four years later, Pei Suijin was awarded the title of General Xuanyi.
In the year of sending, the Liang Dynasty army was preparing for the Northern Expedition. Pei Sui was appointed as the governor to conquer various military forces. He led three thousand cavalry to attack Shouyang first.
In the ninth month of Renxu, the troops arrived in Shouyang overnight, attacked the outer city of Shouyang, killed the soldiers guarding the gate and entered the inner city. Xiang fought nine rounds in one day. Cai Xiucheng, the rear army, did not arrive in time because he was lost. Pei Sui withdrew and returned to the army because of the lack of support.
In Qianxiang, Pei Sui once again reorganized the army and gathered soldiers. Several generals were ordered to use different clothing colors to distinguish themselves from each other.
Pei Sui himself led the cavalry in yellow robes and attacked Diqiu, Zongcheng, Lijiang and other cities first, but they were all captured.
Ancheng, Matou, Shaling and other garrisons were massacred.
In the winter of the next year, construction of Shaopei began.
The next year, he captured Xincai County of Wei State and occupied the territory as far as Zhengcheng. People from Ru River and Ying River responded everywhere.
summary: Pei Sui, styled Yuanming, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong and a descendant of Pei Chuo, a Wei Dynasty governor. His grandfather Pei Shousun served as a former army commander under Emperor Wu of the Song Dynasty, and his father Pei Zhongmu was a general of cavalry. Pei Sui could write essays by age ten and was skilled in the *Zuo Shi Chun Qiu*. During the early Jianwu era of the Southern Qi Dynasty, Governor Xiao Yaochang recommended him as a state government governor. Xiao erected a monument at Bagongshan Temple in Shouyang County and commissioned Pei Sui to write the inscription, which was highly praised. After passing the imperial examination with top honors, Pei Sui was appointed as a minister. When Donghunhou ascended the throne, Xiao Yaoguang, the King of Shi'an, recommended Pei Sui as an army adjutant. After Xiao Yaoguang's defeat, Pei Sui returned to Shouyang, where Governor Pei Shuye surrendered to the Wei State. Pei Sui was forced to move north, but Emperor Xuanwu of Wei valued him and appointed him as Situ, Zhongshu Lang, and Prefect of Wei County. Pei Sui secretly planned to return south and, during the early Tianjian era of the Liang Dynasty, escaped from Wei. He was appointed as a consultant to the rear army and later requested to serve on the border, becoming General of the Auxiliary Country and Governor of Lujiang County. When Wei General Lu Po attacked Lujiang with 50,000 troops, Pei Sui defeated him and was promoted to General of the Right Army. In the fifth year, during the expedition to Shaoyangzhou, Pei Sui built fortresses and won every battle against the Wei army's long bridge across the Huaihe River. Taking advantage of heavy rain and rising water levels, he led a shipborne assault on the bridge, defeating the Wei army. He then conquered Yangshi City, killing City Lord Yuan Kang, and captured Huoqiu City, beheading City Lord Ning Yongren. He also pacified Xiaoxian and captured Hefei. For his merits, Pei Sui was granted the title of Son of Yiling County with 300 households. He was later moved to Champion Changshi and Grand Administrator of Guangling County. After discussing the emperor's achievements in Wei Wu Temple, his wife's nephew Wang Zhuanzhi falsely reported him for disloyalty, leading to his demotion as Governor of Shi'an County. Determined to serve on the border, Pei Sui wrote to Lu Sengzhen, lamenting his situation as "Third Shi." Before reaching Shi'an, the Wei army attacked Suyu, and Pei Sui was ordered to resist, causing the Wei army to retreat. He later served as Governor of Tongling County, where he cultivated farmland for public and private benefit. He was eventually appointed as General Jiajie, Mingwei General, Xirong Xiaowei, and Governor of Beiliang and Qinzhou Prefectures, creating thousands of hectares of farmland and stabilizing the border. After returning to court, he held various high-ranking positions. In the second year of the ordinary era, Yizhou Governor Wen Sengming rebelled and defected to Wei. Pei Sui led an army to attack, penetrating deep into Wei territory and surprising the enemy. He defeated the Wei-appointed Yizhou Governor Qian Zhou, pacifying Yizhou. He was awarded the title of Controller and Governor of Northern Xuzhou, later moving to Governor of Yuzhou, Northern Yuzhou, and Huozhou, based in Hefei. Four years later, he was promoted to General Xuanyi. During the Liang Dynasty's Northern Expedition, Pei Sui led 3,000 cavalry to attack Shouyang, fighting nine rounds in one day but withdrawing due to lack of support. He later reorganized his army, captured several cities, and massacred garrisons. In the following years, he captured Xincai County and expanded Liang territory. When Wei generals Chang Sun Zhi and Wang Yuanchen led 50,000 troops to challenge, Pei Sui used a feigned retreat to ambush and defeat them, beheading over 10,000. Chang Sun Zhi fled and held the city. In May of the same year, Pei Sui died in the military camp. He was posthumously given the title of Shizhong and Zuowei General, promoted to Marquis, and granted 700 households. His posthumous name was Lie.

translation:
Wei's generals guarding Shouyang, Chang Sun Zhi, and Wang Yuanchen of Hejian led an army of 50,000 people and came out of the city to challenge. Pei Sui led four generals to divide into four wings to wait for the Wei army. He ordered General Li Zulian to pretend to escape and lure Chang Sun Zhi. Chang Sun Zhi led all his troops to chase Li Zulian. During the attack, Pei Sui's ambushed four-wing troops were dispatched one after another, and the Wei army was severely defeated.
More than 10,000 people were beheaded.
Changsun Zhi and others ran for their lives. After returning to the city, they closed the city gate and held on, not daring to go out to fight again.
In May of the same year, Pei Sui died in the military camp.
He was forced to be given the title of Shizhong and Zuowei General, and he was given a propaganda department. He was promoted to the title of Marquis and added 700 households.
Mi Hao Lie.
Pei Sui was usually taciturn, unsmiling, deep-thinking, and strategic. He was tolerant and open-minded in politics and could win the heartfelt support of the soldiers.
He was upright and dignified, and the officers and officers respected him, and few dared to break the law.
After his death, all the people in Huaihe and Danshuijian shed tears. They believed that if Pei Sui had not died, Luoyang would not have been captured.
Pei Sui's son Pei Zhili, named Ziyi, was born in the middle of the imperial family. He was appointed as King Shaoling's constant servant of the left side of the country and Xinweixing joined the army.
When King Shaoling was appointed governor of Nanyan Prefecture, Pei Zhili was appointed Changliu to join the army. However, he did not take up the post. He still stayed in Suwei and was appointed as General Zhihe.
When his father passed away in the period of mourning, he assumed his father's title and requested to follow the army to conquer Shouyang. He was appointed General Yunhui and moved to the position of regular servant of Sanqi.
He also attacked Guangling City of Wei State and pacified the city of Weizuo. He was awarded the title of General Xinwu, Governor of Western Yuzhou, General Qingche, Minister of Huangmen, and was moved to Sima of King Xuanxu of the Chinese Army.
Soon he was appointed as the governor of the military affairs of Xuzhou, Renzhou and Suizhou in the north, General Xinwu, and the governor of Jiuzhimaggot.
Later, he was recruited to serve as the prince's left guard, concurrently as the Weiwei Qing, and then as the Shaofu Qing.
After Pei Zhishan died, Mi was named Zhuang.
His son Pei Zheng, during the Chengsheng period, was appointed as the Minister of Huangmen.
After the fall of Siduo, he entered Liwei as usual.
Pei Zhigao, also known as Rushan, was the son of Pei Sui's elder brother, Pei Mao, a doctor in Zhongsan.
When he first entered the officialdom, he served as a state official and Xindu county magistrate. At the invitation of the court, he moved to join the army.
Pei Zhigao read a lot of books. When he was young, he thought that his will and spirit were great. He often followed his uncle Pei Liao on his expeditions to the east and west. He made meritorious deeds wherever he went. He was highly regarded by Pei Sui, who entrusted him with all military and government affairs.
During the Battle of Shouyang, Pei Sui died in the military camp. Pei Zhigao was subordinate to Xiahou Kui and pacified Shouyang. He was awarded the title of Changshi of Yuzhang in Pingbei and the prefect of Liangjun. He was named the male of the capital county and had 250 households in the city.
summary: Pei Sui was taciturn, deep-thinking, and strategic. He was tolerant in politics and won the soldiers' hearts. After his death, people in the Huaihe and Danshui regions mourned, believing that if he had not died, Luoyang would have been captured. His son Pei Zhili succeeded him, serving in various military and governmental roles. Pei Zhili's son Pei Zheng served as Minister of Huangmen. Pei Zhigao, Pei Sui's nephew, was a learned man who followed Pei Sui on expeditions and was highly regarded. He pacified Shouyang and was awarded titles. During the Hou Jing Rebellion, Pei Zhigao led troops to rescue the capital. He later served under Emperor Yuan of Liang and died at age seventy-three. His son Pei Ji fought and died when the Western Wei captured Jiangling. Pei Zhiping, Pei Zhigao's younger brother, also followed Pei Sui on expeditions and was named Dutinghou. He resisted Hou Jing and held various posts. Pei Zhiheng, another younger brother, was initially indulgent but later reclaimed wasteland and became wealthy. He served under Prince Xiao Gang and resisted Hou Jing, eventually dying in battle at age forty-one. He was posthumously given the title of Shizhong and Sikong Gong.

translation:
When Xiao Gang, Taizong of Liang Dynasty, was still the prince, he heard about Pei Zhiheng and invited him to the capital. He was made a regular servant of the King of Hedong, the commander of the Zhidian Palace, and the general of Zhihe.
During Hou Jing's rebellion, Pei Zhiheng served as General Zhenwei, attached to Poyang King Xiao Fan, and joined him in the crusade against Hou Jing.
After Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze River, Pei Zhiheng and Xiao Fan's eldest son Xiao Si returned to Beijing for reinforcements.
They crossed the Huaihe River in a company and occupied Dongcheng.
After Kyoto was captured, Pei Zhiheng retreated back to Hefei, and together with Xiao Fan went upriver to Huancheng.
Hou Jing sent Ren Yue upriver to attack Jinxi, and Xiao Fan ordered Pei Zhiheng to go downstream to rescue him. Before reaching the destination, Xiao Fan died and Pei Zhiheng returned.
At that time, Xunyang King Xiao Daxin was in Jiangzhou. Xiao Fan's deputy general Mei Sili secretly invited Lu Quzu to attack. The tomb owner killed Chuang Moli and then resisted Xiao Daxin.
Xiao Daxin offered Jiangzhou to surrender to Hou Jing.
Pei Zhiheng led his troops and surrendered to Emperor Liang Yuan together with his brother Pei Zhigao. In accordance with the emperor's will, he was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi, a minister of Tingwei, and the internal history of Hedong County.
He also followed Wang Sengbian to resist Hou Jing in Baling. After Hou Jing retreated, Pei Zhi was moved to the post of Chijie, General Pingbei, Governor of Shuxuzhou, and Central Protector. He was named Qiongkong Fort and had a settlement of 3,000 households.
He also followed Wang Zhipan to pursue Zhuijing and pinged Ying, Lu, Jiang, Jin and other states. Pei Zhiheng always served as the vanguard and charged into the battle.
At the stone place, Jing was defeated and Jing ran away to the east. Monk Bianyi ordered Tomb Zhiheng and Siqi to enter the imperial wall to guard.
Later, Duiqu relied on his wings to rebel, and Tomb Zhangzhiheng followed Wang Sengbian to the south to attack Lu Na.
He killed Lu Na's general Li Xianming on the battlefield, thus quelling the Japanese rebellion.
Pei Zhiheng also defeated King Yawuling at Xikou.
After he came back, he was appointed as the prefect of Wuxing County and made a hundred quilts to realize his original wish.
Later, Jiangling was captured, and the Southern Qi Dynasty sent Gao Huan, the king of Shangdang, to support Marquis Zhenyang in attacking Shuguan. Xiao Fangzhi, king of Jin'an, followed the emperor's will and appointed Pei Zhiheng as envoy Chijie, general Zhenbei, governor of Xuzhou, and governor of the army. He was also sent to the Advocacy Department to go out of the capital to guard Qicheng.
Pei Zhiheng had not yet built the barricades of the military camp, but the Southern Qi army had already arrived. Most of the soldiers in Pei Zhiheng's team died in the battle, and their arrows were exhausted. Pei Zhiheng also died on the battlefield at the age of forty-one.
He was posthumously given the title of Shizhong and Sikong Gong, with the nickname Zhongzhuang.
He was succeeded by his son Xiao Fengbao.
Xiahou Dan, named Shilong, was the eldest son of the chariot general Xiahou Xiang.
In the early years of the Southern Qi Dynasty, Xia Houzhi left home to become an official and became an imperial minister.
At the end of the Yongyuan Dynasty, Xiahou Xiang was appointed Sima of King Nankang of Xizhonglang. He followed the palace to guard Jingzhou, while Xiahou stayed in the capital and served as the commander-in-chief of Shuhunhou.
During Cui Huijing's rebellion, Xiahou Xuan was awarded the title of General of Valiant Cavalry for his service in protecting the emperor.
When Emperor Gaozu raised a righteous army, Xia Houxiang and Chief Shi Xiao Yingzhou negotiated and jointly raised the righteous flag. They secretly sent messengers to Kyoto to welcome Xiahou Zhi. Xiahou Zhi carried a warrant from Queen Xuande and ordered King Nankang to compile the throne to inherit the emperor's rule.
After Jiankang City was pacified, Xia Houzhi was appointed Shangshu Libulang, and soon moved to the position of Shizhong. He dedicated the emperor's jade seal to Gaozu.
In the first year of Tianjian, Xia Houzhi served as the prefect of Xuancheng County.
summary: Xiahou Dan, styled Shilong, was the eldest son of Chariot General Xiahou Xiang. He began his official career in the Southern Qi Dynasty and served as an imperial minister. During Cui Huijing's rebellion, he was awarded General of Valiant Cavalry for protecting the emperor. When Emperor Gaozu raised an army, Xiahou Xiang and Xiao Yingzhou raised the righteous flag, and Xiahou Dan carried a warrant from Queen Xuande to order King Nankang to compile the throne. After Jiankang City was pacified, he served as Shangshu Libulang and later Shizhong, dedicating the emperor's jade seal to Gaozu. In the first year of Tianjian, he served as Prefect of Xuancheng County and later as a regular servant of Sanqi and General of Youxiaoqi. After his father's death, he observed mourning rites and gave away his inheritance to his younger brothers. In the eighth year, he was appointed as Chijie, supervising Sizhou's military affairs, and Governor of Sizhou. After the mourning period, he was granted the title of Duke of Fengcheng County. Xiahou Dan was dignified and helpful, favored by border people. He returned to court in the twelfth year and held various high-ranking positions, including Duguan Shangshu and General Shizhong. He served as Governor of Wuxing County, where he implemented benevolent policies, earning statues and stone tablets from the people. In the third year of the ordinary era, he was summoned as a regular servant of Sanqi and General of Youxiaoqi. He was dismissed due to official affairs but later reinstated.

translation:
Soon he was called to serve as a regular servant of Sanqi and concurrently as a general of Youxiaoqi.
In the sixth year, he served as the Changshi of King Shixing of Pingxi and the Grand Administrator of Nanjun. He was relieved of his duties due to the death of his father.
During the mourning period, he fully complied with the etiquette. He built a thatched shed next to his father's grave and lived in Baomian. He gave away all the property left by his father to his younger brothers.
In the eighth year, Xia Houzhi was appointed as Chijie, supervising the military affairs of Sizhou, general Xinwu, governor of Sizhou, and concurrently as the prefect of Anlu County.
After the mourning period expired, he was granted the title of Duke of Fengcheng County.
Xiahou Zhi was very dignified and helpful in his official position in the state, and he was favored by the people on the border.
In the twelfth year, he returned to the court with his original title, was awarded the title of Duguan Shangshu, and was transferred to General Shizhong and Youwei, and concurrently served as Yuzhou Dazhongzheng.
In the fifteenth year, he served as General Xinwu, Changshi of Anxi, and Grand Administrator of Jiangxia County.
In the seventeenth year, he was summoned to serve as a regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi and the prince's right guard. He was moved to the left guard general and concurrently served as the former army general.
Soon he served as General Mingwei and Grand Administrator of Wuxing County.
He also implemented benevolent policies in his position as county governor. The officials and people in the county gave him a statue and set up stone tablets to praise his virtues.
In ordinary three years, he was summoned to serve as a regular servant of Sanqi and concurrently as a general of Youxiaoqi. He was transferred to the position of Taifuqing, and his position as a regular servant remained the same.
He was dismissed from office due to official affairs. Soon after, the emperor issued a special order to reinstate him.
Five years later, he was transferred to the Central Guards Army.
In the sixth year of the Liang Dynasty's large-scale Northern Expedition, he first sent Pei Sui, the governor of Yuzhou, to lead Zhan Sengzhi, the governor of Qiaozhou, Ming Shaoshi, the prefect of Liyang County, Yu Hong, the prefect of Nanqiao County, and Zhang Cheng, the prefect of Jinxi County. These people were all talented generals in the world. They attacked Shouyang City from the south road, but Pei Sui died before they could capture it.
He appointed Xia Houzhi as the envoy to hold the festival, and rode forward to replace Pei Sui. He fought with the Wei generals Hejian Wang Yuanchen and Linhuai Wang Yuanor. He fought frequently and won every time.
Soon, the emperor issued a secret order for them to return to Fei so that the soldiers and horses could rest and wait until the weir was built before marching.
In the summer of the seventh year, the water in the Huaihe River dike was so heavy that the city of Shouyang was about to be submerged. Emperor Gaozu sent the Northern Army Yuanshu to lead Peng Zhousun, Chen Qingzhi and others to gradually advance.
The Soviet army built city walls along both sides of Danba Cheng and rushed out from behind the Xia royal army. Xiahou Zhiyu Zhan Sengzhi returned to attack and defeated the Wei army.
They also attacked Lijing, and Liang Zhenwei's general Wei Fang came from the North Road to join Xiahou's direct troops.
After the two armies joined together, wherever they went, all Wei troops surrendered and the city was captured.
A total of fifty-two cities surrendered, and 75,000 men and women were captured, with rice and 200,000 stones.
The emperor issued an edict to establish Qiongcong in Shouyang Dynasty according to the system of the previous dynasty, and changed Hedanyan to Muliaochuan. He appointed Emperor Xiabao as envoy Chijie, governor of Yuzhou and the military affairs of the five states along the Huaihe River, Huozhou, Yizhou, and Yuchu, and general Yunhui, Suiye, and Luqiongye.
The Shouchun area had long been devastated by war, and most of the people were dispersed. Xiahou Zhi implemented the policy of mitigating penalties and lowering taxes, allowing the people to work hard on farming and save themselves from labor. Soon, the people's household registration funds expanded to the original scale.
In the second year of Datong, Xia Shi Huangjin was titled General Pingbei.
Three years later, he died in office in the state town.
When Emperor Wu of Liang, the founder of the family, heard the bad news, he wore plain clothes to mourn on that day and posthumously awarded him the title of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
The name of Mi is Xiang.
summary: In the sixth year of the Liang Dynasty's Northern Expedition, Pei Sui died while attacking Shouyang. Xiahou Dan replaced him and fought Wei generals, winning every battle. In the seventh year, the Huaihe River dike caused flooding, and Xiahou Dan, along with Zhan Sengzhi, defeated the Wei army. They attacked Lijing, and Wei Fang joined from the North Road. Together, they captured 52 cities, taking 75,000 prisoners and 200,000 shi of rice. Xiahou Dan was appointed as Governor of Yuzhou and the five states along the Huaihe River. He implemented policies to reduce penalties and taxes, allowing the people to prosper. In the second year of Datong, he was titled General Pingbei. He died in office three years later, and Emperor Wu of Liang mourned him, posthumously awarding him General of Chariots and Cavalry. His posthumous name was Xiang. The people petitioned to build a temple for him. Xiahou Dan was personable, generous, and well-read. He was frugal but loved music in his later years, keeping geishas. He had two sons, Xiahou Yi and Xiahou Sun, both of whom died in the Hou Jing Rebellion.

translation:
In the eighth year, the emperor ordered Xiahou Kui to lead Zhuangwu General Pei Zhili and Zhihe General Ren Sizu from Yiyang Road to attack the three passes of Pingping, Muling and Yinshan, and finally captured these three passes.
At this time, Zhan Sengzhi, the governor of Qiaozhou, surrounded Yuan Qinghe, the governor of Yuzhou, Shu State, in Guangling, and entered its outer city.
Wei general Yuan Haobo led his army to rescue. Zhan Sengzhi met the Wei army and defeated the team. Xiahou Kui came from Wuyang to join Zhan Sengzhi and cut off the Wei army's retreat.
Yuan Qinghe built a fence in the city to strengthen his defense facilities. When Xiahou Kui arrived, Yuan Qinghe asked for surrender.
Xiahou Kui wanted to give the credit to Zhan Sengzhi. Zhan Sengzhi said: Yuan Qinghe wants to surrender to you, but is not willing to surrender to me, Sengzhi. If I accept his surrender today, it will definitely be against his will; and I, Sengzhi, command a ragtag group of people recruited and cannot command the surrendering army according to the law.
You have always been very strict in managing the army. No one dares to disobey orders. It is most appropriate for you to accept surrender and surrender.
Therefore, Xia Houkui climbed up the city wall, pulled down the flags of the Wei army, and raised the banners and drums of the Liang Dynasty army. No one dared to act rashly. Yuan Qinghe rectified his troops and left the city, and no one in the army engaged in secret activities.
The total number of men and women who surrendered was more than 40,000, and they had 600,000 hu of millet, and the rest of the items were roughly the same.
After Yuan Xianbo heard the news, he ran away overnight. The Liang Dynasty army pursued him closely, capturing more than 20,000 people alive and killing countless others.
The emperor ordered Zhan Sengzhi to take charge of Yuzhou and guard Guangling.
Xiahou Kui led the army to station in Anyang.
Xiahou Kui sent his generals to massacre Chu City and captured all the troops. From then on, the North Road of Yiyang was cut off from the Wei State.
In the second year of Datong, Wei Yuan Yuanda, the governor of Yingzhou, requested to surrender to the Liang Dynasty. Emperor Wu of Liang ordered Yuanshu, the governor of Yingzhou, to greet Yuan Yuanda. Xiahou Kui also came from Chu City to join him, so he stayed in the county to guard.
The emperor ordered Wei Ying Prefecture to be changed to Beisi Prefecture, and appointed Xiahou Kui as the governor of Beisi Prefecture and to supervise Si Prefecture.
In the third year, he was transferred to the envoy Chijie and was granted the title of General Renwei. He was granted the title of Marquis of Baocheng County with a settlement of 1,500 households.
In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was recruited as a right-guard general, but resigned due to the death of his biological mother.
At that time, Liu Ming, the governor of Southern Yanzhou of Wei State, surrendered to the Liang Dynasty with Qiao City. The emperor ordered to send General Yuan Shu of Zhenbei to lead the army to respond. He appointed Xiahou Kui as General Yunhui to act according to the opportunity and crusade against the north.
Soon, Xia Houkui was appointed as the envoy Chijie, supervising the military affairs of southern Yuzhou, and the governor of southern Yuzhou.
In the sixth year, he was transferred to the envoy Chijie, in charge of the military affairs of the seven states of Yuzhou, Huaizhou, Chenzhou, Banzhou, Jianzhou, Huozhou and Yizhou, and the governor of Yuzhou.
Yuzhou had been invaded by wars for many years, and most people were unemployed. Xia Houkui led his troops to build a dike in Canngling, irrigated more than a thousand hectares of fields with water, and harvested more than one million shi of millet a year later, which was used as a reserve and to provide for poor families. The people in the territory relied on him to survive.
Xiahou Kui's elder brother Xia Houzhi had previously held this official position, and now Xiahou Kui is in this position again.
Both brothers left benevolence to the village, and the common people sang songs to praise them: "I have a state, and I often stay in Xiahou; the former brother and the latter brother are good administrators."
Xia Houkui served as an official in the state for seven years. He made great achievements and gained a good reputation. People near and far relied on him.
There were a total of 10,000 troops and 2,000 horses. These people were all elite soldiers and generals who were good at riding and shooting. It became a grand event at that time.
summary: Xiahou Kui, styled Ji Long, was Xiahou Dan's younger brother. He began his official career in the Southern Qi Dynasty and served in various posts. After his father's death, he mourned and later took charge of building Tai Chi Hall. He served as an adjutant to Pei Sui during the expedition against Zhanye. He replaced his brother as Governor of Yuxing and later served as Governor of Sizhou. In the eighth year, he led an attack on the three passes of Pingping, Muling, and Yinshan, capturing them. He joined Zhan Sengzhi to cut off the Wei army's retreat, and Yuan Qinghe surrendered. Xiahou Kui gave credit to Zhan Sengzhi, who insisted Xiahou Kui accept the surrender. Xiahou Kui climbed the city wall, raised Liang banners, and accepted the surrender of over 40,000 people. He pursued Yuan Xianbo, capturing over 20,000. He later massacred Chu City, cutting off the North Road of Yiyang from Wei. In the second year of Datong, Wei Yuan Yuanda surrendered, and Xiahou Kui was appointed Governor of Beisi Prefecture. He was later granted the title of Marquis of Baocheng County. After his mother's death, he resigned but was soon appointed as Governor of Southern Yuzhou. In the sixth year, he was transferred to Governor of Yuzhou, where he built a dike in Canngling, irrigating over a thousand hectares and harvesting over one million shi of millet. Both Xiahou Kui and his brother Xiahou Dan were beloved by the people, who sang songs praising them. Xiahou Kui served for seven years, maintaining 10,000 troops and 2,000 horses. He was bold and extravagant, with hundreds of geishas and concubines, and enjoyed entertaining guests. He died in Yuzhou at age fifty-six, posthumously given the title of Shizhong and General Anbei. His son Xiahou Zan succeeded him, and his younger son Xiahou Fan was rough and later joined Hou Jing's rebellion, plundering the capital.

Wei Fang, whose courtesy name is Yuan Zhi, is the son of Wei Rui, a general on horseback.

summary: Yu Hong, from Xiangyang, was tall and handsome. He served as a vanguard in many expeditions and as Prefect of several counties. He was known for his hedonistic lifestyle, with over a hundred concubines and luxurious possessions. He died in office. Wei Fang, styled Yuan Zhi, was the son of General Wei Rui. He served as a chief clerk and later as Prefect of Xuyi County. He was granted the title of Marquis of Yongchang County and served as Grand Administrator of Jingling County. During the Northern Expedition, he led troops from the North Road to rendezvous in Shouchun. He attacked Guoyang, defeating the Wei army despite being outnumbered. He captured City Lord Wang Wei and took 4,200 prisoners. He later served as Governor of Liangzhou and Nanqinzhou, and died at age fifty-nine. Wei Fang was generous and loyal, especially to his brothers. He kept his promise to marry his children to the children of his deceased friend Zhang Su. His son Wei Can succeeded him. The historian comments that Pei Sui and Xiahou Dan were talented and accomplished officials, fitting for their civil and military roles, and should be remembered as famous officials of the Liang Dynasty.

summary: Biographical accounts of several officials from the Liang Dynasty, focusing on their careers, conduct, and contributions. Fan Xiu, a native of Kaocheng, was known for his filial piety and extensive knowledge of ritual traditions. He held various official positions, including county magistrate, minister, and general, serving under the Song, Qi, and Liang dynasties. Despite his literary talents being overshadowed by Shen Yue, his reputation for integrity and adherence to etiquette was widely praised. He was frugal in his personal life, using a decades-old scarf box and only making two dental pens during his tenure in Jinling. He died at seventy-five, leaving behind works like "Li Lun" and "Zi Xun." Fu Zhao, from Lingzhou, was orphaned at six and showed remarkable maturity. He was known for his quiet demeanor, simplicity, and adherence to righteousness, avoiding political entanglements during turbulent times. He served in various roles, including minister and prefect, and was noted for his honest governance, such as sharing resources with the people and refusing gifts. He died at seventy-five, and his brother Fu Ying, also an official, was praised for his filial piety and literary skills, though he did not seek fame for his writings.

translation:
Xiao Jing, courtesy name Zizhao, was Gaozu's cousin.
His father, Xiao Chong, also known as Chong, was the son of Xiao Dao, a doctor from Zuo Guanglu.
Xiao Daomo had three sons: the eldest son Xiao Tangzhi, named Maoxian; the second son was Emperor Taizu Wen; and the third son was Xiao Chongzhi.
When Zuo Guanglu Daoyan lived in the countryside, he paid great attention to the practice of courtesy and was highly praised by everyone. He served as a Taiwei of the Song Dynasty and joined the army of King Jiangxia.
Xiao Shangzhi had a kind-hearted character and virtuous conduct. When he joined the army as a soldier of Situ Jianbaoyu, everyone in Fuxiang called him an elder. They valued him especially and often consulted with him before making decisions when encountering matters.
Later, Xiao Shangzhi was moved to the rank of infantry captain and died in his official post.
In the early years of Tianjian, he was posthumously given the title Wenxuanhou.
Xiao Shangzhi's son Xiao Lingjun was appointed magistrate of Guangde County in Qi.
When Gaozu's righteous master arrived, he was carrying out the affairs of Kuaiji County and died soon after.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he was posthumously granted the title of Marquis of Dongchang County, with a settlement of 1,000 households.
His son Xiao Jian succeeded him.
Xiao Chongzhi was famous for his talent and ability. He advocated strictness in politics and became a champion general and Dongyang governor in his palace.
During the Yongming Dynasty, Qian, Tang and Tang Jui rebelled and led their troops to capture Dongyang. Xiao Chongzhi was killed.
In the early years of Tianjian, he was posthumously given the title of Marquis Zhongjian.
When Xiao Jing was eight years old, he lived with his father in Dongyang County. After his father's death, Xiao Jing became famous far and wide because he lost weight due to grief during the period of mourning.
When I grow up, I love to learn, so I can argue with others and be decisive in doing things.
During the Zhibian and Jianwu years, he was awarded the title of King Gui's left-hand minister and moved to Chengkong County Magistrate. His political performance was the best among the local palaces.
Fan Shu, the prefect of Yongjia County, once lived in the county and was known to be honest and fair. He had always admired Xiao Jing's political performance, so he posted a notice on the county gate saying: "Any difficult and backlogged problems in each county can be solved by the Yongning County Magistrate."
Soon, Xiao Jing resigned due to illness.
Hu Zhongxuan, a native of Yongjia, and more than a thousand people came to the palace and petitioned Xiao Jing to continue to serve as county governor, but the emperor did not agree.
Xiao Jing returned to the court and became a knight and joined the army.
In the second year of Yongyuan, Xiao Jing was awarded the title of Infantry Colonel for his contribution to Changsha Xuanwu King Xiao Yi.
In the winter of that year, King Xuanwu was killed and Xiao Jing also fled.
After Gaozu's uprising team arrived, he appointed Xiao Jing as General Ningshuo to carry out the military affairs of Southern Yanzhou.
At that time, the world was not yet peaceful, and the Chu people on the north bank of the Yangtze River each occupied earthen forts for defense. Xiao Jing showed his authority to them, and the leaders were bound one after another and came to plead guilty. Ten days later, everything in the territory calmed down.
In the second year of the Zhongxing Dynasty, Xiao Jingqian was appointed to supervise the military affairs of Southern Yanzhou, assist the country as a general, and supervise Southern Yanzhou.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he granted Xiao Jing the title of Marquis of Wuping County, with a settlement of 1,000 households. He also served as envoy commander, governor of the military of the four states of South Yanzhou, North Yanzhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, champion general, and governor of South Yanzhou.
Emperor Shao ordered Xiao Jing's mother, Mao, to be the concubine of the state, and she was treated ceremonially like a concubine of the kingdom, with fake gold medals and purple ribbons.
When Xiao Jing lived in Zhoujie, he was honest, cautious and authoritative. He clearly understood the responsibilities of the officials and never had a backlog of documents. The staff below did not dare to deceive him. The officials respected and feared him very much, just like a god.
When there was a famine in the year of the millennium, Xiao Jing asked people to provide relief and pensions. He prepared rice and porridge and put them on the roadside for people passing by. Those who died were given coffins. The people are very dependent on him.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, during the Liang Dynasty's Northern Expedition, Xiao Jing led the army from Huaiyang to attack Suyu City.
He resigned due to the death of his mother, and the Emperor Xia Shao appointed him as an acting official.
Five years later, Banshi returned to the court. He was appointed as the prince's right guard, and moved to the post of general of the auxiliary state and Weiweiqing.
In the seventh year, he was moved to General Zuo Xiaoqi and concurrently served as the leading general.
The leader is responsible for the country's military secrets, and the bureaucrats in the Supervision Bureau were mostly arrogant and extravagant in the past. Lu Liang was very strict during his tenure, and the officials were very restrained.
The supervisors of the military attache system were all favored people, and they could not bear Xiao Jing, so Xiao Jing could not stay in the court for a long time.
Soon, he was appointed as envoy Chijie, governor of Yongzhou, Liangzhou, Southern Qinzhou, Northern Qinzhou, Jiantan Tongbao Og, Choubi's donkey Yingzhu military, General Xinwu, Ningman captain, and Yongzhou governor.
In March of the eighth year, Wu Jin, the governor of Jingzhou in the Wei State, led an army of 70,000 to invade and move away. They drove and forced the barbarians, and the barbarians crossed the desert river one after another to seek refuge with the Liang Dynasty.
summary: Xiao Jing, courtesy name Zizhao, was a cousin of Emperor Gaozu. His father Xiao Chongzhi was a son of Xiao Daomo, who had three sons: Xiao Shangzhi, Emperor Taizu Wen, and Xiao Chongzhi. Xiao Shangzhi was known for his virtuous conduct and served as an infantry captain, dying in office. Posthumously titled Wenxuanhou in the early Tianjian era, his son Xiao Lingjun served as a county magistrate and was later granted the title of Marquis of Dongchang County. Xiao Chongzhi, a champion general and Dongyang governor, was killed during a rebellion in the Yongming era and posthumously titled Marquis Zhongjian. Xiao Jing became famous at age eight for his grief during mourning. He loved learning, was decisive, and served as Chengkong County Magistrate, where his political performance was exemplary. After resigning due to illness, he returned to court and was appointed Infantry Colonel. Following Gaozu's uprising, he became General Ningshuo and pacified the Chu people on the Yangtze's north bank. After Gaozu ascended, Xiao Jing was granted the title of Marquis of Wuping County and governed several states. He was known for his honesty, strictness, and efficiency, with no backlog of documents. During a famine, he provided relief and coffins. In the fourth year of Tianjian, he led an army in the Northern Expedition. After his mother's death, he resigned but was later reappointed to various positions, including General Zuo Xiaoqi. He was strict with officials, causing resentment among favored supervisors, leading to his transfer to Yongzhou as governor. The historian comments that Xiao Jing's talent and judgment benefited the government, making him a person of grace and dignity in the You clan.

translation:

When he was in the court, he was watched and admired by everyone.
Although he and Gaozu were cousins ​​in terms of kinship, Gaozu treated him with great courtesy. When encountering military affairs and national affairs, he would discuss decisions with him.
In the fifteenth year, Xiao Jingjia was appointed as the servant.
In the seventeenth year, Xiao Hong, the Taiwei and the governor of Yangzhou, the king of Linchuan, was dismissed for breaking the law.
The emperor's Shaoshu said: Yangzhou must be managed and suitable people must be selected.
The talents of Wu Huhou and Xiao Jing, the leading general of the army, are qualified for this position. General An You can be used to supervise Yangzhou and set up the assistant history. If the position of minister is still maintained, his residence will be used as the official residence.
Xiao Jing's distant relative lived in Yangzhou. He declined the appointment so sincerely that he burst into tears, but Gaozu refused to allow his resignation.
When Xiao Jing took office in Yongzhou, he was particularly famous for his clear-cut decisions, and his instructions were very strict.
There was an old woman in the countryside. After she complained, she received instructions from Xiao Jing. When she returned to the county, the county officials did not send them out immediately. The old woman said: Xiao Jianzhou's talisman will burn your hands like fire. How dare you keep it!
Xiao Jing was so awed by people.
In the eighteenth year, Xiao Jing repeatedly petitioned the emperor to be relieved of his duties, but Gaozu did not agree.
In the second year, Xiao Jing served as envoy Chijie, regular attendant of Sanqi, military commander of Yingzhou, Sizhou and Huozhou, general of Anxi, and governor of Yingzhou.
Before setting off, Emperor Gaozu came to Xingjian Garden to bid farewell to Xiao Jing, for which he burst into tears.
Gaozu returned to the palace and ordered Xiao Jing to preach a piece of music.
Xiao Jing was known for his ability during his tenure.
The counties of Chabao, Deng and Tongduo bordered the Wei State, and there were many thieves. After Xiao Jing conveyed the notice to the Wei State, the Wei State immediately burned the earthen forts defended by the thieves to protect the border and prevent any further invasion of the two counties.
summary: In the eighth year, when Wei's governor Wu Jin invaded, Xiao Jing accepted surrendered barbarians, defeating the enemy and burying the dead. He built barracks, strengthened defenses, and encouraged farming, resulting in a peaceful and theft-free territory. He was later recalled to court and served in various roles, including General Youwei. In the thirteenth year, he was summoned as leading general, receiving a salary increase. Xiao Jing was personable and well-spoken, and Gaozu treated him with great courtesy, consulting him on military and state affairs. He declined a promotion to Yangzhou governor but was eventually appointed. His strictness was legendary; an old woman noted his talismans were like fire. He died at age forty-seven, posthumously titled Shizhong.

translation:
Four years later, Xiao Liang died in Jian maggot at the age of forty-seven.
The emperor decreed that he be awarded the posthumous title of Shizhong, Zhongfujun, and Kaifu Yitong.
Mi Hao Zhong.
He was succeeded by his son Xiao Qin.
Xiao Chang, whose courtesy name is Zijian, is Xiao Jing's second younger brother.
In the last years of Yuzhang of Qi Dynasty, he served as Zuo Changshi of King Jin'an.
In the early years of Liang Tianjian's reign, he served as the Minister of Zhongshu and the internal history of Yuzhang County.
In the fifth year, Xiao Chang was appointed General Ning Shuo.
In the sixth year, he was moved to the post of Chijie, in charge of the military affairs of Guangzhou, Jiaozhou, Yuesu and Guangzhou, general of the auxiliary state, general of Zhonglang in Pingyue, and governor of Luye.
In the seventh year, he was promoted to General Zhengyuan.
In the ninth year, Hengzhou was separated from Xiangzhou, and Xiao Chang was appointed as the governor, supervising Xujian in Guangzhou and Shi'an military affairs in Xiangzhou, General Xinwu, and governor of Hengzhou. He was dismissed from office for crimes.
In the thirteenth year, Xiao Chang was appointed as the Minister of Sanqi, and soon he took the original official position and concurrently served as Zongzhengqing.
In the same year, Xiao Chang became the chief historian of An You.
He was repeatedly moved to serve as the prince's concubine, Tongzhi Sanqi's regular attendant, and also served as Zong Zhengqing.
Xiao Chang is also very understanding and understanding, but he likes to drink by nature, and after drinking, he often makes mistakes.
When he was in office in the state department, he would often go in and out of other people's homes whenever he was drunk, and sometimes go to the wilderness alone.
He also had no limits in using torture and killing.
He killed someone when he was drunk, and then went to find that person again when he sobered up. Just like that, he didn't regret it.
Finally impeached by relevant officials, Luchang was summoned to stay in the capital. He was very unhappy, so he drank all day long, became very weak, and suffered from heart disease.
In Gentijianzhai, Luken stabbed himself with a knife, but his entourage quickly rescued him, but he did not die.
In the seventeenth year, Xiao Chang died at the age of thirty-nine.
His son's name is Xiao Boyan.
Xiao Ang, whose courtesy name is Ziming, is Xiao Jing's third younger brother.
In the early years of Tianjian, he was transferred to Situ Youchangshi many times, served as general of light vehicles, and supervised southern Yanzhou.
At the beginning, when his brother Lu Liang was appointed as the governor of Yinchaye for the second time, his merits and favors were still in people's hearts. When Xiao Ang came to replace him, people compared him to Feng.
Xiao Ang was recruited as the prefect of Langye and Pengcheng counties, and the military trumpets remained as before.
He also served as the governor of Guangzhou with the official position of General Qingche.
In the second year of ordinary life, he was appointed as a regular servant of Sanqi and general Xinwei.
In the fourth year, he was transferred to the rank of minister of Sanqi, the leader of the army, the prince's concubine, and the prefect of Wuxing County.
In the second year of Datong, he was summoned to serve as General Renwei and Weiweiqing. Soon he was appointed as a minister and concurrently as the leading general.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, he was appointed as the leading general.
In the second year, he was granted the title of Marquis of Xiangyin County and was granted a residence of one thousand households.
He served as the governor of Jiangzhou.
In the first year of Datong, Xiao Ang passed away at the age of fifty-three.
Mi shouted Gong.
Xiao Yu, also known as Zizhen, is Xiao Jing's fourth younger brother.
In the early years of Tianjian, he was awarded the title of Secretary Lang, and was moved to the position of Prince Sheren, Xima, Zhongshu Sheren, and Zhongshu Shilang many times.
He often asked for self-examination, and Emperor Gaozu appointed him as the governor of Jinzhi County, Yongjia County, and Xiangyang County, but he refused to take office.
He volunteered to go to the border states and counties. Emperor Gaozu thought that he was frivolous, unstable and lacked prestige, so he suppressed him and refused to allow him to go.
Later he was appointed as the Minister of Huangmen.
Xiao Yu wrote to the emperor and said: The statement I submitted at the beginning of summer was not approved. Looking back on the past, shame and fear, really makes me tremble in my heart.
summary: Xiao Chang, Xiao Jing's second brother, served in various roles, including governor of Hengzhou, but was dismissed for crimes. He was understanding but prone to drinking and making mistakes, often killing people while drunk without remorse. He died at age thirty-nine. Xiao Ang, the third brother, served as governor of Southern Yanzhou and Guangzhou, among other roles. He died at age fifty-three, posthumously titled Gong. Xiao Yu, the fourth brother, served as Secretary Lang and other positions but frequently refused appointments. He wrote a memorial expressing shame and fear, requesting dismissal. Emperor Gaozu replied, criticizing his refusals and dismissing him. Later, Xiao Yu was exiled for minting coins but was recalled. He became a model of propriety and was appointed Prefect of Jinling County, where he implemented beneficial policies. He died after a severe illness, mourned by the people, who built temples and steles for him. He was posthumously appointed governor of Xiangzhou, titled Gong.

translation:
Liu Jun, whose courtesy name was Xiaobiao, was from Pingyuan.
His father, Liu Ge, was the internal historian of Shixing in the Song Dynasty.
When Liu Jun was just one year old, his mother took him back to his hometown.
In the early years of Song Taishi, Qingzhou fell to the Wei people. When Liu Jun was eight years old, he was kidnapped and taken to Zhongshan. Liu Shi, a wealthy man in Zhongshan, sympathized with Liu Jun's plight and redeemed Liu Jun with five pieces of silk and taught him to write and read.
The people of Wei heard that Liu Jun had relatives in Jiangnan, so they moved him to Sangqian.
Liu Jun was eager to learn, his family was poor, and he lived in other people's homes, but he set his own study schedule. He often lit a torch made of hemp straw and read all night. Sometimes he fell asleep and the torch burned his hair. When he woke up, he resumed reading and stayed up all night.
During the next year of Qi Yong, Liu Jun was able to return to Qi from Sangqian. He thought that his knowledge was not extensive, so he went to look for other books that he had never seen. When he heard that there was such a book in the capital, he would rush to ask for it to be borrowed. Cui Weizu of Qinghe called him a "book slut".
At that time, Xiao Ziliang, the real fallen minister, was recruiting scholars, and Xingjun asked for a position in Xiao Ziliang's kingdom through others. Xu Xiaosi, the Minister of Civil Affairs, devalued him and refused to agree. He was only appointed as the minister of Nanhai King, but he refused to take up the post.
By the time of Emperor Ming, Xiao Yaoxin was appointed governor of Yuzhou and appointed Liu Jun as the prisoner of the government. He was treated very generously.
Xiao Yaoxin passed away soon, and Liu Jun was not allowed to raise his tune for a long time.
In the early years of Tianjian, Liu Jun was called to the Western Province and served as the secretary of the school with He Zong, a bachelor.
Liu Jun's brother Liu Longqing was serving as governor at the time. Su asked for leave to visit him. He was impeached by the official for transporting prohibited items without permission and was dismissed from office.
He liked learning. When he was transferred to the governor's office, he was promoted to join the army as a product of Cao. He was provided with some books and asked him to copy them into a book by category and named it "Lei Yuan". Before the book was compiled, Liu Jun left because of illness. He built a house there and lived there because he visited Ziyan Mountain in Dongyang.
Liu Jun wrote "Mountain Qi Zhi", and the writing is beautiful.
Emperor Gaozu recruited literary people, and those with high talents were often recommended for promotion, often without qualifications.
Liu Jun acted according to his own temperament and could not follow the ups and downs of others. Emperor Gaozu disliked him very much, so he did not use him.
Liu Jun then wrote "Discrimination of Fate" to express his feelings. The article said:
The emperor once talked about Guan Ren with many famous sages, and lamented that there were talented people in charge but their official positions were not high.
A friend was in the court at that time and heard this discussion, so he told me when he came back.
I believe that the embarrassment and enlightenment of a scholar's situation are all determined by fate, so I respectfully describe the outline of destiny and my own ambitions.
In my opinion, the governor is a talent sent from heaven, magnificent and outstanding, with outstanding talents and excellent character. He is really a hero in the country, and he is not just an ordinary divination and blessing.
But his official position is only that of Shaofu Cheng, and he is forty-eight years old. How few people God has given him to govern!
However, talented people do not have prominent official positions, while gluttonous, cruel and greedy people are in prominent official positions. This phenomenon has often made people sigh since ancient times, how can it be just Gong Ming?
summary: Liu Jun, courtesy name Xiaobiao, was from Pingyuan. His father was Liu Ge. At age one, his mother took him home. During Song Taishi, Qingzhou fell to the Wei, and at eight, Liu Jun was kidnapped to Zhongshan. A wealthy man, Liu Shi, redeemed him and taught him. The Wei moved him to Sangqian. He was an eager learner, often reading by torchlight all night, sometimes burning his hair. During Qi Yongming, he returned to Qi. He sought out rare books, and Cui Weizu called him a "book slut." He sought a position under Xiao Ziliang but was devalued by Xu Xiaosi. He served under Xiao Yaoxin, who treated him generously. After Xiao Yaoxin's death, Liu Jun was long without promotion. In early Tianjian, he served as a secretary. He was dismissed for transporting prohibited items. He was later given books to compile "Lei Yuan," but left due to illness. He wrote "Mountain Qi Zhi." Emperor Gaozu disliked him for not following others, so he was not used. Liu Jun then wrote "Discrimination of Fate" to express his feelings.

translation:
Therefore, no one can understand the difference between human nature and endowment, a lifetime of embarrassment and enlightenment, setbacks, failures, and successes.
When talking about this issue, Wang Zhongren covered up its root cause, and Sima Zichang expressed his doubts.
As for the poor and humble people who wear humble clothes and live in thatched huts, they must say that their destiny is controlled by God, and good and bad fortunes depend on luck. For wealthy and wealthy families, it is said that misfortunes and misfortunes do not distinguish between families, but are only caused by people's virtues.
There was a lot of talk and arguments, and various opinions emerged one after another.
Li Xiaoyuan talked about the foundation of fate but did not explain its changes. Guo Zixuan talked about the changes of fate but did not clarify its origin.
Let me try to talk about this issue: The Great Way gives birth to all things, so it is called Tao; if it is born without any master, it is called nature.
Nature means that all things grow, but they don’t know why they grow; all things get their own place, but they don’t know why they get their own places.
He stirs up the world and creates all things, but he does not regard it as his own strength or his own achievements. There is no intention to nurture it while alive, and death is not caused by killing. Falling into the abyss and becoming a fish and dragon is not a punishment from God; rising to the sky and becoming a bird is not a favor from God.
This Tao is boundless and broad, and all things change with it; but it is also deep and pure, and it never changes once it is created.
Once it is created, it will not change. This is called destiny.
Fate refers to the fate sent down from heaven.
Destiny is determined in the dark and will never change.
Ghosts and gods cannot predict it, and sages cannot examine it. The force that knocks down the mountains cannot be resisted, nor can the sincerity that causes the sun to return cannot be affected. If destiny comes quickly, it cannot be delayed for a moment, and if it comes slowly, it cannot be missed in advance. The most virtuous sages cannot transcend the destiny, and the wise people cannot escape the constraints of destiny.
Therefore, in the era when Fangxun was in power, the floods were so powerful that the mountains and mausoleums were submerged; in the era when Chengtang was the emperor, droughts were raging and the gold and stone were scorched.
Jin Wengong suffered repeated setbacks, and Kong Xuanni was in Chen Jueliang. Yan Hui's hair turned gray prematurely, and Ran Geng suffered from a serious illness. Boyi and Shuqi starved to death because of the woman's words, and Mencius was embarrassed because of Zang Cang's slander.
Sages can't escape the arrangement of fate, let alone mediocre ordinary people!
As for the corpses of the soldiers who were thrown into the river; Dr. Qu Yuan of Sanlu sank in the Xiang River; Dr. Jia was demoted to Kensha because of frustration in his ambition; Feng Duwei and Feng Tang spent time in the office until his hair turned white; Huan Junshan entered the official career, but his wings were broken due to the Yuntai controversy; Feng Jingtong had the virtue of a phoenix, but his wings were destroyed because of slander and slander. Are these people lacking in talent and lacking in virtue?
In modern times, Liu Shan of Pei State and Liu Shan's younger brother Liu Fa were both outstanding talents at that time.
Liu Shan was none other than Kansai Confucius. He was familiar with the Six Classics extensively, followed instructions and taught the younger generations, and wholeheartedly followed Confucian principles.
Liu Long's character is noble and pure, like autumn frost, and his heart is pure, like the jade from Kunlun Mountain. He is unique and has outstanding character. He does not follow the crowd and conforms to the world.
summary: The article "Discrimination of Fate" argues that a scholar's situation is determined by fate. It laments that talented people like Guan Ren have low positions. It states that the difference between human nature and endowment, and a lifetime of setbacks, cannot be understood. It discusses the concepts of Tao and nature, stating that destiny is determined in the dark and never changes. It lists sages like Jin Wengong and Confucius who could not escape fate. It mentions modern examples like Liu Shan and Liu Fa, who were talented but died in obscurity. It argues that nobility, longevity, and wealth are produced naturally, not by talent. It lists five areas of confusion regarding fate, including the belief that honor and disgrace are determined by people, that success comes from martial power, that good and evil are always rewarded, and that a country's success depends on its ruler. It concludes that a gentleman follows the right path, obeys heaven, and secures his own destiny, understanding that fate is beyond human control.

translation:
Eating rice, eating fish, wearing fox fur and fur, wearing pure white silk, watching wonderful and exquisite dances, and listening to the music of Yunhe's fine materials. These are the needs of the people's life, and they do not require anything to do so.
Cultivate morality, learn benevolence and righteousness, establish deep feelings of filial piety and brotherhood, establish loyalty and integrity, be infiltrated and influenced by ritual and music, and follow the rules of the past kings. These are the needs of a gentleman's life, and it does not require anything to do so.
In this way, a gentleman follows the right path, implements the right path, happily obeys the arrangements of heaven, and secures his own destiny.
They understand that they are helpless in the face of fate, and understand that rise and fall, honor and disgrace do not depend on human wisdom and strength.
Therefore, when blessings pass away, one does not look for them; when disasters come, one does not resist them; when one survives, one does not feel particularly happy; when one faces death, one does not feel sad.
Living in a Yaotai mansion will not make him happy; living in an earthen house and a humble household will not make him worried.
When you are in wealth, you will not be complacent or arrogant. You will not be restless and pursue what you want.
If this is the case, how can there be articles like "A Tragedy Man Is Not Encountered" by Ma Qian of the Taishi Company and Dong Zhongshu, the Prime Minister of Jiangdu!
After Liu Jun's "Distinction of Fate" was written, Liu Bo of Zhongshan wrote to refute Liu Jun. He wrote twice in total, and Liu Jun defended and analyzed each one one by one, and gave Liu Bo a reply.
It happened that Liu Ma passed away, and he did not see Liu Jun's subsequent reply to the letter. Liu Jun then wrote a letter to reply to Liu Ma, who had passed away, describing the incident and his own feelings, saying: Liu Ma has already raised such an inquiry. It was a matter of a brother's death in my family, but he failed to reply to him in time.
Soon, Mr. Liu Bo said goodbye to us forever and became a foreign object. His other remarks were hidden and never came out.
Someone got these remarks from his home and showed them to me. Not all of his good words could be said, but the man had passed away. The handwriting of the article was still new, but the grass on the tomb had grown lush. I was sad for this, and I didn’t know who the tears were flowing to.
Although life is short, like a horse passing by, time flies like an arrow, like water waves passing by, and lightning flashing. His character is like autumn chrysanthemums and spring orchids, and his good reputation will never fade away.
So I wrote down the general story of this incident to repay Liu Zhou's kindness.
If what Mo Zhai said about Du Bo knowing after his death is correct, and what Ye Yi discussed in the announcement room about ghosts and gods has come true, then I hope the trees in your cemetery can be like the trees on the tomb, pointing to the capital to express your longing for your motherland; I hope you can be like the springs in the mountains, which can flow in response to the sound of music.
I can only hang the sword on the tomb like Yanling Jizi to repay my friends. What a pity I feel! Liu Jun's paper is not published because it is too long.
Liu Jun once wrote "Automatic Preface", which roughly stated: I compare myself with Feng Jingtong. He and I have three aspects in common and four aspects that are different.
Why?
summary: After Liu Jun's "Distinction of Fate" was written, Liu Bo of Zhongshan wrote to refute him. Liu Jun replied, but Liu Bo died before seeing the reply. Liu Jun wrote a letter to the deceased Liu Bo, expressing his sorrow. Liu Jun's paper was not published due to its length. Liu Jun wrote an "Automatic Preface" comparing himself to Feng Jingtong, listing three similarities and four differences. He lived in Shuyang, where many studied under him. He died at sixty, and his disciples gave him the posthumous name Mr. Xuanjing.

translation:
Feng Jingtong was outstanding in talent, second to none at the time, and had a strong ambition, as solid as stone. Although I am not as good as him, I am honest, bold and resolute. This is the first aspect that is the same.
Feng Jingtong happened to meet a wise monarch who rejuvenated the national destiny, but was not tried in the end; I also met a wise monarch who was famous for governing the country, but was also reprimanded in his prime. This is the second aspect of the same.
Feng Jingtong had a jealous wife at home, for which he even had to fetch water, grind rice, and take care of the housework. I also had a fierce wife at home, which also made my family life difficult and unstable. This is the third aspect of the same thing.
Feng Jingtong was born in the reform era, and he once served as a general and led troops to fight; from young to old, I have always been sad and frustrated, and my ambitions have not been expanded. This is the first difference.
Feng Jingtong had a son, Feng Zhongwen, who had an official position and a good reputation; I encountered the same misfortune as Deng Bodao, and I never had any biological flesh and blood of my own. This is the second difference.
Feng Jingtong is strong and getting stronger as he gets older; I am suffering from a disease and I don’t know when I will die suddenly. This is the third different aspect.
Although Feng Jingtong was burned like Zhi Cao Hui Cao and died silently, he was admired by famous sages, and the aftertaste of his style exuded a rich fragrance that spread for a longer time. His reputation will be greater; my life is indifferent, my reputation is unknown, and no one in the world understands me. Once I leave this world, I will be like dead autumn grass, no one cares about me. This is the fourth different aspect.
So I tried my best to write a narrative and leave it to those who care about me.
Liu Jun lived in Shuyang, and many Wu and Hui people studied under him.
Two years later, Liu Jun died at the age of sixty.
His disciples gave him the nickname Mr. Xuanjing.
Liu Bo, courtesy name Mingxin, was born in Weichang, Zhongshan.
His grandfather Liu Yu, six generations ago, was posthumously awarded the title of Hussar General during the Jin Dynasty.
Liu Bo was good at writing articles since he was a child. When he grew up, he became knowledgeable.
At the beginning of the Qi Dynasty, he took up an official position and was invited to join the army.
In the early years of the year, Xingtuo was worshiped as the military supervisor and joined the army in the imperial palace of Cong Wangji. He was ordered by Moling. He died during the period of dispatch.
Xie Jiqing was from Yangxia, Chen County.
His great-grandfather Xie Lingyun was the internal historian of Linchuan during the Song Dynasty; his father Xie Chaozong was the Huangmenlang at that time. All were famous in previous generations.
Yao Jiqing was alert, intelligent and eloquent since he was a child. People called him a child prodigy at that time.
Later, Xie Chaozong was demoted to Yuezhou for being convicted. When passing through Xintingzhu, Xie Jiqing couldn't bear to say goodbye to his father, so he threw himself into the river. The people around him hurriedly rescued him and saved him from drowning in the river.
When it came time to mourn for his father, he mutilated his body with grief, exceeding the requirements of etiquette.
After the mourning period expired, he was called to be the son of the country.
summary: Liu Bo, courtesy name Mingxin, was from Zhongshan. He was good at writing articles and knowledgeable. He held various official positions and died during a dispatch.

translation:
Prince Wenhui of Qi personally presided over the examination. He said to Wang Jian, the prince of the country, who was offering wine, "Xie Jiqing's original specialty is to be proficient in metaphysics, and now he can be tested on the classics and meanings."
Wang Jian asked the questions according to Prince Wenhui's wishes. Xie Jiqing answered the questions correctly and spoke fluently. Prince Wenhui praised Xie Jiqing greatly.
Wang Jian said to people: Xie Chaozong has a successor.
When Xie Jiqing grew up, he was very studious. He read extensively and had literary talent.
When he first became an official, he served as a regular attendant of Yuzhang Kingdom. After his meritorious service, he moved to Cao Xing, a chariot and cavalry officer, and joined the army. He served as the prime minister of the country and held wine ceremonies. He left the capital and served as the order of Ningguo. He also entered the capital to supplement the records of the lieutenant of the Shangshu Palace and the Taiwei of Jin'an King.
In the early years of Tianjian, Xie Jiqing was appointed as the Sangonglang of the Prince of Poyang who conquered the captives, and soon he was appointed as the secretary and censor.
In the past, when Lang Guan was transferred to the post of Shi Yushi, people jokingly called him "Nan Ben".
Xie Jiqing felt very frustrated because of this. He often complained that he was ill and stopped interfering in the affairs of the Taifu government.
Xie Jiqing moved to the position of Sanqi Shilang, Zhongshu Lang, Guozi Doctor, Shangshu Zuocheng.
Xie Jiqing understood the old affairs and routines in detail. Xu Mian, the servant, often asked him every time he encountered a problem.
However, Xie Jiqing was open-minded by nature and did not stick to trivial matters. He would do things that suited his heart and was not bound by court laws.
He once participated in a banquet at Le Youyuan and came back without getting drunk. He stopped the car at a roadside restaurant on his way home, raised the curtains, and sat in the car to have a drink with three attendants and grooms in front of the car. The onlookers at that time were like a wall. Xie Jiqing took it calmly as if nothing had happened.
Later, Xie Jiqing was punished by a supervisor because he was wrapped up in the imperial office, wore shorts at night, and his disciples drank and shouted in the pavilion. He was found guilty and removed from his official position.
Soon he was appointed as Doctor of the State, and not long after he was appointed as the governor of Hedong. Before his term was completed, he reported that he was ill and was dismissed.
Soon, Xie Jiqing was appointed as the crown prince and led the order, and was moved to the post of Zhenwei Nanping Wang Changshi.
In the sixth year of Ordinary Years, the emperor issued an edict to send the leading general Xichang Hou Xiao Yuanzao to lead various troops in the Northern Expedition. Xie Jiqing petitioned to accompany the army in the Northern Expedition, and was promoted to Army Division Commander Shi and Jiaweirong General.
The Northern Expeditionary Army was defeated in Guoyang, and Xie Jiqing was convicted and removed from his official position.
Xie Jiqing's residence was in Baiyang Shijing. Officials who were on good terms with him would often bring wine to his place, and his home was often full of guests.
At that time, Zuo Cheng, Yu Zhongrong, was also exempted from official duties. The two of them had similar interests, were both dissolute and informal. Sometimes they would ride in an uncovered gondola to play in the countryside. When they were drunk, they would hit the golden bell with their hands and sing lamentations, ignoring people's comments.
King Shu of Hunan was in Jingzhou and wrote letters to comfort and encourage him.
Xie Jiqing wrote back and said: Your Majesty, I have been living in seclusion in the suburbs of Cambodia since I parted from you in Nanpu. Every time I look at the sun, I stand high in the wind and stand in the distance, recalling your kindness, recalling the scenes of accompanying banquets, driving the osmanthus table in the clear pool, and sitting on the ground on the fallen flowers on the top of the mountain to enjoy the scenery.
summary: Xie Jiqing was from Yangxia. His great-grandfather was Xie Lingyun. He was a child prodigy. He once threw himself into a river when his father was demoted. He was studious and had literary talent. He held various official positions, including Censor. He was open-minded and not bound by court laws. He was once dismissed for misconduct. He later petitioned to accompany the Northern Expedition but was dismissed after the army was defeated. He lived in seclusion, often drinking with friends. He died of illness. He had a collection of essays.

translation:
Liu Xie lost his father in his early years. He was determined, fond of learning, and from a poor family. He did not get married, but relied on the monk Sengyou and lived with the monks. After more than ten years, he became proficient in the Buddhist Tripitaka. He divided the categories and arranged the collections.
The scriptures currently collected in Dinglin Temple were compiled by Liu Xie.
In the early years of Tianjian, Liu Xiechu became an official and was invited by the court. Xiao Hong, the king of Linchuan in the Chinese army, chose him as a concurrent secretary. He also moved to the chariot and cavalry warehouse to join the army.
Liu Xie came to Beijing to serve as Tai Mo Ling, and he had a clean and honest government record.
He was also awarded the title of Renwei Nankang Wang Jishi, and also the general secretary of the Cambodian palace.
At that time, the sacrifices offered to the Seven Temples had switched to fruits and vegetables, but cattle, sheep, and hogs were still used as sacrifices in the suburbs to worship heaven and earth and to worship the gods of agriculture and shrines.
Liu Xie then went to the table and suggested that the rituals of offering sacrifices to heaven and earth in the suburbs should be changed in the same way as those of offering sacrifices to the seven temples, and that the sacrifices should also use fruits and vegetables. The emperor issued an edict and handed it over to the minister for deliberation, and finally decided to follow Liu Xie's report.
Liu Xie was moved to the post of captain of the infantry school, but his concurrent post remained unchanged.
Prince Zhaoming liked literary people. He admired Liu Xie and had close contacts with Liu Xie.
At first, Liu Xie wrote fifty chapters in "The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons", discussing ancient and modern literary styles, which he compiled and arranged in order.
The preface to "Wen Xin Diao Long" says:
Wenxin refers to the intention of writing an article.
In the past, Juanzi wrote "Qin Xin" and Wang Tzu wrote "Qiao Xin". Because the meaning of "heart" expressed is honest and perfect, they used it as the title of their books.
Since ancient times, writing articles has relied on carving and decoration. I am afraid it is based on the example of Ding Xi, so everyone calls writing articles Diaolong.
Throughout the ages, the world has been filled with mediocre and sage people, and those who stand out only rely on their intelligence and strategy.
Time will pass quickly, and human intelligence cannot last forever. If you want to pass down your reputation and career, you can only rely on writing.
The human form symbolizes heaven and earth, and inherits nature from the five elements. The ears and eyes are like the sun and moon, and the voice is like wind and thunder. Human beings are beyond all things and can be regarded as the most supernatural.
However, the human body is more fragile than grass and trees, but reputation can be stronger than gold and stone and last forever. Therefore, when a gentleman lives in the world, he wants to establish meritorious deeds and write books. This is not because he likes to argue, but because he has no choice but to build reputation!
I was already in my thirties, and one night I dreamed that I was following Confucius southward with a red lacquer sacrificial vessel in my hand. When I woke up in the morning, I felt very happy.
Great saints are rare to see, and now he condescended to appear in the dream of a nobody like me!
Since the beginning of mankind, there has never been a saint like Confucius.
summary: Liu Xie, courtesy name Yanhe, was from Ju. He lost his father early, did not marry, and lived with a monk, becoming proficient in Buddhist scriptures. He became an official in early Tianjian. He suggested changing suburban sacrifices to fruits and vegetables, which was adopted. Prince Zhaoming admired him. He wrote "The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons" in fifty chapters. The preface explains his motivation, stating that a gentleman wants to establish merit and write books. He dreamed of following Confucius. He argues that articles are branches of classics. He criticizes previous literary critics like Cao Pi and Lu Ji for being incomplete or trivial. His book discusses rhymed and unrhymed passages, analyzes emotions and literary talents, and covers various aspects of writing. He sought evaluation from Shen Yue, who valued the book. Liu Xie later became a monk, changing his name to Huidi, and died less than a year later.

translation:
Wang Ji could write articles when he was seven years old. When he grew up, he was very studious, read extensively in books, and was talented. Le'an Renla was very impressed when he saw him.
Wang Ji was once a guest at Shen Yue's house and composed an impromptu poem called "Yong Candle", which Shen Yue appreciated very much.
At the end of the Qi Dynasty, Wang Ji served as a champion and joined the army. After accumulating merit, he was promoted to a foreign soldier and a reporter.
In the early years of Tianjian, the royal status was removed and he was granted the title of Chief Secretary of King Ancheng, Sangonglang of Shangshu, and Tingweizheng.
