Successive Yuyao and Qiantang magistrates were dismissed from office because of their misconduct.
After a long time, the royal status was revoked and granted the title of Qingchao. King Xiangshu consulted to join the army and followed the palace to Kuaiji.
There are Yunmen Mountain and Tianzhu Mountain in Kuaiji County. Wang Ji once visited these two mountains, and sometimes he stayed in the mountains for several months without returning home.
Wang Ji wrote a poem when he went to Ruoxie Creek. One of the lines said: The forest with noisy cicadas is more quiet, and the mountain with singing birds is even more secluded.
At that time, people believed that the implication of these two poems was unparalleled.
Wang Ji returned to the capital and served as Grand Sima, working as a lieutenant, and moved to the central government as a doctor. Wang Ji felt particularly frustrated, so he roamed on the market road on foot and interacted with people at will.
The king of eastern Hunan was appointed as the governor of Jingzhou, and he promoted Wang Ji to Anxi Prefecture to consult and join the army, and also served as Tangling.
Wang Ji did not deal with the affairs of the county, but drank alcohol every day. Some people came to the county government to sue, so Wang Ji ordered them to be whipped and then let them go.
Wang Ji died soon after.
There are collections of Wang Ji's writings that are circulated in the world.
Wang Ji's son, Wang Bi, was also very talented and died earlier than Wang Ji.
He Sicheng, whose courtesy name is Yuanjing, was born in Tan, Donghai.
His father, Liu Jingshu, served as Zhengshu Lushi, joined the army, and was ordered to Yuhang during the Qi Dynasty.
He Sicheng has been diligent and studious since he was a child, and is good at writing articles.
He became an official at home and served as the minister of King Nankang. He was promoted to Zuochangshi of King Ancheng and a doctor of Taixue. After defeating King Ancheng of Nankang, he joined the army and also served as a recorder.
He Sicheng went to Si with the prince and wrote "Poetry on a Tour to Mount Lu". After reading this poem, he admired it very much and thought that his own work could not catch up with this poem.
Shen Yue built a new study in his suburban residence, and Shen Yue ordered someone skilled in calligraphy to inscribe this poem on the wall of the study.
Fu Zhao once asked He Sicheng to write "Shidian Poems", with elegant and gorgeous diction.
He Sicheng was dismissed and awarded the title of Tingweizheng.
In the 15th year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu ordered Prince Zhan Shi Xu Mian to recommend bachelors to Hualin Garden to compile the "Qing Lue". Xu Mian recommended He Sicheng and five other people to be selected.
He Sicheng moved to the post of Censor and Censor.
Since the Song and Qi Dynasties, this official position has gradually been ignored. In the early years of Liang Tianjian, Liang Tianjian paid attention to the selection of the censor. According to the specifications of the two ministers, three servants were placed in front of the car, holding a green bag containing the official seal. This arrangement is because according to the old practice, the seals and ribbons of officials who correct illegal activities are placed in front of the car.
After a long time, He Sicheng was moved to the position of moling magistrate, and he entered the dynasty and served as the general manager of the East Palace.
In addition to being granted the title of Lu Shi by King Shu of Anxi and Xiang to join the army, his post as a layman remained unchanged.
At that time, Xu Mian and Zhou She were both in charge of political affairs in the court with their talents and abilities. They both admired He Sicheng's talents and often took turns inviting him to have discussions.
After the death of Prince Zhaoming, He Sicheng came to Beijing to serve as the magistrate of Yi County.
He moved to Xuanhui and Wuling Wangzhonglushi and joined the army. He died during his tenure at the age of fifty-four.
summary: Wang Ji, courtesy name Wenhai, was from Linyi. He could write at seven. He was talented and once wrote a poem that Shen Yue appreciated. He held various official positions, including magistrate, but was dismissed for misconduct. He visited mountains in Kuaiji, sometimes staying for months. He wrote a famous poem with the line "The forest with noisy cicadas is more quiet." He died soon after. His son Wang Bi died before him.

translation:
He Sicheng has fifteen volumes of collected works.
In the past, He Sicheng, He Xun and He Zilang from the same clan were all famous for being good at writing articles. At that time, people said: Among the three in the East China Sea, He Zilang is the most talented.
He Sicheng heard this and said: This is wrong.
As for what I have to say, He Xun should still be considered the most talented.
What He Sicheng meant by this was that the reputation of being the most talented should go to himself.
He Zilang, also known as Shiming, was very talented in his early years. He had unique insights and was good at talking about mystical principles. Zhou She often talked with him and admired his exquisite mystical principles.
He Zilang once wrote "Ode to the Lost Tomb", which was modeled after Zhuang Zhou's "Pian of Joy" about the horse beating the skull. The writing is very exquisite.
At that time, people said: He Zilang is handsome and outstanding.
He held various official positions, including serving as a minister of cavalry outside the country, and went to Beijing to serve as a national mountain magistrate. During this period, he died at the age of twenty-four.
There are collections of articles circulating in the world.
Liu Yao, courtesy name Shishen, was from Pingyuan.
His grandfather Liu Chengmin was the governor of Jizhou during the Song Dynasty.
His father, Liu Wenwei, was the prefect of Shuyang during the Qi Dynasty. He had a clean and honest political record. Liu Wenwei's deeds are recorded in the "Book of Qi". In "The Biography of Good Government".
When Liu Yao was only a few years old, Zhengshi Mingsengshao saw him, patted him and said: This child is indeed a thousand-mile horse.
When Liu Yao was thirteen years old, his father passed away. He cried every time at the funeral, and his grief moved everyone on the road.
In the early years of Tianjian, Liu Yao was appointed as a doctor of Taixue, and Xuanhui Yuzhang Wang Xing joined the army.
Liu Yao had been eager to learn since childhood, and was well-read and proficient in all kinds of books. Shen Yue, Ren Fang and the literati under them always asked Liu Yao if they had forgotten knowledge.
Liu Yao once talked about the sacrificial bottles used to offer sacrifices to the ancestral temple at Shen Yue's guest table. Shen Yue said: Zheng Xuan answered Zhang Yi and said that the sacrificial bottles were painted with dancing phoenix tails.
If there is no such wine vessel now, it means that the ancient regulations are not followed.
Liu Yao said: Zheng Xuan's words may not be able to be used as a basis.
In ancient times, wine vessels such as Zun and Yi were carved out of wood in the shape of birds and animals, with the top of the head and back cut open so that the wine in the vessel could be poured out.
In the past, the Wei Dynasty excavated from the ground in Lu County the ritual utensils used by Qi Dafu Ziwei to accompany his daughter. Among them were sacrificial bottles, which were in the shape of an ox for sacrifice. During the Yongjia period of the Jin Dynasty, the traitor Cao Yi robbed Qi Jinggong's tomb in Qingzhou and obtained two such wine bottles, which were also shaped like oxen.
What was excavated in both places were ritual vessels left over from ancient times. It can be seen from this that the wine vessels such as Zun and Yi wine vessels carved out of wood into the shapes of birds and animals are not fake.
Shen Yue thought Liu Yao was right.
Shen Yue also said: He Chengtian's "Compilation" is a very profound book. It records the affairs of Master Zhang Zhong and the Long-necked King. Where did this incident come from?
Liu Yao said: Zhang Zhongshi was one foot and two inches long. This record is only found in "Lunheng".
The long-necked king is King Biqian. Zhu Jianan's "Funan Yinan Ji" said: The long-necked king has not died from ancient times to the present.
Shen Yue took the two books to search and found that they were all as Liu Cha said.
summary: He Sicheng, courtesy name Yuanjing, was from Tan. He was diligent and good at writing. He held various official positions. Shen Yue admired his poem and had it inscribed on his wall. He was recommended to compile "Qing Lue." He moved to the position of Censor. He was knowledgeable and admired by Xu Mian and Zhou She. He died at fifty-four. He had fifteen volumes of collected works. He once said that He Xun was the most talented among the three Hes, but meant the reputation should go to himself. He Zilang, also from the same clan, was talented and died at twenty-four. Liu Yao, courtesy name Shishen, was from Pingyuan. He was studious and well-read. Shen Yue and Ren Fang often asked him about forgotten knowledge. He corrected Shen Yue's interpretation of ancient sacrificial bottles. He was knowledgeable about many things, including the origin of the "long-necked king." Shen Yue praised his writings. He held various official positions, including magistrate, and had a clean record. He was recommended to compile "Bianlue." He wrote "Lin Ting Fu," which Wang Sengru praised. He died at fifty. He was honest and frugal. He wrote several books, including "Ya Ya" and "Chu Ci Cao Mu Shu."

translation:
Xie Zheng, courtesy name Xuandu, was from Yangxia, Chen County.
His great-great-grandfather Xie Jingren was the minister Zuopushe in the Song Dynasty.
Grandfather Xie Zhi was the chief secretary of Situ during the Song Dynasty.
Father Xie Jing was as famous as his cousin Xie Tiao when he was young.
Xiao Ziliang, the king of Qi Jingling, built the west residence and recruited literary people.
Xie Jing was also recruited. During the Longchang period, Xie Jing served as Emperor Ming's hussar to consult on joining the army and headed the record office.
He was moved to the post of Zhongshu Lang and the internal history of Jin'an.
The capital was pacified with a high cushion, the embankment was invited to serve as a consultant to the Bafu, and the Huangmenlang built a platform.
In the early years of Tianjian, Xie Qiang accumulated merit and was promoted to Sinong Qing, Secretary Supervisor, Zuo Min Shangshu, Mingwei General, and Shuyang Prefect.
Emperor Gaozu wanted to appoint Xie Jing as his minister, but Yingdi refused on the grounds of old age and asked for the post of gold seal and purple ribbon. Before he could be appointed to an official position according to rank, Xie Jing died of illness.
Xie Zheng was smart since he was a child, and he was considered to have excellent talents. He often said to his relatives: This child is not an ordinary person. What is worrying is his life span; if God gives him a long life, I will have no regrets.
When Xie Zheng grew up, he was very handsome, fond of learning, and good at writing articles.
Xie Zheng was initially appointed as Facao, King of Chisheng of Anxi, and then moved to the post of Sangong Ercaolang of the Ministry of Jin of Shangshu, the Prince of Yuzhang, and a member of Zhongshushe.
He also moved to Pingbei to consult and join the army, and concurrently served as minister of Hongshan. His position remained unchanged. At that time, Mengjian, the king of Zhongshan in Wei, returned to the north, and he went to Wushanyao to pay his last respects. Emperor Gaozu asked his ministers to compose thirty rhymes of poetry at the banquet, and the poem was limited to three seconds to be completed.
Xie Zheng finished the poem in a second. The diction was beautiful and Gao Dan read it again and again.
Xie Zheng also wrote Linru Houyuan's "Release Essay", which was also appreciated by contemporary people.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, Tangtang left his job to mourn the death of his father, and then his mother passed away.
The emperor issued an edict and ordered Xie Zheng to resume his duties as General Zhenwei during the mourning period and return to Beijing to temporarily take charge of his original duties.
After the mourning period expired, he was awarded the title of Minister Zuocheng.
In the third year of Zhongdatong, Prince Zhaoming passed away, and Emperor Gaozu appointed Dong Wang as the crown prince. When the edict was about to be issued, Emperor Gaozu just summoned Shangshu Zuopushe He Jingrong, Xuanhui general Kong Shudi and Xie Man to discuss with them.
At that time, Yaotang was still young and his position was not high, but he was appointed and favored very generously.
In the fourth year, Xie Luan was promoted to Zhongshulang due to his meritorious service, while the positions of Hongluqing and Sheren remained unchanged.
In the sixth year of Zhongdatong, Xie Zheng went to Beijing and served as Beizhonglangsui Tonggongshi and Chenluqie prefect.
Xie Zheng died during his tenure at the age of thirty-seven.
Xie Zheng's friend Langye Wangshuan collected his manuscripts and compiled them into twenty volumes.
summary: Xie Zheng, courtesy name Xuandu, was from Yangxia. He was smart and handsome, fond of learning. He held various official positions. He once finished a poem in one second at a banquet, which Emperor Gaozu admired. He was appointed to discuss the appointment of a new crown prince. He died at thirty-seven. His friend Wang Shuan compiled his manuscripts.

translation:
Zang Yan, courtesy name Yanwei, was born in Ju, Dongguan.
His great-grandfather Zang Tao was posthumously granted the title of Dr. Zuo Guanglu during the Song Dynasty.
His grandfather Zang Ning was appointed Minister Youcheng during the Qi Dynasty.
His father, Zang Leng, served in the army and joined the army.
Zang Yan had a filial character when he was young. He became famous for his grief-stricken body during the mourning for his father.
He lost his father and his family was poor, but he was diligent and studious and never put down his books.
Initially, he was appointed as the Minister of King Ancheng, and then as the Permanent Minister.
Zang Yan's uncle Zang Weizhen was appointed as the prefect of Jiangxia and took Zang Yan with him to take office. Zang Yan wrote "Tuenyou Fu" during the trip. Ren Fang admired it very much when he saw the "Tuenyou Fu".
Zang Yan also wrote "Seven Calculations", and the diction is also very rich and gorgeous.
Zang Yan was upright and upright by nature, and did not follow the rules. He had never paid a visit to Xu Mian in this world. Xu Mian wanted to get to know him, but Zang Yan still refused to pay him a visit.
Zang Yan moved to the position of champion to join the army and served as an assistant to King Shu of Hunan Province. He also accumulated merit and moved to the Qingche Mansion of King Xuanhui of Hunan Province to join the army and concurrently served as the recorder's office.
Zang Yan learned and memorized a lot of knowledge, and was especially proficient in "Han Shu". He recited it skillfully and blurted it out.
The King of Xiangdong once tested Zang Yan with four bibliographies. From Volume A to Volume D, Zang Yan answered one thing asked by King Xiangshu in each volume, as well as the name of the author. Zang Yan is so knowledgeable.
King Shu of Hunan moved to serve as the governor of Jingzhou, and Zang Yan followed the palace and was transferred to Xizhonglang Anxi Lushi to join the army.
Wei Yan successively served as the governor of Yiyang County and the prefect of Wuning. He served many times in barbarian areas. In the past, county governors often selected military generals and led troops to guard the area. However, Zang Yan only led a few disciples to ride in a car and entered the county. The barbarians were convinced, so the banditry also disappeared.
The king of eastern Hunan came to Beijing and was appointed as Shitou garrison. Zang Yan was dismissed and appointed as Anyou Lushi.
King Shu of Hunan moved to be the governor of Jiangzhou, and Zang Yan was appointed as Zhennan counselor to join the army.
Zang Yan died during his tenure. He has ten volumes of collected works.
The word "Futing" is Shibiao.
His father Fu Qu served as the internal history of Yuzhang. Fu Qu's deeds were recorded in "Biography of Good Officials".
Futing was smart since he was a child. He could read "The Classic of Filial Piety" and "The Analects of Confucius" by the age of seven.
When he grew up, he was very talented and liked to write articles. His five-character poems were good at imitating Xie Kangle's style.
Futing's father's friend Le'an Renfang admired him deeply and thought he was a genius.
Ren Fang once said: There is no other talent like Fu Ting in Beijing today. At the end of the Qi Dynasty, Fu Ting was promoted as a scholar in the state, and Fu Ting's countermeasures ranked first at that time.
When Gaozu's rebel army came to the capital, Fu Ting rushed to Xinlin to meet the rebel army and pay homage to Gaozu. Gaozu was very happy to see him, called him "Yan Zi", and promoted him to join the army as Zheng Shuxing. Fu Ting was only eighteen years old at this time.
In the early years of Tianjian, Fu Ting was awarded the title of military officer in the Chinese army.
Fu Ting's residence was in Chaogou, and he lectured on "The Analects of Confucius" in his residence. Officials from all over the dynasty came to listen to him.
Fu Ting moved to Jian Kangzheng, but was soon removed from office due to impeachment.
After a long time, Fu Ting went to Beijing again and served as Shangshu Yi Caolang. He moved to Xizhonglang's Ji office and joined the army. He successively served as the order of Jinling and Wukang.
After being relieved of his duties as county magistrate, he returned to the capital, built a house in the eastern suburbs, and stopped serving as an official.
Fu Ting had a great reputation when he was young, and he got along well with people at that time. Most of the powerful ministers in important positions and idle officials without real power in the court had contacts with Fu Ting, so Fu Ting could not remain in retirement for a long time.
At that time, Pushe Xu Mian asked for leave to go home because of illness. Fu Ting wrote to Xu Mian to gauge Xu Mian's thoughts. The letter said:
In the past, when a scholar missed his old friend, his longing lingered for several days; when Wang Fusi missed his friend, he kept worrying about him for ten days.
summary: Zang Yan, courtesy name Yanwei, was from Ju. He was filial and studious. He wrote "Tuenyou Fu," which Ren Fang admired. He was upright and did not follow rules. He was knowledgeable, especially in "Han Shu." He served as a county governor in barbarian areas, where he quelled banditry. He died during his tenure. He has ten volumes of collected works. Fu Ting, courtesy name Shibiao. He was smart and talented, good at five-character poems. Ren Fang admired him. He met Emperor Gaozu at eighteen and was promoted. He lectured on "The Analects." He later built a house in the eastern suburbs and stopped serving. He wrote a letter to Xu Mian, expressing his desire for seclusion. Xu Mian replied, praising him but encouraging him to serve. Fu Ting later became an official again but was accused of accepting bribes. He hid as a Taoist priest. He later served under King Shaoling. He died during Hou Jing's rebellion. He wrote ten volumes of "Yi Shuo" and twenty volumes of collected works. His son, Fu Zhiming, served Hou Jing and died in prison.

translation:
When he first joined the army as Cao Xing of Anxi Fa, Yu Yong had already held a distinguished position at that time. Xu Mian, the Minister of Civil Affairs, planned to let Yu Yong's son Yu Yanying serve as an official of the prince. Yu Yong said to Xu Mian with tears: My brother's son Yu Zhongrong has been an orphan since he was a child, and he has a little talent. I hope to appoint him to the position that Yu Yanying will fill.
Xu Mian agreed to Yu Yong's request and appointed Yu Zhongrong as the crown prince.
Yu Zhongrong was moved to the position of chief administrator of King Ancheng.
At that time, Pingyuan Liu Xiaobiao was also serving as a staff member in the palace. Both of them were treated politely by King Ancheng because of their diligent study.
Yu Zhongrong moved to the post of King Gongcao Shi of Jin'an.
He successively served as the magistrate of Yongkang, Qiantang, and Wukang, but had no outstanding performance in managing county affairs, and was often impeached.
After a long time, Yu Zhongrong was dismissed and granted the title of Prince Ancheng's Zhongji Office, and he was about to leave the capital to follow the royal palace. Because Yu Zhongrong was formerly a vassal of the crown prince, the crown prince made an exception and held a farewell banquet because he missed his old relationship. The crown prince gave Yu Zhongrong a poem and said: Sun Sheng Zhiyang Road, Chaoge County, Wuzi, was not like Fan Linju, and set up wine in Linhua Palace.
At that time, people thought it was a great honor to send Yu Zhongrong away.
Yu Zhongrong moved to King Wuling of Anxi to consult and join the army.
Later, he was awarded the title of Minister Zuocheng, but he was dismissed because he investigated the case and corrected the unfairness of impeachment officials.
Yu Zhongrong was very knowledgeable and had a great reputation when he was young. However, he was very impulsive, used wine to drink, and liked to make upright and extraordinary remarks. His friends among the scholars looked down upon him because of this.
Yu Zhongrong only had similar personalities and good friendships with Wang Ji, Xie Jiqing and others. Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing were not in harmony with everyone at that time, so the three of them socialized together, drank as much as they wanted, and no longer paid attention to ethics.
After a long time, Yu Zhongrong was appointed as a consultant to join the army and left the capital to serve as the magistrate of Yi County.
When the turmoil broke out during the Taiqing period, Yu Zhongrong lived in Kuaiji and died of illness at the age of seventy-four.
Yu Zhongrong copied thirty volumes of books by various scholars, twenty volumes of geography books of various schools, three volumes of Biography of Women, and twenty volumes of collected works. These books are all circulated in the world.
Lu Yungong, named Zilong, was from Wujun.
His grandfather Lu Xian lived in Renzhou.
His father, Lu Wan, had a long history with Ren Ningyuan.
When Lu Yungong was five years old, he could recite "The Analects of Confucius" and "Mao Shi". When he was nine years old, he could read "Han Shu" and memorize everything.
His grandfather Lu Bian and Pei Guo Liu Xian asked him about ten things in the "Book of Han", and he could answer them one by one without making any mistakes. Liu Xian was full of praise and thought he was different from ordinary people.
When he grew up, Lu Yungong was studious and talented.
He was elected as a scholar in the state.
Lu Yun Gongjigong was transferred to the throne of Xuanhui, King of Wuling, and King of Pingxi, Xiangshu, to join the army.
Lu Yungong originally wrote the "Taibo Temple Stele". Zhang Zuan, the governor of Wuxing, left his post and returned to the capital. On the way, he read the inscription written by Lu Yungong and said with emotion: This man is simply the contemporary Cai Bojie.
After Zhang Zuan arrived in the capital, he was in charge of the selection of officials. He recommended Lu Yungong to Emperor Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu then called Lu Yungong to serve as the minister of Yi Cao Lang. He was soon appointed to this position and was assigned to Shouguang Province. He also used his original official position to know how to serve as a minister.
Soon after, in addition to being awarded the title of Writer, he was moved to the post of Zhongshu Huangmenlang and was in charge of writing.
Lu Yungong was good at playing Go. He once accompanied Gaozu at night. The crown he was wearing caught the light of a candle. Gaozu smiled and said to him: The candle burned the mink tail on your hat.
Gaozu was about to appoint Lu Yungong as his minister, and his crown would be decorated with a mink tail, so Gaozu used these words to joke with Lu Yungong.
At that time, a new bream boat was built in Tianyuanchi. The boat was wide and short. Gaozu often took this boat to ride on the waves in his spare time. Among the courtiers, he only brought Taichang Liu Zhilin, Guozi to Gai, and Youwei Zhu Yi. Lu Yungong was young at that time and his position was not high, but he was also among the courtiers who accompanied Gaozu on the boat.
Emperor Gaozu's favor and favor towards him reached such an extent.
In the first year of Taiqing, Lu Yungong passed away at the age of thirty-seven.
Emperor Gaozu was deeply saddened by his death and wrote an edict in his own hand, saying: I serve as the minister of Huangmen and as Duke Lu Yungong. He is a rising star with beautiful demeanor and broad knowledge.
summary: Yu Zhongrong, courtesy name Zhongrong, was from Geling. He lost his father young and was studious. He was appointed as a crown prince through his uncle's request. He was knowledgeable but impulsive and liked to drink. He was friends with Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing. He died at seventy-four. He copied many books and wrote several works. Lu Yungong, courtesy name Zilong, was from Wujun. He could recite classics at a young age. He was studious and talented. He wrote the "Taibo Temple Stele," which Zhang Zuan praised. He was called to serve by Emperor Gaozu. He was good at Go. Emperor Gaozu favored him greatly. He died at thirty-seven. Emperor Gaozu mourned him. Zhang Zan wrote a letter expressing his sorrow.

translation:
Lu Yungong's cousin Lu Caizi was also famous for his talent. He successively served as Zhongshulang, Xuancheng Wangyou, and Prince's concubine. Ting Weiqing died before Lu Yungong.
Lu Caizi and Lu Yungong both have collections of essays, which are also circulated in the world.
Ren Xiaogong, whose courtesy name is Xiaogong, was born in Linhuai.
His great-grandfather was a farmer and the governor of Southern Yuzhou during the Song Dynasty.
Ren Xiaogong lost his father when he was young. He served his mother very filially and became famous for this.
Ren Xiaogong was dedicated and diligent in his studies. His family was poor and he often asked people to borrow books when he had no books to act in.
Every time he read it, he could recite it without missing anything.
Ren Cuoyu's maternal grandfather, Qiu Ta, had a relationship with Emperor Gaozu. Hearing that Ren Xiaogong was talented and learned, he summoned him to the Western Province to compile history books.
Ren Xiaogong was first appointed to the imperial court, and was promoted to Shouguang Province as the Minister of Si Wen. Soon he was also appointed as Zhongshu General Shiren.
Emperor Gaozu issued an edict and ordered Ren Xiaogong to write the "Inscription under the Temple of Jianling Temple". Ren Xiaogong also presented the "Preface" to the collected works of Emperor Gaozu written by himself. The words were rich and gorgeous. From the time of the Han Dynasty, Ren Xiaogong was in charge of the court's documents full-time.
Ren Xiaogong wrote articles quickly, and he could write them immediately after receiving the imperial edict. It seemed that he didn't spend much time on it. He wrote good articles and presented them to memorials. Emperor Gaozu always praised his well-written articles and gave him gold and silk many times.
When he was young, Ren Xiaogong read scriptures with Master Xiao Siyun and was well versed in Buddhist teachings. When he was sent away, Ren Xiaogong only ate vegetables, followed the precepts, and believed in Buddhism very sincerely.
However, Ren Xiaogong liked to show off his achievements by nature, and often relied on his talents to put himself above others. He often showed contempt for famous figures at that time, and the world looked down upon him because of this.
In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing invaded the capital, and Ren Xiaogong started recruiting sergeants. He led the recruited soldiers to be affiliated with Xiao Zhengde and stationed on the south bank of the Yangtze River.
When the rebel army arrived, Xiao Zhengde led his army to surrender to Hou Jing, and Ren Xiaogong returned to rush to the palace city. The gate of the palace city had been closed, so Ren Xiaogong fled into Dongfu. Soon Shufu was attacked by the rebels, and Ren Xiaogong was killed.
Ren Xiaogong's collected works are circulated in the world.
Yan Xie, courtesy name Zihe, was from Linyi, Langxie.
His ancestor Yan Han, seven generations ago, served as Shizhong, Guozi Jijiu, and Jinghou of Xiping during the Jin Dynasty.
His father is far-sighted, knowledgeable, ambitious and ethical.
In the past, when Emperor Qi He was guarding Jingzhou, he appointed Yan Jianyuan to join the army for the green affairs. When Emperor Qi He ascended the throne in Jiangling, he appointed Yan Jianyuan to serve as the official secretary and censor, and soon became the Zhongcheng.
After Emperor Gaozu accepted Qi's abdication, Yan Jianyuan went on a hunger strike and died in anger for several days.
When Emperor Gaozu heard the news, he said: I am following the destiny of heaven and obeying the will of man. What does it have to do with the scholar-bureaucrats in the world?
And Yan Jianyuan actually did such a thing!
Yan Xie lost his father when he was young and was raised by his uncle's family.
summary: Ren Xiaogong, courtesy name Xiaogong, was from Linhuai. He was filial and studious. He was summoned to compile history books. He wrote quickly and was praised by Emperor Gaozu. He was well-versed in Buddhism. He was arrogant and looked down on others. During Hou Jing's invasion, he led soldiers but was killed when the rebels attacked.

translation:
He has been praised for his magnanimity since childhood.
Yan Xie has extensively dabbled in group calligraphy and is good at writing cursive script and official script.
When Yan Xie first became an official, he took up the post of permanent attendant of the Xiangdong Kingdom, and also served as the official secretary of the government.
Shizu came out of the capital to guard Jingzhou, and Yan Xie was transferred to the office of actual professors and records.
At that time, Gu Xie of Wu County also served in the palace. He and Yan Xie had the same names, and their talents and learning were comparable. They were called "Er Xie" in the palace.
Yan Xie's uncle, Chen Jun Xie Chen, passed away. Yan Xie mourned his uncle with the same etiquette as he would an uncle because of his kindness to his uncle. People who talked about this matter valued Yan Xie's friendship more.
Yan Xie also felt that his father at home died for his righteousness, so he did not pursue prominent positions and often refused calls from the court, only serving in the feudal prince's palace.
In the fifth year of Datong, Yan Xie passed away at the age of forty-two.
Shizu lamented his death and wrote "Nostalgic Poems" to mourn him.
One of the chapters says: With great magnanimity and elegant demeanor, he is truly a talent in name and in reality!
Although they have been promoted, they have not yet been promoted, resulting in talented people still staying in positions with low salaries.
Five chapters of "Biography of Jinxian" and two volumes of "Disasters of the Sun and Moon" written by Yan Xie were burned down due to fire.
Yan Xie had two sons: Yan Zhiyi and Yan Zitui, both of whom became famous very early.
During the Chengsheng reign, Yan Zhitui was promoted to Zhengyuan Lang and Zhongshu Sheren.
Yao Cha, the Minister of Civil Affairs of Chen, said: Emperor Wen of Wei said that few ancient scholars could maintain their reputation. Why?
Literati must use their intelligence skillfully and reveal their ambitions differently. Therefore, they are prone to look down on their peers and show off their arrogance.
On big occasions, he will insult and despise princes and kings; on small occasions, he will look down on and insult his friends, which will lead to jealousy and sin.
For example, Qu Yuan and Mai Yi were ostracized and exiled, and Huan Tan and Feng Yan were reprimanded and dismissed. Sending them out was something that only happened once in a generation. It was really the disaster brought about by the arrogance of these literati!
The literary men recorded above were in an era of prosperous education, and they wrote articles with gorgeous rhetoric. They did not have depression and worries, and they did not encounter the disasters that the previous generations of literati suffered. It is really great.
The discussion shows that he is a kind of person who pays attention to destiny.
Sages rarely talk about things like fate. They tend to talk about fate and believe that fate must control life. This is not the meaning of the sages' classics.
summary: Yan Xie, courtesy name Zihe, was from Linyi. He lost his father young. He was magnanimous and good at calligraphy. He served in the Xiangdong Kingdom. He and Gu Xie were called "Er Xie." He mourned his uncle with proper etiquette. He did not pursue prominent positions. He died at forty-two. His works were burned in a fire. His sons, Yan Zhiyi and Yan Zitui, became famous early.

translation:
"Yi" says: A gentleman escapes from the world and does not feel bored. He is independent and does not know fear.
Confucius called Chang Ju and Jie Dun hermits.
Some hermits in ancient times were ashamed to hear about the Zen Dynasty, considered it noble to give up the throne, regarded the Wancheng throne as a disgrace, and went to death without any regrets.
This kind of person despises life and values ​​morality. He is rare in the world and appears occasionally. He is a superior hermit.
Some work as prison gates to support themselves, and work as officials under the pillars to support themselves. They live a simple life to realize their ambitions, and their status is low but they don't show any shame.
He was a so-called great hermit who hid in the city and court, and his status was lower than that of the superior hermits.
Some exposed their bodies, pretended to be crazy, blinded their eyes, made their voices hoarse, renounced the world, abandoned rituals and music to return to the right path, and suppressed the need to talk about filial piety, love, and family affection.
This kind of person protects himself, avoids harm, masters the way of escaping from the world, and his status is lower than that of the great hermit.
However, these people have not forgotten the key to keeping silent, staying on the right path in seclusion, and finally getting good results.
How can they and those who join in troubled times, compete for wealth and cater to the world, say the same thing? "Mencius" says: For people nowadays, regarding juelu, getting it is like gaining life, losing it is like losing life.
"Huainanzi said: People use still water as mirrors, not running water."
To be able to inspire righteousness, wash away filth, curb corruption and bend the law, and stop the pursuit of power and profit, I am afraid only a hermit can do it!
Since ancient times, there has been no emperor who did not respect the conduct of hermits.
Even Tang Yao couldn't make Chaofu and Xu You obey each other, and King Wu of Zhou couldn't make Boyi and Shuqi abandon their integrity and become ministers. Mo Gaozu was arrogant but respectful to Qili Ji and Xia Huang Gong. Mo Guang Wu Emperor governed the world according to the law but was submissive to Yan Guang and Zhou Dang. Since then, this has been the case for generations.
During the Liang Dynasty, the country prospered and inherited the moral education and governance of the previous generation. All the hermits whose morals were worthy of imitation and whose knowledge could serve as role models were included in the "Chushi Pian".
When the word Zixi comes, the Lujiang River sneaks in.
His grandfather, He Shangzhi, served as Sikong during the Song Dynasty.
His father, He Shuo, was appointed governor of Yidu.
He Shuo had always suffered from madness. He killed his wife for no reason and was executed according to the law.
He Dian was eleven years old at the time, and his life was almost destroyed by the grief of losing his parents.
When he grew up, He Dian was saddened by the disasters that had happened in his family and wanted not to get married or become an official, so He Shangzhi forced him to marry the Wang family of Langye.
All other etiquette had been completed, and when the wedding ceremony was about to take place, He Dian cried to He Shangzhi again and again, begging to be allowed to stick to his original wishes, so that the wedding was suspended.
He Dian has a dignified and comely appearance, is well-read, and is good at talking and discussing.
The He Dian family was originally a wealthy family, with many in-laws serving as high-ranking officials.
summary: The highest are those who value morality above life itself, despising wealth and power, and willing to face death without regret—rare figures who occasionally appear. The second tier includes "great hermits" who hide within cities or courts, living simply to fulfill their ambitions without shame despite low status. The third tier consists of those who feign madness, blind themselves, or abandon rituals to protect themselves and escape worldly entanglements. All these hermits, however, master the art of silence and seclusion, ultimately achieving good outcomes, unlike those who chase wealth and cater to the world. The text quotes Mencius and Huainanzi to emphasize that hermits alone can inspire righteousness and curb corruption. Historically, no emperor has failed to respect hermits. Even Tang Yao could not compel Chaofu and Xu You to obey, nor could King Wu of Zhou force Boyi and Shuqi to serve. Emperors like Gaozu of Han and Guangwu of Han showed deference to hermits such as Qili Ji and Yan Guang. During the Liang Dynasty, hermits with exemplary morals were recorded in the "Chushi Pian."

translation:
Although He Dian did not enter the city or enter the government, he only wore household clothes, without hairpins or belts, and traveled among the people. Sometimes he drove a chariot and wore straw sandals. At that time, people called this point "Tongyin".
He Dian's brother He Qiu also lived in seclusion in Huqiu Mountain in Wu County.
After He Qiu's death, He Dian only ate vegetarian food and did not drink alcohol during the period of mourning for his brother. After the three-year mourning period was over, He Dian's waist circumference had been reduced by half.
In the early and late years of the Song and Tai Dynasties, the imperial court conscripted He Dian to serve as the prince to wash horses; in the early years of the Qi Dynasty, the court repeatedly recruited He Dian to serve as Zhongshulang and the prince's concubine, but none of them accepted the call.
He became close friends with Xie Man of Chen Jun, Zhang Rong of Wu State, and Kong Zhigui of Kuaiji.
He Dian's cousin, He Dun, gave He Dian a manor in Donglimen to live in, and Kong Zhigui built a house in the garden for He Dian.
There is Bian Zhongzhen's tomb in the garden. He planted flowers on the side of the tomb. Every time he drank, he must first sprinkle the wine on the ground to pay homage to Bian Zhongzhen.
At first, when Chu Yuan and Wang Jian were prime ministers, He Point said to people: I wrote "Qishu Praise", which said: "Chu Yuan is from a noble family, and Wang Jian is also a talented person in the country. Who can care about the country without relying on these close relatives and old ministers?"
When Wang Jian heard this, he originally wanted to visit Hedian, but later he realized that he could not see Hedian, so he gave up the plan.
Xiao Yi, the king of Yuzhang, drove to visit He Dian, but He Dian escaped through the back door.
Xiao Ziliang, King of Situ Jingling, wanted to condescend to meet He Dian. He Dian was at Falun Temple at that time. Xiao Ziliang went to Falun Temple to request to meet He Dian. He Dian dressed up as a hermit and sat at the table. Xiao Ziliang was so happy that he gave Ji Shuye's wine glass and Xu Jingshan's wine pot to He Dian.
He Diandian suffered from thirsty dysentery when he was young and was not cured for many years.
Later, He Dian established a forum at Wuzhong Shifo Temple. He once took a nap in the place where he lectured. He dreamed that a Taoist with a special appearance gave him a handful of pills. He swallowed the pills in his dream, and he recovered from his illness. People at that time believed that this was a blessing brought by honest virtue.
He Dian was free-spirited by nature, not constrained by trivial matters, and loved to give to others. He would not disobey anything given to him by people near or far, he would accept everything, and then give away what he received to others.
He Dian once passed by Zhuquemen Street in a car. Someone stole He Dian's clothes from the back of the car. He Dian saw it but kept silent. Someone caught the person stealing the clothes and handed it to He Dian. He Dian then gave the clothes to the person who stole the clothes. The person who stole the clothes did not dare to accept it. He Dian threatened to report it to the government. The person who stole the clothes was scared, so he accepted the clothes donated by He Dian. He Dian urged the person who stole the clothes to leave quickly.
He Dian is very discerning in identifying talents, and he has identified and recommended many people. When Wu Xingqiu Chi was still a child, he admired him very much; when Ji Yang Jiangyan was still in a low status, Bao Shu praised him.
Later, both of them showed their talents as He Dian said. When He Dian grew old, he married the daughter of Kong Si of Lu, who was also a hermit.
Although He Dian was married, he did not meet his wife and built another house to accommodate her. No one understood his intention to do this.
Zhang Rong of the State of Wu was dismissed from office when he was young. There are sentences in the poems he wrote that indicated that he did not seek official advancement. The poem "He Dian Reward" said: In the past, I heard about Sedu, but I was not in front of the bamboo slips.
This means that Zhang Rong was removed from his official position and was no longer busy with paperwork.
Although this is a joke, Rei Rong has always regarded writing poems as a problem. Later, when He Dian got married, Zhang Rongcai wrote another poem to He Dian, saying: What a pity, the dusk is so desolate.
Joking about Bao Wei's marriage incident in his later years. He Dian also regarded this poem as a problem in his heart, but he never found a chance to resolve it.
Gaozu and He Dian had a relationship. After Gaozu ascended the throne, he wrote an edict with his own hand and said: In the past, because I had more free time, I was able to associate with you. We sat together in the bamboo forest, perched on the clear pond, forgetting the troubles in front of us, and discussing ancient people and events. How happy it was.
summary: The text then details the lives of several notable hermits. He Dian, from a wealthy family, refused marriage and office after his father’s execution, living simply among the people. He rejected multiple imperial summons, fled from nobles who sought him, and gave away stolen clothes to a thief. He was known for his discerning judgment of talent and his unconventional marriage, where he did not meet his wife. Emperor Gaozu, an old friend, repeatedly invited him to court, offering gifts and honors, but He Dian remained reclusive until his death at sixty-eight.

translation:
He also ordered Yuzhe's younger brother Yuhuang to say: "Brother Zhengjun Baoyan, my virtuous brother, has lived in seclusion since he was weak, and his conduct has remained unchanged until his twilight years."
He set his sights on things other than the world and did not pursue fame, fortune or wealth; he was dissolute and committed to pursuing profound philosophy.
He has an elegant temperament, which is reflected even more when he is interested; he is talented in literature and wine, and his lofty purpose is even more felt during the handover.
I have to accept the chart, become the emperor at the right moment, and want to carry forward the teachings.
There are many modest gentlemen in the court, which can make the elegant people and the secular people admire the gentleman's style; there are ministers who live in seclusion in the countryside, and they should also promote the character of not seeking official career.
I am about to rely on their elegant conversation to prosper the imperial industry.
In the past, when Hengyan was still an ordinary citizen, my friendship with him had already been revealed. I gave him a salary just like Emperor Mozhang treated Zheng Zhongyu, and treated him with courtesy like Emperor Guangwu treated Yan Ziling. On my free days when I was dealing with government affairs, I invited him to see him in common clothes. In the deep and secluded place where he lived, I provided him with food and supplies so that he could rely on him in life.
Suddenly he passed away, which really shocked me and mourned me.
You and Brother Tanwei have a very deep relationship. Now that your relatives have left this world, your wish to share the rest of your life can no longer be realized. How can I bear this lingering regret. What to do if things continue like this!
But Nian had no sons, and his clansmen considered He Ji, the son of He Dian's cousin He Ta, as Yu Yan's heir.
He Yin, whose courtesy name was Wang Ji, was He Dian's younger brother.
When he was eight years old, he mourned his parents and, like adults, his body was damaged by grief. As an adult, he loved learning.
He became a disciple of Peiguo Liu Shan and studied "Yi", "Book of Rites" and "Mao Shi"; he also went to Dinglin Temple in Zhongshan to study Buddhist scriptures. He learned all these things proficiently.
However, he was casual and informal. No one understood him at that time. Only Zhou Yong of Runan deeply valued him and thought he was a genius.
He Yin first served as Secretary Lang of Qi and moved to Prince Sheren.
He left the capital and served as the prefect of Jian'an. He emphasized kindness and trustworthiness in his administration, and the people could not bear to deceive him.
Every winter day, He Yin would release the prisoners home. These prisoners all returned as scheduled, and none of them took the opportunity to escape.
He Yin entered the capital and was appointed as the Third Duke of Shangshu. Before he was appointed, he was moved to the post of Situ's chief secretary.
He Yin annotated the "Book of Changes" and the "Book of Rites". The explanatory sentences were written on the back of the original book, so it is called "The Hidden Meaning of the Book of Rites".
He also accumulated merit and was moved to the post of Zhongshu Lang, a member of the Sanqi Changshi, a Taiwei as a Zhonglang, a Situ Youzhangshi, a Shilang of Huangmen, a concubine of the prince, a doctor of Guozi, and Zhongzheng of Danyang City.
Shangshu ordered Wang Jian to write a new etiquette in accordance with the emperor's order. Wang Jian died before he could finish it. The emperor ordered Zhang Xu to continue writing it. Zhang Xu died again. The emperor entrusted the task of continuing the writing to Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling. Xiao Ziliang gave the task to He Yin. So the imperial court assigned twenty bachelors to He Yin to help him write the new etiquette.
In the 10th year of Yongming Dynasty, He Yin was moved to the position of servant, led the infantry school captain, and became the prince of the country to offer wine.
King Yu Lin succeeded to the throne as emperor, and because He Yin was a relative of the queen, he was favored and treated favorably by his relatives.
After accumulating meritorious service, he was moved to the post of Zuo Min Shangshu, leading Xiaoqi, Zhongshu Ling, and leading the divisions of King Linhai and King Baling.
Although He Yin was rich and powerful, he often wanted to resign and retire.
In the early years of Jianwu, he had built a house in the suburbs, which he called a hill. He often lived in the house with his Shilin friends.
When he arrived, He Yin sold his house and wanted to live in seclusion in Dongshan. Before he started to prepare for the affair, He Yin heard that Xie Quan would not return to the capital after being dismissed from the post of governor of Wuxing County. He was worried that Xie Li would live in seclusion in Dongshan, so he resigned and left the capital without waiting for a reply from the court.
Emperor Ming was very angry and ordered Sai'ang, the censor Zhongcheng, to report to arrest He Yin. Soon after, he asked Shao to allow Bao Huang to resign.
He Yin thought that the mountains in Kuaiji were magical, so he went there to visit and stayed at Yunmen Temple in Ruoye Mountain.
At first, He Yin's two elder brothers had already secluded themselves from the world, and He Qiu had passed away. By this time, He Yin was living in seclusion again. At that time, people called He Point a big mountain and He Yin a small mountain, also known as Dongshan.
During the Yongyuan period, the imperial court conscripted Pan Pan as Taichang, and Prince Zhan did not go to his post.
The Prince of Gaozu's vassal was established, and He Yin was selected to serve as an army advisor and to offer wine sacrifices. Emperor Gaozu wrote to He Yin: If you roam freely in the mountains and forests, you will definitely bring endless joy. I hope you will always be comfortable.
Since the heart has given up the pursuit of fame and fortune, it will no longer have the trouble of being manipulated by external things. Use Tao to maintain inner harmony, and no action will go against one's own will.
If Xie Mountain occupies the beautiful scenery in the east, and the mountains and rivers are connected, the previous generations would have appreciated the beautiful scenery of Jixiang, and Qianhuo is indeed a paradise.
summary: He Yin, He Dian’s younger brother, was a scholar who studied Confucian and Buddhist texts. He served in minor official posts but later resigned to live in seclusion, building a house in the mountains. He refused high-ranking positions, even when Emperor Gaozu personally wrote to him, citing his age and health. He taught students, forbade killing, and was known for miraculous events, such as a deer seeking refuge with him and a strange bird appearing in his lecture hall. He died at eighty-six, leaving extensive annotations on the "Book of Changes" and "Book of Rites."

translation:
Medical doctor Zhong said: How do you know that the next line will not appear in the upper nine Yang Yao?
Ji Zhidao continued to arrange the hexagrams, and finally "Zhu Hexagram" appeared.
Zhang Youdao sighed and said: This image says that there is no disadvantage in fat escape. The hexagram corresponds to your virtue, and your heart and actions are consistent.
Ruan Xiaoxu said: Although the "Ei Gua" was obtained, the upper nine Yang Yao did not appear. The way to live in seclusion is to secede from the world like Xu You.
Zao Buxu then wrote the "Biography of Gao Yin", starting from Yan and Huang to the biography of the hermit in the last years of Zuo Jian, and rated these people as third grade, with a total of several volumes.
Ruan Xiaoxu also wrote "Gao Yin Zhuan Lun" and said: The highest foundation of Tao lies in advocating inaction; the actions of the saints are to save the evils of the times.
To remedy current problems, we must take action. Relying on action to achieve results violates the foundation of Tao. Since the foundation of Tao is advocating inaction, taking action is not the highest criterion of Tao.
However, if we do not take action, the world will not be stable; if we do not implement the fundamentals of Tao, Tao will eventually decline.
Confucius and Ji Dan wanted to insist on taking action, so they temporarily concealed the foundation of Tao; Lao Dan and Zhuang Zhou should conceal their actions as long as they promoted the foundation of Tao.
Actions can be concealed, which is why Lao and Zhuang felt free and at ease; fundamentals can be concealed, so Confucius felt powerless in busying with worldly affairs.
If a scholar cannot grasp one aspect, he will lack wise insights; if he can understand both aspects, he will have a unique ability to examine and discern.
In this way, when the saint has enlightened the world, he will turn around to expand the influence of his actions; before the wise man is in a position of being respected, he should promote the foundation of Tao.
The truth is that actions should remedy the current ills, and those who are not saints cannot undertake this task; principles should be used to explain principles, and wise men can know and show them to the world.
If you can understand the relationship between roots and actions, and understand the principle of ups and downs, then you can understand most of the thoughts of Confucius and Zhuang Zhou.
King Yuanxiang of Nanping heard about Ruan Xiaoxu's reputation and wrote a letter to invite Ruan Xiaoxu, but Ruan Xiaoxu refused to go.
Ruan Xiaoxu said: It's not that I mean to show arrogance in front of noble people, it's just that I'm naturally afraid of seeing the emperor.
If musk deer can drive, what is the difference between them and fine horses?
In the past, during the last years of Jianwu's reign, the Shumen of Qingxi Palace collapsed on its own for no apparent reason, and strong winds blew up the poplar trees outside the Shugong Gate.
Someone asked Ruan Xiaoxu about the incident. Ruan Xiaoxu said: Qingxi Palace was the emperor's original residence.
The five elements of Qi belong to wood, and the east is the direction of wood in the five elements. Now that Shumen collapses on its own, I am afraid that wood is about to decline.
Princess Zhonglie of Poyang is Ruan Xiaoxu's sister.
The King of Poyang once wanted to drive to Ruan Jizhong for fun, but Ruan Xiaoxu broke open the wall and escaped, never wanting to meet the King of Poyang.
Ruan Xiaoxu refused to accept any gifts from his nephews during the holidays.
Some people were surprised that Ruan Xiaoxu did this. Ruan Xiaoxu replied: It is not my original wish to receive the gift, so I do not accept it.
The stone statue that Ruan Xiaoxu worshiped all year round was damaged. Ruan Xiaoxu wanted to repair it. After one night, the stone statue suddenly became intact.
Everyone was surprised by this. In the second year of Datong, Ruan Xiaoxu died at the age of fifty-eight.
Ruan Xiaozhong's disciples listed Ruan Xiaoxu's virtues one after another and determined that his title was Wenzhen.
summary: Ruan Xiaoxu, from a wealthy family, refused inheritance and lived in poverty, avoiding even his prominent cousin Wang Yan. He was known for his filial piety, once finding ginseng for his mother by following a deer. He refused official summons, stating that seclusion depends on personal choice, not the state of the world. He wrote a "Biography of Gao Yin" and a treatise on the balance between action and inaction, arguing that saints act to remedy ills while wise men promote the foundation of Tao. He died at fifty-eight.

translation:
His "Qi Lu" and other books totaled 250 volumes and were circulated in the world.
Tao Hongjing, courtesy name Tongming, was born in Moling, Danyang.
It turned out that Tao Hongjing's mother dreamed that a green dragon came out of her arms, and at the same time she saw two gods coming to her place holding incense burners. Soon after, Tao's mother became pregnant and gave birth to Tao Hongjing.
Tao Hongjing has a unique talent since he was a child.
When he was ten years old, he got the Biography of Immortals written by Ge Hong, and he studied it day and night, and then he came up with the idea of ​​​​preserving health and longevity.
Tao Hongjing said to people: Looking up at the blue clouds and seeing the sun, it doesn't even feel far away.
When he grew up, Tao Hongjing was seven feet four inches tall, with a clean and beautiful expression, bright eyes, broad eyebrows, and long ears.
Tao Hongjing read more than 10,000 volumes.
He is good at playing the piano and chess, and is good at cursive and official script.
When Emperor Gaozu of Qi became the prime minister, Tao Hongjing, who was not yet in his prime, was selected to serve as the attendant of the kings and was awarded the title of court invitation.
Although Tao Hongjing lived in an imperial family, he stayed alone behind closed doors, did not interact with outsiders, and just studied.
The etiquette system of the imperial court largely depended on Tao Hongjing.
In the tenth year of Yongming's reign, Tao Hongjing resigned from his official position. The emperor issued an edict allowing him to resign and giving him a bunch of silk.
When Tao Hongjing left the capital, the officials of the imperial court gave him a farewell party at Zhenglu Pavilion. The banquet was so grand that the carriages and horses of the farewell blocked the road. Everyone said that since the Song and Qi Dynasties, there has never been such a grand farewell scene.
Both the government and the public consider this an honor.
So Tao Hongjing settled in Juqu Mountain in Jurong.
Tao Hongjing often said: At the foot of this mountain is the eighth cave palace, called Jintan Huayangzhitian, with a circumference of one hundred and fifty miles.
Once upon a time in the Mo Dynasty, there was a Sanmao Lord from Xianyang who succeeded in Taoism and came to take charge of this mountain, so this mountain is called Maoshan.
So Tao Hongjing built a house in the middle of the mountain and called it Huayang Seclusion.
Tao Hongjing began to learn the Talisman Sutra from Sun Youyue of Shuyang.
He traveled to famous mountains in search of elixirs.
Whenever he passes by the stream valley, Tao Hongjing must linger in it, chanting and sightseeing without stopping.
At that time, Shen Yue was the governor of Shuyang County. He admired Tao Hongjing's moral integrity and sent letters to Tao Hongjing many times to invite him, but Tao Hongjing did not agree.
Tao Hongjing is a man who understands things, is flexible in dealing with things, and treats others with humility and courtesy. Whether he is serving as an official or retiring, his actions meet this standard.
You can make decisions immediately when encountering problems, speak without being procrastinated and verbose, and feel them immediately even if they happen. During the Jianwu period, Xiao Keng, the king of Yidu in Qi, was killed by Emperor Ming. On the night when Xiao Keng was killed, Tao Hongjing dreamed that Xiao Keng came to say goodbye to him. Tao Hongjing asked Xiao Keng about things in the underworld. Xiao Keng told many secret and strange things in the underworld. Tao Hongjing wrote "Dream Notes" based on these things.
In the early years of Yongyuan, Tao Hongjing built another three-story building. Tao Hongjing lived on the top floor, his disciples lived on the middle floor, and guests stayed on the lower floor when they came. Tao Hongjing cut off contact with the rest of the world from then on, and had only one servant boy at home to serve him.
Tao Hongjing especially loved the sound of wind in the pine forest. Every time he heard the sound of the wind blowing in the pine forest, he felt happy.
Tao Hongjing sometimes played alone by the springs and rocks. People who saw him from a distance thought he was an immortal.
Tao Hongjing was fond of writing by nature, and he advocated strange things in his writings. He cherishes time, and will cherish it even more as he grows older.
He is especially proficient in yin and yang and the five elements, wind angle astrology, mountain geography, surrounding products, and medical materia medica.
Tao Hongjing wrote the "Almanac of the Emperors" and once created the Huntian phenomenon. Tao Hongjing said that the Huntian phenomenon was not only used by historians, but was also necessary for Bi Dao.
After the rebel army against Donghun Hou pacified Jiankang, Tao Hongjing heard that the Hua Dynasty was being discussed, so he quoted the prophecy, and after several deductions, it became the character "Liang", so Tao Hongjing ordered his disciples to submit the deduction results to the court.
Emperor Gaozu had long been friends with Tao Hongjing. After he ascended the throne, his favor and courtesy to Tao Hongjing became even more generous and considerate. He and Tao Hongjing exchanged letters continuously and sent envoys to visit Tao Hongjing one after another.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, Tao Hongjing moved to Jijinshujian.
Tao Hongjing is good at the health-preserving technique of bigu guidance. Although he is over eighty years old, he still maintains a healthy appearance.
Tao Hongjing deeply admired Zhang Liang's character and said that Zhang Liang was a Japanese man. Among the ancient sages, no one could compare with him.
Tao Hongjing once dreamed that the Buddha taught him the Bodhisattva. The god and Buddha said that his name was Shengli Bodhisattva.
Tao Hongjing then went to Ashoka Pagoda in Deng County to swear by himself and receive the five precepts.
Later, Taizong came to southern Xuzhou. He admired Tao Hongjing's style and qualities, so he called Tao Hongjing into the back hall. The two talked together for many days before Tao Hongjing left. Taizong respected Tao Hongjing very much and thought he was different from ordinary people.
In the early years of Datong, Tao Hongjing presented two swords to Emperor Gaozu. One sword was named Shansheng and the other was named Weisheng. They were both exquisite treasures.
In the second year of Datong, Tao Hongjing passed away at the age of eighty-one.
After his death, Tao Hongjing's appearance did not change, and his body flexed and stretched as usual.
summary: Tao Hongjing, a polymath, resigned from office at thirty-six to live in Maoshan, where he studied alchemy and the Talisman Sutra. He built a three-story house, cutting off contact with the world, and was known for his love of pine wind and his expertise in yin-yang, astrology, and medicine. He predicted the rise of the Liang dynasty through prophecies and maintained a close friendship with Emperor Gaozu, who frequently sent envoys. He died at eighty-one, leaving instructions for a modest burial.

translation:
When Fan Lingyu passed away, Fan Yuanyan was still a child, but his grief and longing, abiding by etiquette, and exhausting etiquette surprised his relatives.
When he grew up, Fan Yuanyan was fond of learning, knowledgeable, proficient in classics and history, and at the same time proficient in Buddhist teachings.
But he is humble and respectful by nature and does not treat others arrogantly based on his own strengths.
Fan Yuanyan's family was poor and he only made a living by growing vegetables in the garden.
Once, when Fan Yuanyan went out, he saw someone stealing food from his house. He hurriedly returned home. His mother asked him why he returned home, and he answered her truthfully.
His mother asked him again who stole the food. Fan Yuanyan replied: The reason why he hurriedly returned just now was because he was afraid that the person who stole the food would be ashamed when he saw me. Now I will tell you the name of the person and hope you will not leak it.
So the mother and son kept the incident a secret.
Someone waded across the ditch to steal the bamboo shoots in Fan Yuanyan's home. Fan Yuanyan cut down trees and built a bridge to facilitate the people who stole the bamboo shoots to cross the ditch.
From then on, those who stole things felt very ashamed, and no more thefts occurred in the township.
Fan Yuanyan often stayed at home and never went to the market. Even when he sat alone, he was dignified and respectful, as if he were facing a distinguished guest. Everyone who saw him looked solemn.
Liu Xian of Pei State thought highly of Fan Yuanyan and once praised him in a memorial ceremony.
In the second year of Jianwu of Qi Dynasty, Fan Yuanyan began to be recruited as an official by the imperial court and appointed him to join the military in Anbei. Fan Yuanyan did not take up his post.
In the ninth year of Tianjian's reign, the county magistrate Guan Huibian wrote a letter praising Fan Yuanyan's moral integrity. Yangzhou Governor Linchuan Wang Xiaohong summoned Fan Yuanyan to serve as an official in the name of the palace, but Fan Yuanyan refused.
In the tenth year of Tianjian, King Linchuan recommended Fan Yuanyan, but the court did not recruit him.
In the first year of his reign, Fan Yuanyan died at home at the age of seventy.
Liu Xu, courtesy name Yandu, was from Pingyuan.
His father Liu Lingzhen was the prefect of Wuchang during the Qi Dynasty.
When Liu Xu was young, he was known as filial and sincere. When he was just a few years old, his parents died one after another. During the mourning period for his parents, he cried and mourned and longed for them, almost destroying his own life. Everyone who came to express condolences felt sad for him.
Liu Xu was later raised by his uncle. He served his aunt and treated his brothers and sisters with great respect and kindness, and was praised by people in his clan.
Liu Xu was sad because he lost his parents very early. If someone made a mistake and offended his parents' reputation, he would feel depressed and cry sadly.
The eldest brother Liu Xu had engaged a woman to be Liu Xu's wife, and a date had been set for the marriage. When Liu Yu heard about the affair, he ran away and hid, and returned home only after the incident subsided.
Zhang Ji, the governor of this prefecture, summoned him to be the chief secretary, but he did not go to take office. The official in charge issued a summons to summon Liu Xu, but Liu Xu hung the summons on a tree and escaped.
Liu Xu was good at talking about Taoist mystical principles and was particularly proficient in Buddhist classics.
Liu Xu and his clan brother Liu Di once listened to Buddhist sermons in various temples in Zhongshan. Together, they chose a site to build a house in Shujian of Songxi Temple, and came up with the idea of ​​settling here for the rest of their lives.
In the seventeenth year of Tianjian, Liu Xiang died in Liu Di's home at the age of thirty-one.
When he was dying, Liu Xu took Liu Di's hand and said: I will be buried immediately after I die, and I will be buried immediately after the funeral. There is no need to set up a mourning hall or a memorial ceremony, no sacrifices, no heirs.
Liu Di all followed the instructions.
Liu Xu's fellow clan members and his friends carved an inscription on the stone tablet for him and gave him the title of Xuanzhen virgin.
Liu Xian, whose courtesy name was Shiguang, was the elder brother of the Zhu clan.
Liu Xian's grandfather, Liu Chengmin, was the governor of Jizhou during the Song Dynasty; his father, Liu Wenwei, was a Zhengyuanlang during the Qi Dynasty.
Father and son held the post of two thousand stones one after another, and both of them had a reputation of being pure and beautiful.
Liu Xian was smart and knowledgeable when he was young. When he was four years old, his father died. He is the only one who does not play among children.
Liu Xian could recite "The Analects of Confucius" and "Mao Shi" at the age of six. He could also ask questions and argue with them if he did not understand the meaning of the text.
When Liu Xian was eleven years old, he read "Zhuangzi's Xiaoyao Pian" and said: "I can explain this article."
Someone asked him a question, and he answered the question casually and his explanations were reasonable and reasonable. Everyone in his family was often surprised by this.
When he grew up, Liu Di was knowledgeable and talented. He did not marry a wife or become an official. He lived in seclusion with his brother Liu Xi to realize his pursuits, traveling around mountains, forests, rivers and lakes, and pursuing pleasure in mountains, rivers and books.
Liu Di often wanted to leave the world, but he could not bear to leave because his mother was old, so he often followed his brothers Liu Ji and Xingcha to serve as officials.
When Xingfu was young, he liked to give alms. When others were in need, he would always give alms, and he would not refuse anything given to him.
summary: Other hermits include Zhuge Gu, a teacher who refused office and lived in poverty; Shen Yi, who remained content despite extreme hardship; Liu Huifei, who copied Buddhist scriptures in Kuangshan; Fan Yuanyan, who hid his kindness to thieves; Liu Xu, who fled his own wedding; and Liu Xian, who wrote a treatise on death and burial, advocating simplicity. Yu Shen, a scholar of vast knowledge, lived frugally, forgave a thief, and refused official posts, dying at seventy-eight. Zhang Xiaoxiu and Yu Chengxian also lived in seclusion, the latter known for his lectures on Laozi.

translation:
King Zhonglie of Poyang also ordered Yu Cheng to preach "Laozi" first. Famous monks from near and far gathered together to raise various questions and heresies. Yu Chengxian answered them one by one calmly and calmly. Everyone who attended the meeting heard truths they had never heard of before.
King Zhonglie of Poyang admired and respected Yu Chengxian even more and made him the governor of the state. When King Xiangshu heard the news, he also appointed Yu Chengxian to join the army in the name of his own palace, but Yu Chengxian did not even go to the post.
In the third year of Zhongdatong, Liu Huifei from Lushan came to Jingzhou. Yu Chengxian had a friendship with Liu Huifei, so he went to visit Liu Huifei.
Scholars from Jingshan and Shanxi took this opportunity to ask Yu Cheng to speak about "Laozi" first.
The King of Eastern Hunan came to listen to the lecture in person and discussed it with Yu Chengxian for a whole day. He was deeply impressed by him.
King Xiangshu also invited Yu Chengxian to the palace and stayed there for more than a month before Yu Chengxian returned to the mountains.
When he returned to the mountain, King Xiangshu personally held a farewell banquet for him and wrote poems as gifts. People who lived in seclusion felt that this was an honor.
This year, Yu Chengxian died at the age of sixty.
Yao Chaqiu, the Minister of the Ministry of Official Affairs of Chen, said: Most of the people in the world who speak ill of virgins accuse them of simply stealing empty names without any merits suitable for world use. They are really people who do not deserve their names.
With Zhuge Can's knowledge and Ruan Xiaoxu's family background, how could they have any difficulty in seeking official positions?
It is simply their nature to spend their lives in seclusion.
summary: The text concludes with a reflection by Yao Chaqiu, who defends hermits against accusations of stealing empty names, noting that figures like Zhuge Can and Ruan Xiaoxu could have easily sought office but chose seclusion by nature.

translation:
In the past, Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty believed that if his administration was fair and orderly, and his lawsuits could be heard fairly, he would be considered a good governor!
The history books of the previous dynasties also said: The current county guards are the ancient princes.
Therefore, local governors are called officials who are close to the people. Therefore, they must be responsible for persuading the people to establish virtues, using etiquette to clean up the folk customs, and changing customs.
At the end of the Qi Dynasty, the government was in chaos, and power fell into the hands of a group of villains. All kinds of taxes were levied harshly, and corvees were collected without restraint.
Emperor Gaozu was among the people and understood the sufferings of the people. After the Liang Wangtai Mansion was established, Emperor Gaozu frequently issued orders to treat the people leniently and exempted and suspended all kinds of heavy taxes that were imposed when the government was in chaos. As a result, the people all over the world had the opportunity to recuperate.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he personally understood various affairs, dealt with political affairs at night, and understood the sufferings and illnesses of the people.
So envoys were sent to inspect the customs and sentiments of various places, and lung stones were set up outside the imperial court gates so that the poor and helpless people could complain about their grievances, sympathize with the people and relieve their sufferings and hardships.
In the first year of Tianjian, the taxes levied on minors began to be removed, and taxes were only levied on adults. Emperor Gaozu himself wore washed old clothes, and there were no luxurious decorations hidden in the treasury. The people in the court wore only silk, without pearls and brocades. The eunuchs followed Emperor Gaozu's order and did not have food or wine. They only ate vegetables and vegetarian food every day, and even if they drank no more than three cups, they all used their frugality to set an example for the people of the world.
Every time when Emperor Gaozu selected local governors, he would always select those who were honest and fair. When local governors took office, Emperor Gaozu personally summoned them and encouraged them to implement benevolent policies and govern the people.
The great ancestor promoted Dao Gai, a lieutenant in the Shangshu Palace, to serve as the internal history of Jian'an. Zuo Min's minister Liu was appointed as the prefect of Jin'an. After Dao Gai and others took office, they were all known for their integrity.
Emperor Gaozu also issued an order: If the officials serving as magistrates of small counties are capable, they can be promoted to magistrates of large counties; if the magistrates of large counties are capable, they can be promoted to county governors.
At this time, Qiu Zhongfu, the magistrate of Shanyin County, had outstanding political achievements, so he was appointed as the internal history of Changsha; the magistrate of Wukang He Yuan was honest and fair, so he was appointed as the prefect of Xuancheng.
Those who served as local governors were admired and imitated for a while, and it became a fashion.
People who held the position of local governors, such as Xinye Yumo, used Confucian classics to embellish government orders. Some of them extended favors to the people they governed, and some were still remembered by the people after leaving office. These can be regarded as good officials in the future.
Qian Bao compiled their deeds into "Good Officials".
Yu imitated the courtesy name Xiuye, a new savage.
His father Yu Shenzhi was the governor of Yongzhou during the Song Dynasty.
summary: Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty believed that fair administration and proper handling of lawsuits defined a good governor. Historical records note that local governors, considered "officials close to the people," were responsible for promoting virtue, refining customs, and changing social practices through etiquette. During the chaotic end of the Qi Dynasty, power fell into villainous hands, with harsh taxes and unrestrained corvée labor. Emperor Gaozu, having lived among the people and understood their suffering, frequently issued lenient orders after establishing his rule, exempting heavy taxes and allowing the populace to recuperate. After ascending the throne, Emperor Gaozu personally attended to state affairs, working through the night and understanding the people's hardships. He sent envoys to inspect local customs, set up complaint stones outside the imperial court for the poor to voice grievances, and showed sympathy for the suffering. In the first year of Tianjian, taxes on minors were removed, with only adults taxed. The emperor wore washed old clothes, kept no luxuries in the treasury, and court officials wore only silk without pearls or brocades. Eunuchs followed his example, eating only vegetables and drinking no more than three cups, setting a frugal example for the nation. When selecting local governors, Emperor Gaozu chose honest and fair individuals, personally summoning them to encourage benevolent governance. He promoted capable officials from small counties to larger ones, and from larger counties to governorships. Notable appointees included Dao Gai as internal history of Jian'an and Liu as prefect of Jin'an, both known for integrity. Qiu Zhongfu, magistrate of Shanyin County, was promoted to internal history of Changsha for outstanding achievements, while He Yuan of Wukang became prefect of Xuancheng for honesty. These governors became admired models, with some using Confucian classics to embellish government orders and being remembered fondly by the people after leaving office.

translation:
When Yu Fang was ten years old, his father died. During the mourning period, Yu Fang was so sad that his bones were broken, so he was praised by people in the same state.
In the weak year of his crown, he was selected as the chief bookkeeper by the state, promoted scholars, and was promoted to the chief bookkeeper of Anxi, the lieutenant of the Shangshu Palace, and the hussar cavalry officer.
Yu Fang read extensively in books and was extremely eloquent.
During the Yongming Dynasty, the State of Qi had friendly exchanges with Chong Yu Mi. The imperial court ordered Yu Mi to serve as a regular servant of Sanqi and serve as an envoy to pay a return visit to Qiaoli. After returning to the country, Yu Mi was appointed as a minister of Sanqi, and he was in charge of keeping records of the palace.
When King Yu Lin ascended the throne and was deposed, Yu Fang presided over the writing of Shao Gao. Later, Yu Ming left the capital and served as Jingzhou's charioteer.
Then he was moved to Xizhonglang to consult and join the army, and then he was appointed as Jingzhou Biejia.
In the past, those who held the position of Biejia in Jingzhou relied on this position to make their families rich and wealthy. Yu Ma held this position twice, but he set an example for his subordinates by being honest and incorruptible. He refused to ask for private favors, lived a life of poverty, and lived a life of poverty. His wife and children were inevitably hungry and cold.
When Emperor Ming heard about Yu Mi's situation, he appreciated it very much and wrote an imperial edict to commend Yu Mi himself. People in the state felt that this was a great honor.
Yu Feng moved to the post of Situ to consult and join the army, and became a regular attendant of Tongzhi Sanqi.
Gao Biao pacified the capital, established the royal palace, selected Yu Fang to serve as a hussar cavalry officer to join the army, and moved Yu Fang to serve as Zuocheng, the minister.
He also left the capital to serve as the assistant minister of the state, and was good at meeting with Deng Cheng and handling county government affairs.
At that time, after the country was in turmoil, people's livelihood was in decline, and there were famines. Rice was expensive everywhere, and the price of rice rose to thousands of dollars per stone. As a result, most of the people fled and became homeless. Yu Fang subsidized the people and had very good political achievements.
He himself only enjoys the state salary and adheres to noble moral integrity more strictly. Therefore, his family is very poor. Sometimes he even does not light a fire to cook all day long because of lack of firewood and rice.
When King Yongyang, the prefect of Kuaiji, heard that he was poor, he donated money and property to him, but Yu Cao declined politely and refused to accept it.
