In the first year of Tianjian, Yu Ming died. After his death, Yu Dan's body was left lying there. His family had no money for funeral arrangements and the coffin could not be buried.
When Emperor Gaozu heard the news, he gave the Yu family a hundred bolts of silk and fifty hu of rice.
At the beginning, Yu Mi's family belonged to a prominent family in Western Chu, and he had already held an important official position at an early age. Yu Fang's fellow countryman was cheerful and talented, but he had always been at odds with Yu Fang. The two competed everywhere and refused to give in to each other.
Le Ai served Xiao Yi, the king of Yuzhang in Qi. After Xiao Yi's death, Le Ai's official career was not satisfactory, so he helped handle defensive matters as an infantry captain and returned to Jingzhou. At that time, Yu Miao was appointed as a farewell officer in Jingzhou, so he despised Le Ai even more.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Le Ai was appointed as the Censor Zhongcheng for his meritorious service in helping Liang revitalize the emperor's career. However, Yu Fang was only given the position of Kuaiji County Affairs Bureau. Yu Fang already felt that this was a shame, and he When Yu Cao made minor mistakes in handling government affairs, Emperor Gaozu sent Le Ai to preach to Yu Ge because he was a fellow countryman of Yu Ge. Yu Cao was so angry that he fell ill and died.
summary: The text provides detailed biographies of several officials. Yu Mi, from a prominent Western Chu family, served in various positions including as envoy to Qiaoli. Known for honesty, he twice held the position of Biejia in Jingzhou without seeking personal gain, living in poverty with his family suffering hunger and cold. Emperor Ming commended him, and after his death in Tianjian's first year, Emperor Gaozu provided silk and rice for his burial.

translation:
Shen Zhen, courtesy name Boyu, was from Wukang, Wuxing. His uncle Shen Chang.
Serving Liu Jingsu, King of Song Jianhu, Liu Jingsu rebelled. Shen Chang had left Liu Jisai beforehand. Liu Jisai's rebellion plan was exposed, and Nalong was imprisoned for being implicated. Shen Ma rushed to the Yushitai to present the truth to his uncle and asked for pardon. His uncle Shen Chang was exempted from guilt, and Shen Li became famous.
Shen Zhen first became an official in the state and was invited by the court.
Shen Ma once went to visit Yin Yong, the right prime minister of Qi Shangshu. Yin Pu discussed political affairs with Shen Li. When he heard the opinions on selecting the base, he thought highly of Yi Ji and said to him: "Looking at your talents, you will serve as our official position."
Prince Liang of Situ Jingling heard about Shen Zhen's reputation, so he chose Xuan Ma as his government to join the army and lead Shen Zhen's ministry.
At that time, Shen Li was bullied by his power, and Shen Zhen punished Shen Huifu according to the law. From then on, everyone was afraid of Xuan Ma's strength and integrity.
Xiao Ziliang admired him very much and left even household matters to Shen Ma.
Xiao Ziliang passed away, and Shen Li served Xiao Ziliang, the governor of Nuozhou, Shi'an King.
Bian Jiang was once sent by the state government to escort Min Ding, and he quickly responded without complaint.
Xiao Yaoguang said to the officials who were also dispatched: Why don't you imitate what Shen Ma did?
So Xiao Yaoguang ordered Shen Ma to take charge of the state prison litigation alone.
Fangshan Dai in Hushu County is high and steep. In the cold winter months, passers-by who passed by this place on business and for private purposes thought it was difficult and dangerous, so Mingtong sent Xuanma to repair the place.
Bian Chui then planned to dig out the four dangerous areas of the rapids. He intercepted pedestrians to participate in the construction and completed the work in three days.
Yangzhou Shuzuo was passing through this place on private business and pretended to be an envoy from the state capital. He refused to participate in the construction. Shen Li ordered him to be whipped thirty times.
Shu Zuo went back to complain to Xiao Yaoguang, and Xiao Yaojiu said: Xuanma will definitely not whip you for no reason.
So I sent someone to check, and it turned out that Shu Zuo had committed fraud.
Emperor Ming also sent Shen Xu to build Chishan Pond, and the cost was hundreds of thousands less than the amount expected by the materials official. Dan Hsu was even more convinced that Shou Yuan was talented.
In the first year of Yongtai, Ren Jiande ordered the people to plant fifteen mulberry trees, four persimmon trees, pear trees, and chestnut trees for every adult male. Every adult female planted half of the above number of trees. The people happily followed Shen Xu's instructions, and soon the trees planted by the people formed a large forest.
Shen Yu resigned and returned to the capital, where he also appointed Cao Lang.
Shen Yu then followed Chen Bozhi's army to Jiangzhou. When Gaozu's rebel army surrounded Yingcheng, Shen Yu persuaded Chen Bozhi to surrender to Gaozu.
Bo Zhizhi cried and said: My son is in the capital and cannot leave the city. I have to cherish him.
Shen Ma said: You can't look at it that way. Your men are restless and are thinking of changing the family. If you don't make a plan early, it will be difficult for your men to gather together again if they are distracted.
Chen Bozhi then led the entire army to surrender to Gaozu, and Shen Yu followed Gaozu's army.
Back when Shen Yu was still in Prince Jingling's Mansion, he had always been on good terms with Fan Yunshan.
summary: Shen Zhen, from Wukang, gained fame for pleading for his uncle Shen Chang's pardon. He served under Prince Jingling, punishing bullies according to law and earning respect. He built roads efficiently, completed construction projects under budget, and as Jiande magistrate, ordered planting of mulberry, persimmon, pear, and chestnut trees. He later persuaded Chen Bozhi to surrender to Gaozu during the siege of Yingcheng. As Yuyao magistrate, he curbed powerful families who sought favors, punishing those who came to the yamen without proper cause. However, he used his position to take revenge on wealthy families who had humiliated him when he was poor selling pottery, causing fear and complaints among local gentry. He maintained personal honesty throughout. He was killed by robbers at age fifty-nine, with many believing Xiao Yingda responsible.

translation:
Fan Shuzeng, courtesy name Zixuan, was born in Qiantang Dynasty, Wu County.
He has been interested in learning since childhood. He studied the Five Classics under Yuhang Lu Daohui and became proficient in the interpretation of the Five Classics.
Lu Daohui once had hundreds of students, but he only praised Fan Shuzeng, saying: This man will definitely become the emperor's teacher.
When Prince Wenhui of Qi and King Wenxuan of Jingling were young, Fan Shu once selected them as their mentors.
Fan Shuzeng first became an official and served as the minister of the Xi Kingdom of Song and Jin Dynasties.
In the early years of the Qi Dynasty, Fan Shu once served as the doctor of the kingdom, and then moved to the post of chief guest of Shangshu and the captain of the prince's infantry, leading Kaiyang Ling.
Fan Shu was an upright and outspoken man, and he gave advice on many matters in the palace. Although the prince could not adopt all of them, he did not blame him.
King Jingling thought highly of Fan Shuzeng and called him Zhou She.
At that time, Prince Zuowei led Shen Yue to compare Fan Shuzeng with Mo Dai's Yubi.
Because his parents were old, Fan Shu once requested to return to his hometown to support his parents, so the imperial court appointed Jian Shubi as the doctor of Zhongsan.
After ascending to the throne, Fan Shu was promoted to a guerrilla general and left the capital to serve as the governor of Chengsai.
Fan Shu once governed the government with integrity and fairness, and did not advocate the use of majestic and ferocious methods to govern the people, so the people felt comfortable.
The area where Yongtai belongs to is a difficult area with high mountains, deep valleys, and dangerous terrain. It is a place where fleeing criminals gather. Even the former prefects used conquest methods, but none of them were able to pacify the area.
When Fan Shuzeng first took office, he showed his kindness and loyalty. Those vicious people dragged their children and daughters out of the mountains, and registered more than 200 families as good citizens.
From then on, merchants in this place could travel freely and the people lived and worked in peace and contentment.
When Fan Shuzeng was serving in Yongjia County, he worked hard to maintain his integrity and refused to accept gifts. When Emperor Ming heard about Fan Shuzeng's situation, he admired him very much and went down to praise him.
He was also recruited as a guerrilla general.
When Fan Shuzeng left Yongjia County, the county gave the outgoing prefect more than 200,000 yuan in old money as usual, but he refused to accept it.
When Fan Shuzeng first took office in the county, he did not bring his family with him. When he left the county and returned to Beijing, his subordinates still had simple luggage, and no one needed to carry their luggage by car.
The people, young and old, all came out to pay their respects to Fan and recount their past experiences. The cries of the people reluctant to leave and begging the eunuch to stay could be heard dozens of miles away.
When the Marquis of Cambodia was in power, Fan Shu was appointed as the official of Zhongsan and returned to his hometown.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Fan Shuzeng left his hometown in a small boat, went to the capital to pay homage to Emperor Gaozu, and then bid farewell to Emperor Gaozu and returned home.
Zhidan issued an edict saying: Fan Shuzeng, the official of Zhongsan, once served the Lord with loyalty and uprightness in the Qi Dynasty. When he was the governor of Yongjia, he was honest and simple, and adhered to nobility. He should be given a title and salary to encourage people with noble conduct.
summary: Fan Shuzeng, from Qiantang, studied the Five Classics under Lu Daohui, who predicted he would become the emperor's teacher. He served as mentor to Prince Wenhui and King Wenxuan of Jingling. As governor of Chengsei, he governed with integrity without harsh methods. In Yongjia County, he refused gifts and the customary 200,000 yuan given to outgoing prefects. When leaving, his luggage was so simple no cart was needed, and the people wept for miles. Emperor Gaozu appointed him Taizhong doctor with silk rewards, but Fan donated all his salary and died in poverty at age seventy-nine.

translation:
He should be appointed as Taizhong doctor and rewarded with twenty pieces of silk.
Fan Shuzeng donated all the salary he received throughout his life to others.
When he was old, his family was destitute and had no assets.
Fan Shu had been in Tianjian for eight years and died at the age of seventy-nine.
Fan Shu once wrote annotations for "Yi Wenyan" and wrote ten miscellaneous poems and poems.
Qiu Zhongfu, courtesy name Gongxin, was born in Wucheng, Wuxing.
He was eager to learn since childhood. His grandfather Qiu Lingju knew the art of physiognomy and once called Qiu Zhongfu a thousand-mile horse.
In the early years of Qi Yongming Dynasty, Qiu Zhongfu was elected as a national student and was promoted to a high rank, but he was not drafted, so he returned to his hometown.
Qiu Zhongfu's family was poor and he had no money to support his family, so he made friends with a group of thieves and advised them to plunder in Sanwu.
Qiu Zhongfu is smart and resourceful. The thieves are afraid of him and obey him. His plans can be implemented one by one and succeed, so they will not be exposed.
The prefect Xu Si called Qiu Zhongfu to take up the post of chief secretary. Qiu Zhongfu successively served in Yangzhou. He had a doctorate in Taixue and served in Huling. He had a reputation for being capable.
Lu Wenxian, the governor of Huainan, was a favored minister of the emperor at that time. He often insulted and scolded county officials, but Qiu Zhongfu was not impressed by him alone.
Qiu Zhongfu resigned due to the death of his father.
When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Qiu Zhongfu was appointed as General Liewu and Qu Aling.
Wang Jingze, the prefect of Kuaiji, launched a rebellion. He took advantage of the fact that the court was not prepared to attack him. News of his rebellion had just reached the capital, and the vanguard of the rebel army had already reached Qu'a.
Qiu Zhongfu said to the county officials and people: The rebels took advantage of the victory and advanced. Although they were very energetic, they were a mob and easily separated.
Now we gather the ships and dig long hills to drain the water in the canals and prevent the rebel ships from advancing. If we can hold them back for a few days, the imperial army will definitely arrive, and the counter-rebellion will be successful.
When Wang Jingze's rebels arrived, the water in the canals had been drained. As expected, the rebels were blocked and unable to advance. The rebels were defeated and dispersed.
Qiu Zhongfu moved to the Shanyin Order because of his meritorious service in resisting the rebels. He was very famous during his tenure. The people made up a ballad for him and said: Two Fu Shen Liu are not as good as one Qiu.
In the past, Fu Yan and his son, Shen Xian, and Liu Xuanming successively served as Shanyin orders, and they all had very good political achievements. Ballads said that Qiu Zhongfu's political achievements exceeded them.
During the political chaos at the end of the Qi Dynasty, Qiu Zhongfu was involved in corruption and bribery. He was reported for impeachment and was about to be arrested. Qiu Zhongfu escaped secretly and went straight back to the capital to confess his crime to the court. This coincided with the imperial court issuing a pardon, and Qiu Zhongfu was not punished.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Qiu Zhongfu was appointed Shanzhao again.
Qiu Zhongfu was good at handling complicated and detailed government affairs, and was good at adapting to the current situation and adapting to changes. County officials and people all respected him and believed in him, saying that he was as wise as a god. Qiu Zhongfu's political ability is said to be the best in the world.
Qiu Zhongfu was promoted to the post of Chief of Chariots and Cavalry and Internal History of Changsha. After less than a year in office, he was recruited as Shangshu Youcheng, moved to Zuocheng, and then promoted to Weiweiqing. The emperor favored Qiu Zhongfu deeply and appointed him generously.
The imperial court built two palaces and ordered Qiu Zhongfu to lead the army as a master craftsman. After the project was completed, Qiu Zhongfu left the capital and served as the governor and governor of Anxi.
He moved to the post of Yunhui Changshi and Jiangxia Prefecture, and was responsible for the affairs of Yingzhou Prefecture. When his mother passed away, the court ordered him to seize the opportunity during the mourning period and resume his duties as governor of the prefecture.
Because he was involved in the incident and found guilty, he was removed from his post, his name was removed, and he was appointed as Sikong to join the army.
Soon, Qiu Zhongfu moved to Suitong's internal history. During his tenure, he changed his previous behavior and sharpened his integrity.
Soon, Qiu Zhongfu died at the age of forty-eight.
The emperor issued an edict saying: Qiu Zhongfu, the internal historian of Yuzhang, was re-appointed in Dazhou to see the effect. During his tenure, not only were there no disasters, but he also had outstanding political achievements.
Now that he has unfortunately passed away, it is really sad and sad.
Qiu Zhongfu should be given as a posthumous gift to the Minister of Huangmen.
When Qiu Zhongfu's coffin was about to be transported back, the people of Yutong, old and young, cried to see him off. Many people clung to the hearse, making it unable to move forward.
When Qiu Zhongfu was Zuocheng, he wrote 20 volumes of "Imperial Code", 100 volumes of "Nangong Stories", and "Shang Shu Ju Shi Za Yi". These books have been circulated in the world.
summary: Qiu Zhongfu, from Wucheng, was called a "thousand-mile horse" by his grandfather. Poor and unable to support his family, he advised thieves in Sanwu, successfully avoiding exposure. He later served as Huling magistrate with a reputation for capability, resisting insults from the favored minister Lu Wenxian. During Wang Jingze's rebellion, he drained canal water to block rebel ships, contributing to their defeat. As Shanyin magistrate, he was so effective that people sang "Two Fu Shen Liu are not as good as one Qiu," surpassing previous magistrates. Though involved in corruption during Qi's chaos, he escaped punishment through a pardon. Under Emperor Gaozu, he served as Shanzhao magistrate again, known for handling complex affairs wisely. He wrote twenty volumes of "Imperial Code" and other works.

translation:
Sun Qian, whose courtesy name is Changxun, was born in Ju, Dongguan.
Sun Qian was known and valued by his relative Zhao Bofu when he was young.
When Sun Qian was seventeen years old, Sun Qian was appointed governor of Liaozhou and selected to serve in the Zuo Army. Sun Qian was known for his ability in handling official affairs.
Because his father passed away, Sun Qian left his job to mourn. He lived in Liwu and farmed by himself to support his younger brothers and sisters. People in the same town praised their brothers for their cordiality and harmony.
Liu Yigong, the king of Jiangxia in Song Dynasty, heard about Xun Sui's character and chose to invite him to join the army. Sun Qian successively served in two official offices, Da Sima and Da Zai.
Sun Qian came to the capital to serve as the order of Jurong. He was honest, prudent, and had a strong memory. The people in the county said that he was as wise as a god.
In the early years of Taishi, Sun Qian served Liu Xiuren, King of Jian'an. Liu Xiuren ordered Sun Qian to join the army as a Situ and recommended him to Emperor Ming. Sun Qian was promoted to General Mingwei and Governor of Badong Jianping County.
Both counties are located in the Three Gorges. In the past, they often relied on force to suppress the people in the counties.
Sun Qian was about to take office, and Emperor Ming ordered Sun Qian to recruit a thousand soldiers to follow him.
Sun Qian said: The barbarians refused to submit because they lacked certain rules for treating them. There was no need to send troops to fight and waste national resources!
Sun Qian firmly refused and refused to accept soldiers.
After arriving at the county, Sun Qian extended his benevolence to the government and promoted enlightenment. The barbarians all surrendered one after another and rushed to give Sun Qian gold and silver treasures. Sun Qian comforted them one by one and showed them reason, and then sent them back. He did not accept the gifts of gold and silver treasures at all.
Later, some barbarians who broke the law were caught and released home.
Official salaries, which were originally borne by the officials and the people, were all exempted from the burden on the officials and the people.
As a result, everything in the county was safe, and Sun Qian's prestige was greatly improved.
Sun Qian was in charge of the Second County for three years, and the imperial court called him back to Beijing to serve as a soldier in the Fu army and join the army.
In the early years of Yuanhui, Sun Qian was appointed as the governor of Liangzhou. He refused to be appointed and took up the post. He was also appointed as the captain of the Yueqi school and the chief secretary of the Sima Mansion in Zhengbei.
King Jianping was about to raise his troops to rebel. He was worried that Sun Qian was strong and upright and that Sun Qian would come out to remonstrate, so he sent Sun Qian to the capital under the guise of official business and then launched a rebellion.
After King Jianping was executed, Sun Qian moved to the post of general of the Zuo Army.
In the early years of the Qi Dynasty, Sun Qian was appointed General Ning Shuo and Ling Qian Tang. He handles complex government affairs in a concise manner and does not detain prisoners who have not yet been tried or convicted.
When Sun Qian resigned, because Sun Qian did not accept gifts while he was in office, the people chased Sun Qian with silk ribbons in boats and gave them to Sun Qian after he left the county, but Sun Qian refused to accept them.
Every time he left his job, Sun Qian never had his own private house and often borrowed empty carports from the government to live in.
In the early years of the Yongming Dynasty, Sun Qian was appointed as the chief historian of the championship and the prefect of Jiangxia. He was convicted of leaving Jiangxia County without authorization and was imprisoned in Shangfang Prison.
Soon, Sun Qian was exonerated and appointed as a doctor in Zhongsan.
Emperor Ming wanted to appoint Sun Qian as his confidant, so he ordered Sun Qian to serve as a guard and assigned him a hundred armored guards. Sun Qian did not want to be involved in the power struggle and dismissed the guards on his own initiative. Although Emperor Ming did not blame him, he no longer entrusted him with important responsibilities from then on.
Sun Qian left the capital and served as Nanzhonglang Sima.
In the first year of Yongyuan, the Marquis of Donghun, Sun Qian moved to the post of official of Kou Kou.
In the sixth year of Tianjian, Sun Qian came to the capital to serve as the general of the auxiliary state and the prefect of Lingling. He was old and frail, but he still worked hard to handle political affairs, and the officials and people felt comfortable.
Before Sun Qian took office, there were many tigers in the county, which often hurt people and animals. After Sun Qian took office, the tigers disappeared.
On the night when Sun Qian resigned, the tiger came out again to harm the local people.
Sun Qian served as county magistrate, and he often encouraged and urged the people to cultivate farmland, plant mulberry and raise silkworms, and strive to make the most of the land. The people under him often earned more than those in neighboring counties.
In the ninth year of Tianjian's reign, because Sun Qian was old, the imperial court recruited him as Guanglu doctor.
After Sun Qian returned to Beijing to take up his post, Emperor Gaozu greatly admired Sun Qian's integrity and treated him with great etiquette and great favor.
However, Sun Qian still asked to take on difficult tasks to serve the court every time he met with the court.
Gaozu smiled and said to him: I want to use your wisdom, not your strength.
In the 14th year of Tianjian, Gaozu Xia Shao said: Sun Qian, the Guanglu doctor, is honest, loyal, and very famous. He has not slackened off until his old age. This old and virtuous veteran should be given a generous salary.
Twenty confidants should be allocated and given support.
Sun Qian served as the governor of two counties and five counties from young to old, and he always maintained integrity.
summary: Sun Qian, from Dongguan, was known for ability from age seventeen. He farmed to support his siblings after his father's death. As Jurong magistrate, he was honest with a strong memory. As governor of Badong and Jianping counties in the Three Gorges, he refused soldiers, instead extending benevolence to barbarians who surrendered and offered treasures, which he refused. He exempted officials and people from bearing official salaries. After three years, the counties were peaceful. He served in multiple positions, always maintaining integrity, often borrowing government carports to live in. As Lingling prefect, tigers disappeared during his tenure but returned after he left. He encouraged farming and sericulture, with his people earning more than neighboring counties. At over ninety, he was as strong as a fifty-year-old, arriving at court before others. He cared for his sick brother and took in the homeless Liu Rong, burying him properly. He died at ninety-two in Tianjian's fifteenth year.

translation:
The same goes for most other things.
Although this kind of behavior seems a bit hypocritical, it shows his careful and detailed intentions.
He Yuan's carriages and horses were extremely shabby, and his clothes were very simple. Among his utensils were no exquisite and valuable products such as copperware or lacquerware.
There are many aquatic products in Jiangzuo and the prices are very cheap, but He Yuan only eats a few pieces of dried fish every time.
However, He Yuan was upright and stern by nature, and many officials and common people were whipped and punished for minor offenses. So someone reported He Yuan to the court, and He Yuan was conscripted to the capital and handed over to the court for interrogation. He was found guilty of dozens of crimes.
At that time, the scholar-bureaucrats who committed crimes and were convicted were not subject to the criminal law of the station test. He Yuan thought that he had not taken bribes and had withstood the punishment of the station test for twenty-one days. Even though he refused to plead guilty, he was still expelled for the crime of hiding the emperor's ceremonial guard.
Later, He Yuan was appointed as General Zhennan and Ling Wukang.
He further strengthened his integrity, eliminated all kinds of unethical sacrifices, was impartial and devoted to his duties, and the people praised him very much.
The prefect Wang Bin inspected his counties, and each county held a grand banquet to entertain Wang Bin. When he arrived in Wukang, He Yuan only prepared dry food and tea.
When Wang Ao left, He Yuan sent him to the border and presented him with a bucket of wine and a goose as a farewell farewell to Wang Bin.
Wang Bin and He Yuan joked: In the Jin Dynasty, Lu You gave gifts with a bucket of wine and a plate of venison. If your gift exceeds that of Lu Na, will you be laughed at by the ancients?
When Emperor Gaozu learned of He Yuan's talent, he promoted him to be the prefect of Xuancheng.
Being promoted from county magistrate to governor of a large county near Gyeonggi Province was something that did not happen in modern times.
After Xuancheng County was plundered by rebels, Tanda tried his best to appease the people and handle government affairs. He was also famous for his political achievements.
A year later, He Yuanqian was appointed as General Shugong and Internal Secretary of Zhao Yu.
At that time, Lu Thunlang of Xinglu Fort was the governor of Guaiye. When he took office, he looted and plundered along the road, but when he entered the Shixing territory, he did not even damage the vegetation.
When he was in office, he liked to build roads, build walls and build people's houses, streets and lanes, and city warehouses. He organized them one by one, just like building a home.
He Yuan did not use any of Tian Zhi's salary. At the end of the year, he selected the most disadvantaged people and used his salary as their taxes. He often did this.
However, he handled litigation cases just like others. He was no better than ordinary people. However, he was decisive by nature. People did not dare to do bad things. They were afraid of him but respected and loved him.
Wherever He Yuan served, the people set up shrines to worship him, and reported his political achievements to the public. Emperor Gaozu often issued edicts to praise and commend him.
In the 16th year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu issued an edict saying: He Yuan first served in Wukang and had a reputation for being honest and fair. Then he governed two counties, which further demonstrated his integrity.
Administering government first repairs the roads, leaving a beneficial administration that is respected and loved by the people. Even the virtuous governors of ancient times did not go far beyond that.
summary: He Yuan, from Donghai, participated in Xiao Baoxuan's failed rebellion, fleeing to various protectors before surrendering to Wei. He eventually reached Gaozu's rebel army, who praised him as an outstanding man. As Wuchang prefect, he changed his conduct, refusing gifts and buying cold water from wells in summer. His carriages and clothes were shabby, and he ate only dried fish despite cheap aquatic products. However, he whipped many for minor offenses, leading to accusations and interrogation. He withstood twenty-one days of station test punishment without confessing, but was expelled for hiding the emperor's ceremonial guard. As Wukang magistrate, he eliminated unethical sacrifices and served only dry food and tea to inspecting prefect Wang Bin, presenting a bucket of wine and a goose as farewell. He was promoted to Xuancheng prefect, an unusual promotion from county magistrate. He built roads and organized city warehouses, using his salary to pay taxes for the poorest. Wherever he served, people built shrines for him. He was dismissed from Shuyang after being slandered, but never discussed personal honor or disgrace. He died at fifty-two in the second year of Putong.

translation:
He Yuan should be promoted to a glorious position in the court in recognition of his performance in the county.
He should be given the title of Minister of Huangmen, who is responsible for serving people from far away.
He Yuan immediately returned to the county and was appointed as the chief historian of Renwei.
Soon, He Yuan left the capital and was appointed General Xinwu to supervise Wu County.
In Wujun, he often made mistakes due to drinking and was moved to Dongyang Prefecture.
During He Yuan's tenure, he hated the powerful and wealthy families and treated them as enemies, while treating poor and weak families as his own children. Therefore, those rich and powerful families were particularly afraid of He Yuan.
He Yuan served in Shuyang for more than a year, but was dismissed from his post and returned home because he was slandered by those he had punished.
He Yuan was an upright man and did not attach personal importance to himself. He was in the officialdom, cut off personal requests, and did not meet with powerful people himself.
When He Su writes letters to others, he treats them with the same equal courtesy, no matter how high or low they are.
When he met people at gatherings, he would not show a humble expression to flatter and flatter people, so He Yuan was often hated and hated by some mediocre and shallow scholar-bureaucrats.
He Yuan's integrity and justice are truly the first in the world.
He served in several counties. Although he saw those things he wanted, he still would not change his moral integrity and pursue greed. He Yuan's wife and children suffered from hunger and cold, and their lives were similar to those of the poorest people.
He Yuan was dismissed from Shuyang and returned home for a long time, but he never talked about his personal honor and disgrace. Therefore, the scholars respected He Yuan even more.
He Yuan values ​​righteousness over wealth. He is willing to help others in emergencies and does not talk empty words. This is actually his nature.
He Yuan often said to people jokingly: If you can find a false statement from me, then I will reward you with a piece of string.
Many people were watching and waiting in secret, but still couldn't find him.
Later, He Yuan was appointed to join the army to consult on the expedition to the west and to pacify Sima.
Ordinary two years later, He Yuan died at the age of fifty-two.
Emperor Gaozu gave his family very generous gifts.
Yao Cha, the Minister of the Ministry of Official Affairs of Chen, said: There are biographies of Xun officials in the history books of previous dynasties. What is the reason?
It is the times that have prompted this situation.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, corvee labor was heavy and all kinds of traitors appeared one after another. Appointing good officials and adopting the governance methods of the Qing Dynasty could not stop traitors. Therefore, cruel officials were appointed and executions were used to stop traitors. However, at the same time, the indiscriminate use of punishments also caused a lot of resentment.
With the rise of the Liang Dynasty, harsh punishments and laws were eliminated in favor of simplicity, glitz and glamor were eliminated in favor of simplicity, the people were educated with the principles of filial piety and brotherhood, and encouraged to farm and grow mulberry trees. As a result, fierce and cunning people became sages like You Yu, and frivolous people became loyal and kind people.
Honest folk customs have been generally formed, and people naturally and consciously abide by the prohibitions.
It is true that in the days of Yao and Shun, every family had a man of high virtue who could be given the title of prince.
As for cruel officials, they were not chosen as biographies in the Liang Dynasty.
summary: Yao Cha noted that previous dynasties included biographies of good officials because the times demanded them. During Emperor Wu of Han, heavy corvée and widespread treachery necessitated cruel officials, but excessive punishment caused resentment. With Liang's rise, harsh laws were eliminated, simplicity replaced glitz, people were educated in filial piety and brotherhood, and farming encouraged. Consequently, even fierce people became virtuous, and honest customs formed naturally. No biographies of cruel officials were included in Liang's records.

translation:
"Yi" said: "Kang has regrets". The meaning of the word "Kang" means that he only knows how to advance in officialdom, but does not know how to retire; he only knows how to survive, but does not know how to die.
I am afraid that only a saint can understand the principles of advance and retreat and survive without losing track of the right path!
"The Biography" says: If you are content, you will not be humiliated; if you know how to stop, you will not be in danger.
According to this, if you don’t know how to advance or retreat, if you don’t understand the principle of knowing where to stop and be content, you will be humiliated, embarrassed, and in a dangerous situation, and you will soon be in a dangerous situation.
The advancement of the ancients was to help people govern the world, and the retreat of the ancients was to promote the right path and encourage folk customs.
However, people's advancement in officialdom is glorious and easy, so it is the goal that ignorant people strive to pursue; people's retirement requires adhering to integrity and persisting in hardships and dangers, so it is something that mediocre people are afraid of.
Although it is common for people to see and hear cases of people who seek to advance in officialdom encounter disaster or defeat, people who live in seclusion are rarely seen in previous history books.
Moji retired from the emperor after his success, and was lying in his sick home, practicing the method of immortality. This is better than wandering around after he succeeded in Luanqi and Jianlong.
Later, Zheng Guangde, Shuguang, Shushou and others retired according to the court's etiquette and left their jobs to live in their homes, which is also worthy of praise.
Yu Kun's "Wei Lue Zhizuo Zhuan" compared Tian and Xu with Guan and Hu. In fact, their principles of conduct were originally different.
Xie Lingyun's "Jin Shu Zhizu Zhuan" first comments on those Jin Dynasty literati who escaped from the turmoil. They probably did not belong to the Zhizu type of people; only Ruan Sikuang liked to escape from the world, abandoning glory and wealth, which was considered to be far away from the embarrassing and dangerous situation of humiliation. "Song Book."
In "The Legend of Zhizu" there are biographies of Cha Ao and Wang Miao, both of whom are similar characters to the previous ones.
During the Revolution, Zhou Suyou, also named Wangbi, refused to be an official, insisted on integrity, traveled in the mountains and forests, cultivated his ambition, did not feel sad and sorrowful in poverty, and did not pursue wealth and glory greedily. He was a noble person among Confucian scholars.
After Liang took over the world, the way of villains declined, and wise men and officials invited each other to gather in the court to measure their own strength and stick to their ambitions of retirement. Those who have not been heard of in the contemporary era. Occasionally, some people retired due to old age, and some had little ambition and weak desires. The history of the country recorded the deeds of these people and compiled it into the "Zhizu Zhuan".
Gu Xian's courtesy name was Shisi, and he was a native of Wu County, Wu County.
His grandfather Gu Qianzhi was the general of the town army and the governor of Xiangzhou during the Song Dynasty.
Before he reached the age of twenty, Gu Xianzhi was appointed by the state as a councilor, promoted scholars, and accumulated merits and was promoted to Prince Sheren, Shangshu Bibu Lang, and Fujun Chief.
During the Yuan Dynasty, Gu Xianzhi was appointed as the Jiankang Order.
summary: The principles of advance and retreat in officialdom, noting that those who only know how to advance but not retreat will face humiliation and danger. It contrasts the glorious and easy pursuit of advancement, which ignorant people strive for, with the difficult and principled act of retirement, which mediocre people fear. The text mentions historical figures like Moji, who retired after success, and Zheng Guangde, Shuguang, and Shushou, who retired according to court etiquette. It also references Xie Lingyun's "Jin Shu Zhizu Zhuan," which comments on Jin Dynasty literati who escaped turmoil, and notes that Ruan Sikuang was considered to have avoided humiliation by abandoning glory. The "Zhizu Zhuan" includes biographies of Cha Ao and Wang Miao, and during the Revolution, Zhou Suyou was a noble Confucian who refused office and cultivated his ambition in the mountains.

translation:
At that time, someone was stealing cattle, and the stolen cattle were recognized by the owner of the cattle. The person who stole the cattle also said that the cattle were his own. The verbal evidence on both sides was similar. No one of the previous county magistrates could decide this case.
After Gu Xianzhi arrived, he reviewed the case materials and then said to both parties: "No need to say more, I have thought of a solution."
So Gu Xianzhi ordered his people to untie the rope from which the cow was tied and let the cow go wherever it wanted. The cow went straight back to its original owner's house, and the thief confessed his crime.
Gu Saizhu exposed the evildoers hidden in the dark. He was so smart and decisive in many such things that people at the time called him a god.
As for dealing with the private requests of dignitaries and dignitaries in the imperial court, he never flattered or obeyed. He never tolerated the corruption and cruelty of his officials, and he judged them all fairly and in accordance with the law.
Gu Xianzhi was honest and frugal by nature, and worked hard to handle political affairs, so he won the hearts of the people. Therefore, drinkers in the capital got mellow and delicious wine, and often called the wine "Gu Jiankang". This means that Gu Xian's purity, purity, harmony and beauty are like good wine.
Gu Xianzhi moved to the post of chariot and cavalry meritorious officer, and was a friend of King Xi of Jin Dynasty.
Emperor Qi Gao took charge of the imperial court and ordered Gu Xianzhi to join the army as a hussar and green officer, and to move to the post of Taiwei Xicao.
After the establishment of the Qi Wangtai Mansion, Gu Xianzhi was appointed as the Minister of Zhongshu.
When Emperor Gao of Qi ascended the throne, Gu Xianzhi was dismissed and appointed as the internal history of Hengyang.
Before Gu Xianzhi took office, there had been plagues in Hengyang for several years, and more than half of the people died of the disease. The price of coffins was extremely expensive, so the people all wrapped the dead in reeds and dumped them on the roadside.
As soon as Gu Xianzhi took office, he notified the counties under his jurisdiction to find the relatives of the dead and ordered them to bury the dead.
For those dead people who had no relatives, Gu Xianzhi took out his salary and ordered the chief clerk of the government to organize the burial.
According to the local folk custom in Hengyang, when people in the mountains are sick, they often say that the disaster was caused by their ancestors, so they dig graves, open coffins, and wash the bones of the dead with water. This is called "removing evil spirits".
Gu Xianzhi used principles to educate the people, explaining to them the difference between the living and the dead, and pointed out that diseases were not caused by the dead, and the local customs were therefore changed.
At that time, the governor Wang Huan had just taken office, and there was only one county in Hengyang where no one came to the governor's office to complain. So Wang Huan sighed and said: Gu Hengyang's education has reached a very good level.
Suppose all nine counties of this state are like this. So what else is wrong with me?
Gu Xianzhi returned to Beijing and served as Taiwei and Zhonglang.
He also left the capital and served as the chief historian of Shuzhong and engaged in the affairs of Kuaiji County.
Lu Wendu, a native of Shanyin, was favored by Emperor Wu of Qi, so he built a mansion in Yuyao and acted freely and unscrupulously in the area.
When Gu Xianzhi took office in Kuaiji County, he immediately went to court to demolish Lu Wendu's mansion.
summary: The text then provides a detailed biography of Gu Xianzhi. He was a native of Wu County, served in various official posts, and was known for his intelligence and decisive judgment, such as solving a cattle theft case by letting the cow lead him to its owner. He was honest, frugal, and fair, earning the nickname "Gu Jiankang" for his purity. As an official, he improved local customs, such as ending the practice of "removing evil spirits" in Hengyang and demolishing the mansion of the favored Lu Wendu. He also successfully petitioned King Jingling to lift a ban on collecting firewood. Gu Xianzhi died at home at age seventy-four, leaving instructions for a simple funeral, emphasizing frugality and sincerity over elaborate rituals.

translation:
In the early years of Tianjian, the imperial court sent people to his home to confer him the title of Taizhong doctor.
Emperor Gaozu said: Liang ruled the world, but he could not see this person.
In the tenth year of Tianjian, Tao Jizhi died at home at the age of seventy-five.
Tao Jizhi had always lived a poor life, no one could compare with him, and he had been living in seclusion for more than ten years. When he died, his family was destitute and his descendants had no money to bury him. Everyone who heard about the incident felt sad for his integrity. Xiao Wangsu was born in Lanling.
His grandfather Xiao Sihua was posthumously awarded the title of General Zhengxi and Kaifu Yitong Sansi in the Song Dynasty. His father, Xiao Huiming, served as the prefect of Wuxing. His grandfather and father both had great reputations.
Xiao Wangsu lost his father very early and his family was poor. He was adopted by his uncle Xiao Huixiu.
When he first became an official, he served as Situ Fa of Qi, Cao Xing joined the army, and moved to Zuo Lang, Prince Sheren, and Shangshu Sangong Lang.
In the last years of Yongyuan, Xiao Shisu was appointed as the prince to wash horses.
Liang Wangtai Mansion was established, and Emperor Gaozu selected him as a lieutenant in the Hussar Records Office to join the army.
In the early years of Tianjian, Xiao Shisu was appointed as Wangyou of Linchuan, and then as Prince Zhongsheren, Danyang Yincheng.
When he was first appointed to the official position, Emperor Gaozu gave Xiao Wangsu 80,000 yuan, and Xiao Wangsu gave all the money to his relatives and friends at once.
Xiao Wangsu moved to Situ Zuoxi and governed the center of Xuzhou in the south.
Xiao Shisu had a quiet and humble temperament, a pure heart, and a fondness for learning. He could talk about the mysteries of Lao and Zhuang, and he never talked about wealth and wealth, and his joy and anger were indistinguishable.
Regardless of whether he was living without an official or holding an official position, he acted according to his own temperament, was open-minded and frank, never arrogant, and showed his simple and simple nature. Scholars therefore respected him.
When he took office in Jingkou, he came up with the idea of ​​settling down in Jingkou for the rest of his life, so he built a house in Sheshan.
At this time, the imperial court recruited him as the minister of Zhongshu, so he refused to be an official and took up the post. He returned to his residence in Sheshan and lived alone without being concerned about worldly affairs. If he was not a relative, he would not be able to reach the gate of his residence.
Xiao Wangsu's wife was the daughter of Taiwei Wang Jian. Xiao Wangsu had separated from her a long time ago and had no children.
In the eighth year of Tianjian, Xiao Shisu passed away.
His relatives and friends inspected his deeds and conferred upon him the title of Mr. Zhenwen.
Shi Chen said: Gu Xianzhi and Tao Jizhi were people who retired to prolong their lives, but Xiao Shisu lacked enthusiasm for being an official. Compared with those who miss their salary, indulge in favors, and work hard in the world, there is indeed a big difference.
summary: The text also includes biographies of Tao Jizhi and Xiao Wangsu. Tao Jizhi was known for his intelligence from a young age, refusing to take money from his grandfather. He served in various posts, refused to flatter Emperor Ming of Qi, and eventually resigned to return home. He died in poverty at age seventy-five. Xiao Wangsu was adopted by his uncle, served in official posts, and was known for his quiet, humble, and scholarly nature. He built a house in Sheshan and lived in seclusion, refusing to engage with worldly affairs. He died at an unknown age. The text concludes that Gu Xianzhi and Tao Jizhi were people who retired to prolong their lives, while Xiao Wangsu lacked enthusiasm for officialdom, distinguishing them from those who greedily pursue wealth and power.

translation:
Xiao Zong, the king of Yuzhang, whose courtesy name was Shiqian, was the second son of Emperor Gaozu.
In the third year of Tianjian's reign, he was granted the title of Prince of Yuzhang County and was granted a residence of 2,000 households.
In the fifth year of Tianjian, he left the capital as envoy Chijie, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in South Xuzhou, general Renwei, and governor of South Xuzhou. Soon he was promoted to the title of Beizhonglang General.
In the tenth year of Tianjian's reign, he was transferred to the governorship of Yingsi, Huo Sanzhou Zhujun, General Yunhui, and Yingzhou governor.
In the 13th year of Tianjian, he was promoted to General Anyou and led the stone garrison army.
In the fifteenth year of Tianjian, he was moved to the post of General Xizhonglang and General of the Guard Army, and then moved to General Anqian and Danyang Yin.
In the 16th year of Tianjian's reign, he was appointed as Beizhong Langjiang and South Xuzhou Governor.
In the second year of ordinary life, he entered the court as Shizhong and Zhenyou General, and his subordinates began to set up assistant historians.
At first, his mother Wu Shuyuan was the concubine of the Marquis of Shuhun of Qi. She was favored by Emperor Gaozu and gave birth to Xiao Zong seven months later. Therefore, many people in the palace suspected that she was not Gaozu's biological son. When Wu Shuyuan's favor faded and she became dissatisfied, people in the palace reported their suspicions to Xiao Zong, so Xiao Zong kept the affair in mind.
When he grew up, he was talented and knowledgeable, and was good at writing articles.
Gaozu used etiquette to discipline his children, and his sons did not see him often. Therefore, Xiao Zong often complained that Gaozu did not understand him.
Every time Xiao Zong went to a feudal town, Wu Shuyuan would always go with him.
When Xiao Rong was fifteen or sixteen years old, he was still naked and playing in front of Wu Shuyuan. There was no difference between day and night. This scandal was discussed both inside and outside the palace.
When Xiao Zong was in Xuzhou, his decrees and punishments were very cruel.
Xiao Zong was strong and could subdue a galloping horse with his bare hands.
He often went out at night wearing casual clothes to conceal his identity, and was unrestrained.
Whenever Emperor Gaozu's appointment came, he would always show resentment, and no one among the ministers would dare to advise him.
Xiao Zong built the Qi family's seven temples in a special house and often went to worship. He also wore casual clothes to kneel down at the mausoleum of Emperor Ming in Qu'aqi.
However, he still couldn't convince himself that he was the son of Houhun Hou of Qi Dong. He heard the saying that if the blood of a living person is dripped on the bones of a dead person, and the blood seeps in, it means that there is a father-son relationship.
Xiao Zong secretly dug up Qi Shuhunhou's grave, took out the bones, and dripped blood from his own arm on the bones for testing. At the same time, he killed one of his own sons and took his bones for blood testing. The results could be verified. From then on, Xiao Zong often harbored thoughts of rebellion.
In ordinary four years, Xiao Zong went out of the capital to serve as envoy Chijie, governor of the military affairs of the five states of Nanyan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, general of Pingbei, and governor of South Yanzhou. Emperor Gaozu gave him a propaganda department.
Xiao Zong heard that Xiao Shiyin, King of Qi Jian'an, was in Wei, so he sent people to Wei to get acquainted with Xiao Baoyin, called Xiao Shiyin his uncle, and promised to lead his territory to submit to Wei.
At the time when Emperor Gaozu was launching his Northern Expedition, in the sixth year of Pengcheng, Wei general Yuan Faseng surrendered to Emperor Gaozu in Pengcheng. Emperor Gaozu ordered General Xiao Zong to lead the army and defend Pengcheng City to confront Wei general Anfeng and Wang Yuanyanming.
Later, Emperor Gaozu thought that the continuous war had lasted for a long time and was worried about chaos, so he ordered Xiao Zong to withdraw his troops.
Xiao Zong was afraid that he would never have a chance to see Xiao Shiyin after returning to the south, so he and Fu Qi fled to Yuan Yanming at night and surrendered to Wei. Wei appointed him as Shizhong, Taiwei, Gaoping Gong, and Danyang King.
Xiao Zong changed his name to Xiao Zuan, with the courtesy name Dewen, in memory of the deposed Emperor Shuhunhou of Qi Dynasty. He also wore mourning clothes for him according to the etiquette of treating his father.
So some ministers petitioned Emperor Gaozu to remove his title and fiefdom, expel him from his name, and change his surname to Ni.
Soon, Shao Ming restored his name and made his son Xiao Zhi the Marquis of Yongxin, granting him a land of thousands of households.
In the second year of Datong, Xiao Baoyin occupied Chang'an in Wei and rebelled against Wei. Xiao Zong fled north from Luoyang and was about to flee to Chang'an. He was caught by Jin officials and Wei people killed him. He was forty-nine years old when he died.
At first, when Xiao Zong was frustrated, he wrote "Listening to the Ringing of the Bell" and "Sad Poems on Falling Leaves" to express his thoughts and feelings.
summary: Xiao Zong, Prince of Yuzhang, was Emperor Gaozu's second son. He held various military and civil posts, including governor of South Xuzhou and Yingzhou. His mother, Wu Shuyuan, was a former concubine of the Marquis of Shuhun of Qi, and Xiao Zong was born seven months after Gaozu married her, leading to suspicions he was not Gaozu's biological son. Xiao Zong grew up talented but resentful, believing Gaozu did not understand him. He performed a blood-dripping test on the bones of the Marquis of Shuhun and his own son, confirming his paternity, which fueled his rebellious intentions. He eventually surrendered to Wei, changed his name to Xiao Zuan in memory of the deposed Emperor Shuhun, and was killed by Wei at age 49. His poems, "Listening to the Ringing of the Bell" and "Sad Poems on Falling Leaves," expressed his sorrow and frustration.

translation:
In Bingxu, Fu Sheng, Xu Zichu and others from Basu killed Xiao Ji's lord Gongsun Huang of Xiaokou City and surrendered to the imperial army.
Wang Lin, Song Peng, Ren Yue, Xie Dayen and others took the opportunity to attack Hou Shu and captured three of his fortresses, so more than ten cities on both sides of the Taiwan Strait surrendered.
General Fan Meng captured Xiao Ji and his third son Yuanyuan and killed them both at Kip Kou. Xiao Ji was forty-six years old when he died.
A petitioner petitioned him to expunge his family name, and Shizu agreed to do so, giving him the surname Taotie.
At the beginning, when Xiao Ji was about to usurp and proclaim himself emperor, more than one strange and strange thing happened. The strangest one was that flowers grew out of the brackets surrounding the pillars of the Cypress Palace in the palace. It had forty-six stems, thin and cute, and looked like a lotus.
A knowledgeable person said: It is not a good thing to have flowers growing on Wang Dun's ceremonial guard.
Xiao's reign name is Tianzheng, which is the same as Xiao Dong's. People say that Tianzheng's Tianzi is Erren, and Zhengzi is Yizhi.
Xiao Dong and Xiao Ji pretended to be emperors, but each only lasted a year before being eliminated.
King Xiao Zhengde of Linhe, also known as Gonghe, was the third son of King Jinghui of Linchuan.
When he was young, he was rough, evil, and disrespectful of etiquette.
At first, when Gaozu had no sons, he adopted him as his son. When Gaozu ascended the throne, Xiao Zhengde hoped to make himself the prince. Later, Gaozu established Prince Zhaoming and named Xiao Zhengde the Marquis of Xifeng, with a settlement of 500 households.
From then on, Xiao Zhengde became dissatisfied. He often harbored ulterior motives and coveted the throne of the emperor, hoping that disaster would happen by chance.
In ordinary six years, he appointed Huangmen Shilang as Qingche General and appointed an assistant historian.
Soon, he fled to Wei, and a minister asked Gaozu to remove the officials he had granted.
In ordinary seven years, Xiao Zhengde escaped from Wei again. Emperor Gaozu did not blame him, restored his title, and then appointed him as the general to conquer the captives.
In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, Xiao Zhengde was appointed General Xinwu and Grand Administrator of Wu County.
Later, the imperial court recruited him as a servant, a general of the Fu army, and appointed him as an assistant historian. He was also named the king of Linhe County, with a settlement of 2,000 households, and he was also made a general of the left guard.
But he became increasingly violent and recruited desperadoes.
Hou Jing knew that he had a treacherous plot, so he secretly sent people to seduce and lobby him, and they had close contacts with him and colluded with each other.
Hou Jing sent a letter to Xiao Zhengde saying: Now that the emperor is old, the treacherous ministers are disrupting the country, the rules and regulations are disordered, and the political orders are reversed, in my opinion, Gaozu will definitely be defeated.
Besides, you were supposed to be crown prince, but you were abandoned in the middle. All the righteous people in the world are very sad in private. Although I, Hou Jing, are foolish and loyal, I can't help feeling resentful about this.
Now that the world is in turmoil and people's hearts are turning to you, how can you only care about the personal relationship between father and son and abandon these hundreds of millions of people?
Although I don't have the ability, I really want to work hard.
summary: Xiao Ji, King of Wuling, was Gaozu's eighth son. He was diligent and talented in literature. He held several official positions, including governor of Jiangzhou and Yangzhou. During the Taiqing period, Hou Jing rebelled, and Xiao Ji did not send troops to reinforce the capital. After Gaozu's death, he proclaimed himself emperor in Shu with the reign name Tianzheng. He killed advisors who warned him, and his rule was marked by omens, such as flowers growing from palace pillars. He led an army downriver to attack Hou Jing but was defeated by Western Wei forces. He was captured and killed at age 46. His reign name Tianzheng was considered unlucky, and he was posthumously given the surname Taotie. Xiao Zhengde, Prince of Linhe, was the third son of Prince Jinghui of Linchuan. He was adopted by Gaozu but became dissatisfied when he was not made crown prince. He fled to Wei but later returned. He conspired with Hou Jing, who supported him as emperor with the reign name Zhengping. After Hou Jing captured Taicheng, he demoted Xiao Zhengde and later killed him out of fear of rebellion.

translation:
I hope you will obey the wishes of the people of the world and understand my sincerity. Xiao Zhengde was very happy after reading Hou Jing's letter and said: Hou Jing's meaning coincides with mine. This is God's support for me.
Then he agreed to Hou Jing's request.
When Hou Jing arrived at the river, Xiao Zhengde secretly brought an empty boat, pretending to load it with reeds, but actually using it to carry Hou Jing across the river.
The imperial court did not know Xiao Zhengde's conspiracy and sent him to guard Zhuquehang.
When Hou Jing arrived at Zhuquehang, Xiao Zhengde led his army to attack the capital together with Hou Jing. Hou Jing supported Xiao Zhengde as emperor, changed the year to the first year of Zhengping, and Hou Jing became prime minister.
After the capture of Taicheng, Hou Jing restored the Taiqing era title and demoted Xiao Zhengde to Grand Sima.
Xiao Zhengde had a complaint. When Hou Jing found out about it, he was worried that he would rebel, so he falsely conveyed the imperial edict and killed him.
The great-grandson of Xiao Yu, King of Hedong, was the second son of Prince Zhaoming.
In ordinary two years, he was named the Duke of Zhijiang County.
In the third year of Zhongdatong, Emperor Gaozu changed his title to the king of Hedong County, with a settlement of 2,000 households.
And appointed him as General Ningyuan and Shitou garrison.
Later, he was transferred out of the capital to serve as the prefect of Langxie and Pengcheng counties.
Later, he was transferred back to the capital and served as Shizhong and Qingche General, and was appointed as an assistant historian.
Later, he was transferred to Nanzhong Langjiang and Xiangzhou Governor.
Soon, Hou Jing invaded the capital, and Xiao Yu led the army to come for reinforcements. When the army arrived at Qingcao Lake, Taicheng had fallen. An order was issued to withdraw the troops and turn back. Luo Yu led the army back to Xiangzhou to defend it.
At that time, Shizu led his army and was stationed there. Zhang Zuan, the newly appointed governor of Yongzhou, reported secretly to Shizu: "Kou Yu is recruiting troops to start a rebellion in Hedong and gathering food and grass in Yueyang. These are all illegal things. They plan to attack Jiangling."
Shidan was very frightened after hearing this, so he walked back to Jiangling by a small road, and sent Zhou Hong to consult with Xiao Yu's naxiang to supervise Xiao Yu's grain and army.
Xiao Yu said: We are all governors, why do we suddenly want to be subordinate to others?
Shizu sent people there three times, but Xiao Yu refused to obey Shizu.
Shi Dan was furious and sent his son Lu Chabi to conquer him, but his friends were defeated and killed by Lu Yu.
Shizu also ordered Bao Quan, the governor of Xinzhou, to attack Xiao Yu, and wrote a letter to Chen, pointing out the blessings and misfortunes, and allowing him to change his ways and do good.
Xiao Yu did not reply, so he strengthened the city wall and deepened the moat in order to resist defense. Xiao Yu said to Bao Quan: What qualifications does a defeated general have to talk about bravery?
If you want to hit, just hit forward, no need to say anything.
Bao Quan's army was stationed at Shiceng Temple. Xiao Yu led all the troops to attack him. Xiao Yu failed to capture Bao Quan's military camp and retreated.
Bao Quan marched to Juzhou again, and Xiao Yu sent out all his elite troops to attack him, but failed to win.
When he was dispatched, it was sunset and the soldiers were exhausted. Bao Quan took the opportunity to attack and defeated Xiao Yu. He beheaded three thousand people and drowned more than ten thousand people in the water.
Xiao Yu therefore burned the outer city of Changsha and drove the residents into the city. Bao Quan mobilized troops to surround Changsha City.
summary: Xiao Yu, Prince of Hedong, was the second son of Prince Zhaoming. He held various posts, including governor of Xiangzhou. When Hou Jing invaded the capital, Xiao Yu led reinforcements but arrived after Taicheng fell. He returned to Xiangzhou to defend it. Shizu, suspicious of Xiao Yu's intentions, sent forces to attack him. Xiao Yu was besieged in Changsha for a long time but eventually captured and beheaded. Before his fall, he experienced ominous visions, including his head disappearing in a mirror and a large white dog fleeing the city.

translation:
Xiao Yu was brave and courageous when he was young. He was able to appease the soldiers and was very popular among the soldiers.
After being besieged for a long time, although the inside and outside were cut off, the defense was still very strong.
Later, Shizu sent the leading general Wang Tanluan to attack Ludeng instead of Baose. Wang only avoided building earth mountains and stayed close to the city. He attacked hard day and night. Arrows and stones were like rain, and more than half of the soldiers in the city were killed or injured.
Xiao Yu was very embarrassed and anxious, so he secretly equipped a large ship and prepared to break out.
Just as Xiao Yu's general Murong Hua was leading Wang Shidao into the city, Lu Deng looked around and saw that all the people close to him were scattered, so he was captured.
Xiao Yu said to his guard: "Don't kill me. I want to meet Shizu. I want to rebuke this thief who slandered others. I will die without regret."
The person in charge of guarding him said: I was ordered not to allow it.
So he beheaded him and sent his head to Jingzhen. Shizu sent his head back and buried him.
At first, when Xiao Yu was about to fail, he secretly looked at his face in the mirror, but his head was not visible. He also saw a tall man lying on the house, with his hands on the ground looking down at his navel. He also saw a white dog as big as a donkey, running out of the city and gone somewhere.
Xiao Yu hated this phenomenon, and soon the city was captured.
Shi Chen said: Xiao Zong and Xiao Zhengde were both rebellious and wanted to do as they pleased, so it was right for them to bring about their own destruction.
During the Taiqing period, Hou Jing rebelled and invaded the capital. Xiao Ji took advantage of the rich resources of Yong and Shu, but did not lead his army to rescue the court in danger, which showed his integrity. When the rebel Hou Jing was killed, he began to raise troops, and his troops were unknown, which caused a disaster.
Alas!
He was punished like Guan Shu and Cai Shu, the ministers who caused chaos in the Western Zhou Dynasty. The disaster was brought about by himself.
summary: The historical commentary concludes that Xiao Zong and Xiao Zhengde's rebellions led to their own destruction, while Xiao Ji's failure to aid the capital during Hou Jing's rebellion and his subsequent uprising brought disaster upon himself.

translation:
Hou Jing, whose courtesy name was Wanjing, was from Shuofang. Some people say he was from Yanmen.
When he was young, he behaved wildly and his fellow villagers were afraid of him.
When he reached adulthood, he was vigorous and strong, and was good at horseback riding and archery.
Therefore, he was selected as a garrison in Beizhen and gradually made meritorious service in the army.
In the first year of Wei Xiaochang, Xianyu Xiuli, a soldier from Huaishuo town, rebelled in Dingzhou and captured the county. At the same time, Tujin Luozhou, a soldier from Rouxuan town, led his party to invade Youzhou and Jizhou. They joined forces with Xianyu Xiuli, totaling more than 100,000 people.
Later, Xianyu Xiuli was killed by Yuan Hongye, and his men were scattered. Ge Rong, the general of Huaishuo Town, took the opportunity to gather Xianyu Xiuli's scattered soldiers, attacked and killed Tujinluozhou, and annexed all Tujinluozhou's troops. People called him "Ge Thief".
In the fourth year of Xiaochang, Emperor Wei Ming died, and Empress Dowager Hu came to rule. Tianzhu General Er Zhurong raised troops from Jinyang and entered Luoyang, killing Empress Hu and Hu's relatives.
Hou Jing initially brought his army to see Er Zhurong. Er Zhurong thought that Hou Jing had a genius and immediately appointed him as a general to lead the troops.
When they were dispatched, Ge Rong's bandits marched south to Luoyang. Er Zhurong went to conquer it in person. He ordered Hou Jing to be the vanguard and led his army to Hanoi to attack Ge Rong. He defeated Jiang's army and captured Ge Rong alive. Because of his great achievements, Hou Jing was promoted to the governor of Dingzhou, Daxingtai, and was granted the title of Duke of Puyang.
Hou Jing became famous from then on.
Soon, Emperor Shenwu of Qi became the prime minister of Wei. He led his army into Luoyang and killed the Zhu family. Hou Jing led his army to surrender to Gao Huan and was appointed by Emperor Shenwu.
Hou Jing was cruel and tyrannical, and controlled the army strictly. However, all the treasures he plundered from the enemy were distributed to the soldiers, so the soldiers were happy to serve him and often won battles.
General Hou Jing holds military power, which is equal to that of Emperor Shenwu.
Wei appointed him as Situ and Nandaoxingtai, with an army of 100,000, and he controlled Henan alone.
Later, Emperor Shenwu fell ill. When he was seriously ill, he said to his son Gao Cheng: Hou Jing is cunning, scheming, and capricious. It is difficult to understand and control him. He will definitely not want to be used by you after I die.
So he wrote a letter to summon Hou Jing to come.
Hou Jing knew that he wanted to get rid of himself and was afraid of disaster, so in the first year of Taiqing, he sent his Xingtai doctor Ding He to ask Gaozu for surrender. The surrender letter said:
I heard that if the important ministers of the country unite and cooperate like human limbs, the country will be unified and peaceful; if the top and bottom are jealous and have different intentions, the country will fall apart.
Therefore, his auxiliary ministers Zhou and Shao were of the same mind and had the same virtue, and the kingdoms of Yue Chang also came to pay tribute; while his ministers Fei and E were disloyal, and as a result all the princes betrayed him.
Creation is the reason for success and failure, which is the same truth from ancient times to modern times.
summary: Hou Jing, courtesy name Wanjing, was from Shuofang, possibly Yanmen. Wild in youth, he became a strong, skilled horseman and archer, serving as a garrison in Beizhen. During Wei Xiaochang's first year, Xianyu Xiuli rebelled in Dingzhou, joined by Tujin Luozhou, amassing over 100,000 troops. After Xianyu Xiuli was killed, Ge Rong gathered his forces, killed Tujin Luozhou, and became known as "Ge Thief." In the fourth year, Emperor Wei Ming died, and Empress Dowager Hu ruled. Er Zhurong raised troops, killed her, and appointed Hou Jing as a general. Hou Jing served as vanguard against Ge Rong, capturing him alive, earning promotion to governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Puyang.

translation:
When Ding He arrived, Gaozu summoned the ministers to discuss the matter in the court hall. The minister, Pushe Xieju, and all the officials said that it was not appropriate to recruit Hou Jing. Gaozu did not follow the opinions and decided to accept Hou Jing's surrender.
When Emperor Shenwu died, his son Gao Cheng succeeded him and became Emperor Wenxiang.
Emperor Gaozu then issued an edict to make Hou Jing the King of Henan, a general, an envoy to hold the festival, supervise the military affairs in the north and south of Henan, and the Daxingtai.
Qi Wenxiang sent General Murong Shaozong to surround Hou Jing in Changshe. Hou Jing asked the Western Wei Dynasty for help. The Western Wei Dynasty sent Wuxu Wang Douqing and others to lead troops to rescue him, and Murong Shaozong retreated.
Hou Jing asked Sizhou Governor Yangyaren for help. Yangyaren sent Chief Shi Denghong to lead troops to Rushui. Upon seeing this, the Yuanqing army fled at night.
So he occupied Xuanhu and Xiangcheng, and asked Emperor Gaozu to send governors to guard them.
Gaozu Shao ordered Yang Yaren to be the governor of Yuzhou and Sizhou and move his troops to guard Xuanhu; he ordered Yang Sijian, the prefect of Xiyang, to be the governor of Yinzhou and guard Xiangcheng.
Marshal Wei Gang died, and Yiliang took his parents and surrendered to the Chu Dynasty. Emperor Wenxiang of Qi was worried that Hou Jing's alliance with the West and South would become a disaster for himself, so he wrote to Hou Jing:
It is said that the throne is the most precious thing, and it is not easy to keep it; benevolence is a very important responsibility, and it is really difficult to always maintain it.
Some people are willing to sacrifice their lives to achieve a good reputation. Some people believe that integrity is more important than food. They regard their lives as lighter than a feather, and morality as precious as a bear's paw.
Because of this, their behavior will not violate morality, their actions will not be faulty, their advancement in officialdom will not be disliked by others, and their retirement will not be criticized behind their backs.
The late king and Situ have been friends in life and death, and have calmed down the turmoil. You and I have a deep friendship. We care about each other everywhere, understand each other in affection, and respect each other in conversation. Our interactions have always been benevolent and righteous. Our friendship is like pines and cypresses that do not wither in the severe cold.
You have grown from childhood to adulthood, and your status has grown from humble to prominent. It is not without kindness that I help you succeed and establish a career.
Now your title ranks first among the princes, your status ranks before the superiors, your courtyard can accommodate horses and carriages, your family enjoys a wealth of money, your wealth can be shared by people in the village, and your prosperity can even benefit your relatives and old friends.
The friendship of friends with similar interests and mutual admiration is a virtue that people respect and respect. To appreciate the kindness of a close friend, one must forget oneself in order to uphold integrity.
Those who are favored by a state official should have the ambition of Yu Rang to swallow charcoal and repay the favor resolutely; those who are gifted with a meal should repay the favor like a spirit wheel and die in return.
I still feel like I can't express my gratitude as much as I can, let alone receiving more favor from these people!
Thanks to the friendship of old friends, I want to entrust my children and grandchildren to each other. I just want our two families to be friends of Qin and Jin for generations, and become in-laws like Liu and Fan.
Even if the days and months go by, the times change, and there is no strong protection for the family, there is only a young orphan, the respect and etiquette of beautifying the family with brocade and bib will not be diminished, and they will divide the house and help like Qiu Chengzi, not forgetting the virtues of their ancestors, and helping the descendants of their friends.
summary: Hou Jing later surrendered to Gao Huan, becoming Emperor Shenwu of Qi. He was cruel but shared plunder with soldiers, ensuring loyalty. He held military power equal to Emperor Shenwu, controlling Henan with 100,000 troops. When Emperor Shenwu fell ill, he warned his son Gao Cheng of Hou Jing's cunning. Hou Jing, fearing for his life, surrendered to Liang's Emperor Gaozu in Taiqing's first year, citing Gao Cheng's threats. Emperor Gaozu accepted, making Hou Jing King of Henan. Qi's Murong Shaozong besieged Hou Jing, who sought Western Wei aid, forcing a retreat. Hou Jing then occupied Xuanhu and Xiangcheng.

translation:
In December, Hou Jing led his army to besiege Qiaocheng, but failed to capture it, so he withdrew his troops to attack Chengfu and captured it.
Hou Jing also sent his Xingtai Zuocheng Wang Wei and Zuo Minlangzhong Wangze to Gaozu to offer advice, advocating that a descendant of the Yuan family should be selected as the lord of Wei and help him ascend the throne through the Northern Expedition.
Emperor Gaozu agreed to the plan. An imperial edict was sent to send Prince Sheren Yuan Zhen to be the King of Xianyang, and wait for him to cross the river. After crossing the river, he was allowed to ascend the throne and proclaim himself emperor, and he was provided with an imperial chariot.
Emperor Wenxiang of Qi sent Murong Shaozong to pursue Hou Jing, but Hou Jing retreated into Guoyang. At this time, Hou Jingshang had thousands of horses, tens of thousands of soldiers, and more than 10,000 vehicles, and he and Murong Shaozong were in a stalemate in the north of Woyang.
Hou Jing ran out of food, and his soldiers were all from Jiangbei and were unwilling to cross south. His general Bao Xian and others led their men to surrender to Murong Shaozong.
When Hou Jing saw that his army was in disarray, he crossed the Huaihe River from Xia Shi with a few of his friends, and gradually gathered scattered troops. He got 800 horses and infantry, and fled to Shouchun. Wei An of Jianzhou accepted him.
In Shouchun, Hou Jing sent someone to petition Emperor Gaozu to demote his official position. Emperor Gaozu treated him favorably, but Xia Shao did not agree to his request for demotion and still appointed him as the shepherd of Yuzhou without changing his original official position.
After Hou Jing occupied Shouchun, he became rebellious. All the residents of Shouchun's city were recruited as sergeants, and he stopped collecting taxes and land rent without authorization. All the children of the people were assigned to the soldiers in the army.
He also requested the emperor to provide tens of thousands of pieces of brocade to make military uniforms. Zhu Yi, the leader of the army, believed that the imperial brocade office was only used by the imperial court to award meritorious deeds nearby, and could not be used as military uniforms for border towns, so he asked for permission to provide him with green cloth.
Hou Jing got the cloth and used it all to make robes, so he admired the color cyan.
He also thought that the weapons supplied by Xingtai were not of high quality, and asked for the blacksmiths from Dongye to be rebuilt. Gaozu ordered that all be given to him.
After Hou Jing's defeat in Wuyang, he repeatedly requested funds from the imperial court, but the imperial court was generous and never refused.
Previously, the governor of Yuzhou, Zhenyang Marquis Xiao Yuanming, led all the troops to besiege Pengcheng. He was defeated and fell to Wei. During the period, he sent people back to Liang to state the Wei people's request to restore old friendship.
In February of the second year, Emperor Gaozu discussed peace with Wei again.
Hou Jing was very frightened when he found out, and hurriedly sent someone to send a seal to Gaozu to try his best to dissuade him. Gaozu did not listen to Hou Jing's dissuasion.
Later, Hou Jingshang's memorial was arrogant and his words were arrogant.
Xiao Fan, the king of Poyang, was guarding Hefei. He and Yang Yaren, the governor of Sizhou, repeatedly reported that Hou Jing had the intention to rebel. The leader Zhu Yi said: Hou Jing only has hundreds of rebels, how can he rebel.
They suppressed their official seals and did not report to Emperor Gaozu, but instead increased the rewards to Hou Jing, so Hou Jing's conspiracy to rebel became more and more exposed.
Hou Jing also knew that Linhe King Xiao Zhengde had grudges and complaints against the court, so he secretly sent people to make friends with him and collude with him. Xiao Zhengde agreed to be Hou Jing's internal adviser.
In August, Hou Jing sent troops to rebel, attacked Ma Tou and Muzha, and captured the prefect Liu Shenmao, the garrison leader Cao Zhu and others.
Emperor Gaozu then ordered the governor of Hezhou, Poyang King Xiao Fan, to be the governor of the South Road, the governor of North Xuzhou, Fengshan Hou Xiao Zhengbiao, to be the governor of the north, Sizhou governor Liu Zhongli to be the governor of the west, and Pei Zhigao, the regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi, to be the governor of Shudao.
In October, Hou Jing left one of his troops, Wang Haogui, to guard Shouchun City, while he led his army to pretend to attack Hefei, but actually went to sneak attack Qiaozhou, and Qiaozhou assisted Dong Shao in opening the city and surrendering. The governor, Fengcheng Hou Xiaotai, was captured.
Emperor Gaozu learned of this and sent Wang Zhi, the prince's family commander, to lead three thousand troops to defend along the river.
Hou Jing attacked Liyang. Zhuang Tie, the prefect of Liyang, sent his brother Zhuang Jun to lead hundreds of people to attack Hou Jing's camp at night. They were unsuccessful. Zhuang Jun died in the battle and Zhuang Tie surrendered.
Xiao Zhengde first dispatched dozens of large ships, pretending to be carrying Diwei, but actually carrying Hou Jing across the river.
Hou Jing arrived at Jingkou and was about to cross the river. He was worried about Wang Zhi's obstruction. Soon, Wang Zhi retreated without any reason. Hou Jing still didn't believe it when he heard that he secretly sent someone to spy. He said to the sent person: If Wang Zhi really retreats, you can break the branches of the river as a signal.
The man who went to spy came back as he said. Hou Jing was overjoyed and said, "My mission was successful."
Just crossing the river from Caishi, there were hundreds of horses and thousands of soldiers, but the people in the capital did not notice it.
Hou Jing immediately divided his troops to attack Gushu, captured Wencheng Hou Kukong, the prefect of Jinhu, and then arrived at Cisu.
Zhidan ordered Xiao Daqi, king of Xuancheng, the governor of Yangzhou in Shao, to be the governor of all the military forces in the city, and Yang Kan, the governor of the capital, to be the military advisor and general to assist him; Xiao Tui, the Marquis of Nanpu, guarded Dongfucheng, Xiao Dachun, Duke of Xifeng, guarded Stone City, and Xie Xi, the commander of light chariots, guarded Baixia.
Then Hou Jing arrived at Zhuquehang. Xiao Zhengde originally stationed troops in Dandanyang County. At this time, he led his troops to join Hou Jing.
