Jiankang ordered Yu Xin to lead more than a thousand troops to the north of Zhuquehang. Seeing that Hou Jing's army had attacked Zhuquehang, Yu Xin ordered the removal of the pontoon bridge. After removing one ship, Yu Xin abandoned his army and fled to Nantang. The abandoned stragglers connected to the pontoon bridge and allowed Hou Jing to cross the river.
The crown prince gave the king a pledge of his horse, allotted him three thousand elite soldiers, and sent him to reinforce Yu Xin.
Wang Zhi went to the leader's mansion, met the rebels, and fled without fighting. Hou Jing took advantage of the victory and marched to the palace city.
Xiao Dachun, Duke of Xifeng, abandoned Stone City and fled. Hou Jing sent his Yi Tong and Yu Ziyue to occupy Stone City.
Xie Xi also gave up Baixia City and fled.
summary: Qi's Emperor Wenxiang wrote to Hou Jing, urging his return with promises of rank and family safety. Hou Jing replied, justifying his actions and rejecting the offer. In December, Hou Jing besieged Qiaocheng, failed, but captured Chengfu. He proposed selecting a Yuan descendant as Wei's lord for a Northern Expedition; Emperor Gaozu agreed. Qi's Murong Shaozong pursued Hou Jing to Woyang, where Hou Jing's army disintegrated due to starvation. He fled to Shouchun with 800 horses, where Emperor Gaozu treated him favorably, appointing him shepherd of Yuzhou. In Shouchun, Hou Jing rebelled, conscripting residents and stopping taxes. He requested brocade for uniforms but received green cloth, which he used. After a defeat, he sought funds from the court, which were granted. In the second year, Emperor Gaozu discussed peace with Wei, alarming Hou Jing, who sent arrogant memorials opposing it. Poyang King Xiao Fan and others reported Hou Jing's rebellion intentions, but official Zhu Yi dismissed them. Hou Jing secretly allied with Linhe King Xiao Zhengde. In August, Hou Jing rebelled, attacking Ma Tou and Muzha. Emperor Gaozu ordered multiple governors to counter him. In October, Hou Jing feigned an attack on Hefei but took Qiaozhou, capturing Fengcheng Hou Xiaotai. He crossed the Yangtze from Caishi with hundreds of horses and thousands of soldiers, unnoticed. He divided troops to attack Gushu, then reached Cisu. Defenders fled, and Hou Jing advanced to the palace city, burning gates. After failed assaults, he built a barrier, cutting off supplies. He established Xiao Zhengde as emperor in November, naming himself Prime Minister. Hou Jing attacked Dongfu City, capturing it and killing over 2,000 officials. He built earth mountains to monitor the city, forcing labor, with weak killed to fill them.

translation:
In May, Emperor Gaozu passed away in Wende Hall.
After the fall of Taicheng, Hou Jingxian sent Wang Wei and Chen Qing to meet Emperor Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu said: Where is Hou Jing now?
Go and fetch him.
At that time, Emperor Gaozu was sitting in the Wende Hall. When Hou Jing entered the hall to worship, he brought 500 soldiers in armor to defend himself and went to the hall with swords.
After the obeisance, Emperor Gaozu asked: You have been in the army for a long time, maybe you are too tired?
Hou Jing couldn't answer silently.
Emperor Gaozu asked again: Which state are you from, and you dare to come to Qianbo?
Hou Jing was speechless again, so his entourage answered on his behalf.
After leaving the palace, Hou Jing said to Xiang Gong Wang Senggui: I often ride on a horse to fight with the enemy, with swords and arrows falling alternately, but I am calm and relaxed, without any fear.
When I saw Mr. Xiao today, I couldn't help but feel frightened. Could it be that the power of God is unstoppable?
I can't see him again.
Although Gaozu's actions were restricted, he was still very resentful in his heart and often condemned and denied what Hou Jing heard about.
Hou Jing was deeply in awe of Gaozu and did not dare to force him.
Hou Jing sent soldiers to be on duty in the palace province. Emperor Gaozu asked Zhou Shizhen, the supervisor of the production bureau: "Who sent them?"
He replied: It’s the Prime Minister.
Gao Dan pretended to be confused and said, "What Prime Minister?"
He replied: "It's Prime Minister Hou."
Emperor Gaozu said angrily: "It's the man named Hou Jing." Why call him prime minister!
From then on, Emperor Gaozu had many needs, but many of them were unsatisfactory. Even the food was cut off. Emperor Gaozu then became ill and died of anger.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Hou Jingmi did not mourn, and the coffin was temporarily parked in Zhaoyang Hall. None of the civil and military officials inside and outside knew about the incident.
More than twenty days later, the coffin was carried to the front hall of Taiji to welcome the crown prince as emperor.
Hou Jing then pretended to issue an edict to pardon the Northerners who had been slaves. Trying to bribe these people for his use.
He also sent Yi Tong to Lailiang and led his troops to attack Xuancheng. Yang Hua, the internal historian in Xuancheng, was beheaded by Yang Liang. Hou Jing sent his general Li Xianming to attack Yang Hua, and Yang Hua led the county to surrender.
Hou Jing sent Yi, Song Zixian and others to lead the army eastward and stationed in Qiantang. The new city garrison leader Dai Sengyi seized the county to resist him.
This month, Hou Jing sent the Chinese army Hou Zijian into the Wu army, arrested Yu Ziyue and Zhang Dahei, and returned to the capital to kill them.
At that time, Lincheng Gong Xiao Dalian, the governor of Dongyangzhou, was guarding the state, and Zhang Sheng, the prefect of Wuxing, was guarding the county. From Nanling onwards, they were all guarding each other.
The only areas where Hou Jing's order could be implemented were west of Wu County and north of Nanling.
In June, Hou Jing appointed Guo Yuanjian as Shangshu Pushe, Beidao Xingtai, and general of all military forces in the north of the Yangtze River to guard the New Qin Dynasty.
County residents Lu Ji, Dai Wenju and others raised more than 10,000 troops and killed Su Shanyu, the governor sent by Hou Jing. They elected the former Huainan governor Wencheng Hou Xiaoning as the leader of the alliance to resist Hou Jing.
summary: Reinforcements arrived, but Hou Jing defeated them. Food ran out, leading to cannibalism. Hou Jing sought peace, demanding four Yangtze-right states and hostages. An alliance was made, but Hou Jing broke it, attacking again. The palace city fell; Hou Jing plundered, captured officials, and burned corpses. He falsely issued edicts, demoted Xiao Zhengde, and appointed his own governors. Emperor Gaozu died in May, reportedly from anger after Hou Jing's actions. Hou Jing hid the death for over twenty days before proclaiming the crown prince emperor.

translation:
After Song Zixian learned about it, he led his army to attack them, and Lu Ji and others abandoned the city and fled.
Hou Jing then separated Wujun Haiyan and Xupu counties to form Wuyuan County.
At this time, Hou Jing killed Xiao Zhengde in Yongfu Province. Yuan Luo was granted the title of King of Western Qin, Yuan Jinglong was granted the title of King of Chenliu, and more than ten of his descendants were granted the title of king.
He also used Running Salute as an envoy to hold the festival and the governor, subordinate to the prime minister, to participate in military affairs.
Hou Jing sent the Chinese army Hou Zijian, the supervisory station Liu Shenmao and others to lead an eastward crusade, defeated Wuxing, captured the prefect Zhang Sheng and his son, and sent them to the capital. Hou Jingji killed them together.
Hou Jing appointed Song Zixian as Situ and the leading general, including Zhu Jibo, Chiluo Zitong, Peng Jun, Dong Shaoxian, Zhang Huaren, Yu Qing, Lu Bohe, He Xijin, Shi Anhe, Shi Linghu, and Liu Guiyi, and he was also named the third division of Kaifu Yitong.
This month, Xiao Fan, the successor king of Poyang, led his troops to station at Zhakou. King Daxin of Xunyang, the governor of Jiangzhou, invited him to go west.
Hou Jing sent troops to garrison in Gushu, and Fan generals Pei Zhidi and Xiahou Weisheng led their troops to surrender to Hou Jing.
In November, Song Zixian attacked Qiantang and Dai Seng surrendered.
Hou Jing changed Qiantang to Linjiang County and Fuyang to Fuchun County.
Wang Wei and Yuan Luo were granted the title of "Yitong Sansi" at the same time.
In December, Song Zixian, Zhao Bochao and Liu Shenmao attacked Kuaiji. Xiao Dalian, Linchenggong, the governor of Dongyangzhou, abandoned the city and fled. Hou Jing sent Liu Shenmao to chase him and capture him.
Hou Jing appointed Pei Zhiti as his envoy Chijie, general Pingxi, and governor of Hezhou, and Xiahou Weisheng as his envoy Chijie, general Pingbei, and governor of South Yuzhou.
This month, Baekje's envoys arrived and saw that the capital city was in ruins. People were wailing outside the city, and everyone on the road shed tears when they saw it.
Hou Jing was furious when he heard about this, so he sent Baekje's envoys to Xiaozhuangyan Temple and locked them up, preventing them from entering or leaving.
In the first month of the first year of Dabao, Hou Jing pretended to have Shao's orders and added forty swordsmen to himself without permission. He also appointed himself a front and rear Yu Bao advocate, and also appointed himself a left and right chief minister and four ministers.
The former Jiangdu ordered Zu Hao to raise troops in Guangling, killed Dong Shao, the governor sent by Hou Jing, and elected Xiao Meng, the former prince's native, as the governor. He also contacted the Wei people as backup and used fast riding to publish proclamations to places far and near to denounce Hou Jing.
When Hou Jing heard the news, he was very frightened. On the same day, he led Hou Zijian and others to send troops from Saidan, and all the land, water and rain troops were mobilized.
Hou Jing refused to defend the city, but Hou Jing attacked the city and captured it.
Hou Jing split Zu Hao's chariot to show the public, and killed everyone in the city, old and young.
Hou Jing used the fort to monitor and supervise various affairs in Yanzhou in the south.
This month, Hou Jing summoned Song Zixian back to Jingkou.
In April, Hou Jing appointed Yuan Siqian as the host to guard Qiantang.
Hou Zijian was appointed as the governor of southern Yanzhou.
Xiao Ning, Marquis of Wencheng, raised an army in Wuxi Township. Within ten days, the number grew to 10,000, and he led his army to the west.
Hou Jing's princes Meng Zhen and Hou Zirong defeated him, beheaded Wencheng Hou Xiaoning and gave his head to Hou Jing.
In July, Hou Jing took Qin County as the western Yanzhou and Yangping County as the northern Yanzhou.
Ren Yue and Lu Hui slightly attacked Jinxi County and killed Xiao Si, the eldest son of Prince Poyang.
Hou Jing appointed Wang Wei as the Supervisor of the Zhongshu.
Ren Yue marched to attack Jiangzhou, and the governor of Jiangzhou, Xunyang Wang Xiao Dazhi, surrendered to him.
At that time, Emperor Shizu heard that Jiangzhou had been lost and sent General Xu Wensheng of the Guards to lead all the troops to Wuchang to resist Ren Yue.
Hou Jing also falsely announced that he had been enthroned as prime minister, and granted the title of King of Han Dynasty to twenty counties including Mount Tai. He did not follow the rules when he entered the court, praised and worshiped without honoring his name, and went to the palace with swords and shoes, just like the courtesy enjoyed by Xiao He in the Han Dynasty.
Hou Jing appointed Liu Jingli as the general guarding the army, Jiang Xunyi as the left chief historian of the prime minister, Xu Hong as the left Sima, Lu Yue as the right chief historian, and Shen Zhong as the right Sima.
This month, Hou Jing led his navy back to Anhui.
In October, bandits killed Xiao Zhen, Marquis of Wulin, in Guangmomen.
Because Wulin Marquis Xiao Zhen often came in and out of Taizong's palace, Hou Jing's party members were confused, so they sent people to kill him.
Hou Jing also falsely passed on Taizong's edict and said: Heaven shows signs, and the four seasons obtain their laws from the stars; all living things are nurtured by the earth, and all things rely on the sun and the moon to shine.
summary: Hou Jing continued campaigns, killing Xiao Zhengde and appointing puppet kings. He faced rebellions, including Zu Hao's in Guangling, which he crushed, killing all residents. In Dabao's first year, he granted himself titles and privileges. He defeated various forces, capturing cities. In October, he killed Wulin Hou Xiao Zhen. He falsely issued an edict, granting himself the title "General of the Universe." Qi's Xin Shu besieged Yangping but retreated. Xu Wensheng defeated Hou Jing's navy, but Hou Jing later captured Yingzhou. He failed to take Baling due to disease and fled after Ren Yue's defeat.

translation:
Since Baqiu suffered a setback, Hou Jing's army has been almost wiped out. He was afraid that the Qi people would take the opportunity to attack him from both sides with the army from the western vassal town, so he sent Guo Yuanjian to lead the infantry to Xiaoxian, and Hou Zijian led the navy to Ruxu to show off his strength in Feishui.
Hou Zijian arrived in Hefei, attacked Luocheng and captured it.
Soon, Guo Yuanjian and Hou Zijian heard that Wang's army was nearby, so they burned the city and residents' houses in Hefei and retreated with their troops. Hou Zijian guarded Gushu, and Guo Yuanjian withdrew his troops back to Guangling.
At this time, Xie Taren attacked Liu Shenmao, and Liu Shenmao's generals Wang Ye and Litong defended the outer camp. They surrendered to Xie Taren at the same time.
Liu Guiyi, Yin Sihe and others were afraid and abandoned the city and fled.
Liu Shenmao's lone army was in danger, so he surrendered to Xie Daren.
Wang Sengbian led his army to Wuhu, and the city lord of Wuhu fled overnight.
Hou Jing sent Shi Anhe, Song Changgui and others with two thousand troops to assist Hou Zijian in guarding Gushu. Hou Jing himself caught up with Tian Qian and others and led his army back to the capital.
This month, Guo Chang, a disciple of Hou Jing's party, presented a horse with horns.
In March, Hou Jing went to Gushu, inspected the military fortress, and warned Hou Zijian again: Westerners are good at water warfare, and you should not fight with them on the water to decide the outcome. In previous years, Ren Yue was defeated by them for this reason.
If we can fight them on land, we can definitely defeat them. You just need to strengthen the fortifications to hold on and watch the changes in the war.
In view of the fact that Hou Zi abandoned his ship and landed, he set up camp and could not hold on.
As a result, Wang Sengbian and others stopped military operations for more than ten days. Hou Zijian and others were overjoyed and reported to Hou Jing: The Western Division is afraid of the strength of our army. They will definitely want to escape. If they do not attack them, they will lose a good opportunity.
Hou Jing also ordered Hou Zijian to prepare for a water battle.
Since Hou Zi led more than 10,000 people on foot and cavalry to cross the island, he also led the navy to march together. Wang Sengbian fought and defeated Hou Zijian. Hou Zijian's entire army was wiped out, and only one person escaped back.
When Hou Jing heard about Hou Zijian's defeat, he cried in horror. He covered his head with a quilt and lay down. After a long time, he got up and sighed: "This guy accidentally killed me!"
Wang Sengbian marched and stationed himself at Zhang Gongzhou.
Hou Jing appointed Lu Hui to guard Stone City, and He Xijin to guard the national city. Hou Jing forced all the people and the families of the soldiers to move into Taicheng.
Wang Sengbian burned Hou Jing's water fence, entered the Huai River, and reached the waterside of Chanling Temple. Hou Jing was shocked, so he built a fence along the Huai River, from Stone City to Zhuquehang.
Wang Sengbian and other generals went ashore at the west port of Shitou City and set up a fence all the way to Luoxing Pier.
Hou Jing was so frightened that he personally led Hou Zijian, Yu Qing, Shi Anhe, Wang Senggui and others to build a camp in the northeast of Stone City to resist defense.
Hou Jing sent Wang Wei, Suo Chaoshi, and Lu Jilue to guard Taicheng, and Song Changgui sent to guard Yanzuo Temple.
Hou Jing also sent people to dig up the grave of Wang Sengbian's father, open the coffin, and burn the body.
Wang Sengbian and others marched and set up camp in the north of Stone City, and Hou Jing formed a formation to challenge.
Wang Sengbian led the troops to attack bravely and defeated Hou Jingjun. Hou Zijian, Shi Anhe, and Wang Sengui each abandoned the camp and fled. Lu Huilue and He Xijin led Shitoucheng to surrender to Wang Sengbian.
After Hou Jing's soldiers were defeated, he did not enter the palace city, but collected his scattered soldiers and stationed them under the city so that they could escape at any time.
Wang Wei pulled his horse's bridle to dissuade him and said: Since ancient times, there has never been an emperor who escaped!
Now that the guards in the palace can still fight, how can they just run away, abandon the capital, and plan to escape to where?
Hou Jing said: I attacked Helansheng in the north, destroyed Ge Rong, and became famous in He and Shuo. King Gao is of the same race.
Later, he crossed the river south, captured Taicheng with ease, defeated King Shaoling on the north mountain, and defeated Liu Zhongli on the south bank. These are all things you have seen with your own eyes.
If we are defeated today, I am afraid that God will kill me.
You defend the city well, and I will fight them to the death again.
Looking up at the Stone City Palace, I lingered and sighed for a long time.
Finally, he put his two sons in leather bags and hung them on the saddles, and fled eastward with his Yi, Tian Qian, Fan Xirong and other hundreds of horses.
Wang Wei abandoned Taicheng and fled. Hou Zijian and others also fled to Guangling.
Wang Sengbian sent Hou Yi to lead his army to pursue Hou Jing.
Hou Jing fled to Jinling, kidnapped the prefect Xu Yong and fled eastward to Wujun, where he stationed in Jiaxing. Zhao Bochao took Qiantang to resist him.
Hou Jing withdrew his army and returned to Wu County. When they arrived at Songjiang, Hou Yi's army suddenly attacked. Hou Jing's troops had not yet formed their formation, and they all held up flags and asked Hou Yi to surrender.
Hou Jing couldn't stop him, so he had to escape in a boat with ten of his close friends, pushed his two sons into the water, and then entered the sea from Hudu.
When they arrived at Hudouzhou, Yang Kun, the former prince's servant, killed Hou Jing and gave the body to Wang Sengbian. Yu Sengbian sent Hou Jing's head to the west platform and displayed the body in Jiankang Market. The people competed to cut his flesh and eat it, and burned his bones to ashes and discarded them.
People who had been harmed by Hou Jing mixed Hou Jing's ashes with wine and drank it.
Hou Jing's head was sent to Jiangling, where Emperor Shizu ordered it to be hung for public display, then boiled, painted and handed over to the arsenal.
Hou Jing is less than seven feet tall, but has handsome features.
summary: Hou Jing deposed Taizong, imprisoning him, and established Xiao Dong as emperor. He killed Taizong with a silk cloth weighted with earth. In October, he forced Xiao Dong to abdicate, proclaiming himself emperor with the era name Taishi. He changed Liang's regulations to Han's, but his ignorance of ancestry caused ridicule. In the second year, his forces were defeated by Wang Sengbian. Hou Jing fled east with his sons in leather bags. At Hudouzhou, former prince's servant Yang Kun killed him. His body was displayed, and people ate his flesh, burned his bones, and mixed ashes with wine.

translation:
When Marquis Zhenyang's army was destroyed, the border towns were in fear and panic. Emperor Gaozu was already very worried about this, but he said: Now that we have reached the point of being sent away, do we have to give up the country like the Jin Dynasty?
Previously, Danyang Tao Hongjing lived in seclusion in Huayang Mountain. He was very knowledgeable and knowledgeable. He once wrote a poem and said: The Yifu was willful and unrestrained. He sat in Mangtan and talked about fantasy Buddhism. Unexpectedly, Zhaoyang Palace turned into the Shanyu Palace of the Xiongnu.
In the last years of Datong, scholars competed to talk about mystical principles and did not study military affairs. Now Hou Jing has indeed entered Zhaoyang Palace.
During the Tianjian period, there was a Shi Zhizhi that said: A dog with a tail dug suddenly went crazy, biting people when they were still alive, and then killed itself, fell from the white wall, and died in three embraces.
He also said: The boy from the Shan family stretched out his clothes, raised his arms, and turned into a tiger in front of the Tai Chi Hall, staring eagerly.
The tail-hunting dog and the mountain boy are both shaped like monkeys.
In this way, Hou Jing destroyed and captured Kyoto and poisoned the royal family.
During the Datong period, the imperial physician ordered Zhu Dan to stay in the forbidden province. Not long after, he dreamed that a dog and a sheep were sitting on the emperor's throne. When he woke up, he was disgusted by this. He told others: Dogs and sheep are not good things. They occupy the emperor's throne. Will there be chaos in the country?
Afterwards, it turned out that the emperor suffered a disaster, and Hou Jing ascended the main hall.
When Hou Jing was about to be defeated, there was a monk named Seng Tong. His temperament was like a madman, and he drank and ate meat just like ordinary people. He had been wandering around the world for decades, and no one knew his name and place of origin.
What he said had obscure meanings that could only be verified after a long time. People called him Tianli, and Hou Jing believed and respected him very much.
Hou Jing once shot arrows with his followers in the back hall. At that time, Seng Tong was also there. He took Hou Jing's bow and shot an arrow at Jing Yacan, shouting "I'm a slave."
Wu Jing later held a banquet to gather with his followers, and summoned Seng Tong to the banquet. Seng Tong took the meat, rubbed it with salt, gave it to Hou Jing, and asked: "Is it okay?"
Hou Jing replied: It's just too salty.
Sengtong said: If the meat is not salted, it will stink.
Sure enough, Hou Jing's body was sealed with salt.
Wang Wei, a native of Chen Liu, was very talented and learned when he was young. Hou Jing's tables, letters, letters, and messages were all drafted and produced by Wang Wei.
After Hou Jing succeeded, he planned to usurp the throne, and it was Wang Wei who made the plans for him.
Later, Wang Wei was imprisoned and sent to Jiangling, where he was cooked in the market. The people who had been poisoned by Wang Wei cut off his flesh and roasted it for eating.
Shi Chen said: The way of heaven will not be peaceful for a long time, nor will the destiny of the country be peaceful for a long time. This is because embarrassment and prosperity have a certain end, and prosperity and decline alternate with each other. This is the reason why the Liang Dynasty suffered misfortune.
A boy like Hou Jing was domineering in his own country, his knowledge could not protect him, and his courage was not outstanding, but Wang Wei became his mastermind and made his evil conspiracy succeed.
He led a group of party members to cross the Yangtze River, and with the help of halberds and powerful crossbows, he captured the capital, brought disaster to the emperor, and caused disaster to all the people in the world. He acted arbitrarily, causing the disaster of usurping and stealing the throne.
summary: Hou Jing was under seven feet tall with handsome features but was cruel, often mutilating victims before death. He wore a white gauze hat and green robe, sometimes with a tooth comb in his bun. He rode a white horse; it neighed before victories and lowered its head before defeats. Emperor Gaozu's dream of中原 prefectures surrendering led him to accept Hou Jing, a decision later regretted. Omens, including a poem by Tao Hongjing and a prophecy about a dog and sheep, foretold Hou Jing's rise. A monk named Seng Tong, whom Hou Jing respected, made cryptic remarks about salt, foreshadowing Hou Jing's body being salted after death. Wang Wei, Hou Jing's adviser, was later cooked in the market. The historian noted that Hou Jing's cruelty surpassed previous usurpers, attributing his rise to divine timing and human folly.

translation:
Prince Zhaoming Xiao Tong, courtesy name Deshi, was the eldest son of Emperor Wu of Liang.
The biological mother is Ding Guibi.
At first, Emperor Wu of Liang had no boys. When Emperor Wu of Liang led an uprising against the Marquis of Donghun, Xiao Tong was born in Xiangyang in September of the first year of Zhongxing in Qi.
After Emperor Wu of Liang ascended the throne, a minister submitted a letter requesting the establishment of a crown prince. Emperor Wu of Liang believed that the world had just stabilized and many systems were lacking and needed to be further improved, so he did not agree to appoint a successor to the throne.
Later, at the firm request of the ministers, in November of the first year of Tianjian, Xiao Tong was made the crown prince by Emperor Wu of Liang.
The prince was young at that time and still lived in the palace. Prince Xiao Tong was born with intelligence and cleverness. He started learning "The Classic of Filial Piety" and "The Analects of Confucius" at the age of three. By the age of five, he had learned all the Five Classics and was able to recite them.
On June 17, the fifth year, he moved out of the palace and moved into the East Palace.
Xiao Tong was kind and filial by nature. Since leaving the palace, he often missed his parents and was always in a depressed mood.
After Emperor Wu of Liang knew about this situation, he asked him to visit the court every five days, and he often stayed in Yongfu Province, sometimes for three days, sometimes for five days, before returning to the East Palace.
In September of the eighth year, Emperor Wu of Liang inspected his son's studies in Shou'an Hall and asked Xiao Tong to explain the "Book of Filial Piety". Xiao Tong's explanation was clear and clear.
After the explanation, he personally went to the Chinese Academy of Sciences to arrange a banquet to pay homage to the most holy teacher.
On the first day of the first lunar month of the 14th year, Emperor Wu of Liang met with his ministers on the platform in front of the palace and held a crowning ceremony for Prince Xiao Tong in the Taiji Palace.
In the past, it was stipulated that the prince should wear a crown of distant travel and a golden tassel of green cicadas; this time the emperor issued an order for the prince to wear a crown of Jinbo Mountain.
Xiao Tong was handsome and well behaved.
When reading, you can count the lines at a glance and be able to remember everything.
Every time there is a grand gathering of ancestral feasts, poems can be composed with dozens of rhymes.
Sometimes Emperor Wu of Liang asked him to compose dramatic rhyme poems, and he could always compose them with a little thought without any modification or modification.
Emperor Wu of Liang vigorously promoted Buddhism and personally explained Buddhist scriptures. Prince Xiao Tong also believed in the Three Jewels of Buddhism: Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, and read many Buddhist scriptures.
And the Huiyi Hall was built in the palace as a church to explain Buddhist doctrines. It attracted famous monks and often discussed and studied Buddhist scriptures together.
Xiao Tong himself also created the Two Truths Dharmakaya Sutra, which has his own unique insights.
In April of the first year of the ordinary year, nectar fell on the Huiyi Palace. Everyone thought it was the prince's virtue that moved heaven.
In November of the seventh year, Ding Guibi, the biological mother of Prince Xiao Tong, fell ill. He returned to Yongfu Province and stayed by the hospital bed day and night to observe the condition and did not even take off his clothes when sleeping.
summary: Prince Zhaoming Xiao Tong, the eldest son of Emperor Wu of Liang, was born in Xiangyang in September of the first year of Zhongxing in Qi. His mother was Ding Guibi. After Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Xiao Tong was made crown prince in November of the first year of Tianjian. He was intelligent from a young age, learning the classics by age five. In the fifth year, he moved to the East Palace but often missed his parents, visiting them every five days. In the eighth year, he explained the "Book of Filial Piety" to his father. He was crowned in the 14th year, wearing a Jinbo Mountain crown. Xiao Tong was handsome, well-behaved, and had a remarkable memory, composing poems effortlessly. He believed in Buddhism, built the Huiyi Hall for lectures, and authored the Two Truths Dharmakaya Sutra. In the seventh year, his mother fell ill; he cared for her tirelessly and mourned deeply after her death, eating only one liter of rice porridge daily despite imperial pleas. He lost significant weight. After his coronation, he handled state affairs with diligence, correcting errors without punishment, and showed leniency in judgments. He was generous, nurturing talent, and fostered a literary culture with over 30,000 volumes in the East Palace. He enjoyed nature, rejecting additions like female musicians. He lived frugally, aided the poor, and provided coffins for the dead. He opposed a canal project that would disrupt farming. Xiao Tong died on April 6 at age 31, mourned by all. He authored many works, including the "Selected Works." Prince Ai, named Renzong, was the eldest son of Taizong, born in May of the fourth year. He was granted titles and positions, and during Hou Jing's rebellion, he was made governor. After Taizong's ascension, he became crown prince. In the second year of Dashi, Hou Jing deposed Taizong and killed the prince, who faced death calmly. He was posthumously named Prince Ai. Prince Minghuai, Fang Ju, was the fourth son of Shizu, initially Marquis of Nan'an County. He held military and civil posts, was made prince, and later crown prince. He was killed by Wei soldiers. Yao Cha praised Zhaoming's virtues, comparing him to Shun.

translation:
Fan Yun, courtesy name Yanlong, was born in Wuyin, Nanxiang, and was the sixth-generation descendant of Jiewang, the Pingbei general of the Jin Dynasty.
When he was eight years old, he met Yin Yan, the governor of Yuzhou in the Song Dynasty, on the road. Yin Yan saw that his appearance was very unusual, so he invited him to sit with him.
Yin Yan asked him to compose a poem, and he wrote it immediately.
Everyone present was impressed. Fan Yun once studied with his relative Yuan Zhao and worked tirelessly day and night.
Yuan Zhao patted his shoulder and said, "You are bright and cheerful, and you are diligent in studying." He will definitely be a talented person in the future.
Fan Yun has been smart and flexible since he was a child, and he is insightful when dealing with things. He is good at writing articles and is familiar with various literary styles such as letters.
His father, Fan Kang, served in the Ying Mansion and joined the army. Fan Yun lived with his father in Fubao. At that time, Shen Yue from Wuxing, Yu Daizhi from Xinye, and Fan Kangtong were working in Ying Mansion. Fan Yun immediately became good friends after meeting them.
Fan Yun first served as Shuzuo of Xicao in Yingzhou, and then joined the army as Cao Xing of Facao.
Soon Shen Youzhi rebelled and raised troops to besiege Ying City. Fan Kang was appointed Changliu of Ying Mansion at that time and entered the city to take charge of defense, leaving his family members outside the city.
Fan Yun was captured by enemy soldiers, and Youzhi interrogated him personally. His tone was very stern, but Fan Yun's appearance remained unchanged and he answered calmly.
After hearing this, Youzhi smiled and said: "You are such a pleasant child. Go home for now."
The next morning, Youzhi sent for Fan Yun again and ordered him to deliver a message to Cheng Bao.
Some of the defenders in the city advocated killing Fan Yun. Fan Yun said: I have an old mother and a young brother at home outside the city. Their lives are all in Shen's hands. If I disobey orders, they will be harmed. Today I am killed for them, and I am willing to die without any regrets.
Longshi Ryu Shiryong Pingsuo was friendly with Fan Yun and managed to save him from death.
In the early years of Jianyuan of Qi Dynasty, Prince Liang of Jingling became the prefect of Kuaiji, and Fan Yun just started to follow Prince Jingling at that time.
The king didn't know him well. It happened that King Jingling was visiting Qinwang Mountain. The king asked the people around him to identify the ancient characters on the stone inscriptions, but no one could understand them. Only Fan Yun could read the inscriptions. King Jingling was very happy. From then on, Jiang Zhou was favored more than anyone else in the same house.
When King Jingling was appointed Danyang Yin, Fan Yun was summoned to be the chief administrator, and he was highly valued by his close associates.
When he came to see Emperor Gao of Qi, someone happened to offer a white crow. Emperor Gao asked what this meant was a sign. Because Fan Yun was in a low position, he finally replied: I heard that when the emperor worships the ancestral temple, white crows will come.
At that time, the visit to the ancestral temple had just ended.
Emperor Yigao said: Just as you said.
The principle of induction between heaven and man can be so miraculously consistent.
Fan Yun later transferred to the prison of the North and South County Prince to join the military. He also served as the chief secretary and was promoted to the position of Zhonglang in the Shangshu Palace.
summary: Fan Yun, courtesy name Yanlong, was born in Wuyin, Nanxiang, and was a sixth-generation descendant of Jiewang, a Jin Dynasty general. At age eight, he impressed Yin Yan, a Song Dynasty governor, by composing a poem on the spot. He studied diligently with his relative Yuan Zhao, who predicted he would become a talented person. Fan Yun was intelligent, insightful, and skilled in writing various literary styles. He lived with his father, Fan Kang, in Fubao and befriended Shen Yue, Yu Daizhi, and Fan Kangtong. Fan Yun began his official career as Shuzuo of Xicao in Yingzhou. During Shen Youzhi's rebellion, Fan Yun was captured but remained calm under interrogation, earning his release. He later delivered a message for Youzhi, risking death to protect his family. Longshi Ryu Shiryong saved him. In the early Qi Dynasty, Fan Yun served Prince Jingling, impressing him by reading ancient inscriptions on Qinwang Mountain. He became a trusted chief administrator and was favored by Emperor Gao of Qi for interpreting a white crow as an auspicious sign.

translation:
When Xiao Ziliang was a Situ, Jianyun joined the military affairs department and was soon awarded the title of Minister of Tongzhi Sanqi, and also the chief of the Honshu Dazhongzheng.
Later, he served as the internal history of Lingling. During his tenure, he was able to keep himself clean and tidy, eliminating many cumbersome government orders and unnecessary expenses, so that the people could live and work in peace and contentment.
Emperor Qi Ming summoned Fan Yun back to the capital. After arriving, he was granted the title of Minister of Sanqi.
He also served as the internal history of Shixing.
There are many powerful and cunning families in Shixing County. If the county governor does not treat them well, they will conspire to kill him together. If they fail, they will drive the governor away.
The border counties of Shixing were inhabited by barbarian tribes, and there were particularly many thieves in these areas. In the past, all the officials in the imperial office wore weapons for self-defense.
After Fan Yun arrived in Shixing, he used his kindness to appease them and removed the surveillance post.
The merchants who came and went could sleep in peace, and the people in the county praised him as a god, so he was promoted to Jiajie, General Jianwu, General Pingyue Zhonglang, and Governor of Guangzhou.
At the beginning, Ji Yun was friendly with Shangshu Pu Shesi Yu, and his younger brother served as the magistrate of Diliao County, entrusting Xian Yi to Lian Nuo for care.
Zhanli is a wealthy family in the county. He was punished by Xu Yi and was flogged. Tan Bao felt humiliated and went to the capital to accuse Fan Yun. Fan Yun was recalled to the capital and convicted and imprisoned. It happened to be an amnesty and he was exempted from punishment.
In the second year of Qi Yongyuan, he was re-appointed as Dr. Guozi.
At first, Ji Yun had met Luan Chandan at the residence of King Tuzao of Zhajing. Yi had lived in a nearby lane, and Liang Gaozu thought highly of him.
When the army opposing Shuhunhou arrived in the capital, Fan Yun was in the city.
After Saihunhou was executed, Zhang Ji, the servant, sent Fan Yun out of the city with a mission. Luan Gaozu kept him and made him serve as a staff officer in the army and strategize. He was also awarded the title of Huangmen Shilang, and worked together with Shen Yue to assist Gaozu.
Soon he was promoted to Grand Sima, joined the army and recorded affairs.
After the establishment of the Liang Dynasty, Fan Yun was promoted to the rank of Shizhong.
At that time, Liang Gaozuna married Qi Shuhunhou's concubine Yu, which seriously affected the government affairs of the court. Fan Yun once made a remonstrance about this, but it was not accepted.
Later, Fan Yun and Wang Mao entered Gaozu's bedroom and remonstrated again: When Mo Xuanzu was in Shandong in the past, he was greedy for wealth and loved beautiful women; but after entering the customs and pacifying the Qin Dynasty, he did not collect property or be intimate with women. Fan Zeng believed that this was because of his lofty ambitions.
Now, Your Majesty, you have just stabilized the world, and everyone in the world admires your reputation. How can you follow in the footsteps of the confused king and be dragged down by women and delay the great event?
Wang Mao also took the opportunity to stand up and bow down and said: "What Fan Yun said is absolutely true. My lord, you must put the world's major events first and you should not regret the future."
Emperor Gaozu was silent after hearing this.
Fan Yun then went to Shu and suggested that Wang Mao should be rewarded with the Yu family. Emperor Gaozu thought that what he said was loyal and upright, so he approved it.
The next day, Emperor Gaozu rewarded Fan Yun and Wang Mao with one million coins each.
In the first year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu of Liang received Zen and ascended the throne. He held a ceremony of burning firewood to offer sacrifices to heaven in the southern suburbs. Fan Yun participated in the ceremony as an attendant.
summary: Fan Yun held various positions, including prison officer, chief secretary, and Zhonglang in the Shangshu Palace. As internal history of Lingling, he governed with integrity, reducing burdens on the people. He later served as internal history of Shixing, where he pacified powerful families and barbarian tribes through kindness, removing surveillance posts and ensuring safety for merchants. He was promoted to General Jianwu and Governor of Guangzhou. Fan Yun was recalled to the capital due to a dispute involving his friend's brother and was imprisoned but pardoned. In the second year of Qi Yongyuan, he became Dr. Guozi. He met Liang Gaozu at Prince Jingling's residence and later served as a staff officer during the rebellion against Saihunhou. After the Liang Dynasty's establishment, Fan Yun became Shizhong and remonstrated with Gaozu about marrying Qi Shuhunhou's concubine Yu, advising him to prioritize state affairs. Gaozu accepted his advice and rewarded him.

translation:
After the sacrifice ceremony, Emperor Gaozu boarded the chariot and said to Fan Yun: My mood today is just like what the ancients said: being cautious is like driving six horses with rotten reins.
Fan Yun replied: I hope your Majesty will become more cautious every day.
Emperor Gaozu admired Fan Yun very much.
On the same day, he was awarded the title of Changshi of Sanqi and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel. He was also granted the title of Marquis of Xiaocheng County with the title of Marquis of Xiaocheng County, with a settlement of 1,000 households for his meritorious service in assisting the emperor to ascend the throne.
Fan Yun was promoted based on his old friendship with Emperor Gaozu, and his official position was higher than that of other ministers who served. He also devoted his loyalty to assisting the king and tried his best to do everything he could think of.
Emperor Gaozu also appointed him with confidence and boldness, and most of the things asked by Fan Yun were granted.
Fan Yun once accompanied the imperial banquet. Emperor Gaozu said to Xiao Hong, King of Linchuan, and Xiao Hui, King of Poyang: Fan Shangshu and I have been friendly and affectionate as brothers since we were young. Now that I am the lord of the world, this brotherly courtesy has become the relationship between monarch and minister. You should call Fan Yun brother on my behalf.
The two kings left the banquet to pay homage and offered homage, and took a carriage with Fan Yun back to the lower province of Shangshu. People at that time were very proud of Fan Yun.
In this year, the crown prince was established, and Fan Yun took over the crown prince's concubine with his original official position. Soon he was promoted to the right servant of the minister, and he still held the post of official official.
Later, he was found guilty of employing people against the emperor's will and was dismissed from the official position, but still served as a servant.
Fan Yun has an honest and easy-going temperament, and serves his widowed sister-in-law with all his heart and courtesy. All matters at home must be discussed with his widowed sister-in-law before being implemented.
He likes integrity, advocates great deeds, and is dedicated to helping others in distress.
When he was a child, he was friendly with the commander Shi Wangke. Later Wangke died in the official house. The family was poor and did not have a house of his own, so Fan Yun transported the deceased back to his home and personally handled all the funeral arrangements.
When serving Prince Jingling, he received great favor and courtesy. But every time Fan Yun spoke about his achievements and failures in politics, he never showed any flattery.
Ziliang once asked Emperor Wu of Qi to select Fan Yun as the county governor.
Emperor Wu said: Fan Yun is a mediocre man. I heard that he often shows off his talents. I will not pursue it thoroughly now. I should forgive him and go to a remote place to serve.
Ziliang replied: That's not the case.
Fan Yun often advised and taught me, and the documents of his admonitions are still preserved. Please let me get them and present them to you.
When I took a look, I found more than a hundred pieces of paper, all with sincere and candid words.
Emperor Wu sighed infinitely, so he said to Ziliang: I didn't expect Fan Yun to be like this.
You just let him assist you, how can you let him go out to be a county guard?
Prince Qi Wenhui once went to Shutian to watch the harvest of crops. He turned around and said to his entourage: "It turns out that harvesting crops is also worth seeing."
Everyone is just right.
Only Fan Yun said: The busy farming season three times a year is really a long-term hard work. I hope that Your Highness can understand the hardship of farming and not be greedy for one-day pleasure and ease.
After coming out of Shutian, the servant Xiao Mian, who had not known Fan Yun before, approached Fan Yun's car, held his hand and said: I didn't expect to hear words of loyalty again today.
When Fan Yun was in charge of selecting officials, he held a noble and prestigious position. There were piles of letters and documents, and the house was full of guests. However, Fan Yun was able to cope with the situation smoothly without any obstruction. The official documents and instructions were sent out quickly. People at that time admired his intelligence and erudition.
Fan Yun's character was straightforward and easily excited, lacking dignity and solemnity. He showed his right and wrong in his heart rashly, and some scholar-bureaucrats were dissatisfied with him because of this.
At first, when Fan Yun became the county governor, people praised him for his integrity. However, after he became more powerful, he valued giving gifts to others. However, the family had no savings, so whenever he had income, he immediately distributed it to relatives and friends.
In the second year of Tianjian, Fan Yun died at the age of fifty-three.
summary: In the first year of Tianjian, Fan Yun participated in the southern郊 sacrifice. Gaozu praised his caution, and Fan Yun was appointed Changshi of Sanqi, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Marquis of Xiaocheng County. He was promoted based on his friendship with Gaozu and served loyally. Gaozu instructed his sons to treat Fan Yun as a brother. Fan Yun later became crown prince's concubine and right servant of the minister but was dismissed for employing people against the emperor's will. Fan Yun was honest, easy-going, and devoted to his widowed sister-in-law. He helped the poor, such as transporting the deceased commander Shi Wangke's body for burial. He advised Prince Jingling on political matters without flattery. Emperor Wu of Qi initially considered Fan Yun mediocre but later praised his sincerity after reading his admonitions. Fan Yun advised Prince Qi Wenhui to understand farming hardships. As an official, he handled documents efficiently but was criticized for his straightforwardness. He distributed his income to relatives and friends, leaving no savings.

translation:
Emperor Gaozu burst into tears when he heard the news, and immediately drove to express his condolences in person.
The edict was issued and said: Recalling the past makes people feel sad, which is due to deep emotions; besides, his reputation and reputation are still among us, and he is a highly valued minister.
The late Sanqi Changshi, Shangshu Youpuse, and Xiaocheng Hou Fanyun were loyal and upright in the eyes of the law. They made far-sighted plans for national affairs. They had great ambitions in their early years and had a long-standing reputation for their daily work.
Since he took off his turban and became an official, Qingming's political achievements have been very remarkable.
He is indeed the prime minister and assistant minister that everyone looks up to when co-managing state affairs in the DPRK.
His diligent assistance and his righteousness have always been engraved in my heart. Although he is not in charge of military affairs, he is a civil servant who has long discussed and planned government affairs with me.
Just when he had a long way to go and had been supporting the country for a long time, he suddenly lost his life, which really makes people feel infinitely sad.
Officials, titles, ranks, and salaries should be given to complete the beautiful system.
He can be given the posthumous title of Shizhong or General of the Guard, but the title of Pushe or Marquis remains unchanged.
And rewarded with a drum band.
Officials from the Ministry of Rites requested that the title of Mi be added as Xuan, and the emperor ordered that the title of Mi should be changed to Wen.
There are thirty volumes of collected works.
His son Fan Xiaocai inherited the title and became a prince.
Shen Yue, courtesy name Xiuwen, was born in Wukang, Wuxing.
His grandfather, Shen Linzi, was the general of Nanchi Sai.
His father Yilong once served as the prefect of Kuangzhi.
Xuan Hui was executed in the last years of Yuanjia. The young Shen Yue hid in Tibet to avoid persecution. Only after a general amnesty did he avoid exile.
After that, he lived in a foreign country for a long time and faced a life of loneliness and poverty. However, he was determined to learn and worked tirelessly day and night.
His mother was worried that he would become ill from overwork, so she often cut down the lamp oil and extinguished the lights to make him go to bed early.
However, Shen Yue just read during the day and recited silently at night. Finally, he read a lot of books and wrote good articles.
At the beginning, Yibao served as a court official.
Yuanbao Ji Xingsai heard that he was talented and appreciated him very much. When Cai Xingzong was appointed governor of Yingzhou, he invited foreign soldiers from Anxi to join the army and also served as a recorder.
Tomb Emperor Zong often said to his sons: Shen Jishi's conduct can serve as a model for others, and you should learn from him.
Later, Cai Xingzong was appointed as the governor of Jingzhou, and he asked someone to join the army in the Zhengxi Record Office to lead the magistrate of Youxian County.
After Cai Xingzong's death, he began to appoint Facao, King of Anxi and Jin Dynasties, to join the army, transfer to foreign soldiers to join the army, and also serve as a recorder.
He became Shangshu Duzhilang.
At the beginning of the investigation, Yimian was the record room of Zhenglu, with the order of Sedang, and the one he served was the king of Mansese.
The prince moved into Shu Palace and was appointed as the captain of the infantry school. He was in charge of the secretary of the East Palace, directing Yongshou Province and collating four books.
summary: Fan Yun died at age fifty-three in the second year of Tianjian. Gaozu mourned deeply and issued an edict praising his loyalty and wisdom. He was posthumously given titles and honors, including Shizhong and General of the Guard. His collected works comprised thirty volumes. His son Fan Xiaocai inherited his title. Shen Yue, courtesy name Xiuwen, was born in Wukang, Wuxing. His grandfather was General Shen Linzi, and his father was Prefect Shen Yilong. After his father's execution, Shen Yue hid to avoid persecution. He studied diligently, often reading at night despite his mother's concerns. He served as a court official and impressed Cai Xingzong, who appointed him as a recorder. Shen Yue later held various positions, including Shangshu Duzhilang and captain of the infantry school. He was close to the prince and served in the East Palace.

translation:
During the period of time, there were many talented people in the palace of the prince, but Shen Yue was particularly close and trusted. He went to the palace every morning to pay homage to the prince, and did not come out until the sun was setting in the west.
At that time, the princes went to the East Palace to see the prince, but some of them were not allowed to enter. This matter was often mentioned in the palace.
The prince said: I am always too lazy to get up early. You know this. After listening to your talk, I forget to sleep.
If you want me to get up early, come to the palace early to see me.
He was moved to the crown prince's family, and later he was appointed as an official and a scholar, moved to Zhongshu Lang, Zhongzheng of the city, Situ Youchangshi, and Huangmen Shilang.
At that time, King Jingling was also looking for talented people. Shen Yue, Xiao Chen of Lanling, Wang Rong of Langxie, Xie Tiao of Chenjun, Fan Yun of Nanxiang, Ren Fang of Le'an and others all visited the palace of King Jingling. Everyone in the world praised King Jingling for his ability to know people.
Soon he was appointed as Minister Zuocheng, and then as Yushi Zhongcheng, and he was transferred to the chariot and long history.
In the first year of Longchang, he was promoted to general Ningshuo and prefect of Shuyang in addition to the officials.
When Emperor Ming of Qi came to the throne, Shen Yue was promoted to the title of General of the Auxiliary State, appointed as the Minister of the Five Arms, and moved to the State to offer wine.
Emperor Ming died, and the government returned to the prime minister. Shangshu ordered Xu Xiaosi to let Shen Yue write a decree to dispatch Shao.
He was moved to the left guard general, and soon became a regular servant of Zhi Sanqi.
In the second year of Yongyuan, because his mother was old and petitioned to be relieved of his post, he was awarded the titles of Champion General and Situ Zuo Changshi, and the titles of General Zhenglu and Grand Administrator of Nanqinghe.
At the beginning, when Gaozu was in the west residence of King Jingling, he had an old acquaintance with Shen. After the city of Jiankang was captured, he was sent down to the Hussars and Sima, and he continued to serve as a general.
During the period of Emperor Gaozu's great achievements, ascending the throne and proclaiming himself emperor was the will of God and the people's will. Shen Yue once raised this issue with Gaozu, but Gaozu responded silently.
Another day, Shen Yue spoke to Emperor Gaozu again and said: Today is different from ancient times. We cannot expect everyone to maintain a simple style.
The scholar-bureaucrats all cling to the dragon and the phoenix, hoping to gain a certain amount of merit in order to ensure their fortune.
Now even the children and shepherd boys know that Qi's energy is exhausted, and everyone says that you should take his place.
Moreover, no matter astronomy or human affairs, there are signs of changes in the national destiny, especially since Shuhun Hou Yongyuan.
The prophecy says that if you walk in water, you will become the emperor, and this is clearly recorded.
God's will cannot be disobeyed, and the human heart cannot be lost. If God arranges it this way, even if you want to be humble and courteous, in fact you will not be able to do it. Gaozu said: I am considering this matter.
Shen Yue also said: When Duke Ming first raised his troops between Fancheng and Mianshui, he should have considered this. Now that the emperor's foundation is ready, what else is there to consider?
summary: Shen Yue joined Prince Jingling's circle of talented individuals. He held positions such as Minister Zuocheng and Yushi Zhongcheng. Under Emperor Ming of Qi, he became General of the Auxiliary State and Minister of the Five Arms. After Emperor Ming's death, he wrote decrees for the prime minister. He later served as Left Guard General and Zhi Sanqi. In the second year of Yongyuan, he resigned due to his mother's age but was awarded titles.

translation:
In the past, King Wu of the Zhou Dynasty crusaded against the Shang Dynasty. When he first entered the court, people called him my king. King Wu did not go against people's wishes and had nothing to consider.
Since Ming Gong came to Jiankang in Kyoto, his Qi has been established. Compared with King Wu of Zhou, it is just different sooner or later.
If you do not decide on your great cause in advance, you will delay the hope of heaven and man, and if anyone raises objections, it will damage your majesty.
Moreover, people are not like gold and stone, and current events are unpredictable.
Should we just leave the title of Duke Jian'an to future generations?
If the emperor returns to the capital and the ministers each have their respective positions, then the status between the monarch and his ministers has been determined, and they will no longer have any dissent.
So if the king is a wise man and is at the top, and the ministers are loyal and fulfill their duties below, how can anyone join you in rebelling again?
Gaozu thought it was right.
After Shen Yue resigned, Gaozu summoned Fan Yun again to ask his opinion. Fan Yun's answer was roughly the same as Shen Yue's.
Emperor Gaozu said: What a wise man sees is so coincident. I will come back tomorrow morning with Shen Xiuwen.
After Fan Yun resigned, he told Shen Yue what Gaozu had said. Shen Yue said: Sir, you must wait for me.
Fan Yun promised. The next day, Shen Yue arrived first, and Emperor Gaozu ordered him to draft a Shao letter for Khotan to ascend the throne.
Shen Yue took out the Shao Shu and the list of candidates that had been prepared in advance from his arms. Gao Zu did not make any changes.
After a while, Fan Yun came from outside. He could not enter the palace gate, so he had to wander outside Shouguang Pavilion, making strange "duh" sounds in his mouth.
When Shen Yue came out, Fan Yun asked: What was the result?
Shen Yue raised his hand to the left, indicating that the matter was settled. Fan Yun smiled and said: "It will live up to expectations."
After a while, Emperor Gaozu summoned Fan Yun and said to him: I have been with Shen Xiuwen all my life, and I didn't think there was anything different about him. Today, I see that he is very intelligent and wise.
Fan Yun said: Ming Gong understands Shen Yue only now, just like Shen Yue understands Ming Gong only today.
Emperor Gaozu said: It has been three years since I started the army. All the meritorious officers and generals have indeed made meritorious service. However, it is you two who can make me achieve my imperial career.
When the Liang Kingdom was established, Shen Yue was a regular servant of Sanqi, a minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and a right-hand servant.
Emperor Gaozu was enthroned by Zen, appointed Shen Yue as a minister and a servant, and was granted the feudal title of Marquis of Changxian County.
He also consecrated Shen Yue's mother, Xie, as Mrs. Jianchang.
On the day he was given the order, his right servant She Fan Yun and more than 20 people came to congratulate him. Everyone in the government and the public considered Shen Yue to be extremely honorable.
Soon he was moved to Zuopushe, Shangshu, and served as a regular attendant as before.
Soon he also led the army and served as a servant.
In the second year of Tianjian's reign, Shen Yue's mother passed away. Emperor Gaozu came to pay his respects in person. Because Shen Yue was old and it was not appropriate for his mother's death to affect his health, Emperor Gaozu sent people from Zhongshushe to stop the guests and persuade him to refrain from mourning.
He was appointed Shen Yue, general of the town army, Danyang Yin, and appointed assistant history officer.
When the period of mourning was over, he moved to Shizhong, Youguanglu, the official, and took charge of Prince Zhan Shi. Yangzhou Dazhongzheng reported to the emperor the eight articles of Shangshu, and moved to Shangshu Ling. He served as Shizhong, Zhanshi, and Zhongzheng.
After repeated submissions of resignation, he was granted the title of Shangshu Zuopushe, Lingzhongshuling, former general, appointed assistant historian, and served as a servant as before.
Soon he was moved to the post of Shangshu Ling and led the prince's young master.
In the ninth year of Tianjian, he was transferred to Dr. Zuo Guanglu and served as Shizhong and Shaofu. He was given the title of a drummer band.
At first, Shen Yue had been in the position of prime minister for a long time and often yearned for the position of the Three Dukes. Current commentaries also believed that he was suitable for this position. However, Emperor Gaozu never agreed. Shen Yue then requested to go out to serve, but the emperor did not allow it.
Shen Yueyu Xu Mian was always friendly, so he wrote to Xu Mian to express his feelings. He said: I was lonely when I was young, and I had no relatives around me to rely on. The past is about to become a thing of the past. I am troubled by hard government affairs morning and night. Although I only hold a humble official position with hard work, it is not for my own selfish gain. I just hope to get a meager salary and let me return to my hometown.
Ten years later, I was ashamed to be appointed as the magistrate of Xiangyang County. No matter from the public or private aspects, I was not qualified for the job. However, I had to rely on the help of others and had to enter the official career with difficulty.
In the late years of Qi Yongming, when he was appointed as the prefect of Shuyang, he was already contented. However, in the early years of Qi Jianwu, the world was turbulent and unstable. Once he left his hometown, he was never allowed to return, making things extremely difficult and difficult.
At the end of the Qi Dynasty, when the emperor was in power, the state ordered many people to go out. Therefore, I planned to retire from the world. It was probably okay. At that time, I asked you to express your feelings to Xu Ling on your behalf. I think you have not forgotten it.
Nowadays, the king's way has risen and we are in a prosperous age. The ambitions and wishes of the past have become mistakes again.
Now is the beginning of the founding of the country, and the worship of gods will be repeated in the future. However, I asked to resign and go home, but the emperor was not allowed to do so. If it is really impossible to promote morality and promote the politics of the court, then I will have to look for books and books to discuss the similarities and differences in current affairs.
summary: Shen Yue advised Gaozu to ascend the throne, citing divine signs and public support. Gaozu agreed, and Shen Yue drafted the abdication decree. After the Liang Dynasty's establishment, Shen Yue became a regular servant of Sanqi, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Marquis of Changxian County. His mother was honored as Mrs. Jianchang. He later held positions such as Zuopushe and Shangshu Ling. Despite his high status, Shen Yue lived frugally and built a house in Dongtian, writing "Residence in the Suburbs" to express his feelings.

translation:
Sometimes it is easier to distinguish the colors of Sushan Danqing because we are in different forests. The sudden gust of wind makes the green mountains all over the mountain mixed with the beauty of purple.
The purple lotus blooming at night and the red lotus standing on the water in the morning are even more fragrant and refreshing when blown by the breeze.
The desolate sound of the wind echoed among the trees in the garden, and the cold moonlight shrouded the bamboo trees in the pool.
The osmanthus branches under the eaves are lush and the autumn chrysanthemums are blooming in front of the courtyard steps.
In winter, ice hangs on Kuangxue Mountain! White snow covers the green pine fields, and the land is vast.
The wild ducks are flying around and can't be driven away, and the wild geese are soaring high in the sky and want to come down to rest.
All the seasonal scenes are really nostalgic, but these foreign objects are so real.
This is the place where my nature rests, and it is also the reason why I admire it and cannot abandon it.
I lament that my temperament has become old, but I am sad and mourning for the country's many sufferings.
The sad thing is that although they are on different paths, they end up in the same place. Fortunately, they have lost all kinds of different directions.
Now I have returned to my love for flowers, birds, insects and fish, and now I am back to living in a simple hut.
There are no beauties from Wu land beside her, and there is no stupid Qin Se in front of her.
Therefore, I spend my remaining years here, spending my whole life here.
I am just worried that it will be difficult to repay the kindness of the gods of heaven and earth, and will not be recorded by the officials of the book; I will be valued by the court in vain, but my merits will not be recorded in the annals of history.
It's really sad, so why bother saying more? Besides, it's not just one thing that makes me feel guilty.
Soon he was granted the title of Special Advancement and was appointed Guanglu, Shizhong and Shaofu as before.
He died in office in the twelfth year of his reign at the age of seventy-three.
The emperor issued an edict as a gift to the official, and also gave 50,000 yuan in money and 100 pieces of cloth to finance the funeral ceremony. Mi was kept in hiding.
Shi Kong has two pupils in his left eye and a purple mole on his waist. He is extremely smart.
He likes reading and has a collection of 20,000 volumes of classics. No one in Kyoto can compare with him.
When he was young and poor, he once borrowed rice from his tribe to apply a hundred dendrobium trees. However, he was insulted by the tribe, so he poured the rice on the ground and turned around to leave.
Later, when he became a high official, he did not bear any grudge and still appointed this clansman as the county minister.
Once I was accompanying a banquet, there was a prostitute who was from the palace of Lord Qi Wenhui.

Xuan Diao held official positions in the Se, Man, and Chi dynasties. He was familiar with the laws and regulations of the past and had extensive knowledge. At that time, the court often had to listen to his opinions when formulating policies.
Xie Xuanhui is good at poetry, Ren Yansheng is good at writing, and Shen Yue is good at both, but neither can surpass them.
summary: Shen Yue died at age seventy-three in the twelfth year of Tianjian. He was given posthumous honors. He was extremely intelligent, with two pupils in his left eye and a purple mole on his waist. He owned 20,000 volumes of books. Despite past grievances, he appointed a clansman who had insulted him as a county minister. He was knowledgeable about laws and regulations and excelled in poetry and writing. However, he was arrogant and obsessed with fame, and after becoming prime minister, he failed to recommend talents. He died of fear after Gaozu condemned him for protecting his family. He wrote numerous works, including "Book of Jin," "Song Book," and "Four Tone Spectrum," though Gaozu disliked the latter.

However, Emperor Gaozu still did not follow and use Shen Yue's "Four Tone Scores". His sons, Shen Xuan and Shen Yue, had successively served as ministers of Zhongshu, prefect of Yongtai, Situ Zhonglang and Situ Youzhangshi.

At this time, Gao Dan mobilized the rebel army to save the country in times of crisis, determined to stabilize China, make contributions, strategize, and pin his hopes on people like Zhang Huang and Su Nu.
