translation:
Zongyang, named Mingzha, was a native of Nieyang County, Nanyang County, and had lived in Jiangling for generations.
His grandfather's name was Zong Bing, who was recruited by the Southern Song Dynasty as the crown prince and concubine. He did not accept the appointment and had a high reputation.
Zongyang's father, Zongfan, served as Xizhonglang to consult and join the army.
Zongyang was diligent in studying when he was young, and he was measured and talented.
At the age of twenty, he passed the Yingzhou scholar examination, served as a regular attendant of King Lin, and joined the army as a knight.
King Situ Jingling of the Southern Qi Dynasty gathered the scholars to the West Residence and painted portraits of them, including Zong Yang.
During the Yongming Dynasty, Southern Qi and Wei made peace. The emperor ordered Zong Yang and Ren Fang, the lieutenant of the Shangshu Palace, to receive the Wei envoys. They were all talents selected at that time.
Prince Nanjun, the direct grandson of Emperor Wu of Qi, lived in Xizhou. He asked Zong Yang to be in charge of the secretary. Zong Yang was already known by everyone for his good calligraphy and was praised for his loyalty and integrity, so he made this appointment.
Soon, Prince Wenhui passed away, and Prince Nanjun became the grandson of the emperor. Zongyang was still in charge of the secretary.
After the emperor's grandson ascended the throne and became emperor, Zongyang voluntarily distanced himself from him because of his many failings. He was appointed magistrate of Moling County and moved to Shangshu Duguanlang.
In the last years of Longchang, the Young Emperor was executed, and most of the old officials who had been favored in the past suffered disaster. Only Zong Yang and Fu Zhao were spared from disaster because of their integrity.
After Emperor Ming came to the throne, he appointed Zong Yang to govern Yingzhou. He was famous for his competent work. Later, he resigned and returned to his hometown because his father was old.
When the King of Nankang was the governor of Jingzhou, he regarded Zongyang as his best friend.
After Liang Gaozu rebelled against the division, Zong Yang moved to Xizhonglang to consult and join the army, but the post of Biejia remained.
At that time, in terms of status and reputation in the western countries, only Zong Yang and fellow countrymen Le Ai and Liu Tan were highly respected and trusted by the people of the state. Therefore, the leading general Xiao Yingzhou trusted and relied on him very much and consulted him on everything.
Gaozu's righteous army set out from Yongzhou, and Yingzhou sent Zongyang out from Yang to report the strategy in person and escort military supplies. Gaozu was very polite to him.
In the early years of the Zhongxing Dynasty, Zong Yang moved to the post of Censor Zhongcheng, but resigned due to the death of his father.
When the period of mourning expires, he will be promoted to the title of Champion General and Chief of the Guards.
In the first year of Tianjian, Zong Yang was moved to the post of Chief of the Zhengqi and Grand Administrator of Shuhai County, but his duties as general remained as before.
In the second year, he was called to serve as the crown prince's right guard.
In the winter of this year, Zong Yang moved to the post of Minister of the Fifth Army and participated in the general election of the officials in charge.
Three years later, Zong Yang died at the age of forty-nine.
His son Zong Yaoqing succeeded him.
Zongyang's cousin Zongyue had a good reputation and good behavior. People in the state praised him and said he was more famous than Zongyang.
He served as Shangshu Kubu Lang, governed Yingzhou, and Beizhong Lang recorded affairs and participated in the military.
summary: Zongyang, also known as Mingzha, was from Nieyang County, Nanyang, and had lived in Jiangling for generations. His grandfather Zong Bing was a renowned scholar who declined an official appointment. His father Zongfan served as Xizhonglang. Zongyang was diligent and talented, passing the Yingzhou scholar exam at twenty. He served as a regular attendant and knight for King Lin, and was among scholars painted in the West Residence by King Jingling of Southern Qi. During the Yongming era, he received Wei envoys with Ren Fang. He managed secretarial duties for Prince Nanjun, known for his calligraphy and integrity. After Prince Wenhui's death, he served the emperor's grandson but later distanced himself due to the ruler's failings, becoming magistrate of Moling and Shangshu Duguanlang. During the Longchang era, he survived disasters due to his integrity. Under Emperor Ming, he governed Yingzhou competently but resigned to care for his aging father. He later served Liang Gaozu, providing strategies and supplies, and held various posts including Censor Zhongcheng and Champion General. He died at forty-nine, succeeded by his son Zong Yaoqing. His cousin Zongyue was also renowned.

translation:
Liu Tan, courtesy name Dedu, was a native of Anzhong County, Nanyang County, and the seventh-generation grandson of General Liu Qiao of the Jin Dynasty.
Liu Tan was known to his cousin Liu Qiu when he was a boy.
In the early years of the Qi Dynasty in the Southern Dynasty, Liu Tan became the official servant of the Nanjun King. Soon after, he was appointed as the magistrate of Xiaoling County, and moved to Nanzhonglang to record affairs and join the army. He was famous for his ability in handling affairs in the palace positions he held.
When King Nankang was the governor of Jingzhou, Liu Tan appointed his Xizhong Langzhong soldiers to join the army and also served as Changliu.
After the rise of Emperor Gaozu's righteous army, Liu Tan moved to consult and join the army.
At that time, Yang Gongze, the general of the auxiliary state, was appointed as the governor of Xiangzhou. He led his troops to Xiakou and discussed with the people in charge of state affairs in the western countries. Xingtan said to them: The people in Yiye are easy to be harassed and hard to trust.
If warriors are sent there, the people will be afraid of being embezzled and plundered; if literati are sent there, the prestige will not be enough.
If it is necessary to stabilize this state and city so that the soldiers and civilians have enough food and clothing, then the best candidate is the veteran minister.
After the Battle of Xianwen, I secretly thought that I was still competent.
So the birth-bearer obeyed his words.
He was granted the title of Assistant to the Chief of History of the State and Governor of Changsha to manage nearby affairs.
Xing Dan used to work in the wing industry and had many old friends. Many of them came to welcome Liu Tan.
After Su Pi took office, he selected people who were qualified to do the work as officials and went to ten counties respectively to mobilize all the people. More than 300,000 hu of rice were transported to the rebel troops as military supplies.
At that time, Marquis Shuhun sent Liu Xizu, the governor of Ancheng County, to defeat Fan Sengjian, the governor selected by Xitai, in Pingdu. Liu Xizu issued a letter of war to Xiangzhou, so Wang Tanken, the king of Maggot Castle, responded.
The Wulu people expelled their internal historian Chu Rong, and the Yongyang people Zhou Hui raised troops to attack Shi'an Qi. They all came to respond to Wang Sengsai.
Gua fell into a trap, and Deng Daoli also participated in it in order to avenge himself.
Wang Sencan himself was known as the General of Pingxi and the Governor of Xiangzhou. He appointed Zhou Shu from Yongyang as the mastermind and raised an army in Naipo.
From then on, all the counties within the fishery territory swarmed into existence; only four counties, Zuobao, Laobi, Subi and Luo, were still intact.
The Lao people wanted to escape by boat, but Liu Tan gathered all the boats and set them on fire. He sent General Yin Falue to resist Wang Sencan, and the two armies were in a stalemate.
Zhong Baoti, the commander of Qianyi Town, secretly formulated a plan to respond to Wang Sencan. He invited hundreds of scholars and common people to formulate a plan and agreed on a date to rebel against the city.
Liu Tan heard about their plot, but pretended not to know. He deliberately handled the case until late at night, and the city gate was not closed because of this, deliberately confusing them.
Zhong Xuanshao had not launched a rebellion yet, so he went to Xingtananaguo the next day to ask why the city gate was not closed.
While Liu Dan stayed with him for a long talk, he secretly sent his trusted soldiers to Zhong Baoqi's home to search for letters.
summary: Liu Tan, courtesy name Dedu, was from Anzhong County, Nanyang, a descendant of General Liu Qiao. He served as official servant to the Nanjun King and magistrate of Xiaoling, known for his administrative skills. Under King Nankang, he joined the army and managed Changliu. During Liang Gaozu's uprising, he became a consultant. He advised sending a veteran to govern Xiangzhou, was appointed Assistant Chief Historian and Governor of Changsha, where he mobilized over 300,000 hu of rice for troops. He suppressed rebellions by Wang Sencan and others, using strategy to kill the traitor Zhong Baoti and pacifying the region. For his merits, he was made Lord of Yiqiu Shu and later served as Sima Pingxi and prefect of Xinxing. He died at sixty-two, succeeded by his son Liu Quan.

translation:
Le Ai returned to Zhoubao and repaired the palace and furnished hundreds of buildings. It was all completed quickly, and no common people were used as laborers.
The people of Jingzhou think that this is a mansion that has never existed since King Chen of Jin moved the state government here.
In the ninth year, Xiao Yi, the king of Yuzhang, passed away. Le Ai resigned from office and went to mourn. He led the old officials of Jing and Xiangzhou to erect a monument in front of the tomb of the king of Yuzhang.
Le Ai later served as a chariot and cavalry Pingxi Lushi, joined the army, and became an infantry captain. He asked for help in guarding the border and returned to the west.
When the King of Nankang was appointed Xizhonglang, he asked Le Ai to serve as a consultant to join the army.
After Liang Gaozu's uprising army rose, Lu Zhancheng led Bimai, Sai Qu, and Liu Tan to join the rebel army and appointed them as managers.
After the founding of the Liang Dynasty, Le Ai moved to the post of Sima of Zhenjun, Minister of Zhongshu, and Zuocheng of Shangshu.
At that time, Le Ai had to be consulted on all matters such as the construction of weapons and armor, ships' rations, and the court's etiquette and constitution.
Soon, Le Ai was transferred to serve as the Minister of Huangmen, while Zuo Cheng remained in his post.
On the way to the east with the emperor, Le Ai concurrently served as Wei Weiqing.
In the early years of Tianjian, Le Ai was moved to the post of General Xiaoqi and concurrently the Minister of the Shaofu. Soon he was moved to the post of Yushi Zhongcheng and concurrently served as the Dazhongzheng of the state.
At the beginning, Le Ai set out from Jiangling and got eight spokes on the ship for no reason. Just like Zhong Cheng walking to avoid the road, he was promoted today.
Le Ai has a fair and strong nature, and is very competent in his official position in Xantai.
At that time, King Xuanwu of Changsha was about to be buried, but the official of the Che Prefecture suddenly lost the silk rope net on the car and was about to hold the officer in charge responsible.
Le Ai said: When the weapons depot of the Jin Dynasty caught fire, Zhang Hua believed that it was inevitably caused by the accumulation of oil and thousands of stones.
Now if it is found that there is ashes wrapped in the warehouse, then it is not the fault of the official Che.
Later, after checking the garage, it was found that there was dust accumulation, so people praised Luan Ai for his broad knowledge and magnanimity.
In the second year, Sheng Yin served as Chijie, governor of the military affairs of Lu Cong, Xuan and Kunye, champion general, Pingyue Zhonglang general, and Guangzhou governor.
Tu Wuyu, the former governor of Luye, resigned from office and returned to his hometown. On the way, he encountered a rebellion by maggots, expelled the internal secretary Cui Mushu, and plundered Xu Yuanyu's property.
Tu Chengyu hurried back to Luye and borrowed troops from Diemai, pretending to attack the bandits, but in fact he wanted to attack Leai.
Le Ai noticed his intention and killed Xu Yuanyu.
Soon, Bi Jinmao was awarded the title of General Zhenglu. He died in office.
Bimai's sister is married to Liu Qiu, a fellow soldier from the same county. She is also a sensible, knowledgeable and polite person.
When Le Ai was a state official, he welcomed his sister to live in the official residence and gave her one-third of his official salary. The people in the west praised this very much.
Bimai's son was named Le Nazuo, with the courtesy name Genbei. When he was young, he and his younger brother Shuang Gai both had a good reputation.
When I was young, I studied in the capital and visited Xuan Mat. I admired Xuan Diao very much after meeting him.
When Emperor He of Qi was the prime minister, he called Luan Jizhang to join the army in the prime minister's mansion, and Xiao Yingzhou, the commander of the army, called him to be the chief secretary.
After the founding of the People's Republic of China, Luan Diezuo was awarded the title of Qibu Lang.
In the second year of Yue, Bimai went out to guard Yinghu. Wazuo stayed in Jingyi and moved to Jinbulang. He resigned because of his father's death.
summary: Bimai, courtesy name Lanwei, was a descendant of Bi Tong from Chenmo County, living in Jiangling. As a child, he impressed his uncle Zong Maggot by choosing books over other items. He served King Yi of Yuzhang as chief administrator and later joined the army. After his father's death, he resigned but was recalled. He impressed Xiao Yi with his knowledge of local geography and customs. He restored Jingzhou's official buildings after a rebellion, completing the work quickly without conscripting laborers. He served in various roles under Liang, including Minister of Huangmen and Yushi Zhongcheng. He was known for his fairness and knowledge, once correctly attributing a missing silk net to natural decay. He later became governor of Guangzhou, where he killed the rebellious Xu Yuanyu. He died in office. His sister, married to Liu Qiu, was praised for her virtue. His son Le Nazuo, courtesy name Genbei, was also renowned, serving in various posts including Qibu Lang and Taizhou Qing, known for his integrity and refusal of unearned salary. He died at sixty-three.

translation:
After the mourning period expired, he was awarded the title of Zhongshu Tongshi Shiren and served as the governor of the state.
Later, he was summoned as the Minister of Sanqi in Tongzhi, took charge of Tongshi again, and was moved to the position of Minister Youcheng.
When the King of Jin'an took office, he again granted Fa Cai the title of "Biejia" to engage in history.
Later, he was called to serve as Shangshu Youcheng and served as General Zhaoyi and Mi Ling.
The salary that Die Li did not accept amounted to nearly one hundred gold by the time he resigned. The county magistrate sent this money to the treasury.
Emperor Gaozu commended his father-in-law for his noble integrity and said: "If an official can do this, he can set an example for local officials."
That day Fa Cai was moved to the post of Taizhou Qing.
His mother was soon awarded the title of Internal History of Chen County, but he felt that it was a shame to become famous because of the salary concession, so he refused to accept the appointment.
Soon after he was elected, he was promoted to General Yunqi and Minister of Shaofu.
He also served as the chief historian of Xinwu and the prefect of Jiangxia County.
Since I was replaced, I asked for a way home.
After arriving home, he immediately designated a part of the house as a temple, aloof from the outside world.
Because the crown prince thought that Dieli was an old minister, he repeatedly issued preferential treatment orders and called him to the east to serve as an official. Facai died before he set out at the age of sixty-three.
Yao Cha, the Minister of Chen's Ministry of Civil Affairs in the Southern Dynasty, said: Xiao Yingzhou mobilized the people of the whole state to join the uprising team, but the people at that time could not understand it.
These three people are the deterrent force of Chu Di.
They are all powerful people in the management and establishment of Liang Chaoshang.
In a certain aspect of military and political affairs, Liu Tan had more credit; in terms of official duties, Le Ai was better.
In the end, they all ascended to favored official positions. This is as it should be!
summary: Yao Cha commented that these three men were key figures in Chu, contributing to Liang's establishment: Liu Tan in military affairs, Le Ai in official duties, both achieving high positions as expected.

translation:
Liu Xun, courtesy name Wentong, was born in Jie County, Hedong. His father Shilong was Sikong in the Qi Dynasty.
When Liu Xun was seventeen years old, Emperor Wu of Qi was still a member of the Central Army, so he was appointed to join the army and transferred to the position of chief registrar.
In the early years of the Qi Dynasty, he was appointed Sangonglang of Shangshu, moved to Prince Zhongsheren, and became a friend of Prince Xiang of Badong.
When Zixiang was in charge of Jingzhou, Liu Xun followed him there.
Zi Xiang likes to get close to villains, but Liu Xun knew that this would be a disaster, so he returned to Beijing claiming to be ill.
When the disaster struck, Liu Xun was spared because he returned to Beijing first.
He successively served as the Minister of Zhongshu and the Commander of the Zhonghu Army.
He served as the prefect of Xin'an and lived in the county. He was dismissed and returned home on the grounds that he had no political achievements.
After a period of time, Ren Weijun proposed to join the military.
In the last years of Jianwu, he served as the captain of Xirong and the governor of Liang, Nan and Qin states.
When Emperor Gaozu raised his troops to rebel, Liu Xun led the Hanzhong troops to respond.
Emperor He ascended the throne and appointed him as a servant and a general in charge of the front army.
When Emperor Gaozu was the emperor, he was appointed as a general to protect the army. Before he was appointed, he was still moved to the position of Prince Zhan Shi.
Emperor Gaozu composed a poem and presented it to Liu Xun at the banquet. The poem goes: After you are crowned among the others at the banquet, I am the only one who really thinks about meritorious deeds.
I once chatted with Gaozu again, and Gaozu said: Xu Yuanyu disobeyed orders in Cennan, and the "Book of Zhou" is not related to the crime. I have pardoned his disciples, how about it?
Liu Xun replied: "The punishment will not be imposed on his descendants, and the rewards will be extended to future generations. Today I see the Holy Dynasty again."
At that time people called it wisdom.
Soon he was transferred to the right servant of Shangshu.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, a large-scale Northern Expedition was launched. Liang Hong, the king of Linchuan, supervised the army, with Liu Xun as his deputy.
After the army returned, they still served as servants.
Due to a long illness, he was transferred to the post of Dr. Jin Ziguanglu, with additional Sanqi regular attendants and twenty close followers.
Before becoming an official, he served as envoy Chijie, General Annan, and governor of Xiangzhou.
He died in office in October of the sixth year at the age of forty-six.
Emperor Gaozu wore plain clothes and expressed his condolences.
He was given as a gift to Shizhong and the general of the Fu army, and was given a piece of propaganda, with the posthumous title Mu.
Liu Xun is the author of "The Biography of Renzheng" and many poems and poems, which are rough and meaningful.
His son Liu Zhao succeeded him.
Liu Xun's fourth younger brother, Liu Xin, also had a good reputation and served successively as Shizhong and Zhenxi Chief.
He died in the twelfth year of Tianjian and was given to General Ningyuan and the governor of Yuzhou.
Liu Chen, also known as Wenruo, is Liu Xun's fifth younger brother.
When he was only a few years old, his father Liu Shilong and his mother Yan were often bedridden, and Liu Chen went to bed without undressing for several years.
During the period of mourning and filial piety, people are known for being excessively sad.
When he started his career, he served as Situ Xing and joined the army. He was later moved to the position of Prince Zhongsheren.
Qi Donghunhou sent Liu Shanyang, the governor of Brazil, to attack Emperor Gaozu from Jingzhou. Shi Xiao Yingzhou, the chief of the Xizhong army, could not think of any good strategies. At night, he called Liu Chen and his confidant Xi Shanwen to discuss countermeasures.
Liu Chen said: The current emperor is fatuous and rebellious, doing more and more evil every day.
summary: Liu Xun, courtesy name Wentong, was born in Hedong. He began his official career at seventeen under Emperor Wu of Qi, serving in various posts including Sangonglang and Prince Zhongsheren. He befriended Prince Xiang of Badong but foresaw disaster due to the prince’s association with villains, returning to the capital feigning illness. He later served as Minister of Zhongshu, Commander of the Zhonghu Army, and Prefect of Xin'an, though he was dismissed for lack of political achievements. During the Jianwu era, he became captain of Xirong and governor of Liang, Nan, and Qin states. When Emperor Gaozu rebelled, Liu Xun responded with Hanzhong troops. Under Emperor He, he served as a servant and general, and later as Prince Zhan Shi under Emperor Gaozu. Gaozu praised him in a poem and consulted him on pardoning Xu Yuanyu’s disciples, to which Liu Xun wisely replied, earning acclaim. He died in office in October of the sixth year at age forty-six, posthumously honored as Shizhong and General of the Fu Army, with the title Mu. He authored "The Biography of Renzheng" and various poems. Liu Chen, courtesy name Wenruo, was Liu Xun’s fifth younger brother. Known for filial piety, he cared for his ill parents without undressing for years. He served as Situ Xing and Prince Zhongsheren. During Qi Donghunhou’s reign, he advised Xiao Yingzhou against attacking Emperor Gaozu, warning of mutual destruction and citing past examples. His counsel led Yingzhou to ally with Gaozu. Liu Chen later held posts such as Shangshu Libu Lang, General of the Assistant State, and Prefect of Nanping. He opposed moving the capital to Xia, arguing it would destabilize the people, and was proven correct when Ba Shu attacked. Under Emperor Gaozu, he became Minister of the Five Arms and was enfeoffed as Prefecture Lingbo. He died at home at age forty-one, posthumously honored as Zhongshu Ling with the title Mu.

translation:
Emperor Gaozu raised an army to resist Marquis Shuhun, and Shanwen tried his best to persuade him. Xiao Yingzhou agreed to respond to Emperor Gaozu and join the rebellion. He also sent Tian Zugong to report to Emperor Gaozu secretly, and contributed a silver sword. Emperor Gaozu gave him gold Ruyi in return.
Emperor Qi He ascended the throne and appointed him as the minister of Huangmen, and soon moved to Weiqing.
Yingzhou died suddenly, and the state government was in turmoil. Shanwen thought that Emperor He was young and the tasks in the middle reaches of the Yangtze River were arduous. At that time, Xiao Qi, the king of Shixing, was staying in Yongzhou, so he and the civil and military officials from Jiangling in the Western Dynasty welcomed Xiao Qi to take charge of the affairs of Jingzhou Mansion, so the people were able to stabilize.
Emperor Gaozu accepted Zen and ascended the throne, and Shanwen was appointed as the official minister of the capital and the general of the auxiliary country.
He was granted the title of Shanyang Bo and was granted the title of Shanyang Bo, with a settlement of 700 households.
He was appointed as the prefect of Shuyang, and was granted a new title in Xiangxi, but his residence remained the same.
He served as an official for two years and was known for his innocence. He died while serving as an official.
Emperor Gaozu issued an edict to donate 30,000 yuan and 50 pieces of cloth to help with funeral arrangements.
Mi's name is power.
Wei Rui, courtesy name Huaiwen, was born in Duling, Jingzhao.
Since becoming prime minister, he has assisted the three surnames. Grandfather Wei Xuan did not want to be an official and lived in seclusion in Nanshan, Chang'an.
When Emperor Wu of the Song Dynasty was on the throne, he once offered a conquest for the Taiwei, but was rejected.
Uncle Wei Zuzheng was Guang Luxun in the late Song Dynasty.
His father, Wei Zugui, became the chief historian of Ningyuan.
Wei Rui was very filial to his stepmother, so he was praised by the villagers.
The elder brothers Wei Rui and Wei Chan were famous earlier.
Wei Zuan and Wei Rui were very studious, and Wei Cao was pure.
Wei Zuzheng was the county governor and often took Wei Rui to handle official business, treating him as his son.
At that time, Wei Rui's wife, brother-in-law, Wang Cheng, and aunt-in-law, Du Yun, were both well-known in the countryside.
Wei Zuzheng said to Wei Rui: Compared with Cheng and Yun, what do you think?
Wei Rui was too humble to answer.
Zu Zheng said: Your articles may be inferior to theirs, but your knowledge should surpass them, and in terms of participating in national affairs and making contributions to the country, they are not as good as you.
My cousin Du Youwen was the governor of Liangzhou and asked Wei Rui to go with him.
Liangzhou was very prosperous at that time, and most of the people who served as officials there were dismissed for being greedy for money. Although Wei Rui was very young, he was known for his integrity.
In the early years of Song Yongguang, Yuan Yun was appointed as the governor of Yongzhou. When he saw Wei Rui, he felt that he was extraordinary and took him as the chief official.
After Yuan Zhuan arrived in Yongzhou, he and Deng Wan rebelled against the imperial court. Wei Rui requested in advance to serve in Yicheng County, thus avoiding Yuan Yun's disaster.
Later, he served as the Zuo Changshi of King Ping of Jin Dynasty, moved to Sikong Guiyang to join the army, and followed Qi Sikong Liu Shilong to defend Yingcheng and resist the attack of Shen Youzhi, the governor of Jingzhou.
After the Youzhi rebellion was put down, he moved to the former army to join the army.
Much later, he was appointed magistrate of Guangde County.
He moved to Qixing prefect, Benzhou Biejia, Changshui captain, and general of the right army.
In the last years of the Qi Dynasty, the situation was in turmoil. Wei Rui did not want to stay away from his hometown, so he asked to be appointed as Shangyong Prefect and become a general in Wei.
summary: Xi Chanwen, from Anding, lost his parents young and loved reading. He befriended Xiao Yingzhou and served as a doctor in Xizhong. He persuaded Yingzhou to support Gaozu’s rebellion, secretly sending a silver sword and receiving a gold Ruyi in return. Under Emperor He, he became minister of Huangmen and later Weiqing. After Yingzhou’s sudden death, he stabilized the region by welcoming Xiao Qi to govern Jingzhou. Under Emperor Gaozu, he served as official minister and was enfeoffed as Shanyang Bo. He died in office after two years as prefect of Shuyang, known for his integrity.

translation:
Soon the Taiwei Chen Haoda and the guard general Cui Huijing rebelled against the imperial court and frequently invaded Jiankang, the capital. Everyone was frightened and at a loss.
People from Shu asked Wei San about the current situation, and Wei Shu said: Although Chen Xianda is a veteran, he is not a talented person in governing the world; Cui Huijing knows some things, but is cowardly and lacks courage. They should end up with a reduced clan.
The people who will bring peace to the world will probably come from our state.
So, he sent his two sons to take the initiative to make friends with Gaozu.
When Emperor Gaozu's call for an army came out, Wei San led his county soldiers to cut down bamboos and make bamboo rafts. They traveled day and night to join in, bringing a total of more than 2,000 people and 200 horses.
Emperor Gaozu was very happy to see Wei San who had come to seek refuge. He took pictures of a few cases and said, "I saw you before, but today I see your sincerity. My great mission will definitely succeed."
The rebel army conquered Ying and Lu and pacified Jiahu. Wei Guan proposed many strategies, all of which were adopted by Gaozu.
The Eastern Expedition army was about to set off from Yingcheng. When discussing the candidates for the generals who would stay in Yingcheng, Gaozu found it difficult to determine. After a long time, he turned back to Wei San and said: Give up a good horse without riding it. Where to look for it in such a hurry?
On that day, he was appointed as the champion general and the prefect of Jiangxia to handle the affairs of Ying Prefecture. When Ying City was defended, there were nearly 100,000 scholars, men and women, and the city gates were closed for nearly a year. The plague was prevalent in the city, and seven or eight out of ten people contracted the disease and died. The corpses were piled under the bed, and the living people slept on the bed. Every house was filled with corpses.
Wei Fu personally counted and inspected and comforted those who were still alive. They all cook for him so that the dead can be buried and the living can return to their hometowns to live and work in peace and contentment, so the people all depend on him.
After the establishment of the Liang Dynasty, Wei Fan was conquered as Dali.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he moved to the rank of Tingwei and was enfeoffed as the capital of Liangzi, with a settlement of 300 households.
In the second year of Tianjian, the title was changed to Yongchang, and the city was as before.
The prince is established. He moved to the right guard of the crown prince and became the general of the auxiliary state, the governor of Yuzhou, and the governor of Liyang.
Three years later, the Northern Wei army invaded the border area, and Wei San led the state troops to repel the enemy troops.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, the king's army made a northern expedition and ordered Wei San to lead the army.
Wei Jiang sent Chief Shi Wangchaozong and Liangjun Governor Feng Daogen to attack Xiaoxian City in the Northern Wei Dynasty, but failed to capture it.
When Wei San was patrolling the position, hundreds of enemy soldiers suddenly rushed out of Wei City and set up a formation outside the city gate. Wei He wanted to attack them. All the generals said: "We came here lightly armed and were not well prepared for battle. We should go back and give the soldiers armor first, and then we can attack."
Wei San said: No.
There are more than 2,000 enemy defenders in Wei City. If they defend behind closed doors, they can protect themselves. Now they rush out of the city for no reason. They must be their elite warriors. If they can be defeated, the enemy city will be defeated without attacking.
summary: Wei Rui, courtesy name Huaiwen, was born in Duling. He was filial to his stepmother and praised for his integrity. He served under various officials, avoiding disaster by requesting a post in Yicheng County during Yuan Yun’s rebellion. During the Qi Dynasty turmoil, he predicted the failure of rebels Chen Haoda and Cui Huijing, and allied with Gaozu, bringing 2,000 men and 200 horses. Gaozu appointed him champion general and prefect of Jiangxia. During a plague in Ying City, he personally comforted survivors and ensured proper burials. After the Liang Dynasty’s establishment, he became Dali and later Tingwei. He repelled Northern Wei invasions and led successful campaigns, including the capture of Xiaoxian City and Hefei, using strategic weirs and naval attacks. At Shaoyang, he defeated a massive Wei army, causing over 100,000 casualties. He was promoted to Marquis and served in various high offices. Known for humility, he treated old friends kindly and avoided boasting. He died at seventy-nine, posthumously honored as Shizhong and Chariot and Cavalry General, with the title Yan. His sons included Wei Fang, Wei Zheng, Wei Ling, and Wei An.

translation:
At that time, Hou Jing built two earth mountains on the east and west outside the city, and two earth mountains were built inside the city to compete with them. Taizong personally carried the earth, and all the officials from Prince Ai on down personally picked up dustpans, shovels, and shovels to participate in building the earth.
Wei An was responsible for defending Tushan in the west of the city. He fought hard day and night. For his merits in resisting the enemy, he was awarded the title of "General of Light Chariots" and "Blessing Festival".
When he died in the city, he was given posthumously as a regular attendant of Sanqi and a general of left guard.
Wei Ai, younger brother of Wei San clan.
Wei Ai, whose nickname is Xiaoyou, is calm and thoughtful.
His great-great-grandfather Wei Guang was a general in the rear army of the Jin Dynasty and the prefect of Beiping.
Great-grandfather Wei Gui moved south to Xiangyang in the early Taiyuan years of Emperor Guiwu's reign in the east, where he served as the minister of the local cavalry and scattered cavalry.
His grandfather, Wei Gongxun, served as the prefect of Yiyang in Song Dynasty.
His father, Wei Yizheng, passed away at an early age.
Wei Ai lost his father when he was young. He served his mother very filially and became famous for this.
Wei Aiqing was an upright and upright man who did not want to socialize and was dedicated to learning. He always sat alone in a shabby room, studying ancient books. The tables and chairs in the room were covered with dust and it was as quiet as if there was no one there.
When I was twelve years old, I visited the capital and happened to catch up with the emperor's trip to Nanyuan. The streets and alleys were bustling with people, old and young, vying to see him. Only Wei Ai was still sitting upright reading without letting go of the book. The tribesmen were surprised to see him like this.
When he grew up, he was erudite and talented in literature, especially proficient in the principles of Zhouyi and Chunqiu Zuoshi.
When Yuan Zhuan was the governor of Yongzhou, he recruited him to be the chief register.
When his mother passed away, he built a hut next to the tomb to live in and carried the soil to build the tomb himself.
Emperor Gaozu went to Yongzhou and after hearing about this incident, he went to express his condolences in person.
After three years of mourning, he was drafted into the army.
When Emperor Gaozu's rebel army just started, he appointed Wei Ai as a strong general, champion Nanping Wang Sima, and led Xiangyang County Magistrate.
At that time, the capital had not yet been pacified, and Yongzhou's military equipment was empty. Yan Sengdu, the prefect of Wei Xing, and others occupied the prefectures and counties to resist the rebels. The people in the state were panicked and had two minds.
Wei Ai was calm, alert and strategic. He had always been convinced by the army and the people of the state. He confided in his heart to appease the people and analyzed the changes in the situation between the enemy and ourselves. He also recruited warriors from the countryside and got more than a thousand people. He launched a fierce battle with the rebels such as Sengdu and others in the southern part of Shiping County. He defeated the enemy and the people were able to settle down.
After Xiao Yingzhou's death, Emperor Qi He recruited soldiers in Xiangyang, and Wei Ai followed Xiao Dan, the king of Shixing, to apply for the army.
Before the war, Xiao Suo, the governor of Badong, and Lu Xiulie, the governor of Brazil, invaded Jingzhou. After Xiao Qi arrived, he ordered Wei Ai to write a letter to Xiao Suo, and Xiao Suo immediately asked for surrender.
summary: Wei Ai, courtesy name Xiaoyou, was calm and thoughtful. He lost his father young, served his mother filially, and was dedicated to learning, often studying alone in a dusty room. He was erudite in Zhouyi and Chunqiu Zuoshi. During Gaozu’s rebellion, he pacified local rebels and later followed Xiao Qi to Jingzhou. He died of illness en route to attack Liu Jilian, leaving a legacy of integrity.

translation:
Xie Bei, courtesy name Jingchong, was born in Yangxia, Chen County.
His grandfather Hongwei was Taichang Qing in the Song Dynasty, and his father was Xie Zhuang, a doctor named Youguanglu. Both of them were famous in previous generations.
Xie Sui was smart and smart when he was a child. Xie Zhuang valued him very much and often took him with him.
He could write articles at the age of ten.
Xie Zhuang was playing in Tushan and composing poems. He asked Xie Li to write a poem. Xie Bei picked up his pen and wrote it.
Wang Jingwen of Langye said to Xiezhuang: Your son is enough to be called a child prodigy, and he will become a particularly promising person among future generations.
Xie Zhuang smiled, patted Xie Li's back and said, "You are really the treasure of our family."
Emperor Xiaowu was visiting Gushu, and ordered Xie Zhuang to take Xie Kui to follow the driver. He also ordered Xie Chu to compose "Praise to the Dongjing" and played the "Praise to the Dongjing" while he was sitting.
Emperor Xiaowu said: Although he is young, he is a child prodigy.
Xie Li initially served as Fujun Fa Cao Xing and joined the army. He was promoted to Prince Sheren but resigned due to his father's death.
After serving the funeral, he became a layman again, and successively served as Zhongshulang and General Yuan Can of the Wei.
Yuan Can was simple and strict by nature and rarely interacted with guests. People at the time compared him to Li Ying.
When Xie Li saw that he had retired, Yuan Can said, "This is Xie Ling's immortality."
Soon he was transferred to serve as the minister of Huangmen.
He served as the internal history of Linchuan and was impeached for bribery. The case passed through Yuan Can, who shelved the matter.
Emperor Qi Gao served as a hussar general to assist the government, elected Xie Bei to be the chief historian, and ordered him to enter the court to serve the Song emperor together with Chu Xuan of Henan, Jiang Jiao of Jiyang, and Liu Yu of Pengcheng. They were known as the four friends of the emperor at that time.
Then he was appointed as Shizhong, and was in charge of the Shaoguan documents of Zhongshu and Sanqi provinces.
Emperor Gao was promoted to the rank of Taiwei, and appointed Xie Zhu as the chief official and concurrently as the Grand Administrator of Nanshutu.
The childbirth was about to plot to succeed the emperor. The ministers who were considering assisting him in starting a business thought that Xie Bei had great reputation and respected him deeply.
Discussing the story of Wei and Zhi with Xie Nao, he said: The changes in destiny and destiny of Zhi Dai reform have been foreshadowed for a long time. Hu Bao did not encourage Emperor Wen of Jin to ascend the throne earlier, and only cried for him after his death. Compared with Feng Yi, he did not know the timing.
Xie Chu replied: It turns out that there were ministers in the Wei State who encouraged Emperor Wu of Wei to ascend the throne. Emperor Wu of Wei said to them: If destiny is useful to me, I should probably become King Wen of Zhou!
Emperor Wen of Jin served the Wei family all his life, and he would definitely be a minister to the north for the rest of his life. If Wei had followed the story of Tang Yu's surrender earlier, then Emperor Wen of Jin should have resigned many times to show his noble character.
Emperor Gao was very unhappy after hearing what he said.
Then he recommended Wang Jian to be the chief historian of Zuo, and asked Xie Zhu to write poems and serve as secretary and supervisor.
When Qi arrived, he accepted the abdication. Xie Zhu was on duty that day, and all the officials were sitting with him. The waiter was supposed to take off the jade seal. Xie Li pretended not to understand and asked: "What's the official business?"
The person who passed it on to Shao said: Take off the jade seal and give it to the King of Qi.
Xie Chu said: Qi himself should have an attendant.
summary: Xie Bei, courtesy name Jingchong, was a native of Yangxia, Chen County, born into a distinguished family with his grandfather and father both holding high offices in the Song Dynasty. A child prodigy, he could write essays at age ten and was highly praised by his father Xie Zhuang and Wang Jingwen of Langye. Emperor Xiaowu also recognized his talent. Xie Bei began his official career as Fujun Fa Cao Xing and joined the army, later becoming Prince Sheren but resigning due to his father's death. After mourning, he held various positions including Zhongshulang and Huangmen侍郎. He served as internal history of Linchuan but was impeached for bribery, though the case was shelved by Yuan Can.

translation:
Just pull up the pillow and sleep.
Fu Zhao's people were afraid, so they asked him to claim that he was ill and wanted to find someone else to take his place.
Xie Bei said: I am not sick, what are you talking about?
He put on his court clothes, walked out of Dongye Gate, got in his car, and returned to his residence.
One day later, Wang Jian was appointed as the servant to untie the jade seal.
Soon Emperor Wu asked Emperor Gao to kill Xie Bei.
Emperor Gao said: "Killing him will bring success to his reputation. He should be tolerated and excluded from the law."
So he was dismissed from office and stayed at home.
In the first year of Yongming Dynasty, Xie Chu was summoned from his home to be appointed as a regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi. He was successively transferred to the position of servant and received the doctor of Guozi.
In the fifth year, he was appointed as the champion general and the prefect of Yixing, and received an additional salary of two thousand dan.
When he was in office in the county, he did not check the chores and handed over everything to the rules and regulations. He said: "I can't be a low-level official like the master, I can only be a prefect."
After working for three years, he was appointed as the Du Guan Shangshu and Zhongshu Ling.
In the first year of Longchang, he wrote a poem and accepted the post of master of King Xin'an. Xie Zhu did not accept the offer and insisted on applying for a job abroad.
So he became the general who conquered the captives and the governor of Wuxing. He took up his post after being summoned.
When Emperor Ming was sent to seek his succession to the throne, all the old ministers of the imperial court were summoned to discuss strategies.
Xie Li thought about stopping in his heart, but in fact it was to avoid trouble.
His younger brother Xie Man was the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel at that time.
When Xie Li came to the county, he gave Xie a lot of dendrobium wine and left a note saying: You can drink as much as you can, but don't get involved in personnel disputes.
When Xie Bei was in office in the county, he often ignored official affairs but devoted himself to amassing wealth. People ridiculed him, but he ignored him.
In the fourth year of Jianwu's reign, Xia Shao summoned Xie Bei to serve as Shizhong and Zhongshuling. He submitted a memorial to the emperor and refused to accept Shao's request.
He sent his disciples back to the capital, but he and his mother stayed behind and built a house in the west city of the county.
Emperor Ming issued an edict: On top of transcendent honors, outstanding figures will naturally go away; following the footsteps of the hermit, outstanding brilliance is of rare value.
Therefore, I bow my hands and bow to the Prime Minister of Chu who is praised in the south; I express my gratitude to Mo Chen for choosing a good historian.
The newly appointed Shizhong and Zhongshu Ling Xie Qian had been relied on by the imperial court in the early years. He always showed his innocence and noble character. He came to the imperial court to establish political achievements and became a guard official with great reputation.
Then he stopped his footsteps and walked towards the broad and accessible road of the fields. He turned around and retreated to the mountains, forests and rivers, embracing the lingering fragrance of Jishan and Yingshui. He was willing to be haggard and not to be distressed.
Reminiscing about the past, remembering the old people, and retaining admiring thoughts.
He should be given preferential treatment and courtesy to commend his innocence.
You can give him a bed, tents and mats, give him your salary, and send him to his place for a long time.
He Yin, who sent the emperor to offer wine to Lujiang, also wrote a memorial to the emperor and returned to Huishan.
In the second year of Yongyuan, Xia Shao recruited Xie Chu to be the regular attendant of Sanqi and the supervisor of Zhongshu, and He Yin to be the regular attendant of Sanqi and Taichang Qing. Neither of them gave in.
In the third year, he went to Shao and recruited Xie Li as the servant and the prince's young master, and Yulegs as the regular servant of the Sanqi and the prince Zhanshi.
At this time, Seju Fort came down to where they were, and sent people to force them to be sent. When the rebel army was approaching, neither of them could get it.
When Zhizu pacified the capital and entered the Xiangguo Kingdom, he asked for the appointment of Xie Bei and He Yin, saying: If you don't have the ambition, you should focus on yourself; if you have the ambition, you should help the world.
Although they have different considerations regarding the reasons for becoming an official and retiring, the appointment by the court should only be based on the needs of the times, and only those with outstanding talents and virtues should be appointed.
Xie Zhuo, the Prince's Young Master, and the Sanqi Changshi, Prince Zhan Shi, and Dutinghou Tanhuang were just appointed by the previous dynasty. They were auxiliaries of the imperial court and descendants of aristocratic families. They had good conduct and were born in official positions. They had the ability to succeed in politics and moral reputation, and could appease the world and save the world.
Although he was in the imperial court in the past, he never had any intention of becoming an official. He rarely interacted with guests and rarely participated in the affairs of ministers. Although he did not take off his hairpin and tassel, he was able to get rid of the secular customs.
summary: During Qi Emperor Gao's reign, Xie Bei was among the "four friends" of the emperor, serving as chief historian and later Shizhong. When Emperor Gao sought to usurp the throne, Xie Bei expressed reluctance, citing historical precedents, which displeased the emperor. He was eventually dismissed and stayed at home. In the Yongming era, he was recalled to serve as Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi and later as champion general and prefect of Yixing, where he neglected official duties but amassed wealth. He refused several appointments, including Shizhong and Zhongshuling, preferring to avoid political turmoil. Under Emperor Ming, Xie Bei was summoned but declined, building a house in the county. He was later forced to serve under Emperor Gaozu, accepting positions like Shizhong and Situ, though he often feigned illness. He died at sixty-six, receiving posthumous honors. His son Xie Mo was dismissed for killing cattle, and his nephew Xie Lan, known for his literary talent and demeanor, served in various roles, including prefect of Wuxing, where he suppressed bandits and corruption. Xie Lan died in office at thirty-seven. Yao Cha commented that Xie Bei was loyal to the Song Dynasty, while Xie Lan excelled in governance.

translation:
Zhang Huishao, courtesy name Deji, was from Yiyang.
He had military talent in his youth.
During the reign of Emperor Qi Ming of the Southern Dynasty, he was appointed as Zhihe, and later he was appointed as the garrison commander of Jingling Hengsang.
In the early years of Yongyuan, his mother passed away and he returned to his hometown for burial.
When he heard about the rise of Liang Gaozu's righteous army, he hurried to join Gaozu. He was appointed as a soldier in the army and joined the army as general Ningshuo and military leader.
The righteous army was temporarily stationed in Han Dynasty, and Emperor Gaozu sent Zhu Siyuan, the leader of the Hui Shao Yu army, to patrol the Yangtze River to block the grain transportation channel between Ying and Lu cities.
Shen Nandang, the navy chief of Yingcheng, led ten light warships to challenge Hui Shao, but was defeated by Hui Shao. Shen Nandang was beheaded and all his weapons were seized.
The righteous army stopped at Xinlin and Zhuque, and Hui Shao made many military exploits.
After Jiankang City was captured by the righteous army, Hui Shao moved to serve as the general of the auxiliary state and the front army, the commander of Zhihe and Zuoxi.
After Liang Gaozu ascended the throne, he granted Huishao the title of Marquis of Shiyang County, with a settlement of 500 households.
Hui Shao was again promoted to General of Xiaoqi, and the masters of Zhihe and Xizhan remained the same.
At that time, the remnant party of Donghun Hou, consisting of hundreds of people, secretly sneaked into Nanyemen and Beiyemen, set fire to Shenhumen, and killed the guard Zhang Hongce.
Hui Shao led his men to rush to fight and beheaded them to the tenth level. Only then did the rest of the party escape.
Due to his meritorious service, Hui Shao increased his residence by 200 households, and was moved to the position of the crown prince's right guard.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, Liang Jun launched a large-scale Northern Expedition. Hui Shaoyu champion Hu Xinsheng and Ningshuo general Zhang Baozi attacked Suyu, captured the city lord Ma Chenglong, and escorted him to the capital.
He asked his general Lan Huaigong to build a city on the south bank of the river, forming a cornering force.
Soon, reinforcements from the Wei army arrived in large numbers, defeated Lan Huaigong and captured the city built by Huaigong. Hui Shao could not defend the city of Yu, so he fled back to Huaiyin that night, and the Wei army regained the city.
In the sixth year of Tianjian, the Wei army attacked Zhongli. Emperor Wu of Liang ordered the left guard general Cao Jingzong to supervise the various armies as backup and marched to occupy Shaoyang. Hui Shao, Feng Daogen, Pei Sui and others attacked the Wei army's connecting bridge. The two armies fought in close combat, and the Wei army was defeated.
Hui Shao also added 300 households to the city due to his meritorious service. After returning, he served as General Zuo Xiaoqi.
Soon after, he served as Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Northern Yanzhou, Champion General, and Governor of Northern Yanzhou.
The two cities of Suyu and Huaiyang of the Wei State were surrendered to the Liang Dynasty. Hui Shao was promoted to the title of General Zhiwu due to his meritorious service in recruiting and appeasing them, and was granted an additional 200 households.
Later he was recalled to serve as Wei Qing and moved to Zuowei General.
He also served as Chijie, governor of all military affairs in Sizhou, general Xinwei, governor of Sizhou, and concurrently as prefect of Anlu.
Huishao managed the state well during his term, and the officials and the people loved him very much.
Sai Niu was recalled to the capital to serve as the general of the left guard. He was appointed as a regular attendant on the cavalry and led an armored honor guard of 100 people to guard the palace.
In the eighteenth year of Tianjian, Ji Saichao passed away at the age of sixty-three.
The emperor's Shao Shu wrote: Zhang Huishao's ambition and talent can be used to start a business and save time, and he can stick to the right path and complete it satisfactorily.
He is a sincere and diligent person who abides by principles and has achieved outstanding results in all his official positions.
When he was serving as a guard in the palace, he devoted himself to guarding him day and night.
summary: Zhang Huishao, courtesy name Deji, was from Yiyang. During the reign of Emperor Qi Ming of the Southern Dynasty, he served as Zhihe and garrison commander of Jingling Hengsang. After his mother's death in the early Yongyuan period, he returned home for burial. Upon hearing of Liang Gaozu's righteous army, he joined as a soldier and was appointed General Ningshuo. He defeated Shen Nandang's navy, seized weapons, and made many military exploits at Xinlin and Zhuque. After Jiankang was captured, he became General of the Auxiliary State and was later granted the title of Marquis of Shiyang County with 500 households. When remnants of Donghun Hou's forces attacked the palace gates, Huishao led his men to defeat them, killing many. He was promoted to Crown Prince's Right Guard and increased his residence by 200 households. In the fourth year of Tianjian, he attacked Suyu and captured the city lord Ma Chenglong. However, after Wei reinforcements arrived and defeated his general Lan Huaigong, Huishao fled to Huaiyin. In the sixth year, he fought at Zhongli under Cao Jingzong, contributing to the defeat of the Wei army. He later served as Governor of Northern Yanzhou, where he managed affairs well and was beloved by officials and people. He died at age sixty-three in the eighteenth year of Tianjian, receiving posthumous honors.

translation:
When Cai Daofu died in the army during the Han Dynasty, Chanpai ordered Tongdao Dan to command all the troops of Ji Daohuan.
The rebel army was stationed in Qianta. When they met Daolong and Wang Lu, they fought in Saique and killed many enemies.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he appointed Feng Daodan as General Xiaoqi. He was also granted the title of Male of Zengcheng County and was given the title of a resident of 200 households.
He also led Said Commander and was promoted to guerrilla general.
In this year, Chen Bozhi, the governor of Jiangzhou, rebelled. When he met Daodan and Wang Peng, he attacked him quickly and put down the rebellion.
In the second year of Yujian, Feng Daogen was appointed as General Ningshuo, Grand Administrator of Muliang County, and concurrently as her garrison commander in the imperial palace.
As soon as Yaodaozou arrived in Huanglu, he built a moat and placed sentries at a distance, as if the enemy was about to come. Everyone laughed at him.
Feng Daogen said: Be careful and defensive. Fight bravely, this is what I mean.
The trenches had not yet been built, and General Yu Shifu led 20,000 troops to attack the city. At this time, the trench fortress of Fuling City built by Daogen was not strong enough, and there were few soldiers in the city. Everyone was panicked.
Feng Daogen ordered the city gate to be opened wide. He calmly put on his battle uniform and climbed to the top of the city. He selected 200 elite soldiers and went out to fight the Wei army and defeated the Wei army.
Qiao Jun saw that Dao Dan was looking at ease, but it was not in his best position to fight with him, so he retreated.
At that time, the Wei army divided its forces and deployed them in Zuoxian, Chenmaggot, Sailuo and other places. The cities maintained contact with each other and faced each other with Fuling City in Daogen.
Wei general Gao Zuzhen led 3,000 cavalry to communicate with each other. Feng Daogen led 100 cavalry to defeat the Wei army and captured the Wei army's Gujiao Army honor guard.
As a result, the Wei army's food transportation channels were cut off, and all armies had to retreat.
Feng Daogen was promoted to general of the auxiliary country.
Wei San, the governor of Yuzhou, surrounded and captured Hefei. Feng Daogen and other armies advanced together, making contributions wherever they went.
In the sixth year, Gong's army attacked Zhongpan, and Shandan ordered Wei Ti to go to rescue him. He met Daodan and led 3,000 soldiers as Wei San's vanguard.
After arriving in Xuzhou, Feng Daogen suggested occupying Shaoyangzhou first, building fortresses, and digging trenches to attack the Wei army's fortifications.
Feng Daogen was able to measure the land on horseback, and the length of the land could be obtained by counting the number of steps taken by the horse. The moat was quickly repaired.
When the water in the Huaihe River rose, Feng Daogen took a warship and attacked the Wei army's bridge by 100 feet. The Wei army was defeated.
Feng added 300 households in the settlement and was promoted to the title of uncle.
After returning to the army, he was promoted to General Yunqi and General Zhihe. Later, he was granted the title of Bo of Yuning County, with the same number of households as before.
He was repeatedly appointed as Sima of Zhongquan, General of Right Guerrilla, General of Military Brigade, and Prefect of Liyang County.
In the eighth year, he moved to the post of General Zhenyi, Jiajie, in charge of military affairs in Yuzhou, governor of Yuzhou, and concurrently served as prefect of Ruyinxing.
Feng Daogen's administration was clean and simple, and the county was stable.
summary: Feng Daogen, courtesy name Danji, was from Luluo. Orphaned young and poor, he worked to support his mother, gaining fame for filial piety at thirteen. At sixteen, he rescued fellow villager Tomb Daowang from barbarians, killing many enemies. During the Yongyuan period, after his mother's death, he joined Gaozu's righteous army, leading village youths. He served under Cai Daofu and later commanded his troops after Daofu's death. After Gaozu ascended, Daogen was made General Xiaoqi and Male of Zengcheng County with 200 households. He suppressed Chen Bozhi's rebellion. As Grand Administrator of Muliang County, he prepared defenses despite ridicule, then defeated General Yu Shifu's 20,000 troops by opening the city gates and sending out 200 elite soldiers. He later captured Wei army's Gujiao Army honor guard, cutting off their food supply. At the battle of Zhongli, he built fortresses and attacked the Wei army's bridge, contributing to their defeat. Daogen was cautious and generous, never boasting of his achievements. Gaozu compared him to General Big Tree. He lived frugally in a simple house with no walls or guards. Though uneducated in youth, he later became proficient in writing. He died at fifty-eight in the first year of the ordinary period, with Gaozu personally mourning him.

translation:
Zhu Yi replied: Once upon a time, Liuzhuang died of illness in bed, and Wei Xianggong was performing sacrifices. He asked the person who presided over the sacrifices: There is a minister named Liuzhuang. He is not my minister, but a minister of Sheji. I heard that he was dead, and I asked to see him.
He went to Liuzhuang's house without taking off his sacrificial robes, and presented Liuzhuang with clothes and quilts.

summary: Wang Liang, a sixth-generation descendant of Jin Dynasty Prime Minister Wang Dao, was selected as a prince consort in the late Song Dynasty due to his prestigious family background. After Jiang's death, Wang could not prevent corrupt appointments. When the benevolent army arrived, Wang did not welcome them, but later met Emperor Gaozu, who spared him. He was granted titles like Duke of Yuning County but was stripped of his rank and made a commoner in the fourth year of Tianjian after being impeached for disrespect. He later lived in seclusion, served as Secretary Supervisor, and died in the ninth year of Tianjian, posthumously named Yangzi.

translation:
Jiang Yan, courtesy name Wentong, was a native of Kaocheng, Jiyang.
He was lonely and impoverished when he was young, but he was diligent, studious, calm, and rarely interacted with others.
He was first appointed to the post of Southern Xuzhou, and was transferred to the imperial court at the request of the emperor.
Song Jianping Wang Jingsu liked scholars, so Jiang Yan followed Jingsu and lived in southern Yanzhou.
Guangling ordered Guo Yanwen to be convicted for some reason, and Jiang Yan was imprisoned in the state prison.
Jiang Yan wrote a letter in prison saying: In the past, when humble ministers struck their chests to express their feelings, frost would suddenly hit Yandi; if ordinary women cried out to the sky, wind would suddenly hit Qitai.
Every time I read these words, I shed tears.
Why?
Because scholars have a firm belief, and women also have virtues that cannot be changed.
Honesty is doubted, loyalty is killed, so the heroic and the chivalrous are willing to die and never look back. This is the reason.
I heard that benevolence and kindness cannot be relied on. At first, I thought this was a lie. Only today do I understand the truth behind it.
I sincerely hope that the king will temporarily stop the affairs around him and show me some mercy and observation.
I originally lived in a simple house with a woven straw door and a mulberry tree as the door hinge. I was an unofficial person wearing linen clothes and a Wei belt around my waist. When you retreat, you don't decorate yourself with poems and books to frighten fools; when you enter, you don't buy fame from the world.
Previously, I was lucky enough to be able to walk up and down the Chengming Palace and in and out of the Jinhua Palace. How could I not restrain my figure, condense my solemnity, and walk sideways through the palace gates?
I admire the king's morality, so I became your guest. I prepared some superficial skills such as chickens, dogs, and thieves, and I also prepared the details of three or five low-level skills.
Your Majesty, your Majesty has bestowed upon me your grace and radiance, and looked at me with a cheerful look.
In fact, Qing made me feel like I was wearing a golden reward like Jing Qing. Privately, I felt like I was enjoying the status of a national scholar like Yu Rang.
I often want to tie up my hat, put my sword on my body, and die calmly, just to thank the king for his kindness in case of emergency, and to repay the king with all my heart and soul.
Unexpectedly, the villain was stubborn and despicable, so he left me slanderous and damaging words, causing my career to fall into the clear law and my body to be restricted in the cold prison.
I stepped on my own figure and felt sorry for myself. Every time I had a sore nose, it hurt to my bones.
I have heard that damaging one's reputation is the greatest shame, and damaging one's body is the second most disgraceful thing, so every time these thoughts come up, I feel as if I have lost something.
In addition, it has been a month and it is approaching the end of autumn. The sky was gloomy and there were no good views around.
My body is neither wood nor stone, but it is with the prison officials.
This is also the reason why Chen Xing looks up to the sky and sighs, beats his heart and blames himself, and the tears flow out and then bleed.
Although I lack the praise of the villagers, I have heard of the virtues of a gentleman.
summary: Jiang Yan, courtesy name Wentong, was a native of Kaocheng, Jiyang. He was lonely and impoverished in his youth but diligent, studious, and reserved. He began his official career as an appointee in Southern Xuzhou and later served at the imperial court. He followed Prince Jingsu of Song Jianping to southern Yanzhou. When Guangling Magistrate Guo Yanwen was convicted, Jiang Yan was imprisoned. From prison, he wrote a letter to Jingsu, pleading his innocence and loyalty, citing historical examples of unjust suffering. He described his humble origins and sincere service, lamenting that slander had led to his imprisonment. He begged for mercy, and Jingsu, moved by the letter, released him that day.
