However, I was in prison with deep pain and anger. Even though this incident was trivial, it was worthy of sadness.
I beg the king to look at me for a moment and find out what happened to me. If this is the case, then the innocent souls in Wuqiu will not be ashamed because their heads turned into mud in the water, and the wandering ghosts in Huting will not feel sorry because their bones rotted into ashes.
I can't bear the urgency of my heart, so I can only respectfully let you know about me through the people around the king.
My intention to leave the film has been declared, and I will die and become immortal.
After Jing Su read the letter from Bao Feng, he released Jiang Yan that day.
Soon after, Jiang Yan was promoted as a scholar in southern Xuzhou. Jiang Yan responded to the emperor's policy questions and was ranked among the best. He was transferred to the Zuo Changshi of the Baling Kingdom.
Jing Su served as the governor of Jingzhou, and Jiang Yan followed him to the town.
When a young boy ascends the throne, his words and deeds are unworthy of imperial virtue.
Jing Su specializes in arrogance and controls the upper class. People advise Jing Su to take advantage of this moment to initiate trouble.
Jiang Yan patiently advised Jingsu every time, saying: Rumors will lead to disaster, which is the reason why the two uncles died together. Resistance, resentment and narrow-mindedness led to the destruction of the seven kingdoms.
Your Highness, you do not seek the stability of the ancestral temple, but instead believe in the strategies of the left and right. Then the tragic scene of elk and frost covering Gusu Terrace will happen again.
Jing Su did not adopt his advice. When Jingsu was stationed in Beijing, Jiang Yan joined the army in the army and led the governor of Nandonghai.
summary: Jiang Yan was soon promoted and served in various posts, including as a scholar in Southern Xuzhou and Zuo Changshi of Baling Kingdom. When Jingsu became governor of Jingzhou, Jiang Yan followed him. As Jingsu grew arrogant and plotted rebellion, Jiang Yan repeatedly advised him against it, warning of historical disasters. Jingsu ignored him. When Jingsu was stationed in Beijing, Jiang Yan served in the army and governed Nandonghai. He wrote fifteen poems to satirize Jingsu’s schemes. After a dispute over county governance, Jingsu had Jiang Yan demoted to Jian'an Wuxingling, where he served for three years.

translation:
At this time, Jing Su and his friends were plotting day and night. Jiang Yan knew that a disaster was about to happen, so he wrote fifteen poems and gave them to Jing Su to satirize him.
When the governor of Nandonghai, Lu Cheng, was mourning and leaving his post, Jiang Yan believed that as the county magistrate, he should handle county affairs, but Jing Su appointed Sima Liu Shilong to be in charge of county affairs.
Jiang Yan insisted on managing county affairs. Jing Su was furious and told the election department about the matter. As a result, Jiang Yan was demoted to Jian'an Wu Xingling.
Jiang Yan served in Wuxing County for three years.
At the beginning of the next year, Qi Yi assisted in the government affairs. Hearing about Jiang Yan's talents, he recruited him as a Shangshu Jiabulang and a hussar to join the military.
Soon Shen Youzhi, the governor of Jingzhou, launched a rebellion. Emperor Gao said to Jiang Yan: The world is in such chaos, what do you think we should do?
Jiang Yan replied: In the past, Xiang Yu was strong and Liu Bang was weak, Yuan Shao had many soldiers and Cao Cao had few. Although Xiang Yu ordered the princes, he finally suffered the humiliation of cutting his neck with a sword and died; Yuan Chu once occupied four states, but eventually became a defeated man.
Cultivation is called emphasizing on virtue rather than on eminence.
What are you worried about?
Emperor Gao said: I have heard this a lot, so please try to analyze it for me.
Jiang Yan said: You are majestic and brave, and have strange strategies. This is the first condition for victory; you are generous, tolerant, benevolent, loyal, and forgiving, which is the second condition for victory; all the talented people in the world are willing to do their best for you, which is the third condition for victory; you are a person who is popular with the people, which is the fourth condition for victory; you help the emperor to fight against rebellion, which is the fifth condition for victory.
Although they have sharp ambitions, they have small means, which is the first reason for their failure; they are powerful but mean and unkind, which is the second reason for their failure; their soldiers are distracted and torn apart, which is the third reason for their failure; the officials do not support them, which is the fourth reason for their failure; they go thousands of miles alone, but have no friends to help them, which is the fifth reason for their failure.
Therefore, although they have a hundred thousand wolf soldiers, they will eventually be captured by us.
Gao Di smiled and said: You have gone too far.
When dispatching, Jiang Yan was asked to draft all the military books, tables, and notes.
The Xiangguo Mansion was established, and Jiang Yan was assigned to the Jishi Office to join the military.
In the early years of the founding of the Yuan Dynasty, he served as the Hussar Yuzhang Wang Ji's Office, led Dongwu Ling, participated in the management of imperial edicts, and was in charge of compiling national history.
Soon he was moved to the post of Vice Minister of Zhongshu.
At the beginning of Yongming Dynasty, he was transferred to General Xiaoqi and was in charge of compiling the history of the country.
Later he left Beijing and served as general of Jianwu and internal history of Luling.
After serving as chief minister for three years, he returned to Beijing and served as general of cavalry and concurrently as minister Zuocheng. Soon after, he became the doctor of Guozi with his own official position.
At the beginning of the young emperor's accession to the throne, Jiang Yan concurrently served as the censor Zhongcheng with his official position.
summary: When Qi Yi came to power, he recruited Jiang Yan as Shangshu Jiabulang. During Shen Youzhi’s rebellion, Emperor Gao consulted Jiang Yan, who analyzed the strengths of the emperor and the weaknesses of the rebels, predicting victory. Emperor Gao was pleased and entrusted Jiang Yan with drafting military documents. Jiang Yan held numerous high offices under Qi, including Hussar Yuzhang Wang Ji's Office, Vice Minister of Zhongshu, and General Xiaoqi. He served as governor of Luling and later returned to the capital as General of Cavalry and Minister Zuocheng. As Censor Zhongcheng, he impeached several officials for negligence and corruption, earning praise from Emperor Ming for his strictness.

translation:
At this time, Emperor Ming took up the post of prime minister and said to Jiang Yan: When you were in the Ministry of Finance, you would never act rashly on matters that were not public affairs. As an official, you were both tolerant and strict, and could compromise and reconcile. Now that you are appointed to the post of Nansi, it is enough to scare and purge all officials.
Jiang Yan replied: Today's matter can only be said to be done in accordance with the duties of an official. I am even more afraid that my talents are inferior and my will is weak, and that I will not be commensurate with the wise will of the Holy One.
So Jiang Yan impeached Zhongshu Ling Xie Chu, Situ Zuo Chief Shi Wang Ji, and Guard Chief Shi Yu Hongyuan, all of whom did not participate in the official affairs of the imperial mausoleum because they had been ill for a long time. He also impeached the former Yizhou Governor Liu Tong and the former Governor of Zhiye for embezzling tens of thousands of dollars in money and materials, and these people were handed over to the Tingwei for punishment.
Shen Zhaolue, the governor of Linhai, Yu Tanlong, the governor of Yongjia, as well as Erqianshi of various counties and officials of major counties, were mostly impeached and punished. As a result, the court became solemn and stable inside and outside.
Emperor Ming said to Jiang Yan: Since the Song Dynasty, there has been no strict censor Zhongcheng. You can now be regarded as unique in modern times.
After Emperor Ming came to the throne, he appointed Jiang Yan as the chief historian of the Chariot and Linhai King.
Soon after, he was appointed as Wei Qing of the Imperial Court, and was appointed as Shizhong. He was also promoted to the title of Champion Changshi, and he was also appointed as the general of the auxiliary country.
Later he left the capital and served as the prefect of Xuancheng, and still served as the general of the auxiliary country.
After serving in Xuancheng County for four years, Jiang Yan returned to the capital and served as Huangmen's minister, captain of the infantry, and soon served as secretary and supervisor.
During the Yongyuan period, Cui Huijing raised troops to surround the capital. The gentry and officials all went to submit their names, pay homage and make friends, but Jiang Yan pretended to be ill and refused to go.
When the rebellion was put down, everyone admired Jiang Yan for his foresight.
In the last years of Donghun Hou's reign, Jiang Yan served as secretary and supervisor concurrently as a guard. He insisted on resigning, but did not get permission, so he had to take up the post.
Jiang Yan once said to people: I am not qualified for the position of guard. Even passers-by know this. Let me serve as a guard concurrently, just for my false reputation.
Besides, the weather and human affairs will soon change.
Confucius said: Those who are knowledgeable about affairs must be prepared for martial arts.
If you try to plan something when it comes, what's the point of worrying?
Soon, he was appointed deputy to the leader Wang Ying.
When the righteous army arrived at Saiqiudie, Liao Zha came to join him in civilian clothes. After the birth, Shaoshu appointed Jiang Yan as the champion general, and he still served as secretary and supervisor. Soon he also served as Situ Zuo's chief historian.
In the first year of the Zhongxing Dynasty, he was transferred to the post of Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs. In the second year, he was transferred to the post of Prime Minister, Youchang Shi, and he still served as the champion general.
In the first year of his imprisonment, he avoided serving as the regular servant of Sanqi and the general of Zuowei, and was named the founding uncle of Linju County, with a fief of 400 households.
Jiang Yan said to his disciples: I was originally an ordinary official who did not pursue fame and wealth, but now I am in a high position and have become wealthy.
summary: Under Emperor Ming, Jiang Yan held positions such as Chief Historian of the Chariot and Linhai King, Shizhong, and Prefect of Xuancheng. During the Yongyuan period, when Cui Huijing besieged the capital, Jiang Yan feigned illness and avoided the rebels, earning admiration for his foresight. He later served as Secretary Supervisor and Guard, though he felt unqualified. He was enfeoffed as Founding Uncle of Linju County. In his later years, he expressed contentment and a desire to retire. He died at age sixty-two, and the emperor mourned him with gifts. Jiang Yan was known for his literary talent in youth but declined in later years. He authored over a hundred works and ten records of "History of Qi."

translation:
In my life, I like to talk about knowing and being content, and now I am very complete.
Life is just about having fun, how long will you be greedy for wealth?
Now that my reputation has been established, I want to retreat to the grass.
That year, due to illness, he was transferred to the post of Doctor Jin Ziguanglu and changed his title to Liling Bo.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, Jiang Zha passed away. He was sixty-two years old at this time.
Zhizu mourned Jiang Yan in plain clothes and gave him 30,000 yuan and 50 pieces of cloth for the funeral.
Jiang Yan's nickname is Xian Bo.
When Hongji was young, he was famous for his good writing. However, in his later years, his talents declined and degenerated. People at the time said that he was exhausted.
He wrote more than a hundred works in total, which he compiled into two volumes. He also wrote ten records of "History of Qi", which have been circulated in the world.
Jiang Yan's son Jiang Jian inherited the title of the feudal prince and was promoted from Danyang Yincheng to the Great Wall Order. However, he was stripped of his title because of his guilt.
In ordinary four years, in memory of Tao's achievements, Sijiang was granted the title of Chengdanbo, and the fiefdom remained as before.
Ren Fang, named Yansheng, was a native of Bochang, Le'an, and a descendant of Yao, the imperial censor of Modai.
My father's name is Yao, and he is a doctor of Zhongsan in Qi.
Ren Yao's wife was Yu Dan. She once slept during the day and dreamed of colorful flags and small bells hanging from the four corners falling from the sky. One of the bells fell into Pei's arms. Pei's heart was touched, and soon she became pregnant and gave birth to Ren Chuan.
Ren Chuo is seven feet five inches tall.
He was studious when he was young and became famous early on.
Song Danyang Yin Liu Bingzheng summoned him as the chief bookkeeper.
Ren Zuo was only sixteen years old at the time, and because of his youth and arrogance, he disobeyed Liu Bing's son.
A long time later, he took up the post requested by the imperial court and was recommended as a scholar in Yanzhou. He became an official with Dr. Taichang and moved to the north to join the army.
In the early years of the Yongming Dynasty, General Wang Jian of the Wei Dynasty led Danyang Yin, and he was appointed as the chief secretary.
Wang Qi admired Ren Dui very much and thought that no one could compare with him at that time.
Ren Fang then moved to the post of Chief of Prison and joined the military. He joined the cabinet and served as the lieutenant in the Shangshu Palace. He was transferred to the office of Situ Jingling and joined the army. He later resigned in mourning for his father's death.
Ren Fang had a very filial temperament and exercised all etiquette during mourning.
He had just taken off his mourning clothes, and then suffered the pain of losing his mother. Because he had lived in a hut next to his parents' tomb for a long time and guarded the tomb, the vegetation no longer grew in the place where he cried.
After the mourning clothes were removed, he was appointed as a defense officer and paid homage to the prince's infantry captain and secretary of Guan Dong Palace.
At the beginning, Emperor Ming of Qi had deposed King Yulin and began to serve as Shizhong, Zhongshu Supervisor, Huqi General, Kaifu Yitong Sansi, Yangzhou Governor, and Lu Shangshu. He was named the Duke of Xuancheng County and added five thousand troops.
summary: Ren Fang, courtesy name Yansheng, was a native of Bochang, Le'an. His father was Yao, a doctor of Zhongsan in Qi. Ren Fang was studious and became famous early. At sixteen, he served as chief bookkeeper for Song Danyang Yin Liu Bing. He later held various posts, including Dr. Taichang and chief secretary for Wang Jian. Ren Fang was known for his filial piety, mourning his parents with extreme devotion. He served as a defense officer and secretary of Guan Dong Palace. During Qi Mingdi’s reign, he drafted a memorial declining high honors, citing his inadequacy and the state’s troubles. His refusal angered the emperor, stalling his career.

translation:
Ren Fang has a friend who is the wife of his wife, and Xingjiao's younger brother is Xingjiao. Xingjiao follows Ren Fang to travel through the mountains and rivers.
When the post of Yixing governor was replaced, Ren Fang boarded a ship and traveled far. At this time, he only had five dendrobium rice.
He had arrived in the capital but had no clothes to wear. The general of the town army, Shen Yue, sent someone to send him a shirt to welcome him.
Later, he was appointed as the official of Fang Zhongzhong and paid homage to the doctor of the Ministry of Personnel, and participated in the election affairs. However, he was incompetent for this official position.
Soon he was transferred to the post of censor Zhongcheng, secretary supervisor, and leader of the former army general.
Since Qi Yongyuan, the titles of the four volumes of Secret Pavilion books have been complicated. Ren Fang personally proofread them, so the titles were determined.
In the spring of the sixth year, Ren Fang left the capital and served as General Ningshuo and Prefect of Xin'an.
When Ren Fang was in the county, he was unkempt, dragging his cane casually and walking on foot inside and outside the county. When the common people filed lawsuits, Ren Fang made decisions on the road.
Ren Fang's administration is clean and trouble-free, and officials and the people find it very convenient.
After serving as an official for one year, he died in the official office at the age of forty-nine.
People throughout Xin'an County felt deeply sorry for him, and the common people built an ancestral hall in the south of the city.
After Emperor Gaozu heard about it, he mourned for Ren Fang that day and cried very sadly.
Ren Fang was forced to be given the title of Taichang Qing, and his nickname was Jingzi.
Ren Fang likes to make friends with others, reward and recommend scholars and friends.
Most of those who are praised by Ren Fangyan are promoted. Therefore, there is no one among the dignitaries who does not strive for public support and friendship. There are always dozens of guests sitting at Fang's house.
People at that time envied him and called him Renjun, which meant that he was like the three monarchs of Modai. Yin Yun of Chen County wrote to Gai, the prefect of Jian'an, saying: When a philosopher dies, his appearance disappears forever.
From now on, to whom will we entrust the affairs of Shi Zhan’s writings?
Who will be responsible for guiding scholars and friends?
This is how Ren Fang was praised by scholar friends.
If he failed to take care of his property, he would have no house to live in.
At that time, some people ridiculed Ren Fang for often begging for loans, but the money and goods he borrowed were later distributed to relatives and friends.
Ren Fang often sighed: Those who understand me are Shuze, and those who don't understand me are also Shuze.
Ren Fang was well-read, and there was no book of three tombs or five classics that he had not read. Although his family was poor, he had accumulated more than ten thousand volumes of books, most of which were common and different editions.
After Ren Fang's death, Emperor Gaozu sent scholars He Zong and Shen Yue to examine his family's books together. Whatever the government did not have, they took out the books from Ren Fang's family to make up for them.
The articles written by Ren Fang have hundreds of thousands of words and are widely popular in the world.
At the beginning, Ren Fang was ranked among the scholar-bureaucrats. He often rewarded the scholar-bureaucrats and promoted them. Anyone who liked him would enhance his reputation.
When Ren Fang died, his children were still young, but few people cared for them.
Pingyuan Liu Xiaobiao wrote an article on this matter and said: The guest asked the host: Is Uncle Zhu's "On Severing Diplomacy" correct?
summary: Ren Fang excelled in writing essays, biographies, and memorials, often composing without revision. He was admired by contemporaries like Xuan. After the dynasty’s fall, he served under Liang, holding posts such as Huangmen Shilang and Minister of Personnel. As governor of Yixing, he lived frugally, eating only wheat. He later served as Censor Zhongcheng and Secretary Supervisor, personally proofreading library titles. As governor of Xin'an, he governed simply, deciding lawsuits on the road. He died in office at age forty-nine, and the people built a shrine for him. The emperor mourned deeply. Ren Fang was generous with friends, recommending scholars and hosting many guests. He was called "Renjun" for his patronage. Despite poverty, he accumulated over ten thousand books. After his death, the emperor took rare books from his collection. Ren Fang’s writings totaled hundreds of thousands of words. However, after his death, his children were neglected. Liu Xiaobiao wrote an essay criticizing fair-weather friends, describing five types of snobbish acquaintances: those drawn to power, wealth, reputation, shared misfortune, and calculated gain. He lamented that Ren Fang’s former friends abandoned his family.

translation:
He cherishes guests just like Tian Wen, and likes talented people just like Zheng Zhuang.
When he sees a kind person, he will support his car, open his eyes, look straight at his wrist, and sigh; when he meets a wise man, he will hold his hand and talk with elation.
Ren Fang can refute the truth at any time, and it is up to him to judge whether it is right or wrong.
So the carriages with crowns and covers gathered like clouds, and people gathered in front of Renfang's gate like clouds. The carriages with curtains crowded and bumped into each other, and Renfang's house was always full of guests.
Stepping onto the threshold of Ren Fang's house is like ascending to the main house of Queli; entering the corner of his house is like ascending the hillside of Longmen.
As for Ren Fang, just looking at him will double his worth, praising him will make him display his talents. People who serve as officials in Yuntai are crowded with each other, and people who are running around in Danqi overlap.
There is no one who does not want to be close to Ren Fang and interact with him frequently. He hopes that Ren Fang will patronize him like Hui and Zhuang, and he hopes to be as famous as Yang and Zuo.
When Ren Fang died in Shuyue and his bones were buried in Luopu, when the general ledger was still hanging high, there were few talented and learned people mourning in front of his house; the overnight grass had not yet grown on his grave, and the countryside had been cut off from the guests who came to express their condolences in cars.
All the orphans in Renfang are still naive, and their lives are precarious. They are wandering to the south of the sea, pinning their fate in a place full of miasma.
In the past, those Yingjies who had close relationships with Ren Fang and made friends with Jinlan did not have the kindness of a sheep's tongue and how could they envy Qiu Chengzhai's kindness.
oops!
The world has become so difficult and dangerous!
Taihang Mengmen, I would rather say it is steep and high.
Therefore, the upright people, hating them for being like this, tore their clothes, wrapped their feet, galloped on their horses, and abandoned them far away.
Standing alone on the top of the mountain, happily grouping with the elk, pure and noble, cut off from the confusion and filth of the world, they are indeed ashamed of the ungrateful people, and are indeed afraid of those who are treacherous.
Ren Fang wrote 247 volumes of "Miscellaneous Biography", 252 volumes of "Diji", and 33 volumes of articles.
The fourth son is Seri. He is very like his father, and his official rank is Shangshu Waibinglang.
Yao Cha, the Minister of Official Affairs of the Chen Dynasty, said: Looking at the selection of talents in the Second Han Dynasty, Confucian classics and alchemy were generally given priority; in modern times, the standards for selecting talents are mostly judged by the quality of literature and history.
The works of Jiang Yan and Ren Fang, with their majestic and gorgeous rhetoric, were indeed at the right time.
Jiang Yan has the ability to have a calm personality, be cautious and reserved and focus on inner cultivation, and at the same time start well and end well in terms of reputation and status. This is appropriate.
If Jiang Yan hadn't relied on prior knowledge and had no old favors, then there would be no way for him to get gifts from high-ranking officials and prominent officials.
summary: Yao Cha commented that Jiang Yan and Ren Fang were talented writers of their time. Jiang Yan’s calm and cautious nature allowed him to maintain his reputation, though he relied on prior connections. Ren Fang’s works included 247 volumes of "Miscellaneous Biography," 252 volumes of "Diji," and 33 volumes of articles. His son Seri resembled him and served as Shangshu Waibinglang.

translation:
The character element of Sima Ming is from Wen, Hanoi.
My great-grandfather's name was Chunzhi, and he was the great minister of the Jin Dynasty, Gaomi Jingwang.
His grandfather's name was Rang, and he was appointed as an official and a regular attendant.
His father, Sima Xie, was good at "Three Rites" and served as an official in the Qi Dynasty until he became a doctor of Guozi.
Sima Xian inherited the family business when he was young. He was strong and dedicated in his work. He never let go of the books and read all the books related to etiquette.
Liu Xian, a native of Pei State, was worshiped by Confucian scholars, who also praised his knowledge and admired him very much.
When he was young, he was friendly to Ren Fang, a person from Le'an, and Ren Fang also respected him.
He was born as a son of the country at the beginning. He started his career and was invited by the imperial court. After a while, he moved to the royal palace and joined the army.
In the early years of Tianjian, Shao ordered the learned Confucian scholars to study and manage the Five Rites. The relevant officials recommended Sima Zhuang to study and manage Jiali, and he was appointed as a doctor of the Shangshu Temple.
At this time, the state established rituals and music, and most of what Sima Zhuang proposed was implemented.
He was appointed as an infantry school captain and concurrently as Zhongshu Tongshisheren.
Sima Zhuang's knowledge is especially proficient in the art of predicting the good and bad fortunes of people. The good and bad etiquette of the country. When the world's famous scholars, Shanbin, He Chang, etc. have questions and cannot make decisions, they all depend on him.
After being promoted to Zhengyuanlang, Zhennan consulted to join the army, and he continued to serve as a soldier.
Moved to the post of Minister Youcheng.
He served as the chief historian of Renwei and the internal history of Changsha.
After returning to the capital, he was awarded the title of General Yunqi and concurrently served as Yushi Zhongcheng. Soon the part-time job was changed to a full-time position.
In the 16th year, he served as the chief historian of Xuanyi Nankang King, the governor of the country and the stone garrison military.
Although Sima Zhuang was appointed as a foreign official, there was an edict asking him to participate in the Wende and Wude Halls to draw up the list of official officials, and to communicate with each other for advice without time limit.
In the seventeenth year, he was moved to the post of General Mingwei and King Changshi of Jin'an, and died soon after.
Yu Jianwu, the Mingji Office of the King of Jin'an, collected his articles and compiled them into ten volumes, and compiled "Jia Li Zhu" in 112 volumes.
Maoguan, whose name is Maoguan, is from Wuyuan, Pengcheng.
My great-grandfather came to Yanzhi and was a hussar general in the Song Dynasty.
When my grandfather went to Zhongdu, he served as a hussar to the king of Jiangxia and worked as a lieutenant.
My father came to Tan and served as Zhongshu Lang in the Qi Dynasty.
His father died when he was young, and his family was poor. He and his younger brother Daoqia were both smart and talented. They were appreciated by Ren Fang early on, and their reputation became even wider from then on.
He started out as the royal minister of the left side of the kingdom, then became military commander Cao Xing and joined the army, and successively served as the palace's lieutenant.
He served as the internal history of Jian'an and moved to the post of Zhongshu Lang and Libu Lang. He was the concubine among the princes.
When Xiao Yi, the king of eastern Hunan, was appointed as the prefect of Kuaiji, he was appointed as the chief historian of Qingchao and responsible for the affairs of the county.
Emperor Gaozu said to the king: Daoji is not only acting for you, he can also be your teacher. If you have any progress, you must consult him.
summary: Biographical accounts of several scholars and officials from the Liang Dynasty, focusing on their lineage, careers, and contributions to ritual studies and governance. Sima Xian, from Wen, Hanoi, inherited a family tradition of scholarship in the "Three Rites." He served in various official posts, including as a doctor of the Shangshu Temple, where he contributed to the establishment of state rituals and music. He was known for his expertise in predicting fortunes and was consulted by renowned scholars. He held positions such as Infantry School Captain and Minister Youcheng, and later served as a chief historian and governor. He died in the seventeenth year of the Tianjian era, and his works were compiled posthumously.

translation:
When his mother died, he performed all the mourning rituals and was praised by the court.
After the period of mourning, he gave up his clothes and ate vegetables and wore common clothes for many years.
He was awarded Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi, Yushi Zhongcheng, Taifu Qing, Duguan Shangshu, Yingzhou Governor Shi, Jiangxia Shangshu, and was appointed General Zhaoyuan, and became Zuo Min Shangshu.
He is eight feet tall, has a beautiful demeanor, a kind appearance, and is clean and self-disciplined in all official positions he holds.
He is also very frugal by nature, not fond of sensuality, has only one bed in the empty house, has no concubines around him, wears clothes when traveling, and does not pursue flowers. He wears his crown and shoes every ten years, and his court uniforms even have patches. He shouts to make the road quiet, which only shows that he has court seals.
Soon after, he was demoted to the post of Jinzi Guanglu doctor due to being implicated. Soon after, he was appointed as a regular attendant of Sanqi, a minister in the middle, and a minister of the state.
He had always been a cautious and kind-hearted person until Gai, and he was especially appreciated and accepted by Emperor Gaozu. Every time he played chess with him, it was from midnight to dawn.
There was a strange stone in the mountain pool of Daoji Mansion. Gaozu made a joke with it and bet with it, and added a copy of "Book of Rites". Daoji also lost, but did not bring the gambling items. Gaozu said to Zhu Yi: "Can you tell Daoji if I can send you the things I lost?"
Daoji put away his hand and replied, "Since I serve the king, I dare not be rude."
Gaozu laughed when he heard this. He was loved like this.
Later, he became ill and lost his sight, so he was ordered to take up the post of Jin Ziguanglu doctor and Sanqi regular attendant to recuperate in the mansion.
The family members live in harmony, and the brothers are particularly friendly.
At first, he and his brother lived together in Qiaochang. After Qia died, he donated money to build a temple. From then on, he stopped eating meat and fish and ate vegetarian vegetables all his life. He also built a small room and worshiped and chanted sutras with the monks day and night.
Emperor Gaozu prepared three vegetarian dishes for him every month, which was a very generous gift to him.
There is Yanxian Temple in Jiangshan, which was founded by Mr. Dao Ji. Therefore, all his salary throughout his life was provided to the temple and he received nothing in return.
He was not easy to socialize with by nature, so he was only close friends with Zhu Yi, Liu Zhilin and Zhang Wanzhi.
When he was sick in his home, there were only a few people around. The three princes often made a detour to his house every year when traveling, greeted each other, drank wine and talked about their lives, and left happily.
When he was dying, his descendants who entrusted Zhang and Liu to control him buried him with frugal etiquette. He was seventy-two years old when he died.
An edict was issued to posthumously reward him as an official.
A collection of twenty volumes has been circulated in the world.
At that time, people compared Daoji and Daoqia, brothers and sisters of Erlu, so the ancestor Shizu's poem said: The Wei Dynasty respected Shuangding, and the Jin Dynasty praised Erlu. How can it be compared with Liangdao today, and it is like the green bamboo of Linghan.
Zijing, whose courtesy name was Yuanzhao, served as King Facao Xing of Xiangshu in Anxi and joined the army. The prince passed away long ago.
From Zijing to Gai, he was smart since he was a child. He started his career as a Zuo Lang, and successively served as the prince's minister, the chief secretary of the king of Xuancheng, the prince's horse washer, and the minister's palace minister.
summary: Maoguan, from Pengcheng, was orphaned young but gained recognition for his talent. He served in several official roles, including as a chief historian and governor. Known for his frugality and integrity, he was favored by Emperor Gaozu, who often played chess with him. He was demoted due to implication in a case but later reinstated. He was a devout Buddhist, donating his salary to a temple and living a simple life. He died at seventy-two, leaving a collection of twenty volumes.

translation:

summary: Liu Xian, from Pei State, was a child prodigy known for his vast knowledge. He served in various capacities, including as a legal officer and minister. He was praised for his memory and ability to decipher ancient texts. He held positions such as Infantry School Captain and Doctor Guozi. He died at sixty-three, and his friend Liu Zhilin petitioned the crown prince for an epitaph, which was granted.

translation:
Wang Gui, courtesy name Weiming, was from Linyi, Langxie.
His grandfather Wang Jian was a Taiwei during the Qi Dynasty and was named Nanchang County Duke, while Mi was named Wenxian Gong.
His father, Wang Qian, served as a doctor in Jinziguanglu and was named the Marquis of Nanchang.
When Wang Gui was eight years old, his biological mother died. During the mourning period, Wang Gui was extremely sincere and filial. Every time Taiwei Xu Xiaosi saw him, he was moved to tears by his filial piety and called him a filial boy.
Wang Gui's uncle Wang Chen also thought highly of him. He once said: "My son is my family's horse."
When Wang Gui was twelve years old, he had a general understanding of the meaning of the Five Classics.
When I grow up, I love learning more and become more eloquent.
Wang Gui was promoted as a scholar by the state, and the county chose him as the chief registrar.
Wang Gui was recruited from his family to serve as Secretary Lang, and was promoted to Prince Sheren, An Younan Kang Wang's chief secretary, and Prince Xima.
In the twelfth year of Tianjian, the imperial court rebuilt the Taiji Hall. After it was completed, Wang Gui presented the "New Hall Fu" with exquisite diction.
He was appointed Secretary Cheng.
He successively served as the Prince's Zhongsheren, Situ Zuoxi, and worked as a Zhonglang.
Xiao Gang, king of Jin'an, came to the capital to serve as the governor of Southern Xuzhou. He strictly selected his subordinate palaces, and Wang Gui was selected as Yunhui to consult and join the army.
After a long time, Wang Gui came to the capital again to serve as the prefect of Xin'an, but he resigned because his father died.
After the mourning period expired, he was granted the title of Marquis of Nanchang County and was appointed as the Minister of Huangmen of Zhongshu.
The emperor ordered Wang Gui, Chen Jun Yin Gou, Langxie Wang Xi, Fan Yang and Zhang Mian to serve the prince together. Prince Zhaoming treated them all with courtesy.
At that time, the King of Xiangdong was appointed as the capital of Beijing, and he and the court officials gathered for a banquet. During the banquet, the King of Xiangdong asked Wang Gui to make drinking orders.
Wang Gui replied calmly: This has not happened since the Jin Dynasty moved to Jiangzuo.
At that time, Te Jin Xiao Chen and Jin Zi Fu Zhao were present, and they all thought that Luo's words were very insightful.
In the early years of ordinary times, Chen Qingzhi conquered Luoyang during his Northern Expedition. All the officials in the court congratulated him. After Wang Gui retired from the court, he said: Taoism says that it is not difficult to get things started, but it is difficult to achieve achievements.
Jie Kou is like a wandering spirit. It has lasted for a long time. Wenwen conquered, gained and lost, and Emperor Wu of the Song Dynasty failed in the end. We went deep into the enemy's territory alone, without backup, and went deep into the area occupied by Jie Kou. Our troops could not be connected and our supplies could not be sustained. This battle would bring disaster.
Soon the imperial army was completely wiped out. His thorough understanding of things is much like this.
In the sixth year, Emperor Gaozu hosted a banquet in the Wende Palace to pay farewell to Yuan Jinglong, the governor of Guangzhou. He issued an edict to the ministers to compose poems, stipulating that they should all write one hundred lines of poems. Wang Gui picked up his pen and wrote the memorial immediately, and the poems were very beautiful.
Emperor Gaozu admired Wang Gui's talents very much and appointed him as a minister in Shao that day.
In the third year of Datong, Wang Gui was moved to the post of Minister of the Fifth Army, and soon he was also appointed as the infantry captain.
In the second year of Zhongdatong, Wang Gui came to the capital to serve as general Zhenwei's hussar and chief historian of Jin'an.
That year, King Jin'an was established as the crown prince, and Wang Gui then became the prefect of Wu County.
The home of the chief secretary, Rui Zhenzong, was in Wu, and all the previous governors were devoted to fawning over him. When Wang Gui took office, Zhenzong went home on vacation. Wang Gui treated him very distantly, and then returned to Kyoto. He secretly reported to the king that he ignored the political affairs of the county.
So Wang Dan soon changed his post to Zuo Min Shangshu. More than a thousand officials and people from Wu County in the capital requested Wang Gui to stay in his post. They petitioned three times, but the emperor refused.
Soon Wang Gui concurrently served as the general of the right army in the name of Zuo Min Shangshu. Without any appointment, he was appointed as the regular servant of the Sanqi, the prince's concubine, and concurrently as the infantry captain.
Wang Gui resigned due to illness and refused to take up the post, so he built a house in Songxi Temple to live.
In the second year of his reign, Wang Nie passed away at the age of forty-five.
The emperor posthumously awarded him the rank of Sanqi Changshi and Guanglu Doctor. He also gave him 200,000 yuan and 100 pieces of cloth to organize his funeral, and gave him a Mi title.
The crown prince went to Wang Guiling to cry and mourned, and ordered: "The king died suddenly last night, which is really sad."
summary: Wang Gui, courtesy name Weiming, was from Linyi, Langxie. His grandfather Wang Jian was a Taiwei during the Qi Dynasty, and his father Wang Qian served as a doctor. At age eight, Wang Gui lost his biological mother and showed extreme filial piety during mourning, moving Taiwei Xu Xiaosi to tears. His uncle Wang Chen praised him as "my family's horse." In the second year of Zhongdatong, he became prefect of Wu County, where he distanced himself from the powerful Rui Zhenzong, leading to a transfer. He resigned due to illness and built a house in Songxi Temple. He died at age forty-five, and the emperor posthumously awarded him titles and gifts. The crown prince mourned him, praising his charm and talent. Wang Gui collected different versions of the "Book of the Later Han" and annotated 200 volumes of the "Sustained Book of Han" and 20 volumes of collected works.

During Hou Jing's rebellion, Liu Xiaowei escaped from the siege and followed Liu Zhongli, the governor of Sizhou, to the west. He arrived in Anlu and died of illness.
Liu Xiaoyi's seventh brother Liu Xiaoxian served as King Wuling's Facao and Chief Secretary. King Wuling moved to Yizhou to be the governor. He followed the palace to Yizhou and was transferred to the Anxi Record Office.
During the reign of Prime Minister Liu Xiaosheng, he and his brother Liu Xiaosheng followed Ji's army out of the gorge. After the defeat, they went to Jiangling. The emperor appointed him as the Huangmen Minister and moved him to the position of Minister.
summary: Liu Yu, courtesy name Zhongshi, was a seventh-generation descendant of Yin Liu Zhenchang. Chu Qiu, courtesy name Zhongbao, was poor but studious. He served as magistrate of Liyang and later as censor Zhongcheng, known for his fairness. He died at seventy. He died at sixty-seven, leaving twenty volumes of collected works. His brothers Liu Xiaosheng and Liu Xiaowei were also talented. translation:

Therefore, not much is seen and heard by people.
Now collect their deeds to complete the story of their disappearance. Teng Tanggong was born in Nanchang, Yuzhang.
When he was five years old, his mother, Yang, contracted a fever and wanted to eat cold melons, but they were not produced locally. Teng Tanggong searched everywhere but could not find them. He felt sad and in great pain.
Soon Teng Tangong met a monk. He was in pain and sorrow among the monks. Teng Tangong told the monk everything.
The monk said: I have two cold melons, and I will give one to you.
After Teng Tan respectfully thanked the monk, he took the melon home and presented it to his mother.
The whole family was very surprised.
Everyone was looking for the monk everywhere, but no one knew where the monk was.
After his parents died, Teng Tanggong did not eat or drink for about ten days. He cried so sadly that he vomited blood, fainted and then woke up.
Teng Tanggong did not wear cotton-padded clothes during the mid-winter season and only ate vegetables throughout his life.
Every time on the anniversary of the death of my parents, I can't bear the longing, and I cry heartbroken day and night.
There were two winter trees outside Teng Tangong's house. Suddenly a divine light appeared from the trees. Soon the image of the Buddha and the guards of honor on both sides appeared. Their appearance was clear. They walked into Teng Tangong's house from the gate. Everyone in the Teng family, big and small, bowed and worshiped the Buddha. It took a long time for the Buddha's image to disappear. Monks and people from far and near preached and performed things.
The prefect Wang Sengqian recommended Teng Tanggong to be a meritorious officer, but Teng Tanggong firmly refused to take up the post.
Wang Jian followed Wang Sengqian in the county at that time, and he called Teng Tanggong Teng Zengzi.
In the first year of Tianjian, Lu Lian was ordered to serve as an envoy to visit various places to understand the customs and conditions of the people. He reported Teng Tangong's filial piety and his response to the gods and Buddhas. Teng Tangong had three sons, all of whom were virtuous and accomplished.
At that time, there was also Xu Puji, a native of Linxiang, Changsha.
He was in mourning and the coffin had not yet been buried. A fire broke out in his neighbor's house and the fire spread to his house. Xu Puji howled and cried bitterly and leaned on the coffin, trying to cover the fire with his body.
Neighbors went to rescue him, but he was roasted until he passed out. It took many days for him to wake up.
There was a girl in Wanling, Xuancheng, who was sleeping in the same bed with her mother. Her mother was caught by a tiger. The girl screamed and grabbed the tiger, and all the tiger hairs were caught by her. After running for more than ten miles, the tiger dropped the girl's mother. The girl carried her mother home, and her mother was still alive. It took an hour before she died.
summary: Filial piety as the foundation of virtue, emphasizing its importance for both the people and rulers. Emperor Gaozu promoted filial piety through edicts, transforming customs and encouraging virtuous behavior. The text then recounts the deeds of several individuals known for their exceptional filial piety. Teng Tanggong, from Nanchang, demonstrated filial piety at age five by seeking cold melons for his ill mother, which a monk miraculously provided. After his parents' deaths, he mourned excessively, refusing food and warm clothing. Divine signs, including a vision of Buddha, appeared at his home. He refused official positions and was praised as "Teng Zengzi." Xu Puji, from Linxiang, protected his mother's coffin from a fire, suffering severe burns. A girl from Wanling fought a tiger to save her mother, carrying her home before she died. Shen Chongsu, from Wuxing, mourned his mother with extreme grief, lying on her grave in all weather. Despite an imperial edict promoting him, he refused the position and died from grief at age thirty-nine.

translation:
Xunjiang, also known as Wenshi, was born in Yingyin. He was the ninth generation descendant of Xun Xu, the Taibao of Jin Dynasty.
Xun Jiang's grandfather, Xun Qiong, avenged his father in the Chengdu market when he was fifteen years old, and was therefore famous for his filial piety.
In the late years of the Song and Yuan Dynasties, Xunjiang crossed the river and rushed to King Wuling to join the rebel army. He was killed by the culprit's pursuers. The imperial court awarded him the posthumous title of Yuanwai Sanqi Shilang.
Xun Fachao, the father of Xunjiang, was appointed as Anfu Ling in the late years of Zhongxing in Qi Dynasty, and died while serving.
When the bad news reached the Xun family, Xunjiang howled and cried bitterly. He passed out and his whole body was cold. He didn't wake up until night.
Not long after, Xunjiang went to mourn. Every time he stayed by the river, the business travelers who came and went couldn't bear to hear his mournful cries.
Before the mourning was over, Xun Fei, Xun Jiang's brother, was recruited from home to serve as the governor of Yulin. When he was conquering the slang bandits, he was shot by a stray arrow and died in the battle.
When the coffin was brought back, Xunjiang went to Yuzhang to greet him. He saw the boat carrying the coffin from a distance and jumped into the water. People on both sides rushed to rescue him and barely rescued him.
After the coffin arrived home, he could not be buried on time because his family was poor, so he mourned for his father and brother and did not step out of the mourning hut for four years.
After the mourning began, Xunjiang stopped combing and washing his hair, and all his hair fell out.
He cried without timing, his voice became hoarse and then he cried silently, his eye sockets were all rotten, his body was haggard and emaciated, and he was so skinny that even his family no longer recognized him.
The prefectures and counties reported this situation to the court, and Gaozu Xiashao sent Zhongshushe to remove his mourning clothes and promoted him to the Zuo Changshi of the Yuzhang Kingdom.
Although Xunjiang had removed his mourning clothes, he was even more sad and haggard.
His grandfather Sun Qian told him: Your Majesty governs the world with filial piety, and your conduct exceeds that of the ancients, so I issued an edict to remove you from obedience and promote you to this position.
Not only is your father's order irresistible, but it will also make you famous in future generations. It's not just your reputation that will be made famous!
Xunjiang then accepted the official position.
In the end, he died at home due to grief and physical damage. He died at the age of twenty-one.
Yu Qianlou's courtesy name is Zizhen, a new savage.
Yu Yi, the father of Yu Qian Lou, was recruited as the chief secretary of Situ. He refused to take office, so he was famous.
Yu Qianlou was eager to learn since he was a child. He often discussed and recited the "Book of Filial Piety" with others. He never blushed in front of others because he couldn't answer an answer. Nanyang Gaoshi Liu Qiu and Zong Chai thought he was a genius and praised him greatly.
Yu Qianlou was recruited from his home to serve as the governor of the state, and moved to Pingxi to join the army.
He was also appointed as the county magistrate and had special achievements in governing the county.
summary: Xunjiang, from Yingyin, mourned his father and brother with such intensity that he lost his hair and eyesight. He was promoted by imperial decree but died at twenty-one from grief. Yu Qianlou, from Xinye, tasted his father's excrement to check his health and prayed to die in his father's place. He served as an honest official, refusing treasures, and died at forty-six.

translation:
Danyang Yin Wangzhi visited Jifu and asked him to stay in Danyang. He wanted to recommend him to the court as an outstanding person with filial piety at the beginning of the second year.
Ji Feo said: Wang Yin is so weird. Why do you think that I, Ji Feo, are so shallow?
If the father is humiliated, the son should die. Morality should be like this. If I accept Wang Yin's recommendation with a thick face and no shame, it will be to gain fame through my father. What a shame.
Ji Fei rejected Wang Zhi's request.
When Ji Fol was seventeen years old, he was called up to be the chief registrar of the state.
He was released from prison in Wannian County and served as county magistrate for one year. His education moved the people and benevolence and righteousness prevailed.
Ji Feo returned to Ying from Yong, and Liu Chen, the governor of Xiangzhou, summoned Ji Feo to take charge of the book.
Later, Pei Jian, a fellow countryman of Ji Ce, Danyang Yin Cheng Zang Dun, Yangzhou Zhongzheng Zhang Ping and others jointly recommended Ji Fe, thinking that he was filial, sincere and sincere, and he was proficient in "Yi" and "Laozi".
The emperor ordered Taichang to be commended and recommended.
At first, Ji Fol suffered from heart palpitations because his father was falsely accused of guilt, and later died of heart palpitations.
Zhen Tian, ​​courtesy name Yanyue, was born in Wuji, Zhongshan, and had lived in Jiangling for generations.
Zhen Tian's grandfather, Zhen Qinzhi, was appointed Chang Ningling.
His father selected him and Renzhou engaged in it.
Zhen Tian's father passed away when he was only a few years old. He was as sad and painful as an adult.
The family felt sorry for his young age and fed him rice with broth, but Zhen Tian refused to eat it.
When he was eight years old, he asked his mother about his biological father. He felt sorry for not remembering his father's image, so he cried sadly for several days. Suddenly, he seemed to see someone. The appearance of this person was his father. People at the time thought that this was filial piety that moved the gods.
His family is poor, but he feeds his mother with delicious dishes.
During the mourning time, a thatched cottage was built next to the tomb in the villa area. Black and yellow birds of various colors often gathered in the trees next to the thatched cottage. When Zhen Tian cries, the birds chirp, and when Zhen Tian stops crying, the chirping of the birds stops.
There was also a white sparrow perched on his thatched cottage.
Xiao Dan, the king of Shixing in the state, came to report Zhen Tian's virtue and performance.
The emperor went down to Shao and said: I admire sages with all my heart, think about my dreams all day long, and issue edicts to ministers from all over the world. I must do my best to search for, recommend and commend them.
Zhen Tian's filial piety is particularly outstanding, and her reputation is well-known in her hometown. This has many benefits for the honest and honest folk customs.
The magistrate presented the dispatches just as I saw them with my own eyes.
His whole family should be commended and he should be given a title.
Zhen Tian was appointed an official and went to Annan to join the army.
Han Huaiming, a member of the Shangdang Party, lived in Jingzhou.
When he was ten years old, Han Huaiming's mother suffered from tuberculosis, and each attack was often dangerous.
summary: Ji Feo, from Xiangyang, begged to die for his father, who was falsely accused. At fifteen, he beat the Dengwen drum and faced torture without flinching. His father was pardoned, but Ji Feo later died from heart palpitations. Zhen Tian, from Jiangling, mourned his father from childhood, with birds responding to his cries. He was commended by the emperor and appointed to a military post.

translation:
Han Huaiming was kowtowing and praying under the starry sky at night. It was very cold at that time. He suddenly smelled the fragrance. Someone in the air said to him: Little child, your mother will recover permanently in a while, and you don’t have to worry about it anymore.
Before dawn, his mother's illness had recovered.
The fellow villagers were surprised by this.
When Han Huaiming was fifteen years old, his father passed away. He was extremely sad during the funeral, almost to the point of destroying his life. He piled dirt on his back and made a grave, and did not accept any gifts or help from others.
After the mourning period expired, he and his fellow villager Guo Mo went to Nanyang to worship Liu Qiu as their teacher.
Liu Qiu once stopped teaching one day and was alone, crying sadly.
Han Huaiming secretly asked others why Liu Qiu was sad and alone. Liu Qiu's family replied: Today is the death anniversary of my grandfather's death.
Liu Qiu's mother had also died at that time.
When Han Huaiming heard about this, he stopped studying that day and went home to support his mother.
Liu Qiu sighed and said: Han Sheng no longer has the regret of not being able to support his parents like Qiu Wuzi.
Han Huaiming's family was poor, so he often tried his best to provide his mother with delicious food, and often laughed at his mother's side to make her happy. He would not leave his mother's side all day long.
When his mother was ninety-one years old, she passed away. Han Huaiming was deprived of water and food for ten days, howling and crying incessantly.
A pair of white doves built a nest on the thatched cottage where he was mourning. They laid eggs and raised small birds. They were very close to people, just like poultry. The white doves did not leave until the mourning period of Han Huaiming was over.
After the mourning period expired, Han Huaiming only ate vegetarian food for the rest of his life and did not change his clothes.
In the early years of Tianjian, Xiao Qi, the governor of Shixing, went to the court to commemorate Han Huaiming's filial piety.
Han Huaiming was called up many times by the state capital, but Han Huaiming failed to do so and died at home.
Liu Tanjing, courtesy name Yuanguang, was born in Lu County, Pengcheng.
Liu Tanjing's grandfather, Liu Yuanzhen, served as the prefect of Huainan and was convicted while serving in the county. Liu Tanjing's father, Liu Huijing, went to the court ministers to plead for mercy one by one. His feelings were sad and pitiful, and his words were very sincere, so he became famous for his filial piety.
Liu Tanjing practiced filial piety and possessed the character of his father.
Liu Tanjing first became an official and served as the Zuo Changshi of the Ancheng Kingdom. His father died in the county. He went to attend the funeral and did not eat or drink for many days. He fainted and regained consciousness many times.
Every time I cried, I cried until I vomited blood.
After the mourning period expired, he became thin and sick due to excessive grief during the mourning period.
It happened that the emperor issued the Shao Order, instructing the gentry to recommend talents according to four subjects. Liu Tanjing's uncle Liu Huifei recommended Liu Tanjing to be a filial scholar, and Gaozu appointed Liu Tanjing as the Haining Order.
Because his brother had not yet obtained the post of county magistrate, Liu Tanjing gave up the order of Haining to his brother, and the court then appointed him to join the army for the Anxi expedition.
After Liu Tanjing's father died, he served his mother with utmost sincerity and filial piety. He cooked the rice and porridge himself and did not leave the chores to others.
When his mother was sick, he took care of her day and night without taking any clothes off.
After his mother died, he went without food or water for nearly ten days.
His mother's coffin was temporarily buried at Yaowang Temple. The weather was cold at that time. Liu Tanjing, wearing single clothes, built a thatched cottage at the place where the coffin was buried to observe the mourning. He cried continuously day and night, and his grief moved everyone on the way. Within a year, Liu Tanjing himself passed away.
summary: Han Huaiming, from Jingzhou, prayed for his mother's recovery and heard a divine voice. He mourned his father excessively and served his mother with devotion. White doves nested at his mourning hut. He refused official posts and died at home. Liu Tanjing, from Pengcheng, mourned his father with vomiting blood and later served his mother with care, dying within a year of her death.

translation:
He Jiong, courtesy name Shiguang, was born in Dan County, Lujiang.
His father, He Huan, served as a doctor in Taizhong.
When He Jiong was fifteen years old, he followed his brother He Yin in his profession, and within one year he read through the general outline of the Five Classics.
He Jiong has fair skin and handsome appearance. His cousins ​​He Qiu and He Dian often praise him and say: "Wei Niushi has a clear mind, and Du Hongzhi has a beautiful appearance. Now when I look at the child, I seem to see Wei and Du again."
He Jiong often yearned for a quiet and retired life and was not willing to enter an official career.
He Jiongtang's uncle He Changyu said to him: "Why do you want to live in seclusion? You should not behave like this again."
Moreover, every gentleman has his own way of becoming an official and retiring from office.
When Yu Yan was nineteen years old, he became an official for the first time and held the owner's book.
He was recommended as a scholar, and was successively promoted to the royal palace to join the army, Shangshu Bing, and the second caolang of the Treasury.
He left the capital and served as Yongkang Ling, and was famous for his harmonious handling of affairs.
He returned to Beijing and served as the internal record office of Renwei Nankang King, and moved to the post of official secretary and censor.
Because his father was ill, He Jiong stayed naked for more than ten days without combing or washing his hair. He was busy serving his father. In two or three nights, his appearance suddenly changed a lot.
After his father passed away, He Jiong howled and cried constantly, sitting and lying on the ground, and sleeping with his head on the earth. As a result, his waist and kidneys were weak and his feet were swollen. Eventually, his body was destroyed by excessive grief and he died.
Yu Shami, a native of Yingyin.
The sixth generation grandson of Jin Si Kong Yubing.
His father, Yu Peiyu, served as the official governor of the state and the internal history of Changsha. During the reign of Emperor Shengming of the Song Dynasty, he was executed for being convicted of Yu Shami's affair. Yu Shami had just been born at that time.
When Yu novice was five years old, his biological mother made him a minor's dress, but he often refused to wear it. When his mother asked him why he refused to wear it, he answered with tears: Our family has suffered a tragic disaster, what's the use of sending things away!
After growing up, he wore civilian clothes and ate a vegetarian diet throughout his life.
Yu Shami was recruited from his family to serve as the Zuo Changshi of the Linchuan Kingdom, and moved to the Central Army Tian Caoxing to join the army.
When his aunt passed away and fell ill, Yu novice stayed by her side morning and evening, undressed, and sometimes needed acupuncture treatment, so Yu novice would test it on his own body first.
After his aunt's death, he had no food or drink for many days. Until the period of mourning is over, he does not take off his mourning clothes and does not leave the gate of the mourning hut. He howls and cries day and night, and the neighbors cannot bear to hear his cry.
My aunt's tomb was built in the new forest, and then there were more than a hundred unplanted pine trees growing beside the tomb.
Yu Yong, the official minister of the capital of Yushami tribe, reported Yushami's filial piety and recommended him to the subject of pure filial piety. Emperor Gaozu summoned Yushami, commended him for his filial piety, and appointed him as the replacement magistrate of She County.
After returning to Kyoto, he was given a light chariot by King Shaoling to join the military, and he followed King Shaoling in the palace of Kuaiji.
When his biological mother died again, Yu novice escorted the coffin back to the capital. When crossing Zhejiang, the ship encountered a strong wind in the center of Zhejiang and almost sank. Yu novice hugged his biological mother's coffin and howled bitterly. After a while, the wind dried up and the sea calmed down. This was probably because his filial piety moved the gods.
After the mourning period expired, Yu Shami was awarded the title of Xinwei Penal Prison and joined the army and Danyang County Koukou. He was repeatedly promoted to Ningyuan Lushi, joined the army, and was transferred to Sima.
He served as the Great Wall Order and died.
summary: He Jiong, from Lujiang, served his ill father without rest, changing appearance drastically. He died from grief after his father's death. Yu Shami, from Yingyin, refused fine clothes due to family tragedy. He served his aunt with devotion, and pine trees grew at her tomb. He was commended for filial piety and died in office.

translation:
Jiang Yu, whose courtesy name is Hanjie, was born in Kaocheng, Jiyang.
His father, Jiang Bei, served as doctor Guanglu.
Jiang Bian had a filial nature since he was a child. When he was thirteen years old, his father suffered from an eye disease. Jiang Biao served his sick father for nearly a year without taking off his clothes.
He dreamed of a monk at night who said: People suffering from eye diseases will definitely be cured by drinking Eye Wisdom Water.
Jiang Pu woke up and told the story, but no one could explain the meaning of "Hui Yan Shui".
Jiang Pu's third uncle Liao Zheng had a good relationship with Master Zhizhe of Caotang Temple, so he went to consult Master Zhizhe.
Master Wise said: "The Infinite Life Sutra" says: The wise eye sees the truth and can cross to the other side.
Jiang Hao followed the inspiration of the wise master and dedicated a house in Niutun, Tongxia County, as a temple, asking God to give him a good name.
The imperial edict replied: A loyal minister and a filial son are responsive everywhere.
Yan Han of the Jin Dynasty finally saw the medicine sent from the underworld.
I met a wise man recently and learned that your second son had a dream because of his sincerity, saying that he wanted to drink the water of wisdom.
Wisdom Eye is the name of one of the five eyes. If you want to build a temple, you can use Wisdom Eye as the name of the temple.
When they built the temple, they discovered an old well with clear water, which was different from ordinary spring water.
Jiang Bei took water from the well to wash her eyes and boil medicine according to what Jiang Xia saw in her dream. She gradually felt better and her eye disease was cured.
People at that time thought this was an expression of filial piety.
The King of Nankang was the governor of Southern Xuzhou, and he summoned Pi to be the chief official.
Dou Mian is quiet by nature, likes the mystical words of "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi", is especially proficient in the essence of Buddhism, and is not willing to enter an official career.
After his father passed away, Jiang Huai built a thatched cottage next to his father's tomb, howling and crying all day long. More than a month later, Jiang Pu also passed away.
Liu Ji, courtesy name Shiju, was from Pingyuan.
His grandfather Liu Chengmin was the governor of Jizhou during the Song Dynasty.
His father, Liu Wenwei, was a member of the imperial family during the Qi Dynasty.
When Liu Ji was nine years old, he could recite "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and his relatives were surprised by his talent.
When he was fourteen years old, his father died. Liu Ji had a natural sense of filial piety and cried until he vomited blood every time.
The family was poor, so Liu Ji and his younger brothers Liu Yao and Liu Di encouraged each other and devoted themselves to study.
After growing up, Liu Ji has been involved in a wide range of subjects and is knowledgeable and talented.
During the Tianjian period, Liu Ji was recruited from his home to serve at the court's invitation. He was gradually promoted to Xuanhui and joined the army in Jin'an Palace.
He also went to Beijing and served as Minister of Host and Guest. Within a year, he was appointed as the Order of Haiyan.
Liu Ji served as magistrate of two counties. During his tenure, he was known for his harmonious handling of affairs.
When he returned to the capital, he was appointed as Jian Kangzheng, but he did not like the position. He was soon dismissed because of illness.
Soon he was awarded the Jiankang Order, but he did not accept the appointment.
Liu Ji's mother, Mingshi, fell ill. Liu Ji was already fifty years old at that time. He served his mother untiedly for seventy days and recited the "Avalokiteśvara Sutra" ten thousand times. At night, he had a dream due to emotion. In his dream, he saw a monk saying to him: My wife's life span has been exhausted. With your sincerity and sincerity, I will extend your wife's life for you.
Liu Ji's mother passed away more than sixty years later.
Liu Ji built a thatched hut next to his mother's grave to mourn. His grief exceeded common courtesy.
There is often a pair of white cranes flying docilely beside the thatched cottage.
Ruan Xiaoxu, a virgin, wrote to him to comfort and enlighten him. But Liu Ji still missed his deceased mother endlessly, and died before the mourning was over. He died at the age of fifty-two.
Liu Ji is the author of eight volumes of "Explanation of Common Sayings" and ten volumes of collected works.
The deeds of his younger brother Liu Yao are in "The Biography of Literature", and the deeds of Liu Di are in "The Biography of Chu Shi".
summary: Jiang Yu, from Kaocheng, served his blind father, dreaming of "Wisdom Eye Water." He built a temple where an old well appeared, curing his father's eyes. He mourned his father excessively and died. Liu Ji, from Pingyuan, mourned his father with vomiting blood and served his mother, reciting sutras. White cranes appeared at his mourning hut. He died before mourning ended at fifty-two. Chu Xiu, from Qiantang, mourned his parents with extreme grief, fasting for twenty-three days and dying from weakness. Xie Lin, from Yangxia, refused food before his parents ate. He mourned his father excessively and later his mother, dying from grief at thirty-eight. The text concludes by comparing these individuals to ancient filial exemplars like Zeng Shen, noting that some, like Liu Tanjing, He Jiong, Jiang Yu, and Xie Lin, died from grief, similar to Ruqiu and Wu.

translation:
Wei Can, whose courtesy name is Changxi, is the grandson of Wei Rui, the cavalry general, and the son of Wei Gan, the governor of Northern Xuzhou.
Wei Can has the demeanor of his father, loves to learn, is willful, eight feet tall, and tall.
He first became an official and served as the king of Jin'an in Yunhui and joined the army. Soon he acted as Fa Cao and moved to join the army as a foreign soldier and concurrently as a Chinese soldier.
At that time, Ying! Yu Zhongrong and Wu Jun Zhang Shu were both well-known figures in the past. They were colleagues with Wei Can and had become close friends with each other.
The king of Jin'an moved to be the governor of Yongzhou, and Wei Can also followed the palace and was transferred to the record office, but his position as a military soldier remained unchanged.
King Jin'an was established as the crown prince, and Wei Can was moved to the rank of infantry captain. He entered the court and served as the leader of the East Palace. He resigned when his father died.
Soon he was reinstated as General Zhaoyuan. The army was appointed as the leader.
After the mourning period expired, he inherited the title of Marquis of Yongchang County and was appointed as a consultant to the king of Anxi and Xiangdong. He was repeatedly promoted to the prince's servant, led by Zuowei, and his position as leader remained unchanged.
Because Wei Can had an old friendship with the crown prince, he was often appointed to positions close to him. Although his position changed many times, he often stayed in the palace and served as a guard, which was quite prestigious. Moreover, Wei Can had an unruly and arrogant personality, so the celebrities at the time felt deeply unfair.
The right guard general Zhu Yi once said to Wei Can in a stern voice during a banquet: How can you put on the face of a leader and face others!
In the 11th year of Datong in Central China, Wei Can was moved to serve as a regular servant of Tongzhi Sanqi. Before he took office, he left the capital to serve as the governor, supervising the military affairs of Hengzhou, general Anyuan, and governor of Hengzhou.
The Crown Prince came out of the palace and was farewelling the boy. He took Wei Can's hand and said, "You and I won't be apart for a long time."
In the first year of Taiqing, not long after Wei Can arrived in Hengzhou, he petitioned to be dismissed.
In the second year, the imperial court recruited Wei Can as a regular attendant of Sanqi.
Wei Can returned to the capital and walked to Luling. When he heard about Hou Jing's rebellion, he selected 5,000 elite soldiers and 100 horses from his subordinates, and rushed to the capital day and night to rescue him.
When they arrived in Yuzhang, a messenger reported: The rebels have arrived at Hengjiang. Wei Can immediately went to the internal historian Liu Xiaoyi to discuss countermeasures.
Liu Xiaoyi said: If this is really the case, there should be another order. How can one send an envoy credulously and act in panic? Maybe this is not the case.
At that time, Liu Xiaoyi was giving a banquet to entertain Wei Can. Wei Can became angry, threw the cup on the ground and said: The rebels have crossed the river and are about to invade the capital. All water and land routes have been cut off. Where will there be messengers to return the favor? If the order is not issued, can you feel at ease?
How can I, Wei Can, think about drinking now?
After saying that, he immediately rode out and deployed his troops to prepare for departure. Just as Xiao Daxin, the governor of Dangyang in Jiangzhou, sent an envoy to invite Wei Can, Wei Can rode to see Xiao Daxin and said: Among the vassal towns in the upper reaches of the Yangtze River, only Jiang maggot is the closest to the capital. Considering the situation of His Highness, it is really necessary to go to the rescue first; but the position in the middle reaches is important, and your task of garrisoning Jiangzhou is important. Others also need your support to rescue the capital. Wei Guo cannot be left unattended.
summary: Wei Can, grandson of General Wei Rui and son of Governor Wei Gan, was a tall and learned man who served in various official positions under Prince Jin'an. He became close friends with Yu Zhongrong and Zhang Shu. As the prince rose to crown prince, Wei Can held several palace guard roles, though his arrogant nature caused resentment among peers. General Zhu Yi once rebuked him for his haughty demeanor. In 545, Wei Can became governor of Hengzhou, but resigned shortly after. Recalled in 546, he learned of Hou Jing's rebellion while traveling and rushed to the capital with 5,000 elite troops. After consulting with officials Liu Xiaoyi and Xiao Daxin, he coordinated with his cousin Liu Zhongli and General Pei Zhigao, eventually securing command for Liu. During battle at Qingtang, Wei Can ignored advice to hold position, ordered an attack, and was overwhelmed by Hou Jing's forces. He and his sons, brothers, and cousin were killed at age 54. The emperor mourned him deeply and posthumously promoted him.

translation:
Jiang Ziyi's uncle, Youwei General Sai Yu, was a powerful figure in the dynasty. Whenever he went home on vacation, his house would be crowded with guests, but Jiang Ziyi never came to visit him. His conduct was so noble.
Later, Jiang Ziyi gradually moved to the post of Minister Caolang, and went to Beijing to serve as the magistrate of Suichang and Qu'a counties, all of which achieved good political performances.
Jiang Ziyi was appointed as the Minister of Tongzhi Sanqi. He left Beijing and served as General Rongzhao and Colonel Nanjin.
Jiang Ziyi's younger brother Jiang Zisi once served as Shangshu Jinbulang. In the early years of his reign, he moved to Youcheng.
Both brothers have strong personalities.
Jiang Wangpan, as You Cheng, presented the seal to the court and spoke freely about the court's gains and losses. Gaozu appreciated it very much and ordered the minister to carefully examine it and choose the good ones for implementation.
Zuo Minlang Shen Jiong and Shaofu Cheng Gu Qi once scolded them sternly because of improper performance. Jiang Zisi quickly stepped forward to answer for Shen Jiong and Gu Qi. His words were very fierce and forthright. Gaozu angrily called for people to tie him up. Jiang Zisi fell on the ground and refused to be bound. Gaozu's anger subsided and he asked people to let him go. However, he was still convicted and dismissed.
Hou Jing rebelled, captured Liyang, and was about to cross the Hengjiang River. Jiang Ziyi led more than a thousand naval troops to intercept Hou Jing downstream. His deputy general Dong Taosheng, who lived in the north of the Yangtze River, fled with his accomplices.
So as soon as Jiang Zi retreated to Nanzhou, he gathered the remaining troops and hurried to the capital on foot from the alley.
The rebels soon arrived in the capital. Jiang Ziyi reported to Taizong: The rebels' encirclement has not been closed yet. We can try to break out. If we wait for them to build all the fortresses, then we will have no use.
Jiang Ziyi requested that he and his brothers Jiang Zisi and Jiang Ziwu lead more than a hundred soldiers to open the Chengming Gate and challenge the rebels. The rebels agreed.
Jiang Zi took the lead and rushed into the enemy camp alone with his sword. The rebels attacked him, and the people behind him did not dare to rush in. Seeing that the situation was critical, Jiang Zisi and Jiang Ziwu followed them and rushed into the enemy camp. All three of them were killed.
The emperor wrote to Shao Shu: The former general Rong Zhao, the minister of Tongzhi Sanqi, the Nanjin school captain Jiang Ziyi, the former minister Youcheng Jiang Zisi, and the commander-in-chief of the East Palace Zhidian Jiang Ziwu. I am deeply saddened by the news of their death. According to the original regulations, the awards and memorials for their sacrifices should be given a higher level.
Jiang Shang can be given posthumously as the Minister of Huangmen, Jiang Zisi as the Minister of Zhongshu, and Jiang Ziwu as the Minister of Sanqi.
After the Hou Jing Rebellion was settled, Shidan posthumously gave Jiang Ziyi the title of Shizhong and Mi's adopted son; Jiang Zisi's posthumous title of Huangmen Shilang and Mi's title Yizi; Jiang Ziwu's posthumous title of Zhongshu Shilang and Mi Mi's title Liezi.
Jiang Ziyi once continued to write "Huang Tu" and "Guang Jiupin", as well as dozens of poems, poems, rhymes and prose, all of which have been circulated in the world.
Zhang Sheng, named Sishan, was the son of Zhang Ji, the general of Zhenbei.
When Zhang Sheng was young, he behaved upright and elegantly, had ambition and integrity, and was able to talk about mysteries.
When his father was governing Qingzhou, he was killed by the local people. Zhang Zhu was so sad about the disaster at home that he ate vegetarian food and wore common clothes all his life, without holding a knife in his hand.
summary: Jiangzi, a seventh-generation descendant of Jiang Tong, was a studious and principled man from a poor family. He served as a county magistrate with distinction before becoming a court official. His brother Jiang Zisi served as Youcheng and once boldly defended colleagues Shen Jiong and Gu Qi during a court dispute, angering Emperor Gaozu but eventually being pardoned. During Hou Jing's rebellion, Jiangzi led naval forces to intercept the rebels but was betrayed by his deputy. He retreated to Nanzhou and then to the capital, where he proposed a breakout. He and his brothers Jiang Zisi and Jiang Ziwu charged into enemy lines alone and were killed. The emperor posthumously honored them with high titles. Jiangzi also authored works like "Huang Tu" and "Guang Jiupin."

translation:
The state promoted him as a scholar.
Zhang Sheng first became an official and served as Secretary Lang. He was repeatedly promoted to Prince Sheren, Xima, Situ Zuoxi, and Zhongshu Lang.
He left the capital and served as the internal history of Yongyang. After returning to the capital, he was appointed as the Sima of Xuancheng King of the Chinese Army and the regular attendant of Sanqi.
Later, he went to the capital to serve as the chief historian of Zhennan Yersai and the prefect of Xunyang.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, he was recruited and appointed as Taifu Qing, and soon moved to Wuxing Taishou.
In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged the capital. Zhang Sheng sent his younger brother Zhang Yi to lead thousands of troops from the county to rescue him.
In the third year of the Taiqing Dynasty, the palace city was captured. Shen Jun, the censor Zhongcheng, fled eastward and returned to his hometown. Zhang Sheng went to see him and said: Now the rebels are bullying the lord, and the country is in danger and the king is humiliated. This is the time for the ministers to serve loyally. Now I want to gather troops to defend your hometown of Wuxing.
If God does not bless me and my wish to be loyal and loyal cannot come true, I will have no regrets even if I die because of it.
Xuanjun replied: Although our Wuxing County is small, you resist the rebels with justice. Who dares not to obey!
Xuan Peng firmly encouraged Ji Yan to organize volunteers to resist the rebels.
So Ji Crocodile gathered his soldiers and built a city wall and fortress.
At that time, King Shaoling fled eastward to Bilu. When he heard about the Japanese incident, he ordered Zhang Yan to be appointed General Zhengshu in the name of the royal family and was given the official street of Jiuqing.
Zhang Sheng said: The imperial court is in a critical situation and the emperor has suffered humiliation. How do I feel about accepting the title of Wei Guangrong now?
He just left the document conferring an officialship from the royal palace.
The traitor Liu Shenmao from Xingtai captured Yixing. He sent envoys to persuade Zhang Sheng, saying: If you surrender early, you will still be made the county guard, and you will be given official rewards.
