Zhang Sheng ordered the envoy to be beheaded, and then sent the army leader Wang Xiong and others to lead his troops to meet Shen Mao at Yudu and defeated him. Shen Mao fled.
Hou Jing heard that Shenmao had been defeated, so he sent his central army officer Hou Zijian to lead 20,000 elite troops to help Shenmao attack Zhang Sheng. Zhang Sheng sent his army leader Fan Zhilang to the west of the county to resist, but was defeated by Shenmao and then retreated.
The rebel cavalry took advantage of the victory and burned the camp fence, and the defenders inside the fence collapsed.
Zhang Sheng took off his military uniform and sat in the hall. The rebels threatened him with a knife, but he still refused to give in.
So the rebels tied him up and sent him to Hou Jing. Hou Jing killed him in the capital market, and more than ten of his disciples were killed together with him. Zhang Sheng was sixty-two years old when he died.
After Hou Jing's rebellion was settled, Shizu posthumously awarded him the titles of Shizhong, Zhongwei General, and Kaifu Yitong.
He was given the nickname Zhongzhenzi.
Shen Jun, courtesy name Shuyuan, was born in Wukang, Wuxing.
His grandfather Shen Xian was a regular servant of Sanqi during the Qi Dynasty. There is a biography of Shen Xian in the history of Qi.
Shen Jun was erudite and talented when he was young. He served successively as the magistrate of Shanyin, Wu, and Jiankang counties, and had a reputation for being able to handle affairs.
He went to Beijing and served as Zhongshu Lang and Shangshu Zuocheng.
When Hou Jing besieged the capital, he moved to the post of censor Zhongcheng.
summary: Zhang Sheng, son of General Zhang Ji, was a virtuous and scholarly man who became a vegetarian after his father's murder. He held various official posts, including governor of Wuxing. During Hou Jing's siege of the capital, he sent troops to help. After the city fell, he organized resistance in Wuxing, defeating rebel Liu Shenmao. When Hou Jing sent reinforcements, Zhang Sheng's forces were overwhelmed. He refused to surrender, was captured, and executed at age 62. He was posthumously honored as Zhongzhenzi. Shen Jun, a learned official from Wukang, served as magistrate of several counties and later as censor. During Hou Jing's siege, he negotiated with the rebel leader, boldly condemning his treachery. Hou Jing admired his loyalty but later killed him after breaking through Zhang Sheng's camp.

translation:
At that time, reinforcements from all walks of life arrived near the capital, and Hou Jing petitioned to conclude an alliance, and the emperor agreed.
After the covenant was made, Qiang learned that a plague had broken out in the city, so he had treacherous intentions and delayed leaving.
Several days later, the Crown Prince ordered Shen Jun to go to Hou Jing's military camp. Hou Jing said: The weather is getting hotter. It's not the time to march. How can I leave with 100,000 troops?
I still want to serve the imperial court. You can apply for me. Shen Jun replied: The general's real intention in saying these words is to seize the palace city.
The troops and food in the city can still last for a hundred days. Your food reserves have been exhausted. The court's reinforcements are gathering outside. What will you use to feed one hundred thousand soldiers?
When you say these words, do you want to threaten the court?
Hou Jing put the knife across his knees and scolded Shen Jun with his eyes wide open.
Shen Jun sternly condemned Hou Jing and said: You are a minister of the imperial court, but you launched a mutiny and besieged the capital. The wise monarch has given grace to forgive your sins, and we have also concluded a covenant together. Now that the blood of the covenant has not been dried, you will regret it.
I am already sixty years old, and I am the envoy of the Emperor. I am determined to live or die by my fate. Am I afraid of the blade of a traitor like you?
After saying that, he went out without looking back.
Hou Jing said: This man is truly Sizhi who is loyal to the country!
Yet I still harbor a grudge against him.
After breaking through Zhang Sheng's camp, Hou Jing searched for Shen Jun and killed him.
Liu Jingli is the grandson of Liu Qingyuan, the third minister of Kaifu Yitong.
His father Liu Jin was appointed Prince Zhan Shi.
Liu Jingli and his elder brother Liu Zhongli were famous for their loyalty and bravery when they were young.
Liu Jingli was recruited from his family to serve as Zuo Lang, and gradually he was promoted to the governor of Fufeng.
When Hou Jing was crossing the river, Liu Jingli led 3,000 cavalry and infantry to rescue him. When he arrived near the capital, he defended Qingxidai and fought with Hou Jing many times. He often took the lead in charging into the city and gained far-reaching prestige.
After the palace city was captured, both Liu Jingli and Liu Zhongli went to see Hou Jing. Hou Jing sent Liu Zhongli to govern the upper reaches of the river, leaving Liu Jingli as a hostage and appointing him as a guard.
Hou Jing held a banquet for Liu Zhongli in Houzhu to see him off. Liu Jingli secretly said to Liu Zhongli: Hou Jing came to the banquet today. I hugged him tightly, so you pulled out your sword and killed him. I will die without regrets.
Liu Zhongli thought his words were very heroic and agreed to his request.
After drinking for a few rounds, Liu Jingli signaled Liu Zhongli with his eyes. Liu Zhongli saw that the surroundings were heavily guarded and did not dare to take action, so his plan failed.
Later, when Hou Jing was conquering King Xi of Jin Dynasty, Liu Jingli and Nankang King Xiao Huili discussed sending troops to attack the city where Hou Jing was guarding. They had agreed on a date to prepare for the uprising. Jian'an Marquis Xiao Bi knew about it and reported them, so Liu Jingli was killed.
Shi Chen said: Morality is more important than life, which is the admonition left by the ancient books. This is also the character valued by the sages.
summary: Liu Jingli, grandson of Liu Qingyuan, was known for bravery. He defended Qingxidai during Hou Jing's invasion, leading charges. After the palace fell, he plotted with his brother Liu Zhongli to assassinate Hou Jing at a banquet, but the plan failed due to heavy guards. Later, he conspired with Prince Xiao Huili to attack Hou Jing's stronghold but was betrayed and killed. The historian concludes that these men exemplified the principle of sacrificing life for righteousness, proving that the Liang Dynasty had loyal ministers.

translation:
In the past, the history books of Sima Qian and Ban Gu both compiled the "Biography of Sima Xiangru". Sima Xiangru did not participate in the major affairs of the Han Dynasty, so his articles are particularly famous for his biography.
Ban Gu also wrote the "Biography of Jia Zou Meilu", also because they could write articles and spread them to the world.
Fan Ye's "Book of Houmo" contains the "Biography of Wenyuan". The deeds of the people included in the biography have been recorded in great detail.
Formulating rituals and music, governing the country, understanding the past and present, recording good and bad deeds are all impossible without writing.
Therefore, no one who is a king and governs the world does not respect and value the function of articles; scholars among the Jin gentry also value and value the function of articles. This situation has not changed since ancient times.
Emperor Gaozu was both intelligent and virtuous, well aware of affairs, and had a vast empire. He went to Shao to seek liberal Confucian scholars and accepted talents with special knowledge. As a result, the ritual and music system flourished, and talents of all kinds gathered in the capital, glowing with dazzling brilliance.
Whenever Emperor Gaozu visited a place, he often ordered his officials to compose poems and essays. Those who wrote good poems and essays would be rewarded with gold and silk. Those who went to the palace to present poems and eulogies would sometimes be favored by being received.
Those literati with official titles, such as Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, etc., were all called excellent at the time because of their literary talent.
As for people like Pengcheng Daohang, Wu Xingqiuchi, Shuhai Wang Sengru, Wujun Zhang Shu and others, some of them were honored by the Wende Hall of Zhidai Shao, and some enjoyed the favor of the Shouguang Hall where the monarchs and ministers feasted. These are all outstanding and outstanding talents in the future.
Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, Wang Sengru and Zhang Sui are separately described according to their merits and achievements.
The collection was limited to the Taiqing period, and the deeds of talented and knowledgeable figures such as Dao Hang were collected into "Wenxue Biography".
To Hang, named Mao, was a native of Wuyuan, Pengcheng.
His great-grandfather came to Yanzhi and served as a general in the Song Dynasty.
When his father arrived in Jie, he was appointed Minister of the Fifth Army of Qi Dynasty.
Daehang was smart and alert since he was a child. When he was five years old, his father copied ancient poems on a screen. Daehang asked his father to teach him how to read them, and he was able to recite them immediately without forgetting the words.
When he grew up, Daohang was diligent and studious, good at writing articles, and was good at writing seal script and official script.
She is very beautiful in appearance and demeanor, and her behavior is loved by people.
During the Jianwu period of Qi Dynasty, after serving as an official in Han Dynasty, military law officer Cao joined the army.
In the early years of Tianjian's reign, he was moved to the post of Chief Registrar of Zhenglu.
When Emperor Gaozu first ascended the throne, he focused on recruiting and promoting outstanding talents. Emperor Gaozu admired Hang's talents very much.
After Emperor Gaozu established the crown prince, he ordered him to go to Hang to wash the prince's horses.
summary: The historical tradition of compiling biographies of literary figures, beginning with Sima Qian and Ban Gu, who included Sima Xiangru's biography due to his literary fame, and Fan Ye's "Book of Houmo," which detailed the deeds of literary scholars. It emphasizes the importance of writing in governance, ritual, and recording history, noting that rulers and scholars have always valued literary works. Emperor Gaozu of Liang promoted literature by rewarding poets and scholars, leading to a flourishing of talent in the capital. Notable literary figures like Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, and Ren Fang were celebrated for their skills, while others like Pengcheng Daohang and Wu Xingqiuchi gained favor at court.

translation:
At that time, the imperial court set up a bachelor's department in the Wende Hall, summoned talented and knowledgeable people to stay in the bachelor's department, and ordered them to revise the classics. Emperor Gaozu also sent to Shao to let Dahang enjoy the benefits of a general membership, and his name was registered in the family register, so he could enter and exit the palace.
At that time, Emperor Gaozu hosted a banquet in the Huaguang Hall and ordered the ministers to compose poems. Only one person, Shao, was ordered to write a long poem of 200 words, which was to be completed within three seconds.
Taohang stood at his seat and presented his improvisation, with beautiful diction.
Soon, he went to Hang to take charge of the secretary of the East Palace and the Youcewen of Sanqi Province with the post of washing horses.
In the third year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu ordered Shao to select Shangshulang who was honest, capable or talented and knowledgeable during his tenure and promoted him to the rank of Minister. When he arrived at Han, he was appointed as the Minister of Cao in the palace.
Daohang and his cousins ​​Daogai and Daoqia were both known as talented men. At that time, they all took turns holding positions in the palace, which was considered an honor by contemporary people.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, he moved to Hang and was appointed Prince Zhongsheren.
He was a man who did not boast of his own merits or talk about the merits of others. Le'an Renfang and Nanxiang Fan Yun both had a good friendship with him.
In this year, he was moved to Danyang Yincheng. Because he was ill and unable to take office, he was moved to Beizhonglang to consult and join the army.
In the fifth year of Tianjian, Daohang died during his tenure at the age of thirty.
Zhidan was deeply saddened by his death and issued an edict granting him twenty thousand dollars and thirty pieces of cloth to his family.
Daohang wrote more than 100 poems and poems.
Qiu Chi, courtesy name Xifan, was from Wucheng, Wuxing.
His father, Qiu Lingju, was famous for his talent. He became an official in Qi Dynasty and was promoted to Taizhong doctor.
Qiu Chi could write articles at the age of eight. Qiu Lingju often said that the momentum and strength of articles about making children are similar to mine.
Huangmenlang Xie Shuyi and Zhengshi Hedian both met Qiu Chi and thought he had excellent talents.
When Qiu Chi grew up, he was appointed as an official in the state, promoted as a scholar, and was dismissed from the imperial examination.
Qiu Chi moved to Sima Xing to join the army, but he left his post to mourn his father's death.
At the end of the mourning period, Qiu Chi was dismissed and awarded the title of Xizhonglang to join the army.
After his meritorious service, he was promoted to the position of Lang in the palace, but he left his post to mourn his mother's death.
After the mourning period expired, Qiu Chi was appointed as the palace minister, and then moved to the chariot and cavalry record to join the army.
When Emperor Gaozu pacified the capital and established the Bafu, Qiu Chi was selected as the Hussar Master and received very generous courtesy. At that time, the words to persuade the King of Liang to join the Liang Dynasty and to give the King of Liang special treatment were all written by Qiu Chi.
When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Qiu Chi was worshiped as the Minister of Sanqi, and soon moved to the position of Minister of Zhongshu, leading Zhongzheng in Wuxingyi, and Wende Hall of Waiting for Zhao.
At that time, Emperor Gaozu wrote "Lianzhu" by himself and ordered ten people to follow him. Among them, Qiu Chi's writing was the most beautiful.
In the third year of Tianjian, Qiu Chi came out of the capital to serve as the prefect of Yongjia County. Qiu Chi was incompetent in his duties in Yongjia County and was impeached by the officials. Emperor Gaozu cherished his talent and suppressed the memorial to impeach Qiu Chi.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, the general of the Chinese army, Xiao Hong, king of Linchuan, went on the northern expedition. Qiu Chi was appointed to consult and join the army, and headed the record office.
At that time, Chen Bozhi defected to Wei and joined the Wei army to resist the Northern Expedition. Qiu Chi wrote a letter to enlighten Chen Bozhi, and Chen Bozhi surrendered.
After returning to school, Qiu Chi was worshiped as Zhongshu Lang and moved to Situ to work as Zhongshu Lang.
In the seventh year of Tianjian, Qiu Chi died during his tenure at the age of forty-five.
The poems and poems written by Qiu Chi have been spread all over the world.
summary: The text then provides biographies of several scholars. Daohang, a native of Pengcheng, was intelligent from childhood, excelling in writing and calligraphy. He served in various official roles under Emperor Gaozu, who admired his talent. Daohang was known for his humility and friendships with contemporaries like Ren Fang and Fan Yun. He died at thirty, leaving over a hundred poems. Qiu Chi, from Wuxing, began writing at eight and was recognized for his talent. He held several official positions, including prefect of Yongjia, and was known for his literary contributions, such as writing letters that persuaded Chen Bozhi to surrender. He died at forty-five, with his works widely circulated.

translation:
Liu Bao, courtesy name Xiaochang, was born in Pengcheng.
His grandfather Liu Kuang was Sikong during the Song Dynasty.
His father, Liu Zhi, was the concubine of the crown prince at that time.
When Liu Bao was four years old, his father passed away. When he was six or seven years old, Liu Bao would often cry when he saw his uncles.
At that time, Liu Bao's uncle Liu Chan and uncle Liu Hui were already in high status. Liu Bao's mother thought that Liu Bao was crying out of fear and was very angry about this.
Liu Bao replied: I lost my father very early and did not remember his face. I heard that my uncle and uncle had very similar faces to my father, so I felt sad when I saw them and had no other meaning.
As he spoke, he sobbed again, and his mother became even more sad.
At first, Liu Bao's parents and two brothers died one after another, and they were all buried temporarily. When Liu Bao was sixteen, their coffins were moved to the cemetery. The planning and arrangements for the reburial were all done by Liu Bao alone, without the help of his uncles and uncles. It didn't take long for everything to be done. Liu Hui often praised him and admired his ability.
Liu Bao has been eager to learn since he was a child and can write articles.
When he first became an official, Cao Xing joined the army, but he did not take office.
In the early years of Tianjian, because he was the younger brother of the Princess of Linchuan, he was promoted from the war chief to the military meritorious officer of the Linchuan King. He also accumulated merit and was moved to the post of minister of Shangshu Kubu, Danyang Yin Cheng, Prince Taifu Cheng, minister of Shangshu Palace, and Nanxuzhou Zhizhong. He was dismissed because of official business.
After meeting for a long time, Liu Bao appointed the prince to wash horses, be in charge of the secretary, and serve as a lecturer in Shouguang Palace.
After Emperor Gaozu came to the throne, he selected young scholars with literary talents. Liu Bao, his cousins ​​Liu Xiaochuo, Liu Ru, Dao Gai from the same county, Dao Gai's younger brother Luo Qia, Dao Gai's cousin Dao Hang, Wu Jun Lu Chui, and Zhang Shu were all appreciated for their literary talents and often participated in the banquets of the monarchs and ministers. Although their official positions were different, the rewards they received were the same.
In the tenth year of Tianjian, Liu Bao passed away at the age of thirty.
When Liu Bao was about to die, he called his friends Nanyang and Liu Zhisheng to entrust him with the funeral arrangements and requested that the funeral affairs must be frugal.
Liu Bao had a reputation for being capable when he was an official, and he was gentle by nature. But he is upright in dealing with things, interacts with people, criticizes his friends' shortcomings and mistakes in person, praises their friends' strengths and virtues behind their backs, is frank in his feelings, and does not hide his privacy. His friends all praise him for this.
Yuan Jun, courtesy name Xiaogao, was born in Yangxia, Chen County. He was the eighth generation descendant of Wei Langzhong's order, Yuan Huanzhi.
Yuan Jun lost his father at an early age, but he devoted himself to studying. His family was poor and had no books. He often borrowed books from others to read, and he had to copy the borrowed books. He set a pace for himself, copying fifty pages every day. If the number of pages did not reach the specified number, he would not rest.
Yuan Jun's speech is dull, but he is good at diction.
When Emperor Gaozu's rebel army captured the capital, Xiao Hui, the king of Xianyang, was guarding Su'er in the east, and Yuan Jun followed the whole garrison and took charge of recording events.
summary: Liu Bao, from Pengcheng, lost his father early and showed filial piety by managing family burials alone at sixteen. He was learned and held various posts, including lecturer in Shouguang Palace. He was part of a group of young scholars favored by Emperor Gaozu for their literary talents. Liu Bao died at thirty, known for his upright character and frugal funeral requests. Yuan Jun, from Chen County, was orphaned young and studied diligently, copying books daily. He served in official roles and wrote "Guan Zhen," earning praise and silk from Emperor Gaozu. He also copied historical texts and composed "Xinque Ming" with Lu Jue.

translation:
In the early years of Tianjian, when the vassal state was established, he appointed Yuan Jun as his minister to follow him to guard Jingkou.
Wang Qian was appointed governor of Yingzhou and made Cao the capital of the army.
Gaozu was very fond of poetry. At that time, there was an endless stream of people submitting poems and essays to Gaozu in Nanque. Among them, the authors of poems and essays with gorgeous diction and appreciable words were sometimes rewarded or promoted.
In the sixth year of Tianjian, Yuan Locust imitated Dangbi and wrote "Guan Zhen" and dedicated it to Taizu.
Emperor Gaozu commended him and gave him five pieces of silk.
In addition to being appointed as a member of the Sanqi Shilang, Yuan Jun was appointed as a bachelor of the province. He copied twenty volumes each of "Historical Records" and "Moshu".
Following Emperor Gaozu's order, he and Lu Jue each wrote "Xinque Ming", but because the words were too long, they could not be included in the text.
Yu Yuling's courtesy name was Zijie. He was the younger brother of Qian Lou, who was often served by Sanqi.
When Yu Yuling was seven years old, he could discuss subtle principles with others.
As an adult, he was sharp-witted, knowledgeable and talented.
Xiao Zilong, the Sui King of Qi, was appointed as the governor of Jingzhou. He called Yu Yuling to be the chief bookkeeper and ordered him to copy and compile books together with Xie Tiao, Zong Yang and others.
Xiao Zilong was replaced in his post and returned to the capital. He also ordered Yu Yuling to be the master of farewell.
Xiao Zilong was killed by Emperor Ming soon after. Xiao Zilong's old staff and former officials avoided him out of fear. No one dared to deal with the funeral affairs. Only Yu Yuling and Zong Yang stayed to handle the funeral for Xiao Zilong.
Xiao Yaoguang, the king of Shi'an, was appointed to Fujun. He selected Yu Yuling to join the army and also serve as a recorder.
In the late years of Yongyuan, Yu Yuling was expelled and granted the title of Dongyang Sui'an Order. He was praised by the people and officials for his good management of the county.
In the early years of Tianjian, Yu Yuling was appointed as the official of Jiankang Prison, and he was moved to the post of Shangshu Gonglunlang, waiting for the imperial edict to Wende Hall.
He also left Beijing and served as a special driver in Xiangzhou, moved to the post of Huqi Lushi and joined the army, and also served as Zhongshu general secretary.
Soon after, he led the Zhongzheng of Nanjun County and worshiped him as the prince's horse washer. His position remained unchanged.
According to the old practice, the officials of the East Palace were all people known for their purity and elegance. Prince Xima, who was in charge of documents, was the most outstanding among them.
In modern times, the officials selected for the Shu Palace were all talented and famous scholars from aristocratic families. At that time, Yu Yuling, Yu Zhoushe and others were promoted to serve in the East Palace. Emperor Gaozu said: Appointment as an official requires a pure and elegant character, which cannot be limited to aristocratic families.
At that time, people thought this was a very accurate view.
Yu Yuling soon moved to the post of Minister of Sanqi and changed to the command of Dazhongzheng of Jingzhou.
He also accumulated merit and was promoted to the position of Minister of Huangmen of Zhongshu. His positions of Shiren and Zhongzheng remained unchanged.
Yu Yuling later left the capital and served as the chief historian of Jin'an King Xuanyi and the prefect of Guangling. He was responsible for the affairs of the prefecture and state, but was dismissed due to official business.
He was appointed as Tongzhilang, and soon he was awarded the title of Hongluqing, and also led the Dazhongzheng of Jingzhou.
Yu Yuling died during his tenure at the age of forty-eight.
Yu Yuling has ten volumes of collected works.
Yu Yuling's younger brother Yu Jianwu.
Yu Jian's name is Zi Shen.
He was able to compose poems when he was eight years old, and his elder brother Yu Yuling was particularly friendly to him.
Yu Jianwu first served as a permanent servant of the Kingdom of Jin'an, and then moved to the palace of King Xuanhui of Jin'an to join the army. From then on, every time the King of Jin'an moved the town, Yu Jianwu also followed the palace.
He successively served as the prince's lieutenant, Yunhui joined the army, and also joined the army as a secretary.
In the third year of Zhongdatong, the king of Jin'an became the crown prince, and Yu Jianwu also served as the general secretary of the East Palace. In addition, he was appointed as the official recorder of King Xiangshu of Anxi and joined the army. Soon he took charge of the Dazhongzheng of Jingzhou with his own official position.
After his meritorious service, he was moved to the post of Zhonglu Shi and consulted to join the army. The prince led the army to make more orders, and the prince became a concubine.
At the beginning, when Taizong was in the vassal state, he liked literary scholars very much. At that time, Yu Jianwuyu Shu Hai Xu Gao, Wujun Lu Dai, Pengcheng Liu Zun, Liu Xiaoyi, and Liu Xiaoyi's younger brother Liu Xiaowei were all appreciated and invited.
When Taizong became the crown prince, he also established the Wende Province and established bachelors. Yu Xin, son of Yu Jianwu, Xu Ling, son of Xu Go, Zhang Changgong of Wujun, Fu Hong of Beidi, Bao Zhi of Donghai and others were all outstanding talents who served as bachelors.
When Qi Yong asked next year, scribes Wang Rong, Xie Tiao, Shen Yue and others began to use the four tones changes in their articles, and new changes appeared when writing articles. By the time of Qi Yong, more emphasis was placed on the neatness of the rhyme, and more emphasis was placed on the beauty and beauty, and the requirements for the four tones in the articles were higher than before.
At that time, the prince wrote to King Xiangdong about this trend and said:
summary: Yu Yuling, from a scholarly family, was sharp-witted and served as a bookkeeper for Xiao Zilong. After Xiao Zilong's death, Yu Yuling alone handled his funeral, showing loyalty. He held various posts, including prefect of Guangling, and died at forty-eight, leaving ten volumes of works. His brother Yu Jianwu began writing at eight and served under the Prince of Jin'an, later becoming a scholar in Wende Province. He was part of a literary circle that included his son Yu Xin and Xu Ling. The text includes a letter from the prince criticizing contemporary literary trends for being weak and imitative, advocating a return to classical styles like those of Yang Xiong and Sima Xiangru. Wu Jun, from Wuxing, was a talented writer whose style was imitated as "Wu Jun style." He served under King Jian'an and wrote "Qi Chunqiu," which was criticized for inaccuracies and burned. He later worked on a "General History" but died before completing it, leaving numerous works. Other writers like Gao Shuang, Jiang Hong, and Yu Qian were also noted for their literary skills, with Gao Shuang's "Ode on Wok Fish" being particularly praised.

translation:
He successively served as the Prince of Yuzhang, Xuanhui, and the Prince of Linchuan, Zhongjun.
At first, Liu Zhao's uncle Liu Wei collected the "Books of Jin" from various schools to annotate Qian Shi's "Ji Ji", a total of forty volumes. By the time of the Han Dynasty, Liu Zhao also collected the differences in the "Books of Hou Mo" from various schools to annotate Fan Ye's "Book of Hou Mo". People at that time called the Japanese annotations extensive and comprehensive.
Liu Zhao moved to the post of Tongzhilang and left the capital to serve as Liu Ling. He died during his tenure.
Liu Zhao wrote 180 volumes of "Collected Comments on Houmo", 10 volumes of "Biography of Young Children", and 10 volumes of Collected Works.
Liu Sui, the son of Liu Zhao, was well-spoken and fond of learning, and was proficient in the "Three Rites".
During the Datong period, Liu Juan was appointed minister of the Shangshu Temple, but soon resigned and no longer served as an official.
Liu Sui's younger brother, Liu Sui, also known as Handu, has been famous since he was a child.
He once served as the royal secretary of Xiangdong in Anxi. At that time, there were many literary people gathered in the Xifu, among whom Liu Sui was at the top.
Liu Sui was dismissed and granted the title of Tongzhilang. Soon he moved to Zhennan and was appointed as the official recorder of the affairs of the King of Eastern Hunan Province. He also came with the government and died in Jiangzhou.
He Xun, courtesy name Zhongyan, was born in Tan County, Donghai.
His great-grandfather He Chengtian was the censor Zhongcheng during the Song Dynasty.
Grandfather He Yi was appointed Yuanwailang.
His father, He Xun, served as a lieutenant in the Qi Dynasty and joined the army.
He Xun could compose poems at the age of eight, and was elected as a scholar by the state at the age of 20. Fan Yun of Nanxiang saw the strategies written by He Xun and greatly appreciated them, so he and He Xun formed a lifelong friendship.
From then on, Fan Yun praised every article and poem written by He Xun after seeing it. Fan Yun said to those close to him: Looking at the poems and essays of these literati recently, the simple ones are like Confucian scholars preaching scriptures, and the extravagant ones are a bit immoral. The ability to contain the aura of heaven and earth and include the principles of modern and ancient times can only be seen in He Sheng's poems.
Shen Yue also liked He Xun's poems. He once said to He Xun: Every time I read your poems, I repeat them many times a day, and I still can't get enough of them.
He Xun was praised by celebrities to such an extent.
During the Tianjian period, He Xun took up an official position at home and was invited by the court to move to the Zhongwei Jian'an Wangshui Cao Xing to join the army and also serve as the recorder's office.
King Jian'an loved literary scholars and entertained and feasted with them every day. King Jian'an moved to Jiangzhou, and He Xun was still the secretary in charge.
He Xun returned to the capital and served as King Cheng of Anxi to join the military affairs and serve as Minister of the Ministry of Water. He resigned because of his mother's mourning.
When the mourning period expired, He Xun was dismissed and granted the title of Renwei Luling Prince Ji. He then followed the royal family to Jiangzhou, where he died not long after.
Wang Sengru of the East China Sea collected He Xun's poems and essays into eight volumes.
At the beginning, both He Xun's poems and Liu Xiaochuo's poems were valued by the world, and the world called them "He Liu".
Shizu wrote an article commenting on He Xun, saying: Shen Yue is the one who has many poems but shows his talent; Xie Tiao and He Xun are the ones who show his talent with few poems.
At that time, there was Yu Qian in Kuaiji, who was good at writing five-character poems. His reputation was equal to that of He Xun, and his official position was that of the minister of the kingdom.
Later, there were Kong Wenggui from Kuaiji and Jiangbi from Jiyang, both of whom served as the secretary of the Grand Sima Mansion of Nanping King.
Kong Wenggui was also good at poetry. Jiang Bi was erudite and talented in reasoning. He also wrote annotations for the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety.
Both men have collected works.
Zhong Rong, whose courtesy name was Zhongwei, was from Changshe, Yingchuan. He was the seventh generation descendant of Zhong Bi, a minister of Jin Dynasty.
His father, Zhong Chu, served in the Zhongjun Army during the Qi Dynasty.
Zhong Rong, his elder brother Zhong Xian and his younger brother Zhong Yu are all very studious, good at thinking and discerning.
Zhong Rong was born in the reign of Emperor Yongming of Qi Dynasty, and he was proficient in "Book of Changes". General Wang Jian of the Wei Army led the Emperor to offer wine to him. He admired Zhong Rong very much and highly recommended him.
Zhong Rong was promoted as a scholar of the state.
He first became an official and served as the minister of the kingdom, moved to Fujunxing to join the army, and left the capital to serve as the order of Anguo.
In the last years of Yongyuan, Zhong Rong was dismissed and allowed Situ Xing to join the army.
In the early years of Tianjian, although the etiquette and regulations were changed, things were busy and there was no time to spare. Zhong Rong wrote a letter and said: The cause of the chaos in the Yongyuan period was the arbitrary treatment of the imperial titles. Honors were not obtained by participating in wars, but officials were obtained by bribery.
By squandering gold and silver, one can obtain the rank of Jiuqing, by relying on letters of request, one can join the ranks of military officers, the streets will be full of riding captains, and the streets will be full of lieutenants.
Wearing the attire of an official, he still works as a slave; although his position is such as Huangmen, Sanqi, etc., he still personally undertakes the errands of the government officials.
summary: Liu Zhao, from Pingyuan, was intelligent and studied "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi" early. He annotated Fan Ye's "Book of Houmo" and wrote 180 volumes of commentary, along with other works. He died in office. His sons Liu Sui and Liu Su were also learned, with Liu Su serving as a secretary. He Xun, from Donghai, began writing at eight and was praised by Fan Yun and Shen Yue for his poetry. He served under King Jian'an and died in Jiangzhou, with his poems collected by Wang Sengru. He Xun was compared to Shen Yue and Xie Tiao, and his works were valued alongside Liu Xiaochuo's. Zhong Rong, from Yingchuan, was learned in the "Book of Changes" and served in various roles. He wrote a letter criticizing the misuse of official titles during the Yongyuan period, advocating for merit-based appointments. He later wrote "Poetry Criticism," a review of five-character poetry from ancient times to his era, discussing its evolution and key figures like Cao Zhi, Lu Ji, and Xie Lingyun. He died in office. His brothers Zhong Yan and Zhong Yu also held official posts and wrote works. Zhou Xingsi, from Chen County, was a prolific writer who served Emperor Gaozu, composing inscriptions and poems. He was highly valued by Gaozu and Ren Fang, and died at an unknown age, leaving over 100 volumes of works.

translation:
Zang Dun, whose courtesy name was Xuanqing, was from Ju, Dongguan.
His great-great-grandfather Zang Tao was the doctor Zuo Guanglu during the Song Dynasty.
His grandfather Zang Tanzhi was appointed Minister of Zuo Min.
His father, Zang Weizhen, was extensively involved in literature and history and was very talented. He was highly appreciated by his cousin Runan Zhou Yi when he was young.
At the end of the Song Dynasty, Zang Weizhen was recruited from his family to serve as the leader of the army and serve Emperor Wu of Qi.
After entering the Qi Dynasty, he successively served as Taiwei Jijiu, Shangshu Zhugulang, Jian'an Luling Second Prince's Palace Recorder, Former Military Cao Shi, Tongzhilang, Nanxuzhou Zhongzheng, Danyang Yincheng.
Emperor Gaozu pacified the capital, established the royal palace, and selected Zang Weizhen to serve as a hussar in the prison and join the army.
In the early years of Tianjian, Zang Weizhen was appointed as the Houjun Consultation Zhonglang and Nan Xuzhou Biejia. He also went to Beijing as Huangmenlang, and later moved to the right army Ancheng Wang Changshi and Shaofu Qing.
He came to Beijing to serve as the prefect of Xin'an and was known for his ability in handling affairs.
After returning to the capital, he served as the crown prince's concubine, Sinong Qing, and Taiwei Chief of History.
Zang Weizhen mourned her biological mother and built a thatched cottage next to the cemetery for three years.
After the mourning period expired, he was appointed Tingweiqing.
Zang Weizhen left the capital and served as Changshi of King Ancheng and Grand Administrator of Jiangxia. He died in office.
Zang Dun studied the "Five Classics" from the concubine Langye Zhuge Gu since he was a child, and he was proficient in analyzing chapters, sentences and explaining the meaning of the classics.
Zhuge Can's students often numbered from dozens to hundreds. Zang Dun got along with them every day, but never got close to them.
Zhuge Zhang admired him and sighed: This person is a great weapon to shoulder important responsibilities and a great talent to assist the emperor!
Zang Dun first became an official and served as Fu Junxing to join the army, and later moved to Shangshu Binglang.
He had a handsome demeanor, beautiful appearance, and elegant manners. Whenever he came to pay homage to him, Gaozu was very happy to see him.
Zang Dun entered Beijing and served as Zhongshu General Secretary Shiren, and was later appointed as An Youlushi to join the army, but Shiren's position remained unchanged.
Zang Dun had a filial nature. One day, while he was on duty with his father in Tingwei, his mother Liu was at home and suddenly fell ill and died in the middle of the night.
That night, Zang Dun suffered a sudden severe pain in the middle finger of his left hand and could not sleep. When dawn came, someone at home reported the news of his mother's death. The spiritual connection between him and his relatives had reached such an extent. Zang Dun mourned for his mother before his father died. Zang Dun stayed in mourning for five years without leaving his thatched cottage. He was so haggard and skinny that no one in his family could recognize him.
Wang Duan, a fellow countryman, reported the situation to the court. Emperor Gaozu praised him very much and sent people to comfort him many times.
After the mourning period expired, Zang Dun was appointed Yin Cheng of Danyang, transferred to Zhongshu Lang, and also served as Zhongshu Sheren, and later moved to Shangshu Zuocheng, Shu Zhonglang, Wuling Wang Changshi, conducted state affairs in the prefecture, and served as the governor of Kuaiji County.
After returning to Beijing, he was appointed as Shaofu Qing, led the infantry school captain, and moved to Yushi Zhongcheng.
Zang Dun has a strong and fair character and is very competent in the Yushi Mansion.
In February of the fifth year of Zhongdatong, Emperor Gaozu came to Tongtai Temple to lecture on Buddhist scriptures and held a conference for the four tribes of monks, bhikshunis, Upasakas and Upasikas. Tens of thousands of people attended the meeting.
During the meeting, the tame elephant presented by South Vietnam suddenly ran wild in the crowd. The emperor's chariots, horses, honor guards and people in the public gathering were frightened and fled. Only Zang Dun and Sanqi Lang Pei Zhili remained motionless and calm. Emperor Gaozu admired them very much.
Soon the emperor issued an edict and appointed Xian Dun as a regular servant of the Sanqi. Before Xian Dun was appointed, Gaozu issued another Shao order saying: The post of commanding the six armies cannot be given to people without talent.
Zang Dun, the censor Zhongcheng and the newly appointed Sanqi Changshi, is ambitious, loyal and prudent, knows people well and is cautious and thoughtful. He holds official positions fairly and fairly, and handles government affairs diligently and respectfully. He will definitely be able to handle military affairs well.
summary: Zang Dun, courtesy name Xuanqing, was from Ju, Dongguan. His lineage included notable ancestors: great-great-grandfather Zang Tao served as doctor Zuo Guanglu during the Song Dynasty; grandfather Zang Tanzhi was Minister of Zuo Min; and father Zang Weizhen, a talented scholar versed in literature and history, held various official posts under Emperor Wu of Qi and later under Emperor Gaozu of Liang, including Taiwei Jijiu, Shangshu Zhugulang, and prefect of Xin'an. Zang Weizhen mourned his mother for three years in a thatched hut by her grave and died as Grand Administrator of Jiangxia. Zang Dun studied the "Five Classics" under Zhuge Gu, excelling in textual analysis. Zhuge admired him as a future great leader. Zang Dun began his career as Fu Junxing to join the army, later becoming Shangshu Binglang. He was known for his handsome appearance and elegant manners, which pleased Emperor Gaozu. He served as Zhongshu General Secretary Shiren and An Youlushi. His filial piety was evident when he felt a sudden pain in his finger the night his mother died, leading him to mourn for five years in a thatched hut, becoming emaciated. Emperor Gaozu praised and comforted him. After mourning, Zang Dun held positions including Yin Cheng of Danyang, Zhongshu Lang, Shangshu Zuocheng, and governor of Kuaiji County. He became Yushi Zhongcheng, known for his strong and fair character. In 536, during a Buddhist lecture at Tongtai Temple, a tame elephant ran wild, but Zang Dun remained calm, earning the emperor's admiration. He was appointed Sanqi Changshi and later leader of the army, handling military affairs with intelligence and courage. He died in 543 at age 66, posthumously honored as Attendant.

translation:
He can also lead the army, and his position as a regular servant remains unchanged.
In the second year of Datong, Zang Dun was moved to the position of leader.
The leader is in charge of the military power of the country and is responsible for many affairs.
Zang Dun was smart, agile, well-informed, courageous, and good at handling complex government affairs, so all matters within his scope of responsibility were handled in an orderly manner.
During the Tianjian period, Wu Pinghou Xiao Jing held this position and gained an outstanding reputation. By this time, Zang Dun had succeeded Xiao Jing in gaining such a reputation.
In the fifth year of Datong, Zang Dun came to Beijing to serve as General Renwei and Governor of Wu County. He served for less than a year and petitioned to be dismissed due to illness.
He was appointed Guanglu doctor and was given a gold seal and purple ribbon.
In the seventh year of Datong, Zang Dun recovered from his illness and became the leading general again.
In the ninth year of Datong, Zang Dun died at the age of sixty-six.
On the day of his death, the emperor issued an edict to mourn for him.
Zang Dun was posthumously given the title of Attendant, and his position as leader remained unchanged.
The imperial court gave Shuyuan a secret weapon, a set of court clothes, and a set of funeral clothes? Coins and cloth were given in certain quantities.
Mi cup.
Zang Dun's eldest son Zang Changbo, named Meng Hong, served as the internal history of Guiyang.
The second son Zang Zhongbo was appointed Qu'aling.
Zang Dun's younger brother is Zang Jue.
Zang Jue, also known as Xianqing, was also known for his talent and magnanimity.
When he first took up his official position, he served as Xizhonglang and joined the army, serving as the chief guest of the Shangshu. Later, he entered Beijing and served as the general secretary of the Zhongshu, and was promoted to Zhengyuanlang and Hongluqing. His position as the general secretary of the Zhongshu remained unchanged.
He was moved to the position of Minister Youcheng. Before he could take office, he left the capital to serve as the prefect of Jin'an.
Jin'an County is located near the mountains and the sea, where escaped criminals often gather. Although the former county governor recruited sergeants to carry out raids, the thieves' intrusion could not be stopped.
As soon as Zang Jue took office, he preached enlightenment, and the criminals dragged their sons and daughters and their families out of their hiding places to join them. The local people resumed their normal business, the roads were smooth, and merchants and travelers continued to come and go.
However, Zang Jue believed in severe punishments and strict laws in handling political affairs and was unwilling to be lenient. Officials and people would be punished with rods for even the slightest mistake. The people called him "Zang Hu".
When Zang Jue returned to the capital, he was appointed as a hussar to the king of Luling, where he consulted to join the army and also served as a soldier.
Later, he was moved to serve as a regular servant of the Sanqi outside the Yuan Dynasty, and also as a minister of agriculture. His position remained unchanged.
In the eighth year of Datong, he died in office at the age of forty-eight.
When Zang Jue took office successively, the emperor ordered that all important matters in the official office and matters that the imperial censor Tingwei could not decide were handed over to him.
summary: Zang Dun's brother, Zang Jue, also talented, served as prefect of Jin'an, where he quelled crime through enlightenment but was known for harsh punishments, earning the nickname "Zang Hu." He died in office at 48. Emperor Gaozu valued his judgment, often entrusting him with difficult cases.

translation:
The pressure analysis and judgment should be accurate, thorough and reasonable. After Kuan Hao passed away, someone beat the Dengwen drum to complain, requesting that the case be handed over to Yue Jue, the upright Sheren.
Emperor Gaozu said: Zang Jue has passed away, so there is no one to entrust with this matter.
Zang Jue was understood and appreciated by Emperor Gaozu to this extent.
Xian Jue's son Zang Cao was appointed Sangong Lang of Shangshu.
Fu Qi, named Jingping, was from Lingzhou in the north.
His great-great-grandfather Fu Hongren was Taichang during the Song Dynasty.
Grandfather Fu Yan served as the Shanyin magistrate in the Qi Dynasty. He had the ability to manage political affairs and was promoted from the county magistrate to the governor of Yizhou.
Fu Xie's father, Fu Hui, was a member of the Shanyin and Jiankang orders during the Tianjian period. He was also famous for his talents and served as an official for consultation.
Fu Qi started out as a student of the Imperial Academy of Ming Dynasty. He first became an official and served as Zuo Changshi, King of Nankang. Later, he moved to join the army and served as minister of Jinbulang. He resigned due to the death of his mother, and he did all the etiquette of mourning with all his heart.
After the mourning period expired, he did not serve for a long time due to illness.
During the Han Dynasty, the imperial court rebuilt the altar in the northern suburbs and began to appoint Fu Qi to supervise the construction. After the project was completed, the imperial court appointed him as the new order.
Some people in Shixin County fought with each other and died. The family members of the deceased went to the county to file a complaint. The county guard arrested their enemy and tortured him in every possible way. The man still refused to plead guilty. The county guard transferred the case to Shixin County for trial. Fu Qi immediately ordered the handcuffs to be removed and asked the criminal gently, and the man immediately pleaded guilty.
According to the law, the criminal should be sentenced to pay for his crime with his life. It happened to be the winter solstice, so Fu Qi let the criminal go home for reunion and let him return to prison after the winter solstice.
The county official refused to release him and argued with Fu Qi: "This was done in ancient times, but it cannot be practiced now."
Fu Qi said: If he is not trustworthy, I, the county magistrate, should be punished. You, the supervisor, don't worry.
The criminal returned as scheduled.
The prefect was amazed by this incident and immediately reported it in detail.
Later, when Fu Qili established a new county, all the people, young and old, left the country to say goodbye. The sound of crying could be heard dozens of miles away.
Fu Qi arrived in the capital and was appointed Tingweizheng. He entered the court and served as Zhongshu General Secretary and Shiren. He also moved to the Ningyuan Yueyang Prince's Office to join the army, but his position as Shiren remained unchanged.
Fu Qi left the capital to serve as Jiankang Order, but was dismissed due to official duties.
Soon after, he was appointed as a secretary. After repeated promotions, he was promoted to the Anxi Zhongji Office. He consulted in Zhennan to join the army, but his position as a concurrent secretary remained unchanged.
Fu Qi has a handsome appearance, a smart manner, a wide range of interests, and fluent answers.
During the Datong period, the imperial court made peace with the State of Wei. Envoys from the State of Wei came twice a year, and the emperor often sent Fu Qi to receive them.
In the first year of the Taiqing Dynasty, he was promoted to the rank of Imperial Servant and Minister of Agriculture, but his position remained unchanged.
summary: Fu Qi, courtesy name Jingping, from Lingzhou, had ancestors like Fu Hongren (Taichang) and father Fu Hui (Shanyin magistrate). Fu Qi started as a student, served as Zuo Changshi, and later as Jinbulang. He resigned to mourn his mother. He supervised the northern suburbs altar construction and became Shixin county magistrate, where he released a criminal on the winter solstice, who returned as promised, earning the prefect's praise. He served as Tingweizheng, Zhongshu General Secretary, and Jiankang Order. During the Datong period, he received Wei envoys. In 547, he opposed peace with Wei, warning it would alienate Hou Jing and cause rebellion, but Emperor Gaozu followed Zhu Yi's advice. Hou Jing rebelled in 548, and Fu Qi's predictions proved correct. He refused a marquis title and died at home after Miyagi fell. Yao Cha praised Fu Qi's foresight, noting that if his advice had been heeded, the Taiqing chaos might have been avoided.

translation:
Wang Sengbian, also known as Juncai, was the son of Youwei General Wang Shennian.
During the Tianjian period, Wang Sengbian came to join his father.
He was recruited from his family and served as the Zuo Changshi of the Xiangdong Kingdom.
King Xiangshu was appointed Danyang Yin, and Wang Sengbian was transferred to Fu Xing to join the army.
King Shu of Hunan was appointed as the prefect of Kuaiji, and Wang Sengbian also served as a soldier in the military.
King Xiangshu was appointed governor of Jingzhou, and Wang Sengbian was still appointed as a soldier in the army and held a confidential position.
At that time, Wuning County was in rebellion, and King Xiangdong ordered Wang Sengbian to attack and quell the rebellion.
Wang Sengbian was moved to the post of General Zhenwei and Prefect of Wuning.
Soon he was moved to the post of General Zhenyuan and Grand Administrator of Guangping.
After his term of office expired, Wang Sengbian returned to the Prince of Xiangshu and served as a recorder of affairs in the palace, and his position in the army remained unchanged.
The king of eastern Hunan was conscripted into the capital to serve as a military guard, and Wang Sengbian also served as the Sima of the palace.
The king of eastern Hunan was appointed governor of Jiangzhou, and Wang Sengbian was subsequently appointed as General Yunqi, Sima, and governor of Huancheng.
Soon he moved to oversee Anlu County, and returned to the palace not long after.
Soon he was appointed governor of Xincai, still holding the post of Sima, and his title of general remained unchanged.
King Shu of Xiang was appointed as the prefect of Jingzhou. Wang Sengbian consulted for General Zhenyi's office and joined the military. He was given food for a thousand people. He replaced Liu Zhongli as the prefect of Jingling and changed his title to General Xiongxin.
When Hou Jing rebelled, the king of eastern Hunan ordered Wang Sengbian to go on holiday. The governor sent 10,000 naval troops to aid the capital with food supplies.
When Monk Wang arrived at the capital, the palace was captured and the emperor was humiliated.
Wang Sengbian, Liu Zhongli brothers, Tang Bochao and others first surrendered to Hou Jing, and then entered the palace to see the emperor. Hou Jing confiscated all their weapons and food, and deeply comforted them.
Not long after, Hou Jing sent Wang Sengbian back to Jingling. Wang Sengbian then doubled his travels, traveling day and night, and went west to join Shizu.
Shizu followed the emperor's will and appointed Wang Sengbian as the leading general.
There was a rift between the governor of Jingzhou, King Xiangdong, and the governor of Xiangzhou, King Hedong. They were suspicious of each other, and the army could not be commanded in a unified manner. The emperor ordered Wang Sengbian and Bao Quan to lead the army to attack them, allocate enough military rations, and set a date for departure.
At that time, Wang Sengbian planned to wait for all of Jingling's men to gather before moving forward together because not all of Jingling's men had arrived.
Wang Sengbian said to Bao Quan: You and I accepted the order to march southward, but the army formation is so uneven. What are your plans?
Bao Quan said: Since we have accepted the imperial court's war plan and led our brave soldiers to kill the enemy, the situation is like pouring hot water on snow, so why should we worry more?
Monk Wang argued: What you said is wrong.
What you are saying is nothing more than a truism from scribes.
The King of Hedong had military talent when he was young, and his weapons and equipment were very strong. He had just defeated our army and was now recharging his strength, waiting for us to attack. Without ten thousand elite soldiers, it would not be enough to defeat them.
The Jingling soldiers under my leadership have experienced many battles. I have sent people to summon them and will arrive soon.
summary: Wang Sengbian, son of General Wang Shennian, began his military career during the Tianjian period, serving under various princes in positions such as Zuo Changshi and military advisor. He quelled a rebellion in Wuning County and held several governorships, including Wuning, Guangping, and Anlu. When Hou Jing rebelled, Wang Sengbian led 10,000 naval troops to aid the capital, but the palace was captured. He briefly surrendered to Hou Jing before rejoining Shizu (Emperor Yuan of Liang). Ordered to attack the governor of Xiangzhou, Wang Sengbian delayed departure due to insufficient troops, angering Shizu, who struck him with a sword and imprisoned him. He was later pardoned to defend against King Yueyang's attack, successfully defeating him and replacing Bao Quan to pacify Xiangzhou.

translation:
The ancestors discussed meritorious deeds and rewarded him, and ordered Wang Sengbian to be the general of the East Conquest, the third division of Kaifu Yitong, the governor of Jiangzhou, and the title of Duke of Changning County.
So Shizu ordered Wang Sengbian to immediately lead all the troops in Baling and go down the river to conquer Hou Jingliang.
The army was stationed in Yingcheng and sent infantry to attack Lushan.
Zhi Huaren, the chief defender of Lushan City, was a cavalry officer under Hou Jing. He led his followers to fight with all their strength, but was still severely defeated by Wang Sengbian's army, so Zhi Huaren surrendered.
Wang Sengbian then led various troops to cross the river to attack Ying, and immediately entered Ying's outer city.
Song Zixian gathered all his men and horses to defend the inner city, but Wang Sengbian attacked the city but failed to capture it.
Song Zixian sent his subordinate Tong Xihu to lead 3,000 troops to open the city gate and go out to fight. Wang Sengbian defeated the rebels who left the city, captured Di Xihu alive, and killed more than a thousand people.
Sai Zixian led his army to retreat and defend, relying on the natural dangers to defend around Liao. Wang Mengbiao led his troops to attack repeatedly but failed to conquer it.
Hou Jing heard the news that Lushan had been captured and that the outer city of Ying, an important town, had been lost, so he led the remaining troops to return to Jianye day and night.
Song Zixian and others were in a difficult situation and had nothing to do, so they asked Wang Sengbian to hand over Yingcheng and let him lead his troops back to Hou Jing.
Wang Sengbian pretended to agree to them and ordered more than a hundred ships to be provided to the rebels, thereby paralyzing the rebels.
Song Zixian thought that Wang Sengbian was sincere in letting them go, and when the boat was about to set off, Wang Sengbian ordered Du Chong to lead a thousand capable warriors, climb the city wall, beat drums and shout at the same time, and suddenly attack the warehouse gate.
He ordered Song Yao, the leader of the naval force, to lead a large ship and secretly surrounded Song Zixian's fleet on the river from all sides. Song Zixian fled while fighting. When they arrived at Baiyangpu, Wang Sengbian's army defeated Song Zixian's rebels, captured Song Zixian alive, and sent him to Jiangling.
Wang Sengbian immediately led various armies to march into Jiushui.
The rebels and puppet officials, Fan Xirong and Lu Huilue, still occupied Huancheng. When Wang Sengbian and his troops arrived, Fan Xirong and others took Jiangzhou Governor Lincheng Gong hostage and fled the city.
Shizu gave Wang Sengbian additional official positions such as Shizhong, Shangshu Ling, and General of the Eastern Conquest, and also gave him the Department of Advocacy.
Then he ordered Wang Sengbian to temporarily garrison Jiangzhou until all the troops were concentrated and he got the opportunity before attacking.
Soon, Shizu ordered people from all walks of life in Jiangzhou to launch a massive attack. Wang Sengbian then announced the bad news of the emperor's death and reported the bad news to Shizu in Jiangling.
So he led more than a hundred generals to jointly write a letter to Shizu, urging Shizu to take the throne as emperor. When he was about to march against Hou Jing, he wrote again to persuade him to advance.
Although Shizu did not listen, he received a graceful reply from Shizu.
The incident was recorded in the "Benji" of Emperor Shizu Xiaoyuan.
Wang Sengbian then set out from Jiangzhou and aimed directly at Jianye. He first ordered Hou Tian, ​​the governor of Nanyanzhou, to lead his elite soldiers in a light fast boat to attack Nanling, Quetou and other garrison posts. Wherever they went, they immediately captured them.
Prior to this, Chen Baxian led 50,000 men and set out from Nanjiang, sending 5,000 men as the vanguard and had already arrived at Fankou.
Chen Baxian had outstanding talents and was good at strategy. His reputation surpassed that of Wang Sengbian, and Wang Sengbian respected him.
After Chen Baxian arrived at Fankou, he met Wang Sengbian at Baimaozhou. The two went to the altar and swore an oath of alliance. Chen Baxian wrote an alliance article saying:
summary: Wang Sengbian then defended Baling against Hou Jing's invasion, employing strategies like sinking ships and stockpiling supplies. Despite fierce assaults, including fire attacks and siege equipment, the rebels were repelled. Rewarded as General of the East Conquest and Duke of Changning, he led forces to capture Lushan and Yingcheng, defeating Song Zixian and capturing him alive. He advanced to Jiushui, and after learning of the emperor's death, urged Shizu to take the throne. Marching toward Jianye, he allied with Chen Baxian at Baimaozhou, swearing an oath to destroy Hou Jing. Their combined forces defeated the rebels at Stone City, and Hou Jing fled. Wang Sengbian captured rebel leaders and restored order, earning the title of General of the Town Guard and Situ. Later, Wang Sengbian suppressed the rebellion of Lu Na in Xiangzhou, using cautious tactics to surround and defeat him. He then guarded against Qi invasions, defeating their forces at Dongguan. After his mother's death, he received honors and a eulogy from the emperor. When Western Wei attacked Jiangling, Wang Sengbian was summoned but failed to arrive before the capital fell. He supported Emperor Jing and negotiated with Qi to accept Xiao Yuanming as emperor, sending hostages and meeting him at Jiangningpu. This led to conflict with Chen Baxian, who attacked Jiankang. Wang Sengbian, caught off guard, was captured and killed by Chen Baxian. His sons met various fates: Wang Chan died early, Wang Jie fled to Qi, Wang Hao died of grief, and Wang Ban was captured by Western Wei. The historian notes that despite his merits, Wang Sengbian's decision to install a puppet emperor under Qi coercion led to his downfall.

translation:
The Han Dynasty took the burning books of the Qin Dynasty as a warning and vigorously promoted Confucianism. The number of students in Taixue often reached more than 10,000, and the schools in various prefectures and states were also fully staffed. The schools were located in the mountains and fields, and even shops and markets were opened close to the schools. The prosperity of the schools reached such an extent.
At the end of the Han Dynasty, the political situation was turbulent, and Confucianism declined.
After the Zhengshi period of the Wei Dynasty, the Taoist theory of Xuanyuan Nihility was gradually advocated, and therefore fewer people studied Confucianism.
At that time, Xun Pin, Zhi Yu and others, although they deleted new rituals and changed official positions, they could not change the customs.
After the founding of the People's Republic of China, the Central Plains was in turmoil and even fell. All civilization and ethics were ruined. The Jin Dynasty moved to Jiangzuo. Everything was being created. The country was busy with affairs and had no time to run schools. In the Song and Qi Dynasties, Chinese studies were sometimes opened, but there was no extensive encouragement and supervision. The establishment time was less than ten years, but they were abandoned for many years. Because the state only provided empty provisions in the regulations for the establishment of schools, they were suddenly abandoned.
There are no schools in each township, and few ministers are proficient in the classics. The great scholars in the court only practice the classics themselves but refuse to teach students. The young people are ignorant and have no place to study and study the classics. The three virtues and six arts have been neglected for a long time.
After Emperor Gaozu became emperor, he was deeply saddened and worried about this situation, so he issued an edict to search for knowledgeable scholars, rectify the five rituals, approve the six laws, revise the calendar, and correct the balance.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu issued an edict saying: There are no wise men in the two deserts who have not taught Confucianism by virtue of their classics and skills, and have established a good reputation and achieved moral success.
In the Wei and Jin dynasties, the atmosphere was turbulent and Confucian learning declined. Perhaps because of this, the moral integrity could not be established.
I leave the court very late every day, just because I want to hear news about talented people. If you appoint talented people to get talented people, you should be rewarded.
Doctors on the Five Classics should be established, with one doctor for each classic, and schools should be established widely to accept young people to study.
So Pingyuan Mingshanbin, Wu Jun Lu Lian, Wu Xing Shen Jun, Jianping Yan Zhizhi, Kuaiji Hechang, etc. were appointed as replacement doctors, and each of them presided over a school.
There were hundreds of students in the academy, and the imperial court provided them with salaries.
Among them, those who choose things to report, if they are enlightened and wise, will be awarded as officials.
For more than ten years, people who were proficient in Confucian classics and well-read in Confucian classics gathered in the capital.
He also selected students to go to Yunmen Mountain in Kuaiji and study with He Yin in Lujiang.
Doctors were sent to each state and county to establish schools.
In the seventh year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu issued another edict: To establish a country and be the monarch of all people, establishing enlightenment and promoting education are the most important things; cultivating knowledge and sharpening virtues, classics study is the must way.
I have established a foundation that has spread throughout the world. Although I have worked hard to develop Confucianism, there are not many talented people, and the virtues are still lacking. It is not enough to cultivate the princes and nobles and make them obey the laws of Confucianism. I want to encourage them to respect their elders, practice it at home, and then become a model for the world.
Wherever the prestige is now, the Rong people in China are also inspired. They should vigorously open schools and widely recruit the children of the royal family and nobles to practice the ten ethics and promote the three virtues, so that the imperial education can be spread far and wide, and the exquisite words can be promoted.
So the crown princes, princes, royal families, and princes began to study in schools.
In vain, Emperor Gaozu condescended to go to the school in person to pay tribute to Zizi and other saints of the previous generation, talk to the students, encourage them, and comfort them with silk. The school was solemn and the students were numerous, and the journey of the Great Way reached such a prosperous level.
summary: The Han Dynasty, learning from the Qin Dynasty's book burning, vigorously promoted Confucianism, with the Imperial Academy often hosting over ten thousand students and schools flourishing even in remote areas. However, at the end of the Han Dynasty, political turmoil led to Confucianism's decline. During the Wei Dynasty's Zhengshi period, Taoist philosophy gained prominence, reducing interest in Confucianism. Figures like Xun Pin and Zhi Yu attempted reforms but failed to change customs. After the Jin Dynasty's founding, the Central Plains fell into chaos, and the court moved south, leaving no time for education. During the Song and Qi Dynasties, schools were sporadically opened but quickly abandoned, with no sustained encouragement. Local schools vanished, ministers rarely mastered the classics, and young people had no means to study. The three virtues and six arts were neglected for a long time. Emperor Gaozu of Liang, deeply concerned, issued edicts to seek scholars, rectify rituals, revise laws, and correct standards. In the fourth year of Tianjian, he decreed the establishment of Five Classics doctors, one per classic, and the widespread opening of schools. Scholars like Pingyuan Mingshanbin, Wu Jun Lu Lian, Wu Xing Shen Jun, Jianping Yan Zhizhi, and Kuaiji He Chang were appointed as doctors, each presiding over a school. Hundreds of students received salaries from the court, and those who excelled were appointed as officials. Over a decade, many proficient in Confucian classics gathered in the capital. Students were also sent to study with He Yin in Kuaiji. In the seventh year of Tianjian, Emperor Gaozu further decreed the promotion of education, encouraging the children of nobles to study the ten ethics and three virtues. The crown prince, princes, and nobles began attending schools, and the emperor personally visited to honor sages and encourage students. The school became solemn and prosperous, with scholars like Fu Manrong, He Tongzhi, and Fan Zhen gaining fame.

translation:
Among them, Fu Manrong, He Tongzhi and Fan Zhen were already famous in contemporary times; among the famous Confucian scholars at that time, Yan Zhizhi, He Yu and others were among the top candidates.
Now the deeds of these people are connected together and compiled into "The Scholars".
Fu Manrong, courtesy name Gongyi, was born in Anqiu, Pingchang.
His great-grandfather Fu Tao was a scholar in the Jin Dynasty.
His father Fu Yinzhi was the chief secretary of Sikong during the Song Dynasty.
Fu Manrong lost his father very early, and he lived in the South China Sea with his mother and brother.
Fu Manrong has been attentive and studious since he was a child, and he is proficient in "Laozi" and "Book of Changes". He is bold and free and likes to exaggerate. He once said: He Yan has questions about nine things in "Yi". From my perspective, He Yan does not study at all, so I know that Uncle He Ping has shortcomings.
Fu Manrong gathered students to teach them their studies and regarded this as his profession.
Fu Manrong Ren Piao rode to join the army.
Emperor Ming of the Song Dynasty loved "The Book of Changes" and gathered courtiers to discuss the "Book of Changes" in the Qingshu Palace. He ordered Fu Manrong to hold the scriptures and answer questions.
Fu Manrong was very beautiful in appearance and manners. Emperor Ming of the Song Dynasty often compared him with Ji Shuye. He also ordered the Wu man Lu to explore the portrait of Ji Shuye in Weizhou and give the portrait to Fu Manrong.
Fu Manrong moved to Situ to join the army.
When Yuan Can was appointed Danyang Yin, he requested that Fu Manrong be appointed as Jiangning Order. Fu Manrong entered the capital and was awarded the title of Shangshu Waibinglang.
At the end of the Ming Dynasty, he served as the governor of the auxiliary state and the governor of Nanhai.
In the early years of the Qi Dynasty, he served as the minister of Tongzhi Sanqi.
In the early years of the Yongming Dynasty, he led the crown prince's orders and served the crown prince.
General Wei Wang Jian and Fu Manrong were very friendly and had a deep friendship. Wang Jian ordered Fu Manrong to co-write the "Mourning Clothing Yi" with Sima Xian of Hanoi and Wujun Lu Cheng. After writing the "Mourning Clothing Yi", Wang Jian wanted to review the rituals and music with Fu Manrong.
Coinciding with Wang Jian's death, Fu Manrong was promoted to Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Sima, and joined the army. He also left the capital to serve as the prefect of Wuchang.
During the Jianwu period, Fu Manrong entered Beijing and was awarded the title of Zhongsan doctor.
At that time, Emperor Ming did not attach great importance to Confucianism, and Fu Manrong's residence was beside Waguan Temple. Fu Manrong set up a high seat in the hall of his home. When guests came, he would climb on the high seat and lecture on the scriptures to them. There were often dozens or hundreds of students gathered to listen to the lectures.
Liang Guotai Mansion was established. Because Fu Manrong was a great Confucian scholar with a high reputation, Emperor Gaozu summoned him to worship him as Sima and as the prefect of Linhai.
In the first year of Tianjian, Fu Manrong died during his tenure at the age of eighty-two.
Fu Manrong is the author of "Annotation of Zhouyi", "Annotation of Mao's Poems", "Annotation of Mourning Clothes", "Laoziyi", "Zhuangziyi" and "On Semantics".
The deeds of Fu Manrong's son Fu Qu are in "The Biography of Good Officials".
He Tong, whose courtesy name was Shiwei, was from Sa County, Lujiang. He was the sixth-generation grandson of He Pang, the governor of Yuzhou.
His grandfather He Shaozhi was a member of the imperial court during the Song Dynasty.
His father, He Xin, was invited to the court by Qi Shi.
summary: Fu Manrong, from Anqiu, lost his father early and lived with his mother and brother in the South China Sea. He was studious, proficient in Laozi and the Book of Changes, and bold in speech. He gathered students to teach and held various official positions, including Piaoqi Canjun and Nanhai Prefect. During the Qi Dynasty, he served as Tongzhi Sanqi Changshi and later as Zhongshu Lang. He was known for lecturing on scriptures at home, attracting dozens or hundreds of students. In the Liang Dynasty, he was appointed as Sima and Linhai Prefect, dying at eighty-two. He authored annotations on the Zhouyi, Mao's Poems, and other works. Yao Cha noted that these scholars, despite varying fortunes, contributed to Confucian learning during the Liang Dynasty.

translation:
He Tongzhi has been interested in "Three Rites" since he was a child. He takes his heart as his teacher, studies independently, works hard to improve, and never lets go of the book. He read three hundred chapters of "Li" and read them all with proficiency, and the sentences could be spoken smoothly.
Taiwei Wang Jian was the master of Confucianism at that time, and he also respected He Tongzhi very much.
He Tong first became an official in Yangzhou, and then became a bachelor of Zongming Hall. He was promoted repeatedly, and later he served as Situ Chaqi, a member of the military, and Shangshu Temple Minister.
During the Jianwu period of Qi Dynasty, he served as the Zhenbei Ji Office, joined the army, served as an assistant to the crown prince, and led the Zhongzheng of Danyang City.
At that time, the infantry colonel Liu Shan and the conscript Wu Bao had both passed away, and the only scholar in the capital was He Tong.
He Tongzhiming was familiar with the art of technique and application. At that time, the standard principles of good and bad etiquette in the country all depended on him, and he was famous for a while.
He Tongzhi successively served as an infantry captain and a doctor of Guozi. Soon he was transferred to hussar to join the army and was transferred to Sima.
In the last years of Yongyuan, war broke out in the capital, but He Tongzhi often gathered students to comment on and study the meaning of the classics, and he was very diligent and never slacked off.
In the early years of ZTE, He Tongzhi was worshiped as a general of heroic cavalry.
After Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he respected Confucianism and appointed He Tongzhi as Minister Zuocheng.
At that time, various systems were in the process of being created. He Tongzhi relied on "Li" to determine his views, which was of great help in formulating the system.
In the second year of Tianjian, He Tongzhi died during his tenure at the age of fifty-five.
Emperor Gaozu mourned his death and planned to grant him a title and an official position. According to the previous regulations, there was no precedent for conferring official positions on Zuocheng after his death. However, Emperor Gaozu specifically issued an edict to confer the post of Minister of Huangmen to He Tong. Confucian scholars felt honored by this favor.
He Tongzhi wrote about one hundred articles in "Li Yi".
He Tongzhi's sons were named He Chaoyin and He Chaohui.
Fan Zhen, courtesy name Zizhen, was born in Wuyin, Nanxiang.
He is the sixth generation grandson of Fan Wang, the general of Jin'an North.
His grandfather Fan Xuzhi served as Zhongshu Lang.
His father, Fan Meng, died young.
Fan Zhen lost his father when he was very young. His family was poor and he served his mother with filial piety and respect.
When Fan Zhen was less than 20 years old, he heard that Liu Shan of Pei State had gathered students to discuss the meaning of the classics, so he went to study with Liu Shan as his teacher.
Fan Zhen has outstanding talents, is different from ordinary people, and studies diligently. Liu Shan thinks he is a genius and crowns him personally.
Fan Zhen studied under Liu Shan for many years. Every time he went home, he often wore straw sandals and common clothes and walked back and forth.
Liu Shan's family had many princes and nobles who rode in carriages and horses. Fan Zhen was under Liu Shan's family and did not feel ashamed at all because of his poverty.
When Fan Zhen grew older, he became proficient in classics, especially the "Three Rites".
Fan Zhensheng has a straightforward nature and likes to make honest and extraordinary remarks, so the scholars and friends who associate with him often feel unhappy.
Fan Zhen only has a good relationship with his cousin Xiao Chen. Xiao Chen is known as an eloquent person, but he is often very impressed by Fan Zhen's concise and thoughtful diction.
Fan Zhen first became an official and served as the chief registrar of Qining Man. After his meritorious service, he was promoted to the position of lieutenant in the Shangshu Palace.
During the Yongming Dynasty, the Qi family and the Wei family lived in harmony and friendship, with envoys exchanging visits every year. Qi specially selected talented and learned scholars to serve as envoys. Fan Zhen, his cousin Fan Yun, his cousin Xiao Chen, Langxie Yan Youming, Hedong Pei Zhaoming and others were sent as envoys one after another, and they all left an outstanding reputation in neighboring countries.
At that time, Xiao Ziliang, the king of Jingling, recruited guests extensively, and Fan Zhen was also among those recruited.
During the Jianwu period, Fan Zhen moved to the post of chief military officer.
He left the capital and served as the prefect of Yidu, but resigned due to the death of his mother. He went home to mourn in Nanzhou.
When Emperor Gaozu's rebel army arrived in Nanzhou, Fan Zhen came to greet the rebel army in black mourning clothes.
Gaozu and Fan Zhen once lived together in the west residence owned by Xiao Ziliang, King of Jingling, and had a relationship. Now they were very happy to see Fan Zhen.
After Jiankang City was pacified, Emperor Gaozu appointed Fan Zhen as the prefect of Jin'an. During his tenure, Fan Zhen was honest and frugal, only using the state salary.
After serving for four years, he was recruited as Shangshu Zuocheng.
When Fan Zhen left home and returned home, even his relatives had nothing to give him. They only gave things to Wang Liang, the former minister.
When Fan Zhen was serving in Qi, he and Wang Liang were both ministers in the Taifu Palace. They were originally friendly to each other. By this time, Wang Liang was dismissed and deposed at home.
After Fan Zhen personally welcomed Emperor Gaozu's army, he was determined to serve as a minister. Soon his ambition was not realized, and he often became unhappy, so he became close to Wang Liang in private to correct the current situation.
Later, he was eventually moved to Guangzhou because of Wang Liang's incident, which was recorded in "The Biography of Wang Liang".
At first, when he was still in the Qi Dynasty, Fan Zhen once accompanied Xiao Ziliang, the king of Jingling.
Xiao Ziliang firmly believes in Buddhism, while Fan Zhen strongly claims that there is no Buddha.
Xiao Ziliang asked Fan Zhen: If you don't believe in cause and effect, then how can there be wealth and poverty in the world?
summary: He Tongzhi, from Lujiang, was deeply interested in the Three Rites from childhood, studying independently and mastering three hundred chapters of the Li. Respected by Taiwei Wang Jian, he held various posts, including Shangshu Temple Minister and Infantry Colonel. During the Yongyuan period, despite war, he continued lecturing. After Emperor Gaozu's ascension, he became Zuocheng, aiding in system creation. He died at fifty-five, posthumously honored as Huangmen Shilang. He wrote about one hundred articles on Li Yi. Fan Zhen, from Nanxiang, lost his father young and served his mother filially. He studied under Liu Shan, excelling in the Three Rites. He served as an envoy to the Wei and was known for his straightforward nature. He debated Buddhism with Xiao Ziliang, arguing against the existence of gods. His "Theory on the Destruction of Gods" sparked controversy. He held various posts, including Yidu Prefect and Jin'an Prefect, dying as Zhongshu Lang. His son Fan Xu inherited his knowledge.
