Confucius Qu, from Kuaiji, lost his father young but became proficient in the Guwen Shangshu. He served as a lecturer and helped compile the Liang Guan. He died at fifty-one, authoring works on the Shangshu.

translation:
As soon as the "Lun on the Destruction of Gods" in the Japanese chapter was written, both the government and the public were in an uproar. Xiao Ziliang gathered many monks to question Fan Zhen, but they could not make Fan Zhen reason.
Fan Zhen had been in the south for many years and was recalled to the capital.
After returning to the capital, the imperial court appointed him Zhongshu Lang and Doctor Guozi. He died during his tenure.
Fan Zhen has ten volumes of collected works.
Fan Zhen's son Fan Xu, also known as Changcai.
He inherited his father's knowledge and became a doctor of Taixue at the beginning of his career.
Fan Xu was an eloquent person. During the Datong period, he served as host and guest, responsible for welcoming and answering envoys from the north.
Fan Xu moved to Pingxi to consult with the king of Xiangdong and join the army, and served as an assistant to the king of Xuancheng.
He left the capital and served as the internal history of Poyang and died in the county.
Yan Zhi's courtesy name was Xiaoyuan, and he was a native of Zigui, Jianping.
His grandfather Yan Qin was a regular attendant of Tongzhi Sanqi during the Song Dynasty.
Yan Zhizhi has been proficient in Zhuangzi and Laozi since he was a child. He can talk about the metaphysical theories of Laozi and Zhuangzhuang, and has a very sophisticated understanding of "Mourning Clothes", "The Classic of Filial Piety" and "The Analects of Confucius".
When he reached adulthood, he extensively studied "Li", "Book of Changes", "Mao Shi" and "Zuo Shi Chun Qiu" annotated by Zheng.
He has a simple and filial temperament, is respectful and kind, and does not put his own merits above others.
Yan Zhi's father died when he was young, so he only ate vegetables for twenty-three years. Later, he changed his habit of eating only vegetables because he contracted wind and cold.
During the next year of Qi Yong, he first became an official and served as the minister of the Luling Kingdom. Moved to serve as the Right Changshi of the Guanghan Kingdom.
King Guanghan was executed, and no one in the country dared to deal with the body of King Guanghan. Yan Zhi rushed to mourn him and personally handled the funeral of King Guanghan. He carried the coffin to the cemetery with bare feet. After the burial, he built a tomb for King Guanghan. After the burial, he went home. People at the time thought that Yan Zhi was very righteous.
During the Jianwu period, Yan Zhizhi moved to Yuanwailang and Sanqi Changshi.
Soon he was appointed as the Houxiang of Kangle. During his tenure in the county, he was an honest official. The people and subordinate officials praised him.
In the second year of Tianjian, Yan Zhizhi was appointed as a rear army cavalry member to join the military.
Emperor Gaozu went down to Shao to recruit Confucian scholars who were knowledgeable about ancient and modern times to study the five rituals. There was a report from the minister, and Yan Zhi was able to study the ominous rituals.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, doctors of "Five Classics" began to be established. Doctors of each classics opened schools to teach students. Yan Zhi was appointed to be a doctor of "Five Classics".
Yan Zhi's school was located in Qiaotou, and there were often hundreds of students.
The master of the house explained the meaning of the scriptures, and all the students from the five halls must come. More than a thousand people listened to his lectures.
In the sixth year of Tianjian, Yan Zhizhi moved to the Fujun Record Office to join the army, and also served as a doctor.
In the seventh year of Tianjian, Yan Zhizhi died in the academy at the age of fifty-two.
summary: Yan Zhizhi, from Jianping, was proficient in Zhuangzi, Laozi, and the Three Rites. He served as Luling Kingdom Minister and Guanghan Kingdom Right Changshi, known for his righteousness in handling the Guanghan King's funeral. He was appointed as a Five Classics doctor, lecturing to hundreds of students. He died at fifty-two, leaving his family in poverty. He authored 479 volumes of Annotations on Evil Etiquette.

translation:
After Yan Zhizhi became ill, he refused to accept his salary. As a result, his wife and children lived in poverty.
After the death of Master Yan Zhi, there was no place to store the funeral coffin, so his students bought a house for his family, and only then could the funeral arrangements be completed.
Yan Zhi is kind by nature and likes to do good deeds quietly, even when no one knows about it.
When Yan Zhizhu was young, he was traveling in the mountains and saw a sick man. Yan Shan asked him the name of the patient, but the patient could not answer. Yan Zhizhi then put the patient in the car, took him home with him, and gave him some medicine.
The patient died six days later, and Yan Zhizhi bought a coffin for him to bury him in. In the end, he did not know who the patient was.
Yan Zhi was once walking along Laotan and saw a patient lying by the embankment. Yan Zhi got out of the car and asked the patient about the situation. The patient himself said that his surname was Huang. His family was originally in Jingzhou and he worked as a domestic servant. He fell ill and was very sick and dangerous. The ship owner who hired him threw him on the shore when he was about to sail the ship.
Yan Zhizhi sympathized with him very much, so he took him home in his car and treated him. A year later, the man named Huang recovered from his illness. He asked to be Yan Zhizhi's slave for life to repay Yan Zhizhi's great kindness.
Yan Zhizhi refused to accept it and sent him money and food to ask him to go home.
Yan Zhizhi had many benevolent deeds like this.
Yan Zhizhi wrote four hundred and seventy-nine volumes of "Annotations on Evil Etiquette".
He Yuan's courtesy name was Delian, and he came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.
His grandfather He Daoli was proficient in the "Three Rites" and served as Sangong Lang and Jiankang Ling in the Song Dynasty.
He Tan inherited his family education from an early age.
During the Qi Dynasty, Liu Xian of Pei State was the Prime Minister of Kuaiji. When he saw He Yu, he was very surprised by his talents and thought highly of him.
Liu Xian once visited Zhang Rong of Wu County with He Chang. Liu Xian pointed to the brush and ink and said to Zhang Rong: This young man has a smart and agile mind and will become a master of Confucianism in the future.
After Liu Xian returned to the capital, he recommended He Yuan as the son of the emperor.
He Tuan was recommended as Ming Jing, Jijiu, and soon served as Guozi's assistant.
He successively served as a doctor of Taixue and Taichang Cheng at the invitation of the imperial court. He resigned when his mother died.
In the early years of Tianjian, he was appointed as Taichang Cheng. A minister recommended him to study Bin Li. Emperor Gaozu summoned him to lecture on the meaning of "Li". He was deeply surprised by his knowledge and issued an edict to go to court on the first and fifteenth day of every month and participate in lectures in Hualin Garden.
In the fourth year of his reign, the Five Classics School had just been opened, and he was ordered to hold a doctorate in the Five Classics. He specially ordered Hechang to write the "Five Classics Meanings" for the crown prince.
Hechang was familiar with rituals and related old practices. At that time, he was reforming and creating the ritual and music system. Most of the ideas put forward by Hechang were directly adopted and implemented.
In the seventh year of Yujian, Hua Xun was appointed as an infantry captain and received a doctorate in "Five Classics".
In the ninth year of Tianjian, He Chang fell ill. He was responsible for sending doctors to deliver medicine and often asked questions. He Yi died in the academy at the age of fifty-nine.
He Chang is the author of "Etiquette", "Book of Changes", "Laozi's Explanation", "Zhuangzi's Explanation", "Chaoting Boyi", a total of 100 chapters, and "Bin Rites Notes" in 145 volumes.
summary: He Chang, from Kuaiji, inherited family education in the Three Rites. Recommended by Liu Xian, he served as Taichang Cheng and Five Classics doctor, lecturing on the Li. He authored works on etiquette and the Five Classics, dying at fifty-nine. His son He Ge also became a renowned scholar, lecturing on the Three Rites.

translation:
Sima Yun accumulated merit and moved to the palace to serve as a consultant, with the right to know the affairs of Zuo Cheng. Soon after, he was awarded the title of Shangshu Zuo Cheng.
He came out of Beijing to serve as the internal history of Shixing and died during his tenure.
Sima Yun's son Sima Shou inherited his father's studies and was proficient in the "Three Rites".
During the Datong period, he served as minister of the ancestral hall of Shangshu and went to Beijing to serve as Qu'aling.
Bian Hua, whose courtesy name is Zhaoqiu, was born in Jiyin Yuanju.
He is the sixth generation descendant of Zhongzhen Gongtutong, the hussar general of Jin Dynasty.
His father was a thrifty man who gave everything he wanted.
Bian Hua lost his father when he was young. His family was poor, but he loved to study.
When he was fourteen years old, Bian Hua was called to serve as a national scholar and he was proficient in "The Book of Changes".
After becoming an adult, Bian Hua studied the Five Classics extensively. He studied together with Pingyuan Mingshanbin and Kuaiji He Qian, and they had a good friendship.
When he first became an official, he was appointed as the minister of the Yuzhang Kingdom of Qi. After his meritorious service, he was promoted to the imperial court and went to the west to join the army.
In the early years of Tianjian, Bian Hua moved to Linchuan Wang Gongcao to join the army and served as an assistant to Guozi. He was transferred to Ancheng Wang Gongcao to join the army and was also a doctor of "Five Classics", gathering students to teach Confucian classics.
Bian Hua covered a wide range of subjects, was knowledgeable, witty and eloquent. He explained scriptures and analyzed their meanings. He was the leading figure at that time.
After the Jin Dynasty moved to Jiangzuo, music rhythm became a unique skill, and it was not until Bian Hua that he became proficient in music rhythm.
Bian Long moved to the post of Minister Cao Lang, and left the capital to serve as Wu Ling. He died.
Cui Lingen is from Wucheng, Qinghedong.
He has been attentive and eager to learn since he was a child. He followed his teacher to learn all the Five Classics, and he was especially proficient in the Three Rites and the Three Legends.
Cui Lingen first served as an official in the Northern Dynasties and served as Dr. Taichang. In the thirteenth year of Tianjian, he returned to Liang Dynasty.
Because Cui Lingen was proficient in Confucianism, Emperor Gaozu promoted him to the rank of Minister of Dispersed Cavalry, and he was promoted to the rank of Infantry Colonel and Doctor of the Imperial Academy.
Cui Lingen gathered students to teach Confucian classics, and the number of students who listened to his lectures often reached hundreds.
He was simple by nature and had no literary talent, but when it came to explaining scriptures and analyzing their meanings, he was very interesting. The prestigious Confucian scholars in the capital praised him and valued him. Assistant Kong Yu especially liked his teachings.
At that time, the teaching assistant Yu Sengdan was also proficient in Du Yu's annotations, so he wrote "Shen Du Can't Conquer" to answer Cui Lingen. Their books were circulated in the world at the same time. Yu Sengdan, a native of Yuyao, Kuaiji, taught "Zuo Shi Zhuan" to students, and hundreds of people listened to his lectures.
summary: Sima Yun, from Hanoi, lost his father young but loved learning, excelling in the Three Rites. He served as Shangshu Temple Minister and debated mourning rites for loving mothers. He died as Shixing Neishi. His son Sima Shou inherited his studies. Bian Hua, from Jiyin, lost his father young but studied the Five Classics, especially the Book of Changes. He served as a Five Classics doctor, known for his eloquence and musical expertise. He died as Wuling Prefect. Cui Lingen, from Qinghe, studied the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites and Three Commentaries. He served as Taichang Doctor in the Northern Dynasties before returning to Liang, where he lectured to hundreds. He authored numerous works on the classics. Kong Qian, from Kuaiji, studied under He Yin, excelling in the Five Classics. He served as a Five Classics doctor but was not skilled in governance. He died during the Liqian turmoil.

translation:
Yu Sengxi had a comprehensive understanding of the purpose and style of writing "The Biography of the Zuo Family", and no one could compare with him at that time. Before this, when Confucian scholars discussed the celestial body, two views, Huntian and Gaitian, coexisted. Those who said that the celestial body was Gaitian did not agree with Tantian's point of view, and those who said that the celestial body was Huntian did not agree with Gaitian's point of view.
Zha Ximo established his own point of view and combined the theories of Tantian and Gaitian.
Cui Lingen went to Beijing to serve as the internal history of Changsha. When he returned to Beijing, he was awarded the title of Doctor of the State. There were many students who studied with him.
He went to Beijing to serve as General Mingwei and Governor Guacong, and died during his tenure.
Cui He wrote twenty-two volumes of "Collection of Mao's Poems", forty volumes of "Collection of Zhouli", forty-seven volumes of "Sanli Yi Zong", twenty-two volumes of "Zuo Shi Jing Chuan Yi", ten volumes of "Zuo Shi Regulations", and ten volumes of "Gongyanggu Liang Wen Ju Yi".
Kong Qian came in from Shanyin in Kuaiji.
When he was young, Wang Yu worshiped He Yin as his teacher. He was proficient in the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites, Xiaozhi and the Analects of Confucius. He expounded and taught these scriptures dozens of times and had hundreds of students.
Renxi successively served as an assistant teacher of Guozi, a doctor of "Five Classics" three times, and moved to the post of Shangshu Temple Minister.
He left Beijing and served as magistrate of two counties.
Kong Qian was a Confucian scholar who only knew the classics and was not good at governing the people. He had no political achievements during his tenure as county magistrate.
When turmoil broke out during the Liqian period, Kong Yu died at home.
Kong Chuxuan, the son of Kong Qian, focused on studying Confucianism, and his official position was promoted to Doctor of Taixue.
Kong Chuxuan, the son of brother Kong Ling, was also proficient in the "Three Rites" and had a great reputation, but he died young.
Lu Guang, a native of Fanyang Zhuo, said he was a descendant of Lu Chen, a middle-ranking official in Zhi Sikong.
Lu Chen was trapped and died in the army during the rebellion. During the Jin Dynasty, Lu Chen was still among the famous families in the Central Plains, and there were descendants of Lu Chen.
Lu Guang was proficient in scriptures since he was a child and had Confucian knowledge.
Lu Guang returned to chisel during the Tianjian period.
At first he was appointed as the Minister of Sanqi, a member of the Yuanwai Sanqi family, and then went to Beijing to serve as the prefect of Quanda. However, he was dismissed from office because of his guilt.
Soon, Lu Guang was appointed as General Zhechong, and the imperial court assigned him a thousand soldiers for the Northern Expedition. After returning to the imperial court, he was worshiped as an infantry captain and a doctor of Guozi, and taught all the "Five Classics" in the academy.
At that time, Confucian scholars from the north, including Cui Lingen, Sun Xiang, Jiang Xian and others, gathered students to teach Confucian classics, but their pronunciation was vulgar and clumsy; only Lu Guang spoke clearly and elegantly, unlike the northerners.
Pushe Xu Mian was also proficient in Confucian classics, and he deeply appreciated Lu Guang.
Soon after, Lu Guang was appointed as a regular attendant of Yuanwai Sanqi, but his position as a doctor remained unchanged.
He also left the capital and served as Xinwu, the successor of Guiyang, Changshi, and the prefect of Xunyang.
He was also appointed as the chief historian of Wuling King, and his post as governor remained unchanged. He died during his tenure.
summary: Lu Guang, from Fanyang, was proficient in scriptures and served as a Five Classics doctor, known for his clear pronunciation. He died as Xunyang Prefect.

translation:
Shen Jun, courtesy name Shisong, was born in Wukang, Wuxing.
The family has been a farmer for generations, until Yingkong. He loved learning, and he and his uncle Taishi Shuming chose Shen Jun as their teacher from the same clan. He studied under Shen Junmu for many years. He assigned himself tasks to study day and night. Sometimes he would doze off and hit himself with a wooden stick. He was so concentrated.
After Shen Lin's death, Licai left the capital and traveled to various schools, so he became proficient in the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites.
Shen Jun initially served as the lieutenant of the kingdom, and was gradually promoted to the rank of minister and assistant to the prince.
At that time, Lang Lubao, the official of the Ministry of official affairs, wrote a letter to Pu She Tu Pad to recommend some candidates: Doctor Chen Zhida in the "Five Classics" must be replaced, considering that the imperial court must carefully select suitable talents to replace him.
As long as it is a sage's book that can be studied and its views must be established based on "Zhou Guan", then "Zhou Guan" is actually the source and foundation of various scriptures.
However, the knowledge of "Zhou Guan" has not been taught to each other for many years. Sun Xiang and Jiang Hao from the north also studied and taught it. However, because their pronunciation is like that of Southern Chu and Zhu Xia, which is far apart and difficult to understand, students are reluctant to study. Only the assistant teacher Shen Jun is particularly proficient in the book "Zhou Guan".
Recently, he often opened lectures. Many Confucian scholars, such as Liu Hua, Shen Hong, and Shen Xiong, came to his forum to worship him as their teacher, and brought scriptures to listen to his lectures. None of them were not impressed, and no one had any criticism.
I think that such a person should be recruited immediately and ordered to specialize in this subject of knowledge and teach "Zhou Guan" over and over again, so that the authentic classics of the saints can be valued again after being abandoned, and the knowledge that has been lost for many years can be taught to scholars.
Xu Mian followed Lu Ren's suggestion and wrote a memorial recommending Shen Jun as a doctor of the Five Classics.
Shen Jun lectures in the school, and there are often hundreds of students attending his lectures.
Shen Jun left the capital and served as Huarong Ling. After returning to the capital, he was awarded not only as a member of the Sanqi Shilang, but also as a doctor of "Five Classics".
At that time, He Chen, a member of Zhongshushe, was ordered by the emperor to compile "Liang Guan", so he petitioned Shen Jun and Confucius Qubu to serve as bachelors in the Western Province to help him write "Liang Guan".
After the book "Liang Guan" was completed, Shen Jun entered the court and served as Zhongshu General.
Later he left the capital and served as Wukang Ling, and died during his tenure.
Shen Jun's son, Shen Wen'a, inherited his father's studies, and was especially proficient in "The Biography of the Zuo Family".
During the Taiqing period, Shen Wen'a was promoted from assistant teacher of Guozi to doctor of "Five Classics".
Those who inherited Shen Jun's studies include Zhang Ji of Wujun and Confucius Yun of Kuaiji. Their official positions were promoted to doctor of the Five Classics and minister of the temple.
Taishi Shuming was a native of Wucheng, Wuxing. He was a descendant of Wu Taishi Ci.
Taishi Shuming was proficient in "Zhuangzi" and "Laozi" since he was a child. He also studied "The Book of Filial Piety" and "Book of Rites". He was particularly proficient in the three books of "Zhuangzi", "Laozi" and "Book of Changes". He was second to none at the time. During each lecture, there were often more than 500 people listening.
Uncle Taishi served as Guozi's assistant coach for consecutive years.
He liked Taishi Shuming's knowledge. When he came to Beijing to serve as the governor of Jiangzhou, he also took Taishi Shuming to Jiangzhou.
He was appointed governor of Yingzhou, and Taishi Shuming moved to Yingzhou with the palace. Everywhere he went, Taishi Shuming opened a school to teach, and people in the south of the Yangtze River inherited his teachings.
In the thirteenth year of Datong, Taishi Shuming passed away at the age of seventy-three.
summary: Shen Jun, from Wuxing, studied the Five Classics, especially the Three Rites. Recommended as a Five Classics doctor, he lectured to hundreds. He died as Wukang Ling. Taishi Shuming, from Wuxing, was proficient in Zhuangzi, Laozi, and the Book of Changes, lecturing to over five hundred. He died at seventy-three.

translation:
Confucius was born in Shanyin, Kuaiji.
He lost his father when he was young, and his family was poor, but he loved learning. When he was cultivating fields and collecting wood in the mountains, he often took books with him and read and recited them whenever he had free time.
He worked hard and persevered, and finally became proficient in Confucian classics, especially "Guwen Shangshu".
Confucius Qu initially served as the Minister of the Successor of Changsha and as an assistant to the Confucius of the Kingdom. He lectured on "Shang Shu" forty times, and there were often hundreds of people listening to his lectures.
He Chen, a member of Zhongshushe, was ordered by the emperor to compile "Liang Guan". He petitioned Confucius Qu to be a bachelor of the Western Province to help him write "Liang Guan".
After the book "Liang Guan" was completed, Confucius served as Minister Wen, but he did not take up the post.
A long time later, he also served as host, guest, and guest, and his position as a bachelor remained unchanged.
He also accumulated merit and was promoted to be the minister of the Xiangdong Kingdom, a permanent minister, and a minister of scattered cavalry outside the service. He was also appointed as Yunhui Lujiang Gongji Office to join the army, and was transferred to serve as Zhongshu General Secretary.
Soon he was moved to the rank of infantry school captain, but his position remained unchanged.
When Emperor Gaozu wrote the "Explanations of the Five Classics" and "The True Sayings of Confucius", he specifically ordered Confucius to check various books and find materials to prove his righteousness.
After the matter was completed, Gaozu ordered Jie Ziguai, right guard Zhu Yi, and Zuo Cheng He Chen to take turns every day in the Shilin Pavilion to practice scriptures, ask questions, and assess the scholars.
Zhizi Qu accumulated merit and was promoted to Tongzhi Zhengyuanlang, but his position remained unchanged.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, Confucius died during his tenure at the age of fifty-one.
Confucius Qu wrote a total of 20 volumes of "Shang Shu Yi", 30 volumes of "Collected Comments on Shangshu", a 100-volume continuation of Zhu Yi's "Collected Comments on Zhouyi", and a 150-volume continuation of He Chengtian's "Ji Li Lun".
Huang Kan, a native of Wu County, is the ninth generation descendant of Huang Xiang, the governor of Qingzhou.
Huang Kan loved studying since he was a child. He worshiped He Chang as his teacher and devoted himself to learning from He Chang. As a result, he became proficient in Confucian classics, especially the Three Rites, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Analects of Confucius.
When he first became an official and served as an assistant to Guozi, he gave lectures on classics and meanings in the academy, and hundreds of students attended his lectures.
Huang Kan wrote fifty volumes of the "Book of Rites". After it was completed, it was presented to the emperor, who ordered it to be handed over to the secret pavilion for collection.
Soon, Huang Kan was called to Huayongji to lecture on "Book of Rites". Zhidan thought that he was very knowledgeable, so he was appointed as a member of the Yuanwai Sanqi Shilang, and his position as an assistant teacher remained unchanged.
Huang Kan was very filial by nature, and often required him to recite the "Filial Piety Sutra" twenty times a day, which was modeled on the recitation of the "Avalokiteśvara Sutra".
When Huang Kan's mother passed away, he resigned from his post and returned to his hometown to mourn.
King Shaoling of Qianxi admired Huang Kan's knowledge and went to welcome Huang Kan with generous gifts.
After Huang Kan went to King Shaoling, he contracted a heart disease and died in Xia Shou in the eleventh year of Datong at the age of fifty-eight.
The ten volumes of "On Meaning" and "Book of Rites" written by Huang Kan were valued by scholars at that time, and some scholars inherited his theories.
summary: Huang Kan, from Wu County, studied under He Chang, excelling in the Three Rites. He lectured to hundreds and authored the Book of Rites. He died at fifty-eight.

translation:
Hu Sengyou, whose name is Yuanguo, is a champion in Nanyang. He has been brave and decisive since he was a child, and has the ability to be a soldier.
He served as an official in the State of Wei and reached the rank of Yinqing Guanglu. He returned to the capital in the second year of Datong and frequently applied for titles. Emperor Gaozu thought highly of him and awarded him the title of "Fake Festival", "Super Military General" and "Wende Commander", and sent him to guard Xiangcheng. Xiangcheng was captured, and Hu Sengyou fell to Wei again.
In the first year of Zhongdatong, Chen Qingzhi sent Wang Yuanhao of Wei Beihai to Luoyang. Hu Sengku was able to return to the capital and was awarded the title of prefect of Nantianshui and Tianmen counties. He left good political achievements wherever he served as an official.
Hu Sengku liked reading by nature, but he was not good at writing poems and compositions. However, every time at the court banquet, Hu Sengyou would try his best to compose poems. The poems were vulgar and often ridiculed by others. Hu Sengyou was happy as usual, thinking that his poems were indeed exquisite.
Conceit and boasting are even more powerful. Hu Sengyou served Shizu in his later years and served as Zhenxi Lushi to join the army.
When Hou Jing rebelled, the Western Jumans also rebelled. Shizu ordered Hu Sengcoff to attack the Western Jumans, and ordered Hu Senghu to kill all the barbarian chiefs and leaders. Hu Sengyou came to remonstrate and was imprisoned for violating Shizu's will.
In the second year of Dashi, Hou Jing invaded Jingshan and surrounded Wang Sengbian in Baling. The emperor summoned Hu Sengyou from prison, awarded him the title of General Jiajie and Wumeng, and named him the Marquis of Xinshi County, and ordered him to rush to aid Wang Sengbian.
When Hu Sengyou was about to set off, he said to his son: You can open two gates, one gate is to be turned into a red gate, and the other gate is to be turned into a white gate.
Good luck will enter the house through the red door, and bad luck will enter the house through the white door. I will not go home unless I win.
When Shizu heard Hu Sengyou's words, he felt that he was brave and commendable.
Hu Sengku led his army to Yangpu and sent his general Ren Gou to lead 5,000 elite soldiers to guard the fort and wait for Hu Sengyou's army to fight from a distance.
Hu Sengyou advanced westward by another road. Ren Yue thought that they were retreating because they were afraid of him, so he led his army to pursue them in a hurry. They caught up with Hu Sengku at Qiankou, Nan'an. Ren Yue called to Hu Sengyou and said: "Wu'er, why don't you surrender early?"
Where to escape to?
Hu Sengyou ignored his answer and secretly led his army to retreat. When they arrived at Chisha Pavilion, Lu Fahe and his army arrived. Hu Sengyou and Lu Fahe attacked Ren Yue together with the two armies, defeated Ren Yue's army, captured Ren Yue alive and sent him to Jiangling. Hou Jing led his army to escape after hearing the news that Ren Yue had been captured.
Shizu appointed Hu Sengyou as a minister and general, and recruited him back to Jingzhou.
In the second year of Chengsheng's reign, Hu Senyou was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Kaifu Yitong Third Division, while all other positions remained unchanged.
When the enemies of the Western Wei Dynasty invaded, Hu Sengyou was appointed as the governor of the city to supervise all military affairs.
The Wei army launched attacks from all sides, with many units attacking at the same time. Hu Sengyou personally braved the rock with arrows, supervised the battle day and night, rewarded the soldiers, and strictly rewarded and punished them. The soldiers were moved by him and were willing to fight to the death for him.
Wherever Hu Sengyou went, Naxiang's enemies were destroyed, and no enemy dared to attack again.
Soon Hu Sengyou was shot by a stray arrow and died at the age of sixty-three. When Shizu heard the news, he rushed to the east of the city to mourn.
summary: The lives and military careers of several figures from the Liang Dynasty. Hu Sengyou, a brave champion from Nanyang, served Wei and later returned to Liang, where he was appointed to guard Xiangcheng. After its capture, he returned to Wei but eventually came back to Liang, serving as a prefect with good governance. Despite his poor poetry, he remained confident. He was imprisoned for remonstrating against killing barbarian chiefs but was later released to aid Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing. He defeated Ren Yue, captured him, and caused Hou Jing to flee. He died at 63 from a stray arrow while defending against Wei, leading to the city's fall.

translation:
As a result, everyone inside and outside the imperial court was in panic, and the city was finally captured.
Xu Wensheng, courtesy name Daomao, was born in Pengcheng.
His family has been serving as officials and generals in Wei for generations.
Xu Wensheng's father, Xu Qingzhi, led more than a thousand people to surrender in the early years of Tianjian, but he died on the way before they arrived.
Xu Wensheng continued to command more than a thousand men and horses, and gradually made many achievements. Emperor Gaozu treated him favorably and favored him.
In the last years of Datong, Emperor Gaozu appointed Xu Wensheng as the governor of Ningzhou and the governor of Zhijie.
Before Xu Wensheng took office, Ningzhou was located in a remote area, and the barbarians under its jurisdiction did not understand the etiquette and etiquette of education. They were just greedy for money, and robberies and robberies continued one after another. No one who served as governor could stop it.
Xu Wensheng expressed his sincerity and compassion, showing both power and virtue. All the Yi officials were influenced by him, and the customs of Ningzhou changed.
In the second year of Taiqing, Xu Wensheng heard that the country was in trouble, so he recruited soldiers. He led the recruited 10,000 people to come to the rescue.
The emperor praised his loyalty and appointed him as Chijie, Changshi of Sanqi, General of Zuowei, Supervisor of Liangnan, Qinsha, Shuyi, Babeiba and the six states of military affairs, General Renwei, and governor of Qinzhou, and entrusted him with the strategy of marching eastward.
So Xu Wensheng led the troops down the river and marched eastward. When they arrived at Wuchang, they met Hou Jing's general Ren Yue. Xu Wensheng then faced off against Ren Yue for a long time.
Shizu also ordered the guard general Yin Yue, Pingshu general Du Youan, Bazhou governor Wang Xi and others to lead their troops to meet with Xu Wensheng, asking them to obey Xu Wensheng's command.
Xu Wensheng and others attacked Ren Yue in Beji. Ren Yue was defeated and retreated to Xiyang. Xu Wensheng marched to occupy Luzhou and held a stalemate with Ren Yue.
When Hou Jing heard the news about the Japanese, he led his army up the river and westward to rescue Ren Yue, and also reached Xiyang.
Xu Wensheng did not dare to fight.
All his generals said: Hou Jing's navy advanced rashly, and the soldiers were hungry and tired. If we can seize the opportunity to attack them, we will definitely win a great victory.
Xu Wensheng refused.
Xu Wensheng's wife, Shi, was originally in Jianye. When she was dispatched, Hou Jing took Shi on a boat and sent her back to Xu Wensheng. Xu Wensheng was deeply grateful to Hou Jing, so he sent envoys to secretly communicate with Hou Jing without any intention of fighting. His generals were angry and resentful.
Du Youan and Song Yao led their troops to advance alone, fought with Hou Jing, defeated Hou Jing's army, and captured Hou Jing's ships before returning.
At that time, Hou Jing secretly sent cavalry to attack Yingzhou from the trail. Yingzhou was captured. Xu Wensheng's army was frightened and uneasy, so the whole army was defeated.
Xu Wensheng fled back to Jingzhou, and Shizu appointed Xu Wensheng as the governor of the north of the city.
Xu Wensheng also engaged in corruption and bribery, amassing a lot of property. The emperor was very angry and ordered Xu Wensheng to be punished. He listed ten crimes against him and removed his title.
After Xu Wensheng lost his military power, he was resentful. When Shizu found out about it, he imprisoned Xu Wensheng.
Ren Yue was also captured at that time and was imprisoned in the same place as Xu Wensheng.
Xu Wensheng said to Ren Yue: Why didn't you surrender earlier, and now I am imprisoned in this place.
Ren Yue said: There are no traces of your horse hooves outside the gate of my military camp. How can I surrender?
Xu Wensheng had nothing to say and eventually died in prison.
summary: Xu Wensheng, from Pengcheng, led his father's troops to surrender to Liang and became a governor of Ningzhou, where he reformed corrupt barbarian customs. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he was sent eastward but hesitated to fight, influenced by his wife's return from Hou Jing. His army was defeated after Yingzhou's capture, and he fled to Jingzhou. He was imprisoned for corruption and resentment, dying in prison after a taunt from Ren Yue. Yin Zichun, from Guzang, served as a general and prefect, suppressing barbarian rebellions. He fought with Wang Sengbian and Xu Wensheng against Hou Jing, achieving many victories, but died in Jiangling after the army retreated. The text concludes with a commentary praising Hu Sengyou's loyalty, criticizing Xu Wensheng's failure, and lauding Du Chan's moral choices and achievements.

translation:
Du Chan was born in Duling, Jingzhao.
His ancestors returned to the Southern Dynasty from the north and lived in Xiangyang, Yongzhou, where their descendants settled.
Du Ze's grandfather, Du Lingqi, was appointed to Shizhong during the Qi Dynasty.
Du Qi's father, Du Huaibao, was ambitious and upright since he was a child, and often encountered good opportunities.
Gaozu led the rebel army to denounce Donghun Hou along the river, and Du Huaibao followed Xiao Wei, the king of Nanping, to stay and guard Xiangyang.
During his imprisonment, Du Huaixuan's merits gradually increased, and his official position was promoted to the rank of Fierce General and Liangzhou Governor.
In the early years of Datong, Yuan Luo, the governor of Liangzhou in Wei, led the state to surrender, and Du Huaibao went to supervise Huazhou.
At the time when the king of Genbian District under Qinzhou rebelled, Si Huaiyi led his army to defeat Sanmi.
In the fifth year of Taitong, Du Huaishi died at the place where he served.
Du Ze is Du Huaishi's seventh son.
He has been ambitious since he was a child and is known in his hometown for his courage and bravery.
When he first became an official, he was appointed as a soldier in Lujiang Huqi Prefecture and joined the army.
When Shizu was in charge of Jingzhou, Du Zhu still joined the army for the shogunate and later served as the governor of Qixing.
In the second year of Taiqing, Du Tuan followed King Yueyang to invade Jingzhou. Because of his long-standing friendship with Du Ze, Shizu secretly invited Du Qi to join him. Du Tuan, his elder brother Du An, his younger brother You'an You'an, his elder brother's son Zhuan Xin and others returned to Shisu at night. Shizu conferred the title of Silk Witch as Chijie, General Xinwei, and the governor of Wuzhou.
Soon he was promoted to General Xuanyi, leading the Zhenman Guards and the internal history of Wuling. He was granted the title of Marquis of Zhijiang County and was granted the title of a thousand households in the town.
Shizu ordered Du Ze to follow Wang Sengbian and march eastward to conquer Hou Jing.
When he led his army to Baling, he was met by Hou Jing who came to attack. Hou Jing attacked for ten days and ran away after failing to win.
Du Xun was promoted to Shizhong and Zuowei General, his title was promoted to Duke, and he was granted an additional 500 households.
Du Xun continued to follow Wang Sengbian in pursuit of Hou Jing until he reached Shitou, where he held a stalemate with the rebels at Jinling.
When the two sides fought, Hou Jing personally led the elite soldiers, charging left and right. Du Juan rushed out from behind the ridge, intercepted and killed Hou Jing's army. Hou Jing was defeated and fled east to Jinling, while Du occupied Stone City.
After Hou Jing's rebellion was put down, Du Yajia added Sanqi Changshi, Zhijie, supervised the military in Jiangzhou, and the governor of Jiangzhou, adding thousands of households to the city.
This month, Qi general Guo Yuanjian attacked Qinzhou governor Yan Chaoyuan in Qin County. Wang Sengbian ordered Du Juan to rush to the rescue, and Chen Ba also led his army from Kamu to join Si Ouyanghe.
They fought against Shilin in Yuanjian. Chen Baxian ordered a volley of powerful crossbows, and Yuan Jian's army retreated. Du Juan took the opportunity to attack and defeated Guo Yuanjian's army, killing more than 10,000 people and capturing more than a thousand alive. Jian gathered up the remaining soldiers and fled.
At this time Shizu was holding Wang Lin in Jiangling, and his subordinates such as Shilu Na and others rebelled in Changsha. Shizu recruited Du Chan and Wang Sengbian to fight together.
In the second year of Chengsheng's reign, the people fought in the wheel, were defeated, and captured two of their fortresses. Shilu Na and others fled to Changsha to defend, and Du Chan and others surrounded him.
Later, Shilu Na and others surrendered, and Du Juan and Wang Sengbian marched westward to conquer King Wuling. The army arrived and immediately defeated the rebels and put down the rebellion.
summary: Du Chan, from Duling, was the seventh son of Du Huaibao. He joined Shizu and followed Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing, defeating him at Baling and Shitou. He later fought Qi general Guo Yuanjian and suppressed rebellions in Changsha and against King Wuling. He died of illness. His brothers Du An and Du Youan also served, with Du An killed attacking Xiangyang and Du Youan surrendering to and killed by Hou Jing. Du Chong, Du Chan's nephew, was a brave general who defeated Hou Jing's forces, captured Song Zixian, and later resisted Chen Baxian after Wang Sengbian's death, ultimately surrendering and being killed.

translation:
Queen Taizong gave birth to Prince Xiao Daqi, Prince of Nanjun, Xiao Dalian; Chen Shurong gave birth to Prince Xiao Daxin of Xunyang; Mrs. Zuo gave birth to Prince Xiao Dalin of Nanhai, and Prince Xiao Dachun of Anlu; Mrs. Xie gave birth to Duke Xiao Daya of Liuyang; Mrs. Zhang They gave birth to Xiao Dazhuang, the king of Xinxing; Xiao Dajun, the king of Xiyang, was born to Bao Zhaohua; Xiao Dawei, the king of Wuning, was born to Mrs. Fan; Xiao Daqiu, the king of Jianping, was born to Chu Xiuhua; Xiao Daxin, the king of Yi'an, was born to Mrs. Chen; Xiao Dazhi, the king of Suijian, was born to Mrs. Zhu.
The deeds of the other sons are not recorded in this book.
Xiao Daxin, king of Xunyang, was named Renshu.
He has been smart and enlightened since childhood and is good at writing articles.
In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, he was granted the title of Dangyang Gong because of his status as the emperor's grandson, and was granted a residence of 1,500 households.
In the first year of Datong, he went to Beijing to serve as envoy Chijie, governor of Ying's southern and northern divisions, Dingxin's military forces of the five states, general of light vehicles, and governor of Yingzhou.
Xiao Daxin was only thirteen years old at that time. Because of his young age, Taizong was worried that he would not be able to understand the people's sentiments, so he warned him: No matter how big or small, all matters should be handed over to the Xingfu and state officials who are in charge of the affairs. There is no need to worry about anything.
Although Xiao Daxin does not personally manage state affairs, his opinions are always reasonable. Everyone was amazed and admired.
In the seventh year of Datong, Xiao Daxin was recruited as a servant and a stone garrison.
In the first year of Taiqing, he came to Beijing and served as General Yunhui and governor of Jiangzhou.
In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing invaded the capital. Xiao Daxin recruited soldiers, and people from far and near joined him. The army reached 10,000 people. He and the troops from the upper reaches of the Yangtze River rushed to the capital to rescue the imperial court.
In the third year of Taiqing's reign, the capital city was captured. Xiao Shao, the Marquis of Shangjia, fled south. He read the Emperor's Secret Shao to Xiao Daxin and gave Xiao Daxin the title of "General of Pingnan".
In the first year of Dashi, Xiao Daxin was named King of Xunyang and had 2,000 households in the city.
In the past, Zhuang Tie, the prefect of Liyang, led the city to surrender to Hou Jing, and soon he brought his mother to Xiao Daxin. Because Zhuang Tie was his old subordinate, Xiao Daxin treated Zhuang Tie generously and left all matters of leading the army to war to Zhuang Tie, and then appointed Zhuang Tie as the internal historian of Yuzhang.
Hou Jing repeatedly sent troops westward upstream to invade and plunder. Xiao Daxin ordered Zhuang Tie to defeat the invading rebels, so that the rebels could not advance.
At that time, Poyang King Xiao Fan led his army to abandon Hefei and stationed at Zhakou, hoping to wait until all the reinforcements gathered before marching together.
When Xiao Daxin heard the news, he sent someone to invite Xiao Fan to go up the river and march westward, and gave Xiao Fan the city to garrison. The food supplies were very generous, and the two of them worked together to put an end to the chaos.
When Zhuang Tie occupied Yuzhang and rebelled, Xiao Daxin ordered his soldiers to join the army. Wei Yue and others led the army to attack Zhuang Tie. Zhuang Tie was defeated and asked to surrender.
Xiao Si, the eldest son of King Poyang, had friends with Zhuang Tie before. During the war, he praised Zhuang Tie to King Poyang, saying that Zhuang Tie was talented and well versed in strategy. Moreover, he was a veteran general in the army. If he wanted to achieve great things, he should rely on Zhuang Tie's strength. If Zhuang Tie surrenders to King Xunyang of Jiangzhou, he will definitely not be able to save his life. Xiao Si asked King Poyang to send troops to rescue Zhuang Tie.
Xiao Fan, the king of Poyang, listened to Xiao Si's advice and sent general Hou Ti to lead 5,000 elite troops to rescue Zhuang Tie. Hou Ti made a surprise attack at night and attacked Wei Yue and other military camps.
Xiao Daxin was very panicked and frightened when he heard the news. As a result, a rift developed between the two vassal kings, and their hearts were divided and they had different aspirations.
Hou Jing's general Ren Yue attacked the city and reached Huancheng. Xiao Daxin sent Sima Weizhi to lead his army to resist, but was severely defeated.
At that time, Xiao Daxin still had more than a thousand warriors under his command. Everyone advised Xiao Daxin: Since there is no food reserve in Baogao, it will be difficult to hold on to it. It is best to lead Qingqi to Jianzhou and plan to revitalize it later.
Xiao Daxin was hesitant and did not make a decision. His mother Chen Shurong said: Now that the emperor is old and the prince is in good health, you have been away from the court for a long time and do not care to pay homage to the emperor and the prince. Besides, I am old, but you want me to travel long distances and embark on a dangerous road with insufficient food supply. How can I be considered a filial son?
I will not set off after all.
After saying that, he clapped his chest and cried bitterly, so Xiao Daxin stayed and never left.
Xiao Daxin then made an agreement with Ren.
In the autumn of the second year of Dashi, Xiao Daxin was killed at the age of twenty-five.
Xiao Dalin, king of Nanhai, was named Renxuan.
summary: This historical text records the lineage and fates of the sons of Emperor Taizong and Shizu during a period of rebellion. Queen Taizong bore Prince Xiao Daqi and Xiao Dalian; other consorts and ladies bore numerous other princes, including Xiao Daxin, Xiao Dalin, Xiao Dachun, Xiao Daya, Xiao Dazhuang, Xiao Dajun, Xiao Dawei, Xiao Daqiu, Xiao Daxin, and Xiao Dazhi. The deeds of some sons are not recorded. Xiao Daxin, King of Xunyang, was intelligent and a skilled writer. Ennobled as a duke at age thirteen, he was appointed to military and gubernatorial posts. Despite his youth, his opinions were wise. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he raised a 10,000-man army to rescue the capital. After the capital fell, he was made King of Xunyang. He relied on his former subordinate Zhuang Tie, who later rebelled. A conflict arose with King Poyang, who aided Zhuang Tie, causing a rift. After a military defeat, Xiao Daxin hesitated to flee, persuaded by his mother to stay. He was killed at age twenty-five. Xiao Dalin, King of Nanhai, was also intelligent and known for filial piety after his mother's death. He held various official posts. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he was stationed at Xinting and later oversaw military affairs. He collected cattle to reward soldiers. He was made King of Nanhai. He refused to join a rebel army, deeming it unwise. He was killed at age twenty-five.

translation:
Xiao Dalian was transferred to serve as the Minister of Huangmen, then to the Minister of the Middle School, and soon he also served as the Shitou garrison.
In the first year of Taiqian's reign, he left Beijing to serve as envoy Chijie, General Qingche, and governor of Dongyangzhou.
Hou Jing invaded the capital, and Xiao Dalian led 40,000 troops to rescue him.
Taicheng was captured, the reinforcements dispersed, and Xiao Dalian returned to Yangzhou.
In the third year of Taiqing's reign, bandits Tian Lingqun from Kuaiji gathered tens of thousands of people to attack Yangzhou. Xiao Dalian ordered soldiers to join the army and Zhang Biao met him and killed Tian Lingqun.
In the first year of Dashi, Xiao Dalian was granted the title of King of Nanjun, with a settlement of 2,000 households.
Hou Jing frequently sent his generals Tang Bochao and Liu Shenmao to attack, while Xiao Dalian deployed garrison troops to wait for the enemy.
Just when his general Liu Yi led the city to surrender to the rebels, Xiao Dalian abandoned the city and fled. When he arrived at Xin'an, he was captured by the rebels.
Hou Jing appointed Xiao Dalian as General of Qingche, responsible for conducting affairs in Yangzhou, and moved to General of Pingnan and Governor of Jiangzhou.
After Xiao Dalian was trapped in the hands of the rebels, he often thought about escaping, so he made an appointment with the rebels and said: "I will not participate in the affairs of leading the army and governing the people. If you want to know whether I live or die, just listen to the bells in my house."
This was because he wanted to avoid seeing the traitor less and escape. The traitor also believed him, but his escape failed.
In the autumn of the second year of Dashi, Xiao Dalian was killed at the age of twenty-five.
Xiao Dachun, King of Anlu, was named Ren Jing.
He has dabbled in various books since childhood.
He is respectful and filial by nature, has a beautiful appearance, a strong body, and a belt with ten girths.
In the sixth year of Datong, Xiao Dachun was granted the title of Duke of Xifeng County, with a settlement of 1,500 households.
He was appointed as the Vice Minister of Zhongshu.
Later he was appointed as General Ningyuan and learned about the military affairs of Shitou garrison.
Hou Jing attacked the capital, and Xiao Dachun fled to Jingkou. As King Shaoling rescued the capital, he fought with the rebels at Zhongshan, and Xiao Dachun was captured by the rebels.
After the capital was captured, in the first year of Dabao, Xiao Dachun was granted the title of Prince of Anlu County, with a settlement of 2,000 households.
He left Beijing as envoy Chijie, General Yunhui, and governor of Dongyangzhou.
In the autumn of the second year of Dashi, Xiao Dachun was killed at the age of twenty-two.
Xiao Daya, Duke of Liuyang, was named Renfeng.
In the ninth year of Datong, he was granted the title of Duke of Liuyang County, with a settlement of 1,500 households.
Xiao Daya was smart and alert since she was a child, with beautiful appearance and good demeanor. Gaozu especially loved her.
In the third year of Taiqing's reign, the capital city was captured, and the rebels had climbed onto the city wall. Xiao Daya still ordered his attendants to fight. As the number of rebels gradually increased, he was able to hang himself down from the city wall with a rope.
Xiao Daya became ill and died because of this hatred. She died at the age of seventeen.
The emerging king Xiao Dazhuang was named Renli.
In the ninth year of Datong, he was granted the title of Duke of Gaotang County, with a settlement of 1,500 households.
In the first year of his reign, he was granted the title of Prince of Xingxing County and was granted a residence of 2,000 households.
He left the capital and served as envoy Chijie, governor of Yu Tusu and other military affairs, general Xuanyi, and governor of Southern Xuzhou.
summary: Xiao Dalian, King of Nanjun, was handsome, a skilled writer and painter. He and his brother Xiao Dalin impressed Emperor Gaozu with their riding skills. He held ministerial posts and led 40,000 troops to rescue the capital during the rebellion. After the capital fell, he defended Yangzhou from bandits. He was made King of Nanjun. Captured by rebels after a subordinate's betrayal, he was appointed to posts but plotted escape. He was killed at age twenty-five.

translation:
Dabao was killed in the autumn of the second year at the age of eighteen.
Xiao Dagou, King of Xiyang, was named Renfu.
He is honest and steady by nature and does not play casually.
When he was seven years old, Emperor Gaozu once asked him what book he had read, and he replied that he should study "Poetry".
Emperor Gaozu ordered him to recite it. When he recited it, his voice was clear and loud, so Emperor Gaozu rewarded him with a scroll of calligraphy written by Wang Xizhi.
In the first year of Dashi, Xiao Dagou was granted the title of King of Xiyang County and was granted a settlement of 2,000 households.
He left the capital and served as General Xuanhui and Danyang Yin.
In the second year of Dashi, he was appointed as the governor of Yangzhou, but his title of general remained unchanged.
In the autumn of the Qian year, Xiao Dagou was killed at the age of thirteen.
King Xiao Dawei of Wuning was named Renrong.
Her appearance and temperament are both beautiful, and her eyebrows are as painted.
In the first year of Dabao, he was granted the title of King of Wuning County and had 2,000 households in the town.
In the second year of Dabao's reign, he left the capital and became General Xinwei and Danyang Yin.
In the autumn of this year, Xiao Dawei was killed at the age of thirteen.
Jianping Wang Xiao Daqiu's courtesy name is Renjue.
In the first year of Dabao's reign, he was granted the title of King of Jianping County and was granted a residence of 2,000 households.
Xiao Daqiu is smart and precocious by nature.
When Hou Jing besieged the capital, Emperor Gaozu had always sincerely believed in Buddhism. Every time he swore an oath and made a wish, he often said: If there are any sufferings that sentient beings should suffer, I, Xiao Yan, will bear them all.
Xiao Daqiu was just seven years old at that time. He was surprised when he heard what he said, so he said to his mother: If the emperor is like this, how dare I refuse to suffer?
Therefore, when paying homage to the Buddha at six o'clock in the morning, at noon, at sunset, at the beginning of the night, at the middle of the night, and at the end of the night, he also said: All the suffering and retribution that sentient beings should suffer will be borne by me, Lu Quebi, on your behalf.
This is how he was smart enough to meet people at a young age.
In the second year, he left Beijing and served as general of light vehicles and military commander of Shitousheng.
In the autumn of this year, Xiao Daqiu was killed at the age of eleven.
Xiao Daxin, King of Nghe An, also had the courtesy name Renlang.
When he was four years old, his mother, Mrs. Chen, passed away. He missed his mother and became sad and haggard, just like an adult mourning.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, during the mourning period, he went to greet Tai Sai, crying softly and unable to control himself. Seeing this scene, all the attendants on the left and right also covered their faces and cried.
In the first year of Dashi, Xiao Dating was granted the title of King of Yi'an County and was granted a settlement of 2,000 households.
In the second year of Zuoxuan's reign, he left the capital to serve as General Ningyuan and Governor of Langye and Pengcheng counties. He was killed before he could go to his post. He was eleven years old when he died.
Xiao Dazhi, king of Suijian, had the courtesy name Renying.
He has been brave and strong since he was a child, with courage and courage. After the capital was captured, he said with emotion: The real man will destroy these thieves.
summary: Xiao Dachun, King of Anlu, was well-read, filial, and physically strong. He held posts and was captured by rebels while fleeing. He was made King of Anlu and later killed at age twenty-two. Xiao Daya, Duke of Liuyang, was beloved by Gaozu. During the capital's fall, he fought rebels until overwhelmed and died from illness at age seventeen. Xiao Dazhuang, King of Xinxing, was killed at age eighteen. Xiao Dajun, King of Xiyang, was honest and recited poetry for Gaozu. He was killed at age thirteen. Xiao Dawei, King of Wuning, was handsome and killed at age thirteen. Xiao Daqiu, King of Jianping, was precocious and, at age seven, vowed to bear others' suffering. He was killed at age eleven. Xiao Daxin, King of Yi'an, mourned his mother deeply as a child. He was killed at age eleven before assuming his post. Xiao Dazhi, King of Suijian, was brave and vowed to destroy rebels. He was killed at age ten.

translation:
Seeing this scene, Shizu was very happy. He entered the palace and said to Concubine Xu: If there is another son with such talent, I have nothing to worry about.
Concubine Xu did not answer and left in tears.
Shizu was very angry about this, so he listed Xu Fei's unruly behavior one by one, and wrote it down and published it in the main cabinet.
When Xiao Fang and others entered the palace and saw him, they felt even more dangerous and felt uneasy.
At that time, the King of Hedong was the governor of Xiangzhou and did not obey the orders of the governor. Xiao Fang asked to be sent to conquer the King of Hedong. The ancestor agreed to his request, appointed him the governor, and ordered him to lead 20,000 elite troops to march south to conquer.
When Xiao Fang and others left, he said to his close friends: I am going on an expedition this time. There is no doubt that I will die; if I die well, how can I begrudge my life?
Xiao Fang and others led the army to Maxi, and the King of Hedong led his army to fight. Xiao Fang and others led the army to attack, but were defeated. Xiao Fang and others were drowned. He died at the age of twenty-two.
When Shidan heard the news of Xiao Fang and others' deaths, he was not sad.
Later, in memory of Xiao Fang and others' talents, Shizu posthumously awarded Xiao Fang and others the titles of Shizhong, General of the Chinese Army, and Governor of Yangzhou. Mi was a loyal and strong prince, and he called up his soul to mourn him.
Fang et al. annotated Fan Ye's "Hou Mo Shu", but it was not completed. He wrote "Thirty Kingdoms Spring and Autumn" and "Jingzhuzi", which are popular in the world.
Prince Zhenhui, Xiao Fang, also known as Zhixiang, was the second son of Shizu.
The biological mother is Mrs. Wang.
Xiao Fangzhu has been smart, enlightened and erudite since he was a child. He is proficient in "Lao" and "Yi". He is good at talking about metaphysics. His demeanor is elegant and unconventional, his words are fluent and very sharp. Xiao Fangzhu was especially loved by his ancestors, and his biological mother, Wang, was deeply favored.
After Xiao Fang and others died due to military defeat, Shizu said to Xiao Fangzhu: If it is not abandoned, there will be no prosperity.
He appointed Xiao Fangzhu as his lieutenant in the Zhongfu Army, and appointed him as the governor of Yingzhou to guard Jiangxia. He also appointed Bao Quan to be in charge of prefecture affairs to prevent the rebels from flowing down the river.
At that time, Shizu sent Xu Wensheng to lead the army, and they were in a stalemate with Hou Jing's general Ren Yue. The outcome was still undecided. Xiao Fangzhu relied on Xu Wensheng's army nearby. He did not care about military and political affairs. He and Bao Quan had fun every day by waving cattails and drinking.
Hou Jing heard the news, so he sent his general Song Zixian to lead hundreds of light cavalry to attack Xiao Fangzhu from the trail.
It was a windy and rainy day, and the sky was dark. Song Zixian led his army to Liaoxia. The people ran to report, but Lu Youzhan and Baoxing still didn't believe it and said: Xu Wensheng's army guarded the downstream passage, how could the thieves come here?
Then the city gate was ordered to be closed, but the rebel cavalry had already entered the city gate, and Liaoxia City was captured. Song Zixian captured Xiao Fangzhu and returned.
Wang Sengbian led his army to Caizhou, and Hou Jing killed Xiao Fangzhu.
Shizu was posthumously awarded the title of Shizhong and General.
Mi is the crown prince Zhenhui.
Shi Chen said: Although the sons of Taizong and Shizu founded the country and were crowned kings, the country was in a period of chaos and chaos. They were all imprisoned by bandits, and most of them died unexpectedly.
summary: The text also records Shizu's sons. Xiao Fang, the Zhongzhuang prince, was intelligent and loved nature. He wrote a treatise expressing his desire for a carefree life. After his mother lost favor, he felt endangered. He led troops to rescue the capital and later to conquer the King of Hedong, but was defeated and drowned at age twenty-two. Shizu was not saddened by his death but later posthumously honored him. Xiao Fangzhu, the Zhenhui prince, was erudite and favored. After his brother's death, he was appointed to guard Jiangxia but neglected duties, enjoying leisure. He was captured by a surprise rebel attack and killed. The historian laments that these princes, though ennobled, were imprisoned by bandits and died untimely deaths during the era's chaos.

translation:
Emperor Gaozu Wu's name was Yan, whose courtesy name was Shuda and whose nickname was Lian'er. He was a native of Zhongduli in Nanlanling and a descendant of Xiao He, the Prime Minister of the Han Dynasty.
Xiao He gave birth to Xiao Yan, the Marquis of Fengding, Xiao Yan gave birth to Xiao Biao, Xiao Biao gave birth to Xiao Zhang, the Duke's official, Xiao Zhang gave birth to Xiao Hao, Xiao Hao gave birth to Xiao Yang, Xiao Yang gave birth to the prince Taifu Wangzhi, Wangzhi gave birth to Guanglu doctor Xiao Yu, Xiao Yu gave birth to Xiao Shao, the censor, Xiao Shao gave birth to Guangluxun Xiao Hong, Xiao's boudoir gave birth to Xiao Chan, the prefect of Jiyin, Xiao Chan gave birth to Xiao Bing, the prefect of Wujun. Xiao Bao, the prime minister of Zhongshan, was born in Bing, Xiao Bao was born in doctor Xiao Zhou, Xiao Jiao was born in Xiao Jiao, the chief of Sheqiu, Xiao Kui was born in the state, Xiao Kui was born in Xiao Xiu, Xiao Xiu was born in Xiao Bao, the prime minister of Guangling County, Xiao Bao was born in Xiao Bao, the Taizhong doctor, Xiao Zheng was born in Huaiyin, Xiao Zheng was born in Xiao Ju, the prefect of Jiyin, Xiao Ju was the deputy son of Zhizhong in Nantai, and the deputy son was the son of Nantai Zhizhi. The late father of Emperor Daoci was named Shunzhi, and he was the younger brother of Emperor Qi Gao.
Because he participated in assisting the emperor in starting a business, he was granted the title of Marquis of Linxiang County.
He served successively as a servant, including Prince Wei Zhan Shi, leading general, Danyang Yin, and was given as a gift to General Zhenbei.
Emperor Gaozu was born in the residence of Tongxiali Sanqiao in Moling County in the eighth year of the Ming Dynasty, that is, the Jiachen year of Xiaowu in the Song Dynasty.
He was born strange and abnormal, with two bones connected between his two strands, a protruding top of his head, and a tattoo on his right hand for "Martial".
When the emperor grew up, he was knowledgeable, fond of strategy, and talented in civil and military affairs. He was highly praised by secular people and celebrities.
The room where I live often seems to be surrounded by clouds and mist, and people who pass by are in awe.
When he first became an official, he was appointed as the king of Baling, Nanzhong Lang, Fa Cao Xing joined the army, and was promoted to the general of the guard.
Wang Jian valued him very much when they first met him, and said to Lu Hongren maggot: "This man will be a poet within thirty years old, and beyond that he will be worthless."
Prince Liang of Jingling set up an official residence in Youpan, attracting learned people. Gaozu, Xuanqu, Xie Tiao, Wang Rong, Xiao Chen, Fan Yun, Ren Fang, Lu Bian and others socialized here, and they were known as the Eight Friends.
Wang Rong was handsome and clear, with extraordinary insight and ability to identify talents. He especially respected Gaozu. He often said to those close to him: The ruler of the world must belong to this person.
Zhenxi, who was repeatedly promoted to follow the king, consulted to join the army, but soon resigned due to mourning for his late father.
In the early years of Longchang, Emperor Ming assisted the government and appointed Gaozu as General Ningshuo to guard Shouchun.
After the period of mourning was over, he was appointed as the crown prince's concubine, the assistant minister of Huangmen, and went on duty in the palace and Taiwan Province.
Because of his participation in Xiao Chen and others' efforts to establish the emperor, he was granted the title of male from Jianyang County and had 300 households living in the city.
summary: Emperor Gaozu Wu, named Yan, with the courtesy name Shuda and nickname Lian'er, was a descendant of Xiao He, the Han Dynasty Prime Minister, from Zhongduli in Nanlanling. His lineage traced back through generations of officials, including his father Shunzhi, who was granted the title of Marquis of Linxiang County for assisting the emperor. Gaozu was born in the eighth year of the Ming Dynasty in Moling County, displaying unusual traits like connected bones in his legs, a protruding head, and a tattoo of "Martial" on his right hand. He grew up knowledgeable, skilled in strategy, and talented in civil and military affairs, often surrounded by clouds and mist in his residence. He began his official career as a king of Baling and was later promoted to general. Wang Jian predicted he would become a poet within thirty years. Gaozu socialized with notable figures like Xie Tiao and Wang Rong, known as the Eight Friends. Wang Rong respected him greatly, believing he would rule the world. After his father's death, Gaozu served as General Ningshuo to guard Shouchun, then as crown prince's concubine and assistant minister. He was granted the title of male from Jianyang County for his role in establishing the emperor.

translation:
In the second year of Jianwu's reign, the Northern Wei Dynasty sent generals Liu Chang and Wang Su to lead the army to invade Sizhou. Gaozu was appointed as the champion general and military leader, and Wang Guang, the governor of Jiangzhou, served as reinforcements.
When they were more than a hundred miles away from Yiyang, everyone was afraid and hesitant because of the strong army of the Northern Wei Dynasty. No one dared to march.
Gaozu asked for orders to go ahead, and Wang Guang assigned his elite troops to serve Gaozu.
That night, he marched forward. When he was a few miles away from the Northern Wei army, he went straight to Xianshou Mountain.
The Northern Wei army did not know how many troops came and did not dare to approach.
At dawn, the people in the city saw reinforcements arriving, so the army went out of the city to attack the camp gate of the Northern Wei army. The troops led by Emperor Gaozu attacked from outside.
The troops of the Northern Wei Dynasty were attacked both internally and externally, so they abandoned the siege and withdrew.
After the battle, Gaozu was appointed as Sima, King of Jin'an, and Grand Administrator of Huailing in the right army.
After returning, he served as the crown prince's concubine and led the Yulin Supervisor.
Soon, he went out to guard the stone.
In the fourth year, Emperor Wei personally led an army to invade Yongzhou, and Emperor Ming ordered Zhidan to go to the rescue.
In October, when they arrived at Xiangyang, they were ordered to send Zuo Min Shangshu Cui Huijing to lead the army. Gaozu and Yongzhou governor Cao Hu were all under his control.
In March of the following year, Huijing and Gaozu marched to Dengcheng, and Commander Wei suddenly arrived with more than 100,000 cavalry.
Jiang Jing became panicked and planned to retreat, but Gaozu resolutely stopped him and refused to obey, so he hurriedly withdrew.
The cavalry of the Northern Wei Dynasty took the opportunity to attack him and was defeated.
Only Emperor Gaozu led his army to resist and killed nearly a hundred enemies. The cavalry of the Northern Wei Dynasty retreated slightly, so they were able to form a formation and break off, and they were not able to disembark until evening.
Huijing's army was almost exhausted, and only Gaozu returned with his army intact.
Soon Gaozu was appointed to conduct affairs in Yongzhou.
In July, he was still appointed as Chijie, Commander-in-Chief of the four prefectures of Yongliang, North and South Qin, Yingzhou, Jingling and Sizhou, all military affairs, general of the auxiliary country, and governor of Yongzhou.
In the first month of dispatch, Emperor Ming passed away and ascended the throne in the early evening. Yangzhou governor Shi'an Wang Yaoguang, Shangshu Ling Xu Xiaosi, Shangshu Youpu Jiji, General Shi Xiao Tanzhi, Shi Zhongjiang Si, and Wei Wei Liu Xuan took turns to be on duty in the palace, signing their opinions on memorials every day as imperial orders.
After Emperor Gaozu heard about it, he said to his mother's uncle and brother Zhang Hongce: The administration of government comes from multiple families, which is the cause of trouble.
The Book of Songs says: There are three princes in power in a country. Whose do we obey?
What's more, there are six people in power now, how can it be possible?
If a grudge is formed, they will kill each other. Now there is only one place to avoid disaster.
If you diligently practice benevolence and righteousness, you can naturally become Xibo.
It's just that my brothers are in Kyoto and may encounter troubles in the world, so they need to plan this matter with Yizhou.
At that time, Xiao Yi, the eldest brother of Emperor Gaozu, returned from his dismissal from Yizhou and went on to engage in affairs in Yingzhou. So he sent Hongce to Yingzhou and stated his strategy to Xiao Yi: In the past, Jin Hui was a fatuous master, and kings competed for power. As a result, internal troubles arose nine times and foreign invaders were attracted three times.
summary: In the second year of Jianwu, the Northern Wei Dynasty invaded Sizhou. Gaozu, as champion general, led reinforcements. Despite fear among the troops, he marched ahead, surprising the Northern Wei army and forcing them to retreat. He was later appointed as Sima and Grand Administrator of Huailing. In the fourth year, he defended against another invasion, leading his army to resist and kill nearly a hundred enemies, returning intact while others suffered losses. He was then appointed to conduct affairs in Yongzhou.

translation:
Now six dignitaries are vying for power. Each controls the king's law and controls the monarch's signature on official documents. Each wants to dominate the power, and even the smallest grievances are enmity, and they will kill each other as expected.
Moreover, when the succeeding monarch was in the East Palace, he did not have a good reputation. He was intimate with those around him, was cruel to others, and the prime minister would indulge his desires. How could he be willing to occupy the throne in vain and only express his consent and entrust government affairs to the court ministers?
As mutual suspicion accumulates over time, great killings will surely occur.
Shi'an wants to become Tailun, and the signs have been revealed. There is really no such reason for a lame person to ascend to heaven.
What's more, if you are very jealous and narrow-minded by nature, you will only bring trouble to yourself.
The only people who want to be in power are Jiang Zhe and Liu Xuan.
Jiang Zhe is cowardly and indecisive, Liu Xuan is weak and incapable, and his lack of strength and heavy responsibility will lead to failure.
Xiao Tanzhi is jealous and hurts others with his words. Xu Xiaosi's talents are not the backbone and can be manipulated by others. If conflicts intensify and chaos arises, things will surely fall apart internally and externally.
Now that I can guard the outer vassal, I am lucky enough to find a way to settle down. A wise person can foresee the omens from the subtle changes in things, and it does not take long.
While suspicion and prevention have not yet become widespread, we should summon all the younger brothers to gather in time.
If you take precautions later, there will be no way to escape.
Yingzhou surrounds Jingzhou and Xiangzhou, and flows into Moshui and Mianshui to the west. Yongzhou has tens of thousands of soldiers and horses, and among them are tigers and cypresses to observe the world.
When the era is peaceful and the society is stable, you should be loyal to your dynasty. When the current situation is in chaos, you can cut off violence for the country. You can move forward and retreat freely with the changes of the world. Dismissal is a safe strategy.
If you didn't plan it earlier, you would regret it.
Xiao Jing's expression changed after hearing this, but he didn't agree with it.
After Hongce came back, Gaozu set out to meet his younger brothers Xiao Wei and Xiao Dan, and arrived in Xiangyang in the first year of his life.
So they secretly manufactured military equipment, cut down large quantities of bamboo, and sank it in Tanxi River, secretly using it as spare materials for building ships.
The houses they lived in at that time were often surrounded by five colors of green, red, white, black and yellow, and the shape was like a coiled dragon, with purple air rising from it, and the shape was like an umbrella cover. Everyone who saw it found it strange.
In the winter of the second year of Yongyuan, news of Xiao Yi's murder came. Emperor Gaozu secretly summoned Chang Shi Wang Mao, Zhongbing Lu Sengzhen, Biejia Liu Qingyuan, Gong Cao Shi Ji Shizhan and others to plan.
After the plan was made, in November, Yisi summoned his staff in the official hall and told them: In the past, King Wu held an alliance in Mengjin and said that Yin Zhou could be conquered. Now the fatuous monarch is full of evil, doing his best to commit extreme cruelty, killing the virtuous officials of the court, leaving few descendants, and making the people miserable. It is God's will to kill him.
You must unite to hate evil, work together for righteousness, and obtain the status of princes, generals and ministers. It is indeed on this day that you can do your best. I will never break my promise.
Send one day to set up the banner of uprising.
summary: After Emperor Ming's death, six officials took turns governing, causing chaos. Gaozu warned his brother Zhang Hongce about the dangers of multiple rulers, predicting internal conflict. He advised gathering his brothers and preparing for potential turmoil. He secretly manufactured military equipment and stored bamboo in Tanxi River for shipbuilding. In the second year of Yongyuan, after Xiao Yi's murder, Gaozu summoned his staff and planned an uprising. He recruited over 10,000 soldiers, 1,000 horses, and 3,000 ships, building warships from bamboo.

translation:
So he recruited and gathered more than 10,000 armored soldiers, more than 1,000 war horses, and 3,000 ships. They built warships out of bamboo and wood in Tanxi River.
Previously, Donghun appointed Liu Shanyang as the governor of Brazil, equipped with 3,000 elite soldiers, and sent him to Jingzhou to attack Xiangyang with Xiao Yingzhou accompanying him.
Emperor Gaozu knew of their plan, so he sent soldiers Wang Tianhu and Pang Qingguo to Jiangling to write to all states.
When they were heading west from Shanyang, Emperor Gaozu said to the generals: Jingzhou was originally afraid of the Xiangyang people, and because of the cold lips and teeth, it felt like a bird with a wounded bow. Wouldn't they secretly agree with me?
If I unite the troops of Jingzhou and Yongzhou, sweep and pacify Shuxia, even if Han Xin and Bai Qi are reincarnated, they will not be able to do anything to me.
What's more, what about the group of servants who are used by the incomparable and foolish Lord to convey his will?
I can send Shan Yang to Jingzhou and he will be killed immediately. You guys can try and see what happens.
When Shanyang arrived at Baling, Emperor Gaozu once again ordered Tianhu to bring a letter to Yingzhou brothers.
After he left, Emperor Gaozu said to Zhang Hongce: The best way to use military force is to attack the heart. Siege is second, psychological warfare is the top priority, and fighting between two soldiers is the second priority. This is what happened today.
Not long ago, Tianhu was sent to the state capital, and everyone got letters.
This time the post horse trip was very urgent, and there were only two letters to the acting brothers, saying that Tianhu would state it face to face. When asked about it, Tianhu had nothing to say. The acting brother could not know anything, and he was not allowed to talk nonsense.
Tianhu was Xingxing's most capable confidant. After hearing this, he must have thought that Xingxing and Tianhu were hiding something together, so everyone became suspicious.
Shan Yang was deceived by everyone's words and became suspicious of them, so he couldn't make his own progress and retreat, and he was bound to fall into my plan.
This is sending two empty letters to decide the fate of a state.
When Shanyang arrived in Jiang'an and learned of this situation, he was indeed suspicious of going west.
Yingzhou was very frightened, so he killed Tianhu and gave his head to Shanyang.
Shan Yang believed him and rode in with dozens of people. Ying Zhou ambushed the soldiers, beheaded him, and gave his head to Gaozu.
He also reported his plan to honor King Nankang as emperor, and said: "The time is unfavorable, we should wait until February of the next year; if we march in a hurry."
I'm afraid it's not the emperor's plan for the war. Emperor Gaozu replied: Nowadays, there are 100,000 soldiers in armor waiting for the enemy, and the military supplies of food and grass will soon be exhausted. Moreover, the moral heart based on it is a moment of bravery and sharpness. As time goes by, many things happen, but we are still afraid of suspicion and slackness. If we camp for a hundred days, we will definitely regret.
If children deviate, great things will not succeed.
Now that Taibai Star appears in the West, he acts based on morality and has destiny and plans. What's the disadvantage?
The plan has been decided, how can it be stopped midway?
In the past, King Wu's campaign against Yin Zhou was contrary to Tai Sui's actions. How long do we have to wait?
Cao Jingzong, the prefect of Jingling, sent Du Sichong to persuade Gaozu to welcome King Nankang and build his capital in Xiangbao. After Zheng Zheng confirmed the throne, he then marched, but Gaozu did not listen.
Wang Mao said to Zhang Hongce privately: I serve Jiexia without any hesitation; however, now that Nankang is in the hands of others, others can use the emperor to command the princes, and Jiexia will be ordered around by others. Is this a plan for troubled times?
Hongce told Gaozu about the affair, and Chanzu said: If the great things in the future are not successful, the good and the bad will perish together; if the achievements can be completed, the world will be intimidated, and the world will be commanded, who dares to disobey!
Which Xiang is mediocre and incapable of being manipulated?
When they arrive at Shicheng, they will tell Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong face to face.
Xinye County was established south of Mianshui to gather the newly converted people.
In February of the third year, King Nankang belonged to the Xiangguo, and he appointed Gaozu as the general of Zhengsu, and assigned him to the propaganda department.
Wushen, Emperor Gaozu set out from Xiangyang.
His younger brother Xiao Wei was left to guard Xiangyang City and manage the affairs of the state government, his younger brother Xiao Dan was to guard Licheng, Sima Zhuang Qiuhei was to guard Fan City, Shi Jishixun, the meritorious officer, was also the chief historian, Huang Sizu, the leader of the White Horse garrison, was also the Sima, Du Yong, the county magistrate, was also in charge of farewell, and Guo Yan, the green minister of the Xiaofu, was in charge of transferring food and wages.
summary: Gaozu sent letters to various states, anticipating that Liu Shanyang, sent by Donghun to attack Xiangyang, would be killed. His strategy succeeded, and Shanyang was beheaded. Gaozu then marched from Xiangyang in February of the third year, leaving his brothers to guard key cities. He issued a proclamation condemning the cruel ruler for his tyranny, including killing loyal ministers, indulging in debauchery, and causing widespread suffering.
