translation:
Dongfang Shuo, courtesy name Manqian, was born in Yanci County, Pingyuan County.
Not long after Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he asked the world to recommend scholars with talents such as integrity, virtuousness, and literature, and appointed them with special positions. Scholars from all over the world wrote letters to discuss the gains and losses of national affairs. As soon as Dongfang Shuo arrived in Chang'an, he wrote a letter saying: I, Dongfang Shuo, lost his parents when he was young and was raised by his brother and sister-in-law.
He started studying at the age of thirteen and learned writing and note-taking in three years.
Learned fencing at the age of fifteen.
At the age of sixteen, he studied the Book of Songs and Shangshu and recited 220,000 words.
At the age of nineteen, he studied Sun Wu's Art of War, and recited 220,000 words on battle formations, control of the advance and retreat of troops during battles, etc.
I memorized a total of 440,000 words.
He is also often familiar with Zilu's remarks.
I am twenty-two years old, nine feet three inches tall, my eyes are as bright as hanging pearls, my teeth are as neat and white as strings of shells, I am as brave as Meng Ben, as agile as Qing Ji, as honest as Uncle Bao, and as trustworthy as Weisheng.
A person like this can be a minister of the emperor. My minister Dongfang Shuo risked his life to pay homage to the emperor again.
Dongfang Shuo's letter was not modest, but he praised and promoted himself. However, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty thought that he was a great man and ordered him to stay with Shao in the Gongche Mansion. However, his salary was meager and he could not receive an interview from Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
After a long time, Dongfang Shuo once coaxed the dwarf who guarded the royal horse pen and said: The emperor thinks that you people are of no use to the court. Of course, you cannot keep up with others in farming. You are an official above the people and cannot manage civil affairs. You are not qualified to fight with soldiers when you join the army. You are of no use to the country. You will only waste food and clothing. Now the emperor wants to kill you all.
The dwarfs were very frightened and cried.
Dongfang Shuo instigated them and said: The emperor is about to pass by here, you must kowtow and apologize.
After meeting for a while, they heard that the emperor was passing by, and the dwarfs all knelt on the ground and kowtowed in tears. The emperor asked: Why are you doing this?
The dwarfs replied: Dongfang Shuo said that the emperor wants to kill us all.
The emperor knew that Dongfang Shuohuahua had a lot of intestines, so he summoned Dongfang Shuo and asked him: Why did you threaten those dwarfs?
Dongfang Shuo replied: My minister Dongfang Shuo will say it even when he is alive, and he will say it even after he is dead.
The dwarf is more than three feet tall and his salary is two hundred and forty yuan for a bag of millet.
The minister Dongfang Shuo is more than nine feet tall, and his salary is a bag of millet, worth two hundred and forty yuan.
The dwarf was starving to death, and his minister Dongfang Shuo was starving to death.
If my words can be accepted, I hope you will change your etiquette towards me; if not, please let me go home and don't let me eat rice from Chang'an in vain.
Emperor Wu laughed when he heard this, so he asked Dongfang Shuo to wait for Shao Jin Mamen, and gradually gained the emperor's closeness.
summary: Dongfang Shuo, courtesy name Manqian, was born in Yanci County, Pingyuan County. After Emperor Wu of Han ascended the throne, he sought scholars of integrity and literature. Dongfang Shuo wrote a letter to the emperor, boasting of his abilities: he studied writing at thirteen, fencing at fifteen, and by sixteen had memorized 220,000 words of the *Book of Songs* and *Shangshu*. At nineteen, he memorized another 220,000 words of Sun Wu's *Art of War*. He described himself as tall, brave, agile, honest, and trustworthy, claiming he could serve as a minister. Emperor Wu, impressed by his audacity, ordered him to stay at the Gongche Mansion, though his salary was meager and he received no audience.

translation:
Emperor Wu once asked some magicians who were good at divination to cover the gecko under a basin and asked them to guess what it was, but they couldn't guess it. Dongfang Shuo introduced himself and said: I once studied "Yi", please allow me to guess what it is.
So he arranged the yarrow into various hexagrams and replied: I think it is a dragon without horns, but I think it is a snake with legs, its limbs are connected by pulses, and it is good at climbing walls. This thing is either a gecko or a lizard.
The emperor said: You guessed it right.
Give him ten pieces of silk.
He was also asked to guess other things, and he guessed correctly every time. He was given silk every time.
At that time, there was a favored actor Guo Sheren in the palace. He was very funny and often accompanied Emperor Wu. He said: Dongfang Shuo is too crazy. It was just a lucky guess. There is no real magic.
I hope to let Dongfang Shuo guess again. If he guesses correctly, he will give me a hundred lashes; if he guesses incorrectly, he will give me silk.
So he put the parasitic thing growing on the tree under the pot and asked Dongfang Shuo to guess what it was. Dongfang Shuo said: It is Baosou.
Guo Sheren said: I really know that Dongfang Shuo will not guess correctly.
Dongfang Shuo said: Raw meat is called 荍, dried meat is called preserved meat, attached to a tree is called parasite, and covered under a basin is called dou sau.
The emperor ordered Chang Jian to whip Guo Sheren. Guo Sheren was in unbearable pain and howled loudly.
Dongfang Shuo laughed at him and said: Hey, there is no hair on his mouth, he is screaming, and his butt is getting higher and higher.
Guo Sheren said angrily: Dongfang Shuo dared to slander and insult the emperor's attendants. He should be sentenced to death for abandoning the market.
The emperor asked Dongfang Shuo: Why did you slander and insult him?
Dongfang Shuo replied: I dare not slander or insult him, I just told him a riddle. The emperor asked: What riddle are you talking about?
Dongfang Shuo said: The hairless mouth is a dog hole; the cry is the cry of a mother bird when feeding her chicks; the buttocks are getting higher and higher, which is the look of a crane lowering its head to peck at food.
Guo Sheren was not convinced and said, "I hope to ask Dongfang Shuo a riddle as well. If he doesn't know it, he should also be whipped."
He immediately made up a riddle with homophonic sounds and said: Ling Huhan, Lao Botu, Yiyouya, Biaopanya.
What is said?
Dongfang Shuo said: Ling is an order.
Pots are used to hold things.
It means the teeth are not straight.
Lao is an old man that everyone respects.
Bai is the palace of ghosts.
Painting is a road that is soaked.
Iyoya's words were slurred.
Biaopanya is a fight between two dogs.
Dongfang Shuo answered Guo She's riddles in the world, with many clever and clever changes. No riddle could stump him, and everyone present was very surprised.
The emperor appointed Dongfang Shuo as the Chang Shilang, and he gained the favor and favor of Emperor Wu.
After a long time, on a doggy day, Emperor Wu ordered that meat be rewarded to the attendant officials.
summary: Dongfang Shuo once tricked the dwarfs guarding the royal horse pen, claiming the emperor planned to kill them for being useless. When the dwarfs tearfully begged the emperor, he summoned Dongfang Shuo, who argued that the dwarfs were short and received the same salary as him, a tall man, leading to unfairness. Emperor Wu laughed and promoted him to a closer position. Later, Dongfang Shuo correctly guessed a gecko under a basin using the *I Ching*, earning silk rewards. When a courtier challenged him, he guessed a parasitic growth on a tree, proving his skill. He also cleverly deflected accusations of slander with riddles, impressing the emperor, who appointed him Chang Shilang.

translation:
The high official did not come to divide the meat until nightfall, so Dongfang Shuo drew his sword and cut the meat alone, saying to his colleagues: "I should go home early in the dog days of summer. Please allow me to accept the emperor's reward."
Then he wrapped the meat in his arms and left.
Daguancheng reported this matter to the emperor.
When Dongfang Shuo entered the palace, Emperor Wu said: Yesterday, you gave me meat, but you cut the meat with your sword and left without waiting for the order to be issued. Why is this?
Dongfang Shuo took off his hat and knelt down to apologize.
The emperor said: Sir, stand up and blame yourself.
Dongfang Shuo paid his respects again and said: Dongfang Shuo!
Dongfang Shuo!
How rude to accept a reward without waiting for the order to be issued!
Drawing a sword to cut flesh, how heroic!
Not much meat is cut, but how honest it is!
How kind it is to go home and give meat to your wife to eat!
The emperor smiled and said: Mr. Jean blames himself, but he actually praises himself!
He also gave him a stone of wine and a hundred catties of meat and asked him to go home and give them to his wife.
At the beginning, in the third year of Jianyuan, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty began to travel incognito, traveling to Chiyang Palace in the north, Huangshan Palace in the west, Changyang Palace in the south, and Yichun Palace in the east.
Traveling in private is often done every year when the new wine is brewed and drank in the ancestral temple.
In August and September, the emperor agreed to wait at the gate of the palace with his attendants, regular attendants, and martial cavalry, as well as the good men from Longxi County and Beidi County in Shaoguan who were good at riding and shooting. Therefore, the title of "Qimen" came from this time.
When Emperor Wu traveled incognito, he would wait ten quarters at night before setting off, often pretending to be Cao Shou, Marquis of Pingyang.
At dawn the next day, when they arrived at the foot of Zhongnan Mountain, they shot deer, pigs, foxes and rabbits, or struck bears with their bare hands, running through the rice fields. The farmers shouted and cursed loudly, gathered together, and complained to the magistrates of Yuxian and Duxian counties.
The county magistrate went to the hunting place and asked to see Pingyang Hou. The attendants on horseback wanted to whip the magistrate.
The county magistrate was furious, and his subordinates scolded and stopped him. Several horsemen who were hunting were detained, so they took out the emperor's royal belongings and struggled for a long time before they were able to leave.
At the beginning, the emperor left the palace late at night and returned the next evening. Later, he carried food for five days. He did not return to the capital until the fifth day when it was time to go to Changxin Palace to see the Queen Mother.
Emperor Wu liked this kind of hunting in disguise very much. After that, the people at the foot of Zhongnan Mountain learned that the emperor often went hunting incognito, but Emperor Wu was still under pressure from the Queen Mother and did not dare to travel far.
The Prime Minister and Censor knew the emperor's intentions, so he sent Lieutenant You Fu to patrol east of Changyang Palace, and ordered You Neishi to recruit civilians and go to the place where the emperor hunted to wait for orders.
Later, dressing rooms were privately set up for the emperor, and palace staff were also assigned. A total of twelve dressing rooms were set up from the south of Xuanqu Palace for the emperor to rest and change during the day, and to stay in various palaces at night. Emperor Wu often visited Changyang, Wuzha, Beiyang, Xuanqu and other palaces.
summary: On a dog day, Dongfang Shuo cut meat from the emperor's reward without waiting for orders, taking it home. When questioned, he humorously blamed himself, praising his own actions, which amused Emperor Wu, who rewarded him with wine and meat. Emperor Wu often hunted incognito, causing distress to farmers. He planned to build Shanglin Garden, but Dongfang Shuo admonished him, citing three reasons: it would ruin fertile land, destroy homes and tombs, and waste resources. He warned against luxury, referencing historical examples like King Zhou of Yin and Qin Shihuang. Despite this, Emperor Wu built the garden but promoted Dongfang Shuo to Taizhong doctor.

translation:
If one day I am suddenly unable to fulfill my duties in serving the Emperor, and I have to fill the gap first, I feel regretful privately that I cannot fulfill my wish to repay His Majesty. I hope that Your Majesty can sometimes forget about government affairs, recuperate his spirit, and walk a few more steps to visit my mansion when returning from the courtyard, so that I can offer wine to His Majesty on his birthday and be by your side to make you happy.
If you can do this, even if you are dead, what regrets will there be! The emperor said: What is your Majesty worried about?
Hope you recover soon.
I'm worried that there will be too many ministers and attendants accompanying you, which will cost you too much.
After Emperor Wu finished speaking, he returned to the palace. Soon, the Taishu recovered from his illness and went to court to see the emperor. The Emperor spent 10 million yuan to buy a banquet and drink with the Taishu.
A few days later, Emperor Wu came to the Grand Master's mansion. The Grand Master put on a cook's apron and personally led Emperor Wu into the mansion. He climbed up the steps and invited Emperor Wu to sit down in the hall.
Before he could sit down, Emperor Wu said: I hope to meet the protagonist.
The Grand Master hurriedly went down to the palace, took off the hairpin and earrings, kowtowed with bare feet and apologized, saying: "I have no face to see others, I have failed Your Majesty, and I have committed a capital crime."
Your Majesty will not accuse me of any crime, but I will kowtow to plead guilty.
Emperor Wu issued an edict to absolve the Grand Master of his crime.
The Grand Master put on the hairpin and shoes, stood up, and went to the Shuxiang Room to lead Dong Yan out.
Dong Yan, wearing the green scarf used by servants to wrap their heads and sleeves, followed the Grand Master to the front of the palace and fell prostrate to the ground.
The Grand Master then introduced: Dong Yan, the cook of Princess Guantao, risked his life to pay homage to the Emperor.
Dong Yan took the opportunity to kowtow and plead guilty, and the emperor asked him to get up.
The imperial edict gave him clothes and hats to allow him to go to the palace.
Dong Yan got up, went to change clothes and sit down.
The Grand Master personally presented food and toasts to Emperor Wu.
At this time, although Dong Yan was respected but without a title, he was called the "master". The king and his ministers drank happily and were extremely happy.
The Grand Master then presented a large amount of gold, money, and various colored silks, and asked Emperor Wu to give them to the generals, princes, and attendant officials. From then on, Dong Yan became more prominent and favored, and everyone in the world knew about him.
Dog racing, horse racing, football, and swordsmen from various counties gathered around Dong Yan.
Dong Yan often followed Emperor Wu to play games in Beigong, go to Shanglin Garden to enjoy horse racing and hunting, and watch cockfighting, football, dog racing, horse racing and other games. The emperor liked these entertainments very much.
So the emperor held a banquet in the Xuan room to entertain Mrs. Dou, and sent an audience to introduce Dong Yan into the palace.
At this time, Dongfang Shuo was guarding under the palace steps with his halberd. He put down his halberd and stepped forward and said to Emperor Wu: "Dong Yan has committed three crimes that deserve to be beheaded. How can he be allowed to enter the palace?"
The emperor said: What is the crime?
Dongfang Shuo said: As a subject of the emperor, Dong Yan served the princess privately. This was the first crime.
Corrupting the moral etiquette between men and women, disrupting the marriage ceremony, and destroying the court system are the second crimes.
Your Majesty is in the prime of life and is now devoted to studying the Six Classics, paying attention to state affairs, following the prosperous times of Tang and Yu, and admiring the virtuous monarchs of Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties. Dong Yan did not follow the advice and study of the classics. Instead, he admired extravagant beauty, pursued luxury, indulged in sensual pleasures, and walked the path of evil and lewdness. This man was a great thief of the country and a ghost who deceived the emperor.
Dong Yan was the culprit of sexual immorality, and this was his third crime.
Once upon a time, Song Gongji encountered a fire and was burned to death because she abided by etiquette and waited for her nanny. She was respected by the princes. What should she do? His Majesty.
Emperor Wu remained silent for a long time and then said: I have already arranged a banquet and will correct it later.
summary: When Lord Zhaoping, son of Princess Longlu, killed a nanny and faced execution, Emperor Wu mourned but upheld the law. Dongfang Shuo congratulated him, praising his impartiality. The emperor initially scolded him but later accepted his explanation that wine could relieve sorrow. Dongfang Shuo was demoted for urinating in the palace but reinstated after this exchange. He also advised against allowing Dong Yan, a favorite of Princess Guantao, into the palace, citing three crimes. Emperor Wu heeded his advice, and Dong Yan's influence waned.

translation:
I hope your Majesty will pay attention to the above matters.
Although Dongfang Shuo was humorous and funny, he always observed the emperor's face and spoke out when appropriate. Emperor Wu often adopted his opinions.
From the ministers to the ministers in office, Dongfang Shuo dared to despise and ridicule, and there was no one he was willing to submit to.
Because Dongfang Shuo was witty and quick-tongued, the emperor liked to ask Dongfang Shuo questions deliberately.
Emperor Wu once asked Dongfang Shuo: Sir, what kind of monarch do you think I am?
Dongfang Shuo replied: From the prosperous times of Tang and Yu to the eras of King Cheng and King Kang of Zhou, it can be compared to the current world.
I think your majesty’s merits and virtues can be ranked above those of the Five Emperors and Three Kings.
Not only that, as expected, the wise men in the world were truly obtained, and the ministers and officials in office all had qualified candidates.
For example, Zhou Gongdan and Shao Gongshi were the prime ministers, Confucius was the censor, Jiang Taigong was the general, Bi Gonggao was the Taishi, Bian Yanyu was the Weiwei, Gaotao was Dali, Houji was Simong, and Yi Yin was In the Shaofu, Zigong was sent as an envoy to foreign countries, Yan Hui and Min Ziqian were doctors, Zixia was Taichang, Yi was Youfufeng, Zilu was Zhijinwu, Qi was Dahonglu, Guanlongfeng was Zongzheng, Boyi was Jingzhaoyin, Guan Zhong was Zuo Feng Yi, Lu Ban was the general and great craftsman, Zhong Shanfu was the official of Guanglu, Shen Bo was the imperial servant, Yanling Jizi was the captain of Shuiheng, Baili Xi was the Dianguo, Liu Xiahui was the Da Changqiu, and Shi Yu was the The prime minister was Sizhi, Zang Boyu was the Taifu, Confucius was the Minister of Zhan, Sun Shuao was the Prime Minister of the princes, Zi Chan was the county governor, Wang Qingji was a minister, Xia Yu was a Dingguan, Yi was a Taoist minister, and Song Wan was a Shi Daohou.
Emperor Wu burst out laughing after hearing this.
At this time, there were a large number of capable people in the court, and the emperor asked Dongfang Shuo: Today, Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, Doctor Ni Kuan, Dong Zhongshu, Xiahou Shichang, Sima Xiangru, King Wuqiu Shou, Zhufu Yan, Zhu Maichen, Yan Zhu, Ji An, Jiaocang, Zhongjun, Yan An, Xu Le, Sima Qian, etc. are all eloquent, intelligent and eloquent. Sir, see for yourself, how can you compare with them?
Dongfang Shuo replied: "I see that they have shovel teeth, tree bark gills, turned lips, long necks, knotted feet, even trousers, a meandering and sloping walk, and a bent body. Although Dongfang Shuo is not very good, he still has the advantages of these people."
Dongfang Shuo's speeches and responses are all like this.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty had recruited outstanding men and women, weighed their talents, and was afraid of making mistakes when appointing them.
At that time, the foreign economic strategy was to ensure peace and stability, and the internal system was being established. The country was troubled. From the prime minister, Gong Huanhong, to the Siwuqian capital, they were ordered to go abroad, and some served as county governors, princes, ministers, and even ministers. Hui Zuosu was once an official and became a doctor in Taizhong, and later he often served as a minister. He, Meigao and Guo Sheren were all around Emperor Wu, and they were just humorous and mocking attendants.
After a long time, Dongfang Shuo wrote to Chen Zuonong about his plan to strengthen the country through war. He took the opportunity to say that he had never been a high official and wanted to ask the emperor for a trial.
His memorial only used the remarks of Shang Yang and Han Fei. It was debauched and humorous. It contained tens of thousands of words, but was not reused in the end.
Dongfang Shuo then wrote a book and argued that if a guest accused him, he would use his low status to comfort and relieve himself with good words.
That article said:
Someone asked Dongfang Shuo: As soon as Su Qin and Zhang Yi met the monarch with ten thousand chariots, they became ministers, and their favor was passed down to future generations.
Now, sir, you practice the Taoism of the ancient emperors, admire the morality of the saints, recite and recite the "Poetry", "Books" and the books of hundreds of schools of thought, write books and treatises on bamboo slips and white silk.
However, for a long time, the emperor who tried his best to serve the sage with all his loyalty could no longer hold an official position like a minister, or hold a halberd in his position. It must be that his moral character still has shortcomings, right?
His official position is low, his salary is small, he cannot take care of others, and he has no place even for his brothers. What is the reason?
Mr. Dongfang sighed, raised his head and answered him: "This reason is not completely understandable to you."
Su Qin and Zhang Yi lived in the same era, and now they are in another era. How can they be the same?
In the era of Su Qin and Zhang Yi, the Zhou Dynasty was weak and the princes did not meet the emperor. They fought hard to fight for power and gain. They captured each other by force and merged into twelve vassal states, regardless of male or female. Those who gained scholars became stronger and those who lost them perished. Therefore, talking and lobbying became popular all over the world.
summary: Dongfang Shuo urged Emperor Wu to emulate Emperor Wen's frugality to reform society, criticizing the current extravagance. When asked to compare himself to other scholars, he humorously belittled them. He wrote "Replying to Guests" and "On Mr. Feiyou," defending his low status and arguing that times had changed. In "On Mr. Feiyou," he discussed the dangers of outspoken advice and the importance of wise rulers. His works were recorded by Liu Xiang, though many rumors about him were false. Historians note his wit and humor, comparing him to a comedic figure, but his advice was often insightful.

translation:
Tian Chang usurped the power of the Qi State, and Zhi, Fan, Zhongxing, Han, Tang, and Wei Liuqing divided the power of the Jin State, and they all became warlike countries. This was the beginning of the people's hardship.
At this time, the strong countries are committed to attacking, while the weak countries are repairing their defenses and joining forces vertically and horizontally. Envoys, chariots and horses are galloping and colliding with each other. The soldiers' armor is covered with lice, and the common people have nowhere to complain.
When the King of Qin won the government, he encroached on the world and annexed other countries. He was named "Emperor", unified the domestic decrees, and demolished the castles of the princes.
The captured weapons were destroyed and made into bells, indicating that they would no longer be used.
The common people were spared the pain of the turmoil of the Warring States Period, and everyone thought that they had met the wise emperor and gained a new life.
If the Qin Dynasty had leniently suspended punishments, lightened taxes and levies, eliminated corvees, valued benevolence and righteousness, despised power, advocated loyalty, despised sycophancy, changed customs, and promoted enlightenment at home, then the Qin Dynasty would have had peace from generation to generation.
The Qin Dynasty did not advocate the promotion of such social customs, but continued its old customs. Those who played with cleverness and power were promoted, and those who were honest, loyal, and upright were dismissed. The laws were harsh, the decrees were harsh, and there were many flatterers. The emperor listened to their sweet words and praises every day, and he was full of ambitions and fantasies.
Wanting to show off his power overseas, he sent Meng Tian to lead troops to attack the Xiongnu in the north, expand the territory, and guard Beihe. He ordered the people to quickly transport grain and fodder to follow the army.
He also sent the commander-in-chief Tu Sui to lead the soldiers of the building boats to attack Baiyue, and sent the censor Lu Shilu to dig the Ling Canal to transport grain, and went deeper into the country, and more people fled.
The war lasted for a long time and the food supply was insufficient. The Yue people launched an attack and the Qin army was defeated.
The Qin Dynasty then sent Wei Tuo to lead troops to garrison the territory of Yue. At that time, the Qin Dynasty's troubles were that the north was resentful of the Xiongnu and the south was enmity with the Yue people. The troops were stationed in useless places and could not retreat when they advanced.
More than ten years passed like this, with the male serving as a soldier and the female transporting. They were miserable and hanged themselves on a tree by the roadside, looking at each other.
When Qin Shihuang died, the world was in rebellion.
Chen Sheng and Wu Guang captured Chen, Wu Chen and Zhang Er captured Zhao, Xiang Liang defeated Wu, Tian Dan captured Qi, Jing Ju went to Ying, Zhou Shi fell to Wei, Han Guang raised Yan, and the mountains were full of heroes, which is unforgettable.
However, these people are not the descendants of princes, nor are they local governors. They have no power at all. They started in Yanxiang, holding the handles of spears and halberds. They followed the trend of the times, started troubles at the right time, gathered together by chance, attacked cities and plundered lands, and finally became kings. This was the result of the education at that time.
The emperor of the Qin Dynasty was regarded as the Son of Heaven, rich in the world, and his lineage was exterminated and sacrifices were cut off. This was a disaster caused by military violence.
Therefore, the fault of the Zhou Dynasty was that it was weak, and the fault of the Qin Dynasty was that it was strong. Both of them were unable to adapt to the times, which led to the disaster of national destruction.
Now the Han court wants to appease the Nanyi, send Yelang to come to the court, surrender Qiang Fen and Lingzhou, and build cities there. It also wants to penetrate deeply into the Xiongnu and burn their dragon city. The discussants praise these plans.
summary: Yan An, from Linmiao, wrote a letter as the late Prime Minister Shi, criticizing the extravagance of the wealthy, who decorated their carriages, clothes, and palaces excessively, leading to social ills like greed, lawlessness, and moral decay. He argued that luxury without restraint causes dissatisfaction, drives people from their proper occupations, and fosters treachery and violence. Yan An proposed laws to curb extravagance, reduce envy, and promote harmony, which would lead to peace, reduced crime, and natural prosperity. He contrasted the Zhou Dynasty's long rule with its decline due to weak leadership, leading to the Warring States period and the rise of the Five Hegemons, who upheld the emperor's authority. The Qin Dynasty, under Emperor Qin Shi Huang, unified China but failed to reform its harsh laws and heavy taxes, instead expanding aggressively against the Xiongnu and Baiyue, causing widespread suffering and rebellion. Yan An warned the Han court against similar overreach, advocating for domestic stability over foreign conquests, and noted that the Zhou's weakness and Qin's strength both led to their downfalls due to inflexibility.

When Zhong Jun went to the capital from Jinan to visit the doctor, he walked through Hangu Pass. The official guarding the pass gave Zhong Jun a talisman made of silk.
Zhong Jun asked: What are you using this for?
The official replied: "When I come back, I will use it as a road sign. I will pass this bundle and take it to match it."
Zhong Jun said: When a man travels to the west, he does not need it as a way back.
He threw down the silk talisman letter and left.
After Zhongjun was appointed as the envoy, he was envoyed to inspect the prefecture and the country. He went out to Hangu Pass to patrol the east with the talisman festival. The officials guarding the pass remembered him and said: This envoy is the Confucian scholar who abandoned the silk talisman letter before.
Finally, the army patrolled the prefectures and reported to the court when they encountered suitable things.
After returning from the mission, he reported his work to Emperor Wu, who was very happy to hear it.
When the imperial court sent an envoy to the Xiongnu, Zhongjun himself requested to be envoyed, saying: "I didn't even make the envoy fall, so I was listed as a minister of the Suwei and received a five-year salary."
There are warnings of war on the border from time to time. I should put on strong armor and hold sharp weapons, face the rain of arrows and stones, and open the way forward.
But I am not familiar with the matter of charging into battle. Now that I heard that an envoy is going to be sent to the Xiongnu, I am willing to do my best to inspire the spirit, assist the wise envoy, and plan good and bad things in front of the Xiongnu Chanyu.
I am young and have low talents, and I have failed to live up to my expectations. I cannot serve as an official to defend the border. I am not strong enough to stand alone. I feel depressed in private.
Emperor Wu went down to Shao and asked Zhongjun about his request to send an envoy to the Xiongnu to plan for good or bad luck. Emperor Wu thought that Zhongjun's answer was unusual and promoted him to the position of admonishing doctor.
South Vietnam and the Han Dynasty made peace, so Emperor Wu sent Zhongjun as an envoy to South Vietnam to lobby the King of South Vietnam to allow him to come to Beijing to see him, and his treatment was similar to that of the princes and kings in the mainland.
The final army volunteered and said: I hope your majesty will give me a long tassel, and I will tie up the King of Nanyue and bring him to the palace.
The army went to South Vietnam to lobby the King of Yue. After listening to the army's words, the King of Yue agreed to lead all the Yue people to join the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Wu was very happy and gave the South Vietnamese minister a seal, allowing the South Vietnamese king to uniformly use the legal system of the Han Dynasty to change the customs and habits of the Vietnamese people, and ordered the envoys to stay in the army to stabilize and appease South Vietnam.
Lu Jia, the Prime Minister of South Vietnam, was unwilling to join the Han Dynasty and sent troops to attack the King of South Vietnam. He also killed the Han Dynasty envoy Zhong Jun and others.
The words are in "The Biography of Nanyue".
Zhong Jun was only in his twenties when he died, so the world called him "Zhong Tong".

During the years of Shenjue and Wufeng, the world was prosperous and auspicious signs appeared many times.

The prime minister, Wei Xiang, summoned Tanding from Bohai County and Gong De from Liang who knew music and were good at playing Yaqin. Emperor Xuan summoned them and asked them to wait for the imperial edict.
At this time, Wang Xiang, who made the history of Yizhou, wanted to promote customs and enlightenment among the people. At that time, Fanxiang Hou Hewu was still a minor and was selected to participate in singing.

Emperor Xuan summoned He Wu and others and said to them: This is a matter of Xinglong Dejiao, how can I stop them!

Emperor Xuan summoned Wang Bao.
After Wang Bao arrived in the capital, Emperor Xuan issued an order for Wang Bao to write a song with the theme of a wise monarch getting a wise minister.

summary: Zhongjun, from Jinan, was a talented scholar who became Emperor Wu's envoy. He wrote a response to Emperor Wu's discovery of a white unicorn and a strange tree, interpreting them as auspicious signs of the Han dynasty's virtue and the submission of foreign peoples. He advised the emperor to perform sacrifices and change the reign name, which Emperor Wu did, renaming it Yuanshou. Later, Zhongjun interrogated Dr. Xu Yan for falsely claiming imperial orders to operate salt and iron in Jiaodong and Lu, exposing his deceit and securing his conviction. Emperor Wu praised Zhongjun's handling of the case. Zhongjun also volunteered to envoy to the Xiongnu and South Vietnam, famously requesting a "long tassel" to bind the King of South Vietnam. He successfully persuaded the king to submit to Han rule, but was killed by the South Vietnamese prime minister Lu Jia during a rebellion.

He repeatedly asked Wang Guo and others to participate in large-scale hunting expeditions as attendants. Emperor Xuan went down to Shao and asked Wang Bao and others to go to the palace to serve the prince and try to make him happy. Wang Bao and others read wonderful articles and their own masterpieces morning and night.
The prince's illness recovered, and Wang Guo and others left.
The prince liked "Sweet Spring" and "Ode to the Dongxiao" written by Wang Bao, and asked the nobles in the harem and the attendants to read these two works.

Wang Bao fell ill and died on the way to Yizhou. The emperor felt pity for him.

When Emperor Yuan first came to the throne, he wrote a book about the gains and losses of political affairs, and was summoned to wait for the imperial edict at Jinmamen.

From the establishment of the county to the first year of Emperor Zhao's reign, there were a total of six rebellions in more than 20 years.
In the fifth year of the First Yuan Dynasty, Dan'er County was abandoned and belonged to Zhukuang County.
In the third year of Emperor Xuan's reign, three counties in Zhukuang County rebelled again.
Seven years after this rebellion, in the first year of Ganlu, nine more counties rebelled. The Han government sent troops to quell these two rebellions.
In the first year of Emperor Yuan's reign, there was another rebellion in Zhuli County, and the Han court sent troops to attack.
Counties are even more rebelling against each other, and the situation is uncertain year after year.
Emperor Yuan discussed with relevant ministers about dispatching large forces to suppress the attack, but Jia Xian suggested that they should not attack.
The emperor sent his consort Prince Consort Lechanghou Wang Shang to interrogate Jia Gianzhi, saying: Zhuli Nei has been a county for a long time. summary: Wang Bao, from Shu, was a poet summoned by Emperor Xuan to compose songs and odes. He wrote an ode praising wise rulers and ministers, using metaphors like the Ganjiang sword and fine horses to illustrate the harmony between talent and leadership. He argued that virtuous ministers naturally appear under sage kings, citing historical examples like the Duke of Zhou and Duke Huan of Qi. Emperor Xuan enjoyed Wang Bao's works, which included references to immortals, and promoted him to advisory doctor. Wang Bao also served the prince during illness, reading his compositions to cheer him. He died while on a mission to Yizhou to obtain treasures. Jia Ganzhi, great-grandson of Jia Yi, advised Emperor Yuan against attacking Zhuli County (in modern Hainan), which had repeatedly rebelled since its establishment. He argued that the territory was not worth the cost, citing historical precedents like Yao, Shun, and the Zhou Dynasty, which did not forcibly conquer distant lands. He contrasted Emperor Wen's frugality and peace with Emperor Wu's costly expansions, which led to widespread suffering and rebellion. Emperor Yuan accepted his advice and abandoned Zhuli County. Later, Jia Ganzhi and Yang Xing, a favored official, conspired to recommend each other for high positions, but Shi Xian reported their scheme. They were tried for deceit and leaking palace secrets; Jia Ganzhi was executed, and Yang Xing was reduced to penal servitude.

translation:
He Wu, named Jungong, was from Pixian County, Shu County.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan, the wars in the world subsided and order became stable, and the barbarians surrendered. The gods and the five phoenixes received many auspicious blessings in response to the virtues of the king.
Wang Xiang, the governor of Yizhou, ordered the debater Wang Li to praise Mo De and wrote three poems: "Zhonghe", "Le Shi" and "Xuanxuan".

The emperor said: This is a matter of great virtue, why can I bear it?

He became a doctor by virtue of passing the marksmanship test, and became friendly with Zhai Fangjin.

The five He Wu brothers were all officials in the county, and people in the county respected them.
He Wu's younger brother, He Xian, whose family was registered as a merchant, often failed to pay taxes, and the county paid his taxes many times.
The person in charge of collecting taxes in the market, Qiu Shang, took advantage of this to insult He Xian's family. He Xian was furious and wanted to use his official career to slander Qiu Shang.
He Wu said: Because our family pays rent, taxes, and does corvee work before others, shouldn't officials who put official affairs first and not show favoritism like this?
He Wu finally reported it to the prefect and recruited Qiu Shang as a soldier. People in the state admired him when they heard about it.
过了很久，太仆王音推举何武贤良方正，召他对策，授官做了谏议大夫，升任扬州刺史。
Many high-ranking officials who had been accused of reporting a salary of two thousand dan must first issue a notice to them. If they plead guilty, their charges will be reduced and they will be dismissed; if they do not plead guilty, their charges will be reported with the heaviest penalty to compensate for their responsibilities. Some may even be sentenced to death.
Dai Sheng, the prefect of Jiujiang, was known as Xiao Dai in the Book of Rites. He often punished people for not obeying the laws. The former governor tolerated him because he was a great Confucian.
When He Wu became the governor, the patrol department examined and recorded the crimes of the prisoners, and some of them were reported and handed over to the county for punishment.
Dai Sheng said: What do underachievers know that they want to disrupt other people's management!
There is no ruling.
When He Wu sent someone to investigate his crimes, Dai Sheng was afraid and resigned. Later, he became a doctor and slandered He Wu in the court.
He Wu heard about this incident and never publicized his evil deeds.
Later, the guests of Dai Sheng's son formed a group of thieves and were captured by the officials and imprisoned in Lujiang. Dai Sheng thought that his son would definitely die.
He Wu tried his best to judge the case fairly, and his son was not sentenced to death in the end.
From then on, Dai Sheng was ashamed and convinced.
Every time He Wu went to the capital to carry out business, Dai Sheng never came to his door to express his gratitude.
summary: He Wu, styled Jungong, was from Pixian County, Shu County. During the reign of Emperor Xuan, peace prevailed, and He Wu, at fourteen or fifteen, learned to sing poems composed by Wang Li in Chengdu. Summoned by the emperor, he later studied the *Book of Changes*, became a doctor, and served as county magistrate of E County, though he was dismissed for legal violations. His five brothers all held county offices, earning local respect. He Wu once handled a tax dispute involving his brother He Xian with integrity, reporting the tax collector Qiu Shang to the prefect, who conscripted Qiu Shang, earning admiration.

translation:

The patrolling subordinates must first go to the academy to meet the students, examine their recitations and debates, and inquire about their gains and losses in political affairs. Then they enter the transmission hall and take out records to inquire about the number of cultivated fields and the quality of the grains. Only then will they meet with the county guard, making it a customary order.
At the beginning, when He Wu was an official in the county, he served He Shou, the prefect.
He Shou knew that He Wu had the talents of a prime minister, so he treated him favorably because he had the same surname as himself.
Later, He Shou became the chief agricultural officer, and his brother's son became the chief historian of Lujiang.
At that time, He Wu was playing something in the official residence, and the son of He Shou's brother happened to be in Chang'an. He Shou prepared a banquet and invited He Wu's younger brother He Xian, his old friend Yang Fuzhong and others. They drank happily and asked his brother's son to come out to meet him. He said: "My son is the governor of Yangzhou and has low talents. He has never greeted He Wu."

He is appointed by the emperor and serves as a model for a state. His duty is to recommend good people and eliminate bad people. Only officials who have outstanding achievements in government affairs and people who live in seclusion should be summoned. No private inquiries are allowed.
He Xian and Yang Fuzhong forced him to summon him and gave him a bottle of wine.
In the middle of the year, the prefect of Lujiang promoted the son of brother He Shou.
He Wu obeyed the law in this way and was afraid of neglecting his duty.
He Wu served as governor for five years and then came to Beijing to serve as Prime Minister Sizhi. Prime Minister Xue Xuan respected him very much.
He served as the prefect of Qinghe. A few years later, he was dismissed from office because more than four-tenths of the county suffered disasters.
After a long time, the Grand Sima Quyang Hou Wanggen recommended He Wu and recruited him to be the admonishing doctor.
He was promoted to the governor of Yanzhou, moved to Beijing to be appointed as Sili Xiaowei, and was transferred to Jing Zhaoyin.
Two years later, He Wu recommended Fang Zheng. Because the person he recommended turned around and bowed when he was summoned, some officials thought that he was guilty of fraud and fraud.
He Wu was convicted and demoted to the position of internal history of Chu, promoted to the prefect of Pei County, and then moved to Beijing as a court lieutenant.
In the third year of Suihe, Kong Guang, the imperial censor, was demoted to Tingwei, and He Wu became the censor.
Emperor Cheng was about to establish the rule of Piyong and open the official positions of the three public officials, so he changed the original Yushi Dafu to Da Sikong.
He Wu was appointed as Da Sikong and was granted the title of Marquis of Fanxiang, with a settlement of 1,000 households.
Fanxiang was in Langxie, and Emperor Ai had just ascended the throne. He praised and rewarded ministers, and also made Bowang Township in Nanyangluo the fief of Fanxiang, adding a thousand households to the fiefdom.
He Wu was kind and kind, and liked to recommend scholars and exhort and praise the benefits of others.
When he was the internal history of Chu, he treated Gong Sheng and Gong She favorably. When he was in Pei County, he treated Tang Lin and Tang Zun favorably. When he became a minister, he recommended them to the court.
The reason why these people are prominent in the world is the power of He Hou, and the world respects He Wu for this.
summary: He Wu later became a censor and governor of Yangzhou. He dealt with officials like Dai Sheng, a great Confucian, with fairness, not publicizing Dai Sheng's slander and ensuring his son received a just trial. As governor, He Wu prioritized visiting academies to examine students and assess political gains before meeting county officials. He maintained strict propriety, refusing private requests, as when he resisted pressure from He Xian and Yang Fuzhong to summon a relative. After five years, he became Prime Minister Sizhi, then prefect of Qinghe, but was dismissed due to disasters. Later, he served as admonishing doctor, governor of Yanzhou, Sili Xiaowei, and Jing Zhaoyin. He was demoted for a recommendation error but rose to become Grand Sikong and Marquis of Fanxiang.

Emperor Ai asked the Empress Dowager for instructions again, and the matter was exposed.
The Queen Mother apologized for him, but the Emperor couldn't bear to kill him because of the Queen Mother, so he demoted Wang Yi and appointed him as the captain of the Xihe vassal state, reducing the number of thousands of households.
summary: He Wu was kind and loved recommending scholars, treating people like Gong Sheng and Tang Lin favorably. He disliked cliques, cross-examining Confucians and civil servants. After Emperor Cheng's death, He Wu was accused of unfilial conduct and dismissed by Emperor Ai. Later, Bao Xuan and Wang Jia defended him, and he was recruited as imperial censor, then former general.

summary: When Emperor Ai died, the Queen Mother appointed Wang Mang as Grand Sima. He Wu and Gongsun Lu, fearing relatives' control, recommended each other, but the Queen Mother chose Wang Mang. The jailer asked the names of the virtuous and unworthy people, and Wang Jia said: The virtuous ones are Prime Minister Kong Guang and Sikong Hewu, and they cannot be promoted; the evil ones are Gao'an Marquis Dong Xian and his son, who are flattering and evil and disturb the court, but they cannot be removed.
My crime deserves death, and I will die without any resentment.
Wang Jia was detained in prison for more than 20 days. He refused to eat and vomited blood and died.
The emperor's uncle, the Grand Sima Hussar General Ding Ming, always valued Wang Jia and sympathized with him. The emperor then dismissed Ding Ming and replaced him with Dong Xian. This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Dong Xian".
Wang Jia was executed as prime minister for three years and his country was deprived of his title.
After his death, the emperor read his reply and thought about his words. He replaced Wang Jia with Kong Guang as prime minister, and recruited He Wu as the imperial censor.
In the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, an edict was issued to pursue the loyal ministers. Wang Chong, Wang Jia's son, was granted the title of Xinfu Marquis, and Wang Jia of Mi was granted the title of Zhonghou.
Shidan's courtesy name was Zhonggong, and he was a native of Langye Dongwu.
He studied the Book of Songs and took Kuang Heng as his teacher.
Because of his filial piety and honesty, he became a man.
In the last years of Emperor Yuan's reign, he became a doctor and was later dismissed.
During the first year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the prefecture recommended Maocai, who was also appointed as a doctor and appointed as the Taifu of King Shuping.
Prime Minister Fang Jin and imperial censor Kong Guang recommended Shi Dan to be profound in discussion, honest and upright, and recruited him to Beijing to serve as Dr. Guanglu and Prime Minister Sizhi.
A few months later, he became a doctor of Guanglu and served in Shizhong. From then on, he was appointed Shaofu, Guangluxun and Shizhong, and he was very respected.
In the last years of Emperor Cheng's reign, he appointed King Dingtao as the Crown Prince and Shi Dan as the Crown Prince and Tutor.
When Emperor Ai ascended the throne, Shi Dan was appointed General Zuo, and was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, a food town, and the office of Minister. He then replaced Wang Mang as the Grand Sima and was granted the title of Marquis of Gaole.
More than a month later, he was promoted to Da Sikong.
When the emperor was young and in a feudal state, he saw that Emperor Cheng had entrusted the political power to his relatives and that the Wang family had exceeded their authority and became powerful, so he was often worried and uneasy.
After taking the throne, he often tried to correct this situation.
The Ding family and the Fu family were given titles and officials to deprive the Wang family of their power.
Shi Dan held the third position as a master and was trusted by the emperor, so he wrote a memorial saying: In ancient times, emperors ignored political affairs while in mourning, and all officials obeyed the orders of the emperor, and did not change the policies of his father for three years.
summary: When Dong Xian was favored, Wang Jia opposed granting him a title without proper discussion, warning against losing public trust. The emperor initially relented but later granted the title, reprimanding Wang Jia. Wang Jia continued to admonish, criticizing Dong Xian's extravagance and the emperor's favoritism, which harmed the state. He urged restraint, citing past examples like Emperor Xiaowen's frugality. The emperor grew displeased but doted on Dong Xian more. Wang Jia also recommended Liang Xiang and others, but the emperor, angered by Wang Jia's defense of them, had him questioned. Wang Jia was impeached for confusing the country and died in prison after refusing food. After his death, the emperor regretted it and later honored him. Shi Dan, styled Zhonggong, from Langye, studied the *Book of Songs* under Kuang Heng. He became a doctor, then Taifu of King Shuping. Recommended by Fang Jin and Kong Guang, he served as Dr. Guanglu and Prime Minister Sizhi, later becoming Shaofu, Guangluxun, and tutor to the crown prince. When Emperor Ai ascended, Shi Dan became Grand Sima and Marquis of Gaole, then Grand Sikong. He advised the emperor to be cautious, citing disasters from hasty changes. He opposed honoring Empress Dowager Fu and Empress Ding with imperial titles, arguing it violated ritual propriety. This led to his disfavor.

translation:
When you submit a sealed memorial, it circulates among passers-by and spreads so that everyone in the court and streets knows about it. Those who are impeaching think that the minister is loyal and should be beheaded according to the crime, and gain a false reputation, causing slander and accusations to spread in all directions.
If the close ministers are like this, what will happen to the distant ministers?
Probably the mistake is in the statement of the benefits of two people being of the same mind, and why should they lead the group and make people close to each other from afar?
I consider that your position is noble and you have great responsibilities, but you do not think things through carefully, you have deceitful intentions and confuse the country, you disobey orders between advance and retreat, and you make contradictory statements repeatedly. I am very ashamed of you, and you are not used to realize the common inheritance of the world. To protect the country forever.
Because you were once entrusted as a master, and you cannot bear to let the judge examine you, you have been ordered to pardon you and not to punish you.
He handed over the seal and ribbon of Grand Sikong Gaolehou, dismissed his official position and returned home.
The minister ordered Tang Lin to write a memorial saying: I have privately seen the strategy document of Mian Da Sikong, and the accusation is too profound. A gentleman should cover up his writing for the sage.
Shi Dan was a Confucian scholar of the time, and his virtue was that of an elder in the country. He personally taught His Majesty, and he was ranked as the Third Duke. His crime was very minor, and no one in the country saw him doing any serious wrong. Now that the matter has passed, the punishment of being exempted from the title was too severe. The knowledgeable people in the capital all thought that Shi Dan should be restored to his fiefdom and title, and let him serve at the court's invitation. This is what people from all over the world are looking forward to.
I hope that your Majesty will be able to understand everyone's feelings and be able to comfort and repay the minister who is your master.
The emperor listened to Tang Lin's words and ordered Shidan to be granted the title of Marquis of Guannei, with a settlement of 300 households.
A few months after Shi Dan was deposed, the emperor adopted Zhu Bo's suggestion and honored Empress Dowager Fu as the Empress Dowager, and Empress Ding as the Imperial Empress Dowager, with the same dignity as the Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager. He also built an ancestral temple in the capital for the Communist Emperor, with the same etiquette as Emperor Xiaoyuan.
Zhu Bo was promoted to prime minister, and he and the imperial censor Daxuan Tangxuan reported: Dong Hong, the former Marquis of Gaochang, first proposed the idea of ​​establishing a title, but was impeached by Shi Dan and exempted from being a commoner.
At that time, there was a funeral in the world, and political affairs were entrusted to Shi Dan. Shi Dan did not carefully consider the principle of praising and promoting respect for relatives, but made random remarks, belittled the title, and damaged filial piety. There is no greater disloyalty than this.
His majesty is saintly and kind, so he clearly established his honorary title. Dong Hong was also granted the title of Marquis of Gaochang because of his loyalty and filial piety.
Shi Dan's crime of disobeying the emperor's order was obvious. Although he was pardoned, he should not enjoy the title or fief. I asked him to be exempted from being a commoner.
The petition was approved.
Shi Dan was dismissed and returned to his hometown for many years.
summary: Shi Dan was later accused of leaking a sealed memorial and dismissed for deceit. Despite Tang Lin's plea, he was reduced to Marquis of Guannei. After Zhu Bo's rise, Shi Dan was further demoted for opposing the honorary titles. When Emperor Ping came to power, Wang Mang restored Shi Dan, granting him the title of Marquis of Yiyang. He died shortly after, and his title ended with Wang Mang's fall.

translation:
When Emperor Ping came to the throne, Wang Mang, the Marquis of Xindu, reported to the Empress Dowager that he excavated the tombs of Empress Dowager Fu and Empress Dowager Ding, stripped them of their seals and ribbons, and buried them with common people's rites. Ding Tao destroyed the Gonghuang Temple.
Those who suggested this matter, such as Lingli, Duan You and others, were exiled to Hepu, and Dong Hong, the Marquis of Gaochang, was deposed as a commoner.
He summoned Shi Dan to the public transport department and granted him the title of Marquis of Guannei, enjoying the original fiefdom.
A few months later, the Empress Dowager Shao ordered the Great Situ and the Great Sikong to say: "Reward those who are virtuous and reward the ministers who have made the most contributions. This is the system of the sages and the unchanging rule of emperors of all dynasties."
The former Empress Dowager Tao of Dingtao used her honorary title in vain, which was very contrary to justice. Hou Shidan of Guan Nei was loyal and upright to the country, regardless of adversity, adhered to loyalty and integrity, followed the laws of the Holy King, and clearly distinguished the system of superiority and inferiority.
According to Si Tiao Chen's suggestion, the evil minister who was given the honorary title has been demoted or dismissed, but Shi Dan did not add rewards based on his merits. I am afraid that it violates Miao's principle of rewarding first and punishing later, and cannot promote virtue to repay his merits.
Now, 2,100 households in Zhongxiang, Houqiu, are granted the title of Yiyang Marquis.
More than a month later, Shi Dan passed away and Mi was named Jiehou.
His son Shiye inherited the title, which was discontinued after Wang Mang's defeat.
Praise said: He Wu's memorial, Wang Jia's admonishment, Shi Dan's ideas, and the examination of their misfortunes and blessings all came true in the future.
When Wang Mang arose and everyone inside and outside was convinced, Dong Xian was favored as much as the emperor's relatives. He Wu and Wang Jia's ministers blocked the rivers with a piece of loess, thereby drowning themselves.
Shi Dan and Dong Hong were rewarded and punished alternately. How sad!
Therefore, it is said that following the world will abandon the right path, and going against the world will harm oneself. This is the reason why the ancients found it difficult to receive titles.
summary: The commentary notes that He Wu, Wang Jia, and Shi Dan's warnings proved true. Wang Mang's rise and Dong Xian's favor led to He Wu and Wang Jia's downfalls, while Shi Dan faced alternating rewards and punishments. It reflects the difficulty of receiving titles in turbulent times.
