translation:
Since the establishment of the Han Dynasty, sycophants and favored ministers who flattered the emperor and gained favor continued to appear. There were famous registered children in the Emperor Gaozu's dynasty, and there were Hong children in the Emperor Xiaohui's dynasty.
These two people have no outstanding talents. They just blindly flatter and please the emperor and gain wealth and favor. They follow the emperor closely, go out and go in together, and have a very close relationship. Even the ministers use them to express themselves in front of the emperor. They had a great influence at that time because of their good words for themselves. Therefore, Emperor Hui's ministers and ministers all decorated their hats with delicate feathers, decorated their belts with sea shells, and applied makeup and powder. This custom was caused by the influence of people like boudoir and jiru.
Both of them became rich and noble during their lifetime and moved to Anling.
Later favorites included the scholar Deng Tong, the eunuch Zhao Tan, and Beigong Bozi during the reign of Emperor Wen; the scholar Han Yan and the eunuch Li Yannian during the reign of Emperor Wu; the eunuchs Hong Gong and Shi Xian during the Yuan Emperor; the scholars Zhang Fang and Chun Yuchang during the Cheng Emperor; and Dong Xian during the Emperor Ai's reign.
Emperor Jing, Emperor Zhao, and Emperor Xuan all had no favorite ministers.
If calculated broadly, during the reign of Emperor Jing, only Lang Zhongling Zhou Ren was a favored minister; during the reign of Emperor Zhao, the prince-in-law Duwei surprised Hou Jinshang and inherited the title of marquis from his father, the chariot general Jin Chan. Although the two of them were more favored than ordinary people, they were not particularly favored; Emperor Xuan, who had not yet become the emperor, studied poetry and books at the same table. When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Peng Zu was named Marquis of Yangdu by the emperor based on his friendship at that time. He often served as a guard when he went out and was known as the emperor's favorite. This man was relatively cautious and strict, and did not do anything harmful to others. In the end, he was poisoned by his concubine, and his feudal kingdom was abolished.
Deng Tong, a native of Nan'an, Shu County, was known as Huangtoulang because he could hold a table, sail a boat and wear a yellow hat.
The master boy once had a dream, in which he wanted to ascend to heaven, but could not. Suddenly a yellow-headed man pushed him hard, and he finally ascended to heaven. He turned around and saw that the man who pushed him had his jacket on under the leather belt on his buttocks, which was very unusual.
After Emperor Wen woke up, he went to Jiantai and looked for the Huangtou man dressed in rowing clothes based on what he saw in his dream. He suddenly saw Deng Tong. His clothes were worn from behind, just like the man he saw in his dream.
So he was summoned and asked his name. Deng Tong said his surname was Deng Mingtong.
The pronunciations of Deng and Deng are similar. Emperor Wen was very happy and favored Deng Tong very much, saying that he was very happy.
Deng Tong was very attentive and solemn in character and did not like to interact with outsiders. Even if the emperor rewarded him with a bathing vacation, he would not go out.
Therefore, Emperor Wen rewarded Deng Tong with tens of thousands of dollars, more than a dozen times, and Deng Tong became a high official.
Emperor Wen sometimes went to Deng Tong's house to play games in private, but Deng Tong had no other special acting talents and could not show them to the emperor. He was just cautious to please the emperor.
summary: Since the Han Dynasty's founding, sycophants and favored ministers who gained imperial favor through flattery appeared regularly. During Emperor Gaozu's reign, there was Ji Ru; under Emperor Xiaohui, there was Hong Ru. Neither possessed outstanding talents, relying solely on flattery to gain wealth and favor. They accompanied the emperor closely, influencing even ministers who used them to communicate with the throne. Their impact was so great that Emperor Hui's officials adopted their customs, decorating hats with delicate feathers, belts with seashells, and applying makeup—a trend attributed to figures like Ji Ru and Hong Ru. Both became wealthy and noble in their lifetimes, later moving to Anling. Subsequent favored figures included Deng Tong, eunuch Zhao Tan, and Beigong Bozi under Emperor Wen; Han Yan and eunuch Li Yannian under Emperor Wu; eunuchs Hong Gong and Shi Xian under Emperor Yuan; Zhang Fang and Chun Yuchang under Emperor Cheng; and Dong Xian under Emperor Ai. Emperors Jing, Zhao, and Xuan had no notable favorites, though Zhou Ren under Emperor Jing, Jin Shang under Emperor Zhao, and Peng Zu under Emperor Xuan received some favor without causing harm.

translation:
The emperor once sent a fortune teller who was good at reading Deng Tong's fortune. The fortune teller said: "He will definitely die of poverty and hunger in the future."
The emperor said: I am the one who can make Deng Tong rich. As the king of a country, how can I say that Deng Tong will be poor?
So the emperor rewarded Deng Tong with the Tongshan Mountain in Yandao, Shu County, and asked him to mint coins for use. As a result, the coins minted by Deng Tong spread all over the world, and he became so rich.
Emperor Wen once had abscesses on his body, and Deng often used his own mouth to suck the abscesses for the emperor.
The emperor was unhappy and asked Deng Tong calmly: Who in the world do you think loves me the most and cares about me the most?
Deng Tong said: There should be no one who can surpass the prince.
The prince came in to greet the emperor, and the emperor asked the prince to suck the sore. Although the prince sucked it, he could see that he was very uncomfortable.
Later, the prince heard that Deng Tong had been very active in sucking the emperor's sores. The prince was very ashamed, and the prince secretly hated Deng Tong in his heart.
When Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing came to the throne, Deng Tong was dismissed and returned home to live.
Not long after returning home, someone reported that Deng Tong had gone out to the southwest to mint money, so Emperor Jing sent officials to investigate the matter. There was considerable evidence, so he was convicted and everything was confiscated. In addition, Deng Tong's family also owed tens of millions.
The officials confiscated all the money given to Deng Tong by the eldest princess, and did not even leave him a hairpin to wear. So the eldest princess asked someone to lend him clothes and food.
Deng Tong was penniless and ended up living in someone else's home and died.
Zhao Tan was favored by his observation of stars and weather; Beigong Bozi treated others with the generosity and compassion of an elder, so the emperor got close to him, but neither of them could compare with Dian Tong.
Han Yan, courtesy name Wangsun, is the grandson of Gonggaohou Qidang.
When Emperor Wu was the king of Jiaodong, Han Yan and Emperor Wu studied poetry and calligraphy together. They were friendly to each other and had a friendly relationship.
When Emperor Wu became the prince, Emperor Wu became closer to Han Yan.
Han Yan is good at horseback riding and archery, and is smart and wise.
After Emperor Wu became emperor, he wanted to attack the northern minorities. Since Han Yan had studied military affairs before, Emperor Wu favored him more and Han Yan became more noble. Han Yan later became a high official, and the rewards he received were comparable to Deng Tong.
At first, Han Yan often slept and got up with Emperor Wu.
Once, King Jiangdu came to see the emperor and went hunting with Emperor Wu in Shanglin Garden. Before the emperor's carriage set off, he sent Han Yan to take a auxiliary carriage and lead nearly a hundred knights to check out the wild beasts.
At that time, King Jiangdu saw it from a distance and thought that the emperor had arrived. He avoided the people who followed Han Yan and knelt down by the roadside. Unexpectedly, Han Yan did not see him and rushed over. King Jiangdu was furious and cried to the empress dowager. He demanded that the title be returned to the emperor and that he also serve as a palace guard to compete with Han Yan.
When the Queen Mother heard about this, she hated Han Yan ever since.
Han Yan served the emperor and had no hindrance in entering and leaving the palace. When the news of adultery reached the ears of the Queen Mother, the Queen Mother was furious and sent someone to kill Han Yan.
The emperor personally interceded for Han Yan, but the Queen Mother had already made up her mind and finally refused to change her mind, and Han Yan died.
Han Yan's younger brother Han Shuo was also favored by Emperor Wu. He was named a Case Daohou for his military exploits. In the last years of Emperor Wu, he was killed by the ruthless prince during the witchcraft disaster. Han Shuo's son Han Zeng was later named Long Luohou and Da Sima Cavalry General. There is another biography of him.
summary: Deng Tong, from Nan'an in Shu, was known as Huangtoulang for wearing a yellow hat while rowing. Emperor Wen once dreamed of ascending to heaven but was unable until a yellow-headed man pushed him upward. After waking, the emperor sought the man and found Deng Tong, whose clothing matched the dream. Delighted, the emperor favored him greatly, rewarding him with tens of thousands in cash and high office. Deng Tong was cautious and solemn, avoiding outsiders even during holidays. A fortune-teller predicted he would die poor and hungry, but the emperor, confident in his power, gave him Tongshan Mountain in Shu to mint coins, making Deng Tong immensely wealthy. When Emperor Wen developed abscesses, Deng Tong sucked them with his mouth. The emperor asked who loved him most, and Deng Tong replied the prince. The prince, uncomfortable with sucking the sores, later resented Deng Tong. After Emperor Wen's death, Emperor Jing dismissed Deng Tong. Accused of minting coins outside, Deng Tong was convicted, his property confiscated, and he died penniless in another's home. Zhao Tan gained favor through astrology, and Beigong Bozi through elder-like generosity, but neither matched Deng Tong. Han Yan, grandson of Gonggaohou Qidang, studied with Emperor Wu during his youth. After Emperor Wu became emperor, Han Yan's skills in horseback riding and archery, along with his intelligence, earned him favor comparable to Deng Tong. He often slept and rose with the emperor. Once, while hunting, King Jiangdu mistook Han Yan's entourage for the emperor and knelt, but Han Yan passed without noticing. The king complained to the empress dowager, who hated Han Yan thereafter. When adultery rumors reached her, she had Han Yan killed despite the emperor's pleas. Han Yan's brother, Han Shuo, also favored, was later killed during the witchcraft disaster.

translation:
Li Yannian is from Zhongshan. He and his parents and brothers are all music lovers.
Li Yannian suffered corruption and was in charge of the emperor's dog; his sister was favored by the emperor and was named Mrs. Li. Her biography is in "Biography of Foreign Relatives".
Li Yannian is good at singing, and he sings emerging tunes.
At that time, Emperor Wu was building various temples to worship heaven and earth. When he wanted to create music, he asked Sima Xiangru and others to write poems to praise it.
Li Yannian always adhered to Emperor Wu's orders and composed and sang these poems into new variations.
Li Yannian's sister was adopted by Emperor Wu as his wife and gave birth to the King of Changyi. As a result, Li Yannian's worth doubled, from humble to noble. He became the captain of Xielu, wore a two thousand stone seal ribbon, and lived with the emperor. The favor he received was equal to that of Han Yan.
As time went by, Li Yannian's younger brother Li Ji became promiscuous with the palace officials and became arrogant and domineering.
After Mrs. Li's death, the two brothers could no longer be favored by Emperor Wu, so Emperor Wu killed the Li Yannian brothers and their clan.
From then on, the favored ministers were basically relatives.
Although Wei Qing and Huo Qubing were favored by the emperor, they were promoted based on their true military achievements and talents.
Shi Xian, courtesy name Junfang, was from Jinan; Hong Gong was from Peidi. They both suffered corruption when they were young, and later served as officials in Zhonghuangmen and were elected as Zhongshangshu.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan, Honggong served as the Secretary of the Central Committee. He was familiar with old laws and regulations, and was good at requesting and submitting reports. His talents were sufficient for his position.
Hong Gong was appointed as Zhongshu Ling, and Shi Xian was appointed as Pu She.
A few years after Emperor Yuan came to the throne, Hong Gong died and was replaced by Shi Xian as Zhongshu Ling.
At that time, Emperor Yuan was ill and unable to take care of the government affairs personally. He was also passionate about music. Because Shi Xian had been in this position for a long time and had no outside connections in the palace, he was focused and trustworthy, so Emperor Yuan entrusted Shi Xian with all kinds of government affairs.
All political affairs, big or small, were decided based on Shi Xian's words; Shi Xian's dignity and favor dominated the court, and all officials served Shi Xian respectfully.
Shi Xian was clever and clever, and could understand the emperor's thoughts. He was extremely cunning, and often used various inexplicable reasons to secretly attack others. He would treat people with strict laws for the smallest things.
During the early Yuan Dynasty, former general Xiao Wangzhi and Guanglu doctor Zhou Kan and Zongzheng Liu Gengsheng were all responsible for the work.
Xiao Wangzhi took charge of the affairs of the Secretariat. He knew that Shi Xian was monopolizing power and was evil, so he stated his opinion: "The Secretariat is the foundation of all officials and the key to national power. Fair and transparent people should be allowed to hold this position."
Emperor Wu traveled and feasted in the harem day and night, so he reused eunuchs, which was not in line with the old regulations.
Eunuchs should not be allowed to serve as Zhongshu, in response to ancient etiquette, and people who are still serving their sentences should not be allowed to approach the emperor.
Emperor Yuan did not adopt Xiao Wangzhi's suggestion, so Xiao Wangzhi made Shi Xian very angry.
Later, Xiao Wangzhi and others were persecuted by Shi Xian. Xiao Wangzhi was forced to commit suicide and died. Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng were deposed and imprisoned and were no longer appointed. These contents can be found in "The Biography of Wang".
summary: Li Yannian, from Zhongshan, was a musician who suffered corruption and managed the emperor's dogs. His sister, favored as Lady Li, gave birth to the King of Changyi. Li Yannian's musical talents earned him high rank, equal to Han Yan. After Lady Li's death, his brother Li Ji's promiscuity led to their execution. Thereafter, favored ministers were mostly relatives. Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, though favored, rose through genuine military merit.

translation:
Later, Taizhong doctor Zhang Meng, Wei Jun's prefect Jingfang, Yushi Zhongcheng Chen Xian, Dai Shaojia Gianzhi and others all secretly wrote memorials, often exposing Shi Xian's shortcomings when summoned by the emperor.
Shi Xian sent people to inquire about him and convicted him. The house in Beijing and the house he bought for donation were abandoned on the market. Zhang Meng committed suicide in the bus station. Chen Xian was the one to answer the crime and had his hair shaved off and served the sentence of Cheng Dan.
Later, Su Jian, the governor of Zheng District, obtained Shi Xian's private message and reported it to the emperor. Shi Xian later sentenced him to death for other reasons.
From then on, ministers and officials below the Duke were very afraid of Shi Xian and did not dare to act rashly.
Shi Xian also formed a party with Zhongshu Pu Shelaoliang and Shaofu Wulu Chongzong. Those who attached to them could obtain high-ranking officials.
A folk song goes: Lao Liang and Shi Xian are all frequent visitors to the Wulu Chong family!
How many official seals are in their hands! How long are the ribbons they wear!
This folk song tells the story of their official position and great power.
Shi Xian saw that General Zuo Feng Fengshi and his son were very prestigious as ministers, and Feng Fengshi's daughter was Zhaoyi in the emperor's inner palace, so he wanted to attach himself to him, so Shi Xian recommended Zhaoyi's brother Feng Kui to the emperor, saying that Feng Kui had a strict temperament and could serve in the palace.
Therefore, the emperor summoned Feng Kui and wanted to appoint him as a minister. Feng Kui took the opportunity and asked to tell the emperor something secretly.
When the emperor heard that Feng Kui said that Shi Xian had monopoly power, he was very angry and immediately dismissed Feng Kui from his position and became a Langguan.
Later, when the position of the imperial censor became vacant, all the ministers recommended Feng Kui's brother, Da Honglu, Ye Wang, for his unparalleled character and talent. The emperor asked Shi Xian about this, and Shi Xian said: "No one among the nine ministers is more qualified for this position than Ye Wang."
However, Ye Wang is Zhaoyi's brother. I am worried that future generations will think that Your Majesty does not need many talented people to get close to the relatives of the harem and concubines and let them hold the position of the three princes.
The Emperor said: Well, I don't see that.
So an edict was issued to praise the Ye King, but in fact he was discarded and not reused. This situation can be found in "The Biography of the Ye King".
Shi Xian knew that his expertise in authority was widely known, and he was worried that once the emperor's subordinates would detect his situation, he often took the initiative to confess his faults to the emperor and show himself, and took a letter as verification.
Shi Xian once left the palace to go to the government office to requisition people's property. Shi Xian explained to the emperor in advance that he was worried that the palace gate would be closed and he would not be able to come in after returning late, so he asked the emperor to send someone to send an edict to let the gatekeepers open the door at that time.
The emperor agreed.
Shi Xian deliberately returned late at night, claiming that the emperor had ordered someone to open the door and enter.
As expected, someone later wrote a letter accusing Shi Xian of monopolizing power, forging the emperor's edict, and opening palace doors privately. When the emperor heard about it, he smiled and showed the letter to Shi Xian.
Shi Xian took the opportunity to cry and said: Your Majesty is very fond of me, the villain, and leaves political affairs to me. All the ministers below are jealous. They always want to frame me. There must be more than one thing that harms me by writing letters like this. I hope that you, the wise emperor, will understand my loyalty and situation.
I am humble and humble, and I really do not have the ability to make everyone happy, nor can I bear the anger of the people in the world. I demand that the important official position of Cardinal in charge of the country be returned, and I accept the job of cleaning the steps in the harem, and die without regrets! I hope your majesty will have mercy on me so that I can live in peace.
The emperor believed that what he said was true and sympathized with him. He comforted and encouraged Shi Xian many times and even increased his rewards. In this way, Shi Xian received as many as ten million in rewards and gifts from courtiers to please him.
summary: Shi Xian, from Jinan, and Hong Gong, from Pei, both suffered corruption and served as eunuchs. Under Emperor Xuan, Hong Gong became Zhongshu Ling, skilled in laws and reports. After Hong Gong's death, Shi Xian succeeded him under Emperor Yuan. When Emperor Yuan fell ill, he entrusted all government affairs to Shi Xian, who became all-powerful. Shi Xian was cunning, using strict laws to attack opponents. He persecuted Xiao Wangzhi, Zhou Kan, and Liu Gengsheng, leading to Xiao's suicide and the others' imprisonment. Later, Zhang Meng, Jing Fang, Chen Xian, and others who exposed Shi Xian's faults were convicted. Su Jian, who reported Shi Xian's private letters, was executed. Officials feared Shi Xian, who formed a clique with Lao Liang and Wulu Chongzong. A folk song mocked their power. Shi Xian tried to attach himself to Feng Fengshi but recommended Feng Kui, who then exposed Shi Xian's monopoly. The emperor dismissed Feng Kui. When the censor position opened, ministers recommended Feng Kui's brother, but Shi Xian blocked it. Shi Xian often feigned self-criticism to maintain trust. After Emperor Yuan's death, Emperor Cheng demoted Shi Xian, who died on the road. His followers were dismissed.

translation:
He married many beautiful wives and concubines, Shen? In the face of sexual pleasure, they do not abide by the laws and regulations of the country and do whatever they want.
At the beginning, Queen Xu committed a crime because she believed in witchcraft and was deposed as queen and thrown into Changding Palace. At that time, Queen Xu's sister Xu Wei was the wife of Long'e Sihou. Long'e Sihou was dead and was living as a widow at home.
Chunyu Chang took the opportunity to have an affair with Xu Marry and married her as a side wife.
Empress Xu saw that Chun Yuchang was favored by the emperor, so she bribed Chun Yuchang through her sister Xu Ma, hoping that Chun Yuchang would say a few good words for her in front of the emperor, so that she could step out of the cold palace and return to the harem as Jieyu. Chunyu Chang accepted the money, carriages, horses, clothing for riding in the carriage, and tools for driving, etc. from Empress Xu, which amounted to tens of thousands of dollars. Chunyu Chang deceived Empress Xu and said that he would explain to the emperor that he would re-establish her as the Zuo Empress.
Every time Marry Xu went to Changding Palace, Chunyu Chang would write letters to Aunt Xu, teasing and insulting Queen Xu, and saying all kinds of profane and contemptuous words.
Empress Xu and Chun Yuchang exchange letters with each other. Empress Xu bribes Chun Yuchang every year?
At this time, the emperor's uncle Wanggen, Marquis of Quyang, was serving as the Grand Sima Hussar General and had been assisting the government for several years. He had been ill for a long time, so he repeatedly asked the emperor to resign and retire.
Chunyu Chang held the official position of Jiuqing by virtue of his status as a relative of the emperor; in order, Chunyu Chang could hold the position.
Wang Mang, the son of Wang Gen's brother, the Marquis of Xindu, was worried that Chunyu Chang would be favored. He heard privately that Chunyu Chang had married Xu Marry as his mistress, and had taken a large amount of bribes from Queen Xu, who had been banished to Changding Palace.
Wang Mang was serving Wang Gen, the Marquis of Quyang, who was ill, so he took the opportunity to say: Chunyu Chang was secretly happy when he saw you were sick, thinking that as soon as you die, he can take your place and assist in the government; he has even arranged for someone to serve as a certain official at home.
Wang Mang tried his best to expose Chun Yuchang's crimes to Wang Genlinwei.
After Wang Gen heard this, he became furious and said: Since Chunyu Chang is such a bad guy, why didn't you tell me clearly earlier?
Wang Mang said: I don't know what the general wants, so I dare not tell him.
Wang Gen said: Go to the Empress Dowager quickly and report to her to make a decision.
Wang Mang immediately went to see the Empress Dowager and exposed Chun Yuchang's various crimes. He was arrogant and lewd. He tried to replace Wang Gen in assisting the government. He got into the car in front of his aunt, was extremely rude, committed adultery with Empress Xu in private, and accepted Empress Xu's property.
After hearing this, the Queen Mother became furious and said: My nephew is so bad!
Go and report to the emperor truthfully.
Wang Mang also recounted Chunyu Chang's sins to the emperor. After hearing this, the emperor removed Chunyu Chang from his official position and sent him to other princely states.
At the beginning, Chunyu Chang served as a servant and acted as an envoy to convey messages between the emperor and the queen mother, and he was very close to them.
Hongyang Houli could not hold the post of Grand Sima and assist in government affairs, so he suspected that Chunyu Chang was obstructing him and slandering him in front of the emperor. Therefore, Hongyang Houli always felt resentful towards Chunyu Chang.
The emperor knew these circumstances.
When Chunyu Chang was sent away for his crime, Hongyang Houli's eldest son Rong followed Chunyu Chang and asked for a ride. Chunyu Chang bribed Hongyang Houli with rare treasures through Hongyang Houli's son Rong, and Hongyang Houli in turn spoke for Chunyu Chang.
The emperor saw the great change in Hongyang Houli's attitude and knew that there must be something fishy, ​​so he sent relevant departments to investigate the matter.
Officials captured Rong, and Hongyang Houli forced Rong to commit suicide.
The emperor became more suspicious that there must be serious treachery involved, so he ordered Chun Yu to be arrested and handed over to Shao Prison in Luoyang for investigation into the case.
Chunyu Chang truthfully confessed that he was teasing Queen Xu of Changding Palace and wanted to re-establish Queen Zuo. Chunyu Chang rebelled and died in prison.
Chunyuchang's wife and son were punished and exiled to Hepu. If his mother is sent back to her hometown.
Hongyang Houli was also deported from Kyoto to the vassal states.
Because Chun Yuchang lost power, dozens of generals, ministers, officials, and county guards related to him in the court were dismissed from office.
Wang Mang then replaced Wang Gen as the Grand Sima.
Not long after, Chun Yuchang's mother and her son Chun Yuchou were moved back to Chang'an. Later, Chun Yuchou committed a crime, and Wang Mang killed him and sent his family members home.
At first, Chunyu Chang was close to the emperor because of his status as a relative, but he was not as favored as Fuping Hou Zhang Fang.
Zhang Fang often went out and lived together with the emperor. He changed his clothes and went in and out together with the emperor.
summary: Chun Yuchang, from Yuancheng, served Wang Feng diligently, becoming his nephew. Before Wang Feng's death, he recommended Chun Yuchang to the empress dowager and emperor. Chun Yuchang helped make Feiyan empress, earning a marquis title. He became wealthy, marrying many concubines and having an affair with Xu Wei, sister of deposed Empress Xu. Empress Xu bribed Chun Yuchang to regain favor, but he deceived her. Wang Mang, fearing Chun Yuchang's rise, exposed his crimes to Wang Gen and the empress dowager. Chun Yuchang was dismissed and exiled, dying in prison. His family was exiled, and many officials lost their posts.

translation:
Isn't this what a common man can do?
Wang Hong was resourceful by nature, and he understood what Xiao Xian said. Then he replied to Dong Gong and conveyed Xiao Xian's humble intention in detail.
Dong Gong sighed and said: What can my family do to the world that makes people fear it so much?
Feeling unhappy.
Later, Emperor Ai held a banquet in the Qilin Hall. Dong Xian's father and son's relatives were invited to drink. Wang Hong's brothers and other attendants were all nearby.
After Emperor Ai drank his wine, he looked at Dong Xian and said with a smile: "I want to follow the example of Yao and give way to Shun. How about that?"
Wang Hong dissuaded him and said: "The world belongs to Emperor Gao, not His Majesty's private property."
Your Majesty has inherited the authority of worship in Liu's ancestral temple and should pass it down to endless descendants.
The great cause of imperial unification is of vital importance, and the emperor has no joke!
Emperor Ai was silent and unhappy, and everyone on the left and right were frightened.
So Wang Hong was kicked out and could no longer attend the banquet.
Dong Xian's house was newly built and very solidly built, but the outer gate was damaged for no reason. Dong Xian was very disgusted.
A few months later, Emperor Ai died.
The Empress Dowager summoned Chief Sima Dong Xian to introduce him in Shuxiang Hall and inquire about the arrangements for the funeral.
Dong Xian felt uneasy and couldn't answer correctly, so he went to the crown to apologize.
The Queen Mother said: Wang Mang, the lord of Xindu, used to attend the funeral of the late emperor as the Grand Sima and was familiar with the rituals. I ordered Wang Mang to assist you.
Dong Xian kowtowed in thanks.
The Queen Mother sent an envoy to summon Wang Mang.
As soon as Wang Mang arrived, he asked the Minister to impeach Dong Xian in the name of the Queen Mother for not taking the medicine himself when Emperor Ai was ill, and banned Dong Xian from entering the palace and Sima's official office again.
Dong Xian was at a loss and went to the palace to apologize for his crime.
Wang Mang sent an audience with the Queen Mother's edict to write in the palace: Recently, the yin and yang have been out of balance, disasters have occurred at the same time, and the people have suffered.
The three princes are the ministers who are supporting the tripod. Dong Xian, the Marquis of Gao'an, is ignorant of the principles. As a great commander, he is not in line with the public opinion and fails to fulfill the important task of resisting foreign aggression and stabilizing the distant country.
The Grand Sima seal should be taken back, dismissed from office and returned home.
When Dong Xian and his wife both committed suicide, their family members panicked and buried them overnight.
Wang Mang suspected that he had faked his death, so the deacon officials asked him to send the coffin and go to the prison to inspect it.
Wang Mang also hinted that the great Situ Kong Guang had written a letter, saying that Dong Xian's character was cunning and flattering, and he was granted a title by virtue of his treachery. His father and son were good at government affairs, and his brothers were favored at the same time, and received many rewards.
The father and son were arrogant and foolish. They did not receive the emperor's envoys with courtesy and did not thank them when receiving rewards. Their sins were obvious.
summary: Dong Xian, from Yunyang, served as prince's minister under Emperor Ai. His handsome appearance won favor, and he became Huang Menlang. He rode with the emperor and slept with him. Once, when Dong Xian slept on Emperor Ai's sleeve, the emperor cut it off rather than wake him. Dong Xian's family received immense rewards, and he became Grand Sima at age twenty-two. After Emperor Ai's death, the empress dowager summoned Wang Mang, who impeached Dong Xian for failing to care for the emperor. Dong Xian and his wife committed suicide. Their property was confiscated, and his family exiled. The text concludes that these favored ministers, lacking virtue, met bad ends, and their rise contributed to the Western Han's decline.

translation:
Fu Jiezi was from the North and was promoted to an official because he joined the army.
It turns out that both Qiuci and Loulan had killed envoys of the Han Dynasty, which was recorded in "Biography of the Western Regions".
During the Yuanfeng period, Fu Jiezi requested to be sent to Dayuan as an envoy of Junma, and took the emperor's Shao letter to condemn Loulan and Qiuci.
When Fu Jiezi arrived in Loulan, he blamed the King of Loulan for encouraging the Huns to intercept and kill the Han Dynasty envoys. He said: The large army is about to arrive. If you don't encourage the Huns, why don't you report the Huns' envoys to other countries after passing through?
King Loulan expressed his guilt and said: The Huns envoy has just passed by. He should have gone to Wusun and passed through Qiuci on the way.
When Fu Jiezi arrived at Kucha, he blamed the King of Kucha again, and the King of Kucha also admitted his guilt.
Fu Jiezi returned to Kucha from Dayuan. The Kucha people said that the Huns envoy was here after returning from Wusun.
Fu Jiezi took the opportunity to lead his officers and soldiers to kill the Huns envoy.
Fu Jiezi returned to the capital to report the situation, and the emperor issued an edict appointing him as Zhonglang and promoted him to Ping Yue Supervisor.
Fu Jiezi said to the general Huo Guang: Loulan and Qiuci have been capricious many times but have not been condemned. They cannot be used to punish other countries.
When I passed through Qiuci, their king was very close to others and could easily be attacked. I was willing to go and assassinate him, so as to establish my prestige and announce it to other countries.
The general said: "Qiuci country is far away, so let's go to Loulan to test this method for now."
So he told the emperor to send him there.
Fu Jiezi and the soldiers brought gold and silver coins together, claiming that they were gifts to foreign countries.
When they arrived at Loulan, King Loulan seemed unwilling to get close to Fu Jiezi, so Fu Jiezi pretended to leave. After arriving at the western border of Loulan, Fu Jiezi ordered an interpreter to say to King Loulan: The envoys of the Han Dynasty traveled around with gold and brocade to give to various countries. If the king does not come to receive the gift, I will leave for the country to the west.
He immediately took out the gold coins and showed them to the translator.
The translator came back and reported the situation to King Loulan. King Loulan was greedy for the property of the Han Dynasty, so he came to meet the envoy.
Fu Jiezi sat drinking with him and showed him his belongings.
After drinking, Fu Jiezi was drunk and said to King Loulan: The emperor sent me to report some things to the king privately.
King Loulan got up and followed Fu Jiezi into the tent. The two were talking alone. Two strong men stabbed King Loulan from behind. The blades met in the chest. King Loulan died immediately.
His nobles and left and right officials all fled.
Fu Jiezi told them that King Loulan was guilty of the Han Dynasty, and the emperor sent me to kill him. The prince who had been left as a hostage in the Han Dynasty should be replaced as king.
The Han army has just arrived. Don't act rashly. If you make any move, your country will be wiped out!
After that, he took the head of King Loulan back to Beijing to deliver the order. The ministers, generals and others all praised his achievements.
summary: Fu Jiezi, from the North, became an official through military service. During the Yuanfeng period, he was sent as an envoy to Dayuan and condemned the kings of Loulan and Qiuci for killing Han envoys. After returning, he proposed to General Huo Guang to assassinate the King of Loulan to establish Han prestige. Huo Guang agreed, and Fu Jiezi used gold and silk as bait to lure the king. During a private meeting, two soldiers stabbed the king to death. Fu Jiezi declared the king's guilt and installed a new ruler. He was rewarded with the title of Marquis of Yiyang and 700 households. His title was later abolished due to his son's crime but restored under Wang Mang.

translation:
The emperor then issued an edict saying: King Angui of Loulan had acted as a spy for the Huns, secretly spying on the envoys of the Han Dynasty, and sent troops to kill and plunder three guards, including Ma Anle, Guanglu Dafuzhong, and Qi Menlang Suicheng, as well as envoys from Anxi and Dawan.
Fu Jiezi, the supervisor of Pingle, went out as an envoy with the talisman and killed King Angui of Loulan. He hung his head on the north tower and repaid the resentful people with integrity without disturbing the troops and stirring up the crowd.
Fu Jiezi was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang and given to 700 households in the city.
Among the soldiers who assassinated King Loulan, they all replaced their officials as ministers.
After Fu Jiezi died, his son Fu Chang was guilty and could not inherit the title, and the feudal state was abolished.
In the middle of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the descendants of the heroes were renewed, and Fu Chang, the great-grandson of Fu Jiezi, was granted the title of Marquis of Yiyang. It was only after Wang Mang's failure that the throne was cut off.
Chang Hui is from Taiyuan.
When he was young, his family was poor, so he volunteered to join the army. He followed Su Wu, the eunuch of Zhizhong, on an envoy to the Huns. They were detained by the Huns for more than ten years and were not able to return until Emperor Zhao.
In order to reward his hard work, the Han Dynasty appointed him Guanglu Doctor.
At this time, Princess Wusun wrote a letter saying: The Xiongnu mobilized their cavalry to colonize the Che Division. The Che Division and the Xiongnu army merged into one to jointly invade Wusun. I hope the emperor will come to rescue us. The Han Dynasty recruited troops and raised horses, and discussed preparations to attack the Xiongnu.
After the death of Emperor Zhao, Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne. In the second year of his reign, Chang Hui was sent as envoy to Wusun.
Princess Wusun and King Wusun both sent envoys to the court, and wrote through Chang Hui that the Xiongnu sent large troops to attack Wusun one after another, captured Cheyan, Eshi and other places, and robbed all the local people. They also sent envoys to threaten to marry Wusun Gonggui, in an attempt to isolate Banjie from Xuansu.
King Wu Zhu was willing to recruit half of the elite troops in the country, equip himself with 50,000 soldiers and horses, and do his best to attack the Xiongnu.
I hope the emperor will send troops to save the princess and King Wusun!
So the Han Dynasty mobilized a large scale of 150,000 cavalry, and the five generals set off in separate directions. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of the Xiongnu".
Chang Hui was appointed as the captain of the school and commanded Wusun's army with the talisman.
King Wusun himself led more than 50,000 cavalrymen under Linghou to march from the west to Yougu Liting, and captured Chanyu's father and his entourage, his sister-in-law and princess, famous princes, cavalry generals and 39,000 subordinates, and captured more than 50,000 horses, oxen, donkeys, mules, camels, and more than 600,000 sheep. Wusun took the captured things himself.
Jusai led more than a dozen officers and soldiers to return to the army with King User. Before arriving at Wusun, the Wusun people stole Chang Hui's official seal and talisman.
Chang Hui returned to the capital, thinking that he would be beheaded.
At that time, the five generals of the Han Dynasty had no merit. The emperor felt that Chang Hui's mission was successful, so he named him Changluo Hou.
He also sent Chang Hui back with gold silk ribbons to reward Wusun dignitaries and meritorious people. Chang Hui took the opportunity to report that the Kucha Kingdom had killed the captain Lai Dan and did not punish them. Please go and attack Kucha. Emperor Xuan did not agree.
General Huo Guang hinted that Chang Hui would make his own decisions based on the situation.
Chang Hui arrived at the Wusun Kingdom with 500 officers and soldiers. When he came back and passed by Kucha, he recruited 20,000 troops from the western country. He ordered his deputy to send 20,000 troops from Kucha to tie up the country. Wusun sent 7,000 troops to attack Kucha from three sides. Before the army could gather together, they sent someone to accuse King Qiuci of killing the envoys of the Han Dynasty in the past.
King Qiuci apologized and said: This is the result of being harmed by the noble Gu Yi when I was the late king. I am not guilty.
Chang Hui said: Even so, Gu Yi must be tied up, and I can let the king go.
King Qiuci tied up Guyi and took him to Chang Hui. Chang Hui killed Guyi and went back.
Later, Chang Hui replaced Su Wu as the vassal state. He was familiar with the situation in foreign countries and worked hard many times with meritorious deeds.
In the middle of the year of Ganlu, the later general Zhao Chongguo passed away, and the emperor appointed Limulus Tomb as the right general, and the official position of the Dian vassal state remained as before.
When Emperor Xuan died, Chang Hui served Emperor Yuan. He died three years later, and his nickname was Zhuang Genyao.
summary: Chang Hui, from Taiyuan, was detained by the Xiongnu for over a decade while accompanying Su Wu. After Emperor Zhao's reign, he was sent to Wusun, where he coordinated a joint Han-Wusun attack on the Xiongnu, resulting in significant victories. He later executed a noble from Qiuci for killing a Han captain. Chang Hui succeeded Su Wu as a vassal state official and served under Emperors Xuan and Yuan, earning the posthumous title Zhuang Genyao.

translation:
The feudal state was passed down to the great-grandson, and was discontinued in the middle of Jianwu year.
Zheng Ji is from Kuaiji. Because he served in the army and went on several missions to Yousu, he was named Lang.
Dian Mu is a strong and persistent person and is familiar with foreign affairs.
Since the fortress was connected to Youqiu and Kui Luxing was conquered, school captains were set up to work in Quli.
At the time of Emperor Xuan, Zheng Ji worked in Quli as a minister and accumulated grain. He then mobilized armies from various countries to defeat the chariot division. He was promoted to Sima of the Guard and sent to guard the southern road west of Shanshan.
In the middle of the year of Shenjue, internal turmoil broke out among the Xiongnu. The Xianxian Shan, the king of Chu, planned to surrender to the Han Dynasty and sent someone to contact Zheng Ji.
Zheng Ji mobilized 50,000 people from Quli, Qiuci and other countries to meet King Yue Zhu. There were 12,000 people. Xiao Wang sent 12 people to follow Zheng Ji to Hequ. Many people fled. Zheng Ji chased these people and killed them, and then brought the remaining people to the capital.
Emperor Mo granted King Ri Zhu the title of Marquis of Guide.
After Zheng Ji defeated the chariot division, he surrendered and surrendered to the king. His reputation shocked the Western Regions, so he also took charge of the North Road to the west of the chariot division, so he was known as the Protector.
The establishment of Duhu began with Zheng Ji.
In order to commend him for his achievements, the emperor issued an edict saying: Zheng Ji, the captain of the cavalry in the Western Regions, appeased the foreign barbarians, declared his hope and credibility, welcomed the cousin of the Xiongnu Chanyu, King Ri Zhu, and his men, and attacked the Cheshi Douzi City, which was a remarkable achievement.
Zheng Ji was granted the title of Marquis of Anyuan, and was granted food to 1,000 households in the city.
Zheng Ji then established a shogunate in the center of various countries in the Western Regions, and the official office was in Wulei City to pacify the various countries, kill, conquer, appease and recruit them.
The orders of the Han Dynasty were issued to the Western Regions, and construction was started by Zhang Qian and completed by Zheng Ji. These are recorded in the "Biography of the Western Regions".
After Zheng Ji passed away, he was given the title of Marquis Mu.
His son Zheng Guang inherited the title, but he died without a son and the feudal state was abolished.
In the middle of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, among the meritorious officials who were not expelled due to crimes, Zheng Yong, the great-grandson of Zheng Ji, was granted the title of Marquis of Anyuan.
Gan Yanshou, courtesy name Junkuang, was from Yuzhi in the north.
When he was young, he was selected as Yu Lin because he was good at horseback riding and archery. His skills in throwing stones and jumping were unparalleled among his peers. He once jumped into Yu Lin's pavilion, so he was promoted to Lang.
After testing his hand-fighting skills, he was appointed as a disciple. He relied on his strength and was favored.
Soon he was transferred to the post of governor of Liaodong and was dismissed.
The cavalry general Xu Jia recommended Gan Yanshou as a doctor and admonished the doctor. He went to the Western Regions as an envoy to protect the cavalry captain. Together with the deputy captain Chen Tang, he killed Zhizhi Shanyu and was named Yichenghou.
After Gan Yanshou died, Mi was named Zhuanghou.
The feudal state was passed down to his great-grandson. After Wang Mang failed, the feudal state was ended.
Chen Tang, whose courtesy name is Zigong, is from Shanyang Xiaqiu.
When he was young, he liked to read, he was knowledgeable and well-versed in affairs, and he could write good articles.
The family was poor and relied on begging and borrowing money to make a living. He had no moral integrity and was not praised by the people in the state.
summary: Zheng Ji, from Kuaiji, served as a military officer and became an expert in foreign affairs. He established agricultural colonies in Quli and defeated the Che division, earning the title of Protector of the Western Regions. He was granted the title of Marquis of Anyuan with 1,000 households. His son died without an heir, ending the title, but it was later restored to his great-grandson. Gan Yanshou, from Yuzhi, was a skilled horseman and archer. He served as an envoy to the Western Regions and, with Deputy Captain Chen Tang, killed Zhizhi Chanyu. He was named Marquis of Yicheng. His title passed to his great-grandson before ending under Wang Mang. The text concludes that from Zhang Qian's time to Wang Mang's era, 18 protectors served, with notable figures like Zheng Ji, Gan Yanshou, and Chen Tang. Chen Tang's unruliness led to his downfall, but his deeds are recorded for posterity.

translation:
Uncensored cases should be promptly lifted, allowing them to come and go freely without being held accountable, and be given favors and titles to reward those who have made meritorious deeds.
So the emperor issued an edict saying: The Xiongnu Zhizhi Chanyu betrayed propriety and justice, detained and killed the Han Dynasty envoys, officers and soldiers, which was against the law. How can I forget it?
The reason why he hesitated to go on a conquest was because it was difficult to mobilize the troops and the generals were tired, so they refrained from mentioning this matter.
Now Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang saw that they could take advantage of the opportunity, so they took advantage of the convenience of time, gathered all the countries with towns, and arbitrarily relied on the emperor's order to use troops to conquer the enemy. Relying on the blessing of the gods of heaven, earth and the ancestral temple, they conquered Zhizhi Chanyu and beheaded him, as well as Ban's wife, dignitaries, famous kings and more than a thousand others.
Although they deviated from morality and violated national laws, they did not bother anyone in the country to perform military service, did not use the national treasury's reserves, borrowed the enemy's food to supply the troops, established meritorious service thousands of miles away, shocked all barbarians with their power, and quickly spread their fame all over the world.
Eliminate brutality for the country, cut off the source of war, and stabilize the border.
However, the sorrow of death and injury cannot be avoided. The blame should lie on obeying the law. I deeply feel sorry for this!
Special pardon for Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang's crimes, and do not pursue them further.
Shao ordered his ministers to discuss the reward.
Everyone who discussed it thought that it was appropriate to kill Shan Yu in accordance with military law.
Kuang Heng and Shi Xian believed that Zhizhi originally lost his country and fled abroad. He only stole his name in a deserted place and was not a real Chanyu.
Emperor Yuan followed the old example of Anyuan Marquis Zheng Ji and granted them a settlement of 1,000 households. Kuang Heng and Shi Xian protested again.
So Gan Yanshou was granted the title of Marquis of Yicheng, and Chen Tang was given the title of Marquis of Guan Nei. Each of them was given three hundred households in the city, and a hundred catties of gold.
Offer sacrifices to heaven and the ancestral temple, and grant amnesty to the world.
Gan Yanshou was appointed as the captain of Changshui, and Chen Tang was appointed as the captain of Shesheng.
Gan Yanshou was promoted to the rank of captain of the city gate and captain of the guard army. He passed away in his official position.
Emperor Cheng had just ascended the throne, and Prime Minister Kuang Heng reported again: Chen Tang was ordered to go on an envoy as an official with two thousand stones. He acted among the barbarians without waiting for orders. He did not set strict requirements to set an example for his subordinates. Instead, he took the property he had captured from Kangju and warned the officials not to re-examine the affairs in remote areas.
Even if the matter is pardoned, he is still not suitable for office.
Chen Tang was dismissed from office.
Later, Chen Tang wrote a letter saying that the son sent by King Kangju to serve the emperor was not a prince.
After review and verification, it was indeed the prince.
Chen Tang was imprisoned and should be executed.
summary: Chen Tang, from Shanyang, was a learned but poor man who sought office in Chang'an. He was recommended by Zhang Bo but imprisoned for failing to attend his father's funeral. Later, as Deputy Captain of the Western Regions, he and Gan Yanshou led a campaign against Zhizhi Chanyu, who had killed Han envoys. They mobilized over 40,000 troops, besieged Zhizhi's city, and killed the chanyu. Despite their success, they faced criticism for acting without orders. After a lengthy debate, Emperor Yuan granted them titles and rewards, though Chen Tang was later dismissed for misconduct. He was eventually exiled to Dunhuang but recalled before his death in Chang'an.
rel_path: 汉书/传/傅常郑甘陈段传

translation:
Taizhong doctor Gu Yong wrote a letter to defend Chen Tang and said: I heard that the state of Chu had Ziyu as a minister, and Duke Wen of Jin was uneasy because of him; there were Lian Po and Ma Fu in the state, and the powerful Qin state did not dare to plot against Jingxing; in the modern Han Dynasty, there were Zhidu and Wei Shang, so the Xiongnu did not dare to cross the desert and go south.
Judging from these circumstances, the general who defeated the enemy is the country's most effective military minister and cannot be ignored.
So When a gentleman hears the sound of military drums, he thinks of ministers who can lead troops in battle. I privately believe that Chen Tang, the Marquis of Guannei, who was sent to the Western Regions as a deputy governor, resented Zhizhi Chanyu for being inhumane and worried that the king could not punish him. Crossing Wusun, gathered on the Du Lai River, broke through the three-story city wall, beheaded Zhizhi Chanyu, avenged the grudge that had not been able to kill him for ten years, and wiped out the past humiliation of the border officers and soldiers. Their majesty shocked all the barbarians, and their martial arts spread far and wide. Since the establishment of the Han Dynasty, there has never been such a scene for generals who have conquered foreign countries.
Now Chen Tang broke the law because what he said was wrong, and he has been in jail for a long time. He has not been able to be sentenced for a long time. The law enforcement officials want to use Dapi's criminal law against him.
In the past, Bai Qi was the general of the Qin State. He captured the capital of Ying in the south and killed Tongkuo in the north. Because of a small mistake, he was killed by Du You. The people of Qin mourned for him and all of them shed tears.
Now Chen Tang personally carries weapons and fights thousands of miles away with bloodshed. He sacrifices his military exploits to the ancestral temple and reports to heaven. All warriors admire his integrity.
There is no great sin in committing a sin because of telling something.
"Book of Zhou" says: If you keep in mind the merits of others and forget the faults of others, you will be fit to be a monarch.
Besides, if dogs and horses work hard for people, they can still get shacks built for them in return, not to mention the meritorious officials of the country!
Privately, I worry that your Majesty has ignored the sound of the military drums, failed to understand the meaning of the "Book of Zhou", and forgotten the kindness of building a shack, treated Chen Tang as a mediocre minister, and finally obeyed the officials' decision. Letting the people also have the resentment of the people of Qin is not a way to spur ministers who risk their lives.
After the memorial was submitted, the emperor released Chen Tang, revoked his title and became an ordinary soldier.
A few years later, Duan Huizong, the protector of the Western Regions, was surrounded by the Wusun army. People from the post station came on horseback to report, hoping to send troops from countries with towns in the Western Regions and Dunhuang troops to rescue them.
Prime Minister Wang Shang, General Wang Feng and hundreds of officials discussed the matter for several days with no result.
Wang Feng said: "Chen Tang is very good at planning and familiar with foreign situations. You can call him to ask."

summary: The history and transmission of Confucian classics from ancient times through the Han dynasty. Ancient Confucians studied the "Six Arts," a classic of the Wang Sect used by sages to clarify the Tao, correct human relations, and achieve governance. Due to his saintly virtue but encountering difficult times, he sighed about the phoenix not coming and the river not flowing out the map. He traveled among princes, entering Zhou in the west and Chu in the south, facing hardships like being frightened in Kuang and short of food in Chen. He revised music after returning from Wei to Lu, ensuring "Ya" and "Song" found their places. He explored ancient and modern books, praising Yao and Zhou, and reviewed the "Books," "Shao Wu," and "Zhou Nan." He connected Zhou rites with Lu's "Spring and Autumn," listing actions of twelve princes using civil and military methods as standards. In his later years, he liked "Yi," reading it so much that the bamboo slip bindings broke several times, and he wrote a biography for it. After Confucius's death, his seventy disciples scattered among princes, with some becoming masters and others mentors. During the Warring States period, Confucianism was denounced, but scholars in Qilu did not abandon the great way. Mencius and Sun Qing followed Confucius's cause and became famous. When Qin Shihuang burned "Poems" and "Books" and killed magicians, the Six Studies became incomplete. When Chen She became king, Confucian scholars from Lu took Kong's ritual vessels to him, and Kong Jia became his doctor, dying with him. Emperor Gao besieged Lu, but Confucian scholars there still recited rituals and sang. Then Confucian scholars began studying classics and teaching rituals. After a year, those specializing in one subject and learning more arts could become doctors. Those not proficient would be exempted. The edict was issued, and from then on, many officials were virtuous and literary. During Emperor Zhao's reign, virtuous literature was recommended, and doctoral disciples increased. At the end of Xuanlong's reign, the number doubled. Gencha liked Confucianism, and those mastering classics were exempted from corvee. Later, due to insufficient funds, the number was changed to 1,000, and counties established "Hundred Stones" History of the Five Classics. Forty in the first class served as doctors, twenty as prince's family, and forty made up for literary stories. Ding Kuan, a native of Liang, studied with Dan Bao and later taught Wang Se, leading to the Shi, Mencius, and Liangqiu schools. The Marquis of Gaoping had neither talent nor fame. He died that year and was given the title of Marquis of Dai. His son Wang Maizhi succeeded him as Marquis of Dai.
In the first year of Suihe, Emperor Cheng had ascended the throne for more than 20 years and still had no heirs. King Dingtao Gong had died and his son succeeded to the throne.
Queen Dingtao, the grandmother of King Dingtao, bribed General Wang Gen with generous gifts in the hope of making King Dingtao the prince. Wang Gen spoke on her behalf. Emperor Cheng also planned to make King Dingtao the prince, so he summoned him to the capital to be crowned prince.
At this time, Wang Gen had been assisting the government for five years. He asked to resign and return to his hometown. Emperor Cheng added 5,000 households to Wang Gen's fiefdom, rewarded him with a carriage, four horses, and five hundred catties of gold. He dismissed his official position and returned to his mansion.
Previously, Chun Yuchang, the Marquis of Dingling, was able to make suggestions as a relative and served as a guard official, assisting in government affairs.
In this year, Wang Mang, the Marquis of Xindu, reported Chun Yuchang's past crimes and had colluded with Hongyang Marquis Wang Li. Chun Yuchang was imprisoned and died, and Wang Li returned to his fiefdom. This incident was recorded in "The Biography of Chunyu Chang".
Therefore, Wang Gen, the Marquis of Quyang, recommended Wang Mang to replace him. Emperor Cheng also believed that Wang Mang was loyal and upright, so he promoted Wang Mang from the position of Guanglu Guanglu to the rank of Chief Sima.
More than a year later, Emperor Cheng died and Emperor Ai ascended the throne.
summary: Emperor Cheng had no heirs for over twenty years. King Dingtao's grandmother bribed Wang Gen to make him crown prince. After Emperor Cheng's death, Emperor Ai ascended but was unhappy with the Wang family's power. He eventually forced Wang Mang and others to return to their fiefdoms. When Emperor Ai died without an heir, the Empress Dowager appointed Wang Mang as Grand Sima, and they installed Emperor Ping, who was only nine years old.

translation:
Whenever the Queen Mother passed through a county, she would show great kindness to the people and reward the people with money, silk, cattle and wine. This gradually formed a habit.
The Queen Mother said with a gentle face: When I first entered the Prince's house, I was summoned in the Bing Hall. It has been fifty or sixty years now, and I can still remember the scene at that time.
Wang Mang said, "The prince's palace is nearby. You can go there for fun without any trouble."
Therefore, the Queen Mother visited the Prince's palace and was very happy.
Nong'er, who was beside the Queen Mother, fell ill and lived in a foreign house. Wang Mang went to greet him personally.
Wang Mang went so far as to cater to the Queen Mother's wishes.
Emperor Ping died without heirs, so Wang Mang summoned Liu Ying, the youngest great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan and the son of Marquis Guangqi, who was only two years old, on the pretext that he would divine the most auspicious divination.
It suggested that the ministers petitioned to establish Liu Ying as a son, and let the Prime Minister Anhan Duke Mang temporarily occupy the position of emperor and handle political affairs, just like the story of Zhou Gong assisting the king.
The Queen Mother believed that this was not allowed, but she could not stop it with her own strength, so Wang Mang became the regent, changed the reign name, and exercised the power of the emperor.
Not long after, Liu Chong, the Marquis of Anzhong of the clan, Zhai Yi, the prefect of Shujun, and others were disgusted with Wang Mang and raised troops one after another to kill him.
When the Queen Mother heard the news, she said: People think the same thing.
Even though I am a woman, I also know that Wang Mang will definitely be worried about his own safety and cannot do this.
Later, Wang Mang used the talisman to establish himself as the true emperor, and first presented those auspicious signs to the Queen Mother, who was shocked.
At the beginning, when Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty entered Xianyang and reached Bashang, Prince Qin Ying surrendered at Zhidao Pavilion and presented Qin Shihuang's national seal.
When the great ancestor executed Xiang Ji and ascended the throne as the emperor, he personally wore this national seal and passed it down from generation to generation, known as the Mochuan national seal. Because Ruzi had not yet ascended the throne, the imperial seal was kept in Changle Palace.
When Wang Mang came to the throne, he wanted to pass on the national seal, but the Queen Mother refused to give it to him.
Wang Mang instructed Anyang Marquis Wang Shun to convey his intention to the Queen Mother.
Wang Shun has always been cautious and thoughtful, and the Queen Mother usually likes to trust him.
Wang Shun paid a visit to the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother knew that he was here to ask for the imperial seal for Wang Mang, so she angrily scolded him and said: Your father and son families have been favored by the Han family and have been rich and powerful for generations. Not only did you not repay the favor, you accepted the task of entrusting the orphans, but you took the opportunity to seize other people's countries. You no longer care about your kindness.
People like this are worse than pigs and dogs. How can there be brothers like you in the world!
Besides, I used the Golden Chamber Talisman to become the new emperor and changed the calendar and the system of clothing, carriages and horses, so I should make my own national seal and pass it on to all generations. Why do I need to come here to get the national seal that is unlucky for the country to perish?
I am an old widow of the Han family. I am about to die. I want to be buried with this Fang Chuanguo Seal, but you will not be able to get it in the end!
summary: Wang Mang gradually consolidated power, eventually becoming regent and later usurping the throne to establish the Xin dynasty. The Empress Dowager refused to give him the imperial seal, angrily denouncing him for betraying the Han dynasty. She threw the seal on the ground, predicting the Wang family would be exterminated. Wang Mang changed her title to "New Empress Dowager Wenmu," severing her connection to Han. She died at eighty-four, and ten years later, Han soldiers killed Wang Mang.

translation:
Wang Mang changed the system of wearing sable among the servants of the Mo family, so that all the servants wore yellow sable. He also changed the dates of Zhengshuo and Fula in the Han family.
The Queen Mother made her subordinates all wear sable. On New Year's Day and the twelfth lunar month of the Han Dynasty, she would sit and drink with the waiters around her to show that she did not forget the Han Dynasty.
When the Queen Mother was eighty-four years old, in February of the fifth year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Guichou died.
In March Yiyou, he was buried in Weiling together with Emperor Yuan.
Wang Mang issued an edict and asked the doctor Yang Xiong to write a sacrificial text, saying: The essence of Taiyin, the spirit of Shalu, the sky unites with Han, and the matching element is generated.
It shows that she is in harmony with Shalu of Yuancheng.
The essence of Taiyin means that the Queen Mother was born from a dream of the moon.
Ten years after the death of the Queen Mother, Han soldiers killed Wang Mang.
At the beginning, Wang Li, the Marquis of Hongyang, returned to his fiefdom of Nanyang and formed a relationship with the Liu family's children. Wang Li's youngest son, Wang Dan, became the prefect of Zhongshan.
When Emperor Guangwu of Shizu just raised an army, Wang Dan surrendered and he became a general and died in battle.
Shizu took great pity on him and named his son Wang Hong the Marquis of Wuhuan. This title has been passed down to this day.
Situ Peng Ban Biao said: Since the Three Dynasties, the reasons for the demise of princes and monarchs recorded in the "Spring and Autumn" have rarely been caused by favored women.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, the concubines' families, the Lu family, the Huo family, and the Shangguan family, nearly endangered the country several times.
The rise of Wang Mang was due to the fact that after Xiaoyuan, there were four generations of emperors in the Han Dynasty. Her mother respected the world. She reigned for more than sixty years. Her younger brothers came to power one after another and controlled the government. They granted a total of five generals and ten princes. Finally, Wang Mang, the new prince of the capital, realized his ambition.
The dynasties have changed, but the Queen of the Yuan Dynasty is still loyal and holds the imperial seal in her hand, and does not want to hand it over to Wang Mang. The kindness of a woman is really pitiful!
summary: The historian Ban Biao noted that since the Three Dynasties, few dynasties fell due to favored women. The Wang family's rise came through four generations of empresses, with five generals and ten marquises, culminating in Wang Mang's usurpation. The Yuan Empress Dowager's loyalty, holding the imperial seal and refusing to surrender it, was truly pitiful.

translation:
Gongsun He, courtesy name Zishu, was born in Yiqu County, Beidi County.
Gongsun He's grandfather Kunxie was the prefect of Longxi County during the Han Dynasty. He was named Pingquhou because of his meritorious service in leading the army to attack the rebellious Wu, Chu and other countries. He wrote more than a dozen books.
Gongsun He was a knight when he was young, joined the army and made many military exploits.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was the crown prince, Gongsun He sacrificed his life for the prince. When Emperor Wu came to the throne, he promoted Gongsun He to the rank of servant.
Gongsun He's wife Wei Junru was the sister of Queen Wei, and Gongsun He was favored for this reason.
During the Yuanguang period of Emperor Wu, he was appointed General of Qingche and garrisoned in Mayi.
Four years later, he led his army out of Yunzhong to attack the Xiongnu.
After another five years of encountering him, he followed the general Wei Qing as a chariot and cavalry general to attack the Huns. With meritorious service, he was named Marquis of Nanao.
Later, as General Zuo, he attacked the Xiongnu from Dingxiang County, but failed. He was convicted of offering gold of insufficient quality and lost his title as a marquis.
Then General Fuju went out of Wuyuan County for more than 2,000 miles to attack the Xiongnu, but to no avail.
Eight years later, he finally replaced Shi Qing as prime minister and was named Ge Yihou.
At that time, the imperial court was very busy, supervising and punishing ministers.
After Gongsun Hong, the prime ministers Li Cai, Yan Qingzhai, and Zhao Zhou were convicted and died one after another.
Although Shi Qing died a good death because of his caution, he was criticized many times.
When Gongsun He was appointed as prime minister, he was unwilling to accept the Prime Minister's seal, kowtowed and cried, saying: I am originally from the border, and I became an official by relying on my ability to ride and shoot on horseback, but I am really not qualified to be prime minister.
When the emperor and his ministers saw Gongsun He's sorrow, they were moved to tears. Emperor Wu said: Help the prime minister up.
Gongsun He refused to get up, so the emperor got up and left. Gongsun He had no choice but to accept the appointment.
After leaving the palace, the ministers asked Gongsun He why he did not want to be the prime minister. Gongsun He said: Your Majesty is wise, but I am not qualified to be the prime minister. I am afraid of heavy responsibility, and I will be in danger from now on.
Gongsun He's son Gongsun Jingsheng replaced Gongsun He as the imperial servant, and father and son lived together as ministers.
Gongsun Jingsheng relied on the fact that he was the son of the queen's sister. He was arrogant and extravagant and did not abide by the law. During Emperor Wu's Zhenghe period, he embezzled 19 million of the Northern Army's money without authorization. After the incident was discovered, he was arrested and imprisoned.
At this time, the emperor issued an edict to search for Zhu Anshi from Yangling County, but he had not yet been captured. The emperor was eager to arrest him and bring him to justice. Gongsun He himself requested to hunt down Zhu Anshi to atone for Gongsun Jingsheng's crime.
The emperor agreed to Gongsun He's request.
Later, Gongsun He indeed captured Zhu Anshi.
Zhu Anshi was a great knight in the capital. Hearing that Gongsun He wanted to use him to atone for his son's sins, he smiled and said: The prime minister's disaster has implicated his clan.
summary: Gongsun He, a native of Beidi Commandery, rose from a knight-errant background through military merit. He became favored due to his marriage to Empress Wei's sister and served as a general under Emperor Wu, earning the title of Marquis of Nanao for attacking the Xiongnu. After losing his marquisate for presenting inferior gold, he eventually became Chancellor and was titled Marquis of Ge Yi. He reluctantly accepted the position, weeping and predicting his own danger. His son Gongsun Jingsheng, arrogant and corrupt, embezzled military funds. To atone for his son, Gongsun He captured the knight Zhu Anshi, who retaliated by reporting Gongsun Jingsheng's affair with a princess and accusations of witchcraft against the emperor. Both father and son died in prison, and their clan was exterminated. This incident sparked the witchcraft disaster that ultimately led to the deaths of the princess, empress, and crown prince.
