translation:
The prince's retainers, all who had ever entered or exited the palace, were beheaded.
Those who followed the prince and launched an army to rebel would have their entire families exterminated in accordance with the laws that punished rebels.
Officials and soldiers who took advantage of the chaos to rob were all exiled to Dunhuang County.
Since the prince was on the run, troops were stationed at the gates of Chang'an City from this time on.
More than twenty days later, the prince was captured in Hu County.
The words are in "The Story of the Prince".
The next year, General Li Guang of the Second Division led his troops to attack the Huns. Prime Minister Liu Quyou hosted a farewell banquet for Li Guangli and sent it to Weiqiao. Liu Quyou and Li Guangli said goodbye.
Li Guangli said: I hope that the king will ask the emperor to make the king of Changyi the crown prince soon.
If King Changyi is established as emperor, what will you worry about in the future?
Liu Quyou agreed to Li Guangli's request.
King Changyi was the son of Li Guangli's sister, Mrs. Li.
Li Guangli's daughter was the wife of Liu Quya's son, so both Li Guangli and Liu Quya wanted to make the king of Changyi the crown prince.
At this time, the investigation of the witchcraft prison was very tight. The insider ordered Guo Chen to report the wife of Prime Minister Liu Qumo because Liu Qumo was reprimanded by the emperor many times, instructing the wizard to curse the emperor when offering sacrifices to the earth god. There were vicious words, and Liu Qumo and Li Guangli prayed and sacrificed together, hoping to make King Changyi the emperor.
The officials in charge reported the matter to Emperor Wu and requested an interrogation and examination. Emperor Wu approved it, and the investigators convicted Liu Quya of treason.
Emperor Wu ordered Liu Quya to be put on a cart carrying food and paraded through the streets, and then beheaded in half in Shushi, Chang'an. Liu Quli's wife was taken to Huayang Street and beheaded in public.
Li Guangli's wife and children were also imprisoned.
When Li Guangli heard the news, he surrendered to the Huns and all his clan were executed.
Che Qianqiu's original surname was Tian, ​​and his ancestors were the Tian family from Qi State in the Spring and Autumn Period. Later, a branch of the Tian family moved to Changling County.
Che Qianqiu served as the official guarding the tomb of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
When Prince Wei was slandered by Jiang Chong and was defeated, after a long encounter, Che Qianqiu submitted a memorial of serious emergency, defending the crown prince, saying: The son who played tricks on his father's army should be whipped; the emperor's son accidentally killed someone due to negligence, what crime should he be sentenced to?
I once saw an old man with white hair in a dream who told me how to convict someone.
At this time, Emperor Wu already knew clearly that the prince sent troops out of fear and had no intention of rebellion. After reading Che Qianqiu's letter, he was deeply touched and came to his senses, so he summoned Che Qianqiu.
Che Qianqiu came forward to pay homage to Emperor Wu. Emperor Wu saw that Che Qianqiu was more than eight feet tall and handsome and liked him very much. He said to him: It is difficult for others to talk about matters between father and son. Only you understand that this is not the case.
This is the god of Gaomiao asking you to enlighten me, so you should be my assistant.
Immediately ordered the car to be sealed for Qianqiu as Da Honglu.
A few months later, he succeeded Liu Quyou as prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Fumin.
summary: Liu Quli, son of Prince Jing of Zhongshan, replaced Gongsun He as Left Chancellor. Emperor Wu issued an edict condemning Gongsun He's corruption and appointed Liu Quli as Marquis of Peng. During the witchcraft rebellion, Crown Prince Ju killed the accuser Jiang Chong and raised troops. Liu Quli led imperial forces against the prince, resulting in a five-day battle with tens of thousands dead. The prince fled but was captured twenty days later. The following year, Liu Quli conspired with General Li Guangli to make the Prince of Changyi crown prince. This conspiracy was discovered, and Liu Quli was executed by waist-cutting, while Li Guangli surrendered to the Xiongnu. Che Qianqiu, originally named Tian, served as guardian of Emperor Gaozu's tomb. After the crown prince's defeat, Che submitted a memorial defending the prince, arguing that a son who mobilizes troops against his father should only be whipped. Emperor Wu, already regretting his actions, was moved and appointed Che as Grand Herald, then Chancellor within months, creating the unprecedented precedent of becoming Chancellor through a single memorial. Though lacking scholarly talents, Che proved competent and kind-hearted. After Emperor Wu's death, Che served under Emperor Zhao alongside General Huo Guang, deferring to Huo's authority while maintaining loyalty. He served as Chancellor for twelve years and was posthumously titled Marquis Ding.
rel_path: 汉书/传/公孙刘田王杨蔡陈郑传

translation:
Che Qianqiu is the prime minister, loyal, honest and virtuous.
Whenever ministers and ministers met, Huo Guang would say to Che Qianqiu: "Back then, I accepted the Emperor's mission with you. Now that Huo Guang is in charge of internal affairs and you are in charge of foreign affairs, what should I have to enlighten and urge me so that I don't let down the trust of the people of the world?"
Che Qianqiu said: General, please pay more attention, it will be the greatest honor in the world.
He always refused to express any objection to Huo Guang's dictatorship.
Huo Guang therefore valued Che Qianqiu very much.
Every time an auspicious occasion appears, he will praise and reward the prime minister with a thousand-year-old car.
Until the death of Emperor Zhao, the country had few affairs and the people gradually became rich and fulfilled.
In the sixth year of the First Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Zhao Shao ordered the county to recommend virtuous and literary people, and asked them about the sufferings of the people, which led to the discussion of salt and iron.
Che Qianqiu served as prime minister for twelve years. After his death, Mi was named Dinghou.
At first, when Che Qianqiu was old, the emperor treated him favorably and showed up to the court. He was allowed to enter the palace in a small car, so he was known as the "Prime Minister of Cars".
Che Qianqiu's son Tian Shun succeeded him as a marquis and became the prefect of Yunzhong County. At that time, Emperor Xuan was serving as General Huya to attack the Xiongnu. He was convicted of committing suicide for illegally increasing the number of prisoners and taking credit, and the feudal state was cancelled.
Sang Hongyang worked as a censor for eight years. He thought it would benefit the country and boasted about his achievements. He wanted to get official positions for the children of the Sang family. He resented Huo Guang and rebelled against Shangguan Jie and others, and was finally executed.
Wang Xin is from Jinan County.
As a junior official in the county, he accumulated merit and was gradually promoted to the magistrate of Baiyang County.
In the last years of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the army often went on expeditions, and thieves gathered in the counties and counties. The embroidered censor's sudden victory directed the envoys to hunt down the thieves with axes, and dealt with the property collected by the local officials according to the amount of property collected and handed over to the court for military use. Officials with less than 2,000 dan who disobeyed orders were executed.
Baoshengzhi inspected Beiyang and wanted to kill Wang Xin. Wang Xin had undressed and was lying on the chopping board under the guillotine. Gongxin raised his head and said to Baoshengzhi: You have the power of life and death and are powerful in the county. Killing another Wang Xin now will not increase your prestige. It is better to be lenient according to the situation to show your kindness and mercy. Let me try my best to repay you.
Bao Shengzhi admired what he said and forgave him without killing him. Therefore, Bao Shengzhi and Wang Xin became close friends.
After Shengzhi completed his mission and returned to Beijing, he recommended Wang Xin to the emperor. Emperor Wu recruited him to serve as the captain of Youfu, acting as Youfu Feng.
Emperor Wu visited Saitong and Jiidi many times. When he passed through Diehuang, Tanqiu sent people to clean the palace, make the roads smooth, and set up curtains and curtains for comfort.
Emperor Wu was very happy, commended Wang Xin, stopped the car, and changed Wang Xin's official position to a regular one, and he ruled for more than ten years.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao, Wang Xin served as the imperial censor, succeeded Che Qianqiu as prime minister, and was named Marquis of Yichun.
summary: Wang Xin of Jinan Commandery rose from minor official to magistrate. When Imperial Censor Bao Shengzhi investigated and prepared to execute him, Wang Xin pleaded for mercy, arguing that killing him would not increase Shengzhi's prestige. Impressed, Shengzhi spared him and later recommended him. Wang Xin served Emperor Wu competently, becoming You Fufeng. Under Emperor Zhao, he succeeded Che Qianqiu as Chancellor and was titled Marquis of Yichun, dying the following year.
rel_path: 汉书/传/公孙刘田王杨蔡陈郑传

translation:
He died the next year and was named Jinghou.
Wang Xin's son Wang Tan inherited his father's title, and as a prince participated in the plan to abolish the king of Changyi, support Emperor Xuan, and increase the number of 300 households in the land.
After Wang Tan died, his son Wang Xian inherited his title.
Yucha's wife was Wang Sheng's daughter. After Wang Chai usurped the throne, Wang Sheng's family respected her because she was a relative.
Starting from Wang Xin, the feudal state was passed down to Great-grandson, and was discontinued after Wang Mang's defeat.
Yang Chang is from Huayin County.
When he served in the general Tingguang shogunate, he was appointed military commander. Huo Guang liked and treated him favorably, and he was gradually promoted to chief agricultural officer.
During the Wuhuang period of Guitong, the rice field envoy You Dong learned of the rebellion conspiracy of Emperor Jie and others and informed Yang Chang of the matter.
Yang Chang was always cautious and fearful, and did not dare to report to Emperor Zhao, so he wrote a letter claiming to be ill and emigrated.
Yan Cang told the news to Du Yannian, the admonishing doctor, and Du Yannian reported it to Emperor Zhao.
Yan Cang and Du Yannian were both granted the title of marquis for their meritorious service. As the ninth minister, Yang Chang heard the news of the rebellion but failed to report it in time, so he was not granted the title of marquis.
Later, he was promoted to imperial censor, succeeded Wang Xin as prime minister, and was granted the title of Marquis of Anping.
In the second year, Emperor Zhao died.
The king of Changyi came to Beijing to take the throne after being summoned by the ministers. He was promiscuous and immoral. The general Huo Guang conspired with the chariot general Zhang Anshi to depose the king of Luyi and reestablish the emperor.
It was agreed upon that Da Si’s farmland would be extended to inform Yang Chang.
Yang Chang was very frightened after hearing this. He didn't know what to say. His back was wet with sweat and he could only make a "weiwei" sound.
Tian Yannian got up and went to the dressing room to change clothes. Yang Chang's wife hurriedly came out of the side room and said to Yang Chang: This is a national event. Now the general's plan has been decided. I asked Dasi Nanyang Yannian to tell you.
If you don't agree quickly and work together with the general, if you hesitate, you will be killed first.
When Tian Yannian came back from the dressing room, both Yang Chang and his wife and Tian Yannian agreed with the general's decision and asked to obey the general's order. So the court ministers deposed King Changyi and established Emperor Xuan.
More than a month after Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Yang Chang died, and Mi was named Jinghou.
His son Yang Zhong inherited the title. Because Yang Chang was the prime minister, he participated in the formulation of the strategy of deposing the king of Changyi and replacing him with Emperor Xuan. He made great contributions to the stabilization of the Moshi ancestral temple and the increase of 3,500 households in the city.
Yang Zhong's younger brother Yang Yun, named Ziyou, relied on Yang Zhong's official position and was appointed Lang Guan according to the Han Dynasty's son appointment system, filling the post of Chang Shiqi. Yang Yun's mother was Sima Qian's daughter.
Yang Yun first read "Tai Shi Gong Ji" written by his grandfather, and was also familiar with "Spring and Autumn".
Because of his talent, he is praised by people.
He liked to make friends with handsome and outstanding Confucian scholars. He became famous in the court and was promoted to Zuocao.
summary: Yang Chang of Huayin Commandery served in General Huo Guang's staff, rising to Minister of Agriculture. Learning of a rebellion conspiracy, Yang Chang, being cautious, feigned illness rather than reporting it. Another official reported the matter and received a marquisate, while Yang Chang was denied this honor. He later became Imperial Censor and succeeded Wang Xin as Chancellor, titled Marquis of Anping. After Emperor Zhao's death, when Huo Guang planned to depose the immoral King of Changyi, Yang Chang initially hesitated but was persuaded by his wife to cooperate. He died shortly after Emperor Xuan's accession.

translation:
Gongsun Hong was born in Xue County, Sichuan State.
He worked as a jailer when he was young. Removed from office for committing a crime.
Because his family was poor, he made a living by herding pigs on the beach.
When he was in his forties, he began to study "Spring and Autumn" and miscellaneous treatises of various schools.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he recruited virtuous and literary people. At this time, Gongsun Hong was sixty years old and got a doctorate as a virtuous and literary person.
He was sent as an envoy to the Huns and returned to the court to report, which was not in line with the emperor's wishes. Emperor Wu was very angry and thought he was incompetent, so Gongsun Hong wrote a letter claiming to be ill and was dismissed from office and returned to his hometown.
In the fifth year of Yuanguang, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty once again selected virtuous literary people, and Dong Weihui once again recommended Gong Zhucong.
Gong Chuicong declined and said: I went west to Beijing in the past and was dismissed because of my incompetence. I hope to choose someone else.
But the people of the country insisted on recommending him, so Gongsun Hong came to Taichang.
The emperor went down to Shao Shu Ce and asked all the Confucian scholars:
The bookmaker wrote: I heard that in ancient times, when politics was perfect, the punishment for criminals was to mark their clothes and hats and let them wear special clothes, but the common people did not break the law. At that time, Yin and Yang were in harmony, the grains were abundant, the livestock were multiplying, the dew fell from the sky, the weather was smooth, the rice with full grains grew, the red auspicious grass appeared, the mountains were covered with dense forests and lush grass, and the lakes did not dry up. Unicorns and phoenixes appear in the lakes on the outskirts of the city. Turtles and dragons swim in the ponds, rivers produce pictures, and Luo produces books. A son will not die before his father, nor will a younger brother die before his elder brother. At that time, as far as Qusou in the north and Jiaodu in the south, as long as it was reachable by cars and boats and people could walk, all living beings had their own place.
I admire that era very much. How can we govern the country now to reach this state?
You have studied the laws of the sages, you are well versed in the principles of the superiority and inferiority of kings and ministers, and you are very insightful in your discussions. You are all very famous today. I dare to ask you: What is the most fundamental way of heaven and man?
How to predict good and bad luck?
Floods and droughts occurred during the reign of Yu and Tang. What were their faults?
What methods should be used to perfect and coordinate the four aspects of benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom?
The succession of the imperial line, the vagaries of life and death, the signs of divine destiny, how did all these rise and fall happen?
The laws of astronomy, geography, and human affairs, flowers are what you study.
Please write down what you think is a comprehensive and correct discussion into a detailed article. I will read it personally and don’t hide anything.
Gongsun Hong replied:
summary: Gongsun Hong, born in Xue County, Sichuan State, began his career as a jailer but was dismissed for a crime. Left impoverished, he herded pigs until his forties, when he started studying the "Spring and Autumn" and various philosophical texts. At sixty, he was recruited as a virtuous and literary person under Emperor Wu of Han, but his mission to the Huns displeased the emperor, leading to his dismissal. In the fifth year of Yuanguang, he was recommended again and, despite initial reluctance, presented a detailed policy response. His essay emphasized governance through righteousness, trust, and eight principles: appointing by talent, avoiding useless discussions, reducing taxes, not harming agriculture, promoting the virtuous, rewarding merit, punishing crime appropriately, and rewarding virtue. He argued that harmony between heaven and earth arises from unified virtue, and that floods and droughts under Yu and Tang were due to prior misrule. His response was ranked first by the emperor, who appointed him as a doctor.

translation:
From this, the emperor saw that his behavior was cautious and honest, he left room for debate, he was familiar with documents, laws and official duties, and he decorated it with Confucianism, so he liked him very much and promoted him to Zuo Neishi within a year.
When Gongsun Hong went to court, he did not argue in court if he thought something was wrong.
He often went to see the emperor one after another with Ji An, the lord captain. Ji An raised questions first, and Gongsun Hong then elaborated. The emperor was often very happy and listened to everything he said. As a result, Gongsun Hong became more and more favored.
He once made an appointment with the minister to make some suggestions, but when he came to the emperor, he completely reneged on the agreement and followed the emperor's intention.
Ji An accused Gongsun Hong in court: Many people in Qi are hypocritical and dishonest. They first made the above suggestions to the ministers, and now completely betrayed the previous agreement. This is disloyal to the king.
The emperor asked Gongsun Hong, and Gongsun Hong apologized and said: Those who know me well think that I am loyal to the king; those who do not know me think that I am unfaithful.
The emperor thought his words made sense.
The emperor's favorites slandered Gongsun Hong, but the emperor treated him more and more favorably.
Gongsun Hong was good at talking and well-informed. He often said that what a monarch fears is not being magnanimous and magnanimous, and what a minister fears is not being frugal.
He served his stepmother respectfully and filially. When his stepmother died, he spent three years in mourning.
After working as a historian for several years, Gongsun Hong was promoted to the imperial censor.
At that time, Canghai County was newly established in the east, and Shuofang County was built in the north.
Gongsun Hong advised him several times, thinking that it was a waste of money and people to manage a useless place, and it was not worth the exhaustion of the Central Plains area, so he hoped to stop it.
The emperor then ordered Zhu Maichen and others to refute Gongsun Hong and demonstrate the necessity of establishing Shuofang County.
Zhu Maichen and others raised ten questions, but Gongsun Hong could not refute any of them.
So he apologized to the emperor and said: I am a vulgar person from Shandong. I don't understand how beneficial it is to establish Shuofang County. I hope to stop moving to Southwest Yi and Canghai County and focus on running Shuofang County.
The emperor then agreed to his request.
Ji An said: Gongsun Hong is ranked among the three nobles and has a lot of salary, but he uses cloth to make quilts. This is hypocrisy.
The emperor asked Gongsun Hong, and he apologized and said: There is such a thing.
Among the nine ministers, no one has a better friendship with me than Ji An, but today when he questioned me in court, he really hit on my weakness.
As one of the Three Lords, using a cloth quilt is indeed a pretense and deception, in order to gain fame and reputation.
I heard that when Guan Zhong was the prime minister of Qi, he married three women with different surnames. His luxury was comparable to that of a monarch. Duke Huan of Qi relied on his assistance to dominate, but he was against an arrogant king.
Yan Ying served as Qi Jinggong's prime minister. He did not eat two portions of meat and vegetables for one meal, and his concubines did not wear silk clothes. Qi State was also governed very well. He was looking down on the common people.
Now I, Gongsun Hong, serve as the imperial censor. I use cloth quilts to eliminate the distinction between high and low officials from Jiuqing to the junior officials. It's exactly what Ji An said.
Besides, without Ji An, how could your Majesty hear what I said?
The emperor thought he could be polite and respected him more and more.
During the Yuanshuo period, Gongsun Hong replaced Xue Ze as prime minister.
summary: Gongsun Hong rose quickly, becoming Zuo Neishi within a year, known for cautious debate and Confucian decorum. He avoided court confrontations, often aligning with the emperor’s wishes, which drew accusations of hypocrisy from Ji An. Gongsun Hong defended himself, and the emperor favored him more. He served as imperial censor and later prime minister, receiving the title Marquis of Pingjin. Despite his high rank, he lived frugally, eating simple meals and using cloth quilts, spending his salary on guests and relatives. However, he was inwardly vengeful, contributing to the downfall of rivals like Dong Zhongshu. During the Huainan and Hengshan rebellions, he fell ill and offered to resign, but the emperor refused, granting him leave. He died in office at eighty.

translation:
An unruly minister cannot be used as an example to follow. I hope Your Majesty will not agree.
The emperor did not accept Bu Shi's request, and returned to Bu Shi a few years later.
After Bu Shi returned to his hometown, he resumed his sheep herding business.
A year later, King Hunxie and others surrendered to the Han Dynasty. The state expenses were too high, the warehouses were empty, and the poor people were migrating. They all relied on state supplies, but they could not fully provide them.
Bu Shi also gave 200,000 yuan to the governor of Henan to save the refugees.
When Henan reported a list of rich people to help the poor, the emperor recognized Bu Shi and said: He is the one who insists on giving half of his family property to help the poor.
So Bu Shi was given 400 servants, and all of them were returned to the government.
At that time, the rich were all scrambling to hide their property, but Bu Shi especially wanted to help the country with expenses.
The emperor then respected Bu Shi as an elder, summoned Bu Shi to be the middle man, granted him the rank of Zuo Shu Zhang, and ten hectares of farmland, and announced it to the world to show his respect and encourage the people to follow his example.
At first, Bu Shi was unwilling to become a husband. The emperor said, "I have sheep in Shanglin Garden, and I want you to graze them."
After Bu Shi became a Langguan, he still wore commoners and straw sandals to herd sheep.
After more than a year, the sheep became fat and multiplied.
The emperor passed by the sheep herding field and praised him very much.
Bu Shi said: Not only shepherding sheep, but also governing the people.
Live on time, get rid of the bad ones immediately, and don't let them harm others.
The emperor was surprised by his words and wanted him to try to govern the people.
Renbu Shi was appointed as the Feng family order, and the Feng family was in great control; he was moved to the Gao order to be in charge of water transportation, and he was the best in the assessment.
The emperor was honest and honest in his divination style, and he became the Tutor of the King of Qi, and then became the Prime Minister.
When Lu Jia rebelled, Bu Shi wrote: I heard that the Lord was ashamed and I died.
The ministers should be loyal to each other, and the most stupid ones should contribute money to help the army. This is the guarantee that powerful countries will not dare to invade.
I am willing to invite my son and the people who practice crossbows in Lin Miao and those who practice boats in Bochang to fight and die in battle to fulfill my integrity.
The emperor thought he was virtuous, so he went to Shao and said: I have heard that repaying kindness with kindness and repaying evil with straightness.
There are many misfortunes in the world today, and the princes in the counties and counties have no upright people who can rise up and repay grievances directly.
Prime Minister Qi behaved elegantly and uprightly, plowing the land himself, grazing with the animals, helping his younger brother with his assets, and starting the business from scratch, without any profit or confusion.
Not long ago, troops were mobilized on the northern border to attack the Xiongnu, and Bu Shi wrote a letter to provide money to help the officials.
In previous years, there was a famine in Xihe, and Bu Shi led his people to send grain to Xihe.
Now he took the initiative to sign up to join the army. Although he did not fight, it can be said that righteousness is seen in his heart.
I should give Divination to the Marquis of Guannei, forty kilograms of gold and ten hectares of fields, and inform the world so that my intentions will be known.
During the Yuanding period, Bu Shidai Genqing was recruited as the imperial censor.
After Bu Shi took office, he said that the prefecture was inconvenient to use salt and iron but the ships had a tax, which could be abolished.
The emperor therefore disliked Bu Shi.
In the second year, it was time for him to be enfeoffed, but Bu Shi was not good at writing and etiquette, so he was demoted to the crown prince and tutor, and replaced Bu Shi with Ai.
The above will end with longevity.
The child is wide, and the people can ride on thousands.
summary: Bu Shi, a farmer and herder from Henan, donated half his wealth to support border campaigns against the Xiongnu, but Gongsun Hong advised against accepting, calling it irregular. Later, during a famine, Bu Shi gave 200,000 yuan to aid refugees, earning imperial recognition. He was appointed as a langzhong to herd sheep in Shanglin Garden, where he excelled. The emperor, impressed, made him a magistrate, then tutor to the King of Qi, and eventually prime minister. During the Lu Jia rebellion, Bu Shi offered to fight, but the emperor honored him instead. As imperial censor, he criticized salt and iron taxes, displeasing the emperor, and was demoted.

translation:
He studied "Shangshu" and studied under Yu Fouwusheng.
As a doctor selected by the county and the country, he studied in Kongshili.
Because he was poor and had no resources, he was supported by his disciples.
He often rented fields and plowed them, brought scriptures with him to work, and recited them during his breaks. His reading was so profound.
Use Ce Wen as anecdotes, and use merits to make up for the history of Tingwei's literary career.
Kuan is a gentle man, honest and wise, capable of self-defense, good at writing, weak in martial arts, and unable to express himself verbally.
At that time, he was appointed as a Tingwei, and the Tingwei government was full of officials of literature, history and law, but Zhe was among them as a Confucian scholar. He showed that he was not familiar with affairs and could not be a low-level official. He was appointed as a Congshi and went to Jidian to guard livestock for several years.
Returning to the mansion, he submitted the livestock register. When the imperial officer encountered a problem, the memorial had been returned many times, and the officials did not know what to do.
Ni Kuan explained to him how to write it, and the officials asked Ni Kuan to write the memorial.
After the performance was completed, everyone who read it was convinced and told the official Zhang Tang.
Zhang Tang was shocked and called Ni Kuan to talk. He appreciated his talent and appointed him as his assistant.
Submit the memorial written by Ni Kuan and get immediate permission.
The next day, Zhang Tang met with the emperor.
Asked: The last memorial was beyond the reach of ordinary officials. Who wrote it?
Zhang Tang said it was Ni Kuan.
The emperor said: I have heard of him a long time ago.
Zhang Tang yearned for learning from then on, and appointed Ni Kuan as an official to report cases. He used the meaning of ancient law to judge difficult cases, which was very popular.
When he went to Zhangtang, he was appointed as the official censor, Ni Kuan was appointed as a subordinate official, and he was promoted to serve as the censor.
Meet the emperor and talk about Confucian classics. The emperor was delighted and asked about another article in "Shang Shu".
He was promoted to Zhongdafu and moved to Zuo Neishi.
After being leniently appointed to the post of civil administration, he encouraged farming, reduced sentences and punishments, and managed prison litigation. He was courteous to his subordinates and devoted himself to winning the hearts of the people. He chose benevolent people, treated his subordinates favorably, and did not seek reputation. The officials and the people were extremely trustworthy and loved.
Ni Kuanbiao opened six auxiliary canals and issued water control regulations to expand irrigated fields.
Rent taxes are collected according to seasonal harvests and are not collected urgently. They are borrowed from the people, so excessive rents are not put into the treasury.
Later, when military service was called for, Zuo Neishi ranked last due to rent debt and was dismissed from office.
When the people heard that he was about to be dismissed from office, they were afraid of losing Ni Kuan. Everyone drove the oxcart and the small family was responsible for the burden. Rent losses continued one after another, and rent and taxes topped the list.
The emperor was even more amazed at Ni Kuan's talent.
When discussing the matter of imitating ancient hunting patrols and fengdang, there were more than fifty scholars who opposed it, but they could not make up their minds.
summary: Ni Kuan, a scholar of "Shangshu," worked as a farmer while studying. He became a Tingwei official, known for his writing and legal expertise. Promoted by Zhang Tang, he served as Zuo Neishi, where he encouraged farming, reduced punishments, and built irrigation canals. When dismissed for poor tax collection, the people paid their debts, restoring his position. He advised on the Fengshan ceremonies, supporting the emperor’s plans, and helped establish the Taichu calendar. As imperial censor, he became complacent and died in office after nine years.

translation:
When there was a vacancy for the imperial censor, Chu Da came to take up the post. Chu Da thought he was qualified to be the censor.
When he arrived in Luoyang, he heard that Ni Kuan had taken office, and Chu laughed.
When he arrived at the court and discussed with Ni Kuan in front of the emperor, Chu was not as good as Ni Kuan, so he stood back and said in admiration: Your Majesty really knows people.
Ni Kuan was the imperial censor. Because he was satisfied with his position, he did not give any advice to the emperor for a long time, and his officials despised him.
He reigned for nine years and died in office.
Zan said: Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi and Ni Kuan all used Hongjian's wings to be trapped in the sparrows, traveling far between sheep and pigs. How could they have reached this point without luck?
At that time, the Han Dynasty had been prosperous for more than sixty years. The country was stable and the treasury was abundant. However, the four sides were not convinced and there were many systems lacking.
The emperor had just started a great civil and military undertaking, but he could not find the talents he asked for, so he started to use a pulsar cart to welcome Mei Cheng, and sighed when he saw his master's father dying.
The people were envious and yearned for it, and strange people and talents appeared at the same time.
Bu Shiba was promoted from herding, Hongyang was promoted from the Jia people, Wei Qing was promoted from the slaves, and Jin Yuechan was promoted from the captives. These are the ancient version of building and selling cattle.
Mozhi has its talents flourished here, Confucianism and elegance include Gongsun Hong, Dong Zhongshu, and Ni Kuan, loyalty includes Shi Jian and Shi Qing, simplicity includes Ji An and Bu Shi, recommending sages include Han Anguo and Zheng Shi, enacting laws and regulations include Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang, writing articles include Sima Qian and Sima Xiangru, and humor includes Dongfang Shuo and Meigao, Yan Zhu and Zhu Maichen responded to the emperor's questions, Tang Du and Luoxia Hong were listed, Li Yannian coordinated music, Sang Hongyang was responsible for financial planning, Zhang Qian and Su Wu were sent as envoys, Wei Qing and Huo Qubing were leaders, Huo Guang and Jin Yueyan were sent to protect the young master, and the rest are indescribable.
Therefore, he made great achievements and established the system, which was not as good as that of later generations.
Xiao Xuan inherited the great unification, continued to build the magnificent imperial cause, taught the six arts, and recruited outstanding talents. Xiao Wangzhi, Liang Qiuhe, Xia Housheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi were promoted through Confucianism. Liu Xiang and Wang Bao became famous with their articles, and their generals and ministers were well-prepared. An Shi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bingji, Yu Dingguo, Du Yannian, and others who governed the people included Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Zhao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Zhao Guangmo, Yan Yannian, and Zhang Chang, all of whom have made great achievements in the world.
Examining his famous ministers, he was second only to the talents of Emperor Wu's era.
summary: The text concludes that Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi, and Ni Kwan rose from humble origins due to the Han dynasty’s prosperity under Emperor Wu, who recruited diverse talents. This era saw a flourishing of Confucians, loyalists, legalists, writers, and generals, achieving great deeds. Later, under Emperor Xuan, similar talents emerged, but none matched the brilliance of Emperor Wu’s reign.

translation:
Feng Fengshi, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Lu County, Shangdang County, and later moved to Duling.
His ancestor Feng Ting was the governor of Shangdang County in South Korea.
Qin attacked Shangdang and blocked the passage in the Taihang Mountains. South Korea could not defend it, so Feng Ting dedicated Shangdang City to Zhao and defended it.
The State of Zhao granted Feng Ting the title of Lord of Huayang, and together with General Zhao Kuo of the State of Zhao, he resisted the State of Qin and died in battle in Changping.
Since then, the Feng family has dispersed in various places, some staying in Lu County and some traveling to other places.
Those in Zhao became official generals, and the sons of official generals became prime ministers of the country.
After Qin destroyed the six kingdoms, Feng Ting's descendants Feng Wuze, Feng Quji, and Feng Jie all became Qin's generals.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, Feng Tang was very famous during the reign of Emperor Wen. He was the son of the Prime Minister of Dai.
By the end of Emperor Wu's reign, Feng Fengshi was elected as a Langguan because he was a son of a good family.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao, he was appointed as the Chang Palace of Wu'an County in accordance with the size and order of his achievements.
When he was dismissed from office, he was already in his thirties. He only studied "Spring and Autumn", studied its subtle meanings, read the art of war, and knew its contents and examples. Former general Han Zeng reported to him and appointed him as the military commander.
During this period, he accompanied the army to attack the Xiongnu.
After the war, he became a Langguan again.
Prior to this, the Han Dynasty sent envoys to the Western Regions several times, but most of them failed to fulfill their mission, some were corrupt, and some were made difficult and insulted by foreign countries.
At this time, the Wusun Kingdom was very powerful and had the merit of attacking the Xiongnu. At the same time, the countries in the Western Regions had just reconciled with the Han Dynasty. The Han Dynasty was preparing to treat them well. If they wanted to take the opportunity to appease these countries, they selected people who could be sent as envoys to foreign countries.
Former general Han Zeng recommended Feng Fengshi to escort guests from Dawan and other countries back home as an envoy.
When they arrived at Yixiu City, Captain Song said that the Shache people, together with some other countries, had attacked and killed King Wannian of Shache appointed by the Han Dynasty, and also killed Xi Chongguo, the envoy of the Han Dynasty.
At this time, the Xiongnu sent troops to attack Cheshi City again, but they went back because they failed to capture it.
The Shache Kingdom sent envoys to threaten that the Northern Kingdoms had belonged to the Xiongnu. At that time, they attacked and plundered the Southern Kingdoms, and made a blood alliance with them to betray the Han Dynasty, cutting off all traffic from the Shanshan Kingdom to the west.
The Protector Zheng Ji and the Colonel Sima Yi were both trapped among the countries on the North Road.
Feng Fengshi discussed with his deputy Yan Lu and believed that if they did not attack quickly, the Shache Kingdom would become increasingly powerful, making the situation difficult to control and jeopardizing the entire Western Region.
So he notified the kings by envoys and mobilized their armies. A total of 15,000 people from the north and south attacked the Shache Kingdom and captured its city.
King Shache committed suicide and his head was sent to Chang'an.
All the countries were pacified, and Feng Fengshi's reputation shocked the Western Regions.
Feng Fengshi withdrew his troops and returned home, reporting the situation to the court.
Emperor Xuan summoned Han Zeng and said: Congratulations to the general on the competent person he recommended.
Feng Fengshi traveled west to the Kingdom of Dayuan.
The Kingdom of Dawan heard that he had killed King Shache and respected him more than other envoys.
After getting the famous horse Xianglong from Dayuan, he returned to Chang'an.
The emperor was very happy and issued an order to discuss the matter of rewarding Feng Fengshi.
summary: Feng Fengshi, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Lu County in Shangdang, later moving to Duling. His ancestor Feng Ting, governor of Shangdang under South Korea, surrendered the city to Zhao during Qin's invasion and died at Changping. The Feng family dispersed; some became officials in Zhao, and after Qin's unification, descendants like Feng Wuze served as Qin generals. Under Han, Feng Tang gained fame under Emperor Wen. Feng Fengshi was elected as a Langguan under Emperor Wu, later serving as a military commander under General Han Zeng, accompanying campaigns against the Xiongnu. During Emperor Xuan's reign, Feng Fengshi was sent as an envoy to the Western Regions. At Yixiu City, he learned that the Shache Kingdom had killed Han-appointed King Wannian and envoy Xi Chongguo, while the Xiongnu attacked Cheshi. Shache threatened the southern kingdoms, cutting off traffic from Shanshan westward. Protector Zheng Ji and Colonel Sima Yi were trapped. Feng Fengshi, with deputy Yan Lu, mobilized 15,000 troops from northern and southern kingdoms, attacked Shache, and captured its city. King Shache committed suicide, and his head was sent to Chang'an. Feng Fengshi's reputation spread across the Western Regions. After returning, Emperor Xuan praised Han Zeng for his recommendation. Feng Fengshi later obtained a famous horse from Dayuan. The court debated rewards: the prime minister and generals favored a title, but Shaofu Xiao Wangzhi argued against it, citing the precedent of unauthorized military action. The emperor agreed, granting Feng Fengshi the titles of Doctor Guanglu and Captain Shuiheng.

translation:
The Qiang thieves were defeated and thousands of their heads were beheaded, while the rest fled across the border.
When the outcome of the war was still undecided, the Han Dynasty recruited another 10,000 soldiers and appointed Han Anguo, the prefect of Dingxiang, as General Jianwei.
Before setting off, I heard that the Qiang rebels had been defeated. The emperor said: The Qiang rebels were defeated and punished, and fled from the border. Those soldiers who had a truce should leave more field guards to defend key points.
In February of the next year, Feng Fengshi returned to the capital and was appointed General Zuo, while Guang Luxun's position remained unchanged.
After recording his meritorious service and conferring a title, the emperor issued an edict saying: The Qiang thieves were cruel and cunning, killing officials and common people, attacking Longxi County government offices, burning post houses, and cutting off roads and bridges, which greatly violated the law of heaven.
The general of the left, Guang Luxun and Feng Fengshi, led an army to conquer the area, beheading more than 8,000 prisoners and seizing tens of thousands of cattle, horses and sheep.
Feng Fengshi was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, a settlement of 500 households, and 60 kilograms of gold.
More than thirty generals and lieutenants were rewarded.
More than a year later, Feng Fengshi died of illness.
He served as a military general for ten years. He was a veteran general who killed enemies and defended the country, and his reputation was second only to Tong Chongguo.
General Fenwu was appointed Qianqiu, and his father was appointed to the palace. During Emperor Zhao's reign, he used the prime minister's campaign to capture and kill the rebellious left general Shangguan Jie, and granted him the title of Marquis. Emperor Xuan was appointed Taichang and died.
Qianqiu inherited the title and was appointed Taichang.
When he became emperor, Wang Shang, the Marquis of Lechang, replaced Feng Fengshi as the left general, while Ren Qianqiu was appointed the right general, and later the left general.
Descendants inherited the title from generation to generation until the era of Wang Mang.
Two years after Feng Fengshi's death, Gan Yanshou, the governor of the Western Regions, was named a prince because he killed the Zhizhi Chanyu.
At that time, Prime Minister Kuang Heng also used Gan Yanshou's counterfeit edicts to cause trouble as an excuse. Based on Xiao Wangzhi's case, he believed that Gan Yanshou should not be made a marquis. However, the commentators all praised Gan Yanshou's achievements, and the emperor followed everyone's opinions and made him a marquis.
At that time, Du Qin went to Shangshu and praised Feng Fengshi's previous contributions: In the past, King Yarkand killed the envoys of the Han Dynasty and formed an alliance with other countries to betray the Han Dynasty.
General Feng Fengshi of the left, as a guard, sent troops to annihilate the King of Shache according to convenient conditions, used strategies to stabilize the city, and made great contributions to the border areas.
Commentators believed that Feng Fengshi had his mission as an envoy. According to the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, ministers cannot act arbitrarily. According to the laws of the Han Dynasty, it was a crime of restraint, so he could not be granted a title.
Now the Xiongnu Zhizhi Chanyu killed the envoys of the Han Dynasty and fled to the state of Kangju. The governor Gan Yanshou sent more than 40,000 soldiers from the city and soldiers in the field to kill him and made him a prince.
In my humble opinion, in terms of crime, Zhi Zhi Shan is lighter than Zhi Zhi; in terms of military strength, Yash Che is more than Zhi Zhi; in terms of the use of troops, Feng Fengshi is less; in terms of the degree of victory, Feng Fengshi has contributed to the peace of the border; in terms of failure, it is the disaster that Yanshou has brought to the country.
They had the same crime of disobeying orders and causing trouble. However, Yanshou ceded lands and made lords, but Feng Fengshi did not remember the rewards.
summary: Under Emperor Yuan, Feng Fengshi became Jinwu and later Right General of the Dian Kingdom. In the second year of Yongguang, the Qiang rebelled in Longxi. Amid famine, Feng Fengshi volunteered to lead an army, proposing 40,000 troops for a swift campaign. The prime minister and others advocated for only 10,000, but Feng Fengshi warned that insufficient forces would embolden the Qiang and other tribes. He was granted 12,000 troops initially, later reinforced to 60,000 under General Fenwu Ren Qianqiu. After initial defeats, the combined forces defeated the Qiang in November, beheading thousands and driving the rest across the border. Feng Fengshi was appointed General Zuo and Marquis of Guannei with 500 households and gold. He died of illness over a year later, having served as a military general for ten years, with a reputation second only to Tong Chongguo. After Feng Fengshi's death, Gan Yanshou was made a marquis for killing the Zhizhi Chanyu. Du Qin later petitioned, arguing that Feng Fengshi's similar merits had been overlooked due to Xiao Wangzhi's precedent, creating inconsistency in rewards. The emperor declined to revisit the matter.

translation:
I heard that if the merits are the same and the rewards are different, the ministers who have worked hard will have doubts; if the crime is the same but the punishment is different, the people will be confused; doubts will lead to uncertainty, and confusion will lead to not knowing what to do; uncertainty will lead to unclear systems and directions, and not knowing what to follow will lead to the people not knowing how to act.
Feng Fengshi relieved the danger, risked his life in the battle, completed the mission with extraordinary achievements, and achieved a remarkable reputation. He was a model for generations of envoys, but he was suppressed and did not praise him. This is not the meaning of a sage monarch who eliminates doubts and encourages integrity.
I hope it will be handed over to the relevant departments for discussion.
The emperor believed that this was a matter of the late emperor's time, so he no longer accepted his opinion.
Feng Fengshi had nine sons and four daughters.
The eldest daughter Feng Yuan was elected to the palace as Emperor Yuan Zhaoyi and gave birth to Prince Xiao of Zhongshan.
After the death of Emperor Yuan, Feng Yuan became the Queen Mother of Zhongshan and followed King Xiao of Zhongshan to the feudal state.
Feng Fengshi's eldest son, Feng Tan, was recommended by Taichang as Xiaolian to be a Langguan, and he was appointed Tianshui Sima in order of merit.
Feng Fengshi attacked Xiqiang. Feng Tan was a captain. He served in the army with his father and died of illness before he was promoted to an official.
Feng Tan's younger brothers Feng Yewang, Feng Kui, Feng Li, and Feng Shen all became high officials.
Feng Yewang, nicknamed Junqing, studied with a doctor and was proficient in the Book of Songs.
When he was young, he was appointed as the crown prince's concubine because his father was an official.
When he was eighteen years old, he wrote to the emperor hoping to be tried as the magistrate of Chang'an County.
Emperor Xuan was surprised by his ambition and asked Prime Minister Wei Xiang, who thought it was unacceptable.
Later, he was appointed Dangyang County Magistrate in order of merit, promoted to Liyang County Magistrate, and transferred to Xiayang County Magistrate.
During the reign of Emperor Yuan, he was promoted to the prefect of Longxi County. Because of his outstanding political achievements, he entered the court and served as Zuo Fengyi.
For more than a year, the magistrate of Chiyang County, who was not known to be corrupt, despised King Feng Ye as a young relative, and did not correct his misdeeds in governance.
King Feng Ye deployed the postal supervisor Zhao Du from Touxu County to file a case for investigation and found out that the person in power was responsible for stealing ten gold coins from himself and arrested him.
When he refused to obey the arrest, Zhao Duge killed him.
Bing's family wrote a letter stating their grievances, and the matter was handed over to Tingwei.
Zhao Du committed suicide in front of the officials to prove that he had nothing to do with King Feng Ye. People in the capital praised his prestige and promoted him to Dahonglu.
A few years later, the imperial censor Li Yanshou died of illness, and many officials recommended King Feng Ye to succeed him.
The emperor sent the minister to select two thousand-level officials, and King Feng Ye ranked first in terms of character and ability.
The emperor said: If I use King Feng Ye as the three princes, future generations will definitely use this as an example to say that I prefer concubines in the harem.
Then Xia Shao said: The man who is strong and resolute, and truly has no selfish desires, is the king of Da Honglu and Feng Ye.
He can speak eloquently and can be sent to various places, such as Shaofu Wulu Chongzong.
summary: Feng Fengshi had nine sons and four daughters. His eldest daughter Feng Yuan became Emperor Yuan's Zhaoyi and mother of Prince Xiao of Zhongshan. His sons—Feng Tan, Feng Yewang, Feng Kui, Feng Li, and Feng Shen—all held high offices. Feng Yewang, known for his character, was recommended for high posts but was passed over due to his sister's imperial favor, leading him to lament that their family was humbled by her status. He later served as prefect of several commanderies but was dismissed after being implicated in a political dispute. Feng Kui was known for his governance and died in his forties. Feng Li served as prefect of five commanderies, praised for his fairness. Feng Shen, cautious and dignified, was made Marquis of Yixiang but committed suicide under Emperor Ai after being framed for treason, along with seventeen family members. The Feng family then returned to their hometown. The historical commentary laments their tragic fate, comparing it to ancient figures like Boqi and Qu Yuan.

translation:
The ancestor of the Xiongnu was a descendant of the Xiahou family, named Chunwei.
Before Yao, Yu and Shun of the Tang Dynasty, there were Shanrong, Yanyun, Xunzhou and other branches. They lived in the northern border of China and moved along with water, grass and livestock husbandry.
Most of the livestock raised are horses, cattle, and sheep. The exotic livestock include camels, donkeys, mules, Yaosao, colts, and Yixi.
They migrated in pursuit of water and grass. They did not have cities or agriculture for permanent residence, but they also had separate grazing lands.
There are no written books, only words are used for restraint and management.
When the men were young, they could ride sheep, draw bows and shoot mice, and learn archery. When they grew up, they could shoot foxes and rabbits, and mostly ate meat.
Men in their prime are strong and can bend bows and shoot arrows, so they serve as armored cavalry.
The living customs of the Huns were that when there was no war, they would graze and hunt birds and animals as a way of making a living; in case of emergency war, people would practice battle formations to attack and plunder others. This was the nature of the Huns.
Their long weapons are bows and arrows, and their short weapons are swords and spears.
When fighting, attack if things go well, retreat if things go wrong, and don't be ashamed to run away.
If there is a profit, then etiquette and justice will be ignored.
The Huns, from the king on down, all eat animal meat, wear animal hides, and wear felt fur.
Strong young people eat rich food, and old people eat leftovers.
Those who are strong are valued and those who are old and weak are looked down upon.
When his father died, his son took his stepmother as his wife; when his brothers died, the surviving ones took their wives as wives.
The custom in terms of names is to have names, no taboos, and no epithet.
The Xia Dynasty declined, and Gong Liu, the ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty, lost his position as a farmer, so he reformed and changed the customs of Xirong and established a capital in Bin.
More than three hundred years later, Rong Di attacked Yifu, King Tai of Zhou, and Yifu fled to the foot of Qishan Mountain. The Bin people followed Yifu to build houses and settle down under Qishan Mountain, and began to establish the Zhou Kingdom.
More than a hundred years later, King Wen of Zhou Dynasty Xi Bo Jichang attacked Yi.
More than ten years later, King Wu of Zhou attacked and destroyed him, and then built Luoyi. King Wu returned to Fengjing and Haojing to live, and exiled the Rong and Yi to the north of Jinghe and Luohe, requiring them to contribute gifts on time, and called them "Huangfu".
After more than two hundred years, the Zhou Dynasty declined, and King Zhou Duo went to attack Zuo Xi and returned with four white wolves and four white deer.
From then on, people from Huangfu no longer paid tribute to the Zhou Dynasty.
The Zhou Dynasty formulated the law of "Lu Xing" at that time.
By the time of King Zhou Yi, the grandson of King Mu of Zhou, the royal family of Zhou declined, and Rong and Di repeatedly attacked and ravaged various countries in the Central Plains.
The people of the Central Plains were deeply affected, and poets began to sing poems that hated them: No house, no home, this is all because of Yan Yun; When will I not be on guard? Yan Yun's attack was really urgent.
summary: The Xiongnu, whose ancestor Chunwei was a descendant of the Xia dynasty, were a nomadic people living in the northern border of China. They raised horses, cattle, sheep, and exotic livestock, migrating with water and grass without permanent cities or agriculture. They had no written language, relying on oral agreements. Men learned archery from youth, and in adulthood served as armored cavalry. Their customs prioritized the strong, who ate well while the elderly ate leftovers. Upon a father's death, a son married his stepmother; upon a brother's death, the surviving brother married the widow. They had no naming taboos or posthumous titles.

translation:
When King Xuan, the great-grandson of King Yi, sent a general to lead an army to attack Yan Yun, the poet praised: The expedition against Yan Yun reached Taiyuan; the chariots were dispatched to build a city in the north.
At that time, the surrounding ethnic minorities all surrendered to the Zhou Dynasty, which was known as Zhongxing.
When King You of Zhou Dynasty arrived, he had a conflict with Queen Shen's father, Shen Hou, because he doted on his beautiful concubine Gui Si.
The Marquis of Shen was very angry and joined forces with Quan Rong to attack King You, killed him under Mount Li, occupied the land of the Zhou Dynasty, plundered and lived between the Jingwei River, and invaded and ravaged the people of the Central Plains.
Qin Xianggong sent troops to rescue the Dan Dynasty, so King Qiewen left; Yan and Guzhi moved eastward to the capital of Tao Dan.
At that time, Tong Saigong attacked Zuosheng and went all the way to Guishan. At this time, Tong Cai began to be named a prince.
Sixty-five years later, the Shanrong crossed Zangli again to attack Bianli. Duke Manli led his army to fight the Shanrong at the border of Bianxi. Forty-four years later, Shanrong attacked Yan again.
Yan State asked Qi State for help. Duke Huan of Qi led his army to attack Shanrong in the north, but Shanrong fled.
More than twenty years later, Rong Zhai went to Luoyi and attacked King Xiang of Zhou Dynasty. King Xiang fled to Panyi in Zheng State.
At first, King Xiang of Zhou wanted to attack the State of Zheng, so he married Rong Zhai's daughter as his queen and joined forces with Rong Zhai to attack the State of Zheng.
Soon after, Empress Zhai was deposed, and Empress Zhai was very resentful. King Xiang's stepmother was named Empress Hui, and she had a son named Zidai. Queen Hui wanted to make Zidai king. So Empress Hui, together with Empress Zhai and Ziying, responded internally and opened the city gate to welcome Rong Zhai. Rong Zhai therefore attacked the city, defeated and drove away King Xiang, and established Zidai as King of Zhou.
At that time, some Rong Zhai were already living in Luhun, and Shu Bian arrived in Wei State, and the invasion became even more severe.
King Xiang of Zhou had been wandering for four years, so he sent an envoy to Jin to ask for help.
Duke Wen of Jin had just ascended the throne and wanted to establish hegemony, so he sent troops to attack Rong Zhai, killed Zidai, and welcomed King Zhou Xiang back to Luoyi.
At this time, Qin and Jin were very powerful.
Duke Wen of Jin attacked and expelled Rong Di. Rong Di lived between the Huan River and Luo River in the Xihe River, and they were called Chidi and Baidi.
Duke Mu of Qin got Yu Yu, and the eight kingdoms of Xirong surrendered to Qin.
Therefore, there are Rong tribes such as Mianzhu, Dengrong and Diyuan living in Longxi. To the north of Qishan, Liangshan, Jinghe and Qihe there are Rong tribes such as Yiqu, Dali, Wushi and Quyan. To the north of Jin there are Rong tribes such as Linhu and Loufan. To the north of Yan there are Donghu and Shanrong.
They live scattered in the valley, each with its own leader. There are more than a hundred Rong tribes living together, but they cannot be unified.
More than a hundred years later, the Duke of Jin sent Wei Jiang to negotiate peace with Rong Di, and Rong Di began to pay homage to the king of Jin.
More than a hundred years later, Tsai Xiangzi led his troops across Juzhu Mountain, conquered and annexed the state of Dai, and approached Hu Xian.
Later, Zhao Xiangzi, together with the Han and Wei families, destroyed Zhi, and the three families occupied the land of Jin. In this way, Zhao State occupied Daidi and the area north of Juzhu Mountain, while Wei State occupied Xihe and Shangjun, adjacent to the Rong people.
Later, the Rong people in Yiqu built cities for self-defense, while the Qin State slowly encroached on the land of Yiqu. When King Hui arrived, he captured twenty-five cities in Yiqu.
King Hui of Qin attacked the State of Wei, and the State of Wei dedicated all the areas of Xihe and Shangjun to the State of Qin.
During the reign of King Zhao of Qin, King Yiqurong had an affair with Queen Mother Xuan and gave birth to two sons. Queen Mother Xuan deceived King Yiqurong and killed him in Ganquan, and then raised troops to attack and eliminate Yiqu.
Therefore, the Qin State occupied Longxi, Beidi, and Shangjun, and built the Great Wall to resist the Hu people.
King Wuling of Zhao also mutated the customs of his own country, wore the clothes of the barbarians, learned horseback riding and archery, and attacked Linhu and Loufan to the north. From Daidi along the foothills of Yinshan Mountain to Gaoque, he used it as his frontier fortress. And established Yunzhong County, Yanmen County and Dai County.
summary: The text traces the history of interactions between the Xiongnu and various Chinese dynasties, beginning with the Zhou dynasty. The Zhou declined, and Rong and Di tribes frequently attacked. King Xuan of Zhou attacked the Xiongnu, but later King You was killed by Quan Rong. Qin and Jin became powerful, with Duke Mu of Qin conquering Xirong and Duke Wen of Jin expelling Rong Di. During the Warring States period, Qin, Zhao, and Yan built walls to resist the Xiongnu. Qin Shihuang sent Meng Tian to attack the Xiongnu, recovering land south of the Yellow River and building the Great Wall. After Meng Tian's death, the Xiongnu regained strength under Chanyu Touman.

translation:
King Shuhu became more arrogant and invaded westward.
There is an uninhabited wasteland between the Xiongnu and Donghu, which is more than a thousand miles away. The Xiongnu and Donghu each live on one side and set up observation posts.
Shuhu sent an envoy to Modu and said: The Huns cannot reach the deserted land guarded by the observation post on the border with us, and we want to occupy it.
Mao Dun asked the ministers, and some ministers said: "This is abandoned land, give it to them."
After hearing this, Mo Dun was furious and said: Land is the foundation of the country, how can you give it to others!
Those who said they could give land to Shuhu were killed.
Maodun mounted his horse and ordered his countrymen to kill anyone who retreated, so he went east to attack Donghu.
At first Shu Hu looked down upon Mao Dun and took no precautions.
When Mao Dun arrived with his troops, he completely defeated and eliminated King Donghu, captured the people of Ding Donghu, and plundered their livestock and products.
After returning, he sent troops to the west to drive away the Yuezhi, and to the south he annexed Loufan and the Aries King of Henan. He also completely recovered the Xiongnu territory that Qin sent Meng Tian to invade. Using the original Henan fortress as the boundary with the Han Dynasty, he reached Chaona and Fushi, and then invaded Yan and Dai.
At that time, Liu Han was fighting Xiang Yu, and the Central Plains was exhausted by the war, so Maodun was able to become strong and strong, with more than 300,000 warriors who could bend bows, ride and shoot.
It was more than a thousand years from Chunwei to Touman. Sometimes the Xiongnu were large, sometimes small, and their residences were scattered and separated. They were so long ago that their lineage inheritance cannot be arranged one by one in order.
However, when Maodun became the Chanyu, when the Huns were at their most powerful, all the ethnic minorities in the north were subject to his rule and became enemies of the Chinese ethnic groups in the south. It was only then that its lineage, surnames and official titles could be recorded.
The Chanyu's surname was Lyuta, and their people called the king "Pengli Gutu Chanyu".
The Huns called the sky "Plough Holder" and the son "Gu Tu". The name "Chanyu" means vast. This name means that the Chanyu is as big as the sky.
The Xiongnu had left and right Xian kings, left and right Guli kings, left and right generals, left and right captains, left and right Danghu, and left and right Guduhous.
The Huns called the wise "Tu Qi", so the prince often served as the Zuo Tu Qi King.
From King Youyouxian down to Danghu, the older ones led more than ten thousand cavalry, while the younger ones led thousands of cavalry. There were twenty-four leaders in total, and they were given the title of Ten Thousand Cavalrymen.
Their ministers all have hereditary official positions.
The Huyan family, the Lan family, and later the Xubu family, these three surnames were the noble families of the Xiongnu.
Those left kings and left generals all live in the east, facing the area bounded by Shanggu and Shu, which connects Hui Raccoon and North Korea; those of right kings and right generals live in the west, facing west of Shangjun, bordering the Di and Qiang; and the royal court of the Shanyu faces Daijun and Yunzhong areas.
They each have their own area and move with the quality of the water and grass.
The left and right Xianwang and the left and right Guli led the largest tribe, and the left and right Guduhou assisted in government affairs.
The twenty-four leaders also each have official positions such as Qianchang, Baichang, Shichang, Xiaowang, Xiang, Duwei, Duhu, and Qiequ.
In the first month of each year, the leaders of various tribes held a small gathering in the court of Chanyu and held a spring festival.
summary: Touman's son, Maodun, trained his cavalry with a signaling arrow, killing his father and establishing himself as Chanyu. Maodun defeated the Donghu, drove away the Yuezhi, and annexed Loufan and the Aries King of Henan, becoming powerful with over 300,000 warriors. The Xiongnu's official structure included left and right kings, generals, and governors, with the Chanyu's surname being Luanti. They held annual meetings, had strict laws, and practiced burial with concubines. Maodun later conquered northern countries, and the Han dynasty, under Emperor Gao, made peace through marriage alliances and tribute. The text concludes with the Xiongnu's continued decline, internal power struggles, and eventual submission to the Han. The Xiongnu Chanyu's lineage and official titles are recorded, highlighting their complex relationship with the Han dynasty, marked by periods of war, peace, and tribute.

translation:
Now that we have obtained Han territory, Shanyu you will not be able to live here after all.
Besides, the Lord of Han is blessed by the gods, so Shanyu, you should consider it carefully.
Mao Dun had made an appointment with Han Xin's generals Wang Huang and Cao Li, but the troops of Wang Huang and Bao Li were still late in arriving. Mao Dun suspected that they were conspiring with the King of Han, so he listened to Ban's words and opened a corner of the encirclement.
So Emperor Gao ordered the soldiers to draw their bows fully, nock their arrows, face outwards, and rush out from the corner of the siege. Finally they joined the army, and Mao Dun led his army to retreat.
The King of Han also retreated with his troops and sent Liu Jing to make peace with the Xiongnu.
After that, Han Xin became the general of the Xiongnu, and together with Zaili, Wang Huang and others, he repeatedly betrayed the Han-Hungarian peace treaty and invaded Daijun, Yanmenjun and Yunzhongjun.
Soon after, Chen Xi rebelled against the Han Dynasty and conspired with Han Xin to attack Dai County.
The Han Dynasty sent Fan Sha to lead his troops to attack them, and recovered Daijun, Yanmenjun, Yunzhongjun and other counties without leaving the frontier to fight.
At that time, the Xiongnu generals of the Han Dynasty led their troops to surrender many times, so Maodun often came and went to invade Dai.
Emperor Gaozu was deeply worried, so he sent Liu Jing to send the royal daughter to the Que family who pretended to be a princess and sent a certain amount of silk floss, silk silk, wine and food to the Xiongnu every year.
Later, King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled against the Han Dynasty and led nearly 10,000 of his associates to surrender to the Huns. They came and went to harass the people in the Shanggu Yisu area until the death of Emperor Gaozu.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Dowager Lu, Maodun gradually became arrogant and even wrote a letter and sent an envoy to Empress Lu, saying: I am a lonely and helpless monarch. I was born in a humid swamp and grew up in a vast place where cattle and horses are grazed. I have been to the border many times, hoping to visit the Central Plains.
Your Majesty, you are an independent king, but you are also lonely and helpless, living alone.
We two monarchs were very unhappy and had nothing to entertain us. I hope that both of us can exchange what we have for what we don’t have.
Empress Dowager Lu was very angry after reading the letter. She summoned the prime ministers Chen Ping, Fan Sha and Ji Bu to discuss killing the Xiongnu envoys and sending troops to attack the Xiongnu.
Fan Sha said: I am willing to lead an army of 100,000 people to attack the Xiongnu territory.
Empress Lu asked Ji Bu, and Ji Bu said, "You can kill Fan!"
In the past, when Chen Xi rebelled in Dai, there were 320,000 Han soldiers, and Fan Sha was the general. At that time, the Huns besieged Emperor Gao in Pingcheng, but Fan Sha could not break through the siege.
People all over the world sang: It’s too hard under a flat city!
After seven days without food, the soldiers could not even draw their bows. Now the sound of people singing is still in their ears, and the wounded people have just stood up. But Fan Sha wants to shake the world, and talks nonsense about bringing a hundred thousand soldiers to the Xiongnu to go on a rampage. This is deceiving the emperor in person.
summary: During the reign of Empress Dowager Lu, Maodun sent an insulting letter, but she responded diplomatically. Emperor Wen continued marriage alliances, though the Xiongnu frequently invaded. The Xiongnu Chanyu wrote to the Han, claiming to have conquered the Yuezhi and other states, and sought peace. The Han agreed, sending gifts. After Maodun's death, his son Laoshang Chanyu succeeded. A eunuch, Zhongxing, defected to the Xiongnu and taught them Chinese customs, advising against adopting Han ways. He argued that Xiongnu simplicity and mobility were strengths, while Han complexity led to internal strife.

translation:
After that, the Xiongnu fled far away, and Monan no longer had the royal court of Shan Yu.
The Han people crossed the Yellow River and went west from Shuofang to Lingju. They built canals and opened fields everywhere, and set up officials. There were fifty or sixty thousand officials and soldiers. They slowly encroached on the Xiongnu territory, and the land was connected to the north of the Xiongnu's old territory.
At the beginning, generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing of the Han Dynasty sent troops to besiege Shanyu, killing and capturing 89,000 Xiongnu people. Tens of thousands of Han soldiers died, and more than 100,000 Han army horses died.
Although the Xiongnu were exhausted and fled far away, the Han army lacked horses and could not pursue them.
Chanyu adopted the letter's suggestion and sent an envoy to say good things and ask for a marriage.
The emperor handed the matter over to the ministers for discussion. Some of the ministers said that they should make peace with the Huns, while others said that they should be made vassals.
Prime Minister Shi Renchang said: The Xiongnu were newly defeated and tired. They should be allowed to serve as foreign ministers and go to the frontier areas to pay homage to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty.
The Han Dynasty sent Ren Chang as an envoy to Shan Yu Nahuo. After Shan Yu heard about Ren Chang's idea, he became furious and detained Ren Chang and refused to let him go back.
Prior to this, the Han Dynasty also recruited and surrendered some Huns envoys, and the Chanyu always detained the Han Dynasty's envoys to compensate.
The Han Dynasty was mobilizing troops and horses, but Huo Qu, the general of the Hussars, died of illness. Therefore, the Han Dynasty did not attack the Xiongnu in the north for a long time.
A few years later, Yi Zhixie Chanyu died, having reigned for thirteen years. His son Uwe succeeded as Chanyu.
This year is the third year of Yuanding.
After Uwe Chanyu succeeded to the throne, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty began to inspect various counties and counties.
Later, the Han Dynasty went to conquer the two Vietnames in the south, but did not attack the Xiongnu, and the Xiongnu did not invade the border.
Three years after Uwe Shanyu succeeded to the throne, the Han Dynasty wiped out both Vietnams. He sent Sun He, the former Tai servant, to lead 15,000 cavalry out of Jiuyuan for more than 2,000 miles to Fujujing. He sent Piaohou Tangponu to lead more than 10,000 cavalry out to the Xiongnu River for several thousand miles to the Xiongnu River. Both armies came back without encountering a single Huns.
At this time, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty inspected the border and personally arrived at Shuofang City. He commanded 180,000 cavalry to show his military might. At the same time, he sent Guo Ji as an envoy to advise Shan Yu.
After arriving at the Xiongnu, the Xiongnu official in charge of receiving guests asked Guo Ji what his mission was. Guo Ji humbly said kindly and said: I want to tell Shan Yu in person when I see him in person.
Shanyu then met with Guo Ji, who said: The head of the King of Nanyue has been hung under the north gate of the Han Dynasty palace. If you, Shanyu, can go to fight the Han soldiers now, then the emperor of the Han Dynasty is waiting at the border with his troops; if you cannot go, you should face south and surrender to the Han Dynasty.
Why just run away to the north and hide in the cold and miserable place with no water and grass in the north of the desert?
After Guo Ji finished speaking, Shanyu was furious and immediately killed the concierge responsible for the reception. He detained Guo Ji and refused to let him go back. In order to humiliate Guo Ji, he exiled him to the North Sea.
summary: Under Emperor Wu, the Han attempted to ambush the Xiongnu at Mayi but failed, leading to open conflict. The Han sent multiple campaigns, with generals like Wei Qing and Huo Qubing achieving victories, killing tens of thousands of Xiongnu and capturing their kings. The Xiongnu suffered heavy losses and fled north. The Han also expanded into the Western Regions, isolating the Xiongnu from allies. Despite peace negotiations, the Xiongnu continued border raids. The Han detained Xiongnu envoys, and the Xiongnu retaliated.

translation:
At this time, there happened to be heavy snowfall, which was more than ten feet deep in one day. Many of the tribesmen and livestock froze to death, and less than one tenth of them came back alive.
So Ding Lingguo took advantage of the Xiongnu's weakness to attack it from the north, Wuhuan State attacked it from Shubian, and Wusun State attacked it from the west.
These three countries killed tens of thousands of Huns and robbed tens of thousands of horses, as well as many cattle and sheep.
In addition, many people died of starvation, three-tenths of the Xiongnu people died, and five-tenths of the livestock died. The Xiongnu country declined greatly. Those subordinate countries of the Xiongnu rebelled and left one after another, attacking and harassing each other, and no one was able to govern them.
Later, the Han Dynasty sent more than 3,000 cavalry, divided into three groups, to attack the Huns together, and captured and brought back thousands of people.
In the end, the Xiongnu did not dare to retaliate against the Han Dynasty to compensate for the losses, but wanted to make peace with the Han Dynasty even more, and the borders of the Han Dynasty became peaceful and less troublesome from then on.
Hu Yanqian Chanyu died in the seventeenth year of his reign, and his younger brother Zuoxian Wang succeeded him as Chanyu. This is Xulu Quanqu Chanyu.
This year is the second year of the Earth Festival.
After Xulu Quan Qu Chanyu succeeded to the throne, he established the right general's daughter as the Pi family and deposed the Zhuan Quque family who was favored by the late Chanyu.
Zhuan Quban's father, Zuo Daqiequ, was very resentful.
At that time, because the Xiongnu did not dare to invade the border again, the Han Dynasty abandoned the cities on the border fortress so that the people defending there could rest and recuperate.
When Shanyu heard about this, he was very happy and summoned the Xiongnu nobles to discuss the matter and wanted to make peace with the Han Dynasty.
Zuo Daqiequ was jealous of this, so he said to Shanyu: In the past, the Han Dynasty sent envoys, and the army followed closely and came to attack us.
Now we can also follow the example of the Han Dynasty in dispatching troops, and first send envoys to pay homage to the Emperor of Han. So he asked Shan Yu to allow himself and King Huluzi to lead 10,000 cavalry to the south to hunt along the Han Dynasty's border fortress. After meeting, they attacked the border fortress together.
Before reaching the border fortress, three Xiongnu cavalrymen happened to escape and surrendered to the Han Dynasty, saying that the Huns were coming to invade.
So the Emperor of the Han Dynasty issued an edict to station the cavalry on the frontier fortress in key places. He sent four people including the general, the general, and the supervisor to lead 5,000 cavalry. They were divided into three groups, and each went hundreds of miles away from the frontier fortress. Each captured dozens of Huns and returned.
At that time, the Huns escaped with three cavalrymen, so they did not dare to invade the border fortress and led their troops to retreat.
This year there was a famine in the Huns, and sixty-seven out of ten people and livestock died.
Xiongsu also sent two villages with 10,000 cavalry each to guard against the Han army's attack.
In the autumn of this year, thousands of people from the Ximo tribe who lived in the left area who had previously belonged to the Xiongnu, starting from their monarch, drove their livestock to escape from the Xiongnu. They fought with the Xiongnu in the Outuo area. Many people were killed and injured in the battle, so they surrendered to the south and surrendered to the Han Dynasty.
summary: Later, the Xiongnu faced internal strife and external attacks from Dingling, Wuhuan, and Wusun, leading to decline. The Han sent multiple expeditions, further weakening the Xiongnu. The Xiongnu Chanyu sought peace, but the Han demanded the prince as a hostage, which the Xiongnu refused. The Xiongnu continued to raid, but the Han's military campaigns and alliances with Wusun and other states devastated them. The Xiongnu suffered from famine, disease, and livestock losses, with many tribes rebelling or surrendering to the Han.

translation:
A few months after Huhanxie Shanyu returned to the royal court, he stopped the war and asked everyone to return to their original places. He summoned his brother Hutuwusi, who was a commoner, and appointed him King Zuoguli. He also sent people to inform the nobles of Youxian, asking them to kill King Youxian.
That winter, Dulongqi and King Youxian jointly supported the king Zhu Wanglian and set up the hall as Kenzhouliyu, and sent tens of thousands of troops to the east to attack Huhanxie Chanyu.
Huhanxie Chanyu's army was defeated and fled. Tuqi Chanyu returned to the court of the Xiongnu, and appointed his eldest son Dutuwuxi as the king of Zuoguli, and his youngest son Gujiloutou as the king of rightguli, leaving them in the court of the Shanyu.
In the autumn of the next year, Tuqi Chanyu appointed King Youaota, the elder brother of the Richu King Xianxian Shan, as the Wujie Captain, and asked them to lead 20,000 cavalry respectively and station them at Shubian to guard against Huhanxie Chanyu.
At this time, the king of Hujie from the west came to plan with Weili, and together they slandered the Shanyu of Tu Qi and slandered King Youxian, saying that he wanted to establish himself as a Uprising Chanyu.
So Tuqi Chanyu killed King Youxian and his son. Later, Tuqi Chanyu knew that King Youxian had been wronged, so he killed Weili in his own right.
