Therefore, King Hujie was very frightened, so he betrayed Tuqi Chanyu and ran away, and established himself as Hujie Chanyu.
When King Youao Tartar heard about it, he established himself as the chayu chanyu.
Wujiu Duwei also established himself as Wujii Chanyu.
In this way, the Xiongnu had five chanyus.
Tuqi Chanyu personally led his troops eastward to attack Cheli Chanyu, and sent Dulongqi to attack Wujii Chanyu.
Both Wujii Chanyu and Chesai Chanyu were defeated and fled to the northwest to join Hujie Chanyu's army, which totaled 40,000 people.
King Wujie and King Hujie both removed their titles of Chanyu and worked together to assist Chanyu Cheli.
When Tuqi Chanyu heard about it, he sent General Zuo and Duwei with 40,000 cavalry to station in the east to guard against Huhanxie Chanyu. King Xingzhouli himself led 40,000 cavalry to the west to attack Cheli Chanyu.
Cheli Chanyu was defeated and fled to the northwest. Tuqi Chanyu led his army to the southwest and garrisoned at Mengdun.
The next year, Huhanxie Chanyu sent his younger brother Yougu Li Wang and others to lead troops west to attack Tuqi Chanyu's army stationed in Hedun, killing and plundering more than 10,000 people.
When Tu Qi Chanyu heard about it, he personally led 60,000 cavalry to attack Huhanxie Chanyu. They had traveled nearly a thousand miles, but they hadn't arrived yet! In the cricket area, they encountered Huhanxie Chanyu's nearly 40,000 troops.
The two sides fought, and Tu Qi Shanyu was defeated and committed suicide.
Tsang Longtong escaped with Tu Qi Chanyu's youngest son, Youguli Wang Guzhong Loutou, and surrendered. Cheli Chanyu went east and surrendered to Huhanxie Shanren.
Hu Hanxie Shanyu's left-hand general Dan Quli and his father Hu Yingleigu Nie Wenzheng saw Bao Nui in such chaos, so they led tens of thousands of their troops to surrender to the south and surrendered to Forsythia.
He also sealed Wu Li Zhou as the new city marquis and Gu Li Wen Chi as the Zhan Wu Fort.
At this time, Kui Lu's son supported Zhou Jiedu as Chanyu. Huhanxie Chanyu sent people to hunt and kill them. So Huhanxie Chanyu returned to the court of the Xiongnu. However, there were only tens of thousands of people in his tribe.
King Xiu Xun, cousin of Tu Qi Chanyu, led his five or six hundred cavalry to attack and kill Zuo Daqiequ, annexed his army, arrived at Youdi, and established himself as Runzhen Chanyu, living in the west of the Xiongnu.
Later, Huhanxie Chanyu's brother Zuoxian King Hutuwusi also established himself as Chanyu, the Marquis of Zhizhigu, and lived in Baosusubu.
Two years later, Runzhen Chanyu led his troops to attack Zhizhi Chanyu eastward.
Zhizhi Chanyu faced off against Runzhen Chanyu, killed him, annexed his troops, and then attacked Huhanxie Chanyu. The army was defeated, and Zhizhi Chanyu made his capital in the royal court.
When Huhanxie was defeated and Huhanxie Shanyu was defeated, King Zuoyi Zhizi made plans for King Lizheng Wuli, and persuaded him to surrender to Han and serve the emperor, so as to seek help from Huansu Nabuo, so that he could stabilize his body.
Huhanxie Shanyu discussed with the ministers and asked them. The ministers all said: This cannot be done.
summary: After Huhanxie Chanyu returned to his court, he ended the war and appointed his brother Hutuwusi as King Zuoguli. He also ordered the killing of King Youxian. That winter, Dulongqi and King Youxian supported Zhu Wanglian as a rival chanyu and attacked Huhanxie, who was defeated and fled. Tuqi Chanyu then took control, appointing his sons as kings. The following autumn, Tuqi Chanyu stationed troops to guard against Huhanxie. Internal strife escalated when King Hujie slandered King Youxian, leading to his execution. This caused King Hujie to flee and declare himself Chanyu, followed by others, resulting in five rival chanyus. Tuqi Chanyu attacked Cheli Chanyu and Wujii Chanyu, both of whom fled to join Hujie Chanyu. Tuqi then sent forces east and west, but Huhanxie Chanyu attacked and killed over 10,000 of Tuqi's troops. Tuqi retaliated with 60,000 cavalry but was defeated and committed suicide. Huhanxie Chanyu's general Dan Quli surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Huhanxie returned to his court with only tens of thousands of followers. Runzhen Chanyu and Zhizhi Chanyu emerged, with Zhizhi killing Runzhen and attacking Huhanxie, who was defeated.

translation:
When the emperor ascended the hillside of Changping, Shao ordered Shanzi not to come to pay him a visit. The ministers of the left and right households were allowed to line up to see him. There were also tens of thousands of Ganhou, the leaders of the barbarian tribes, who lined up along the road to greet the emperor under the Wei Bridge.
When the emperor boarded the Wei Bridge, people shouted long live.
Chanyu lived in Guanyi and stayed there for more than a month. The emperor sent him back to his country.
Chanyu himself requested that he be allowed to stay and live under Guanglu Fortress so that he could defend the surrendered city of the Han Dynasty in case of emergency.
The Han Dynasty sent Changle Guardsman Gaochanghou Dong Zhong and Chariot and Cavalry Commander Han Chang to lead 16,000 cavalry, as well as thousands of troops from border prefectures and counties to escort Huhanxie Chanyu out of Jilusai in Shuofang City.
The emperor ordered Dong Zhong and others to stay there to protect Shanyu and help him attack the rebellious and disobedient people. He also transported 34,000 hu of grain and rice to the frontier for food to the Huns.
In this year, Zhizhi Shanyu also sent envoys to the Han Dynasty to pay tribute. The Han Dynasty treated the envoys very well.
The next year, both Chanyus sent envoys to the Han Dynasty to meet the emperor and contribute gifts. The Han Dynasty treated Huhanxie Chanyu's envoy more favorably.
The next year, Huhanxie Shanyu came to the Jin Dynasty again to see the emperor. The emperor continued to offer the same gifts and rewards as before, and added 110 sets of clothes, 9,000 pieces of brocade and silk, and 8,000 catties of thick silk and cotton.
Because there were already troops stationed in the Huns, no more troops were sent to escort them.
At first, Zhizhi Chanyu thought that Huhanxie Chanyu had surrendered to the Han Dynasty and his troops were weak and would not come back again, so he led his army to the west, hoping to attack and pacify Youdi.
In addition, Tuqi Chanyu's younger brother originally served Huhanxie Chanyu, but now he also fled to the right place, gathered the tribes of his two brothers, got several thousand people, and established himself as Yili Mu Chanyu. On the road, he met Zhizhi Chanyu, and the two sides fought. Zhizhi Chanyu defeated and killed Yilimu Chanyu, and annexed his army of more than 50,000 people.
Hearing that the Han Dynasty sent troops and food to help Huhanxie Shanyu, he simply stayed and settled in Youdi.
Zhizhi Shanyu considered that his own strength could not defeat the Xiongnu, so he went further west and approached Wusun. He wanted to unite with Wusun and sent an envoy to see Xiaokun Miwu and slaughter him.
When Wujiutu saw that Huhanye Chanyu was receiving courtesy and help from the Han Dynasty, while Zhizhi Chanyu was on the run, he wanted to attack Zhizhi and cater to the Han Dynasty, so he killed Zhizhi's envoy, sent his head to the Han Dynasty's Western Region Protector, and dispatched eight thousand cavalry to attack Zhizhi.
Chanyu Zhizhi saw that Wusun had many soldiers and his envoy failed to return, so he led his army to attack Wusun and defeated Wusun.
Taking the opportunity to attack Wujie to the north, Wujie surrendered.
He also sent his own troops to the west to conquer Jiankun and to the north to defeat Ding Ling, and annexed these three countries.
Zhizhi Chanyu sent troops to attack Wusun many times and often won.
Jiankun was seven thousand miles away from the king's court in the east and five thousand miles away from Cheshi in the south. The Zhi branch stayed there and established its capital there.
Emperor Yuan had just ascended the throne, and Huhanxie Shanyu wrote to the Emperor of Han again, saying that the people of Baoqu were very poor and impoverished.
summary: King Zuoyi Zhizi advised Huhanxie to surrender to the Han Dynasty for stability. Despite opposition from ministers who valued Xiongnu martial traditions, Huhanxie agreed and led his people south, sending his son as a hostage. The Han emperor received Huhanxie with great honor, granting him titles, gifts, and troops for protection. Huhanxie requested to stay near the Han border for defense. The Han provided food and military support. Zhizhi Chanyu, meanwhile, moved west, attacking Wusun and other tribes, establishing his capital in Jiankun.

translation:
Xing issued an edict ordering Yunzhong County and Wuyuan County to transport 20,000 hu of grain for packaging.
Because his residence was far away from the road of the Han Dynasty, and he was very resentful of the Han Dynasty's support and help to Huhanxie Chanyu, Zhizhi Chanyu sent an envoy to Zhuimou to submit a letter, requesting to take back his son who had become a servant.
Xuansu sent Zhuzao to send him back, but Shanyu Zhuzhi killed Gu Ji.
The Han Dynasty did not know the news about Gu Ji. The Huns who came to surrender to the Han Dynasty reported that they had heard from the Huns in Ou Tuo that Gu Ji had been killed.
Hu Hanxie Chanyu sent envoys to the court, and the Han Dynasty was always very anxious to send documents asking for news about Gu Ji.
The next year, the Han Dynasty sent Han Chang, the captain of chariots and cavalry, and Zhang Meng, the Guanglu doctor, to escort Hu Hanxie Shanyu's son, who was serving as a servant, back to the Huns. They also inquired about Gu Ji and others, and announced a pardon for the Huns' sins, lest they worry that the Han Dynasty would attack them.
Han Chang and Zhang Meng saw that the Xiongnu tribe was prosperous and that all the animals under the fortress had been hunted down. The Chan Yu was strong enough to defend himself and was no longer afraid of Zhizhi.
Han and Zhang heard that many Xiongnu ministers advised the Shanyu to return to the north where they originally lived. They were worried that it would be difficult to govern the Xiongnu after they returned to the north. Han Chang and Zhang Meng made an alliance with the Shanyu, saying: From now on, the Han Dynasty and the Xiongnu are one family, and they are not allowed to deceive or attack each other from generation to generation.
When theft or robbery occurs, both parties must report to each other, punish the thief, and compensate for the lost property; when an enemy invades, they must send troops to rescue each other.
If either the Han Dynasty or the Xiongnu dared to betray the alliance first, they would be willing to accept the punishment of heaven.
Let their descendants and descendants suffer disaster just as the covenant says.
Han Chang, Zhang Meng, Hu Hanxie Chanyu and his ministers climbed to Nuoshuishu Mountain of the Xiongnu and killed the white horse. The Chanyu used a path knife and a golden plow to stir the wine mixed with the blood of the horse, and used the head of the Yuezhi King whom the old Shanyu had killed as a wine cup, and they drank the blood wine together as an alliance.
Han Chang and Zhang Meng reported this matter after they returned to the Han Dynasty. The ministers discussed the matter and said: "The Chanyu has promised us that we are willing to serve as a vassal to protect the frontier. Even if we want to return to the north, it will not pose a threat or hindrance to the Han Dynasty."
Han Chang and Zhang Meng acted without authorization and made an alliance with the Xiongnu on the future of the descendants of the Han Dynasty. This allowed the Chanyu to use evil words to tell heaven, humiliating the Han Dynasty and damaging the prestige of the country. This must not be done.
Envoys should be sent to appeal to Heaven and dissolve the former alliance with the Xiongnu.
Han Chang and Zhang Meng were ordered to go on a mission, which was not proper and their crimes were extremely treasonous.
The emperor alleviated their sins and issued an edict that Han Chang and Zhang Meng could be punished for their crimes but not terminate their alliance with the Huns.
Later, Huhanxie Chanyu finally returned to the court of Chanyu in the north. The Huns gradually surrendered to him, and the country settled down.
summary: Emperor Yuan succeeded and Huhanxie requested aid due to poverty. The Han sent grain. Zhizhi, resentful of Han support for Huhanxie, killed a Han envoy. The Han sent envoys to escort Huhanxie's son back and made an alliance with him, pledging mutual defense. However, Han officials criticized the alliance as unauthorized. Huhanxie eventually returned north, stabilizing his rule. Zhizhi, fearing Han retaliation, moved further west and allied with Kangju, but was later killed by Han forces. Huhanxie, relieved, requested to visit the Han court again.

translation:
Chanyu Zhizhi killed the envoy of the Han Dynasty, and he knew that he had failed the Han Dynasty. He also heard that Huhanxie was getting stronger, so he was worried about being attacked and wanted to move to a distant place.
It happened that King Kangju was besieged by the Wusun Kingdom many times at this time. He discussed with his Xihous that the Xiongnu was a powerful country and the Wusun Kingdom had always been subordinate to it. Now that Zhizhi Chanyu was living in exile, he could welcome him and live in Shubu. The two sides worked together to defeat Wusun and let Zhizhi Chanyu become king there. In this way, there would never be worries from the Huns.
So he sent an envoy to Jiankun to tell Chanyu Zhizhi these words.
Chanyu Zhizhi was often worried about being invaded by Huhanxie and resented Wusun. He was very happy when he heard King Kangju's plan, so he joined forces with Kangju and led the army to the west.
Kangju also sent nobles with thousands of camels, donkeys, and horses to meet Zhizhi.
Many of Zhizhi's tribe died of cold and starvation on the road, and finally only 3,000 people were left to reach Kangju.
Later, the governor Gan Yanshou and the deputy governor Chen Tang sent troops to Kangju to kill Zhizhi Shanyu. These are recorded in the biographies of Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang.
After Zhizhi Chanyu was killed, Huhanxie Chanyu was happy and scared, and wrote to the Emperor Xuan: I often hope to go to see His Majesty, but it is actually because Zhizhi Chanyu lives in the west, and I am worried that he will attack me with Mercer, so I cannot go to see the Emperor.
Now that Wai Mu has been convicted and killed, I hope that I can be allowed to come to the court to pay my respects.
In the first year of Jingning, Huhanxie Chanyu came to the Han Dynasty again. The Han Dynasty treated him with the same courtesy and rewards as before, and increased the rewards of clothes, brocade, silk, and thick silk and cotton, which were twice as much as in the Huanglong year.
Chanyu himself said that he would like to be the son-in-law of the Han Dynasty to get closer to the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty gave Shanyu Wang Qiangzi Zhaojun, a good woman who was a servant of the harem, as his wife.
The Chanyu was very happy and wrote to the emperor, saying that he was willing to protect the Han Dynasty frontier from Shanggu west to Dunhuang and pass it on forever. He asked the emperor to withdraw the officials and soldiers guarding the border fortress so that the emperor's subjects could rest and recuperate.
The emperor handed the matter over to the ministers for discussion, and the ministers in charge thought it was very convenient.
Langzhong Linghou should be familiar with the affairs of the frontier fortress and thought that he could not agree to the Huns like this.
Emperor Mo Yuan asked him why, and Hou Ying replied:
Since the Zhou and Qin Dynasties, the Xiongnu have been very violent and unruly, invading the frontiers. After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, they suffered particularly serious consequences.
I heard that our northern border fortress reaches all the way to Liaodong. Outside is the Yinshan Mountains, which is more than a thousand miles long from east to west, with lush vegetation and many animals. This place was originally the place where Maodun Shanyu relied on. He made bows and arrows here, trained his troops, and came in and out of Yinshan to harass us. Yinshan was the garden where they raised animals.
When Emperor Xiaowu arrived, he sent troops to attack and capture the area and drove them to the north of the desert.
summary: In the first year of Jingning, Huhanxie visited the Han court and received generous gifts. He requested to become a Han son-in-law, and Emperor Yuan gave him Wang Zhaojun as a wife. Huhanxie offered to defend the Han border from Shanggu to Dunhuang and asked for the withdrawal of Han border troops. The emperor consulted officials, and Hou Ying argued against withdrawal, citing ten reasons: the strategic value of the Yinshan Mountains, the Xiongnu's untrustworthy nature, the need to prevent internal crime and defections, and the risk of future emergencies. The emperor agreed and declined Huhanxie's request.

translation:
Hu Hanxie Shanyu reigned for twenty-eight years and died in the second year of Jianshi.
At first, Huhanxie Chanyu doted on the two daughters of King Huyan, brother of Zuoyi Zhizi.
The eldest daughter is Zhuanquban, and she gave birth to two sons. The eldest son is named Qiemoche, and the second son is named Nangzhiyasi.
The second daughter of King Hu Xian was of the Dapi family, and she gave birth to four sons. The eldest son was called Diao Tao Mogao, and the second son was named Qie Mixu, both of whom were older than Qie Moche. The two younger sons were Xian and Le, both younger than Nangzhi Yasi.
There were also more than ten other sons born to Pi.
Zhuanquban's family was noble, and Moche was also favored by Shanyu.
Hu Hanxie Shanyu was about to die of illness and wanted Qie Moche to succeed him. His mother, Zhuan Qupi, said: The Xiongnu have been in chaos for more than ten years, and this situation cannot be cut off like hair. Fortunately, with the help of the Han Dynasty, the Xiongnu was able to stabilize. The country has not been peaceful for a long time, and many people have been killed and injured in wars.
Moreover, Mo Che was still young and the people failed to rally to him. If he were to take the throne, it would probably put the Xiongnu in danger again.
Zuo Tiya and I are sisters, and we have the same sons. It would be better to have Tao Mogao carved as a chanyu.
Tai Laoya said: Although Mu Moche is young and has ministers to help handle national affairs, if he abandons the noble now and supports the humble, I am afraid there will be trouble in the future.
Huhanxie Chanyu finally followed Zhuanquban's suggestion and sculpted Tao Mogao as Chanyu and made a covenant to pass the country to his younger brother in the future.
After the death of Hu Hanxie, Diao Tao Mogao came to the throne and was called Fuzhuanruo Qianchanyu.
After Fuzhu case Ruo Qian Chanyu came to the throne, he sent his son Youzhi to King Lu'er, Xiexie Tu Nuhou, to serve the emperor in He, and appointed the emperor. Mi Xu was appointed King of Zuo Xian, Danhuang Nuo was appointed King of Zuo Guli, and Nangzhi Yasi was appointed King of You Xian.
In the Fuzhu case, Shanyu also took Yudan Donkey as his wife and gave birth to two daughters. The eldest daughter Yun was the second, and the second daughter was the second.
In the first year of Heping, the Chanyu sent Yougao Lin Wang Yixiemoyan and others to the Han Dynasty to pay tribute and participate in the first month worship.
At the end of the dynasty, the Han Dynasty sent envoys to escort Yixiemoyan and others to Pufan.
Yixiemo made a speech: I want to surrender to the Han Dynasty. If you don't agree to this, I will commit suicide. Why won't I return to the Huns?
The envoys from the Han Dynasty came back to report, and the emperor handed over the matter to the ministers for discussion. Some people said that those who surrendered should be accepted as before.
Gu Yong and Yilang Duqin, Guanglu officials, believed that since the founding of the Han Dynasty, the Huns had repeatedly invaded and harmed the border areas, so we set up a generous reward of titles and money to attract the Huns who surrendered.
Now the Chanyu is very submissive, professing vassalage to the Han Dynasty, and is listed as a vassal state in the north. He sends envoys to the Han Dynasty to pay homage and congratulate him without any second thoughts. Therefore, the Han Dynasty should treat those who surrender differently from the past.
Now, since we have accepted the loyal invitations and tributes from Shan Yu, but also accepted their defected ministers, doing so is greedy for one person, but losing the loyalty of the people of the country, politely supporting the guilty ministers, and abandoning the monarch who admires benevolence and righteousness.
If the Shanyu has just ascended the throne and wants to get close to the Han Dynasty and come to pay homage to the Han Dynasty, but does not know what the attitude of the Han Dynasty is, whether it is good or bad for him, and secretly sends Yixie Moyan to pretend to surrender to see what the future will be like, if we accept the surrender, it will destroy the good deeds and be virtuous. Unfortunately, the Shanyu himself alienated us and did not get close to the officials on our frontier; or someone used rhetorical tactics to create discord between us. If we accepted the surrender, we would have fallen into his trap, allowing the Huns to accuse us of doing something wrong and blame us for being wrong.
This is actually the root cause of whether our border is safe or not. The starting point of whether the army is dispatched or not cannot be taken lightly.
It is better not to accept those who surrender, to show the Xiongnu our trust that is as unchangeable as the sun and the moon, to suppress the deceitful and evil plots, and to protect those who surrender to the Han Dynasty. This is a convenient strategy.
summary: King Zuoyi Zhizi, who had advised Huhanxie to submit to Han, later fell under suspicion and surrendered to Han. Huhanxie later apologized and asked him to return, but he refused. Huhanxie died after 28 years, succeeded by his son Diao Tao Mogao as Fuzhuanruo Qianchanyu, following the advice of his mother Zhuanquban to avoid instability. The new chanyu appointed his brothers as kings and continued relations with Han. Subsequent chanyus maintained ties, sending sons as hostages and visiting the Han court.

translation:
At first, the Chanyu refused because Xiahou Fan asked for land from the Xiongnu. Later, because he failed to collect taxes from Wuhuan, he invaded and plundered Wuhuan's tribes. This conflict arose, and the seal was changed, so he was very resentful.
So he sent a dozen people including You Da Qie Qu Pu Hulu Zi to lead 10,000 cavalry to garrison under the Shuofang border fortress in the name of escorting Wuhuan's prisoners.
The prefect Shuofang reported the matter to the court.
In the second year, King Xuzhili, the queen of Cheshi in the Western Regions, attempted to surrender to the Huns, but Danqin, the governor of the Western Region, had him executed.
Zhili's elder brother Hulanzhi led more than 2,000 people, driving livestock, and the whole country fled and surrendered to the Huns, and the Chanyu accepted it.
The Hulanzhi invaded with the Xiongnu, attacked the chariot division, killed the leader of Houcheng, killed and wounded the guard Sima, and then returned to the Xiongnu.
At that time, Wuji Colonel Shi Chenliang, Zhongdai, Sima Cheng Han Xuan, Youquhou Renshang and others saw that many people in the Western Regions had betrayed the Central Plains, and heard that the Huns were about to invade the Central Plains. They were worried that they would be killed together, so they discussed together and hijacked hundreds of officials and soldiers.
General Nan of the Xiongnu led 2,000 cavalry into the Western Region to meet Chen Liang and others. Chen Liang and others hijacked more than 2,000 men and women, officials and soldiers under Wuji Xiaowei, and brought them to the Xiongnu.
Han Xuan and Ren Shang stayed with General Nan, while Chen Liang and Zhen took them directly to the court of Shan Yu. The people they brought were placed at the Lingwu River to farm.
The Chanyu gave them the names Chen Liang and Zhongdai, and called them General Wuhuandu. He kept them in the court of the Chanyu and invited them to drink and dine many times.
Danqin, the Protector of the Western Regions, wrote to the court, reporting that the Xiongnu's Southern General Youyi Zhizi led his troops to invade the Western Regions.
So Wang Mang greatly increased the number of Xiongnu chanyu titles to fifteen, and sent 10,000 cavalry led by Zhonglang General Lin Bao and deputy captain Dai Jie to the border fortress of Yunzhong County with many pearls and treasures. He lured several sons of Huhanxie Shanyu by seduction, hoping to make them chanyus one by one.
He sent an interpreter outside the border fortress to lure King Xian of Youli Khan, his sons Deng and Zhu, and three others. After arriving, he was forced to accept the title of Xiao Chanyu, and was rewarded with an An chariot and a drum chariot, one thousand catties of gold, one thousand pieces of miscellaneous silk, and ten halberds with flags.
Wang Mang also granted Lin Bao the title of Duke Xuanwei and appointed him General Huya; he conferred the rank of Dai to Duke Yangwei and appointed him General Huben.
When the Chanyu heard these things, he said angrily: "The Chanyu has been favored by Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty, but he cannot bear the responsibility to the Han Dynasty."
The current emperor is not a descendant of Emperor Xuan, how can he become the emperor?
He sent Zuo Guduhou, Youyi Zhizi King Huluzi and Zuoxian Wangle to lead troops to invade Yishousai in Yunzhong County and killed many officials and people.
This year is the third year since the founding of the People's Republic of China.
After that, the Chanyu repeatedly sent the left and right captains and the feudal kings on the frontier to invade the frontier to kill and plunder. The large-scale ones had more than 10,000 people, the medium-scale ones had thousands of people, and the smaller ones had hundreds of people. They killed the prefects and captains of Yanmen and Shuofang, and plundered countless officials, people, livestock and property, so the frontier fortress was greatly weakened.
Wang Mang had just become emperor and wanted to rely on the wealth of the national treasury to establish his own prestige, so he appointed twelve generals, dispatched warriors from various counties and counties, took out the sophisticated weapons from the arsenal, and ordered them to station in one side and gradually transport them to the frontier.
The plan was to wait for the number of 300,000 people, bring enough food for three hundred days, attack in ten groups at the same time, chase and beat the Xiongnu, drive them to Dingling, divide the territory of the Xiongnu, and establish Hu Hanxie's fifteen sons as chanyus.
Wang Mang's general Yan You advised him and said: I heard that the Huns were harming the Central Plains. It has been a long time since the beginning. I have never heard that the previous generation must go to conquer.
Later Zhou, Qin, and Mo dynasties went on conquests, but none of them could be said to have superior strategies.
It can be said that the Zhou Dynasty had the right strategy, the Han Dynasty had the wrong strategy, and the Qin Dynasty had no strategy at all.
During the reign of King Xuan of Zhou Dynasty, Mi Yun invaded the interior and reached Jingyang. King Xuan of Zhou sent generals to conquer the area and returned after reaching the border.
The Zhou Dynasty treated the invasion of Rong and Di as if they were biting mosquitoes and flies, they just drove them away.
summary: During the reign of Wuzhuliu Chanyu, Han envoy Xiahou Fan requested land from the Xiongnu, but the chanyu refused, citing ancestral rights. The Han emperor punished Xiahou Fan. Later, conflicts arose over Wusun raids and Wuhuan tax issues. Wang Mang, after usurping the Han throne, changed the Xiongnu seal and imposed new regulations, causing resentment. The Xiongnu resumed border raids. Wang Mang's military campaigns failed, leading to chaos. The Xiongnu chanyu died, and his successor Xian sought peace with Han but continued raiding. Wang Mang's attempts to control the Xiongnu through titles and gifts ultimately failed, and the border remained unstable.

translation:
Yang Xiong was rewarded with fifty pieces of silk and ten pounds of gold.
It happened that Chanyu fell ill before he set out, so he sent an envoy to say that he hoped to come to the court next year to see him.
According to the old rules in the past, when Chanyu came to worship, more than 200 people from the title of king to the following and his attendants were allowed to follow him into the court.
The Chanyu wrote to the emperor again, saying: Thanks to the blessing of the emperor's spirit, the Xiongnu people are strong and numerous. I hope that I can be allowed to bring 500 people to meet the emperor to show his great kindness.
The emperor all agreed to Shan Yu's request.
In the second year of Yuanshou, Shanyu came to the Han Dynasty to meet him. The emperor let Shanyu live in Putao Palace in Shanglinyuan because Tai Sui, who brought bad omens, and Weisheng, who could curse people, were there.
He also sent someone to inform Shanyu that this was a sign of extra respect for him, and Shanyu understood.
This time when Chanyu came to court, the emperor's additional rewards included 370 sets of clothes, 30,000 pieces of brocade silk, and 30,000 jins of thick silk and cotton. Other rewards were the same as during the Heping period.
After the first month of the dynasty, the Han Dynasty sent Zhonglang to escort Han Kuang back to the Xiongnu.
Shanyu left the frontier fortress, arrived at Xiutunjing, and crossed Chetianlu River to the north. The road was long and winding.
Han Kuang and others were short of food, so the Chanyu provided them with food. Han Kuang and others came back more than fifty days after the deadline.
At first, the emperor sent Jiliu Kun to follow Shan Yu back. After Shan Yu returned to the royal court, he sent Ji Liu Kun, his uncle You Daqifang and his wife to serve the emperor.
After returning from this pilgrimage, he sent his half-brother Zuo Yue, Daqifang on the right, to Zhuwangdu and his wife to serve in the court.
At this time, Emperor Ping of the Han Dynasty was young, the Empress Dowager came to the court to take the throne, and Wang Mang, the new capital lord, presided over the affairs of the court. Wang Mang wanted to please the Empress Dowager by praising her great virtue, so he asked Shanyu to tell Shan Yu from the side that he should send Wang Zhaojun's daughter Xubu Juciyun to the court to serve the Empress Dowager, and the rewards were very generous.
It happened that at this time, Wang Jugu, the queen of chariots in the Western Regions, and Tangdou, the king of Hu Lai, both resented the captain of the military guard. They led their wives and children to escape and surrendered to the Huns. The incident was recorded in "Biography of the Western Regions".
The Chanyu accepted the surrendered people, placed them in Zuoguli, and sent an envoy to the Han Dynasty to report the situation and said: I have accepted them all.
The imperial edict sent the lieutenant generals Han Long and Wang Chang, the deputy captain Zhen Fu, the minister's visitor Bo Chang, and the Changshui captain Wang She as envoys to the Xiongnu, telling the Shanyu: The Western Region is under the jurisdiction of the Han Dynasty, and the Shanyu should not accept surrendered people. I want you to release them.
Shanyu said: Emperor Xiaoxuan and Emperor Xiaoyuan took pity on us and made an agreement with us that the area south of the Great Wall would belong to the Emperor of the Han Dynasty, and the area north of the Great Wall would belong to Shanyu.
If someone invades the frontier fortress, they must inform each other of the situation; if someone comes to surrender, they must not accept it.
My father, Huhanxie Shanyu, received immeasurable kindness from the Han Dynasty. Before he died, he left a message: If there are people who surrender from the Central Plains, they are not allowed to accept it. They must be sent back to the frontier fortress and returned to the Han Dynasty to repay the kindness of Emperor Mo. But this time the people who surrendered are from countries other than the Great Wall, I can accept it.
The envoy of the Han Dynasty said: At the beginning, the Xiongnu's relatives attacked each other, and the country was almost completely reduced. Thanks to China's great kindness, it supported the Chanyu, so that the Xiongnu who were in danger could continue to survive, and their families, wives and children could be kept safe. From generation to generation, the Xiongnu should repay the great kindness to the Han Dynasty.
After hearing this, the Shan Yu kowtowed to the envoy to apologize, and captured the two princes who had surrendered and handed them over to the Han Dynasty envoy.
The Han Dynasty issued an edict to send Zhonglang General Wang Meng to the border of Badunu in the Western Regions to meet and accept the returned people.
Chanyu sent an envoy to escort him to the Han Dynasty and asked the emperor for forgiveness.
The envoy reported to the court, but the court issued an edict not to forgive them, and gathered the kings of the Western Regions to kill Gou Gu and Tang Dou to show their guilt.
summary: After Wang Mang's death, the Han Dynasty restored relations with the Xiongnu, but the chanyu remained arrogant. The historian concludes that peace treaties and military campaigns both had limitations, and the Xiongnu's nature made lasting peace difficult.

translation:
Kuang Heng, courtesy name Zhigui, was born in Haicheng County, Cambodia.
His grandfather had been farming for generations, and when he came to Kuangheng, he liked to study. Because his family was poor, Kuangheng worked as a hired worker to pay for his expenses.
Kuang Heng's energy exceeded ordinary people. Many Confucian scholars praised him and said: Don't talk about "Poetry", Kuang Heng will come; Kuang Heng comes to talk about "Poetry", making people happy and laughing.
Kuang Heng was awarded the title of "Jia Ke", but because he failed to pass the "Jia Ke" regulations, he was only appointed as Taichang's storyteller, and later he was appointed as "Pingyuan County Literature".
Many scholars wrote letters recommending that Kuang Heng was proficient in classics and was unparalleled in the world. He should be appointed as a literary scholar and go to the capital as an official. The younger generation were willing to follow Kuang Heng to study in Pingyuan County. Kuang Heng should not be an official far away from the capital.
The emperor handed this matter over to Prince Taifu Xiao Wangzhi and Shaofu Liang Qiuhe for questioning. Kuang Heng answered with the righteousness of the Book of Songs, which was very profound and brilliant.
Xiao Wangzhang reported that Kuang Heng was proficient in classics and his lectures were passed down from a teacher's perspective, which can be viewed.
Emperor Xuan did not make much use of Confucian scholars, so he sent Kuang Heng back to his original place.
However, after the crown prince saw Kuang Heng's correct question, he secretly appreciated him.
When Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, a relative of Leling Marquis Shi Gao was appointed as the Great Sima Cavalry General and concurrently as Minister, with former general Xiao Wangzhi as his deputy.
Xiao Wangzhi was a famous Confucian and the emperor's mentor. The emperor valued him and made great contributions in recommending talents.
Shi Gao, on the other hand, had no interest in political affairs and only had a reputation, which created a gap between him and Xiao Wangzhi.
Yang Xing, the magistrate of Chang'an County, persuaded Shi Gao: "The general assists in political affairs with relatives, and his reputation is noble and unparalleled in the world. However, in everyone's discussion, the good reputation and honor are not all attributed to the general. Why?"
Because they heard that generals cannot recommend virtuous and talented people.
As the shogunate of the shogunate, everyone in the world looks up to and admires him, but the people recommended by the shogun are just private guests and the children of wet nurses.
The general ignored everyone's comments because of favors and did not know that there was anything wrong with him. However, as long as one person discusses it in private, it will spread throughout the world.
Although you are rich and noble, the scholars do not praise you. It is like wearing a pure white fox fur coat, which is flashy.
The ancients were very taboo about such things, so they deigned to take the trouble to find worthy people as their own duty.
The Sutra says: Because wise men are rare, you cannot wait for wise men to arrive when doing things; because food is rare, you cannot wait for food to arrive when you are full.
There are more serious situations than this kind of waiting. Pingyuan Literature Kuang Heng's talents and wisdom were more than enough, and his attainments in classics were outstanding. Because he had no chance of promotion in the imperial court, he had to follow the selection and supplementary documents and move to a place far away from the capital to serve as an official.
If the general summons Kuangheng to serve in the shogunate, scholars all over the world will definitely follow him, let him participate in discussing political affairs, and recommend him to the court based on his expertise, and he will definitely become a pillar of the country. If you do this for everyone to see, your reputation will spread throughout the world.
Shi Gao thought Yang Xing was right, so he appointed Kuang Heng as the historian of Cao and recommended him to the emperor. The emperor asked him to be a doctor, and later he was promoted to a doctor and served concurrently as Shizhong.
At this time, disasters such as solar eclipses and earthquakes occurred. The emperor asked about the relationship between these changes and political gains and losses. Kuangheng Shangshu said:
I heard that the rituals of the five emperors were different, the politics and religion of the three kings were different, and the people's customs were very different. The reason is that the times have changed.
summary: Kuang Heng, courtesy name Zhigui, was born in Haicheng County. His family had farmed for generations, and despite poverty, he loved studying and worked as a hired laborer to fund his education. His energy exceeded ordinary people, and many Confucian scholars praised him. He was awarded the title of "Jia Ke" but failed to pass its regulations, so he was appointed as Taichang's storyteller and later as Pingyuan County Literature. Scholars recommended him as unparalleled in classical studies, but Emperor Xuan did not favor Confucian scholars and sent him back. However, the crown prince secretly appreciated him. When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, Shi Gao appointed Kuang Heng as historian of Cao and recommended him to the emperor, who made him a doctor. During disasters like solar eclipses and earthquakes, Kuang Heng submitted a memorial stating that different times required different governance. He observed that amnesty did not reduce crime and argued that education should promote etiquette and humility. He criticized corrupt customs, greed, and luxury, urging the emperor to set an example through moral leadership. He cited classical texts to support his arguments and recommended reducing palace expenses, eliminating extravagance, promoting virtuous officials, and reforming education. The emperor was pleased and promoted him to Guanglu Doctor and Prince Shaofu.

translation:
Soon after, Kuang Heng made a memorial to renovate the northern and southern suburban temples and cancel all kinds of extravagant and extravagant sacrifices. His memorial was recorded in "Jiao Sacrifice Chronicles".
When Emperor Yuan was in power, Zhongshu ordered Shi Xian to take charge of court affairs. From the former prime minister Wei Xuancheng to Kuang Heng, everyone was afraid of Shi Xian and did not dare to go against his wishes.
When Emperor Cheng first came to the throne, Kuang Heng and the imperial censor Zhen Tan jointly submitted an impeachment report to Shi Xian, investigating his old evil deeds one by one and tracking down his party members.
At this time, Wang Zun, the lieutenant of the Sili School, submitted an impeachment report saying: Kuang Heng and Zhen Tan were serving as ministers, and they knew that Shi Xian and others were dictatorial, tyrannical, and a great harm to the country. However, Kuang Heng and Zhen Tan did not file an impeachment report in time to punish them.
After impeaching Shi Xian and others, he did not state his crime of disloyalty to the emperor. Instead, he publicized the fault of the late emperor for appointing bad guys who subverted the country and the country. He committed an unethical and grave crime.
The emperor issued an edict not to impeach Kuang Heng.
But Kuang Heng still felt ashamed and frightened. Shangshu confessed, claimed that he was ill and asked to return to his hometown, and handed over the seal of Prime Minister Le'an Hou.
The emperor replied: You have high moral cultivation and hold the important position of the Three Dukes. The late emperor entrusted you with political affairs, and now you are helping me with political affairs.
You follow and amend the legal system and serve the country diligently. I am very happy to work with you to govern the country together.
Now Wang Zun, the captain of Sili School, is arrogantly slandering you and saying what you are wrong about. I sympathize with you.
Wang Zun will be submitted to a competent authority for interrogation. Why are you still suspicious and writing a letter asking for resignation? This is publicity and I don’t realize it.
Didn't "Yi Zhuan" say: As long as there are no faults in etiquette and morality, why should you worry about other people's opinions?
You should understand this.
Concentrate, take your medicine, eat hard, and take care of your body.
He was also rewarded with fine wine and raised beef cattle.
Kuang Heng took charge of government affairs again.
Because the emperor had just ascended the throne, he praised his ministers a lot, but most of the court officials were people like Wang Zun.
Kuang Heng was very uneasy. Every time there were floods, droughts, or bad weather, he would write letters to resign and ask to give up his position.
The emperor always comforted and encouraged Kuang Heng with edicts and did not allow Kuang Heng to abdicate in old age.
Later, Kuang Heng's son Kuang Chang served as a captain of the Yue Cavalry School. He killed someone while drunk and was imprisoned.
Yueqi officials and Kuang Chang's brother prepared to conspire to save Kuang Chang.
After the incident was discovered, Kuang Heng took off his official hat and went to plead guilty with bare feet. The emperor sent envoy Shao Ling to restore Kuang Heng's official hat and shoes.
However, a supervisor impeached Kuang Heng for monopolizing land theft, and Kuang Heng was implicated and was dismissed from office.
At the beginning, Kuang Heng's fiefdom was in Le'an Township, Tong County, Linhuai County. The entire township had a total of 3,100 hectares of farmland, bounded by Fujian and Bai in the south.
summary: Kuang Heng frequently advised the emperor on proper conduct, emphasizing that governing a country begins with governing one's family. He stressed the importance of distinguishing between the queen and concubines and establishing proper hierarchies. After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, Kuang Heng warned about choosing a spouse according to Confucian etiquette. He later submitted a memorial to renovate suburban temples and cancel extravagant sacrifices. During Emperor Yuan's reign, Kuang Heng feared Zhongshu Ling Shi Xian and did not oppose him. When Emperor Cheng first ruled, Kuang Heng and Zhen Tan impeached Shi Xian, but were themselves impeached for not reporting Shi Xian's crimes earlier. The emperor did not punish Kuang Heng, but he felt ashamed and asked to resign. The emperor refused and encouraged him.

translation:
In the first year of the Chu Yuan Dynasty, the county map of Linhuai County mistakenly identified Min Bai as Pingling Bai.
For more than ten years, the Kuangheng fiefdom in Linhuai County actually used the original Pingling Bai as the boundary of the fiefdom, which was 400 hectares more than the real Minbai as the fiefdom.
In the first year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the national boundaries were demarcated, the acres were re-counted, new books were made, the maps were re-drawn, and the matter was reported to the Prime Minister's Office.
Kuang Heng said to Zhao Yin, a close official: Lu Ci, the chief secretary, used to serve as a memorial to Cao and was familiar with the division of fief boundaries. Now he serves as a gathering of Cao.
When conducting land statistics the next year, Kuang Heng asked Cai Yin about the boundaries of the fiefdom: What does the clerk in charge of this matter want to do?
Zhao Yin replied: Lu Ci believed that he should take the initiative to truthfully report the statistical land account books, and asked the local officials to change the fiefdom to Pingling Bai as the boundary according to the actual situation.
I'm afraid the local people are unwilling to change it like this, so we can ask Jiacheng to write to the emperor.
Kuang Heng said: "The main consideration is whether we should get it. Why should we write to the emperor?"
However, Kuang Heng did not instruct the official in charge of the matter to report the accounts of the fields, leaving it to the clerks.
Later, Lu Ciyu's subordinate official named Ming reported land statistics and said: According to the original territory, the south of the Le'an Township fiefdom is bounded by Pingling Bai. It does not follow the original demarcation, but Min Bai is used as the boundary. What does it mean?
Linhuai County immediately allocated another 400 hectares of land to Le'an Kingdom.
Kuang Heng sent responsible clerks to Tong County to collect the rent for the returned land, which amounted to more than a thousand stones of millet.
Sili Xiaowei Jun and Shaofuzhong were responsible for the affairs of acting Tingwei. They impeached Kuang Heng and said: Kuang Heng supervised the fiefdom of Linhuai County and stole local property privately. The crime is punishable by a fine of more than ten gold.
The principles of "Spring and Autumn" indicate that princes cannot monopolize land and must abide by the country's legal system.
Kuang Heng had a high official position among the three public officials, assisting the state in government affairs, mastering the land acreage book of the fiefdom, and knowing the actual situation of demarcating the boundaries of the county and land. He should draw the boundaries correctly. However, after the local land recalculation and the redrawing of the fiefdom boundaries, Kuang Heng still violated the national regulations. According to the family's legal system, land was stolen and arbitrarily used to increase personal gain. His subordinate officials Lu Ci and Ming Ai flattered Kuang Heng's will, distorted the statistics of reported fiefdoms, reduced county boundaries indiscriminately, deceived superiors and subordinates, and annexed land to ministers without authorization, which was all illegal.
So the emperor approved the two men's memorials and did not punish Kuang Heng. He was only removed from the post of prime minister and demoted to a commoner. Kuang Heng finally died at home.
Kuang Heng's son Kuang Xian was also proficient in classics and righteousness, and once held the position of Jiu Qing.
His descendants produced many doctors of Confucian classics.
Zhang Yu, whose courtesy name was Ziwen, was a native of Ruan County, Hanoi County. When his father arrived, he moved to Lianshao County.
summary: Kuang Heng's son Kuang Chang killed someone while drunk and was imprisoned. Kuang Heng's brother conspired to rescue him, and when discovered, Kuang Heng pleaded guilty. The emperor restored his position, but Kuang Heng was later impeached for land theft. His fiefdom in Le'an Township had mistakenly used incorrect boundaries for over ten years, gaining 400 extra hectares. Kuang Heng did not correct this and collected rent from the additional land. He was impeached, and although the emperor did not punish him severely, he was removed from the post of prime minister and demoted to a commoner. He died at home. His son Kuang Xian was also proficient in classics and held the position of Jiu Qing.

translation:
When Zhang Yu was a child, he often went to the market with his family and liked to watch those who performed divination and fortune telling.
As time goes by, I am very good at identifying the good and bad meanings of yarrow and gossip, and I often tell what I mean from the sidelines.
The fortune teller liked him very much and thought he was extraordinary in appearance, so he said to Zhang Yu's father: This child is very smart and he can learn scriptures.
When Zhang Yu grew up, he went to Chang'an, the capital, to study. He learned the Book of Changes from Shi Yu, a native of Peijun, and the Analects of Confucius from Wang Yang, a native of Langxie, and Yongsheng, a native of Jiaodong. When he became proficient in these classics, he gathered his disciples to teach them, and was later recommended as a county literature scholar.
During the Ganlu reign of Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty, various Confucian scholars recommended Zhang Yu, and the emperor ordered the prince and Taifu Xiao Wangzhi to be responsible for inspecting Zhang Yu's knowledge.
Zhang Yu answered about the great meaning of "The Book of Changes" and "The Analects of Confucius". Xiao Wangzhi appreciated it very much and reported to the emperor that Zhang Yu was very proficient in Confucian classics and had learned the classics. He suggested that the emperor should try Zhang Yu as an official.
However, this report was not approved, and Zhang Yu returned to his original official position.
Much later, the emperor tried Zhang Yu as a doctor.
In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the crown prince was established. At that time, Dr. Zheng Kuanzhong taught the prince "Shang Shu". He recommended that Zhang Yu was good at "The Analects of Confucius", so the emperor ordered Zhang Yu to teach the prince to learn "The Analects of Confucius".
Therefore, Zhang Yu was promoted to doctor Guanglu.
A few years later, he served as the internal history of Shuping County.
Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng ascended the throne. Zhang Yu and Zheng Kuanzhong were recruited to Chang'an. They were both given the title of Marquis of Guannei because they had been teachers of the prince. Zheng Kuanzhong had a settlement of 800 households, and Zhang Yu had a settlement of 600 households.
Zhang Yu was appointed to the various officials as Guanglu Dafu, with an official rank of two thousand shi, and was assigned to Shizhong, and he was in charge of the secretarial affairs.
When he was sent, Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty's uncle Yangpinghou Wang Feng was appointed as a general. He was called assistant to the government, but he was actually authoritarian. The emperor was very young, modest, fond of classics, and respected teachers.
At that time, Zhang Yu and Wang Feng concurrently served as ministers, and he felt very uneasy. He petitioned to resign and return to his hometown several times due to illness, and wanted to avoid working with Wang Feng.
The emperor replied: I ascended the throne at a young age and was very worried about making mistakes. You became my teacher because of your high moral character, so I entrusted the affairs of the country to you.
What do you have to worry about, so that you repeatedly asked to resign? Are you forgetting our master-disciple relationship, or are you avoiding some rumors?
I haven't heard any rumors about you.
You should work with peace of mind, still be in charge of political affairs, show your tireless spirit, and don't go against my wishes.
summary: Zhang Yu, courtesy name Ziwen, was born in Ruan County. As a child, he liked watching fortune tellers and became skilled at divination. He studied the Book of Changes and the Analects of Confucius in Chang'an, then gathered disciples to teach. During Emperor Xuan's reign, Xiao Wangzhi praised his knowledge, but the emperor did not approve his appointment. Later, he became a doctor and taught the prince the Analects of Confucius. When Emperor Cheng ascended, Zhang Yu was appointed Guanglu Dafu and served as Shizhong. He felt uneasy serving alongside the authoritarian Wang Feng and repeatedly asked to resign, but the emperor refused and rewarded him generously. Zhang Yu eventually became prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Anchang. After six years, he resigned due to old age and illness.

translation:
Although Wang Gen was the emperor's uncle, the emperor did not respect him as much as Zhang Yu. Although Wang Gen spoke very sincerely, the emperor did not listen to his dissuasion and finally gave the Fei Niu Pavilion to Zhang Yu.
Wang Gen was jealous of Zhang Yu's favor, so he wrote many times to slander Zhang Yu.
But the emperor respected Zhang Yu even more and treated him favorably.
Every time Zhang Yu fell ill, the emperor would ask about his daily life and even visit Zhang Yu in person.
When the emperor arrived, Zhang Yu was grateful, kowtowed and thanked him, and took this opportunity to report to the emperor: I have four sons and one daughter, and I prefer my daughter, but she is married to Xiao Xian, the prefect of Zhangye. I miss her very much and hope she will be closer to me.
The emperor immediately ordered Xiao Xian to be transferred to be the prefect of Hongnong.
In addition, Zhang Yu's youngest son did not have an official title at that time. When the emperor visited him, he looked at his youngest son many times. After the emperor understood what he meant, he appointed his youngest son as Huang Menlang in front of his bed, giving him the title of "Huang Menlang".
Although Zhang Yu has resigned, he still serves as the emperor's teacher as a special official. Whenever the country makes major decisions, the emperor must ask Zhang Yu.
During the reigns of Emperor Cheng Yongshi and Yuanyan, there were many solar eclipses and earthquakes. Officials and people wrote letters saying that these were disasters, and ridiculed that they were caused by the Wang family's monopoly.
The emperor was afraid that disasters would occur many times, and he was worried and uneasy. He did not express his clear position on the petitions from ministers and people, so he drove to Zhang Yu's mansion, dismissed the guards on the left and right, and then asked Zhang Yu about his views on food and earthquakes, and stated the opinions of the officials and people on the Wang family.
Zhang Yu considered that he was old and his descendants were weak. His relationship with Quyanghou Wanggen had always been mediocre, and he was afraid of being resented by him.
So he told the emperor: During the two hundred and forty-two years of the Spring and Autumn Period, there were more than thirty solar eclipses and five earthquakes. During this period, sometimes the princes killed each other, and sometimes the barbarians invaded the Central Plains. The disasters were unpredictable. Therefore, ancient saints rarely talked about destiny, nor did they blame gods.
Starting from the time of Zigong, the relationship between life and the way of heaven has no longer been discussed, let alone what Qianjian despised Confucianism said!
It is only natural that Your Majesty should revise his country's governance policies to adapt to the current situation and share the well-being of the people.
New students who mislead others should not be trusted and reused, and should use classics to judge what they say.
Because the emperor usually trusted and favored Zhang Yu, Zhang Yu's words dispelled the emperor's doubts about Wang.
Afterwards, when King Gen of Quyanghou and the descendants of various princes and kings heard about Zhang Yu's remarks, they were all delighted and began to approach Zhang Yu.
Zhang Yu saw that abnormal phenomena often occurred at that time, and the emperor was in poor health, so he chose auspicious days to cleanse himself and fast, and exposed yarrow under the stars to catch the heavenly energy.
After Emperor Cheng died, Zhang Yu served Emperor Ai again. He died in the second year of Jianping, Emperor Ai's reign, and was given the title of Marquis of Jie.
Zhang Yu had four sons. The eldest son, Zhang Hong, inherited his father's title as Marquis of Anchang. His palace was in Taichang and he was among the nine ministers.
summary: Zhang Yu was cautious and kind, engaging in business and farming. He bought 400 hectares of fertile farmland and lived luxuriously, enjoying music. He treated his students differently: with Dai Chong, he shared wine and music in the back hall, while with Peng Xuan, he had simple meals in the main hall. When old, he built a tomb at Fei Niu Pavilion in Pingling, which was a royal ancestral worship site. Despite Wang Gen's objections, the emperor granted his request. Wang Gen slandered him, but the emperor respected Zhang Yu even more. When the emperor visited him during illness, Zhang Yu requested that his daughter be closer, and the emperor transferred her husband. The emperor also appointed Zhang Yu's youngest son as Huang Menlang. Zhang Yu served as the emperor's teacher even after resigning, and the emperor consulted him on major decisions. During solar eclipses and earthquakes, when officials blamed the Wang family, Zhang Yu advised the emperor not to trust such claims, dispelling doubts about Wang. He died in the second year of Jianping and was given the title of Marquis of Jie.

translation:
Guang Luxun Kuang Heng recommended Kong Guang to be an admonishing doctor because of his good conduct.
Because his discussion of political affairs was inconsistent with the emperor's wishes, he was demoted to the magistrate of Hong County. Kong Guang was dismissed in vain and went home to teach Confucian classics.
When Emperor Cheng first came to the throne, Liao Guang was elected as a doctor. He was repeatedly asked to be responsible for redressing injustices, regulating customs, and providing relief to victims. Kong Guang successfully completed the mission every time he was ordered to go on an envoy, and Kong Guang's reputation spread throughout the government and the public.
At this time, doctors were divided into three subjects to select officials. Those with excellent grades were selected as ministers, and those with lower grades were selected as governors. Those who were not familiar with government affairs were left to serve as princes and tutors in the future. The ones with excellent grades were appointed as ministers, responsible for inspecting the laws, regulations, etiquette and rituals of the previous dynasties. After many years of study, they became proficient in the systems and laws of the Han Dynasty.
The emperor trusted him very much and was successively promoted to Pu She and Shan Shu Ling.
The emperor had a letter from Shao to commend Kong Guang for his careful and prudent work and never making any mistakes. He was promoted to an official and appointed his son Kong Fang as the minister of ministers to the Huangmen.
A few years later, Kong Guang was promoted to the official position Guanglu Dafu, with a salary of 2,000 dan, a reward of 100 jin of gold, and the title of Shangshu.
Later, he was promoted to Guang Luxun, still responsible for the affairs of the minister, and served as an official in charge of affairs as before. Kong Guang was in charge of the government affairs for more than ten years, maintaining laws and revising systems.
When the emperor asked about political affairs, Kong Guang always answered with the answer he thought was right according to the classic laws, and did not want to be in conflict with the emperor's will. Just as sometimes the emperor did not obey, Kong Guang did not dare to forcefully remonstrate, so Kong Guang served as an official for a long time and was safe.
Sometimes he wrote letters to express his opinions, and the memorials he had already written were always deleted and revised. He believed that writing letters to publicize the emperor's faults in order to gain a reputation for loyalty and uprightness was a major sin in officialdom.
When Ziguang recommended others to become officials, he was also afraid that others would hear him.
When it was my turn to have a holiday, I would go home to rest and talk to my brothers, wives and children about everyday things, but never mention the political affairs surrounding the imperial court.
Someone asked Kong Guang: What kind of trees are there in the greenhouse of Changle Palace?
Kong Guang just smiled, did not answer, and then distracted him with other words. This is how Kong Guang did not leak the political affairs of the court.
Kong Guang was the son of the emperor's teacher. He was famous for his classical studies and conduct when he was young. He became famous very early when he became an official. He did not form a party, support or train lobbyists, nor did he seek help from others.
This is not only the result of his introverted and rigorous personality, but also determined by his early academic life.
Later, Kong Guang was promoted from Guang Luxun to imperial censor.
During the Suihe period, the emperor ascended the throne for twenty-five years and had no son to inherit the throne. His closest relatives were his half-brother, King Zhongshan Xiao, and his half-brother's son, King Dingtao.
King Dingtao was as knowledgeable as the emperor's son.
summary: Kong Guang, courtesy name Zixia, was the fourteenth generation grandson of Confucius. His father Kong Ba was a doctor and teacher to the crown prince. Kong Guang was proficient in classics and was elected as Yilang before age twenty. Kuang Heng recommended him as an admonishing doctor, but he was demoted for disagreeing with the emperor. He later became a doctor and successfully completed missions, gaining fame. He was promoted to Guanglu Dafu and served as Shangshu for over ten years, maintaining laws and revising systems. He was cautious, never leaking court affairs, and avoided forcefully remonstrating. He recommended officials secretly and did not form factions. He became imperial censor and later prime minister, granted the title of Marquis of Boshan.

translation:
Chang's surname is Chenggong, and he is from Shuhai County.
Kong Guang served as doctor for a month. Prime Minister Wang Jia was imprisoned and died. The censor doctor bought an extension and was dismissed.
Kong Guang resumed his role as the imperial censor, and two months later he resumed his role as prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Boshan again.
Only then did the emperor realize that the reason why Kong Guang had been dismissed from his official position was not that Kong Guang had committed a crime, but that the ministers around him had slandered and framed him, so he dismissed Fu Jia from his official position, saying: When Fu Jia was serving as a minister, he slandered and framed people who were benevolent, righteous and virtuous, and falsely accused ministers, so that virtuous and handsome people could not be reused for a long time.
On the contrary, Fu Jia was clever and hypocritical, harbored treachery, deceived the emperor, formed cliques for personal gain, blocked the sky with one hand, slandered loyal ministers, and acted unscrupulously.
Didn't the "Book of Songs" say: The flattering villain was rampant in deception and caused chaos in the country, so Fu Jia was removed from his official position and became a civilian, and was sent back to his original county.
The next year, the official position of the three princes was evaluated, and Kong Guang was changed to the post of Grand Situ.
Coinciding with the death of Emperor Ai, the Empress Dowager took Wang Mang, the new capital lord, as the Grand Sima and elected King Zhongshan as the emperor, namely Emperor Ping of the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Ping was very young, so the Empress Dowager was in charge of the government, and the Empress Dowager entrusted political affairs to Wang Mang.
During the reign of Emperor Ai, the Wang family was deposed. Therefore, the Queen Mother and Wang Mang were very resentful towards Ding, Fu and Dong Xian.
Wang Mang believed that Kong Guang was the former prime minister, a famous Confucian, trusted and admired by the world, and the Queen Mother also respected him and always received him with courtesy.
Whenever it was necessary to attack political opponents, Li Guang was always asked to help draft documents. According to the Queen Mother's orders, Kong Guang was asked to write the memorial. Anyone who has enmity against the Queen Mother, even if it is a small amount of hatred, will be retaliated and no one will be killed.
Wang Mang's power became stronger day by day. Kong Guang was very frightened and worried. He didn't know what to do, so he wrote to the emperor to resign.
Wang Mang then said to the Queen Mother: The emperor is very young and should be given a teacher.
He appointed Kong Guang as the emperor's Taifu, with the official position of Fourth Assistant. He was responsible for providing food, clothing, carriages, horses and food.
In the second year, he was promoted to Taishi, and Wang Mang served as Taifu.
Kong Guang often complained of illness and did not dare to take the throne with Wang Mang in the court.
The emperor ordered Wang Mang to go to court on the first and fifteenth day of each month and asked Wang Mang to command the city gate guards.
Wang Mang also ordered his officials to submit a memorial praising Wang Mang's merits. Emperor Ping of the Han Dynasty gave Wang Mang the title of Prime Minister, ranking him above the princes and kings and commanding hundreds of officials.
Seeing this situation, Ziguang felt even more panicked and insisted on resigning due to illness.
The Queen Mother then issued an edict saying: Taishi Kong Guang is a descendant of a saint and the son of the late emperor's teacher. He is pure and upright in virtue, proficient in morality and academics, and serves as the fourth assistant to assist the emperor.
Now I am old and sick. But highly respected ministers like Kong Guang are important ministers of the country and are still indispensable. "Book of Zhou."
Zhao Gao said: "Never abandon mature people. If the country wants to prosper, it must respect and reuse teachers."
He ordered Grand Master Kong Guang not to go to court, but to reward him with a meal every ten days.
The Grand Master was given a longevity stick, and the Huangmen Order set up a place for the Grand Master to sit within the palace. The Grand Master could hold the staff when entering the palace, and was rewarded with seventeen kinds of food. Then he returned to the mansion to retire, while his subordinate officials continued to work as usual.
Kong Guang served as the imperial censor and prime minister twice, and once as the chief situ, Taifu and Taishi. He experienced three generations of emperors and held the high position of auxiliary minister for a total of seventeen years.
After becoming the minister, he stopped teaching activities, and later became the prime minister. Sometimes he would meet his disciples to discuss and raise difficult questions, and Kong Guang would often explain his principles to them.
Many of Kong Guang's disciples were successful in their studies and became doctors and doctors. When they saw their teacher holding important positions, they all wanted his help. However, Kong Guang never recommended them, so some people complained about him.
Kong Guang acted fairly, that's all.
Kong Guang was seventy years old and died in the fifth year of Yuanshi.
Wang Mang told the Queen Mother that he would give Jiu Qing's policy book to the Taishi Boshan Hou Yinshou, and give him a carriage, a coffin, money, and miscellaneous silk.
summary: During the succession debate, Kong Guang argued for King Zhongshan based on blood relations, but the emperor chose King Dingtao. Kong Guang was demoted to Tingwei. Later, he argued that Chunyu Chang's concubines who left before his crime should not be implicated, and the emperor agreed. After Emperor Cheng's sudden death, Kong Guang was appointed prime minister. When Emperor Ai ruled, Kong Guang advised against Empress Dowager Fu living close to the emperor, but was overruled. He later opposed retaining the treacherous Fu Qian, but the emperor kept him. Kong Guang was eventually dismissed for failing to advise properly during disasters. After several prime ministers failed, the emperor recalled Kong Guang during a solar eclipse. Kong Guang explained that eclipses occurred when ministers became too powerful and advised the emperor to reform governance. The emperor reappointed him as prime minister. Under Empress Dowager and Wang Mang's rule, Kong Guang was used to draft documents attacking political opponents. Fearing Wang Mang's growing power, Kong Guang tried to resign. Wang Mang appointed him as the emperor's Taifu, and later Taishi. Kong Guang often claimed illness to avoid attending court with Wang Mang. He served as imperial censor and prime minister twice, and as chief situ, Taifu, and Taishi, holding high positions for seventeen years. He died at age seventy in the fifth year of Yuanshi, receiving an elaborate funeral with thousands of mourners. His title was Jian Liehou. His descendants inherited his title, and Wang Mang later appointed his nephew as Grand Sima.

translation:
The Shaofu set up the curtains, and sent the admonishing doctor to hold the talisman and the visitor to receive the guests to take charge of the funeral. The doctor was responsible for the funeral ceremony.
The Queen Mother also sent visitors to come with talismans in hand to express their condolences.
All the ministers and officials paid their condolences and paid their respects together.
A funeral car and an auxiliary funeral car were used to carry the emperor's Habayashi guards and many Confucian scholars, a total of four hundred people.
There were more than 10,000 funeral vehicles. Everywhere they went, passers-by burst into tears. The crying stopped after the motorcade finished.
Five hundred soldiers were used to dig a hole and lower the coffin, and the tomb was raised, just like the funeral of General Wang Feng.
He was given the title of Jian Liehou.
At first, Kong Guang was granted the title of prime minister, and later he was granted additional titles, with a total of 11,000 households.
When Kong Guang was seriously ill, he wrote a letter to return 7,000 households and the first house given by the emperor.
Kong Guang's son Kong Fang inherited the title.
After Wang Mang usurped the throne, he appointed Kong Yong, the son of Kong Guang's brother, as the Grand Sima and a marquis.
Four or five of my brothers' sons became officials and reached the rank of minister.
At the beginning, Kong Guang's father Kong Ba was granted the title of Guannei Hou Shiyi in the first year of Chuyuan.
Kong Ba wrote a letter requesting that Confucius be enshrined and sacrificed. Emperor Yuan issued an edict saying: My respected master, I commend Kong Ba, the Marquis of Guan Nei, to sacrifice 800 households with the enfeoffed food town. son.
Therefore, Kong Ba moved his eldest son's household registration back to Lu to worship Confucius.
After Kong Ba's death, his son Kong Fu succeeded to the throne.
After Kong Fu died, his son Kong Fang succeeded to the throne.
After Kong Fang died, his son Kong Mang succeeded to the throne.
In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the emperor granted the descendants of Zhou Gong and Confucius the title of marquis, with 2,000 households each.
Kong Mang was later granted the title of Marquis of Baocheng, and was later renamed Kong Jun to avoid Wang Mang's taboo.
Ma Gong, courtesy name Youqing, was born in Qixian County, Shuhai.
After studying Yan's "Spring and Autumn Annals", he was selected as a member of the Jia Division in response to the examination, and served as a minister. He was later promoted to the chief historian of Chu, and was dismissed soon after.
Later he served as Prime Minister Shi Sizhi.
Shi Dan recommended that Ma Gong was of high moral character and was promoted to Ting Weiping. He served successively as the governor of Qingzhou and the prefect of Runan and Jiujiang. He was qualified for official positions and received praise everywhere he went.
Therefore, he was recruited by the emperor as Zhan Shi, Guang Luxun, and General You. He replaced Kong Guang as the chief disciple and was granted the title of Fudehou.
After Kong Guang's death as Grand Master, Ma Gong succeeded Kong Guang as Grand Master and concurrently served as Situ.
During the reign of Emperor Ai, Ma Gong discussed the issue of the title of the emperor's grandmother, the Empress Dowager Fu, with the prime minister and the imperial censor. During the Yuanshi period, Wang Mang moved the tomb of Empress Dowager Fu back to Dingtao, buried it according to common people's etiquette, and investigated the charges against those who had discussed the funeral.
Because Ma Gong had a close friendship with Wang Mang, he was the only one who was not forced to investigate. Ma Gong felt ashamed and frightened, so he wrote a letter to the emperor to confess his guilt and asked to retire.
Wang Mang issued an edict in the name of the Empress Dowager and gave Ma Gong a policy letter saying:
Taishi and Grand Situ Fudehou wrote a letter saying: When I was serving as Guangluxun, I discussed the nickname of the mother of the late Dingtao Gongwang. It was said that a woman should be honored by her husband's title, and the nickname should be Empress Xiaoyuan Fu, and she should be called Weiling Shuyuan.
summary: Ma Gong, courtesy name Youqing, studied Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals and served as a minister. He was promoted to Ting Weiping and served as governor of several provinces, gaining praise. He replaced Kong Guang as chief disciple and was granted the title of Fudehou. After Kong Guang's death, Ma Gong succeeded him as Grand Master and Situ. During the Yuanshi period, Wang Mang investigated those who discussed Empress Dowager Fu's funeral. Because Ma Gong was Wang Mang's friend, he was not investigated, but he felt ashamed and resigned. Wang Mang allowed him to return home. After Wang Mang usurped the throne, Ma Gong became the crown prince's counselor and died in office.

translation:
Wei Qing, courtesy name Zhongqing.
His father, Zheng Ji, was from Pingyang, Hedong Province. He served as a county official and worked as an errand in the Pingyang Hou family.
Pingyang Hou Cao Shou married Princess Yang Xinchang, the sister of Emperor Mowu.
Zheng Ji had an affair with his master's servant Wei Wei and gave birth to Wei Qing.
Wei Qing had an elder brother, Wei Changjun, and an elder sister, Wei Zifu. Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu in Princess Pingyang's family, so Wei Qing assumed the surname Wei.
Wei's eldest daughter is Junru, her second daughter is Shaoer, and her third daughter is Wei Zifu.
Wei Zifu's younger brother Bu Guang took the surname Wei.
Wei Qing was considered a member of Pingyang Hou's family and returned to his father's home when he was a child.
His father made him herd sheep, and his aunt's sons treated him as a slave and were not counted among their brothers.
Wei Qing once followed someone to the prisoner's room in Ganquan Palace. A prisoner who was being tortured came to him and said, "You are a noble person. If you become an official, you can become a marquis."
Wei Qing smiled and said: "A son born from a slave would be very satisfied if he could not be beaten or scolded. How could there be such a good thing as becoming a prince?"
When Wei Qing grew up, he became a knight of the Pingyang Hou family and followed Princess Pingyang.
In the spring of the second year of Jianyuan, Wei Qing's sister Wei Zifu entered the palace and was favored by the emperor.
Queen Chen is the daughter of the eldest princess. She has no son and is jealous of others.
The eldest princess heard that Wei Zifu was favored and was pregnant. She was jealous of her and sent people to arrest Wei Qing.
Wei Qing was working as an errand in Jianzhang Palace at that time and was not yet famous.
The eldest princess caught Wei Qing, imprisoned him, and wanted to kill him.
Wei Qing's friend Qi Lang Gongsun Ao and the warriors went to snatch him out, and Wei Qing avoided death.
When the emperor heard about this, he summoned Wei Qing and asked him to be the eunuch of Jianzhang Palace and serve as a minister.
When his half-brothers became prominent, the rewards amounted to thousands of gold in a few days.
Jun Ru married Grand Servant Sun He as his wife.
Wei Shaoer originally had an affair with Chen Zhang, and the emperor summoned Chen Zhang to make him an official.
Gongsun Ao thus became more prominent.
Wei Zifu became the emperor's wife.
Wei Qing became a doctor in Taizhong.
In the sixth year of Yuanguang, Wei Qing served as the cavalry general and attacked the Xiongnu and sent troops to Shanggu County; Gongsun He served as the light chariot general and left Yunzhong County; Taizhong doctor Gongsun Ao served as the cavalry general and left Dai County; Wei Wei Li Guang served as the Xiaocai general and left Yanmen County.
Each army has one cavalry. Wei Qing marched to Longcheng and annihilated hundreds of enemy troops.
The cavalry general Gongsun Ao lost 7,000 cavalry, and the guard Li Guang was captured alive by the enemy, but fortunately escaped. Both of them were sentenced to death and made atonement by becoming commoners.
Gongsun He also had no military exploits.
Only Wei Qing conferred the title of Marquis of Guannei.
After that, the Huns continued to invade the borders.
The incident is recorded in "The Biography of the Huns".
In the spring of the first year of Yuanshuo, Mrs. Wei gave birth to a son and was made queen.
summary: Wei Qing, courtesy name Zhongqing, was the illegitimate son of Zheng Ji, a county official in Pingyang, and a servant named Wei. He assumed the surname Wei after his sister Wei Zifu gained favor with Emperor Wu. As a youth, Wei Qing herded sheep and was treated poorly by his relatives. A prisoner once prophesied he would become a marquis, but Wei Qing dismissed this, content to avoid beatings. He later became a knight for the Pingyang Hou family. Wei Zifu's entry into the palace and pregnancy provoked jealousy from Empress Chen and her mother, the Grand Princess, who imprisoned Wei Qing. His friend Gongsun Ao rescued him, and the emperor subsequently appointed Wei Qing as a eunuch and minister. His rise brought wealth to his family. In 129 BC, Wei Qing led a cavalry attack on the Xiongnu, reaching Longcheng and killing hundreds. He was made Marquis of Guannei, while other generals faced punishment for failures.

translation:
