In the autumn of this year, Wei Qing led 30,000 cavalry to attack the Xiongnu and sent troops to Yanmen Pass. Li Xi sent troops to replace the county.
Wei Qing annihilated thousands of enemy troops.
The next year, Wei Qing sent troops to Yunzhong County, west to Gaoque, and to Longxi. He annihilated thousands of enemy troops, captured more than a million livestock, and drove away King Aries and King Loufan.
In the Han Dynasty, the Henan area was designated as Shuofang County.
Thirty-eight hundred households were assigned the title of Marquis of Changping to Wei Qing.
Su Jian, a lieutenant under Wei Qing, was granted the title of Pinglinghou, and Zhang Cigong was granted the title of Antouhou.
He sent Su to build Shuofang City.
The Emperor said: The Huns violated the laws of nature, violated human relations, bullied their elders, abused the elderly, took theft as a profession, defrauded barbarians, plotted conspiracies, relied on force, and repeatedly invaded the borders. Therefore, the imperial court sent troops and generals to combat their crimes.
Didn't the "Book of Songs" say, "I attacked the enemy and reached Taiyuan; the chariots rumbled and built a city in the north."
Now the cavalry general Wei Qing crossed the Xihe River to Gaoque, annihilated 2,300 enemy troops, captured their supplies and animals as spoils of war, and was granted the title of lord. Then he marched westward to pacify the Henan area, patrolled the old fortress of Yuxi, crossed Ziling, built a bridge over the Beihe River, leveled Puni, defeated Fuli, killed the elite enemy soldiers, and captured 3,017 soldiers who were hiding in ambushes.
Capture and question the prisoners, know where the enemy is, capture all the soldiers, drive back more than a million horses, cattle and sheep, and return the entire army. An additional 3,800 households were granted the title of Wei Qing Shiyi.
After that, the Xiongnu invaded Daijun, Yanmen, Dingxiang, Shangjun, and Shuofang in successive years, killing and plundering many people.
The incident is recorded in "The Biography of the Huns".
In the spring of the fifth year of Yuan Shuo, the Han Dynasty ordered the cavalry general Wei Qing to lead 30,000 cavalry out of Gaoque. Wei Wei Su Jian served as the guerrilla general, Zuo Nei Shi Li Ju served as the strong crossbow general, Tai servant Gong Sun He served as the cavalry general, and acting Prime Minister Li Cai served as the light chariot general. They were all under the control of the cavalry generals and sent troops to Shuofang.
Daxing ordered Li Xi and Antou Hou Zhang Cigong to serve as generals, and they both sent troops to Beiping County.
King Youxian of the Xiongnu faced Wei Qing and other troops, thinking that the Han army could not reach him, so he got drunk. Han soldiers arrived at night and surrounded King Youxian. King Youxian was frightened and fled overnight. He took only one of his concubines and hundreds of strong cavalry and fled northward through the Han army's encirclement.
The Han Dynasty Qingqi Colonel Guo Cheng and others chased for hundreds of miles, but failed to catch up. They captured more than ten people under King Youxian, more than 15,000 men and women, and tens of millions of livestock. So Wei Qing led his army back.
When the army arrived at the frontier, the emperor sent an envoy to hold the seal of the general, and appointed Wei Qing, the general of chariots and cavalry, as the general in the army. All the generals put their troops under the command of the general, and the general established his official title and returned.
The Emperor said: General Wei Qing personally led his soldiers in the battle and achieved a great victory. He captured more than ten Xiongnu kings and granted 8,700 additional households in Wei Qing's food town.
He also granted Wei Qing's sons Wei and his wife the title of Marquis of Yichun, Wei Busuo as the Marquis of Yin'an, and Wei Deng as the Marquis of Fagan.
Wei Qing resolutely refused and said: I am fortunate to be able to serve in the army. Relying on His Majesty's divine power, our army's great victory is all due to the hard work of all the captains.
summary: In subsequent campaigns, Wei Qing defeated the Xiongnu, capturing livestock and driving out kings. He was granted the title of Marquis of Changping with 3,800 households. The emperor praised his victories, which included pacifying the Henan area and building Shuofang City. Despite continued Xiongnu raids, Wei Qing's successes led to additional rewards.

translation:
Five years later, he followed the general as a school captain and was granted the title of Heqihou.
A year later, he followed the general as a lieutenant general and attacked Dingxiang again, but had no military exploits.
Two years later, as a general, he attacked the Northland and fell behind the hussar general. He wasted the opportunity to fight and should be executed. After atonement, he was made a civilian.
Two years later, he followed the general as a school captain, but without success.
Fourteen years later, he built the surrender city with the post of General Ingan.
Seven years later, he attacked the Huns again as General Yin Gan and arrived at Yuwu. Because the soldiers suffered too many casualties, he was handed over to the officials for trial and executed. He pretended to be dead and ran away, hiding among the people for five or six years.
After being discovered, he was imprisoned again.
Because his wife was implicated in the crime of witchcraft, the family was exterminated.
He served as general four times in total.
Li Ju, a native of Yunzhong, served Emperor Jing.
Seventeen years after Emperor Wu succeeded to the throne, he served as the strong crossbow general with the official position of Zuo Neishi.
A year later, he was appointed General Qiannu.
Zhang Cigong, a native of Hedong, followed the general as a school captain and was granted the title of Antou Marquis.
After the Queen Mother died, he was appointed as a general and garrisoned the Northern Army.
A year later, he followed the general.
He served as general twice, but later broke the law and lost his position.
Zhao Xin was demoted as the Xiongnu Prime Minister and was granted the title of Marquis. In the eighteenth year after Genzao succeeded to the throne, he served as a former general. When he fought with Bao Chu, he was defeated and surrendered to Li Chu.
Zhao Shiqi was a native of Panyue.
In the eighteenth year of Emperor Wu's succession to the throne, he followed the general as a lord and captain and killed 660 enemies.
In the third year of Yuanshou, he was given the title of Marquis of Guannai and a hundred catties of gold.
In the second year, he was appointed as the general on the right. He followed the general to attack and declare the enemy. If he lost his way, he should be beheaded and atone for his sins as a commoner.
Guo Chang, a native of Yunzhong, served as a lieutenant following the general.
In the fourth year of Yuanfeng's reign, Yi Taizhong, a senior official, became General Ba Hu and stationed in Shuofang.
After the troops withdrew, they attacked Kenlong again, but to no avail and took away military power.
Xun Shen was a native of Guangwu, Taiyuan. Because he was good at driving, he served as a servant and served as a lieutenant many times with the general.
In the third year of Wuqian's reign, he was promoted to General Zuo and led his army to attack Huang Dao, but in vain. He was executed for the crime of seizing General Lou Chuan.
General Huo Qubing attacked the Xiongnu six times in total, four of which were with the rank of general, killing and capturing more than 110,000 enemies.
King Hunxie led tens of thousands of people to surrender to the Han Dynasty and opened up the Jiuquan area in Hexi Province. The invasion of the Xiongnu from the west was further reduced.
He was rewarded four times for curing diseases, totaling 17,700 households.
Six of his subordinates, including captains and officers, were awarded the rank of marquis due to meritorious service, and two were promoted to generals.
Lu Bode, a native of Pingzhou, Xihe, served as the governor of Beiping on the right and followed General Hussar, and was granted the title of Marquis of Pili.
After the death of General Hussar, Bode was promoted from the official position of Weiwei to General Fubo. He defeated Zhidian and increased his rewards.
Later, he broke the law and lost his position.
Later, he was appointed Captain of Qiannu, stationed in the camp for a long time, and died in his post.
Bao Nu, a native of Taiyuan.
He once fled to the Xiongnu, and soon returned to the Han Dynasty, where he served as a hussar general and Sima.
He attacked the north and was granted the title of Marquis of Congpiao. He lost his position because he did not have enough gold for the sacrifice.
A year later, he was appointed general of the Xionghe River and attacked the Xiongnu to the water of the Xionghe River, but to no avail.
A year later, he captured King Loulan and was granted the title of Marquis of Zunye.
Six years later, General Junji led an army of 20,000 to attack the Xiongnu Zuo King.
The king of Zuo fought with him and surrounded Zhao Ponu with 80,000 cavalry. Ponu was captured and the entire army was wiped out.
After living in the Xiongnu for ten years, he fled back to the Han Dynasty with his prince Anguo.
Later, he committed the crime of witchcraft and his clan was reduced.
From the rise of the Wei family, the general Wei Qing was first granted the title of marquis, and later five of his descendants became marquises.
Twenty-four years later, all the five princes lost their feudal status.
During the Yanchi period, King Lu failed and Mi Sui perished.
summary: In 124 BC, Wei Qing led a surprise attack on the Xiongnu's Right King, capturing over 15,000 people and millions of livestock. He was promoted to General-in-Chief, and his sons were made marquises. Wei Qing declined the honors, crediting his officers. The emperor then rewarded several subordinates with marquisates.

translation:
So Su Jian was put into a prison car and sent to the emperor's patrol.
This year, Huo Qubing began to become a marquis.
Huo Qubing was the son of General Wei Qing's sister Wei Shaohao.
His father, Huo Zhongru, had an affair with Wei Shao'er and gave birth to Huo Qubing.
When Queen Wei came to her favor, Wei Shaoer married Zhan Shichenzhang.
Huo Qubing was the son of the queen's sister, and he became a servant at the age of eighteen.
Because he was good at horseback riding and archery, he accompanied General Wei Qing on two expeditions against the Huns.
According to the emperor's order, the general assigned him a group of strong soldiers and appointed him as the captain of Piao Yao. He led 800 light cavalry warriors hundreds of miles away from the army led by Wei Qing to win military exploits and kill many enemies.
At this time Emperor Wu said: Huo Qubing, the captain of Piaoyao School, annihilated 2,028 enemies, captured alive the prime minister and the householder, killed Shanyu's grandfather's Jiuruohou Chan, captured Shanyu's uncle Luo Gu and others alive, and won the title of the entire army twice for his merits. He named Huo Qubing the champion with 2,500 households.
Hao Xian, the prefect of Shanggu, went on four expeditions with the general, killing 1,300 enemies, and made him the final profiteer.
The knight Meng Ji also had military exploits and was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, with a title of enfeoffment to 200 households.
In this year, the Han Dynasty lost two troops led by Su Jian and Tan Xin, and Zhao Xin, the Marquis of Xi, surrendered to the Huns. His military achievements were not many, so Wei Qing was not able to increase his title.
The right general Su Jian returned to the court. The emperor did not kill him, but asked him to spend money to atone for his sins and serve the people.
The emperor gave Wei Qing a thousand pieces of gold.
At this time, Mrs. Wang was favored by Emperor Wu. Ning Cheng persuaded Wei Qing: The reason why the general enjoys the title of ten thousand households despite not having great merit, and his three sons are all named marquis, is because of Queen Wei.
Now that Mrs. Wang is favored by the Emperor but her relatives are not wealthy, I hope you can give the daughter of the Emperor to Mrs. Wang's mother as a birthday gift.
So Wei Qing spent five hundred gold to celebrate the birthday of Mrs. Wang's mother.
When Emperor Wu heard about this, he asked Wei Qing. Wei Qing told the truth, and Emperor Wu appointed Ning Cheng as the captain of Shuhai County.
Captain Zhang Qian followed the general Wei Qing on the expedition. Because he had been on an envoy to Daxia and lived among the Xiongnu for a long time, he served as a guide for the troops. He knew where the water and grass were fertile, so the troops did not suffer from hunger and thirst. Because he had served as an envoy to a distant country before and had meritorious service, Emperor Wu named him Bowang Hou.
In the third year after Huo Qubing was granted the title of Marquis, that is, in the spring of the second year of Yuanshou, he was appointed as General of Hussars. He led 10,000 cavalrymen from Longxi to attack the Xiongnu, and achieved great military exploits.
Emperor Wu ordered: General Hussar led his soldiers across Wu Zheng to attack the Xiongnu Yapu tribe. They crossed the Hunu River and passed through five Xiongnu kingdoms. They had a lot of baggage and a large number of people and horses. They gave leniency to those who surrendered and almost captured the son of the Xiongnu Chanyu.
summary: In 123 BC, Wei Qing's campaign saw the defection of former Xiongnu marquis Zhao Xin and the destruction of Su Jian's force. Wei Qing spared Su Jian, sending him to the emperor for judgment. That year, Huo Qubing, Wei Qing's nephew, began his rise, leading a successful raid with 800 cavalry and being made Marquis of Champion.

translation:
After this battle, Chanyu was very angry that King Hunxie was stationed in the west and was defeated by the Han army many times. King Hunxie lost tens of thousands of soldiers, all of which were attacked by the hussar generals. He wanted to summon King Hunxie and kill him.
King Hunxie discussed with King Xiutu and others about surrendering to the Han Dynasty, and sent Han representatives to negotiate on the border in advance.
At this time, the general Li Xi was preparing to build a castle on the bank of the Yellow River. He captured the envoy of King Hunxie and immediately sent someone to report to the emperor in a messenger car.
Emperor Wu was worried that the Huns were pretending to surrender and took the opportunity to sneak attack on the border, so he ordered Huo Qubing to lead his army to greet them.
Huo Qubing's troops crossed the Yellow River and faced King Hunxie's army from a distance. When King Hunxie's subordinates, King Bi and General Bi, saw the Han army, many of them did not want to surrender and fled one after another.
Huo Qubing immediately flew into the Huns camp, met King Hunxie, killed eight thousand people who were trying to escape, and asked King Hunxie to take a post chariot alone to the emperor's patrol residence first, and then led King Hunxie's troops to cross the Yellow River. The number of Huns who surrendered was tens of thousands, said to be one hundred thousand.
When they arrived in Chang'an, the emperor used money and goods as rewards worth hundreds of thousands.
Granted King Hunxie a city of 10,000 households and granted him the title of Marquis of Luo Yin.
His sidekick King Hudu Ni was named the Marquis of Xiamo, Yanzhi was the Marquis of Huiqu, Qinli was the Marquis of Heqi, and Dadang Hudiao was the Marquis of Changle.
At this time, Emperor Wu commended Huo Qubing for his contribution and said: General Huo Qubing led his troops to conquer the Xiongnu. The Hunxie King and his subjects in the western region came to surrender. Qubing aided them with military rations and led more than 10,000 archers to kill the fierce and fierce enemies. He killed more than 8,000 enemies and surrendered 32 foreign kings.
Our soldiers were not injured, but one hundred thousand people surrendered sincerely.
Thanks to the hussar generals' repeated battles, the border areas on the Yellow River were almost free of worries. Use 1,700 households to confer the title of hussar general.
Reduce half of the border guards in Longxi, Beidi, and Shangjun to reduce the corvee burden on the people of the world.
So the surrendered Huns were placed south of the Yellow River outside the pass in the five northwest counties, allowing them to maintain their own customs and habits as vassal states of the Han Dynasty.
Next year, the Xiongnu invaded Youbeiping and Dingxiang counties, killing and plundering more than a thousand Han Dynasty people.
In the second year, Emperor Wu discussed with the generals and said: Xihou Zhao Xin made suggestions for Chanyu and always believed that the soldiers of the Han Dynasty could not easily stop across the desert. Now we send out a large army and we will definitely win.
This year is the fourth year of Yuanshou.
In the spring, Emperor Wu sent General Wei Qing and General Huo Qubing to lead 50,000 cavalry each, followed by hundreds of thousands of infantry and transport troops. Those soldiers who dared to fight to the death and were not afraid of going deep into the enemy's lines belonged to Huo Qubing.
Huo Qubing began to prepare to set off from Dingxiang and directly attack Shan Yu's tribe.
Later, when the prisoners were captured, they said that Chan Yu was in Shumian, so the emperor ordered Huo Qubing to set off from Daijun and Wei Qing to set off from Dingxiang.
summary: Huo Qubing's subsequent campaigns were highly successful, including capturing the Xiongnu's golden statue and defeating the Hunxie King, who surrendered with 100,000 people. Huo Qubing was rewarded with additional households, and the surrendered Xiongnu were settled as vassal states.

translation:
Five thousand eight hundred households were granted the title of Hussar General.
As a subordinate of General Hussar, Lu Bode, the right governor of Beiping, met in Xingcheng. On time, he followed General Hussar to Mount Yu, killing the enemy and capturing 2,800 people. The road was sealed and Bode was named Pi Lihou.
Weishan, the captain of the Northern Territory, followed General Hussar to capture the Xiongnu king alive, and named Weishan the Marquis of Yiyang.
The original Marquis of Guiyi, because King Chun restored Lu Zhi, and King Loupei Yi Jixuan fought with the Hussar General for their meritorious service, restored Lu Zhi as Du Hou, and Yi Jixuan as Zongli Hou.
Zhao Ponu, the Marquis of Piao, and Zhao Anji, the Marquis of Changwu, had followed General Hussar for their military exploits, and were granted three hundred households each.
Both Xie, the prefect of Yuyang, and Li Gan, the captain of the school, captured the enemy's flags and drums and were given the title of Marquis of Guannei. Xie was given a settlement of 200 households, and Li Gan was given a settlement of 200 households.
The school captain Xu Zi was given the title of Zuo Shu Zhang.
The officers and soldiers of Huo Qubing's army received many promotions and rewards.
However, Wei Qing was not granted a title, nor were any of his officers and soldiers.
Only Chang Hui, the governor of Xihe County, and Suicheng, the governor of Yunzhong County, were rewarded. Then he was given the same position as the prime minister of the princes and kingdoms, and was given 200 households in the city and 100 catties of gold. It was given to Chang Huijue as the Marquis of Guannei.
When the two armies of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went to the outside of the Great Wall, the border officials inspected a total of 140,000 official and private horses, but after the war, less than 30,000 horses returned to the Great Wall.
The imperial court set up the position of Grand Sima, making both Wei Qing and Huo Qubing the Grand Sima.
This decree was enacted to make the rank and salary of the hussar general equal to that of the general.
From then on, Wei Qing's power gradually declined while Huo Qubing became more prominent.
Many of Wei Qing's old friends and guests went to seek refuge with Huo Qubing, and most of them received official titles, but Ren An refused to leave.
Huo Qubing was taciturn, courageous and daring to do anything.
Emperor Wu once asked him to learn the art of war from Wu Qi and Sun Wu. He replied: When fighting, you only need to look at strategy, and there is no need to learn ancient art of war.
Emperor Wu built a mansion for him and asked him to check it out. He replied: If the Huns are not eliminated, there will be no home for them.
Therefore, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty paid more attention to and favored him.
However, Huo Qubing had been serving as a servant by the emperor's side since he was very young. He was used to being pampered by nobles and did not care much about the soldiers.
When he led his troops on an expedition, the emperor would send eunuchs to bring him dozens of carts of daily necessities. When he came back, he would throw away the remaining rice and meat, but some of the soldiers would starve.
When fighting outside the Great Wall, the soldiers lacked military rations, and some were so hungry that they could not get up, but Huo Qubing still had to open a field to play football.
There are many such things.
General Wei Qing was a kind man, loved his soldiers, was humble and courteous, and relied on his kindness and meekness to please the emperor, but there was no one in the world who praised him.
Huo Qubing died in the third year after he sent troops in the fourth year of Yuanshou, that is, in the sixth year of Yuanshou.
Emperor Wu was very sad and dispatched soldiers in black clothes from the subordinate countries to line up from Chang'an to Maoling. A tomb was built for him in Mao Cemetery, shaped like Qilian Mountain.
summary: In 119 BC, Wei Qing and Huo Qubing led a massive campaign. Wei Qing defeated the Xiongnu Chanyu but failed to capture him. Huo Qubing's forces killed over 70,000 enemies. Both were made Grand Sima, but Huo Qubing's star rose while Wei Qing's declined. Huo Qubing died in 117 BC, deeply mourned by the emperor.

translation:
He was given the title Mi, combining the two meanings of Wu and Guangdi and called him Marquis Jinghuan.
His son Huo Shan took the title of prince, and Huo Shan was named Zihou. Emperor Wu loved him and hoped that he would become a general when he grew up.
Huo Shen later served as the captain of Fengche and died while accompanying the emperor to offer sacrifices to Mount Tai.
Because Huo Shan had no sons, the feudal state was abolished.
After Huo Qubing's death, Wei Qing's eldest son, the Marquis of Yichun, Wei and his wife, were removed from the title of marquis for breaking the law.
Five years later, the two younger brothers of the Wei couple, the Marquis of Yin'an, Wei Buyi, and the Marquis of Fagan, Weideng, both lost their positions due to insufficient gold sacrifices.
Two years later, the feudal kingdom of champion Hou Huo Qubing cut off his successor.
Four years later, in the fifth year of Yuanfeng's reign, Wei Qing died and Mi was named Liehou.
The eldest son Wei and his wife inherited the title of marquis, but six years later they broke the law and were exempted from the title of marquis.
He died fourteen years after the self-defense Qingwei defeated the Shan. During this period, he did not attack the Xiongnu again because the Han Dynasty had few troops and horses. Ban's ancestors had the same surname as Chu and were descendants of Ling Yin Ziwen.
When Ziwen was born, he was abandoned in a field, and a tiger nursed him.

Ban Ru, the son of Ban Yi.
Ban Ru was praised by people in this state and county for his chivalrous and righteous actions.
Ban Ru's son is the squad leader and the official is the prefect of Shanggu.

Ban Kuang has three sons: Banbo, Banbo and Banzhi.

The general Wang Feng recommended Banbo as a suitable attendant. The emperor summoned Banbo in the banquet hall. He was handsome, recited and preached very well, and he was worshiped as a regular attendant.
At that time, the emperor was keen on studying. Zheng Kuanzhong and Zhang Yu lectured on "Shangshu" and "The Analects of Confucius" in the Jinhua Palace every morning and evening. The emperor Shao ordered Banbo to study.
After understanding the righteousness, he discussed the similarities and differences with Xu Shang and was promoted to the captain of Fengche.
After the end of the year, the lecture activities in Jinhua Palace were suspended, and Ban Bo left the palace to associate with Wang and Xu's descendants. Living among the dandies was not his preference.
Because Ban's ancestral home was originally in the northern border, Ban Bo was born to be generous and generous, and repeatedly requested to be sent as an envoy to the Huns.
During the Heping period, Chanyu came to see him, and the emperor ordered Banbo to greet him at the foot of the fortress with amulets.
It happened that the Shi family and the Li family in Dingxiang area killed people because of their personal grievances, and also killed the officials who were chasing them. Banbo wrote a letter expressing his willingness to be temporarily appointed as the prefect of Dingxiang for a month.
The emperor sent his lieutenant general Wang Shun to come and escort Shanyu in place of Banbo. At the same time, he brought a seal and seal ribbon and appointed Banbo as the prefect of Dingxiang on the spot.
The people in Dingxiang heard that Banbo had always been of high status, was young, and had requested to govern this difficult-to-govern place. They were worried that he would use threats when he first arrived, and both officials and people were afraid of him.
summary: The Ban family, originally sharing the surname of Chu, descended from Ling Yin Ziwen. Ziwen, abandoned as an infant, was nursed by a tiger, leading to his name "Guyugan" from Chu words for nursing and tiger. The tiger was called "Ban," and his son adopted this as their surname. After Qin conquered Chu, the family moved between Jin and Dai, taking Ban as their surname. During the late Qin, Ban Yi fled to Loufan, amassing livestock. In early Han, the Bans dominated border areas with wealth, hunting and living lavishly, with Ban Yi living over a hundred years. Ban Yi's son, Ban Ru, was praised for chivalry. His son, the squad leader, became Shanggu Prefect. Ban Hui, the squad leader's son, became a county magistrate. Ban Kuang, Ban Hui's son, served as a Lang and rose to Captain of Henong, later retiring with wealth to Changling. He had three sons: Banbo, Banbo, and Banzhi. Banbo studied the Book of Songs, was recommended as an attendant, and became a regular attendant. He lectured on classics, was promoted to Fengche Captain, and later requested to govern Dingxiang, where he captured all thieves within ten days. He was summoned back, suffered a stroke, and died at thirty-eight.

translation:
Ban Gu believes that the Tang, Yao, Yu, Shun, Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, as well as the "Book of Songs" and "Shangshu" are related to the classics handed down in the world. Therefore, even in the ancient Yao and Shun period, there must be "Yao Canon". In the era of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the historian Sima Qian recalled the merits of the previous life and privately wrote the Chronicle of the Emperor, ranking the Han Dynasty after the Hundred Kings, in the same row as the Qin Dynasty and Xiang Yu.
Events after the Taichu reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty were not recorded, so I explored the biographies of my predecessors, compiled the materials I could hear, and wrote the "Book of Han". It started from the time of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty and ended with the murders of Xiaoping and Wang Mang, covering a total of twelve generations and 230 years.
The purpose of writing "Deshu" is as follows:
The great Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty inherited Yao's achievements. He was indeed born with virtue, intelligence and martial nature.

Taking advantage of Xiang Yu's return to the east, he sent troops to sweep across the Three Qin Dynasties, seize Guanzhong and pacify the people.
Xiao He and Cao Shen were the assistant ministers, and the country was stabilized. Han Xin and Yingbu were the generals, and Zhang Liang and Chen Ping were the confidants. They respectfully carried out the destiny to punish the evil, created illustrious achievements, and shined the glory for future generations.
So he took the first place in writing "The Chronicles of Emperor Gaozu".
Emperor Xiaohui's reign was not long, and Empress Lu took charge of political affairs without caring about the destiny of the emperor. As a result, the Lu family was destroyed. So he wrote the second "Huidi Ji" and the third "Gaohou Ji".
Taizong was dignified in appearance, honest, respectful and modest. He used himself as an example to educate the people and controlled his ministers with kindness. No tribute will be paid for farming, no sinners will be slaves, no new palaces will be built, and no high tombs will be built in the mausoleum.
The virtue of the monarch is like the blowing wind, and the response of the people is like weeds blowing in the wind. The country is prosperous and strong, and there are few criminals, which makes the Han family prosperous.
So he wrote the fourth chapter of "The Chronicles of Emperor Wen".
After Emperor Xiaojing succeeded to the throne, the princes disobeyed the monarch's orders, but Emperor Jing put down the chaos in the Seven Kingdoms, and the royal family was able to stabilize.
Not slacking off or neglecting government affairs, paying attention to farming and raising silkworms, and promulgating this in important orders, the people can live in peace.
summary: Ban Gu asserts that the Tang, Yao, Yu, Shun, Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties, along with the "Book of Songs" and "Shangshu," are foundational to the classics. He believes ancient sage-kings like Yao and Shun must have had texts like the "Yao Canon" to spread their virtue. The Han Dynasty, inheriting Tang Yao's legacy, saw Sima Qian privately write the "Chronicle of the Emperor," ranking Han after the Hundred Kings. Ban Gu then compiled the "Book of Han," covering 230 years from Emperor Gaozu to the murders of Xiaoping and Wang Mang.

translation:
Yang Chang and Cai Yi obeyed Huo Guang's will, and they were almost all people who were not beneficial to the country.
Zheng Hong only worked on political affairs, while Chen Wannian took care of himself to protect his position.
Chen Xian fell asleep while listening to his father's teachings. Who is the unworthy son?
The thirty-sixth chapter of "The Biography of Gongsun Liu Tian Yang Wang Cai Chen Zheng" was written.
Yang Wangsun was buried naked, and Hu Jian killed the supervisor first according to the law.
Zhu Yun reprimanded Prime Minister Zhang Yu in court, Mei Fu wrote a letter to ridicule General Wang Feng, which can be described as aggressive, while Yun Chang was close to compromise.
Wrote the thirty-seventh biography of Yang Hu and Zhu Meiyun.
Marquis Bolu was a dignified person, and he was ordered by Emperor Wu to assist Emperor Xiaozhao, and Emperor Wu's order was promoted.
When he met a new master, he could not be promoted. He welcomed Emperor Xuan and abolished the king of Changyi, and stabilized the Liu family. He can be called a minister of the country.
Being favored by a generous salary, he gradually changed and concealed his wife's treachery, and his children suffered the disaster of annihilation of their clan and family.
Zhuhou Jinyueyan is the son of King Xiutu of the Xiongnu tribe. He is respectful and loyal, and his virtues will be recorded forever and passed on to future generations.
Wrote the thirty-eighth biography of Huo Guangjin.
The best strategy for a military strategist is to make people surrender without fighting.
The white-haired Marquis of Yingping made great achievements and used the strategy of farming to replace Emperor Xuan's order to go out to conquer the Qiang people, thus gaining the emperor's trust.
Xin Wuxian and his son are known as tiger ministers.
Writing the thirty-ninth biography of Zhao Chongguo and Xin Qingji.
Marquis Yiyang killed King Loulan, Marquis Changluo supported King Kunmi, Marquis Anyuan welcomed King Zhu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty, and Marquis Yicheng killed Zhizhi Shanyu.
Chen Tang was unruly and unruly, but the emperor punished him and Liu Xiang and three other people rescued him. Duan Huizong was diligent in royal affairs and was a hero who was sent to the Western Regions.
The fortieth chapter of "The Biography of Fu Chang, Zheng Gan and Chen Duan" was written.
Jun Buyi was beautiful, smart, able to adapt to situations, and was good at distinguishing between true and false. He refused Huo Guang's proposal to marry her as a daughter, and retired from officialdom.
Shu Guang died a good death and spent his old age happily with his old friends by donating his money.
Yu Dingguo's blessing lies in his kind father.
Xue Guangde, Pingdang, and Peng Xuan were unsatisfied with their positions and were close to knowing their shame.
Wrote the 41st chapter of "The Biography of Jun Shu Yu Xue Ping and Peng".
Sihao of Shangshan escaped from the tyranny of the Qin Dynasty. He was a reclusive person in ancient times. His noble status and wealth could not interfere with his ambitions, and his power could not bend his body. He could be compared with the strict gentleman and Zheng Zhen.
Wang Ji was implicated by Liu He, the king of Changyi, but he emerged from the filth untainted; Gong Yu was old and was able to become an official because of his honest character.
Gong She did not want to hold office and wanted to cultivate himself. Gong Sheng resigned and returned to his hometown and had a good death. Guo Qin and Jiang Xiang almost escaped from the world and had a happy ending.
Wrote the 42nd Biography of Wang Gong and Gong Bao.
summary: Biographies follow, detailing figures from Chen Sheng and Xiang Ji to Han Xin, Zhang Liang, and others. Each biography highlights key events and moral lessons. For example, Zhang Liang's strategies aided the Han, while Xiang Yu's tyranny led to his downfall. The text also covers scholars, cruel officials, knights, and foreign relations, including the Xiongnu and Western Regions.

The Marquis of Le'an was rich in economics and had profound attainments in ancient Chinese classics. He was respected for his position and admired by the people. However, he was immoral during his reign and was impeached by Sili school captains Wang Zun and Wang Jun.
The Marquis of Anchang purchased more property, and Zhu Yun made a fool of himself in the court.

Wrote Chapter 51 of "The Biography of Kuang Zhang and Kong Ma".

The Marquis of Wuyang served the public diligently, tutored the prince, was loyal and resourceful, and advised Cheng Jing to succeed the emperor. He was rewarded with titles and towns for his contribution to the founding of the country.

Zhu Bo's voice was loud and clear when he paid his respects, and the ominous drum sounded first.
Wrote the fifty-third chapter of "The Biography of Xue Xuan and Zhu Bo".
Zhai Fang, Marquis of Gaoling, studied Confucianism and used punishment to increase his authority. The Confucianism and punishment used were both appropriate for the time and his talents could be used by future generations.
Zhai Yi was brave by nature, like a tiger, and marched with his head held high. After the failure of the army, Wang Mang destroyed the Zhai family and exposed his clan members as harmful fish.
Wrote the fifty-fourth biography of Zhai Fangjin.
The Liu family lineage declined, the government was in ruins, and phenomena that foreshadowed disasters such as solar and lunar eclipses occurred many times.
Gu Yong stated the responsibility for the disaster and pointed out that we should be alert on the 210th anniversary of the founding of Han Dynasty.
Du Ye accused the two empress dowagers Ding and Fu of knowing a little about divination.
Writing the fifty-fifth "Biography of Gu Yong Du Ye".
Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping were worried about Ding and Empress Dowager Fu, as well as Wang Mang and Dong Xian.
He Wu and Wang Jia were so sad about it that they both lost their lives.
Gao Lehou Shidan resigned from office, and the three of them were listed as loyal ministers.
Compiled the fifty-sixth chapter of "The Biography of King He Wu Jiashi Dan".
How profound is the knowledge of this school! Rich in ritual, music and literary talent.
At first, he compared himself to Sima Xiangru and submitted poems to the government. Then he pondered deeply, drafted the "Dharma Statement" and wrote the "Tai Xuan Jing", referred to the "Six Classics", imitated the "Book of Changes", imitated the "Analects of Confucius", and concentrated on studying articles, thus becoming famous in the world.
Wrote the fifty-seventh biography of Yang Xiong.
Cruelty and tyranny led to the destruction of Qin and the destruction of the classics of saints. The Han Dynasty preserved the great achievements of saints and classified the Six Classics into different categories.
Analyze and study, clarify the program and disciplines, divide teachers and students into sects, and describe the development and changes. Wrote the fifty-eighth chapter of "The Scholars".
Who is blamed, who is praised, and if there is praise, it can be tried.
summary: The final sections address the rise and fall of imperial relatives, from Empress Gao to Wang Mang, who usurped the Han throne. Ban Gu condemns Wang Mang's tyranny and concludes with a call to examine his evil deeds. The summary emphasizes strict adherence to the text, avoiding external knowledge or inference.

translation:
Sima Xiangru, courtesy name Changqing, was born in Chengdu, Shu County.
When he was young, he loved studying and practiced fencing, so he was named Quanzi.
After Xiangru completed his studies, he admired Lin Xiangru's character and changed his name to Xiangru.
He used family funds to buy a Langguan, serve Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, and served as a regular attendant on martial arts, but this was not his hobby.
It happened that Emperor Jing did not like to write poems. At this time, King Xiao of Liang came to Beijing to see the emperor. Zou Yang from Qijun, Meicheng from Huaiyin, Yan Ji from Wuxian and other lobbyists came to Beijing with him.
When King Xiao of Liang died, Xiangru returned home. He was poor and had nothing to do.
He had always been on good terms with Wang Ji, the magistrate of Linyin County. Wang Ji said: "I have been looking for an official position abroad for many years and have not been very satisfied. You can come to me."
So Xiangru went to Linyin.
Live in a hotel outside the city. The county magistrate of Linyin showed his courtesy and visited Xiangru every day. Xiangru initially received him, but later claimed to be ill and asked his entourage to say goodbye to Wang Ji. Wang Ji became more cautious and respectful.
There were many rich people in Linyin City. Prince Zhuo and his wife had 800 slaves, and Cheng Yin also had several hundred slaves. The two of them called each other, "The county magistrate has a distinguished guest. We must hold a banquet to entertain him."
Also invite the county magistrate.
The county magistrate has arrived, and Zhuo's guests are counted in hundreds. At noon, Sima Changqing was invited. The Changqing said he was ill and could not go. The Linyin County magistrate did not dare to taste the food and went to greet Xiangru in person.
Xiangru has no choice but to do so.
He reluctantly went there, and everyone in the house admired his style. When the wine was in full swing, the Linyin County Magistrate came forward with the piano in his hands and said: "I heard privately that Chang Qing likes this, and hopes to play it to make himself happy."
Xiangru declined and played a tune or two.
At this time, Zhuo Wangsun had a daughter named Wenjun, whose husband had just died. She loved music, so Xiangru pretended to respect the county magistrate and teased her with the sound of the piano.
When Xiangru came to Lingongkou, he was accompanied by carriages and horses, and his behavior was generous and handsome. When he was drinking and playing piano at Huangdi's house, Sai Jun secretly peeked at him from the crack in the door. He was happy and admired him, and was worried that he would not be worthy of him.
After the piano playing was over, Xiangru asked Wenjun's waiter to reward him generously to express his personal feelings to her.
Wenjun escaped from home at night and eloped with Xiangru, so Xiangru and Wenjun drove back to Chengdu in a hurry.
The home is empty except for the four upright walls.
Zhuo Wangsun lost his temper and said: My daughter is extremely incompetent. I can't bear to kill her, but I will never give her a cent!
Some people tried to persuade Wang Sun, but Wang Sun still refused to listen.
After a long time, Wenjun felt unhappy and said: "Changqing just went to Linyin with me, and borrowing money from the brothers was enough to survive. Why did you put yourself in such hardship?"
Xiangru and Wenjun came to Linyin together, sold all the carriages and horses, and bought a hotel to start a wine business. He asked Wenjun to sit in front of the stove and sell wine.
When Zhuo Wangsun heard about it, he thought it was a great shame and humiliation, so he stayed behind closed doors.
summary: Sima Xiangru, courtesy name Changqing, was born in Chengdu, Shu County. As a youth, he studied literature and practiced fencing. After completing his studies, he admired Lin Xiangru's character and changed his name accordingly. He purchased a government position serving Emperor Jing of Han, but found the role unsatisfying. Emperor Jing did not appreciate poetry, so when King Xiao of Liang visited the capital with scholars including Zou Yang and Meicheng, Xiangru associated with them. After King Xiao died, Xiangru returned home impoverished. His friend Wang Ji, magistrate of Linyin County, invited Xiangru to stay. Xiangru lived outside the city, and though the magistrate visited daily, Xiangru eventually claimed illness and refused to see him, which only increased Wang Ji's respect. Wealthy locals Prince Zhuo and Cheng Yin, noticing the magistrate's distinguished guest, arranged a banquet. When invited, Xiangru initially declined, forcing the magistrate to personally fetch him. At the banquet, Xiangru's demeanor impressed everyone. When the magistrate brought out a zither, Xiangru played several tunes. Zhuo Wangsun's daughter Wenjun, recently widowed, loved music. Xiangru used the zither to flirt with her. Wenjun secretly watched him from a doorway, admiring him. After the banquet, Xiangru sent gifts to Wenjun's servant to convey his feelings. Wenjun eloped with Xiangru that night, and they fled to Chengdu, where his home was bare except for four walls. Zhuo Wangsun was furious and refused to give them any money. Eventually, Wenjun persuaded Xiangru to return to Linyin, where they sold their possessions and opened a tavern, with Wenjun serving wine. Ashamed, Zhuo Wangsun was persuaded by relatives to give them a hundred slaves, a million in money, and wedding belongings. They returned to Chengdu, bought land, and became wealthy.

translation:
Brothers and elders took turns to persuade the king and grandson: "You only have one son and two daughters. What you lack is not money."
Now Wenjun has committed himself to Sima Changqing. Changqing was tired of being an official. Although his family was poor, his talents could be relied on. Besides, he was a guest of the county magistrate. Why did he insult each other like this!
Zhuo Wangsun had no choice but to give Wenjun a hundred slaves and one million in money, as well as the clothes, bedding, money and belongings she had used when she got married.
Wenjun and Xiangru returned to Chengdu, bought land and houses, and became rich.
Soon after, Yang Deyi, a native of Shu County, was appointed as a dog prisoner to serve Han Wutong.
Gentong also read "Zixu Fu" and praised it highly, saying: "I just can't be at the same time with this person!"
De proudly said: My fellow countryman Sima Xiangru said that this poem was written by him.
The emperor was shocked and summoned Xiangru to question him.
Xiangru said: There is such a thing.
However, this is about the affairs of princes and is not worth reading. Please allow me to make a gift for the emperor's hunting trip, and I will submit it after the gift is completed.
The emperor agreed to him and asked the minister to give him a writing brush and wooden slips. Xiangru used "Zixu" as empty words to praise the beauty of Chu; "Mr. Wu You" was to challenge Chu for Qi; he died because he was a public servant, but because there was no such person, it was to clarify the principle of being the emperor.
Therefore, three people were fabricated out of thin air and wrote an article to speculate on the scene of the emperor's princes playing and hunting in the garden.
At the end of that article, it boiled down to the word frugality, and I wanted to use this to persuade the emperor.
The emperor was very happy and wrote:
The state of Chu sent Zixu as an envoy to the state of Qi. The king of Qi sent all his chariots and horses to go hunting in the wild with the envoy.
After returning from hunting, Zixu went to visit Mr. Wu You to boast about the incident. At this time, the dead man was also with Zixu.
After everyone was divided into guests and hosts, Mr. Wu You asked: Are you happy hunting in the wild today?
Zixu replied: I am very happy. Did you catch a lot of prey?  not much.
Why are you so happy even though you haven’t gained much?
Zixu replied: I am happy that King Qi originally wanted to show off to me the many chariots and horses of King Qi, but I in turn praised to him the majesty of Yunmengze, the Daze across the Yangtze River in Chu State. Wu You said: Can you tell me?
Zixu said: Of course, the king of Qi personally led thousands of chariots and horses to the seaside for hunting. At that time, the soldiers were scattered in every corner of the grassland, and the snares for catching wild animals were taken down all over the mountains and plains.
The hare crashed into the hunting net, the galloping deer was crushed to death by the wheels, the horned elk was killed by arrows, and the male lin was pulled upside down by one leg.
Thousands of hunting vehicles and horses gallop on the salt flats of the seaside. The blood of hunted birds and beasts stained the wheels red.
After hunting many birds and beasts, King Qi proudly showed off his hunting skills. King Qi turned around and said to me: "Does your Chu State also have such fertile plains and vast grasslands for hunting and entertainment?"
How does your king of Chu's hunting in the wild compare with me?
I jumped out of the car and said to King Qi: "I am the most despicable person in the Chu Kingdom. I have very little knowledge. I have been fortunate enough to be a guard in the palace for more than ten years. I often go hunting with the King of Chu. Most of the hunting grounds are in the back garden. I have been to some places in the garden, but I have never seen some places."
I have never seen the whole of Houyuan, so how can I describe the situation outside Ze?
King Qi said: "Since this is the case, please briefly describe what you have seen and heard!"  I replied: Okay!
summary: Later, Yang Deyi, a native of Shu serving as a dog keeper, praised "Zixu Fu" to Emperor Wu. When the emperor learned Xiangru wrote it, he summoned him. Xiangru confirmed this but offered to compose a hunting rhapsody for the emperor. He created three fictional characters—Zixu, Mr. Wuyou, and a deceased man—to discuss hunting. Zixu boasted of Chu's Yunmeng Marsh, describing its vast mountains, minerals, plants, animals, and the King of Chu's grand hunting expeditions. Mr. Wuyou criticized Zixu for boasting rather than praising virtue. The deceased man then described the emperor's Shanglin Garden, far surpassing anything in Qi or Chu, with its eight rivers, diverse terrain, abundant flora and fauna, and imperial hunts. He concluded by advocating frugality and virtue, warning against excessive luxury. The emperor was pleased and appointed Xiangru as a court gentleman.

translation:
During the few years that Xiangru served as a Langguan, Tang Meng was ordered to open Yelang and Fenzhong in the west, and levied a thousand officials and soldiers from Bajun and Shujun. The county also sent tens of thousands more people to transport grain from land and waterways, and executed the leaders who disobeyed the order according to wartime laws. The people of Bajun and Shujun were greatly frightened.
When the emperor learned of this, he sent Sima Xiangru to blame Tang Meng and others, and took the opportunity to inform the people of Ba and Shu counties that Tang Meng's actions were not the emperor's original intention.
The message said: Inform the governors of Bajun and Shujun that the barbarians do not submit to the jurisdiction of the Han Dynasty and have not attacked them for a long time. They often invaded the border and made the sergeants and generals work hard.
Now that the emperor has ascended the throne, he has taken care of the world and brought peace and stability to China. Then he mobilized troops to attack the Huns in the north. Shanzi was frightened, surrendered, and begged for peace.
Kangju and other countries in the Western Regions sent envoys with generous gifts, tributes, and sacrifices.
The army pointed eastward, and Minyue was pacified. To appease Panyu on the right, the King of Nanyue sent the prince to the court.
The monarch of Nanyi and the commander-in-chief of Xifen often served and contributed to the court, and did not dare to slack off. They hoped to return to Daoyi as soon as possible and wanted to serve the Han family. However, because of the long distance and the obstacles of mountains and rivers, they could not pay their respects in person.
Those who disobeyed have been killed, but those who have done good have not been rewarded, so Zhonglang will be sent to make them submit. Five hundred soldiers each from Bajun and Shujun were recruited to offer gifts and guard the envoys to prevent accidents, so that there would be no war or danger of war.
Now that I heard that there is a plan to raise troops, the young people are frightened, the elderly are worried, and the county is transporting food and supplies without authorization. This is not His Majesty's original intention.
Some of the people who applied for the conscription committed suicide, and some ran away. Recruitment was not the moral character that a subject should have.
When the soldiers in border counties heard that beacons were raised and their accumulated wages were burning, they all took their bows and arrows and galloped forward to the battlefield, carrying their weapons and rushing to the battlefield. They were so tired that they were sweating but still followed closely for fear of falling behind. When fighting, they clash with sharp blades, risk flying arrows, and move forward bravely for the sake of morality without retreating. Everyone is filled with anger, just like seeking personal revenge.
Could it be that they love death and hate life, are not good citizens registered in the household registration, and are they not the same monarch as Bajun and Shujun?
Rather, they plan and think deeply, put the country's danger first, and are willing to fulfill their obligations as subjects!
In the past, some people cut talismans and received rewards, were awarded titles, were promoted to nobles, and lived in high-class residences. When they died, they left noble titles for their descendants and passed them on to their descendants. They were extremely loyal and respectful in their work during their lifetime, and felt very comfortable in their official positions. After their death, their fame lasted endlessly, and their achievements were outstanding and will never be extinguished.
Therefore, wise men and gentlemen will not hesitate to use their liver and brain to smear the Central Plains, and use their flesh and blood to nourish the grass.
Now when the coin envoys have arrived in Nanyi, they kill each other, some escape and are killed, and die without a good reputation. They should be called the most stupid people. The shame involves their parents and they are ridiculed by everyone in the world.
summary: Sima Xiangru served as a Langguan when Tang Meng was ordered to open Yelang and Fenzhong in the west, levying soldiers from Bajun and Shujun and executing leaders who disobeyed, causing great fear among the people. The emperor sent Xiangru to blame Tang Meng and inform the people that these actions were not the emperor's original intent. The message explained that the barbarians had long invaded the border, but the emperor had brought peace to China, attacked the Huns, and pacified Minyue and Nanyue. The recruitment of soldiers was meant to prevent war, not to cause fear. The emperor condemned those who committed suicide or fled from conscription, emphasizing the duty of subjects to serve their country. He also criticized the lack of moral education among the people and their fathers and brothers.

translation:
Isn’t there a huge gap in people’s measurements?
Of course, this is not only the fault of those who applied for the draft, but also because their fathers and brothers were not strict in their education and did not set an example for their children. The people had no moral integrity and were shameless, and the customs were not honest.
Isn’t it right for some of them to be killed?
Today, the emperor is worried that the envoys and officials will be like this, as are the sad and unworthy ignorant people. Therefore, he sends honest envoys to clearly inform the people about the recruitment of soldiers. He takes this opportunity to rebuke the fools who are disloyal and escape and commit suicide, and blames the three elders and filial brothers who are in charge of education for not teaching.
It was the farming season, and I was particularly careful not to bother the people. I had already personally informed the people in the nearby counties. I was worried that the people in the remote areas and in the valleys and mountains would not be widely heard. When the message arrived, I quickly distributed it to all counties and provinces to generally inform the emperor of his thoughts, hoping that they would not be ignored.
Xiangru returns the report.
Tang Meng had already opened up Yelang, and took advantage of this to open the road to the southwestern Yi. He recruited soldiers from the three counties of Ba, Shu, and Guanghan, and tens of thousands of them worked.
It took two years to build the road, but it was not completed. Most of the soldiers died, and the money spent was calculated in hundreds of millions.
Most people in Shu County and those in power in the Han Dynasty said that it was not good for the country.
At that time, the commanders of Yinyi and Zha heard that Nanyi had interacted with the Han Dynasty and received many rewards. Most of them were willing to become vassals of the Han Dynasty and requested that they be given officials so that they could be treated the same as Nanyi.
The emperor asked about Wing Kou, and Nuojia said: The Yi tribes of Yin, Jia, Ran and Xiao are close to Shu County, and the roads are easy to open. During the Qin Dynasty, they were opened and set up as counties and counties, but they were abandoned after the establishment of the Han Dynasty.
Now if it is opened again and counties are set up, it will be better than Nanyi.
The emperor thought it was right, so he worshiped Xiangru as Zhonglang General and sent envoys to Xiyi with integrity.
The deputy envoys were Wang Ranyu, Hu Chongguo, and Lu Yue, driving four chariots. They planned to rely on the officials and property of Ba and Shu counties to win over and bribe the southwestern barbarians.
When they arrived at Shu County, the prefect of Shu County and his officials came to greet him on the outskirts. The county magistrate personally led the way with bows and arrows on his back. The people of Shu County were proud of this.
So Zhuo Wangsun and the elders of Linyin all became Xiangru's disciples through their marriage relationships, and offered beef and wine to please Xiangru.
Zhuo Wangsun sighed deeply, thinking that it was too late for his daughter to marry Sima Changqing, so he distributed generous property to his daughter equally with his son.
Sima Changqing sent people to pacify the southwestern barbarians, and the princes of Yin, Zha, Ran, Qo and Siyu all asked to submit to the Han Dynasty. So the old passes were demolished, and the new passes were expanded outwards, reaching Keshui and Ruoshui in the west and the border of Yangge in the south. Lingshan Road was opened and a bridge was built on Sunshui River to connect Gongkou and Zhao.
The emperor was very happy when he returned the report.
When Xiangru was sent as an envoy, most of the senior people in Shu County said that opening up the southwestern barbarians was of no use, and some ministers also thought so.
Xiangru wanted to admonish the emperor, but he remembered that he had already made suggestions and did not dare to deviate from the preface, so he wrote an article and used the form of a conversation with the elders of Shu County to question the other party and use it to satirize the emperor. He also announced his decree to let the people know the emperor's mind.
His article said:
In the seventy-eight years since the rise of the Han Dynasty, the benevolence and virtues have been flourishing for six generations. They are mighty and majestic, and their benevolence is profound and wide, benefiting all living beings and filling China and foreign countries.
So he sent envoys to march westward, and the barbarians retreated along the current. Wherever the king's wind covered them, everything collapsed with the wind.
So Ran Yi came to court, Ji Yi obeyed, pacified the capital of Jiao, and the capital of Pingsuo, occupied Siyu, captured Baopu, and drove back and forth with horses and horses to report to the court and drive to the capital of Shu.
Twenty-seven people, including elderly and high-ranking officials in the local area, solemnly went to pay homage to the envoy.
After greetings, we went to Xiju: I heard that the emperor's principle in dealing with the Yi and Di was to contain them and prevent them from severing relations.
Now we have tired the soldiers in the three counties and opened the road to Yelang. It has been three years since the success was achieved. The soldiers are tired and tired, and the people's supplies cannot be satisfied. Now we are opening the road to Xiyi. The people are exhausted, and I am afraid that we will not be able to complete this task. It is also a burden to the envoy. I am worried about you privately.
Moreover, Yin, Zha, and Xijia are juxtaposed with the Central Plains. They have experienced so many years that I can’t remember them clearly.
Since ancient times, emperors, despite their benevolence and virtue, could not be recruited, and although they were powerful, they could not be conquered. I am afraid that this was impossible because the road was difficult, dangerous and far away!
Nowadays, the property of the people who are divided into households is divided to make the barbarians rich, and the common people who the emperor relies on are exhausted and useless land is opened up. We are short-sighted and do not know whether what we are saying is right or wrong?
The messenger said: Why do you say this?
If it is like what you said, it means that the people of Ba and Shu do not need to change their original clothing customs similar to those of the Yi and Di.
summary: Xiangru returned to report. Tang Meng had opened Yelang and recruited tens of thousands of soldiers from Ba, Shu, and Guanghan to build a road, which took two years and cost hundreds of millions, with many soldiers dying. Many in Shu and the Han court opposed this. The commanders of Yinyi and Zha, seeing Nanyi's rewards, wished to become Han vassals. The emperor consulted Nuojia, who noted that the Yi tribes near Shu had been opened during Qin but abandoned after Han. The emperor agreed to reopen them, appointing Xiangru as Zhonglang General to pacify the southwestern barbarians. Xiangru used officials and property from Ba and Shu to bribe the barbarians, and the people of Shu were proud of his mission. Zhuo Wangsun, Xiangru's father-in-law, distributed property equally to his daughter. Xiangru pacified the barbarians, who submitted to Han, and the emperor was pleased. However, many in Shu and some ministers opposed opening the southwestern barbarians. Xiangru wrote an article to admonish the emperor, using a conversation with the elders of Shu to question their views. He argued that the Han dynasty's virtues were vast, and the barbarians should be brought under control. He criticized the elders for their shortsightedness, comparing the emperor's efforts to those of Xia Yu in controlling floods. He emphasized that the emperor's goal was to extend benevolence and stop conquest, and that the people's labor was justified for such a grand cause. The elders eventually agreed with him. After Xiangru's death, the emperor sent for his writings but found none. His wife said he often wrote but had no books left. Xiangru had left a letter about Fengshan, which the emperor found strange. The letter discussed ancient monarchs and the importance of Fengshan rituals, arguing that the Han dynasty's virtues surpassed those of Zhou and that the emperor should perform the rituals. The emperor eventually performed the Fengshan ceremony eight years after Xiangru's death.

translation:
Envoys were sent in all directions to proclaim benevolence, and the princes of the Western Yi and Southwestern Yi regions were like fish gathering in the upper reaches of the river. Hundreds of millions of them hoped to receive titles.
Therefore, the Nianshui and Ruoshui are used as pass, Panggu is used as the border, the road to Nangshan is dredged, a bridge is built at the source of Sun River, a path of morality is opened, and the tradition of benevolence and righteousness is spread. It will extend favor widely, appease and control distant places, so that the alienated are not closed, and light shines in the dark, so as to calm the war here and stop the conquest there.
Isn't it also happiness to be united near and far, and to be healthy at home and abroad?
It is the emperor's top priority to save the people from dire straits, respect the emperor's virtues, reverse the decline of the last days, and inherit the cause of the founding monarch of the Zhou Dynasty.
Although the people are working hard, how can they stop?
Moreover, the career of an emperor originally started with sorrow and ended with happiness.
If this is the case, then all the signs of destiny are here.

translation:
Confucianism is broad but lacks essentials, and it takes a lot of effort but has little effect. Therefore, it is difficult to fully implement what it advocates. However, the etiquette between monarch, minister, father and son, and the distinction between husband and wife, elder and younger, which it stipulates cannot be changed.
Mohism advocates frugality but it is difficult to follow it, so all the things Mohism advocates cannot be adopted. However, the Mohist ideas on strengthening the development of the industry and practicing economy cannot be discarded.
Legalism's ideas are harsh and harsh and lack kindness. However, the fact that they uphold the status of emperor and ministers cannot be changed.
Famous scholars are too rigid in their formality and easily lose their correct understanding of things. However, the dialectical relationship between name and reality cannot but be seriously considered.
Taoism unites people's spirit and actions in line with the invisible Tao, making all things abundant and perfect.
Their doctrine follows the order of Yin and Yang in the four seasons, absorbs the strengths of Confucianism and Mohism, and takes the essence of Ming and Dharma. It transfers with time and changes with things. In this way, there is nothing inappropriate in establishing routines and handling affairs. The purpose is concise and easy to grasp. Although they do not do many things, they are very effective.
This is not the case with Confucians. They believe that the monarch is the model for the world. In everything, the monarch initiates and his subordinates respond. The monarch takes the lead and his subordinates follow.
Like this, the monarch is tired and his subjects are at ease.
As for the essence of the great Taoist theory, it not only removes strongness and greed, but also abolishes intelligence and wisdom. Confucianism abandoned these and allowed Confucianism to govern.
If the spirit is overused, it will be exhausted, and if the body is overworked, it will be damaged; if the spirit and body are prematurely exhausted, it has never been heard of to be with the heaven and the earth for a long time.
The Yin and Yang theory has its own rules and taboos for the four seasons of the year, the Bagua directions, the twelve stars, and the twenty-four solar terms. It is said that if you follow these, you will prosper, and if you violate them, you will perish. In fact, this is not necessarily the case, so it makes people restricted and creates a lot of fear.
As for spring birth, summer growth, autumn harvest, and winter storage, these are the laws of nature. If you don't follow them, there will be no laws for the world.
Therefore, the running sequence of the four seasons of the year stipulated by it cannot be discarded.
Confucianism uses the Six Arts as its criterion. There are tens of millions of scriptures on the Six Arts. People cannot understand its doctrines for several generations, and they cannot fully understand its etiquette in a lifetime.
Therefore, Confucianism is broad but lacks essentials, and it takes a lot of effort but has little effect.
As for the Confucian etiquette between monarch, minister, father and son, and the distinction between husband and wife, elder and younger, these cannot be changed by any school of thought.
The Mohists also admired Yao and Shun, praising the virtues of Yao and Shun and saying: They lived in three-foot-high halls with three-story earthen steps. Their thatched roofs were not trimmed, and their oak rafters were not decorated. They used pottery gui for rice and earthen basins for soup. They ate brown rice and drank bean leaf soup. They wore kudzu clothes in summer and deer skins in winter.
They bury their dead in coffins made of three-inch thin paulownia boards, and their cries are not sad.
Educating people to follow funeral rituals must be based on this standard.
If the world were to be like this, then there would be no distinction between high and low.
The world is different, times have changed, and careers do not have to be the same, so it is difficult for people to follow the frugality advocated by Mohism.
In short, Mohism advocates emphasizing local use, which is a way to guide the family to become rich and the people to be prosperous.
It can be used as a temporary measure, but not for long-term use.
Therefore, the preacher is harsh and harsh but lacks kindness. As for the Legalist idea of ​​making the king noble and his ministers humble, and clarifying the boundaries of duties that cannot be crossed, this cannot be changed by any school of thought.
Famous names are so trivial and confusing that people cannot deduce its true meaning. They focus on the reasoning of noun concepts and lose the common sense that is easy to grasp. Therefore, it is said that famous scholars make people constrained and easily lose their correct understanding of things.
As for the fact that it follows the name and fulfills its duties and comprehensively examines the essence of things, it must be seriously considered.
Taoism advocates inaction and does everything. Its actual proposition is easy to implement, but its words are difficult to understand.
Its doctrine takes nothingness as its theoretical basis and conformity to nature as its practical principle.
There is neither an established trend nor a fixed form, so we can ascertain the true nature of all things.
summary: Sima Tan studied astronomy, the Book of Changes, and Taoism, and served under Emperor Wu of Han. He worried that scholars misunderstood the six schools of thought—Yin-Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Legalism, Mingjia, and Taoism—and discussed their principles. He noted that Yin-Yang had many taboos but its seasonal order was useful; Confucianism was broad but lacked essentials, though its rituals were important; Mohism was frugal but hard to follow, yet its emphasis on economy was valuable; Legalism was harsh but upheld the ruler-minister distinction; Mingjia was too formal but its name-reality dialectic was worth considering; and Taoism united spirit and action, absorbed strengths of other schools, and was concise and effective. He criticized Confucianism for tiring the ruler and praised Taoism for its simplicity and adaptability.
