Emperor Gaozu became the king of Han, and in the first year he granted Duke Lu the title of Marquis of Linsi. In the second year, he made Emperor Xiaohui the crown prince.
Later, the king of Han married Qi Ji of Dingtao and loved her very much. Qi Ji gave birth to King Ruyi of Zhao Yin.
The prince was kind and cowardly. Emperor Gaozu thought that he was not like himself, so he often planned to abolish the prince and replace him with Ruyi, saying that Ruyi was like me.
Qi Ji often followed the emperor on expeditions to Guandong, crying day and night, hoping to make her son the crown prince.
As Queen Lu was getting older, she often stayed in Guanzhong and rarely saw the emperor, so she became even more alienated.
Ruyi was named King of Zhao and lived in Chang'an. He was almost made a prince several times.
Fortunately, the ministers strongly opposed it. When Shusun Tong came to remonstrate, he adopted the strategy of staying in the marquis, so the prince was not replaced.
Empress Lu was a resolute person and assisted Gaozu in bringing peace to the world. Her two brothers were both generals and fought with Gaozu.
The eldest brother Lu Ze was granted the title of Marquis of Zhou Lu, and the second brother Lu Shizhi was granted the title of Marquis of Jiancheng. By the time Gaozu proclaimed himself emperor, three people in the Lu family had been granted the title of marquis.
In the fourth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Duke Lu, the Marquis of Linsi, passed away.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, Emperor Hui ascended the throne, and Empress Lu became the empress dowager, she ordered Mrs. Qi to be imprisoned in Yongxiang. Her hair was shaved, an iron ring was tied around her neck, she was put on the red clothes of a prisoner, and she was asked to do hard labor by pounding rice.
Mrs. Qi sang a song while pounding rice: The son is a king, the mother is a slave, pounding rice all day long, often accompanied by death!
Three thousand miles apart, who can tell you?
Queen Mother Lu was furious when she heard about it and said: Do you still want to rely on your son?
He summoned King Zhao to Chang'an and planned to kill him.
The envoy went back and forth three times, but Zhou Chang, the Prime Minister of Zhao, refused to let King Zhao go.
The Queen Mother summoned Prime Minister Zhao and summoned him to Chang'an.
Then he sent someone to summon King Zhao, and King Zhao came.
Emperor Hui was kind by nature and knew that the Queen Mother hated King Zhao, so he went to Ba Shang to greet King Zhao in person, and they entered the palace together, eating and living in the same place.
A few months later, Emperor Hui went out to hunt in the morning, but King Zhao did not get up early. The Queen Mother sent someone to give him poisoned wine while he was sleeping.
When Emperor Hui came back, King Zhao was already dead.
The Queen Mother cut off Mrs. Qi's hands and feet, gouged out her eyes, smoked her deaf ears, drank dumb medicine, and threw her in a cave to wrap her up, calling her a "human pig."
A few months later, Emperor Hui was called to see the pigs.
When Huitong saw and asked, he realized that this was Mrs. Qi, and he burst into tears. From then on, he became ill and did not recover for more than a year.
summary: Empress Lu of Emperor Gaozu was the daughter of Lu Gong, who married her to Gaozu when he was poor, seeing him as extraordinary. She gave birth to Emperor Hui and Princess Lu Yuan. Gaozu became king of Han and made Lu Gong the Marquis of Linsi. He later married Qi Ji of Dingtao, who gave birth to King Ruyi of Zhao. Gaozu wanted to replace the kind-hearted prince with Ruyi, but ministers opposed it. Empress Lu, resolute and assisting Gaozu, had brothers Lu Ze and Lu Shizhi as generals. After Gaozu's death, Empress Dowager Lu imprisoned Qi Ji, shaved her hair, and made her pound rice. Qi Ji sang about her son being a king and she a slave, angering the Queen Mother, who summoned King Zhao to Chang'an. Emperor Hui protected him, but the Queen Mother poisoned King Zhao. She then mutilated Qi Ji, calling her a "human pig." Emperor Hui, horrified, fell ill and died seven years later. The Queen Mother, advised by Zhang Piqiang, appointed Lu Tai and Lu Chan as generals, consolidating Lu family power. She killed several of Gaozu's sons and named Lu family members kings. After her death, ministers Zhou Bo and Chen Ping executed the Lu family and established Dai Wang as Emperor Xiaowen.

translation:
The Queen Mother issued an edict to depose him, and this incident was recorded in the "Gaohou Ji".
The young emperor was imprisoned and died. The Queen Mother changed the name of Hengshan King Liu Hong to the emperor and made Lu Lu's daughter the queen, hoping to fundamentally consolidate the Lu family's status, but these did not have much effect.
After the death of Empress Dowager Lu, the ministers brought order to the chaos and finally annihilated the Lu family.
The young emperor Hengshan King, Huainan King, and Jichuan King were all killed because they were not the biological sons of Emperor Xiaohui.
Only Queen Xiaohui remained, and her title of queen was abolished, and she lived in the North Palace. In the first year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Queen Xiaohui died and was buried in Anling without building a mausoleum.
Gaozu's Bo Ji was the mother of Emperor Wen.
Bo Ji's father was from Wu. During the Qin Dynasty, he had an affair with Wei Lao, a woman from the original clan of the King of Wei. Give birth to Bo Ji.
Bo Ji's father died in Shanyin and was buried there.
When the princes rebelled against the Qin Dynasty, Wei Bao proclaimed himself king, and Wei Yu sent her daughter to the Wei palace.
Xu Fu met Bo Ji and said that she could give birth to the emperor.
At this time, Xiang Yu was confronting the King of Han in Rongyang, and the world was not yet peaceful.
Wei Bao initially attacked Chu with Mo. After hearing Xu Negi's words, he was overjoyed, betrayed Han, implemented neutrality, and made friends with Chu.
The king of Han sent Cao Shen and others to capture King Bao of Wei and set his territory as a county, while Bo Ji was sent to the weaving room.
After Wei Bao's death, the King of Han entered the weaving room and saw Bo Ji, so he issued an edict to include her in the harem. However, he did not receive the emperor's favor for more than a year.
When Bo Ji was young, she was very close to Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier, and she swore: Whoever gets the honor first, don't forget the others!
Soon Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier were the first to be favored by the King of Han.
In the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, when he was visiting Lingtai in Chenggao, Henan, these two beauties stood aside and laughed at Bo Ji's alliance with them.
The king of Han asked about the reason, and the two men told him the truth.
The King of Han felt pity for Bo Ji, so he summoned her that day and planned to protect her.
Bo Ji said to the King of Han: Last night, I dreamed of a dragon coiled on my chest.
The King of Han said: This is a sign of your honor. I will help you achieve it.
Fortunately, Bo Ji became pregnant.
Emperor Wen was born in this year and was made king at the age of eight.
Since Bo Ji gave birth to her son, she rarely saw the emperor.
After the death of Emperor Gaozu, those favored concubines such as Mrs. Qi were hated by Empress Lu and were imprisoned and unable to leave the palace.
Because Bo Ji was rarely summoned by the emperor, she was able to follow her son to Dai and became the Queen Mother of Dai.
Bo Zhao, the younger brother of the Queen Mother Dai, also followed to the Kingdom of Dai.
In the seventeenth year of the reign of King Dai, Empress Dowager Lu died.
The ministers discussed the establishment of a new emperor. They hated the tyranny of their relative, Lu, and praised Bo for her kindness and kindness. Therefore, they welcomed King Dai as the emperor, honored the Queen Mother Dai as the Queen Mother, and named Bo Zhao, the Queen Mother's younger brother, Zhihou.
summary: Empress Zhang of Emperor Xiaohui was the daughter of Zhang Ao and Princess Lu Yuan. Empress Dowager Lu married her to Emperor Hui, hoping for a son. When she had none, the Queen Mother pretended she was pregnant and passed off a beauty's son as hers, killing the mother. After Emperor Hui's death, the prince became emperor but learned the truth and threatened revenge. The Queen Mother imprisoned and deposed him, then made Hengshan King Liu Hong emperor. After her death, ministers killed the Lu family and the non-biological sons of Emperor Hui, leaving only Queen Xiaohui, who died in the first year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign. Gaozu's Bo Ji was the mother of Emperor Wen. Her father had an affair with Wei Lao, giving birth to Bo Ji. During the Qin Dynasty, Wei Bao proclaimed himself king, and Bo Ji entered his palace. Xu Fu predicted she would give birth to an emperor. Wei Bao betrayed Han, was captured, and Bo Ji was sent to the weaving room. Gaozu saw her and included her in the harem but did not favor her for over a year. She was close to Mrs. Guan and Zhao Zier, who later laughed at her alliance. Gaozu pitied her, summoned her, and she became pregnant, giving birth to Emperor Wen. After Gaozu's death, Bo Ji, rarely favored, followed her son to Dai and became Queen Mother Dai. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, ministers, hating the Lu family, praised Bo Ji's kindness and made King Dai emperor. Bo Ji became Empress Dowager, and her brother Bo Zhao was named Zhihou. She died in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign and was buried in Nanling.

translation:
One evening at dusk, more than a hundred people were sleeping on the edge of the cliff. The cliff suddenly collapsed and everyone sleeping on the edge of the cliff was crushed to death. Only Shaojun survived.
He divined for himself, and the divination showed that he would become a prince in a few days.
He followed his master to Chang'an and heard that the newly canonized queen was originally from Guanjin and her surname was Bao.
Although Guangguo was young when he left home, he still remembered his place of origin and surname. He also remembered that he and his sister once went to pick mulberry leaves and fell from the tree. He used these things as evidence and wrote a letter describing his life experience.
Empress Dou told Emperor Wen these things, and then summoned Guang Guo for questioning. He told the whole story in detail, and it turned out to be true.
Asked about some past events he still remembered, he said: When my sister left me to go west, she said goodbye to me at the inn, asked for rice juice to wash my hair, and then gave me a meal before leaving.
So Queen Dou held his hand and cried loudly, and the waiters on the left and right also became sad.
He rewarded Guang Guo heavily and allowed him to live in Chang'an.
Jianghou Zhou Bo, General Guan Ying and others said: If we people do not die, our lives will be in the hands of these two people.
They were from a humble background and had to choose a good mentor for them, lest they follow the old example of the Lu family again.
Therefore, virtuous elders were selected to live with them.
From then on, Dou Changjun and Dou Shaojun became humble and courteous gentlemen, who did not dare to be arrogant because of their high status.
Queen Dou later became ill and became blind.
Emperor Wen also favored Mrs. Handan Shen and Yin Ji, but they had no sons.
After Emperor Wen passed away and Emperor Jing ascended the throne, Empress Bao became the Empress Dowager and granted Dou Guangguo the title of Marquis Zhangwu.
Dou Changjun died early and named his son Dou Pengzu the Marquis of Nanpi.
When Wu, Chu and other seven countries rebelled, Dou Ying, the cousin of the Queen Mother, was chivalrous and brave, and liked to make friends with scholars. He was appointed as a general. After the Wu and Chu rebellions were suppressed, he was named Wei Qihou.
There are three people in the Dou family who have been granted the title of Marquis.
Empress Dowager Dou liked the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi. Emperor Jing and the Dou family had to read "Laozi" and admire Huang and Laozi's techniques.
Empress Dowager Dou died six years after Emperor Jing's death, fifty-one years after she was established as queen, that is, in the sixth year of Yuanguang, and was buried in Ba Ling with Emperor Wen.
According to his instructions, Shao rewarded the eldest princess Liu Prostitute with all the gold and silver belongings in Shu Palace.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Wei Qihou Dou Ying became prime minister and was later killed.
Emperor Xiaojing and Empress Bo were the daughters of Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Bo.
When Emperor Jing was the crown prince, Empress Dowager Bo married Bo as the crown prince for him.
After Emperor Jing ascended the throne, he made Concubine Bo the queen. Empress Bo had no sons and was not favored by Emperor Jing.
Bo served as queen for six years, but after the death of Empress Dowager Bo, she was deposed.
Empress Bo died in the fourth year after she was deposed and was buried south of Shupingwang Pavilion in Chang'an City.
Empress Xiaojing was the mother of Emperor Wu.
Queen Wang's father is Wang Zhong, who is from Huaili.
summary: Empress Xiaowen Dou was the mother of Emperor Jing. She was elected to the palace during Empress Dowager Lu's reign. When maids were sent to princes, she wanted to go to Zhao but was mistakenly sent to Dai. In Dai, King Dai favored her, and she gave birth to Emperor Jing. After King Dai became emperor, Dou Ji was made queen. Her brother Dou Guang, sold as a child, was later found and rewarded. Dou Changjun and Dou Shaojun became humble gentlemen. Queen Dou later became blind. After Emperor Wen's death, she became Empress Dowager and granted Dou Guang the title of Marquis Zhangwu. During the rebellion of the seven states, Dou Ying was made a general and later Marquis Weiqi. Empress Dowager Dou liked Huang-Lao teachings and died in the sixth year of Yuanguang, buried with Emperor Wen. Emperor Xiaojing and Empress Bo were the daughters of Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Bo. Empress Dowager Bo married her to Emperor Jing as crown prince. After becoming emperor, he made her queen, but she had no sons and was not favored. After Empress Dowager Bo's death, she was deposed and died four years later.

translation:
The mother's name is Zang'er, the granddaughter of Zang Tu, the original king of Yan. She married Wang Zhong and gave birth to a son, Wang Xin, and two daughters.
After Wang Zhong died, Zang'er remarried to the Tian family in Changling and gave birth to sons Tian Pan and Tian Sheng.
Zang'er's eldest daughter married Jin Wangsun and gave birth to a daughter. However, Zang'er divined and found that both daughters were destined to be rich and noble. He hoped to gain respect and favor through his two daughters, so he divorced his daughter from the Jin family.
The Jin family was furious and refused to give up, so Zang'er sent his daughter to the crown prince's womb.
The prince loved Mrs. Wang very much, and she gave birth to three daughters and a son.
When Mrs. Wang was pregnant with her son, she dreamed of a sun rising into her belly, so she told the prince about it. The prince said: This is a sign of noble status.
Before the child was born, Emperor Wen passed away and after Emperor Jing came to the throne, Mrs. Wang gave birth to a son.
At this time, Queen Bo did not have any children.
A few years later, Emperor Jing appointed Qi Liji's son as the prince, and the son of the king's wife as the king of mice.
The eldest princess Liu had a daughter who planned to marry the prince as a concubine, but Li Ji was jealous by nature, and the beauties in Emperor Jing's harem often relied on the eldest princess's efforts to gain favor from the emperor. Li Ji became more and more resentful of the eldest princess, so she rejected the eldest princess and did not agree.
The eldest princess wanted to marry her daughter to Mrs. Wang's son, but Mrs. Wang agreed.
At this time, Queen Bo was deposed, and the eldest princess spoke ill of Li Ji in front of Emperor Jing every day.
Emperor Jing once entrusted Li Ji with the princes born to his wives, saying: After I die, you must take good care of them.
Li Ji was very angry, refused to agree, and spoke rudely. Emperor Jing was very dissatisfied, but he did not show it.
The eldest princess praised Mrs. Wang's son every day, and Emperor Jing himself thought the child was talented.
Coupled with the auspicious news that the child was born in a dream, Emperor Jing thought about it over and over again and could not make up his mind.
Mrs. Wang secretly sent people to urge the ministers to propose canonizing Li Ji as queen.
Daxing wrote a letter to commemorate the matter, and one sentence said: A son is more valuable than his mother, and a mother is more valuable than his son. Now the title of the prince's mother should be the queen.
Emperor Jing was furious and said: Is this what you should say?
So he went to Shao and killed Daxing, deposed the prince and changed his title to King Linjiang.
Li Ji was even more angry and could not be summoned by the emperor, so she died of fear.
Finally, Mrs. Wang was appointed queen, and Mrs. Wang's son became the prince.
He also made Wang Xin, the brother of Queen Wang, the Marquis of Gai.
At first, the queen had just entered the crown prince's womb, and later her sister Ergu was also brought in and gave birth to four sons.
Erku died very early, and all four sons became kings.
The queen's eldest daughter was named Princess Pingyang, her second daughter was named Princess Nangong, and her third daughter was named Princess Longlu.
In the ninth year after Queen Wang was enthroned, Emperor Jing died.
summary: Empress Xiaojing Wang was the mother of Emperor Wu. Her father Wang Zhong died, and her mother Zang'er remarried. Zang'er, divining that her daughters would be noble, sent her eldest daughter to the crown prince's womb. Mrs. Wang dreamed of a sun entering her belly, giving birth to a son. After Emperor Jing became emperor, Mrs. Wang's son became prince. The eldest princess Liu Piao wanted to marry her daughter to the prince, but Li Ji refused. The princess then spoke ill of Li Ji and praised Mrs. Wang's son. Emperor Jing deposed the prince and made Mrs. Wang queen. Her son became Emperor Wu. Empress Dowager Wang reigned for twenty-five years and died in the third year of Yuanshuo, buried with Emperor Jing.

translation:
When Emperor Wu came to the throne and Queen Wang became the empress dowager, he honored his mother Zang'er as Lord of Pingyuan, Tian Pan as Marquis of Wu'an, and Tian Sheng as Marquis of Zhou Yang.
There are three people in the Wang and Tian families who have been granted the title of marquis.
Gaihou Wang Xin likes to drink, while Tian Xi and Tian Sheng are greedy and good at eloquence.
Tian Jin's officials continued to be prime ministers, and he honored Wang Zhong as a co-marquis. He set up a cemetery and 200 households in Huaili, and set up a garden director and a garden chief to guard the sacrifices.
After Lord Pingyuan passed away, he was buried with the Tian family in Changling, and a garden was also set up. The specifications and ceremonies were the same as those of Gonghou.
At the beginning, when the Empress Dowager was humble, she gave the name of the daughter she gave birth to to King Jin's grandson, because among the people, she did not want anyone to know.
When Emperor Wu first came to the throne, Han Yan told him about the incident.
Emperor Wu said: Why didn't you tell me earlier?
So he went to greet him in person.
Her family lived in a small market in Changling. Emperor Wu and others went straight to her door and sent their men in to invite Jin.
His family was horrified, and Kim was so frightened that he hid.
The servants helped her out to pay homage to the emperor. As soon as Emperor Wu got out of the car, he said: Sister, why are you hiding so deeply?
Then they got in the car and went to Changle Palace to meet the Queen Mother together. The Queen Mother shed tears, and Jin also cried sadly.
Emperor Wu raised a glass of wine and came forward to wish them longevity.
Emperor Wu rewarded his sister with 10 million guan of money, 300 slaves, 100 hectares of land, and a luxurious mansion.
The Queen Mother thanked her and said, "It's a waste of time for the Emperor."
He also gave her Tang Muyi and named her Xiuchengjun.
Lord Xiucheng had one son and one daughter each. His daughter was married to a prince, and his son was called Xiucheng Zizhong. He relied on the power of the Queen Mother to run rampant and tyrannical in the capital.
The Queen Mother reigned for a total of twenty-five years. Fifteen years after the death of Emperor Jing, that is, the third year of Yuan Shuo, the Queen Mother died and was buried with Emperor Jing in Yangling.
Empress Chen, Emperor Xiaowu, was the daughter of the eldest princess Liu Piao.
Her great-grandfather Chen Ying and Xiang Yu fought together, and later surrendered to the King of Han and were granted the title of Marquis of Tangyi.
The title was passed on to his son, and then to his grandson Chen Wu. Chen Wu married the eldest princess and gave birth to a daughter.
At the beginning, when Emperor Wu was able to be established as the prince, the eldest princess contributed a lot, so he married the eldest princess's daughter as his concubine.
After Emperor Wu came to the throne, Chen was appointed as the queen. She was extremely favored, proud and domineering. She had not had children for more than ten years. When she heard that Wei Zifu was favored by the emperor, he repeatedly harmed her.
Emperor Wu became even more angry.
Empress Chen once again used women's pleasing skills to try to win the emperor's favor, and things gradually came to light.
In the fifth year of Yuanguang, Emperor Wu investigated and punished the incident. The woman Chu Fu and others were convicted of using sorcery to bring disaster to others on behalf of the queen. The crime was so heinous that more than 300 people were killed. Chu Fu was beheaded in public display.
The emperor sent an official to reward the queen with a document saying: The queen does not abide by etiquette, prays to ghosts and gods, brings disaster to others, and cannot bear the destiny.
He should return the queen's seal and ribbon, leave the position of queen, and retreat to Nagato Palace.
summary: Empress Chen of Emperor Xiaowu was the daughter of the eldest princess. She was favored but had no children for over ten years. When Wei Zifu was favored, Empress Chen used sorcery, leading to her deposition and retreat to Nagato Palace. She died and was buried in Baling.

translation:
In the second year, Chen Wu, the Marquis of Tangyi, passed away, and the princess's son Chen Xu succeeded to the throne.
The princess was a widow at home and secretly had an affair with Dong Yan.
More than ten years later, the princess died.
Chen Xu was convicted of fornication and fighting for property with his brothers and should be sentenced to death. Chen Xu committed suicide and his national title was abolished.
A few years later, the deposed Empress Chen also died and was buried in Shumian of Baling Langguan Pavilion.
Empress Xiaowu, Emperor Wei, also known as Zifu, was born in a lowly position.
Her family name is Wei, and she comes from the fiefdom of Bai Pingyang Marquis.
Zifu is the singer of Princess Huyang. After Emperor Wu came to the throne, he had no sons for many years.
Princess Pingyang selected a dozen girls from good families and dressed them up to stay at home.
Emperor Wu went to Bashang to pray for blessings and eliminate disasters, and when he came back, he paid a visit to Princess Pingyang.
The princess called out the selected beauties, but Emperor Wu didn't like them all.
While drinking, the singer came in, and Emperor Wu fell in love with Zihu.
Emperor Wu got up and went to change his clothes. Zifu served him in the dressing cart, and was favored by Emperor Wu.
Emperor Wu came back and sat down. He was very happy and rewarded Princess Pingyang with a thousand catties of gold.
The princess then asked her husband to be sent to the palace.
When Zihu got into the car, the princess stroked her back and said, "Go!"
Live well.
If you become rich, I hope you won’t forget me.
It has been more than a year since Madam Weizi's palace was visited by the Emperor again.
Emperor Wu selected the maids who were no longer needed in the palace and drove them out of the palace. Zifu was able to see Emperor Wu and cried and begged to be allowed to leave the palace.
Emperor Wu was very fond of her. Fortunately, Zihu became pregnant again, and she was deeply favored by Emperor Wu.
Emperor Wu called Zifu's elder brother Wei Changjun and younger brother Wei Qing to serve as servants.
Zifu gave birth to three daughters. In the first year of Yuanshuo, his son Liu Shi was born, and she was named queen.
After the death of Wei Changjun, Wei Qing was made a general. He made great achievements in conquering the Xiongnu and was granted the title of Marquis of Changping.
Wei Qing had three sons who were ennobled as marquises when they were still in their infancy.
Huo Qubing, the son of Empress Wei's sister, was also awarded the title of Champion Marquis for his military merits, and his official rank reached the rank of Grand Sima Hussar General.
Wei Qing is the great general of Sima.
Five of Wei's relatives were granted the title of marquis.
Wei Qing returned from the expedition and married Princess Pingyang.
In the seventh year after Queen Wei was enthroned, her son was established as the prince.
Later, the queen's appearance deteriorated, and Mrs. Wang of Zhao and Mrs. Li of Zhongshan were favored by Emperor Wu, and they both died young.
Later, Mrs. Yin Jiandan and Mrs. Gou Yi were favored by Emperor Wu one after another.
In the thirty-eighth year of Queen Wei's reign, she encountered a witchcraft disaster and Jiang Chong used treacherous tactics. The prince was afraid but could not prove his innocence, so he and Queen Wei killed Jiang Chong and raised an army. As a result, the battle was defeated and the prince escaped.
Emperor Wu issued an edict and sent Zongzheng Liu Changle and Zhijinwu Liu Gan to take back the queen's seal with documents, and Queen Wei committed suicide.
Huangmen Suwen and Yao Dinghan carried the body of Empress Shangwei in a car and placed it in an empty room in the public carriage. They also put it into a small coffin and buried it in Tongbai in the south of the city.
The entire Wei family was killed.
After Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Empress Wei was buried instead, and she was given the posthumous title of Empress Mi. A cemetery and 300 households were set up, and the director and the chief minister were ordered to offer sacrifices to her.
Mrs. Li, Emperor Xiaowu, originally entered the palace as a singer.
summary: Empress Xiaowu Wei, also known as Zifu, was a singer of Princess Pingyang. Emperor Wu favored her, and she gave birth to a son, Liu Shi, who was made prince. Wei Qing and Huo Qubing became generals. Later, Empress Wei's appearance deteriorated, and she faced a witchcraft disaster. The prince killed Jiang Chong and raised an army but was defeated. Empress Wei committed suicide. After Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, she was reburied with the posthumous title of Empress Mi.

translation:
At first, Mrs. Li's brother Li Yannian was proficient in music and good at singing and dancing, and Emperor Wu liked him very much.
Every time Li Yannian composed a new piece of music, everyone who heard it was moved.
He danced for Emperor Wu and sang: There is a beauty in the north, whose beauty is unparalleled in the world. Look back and smile, overturning the country. Look back and smile again, overturning the country.
It’s not that we don’t cherish the city and country, it’s just that beauty is hard to come by again.
The emperor sighed and said: OK!
Is there really such a person in the world?
Princess Pingyang said that Li Yannian had a sister, and Emperor Wu summoned her. She was indeed beautiful and good at dancing.
Therefore, he was favored by Emperor Wu and gave birth to a son, King Ai of Changyi.
Mrs. Li died young but died young. Emperor Wu felt very sorry for her, so he painted a portrait of her and hung it in Ganquan Palace.
Four years after Wei Si was deposed, Emperor Wu died. General Huo Guang followed Emperor Wu's wishes and gave Mrs. Li the title of Queen Xiaowu in the ancestral temple.
At first, Mrs. Li was seriously ill, and Emperor Wu went to visit her in person. The wife covered her face with a quilt and said: I have been ill for a long time and am ugly, so I cannot see the emperor.
Please take good care of my son and brother, Your Majesty. Emperor Wu said: My wife is very ill and may be dying.
Aren't you happy to meet me and tell me about your son and brothers? The lady said: A woman cannot see her father without dressing up.
I don't dare to see the emperor in a disheveled manner.
Emperor Wu said: Madam, as long as you meet me once, I will reward you with a thousand pieces of gold, and give your brother a promotion.
The lady said: The promotion is decided by the emperor, not just to meet me.
Emperor Wu said again that he must see her, so the lady turned away and sobbed and stopped talking.
So Emperor Wu left very unhappy.
The madam's sister complained to her and said, "Can't you meet with the emperor and ask about your brother's affairs?"
Why are you so resentful of the emperor?
The lady said: The reason why I don't want to see the emperor is to take this opportunity to entrust my brother.
By virtue of my beauty, I was able to win the favor of the emperor from a humble person.
Those who rely on their appearance to serve others will lose their friendship as their appearance fades. As their friendship becomes shallower, their kindness will be cut off.
The reason why the emperor still misses me affectionately is precisely because of my original appearance.
Now if you see my ugly appearance, you will definitely be scared, bored, and disgusted with me. How can I miss my brother who sympathized with me and treated me well?
After his wife's death, Emperor Wu buried her with the courtesy of a queen.
Then, Emperor Wu made Mrs. Li's brother Li Guangli the general of the Second Division and the Marquis of Haixi, and Li Yannian the captain of Xielu.
Emperor Wu had always been obsessed with Mrs. Li, and the young alchemist Qi Ren said that he could attract Mrs. Li's soul.
At night, they lit lamps and candles, hung up the curtains, put out wine and meat, and asked Emperor Wu to go to another tent to wrap up. Emperor Wu saw a beautiful woman from a distance, just like Mrs. Li, sitting down in the tent, getting up and walking slowly.
But he couldn't get close to see her, so Emperor Wu missed Mrs. Li even more. He felt sentimental in his heart and wrote a poem for her, saying: Is it you?
I stood there looking at you, but why did I walk so slowly and calmly!
Order the Yuefu musicians to sing along with the music.
Emperor Wu wrote another poem to commemorate Mrs. Li, which goes like this:
Your appearance is blazing and beautiful, but it is a pity that life is short and short-lived. I have decorated the new palace and waited for you for a long time, but you disappeared and never returned to your hometown.
summary: Mrs. Li of Emperor Xiaowu was a singer. Her brother Li Yannian sang about a beauty, and Emperor Wu summoned her. She gave birth to King Ai of Changyi but died young. Emperor Wu mourned her and later gave her the title of Queen Xiaowu. Her brothers Li Guangli and Li Yannian were rewarded, but the Li family was later exterminated.

translation:
The gate of the palace where the child was born was called Yao Mu Gate.
Later, Crown Prince Wei was defeated. King Liu Dan of Yan and King Liu Xu of Guangling often did wrong things. King Qi Huai, son of the doting Queen, and King Ai of Changyi, son of Mrs. Li, both died early. When Gou Yizi was five or six years old, he was born with a great body and very smart. Emperor Wu often said: "Like me" , and felt that his birth was different from others, so he loved him especially, and planned to make him the prince. And because he was young and his mother was young, he was worried that the heroine's dictatorship would cause chaos in the country again, so he always hesitated.
Gou Yi Jiandan followed Emperor Wu to Ganquan Palace. He made a small mistake and was scolded by Emperor Wu. As a result, he died of fear and was buried in Yunyang.
Later, Emperor Wu became seriously ill and appointed Gou Yizi as the crown prince.
He also named Huo Guang, the captain of Fengche, as the Great Sima General and asked him to assist the young monarch.
The next day, Emperor Wu died.
After Emperor Zhao ascended the throne, he honored Gou Yi's nephew as the empress dowager, sent 20,000 soldiers to build Yunling Tomb, and set up 3,000 families to guard the mausoleum.
He also honored his maternal grandfather, Father Zhao, as the Marquis of Shuncheng, and issued an edict to set up a cemetery and 200 households in Youfufeng, and set up a Changcheng to guard it in accordance with the law.
Marquis Shuncheng had a sister named Junju, and he rewarded her with two million yuan, slaves and a house.
The brothers of Marquis Shuncheng each gave rewards according to their closeness.
There was no official in the Zhao family, only Zhao Jiantun's father was forced to become a marquis.
Emperor Xiaozhao and Queen Shangguan.
Her grandfather Shangguan Jie was from Shangbang in Longxi.
When he was young, he was a disciple of the Yulin period and followed Emperor Wu to Ganquan Palace. When there was a strong wind and the car could not move forward, he took off the hood and let Shangguan Jie hold it.
Shangguan Jie held the hood of the car, but despite the strong wind, he was not dropped by the car. Soon it started to rain, so he used the hood to protect Emperor Wu from the rain.
Emperor Wu admired his bravery very much and promoted him to Weiyang Stable Order.
Emperor Wu was not feeling well. After he recovered, he went to see the horses and found that most of the horses had lost weight. Emperor Wu was furious and said: "Do you think I will never see these horses again?"
Wanting to punish him, Shangguan Jie kowtowed and said, "I heard that the emperor was unwell, so I worried about you day and night. How could I care about watching the horses?"
Before he finished speaking, tears fell one after another.
Emperor Wu thought that he was very loyal to him, so he trusted him very much and made him a servant, and gradually he was promoted to a servant.
Emperor Wu was seriously ill and made Huo Guang the general and his servant Shangguan Jie the general of the left. They both accepted the imperial edict to assist the young master.
Because of his meritorious service in the previous killing of Mang Tong, Shangguan Jie was granted the title of Marquis of Anyang.
At the beginning, Shangguan Jie's son Shangguan An married Huo Guang's daughter, and the two families were married and had a close relationship. Whenever Huo Guang went out on vacation, Shangguan Jie often handled state affairs on his behalf.
Emperor Zhao was only eight years old when he came to the throne. His sister, Princess Egai, lived in the palace and raised Hantong.
summary: Gouyi of Emperor Xiaowu was the mother of Emperor Zhao. Emperor Wu summoned her, and she gave birth to Emperor Zhao after fourteen months. After Crown Prince Wei's defeat, Gou Yizi was made prince. Emperor Wu appointed Huo Guang to assist him. After Emperor Zhao ascended the throne, Gouyi was honored as empress dowager, and her father was named Marquis of Shuncheng.

translation:
After the memorial was presented, Emperor Zhao asked Huo Guang for his opinion, but Huo Guang insisted that he disagreed.
When King Yan wrote another letter accusing Huo Guang of being guilty, Emperor Zhao became more suspicious. He became closer to Huo Guang and alienated Shangguan Jie and Shangguan An.
Shangguan father and son gradually became angry from shame, so they secretly gathered their party members to plot to kill Huo Guang, tricked King Yan into coming to Beijing to kill Huo Guang, and then deposed Emperor Zhao and established Shangguan Jie as emperor.
Someone said: What can the queen do?
Shangguan An said: Can a hunting dog chasing a moose care about a little rabbit?
Moreover, relying on the queen to obtain the honorable position, once the emperor changes his mind, it is impossible to become a commoner. This is true no matter what dynasty.
After the incident was revealed, both King Yan and Princess Gai committed suicide.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Huo Guang".
Shangguan Jie and Shangguan An's father and son were exterminated. The queen was young and did not participate in the rebellion. She was Huo Guang's granddaughter, so she was not deposed.
The queen's mother had died before that and was buried to the east of Maolingguo. She was given the honorific title Lady Jing, and a cemetery and 200 households were set up.
The queen sent her slaves to guard the tombs of Shangguan Jie and Shangguan An.
Huo Guang hoped that the queen would be pampered and give birth to a son. Emperor Zhao was often in poor health. The waiters and medical officers around him all agreed with Huo Guang and said that desires should be controlled. Even the maids ordered them to wear crotchless pants and many belts, so no women in the harem could enter the palace.
In the tenth year after Queen Shangguan was enthroned, Emperor Zhao died. The queen is only fourteen or fifteen years old.
Liu He, the king of Changyi, was summoned to become the emperor, and Queen Shangguan was honored as the empress dowager.
Later, Huo Guang and the Queen Mother deposed Liu He and established Emperor Xiaoxuan instead.
After Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, the Queen Mother became the Empress Dowager.
Shangguan reigned for a total of forty-seven years. She died at the age of fifty-two in the second year of Jianzhao, and she and Emperor Zhao were buried together in Pingling.
Shi Liangdi, the crown prince of Wei, was the grandmother of Emperor Xuan.
The prince has concubines, concubines, and children. The wives and concubines are divided into three levels, and the sons are called the emperor's grandchildren.
Shi Liangdi was originally from the state of Lu. Her mother was named Zhenjun and her brother was named Shi Gong.
In the fourth year of Yuanding, Shi entered the palace and became the crown prince Liangdi. She gave birth to a son, Liu Jin, who was called the grandson of Emperor Shi.
In the last years of Emperor Wu's reign, a witchcraft disaster occurred, and Prince Wei, Liang Di, and Emperor Shi's grandson were all killed.
Shi Huangsun had a son, called Huang great-grandson, who was just a few months old at the time. He was also implicated by the prince and imprisoned. He was not pardoned until he was five years old.
Bing Ji, the envoy in charge of the prison, took pity on the emperor's great-grandson and gave him to Shi Gong to raise him.
Shi Gong's mother, Zhenjun, was old. Seeing the child alone, she felt very sad, so she took care of the child herself.
Later, the great-grandson of the emperor was adopted in Yeting and became emperor again, namely Emperor Xuan.
At this time Zhenjun and Shi Gong had passed away, and Shi Gong's three sons were all rewarded for their old kindness.
The eldest son Shi Gao was granted the title of Marquis of Leling, Shi Zeng was granted the title of Marquis of General Ling, and Shi Xuan was granted the title of Marquis of Platform. When Shi Gao's son Shi Dan was granted the title of Marquis of Wuyang due to his merit and virtue, there were four people in the Shi family who were granted the title of marquis.
Shi Gaoguan was promoted to the Great Sima Cavalry General, and Shi Dan was promoted to Zuo General. They each have their own biographies.
summary: Emperor Xiaozhao and Queen Shangguan were the granddaughter of Huo Guang. She became queen at six years old. Shangguan Jie and Shangguan An plotted to kill Huo Guang but were exposed and exterminated. The queen, young and uninvolved, was not deposed. After Emperor Zhao's death, she became empress dowager and died at fifty-two, buried with Emperor Zhao. Shi Liangdi of Crown Prince Wei was the grandmother of Emperor Xuan. She gave birth to Liu Jin, who was killed in a witchcraft disaster. Emperor Xuan, as a baby, was saved and raised by Shi Gong. After becoming emperor, he honored Shi Liangdi as Mourning Queen.

translation:
Mrs. Wang Sun, Emperor Xuan's mother, was named Wengxu. She was favored by Sun Huang during the Taishi period.
The wives and concubines of the emperor's grandson have no names and are all called family members.
In the second year of Zhenghe, Wengxu gave birth to Emperor Xuan.
Only a few months after Emperor Xuan was born, Crown Prince Wei and Emperor Shi's grandson were defeated, and all their family members were implicated and killed. Their bodies could not be collected and buried. Only Emperor Xuan survived.
After Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he honored his mother, Mrs. Wang, with the title of Mourning Queen, and his grandmother, Shi Liangdi, with the title of Mourning Queen. They were all reburied, a cemetery and a family home were set up, and Chang Cheng guarded them.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Prince Ru."
In the third year of Dijie, Emperor Xuan found his grandmother Wang Yu. Wang Yu's son Wang Wuyou and Wuyou's younger brother Wang Wu both followed the envoys to the palace.
At that time, they were riding in a scalper's cart, so the people called Wang Lao the scalper woman.
At the beginning, after Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he sent envoys many times to find people in his grandmother's family. However, due to the passage of time, many people looked similar but were not.
After finding Wang Nu, he sent Taizhong doctor Ren Xuan and the officials under the Prime Minister and Yushi to ask people in the same town who knew her, and they all said she was Wang Nu.
Concubine Wang said that her name was Huanren and that she was originally from Liwuping Township, Zhuo County.
When she was fourteen years old, she married the king of her hometown, Geng.
Even more so after death. She married King Guangwang Naishi and gave birth to sons Wang Wuyou, Wang Wu and daughter Wengxu. When Wengxu was eight or nine years old, she was fostered in the home of Liu Zhongqing, the son of Marquis Guangwangjie. Zhongqing said to Naishi, "Give Wengxu to me and I will help you raise her."
Wang Lao made spring and summer clothes for Weng Xu and sent them to Zhongqing's house.
Zhongqing taught Wengxu how to sing and dance. Wengxu came back several times to pick up winter and summer clothes.
Four or five years later, Weng Xu came back and said, "Jia Changer from Handan is looking for someone who can sing and dance, and Zhongqing wants to give me to him."
Wang Lao and Weng Xu fled together and arrived in Pingxiang.
Zhongqing took Nai Shi to look for Wang Lao. Wang Lao was very frightened, so she took Weng Xu back and said, "My daughter lives in your house and has not received any money. How can I give her to others?"
Zhongqing lied to her and said: No.
A few days later, Wengxu was sitting in Mai Changer's car and passed by the house. She shouted loudly: I have been sent away as expected, and I have to go to Liusu.
Wang Lao and Nai Shi arrived at Liusu. When they saw Weng Xuhou, they cried to each other and said to her: "We want to file a complaint for you."
Weng Xu said, "Forget it, mother. Which family can't live in it?"
Complaints are of no use.
Wang Yu and Naishi went back to collect money, and then followed them to Lunu, Zhongshan. They saw Weng Xu and several singing and dancing girls, a total of five people together. Wang Yu and Weng Xu slept together.
The next day, Naishi stayed there to take care of Wengxu. Wangla went back to get the money and planned to follow them to Handan.
After Wang Lao returned home, she had not prepared any money or supplies. Naishi came back and said, "Weng Xu has left. I have no money and cannot follow them."
So contact was severed and Weng Xu was never heard from again.
Jia Chang'er's wife Zhen and the singing and dancing teacher who followed Sui said in their confessions: Twenty years ago, the prince's minister Hou Ming came from Chang'an and wanted some singing and dancing girls, so he chose Weng Xu and five others.
summary: Mrs. Wang Sun, Emperor Xuan's mother, was named Wengxu. She gave birth to Emperor Xuan but was killed in the disaster. Emperor Xuan honored her as Mourning Queen and found his grandmother Wang Yu, who was named Lord Boping. The Wang family had two marquises.

translation:
Her mother asked a fortune teller to tell her that she would be rich and wealthy, and her mother was secretly happy.
Zhang He heard that Xu Shifu had a daughter, so he held a banquet for him. When he was drinking well, he said, "The emperor's great-grandson is close relatives with the emperor. Even if his talents are inferior, he can still be a Marquis of Guannei. You can betroth your daughter to him as your wife."
Guangmo agreed. The next day, Pingjun's mother heard the news and was very angry.
But Guangmo hired someone to act as a matchmaker again, so he married his daughter to the emperor's great-grandson, and gave birth to Emperor Yuan a year later.
A few months later, the emperor's great-grandson was appointed emperor, and Lord Xu Ping was named Qizai.
At this time, General Huo also had a young daughter who was not married and was related to the Empress Dowager.
The ministers proposed to appoint a queen, and they all preferred General Huo's daughter, but no one spoke.
Emperor Xuan issued an edict to find an old sword he had owned when he was poor and humble. The ministers understood the emperor's intention and petitioned to appoint Xu Jianzi as queen.
After the queen was appointed, Huo Guang believed that the queen's father Xu Guangmo was a man who had been castrated and was not suitable for managing the place. It took more than a year before he named him Lord Changcheng.
Huo Guang's wife Huo Xian wanted to make her little daughter noble, but she couldn't think of a way.
The next year, Queen Xu fell ill when she was about to give birth.
The female doctor Chun Yuyan had a close relationship with the Huo family and once went to the palace to serve the queen.
Chunyu Yan's husband was appointed as a household guard in Yeting, and he said to Chunyu Yan, "Go and say goodbye to Mrs. Huo, and ask for the position of Anchi Supervisor for me."
Chunyu Yan told Huo Xian.
Huo Xian had an idea. He backed away and said to Chunyu Yan, "Young master, please ask me for something. I also want to ask you for help. Is that okay?"
Chunyu Yan said: There is nothing wrong with what Madam said!
Huo Xian said: The general has always loved his youngest daughter Chengjun. He hopes that she will be noble and wants to trouble the young husband.
Chunyu Yan said: What does this mean?
Huo Xian said: A woman's childbirth is a big event, and she will escape death.
Now that the queen is about to give birth, we can take this opportunity to throw poison to get rid of her, and Chengjun can become the queen.
If you are willing to work hard to accomplish this, I am willing to share the wealth with you, young husband.
Chunyu Yan said: The medicine was prepared by many imperial doctors, and others had to taste it first. How could it be poisoned?
Huo Xian said: "It depends on your ability, young master." The general is in charge of the world, who dares to say anything about him?
I will protect you in times of crisis, but I'm afraid you don't mean it.
Chunyu Yan thought for a long time and said: I am willing to do my best.
She pounded the aconite into powder and brought it into Changding Palace.
After the queen gave birth, Chun Yuyan took out aconite and mixed it with the imperial physician's pills, and served the queen to take them.
After a while, the queen said: I have a headache. Is the medicine poisonous?
Chunyu Yan replied: No.
The queen became even more depressed and restless, and finally died.
Chunyu Yan left the palace and met with Huo Xian. Huo Xian comforted her but did not dare to thank her heavily.
summary: Empress Xu of Emperor Xiaoxuan was the mother of Wuhu. Her father Xu Guanghan was a eunuch. Emperor Xuan, as a great-grandson, married Xu Pingjun, who gave birth to Emperor Yuan. After becoming emperor, Xu was made queen. Huo Guang's wife Huo Xian had her poisoned to make her daughter queen. Queen Xu died and was named Queen Gongai.

translation:
Later, someone wrote a letter accusing the doctors of being useless in treating the queen, so they were imprisoned in Shao County to expose their treasonous crimes.
Huo Xian was afraid that the matter would be exposed, so he told Huo Guang everything about the incident, and said: Since this matter has been done wrongly, you should find a way to prevent the officials from questioning Chunyu Yan.
Huo Guang was stunned after hearing this and could not say a word.
Then he went to petition the emperor not to hold Chunyu Yan responsible anymore.
Queen Xu died three years after she was made queen. She was named Queen Gongai and was buried in Dunan, also known as Duling South Garden.
Five years later, she made her son the crown prince, and made the crown prince's grandfather, Changchengjun Xu Guanghan, the Marquis of Ping'en, granting him special advancement.
Four years later, Xu Guangmo's two younger brothers were also granted the title of Xu Shun as Bowang Marquis and Xu Yanshou as Lecheng Marquis.
There are three people in the Xu family who have been granted the title of marquis.
After Xu Guanghan's death, Mi was given the title Marquis of Dai. He had no sons, so the title was discontinued.
He was buried next to the South Garden, and three hundred households were set up. The chief of the garden and the chief minister were set up to guard and sweep in accordance with the law.
Emperor Xuan granted Xu Yanshou the title of Chief Chariot and Cavalry General to assist in government affairs.
After Emperor Yuan came to the throne, he also named Xu Yanshou's middle son Xu Jia the title of Marquis of Ping'en. After inheriting the title of Marquis Dai, he also became the Great Sima Cavalry General.
Empress Huo of Emperor Xiaoxuan was the daughter of Sima General Bolu Hou Huo Guang.
Queen Huo's mother, Huo Xian, sent Chunyu Yan to kill Queen Xu secretly. Then she made Chengjun's wedding clothes, prepared the tools for entering the palace, and persuaded Huo Guang to send his daughter to the palace. Sure enough, Chengjun was appointed queen.
At the beginning, Empress Xu was from a humble background, and her time as empress was very short. Her servants, drivers, and attire were all very frugal. She went to Changle Palace to see the Empress Dowager every five days, and personally held a food table to offer food to the Empress Dowager, as a filial piety to her granddaughter-in-law.
When I arrived at Queen Huo, I also followed the old practices of Queen Xu. However, the Queen Mother was the daughter of Queen Huo's sister, so she was always cautious and respected her very much.
The queen's chariots and horses were very impressive, and she rewarded her subordinates with tens of millions of dollars, which was very different from that of Queen Xu.
Emperor Xuan also doted on her very much, and Queen Yuzu was the only one who was good at doting on her.
In the third year after Queen Huo was enshrined, Huo Guang passed away.
Another year later, Emperor Xuan appointed Queen Xu's son as the prince, and granted Chang Chengjun the title of Ping'enhou.
Huo Xian was so angry that he couldn't eat and even vomited blood. He said, "This is a child born in the common people. How can he be made a prince?"
If the queen gives birth to a son, can she only become the king?
She also instructed Queen Huo to poison the prince.
The queen summoned the prince many times to give him food, but the nanny always tasted it first, and the queen hid poison but could not use it.
Later, the murder of Queen Xu was gradually leaked out, and Huo Xian conspired with his son-in-law and his children. The plot was leaked, and Emperor Xuan had the Huo family wiped out.
He also sent a secretary to give the queen a document, saying: The queen has evil intentions and evil intentions. She conspired with her mother, Huo Xian, the wife of Hou Xuancheng and Bo Lu, to harm the prince. She has no kindness as a mother and is not suitable to worship the ancestors anymore, let alone accept the destiny. well!
He should retreat to the cold palace and return his seal and ribbon.
Queen Huo reigned for five years and was deposed and took refuge in Zhaotai Palace.
Twelve years later, when Huo was asked to move to Yunlin Pavilion, she committed suicide and was buried east of Kunwu Pavilion.
At first, Huo Guang and his brother Huo Qubing, the cavalry general, were both granted the title of marquis for their merits. Because of Huo Guang, Emperor Xuan made Huo Qubing's grandson Huo Shan and Huo Shan's younger brother Huo Yun both marquises. There were four people in the Huo family who were granted the title of marquis.
summary: Empress Huo of Emperor Xiaoxuan was the daughter of Huo Guang. After Queen Xu's death, she became queen. Huo Xian tried to poison the prince but failed. The murder was exposed, and the Huo family was wiped out. Queen Huo was deposed and committed suicide.

translation:
Emperor Xiaoxuan and Queen.
Queen Wang's ancestors were given the title of Marquis of Guannei due to their merit during Emperor Gaozu's reign, and they moved from Pei to Changling. The title was passed down to the Queen's father, Wang Fengguan.
Wang Fengguan liked cockfighting when he was young. Emperor Xuan met him many times when he was among the people and got to know each other.
Fengguang has a teenage daughter. Whenever she wants to get married, the other party always dies, so she has not been able to get married for a long time.
After Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he summoned Fengguang's daughter into the harem and was gradually promoted to Jianxian.
At this time, Hua Jianzai, the mother of King Guantao, Zhang Jiandan, the mother of King Xian of Huaiyang, and Wei Jianzai, the mother of King Xiao of Chu, were all deeply favored by Emperor Xuan.
After Queen Huo was deposed, Emperor Xuan took pity on Prince Xu who lost his mother very early and was almost killed by the Huo family. Therefore, he selected people in the harem who were usually cautious and had no children.
Since Queen Wang became the queen, she was rarely summoned by the emperor and was not favored.
Emperor Xuan made the queen's father Wang Fengguan the Marquis of Qiongcheng.
In the sixteenth year after Queen Wang was enthroned, Emperor Xuan died, Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, and Queen Wang became the empress dowager.
Emperor Yuan granted the Queen Mother's brother Wang Shun the title of Marquis of Anping.
Two years later, Wang Fengguang died. Mi was named Gonghou and was buried south of Changmen. A cemetery and 200 households were set up, and Chang Cheng was ordered to guard it according to the law.
After Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, the Queen Mother became the Empress Dowager.
He also granted the title of Marquis of Guannei to Wang Jun, the younger brother of the Empress Dowager, and granted him the title of a thousand households.
Two members of the Wang family were named marquis, and one was named Guannei marquis.
Wang Shun's son Wang Zhang and Wang Zhang's cousin Wang Xian both served as generals.
At that time, Emperor Cheng's mother was also named Wang, so the Empress Dowager was known as Empress Dowager Qiongcheng.
Empress Dowager Qiongcheng reigned for forty-nine years. She died in her seventies in the first year of Yongshi. She was buried with Emperor Xuan in Duling, called Shuyuan.
Wang Fengguan's grandson Wang Xun broke the law and was deprived of his title.
During the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the Empress Dowager of Emperor Cheng issued an edict, saying: The Queen Mother of Emperor Xiaoxuan is my mother-in-law. I deeply miss her upbringing and teaching, and I will keep her kindness in my heart.
However, the title of Gonghou of Qiongcheng was abolished. I felt very sorry for him, so I named Wang Jianhou, the great-grandson of Gonghou, as the Marquis of Qiongcheng.
This title was not abolished until Wang Mang.
summary: Emperor Xiaoxuan and Queen Wang were from a family with a marquis title. She became queen after Queen Huo's deposition, rarely favored. After Emperor Xuan's death, she became empress dowager and died in her seventies, buried with Emperor Xuan.

translation:
The queen of Emperor Xiaoyuan was the mother of Emperor Cheng.
The Wang family has a total of ten princes and five chief ministers. Among the relatives, no one is more prosperous than their family.
Queen Wang's relatives have their own biographies.
Empress Xu of Emperor Xiaocheng was the daughter of Ping Enhou Xu Jia, the general of the Great Sima Chariot Cavalry.
Emperor Yuan mourned the death of his mother and mourned the murder of the Huo family for a short period of time in her reign. He specially selected Xu Jia's daughter to be betrothed to the crown prince.
When Mrs. Xu first entered the crown prince's palace, the emperor sent his ministers and close associates from Huangmen to serve him. When these people came back, they told how happy the crown prince was. Emperor Yuan was overjoyed and said to his left and right: "Please pour some wine to congratulate me!"
Everyone on the left and right shouted long live.
After meeting for a long time, Concubine Xu gave birth to a son who died in infancy.
After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he appointed Concubine Xu as empress. Empress Xu gave birth to another daughter, who also died in infancy.
At first, the queen's father, Xu Jia, had been appointed as a general in charge of carriage and cavalry to assist the government since the Yuan Dynasty. It had been eight or nine years.
After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he named his uncle Wang Feng, Marquis of Yangping, the Great Sima General, alongside Xu Jia.
Du Qin believed that according to the old rules, the queen's father's status should be more noble than the emperor's uncle, so he advised Wang Feng: "The chariot general's status is extremely noble. General, you should respect him and do not go against his wishes."
Even small differences can lead to catastrophic hostility, so we must not be careless.
At that time, the glory of General Wei was greater than that of Gaihou. In modern times, older people often talk about it and hope that the general will consider it carefully.
Later, the emperor planned to appoint only Wang Feng, so he gave Xu Jiawen a letter saying: The general has a distinguished status and should not be burdened by his official position.
He was rewarded with two hundred catties of gold and established in the court with a special promotion position.
More than a year later, Xu Jia passed away and was given the title Gonghou.
Queen Xu was intelligent by nature and good at writing official scripts. From the time she became the crown prince to the time she was appointed queen, she was often favored by the emperor. Women in the harem were rarely summoned by the emperor.
The empress dowager and the emperor's uncles were worried that the emperor would have no heirs. At this time, disasters occurred repeatedly. Liu Xiang, Gu Yong and others all reported that the fault was in the harem.
The emperor thought they were right. Therefore, the expenses for the Queen's Palace and Yeting were reduced.
The queen went to the court and said:
I came from a poor family with a poor diet, and I was young, ignorant, and ignorant of the truth. I was fortunate enough to be able to leave a commoner's home and serve His Majesty in the harem.
Thanks to your majesty's wrong love, I am in the position of queen that I should not have earned. However, I cannot keep myself clean and fulfill my duties. I have always violated laws and regulations and undermined the system. Even though I was sentenced to exile, it was not enough to justify my crime.
So the edict was read out in the Changqiu period of Renyin: The queen should follow the etiquette and laws, dress her carriages and horses, take the property from the official office, make useful items, and reward her relatives and families, all in accordance with the old practices before Emperor Xiaoyuan.
summary: The Wang family, relatives of Emperor Xiaoyuan's queen, produced ten princes and five chief ministers, making them the most prosperous among all imperial relatives. Empress Xu of Emperor Xiaocheng was the daughter of General Xu Jia. Emperor Yuan selected her for the crown prince after mourning his mother's death. She initially brought joy to the court, but her children died in infancy. After Emperor Cheng ascended, he appointed her empress and appointed his uncle Wang Feng alongside Xu Jia as co-regents. Du Qin advised Wang Feng to respect Xu Jia's superior status according to tradition. Eventually, the emperor appointed only Wang Feng and granted Xu Jia a special retirement with gold. Xu Jia died over a year later.

translation:
Establish a good reputation and show off your good virtues, so as to calm the discussions of the people in the world, and let the law be spread in the harem so that the concubines can obey the law.
Please think deeply and don't take these things lightly.
At that time, it was General Wang Feng who was in charge of the government and had the greatest power.
Later, there were food shortages for three consecutive years, and most of the people who came to remonstrate blamed Wang Feng.
But Gu Yong and others thought it was Queen Xu's fault. Queen Xu knew in her heart that Wang Feng would not help her.
After a while, Emperor Cheng's favor for the queen diminished, and many people in the harem were favored.
The queen's sister, Ping'an Ganghou's wife, Xu Ye, and others used benign ways to curse Wang Mei, Wang Feng, and others in the harem who were pregnant. When the incident was revealed, the queen mother was furious and threw these people into prison for torture. Xu Ye and others were executed. Queen Xu was convicted and deposed.
Empress Xu reigned for a total of fourteen years before being deposed. She lived in Zhaotai Palace for more than a year and then moved to Changding Palace.
Nine years later, Emperor Cheng took pity on the Xu family and issued an edict saying: It is said that benevolence does not forget those who are far away, and righteousness does not forget relatives.
Xu Ye, the wife of Ping'an Ganghou, had previously committed a crime of treason and injustice. Fortunately, her family was pardoned and returned to their place of origin.
I think that Marquis Ping'endai is the late emperor's grandfather. His soul has nowhere to live, and there is no one to keep vigil and offer sacrifices to him. I have always kept this incident in my heart and will never forget it.
He ordered Ping Enhou Xu Dan and Xu's relatives in Shanyang County to return to the capital.
This year, Xu Feihou died. At first, Xu Feihou's sister Xu Biao was widowed and living alone. She had an affair with Chun Yuchang, the Marquis of Dingling, and she became his concubine.
Chunyu Chang lied to her and said: I can report to the Queen Mother and re-establish Queen Xu as Queen Zuo.
After Xu was abolished, he secretly bribed Chun Yuchang through Aunt Xu, and exchanged letters to thank each other many times.
Chunyu Chang made rude remarks in a letter and was reported. Emperor Cheng sent his court official Kong Guang to give Xu Feihou poison with a talisman. She had no choice but to commit suicide and was buried to the west of the Yanling Road Stables.
Emperor Xiaocheng's classmate was selected into the harem when Emperor Cheng just ascended the throne.
He started as a young envoy, but soon became favored by Emperor Cheng. He was granted the title of Jiantun and lived in Zengchengshe. He gave birth twice in the outer house, giving birth to a boy, who died a few months later.
When Emperor Cheng was playing in the harem, he once planned to ride in a chariot with Ban Shizuo. Ban Tuzai refused and said: "Looking at the pictures from ancient times, the wise monarchs are sitting next to famous ministers. Only the kings of the three generations of subjugation will have favored women. If your majesty rides in the chariot with me now, won't you be similar to those monarchs who have subjugated their countries?"
Emperor Cheng thought what she said made sense, so he gave up.
When the Queen Mother heard about this, she said happily: "In ancient times, there was Fan Ji, and now there is Ban Shidan."
Ban Jiantan recited "The Book of Songs" and "Youyao", "Dexiang", "Female Master" and other articles.
Every time you are summoned by Emperor Cheng or have a speech, you must act in accordance with ancient etiquette.
Since the Hongjia period, the number of concubines favored by Emperor Cheng gradually increased.
Ban nephew offered his maid Li Pingjin to Emperor Cheng. Li Ping was favored and named Jieyu.
Emperor Cheng said: In the past, Queen Wei also came from a humble background.
He gave Li Ping the surname Wei, which is also the so-called Wei envoy.
Later, the Zhao Feiyan sisters also rose from a humble position and transcended etiquette to a greater extent than before.
Both Ban Jianzi and Queen Xu fell out of favor and were rarely summoned by Emperor Cheng.
In the third year of Hongjia, Zhao Feiyan falsely accused Empress Xu and Ban Jianzi of behaving like women, cursed the harem, and even cursed the emperor.
Queen Xu was offended and deposed.
When interrogating Ban Jianzi, she replied: I heard that life and death are determined by destiny, wealth is in heaven, and being kind and upright has not been blessed, so what do you want to gain by doing these evil things?
summary: Empress Xu was intelligent and skilled in calligraphy, enjoying the emperor's favor for many years while other concubines were rarely summoned. When disasters occurred repeatedly, officials Liu Xiang and Gu Yong blamed the harem, leading to reduced expenses for the queen's palace. The empress petitioned the emperor, arguing that her rewards to her family had never exceeded proper limits, that changing times required adapting systems, and that officials were using vague edicts to restrict her unfairly. She requested clarification on what property she could obtain and asked to maintain traditional practices for sacrifices and family rewards. Emperor Cheng responded by citing numerous natural disasters and celestial omens—solar eclipses, white vapors, meteors, floods, earthquakes, and fires—as evidence that excessive yin energy from the harem was causing the royal family's lack of heirs. He urged the empress to practice frugality and virtue. As Wang Feng dominated the government, three years of famine led critics to blame him, but Gu Yong continued faulting Empress Xu. The emperor's favor diminished, and the empress's sister Xu Ye was discovered cursing pregnant concubines and Wang Feng. The empress dowager had Xu Ye executed, and Empress Xu was deposed after fourteen years. Nine years later, Emperor Cheng showed mercy to the Xu family, allowing them to return to the capital. The deposed empress died after her sister's affair with Chunyu Chang led to a scheme to reinstate her. Chunyu Chang made inappropriate remarks in letters, and when reported, the emperor sent poison for her to commit suicide. Ban Jiantun entered the harem when Emperor Cheng ascended and soon gained favor. When the emperor wanted her to share his chariot, she refused, citing ancient examples of wise monarchs accompanying ministers rather than favored women. The empress dowager praised her comparison to Fan Ji of ancient times. Ban Jiantun studied classical texts and always followed ancient etiquette. As the emperor's favor shifted to other concubines, she presented her maid Li Ping to the emperor, who became favored and was given the surname Wei. Later, the Zhao sisters rose to even greater prominence. When Zhao Feiyan falsely accused Empress Xu and Ban Jiantun of cursing the harem, Ban Jiantun defended herself by stating that if ghosts and gods were aware, they would not accept improper prayers, and if ignorant, prayers were useless. The emperor pitied her and rewarded her. Fearing the Zhao sisters' jealousy, she requested to serve the empress dowager in Changxin Palace, where she wrote poems lamenting her fate and describing her lonely life in the palace. After Emperor Cheng's death, she guarded his cemetery until her death.

translation:
After the death of Emperor Cheng, Ban Jianzi was sent to guard the cemetery, where she was buried after her death.
Empress Zhao of Emperor Xiaocheng was originally a palace official in Chang'an.
When she was first born, her parents didn't want to feed her, but after throwing her away for three days, she didn't die, so they took her home and raised her.
When she grew up, she went to Princess Yang's house to learn singing and dancing, and was called Feiyan.
Emperor Cheng once left the palace incognito and visited Princess Yang'a. The princess made people sing and dance for her.
Emperor Cheng liked Zhao Feiyan very much when he saw her, so he invited her to the palace, where she was extremely favored.
Feiyan had a younger sister who was also summoned to the palace. Both sisters were named disciples, and their status was higher than that of the entire harem.
After Queen Xu was deposed, the emperor planned to appoint Zhao Tudan as the queen.
The empress dowager thought she was of low origin and refused to agree.
Chunyu, the son of the Queen Mother's sister, wrote poems and sent messages to and from him many times. Emperor Cheng understood the Queen Mother's thoughts and made Zhao Lin, the father of Zhao Nephew, the Marquis of Chengyang.
More than a month later, Zhao Tudan was appointed queen.
He also recalled Chunyu Chang's contribution to the construction of Changling, and was granted the title of Marquis of Dingling.
After Zhao Feiyan was appointed queen, she was no longer so favored, but her sister was the most favored and was named Zhaoyi.
Living in Zhaoyang House, the courtyard is decorated with red, the hall is painted with two layers of paint, the steps are made of copper, coated with a layer of gold, and the steps are made of white marble. The wall strips are often made of gold and decorated with blue field jade, pearls, and green feathers. The entire harem has never been so luxurious.
The Zhao sisters have been doting on her for more than ten years, but they have never had children.
In the last years of Emperor Cheng's reign, King Dingtao came to pay homage. King Dingtao's grandmother, the Queen Mother Fu, secretly bribed Queen Zhao and Zhao Zhaoyi, and King Dingtao was finally appointed as the crown prince.
In the spring of the next year, Emperor Cheng died.
Emperor Cheng was usually in good health and had no illnesses.
At this time, King Liu Yan of Chu Si and King Liu Li of Liang came to see him. They had to leave early the next morning, so Emperor Cheng arranged a curtain and stayed in the White Tiger Palace.
He also plans to make Kong Guang, the general of the left, prime minister, and the official seal and official announcement have been prepared.
After a night of nothing, I woke up in the morning, put on my pantyhose, and tried to sit up, but my clothes suddenly fell off and I was speechless. At ten quarters of the day, Emperor Cheng died.
The people believed that Zhao Zhaoyi was guilty, and the Empress Dowager issued an edict to the Grand Sima Wang Mang and the Prime Minister Da Sikong, saying: The emperor suddenly died, and people were talking about it and they didn't know what was going on.
Yeting Lingfu and others waited on the emperor's daily life near the harem, and asked them to inquire about the emperor's daily life and illness together with the censor, prime minister, and court officials.
Zhao Zhaoyi committed suicide.
After Emperor Ai ascended the throne, he honored Empress Zhao as the Empress Dowager, and granted the title of Xinchenghou to the Empress Dowager's younger brother, Prince Consort Zhao Qin.
There are two people in the Zhao family who have been granted the title of marquis.
summary: Empress Zhao, originally a palace official in Chang'an, was abandoned at birth but survived. She learned singing and dancing at Princess Yang'a's house and was called Feiyan. Emperor Cheng visited incognito, became enamored with her, and brought her to the palace. Her sister also entered the palace, and both received unprecedented favor. After Empress Xu was deposed, the emperor wanted to make Zhao empress, but the empress dowager objected due to her low birth. Through Chunyu Chang's mediation, the emperor made Zhao's father a marquis, and Zhao became empress. Her sister became Zhaoyi and lived in unprecedented luxury. After more than a decade without children, they were bribed by King Dingtao's grandmother to support him as crown prince. Emperor Cheng died suddenly while in good health, and Zhao Zhaoyi was blamed. An investigation revealed that two other concubines had borne sons who were killed by Zhao Zhaoyi's orders. After Emperor Ai's death, Wang Mang reported to the empress dowager, who demoted and then deposed Empress Zhao, who committed suicide after sixteen years as empress.

translation:
Ji Bu, a native of Chu, was famous for his chivalry.
Xiang Yu asked him to lead troops, which put the king of Han in difficulty several times.
After Xiang Yu was wiped out, Emperor Gaozu spent a thousand taels of gold to purchase Ji Bu. Anyone who dared to harbor Ji Bu would be punished by the three tribes.
Ji Bu hid in Zhou's house in Puyang. Zhou said: The Han Dynasty is anxious to find the general and will come to my house to look for him soon. If you can listen to me, I will dare to find a way for you; if you can't listen to me, I am willing to commit suicide first.
Ji Bu agreed.
So he treated Ji Bu as a criminal, shaved off his hair, tied his neck with an iron ring, put on the prisoner's coarse cloth, and put him in a funeral car. Together with dozens of his slaves, he went to the Zhu family's home in Ludi and wanted to sell them.
Zhu Jiaxin knew that he was Ji Bu, so he bought it and placed it in a house in the countryside.
He himself went to Luoyang to see Xia Houying, the Marquis of Ruyin, and asked, "What crime did Ji Bu commit?"
As ministers, they were their own masters at the beginning and were in charge of their duties. Should all Xiang Yu's ministers be executed?
Now, the emperor has just brought peace to the world, and if he rewards a person with a thousand pieces of gold for his personal grudge, doesn't it show that he is not broad-minded?
Moreover, given Ji Bu's talents, the Han Dynasty captured him so quickly. Didn't this force him to flee north to the Huns and south to South Vietnam?
To hate strong men and force them to go to the enemy's country is not the lesson of Wu Zixu who helped Wu destroy Chu and dug up the tomb of King Ping of Chu and whipped his corpse.
Why don't you speak to the Emperor in a gentle manner?
Xiahou Ying knew in his heart that the Zhu family were famous chivalrous people, and guessed that Ji Bu was hiding in the Zhu family's home, so he agreed.
While serving Tian Guang, he indeed told the emperor what the Zhu family said.
Liu Bang then pardoned Ji Bu.
At that time, some elders in the society praised Ji Bu for his ability to turn toughness into softness, and the Zhu family became famous all over the world because of this incident.
Ji Bu was summoned by the emperor. Ji Bu expressed his gratitude and confessed his crime, and the emperor appointed him as a doctor.
During the reign of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, Jibu Guan rose to Zhonglang General.
The Xiongnu Chanyu once wrote a letter to insult the Queen Mother Lu. The Queen Mother was very angry and summoned the generals to discuss countermeasures.
General Fan Kuai said: I am willing to lead an army of 100,000 to sweep across the Xiongnu.
The generals all obeyed Empress Lu's will and believed that Fan Kuai's statement was correct. Ji Bu said: Fan Kuai should be beheaded.
In the past, Emperor Gao led more than 300,000 soldiers and was surrounded by the Xiongnu in Pingcheng. At that time, Fan Kuai was also surrounded and surrounded.
How could Fan Sha be able to sweep away the Xiongnu with more than 100,000 men now? This is a lie to his face.
Moreover, the Qin Dynasty's use of troops against the Xiongnu led to an uprising by Chen Sheng and others.
A few days ago, the wounds of the war had not yet been healed, and Fan Kuai flattered him in person, hoping to shake the world.
At that time, everyone in the palace was frightened, and the Queen Mother immediately withdrew from the court and never discussed the attack on the Xiongnu again.
summary: Ji Bu, a native of Chu, was known for his chivalry and served as a general under Xiang Yu, causing difficulties for Liu Bang, the King of Han. After Xiang Yu's defeat, Emperor Gaozu of Han offered a reward for Ji Bu's capture, threatening punishment for anyone who harbored him. Ji Bu hid at Zhou's house in Puyang, and with Zhou's help, disguised himself as a prisoner and was sold to the Zhu family in Lu. Zhu Jia, recognizing Ji Bu, bought him and later persuaded Xia Houying, the Marquis of Ruyin, to intercede with the emperor. Xia Houying conveyed Zhu Jia's argument that pursuing Ji Bu would show a lack of magnanimity and might drive him to enemy states. The emperor pardoned Ji Bu, who then became a doctor. During Emperor Hui's reign, Ji Bu served as Zhonglang General. When the Xiongnu Chanyu insulted Empress Lu, General Fan Kuai proposed leading 100,000 troops against them. Ji Bu opposed, citing Emperor Gaozu's past defeat with 300,000 soldiers and warning that such action could incite rebellion. The Empress abandoned the plan. Later, as Governor of Hedong, Ji Bu was summoned by Emperor Wen but sent back after a month. He criticized the emperor for being swayed by praise and slander, and Emperor Wen, ashamed, allowed him to return to his post. The text praises Ji Bu for his resilience and eventual fame, Luan Bu for his loyalty, and Uncle Tian for his integrity, emphasizing that their actions were driven by faith and purpose.
