translation:
Later, Ji Bu became the governor of Hedong County.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, someone told Emperor Wen that Ji Bu was talented and virtuous, and Emperor Wen wanted to summon him to the capital to serve as a censor.
Others said that Ji Bu was very brave, but he drank too much and was willful, so he was not suitable for being a close minister.
Jibu arrived in the capital and stayed in a guest house for a month. After being summoned, he was sent back to his original county.
Ji Bu then advanced and said: "I am in Hedong, fearing that I will be punished for not doing my job well. Your Majesty summoned me to the capital for no reason. Someone must have falsely praised me and deceived Your Majesty."
Now that I have come, your Majesty has not given me any ministry, and has asked me to return to my original county. Someone must be slandering me.
Your Majesty summoned me because someone praised me, and sent me back because someone slandered me. I am worried that the knowledgeable people in the world will know the depth of your Majesty after hearing about this incident.
Emperor Wen was silent after hearing this, and said with shame: Hedong County is a county that I rely on as much as my thighs, so I specially summoned you!
Ji Bu resigned and returned to his original post as governor of Hedong County.
Cao Qiusheng, who was good at rhetoric, repeatedly sought power and was entrusted by others to collect money from the entrusters. He served the eunuch Tantan and others, and was friendly with Baochangjun, the uncle of Emperor Jing.
Ji Bu knew about it and wrote a letter to advise Baochangjun, saying: "I heard that Cao Qiusheng is not an honest and honest person. Don't associate with him."
Later, when Cao Qiusheng returned to his hometown, he wanted to ask Bao Changjun to write a letter to introduce him to Ji Bu.
Mr. Chang said: "General Ji doesn't like you, so don't go."
Keep asking for letters, and then hit the road.
Cao Qiusheng sent someone to deliver the letter first. Ji Bu was really angry and waited for Cao Qiusheng to come.
When Cao Qiusheng arrived, he bowed to Ji Bu and said, "There is a proverb in the Chu region: It is better to get Ji Bu's promise than to get a hundred catties of gold. How did you get such a good reputation in the Liang and Chu areas?"
Besides, you and I are both from Chu. Wouldn’t it be great if I could make your name known to the world?
Why are you so distant from me?
Ji Bu was very happy to hear this, and welcomed him into the inner room, where he stayed for several months and was treated like a distinguished guest. Before leaving, I prepared a generous gift for him.
The reason why Ji Bu's reputation grew bigger and bigger was because Cao Qiusheng promoted it to him.
Ji Bu's younger brother Ji Xin was the most brave in Guanzhong. He was respectful and cautious to others, and he was a chivalrous and righteous man. Scholars from thousands of miles around rushed to work for him.
Because he killed someone, he fled to the state of Wu and hid in Yuan Ang's house. He served Yuan Ang as an elder brother and regarded Guan Fu, Ji Fu and others as brothers.
Lieutenant Zhi did not dare to treat him disrespectfully as he was a Sima who was subordinate to the lieutenant.
Some young people often use his name to do things.
At that time, Ji Xin was famous for his bravery and Ji Bu for his promise.
Ji Bu's half-brother Ding Gong served as Xiang Yu's general. He once pursued Han Emperor Gaozu and trapped him west of Pengcheng.
summary: Cao Qiusheng, a rhetorician, sought Ji Bu's favor through a letter from Baochangjun. Despite initial anger, Ji Bu welcomed him after Cao explained that he could enhance Ji Bu's reputation. Ji Bu's fame grew due to Cao's promotion. Ji Bu's half-brother Ding Gong, who had spared Liu Bang during a battle, was executed by Emperor Gaozu for disloyalty.

translation:
During the hand-to-hand fight, the king of Han was in danger and turned back to Ding Gong and said: Are two wise men going to persecute each other?
Ding Gong then led his troops to withdraw, and the king of Han was able to escape.
After Xiang Yu's death, Duke Ding went to pay homage to Emperor Gaozu. Emperor Gaozu asked him to be paraded in the military camp and said: Duke Chang was disloyal because he was a subject of Xiang Yu, and he was the one who caused King Xiang to lose the world.
So he beheaded Duke Ding and said: "I want all future ministers not to imitate Duke Ding!" Luan Bu was from Liang.
When Peng Yue was still a civilian, he had a relationship with Le Bu. Because of poverty, he worked as a laborer in Qi and was employed by Qi Diyi. hotel.
He left a few years later and was kidnapped and sold as a slave to the State of Yan.
He avenged his master and was elected as the captain by Yan general Zang Tu.
Later Zang Tu became king of Yan, and Lebu was appointed as a general.
When Zang Tu rebelled, the Han army attacked Yan and captured Le Bu.
The king of Liang, Peng Yue, found out about this and interceded with the Emperor of Han, asking for Le Bu to atone for his sins and let him be appointed as the official of the Liang Kingdom.
Peng Yue sent him as an envoy to Qi, but before he returned, the Han court summoned Peng Yue, accused him of treason, and killed all members of the Pengyue clan. Peng Yue's head was hung under the gate of Luoyang City for public display. He also issued an order from Shao: Anyone who cries or cares for Peng Yue's head will be arrested immediately.
Lebu returned from Qi and reported under Peng Yue's head. While offering sacrifices, he cried bitterly.
The messenger arrested Le Bu and reported it to the emperor.
The emperor summoned Le Bu and scolded him: Are you plotting rebellion with Peng Yue?
I forbid people to collect or see his head, but you still go to sacrifice and cry bitterly, which shows that you are conspiring with Peng Yue, and I will cook you to death as soon as possible.
Just as he was about to lift Lebu closer to the oil pan, Lebu turned around and said: I want to say something before I die. The emperor said: What did you say?
Le Bu said: When you were trapped in Pengcheng and defeated Rongyang and Chenggao, the reason why King Xiang could not successfully attack to the west was because King Peng was guarding Liang and united with Han to trouble the Chu army.
At that time, King Peng was a little sidelined. If he united with Chu, Han would be defeated. If he united with Mo, Chu would be defeated.
Moreover, in the siege of Gaixia, without King Peng, Xiang Yu would not have perished.
Now that the world has been peaceful, King Peng accepted the court's letter and became king, hoping to pass it on to his descendants for generations to come.
Now the imperial court is recruiting troops from the Liang Kingdom. King Peng is ill and cannot come, so he is suspected of treason.
I didn't see the fact that he wanted to rebel, but I punished him for trivial matters. I'm worried that all the meritorious officials will be in danger.
Now that King Peng is dead, it would be better for me to be alive than to be dead. Please cook it immediately.
So the emperor released him and worshiped him as captain.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Lebu was the prime minister of Yan State, and his official rank was general.
He publicly declared: If poverty fails to lower one's ambitions and humiliate one's body, one is not a good man; if wealth fails to bring comfort, one is not a wise man.
Therefore, he will give generous rewards to those who have been kind to him; he will definitely try to destroy those who have hatred towards him.
When Wu Chu rebelled, Lebu was named Langhou for his meritorious service. Once again, he was the prime minister of Yan State.
summary: Luan Bu, a former slave and general under Peng Yue, mourned Peng Yue after his execution for treason. Arrested and threatened with death, Luan Bu defended Peng Yue's loyalty and criticized the emperor's harshness. He was released and made a captain. Later, he served as prime minister of Yan and was known for rewarding kindness and avenging wrongs.

translation:
A few years later, Uncle Tian lost his official position for breaking the law.
Emperor Jing's brother Liang Xiaowang Liu Wu sent people to assassinate Yuan Ang, the minister in charge of discussing political affairs in the Han Dynasty. Emperor Jing summoned Uncle Tian to investigate the matter and fully grasped the facts.
After he came back, he reported it to Emperor Jing. Emperor Jing said: "Did King Xiao of Liang do this?" He replied: "It is true."
Emperor Jing asked: What is the specific situation?
Uncle Tian said: Your Majesty, it is best not to ask about King Liang Xiao's affair.
Now the King of Liang is being punished for not obeying the law, but for abandoning the laws of the Han Dynasty. If he is sentenced to death according to the law, the Queen Mother will not be able to eat well or sleep well, and Your Majesty will also be worried about it.
So Emperor Jing thought Uncle Tian was very virtuous and appointed him prime minister of Lu.
Uncle Tian was the prime minister of Lu. When he first took office, more than a hundred people reported to King Lu that he had taken away their property.
Uncle Tian caught the twenty leaders and whipped them, and said angrily: "Isn't King Lu your master?"
How dare you sue the master!
King Lu was deeply ashamed when he heard this. He took the money out of the treasury and asked Uncle Tian to pay it back to the people.
Uncle Tian said: King Lu will send someone to repay it himself. Otherwise, you become the bad guy and I become the good guy.
King Lu loved hunting, and Uncle Tian often followed him into the gardens. King Lu immediately stopped him and asked him to rest in the garden.
But Uncle Tian often sat outside his room to wrap himself in the open air, and never went into the house to rest. He said: "The king of Lu is wrapping his clothes in the open air, how can I wrap myself in the house alone?"
For this reason, King Lu did not go out much for hunting.
A few years later, Uncle Tian died in office. The State of Lu offered a hundred catties of gold as a sacrifice, but his youngest son Tian Ren refused to accept it, saying: Morally, the honor of his father cannot be harmed.
Because Tian Ren was strong and brave, he became a household official of General Wei Qing. He followed Wei Qing to attack the Xiongnu several times.
General Wei recommended him to Emperor Mowu, and he was appointed as a doctor. He was transferred to Erqianshi and served as prime minister for a long time. Later, he was dismissed due to some affairs.
Later, he was appointed as the governor of Sanhe County. When he returned to Beijing to report his affairs, he was in line with Emperor Wu's wishes and was appointed as the capital of Jingfu.
More than a month later, he was promoted to Prime Minister Sizhi.
A few years later, Liu Zheng, the crown prince of Emperor Wu, raised an army due to an incident. At that time, Tian Ren was in charge of opening and closing the city gates. He asked the prince to flee the city. He was exterminated for indulging the rebels.
Praise said: While Xiang Yu was heroic, Ji Bu was famous for his bravery in Chu State. He defeated the enemy many times and took up his banner. He can be called a hero!
Even when he was in trouble and became a slave, he still lived quietly without changing. What is the reason?
It's because he is conceited of his talents. Being insulted without feeling ashamed is to hone some of your deficient qualities. As a result, Ji Bu finally became a famous general in the early Han Dynasty.
A virtuous person attaches great importance to the value of his own death.
summary: Uncle Tian, a native of Zhao, served as a doctor under King Zhang Ao. When Zhang Ao was implicated in a plot against the emperor, Uncle Tian followed him to Chang'an in prison garb. After Zhang Ao's release, Uncle Tian became a county guard. Emperor Wen appointed him prime minister of Lu, where he handled disputes and discouraged King Lu from hunting. He died in office, and his son Tian Ren refused funeral gifts, later serving as a general under Wei Qing. Tian Ren was executed for allowing the crown prince to flee during a rebellion.

translation:
Emperor Xiaoxuan had five sons.
Note that the empress gave birth to Emperor Xiaoyuan, the urgent maggot gave birth to King Xian of Huaiyang, Zhiyin, the envoy of Wei gave birth to King Xiaoxiao of Chu, Xingxiao, the nephew of Gongsun, Prince Shuhusi, King Liu, and the nephew of Rong, Prince Ai of Zhongshan, died.
Huaiyang Xianwang Liu Qin was established as king in the third year of Yuankang, and his mother Zhang Shidan was favored by Emperor Xuan.
After Queen Huo was deposed, the emperor wanted to make Zhang Tuzi his queen.
As time went by, I was wary of Huo's intention to harm the crown prince, so I changed my mind and chose someone who had no sons in the harem and was cautious. So I made Wang Jiantun, a native of Changling, the queen, and asked her to raise the crown prince like a mother.
The queen was not favored and rarely slept with or met the emperor. Only Zhang Jiantun was favored the most.
When King Xian of Huaiyang grew up, he liked scriptures and laws, was smart and talented, and Emperor Xuan liked him very much.
The prince was kind-hearted and fond of Confucianism. Emperor Xuan praised King Xian several times and said, "You are really my son!"
I often wanted to make Zhang Jianzi the queen and Prince Xian the prince. However, because the prince grew up in civilian life, Emperor Xuan relied on the Xu family when he was young, and Empress Xu had been killed when he came to the throne. The prince lost his mother when he was young, so he couldn't bear it.
After a long time, Emperor Xuan summoned and made Wei Xuan the lieutenant of Huaiyang Kingdom because Wei Xuancheng, the son of the former prime minister Wei Xian, pretended to be crazy and gave the marquis to his brother. He was praised by the court for his knowledge of Confucian classics and noble conduct.
When Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan came to the throne, he ordered King Xian to go to the feudal country.
At this time, Zhang Biandan had passed away. King Xian had a maternal grandmother. His uncle Zhang Bo and his three brothers would be rewarded by King Xian if they went to Huaiyang to visit their mother every year.
Later, King Xian wrote a letter asking for the relocation of the Zhang family to Huaiyang. Zhang Bo wrote a letter saying he hoped to stay at his ancestral graves but refused to move.
King Xian resented him.
Later, when Zhang Bo went to Huaiyang, King Xian rewarded him less.
Zhang Bo said: The debt is several million. I hope King Xian will repay it for me.
King Xian refused. Zhang Bo left and sent his brother Zhang Guang to threaten King Xian, saying that he was even more lax in treating his grandmother. Zhang Bo wanted to write a letter to his mother asking for leave to go home.
King Xian sent someone to give Zhang Bo fifty pounds of gold.
Zhang Bo was happy and wrote back a letter of thanks. He praised King Xian very much with flattering words, and said: There are no good ministers in the court today, and disasters have occurred many times, which makes the court miserable. later.
The people all place their hopes on the king. Why does the king quietly do not ask to visit the court and assist the emperor?
His younger brother Zhang Guang persuaded King Xian several times to follow Zhang Bo's strategy. He himself went to the capital to lobby the powerful dignitaries to request an audience on King Xian's behalf.
King Xian did not adopt his opinion.
Later, Zhang Guang wanted to go to Chang'an. When he said goodbye to King Xian, he said that he would do his best to work with Zhang Bo to petition for the king's admission to the court.
The king is about to arrive in Chang'an and can rely on Marquis Pingyang.
When Zhang Guang heard that King Xian wanted to request an audience, he sent Pegasus to tell Zhang Bo.
Zhang Bo knew about King Xian's change of mind and sent another letter to King Xian, saying: "Zhang Bo is fortunate to be the king's confidant. He has made stupid suggestions several times, but they have not attracted your attention."
I traveled north to Yanzhao and other places, and wanted to visit the reclusive scholars in various places. I heard that there was a Mr. Si in Qi who was familiar with "Sima's Art of War" and was a talented general. Zhang Bo once paid a visit to him and took the opportunity to go and inquire about the ruling principles of the Five Emperors and Three Kings. His words were brilliant and could not be understood by ordinary people.
summary: Emperor Xiaoxuan had five sons. The empress gave birth to Emperor Xiaoyuan, while other consorts bore Huaiyang Xianwang Liu Qin, Chu Xiaowang Liu Xiao, Dongping Siwang Liu Yu, and Zhongshan Aiwang Liu Tong, who died young. Liu Qin, made king in the third year of Yuankang, was favored by Emperor Xuan due to his mother Zhang Shidan’s influence. After Empress Huo was deposed, Xuan initially wanted to make Zhang queen but feared for the crown prince’s safety, instead choosing Wang Jiantun, a childless and cautious woman, to raise the prince. Zhang remained the most favored consort. Liu Qin, intelligent and fond of scriptures, was admired by Xuan, who considered replacing the crown prince but relented due to the prince’s early loss of his mother. After Xuan’s death, Emperor Yuan ordered Liu Qin to his fief. Zhang Shidan died, and Liu Qin’s maternal uncle Zhang Bo and his brothers were rewarded for visits. Liu Qin requested the Zhang family’s relocation to Huaiyang, but Zhang Bo refused, causing resentment. Zhang Bo later demanded debt repayment and, after receiving gold, flattered Liu Qin in letters, urging him to seek court audience and assist the emperor. Liu Qin initially declined but eventually agreed, sending gold and gifts. Zhang Bo’s son-in-law Jingfang, favored by Emperor Yuan for his knowledge of the *I Ching*, shared court secrets with Zhang Bo, who fabricated claims of influence with officials. Liu Qin was persuaded to pursue audience, but Jingfang’s departure and Shi Xian’s exposure led to arrests. The emperor, sparing Liu Qin, sent an admonishing official to rebuke him, citing his correspondence with Zhang Bo as treasonous. Liu Qin apologized, and Zhang Bo and his brothers were exiled. Under Emperor Cheng, Liu Qin requested the exiles’ return, which was granted despite official objections. He died in his thirty-sixth year, succeeded by his son Liu Xuan, then grandson Liu Yan, whose line ended under Wang Mang.

translation:
The meaning of "Spring and Autumn" is that the most important thing is to be able to change one's past.
"The Book of Changes" says that if you use Imperata for sacrifices, you will not encounter any mistakes. It means that the ministers must correct their mistakes and purify themselves to assist the emperor, and then they can avoid mistakes.
You should be careful and vigilant, consider how to repent and change your behavior, make up for the heavy responsibility, and express the emperor's great kindness.
In this way, you will enjoy long-lasting wealth and honor, and the country will be stable.
At that time, King Liu Qin of Huaiyang took off his hat, kowtowed and apologized, saying: I failed to fulfill my duties as a king of princes, and my crime was so obvious that your Majesty could not bear to punish the crime according to law, so he showed great kindness and sent envoys to explain the truth and fulfill the duties of princes.
Considering that Zhang Bo's crime is particularly serious, he should be sentenced to death.
The minister Liu Qin is willing to reform himself wholeheartedly and accept the edict respectfully.
I should deserve to die.
The three brothers Jingfang and Zhang Bo were all exiled from the city, and their wives and children were exiled to the border.
When Emperor Cheng came to the throne, because King Huaiyang was his uncle as a relative, he was respected by Emperor Cheng, far above other princes and kings.
The King of Huaiyang wrote a letter stating that his uncle Zhang Bo was being bullied by Shi Xian and others, so he requested to return to his hometown for the exiled Zhang Bo's family.
The prime minister and the imperial censor impeached the King of Huaiyang again: He and Zhang Bo had communicated privately with each other in the past, and their intentions were not what a prince should have. Thanks to the emperor's grace, he was not punished. The matter happened before the pardon.
Instead of repenting, he quoted past events and thought he was upright, which was unbecoming of a prince and committed the crime of disrespect.
However, the emperor granted King Huaiyang's request and promised King Xian to move the exiles back.
King Xian died in his thirty-sixth year.
His son King Wen Liu Xuan succeeded to the throne and died after reigning for twenty-six years.
His son Liu Yan succeeded to the throne, but was cut off by Wang Mang.
Liu Xiao, King Xiao of Chu, was established as King Dingtao in the second year of Ganlu's reign, and was granted the title of King of Chu three years later. Emperor Cheng entered the dynasty during the Heping period. He was ill at that time. The emperor took pity on him and issued an edict: It is said that human beings are the most noble of life in the world, and filial piety is the most important thing in human behavior. King Liu Xiao of Chu has always been filial and kind. In the more than 20 years since he became a feudal country, he has not heard of any minor mistakes. I admire him very much.
Now he is suffering from bad luck and is seriously ill. The Master deplored it and said: What a sad fate! Can such a person suffer from such a disease?
I feel sorry for him.
He is kind and noble without appearing to be different from the public. How will the princes be encouraged?
Didn't "Shang Shu" say that? Rewards are given to virtuous people in recognition of their kindness. Now is the first month of the dynasty. King Xiao is ordered to come to court with one of his sons, and his son Liu Xun is named the Marquis of Guangqi with a settlement of 4,300 households in Guangqi County.
The next year, Liu Xiao died.
His son Liu Wen, King Huai, succeeded to the throne and died a year later. He had no sons and was cut off.
In the second year, Emperor Cheng appointed Liu Wen's younger brother Liu Yan, Marquis of Lu, as King Si.
He died in the 21st year of his reign, and his son Liu Yu succeeded to the throne, which was cut off by Wang Mang.
At the beginning, when he became emperor, Liu Jing, Liu Yu's younger brother, was appointed King of Dingtao.
When Liu Xun, Marquis of Guangqi, died, Mi was named Yanghou, and his son Liu Xian succeeded him.
Emperor Ping died without a son, so Wang Mang made Liu Xian's son Liu Ying his son, who succeeded Emperor Ping.
Wang Mang usurped the throne and made Liu Ying the Duke of Ding'an.
After Wang Mang was executed by the Han Dynasty, Liu Ying was in Chang'an during the Gengshi period. Fang Wang and others from Pingling knew the astronomical phenomena very well and believed that the Gengshi Emperor would definitely fail. Liu Ying was the one who should be established as emperor according to the imperial tradition. Together they sent troops to take Liu Ying to Linjing and established him as the emperor.
Emperor Gengshi sent Prime Minister Li Song to defeat them and kill Liu Ying.
Liu Zi, the king of Dongping, was established as king in the second year of Ganlu.
Emperor Yuan ascended the throne and went to the feudal state.
When he grew up, he committed a crime for colluding with bad people. The emperor refused to punish him because he was the closest relative. His master was in line with the country.
summary: Liu Xiao, Chu Xiaowang, was made king in the second year of Ganlu. Emperor Cheng, during a court visit, praised his filial piety and kindness, granting his son Liu Xun a marquisate. Liu Xiao died the next year, succeeded by his son Liu Wen, who died without heirs. Emperor Cheng then appointed Liu Wen’s brother Liu Yan as king, whose line ended under Wang Mang. Liu Jing, Liu Yu’s brother, was made King of Dingtao. Liu Xun’s descendant Liu Xian had a son, Liu Ying, whom Wang Mang made Duke of Ding’an after Emperor Ping’s death. During the Gengshi era, Liu Ying was proclaimed emperor by rebels but was killed by Gengshi’s forces. Liu Yu, Dongping Siwang, was made king in the second year of Ganlu. He committed crimes and was leniently treated by Emperor Yuan. Later, he served his mother poorly, leading to an imperial reprimand. He repented but, after Emperor Yuan’s death, showed disrespect by drinking and eating meat during mourning. He hanged a concubine who recorded his faults, leading to the reduction of his fief. He later reformed, and the emperor restored his lands. During a court visit, he requested books of the philosophers and *Historical Records*, but Wang Feng advised against it, citing their unsuitability for princes. Liu Yu died in his thirty-third year, succeeded by his son Liu Yun. During Emperor Ai’s reign, Liu Yun and his queen performed sacrifices at a stone formation, which was reported as treason. They were accused of cursing the emperor, and Liu Yun committed suicide. His fief was abolished but later restored by Wang Mang, who appointed Liu Kaiming as king. Liu Kaiming died without heirs, and his brother’s son Liu Xingkuang succeeded, but was killed by Wang Mang after a failed rebellion.

translation:
King Dongping Si died in the thirty-third year of his reign, and his son Yang King Liu Yun succeeded him.
During the reign of Emperor Ai, the ground of Wuyanwei Mountain swelled up on its own and was covered with grass, resembling the shape of a galloping road, and stood up on the side of the stone of Hushan Mountain.
Liu Yun and Queen Ye personally went to the stone to offer sacrifices, carved a stone like the stone in Hushan, used Shubeicao as a god, and offered sacrifices together.
In the third year of Jianping, Xifu Gong, Sun Chong and others relied on the favored minister Dong Xian to report the matter.
At this time, Emperor Ai was ill and disgusted with many things. He handed the matter over to the relevant departments, arrested King Yang and Queen Ye, put them in prison for interrogation, and sent wizard Fu Gong, maid Hehuan and others to curse the emperor during sacrifices and pray for Liu Yun to become emperor.
Liu Yun and Gao Shang, who knew about the disaster, observed the stars and said that the emperor's illness would definitely not be cured, and Liu Yun should win the world.
The standing stone symbolizes the rise of Emperor Xuan.
Relevant departments requested that King Yang be killed, and the emperor issued an edict to depose him and move him to Fangling.
Liu Yun committed suicide and Ye was executed and abandoned in the market.
In the seventeenth year of his reign, the feudal state was eliminated.
In the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, Wang Mang wanted to change Emperor Ai's approach, so he petitioned the Empress Dowager to appoint Liu Yun's prince Liu Kaiming as King of Dongping, and he also appointed Liu Chengdu, the grandson of King Si, as King of Zhongshan.
Liu Kaiming reigned for three years and died without any sons.
He also established Xingkuang, the son of Liu Kaiming's elder brother Yanxiang Hou Liu Xin, as the king of Sechu, succeeding Liu Tilong.
Wang Ling assumed the position of regent, and Yizhan, the governor of Sejing, and Xingzhi of Leisubao planned to send troops to kill Yuling, and he was declared emperor.
The army was defeated and all were destroyed by Wang Ling.
Liu Tong, the Ai King of Zhongshan, was established as the King of Qinghe in the 52nd year of Niu. Three years later, he moved to Zhongshan, but he did not go to the feudal country because he was young.
In the fourth year of Jianzhao's reign, he died in his official residence and was buried in Duling. He had no sons and was cut off.
The Queen Mother went back to live in the Rong family of her relatives.
Emperor Xiaoyuan had three sons.
Queen Wang gave birth to Xiao Chengdi, Fu Zhaoyi gave birth to Liu Kang, King of Dingtao, and Feng Zhaoyi gave birth to Liu Xing, King of Zhongshan.
Liu Kang, the co-king of Dingtao, was established as King of Jiyang in the third year of Yongguang.
Eight years later, he moved to Shanyang King.
After another eight years, he moved to Dingtao.
King Dingtao Gong was loved by Emperor Yuan when he was young. When he grew up, he was versatile and familiar with music. The emperor valued him very much.
His mother Fu Zhaoyi was favored again and almost replaced the queen and crown prince.
The incident was recorded in "Emperor Yuan" and "Standard's Biography".
After Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he abided by the wishes of the late emperor and treated King Dingtao Gong differently from other kings.
He died in the 19th year of his reign and was succeeded by his son Liu Xin.
Fifteen years after he ascended the throne, Emperor Cheng had no sons and was conscripted into the palace as the crown prince.
summary: Liu Tong, Zhongshan Aiwang, was made King of Qinghe and later moved to Zhongshan but died young without heirs. Emperor Xiaoyuan had three sons: Empress Wang gave birth to Emperor Cheng, Fu Zhaoyi to Liu Kang of Dingtao, and Feng Zhaoyi to Liu Xing of Zhongshan. Liu Kang, favored by Emperor Yuan, was treated specially by Emperor Cheng. He died after nineteen years, succeeded by his son Liu Xin, who became Emperor Ai. Emperor Ai honored his father as Emperor Gong. Liu Xing, Zhongshan Xiaowang, was made king and later moved to Zhongshan. Emperor Cheng considered him as heir but chose Liu Xin instead. Liu Xing died after thirty years, succeeded by his son Liu Yan, who became Emperor Ping. Emperor Ping’s line ended under Wang Mang.

translation:
Because the prince wanted to serve as a great clan and could not only care about his private relatives, the emperor appointed Liu Jing, the son of King Chu Si, as King Dingtao to succeed King Gong.
When Emperor Cheng died and the crown prince ascended the throne, he was the Emperor Xiaoai.
Two years after he ascended the throne, he honored the King of Gong as the Emperor of Gong, placed his dormitory temple in the capital, and arranged the order of Zhao and Mu with the same etiquette as Emperor Xiaoyuan.
Tao Wangjing was changed to King Xindu.
Liu Xing, the Xiaowang of Zhongshan, was established as King of Xindu in the second year of Jianzhao.
Fourteen years later, he moved to the throne of Zhongshan. When Emperor Cheng was discussing the establishment of a crown prince, Kong Guang, the imperial censor, believed that "Shangshu" contained lessons from the demise of the Yin Dynasty and inherited the throne. When the elder brother died, the younger brother succeeded. King Zhongshan was the son of Emperor Yuan and should be the next emperor.
Emperor Cheng believed that King Zhongshan had no talent and they were brothers, so they could not enter the ancestral temple together.
Both Wang and Zhao Zhao wanted Emperor Ai to be the crown prince, so they made him the crown prince.
The emperor named Xiao Wang's uncle Feng Shen the Marquis of Yixiang, and also granted Xiao Wang Wanhu the title to express his comfort.
He reigned for thirty years and died. His son Liu Yan succeeded to the throne.
After reigning for seven years, Emperor Ai died without a son, so he recruited Liu Shu, King of Zhongshan, to the palace and ascended the throne, becoming Emperor Ping.
The Empress Dowager believed that the emperor was a descendant of Emperor Cheng, so she established Liu Chengdu, the son of Taoxiang Qinghou, the grandson of King Shu Pingsi, as King of Zhongshan, succeeding King Xiao.
It was cut off when Wang Mang died.
Zan said: The descendants of Emperor Xiaoyuan are all over the world, but the heirs are cut off in the generation of his grandchildren. Isn't it God's will?
Huaiyang Xianyu was very smart among the princes at that time. He seduced him and almost fell into a state of immorality.
"The Book of Songs" says that greedy people are the black sheep, and this has been true in ancient and modern times.
summary: The commentary notes that Emperor Xiaoyuan’s descendants spread widely but were cut off in his grandchildren’s generation, perhaps by fate. Liu Qin was intelligent but nearly fell into immorality due to Zhang Bo’s greed, echoing the *Book of Songs*’ warning about greedy people.

translation:
Zhang Shizhi, courtesy name Ji, was born in Duyang, Nanyang.
Lives with his brother Zhang Zhong. He used his family wealth to buy a job as a knight and served Emperor Wen of Han. He had not been promoted for many years and had no reputation.
Zhang Shizhi said: I feel uneasy about being a Langguan for a long time and depleting my brother's family property.
I want to automatically request to be dismissed and go home.
The lieutenant-general Yuan Ang knew that he was talented and could not bear to see him leave, so he asked Zhang Shizhi to be transferred to fill the vacant post.
After Zhang Shizhi's audience was over, he took advantage of this opportunity to step forward and state things that would benefit the country and the people.
Emperor Wen said: Be realistic. Don't talk too much about ancient things, but talk about what can be implemented in the present.
So Zhang Shizhi talked about the affairs between Qin and Mo, and talked about the reasons for the demise of Qin Dynasty and the rise of Han Dynasty.
Emperor Wen praised Zhang Shizhi and promoted him to the rank of Servant.
Zhang Shizhi traveled with the emperor and visited the tiger enclosure. The emperor asked Shang Lin about the registration of various animal books and asked more than a dozen questions. Shang Lin looked around but couldn't answer.
The stingy man who was in charge of the tiger enclosure answered the emperor's questions on behalf of Lieutenant Shang Lin. He was very detailed and wanted to show that his answers were as fluent as the responses to the dance.
Emperor Wen said: Shouldn't officials be like this?
You can't go to Lieutenant Lin!
So Zhang Shizhi was ordered to declare the stingy husband as the Shanglin Order.
Zhang Shishang stepped forward and said: What kind of person does Your Majesty think Jianghou Zhou Bo is?
The Emperor replied: A loyal elder.
Asked again: What kind of person is Zhang Xiangru, the Marquis of Cambodia?
The emperor still replied: A loyal elder.
Zhang Shizhi said: Jianghou and Jianyanghou are known as loyal elders, but these two people couldn't even speak when they talked about things. Should people be allowed to imitate this stingy man’s eloquent talk?
Moreover, because the Qin Dynasty appointed those scribes who were good at writing, the scribes competed with each other on the speed of doing things and the harshness of supervision. However, the disadvantage of doing so was that they just followed the rules and there was no mercy at all.
Because of this, the emperor could not hear his own faults, and he declined day by day. By the second generation, the world fell apart.
Now that Your Majesty has promoted a stingy man to a higher level because of his eloquence and eloquence, I am worried that people in the world will follow the trend and rush to exaggerate instead of being practical.
Moreover, the following imitates the response from above, which is faster than a shadow and echoes. Your Majesty, you can do whatever you want, so you must be cautious! Emperor Wen agreed and said: OK!
So no more promotion of stingy men.
The emperor got into the carriage and summoned Zhang Shizhi to accompany him. As the car moved forward slowly, the emperor asked about the shortcomings of the Qin Dynasty, and Zhang Shizhi answered truthfully.
When they arrived at the palace, the emperor granted Zhang Shizhi the official carriage order.
Soon, the prince and the King of Liang entered the court together in a car. They passed by Sima Gate without getting off the car. At that time, Zhang Shizhi chased after him and stopped the prince and the King of Liang from entering the palace gate.
summary: Zhang Shizhi, a native of Nanyang, served Emperor Wen of Han but remained unpromoted for years. He sought to resign, but Lieutenant-General Yuan Ang recognized his talent and arranged a transfer. During an audience, Emperor Wen advised him to focus on present matters rather than ancient ones. Zhang Shizhi discussed the fall of Qin and the rise of Han, earning promotion to Servant. While visiting a tiger enclosure, the emperor questioned officials about animal records. A lowly keeper answered fluently, impressing the emperor, who wanted to promote him. Zhang Shizhi cautioned against valuing eloquence over substance, citing Qin's decline due to such practices. The emperor agreed and halted the promotion. Later, Zhang Shizhi stopped the prince and King of Liang from entering the palace gate without dismounting, accusing them of disrespect. Empress Dowager Bo pardoned them, but Emperor Wen appointed Zhang Shizhi as a senior official. At Ba Ling, the emperor lamented the difficulty of securing his tomb, but Zhang Shizhi argued that greed, not materials, determines security. Promoted to Tingwei, he handled cases with fairness. When a man startled the emperor's horse, Zhang Shizhi imposed a fine, not execution, insisting on legal consistency. In another case, he opposed executing a thief's entire clan for stealing from Gaozu Temple, arguing proportionality. Emperor Wen approved his verdict. After Emperor Jing's accession, Zhang Shizhi feared retribution for past offenses but was forgiven. He later died of illness.

translation:
At that time, the Huns had recently invaded Chaona and killed Sun Yin, the captain of Beidi County.
The emperor was worried about the Huns' invasion, so he finally asked Feng Tang: "How do you know that I cannot appoint Lian Po and Li Mu?"
Feng Tang replied: I heard that in ancient times, kings sent generals to go on expeditions. Before leaving, they knelt down and pushed the cart, saying: I will decide the affairs within the country, and the general will decide the matters outside the country. Military merits, titles and rewards are all decided by the general, and he will report to the court when he returns. This is not empty talk.
My grandfather said that when Li Mu led troops to guard the border with Tongguo, he used all the taxes collected from the military trading market to reward the soldiers. The rewards were decided by the generals and the court did not interfere.
Entrusting him with important tasks and ordering him to succeed, Li Mu could use his wisdom and talent to select 1,300 qualified chariots, 13,000 cavalry who were good at shooting, and 100,000 elite soldiers. Relying on this force, he could drive out the Xiongnu Chanyu in the north, defeat Shu Hu, and destroy Danlin; suppress the powerful Qin in the west; and resist Han and Wei in the south.
At this time, Tangguo almost became the overlord.
After that, Wang Qian happened to come to the throne. His mother was originally a singing artist. When Wang Qian came to the throne, he believed the slander of his favored minister Guo Kai and finally had Li Mu killed and replaced him with Yan Ju.
Therefore, the army was defeated and the soldiers fled and were destroyed by Qin.
Now I heard privately that Wei Shang was appointed as the prefect of Yunzhong. He used all the taxes from the military market to reward the soldiers. He also used his personal salary to kill cattle every five days and entertain guests, military officials and close subordinate officials. Therefore, the Xiongnu stayed far away and did not dare to approach the Yunzhong Fortress.
The Huns once invaded, and Wei Shang led his troops to fight back, killing many enemy troops.
Those soldiers were all sons of ordinary people. They came from Tianwen to join the army. How could they know military laws and regulations such as "Chi Ji" and "Wu Fu".
They fought hard all day long, beheaded enemies, and captured prisoners. But when they reported their merits to the Yamen, as long as they did not comply with one sentence, the judges would invoke the law to punish them.
Their rewards are not fulfilled but the laws of the justices are enforced.
I think His Majesty's laws are too fastidious, the rewards are too light, and the punishments are too severe.
Moreover, Wei Shang, the governor of Yunzhong County, was only six heads short of the number of enemy soldiers he reported killed. Your Majesty handed him over to the judicial officer for punishment, deprived him of his title and sentenced him to one year in prison.
From this point of view, even if His Majesty gets Li Mu, it is impossible to reuse him.
I was indeed stupid and violated a taboo, a capital crime!
Emperor Wen was happy after hearing this.
On the same day, he ordered Feng Tang to send an envoy to Chijie to pardon Wei Shang, and appointed him as the governor of Yunzhong County again. He also appointed Feng Tang as the chariot and cavalry captain, in charge of the lieutenants and chariot warriors of various counties and countries.
Ten years later, Emperor Jing of Han came to the throne and asked Feng Tang to be the prime minister of Chu.
After Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he issued an imperial edict to recommend virtuous people and recommended Feng Tang.
Feng Tang was over ninety years old at the time and could no longer hold an official position, so he made his son Feng Sui the official.
Feng Sui, also known as Wang Sun, was also an outstanding talent.
Wei Shang was from Huaili.
Ji An, whose courtesy name is Changru, was born in Puyang.
His ancestors were favored by Nao in ancient times.
summary: Feng Tang, known for filial piety, served Emperor Wen. The emperor lamented not having generals like Lian Po and Li Mu to fight the Xiongnu. Feng Tang boldly claimed the emperor could not use them, citing harsh laws and unfair rewards. He used the example of Wei Shang, a capable governor punished for minor discrepancies in battle reports. Emperor Wen, initially angered, later pardoned Wei Shang and appointed Feng Tang as chariot and cavalry captain. Under Emperor Jing, Feng Tang became prime minister of Chu. Emperor Wu later recommended him, but he was too old to serve.

translation:
The emperor is yearning for Confucian scholarship and respects Gongsun Hong. When things get more complicated, the lower-level officials resort to tricks and the people use tricks to escape.
The emperor analyzed the regulations and added additional laws. Zhang Tang and others repeatedly reported the cases decided by the Tingwei to the emperor for ruling, thereby gaining his favor.
However, Ji An often slandered Confucianism and accused Gongsun Hong and others face to face of blindly resorting to deceit and cleverness in order to cater to the emperor's intentions and win the favor of the emperor. The swordsman and penman specially analyzed the legal provisions one-sidedly and cleverly slandered them, framed people in the law, and thought they had merit for this.
The emperor valued Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang more. Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang deeply hated Ji An. Even the emperor disliked him and wanted to kill him for an excuse.
When Gongsun Hong became the prime minister, he made a speech to the emperor and said: The area under the jurisdiction of You Nei Shi is home to many high-ranking officials and royal families, and it is difficult to govern. It is not that ministers who are usually well-known and hold important positions in the court are not qualified. Please transfer Ji An to be You Nei Shi.
Ji An had been the internal history of You for several years, and he had not slackened his official duties.
The general Wei Qing was already more noble, and his sister Wei Zifu became the queen, but Ji An treated Wei Qing as an equal.
Someone advised Ji An and said: In the past, the emperor wanted all ministers to be humble to the general. Now that the general is respected and valued by the emperor, his status is even more noble. You have to kneel down and worship.
Ji An said: "If the general has guests who bow his hands as equals, isn't that respecting him?"
When the general heard this, he thought Ji An was more virtuous. He asked him many times for advice on difficult matters related to the country and the court, and treated Ji An more favorably than usual.
Liu An, the king of Huainan, conspired to rebel. He was afraid of Ji An and said: This man likes to speak bluntly to persuade, stick to his integrity, and will sacrifice his life for justice. As for persuading Prime Minister Gongsun Hong, it is as easy as teaching children to do things.
The emperor had already conquered the Xiongnu many times and achieved success, so Ji An's words were even less adopted.
When Ji An was in Jiuqing, Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang were the lower-level officials.
When Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang gradually became noble and equal to Ji An, Ji An again accused and slandered Gongsun Hong and Zhang Tang.
Soon, Gongsun Hong was promoted to prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Pingju; Zhang Tang was promoted to the imperial censor; the assistants such as the prime minister and Shi who were under Ji An's jurisdiction were all promoted to the same status as Ji An, and some were promoted to more important positions than him.
Ji An was narrow-minded and could not help but complain a little. When he went to see the emperor, he said: Your Majesty uses his ministers like stacks of firewood, and those who come later take precedence.
After Ji An left, the emperor said: "A person cannot be uneducated. If you think about Ji An's words, you will be very stupid every day."
Soon after, King Hunxie of the Xiongnu led his troops to surrender, and the Han Dynasty conscripted 20,000 vehicles to pick them up.
The public treasury had no money, so it had to borrow horses from the people.
Some of the people hid their horses, so they couldn't get enough of them.
The emperor was angry and wanted to kill the magistrate of Chang'an.
Ji An said: The magistrate of Chang'an County is not guilty. Only if he kills me, Ji An, will the people be willing to sacrifice their horses.
Moreover, these Huns betrayed their Shanyu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. If the Han Dynasty slowly provided them with post carriages from the counties along the way to transport them, how could it disturb the whole country and make its own people tired and sleepy to serve these Huns?
The emperor was silent.
When King Hunxie came, more than 500 merchants who did business with the Xiongnu surrenderers were sentenced to death for their crimes.
Ji An entered the palace and asked to use his free time to avoid the crowd. He met the emperor in the Gaomen Hall of the Weiyang Palace and said: In the past, the Huns attacked the border fortresses on the road to our country, severing the friendly relations with relatives. We, the Han Dynasty, raised troops to attack, and the number of casualties was too many to count, and the money spent was counted in tens of billions.
I was foolish enough to think that when I acquired the Huns, I would give them as slaves and maids to the families of those who died in the war. I would also distribute the property captured after defeating the enemy to these people to comfort the people of the world for their hard work and satisfy the hearts of the people.
Although this cannot be the case now, King Hunxie led tens of thousands of his tribesmen to surrender, but he emptied the national treasury to reward them, and conscripted kind-hearted people to serve them as if they were arrogant.
How did the ignorant people know that when they were asked to buy local supplies in Chang'an, the eloquent legal officials punished them with the crime of smuggling contraband out of the border?
Even though Your Majesty could not use the supplies captured from the Huns to comfort the people of the world, but still used vague and unclear legal provisions to kill more than 500 ignorant people, I think it is not appropriate for Your Majesty to punish him like this.
The emperor refused to listen and said, "I haven't heard what Ji An said for a long time, and now I'm talking nonsense again."
A few months later, Ji An committed a minor crime, which coincided with the general amnesty, and he was only relieved of his official position.
So Ji An lived in seclusion in the countryside for several years.
After a few years, when the five-baht coin was re-minted, many people among the people minted coins privately, especially in the hometown of Chu State.
summary: Ji An, from Puyang, served Emperor Wu. He was known for his blunt advice and disdain for trivialities. Sent to inspect conflicts, he deemed them unworthy of imperial attention. During a famine, he distributed grain without authorization, earning the emperor's favor. As a governor, he favored quiet governance, delegating tasks and achieving stability. In court, he criticized the emperor's hypocrisy and opposed Confucian scholars. He clashed with officials like Zhang Tang, accusing them of manipulating laws. Despite his integrity, he was demoted for minor offenses. Later appointed governor of Huaiyang, he warned General Li Xi against Zhang Tang's cunning. Ji An died after ten years, leaving a legacy of principled governance.

translation:
At that time, Zheng was proud of his chivalrous deeds and rescued Zhang Yu, the general of King Xiao of Liang, from the trouble, and his reputation spread throughout the Liang-Chu region.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, he sacrificed his life for the prince.
During every five-day holiday, stagecoaches are often set up in the suburbs of Chang'an to invite or thank guests, working day and night until dawn, which is often not thoughtful.
Zheng Zhuang liked the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi. He admired the elderly and virtuous people, fearing that they would not be satisfied with them.
Although he was young and held a low official position, the close friends he made were all famous scholars from his grandfather's generation.
Emperor Wu Liu Che ascended the throne, and Zheng Zhuang was successively promoted to lieutenant of Lu State, prefect of Jinan County, prime minister of Jiangdu State, and finally to Jiuqing as the right internal history.
Because of his involvement in the dispute between Wu'an Hou Tianchi and Wei Qihou Dou Ying, he was demoted to Zhan Shi, and later promoted to Da Sinong.
Zheng Zhuang, as a high official, warned the gatekeeper: When guests arrive, please come in immediately. No matter whether they are noble or cheap, do not wait at the door.
He performs the courtesy of a host to his guests and treats his guests humbly with his noble status.
Zheng Zhuang has a clean character and does not acquire any private property. He relies on his salary and rewards to provide for his elderly friends.
But the gift he gave to people was just a plate of food.
Every time he goes to court, when the emperor is free, he always makes remarks without praising the wise people in the world.
When recommending scholars, prime ministers, historians and other subordinate officials, he praised them with great enthusiasm and often mentioned that he thought they were more talented than himself.
He never calls his subordinates by their first names, and talks to them as if he is afraid of hurting them.
I heard the kind words spoken by others and recommended them to the emperor, but I was afraid that I would be too slow.
Therefore, all the scholars in Jingshan Yishu praised Zhengzhuang in unison.
Zheng Zhuang was sent to inspect the breach of the Yellow River, and he applied for a five-day leave to repair his luggage.
The emperor said: I heard that Zheng Zhuang traveled thousands of miles without food. Now I am applying for leave to pack my luggage. Why?
However, when Zheng Zhuang was discussing matters in the court, he often echoed and catered to the emperor's wishes and did not dare to clearly state whether his position was right or wrong.
The Han Dynasty conquered the Xiongnu and recruited the Yi tribes from all directions. The country spent a lot of money and became increasingly depleted of financial and material resources.
When Zheng Zhuang was appointed as the chief minister, some of the people he recommended and the guests who were familiar with him were engaged in transportation for the chief minister, and they owed a lot of money.
Sima An, the governor of Huaiyang County, exposed this incident, and Zheng Zhuang committed a crime. After Nasu atones for his crime, he was demoted to a commoner.
Soon, he temporarily served as the chief historian in the Prime Minister's Mansion.
He was also promoted to the post of prefect of Runan County. He died in office a few years later.
Due to Zheng's status at that time, six or seven of his brothers had an official rank of two thousand shi.
Yinzhuang and Ji'an were originally listed in Jiuqing, so they paid attention to personal moral cultivation.
The two men resigned from office midway, and the guests became even more scattered.
After Zheng died at that time, his family had no property left.
summary: Zheng Zhuang, from Chen County, admired Huangdi and Laozi teachings. He treated guests humbly, regardless of status, and lived frugally, using his salary to support friends. He recommended scholars enthusiastically, often praising them as superior to himself. However, he avoided taking clear stances in court, echoing the emperor's wishes. During the Xiongnu campaigns, his recommendations led to financial mismanagement, resulting in his demotion. He died as governor of Runan, leaving no property. The text reflects on the fickleness of human relationships, noting that guests flock to the powerful but abandon the fallen.

translation:
Zhang Cang, a native of Yangwu, Henan, was fond of writing, music and calendars.
In the Qin Dynasty, he served as censor and was in charge of household registration albums all over the world.
He fled back to his hometown because he broke the law.
When Pei Gong was marching through Yangwu, Zhang Cang followed Pei Gong as a guest to attack Nanyang.
When Zhang Cang was about to be executed, he took off his clothes and leaned on the chopping block of the torture instrument, revealing his tall figure and fat muscles as white as gourds. At that time, Wang Ling saw Zhang Cang and was very surprised by this beauty, so he told Pei Gong that he would not be punished by beheading if he was pardoned.
So he entered Wuguan in the west and arrived in Xianyang.
Pei Gong became the king of Han, entered Hanzhong, and returned to the army to pacify the Sanqin area.
Chen Yu drove away Zhang Er, king of Changshan, and Zhang Er defected to the king of Han. The king of Han appointed Zhang Cang as the governor of Changshan County.
Following Han Xin to attack Zhao, Zhang Cang captured Chen Yu.
After the Zhao area was pacified, the King of Han appointed Zhang Cang as acting prime minister to guard against border bandits.
Soon he was moved to the state of Zhao and became the prime minister of Zhao Wang Zhang Er.
Zhang Er died, and Zhang Cang became his son Zhang Ao, the prime minister.
Later, he was appointed as the Prime Minister of Daiguo.
King Zang Tu of Yan rebelled, and Zhang Cang served as the Prime Minister and accompanied the army to attack Zang Lai. He was granted the title of Marquis of Beiping and was granted a settlement of 1,200 households.
Zhang Cang changed his plan, and one month later, he made Liehou the leader for four years.
At that time, Xiao He was appointed as the prime minister, and Zhang Cang had been the censor under the pillar since the Qin Dynasty. He was familiar with the world's atlas and household registration, and was good at calculating the calendar. Therefore, Zhang Cang was appointed to serve in the prime minister's mansion as a lieutenant, in charge of the books sent by the county.
Ying Bu rebelled, and the Han Dynasty established the prince Liu Chang as the King of Huainan, and Zhang Cang as the Prime Minister of Huainan.
After serving for fourteen years, he was promoted to the imperial censor.
Zhou Chang was from Peijun.
His cousin Zhou Ke and he were both soldiers of the Qin Dynasty in Surabaya.
When Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty raised an army in Peixian County, he defeated the governor and supervisor of the Sishui County, so the two brothers Zhou Ke and Zhou Chang went to Pei Gong as soldiers. Pei Gong took Zhou Chang as the flag bearer and Zhou Ke as the guest in the tent.
Follow the army into the pass to reduce the Qin Dynasty.
Peigong was the king of Han, with Zhou Ke as the censor and Zhou Chang as the lieutenant.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, the Chu army surrounded the King of Han in Rongyang. The situation was critical. After the King of Han escaped, he asked Zhou Ke to defend Rongyang.
The Chu army defeated Rongyang and planned to appoint Zhou Ke as general. Zhou Ke scolded him and said: Surrender to the King of Han as soon as possible!
Otherwise, you will be a prisoner today!
Xiang Yu was furious and had Zhou Ke killed.
The king of Han then appointed Zhou Chang as the imperial censor.
He often followed the King of Han to defeat Xiang Yu.
In the sixth year of the Han Dynasty, Zhou Changyu Xiao He, Cao Shen and others were granted the title of Fenyin Marquis at the same time.
Zhou Ke's son Zhou Cheng was granted the title Gao Jinghou because of his father's death.
summary: Zhang Cang, from Yangwu, Henan, was a scholar of writing, music, and calendars. He served as a censor under the Qin Dynasty, managing household registries, but fled home after breaking the law. He later joined Pei Gong (Liu Bang) as a guest, and was spared execution after Wang Ling admired his physique. He followed Pei Gong to Xianyang, served as governor of Changshan, and helped capture Chen Yu. He became prime minister of Zhao and Dai, and was made Marquis of Beiping for suppressing a rebellion. As censor-in-chief, he used his expertise in calendars and registries to serve in the prime minister's office. He later became prime minister of Huainan and then censor-in-chief. He corrected the calendar, adopting the Qin system with October as the new year, and advocated for water virtue. He served Wang Ling like a father after being saved by him. He was dismissed after opposing Gongsun Chen's proposal for Han's earth virtue, which was later confirmed by a yellow dragon sighting. He died around age 100, leaving writings on yin-yang and calendars.
rel_path: 汉书/传/张周赵任申屠传

translation:
Zhou Chang was strong and upright, and dared to speak out. Officials from Xiao He and Cao Shen down were cautious and despicable towards him.
Zhou Chang once played an important role when Emperor Gao was having a banquet. Emperor Gao was hugging Qi Ji, and Zhou Chang retreated.
Emperor Gao caught up with Zhou Chang, rode on his neck and asked, "What kind of monarch am I?"
Zhou Lu raised his head and said: Your Majesty is the lord of Jie and Zhou.
Then the emperor laughed, but he was still afraid of him.
At that time, Emperor Gao wanted to depose the crown prince and make Qi Ji's son Ruyi the crown prince. The ministers insisted on admonishing and arguing, but they failed. The emperor gave up because of his plan to keep Zhang Liang as a marquis.
However, Zhou Chang argued vigorously in the court. When the emperor asked him for his reasons, Zhou Chang was very angry and said: I know that I cannot tell you, but I have always known that I cannot do it.
Your Majesty wants to depose the crown prince, but I refuse to accept the order every time.
The emperor smiled happily and stopped deposing the prince.
Empress Lu eavesdropped in the Shuxiang room. When she saw Zhou Chang, she knelt down and thanked him, saying: Without your force, the prince would have been deposed.
This year, Qi Ji's son Ruyi became the king of Zhao, and he was only ten years old. Gaozu was worried that he would not be able to protect himself after his death.
Zhao Yao was serving as the imperial censor of Fuxi at that time. Fang Yugong, a native of Zhao, said to Zhou Chang, the imperial censor: Although your subordinate Zhao Yao is very young, he is a genius. You must pay special attention to him and let him replace you in the future.
Zhou Chang smiled and said: "Zhao Yao is young and is a small official with a sword and a pen. Why would you exalt him like this?"
Soon, Zhao Yao served Gaozu. Gaozu was alone and unhappy, humming tragic songs. The officials did not know why the emperor was like this.
Zhao Yao came in to say hello and asked: "Your Majesty is unhappy because King Zhao is young and Mrs. Qi is at odds with Empress Lu. Are you worried that King Zhao will not be able to protect himself after you live forever?"
Emperor Gaozu said: I am privately worried and don’t know what strategy to use.
Zhao Yao said: Your Majesty only needs to arrange a noble and strong prime minister for King Zhao. He is someone who is always respected and feared by Empress Lu, the prince, and the ministers.
Emperor Gaozu said: That’s right.
This is what I want to do, but who among the ministers can do it?
Zhao Yao said: Zhou Chang, the imperial censor, is a strong and upright man. From Empress Lu to the crown prince, as well as the ministers, they are usually afraid of him.
Only Zhou Chang can.
Gaozu said: OK.
So he summoned Zhou Chang and said: I must trouble you, and you must be the prime minister for me.
Zhou Chang cried and said: I have followed your majesty from the beginning. Why did your majesty abandon me to the vassal kingdoms?
Emperor Gaozu said: I know very well that this is demoting you from the official position, but I am secretly worried about King Zhao. After much thought, I think you can't be in this position except you.
You'd better not refuse and force yourself to go and take up the post!
So Zhou Chang, the imperial censor, was appointed as the prime minister of Zhao.
Long after Zhou Chang left, Emperor Gaozu held the seal of the imperial censor and touched it and said: Who can be the imperial censor?
He looked at Zhao Yao carefully and said: No one can replace Zhao Yao.
So he worshiped Zhao Yao as the censor.
summary: Zhou Chang, from Pei, served as a soldier under Pei Gong with his cousin Zhou Ke. Zhou Ke died defending Xingyang against Xiang Yu, and Zhou Chang became censor-in-chief. He was known for his bluntness, once calling Emperor Gaozu a tyrant. He opposed deposing the crown prince, earning gratitude from Empress Lü. He was appointed prime minister of Zhao to protect Prince Ruyi, despite his reluctance. After Gaozu's death, Empress Lü summoned and killed Ruyi; Zhou Chang died of illness three years later. His descendants lost the marquisate.
rel_path: 汉书/传/张周赵任申屠传

translation:
Zhao Yao also had military merits in the past and had food and towns. As a censor, he accompanied the army to attack Chen Jinji and was granted the title of Marquis of Jiangyi.
When Emperor Gaozu passed away, the Queen Mother sent envoys to summon King Zhao to the capital. Zhao Prime Minister Zhou Chang told King Zhao that he was ill and could not go.
The envoy returned to Zhao State for the third time. Zhou Chang said: Emperor Gao entrusted King Zhao to his protection. The king was young. He heard that the Queen Mother resented Madam Qi and wanted to summon King Zhao to kill him.
I dare not send King Zhao away. King Zhao is ill and cannot accept the imperial edict to go.
The Queen Mother was furious and sent envoys to summon Prime Minister Zhao.
When Prime Minister Zhao arrived in Beijing, he paid a visit to the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother scolded Zhou Chang and said, "Don't you know that I hate the Qi family?"
He didn’t even send King Zhao here!
After Zhou Chang was summoned to Beijing, Empress Gao sent envoys to summon King Zhao.
As expected, King Zhao came to Beijing and was poisoned to death after arriving in Chang'an for more than a month.
Zhou Chang refused to go to court due to illness. He died three years later and was given the title of Mourning Hou.
It was passed down to the marquis to his son, and then to Sun Zhouyi, who violated the law and was removed from the marquis state.
Emperor Jing also made Zhou Chang's grandson Zhou Zuoche the Marquis of Anyang. He was removed from the Marquis State due to his crimes.
At the beginning, after Zhao Yao replaced Zhou Chang as the imperial censor, Emperor Gaozu died and served Emperor Hui until his death.
In the first year of Gaohou, Gaohou resented Zhao Yao for proposing a strategy to protect King Zhao Ruyi, so he convicted Zhao Yao and asked Guang'ahou to appoint Ao as the censor.
Ren Ao, a native of Peijun, worked as a jailer when he was young.
Emperor Gaozu once escaped from the pursuit of officials. The officials captured Empress Lu and acted frivolously towards her.
Ren Ao always valued Gaozu, so he was furious and injured the minor official who was guarding Empress Lu.
When Emperor Gaozu started to raise troops, Ren Ao followed Zhidan as a guest and became the censor, and stayed in Fengdan for two years.
Zhisu became the king of election, marched eastward to attack Xiang Yu, and appointed Ao as the governor of Shangdang County.
Chen Xi rebelled, but Ren Ao held on and was granted the title of Marquis of Guang'a, with a settlement of 1,800 households.
After high school, he served as the imperial censor. Removed in three years.
Emperor Xiaowen died in the first year of his reign, and Mi was given the title Yihou.
The Marquis was passed on to his son, and then to his great-grandson Ren Yue. He was removed from the Marquis State because of the crime of being sour and disrespectful in the wine offered at the Taichang Temple.
At the beginning, Ren Ao was dismissed, and Pingyang Marquis Cao Zhuo replaced Ren Ao as the imperial censor.
After the death of Empress Gao, she and her ministers jointly annihilated the Lu family.
Later, he was dismissed from office for violating the law and appointed Huainan Prime Minister Zhang Cang as the imperial censor.
Zhang Cang, Jianghou Zhou Bo and others established Emperor Xiaowen as emperor. Four years later, they replaced Guan Ying as prime minister.
summary: Ren Ao, from Pei, was a jailer who protected Empress Lü from abuse. He followed Gaozu, became censor-in-chief, and was made Marquis of Guang'a. He was later dismissed.
rel_path: 汉书/传/张周赵任申屠传

translation:
After long consideration, it was decided that it was not possible, and there was no living minister who could serve as the prime minister, so he appointed Shentujia, the imperial censor, as the prime minister, and named him Gu'anbao after his original food town.
Shen Tujia is an upright person and does not accept private visits at home.
At that time, Deng Tong, the Taizhong doctor, was favored and received hundreds of millions of rewards.
Emperor Wen often went to Deng Tong's house to drink in his spare time, and he was so favored.
When Shen Tujia entered the dynasty in this temple, Deng usually stayed next to the emperor, showing signs of neglect and disrespect.
After Shen Tujia finished the divination, he immediately said: Your Majesty loves his ministers and makes them rich and noble. As for court etiquette, it must not be lax!
The emperor said: "Don't say anything. I will warn him privately."
After retiring from the court, Shen Tujia sat in the Prime Minister's Mansion and personally wrote a message to summon Deng Tong to come to the manor. If he did not come, Deng Tong would be executed immediately.
Deng Tong was frightened and went to court to tell Zaoshang.
The emperor said: Just go, I will send someone to call you out immediately.
When Deng Tong arrived at the Prime Minister's Mansion, he took off his hat and went barefoot, kowtowed to apologize to Shen Tujia.
Shen Tujia sat calmly as usual, without any courtesy to the guests, and scolded Zhen, saying: "The imperial court is the imperial court of Emperor Gao. It is the greatest disrespect for a minor minister to play in the palace and should be beheaded."
Prime Minister Shi went to execute the beheading!
Deng Tong kowtowed, and blood flowed from his head, but it still didn't stop.
The emperor estimated that the prime minister had already punished Deng Tong, so he sent an envoy to recall Deng Tong with a talisman, thanked the prime minister, and said: "This man is my mocking minister, please let him go."
Deng Tong went to the palace, cried to the emperor, and said: The prime minister almost killed me.
Shen Tujia served as prime minister for five years, Emperor Wen died, and Emperor Jing ascended the throne.
In the second year, Chao Cuo was in office and was highly appreciated by Zaoshang. He proposed to change many laws and regulations, and also proposed punishments to weaken the power of the princes. However, Prime Minister Shen Tujia demoted himself and his words were not accepted. He hated Chao Cuo very much.
During Chao Cuo's tenure, it was inconvenient to enter and exit the east gate, so he opened another gate and entered and exited from the south.
Entering and exiting from the south, pass through the open space outside the inner wall and within the outer wall of Taishanghuang Temple.
Shen Tujia heard that Chao Cuo had passed through the ancestral temple wall and was preparing to petition Chao Cuo to be killed.
A guest told Chao Cuo in advance. Chao Cuo was so frightened that he went to the palace late at night to see the emperor and took the initiative to confess to the emperor.
The next day, when he went to court, Shen Tujia petitioned to kill Chao Cuo, the internal official.
The emperor said: What Chao Cuo opened was not the real temple wall, but the outer wall outside the inner wall, so that the officials could live in it. Besides, I asked him to do it, so Chao Cuo was not guilty.
After retiring from the court, Shen Tujia said to Chang Shi: I regret that I didn't kill him first and report later, but I was betrayed by Chao Cuo.
After returning home, he vomited blood and died.
Mi Hao Jiehou.
summary: Shen Tujia, from Liang, rose from a crossbowman to censor-in-chief and then prime minister. He was upright, refusing private visits. He once ordered the execution of the favored courtier Deng Tong for disrespect, but Emperor Wen intervened. As prime minister, he clashed with Chao Cuo over legal changes. When Chao Cuo opened a gate through a temple wall, Shen Tujia sought his execution but was thwarted. He died of anger after being outmaneuvered. Subsequent prime ministers were competent but unremarkable.
rel_path: 汉书/传/张周赵任申屠传

translation:
Zhang Tang was from Duling.
His father was the magistrate of Chang'an County and was away on business, so Zhang Tang took care of the house as his son.
When his father returned home, he found that the mice had stolen the meat. He lost his temper and whipped Zhang Tang.
Zhang Tang dug a rat hole and found the rat that had stolen the meat and the leftover meat. He stated the crime of the rat, tortured and interrogated it, sent out the interrogation record, and specified the procedure for reporting the verdict after the interrogation.
When his father saw this scene and saw that the diction of his judgment was like a seasoned judge, he was very surprised and asked him to learn prison documents.
After his father's death, Zhang Tang served as a county official in Chang'an.
When Zhou Yanghou Tiansheng was serving as the ninth minister, he was imprisoned in Chang'an Prison. Zhang Tang did his best to help and take care of him.
After Zhou Yanghou was released from prison, he was granted the title of Marquis. He became very friendly with Zhang Tang and introduced Zhang Tang to important people.
Zhang Tang was a subordinate of the internal historian and served as an official of Ning Cheng. Ning Cheng believed that Zhang Tang was extremely talented and recommended him to the Prime Minister's Office. He was transferred to Maolingwei to be in charge of the civil engineering of the mausoleum.
Marquis Wu'an served as prime minister, and Zhang Tang was appointed as an official in the prime minister's palace.
He recommended him to the emperor and served as his censor. When dealing with Queen Chen's witchcraft case, he investigated his accomplices in depth. The emperor believed that he was capable and promoted him to Taizhong doctor.
He and Zhao Yu jointly formulated various laws, focusing on strict binding and strict restraint on serving officials.
Soon, Zhao Yu was promoted to Shaofu, and Zhang Tang was appointed as a court captain. The two became friendly, and Zhang Tang treated Zhao Yu like an elder brother. Zhao Yu was honest and arrogant, while Zhang Tang liked to control others by playing tricks.
At first he became a minor official, speculating for profit, and secretly colluded with the wealthy businessmen Tian Jia and Yu Wengshu in Chang'an.
When he was in the position of Jiuqing, he recruited famous people and officials from all over the country. Although he disagreed with them in his heart, he pretended to respect them.
At this time, the emperor was fond of Confucianism. Zhang Tang decided a major case and wanted to adhere to the ancient principles, so he asked his disciples to study "Shangshu" and "Spring and Autumn" and serve as the history of the imperial court to correct the doubtful aspects of the law.
When submitting difficult cases for adjudication, all aspects of the reasons must be analyzed in advance to the emperor. Whatever the emperor affirms, the case will be accepted as a case decided in accordance with the law and entered into the court's written regulations to promote the sage of the Lord.
If the report work was criticized, Zhang Tang would admit his mistake and apologize. Following the emperor's intention, he would definitely name the capable assistant officials or clerks and say: They originally suggested to me, just as the emperor asked me to do. I was stupid enough not to adopt it.
Therefore his faults are often forgiven.
Sometimes he would submit a memorial to discuss matters. When the emperor approved of the memorial, he would say: I didn't know that such a memorial was written.
He wants to recommend his subordinates, promote someone's strengths or cover up someone's shortcomings.
summary: Zhang Tang, a native of Duling, demonstrated legal acumen early in life when, as a boy, he interrogated a rat for stealing meat, impressing his father, a county magistrate. After his father's death, Zhang Tang served as a county official in Chang'an. He befriended Zhou Yanghou Tiansheng, who later introduced him to influential figures. Recognized for his talent by Ning Cheng, Zhang Tang was recommended to the Prime Minister's Office and later appointed as an official in the prime minister's palace under Marquis Wu'an. He was promoted to censor after investigating Queen Chen's witchcraft case, and later became Taizhong doctor. Alongside Zhao Yu, he formulated strict laws, eventually becoming a court captain. Zhang Tang was known for his cunning, often colluding with wealthy merchants while pretending to respect Confucian scholars to please the emperor. He manipulated legal cases to align with the emperor's wishes, admitting faults to gain forgiveness and promoting subordinates to deflect blame. His private life was serious, and he cared for old friends and poor relatives, earning a good reputation despite his harsh methods.

translation:
If the emperor wants to impose more crimes on a case, he will hand it over to supervisors who enforce the law strictly; if the emperor wants to tolerate a case, he will hand it over to supervisors who enforce the law lightly.
If the person being tried is a powerful person, he will definitely play with the legal provisions and severely punish him; when he encounters a poor person being tried, he often says that even if he is convicted according to the law, the emperor will still make a ruling and review.
So it is often as Zhang Tang said.
Although Zhang Tang was a high official, his private life was very serious. He made friends with guests, entertained and dined, and took better care of his old friends and children who were serving as subordinates, as well as his poor brothers of the same clan. He went to greet Sangong without avoiding the severe cold and heat.
Therefore, although Zhang Tang was profound in his methods but not pure and fair in his heart, he still gained this good reputation.
Most of the harsh and vicious officials who worked for him relied on Confucian scholars.
Prime Minister Gongsun Hong praised him many times.
When investigating the rebellion cases of Huainan King, Hengshan King, and Jiangdu King, they all got to the bottom of it.
The emperor wanted to pardon Yan Zhu and Wu Bei, but Zhang Tang argued: Wu Bei originally planned a rebellion, while Yan Zhu was deeply favored and was a confidant who went in and out of the forbidden gates of the palace, but he had liaisons with the princes. If such people are not killed, similar situations in the future will not be easy to deal with.
So the emperor agreed to their sentence.
He handles cases to attack ministers and thinks it is his own merit. There are many such things.
As a result, Zhang Tang became more favored and trusted, and soon he was promoted to the imperial censor.
At that time, King Hunxie and others surrendered, and the Han Dynasty sent large-scale troops to attack the Xiongnu. Shandong was hit by floods and early disasters. The poor people were displaced and moved, relying on the government to provide food and clothing, and the warehouses were empty.
At this time, Zhang Tang obeyed the emperor's wishes and petitioned to mint silver coins and five-baht copper coins, monopolize the country's salt and ironware, squeeze out wealthy merchants, issue proclamations, eradicate the powerful mergers and acquisitions of large households, and play tricks on the legal provisions to assist the implementation of severe punishments.
Every time Zhang Tang went to court to report on his work, it took so long to talk about the state's financial expenses that the emperor forgot to eat.
The prime minister at the right time is just a vacant position, and all national affairs depend on Zhang Tang.
The common people could not live peacefully, there were riots, the government's undertakings did not gain benefits, and corrupt officials stole and embezzled, so they were punished severely.
Therefore, everyone from the ministers to the common people blamed Zhang Tang.
Zhang Tang fell ill once, and the emperor went to inquire about his illness in person. He was such a noble person.
The Xiongnu came to ask for peace, and the ministers discussed it in front of the emperor. Dr. Dishan said: It is suitable to get married.
The emperor asked him the appropriate reason, and Di Shan said: Weapons are deadly weapons, so don't use them easily and frequently.
Emperor Gao wanted to attack the Xiongnu, but was besieged in Pingcheng, so he finally concluded a peace.
During the period of Emperor Hui and Queen Gao, the country was peaceful and happy. When Emperor Wen wanted to deal with the Xiongnu, the northern border was harassed and the people suffered from war.
During the period of Emperor Jing, seven kingdoms including Wu and Chu rebelled. Emperor Jing went back and forth between the two palaces to discuss the matter and worried about it for several months.
After the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu were crushed, Emperor Jing never talked about war, and the country became rich and fulfilled.
Since your Majesty deployed troops to attack the Xiongnu, the country has become empty, and most of the people on the border are in embarrassment and poverty.
From this point of view, it is better to get married.
The emperor asked Zhang Tang, and Zhang Tang said: This is a stupid Confucian scholar who is ignorant.
Di Shan said: Although I am foolish and loyal, but Zhang Tang, the imperial censor, is deceitful and loyal.
