The princess was the daughter of Emperor Xiaowen and the wife of Prince Zhou Bo Shengzhi, so the jailer taught him to let the princess testify.
At first, Zhou Bo gave all the land he had sealed to Bo Zhao.
When it became urgent to be arrested, Bo Zhao spoke for him in front of Queen Mother Bo, who also believed that there was no treason.
When Emperor Wen went to court, the Queen Mother threw her turban to Emperor Wen and said: Marquis Jiang held the emperor's seal and led troops in the Northern Army. He did not rebel at this time. Now he lives in a small county, but he wants to rebel!
Emperor Wen had read Zhou Bo's judgment and apologized, saying: "The officials are verifying and releasing him."
So he sent an envoy with a talisman to pardon Zhou Bo and restore his title and title.
Zhou Bo was released from prison and said: I once commanded an army of millions, how did I know that the jailer was so noble?
Zhou Bo returned to the feudal state again. Xiaowen died in the eleventh year, and Mi was given the title of Marquis Wu.
His son Shengzhi succeeded to the throne, but his marriage to the princess was unsatisfactory. He was executed for murder and the feudal state was abolished.
A year later, Emperor Wen selected Zhou Bo's son Yafu, the virtuous governor of Hanoi, and made him a marquis.
Yafu was a punctual person in Hanoi, and Xu Fu gave him a face: "You will be a marquis in three years."
After eight years as a marquis, he became a general and prime minister, in charge of the country, and had a noble status, unique among ministers.
Starved to death nine years later.
Yafu smiled and said: My brother has succeeded his father as a marquis. If he dies, his son will inherit. How can I talk about becoming a marquis?
But if you are as noble as Xu Negiyan said, how can you say that you will starve to death?
Point it out to me.
Xu Negiyan pointed to his mouth and said: "The vertical lines at the entrance are the lines of starvation."
Three years later, his elder brother Jianghou Sheng was found guilty. Emperor Wen selected the virtuous among Zhou Bo's sons. They all recommended Yafu and made him Tiaohou.
Six years after Emperor Wen's reign, the Xiongnu invaded the border in large numbers.
He appointed Zongzheng and Liu Li as the generals and garrisoned at Ba Shang, Zhu Zihou Xu Li as the generals and garrisoned at Jimen, and appointed Hanoi Shou Yafu as the generals and garrisoned at Xiliu to guard against the barbarians.
summary: Zhou Bo became Right Chancellor but feared his power and resigned. Later accused of rebellion, he was imprisoned and bribed a jailer for advice. He was released after his wife, the emperor's daughter, testified for him. He remarked on the harshness of jailers. His son Zhou Yafu succeeded him.

translation:
The emperor personally expressed his condolences to the army. He went to Bashang and the Thorny Gate Army and drove straight in. The following officials rode in and out to greet them.
Then we went to the Binaliu Army. The officers and soldiers in the army were wearing armor, sharpening their swords, drawing their bows and crossbows, and drawing the strings fully. The emperor's pioneers arrived, but they could not get in.
The pioneer said: The emperor is coming!
The captain of the military gate said: The army obeys the general's orders but not the emperor's edicts.
After a while, the emperor arrived, but he couldn't get in.
So the emperor sent an envoy to take the talisman and tell the general: "I want to comfort the army."
Yafu sent word to open the camp gate.
The gatekeeper of the camp asked for the cavalry and said: "The general has stipulated that horses are not allowed to gallop in the army."
So the emperor fastened his horse's reins and walked slowly.
When he arrived at the middle camp, he bowed to the general and his husband and said: "Men in armor do not kneel down to worship. Please allow me to show you military salutes."
The emperor was moved by this, looked solemn, and supported Che Shi. Send someone to announce: The emperor respectfully expresses his condolences to the general.
Leave after the ceremony.
After leaving the camp gate, the ministers were all frightened.
Emperor Wen said: Ah, this is the real general!
Previously, Bashang and Thorny Gate were like child's play, and the general would definitely be attacked and captured.
As for Yafu, can he invade?
Praise him for a long time. More than a month later, all three armies withdrew.
He appointed Yafu as lieutenant.
Before Emperor Wen died, he warned the prince: If there is an emergency, Zhou Yafu can really be appointed to lead the army.
Emperor Wen died, and Yafu became a chariot and cavalry general.
In the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, Wu Chu rebelled.
As a lieutenant, Yafu performed the duties of a Taiwei and went east to attack Wu Chu.
So he asked the emperor: "The Chu soldiers are strong and agile, and it is difficult to compete with them."
I hope that by abandoning Liang to it and cutting off their food routes, they can conquer it.
The emperor agreed.
Yafu set out and arrived at Bashang. Chang She stopped Yafu and said, "General, go eastward to destroy Wu and Chu. If you win, the ancestral temple will be stable. If you fail, the world will be in danger. Can you adopt my opinion?"
Yafu got out of the car and asked him after saluting.
Zhao She said: The King of Wu has always been rich and has long recruited scholars who are willing to die for service. Now that he knows that the general is going, he will definitely set up an ambush at a narrow and dangerous place, and the secret of war is important. Why doesn't the general go to the right from now on, pass through Lantian, leave Wuguan, and arrive at Luoyang, which is only a day or two away. He can directly enter the weapons warehouse and beat the war drums.
When the princes heard this, they thought the general had fallen from the sky.
The Taiwei acted according to his plan.
When they arrived in Luoyang, they sent a small official to search Sanxingjian, and sure enough they found Wu's ambush.
So he asked Zhao She to be the guard.
After Yafu arrived, he gathered his troops in Rongyang.
summary: Zhou Yafu, known for his strict military discipline, refused to let Emperor Wen enter his camp without proper protocol, earning the emperor's praise as a "true general." During the Rebellion of the Seven States, he advised letting Liang bear the enemy's attack while cutting off their supply routes. He ignored the emperor's order to save Liang, focusing on his strategy, which ultimately defeated Wu and Chu.

translation:
Wu Zheng attacked Liang, and Liang was in danger and asked for help.
Yafu led his troops to the northeast toward Changyi and built a stronghold to defend it.
The king of Liang sent an envoy to request Yafu, but Yafu considered the situation and refused to go.
King Liang wrote to Emperor Jing and Emperor Jing issued an edict asking him to save Liang.
Yafu disobeyed Shao's order and defended the camp without sending troops. He sent light cavalry, Gong Gaohou and others to cut off the Wu Chu army's rear food route.
Wu Chu's soldiers were short of food and hungry, and wanted to retreat. They challenged him many times but refused to go out.
At night, there was a commotion in the army, internal attacks and commotion, and they arrived at the tent.
Yafu lay still and couldn't get up.
After a while, it settled down again.
Wu Jun rushed to the southeast corner of the camp, while Yafu Rang guarded the northwest corner.
Soon the enemy's elite troops rushed to the northwest and could not attack.
Wu Chu's army was short of food, so they withdrew their troops. Yafu sent out elite troops to pursue and defeated Wu Wangbi.
Wu Wangbi abandoned his army and fled with thousands of warriors to protect himself in Dantu in the south of the Yangtze River.
Taking advantage of the victory, the Han soldiers finally captured them all, surrendered all counties, and offered a reward of thousands of gold to the King of Wu.
More than a month later, the Yue people chopped off King Wu's head to report.
After a total of three months of attack and defense, Wu Chu was pacified. Then the generals believed that the Taiwei's plan was correct.
From then on, there was a conflict between King Xiao of Liang and Yafu.
After returning, he appointed Taiwei officers.
Five years later, he was promoted to prime minister, and Emperor Jing valued him very much.
The emperor abolished Prince Li. Yafu argued resolutely but failed.
The emperor therefore distanced himself from him.
And every time Liang Xiaowang went to court, he often talked to the Queen Mother about Yafu's shortcomings.
Empress Dowager Dou said: The empress's brother Wang Xin can be made a marquis.
The emperor reproached him and said: In the past, Nanpi and Zhangwu, the first emperors, did not ennoble themselves as marquises, but when their ministers came to the throne, they would do so. Wang Xin could not do so.
Empress Dowager Dou said: In life, everyone acts according to the current situation.
When Dou Changjun was still alive, he could not be granted the title of marquis in the end. After his death, his son Peng Zu was granted the title of marquis.
I regret it very much.
The emperor quickly makes Wang Xin a marquis!
The emperor said: Please allow me to discuss this with the prime minister.
Yafu said: Emperor Gao stipulated that it was not that the Liu family could not be granted the title of king, nor that the Liu family could not be granted the title of marquis without merit.
If he did not abide by the regulations, everyone in the world attacked him. Now, although Wang Xin is the elder brother of the queen, he has no merit and is granted a title, which is against the regulations.
The emperor remained silent and stopped the matter.
Later, King Xu Lu of the Xiongnu and five others surrendered to the Han Dynasty. The emperor wanted to make him a marquis to encourage his descendants.
summary: As prime minister, Yafu opposed enfeoffing the queen's brother and Xiongnu defectors, arguing it violated Emperor Gao's rules. The emperor overruled him. Later, Yafu's son bought imperial burial items, and Yafu was accused of rebellion. He starved himself in prison, fulfilling a prophecy that he would die of hunger.

translation:
Zhang Qian was from Hanzhong. During the Jianyuan period, he was appointed as Lang Guan.
People who surrendered to the Xiongnu at that time said that the Xiongnu defeated the Yuezhi King and used the Yuezhi King's head as a drinking vessel. The Yuezhi fled and resented the Huns because they had no one to fight with them.
The Han Dynasty was planning to engage in a war to eliminate the Xiongnu. When they heard this, they wanted to send people as envoys to the Yuezhi. However, the Xiongnu Kingdom was the only way to go, so they recruited people who could go as envoys.
Zhang Qian was recruited as an envoy to Yuezhi as a Langguan. He left Longxi with Gan Fu, Tangyi's servant.
Passing by the Huns, he was intercepted by the Huns and sent to the Shanyu in a conveyor.
Shanyu said: The Yueshi are to the north of me. How can the Han Dynasty people send envoys there?
If I want to send someone as an envoy to South Vietnam, will the Han Dynasty let our people pass by?
Zhang Qian was detained for more than ten years. He married him and gave birth to a son. However, Zhang Qian still insisted on the Han Dynasty and still maintained his status as an envoy.
Because he lived in the western part of the Huns, Zhang Qian took the opportunity to lead his subordinates to flee towards the Yueshi. After running west for dozens of days, we arrived in Dawan.
Dawan heard that the Han Dynasty was rich in wealth and wanted to have contacts with the Han Dynasty but could not find the opportunity. He was very happy to see Zhang Qian and asked him where he was going.
Zhang Qian said: We were sent as an envoy to the Yuezhi on behalf of the Han Dynasty, but the Huns blocked the road and refused to allow passage. Now we are fleeing to your country. I hope that the king can send someone to lead the way and send us there. If we can reach the Yuezhi, after we return to the Han Dynasty, the property that the Han Dynasty will give to the king will be indescribable.
Dawan thought it was okay, so he sent them there and sent translators and guides for them.
They were sent to Kangju, who sent them to Dayuezhi in a conveyor.
At this time, the original King of Dayuezhi had been killed by the Xiongnu, and his wife was made king.
Da Yuezhi had made Daxia surrender and ruled over it.
The land there was fertile, the produce was abundant, there was no intrusion, and they felt relaxed and happy. They considered themselves far away from the Han Dynasty and did not want to get close to the Han Dynasty. They had no intention of revenge against the Huns. From Yuezhi to Daxia, Zhang Qian never received a clear statement from the Yuezhi King.
After staying for more than a year, I had to return. Along the Nanshan Mountains, I wanted to return to the Han Dynasty from the place where the Qiang people lived, but I was intercepted by the Xiongnu again.
After being detained for more than a year, it happened that the Chanyu died and the Xiongnu country was in chaos. Zhang Qian fled back to the Han Dynasty with his Hun wife and Tangyi Ganfu.
The imperial court granted him the official position of Taizhong Taifu, and Tangyi Ganfu also became the envoy.
Zhang Qian is strong and perseverant, magnanimous and sincere in his treatment of others. He is liked by ethnic minorities.
Tangyi's father was a Huns who was good at archery. When he was extremely poor, he shot animals for food.
At the beginning, there were more than a hundred people when Zhang Qian traveled. After thirteen years, only he and Tang Yi's father came back.
summary: Zhang Qian, a native of Hanzhong, was appointed as Lang Guan during the Jianyuan period. Hearing from surrendered Xiongnu that the Yuezhi had been defeated by the Xiongnu and sought allies for revenge, the Han Dynasty, planning to attack the Xiongnu, recruited envoys to the Yuezhi. Zhang Qian was recruited and departed with Gan Fu, a servant from Tangyi. Captured by the Xiongnu, he was detained for over ten years, married, and had a son, but he retained his Han envoy status. Escaping westward, he reached Dawan, which aided him due to interest in Han wealth. He was sent via Kangju to Dayuezhi, but the Yuezhi, now settled in fertile Daxia, had no desire for revenge. After over a year without a clear response, Zhang Qian returned but was recaptured by the Xiongnu. He escaped after a year during Xiongnu turmoil, returning to Han with his wife and Gan Fu. He was appointed Taizhong Taifu.

translation:
Zhang Qian had personally visited places such as Dayuan, Dayuezhi, Daxia, Kangju and other countries. He heard that there were five or six big countries next to these countries. He told Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty one by one about the topography and products of these countries. The contents mentioned are all contained in "The Biography of the Western Regions".
Zhang Qian said: When I was in Daxia, I saw bamboo sticks from Qiong and fine cloth produced in Shu County. I asked them where they got them. The people of Daxia said: Our merchants bought them from the country of Shendu.
Shendu Country is located in the southeast of Daxia, about thousands of miles away.
The custom of Nahuo is to live a settled life, which is the same as that of Daxia, but the terrain is low-lying, humid, and the climate is hot.
People there rode elephants to fight, and the country was bordered by floods. According to my guess, Daxia was about 12,000 miles away from the Han Dynasty and to the southwest of the Han Dynasty.
Now Shendu is thousands of miles southeast of Daxia, and there are products from Shu County. It seems that Shendu is not far from Shu.
It is very dangerous for the envoy to Daxia to pass through the Qiang area. The Qiang people hate the Han Dynasty. If you go a little north, you will be captured by the Huns. If you go from Shu County, it will be a convenient road and there will be no intrusion.
Emperor Mowu heard that Dayuan, Daxia, Parthia and other countries were big countries with many strange products and lived a settled life, which was the same as the customs of the Han Dynasty. However, the military strength is very weak and they value the property of the Han Dynasty. To the north are the Dayuezhi, Kangju and other countries, which have strong military strength. They can be lured to come to see the Emperor of Han by giving them property and benefits.
If we can really do this and use moral power to make them join the Han Dynasty, then the Han Dynasty can expand its territory by more than 10,000 miles. People from some ethnic groups who come to the court will have to go through multiple translations to understand the language. Some ethnic minorities with strange customs will also come to join the Han Dynasty. The prestige and virtue of the Han Dynasty will spread all over the world.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was very happy and thought Zhang Qian's words made sense.
So he ordered envoys to be sent to explore the road through Shu County and Jianwei County, and they set off in four groups at the same time. Starting from Ranchi all the way, starting from Jedudu all the way, starting from Yiheqiong all the way, and starting from Fen all the way, each has a distance of one or two thousand miles.
However, the northern passage was blocked by the clans and Jeduyi, and the southern passage was blocked by Ling and Kunming.
Kunming and other ethnic minorities have no rulers and are good at plundering and stealing. Every time they killed passing Han envoys and took away their property, this road finally failed to open.
However, I heard that about a thousand miles west of Kunming, there is Chengxiang Kingdom, named Dianyue. Some businessmen from Shu County who privately trade goods have been there. So the Han Dynasty began to communicate with the Dian Kingdom in search of the road to Daxia.
At first, the Han Dynasty wanted to communicate with the southwestern barbarians, but stopped this work because it was too expensive.
When Zhang Qian said that it was possible to reach Daxia via the Southwest Yi, the Han Dynasty began to open up the route to the Southwest Yi.
Zhang Qian followed the general Wei Qing to attack the Huns as a captain. Because he knew where the water and grass were distributed, the army could not lack supplies, so he made Zhang Qian the Marquis of Bowang.
summary: Zhang Qian, known for his perseverance and sincerity, visited Dawan, Dayuezhi, Daxia, and Kangju. He reported to Emperor Wu that Daxia had Shu products, suggesting Shendu was near Shu. He proposed a route via Shu to Daxia, avoiding dangerous Qiang and Xiongnu territories. Emperor Wu, intrigued by the wealth of western states, sent envoys to explore Shu routes, but they were blocked by local tribes. Zhang Qian later joined General Wei Qing against the Xiongnu, becoming Marquis of Bowang. After a failed campaign with Li Guang, he was reduced to commoner status. Following Han victories over the Xiongnu, Zhang Qian advised allying with Wusun to weaken the Xiongnu and recruit western states. Emperor Wu agreed, sending Zhang Qian with gifts to Wusun. Though Wusun did not commit, Zhang Qian sent deputies to other states. Wusun later sent envoys to Han, and Zhang Qian died over a year after returning.

translation:
In the first year of Taichu, Guangli was appointed as the general of the Second Division. He led six thousand cavalry from the vassal state and tens of thousands of young men with bad conduct from the county. He used these troops to attack Dawan. He expected to capture good horses from the city of the Second Division, so he was called "General of the Second Division".
Wang Hui, the former Haohou, led the army and served as a guide.
The troops of the General of the Second Division had already encountered Yanyan to the west. The small countries along the route were in panic and tightly defended their castles. They did not supply the Han army with food and could not be defeated.
Those who can be captured will have food to eat, and those who cannot be captured will have to leave in a few days.
By the time they reached Yucheng, there were only a few thousand soldiers left, and they were all hungry and tired.
They attacked Yucheng City and were defeated, with many casualties.
The general of the Second Division discussed with his left and right: We can't capture it until Yucheng, let alone the capital of King Dawan?
Just retreat with the troops.
It took two years of traveling back and forth. When we returned to Dunhuang, only one-tenth of the soldiers were left.
He sent an envoy to write a memorial to the emperor saying: The journey is long and there is a shortage of food. The soldiers were not afraid of war, but of starvation.
With few troops, Wan cannot be captured.
I hope to withdraw the troops temporarily and send more troops before going back.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty heard what had been reported, he became furious and sent envoys to guard Yumen Pass, saying that if any soldier dared to enter the pass, he would be killed immediately!
General Li Guangli of the Second Division was afraid and stayed in Dunhuang.
In the summer of that year, the Han Dynasty fought against the Xiongnu, and the soldiers of the Hou Po Nu were killed by more than 20,000 people. After discussion, senior officials of the Han Dynasty hoped to call back the troops that attacked Dawan and focus on dealing with the Xiongnu.
However, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty believed that since he had sent troops to attack Dayuan, if a small country like Dayuan could not defeat it, countries like Daxia would gradually look down on the Han Dynasty, and the good horses from Dayuan would be stopped from coming to the Han Dynasty. Countries such as Wusun and Luntai would also make it difficult for the Han Dynasty's envoys, and they would laugh at foreign countries.
So Deng Guang and others were punished for discussing that the attack on Dawan was particularly inappropriate.
The prisoner soldiers were pardoned, and the young men with bad conduct and the cavalry on the border were sent to the army. After more than a year, 60,000 troops were sent from Dunhuang, not counting those who personally brought food and followed the troops to fight.
This team contains 100,000 cattle, 30,000 horses, and tens of thousands of donkeys and camels.
They brought plenty of food and were well equipped with weapons, bows and arrows. The whole country was in turmoil, and supplies were supplied one after another for the expedition to Dawan. A total of more than fifty officers of the army went out for the expedition.
There were no wells in the capital of Dawan, so water had to be brought in from outside the city. So the Mo army sent water control craftsmen to divert the water from the city to prevent it from flowing under the city. Instead, they diverted the water into holes and attacked the city with water.
summary: After Zhang Qian's missions, Han envoys frequently traveled to the Western Regions, often exaggerating to gain favor. Emperor Wu, seeking Dawan horses, sent Li Guangli as General of Ershi to attack Dawan. The first campaign failed due to food shortages, and Li Guangli was ordered to halt at Dunhuang. Despite opposition, Emperor Wu launched a massive second campaign with 60,000 troops, 100,000 cattle, and 30,000 horses. After a 40-day siege, Dawan nobles killed their king and offered horses, ending the war. Li Guangli was made Marquis of Haixi. The campaigns opened routes to the Western Regions, with Han establishing Jiuquan County and building fortresses. Envoys continued, but conflicts arose with small states like Loulan and Gushi, leading to Han military actions. The Han Dynasty's influence expanded, though some states remained distant. The text concludes with a note on the reliability of ancient texts regarding the Yellow River's source.

translation:
At the beginning of the rise of the Han Dynasty, the bad governance of the Qin Dynasty was reversed, so that the people could recuperate and live, everything was simplified, and prohibitions and laws were greatly relaxed. The prime ministers Xiao He and Cao Shen became models for the world with their generous and quiet style of work. The people therefore compiled a "painting and a song" to praise them.
Emperor Hui ruled without doing anything, Empress Lu lived in seclusion in the palace, but the world was peaceful, the people concentrated on agricultural production, and there was a scene of plenty of food and clothing.
During the reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing, customs changed again.
At that time, officials who were able to obey the law and obey the law, such as Wu Gong, the governor of Henan County, and Weng Weng, the governor of Shu County, were strict with themselves, set examples for others, acted honestly and justly, and could make the people obey and accept the influence without using coercion.
During the reign of Emperor Wu, he resisted the barbarians from all directions externally and revised laws and regulations internally. As a result, the people were exhausted and internal strife and external troubles could not be prevented.
At that time, there were very few people who were famous for their education and governance. Only Dong Zhongshu, the Prime Minister of Jiangdu, Gongsun Hong and Ni Kuan, the internal historian, whose political performances are worthy of a book.
The three of them were all Confucian scholars, who were both proficient in the way of life and writing. They used Confucian thinking and methods to help themselves handle government affairs, and the emperor valued them very much.
Dong Zhongshu resigned from office many times due to illness, while Gongsun Hong and Ni Kuan fulfilled their duties as officials.
Emperor Zhao ascended the throne at a young age, and Huo Guang took charge of government affairs on his behalf. At this time, after years of war, domestic consumption was very high. Huo Guang followed this and abide by his duties without changing his previous practices.
In the Shiyuan and Yuanfeng years, the Xiongnu surrendered, and the people's lives gradually became richer, so they began to recommend talents, care about the people's sufferings, abolished the wine tax, and discussed the benefits of salt and iron.
When Emperor Xuan arrived, because he was an emperor who came from a humble background and started his family in an alley, he was well aware of the people's joys and sorrows.
After Huo Guang's death, he began to personally handle various court affairs and worked hard to govern. He went to court every five days to listen to government affairs and reported to the court in order from the prime minister to the other officials.
When officials such as governors, governors, and princes are conferred, they must be interviewed in person to understand their thoughts, and then their actions are examined to compare with their words. If the names are inconsistent with reality, the root cause must be found.
Emperor Xuan once said: The reason why the people can rest assured in agricultural production and eliminate the bad mood of worry and resentment is because the politics are peaceful and the law can uphold justice.
The only people who jointly guarantee this with me are those good county guards. He believes that county guards are the basis for managing officials and the people. Frequent changes will cause local unrest. When the people know that the selection of the prefect is very stable and cannot be deceived, they will obey his teachings.
summary: During the early Han Dynasty, the harsh policies of the Qin Dynasty were reversed, allowing the people to recover and live simply, with relaxed laws. Prime Ministers Xiao He and Cao Cao set an example with their generous and quiet governance, earning praise from the people. Emperor Hui ruled without intervention, and Empress Lu remained secluded, yet the realm was peaceful, with abundant food and clothing. Under Emperors Wen and Jing, customs improved, and officials like Wu Gong and Weng Weng governed with integrity, inspiring obedience without force. Emperor Wu's reign saw external conflicts and internal legal reforms, exhausting the people and causing unrest. Few officials were noted for good governance, except Confucian scholars Dong Zhongshu, Gongsun Hong, and Ni Kuan, who used Confucian principles in administration and were valued by the emperor. Emperor Zhao ascended young, with Huo Guang as regent, who maintained stability after years of war. During the Shiyuan and Yuanfeng years, the Xiongnu surrendered, and the people grew prosperous, leading to talent recommendations, care for the people, and discussions on salt and iron taxes. Emperor Xuan, who rose from humble beginnings, understood the people's hardships. After Huo Guang's death, he personally managed court affairs, holding court every five days and interviewing officials to ensure their actions matched their words. He believed that stable county governors were key to peace, rewarding effective ones with promotions and titles. This led to a flourishing of virtuous officials, known as the ZTE era. Some, like Zhao Guanghan and Han Yanshou, were diligent but faced punishment, while others like Wang Cheng and Huang Ba were honored in life and remembered after death.

translation:
Therefore, if the county governor is effective in governance, he will always issue letters to encourage him personally, increase his salary and give him a large sum of money, or confer a title to a marquis in Guannei. When the official position is vacant, he will be appointed in turn by those who have been commended.
For this reason, Xunliang officials emerged in endlessly in the Han Dynasty, which is known as the ZTE.
People such as Zhao Guanghan, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Yan Yannian, and Zhang Chang were all competent and conscientious in their duties, but they were punished and some even committed capital crimes.
Wang Cheng, Huang Ba, Zhu Yi, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Zhao Xinchen and others were prosperous when they were in office, but missed by the people after they left office. They were given honorary titles during their lifetimes, and were worshiped and remembered after their deaths. This kind of style may be the style of gentlemen who are benevolent and courteous.
Wen Weng was from Shu County, Lujiang County.
When he was young, he loved learning and was proficient in "Spring and Autumn". He was promoted to the imperial court as a county official.
In the last years of Emperor Jing's reign, Weng Weng served as the prefect of Shu County. He was tolerant and caring for the people, and liked to use political enlightenment to influence and govern the people of Shu County.
He saw that Shu County was located in a remote and remote border area and was affected by the backward customs of ethnic minorities, so he wanted to educate and inspire it in many aspects to make progress. So he selected more than ten people from the county officials who were enlightened, wise and talented, such as Uncle Zhang, to personally instruct and encourage them. , and sent them to the capital Chang'an, either to study Confucian classics with the doctors, or to learn laws and regulations from the officials; to reduce the expenses of the county and magistrates, buy the precious specialties of Shu, golden knives and cloth, and let the officials in charge of accounting books bring them with them when they report the situation to Beijing, and give them to the doctors.
A few years later, when the students who had been sent out to study returned to school, Wen Weng appointed them to high-level positions in the county, and successively recommended them to the court through inspections and other channels, and some of them became county governors or governors.
In addition, Wen Weng also established a school in Chengdu City, recruiting young children from counties outside Chengdu as students, exempting them from paying more taxes and corvee, and those with good academic performance supplemented the county officials, while those with poor academic performance served as filial piety, Litian and other township officials.
They often select young students from schools and let them help handle government affairs in the county government's side houses.
Whenever he went out to patrol various counties, Wen Weng always asked many students who were well versed in scriptures and of good conduct to go around with him to preach enlightenment policies and go in and out of county offices.
When the county officials and people saw this situation, they were very envious. Within a few years, everyone was vying to become a student in the school, so that wealthy families paid for the education.
From then on, enlightenment prevailed and the atmosphere in Shu County changed greatly. The number of people from Shu County studying in the capital is comparable to that of Qi, Lu and other places.
When Emperor Wu arrived, he ordered counties and counties to set up schools and relevant management officials. This was started by Wen Weng.
After Wen Wengshou returned to Shu County, the local officials and people built an ancestral hall for him, and offered sacrifices continuously during every year and festival.
To this day, the people in the Bashu region like elegance and are influenced by Wen Weng's teachings.
summary: Wen Weng, a native of Shu County, was known for his love of learning and governance. As prefect of Shu, he selected talented officials to study in Chang'an, reducing expenses and providing gifts to scholars. He established schools in Chengdu, exempting students from taxes and appointing them to official positions. His efforts transformed Shu's culture, making it comparable to Qi and Lu. Emperor Wu later ordered all counties to establish schools, following Wen Weng's example. After his death, the people built a temple for him, and his influence persists in the Bashu region.

translation:
Wang Cheng, I don’t know which county he is from.
He once served as the minister of mice and was very prestigious in governing the place.
Emperor Xuan was the first to praise him. The Book of Shao issued in the third year of Dijie said: If you don't reward those who have merit and punish those who are guilty, then even the names of Yao and Shun of Tang Dynasty will not be able to educate the world.
Now the Prime Minister Wang Cheng has never slackened his efforts to encourage the people, and has attracted more than 80,000 refugees. He has made special achievements in governing the place.
Wang Cheng was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and a salary of two thousand stones.
But before the time of requisition, Wang Cheng fell ill and died.
Later, he asked the prime ministers and censors to inquire about the gains and losses of the county's chief accountants, prefects, and government officials. Some reported that the former prime minister Wang Cheng had made false reports and exaggerated his own achievements in order to defraud prominent officials. As a result, mediocre officials later also used all means to pursue false fame.
Huang Ba, courtesy name Cigong, was a native of Yangxia County, Huaiyang County. His family was a wealthy gentry and moved to Yunling.
Huang Ba studied laws and regulations when he was young and liked to be an official. In the last years of Emperor Wu, he donated money as an imperial edict and was rewarded with an official position.
Later, he donated grain to Shenli County to supplement Zuo Feng Yi's official salary of 200 shi.
Because Huang Ba donated money to serve as an official, Zuo Fengyi despised him and refused to give him a high position, making him responsible for the county's money and grain access.
Huang Ba did not deceive in accounting, and after his integrity was found out, he was promoted to the chief of Hedong County, and later he was promoted to the prefect of Henan County because of his integrity.
Huang Ba is good at observation, quick thinking, and familiar with legal provisions. He is gentle and modest in dealing with others, considerate of his family, and good at uniting everyone.
When he was the prefect, he acted in accordance with the law and complied with the people's hearts. The prefect trusted him very much, and the people also respected and loved him.
Since the last years of Emperor Wu, the use of laws has become more stringent.
Emperor Zhao was still very young when he came to the throne, and the general Huo Guang assisted in the administration. Ministers fought for power and profit. Shangguan Jie and others also conspired with King Yan to cause rebellion. Huo Guang killed them. Therefore, he still abided by the laws of Emperor Wu's era and used severe punishments to restrain the ministers and people. As a result, some vulgar officials used harsh criminal laws to do their best. Huang Ba was the only one known for his tolerance and gentleness.
When Emperor Huixuan came to the throne, he was well aware that the people suffered from the harsh punishments imposed by officials when he was among the people. He also heard that Huang Ba upheld the law fairly, so he summoned Huang Ba to be the court official. Huang Ba adjudicated difficult cases several times, and the court unanimously believed that the verdict was fair.
So he temporarily served as Prime Minister Chang Shi. In a high-level meeting of ministers, Huang Ba failed to report the disrespectful words and deeds of Xia Housheng, the young minister of Changxin Palace, who criticized the emperor's edict without reporting it. Huang Ba and Xia Housheng were handed over to the Tingwei for trial. As a result, they were sentenced to death and imprisoned.
As a result, Huang Ba studied "Shang Shu" with Xia Housheng in prison. He was not released from prison until the third year after two winters. His detailed deeds can be found in "The Biography of Xiahou Sheng".
After Xia Housheng was released from prison, he became an admonishing doctor again, and asked Zuo Fengyi and Song Wei to recommend Huang Ba as a virtuous man.
Xia Housheng personally recommended Huang Ba to the emperor, and the emperor promoted Huang Ba to be the governor of Yangzhou.
Three years later, Emperor Xuan issued an edict saying: Order the censor: Huang Ba, who served as the governor of Yangzhou as a virtuous Gaodi, was appointed as the prefect of Yingchuan County. His salary was two thousand dan per month. When he took office, he was given a high cover for the car, which was allowed to be one foot high. His subordinates drove the car and the chief registrar. A mud-blocking red curtain could be hung in front of the car to show benevolence.
At that time, the emperor was concentrating on governing the world and issued Shao letters to the people many times, but some officials did not let the people know.
However, the prefect Huang Ba specially selected outstanding subordinate officials and assigned them to various places to issue the Emperor's Shao Order so that the people could know the Emperor's will. He also asked the Youting township officials to raise chickens and pigs to support the widowed and poor people.
summary: Wang Cheng, whose origins are unknown, served as a minister and attracted over 80,000 refugees, earning Emperor Xuan's praise and a marquis title. However, after his death, it was reported that he had exaggerated his achievements, leading to a trend of false fame among officials. Huang Ba, from Yangxia County, studied law and became an official through donations. He was known for his integrity, gentle demeanor, and ability to unite people. As prefect of Yingchuan, he implemented policies to support the poor, promote agriculture, and reduce crime. His governance was so effective that the county's household registration increased, and he was praised by Emperor Xuan. However, as prime minister, his performance declined, and he was criticized for overstepping his duties. Despite this, he is remembered as one of the best local officials in Han history. He died in office, and his descendants continued to serve as officials until Wang Mang's era.

translation:
Zhu Yi was a minister, but his family was very frugal. He shared his salary and rewards with his elders in his hometown, but he had no extra money.
Zhu Yi passed away in the first year of Shenjue.
The emperor took pity on him, so he went down to Shao and praised him, saying: "The great minister, Zhu Yi, is honest, honest and public-minded. He does not make casual friends or accept bribes. He can be called an upright gentleman." I feel very sorry for this misfortune.
One hundred catties of gold were specially given to the son of Zhu Yi for the purpose of offering sacrifices.
When Zhu Yi was critically ill, he told his son: I was originally a minor official in Tongxiang. The local people loved me and I will be buried in Tongxiang after my death.
The descendants of future generations will not be as good as the fathers and fellows of Tongxiang in offering sacrifices to me.
After his death, his son buried him outside the west city of Tongxiang. As expected, the people built a tomb and an ancestral hall for Zhu Yi and offered sacrifices on time every year, which has never stopped to this day.
Gong Sui, whose courtesy name was Shaoqing, was a native of Pingyang County in the south of Shanyang County.
Because he was proficient in Confucian classics, he went to work as an official and became a doctor in Changyi. He served Liu He, the king of Changyi.
Liu He's behavior was very unruly, while Gong Sui was loyal, strong and decisive. He was never ambiguous on important matters. He gave outspoken advice to the king internally, and supervised the Taifu and the Prime Minister externally. He always cited scriptures and stated the good and bad fortunes and gains and losses until he shed tears. He was extremely loyal.
He never flattered, and often pointed out Liu He's faults to his face, which made him unable to listen. He covered his ears and stood up and walked away, saying: "Mr. Zhongling is really embarrassing."
Liu He and all the ministers in the country did not respect him.
Liu He used to eat, drink and have fun with his servants and caterers, and gave them endless rewards. Gong Sui went to the palace to admonish him. He knelt down and burst into tears, crying softly. The people who were waiting around Liu He were moved to tears. Liu He asked: Why is Lang Zhongling crying?
Gong Sui replied: I am sad that the country is in danger!
I hope you can spare some free time and let me finish my ignorant opinion.
Liu He told the people around him to stay away, and Gong Sui asked: "Does the king know that the King of Jiaoxi did not do good things and perished?" Liu He said: I don’t know.
Gong Sui then said: I heard that the king of Jiaoxi had a courtier named Hou De who was good at flattery. The king of Jiaoxi obviously did the same as Xia Jie and Shang Zhou, but Hou De said that he was the same as Yao and Shun.
The King of Jiaoxi liked his flattery, often lived with him, and listened to his evil words, which led to his death and the country's destruction.
Now that the king is close to those villains, he will gradually become infected with their bad habits. This is a matter related to the survival of the country, so you must be cautious!
Please allow me to select some people who are proficient in Confucianism and of high moral character in Lang Palace to live with the king. We will read "Poems" and "Books" together when we sit down, and practice etiquette together immediately. This may be of some help to the king.
Liu He agreed to this suggestion.
So Gong Sui selected Zhang An and ten other people to serve him.
However, within a few days, Liu He drove them all away.
After a long time, strange phenomena occurred many times in the palace. Liu He asked Gong Sui why. Gong Sui believed that a big misfortune would happen, which was a sign that the palace would be empty. This matter is described in the "Biography of the King of Changyi".
It happened that Emperor Zhao died without a son. Liu He, king of Changyi, succeeded to the throne, and all his officials were recruited to Beijing.
Xiangguo Anle was transferred to Changle Palace Guard. Gong Sui went to see him and told him with tears: Since the king became emperor, he has become more and more proud and complacent every day. He no longer listens to the advice of others. Now he is still in mourning and observes filial piety. He drinks and hases with his relatives and officials every day. When he is not fighting tigers and leopards, he or she gathers in leather carts with nine streamers on them. They run around everywhere. What they do is contrary to the right path.
summary: Zhu Yi, from Shu County, was known for his honesty and fairness as a minor official. He rose to become a minister of agriculture, living frugally and sharing his salary with his hometown elders. He died in 61 BC, and Emperor Xuan praised his integrity, granting gold for sacrifices. He was buried in Tongxiang, where the people built a temple for him.

translation:
Gong Sui then opened a warehouse to provide relief to the poor, and selected honest officials to appease the people and allow them to live in peace and prosperity.
Gong Sui saw that the local customs in Bohai were extravagant, favored industry and commerce, and despised farming, so he personally took the lead in practicing frugality and persuaded the people to farm and grow mulberry trees. He asked everyone to plant an elm tree, a hundred scallions, fifty green onions, and a row of leeks. Each family raised two sows and five leeks.
If you find any of the people carrying swords or swords, ask them to sell their swords to buy oxen and sell their knives to buy calves, saying: "Why do you wear oxen and calves on your body?"
In spring and summer, people were urged to farm in the fields, and in autumn and winter, they were urged to harvest. They also asked every household to store more fruits, water chestnuts, gorgon seeds and the like.
Thanks to Gong Sui's inspection and encouragement, the county had savings, the officials and the people were prosperous, and there were no more lawsuits.
A few years later, Emperor Xuan sent an envoy to recall Gong Sui and discuss Cao Wangsheng's request to go with him.
Gong Cao thought that Wang Sheng had always been addicted to drinking and had no control over it, so it was inappropriate for him to follow him.
But Gong Sui couldn't bear to refuse, so he asked him to follow him to Beijing.
When Wang Sheng arrived in the capital, he just drank every day and never visited Gong Sui.
One day, Gong Sui was summoned to the palace. Wang Sheng was drunk. He followed him and shouted loudly: "Ming Mansion will stop for a moment. I have a few words to say to you."
Gong Sui turned around and asked him what he was shouting for. He said: If the emperor asks you how you manage the Bohai Sea, you must not say anything more. You should only answer: It all depends on the power of the Holy Spirit. It is not that I have any ability! , Gong Sui accepted his opinion.
Gong Sui arrived in front of Emperor Xuan. As expected, the emperor asked him about the management of the Bohai Sea, and he answered according to Wang Sheng's words.
Emperor Xuan was pleased with his humility and courtesy, and said with a smile: "Where did you learn the words of a loyal elder?"
Gong Sui took the opportunity to step forward and said, "I don't know what I should say. It was my advisor Cao Wangsheng who warned me."
Because Gong Sui was old and could not take on the important responsibilities of a minister, Emperor Xuan appointed him as the Commander-in-Chief of Shuiheng, and proposed that King Cao be appointed Shuihengcheng to express his praise and respect for Gong Sui.
Shuiheng Duwei was in charge of Shanglin Garden, responsible for the furnishings of the palaces and pavilions, and providing sacrifices for the ancestral temple. It was an official position that was close to the emperor.
Gong Sui was highly regarded by Emperor Xuan and died in office.
Zhao Xinchen, named Wengqing, was from Shouchun County, Jiujiang County.
He was appointed as a Langguan as Ming Jingjia Ke, and left the capital to serve as the county magistrate of Guyang.
Ranked first in the performance appraisal, he was transferred to Shangcai County Magistrate.
He called his trusted ministers to love the people like his own sons, and was highly praised during his tenure as an official. Later, he was promoted to the prefect of Lingling County, but he returned due to illness.
After recovering from the illness, he was recruited as an admonishing doctor and later transferred to the post of governor of Nanyang County. His governance was as good as when he was in Shangcai.
summary: Gong Sui, from Pingyang County, was a loyal advisor to King Liu He of Changyi, often admonishing him for his unruly behavior. After Liu He was deposed, Gong Sui was sentenced to hard labor but later appointed governor of Bohai County. He quelled a rebellion by offering amnesty to farmers and promoting agriculture, leading to prosperity. He died in office, highly regarded by Emperor Xuan.

translation:
Zhao Xinchen is diligent and resourceful, likes to provide welfare for the people, and is committed to making them rich.
I personally work hard at farming, go to and from the fields, and stay in country houses. I rarely have any leisure time.
He inspected water springs in the county, presided over the opening of ditches, and erected dozens of water gates and sluices, which increased the irrigated farmland, reaching a maximum of 30,000 hectares.
The people benefited from water conservancy and irrigation, and the harvested grain was sufficient for storage.
Zhao Xinchen also formulated water regulations for the people, and engraved these regulations on stone tablets and erected them at the boundaries of the fields to prevent competition.
In addition, he also prohibited extravagance and waste during weddings and funerals, and was committed to promoting the trend of diligence and thrift.
If the children of prefecture and county officials roam freely, and if the prefecture and county officials do not regard farming as their official duties, they will all be reprimanded and dismissed from office. In serious cases, they will be brought to justice to observe the good and evil.
Through the above measures, education has been widely implemented in the county. Everyone in the county is engaged in agriculture. The people support county officials. The number of households in the county has also doubled, and the number of thieves and lawsuits has been reduced to a very small level.
Officials and people all loved Zhao Xinchen and called him Zhaofu.
The governor of Jingzhou praised the summoned ministers for their ability to seek benefits for the people, and the counties under their jurisdiction became rich, and they were given forty catties of gold.
Later, he summoned his ministers and was transferred to the post of governor of Henan. His governance performance always ranked first in the world, so his salary was increased many times and he was given gold.
During the Jingning period, Zhao Xinchen was conscripted into the Shaofu and was listed among the nine ministers. He asked the emperor not to repair and manage some distant palaces in the Shanglin area that the emperor rarely visited. He also asked the emperor to reduce the number of entertainment activities such as Yuefu Huangmen and advocating excellence, and to reduce the number of crossbows and equipment in the palaces by half.
The winter green onions and leeks grown in the Taiguan Garden had to be grown in a greenhouse, with fires burning day and night, and required warm air to grow. Zhao Xinchen believed that these did not grow naturally according to the seasons, and would be harmful to people if eaten. They were not suitable for the needs of the palace. They should be asked to stop planting them along with other crops that are not grown according to seasonal seasons. This would save tens of millions every year.
Later, he summoned his trusted ministers to die of old age while serving in office.
In the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, the emperor issued an edict to commemorate those who had done good things for the people among the hundreds of officials and officials. Shu County appointed Wen Weng, and Jiujiang summoned trusted ministers to respond to the edict.
Every year when the time comes, the prefect of the county leads his subordinate officials to pay homage to Zhao Xinchen's tomb, and a temple is built for him in Nanyang.
summary: Zhao Xinchen, from Shouchun County, was a diligent official who improved agriculture through irrigation, opening ditches and building water gates. He prohibited extravagance and promoted thrift, leading to increased household numbers and reduced crime. He served as governor of Henan and later as a minister, advising against wasteful palace projects. He died in office, and a temple was built for him in Nanyang.

translation:
Yang Xiong, courtesy name Ziyun, was from Chengdu, Shu County.
His ancestors were descendants of Zhou Boqiao. As a side branch of the common people, they took Yang of Jin as their food town and took it as their surname. It is not known which branch of Zhou Boqiao belonged to.
Yang is located between He and Fen. After the decline of Zhou Dynasty, some people in the Yang family were called marquises and were known as Yanghou.
When the six ministers of the Jin Dynasty struggled for power, Han, Wei, and Zhao rose, while Fan, Zhongxing, and Zhibo declined.
At this time, Yang Hou was forced to flee to Chuwu Mountain and settled there.
When the Chu and Han Dynasties arose, the Yang family traveled up the river and lived in Bajiang Prefecture.
Yang Jiguan became the prefect of Lujiang.
In the Dingjian of Han Dynasty, he avoided his enemies and went upriver. He lived in Pi, south of Mount Laoshan, where he had a farm and a house. He had been farming and raising silkworms for generations.
From Ji to Xiong, there was only one son in the Five Dynasties, so Yang Xiong had no other Yang clan in Shu.
Yang Xiong was eager to learn when he was a child. He did not study chapters and sentences. He only knew the explanations of words. He was well-read and read everything.
He is easy-going and tolerant, stutters and cannot speak quickly, is silent and contemplative, is quiet and inactive, has no hobbies and desires, does not pursue wealth, does not worry about poverty, and does not deliberately cultivate his character to gain fame in the world.
The family property does not exceed ten pieces of gold, and he is so poor that he does not have a stone to spare, but he is very safe.
If you have a broad mind, you won't like the books of sages; if they don't suit your own needs, you won't do them even if you can get rich and powerful.
But I like Ci Fu very much.
Previously, there was Sima Xiangru in Shu, and his poems were magnificent and elegant. Yang Zhongzhi admired him, and often used him as an example to imitate every time he wrote poems.
I was also surprised that Qu Yuan's writing was more talented than Xiangru, but he was not accepted. He wrote "Li Sao" and threw himself into the river to die. I felt sad for his article, and everyone read it without crying.
I believe that a gentleman can accomplish much when the times are going well, but when the times are not going well, he is just like a dragon and a snake dormant, and whether the opportunities are good or not depends on his destiny, so why bother throwing yourself into the water!
So he wrote an article, often excerpting sentences from "Li Sao" to refute it, and threw himself from Shushan into the river to mourn Qu Yuan, which was called "Reverse Lisao";
There are many texts in "Ban Lao Chou" and "Guang Sao" that do not record it. They only record "Anti Lisao", which says:
It is related to the Zhou family, which originated from Fenpan. The descendants of the gods began to write genealogies from Boqiao and developed to the last generation of Yanghou.
After experiencing the great turbulence of the river, he received the beauty of Zhou and Chu. He dropped memorials along the riverside to mourn the innocent dead ministers of Chu and Xiang. The road to heaven is impassable, so why are the innocent beings in trouble?
Dirty and unclear things are mixed and confused. In the tenth generation of the Han Dynasty, Yangshuo was reached, and the time of the swagger was the first month of Zhou Dynasty, which was based on the Qingming Festival of the emperor and the Zhouzheng of the earth.
summary: Yang Xiong, courtesy name Ziyun, was from Chengdu, Shu County. His ancestors were descendants of Zhou Boqiao, but as a side branch, they took Yang of Jin as their surname. After the Zhou Dynasty declined, some Yang family members became marquises. During the power struggles of the six ministers of Jin, Yang Hou fled to Chuwu Mountain. Later, during the Chu-Han conflict, the Yang family moved to Bajiang Prefecture. Yang Jiguan served as prefect of Lujiang, and during the Han Dynasty, his ancestor Yang Ji settled in Pi, south of Mount Laoshan, where the family farmed and raised silkworms for generations. From Ji to Xiong, there was only one son per generation for five generations, so Yang Xiong had no other Yang clan in Shu. Yang Xiong was eager to learn as a child, not studying chapters and sentences but focusing on word explanations. He was well-read, easy-going, and tolerant, with a stutter that made him speak slowly. He was contemplative, quiet, and without strong desires, not pursuing wealth or fame. His family property was meager, but he remained content. He admired Sima Xiangru's poetry and imitated him. He also felt sorrow for Qu Yuan's fate, believing a gentleman should adapt to circumstances rather than drown himself. He wrote "Reverse Lisao" to refute Qu Yuan's actions, excerpting from "Li Sao" to express his views.

translation:
After thinking that you are a noble, I also see your beautiful words, wearing rules and scales, and walking in the footsteps of the demon star.
She usually wears beautiful clothes, but why is her literary talent so narrow-minded?
She had Kunwa's beautiful hair, but she sold it to Jiurong for profit.
The phoenix is ​​flying on the wall, but it can't be caught by a goose!
Yiliu ran through twists and turns and had difficulty keeping up with the donkeys and mules.
Zhijiji is dirty and messy, and Yuan Hang is too worried to go down. Since King Chu believed Tan and Yan’s slander, why didn’t you notice it earlier? Wearing green clothes of lettuce and red clothes of hibiscus, the fragrance is so strong that no one can find it in this world, so it is better to fold it up and put it in another room.
The women compete with each other with their graceful looks, competing with each other in beauty. You know how jealous the beauties are, why do you frown?
The beautiful dragon lurks in the abyss, waiting for the clouds to rise and take off. Without the spring breeze, who knows where the dragon is?
It's a pity that your fragrant fragrance, the fragrant lings that floated in full bloom, were hit by the cold frost of the summer, died young and lost their beauty.
Cross the Hengjiang and Xiangjiang rivers and go south to Cangwu, riding the waves of Liaotan to seek justice from Chonghua.
Telling the troubles in my heart, I am afraid that Chonghua will not turn to you. If I ride on the white waves of Yanghou, will I only praise you?
Jingqiongmi and Qiuju should be used to enjoy life for a long time. They will sink themselves in the face of difficulties and are afraid of the sunset. Untie the bridle of Fusang's car and let it run wildly. Even Luanhuang's soaring speed can't keep up. It's not just Yingqing and Nuomian!
Roll up the rhizome and ruohui and throw them into the bottom of Hunan; a lot of pepper and fungus are drowned in the rivers and lakes. He used pepper paste to pray to the gods, and found a lot of Qiongmao. He did not listen to the spirit's divination, but he drowned by the river!
Since you admire what Fu said, why don't you really put it into practice?
It is in vain to worry that the doves will crow, but there will be no fragrance before the herbs!
It turns out that you abandoned your virgin concubine, and you wanted the beauties from Yaotai, so you asked the male concubine to be your matchmaker. Why did you leave so many times and not even one was worthy of you?
Riding on the beautiful clouds, traveling around Kenhe, looking around and feeling sentimental, why do you have to be an official in Gaoqiu?
If you don't have a magnificent chariot, how can you drive the eight dragons? Wiping tears by the riverside, how can there be "Nine Moves" and "Nine Songs"?
What happened to the sage was a matter of time and fate. Even though you often lament, I am afraid that your spiritual practice will not change because of you.
Once upon a time, Zhongni left Lu and traveled around, and finally returned to his old country. Why would he have to join the rapids at the bottom of Hunan!
Thinking that the fisherman was polluted by eating bad food and drinking pickled food, he shook off his clothes after taking a bath to be pure and pure, throwing away what was cherished by his pride and pride, and made the same mistake as Peng Xian!
When Xiao became emperor, a retainer recommended Yang Xiong's article as Dan Ying. The emperor spent three hours cultivating the ancestral temple in the outskirts of the city, and came to ask for an heir. He summoned Yang Xiong to wait for the imperial edict in Cheng Long's court.

summary: During Emperor Cheng's reign, a retainer recommended Yang Xiong's writing. The emperor summoned him to wait for an imperial edict. In the first month, Yang Xiong presented "Ode to Sweet Springs" as a satirical remonstrance. The ode described the grand procession to Ganquan Palace, its magnificent architecture, and the emperor's prayers for blessings. Yang Xiong praised the palace's splendor but subtly criticized its extravagance, comparing it to the imperial Purple Palace and suggesting it was built by ghosts and gods. He also noted that Zhaoyi, the emperor's favored consort, accompanied him, which he tactfully advised against.

So when the work was done, I changed my car and returned, passing through Sanman, resting in the fortress, where did I go?
The gates of heaven and the earth are opened, and the eight wastelands are harmonious with all nations.
The king of the land reclamation beats the thunder drum, the sound is loud and the ten brave men rise up, the clouds are flying and the rain is pouring, it is said that virtue shines on the world. Luan said: The high circular hills, the high and far sky, rise and fall, and circle around. The palaces are staggered, tall and connected, and the layers are deep and boundless. The things of heaven are high and swift, the Holy Emperor is beautiful, and they are in harmony with heaven and earth.
Come to the suburbs to offer sacrifices, the gods are attached to you, wandering and swaying, relaxed and relaxed.
The brilliance is dazzling, and the blessings are brought down, and the descendants will be endless forever.
Ganquan was originally built on the basis of Qin Li Palace. It was already very luxurious and gorgeous. Emperor Wu also added a towering, high-gloss, and wind-facing building.
Outside the palace are Hongya, Panghuang, Chuxu, and Nulu in the distance, and in the distance are Shiguan, Fengluan, Zhique, Luhan, Tangli, and Shide. The tour is magnificent and majestic. There are no wooden vessels that are not carved, and there are no walls that are not painted.
