He wanted to be silent but couldn't do it himself, so he praised it and compared it to the Purple Palace of the imperial family, as if it was not built by human power. It would be okay if it was built by ghosts and gods.
At this time, Zhaoyi was being favored. Whenever he went to Ganquan, he would always let her follow him according to etiquette and sit in the leopard's tail of the carriage.
Therefore, Yang Xiong tries his best to describe the chariots as numerous and beautiful, but they cannot be used to move heaven and earth and pray for blessings from the three gods.
He also said that he would repel jade girls and worry about concubines to tactfully exhort him to be pious.
The emperor was very surprised when the poem was completed.
In March of that year, when he wanted to offer sacrifices to his queen, the emperor led his ministers across the river and arrived at Fenyin.
After the sacrifice, we visited Jieshan on the road, bypassed Anyi, visited Longmen, Yanchi, climbed to the Li Temple, went up to the Huashan Mountains and looked at the eight wastelands, walked on the site of the Yin and Zhou dynasties, looked far away and missed the wind of Tang and Yu.
Yang Xiong thought that it would be better for the fish in Linchuan to retreat and build a net. After returning, he offered "Hedong Fu" to satirize and admonish him. The poem said:
In the late spring of this year, I wanted to offer sacrifices to my ancestors and worship the spirits. I went to Fenyin in the suburbs of Shu, where I carved my honorary name, passed down my great deeds, brought good fortune and brought blessings, and respected and obeyed the gods. It was so magnificent that I can’t finish the book! Then he ordered the ministers to dress up their legal uniforms and spiritual flags, carry a chariot decorated with emerald phoenixes, ride on six swift horses, turn around and run on a star-like flow, opening up the majestic arc of the Sirius.
Open the Xuanyuan that shines in the sun, raise the left 纛, and cover it with clouds.
Raise the electric whip, drive the thunder chariot, ring the bell, and raise the five flags.
Xihe is in charge of the sun, Yan Lun is driving, the wind is blowing, gods and ghosts are galloping; thousands of chariots and cavalry are vigorous and vigorous, and they are contented and contented, and the heaven and earth are shaken.
summary: In March, the emperor went to Fenyin for sacrifices, visiting various historical sites. Yang Xiong offered "Hedong Fu" to satirize, praising the emperor's journey and reflecting on ancient rulers. He emphasized the importance of virtue and following the examples of the Three Emperors and Five Emperors.

translation:
Jump over hills and mountains, jump over Jingwei rivers.
The god of Qin jumps in fear, and his soul leans on the embankment; the spirit of the river is startled, and his palms are in China, and his feet are falling.
Then he arrived at the Yin Palace, solemn and solemn, and his actions were measured.
The spirit has arrived, the order of the gods of the five directions has been determined, the sky is mysterious and the earth is yellow, and the great prosperity will follow.
So Lingyu stabilized his position and traveled around Anyu. Visit the company.
Sighing at Se Gong, he became a hero and felt sad. He mourned Yu the Great in the ridges, dug ditches to divert the floods, and spread the nine rivers along the coast of the East China Sea.
Climb the calendar to look far away and plan your travels. Appreciate the wind of the past, and like the land where the Yu family cultivated.
I saw the height of Emperor Tang and the tranquility of Sheng Zhou.
I couldn't leave because I wanted to see Peixia and Pengcheng. I hate the ruggedness of Nanchao, but I love the Guangping of Binqi.
Cross the river on a green dragon and climb the majestic Mount Huashan. The clouds floated in to greet me, the rain and dew fell, the silence was deep and the clouds lingered.
Encourage the gods to set an example and praise the Six Classics to express their aspirations. To be virtuous is too Zhou; to imitate the Three Emperors is better than the Five Emperors.
Starting from Pinglu, who said we can't follow if we have a long way to go? In December of this year, Yu hunted and Yang Xiong followed.
It is believed that during the time of the second emperor and the third king in ancient times, the products of the palaces, pavilions, marshes, ponds, gardens, woods, and deep lakes were enough to serve suburban temples, receive guests, and fill the kitchen, without robbing the people of their fertile grain fields and land for growing mulberry trees.
Women have surplus cloth, men have surplus grain, the country is rich and abundant, so the dew falls in the garden, the sweet spring gushes out from the pond, the phoenix builds its nest in the tree, the yellow dragon swims in the pond, the unicorn comes to the garden, and the divine sparrow roosts in the forest.
In the past, Yu appointed Yi to be in charge of the mountains and rivers, which were harmonious and luxuriant. Chengtang loved hunting in the fields and the world had sufficient wealth. King Wen's garden was a hundred miles long, but the people still thought it was too small. King Xuan of Qi's garden was forty miles long, but the people thought it was too big. This is the difference between making the people rich and robbing them of their wealth.
Emperor Wu expanded Shanglin to Yichun, Dinghu, Yusu, and Kunwu in the south, Nanshan Mountain in the west, Changyang and Wuzha, Huangshan Mountain in the north, and Weishui River in the east, with a circumference of several hundred miles. Following the example of the Dian River, the Kunming Pool was excavated to build Jianzhang, Fengque, Shenming, Yusuo, Jiantai, Taiye and Xiangxiang seawater to surround Fangzhang, Yingzhou and Penglai.
The sightseeing is luxurious and wonderful.
Although a lot of the three sides of Shanglin Garden were cut off for the common people, the construction of palace walls for hunting fields, chariots, horses, and equipment was still too extravagant and flashy, which was not the original intention of Yao, Shun, Cheng Tang, and King Wen.
Yang Xiong was also afraid that his descendants would add more repairs due to hobbies, so he did not take Quantai as a lesson, so he used "Xiao Xie Fu" to satirize and admonish him, saying in his speech:
Some people praise Xi Nong, but are future emperors more decorated?
The commentators said no, each one should adapt to the circumstances, so why should we follow one standard?
Otherwise, how could there be seventy-two rituals for sealing Mount Tai?
Therefore, those who start a business are not wrong. Who knows what is right or wrong among the Five Emperors and Three Kings near and far?
So he sang a poem: It is sacred and magnificent, living in Xuan Palace, as rich as the earth, as noble as the sky.
Qi Huan is not worthy to support the chariot, and Chu Yan is not worthy to drive the horse; break through the remoteness of the three kings and stride forward; be as grand as the five emperors, as high as the three emperors; use morality as a teacher, and make friends with benevolence and righteousness.
So in the last month of Yanyan, when the Yin Qi is strong, everything is born inside and dies outside. The emperor wants to go hunting in Lingde's garden, open up the north, and brave the northwest wind to inherit the legacy of Zhuanxu and Xuanming.
The people of Yu were ordered to take charge of the lake, and it was sent to Kunbian and to Guihe in the west.
summary: In December, Yang Xiong accompanied the emperor on a hunt. He believed that ancient rulers managed resources wisely, ensuring prosperity without harming the people. He criticized Emperor Wu's expansion of Shanglin Garden and the construction of lavish palaces, arguing they were excessive. He presented "Xiao Xie Fu" to satirize, describing the grand hunt and its impact on the land and people. He urged the emperor to focus on virtue, share resources with the people, and avoid extravagance. The ode concluded with a call for moral governance and a return to simplicity.

translation:
The next year, the emperor wanted to boast to the barbarians about the abundance of animals. In autumn, he ordered You Fufeng to recruit the people into Nanshan, starting from Baoxie in the west, Hongnong in the east, and Hanzhong in the south. He opened nets and set traps to catch bears, porcupines, tigers, leopards, and even foxes, dodders, and elk. They were loaded on carts and transported to the Changyang Shooting Bear Pavilion.
They used nets as a siege, wrapped the animals in dough, and taught the barbarians to fight with their bare hands. They took away the ones they caught, and the emperor went to watch them in person.
At this time, farmers cannot harvest crops.
Yang Xiong followed him to Shexiong Pavilion, and when he came back, he presented "Ode to Chang Yang". Since it was written in pen and ink, he used Hanlin as his host and Zimo as his guest to satirize him.
The words said:
Zimo Keqing asked the master of Hanlin: I heard that the Holy Lord nourishes the people, is benevolent and nourishing, and does not act for himself.
This year when hunting in Changyang, we first ordered the right to Fufeng, the left to Taihua and the right to Baoxie, cut down the banks for cruising, and arranged them around Nanshan. Thousands of horses were arranged in the forest, and tens of thousands of cavalry were distributed at the foot of the mountain. They led the troops to the paddocks and rewarded Rong, Di, and animals.
Catching bears, catching porcupines, and piling up wooden guns as savings is something you only see in the world.
Even so, it is very harassing to the farmers.
More than thirty years old, very hardworking, but unable to achieve anything. I am afraid that people who don’t know better will think of it as an entertainment trip outside, but not as a dried bean sacrifice inside. Isn’t it for the people?
Moreover, the monarch regards silence as his spiritual thought and indifference as his moral character. Now he likes to go far away to show his power. He has mobilized many armies and exhausted his chariots and soldiers. This is not something that the monarch needs to do urgently. I am privately puzzled.
The master of Hanlin said: Hey, that’s really weird!
Like you, you only know one but not the other. You see the outside but don’t know the inside. I'm too tired to talk about it in detail. Please allow me to give you a rough outline. You can decide for yourself what's necessary. The guest said: OK, OK.
The master said: In the past, there was a strong Qin Dynasty, which killed the scholars and the people like Feng Bo and Mo Nu. The chisel-toothed people grinded their teeth and fought with each other. The heroes were like elk boiling and the clouds were turbulent, so the people were restless.
So God favored the great ancestor, and he was ordered to follow the dipper, move the Tianguan, cross the sea, shake Kunlun, raise his sword and shout angrily, attack the city and seize the town, and defeat the generals. One day's battle cannot be fully remembered.
After working so hard, his hair was messy and he had no time to comb it. He was hungry and had no time to eat. Qian Sun was infested with lice and his armor was covered with sweat. He came to ask the emperor for orders for Wan Xing.
So he extended the people's subjugation, raised what the people lacked, planned for ten thousand years, restored the emperor's business, and made the world peaceful in seven years.
summary: The emperor, seeking to impress barbarian envoys with the empire's abundance of animals, ordered a massive hunt in the Nanshan region. Nets and traps were set to capture bears, porcupines, tigers, leopards, foxes, and elk, which were transported to the Changyang Shooting Bear Pavilion. The animals were enclosed in nets, and the barbarians were taught to fight them bare-handed. The emperor personally watched, while farmers were unable to harvest their crops due to the disruption. Yang Xiong accompanied the emperor and later presented "Ode to Chang Yang," using a dialogue between Zimo Keqing and the master of Hanlin to satirize the hunt. Zimo criticized the hunt for harassing farmers and questioned the emperor's priorities, arguing that such displays of power were not the monarch's urgent duty. The master of Hanlin defended the hunt by recounting past military campaigns against the Qin and various barbarian tribes, framing the hunt as a necessary demonstration of strength to maintain peace and deter future invasions. He argued that the hunt was part of a broader strategy to uphold the emperor's legacy and ensure the prosperity of the people.

translation:
During the reign of Emperor Ai, Ding, Fu, and Dong Xian were in power, and some of their vassals were appointed officials up to two thousand shi.
At that time, Di was drafting "Tai Xuan" to keep himself indifferent.
Some people mocked the slut for using black and advocating white. La gave an explanation for this, which was called "Explanation of Mockery".
The words said:
The guest laughed at Yangzi and said: I heard that the scholars of the past world were guided by the following principles: before they were born, they would respect the king upwards, honor their parents below, distinguish people's honors, receive other people's titles, own other people's talismans, receive other people's salaries, wear blue and purple ribbons, and ride in the car of Zhu Dan.
Now you are lucky enough to meet the Ming Dynasty, to be in the court where you don't have to worry about, and to be among the wise men. It has been a long time since you passed through the Golden Gate and went to the Jade Hall.
His eyes are like stars, his tongue is like lightning, he moves vertically and horizontally, no one can resist the debating, but he wrote "Tai Xuan" with five thousand words, spread out among the branches and leaves, and only explained more than one hundred thousand words. The depth is as deep as the underworld, the height is as high as the sky, the big one contains the vitality, and the fine one is incomparable. However, he cannot be ranked as a minister, and he has only been promoted to serve in the Huangmen.
Did you expect that Xuan can't be used to worship the color white?
Why is being an official so reclusive?
Yangzi smiled and replied: You just want my chariot and horses to be gorgeous, but you don't know that one mistake will make my family bleed!
In the past, the Zhou Dynasty was weakened and the feudal princes were in dispute. They were divided into twelve, which were combined into six or seven. They were divided into four parts and became the Warring States Period.
Scholars do not have a permanent monarch, and the country does not have fixed ministers. When they gain wealth from scholars, they become poor when they lose them. They fly with their wings and rest wherever they want. Therefore, some scholars use bags to pack themselves, and some cut through walls to escape.
Therefore, Kuiyan gained fame due to his uncertainty, and Meng Ke was still a master of ten thousand chariots despite encountering difficulties.
Now the Han Dynasty has the East China Sea on its left, Qusou on its right, Panyu in front, and Taotu in the back.
There is a lieutenant in the southeast and a lieutenant in the northwest.
The guilty were tied to Hui Mo, and the more serious ones were beheaded with a sword, the rituals and music were distributed, the "Poems" and "Books" were taught, and the schools were built, which lasted for a long time.
The scholars in the world all move like thunder, gather like clouds, and overlap like fish scales. They are all operating in all directions. Every family thinks they have a bond with Ji, and everyone thinks they are guilty. Those who wear tassels on their heads and talk about themselves are compared to Aheng, and a five-foot boy is ashamed. Compared with Yan Yingyiwu, those who have a smooth journey are as high as the blue clouds, and those who have nowhere to go are abandoned in ditches. In the morning, they are ministers, and in the evening, they are ordinary men. They are like small sparrows in rivers and lakes, and small birds in Bojie. The gathering of four wild geese is not too many, and the flying of two ducks is not too few.
In the past, Yin was weak after the three benevolent men left, and the two old men returned to the Zhou Dynasty and became strong. Zixu died and the Wu subjugated the country.
Therefore, when the world is in turmoil, it will not be stable unless it is Xiao, Cao, Zifang, Ping, Bo, Fan, and Huo; when the world is stable, there is nothing to be afraid of if the Confucian scholars of Zhang, Ju and Xiao sit together to guard.
Therefore, when the world is in turmoil, it is not enough for the sages to drive; when the world is stable, it is enough for the mediocre to rest easy.
Scholars of the past generations, some were untied to make appearances, some took off their brown clothes, some leaned on their clothes to laugh, some crossed the rivers and lakes to fish; some lobbied for seventy times but were not used, some were made marquises while standing and talking; some let the king of thousands of chariots come to the back alley, and some made the king hold a broom as a guide.
Therefore, scholars are very good at sticking out their tongues and picking up their pens, and there is no limit to how they can squeeze into gaps.
Nowadays, county magistrates do not invite scholars, county guards do not welcome teachers, ministers do not treat guests politely, and generals do not lower their eyebrows. Those who talk about strange things are suspected, and those who behave strangely are punished. Therefore, those who want to talk are silent, and those who want to go are hesitant.
If the scholars of the previous generations were to be in today's situation, if their strategy was not to be disciplined, their behavior was not to be filial and honest, their behavior was not to be upright, they could only be sparse, they often commented on right and wrong, if the good ones waited for Shao Shu, if the bad ones were reported, they were dismissed, how could they be covered with bruises?
summary: Yang Xiong also wrote "Explanation of Mockery" in response to critics who questioned his reclusive lifestyle and his work on "Tai Xuan." He defended his indifference to worldly success by contrasting the chaotic Warring States period, where scholars could rise and fall rapidly, with the stable Han Dynasty, where opportunities were limited. He argued that his focus on "Tai Xuan" was a deliberate choice to avoid the dangers of political ambition, comparing himself to historical figures who thrived or perished based on timing. In "Resolving Difficulties," Yang Xiong addressed complaints that "Tai Xuan" was too obscure. He argued that profound truths are inherently difficult to communicate, comparing his work to the "Book of Changes" and classical texts that required deep understanding. He maintained that his writings were meant for discerning readers, not the masses, and that their value would be recognized over time.

translation:
During the reign of Wang Mang, both Liu Xin and Zhen Feng became princes. Since Wang Mang relied on the talisman to establish himself, after he came to the throne, he wanted to ban this practice in order to deify his past affairs. Zhen Feng's son Zhen Xun and Liu Xin's son Liu Fen also presented the talisman's fortune.
Wang Mang killed Zhen Feng and his son, and exiled Liu Fen to the fourth generation. Anyone implicated in his confession was immediately dismissed without any need to report.
At that time, Yang Xiong was writing to the colonel in Tianlu Pavilion. The envoy handling the case came and wanted to arrest Yang Xiong. Yang Xiong was afraid that he could not escape, so he jumped from the pavilion and almost died.
After hearing this, Wang Mang said: Yang Xiong has never been involved in this matter, why is he in this case?
They secretly inquired about the reason and found out that Liu Fen had learned to write strange characters from Yang Xiong, but Yang Xiong didn't know about it.
Shao Shao will not pursue him.
However, the capital master commented on this: Because of loneliness, he is in harmony with himself; because of tranquility, he is a talisman.
Yang Xiong was dismissed from his post due to illness and was called a doctor again.
His family has always been poor and he likes to drink. People rarely come to his home.
At that time, troubled people brought wine and food to study with him. Julu Houba often lived with Yang Xiong and learned "Tai Xuan" and "Fa Yan".
Liu Xin also saw it and said to Yang Xiong: You have made yourself suffer in vain!
Nowadays, scholars with good fortune cannot understand "Yi", let alone "Xuan"?
I'm afraid that future generations will use it to cover sauce pots.
Yang Xiong smiled but didn't answer.
He lived to be seventy-one years old and died in the fifth year of Tianfeng. Houba built a tomb for him and kept a mourning for him for three years.
At that time, Grand Sikong Wangyi and Nayan Yanyou heard that Yang Xiong had died and said to Huan Tan: Can your book praising Yang Xiong be passed down to future generations?
Huan Tan said: It will definitely spread.
But you and Huan Tan can’t see it.
Mortals despise the near and value the far. Seeing with their own eyes that Yang Ziyun's status and appearance are not impressive, they despise his books.
In the past, Lao Dan wrote two articles on nothingness, which underestimated benevolence and righteousness and refuted rituals. However, later generations liked it and thought it surpassed the Five Classics. Emperors Wen, Jing, and Sima Qian of the Han Dynasty all said this.
Nowadays, Yangzi's books have the deepest meaning, and their expositions do not violate the saints. If they meet the monarchs of that time, read them by the wise men, and are praised by them, they will definitely surpass the scholars.
Some scholars ridiculed Yang Xiong for not being a saint but writing scriptures, just like the Spring and Autumn Period monarchs of Wu and Chu who overrode and proclaimed themselves kings, which should be the crime of annihilating their clans and their descendants.
It has been more than 40 years since Yang Xiong's death, and his "Fayan" has become popular in the world. However, "Xuan" has not been revealed in the end, but the chapters are there.
summary: Yang Xiong's later years were marked by political turmoil during Wang Mang's usurpation. Despite being implicated in a scandal involving Liu Xin's son, he was spared due to his lack of involvement. He lived in poverty, indifferent to fame, and died at seventy-one. His works, particularly "Fayan," gained popularity after his death, though "Tai Xuan" remained less understood. Critics compared his writing of scriptures to unauthorized claims of kingship, but Huan Tan predicted his works would endure, noting that future generations would appreciate their depth.

Entered the DPRK in the twenty-fourth year.
Twenty-five years later, he entered the DPRK again.
At that time, the emperor had not decided on the crown prince, so he casually said while having a banquet with Xiao Wang Liu Wu: I will pass the throne to you after my death.
King Xiao resigned.
Although King Xiao knew that what the emperor said was not true, he was very happy.
The same is true for the Queen Mother.
In the spring of this year, the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Tang rebelled. They first attacked Liang Guo Jibi and killed tens of thousands of people.
Liang Wang Liu Wu stayed in Suiyang and sent Han Anguo, Zhang Yu and others as generals to fight against Wu and Chu.
Wu and Chu were stopped by Liang Guo and did not dare to go westward. They faced off with Taiwei Zhou Yafu and others for three months.
Wu, Chu and other countries were defeated, and the number of enemy troops killed by Liang and Han was approximately the same.
In the second year, the Han Dynasty established a prince.
The Liang Kingdom was the closest to the emperor, had military exploits, and was a big country with fertile territory. It stretched from Mount Tai in the north to Gaoyang in the west. It had more than 40 cities in total, most of which were large counties.
Xiao Wang Liu Wu was the youngest son of the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother liked him very much and gave him countless rewards.
King Xiao then built Shuyuan, with a radius of more than 300 miles, which was 70 miles wider than Suiyang City. He built a large palace in Dongyuan, built an air passage between the pavilions, and built a road more than 30 miles from the palace to the platform to leave the palace.
Under the banner of the emperor's gift, he followed thousands of people on horseback and avoided pedestrians when he came in and out, just like the emperor.
He also recruited heroes from all over, and Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, Zou Yang and other wanderers from Shandong came to him one after another.
Gongsun Gui was a man of many tricks. After the first meeting with King Xiao, he gave him a thousand pieces of gold, promoted him to lieutenant, and became known as General Gongsun.
King Xiao also ordered hundreds of thousands of crossbows, bows and arrows to be made, and the money in the treasury was millions, and the jewels and jades were more than those in the capital.
In October of the 29th year, King Xiao entered the court.
Emperor Jing sent someone in a four-horse chariot to meet him outside the city. After arriving at court, King Xiao wrote to Emperor Jing and stayed.
summary: Emperor Xiaowen had four sons. Empress Dou bore Emperor Xiaojing and Liu Wu, King Xiao of Liang, while Zhu Ji bore Liu Shen, Prince Xiao, and Liu Yi, King Huai of Liang. Liu Wu was initially made King of Dai, later transferred to Huaiyang, and finally to Liang in the twelfth year of Emperor Xiaowen’s reign, serving as king for eleven years. He frequently entered the court, and during one banquet, Emperor Xiaojing casually offered to pass the throne to him, which Liu Wu declined but was pleased by. In the spring of the twenty-fourth year, the seven kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and others rebelled, attacking Liang. Liu Wu defended Suiyang with generals Han Anguo and Zhang Yu, holding off Wu and Chu for three months until they were defeated. Liang’s military exploits and proximity to the emperor made it a large, fertile kingdom with over forty cities.

translation:
Because of the empress dowager, King Xiao was of the same generation as Emperor Jing when he went in, and rode with Emperor Jing when he went out, and went hunting in the mountains and forests together.
The servants, ministers and eunuchs of the Liang Kingdom could enter and leave the Emperor's Palace with their name certificates, just like the eunuchs in the desert.
In November, the emperor deposed Prince Li, and the Queen Mother wanted to let Prince Liang succeed him.
The ministers and Yuan An and others remonstrated with Emperor Jing, and the Queen Mother's suggestion was shelved. King Xiao did not dare to discuss the succession with the Queen Mother anymore.
The matter was a secret and unknown to the world, so King Xiao immediately left and returned to his country.
In the summer, the emperor made King Micellar the crown prince.
The King of Liang hated Yuan An and the ministers who made suggestions, so he conspired with Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and others, and secretly sent people to assassinate Yuan An and a dozen other ministers.
As a result, the assassin failed.
The emperor suspected that this matter was done by Liang Guo, and after further investigation, he found out that it was indeed sent by Liang Guo.
So he sent a large team of people to Liang Guo to investigate the matter.
Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng were hunted down and hid in the palace of Queen Liang.
The envoy sent two thousand stone officials to urge the king of Liang to surrender. Liang's Prime Minister Xuan Qiubao and Internal Secretary Han Anguo cried to persuade the King of Liang, and the King of Liang ordered Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to commit suicide and then hand them over.
The emperor was angry with King Liang because of this.
The King of Liang was in panic, so he sent Han Anguo to apologize to the Queen Mother through the eldest princess, and then he calmed down.
After the emperor's anger subsided, King Xiao of Liang immediately submitted a letter to the court.
When they arrived outside the city, the doctor Mao Lan advised King Xiao to enter the city in a carriage with a cloth curtain, taking only two knights with him, and first hid in the eldest princess's garden.
When the Han Emperor's envoy came to pick up King Xiao, King Xiao had already entered the city, but his carriage and horses were outside the city, and others did not know where he had gone.
The Queen Mother cried and said: The emperor has killed my son!
The emperor was also very nervous.
Soon King Xiao of Liang came to the palace to plead guilty. The Queen Mother and the Emperor were overjoyed to see him. After crying with each other, they reconciled as before.
King Xiao's followers were also summoned into the city.
However, Emperor Jing became more distant from Prince Xiao and stopped riding in the chariot with him.
In the winter of the thirty-fifth year, King Xiao entered the court again and wrote a letter to stay, but the emperor refused.
King Xiao felt unhappy after returning home.
One day, King Xiao went hunting on Liangshan Mountain in the north. Someone offered a cow with legs growing out of its back. King Xiao didn't like it very much.
On June 6, King Xiao fell ill with fever and died.
King Xiao was very filial. Every time he heard that the Queen Mother was ill, he couldn't eat and often wanted to stay in Chang'an to accompany the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother also liked him very much.
After hearing that King Xiao died, Queen Mother Dou cried very sadly, refused to eat or drink, and said: The emperor really killed my son!
The emperor was sad and scared, and didn't know what to do.
After discussing with the eldest princess, the emperor decided to divide the Liang Kingdom into five kingdoms, grant the title of king to each of King Xiao's five sons, and grant land and salary to King Xiao's five daughters.
This matter was reported to the Queen Mother, who became happy and had a meal for the sake of the Emperor.
Before the death of King Xiao, his property was in the tens of millions, which was countless.
By the time of his death, there were more than 400,000 kilograms of gold hidden in the house, and other properties were also equivalent to that.
summary: Liu Wu, favored by the Queen Mother, built a grand garden and palace, amassed vast wealth, and recruited heroes like Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and Zou Yang. He manufactured weapons and stored treasures exceeding the capital’s. In the twenty-ninth year, he entered the court and was honored by Emperor Jing, riding together and hunting. After the emperor deposed Prince Li, the Queen Mother wanted Liu Wu to succeed, but ministers like Yuan An dissuaded the emperor, and Liu Wu left. Later, Liu Wu conspired to assassinate Yuan An and others, but the plot failed. The emperor investigated, and Liu Wu’s men hid. After pressure, Liu Wu ordered them to commit suicide. The emperor grew distant, and Liu Wu, in panic, apologized through the eldest princess. He later hid in the princess’s garden, causing the Queen Mother to weep, but reconciled with the emperor. However, Emperor Jing stopped riding with him. In the thirty-fifth year, Liu Wu entered the court but was denied stay, becoming unhappy. He died of fever on June 6 after hunting and seeing a strange cow. He was filial, often wanting to stay with the Queen Mother when she was ill. Her grief led the emperor to divide Liang into five kingdoms for Liu Wu’s sons and grant land to his daughters. Liu Wu’s wealth was immense, with over 400,000 kilograms of gold at death.

translation:
On behalf of Xiao Wang Liu Canchu was granted the title of King of Taiyuan.
In the fourth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the original king Liu Wu was granted the title of King of Huaiyang. Liu Shen was renamed the acting king and continued to be in charge of Taiyuan, with Jinyang as the capital.
He went to Beijing to pay homage once every five years and visited the court three times in total.
Seventeen years later, King Dai died and his son, King Liu Deng, succeeded him.
Twenty-nine years later, Liu Deng died and his son Liu Yi succeeded him.
During the Yuanding period, the Han Dynasty expanded the mountain passes and used Changshan as a dangerous pass. The Prince Dai's Mansion was moved to Qinghe and renamed Prince Gang's Mansion.
Including the time of the current king, he died after reigning forty years. His son Liu Tang, King Qing, came to the throne.
He died twenty-four years later and was succeeded by his son Liu Nian.
During the Dijie period, Lin, the governor of Jizhou, wrote a letter stating that when Liu Nian was the prince, he had an affair with his sister Liu Ze.
After Liu Nian was crowned king, Liu Ze became pregnant with Liu Nian's child.
Liu Ze's husband refused to let her raise the child, so Liu Ze said: "Come and kill him yourself."
Her husband said angrily: If you give birth to a child for King Gang, of course you have to raise it for him.
Liu Ze sent the child to the Queen Mother Qing's home.
When the prime minister of the palace found out, he stopped her and refused to let her enter the palace.
However, Liu Nian sent his father Ji to greet and see off Liu Ze, which continued year after year.
A superior reported that Liu Nian was guilty of promiscuity, so Liu Nian was deposed as a commoner, moved to Fangling, and granted a hundred households a fief.
Three years later, the state was abolished.
In the second year of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the prince of Xindu sent a mission to support the extinct kingdom. He sent a report to the Empress Dowager and established his younger brother's son, Zhuxuan, as King Chensai to succeed King Xiao.
After Wang Ling usurped the throne, the feudal state was abolished.

He likes "Shi Zhen" and "Shang Shu", and the chief inspector likes him differently from other sons.

In the second year, King Luan Xiao died and moved to Feng Kuang.
The five sons of King Xiao of Liang were all named kings: the eldest son Liu Mai was the King of Liang Gong, the second son Liu Ming was the King of Ji, the third son Peng Li was the King of Ji Shu, the fourth son Liu Xuan was the King of Shanyang, and the fifth son Pi Yao was the King of Nadan Mu. They were all crowned kings on the same day in the sixth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign.
Liang Communist King Liu Mai died after reigning for seven years, and his son Ping Wang Liu Xiang succeeded to the throne.
Liu Ming, the king of Jichuan, was granted the title of king from the title of Marquis of Yuanyi.
When he was in power for seven years, he shot and killed one of his lieutenants. His superiors reported that he should be executed. Jihu could not bear to kill him, so he was deposed as a civilian and moved to Fangling County, thus deposing his kingdom.
King Pengli of Jidong reigned for twenty-nine years.
summary: Liu Shen, King of Taiyuan, visited court three times before dying. His descendants ruled until Liu Nian was deposed for incest with his sister. Liu Yi, King Huai of Liang, died from a fall, leaving no heirs. Liu Wu’s five sons were all made kings on the same day. Liu Mai, King Gong of Liang, died after seven years. Liu Ming was deposed for murder. Peng Li, King of Jidong, was deposed for robbery and murder. Liu Ding, King Ai of Shanyang, died without heirs. Another son died without issue.

translation:
Peng Li has an arrogant temperament. He often goes out secretly at night to rob with dozens of his desperate youths, taking pleasure in killing people and grabbing money.
As far as anyone knew, they killed more than a hundred people. The whole country knew about this, and the people did not dare to go out at night.
The victim's children complained, and a minister petitioned the emperor to behead him. Emperor Wu couldn't bear it, so he deposed him as a commoner and moved him to Shangyong County. He abolished his feudal state and changed it to Dahe County.
Liu Ding, the Ai King of Shanyang, died after reigning for nine years. Because he had no children, the feudal state was abolished.
King Ji Yin'ai died without a son within a year of his reign, and the feudal kingdom was abolished.
Prince Xiao and his concubine were all crowned kings, but they all died without heirs.
The mother of Liang Ping Wang Liu Xiang was the Queen Mother Chen.
The mother of King Gong of Liang was Queen Mother Li.
Queen Mother Li is the biological grandmother of King Liang Ping.
The queen of King Ping of Liang was Queen Ren, and she was very favored by Liu Xiang.
At that time, King Xiao had a wine bottle decorated with cloud and thunder patterns, which was worth thousands of gold. King Xiao once told his descendants to take good care of it and never give it to others.
After Ren Hou heard about this wine bottle, he wanted to get it.
Queen Mother Li said: The late king has a destiny, and this wine bottle cannot be given to others.
You can take other things no matter how much they are worth.
But Ren Hou insisted on getting it.
So Liu Xiang directly sent someone to open the door of the mansion, take out the wine bottles, and give them to the queen. Liu Xiang and his mother, Queen Mother Chen, were not filial enough to Queen Mother Li.
One time, Emperor Mo's envoy came, and Empress Dowager Li wanted to complain in person. Liu Xiang sent his envoy Zhonglang Hu and others to stop him and closed the door.
Empress Dowager Li tried to rush out and injured her finger. She cried and shouted, but she still didn't see the Han envoy.
Because Empress Dowager Li had committed adultery with the Chief Food Officer and Lang Guan Yin Ba, King Ping and Empress Ren sent people to dissuade Empress Dowager Li, and Empress Dowager Li gave up.
Later Empress Dowager Li died of illness. When Empress Dowager Li was ill, Empress Ren did not visit her; when she died, Empress Ren did not go to mourn her either.
During the Yuanshuo period, someone insulted the father of a rebel named Suiyang. The man went out to ride with the guests of Suiyang Prefect, and then he jumped on the train and killed the enemy, and then ran away.
The prefect of Suiyang was furious and ordered two thousand officials from Liang State to capture the fugitive.
Er Qian Shi's men were very anxious to capture Mian Fan, so they first took his relatives as hostages.
Wan Fu knew about the scandal in Liang's palace, so he complained to the king of Liang about the dispute over the wine bottle with his grandmother.
At that time, everyone below the prime minister knew about this and wanted to use it to punish the senior officials of Liang State.
Someone wrote a letter to the emperor, and the emperor sent someone to inquire and found that the matter was true.
After the minister investigated the case, he reported to the emperor that he wanted to kill the King of Liang and the Queen Mother Chen for being unfilial.
The emperor said: The culprit is Empress Ren.
As for the King of Liang, I appointed the prime minister and officials inappropriately and failed to assist him properly, which led to his inappropriate behavior. I couldn't bear to let him die.
So he only cut off the territory of the five counties of Liang Wang, took away the Chengyang city of Empress Dowager Chen, and put the heads of the queen's oars in public, and beheaded the middle men and Hu.
In this way, Liang Guo still had eight cities left.
Liu Xiang died after reigning for forty years, and his son Qing Wang Wushang succeeded him.
Wushang died eleven years after he ascended the throne, and his son Jingwang Dingguo succeeded him.
Dingguo died after reigning for forty years, and his son Liu Sui, King of Yi, succeeded him.
Liu Sui died after reigning for six years and was succeeded by his son Liu Jia, King Huang.
Liu Jia died after reigning for fifteen years, and his son Liu Li succeeded him.
summary: Liu Xiang, King Ping of Liang, favored Queen Ren, who coveted a wine bottle left by Liu Wu. Queen Mother Li refused, but Liu Xiang took it. Conflicts arose, and Queen Mother Li’s adultery was exposed. After her death, Queen Ren failed to mourn. During the Yuanshuo period, a fugitive revealed palace scandals. The emperor investigated, found Queen Ren guilty, and reduced Liang’s territory. Liu Xiang died after forty years. His descendants ruled until Liu Li, King Huang, committed adultery with his aunt and murdered officials. Despite multiple crimes, the emperor showed mercy, only reducing territory. Liu Li later committed suicide after being deposed. The kingdom was eventually abolished.

translation:
Emperor Xiaojing had fourteen sons.
Queen Wang gave birth to Emperor Xiaowu.
Li Ji was born to Liu Rong, the Min king of Linjiang, Liu De, the Xian king of Hejian, and Liu Yan, the Ai king of Linjiang.
Cheng Ji gave birth to Liu Yu, king of the Communist Party of Lu, Liu Fei, king of Yi in Jiangdu, and Liu Duan, king of Jiaoxi.
Buying a wife gave birth to King Zhao Jingsu, Liu Pengzu, and King Jing of Zhongshan, Liu Sheng.
Tang Ji grew up and settled with King Liu Fa.
Mrs. Wang was born as Prince Hui of Guangchuan, Liu Yue, Prince Kang of Micellar, Liu Ji, Prince Ai of Qinghe, Liu Cheng, and Prince Xian of Changshan, Liu Shun.
Liu De, the king of Hejian, was granted the title of king in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign. He studied academically and loved ancient affairs. He always started from reality and reached correct conclusions.
If you get a good book among the people, you must make a good copy to the book owner, leave the original copy of the book, and give money and silk to widely recruit good books.
In this way, people with moral knowledge from all over came from far and wide, some of whom had books collected by their ancestors, and most of them donated to King Xian, so the number of books obtained was as large as that of the Han Dynasty.
At the same time, Huainan King Liu An also loved books, and most of the books he recruited were useless.
The books that King Xian obtained were all old ancient texts from before the Qin Dynasty, such as Zhou Guan, Shangshu, Rites, Book of Rites, Mencius, Laozi and other books. They were all written by seventy disciples of Confucius.
King Xian studied and applied the Six Classics, and established doctors of Mao's Poetry and Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.
Practice rituals and music, experience Confucian academics personally, and everything you learn must be based on Confucianism.
Many scholars from Shandong followed him there.
During the period of Emperor Wu, King Xian came to court, offered elegant music, and answered more than 30 questions from Sanyong Palace and imperial edicts.
As far as the moral scholarship he talks about is concerned, it is reasonable and the language is concise and clear.
King Xian died after reigning for twenty-six years.
Lieutenant Chang Li reported to the court, saying: The king himself is upright and clear in his behavior. He is gentle, kind, respectful and frugal. He sincerely respects and loves his subordinates. He knows deeply and is kind to widowers.
Daxing ordered: "Mi Fa said that the wise and wise people are called Xian, and Mi should be Lu Zhi."
His son King Pi Zhou succeeded him and died after reigning for four years.
His son Liu Kan, King Gang, succeeded him and died after reigning for twelve years.
His son Liu, the king of Qing, succeeded him and died after reigning for seventeen years.
His son, Xiaowang Liu Qing, succeeded him and died after reigning for forty-three years.
His son Liu Yuan succeeded to the throne.
Liu Yuan married the deceased King Li of Guangling, his crown prince, and the former concubine Lian of King Huai of Zhongshan as his concubines.
During the Ganlu period, the governor of Jizhou Chang reported Liu Yuan's case. The emperor handed the matter over to Tingwei for trial and wanted to arrest Lian and others.
Liu Yuan forced and threatened Gong Qi and ordered them to commit suicide.
Relevant officials petitioned Liu Yuan to be executed, and the emperor issued an edict to cut down two counties, totaling 11,000 households.
Later, Liu Yuan resented the young official Liu Gui. Liu Gui was afraid of escaping over the wall and wanted to report Liu Yuan. Liu Yuan sent people to kill Liu Gui's mother.
summary: Emperor Xiaojing had fourteen sons by various consorts. Among them, Liu De, the King of Hejian, was a notable scholar who loved ancient texts. He diligently collected books from the people, offering generous compensation for rare copies, amassing a collection as vast as the imperial library. Unlike King Huainan of An, whose books were often useless, Liu De’s collection consisted of pre-Qin classics like the *Zhou Guan*, *Shangshu*, *Rites*, *Mencius*, and *Laozi*, all attributed to Confucius’s seventy disciples. He established doctors for the *Mao Poetry* and *Zuo’s Spring and Autumn Annals*, practiced rituals and music, and adhered to Confucian teachings, attracting many scholars from Shandong. During Emperor Wu’s reign, he presented elegant music and answered over thirty questions from the court with clarity and reason. After reigning for twenty-six years, he died, praised by officials for his uprightness, kindness, and frugality. His descendants ruled Hejian for generations, though later kings like Liu Yuan faced scandal and deposition for cruelty and misconduct, leading to the kingdom’s abolition and restoration under Emperor Cheng.

translation:
Relevant officials reported that Liu Yuan's cruel nature would not change and he could not govern his subjects as the king of the country.
So he was deposed and allowed to live in Fanling, Hanzhong.
After several years of encountering each other, he became angry with Ruo because he and his wife were riding a chariot together, so he whipped her and ordered her to shave off her hair.
The prefect of Hanzhong asked Liu Yuan to be punished, but Liu Yuan later died of illness.
In the seventeenth year of Liu Yuan's reign, the Hejian Kingdom was abolished.
The Hejian Kingdom was cut off for five years, and in the first year of Emperor Cheng's founding, Liu Liang, Liu Yuan's younger brother, was re-established as King Hui of Hejian.
Liu Liang learned the behavior of offering sacrifices to the king. His mother, the Empress Dowager, passed away and observed the funeral as a courtesy.
Emperor Ai issued an edict of praise and said: Liu Liang, the king of Hejian, stayed in mourning for the Queen Mother for three years. He actually set an example for the clan and granted him the title of Ten Thousand Households.
He died after reigning for twenty-seven years.
His son Liu Shang succeeded to the throne, but Wang Mang's line of succession was cut off.
Linjiang Ai Wang Xing'er was granted the title of king in the second year of the Yuan Dynasty in Jicha. He died after reigning for three years without leaving any sons, and the title was abolished as a county.
Linjiang Min King Liu Rong was the crown prince in the fourth year of Emperor Jing's reign. Four years later, he was deposed as the prince of Linjiang.
Another three years passed. Because he occupied the open space of the temple to build a palace, the emperor conscripted Liu Rong.
When Liu Ming set out, he worshiped his ancestors at the north gate of Jiangling. After getting on the car, the axle broke and the car broke down.
The elders of Jiangling cried privately and said: Our king will not come back!
After Liu Rong arrived in the capital, he went to the Lieutenant's Mansion for trial.
Lieutenant Zhidu interrogated the king with a confession. The king was frightened and committed suicide.
He was buried in Lantian, and tens of thousands of swallows placed earth on the grave. The people felt pity for his plight.
Liu Rong was the oldest and had no sons, so his feudal state was abolished.
The fiefdom was transferred to the Han Dynasty and became Nanjun.
King Gong of Lu, Liu Yu, was granted the title of King of Huaiyang in the second year of Emperor Jing's reign.
Wu Chu rebelled, and after being defeated, Liu Yu moved to Lu in the third year of Emperor Jing's reign.
Liu Yu liked to build palaces, gardens, and raise dogs and horses. In his later years, he liked music but disliked literature.
He was born with a stutter and had trouble speaking.
King Liu Gong of Lu died after reigning for twenty-eight years.
His son An Wang Liu Guang succeeded to the throne. He was initially fond of music, carriages and horses, but in his later years he was greedy and stingy for fear of insufficient wealth.
He died after reigning for forty years. His son Xiao Wang Qingji succeeded him and died after reigning for thirty-seven years.
His son Liu Jin, King of Qing, succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-eight years.
His son, King Wen Liu, succeeded him to the throne. He died after reigning for eighteen years without any sons, and the feudal state was abolished.
In the third year of Emperor Ai's reign, he also made Liu Min, Marquis of Buxiang, the younger brother of King Wen Liu Sui, the son of King Qing, as king.
It was cut off when Wang Mang died.
Prince Gong initially liked to expand his palace and destroyed Confucius' old house to expand his palace. When he heard the sound of bells, chimes, harps and harps, he did not dare to destroy it any more, and he obtained ancient scriptures and scriptures in the walls of the old house.
Liu Fei, the king of Yi in Jiangdu, was granted the title of King of Runan in the second year BC of Xiaojing.
summary: Other sons of Emperor Xiaojing had varied fates. Liu Rong, the Min King of Linjiang, was once crown prince but was deposed and later committed suicide after being accused of building a palace on temple grounds. Liu Yu, the King of Lu, was known for building palaces and raising dogs and horses, but he had a stutter and disliked literature. His descendant, Liu Gong, destroyed Confucius’s old house to expand his palace but stopped upon hearing music, discovering ancient scriptures in the walls. Liu Fei, the King of Yi in Jiangdu, was a talented youth who fought against Wu during the rebellion, but later became arrogant and extravagant. His son, Liu Jian, was notoriously depraved, committing adultery, murder, and even plotting rebellion with weapons and seals. He was eventually forced to commit suicide, and his kingdom was abolished. Liu Duan, the King of Jiaoxi, was cruel and physically weak, often killing officials who tried to govern lawfully, leading to his kingdom’s reduction and eventual abolition.

translation:
Jie Dan is hypocritical, flattering, overly respectful to others, but cruel at heart, accustomed to using the law, and using sophistry to frame people.
Dona's favorite concubine has many descendants.
Xiang Erqianshi planned to govern according to Han law, which would be harmful to the Wang family.
Therefore, every time he saw someone arriving with a promise of two thousand stones, Peng Zu would wear a single coat of silk and go to the front door of the hall to greet him. He would deceive him with many suspicious things and make him shake. If Erqianshi's words were wrong or consistent with taboo things, he would write them down.
If Erqianshi wanted to govern, he would use these records to coerce and threaten; if he did not obey, he would write a letter to report and falsely accuse him of greed for profit.
Pengzu had been in power for more than sixty years, and Erqianshi's term of office could not last more than two years. He resigned due to crimes. The elder was executed and the younger was tortured. Therefore, no one in Erqianshi dared to govern, and King Zhao had exclusive power.
Envoys were sent to various counties to negotiate deals with merchants and collect taxes. The revenue was more than the national tax.
Therefore, King Zhao's family had a lot of money, but all the gifts given to Ji and his disciples were spent.
Pengzu did not like to build palaces to worship ghosts and gods for blessings, but preferred to govern for officials.
Write a letter willing to supervise thieves in the country.
He often patrols Handan with his officers at night.
Many envoys and travelers did not dare to stay in Handan because of Peng Zu's evil flattery.
For a long time, Prince Liu Dan and his younger sisters had committed adultery.
Jiang Chong accused Liu Dan of promiscuity and sent people to kill and rob Liu Dan. He committed many evil deeds.
Emperor Wu sent envoys to mobilize officials and soldiers to arrest Liu Dan, and went down to the place where prisoners were imprisoned in Wei Shao to punish him with death.
Peng Zu wrote a letter to avenge Liu Dan, and was willing to attack Xiongxi together with the brave and courageous people in the country to atone for Liu Qie's sins. Zha did not agree.
After a long time, he was pardoned.
Later, Pengzu entered the court and requested through the emperor's sister, Princess Pingyang Longlu, to make Liu Dan the crown prince again, but Emperor Wu disagreed.
Peng Zu married the favored concubine of King Yi of Jiangdu, Naoji, who had been raped by Wang Liujian. He loved her very much and gave birth to a son named Naozi.
Peng Zu died in the first year of Zhenghe, and Mi Jingsu paid homage to King Su.
When Peng Zu died, Naoji's brother was a eunuch of the Han Dynasty. The emperor summoned him and asked: How is Naozi?
The answer is: He is greedy.
The emperor said: Greedy is not suitable for being a monarch to manage the people.
Wu Shi also asked how Hou Chang was doing, and he replied: He has nothing to blame and nothing to praise.
The emperor said: Just like this. So he sent envoys to establish Liu Chang as king. He was the king of Qing, and he died after reigning for nineteen years.
His son, King Huai, ascended the throne and died after reigning for five years.
Without a son, the feudal state was closed for two years.
Emperor Xuan appointed Liu Zun's younger brother Liu Gao. This was King Ai, who had died in a few months.
His son Liu Chong, the co-king, succeeded him and died after reigning for fifty-six years.
His son Liu Yin succeeded to the throne, but Wang Mang was cut off.
In the past, Emperor Wu, because of his love for his relatives, appointed Liu Yan, the youngest son of King Jingsu, as King Pinggan, making him King Qing. He reigned for eleven years until his death.
His son Liu Yuansi, King Miao, succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-five years.
Dahong Yu Yu reported: Liu Yuan used a knife to kill a slave, and his son killed someone who came to see him. He was reported by the governor and the crime was confirmed.
During the illness, an order was issued to bury the slaves who could enjoy themselves. A total of sixteen people were forced and threatened to commit suicide. They were cruel and cruel.
According to the principles of "Spring and Autumn", the son of the king who was executed should not be crowned.
Although Liu Yuan was not sentenced to death, he should not have an heir.
Permission is given. The feudal state was abolished.
Liu Sheng, Prince Jing of Zhongshan, was granted the title of king in the third year of Emperor Jing's reign.
When Emperor Wu first came to the throne, the ministers took into account the actions of the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu. Most of the people who discussed it defended Chao Cuo's strategy. They all believed that the princes, with dozens of cities in their ranks, were too powerful and wanted to gradually weaken them. They wrote several memorials to disclose their faults.
The princes and kings thought that their flesh and blood were the closest to them. The reason why the late emperor encircled the city and made them intertwined was to make the clan as strong as a rock.
Nowadays, some are innocent but are violated and humiliated by their ministers. Some officials find fault and torture their ministers to obey, forcing them to testify for their monarch. Most of the injustices are caused in this way.
In the third year of Jianyuan, King Liu Deng, King Liu Fa of Changsha, King Liu Sheng of Zhongshan, and King Liu Ming of Jichuan came to court. The emperor prepared wine. Liu Sheng heard the music and cried. When asked why, Liu Sheng replied:
summary: Liu Pengzu, the King of Zhao, was deceitful and flattering, using sophistry to frame officials and amassing wealth through trade. He died after sixty years of rule, but his son Liu Dan was executed for promiscuity and murder. Liu Sheng, the King of Zhongshan, was a drunkard with over 120 children, but he famously wept before Emperor Wu, complaining of officials’ encroachments on princes’ rights. This led to Emperor Wu’s policy of dividing princes’ lands among their sons, weakening their power. Liu Fa, the King of Changsha, was born from a concubine’s deception and ruled a poor, humid kingdom. His descendants faced scandals, including a king who burned houses and killed people. Liu Yue, the King of Guangchuan, died early, and his son Liu Qi was accused of incest and false accusations, leading to his kingdom’s temporary abolition. Liu Qu, a later king, was a scholar who studied the *Yi* and *Analects*, but he became tyrannical, torturing and killing concubines under the influence of his queen, Zhaoxin. He was deposed and committed suicide.

translation:
His son Liu Chi succeeded to the throne, but Wang Mang cut off the throne.
King Kang Xingzhou of Jiaodong was granted the title of king in the second year of Zhongyuan in Jihu, and he died after reigning for twenty-eight years.
When the King of Huainan rebelled, Xingyi heard about it secretly, secretly made chariots, bows and arrows, and prepared all the troops to guard against the rebellion.
When the officials dealt with Sui's affairs, he confessed to King Chen.
Cho Yi faced her closest relative, secretly sad, fell ill and died, not daring to have any heirs.
So I heard that Liu Ji had his eldest son Liu Xian, who was not favored by his mother, but his younger son Liu Qing was favored. Liu Ji often wanted to make him king, but it was not in the right order. Because of his mistakes, he finally had something to say.
The emperor took pity on him and made Liu Xian the King of Micellar to accept the sacrifices of King Kang. He also made Liu Qing the King of Liu'an and the king of the former Hengshan Mountain.
Wang Xian died after reigning for fifteen years, and he became King Ai.
His son Dai Wangtongping succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-four years.
His son Liu Yin, King of Qing, succeeded him and died after reigning for fifty-four years.
His son Liu, the co-king, succeeded him and died after reigning for fourteen years.
His son Liu Yin succeeded to the throne, but Wang Mang cut off the throne.
Liu Qing, the communist king of Liu'an, passed away after reigning for thirty-eight years.
His son Liu Lu, King of Yi, succeeded him and died after reigning for ten years.
His son Liu Ding, King Mu, succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-two years.
His son Liu Guang, King of Qing, succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-seven years.
The son Jianyu succeeded to the throne, but Wang Mang cut off the throne.
King Ai Xingchui of Qinghe was crowned king in the third year of Zhongyuan in Mancha, and died after reigning for twelve years.
Without a son, the feudal state was abolished.
Liu Shun, the Xianwang of Changshan, was granted the title of king in the fifth year of Emperor Jing's reign.
Liu Shun, the emperor's youngest son, was arrogant and extravagant and violated the ban several times, but the emperor often forgave him.
After reigning for thirty-two years, his son Liu Bo succeeded him as king.
Once upon a time, King Xian's unloved Ji gave birth to his eldest son Liu Shui. Liu Yue was not loved by the king because his mother was not favored.
The queen concubines the prince Liu Bo.
The king had many wives and concubines, and his beloved Ji gave birth to sons Liu Ping and Liu Shang. The queen was rarely lucky.
When King Xian was seriously ill, all his beloved concubines served the sick man. The queen was not always around due to jealousy, so she often retired to rest.
The imperial doctor brought medicine, but Prince Liu Bo did not try the medicine himself, nor did he stay overnight to treat the disease.
The queen and the prince did not arrive until the king died.
King Xian never regarded Liu Yue as his son and did not give him any property.
Lang sometimes persuaded the prince and queen to give Liu Yue's property, but they didn't listen.
The prince succeeded to the throne, but Liu Yue was not placed there.
Liu Shui resented the queen and the prince.
The Han Dynasty sent envoys to inspect the funeral of King Xian. Liu Yue said that when King Xian was ill, the queen and the prince did not serve him. When the king died, he went out of the house after six days of mourning.
The emperor sent Zhang Qian, a high official, to investigate and arrest all the witnesses. The king hid the witnesses again.
The officials requested that they be arrested, but Liu Bo sent people to beat the officials and released the suspects detained by the Han without authorization.
Some officials requested that Liu Bo and King Xian and Queen Xiu be killed.
The emperor said: "Xiu Ping has no virtue, so let Liu Yue make her fall into sin."
Liu Bo had no good teachers and could not bear to kill him.
Some officials asked him to depose him as king and move King Liu Bo and his family to live in the mausoleum, and the emperor agreed.
Liu Bo was granted the title of king for several months, but was abolished and the fiefdom was taken back.
More than a month later, because the emperor was closest to the king, he issued an edict to Yousi, saying: King Xian of Changshan died early, and later he was at odds with his concubines. His concubines and concubines made false accusations and fought with each other. They fell into injustice and reduced the country. I have great sympathy for him.
He ordered Liu Ping, the son of King Xian, to have 30,000 households and be the king of Zhending; his son Liu Shang to have 30,000 households and be the king of Surabaya.
Liu Ping, the king of Qing, died after reigning for twenty-five years.
His son, King Lie, Liu Yan, succeeded him and died after reigning for eighteen years.
His son, Xiao Wang Liu, succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-two years.
His son Liu Yong, King An, succeeded him and died after reigning for twenty-six years.
His son, King Liu Pu, succeeded him and died after reigning for fifteen years.
His son Liu Yang succeeded to the throne, but Wang Mang cut off the throne.
Liu Shang, the king of swimming, died after reigning for twelve years.
His son Ai Wang Anshi succeeded him, but he died after one year of reign and had no children.
So Emperor Wu took pity on the swimming king's heir, and appointed Liu He, An's younger brother, as King Dai.
After his death in the 22nd year of his reign, he sent his son Liu Nuan away, but the Prime Minister did not report this matter.
The Empress Dowager wrote that Emperor Zhao took pity on them and punished Xiang Neishi accordingly, and granted Liu Nuan the title of King Qin.
He died after reigning for thirty-nine years.
His son, King Liu Jun, succeeded him and died after reigning for thirty-one years.
His son Liu Jing succeeded to the throne, but Wang Mang cut off the throne.
summary: Other kings included Liu Shun of Changshan, who was arrogant but often forgiven by his father. His son Liu Bo was deposed for neglecting his father’s funeral, and the kingdom was divided among his brothers. Liu Ji of Jiaodong was cautious during the Huainan rebellion, but his sons were made kings of smaller states. The text concludes with a reflection on the dangers of luxury and power, noting that most princes became arrogant and immoral, except for the noble King Xian of Hejian.

translation:
Li Guang, a native of Shengqi, Longxi County.
His ancestor Li Zhi was a general in the Qin Dynasty and once hunted down Prince Dan of Yan State.
Li Guang's family has been learning archery for generations.
In the fourteenth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the Huns invaded Xiaoguan in large numbers. Li Guang joined the army to fight against the Huns as a son of a good family. Because he was good at archery, he killed and captured many enemies. He became a Langguan of the Han Dynasty and served as a riding attendant.
Li Guang often went hunting with Emperor Wen and killed fierce beasts, so Emperor Wen said: It's a pity that you didn't get the chance; if you were in the era of Emperor Gao, it wouldn't be a problem to be granted the title of Marquis of Ten Thousand Households!
Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne, and Li Guang was appointed Cavalry General.
When the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, Li Guang served as the commander of Xiaoqi. He followed Taiwei Zhou Yafu to attack Wu and Chu, and made outstanding achievements in Changyi City.
Because the King of Liang privately awarded General Li Guang the seal, he did not receive the reward after returning to the court.
He was transferred to the prefect of Shanggu and fought many battles with the Xiongnu.
Sun Kunxie, the Duke of Dian, said to the emperor with tears in his eyes: "Li Guang's talent is unparalleled in the world." He relied on his own ability and fought against the enemy many times, fearing that he would be sacrificed.
So he was transferred to the prefecture of Shangjun.
The Huns invaded Shangjun, and the emperor sent noble men to follow Li Guang and lead his own troops to fight against the Huns.
The noble man galloped with dozens of cavalry, met three Huns, and fought with them.
The three Huns turned around and fired arrows, wounding the noble man and killing almost all the cavalry he had brought with him.
The noble man ran to Li Guang. Li Guang said: This must be the Condor Shooter.
Li Guang then led a hundred cavalry to chase the three men.
The three men walked dozens of miles without riding horses.
Li Guang ordered his cavalry to disperse to the left and right, and Li Guang shot the three men himself, killing two and capturing one alive. It turned out to be the Huns' eagle shooter.
As soon as they tied up the man and went up the mountain, they saw thousands of Xiongnu cavalry. They saw Li Guang and thought it was the cavalry who was seducing them. They were all surprised and went up the mountain to get ready.
Li Guang's one hundred cavalry were frightened and wanted to run back quickly.
Li Guang said: We are dozens of miles away from the main army. If we run away with a hundred cavalry like this, if the Huns chase and shoot us, we will all die immediately.
Now that we stop, the Xiongnu must think that we are decoys of the army and will not dare to attack us.
Li Guang ordered: Forward!
After entering about two miles away from the Huns' position, they stopped and ordered: "Everyone, dismount and unsaddle!"
His cavalry said: There are many enemies and they are close. What if there is an emergency after unsaddled?
Li Guang said: Those enemies thought that we would escape, and now they took off their saddles to show that they would not leave. They used this method to confirm their suspicions.
So the Huns' cavalry finally did not dare to attack.
A general on a white horse came out to guard his soldiers. Li Guang mounted his horse, galloped over with more than a dozen cavalry, and shot the Xiongnu general on a white horse to death. Then he returned to his cavalry, took off the saddle, and ordered the soldiers to let go of their horses and lie down.
summary: Li Guang, a native of Longxi County, was a descendant of a Qin general and came from a family skilled in archery. He began his military career during Emperor Wen's reign, fighting the Xiongnu at Xiaoguan, where his archery skills earned him a position as a Langguan. Emperor Wen lamented that Li Guang's talents would have earned him a marquisate in the era of Emperor Gaozu. Under Emperor Jing, he served as a Cavalry General and fought in the campaign against the rebellious seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu, but was denied a reward due to accepting a seal from the King of Liang. He later served as the Prefect of Shanggu and other border commanderies, frequently battling the Xiongnu.

translation:
It was almost dusk on this beautiful day, and the Huns soldiers were always uncertain and did not dare to attack.
In the middle of the night, the Huns also thought that the Han army had an ambush nearby and would attack them at night, so the Huns all retreated.
Early the next morning, Li Guangcai returned to his main army.
Later, he successively served as the prefect of Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen and Yunzhong.
When Emperor Wu came to the throne, his ministers said that Li Guang was a famous general, so Li Guang was transferred to the Weiyang Palace Guards, while Cheng Bushi also served as the Changle Palace Guards at that time.
In the past, Cheng Bushi and Li Guang both led the army as governors of border counties and stationed fields to guard the border.
When he sent out troops to attack the Huns, Li Guang's army did not have strict organization, queues or formations. They stationed themselves near good water sources and grasslands, and stayed and stayed at their own convenience. They did not patrol or patrol at night to defend themselves. The military's documents and books were kept simple, but reconnaissance posts were also set up in the distance, so they did not encounter any danger.
Cheng Bushi strictly required the establishment, formation and formation, and patrolled at night, and the officers processed military documents until dawn, and the troops were not allowed to do what they wanted.
Cheng Bushi said: Li Guang's troops were very casual, but when the enemy suddenly attacked them, they were unable to parry them; and his soldiers were comfortable and happy, and they were all willing to die for him.
Although my troops are busy and busy, the enemy does not dare to invade us.
At that time, Li Guang and Cheng Bushi, the prefects of border counties in the Han Dynasty, were famous generals. However, the Huns were afraid of Li Guang's strategy, and the soldiers mostly liked to follow Li Guang but were reluctant to follow Cheng Bushi.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, Cheng Bushi was appointed Taizhong doctor because of his repeated outspoken advice. He is an honest man and obeys the law.
Later, the Han Dynasty used the city of Mayi to lure Chanyu. A large army was sent to ambush in the valley near Mayi. Li Guang served as the general of the cavalry and was controlled by the guard general Han Anguo.
At that time, Shanyu noticed this situation and retreated, leaving the Han army with no military exploits.
Four years later, Li Guang was transferred from a guard to a general and attacked the Huns from Yanmen County.
The Huns had more soldiers and defeated Li Guang's army and captured Li Guang alive.
Shan Yu always heard that Li Guang was talented and issued an order: If Li Guang is captured, he must be delivered alive.
The Huns cavalry captured Li Guang, who was injured at the time. They placed Li Guang between the two horses and used ropes to form a net bag for Li Guang to lie down.
After walking for more than ten miles, Li Guang pretended to be dead and squinted at a Hun boy riding a good horse next to him. Li Guang suddenly jumped up, climbed on the Hun boy's horse, held the boy in his arms and rode south for dozens of miles, and gathered the remaining troops of him.
Hundreds of Xiongnu cavalry chased him. As he ran, Li Guang picked up the bow and arrow of the Xiongnu boy and shot the chasing cavalry to death, thus escaping.
So he returned to the Han capital, and the Han court handed Li Guang over to the judge.
summary: During a campaign in Shangjun, Li Guang, with only a hundred cavalry, encountered thousands of Xiongnu. He cleverly halted his men and dismounted, convincing the enemy they were a decoy, which prevented an attack. After nightfall, the Xiongnu withdrew, suspecting an ambush. Li Guang later served as a palace guard under Emperor Wu, alongside Cheng Bushi. While Cheng Bushi's army was strictly disciplined, Li Guang's was more relaxed, yet his soldiers were loyal and willing to die for him. The Xiongnu feared Li Guang's strategies, and soldiers preferred serving under him.

translation:
The judge ruled that Li Guang had lost many men and horses and was captured alive by the enemy. He should be beheaded and use money to atone and become a civilian.
A few years later, Li Guang and Guan Qiang, the grandson of the former Yingyin Marquis who had retired to Lantian County, often went hunting in the Nanshan Mountains.
One night, I went out with a cavalryman and drank with others in the fields.
Returning to Ba Ling Pavilion, Ba Lingwei was drunk and yelled at Li Guang to stop him. Li Guang's subordinates said: This is the former General Li.
Tingwei said: The current general cannot pass at night, let alone his predecessor!
Li Guang was detained and lodged under Baling Pavilion.
Soon after, the Xiongnu invaded and killed the governor of Liaoxi and defeated General Han.
Later, General Han was transferred to Youbeiping and died.
So the emperor recruited and appointed Li Guang as the right governor of Beiping.
Li Guang then asked to send Lieutenant Ba Ling to go with him and kill him when he arrived in the army. Then he wrote a letter to apologize.
The emperor replied: Generals are the backbone of the country's defense.
The Art of War in "Sima Fa" says: There is no need to salute when boarding a chariot, and there is no need to wear mourning clothes when encountering a funeral. Reorganize and appease the army to conquer rebellion; unify the will of the three armies and stimulate the combat effectiveness of the soldiers. Therefore, showing anger can shock thousands of miles, and showing majesty can surrender. All things; therefore, the prestige is applied to the minority areas, and the power of the gods frightens the neighboring countries. He uses his anger to eradicate the harm and makes them give up cruelty and massacre. This is exactly what I want the general to do; if he takes off his hat, barefoot and kowtows to apologize, it is not my will!
The general should lead his army to consolidate the army and stabilize the frontiers to welcome the battle in the golden autumn of Youbeiping.
When Li Guang was in the border county, the Huns gave him the title of "Han Fei General", and they avoided Li Guang and did not enter the border for several years.
Li Guang went out hunting and saw a stone in the grass. He thought it was a tiger and shot an arrow. The arrow penetrated the stone. When he got closer, he saw that it was a stone. Then I tried to ejaculate again, but I couldn't ejaculate anymore.
In the county where Li Guang was located, when he heard that there was a tiger, he often went to shoot it himself.
When he was stationed in Youbei, he shot a tiger once. The tiger jumped up and wounded Li Guang. Li Guang also shot the tiger to death.
Lang Zhongling Shi Jian passed away, so the emperor recruited Li Guang to replace Shi Jian as Lang Zhongling.
In the sixth year of Yuanshuo, Li Guang was transferred to the rank of general and followed the general's army to attack the Huns from Dingxiang County.
Many of the generals were awarded the title of Marquis for their meritorious service for killing and capturing the enemy, but Li Guang's troops had no merit.
Three years later, Li Guang, as Lang Zhongling, led four thousand cavalry from Youbeiping. Bowang Hou Zhang Qian led 10,000 cavalry and went with Li Guang in two directions.
After walking for several hundred miles, King Zuoxian of the Xiongnu led 40,000 cavalry to surround Li Guang. Li Guang's soldiers were frightened, so Li Guang sent his son Li Gan to attack the enemy with a fast horse.
Li Gan galloped away with dozens of cavalry alone, passed through the encirclement of the Huns' cavalry, picked out the enemy's left and right wings, and returned, reporting to Li Guang: "The Huns are easy to deal with."
The soldiers finally settled down.
Li Guang formed a circular formation, facing the outside world. The Huns attacked them fiercely, raining down arrows.
More than half of the Han soldiers died, and the Han army was almost running out of arrows.
Li Guang ordered the soldiers to draw their bows and not to release arrows. Li Guang personally used the big yellow crossbow to shoot at the enemy's lieutenants, killing several of them, and the Huns gradually relaxed.
It happened to be dark, and the officers and soldiers were pale, but Li Guang looked as usual and commanded the army more energetically.
The soldiers in the army admired his courage.
The next day, they continued to fight hard, and Bowang Hou's army also arrived, and the Huns army finally relieved the siege.
The Han army was tired and could not pursue him.
At this time, Li Guang's army was almost wiped out and he had to withdraw his troops.
According to the laws of the Han Dynasty, Bowang Hou delayed the scheduled date and was sentenced to death. He paid for his sins and was reduced to a commoner.
Li Guang's military merit was equal to his criminal responsibility, so he was not rewarded.
At the beginning, Li Guang and his cousin Li Cai were both appointed as Langguan and served Emperor Xiaowen together.
summary: Li Guang was captured by the Xiongnu in a later campaign but escaped by feigning death, stealing a horse, and shooting his pursuers. He was sentenced to death for his losses but redeemed himself with money, becoming a commoner. He later served as the Right Governor of Beiping, where the Xiongnu avoided him for years. During a hunt, he famously shot an arrow into a stone, mistaking it for a tiger. Despite his reputation, Li Guang never received a marquisate, a fact he lamented to Wang Shuo, who attributed it to Li Guang's past deception and killing of surrendered Qiang rebels.

translation:
Li Guang personally requested: "I am a former general of the army, but now the general has asked me to send troops from the east route. Besides, I have been fighting against the Xiongnu since I was young. Today is the first time I have to fight against the Shanyu. I am willing to be the vanguard and fight the Shanyu to the death first."
General Wei Qing was secretly instructed by the emperor, thinking that Li Guang was old and had suffered many embarrassments, so he should not be allowed to confront Shanyu head-on, as he might not be able to realize his wish.
At this time, Gongsun Ao had recently lost a marquis and was serving as lieutenant general. The general also wanted Gongsun Ao to fight against Shanyu with him, so he transferred former general Li Guang.
Li Guang knew this situation at the time and resolutely refused to be transferred to the general.
The general refused to listen and ordered the chief historian to send a document to Li Guang's shogunate, saying: Go to the military headquarters where you are and do as the document says.
Li Guang set out without saying goodbye to the general. He went to the military headquarters in anger, led his soldiers and the right general to the place where they joined forces, and set off from the east road.
He lost his way and fell behind the general.
The general fought with Shanyu, but Shanyu fled and returned without any victory.
The army crossed the desert southward before meeting the former general and the right general.
After Li Guang met with the general, he returned to his army.
The general sent Chang Shi to bring wine and food to Li Guang, and asked Li Guang and Zhao Shiqi how they had lost their way, and said: "Wei Qing wants to write a letter to report the twists and turns in the emperor's army."
Li Guang didn't answer.
