General Shi ordered Li Guang's shogunate staff to write a report and go to the hearing.
Li Guang said: "The captains are not guilty. It was me who lost my way. Now I will give a confession in person and wait for interrogation."
Returning to his shogunate, Li Guang said to his subordinates: I have experienced more than seventy battles with the Xiongnu since I was young. This time I had the honor to follow the general to fight against Shanyu's direct troops. However, the general sent my troops to take a circuitous and distant road, and they lost their way again. Isn't it God's will?
Besides, I am over sixty years old, and after all, I can no longer deal with the insults of interrogators.
Then he took out his knife and killed himself.
When the people heard this, whether they knew him or not, whether they were old or young, they all shed tears for him.
The right general Zhao Shiqi was sent to the judge alone and sentenced to death. He paid for his sins and was reduced to a civilian.
Li Guang had three sons, named Li Danghu, Li Jiao, and Li Gan, all of whom served as Lang Guan.
One time the emperor was playing with Han Yan, and Han Yan was a little rude. Li Danghu hit Han Yan, and Han Yan ran away, so the emperor thought Li Danghu was brave.
Li Danghu died early, and the emperor appointed Li Jiao as the prefect of Daijun, both of whom died before Li Guang.
When Li Guang died in the army, Li Gan was following the hussar general.
In the second year after Li Guang's death, Li Cai became the prime minister. He should be punished by the judge for occupying the open space of Emperor Xiaojing's Yangling Mausoleum. The open space given to him at that time was only 20 acres, and Li Cai occupied three hectares. After selling the land, he received more than 400,000 yuan. He also occupied an acre of land outside the Shinto as a cemetery. He was sentenced to prison, so Li Cai also committed suicide.
summary: In his final campaign, Li Guang served as a former general under Wei Qing. Ordered to take a circuitous eastern route, he lost his way and failed to join the main force. After Wei Qing's interrogation, Li Guang, feeling humiliated and over sixty, committed suicide. His death caused widespread mourning. His son Li Gan later wounded Wei Qing in revenge and was killed by Huo Qubing, who claimed it was a deer attack. Li Guang's grandson Li Ling led a campaign against the Xiongnu with 5,000 infantry, fighting bravely but ultimately surrendering after running out of arrows and reinforcements. The emperor, misled by reports that Li Ling was training the Xiongnu, executed his family. Li Ling remained with the Xiongnu, marrying a Chanyu's daughter and dying there years later.

translation:
Su Wu said: Now that things have developed to this point, I will definitely be involved.
To die after being insulted would be a greater disservice to the country.
So he wanted to commit suicide, but Zhang Sheng and Chang Hui persuaded him to stop him.
As expected, Yu Chang confessed to Zhang Sheng.
Chanyu was furious and summoned the Xiongnu nobles to discuss killing the Han envoys.
Zuo Yi Zhizi said: If someone murders Shanyu, how should the punishment be increased?
It's better to let them all surrender.
Chan Yu then sent Wei Lu to summon Su Wu for interrogation. Su Wu said to Chang Hui and others: If you humiliate your integrity and the country's mission, even if you don't die, how can you have the face to return to the court?
He pulled out his sword and committed suicide.
Wei Lu was so shocked that he hugged Fu Wu personally and sent people to ride horses to find the doctor.
The doctor dug a hole in the ground, put in the fire, made Su Wu lie down on the fire pit, and tapped his back with his hand to make the blood flow out from the wound.
Su Wu fainted and took a long time to wake up.
Chang Hui and others carried him back to the camp in tears.
Chanyu admired his integrity very much, and sent people to inquire about his condition morning and night, and arrested Zhang Sheng.
Su Wu's injuries gradually improved. Shan Yu sent envoys to persuade him to surrender, and jointly tried Yu Chang, hoping to take this opportunity to force Su Wu to surrender.
After killing Yu Chang with a sword, Wei Lu said: Zhang Sheng, the envoy of the Han Dynasty, murdered the ministers close to Shanyu, and his crime should be executed. However, Shanyu recruited surrendered people and pardoned his crime.
He raised his sword to kill Zhang Sheng, but Zhang Sheng asked for surrender.
Wei Lu then said to Su Wu: The deputy envoy is guilty and you should sit with him.
Su Wu said: I didn't participate in the conspiracy, and I'm not his relative. Why should I join him?
Wei Lu gestured with his sword to stab Su Wu, but Su Wu did not waver.
Wei Lu said: Mr. Su, I, Wei Lu, betrayed the Han Dynasty and surrendered to the Xiongnu. Fortunately, thanks to the kindness of Shan Zi, I was given the title of king, so that I have tens of thousands of followers, horses and livestock all over the mountain, and I am so rich.
If you surrender today, you will do the same tomorrow.
Otherwise, you will be killed and buried in the wilderness in vain. Who knows that you died for the Han Dynasty?
Su Wu ignored it.
Wei Lu said again: If you surrender with the help of me, I will become your brother. If you don't listen to me today, will you still want to see me again in the future?
Su Wu scolded Wei Lu and said: As a subject of the Han Dynasty, you betrayed the emperor and your relatives and surrendered to the barbarians, regardless of your kindness, justice and shame. Why should I see you?
Moreover, Shanyu trusted you and asked you to judge people's life and death, but you did not act out of public interest and uphold justice. Instead, you made the two leaders fight each other and watched the chaos caused by the melee between the two sides.
South Vietnam killed the Han envoys and was razed into nine counties of the Han Dynasty; King Dayuan killed the Han envoys, and his head was hung in the north palace of the Han Palace; North Korea killed the Han envoys and was immediately punished by having his head reduced.
Only the Huns did not have this happen.
You know that I will not surrender. If you want the two countries to attack each other, the Xiongnu's defeat will begin with killing me.
Wei Lu knew that he could not threaten Su Wu to surrender in the end, so he reported the situation to Shan Yu.
The Chanyu wanted Su Wu to surrender more and more, so he imprisoned him in Dajiaoxiang and cut off food and drink from him.
It snowed heavily, so Su Wu lay down on the ground and ate snow balls and felt wool, so that many of them did not starve to death.
The Xiongnu thought he was a man of God, so they moved him to an uninhabited place in the North Sea and let him herd rams. He was not allowed to come back until the rams gave birth to babies. They separated him from his subordinates Chang Hui and others and placed him in different places.
After Su Wu was exiled to Beihai, the Huns did not provide him with food, so he had to dig grass seeds stored by wild rats to satisfy his hunger.
He used Han Chao Jie to shepherd sheep and carried Han Chao Jie with him all the time, so that the shackles on the Han Chao Jie fell off.
Five or six years later, Shan Yu's younger brother, King Yu Xuan, went to the sea to hunt. Because Su Wu knew how to make hunting nets and arrows, and calibrate bows and crossbows, King Yu Xuan liked him very much and gave him clothes and food.
More than three years later, King Yu Xuan fell ill, so he presented Su Wu with livestock, wine and cheese utensils, and felt tents.
After King Yu Xuan died, his followers also left.
That winter, Ding Ren stole Su Wu's cattle and sheep, and Su Wu was once again in trouble.
At first, Su Wu and Li Ling were serving as ministers in the Han Dynasty. In the second year after Su Wu went to the Huns as an envoy, Li Ling surrendered to the Huns and did not dare to see Su Wu.
After a long time, the Chanyu sent Li Ling to the sea to hold a banquet for Su Wu, with music and dancing. He took the opportunity to say to Su Wu: The Chanyu heard that I have a close relationship with you, so he sent me to persuade you. The Chanyu will treat you sincerely.
summary: Su Wu was sent as an envoy to the Xiongnu in 100 BCE. When a conspiracy involving his deputy Zhang Sheng was exposed, Su Wu attempted suicide to avoid disgrace. He survived and was imprisoned, surviving on snow and felt. Exiled to the North Sea to herd rams, he steadfastly refused to surrender, even when his former friend Li Ling tried to persuade him. After nineteen years, the Han Dynasty learned he was alive through a clever ruse involving a wild goose with a message. Su Wu returned to Chang'an, honored for his loyalty, though his son was later executed for conspiracy. He died in his eighties, and his portrait was later placed in the Qilin Pavilion among eleven notable ministers of Emperor Xuan's reign. The text praises Li Guang's integrity and Su Wu's unwavering loyalty, noting the tragic fate of the Li family and the exemplary virtue of Su Wu.

translation:
Du Zhou was born in Du Yan County, Nanyang County.
When Yi Zong was the governor of Nanyang County, he regarded him as his right-hand assistant, and later recommended him to Zhang Tang as the official history of the court.
He was sent to investigate the losses in border counties, and many people were convicted and executed.
The affairs of the memorial were in line with the emperor's wishes, and he was trusted. He succeeded each other with the reduction of propaganda, and served as Zhongcheng for more than ten years.
Du Zhou is taciturn and slow-tempered, but has a kind heart.
Jiaxuan served as Zuo Neishi, and Du Zhou served as Tingwei. Most of his governance followed Zhang Tang's example and he was good at observing the emperor's intentions.
If the emperor wants to exclude him, he will be framed; if the emperor wants to forgive him, he will be imprisoned for a long time, and he will secretly visit him to reveal his grievances.
Someone among the disciples reproached Du Zhou and said: You judge cases for the emperor, do not follow the established laws, and handle cases exclusively according to the monarch's will. Is this what judicial officials should be like?
Du Zhou said: How did the law come into being?
In the past, whatever the monarch thought was correct was enacted into law, and later monarchs thought it was correct and wrote it down as decree. If it suits the situation at that time, it is correct. Why use the laws of the past?
When Du Zhou served as a court lieutenant, the emperor assigned more cases.
Two thousand officials were imprisoned, old and new, and no less than a hundred people were imprisoned.
Cases from the county governor, prime minister and censor's office were all sent to the court, reaching more than a thousand cases a year.
A big case involves hundreds of arrest witnesses, and a small case involves dozens; these people are thousands of miles away and hundreds of miles away.
During the trial, the judge ordered these people to plead guilty according to the indictment. If they refused to plead guilty, they would be tortured to extract confessions and be convicted.
At that time, when people heard the news that someone was going to be arrested, they ran away or hid.
The case dragged on for a long time and went through several amnesties. It lasted for more than ten years and was still being prosecuted. Most of them were framed on charges of "injustice" or more. The prisons of various government offices in Tingwei and the capital housed 60,000 to 70,000 criminals, and the number of criminals added by ordinary officials was as high as 100,000.
Du Zhou was deposed midway, and later served as Jinwu, hunting down thieves, arresting and interrogating the sons of Sang Hongyang and Queen Wei's brothers. He was harsh and vicious. The emperor believed that he did his best and had no selfish motives, so he was promoted to the imperial censor.
Du Zhou initially served as a court official and had a horse. After he had been an official for a long time, he was promoted to the position of three princes. One of his two sons was the governor of Hanoi and the other was the governor of Henan. His family wealth accumulated to hundreds of millions.
Everyone handles cases very violently, but only Shaozi Yannian is kind-hearted.
Du Yannian, named Yougong, was also well versed in law.
Emperor Zhao ascended the throne, and General Huo Guang took power. Because Du Yannian was the son of the Three Lords, he had the talent to serve as an official to supplement the army.
summary: Du Zhou, a native of Du Yan County in Nanyang, rose from being an assistant to Governor Yi Zong to an official historian under Zhang Tang. He gained the emperor's trust by convicting and executing many during investigations of border counties, serving as Zhongcheng for over a decade. Taciturn and slow-tempered but kind-hearted, Du Zhou succeeded Xuan as Tingwei, modeling his governance after Zhang Tang and adeptly reading the emperor's intentions. He would frame those the emperor wished to exclude and prolong imprisonment for those the emperor wished to forgive, secretly revealing their grievances. When criticized for not following established laws, Du Zhou argued that laws were created by monarchs and should adapt to current circumstances. As Tingwei, he handled over a thousand cases annually, with large cases involving hundreds of witnesses. Many fled or hid upon hearing of impending arrests, and cases could drag on for over a decade through multiple amnesties. Prisons held 60,000 to 70,000 criminals, with ordinary officials adding up to 100,000. Du Zhou was later deposed but returned as Jinwu, harshly pursuing thieves and interrogating Sang Hongyang's sons and Queen Wei's brothers. Promoted to imperial censor, his family wealth accumulated to hundreds of millions. His two sons served as governors, but only his youngest, Du Yannian, was kind-hearted.

translation:
In the fourth year of the First Yuan Dynasty, barbarians invaded Yizhou. As a school captain, Yannian led the Nanyang soldiers to attack the Yizhou rebellion, returned to the army, and served as an admonishment official.
The left general Shangguan Jie and his son plotted rebellion with the Lord of Gai and the King of Yan. Yancang, the acting rice envoy, knew about the plot and reported it to Yang Chang, the chief agricultural officer.
Yang Chang was frightened and moved away because of illness, and reported to Yannian.
Yannian reported to the emperor, and Shangguan Jie and others were executed.
Yannian was granted the title of Marquis of Jianping.
Du Yannian was originally a subordinate of the general Huo Guang. He was the first to report the traitor. He had a reputation for loyalty and integrity, so he was promoted to the position of Imperial Servant Youcao to Shizhong.
Huo Guang held strict punishments and extended his life with lenient punishments.
When handling the case of King Yan, Sang Qian, the son of Sang Hongyang, the imperial censor, stayed at the home of his father's old subordinate Hou Shiwu when he escaped.
After Sang Qian was arrested, he was executed.
At the time of the amnesty, Hou Shiwu was released from prison. When Prince Tingwei and Shaofu Xu Ren tried the rebellion case, they both believed that Sang Qian was implicated in his father's rebellion, but Hou Shiwu only stayed with Sang Qian, not to hide the rebels, but to hide his followers, so Hou Shiwu was pardoned.
Later, the imperial censor inspected and found that Sang Qian was a proficient in Confucian classics. He knew that his father was plotting rebellion but did not protest, which was no different from a rebel. Hou Shiwu was originally a three hundred stone official, and he first hid from Sang Qian. He should not be treated like a commoner who hid as a follower. Hou Shiwu was not allowed to be pardoned.
The memorial is requested for a review, and those who indulge in rebels such as the imperial officers and the young government officials are impeached.
Shaofu Xu Ren was the son-in-law of Prime Minister Che Qianqiu, so Qianqiu explained to Hou Shiwu many times.
Afraid that Huo Guang would not listen, Qianqiu summoned Er Qian Shi and the Doctor to the bus door to discuss how Hou Shi Wudang should deal with it.
The discussants all knew the general's intention and insisted that Hou Shiwu was illegal.
The next day, Qianqiu reported it to the public, and Huo Guang claimed that Qianqiu was good at summoning two thousand stones to hold a meeting. There were objections both inside and outside the court, so he had Wang Ping, the imperial officer, and Xu Ren, the Shaofu, imprisoned.
The imperial court was afraid that the prime minister would be implicated.
Yannian went to court to argue with Huo Guang. He believed that officials indulged criminals and had the basis of regular laws. Now, instead of falsely accusing Hou Shiwu of being treasonous and immoral, it was probably too serious.
The prime minister has always been unruly, but always speaks kind words to his subordinates, and this is what he has always done.
As for saying that he is good at summoning two thousand stones, there is no basis for it.
Yannian was stupid and thought that the prime minister had been in office for a long time and had served under the late emperor. He should not be abandoned unless there was a major change.
Recently, people have been saying that the prison system is harsh and the prison officials are harsh and cruel. What the Prime Minister is discussing now is prison matters. If this matter also involves the Prime Minister, it may not be popular with everyone.
The crowd was in an uproar, the common people were talking among themselves, and rumors were spreading. Yannian was worried that the general would lose his reputation in the world because of this incident!
Huo Guang, based on the severity of the tactics of the Tingwei and the Shaofu, sentenced them all to death for abandoning the city, but not to the Prime Minister, nor to demotion.
This is how the discussion about prolonging life can be balanced and the court can be harmonious.
summary: Du Yannian, well-versed in law, served under Emperor Zhao with General Huo Guang in power. He led Nanyang soldiers to suppress a rebellion in Yizhou and later reported the rebellion of Shangguan Jie and others, earning the title of Marquis of Jianping. As a subordinate of Huo Guang, Yannian advocated lenient punishments. When Hou Shiwu was implicated for harboring Sang Qian, Yannian argued against harsh penalties, balancing the court's harmony. He advised Huo Guang to promote frugality and tolerance, leading to the abolition of monopolies on wine, salt, and iron. During Emperor Zhao's illness, Yannian managed prescriptions. After the emperor's death, he helped establish Emperor Xuan, gaining additional fiefs. Despite being an old member of the Huo family, Yannian was dismissed after Huo Guang's death due to legal violations but later reinstated as governor of Xihe, where he achieved peace. He served as censor during the Wufeng period but resigned due to old age and illness, dying a few months later. His son Du Xu succeeded him as marquis.

translation:
During the Wufeng period, he was transferred to the imperial court as a censor.
He lived in his father's official residence and did not dare to use his father's seat. He moved to another place to sit and lie down.
At this time, the four barbarians were harmonious and the country was at peace. He served for three years and resigned due to old age and illness. The emperor treated him favorably and sent Dr. Guanglu to give him a hundred catties of gold and wine, as well as medicine. Du Yannian was seriously ill, and the emperor gave him a chariot and horses, and he was dismissed from office.
Died a few months later. Mi was given the title Jinghou, and his son Du Xu succeeded him as Marquis.
Du Xu served as a Langguan when he was young. In this year, he followed General Pulei to attack the Xiongnu as a school captain. He also served as an admonishing official in the court, and was transferred to the captain of Shanggu and the prefect of Yanmen.
When his father passed away in Yannian, he was in charge of funerals. Afterwards, he became Taichang and managed the counties where the tombs were located. Whenever the verdict was finalized in the winter months, he often went to drink and save food. All the subordinate officials praised him for his kindness.
When Emperor Yuan first came to the throne, the price of grain was high and the people were scattered. During the Yongguang period, the Western Qiang rebelled, so Du Su sent a letter to donate money to the valley to support the army, worth millions.
Du Xu had six younger brothers, five of whom reached senior officials. The younger brother Du Xiong successively held the official position of two thousand stones in five counties and was the governor of three states. He was famous for his ability. Only the middle brother Du Qin is the most famous without being an official.
Du Qin, whose courtesy name was Wang Xia, was a young man who loved scriptures. His family was rich but he was blind, so he was not good at being an official.
Maoling Du Ye and Du Qin had the same surname, and both were famous for their talents in the capital. Therefore, the scholar-bureaucrats called Du Qin "Blind Du Zixia" to distinguish them.
However, Du Qin was afraid of being looked down upon because of his illness, so he wore a small hat and was only two inches tall and wide. Therefore, people in the capital renamed Du Qin "Little Crown Du Zixia" and Du Ye called him "Big Crown Du Zixia".
At that time, the emperor's uncle, General Wang Feng, was assisting the government by his relatives, and he was looking for someone with good moral character and knowledge to assist him.
Wang Feng's father, Wang Jin, the Marquis of Qing, was a good friend of Du Qin's brother, Du Xu. Therefore, Wang Feng knew that Du Qin was talented, so he petitioned Du Qin to be the general's military arsenal order.
Having nothing to do at work is exactly what Du Qin wants.
Du Qin was a knowledgeable and strategic man.
When the emperor was the prince, he was lustful. After he ascended the throne, the empress dowager ordered the selection of girls from good families.
Du Qin told the general Wang Feng about this matter: The emperor wants to marry nine daughters at a time, which is the limit of the number of yangs, in order to spread heirs, respect the ancestors, and promote the emperor's legacy; the nine daughters should be selected from the countryside, regardless of their beauty, just to help with virtue and manage the harem; although there is a shortage of concubines, it is not necessary to make up for them, which will help to maintain longevity and prevent competition for favor.
summary: Du Xu served as a Langguan, followed General Pulei against the Xiongnu, and later became Taichang. He was known for his kindness, often drinking and saving food during winter verdicts. During Emperor Yuan's reign, he donated money and grain to support the army. Du Xu had six younger brothers, five of whom became senior officials. His brother Du Qin, though blind, was renowned for his knowledge and strategy. Du Qin advised General Wang Feng on establishing a system of nine concubines to ensure heirs and longevity, warning against lust and its consequences. He also addressed solar eclipses and earthquakes as signs of weak yang and strong yin, urging the emperor to restrain female favors and promote frugality. His countermeasures at the White Tiger Palace emphasized filial piety, righteousness, and the importance of knowing and employing people. Du Qin later warned Wang Feng against excessive power, citing historical examples. After Wang Zhang's death, Du Qin advised Wang Feng to clarify the matter to dispel rumors. Du Qin never became an official and died of old age.

translation:
Everyone in the world looked at the wind and stood still. From the minister to the minister, all the ministers were dumbfounded, and all the relatives of the flesh and blood trembled.
Too much authority without loyalty will not stabilize the country.
Now that I heard that Fang Jin died of a sudden illness, instead of comforting the world, he was given a generous burial. I hope your majesty will think deeply about the past and warn the future.
When Emperor Cheng died and Emperor Ai ascended the throne, Du Ye wrote another letter saying: The Wang family has been in power for too long, and there are no honest and upright ministers in the court.
Prince Quyanghou was an assistant to the three princes in the past. When he knew that Zhao Zhaoyi had killed the prince, he did not report it immediately. Instead, he became friends with the Zhao family and acted arbitrarily. He framed Xu's wife and committed crimes. He killed the Xu family and destroyed the Yuan Emperor's family.
I was jealous of my mother, brother, and sister Hongyanghou Wangli and Chunyu, who all gave up when they were old.
Recently, there has been bloodshed in the capital, and the authority is formidable.
Xue Xuan, the Marquis of Gaoyang, was known as an unnurturing mother, and Zhang Yu, the Marquis of Anchang, was the leader of the traitors. They confuse the court and make the late emperor bear the name of domestic slander. We must not be careless.
When Your Majesty first came to the throne, he had no time to be humble. He was alone and independent, with no support to rely on. The changes in power officials were like testing boiling water with his hands.
We should show kindness with great righteousness as early as possible to comfort the hearts of the people.
The minister privately saw that Zhu Bo was loyal, brave, and talented, which was rarely seen in modern times. He was actually a great and treasured minister of the country. He was called upon to serve Zhu Bo and placed him on his left and right to control the world.
With this person in court, Your Majesty can sit back and relax.
In the past, when Zhu Lu wanted to harm the Liu family, it was only because Zhou Bo and Chen Ping were still there, otherwise they would have been ridiculed by the treacherous ministers.
Du Ye also said that a temple should be built in the capital for Prince Gong to show his filial piety.
At that time, Dong Hong, the Marquis of Gaochang, also said that the emperor's mother should be respected and Queen Tao Ding should be honored as the emperor's empress dowager.
Grand Sikong Shidan and others impeached Dong Hong for his wrongdoing in the government, so he was convicted and exempted from being a commoner. Du Ye wrote a letter to defend Dong Hong.
What Du Ye said before and after was in line with his purpose and was carried out, and Zhu Bo was indeed promoted and reused.
Du Ye was thus recruited and appointed as Taichang.
After more than a year, he was demoted to captain of Shangdang.
When the official reported that Du Ye's appointment as Taichang was false, Du Ye committed a crime and was dismissed from office, and returned to the feudal state.
When Emperor Ai died and Wang Mang came to power, all those who had proposed temple titles were dismissed from office and moved to Hepu.
Du Ye had been deposed before, so he treated him leniently, but due to fear, he fell ill and died.
In his early years as emperor, Du Ye married the emperor's sister, Princess Yingyi, but the princess died without any children. Du Ye's family wrote a letter requesting that the coffin be returned to the capital to be buried with the princess, but the court did not allow it. Instead, Mi was given the title of Huanghou, and his descendants passed on to his grandson Juefeng.
summary: Du Ye, Du Qin's nephew, inherited the marquis title and served as Taichang. He criticized Prime Minister Zhai Fangjin for bias and corruption, and later defended Dong Hong's proposal to honor the emperor's mother. Du Ye was demoted to captain of Shangdang and eventually dismissed from office. When Wang Mang came to power, Du Ye, fearing punishment, fell ill and died. The Du family, starting with Du Zhou and Du Yannian, were known as harsh officials but produced virtuous sons. Their lineage continued until the end of the Han Dynasty, with no one surpassing them after the great heroes and scholars.

translation:
Yang Wangsun was from the time of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
Learn the art of Huang Lao, make a fortune, pay attention to health preservation, and try to get everything that is beneficial to health.
When he was critically ill and dying, he first ordered his son in his instructions: "When I die, I will be buried naked. Let me return to the way of nature. I must not change my wishes."
After death, I put the body in a cloth bag and put it seven feet into the ground. After putting it down, I pulled the cloth bag off my feet so that my body was in direct contact with the soil.
His son wanted to silently disobey, but found it difficult to disobey his father's orders; he wanted to obey his father's wishes, but he couldn't bear it, so he went to visit his father's friend Qi Hou.
Qi Hou wrote a letter to Yang Wangsun saying: You are suffering from illness. I was eager to follow the emperor to Yong County to offer sacrifices, so I was unable to visit you at the house.
I hope you can keep your spirits up, think less about problems, seek medical treatment, and take good care of yourself.
I heard that you made an order to be buried naked after death. If the deceased is unconscious, forget it. If the deceased is conscious, you will kill the body underground and go to see the ancestors naked. I don’t think you should do this.
Moreover, the "Book of Filial Piety" says that coffins, coffins, and quilts are provided for the deceased. This is also a system passed down by the saints. Why should you insist on your own opinions alone?
I hope you will review my comments.
Yang Wangsun wrote back and said: I heard that the ancient sage kings followed human feelings and did not suppress their relatives, so they planned funerals for people. Now they go beyond the etiquette regulations and practice rich burials. Therefore, I asked for a naked burial, intending to correct the social trend of rich burials.
A grand burial is really not beneficial to the deceased, but secular people compete with each other and spend all their money to buy funeral objects, leaving these things to rot in the ground.
Or it may be buried in the ground today and exhumed tomorrow. It is really no different from the corpse wilderness!
Moreover, the so-called death is the end of life and the destination of all things.
The destination can be reached, the dead can be transformed, and creation means that objects return to their origins.
Returning the origin to the underworld, invisible and silent, is in line with reason and emotion.
Decorating the appearance to attract attention, burying it in a luxurious manner and isolating the origin, making it impossible to reach the final destination and unable to change the deceased, are causing objects to lose their place.
And I heard that the spirit belongs to heaven, and the body belongs to the earth.
The spirit leaves the body and returns to its original state, so it is called a ghost. Ghost means returning.
How can a dead body be conscious when it is as empty and alone as a clod of soil?
The corpse was wrapped in silk, and the coffin was used to isolate the soil. The limbs were wrapped and bound, and the jade was held in the mouth. He tried to melt it but couldn't, and turned into a mummy in depression. After a thousand years, the coffin rotted, and he could return to the earth and his true destination.
From this point of view, why stay as a guest for a long time?
In the past, when Yao was buried, he hollowed out wood to make a coffin and tied it with kudzu vines on the outside. The grave was dug so deep that it was not as deep as the spring water, so that the rotten gas did not leak out.
Therefore, it is easy to respect a wise king when he is alive, and easy to bury him when he is dead.
Don't spend your time on useless things, and don't waste money without a purpose.
Nowadays, money is wasted on lavish burials, preventing the deceased from returning to the earth, and isolating them from their origins. The dead do not know, and the living cannot realize their wishes of filial piety. It can be said that it is too confusing. Alas!
I won’t give him a grand burial!
summary: Yang Wangsun, a man from Emperor Wu's reign, studied Huang-Lao teachings and focused on health preservation. When terminally ill, he ordered his son to bury him naked, directly in contact with soil, to return to nature. His son consulted their friend Qi Hou, who argued against this, citing filial piety traditions requiring coffins and burial clothes. Yang Wangsun responded that lavish burials were wasteful and harmful, preventing the dead from returning to their natural state. He argued that the spirit returns to heaven and the body to earth; elaborate burials only create mummies that cannot decompose properly. He insisted on naked burial, which was ultimately carried out.

translation:
Hu Jian became famous from then on.
Later, Hu Jian became the magistrate of Weicheng County and was famous for his achievements.
When Emperor Zhao was young, the queen's father, the hussar general Shangguan An, was very close to Ding Wairen, the lover of Emperor Zhao's sister, Princess Gaichang.
Foreigner Ding was arrogant and unruly. He resented his predecessor, Jing Zhao Yin Fanfu, so he sent an assassin to shoot him.
The assassin was hiding in the building owner's villa, and the officials did not dare to catch him.
Weicheng County Magistrate Hu Jian led officers and soldiers to surround the villa to arrest the assassin.
When Gai Zhu heard about it, he and his fellow Ding, Hussar General Shangguan'an, and many slaves and soldiers came over. They ran and shot at the officials, who then fled in all directions.
Lord Gai ordered his servants to impeach Weicheng County Magistrate Hu Jian, who sent a parade to injure Lord Gai's servants.
Hu Jian wrote a letter pleading that he was not guilty.
Lord Gai was very angry and sent a letter to falsely accuse Hu Jian of violating and insulting the eldest princess, and shot an arrow at the gate of Lord Gai's mansion.
Hu Jian knew clearly that his subordinate officials had harmed the princess's domestic slave, but he avoided retribution and deliberately did not pursue the investigation.
General Huo Guang suppressed their memorial.
Later, when Huo Guang fell ill, Shangguan Jie took charge of government affairs and ordered the officials to arrest Hu Jian. Hu Jian was forced to commit suicide.
Officials and people all said that he died unjustly, and his ancestral hall is still built in Weicheng.
Zhu Yun, whose courtesy name was You, was a native of Lu and later moved to Pingling.
When he was young, he made friends with the agile and powerful knights, and used the knights to take revenge.
He is more than eight feet tall, has a majestic appearance, and is famous for his courage.
At the age of forty, he changed his moral integrity and studied "The Book of Changes" with Dr. Bai Ziyou, and also studied "The Analects of Confucius" with former general Xiao Wangzhi, and was able to pass on the "Book of Changes" and "The Analects of Confucius".
He liked to be suave and free-spirited, and people in the society valued him for this.
During the reign of Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty, Gong Yu, a native of Langye County, was appointed as the imperial censor. On behalf of Cheng Jia of Huayin County, he submitted a sealed memorial to the emperor, saying: The method of governance is to obtain talents. The censor is the deputy prime minister, ranking above the nine ministers, and must be selected.
Zhu Yun, a native of Pingling, is good at both civil and military affairs, loyal and wise. He can be allowed to try his best to serve as the imperial censor with an official rank of 600 stones.
Emperor Yuan asked the ministers for their opinions on this matter.
Prince Fu Kuangheng believed in the countermeasures: Ministers are the pillars of the country and the objects of admiration by all the people. Sage kings choose carefully.
Ancient books say that if the people despise high officials and humble people try to become powerful ministers, the country will be shaken and the people will be uneasy.
Now Jia Cong is acting as the county magistrate and is trying to become a minister. He wants a commoner to be promoted above the nine ministers. This is not an approach that values ​​the country and respects the country and the country.
summary: Hu Jian served as a military official during Emperor Wu's Tianhan period. When a military censor illegally built a shop within the army fortress for profit, Hu Jian gathered his officers, seized and executed the censor on the spot. He submitted a memorial citing military law, arguing the censor's crime warranted death and that military officers could handle such matters without civilian court involvement. The emperor approved his actions, citing the principle that military and civil laws differ. Hu Jian later became magistrate of Weicheng County. During Emperor Zhao's reign, he arrested an assassin hiding in a noble's villa, angering Princess Gaichang and General Shangguan An. After General Huo Guang fell ill, Hu Jian was forced to commit suicide, though people considered his death unjust.

translation:
From Yao's selection of Shun, to King Wen of Zhou's high appointment of Jiang Taigong, he was only entrusted with high officials and high titles after trial, not to mention people like Zhu Yun?
Zhu Yun always liked martial arts and broke the law many times to escape for his life. Although he was very good at studying "The Book of Changes", there was nothing special about his virtues and benevolence that others praised.
At present, Gong Yu, the imperial censor, is honest, proficient in classics, and has the demeanor of Boyi and Shi Yu. Everyone in the world knows it. However, Jia deliberately praised Zhu Yun and wanted him to be the censor. He praised and recommended him arbitrarily. He was afraid that he had treacherous thoughts. This kind of fraud should not be promoted. He should be interrogated and examined by the relevant officials to understand his intentions.
Jia was actually convicted of this.
At this time, Wulu, the Shaofu, was honored and favored by the clan. He studied "Liangqiu Yi".
From the time of Emperor Xuan, Emperor Yuan began to advocate Liangqiu's theory of interpretation of "Yi". Emperor Yuan loved "Liangqiu Yi" and wanted to examine the similarities and differences between "Liangqiu Yi" and other interpretations of "Yi", so he asked Wulu Chongzong to debate with other "Yi" scholars.
Wulu Chongzong relied on his high status and good eloquence. No one among the Confucian scholars could compete with him. They all said they were sick and did not dare to argue with him.
Someone recommended Zhu Yun, and Emperor Yuan called him into the palace to debate with Wulu Chongzong. Zhu Yun lifted up the hem of his long coat, climbed the steps to the hall, raised his head to ask, and his loud voice shook everyone around.
After the debate began, Zhu Yun ridiculed Wulu Chongzong one after another, so the Confucian scholars commented on their debate and said: Wulu Chongzong had horns on his head, and Zhu Yun broke his horns.
Zhu Yun therefore became a doctor.
Later, Zhu Yun was promoted to the county magistrate of Duling County. He was convicted of deliberately letting the outlaws go. When the emperor granted amnesty, he was recommended as Founder and became the magistrate of Huaili County.
At that time, Zhongshu ordered Shi Xian to have exclusive power and formed an alliance with Wulu Chongzong. All officials in the court were afraid of them.
Only Chen Xian, the censor Zhongcheng, was young and adhered to noble moral integrity. He did not rely on Shi Xian and others, but had friendship with Zhu Yun.
Zhu Yun went to court many times, saying that Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng was secure in his position and could not advance or retreat, while Chen Xian criticized Shi Xian many times.
After a long time, the relevant officials tortured Zhu Yun, suspecting that he secretly instigated the officials to kill.
When the officials met in court, Emperor Yuan asked Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng about Zhu Yun's achievements in government affairs.
Wei Xuancheng said that Zhu Yun was tyrannical and had no good governance.
Chen Xian was nearby at the time and heard what Wei Xuancheng said and told Zhu Yun.
Weiyun wrote a letter to defend himself, and Chen Xian drafted a draft memorial for him, requesting the emperor's approval to hand over the matter to Yushi Zhongcheng.
As a result, the emperor handed the matter over to the prime minister. Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng arranged for his subordinates to torture Zhu Yun and convicted Zhu Yun of murder.
Zhu Yun fled to Chang'an and approached Chen Xian to discuss countermeasures.
Prime Minister Wei Xuancheng found out all these things and reported to the emperor: Chen Xian, as a minister who stayed in the imperial palace and was in charge of laws and regulations, was fortunate enough to be able to see the emperor. However, he leaked what he heard and told Zhu Yun privately. He also drafted a draft of a memorial for Zhu Yun, hoping that the emperor would let him handle Zhu Yun's case. Later, he knew that Zhu Yun was a criminal who was on the run, but he colluded with him, so the officials could not catch Zhu Yun.
The emperor then ordered Chen Xian and Zhu Yun to be imprisoned and sentenced to death as a punishment.
Chen Xian and Zhu Yun were deposed and imprisoned until the death of Emperor Yuan.
When he became emperor, Zhang Yu, the former Prime Minister and Marquis of Anchang, was given a special position and favored by him because he was the emperor's teacher.

The words are in "Chronicles of Emperor Cheng".
At this time, Mei Fu lived at home and often took reading and self-cultivation as his job.
During the Yuanshi period, when Wang Mang was in power, Mei Fu abandoned his wife and children one morning and went to Jiujiang. It is now said that he became a god.
After that, someone saw him in Kuaiji County. He changed his name and worked as a market servant in Wu County. Yunchang, named Youru, was born in Pingling.

Zanri: In the past, Confucius said that if you can't meet a mediocre person and discuss the Tao with him, you should think about making progress and do nothing.

Kill the evildoers so that the army will not be lazy.

summary: Fan Kuai, a native of Peixian County, was a dog butcher by trade. He hid with Emperor Gaozu in the Mangshan and Cishan areas to avoid official duties. During Chen Sheng's uprising, Xiao He and Cao Shen sent Fan Kuai to retrieve Gaozu, who became Peigong. Fan Kuai served as a Sheren, attacking Huling, Fangyu, and Fengyi, defeating the Sishui County Supervisor. He pacified Peixian County and defeated the Sishui County Governor at Xuexian. He fought Sima Chao in Ci County, beheading fifteen enemies, earning the title of doctor. Fan Kuai frequently followed Peigong, leading assaults on Puyang, Chengyang, and Hufu, beheading many enemies and receiving promotions. He fought at Chengwu, Boyi, Gangli, and Kaifeng, beheading a commander and sixty-eight enemies, earning the title of minister. He defeated Yang Xiong at Quyu, ascended Wanling first, and was named Xianchengjun. He fought at Changshe, Nianyuan, and the Yellow River ferry, defeating Qin forces at Xixiang and Nianyi. He defeated Nanyang's Shouling at Yangcheng, ascended Wancheng first, and repelled enemies at Li County. At Wuguan and Bashang, he beheaded a captain and ten enemies, capturing 146 and surrendering 2,900 soldiers.

Besides, Pei Gong first entered to pacify Xianyang and camped on the top to wait for the king.

Attacking Zhao Bi, occupying Jun, Huaili, Liuzhong, and Xianyang; diverting water to irrigate waste hills, Fan Kuai made the greatest contribution.

Surrounded Xiang Yu in Chen County, defeated him and bloodbathed Hu Ling.

Emperor Gaozu added 1,300 households to Fan Kuai, and designated 5,400 households in Wuyang as Fan Kuai's food territory.
Fan Kuai followed Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty to fight, beheading 176 enemies and capturing 287 people. During the previous rebellion of Yingbu, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty was very ill and did not want to see anyone. He lived in the inner palace and ordered the guards not to let the ministers in.
No one, including ministers Jianghou and Guan Ying, dared to enter.

The emperor was lying alone with a eunuch on his pillow.
Fan Kuai and others saw the emperor weeping and said: Your Majesty led us to raise troops in Fengyi, Pei County to pacify the world. How majestic it was!

Gaozu stood up with a smile.

translation:
When they arrived in Chang'an, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had already passed away. Empress Lu released Fan Kuai and restored his title and estate to him.
In the sixth year of Xiaohui, Fan Kuai died, and Mi was named Marquis of Wu. His son Fan Kuai succeeded him as Marquis.
Fan's mother, Lu Xu, was also granted the title of Marquis of Linguang. During Queen Lu's period, she had monopolized power and the ministers were all afraid of her.
After Empress Lu died, the ministers killed Lu Xu and others, and also killed Fan and his wife. The title of Wuyang Marquis was suspended for several months.
After Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, he granted Fan Kuai's concubine Fan Shi the title of Marquis of Wuyang and restored his original title and fiefdom.
After the death of Fan Shi, Mi was named Huanghou.
His son Fan Tuoguang inherited the title.
Six years later, the family members of Hou Wuyang wrote a letter saying: Huanghou Fan was sick and infertile, so his wife had an affair with his younger brother and gave birth to Fan Tuoguang. Fan Tuoguang was not actually the son of Huanghou.
The emperor ordered that he be handed over to the officials and dismissed from the title.
In the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Ping inherited the severed title and granted Fan Zhang, the son of Fan Kuai's great-great-grandson, the title of Marquis of Wuyang, with a land of 1,000 households.
Li Shang was born in Gaoyang County.
He gathered thousands of young people during Chen Sheng's uprising.
More than six months after Pei Gong captured some areas, Li Shang led his troops in Qidi and surrendered 4,000 people to Pei Gong. He followed Pei Gong to attack Changshe. He was the first to ascend the city. Pei Gong granted him a title and named him Xinchengjun.
He also followed Pei Gong to attack Fengshi County, blocked the Yellow River ferries, and defeated the Qin army in Luoyang.
He then followed up and captured Wan and Xing, and pacified seventeen counties.

He followed the King of Han to attack Xiang Ji's army and fought a fierce battle with Zhong Limei. After winning the battle, he was awarded the Prime Minister's Seal of Liang State and added four thousand households to the city.
He followed the King of Han to attack Xiang Yu for two years, and then went to attack Hu Ling.

He Jianghou and other generals pacified Dai County and Yanmen, and captured Dai's Prime Minister Cheng Zong, Acting Prime Minister Guo Tong, and 19 people ranging from generals to 600 shi.
He returned in triumph and commanded the Imperial Guard as a general for one year.

He then followed to attack the Tingbu rebels, broke down the barriers in front of the rebels, captured two formations, and was able to annihilate the Tingbu army. So he was renamed the Marquis of Qu Zhou, and the food town was 5,100 households, and the previous food town was abolished.
To sum up his military achievements, Li Shang led his army to defeat three rebels, pacify six counties and seventy-three counties, and captured one prime minister, one acting prime minister, one general, two minor generals, and a total of 19 people with salaries ranging from less than 2,000 shi to 600 shi.

Following Gaozu, he attacked Trip Ben's army in Kaifeng, and attacked Yang Xiong's army in Quyu.

Attack Fu Yang and march to Tong, Qili and Xu in the southeast of Xiaxiang.

Attacked Xuanse and Zhese, and captured another deputy general.
He joined the King of Han in Yixiang and followed the King of Han to defeat Xiang Lan in Chen.
The soldiers he led killed two generals and captured eight generals.
summary: Guan Ying of Suiyang County was a silk merchant. He served as a follower in Zhongjuan under Peigong. He defeated Qin's Shujun at Chengwu and Gangli, becoming Seventh Doctor. He attacked Qin at Bo, Kaifeng, and Quyu, becoming Xuanling Jun. He attacked west of Yangwu to Luoyang, defeating Qin north of Xi. He followed the king east, defeated King Yin, and pacified his territory. He attacked Xiang Yu's general Long Qie and Xiang Tuo at Dingtao, defeating them. The king granted him the title of Changwen Marquis with a seat in Pingxiang. He followed the king to conquer Ci and attack Pengcheng. After Xiang Yu's victory, he garrisoned Yongqiu, defeating Wang Wu and Wei Gongshen. He captured Wai and went to Rongyang. The king appointed him as a cavalry general with Li Bi and Luo Jia. He attacked Chu cavalry at Rongyang, cutting off their food routes. He attacked Xiang Guan at Lu, killing a You Sima and a cavalry general. He defeated Duke Zhe and Wang Wu at Yan, killing five generals. He defeated Dan Ying at the imperial palace. He led cavalry across the Yellow River, escorted the king, and met the prime minister's army at Yisu. He returned to Aocang, becoming imperial censor. In the third year, he received a food town in Pingxiang. As censor, he led cavalry east, defeating rebels at Lixia, capturing Hua Wushang and 46 officials. He captured Linzi and Qi Prime Minister Tian Guang. He pursued Tian Heng to Ying and Bo, defeating his cavalry. He captured Gu and Bo, killing Tian Su at Qiancheng. He followed Han Xin to attack Longdan at Baoshi, killing Longdan and capturing Zhou Lan. After Qi was pacified, Han Xin became king of Qi, sending Guan Ying to attack Chu's Gong Dai at Lu. He defeated the Xue County governor, capturing a cavalryman. He attacked Fu Yang and marched to Tong, Qili, and Xu. He crossed the silver carp, capturing cities to Guangling. He defeated Xideng and Langsheng at Gongpi, killing Zheng Gong. He defeated Chu cavalry at Wangdang, pacified Pengcheng, capturing Xiang Tuo and Liu, Xue, Pei, Deng, Lu, and Dao. He attacked Xuanse and Zhese, capturing a deputy general. He joined the king at Yixiang, defeating Xiang Lan at Chen. His men killed two generals and captured eight. The king added 2,500 households. He pursued Xiang Ji to Shucheng, defeating him. Five of his men killed Xiang Ji, becoming marquises. He captured 12,000 enemies and all generals. He captured Shucheng and Liyang. He crossed Dansi, defeated the Chengsu county magistrate, and pacified 52 counties north of Jin Hui. After the king's ascension, he added 3,000 households. As a chariot general, he attacked Zang Tu and captured Han Xin. He received a talisman and 2,500 households in Yingyin. He attacked King Xin of Han at Daidi, capturing six counties north of Loufan, beheading the left general. He defeated Xiongnu cavalry at Wuquan. He attacked Han Zhi and Bao Chu at Jinyang, killing a general. He led troops from Yan, Zhao, Qi, Liang, and Chu to defeat Xiongnu at Bishi. Surrounded at Pingcheng, he followed the emperor to attack Chen Xi, killing Hou Chang and five generals. He attacked Quni, Lunu, Shangquyang, Anguo, and Anping. He captured Dongdanse. When Yingbu rebelled, he attacked first, defeating Yingbu's generals at Xiangdi, beheading three deputy generals. He destroyed Yingbu's Shangzhu State and Da Sima. He defeated Fei Zhu. He captured Zuo Sima, and his men killed ten young generals, pursuing to the Huaihe River. The emperor added 2,500 households. After Yingbu's defeat, the emperor granted him 5,000 households in Yingyin. He captured two generals with 2,000 stone salaries, destroyed the enemy 16 times, occupied 46 cities, and pacified one traitor, two counties, and 52 counties. He captured two generals, one Zhuguo, and one Xiang. He served Emperor Hui and Empress Lu. After Empress Lu's death, Lu Lu and others rebelled. Guan Ying was sent to attack the Qi army but stationed at Rongyang, persuading the King of Qi to focus on the Lu family. After the Lu family was punished, he supported Emperor Wen, receiving 3,000 households and 1,000 catties of gold, becoming Taiwei. In the third year of Emperor Wen, he became Prime Minister. He led 85,000 cavalry against the Xiongnu, who retreated. He died as prime minister. The title passed to his grandson Bi Qiang, who lost it for crimes. During Emperor Wu's reign, his grandson Yi Zi was made Marquis of Linru but later deposed.

translation:
When Zhengying arrived at Mingchang, he and Jihuangdong waited for the plan, stationed troops in Rongyang, and persuaded the King of Qi to focus on the execution of the Lu family, and the Qi troops stopped advancing.
After Jianghou and others punished the Lu, the King of Qi withdrew his troops and returned to the country.
Guan Ying returned from Rongyang and joined ministers Jianghou and Chen Ping to support Emperor Wen.
So Guan Ying was given three thousand households to live in, he was rewarded with a thousand catties of gold, and he was worshiped as a Taiwei.
In the third year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, Zhou Bo, the Marquis of Jiang, was dismissed as Prime Minister. Zhuo Ying became Prime Minister and no longer served as a Taiwei officer.
This year the Huns invaded the north in a large scale, and the emperor ordered Guan Ying to lead a cavalry of 85,000 people to fight against the Huns.
The Xiongnu retreated, and the King of Jibei rebelled. The emperor issued a letter to Shao and ordered Guan Ying to withdraw his entire army.
More than a year later, Guan Ying died while serving as prime minister. The whole house is filled with Mi.
The title was passed on to his grandson: Bi Qiang, because of his crime, his title was cut off.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Luo Ying's grandson Yi Zi was granted the title of Linru Marquis and was regarded as a descendant of Luo Ying. Later, he was deprived of his land for committing crimes.
Fu Kuan, as one of the five cavalry officers of Wei State, followed Pei Gong in the campaign. He appointed his troops and raised troops in Hengyang.
Following Pei Gong, he captured Anyang and Gangli, defeated Zhao Ben's army in Kaifeng, and attacked Yang Xiong's army in Quyu and Yangwu. He killed twelve enemies and was awarded the title of Duke of Pei.
Follow Pei Gong to Bashang.
Pei Gong became the king of Han and gave Fu Kuan the title of Gongdejun.
He followed the King of Han into Guanzhong and became a right-hand cavalry general.
After pacifying the Three Qin Dynasties, he was given Diaoyin as a food town.
He followed the attack on Xiang Ji and followed the King of Han in Huai County. The King of Han gave him the title of Marquis of Tongde.
He followed and attacked Xiang Guan, Zhou Lan, and Long Qie. The soldiers he led killed one of the enemy cavalry generals under Ao, and the king of Han increased his food.
Under the command of Huaiyin Hou Han Xin, he defeated Qi Zaili's army and attacked Tian Jie.
Under the command of Prime Minister Cao Shen, he destroyed Bo County and increased the number of food towns due to his merits.
Because of his meritorious service in pacifying Qi, the King of Han cut his talisman with him as proof. His title was passed down from generation to generation, and he was granted the title of Marquis of Yangling, with a settlement of 2,600 households, exempting him from the previous settlement.
He became the right prime minister of Qi and stationed in Qi.
Five years later, he became the prime minister of Qi.
In April, Chen Xi was attacked, led by Lieutenant Zhou Bo, who replaced Prime Minister Fan Yan as Prime Minister to attack Chen Xi.
In January, Xiangguo, who was moved to Dai, led the garrison.
Two years later, he was appointed Prime Minister of Dai State and commanded the garrison.
In the fifth year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign, Fu Kuan died and Mi was given the title Jinghou.
The title was passed to his great-grandson Fu Yan, who was killed for treason and the feudal state was abolished.
Zhou Jie, a native of Pei, followed Gaozu as Zhongjuan and raised troops in Wanqu.
summary: Fu Kuan, a cavalry officer of Wei, followed Peigong, raising troops in Hengyang. He captured Anyang and Gangli, defeated Zhao Ben at Kaifeng, and attacked Yang Xiong at Quyu and Yangwu, killing 12 enemies, becoming a duke. Peigong became King of Han, making him Gongdejun. He entered Guanzhong as a right-hand cavalry general. After pacifying the Three Qin Dynasties, he received Diaoyin as a food town. He attacked Xiang Ji, following the king at Huai County, becoming Marquis of Tongde. He attacked Xiang Guan, Zhou Lan, and Long Qie, killing a cavalry general. Under Han Xin, he defeated Qi Zaili and attacked Tian Jie. Under Cao Shen, he destroyed Bo County. For pacifying Qi, he received a talisman and 2,600 households in Yangling, becoming Marquis of Yangling. He became Right Prime Minister of Qi, then Prime Minister. In April, he attacked Chen Xi under Zhou Bo. In January, he became Xiangguo of Dai, commanding the garrison. Two years later, he became Prime Minister of Dai. He died in the fifth year of Xiaohui, posthumously named Jinghou. The title passed to his great-grandson Fu Yan, who was executed for treason.

translation:
Attack Jiyang.
Defeat Li You's army.
Attacked the Qin army in Shumian, Kaifeng, beheaded one of the thousand generals, killed fifty-seven enemies, captured seventy-three prisoners, and granted him the title and title of Lord Linping.
They fought again in the north of Lantian, killing two chariots and horses, one cavalry commander, twenty-eight enemies, and captured fifty-seven prisoners.
Go to Bashang. Pei Gong became the king of Han, bestowed upon him the title of nobility, the title of Marquis of Jianwu, and the rank of Captain of Cavalry.
He followed the King of Han to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, and then went west to attack Zhang Ping's army in Longxi and won.
Occupying six counties in Longxi, his men killed four chariot commanders, four horsemen, and twelve cavalry commanders.
Following the king of Han, he attacked the Chu army eastward and fought as far as Pengcheng.
The Han army was defeated and retreated, holding on to Yongqiu and defeating the rebellious Wang Wu and others.
He captured the Liang area and led an army westward to attack Xing Shuo's army in the south of Jun County. He won and personally captured two Xing Shuo captains, 12 Sima and Hou, and surrendered 4,680 enemy troops.
Yishu defeated the Chu army in Rongyang. There were 4,200 households in the enfeoffed towns.
He led his army to Hanoi alone and defeated the army of Chu Bi in Chaoge. His subordinates captured two enemy cavalry generals and 250 horses and chariots.
Following the king of Han, he attacked Anyang Yishu, fought as far as Jipu, and occupied ten counties.
He also led another army to defeat Tong's army and captured two enemy generals, Sima and four others, and 2,400 officials and soldiers surrendered.
He followed the King of Han to capture Handan, and then led his army to capture Pingyang. He personally beheaded the governor, and his subordinates beheaded an enemy governor and pacified Ye County.
He followed the King of Han to attack Chaoge and Handan, and led his own army to defeat the army of Chang, and captured six counties in Handan County.
Returning to Aocang, he defeated Xiang Ji in the south of Chenggao, cut off the Chu army's food and salary route, and blocked the area from Rongyang to Xiangyi.
Defeat a champion in Ludi.
The occupied land extended to Gao, Tan and Xiapi, and to Qixian and Zhuyi in the south.
Attack Xiang Han in Jiyang.
Returning his army to Chen, he attacked Xiang Ji's army and won. He led his army to pacify Jiangling.
summary: Zhou Jie of Pei followed Gaozu as Zhongjuan, raising troops in Wanqu. He attacked Jiyang, defeated Li You, and attacked Qin at Shumian and Kaifeng, beheading a thousand-general and 57 enemies, capturing 73, becoming Lord Linping. He fought at Lantian, killing two chariot commanders, one cavalry commander, and 28 enemies, capturing 57. At Bashang, Peigong became King of Han, making him Marquis of Jianwu and Captain of Cavalry. He pacified the Three Qin Dynasties, attacking Zhang Ping at Longxi, occupying six counties, killing four chariot commanders and four horsemen. He attacked Chu eastward to Pengcheng. After defeat, he held Yongqiu, defeating Wang Wu. He captured Liang, attacking Xing Shuo at Jun County, capturing two captains, 12 Sima, and surrendering 4,680. He defeated Chu at Rongyang, receiving 4,200 households. He led an army to Hanoi, defeating Chu Bi at Chaoge, capturing two cavalry generals and 250 chariots. He attacked Anyang to Jipu, occupying ten counties. He defeated Tong's army, capturing two generals and four Sima, surrendering 2,400. He captured Handan, leading an army to capture Pingyang, beheading a governor and pacifying Ye County. He attacked Chaoge and Handan, defeating Chang's army, capturing six counties in Handan. He returned to Aocang, defeating Xiang Ji south of Chenggao, cutting off Chu's food routes. He defeated a champion in Ludi, occupying Gao, Tan, Xiapi, Qixian, and Zhuyi. He attacked Xiang Han at Jiyang. He returned to Chen, defeating Xiang Ji's army, pacifying Jiangling.
