translation:
Emperor Xiaowu had six sons.
Queen Wei gave birth to Prince Ru, Zao Jieyu gave birth to Emperor Xiaozhao, Mrs. Wang gave birth to King Huai of Qi Liu Hong, Li Ji gave birth to King Liu Dan of Yanla, King Li of Guangling Liu Xu, and Mrs. Li gave birth to King Ai Liu of Changyi.
The ruthless prince Liu Ju was established as the crown prince in the first year of Yuanshou. He was seven years old at that time.
At the beginning, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was only 29 years old and he was the crown prince. He was very happy and built a Plum Temple for this purpose. He ordered Dongfang Shuo and Meigao to write congratulations to worship the Plum God.
When the prince grew up, he was ordered to study "Gongyang Chunqiu" and "Gu Liang Chunqiu" from Duke Xiaqiu Jiang.
When he was twenty years old, he was crowned and lived in the Tai Palace. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty built Bowang Garden for him, allowing him to interact with guests and act according to his interests. As a result, many heresies came to him as tribute.
In the fourth year of Yuanding's reign, he married Shi Liangdi and gave birth to his son Liu Jin, who was called the grandson of Emperor Shi.
In the later years of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the imperial guard fell out of favor and Jiang Chong was reused. Jiang Chong had grudges against the prince and the Wei family, and was worried that the prince would execute him after Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. At this time, a witchcraft case occurred, and Jiang Chong took advantage of this to seek personal revenge.
At that time, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was already old and tired of things. He suspected that everyone around him was guilty of curses and poisons, and issued an edict to investigate the matter severely.
Prime Minister Gongsun He and his son, the princesses of Yangshi and Zhuyi, and the Queen's brother's son Changping Houwei and his wife were all implicated and killed.
All these are recorded in "The Biography of Gongsun He" and "The Biography of Jiang Chong".
Jiang Chong was responsible for investigating the witchcraft case. He already knew the emperor's mood, so he told the emperor that there was a poisonous atmosphere in the palace. He entered the palace and went to the emperor's residence, demolished the throne and dug up the ground.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty sent Hou Hanshuo, Yushi Zhanggan, Huangmen Suwen and others to assist Jiang Chong.
Jiang Chong went to the prince's palace to dig for poisonous things and found a little figure carved from paulownia wood.
At that time, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was ill and went to Ganquan Palace to escape the summer heat. Only the queen and the prince were in the palace.
The prince summoned his young master Shi De and asked him what he should do about this matter. Shi De was afraid that he would be executed together because he was the master, so he said to the prince: Before this, the prime minister and his son, the two princesses, and the Wei family were all implicated and punished. Now the witch and the officials who came to investigate the matter dug up the ground and found the evidence. We don't know if the witch put it there intentionally, or if it was really there. We can't explain it ourselves. We can pretend to be an imperial edict and use talismans to arrest Jiang Chong and others in jail, and trace out their treacherous conspiracy.
Besides, the emperor is recuperating in Ganquan Palace, and the greetings from the queen and the prince's staff have not been answered. The emperor's life or death is unknown. And now that a traitor has done such a thing, prince, don't you remember the murder of Prince Fusu of the Qin Dynasty?
The prince was very anxious and accepted Shi De's opinion.
On Renwu day in the seventh month of the second year of Zhenghe, the prince sent a retainer to pretend to be a messenger and arrest Jiang Chong and others.
According to Dao Hou Han Shuo, he suspected that the envoy was deceitful and refused to obey the edict, so the retainers killed Han Shuo.
Yushi Zhanggan escaped after being chopped and ran back to Ganquan Palace.
The prince ordered his family to be abandoned and entered the Changqiu Gate of the Weiyang Palace overnight with the talisman. He reported it to the queen through Changyu Yihua, sent a carriage wrapped in the middle stable to load the archers, moved the weapons from the arsenal, dispatched the Changle Palace guards, declared to the civil and military officials that Jiang Chong was rebelling, and then killed Jiang Chong to patrol the government and the public, and burned the barbarian shaman to death in Shanglin Garden.
Then he deployed the guests as generals to fight against the army of Prime Minister Liu Quli and others.
There was great chaos in Chang'an City, and there were rumors that the prince was rebelling, so the people refused to join the prince.
The prince's army was defeated and he fled without being caught.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was furious, and his officials were worried and didn't know what to do.
summary: Emperor Xiaowu had six sons from various consorts. Prince Ru, born to Queen Wei, was established as crown prince at age seven in the first year of Yuanshou. Emperor Wu was delighted and built a Plum Temple, ordering Dongfang Shuo and Meigao to write congratulations. The prince studied classical texts under Duke Xiaqiu Jiang, was crowned at twenty, and resided in the Tai Palace, where Emperor Wu built Bowang Garden for him to interact with guests. In the fourth year of Yuanding, the prince married Shi Liangdi and fathered Liu Jin. In Emperor Wu's later years, Jiang Chong gained favor and held grudges against the prince and the Wei family. When witchcraft accusations arose, Jiang Chong exploited them for revenge. Emperor Wu, elderly and suspicious, ordered severe investigation. Prime Minister Gongsun He, his son, princesses, and the queen's brother's son were all implicated and killed. Jiang Chong investigated the witchcraft case, claiming poisonous air in the palace. He entered the palace, demolished the throne, and dug up ground. Assisted by others, he went to the prince's palace and found a small figure carved from paulownia wood. Emperor Wu was ill at Ganquan Palace, leaving only the queen and prince in the palace. The prince consulted his young master Shi De, who warned him about the fate of Prince Fusu of Qin and advised pretending to issue an imperial edict to arrest Jiang Chong. The prince agreed. On Renwu day in the seventh month of the second year of Zhenghe, the prince sent retainers to arrest Jiang Chong and others. One official was killed, another escaped to Ganquan Palace. The prince entered Weiyang Palace, reported to the queen, mobilized weapons and guards, declared Jiang Chong a rebel, killed him, and burned a shaman. He then deployed guests as generals against Prime Minister Liu Quli's army. Chang'an fell into chaos, and the prince's army was defeated. He fled but was not caught.

translation:
A Huguan elder named Mao wrote a letter saying: Sir, I heard that father is like the sky, mother is like the earth, and children are like all things in the world.
Therefore, if the balance of the heaven and earth is peaceful and the yin and yang are harmonious, all things can flourish and grow; if a father is kind and the mother is loving, within the family, the children will be filial.
If Yin and Yang are not in harmony, all things will be injured and die prematurely; if father and son are not in harmony, the family will be in disarray and die.
Therefore, if the father is not like the father, the son will not be like the son; if the king is not like the king, the subjects will not be like the subjects. Even if there is food, can we eat it?
In ancient times, Yu Shun was the most filial person, but he did not please his father Gusou. His filial piety was slandered, and Boqi was exiled. Although they were the closest relatives, father and son were suspicious of each other.
Why is this?
It is caused by the accumulation of more and more slander.
From this point of view, no son is unfilial, but fathers are sometimes unaware. The current crown prince is the direct heir of the Han Dynasty, inheriting the legacy of thousands of generations, and feeling the weight of the creation of his ancestors. In terms of kinship, he is your eldest son.
Jiang Chong is just a commoner, a lowly official in the countryside. Your Majesty allows him to be prominent and put him in important positions. He passes your supreme orders to persecute and embarrass the crown prince. He forges to cover up his evil deeds and deceit. He is a bunch of villains who confuse right and wrong, causing a gap between relatives and preventing them from communicating.
The prince came forward to express his gratitude but was not received by the emperor. He retreated and defended himself and was besieged by the rebellious ministers. Because he had been wronged and had nowhere to appeal, he could not bear the grief and anger, so he raised an army to kill Jiang Chong. Afterwards, he was frightened and fled out. This was just the son secretly using his father's troops to solve problems and save himself. I privately believe that the prince has no evil intentions.
"The Book of Songs" says: The black flies flying around are covered with fences; a gentle and kind-hearted gentleman should not listen to simple words; endless slanders will cause chaos and unrest in neighboring countries.
In the past, Jiang Chongjin slandered and killed the crown prince of King Zhao. Everyone in the world knew that he should have been killed.
Now, without understanding the truth, His Majesty thought that the Crown Prince had made a mistake and severely blamed him. He was so angry that he sent a large army to capture the Crown Prince. My lord, I secretly feel sad for this.
I heard that Wu Zixu lost his title for being loyal, Bigan sacrificed himself for being benevolent, and the loyal ministers were loyal and expressed their opinions regardless of the sword or ax on their necks. Their purpose was to help the king stabilize the country.
The Book of Songs says: Catch those bad guys who are slandering and throw them to the wolves, tigers and leopards. I hope your majesty will feel relieved and appreciate the relationship between father and son a little. Don't worry about the prince's mistakes, withdraw your troops quickly, and don't let the prince live in exile for a long time.
Your Majesty, I am very sincere. Once the king's order is issued, I will be punished respectfully under the Jianzhang Gate.
After reading the letter, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was moved and woke up.
summary: Emperor Wu was furious. A Huguan elder named Mao wrote a letter arguing that the prince had no evil intentions, comparing the situation to ancient examples of slander causing family discord. He urged the emperor to understand the prince's actions and withdraw troops. Emperor Wu was moved and awakened.

translation:
The prince fled eastward to Hu County and hid in a common people's house in Quanjiu.
The family was poor and often sold shoes to support the prince.
The prince had an old friend living in Hu County. Hearing that he was wealthy, he sent someone to call him, and he was discovered.
The local officials brought people to round up the prince. The prince thought that he could not escape, so he went into the house, closed the door and hanged himself.
Zhang Fuchang, a big man from Shanyang County, was a soldier. He kicked the door open. Shi Lishou, the magistrate of Xin'an County, hurriedly stepped forward to untie the prince and hug him. The owner of the house fought with the soldiers and died, and the two royal grandchildren were killed together.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was already sad about the death of the prince, but he still issued a Shao Shu saying: "The promised reward is to prove our faith."
Li Shou was granted the title of Marquis of Han, and Zhang Fuchang was granted the title of Marquis of Ti.
After a long time, most of the stories about witchcraft harming people were untrue.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty knew that the prince was just scared and ran away, and had no other intentions. In addition, Che Qianqiu once again appealed for the prince's grievances. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty promoted Che Qianqiu to the rank of prime minister, and then executed Jiang Chong's entire family.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was saddened that the prince had died innocently, so he built the Palace of Thoughts and a Tower for Returning and Watching Thoughts upon Return in Hu County.
Everyone in the world felt sad after hearing about it.
At the beginning, the prince had three sons and one daughter. The daughter was married to the son of Chengsi of Marquis Pingyu.
When the prince failed, they were all killed at the same time.
Empress Wei and Shi Liangdi were buried in the south of Chang'an City after their deaths.
His grandson, his concubine, his wife, and his granddaughter were buried in Guangmingyuan.
The two grandsons who fled with the prince were buried in Hu County with the prince.
The prince had a grandson who survived, and he was the son of Emperor Shi and Mrs. Wang. When he was eighteen years old, he inherited the throne and became Emperor Mo Xiaoxuan. As soon as Emperor Xiaoxuan came to power, he issued an edict saying: The former crown prince is buried in Hu County. There is no Mi name and a temple to hold sacrifices throughout the year. It is necessary to decide on the Mi name, build a cemetery and arrange for the households to guard the tomb.
Relevant officials petitioned and said: According to etiquette and law, if you become someone else's heir, you must be someone else's son. Therefore, your biological parents were demoted and condescended to enjoy no sacrifices. This was out of respect for their ancestors.
Your Majesty is the successor of Emperor Xiaozhao. He must inherit the great sacrifices to his ancestors and the etiquette must not go beyond the limits.
You must act respectfully and in accordance with Emperor Xiaozhao's decision: the former crown prince's mausoleum will be built in Hu County, Shi Liangdi's mausoleum will be built in the north of Bowang Garden, and the mausoleum of your father Shi Huang's grandson will be built in the north of the Guangming Garden wall.
According to the Mi method, Mi is an actual assessment of the behavior during life. I think your biological father's Mi name can be used as a mourning, and your biological mother can be mourned. After that, a cemetery will be built according to the specifications of the princes and kings, and three hundred households will be allocated with the land for worship.
The former crown prince Mi's nickname was Ru, and he was assigned 200 households to enshrine the land.
Shi Liangdi was Mrs. Ru, and she was assigned thirty families to guard the tomb.
summary: The prince fled east to Hu County, hiding in a commoner's home. The family was poor, selling shoes to support him. When discovered by local officials, the prince hanged himself. His two grandsons were also killed. Emperor Wu, saddened, later learned the witchcraft accusations were mostly untrue. He executed Jiang Chong's family, built the Palace of Thoughts and a tower in Hu County, and mourned the prince's death. The prince had three sons and one daughter, all killed when he failed. Empress Wei and Shi Liangdi were buried south of Chang'an. One grandson survived and later became Emperor Xiaoxuan. Upon ascending, he issued edicts regarding proper burial and memorial arrangements for his father, the former crown prince, establishing cemeteries and households for worship.

translation:
When Liu Dan grew up, he came to the feudal state. He was an eloquent person, studied classics and various schools of thought extensively, and was fond of astrology, calendars, mathematics, advocating leisure travel, archery and hunting, etc., and attracted knights and warriors.
When Prince Wei was defeated and King Huai of Qi died again, Liu Dan thought that he should be made the crown prince according to the ranking of his brothers, so he wrote a letter requesting to return to Beijing to stay in the palace.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty was angry and imprisoned the envoy he sent to write the letter.
Later, because of harboring fugitives, his fiefdom was cut off from Liangxiang, Anci, and Wen'an counties.
From then on, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty disliked Liu Dan, and later made his youngest son the prince.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty died, the prince succeeded to the throne and was named Emperor Xiaozhao. He issued letters stamped with jade seals to various princes and kings.
When Liu Dan received the letter, he refused to mourn. He said: The envelope containing the seal is small. I suspect there has been a change in the capital.
He sent his cronies Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi, Wang Ru and others to Chang'an to inquire about the news in the name of asking about etiquette.
Wang Ru went to see Jinwu Guo Guangyi and asked what kind of illness the emperor had when he died, who succeeded him and how old he was.
Guo Guangyi said that at that time, he was waiting for the emperor's edict in Wuzha Palace. People in the palace were clamoring that the emperor had died. The generals supported the prince as emperor. The prince was about eight or nine years old and would not leave the palace during the funeral.
Wang Ru and others came back and reported to King Yanla.
King Yanla said: "The emperor abandoned his ministers and left without saying anything. The eldest princess of Gaiyi was not seen. It's very strange."
Then he sent a senior official to Chang'an, the capital, to write a letter saying: I privately saw Emperor Xiaowu practicing the way of a sage. He was filial to his ancestors and loving to his relatives. He harmoniously united his subjects and billions of people. His benevolence united the heaven and earth. The sun and the moon shined brightly. Might permeated the world. Countries from far away offered treasures. Come to worship, add dozens of counties and counties, nearly double the territory, offer sacrifices to Mount Tai, worship Father Liang, travel around the world, and place treasures and foreign objects from far away in the Ancestral Temple. His benevolence is so majestic and grand. I request that temples be built for Emperor Xiaowu in every county.
The memorial was submitted and reported back that the emperor had read it.
At that time, the general Huo Guang was in charge of the government and rewarded King Yan with 30 million yuan and increased the number of 13,000 households in the fiefdom.
Liu Dan said angrily: I should be the emperor, how can you reward me!
So he formed a conspiracy with Liu Chang, the son of King Ai of Zhongshan, and Liu Ze, the grandson of King Xiao of Qi, and others in the clan. They lied that they had received an edict from Emperor Wu and could take charge of local administration, build military preparedness, and prepare for extraordinary incidents.
Liu Chang then issued an order to the ministers on behalf of Liu Dan: "I relied on the virtue of the late emperor to lead the northern vassal country. I personally accepted the wise edict. I have to take charge of local administration, command the arsenal and weapons, organize the military equipment. I have important responsibilities and work hard from morning to night. How will you, the officials, assist me with advice?"
Furthermore, although the Yan State was small, it was founded in the Zhou Dynasty. The first was Zhao Gongxi, and the second was King Zhao and Xiang of the Six Kingdoms period. It has been a thousand years, how can we say that there are no wise men in the Yan Kingdom?
It has been more than 30 years since I took charge of the government and listened to the government, but I haven't heard anything yet.
summary: King Huai of Qi, Liu Hong, died without son after eight years. King Liu Dan of Yanla was eloquent, studied classics, and attracted knights. After Prince Wei's defeat and Liu Hong's death, Liu Dan believed he should be crown prince. Emperor Wu became angry, imprisoned his envoy, and later cut off his fiefdom. Emperor Wu disliked Liu Dan and made his youngest son prince instead. When Emperor Wu died and the prince succeeded as Emperor Xiaozhao, Liu Dan refused to mourn, suspecting changes in the capital. He sent inquiries and later requested temples be built for Emperor Wu. General Huo Guang rewarded him, but Liu Dan angrily claimed he should be emperor. He conspired with others, claiming the young emperor was not Emperor Wu's true son. The plot was discovered, and Liu Dan's co-conspirators were executed. Later, Liu Dan's sister and others conspired with him against Huo Guang. The fourteen-year-old Emperor Zhao trusted Huo Guang and distrusted Liu Dan. The conspiracy was exposed, and Liu Dan hanged himself after receiving an imperial seal condemning his actions.

translation:
When Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, he granted Liu Xu an additional 13,000 households. When Liu Xu came to court in the Yuanfeng year, he granted another 10,000 households. He also rewarded 20 million yuan, 2,000 kilograms of gold, a special car for riding, a cart with four horses and a sword, and a sword.
When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Liu Xu's four sons Liu Sheng, Liu Zeng, Liu Bao, and Liu Chang were all granted the title of marquis, and Liu Xu's youngest son Liu Hong was also appointed as King of Gaomi.
The praises and rewards given were very generous.
When Emperor Zhao was in power, Liu Xu saw that the emperor was young and had no sons, so he coveted the throne.
Chu Di was also superstitious about ghosts, gods and witches, so Liu Xu took the witch Li Nuxu and asked her to invite the gods to the lower world to pray for disaster.
Li Nuxu cried and said: Emperor Xiaowu surrendered to my body.
Liu Xu's left and right attendants all knelt down.
Li Nuxu then said in the tone of Emperor Wu: I must make Liu Xu the emperor.
Afterwards, Liu Xu rewarded Li Nuxu with a lot of money and asked her to go to Wushan to pray.
While it was being built, Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty passed away. Liu Xu said: Li Nuxu is a witch who can really communicate with gods!
In return, a cow is killed as a sacrifice.
When King Changyi was conscripted into the capital and succeeded to the throne, Liu Xu asked witches to sacrifice to the gods in order to bring disaster.
Later, when King Changyi was deposed, Liu Xu became even more superstitious about Li Nuxu and other witches, and rewarded them with money and materials many times.
When Emperor Moxuan ascended the throne, Liu Xu asked: Why was the grandson of the former prince made emperor instead?
Let Li Nuxu pray to God for curses again as before.
In addition, Liu Xu's daughter was the younger brother-in-law of Chu King Liu Yanshou. They often exchanged gifts and exchanged private letters with each other.
Later, Liu Yanshou was executed for treason, and his confession implicated Liu Xu.
The emperor ordered Liu Xu not to be held accountable, and gave Liu Xu gold, weighing five thousand kilograms before and after, and many other utensils.
When Liu Xu heard that the imperial court had appointed a prince, he said to Ji Concubine and others: I can never be made emperor.
It also stops letting witches curse.
Later, Liu Xu's son Nanlihou Liu Shi was deprived of his title for committing murder. He returned to Guangling and committed adultery with Liu Xu's concubine Zuo Xiu.
After the incident, Liu Shi was thrown into prison and his head was beheaded in public.
Guangling Xiangshengzhi asked the court to seize Liu Xu's grassland at Sheshuibei and distribute it to the poor people, and the court agreed.
For this reason, Liu Xu asked the witch to pray to God to bring disaster to the emperor as before.
In Liu Xu's palace garden, the jujube tree sprouted more than ten new branches. The branches were straight and red in color, but the leaves of the tree were as white as plain silk.
The water in the garden turned a dull color and all the fish died.
During the day there were mice dancing in the Queen's courtyard.
Liu Xu said to Ji Concubine and others: The strange phenomena of jujube trees, pond water, fish, and rats are too abominable.
A few months later, the matter of asking God to bring disaster was exposed, and relevant officials came to investigate. Liu Xu became frightened and poisoned more than 20 witches and maids to silence him.
The ministers of the imperial court requested that Liu Xu be executed. The emperor sent Ting Wei and Da Honglu to interrogate.
Liu Xu apologized and said: I deserve to die, and there are indeed all the things I reported to you.
It's been a long time since this happened. Please go back first. I'll tell you frankly after I've thought about it.
When Liu Xu saw that the court officials had left, he set up a banquet in the Xianyang Hall and invited the prince Liu Ba and his other children Liu Dongzi and Liu Husheng to have a night of drinking. He also asked his favorite eighth lady Guo Zhaojun and his domestic singer Tzuo Jun to play the harp and sing and dance.
summary: King Li of Guangling, Liu Xu, was strong and liked entertainment. He coveted the throne when Emperor Zhao was young and childless. He employed witches to pray for his ascension. When Emperor Zhao died and King Changyi succeeded, Liu Xu had witches curse him. After King Changyi was deposed and Emperor Xuan ascended, Liu Xu continued his schemes. His treason was discovered, and he hanged himself after a final banquet.

translation:
Liu Xu himself sang: The reason why people want to live forever is because there is no end to comfort and enjoyment.
But I am never happy in this life, why should I live till the end of my life? I must abide by the time limit given to me by the emperor, and I must not live any longer. Look at the imperial envoy's thousand-mile horse, parked at the inn, waiting to go on the road.
Under the Yellow Spring, there is no bottom. People are going to die eventually. Why should we suffer and be sad about death?
What is the joy of living in this world? It lies in being able to do whatever you want. Now that I am not happy when I go out, I will just have a brief moment of happiness.
The wormwood is calling me to go, and I have seen its outline. You can't use money to hire someone to die. Go die yourself!
People on the left and right were crying and toasting each other, and the banquet didn't end until dawn.
Liu Xu said to Prince Liu Ba: The emperor treated me very well, and I feel so sorry for him now.
When I die, my body will be exposed to the public.
If you are lucky enough to be allowed to be buried, just bury it hastily and don’t give it a grand burial.
After saying this, he hanged himself with a ribbon and died.
Guo Zhaojun, the eighth aunt, and two others committed suicide.
The emperor was lenient and kind, pardoned Liu Xu's sons from the death penalty, demoted them to common people, and gave Liu Xu the honorific title of King Li.
Liu Xu was granted the title of king for sixty-four years, and was finally executed and the feudal state was abolished.
Seven years later, Emperor Mo Yuan appointed Liu Xu's crown prince, Liu Ba, as Prince Xiao, who reigned for thirteen years before his death.
Liu Ba's son Liu Yi, the co-king, succeeded him and died after reigning for three years.
Liu Yi's son, King Ai Liu Hu, succeeded him and died after reigning for sixteen years. Liu Hu had no sons and died without any heirs.
Six years later, Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty established Liu Shou, the son of Liu Ba, the filial king, and made him King Jing. He reigned for twenty years until his death.
Liu Shou's son Liu Hong succeeded him until Wang Mang usurped the Han Dynasty.
Initially, Liu Hong, the Ai King of Gaomi, was granted a title in the first year of Benshi because he was the youngest son of Liu Xu, King of Guangling. He died nine years after becoming queen.
Liu Hong's son Liu Zhang, the king of Qing, succeeded him and died after reigning for thirty-three years.
Liu Zhang's son, King Huai Liu Kuan, succeeded him and died after reigning for eleven years.
Liu Kuan's son Liu Shen succeeded to the throne and ended the Wang Mang era.
Liu Zhen, the Ai king of Changyi, was established in the fourth year of Tianhan Dynasty. He died in the eleventh year of his reign and was succeeded by his son Liu He.
Thirteen years after the establishment of the Han Dynasty, Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty died without heirs. General Huo Guang summoned the mourning king Liu He to preside over the funeral.
The seal said: The king of Changyi heard the order: Shi Lecheng, Zongzheng Liude, Guanglu doctor Bingji, and Zhonglang general Limo were sent to recruit the prince to take a seven-horse post carriage to the Chang'an mansion.
It took less than a moment and the book was published quickly overnight.
At about noon, Liu He set out from Changyi and arrived at Dingtao in the evening. After running for 135 miles, the horses ridden by his attendants died of exhaustion one after another on the road.
summary: King Ai of Changyi, Liu He, was summoned to preside over Emperor Zhao's funeral. He traveled hastily, causing horses to die. During his twenty-seven days as emperor, he behaved lewdly. General Huo Guang deposed him and returned him to his hometown. Later, Emperor Xuan granted him the title of Marquis of Haihun. After his death, his title was terminated.

translation:
A few years later, Liu He, the governor of Yangzhou, Ke La, became friends with Sun Wanshi, the former governor's soldier. Sun Wanshi asked Liu He: When he was deposed, why didn't he stay in the palace and kill the general, but instead allowed others to take the jade seal away?
Liu He said: You are right, I was wrong.
Sun Wanshi also believed that Liu He would be named King of Yuzhang and would not be a prince for a long time.
Liu He said: It's almost like this, but we shouldn't say it out loud.
Relevant officials investigated and found out the truth and asked Liu He to be arrested.
The emperor issued an order: Cut off three thousand households in the city.
Afterwards Liu He passed away.
Liao Shang, the prefect of Yuzhang, reported: Shun sealed the elephant with a trunk. After the death of the elephant, he did not establish a queen for him. He believed that a violent and confused person should not be the founder of a feudal state.
After the death of Liu He, Marquis of Haihun, it was reported to the government that his son Liu Chongguo was the heir. When Liu Chongguo died, his brother Liu Fengqin was reported to the government. Liu Fengqin also died. This was God cutting off his heirs!
Your Majesty was wise and kind, and was very kind to Liu He. Even Shun did the same to his subjects.
Liu He's title should be terminated according to etiquette to comply with the will of the Emperor of Heaven.
The request was handed over to the relevant officials for discussion.
The result of the discussion was that they should not establish heirs for the sake of plastic fall, and abolish the feudal state.
After Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he also granted Xinghe's son Liu Fese the title of Marquis of Haihun. The succession was passed on to his grandson, and he is still a marquis.
Praising: How sad the harm caused by the witchcraft case!
But this is not Jiang Chong's fault alone. It is also God's will and cannot be caused by human power.
In the sixth year of Jianyuan, the demon star Chiyou Banner appeared, and its tail grew to the horizon.
After that, the imperial court ordered generals to go out to conquer Henan and establish Shuofang County.
In the spring of that year, Prince Ru was born.
From then on, during the thirty years of the war, the army killed and destroyed countless people.
When the witchcraft case broke out, the capital Chang'an became a river of blood, with tens of thousands of corpses lying on the ground. The prince's family, father and son, were all destroyed.
Therefore, the prince was born and grew up during the military era, and was always accompanied by wars. How can it be said that it was caused by just a favored minister?
During the thirty-nine years of Qin Shihuang's reign, he flattened six kingdoms internally and defeated barbarians from all directions externally. Many people died, their bones were exposed under the Great Wall, and their heads were visible along the way. There was no day without fighting.
Therefore, the Shandong Incident occurred, and the rule of the four parties collapsed and rebelled against Qin.
The military generals and civil servants of the Qin Dynasty rebelled outside, and the treacherous official Ni Xing made trouble within the court. The chaos started within Xiao Qiang, and the disaster was caused and broke out during the reign of Hu Hai, the second generation.
Therefore, it is said: War is like setting fire. If it cannot be stopped, it will burn itself.
Indeed. Therefore, Cangjie coined the character Zhijia Ge which is the character for 武.
summary: The text concludes with a reflection on the witchcraft case's harm, noting it was not solely Jiang Chong's fault but also divine will, comparing the situation to the Qin dynasty's downfall and emphasizing that war, like fire, burns itself if not stopped.

translation:
King Li of Huainan, with a long name, was the youngest son of Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty. His mother used to be the beauty of King Zhao Zhang Ao.
In the eighth year of Emperor Gao's reign, Emperor Gao passed by the State of Zhao from Dongyuan. King Tong presented a beautiful woman to Emperor Gao. This was King Li's mother. She became pregnant after being favored.
King Zhao did not dare to let her return to the palace, so he built an outer palace for her to live in.
When the rebellion by Guangao and others was discovered and King Zhao was implicated, King Tong's mother, brothers and beauties were all arrested and imprisoned in Hanoi.
King Li's mother was also imprisoned. She told the officials: I was once favored by the emperor and had a son.
After hearing this, the officials told the emperor that the emperor was very angry with King Zhao and ignored King Li's mother.
King Li's uncle Chang Jian told Empress Lu through Piyanghou. Empress Lu was jealous and refused to defend them, and Piyanghou did not fight for him.
Queen Li's mother committed suicide out of resentment and anger after giving birth to Queen Li.
The officials sent King Li to the emperor. The emperor regretted it very much and asked Queen Lu to raise King Li, and she was buried in the county where King Li's mother lived.
In the eleventh year of the Han Dynasty, the king of Huainan, Yingbu, rebelled. The emperor personally led his troops to destroy Yingbu, so he made his son Liu Chang the king of Huainan.
King Huainan lost his mother when he was young and often relied on Empress Lu. During the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu, he was favored for this reason and had no trouble. However, he often resented Marquis Piyang in his heart, but he did not dare to show it.
In the early days of Emperor Xiaowen's accession to the throne, he thought he was the closest person to the royal family and was proud and indulgent, breaking the law several times.
The emperor forgave him.
In the third year of Emperor Wen's reign, he behaved very arrogantly when he came to court.
He followed the emperor to the royal gardens for hunting, rode in the same car with the emperor, and often called the emperor "big brother".
King Li was powerful and could lift the cauldron, so he went to pay homage to Marquis Piyang.
When Marquis Piyang came out to receive him, King Li took out the iron spine hidden in his sleeve and struck Marquis Piyang, and ordered his followers to chop off his head.
Then he drove his horse to the emperor's palace, took off his shirt, exposed his arms, and apologized to the emperor, saying: "My mother should not have committed a crime and been imprisoned for visiting the king. Marquis Piyang had the ability to persuade Empress Lu to save her, but he did not try his best to save her. This is the first crime."
King Zhao Ruyi and his mother were both innocent. Empress Lu murdered them, and Marquis Piyang did not try his best to dissuade them. This was the second crime.
Empress Lu wanted to harm our Liu family by conferring the title of king on the Lu family. Marquis Piyang did not try to dissuade her. This is the third crime.
I just killed bad guys for the people of the world and avenged my mother. I am willing to confess my sin to Your Majesty.
Emperor Wen took pity on him because he was avenging his relatives and pardoned his sin.
At that time, everyone from Queen Mother Bo to the Crown Prince and all the ministers were afraid of King Li. As a result, King Li returned to the feudal state and became more arrogant and indulgent. He did not obey the laws of the Han Dynasty. He had left and right guards and clear roads like the emperor when he came in and out. He made his own laws and showed disrespect when writing to the emperor several times.
Emperor Wen could not blame him personally.
At that time, the emperor's uncle Bo Zhao was a general. Emperor Wen respected him and ordered Bo Zhao to write to King Li, admonishing him many times:
summary: King Li of Huainan, the youngest son of Emperor Gao of Han, was born to a former beauty of King Zhao Zhang Ao. His mother became pregnant after being favored by Emperor Gao during a visit to Zhao. When King Zhao was implicated in a rebellion, she was imprisoned and revealed her pregnancy, but Emperor Gao ignored her pleas. After giving birth to King Li, she committed suicide out of resentment. Emperor Gao regretted this and had Empress Lu raise the child. In the eleventh year of his reign, Emperor Gao made Liu Chang the King of Huainan after suppressing a rebellion. King Li grew up relying on Empress Lu and was favored during the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Lu, but he resented Marquis Piyang for not saving his mother. After Emperor Xiaowen ascended, King Li became arrogant and broke laws repeatedly. In the third year of Emperor Wen's reign, he killed Marquis Piyang in revenge, claiming three crimes: failing to save his mother, not preventing Empress Lu's murder of King Zhao Ruyi, and not stopping Empress Lu from ennobling the Lu family. Emperor Wen pardoned him out of pity, but King Li grew more defiant, making his own laws and acting like an emperor.

translation:
In the sixth year, he sent Dan and other seventy men to conspire with Chai Qi, the prince of Chaiwu, the Marquis of Jipu, and sent forty military chariots back to the valley, and sent people to Minyue and Xiongnu.
After the incident was discovered, the emperor wanted to punish him, so he sent someone to summon King Huainan to Beijing.
After the King of Huainan arrived in Chang'an, Prime Minister Zhang Cang and Dianke Feng Jing acted on behalf of the imperial censor. After interrogating Zong Zheng and Ting Wei, they reported: Liu Chang abandoned the laws of the late emperor and did not obey the orders of Emperor Shao. He lived extravagantly. He made chariot and horse umbrellas that could be compared with those of the emperor. He made laws without implementing the laws of the Han Dynasty.
He appointed officials on his own, made Lang Zhongchun the prime minister, gathered the guilty fugitives among the princes and kings of the desert, made them hide and arranged residences for them, managed their families, gave them money and items, granted them titles, and gave them land and houses as salaries. Some were as high as Guannai Marquis, and were given a salary of two thousand dan.
Seventy people, including Dan, the doctor, and Kaizhang, who had lost his official title due to guilt, and Chai Qi, the prince of Jipuhou, conspired to rebel, endangering the national power of the Han Dynasty, and planned to let the Minyue and Huns send troops.
After the incident was revealed, Chang'an Wei Qi and others went to arrest Kaizhang. Liu Chang hid him instead of handing him over to the officials, and conspired with the former lieutenant Lin Ji to kill Kaizhang. They prepared a coffin and clothes for him, buried him in Feiling, deceived the officials sent by the court and said: I don't know where he is, and built a tomb for him.
In addition, Liu Chang secretly killed an innocent person; ordered officials to kill six innocent people; made those guilty who should be punished in public hide; deceived the arresting officials in order to absolve them of their crimes; and gave people without authorization Fourteen people were sentenced to death for crimes above Chengdu without reporting the crime; 18 people were pardoned for crimes that should have been punished by death; 58 people were pardoned for crimes that should have been less than Chengdu; 94 people were given titles below Guannei Marquis.
Liu Chang fell ill a few days ago. His Majesty was very worried and sent an envoy to deliver preserved dates. However, Liu Chang refused to go out to see the envoy sent by the emperor.
The common people in the Nanhai area on the border of the Lujiang River made trouble. The King of Huainan sent troops to attack the rebels. His Majesty sent an envoy to deliver fifty pieces of silk as rewards to those who worked hard among the officers and soldiers.
Liu Chang did not want to accept the reward, but said contemptuously: "There is no hard work."
Wang Zhi of Nanhai wrote a letter to the emperor asking for jade and silk, but Qu Ji burned the letter without reporting it to the emperor.
Officials asked to summon Qu Ji to Chang'an, but Liu Chang refused to let Lin Ji come, saying that "Yin Ji was ill."
The crime Liu Chang committed should be beheaded in the market, and we request that he be sentenced in accordance with the law.
The emperor issued an edict saying: I cannot bear to punish King Li, so I should discuss it with the princes and the two thousand officials.
After discussion, the princes, 2,000 officials and 43 officials and infants all agreed that the matter should be dealt with according to law.
The emperor ordered: Then pardon Liu Chang's death penalty and dethrone him from the throne.
The officials reported: I request Zaoshang to exile him to Qiongdi, Yandao County, Shu County, and order his children and their mother to live with them. The Yandao County magistrate can build a house for them, and provide firewood, vegetable salt, cooking utensils and mats for each meal.
The emperor ordered: Supply Liu Chang with food, give him five kilograms of meat and two measures of wine.
He ordered ten favored concubines of his past to live with him.
So all the people who conspired with Liu Chang were killed.
He dispatched Liu Chang and sent them heavy-loaded carriages and horses, and all the counties they passed through were equipped with carriages to transport them one by one.
Yuan Ang remonstrated with the emperor and said: The emperor has always indulged the King of Huainan and did not set up strict prime ministers and tutors, which has led to this situation today.
summary: Emperor Wen's uncle Bo Zhao admonished King Li in a letter, listing eight dangerous behaviors: abandoning his state, disobeying orders, prioritizing his mother's grave over his father's, and more. He warned that disaster would follow if King Li did not reform. King Li was displeased and ignored the advice. In the sixth year, he conspired with seventy men, including Chai Qi, to rebel, contacting Minyue and Xiongnu. The plot was discovered, and King Li was summoned to Chang'an. After interrogation, officials reported his crimes: abandoning Han laws, appointing officials without authorization, harboring fugitives, and planning rebellion. They demanded his execution, but Emperor Wen commuted the sentence to exile in Shu County.

translation:
The King of Huainan has an upright character, and now the Emperor has suddenly given him such a big blow. I am afraid that he could not withstand the fog, cold and dew and died of illness on the road. Then His Majesty has the reputation of killing his brothers. What should I do?
The emperor said: I am also troubled by this. I just let him regret himself and recalled him.
The King of Huainan asked the waiter: Who said you, me, and I are brave?
I ended up like this because I was arrogant and didn't know my fault.
So he stopped eating and starved to death.
The county escort did not dare to open the prison van.
When they arrived at Yongxian County, the magistrate of Yongxian County opened the prison car and reported to the emperor that King Huainan was dead.
When the emperor heard about it, he cried sadly and said to Yuan An: I didn't listen to you, and the result was that King Huainan died.
Yuan Ang said: The King of Huainan is already like this. There is no other way. Please be at ease, Your Majesty.
The emperor asked: What should we do?
He replied: Only by killing the prime minister and censor can we apologize to the world.
The emperor immediately ordered the prime minister and censors to arrest those who did not deliver food and food to the king of Huainan from various counties and beheaded them on the street. So the King of Huainan was buried in Yongdi according to the treatment of the princes, and thirty families were arranged to guard his tomb.
In the eighth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the emperor took pity on King Huainan. He still had four sons, all seven or eight years old, so he named his sons Liu An the Marquis of Fuling, Liu Bo the Marquis of Anyang, Liu Ci the Marquis of Yangzhou, and Liu Liang the Marquis of Shucheng.
In the twelfth year, there was a folk song about the King of Huainan, saying: A foot of cloth can be sewed; a bushel of millet can be pounded.
The two brothers are incompatible!
After hearing this, the emperor said: In the past, Yao and Shun exiled their own flesh and blood, and Zhou Gong killed Guan Shu and Cai Shu. The whole world called them saints, and they would not harm the national interests for selfish reasons.
How can people in the world think that I am coveting the land of King Huainan?
So King Chengyang was moved to the old land of Huainan to become king, and King Mi of Huainan was named King Li, and his cemetery was set up according to the etiquette of the princes.
In the 16th year, the emperor took pity on King Huainan because he abolished Han law without authorization and behaved indulgently, which caused him to lose his feudal status and died at an early age. Therefore, he moved King Liu Xi of Huainan back to Chengyang as king, and established King Li's three sons as kings in his hometown of Huainan. They are: Fuling Hou Liu An as the King of Huainan, Anyang Hou Liu Bo as the King of Hengshan, and Yangzhou Hou Liu Ci as the King of Lujiang. Liu Liang, the Marquis of Shucheng, died young and had no descendants.
In the third year of Xiaojing's reign, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled. Wu's envoys went to the King of Huainan, who wanted to send troops to meet the King of Wu.
His prime minister said: If your Majesty must raise an army with King Wu, I would like to be a general.
The king of Huainan then handed over the army to the prime minister.
After the prime minister had led the army, he held fast to the city and refused to obey the king's orders and went to the Han Dynasty.
summary: King Li refused food and died on the way. Emperor Wen mourned and executed the officials who failed to provide food. He later enfeoffed King Li's four sons as marquises. In the sixteenth year, he made three of them kings in Huainan. During the Rebellion of the Seven States, King Huainan Liu An initially considered joining Wu but was restrained by his prime minister. Liu An, known for his literary pursuits, compiled the "Inner Books" and other works. He plotted rebellion after a comet appeared, believing the emperor had no heir. His daughter Liu Ling spied in Chang'an. The plot was exposed when his grandson Liu Jian informed on him. King Huainan committed suicide, and his kingdom was abolished as Jiujiang County.
