translation:
Queen Chengshu of Hengshan King Liu Ci gave birth to three children: the eldest son Liu Shuang was the prince, the second daughter Liu Wucai, and the youngest son Liu Xiao.
The beloved concubine Xu Lai gave birth to four children, and the beautiful concubine Jue Ji gave birth to two children.
The king of Huainan and the king of Hengshan blamed each other and complained, and there were constant conflicts.
The King of Hengshan heard that the King of Huainan was preparing to use the utensils for rebellion, and secretly recruited talents to deal with them to prevent them from being annexed by him. In the sixth year of Yuanguang, King Hengshan went to the capital to pay homage. The visitor, Wei Qing, knew magic and wanted to write a letter to serve the emperor. The King of Hengshan became angry and impeached Wei Qing for committing a capital crime. He tortured Wei Qing to extract a confession and made him admit to the capital crime.
The internal historian believed that the case was untrue and withdrew.
King Hengshan sent a letter to the internal historian. When the internal historian was interrogated, he pointed out that King Hengshan was not upright and had repeatedly invaded other people's fields and used other people's cemeteries as fields.
Some officials requested that King Hengshan be arrested and punished, but the emperor did not allow it. He only deprived King Hengshan of the right to appoint officials with a salary of more than 200 shi.
The King of Hengshan was very dissatisfied and conspired with Xi Ci and Zhang Guangchang to find people who could use military astrology to plot rebellion day and night.
After Queen Chengshu died, King Hengshan made Xu Lai his queen, and Jue Ji was also favored.
Xu Lai and Jue Ji were jealous of each other. Jue Ji slandered Xu Lai in front of the prince: Xu Lai sent his slaves to kill the prince's mother using witchcraft.
The prince resented Xu Lai.
Xu Lai's brother came to Hengshan. The prince drank with him and stabbed him with a knife.
The queen hated the prince because of this and slandered the prince in front of King Hengshan.
After the prince's sister Wucai got married, her husband divorced her and she committed adultery with a guest.
The prince scolded her many times, and she was unhappy and stopped interacting with the prince.
After the queen heard about it, she won over Wucai and Liu Xiao.
Liu Xiao lost his mother when he was young and grew up with the queen. The queen doted on him because of her plans. Liu Xiao and the queen went to King Hengshan to slander the prince, and King Hengshan whipped the prince many times.
During the fourth year of Yuanshuo, someone injured the queen's stepmother. King Hengshan suspected that the prince had sent someone to do it, so he whipped him.
Later, when the King of Hengshan fell ill, the prince said that he was also ill and refused to attend to him.
Liu Xiao and Liu Wucai slandered the prince together and said: He is actually not sick. He said this himself, and he was very happy when he said it. King Hengshan was furious and wanted to depose the crown prince and install his younger brother Liu Xiao.
After the queen learned that King Hengshan was determined to depose the crown prince, she wanted him to depose Liu Xiao together.
The queen had a waiter who was good at dancing, and the King of Hengshan favored her. The queen wanted to send the waiter to have an affair with Liu Xiao, and after making Liu Xiao responsible for the crime, she also deposed the two brothers so that her son Liu Guang could replace them.
After the prince found out, he hated the queen for harming him many times and there was no end to it, so he also wanted to silence her with the crime of fornication.
The queen invited the prince to drink. When the prince came to celebrate her birthday, he hugged her thigh and asked to sleep with her.
The queen was furious and told the king of Hengshan.
The King of Hengshan summoned the prince and wanted to tie him up and whip him.
The prince knew that the king often wanted to depose him and make Liu Xiao the prince, so he told the king of Hengshan: Liu Xiao has committed adultery with the king's attendants, and Wucai has committed adultery with his slaves. Your king, please pay attention to your diet. I am going to sue the emperor.
summary: King Hengshan Liu Ci, brother of King Huainan, also plotted rebellion. He feuded with his son, Prince Liu Shuang, and favored his younger son Liu Xiao. After Queen Chengshu died, Queen Xu Lai and concubine Jue Ji slandered the prince. The prince was whipped and later accused his father of rebellion. King Hengshan committed suicide when investigated. His kingdom was also abolished. The historian comments that both kings, despite being imperial relatives, perished due to their rebellious nature and the corrupting influence of their ministers, noting that people of Jingchu have historically been prone to insurrection.
rel_path: 汉书/传/淮南衡山济北王传

translation:
In ancient times, when the emperor established a country, the princes established their families, and there were certain levels of hierarchy from officials to common people, so that the people could obey their superiors and subordinates would stop having any wrong ideas.
Confucius said: When the world is at peace, the highest political power of the country will not be in the hands of the officials.
All officials can obey the law and perform their duties, those who neglect their duties will be investigated and those who violate the law will be punished.
Only in this way can everything go smoothly and everything is in order.
With the decline of the Zhou royal family, the formulation of ritual and music conquests began to be made by the princes individually.
After Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, the officials had exclusive power and issued orders to important ministers in the court.
When the situation evolved into the Warring States Period, the princes began to join forces with each other. They abandoned propriety and justice and fought with prestige and force.
As a result, some princes from various countries, such as Lord Xinling of Wei, Lord Pingyuan of Zhao, Lord Mengchang of Qi, and Lord Chunshen of Chu, all relied on the authority of princes and nobles to compete to become knight-errants. Those who croaked, roosters, and dogs were all disrespectful and submitted to them.
The Prime Minister Yu Qing did not hesitate to leave the country and the monarch to save his friend Wei Qi from danger; Wei Wuji, the Lord of Xinling, stole the military talisman, falsely conveyed the monarch's orders, hunted down the generals, and sent out a dedicated army to relieve the Pingyuan Lord of Zhao State from being besieged by the Qin soldiers. They are all famous for their emphasis on relations between princes. Those chivalrous people who hold hands and talk are all led by the "four heroes": Lord Xinling, Lord Pingyuan, Lord Mengchang and Lord Chunshen.
As a result, the agreement to betray the imperial court and form secret alliances with best friends became a reality, and the culture of strictly observing official duties and respecting the monarch began to decline.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, bans and regulations were very loose, so the situation of deportation remained unchanged.
Therefore, the Prime Minister sent thousands of chariots with rare entourage, and King Liu Bi of Wu and King Liu An of Huainan both invited thousands of guests.
The subordinates of the foreign ministers Wei Qihou Dou Ying and Wu'an Hou Tianyi were wandering around in the capital to cause trouble. Meng and Guo Xie, who were civilians, wandered in the lanes and rampaged through the prefectures and counties, and their power overran the princes.
Many ordinary people regard their fame and deeds as a kind of honor, yearning for and admiring them.
Even though they were punished by the criminal law, they did not hesitate to kill themselves to become famous, just like Ji Lu and Qiu Mu, who died without regrets.
Therefore, Zengzi said: If those in high positions do not act according to the rules, the people will have long since abandoned their moral principles.
Without a sage king above him to instruct the good and evil in the world and formulate the country's etiquette, how can the people know the prohibitions and correct themselves!
The ancient orthodox view is that the Five Hegemons are the sinners of the Three Kings; and the Six Kingdoms are the sinners of the Five Hegemons.
From this point of view, these four tycoons should be the sinners of the Six Nations.
What's more, people like Guo Xie, in their low status as civilians, stole the power of life and death. Their crimes are already intolerable in heaven and earth.
However, on the other hand, they are gentle and friendly, helpful, humble and courteous, and they all have extraordinary charm.
It is a pity that those who do not conform to the orthodox moral standards can only be classified as the lowest class of unrefined people. It is only natural that they should be killed and exterminated!
summary: In ancient times, the emperor established a country with a clear hierarchy from officials to common people, ensuring order and obedience. Confucius noted that when the world is at peace, political power does not rest with officials, who must obey the law and face punishment for neglect or violation. However, with the decline of the Zhou royal family, princes began to control rituals and military campaigns. After Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, officials gained exclusive power, leading to the Warring States Period, where princes abandoned propriety for force. Figures like Lord Xinling, Lord Pingyuan, Lord Mengchang, and Lord Chunshen relied on noble authority to become knight-errants, attracting followers who valued personal bonds over official duties. This trend continued into the Han Dynasty, where bans were loose, and powerful figures like King Liu Bi of Wu and King Liu An of Huainan hosted thousands of guests. Commoners like Guo Xie gained influence, often resorting to violence and crime, yet were admired for their generosity and charm. Despite their crimes, they were seen as sinners against orthodox moral standards, and the emperor eventually ordered Guo Xie's execution for forming a secret faction and abusing power.

translation:
He was willing to sacrifice his life to avenge himself with blood. He also hid desperadoes and carried out robbery and theft. When he had nothing to do, he minted counterfeit money and dug graves. His misdeeds were countless.
Thanks to God's blessing, he was often relieved in times of crisis, as if he had experienced amnesty.
When Guo Xie grew up, he began to reflect on his mistakes, exercise self-discipline, respond to grudges with kindness, be willing to do good, and be pure of desire.
However, his desire to be a knight became stronger and stronger.
Although he has done some good deeds to save lives without seeking fame, his sinister nature is often shown between his eyebrows and remains the same as before.
Many young men admired his character and always took risks and hurt others for revenge, but Guo Xie himself had no way of knowing these things.
Guo Xie's sister's son relied on Guo Xie's reputation and became very domineering. Once he drank with others and made someone drink all the wine in the palace. The person couldn't bear it, so he forced the person to drink.
The man was furious, assassinated Guo Xie's sister's son and fled.
Guo Xie's sister said: You dared to kill my son while Guo Xie was still alive, but the murderer escaped. So she abandoned the son's body on the roadside without burial, hoping to anger Guo Xie with humiliation.
Guo Xie sent people to find out where the murderer was.
He was desperate, so he came over and told Guo Xie the truth.
Guo Xie said: You are right to kill him, it is my son who is shameful.
So he let the murderer go, and Guo Xie placed the blame on his sister's son, collected his body and buried it.
When everyone heard about this, they all respected Guo Xie's benevolence and righteousness, and more and more people followed him.
One time when Guo Xie went out, everyone avoided him. Only one person sat there with his legs stretched out and looked at him.
Guo Xie asked him his name, and his followers wanted to kill the man.
Guo Xie said: Someone disrespected me in the alley because my moral character was questionable. What crime did he have?
So he secretly told Wei Shi: "This man is someone I respect. Please don't use him when recruiting soldiers who are on duty."
Whenever it was time to change the duty, he went there several times, but the officials in charge did not let him change the duty.
He was very surprised and asked the reason. The official told him that it was Guo Xie who exempted him from duty.
Only those who showed disrespect to Guo Xie bared their chests and apologized to Guo Xie.
When the young people heard this, they all admired Guo Xie's character even more.
Someone in Luoyang had an enemy, and more than ten famous people and wealthy people in the city intervened, but the enemy did not listen to his advice.
Someone came to ask Guo Xie.
Guo Xie went to his enemy's house at night to see him, and the enemy finally succumbed to him.
Guo Xie said to the man: I heard that everyone in Luoyang was trying to mediate, but you didn't listen.
Now I am fortunate to have listened to my Guo Xie's advice, but how can I, Guo Xie, compete for the power of local celebrities as a foreigner!
So he returned home at night without letting anyone else know about it. He said: "It won't count this time. It will be counted when I leave and let the wealthy people from Luoyang come to mediate again."
Guo Xie was short in stature, humble and frugal. He never had a chariot accompanying him when he went out, and he did not dare to ride into the official court of the county.
When you arrive in a neighboring county, if you are asked to find something to do, if you can shirk it, you can shirk it; if you can't shirk it, you must satisfy everyone before you dare to eat and drink from others.
summary: Guo Xie, a native of Zhi County, was the grandson of a good minister. His father was a chivalrous man killed during Emperor Xiaowen's reign. Guo Xie was calm and brave but vicious in his youth, committing murder, robbery, and grave robbing. As he matured, he reflected on his mistakes, practiced self-discipline, and responded to grudges with kindness, though his sinister nature persisted. His sister's son was killed for forcing someone to drink, and Guo Xie, deeming the victim at fault, let the murderer go, earning respect. Another incident involved a man who disrespected Guo Xie; instead of retaliating, Guo Xie secretly exempted him from duty, leading to the man's apology and increased admiration for Guo Xie. In Luoyang, Guo Xie mediated a dispute where local celebrities failed, and he ensured the credit went to them. Despite his humble and frugal lifestyle, Guo Xie's influence grew, and he was eventually forced to move to Maoling due to imperial suspicion. After his move, conflicts arose, leading to murders and his eventual arrest. Although many crimes were pardoned, Guo Xie was executed for treason after a Confucian scholar was assassinated by his followers.

translation:
Everyone took this matter seriously and scrambled to use those people.
Young people from towns and wealthy people from neighboring counties came to visit Guo Xie in the middle of the night. More than ten carriages often stopped in front of his door. Most of them came to ask for Guo Xie's adoption.
When it was time to move the wealthy people to Maoling, Guo Xie was poor and his property did not meet the standards for the move. But the officials in charge were too timid to prevent him from moving.
General Wei Qing spoke for him: Guo Xie's family is poor and is not eligible for migration.
The emperor said: Guo Xie is just a commoner, but he can get the general to intercede for him. How can this be considered poverty?
Guo Xie had no choice but to move away. Before his departure, people rushed to see him off, bringing tens of thousands of items to see him off.
The son of Yang Jizhu, a native of Ga County, was appointed as an official in the county. He stopped the people who came to see him off, but the son of Guo Xie's brother actually killed the man named Yang and took his head.
After Guo Xie entered the Pass, the celebrities and wealthy guests in Guanzhong, whether they knew him or not, came to make friends with him.
The local people killed Yang Jizhu again, and Yang Jizhu's family complained and was killed in the palace.
When the emperor heard about this, he sent officials to arrest Guo Xie.
Guo Xie fled upon hearing the news and moved his mother's family to Xia Yang while he went to Linjin.
There was a man named Ji Shaoweng in Linjin who admired his name but had never seen Guo Xie, so he released him privately.
The young man released Guo Xie, and Guo Xie went to Taiyuan. Wherever he went, he often told the host of the incident.
The arrester followed the traces and found the young man, who was so anxious that he committed suicide, thus cutting off all witnesses.
After a long time, Guo Xie was finally arrested and the crimes he committed were comprehensively investigated. However, his murders all occurred before the amnesty and it was difficult to pursue them.
There was a Confucian scholar sitting with the envoy in Zhi County. Most of the people spoke well of Guo Xie, but the Confucian scholar said: Guo Xie specialized in violating public laws with treachery and robbery. How can we say he is a wise man?
Upon hearing this, Guo Xie's family members assassinated the Confucian scholar and cut off his tongue. For this reason, the officials brought Guo Xie up for questioning. Guo Xie really did not know who the murderer was, and the murderer was not identified at the time. The officials reported that Guo Xie was not guilty.
Gongsun Hong, the imperial censor, pointed out: As a commoner, Guo Xie formed a secret faction, abused his power, and killed people wantonly for trivial matters. Guo Xie himself did not know that this crime exceeded the crime of beheading that Guo Xie knew about.
It should be punished as a crime of treason.
So the emperor ordered Guo Xie's entire family to be executed.
From then on, there were many knights from various places, but there were none worth mentioning.
But Fan Zhongzi from Chang'an in Guanzhong, Wangsun Fang from Huaili, Gongzi Gao from Changling, Guo Wengzhong from Xihe, Lu Wengru from Taiyuan, Er Changqing from Linhuai, Chen Junru from Shuyang, etc., although they are knights, they all have the courtesy and humility of gentlemen.
As for the Yao family in the North Road, the Du families in the West Road, Qiu Jing in the South Road, Young Master Tuo Yu in Shu Road, Zhao Diao in Nanyang and others, they are all bandits and are mixed among the common people, so why bother!
Even people like the Zhu family would feel humiliated. Wan Zhang, courtesy name Zixia, was from Chang'an.
Chang'an is a very prosperous place, and there are many heroic people in the streets. Wan Zhang lived in Liushi, west of the city, and was known as Wan Zixia in the west of the city.
Later, he became Jing Zhaoyin's secret friend and followed Jing Zhaoyin to the palace. Among the servants, princes and nobles, they were all vying to bow to Wan Zhang, but no one went to talk to Jing Zhaoyin.
Wan Zhang was very embarrassed and frightened.
From then on, Jing Zhaoyin never asked Wan Zhang to accompany him again.
Wan Zhang was very close to Zhongshu Ling Shi Xian, and they also took advantage of Shi Xian's power, so there was always a continuous flow of cars and horses in front of his house.
In the early years of Emperor Cheng's reign, Shi Xian was dismissed from office because of the crime of taking advantage of power and moved back to his hometown.
At that time, Shi Xian's family had a fortune of tens of millions. Before leaving, he left some bed mats and utensils worth several millions and wanted to give them to Wan Zhang, but Wan Zhang did not accept them.
Some guests asked about the reason, and Wan Zhang sighed and said: I am a commoner wearing cloth, and I owe you the pity of Mr. Shi. Now that Mr. Shi has ruined his family and career, I cannot save him, but I still accept his property. Could it be that this misfortune of the Shi family, I, the Wan family, regard it as a blessing?
summary: After Guo Xie, many knights emerged but none were notable. Figures like Fan Zhongzi, Wangsun Fang, and others were courteous and humble, while others like the Yao and Du families were bandits. Wan Zhang, a knight from Chang'an, became a secret friend of Jing Zhaoyin but was embarrassed by the attention he received. He later refused gifts from the disgraced Shi Xian, earning praise for his conduct. During the Heping period, Wang Zun captured and killed many heroes, including Wan Zhang. Lou Hu, from Qi State, initially practiced medicine but later studied classics and became a minor official. He gained fame by serving the five Wang brothers simultaneously, known for his eloquence and integrity. After his mother's death, thousands mourned. Lou Hu later served as an envoy, distributing gifts to relatives, and was promoted to prefect of Tianshui. He was dismissed but later reinstated, and during Wang Mang's regency, he captured a fugitive, earning a marquisate. However, he was eventually dismissed again and lived in obscurity, though he maintained his principles by supporting an old friend, Lu Gong, for life.

translation:
Chen Sui then resigned and thanked Emperor Xuan, saying: "These things all happened before the pardon was issued in the first year of Yuanping, and they should not be investigated any further."
He was treated so favorably by Emperor Xuan.
During the reign of Emperor Yuan, Chen Sui was recruited to serve as Jing Zhaoyin, and later he became Tingwei.
Chen Zun lost his father in his early years, and later became a Jingzhao historian with a man named Zhang Changhao Bosong.
Zhang Song was knowledgeable, knowledgeable, and self-disciplined with integrity and frugality, while Chen Zun was indulgent and unruly. Although the two had different moral conduct, they were very close and friendly to each other. In the last years of Emperor Ai's reign, they were both well-known and became the best among the underachievers.
They both entered the palace again. All the officials in the palace only had thin horses and poor carriages, and never paid attention to their appearance. Only Chen Zun showed off his carriages and horses in gorgeous clothes. Outside his door, there were always carriages and horses meeting each other, which was very grand.
Every day when he went out to drink, he would always come home drunk, often neglecting to deal with official matters.
Xicao punished him according to the old rules. The clerk who served him always went to the official residence to inform Chen Zun: "Chen Qing was punished for something again today."
Chen Zun said: "When it reaches one hundred items, come back and let me know."
According to the old rules, those who were punished a hundred times would be dismissed. Later, when the number of punishments reached 100, west Cao asked the officials to dismiss Chen Zun.
At that time, Grand Situ Ma Gong was a man of great magnanimity. He was tolerant of scholars and valued Chen Zun very much, so he said to Xicao: "This man is a very talented scholar. How can you scold him with small rules?"
He recommended Chen Zun, saying that he could manage the difficult and difficult counties in Sanfu, so he made him the magistrate of Yuyi County.
After a long time, due to disagreements with Fufeng, he resigned and left.
The big thieves Tampeng and Huo Hong in Huaili started a rebellion. Chen Zunzheng was appointed as the school captain. He made great achievements in attacking Tampeng, Huo Hong and others, so he was named Jiaweihou.
He lived in Chang'an City, and all the princes, ministers, and nobles valued him.
All the county officials and heroes who came to the capital came to visit Chen Zun.
Chen Zun liked drinking. Whenever he held a big banquet, when the hall was full of guests, he would often close the door and throw the keys from the guests' cars into the well. Even if there was an emergency, he could not go out.
Once, a provincial governor came to visit Chen Zun on business, and he happened to be drinking heavily. The governor was very embarrassed. When Chen Zun was drunk, he suddenly went in to see Chen Zun's mother, kowtowed to her and told her that he had an appointment with the minister and had business to discuss. Chen Zun's mother asked him to go out through the back door.
Chen Zun probably got drunk from time to time, but his official duties were not delayed.
Chen Zun is more than eight feet tall, has a long head and a big nose, and has a dignified appearance.
After skimming some biographies, I can write prose.
He was fond of writing by nature, and the letters he wrote to others were all treasured by them as an honor.
No one dared to refuse him every request. Wherever he went, the entire upper class envied him for fear of neglecting him.
At this time, there was a man with the same surname as Chen Zun. Whenever he visited someone else's door, he would shout, "Chen Menggong is here."
Wang Mang had always been amazed by Chen Zun's talents, and most of the officials in office praised him, so he made him the governor of Henan County.
Now that Chen Zun had arrived, he sent an envoy to the west and recruited ten clerks who could write letters to write private letters for him to thank his old friends in the capital.
Chen Zun leaned on the coffee table, dictating his thoughts to the clerk, and also reviewing official matters. He soon wrote hundreds of letters. The contents and meanings of the close and distant letters were also different. The people in Henan County were greatly frightened by this.
After a few months, he was dismissed from office.
When Chen Zun was appointed as the governor of Henan County, his younger brother Chen Ji was appointed as the pastor of Jingzhou. On his way to take office, the two brothers passed by the home of a rich man in Chang'an. This rich man was the Zuo family of the late King of Huaiyang. They drank and had fun at his home.
Later, a Sizhi named Chen Chong heard about this and reported to the court: Brother Chen Zun was lucky enough to receive divine grace, transcended his rank, and held successive official positions. Chen Zun's title has reached the rank of lord, his official position has reached the level of county guard, and Chen's rank has also been promoted to prefecture pastor. When ordered to go on missions, they should be responsible for upholding integrity, monitoring evil songs, and promoting the teachings of the Holy King. However, they are not self-cultivation and self-discipline now, and they only do unseemly things.
When Chen Zun first became an official, he actually rode a covered car into Yan Alley and went to the widow Zuo Ajun's house to serve wine and sing. Chen Zun got up and danced wildly, but actually lost his footing and fell down on his seat. He stayed at the widow's house at night and was supported by the maid before going to bed.
Chen Zun knew clearly that etiquette should be followed during drinking and banquets, and according to etiquette, he was not allowed to enter the widow's house, but he still indulged in eating and enjoying, did not care about the different etiquette rules for men and women, insulted the title given by the court, and brought shame to the official seal. This kind of bad reputation cannot be tolerated.
Therefore, it is requested that both of them be removed from office.
After Chen Zun was dismissed from office, he returned to Chang'an. There were more and more guests, and the food and entertainment remained the same as before.
After a long time, Chen Zun served as the captain of Jiujiang and Hanoi. In total, he served as an official three times with a salary of two thousand dan.
Zhang Song also became the governor of Danyang and was given the title of Marquis of Shude.
Later, they were all dismissed from their official positions, and returned to Chang'an with only the titles of princes.
Zhang Song's residence was very simple, with no guests coming and going. There were often good people following him to criticize and ask questions, and they just talked about the Tao Te Ching.
But Chen Zun was shouting day and night, the house was full of chariots and cavalry, and there were continuous banquets and meat feasts.
Previously, Huangmenlang Yangxiong wrote "Wine Admonition" to satirize and admonish the emperor. In the article, he assumed that a drunkard criticized the righteous Dharma minister and used objects as a metaphor for people. The article wrote: You are like a bottle.
summary: Chen Zun, from Duling County, was known for his indulgence and extravagance, contrasting with his friend Zhang Song's frugality. Despite his reckless behavior, Chen Zun was valued for his talent and became a magistrate. He was later dismissed for misconduct but continued to host lavish parties. During Wang Mang's reign, he served as governor of Henan County but was dismissed again. Chen Zun was known for his eloquence and charm, and his letters were treasured. He died in Shuofang after being captured by bandits. Yuan She, from Maoling, gained fame by returning funeral donations and mourning his father for three years. He became a magistrate but was dismissed after seeking revenge for his uncle's murder. Yuan She was known for his generosity and ability to mobilize people, often helping the poor and organizing funerals. However, he was also involved in violence, killing a man who slandered him. During Wang Mang's reign, Yuan She was appointed as an official but was eventually executed after ordering the assassination of a chief registrar. Since the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, many heroes emerged in various counties, but their numbers were too many to count.

translation:
Yuan Ang, Zisi.
His father was a native of Chu. He once worked as a thief and later moved to Anling.
During the period of Empress Lu, Yuan Ang once served as Lu Lu's retainer.
When Emperor Wen of Han came to the throne, Yuan An's brother Yuan Sha recommended Yuan An to be a doctor.
Jianghou Zhou Bo became the prime minister. After retiring from the court, he walked out quickly, feeling very contented.
The emperor treated him with great courtesy and often saw him off with his eyes.
Yuan Ang stepped forward and said, "What kind of person is the Prime Minister?"
The emperor said: An important minister of the country.
Yuan An said: Jianghou is what is usually called a hero, not an important minister of the country.
The important ministers of the country are the master and the minister, and the master will die and the minister will perish.
During the period of Empress Lu, Zhu Lu was in power and granted the title of king without authorization. Although the Liu family's world was not cut off, it was as weak and weak as a belt.
At that time, Jianghou was serving as the Taiwei and had military power, so he could not help or save him.
After Empress Lu died, the ministers worked together to punish Lu. The Taiwei controlled the army, which happened to make him successful. He was a hero in general, not an important official of the country.
If the prime minister shows pride towards his lord, and your majesty humbly gives in, it would be a violation of etiquette for both the minister and the lord. I think your majesty should not adopt this attitude.
After the court meeting, the emperor gradually became more solemn and the prime minister became more and more fearful.
Afterwards, Jianghou scolded Yuan Ang and said: I am close to your brother, but now you are slandering me in the court!
Yuan An never admitted his mistake.
When Jianghou was dismissed as prime minister and returned to the feudal state, someone in the feudal state wrote a letter accusing him of treason. Jianghou was arrested, tied up and imprisoned. The royal family and other ministers did not dare to speak for him. Only Yuan An defended Jianghou's innocence.
Jianghou was able to be released, and Yuan An made great efforts.
Jianghou then became close friends with Yuan Ang.
Liu Chang, the king of Huainan, went to the capital to see him and killed Piyanghou. He behaved very arrogantly.
Yuan An advised the emperor: If the princes are too arrogant, chaos will inevitably occur, and their fiefdoms can be appropriately reduced.
The emperor did not adopt his opinion.
The king of Huainan became even more arrogant.
The plot to rebel was discovered, and King Huainan was summoned. The emperor exiled him to Shu County and escorted him in a prison car.
Yuan An was serving as Zhonglang General at that time, so he remonstrated and said: You have always been arrogant and indulgent to the King of Huainan without imposing any restrictions, even to this extent. Now it suddenly destroyed him.
The King of Huainan is a staunch man. If you die from the cold on the road, you will eventually be considered as the incompatible people in the world and will have the reputation of killing your brother. What should you do?
Zaoshang didn't listen and did it anyway.
The king of Huainan arrived in Yong County and died of illness. The news came that the emperor could not eat and cried very sadly.
Yuan An entered and kowtowed to apologize.
The emperor said: This situation occurred because your opinions were not adopted.
Yuan An said: If the emperor wants to think about it himself, this matter has already passed, how can he regret it?
Besides, you have three outstanding behaviors, which are not enough to ruin your reputation.
summary: Yuan Ang, also known as Zisi, was a native of Chu who later moved to Anling. He served as a retainer to Lü Lu during Empress Lü's reign and was recommended as a doctor by his brother Yuan Sha under Emperor Wen of Han. Yuan Ang famously criticized Prime Minister Zhou Bo, calling him a "hero" rather than an "important minister," arguing that Zhou Bo had failed to act against the Lü clan during their usurpation and only succeeded after Empress Lü's death. Despite Zhou Bo's initial anger, Yuan Ang later defended him when Zhou Bo was falsely accused of treason, leading to their friendship.

translation:
The emperor said: What are the three things that make me superior to others?
Yuan Ang said: When you were in the Kingdom of Dai, the Queen Mother was ill. For three years, you never closed your eyes, went to bed without undressing, and refused to give the medicine to the Queen Mother unless you tasted it yourself.
As a commoner, it was difficult for Zeng Shen to do this, but now as a king, you have implemented it, and you are far ahead of Zeng Shen in terms of filial piety.
Zhu Lu is in power, and the powerful ministers do their own thing. However, you took six post cars from Dai State to the capital city where misfortune and fortune are unpredictable. Even warriors like Meng Ben and Xia Yu cannot compare with you.
When you arrive at the official residence of the King of Dai, you sit to the west to abdicate the throne of emperor three times, and to the south to abdicate the throne of emperor twice.
Xu You surrendered only once, but you surrendered the world five times, more than Xu You surrendered four times.
Besides, you exiled the King of Huainan because you wanted to put some hard work on his mind and make him correct his mistakes. Because the officials were careless in protecting him, he died of illness.
The emperor was relieved at this time, and Yuan An became famous in the court.
Yuan Ang often talks about great principles and is impassioned.
Because the eunuch Tangtan had been favored by the emperor many times, he often secretly harmed Yuan An, which made Yuan An feel worried.
Yuan An's nephew Yuan Zhong served as an attendant knight, guarding the emperor with talismans. Yuan Zhong advised Yuan Ang: "You have humiliated him in the court. If you say bad things about you in the future, the emperor will not believe him."
When Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty went out, Zhao Tan accompanied him in the carriage. Yuan Ang bowed in front of the carriage and said: I heard that those who accompanied the emperor in the six-foot-tall carriage were all domestic heroes. Even if the Han Dynasty lacks talents, why do you only ride in the same carriage with people with broken bodies?
The emperor then laughed and asked Zhao Tan to get out of the car.
Zhao Tan got out of the car crying.
Emperor Wenwen of the Han Dynasty went up the mountain from Baling and wanted to gallop down the hillside from the west.
Yuan Ang took the reins of Emperor Wen's horse. The emperor said: General, are you timid?
Yuan Ang said: I have heard that people with a rich family do not sit close to the eaves, and people with a rich family do not sit on the railings beside the balcony. The wise master does not take risks and does not succeed by chance.
Now you want to indulge the six horses in the chariot and gallop down the mountain. If the horses are frightened and the chariot is destroyed, even if you underestimate yourself, how can you be worthy of Gaozu and the Queen Mother?
The emperor then stopped.
The emperor arrived at Shanglin Garden, accompanied by the queen and Mrs. Shen.
They often sit on the same level of seats in the palace.
When they were seated, Chief Lang arranged the seats, and Yuan Ang pulled Mrs. Shen's seat back a little.
Mrs. Shen was angry and refused to sit down.
The emperor was also angry and got up.
Yuan An took the opportunity to step forward and persuade: I heard that if there is an order of superiority and inferiority, then there will be harmony between the superiors and inferiors. Now that His Majesty has confirmed the Queen, Mrs. Shen is just a concubine. How can the concubine and the Lord sit at the same table?
Besides, if you dote on her, reward her even more.
The method His Majesty used to pamper Mrs. Shen turned out to be a disaster.
summary: Yuan Ang advised Emperor Wen against indulging Liu Chang, the King of Huainan, whose arrogance led to rebellion. When the king died in exile, Yuan Ang consoled the grieving emperor by listing his three great virtues: filial piety during his mother's illness, courage in facing danger when coming to the capital, and humility in repeatedly declining the throne. Yuan Ang also clashed with the eunuch Zhao Tan, insisting he should not ride in the emperor's carriage, and prevented the emperor from reckless chariot racing. He corrected the seating order between the queen and Consort Shen, warning against favoritism by citing the tragic fate of "human pigs."

translation:
Hasn't your majesty heard about human pigs?
The emperor was happy and went inside to tell Mrs. Shen what Yuan An had said.
Mrs. Shen gave Yuan Ang fifty catties of gold.
However, Yuan An could not stay in the court for a long time because of his many blunt admonitions.
He was transferred to the captaincy of Longxi. He loved the soldiers, and the soldiers rushed to do their best for him.
He was promoted to prime minister of Qi and then prime minister of Wu.
When saying goodbye and setting off, Yuan Zhong said to Yuan An: King Wu has been arrogant for a long time, and there are many traitors in the country. If you want to expose and punish him now, those people will either write a letter to accuse you, or they will kill you with a sharp sword.
The land in the south is low and humid. You drink wine every day and do nothing more than persuade the King of Wu not to rebel.
If you can do this, you may be able to get away from trouble.
Yuan Ang adopted Yuan Zhong's strategy, and the King of Wu treated him favorably.
Yuan Ang took leave and went home. He met Prime Minister Shen Tujia on the road and got out of the car to worship him. The prime minister only expressed his gratitude to Yuan Ang from the car.
When Yuan An returned home, he felt ashamed in front of his subordinates, so he went to the Prime Minister's residence to send a name card and asked to see the Prime Minister.
It took a long time for Cheng to meet Yuan Ang.
Yuan Ang knelt down and said, "I hope to receive you alone."
The prime minister said: If what you are talking about is a public matter, go to the official office to discuss it with the official, and I will report your opinions. If it is a private matter, I will not accept private requests.
Yuan Ang knelt down and persuaded him: "As the prime minister, you can weigh it yourself. How do you compare to Chen Ping and Jianghou?"
The prime minister said: I can't compare.
Yuan Ang said: Yes, you think you can't compare.
Chen Ping and Jianghou assisted Emperor Gao to pacify the world, served as generals, eradicated the Lu, and preserved the Liu family. You are just a warrior with a strong bow. You were promoted to captain and accumulated merits to become the governor of Huaiyang. You have no military exploits for attacking cities and seizing territory with unexpected plans.
Moreover, when the emperor came to Beijing from Daiguo, every time he met with the ministers and officials, he would not stop to accept their opinions and put them aside. If the opinions were acceptable, he would adopt them. There was never a time when he would not approve them.
What's the reason?
I just want to use this method to attract the world's most capable scholars and officials. The emperor hears things he has never heard before, understands things he has never understood before, and becomes wiser day by day. Now you have closed the mouths of the people in the world and are becoming stupid day by day.
As a wise monarch, you come to rebuke the foolish prime minister. Your son who will suffer disaster is not far away.
The prime minister then bowed twice to Yuan Ang. Said: I am a vulgar and vulgar person, but I am not smart. Fortunately, the general taught me.
Invite Yuan An into the inner room and sit together as the most distinguished guest.
Yuan Ang has never liked Chao Cuo. Where Chao Cuo stayed, Yuan An left; when Yuan An was there, Chao Cuo also left. The two have never spoken together.
When Emperor Mojing came to the throne and Chao Cuo became the imperial censor, he sent officials to investigate Yuan An's acceptance of the property of King Wu and punished him. The emperor issued an edict to exempt him from punishment and demote him to a commoner.
summary: Yuan Ang served as governor of Longxi, prime minister of Qi, and later of Wu, following his nephew Yuan Zhong's advice to avoid conflict with the rebellious King of Wu by drinking daily and not interfering. He later confronted Prime Minister Shen Tujia, criticizing him for being less capable than Chen Ping and Zhou Bo and for stifling open discourse. Shen Tujia eventually apologized and treated him as a guest.

translation:
When news of Wu and Chu's rebellion came, Chao Cuo said to the Prime Minister: Yuan Ang accepted a lot of money from the King of Wu and specifically covered it up for him, saying that he would not rebel.
Now that he has really rebelled, if he wants to ask Yuan An to be punished, he must know about the rebellion plot.
The Prime Minister said: The matter has not been exposed. Punishing him may interrupt the rebellion conspiracy.
Now that the rebels are marching westward, what is the benefit of punishing him!
Besides, Yuan Ang shouldn't have any conspiracy.
Chao Cuo hesitated.
Someone told Yuan An what had happened. Yuan An was frightened and met Dou Ying at night. He explained to him the reasons for King Wu's rebellion and was willing to confront him personally in front of the emperor.
Dou Ying went to the palace to report to the emperor, and the emperor asked Yuan Ang to go to the palace to meet him. When he came to the meeting, he explained the situation of King Wu's rebellion. It was because of Chao Cuo. Only by killing Chao Cuo quickly and confessing his mistake to the king of Wu could the Wu army stop.
The emperor appointed Yuan Ang as Taichang and Baoying as general.
The two men had always been friendly, but when the king of Wu rebelled, the leading figures in the tombs near the capital and the wise officials in Chang'an City all scrambled to attach themselves to these two men, with hundreds of cars following them every day.
After Chao Cuo had been executed, Yuan Ang went to Yu Li as Taichang.
King Cheng wanted Sai'an to be a general, but Tomb Sai was unwilling.
The King of Wu wanted to kill him, so he sent a captain and five hundred soldiers to surround Yuan Ang in the army.
When Yuan An was the prime minister of the state of Wu, a Cong Shi had an affair with Yuan An's maid. Yuan An knew about this but did not reveal it, and treated Cong Shi as before.
Someone told Cong Shi that the prime minister knew that you were having an affair with your maid, so Cong Shi fled back.
Yuan Ang personally drove his car to chase Cong Shi, and finally gave him his maidservant, and still let him serve as Cong Shi.
When Yuan An went on his mission to Wu and was besieged, Cong Shi happened to be the captain who besieged Yuan An, so he exchanged all his luggage for two stones of strong wine, and the weather was cold. The soldiers were hungry and thirsty, and the soldiers besieging the southwest corner were all drunk. Sima took Yuan Ang to his feet at night and said, "You can go." King Wu expects to kill you tomorrow. Yuan An didn't believe it and said: What do you do?
Sima said: I was originally a maidservant who had an affair with Shi.
Yuan Ang then thanked him in horror and said: "You are lucky to have parents. I can't harm you."
Sima said: Just leave, I am about to run away and hide my parents, what are you worried about!
So he used a knife to open the tent of the military camp and led Yuan Ang straight out from the road guarded by the drunken soldiers.
Sima and Yuan An went their separate ways. Yuan An untied his knot and carried it in his arms. They walked for seventy miles. At dawn, they encountered Liang's cavalry. They galloped away on horseback and finally reported back to the court.
The Wu and Chu rebels had been defeated, and the emperor changed the title of Pingluhou Liu Li, son of King Chu Yuan, to King of Chu, and Yuan An became Prime Minister of Chu.
He once wrote a letter to speak out, but it was not adopted.
Yuan Ang resigned from his job and went home to live leisurely due to illness. He followed the local customs and participated in cockfights and dog racing with the villagers.
Ju Meng, a native of Luoyang, once visited Yuan An, who entertained him warmly.
summary: Yuan Ang had a long-standing feud with Chao Cuo. When the Rebellion of the Seven States broke out, Yuan Ang advised Emperor Jing to execute Chao Cuo to appease the rebels. After Chao Cuo's death, Yuan Ang was sent as an envoy to Wu but was surrounded by Wu forces. A former subordinate, whom Yuan Ang had once forgiven for an affair with his maid, helped him escape. Yuan Ang later became Prime Minister of Chu but resigned due to illness. He was assassinated by agents of the King of Liang after opposing the king's succession to the throne.

translation:
A rich man in Anling said to Zhichou: I heard that Ju Meng is a gambler. Why do you associate with him?
Yuan Ang said: Although Ju Meng was a gambler, his mother died, and more than a thousand cars came from other places to pay tribute, making him a place that surpassed everyone.
Besides, everyone has emergencies.
Once someone knocks on your door to beg you for something urgent or difficult, there is no need for your parents to be alive to shirk it, and there is no need to leave home to shirk it. The only people in the world who look up to them are Ji Xin and Ju Meng.
Nowadays, you are often followed by several warriors on horseback. In case of emergency, can you rely on them?
After rebuking the rich man, he stopped communicating with him.
When all the princes and noble officials heard about this, they all praised Yuan An.
Although Yuan An was leisurely at home, Emperor Jing often sent people to ask him about strategies.
The King of Liang wanted to become the heir to the throne, and Yuan An advised him not to have such discussions in the future.
The King of Liang resented Yuan An and sent people to assassinate Yuan An.
The assassins came to Guanzhong and asked Yuan Ang about his character. Many famous people praised him.
The assassin met Yuan Ang and said: I accept the money from King Liang to assassinate you. You are a cultivated person and I cannot bear to kill you.
But there will be more than ten groups of assassins in the future, so be on guard.
Yuan Ang felt unhappy and there were many strange things going on at home, so he went to Mr. Jue's house to ask for fortune telling.
When returning, the assassins from Liang who came later stopped Yuan An outside the gate of Anling City and stabbed him to death.
Chao Cuo was from Yingchuan.
I once studied the criminal naming theories of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang from Mr. Zhang Hui of Zhi County, and I was the same teacher as Song Meng and Liu Dai from Luoyang.
Because he was familiar with literature and classics, he served as Taichang's anecdote.
Chao Cuo was a severe, upright and harsh person.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, there was no one in the court who studied "Shang Shu". He only heard that there was Fu Sheng in Qi State. He was a doctor from the Qin Dynasty and was proficient in "Shang Shu". He was over ninety years old and could not be recruited because of his old age. Emperor Wen then ordered Taichang to send people to study.
Taichang sent Chao Cuo to Fu Shengna to study Shangshu. After returning, he took the opportunity to write a letter reporting on his study and praised his explanation of Shangshu.
Emperor Wen issued an edict and appointed him successively as the prince's minister and the family doctor, and later he was promoted to doctor.
Chao Cuo wrote again and said: The reason why the king has a noble and distinguished position and his fame has been spread for generations is because he knows how to use punishment and reputation.
Therefore, if you know how to control your ministers and govern the people, then the ministers will be fearful and obedient; if you know how to listen to various opinions, then you will not be deceived; if you know how to stabilize the society and make the people wealthy, then the people of the world will obey; if you know how to be loyal and filial to the elders, then the ministers will have the behavior. These four items, I believe, are the crown prince’s top priorities.
Some people think that the Crown Prince does not need to know what he is doing. Although I am stupid, I actually think this is not the case.
Look at the reason why the kings in the previous world could not worship in the ancestral temple and were coerced and killed by their ministers was because they did not understand the art of punishment.
The Crown Prince has read a lot, so the reason why he has not thoroughly mastered the art of punishment and naming is that he has not studied the meaning of the book.
summary: Chao Cuo, a native of Yingchuan, studied Legalist philosophy under Zhang Hui and became a doctor under Emperor Wen. He was sent to study the *Book of Documents* from Fu Sheng and later served as a tutor to the crown prince, earning the nickname "think tank." Chao Cuo wrote extensively on military strategy, advocating for selecting good generals, training soldiers, and using superior weapons. He proposed using surrendered barbarians and border settlers to defend against the Xiongnu, emphasizing the importance of terrain and equipment. He also criticized the Qin dynasty's harsh policies and recommended settling families in border fortresses with proper housing, tools, and incentives.

translation:
The prime minister fell ill and died, making Chao Cuo even more powerful.
Chao Cuo was promoted to the imperial censor, and he stated the sins of the princes and requested that their lands be reduced and their neighboring counties be recovered.
After the memorial was sent, the emperor ordered the ministers, princes and royal family to gather for discussion. No one dared to criticize him, except Baoying who disagreed. From then on, there was a gap between him and Chao.
The decree revised by Chao Cuo had thirty chapters. The princes were in an uproar and hated Chao Cuo.
When Chao Cuo's father heard the news, he came from Yingchuan and said to Chao Cuo: Your Majesty has just ascended the throne. You have been in power, infringing and weakening the princes, and alienating other people's flesh and blood. People blame you and resent you. Why do you do this?
Chao Cuo said: Of course.
Otherwise, the emperor will not be noble and the country will not be peaceful.
Chao Cuo's father said: The Liu family's world is at peace, but the Chao family is in danger. I leave you and go back!
He took poison and died. When he was dying, he said: I can't bear to see a disaster involving myself.
Ten days later, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu all rebelled against Chao Cuo.
The emperor and Chao Cuo discussed sending troops. Chao Cuo wanted the emperor to personally lead the troops and let him guard the rear.
At that time, Dou Ying was recommending Yuan An, and Shou Shao came to see him. The emperor was planning military rations with Chao Cuo.
The emperor asked Yuan Ang: "You once served as the prime minister of Wu. Do you know Wu Chen Tian Lubo's character?"
What do you think about Wu and Chu's rebellion today? He replied: "Don't worry, we can defeat them today."
The emperor said: King Wu minted money from the mountains, boiled the sea into salt, seduced the world's heroes, and started a rebellion with a white scarf on his head. This plan has not been completed yet, so how can we give up?
Why do you say he has nothing to worry about?
Yuan Ang replied: The copper salt in Wu State is of great benefit, so why not find heroes to seduce it?
If the country of Wu is really blessed with heroes, they will only serve as assistants and will not rebel.
The people Wu Guo seduced were all scoundrels who were desperate to make money and treacherous people, so they attracted chaos later.
Chao Cuo said: Yuan Ance is very good.
The emperor said: How to plan for quelling the chaos?
Yuan An said: "Please everyone on the left and right please step back."
The people on the left and right left, leaving Chao Cuo alone.
Yuan An said: What I want to say is not known to others.
So Chao Cuo was asked to step aside.
Chao Cuo hurriedly fled to the Shuxiang room, hating Yuan Ang deeply.
The emperor asked Yuan An urgently and replied: The ministers of Wu and Chu sent letters saying that Emperor Gao made his children kings and each had their own land. Now Chao Cuo, the traitor, is good at punishing the princes and depriving them of their land. Therefore, he went west to attack Chao Cuo in the name of rebellion. He restored the original fiefdom and then stopped.
The current strategy is to kill Chao Cuo, send envoys to pardon the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu, and restore their old lands. Then they can all stop fighting without bloodshed.
So the emperor remained silent for a long time and then said: "Look at the situation, I don't love anyone to thank the world."
Yuan Ang said: If you take out the Yu Ji, you can only make a careful calculation by the emperor.
So Ren Yuan Ang thought it was too often, secretly packed his bags and set off.
More than ten days later, Prime Minister Qing Zhai, Lieutenant Jia, and Ting Lieutenant Zhang Ou impeached Chao Cuo, saying: King Wu is rebellious and wants to harm the ancestral temple, and the whole world should punish him.
Now Chao Cuo, the imperial censor, suggested: "With millions of soldiers, it is not reliable to hand them over to the ministers alone. It is better for your majesty to lead the troops yourself and let Chao Cuo stay behind."
The unconquered areas around Xu and Tong can be given to Wu.
Chao Cuo did not praise His Majesty's virtue and integrity, but wanted to alienate the ministers and people, and also wanted to give the city to Wu. He did not fulfill the courtesy of a minister, and was treasonous.
Chao Cuo should be punished by being cut in half, and his parents, wives, brothers, young and old, should be put to death.
Please handle the matter according to law.
The emperor's instructions said: "Okay."
Chao Cuo had no idea.
He sent a lieutenant to summon Chao Cuo and tricked him into getting into a car and passing through the market. Chao Cuo was beheaded in Shushi wearing court clothes.
Chao Cuo was dead, and his servant, Duke Deng, served as a school captain. At this time, he served as a general to attack the rebels of Wu and Chu.
He returned to the capital, wrote a letter reporting the military situation, and went to see the emperor.
The emperor asked: When you came from the army and heard that Chao Cuo was dead, did Wu and Chu retreat?
邓公说： 吴王谋反已有几十年了，因削减他的封地而发怒，以诛杀晁错为名，他的本意不在晁错呀。
Moreover, I am worried that the scholar-bureaucrats in the world will keep silent and dare not speak out. The emperor said: Why?
Deng Gong said: Chao Cuo was worried that the princes were too strong to be subdued, so he asked to reduce the fiefdoms of the princes in order to respect the imperial court. This is a good thing for all times.
The plan had just started to be implemented, but he was killed. Internally, it blocked the mouths of loyal ministers. Externally, it avenged the princes. I privately think that it is not advisable for you to do this.
At this time, Emperor Jing sighed loudly and said: You are right, I also regret this.
summary: Under Emperor Jing, Chao Cuo rose to power as Imperial Censor and pushed for reducing the fiefs of feudal princes, sparking widespread resentment. His father warned him of the danger, but Chao Cuo insisted it was necessary for the state's stability. When the Seven States rebelled, Chao Cuo was executed on the advice of Yuan Ang and others, despite his loyalty. After his death, Deng Gong defended him, noting that the rebellion was premeditated and not truly about Chao Cuo. Emperor Jing later regretted the execution.

translation:
So Deng Gong was appointed as the lieutenant of Chengyang.
Deng Gong was from Chenggu and had many strange strategies.
In the first year of Jianyuan, the imperial court wanted to recruit virtuous people, and the ministers recommended Deng Gong. At this time, Deng Gong was dismissed from his post and was appointed as the ninth minister by common people.
A year later, Mr. Deng resigned and returned home again due to illness.
His son Sutong was very famous among the court ministers because of his research on the theories of Jianhu and Wang.
Zan said: Although Yuan Ang is not eager to learn, he is also good at understanding and understanding. He still has the essence of benevolence and is often passionate and generous when citing great causes.
When Emperor Wen of Han came to the throne, his talents came at the right time.
Times changed, and during the reign of Emperor Jing, he used a trick to kill Chao Cuo for his suggestion of Wu and Chu rebellion, and he himself finally suffered an accident.
Chao Cuo was keen on making foresight for the country, but he could not see that his own disaster was coming.
His father could see clearly, but committed suicide in a ditch, which was of no use to save the country from defeat. It is not as good as Zhao's mother to blame Zhao Kuo. Although Zhao Kuo was defeated by Changping, he saved the Zhao family from being killed by Lian Lifa.
How sad!
Although Chao Cuo did not die well, the world still lamented his loyalty.
Therefore, his remarks related to the implementation of political affairs were collected and recorded in his biography.
summary: The historian's commentary notes that Yuan Ang, though not deeply learned, was perceptive and benevolent, but his scheme to kill Chao Cuo ultimately led to his own downfall. Chao Cuo was farsighted in statecraft but blind to his personal peril, unlike Zhao Kuo's mother who saved her family from destruction. Despite his unjust death, Chao Cuo's loyalty was mourned, and his policy writings were preserved.

translation:
Wang Shang, named Ziwei, was originally from Liwu County, Zhuo County, and later moved to Duling.
Wang Shang's father, Wang Wu, and Wang Wu's brother were all granted the title for no reason because they were relatives of Emperor Xuan.
For no reason, he was granted the title of Marquis of Pingchang, and Wang Wu was granted the title of Marquis of Lechang.
These words are recorded in "The Biography of Wai Qi".
Wang Shang Shi Danfu Xi said that when Wang Shang was young, he was the concubine of the crown prince and was praised for his serious, respectful and loyal character.
After his father's death, Wang Shang succeeded his father as the Marquis of Lechang. He transferred his property and distributed it to his half-brothers. He left nothing behind, and he mourned during the mourning period.
So the minister recommended that the king's business can encourage the ministers, his benevolence and righteousness can make the customs honest, and he should be used as a close minister.
As a result, Wang Shang was promoted to the rank of lieutenant general among all the Cao officials.
During the reign of Emperor Yuan, he was promoted to General You and Doctor Guanglu.
At that time, King Dingtao was favored and almost replaced the prince.
As a relative and important minister, Wang Shang assisted the government and supported the prince, which played a great role.
After the death of Emperor Yuan, Emperor Cheng came to the throne. He respected Wang Shang very much and was appointed General Zuo.
When Emperor Cheng became emperor, his uncle Sima General Wang Feng took over all the power and acted too proudly.
Wang Shang could not treat Wang Feng fairly when discussing courtiers. Wang Feng knew about this and alienated Wang Shang.
In the autumn of the third year after the founding of the People's Republic of China, the people of Kyoto panicked for no reason. There were rumors that a flood was coming.
The emperor personally came to the front hall and summoned the ministers to discuss the matter.
General Wang Feng thought that the Queen Mother, the Emperor, and the concubines in the harem could take a boat, allowing officials and people to board the Chang'an city wall to avoid the flood.
All ministers obeyed Wang Feng's advice.
Only General Wang Shang of the Left said: Since ancient times, floods have never flooded the cities of countries without moral governance.
Now the political situation is stable, there have been no wars for generations, and the monarchs and ministers are in peace. Why would a flood suddenly appear in one day?
This must be Mi's words, and the people should not be allowed to go to the city wall to make the people even more panicked.
The emperor gave up because of this.
Soon, the city of Chang'an gradually settled down. After verification, it turned out to be true.
The emperor then greatly praised Wang Shang's insistence on staying behind and repeatedly praised his ideas.
Wang Feng was greatly ashamed and regretted his mistake in speaking.
The next year, Wang Shang replaced Kuang Heng as prime minister, and granted a title to a thousand households in the city. The emperor respected and trusted him very much.
Wang Shang was a simple man with a majestic appearance. He was more than eight feet tall, had a burly build, and had a majestic appearance. He was extraordinary.
In the fourth year of Heping's reign, Chanyu came to worship and was led to the White Tiger Hall to see him.
Prime Minister Wang Shang was sitting in the court of Weiyang Palace. Chanyu came forward to pay homage to Wang Shang.
Wang Shang stood up and left his seat to talk to him. Shan Yu looked up and saw Wang Shang's face. He was very frightened and walked out tremblingly.
When the emperor heard about it, he exclaimed: "You are worthy of being the prime minister of the Han Dynasty!"
summary: Wang Shang, styled Ziwei, originally from Liwu County in Zhuo Commandery, later moved to Duling. His father Wang Wu and uncle were granted marquisates as relatives of Emperor Xuan, with Wang Wu becoming Marquis of Lechang. Wang Shang succeeded his father, distributed his inheritance to half-brothers, and was praised for his seriousness and loyalty. He rose to become General of the Left and Guanglu大夫 during Emperor Yuan's reign, supporting the crown prince against the favored King Dingtao. Under Emperor Cheng, Wang Shang served as General of the Left. When false rumors of a flood caused panic in the capital, General Wang Feng proposed evacuating to the city walls. Wang Shang argued that floods had never breached a virtuous capital, and the panic would worsen. The emperor agreed, and calm was restored. Wang Shang replaced Kuang Heng as Chancellor, earning the emperor's trust. During a visit by the Xiongnu Chanyu, Wang Shang's imposing stature so frightened the Chanyu that he trembled, prompting the emperor to praise him as a worthy Chancellor.

translation:
At the beginning, Yang Wei, the in-law of General Wang Feng, was appointed as the prefect of Langye. Four out of ten of his counties suffered disasters and reported them to the emperor.
Wang Shang arranged for examination and interrogation in turn, and Wang Feng told Wang Shang: "Disasters and strange disasters are a matter of God and cannot be caused by human power."
Yang Wei has always been a good official and should be given a lighter sentence.
Wang Shang refused to listen and went so far as to submit a memorial requesting that Yang Wei be dismissed. As expected, the memorial was withheld and not released. Wang Feng became increasingly resentful of Wang Shang and secretly searched for Wang Shang's shortcomings and sent someone to submit a memorial to expose Wang Shang's family privacy.
The emperor believed that this was a private matter that did not need to be disclosed and was not enough to slander the minister. Wang Feng argued stubbornly and handed the matter over to Sili.
Previously, the Empress Dowager summoned Wang Shang to inquire about his daughter and wanted to include her in the harem.
At that time, Wang Shang's daughter was seriously ill. Wang Shang also thought this matter was very difficult, so he responded by saying that his daughter was seriously ill and did not allow his daughter to enter the harem.
When Wang Shang was questioned about family privacy, he knew that he had been slandered by Wang Feng. He was very frightened and wanted to offer his daughter as a rescue, so he relied on the report of the newly favored Li Jieyu family to get his daughter into the harem.
There happened to be another solar eclipse. Zhang Kuang, a Taizhong doctor from Shu County, was a treacherous and clever man. He presented a memorial saying that he was willing to respond to the ministers close to him and state the reasons for the solar eclipse.
After leaving the court, Zuo General Shi Dan and others asked Zhang Kuang. Zhang Kuang replied: I think Prime Minister Wang Shang is acting arrogantly and citing external forces to control the court. He must achieve what he wants. He is cruel and vicious, has no mercy, punishes crimes quickly, despises officials, privately seeks out the faults of others, and wants to use it to build up his prestige. People in the world regard him as a pain and disaster.
Geng Ding, a native of Pinyang, had previously written a memorial to expose Wang Shang's affair with his father's maid, as well as his sister's adultery. The slave killed her adulterer, suspecting Wang Shang's instigation.
The memorial was handed over to the Secretary for processing, and Wang Shang was privately dissatisfied.
Wang Shang's son Wang Jun wanted to file a memorial against Wang Shang. Wang Jun's wife was the daughter of Zuo General Shi Dan, so he took Wang Jun's memorial to Shi Dan. Shi Dan was disgusted with the conflict between the father and son and asked for a divorce for his daughter.
Wang Shang did not exhaust his loyalty and offered good advice to assist the virtuous monarch. He knew that the wise emperor respected filial piety, stayed away from women, and obeyed the empress dowager in matters concerning the harem. The empress dowager had heard that Wang Shang had a daughter and wanted to include her in the harem. Wang Shang claimed that his daughter had a disease that could not be cured for a long time. Later, Geng Ding wrote a letter, and violated the right rules and used Li Gui's family to introduce his daughter. Wang Shang practiced evil ways to disrupt the government, deceived people with false statements, and violated the ethics of ministers, so a solar eclipse occurred.
summary: Wang Shang clashed with Wang Feng over the punishment of Yang Wei, a corrupt official. Wang Feng urged leniency, but Wang Shang insisted on dismissal, deepening Wang Feng's resentment. Wang Feng secretly sought Wang Shang's faults and exposed a family scandal: Wang Shang had initially refused to send his ill daughter to the harem at the Empress Dowager's request, but later used a favored concubine's influence to do so after being threatened. A solar eclipse occurred, and Zhang Kuang blamed Wang Shang for moral failings, citing his alleged adultery, murder, and deceit. Despite Wang Feng's demands for execution, the emperor spared Wang Shang, stripping him of his title. Wang Shang died three days later from vomiting blood.

translation:
The emperor always respected Wang Shang, and knowing that Zhang Kuang's words were sinister, he issued an order saying: "This should not be investigated."
Wang Feng argued stubbornly, and the emperor then ordered the censor: The prime minister should assist and support the emperor with virtue, command all officials, and coordinate various feudal states. There is no more important duty than this.
Now the Marquis of Lechang, Wang Shang, has been appointed prime minister and has served for five years. He has not listened to his sincere advice and good strategies, but he has committed the crime of disloyalty and practicing evil, and is guilty of a capital crime.
Previously, Wang Shang's sister did not practice women's virtues, and a domestic slave killed her lover. They suspected that Wang Shang had instigated it. Because Wang Shang was a minister in an important position, he restrained himself and did not pursue the case.
Now that someone has reported Wang Shang, he does not regret it, but instead harbors resentment. I am very sad.
Wang Shang was related to his late father and could not bear to send him to the judge.
Forgive Wang Shang's sins.
The envoy confiscated his Prime Minister's seal.
Three days after Wang Shang was deposed as prime minister, he suffered from an illness and vomited blood and died. He was named a violent marquis.
However, Wang Shang's relatives and descendants who served as Prince Consort, Shizhong, Zhongchangshi, and various Cao officials were all appointed as alternate officials, and no one could stay to serve as a guard.
A secretary reported that Wang Shang's crime had not yet been judged, and requested that Wang Shang be exempted from the fiefdom.
The emperor ordered Wang Shang's eldest son Wang An to inherit the title of Marquis of Lechang, and his official rank was Changle Palace Weiwei and Guanglu Xun.
After Wang Shang's death, there were consecutive solar eclipses and earthquakes for many years. The upright minister Jing Zhaoyin Wang Zhang was summoned to present a sealed memorial, avenging Wang Shang, saying that he was honest and upright and had no fault, and exposed Wang Feng's monopoly of power to deceive the Lord.
Wang Feng actually used the law to kill Wang Zhang. These words can be found in the "Biography of the Empress of the Yuan Dynasty" for details.
During the Hula period, Wang Ling became a violator and punished those who did not surrender to him. Wang An, the Marquis of Lechang, was charged with committing suicide and his fiefdom was removed.
Shi Dan, whose courtesy name was Junzhong, was originally from Lu and later moved to Duling.
Grandfather Shi Gong had a sister who was the concubine of Prince Wei during the reign of Emperor Wu, and gave birth to Emperor Mourning Kao.
Huang Kao was the father of Emperor Xuan.
When Emperor Xuan was poor and humble, he relied on the Shi family.
These words are recorded in "The Biography of Shi Liangdi".
By the time Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Shi Gong was already dead and had three sons, Shi Gao, Shi Zeng, and Shi Xuan.
Both Shi Zeng and Shi Xuan were granted the title because they were relatives from their maternal family and had the kindness of their ancestors. Shi Zeng was granted the title of General Linghou, and Shi Xuan was granted the title of Platform Marquis.
Shi Gao served as a minister and was honored and favored. He was named the Marquis of Leling for his role in exposing the rebel commander Huo Yu.
Emperor Xuan was seriously ill and appointed Shi Gao as the Grand Sima Cavalry General and concurrently as the Minister.
When Emperor Xuan died, the prince inherited the title of emperor, creating Emperor Xiaoyuan.
Shi Gao assisted the government for five years. He asked to retire because of his old age. He was given a chariot drawn by four horses and brass, and was dismissed from his post and returned home.
After his death, he was honored as Anhou.
When Emperor Yuan became the crown prince, Shi Dan was appointed as the concubine because of his father Shi Gao, and he followed him for more than ten years.
After Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, Shi Dan was appointed Prince Consort Duwei's Attendant. The Emperor often rode on the right side of the carriage when traveling, and was very favored.
Because Shi Dan was a former minister and a relative of his late father's family, the emperor trusted him closely and ordered Shi Dan to protect the prince's family.
At that time, Fu Zhaoyi's son, King Dingtao, was talented, and both mother and son were favored. However, the prince had some faults in drinking and sex, and his mother, the Queen, was not favored.
During the Jianzhao period, Emperor Yuan fell ill and could not personally manage the affairs of the court. He was just greedy for music.
summary: Shi Dan, styled Junzhong, from Lu, later moved to Duling. His grandfather's sister was a concubine of Prince Wei, mother of Emperor Xuan's father. Shi Dan served as a crown prince's attendant for over a decade. When Emperor Yuan fell ill and favored King Dingtao over the prince, Shi Dan wept before the emperor, arguing the prince was established and respected. The emperor relented, securing the prince's succession. After Emperor Cheng's accession, Shi Dan became General of the Left and Marquis of Wuyang. He was outwardly suave but cautious, trusted by the emperor. He lived extravagantly with many concubines and servants, serving as general for sixteen years before retiring due to illness and dying shortly after.

translation:
Emperor Yuan fell ill, and Emperor Cheng had just ascended the throne. He promoted Shi Dan to the position of Changle Guardsman and General Right, and granted him the title of Marquis of Guannei and three hundred households of food. He was promoted to Shi Zhong, and later transferred to General Zuo and Doctor Guanglu.
In the first year of Hongjia, the emperor issued a letter to Shao saying: Praising virtuous people and rewarding ministers with meritorious service is a common principle from ancient times to the present.
General Shi Dan of the Left used to guide me with his honest and upright character. He upheld morality, simplicity and single-mindedness, and was the most virtuous and prosperous person in the past.
Shi Dan was granted the title of Marquis of Wuyang, and Wu Qiangju of Tan County in the East China Sea was made a fief with a settlement of 1,100 households.
Stan is resourceful and approachable. He looks suave and unruly on the outside, but he is very cautious on the inside, so he can be trusted by the emperor.
Stan's elder brother succeeded his father as a marquis and refused to accept the title.
Stan obtained all of his father's property, and received the taxes of a large fief himself. In addition, he was praised and rewarded many times for his past favors. The rewards he received accumulated to a thousand gold, and his servants were counted in hundreds. He had dozens of wives and concubines in the inner room. He was extravagant at home, loved drinking, and indulged himself in the pleasures of delicious food, music, and women.
He served as a general for a total of sixteen years. During the Yongshi period, he became seriously ill and asked to retire. The emperor gave him a policy letter saying: General Zuo is getting seriously ill and is not declining. He hopes to return home to cure his illness. I feel sorry for him. He has kept the general for a long time with his official duties, so that his body has not recovered.
He sent Guang Luxun to give the general fifty kilograms of brass, a carriage drawn by four horses, and handed over the general's seal.
You should concentrate your energy and mind, and be sure to get close to the doctor and take medicine to support your body and prevent it from failing.
Shi Dan died a few months after returning home and was named the Marquis of Qing.
He had twenty sons and daughters. Because of Shi Dan's trust, all nine sons became ministers and ministers, close to the emperor and often at his side.
There were a total of four people in the Shi family who were granted the title of marquis, and there were more than ten people who had the salary of 2,000 dan as official or minister. They were all extinct until the period of Wang Mang. Only Shi Zeng, the Marquis of Jiangling, had no heirs and was exterminated by himself.
Fu Xi, courtesy name Zhiyou, was a native of Wenxian County, Hanoi. He was the cousin of Empress Dowager Dingtao, the grandmother of Emperor Ai.
When he was young, he liked to learn and inquire, and he had ambition and integrity.
Emperor Ai was established as the crown prince, and Emperor Cheng selected Fu Xi as the crown prince's concubine.
As soon as Emperor Ai ascended the throne, he appointed Fu happy as a guard and promoted to general on the right.
At that time, Wang Mang was serving as Chief Sima, so he asked to resign and took refuge in the emperor's uncle's house.
The emperor has allowed Wang Mang to retire, and everyone has placed high hopes on Fu happy.
Fu Xi's cousin Fu Yan, the Marquis of Kongxiang, has the same kinship relationship with the emperor as Fu happy, and his daughter is the queen.
There was also the emperor's uncle, Hou Dingming of Yang'an, who was also granted the title because of his close maternal relatives.
summary: Fu Xi, styled Zhiyou, from Wen County, was cousin to Emperor Ai's grandmother. He served as a crown prince's attendant and later as General of the Right. When Wang Mang resigned, Fu Xi declined power, citing illness. Empress Dowager Fu wanted to claim equal status with Emperor Cheng's mother, but Fu Xi, with Kong Guang and Shi Dan, opposed this. The emperor dismissed Shi Dan and then Fu Xi, accusing him of failing to correct errors and fostering treachery. Fu Xi was sent to his fiefdom, later recalled by Wang Mang, but died of old age. His son inherited the title, which ended after Wang Mang's fall.
