translation:
Wang Mang, also known as Jujun, is the nephew of Queen Xiaoyuan.
Empress Yuan's father and brothers all became marquises during the reigns of Emperor Yuan and Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty, held important positions, and assisted in government affairs. There were nine people in the family who were granted the title of marquis and five chief ministers. These words are recorded in the "Biography of the Empress of the Yuan Dynasty".
Only Wang Mang's father, Wang Man, died earlier and was not granted a title.
Wang Mang's uncles and brothers were all the sons of generals and marquises. They took advantage of the time when their fathers were powerful and lived a luxurious and lavish life. They showed off and compared each other with tall carriages and horses, talented singers and concubines, beautiful concubines, and novel games. Wang Mang was the only one who was lonely and poor, so he treated others with humility and lived a simple life.
He worshiped Chen Shen, a native of Pei County, as his teacher, studied "Etiquette" and "Zhou Rites", worked diligently and extensively, and dressed like an ordinary scholar.
He served his mother and widowed sister-in-law, raised his fatherless nephew, and behaved with great caution.
In addition, he made friends with outstanding talents outside and served his uncles and uncles in the family with tact, thoughtfulness and courtesy.
During the Yangshuo period, his uncle, the general Wang Feng, fell ill. Wang Mang served him and took the medicine himself. He did not comb his hair or wash his face, resulting in unkempt appearance. He went to bed without taking off his clothes for several months.
When Wang Feng was dying, she entrusted Wang Mang to the Queen Mother and Emperor Cheng. He was appointed Huang Menlang and was later promoted to Shesheng Xiaowei.
After a long time, his uncle Chengdu Marquis Wang Shang wrote to the emperor, expressing his willingness to allocate his own households to Wang Mang. Others, such as Changle Shaofu Dai Chong, Shi Zhong Jin She, Hu Qi Xiao Lieutenant Ji Hong, Shanggu Du Wei Yang Bing and Zhonglang Chen Tang, were all very famous people at the time. They all spoke for Wang Mang. From then on, the emperor considered Wang Mang to be a wise man.
In the first year of Yongshi, Emperor Cheng granted Wang Mang the title of Marquis of Xindu. The Marquis was built in the capital of Xinye County, Nanyang County, with 1,500 households.
Later he was promoted to the rank of Cavalry Captain and Guanglu Doctor, and he served as a guard in the palace. He was cautious and considerate. As his official position became higher and higher, his attitude became more and more humble.
He distributed carriages, horses, and light warm clothing, and gave alms to the guests, so that there was no extra clothing in the house.
He accepted and supported famous people and made friends with many generals, prime ministers, and officials.
Therefore, people in important positions recommended him more, and celebrities in the society advocated for him. His reputation spread throughout the government and the public, surpassing his uncles.
He dares to behave in a pretentious manner without feeling ashamed.
Wang Mang's brother Wang Yong, who had served in various Cao Cao positions, had died long ago. He had a son named Wang Guang, and Wang Mang asked him to study under a doctor.
When Wang Mang was on vacation, he drove his chariot and horses, brought sheep and wine, and went to comfort his teacher. He even gave gifts to his classmates.
It attracted many scholars to watch and the old people admired it.
Wang Guang was younger than Wang Mang's son Wang Yu, so Wang Mang asked them to get married on the same day. The hall was filled with congratulatory guests.
After a while, one person said that his mother had some kind of illness and what medicine she should take. By the time the guests left, he had already gotten up several times.
summary: Wang Mang, also known as Jujun, was the nephew of Empress Xiaoyuan. During the reigns of Emperors Yuan and Cheng of the Han Dynasty, Empress Yuan's father and brothers all became marquises, held important positions, and assisted in government affairs. Nine family members were granted the title of marquis, and five served as chief ministers. Only Wang Mang's father, Wang Man, died early and was not granted a title. Wang Mang's uncles and brothers, as sons of generals and marquises, lived luxurious lives, but Wang Mang, being lonely and poor, treated others with humility and lived simply. He studied "Etiquette" and "Zhou Rites" under Chen Shen, dressed like an ordinary scholar, served his mother and widowed sister-in-law, raised his fatherless nephew, and behaved with caution. He made friends with outstanding talents and served his uncles with tact and courtesy. During the Yangshuo period, his uncle Wang Feng fell ill, and Wang Mang served him diligently, not combing his hair or washing his face for months. When Wang Feng was dying, he entrusted Wang Mang to the Queen Mother and Emperor Cheng, leading to Wang Mang's appointment as Huang Menlang and later promotion to Shesheng Xiaowei. Over time, his uncle Chengdu Marquis Wang Shang and other notable figures spoke highly of Wang Mang, leading Emperor Cheng to consider him a wise man. In the first year of Yongshi, Wang Mang was granted the title of Marquis of Xindu with 1,500 households. He was later promoted to Cavalry Captain and Guanglu Doctor, serving as a guard in the palace. As his official position rose, his attitude became more humble. He distributed his wealth to guests, leaving no extra clothing in his house, and supported famous people, making friends with many officials. His reputation spread throughout the government and public, surpassing his uncles. Wang Mang's brother Wang Yong had died, leaving a son named Wang Guang, whom Wang Mang had study under a doctor. During his vacations, Wang Mang visited his teacher with gifts and gave presents to classmates, attracting admiration from scholars and elders. Wang Guang married on the same day as Wang Mang's son Wang Yu, with a hall full of congratulatory guests. Wang Mang once secretly bought a maidservant, claiming he bought her for General Zhu Ziyuan because she could bear many sons, and gave her away that day, hiding his true feelings to pursue fame.

translation:
He once secretly bought a maidservant, and word gradually spread among his brothers. Wang Mang said: "The later general Zhu Ziyuan has no sons. I heard that this woman can have many sons, so I bought her for him."
The maidservant was given to Zhu Ziyuan that day.
Wang Mang went to such an extent to hide his true feelings and pursue fame.
At this time, Chun Yuchang, the son of the Queen Mother's sister, was ranked among the nine ministers because of his talents. He was an official before Wang Mang and his reputation and status were above Wang Mang.
Wang Mang secretly collected his crimes, and reported his situation to Emperor Cheng through the Grand Sima Quyanghou Wanggen. Chunyu Chang was killed by the law, and Wang Mang gained a reputation for loyalty and integrity. These words are recorded in the "Chun Yu Chang Biography".
Wang Gen therefore requested to retire and recommended Wang Mang to replace him. The emperor then promoted Wang Mang to be the Grand Sima.
This year is the first year of Suihe, and Wang Mang is thirty-eight years old.
Since Wang Mang had surpassed his peers and assisted the emperor after his four uncles, he planned to make his reputation better than that of his predecessors, so he set strict demands on himself and worked tirelessly. He hired many virtuous people to serve as subordinate officials, and all the rewards from the emperor and the income from fiefdoms were used to entertain the scholars. He himself became more frugal and frugal.
His mother was ill, and the princes, ministers and princes sent their wives to inquire about her condition. Wang Mang's wife went out to greet her, but she did not have a floor-length gown, and her sarong only reached her knees.
Those who saw her thought she was a slave, but when they asked, they found out that she was Wang Mang's wife, and they were all surprised.
Wang Mang assisted the government for more than a year. Emperor Mo Cheng died and Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne. He honored the Empress Dowager as the Empress Dowager.
The Queen Mother ordered Wang Mang to resign and go home, giving up power to Emperor Ai's maternal family.
Wang Mang then submitted a memorial and asked to resign. Emperor Ai sent his minister Shao to order Wang Mang to say: The late emperor entrusted the government to you and abandoned his subordinates. I can take over the country and I really hope to be of the same mind as you.
Now that you have written a letter saying that you are ill and requesting resignation, it seems that I cannot obey the late emperor's will. I am very sad about this.
The minister has been ordered to wait for you to come to court to report.
He also sent Prime Minister Kong Guang, Grand Sikong Hewu, General Zuo Shidan, and Weiwei Fu happy to report to the Queen Mother: The emperor was very sad when he heard the Queen Mother's edict.
If Da Sima did not become an official, the emperor would not dare to handle government affairs.
The Queen Mother also appointed Wang Mang as director.
At this time, Emperor Ai's grandmother, the Empress Dowager Dingtao, and her mother, Liao Ji, were still alive. Dong Hong, the Marquis of Gaochang, wrote a letter saying: According to the meaning of "Spring and Autumn", mothers are more valuable than their children, so Ding Ji should be given the honorific title.
Wang Mang and Shi Dan jointly impeached and exposed Dong Hong for misleading the court and violating principles. These words were recorded in "The Biography of Shi Dan".
Later, a banquet was held in Weiyang Palace, and the insider ordered a curtain to be set up for Empress Dowager Fu to sit next to the Empress Dowager.
summary: Wang Mang secretly collected crimes of Chun Yuchang, the son of the Queen Mother's sister, and reported him to Emperor Cheng through Grand Sima Wanggen. Chunyu Chang was executed, and Wang Mang gained a reputation for loyalty. Wang Gen then recommended Wang Mang to replace him, and Emperor Cheng promoted Wang Mang to Grand Sima at age thirty-eight. Wang Mang set strict demands on himself, hired virtuous people as subordinates, and used his rewards and fiefdom income to entertain scholars, living frugally. His wife, when greeting guests, wore a sarong that only reached her knees, surprising those who mistook her for a slave. After Emperor Cheng died and Emperor Ai succeeded, the Queen Mother ordered Wang Mang to resign, but Emperor Ai refused his resignation and reappointed him. Wang Mang later clashed with Empress Dowager Fu, leading to his resignation again. He was rewarded with gold and chariots and returned to his palace. Many officials praised him, and the emperor treated him with favor, sending special envoys to serve him at home.

translation:
The Queen Mother appointed Wang Mang as Grand Sima and discussed with him the selection of a successor to the throne.
Wang Shun, the Marquis of Anyang, was Wang Mang's cousin. He was cautious and trusted by the Queen Mother. Wang Mang proposed that Wang Shun be the chariot general and asked him to greet the King of Zhongshan to succeed him as emperor, creating Emperor Xiaoping.
When Emperor Ping was just nine years old, the Queen Mother came to the court to act as an agent in government affairs and entrusted the government affairs to Wang Mang.
Tu Mang pointed out that the Tang family had killed the prince in the past, and the Fu family was proud and arrogant, so he deposed Empress Xiaocheng Tang and Empress Xiaoai Fu and ordered them to commit suicide. These words are recorded in "The Biography of the Wife".
Because the great Situ Kong Guang was a famous Confucian scholar, Wang Mang had assisted three emperors, namely Cheng Emperor, Ai Emperor and Heping Emperor. He was respected by the Empress Dowager and trusted by the people of the country, so he treated Kong Guang with great respect and recommended Kong Guang's son-in-law Zhen Han to serve as a servant and captain of the car.
For all the relatives of Emperor Ai and the ministers in important positions whom he disliked, Wang Mang wrote a memorial asking for instructions and asked Zhen Han to bring them to Jie Guang.
Kong Guang has always been fearful and cautious, and he dared not fail to report the matter. Wang Mang reported to the Queen Mother again, and the Queen Mother agreed to these memorials.
So the former general He Wu and the latter general Gongsun Lu were dismissed from their posts because they recommended each other to be appointed as Grand Sima. The relatives of Ding, Fu and Dong Xian were all removed from their official positions and titles and were exiled to distant places.
Wang Li, the Marquis of Hongyang, was the younger brother of the Queen Mother. Although he was not an official, Wang Mang respected him in his heart because he was his uncle. He was afraid that Wang Li would enlighten the Queen Mother when he was free so that he would not be able to do whatever he wanted. He also asked Kong Guang to report Wang Li's past crimes to the Queen Mother: Wang Li knew that Dingling Marquis Chunyu was a long-time criminal. After committing the crime of treason, he also accepted a large amount of bribes from him, interceded for him, and misled the court; later, he reported that the illegitimate son of the official slave Yang Ji was used as the prince. Everyone said that Empress Lu and the young emperor were resurrected. There were different opinions, making the world suspicious. This made it difficult to show future generations and complete the task of protecting the young master.
Please let Wang Li return to his feudal kingdom.
The Queen Mother did not follow his advice.
Wang Mang said: Now that the Han Dynasty is in decline and there are no heirs for several generations, it is really terrible for you, Queen Mother, to take charge of the government on your own instead of your young master. You try hard to set an example for the world with a fair attitude, but you may not obey me. If you don't listen to my opinion out of personal love, then the officials will have evil thoughts, and disaster will happen!
He should be sent back to the feudal country for the time being, and then transferred back after the country's affairs have stabilized a bit.
The Queen Mother had no choice but to let Wang Li return to his country.
These were all the methods Wang Mang used to coerce and blackmail the Queen Mother and her ministers.
In this way, those who relied on and obeyed him were promoted, and those who opposed and resented him were killed.
Wang Shun and Wang Yi became his confidants, Zhen Feng and Zhen Han were in charge of pickets, impeachments, and trials, Ping Yan was in charge of confidential military and political affairs, Liu Xin was in charge of rituals, music, and regulations, and Sun Jian became his right-hand assistant.
Zhen Feng's son Zhen Xun, Liu Xin's son Liu Cai, Cui Fa from Zhuojun, and Chen Chong from Nanyang were all favored by Wang Mang because of their talents.
Wang Mang looked stern and spoke seriously. If he wanted to do something, he only needed to give a slight hint with his expression and face, and the party members would clearly report his intention to the superiors. Wang Mang would kowtow and cry and resolutely refuse to give in. This was used to confuse the Queen Mother, and to show integrity to the common people.
At first, Wang Mang politely signaled to the Yizhou Order to let the barbarians outside the Great Wall donate white-feathered pheasants. In the first month of the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, Wang Mang reported to the Queen Mother and issued an edict to use white-feathered pheasants as offerings to the ancestral temple.
The ministers then reported to the Queen Mother: The Queen Mother appointed Grand Sima Wang Mang to make the decision to support the new emperor, thus bringing stability to the court.
The previous great Sima Huo Guang was credited with stabilizing the country and adding 30,000 households in the fiefdoms. It was also stipulated that after his death, his descendants would inherit the title and the number of fiefdoms would be equal to his, just like that of Xiao Xiangguo.
Wang Mang should be awarded the title according to Huo Guang's example.
The Queen Mother asked the princes and ministers: Is it really because Da Sima has made great contributions that he should be praised?
summary: After three years in his feudal state, hundreds of officials petitioned for Wang Mang's recall. In the first year of Yuanshou, a solar eclipse occurred, and virtuous men praised Wang Mang's merits, leading the emperor to recall him. When Wang Mang returned to the capital, Emperor Ai died without a son, and the Queen Mother summoned Wang Mang to take control. Wang Mang reported that Da Sima Gao'an Hou Dong Xian was too young and not suitable, so his seal was confiscated, and Dong Xian committed suicide. The Queen Mother appointed Wang Mang as Grand Sima, and they selected the King of Zhongshan to succeed as Emperor Xiaoping. When Emperor Ping was nine, the Queen Mother acted as regent and entrusted government affairs to Wang Mang. Wang Mang deposed Empress Xiaocheng Tang and Empress Xiaoai Fu, ordering them to commit suicide. He treated Grand Situ Kong Guang with respect and used him to report on officials he disliked, leading to their dismissal or exile. Wang Mang also forced his uncle Wang Li to return to his feudal country, using coercion and blackmail to control the Queen Mother and her ministers. Wang Mang promoted those who obeyed him and killed those who opposed him. He used false humility to confuse the Queen Mother and the public. When the Yizhou Order offered white-feathered pheasants, Wang Mang reported it to the Queen Mother, and the ministers recommended he be granted the title of Anmo Gong with increased fiefdoms. Wang Mang refused multiple times, but the Queen Mother eventually granted him the title. He accepted the titles of Taifu and An Mogong but resigned from the increased fiefdom and hereditary rewards. He suggested rewarding other officials and implementing benevolent policies. After winning public favor, Wang Mang wanted to be dictatorial and hinted to officials to write memorials saying the Queen Mother should not interfere in trivial matters. The Queen Mother issued an edict allowing Wang Mang to evaluate and decide on official matters, giving him power equal to the emperor. Wang Mang refused the rewards, but the Queen Mother insisted. He eventually accepted the titles and rewards, including the prime minister's seal. Wang Mang proposed building a Mingtang, a national imperial college, and other structures, recruiting scholars from across the country. The ministers reported that Wang Mang's merits were evident, and the construction was completed quickly. The Queen Mother agreed to reward Wang Mang with nine kinds of utensils. In the fifth year of the Yuan Dynasty, many princes and officials petitioned for Wang Mang's rewards. Wang Mang wrote a letter declining, but the Queen Mother insisted. The ministers reported that Wang Mang's merits were like those of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, and they requested the reward of nine tins. The Queen Mother approved, and Wang Mang received various honors and items, including a green apron, formal dress, a jade-inlaid saber, chariots, and military equipment. He was also given a red painted door and steps inside the eaves, with guards and officials appointed to assist him. A white stone with vermilion words reading "Announcement of Prince Mang of Anhan to be the emperor" was discovered. Wang Mang asked the princes to report this to the Queen Mother, who initially refused but eventually agreed to let Wang Mang act as regent. The ministers reported that Wang Mang should ascend the throne and exercise imperial power, following the example of the Duke of Zhou. The Queen Mother issued an edict allowing Wang Mang to serve as regent and act as the emperor. Wang Mang then sat on the throne, wore the emperor's clothes, and accepted the worship of the ministers. The next year, the name was changed to Jushe. In the first year of Jushe, Wang Mang worshiped the gods and held ceremonies. Liu Ying was made the crown prince, known as Ruzi. Wang Shun, Zhen Feng, and Zhen Han were appointed as officials. In April, Liu Chong, Marquis of Anzhong, attacked Wancheng but failed. Wang Mang pardoned those who surrendered. Liu Jia wrote a memorial praising Wang Mang and suggesting severe punishment for Liu Chong. Wang Mang was pleased and granted Liu Jia a fiefdom. The ministers reported that Wang Mang's power should be increased to conquer the world. The Queen Mother ordered Wang Mang to call himself the "fake emperor" when seeing her. In December, the ministers petitioned to increase Wang Mang's official offices and household staff. The memorial was approved.

translation:
I hope you will be compassionate and considerate!
Wang Mang also asked the Queen Mother to write a letter to Shao, saying: I heard that the Queen Mother's rule is that ideological activities should not exceed the boundaries of the palace.
The country has not been blessed by God, and the emperor is still young and cannot govern himself. I am frightened and cautious, fearing that the country will not be peaceful.
Without me, who would be in charge of the country's supreme power?
Therefore, Confucius met Nanzi and Duke Zhou took charge of the government, which was based on the needs of the situation at that time.
I have exhausted my body, exhausted my mind, worried and toiled, and have no peace of mind. Therefore, when the world advocates luxury, I use frugal style to show the world that correcting deviations often requires more than the limit. If I don't take the lead personally, what will the people of the world do?
I dream about a good harvest day and night, so that every household of the common people can have enough food and clothing. When the emperor comes of age, I will hand over the government to him.
Now I really don’t have time to enjoy soft clothes and delicious food. I hope to achieve something with the officials, so I should encourage you!
Whenever there was a flood or drought, Wang Mang would only eat vegetables and his attendants would report the situation to the Queen Mother.
The Queen Mother sent an envoy to Wang Mang and said: I heard that you only eat vegetables. You are too worried about the suffering of the people.
Fortunately, the harvest this year is abundant. As you are so diligent and dedicated, you should eat some meat on time. Please take good care of your body for the sake of the country.
Wang Mang considered that the Central Plains had been stabilized and that only the Yi tribes in the four directions had not changed much, so he sent an envoy with gold and property, generous gifts to the Xiongnu Chanyu, and asked him to write a letter saying: I heard that the Central Plains ridiculed double names. My original name was Nangzhi Yasi, but now I changed my name to Zhi to express my admiration and compliance with the system of the Central Plains.
Wang Zhaojun's daughter was also sent to serve the Queen Mother.
In order to deceive, confuse and flatter the Queen Mother, as well as the eunuchs and maids around her, Wang Mang's methods were so varied.
After Wang Mang became a powerful emperor, he wanted to give his daughter to Emperor Ping as a queen in order to consolidate his power, so he wrote to the emperor: "It has been three years since the emperor ascended the throne, but he has not yet established a queen, and he has not provided enough concubines."
In the past, the country's crises were caused by the lack of heirs and improper marriages.
Please examine and apply the theory of the Five Classics to formulate the principles of marriage etiquette and correct twelve daughters, in order to give birth to more heirs.
The descendants of the Shang and Zhou royal families and the descendants of the principal wives of the princes in Chang'an during the Zhou Gong and Confucius eras were widely selected and betrothed to their children.
This matter was handed over to the officials in charge and a list of many women was submitted. Many daughters of the Wang family were on the candidate list.
Wang Mang was afraid that they would compete with his own daughters, so he wrote a memorial saying: "I have no virtue myself, and my daughter's appearance is inferior. It is not suitable to be selected at the same time as other women."
The Queen Mother thought that he was sincere, so she wrote to Shao Shu: "The daughters of the Wang family are my natal family, so don't choose them."
summary: Wang Mang used false reputations to please the Queen Mother, donating money and land to help the poor. He led ministers in reporting auspicious omens and asked the Queen Mother to conserve her energy. During floods or droughts, Wang Mang only ate vegetables, and the Queen Mother urged him to eat meat for his health. Wang Mang sent envoys to the Xiongnu Chanyu, who changed his name to comply with Chinese customs. Wang Mang also gave his daughter to Emperor Ping as queen to consolidate his power, despite initial refusal. The ministers insisted, and Wang Mang's daughter became queen. Wang Mang declined increased betrothal gifts and distributed them to poor families. Chen Chong, a Grand Situ Sizhi, wrote a memorial praising Wang Mang's virtues and merits, comparing him to the Duke of Zhou and recommending he be granted the title of prime minister. The Queen Mother showed the memorial to the ministers, and they discussed it.

translation:
So Zhen Feng was sent to hold the seal and confer the title of Empress Xiao of Zhongshan on Emperor Ping's mother Wei Ji on the spot. He also granted Emperor Ping's uncle Wei Shi and Wei Bao's brother Wei Xuanguan the title of Neihou, so that they could stay in Zhongshan and not be allowed to come to Chang'an.
Wang Mang's son, Wang Yu, blamed Wang Mang for separating the Wei family from the royal family, fearing that Emperor Ping would be resentful when he grew up.
Wang Yu secretly sent a message to Wei Bao and others, asking Emperor Ping's mother to write a letter requesting to come to the capital.
These words are recorded in "The Biography of Queen Wei."
Wang Mang refused.
Wang Yu discussed this matter with his teacher Wu Zhang and brother-in-law Lu Kuan. Wu Zhang believed that Wang Mang would not listen to the persuasion, but he believed in ghosts and gods and could cause disasters to frighten him. Wu Zhang then took the opportunity to deduce and persuade him to hand over power to the Wei family.
Wang Yu asked Lu Ye to smear Wang Mang's mansion with blood. When the gatekeepers discovered what had happened, Wang Mang arrested Wang Yu and threw him into prison, where he drank poison and died.
Wang Yu's wife Lu Yan was pregnant and was imprisoned. He waited until she gave birth to a child before killing her.
Wang Mang reported: Wang Yu was implicated by Lu Kuan and others, went astray, spread rumors to confuse everyone, and committed the same crime as Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai. I dare not hide it, so he should be punished.
Zhen Han and others reported to the Queen Mother and issued an edict: Tang Yao had a son Danzhu, and King Wen of Zhou had sons Guan Shu and Cai Shu. These are all examples of people with high virtues, talents and wisdom having no choice but to deal with the stupidest sons, because their nature is hard to change.
You are in the position of Duke of Zhou, assisting young masters like King Cheng, and punishing Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai just like Duke Zhou did to Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai. You do not hinder respect for the court because of your love for your son. I appreciate your actions very much.
In the past, Duke Zhou punished the descendants of the three prisons and the four kingdoms of Huai and Yi, completing a profound enlightenment to the point where no one committed a crime and the punishment was shelved.
You should concentrate on assisting the government and hope to achieve peace.
Wang Mang took advantage of this opportunity to kill the Wei family, thoroughly investigated Lu Kuan's case, and implicated various counties and feudal states. He always criticized those with outstanding talents. The court involved Princess Jingwu, Liang Wang Liu Li, Hongyang Hou Wangli, and Ahou Wangren. He sent envoys to persecute them, but they all committed suicide.
Hundreds of people died, and the world was shocked.
Chen Zuo, named Bao, the great Sima Hujun, said: When Duke Anhan met his son Wang Yu and committed crimes like Uncle Guan and Uncle Cai, although he loved his son deeply, he did not dare to take into account personal affairs for the benefit of the royal family.
Considering Wang Yu's crime, he wrote eight articles with emotion to warn his descendants.
These articles should be distributed throughout the country and ordered to be used by academic officials to teach students.
The matter was handed down to the ministers. They requested that all officials in the country who could recite An Mo Gong's admonitions to his descendants should be recorded in the official archives and treat An Han Gong's text as the "Book of Filial Piety".
In the spring of the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, people worshiped heaven in the suburbs, and at the same time offered sacrifices to Emperor Gaozu, and worshiped heaven in the ancestral temple, and at the same time offered sacrifices to Emperor Xiaowen.
On the last day of April, Wang Mang's daughter was made queen and a general amnesty was announced.
Eight people including Da Situ Sizhi, Chen Chong and others were dispatched to various parts of the country to inspect social customs.
summary: Wang Mang's son Wang Yu, fearing Emperor Ping's resentment, conspired with his teacher Wu Zhang and brother-in-law Lu Kuan to smear Wang Mang's mansion with blood to frighten him. Wang Mang arrested Wang Yu, who drank poison and died. Wang Mang killed Wang Yu's wife after she gave birth and used the incident to kill the Wei family and others, implicating many counties and feudal states. Hundreds of people died, shocking the world. Chen Zuo, the Grand Sima Hujun, praised Wang Mang for punishing his son like the Duke of Zhou. The ministers requested that Wang Mang's admonitions be distributed and treated like the "Book of Filial Piety." In the spring of the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, people worshiped heaven and offered sacrifices to Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Xiaowen. Wang Mang's daughter was made queen, and a general amnesty was announced. Eight officials were dispatched to inspect social customs. Taibao Wang Shun and others reported that Wang Mang's merits should be rewarded like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. The ministers requested that Wang Mang be given the title of prime minister, ranking above the three dukes, with various honors and rewards.

translation:
Kirin, phoenix, turtle, yellow dragon and many other auspicious omens appeared more than 700 times.
Therefore, he formulated ritual systems, created music and teachings, and made great contributions to the stability of the country.
All the hopes of the whole world are pinned on you. You are the prime minister, and your title is the same as that of the Grand Duke.
The reward given to Jiuxi now should be used to participate in sacrifices and appoint hundreds of civil and military officials. The honor you have received will finally bring glory to your ancestors. Wow, isn't it beautiful?
So Wang Mang kowtowed again and accepted the green apron, formal dress, top hat and daily clothes, the jade-inlaid saber, the boots with different heads, the chariot with bells and four horses, the dragon flag with nine bunches of tape as decoration, the leather military crown and white war robe, and the military chariot. There are four war horses, a red bow and a black bow and arrow. There is a red ax and iron on the left side of the palace gate and a golden ax and iron on the right. There is a collar for each armor, two coins of fragrant wine, two jade spoons, and two nine-life sapphire gui that symbolizes the highest-ranking officials. It is allowed to install a red painted door and build steps inside the eaves.
There were set up Zongguan, Zhuguan, Buguan, and Shiguan, with 300 Huben officials. There was one family magistrate and family minister each. Zongguan, Zhu, Buguan, Shiguan and other officials were all appointed to assist Anhan Gong.
In government offices and private residences, tiger warriors served as doormen, and those who wanted to enter and exit had to be registered.
Starting from Si Fu and San Gong, if you want to enter the official office or house for something, you must use the command talisman.
The official residence of the King of Chu in Beijing was used as the residence of Duke Anhan, and it was greatly repaired and renovated to make it accessible to the surrounding guards.
Both ancestral sacrificial temples and dormitory temples can install red painted doors and create steps within the eaves.
Su Chong reported again: When Duke Anhan went out from the city gate to offer sacrifices to his ancestors, the captain of the city gate should send knights to follow him.
When you enter the city, you are protected by guards, and when you leave the city, you are followed by knights. This is to respect the country.
The memorial was approved.
In the autumn of this year, Wang Mang dug the Ziwu Road because his daughter, Queen Wang, had an auspicious sign of giving birth.
The Ziwu Road starts from Duling, crosses Zhongnan Mountain, and reaches Hanzhong.
Eight custom envoys came back and said that the customs of the world were uniform. They forged folk songs and folk songs of each county and feudal state to praise virtues, a total of 30,000 words.
Wang Mang reported it to the public and clearly recorded it in the documents.
He also reported that everything in the market has a second price, there are no lawsuits in the government, there are no thieves in the city, there are no hungry people in the suburbs, people do not pick up people on the road, and the system of men and women not walking together is implemented, and violators only receive symbolic punishment.
Twelve people including Liu Xin and Chen Chong were all granted the title of marquis for building Mingtang and promoting enlightenment.
Wang Mang has achieved peace, the north has influenced the Xiongnu, the east has attracted overseas countries, and the south has embraced the Huangzhi, but only the west has not been affected.
He sent Zhonglang, General Hu Xian and others to bring many gold and silver treasures to attract the Qiang people outside the Great Wall, and asked them to donate their land and express their willingness to belong to the Han Dynasty.
summary: In the autumn, Wang Mang dug the Ziwu Road due to an auspicious sign from his daughter, Queen Wang. Eight custom envoys returned, reporting that the customs of the world were uniform and forging folk songs praising virtues. Wang Mang reported this and recorded it in documents. He also reported that there were no lawsuits, thieves, or hungry people, and the system of men and women not walking together was implemented. Twelve people, including Liu Xin and Chen Chong, were granted the title of marquis for building the Mingtang. Wang Mang sent envoys to attract the Qiang people, who offered their land to become subjects. Wang Mang proposed establishing Xihai County and revising state names and boundaries. The memorial was approved, and fifty additional laws were added, with violators exiled to Xihai County. The people became resentful. Liu Qing, Marquis of Quanling, wrote a letter suggesting Wang Mang act as regent like the Duke of Zhou. The ministers agreed. When Emperor Ping fell ill, Wang Mang prayed for his safety and offered to sacrifice his own life. Emperor Ping died, and Wang Mang recruited scholars to participate in the decision to mourn for three years. He selected Liu Ying, a two-year-old great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan, as the successor.

translation:
The official office of Lord Anhan was called the Regency, the official office was the Regent Palace, and the residence was the Regent Palace.
The memorial was approved.
Wang Mang reported to the Empress Dowager Ming and issued an edict saying: Although the former Grand Master Kong Guang has passed away, his achievements have been arranged.
Taibao Wang Shun, Grand Sikong Zhenfeng, Qingchao General Zhen Han, and Infantry General Sun Jian all made suggestions for the recruitment of Chanyu. They also presided over the construction of a spiritual platform for observing the sky, a Mingtang for grand ceremonies, a central imperial school, and altars in the suburbs. They established systems and opened the Ziwu Road. They worked together with the Prime Minister and made outstanding contributions.
Wang Kuang, the son of Wang Shun, was granted the title of Tongxinhou, Wang Lin was granted the title of Shuodehou, Kongguang's grandson Jieshou was granted the title of Heyihou, and Zhenfeng's grandson Zhenkuang was granted the title of Binglihou.
Zhen Han and Sun Jian were given additional 3,000 households each.
This year, Pang Tian, ​​Fu Fan and others of the Xiqiang people resented Wang Mang for taking away their land as Xihai County, so they counterattacked Cheng Yong, the prefect of Xihai County, and Cheng Yong fled.
Wang Mang killed Cheng Yong and sent the captain to protect the Qiang to attack the Western Qiang.
In the spring of the second year, Dou Kuang and others defeated the Xiqiang.
In May, new currencies were minted: Wrong knives, each worth 5,000 yen; deed knives, worth 500 yen each; large coins, worth 50 yen each, and circulated at the same time as the five baht coins.
There are many people in the private sector who mint currency privately.
Therefore, a ban was issued on people from the princes down to the princes to not carry gold privately. Those who handed it over to the imperial palace could get the same price, but those who handed over the gold never got the coins of the same price.
In September, Zhai Yi, the prefect of Dongjun, took advantage of the day of the general test of knights. He assembled chariots and cavalry, mobilized emergency troops, and elected Liu Xin, Marquis of Yanxiang, as emperor. He sent a message to all counties and feudal states, accusing Wang Mang of poisoning Emperor Ping to death. He acted as emperor and wanted to cut off the Han Dynasty. Now I am ordered by heaven to attack Wang Mang.
The counties and feudal states were shaken, and Zhai Yi's army numbered more than 100,000.
Wang Mang was so frightened that he couldn't eat. He carried the boy to the suburbs and prayed at the ancestral temple day and night, imitating the "Book of Zhou". "Da Gao" wrote a policy book and sent Huan Tan and others to admonish the emperor to announce his intention to act as the emperor and return the power to Ruzi in the future.
Eight generals including Wang Yi and Sun Jian were sent to attack Zhai Yi and stationed at various passes to guard dangerous places.
Tang Ming, Huo Hong and others from Huaili County raised troops to respond to Zhai Yi and conspired with each other: "The generals and elite troops have been sent away, and the capital is empty. We can attack Chang'an."
The army gradually increased and grew to nearly 100,000 people. Wang Mang was afraid and sent generals Wang Qi and Wang Ji to lead their troops to resist them.
He appointed Taibao Zhen Han as the general, awarded him an ax and iron in Gaodi Temple, and led the army of the whole country, holding a knot in his left hand and an ax and cymbal in his right hand, stationed outside the city of Chang'an.
Wang Shun and Zhen Feng patrolled the palace day and night.
In December, Wang Yi and other generals defeated Zhai Yi in Yu County.
summary: In the spring of the second year, new currencies were minted, and a ban was issued on carrying gold privately. In September, Zhai Yi, the prefect of Dongjun, raised troops and elected Liu Xin as emperor, accusing Wang Mang of poisoning Emperor Ping. Wang Mang was frightened and sent eight generals to attack Zhai Yi. Tang Ming and Huo Hong also raised troops to respond, growing to nearly 100,000 people. Wang Mang sent generals to resist them and appointed Zhen Han as the general. In December, Wang Yi and other generals defeated Zhai Yi. Chen Chong wrote a memorial praising Wang Mang's wisdom. Wang Mang was very happy. In the spring of three years, an earthquake occurred, and Wang Mang announced a general amnesty. Wang Yi and others defeated Ming Dynasty and Huo Hong. Wang Mang held a banquet to reward the generals and wrote a memorial suggesting that the Zhou system be followed for titles and fiefs. The memorial was approved, and several hundred people were granted titles. The ministers reported that Wang Mang's sons should be promoted to the title of Duke. The Queen Mother agreed, and Wang An and Wang Lin were made dukes. Wang Guang was granted the title of Yan Gonghou. Wang Mang then planned to ascend to the true throne.

translation:
Siwei Chen Chong reported that Yan Gong Hou Wang Guang privately told Zhi Jinwu Shi Ji and taught him to kill for him. Shi Ji arrested the man and sentenced him to death and beheading.
Wang Mang was furious and scolded Wang Guang severely.
Wang Guang's mother said: Which one do you think is closer to Wang Yu or Wang Huozhong?
The mother and son committed suicide as a result, and even the real person died.
At first, Wang Mang gained a good reputation by serving his mother, supporting his widowed sister-in-law, and raising his nephew. Later, when he became arrogant and cruel, he used this to show his fairness and selflessness.
Let Wang Guang's son Wang Jia inherit the title and become Ding Yangonghou.
Wang Mang wrote a letter saying: The rule prohibiting playing music will end at the end of the twelfth lunar month of this year, and all musical instruments can be played during the first lunar month of next year to offer sacrifices to heaven and earth.
What are the grades of music used by princes, kings, princes, ministers, and scholar-bureaucrats?
Five tones and eight tones, what is each one?
You and the Confucian scholars you belong to should try your best to think about them and state their meaning in detail.
In this year, Liu Jing, the Marquis of Guangrao, Hu Yun, the general of chariots and cavalry, and Zang Hong, the Taibao officer, reported their orders.
Liu Jing said that a new well suddenly appeared in Qi County, Hu Yun said that a stone cow was found in Ba County, and Zang Hong said that an immortal stone was found in Yong County, Fufeng. Wang Mang readily accepted it.
On Jiazi Day in November, Wang Mang wrote a memorial to the Queen Mother:
Your Majesty is the most sage and wise. When the royal family was in adversity, faced with the dangerous fate of the 12th generation of the Han Dynasty for 210 years, and accepting the majestic order of heaven, he ordered Wang Mang to serve as regent, act on behalf of the emperor, accept the commission of Fu Ruzi, and shoulder the great hope of the world.
The minister Wang Mang works hard, fearing that he will be incompetent.
Liu Jing, Marquis of Guangrao in the royal family, wrote to him: In mid-July, Xin Dang, the head of Changxing Pavilion in Linzi County, Qi County, had several dreams one night. He dreamed that someone said to him: I am the messenger of the Emperor of Heaven.
The Emperor of Heaven sent me to tell the pavilion chief: The acting emperor should become the real emperor.
If you don't believe me, a new well will appear in this pavilion.
The director of the pavilion got up in the morning and looked at the pavilion. There was indeed a new well, which was nearly a hundred feet underground. On Renzi day in November, when Jianchen met the winter solstice, the stone oxen from Bajun, Wuwu day, and Yong's stone inscriptions were all sent to the front hall of Weiyang Palace.
I went to watch with Tai Baoyang Marquis Wang Shun and others. Suddenly there was a strong wind in the sky, dust was flying, and the sky was dark. When the wind stopped, I saw a copper talisman letter and pictures and characters written on silk in front of the two stones. The content was: God notified the emperor of the talisman's fate, and the person who presented it could be made a marquis.
Accept destiny and carry out divine orders.
Cavalry Captain Cui Fa and others read the full text and explained its meaning.
In the past, Emperor Xiaoai issued an edict on Jiazi in June of the second year of Jianping, changing it to the first year of Taichu Yuanjiang. To examine the process of Emperor Xiaoai's change to Yuan Dynasty, Gan Zhongke and Xia Heliang's mysterious prophecies and omens were hidden in Lantai.
summary: In September, Wang Mang's mother died. Instead of expressing grief, Wang Mang asked the Queen Mother to discuss his mourning clothes. The doctors and Confucian scholars said that the regent should not wear mourning clothes for his biological mother. Wang Mang implemented their suggestion. Chen Chong reported that Wang Guang had privately told Zhi Jinwu Shi Ji to kill for him. Wang Mang was furious, and Wang Guang and his mother committed suicide. Wang Mang wrote a letter about the prohibition of playing music and asked about the grades of music. In this year, Liu Jing, Hu Yun, and Zang Hong reported auspicious omens. Wang Mang readily accepted them. On Jiazi day in November, Wang Mang wrote a memorial to the Queen Mother, citing various omens and requesting to be called the "false emperor" and to change the calendar. The memorial was approved. The common people learned of his belief in the talisman, and the ministers discussed it widely. Aizhang, a native of Zitong County, made a copper cabinet with inscriptions claiming Wang Mang was the true emperor. Wang Mang went to the Gaodi Temple to receive the copper cabinet, wore the crown, and ascended the throne as the True Dragon Emperor. He declared a new country, changed the calendar, and set the colors of carriages, horses, and clothing to yellow.

translation:
In May of the fourth year, Wang Mang said: "Baocheng's masters and friends offered wine to Tang Lin and Yuan Jianyi to offer wine to Langye County. He was a man of discipline, filial to his parents, respectful to his elder brothers, loyal to things, benevolent to others, respectful of the court, and caring for the people. He was widely familiar with ancient books, and his virtues were pure and perfect until he was old, without any fault."
Lu Ta was granted the title of Jianshan Fortress, and Xian Zhi was granted the title of Dehou. They were both given the rank of special advance. The etiquette for receiving them was the same as meeting the three princes.
He was rewarded with a big house, three million in money, and the treatment of a pen and a cane.
In June, he again awarded the thatched soil that symbolized the feudal state to the princes in the Mingtang, saying: I planned the land system and the five feudal princes according to the text of the classics, in line with the explanations of the classics, and through the principles of the classics. After thinking and discussing again and again, it has been almost nine years since the first year of the founding of the country, and it was officially finalized today.
I personally set up the aragonite steps, displayed jingmao and four-color soil, prayed respectfully to Mount Tai, the national clan, the God of the Earth and my ancestors, and then conferred it.
Each returned to his own feudal state to educate and discipline the people in order to establish meritorious deeds.
Those princes in the border areas or in the Jiangnan area, although they were not summoned by Shaoling but were sent to the capital to serve the emperor, Na Yan was in charge of the goods and the money in the capital was allocated to distribute their salaries. The duke was 800,000 yuan per year, the marquis and earl were 400,000 yuan per year, and the viscount and baron were 200,000 yuan per year.
Still can't quite get it though.
Wang Mang liked to talk empty words, envied the ancient system, and often granted titles to people. His character was actually stingy, and he used the undetermined land plan as an excuse, so he first granted the title of thatched land to symbolize the feudal state to comfort those who liked the title.
This year, six financial and economic management systems were reaffirmed.
Every time a management system is issued, laws and regulations must be set up to prevent it. Those who violate it may even be executed for the most serious crimes. Officials and civilians are punished for more crimes.
He also levied a tax on all those who kept slaves and slaves, each slave had to pay 3,600 yuan. The people of the world became more resentful and thieves rose up.
Nayan and Feng Chang advised him on the six management systems. Wang Mang was furious and removed Feng Chang from his official position.
Set up law enforcement on the left and law enforcement on the right.
Select capable officials, Hou Baren, to supervise the Sixth Lieutenant and the Sixth Team respectively. Their powers are like the governors of the Han Dynasty, and they will accompany one person from each county to handle relevant matters.
Guatianyi and others from Linhuai County acted as thieves and occupied Changzhouyuan, the capital of Kuaiji County. Lu Mu, a woman from Langxie County, also started to rebel.
At first, Lu's mother's son was a county official and was unjustly killed by the county magistrate.
Lu's mother used her family's property to buy wine, meat, and weapons. She secretly treated poor young men and gained more than a hundred people, then attacked Haiqu County, killed the county magistrate and went to worship her son's grave.
Then she led her troops to the sea, and her team gradually grew, eventually totaling tens of thousands of people.
summary: In the fourth year of his reign, Wang Mang granted titles and rewards to several officials, including Lu Ta and Xian Zhi, who received the rank of special advance and were treated with the same etiquette as the three princes. He also awarded them houses, money, and ceremonial items. In June, he formally enfeoffed princes at the Mingtang, claiming he had spent nearly nine years planning the land system and feudal hierarchy based on classical texts. However, Wang Mang was known for his empty rhetoric and stinginess, using the undetermined land plan as an excuse to delay actual implementation while granting symbolic titles to appease those who desired rank. Wang Mang reaffirmed six financial management systems, establishing harsh laws with punishments including execution for violations. He levied taxes on slave owners, requiring 3,600 yuan per slave, which caused widespread resentment and led to the rise of bandits. When officials like Nayan and Feng Chang advised against these policies, Wang Mang removed them from office. He appointed law enforcement officers with powers similar to Han dynasty governors to supervise the six systems. Rebellions erupted across the country, including Guatianyi's occupation of Changzhouyuan and Lu Mu's uprising in Langxie County, where a woman whose son was unjustly killed by a county magistrate gathered followers, attacked Haiqu County, and eventually commanded tens of thousands of troops.

translation:
Wang Mang sent an envoy to pardon the thieves on the spot. The envoy came back and said: The thieves dispersed and often reunited again.
When asked about the reason, they all said that they were unable to take action because of the cumbersome and strict prohibitions.
The income from hard work is not enough to pay taxes.
If you keep the door closed and stay safe, you will be implicated by your neighbors who secretly mint money and hide copper, and the traitors will use it to blackmail the people.
The people had no choice but to turn into thieves.
Wang Mang was furious and removed them from their official positions.
Some of them followed his intention and said that the rebellious people were arrogant and cunning and should be punished. They also said that the fate of the people was like this and they would soon be eliminated. Wang Mang was happy and always promoted them.
In August of this year, Wang Mang personally went to the southern suburbs to create a powerful force.
Weidou was made of copper mixed with five-color stones. It was shaped like a Big Dipper and was two feet and five inches long. It was intended to be used to intimidate various peasant armies.
The mighty battle was forged, and Siming was asked to carry it. When Wang Mang went out, it was in front of him, and when Wang Mang entered the palace, he put it next to him.
On the day when Wei Dou was cast, the weather was extremely cold, and hundreds of officials and horses froze to death.
On the first day of the first lunar month of the fifth year, a fire broke out at the south gate of the Northern Army camp.
The Grand Sima Sima Yun Fei Xing was appointed as the shepherd of Jingzhou. Wang Mang met him and asked him about his plans after taking office. Fei Xing replied: Most of the people in Jingzhou and Yangzhou rely on the mountains, forests and lakes, and use fishing and woodcutting as their occupations.
Some time ago, the country implemented the six-management system and levied taxes on mountains, forests, lakes and swamps, which harmed and deprived the people of their interests. Coupled with successive years of drought, the people were hungry and poor, so they became thieves.
After I arrived at my post, I wanted to order the thieves to return home, loan them farm tools, cattle, seeds, and grain, and reduce or exempt them from taxes, hoping to disband and appease them.
Wang Mang became angry and dismissed Fei Xing from his official position.
Officials all over the country sought illegal profits one after another because they could not get their salaries. The property of the county chiefs and governors accumulated thousands of gold.
Wang Mang wrote a letter to Shao saying: After a thorough investigation of the Huns' invasion of the Central Plains in the second year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, all military officers and border officials who have made illegal profits and increased their property and made a fortune will have four-fifths of their family property confiscated to support the urgent needs of border defense.
Government officials traveled all over the country in carriages, carefully examining corruption cases, mobilizing officers to report on their generals, and slaves to report on their masters. They hoped to use this method to suppress evil, but the evil became more and more serious.
The emperor's grandson Gong Chonggong Wang Zong drew a portrait of himself, wearing the emperor's clothes and the emperor's crown, and engraved three seals: the first is "Wei Zhi Guan, Cun Ji Xia, Nanshan, Hidden by Thin Ice", the second is "Su Sheng Bao Ji", and the third is "De Feng Chang Tu".
summary: Wang Mang's envoys reported that thieves dispersed but regrouped due to harsh prohibitions, heavy taxes, and the inability of people to make a living. Wang Mang dismissed officials who reported these truths and promoted those who flattered him. In August, he forged a copper weapon shaped like the Big Dipper to intimidate peasant armies, but during its casting, extreme cold killed many officials and horses. Fires broke out at the Northern Army camp, and when newly appointed officials like Fei Xing suggested lenient policies to address the root causes of rebellion, Wang Mang dismissed them. Officials across the country sought illegal profits due to unpaid salaries, amassing fortunes.

translation:
In addition, Wang Zong's uncle Lu Kuan's family was exiled to Hepu County, and he secretly contacted Wang Zong. After being discovered, Wang Zong committed suicide after investigation and verification.
Wang Mang said: Wang Zong's kinship is that of the emperor's grandson, and his title is that of Grand Duke. He knew that Lu Kuan and others were rebels, so he tried to associate with them. He engraved three steel seals. The meaning of the seals is very sneaky, not satisfied, and coveting undue hope.
The principle of "Spring and Autumn" is that you should not have any evil thoughts towards the king and your parents, and if you have evil thoughts, you should punish them.
I was so confused that I deviated from the right path. I committed such a crime. How sad!
Wang Zong was originally named Wang Huizong. Because the system stipulated that double names should be abolished, the original name is now restored to Wang Huizong.
He devalued his title, changed his name, gave him the title of Gong Chong Miao Bo, and buried him in Gucheng County, his original feudal state, according to the etiquette of an earl.
Wang Zong's sister Wang Zhi was the wife of General Wang Xing. She prayed to ghosts and gods to bring disaster to her mother-in-law and killed her maid in order to silence her.
Finally, when the incident was discovered, Wang Mang asked the official Zhongchang to question Wang Zhi and blame Wang Xing for the incident. Both Wang Zhi and Wang Xing committed suicide.
The incident involved Si Ming Kong Ren's wife, who also committed suicide.
When Kong Ren saw Wang Mang, he took off his hat to plead guilty. Wang Mang asked the minister to impeach Kong Ren: He was sitting in a cart with astronomical images and a mare, with the green dragon symbol on the left, the white tiger symbol on the right, the bird symbol in the front, and the turtle symbol in the back. He held the Five Power Festival in his right hand and the Mighty Dou on his left shoulder. The title was called Red Star. These were not used to let Kong Ren do whatever he wanted, but to respect the majestic orders of the new dynasty.
Kong Ren took off the astronomical crown without authorization, which was a crime of disrespecting the emperor.
Wang Mang issued another edict instructing him not to impeach him, but to replace him with a new hat.
He's moody like this.
Appoint Zhidaohou Wangshe as the general of the guard.
Wang She is the son of Quyanghou Wanggen.
Wang Gen served as Chief Sima during the reign of Emperor Cheng and once recommended Wang Mang to succeed him. Wang Mang was grateful to him and thought that Quyang was not a good name, so he followed Wang Gen as Zhidao and let Wang She inherit his title.
This year, the Red Eyebrow Army Li Zidu, Fan Chong and others gathered together due to famine, and started an uprising in Langxie County. They looted everywhere, with a total of ten thousand troops.
Wang Mang sent envoys to mobilize local troops to attack them, but they could not win.
In the spring of the sixth year, Wang Mang saw that there were many thieves, so he asked Taishi to calculate the outline of the calendar for 36,000 years. He changed the year name every six years and announced it to the whole country.
The following report says: "Purple He Tu" says: Taiyi and Huangdi both became gods and ascended to heaven, playing fairy music on Qianshan Mountain in Kunlun Mountains.
The wise emperors whose descendants have gained auspiciousness should play fairy music on Zhongnan Mountain in Qin.
I wasn't smart enough to follow it consciously, and I didn't understand it until now.
Then General Ningshi was called General Gengshi. It means obeying the destiny.
Didn't the "Book of Changes" say it? It is said that renewal is excellent moral character. In the process of movement and change, new things are constantly produced, which is called Yi.
I will enjoy this happiness!
summary: Wang Mang's grandson Wang Zong was discovered drawing himself in imperial regalia and engraving seals with rebellious inscriptions. After investigation, Wang Zong committed suicide, and his sister Wang Zhi also died after being implicated in murder and witchcraft. The Red Eyebrow Army, led by Li Zidu and Fan Chong, began their uprising in Langxie County due to famine, gathering ten thousand troops. Wang Mang's attempts to suppress them failed. In the sixth year, Wang Mang calculated a 36,000-year calendar and changed the year name, claiming to follow divine instructions, but people laughed at these practices.

translation:
I want to use this method to dazzle the people and eliminate thieves.
Everyone laughed at these practices.
For the first time, he presented "Xin Yue" to Mingtang and Ancestral Temple.
Ministers began to wear buckskin hats.
Someone heard the melody of the music and said: It is sad, serious and low, not the music to revitalize the country.
At this time, the Kanto region suffered from drought and famine for several consecutive years, and the number of tribes such as Lizidu gradually increased. Gengshi general Lian Dan failed to win in Yizhou and was recalled.
After the restoration, he sent Guo Xing, the Great Sima Protector, and Li Bi, the Yongbu Mu Li Bi, to attack the tribal leader Ruodou and others, and sent Taifu Xishu Shi Sun Xi to pacify the thieves in various places.
At the same time, the Xiongnu invaded the border very severely.
Wang Mang then recruited a large number of strong men from all over the country, as well as condemned criminals and domestic slaves of officials and civilians. He named them Zhutu Xiyong and used them as elite soldiers.
All fees were collected from officials and civilians across the country, one-thirtieth of the estimated property was taken, and all silk and silk were transported to Chang'an.
Officials from the ministerial level to the county officials wearing yellow seals were ordered to maintain military horses. The number of horses was determined according to each person's salary.
He also extensively recruited specialized talents who had unique skills that could be used to attack the Xiongnu, and planned to hire them by upgrading their positions.
There are tens of thousands of people who suggest things that are beneficial to the country: some say that you can cross rivers without boats and connect people and horses, and you can cross an army of millions; some say that you don’t need to carry a bucket of grain, but just take medicine, and the army will not be hungry; some say that you can fly, flying a thousand miles a day, to spy on the Huns.
Wang Mang asked him to try it. The man made two wings from the feathers of a big bird, attached feathers to his head and body, and wrapped them with ring ties all over his body. After flying a few hundred steps, they fell off.
Wang Mang knew that they could not be used, so he insisted on gaining the reputation of cherishing talents, so he appointed them all as commanders, rewarded them with chariots and horses, and waited for their departure.
At the beginning, the right bone of the Xiongnu was Hou Xudang, and his wife was the daughter of Wang Zhaojun, who had returned to the Central Plains.
Wang Mang sent Wang Zhaojun's nephew and prince Wang She to lure Xu Budang to the border, coerced him to come to Chang'an, and forced him to be the Duke of Xu Bushan Hou'an.
At first Wang Mang wanted to seduce Xubutang, but Grand Sima Yanyou advised: Xubutang is on the right side of the Xiongnu. His army has never invaded the border and always tells the Central Plains news about Chanyu. This is a huge help.
Now we welcome Subudang to Chang'an East Street. He is just a Huns. It is better to let him stay with the Huns.
Wang Mang didn't listen.
Xu Bu Dang has been brought here, and he wants to send Yan You and Lian Dan to attack the Xiongnu. They are both given the surname Zheng and are called the Second Zheng General. They want to kill Shan Yu Yu and set up Xu Dang to replace him.
They sent troops to West Malan of Chang'an City but did not set off.
Yan You, who had always been resourceful and talented, opposed Wang Mang's attack on foreigners in the West. Wang Mang did not listen to his repeated advice, so he wrote three articles about the historical lessons of the distrust of ancient famous generals Le Yi and Bai Qi, and about border defense matters, and submitted them to Wang Mang in a tactful and tortuous way.
When the court meeting was held, Yan You firmly stated that the Xiongnu could put their power aside and worry about the thieves in Shandong first.
Wang Mang was furious and wrote a policy letter to Yan You, saying: You have been in office for four years. The foreign tribes that disturbed the Central Plains cannot be suppressed. The thieves and evil spirits cannot be eradicated. You are not afraid of the majesty of heaven and do not obey the emperor's orders. You are vicious in appearance and think you are kind in vain. You are stubborn and unchangeable. You have second thoughts and destroy military plans.
I can't bear to hand it over to the judicial department. I should hand over the seal of Grand Sima Wu Jianbo and return to my hometown.
Dong Zhong, the descendant of Fu Bo, was appointed as the Grand Sima.
The Yiping County Company led the field report to the county. The county's estimate of the people's property was untrue, and Wang Mang levied it at one-thirtieth.
Thinking that Tian Kuang was loyal and caring about the country, he promoted his title to earl and rewarded him with two million yuan.
summary: The Kanto region suffered from drought and famine for consecutive years, causing rebel numbers to grow. Wang Mang recruited strong men, condemned criminals, and slaves to form elite troops, collecting one-thirtieth of property from officials and civilians to fund military campaigns. He also recruited specialists with unique skills to attack the Xiongnu, including a man who claimed to be able to fly but only managed a few hundred steps before falling. Wang Mang appointed them all as commanders despite knowing their claims were false.

translation:
The general public cursed him.
Many people in Qingzhou and Xuzhou abandoned their homes and fled. The old and weak died on the road, while the strong joined the ranks of thieves.
Suye Junlian led Han Bo to report: A strange man, ten feet tall and ten feet tall, came to my palace and said he wanted to fight against the Xiongnu.
He said his name was Juwuba, and he grew up in Zhaoru, southeast of Penglai and northwest of Wucheng. He could not fit in a light vehicle and could not be dragged by three horses.
Immediately, he hitched four horses to a large cart, set up a tiger flag, and loaded up the giant horse to come to the capital.
Juwuba sleeps with his head resting on a pillow and eats with iron chopsticks. This is God asking him to assist the new dynasty.
I hope you will build a large armored chariot, a suit of clothes worn by Meng Ben and Xia Yu, and send a general and a hundred warriors to meet him on the road.
If the gates of the capital cannot accommodate him, open them higher and wider, and show him to the foreign tribes, so that he can intimidate and stabilize the world.
Han Bo wanted to use it to ridicule Wang Mang.
Wang Mang heard this and resented Han Bo. He asked Ju Guuba to stay in Xinfeng County where he was located, and changed his surname to Ju Mu, which meant that thanks to the birth of this person, Queen Mother Wen, this was the destiny that made him the overlord.
Put Han Bo in jail, thinking that those words were not what he should say, and put him to death.
In the second year, the year name was changed to Emperor of the Earth, which was based on the outline of the 36,000-year calendar.
On the last day of the first lunar month of the first year of the Earth Emperor's reign, a nationwide amnesty was announced.
The following report said: When the troops are marching, anyone who dares to run around and make noise and violate the law will be beheaded. Do not wait until the execution season. This order will be implemented until the end of the year.
So in the spring and summer, people were killed in the city, and the people were terrified. When they met on the road, they only looked at each other and did not dare to talk.
On Renshen Day in February, the sky was dark when the sun was at its peak.
Wang Mang hated this phenomenon and reported below: Some time ago, there was darkness, the Yin energy invaded the Yang energy, and the black energy caused disasters. The people were all surprised.
Wang Kuang, the general of Zhaoyu, sent his subordinates to pursue the person who reported the abnormal accident in order to cover up the emperor's ears and eyes. Therefore, he was condemned from heaven and should be punished by law to remedy such a catastrophe.
Wang Mang saw that there were many thieves from all directions, and wanted to deter them again, so he sent a message: My great emperor Huangdi brought peace to the world. He led his army as a general, erected gorgeous chariot covers, and set up Beidou-shaped ritual vessels. He set up generals in the base camp, and set up five generals outside the camp, twenty-five generals, and one hundred and twenty-five partial generals. , there are 1,250 generals, 12,500 lieutenants, 37,500 commanders, 112,500 military commanders, 225,000 chiefs, 450,000 palace officials, and 13.5 million soldiers, which is consistent with what the "Book of Changes" says Bows and arrows are sharp, used to intimidate the world.
I accepted the words of the talisman, followed the ancients, and planned to gradually set it up.
summary: Wang Mang's policies led to widespread suffering. People abandoned their homes, the old and weak died on roadsides, and the strong joined thieves. Officials like Han Bo tried to ridicule Wang Mang with absurd reports, but Wang Mang executed them. He changed the year name to Emperor of the Earth and issued harsh decrees allowing executions even in spring and summer, terrifying the people. When natural disasters occurred, Wang Mang blamed his officials rather than his own policies.

translation:
Wang Mang's Yangzhou shepherd Li Sheng and his commander Kong Ren were defeated in the Shandong area. Li Sheng died in a fight, and Kong Ren led his troops to surrender. Then he sighed and said: I heard that if you enjoy someone's salary, you have to die for his cause.
Then he drew his sword and committed suicide.
Du Pu, the eunuch of Cao's Ministry, Shen Yi, the great Yin of Chending County, and Jia Meng, the leader of Jiujiang County Company, all defended the county and refused to surrender, so they were killed by the Han army.
Wang Qin and Guo Qin, the great Yins of Shangdu County, were guarding the capital warehouse. When they heard that Wang Mang was dead, they surrendered. Emperor Gengshi believed that they had upheld integrity and granted them the title of marquis.
Taishi Wang Kuang and General Aizhang surrendered in Luoyang and were sent to Wancheng to kill them.
After Yan You and Chen Mao were beaten at the foot of Kunyang City, they fled to Qiao County, Pei County. They claimed to be generals of the Desert Army and called a gathering of local officials and civilians.
Yan You preached to them about Wang Mang's theft of the throne, God's will to destroy him, and the revival of the wise Han Dynasty. Chen Mao fell to the ground and cried.
Hearing that Liu Sheng, the former Zhongwu Marquis of the Han Dynasty, gathered his troops in Runan County and claimed to be emperor, Yan You and Chen Mao surrendered to him.
Liu Sheng appointed Yan You as Grand Sima and Chen Mao as Prime Minister.
They failed for more than ten days, and both Yan You and Chen Mao died.
All counties and counties surrendered, and the whole country returned to the rule of the Han Dynasty.
Earlier, Shentu Jian had followed Cui Fa to study the Book of Songs. When Shentu Jian came to Chang'an, Cui Fa surrendered to him.
Later, he promoted Wang Mang's replacement of the Han Dynasty, and Shentu Jian asked Prime Minister Liu Ci to kill Cui Fa to show the public.
Shi Chen, Wang Yan, Wang Lin, Wang Wu and Zhao Hong also surrendered and were killed.
At first, everyone in the troops who established their own names wanted to be granted the title of marquis.
Shen Tujian had not only killed Wang Xian, but also threatened that the people in the Sanfu area were cunning and killed his monarch together. Therefore, the officials and civilians in the Sanfu area became frightened, and the counties under their jurisdiction gathered troops to separate themselves. Shen Tujian and others failed to capture it, so they sent flying horses to report to Gengshi Emperor.
In February of the second year of Gengshi, Emperor Gengshi came to Chang'an and issued an edict announcing a general amnesty. As long as they were not Wang Mang's children, everyone else would be pardoned for their crimes, so the Wang family could be preserved.
All the Sanfu areas were pacified, and Emperor Gengshi made his capital Chang'an and lived in Changle Palace.
The treasury was intact, except for the Weiyang palace fire that attacked Wang Mang for three days. Once Wang Mang died, he settled down and returned to his original state.
After the arrival of Emperor Gengshi, it took more than a year for the political education to be implemented throughout the country.
In the summer of the next year, hundreds of thousands of people from the Red Eyebrow Army, Fan Chong and others entered Hangu Pass, supported Liu Penzi as emperor, and attacked Emperor Gengshi, who surrendered to them.
The Red Eyebrow Army burned the palaces and streets of Chang'an and killed Emperor Gengshi.
The people were starving to the point of cannibalism, and hundreds of thousands of people died. The city of Chang'an was in ruins, and no one walked in the city.
All the ancestral temples and tombs of the ancestors of the Han Dynasty have been excavated, but only Du Ling and Ba Ling are still intact.
summary: The rebellion continued to spread, with various leaders emerging across the country. Wang Mang's attempts to suppress them through military force and harsh laws only worsened the situation. His officials grew increasingly fearful, and the people's suffering intensified. The Han dynasty eventually revived under Emperor Gengshi, who captured Chang'an and executed Wang Mang's supporters. The Red Eyebrow Army later overthrew Emperor Gengshi, causing further destruction, until Emperor Shizu restored order and peace to the realm.

translation:
On the first day of the first lunar month of the first year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Wang Mang led the princes and ministers to hold the newly made Imperial Seal of the Empress Dowager and presented it to the Empress Dowager. In compliance with the order, the name of the Han Dynasty was removed.
It turned out that Wang Mang married the daughter of the Wang family of the Marquis of Yichun and made her his queen.
She originally gave birth to four sons: Wang Zi, Wang Huo, Wang An, and Wang Lin.
Two of his sons had been executed earlier. Wang An looked a little confused, so he made Wang Lin the crown prince and Wang An the new Jiapi.
There are six sons who are given the title of king: Wang Qian is Gonglong Gong, Wang Shou is Gongming Gong, Wang Ji is Gongchenggong, Wang Zong is Gongchong Gong, Wang Shi is Gongzhao Gong, and Wang Li is Gongzhu Gong.
An amnesty was announced for the whole world.
Wang Mang then wrote a policy letter and ordered the boy to say: Alas! You Liu Ying, the ancestor who was helped by heaven in the past, has been passed down for twelve generations and has enjoyed state power for two hundred and ten years. It is my turn according to destiny.
Didn’t it say so in the Book of Songs? The descendants of the Yin Dynasty became princes and surrendered to the Zhou Dynasty. It can be seen that destiny is not certain. I will grant you the title of Ding'an Gong and always be the guest of the new dynasty.
Ouch!
You must be grateful to God for his kindness, go and take your place, and do not disobey my orders.
He also said: Pingyuan County, Ande County, Luoyin County, Li County and Chongqiu County, with a total of 10,000 households and a land of 100 miles each, should be regarded as the Ding'an Principality.
Build an ancestral temple of the Han Dynasty ancestors in your feudal state, and treat it equally with the descendants of the Zhou Dynasty. You can use your own calendar and the colors of your carriages, horses, and clothing.
Serve your ancestors from generation to generation, always rely on your noble virtues and outstanding achievements, and enjoy the sacrifices of endless descendants.
Queen Xiaoqian was named the Queen Mother of Ding'an.
After reading out the policy, Wang Mang personally held the boy's hand, sighed with tears, and said: In the past, Duke Zhou acted as the king and was finally able to return the power of Mingjun to King Zhou Cheng. Now I am forced by the majestic order of God and cannot do what I want!
A long sigh of sadness.
The middle master took the boy down to the palace and faced the north, calling himself a minister.
Hundreds of officials accompanied him, and no one was unmoved.
According to the instructions on the gold cabinet, the auxiliary ministers held appointment ceremonies.
The Taifu, Zuo Fu, and Husband General Anyang Hou Wang Shun were appointed as the Grand Master, and were granted the title of An Xingong; the Great Situ Juudehou Pingyan was appointed as the Grand Tutor, and he was granted the title of Xingong; Shao'a, Xihe, and Jingzhao Yin Hongxiu Hou Liu Xin were appointed as the Imperial Preceptors and were granted the title of Jiaxin Gong; Aizhang, a native of Zitong County in Guanghan County, was appointed as the State General and was granted the title of Mei Xingong: these are the fourth assistants, ranking in the rank of Grand Duke.
The Taibao and later Chengyang Marquis Zhen Han was appointed as the Great Sima, and was granted the title of New Gong; the Marquis of Pi Jin, Wang Xun, was granted the title of the Great Situ, and was granted the title of the New Duke; the infantry general, the Marquis of Chengdu, was granted the title of the Grand Sikong, and was granted the title of Long Xingong: these are the three Dukes.
Da'a, Youfu, Da Sikong, and Wei generals Guangyang Hou Zhenfeng were appointed as Gengshi generals and were granted the title of Guangxin Gong; Wang Xing from Jingzhao Yin was appointed as the Wei general and was granted the title of Xingong; General Qingche Cheng Wuhou Sun Jian was appointed as the founding general and was granted the title of Xingong; Wang Sheng from Jingzhao Yin was appointed as the former general and was granted the title of Chongxin Gong: these are the four generals.
Eleven males in total.
Wang Xing was the original official of the city gate.
Wang Sheng is a cake seller.
Wang Mang found more than ten people with such names according to the talisman. The appearance of these two people met the requirements of divination and fortune telling, and they were directly recruited from civilians to show their magic.
Others with the same name were awarded the title of Langguan.
