Mingguang Palace was changed to Ding'an Pavilion, and Queen Mother Ding'an was allowed to live there. The former Dahonglu official residence was used as a public residence in Ding'an, with guards and envoys set up to monitor and manage it. The nursery staff and nanny were warned not to talk to him, and he was allowed to stay in a small room surrounded by four walls. Later, Wang Ling married his granddaughter Wang Yu's daughter to him.

translation:
Guang Luxun was renamed Sizhong, the imperial servant was renamed Taiyu, the Weiwei was renamed Taiwei, Zhijinwu was renamed Fenwu, the lieutenant was renamed Junzheng, and a large official was set up to be in charge of the emperor's vehicles, clothes and utensils, and later in charge of military supplies. The positions were all senior ministers, called the Sixth Supervisor.
The prefect of the county was renamed Taiyin, the captain was renamed Taiwei, the county magistrate and magistrate were renamed Zai, the censor was renamed Enforcement, the carriage driver was renamed Wanglu Simen, Changle Palace was renamed Changleshi, Weiyang Palace was renamed Shouchengshi, the front hall was renamed Wanglutang, and Chang'an was renamed Chang'an.
The people with a salary of 100 stones were renamed common people, those with a salary of 300 stones were renamed corporals, those with a salary of 400 stones were renamed sergeants, those with a salary of 500 stones were renamed Mingshi, those with a salary of 600 stones were renamed yuanshi, those with a thousand stones were renamed xiaodafu, those with 2000 stones were renamed middle doctors, 2000 stones were renamed shangdafu, and those with 2000 stones were renamed qing.
The carriages, horses, dresses, and hats they use all have different levels.
Doctors Sigong, Situ, Siming, Sicong, Sizhong, poetry reciters, and Che Shanzai were also appointed to detect faults.
The policy book said: I heard that the Sage wanted to demonstrate his virtue and cultivate his body and mind carefully to carry it out for a long time. Therefore, I set up officials like you to supervise in five aspects.
Don't cover up your mistakes, don't encourage vanity, so that you can make no mistakes in your own likes and dislikes, stand in the center of truth, and be selfless. Ouch, that’s encouraging!
Flags of suggestions, wooden signs of criticism and drums were ordered to be set up around the palace.
The four officials who were sent to remonstrate often sat at the four gates of Wang Road to receive people who reported the situation.
Relatives of the royal family who have been in mourning for one year are given the title of marquis, relatives who have been in mourning for nine months are called earls, relatives who have been in mourning for five months are called viscounts, relatives who have been in mourning for three months are called barons, and all female relatives above are granted the title of nobility.
Men use the character "mu" as their title, and women use the character "long" as their title, and both are awarded seals.
Let the princes establish wives, wives and princes, and also grant seals.
He also said: There are no two suns in the sky, and there are no two kings on the earth. This is a principle that cannot be changed by emperors for generations.
Some of the princes of the Han Dynasty were called kings, until foreigners from all over the world also imitated the title of king, which violated the ancient system and deviated from the principle of unification.
It should be ensured that the names of princes and kings are all called Gong, and that the names of foreigners from all over the world who steal their names and call themselves kings are changed to Hou.
He also said: The emperor's lineage should be inherited, developed and integrated; the lineage with noble virtues should enjoy sacrifices for a long time.
I thought that Huangdi, Shaohao, Zhuanxu, Diru, Yao of Tang, Yushun, Xia Yu, Gaotao and Yiyin all had sage virtues. They were connected to heaven, their achievements were majestic, and their glory spread for a long time.
summary: Wang Mang issued a policy document stipulating the responsibilities of the officials, linking them to the five planets and the moon, sun, and Beidou. Other officials made regulations according to their duties. There were appointed Grand Sima Siyun, Grand Situ Sizhi, and Grand Situ Kong Siruo, all of whom were appointed as Guqing. Da Sinong was renamed Xihe, and later Nayan, Dali was renamed Zuoshi, Taichang was renamed Zhizhong, Dahonglu was renamed Dianle, the Shaofu was renamed Gonggong, and the Shuiheng Duwei was renamed Yuyu. In addition, the three company ministers were renamed nine ministers in total, and they were placed under the jurisdiction of the three princes. There were three officials under each minister, and three officials under each official. A total of twenty-seven officials and eighty-one officials were in charge of all the duties of various government offices in the capital. Guang Luxun was renamed Sizhong, the imperial servant was renamed Taiyu, the Weiwei was renamed Taiwei, Zhijinwu was renamed Fenwu, the lieutenant was renamed Junzheng, and a large official was set up to be in charge of the emperor's vehicles, clothes and utensils, and later in charge of military supplies. The carriages, horses, dresses, and hats they use all have different levels. Doctors Sigong, Situ, Siming, Sicong, Sizhong, poetry reciters, and Che Shanzai were also appointed to detect faults.

translation:
I admire them, seek their descendants, and intend to continue their sacrifices.
He believed that the surname Wang was a descendant of Yu Shun and came from imperial learning; the surname Liu was a descendant of Tang Yao and came from Zhuan Xu.
So Yao Xun was granted the title of Marquis of Chumu, the descendant of the Yellow Emperor; Liang Hu was the descendant of Xiu Yuanbo, the descendant of Shaowu; the grandson of the emperor Gonglong Gongwang Qian was the descendant of the emperor; Liu Xin was the descendant of Qi Liebo, the descendant of Zhuan Xu; the country Liu Xin's son Liu Die was Yixiuhou and inherited the descendants of Tang Yao; Machang was Shimuhou and inherited the descendants of Yu Shun; Shan Zun was Baomou's son and inherited Gaotao's descendants; Yixuan was Baohengzi and inherited Yiyin's descendants.
Liu Ying, the descendant of the Han Dynasty, Ding'an Gong, was a state guest.
Ji Dang, a descendant of Duke Wei of the Zhou Dynasty, was renamed Duke Zhang Ping and was also a state guest.
Song Gong Kong Hong, a descendant of the Yin Dynasty, had his fortune changed and his position moved. He was renamed Zhang Zhaohou and his status was that of a distinguished guest.
Si Feng, a descendant of the Xia Dynasty from Liaoxi County, was granted the title of Zhang Gonghou and was also an honored guest.
The ancestors of the Xia, Yin, Zhou, and Han dynasties were worshiped together in the Mingtang, and they were allowed to follow the great imperial ancestor Yu Shun to share.
The descendants of Zhou Gong praised Lu Zi Ji Ji, and the descendants of Confucius praised Cheng Zi Ji Gou. It has been determined before.
Wang Mang continued: When I was the regent, I built suburban sacrificial altar sites, established ancestral temples, and set up Tugu Shrine. The gods repaid me with brilliance from above covering the bottom, flowing down and turning into old crows, and yellow air rising and shining brightly to highlight the afterglow of Huangdi and Yushun.
From the Yellow Emperor to King Bo of Jinan, there were five surnames of our ancestors.

translation:
At that time, King Wu of Zhou attacked King Zhou of Shang, destroyed the Shang Dynasty, and moved the Nine Tripods, which symbolized state power, from the Shang capital to Luoyi. Boyi and Shuqi believed that King Wu was unfaithful and unfilial, so they ate Zhou millet in shame and starved to death in Shouyang Mountain. Even the people of Zhou praised them for their noble moral character.
Confucius thought the two of them were virtuous and praised them for not changing their ambitions and not allowing themselves to be humiliated.
Mencius also said: Hearing Boyi's demeanor is enough to make greedy people honest and cowardly people to establish their ambitions; to inspire behavior before a hundred generations, everyone after a hundred generations will be deeply inspired. Who can do this if he is not a sage?
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, there were Yuan Gong, Qili Ji, Xia Huang Gong and Mr. Jiao Li. When the Qin Dynasty ruled the world, these four people fled to the depths of Shangluo Mountain and waited for the world to be peaceful.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty heard about it and summoned them, but they did not come.
Later, Empress Lu adopted the strategy of leaving Zhang Liang behind, and asked the crown prince to bring silk fabrics, bow down and greet him with humility, and use a small car to welcome him to her side to assist her.
After the four arrived, they followed the prince to see Gaozu. Gaozu respected them and treated them as honored guests. From this, the prince was taken seriously and his position was stabilized.
This incident is recorded in detail in "The Biography of Liuhou".
Later, there was Zheng Zizhen in the mouth of the valley, and there was a strict gentleman in Shu. They were able to cultivate themselves and respect themselves, not wearing what they shouldn't wear, and not eating what they shouldn't eat.
When Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty was in power, his uncle and general Wang Feng recruited Zizhen with courtesy, but Zizhen did not accept the call and ended up not yielding.
A gentleman was doing divination in the Chengdu market. He thought: Although divination is a humble profession, it can benefit everyone.
If someone inquires about something evil or unfair, tell him the pros and cons according to the yarrow and the shell of a tortoise.
The divination for a son is based on the principles of filial piety; the divination for a younger brother is based on the principle of obedience; the divination for a minister is based on the idea of ​​loyalty to the king. In this way, we can take advantage of the situation and guide different people towards the good side. More than half of the people obey my words.
He only receives a few people every day. When he can earn a hundred yuan to survive, he closes the stall and teaches "Laozi" at home.
He also read a lot of various books and became proficient in them all. According to the theories of Laozi and Zhuangzhou, he wrote more than 100,000 words of books.
Yang Xiong studied with him when he was young, and later became an official in the capital and became famous. He repeatedly praised Yan Junping's conduct to the virtuous officials in the court.
Li Qiang, a native of Duling, had always been very good with Yang Xiong. Later he became an official and became a shepherd in Yizhou. He happily said to Yang Xiong: Now I really want to get King Yan Zhou. Hexiong said: You have to treat him with courtesy. He is a person who can be seen and cannot be used by others.
Li Qiang disagreed in his heart.
After he took office in Shu, he met Junping with courtesy, but he still dared not bring up the matter of calling him as an official, so he sighed: "Yang Ziyun really understands people!"
Yan Junping lived to be more than ninety years old, and he continued to work on divination and fortune-telling until his death. People in Shu loved and respected him, and they still praise him to this day.
Later, Yang Xiong wrote a book about the people of the world, praising these two people in particular.
summary: King Wu of Zhou overthrew King Zhou of Shang, moving the Nine Tripods to Luoyi. Confucius lauded their unwavering resolve, and Mencius declared that hearing of Boyi’s conduct could reform the greedy and cowardly, inspiring generations. Their presence stabilized the prince’s position, as recorded in the *Biography of the Marquis of Liu*. Later, Zheng Zizhen of Gu Valley and Yan Junping of Shu cultivated self-respect, refusing improper attire or food. Zheng Zizhen declined recruitment by General Wang Feng. Yan Junping, a diviner in Chengdu, used his trade to guide people toward filial piety, obedience, and loyalty, earning a modest living before teaching Laozi. He authored over 100,000 words on Daoist philosophy. Yang Xiong, who studied under him, praised his conduct to officials, noting that Yan could be seen but not employed. Yan lived past ninety, revered by the people of Shu. Yang Xiong later wrote that a gentleman’s virtue establishes his reputation, contrasting the wealth of princes with the enduring fame of recluses like Zheng Zizhen and Yan Junping, whom he deemed national treasures.

This shows Wang Ji's motivation for his own will.
Wang Ji and Gong Yu were good friends, and people said that when Wang Yang was an official in the court, Gong Yu would also become an official, which meant that they both had the same interests.
Not long after Emperor Yuan of Han came to the throne, he sent envoys to recruit Gong Yu and Wang Ji to join the court.
Because Wang Ji was old, he contracted an illness and died on the way. Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty mourned him and sent envoys to pay tribute to him.
At the beginning, Wang Ji was proficient in the Five Classics and was familiar with Li's Spring and Autumn Annals. He taught students the Book of Songs and the Analects of Confucius. He especially liked the Book of Changes explained by Liang Qiuhe and asked his son Wang Jun to study with him.
Wang Jun appointed Xiao Lian as Lang.
Chen Xian, the Zuo Cao, recommended Wang Jun, saying that both his father and son were virtuous, knowledgeable about the classics, and cultivated moral principles. They should be placed in a distinguished position to encourage the worldly people.
Guangluxun Kuangheng also recommended Wang Jun, saying that he was right when asked and had no doubts.
As a result, Wang Jun was promoted to the position of admonishing doctor, and represented the imperial court to criticize and criticize Huaiyang King Xian's misconduct.
Later, he was appointed as the internal history of Zhao State.
After Wang Ji was implicated in the affairs of King Changyi and was sentenced, he warned his descendants not to be officials in the princely kingdoms. Therefore, Wang Jun claimed to be ill and was relieved of his duties and returned home.
Later, he was appointed as the governor of Youzhou from his family, and was promoted to the rank of Sili Xiaowei. He dismissed the prime minister Kuang Heng in a memorial, and was later appointed as the Shaofu. After eight years of this, Emperor Cheng was ready to entrust him with an important task and let him serve as Jing Zhaoyin to test his ability to handle political affairs.
Prior to this, those who served as Zhaoyin in the capital included Fang Guanghan, Zhang Chang, Wang Zun, Wang Zhang and others. Up to Wang Jun, they all had a reputation for being capable. Therefore, people in the capital praised him and said: There were Zhao and Zhang before him, and there were three kings after him.
At that time, Xue Xuan took the post of Zuo Feng Yi and succeeded Wang Jun as the Shaofu. Just in time to catch up with the vacancy of the imperial censor, Gu Yong reported: A wise king does not listen to false names but pays attention to actual results when employing people.
The method of employing people must examine their merits. Xue Xuan passed the inspection and had great political achievements.
Emperor Cheng agreed with Gu Yong's opinion. Therefore, Xue Xuan was promoted to the post of Shaofu for more than a month, and was promoted to Yushi doctor, and finally to prime minister. Wang Jun took over the post of imperial censor instead of Xue Xuan. The two were officials in the same dynasty and held high positions.
Six years later, Wang Jun died of illness, and Zhai Fangjin succeeded Wang Jun as the imperial censor.
A few months later, Xue Xuan was dismissed and Zhai Fangjin took over as prime minister.
Everyone felt sorry that Wang Jun was not granted the title of Marquis.
When Wang Jun was the Shaofu, his wife died and he did not marry again. Someone asked him why. He said: I have no virtue like Zeng Shen, no beautiful son, no virtuous son, how dare I marry again?
Wang Chong, the son of Wang Jun, was appointed as Lang under the influence of his father. He successively held the positions of governor and county governor, and had a reputation for being able to govern.
In the third year of Jianping, when he took office as the governor of Henan, he was recruited into the court and served as a censor for several months.
At that time, the wife of An Chenggonghou, the uncle of Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty, was released into mourning and widowed, and was supported in the Changxin Palace. She was imprisoned for the crime of witchcraft and curses. Wang Chong submitted a sealed seal to plead for her release.
Fang's natal family Xie and Wang Chong were related by marriage. Therefore, Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty thought that Wang Chong was not loyal to the emperor, so he made a plan to Shao and warned Wang Chong: "Because your family has a good reputation for many generations, I chose you as an exception."
summary: Wang Ji (Ziyang) of Langxie excelled in classics, serving as a county official and later as lieutenant of Changyi. He admonished King Changyi for excessive hunting, citing ancient customs and the *Book of Songs* to urge moderation, warning that reckless travel harmed health and governance. He advocated study, ritual, and self-cultivation over indulgence. The king, though flawed, rewarded Wang Ji for his loyalty but continued his ways. After Emperor Zhao’s death, General Huo Guang summoned King Changyi to the capital. Wang Ji advised the king to mourn silently and defer to Huo Guang, comparing him to Zhou Gong and Yi Yin. The king was deposed after 20 days for lewdness; most of his officials were executed, but Wang Ji and Gong Sui were spared due to their admonitions, though sentenced to shave their heads and build cities. Wang Ji later served as governor of Yizhou and a court doctor. Under Emperor Xuan, he criticized the court’s focus on trivial matters over foundational governance, urging ritual education, selection of virtuous aides, and rejection of hereditary offices. He proposed reducing extravagance, abolishing coinage, and promoting agriculture. The emperor deemed his ideas impractical, so Wang Ji resigned, returning to Langxie. His reputation for integrity was marred by a minor incident: he divorced his wife for picking dates from a neighbor’s tree, though neighbors persuaded him to take her back. Wang Ji taught the Five Classics and died en route to a summons from Emperor Yuan. His son Wang Jun, also virtuous, served as an admonisher and governor, known for his capability alongside Zhao Guanghan and Zhang Chang. Wang Jun, after his wife’s death, refused remarriage, citing lack of virtue. His son Wang Chong became a censor but was demoted for pleading for a relative; later, under Wang Mang, he became Grand Sikong and Marquis of Fuping, but died by poisoning. The Wang family maintained honesty across generations, though their love for fine carriages and clothes puzzled contemporaries, leading to the saying “Wang Yang could turn gold.”

More than a year later, Wang Chong was poisoned to death by his maid, and his feudal kingdom was abolished.
From Wang Ji to Wang Chong, the Wang family has a reputation of being honest and honest for several generations. Generations of the Wang family have been fond of carriages, horses, and clothes. Their food, clothing, housing, and transportation are all very particular and outstanding, but they do not have gold, silver, brocade, and other items.
Every time we moved, all the car carried was a bag of spare clothes. They don't store excess belongings.
When he left his official home, he also lived in common people's clothing and ate vegetarian food.
People all over the world admired their honesty, but they were very surprised that they were so particular about food, clothing, carriages and horses. Therefore, it was said among the people that "Wang Yang could turn gold".
Gongyu, courtesy name Shaoweng, was born in Langxie.
Known for his proficiency in classics and good conduct, he was recruited as a doctor and served as the governor of Liangzhou. He resigned due to illness.
Later, he was elected as a virtuous person and appointed as the order of Henan.
After being exposed for more than a year, he was accused by government officials on official business and was forced to take off his hat and apologize.
Gong Yu said: Once you take off your hat, how can you put it on again?
So he resigned and left.
Not long after Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he recruited Gong Yu as an admonishing official and condescended to ask him about political affairs many times.
At that time, the year was not good, the agricultural harvest was poor, and the prefectures, counties and kingdoms all over the world were in a difficult situation. Gongyu reported to him:
In ancient times, palaces had a certain standard system. There were no more than nine maids and no more than eight horses. Palace walls were painted but not painted, and the wood was polished but not carved. Cars, carriages, utensils, etc. were not decorated with colors and patterns. The radius of the royal gardens did not exceed dozens of miles, and they were shared with the common people. Talented people were appointed, Only a tax equivalent to one-tenth of the people's income is collected. Apart from this, there are no other taxes or labor and border guards. The people are enslaved for no more than three days a year. With the capital as the center, the emperor within a thousand miles collects taxes for himself. A thousand miles away, the emperor determines a certain type and quantity based on their production, so that they can pay tribute on time.
summary: Gong Yu (Shaoweng) of Langxie, known for his classic learning, served as a doctor and governor of Liangzhou before resigning. Recruited by Emperor Yuan, he advised frugality, citing ancient standards: few concubines, simple palaces, and light taxes. He criticized the extravagance of Emperor Wu’s era, noting that officials and nobles overstepped ranks, leading to waste and poverty. He urged reducing palace horses, craftsmen, and concubines, and returning gardens to the poor. Emperor Yuan adopted some suggestions, cutting horse feed and distributing land. Gong Yu later became a censor, submitting dozens of memorials. He argued that taxes on three-year-olds caused infanticide, proposing taxes start at age seven. He condemned coinage for diverting labor from farming, causing hunger, and advocated returning to barter. He also criticized atonement laws for encouraging corruption, urging strict punishment for dishonest officials. Emperor Yuan implemented the seven-year tax rule and reduced palace guards, though other reforms stalled. Gong Yu died shortly after becoming censor; the emperor granted his son a post. His proposals on temple abolition were later enacted but criticized by scholars.

He accused Dong Xian of disrupting court order, leading to conflict with colleagues. After a dispute with Xiahou Chang over ritual, he was demoted and resigned. Recruited again, he refused to serve under Wang Mang, who sent envoys with lavish gifts. Gong Sheng, bedridden, refused the seal, saying he could not serve two dynasties. He starved himself to death at 79, instructing simple burial. Gong She, also a classicist, served briefly as governor of Taishan but resigned due to illness. He died at 68 during Wang Mang’s regency. Bao Xuan (Zidu) of Bohai, a diligent scholar, served as an admonisher under Emperor Ai. He wrote vehemently against the favoritism shown to Dong Xian and the Fu and Ding clans, warning that corruption, heavy taxes, and harsh laws caused seven reasons for displacement and seven causes of death. He urged the recall of virtuous officials like He Wu and Kong Guang. Emperor Ai initially tolerated him, but after Bao Xuan humiliated a prime minister’s subordinate, he was imprisoned. Over a thousand students protested, leading to his sentence being reduced to shaving and iron chains. He later moved to Shangdang, where Wang Mang had him executed for associating with a wanted man. Other figures like Xin Xing, Ji Kui, and Xue Fang displayed varying degrees of integrity, with some refusing Wang Mang’s summons. The historian concludes that while hermits and officials each have merits, true virtue lies in unwavering adherence to the good path, as exemplified by Gong Sheng and Xue Fang.

translation:
Gai Kuanrao, courtesy name Cigong, was from Weijun.
Because he was proficient in classics, he served as a county scholar, and because of his filial piety and integrity, he became a Langguan.
He was promoted to the title of Founder, took the imperial examination and achieved excellent results, was promoted to the imperial censor, and acted as the deputy general of the household.
He impeached Pengzu, the son of General Zhang Anshi of the Imperial Guard, for refusing to get out of the car in front of the palace gate, and because Anshi had no political achievements in his official position.
Peng Zu actually got off the car in front of the palace gate at that time. Kuan Rao committed the crime of reporting the minister's misrepresentation and was demoted to Sima Wei.
Before that, Sima Wei was in the official office. When he saw the Wei Wei, he wanted to pay homage and often went out to buy things for the Wei Wei.
After Kuanrao became the Sima of the Guards, according to the previous system, he bowed his hands and saluted the officials who were responsible for patrolling the guards.
Weiwei sent Kuanrao out privately, and Kuanrao went to Shangshu Yamen to submit an application according to the system.
The minister then questioned the Wei Wei, and from then on the Wei officials no longer sent Pai Hou and Sima without permission.
Hou and Sima no longer paid homage to the emperor. When the emperor traveled, Hou and Sima, as the forerunners, had to give memorials first, and this was institutionalized from then on.
Kuanrao was appointed as Sima Chu. He did not leave the palace gate, cut his single coat short so that it could leave the ground, wore a big hat, and carried a long sword. He personally visited the soldiers' houses, inspected their diet and daily life, personally comforted and asked the sick soldiers, gave them medicine, and treated them very kindly.
When the shift was handed over at the end of the year, the emperor personally rewarded the retired soldiers. Thousands of soldiers kowtowed and asked to stay and serve for another year to repay the generous kindness.
Emperor Xuan commended him for his kindness, appointed him as Taizhong doctor, and asked him to inspect the customs of various places. He commended, recommended, demoted, and deposed many people, and completed the mission in line with the emperor's wishes.
Therefore, he was promoted to the rank of Sili Xiaowei, and he was able to inspect and expose the mistakes of officials without hesitation. Small and big matters were reported to the public, and many people were impeached. The Tingwei dealt with them according to the law, and half of his opinions were adopted and half were not adopted. However, the ministers, nobles, and officials of the county and state who were envoys to Chang'an were all too afraid to violate the ban, and the capital was peaceful.
When Ping Enhou Xu Bo moved into his new residence, all the prime ministers, censors, generals, and officials with a salary of two thousand dan went to congratulate him, but Kuan Rao did not go.
Uncle Xu invited him, so he went up to the hall from the west steps and sat alone facing the east.
Uncle Xu poured him wine himself and said: "You are late."
Kuanrao said: Don't pour more wine for me. I'll go crazy if I drink too much.
Prime Minister Wei Hou smiled and said: "You are a little crazy when you are awake. Why do you have to drink?"
Everyone present looked at him with contempt.
When the wine was in full swing, the music started playing. Tan Changqing, the young master of Changxin, got up and danced, performing a monkey and dog fight, and everyone present laughed.
Kuangrao was unhappy, looked up at the roof and sighed, "How beautiful!"
summary: Gai Kuanrao, from Weijun, rose through the ranks due to his classical knowledge and filial piety. As an imperial censor, he impeached Pengzu, son of General Zhang Anshi, for refusing to dismount at the palace gate. However, since Pengzu had actually dismounted, Kuanrao was demoted for misrepresentation. As Sima of the Guards, he reformed protocols, personally cared for soldiers' welfare, and earned such loyalty that retiring soldiers requested to serve another year. Emperor Xuan promoted him to Sili Xiaowei, where he fearlessly investigated officials, creating peace in the capital. At a celebration for Xu Bo's new residence, Kuanrao sat apart and warned about the impermanence of wealth. He later impeached a performer for disrespectful dancing. Despite his integrity and poverty—using half his salary to pay informants—his harshness and tendency to frame others created enemies. Wang Sheng advised him to be more cautious, but Kuanrao ignored this counsel. He submitted a memorial criticizing the emperor's reliance on eunuchs and suggesting that rulers should yield to the worthy. The emperor deemed this treasonous. Despite Zheng Chang's defense, Kuanrao was imprisoned and committed suicide.

translation:
Zhuge Feng, a former Sili school captain, did not follow the seasons or follow the rule of law, but specialized in harsh cruelty, thus gaining false prestige. I could not bear to hand him over to the jailer, so I asked him to serve as the city gate school captain.
Instead of introspecting, he instead resented Zhou Kan and Zhang Meng, seeking revenge. His words of conviction had no evidence, he exposed crimes that were difficult to verify, and he relied solely on subjective wishes to slander and praise others, regardless of what he had said before. This was a serious act of not being trustworthy.
I pity Zhuge Feng that he is old and cannot bear to impose punishment, so I order him to be removed from his official position and become a commoner.
Zhuge Feng died at home.
Liu Fu is a member of the royal family of Hejian Kingdom.
He was promoted to Xiaolian and served as the county magistrate of Xiangbi.
He wrote a memorial to discuss the gains and losses of national affairs, and was summoned by the emperor. The emperor appreciated his talents and promoted him to the position of admonishing doctor.
Just in time when Emperor Cheng wanted to make Tang Jiandan his queen, he first issued an edict to confer the title of prince to Lin, the envoy's father.
Liu Fu wrote a letter and said: I heard that if God agrees, he will definitely give auspicious signs, and if God disagrees, he will definitely send disasters and changes. This is a sign from the gods and a natural prediction.
In the past, King Wu and Duke Zhou obeyed the will of heaven and earth, and thus received the auspiciousness of white fish and red crows. However, the monarchs and ministers were still worried, shocked, and vigilant in admonishing each other. How much more so in today's last days, when they have not received the blessing of offspring and descendants, but have repeatedly suffered disasters caused by the power and wrath of heaven?
Even if you blame yourself every day, correct your mistakes and behavior, fear the destiny, think of the achievements of your ancestors, choose a virtuous family, pray for a beautiful and capable woman to inherit the ancestral temple, comply with the will of the gods, and satisfy the wishes of the people of the world, The auspiciousness of procreating descendants, which I was worried had come too late, now triggers my affection and indulges my desires. I am devoted to this humble woman and want to regard her as the mother of all people in the world. I am not in awe of God and not ashamed of the people. There is nothing more stupid than this.
As the saying goes: Rotten wood cannot be used to make pillars, and lowly people cannot be made masters. If God and the people disapprove of it, it must be harmful but not beneficial. This is a truth that everyone in the market and on the road knows, but no one in the court is willing to tell the truth. I secretly feel sad.
I thought that because I was promoted because I have the same surname as the emperor, I only enjoyed the salary but did not show loyalty, and insulted the official position of the remonstrance. I dare not risk my life to speak out. I hope that your majesty will examine it deeply.
After the memorial was presented, the emperor sent his censor to arrest Liu Fu and imprison him in a secret prison in the harem. None of the ministers understood the reason.
At that time, the Chinese left general Xin Qingji, the right general Lian Bao, Guang Lu Xun Crocodile, and Taizhong doctor Gui Su all reported: We have heard that a wise king listens widely to opinions, pays attention to the admonition of quiet officials, opens the way for loyal and upright people, and does not punish arrogant and impatient remarks. Then all ministers keep their own positions and try their best to contribute their loyalty and wisdom. The court has no worries, there are no flattering officials in the court, and the monarch has no fault of deviating from the right path.
We have privately seen that Liu Fu, the admonishing doctor, used to meet the emperor as a county magistrate and was promoted to admonishing doctor. This shows that his opinions must be extraordinary, accurate and in line with the holy content, so he can be promoted to such a position.
However, within ten days, he was arrested and imprisoned in a secret prison. We were ignorant and thought that Liu Fu was lucky enough to be entrusted as a relative of the royal family and to be in the ranks of admonishers. He came from a lower position and did not know the imperial system. He violated taboos on his own and was not worthy of further investigation.
Small crimes should be tolerated. If there are major crimes, they should be handed over to judicial officials for public trial, so that everyone can know his crimes and punish him together.
Once upon a time, Confucius went to Jianzi to kill his doctor Mingdu. Confucius walked to the Yellow River and returned.
Nowadays, God's will is not happy, disasters are coming frequently, and floods and droughts are coming one after another. It is the time to be generous, solicit opinions widely, and praise integrity to maximize the power of the people.
However, he carried out tragic and sudden executions on ministers who dared to remonstrate, which shocked everyone and chilled the hearts of loyal and upright people.
If Liu Fu did not commit a crime because he spoke out and dared to remonstrate, then no one in the world would know about the crime he committed if he did not publicly announce it.
A minister who has the same surname as the emperor and is close to the emperor originally gained high status because he dared to tell the truth. From the perspective of dealing with relatives and protecting loyal people, he should not be secretly imprisoned in Yeting Prison.
When the ministers and officials below saw that Your Majesty was so eager to promote Liu Fu, but was so brutal in attacking and injuring him, everyone was filled with fear. Their will to be enterprising disappeared and they became weak. They no longer dared to perform their duties faithfully and uphold the right opinions. This was not the practice of Yu and Shun who listened to the opinions of his ministers and promoted good moral character.
We are privately deeply saddened by this and hope you will pay attention and review it.
The emperor then moved and imprisoned Liu Fu to the imperial prison under the control of the Shaofu, reduced the death penalty to one degree, and sentenced him to hard labor in the ancestral temple.
He is always at home.
summary: Zhuge Feng, from Langxie, became Sili Xiaowei under Emperor Yuan. He attempted to arrest the favored relative Xu Zhang but was thwarted when Xu fled to the palace. The emperor confiscated Zhuge's talisman, ending the Sili's traditional authority. Zhuge apologized in a memorial but continued criticizing corrupt officials. He was transferred to city gate captain after arresting prisoners in spring and summer. When he accused former colleagues, the emperor removed him from office for untrustworthiness, and he died at home. Liu Fu, a royal family member, became an admonishing doctor under Emperor Cheng. He opposed making Tang Jiandan queen, arguing it defied divine will. The emperor imprisoned him in a secret prison. Several high officials petitioned for his release, arguing that punishing remonstrators chilled loyal hearts. The emperor reduced his sentence to hard labor.

translation:
Zheng Chong, also known as Ziyou, originally belonged to a wealthy family in Gaomi Kingdom and had been intermarrying with the Wang family for generations.
My grandfather moved to Pingling because he had money.
His father, Zheng Bin, was well versed in laws, served as a royal censor, and served Duke Gong. He was known for his fairness and uprightness.
Zheng Chong served as the literary historian of the county when he was young, and later became a chariot attendant in the Prime Minister's Mansion.
His younger brother Zheng Li and Gao Wuhou Fu Xi studied under the same teacher and were friendly to each other.
When Fu happy became the Grand Sima, he recommended Zheng Chong, and Emperor Ai promoted him to the position of Minister of Public Affairs.
He asked to see the emperor several times to remonstrate, and the emperor initially accepted his opinions.
Every time he saw him dragging his rawhide shoes, the emperor smiled and said: I can hear Zheng Shangshu's footsteps.
After a long time, the emperor wanted to knight Fu Shang, the cousin of his grandmother, the Empress Dowager Fu. Zheng Chongjin advised him: Emperor Xiaocheng made five of his uncles marquis. As a result, the sky turned red and yellow, the daytime became dim, and there was black energy in the sun.
Now your grandmother's two cousins ​​have become marquises.
Marquis Kongxiang was the father of the queen; Marquis Gaowu was granted the title of Marquis based on his status as the Third Duke. It can be said that there are certain reasons for these.
Now he wants to ennoble Fu Shang for no reason, which creates havoc and disrupts the system. It goes against the will of God and people's hearts, and is not Fu Kuang's blessing.
I heard the teacher say: Those who violate Yang are extremely weak, and those who violate Yin will be short-lived and premature. Those who violate others will be in danger of disaster and destruction, and those who offend the gods will be in danger of illness and death. So the Duke of Zhou wrote a precept and said: The king who does not know the difficulties of the country and indulges in entertainment rarely can live a long life. Therefore, the king in the period of decline will die young and die prematurely, which is a disaster that violates the principles of Yin.
I would rather use my own life to resist the disaster of the country.
Zheng Chong then stood up holding the edict board.
Empress Dowager Fu said angrily: How could anyone who is the emperor be subdued by a minister?
The emperor then issued an edict saying: I became an orphan when I was young. I was raised by the emperor's wife herself. She educated me when I was a baby and taught me etiquette and justice until I grew up. I was deeply benevolent. I want to repay this kind of kindness, God, my heart is endless. In the past, the father of the Queen Mother was named Chongzu Hou. I feel very ashamed when I think that I have not repaid her kindness enough.
Fu Shang, the Guanglu doctor in the service, was the nephew of the Empress Dowager's father. The Empress Dowager raised him since he was a child, and he was the closest to him in kindness and kindness.
The order was given to seal the fort as this Danbao, let him be the descendant of Sai Lord, and changed the title of Sai Danhou to Rulu Aihou.
Zheng Chong also remonstrated with the emperor because Dong Xian was too favored by the nobles, and therefore committed a serious crime.
He was reprimanded several times for his duties, and he developed paralysis in his neck. He wanted to request that he return to his hometown for retirement, but he did not dare to complain.
The minister ordered Zhao Chang to be a treacherous and flattering person. He had always been jealous of Zheng Chong and knew that he had been alienated. Therefore, he sent a report saying that Zheng Chong was colluding with the royal family and suspected of being a treacherous person. Please investigate him.
summary: Zheng Chong served under Emperor Ai, known for his distinctive leather shoes. He opposed ennobling Fu Shang, the emperor's grandmother's cousin, citing precedents where such actions caused celestial disturbances. Despite the Empress Dowager's anger, Zheng persisted. He also criticized Dong Xian's excessive favor. After being alienated, he was accused of colluding with the royal family and died in prison.

translation:
Sun Bao submitted a memorial requesting for investigation. Empress Dowager Fu was furious and said: The emperor set up a secretary and sent an envoy to interrogate me.
The fact of Feng's rebellion is very clear, and some people deliberately want to find fault with me.
I want him to sit down together.
The emperor then followed the Queen Mother Fu's order and put Sun Bao in prison.
Shangshu Pushe Tang Lin argued the matter. The emperor believed that Tang Lin had formed a clique for personal gain and demoted him to the post of Dunhuang Yuzezhan Marquis.
Grand Sima Fu happy and Guanglu Doctor Gong Sheng persisted in their efforts, and the emperor interceded on their behalf with the Queen Mother, and then Sun Bao was released and his official position was restored.
Soon after, Zheng Chong was imprisoned. Sun Bao wrote a letter saying: I heard that people with distant relationships do not interfere with those who are close to each other, and outsiders do not consider other people's family affairs.
I am fortunate to be able to accept the mission and have the responsibility of prosecuting and reporting. I dare not avoid the power of the powerful and favored people to block the emperor's hearing and hearing so that the emperor does not know the true situation.
Shangshu Lingchang falsely accused his servant of shooting Zheng Chong and put him in prison for investigation and investigation. Zheng Chong was tortured to death. As a result, he did not give a confession. Even passers-by on the road said that he was unjustly accused.
I suspect that Chang and Zheng Chong have a rift, and the slanders are gradually increasing to frame each other. He is a close minister of the emperor, and he has been wronged, harming the country, and causing a lot of public criticism.
I sincerely request that Chang be punished to ease the people's sentiments.
After the report was made, the emperor was not happy. Because Sun Bao was a famous minister, the emperor could not bear to kill him, so the emperor issued an order to the prime minister and Grand Sikong: Sun Shi, the minister, reported that Zheng Chong, the former minister's servant, had been wronged, and requested that Shangshu Lingchang be imprisoned for review.
Zha Zhengchong is a minister around me, and his crimes are obvious, but Sun Shi has evil intentions, colludes with his ministers to deceive the emperor, and slanders and deceives him in the spring moon to realize his evil intentions. Isn't it said in "The Analects of Confucius"?
A person who subverts the country with his evil words and sophistry. He ordered Sun Bao to be dismissed as a civilian.
When Emperor Ai passed away, Wang Mang asked the Queen Mother to recruit Sun Shi to serve as Guanglu doctor, and went with Wang Shun and others to welcome the King of Zhongshan.
Emperor Ping ascended the throne, and Sun Bin served as chief agricultural officer.
It happened that Yuejun County reported that Huanglong was traveling in the river. Grand Master Kong Guang, Da Situ Ma Gong and others praised Wang Mang for his merits and virtues, which were comparable to those of Zhou Gong, and he should be sacrificed to the ancestral temple.
Sun Shi said: Duke Zhou is a great sage, Duke Zhao is a great sage. There were times when there was disharmony, as recorded in the scriptures, but this did no harm to either.
Nowadays, the wind and rain are unpredictable and the people are not yet rich. Whenever something happens, all the ministers agree with it. I'm afraid it's not very good.
At that time, the expressions of the ministers all changed, and Zhen Han, the captain of the imperial court, immediately ordered to stop the discussion.
It happened that Sun Shi sent officials to greet his mother. His mother fell ill on the way, so he stayed at his younger brother's house and only sent his wife and children to the capital.
Si Zhi Chen Chong made a case against Sun Bin, and the emperor handed the matter over to Sangong for interrogation on the spot.
Sun Shi replied: I am already seventy years old and my mind is confused. My affection for supporting my mother has become weak. I only care about my wife, family and children, just as the memorial said.
As a result, Sun Bao was dismissed from office and stayed at home for the rest of his life.
During the Jianwu period, virtuous ministers were appointed, and Sun Bao's grandson and his wife were appointed county magistrates of various counties.
Wu Jianglong, named Junfang, was from Lanling, Shuhai.
Wang Yin, the cavalry general of the Grand Sima, was in charge of Shangshu affairs inside the court and commanded troops and horses outside the court. Following the old practice, he selected and set up a Zhonglang to participate in the discussion and decision-making. He petitioned Wu Jianglong to be appointed Zhonglang, and was later promoted to an admonishing doctor.
In the last years of Emperor Cheng's reign, Wu Jianglong handed over a sealed memorial saying: In ancient times, princes were selected to serve as ministers in the imperial court in order to praise their merits. King Dingtao should be recruited and let him live in the mansion in Beijing in order to pacify the world.
After that, the emperor finally appointed King Tao as the crown prince, and Wu Jianglong was promoted to Jizhou Mu and Yingchuan Prefect.
After Emperor Ai came to the throne, Wu Jianglong was promoted to Jing Zhaoyin because of his excellent examination results, and was later promoted to Zhi Jinwu.
summary: Sun Bao served as Yizhou governor, quelling rebellions by offering amnesty to non-leaders. He exposed corruption involving the emperor's uncle Wang Li. As Jing Zhaoyin, he was pressured to protect the knight Du Zhiji but managed to avoid confrontation. He was dismissed when Chunyu Chang fell from power. Recalled under Emperor Ai, he investigated Empress Dowager Feng's death, angering Empress Dowager Fu, who had him imprisoned. Released after appeals, he later defended Zheng Chong but was dismissed. Under Emperor Ping, he opposed praising Wang Mang's virtues, was dismissed again, and lived in retirement.
rel_path: 汉书/传/盖诸葛刘郑孙毋将何传

translation:
At that time, Dong Xian, the servant, was being favored. The emperor sent Zhong Huangmen to take out the weapons from the arsenal. There were ten batches before and after, and they were sent to the homes of Dong Xian and the emperor's wet nurse Wang A.
Wu Jianglong wrote in his memorial: The weapons contained in the arsenal are common to the whole world and are designed for national armament. The funds required for their repair and manufacture are all paid by Bai Dasinong.
Even the emperor's carriages, horses and utensils could not be used for expenditures in Da Sinong's funds. The emperor's offerings and rewards were all paid from the Shaofu.
The reason is that fundamental economic reserves cannot be used for unimportant expenditures, and people's financial resources cannot be used for flashy expenditures, so as to distinguish between public and private affairs and show the right way.
In ancient times, princes and magistrates could independently control the power of conquest, and the emperor gave them axes and iron. The officials on the Han border were responsible for resisting the enemy, so they were given weapons from the arsenal. They all performed such duties and then accepted these weapons.
According to the meaning of "Spring and Autumn", the family of a senior official is not allowed to collect bells and armors. This is used to suppress the power of ministers and reduce personal power.
Nowadays, Dong Xian and others are either used to courting the emperor's jesters, or they are women of low status who only have personal favors, but you, the emperor, give them private things that are common to the world, and provide them with utensils that represent the majesty of the country for their private use.
The people's financial resources are distributed to jesters, weapons are placed in the homes of women of low status, and the system established is not in line with the national system, so as to condone and breed arrogance and overstep the bounds of etiquette. This cannot be used to show the world.
Confucius once said: How can the emperor's etiquette appear in the halls of three officials?
I ask that you return the weapons.
The emperor was very unhappy.
Soon after, Empress Dowager Fu sent a visitor to buy some official maids, and bought them at a very low price. She also bought eight official maids for Jinwu.
Don't tell the emperor that the price is too low and ask for a fair price.
The emperor then issued an order to the prime minister and the imperial censor, saying: If the etiquette of mutual humility prevails, then lawsuits like the one between Yu and Rui will naturally subside.
Wu Jianglong was ranked as the ninth minister, and he had no ability to correct the improper handling of the court. Instead, he petitioned Yongxin Palace to dispute the purchase and sale price, and announced the content of the petition. Everyone knew about it.
His actions and behavior were unreasonable, and the trend of fishing for fame and reputation began.
Because Wu Jianglong had previously made plans to stabilize the country, he was only demoted to the rank of captain of Peijun, and was later promoted to the prefect of Nanjun.
When Wang Mang was young, he wanted to make friends with Wu Jianglong, but Wu Jianglong didn't attach much importance to him.
After the death of Emperor Ai, Wang Mang came to power and asked the great situ Kong Guang to report Wu Jianglong's handling of the case of Empress Dowager Feng of Zhongshan when he was the shepherd of Jizhou. He wronged and framed a person who was not guilty and was not suitable to hold an official position in the central area of ​​​​the country.
In fact, it was the ministers who originally ordered Shi Li and Shi Dingxuan to investigate and interrogate the case in person. They only wrote a joint letter with Wu Jianglong to discuss the matter.
summary: Wu Jianglong advised Emperor Cheng to recruit the Prince of Dingtao as heir. Under Emperor Ai, he criticized giving weapons from the imperial arsenal to Dong Xian and the emperor's wet nurse. After Empress Dowager Fu's maid purchase dispute, he was demoted. Wang Mang later exiled him for his role in Empress Dowager Feng's case.
rel_path: 汉书/传/盖诸葛刘郑孙毋将何传

translation:
At this time, Shi Li was the servant of Zhongtai, Ding Xuan was the governor of Taishan, and Zhao Chang, the minister, who had framed Zheng Chong, was the governor of Hanoi. They were all removed from the palace and exiled to Hepu.
He Bing's courtesy name was Zilian. His grandfather moved from Pingyu to Pingling as an official with a rank of 2,000 stone.
He Bing served as a county official and became a ministerial official, serving He Wu.
He Wu believed that he had noble aspirations and moral integrity, and praised him for his ability to handle heavy government affairs, so He Bing served as the magistrate of Changling County. His political performance was so good that he was not dismissed.
Once upon a time, the Wang family of Empress Dowager Qiongcheng's maternal grandfather had a prominent position. Wang Linqing, the servant in charge, exchanged views with the Jianghu knights, and they were powerful in the capital.
Later, he was dismissed from his official position for breaking the law, and there were more and more guests. He returned to Changling to sweep the tomb, and drank with the guests for many days.
He Bing was afraid that he would break the law, so he went to see Lin Qing personally and said to Lin Qing: "The tomb is outside, you should go home in time."
Lin Qing said: Okay.
Before this, Lin Qing had killed the husband of a maidservant and buried him in a tomb. He Bing knew all about this, but he thought that the incident did not happen when he was in office, and saw that he had recently been removed from his official position, so he did not want to expose him, but just wanted him not to stay in his territory, so he sent his subordinates with business cards to send him away.
Lin Qing was always proud and did not want to embarrass himself in front of the guests, so he expected that he would cause trouble, so he arranged troops to deal with him.
After Lin Qing left, he passed the Jinghe Bridge north and asked a servant on horseback to return to the county government office, where he slashed the drum hanging on the pillar of the county government office with a knife.
He Jing personally led the officials and soldiers to chase Lin Qing.
After walking for dozens of miles, Lin Qing was desperate, so he asked his servant to put on his hat and short coat instead. He got into the car and asked the servant on horseback to follow him. He changed his clothes and ran forward from the road.
Just as the sun was going down, He Jing caught up with him and tied up the servant wearing Lin Qing's hat. The man said, "I am not a servant, just his servant."
He Bing knew that Lin Qing had escaped, so he said: The king was forced to have nowhere to hide, and he claimed to be a servant. Do you want to escape the death penalty?
So he ordered his men to cut off his head and bring it back, hang it on a broken drum, and put it under the pavilion of the city. He wrote: The former servant Wang Linqing committed murder. He buried the murdered man in the house guarding the tomb, and asked his servants to chop up the drum in front of the government office.
Officials and people were shocked and frightened.
Lin Qing then ran for his life, and people started talking, thinking that he was really dead.
Because Empress Dowager Qiong Cheng loved Lin Qing, Emperor Cheng shed tears when she heard about this incident, and told Emperor Ai about it.
Emperor Ai inquired about the situation and thought that the matter was done well, so he promoted him to be the governor of Longxi.
Later, He Bing was transferred to Yingchuan Prefecture, succeeding Yan Xiang from Lingyang.
Yan Xiang originally became an official based on his filial piety. He regarded his subordinates as teachers and friends. When he made mistakes, he would blame himself behind closed doors and never spoke much.
There was a riot in the county. Wang Mang sent people to recruit Yan Xiang. Several hundred officials gathered to prepare a farewell banquet for him. Yan Xiang fell on the ground and cried.
The subordinates said: It is a good thing that you were called up today. It should not be like this.
Yan Xiang said: I am a scholar who pities Yingchuan. I have nothing to worry about: I was recruited because of my weakness, and the court will inevitably choose a strong person to replace me.
Once the replacement arrives, there will be people who are bedridden, so it will be sad.
After Yan Xiang arrived, he was appointed as the envoy of beauty and customs.
At this time, Zhong Yuan, a native of Yingchuan, served as Shangshu Ling and concurrently as Ting Wei, handling affairs with authority and making changes.
His younger brother Zhong Wei was a subordinate of Yingchuan County and illegally hid a large amount of gold.
He Bing served as the prefect and told Zhong Tingwei about the incident when he saw him. Zhong Tingwei took off his hat and asked for a reduced death penalty for his brother, hoping to accept the punishment of crotch clamps as soon as possible.
He Bing said: The fault lies with your brother for violating the king's law, not with the prefect.
Zhong Yuan was afraid and sent Pegasus to greet his brother.
Yangdi's rangers Zhao Ji and Li Kuan supported many guests, used their strength to rob the neighbors, and even raped other people's wives and daughters. They took advantage of the officials' shortcomings and ran rampant in the county. When they heard that General He was coming, they all fled.
As soon as He Bing took office, he sought out nearly ten officials who were brave and knowledgeable about the law. He sent civilian officials to review the cases of the three people and military attachés to arrest them. Each had their own arrangements.
The order said: These three people did not fail the prefect, but violated the king's law, so they had to be punished.
Zhong Wei had committed many crimes before the amnesty, so he was driven into Hangu Pass to prevent him from harming the people. If he did not enter the pass, he would be arrested.
Zhao and Li are the chief culprits. Although they have escaped far away, they should be killed and apologize to the people.
Zhong Wei relied on his elder brother to stay in Luoyang, and the officials who pursued him killed him.
They also captured Tong and Li in other counties and brought their heads back. He then hung their heads and all the charges against them in the downtown area.
There was a peaceful and quiet situation in the county. He commended the good deeds and respected the scholars. He was well-known in Yingchuan, and his reputation was second only to Huang Ba.
How can he be honest and honest, and his wife and children are not in the government office.
Died a few years later.
When he was seriously ill, he asked his assistant to write a suicide note, saying: Tell my son Hui that I have spent a long time eating for nothing in my life. Although I will receive the legal condolence gift after my death, I do not want to receive it.
Use a small coffin for burial, as long as it can accommodate the coffin.
summary: He Bing, as Changling magistrate, killed the fugitive Wang Linqing, who had murdered a servant. Though Empress Dowager Qiong Cheng grieved, Emperor Ai promoted He Bing. As Yingchuan prefect, he arrested criminals Zhao Ji and Li Kuan, and drove out Zhong Wei, whose brother was a powerful official. He Bing governed with integrity, his family not living in the government office. On his deathbed, he requested a simple burial.

translation:
Bao Zheng did as his father said.
Yuling selected Hengzheng as Guan Duwei.
During the Jianda period, Tan Bing's grandson was appointed as Lang Guan.
Praise said: As a procurator, Gai Kuorao stood above the court with integrity. Even the "Director of the State" mentioned in the "Book of Songs" was nothing more than this.
If he can adopt Wang Sheng's words until he is old, he will be close to the wise ministers of ancient times.
Although Zhuge, Liu, and Zheng were somewhat arrogant and ignorant, they had unique ambitions.
Confucius said: I have never seen an upright person.
With the reputation and deeds of these people, there are still things like Wu Jianglong being stained in Jizhou and Sun Bao succumbing to Dingling Hou, let alone ordinary people?
He Bing's integrity is second only to Yin Wenggui.
summary: The commentary praises Gai Kuanrao's integrity but notes he should have heeded Wang Sheng's advice. Zhuge, Liu, and Zheng had unique ambitions. Even these upright officials had flaws, showing how difficult true integrity is. He Bing's character rivaled Yin Wenggui's.

translation:
Suihong, courtesy name Meng, was from the state of Lu and Fan.
He was young, fashionable and chivalrous, and liked cockfighting and horse racing. Later, his style changed drastically and he studied "Spring and Autumn" with Ying Gong.
Because he was proficient in Confucian classics, he became a Yilang, and he reached the official position of Fuli Jieliang.
In the first month of the third year of Emperor Zhao Yuanfeng's reign, there was a roar like thousands of people coming together from the south of Laiwu Mountain in Mount Tai. When the people went to look, they saw a big stone standing up by itself. It was one foot to five feet high, as thick as forty-eight people surrounded it, and it was eight feet deep into the ground. There were three other stones as the feet of the big stone.
After the boulder stood on its own, thousands of white crows flew down and gathered around it.
At the same time, the dead trees in the Changyi Shrine and Temple came to life again, and the big willow tree that had been broken and withered and lying on the ground in Shanglin Garden actually stood up on its own and regained its vitality. There were many insects eating the leaves of the tree, and the leftover leaves were shaped like these words: Gongsun Bing has been established. Suihong then deduced the main idea of ​​"Spring and Autumn" and believed that: Stones and willows are both negative objects, symbolizing the common people at the bottom, while Mount Tai is the head of the mountains, and it is the place where emperors worshiped heaven to repay their merits after the change of dynasties.
Nowadays, big rocks stand on their own and dry willows come back to life. They are not made by human beings. Their creation shows that ordinary people will become emperors.
The resurrection of dead trees in the temple symbolizes the revival of the previously deposed Gongsun clan.
Suihong didn't know where the Gongsun family was, so he said: My ancestor Dong Zhongshu once said that even if there is a monarch who succeeds the emperor and abides by virtue, it will not prevent the saint from receiving orders from heaven.
The Han family is a descendant of Yao, and they are destined to pass on their surname to the country. Emperor Mo should tell the world about it.
He solicited talented people and abdicated the throne to him, while he abdicated and granted a land of hundreds of miles, just like the descendants of King Zhou of Yin, in order to obey the destiny.
Suihong asked his friend who was an internal official to write this book for him.
At that time, Emperor Zhao was still very young, and the general Huo Guang was in charge of the government. Huo Guang hated this very much, so he handed Suihong's memorial to Tingwei.
Huo Guang sent a memorial to Ci and Sui Hong, who deceived the public with their demonic words and committed treason. Both of them were sentenced to death.
Five years later, Emperor Xiaoxuan rose from the ranks of the people and ascended the throne, so he recruited Suihong's son as Lang.
Xiahou Shichang was from Lu.
Proficient in the Five Classics, he teaches Qi Shi and Shangshu.
After the deaths of Dong Zhongshu and Han Ying, Emperor Wu paid great attention to Xiahou Shichang.
Shichang knew the way of yin and yang. He once predicted the date when a fire would break out in Bailiang Terrace, and it turned out that a fire broke out on that day.
At that time, King Changyi was favored because he was the youngest. Emperor Wu chose a teacher for him, and Shichang became a tutor.
Shichang died of old age.
Xia Housheng, the son of his brother, was also famous as a Confucian scholar.
Xiahou Sheng's courtesy name is Chang Gong.
When the King of the Communist Party of Lu granted Ningxiang in western Lu to his son Jiehou, Ningxiang belonged to Dahe. Dahe was later renamed Shuping, so Xiahou Sheng was from Shuping.
summary: Suihong, courtesy name Meng, was from the state of Lu. Initially fond of cockfighting and horse racing, he later transformed his character and studied the "Spring and Autumn" with Ying Gong. Through his mastery of Confucian classics, he became a Yilang and reached the position of Fuli Jieliang. In the first month of the third year of Emperor Zhao's Yuanfeng reign, a great roar was heard south of Laiwu Mountain in Mount Tai. A large stone stood up by itself, measuring one to five feet high, as thick as forty-eight arm spans, and eight feet deep into the ground, with three other stones serving as its feet. Thousands of white crows gathered around it. Simultaneously, dead trees in the Changyi Shrine revived, and a broken willow in Shanglin Garden stood up and regained life, with insects eating its leaves into shapes resembling the words "Gongsun Bing has been established." Suihong interpreted these events through the "Spring and Autumn," concluding that stones and willows symbolized common people, while Mount Tai represented the site of imperial ceremonies. He argued that these phenomena indicated commoners would become emperors and the deposed Gongsun clan would revive. He advocated for the Han emperor to abdicate in favor of a worthy successor. His friend, an internal official, submitted this memorial. Since Emperor Zhao was young and General Huo Guang governed, Huo Guang was angered and had Suihong and his friend executed for treason. Five years later, when Emperor Xiaoxuan rose from the people to the throne, he recruited Suihong's son as a Lang. Xiahou Shichang, from Lu, was proficient in the Five Classics and taught Qi Shi and Shangshu. After Dong Zhongshu and Han Ying died, Emperor Wu valued him greatly. Shichang understood yin and yang, once predicting the exact date of a fire at Bailiang Terrace. He served as tutor to King Changyi and died of old age. His nephew Xiahou Sheng, courtesy name Changgong, was also a renowned Confucian scholar. Xiahou Sheng lost his father young but studied diligently, learning "Shang Shu" and "Hong Fan's Five Elements" from Shichang, and later studied under Jian Qing and Ouyang. He was sophisticated and learned from multiple teachers.
rel_path: 汉书/传/眭两夏侯京翼李传

translation:
Xia Housheng lost his father when he was young, but he was very studious. He studied "Shang Shu" and "Hong Fan's Five Elements" with Shi Chang, and discussed disasters and strange phenomena.
Later, he studied under Jian Qing and then studied under Ouyang.
Xia Housheng was sophisticated and proficient in learning, and he studied under more than one person.
Xia Housheng is good at telling the ceremony of dress.
He was recruited as a doctor and Guanglu doctor.
At this time, Emperor Zhao died and King Changyi succeeded to the throne. King Changyi often traveled.
One time, Xia Housheng blocked the carriage of the King of Changyi and came forward to remonstrate: "It has been overcast for a long time without raining, which may lead to some ministers plotting against the emperor. Where else is your majesty going to go?"
The king of Changyi was furious and said that Xia Housheng was deceiving the public with his evil words, so he tied him up and handed him over to the officials.
The official reported the incident to the general Huo Guang, but Huo Guang did not punish Xiahou Sheng.
At this time, Huo Guang and the cavalry general Zhang Anshizheng were discussing how to depose the king of Changyi.
Huo Guang blamed Zhang Anshi for leaking the truth, but in fact An Shi did not leak it.
So Xia Housheng was interrogated, and Xia Housheng replied: "The Biography of Hong Fan" says that if an emperor does not rule according to the rules, he will be punished by the constant evil. At this time, there will be a crusade against him by the subordinates. It is just because the taboo is so obvious, so it is only said that there are ministers plotting against the emperor.
Huo Guang and An Shi were both shocked, and they valued Confucian scholars even more from then on.
More than ten days later, Huo Guang and An Shi finally petitioned the Queen Mother to depose King Changyi and establish Emperor Xuan.
Huo Guang believed that the ministers reported political affairs to the East Palace and the Queen Mother inspected government affairs, so they should understand the classics, so he asked Xia Housheng to teach the Queen Mother "Shangshu".
After Xiahou's victory, he was appointed as the Shaofu of Changxin and was given the title of Marquis of Guannei. He participated in the planning of the abolition of the establishment and the major decision-making of the ancestral temple and the country. Later, he was added to the food fiefdom of a thousand households.
As soon as Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he wanted to praise Emperor Wu's achievements. Prime Minister Xuan Shao said: In my humble status, I have received the kindness of my ancestors, inherited the saint's career, and worshiped the ancestral temple. I dare not forget it day and night.
Emperor Xiaowu himself was benevolent and righteous, and he was mighty and swift. He went north to conquer the Xiongnu, and the Chanyu fled far away. He went south to pacify Diqiang, Kunming, and Ouluo. He went east to pacify Ling, Raccoon, and Korea. He opened up our territory and established prefectures and counties. All barbarian countries also surrendered. Well-known envoys came uninvited. Precious tributes were displayed in the ancestral temple. Harmonious rhythms, Transform the songs of Yuefu, recommend them to heaven, seal Mount Tai, build Mingtang, change the month of Jianyin as the first year of the year, and change the colors of chariots and horses for sacrifice; create the achievements of saints, respect the virtuous and reward the meritorious, revive the decayed princes and noble families, praise the descendants of the Zhou Dynasty; sacrifice to heaven and earth with complete and grand gifts, and make the road of Taoism more bright and upright.
God also rewarded him. Various auspicious symbols and auspicious signs were fulfilled. A treasure tripod was unearthed from the ground, a white lin was obtained, a big fish was caught from the sea, gods and saints appeared, and even the mountains were saying long live.
His merits and virtues are so vast that they cannot be mentioned here. However, his temple music does not match his great achievements. I really feel sad for this.
So I brought this matter up to discuss with the princes, Erqianshi, and the wise men.
summary: When King Changyi succeeded Emperor Zhao, he frequently traveled. Xiahou Sheng once blocked the king's carriage to remonstrate, warning that prolonged overcast weather without rain indicated ministers plotting against the emperor. The king was furious and had him bound, but Huo Guang did not punish him. When Huo Guang and Zhang Anshi were discussing deposing the king, Xiahou Sheng explained his prediction came from the "Hong Fan" biography, which stated that when an emperor rules improperly, subordinates will rebel. Huo Guang and Anshi were impressed and valued Confucian scholars more thereafter. They eventually petitioned the Queen Mother to depose King Changyi and establish Emperor Xuan. Xiahou Sheng was appointed Shaofu of Changxin and given the title of Marquis of Guannei.
