translation:
So the ministers had a heated discussion in the court, and they all said: It should be like the imperial edict.
Xia Housheng, the Shaofu of Ganmu Duchangxin, said: Although Emperor Wu did have the merit of defeating the barbarians and opening up the territory, he killed many ministers and people, exhausting the people's financial resources and squandering them. The world was very weak, the people were displaced, and more than half of them died.
Locust plagues spread across thousands of miles of bare land, and tragedies of cannibalism even occurred. The original reserve accumulation has not yet been restored.
Therefore, Emperor Wu was not benevolent to the people and could not establish another temple music for him.
The ministers all criticized Xia Housheng and said, "This is Shao Shu."
Xia Housheng said: This Shao calligraphy cannot be used.
As a minister, you should tell the truth and not bend your will to suit other people's wishes.
I've said what I want to say, and I won't regret it even if I die.
So Prime Minister Yi and Yushi Guangming impeached Xia Housheng for talking nonsense about Shaoshu, slandering the late emperor, and treason. Moreover, Prime Minister Huang Ba also refused to impeach Xia Housheng because he indulged Xia Housheng, and both of them were thrown into prison.
So the officials in charge asked the Temple of Emperor Wu to be revered as the Temple of Sejong, and perform music and dance performances of "Shengde", "Wenshi", and "Five Elements", and worship them for generations to come to highlight the virtues.
The forty-nine counties that Emperor Wu visited also had temples, just like Gaozu and Taizong.
Xia Housheng and Huang Ba have been imprisoned for a long time. Huang Ba wanted to learn Confucianism from Xia Housheng, but Xia Housheng rejected him on the grounds that he had been sentenced to death. Huang Ba said: If you hear the Tao in the morning, you will die in the evening.
Xia Housheng thought he spoke very well, so he taught him Confucian classics.
Another winter passed like this, but the lectures remained the same.
In the summer of the fourth year of Emperor Xuan's reign, there was an earthquake or landslide in the forty-nine counties of Guandong on the same day. City walls and houses collapsed, and more than 6,000 people died.
Emperor Xuan wore plain clothes and did not attend court in the main hall. He sent ministers to express condolences to officials and people, and gave the deceased money to pay for his coffin.
Emperor Xuan issued an edict saying: The occurrence of disasters is a warning from heaven and earth to us.
I inherited the achievements of my ancestors and placed myself above the people, but I did not let them live a good life.
In the past, there was an earthquake in Beihai and Langye, which damaged the ancestral temple. I was also very afraid. All the learned men among the princes and the middle two thousand stones, if you can find a way to deal with the disaster and make up for my shortcomings, don't be afraid.
So a general amnesty was granted to the whole country. Xia Housheng was pardoned and served as an admonition to the officials, and Huang Ba was appointed as the assassin of Yangzhou.
Xia Housheng was a simple and upright man, approachable but not dignified.
When meeting Emperor Xuan, he addressed Emperor Xuan as king, and addressed his colleagues by names in front of Emperor Xuan. These practices were not etiquette, but Emperor Xuan became closer and more trusting to him because of these practices.
summary: When Emperor Xuan wanted to honor Emperor Wu's achievements, Xiahou Sheng opposed, arguing that although Emperor Wu defeated barbarians and expanded territory, he killed many ministers, exhausted resources, and caused widespread suffering and cannibalism. The ministers impeached Xiahou Sheng for slandering the late emperor, and he was imprisoned. After an earthquake killed over six thousand people, Emperor Xuan issued a general amnesty, and Xiahou Sheng was pardoned and served as an admonition official. He was known for his forthrightness, addressing the emperor as "king" and calling colleagues by name in court. Emperor Xuan trusted him for this honesty. Xiahou Sheng died in office at ninety, and the Queen Mother mourned him for five days.
rel_path: 汉书/传/眭两夏侯京翼李传

translation:
One time after Xiahou Sheng was received, he went out to tell others what Emperor Xuan had said. Emperor Xuan heard about it and blamed Xiahou Sheng. Xiahou Sheng replied: Your Majesty said it very well, so I will publicize it.
Yao's words spread throughout the world and are still recited today.
I thought these words could be spread, so they spread.
The last time the court had something important to discuss, because Emperor Xuan had always known that Xia Housheng was very forthright, Emperor Xuan would say to Xia Housheng: Sir, please speak frankly, don't be afraid because of past events.
Xia Housheng once again became the Shaofu of Changxin, and was promoted to Prince Taifu.
He was ordered by Emperor Xuan to write "Shangshu" and "The Analects of Confucius" and was given a hundred pounds of gold.
Xia Housheng died in office when he was ninety years old. He was given a cemetery and buried in Pingling.
The Queen Mother gave him two million and wore mourning clothes for Xiahou Sheng for five days to repay his master's kindness. Confucian scholars were proud of it.
In the past, Xia Housheng often told his students in lectures: Confucian scholars are most afraid of not understanding the classics. If they can master the classics, getting a high official will be as easy as picking up grass on the ground.
If you are not good at studying the classics, you might as well go home and farm.
Among the children of Xia Housheng's uncles, there was a man named Jian named Changqing. Since he became a teacher of Xia Housheng and Ouyang Gao, he often asked questions about doubts. He also asked Confucian scholars who studied the "Five Classics" and asked them about the differences from "Shang Shu".
Xia Housheng disagreed with this. He said: Xia Houjian is the kind of little Confucian who only seeks words and sentences, and has made Confucianism and Taoism into pieces.
Xiahou Jian was also dissatisfied with Xiahou Sheng. He thought that Xiahou Sheng was not knowledgeable and could not cope with the enemy.
Xiahou Jian finally established his own school in Confucian classics. He served as Dr. Yilang and became the prince's young master.
Xiahou Sheng's son Xiahou also served as Zuocao Taizhong's doctor, his grandson Xiahou Yao served as the official of Changxin Shaofu, Sinong, and Honglu, and his great grandson Xiahoufan served as county governor, prefectural pastor, and Changle Shaofu.
Xiahou Shang, the son of Xiahou Sheng's half-brother, became Liang Neishi, and Xiahou Shang's son Dingguo became the prefect of Yuzhang.
Xiahou Jian's son Qianqiu also served as the Shaofu and Prince Shaofu.
Jingfang, whose courtesy name is Junming, was born in Dunqiu, Shujun County.
He studied "The Book of Changes" and studied under Jiao Yanshou from Liang Dynasty.
The word for longevity is Gan.
Jiao Gan was born in a poor family, but because of his love of learning, he received courtesy from the King of Liang. The King of Liang provided him with the necessary expenses so that he could study with peace of mind.
After completing his studies, Jiao Gan served as county historian and was selected to replace Xiaohuang County Magistrate.
Because Jiao Gan could often know evil things in advance, the thieves did not dare to commit crimes.
Jiao Gan also cared deeply about lower-level officials and ordinary people, so the atmosphere in Xiaohuang County was very good.
As a result, his political performance scored very high in the examination, and according to regulations, he should be promoted to another official. However, the three elders of Xiaohuang County wrote a letter expressing their hope to keep Jiao Gan. As a result, the edict was issued to allow Xiaohuang County to keep Jiao Gan and increase his salary. Jiao Gan died in Xiaohuang County.
Jiao Gan often said: The person who can get my way but die because of it must be Jingfang.
Jiao Gan was the best at talking about disasters. He connected the sixty-four hexagrams with things to be done every day, and used meteorological changes such as wind, rain, cold and temperature as symptoms, each with its own calculation and fulfillment.
summary: Jingfang, courtesy name Junming, studied "The Book of Changes" under Jiao Yanshou. Jiao Gan, his teacher, was known for predicting evil events and governing Xiaohuang County well. Jingfang was particularly skilled in connecting hexagrams with daily events and using meteorological changes as symptoms. During Emperor Yuan's reign, he predicted events accurately and was frequently consulted. He warned about disasters and criticized the appointment of flattering officials like Shi Xian. Jingfang recommended implementing a system to inspect officials' performance, but faced opposition from powerful ministers. He was eventually appointed prefect of Wei County but feared being isolated from the emperor. After sending several sealed memorials warning about yin energy overwhelming yang and predicting disasters, he was imprisoned and executed at age forty-one.
rel_path: 汉书/传/眭两夏侯京翼李传

translation:
More than a month after Jingfang left, he was finally thrown into prison.
At the beginning, Zhang Bo, the uncle of King Xian of Huaiyang, studied with Jingfang and married his daughter to Jingfang.
Jingfang was very close to Zhang Bo. After every court meeting, he always told Zhang Bo what the emperor said, thinking that the emperor originally wanted to adopt Jingfang's opinions, but the ministers were afraid that this would harm their own interests, so Jingfang was ostracized by everyone.
Zhang Bo said: King Huaiyang is the emperor's younger brother. He is agile and knowledgeable, likes to engage in politics, and wants to be loyal to the country.
Now I would like to ask the King of Huaiyang to write a letter requesting to join the court to assist you.
Jingfang said: I'm afraid not.
Zhang Bo said: In the past, the king of Chu had recommended scholars to the court, why couldn't the king of Huaiyang do the same?
Jingfang said: Zhongshu Ling Shi Xian and Shangshu Ling Wulu Chongzong colluded with each other. They are treacherous villains who have served the emperor for more than ten years. There is also Prime Minister Wei Hou. They have not done anything good for the people for a long time, so they have no merit.
These are the people who are particularly unwilling to implement the system of inspecting the performance of officials.
It would be best if the King of Huaiyang could come to court and advise the emperor to implement the system of inspecting officials. If that doesn't work, just say that the prime minister and Zhongshu Ling have been doing things for a long time but have not managed them well. You can remove the current prime minister and replace him with the imperial censor Zheng Hong. Let the current Zhongshu Ling be reassigned to another official position and replace him with Goudun Ling Xu Li. In this way, my suggestion of inspecting the officials can be implemented.
Zhang Bo completely listened to what Jingfang said about various disasters and strange events, so he asked Jingfang to write a memorial for the King of Huaiyang to meet the emperor, and wrote all these to the King of Huaiyang.
Shi Xian secretly investigated, and he knew all these things, but because Jingfang was close to the emperor, he did not dare to say anything.
When Jingfang became the county governor, Shi Xian falsely accused Jingfang of conspiring with Zhang Bo to slander the government, speak ill of the emperor, and implicate the princes and princes. This has been mentioned in the "Biography of King Xian".
At first, Jingfang was summoned to talk about the affairs of King You and King Li. After he came out, he told Zheng Hong, the imperial censor.
Jingfang and Zhang Bo were both executed in Zha City and their bodies were displayed on the street. Zheng Hong was also implicated and was dismissed from office and became a civilian.
Jingfang's original surname was Li, but he later changed his surname to Jing according to Lu's own calculation. He was only forty-one when he died.
Yi Feng, courtesy name Shaojun, was from Xiapi, Donghai.
He studied "Qi Shi" and studied under the same teacher as Xiao Wangzhi and Kuang Heng.
The three of them were all proficient in the classics. Kuang Heng was a junior and hoped to apply the classics to political affairs, while Yi Feng was diligent in studying and did not want to be an official, and liked the art of calendar yin and yang divination.
Not long after Emperor Yuan came to the throne, many Confucian scholars recommended him. He was conscripted into the office of eunuchs waiting for edicts. He wrote many times to express his opinions and was summoned to the emperor in his spare time. The emperor respected him very much.
At this time, Pingchang Hou Wanglin, because he was a relative of Emperor Xuan, served as his minister, and said that he would study Confucian classics with Yi Feng.
Yi Feng refused to talk to him, so he wrote a sealed memorial saying: I heard from my teacher that the most important thing in treating people is to know the good and evil of people.
summary: Yi Feng, courtesy name Shaojun, studied "Qi Shi" and was diligent in learning, preferring calendar and yin-yang divination to officialdom. Emperor Yuan respected him greatly. Yi Feng wrote extensively about using the twelve laws to understand human emotions and predict disasters. He warned about the dangers of powerful relatives and advocated for frugality, criticizing excessive palace construction. He proposed moving the capital to Chengzhou to reform institutions and reduce expenses. Although Emperor Yuan found his views unusual, Yi Feng became a doctor and admonishing official, dying in old age.
rel_path: 汉书/传/眭两夏侯京翼李传

translation:
I am very worried and trembling, fearing that the country will gradually weaken and perish.
Thinking that it has been two hundred years since the rise of the Han Dynasty, the fortune of the country has begun again, the emperor has given me grace to protect me, and the country has regained the fortune to bear the destiny of heaven. Although I have no saintliness, how dare I not obey and accept the great destiny of heaven. We must work with the people of the world to eliminate the old and establish the new.
I hereby decree a general amnesty for the whole world, and regard the second year of Jianping as the first year of Taichu. My title is Emperor Chen Sheng and Liu Taiping.
The scale of the clepsydra is divided into one hundred and twenty degrees.
Announce it to the world and let everyone know clearly.
More than a month passed after this, and the emperor was still ill.
He Liang and others wanted to make random changes in political affairs, but the ministers advised the emperor that they could not allow it.
He Liang and others reported that the ministers did not know the destiny, so they should dismiss the prime minister and censor, and use Jie Guang and Li Xun to assist the government.
Because what they said before had no effect, the emperor handed He Liang and others over to the law enforcement officials and issued an edict saying: I can succeed to the throne and protect the ancestral temple, but my governance is poor and disasters occur frequently. I am worried and afraid, and I don't know what to do.
After the edict, He Liang and others suggested that changing the name of the Yuan Dynasty and increasing the scale of the clepsydra would make the country more stable for a long time.
I did not believe in the teachings of the saints and misunderstood their words, hoping to seek blessings for the people.
But in the end there was no good effect, and the long-term drought caused disaster.
He questioned He Liang and others about this, and they replied that the system should be changed again. Everything he said deviated from the meaning of the scriptures, violated the system of the saints, and was inappropriate for the times.
Making a mistake and refusing to correct it is the real mistake.
All the edicts issued on Jiazi Day in June were abolished except for the Amnesty Day Order.
He Liang and others have deviated from the truth and confuse the public with their evil words. Their crimes must be thoroughly investigated.
They were all imprisoned. Guanglu Xunping, Guanglu doctor Mao Moru, Yushi Zhongcheng and Tingwei jointly tried the case and sentenced He Liang and others to use evil ways to disrupt the government, subvert the country, deceive the emperor and commit treason.
He Liang and others were all killed.
Li Xun's crime was reduced to one level and he was exiled to Dunhuang County.
Praising: "Book of Changes" and "Spring and Autumn" should be recommended first among those who can profoundly explain the supernatural powers of gods and understand the way of heaven and man.
However, Zigong still said: We can hear the Master's articles, but we cannot hear the Master's remarks about sex and the way of heaven.
Since the founding of the Han Dynasty, those who have speculated on the differences between yin and yang in discussing disasters include Dong Zhongshu and Xiahou Shichang during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu; Suimeng and Xiahou Sheng during the reigns of Emperors Zhao and Xuan; Jingfang, Yifeng, Liu Xiang, and Gu Yong during the reigns of Emperors Yuan and Cheng; and Li Xun and Tian Zhongshu during the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping.
These are some of the famous figures whose theories were adopted by the monarchs of the time.
Looking at what they said, it seems to be exactly the same.
Under the guise of borrowing scriptures and relying on anomalies in celestial phenomena to discuss the gains and losses of political affairs, sometimes it is unavoidable to make repeated guesses.
summary: Li Xun, courtesy name Zichang, studied "Shangshu" and liked theories of disasters and strange phenomena. He served under various officials and warned about impending floods and chaos. During Emperor Ai's reign, he was summoned to discuss disasters and advised restraining relatives, selecting virtuous officials, and following seasonal orders. He later supported Gan Zhongke's forged texts about the Han dynasty's fate declining, advocating for changing the reign name to prolong the dynasty. Emperor Ai, ill for a long time, agreed and issued an edict changing the reign name to Taichu. When this had no effect, He Liang and others were executed for treason, and Li Xun was exiled to Dunhuang County. The historian's commentary notes that since the Han dynasty's founding, those who discussed disasters and yin-yang differences included Dong Zhongshu, Xiahou Shichang, Suimeng, Xiahou Sheng, Jingfang, Yifeng, Liu Xiang, Gu Yong, Li Xun, and Tian Zhongshu. Their theories were sometimes adopted by rulers but often led to imprisonment or death. Suimeng was brutally killed, and Li Xun was exiled—warnings for scholars who spoke frankly about current affairs, offending powerful ministers and meeting tragic ends.

translation:
Dou Ying, courtesy name Wangsun, was the son of Queen Xiaowen's cousin.
Tracing back to his father, he has lived in Guanjin for generations and likes to entertain guests.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, Baoying was the prime minister of Wu State, but was dismissed due to illness.
Emperor Xiaojing came to the throne and appointed Dou Ying as Zhan Shi.
Emperor Xiaojing's younger brother, King Liang Xiao, was doted on by his mother, Queen Mother Dou.
Once, when King Xiao of Liang entered the court, Emperor Xiaojing drank with his brothers.
There was no crown prince at this time, and when everyone had finished drinking, Emperor Xiaojing said calmly: After my death, I will pass the throne to King Liang.
Queen Mother Dou was very happy to hear this.
At this time, Dou Ying brought a glass of wine to the emperor and said: The world belongs to Emperor Gaozu, and the throne should be passed down from father to son. This is a legal restriction of the Han Dynasty. How can the emperor pass it on to King Liang?
The Queen Mother hated Bao Ying because of this, and Dou Ying also felt that Zhan Shi's official position was too young, so she resigned due to illness.
The Empress Dowager then removed the name list that allowed Dou Ying to enter and leave the palace. During festivals, he was not allowed to enter the palace to see him.
In the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, Wu and Chu rebelled. At this time, the emperor investigated and found that neither the Liu clan nor the Dou family members were as wise as Dou Ying, so he recruited Dou Ying. After Dou Ying came to see him, he resolutely declined, saying that he was ill and could not take on this important task.
The Queen Mother also felt ashamed.
The emperor said: "Now the world is in crisis, how can Wang Sun refuse?"
So he made Dou Ying a general and rewarded him with a thousand pieces of gold.
At this time, Yuan An, Le Bu and other famous generals and wise men retired from their posts and stayed at home, so Dou Ying recommended them to Emperor Jing to recruit them.
Dou Ying placed all the gold given to him by the emperor in the hallway. Whenever his military officials came to see him, he would ask them to use the gold according to their own expenses. He never took the gold given by the emperor to his private residence.
Dou Ying sat in Rongyang and supervised the armies of Qi and Zhao.
After the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms was put down, Dou Ying was granted the title of Marquis of Wei.
At this time, many tourists and guests rushed to join Wei Qihou's family.
Whenever Emperor Xiaojing went to court to discuss important matters with his ministers, all the princes would not dare to treat him with courtesy like Tiaohou and Wei Qihou.
In the fourth year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he established Prince Li and ordered Wei Qihou to be the prince's teacher.
In the seventh year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, Prince Li was deposed. Wei Qihou argued for Prince Li many times, but to no avail. Wei Qihou claimed that he was ill and stayed at the foot of Nanshan Mountain in Lantian for several months. People named Dou, many guests and debaters asked him to come out, but he was unwilling to come out.
Liang Guoren Zhisui said to Bin Ying: The one who can make you rich is the emperor, and the one who can make you a confidant of the court is the Queen Mother.
Now the general is the master of the prince. The prince has been deposed and cannot fight for it. He cannot fight hard and cannot die. He retires due to illness, embraces a beautiful singer, and lives in Nanshan, refusing to go to the capital to see him.
Comparing these situations, it is obvious that you are exposing the emperor's fault.
If the emperor and the queen mother are dissatisfied with you and want to harm you, then your wife and children will be killed, and no one in the family will be left.
Dou Ying thought what he said was right, so he resumed his duties and went to court to see the emperor as before.
summary: Dou Ying, courtesy name Wangsun, was the son of Queen Xiaowen's cousin. He lived in Guanjin and enjoyed entertaining guests. During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he served as prime minister of Wu State but was dismissed due to illness. Under Emperor Xiaojing, he became Zhan Shi. When Emperor Xiaojing offered the throne to his brother King Liang Xiao, Dou Ying objected, citing Han law that the throne must pass from father to son. This angered Queen Mother Dou, leading to Dou Ying's resignation and exclusion from court. In the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, during the Wu-Chu rebellion, Dou Ying was appointed general and granted gold, which he distributed to his officers. After suppressing the rebellion, he was made Marquis of Wei. He later served as the prince's teacher but argued for the deposed prince, leading to his retirement. Persuaded by Zhisui, he resumed his duties. Despite Queen Mother Dou's recommendations, Emperor Xiaojing refused to make Dou Ying prime minister, citing his pride and rashness.

translation:
When Taohou was removed from his position midway, Empress Dowager Dou repeatedly recommended Wei Qihou to be the prime minister. Emperor Xiaojing said: Does the Queen Mother think that I am stingy by not letting Wei Qihou become prime minister?
Wei Qihou was proud and complacent, and often acted rashly and casually. It was difficult for him to be the prime minister and shoulder important responsibilities.
In the end, he was not appointed, but Wei Wan, Marquis of Jianling, was appointed as prime minister.
Tian Fu was the half-brother of Emperor Xiaojing and Queen Wang, and was born in Changling.
After Dou Ying became the general, he was in his prime. Tian Fu, then a minister and not yet a nobleman, went to and from Dou Ying's house, accompanying Yi Ying to drink, kneeling and rising, as if he were a junior member of the Dou family.
In the later years of Emperor Xiaojing's life, Danxuan became more and more noble and fortunate, and became a middle-aged doctor.
Tian Fu was very talented in literature and had studied some ancient books such as "Pan Yu". Queen Wang thought he was very talented.
Emperor Xiaojing passed away and Emperor Wu Liu Che had just ascended the throne. Tian Fu was named Marquis of Wu'an as his uncle, and Tian Sheng, Tian Fu's younger brother, was named Marquis of Zhou Yang.
Tian Fu had just gained power and was very humble to his retainers. He also introduced those who had not served as officials among his retainers and made them serve as officials, hoping to overwhelm the power of the generals and ministers in the court.
Most of the emperor's efforts to calm the political situation at that time were planned by Tian Fu's guests.
When the Prime Minister Wei Wan was dismissed due to illness, the Emperor discussed setting up the Prime Minister and the Taiwei.
He persuaded Tian Fu to borrow the opportunity and said: "Wei Qihou has been a noble man for a long time, and all the talents in the world have always been loyal to him. General, you have just become more prosperous and cannot be compared with Wei Qihou."
Even if the emperor intends to use the general as prime minister, the general must give up the position to Wei Qihou.
When Wei Qihou becomes prime minister, the general will definitely become a Taiwei.
The noble status of the Taiwei and the Prime Minister are the same. The general not only gets the Taiwei, but also has a good reputation of giving his position to the wise.
Tian Fu secretly revealed his thoughts to the Queen Mother and asked the Queen Mother to hint to the emperor. So Dou Ying was made prime minister and Tian Fu was made Taiwei.
I congratulated Dou Ying by taking advantage of his blessings, and advised him by the way: The nature of a prince is to like good and hate evil. Now good people praise the prince, so the prince can be the prime minister. But there are many evil people, and they will also slander the king.
If the ruler can be tolerant to both good and bad people, then the ruler's position is expected to last for a long time; otherwise, he will be slandered and leave his job immediately.
Dou Ying didn't listen to him.
Dou Ying and Tian Fu both liked Confucianism, so they elected Zhao Wan as the imperial censor and Wang Zang as the doctor.
Welcoming Lord Shen of Lu State to the capital and preparing to set up a Mingtang. Let the princes return to their respective fiefdoms, cancel the confinement, and uniform them according to ancient rituals to show peace.
He also reported all the descendants of the sinister clan and the clan, and all those with bad conduct would be removed from the genealogy.
At this time, the princes of the foreign relatives married many princesses and were unwilling to return to their fiefdoms. Therefore, the slanderous words of Dou Ying and others reached the ears of Queen Mother Dou every day.
The Queen Mother was interested in Huang Lao's scholarship, but Dou Ying, Tian Fu, Zhao Wan and others insisted on respecting Confucianism and belittling Taoism. Therefore, Queen Mother Dou became increasingly dissatisfied with Dou Ying and others.
In the second year of Jianyuan, Zhao Wan, the imperial censor, did not want the Queen Mother to continue to interfere in political affairs, so he asked the emperor not to make trouble against the Queen Mother in the future.
When Empress Dowager Dou found out, she was furious and said, "Are you trying to repeat Aragaki Ping's tricks?"
So Zhao Wan, Wang Zang and others were dismissed and expelled, and Dou Ying was removed from the post of prime minister and Tian Fu from the post of Taiwei. In addition, Bai Zhi Hou Xuchang was appointed as the prime minister, and Wuqiang Hou Zhuang Qingzhai was appointed as the censor.
From then on, Dou Ying and Tian Fu only lived at home as Hou.
Although Tian Fu, the Marquis of Wu'an, did not hold an official position, he was still favored by the emperor because of his relationship with the Queen Mother. He discussed political affairs many times, and most of them were adopted and came into effect. Those officials and scholars who were in favor of others left Wei Qihou Dou Ying and joined Tian Fu.
As a result, Marquis Wu'an became more and more arrogant day by day.
In the sixth year of Jianyuan, Empress Dowager Dou passed away. Prime Minister Xuchang and Yushi doctor Zhuang Qingzhai were removed from their official positions because they failed to organize the funeral.
The emperor then appointed Tian Fu as the prime minister and the chief minister Nong Han Anguo as the censor.
As a result, the scholars of the world, the officials of the prefectures, and the princes and kings became even more attached to Wu'an Marquis Tian Fu.
Tian Fu is ugly in appearance but considers himself to be very noble by nature.
He believed that the princes and kings at that time were all older, and the emperor had just ascended the throne and was very young. Tian Fu himself regarded the emperor's closest relative as the prime minister. If he did not thoroughly rectify the situation and use etiquette to restrain them, the people of the world would not obey.
At that time, the prime minister would often sit there for most of the day when he came in to perform business, and the emperor accepted all his suggestions.
Some of the people he recommended reached the position of two thousand stones, and their power almost exceeded that of the emperor.
The emperor then said: Have you used up all the people you want to appoint?
I also want to appoint a few people!
Once, he asked the emperor to allocate the official land of the examination room for him to expand his private residence. The emperor was furious and said to him: Why don't you take away my arsenal too?
summary: Tian Fu, half-brother of Emperor Xiaojing and Queen Wang, rose in prominence after Emperor Wu's ascension, becoming Marquis of Wu'an. He initially humbled himself before Dou Ying but later gained power. Tian Fu recommended Dou Ying as prime minister while becoming Taiwei himself. Both favored Confucianism, promoting Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, and planned to establish a Mingtang. However, Queen Mother Dou, a Huang-Lao adherent, opposed them, leading to their dismissal. Tian Fu remained influential due to his ties to the Queen Mother, while Dou Ying's power waned. After Queen Mother Dou's death, Tian Fu became prime minister, growing arrogant. He built lavish residences, acquired fertile lands, and received countless treasures. Dou Ying, by contrast, became alienated and powerless, finding solace only in his friendship with Guan Fu. In summary, Dou Ying and Tian Fu rose through family ties, while Guan Fu gained fame through valor. Their conflicts, fueled by pride and arrogance, led to their downfalls. Han Anguo's wisdom and loyalty were overshadowed by fate, and Wang Hui's war advocacy ended in tragedy.

translation:
After this time, he restrained himself a little.
Once, he invited guests to a banquet and asked his elder brother Gaihou to sit facing north, but he sat facing east. He believed that the prime minister of the Han Dynasty was noble and he could not wrong himself in private just because he was his elder brother.
From then on, Tian Fu, the Marquis of Wu'an, became even more arrogant. The residences he built were extremely gorgeous and majestic, surpassing those of all nobles. His fields and manors are extremely fertile, and there is an endless stream of people he sends to counties to buy valuable artifacts on the road.
There are bells, drums and music in the front hall, and there are hundreds of women in the back room.
The treasures, dogs, horses, antiques and furnishings presented to him by the princes are countless.
Contrary to Tian Fu, Wei Qihou Dou Ying became even more alienated, not reused, and had no power since the death of Queen Mother Dou. All the guests gradually retreated and even treated Dou Ying with arrogance. Only Guan Fu still treated him the same way.
Dou Ying felt depressed every day, but he only had a particularly good relationship with Guan Fu. Guan Fu, courtesy name Zhongru, was born in Yingyin.
His father was Zhang Meng, who had once been the servant of Guan Ying, the Marquis of Yingyin. He was very favored, so he promoted him to an official of two thousand shi, so he took the surname of Guan and changed his name to Guan Meng.
When Wu and Chu were in power, Guan Ying, Marquis of Yingyin, was a general and was subordinate to Taiwei Zhou Yafu. He recommended Guan Meng to the Taiwei as a school lieutenant.
Guan Fu also brought a thousand people with him to be with his father.
At that time, Guan Meng was already very old, and the Taiwei did not want to use him. However, because Marquis Yingyin firmly recommended him, he agreed to let Guan Meng be the captain. Therefore, Guan Meng was depressed and frustrated. Whenever he fought, he often broke into the enemy's strong points, so he died in the Wu army.
According to the military law of the Han Dynasty at that time: if both father and son were in the army, and if someone died in the war, the surviving people could escort the remains back to their hometowns.
But Guanfu refused to do this. He said impassionedly: I am willing to behead the king of Wu or the general of Wu to avenge my father.
So Guan Fu put on his armor and held a halberd, and recruited dozens of strong men in the army who were friendly with him and willing to go with him. When they walked out of the gate of the military camp, no one dared to go forward. Only two people and more than ten slaves under Guan Fu's horse rushed into the Wu army and attacked until they were under the Wu army's general flag, killing and wounding dozens of people.
Because he could no longer attack, he rushed back to the Han army's camp. All the slaves he brought out died in the battle, and only he and a knight returned.
Guan Fu suffered more than a dozen serious injuries on his body. He happened to have precious medicine to heal the wounds, so he survived.
Guan Fu's wounds recovered slightly, and he asked the general again: "I now know more about the twists and turns of the Wu camp. Please allow me to go there again."
The general admired Guan Fu's courage and sympathized with his behavior. He was worried that Guan Fu's life would be in danger if he went again, so he reported it to the Taiwei, who then firmly stopped him and refused to let him go.
When the Wu army was defeated, Guan Fu became famous all over the world.
Marquis Yingyin reported Guan Fu's situation to the emperor, and the emperor appointed Guan Fu as lieutenant general.
summary: Guan Fu, courtesy name Zhongru, was born in Yingyin. His father, Zhang Meng, served Guan Ying and took the surname Guan. During the Wu-Chu rebellion, Guan Fu fought fiercely to avenge his father, earning fame despite severe injuries. He later served as a general but lost his position due to legal troubles. Known for his uprightness and disdain for flattery, Guan Fu respected the poor and insulted the powerful. He associated with heroes and rogues, amassing wealth and a large following. His family's arrogance in Yingchuan led to a local song warning of their downfall. After losing power, Guan Fu bonded with Dou Ying, each seeking to bolster the other's status. Their friendship deepened, though Guan Fu's bluntness often caused conflict.

translation:
After a while, Wei Qihou Dou Ying stood up to propose a toast. Only those who had old acquaintances with him left their seats, and the other half of the people just sat there without even leaving the table.
Guan Fu got up and left his seat, and toasted to Tian Fu one after another. When he came to Tian Fu, Tian Fu still sat there and said, "I can't drink a full cup anymore."
Guan Fu was very angry and said with a smile: "You are a noble man, but you still have to drink a full cup!"
But Tian Fu refused to toast.
A toast came to Lin Ruhou Guan Xian. Guan Xian was talking quietly to Cheng Bushi without moving away from his seat.
Guan Fu was so angry that he had nowhere to vent his anger, so he scolded Guan Xian and said, "Normally, it is worthless to slander Cheng Bu Shi. Now that the elders are toasting you, you are just like a girl, biting your ears and talking to Cheng Bu Shi."
Tian Fu said to Guan Fu: Cheng and Li are both guards in the East and West Palaces. Now that you insult Cheng Bushi in public, won't you leave room for your beloved General Li?
Guan Fu said, "I don't care if you kill my head or pierce my chest today. What else do I care about Cheng and Li?"
Seeing that the situation was not good, the guests at the table got up and excused themselves to go to the toilet, and gradually dispersed.
Shi Ying also stood up and left, waving to Guan Fu to leave quickly.
When Guan Fu had just left, Tian Fu said angrily: "It's my fault, because I spoiled him so much that he became so presumptuous."
He ordered his knights to detain Guan Fu so that Guan Fu could not leave.
Taking advantage of the blessing, he quickly got up and apologized to the prime minister for Guan Fu. He pressed his hand on Guan Fu's neck and asked him to bow his head and apologize.
Guan Fu became even more angry and refused to apologize.
Tian Gou then ordered the knights to tie up Guan Fu and keep him in the transfer house. He also called for Chang Shi and said to him: "Today we invite guests from the royal family to a banquet here in accordance with the order of the Queen Mother Shao."
So Guan Fu was impeached, saying that he insulted the guests at the banquet, insulted Shao Ling, and committed the crime of disrespect. He was imprisoned in the living room.
At the same time, a thorough investigation was made of Guan Fu's various illegal activities in Yingchuan, and officers were dispatched to arrest relatives of each branch of the Guan family. They were all sentenced to death by beheading in public.
Dou Ying felt so ashamed that he paid and sent guests to plead with the prime minister, but in the end he could not get Guan Fu released.
Since Tian Fu's subordinates were all the prime minister's eyes and ears, the people in Guan's family who had slipped through the net were all running away and hiding, and Guan Fu himself was being detained, so he could not report all the bad things Tian Fu had done secretly.
Dou Ying desperately tried to rescue Guan Fu, but his wife persuaded him: General Guan offended the prime minister and went against the Queen Mother's family. Can he be saved?
Dou Ying said: I earned the Marquis by myself, and now I throw it away without any regrets.
Besides, I can't let Guan Zhongru die alone, while I, Dou Ying, live alone.
So he went out privately to write to the emperor without telling his family.
The emperor read the memorial of Wei Qihou Dou Ying and immediately summoned him into the palace. Dou Ying explained in detail the situation where Guan Fu made a mistake because he was drunk at the banquet, and believed that it was just a trivial matter of excessive drinking and not worthy of the death penalty. The emperor agreed with him, so he gave Dou Ying a meal together and said to him: "You can go to the Empress Dowager of the Eastern Dynasty to plead her case in court."
When Dou Ying arrived in the Eastern Dynasty, he praised Guan Fu's merits and said that he made a blunder while drunk, but the prime minister used other crimes to frame Guan Fu.
Tian Fu then tried his best to slander Guan Fu for what he had done, which was arrogant and indulgent, and committed the crime of treason.
Baoying had no other choice but to attack the prime minister's shortcomings.
summary: Tian Fu once agreed to visit Dou Ying with Guan Fu but forgot, causing Guan Fu to confront him. At a banquet, Guan Fu insulted Tian Fu, leading to a rift. Tian Fu later demanded land from Dou Ying, who refused, deepening their enmity. In the fourth year of Yuanguang, Tian Fu reported Guan Fu's family's arrogance, and Guan Fu retaliated by exposing Tian Fu's misdeeds. At a wedding feast for Tian Fu, Guan Fu insulted guests, leading to his arrest. Tian Fu accused him of disrespect, and Dou Ying tried to save him, arguing his drunken mistake was minor. In court, Tian Fu slandered Guan Fu as treasonous. The emperor asked ministers to judge, but opinions were divided. Queen Mother Dou pressured the emperor, leading to Guan Fu's execution and Dou Ying's imprisonment. Dou Ying was later executed for allegedly forging an imperial edict. Tian Fu died soon after, haunted by ghosts of Dou Ying and Guan Fu. His son's title was later revoked.

translation:
Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng lobbied King Xiao and asked him to request to be the heir to the throne and increase the fiefdom. They were afraid that the ministers of the Han court would not agree, so they secretly sent people to assassinate the powerful advisers of Moting.
When Yuan An, the former Prime Minister of Wu, was killed, Emperor Jing heard about the plans of Gongsun Gui, Yang Sheng and others, so he sent people to capture Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng.
The Han Dynasty sent many envoys to Liang one after another, and a nationwide search was carried out from the Prime Minister of Liang on down. After more than a month, no one was caught.
The internal history of Han Anguo heard that Gongsun Gui, Yang Sheng and others were hiding in Xiaowang's palace, so he went to the palace to see the king and cried and said: If the monarch is humiliated, the ministers should die.
The king has no good ministers, so things have become such a mess.
Now that I can't catch Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng, please let me say goodbye to you and grant my death.
King Liang said: "Why are you doing this?"
Han Anguo burst into tears for several lines and said: The king himself is thinking about the relationship between you and the emperor. Compared with the Supreme Emperor and Emperor Gao, or the emperor and King Linjiang, who is closer?
King Xiao said: Not as good as them.
An Guo said: The Supreme Emperor, Prince Linjiang, Emperor Gao and the Emperor all have a father-son relationship, but Emperor Gao said that I am the one who conquers the world with a three-foot sword, so the Supreme Emperor has never had the right to interfere in political affairs and only lives in Liangyang Palace.
King Linjiang was the eldest prince, but because his mother made a mistake, he was deprived of the title of King Linjiang; and because of the palace wall incident, he finally committed suicide in the Lieutenant's Mansion.
Why is this happening?
Because in governing the world, one cannot harm the public for private reasons.
As the saying goes: Although I have a biological father, how do I know that he is not a tiger?
Although he has a biological brother, how do you know that he will not turn into a wolf?
Now the king is a prince, but he listened to the false words of an evil official, violated the monarch's prohibition, and distorted the strict law.
Because of the Queen Mother, the Emperor cannot bear to use laws against you.
The Queen Mother cried at night, hoping that the king would realize and change his ways, but the king still could not wake up.
If the Queen Mother dies, who else can you cling to, Your Majesty?
Before he finished speaking, King Xiao burst into tears and blamed himself to Han Anguo: "I will hand over Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng immediately."
On that day, Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng committed suicide.
The Han envoys returned to answer their orders, and Liang's troubles were completely resolved. This was all due to An Guo's contribution.
So Emperor Jing and Empress Dowager Dou valued Han Anguo even more.
After the death of King Xiao, King Gong came to the throne. Han Anguo lost his official position because of breaking the law and lived at home.
After Liu Che, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, ascended the throne, Tian Fu, Marquis of Wu'an, became the Taiwei, favored and trusted and held great power.
Han Anguo gave five hundred gold to Tian Fu. Tian Fu mentioned Han Anguo to the Queen Mother. The emperor often heard about Anguo's talents, so he called him the captain of the North, and later he was promoted to Da Si Nong.
summary: Han Anguo, courtesy name Changru, was born in Cheng'an County, Liang State. He studied Han Feizi and served King Xiao of Liang during the Wu-Chu rebellion, helping repel the Wu army. After the rebellion, his reputation grew. When Emperor Jing was displeased with King Liang's extravagance, Han Anguo defended him to the eldest princess, easing tensions. He later became internal history of Liang, resolving conflicts by persuading King Xiao to surrender conspirators. After King Xiao's death, Han Anguo lost his position but regained favor under Emperor Wu through Tian Fu's patronage. He became a censor and advocated peace with the Xiongnu, opposing Wang Hui's war plans. Despite initial success, the Mayi ambush failed, and Wang Hui committed suicide. Han Anguo later served as a general but was demoted due to military setbacks. He died of illness, frustrated and unhappy. His colleague Husui, a virtuous official, also died before becoming prime minister.

translation:
Zhai Fangjin, courtesy name Ziwei, was from Shangcai, Runan.
His family has been humble and humble for generations. Fang Jin's father Zhai Gong was fond of learning and served as a county scholar.
When Fang Jin was twelve or thirteen years old, his father died and he could no longer continue his studies. He worked as a minor historian in the prefect's mansion. He was considered slow and could not do good things, and was repeatedly scolded and insulted by the governor.
Fang Jin was very sad, so he went to meet Cai's father in Runan and asked him what he was suitable for.
Cai's father thought that his appearance was unusual and told him: You have the bone image of a feudal lord. You should use it according to the classics and study the knowledge of Confucian scholars.
Fang Jin was tired of being a minor historian. After hearing what Cai's father said, he felt very happy, so he returned home saying he was ill, said goodbye to his stepmother, and wanted to go west to the capital to study scriptures.
His mother felt pity for Fang Jin when he was young, so she came to Chang'an with him, knitted shoes for him to study, and taught him "Spring and Autumn" by a doctor.
After more than ten years of accumulation and study, he became proficient in Confucian classics, and his number of disciples increased day by day, and all the Confucian scholars praised him.
Take Shece Jiake as the man.
Two or three years later, he was promoted to Mingjing and moved to Yilang.
At this time, there was a mature and knowledgeable scholar Hu Chang from Qinghe, who was studying the same classics as Fang Jin.
Hu Chang was a senior, but his reputation was not as good as Fang Jin's. He was jealous of Fang Jin's talent, and did not praise Fang Jin when discussing.
After Fang Jin knew about it, he waited for Hu Chang to gather his students to give lectures, and sent students under his disciples to Hu Chang's place to ask for advice on difficult issues in the scriptures, and record Hu Chang's teachings accordingly.
After such a long time, Hu Chang felt uneasy knowing that Fang Jin respected and humbled him. From then on, he was known as Fang Jin among the scholar-bureaucrats, and they became close friends.
During the Heping period, Fang Jin became a doctor.
A few years later, he was moved to Shuofang as governor. When serving as an official, he is not cumbersome and harsh, and his observations are carried out in an orderly manner, which is very prestigious.
He reported to the imperial court many times and was moved to the position of Prime Minister Sizhi.
He followed Emperor Cheng to Ganquan and drove on the Chi Road. Chen Qing, the captain of Sili School, impeached him, so Fang Jin had his carriage and horses confiscated.
After arriving at Ganquan Palace, they gathered in the palace and talked with Chen Qing and Tingwei Fan Yanshou. At that time, Chen Qing was being impeached by a memorial. Chen Qing said himself: "What happened in the past should be punished as a crime. Now that the Minister has come with a memorial to impeach me, the verdict should be wrapped up here."
When I was a minister, I had something to report, but I suddenly forgot about it and put it aside for more than a month.
Fang Jin therefore impeached Chen Qing and said: Chen Qing was ordered to investigate and expose the ministers, so he was the minister. He understood that confidential matters were carefully arranged and planned, and the Ming Lord personally handled them without slacking off.
Chen Qing was guilty but did not punish him. He was not afraid of it and set up an example of not convicting him in advance.
summary: Zhai Fangjin, courtesy name Ziwei, was from Shangcai, Runan, born into a humble family. After his father died when he was twelve or thirteen, he worked as a minor historian but was often scolded. Seeking guidance, he consulted Cai's father in Runan, who noted his noble bone structure and advised him to study Confucian classics. Inspired, he feigned illness, left his job, and traveled to Chang'an with his stepmother, who supported him by knitting shoes. He studied the "Spring and Autumn Annals" under a doctor, and over a decade became proficient in Confucian classics, gaining many disciples and acclaim.

translation:
However, Juanxun was an official with two thousand stones. He was fortunate enough to be sent on an envoy, but he did not abide by the etiquette. He looked down upon the prime minister and despised the minister. He also distorted etiquette and lost his grace. He was treacherous and flattering and had no normal heart. He was dignified in appearance and cowardly in heart.
Those who destroy the dignity of the country and disrupt the order of the court should not hold official positions.
I request the Prime Minister to dismiss Juan Dong.
At that time, Taizhong doctor Ping was in charge of the affairs. He reported that Fang Jin was the minister of the country. He did not first correct himself to set an example for others. He had previously violated the law and drove on the road. Chen Qing, the minister, tried to impeach him fairly. Fang Jin did not feel guilty or regretful but harbored personal hatred. He recorded Chen Qing's chatting words in order to slander and deceive him and convict him.
Later, Prime Minister Xue Xuan asked to send a military official to supervise Sili Xiaowei because of a bad guy who killed six innocent family members. Sili Xiaowei Juanxun himself submitted a memorial to the court, and now Fang Jin impeached Juanxun again.
Commentators believe that Fang Jin does not use morality to assist the prime minister, but only favors and helps ministers. If he wants to win and establish authority, this source should be stopped and cut off.
Juanxun has always acted fairly and upright, and is disgusted by traitors. You can be a little tolerant and let him achieve his fame.
Because the emperor's impeachment by Fang Jin was appropriate, he could not abolish the law just because he suspected others of fraud in advance, so he demoted Juanxun to the rank of Changling Order.
Fang Jin dismissed two ministers in one year, and everyone in the court was afraid of him.
Prime Minister Xue Xuan valued Fang Jin very much and often warned the minister: "Serve Si Zhi with caution, and Zhai Fangjin will definitely be in power soon."
At this time, Changling was being built and the imperial mausoleums and cities were being built. Many of the emperor's internal and external relatives and the children and guests of his close ministers had exclusive power for personal gain. Fang Jin arranged for a historical inspection and revealed that tens of millions of filthy items had been secretly hidden.
The emperor believed that he was qualified for the position of public minister and wanted to use him to govern the people. He transferred him to the position of Jing Zhaoyin. Fang Jin attacked the powerful and powerful, and everyone in the capital was afraid of him.
At that time, Hu Chang was the governor of Qingzhou. When he heard about this, he wrote to Fang Jin: I heard privately that your decrees are very strict. With Jing Zhaoyin's talents, I am afraid that he will feel uncomfortable.
Fang Jin knew in his heart what Hu Chang was referring to, and then relaxed his dignity a little.
Fang Jin served as Jingzhaoyin for three years, and was promoted to imperial censor in the second year of Yongshi.
A few months later, Prime Minister Xue Xuan happened to be exempted from being a civilian because of the riots caused by thieves in the vast desert and the three auxiliary officials of Zha during the funeral of the Empress Dowager.
Fang Jin was also demoted to Zhijinwu because he was ordered to hold funerals when he was appointed Jingzhao Yin and disturbed the people.
Twenty days later, the official position of prime minister became vacant. Most of the ministers recommended Fang Jin. The emperor also valued Fang Jin's talents, so he promoted Fang Jin to be prime minister and made him the Marquis of Gaoling, granting him a land of thousands of households.
Fang Jin was already rich, but his stepmother was still alive. He paid attention to cultivating family conduct and worshiped his mother very piously and generously.
When his stepmother passed away and was buried twenty-six days later, he took off his funeral clothes and started working. He believed that as the prime minister of the Han Dynasty, he did not dare to go beyond the country's system.
As prime minister, he was impartial and honest, and did not ask the four counties and counties for personal matters.
The law is strict and strict, and the ministers and ministers are reported to the nine ministers. The laws are strict and detailed and are deeply slandered. There are many people who conspire to frame him.
summary: He passed the imperial exams, became a doctor during the Heping period, and later served as governor of Shuofang, known for orderly governance. He was promoted to Prime Minister Sizhi. While accompanying Emperor Cheng to Ganquan, he violated road rules, leading to his carriage being confiscated by Sili Xiaowei Chen Qing. Later, Fangjin impeached Chen Qing for disrespect, resulting in Chen's dismissal. He also impeached Juanxun, another Sili Xiaowei, for arrogance and disrespect, leading to Juanxun's demotion. Within a year, Fangjin dismissed two high officials, instilling fear in the court. As Jingzhaoyin, he cracked down on powerful families, but at Hu Chang's advice, he moderated his strictness. After three years, he became imperial censor, then prime minister and Marquis of Gaoling. He was impartial and strict, often impeaching ministers like Chen Xian and Feng Xin for corruption, leading to their dismissal. He also targeted Chunyu Chang's associates, removing over twenty officials. Despite his harshness, Emperor Cheng trusted him.

translation:
Even if the eagle's wings are injured, it will not escape.
It is indeed difficult to offend a noble relative's close friends. If they are offended, all the enemies will be resentful, and good and evil will cover up each other.
I am fortunate enough to serve as prime minister, and I dare not not do my best.
Ask the emperor to remove Zhu Bo, Sun Hong, and Chen Xian and return them to their former counties to eliminate the evil gangs and cut off the hope of the evil gangs.
The emperor is ready to play.
Chen Xian had been dismissed from office and prohibited from holding office again. He was sent back to his hometown and died of illness due to worry and anger.
Fang Jin was rich in knowledge and talent, and he also knew the law and officials. He decorated the law with elegant writing and was called the Tongming Prime Minister. The emperor valued him very much. Fang Jin reported to the emperor everything that was not in line with his wishes and ordered him. He also explored the emperor's hidden will to consolidate his position.
Previously, Dingling Marquis Chunyu Chang was a relative, but because he was good at strategy, he was listed as the Jiuqing. When he first took office, Fang Jin interacted with Chun Yuchang alone, praised and recommended him.
When Chun Yuchang was executed for treason, all those who were friendly to Chun Yuchang were dismissed from their posts because of him. Because Fang Jin was a minister, the emperor always valued him and concealed the secrets for him.
Fang Jin felt guilty and asked to resign and go home.
The emperor replied: Dingling Marquis Chunyu Chang has already confessed his crime. Although you associate with him, doesn't it say so in the scriptures? If you know your mistakes in the morning, you will correct them in the evening. A gentleman praises him. What doubts do you have?
Please stay focused and don't slack off. See your doctor and take medicine to take care of yourself.
Fang Jin just got up to do things, and reported one by one to Chunyu's elders, Yin Sunbao of Jingzhao and Xiao Yu of Youfufeng. There were more than 20 people who had been dismissed from their posts as governors with more than 2,000 shi. Fang Jin was trusted by the emperor.
Although Fang Jin studied "Gu Liang Zhuan", he loved "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and astronomical ephemeris. His "Zuo Shi Zhuan" was taught to the national teacher Liu Xin, and the ephemeris was taught to Chang'an Lingtian Zhongshu.
Fang Jin valued Li Xun and appointed him as Yi Cao.
Fang Jin had been prime minister for nine years. In the spring of the second year of Suihe, Mars entered the heart of the sky. Li Xun wrote in a memorial: You know the tactics of dealing with changes.
It has been reported many times in the past that Yingshisu, Dongjingsu, and Mars show signs and changes, and mountains, rivers, and springs show disasters contrary to common sense, but the rumors spread by the people have come true.
These three things have been fulfilled, which can be said to be chilling.
In this photo, the Ti star raises its horns, the Wandering Star is in the center of the arc, Sirius raises its horns, the Tiangong star shines, Venus crosses the sky, Saturn goes retrograde, the auxiliary stars sink and disappear, Mars guards the home for thirty years, and the day of death is approaching.
You have no merit in saving the world, and you have no excuse to be humble and avoid the virtuous people. If you want to be in a high position and be a minister without merit to protect yourself, how difficult it is!
The great punishment is getting worse day by day. How can we only guarantee the result of being expelled?
summary: Fangjin studied "Guliang Zhuan" but favored "Zuo Shi Zhuan" and astronomy. After nine years as prime minister, Mars entered the heart constellation, and his subordinate Li Xun warned of impending disaster. Fangjin grew anxious. The emperor later criticized him for poor governance and tax policies, but spared him. Fangjin committed suicide that day. The emperor honored him with posthumous titles and gifts.

translation:
When Zhai Yigang first launched his army, he wrote a letter saying that Yu, Xin and others had conspired with King Shuping Xiangfu to rebel. He arrested them and put them in shackles and handcuffs. In order to intimidate the masses, they first stigmatized each other for rebellion, and then arrested each other and put weapons on them. This was clear evidence that they would be defeated and exterminated.
Liu Xin's two sons, Guxiang Hou Zhang and Deguang Hou Tuna, have been arrested and executed. Zhai Yi's mother Lian, brother Zhai Xuan, and 24 relatives have also laid out their corpses in the streets of Chang'an.
When they were killed, there were many people watching and the weather was clear, which can be said to be in accordance with God's will.
The generals dispatched by destiny respectfully exercised heaven's punishment and attacked the enemies of the country. The results were very obvious and I am very satisfied.
Didn't "Sima Law" say it? Rewards should not be given beyond their due time.
This is to let everyone see the benefits of being kind as early as possible.
Now, fifty-five people including Sun Xian, the captain of chariots and cavalry, are enfeoffed as marquises, and the number of households and towns to be enfeoffed will be announced later.
Send envoys with gold seals, red ribbons, and red chariots to the army to confer duties.
Therefore, the world is amnesty.
At this time, the elite soldiers attacked and surrounded Zhai Yi in Yucheng and broke through the city. Zhai Yi and Liu Xin abandoned the army and escaped.
When they arrived at the border of Gushi, Wang Mang's army captured Zhai Yi and wrapped his body in the city for public display.
But Liu Xin was not caught in the end.
At first, Sanfu heard that Zhai Yi had raised an army, and thieves from twenty-three counties from the west of Maoling to Fen also rebelled. Ming, Huo Hong and others claimed to be generals, attacked and burned down the government, killed the captain of Youfu and the county magistrate of Ya, and looted and looted the officials and people, numbering more than 100,000. The fire burned all the way to the front hall of Weiyang Palace.
Wang Mang held the baby in his arms and prayed in the ancestral temple from morning to night.
Later, Wang Mang was appointed as a guard at the king level and was appointed General Huben. Yan Qian, Marquis of Dahonglu Wangxiang, was appointed General Zhechong. Together with Zhen Han and Wang Yan, he went west to attack Zhao Ming and others.
In the first month of the first month, Huya General Wang Yi and others returned from Guandong and led the army to conquer the west.
Wang Jun, the strong crossbow general, was dismissed from his post because he had not performed meritorious service, and Liu Xin, the Yangwu general, was restored to his old post.
Wang Mang also appointed Wang Yi's younger brother, Shizhong Wang Qi, as General Yangwu, General Chengmen Tso Hui as General Qiannu, and General Li Qin as General Weaning, and led the army to the west again.
In February, Tong Ming and others were wiped out, and all counties were pacified. Wang Mang's army returned to the court in victory.
Wang Mang then held a banquet in the White Tiger Palace, rewarded the general, and awarded him many titles.
Previously, the barbarians in Yizhou and the Qiang people outside the Jincheng Wall rebelled, and the army of the prefecture and county defeated them.
Wang Mang then recorded them all together. According to the merits, a total of 395 Hou Bozi men were enfeoffed. It was said that they were all enfeoffed because they were all out of anger. They conquered the west, Qiang bandits, and rebels against the enemy. In a moment, they were eliminated in time, and everyone in the world was convinced by their merits.
Wang Mang therefore believed that he had received great help from heaven and gods, and in December of that year, he usurped the throne and proclaimed himself emperor.
At first, Liu Li, the county magistrate of Wan who was arrested by Zhai Yi, heard that Zhai Yi had launched a mutiny, so he wrote a letter saying that he was willing to serve as a military official to fight against the rebellious ministers for the country. In fact, he wanted to avenge his personal grievances.
Wang Mang promoted Liu Li to be the prefect of Chenliu and granted him the title of Marquis of Mingde.
summary: His son Zhai Xuan was a gentleman, while another son, Zhai Yi, became a governor. During Wang Mang's regency, Zhai Yi rebelled, declaring Liu Xin emperor and amassing over 100,000 troops. Wang Mang crushed the rebellion, executing Zhai Yi and his family, and desecrating Fangjin's grave. The rebellion's failure led to Wang Mang's usurpation. Historian Ban Biao noted Fangjin's rise from poverty to prominence, but lamented Zhai Yi's doomed uprising.

translation:
Jing Wang Liu Jia, the cousin of Mo Gaozu Liu Bang, did not know when he participated in the uprising.
In the first year of Han Dynasty, when the king of Han Dynasty returned to the Three Qin Dynasty, Liu Mai was appointed as the general. After pacifying Sima Xin's territory, he followed Liu Bangdong to attack Xiangji.
The King of Han was defeated by Chenggao, crossed the Yellow River to the north, captured the armies of Zhang Er and Han Xin, and stationed their troops in Xiuwu County. On the one hand, they dug deep trenches and built high barriers; on the other hand, they sent Liu Mai to lead 20,000 troops and hundreds of cavalry to attack Chu, crossed Baima Jin, and entered the Chu land. They burned Chu's grain and grass, destroyed the Chu army's military supply, and made it impossible to supply food to King Xiang's army.
Soon, the Chu soldiers attacked, but Liu Jia always avoided it and did not fight the Chu soldiers. Instead, he and Peng Yue relied on each other to protect themselves.
The king of Han pursued Xiang Ji to Guling and sent Liu Mai to lead his troops south across the Huaihe River to surround Shouchun.
After returning, he sent people to alienate and recruit Zhou Yin, the great commander of Chu State, to surrender.
Zhou Yin rebelled against Chu and returned to Han, assisted Liu Mai in capturing Jiujiang, catered to Yingbu's army, fought at Gaixia, and defeated Xiang Yu.
Therefore, the King of Han sent Liu Jia to lead the Jiujiang soldiers, together with Taiwei Lu Wan, to attack Linjiang King Gongwei in the southwest. After Wei Gong's death, Linjiang was renamed Nanjun.
Since Liu Jia had achieved great military exploits, the emperor's son at that time was young, had few brothers, and was not very talented and virtuous. He wanted to make someone with the same surname king to conquer the world, so Xia Shao said: "General Liu Mai has meritorious service, and he is qualified to choose the king among his descendants."
The ministers said: Let Liu Mai be made King of Jing and take charge of Huaidong.
Six years later, King Yingbu of Huainan rebelled and attacked Jingdi eastward.
Liu Mai fought with him but failed to win. He fled to Fuling County and was killed by Yingbu's pursuers.
Liu Ze, King of Yan, was the brother of Gaozu and his great-grandfather.
In the third year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Liu Ze became a doctor.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, as a general, he led troops to defeat Chen Xi's general Wang Huang and was named Yinglinghou.
When Empress Gao was in power, Tian Sheng, a native of Qi, was short of funds when lobbying outside, so he turned to Liu Ze for help by offering suggestions.
Liu Ze was very happy and gave Tian Sheng two hundred pounds of gold when he passed away. Tian Sheng got the gold and immediately returned to Qi.
The following year, Liu Ze sent a messenger to Tian Sheng: We are no longer friends!
When Tian Sheng came to Chang'an, he did not go to see Liu Ze. Instead, he stayed in a big house and asked his son to find a way to work under Zhang Qing, the great emissary favored by Empress Lu.
A few months later, Tian Sheng's son invited Zhang Qing to his home as a guest, and Tian Sheng hosted a banquet for him in person.
Zhang Qing went there and was greatly surprised when he saw that the curtains and other decorative appliances wrapped in Tiansheng's house were in compliance with the standards of the princes.
When the wine was in full swing, Tian Sheng asked everyone to retreat and said to Zhang Qing: I have seen more than a hundred princes' postal residences, all of which were occupied by the meritorious officials of Emperor Gaozu.
summary: The histories of three Han dynasty princes: Liu Jia (King of Jing), Liu Ze (King of Yan), and Liu Bi (King of Wu). Liu Jia, a cousin of Emperor Gaozu, served as a general, leading campaigns against Chu forces, burning supplies, and later capturing Jiujiang. He was made King of Jing but was killed in battle against the rebel Yingbu. Liu Ze, a brother of Gaozu, was initially a marquis. Through a scheme by Tian Sheng, he was made King of Langye after persuading Empress Lu to enfeoff the Lü clan. After Empress Lu’s death, he joined others in supporting Emperor Xiaowen and was renamed King of Yan. His descendants included a son, Kang Wang, and a grandson, Dingguo, who committed adultery with his father’s concubine and sisters, leading to his suicide and the abolition of his state. Liu Bi, son of Liu Zhong, was made King of Wu after defeating Yingbu. He grew wealthy from copper and salt, and after his son was killed by the crown prince, he feigned illness and plotted rebellion. During Emperor Jing’s reign, Chao Cuo advocated reducing the princes’ territories, prompting Liu Bi to lead a rebellion of seven states (Wu, Chu, Zhao, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Jinan, and Zichuan) in 154 BCE. Liu Bi issued a call to arms, offering rewards for killing Han officials. Emperor Jing executed Chao Cuo to appease the rebels, but the rebellion continued. Zhou Yafu, a Han general, cut off Wu’s supply lines and defeated them. Liu Bi fled to Dongyue, where he was killed. The other rebel princes were also defeated or committed suicide. The text concludes that Liu Jia’s kingship was due to the unstable times, Liu Ze’s was based on a risky scheme, and Liu Bi’s rebellion stemmed from his wealth and personal grievance, leading to disaster.

translation:
Xiao He was from Peidi.
Because he could write documents without defects, he was appointed as an official of Pei Lord.
When Gaozu was still a commoner, Xiao He supported Gaozu in official affairs many times.
After Gaozu became the chief of the pavilion, he helped him again.
Gaozu went to Xianyang to serve as an official. The minor officials all contributed 300 yuan to see Gaozu off, but only Xiao He contributed 500 yuan.
Qin Yushi supervised the people of the county and was engaged in the inspection of his duties. Xiao He was awarded the post of official of Sishui County and was the best in the examination.
Qin Yushi planned to report to the court to recruit Xiao He, but Xiao He refused and was able to stay.
When Emperor Gaozu rose up and became Duke of Pei, Xiao He was appointed as the prime minister and governor.
When Pei Gong arrived in Xianyang, all the generals rushed to the treasury where gold and silk were stored to divide them up.
Only Xiao He went in first to collect the books on laws and regulations written by Qin Prime Minister and Censor. The reason why Pei Gong knew the fortresses in the world in detail, the number of households, the distribution of strength and weakness, and the people's hatred and sorrow was because Xiao He had received Qin's books.
Xiao He took over the remaining Ba and Shu as prime minister, pacified the people in the territory, and asked them to provide food for the army.
In the second year of the Han Dynasty, the king of Han and the princes attacked Chu. Xiao He stayed in Guanzhong, guarding the prince and governing Yueyang.
Formulate laws and regulations, establish ancestral temples, communities, palaces, and counties. They should be reported regularly and implemented if the emperor agrees. If it is too late to report the matter, then implement it in an appropriate manner and tell the Emperor after he comes back.
Calculating the number of households and transferring grain and wages to supply military supplies, the King of Han led his troops to escape many times. Xiao He often recruited soldiers from Guanzhong to supplement the front line. Therefore, the emperor specifically handed over Guanzhong affairs to Xiao He.
In the third year of the Han Dynasty, there was a confrontation with Xiang Yu in Beijing and Suo. The emperor sent envoys many times to comfort the prime minister.
Bao Sheng said to Xiao He: Your Majesty, your clothes are drying in the sun and the hood of your car is wet with dew, but you have comforted you many times. This is because you are suspicious of you.
For your sake, it would be better to send all your descendants and brothers who are capable of fighting into the army, so that the emperor will trust you more.
So Xiao He followed his plan, and the king of Han was very happy.
In the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu had passed away, and Liu Bang ascended the throne. He was awarded according to his merit. The ministers competed for merit. It was difficult to decide for more than a year. The emperor believed that Xiao He had made the greatest contribution, so he was first granted the title of Marquis of Feng, with a settlement of 8,000 households.
The heroes all said: We personally wore mail armor and held weapons. We experienced more than a hundred battles and dozens of rounds, conquering cities and territories.
Now Xiao He has no great achievements. He just expresses his opinions through writing and writing. He does not go to war, but his status is above us. Why is this?
The emperor said: Do you know about hunting? Everyone said: I know.
Asked again: Do you know hunting dogs?
Answered: I know.
The Emperor said: In hunting, dogs are the ones who chase and kill wild beasts, but humans are the ones who let loose and indicate where the wild beasts are.
Now you can only chase wild beasts, and the merit is similar to that of hunting dogs; as for Xiao He, he issues instructions, and the merit is the same as that of hunters.
And you are just following me with your own body, there are only three or two people, and dozens of people from Xiao He’s family are following me. The credit must not be forgotten!
summary: Xiao He, from Peidi, began his career as a meticulous official under Pei Lord, supporting the future Emperor Gaozu (then a commoner and later a pavilion chief) in official matters. When Gaozu served in Xianyang, Xiao He contributed 500 yuan for his farewell, exceeding the 300 yuan given by others. As an official in Sishui County, he excelled in inspections, but declined a court recruitment to remain. When Gaozu rose as Duke of Pei, Xiao He became his prime minister and governor. Upon entering Xianyang, while others seized gold and silk, Xiao He collected Qin’s legal and administrative books, enabling Gaozu to understand the empire’s geography, households, and people’s grievances. As prime minister, he governed Ba and Shu, pacifying the people and supplying the army. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, Xiao He stayed in Guanzhong, governing Yueyang, establishing laws, temples, and counties, reporting to the emperor when possible. He recruited soldiers and supplied grain, earning the emperor’s trust. During the confrontation with Xiang Yu, the emperor’s frequent consolations led Bao Sheng to advise Xiao He to send his capable relatives to the army to allay suspicion, which he did, pleasing the emperor. After Xiang Yu’s death, Liu Bang ascended the throne and awarded Xiao He first among the marquises, granting him 8,000 households. When ministers protested, the emperor compared their merit to hunting dogs and Xiao He’s to a hunter, silencing them. Later, Eqiu argued Xiao He’s contributions—preserving Guanzhong and supplying troops—were eternal, securing him the top rank. Xiao He was granted special court privileges.

translation:
From now on, all the ministers will not dare to say anything.
After the princes were awarded the title and their rankings were announced, they all said: Pingyang Hou Cao Shen was injured in seventy places. He made the greatest contribution to conquering the city and captured the territory, so he should be ranked first.
The emperor had already made the heroes surrender and granted Xiao He more titles. As for the position, there was no way to embarrass them anymore, but in his heart he still wanted Xiao He to be ranked first.
At that time, Eqiu, the Marquis of Guan Nei, came to visit him and said: "The opinions of all the ministers are wrong."
Although Cao Shen had the credit for strategically planning the country, this was only a temporary matter.
The emperor had a stalemate with Chu for five years, losing troops and generals, and fleeing many times. However, Xiao He often sent troops from Guanzhong to supplement them.
It wasn't the emperor's order to summon soldiers, but tens of thousands of people arrived when the emperor was in trouble.
Han and Chu had been guarding each other in Rongyang for many years, and there was no existing food in the army. Xiao He transferred food and wages from Guanzhong, and there was no shortage of supplies.
Although His Majesty lost Shandong many times, Xiao He always preserved Guanzhong and waited for His Majesty to return again. This is a tribute to all generations.
Now even if there are a hundred less people like Cao Shen, what will the Han lose?
The acquisition of Han does not necessarily have to wait for them to be preserved.
Why should the merit of one day be added to the merit of eternity!
Xiao He should be first, followed by Cao Shen.
The emperor said: OK.
So he made Xiao He the first, and gave him a sword and shoes to wear to the palace, so he didn't have to take small steps to enter the court.
The emperor said: I heard that those who want to be worthy will be rewarded. Although Xiao He's contribution is high, it can be clearly seen because of E Jun.
Therefore, Eqiu was granted the title of Marquis of Anping in addition to the two thousand households in the neighboring towns where Eqiu originally lived.
On this day, more than a dozen of Xiao He's parents and brothers were all rewarded with food.
Xiao He was also granted the title of 2,000 households to repay me for serving in Xianyang. Xiao He was the only one who gave me an extra 200 yuan.
Chen Xi rebelled, and the emperor personally led the army to Handan.
Han Xin rebelled in Guanzhong, and Empress Lu adopted Xiao He's strategy to kill Han Xin.
It is recorded in "Xin Zhuan".
When the emperor heard that Han Xin had been killed, he sent an envoy to worship the prime minister as the prime minister, granted five thousand households, and ordered 500 soldiers and a captain to protect the prime minister.
All the kings celebrated, but Zhao Ping expressed condolences.
Zhaoping was the original Marquis of Shuling of Qin.
After the fall of Qin, he became a commoner and very poor. He planted melons in the east of Chang'an City. The melons were very sweet, so the so-called "Shuling melon" in the world began in Zhaoping.
Zhao Ping said to Xiao He: The disaster began from now on.
The emperor is camping outside, but you stay behind in the court and do not suffer the pain of stone arrows. The reason why you are granted a title of guard is because the Marquis of Huaiyin has just rebelled internally and is suspicious of you.
Guards are assigned to you to protect you, not to favor you.
I hope you will refuse the reward and use all your family property to fund the army.
Xiao He followed Zhao Ping's plan, and the emperor was very happy.
summary: During Chen Xi and Han Xin’s rebellions, Xiao He helped Empress Lu kill Han Xin.
