The emperor granted him 5,000 households and a guard, but Zhao Ping warned this was due to suspicion, advising Xiao He to refuse the reward and fund the army. He complied, pleasing the emperor. When Yingbu rebelled, a retainer warned Xiao He’s popularity could lead to his extermination, urging him to damage his reputation by buying land cheaply. He did so, and the emperor was happy. Later, the emperor imprisoned Xiao He for requesting Linyuan for the people, but a courtier argued his loyalty, leading to his release. Xiao He served Emperor Hui, recommending Cao Shen as his successor. He died in the second year of Xiaohui’s reign, posthumously named Wen Zhonghou. His descendants inherited his title, with later emperors restoring it after extinctions. The praise notes that both Xiao He and Cao Shen, born in Qin, rose with Han, stabilizing the state through their complementary roles—Xiao He guarding Guanzhong and Cao Shen leading expeditions. Their reputations endured, benefiting future generations.

translation:
He went north to rescue Shu'a, defeated Zhang Han's army, charged into battle, and pursued him to Puyang.
Capture Dingtao and occupy Linji.
He went south to rescue Yongqiu, attacked Li Youjun, and won a great victory. He killed Li You and captured one of the Marquis of Qin.
When Zhang Han defeated and killed Xiang Liang, Pei Gong and Xiang Yu led their troops to the east. King Huai of Chu made Pei Gong the leader of Qiang Deng and led the troops of Dan County.
So Xuan Shen was granted the title of Silk Holder and was named Jiancheng Jun.
He was promoted to Qi Gong and was subordinate to Yang County.
After that, he followed up and attacked Shujun Wei's army and defeated it south of Chengwu.
Attacked Wang Lijun in the south of Chengyang, and then attacked Gangli, and won a great victory.
He pursued the defeated army and went west to Kaifeng, where he attacked Zhao Ben's army and won. Surrounded Dun Bi in Kaifeng City.
They attacked Qin general Yang Xiong's army in Quyu to the west, and were victorious. They captured Qin Sima and Yu Shi, one person each.
Promoted to Zhigui.
The followers followed to attack Yangwu to the west, and reached Nianyuan and Fengshi to block the crossing of the Yellow River.
Attacked Zhao Ben's army in Xibei and won.
The entourage went south to attack Zhao, fought with Nanyang Shouji in Guodong of Yangcheng, charged into the battle, captured Wan, captured Qi, and pacified Nanyang County.
The followers went west to attack Wuguan and Xiguan and occupied the two places.
He advanced to attack the Qin army in the south of Lantian, and then attacked the northern army at night. He won a great victory, and then went to Xianyang to defeat Qin.
Xiang Yu arrived and made Peigong King of Han.
The king of Han granted Cao Shen the title of Marquis of Jiancheng.
He followed him to Hanzhong and was promoted to general.
He then followed back to pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, and attacked Xia Bian, Gudao, Yong, and Yak.
Attacked Zhang Ping's army in the south of Haozhi and won. They surrounded Haozhi and occupied Rangxiang.
Attacked the San Qin army in Rangshu and Gaoliang and won. They also surrounded Zhang Ping, who escaped from Haozhi.
So he attacked Zhao Bi and Nei Shi Baojun and won.
He captured Xianyang to the east and renamed it Xincheng.
Cao Shen led his troops to guard Jingling for twenty-three days. The Three Qin Dynasty sent Zhang Pingping to attack Cao Shen. Cao Shen attacked and won a great victory.
Give him Ning Qin as a food town.
As a general, he led the army to besiege Zhang Han in Feiqiu; as a lieutenant, he followed the King of Han to Jin Pass.
Arriving at Hanoi, Xiuwu, crossing Weijin, and heading east to attack Long Qie and Xiang Tuo at Dingtao, and won.
Head east to capture Jie, Xiao and Pengcheng.
Attacking Xiang Ji's army, the Han army was defeated and fled.
Cao Shen surrounded Yongqiu as a lieutenant.
Wang Wu rebelled in Waihuang, Cheng Chu rebelled in Yan, and Cao Shen attacked, and they all won.
Zhu Tianhou rebelled in Yanshi, and Cao Shen marched to defeat Yanshi.
Attack Yu Ying in Kunyang and catch up with Ye.
He went back to attack Wu Qiang and arrived at Rongyang.
Cao Shen served as a general and lieutenant from the desert, following him to attack the princes. When King Xiang failed, he returned to Yang.
In the second year of Han Dynasty, he worshiped as the fake Prime Minister Zuo and entered Guanzhong to station troops.
More than a month later, King Bao of Wei rebelled. As a false prime minister, he and Han Xin attacked Shuzhang at Shubian where Wei general Sun Yao was stationed, and won a great victory.
Then he attacked Anyi and captured Wei general Wang Xiang.
Attacked the King of Wei in Quyang, pursued him to Shuyuan, and captured King Bao of Wei alive.
He captured Pingyang, captured Bao's mother, wife and children, and pacified Wei, a total of fifty-two counties.
Give food to Pingyang.
So he followed Han Xin to attack the Prime Minister Xia Shuo's army in Wudong, and won a great victory, killing Xia Shuo.
Han Xin and Zhang Er, the former king of Changshan, led their troops to Jingxing and attacked Chen Yu, the king of Cheng'an. They ordered Cao Shen to go back and besiege Zhao Bie's general Qi Gong in Wucheng.
Qi Gong fled and chased him.
So he led his troops to where the king of Han was.
Han Xin had defeated Fang, became prime minister, and went east to attack Qi. Cao Shen followed him as prime minister of Zuo.
He defeated Qi Li's army and occupied Linzi.
Go back and pacify Jibei County, and recover Zhuge, Luoyin, Pingyuan, Li, and Lu.
Then he followed Han Xin to attack Long Qie's army in secret, and won a great victory. He killed Long Qie and captured the general Zhou Lan.
Qi County was pacified and a total of seventy counties were obtained.
Captured the former Qi King Tian Guang, Prime Minister Tian Guang, the Prime Minister Xu Zhang, and the former general Tian Ji.
Han Xin was appointed King of Qi, led his troops east to Chen, and defeated Xiang Yu together with the King of Han. Cao Shen left behind to pacify the areas where Qi had not yet surrendered.
The King of Han became the emperor, and his title was changed to King of Chu.
The stems and ginseng are cross-linked.
He conferred the title of eldest son, Chu Xun, as king of change, and appointed Xuan Shen as prime minister.
In the sixth year of his reign, he cut the talisman with the princes and granted the title of Emperor Xuan as a prince. The number of households in the city was reduced to 10,630, which lasted from generation to generation.
Cao Shen, as Prime Minister of Qi, attacked Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun and won. When Tingbu rebelled, Cao Shen followed King Hui Hui and led 120,000 chariots and cavalry. Together with Gaozu, he attacked the Tingbu army and won a great victory.
Go south to Qi, return to the army and pacify Zhuyi, Xiang, Xiao and Liu.
Cao Shen's achievements: conquered two countries and 122 counties in total; captured two kings, three prime ministers, six generals, and one each of Da Mo Zhen, county guard, Sima, marquis, and censor.
In the first year of Xiaohui, the law of princes and ministers was abolished and Cao Shen was appointed as the prime minister of Qi.
When Cao Shen and Cao were together, there were seventy cities in Qi.
The world had just been peaceful and King Hui was young. Cao Shen summoned all the elders and gentlemen to ask how to assemble the people.
There are hundreds of scholars in Qi, and everyone says it differently. Cao Shen doesn't know how to be sure.
I heard that there was a Duke Gai in Jiaoxi who was good at studying Huang Lao's words, so he sent someone to invite him with generous gifts.
summary: Cao Shen, also from Peidi, served as a jailer in Qin and followed Gaozu as Zhongjuan. He achieved numerous military victories, including defeating Qin forces, capturing cities, and killing generals. After Xiang Yu made Peigong King of Han, Cao Shen became Marquis of Jiancheng. He pacified the Three Qin Dynasties, captured Xianyang, and fought in key battles. As a general and lieutenant, he attacked princes, and after King Xiang’s defeat, he served as false prime minister, defeating Wei and capturing King Bao. He followed Han Xin to attack Zhao and Qi, capturing cities and generals. After the Han emperor’s ascension, Cao Shen became prime minister of Qi, attacking Chen Xi and Yingbu. His achievements included conquering two countries and 122 counties, capturing two kings and three prime ministers.

translation:
When he met Gai Gong, Gai Gong told him that the key to peace is tranquility and the people will be at peace, and so on and discussed in detail.
Cao Shen then left the main hall and asked Gai Gong to live there.
He adopted the methods of Huang and Lao in his administration, so in the ninth year of his reign as Prime Minister of Qi, the State of Qi settled in peace, and people praised him as a wise Prime Minister.
When Cao Shen heard about Xiao He's death, he told his family to pack up their luggage as soon as possible. I will be the prime minister of the court.
Soon after, the messenger came to summon Cao Shen.
Cao Shen was about to leave, and he told the person who took over his position: "I entrust Qi's prison litigation and market trade to you, and do not disturb it."
The later prime minister said: Isn't there anything bigger than running a country? Cao Shen said: No.
Prison litigation and market trade are places for inclusion. If you invade it, where will the traitor find shelter?
So I put that first.
At first, when Cao Shen was humble, he was friendly with Xiao He. When he became prime minister, the two had conflicts.
When Xiao He was about to die, the only wise man he recommended was Cao Shen.
Cao Shen replaced Xiao He as prime minister, and everything remained unchanged and everything was in accordance with Xiao He's agreement.
Select a loyal elder who was born as a minor official in the county and was not good at eloquence, and he was called to be the prime minister.
Among the minor officials, those who interpreted the legal provisions profoundly and wanted to gain fame were excluded.
Drinking day and night, the officials and guests below the Qing officials saw that Cao Shen was doing nothing, and everyone who came wanted to give advice.
As soon as the person arrived, Cao Shen gave him wine. Guessing that he was about to talk, he let him drink again. He went back after he was drunk. Finally, no one could speak, so he got used to it.
The back garden of the Prime Minister's Mansion was close to the residence of the minor officials. The minor officials drank and sang in their residences every day. The subordinate officials felt that they were in trouble and had nothing to do with them, so they invited Cao to visit the back garden.
Hearing a young official singing drunkenly, the official wanted to be summoned by the Prime Minister to interrogate him.
Instead, Cao Shen asked people to get some wine, sit down and drink, and sang loudly to keep him company.
When Cao saw someone making a small mistake, he covered it up for him, so that everything was safe in the house.
Cao Shen's son, Cao Cheng, became the middle doctor.
Emperor Hui blamed the prime minister for not paying attention to political affairs, thinking he was looking at my youth?
So he said to Cao Zhou: Go back and ask your father privately and casually: Emperor Gao has just abandoned his ministers and left. The emperor is young and powerful. You are the prime minister, drinking every day and doing nothing. How can you share the worries of the world?
But don't say I told you that.
Cao Shen went home on vacation. When she had time, she admonished Cao Shen as she pleased. Cao Shen angrily beat him two hundred times and said, "Go and serve in the court. It is not your place to talk about world affairs."
When he went to court, the emperor scolded Cao Shen and said, "What does it have to do with Cao Zhou?"
That's why I asked him to ridicule you.
Cao Shen took off his hat and apologized and said: Your Majesty, what do you think about the emperor's sage, valor and valor?
The emperor said: How dare I compare with the late emperor!
Cao Shen said: Your Majesty, who is more worthy between me and Xiao He?
The emperor said: You seem to be inferior to him.
Cao Shen said: Your Majesty is right.
summary: As prime minister of Qi, Cao Shen adopted Huang-Lao principles, governing with tranquility and earning praise. Upon hearing of Xiao He’s death, he prepared to become prime minister of the court, advising his successor to prioritize prison litigation and market trade. Despite past conflicts, Xiao He recommended Cao Shen. As prime minister, Cao Shen adhered to Xiao He’s laws, selecting loyal elders and excluding those seeking fame. He drank daily, avoiding advice, and covered minor mistakes. When Emperor Hui criticized his inaction, Cao Shen argued that Emperor Gao and Xiao He had established clear laws, and he merely maintained them, which the emperor accepted. He died after three years as prime minister, posthumously named Yihou. His descendants inherited his title, with later generations continuing until Wang Mang’s era.

translation:
Xiao Wangzhi, whose courtesy name is Changqian, was born in Lanling County, Shuhai County, and later moved to Duling.
Farming has been a career for generations. When Xiao Wangzhi arrived, he was interested in learning and studied "Qi Shi". He studied under Houcang from the same county for nearly ten years.
According to the system, he studied under Taichang, and also studied under his former classmate Dr. Bai Qi. He also followed Xia Housheng to discuss "The Analects of Confucius" and "Etiquette". Mourning Clothes".
The Confucian scholars in the capital all praised him.
At that time, General Huo Guang was in power. Chief Shi Bingji recommended Confucian scholars Wang Zhongweng and Xiao Wangzhi, and several others were summoned.
Before this, the left general Shangguan Jie and Princess Gaiyi conspired to assassinate Huo Guang. Huo Guang killed Shangguan Jie and others, and then took precautions when going out.
Officials and common people who must be interviewed must be stripped and searched, their weapons removed, and held hostage by two officials.
Only Xiao Wangzhi refused to obey. He withdrew from the small door and said, "I don't want to see you."
The official pulled him away aggressively.
When Huo Guang heard about this situation, he told the officials not to hold him hostage.
Xiao Wangzhi came to Huo Guang and advised him: "The general assists the young emperor with his merits and virtues, and will implement a grand enlightenment policy to achieve a harmonious and peaceful rule. Therefore, scholars all over the world stretch their necks and stand on their heels, vying to personally serve and assist you, a wise man."
Now the scholars who want to visit you must first be stripped and searched and held hostage. This may not be in line with the courtesy of the Duke of Zhou, who ate three meals, vomited food three times, and washed his hair three times to incur poor scholars.
At that time, Huo Guang only did not appoint Xiao Wangzhi, and Wang Zhongweng and others were appointed as General Shi.
Within three years, Wang Zhongweng was promoted to Guanglu doctor, and Xiao Wangzhi became a Langguan because he passed the A-level exam, acting as Xiaoyuan East Gate Marquis.
Wang Zhongweng was followed by servants when he came in and out. He got off the car and entered the door. He was greeted in front of and behind him. He was very respectful. He turned around and said to Xiao Wangzhi: You refused to follow the rules and instead just became a gatekeeper.
Xiao Wangzhi said: Everyone pursues his own ambitions.
A few years later, because his younger brother had committed a crime and was in jail, he could no longer serve as a palace guard. He was dismissed and returned to his hometown as a county official.
When Wei Xiang, the imperial censor, appointed Xiao Wangzhi as a subordinate official, he was appointed as the Minister of Ceremonies of Daxing after examination.
At this time, the general Huo Guang passed away, and his son Huo Yu became the chief minister again. His nephew Huo Shan was appointed the minister, and all his relatives served as guards and attendants in the palace.
In the summer of the third year of Dijie, there was hail in the capital. Xiao Wangzhi complained to the emperor about this, hoping that the emperor would give him a chance to tell him the meaning of the natural disaster and vision.
Emperor Xuan heard about Xiao Wangzhi's reputation among the people and said: Is this Xiao Sheng from Shuhai?
Bring him to Shaofu Song Wei to inquire about the situation and ask him not to hide anything.
Xiao Wangzhi answered the inquiry. He believed that "Spring and Autumn" records that there was a hailstorm in the third year of Duke Zhao of Lu. At that time, the Ji family was in power and eventually exiled Duke Zhao of Lu.
If Lu Zhaogong could detect the signs of natural disasters in the past, this disaster would not have happened.
summary: Xiao Wangzhi, courtesy name Changqian, was a scholar from Lanling who later moved to Duling. He studied the "Qi Shi" under Houcang for nearly ten years, and also studied under Dr. Bai Qi and Xia Housheng, mastering "The Analects of Confucius" and "Etiquette." His reputation grew among Confucian scholars in the capital. During the reign of General Huo Guang, Xiao Wangzhi was recommended for office but refused to submit to the humiliating security procedures of being stripped and searched before meeting Huo Guang. He advised Huo Guang to treat scholars with respect, but Huo Guang did not appoint him. Xiao Wangzith later became a Langguan after passing an exam, serving as Xiaoyuan East Gate Marquis. When his younger brother committed a crime, he was dismissed and returned to his hometown as a county official.

translation:
Now your Majesty is occupying the position of emperor by virtue of being wise and wise. He is thinking about political affairs and seeking talents. This is the intention of Yao and Shun in governing the world.
However, the auspicious omen has not yet appeared, and the yin and yang are not in harmony. This is caused by the ministers being in power and the exclusive power of one surname.
If the branches are too large, they will damage the trunk. If the ministers have too much power, they will endanger the court.
Only a sage monarch personally governs all affairs of the country, selects people with the same surname, appoints talented people, treats them as confidants, plans political affairs with them, orders ministers to report to the emperor, clearly states his responsibilities, and examines their merits and talents.
In this way, all kinds of things can be dealt with, all kinds of things can be dealt with, the way of justice can be established, the way of evil and evil can be blocked, and private rights can be abolished.
This exchange was reported to the emperor, and Emperor Xuan appointed Xiao Wangzhi as the visitor.
At that time, Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne and hoped to promote virtuous people. Many people wrote letters stating strategies that would benefit the country and the people. Emperor Xuan often gave these memorials to Xiao Wangzhi to inquire about the pros and cons. The wise ones were asked to be selected by the prime minister and censor, and the inferior ones were given to Jiuqing for trial. After a year, the situation was reported. The inferior ones were given approval or dismissed from office and sent back to their hometown. Everything Xiao Wangzhi reported was approved.
He was successively promoted to admonish the doctor and prime minister Sizhi. He was promoted three times within a year and became an official of two thousand stone level.
Later, the Huo family was actually executed for treason, and Xiao Wangzhi became even more important.
At this time, doctors and admonishment officials who were knowledgeable in political affairs were being selected to serve as county governors and prime ministers, and Xiao Wangzhi was appointed as the governor of Pingyuan.
Xiao Wangzhi had always wanted to serve in the imperial court, so he was sent to serve as a county guard in a distant place. He didn't like it, so he wrote a memorial saying: Your Majesty is considerate of the people and is worried that moral education will not be popularized, so he sends his admonishers to serve as local officials. It is said that he is worried about the details of things and forgets their roots.
If there are no admonishers in the court, the emperor will not be able to find faults; if there are no knowledgeable people in the capital, the emperor will not be able to hear good words.
I hope that your Majesty will select far-sighted and far-sighted people who understand the classics, are familiar with history, are able to grasp new situations, and are proficient in affairs, as ministers of the DPRK and China to participate in government affairs.
When the princes heard about this situation, they knew that the country had adopted the words of loyalty and advice, and they were worried about politics and there were no mistakes or omissions.
If you persevere like this, the rule of King Zhou Cheng and King Zhou Kang will almost be realized!
Is it worth worrying about the poor governance of local counties?
After his memorial was submitted, he was recruited into the imperial court to manage the Shaofu.
Emperor Xuan learned that Xiao Wangzhi had learned classics at dawn, was prudent in handling matters, and had room for discussion and reasoning, so he was qualified to serve as prime minister. He wanted to carefully examine his ability to handle government affairs, and appointed him as Zuo Fengyi.
Xiao Wangzhi was transferred from the Shaofu and demoted to a lower position. He was afraid that he would offend the emperor, so he wrote a letter claiming to be sick and asking for leave.
When the emperor found out about this, he sent his minister, Hou Jin'an of Chengdu, to convey the decree: "Everyone employed by the imperial court has been governed by the people to assess their merits."
You used to be the governor of Pingyuan for a short time, so I sent you to Sanfu for inspection because I didn't hear anything bad.
Xiao Wangzhi took up his post immediately.
This year the Xiqiang rebelled, and the Han Dynasty sent generals to attack them.
Jingzhao Yin Zhang Chang wrote to Zhang Chang: The country's army is on the border. The army sets out in the summer, north of Longxi County and west of Anding County. Officials and people are involved in supply operations. Agriculture will be a lot of waste. There was no surplus grain reserves in the past. Although the Qiang rebellion was defeated, the people will definitely be short of food in the next spring.
summary: After Huo Guang's death, Xiao Wangzhi was appointed as Minister of Ceremonies of Daxing. He warned Emperor Xuan about the dangers of ministers holding too much power, citing historical precedents. Emperor Xuan appointed him as a visitor, and he quickly rose through the ranks to become an official of two thousand stone level. He was later appointed as the governor of Pingyuan but preferred to serve in the court. He was eventually recalled to manage the Shaofu and later became Zuo Fengyi.

translation:
Nowadays, the Western Qiang pirates are a small tribe in a corner, clamoring for tyranny in the valley. The Han Dynasty can only order the criminals to pay and reduce their crimes to kill them. This will have a much better reputation than harassing good people and imposing excessive taxes.
In addition, those robbers and murderers who are unjust and hated by the people cannot atone for their sins; the leaders who harbor criminals, those who knowingly release criminals, those who benefit themselves at the expense of others, etc. Some of the commentators think that their punishments can be exempted. Now because this order can atone for sins, its benefits are obvious. What kind of education has been disturbed?
The punishments in "Fu Xing" include forgiveness of minor offenses, atonement for minor crimes, and the level of atonement with money has been around for a long time. How could thieves appear for this purpose?
I have been an official in the imperial court for more than 20 years. I have heard about the redemption of sinners, but I have never heard of thieves appearing as a result.
I privately expressed my pity that the bandits had disturbed Jiazhou. It was the time of autumn harvest, and the people were still hungry and sleepy, and some were sick and died on the roads. What’s more, there will be even greater difficulties in the coming spring!
If you don't think about ways to help the people early, but use general principles to criticize, you may have to bear greater responsibilities later.
The mediocre can abide by the rules with him, but cannot discuss contingency matters with him.
I am fortunate enough to be ranked among the ministers, and it is my duty to assist the two governments. I dare not fail to do my best.
Xiao Wangzhi and Li Qiang retorted: The late emperor was a sage, benevolent and virtuous man who served in the imperial court. He formulated charters and promulgated decrees as a permanent system and long-term consideration of the living difficulties of the people on the border. Therefore, the first article of "Jinbulingjia" said The border counties suffered from wars several times and suffered from hunger and cold. The people could not live to the end of their lives and would die young. The father and son were separated and ordered the people of the world to jointly provide for their expenses. It turned out to be preparations for the sudden outbreak of war.
It is said that in the fourth year of Tianhan Dynasty, prisoners on death row were asked to pay 500,000 yuan to avoid the death penalty and have their sentences commuted to one level. Powerful officials, officials and the people begged, robbed, borrowed, and even acted as thieves to obtain money to atone for their crimes.
From then on, treacherous and evil people were rampant, and many thieves appeared at the same time, attacking cities and killing county guards. These people spread all over the mountains and plains, and officials could not stop them. The state publicly ordered to send embroidered messengers to lead the army to attack them, killing more than half of them, and then they declined and disappeared.
We believe that this is caused by letting the death row inmates redeem themselves, so it is inappropriate to do so.
At this time, Prime Minister Wei Xiang and Yushi doctor Bingji also believed that the Xiqiang rebels would be defeated and the transshipment supply could basically meet the needs, so they did not implement Zhang Chang's suggestions.
Xiao Wangzhi served as Zuo Fengyi for three years, and everyone in the capital praised him. Was promoted to Dahonglu.
summary: During the Xiqiang rebellion, Xiao Wangzhi opposed Zhang Chang's proposal to allow criminals to atone for their sins by donating food, arguing it would lead to inequality and moral decay. His views were supported by Prime Minister Wei Xiang and Yushi doctor Bingji, and the proposal was not implemented.

translation:
Prior to this, King Weng Guimi of Wusun submitted a document through Changluo Hou Changhui, willing to take his grandson Yuan Guimi of the Han Dynasty as his heir, hoping to marry the young princess again, become an in-law, join the Han Dynasty, and betray the Huns.
The emperor issued an edict to the ministers to discuss the matter. Xiao Wangzhi believed that Wusun was a remote area, and it was not a long-term solution to believe their good words and enter into a marriage thousands of miles away.
The emperor didn't listen.
In the second year of Shenjue's reign, Changluo Houhui was sent as an envoy to escort the princess to be betrothed to Yuan Guimi.
Before leaving the border, Weng Guimi died, and his nephew Kuang Wang broke the agreement and proclaimed himself king.
Chang Hui wrote to the emperor from under the fortress, hoping to let the princess stay in Dunhuang County temporarily.
Chang Hui went to Wusun and blamed them for breaking the promise, so he made Yuan Guimi king and came back to welcome the princess.
The emperor issued an edict to the ministers for discussion, but Xiao Wangzhi thought it was impossible.
Wusun, the head of the rat, can't stick to the promise, and the consequences have been seen.
The former princess had been in Wusun for more than forty years, and the relationship between husband and wife was not deep, so the border was not stabilized. This was already a test of the matter.
Now that the young princess has come back because Yuan Guimi cannot inherit the throne, she has indeed failed the Yi people in all directions. This is a great thing for the Han Dynasty.
If the young princess does not stay, corvee service will arise, and the root of the matter lies in Zaojie.
The emperor followed his advice and summoned the princess back to the court.
Later, although Wusun was divided into two parallel countries and made Yuan Guimi the great king, the Han Dynasty no longer entered into marriage with him.
In the third year of Shenjue's reign, Xiao Wangzhi replaced Bingji as the imperial censor.
During the Wufeng period, the Huns were in chaos. Most commentators believed that the Huns had been causing harm for a long time, and they could take advantage of the civil strife to send troops to eliminate them.
The emperor went down to Shao and sent Han Zeng, Fupinghou Zhang Yanshou, Guangluxun Yang Tan, and Tai servant Dai Changle to ask Xiao Wangzhi what his plan was. Xiao Wangzhi responded: According to the "Spring and Autumn" records, Jin State Shiju led an army to invade Qi. When he heard that the Marquis of Qi had died, he led his army back. The gentleman praised him for not conquering the country where there was a funeral. He believed that his kindness was enough to impress the new monarch of Qi and his morality was enough to shock the princes.
In the past, the Chanyu admired our dynasty's teachings, was dedicated to doing good, and regarded himself as his younger brother. He sent envoys to ask for peace. People in the four seas were very happy, and all the Yi and Di tribes heard about it.
The treaty was not carried out to the end, and Shanyu was unfortunately killed by the rebels. To attack him now is to take advantage of the civil strife of others and take pleasure in others' misfortune. They will definitely run away.
If we do not fight with benevolence and righteousness, we may be in vain.
Envoys should be sent to express condolences, help them when they are weak, and rescue them when they are in trouble. The barbarians from all over the world will admire the benevolence and righteousness of the Han Dynasty.
If he can return to the throne due to this favor, he will definitely surrender to the Han Dynasty. This is a grand act of virtue.
The emperor followed his advice and finally sent an army to escort Huhanxie Shanyu to stabilize his country.
summary: Xiao Wangzith served as Zuo Fengyi for three years and was promoted to Dahonglu. He advised against marrying a princess to Wusun, citing the unreliability of the alliance, and the emperor eventually recalled the princess. During the Wufeng period, he advised against attacking the Huns during their civil strife, advocating for a policy of benevolence and assistance instead.

translation:
When Xiao Wangzhi heard about this, he used it to question Hong Gong and Shi Xian.
Shi Xian and Hong Gong were afraid that Xiao Wangzhi would file a complaint on his own and the emperor would hand over the case to other officials, so they would threaten Zheng Peng and Hua Long.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan, Hualong was waiting for an imperial edict with Zhang Zijiao and others. He was not appointed because of his bad conduct and wanted to attach himself to Zhou Kan and others. Zhou Kan and others did not accept him, so he made friends with Zheng Peng.
Hong Gong and Shi Xian ordered them to report Xiao Wangzhi and others' intention to depose General Chaoqiu and alienate the Xu and Shi families. They waited for Xiao Wangzhi to go on vacation and instruct Zheng Peng and Hua Long to report to them.
This matter was handed over to Hong Gong to inquire about the situation, and Xiao Wangzhi responded: Most of the relatives who hold important positions are extravagant and extravagant. I am here to help the country, not to do bad things.
Hong Gong and Shi Xian reported that Xiao Wangzhi, Zhou Kan, and Liu Gengsheng colluded with their cronies to recommend each other, repeatedly slandered ministers, attacked and alienated the emperor's relatives, and wanted to use their power to gain power.
At that time, the emperor had just succeeded to the throne and did not understand that summoning the eunuchs to deliver them to the court captain was equivalent to sending them to prison and approved their memorial.
Later, the emperor summoned Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng and replied that they had been put in prison.
The emperor was shocked and said: "Isn't it just for the Tingwei to ask about the situation?"
He blamed Hong Gong and Shi Xian for this incident, and they both kowtowed and apologized.
The emperor said: Let them come out to do business.
Hong Gong and Shi Xian sent Shi Gao to say: The emperor has just succeeded to the throne and has not taught the world about his moral education. He should first interrogate the master. Since Dr. Jiuqing was imprisoned, he should be interrogated and then commuted.
At that time, an edict was issued to the prime minister and the imperial censor: Former general Xiao Wangzhi taught me for eight years and had no other sins. It has been a long time now and my memory is unclear and it is difficult to explain.
Xiao Wangzhi should be pardoned for his crimes, the seal and ribbon of former general Guang Luxun should be taken back, and Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng should be dismissed from their posts and become common people.
And Zheng Peng became Huang Menlang.
A few months later, the emperor issued an edict to the imperial censor: If the country is going to prosper, we should respect the master. The former general Xiao Wangzhi taught me for eight years and guided me with classics. He has made great contributions.
Xiao Wangzhi should be given the title of Marquis of Guannei, with a settlement of 600 households, and be given a position in the affairs. He should pay homage on the first and fifteenth day of every month, and his seat should be second to that of the general. The emperor was about to rely on him to become the prime minister when he encountered Xiao Wangzhi's son, Sanqi Zhonglang Xiao Ji, writing a letter complaining about Xiao Wangzhi's previous grievances. The matter was handed over to the relevant departments and reported.
Hong Gong, Shi Xian and others knew that Xiao Wangzhi had a long history of noble integrity and refused to give in and be insulted. They suggested: Xiao Wangzhi, a former general who assisted in state affairs, wanted to exclude the Xu and Shi families and control the state affairs exclusively.
Fortunately, he was not punished, and was given a title, a house, and participated in the discussion of national politics. He did not repent of his mistakes and confessed his crimes. He also harbored resentment and instigated his son to write a letter attributing his fault to the emperor. He thought that because of his status as a master, he would not be punished.
If Xiao Wangzhi is not allowed to suffer some humiliation in prison and block his dissatisfaction, then the Holy Dynasty will not be able to bestow favors on him.
The emperor said: Mr. Xiao has always been upright, how can he accept the interrogation of officials?
Shi Xian and others said: Human life is of vital importance. The crime committed by Xiao Wangzhi is a small crime of saying the wrong thing. It will definitely not worry you.
The emperor approved his report.
Shi Xian and others sealed the emperor's approval and handed it over to the visitor, and ordered it to be delivered to Xiao Wangzhi personally. Then they ordered Taichang to quickly lead the Jinwu cavalry to surround his house.
The messenger arrived and sent word to Xiao Wangzhi.
Xiao Wangzhi wanted to commit suicide, but his wife stopped him, thinking that this was not the emperor's will.
Xiao Wangzhi asked his disciple Zhu Yun about this.
Zhu Yun was a man who loved fame and honor, so he advised Xiao Wangzhi to commit suicide.
At that time, Xiao Wangzhi looked up to the sky and sighed and said: I once served as a general, and I am over sixty years old. Isn't it too despicable to go to prison at an old age and live an ignoble life? The factory called Zhu Yun and said: You, come and get the medicine. I would rather die than stay alive for a long time!
Finally he committed suicide by drinking poisonous wine.
The emperor was shocked when he heard about this. He clapped his hands and sighed and said: I suspected that he refused to go to jail before, but he really killed my good teacher!
At that time, the eunuch had just served lunch when the emperor pushed away the food and cried for Xiao Wangzhi. His sorrow moved the attendants around him.
Immediately summoned Shi Xian and others to question them for their poor planning.
They all took off their hats to apologize, and it took a long time before they gave up.
Xiao Wangzhi died guilty, and the relevant departments requested that his title and title be abolished.
However, the emperor issued an edict to increase his favor, and his eldest son Xiao Ji succeeded him as Marquis of Guannei.
The emperor could not forget Xiao Wangzhi's memory, and sent envoys to pay homage to Xiao Wangzhi's grave during every year and festival. This was the case throughout the Yuan Dynasty.
Xiao Wangzhi had eight sons, among whom Xiao Yu, Xiao Xian and Xiao You became high officials.
summary: Xiao Wangzhi later became the imperial censor but fell out of favor with Emperor Xuan due to conflicts with the prime minister and accusations of arrogance and misconduct. He was demoted to Crown Prince Tutor. After Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, Xiao Wangzhi served as a trusted advisor but clashed with eunuchs Hong Gong and Shi Xian. He was falsely accused of conspiring to depose the general and alienate the emperor's relatives, leading to his imprisonment. He committed suicide by drinking poison, deeply saddening Emperor Yuan.

translation:
At that time, Zhu Bo was still the head of Duling Pavilion. He was introduced by Chen Xian and Xiao Yu and entered the Wang family.
Later, he served as governor, county governor, and state minister at the same time, and later he served as Jiuqing. Zhu Bo first served as general and minister, and experienced more official positions than Chen Xian and Xiao Yu, all the way to prime minister.
Xiao Yu and Zhu Bo later had a quarrel and could not end well, so the world thought it was difficult to make friends.
Xiao Xian lived there and became prime minister. He was promoted to Maocai and appointed magistrate of Liaoqi County. He was promoted to Jinbao, Hui Neishi, Zhang Zheng, Wang Di, and Jiongsai prefect.
Wherever he went, he made political achievements and received many increases in salary and gold rewards.
Later, he was dismissed from the official position and served as the captain of the Yue Cavalry School, the captain of the guard army, and the general of Zhonglang. He was sent as an envoy to the Huns and reached the rank of Da Sinong. He died in his post.
Xiao You, whose courtesy name was Zijiao, was appointed as the Prime Minister's general of Xicao Wei. He was promoted to the rank of Yezhi and was appointed as the deputy captain of the envoy to the Xiongnu.
Later, he was recommended as a virtuous person and appointed as magistrate of Dingtao County. He was promoted to captain of Taiyuan and prefect of Anding.
He is prestigious in governing states and counties, and many people praise and recommend him.
When Emperor Ai became King of Dingtao, Xiao You was appointed as the Dingtao Order, which went against the wishes of King Dingtao. Soon, the court dismissed Xiao You as a commoner.
After the death of Emperor Ai, he was appointed Captain of Futu, Captain of Jingfu and Zuofu, and was promoted to prefect of Jiangxia.
Because of their meritorious service in wiping out the bandits on the Yangtze River, Cheng Zhong and others were given an increased salary and were appointed as the prefect of Chenliu. During the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, Mingtang and Piyong were built, princes and kings were convened for large-scale court meetings, and Xiao You was recruited to serve as Dahonglu. It happened that he was ill and could not host etiquette and receive guests. He returned to his original official position, but was dismissed due to illness.
Later, he served as a doctor in Zhongsan and died in office.
There are six or seven people in the Xiao family who have reached the level of two thousand stone officials.
Zan said: Xiao Wangzhi's official position is general and deputy prime minister. By virtue of being the emperor's master, it can be said that he and the emperor are close to each other.
When the plot was revealed, suspicion arose, evil-mouthed and evil people framed him, and he was eventually killed by the sycophant, eunuch, and villain. What a pity!
Otherwise, Xiao Wangzhi was upright and unyielding. As a leading Confucian scholar and capable of assisting the emperor, he was almost like a minister of the country in ancient times.
summary: Xiao Wangzhi had eight sons, including Xiao Yu, Xiao Xian, and Xiao You, who became high officials. Xiao Yu was known for his bravery and integrity, serving in various positions despite frequent dismissals. Xiao Xian and Xiao You also held significant posts, with the Xiao family producing six or seven officials of two thousand stone level. The historian praised Xiao Wangzhi as a leading Confucian scholar and capable minister, lamenting his tragic death at the hands of sycophants and eunuchs.

translation:
Dong Zhongshu is from Guangchuan.
He studied "Spring and Autumn" when he was young, and became a doctor during the reign of Emperor Jing of Han Dynasty.
He hung a curtain indoors and sat behind the curtain to give lectures. The disciples who entered the school first taught their studies to those who entered later. Some students had not even seen him.
Dong Zhongshu didn't look at the garden for three years and studied his knowledge carefully to this extent.
The bachelors all respected him as their teacher because of his manners and manners when advancing and retreating, and did not do anything that was not in line with etiquette.
After Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne, he ordered the recommendation of more than 100 virtuous writers. Dong Zhongshu responded to the emperor's policy questions as a virtuous person.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty asked: I have inherited the highest status and the most beautiful virtues of the late emperor, and they must be passed on forever and extended to the endless future. This task is huge and the duties are important, so I have no time to enjoy and rest from morning to night. I have to think about the whole story for a long time, lest I am not thoughtful.
Therefore, I widely invite heroes and talents from all over the country, virtuous, virtuous, and knowledgeable talents who are justly selected by governors, kings, and princes. I want to know the outline of the road to governing the country and the highest principles of the theory of peace and security for the people.
Nowadays, doctors are regarded as the first choice for virtuous people, which I think is very good.
Doctors should think carefully. What I really want to know and ask is as follows.
It is said that the way the Five Emperors and Three Kings governed the country was to reform the system and create music, so that the world was stable. Hundreds of subsequent kings also did the same thing.
The most beautiful music of Yu and Shun was "Shao", and the most beautiful music of Zhou Dynasty was "Shao".
After the death of the sage king, the sound of bells, drums, and orchestras still existed, but the Great Way declined and gradually deteriorated to the point where Jie and Zhou behaved like that, and the royal way was greatly corrupted.
In the past five hundred years, the kings and scholars in power who abided by the old system wanted to learn from the legal system of the previous kings to assist the politics of the time, but they were not reversed, and the royal way continued to perish day by day. It was not until the rise of the later kings that this declining trend was stopped. Could it be that what they believe in is wrong and they have lost the tradition of Tao?
Or is destiny just like this, it cannot be reversed by human power, and it must evolve until the country is in danger before it stops? well!
Doesn’t all the hard work day and night and trying to imitate the distant ancient times have no effect?
So, what was the basis for the monarchs of the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties to accept the mandate of heaven?
What caused the disaster?
The reality of life may be death, longevity, benevolence, or despicability. We often hear these names, but we fail to fully understand the truth behind them.
summary: Dong Zhongshu, a scholar from Guangchuan, studied the "Spring and Autumn" Annals in his youth and became a court academician during Emperor Jing's reign. He lectured from behind a curtain, with senior disciples teaching junior ones, and some students never saw him. He was so devoted to his studies that he did not look at his garden for three years. His dignified conduct earned him the respect of all scholars. When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he sought virtuous scholars, and Dong Zhongshu responded to the emperor's policy questions. The emperor asked about the principles of governance, the rise and fall of dynasties, and how to achieve harmony between heaven and humanity. He inquired why the virtuous ways of ancient sage kings declined, why disasters occurred, and how to reform governance to bring peace and prosperity.

translation:
That's what it means. I carefully studied the meaning of "Spring King's first month" in "Spring and Autumn", looking for the beginning of the king's way, and got the correct answer. Zheng is inferior to Wang Wang, and Wang Wang is inferior to Chun.
Spring is the work of heaven. That’s what the king does.
It means that when a monarch flatters Heaven above and corrects his own behavior below, this is the beginning of the kingly way.
However, if a king wants to make a difference, he should ask heaven for this beginning.
The greatest thing in the way of heaven is yin and yang, yang is the virtue, yin is the punishment, punishment is the main force of killing, and virtue is the main force of life.
Therefore, Yang is always in the midsummer, taking birth and growth as its own business; Yin is often in the harsh winter, accumulating in empty and ineffective places.
It can be seen from this that Heaven uses moral education and does not use punishment.
The angel Yang appears, gives alms above, and is in charge of the harvest of the year; he makes the yin enter, hide below, and often comes out to help the yang; without the help of the yin, the yang cannot complete the years alone.
From the beginning to the end, Yang is in the name of completing the years. This is God's will.
The king does things according to the will of God, so he uses moral education instead of punishment.
Punishment cannot be used to govern society, just as Yin cannot be used to complete the years.
To use punishment while in power is not to obey the will of heaven, so the former king was not willing to do so.
Now that the former king's officials in charge of moral education have been abolished, and only law enforcement officials are used to govern the people, is this the original intention of the former king's use of punishment?
Confucius said: Killing people without education is called tyranny.
It is difficult to achieve the goal of spreading moral education to the whole world when brutal politics is applied to the lower levels.
I carefully examine the meaning of "Yi Yuan" in the Spring and Autumn Annals. "Yi Yuan" is the beginning of all things, and "Yi Yuan" is what is said in the vocabulary.
Saying that one is Yuan shows a big beginning and wants to correct its fundamentals.
"Spring and Autumn" deeply explores its origin, but it turns out that it starts with noble people.
Therefore, as a monarch, you must first rectify your heart before you can rectify the court. Only by rectifying the court can you rectify the hundreds of officials. Only by rectifying the hundreds of officials can you rectify the people. Only by rectifying the people can you rectify the four directions.
When the four directions are upright, no one near or far dares not to be upright, and there is no evil spirit mixed in the surface.
Therefore, the yin and yang are harmonious and the wind and rain are timely, all things are in harmony and the people are growing up, the grains are harvested and the vegetation is luxuriant, the heaven and the earth are blessed, and a very rich and beautiful scene is presented, and people from all over the world come to pay homage to the monarch when they hear his virtues.
Confucius said: If the phoenix bird does not come and the river map does not appear, I am afraid I will be finished!
This is because he is sad that his virtue can bring about such auspiciousness, but he cannot because of his humble status.
Now His Majesty is the emperor, rich in the world, in a position that can attract auspiciousness, has mastered the situation that can attract auspiciousness, and has the qualifications that can attract auspiciousness. His behavior is noble and virtuous, his intelligence is bright and his intentions are good, he loves the people and likes the scribes, and he can be said to be a moral monarch.
However, the heaven and earth did not respond, and the beautiful auspiciousness did not arrive. What is the reason?
summary: Dong Zhongshu's countermeasure explained that heaven sends disasters to warn rulers of moral failings. He emphasized that diligent study and virtuous conduct are essential for good governance. He argued that ritual and music are tools for education, and that a ruler must first rectify his own heart to rectify the court and the people. He criticized the Qin dynasty for abandoning moral education and relying solely on punishment, leading to its rapid downfall. He urged the Han dynasty to reform its institutions, establish a national university, and promote Confucian education to cultivate virtuous officials.

translation:
Dong Zhongshu's countermeasures said: I heard that Yao had received the mandate of heaven, and I was worried that the world would not be easy to govern. I did not take pleasure in being the emperor, so I killed and exiled the ministers who disturbed the country. I tried hard to find virtuous people, so I got Shun, Yu, Hou Ji, Gao, and Jiu Yao.
Many sage people came to help him improve his moral character, and many virtuous people came to assist him in fulfilling his duties. As a result, enlightenment flourished, the world was peaceful, and the people were content to be benevolent and happy to do righteousness. Everyone found their place, acted in accordance with etiquette and justice, and moved forward calmly on the right path.
So Confucius said: If there is a king, it will take thirty years to realize benevolent government. This is what he meant.
Yao reigned for seventy years and gave way to Yu Shun.
After Yao's death, the people of the world did not turn their hearts to Yao's son Danzhu, but turned their hearts to Shun.
Shun knew that he could not escape, so he ascended the throne and became the emperor, made Yu the prime minister, continued to appoint the people appointed by Yao, and inherited Yao's tradition and career. Therefore, he handed over his clothes and did nothing to bring peace to the world.
Confucius said that the music of "Shao" is very beautiful and very good. This is what it means.
As for Shang Zhou, he violated God's will, destroyed all things, killed virtuous and intelligent people, and harmed the people.
Both Boyi and Jiang Taigong were wise men at that time. They hid themselves and did not want to become officials.
Those who were serving as officials fled to rivers and seashores.
The world was dark and chaotic, and the people had no peace, so the people in the world abandoned King Zhou of Yin and supported King Wen of Zhou.
King Wen of Zhou obeyed the will of God to govern all things, and appointed virtuous and virtuous people as teachers. Therefore, Hong Yao, Dadian, San Yisheng and other wise men gathered in the Zhou court.
He showed benevolence to the people, and everyone in the world obeyed him, so Jiang Taigong came from a remote seaside to join him, and later became the third Duke of the Zhou Dynasty.
At this time, King Zhou of Shang was still the emperor, and the order of hierarchy was chaotic. The people fled in all directions. King Wen of Zhou was very sad and wanted the people to live a stable life, so he was too busy all day to tilt his head to the west and had no time to eat.
When Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, he first wrote about Wang Zhengzheng, and then recorded various things. This showed the so-called Su Wang who was in a lower position and was virtuous.
From this point of view, the emperor's organizational system is the same, but diligence and ease are different because the times they encountered are different.
Confucius said that the music of "Wu" is very beautiful, but it is not very good. This is what it means.
I heard that the institutional literary style and black and yellow decorations are used to distinguish between superior and inferior, to distinguish between high and low, and to encourage people to be virtuous.
"Spring and Autumn" was written under the mandate of heaven, so the first thing it formulated was to change the calendar and the color of clothes to conform to heaven.
Then, the system of palaces and banners is based on effective laws.
Therefore Confucius said: If you are extravagant, you are not humble enough; if you are frugal, you are simple.
Frugality is not a system of sage moderation.
summary: The emperor, impressed, asked further about the differences between ancient rulers like Yao and Shun, who governed with ease, and King Wen of Zhou, who was constantly busy. Dong Zhongshu explained that the times differed: Yao and Shun inherited a peaceful world, while King Wen faced chaos. He stressed that the essence of governance—benevolence, righteousness, and ritual—remains constant, but methods must adapt to circumstances. He advocated for selecting officials based on merit, not seniority, and for establishing schools to train talent.

translation:
Therefore, Yao cautiously carried out his way of governing the country every day, and Shun fulfilled his filial piety every day carefully and fearfully. As he accumulated more good deeds, he naturally became famous, had outstanding virtues, and was respected by others. This created the principle of gradual prosperity.
Accumulating good in oneself is like a person growing up without realizing it; accumulating evil in oneself is like a lamp burning oil, and it is not easy for people to see it.
Who can understand this truth unless he is a person who understands emotions and has insight into worldly situations?
This is the reason why Tang Yao and Yu Shun gained good reputations, but Xia Jie and Shang Zhou caused people pain and fear.
The consequences of good or evil actions are like shadows following human figures, reverberations following sounds.
Therefore, Jie and Zhou were violent and neglectful, the slanderous people were exploited, and the virtuous and wise people were hidden. As a result, Jie and Zhou's crimes became more and more obvious day by day, and the country became more and more chaotic. However, they were still peaceful and contented, thinking that they were like the sun in the sky, and finally gradually became corrupted and destroyed.
Those cruel and unkind monarchs did not perish all at once, but also gradually. Therefore, even though Jie and Zhou were immoral, they still reigned for more than ten years, which meant that they gradually declined and even perished.
Ce Wen said: The teachings of the three kings are imitated in different ways, and all have shortcomings. Some people say that they are eternal. Is there any difference in the intention of these two statements?
I have heard that the way of enjoying things without becoming sexually immoral and practicing them repeatedly without getting tired of them is called Tao.
The ways of the former kings must be biased and cannot be implemented, so in politics, there are sometimes dark and unworkable aspects. Just point out its biases and remedy its shortcomings.
Although the three kings follow different ways, they are not opposite. They are all designed to remedy mistakes and support decline. The reason why they are different is because the environment they encounter has changed.
Therefore Confucius said: The one who can govern the country without doing anything is Shun!
Shun only changed the calendar, changed the colors of carriages, horses, sacrifices, and clothing to comply with the destiny of heaven. The rest completely followed Yao's way of governing the country. Why should he change it!
Therefore, the king only changed the name of the system, but did not change the essence of the Tao.
However, the reason why the Xia Dynasty valued loyalty, the Yin Dynasty respected respect, and the Zhou Dynasty respected Wen is because when dynasties changed, the previous generation had faults, and this should be done in order to remedy them.
Confucius said: It can be known that the Yin Dynasty has increased or decreased according to the ritual system of the Xia Dynasty; that the Zhou Dynasty has increased or decreased according to the ritual system of the Yin Dynasty; and that others who succeeded the Zhou Dynasty have experienced hundreds of generations, but this can also be known.
Creation means that what hundreds of kings use are loyalty, respect, and culture.
The Xia Dynasty followed Yu and Shun, but did not mention additions or decreases. This is because the principles of the Xia Dynasty and Yu Shun were the same; the loyalty that the Xia Dynasty advocated was the same as that of Yu Shun.
The root of Tao comes from heaven. Heaven does not change and Tao does not change. Therefore, Yu inherited Shun's Tao, and Shun inherited Yao's Tao. The three saints taught each other and followed the same Tao. There were no measures to remedy disadvantages, so we do not say that they added or subtracted from Tao.
From this point of view, those who inherit the rule of the world have the same way; those who inherit the troubled times have to change their way.
Now that the Han Dynasty has inherited great chaos, it should reduce the literature of the Zhou Dynasty and use the loyalty of the Xia Dynasty.
Your Majesty has sage virtues and beautiful ways. He is saddened by the decline of the secular world and the unclearness of the royal way. Therefore, he elects virtuous and upright scholars, conducts discussions and tests, and intends to raise the virtues of benevolence and righteousness, clarify the emperor's legal system, and establish a peaceful way of governing the country.
I am ignorant and dishonest, recounting what I have heard, reciting what I have learned, and speaking the principles taught by the teacher, just to avoid forgetting them.
As for discussing the gains and losses of political affairs and studying the prosperity and poverty of society, these are the duties of ministers and assistants. The responsibilities of the three ministers and nine ministers are beyond the knowledge of Zhongshu. But I have a strange problem privately.
The world in ancient times is the world now, and the world now is the world in ancient times. They are the same world. In ancient times, the world was peaceful, in harmony, with beautiful customs. Things were done without orders and without restraint. Officials did not Evil, there are no thieves among the people, the prisons are empty, there are no prisoners, the kindness of the Lord has nourished the grass and trees, and spread to the four seas, the phoenix has flown, and the unicorn has appeared. If we compare the situation in ancient times to the present, how can it be so different?
What went wrong that led to this decline? I think maybe it goes against the ancient way of governing a country?
summary: In a third response, Dong Zhongshu elaborated on the harmony between heaven and humanity. He argued that heaven's will is reflected in natural phenomena, and rulers must align their actions with it. He criticized the Qin for its harsh laws and urged the Han to adopt the Xia dynasty's emphasis on loyalty to remedy the Zhou's excessive refinement. He proposed banning non-Confucian teachings to unify thought and law.

translation:
Prior to this, fires broke out successively in the Gaomiao Temple in Liaodong County where emperors of the Han Dynasty worshiped their ancestors, and in the Gaoyuan Hall in Changling, where the emperors of the Han Dynasty worshiped their ancestors. Dong Zhongshu deduced the relationship between fires from heaven and the human world. He wrote the draft of the memorial but did not submit it. The master's father Yan came to visit Dong Zhongshu and read the draft of the memorial in private. He was always jealous of Dong Zhongshu, so he stole the draft of the memorial and handed it to Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty summoned many Confucian scholars and asked them to read the draft of Dong Zhongshu's memorial. Dong Zhongshu's student Lu Bushu didn't know that this draft of the memorial was written by his teacher, and thought it was very ignorant.
So Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty handed Dong Zhongshu over to the officials for questioning and sentenced him to death. Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty issued an edict to pardon him. From then on, Dong Zhongshu did not dare to talk about disasters and changes.
Dong Zhongshu is honest and upright.
At that time, the Han Dynasty was using troops from surrounding ethnic minorities. Gongsunhong's research on "Gongyang Chunqiu" was not as good as Dong Zhongshu's. However, Gongsunhong catered to the secular world, gained great power, and became a high official.
Dong Zhongshu thought Gongsun Hong was flattering, but Gongsun Hong hated Dong Zhongshu.
Liu Duan, the king of Jiaoxi, was also the brother of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. He was particularly indulgent, cruel and arrogant, and repeatedly murdered two thousand stone officials sent by the imperial court.
Gongsun Hong told Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty: Only Dong Zhongshu can serve as the king of Jiaoxi.
King Liu Duan of Jiaoxi heard that Dong Zhongshu was a famous Confucian master and treated him with respect.
Dong Zhongshu was afraid that he would be punished by accident over time, so he resigned and went home on the grounds of old age and illness.
Dong Zhongshu served as prime minister of Jiangdu and Jiaoxi, assisting the arrogant princes and kings. He set an example for his subordinates by setting an example for his subordinates. He went to the eunuch many times to give outright advice, and formulated edicts to be implemented in the country. Both Jiangdu and Jiaoxi where he was located were well governed.
After he resigned from office and returned home, he didn't care about the family property at all. He just immersed himself in reading and writing books.
Dong Zhongshu was recuperating at home. If the court discussed important issues, it would send envoys and the court official Zhang Tang to his home to ask for his opinions. Dong Zhongshu's answers were all well-founded.
From the time when Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty first came to the throne, Wei Qihou Dou Ying and Wu'an Hou Tian successively became prime ministers and began to promote Confucianism. Dong Zhongshu responded by promoting Confucius and suppressing hundreds of schools of thought.
It was Dong Zhongshu who set up officials to manage schools and recommended talents, filial piety and honesty in the prefectures and counties.
Dong Zhongshu died at home in old age. Later, his family moved to Maoling County, and his son and grandson became high officials based on their knowledge.
Dong Zhongshu's works all clarify the purpose of Confucian classics. Together with memorials and teachings, there are a total of 123 works.
There are dozens of articles explaining the gains and losses of the "Spring and Autumn" records, as well as "Wen Ju", "Jade Cup", "Fan Dew", "Qingming" and "Bamboo Forest", with more than 100,000 words, all of which have been passed down to later generations.
I selected the content that is relevant to today's society and the imperial court and wrote it in the article.
summary: After his countermeasures, Dong Zhongshu served as prime minister to the King of Jiangdu, advising him with propriety. He later became a palace attendant but was nearly executed after a rival stole a draft of his memorial on disasters. Pardoned, he remained honest and upright. He later served the King of Jiaoxi, but fearing danger, he retired to write. His works, including over 100,000 words on the "Spring and Autumn," clarified Confucian principles. He died at home, and his descendants became high officials.

translation:
Praising day: Liu Xiang praised: Dong Zhongshu has the ability to be an assistant to the king. Even Yi Yin and Lu Wang cannot surpass him. Guan Zhong and Yan Ying are the assistants of the overlord, so I am afraid they are not as good as him.
Liu Xiang's son Liu Xin believed that Yi Yin and Lu Wang were the companions of a saint, and a king could not rise without them.
So when Yan Yuan died, Confucius said, "Oh!"
Heaven destroys me. Only Yan Yuan can compare with Yi Yin and Lu Wang. As for Zai Wo, Zigong, Ziyou, Zixia and others, they cannot be included in the ranks of saints.
After the Western Han Dynasty succeeded the Qin Dynasty and the burning of scholarship, Dong Zhongshu's "Six Classics" fell apart. So he put down his work and devoted himself to studying Confucian classics, which enabled later scholars to have a systematic and consistent understanding of Confucianism and became the leader of the group of Confucian scholars.
However, when examining the origins of his mentors and friends and looking at their influence on each other, Dong Zhongshu could not catch up with Zi You and Zi Xia, but it is wrong to say that Guan Zhong and Yan Ying were not as good as him, and Yi Yin and Lu Wang were not as good as him.
Liu Xiang's great-grandson Liu Gong is a gentleman who is good at commenting on figures. He believes that Liu Xin's evaluation of Dong Zhongshu is appropriate.
summary: Liu Xiang praised Dong Zhongshu as a king's assistant, comparable to Yi Yin and Lu Wang, surpassing Guan Zhong and Yan Ying. However, Liu Xiang's son Liu Xin argued that Dong, while a leader among Confucians after the Qin's destruction of texts, could not match Yi Yin or Lu Wang, though he was greater than Guan Zhong and Yan Ying. Liu Xin's view was later deemed accurate.

translation:
Kuai Tong, a native of Fanyang County, had the same name as Emperor Wu, Kuai Che.
When the Chu and Han Dynasties first emerged, Wu Chen attacked and pacified Fangdi, and was known as Wu Xinjun.
Kuai Tong lobbied Xu Gong, the magistrate of Fanyang County, and said: "I am a citizen of Fanyang, my name is Kuai Tong. I feel sorry for you that you are about to die, so I express my condolences."
Nevertheless, I congratulate you for having a chance to survive because of me, Kuai Tong.
Xu Gong thanked him repeatedly and asked: "Why do you express condolences?"
Kuai Tong said: You have been the county magistrate for more than ten years. You have killed other people's fathers, made other people's sons orphans, chopped off people's feet, and given people tattoos. Too many people have suffered.
The reason why loving fathers and filial sons dare not insert a knife into your belly is because they are afraid of the laws of the Qin Dynasty.
Now the world is in chaos, and the Qin Dynasty's decrees cannot be implemented. In this case, those loving fathers and filial sons will rush to stab you with bayonets in your belly to avenge you and achieve fame. This is the reason for my condolences.
Xu Gong asked again: "Why do you congratulate me on getting a husband and finding a way out?"
Kuai Tong replied: Lord Wu Xin who traveled to the country did not know that I was incompetent, so he sent people to inquire about his good or bad luck. Now I am going to meet and persuade him, and say to him: You must defeat the enemy before you gain the territory, and conquer the city before occupying it. I privately feel that it is very dangerous.
If you adopt my strategy, you will gain land without fighting, occupy the city without attacking, and be able to pacify thousands of miles by sending messages. Is this okay?
He will ask: What is your strategy?
I took the opportunity to reply: Magistrate Fan Yang should have organized his army, guarded the city, and resisted, but because he was cowardly and fearful of death, greedy and fond of wealth, he wanted to surrender the city to you first.
If he is the first to surrender to you and you do not give him any favors, then all the cities in the border areas will tell each other: The magistrate of Fanyang County was the first to surrender and was killed. We will definitely defend the city and it will be as difficult to capture as Jincheng Tangchi.
For your sake, it would be better to welcome Magistrate Fanyang with a yellow-covered and red-wheeled chariot, and let him ride on the border between Yan and Pang to show off. Then the cities on the border will tell each other: Magistrate Fanyang surrendered first and gained wealth. There will be a race to surrender, as easy as a mud ball rolling down a hillside.
Create what I call the strategy of pacifying Qianli by sending a message. , Xu Gong thanked him repeatedly and prepared carriages and horses to send Kuai Tong away.
Kuai Tong persuaded the military ministers with these words.
The military officials used a hundred chariots and two hundred cavalry to greet Duke Xu.
When Yan and Fang heard about this, more than thirty cities surrendered, just as expected by Kuai Tong's strategy.
Later, the Han general Han Xin captured the King of Wei, conquered Tiao and Dai, made Yan surrender, and pacified the three kingdoms one after another, and then led his troops eastward to attack Qi.
The army had not yet passed Pingyuan County. When I heard that Liu Bang, the king of Han, had sent Li Shiqi to persuade Qi to surrender, Han Xin wanted to stop the advance.
Kuai Tong lobbied Han Xin and said: General, you were ordered by the King of Han to attack the State of Qi, and the King of Han sent a separate envoy who was also a spy to persuade the State of Qi to surrender. Is there an edict ordering you to stop attacking?
Why not march?
Moreover, Mr. Li, as a scholar, rode there and persuaded more than 70 cities of Qi to surrender with his sharp tongue. General, you led tens of thousands of troops to capture more than 50 cities of Zhao.
summary: Kuai Tong, a native of Fanyang, lobbied Xu Gong, the magistrate of Fanyang, during the Chu-Han conflict. He warned Xu Gong that his harsh rule had created many enemies, and with Qin laws no longer enforceable, he was in danger. Kuai Tong then proposed a plan to Wu Chen, Wu Xinjun: rather than attacking cities, he should welcome Xu Gong with honor to encourage other cities to surrender. Wu Chen followed this advice, and over thirty cities surrendered without battle. Later, Kuai Tong persuaded Han Xin to attack Qi despite Li Shiqi's diplomatic mission, arguing that military conquest would earn greater merit. Han Xin agreed, crossed the Yellow River, and defeated Qi, leading to Li Shiqi's execution. Kuai Tong later urged Han Xin to betray Liu Bang and create a tripartite balance of power, warning that Han Xin's achievements made him a threat to the Han king. Han Xin hesitated, citing Liu Bang's kindness, and declined. Kuai Tong, fearing retribution, feigned madness. After Han Xin's execution, Liu Bang summoned Kuai Tong, who defended himself by saying a dog barks at those not its master. Liu Bang pardoned him. Kuai Tong later served as a guest to Cao Shen, the prime minister of Qi, and recommended the reclusive scholars Shu Guo and Liang Shijun. He also wrote a book on lobbying strategies.

translation:
So he went to see Cao Xiangguo and said: Some women remarry just three days after their husbands die, while some women would rather live in seclusion and remain widowed. If you want to marry a daughter-in-law, which one will you choose?
Cao Xiangguo said: I will marry the one who doesn't want to get married.
Kuai Tong said: Then, the same should be done when seeking ministers. Mr. Shuguo and Liang Shijun were virtuous and handsome men of Qi State. They lived in seclusion in the mountains and forests. They did not want to get married and never came out to seek official positions.
I hope you will send someone to treat me with courtesy.
Cao Xiangguo said: I respectfully accept your order.
Treat both of them as distinguished guests.
Kuai Tong discussed the contingency techniques of lobbyists during the Warring States Period, also added his own comments, and wrote a book called "Juan Yong".
At the beginning, Kuai Tong had a good relationship with Qiren An Qisheng. An Qisheng once made suggestions for Xiang Yu, but Xiang Yu could not adopt them.
Xiang Yu wanted to give Kuai Tong and An Qisheng titles and fiefs, but these two were always unwilling to accept them.
Wu Bei, a native of Chu.
Some people say that his ancestor is a descendant of Wu Zixu.
Wu Bei became famous for his talents and served as a lieutenant in Huainan Kingdom.
At that time, the king of Huainan, Liu An, loved academics and was devoted to the virtuous. He recruited hundreds of handsome and learned people, and Wu was ranked first.
After a long time, the king of Huainan conspired to rebel, and Wu was admonished privately many times.
Later, the King of Huainan was sitting in Shu Palace and summoned Wu Bei to discuss matters with him. He called: General, please come forward.
Wu was asked: Where did the king get the words of subjugation?
Once upon a time, Wu Zixu advised the king of Wu, but the king did not accept it. Wu Zixu said: "Now I see elk roaming on the Gusu platform, and now I will also see thorns growing in the palace, and dew soaking the skirts of my clothes."
So the King of Huainan was very angry and detained Wu Bei's parents and imprisoned them for three months.
The king of Huainan summoned Wu Yuan again and said, "General, have you listened to me?"
Wu Bei said: No! I will advise you, your Majesty.
I heard that smart people are wise and can predict things before they appear, so the saints are foolproof when doing things.
King Wen of Zhou's actions made him famous in later generations, and he was listed as the second king. Creation means that he should act in accordance with the heart of heaven.
King Huainan asked: Is the Han Dynasty now stable or chaotic?
Wu was said: The world is safe and sound.
King Huainan said unhappily: "Why do you say that the world is stable?"
Wu Bei replied: I have privately observed that the relationship between the emperor and his ministers, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger are all orderly and reasonable. Everything the emperor does follows the way of the ancient sage kings. The customs are honest and the rules and regulations are perfect.
Wealthy merchants traveled around the world carrying large amounts of goods in their vehicles. Roads were open to all directions and trade was very prosperous.
South Vietnam surrendered, Qiang and Fen paid tribute and became ministers, and Shu Ou entered the court to pay homage to the emperor. Expanding Changyusai and expanding Shuofang County, the Huns suffered setbacks and were severely weakened.
Although it cannot keep up with the peaceful and prosperous times of ancient times, it is still safe and sound.
summary: Wu Bei, a descendant of Wu Zixu, served as a lieutenant in Huainan under King Liu An. When the king plotted rebellion, Wu Bei repeatedly admonished him, arguing that the Han dynasty was stable and prosperous, with orderly governance, thriving trade, and subdued enemies. The king dismissed this, citing the Qin collapse as precedent. Wu Bei countered that Qin's tyranny had caused widespread suffering, while the Han emperor ruled with benevolence and had popular support. He warned that rebellion would fail, as the king's forces were weak and the times were peaceful. The king ignored him and proceeded with plans, but the conspiracy was discovered. Wu Bei surrendered and confessed, but was executed despite his earlier praise of Han, as Zhang Tang argued his initial role in planning the rebellion was unforgivable.

translation:
So the sons of these dignitaries and relatives were very frightened, and they all went to see the emperor, kowtowed and begged for mercy, and were willing to pay money to atone for their sins.
Emperor Wu agreed to their request and ordered them to hand over the money to the Northern Army according to their official levels, totaling tens of millions of dollars.
Emperor Wu believed that Jiang Chong was loyal and upright, and enforced the law without favoritism, and was very satisfied with his suggestions.
When Jiang Chong came out for inspection, he met Princess Guantao riding a car on Chidao. Jiang Chong stopped her and asked why. The princess said: "I am allowed to walk on Chidao under the order of the Queen Mother."
Jiang Chong said: "Only the princess is allowed to walk on the horse road, and the accompanying carriages and horses are not allowed to pass."
All the accompanying carriages and horses were reported and confiscated.
Later, Jiang Chong followed Emperor Wu to Ganquan Palace. When he saw the envoy sent by the prince to greet the emperor in a carriage walking on the road, Jiang Chong detained the envoy.
When the prince heard about this, he sent someone to apologize to Jiang Chong and said: It's not that I begrudge the carriages and horses, but I really don't want the emperor to hear about this, thinking that I usually don't discipline my subordinates.
I hope Mr. Jiang can forgive this.
Jiang Chong refused to listen and finally reported to Emperor Wu.
Emperor Wu said: This is what ministers should do.
As a result, Jiang Chong gained great credibility and became a powerful figure in the capital.
Jiang Chong was promoted to Captain Shuiheng, and many of his family and friends received help from him.
After a long time, he was dismissed from office because of his crime.
It happened that Zhu Anshi of Yangling reported that Prime Minister Gongsun He's son and Grand Servant Gongsun Jingsheng had cursed the emperor with witchcraft, which implicated Princess Yangshi and the princesses of Zhuyi. Gongsun He and his son were killed as a result.
See "The Biography of Gongsun He" for details.
Later, Emperor Wu visited Ganquan Palace and fell ill. Jiang Chong saw that Emperor Wu was old and was afraid that he would be killed by the prince after his death, so he took the opportunity to cause trouble and wrote a letter saying that the emperor was ill because someone was practicing witchcraft.
So Emperor Wu appointed Jiang Chong as an envoy to investigate and deal with those who practiced witchcraft.
