Jiang Chong directed the Hu wizards to dig in the ground everywhere, looking for puppets, and arresting those who engaged in witchcraft and night-time ritual curses. Let the Hu wizards observe the places contaminated by ghosts, mark them, dig out the puppets, arrest the people in the package, torture them, heat the iron, roast the interrogated person, and force him to confess.
The common people turned around and falsely accused each other, and the officials convicted the falsely accused of treason and injustice. As a result, tens of thousands of people were killed before and after.
At that time, Emperor Wu was already old and suspected that everyone around him was practicing witchcraft to curse him. No matter whether he was guilty of this crime or not, no one dared to file a lawsuit.
Jiang Chong had already understood the emperor's thoughts and took the opportunity to say that there was a witchcraft spirit in the palace. He first investigated the wives in the harem who were not favored by the emperor, and then in turn got the queen's head. Finally, he dug out the witchcraft in the palace and obtained the Tongmu Ren.
The prince was very frightened and could not explain to the emperor himself, so he arrested Jiang Chong and personally supervised and executed him.
He scolded: You are a slave of the country!
summary: Jiang Chong, originally named Jiang Qi, fled to Chang'an after a feud with Prince Liu Dan of Zhao. He reported the prince's incest and adultery, leading to Liu Dan's deposition. Jiang Chong gained Emperor Wu's favor through his appearance and advice on foreign policy. He was appointed to supervise the capital, enforcing laws against luxury and arresting offenders. He detained the prince's envoy for using the imperial road, earning the emperor's praise. Later, fearing the prince would harm him after the emperor's death, Jiang Chong fabricated a witchcraft scandal, accusing the prince of cursing the emperor. He tortured confessions, killing tens of thousands. The prince, unable to defend himself, arrested and executed Jiang Chong. The prince's rebellion failed, and Emperor Wu later annihilated Jiang Chong's clan.

translation:
Isn't it enough to disturb your king and his son?
Come to disturb our father and son again!
The prince was finally defeated because of this.
For details, see "The Biography of Prince Ru."
Later, Emperor Wu found out that Jiang Chong was responsible, so he annihilated his three clans.
Xifu Gong, whose courtesy name is Ziwei, is from Heyang County, Hanoi County.
When he was young, he was a doctoral student, studied "Spring and Autumn", and read biographies and books of hundreds of schools of thought.
His majestic appearance made everyone feel strange.
When Emperor Ai first came to the throne, the queen's father, Fu Yan, the Marquis of Kongxiang, and Xifu Gong were from the same county. They had a good relationship. Therefore, through Fu Yan's introduction, Xifu Gong's circle of friends became wider and wider.
Before this, Sun Chong of Chang'an was also known for his good lobbying skills. He was dismissed when he was the governor of Runan County. He made friends with Xi Fu Gong, and they both submitted letters at the same time and were recruited to obey the emperor's orders.
At that time, Emperor Ai was ill and had just ascended the throne. Someone reported that the Queen Mother of King Xiao of Zhongshan had cursed the emperor with witchcraft. The Queen Mother and her brother Feng Shen, the Marquis of Yixiang, committed suicide, but their charges have not yet been found out.
After that, a large boulder stood up automatically on the dangerous mountain in Wuyan County, and a passage emerged.
Xifu Gong and Sun Chong planned and said: The emperor has no son to be his heir, and he is ill for a long time. The princes of Guandong are all trying to compete for the throne.
Nowadays, there are big rocks standing up on their own in Wuyan County. I heard that those evil ministers relied on past events and thought that there were big rocks standing up on their own when Emperor Xuan rose up among the people.
Therefore, Shuping King Liu Yun and his queen worshiped and cursed the emperor day and night, hoping to obtain the throne.
On the contrary, Wu Hong, the queen's uncle, was favored by the emperor because of his knowledge of alchemy and ability to cure diseases, and was allowed to enter and exit the forbidden gates of the palace.
Huo Xian's conspiracy will be carried out on the medicine cup and spoon, and Jing Ke's incident will definitely happen on the emperor's curtain.
The situation is so dangerous that the whistleblower will definitely succeed. Exposing the country's treacherous officials and killing the emperor's enemies is a clever way to gain a title.
Xifu Gong, Sun Chong and Tan, the right master of the Zhonglang, reported to the court through Song Hong, the official of the Zhongchang, about King Dongping's rebellion.
Emperor Ai was very angry and handed the case to the relevant departments for investigation. King Shuping Liu Yun, Liu Yun's queen Ye and Wu Hong were all killed for the crime.
Emperor Ai promoted Sun Chong to be the prefect of Nanyang County, Tan, the right master, to be the captain of Yingchuan County, and Song Hong and Xifu Gong were both appointed to the post of Zuo Cao, the official of Guanglu.
At that time, Dong Xian, the servant, was very favored by the emperor. The emperor wanted to make him a marquis, so he issued an edict saying: Xifu Gong and Sun Chong reported the conspiracy through Dong Xian. Now Dong Xian is made Marquis of Gao'an, Sun Chong is Marquis of Fangyang, and Xifu Gong is Marquis of Yiling. Each of them has a thousand households.
The right master was given the title of Marquis Tan Guannei and was given the title of food town.
summary: Xifu Gong, a scholar from Heyang, gained fame through his friend Fu Yan, the queen's father. With Sun Chong, he fabricated a plot against King Shuping Liu Yun, accusing him of witchcraft. The king and his associates were executed, and Xifu Gong was made Marquis of Yiling. He became a close advisor to Emperor Ai, criticizing officials and proposing policies, including expanding irrigation canals. He suggested a deceptive strategy to weaken the Xiongnu by forging letters, but General Gongsun Lu opposed it. Xifu Gong also urged military preparations based on astrological signs, but Prime Minister Wang Jia warned against flattery and deceit. The emperor initially supported Xifu Gong, but after a solar eclipse, Dong Xian undermined him. Xifu Gong was dismissed and later accused of cursing the emperor. He died in prison, and his family was exiled. After Emperor Ai's death, Sun Chong and others were also exiled.

translation:
Having been a general for several years is not as great as the contribution of a Confucian scholar.
So Han Xin thought what he said made sense, adopted his suggestion, and finally crossed the Yellow River.
The King of Qi had listened to Li Shiqi's persuasion, so he left him behind, drank and had fun together, and removed the defense against the Han Dynasty.
Han Xin therefore attacked the Qi army in Lixia and came to Linmiao City.
The King of Qi thought that Li Shiqi had deceived him, so he put him in boiling water and boiled him to death. As a result, he was defeated and fled.
Han Xin finally pacified Qi and established himself as the acting king of Qi.
At that time, the King of Han was under siege in Rongyang, so he sent Zhang Liang to make Han Xin the official King of Qi, comfort him, and make him firmly side with the King of Han.
Xiang Yu also sent Wu She to persuade Han Xin to join forces with him.
Kuai Tong knew that the change of the world situation depended on Han Xin, and wanted to persuade Han Xin to betray the Han Dynasty, so he first hinted at Han Xin in cryptic words: I once learned the art of physiognomy, and observing your face, I can only be made a marquis, and you will always be in danger; but looking at your back, it is very noble and difficult to tell.
Han Xin asked: What do you mean?
Kuai Tong then asked others to go away, and then said: When the world first rises up, heroes and heroes establish themselves as princes and kings, raise their arms and shout, and the people of the world gather like clouds and mist, are mixed and accumulated like fish scales, and rise up quickly like a strong wind.
People often only worry about overthrowing the Qin Dynasty.
Now Liu Bang and Xiang Yu are fighting, and countless people have been displaced.
The King of Han led hundreds of thousands of troops to defend Gong and Luo. Taking advantage of the dangers of the mountains and rivers, he fought several battles in vain. He was defeated and fled without rescue. He was defeated in Rongyang, wounded in Chenggao, and fled to Wan and Ye. This is said to be a person whose wisdom and courage are in trouble.
The Chu people raised their troops in Pengcheng, fought many battles, and were invincible. They marched to Rongyang, taking advantage of the victory, and shocked the world. However, they were blocked between Jing and Suo, and they were unable to advance near Xishan. It has been three years now.
Their vigor was thwarted at the steep pass, the treasury was depleted of food, and the people were miserable, not knowing who to surrender to.
In my opinion, unless there are sages in the world. Otherwise, it will be impossible to eliminate the disasters in the world.
Now the fate of Liu Bang and Xiang Yu is in your hands.
If you help the King of Han, the King of Han will win; if you join forces with the King of Chu, the King of Chu will succeed.
I am willing to express my sincere sincerity to you, but I am afraid that you will not accept my suggestion.
Now for your sake, it would be better for both of them to benefit and coexist together. If the world is divided into three parts and they stand as a tripod, no one will dare to attack first.
With your wisdom and wisdom, you have many armies in mail, occupying the powerful state of Qi, uniting Yan and Zhao, sending troops to the empty land to control their rear, obeying the people's will, heading west to stop the fighting between Chu and Han, and saving the soldiers from death. No one in the world dares to disobey!
If you own the land between Huai and Si according to the original territory of Qi, appease the princes with your kindness, give them a home in peace, and treat the wise men with courtesy, then all the princes in the world will come to worship Qi.
summary: The text concludes with a lament on the dangers of eloquent but harmful advisors, citing historical examples from the Spring and Autumn period to the Han dynasty, where slander and deceit led to disasters, including the deaths of rulers and the ruin of states.

translation:
When Xue Xuan was the prime minister, Xue Xiu was appointed as the Order of Chuojian. Sa Xuan welcomed his stepmother, but Xue Xiu refused to send her away.
When his stepmother fell ill and died, Xue Xiu resigned from his official position to mourn.
Xue Xuan told Xue Xiu that three years of mourning was rarely possible. The brothers refuted each other and had disagreements. Xue Xiu then completed the mourning period, so the brothers were not harmonious.
A long time later, when Emperor Ai had just ascended the throne, Dr. Shen Xianren came to Shizhong, who was also from Donghai. He slandered Xue Xuan by saying that Xue Xuan did not provide for his mother, that he did not wear mourning clothes after his mother died, and that he had little affection for his flesh and blood. He had previously been dismissed from office due to disloyalty and unfilial piety, and he should not be made a marquis and stay in the imperial office again.
Zhengxuan's son Bichi was appointed as the minister of Youcao. Hearing his words many times, he bribed Yang Ming, a retainer, in order to disfigure Shenxian's face and prevent him from holding an official position.
There happened to be a vacancy in the post of secretary, and Xue Kuang was worried that Shen Sheng would become the secretary, so he ordered Yang Ming to block the road outside the palace gate and attack Shen Qi, cutting off his nose and lips, and causing eight wounds on his body.
The matter was handed over to Yousi, and Yushi Zhongchengzhong and others reported: Xue Kuang is a minister in the court, and his father was the original prime minister. He was named a prince twice. He did not warn each other and uphold the teachings. Instead, his flesh and blood were suspicious of each other. He suspected that Shen Xian listened to Xue Xiu's words and slandered Xue Xuan.
What Shen Xian said was what Xue Xuan had done, what everyone had seen, and what the court should have heard.
Xue Kuang knew that Shen Xian was involved in the affair, and was worried that he would file a report against Xue Xuan after becoming a minister, so he openly ordered Zhelong and others to approach the palace, block the road and injure the ministers, hoping to block the hearing and vision of the court and block the way to cut off discussion.
Xue Kuang was ferocious and cunning and had nothing to fear him. The people were noisy and spread rumors, which was different from ordinary people fighting and fighting out of resentment and anger.
We have heard that respecting one’s neighbors means being close to the Lord.
According to etiquette, you have to get off the vehicle after passing the monarch's gate. When you see the horses of the monarch's carriage, you should touch the crossbar in front of the carriage. The monarch's livestock must also respect them.
According to the principle of "Spring and Autumn", if the intention is bad but succeeds, you cannot escape punishment, and the beginning of such behavior that offends the emperor cannot be encouraged. Xue Kuang is the chief villain. He hurt others with his own hands. The consequences and intentions are both bad and disrespectful.
Yang Ming should be severely convicted, and both Yang Ming and Xue Kuang should be executed in a busy city and their bodies should be displayed to the public.
Ting Weizhi believed: Legally speaking, if someone cuts someone with a knife in a fight, he will be sentenced to a full sentence or a penalty of Cheng Dan. The person who hurts someone will be charged with an additional level, and he will be charged with the same crime as the person who planned it.
The emperor's proclamation ordered that no charges should be brought against him for defamation and deception.
Ancient books say: A person who does not treat others morally and is beaten is as guilty as the person who beats him because he hates him for being dishonest.
Shen Xian was very friendly with Xue Xiu, but he repeatedly publicized Xue Xuan's sins and spread them widely, which was very inappropriate and could not be said to be honest.
Xue Kuang hurt Shen Xian because of his father, and the plan had already been decided. Later, when he heard about the appointment of candidates for Sili, he urged Yang Ming according to the previous plan. He did not set up the plan because he was worried about Shen Xian being appointed Sili.
It was originally a fight that turned out to be private. Although Shen Xian was stabbed and injured on the road outside Yemen, it was no different from the fights between ordinary people.
Those who kill are put to death and those who injure others are sentenced. This is a common principle from ancient times to the present, and it cannot be changed in three generations.
Confucius said: We must distinguish our correct names.
If the status is not correct, the punishment will be inappropriate. If the punishment is inappropriate, the people will not know what to do.
Now that Xue Kuang is regarded as the chief villain, it is disrespectful for Yang Ming to hurt people with his own hands, which makes no distinction between public and private affairs.
The main meaning of "Spring and Autumn" is to determine the crime by inferring the original intention.
Investigating the root cause, Xue Kuang vented his anger because his father was slandered, and had no other major sins.
But to add slanderous and deceptive words, to aggregate small faults to promote the crime of great punishment, to subject people to the death penalty, and to violate the edicts of the sages, I am afraid that this is not the original intention of the law and cannot be implemented.
A wise ruler does not increase punishment because of his anger.
Yang Ming should be sentenced to the crime of injuring others. Xue Kuang and the conspirators should have their titles lowered and be sentenced to death and Cheng Dan.
The emperor asked the ministers about this matter.
summary: Xue Xuan, a native of Tan County, Shuhai, rose from minor official posts to become a respected administrator. Known for his integrity and legal expertise, he served as Censor Zhongcheng under Emperor Cheng, advocating for simpler governance and criticizing harsh laws that disrupted social harmony. His memorials urged leniency and moral cultivation, which the emperor approved. As governor of Linhuai and later Chenliu, he quelled bandits and earned widespread respect. In Zuo Fengyi, he skillfully handled corrupt officials like Yang Zhan and Xie You, using subtle pressure to force their resignations, while also reassigning ineffective magistrates to improve governance. Xue Xuan’s fair and compassionate rule, including his handling of a jailer’s suicide, won him praise. He was promoted to Shaofu and later, on Gu Yong’s recommendation, became Imperial Censor and then Prime Minister, enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoyang. However, his tenure was marred by criticism for being overly meticulous and lacking depth in classical learning. After failing to quell uprisings in Guanghan and mishandling tax collection during a funeral, he was dismissed by the emperor for incompetence. Later reinstated as a special advisor, he was again dismissed for associating with the disgraced Chunyu Chang. His later years were troubled by family discord with his brother Xue Xiu over mourning rites, and his son Xue Kuang’s violent attack on Shen Xian, who had slandered Xue Xuan. Despite legal debates, Xue Kuang was exiled, and Xue Xuan died at home as a commoner.

translation:
At that time, Xiao Yu, the son of the former general Wangzhi, and Chen Xian, the son of the imperial censor Wan Nian, were known for their outstanding talents because they were the sons of Gongqing, and Zhu Bo was friendly with them.
At that time, the counties where the imperial mausoleums were located were all under the jurisdiction of Taichang, and Zhu Bo was appointed as Anlingcheng because Taichang was found to be clean and honest.
Later he resigned from the official position and went to Jingzhao. He successively served as Cao Shilie's deputy, and went out of Beijing to become the postal governor and secretary. He handled the local affairs under his jurisdiction very well, and everyone in the county praised him.
Chen Xian was appointed as Yushi Zhongcheng. He was convicted of leaking words that were prohibited by the palace and was imprisoned.
Zhu Bo resigned from his official position and secretly walked to Tingwei's house to investigate Chen Xian's case.
Chen Xian was tortured and interrogated and was seriously injured. Zhu Bo pretended to be a doctor and went to prison. He was able to see Chen Xian and fully knew the crime he had committed.
Zhu Bo was released from prison, changed his name, and suffered the punishment for Chen Xian. He was beaten hundreds of times, and Chen Xian was finally exempted from the death penalty.
Chen Xian was sentenced to be released from prison, and Zhu Bo became famous because of this incident and became a county meritorious official.
After a long time, Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, and General Wang Feng took control of the government. He petitioned Chen Xian to be the chief historian.
Chen Xian recommended Xiao Yu and Zhu Bo as shogunate officials. Wang Feng was surprised by Zhu Bo's talents, so he recommended Zhu Bo to be the magistrate of Luyang. Later, he was transferred to Yunyang and Pingling counties. Because of his best political performance, he was appointed to the capital as the magistrate of Chang'an.
After the Qingming Dynasty in Kyoto, he was promoted to governor of Jizhou.
Zhu Bo was originally a military attaché and had no experience in handling matters in a civil service. When he became a governor and inspected his subordinates, hundreds of officials and civilians blocked the road and complained on their own. The government offices were full. Officers came to report and requested to stay in the county temporarily. They registered and met with everyone who complained on their own. After the matter was completed, they set off. They wanted to use this to observe and test Zhu Bo.
Zhu Bo understood in his heart and told the outsiders to prepare the carriages and horses quickly.
The officers reported that the carriages and horses were ready. Zhu Bo came out and boarded the carriages to meet with those who had complained on their own. He sent officers to clearly inform the officials and the people: Those who want to complain to the county magistrate, and the governor does not supervise the officials in Huang Shou, should go to the county on their own.
If you want to complain to the official Mo Shou, who has two thousand stones, wait for the envoy to come back from inspecting his subordinates and go to the governor's office.
People who were wronged by officials or who complained about robbers and thieves had to go to their respective departments to handle the matter.
Zhu Bo stopped the car and issued a verdict, and four to five hundred people left, like gods.
The officials and the people were shocked. They did not expect Zhu Bo to deal with the unexpected events to such an extent.
Later, Zhu Bo slowly investigated and found out that he was always engaged in instigating people to gather in gatherings.
Zhu Bo killed this official, and all the prefectures and counties were afraid of Zhu Bo's majesty.
Zhu Bo was transferred to Bingzhou governor and canal guard, and was promoted to Langxie prefect.
The custom in Qi County is that people are slow-tempered and arrogant to cultivate their reputation. Zhu Bo had just taken office, and the right Cao Shidu wrote a letter saying that he was ill and bedridden.
Zhu Bo asked the reason and replied: Fear!
summary: Zhu Bo, from Duling, began as a poor county official, known for his boldness and friendship with elite sons like Chen Xian. He famously disguised himself to save Chen Xian from prison, enduring punishment himself, which launched his reputation. Under Wang Feng, he became magistrate of several counties, excelling in governance. As governor of Jizhou, he astutely handled a flood of complaints by issuing swift verdicts, astonishing officials. In Langye, he aggressively reformed lax customs, dismissing sick officials and enforcing strict dress codes, while using intimidation and rewards to control subordinates. His tenure in Zuo Fengyi was marked by cunning and harshness, such as rehabilitating a scarred thief as an informant and exposing corrupt officials through psychological tactics. Promoted to Da Si Nong and later Tingwei, he demonstrated legal acumen by correctly predicting case outcomes. He became Grand Sikong under Emperor Ai, advocating for restoring the Censor’s office over the Grand Sikong post, arguing it better suited the Han system. He also reversed the abolition of provincial governors, favoring their supervisory role. Frugal and workaholic, Zhu Bo shunned luxury but cultivated a network of guests, aiding their ambitions. However, he became entangled in court intrigues, allying with Fu Yan to please Empress Dowager Dingtao, leading to the dismissal of rivals like Kong Guang. As Prime Minister, he was pressured by the empress dowager to impeach Fu Xi, but the emperor discovered his collusion. Interrogated, Zhu Bo was charged with treason for manipulating affairs with relatives, and he committed suicide, his fief revoked. His rise and fall exemplified ambition without moral restraint, as noted in historical critiques.

translation:
Among the rulers of Nanyi, Yelang is the largest. To the west, Mimo is the largest, and Dian is the largest. From Dian to the north, Qiongdu is the largest.
People in these countries all wear cone-shaped buns, cultivate fields, and have their own small towns and villages.
In addition, from Tongshi in the west to Yeyu in the north, they are named Lun and Kunming. They all have braided hair and move around with the grazing livestock. They have no fixed residence and no ruler. Their range of activities is about several thousand miles.
From Song to the northeast, the king's length is calculated by ten, and the migration and extraction are the largest.
From Judu to the northeast, the ruler's length is calculated by ten, and Ran Xiao is the largest.
Among the customs there, some are settled and some are migrating.
To the west of Shu County, from Ranji to the northeast, the king's length is calculated by ten, and the white horse is the largest. These are all Di tribe.
The above are all barbarians outside the southwest of Bajun and Shujun.
At first, King Chu Wei sent General Zhuang Cuo to lead his army up the Yangtze River and captured the area west of Bajun and Qianzhong County.
Zhuang Qi is a descendant of King Zhuang of Chu. Zhuang Chu arrived at Dianchi Lake.

translation:

Tang Meng rewarded Duotong heavily, told him the stakes, and agreed with Duotong to appoint officials to Yelang and let Duotong's son hold an official position similar to a county magistrate.

Tang Meng reported to the court, and the court designated the location of Yelang and these small countries as Jianwei County.
The Han Dynasty recruited infantrymen from Bajun and Shujun to build roads from Fendao to the Yangke River.

These situations made the emperor very worried, so he sent Gongsun Hong to those places to inspect and understand.

Gongsun Hong and others took the opportunity to state the damage caused by the campaign against the southwestern barbarians, and believed that the campaign against the southwestern barbarians could be temporarily suspended in order to concentrate on dealing with the Xiongnu.

If the road to Shu could be opened, it would be convenient for Shendu to communicate with the Han Dynasty, which would be beneficial to the Han Dynasty.
Therefore, the emperor ordered Wang Ranyu, Bai Shichang, Lu Yueren and more than ten people to search for a small road and set out from the southwestern Yi area to find the country of Shendu.

The leader of Qielan was worried that his army would go away during the expedition, and nearby countries would take the opportunity to plunder their own old and weak people, so he and his tribe launched a rebellion and killed the Han Dynasty envoys and the governor of Jianwei County.
The Han Dynasty dispatched criminals from Bajun and Shujun, who were supposed to attack southern Guangdong, and the Eighth School Lieutenant to attack Qielan.
Just in time to catch up with the defeat of South Vietnam, the eight lieutenants of the Han Dynasty did not go down the Yangke River as originally planned. Zhonglang generals Guo Chang and Wei Guang led their troops back and took advantage of the march to punish Qielan, who had blocked the Han Dynasty's road to the Dian Kingdom. He killed tens of thousands, and then pacified Nanyi and used the land as Yangke County.
Yelanghou relied on Nanyue at first. After the fall of Nanyue, the Han Dynasty's army returned and punished the rebellious countries. Yelanghou went to Beijing to see the emperor, who named him King Yelang.
After the fall of Southern Guangdong, the Han Dynasty killed Qielan and Qiongdu Lord, and also killed the Lord of Zhadu. The leaders of Ran Xiaoyi were shocked and panicked, and asked to submit to the Han Dynasty and let the Han Dynasty appoint officials. Therefore, the Han Dynasty designated the residence of Qiongdu Yi as Guangdong County, the residence of Zhadu Yi as Shenli County, the residence of Ran Xiaoyi as Wenshan County, and the residence of Baima Yi to the west of Guanghan County as Wudu County.
The emperor ordered Wang Ranyu to persuade the Dian king to join the dynasty with the military situation of destroying Eastern Guangdong and conquering the southern barbarians.
The King of Dian has tens of thousands of tribesmen, and in the northeast there are Laoshen and Mimo. They have the same surname as Dian and rely on each other. They do not listen to the advice about the King of Dian entering the dynasty.
Lao Shen and Mi Mo repeatedly offended the envoys, officials and soldiers of the Han Dynasty.
In the second year of Yuanfeng, the emperor mobilized troops from Bajun and Shujun to attack Laoshen and Mimo. The troops came to Dian Kingdom.
Since the King of Dian was originally friendly with the Han Dynasty, the Han Dynasty did not execute him.
The King of Dian broke away from the Western Yi, and the whole country surrendered to the Han Dynasty. He asked the Han Dynasty to appoint officials and go to Beijing to see the emperor. So the Han Dynasty made Nahuo a Yizhou county and gave the king of Dian the royal seal so that he could still rule his people.
There were hundreds of leaders of the southwestern barbarians, but only the leaders of Yelang and Dian received the royal seal.
Dian is a small country that was most favored by the Han Dynasty.

translation:
Twenty-three years later, in the first year of Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty, the people of Liantou and Guzhen in Yizhou rebelled and killed the chief officials.
More than 30,000 people from 24 countries including Pang Ke, Tan Zhi, and Tong Bing also rebelled.
The Han Dynasty sent Captain Shuiheng to mobilize more than 10,000 soldiers from Shu and Jianwei counties to attack Qunke and completely defeat the rebels.
Three years later, Guzhen and Ye Yu rebelled again. The Han Dynasty sent Shuiheng Captain Lu Pihu to lead county troops to attack the rebels.
Before Lu Pihu's army could advance to Yeyu and Guzhen, the barbarians killed the prefect of Yizhou and took advantage of the victory to fight Lu Pihu. More than 4,000 Han soldiers died in battle or drowned.
The next year, he sent troops such as Wang Ping and Dahong Tian Guangming to attack, completely defeating the rebels in Yizhou, capturing and killing more than 50,000 people, and capturing more than 100,000 livestock.
The Emperor said: Gou Ding Hou Neng Bo led the leaders and people of the small country under his jurisdiction to attack the rebels. He captured and killed them with meritorious service, and established Nang Bo as the King of Xuan Ding.
Dahonglu Tian Guangming was rewarded with the title of Marquis of Guannei and a settlement of 300 households.
A year later, the Di people in Wudu County rebelled. The imperial court dispatched Jinwu Ma Shijian, Long'ehou Han Zeng and Dahonglu Tian Guangming to lead troops to attack the rebels.
During the reign of Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty in Heping, Wang Xing of Yelang, Wang Yu of Gouding, and Hou Yu of Luwo raised their troops to attack each other.
The governor of Yangke requested to attack Yelang Wang Xing and others. Those who discussed troop deployment believed that the road was too far to attack, so the imperial court sent Zhang Kuangchijie, a Taizhong doctor from Shu County, to reconcile the conflicts between the barbarian princes.
Yelang, Wang Xing and others did not obey the orders of the Han Dynasty officials. They carved wooden figures that looked like Han Dynasty officials and stood on the roadside to shoot.
Du Qin said to General Wang Feng: Taizhong official Zhang Kuang sent an envoy to reconcile the disputes between the barbarian princes. The princes accepted the Shao Order of the Han Dynasty, but further attacked each other, despised the Han Dynasty envoys, and were not afraid of the country's power. This shows the effect of reconciliation.
Worried that the people who discussed sending troops were weak and insisted on reconciliation, the prefect observed the movements of the barbarians and reported to the police only when something happened.
Like this, it will take a few more months for the barbarian princes to organize their tribes and stubbornly adhere to their own strategies. They have many followers and are extremely angry, and they will definitely kill each other and eliminate them.
If he knows that he has committed a crime, he will suddenly become mad and rebellious and kill the prefect or captain. Traveling far and deep into hot, humid and poisonous weeds areas, even if there are generals like Sun Wu and Wu Qi, and warriors like Meng Ben and Xia Yu, is equivalent to being plunged into fire and water. If you go there, you will definitely be scorched and submerged, and you will not be able to use your wisdom and courage.
It would be too expensive to defend them in the field.
They should take advantage of the fact that their crimes have not yet been committed and there is no doubt that the Han Dynasty is going to attack them. They should secretly order the governors and captains of nearby counties to select soldiers and war horses. Da Sinong will allocate grain to key places in advance and select competent governors to go there. In the cool autumn, they will enter the area and kill the most unruly princes.
If you think that sage kings will not tire China with barren land and useless people, you should abolish the establishment of Naguo County, abandon the people of Naguo, sever relations with the princes of Naguo, and no longer have contact with them.
If the achievements made by the late emperor cannot be destroyed, we should eradicate the disaster when it is budding. Wait until the disaster has already occurred, and then go out to attack, hundreds of millions of people will suffer.

translation:
At this time, General Wang Feng recommended Chen Li, Sima of Jincheng, as the prefect of Yangke County.
Chen Li was a native of Linqiong. He had previously served as the magistrate of Lianran County and the magistrate of Buwei County. The barbarians were afraid of him.
When Chen Li arrived at Qunke, he informed Yelang Wang Xing of the court's intentions, but Xing did not obey the order. Chen Li requested to attack him.
Before receiving approval, Chen Li accompanied dozens of officials to the lower counties. When they arrived at Qie Tong Pavilion of Yelang Kingdom, they summoned Yelang Wang Xing. Yelang Wang Xing led thousands of people there. When they arrived at Qie Tong Pavilion, Yelang Wang Xing and dozens of Yijuns went in to see Chen Li.
Chen Li condemned and scolded them, and took the opportunity to kill King Yelang.
The princes who followed Yelang King said: The general killed the rude people who did not abide by the law and eliminated harm for the people. They hope to show Yelang King Xing's head to the public.
The head of King Yelang Xing was displayed to the public, and all the people of King Yelang laid down their weapons and surrendered.
King Yu of Gouding and Hou Yu of Luwo were frightened, so they paid a thousand bushels of dendrobium and some cattle and sheep to reward the officers and soldiers of the Han Dynasty.
When Chen Li returned to Pangke County, Yelang Wang Xing's father-in-law Weng Zhi and his son Zie Wu gathered up the remaining soldiers and forced twenty-two nearby cities to rebel.
In winter, Chen Li asked to recruit all the barbarians, and he would lead an army to attack Wengzhi and others separately from the captain and Chang Shi.
Weng Zhi relied on the steep terrain as a fortress. Chen Li used extraordinary troops to cut off Weng Zhi's route of transporting food and wages, and sent out questioners to seduce Weng Zhi's tribe.
Captain Wannian said: The army has not fought decisively for a long time, and the cost and supply cannot keep up.
So he led his army to attack alone. The attack failed and he fled to Chen Li's military camp.
Chen Li was angry and reprimanded Wan Nian under the banner of the general and ordered him to resist the enemy.
Captain Wannian returned to fight again, and Chen Li led his army to rescue him.
At this time, there was a severe drought, and Chen Li attacked to cut off the water channel.
So the barbarians beheaded Weng Zhi together and came out with Weng Zhi's head to surrender.
Chen Li had already pacified Xiyi, and the emperor summoned them to the capital.
When he caught up with thieves in Bajun, he appointed Chen Li as the prefect of Bajun, with Zhong Two Thousand Stones in his official position. The court rewarded him with the title of Zuo Shu Zhang.
Later, he was appointed as the prefect of Tianshui County. He encouraged the people to devote themselves to farming and mulberry trees, and he was the most outstanding in the world. The court rewarded him with forty pounds of gold. He entered the court and served as General Zuo Cao Wei and Captain of the Guards. He died in office.
Wang Mang usurped the throne, changed the system of the Han Dynasty, and demoted King Gouding to the title of Marquis of Gouding.
Wang Han of Gouching was resentful, and Zhou Qin, the great Yin of Yangke County, killed Han by deceitful means.

translation:
Zhao Tuo, King of Southern Guangdong, was a native of Zhending County.
After Qin unified the world, he pacified Yangyue, established Guilin County, Nanhai County and Xiang County, and moved the people who were punished to Nahuo to live together with the Cantonese people.
Thirteen years later, during the reign of Qin II, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai County, fell ill and was about to die. He summoned the magistrate of Long County, Tuo Tuo, and said to him: I heard that Chen Sheng and others started an army to rebel, and the heroes rebelled against Qin and established themselves as kings. Nanhai County is in a remote place, and I am afraid that the bandit army will capture it.
I wanted to send troops to cut off the new road, defend myself, and observe the movements of the princes, but unfortunately I fell seriously ill.
The Panyu area is backed by mountains, the terrain is difficult, and it is thousands of miles in radius. With the help of many Central Plains people, it can also become the lord of a state and establish a country.
There is no one among the officials in the county who is worthy of my seeking advice, so I have invited you here to tell you what I think.
The relevant documents were immediately issued to Tuo Tuo, and he was asked to act as Nanhai County Lieutenant.
After Ren Xiao's death, Tu Tuo immediately issued a message, notifying Hengpu, Yangshan, Huangxiguan and others: The bandits' army is about to attack. Please cut off the passage immediately and gather troops to defend yourself!
So he used legal means to gradually kill the officials appointed by the Qin Dynasty, and appointed his cronies to perform their duties.
After the fall of the Qin Dynasty, Tuo Tuo attacked and annexed Guilin County and Xiang County, and established himself as King Wu of Southern Guangdong.
After Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty pacified the world, due to the continuous wars in the Central Plains and the hard work of the people, he spared Zhao Tuo and refused to punish him.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the Han Dynasty sent Lu Mai to establish Zhao Tuo as the king of southern Guangdong. He made a talisman with him and asked him to coordinate the security and control of Guangdong and avoid causing trouble on the southern border. Southern Guangdong borders the Changsha Kingdom of the Han Dynasty.
During the reign of Emperor Gao, officials from relevant departments petitioned to prohibit the Southern Guangdong Kingdom from purchasing ironware in the Guan market.
Tu Tuo said: Emperor Gao made me the king of Nanyue, and the two sides exchanged envoys and goods. Now Gaohou listens to the slanderous ministers, regards the barbarians as aliens, and cuts off the circulation of artifacts. This must be the strategy of King Changsha. He wants to rely on the Han Dynasty to destroy Nanyue, swallow up Nanhai County, and rule together for his own benefit.
Therefore, Zhao Tuo proclaimed himself Emperor Wu of Nanyue and sent troops to attack the border areas of Changsha and defeated several counties.
Empress Gao sent General Long Luhou Zhou Zao to fight back. It was a hot and rainy day. Many soldiers were infected with the plague and the army could not cross the mountains.
More than a year later, Queen Gao died, and the Han Dynasty stopped military operations.
Tu Tuo took the opportunity to threaten Minyue and Xiouluo with force and bribe them with property, thereby enslaving them and making them belong to Nanyue.
In this way, the south of Guangdong reaches more than 10,000 miles from east to west.
Tu Tuo then rode in Zuohuan of Huangwu, proclaimed himself emperor, and competed with the emperor of Han Dynasty.

translation:
In the first year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, when the emperor had just begun to rule the world, he sent envoys to all the princes and foreign princes to inform them of his plans after entering the imperial court from Daiguo and becoming emperor, so that everyone would know about the emperor's holiness.
Therefore, a tomb guard house was set up for the tomb of Zhao Tuo's parents in Zhending, and sacrifices were made on time.
He summoned Zhao Tuo's cousins ​​and won them over with official posts and rewards.
He also issued an edict and ordered Prime Minister Chen Ping to recommend people who could be sent as envoys to Southern Guangdong. Chen Ping said that Lu Jia had been on an envoy to Southern Guangdong during the reign of Emperor Gao.
Emperor Wen summoned Lu Jia, appointed him Taizhong doctor, and appointed an emissary as deputy envoy. Emperor Wen's letter to Zhao Tuo said: The emperor respectfully greets the King of Nanyue with the most sincere heart.
I was not the legitimate son of Emperor Gao, but was sent to govern the country of Dai in the north. Due to the long distance and my own isolation and ignorance, I never exchanged envoys with southern Guangdong.
Emperor Gao passed away and left his ministers. Emperor Xiaohui came to the throne. Empress Gao personally took charge of the government. Unfortunately, she fell ill and her illness became increasingly serious. Therefore, the politics were harsh and unconventional.
The Lu family rebelled and deliberately violated laws and regulations. They could not rule alone, so they regarded other people's children as the heirs of Emperor Xiaohui and implemented puppet politics.
Relying on the blessing of the gods of the ancestral temple and the efforts of the heroes, the Lu family has now been exterminated.
I have repeatedly abdicated the throne, but the ministers did not allow it, so I had to establish myself as emperor, and now I have ascended the throne.
I once heard that you wrote to General Longluhou Zhouzao, requesting that your brothers in Zhending be found and that the two generals in Changsha be withdrawn.
In accordance with the request in your letter, I have withdrawn General Boyang Hou Chen Bi, your brother in Zhending, and I have also sent people to comfort and repair the tombs of your ancestors.
I heard before that you sent troops to attack the border and continued to cause trouble.
At that time, Changsha State suffered a disaster, and Nanjun suffered even more. Even your Nanyue State could only benefit?
We must sacrifice a large number of soldiers, harm excellent generals and officials, and cause the common people's wives to lose their husbands, their sons to lose their fathers, and their parents to lose their sons. This is what I cannot bear to do.
I wanted to add the intersecting border between Han and Southern Guangdong to Southern Guangdong, so I asked the relevant officials. The officials said that the boundary line was created by Emperor Gao to demarcate the land of Changsha, so I could not change it without authorization.
The officials said: The land obtained by the King of Nanyue is not enough to make the Han Dynasty large, and the wealth obtained by the King of Nanyue is not enough to make the Han Dynasty rich. The south of the country is ruled by the King of Nanyue.
Despite this, you are called the emperor, and the two emperors stand side by side, but you did not send an envoy's car. This is a competition for position; fighting without humility is what virtuous people do not do.
I hope that we can put aside our past grievances and that from now on and forever, the two sides will communicate with each other as before.
Therefore, I sent Lu Mai to quickly express my thoughts to you. I hope you will accept my opinion and stop creating border troubles.

translation:
Lu Jia came back to report, and Emperor Wen was very happy.
Until the time of Emperor Xiaojing, Tuo Tuo proclaimed himself a minister and sent envoys to pay homage to the emperor on time.
However, the King of Nanyue continued to use the title of emperor in his own country; he only proclaimed himself king when envoys paid homage to the emperor, and accepted the emperor's orders like other princes and kings.
In the fourth year of the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Zhao Hu, the grandson of Tu Tuo, became the king of Southern Guangdong.
In the third year, Ying, the king of Fujian and Guangdong, raised his troops to attack the cities on the border of southern Guangdong.
The King of Nanyue sent a letter to the Han Dynasty saying: Nanyue and Minyue are both vassals of the emperor, and they cannot send troops to attack each other without permission.
Now Shu Yue is raising troops to attack Nan Yue without authorization. I dare not send troops, so I ask the emperor to issue an edict.
So Emperor Wu praised Nan Yue for his loyalty, abiding by his duties and not breaking the rules, so he sent troops for it and sent two generals to attack Fujian and Guangdong.
Before the Han army could cross the mountains, Yu Shan, the younger brother of the King of Fujian and Guangdong, killed Ying and surrendered to the Han Dynasty, so the two generals stopped their troops.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty sent Yan Zhu to explain the imperial intention to the King of Nanyue. The King of Nanyue, Zhao Hu, kowtowed and said: How could the emperor send troops to conquer Fujian and Guangdong for me? Even if I die, I will not be able to repay the emperor's kindness!
Send the prince to the imperial guard together with the infant.
Zaihu said to Yanzhu: The country of Southern Guangdong has been attacked by invaders. Your envoy, please go ahead. I am getting ready day and night to go to court to see the emperor.
After Yan Zhu left, the ministers of Southern Guangdong advised Zhao Hu and said: The Han Dynasty sent troops to attack Fujian and Guangdong, and also used this to intimidate Southern Guangdong.
Moreover, the late king once said that when serving the emperor, one only needs to be courteous. The most important thing is not to be deceived by the good words of the Han Dynasty envoys and enter the court to pay homage to the emperor.
Once you enter the court to pay homage to the emperor, you will not be able to come back again. This is a situation of national subjugation.
So Zhao Hu pretended to be ill and did not go to the court to pay homage to the emperor.
More than ten years later, Tread Hu did become seriously ill, and Prince Tread Yingqi asked to return to the country.
After Zai Hu died, he was given the title King Wen.
When Zhao Yingqi succeeded to the throne of Nanyue, he collected the seals of his ancestors who had pretended to be Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen.
When Te Yingqi was in Chang'an, he married a woman named Do from Handan and gave birth to his son Te Xing.

translation:
The Western Regions began to communicate with the Central Plains from the time of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. There were originally thirty-six countries in that area. Later, it was gradually divided into more than fifty kingdoms, all of which were located to the west of the Xiongnu and south of the Wusun.
The Western Region has large mountains in the north and south, and a river in the center. It is more than 6,000 miles wide from east to west and more than 1,000 miles long from north to south.
It is connected to the Han Dynasty in the east, with Yumen Pass and Yang Pass as dangerous fortresses, and Congling as the boundary in the west.
Its Nanshan Mountain starts from Jincheng County and is connected to the Nanshan Mountain of the Han Dynasty.
Its river has two sources: one originates from Congling Mountain and the other originates from Khotan.
Khotan is at the foot of Nanshan Mountain. The river flows north, merges with the Congling River, and then flows eastward into the Puchang Sea.
Puchanghai, also known as Yanze, is more than 300 miles away from Yumenguan and Yangguan. The length and width of the lake are about 300 miles.
The lake water is stable and does not increase or decrease in winter and summer. The lake water flows underground and emerges from Jishi Mountain to the south, which is the Huanghui in the Central Plains.
There are two roads from Yumenguan and Yangguan to the Western Regions. From Shanshan, follow the north side of Nanshan and go west along the Tarim River to Yarkand, which is the south road; the south road goes west across Congling to reach Dayuezhi and Anxi.
From Cheshiqian Wangting, follow the south side of Beishan and go west along the Tarim River to Shule, which is the north road: the north road goes west across Congling to reach Dawan, Kangju, and Yancai.
Most of the countries in the Western Regions lived a settled life, with cities, fields, and livestock. They were different from the customs of the Xiongnu and Wusun. They were all enslaved and subordinate to the Xiongnu in the past.
King Yue Zhu in the western Xiongnu set up a boy servant captain to manage the western regions. He was often stationed in Yanqi, Weixu, Weili and other places, collecting taxes from various countries, and he was very wealthy.
Since the decline of the Zhou Dynasty, the Rong, Di and other ethnic groups have lived together in the north of the Jingshui and Weishui rivers.
When Qin Shihuang arrived, he drove away the Rong and Di and built the Great Wall as the border of the Central Plains countries, but the west of Qin did not exceed Lintao County.
From the establishment of the Western Han Dynasty to the time of Emperor Wu, he managed the surrounding ethnic areas and promoted mighty virtue, so Zhang Qian began to open the road to the Western Regions.
Later, Husband General Huo Qubing defeated the Xiongnu in the right area, and King Hunxie and Xiutu surrendered. There were no Xiongnu in the right area. The Han Dynasty began to build beacons to the west of Lingju and began to establish Jiuquan County. Later, the people were recruited to live here, and Wuwei, Zhangye, and Dunhuang were established in four counties, and they guarded Yumen and Yangguan Pass.
Since Li Guangli, the general of the Second Division, attacked Dayuan, all countries in the Western Regions were frightened. Most countries sent envoys to Chang'an to pay tribute. The Han Dynasty's envoys to the Western Regions were increasingly rewarded and promoted.
So from the west of Dunhuang to Yanze, pavilions and barriers were built everywhere. Hundreds of field soldiers were stationed in Luntai and Quli. Envoys and captains were set up to supervise the field affairs and provide livelihood for the Han Dynasty's envoys to foreign countries.
During the reign of Emperor Xuan, Wei Sima was assigned to oversee several countries west of Shanshan.
When it came time to defeat Gu Shi, he did not eliminate them all, but divided them into the former king of Cheshi, the queen of Cheshi, and the six kingdoms of Shanbei.
At that time, the Han Dynasty only supervised the southern route and did not annex all the northern routes, but the Huns were already feeling very uneasy.
Later, King Rizhu betrayed Chanyu and led his troops to surrender to the Han Dynasty. Zheng Ji, the envoy of the Han Dynasty who protected Shanshan from the west, met King Rizhu.
In the Han Dynasty, the Han Dynasty named Zhu Wang as the Marquis of Guide and Zheng Ji as the Marquis of Anyuan.
This year is the third year of Shenjue.
The Han Dynasty sent Zheng Ji to protect the North Road, so it was called "Duhu".
The establishment of the Protectorate began with Zheng Ji.
The Xiongnu's child servant captain originally stationed in the Western Regions has since been dismissed. The Xiongnu has become even weaker and cannot approach the Western Regions.
So the Han Dynasty moved the people to farm in Beixu Tar, dividing the land of Shache. From then on, the military commander of the farm began to belong to the military guard.
The Protectorate monitors the situation in Wusun, Kangju and other foreign countries, and reports to the emperor immediately if there is any movement.

The Han Dynasty built pavilions and barriers from Dunhuang to Yanze, stationed field soldiers in Luntai and Quli, and set up envoys and captains to supervise farming. Wang Hui and his 700 Qing cavalrymen went to Loulan first and captured the King of Loulan. Then he defeated Gu Shi and showed off his military power to shake up Wusun, Dawan and others.
They returned to Chang'an, and Emperor Wu made Zhao Ponu the Marquis of Zhuoye and Wang Hui the Marquis of Hao.
So the Han Dynasty built pavilions and barriers westward to Yumen Pass.
Loulan had surrendered to the Han Dynasty and paid tribute. When the Xiongnu learned about it, they sent troops to attack.
So King Loulan sent one of his sons to the Huns as a hostage, and another son to the Han Dynasty as a hostage.
Later, General Ershi attacked Dawan, and the Xiongnu wanted to intercept the Han army. However, the Han army was so powerful that the Xiongnu did not dare to resist, so they sent knights to borrow Loulan's help to wait for the Han envoys who were walking behind, and stopped them from passing.
At that time, Ren Wen of the Han army led his troops to garrison at Yumen Pass and served as the rear guard of the general of the Second Division. He captured prisoners and reported the situation to Emperor Wu.
Emperor Wu ordered Ren Wen to lead troops from Xiaolu to arrest King Loulan.
King Loulan was taken to the Han Palace and questioned one by one according to the book. King Loulan said: A small country is sandwiched between big countries. If it does not adopt the approach of two subordinates, it will not be able to secure itself.
I hope that my country will be moved to the territory of the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Wu thought his words were straightforward, so he sent him back to his country and also asked Loulan to spy on the Xiongnu's movements.
From then on, the Huns did not trust Loulan very much.
In the first year of Zhenghe, King Loulan died. The people of Loulan came to invite the hostage in the Han Dynasty to return to their country and make him king.
The hostage often violated Han law and was sent to the silkworm room and executed by castration, so he could not be sent back.
He replied to Loulan: "The servant is very popular with the emperor, so I cannot send him back to his country."
You can establish a person who should be established.
Loulan established a new king, and the Han Dynasty asked King Loulan to send a proton, and King Loulan also sent a proton to the Xiongnu.
Later, King Loulan died again. The Huns knew this and sent a proton back to make him king.
The Han sent an envoy to order the new King of Loulan to go to Chang'an to see Emperor Wu, saying that Emperor Wu would give him a generous reward.
King Loulan's stepmother, who was his original stepmother, told him: The late king sent two protons to the Han Dynasty, but they did not come back. Why do you still go to see the emperor?
King Loulan used her trick and declined to the envoy Mo, saying: I have just been established as king, the country is not stable, and I hope to wait until the year after tomorrow to become emperor.
However, the Loulan Kingdom was at the border of the Western Region, close to the Han Dynasty, right at the White Dragon Pile, with little water and grass. It often sent guides for desert envoys, carried water and food, and sent Han envoys to greet them. It was robbed many times by the officials of the Han Dynasty. Their lesson was that there was no benefit in communicating with the Han Dynasty.
Later, the Huns counterattacked and intercepted and killed Han envoys several times.
Later, Wei Tuqi, the younger brother of King Loulan, surrendered to the Han Dynasty and told the relevant situation.
In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, after reporting to Emperor Zhao, the general Huo Guang sent Pingyue supervisor Fu Jiezi to assassinate King Loulan.
Fu Jiezi led the warriors lightly equipped with gold coins and silk, threatening to give them to foreign countries.
When he arrived at Loulan, he lied to the King of Loulan and said that he would give it to him. The king was very happy and drank with Fu Jiezi. When he was drunk, Fu Jiezi talked with the king alone. Two strong men assassinated the king from behind, and the nobles and relatives of Loulan all ran away.
Fu Jiezi declared: King Loulan has failed the Han Dynasty, and the emperor has sent me to kill him. He should make Wei Tuqi, the king's younger brother in the Han Dynasty, king.
The Han soldiers are about to arrive, don't move, otherwise, you will be destroyed!
Fu Jiezi cut off the head of King Loulan Changgui and sent it to the Chang'an court in a post carriage, where he hung his head under the North Tower.
The Han Dynasty granted Fu Jiezi the title of Marquis of Yiyang.
He established Wei Tu Qi as the King of Loulan and changed the name of the country to Shanshan. The court carved a seal for him and gave him a palace maid as his wife. He was equipped with chariots and riding supplies. The prime minister led hundreds of officials to send him outside Hengmen. After worshiping the road god, he was sent back to his country.
King Shanshan personally petitioned Emperor Wu: I have been in the Han Dynasty for a long time. When I go back today, I am weak. The former king has a son who is still alive, and I am afraid he will kill him.
There is a city called Yixun in the country with fertile land. I hope that the Han Dynasty will send a general to farm and accumulate grain there so that I can have something to rely on.
So the Han Dynasty sent one Sima and forty officials to garrison Yixun to intimidate and pacify them.
Later, he was changed to captain.

summary: During Emperor Yuan's reign, Wuji Xiaowei was appointed to man fields. Wang Zilizhi of Baotui Dongpu surrendered with over 1,700 people, and the Protectorate allocated land for them. Since the Xuancha and Wutong period, Li Sculpture Chanyu Xianghui became a vassal, and details of land, mountains, rivers, and distances were recorded. Starting from the nearest west of Yangguan, the Laoqiang Kingdom had 450 households, 1,750 people, and 500 troops, living with livestock and not farming. The Shanshan Kingdom (formerly Loulan) had 1,570 households, 14,100 people, and 2,912 troops, with officials including Fu Guohou and translators. It produced jade, reeds, and willow, and its people lived with livestock. Initially, Emperor Wu was moved by Zhang Qian's words and sent many envoys to Dawan. Loulan and Gushi, on the main road, attacked Han envoys and acted as Xiongnu spies. Emperor Wu sent Zhao Ponu and Wang Hui to attack Gushi and capture the King of Loulan, leading to the construction of pavilions west to Yumen Pass. Loulan surrendered but later sent hostages to both the Han and Xiongnu. After King Loulan died, the Han Dynasty could not send back a castrated hostage, leading to a new king who declined to visit the Han emperor. Later, Wei Tuqi, the king's brother, surrendered to the Han Dynasty. In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, Fu Jiezi assassinated King Loulan, established Wei Tuqi as king, and renamed the country Shanshan. The Han Dynasty sent a Sima and forty officials to garrison Yixun, marking the beginning of official establishment there. Shanshan was a strategic point on the road to the Western Regions, with various countries like Qiemo, Xiaowan, Jingjue, Ronglu, Shanmi, Qule, Khotan, Pishan, Wushuo, Xiye, Puli, Yinai, Wulei, Nandou, and Jibin, each with specific populations, troops, and distances from Chang'an. Jibin, a large country not under the Western Region Protector, had a mild climate, produced various crops and metals, and had a market with gold and silver coins. The Han Dynasty's communication with Jibin began under Emperor Wu, but later conflicts arose, including the killing of Han envoys. Du Qin advised against further engagement due to the dangers and costs, and the Han Dynasty eventually limited contact. Wuyi Mountain, another large country, had similar customs to Jibin, with a hot climate and lush vegetation. Anxi Kingdom, a very large country with hundreds of cities, used silver coins and had a written language. Emperor Wu sent envoys to Parthia, who were greeted by a general with 20,000 cavalry. Dayuezhi, originally a nomadic country, was defeated by the Xiongnu and moved west to Daxia, establishing their capital. Daxia was divided into five tribes, each with its own marquis, all belonging to Dayuezhi. Kangju, with 120,000 households and 600,000 people, had customs similar to Dayuezhi and was restrained by the Xiongnu. During Emperor Xuan's reign, the Han Dynasty killed Zhizhi Chanyu. Under Emperor Cheng, King Kangju was arrogant, and the Protectorate recommended cutting ties, but the court maintained relations. Yancai, northwest of Kangju, had over 100,000 warriors and customs similar to Kangju. Dayuan, with 60,000 households and 300,000 people, produced good horses and used grapes for wine. Emperor Wu sent Li Guangli to attack Dayuan, resulting in the dedication of two Pegasus horses annually. From Dawan to Parthia, residents had different languages but similar customs, with deep-set eyes and long beards. They were skilled in business and obtained gold and silver from the Han Dynasty. After Huhanxie Chanyu submitted to the Han Dynasty, these countries respected the Han. Various other kingdoms like Taohua, Xiuxun, Zhendu, Shache, Shule, and Weitou had specific populations, troops, and distances, with some farming and raising livestock.

The emperor urgently wanted to become a country of brothers and used this method to restrain the Xiongnu.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Zhang Qian". Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne and ordered Zhang Qian to bring gold coins and treasures to Wusun.
Kun Mo met Zhang Qian with the attitude of the Xiongnu Chanyu. Zhang Qian was very ashamed and angry, and said to Kun Mo: If you don't thank the emperor for giving you a gift, then return the gift to us.
Kunmo stood up and thanked him, but in other respects he remained the same.
At the beginning, Kunmo had more than a dozen sons. The middle son Dalu was very strong and good at leading troops. He led more than 10,000 cavalry and lived elsewhere.
Dalu's brother was the prince, and the prince had a son named Cen Zuo.
The prince died early. Before his death, he said to Kunmo: "Cen Zou must be the prince."
Kunmo was sad and agreed.
Dalu was very angry about this incident, so he captured all the other brothers, led his soldiers to rebel, and prepared to attack Cen Zuo.
Kunmo gave Cen Zuo more than 10,000 cavalry and ordered him to station elsewhere. He also had more than 10,000 cavalry for self-defense.
At this time, the country was divided into three parts, all under the control of Kunmo.
After Zhang Qian handed over the gifts given to Kunmo by the Han Dynasty, he said to Kunmo: If Wusun can return to his hometown, the Han Dynasty will send the princess as Kunmo's wife. The two countries will become brotherly countries and resist the Xiongnu together. The Xiongnu will definitely be defeated.
summary: The Wusun Kingdom, governed by Da Kunmi from Chigu City, was located 8,900 miles from Chang'an. It had 120,000 households, a population of 630,000, and an army of 188,800. The kingdom had a structured government with officials including a prime minister, generals, marquises, and eunuchs. The land was grassy, rainy, and cold, with residents practicing nomadic herding like the Xiongnu. The country was rich in horses, with wealthy individuals owning up to 4,000-5,000. The people were strong-willed but greedy and unfaithful. Wusun originally submitted to the Xiongnu but later became powerful and resisted them. It bordered the Xiongnu, Kangju, Dawan, and various Chengguo Kingdoms. The region was originally inhabited by the Sai people, then conquered by the Dayuezhi, and later by Wusun Kunmo, who incorporated both Sai and Dayuezhi populations.

translation:
But Wusun was far away from the Han Dynasty, and the size of the Han Dynasty was unknown. Wusun himself was close to the Xiongnu and had obeyed the Xiongnu for a long time. None of the ministers were willing to move eastward.
Kunmo is old, the country is divided, and power cannot be concentrated. So an envoy was sent to take Zhang Qian back to Chang'an, and at the same time, he offered dozens of horses as a thank you.
The envoy saw that the Han Dynasty had a large population and rich products. After returning home, Wusun respected the Han Dynasty more and more.
When the Xiongnu heard that Wusun had contact with the Han, they were very angry and wanted to attack Wusun.
In addition, the envoys of the Han Dynasty passed south of Wusun to Dayuan and Yuezhi, and they were not stopped on the road.
Wusun was very frightened, so he sent an envoy to offer horses to the Han Dynasty and offered to marry Princess Mo, and the two countries became brothers.
The emperor asked the ministers for their opinions, and the court agreed. Decision: The bride price must be paid first, and then the princess must be sent away.
Wusun gave a thousand horses as a betrothal gift.
During the Yuanfeng period of the Han Dynasty, Xijun, the daughter of King Liu Jian of Jiangdu, was sent to marry Kunmo as a princess. The emperor gave her carriages, horses and royal utensils. He also equipped her with hundreds of officials, eunuchs, maids and servants, and gave her rich gifts.
Wusun Kunmo took Mr. Bin as his right wife.
The Xiongnu also sent women to marry Kunmo, and Kunmo took the Xiongnu girl as his left wife.
After the princess arrived in Wusun, she built a palace to live in. She had gatherings with Kunmo several times a year, drank and ate, and rewarded the nobles around Kunmo with property, silk fabrics, etc.
Kunmo was old and couldn't understand the language. The princess was very sad and composed a song by herself: My family married me to the far side of the sky, and asked King Yan of Wu to come to a foreign country far away.
The dome is the room, the walls are the walls, the meat is the food, and the cheese is the pulp.
Living in this land, I miss you and my heart hurts. I wish you could return to your hometown as a yellow swan.
When the emperor heard about it, he felt pity for her and sent envoys every other year to deliver curtains, brocade and other items.
Kunmo is old and wants his grandson Cen Zuo to marry the princess.
The princess disagreed and wrote to the emperor explaining the matter. The emperor replied: Following the custom of Wusun country, Mo wants to join forces with Wusun to destroy the Xiongnu.
Cen Zuo married the princess.
Kun Mo died, and Cen Zou became king in his stead.
Cen Zuo is an official title, and his name is Jun Xumi.
Kunmo is the king's name, and his name is Liejiaomi.
Later, the king was named Kunmi.
Cen Zuo married the princess of Jiangdu and gave birth to a daughter named Shaofu.
After the princess died, the Han Dynasty sent Jieyou, the granddaughter of King Liu Wu of Chu, to marry Cen Zou for the princess.
Cen Zou's son Nimi by his Hun wife was still young. When Cen Zou was about to die, he passed the throne to his uncle Dalu's son Weng Guimi. He said: When Nimi grows up, he will return the throne to Nimi.
summary: Zhang Qian, sent by Emperor Wu of Han, attempted to persuade Wusun to return to their homeland and ally with Han against the Xiongnu. Kunmo initially treated Zhang Qian with Xiongnu-like arrogance but eventually showed respect. Wusun was divided among Kunmo's sons, with internal conflicts over succession. Despite Zhang Qian's efforts, Wusun was reluctant to move east due to distance and longstanding ties with the Xiongnu. However, after envoys saw Han's wealth, Wusun grew more respectful. The Xiongnu, angered by Wusun's contact with Han, threatened attack, leading Wusun to propose marriage to a Han princess. The Han agreed, and during the Yuanfeng period, Princess Xijun was sent to marry Kunmo. The Xiongnu also sent a bride, and Kunmo took both as wives. The princess, homesick and unable to communicate with the elderly Kunmo, composed a sorrowful song. Emperor Wu, pitying her, sent gifts regularly.

translation:
Weng Guimi came to the throne and was named King Fei. He married Jieyou and gave birth to three sons and two daughters: the eldest son was named Yuan Guimi; the second son was named Wannian and was the king of Shache; the third son was named Dalue and was the general of Zuo; the eldest daughter was named Shi and was the wife of King Jiangbin of Qiuci; the younger daughter was named Suguang and was the wife of Ruohulinghou.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty, Princess Jieyou wrote to the emperor, saying that the Xiongnu sent cavalry to farm in Cheshi, and that the Cheshi and the Xiongnu united to invade Wusun, hoping that the emperor would rescue them.
The Han Dynasty prepared soldiers and horses to attack the Xiongnu.
When Emperor Zhao died and Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne, Princess Jieyou and Kunmi both sent envoys to write, saying that the Xiongnu invaded and attacked Wusun in succession, captured Cheyan, Eshi and other places, and plundered all the local residents. He also sent an envoy to tell Wusun to send the princess to the Huns as soon as possible, hoping to destroy the relationship between Wusun and Han.
Kunmi is willing to send half of the country's elite troops and prepare 50,000 cavalry to attack the Xiongnu with all his strength.
I hope the emperor will send troops to rescue the princess and Kunmi as soon as possible.
The Han Dynasty sent an army of 150,000 cavalry, led by five generals.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of the Huns".
The Han Dynasty also sent Lieutenant Chang Hui as an envoy to protect the Wusun soldiers. Kunmi personally led a total of 50,000 knights under the Marquis of Ji to attack the Xiongnu from the west. When the Xiongnu arrived at the royal court of Yougu Li, they captured 40,000 people including Shanyu's father, sister-in-law, Juzi, Ming Wang, Ligu Duwei, Qian Chang, and cavalry generals, as well as more than 700,000 horses, cattle, sheep, donkeys, and camels. Wusun took these trophies away.
When the Han army returned home, Emperor Xuan granted Chang Hui the title of Marquis of Changluo.
This year is the third year of the original year.
The Han Dynasty also sent Chang Hui with valuable belongings and silk fabrics to be given to the nobles of Wusun who had made military exploits.
In the second year of Yuankang, Wusun Kunmi wrote to Emperor Xuan through Chang Hui, saying: I would like to make my grandson Yuan Guimi of the Han Dynasty the heir to the throne, and let him also marry a Han princess, form a double marriage, and sever ties with the Huns. I am willing to use a thousand horses and mules as a betrothal gift.
Emperor Xuan ordered ministers to discuss the matter. Xiao Wangzhi, the great emperor, thought: Wusun is located very far away and there is no guarantee that it will not change. Don't agree to their request.
Emperor Xuan admired Wusun's recent great achievements and found it difficult to sever the established marriage relationship, so he sent an envoy to Wusun to receive the betrothal gift first.
Kunmi, the crown prince, the left and right generals, and the captain sent a delegation of more than 300 people to the Han Dynasty to welcome the young princess.
Emperor Xuan took Princess Jieyou's niece and husband as the princess, and appointed more than a hundred officials, maids, etc. to live in Shanglin Garden and learn the Wusun language.
Emperor Xuan personally came to Pingganguang, met with the Huns envoys and foreign princes, performed a jiaoduan drama, music, singing and dancing, and then sent the princess to the west to marry. The envoy Chang Luohou Guanglu, the doctor Chang Hui assisted, and four people were envoys to send the young princess to Dunhuang.
Before leaving the frontier fortress, they heard that Wusun Kunmi Weng Guimi had died. According to the agreement made by Cen Zou during his lifetime, the Wusun nobles appointed Cen Zou's son Nimi as Kunmi, named Kuangwang.
Chang Hui wrote to Emperor Xuan saying: He wanted to keep the young princess in Dunhuang temporarily. Chang Hui rushed to Wusun and blamed Yuan Guimi for not appointing Yuan Guimi as Kunmi, and then took the young princess back to Chang'an.
The matter was discussed by the ministers, and Xiao Wangzhi said: "It is difficult to make a treaty with Wusun, who is headed by a rat."
Princess Jieyou has been in Wusun for more than 40 years. The relationship between the two countries is not close and the border is not peaceful. This is proved by creation.
Today, the young princess returned to Chang'an because Yuan Gui was not able to stand up. She did not feel sorry for Wusun, and it was also a blessing for the Han Dynasty.
If the young princess does not stop going to Wusun, the corvee will flourish, and this is where the roots begin.
Emperor Xuan accepted this opinion and took the young princess back to Chang'an.
summary: After Kunmo's death, his grandson Cen Zuo married the princess per Wusun custom, as Emperor Wu approved to maintain the alliance. Cen Zuo became king, and the princess bore a daughter. Upon her death, Princess Jieyou, granddaughter of a Han king, was sent to marry Cen Zuo. Cen Zuo's son by his Xiongnu wife was young, so the throne passed to his uncle's son, Weng Guimi, who married Jieyou and had three sons and two daughters. During Emperor Zhao's reign, Princess Jieyou sought Han aid against Xiongnu attacks. Emperor Xuan later sent a large force, including 150,000 Han cavalry and 50,000 Wusun troops, defeating the Xiongnu and capturing many people and livestock. Wusun took the spoils. Emperor Xuan rewarded Chang Hui, who had led the Wusun forces. Wusun Kunmi proposed making his Han-descended grandson Yuan Guimi heir, with a double marriage to sever ties with the Xiongnu. Emperor Xuan agreed but faced opposition from officials like Xiao Wangzhi, who doubted Wusun's reliability. Despite this, the emperor proceeded, sending a young princess to Wusun. However, Weng Guimi died before her arrival, and the throne passed to Nimi, Cen Zuo's son. Chang Hui advised keeping the princess in Dunhuang, and after debate, Emperor Xuan recalled her. Princess Jieyou remained in Wusun for over 40 years, and the mad king, who succeeded, was cruel and unpopular. A plot to kill him failed, leading to conflict. The Han intervened, executing those involved. Later, Wujiutu, a son of Weng Guimi, killed the mad king and declared himself Kunmi. The Han sent forces but ultimately negotiated, dividing Wusun into two Kunmi with separate households. Princess Jieyou, now elderly, was allowed to return to Chang'an, where she died two years later.

translation:
At this time, Wang Mang changed the Seal of the Xiongnu Chanyu to the New Xiongnu Chanyu Zhang. The Chanyu was very resentful about this matter. When Hulanzhi came to surrender, he accepted it and sent troops to attack Che Division together with Hulanzhi. They killed the commander of the rear city of Che Division and wounded Sima, the capital guard. Hulanzhi troops returned to the Xiongnu. At this time, Wuji Xiaowei Daohu fell ill, so he sent Shi Chenliang to lead his troops to garrison in Huanqie Valley to prevent the Huns from invading. Shi Zhong was responsible for transporting grain, Sima Cheng Han Xuan was in charge of each wall, and You Qu was appointed Shang Guan to lead each base. Chen Liang and others discussed and said: Now many countries in the Western Region have rebelled against the Han, and the Huns are about to invade on a large scale. We are probably going to die.
We might as well kill the captain and lead the troops to surrender to the Huns.
So he led thousands of cavalry to the captain's mansion, threatened the pavilions and lit beacon fires, and informed the fortresses separately: "The Huns are coming to attack with one hundred thousand cavalry." Officials and soldiers must take up arms to face the enemy, and those who lag behind must be beheaded!
Three to four hundred people gathered together and stopped advancing a few miles away from the captain's mansion.
At dawn, light the beacon fire. The school captain opened the city gate and beat drums to gather the officials and soldiers. Chen Liang and others took the opportunity to enter and killed the school captain Dao Hu and his four sons, as well as their brothers, nephews, and only the women and children were left alive.
Chen Liang and others stayed in Wuji Xiaowei City and sent people to report the situation to the Xiongnu General Nan. General Nan sent 2,000 knights to greet Chen Liang and others. Chen Liang and others threatened Wuji Xiaowei, officers, men and women, a total of more than 2,000 men and women, to defect to the Huns.
The Xiongnu Chanyu was appointed Chen Liang, and eventually he was made the captain of Wuben.
Three years later, the Chanyu died. His younger brother Wu abandoned the Chanyu and established him as the Chanyu in Xian. He also made peace with Wang Mang.
Wang Mang sent an envoy to bring a lot of gold, treasure, silk and satin to Shan Yu, demanding that Chen Liang, Zhong Dai and others be handed over.
Chanyu arrested a total of twenty-seven people, including Chen Liang, Zhong Dai, Han Xuan, and Ren Shang, as well as Zhiyin, who killed Dao Hu himself, and their wives. They were all put into prison carts and handed over to the Han envoys.
After arriving in Chang'an, Wang Mang burned and killed all these people.
Later, Wang Mang deceived Shanyu again, and the harmonious relationship between the Xiongnu and Han was severed.
The Huns invaded Han's northern border and Han's rule in the Western Regions collapsed.
The Yanqi Kingdom was close to the Xiongnu, and they rebelled against the desert first and killed Danqin, the governor. Wang Mang was unable to send troops to conquer.
It was only in the third year of Tianfeng's reign that he sent General Wang Jun of the Five Powers, Li Chong, the Protector of the Western Regions, and Guo Qin, the captain of the Wuji School, to the Western Regions. All countries in the Western Regions welcomed him in the suburbs and supplied him with food. King Yanqi also pretended to surrender to the Han Dynasty, but secretly prepared his own troops.
Wang Jun and others led more than 7,000 soldiers from Yarkand and Qiuci into several groups and entered Yanqi. Yanqi set up an ambush to intercept Wang Jun and others. National soldiers such as Zhumo, Xianken and Yuti secretly communicated with Nie Yi and jointly attacked Wang Zhui and others, killing all Wang Zhui's officers and soldiers.
Only Wuji captain Guo Qin led another army to Yanqi later.
Yanqi's soldiers had not returned from the battle, so Guo Qin killed all the old and weak in their city and retreated back to the chief's room.
Wang Ling conferred the title of Ginsengzi.
Kuise gathered up the remaining soldiers and retreated to Kucha.
A few years later, Wang Mang died, and Li Chong fled to the Western Regions, which cut off contact with the Central Plains dynasty.
