summary: The text also details various other kingdoms in the Western Regions, including Gumo, Wensu, Qiuci, and others, with their distances from Chang'an, populations, armies, and administrative structures. It describes the Han Dynasty's efforts to establish agricultural colonies, such as in Luntai, and the challenges of maintaining control over distant territories. Emperor Wu's later years saw a shift away from expansion, with a focus on domestic recovery and reduced military campaigns. The narrative covers conflicts with the Xiongnu, internal rebellions, and the eventual decline of Han influence in the region, culminating in the collapse of the Western Regions Protectorate during Wang Mang's reign. The summary concludes with a reflection on the costs and benefits of Han's Western Regions policy, noting that while the region offered exotic goods, it also drained resources and led to instability.

translation:
Gu Yong, named Ziyun, was from Chang'an.
His father, Gu Ji, served as Sima of the Wei Dynasty. As an envoy, he sent Shanyu Zhizhi's servant back to his country, but was killed by Zhizhi. This incident was recorded in the "Chen Tang Biography".
Gu Yong wrote a short history of Chang'an when he was young, and later studied the classics extensively.
During the reign of Emperor Jianzhao, Fan Yanshou, the imperial censor, heard that he had outstanding talents and appointed him as his subordinate. Later, he recommended him as Taichang Cheng. He wrote many memorials to discuss political gains and losses.
In the winter of the third year of Jianshi's reign, a solar eclipse and an earthquake occurred on the same day. The emperor ordered the selection of scholars who were upright, dared to speak out, and could try their best to persuade. Tai Chang Yangcheng Marquis Liu Qingji recommended Gu Yong to wait for the imperial edict.
Gu Yong replied:
Your Majesty has the purest moral character of the most sage. He is worried about the strange phenomena warned by heaven and earth. He organizes his own state affairs, inquires and adopts the suggestions of the ministers, and issues wise orders, asking the officials to recommend people who dare to speak out. He takes the time to summon them to explore the origins of the changes, to find the reasons for the heaven's punishment, so that we scholars can come to the court of the sage to accept the inquiry of the sage.
I am not very talented and have little knowledge, and I am not familiar with political affairs.
I have heard privately that when a sage emperor ascends the throne, he should correct his appearance, speech, sight, hearing, and thinking, establish the rules of imperial rule, and obey the will of the Emperor of Heaven. Only in this way can many auspicious signs appear in sequence below, and only when the sun and moon move in the sky can there be Laws; if the king is too indulged in the harem, content with pleasure and hunting, and loses the correction of the five things, and the rules of rule cannot be established, then the signs of disaster will come and the six abnormal phenomena of punishment will appear.
All disasters and visions appear, each symbolizing a fault and warning the world according to its type.
So on the first day of the twelfth lunar month, when the solar eclipse was in Wu Nu, and the earthquake was in Xiao Qiang, both happened on the same day. I repeatedly told Your Majesty that those mistakes are not too far away, and you should deeply look for the reasons in yourself.
Is it God's will that His Majesty pays attention to women's sex, does not worry about political affairs, does not behave prudently, and repeatedly loses his integrity?
Is it because she dotes on concubines too much, because women do not abide by women's ethics, because they want to possess the Holy One alone due to jealousy, and hinder the prosperity of their descendants?
The ancient kings abolished the five principles of justice and lost the moral relationship between husband and wife. If their wives and concubines were favored, they could fulfill their requests internally and abuse their power externally, to the point of overthrowing the country and confusing and disrupting the order of yin and yang.
In the past, Guo Si was in power, and Zong Zhou lost his country because of it; Yan's wife was arrogant and pampered, so she became prosperous, so there was a solar eclipse.
This is a sign of a vision.
The scriptures say: The principle of imperial rule is to greatly establish the rule of justice.
summary: Gu Yong, styled Ziyun, was from Chang'an. His father, Gu Ji, served as a Sima of the Wei Dynasty and was killed by Shanyu Zhizhi while on a diplomatic mission. Gu Yong wrote a short history of Chang'an in his youth and later extensively studied the classics. During Emperor Jianzhao's reign, Fan Yanshou, the imperial censor, recognized his talents and appointed him as a subordinate, later recommending him as Taichang Cheng. Gu Yong wrote many memorials discussing political gains and losses. In the winter of the third year of Jianshi's reign, a solar eclipse and earthquake occurred on the same day. The emperor ordered the selection of upright scholars who dared to speak out. Tai Chang Yangcheng Marquis Liu Qingji recommended Gu Yong to await the imperial edict. Gu Yong replied that the emperor, with his pure moral character, was worried about the strange phenomena and sought advice. He stated that when a sage emperor ascends the throne, he must correct his appearance, speech, sight, hearing, and thinking, and establish imperial rules to obey the will of the Emperor of Heaven. If the king indulges in the harem, pleasure, and hunting, disasters will appear. The solar eclipse and earthquake were signs of faults, and the emperor should look for reasons within himself, possibly due to excessive attention to women, lack of political concern, or improper behavior. When a black dragon appeared, Gu Yong explained it as a sign of the same surname, possibly indicating a threat from a relative or a cruel successor. He warned about the dangers of women and evil people in power, citing historical examples. He criticized the emperor for indulging in private pleasures, neglecting duties, and causing disasters. He urged the emperor to reform, reduce taxes, stop excessive construction, and care for the people. The emperor was moved but did not fully trust Gu Yong.

translation:
The Sutra says: If the rules of governance are not upright, this is called non-establishment. At this time, the movement of the sun and the moon will be chaotic.
Your Majesty ascended the most noble throne and became the monarch of the world. He accepted the responsibilities of an emperor to rule all living beings. Peace and instability in the four directions are all under your control.
If you really can pay attention to self-correction, strive to do things to the best of your ability, reduce the time for private banquets to worry about the affairs of the world, give up and stay away from over-indulged pleasures, stop advocating for the entertainment of outstanding artists, put an end to behaviors that are not enjoyed by ghosts and gods, carefully control the fun of hunting and hunting, have certain rules in your daily life, follow the etiquette and law, manage political affairs personally, devote yourself to practical actions without being tired, and do everything with peace of mind as natural as nature.
The scriptures say: From now on, kings who inherit the ancestral inheritance should not indulge too much in banquets or indulge in hunting, but should only revise themselves respectfully.
There is no such thing as a lord who can cultivate the righteousness himself while his ministers are treacherous.
The relationship between husband and wife is the rule of law for the king and the key to the safety of the country. It is what a wise king should be most cautious about.
In the past, Shun warned the two women to speak and behave in a correct manner to make his noble character even nobler; King Zhuang of Chu endured the pain and did not see Danji, thus achieving the feat of overlord; King You of Zhou was deceived by Bao Si, and Zhou's virtue declined and the country perished; Duke Huan of Lu was coerced by Qi's daughter Jiang, and the state of Ji was overthrown.
If you can really regulate the affairs of the harem and clarify the order of superiority and inferiority, those with high status cannot monopolize the emperor's favor due to jealousy, so as to cut off the traces of arrogance and arrogance, and suppress the troubles such as Guo Si and Yan's wife. Those with low status can serve the monarch in order, and each can perform their duties. It can expand the continuation of future generations, quell the resentment of "White Flowers" and the like, and make them rich financially with relatives in the harem, and do not let them participate in political affairs. This can alienate people like the emperor's father who rely on favor to get official positions, weaken the power of the wife's party, and the world will be in chaos without the maintenance of the boudoir.
To conquer the distant place, we must start by governing the near place, and to learn good conduct must start from the people around us.
In the past, the dragon was in charge of Nayan, and Shun's orders were honest and obedient; the four assistants were complete, and the king made no mistakes.
If you can really tell the ministers who are in charge of everything, those who wear the golden mink ornaments and hold the responsibilities of Chang Bo, let them learn the ways of the previous kings and understand the righteousness between monarchs and ministers. Everyone will learn to be cautious and trustworthy, and will not play the fault of arrogance and indulgence. Then the ministers on the left and right will be respectful and obedient, and the officials will look up to them and follow their example, and the education will spread to all directions.
The scriptures say: We must first rectify and control the ministers on the left and right.
There is no right and left ministers who are upright but all the officials are dishonest.
If those who rule the world respect the virtuous and judge their merits, then the world will be peaceful; if they despise the virtuous, regardless of their merits, the world will be in chaos.
If you really can carefully consider the method of governing the people, rejoice in the blessing of capable people, select scholars based on their talents, and be sure to put them on trial for their positions, clearly define the assessment standards to measure their abilities, and examine their actual merits to evaluate their virtues, and do not use gangs to engage in private interests. If you don't listen to the false praises of others, and don't listen to the false accusations that are accumulated, then the officials who have the responsibility of correcting their merits will not have to worry about their merits being hidden and slandered. People who form cliques and engage in evil and cunning can't get official positions. The number of villains is decreasing day by day, and the number of talented and capable people is increasing day by day.
The scriptures say: The performance of officials is assessed once every three years. After three assessments, those who have done nothing but have no merit will be dismissed, and those who have merit will be promoted.
He also said: People with nine virtues are appointed to work, and those who are outstanding and capable are given official positions.
If rewards based on merit are not implemented, many talented people are placed in official positions, but the country is not peaceful.
summary: Gu Yong cited historical examples: Guo Si caused Zong Zhou's downfall, and Yan's wife's arrogance led to a solar eclipse. He emphasized that the relationship between husband and wife is crucial for national safety. He advised regulating the harem, clarifying superiority and inferiority, and preventing jealousy and arrogance. He urged the emperor to correct himself, reduce private banquets, stop excessive pleasures, and follow etiquette and law. He also stressed the importance of selecting virtuous officials, assessing their merits, and avoiding favoritism. He warned that disasters are warnings from heaven, and if ignored, punishments will increase.

translation:
The emperor specifically asked Gu Yong, and Gu Yong replied: The solar eclipse and earthquake were caused by the exclusive favor of the queen's concubine.
This incident is recorded in the "Five Elements Chronicles".
At this time, the emperor had just ascended the throne. He was modest and courteous and entrusted the political affairs to the general Wang Feng. Most of the ministers blamed Wang Feng.
Gu Yong knew that Wang Feng had just been trusted and took power, and secretly wanted to rely on Wang Feng, so he said:
Now that all the barbarians have surrendered, they have all become your concubines. There is no need to worry about making porridge or food in the north, and there is no need to worry about Zhao Tuo or Lu Jia in the south. The borders on three sides are stable, and there is no warning of military revolution.
The big princes only had salaries in several counties, and the officials of the imperial court controlled their power, preventing them from doing anything. There was no longer a situation where Wu, Chu, Yan, and Liang stood side by side.
Hundreds of officials are intertwined, close to each other, and the flesh and blood ministers are as loyal as Shen Bo, pious and respectful, cautious and fearful, and there are no rebellions such as Chonghe, Anyang, and Bolu.
These three aspects are not as fine as a hair, and cannot be blamed on the uncles.
This and those who want to use political affairs to find fault with the prime minister and his son, slander the ministers and eunuchs, and excuse unusual visions, are all people who use unreasonable fallacies to deceive the emperor of heaven.
Privately, I am afraid that Your Majesty will make obvious mistakes, ignore the clear warnings of heaven and earth, listen to the unreasonable fallacies of ignorant people, blame innocent people, attribute the occurrence of disasters to political affairs, and deeply lose the will of the Emperor of Heaven. This is extremely unacceptable.
His Majesty ascended the throne and appointed officials according to the old rules without any political fault.
In the first month of the first year, white air clearly rose from the east. By April of the first year, yellow turbid air filled everywhere, covering the capital, and major floods occurred, which were manifested by earthquakes and solar eclipses.
Each has its own account and fulfillment, and the exterior and interior are related to each other. There is nothing to attribute and rely on in all officials and affairs. Isn't it strange to Your Majesty?
The white air rising from the east is a sign that lowly people will rise; the yellow turbid air covering the capital is a sign of the decline and severance of the king's way.
The sluts are rising while the royal power in the capital is declining, which creates a bad experience in both aspects.
Your Majesty can really understand the words of my foolish minister, devote himself to worrying about the vision of heaven and earth, think long-term about the grand plan of the ancestral temple, change the mistakes of the past, get rid of indulgence, eliminate biased favor, strengthen the power of hard work, equally share the favor of the Emperor of Heaven, so that all the concubines can be served in turn.
Judging from this method, it is actually a blessing for Your Majesty to have descendants among humble people.
It's just to get the descendants to inherit. There is nothing mean about a mother.
Send harems and concubines who are suitable for the emperor's wishes, and widely seek among humble people, so that they can encounter the help shown by the emperor, comfort and resolve the worries and resentments of the empress dowager, reconcile and eliminate the blame and anger of the emperor, then the descendants will multiply, and disasters and strange phenomena will cease.
If your majesty fails to observe my words deeply and ignores the warnings of heaven and earth, the source of the disaster will not be eliminated. Water and rain disasters, mountain and rock strange phenomena will occur soon; so many disasters have occurred and have reached the extreme, and the changes in the celestial phenomena have taken shape. Even if I want to sacrifice my life and offer advice, it will be of no use.
He who alienates humble ministers dares to state the will of God forthrightly, rebukes and ridicules the privacy of the palace curtains, wants to alienate the noble queen and the favored concubine, but knows that his harsh words are not in line with the emperor's will, and he will definitely not be exempted from the punishment of soup and wok.
summary: The emperor was surprised by Gu Yong's countermeasures and summoned him. Gu Yong continued, stating that the solar eclipse and earthquake were caused by the exclusive favor of the queen's concubine. He knew that General Wang Feng had just gained power and secretly wanted to rely on him. He argued that the borders were stable, the princes had limited power, and officials were loyal, so the disasters could not be blamed on the uncles. He advised the emperor to understand the warnings, change past mistakes, eliminate biased favor, and ensure all concubines served in turn to secure descendants and end disasters.

translation:
I'm personally unhappy for you.
You should resolutely demand to resign, state that your talents are not enough to strengthen the guards of the city gate, accept the name of Taibo's humility, keep the path of humility, close the door and sleep in peace, and be the leader of wise people.
I hope you will consider this matter with knowledgeable people, and I have arranged it for you.
Wang Tan was very moved by his letter, so he refused to accept the position of leading the city gate.
From then on, Wang Tan and Wang Yin were at odds with each other.
Gu Yong was working as a county official in a distant place. He was worried about being harmed by Wang Yin, so he claimed that he had been ill for three full months and was relieved of his duties.
Wang Yinzhuo asked Gu Yong to be appointed as the commander of the camp. Gu Yong apologized many times and stated his case, so he was transferred to the post of Chang Shi.
Because Wang Yin transcended his close relatives and assisted in political affairs as a cousin, his power and influence were lower than those of Wang Feng. Gu Yong then persuaded Wang Yin and said: "The general holds the position of general, enfeoffs the fertile land of the big city, bears the same responsibilities as Duke of Zhou and Duke of Zhao, and controls the secrets of the world. It can be called the ultimate wealth. If there is no second among ministers, the world's blame will come from all sides. What will you rely on to occupy this position?"
You should work tirelessly day and night, with a strong character like Yi Yin, to uphold your duties and assist the emperor, punish evildoers without avoiding those who are close to you, believe in and love them, and promote virtuous people without avoiding those who are hostile and hostile, so as to show the greatest justice and establish credibility in all directions.
Only by concentrating on implementing these three aspects can you be able to shoulder heavy responsibilities for a long time and enjoy deep favor for a long time.
Taibai appeared in the west for sixty days. According to the law, it should reach the sky. Now it has expired and is still among the mulberry trees. Its body is weak and its movement is slow. Its shape is small and its light is weak.
Yinghuojiao is strong, large and bright, and is located in Ojuku in retrograde motion.
When Mars is retrograde, it is fixed; when Mars is in Osu, it is mutable.
Does God's will mean that the general forgets the deep and hidden righteousness, is submissive, the deacon is not strong, does not widely appoint scholars, still has taboos about likes and dislikes, and the magnanimous character is not pure, and is the beginning of betrayal by the generals and ministers?
Why did Venus and Mars mutate like this when you just inherited the title of Sima?
God is the most holy and will not show visions out of thin air. I hope that the general will look at all this with awe and caution, think deeply about the reasons for the changes, and change the way to seek governance to comply with God's will.
Wang Yin still couldn't calm down and recommended Gu Yong to be the guardian envoy.
When Wang Yin died, Wang Shang, the Marquis of Chengdu, took his place as the Great Sima Wei General, and Gu Yong was promoted to the governor of Liangzhou.
After finishing the performance in the capital, it was time to go to the ministry. At that time, a black dragon appeared in Shulai. The emperor sent a minister to ask Gu Yong to hear what he had to say.
Gu Yong replied:
summary: Gu Yong was promoted to Doctor Guanglu. He wrote to thank Wang Feng, praising his support. Later, when Wang Feng died, Wang Yin succeeded him. Gu Yong advised Wang Tan to resign from leading the city gate soldiers, which Wang Tan did, causing a rift with Wang Yin. Gu Yong then advised Wang Yin to work diligently, punish evildoers, and promote virtuous people. He warned about celestial signs like Taibai and Yinghuo, urging Wang Yin to change his ways to comply with God's will.

translation:
I have heard that the Lord can do good with him but not evil with him, and that the Lord can do evil with him but not good with him.
Your Majesty’s natural character, understanding and wisdom are the attributes of God.
As long as you can reflect on the words of the foolish minister for a moment, realize the three disasters, be deeply worried about the great vision, make up your mind to implement good governance, abandon and forget the evil ambition, do not make the same mistakes again, cheer up and devote yourself to governance, and transmit the greatest sincerity to heaven, then the long-standing vision in the sky will be stopped, and the disaster and rebellion on the ground will be subdued, what else is there to worry about?
Privately, I am worried that Your Majesty is not single-minded in his public ambitions, that he is very reserved in his private hobbies, and that he still loves all the villains and is unwilling to pursue them!
The emperor was very moved by his words.
Gu Yong was generally as clear and accessible as Du Qin and Du Ye about scriptures, but he was not as comprehensive as Liu Xiang, his son and Yang Xiong.
He was the most proficient in Tianguan and "Jingshi Yi", so he was good at talking about disasters and phenomena. He recounted more than 40 things before and after, with slight repetitions, and specifically blamed the lord himself and the harem.
Being protected by the Wang family, the Lord also knew that he was not very close and trusted him.
Gu Yong was very competent in every position he held. He served as the governor of the North for more than a year. General Wang Shangguan of the Guard and Wang Gen, the Marquis of Quyang, became generals of hussars. They recommended Gu Yong and conscripted him into the capital to be the chief agricultural officer.
More than a year later, Gu Yongsheng became ill. Two months later, a supervisor petitioned to remove Gu Yong from his position.
As a precedent, when a minister fell ill, the emperor granted him a leave of absence, and Shan Shan was immediately dismissed from his post when he arrived in Gu Yong.
A few months later, Gu Yong died at home.
His real name was Gu Bing, but it is said that he changed his name to Gu Yong because of Fan Bing's rebellion.
Du Ye, named Zixia, was originally from Fanyang, Wei County.
After accumulating meritorious service, my grandfather and father were promoted to county governors. During the reign of Emperor Wu, they moved to Maoling.
Du Ye lost his father when he was young, and his mother was Zhang Chang's daughter.
When Du Ye was in his prime, he studied with Zhang Chang's son Zhang Ji and obtained books from his family collection.
He became a man because of his filial piety and integrity.
Du Ye was friendly with the chariot general Wang Yin.
Ping'a Hou Wang Tan refused to accept the city gate post and later died. The Lord was sad and regretful about this, so he ordered Wang Tan's younger brother Chengdu Hou Wang Shang to be promoted to a special rank and lead the city gate soldiers, so that he could promote officials like a general's palace.
Du Ye saw that Wang Yin had a quarrel with Ping'ahou before, so he persuaded Wang Yin and said: I heard that it is human nature to treat those who are kind to you, to treat those who are kind to you, and to treat those you love most, to respond to requests.
Being close but not being treated specially, who can be without resentment?
This is the purpose of the poems "Tangdi" and "Jiao Gong".
In the past, Uncle Qin's country had thousands of chariots, but it could not accommodate his half-brother. The "Spring and Autumn" also recorded and ridiculed him.
summary: Gu Yong served as governor of the North and later died at home. He was proficient in Tianguan and "Jingshi Yi," and his memorials focused on the lord and the harem. Du Ye, styled Zixia, was from Fanyang and studied with Zhang Ji. He was friendly with Wang Yin and advised him to cooperate with Wang Shang. Du Ye later served as governor of Liangzhou but was dismissed due to illness. During Emperor Ai's reign, he criticized the influence of the Fu and Ding families, warning about solar eclipses and earthquakes as signs of imbalance. He urged the emperor to follow ancient laws and satisfy the people's wishes. Du Ye died without an official title.

translation:
I heard that the pheasant behaved strangely, and Emperor Gaozong was deeply moved; a strong wind blew violently, and King Cheng was frightened.
I hope that your majesty will be more careful and sincere, consider inheriting the prosperity of the early period of the country, and examine ancient laws in everything to satisfy the people's wishes. Then the people of Li will not be unhappy. When the gods in heaven withdraw their power and anger, there is no need to worry about whether blessings and blessings will come in return:
Du Ye died of illness without being awarded an official title.
Du Ye talks about people spreading rumors to prepare for divination, and Gu Yong talks about kings buying private fields, and the divination of comets, meteorites and lock springs being lost. These are all recorded in "Five Elements Chronicles".
At first, Du Ye studied with Zhang Ji. Zhang Ji's son Zhang Song lost his father when he was young and studied with Du Ye. He was also famous at that time, especially good at writing.
Du Ye's son, Du Lin, was a quiet and ancient man, and also had great talents. He was a minister in Jianwu and the highest in the palace, Sikong.
His writing skills were better than those of Du Ye and Zhang Song, so people say that the study of writing began with Si Gong.
Zan said: During the era of Emperor Xiaocheng, the political power was entrusted to the family of relatives, and the uncles controlled the political power. Their power was even greater than that of the Lie family and the Fu family during the period of Emperor Xiaoai.
Therefore, Du Ye dared to accuse the Ding family and the Fu family, while Qin did not dare to talk about the Wang family. This was because the situation made them like that.
Du Qin wanted to suppress and reduce Wang Feng's power, but Du Ye relied on Wang Yin and Wang Shang. The same was true.
Gu Yong stated Sanqi's warning, which showed his loyalty. When he cited Shen Bo's story to flatter Wang Huang, alienated Ping Ahou and General Chaoqi, and stated the changes of Jinhuo to seek reconciliation, he can be called a person who lacks integrity but is more than capable of talking.
Confucius said that "you have many friends", and these three people are similar to this statement.
summary: The commentary notes that during Emperor Xiaocheng's era, power was with relatives, while during Emperor Xiaoai's era, the Fu and Ding families held power. Du Ye dared to accuse the Ding and Fu families, but Gu Yong avoided criticizing the Wang family due to circumstances. Gu Yong's loyalty was shown in his warnings, but he also flattered Wang Feng and alienated others, lacking integrity but excelling in rhetoric.

translation:
In the past, the system of the kings, from the emperor, princes to slaves, their official titles, salary, life and death system had different levels. The small ones could not surpass the big ones, and the lowly ones could not surpass the noble ones. Therefore, the top and bottom were orderly and the people's hearts were stable. Therefore, different geographical conditions such as land, rivers, lakes, hills, fertile land, plains, and depressions were identified, and the people were taught planting and livestock raising techniques. In this way, the people's supplies for daily life and funerals, including grains, livestock, fish, turtles, birds, beasts, firewood, wood, instruments, and other materials were produced. Production must follow certain seasons, and consumption must be controlled.
Before the first month of the lunar calendar, one cannot go into the mountains and forests to cut down trees. Before the first month of the lunar calendar, one cannot go to the rivers and lakes to fish.
In addition to complying with seasonal production, they are also not allowed to cut down small trees in the mountains, cut young grass by the lake, catch young insects, fish, or beasts, or collect bird eggs. This is to adapt to the seasonal climate and allow various organisms to reproduce and thrive. In this way, you can give full play to the effects of nature and make all kinds of property reserves abundant.
Then, according to the natural conditions of the area, the scholars, farmers, industry and merchants gave full play to their intelligence and physical strength, got up early and went to bed late, managed their own industries, and exchanged with each other: the results of their work met their respective needs. In this way, there is no additional requisition of civilian manpower and material resources, and there is sufficient property in areas near and far.
Therefore, the "Book of Changes" says: The monarch uses decrees to determine the changes in nature, assists the heaven and earth to suit the needs of the world, teaches the people to engage in production, produces various kinds of property, uses it in various aspects, and makes various utensils so that the world can benefit. This is the greatness of the sage, and this is what it means.
"Guanzi" said: In ancient times, scholars, farmers, workers, and merchants were not allowed to live together.
Scholars discuss benevolence and righteousness with each other in the place where they study, craftsmen discuss skills with each other in the government office, businessmen discuss wealth and profit with each other in the market, and farmers discuss farming affairs with each other in the fields. They are engaged in one occupation from morning to night and do not change when things change.
Therefore, even if their father and brother's teachings are not strict, they can teach their children well; their children can learn skills even if they do not work hard. They are content with where they live and are happy to pursue their own professions. Even if they see strange and gorgeous items, they will not accept them because they are not suitable for their customs. This is just like the customs of the Rong people and Di people in the northwest and the Wuyue people in the southeast cannot be integrated.
In this case, people's desires are few and things are simple, and property is abundant without competition.
So the rulers use morality to guide them and use rituals to unify them. Therefore, the common people have integrity and courtesy, value benevolence and righteousness, and despise wealth.
This is the summary of why the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties were able to develop along the right path and govern the country without resorting to harsh politics.
summary: The ancient system of kings established hierarchical distinctions from emperor to slave, with graded official titles, salaries, and life-and-death rites, ensuring that the lowly did not surpass the noble, thus stabilizing society. People were taught to cultivate land and raise livestock according to seasonal and geographical conditions, with strict rules against cutting trees or fishing before the first lunar month, and prohibitions on harvesting immature plants, animals, or eggs to allow natural reproduction and abundant reserves. Scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants each specialized in their occupations, exchanging goods to meet needs without excessive taxation, as noted in the "Book of Changes" and "Guanzi," which emphasized that people content with their professions and customs would have few desires and ample property, guided by morality and ritual.

translation:
When the Zhou royal family declined and etiquette was destroyed, Duke Zhuang of Lu violated Zhou etiquette by carving on the rafters of his father Huan Gong's temple and dyeing the pillars red.
Zang Wenzhong, a senior official in the State of Lu, violated the Zhou rites by carving mountain shapes on the tops of the columns and painting algae on the short columns on the beams. Shiqing Ji of Lu State played music and dance in the temple with eight hundred people. The three families of Meng Sun, Shu Sun and Ji Sun of Lu State actually sang the poem "Yong" to remove the sacrifices when worshiping their ancestors. This trend spread to ordinary scholars and civilians. Everyone deviated from the system of the Holy King and gave up their business. The number of people working in agriculture decreased, and the number of people doing business increased. There was a shortage of food and an abundance of luxury goods. This trend of decline developed after Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, etiquette and righteousness were greatly destroyed, superiors and subordinates offended each other, the politics of various countries were very different, the ethos of the officials were different, the activities of pursuing profit could not be curbed, and there was no end to the behavior of destroying the hierarchy.
As a result, merchants sold rare and exotic goods, craftsmen produced utensils with no practical value, and scholars engaged in crooked activities to obtain wealth in pursuit of the favor of the times.
A deceitful person goes against the facts and obtains a name by deception; a treacherous person violates the law and harms others to seek profit; a person who murders the monarch and usurps the power of the country becomes a prince; and a person who robs the fiefdom of a great official becomes a hero.
Etiquette and righteousness cannot restrain a gentleman, and punishment and killing cannot frighten the common people.
The rich use silk to decorate their houses and walls, and their dogs and horses eat grain and meat with leftovers, while the poor cannot even wear coarse cloth and often eat beans and drink raw water.
They are all common people with registered households, but their status is different due to different financial resources. Although some become slaves, they still have no resentment.
Therefore, those who play political tricks and do evil can be rich all their lives; those who follow justice and stick to the right path are not immune to the threat of hunger and cold.
This trend emerged from the upper echelons of society and stemmed from the destruction of the legal system.
Therefore, these things are listed to record the changes in the world.
In the past, when King Gou Jian of Yue was besieged on Kuaiji Mountain by Wu soldiers, he appointed Fan Li and Ji Ran to assist in state affairs.
Ji Ran said: If you know how to fight, you will organize your defense; if you know when to use what, you will truly understand the value of things.
If you understand the relationship between time changes and the supply and demand of goods, you can understand the market conditions of various goods.
Therefore, when there is a drought, ships are purchased in advance to prepare for floods, and when there are floods, vehicles are purchased in advance to prepare for drought. This is in line with the laws of development and change of things. The State of Yue pursued the policy of Ji Ran, and after ten years of rule, the country became greatly wealthy. It rewarded the soldiers with large sums of money, and finally avenged the State of Wu and washed away the shame of being besieged in Kuaiji.
Fan Li sighed and said: Ji Ran had ten strategies, but the king of Yue only used five to realize his wish.
summary: The decline began when the Zhou royal family weakened and etiquette collapsed, exemplified by Duke Zhuang of Lu violating Zhou rites by carving and painting his father's temple, and other officials like Zang Wenzhong and the three Huan families of Lu exceeding their ranks in music and sacrifices. This spread to commoners, who abandoned farming for commerce, leading to food shortages and luxury excess. After the reigns of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, ritual and righteousness were destroyed, superiors and subordinates offended each other, and deceitful, treacherous, and murderous individuals gained wealth and status. The rich decorated homes with silk and fed dogs and horses grain, while the poor wore coarse cloth and ate beans, yet the poor did not resent their status. Those who followed justice faced hunger, while the wicked prospered, all stemming from the destruction of the legal system. In response, King Gou Jian of Yue, besieged on Kuaiji Mountain, appointed Fan Li and Ji Ran to govern. Ji Ran advised buying ships during droughts and vehicles during floods to prepare for opposite conditions, understanding market cycles. Yue followed this policy, became wealthy, and avenged Wu. Fan Li later applied these principles to enrich his family, changing his name to Zhu Gong in Taoyi, a central trading hub. He hoarded goods, adapted to circumstances, and lent money wisely, amassing a fortune three times over 19 years, distributing wealth to the poor, and leaving a legacy that made "Duke Tao Zhu" synonymous with riches.

translation:
Since it can be used to enrich the country, I also want to use it to enrich the family.
So he took a small boat and wandered around the rivers and lakes, changing his name and surname. When he went to Qi, he was called Yi Yi Zipi, and when he went to Taoyi, he was called Zhu Gong.
Fan Li believed that Taoyi was at the center of the world and was well connected with the princes and countries in all directions, making it very convenient to trade goods. So he managed the property, hoarded it, adapted to circumstances, used his ingenuity to make profits, and selected people to lend money, so that the debt could be recovered without the need for recovery.
Therefore, people who are good at making money must first be able to choose people, and secondly, they must be good at seizing opportunities.
In his 19th year, Duke Zhu earned a thousand pieces of gold three times and distributed it twice to his poor friends and distant brothers.
Later, when he got old and frail, he left it to his children and grandchildren to make the decision. The children and grandchildren could inherit the family business and develop it, and eventually the family would be rich.
Therefore, when people in later generations talk about rich men, they all praise Duke Tao Zhu.
After Zi Gan studied under Confucius and became an official, he returned to Wei and became an official. He also made money by doing business between Cao and Wei.
Among the seventy disciples of Confucius, Duanmu Ci, Zigong, was the richest. Another favorite disciple of Confucius, Yan Yuan, was so poor that he lived in a narrow alley.
Zigong, with his high chariot and four horses, followed by knights cheering in front and behind him, went out as envoys to the princes with bundles of silk and generous gifts. Wherever he went, he fought with the king in the same court.
However, Confucius praised Yan Yuan for his wisdom and ridiculed Zigong, saying: Yan Hui's knowledge is almost close to the holy way. Although his pocket is often short, he enjoys it.
Zigong did not follow the teachings, he only made money through business, speculated about right and wrong, and got lucky.
Bai Gui, a native of Zhou. During Wei Wenhou's time, Li Ke was the prime minister and devoted himself to guiding farming and land utilization, while Bai Gui liked to observe the price changes in the market in different periods, so he advocated that when others give up, I take, and when others take, I give.
Bai Gui can not pay attention to food and drink, restrain his hobbies and desires, save on clothing, share the joys and sorrows with the servants and servants in charge, and seize opportunities for wealth as quickly as beasts and ferocious birds seize food.
Therefore Bai Gui said: My business pursuit is just like Yi Yin and Lu Shang plotting state affairs, Sun Tzu and Wu Qi using troops to fight, and Shang Yang promoting reforms.
Therefore, for those who are not smart enough to adapt to changes like me, not brave enough to be resolute and decisive, not benevolent enough to make correct choices, and not strong enough to stick to principles, even if they want to learn my way of making money, I will never tell them.
Most people today who talk about how to make money in business regard Bai Gui as their ancestor.
Yidun made his fortune by operating Chiyan, while Guo Zong, a Handan native, accumulated his family fortune by smelting iron and casting ironware, and his wealth was comparable to that of princes.
Wu Shiying was engaged in animal husbandry. When the livestock multiplied in large numbers, he sold them all, purchased strange things and silk fabrics, and secretly presented them to the Rong King.
summary: Other wealthy figures included Zi Gong, a disciple of Confucius who traded between Cao and Wei, becoming richer than Yan Yuan, though Confucius praised Yan's wisdom. Bai Gui of Zhou, during Wei Wenhou's time, observed market price changes, advocating buying when others sold and vice versa. He lived frugally, shared hardships with servants, and seized opportunities swiftly, comparing his methods to Yi Yin, Sun Tzu, and Shang Yang. He taught only those who were intelligent, brave, benevolent, and strong. Yidun made a fortune from salt, Guo Zong from iron, and Wu Shiying from livestock, who bribed the Rong King and became so wealthy that Qin Shihuang honored him. The widow Qing of Ba preserved her family's cinnabar mine, and Qin Shihuang built a platform for her as a chaste woman.

translation:
King Rong rewarded him with livestock worth ten times as much as the donated items. The livestock given were so many that the number of cattle and horses was calculated using the valley as a unit.
Qin Shihuang ordered that Wu Shizhen be treated as a monarch and that he and his ministers should go to the palace to meet him at the specified time.
The widow of Bajun was named Qing. Her ancestors discovered a cinnabar mine. Several generations of people had been enjoying the profits from the mining, and their family wealth was countless.
Qing is a widow. She can keep her ancestors' family property and use money to protect herself from infringement.
Qin Shihuang believed that she was a chaste woman and treated her like a guest, so he specially built a Nuhuaiqing platform for her.
According to the system of the Qin and Han Dynasties, princes and feudal lords levied rent taxes, usually two hundred yuan per household per year.
The annual income of a thousand-household prince is 200,000 yuan, and expenses such as meeting the emperor, visiting princes, offering sacrifices, and locking gifts all depend on 200,000 yuan.
Farmers, craftsmen, merchants, etc. among the common people, if their families have 10,000 yuan, they can get 2,000 yuan in interest every year, and those with one million yuan can have an income of 200,000 yuan every year, and all the labor, rent and taxes are spent from the house. This kind of family.
General desires for food and clothing can be satisfied as best as possible. Therefore, fifty horses are raised on the land, one hundred and sixty-seven cattle are raised, two hundred and fifty sheep are raised, two hundred and ten pigs are raised in the swamps, thousands of rocks of fish are raised in the ponds, and large tree trunks are planted in the mountains.
There are thousands of jujube trees in Anyi; thousands of chestnut trees in Yan and Qin; thousands of orange trees in Shu, Mo, and Jiangling; thousands of tangerine trees in Huaibei and south of Rongshui, between the Yellow River and Jishui; thousands of acres of lacquer trees in Chen and Xia; thousands of acres of mulberry trees in Qi and Lu There are thousands of acres of bamboo orchards in the Wei River; and there are thousands of acres of fertile farmland with a yield of one bell per acre in the suburbs of the famous cities with thousands of households in the county, or thousands of acres of gardenias and madders, or thousands of acres of ginger and leeks: all such families are as wealthy as Qianhuhou.
The proverb says: If a poor man wants to get rich, it is better to work than to farm, to do business than to work, and to do business on the street than to embroider.
This means that doing business is a reliable way for poor people to get rich.
In a city that extends in all directions, in a year, one can sell thousands of jars of wine, thousands of jars of vinegar and sauce, and thousands of jars of syrup, slaughter and sell thousands of cattle, sheep, and pigs, sell thousands of clocks of rice, thousands of carts of firewood, thousands of ships, and thousands of timber buildings. Thousands of bamboo poles, hundreds of chariots, thousands of ox-carts, thousands of lacquered wooden vessels, 30,000 jins of bronzes, unvarnished wooden vessels, iron vessels and thousands of stones of gardenias and madders, 200 horses, 250 oxen, sheep and pigs Two thousand, a hundred servants, a thousand catties of sinew and cinnabar, thirty thousand catties of other silk, wadding, and bundles of cloth, a thousand bolts of satin, a thousand stones of coarse cloth and leather, a thousand buckets of lacquer, a thousand bucks of distiller's yeast, salt, and black beans, sea fish, and knives Thousands of catties of fish, thousands of small miscellaneous fish, thirty thousand catties of salted fish, three thousand jin of dates and chestnuts, thousands of fox and mink fur coats, thousands of lambskin coats, thousands of felt blankets, thousands of various fruits and vegetables, and thousands of usury money. Brokers regulate prices. A greedy businessman makes a profit of three-tenths if he makes a large profit but does not sell well. A calm businessman makes a profit of five-tenths if he makes a small profit but quick turnover. Their income can also be compared with that of Qian Huhou.
summary: Under Qin and Han systems, a prince with a thousand households earned 200,000 yuan annually from rents, while commoners with 10,000 yuan could earn 2,000 yuan in interest. Wealthy families raised livestock, planted trees, or cultivated crops like jujubes, chestnuts, oranges, lacquer, mulberries, bamboo, or ginger, matching the income of a thousand-household prince. The proverb said that for a poor man to get rich, commerce was better than farming or crafts. In a bustling city, annual sales of wine, vinegar, grain, livestock, timber, and other goods could yield profits comparable to a prince's income.

translation:
This is the general picture. The ancestors of the Zhuo family in Shu County were from Zhao State and made their fortune by smelting iron.
When the Qin State conquered the state of Fang, it exiled the Zhuo family to Shu County. The couple pushed a cart to the place of exile.
Among the fellow exiled prisoners, those who had a little extra money rushed to give it to the officials in charge, begging to be moved to a closer place and placed in Jiameng County.
Only the Zhuo family said: Jiameng County is a small place and the land is barren.
I heard that the land at the foot of Marriage Mountain is fertile and produces big taro. With it, you will not be hungry until you die.
The people there are very good at doing business and it is easy to do business.
So he asked to be exiled further away.
The officials sent his family to Lin. The whole family was very happy. They mined and smelted iron in the mountains where there were iron ores, cast iron tools, planned and managed carefully, and did business with people in the Yunnan and Shu regions. He was so wealthy that he had eight hundred servants. He usually goes fishing and hunting, and is as happy as the king.
Cheng Zheng was a captive exiled from Shandong to the southwest region. He also ran a smelting and casting industry and sold ironware to local ethnic minorities. He was as wealthy as the Zhuo family.
After the decline of the Cheng and Zhuo families, during the reigns of Emperor Cheng and Emperor Ai, the wealth of Chengdu native Luo Pei reached tens of millions.
When Luo Ai went to the capital to do business, he took nearly a million dollars with him, and he managed the money for the Shi family from Pingling.
Luo Fei is a strong and courageous person.
The Shi family's wealth was slightly inferior to that of the Pinglingru family and the Ju family. He trusted Luo Pei very much and gave him a lot of money to do business in Ba, Shu and the capital. After a few years, he made more than 10 million yuan in profits.
Luo Fei used half of the money to bribe Wanggen, the Marquis of Quyang, and Chun Yuchang, the Marquis of Dingling, and relied on their power to lend the remaining half to the county. No one dared to owe him anything.
He monopolized the profits from the well salt business and made a fortune twice as much as his capital in one year.
The ancestors of the Kong family in Wan County were from Daliang and were engaged in the smelting and casting industry.
Qin destroyed Wei and moved the Jie family to Nanyang. The Kong family vigorously engaged in the smelting and foundry industry, and planned farmland and water conservancy. They traveled with chariots and horses, made friends with the princes, and took the opportunity to trade with the princes and make profits, and won the reputation of "the leisurely son".
However, his profit exceeded the capital spent, and he made more money than those who care about everything. His family accumulated wealth worth thousands of gold. Therefore, everyone doing business in Nanyang imitated Kong's grace and generosity.
The people of Lu are frugal in their customs, and the Bing family is even more prominent. Mr. Bing started his career by smelting iron and his wealth reached tens of millions.
But his family, from father to brother to descendants, all abide by a family rule: when you bend down, you must gain something, when you raise your head, you must gain something, and every move must be profitable. His family made loans and did business throughout the counties.
Because of the influence of the Bing family, many people in Zou and Lu areas abandoned literature and went into business to make profits.
The custom in Qi despises slaves, but Dao Xian likes to value slaves.
summary: The Zhuo family of Shu, exiled from Zhao, chose fertile land at Marriage Mountain, mined iron, and traded with Yunnan and Shu, amassing wealth with 800 servants. Cheng Zheng, a captive, also prospered in iron. Later, Luo Pei of Chengdu, trusted by the Shi family, made millions in Ba, Shu, and the capital, bribing nobles to monopolize well salt. The Kong family of Wan, exiled to Nanyang, combined iron smelting with farming and trade, earning a reputation for generosity. The Bing family of Lu, frugal and meticulous, made millions from iron, influencing many to abandon literature for commerce. Dao Xian of Qi valued cunning slaves, using them to trade fish and salt, accumulating tens of millions. After his decline, Wei of Linzi had 50 million. Shishi of Zhou, with hundreds of carts, traded across counties, making 100 million, followed by Zhang Changshu and Xue Zizhong under Wang Mang.

translation:
The fierce and cunning servants gave people a headache, but Dao Xian took them in and sent them to run the fish and salt merchants' profits. Some of them went out in teams to make friends with the county guards and ministers, and Dao Xian trusted such servants even more. Dao Xian finally relied on their strength to accumulate tens of millions of money.
So the slaves said: It is better to be a slave in Dao's family than to go out to seek officialdom. It means that Dao Xian can make Hao Nu personally wealthy and make them do their best for themselves.
After the decline of Daoxian, during the reigns of Emperor Cheng and Emperor Ai, a man named Wei from Linzi had assets of fifty million yuan.
The people of Zhou were frugal and stingy enough to begin with, and Shishi was even more generous. He dispatched hundreds of vehicles loaded with goods to do business in various counties and states.
Luoyang is located in the center of Qi, Qin, Chu and Tang. Rich families boast to each other that they have been doing business abroad for a long time, so they often pass by Luoyang without entering their homes.
Being able to use this kind of people, Shishi can make as much as 100 million.
After the decline of Shishi, by the time of Emperor Cheng, Emperor Ai, and Wang Mang, the wealth of Luoyang natives Zhang Changshu and Xue Zizhong also amounted to tens of millions of dollars.
Wang Mang appointed them all as Nayanshi, hoping to follow the example of Emperor Mowu, but he failed to get the benefits of appointing them as officials.
An ancestor of the Ren family in Xuanqu County worked as a warehouse manager in a local area.
When the Qin Dynasty was defeated, local heroes scrambled to seize gold, silver and jade, but only the food stored in Ren's kiln warehouses.
When the Chu and Han Dynasties were fighting over Rongyang, farmers were unable to farm, and the price of food rose to ten thousand yuan per stone. As a result, all the gold and jade of the heroes fell into the hands of the Ren family. As a result, Ren became rich.
The rich compete for luxury, but the Ren family does not pretend to be frugal and frugal, and vigorously engages in farmland and animal husbandry.
People rush to buy bargains, but Ren prefers expensive and high-quality things.
His family's wealth lasted for several generations. But the family rules of the protagonist Ren stipulate that he will not eat anything that is not produced by his own farming and livestock, and he is not allowed to drink alcohol or eat meat until official business is completed.
Therefore, the Ren family became a role model in the village, so he was rich and respected by the emperor.
When the country opened up the frontier area, only Qiaotao had a thousand horses, two thousand cattle, ten thousand sheep, and tens of thousands of grains.
During the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu, the princes and princes in Chang'an City wanted to follow the army out of the country to fight, and borrowed money from moneylenders at usurious rates for their travels. The moneylenders believed that their food towns and feudal states were all in the Guandong area, and the outcome of the war in Guandong was uncertain, so they refused to lend money.
Only the Wuyan family loaned them a thousand gold coins and charged ten times the interest.
After three months of fighting, the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu was put down.
Within one year, Wu Yan earned ten times the interest and became a rich man in Guanzhong.
Most of the wealthy businessmen in the Guanzhong area were from wealthy families with the surname Tian, ​​among which Tian Qiang and Tian Lan were the richest.
summary: The Ren family of Xuanqu stored grain during Qin's fall, profiting when war drove prices to 10,000 yuan per stone. They focused on farmland and livestock, eating only what they produced, and became a model village, respected by the emperor. During the Seven Kingdoms' rebellion, Wuyan family lent money at tenfold interest, earning a fortune in Guanzhong. Other wealthy families included the Tian clan, Fan Jia, Zhi Gang, and Wang Junfang, with Fan Jia having 50 million. Countless others gained wealth through patents, bribery, or illegal means like tomb robbing and gambling, corrupting society and leading to chaos.

translation:
Jia Yi, a native of Luoyang, was famous locally for his ability to recite poems and write articles when he was eighteen years old.
When Wu Gong, the governor of Henan Province, heard that he had excellent talents and studies, he summoned him to his sect and thought highly of him.
Not long after Emperor Wen of Han came to the throne, he heard that Wu Gong, the governor of Henan Province, had the best political performance in the country. He was from the same hometown as Li Si and had learned from Li Si, so he recruited him as a court captain.
Tingwei recommended that although Jia Yi was young, he was well versed in the books of various schools of thought.
Emperor Wen of Han called Jia Yi to become a doctor.
At this time, Jia Yi was in his twenties and the youngest among the Ph.D.
Every time Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty ordered the questions to be discussed, the older doctors could not say anything, but Jia Yi could answer them one by one, and everyone felt that they had said what they meant. The doctors then thought that Jia Yi had outstanding talents.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty liked him and promoted him unusually, and within a year he was promoted to Taizhong doctor.
Jia Yi believes that the Han Dynasty has been established for more than 20 years and the country is peaceful and harmonious. The calendar should be revised, the colors of carriages and horses should be changed, the legal system should be formulated, the names of official positions should be determined, and rituals and music should be revitalized.
So he drafted regulations for various ceremonies, using yellow as the color of nobility, using a five-character seal for the official seal, confirming the title of the official position, changing all the old systems, and Jia Yi reported to the emperor.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty was cautious and had no time to implement it.
However, the changes in various laws and regulations and the fact that various princes moved to their own feudal states were all proposed by Jia Yi.
So Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty discussed with his ministers and let Jia Yi take the position of public minister.
Jianghou, Guanhou, Dongyanghou, Feng Jing and others were jealous of him and slandered him: "This young man in Luoyang is young and has little knowledge. He wants to monopolize power and causes chaos in many things."
Because of this, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty later alienated him, did not adopt his opinions, and made him the Prince of Changsha.
Jia Yi left because he was demoted, and his will was not exerted. When crossing the Xiang River, he wrote a poem in memory of Qu Yuan.
Qu Yuan was a wise minister of the Chu State. He was slandered and exiled. He wrote "Li Sao Fu" and wrote at the end: Forget it!
There is no one in the country who understands me.
So he threw himself into the river and died.
Jia Yi remembered and mourned him, so he compared himself with Qu Yuan.
His poem reads:
In accordance with the emperor's decree, I went to Changsha to take up my post.
I once listened with humility to others saying that Qu Yuan committed suicide by throwing himself into the Miluo River.
Now I come to the bank of the Xiangjiang River to use the water of the Xiangjiang River to express my grief and condolences to Qu Yuan.
A lot of worldly slanderous words are thrown at you, sir. You can only throw yourself into the river and destroy your body.
How sad! You were born at the wrong time and did not encounter a good era.
The magical bird hides or flies away, but the hawk flies in the sky.
There are people in the world who say that Bian Sui, who was not greedy for the world and drowned to death, and Boyi, who did not eat Zhou millet and starved to death, are greedy. Instead, they say that the great thieves Zhi and Jiao are honest. They argue that the famous sword Mo Xie in ancient times is very sharp and slow, while ordinary lead and iron knives are very sharp. well!
summary: Jia Yi, a native of Luoyang, was renowned for his literary talents at eighteen. Governor Wu Gong of Henan summoned him after hearing of his abilities. When Emperor Wen of Han ascended the throne, he appointed Wu Gong as a court captain due to his excellent governance and connection to Li Si. Wu Gong recommended Jia Yi, who was then made a doctor at around twenty years old, the youngest among them. Jia Yi excelled in court discussions, impressing the emperor, who promoted him to Taizhong doctor within a year. Jia Yi proposed reforming the calendar, legal system, and rituals, drafting regulations with yellow as the noble color and a five-character seal. Emperor Wen hesitated to implement these changes, but many legal reforms and the relocation of princes were Jia Yi's ideas. Jealous officials slandered Jia Yi, leading to his demotion as Tutor to the Prince of Changsha. On his journey, he wrote a poem mourning Qu Yuan, comparing their fates. The poem lamented Qu Yuan's unjust exile and suicide, criticizing a world that values the worthless over the worthy. Jia Yi advised retreat and self-preservation, using metaphors of dragons and phoenixes to urge distancing from corruption. He argued that Qu Yuan should have sought a wise ruler rather than cling to Chu. Jia Yi emphasized the importance of ritual over punishment, arguing that ritual prevents wrongdoing subtly, while punishment only reacts. He urged the emperor to respect ministers, using historical examples to show that honor fosters loyalty. He advised against humiliating officials, as it erodes their integrity. He used the case of Zhou Bo, falsely accused of treason, to argue for leniency. Emperor Wen heeded this, and thereafter, guilty ministers committed suicide rather than face execution.

translation:
You are so silent and helpless that you are being persecuted for no reason.
He gave up the Zhou Ding treasure that was passed down to the country, but regarded the broken earthen jar as a treasure.
A tired ox is used to drive the shaft, and a lame donkey is used to pull the cart harness; a horse with drooped ears pulls an overweight salt cart.
With Yin people's hats as shoes, can this chaotic situation last long? Hee! Mr. Qu Yuan, who is suffering! You are the only one who has suffered these disasters. Declare: Come on!
Who in the country can understand you? Sir, if you are sulking alone here, who can you tell your innermost thoughts?
If no one understands it, it should fly high and disappear into the distance like a phoenix bird, retiring on its own.
Imitate the dragon hidden in the abyss, hide yourself deep in the water and cherish yourself. How can the dragon associate with water bugs, fish, shrimps, toads, leeches, earthworms and the like?
To stay away from the filthy realm and cherish it yourself, you must cherish the virtues passed down by the saints!
If a horse can be tethered and controlled by others, how is it any different from a dog or a sheep?
You have encountered all kinds of persecution and misfortunes because you did not keep yourself clean and stay away from this dirty world!
You can travel around the land of China and choose a wise king to assist him. Why do you have to miss Chu State?
A gentleman like a phoenix can fly thousands of miles into the sky, and will only come down when he sees a wise king with glorious virtues. When he sees signs of danger in his shortcomings and despicable virtues, he immediately flaps his wings and flies away.
How could a large fish that could swallow a boat be accommodated in a stagnant puddle with only a dozen feet in length and width?
The big fish swimming back and forth in rivers and lakes will inevitably be attacked by mole crickets and ants once they swim into stagnant puddles.
In Jia Yi's third year as the Tutor of Changsha, an owl flew into Jia Yi's room and stopped next to his seat.
The owl is like a cuckoo and is an unlucky bird.
Jia Yi had been demoted and came to live in Changsha. Changsha was low-lying and humid. Jia Yi was often sad and thought that his life would not be long, so he wrote poems to comfort himself.
Fu wrote:
On the evening of the 23rd day of the first month of summer in the year Dingmao, when the sun was about to set, an owl perched in my living room, staying on the corner of the seat with a very leisurely and unhurried look.
This strange bird perched in my home. When I saw the owl flying into my room, I secretly guessed the reason for its arrival. I opened the divination book and checked the predictions based on the predictions in the book.
The book says: Wild birds fly into the house, and the owner of the house will leave this place.
I asked the owl: Where am I going?
If something auspicious happens, tell me. Even if something bad happens, please tell me what the disaster is.
Is my life span long or short? Please tell me a period.
The owl sighed, then raised its head and flapped its wings vigorously. Although it could not speak human language, it could answer with gestures and guess its mood based on its expression.
It means: Thousands of species in the world cycle and change, and there is no end to them. They rotate, flow, and change. Sometimes they rotate and disappear, and sometimes they move and return.
The transformation of form and energy is continuous and endless, just like the transformation of a cicada.
summary: In his third year in Changsha, an owl, an unlucky bird, entered Jia Yi's room. He wrote a poem exploring fate and fortune, reflecting on the cyclical nature of life and the futility of human concerns. The poem discusses the interplay of fortune and misfortune, using examples like Li Si and Fu Yue to illustrate unpredictability. It advocates detachment from worldly desires, embracing the Dao, and accepting life's transience. Jia Yi concluded that the owl's omen was trivial.

translation:
More than a year later, Emperor Wen of Han missed Jia Yi and summoned him back to the capital Chang'an.
Jia Yi arrived and entered the court to ask for an audience. Emperor Wen of Han was receiving the blessings from the gods and sat in the Xuan room to receive Jia Yi.
Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty had some feelings about ghosts and gods, so he asked Jia Yi about the origin of ghosts and gods.
Jia Yi explained the rationale in detail.
The conversation lasted until late at night, and Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty moved to the front of the table without noticing.
After the discussion, Emperor Wen of Han said: I haven't seen Jia Sheng for a long time. I thought I was better than him, but today it seems that I am still not as good as him.
So Jia Yi was appointed as the Taifu of King Huai of Liang.
King Huai of Liang was the youngest son of Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty. He was very favored and liked to read, so he asked Jia Yi to be his teacher. He asked Jia Yi many times for advice on success and failure.
During this period, the Xiongnu became powerful and often invaded the Han Dynasty's borders.
The Han Dynasty had just been established, and the laws and regulations were rough and unclear.
The princes and kings exceeded the scope of their power and occupied more land than the ancient system. The king of Huainan and the king of Jibei were both executed for rebellion.
Jia Yi went to Shu to state political affairs many times. Most of his opinions were to change and establish a new system. The general idea was:
I have privately considered the current national situation and believe that there is one thing that can be cried over, two things that can be shed tears over, and six things that can be sighed over. As for the other things that go against the truth and harm the right path, it is difficult to list them in detail.
Those who advise His Majesty say that the country is already peaceful and well-governed, but I personally think that the country is far from being well-governed.
Those who say that the country is stable and well-governed are either stupid or flattering. They are not people who understand the fundamentals of governing chaos based on facts.
This is like putting fire under a pyre and sleeping on it. If the pyre is not lit, it is safe. How is the current situation in the country different from this situation?
The beginning and end have been reversed, the front and rear embankments have been destroyed, the country's system is in chaos, and it is not very disciplined. How can it be said that it has been governed well?
Your Majesty, why don't you allow me the opportunity to state in detail the strategies for national political improvement and social stability, and let you choose carefully?
Which is more important, the entertainment of hunting, or the key to grasping the security of the country? It is wrong to think that governing a country requires hard work and pain on the body, and lacks the entertainment of bells and drums.
Entertainment was the same as it is now, coupled with the fact that the princes abide by the law, there was no war in the country, the people were stable, the Xiongnu surrendered, people in remote areas submitted to the court, the people were simple and unpretentious, and disputes and lawsuits gradually disappeared. If the general plan of governing the country is mastered, the world will be governed smoothly, the social climate will be peaceful and harmonious, and everything will be reasonable. When you are alive, you will be a wise emperor, and when you die, you will be a god. Your good reputation will be passed down through the ages. "The Rites of Zhou" says that as a founding monarch, you must be meritorious, and as a successor monarch, you must be virtuous, so that your majesty's imperial merits will match those of the great ancestor Liu Bang, and will be immortalized together with the rule of the Han Dynasty.
summary: Emperor Wen later recalled Jia Yi, discussing ghosts and gods late into the night. Impressed, he appointed Jia Yi as Tutor to his favored son, King Huai of Liang. Jia Yi frequently advised on state affairs, highlighting crises: the Xiongnu threat, rebellious princes, and corrupt customs. He argued that the realm was not truly peaceful, comparing it to sleeping on a pyre. He proposed dividing large fiefdoms to weaken princes, using historical examples to show that power leads to rebellion. He urged the emperor to adopt a system of smaller states to ensure stability, warning that inaction would lead to disaster. Jia Yi criticized the Xiongnu policy of appeasement, calling it humiliating and ineffective. He offered to subdue them through strategy. He also condemned lavish dress among commoners, which drained resources and undermined social hierarchy. He lamented the decline of moral standards, tracing it to Qin's abandonment of propriety. He advocated for early education of the crown prince, citing the long reigns of Xia, Shang, and Zhou, which prioritized ritual and moral instruction, unlike Qin's harsh laws that led to rapid collapse.

translation:
Qin Chaoye worked hard to eliminate the disasters of the Six Kingdoms. Now His Majesty controls the world with power. He only uses his cheek expressions to indicate to others, and what he wants to achieve will be achieved. If His Majesty's hands are high and cause the disasters of the Six Kingdoms, it is difficult to say whether he is smart or not.
Gouquan himself did not cause trouble, but kept troubles, and looked carefully without making a decision. Thousands of years later, if he passed it on to the old mother and weak son, they would not be able to live in peace. This cannot be said to be benevolent.
I heard that when the Holy Spirit wanted to speak, he first asked his ministers instead of speaking first. Therefore, the ministers can show their loyalty.
I hope your Majesty will accept my words.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty then adopted Jia Yi's strategy and appointed Liu Wu, King of Huaiyang, as King of Liang. The Liang Kingdom was bounded by Mount Tai in the north and Gaoyang in the west, with more than 40 large counties. He appointed Liu happy, King of Chengyang, as King of Huainan to appease his people.
At that time, the four sons of Liu Chang, King Li of Huainan, were all made marquises.
Jia Yi knew that the emperor must restore the titles of princes and kings, so he admonished him and said: "I am privately worried that your majesty will make several sons of King Li of Huainan king. This has not been carefully discussed with the ministers."
The King of Huainan rebelled and started rebellion. Who in the world didn’t know about his crime?
Fortunately, His Majesty was lenient and banished him. He committed suicide and died. Who in the world thinks that his death was undeserved?
Today's use of the son of a sinner has just lived up to the condemnation of King Li by the people of the world!
When King Li's son grew up, could he forget his father's hatred? Bai Gongsheng avenged his father, targeting his grandfather, uncle, and uncles.
Bai Gongsheng launched a coup, not to seize power, but to vent his resentment. He stabbed his enemy in the chest with a sharp knife, intending to die together with his enemy.
Although Huainan is a small place, Yingbu once used it to rebel against the Han Dynasty. It was really lucky for the Han Dynasty to exist.
It would be unwise to let the enemy possess capital that could endanger the Han Dynasty.
Although King Li's four sons were separated, they had the same idea of ​​avenging their father.
Give them a lot of people and enable them to accumulate a lot of property. If they do not openly raise armies in the capital to avenge like Wu Zixu and Bai Gong, there will be assassinations like Zhuanzhu and Jingke. This is the so-called lending weapons to thieves and giving wings to tigers.
I hope your Majesty will give it some thought!
Liang Wang Liu Sheng fell from his horse and died. Jia Yi lamented that he had failed in his duty as a tutor and often cried. More than a year later, he also died.
Jia Yi was thirty-three years old when he died.
Four years later, King Qi Wen died without a son.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty remembered Jia Yi's words, so he divided Qi into six small kingdoms and made King Hui's six sons king respectively. He also transferred Huainan King Liu happy to Chengyang, divided Huainan into three small countries, and made King Li's six sons king respectively.
In the next ten years, Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty died and Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty succeeded to the throne. In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Wu, Chu, Zhao and the four Qi kings jointly rebelled and marched westward to the Mojing city of Chang'an. Liang Xiao Wang Liu Wu defended Chang'an and finally defeated the Seven Kingdoms.
By the time of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the son of King Li of Huainan became king, and some of the two rebelled against him and were executed.
Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty ascended the throne and appointed Jia Yi's two grandsons as prefects of the county.
summary: Jia Yi later proposed strengthening the kingdoms of Huaiyang and Liang to counter powerful princes like Huainan. He warned against granting titles to the sons of the rebellious King Li of Huainan, predicting they would seek revenge. Emperor Wen partially adopted his advice, appointing Liu Wu as King of Liang. After Jia Yi's death at thirty-three, his predictions came true: the Seven Kingdoms rebelled, but Liang's strength helped suppress them. Emperor Wu later executed some of King Li's sons for rebellion. The historian praised Jia Yi's insights on governance, comparing him to Yi Yin and Guan Zhong. Though his ideas were only partially implemented, his writings on statecraft were influential. His early death prevented him from reaching high office, but his legacy endured through his fifty-eight essays.

translation:
Jia Shan is from Yingchuan.
His grandfather Jia Qu was a doctoral student of King Wei during the Warring States Period.
Jia Shan studied under Jia Qu, and his remarks were widespread in various schools of thought, but he could not specialize in Confucianism.
He once worked under Marquis Yingyin as a riding attendant.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, Jia Shan used Qin as an example to talk about the way to control chaos. He titled it "Zhi Yan" and said this:
I heard that as a minister, you should use your wholeheartedness and wisdom to advise your superior directly, even if you don't hesitate to behead him. This is what I did with Jia Shan.
I dare not give examples that are too far back. I would like to use Qin as an example. I hope your majesty will pay more attention to it.
People who are poor and humble can cultivate their own moral character, become famous in the world, and make future generations prosperous.
But the Qin Dynasty was not like this. With the dignity of the emperor and the great wealth in the world, it imposed tyranny and extorted money, which made the people tired of coping. The roads were filled with criminals, and there were hordes of thieves in the mountains and fields. Everyone in the world was eager to cause chaos.
One person raised his arms and shouted, and the whole country responded, creating the anti-Qin movement initiated by Chen Sheng.
Not only that, the Qin Dynasty also built more than 300 palaces from Xianyang to the west to Yongcheng, and added bells, drums and curtains to them, so that they can be enjoyed everywhere without having to remove them from elsewhere.
He also built the Epang Palace, which was dozens of feet high, five miles long from east to west, and a thousand paces wide from north to south. Cars and horses could gallop through it without any hindrance, and even the flags on the carriages could not be crooked.
He built such a magnificent palace, but his descendants did not even have a house to stay in.
He also built roads leading to various places, reaching as far as Yanqi, Wuchu in the south, the rivers and lakes, and the shores of the East China Sea, reaching everywhere.
The road is fifty steps wide, with trees planted every three feet. A thick wall is built outside the road, tamped with iron vertebrae, and green pine trees are planted.
Building such a spectacular road has left no room for future generations to pass through.
The Lishan Mausoleum, where the First Emperor was buried after his death, took ten years to build with the labor of hundreds of thousands of prisoners under the supervision of officials.
The tomb is deep, with spring water flowing down from it. Ore is collected, copper is smelted and the inner wall is cast to seal it. The outside is painted with raw lacquer and decorated with pearls, jade and jade. There are palaces and other playgrounds inside the tomb, and vegetation is planted on the tomb, just like a mountain forest. Building such a luxurious mausoleum deprived his descendants of even a small earthen grave with grass growing there.
Qin, with its strong national power, was as greedy as tigers and wolves, cannibalizing the princes and swallowing up the world without committing to the implementation of etiquette and justice, so the heaven sent disasters to punish it.
I'm risking my life to tell you. I hope you'll pay attention and carefully choose where it makes sense.
