summary: Jia Shan, from Yingchuan, studied under his grandfather Jia Qu and was known for his broad knowledge across various schools of thought, though he did not specialize in Confucianism. He served as a riding attendant under Marquis Yingyin. During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Jia Shan used the Qin Dynasty as a cautionary example to discuss governance, titling his work "Zhi Yan." He criticized Qin's tyranny, excessive construction of palaces like Epang, extravagant roads, and the lavish Lishan Mausoleum, which drained resources and oppressed the people, leading to widespread rebellion. He emphasized the importance of loyal ministers and open communication, warning that rulers who suppress criticism and act tyrannically risk losing their realm. Jia Shan urged the emperor to adopt benevolent policies, listen to advice, and avoid Qin's mistakes.

translation:
In ancient times, ministers were courteous and unobtrusive, so the monarch did not always appear very serious and intimidating.
Ministers cannot have fun with the monarch, and upright and honest people cannot go hunting with the monarch. Instead, they should devote themselves to their own duties and cultivate noble moral integrity. In this way, the ministers will not dare not correct their conduct, strengthen their self-cultivation, and perform solemn etiquette with all their heart.
In this way, your monarchy will be respected, your achievements will be promoted throughout the world, and passed down to future generations.
If you don't do this, your character and honor will be damaged day by day.
I secretly feel pity that the moral character cultivated by the wise men at home was destroyed in the emperor's court.
Your Majesty, you can have fun with the ministers, and discuss state affairs with the ministers and founders in the court.
The most important principles are to patrol without being disappointed, to go to court without being disrespectful, and to discuss politics without failing in policy.
Later, Emperor Wen abolished the law prohibiting private coinage, and Mai Shanyi wrote a letter to remonstrate, believing that it was wrong to change the former emperor's law.
He also appealed to the King of Huainan, believing that he was not guilty of any serious crime and that he should be returned to his own kingdom immediately instead of being exiled.
He also said that the prince of Chaiwu, the Marquis of Jipu, had evil intentions and deserved to be warned.
Emperor Wen asked the relevant departments to question Maishan about the content of the petition. When answering the question, Maishan believed that: although money is a useless thing, it can be used to exchange for wealth.
Wealth and honor are the emperor's handle for governing the world. Allowing the people to mint their own money means letting the people and the emperor hold this handle together, and it will be difficult to maintain it for a long time.
Maishan's remonstrance was urgent and good at getting to the point of the matter, but Emperor Wen never punished him in order to open up the road to remonstration.
Later, private coinage was banned again. Zou Yang, a native of Qi.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, the princes and kings personally governed the people and recruited talents.
King Wu Liu Bi recruited lobbyists from all over the country. Zou Yang, Yan Ji and Mei Cheng of Wu State all served as officials in Wu State. All three of them were famous for their ability to write articles and be good at debating.
After a long period of time, the King of Wu was dissatisfied because his prince was playing chess with Liu Qi, the prince of Emperor Wen at that time. The two had a dispute and the prince of Wu was beaten to death by Liu Qi. So he was dissatisfied and claimed that he was ill and could not go to court to see the emperor. He secretly had a conspiracy to rebel. Zou Yang wrote a letter to advise him.
Because the rebellion was not yet clear and could not be directly accused, I first used Qin as a metaphor, and then transferred to the speculation that Hu, Yue, Qi, Fang, Huainan, etc. were in trouble with the Han court, and then expressed my true intention.
The remonstrance is written like this:
I heard that the First Emperor of Qin was sitting in the Qutai Palace, imposing laws on the world, and drawing the boundaries of the land, but no one dared to offend, and the military power was imposed on Hu Yue; and when the Qin Dynasty declined, Zhang Er and Chen Sheng united with various soldiers and horses to attack Hangu Pass, thereby endangering Xianyang City.
Why is this happening?
Because the counties did not attach themselves to the Qin Dynasty, the people did not help the Qin Dynasty.
summary: Jia Shan also highlighted the Qin Dynasty's failure to maintain stability despite its vast power, contrasting it with the Zhou Dynasty's more moderate rule. He noted that Qin's harsh laws and exploitation led to its downfall, while wise rulers like King Wen of Zhou attracted talented ministers through benevolence. He advised the emperor to cultivate virtue, reduce punishments, and encourage honest counsel. Later, Jia Shan opposed Emperor Wen's decision to allow private coinage, arguing it would undermine imperial authority. Despite his urgent remonstrations, Emperor Wen did not punish him, aiming to keep open the path for advice.

translation:
His beloved son Liu Yi was granted the title of King of Liang, Liu Wu was granted the title of acting king, and Huaiyang was merged into the Liang Kingdom.
As a result, the King of Jibei was executed for treason, and his younger brother Liu Chang, King of Huainan, was exiled because of his guilt and died in Yong County. Isn't this because there were treacherous ministers like Xinyuan Ping in the two countries who persuaded the king to rebel? The current emperor has just inherited the late emperor's mission. He plans Shandong on the left and controls Guanzhong on the right. He has changed his plans and the ministers are unpredictable.
Your Majesty, if you do not investigate, I am afraid that the people who are planning for Wu will make wrong suggestions just like Xinyuan Ping lied about getting Zhou Ding in the Han court. If so, our country of Wu will be destroyed, the family will be destroyed, and the descendants will be extinct.
Emperor Gao burned down the plank road and poured water into Zhanghan. He destroyed everything he attacked. He gathered the exhausted people without stopping and rushed eastward out of Hangu Pass, defeating the army of Xiang Yu, the overlord of Western Chu.
Attack by water, Zhang Han lost the city, attack on land, Xiang Yu lost the territory, the Han Dynasty was stable, and the princes could not have any evil intentions.
I hope your Majesty will give it more thought.
The king of Wu did not listen to him.
At this time, King Liang Xiao, the younger brother of Emperor Jing, gained power and recruited scholars. So Zou Yang, Meicheng, and Yan Ji all knew that King Wu could not accept the advice, so they left King Wu and went to Liang to have friends with King Liang.
Zou Yang is very strategic and has a strong temperament. He is uncompromising and independent. He is independent between Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui.
Yang Sheng and others hated him and slandered him in front of King Liang.
King Liang was very angry and threw Zou Yang into prison, preparing to kill him.
Zou Yang was traveling in a foreign country and was slandered and arrested. He was afraid that he would leave a bad reputation after his death and be reviled by others, so he wrote to the King of Liang from prison:
I heard that loyalty is always rewarded, and honest people will not be suspected. I have always thought this is the case, but now it seems that it is just empty words.
In the past, Jing Ke admired the faith of Prince Dan of Yan, and his sincerity moved heaven, so that a white rainbow passed through the sun, but Prince Dan was afraid that Jing Ke would not assassinate the King of Qin; Mr. Wei planned the strategy of the Changping Battle for Qin, and the Taibai Star entered the Pleiades, covering up the brilliance of the Pleiades stars, but King Zhao of Qin expressed doubts.
The sincere heart caused the heaven and earth to mutate, but could not make Prince Dan and King Qin Zhao believe in them. Isn't this very sad!
Now I am sincerely stating my plan, hoping that you will know it, but your ministers are unclear, and finally I was interrogated by the judge and became suspicious of the world.
The creation is like Mr. Jing Ke and Mr. Wei being reborn, but Prince Dan and King Qin Zhao are still unaware.
I hope your Majesty will take a closer look.
In the past, Bian He offered jade to the King of Chu, but the King of Chu did not know the goods and punished Bian He instead. Li Si was loyal to Qin, but was severely tortured by Hu Hai.
Therefore, Jizi pretended to be crazy and took Yu to escape from the world because he was afraid of suffering such a disaster.
I hope that your Majesty, you will examine the sincerity of Bian He and Li Si, and do not listen to wrong opinions like King Chu and Hu Hai, and do not let me be laughed at by Ji Zi and Jie Yu.
I heard that Bigan was betrayed for his loyalty, and Wu Zixu was killed for his direct remonstrance. Put it into the horse leather, I didn't believe it at first, but now I understand.
I hope your Majesty will consider this in detail and show some sympathy.
summary: Zou Yang, a native of Qi, served under King Wu Liu Bi of Wu. When the king harbored rebellious intentions after his son's death, Zou Yang wrote a letter advising against rebellion, using Qin's fall as a warning. He argued that unity and loyalty to the Han court were essential, warning that rebellion would lead to destruction. When King Wu ignored him, Zou Yang joined King Xiao of Liang. However, he was slandered and imprisoned. From prison, he wrote to King Liang, citing historical examples of loyal ministers who were misunderstood, such as Jing Ke and Bian He, and urged the king to trust his sincerity. King Liang eventually released him and made him a guest.

translation:
Zhang Yu and Han Anguo led their troops to the north of Wu Bing, and Gonggao Hou Han Daidang led his troops to the left and right of Wu Bing. Wu Bing could not capture Liang's castle, and the soldiers could not rest well. I was secretly sad.
I hope your Majesty you will think about it again and again.
King Wu did not take Mei Cheng's advice and was eventually killed.
After the Han Dynasty put down the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms, Meicheng became famous for it.
Emperor Jing summoned Meicheng and appointed him as the captain of Hongnong County.
Meicheng had been a distinguished guest of the princes and great powers for a long time, and he had socialized with heroes, which was very satisfactory to him. He did not like being a county official, so he resigned due to illness.
Meicheng visited Liang again. The guests of Liang State were all good at writing essays and poems, and Mei Cheng was the best.
After the death of King Xiao of Liang, Meicheng returned to Huaiyin County.
Emperor Wu had heard of Mei Cheng's reputation since he was the crown prince. When he ascended the throne as emperor, Mei Cheng was already old, so Emperor Wu used an "an chariot" wrapped in cattails to recruit him, but died of illness on the way.
Emperor Wu issued an edict to inquire about Mei Cheng's sons, but none of them were good at writing articles. Only later did he find his son Mei Gao, who was born to his concubine.
Meigao, named Shaoru. When Mei Cheng was in the Liang Kingdom, he took Mei Gao's mother as his concubine.
When Mei Chengshu returned to Huaiyin County, Mei Gao's mother was unwilling to follow Mei Cheng. Mei Cheng was furious and gave Meigao several thousand dollars, leaving him to live with his mother.
When Meigao was seventeen years old, he wrote to the King of the Communist Party and was called to be a Langguan.
Three years later, Meigao was on a mission to a certain place for King Liang Gong. He had a conflict with the King of Liang's attendants. He was slandered by the King of Liang's attendants and was convicted. His family members were taken into the government and their property was confiscated.
Meigao fled to Chang'an.
Just in time for the emperor to grant amnesty to criminals, Mei Gao wrote to the emperor in Beique, saying that he was Mei Cheng's son.
When the emperor learned about this, he was very happy. He called him into the palace to receive him and asked him to obey the imperial edict. Mei Gao then wrote a poem in the palace.
Emperor Wu issued an edict asking him to compose a poem for Pingle Hall. After the poem was written, Emperor Wu appreciated it and appointed him Lang Guan, sending him as an envoy to the Huns.
Meigao did not know the classics, he talked and laughed like a haiku actor in a variety show, and he also liked to use frivolous and indecent words when writing poems and poems. Therefore, he won the favor of the emperor and a high position of power because of his comedy and lack of solemnity. He was on par with Dongfang Shuo, Guo Sheren, etc., but he could not obtain high officials like Yan Zhu and others.
Emperor Wu had a son when he was twenty-nine years old, and all the officials were very happy. Therefore, Mei Gao and Dongfang Shuo wrote a poem for the birth of the crown prince and wrote "Mei Zhu" for the establishment of the prince. Because they were written under the emperor's order, they could not use teasing and disrespectful words to respect the prince.
When Wei Zifu was established as queen, Meigao presented her with a gift and warned her to be cautious about ending as she began.
Mei Gao was better than Dongfang Shuo in writing poems.
Meigao followed Emperor Wu to Ganquan Palace, Yongxian County, and Hedong County, toured the east, held a Zen ceremony in Mount Tai, blocked the Yellow River in Xuanfang, had fun in various palaces in the Sanfu area, traveled to the mountains to enjoy the scenery, shot birds and beasts, rode chariots and dogs, played Cuju and carved carvings. Whenever Emperor Wu felt emotional, he asked Meigao to write a poem to express his feelings.
Meigao wrote articles very quickly, and every time there was an edict, it could be completed immediately, so he wrote many poems and poems.
Sima Xiangru was also good at writing articles, but he wrote very slowly, so he did not have many poems, but the quality was higher than that of Mei Gao.
In his poems, Meigao admitted that he was not as good as the poems written by Sima Xiangru. He also said that writing poems was the specialty of opera performers. He was regarded as a haiku and was not respected. He was annoyed that he was similar to a haiku.
So he wrote a poem to mock Dongfang Shuo and himself.
His poems are full of twists and turns, and they follow the situation. He always grasps the key points without losing the original intention, and is humorous and humorous without being too graceful and gentle.
There are one hundred and twenty chapters that can be read, but there are dozens more that are too frivolous and inelegant to be read.
Lu Wenshu, also known as Changjun, was from Shuli, Julu County.
summary: Mei Cheng, from Huaiyin, also served King Wu and advised him against rebellion, warning that the Han Dynasty's strength far exceeded Wu's. He used metaphors like a thread holding a heavy weight to illustrate the danger of rebellion. When King Wu persisted, Mei Cheng left for Liang. After Emperor Jing ascended, Chao Cuo's policies provoked the Seven Kingdoms' rebellion. Mei Cheng again advised King Wu to withdraw, but the king refused and was eventually killed. Mei Cheng later served King Xiao of Liang and became famous for his writings. Emperor Wu later summoned him, but he died en route.

translation:
This is one of the ten major faults of the Qin Dynasty that exists to this day.
I heard that where the eggs of crows and owls are not harmed, the phoenix will fall; the crime of slandering the monarch will not be punished, and only then will someone give honest advice.
Therefore, someone in ancient times said: The mountains have vegetation and poisonous things live in them; the rivers and lakes are vast and can accommodate muddy water; and the beautiful jade contains slight flaws. A ruler who is good at controlling his ministers should also tolerate the shame of being criticized.
As long as you exempt those who slander the monarch from the blame and accept straightforward advice, open up the channels of speech, eliminate the mistakes that led to the fall of Qin, follow the virtuous policies of King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, reduce legal provisions, relax penalties, and abolish the prison of torture, then the age of peace and prosperity will come, with eternal peace and happiness, coexisting with heaven and earth, and everyone in the world will feel infinite joy.
Emperor Xuan appreciated Lu Wenshu's petition and promoted him to the position of head of Guangyang's private palace.
The internal history recommended Lu Wenshu as the first-class scholar in literature, and he was promoted to You Fufeng Cheng.
At that time, the emperor issued a Shao letter instructing the ministers to recommend people who could be sent as envoys to the Huns. Lu Wenshu submitted a letter, requesting that he be sent as an entourage to accompany the envoys on missions to the Huns in order to serve the emperor. The emperor reviewed the letter and forwarded it to General Fan Mingyou and his servant Du Yannian to inquire about the situation. Because his words were unreasonable, he returned to the Forbidden City.
A long time later, he was promoted to the prefect of Linhuai County. His political performance was very outstanding, and he died in office.
Lu Wenshu, who had learned almanac and astronomy from his grandfather, believed that the Han Dynasty would encounter a great disaster around 210 years after the founding of the People's Republic of China, so he secretly wrote to the emperor to take precautions.
When he became emperor, Gu Yong also said the same thing.
When Wang Mang usurped the throne and announced to the world the basis of Dai Mo, he publicized these words.
Lu Wenshu's sons and grandsons all became high-ranking officials such as state pastor and prefect.
Praise says: In the Spring and Autumn Period, Zang Sunda of the Lu State admonished the monarch with etiquette and righteousness. People with high moral character believed that his descendants would be prosperous.
Maishan pointed out the emperor's faults from below, and Zou Yang and Mei Cheng traveled to kingdoms that were in danger of collapse, but they were able to avoid being tortured and killed because they strictly adhered to the right way of speaking.
Lu Wenshu speaks softly and is sincere, so his descendants will serve as high-ranking officials for generations to come. It’s only fitting!
summary: Lu Wenshu, from Julu, studied law and the Spring and Autumn Annals. During Emperor Xuan's reign, he wrote a memorial advocating benevolence and lighter punishments, criticizing the harsh legal system inherited from Qin. He argued that severe torture led to false confessions and injustice, undermining peace. He urged the emperor to follow the virtuous policies of King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, reduce penalties, and open channels for advice. Emperor Xuan appreciated his petition and promoted him. Lu Wenshu later served as prefect of Linhuai, where he performed excellently until his death. His descendants became high-ranking officials.

translation:
Zhao Chongguo, named Wengsun, was from Shangbang in Longxi. He later moved to Jincheng Lingju.
He was just a knight at the beginning, but later he was a member of a good family in six counties and was good at horseback riding and archery and was promoted to a guard of the feather forest.
He was calm and courageous, with profound strategies. When he was young, he liked the integrity of a general, so he went to study the art of war and became familiar with the affairs of the barbarians in all directions.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Zhao Chongguo followed the Second Division General as a fake Sima to attack the Xiongnu, and was heavily surrounded by the enemy.
The Han army was without food for several days and suffered many casualties. Zhao Chongguo and more than 100 strong men broke through the siege and captured the enemy's formation. The general of the Second Division led the soldiers to follow him, and they were able to escape the siege.
Zhao Chongguo suffered more than 20 injuries all over his body. General Ershi reported the situation to Emperor Wu, who ordered Zhao Chongguo to be summoned to the place where he was traveling. Emperor Wu personally received Zhao Chongguo and visited his injuries. He praised him, awarded him the title of Zhonglang, and promoted him to the post of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
During the reign of Emperor Zhao, the Di people in Wudu County rebelled. Zhao Chongguo led troops to attack and quelled the rebellion as a general to protect the army. He was promoted to Zhonglang General and led his troops to garrison in Shanggu County. After returning, he was appointed as the captain of Shuiheng.
Later, he went to attack the Xiongnu and captured King Xiqi. He was promoted to the post-general, and he still served as the captain of Shuiheng.
Zhao Chongguo and General Huo Guang decided to support Emperor Xuan and were named Yingpinghou.
During the Benshi period, he used the post of General Pulei to conquer the Xiongnu and killed hundreds of enemies. After returning the army, he was appointed as the Hou General and Shaofu.
The Xiongnu mobilized more than 100,000 cavalry and went south to approach the Han Dynasty border fortress. They reached Mount Fuxi and prepared to invade and plunder.
Tichu Qutang, who had escaped from the Xiongnu, surrendered to the Han Dynasty and told the story. The Han Dynasty sent Zhao Chongguo to lead 40,000 cavalry to garrison the nine counties on the border.
After Shanyu heard what had happened, he led his troops and left.
At this time, Guanglu doctor Yiqu Anguo was on an envoy to inspect various Qiang tribes. The chief Xianling expressed his hope to cross the river to the north bank of the Huangshui River at a certain time to find places where Han people did not cultivate their livestock.
Anguo reported the dispatch to the emperor.
Zhao Chongguo impeached Anguo for the crime of disrespect after being ordered to send an envoy.
After that, the Qiang people violated Han law and crossed the Huangshui River as mentioned above, but the counties and counties could not stop them.
In the third year of Yuankang, Xianling resolved his grudges with more than 200 Qiang chiefs, exchanged hostages and signed an oath of alliance.
After the emperor learned about this, he consulted Zhao Chongguo. Zhao Chongguo replied: The reason why the Qiang tribe was easily suppressed is because each tribe has its own leader. They often attack each other and their forces cannot be unified.
More than 30 years ago, when the Xiqiang people created the Han Dynasty, they resolved their enmities in advance and made an alliance to attack Lingju and compete with the Han Dynasty. It took five or six years to calm down.
In the fifth year of Zhenghe, Xianling leader Feng Jian and others sent envoys to the Xiongnu, and the Xiongnu sent envoys to Xiaoyueshi. Rumors told the tribes that: General Ershi of the Han Dynasty led more than 100,000 people to surrender to the Xiongnu.
The Qiang people had a hard time serving the Han Dynasty.
Digging? The land was originally our place, the land was fertile, and we could attack and occupy it together. From this, we can see that Bao Xi wanted to unite with the police for a long time.
Not long ago, the west side of Lisu was trapped. Hearing that Wudan was coming to defend the frontier, and fearing that the war would start from the east, he sent envoys to Weili and Weisu countries many times, promising to give them men and women and mink clothes, in an attempt to alienate the friendly relationship between them and Lian.
summary: Zhao Chongguo, styled Wengsun, was from Shangbang in Longxi and later moved to Jincheng Lingju. He began as a knight, was promoted to a guard of the feather forest for his skill in horseback riding and archery, and was known for his calm courage and strategic depth. He studied military strategy and became familiar with barbarian affairs. Under Emperor Wu, he served as a fake Sima under the Second Division General against the Xiongnu, breaking through an enemy siege with over 100 strong men despite heavy casualties and over 20 wounds. Emperor Wu personally honored him, appointing him Zhonglang and later General of Chariots and Cavalry. Under Emperor Zhao, he quelled a Di rebellion in Wudu, was promoted to Zhonglang General, and later captured Xiongnu King Xiqi, becoming a post-general. He supported Emperor Xuan’s ascension with Huo Guang and was named Yingpinghou. During the Benshi period, he led a campaign against the Xiongnu, killing hundreds, and was appointed Hou General and Shaofu. When the Xiongnu mobilized over 100,000 cavalry near the border, Zhao Chongguo led 40,000 cavalry to garrison nine counties, causing the Shanyu to retreat. He later impeached Yiqu Anguo for disrespect after Anguo mishandled Qiang affairs. In the third year of Yuankang, Qiang chief Xianling formed alliances, and Zhao Chongguo warned of potential rebellion, citing past Qiang uprisings and Xiongnu collusion. He advised preparations, but Anguo’s subsequent actions—killing over 30 Qiang leaders and attacking their tribes—provoked a widespread Qiang revolt. Zhao Chongguo, over 70, was tasked with leading the campaign. He insisted on personal command, saying “seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times,” and Emperor Xuan agreed.

translation:
The enemies of the Xianling Qiang wanted to betray the Han Dynasty, so they made an alliance with the Han Qiang and Kai Qiang to dissolve their former enemies. However, in their hearts they had to be afraid that the Han army would betray them when Houhan and Kai Qiang arrived.
The minister foolishly believed that Xianling Qiang's strategy was often to go to Hanqiang first and open the Qiang's critical situation to strengthen their alliance. If they attacked Hanqiang first, Xianling would definitely come to their aid.
Now that the enemy's horses are fat and their food and grass are plentiful, attacking him will probably not cause any harm to them. This will allow Xian Ling to show kindness to the Han Qiang, allowing them to strengthen their alliance and unite their party members.
If the enemy makes a strong alliance and unites their party members, their elite troops can reach more than 20,000 people. If they coerce other weak tribes, the number of people who will join them will gradually increase, and small tribes like Mosu will not leave easily.
If this is the case, the enemy's strength will gradually increase, and it will take several times the force to kill them. I am afraid that the country's worries and burdens will take ten years to calculate, not two or three years.
The ministers were favored by the emperor, and both father and son were important officials of the court.
The minister's official position reaches Jiuqing. I have reached the rank of lord and am seventy-six years old. I threw my body into a ditch in pursuit of a wise edict. Even though I am immortal, I have nothing to worry about.
I just consider that I am most familiar with the advantages and disadvantages of using troops, so as a minister, I attack the zeros first and then conquer the Han Qiang, Ji Qianqiang and so on without using troops.
After the Ling Qiang was killed, the Han Qiang and Kai Qiang still refused to surrender. They waited until the first month to attack them, which not only had the rationale for using troops, but also the timing of using troops.
It is really not profitable to march at this time, so I hope your Majesty will make a clear decision.
In June, Wushen submitted a memorial, and in July, Emperor Jiayin sealed a letter to Zhao Chongguo telling him to follow his strategy.
Zhao Chongguo led his troops to where Xianling Qiang was.
The enemy had been stationed for a long time and relaxed their vigilance. When they saw the large army, they abandoned their vehicles and baggage and wanted to cross the Huangshui River. The road was narrow, so Zhao Chongguo marched slowly to catch up with the enemy.
Some people say that chasing and winning should be fast, but it is too slow to move forward like this. Zhao Chongguo said: This is the so-called pursuit of poor enemies.
If you pursue slowly, they will run away without looking back; if you pursue them too quickly, they will turn back and fight to the death. All the captains said: OK.
Hundreds of people were drowned by the enemy. More than 500 people surrendered or were beheaded. More than 100,000 horses, cattle and sheep were captured, and more than 4,000 vehicles were captured.
When the army arrived at a place where the Qiang were rare, they were ordered not to burn villages and not to cut grass in the fields for grazing.
After hearing this, the Han and Qiang people said happily: The Han army will not attack us as expected!
The leader Miwang sent someone to say: I hope to return to the original place.
Zhao Chongguo reported this to the emperor, but received no answer.
Mi Wang came to surrender in person, and Zhao Chongguo gave him food and drink and let him go back to inform his people.
The officers below the guard army all argued with Zhao Chongguo about this matter, saying: "This is a traitor and we cannot let him go without permission."
Zhao Chongguo said: You just want to completely comply with the official document and plan for your own sake, not for the sake of loyalty to the country.
Before he finished speaking, the seal came down, ordering Mi Wang to be punished as atonement.
Later, Hanqiang was finally conquered without any troops.
In the autumn of this year, Zhao Chongguo fell ill, and the emperor sent a letter saying: General after issuing the imperial edict: I heard that you are suffering from pain in your legs and feet, and the wind and cold are coming down. The general is old and sick, and I cannot hide the changes. I am very worried about this.
Now Shao ordered General Po Qiang to arrive at the station. As the general's deputy, he quickly took advantage of the favorable weather and the vigor of the officers and soldiers to attack Xianling Qiang in December.
If the condition is serious, you can stay at the station and only send Poqiang and Qiannu generals.
By this time, more than 10,000 Qiang people had surrendered.
Zhao Chongguo considered that the enemy would definitely fail, so he prepared to withdraw his cavalry to garrison the fields to wait for the enemy to be trapped.
Before the memorial was written and reported, the seal requesting the march was received. General Zhao Yin of Zhonglang was frightened, so he sent his disciples to admonish Zhao Chongguo, saying: "Ordering the army to attack will really cause the army to suffer defeat. If the general is killed and the country is in danger of overthrow, it is okay for the general to stand firm."
summary: At Jincheng, Zhao Chongguo crossed the Yellow River cautiously, avoiding enemy traps. He prioritized reconnaissance, fortifications, and soldier welfare, refusing to engage in small skirmishes. His son Zhao Yin led reinforcements, but Zhao Chongguo advocated a strategy of kindness and power, recruiting Qiang tribes like Han and Kai to disrupt enemy plans. Emperor Xuan assembled 60,000 troops, but Zhao Chongguo opposed a proposed attack by Xin Wuxian, arguing it risked logistical failure and enemy ambush. He recommended a defensive approach, focusing on farming and waiting for the enemy to weaken. Despite imperial pressure, Zhao Chongguo submitted a memorial detailing a plan to withdraw cavalry and station 10,281 soldiers for farming, listing twelve benefits including cost savings, enemy attrition, and border security. Emperor Xuan eventually approved his strategy.

translation:
Ruo Ling and Di Ze were named Shuai Wang, Liliu and Qizhong were named Marquis, Erku was named Lord, Yang Diao was named Yan Binghou, Liang Er was named Lord, and Mi Wang was named Xian Niu Lord.
Wen Shi set up the Jincheng vassal state to arrange the surrender of the Qiang people.
Shaoling elected people who could serve as captains to protect the Qiang. At this time, Zhao Chongguo fell ill, and all the four prefectures recommended Xin Wuxian's younger brother Xin Tang.
Zhao Chongguo got up in a hurry and reported: "Xin Tang is drunk and cannot be in charge of barbarian affairs. It is better to send Xin Tang's brother Xin Linzhong."
At that time, Xin Tang had already accepted Fu Jie and issued an edict to change his position to Xin Linzhong.
Later, Xin Linzhong was dismissed from office due to illness, and the Five Governments again recommended Xin Tang. Xin Tang often got drunk and cursed the Qiang people, so the Qiang people rebelled, and finally agreed to what Zhao Chongguo said.
At first, Po Qiang general Xin Wuxian often chatted with Zhao Yin, the Zhonglang general in the army. Zhao Yin said: Chariot general Zhang Anshi was not in line with Emperor Xuan's wishes at the beginning, and Emperor Xuan wanted to kill him. My general believed that Zhang Anshi had served Emperor Xiaowu for decades with a book bag in his hand and a brush in his hair. He was recognized as loyal and prudent, so he should be preserved.
Zhang Anshi was able to avoid death because of this.
When Zhao Chongguo came back and discussed military affairs with the emperor, Xin Wuxian was dismissed from office and returned to his original post. Feeling deeply resentful, he wrote a letter to sue Zhao Yin for leaking what was said in the palace.
Zhao Yin violated the ban and entered Sima Zhong, the shogunate of Zhao Chongguo, and disrupted the military regulations. He was sent to a judge for trial. He committed suicide.
Zhao Chongguo asked for retirement and was given a four-horse carriage, sixty pounds of gold, and was relieved of his duties and returned home.
Whenever there was a major discussion about Sebari, the imperial court often invited him to participate in military planning and asked him about plans and strategies.
He died at the age of eighty-six, two years after Ganlu died, and was given the title Zhuanghou.
The title was passed from his son to his grandson Zhao Qin, who married Princess Jingwu.
The princess had no son, so she asked Zhao Qin's husband Xi to pretend that she was pregnant, but in fact she was someone else's son.
Zhao Qin died, his son Zhao Cen succeeded to the throne, and Xi became the dowager.
Zhao Cen's biological parents had no end to their demands for money, so they resentfully reported on each other.
Zhao Cen was exempted from his title and fiefdom because he was not his biological son.
During the first year of the Yuan Dynasty, the descendants of the heroes were reborn and Zhao Ji, the great-grandson of Zhao Chongguo, was granted the title of Yinghuhou.
At the beginning, Zhao Chongguo painted his portrait in Weiyang Palace because his merits and virtues were comparable to Huo Guang's.
When he became emperor, there was an alarm in Xiqiang. The emperor missed the generals and ministers, commemorated and praised Zhao Chongguo, so he summoned Yang Xiong, a man from Huangmen, to write a eulogy next to Zhao Chongguo's portrait:
In the era of Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty who was wise and holy, there were Xianling in Rong and Di.
Xian Ling was rampant and invaded the western frontier of the Han Dynasty.
summary: Zhao Chongguo’s campaign succeeded: over 10,000 Qiang surrendered, and by the following year, only about 4,000 enemies remained. He was praised for his foresight, though his son Zhao Yin committed suicide after a dispute. Zhao Chongguo retired with honors and died at 86. His portrait was placed in Weiyang Palace, and a eulogy by Yang Xiong celebrated his achievements. The text also covers Xin Wuxian and his son Xin Qingji, noting their military roles and eventual decline under Wang Mang. The commentary reflects on the martial traditions of western regions like Tianshui and Longxi, attributing the prevalence of generals there to proximity to Qiang and Hu peoples.

translation:
Zhao Guang, whose Chinese name is Zidu, was a native of Liwu County, Zhuo County. Liwu County was originally part of the Hejian Kingdom.
When he was young, he worked as a county official and a state official. He was famous for his integrity, savvy, courtesy and corporal.
He was elected as Maocai and made a leveling order to manage market prices.
After assessment, he was appointed as the Yangdi Order.
Because his performance in managing government affairs was particularly outstanding, he was promoted to the rank of Lieutenant of Jingfu, acting as Jing Zhaoyin.
When Emperor Zhao died, Xinfeng Du Jian was appointed as Jingzhao and was responsible for the construction of Emperor Zhao's tomb.
Du Jian has always been a hero, and his guests made illegal profits from it. When Guanghan heard about this, he tactfully warned him in advance.
Du Jian refused to change, so the case was closed and punished.
Many powerful people and eunuchs interceded on his behalf, but Guanghan finally did not listen.
The clan and guests planned to kidnap Du Jian. Guanghan learned all of their plans and the name and residence of the mastermind. He sent officials to tell them: If they plot like this, the whole family will be destroyed.
He ordered all the officials to execute Du Jian in the busy city, but no one dared to approach him.
Everyone in the capital praised him.
At that time, Liu He, the king of Changyi, was summoned to Beijing to ascend the throne. He behaved lewdly. General Huo Guang and his officials deposed the king of Changyi and established Emperor Xuan.
Guanghan was given the title of Marquis of Guannei because he participated in the discussion and formulation of strategies.
Guanghan moved to Yingchuan as governor.
The Yuan and Chu tribes in the county were rampant and their guests broke the law and became thieves. None of the former officials of two thousand stone could capture and subdue them.
A few months after Guanghan arrived, he killed the evildoers led by Yuan and Chu. The people in the county were shocked and frightened.
In the end, Yingchuan heroes entered into marriages with each other, and the government and the people formed a party.
Guanghan was very worried about this matter, so he rewarded those who could use it and let them know the contents of the indictment in advance. When there was a case to be interrogated, and the charges had been obtained, he would punish them according to the law. Guanghan deliberately leaked their words to make them blame each other.
He also asked the officials to make a snitch bucket. When he received the letter, he cut off the name of the snitch and pretended to be a son of a hero.
From then on, powerful families became enemies, traitors were dispersed and defeated, and customs changed greatly.
Officials and common people came to complain and expose, and Guanghan could use them as eyes and ears. Therefore, thieves could not commit crimes, and they would be caught if they committed crimes.
Everything was managed, and Guanghan's reputation spread so widely that the surrendered Huns said that all the Huns had heard of Guanghan.
In the second year of this year, the imperial court sent five generals to attack the Xiongnu, and requisitioned Guanghan to lead the army as a prefect, subordinate to Pulei general Zhao Chongguo.
After returning from the army, he still acted as Jing Zhaoyin, and was actually awarded Jing Zhaoyin a year later.
As a Yin of the capital, Zhao Guanghan accepted scholars and looked good. He treated his subordinates with comfort and recommendation, and was diligent and diligent.
When he succeeded, he declined the credit and attributed it to his subordinates, saying: "It was a certain officer who did it, and it is not what I can do with two thousand stones."
summary: Zhao Guanghan, a native of Zhuo Commandery, began his career as a county and commandery official, known for his integrity and talent. He was elected as Maocai and served as a market price regulator before becoming the magistrate of Yangdi. His exceptional governance led to his promotion to Lieutenant of Jingfu and acting Jing Zhaoyin. After Emperor Zhao's death, he executed the corrupt Du Jian despite powerful intercessions, earning praise from the capital. He participated in deposing King Changyi and establishing Emperor Xuan, receiving the title of Marquis of Guannei. As Governor of Yingchuan, he suppressed the powerful Yuan and Chu clans and used innovative methods like the "snitch bucket" to break up local factions, restoring order. His reputation spread even to the Xiongnu.

translation:
Guanghan petitioned to increase the salary of the traveling wardens in Chang'an to a hundred shi. From then on, the subordinate officials who received a salary of a hundred shi were more self-respecting and did not dare to arrest people arbitrarily in violation of the law.
Jingzhao's politics were clear and clear, and officials and people were full of praise for him.
The elders rumored that no one who had managed Jingzhao since the rise of Bai Han could match him.
The official offices of Zuo Fengyi and You Fufeng were both located in Chang'an, and criminals often traveled to the boundaries of Jingzhao to commit crimes.
Guang Han sighed and said: Those who disrupt my management are often Zuo Fengyi and You Fufeng. If I can control the second assistant at the same time, it will be easier to govern Chang'an.
At the beginning, the general Huo Guang was in power, and Guanghan served Huo Guang.
After Huo Guang died, Guanghan knew the emperor's intentions and sent the Chang'an officials to lead him personally. They went with him to the residence of Huo Guang's son, Bolu Marquis Huo Yu. They broke into the palace gate, searched and arrested those who secretly slaughtered animals and sold wine, smashed Lu Yue with his spine, and cut off the door bolt with an axe.
Huo Guang's daughter was the queen at the time. When she heard about this incident, she cried to the emperor.
The emperor applauded this matter in his heart, so he only summoned Guanghan for questioning.
Guanghan offended his relatives and ministers.
Guang Hanping likes to appoint the young descendants of the old officials and blindly promote their strong and sharp spirit. When they see something happen, they can't avoid it. Most of them have the intention of making a decisive decision with him, and no one can support him in the crisis situation.
Guanghan eventually got into trouble because of this.
At first, a retainer from Guanghan was selling wine secretly in the Chang'an market, but the prime minister's officials drove him away. The retainer suspected that the man Su Xian had reported the matter, so he told Guang Han.
Guanghan sent Chang An Cheng to track down Su Xian, and Wei Shiyu therefore impeached Su Xian as a knight to station in Ba Shang, but he could not reach the station and lacked military supplies.
Su Xian's father filed a complaint against Guang Han, and the matter was dealt with again by the department. Yu was sentenced to death and asked to arrest Guanghan.
There was an edict to interrogate him on the spot, and Guanghanzhong surrendered. It happened that he was pardoned, and his salary was only reduced by one level.
Guanghan suspected that this incident was instigated by Rongwu, a man from Tongyi, and later killed Rongwu on other charges.
Someone wrote a letter to report this matter, and Emperor Xuan handed the case over to the prime minister and the imperial censor. The investigation was very urgent.
A Chang'an man who was closely trusted by the Guanghan faction served as a pawn in the prime minister's house and asked him to secretly inquire about illegal affairs in the prime minister's house.
In the middle of the seventh month of the third year of Dijie, the prime minister committed suicide by hanging himself with his maid.
Guanghan heard about this and suspected that the prime minister's wife had killed her in the mansion out of jealousy, while the prime minister was fasting to attend the ancestral temple for worship.
When Guanghan learned of the incident, he sent his lieutenant Zhao Fengshou to advise the prime minister, hoping to blackmail him and prevent him from pursuing his own affairs.
The Prime Minister refused to listen and the investigation became more urgent.
Guang Han wanted to report him, so he first asked Tai Shi, who knew the stars, and Tai Shi said that a minister would be killed this year, so Guang Han immediately wrote a letter to report the prime minister's crime.
The emperor ordered: Leave it to Jing Zhaoyin to handle.
Guanghan knew that the matter was urgent, so he led his troops to the prime minister's house, summoned the prime minister's wife to kneel in the court to listen to her speech, took away more than ten slaves, and interrogated them about killing the maid.
Prime Minister Wei Xiang wrote a letter stating: My wife did not kill her maid.
Guanghan committed many crimes and failed to acquit himself according to the law. He used deceptive means to coerce his minister Wei, but fortunately his minister Wei tolerated and did not complain.
I hope to send Qingming envoys to deal with the family affairs of the minister Wei Xiang confirmed by Guanghan.
The matter was handed over to the Tingwei. It was indeed the prime minister who whipped and expelled the maid because of his fault. The maid died after being driven out of the prime minister's house. This was not what Guang Han said.
Xiao Wang, the commander-in-chief, impeached him and said: "Guanghan insulted the ministers, wanted to threaten the prime minister, violated the law and harmed the morals. It was an unethical crime."
Emperor Xuan was disgusted with him and sent Guanghan to Tingwei Prison. He also killed innocent people, deliberately interrogated the case without knowing the truth, and arbitrarily rebuked the knights for their lack of armaments. The emperor approved his memorial.
Tens of thousands of officials and common people stood by the palace and wailed. Some said that the emperor's life was of no benefit to the imperial court, and were willing to die for Zhao Jingzhao so that he could live to support the people.
Guanghan was finally cut in half.
Although Guanghan was punished for breaking the law, he was an honest and upright person, restrained the powerful, and allowed the common people to take their own positions.
The people still miss him and praise him.
summary: As Jing Zhaoyin, Guanghan was diligent and generous, attributing successes to his subordinates. He was skilled in the "hook distance" method of investigation, uncovering crimes with precision. He once prevented a kidnapping by negotiating with the kidnappers and later treated them with dignity before their execution. He also exposed private affairs with uncanny accuracy, such as knowing a pavilion chief's message before it was delivered. He increased the salary of traveling wardens to prevent corruption, leading to a well-governed capital. However, after General Huo Guang's death, Guanghan raided his son's residence, offending the queen and powerful relatives. He eventually fell from favor after a series of conflicts, including a false accusation against the prime minister's wife. Despite his integrity and popularity among the people, he was executed by waist-cutting.

translation:
Yin Wenggui, named Zixiong, was originally from Pingyang, Hedong, and later moved to Duling.
Weng Gui lost his father when he was young and lived with Ji's father.
He works as a prison clerk and is familiar with the law.
He loves fencing and no one can resist him.
At this time, the general Huo Guang was in charge of the government. The Huo family lived in Pingyang. The slaves and guests of the family came to the market with swords and weapons to fight and cause chaos. The officials could not stop it. When Weng returned to work as a market official, no one dared to break the law and cause chaos.
He is fair and honest and does not accept gifts from concubines. Merchants are afraid of him.
Later he resigned and stayed at home.
It happened that Tian Yannian was the governor of Hedong and inspected various counties when he arrived in Pingyang. He summoned all the officials and soldiers in the past, fifty or sixty people.
After inspecting dozens of people, when it was Wenggui's turn, he fell to the ground alone and refused to get up. He replied: Wenggui is both civil and military, please arrange him.
The meritorious officer thought that this officer was arrogant and arrogant, so Yannian said: "What's the harm?"
So he called him forward to ask questions, and was surprised by his answers. He made him a soldier and followed him back to the county government.
Weng Gui inquired about the matter and exposed the adultery, and was able to tell the whole story. Yannian valued him very much and thought he was not as capable as Weng Gui, so he was transferred to acting postal supervisor.
There are twenty-eight counties in Heshu, which are divided into two parts. Hongru is in charge of the north of Fenshui, and Wenggui is in charge of the south of Fenshui.
Weng Gui acted in accordance with the law and arrested those who committed crimes. Even if the county magistrate secretly framed him, no one resented him.
After the assessment, he was appointed as the Lieutenant of the Feng family. He successively held various positions in the county. He managed the places he went to well. He was promoted to the imperial edict and became the Lieutenant of Hongnong.
He was appointed as the governor of Donghai and went to visit Yu Dingguo to bid farewell to the imperial officer.
Ding's country is in the East China Sea, and he wants to entrust the sons of two people from the same city to Weng Gui and let them sit in the back hall to wait for an audience.
Dingguo talked with Weng Gui for a whole day, but he did not dare to let the son of his fellow countryman come to see him.
After Weng Gui left, Dingguo said to Yizi: "He is a wise official. You don't know how to do things, and I can't ask for help based on personal relationships."
Weng Gui governs Shuhai and governs the Qingming Dynasty. We all know the virtuous and unvirtuous officials and people in the county, as well as their treacherous and evil crimes. Each county has its own registration book.
He personally handles the political affairs of each county. If there is an urgent order, he will delay it for a while; if the officials and people are slack, he will disclose the list of guilty persons.
Counties and counties arrested cunning officials and wealthy people, and after examination, they determined the charges, which could lead to the death penalty.
The arrests must be made during the official evaluation meetings in autumn and winter, and when going out to inspect various counties, not when there is nothing wrong.
He arrested people in order to convince the officials and the people to change their ways out of fear.
summary: Yin Wenggui, from Hedong, lost his father early and worked as a prison clerk. As a market official, he curbed the violence of Huo Guang's retainers. Governor Tian Yannian recognized his talent and appointed him to oversee half of the commandery's counties. He later served as Governor of Donghai, where he maintained detailed records of officials' conduct and arrested criminals during official meetings, instilling fear. He executed the cunning Xu Zhongsun, pacifying the region. As You Fufeng, he continued his strict governance, targeting the powerful while being lenient with the weak. He was known for his integrity and modesty, dying in office with no surplus property. The emperor praised him and granted gold to his family.

translation:
In the past, King Yan behaved unethically, and Han Yi stood up to remonstrate with him, but was killed by King Yan.
Han Yi did not have the same kinship with King Yan as King Zhou did than Gan did, but he practiced the same moral integrity as King Yan. His son should be greatly rewarded, so as to show the world and clarify the principles of being a minister.
Huo Guang accepted his suggestion and promoted Yanshou to the position of admonishing doctor and to the post of Huaiyang prefect.
Yanshou was very famous in politics and was transferred to Yingchuan.
Yingchuan has many powerful people and is difficult to govern, so the state often selects powerful governors for it.
Before that, he went to Guanghan to serve as the governor. He was worried about the local custom of gathering friends and forming cliques, so he made friends with officials and people and asked them to report on each other. This expedient was to keep a close eye on political affairs. As a result, Yingchuan's reporting became common and the people often became enemies.
Yanshou wanted to change this trend and educate the people with courtesy, but he was worried that the people would not follow suit, so he summoned dozens of county elders who were trusted and respected by the villagers one after another. He held a banquet and personally accompanied them. He told them his idea of ​​implementing etiquette, asked them about the folk songs and the people's sufferings, and told them the way to eliminate hatred with harmony and love.
The elders all thought it was very beneficial and could be implemented, so they jointly agreed on the etiquette and levels of weddings and funerals, which were roughly based on ancient rituals and must not exceed legal limits.
Yanshou then ordered the officials and students of the liberal arts school to wear leather benches and hold ceremonial utensils such as beans in their hands to conduct funerals, weddings and other ceremonies for officials and people.
The people followed his teachings and abandoned the imitation civil and wooden carriages and horses used for funerals on the road.
A few years later, Yanshou was transferred to the post of prefect of Shujun. Huang Ba replaced Yanshou to govern Yingchuan. Huang Ba followed his method and thus Yingchuan was established!
Very stable. To extend life and serve as an official, he advocates etiquette and righteousness, and likes ancient teachings. He must hire local wise men wherever he goes, treat and appoint them according to etiquette, expand plans, and accept advice; he praises the behavior of giving up money in mourning, and commends filial piety and brotherhood; When repairing city walls and collecting taxes and rents, we must first make clear the date when the announcement will begin, and start taking action within the specified time limit. Officials and people will respect and abide by the regulations.
He also appointed the chief and the fifth chief as an example of filial piety and brotherhood, and did not tolerate treacherous people.
Once an accident occurs in Banli Qianbai, the officials will receive a report and the traitors will not dare to enter its territory.
This approach seemed very cumbersome at first, but later the officials did not have the trouble of chasing criminals, and the people did not have to worry about being punished, and they were all content with this kind of governance.
Yanshou treated his officials with great kindness and clear rules.
If someone cheats and betrays him, he will deeply blame himself: Did I betray him? Why did he do this?
When the officials heard this, they secretly regretted it. His county captain died of white thorns.
There was a robbery at the back door, but he was saved from death. As a result, he became mute and could not speak.
When Yanshou heard about this, he cried to Fu Shi and sent officials to treat him and take care of him.
summary: Han Yanshou, from Handi, was promoted after his father died admonishing King Yan. As Governor of Yingchuan, he replaced Zhao Guanghan's confrontational methods with education in rites, consulting local elders and standardizing ceremonies. The people followed his teachings, abandoning lavish funerals. He later governed Shujun, hiring local worthies and promoting filial piety. He treated officials with kindness, blaming himself for their failures. As Zuo Fengyi, he resolved a land dispute by blaming himself, leading to the brothers' reconciliation. However, he was impeached for exceeding his authority and executed, despite public mourning. His sons resigned from office as he advised.

translation:
At this time, only a few days had passed in the winter months. The officials handling the case dealt with Xu Shun's case day and night, and finally sentenced him to death.
Xu Shun was about to go out to receive the death penalty. Zhang Chang sent the chief clerk to tell Xu Shun with a proclamation: What will the Beijing omen be like on the fifth day?
The winter months have passed, don’t you want to extend your life?
So he killed Xu Shun in the market.
At the beginning of spring, the messenger who had been wrongly imprisoned was traveling. Xu Shun's family carried his body, compiled Zhang Chang's proclamation, and filed a lawsuit against the messenger in person.
The envoy sent a memorial to Zhang Chang to kill innocent people. The emperor believed that his crime was very minor and wanted to exempt Zhang Chang from punishment. He first approved Zhang Chang's previous memorial that he should not be an official because of Yang Zang's crime, so that he could be exempted from being a commoner.
After the memorial for his dismissal was issued, Zhang Chang went to the palace to hand over his seal and ribbon, and then fled for his life under the palace palace.
After several months of encounters, the officials and people in the capital became lax, the alarm drums sounded frequently again, and thieves appeared in the Jizhou official offices.
The emperor remembered Zhang Chang's achievements in governance and sent envoys to his residence to recruit him.
Zhang Chang was severely impeached. When the envoy arrived, his wife and family were crying and frightened, but Zhang Chang simply smiled and said: I am already a fugitive, and the county officials are here to arrest me. Now that the envoy is here, the emperor wants to use me.
Immediately dressed up and followed the envoy to the bus, he wrote a letter saying: I was once fortunate enough to be a minister, but I was awaiting trial in Jingzhao. I was convicted of killing a thief and capturing Xu Shun.
Xu Shun was originally a minor official who was treated kindly by his minister Zhang Changhu. He had been favored and treated leniently many times.
In private, I used the law to execute Xu Shun in vain because of his unspeakable crimes.
The minister Zhang Chang killed innocent people, and the trial was intentionally unfair. Although he was punished by the law of the Ming Dynasty, he still died without complaint.
The emperor summoned Zhang Chang and appointed him as the governor of Jizhou.
Zhang Chang was appointed from exile and sent as an envoy to manage a state.
Zhang Chang arrived at the official office, but everyone in the Guangchuan Kingdom was unjust and rebellions broke out one after another, but he could not be captured.
Zhang Chang sent his spies to find out the names and residences of the rebel leaders, and killed their leaders.
The brothers of Wang Ji of Guangchuan and Liu Tiao, a member of the king's clan, usually protected them. The officials hunted them down until the end, and all traces of the rebels entered the palace.
Zhang Chang personally led the officials of the county and drove hundreds of vehicles to surround the palace and search for Liu Tiao and others. Sure enough, they were found among the heavy rafters of the palace.
Zhang Chang personally supervised the officials to kill them, cut off their heads, and hung them in the palace, so he impeached King Guangchuan.
The emperor could not bear to subject him to legal punishment and deprived him of his title.
Zhang Chang was in the official office for more than a year, and the thieves in Jizhou stopped him.
He was also tried as the governor of Taiyuan, and after one year he was promoted to full-time official, which brought stability to Taiyuan County.
Soon, Emperor Xuan died.
Emperor Yuan had just ascended the throne and was waiting for an edict. Zheng Peng recommended Zhang Chang as a famous minister of the late emperor and the most suitable teacher for the crown prince.
The emperor asked former general Xiao Wangzhi about this matter. Wangzhi believed that Zhang Chang was a capable official who was qualified to govern troubles, and that his frivolous qualifications were not suitable for being a master.
The emperor sent an envoy to recruit Zhang Chang, hoping to make him Zuo Fengyi.
It happened that Zhang Chang died of illness.
The family of the Taiyuan official whom Zhang Chang killed hated Zhang Chang and followed him to Duling to assassinate his second son Zhang Huang.
Zhang Chang's three sons all rose to the rank of captain.
At the beginning, Zhang Chang was appointed as Jing Zhaoyin, and his younger brother Zhang Wu was appointed as Liang's prime minister.
At that time, the king of Liang was arrogant and the people were so powerful that it was said to be difficult to govern.
Zhang Chang asked Zhang Wu: How do you want to govern Liang?
Zhang Wu was afraid of his elder brother and was too humble to say anything.
Zhang Chang sent officials to escort him to the pass and asked the officials to ask Zhang Wu themselves.
Zhang Wu replied: Those who drive cunning horses are good at using horse bits and whips. Liang is a big city and the officials and people are in decline. It is appropriate to use Zhu Huiwen to suppress and govern them.
During the Qin Dynasty, the prison official Dai Zhuhou Huiwen and Zhang Wu meant to manage Liang with criminal law.
When the officials came back and said these words, Zhang Chang smiled and said: "It is indeed like what Chu said, Zhang Wu will definitely manage Liang well."
When Zhang Wu reached the official position, he was very successful in governing and was also a capable official.
Zhang Chang's grandson, Zhang Chang, was the governor of the county during Wang Mang's reign, and was granted the title of marquis. He was more knowledgeable and elegant than Zhang Chang, but he was not as good as him in handling political affairs.
After Zhang Chang died, Zhang Chang had no descendants.
Wang Zun, whose courtesy name was Zigan, was from Gaoyang, Zhuo County.
summary: Zhang Chang, from Hedong, gained fame for admonishing King Changyi. He warned Emperor Xuan about the Huo family's power, advocating for their removal. As Governor of Shanyang, he requested to suppress bandits in Bohai, using rewards and amnesty to disperse them. He also advised the Empress Dowager to stop hunting. As Jing Zhaoyin, he recruited thief leaders to capture others, arresting hundreds in one day. He was known for his wit and leniency, but his frivolous behavior, like thrushing his wife's eyebrows, drew criticism. He served for nine years but was dismissed after killing a subordinate. He later governed Jizhou and Taiyuan, dying of illness. His brother Zhang Wu also governed Liang effectively. Wang Zun, from Zhuo Commandery, began as a prison clerk and studied the classics. As magistrate of Guo County, he executed an unfilial son by shooting. As Governor of Anding, he issued strict notices and killed the corrupt Zhang Fu, shocking the commandery. He was dismissed for excessive killings but later served as Governor of Yizhou, famously scolding his horse at a dangerous pass. As Prime Minister of Dongping, he confronted the arrogant king, who eventually avoided him. He impeached Prime Minister Kuang Heng for misconduct but was demoted. As Jing Zhaoyin, he eliminated bandits in Nanshan and executed powerful criminals, but was dismissed again. He later prevented a Yellow River flood by personally staying on the embankment, earning a promotion. He died in office, remembered by the people.

translation:
After Wang Zun was dismissed from office, his successor was incompetent and Wang Zhang was elected as Jing Zhaoyin.
At that time, the emperor's uncle, the general Wang Feng, assisted in political affairs. Although Wang Zhang was recommended by Wang Feng, he accused Wang Feng of being monopolistic and not close to Wang Feng.
It happened that there was a solar eclipse in the sun. Wang Zhang went to report to the emperor and was summoned. He said that Wang Feng could not be appointed and that loyal and capable ministers should be selected to assist the government.
The emperor initially accepted Wang Zhang's suggestion, but later he couldn't bear to dismiss Wang Feng.
Wang Zhang was suspected of this, so he was framed by Wang Feng and accused of treason.
This incident is recorded in the "Yuan Hou Zhuan".
At first, Wang Zhang was studying in Chang'an as a scholar, and he was the only one living with his wife.
Wang Zhang was seriously ill and lay in cow clothes without a quilt, crying and saying goodbye to his wife.
His wife angrily scolded him and said: Zhongqing, who is more distinguished in the imperial court than you?
Now that I am trapped by a serious illness, instead of encouraging myself, I start crying instead. How shallow!
Later, Wang Zhang held various official positions, and when he became King Zhaoyin, he wanted to submit a petition, but his wife stopped him and said: "People should be content. Don't you want to lie down in your cow's clothes and cry?"
Wang Zhang said: This is not something women should know.
The memorial was then entered, and as expected, he was sent to Tingwei's prison, and his wife and children were arrested.
Wang Zhang's youngest daughter, who was just twelve years old, woke up at night and cried loudly: "In the past, the jailer used to call the prisoners, and there were always nine prisoners, but now they stop calling when there are eight."
My father has always been upright, so he must be the first to die.
After questioning the next day, Wang Zhang was indeed dead.
His wife and children all moved to Hepu.
After the death of General Wang Feng, his younger brother Hou Shang of Chengdu became a general and assisted in political affairs. He informed the emperor that Wang Zhang's wife and children should return to their hometown.
His family members are all still alive, and pearl fishing has brought the property to millions. At that time, Xiao Yu was the prefect of Taishan and asked them all to redeem their original fields and houses.
Wang Zhang served as Jingzhao Yin for two years and died without punishment. The people thought he was wronged and commemorated him, so he was known as the Three Kings.
Wang Jun himself has a legend that Wang Jun is Wang Yang's son.
Zan said: Since Emperor Xiaowu established Zuo Fengyi, You Fufeng, and Jing Zhaoyin, the officials and the people have compiled a saying: There are Fang and Zhang in the front, and there are three kings in the back.
However, Liu Xiang's "New Preface" only wrote about the trip to Guanghan, Yin Wenggui, and Han Yanshou, Feng Shangxu's "Historical Records" wrote a biography of Wang Zun, and Yang Xiong's "Fayan" also praised Wang Zun.
Guanghan is wise and observant, and his subordinates cannot deceive him. Yanshou is strict and kind, and he can change customs wherever he goes. However, both of them revealed that their superiors were not trusted, so they lost their lives and ruined their achievements.
Weng Guijie was self-sufficient and dedicated to serving the public, which was a model for modern times.
summary: Wang Zhang, from Taishan, was a blunt admonisher who slandered Zhongshu Ling Shi Xian, leading to his dismissal. Recalled by Emperor Cheng, he became Sili Xiaowei and later Jing Zhaoyin. He accused General Wang Feng of monopolizing power, leading to his execution for treason despite his wife's warnings. His family was exiled but later returned. He served for two years and was mourned by the people. The text concludes that Zhao Guanghan, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Zhang Chang, Wang Zun, and Wang Zhang were notable officials, though some met tragic ends due to their integrity or conflicts with power.
