translation:
Li Shiqi was born in Gaoyang, Chenliu County.
He likes to study, but his family is poor and he has no job to obtain food and clothing.
He worked as a gatekeeper for the village, but neither the officials nor the powerful people in the county dared to use him, thinking that he was a wild young man.
When Chen Sheng, Xiang Liang and others revolted, various generals captured many areas. Dozens of them passed through Gaoyang County. Li Shiqi heard that these generals were narrow-minded, rigid about trivial etiquette, self-righteous, and unable to listen to good advice, so Li Shiqi hid.
Later, I heard that Pei Gong led his army to the suburbs of Chenliu. There was a cavalryman under Pei Gong who happened to be Li Shiqi's fellow villager. Pei Gong often asked him whether there were sages and heroes in the city.
When the knight returned home, Li Shiqi said to him: I heard that Pei Gong was arrogant and contemptuous of others, but he was very far-sighted. This is really the person I want to associate with. Let me introduce him first.
If you see Pei Gong, tell him: There is a gentleman named Li in my hometown, who is over sixty years old and eight feet tall. People think he is arrogant, but he himself said that I am not frivolous.
The cavalry said: Pei Gong does not like to associate with scholars. If any of the invited guests wears a Confucian hat, Pei Gong will take off his hat and urinate in the hat.
When talking to people, they often curse scholars, so don't talk like a Confucian scholar.
Li Shiqi said: Just say so.
The cavalryman calmly explained to Pei Gong as Li Shiqi had warned him.
Pei Gong arrived at the official residence in Gaoyang County and sent someone to summon Li Shiqi. When Li Shiqi arrived, Pei Gong sat on the bed and asked two women to wash his feet. This was how he summoned Li Shiqi.
When Li Shiqi entered the room, he handed over his hands without bowing and said: "Do you want to help Qin attack the princes?"
Or do you want to lead the princes to destroy the Qin Dynasty?
Pei Gong scolded: You despicable Confucian scholar!
The people of the world have suffered from Qin for a long time, so the princes led their troops to attack Qin one after another. How can you say you are helping Qin?
Li Shiqi said: If you want to gather the people and rally the rebels to overthrow the tyrannical rule of Qin, you should not sit by the bedside and summon the old man.
So Pei Gong stopped washing his feet, got up, put on his clothes, asked Li Shi to sit on his seat, and apologized to Li Shi.
Li Shiqi then talked about the situation when the six countries united. Pei Gong was very happy, gave Li food to eat, and asked: "Do you have any good plans?"
Li Shiqi said: You have gathered less than 10,000 untrained men. If you want to directly attack the powerful Qin State, it can be said that you are putting your hand into the tiger's mouth!
Chenliu County is located at the heart of the world and is connected in all directions. Now there is a lot of food stored in the city. I have always been friendly with the magistrate of Chenliu. Now please appoint me as your envoy to order him to surrender.
If he doesn't obey, you send troops to attack him, and I will respond internally.
So he sent Li Shiqi to Chenliu County, and Pei Gong led his troops to follow him, and finally captured Chenliu.
Pei Gong granted Li Shi the title of Lord of Guangye.
Li Shiqi recommended his younger brother Li Shang to lead thousands of people to follow Peigong to the southwest to seize land.
Li Shiqi often worked as a lobbyist, traveling among the princes to lobby.
summary: Li Shiqi of Gaoyang was a learned man from a poor family who worked as a village gatekeeper. When various rebel generals passed through Gaoyang during the uprisings against Qin, he hid from them, considering them narrow-minded. Upon hearing that Pei Gong (later Emperor Gaozu of Han) was far-sighted, Li Shiqi arranged an introduction through a fellow villager serving under Pei Gong. Despite Pei Gong's disdain for Confucian scholars, Li Shiqi boldly criticized him for washing his feet while receiving visitors. Pei Gong apologized, and Li Shiqi advised him to seize Chenliu County, which had abundant food stores. Li Shiqi persuaded the magistrate to surrender, and Pei Gong captured Chenliu, granting Li Shiqi the title of Lord of Guangye. Later, when the Han army was besieged, Li Shiqi urged the King of Han to seize Aocang's grain supplies and strategic positions. He then volunteered to persuade the King of Qi to submit to Han, successfully convincing Tian Guang to surrender. However, Han Xin attacked Qi anyway, and Tian Guang, believing Li Shiqi had deceived him, executed him.
rel_path: 汉书/传/郦陆朱刘叔孙传

translation:
In the past five years, the country has been peaceful. This is not the result of human power, but the work of God.
The emperor heard that the emperor was proclaimed king in South Vietnam and did not help the people of the world to eliminate the tyrannical forces. The general originally wanted to send troops to kill the emperor, but the emperor took pity on the people who had just finished their hard work and needed to rest and recuperate, so he sent me to grant the emperor the seal, divide the talisman letters, and exchange envoys.
The king should go to the outskirts to welcome him, and to the north to proclaim his vassalship, but you actually want to use this newly-established country with unpopular hearts and unconsolidated political power to claim strength here.
If the King of Han really hears about it, he will dig up and burn the graves of your ancestors, annihilate your clan, and send a lieutenant general to lead a hundred thousand people to attack Yue. The Yue people will kill the king and surrender to the Han. It will be easy to conquer.
So Wei Tuo stood up in shock and apologized to Lu Jia: "I have lived among barbarians for a long time. It is really rude."
So he asked Lu Jia: Who is better among me, Xiao He, Cao Shen, and Han Xin?
Lu Mai said: The king is wiser than them.
He asked again: Who is more worthy than the emperor?
Lu Jia said: The emperor raised troops in Fengpei to attack the violent Qin, destroyed the powerful Chu army, brought benefits and eliminated harm to the people of the world, inherited the great cause of the five emperors and three kings, unified the world, and governed the country.
The Central Plains has hundreds of millions of people and thousands of miles of land. It is the most fertile land in the world. It has a large number of people, prosperous carriages and horses, rich everything, and unified political power. It has never been seen since the beginning of the world.
Now the king's population is only tens of thousands, and they are all barbarians. They are located between rugged mountains and seas, just like a county in Han Dynasty. How can the king compare with the king of Han?
Wei Tuo laughed and said: I did not raise troops in the Central Plains, so I became king here.
If I were in the Central Plains, how could I be inferior to the Han people?
So he liked Lu Jia very much and kept him feasting for several months.
Said: There is no one in South Vietnam who can talk to me. Since my husband came, I heard things I had never heard before.
The jewelry Lu bought as a reward was worth thousands of gold, and the other gifts he gave were also worth thousands of gold.
Lu Jia finally worshiped Wei Tuo as the King of Nanyue and asked him to surrender to the Han Dynasty and obey the orders of the Han Dynasty.
Lu Jia came back and reported that the emperor was very happy and worshiped Lu Mai as Taizhong doctor.
Lu Jia often discussed "The Book of Songs" and "Book of Songs" in front of the emperor.
The emperor scolded him and said: You and I conquered the world on horseback, why do we study the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents?
Lu Mai said: If you can conquer the world on a horse, can you also rule the world on a horse?
Moreover, King Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou used force to seize the world but defended it with benevolence and righteousness. The combination of civil and military forces is the long-term way to govern the country.
In the past, the kings of Wu, Fu Chai and Zhi Bo, perished because of their aggressive military tactics. The Qin State, which blindly used criminal laws without changing them, finally perished.
If Qin can practice benevolence and righteousness after unifying the world and imitate the ancient sages, how can your majesty conquer the world?
Emperor Gao looked displeased and ashamed, so he said to Lu Jia: Please try to write for me the reasons why Qin lost the world and I was able to gain it, and the situations of successful and failed countries since ancient times.
summary: Lu Jia of Chu was a skilled orator who served as an envoy for Emperor Gaozu. He was sent to South Vietnam to grant Wei Tuo the king's seal. When Wei Tuo received him disrespectfully, Lu Jia warned him that the Han emperor could easily destroy him. Wei Tuo apologized and acknowledged Han's superiority. Lu Jia successfully secured South Vietnam's submission. Later, when Emperor Gaozu dismissed the value of studying the classics, Lu Jia argued that while one could conquer the world on horseback, one could not govern it that way. He wrote twelve essays explaining why Qin fell and Han succeeded, which became known as the "New Speeches." During Empress Dowager Lu's regency, Lu Jia retired but later advised Chancellor Chen Ping to ally with General Zhou Bo to counter the Lu family's conspiracy. His strategy helped preserve the Liu imperial house.
rel_path: 汉书/传/郦陆朱刘叔孙传

translation:
Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne and wanted to send someone as an envoy to South Vietnam. Prime Minister Chen Ping reported to the emperor that Lu Mai should be appointed as the Taizhong doctor and sent as an envoy to South Vietnam. Wei Tuo gave up his imperial title and agreed with the princes, which was in line with the court's wishes.
These events are recorded in "The Biography of South Vietnam".
Lu Jia finally died.
Zhu Jian, a native of Chu, once served as the prime minister of Huainan King Yingbu. He fled because of a crime and later followed Yingbu again.
When Ying Bu wanted to rebel, he asked Zhu Jian. Zhu Jian advised him not to rebel, but Ying Bu refused to listen and listened to his father Liang, so he rebelled.
The Han Dynasty suppressed Ying Bu. Hearing that Sai Jian had discouraged Yun Hu from making it, he gave Gui Jian the title of Lili Jun and his family moved to Chang'an.
Sai Jian is a eloquent and talented person, with a clean and upright character. His behavior is different from that of others, and he does not agree with others casually when interacting with others.
Marquis Piyang behaved improperly and was favored by Empress Dowager Lu. He wanted to make friends with Zhu Jian, but Zhu Jian refused to see him.
When Zhu Jian's mother passed away, she had no money to pay for the funeral because of poverty, so she borrowed money to buy mourning clothes and funeral utensils.
Lu Jia had always been friendly with Ji Jian, so he went to see Piyang Hou and congratulated him: "Pingyuan Jun's mother is dead."
Marquis Piyang said: Lord Pingyuan's mother is dead, why do you congratulate me?
Lu Mai said: A few days ago, Junhou wanted to make friends with Guijian. Mr. Pingyuan insisted on the principle of righteousness and refused to see you because of his mother.
Now that his mother is dead, if you really give generous gifts at the funeral, then he will become a good friend who will die for you.
Marquis Piyang then presented him with a hundred gold pieces of clothing and quilt. Other princes and nobles also went to send a total of five hundred gold to support the funeral because of Lord Piyang.
As time went by, some people slandered Piyanghou. Emperor Hui was furious and arrested Piyanghou and wanted to kill him.
The Queen Mother felt very ashamed, but could not say it herself.
Most of the ministers were deeply dissatisfied with the behavior of Marquis Piyang, so they all wanted to kill him.
The Marquis of Piyang was afraid and anxious, so he sent someone to see Sai Jian.
Sejian declined and said: Your case is at a critical moment and I dare not see you.
Zhu Jian then asked to see Ji Qiang, Emperor Xiaohui's lucky minister, and said: "You are favored by the emperor, and everyone in the world knows it."
Now that Hou Piyang was favored by the Queen Mother and was imprisoned, people on the road said that you had said bad things to the emperor, so the emperor wanted to kill him.
Today Marquis Piyang was killed, and tomorrow the Queen Mother will be angry and kill you too.
Why don't you speak kindly to the emperor for Piyanghou?
If the emperor listens to your words and releases Piyanghou, the queen mother will be very happy.
If both monarchs favor you, you will be doubly rich.
So Hong Jiru was frightened, followed Zhu Jian's plan, and advised the emperor, and the emperor released Piyanghou.
When Marquis Piyang was about to be imprisoned, he wanted to see Zhu Jian, but Zhu Jian didn't see him. Marquis Piyang thought Sai Jian had betrayed him and was furious.
It was a surprise when he managed to get out of prison.
After the death of Queen Mother Lu, the ministers wanted to kill all the Lu family members. The Marquis of Piyang had a close relationship with the Lu family, but in the end he was not killed.
The success of the plan was all due to the efforts of Lu Jia and Pingyuan Jun.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, King Li of Huainan killed Marquis Piyang because he had formed a party with the Lu family.
Emperor Xiaowen learned that it was Zhu Jian who was advising him, so he sent officials to arrest him and punish him.
When he heard that the official had arrived at the door, Zhu Jian wanted to commit suicide.
His sons and officials all said: "We don't know what happened, so why did we commit suicide?"
Zhu Jian said: If I die, the disaster will be gone and it will not affect you.
So he drew his sword.
When Emperor Wen found out, he said regretfully: I have no intention of killing Zhu Jian.
So he summoned Zhu Jian's son and worshiped him as a senior official.
He was sent as an envoy to the Xiongnu, but the Xiongnu Shanyu was rude. He died among the Xiongnu because he scolded the Xiongnu Shanyu.
summary: Zhu Jian of Chu served as prime minister to Yingbu, King of Huainan, and advised against rebellion. After Yingbu rebelled and was suppressed, Zhu Jian was rewarded. He was known for his integrity and refused to associate with the corrupt Marquis of Piyang, who was favored by Empress Dowager Lu. When Zhu Jian's mother died, Lu Jia advised the Marquis of Piyang to offer generous funeral gifts, which led to reconciliation. Later, when the Marquis of Piyang was imprisoned, Zhu Jian secretly instructed the emperor's favorite minister to plead for his release, saving his life. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, Zhu Jian's earlier advice helped protect the Marquis of Piyang from execution. During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Zhu Jian was implicated in a case involving the Marquis of Piyang and committed suicide to protect his family.
rel_path: 汉书/传/郦陆朱刘叔孙传

translation:
Lou Jing, a native of Qi.
In the fifth year of Mo, I guarded Longxi and passed through Luoyang. Gaozu was there.
Lou Jing got rid of the crossbar in front of the cart and saw General Yu, a native of Qi, and said: I want to see the emperor to discuss something meaningful.
General Yu wanted to change him into gorgeous clothes. Lou Jing said: "I am wearing silk clothes, so I will wear silk clothes to greet you; if I am wearing coarse cloth clothes, I will wear coarse clothes to greet you. There is no need to change my clothes."
General Yu entered the palace to report to the emperor, who summoned him and gave him food.
After a while, the emperor asked Lou Jing, and Lou Jing said: Your Majesty established the capital in Luoyang, do you want to compete with the Zhou royal family in prosperity? The emperor said: Yes.
Lou Jing said: Your Majesty's attempt to conquer the world is different from that of the Zhou royal family. The ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty was Hou Ji. Yao granted him the title of Tai, and he accumulated good deeds for more than ten generations.
Gong Liu avoided Xia Jie and lived in Bin.
Because of Di's invasion, the king left Bin and came to live in Qi with his horse whip in hand, but everyone in the country rushed to submit to him.
When King Wen of Zhou Dynasty was the Western Bodhisattva, due to his virtue, the fighting between the Yu people and the Rui people calmed down. After they began to accept the mission, Lu Wang and Boyi returned from the seaside.
King Wu of Zhou attacked Shang Zhou, and eight hundred princes unexpectedly gathered in Mengjin, thus annihilating Shang and Yin.
King Cheng of Zhou succeeded to the throne, and the Duke of Zhou and others assisted him, so he built the Zhou Dynasty and established its capital at Luoyang, thinking that Luoyang was the center of the world. The princes paid tribute from all directions and reported their duties. The distance of the road was relatively even. If you have virtue, it is easy to become king, but if you don't have virtue, it is easy to perish.
Everyone who lives here must treat others virtuously, and do not want to rely on the dangers of the terrain to protect the world, and allow future generations to be arrogant, luxurious and abuse the people.
When the Zhou Dynasty declined, they were divided into the kings of Eastern Zhou and the kings of Western Zhou. No one in the world came to see the king of Zhou, and the king of Zhou could not control them.
Not because the morals are weak, but because the strength is too weak.
Now your Majesty raised troops from Feng and Pei, and recruited 3,000 soldiers. He used these people to sweep the Shuhan area, pacify the Three Qin Dynasties, and fought with Xiang Yu in Rongyang. There were seventy major battles and forty minor battles, causing the lives of all the people in the world.
Moreover, the land of Qin is surrounded by mountains and rivers, and the terrain is difficult. If there is a sudden war, millions of troops can gather.
With the old conditions, abundant resources and fertile land, it can become a natural treasury.
Your Majesty entered Guanzhong and made it the capital of the country. Although there was war in Huashan, Qin's old land could still be preserved and occupied.
If you fight with someone, you can't win completely without grabbing his throat and blowing his spine.
Now that your majesty has entered Guanzhong to build the capital and pacify the old land of Qin, this is also strangling the throat of the world and striking its backbone.
Emperor Gao asked the ministers, all of whom were from Shandong, and they all said that the Zhou Dynasty ruled for hundreds of years, while the Qin Dynasty only extended to the second generation, so it would be better to build the capital of Luoyang.
Emperor Gaoti hesitated and could not decide where to make his capital.
It was not until Zhang Liang, the Marquis of Liu, made it clear that he should enter Guanzhong, that he set off to the west to make Guanzhong his capital.
So the emperor said: The first person who was determined to be in Qin was Lou Jing, and Lou was Liu.
He gave Lou Jing the surname Liu, made him a doctor, and titled him Feng Chunjun.
summary: Lou Jing of Qi advised Emperor Gaozu to establish the capital in Guanzhong rather than Luoyang, arguing that Qin's former territory had natural defenses and abundant resources. Despite opposition from ministers from Shandong, Zhang Liang supported this plan, and the emperor adopted it, granting Lou Jing the surname Liu and the title of Feng Chunjun. Later, when the emperor planned to attack the Xiongnu, Lou Jing warned that the Xiongnu were deliberately showing weakness to ambush the Han army. The emperor ignored this advice, was besieged at Baideng, and later released Lou Jing, rewarding him. Lou Jing then proposed a marriage alliance with the Xiongnu, suggesting the emperor send his eldest princess to marry the Chanyu. Although Empress Lu objected, a substitute princess was sent. Lou Jing also recommended relocating powerful clans from various states to Guanzhong to strengthen the region.

translation:
Shusun Tong said: You don't know that I can hardly escape from the tiger's mouth.
So he fled to Xue County, which had surrendered to Chu.
Xiang Liang came to Xue County, and Shusun Tong followed him.
Xiang Liang was defeated in Dingtao, and he followed King Huai again.
King Huai became the Righteous Emperor and moved to Changsha County. Shusun Tong stayed behind to assist King Xiang. In the second year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han led the troops of the five princes into Pengcheng, and Shusun Tong surrendered to the King of Han.
Shusun Tong wore the clothes of a Confucian scholar, and the King of Han was disgusted, so he changed his clothes and wore short clothes in the style of the Chu people. The King of Han was very happy.
Shusun Tong surrendered to the King of Han, and there were more than a hundred scholars who followed him. However, Shusun Tong did not recommend him, only the strong men and reckless grassroots bandits.
The disciples all said: I have served you for many years, and I was lucky enough to defect to the King of Han. Now I do not recommend ministers, but only treacherous people. Why?
Shusun Tong then said: The king of Han is fighting for the world by force. Can you go and fight?
Therefore, I first recommend you to those heroes who are brave enough to kill the enemy. Please wait for me for now. I will not forget you.
The king of Han worshiped his uncle Sun Tong as a doctor and named him Sijun Ji.
The King of Han unified the world, and the princes in Dingtao jointly respected him as emperor. Shusun Tong formulated the court etiquette and the titles of duties of the monarch and his ministers.
Emperor Gao deleted the harsh etiquette laws that had destroyed the Qin Dynasty and implemented simple and easy-to-implement laws.
The ministers drank and competed for merit. When they were drunk, they talked nonsense and drew their swords to hit pillars. The emperor was very worried.
Shusun Tong knew that the emperor was getting more and more upset about this matter, so he persuaded the emperor: Those scholars cannot attack and kill with your majesty, but they can consolidate the country.
I am willing to recruit some scholars from the State of Lu to draft court rituals together with my disciples.
Emperor Gao said: Isn't it difficult to formulate etiquette?
Shusun Tong said: The five emperors have different music systems, and the three kings have different etiquette.
Etiquette is formulated based on the situation, people and customs at that time.
Therefore, we can understand the inheritance, deletion, and addition of etiquette in the Xia, Yin, Shang, and Zhou dynasties. It can be said that they are not repeated.
I hope to learn from the ancient etiquette and the rituals of the Qin Dynasty and formulate it accordingly.
The emperor said: We can try to formulate it. We must make it easy to understand the Han rites and consider whether I can implement it.
So Shusun Tong served as an envoy to recruit more than thirty Confucian scholars from the state of Lu. Among them, two Confucian scholars refused to go with him, saying: "You have already assisted ten masters, and you all flatter them in person."
Now the world has just settled down, the dead have not yet been buried, the injured have not yet recovered, and rituals and music must be established.
The rise of ritual and music is due to hundreds of years of accumulated virtue. We cannot accept what you are asking us to do.
What you are doing is not in line with the ancient ways, so we will not go.
Go ahead and don't tarnish our character.
Shusun Tong smiled and said: You are really pedantic and ignorant of worldly affairs. You do not understand the changes in the current situation.
So he went west with the 30 people he had recruited, and together with Gaodi's close officials and Shusun Tong's disciples, a total of more than 100 people tied thatches in the wild to determine the ceremonial positions. After practicing for more than a month, Shusun Tong said: "Your Majesty, you can give it a try."
After exercising the etiquette, the emperor said: I can do it.
So he ordered all the ministers to practice, and the rituals were completed just in time for the beginning of October.
summary: Shusun Tong of Xue served under Qin II, cleverly avoiding punishment by calling rebels mere thieves. He later served Xiang Liang, King Huai, and finally surrendered to the King of Han. Noticing the disorderly behavior of ministers at court, he offered to create court rituals. Despite criticism from conservative Confucian scholars, he adapted ancient and Qin rituals to create a practical system. After the completion of Changle Palace, the new rituals were implemented, impressing Emperor Gaozu, who remarked, "Now I know the dignity of being emperor." Shusun Tong was appointed Fengchang and rewarded with gold, which he distributed to his disciples. He later served as Crown Prince Tutor and successfully dissuaded Emperor Gaozu from replacing the crown prince. Under Emperor Xiaohui, he continued to formulate rituals and established the practice of offering fruits at ancestral temples.

translation:
Confucius said: If you use political decrees to induce them and punishments to rectify them, the people will only be temporarily exempted from their sins, but they will have no sense of shame; if you use morality to induce them and use rituals to rectify them, the people will not only have a sense of shame, but also have people's hearts subdued.
Laozi said: Superior virtue is in line with nature and is truly virtuous; inferior virtue is created subjectively and is actually unvirtuous.
The multiplicity of laws and regulations breeds cunning and deceit, so the number of thieves increases.
This is really a wise and clear statement!
Laws and regulations are tools of governance, not the source of good or bad governance.
In the past, when the law was tight in the world, thieves became more and more numerous and developed to the extreme, causing the monarchs, ministers and people to avoid each other, resulting in the world being ruined and unable to be saved.
At this time, local governance was in crisis. If tough and harsh measures were not used, how could the governance be maintained?
Those who advocate morality adopt a relaxed approach.
Therefore, Confucius said: When trying lawsuits, I am no different from others. I must completely eliminate the litigation events!
Lao Tzu also said: It is in vain to ridicule a mediocre person who does not know the way.
These are not lies.
The rise of the Han Dynasty broke the square into a circle, returned to simplicity and truth, and the legal framework was extremely broad and sparse. However, the situation of officialdom is flourishing, banditry and chaos are not prevalent, and the people live and work in peace and contentment.
From this point of view, the key to official governance is not the harshness of the law.
When he was a high-ranking empress, the only cruel official was Hou Feng, who trampled on the clan and insulted the meritorious officials.
After the Lu family was defeated, Hou Feng's family was eradicated.
During the reign of Emperor Jing, Chao Cuo used sharp tactics to support his talents, and the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms was also caused by Chao Cuo, and finally Chao Cuo was killed.
Later, Zhidu and Ningcheng appeared again.
Zhidu was born in Dayang County, Hedong County.
Serve Emperor Wen as a Langguan.
Emperor Jing was the Zhonglang General at that time, and he dared to speak out to the emperor and rebuke the ministers' faults in person at the court.
Zhidu once accompanied the emperor to Shanglin Garden. Jia Ji was in the toilet, and the wild boar also entered the toilet. The emperor looked at Zhidu, but Zhidu was unmoved.
The emperor wanted to personally take the sword to rescue Maiji. Zhidu knelt down in front of the emperor and said: "We have lost a Jiajie and a new Maiji has come in. Is it possible that the world lacks people like Maiji?"
Even if your Majesty doesn't care about yourself, how can you be worthy of the country and the Queen Mother?
After hearing Zhidu's words, the emperor retreated, and the wild boar did not harm Maiji.
When the Queen Mother heard about this, she rewarded Zhidu with one hundred catties of gold. The emperor also rewarded Zhidu with one hundred catties of gold. From then on, Zhidu was highly valued.
There were more than 300 families in Jinan's Kun clan. They were powerful and committed all kinds of evil. The prefect of the county could not subdue them, so Emperor Jing appointed Zhidu as the prefect of Jinan.
After Zhidu arrived, he immediately killed the chief culprit of the Shu clan, and the remaining members of other clans were so frightened that their thighs trembled.
summary: Confucius taught that governance through laws and punishments only temporarily prevents wrongdoing without instilling shame, while governance through morality and rituals creates both shame and willing compliance. Laozi similarly distinguished between superior virtue aligned with nature and inferior virtue that is subjectively created. The text observes that excessive laws breed cunning and increase thieves, noting that laws are merely tools of governance, not its source. During the Han Dynasty's rise, broad and sparse legal frameworks allowed officials to flourish and people to live peacefully, demonstrating that effective governance depends not on harsh laws.

translation:
Zhidu served as the prefect for more than a year, but Jinan County did not pick up the troops. The prefects of more than ten nearby counties feared Zhidu as they feared the superior palace.
Zhidu is brave and powerful, fair and honest, he does not open personal letters, and does not accept gifts or private entrustments from relatives and friends.
He often declares: I left my family behind and left my hometown to serve as an official. Of course I should be loyal to my duties and be loyal to the last bit of my life. In the end, I couldn't care about my wife and children.
Zhidu transferred the lieutenant, and Prime Minister Tiaohou was extremely noble and arrogant, but Zhidu bowed to him and refused to bow to him.
At this time, the folk customs were simple, and the officials and the people were afraid of offending the dignitaries and protected themselves wisely. Only Zhidu dared to take the lead in enforcing the law extremely harshly, without avoiding the emperor's relatives. When the princes and clans saw Zhi, they did not dare to look at him directly, and called him "Goshawk".
King Linjiang was summoned to the Lieutenant's Mansion to investigate the case. He wanted to get the knife, pen and ink to write a letter to apologize to the emperor, but Zhidu prohibited the jailer from giving it to him.
Wei Qihou sent someone to secretly deliver the sword and pen to King Linjiang.
After King Linjiang got it, he wrote a letter to apologize to the emperor and then committed suicide.
When Empress Dowager Dou heard about this, she was furious and slandered Zhidu with severe punishments. Zhidu was dismissed from his official position and returned home.
However, Emperor Jing sent someone to Zhidu's home to appoint him as the governor of Yanmen. He did not have to go to the court to say goodbye, but took a shortcut to his post. He could take advantage of the situation and handle government affairs with full authority.
The Huns were aware of Zhidu's integrity and all evacuated their border troops. After Zhidu's death, they did not dare to take a step near Yanmen.
The Huns carved a puppet figure that looked exactly like Zhidu, and ordered the cavalry to gallop and shoot, but none of them could hit. They were so frightened by Zhidu.
The Huns were worried about this situation and used the laws of the Han Dynasty to frame Zhidu. Emperor Jing said: "Zhi are all loyal ministers."
Want to free him.
Queen Mother Dou said: Isn't King Linjiang a loyal minister?
So Zhidu was beheaded.
Ningcheng was born in Zhang County, Nanyang County.
Serve Emperor Jing as a Langguan and a visitor.
He likes to be aggressive, and when he is a junior official, he must be superior to his superiors; when he is someone else's boss, he treats his subordinates as harshly and eagerly as tying wet sticks.
Cunning and cruel, domineering and domineering.
Gradually he was promoted to the rank of captain of Jinan, and he was appointed as the prefect of Jinan by Zhidu.
In the past, several captains walked into the county government and paid homage to the prefect, just like the county magistrate paying homage to the prefect. They were so afraid of Zhi.
When Ning Cheng went to the county government, he broke in directly and insulted Zhidu. His arrogance was even higher than that of Zhidu.
Zhidu Sujian Ningcheng became famous, treated him well, and became a good friend with him.
After a long time, Zhidu died. After that, many of the clan nobles in and around Chang'an violated the law, and the emperor called Ning Cheng to serve as lieutenant.
Ning Cheng followed the example of Zhi Du in governing the area, but was not as honest as him. However, everyone in the clan, nobles and powerful people were frightened and trembled.
summary: The text then chronicles several cruel officials. Zhidu served Emperors Wen and Jing, known for his bravery, integrity, and harsh enforcement. He once prevented Emperor Jing from risking his life to save a palace attendant from a wild boar. As governor of Jinan, he executed the chief culprit among powerful clans, causing such fear that the county became orderly. He declared his loyalty to duty over family. The Huns feared him so much they carved his likeness for target practice but could never hit it. Despite Emperor Jing recognizing him as a loyal minister, Empress Dowager Dou had him executed for his role in Prince Linjiang's suicide.

translation:
Emperor Wu ascended the throne and Tiao Ning became the internal historian.
Most of the relatives slandered Ning Cheng's shortcomings to Emperor Wu, and Ning Cheng was sentenced to tweezers, his hair was shaved, and an iron ring was placed around his neck.
At that time, those who committed crimes among the nine ministers were executed, and no other punishment was given. However, Ning Cheng was sentenced to severe punishment. Bai thought that he would not be used again, so he took off the iron ring around his neck, forged documents, sneaked out of Hangu Pass, and fled home.
He threatened: If you can't earn two thousand dan as an official, and you can't earn tens of millions in business, how can you stand in the world!
So he took out a loan to buy more than a thousand hectares of paddy fields, and then leased them to the poor, enslaving thousands of families.
A few years later, when the amnesty was granted, Ning Cheng had accumulated tens of millions of property and became a chivalrous man who fought against injustice and fought against injustice. He held the officials' shortcomings and secrets in his hands and threatened them at any time. He was followed by dozens of knights guarding him when he went out.
He served the people with greater authority than the county governor.
Zhou Yangyou, whose father Tong Jian was named Zhou Yanghou as the uncle of the King of Huainan, changed his surname to Zhou Yang.
Zhou Yangyou was appointed Langguan for family reasons and served Emperor Wen.
During the reign of Emperor Jing, Zhou Yang was appointed as the county governor.
After Emperor Wu came to the throne, officials advocated strict governance, but Zhou Yangyou was the most strict and arrogant among all the county guards.
He would bend the law and let people live if they were friendly to him, even if they deserved death; and he would bend the law and put people to death even if they did not commit a capital crime for those he hated.
The county where he lives as an official must eradicate all the tyrants.
When he was appointed as the prefect, he regarded the captain as the county magistrate; once he became the captain, he placed himself above the prefect and deprived him of his legitimate power.
Ji An was stubborn and stubborn in vain, while Sima An used his articles to hurt people. They were also among the officials at the county level, but when they were in the same car with Zhou Yangyou, they all took the initiative to avoid it and hid aside to sit.
Later, Zhou Yangyou was appointed as the captain of Hedong, and he and the prefect of the county, Shengtu Gong, fought for power and appealed to each other. Shengtu Gong was found guilty, but he committed suicide without being severely punished, while Zhou Yangyou was executed and abandoned the market.
Since Ning Cheng and Zhou Yangyou, the world has become more and more unstable. The people use clever methods to resist the law, and the officials are mostly similar to Ning Cheng and Zhou Yangyou.
Zhao Yu was a native of Yaxian County.
As an assistant historian, he was appointed as the official of Zhongdu. Because of his integrity, he was appointed as the commander of the order and served the Taiwei Zhou Yafu.
Zhou Yafu became the prime minister, and then Yu became the prime minister. Everyone in the government praised him for being honest and fair.
However, Zhou Yafu did not reuse him and said: I know that Yu's character and talent are extraordinary, but he is too harsh in upholding the law and cannot be entrusted with important tasks.
During the reign of Emperor Wu, Tào Yu had accumulated achievements as a swordsman and pen official and was transferred to the imperial censor.
summary: Ningcheng succeeded Zhidu as governor of Jinan, known for aggression and cruelty. After Zhidu's death, he became lieutenant and terrorized nobles. Under Emperor Wu, he was sentenced to shaving and iron collar, but escaped, became wealthy through land leasing, and wielded power greater than county governors. Zhou Yangyou was known for bending laws according to personal feelings, eradicating tyrants, and competing with superiors for power, eventually executed for his conflicts.

translation:
Yi Zong was transferred from Hanoi to be the prefect of Nanyang. He heard that Ning Cheng's family was in Nanyang. When he arrived at the pass, Ning Cheng had come to the roadside to greet him. However, Yi Zong was so angry that he did not salute Ning Cheng.
As soon as he arrived in Nanyang County, he investigated the Ning family and ransacked his home.
Ning Cheng was convicted, but the Kong family, Bao family and other powerful people fled. The officials and people in Nanyang were afraid of Yi Zong and did not dare to disobey his orders.
Zhu Qiang of the Ping family and Du Zhou of Du Yan became Yi Zong's minions and subordinates, and were appointed and promoted to imperial officials.
At that time, the army was transferred out of Dingxiang several times. The officials and people in Dingxiang were very chaotic and corrupt, so the court transferred Yi and appointed him as the prefect of Dingxiang.
As soon as Yi Zong arrived, he detained more than 200 felons in Dingxiang Prison, as well as more than 200 guests and brothers who secretly visited them in the prison.
Yi Zong arrested them all and convicted them of "death penalty".
That day Yi Zong petitioned for permission to kill more than 400 people.
From then on, everyone in the county trembled with fear, and even cunning and cunning people helped the officials to govern the place.
At that time, Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang were already nine ministers, but their governance was still relatively loose. All auxiliary laws were implemented, and only Yi Zong used harsh methods like an eagle catching a parrot to govern.
Later, with the replacement of the five-baht coin and the rise of silver, traitors and thieves were prevalent among the people, especially in the capital. The imperial court appointed Yi Zong as the right internal history and Wang Wenshu as the lieutenant.
Wang Wenshu was very cruel and never told Yi Zong beforehand when doing things, but Yi Zong would definitely use his power to ruin his reputation.
They governed the people and killed too many people, but they could only achieve small governance. The number of traitors and thieves increased and it was difficult to catch them.
Officials used killing, kidnapping, and kidnapping as their main method to govern the people, so Yan Feng was appointed because of his cruelty and cruelty.
He is righteous and honest, and his method of governing the people is based on the example of Zhidu.
The emperor came to Dinghu. He had been ill for many days. After recovering, he drove to Ganquan, but the road had not been repaired yet.
The emperor said angrily: "Does Yi Zong think that I will not take this path?"
So I wrote it down.
In winter, Yang Ke had just presided over the complaint. Yi Zong thought it was an act of chaos, so he sent officials to capture the envoy sent by Yang Ke.
When the emperor heard about this incident, he asked Du Shi to try it, and he was convicted of infringing and abolishing Shaoshu. Yi Zong was executed and his body was abandoned in the market.
A year later, Zhang Tang also died.
Wang Wenshu was from Yangling.
When he was young, he killed people with vertebrae, buried them privately, and became a thief.
Later, he broke away from the traitorous party and became the county pavilion chief. He was deposed several times.
After being appointed to official positions several times, Wang Wenshu was promoted to the rank of Ting Wei Shi because of his ability in managing the prison.
Under Zhang Tang, he was transferred to the post of censor, supervising the arrest of thieves and killing many people.
Later, he gradually rose to the rank of Captain of Guangping. He chose more than a dozen brave heroes from the county to be his minions. He concealed their serious crimes and let them supervise the arrest of thieves. Wang Wenshu was very happy because he captured the people he wanted to arrest.
summary: Zhao Yu served under Zhou Yafu, who recognized his integrity but considered him too harsh for important positions. Under Emperor Wu, he helped formulate legal regulations and became known for honesty, refusing all social invitations. Yi Zong rose from banditry to become an official through his sister's connection to the Empress Dowager. He governed with daring severity, eradicating powerful families in Hanoi. As governor of Dingxiang, he executed over 400 prisoners in one day. He was eventually executed for his actions.

translation:
Therefore, although this person has hundreds of sins, he has not been questioned or punished; but if he does not try his best to supervise the arrest and adopts an evasive attitude, he will be executed immediately and his clan will be exterminated.
As a result, thieves from the Qi-Zhao border areas did not dare to approach Guangping, and the Guangping area began to be famous for not picking up people on the road.
When the emperor heard about this, he transferred Wang Wenshu to be the prefect of Hanoi County.
Wang Van Thu always lived in Quang Binh and was already aware of the home of gangsters and rapists in Ha Noi County.
When he arrived in September, he ordered the county to prepare fifty private horses and set up post stations on the road from Hanoi to Chang'an. He also ordered the officials to use the method originally used in Guangping to arrest the powerful and traitorous people in the county. More than a thousand people were involved in each other and were guilty.
Then he reported to the court, requesting that those who committed the most serious crimes should have their clan destroyed, those who had committed the minor crimes personally be put to death, and all their family possessions should be confiscated.
Only two days after the memorial was sent, the news of the accurate memorial was received, and the execution was carried out according to the order, causing the blood of the murdered person to flow for more than ten miles.
The people in Hanoi were surprised by this performance and thought it was so fast.
By the end of December, there were no traces of thieves in the county.
The thieves could not be caught because they all fled to neighboring counties, and they sent people to hunt for them in neighboring counties. However, it was already the spring season. Wang Wenshu paused and sighed: What a pity, what a pity! If the winter season is extended for another month and all thieves are wiped out, it will be done!
This shows how far he has reached in terms of his cruelty, love of killing, and lack of benevolent governance.
The emperor heard about Wang Wenshu and thought he was talented, so he transferred him to lieutenant.
Its governance was modeled after Hanoi County, and some officials who were prone to suspicion and trouble were summoned and appointed. In Hanoi County, there were Yang Jie and Ma Wu, and in Guanzhong, there were Yang Gan, Cheng Xin, etc.
Yi Zong served as internal history, and Wang Wenshu was afraid of him, so he did not dare to impose tyranny.
After Yi Zong died and Zhang Tang was defeated, Wang Wenshu was transferred to Tingwei.
However, when Yin Qi was charged with breaking the law while serving as lieutenant, Wang Wenshu was appointed as lieutenant again.
He lacked literary talent and was often absent-minded and indifferent to official duties when holding other official positions. However, he became energetic after becoming a lieutenant.
He had always been familiar with the customs of Guanzhong and had many acquaintances with the abominable officials. Therefore, after he became a lieutenant, all the abominable officials were re-appointed.
The officials strictly inspected the promiscuous young people, set up reporting gates to collect reports, and set up officials and chiefs of the towns to arrest the traitors.
Wang Wenshu loves flattery and is very good at flattering and winning over powerful people; but he treats powerless people like slaves.
To powerful people, even if they have adultery, they will not offend; to powerless people, even if they are noble relatives, they will be insulted.
He was cunning and deceitful, and he once petitioned to punish lawless elements among the common people, and used his satire to impress wealthy families.
It can be seen how smooth his ruling skills have been.
Those cunning and lawless people were thoroughly punished, and most of them died in prison, and very few of them came out.
summary: Wang Wenshu began as a thief but became an official known for managing prisons. As governor of Guangping, he recruited brave men as informants, concealing their crimes while executing those who failed him. As governor of Hanoi, he arrested over a thousand people, executing the worst and confiscating property, with blood flowing for miles. He regretted that winter ended before he could eliminate all thieves. He became lieutenant but committed suicide when facing execution for his crimes, with his entire family executed.

translation:
Wang Wenshu's minions and subordinates are all like wolves and tigers.
As a result, all the cunning thieves below the average level in the lieutenant's jurisdiction were brought to justice, and the powerful tycoons praised him and praised him for his ability to govern the people.
A few years later, all of his petty officials became rich thanks to the protection of powerful people.
Wang Wenshu came back from the attack on Shuyue. When he discussed political affairs, he went against the emperor's will, so he was dismissed from office.
At this time, the emperor just wanted to build the Tongtian Tower but lacked manpower. Wang Wenshu petitioned to call all the outstanding soldiers who were former lieutenants, and obtained tens of thousands of manpower in total.
The emperor was very happy and appointed Wang Wenshu as the young master.
Later, he was transferred to You Neishi, but his governance remained the same, and the number of cunning and evil people was reduced until they were completely banned.
Later, he was dismissed from office because of his conviction. After his comeback, he served as right assistant and concurrently as lieutenant, and his conduct remained the same as before.
More than a year later, when the imperial court sent troops to conquer Dawan, the emperor issued an edict to recruit powerful officials.
Wang Wenshu hid his powerful official Hua Cheng, and someone reported that Wang Wenshu secretly accepted dirty money from soldiers and did other illegal things. The crime should be punished by the clan. Wang Wenshu could not bear this blow, so he committed suicide out of fear of the crime.
At that time, Wang Wenshu's two younger brothers and his wife's entire family were also executed together as a clan for his crimes.
Guang Luxun Xu Ziwei said: How sad! How sad!
In ancient times, there was a plan to exterminate three tribes, but Wang Wenshu actually committed the crime of annihilating five tribes at the same time!
After Wang Wenshu's death, his family property was worth thousands of gold.
Yin Qi is from Chiping County, Dongjun.
Officials with swords and pens were gradually promoted to censors.
Working under Zhang Tang, Zhang Tang praised him many times for his integrity.
Emperor Wu sent him to supervise thieves. He killed and eradicated thieves without fearing their fame and power.
Later he was transferred to Guandu Lieutenant, and his reputation surpassed that of Ning Cheng.
The emperor thought he had talent and appointed him lieutenant.
However, the situation of the officials and the people was deteriorating. The world was hypocritical and untrue. Yiqi Muqiang was looked down upon for his lack of literary talent. Evil officials refused to take up their posts. Good officials were incapable of managing affairs. Yin Qi was also accused because most of his duties were neglected.
Later he came back and became the captain of Huaiyang.
A few years after Wang Wenshu's defeat, Yin Qi fell ill and died, leaving behind less than fifty gold.
Because he killed too many people in Huaiyang, after his death, his enemies wanted to burn his body to satisfy their hatred, so his wife fled with the body and was able to bury him.
Yang Pu is from Yiyang.
Because thousands of people donated money and grain, he became a minor official.
Later, the governor of Henan recommended him as a censor and was sent to Guandong to supervise thieves. He imitated Yi Qi in governance and was daring to do anything.
Gradually promoted to Lord Commander, the emperor thought he had talent.
South Vietnam rebelled, and Yang Pu was appointed General Lou Chuan. For his meritorious service, he was awarded the title of General Liang Hou.
Later, Shu Yue rebelled again, and the emperor wanted to appoint him as a general again. Because he was relying on his previous achievements in vain, he issued an edict to reprimand him: Your achievements as a general are only the first to capture dangerous places such as Shimen and Xunjun. There is no real military merit in killing generals and flags. What is there to be proud of?
The first mistake was to conquer Panyu, capture the surrendered people as prisoners, and exhume the dead as harvest.
The rebellion committed by King Jiande of South Vietnam and Prime Minister Lu Jia is intolerable in heaven and earth. General, you have elite troops and did not pursue them to the end, allowing Shu Yue to calmly send troops to rescue. This is the second fault.
The sergeants and soldiers of the army have been exposed to the rain for years, and there is no wine to drink in the court meetings. General, you do not appreciate their hard work, but make clever words to show off yourself. When you return to your hometown, you carry three groups of silver and gold seals. Showing off in the countryside is the third fault.
Because he was greedy for keeping his wife and concubines home late, he excused himself by saying that the road was dangerous. This violated the ancestral etiquette, which was the fourth fault.
If you want to be equipped with a Shu knife, I ask you how much it costs, and the answer is hundreds of dollars. Weapons are coming in and out of the weapons warehouse every day, but you pretend not to know. This is the fifth fault.
After receiving the edict, he did not come to Lanchi Palace to see you, and he did not come to explain later.
If, general, your subordinates refuse to answer questions or obey orders, how should you punish them?
Just imagine if everyone is like this, how can there be any trust between heaven and earth?
summary: Yan Yannian served as governor of Zhuojun and Henan, known for suppressing powerful families while protecting the poor and weak. He executed dozens from powerful clans, earning the nickname "Butcher." His mother rebuked him for relying on killing rather than kindness, predicting retribution. She returned home to prepare his burial place, and indeed he was later executed for his crimes. Yin Shang, as magistrate of Chang'an, built "Tiger Caves" - deep pits where he threw hundreds of criminals to die. He warned his children that being dismissed for cruelty was preferable to being dismissed for weakness.

translation:
Please be careful and don’t neglect your duties!
Yin Shang's four sons all became officials and became county guards, and the eldest son Yin Li became a Jingzhao Yin. They all respected majesty and had a reputation for being good at governance.
Zan said: The recorded masters from Zhidu on down were all famous for their harshness and violence. However, Zhidu was upright, knew right from wrong, and understood the general picture.
However, Zhang Tang flattered the monarch and was valued for his appearance and deeds. He often used clever words to stir up trouble and made the trend of flattery prevail in the country.
Yu acted according to the law and strictly observed justice.
Du Zhou was obedient to flattery, and it was important to speak less in everything.
After Zhang Tang's death, the law was strict and troubled, and the country became increasingly chaotic and desolate. The nine ministers were busy rescuing and fighting the chaos, so they had no time to discuss matters other than the rule of law!
From then until the reigns of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, there were many cruel officials, but it is impossible to count them. Here we only select the famous ones and see them in the records.
Among them, those who are honest can serve as examples, while those who are dirty may have strategies and education, or may have the courage to punish traitors and thieves, and may also have literary talents and military strategies.
Although they are harsh, they are capable of doing their jobs.
The descendants of Zhang Tang and Du Zhou were famous and prosperous, so they were recorded in separate biographies.
summary: The text concludes that while these officials were harsh, some were upright and understood principles, while others flattered monarchs and stirred trouble. Their descendants became prominent, recorded in separate biographies.

translation:
Chen Ying did not dare to claim the throne and said to his officers: "The surname Xiang has been a general for generations and is very famous in the Chu Kingdom." If you want to do big things now, the coach must be this kind of person.
We rely on famous families and the destruction of the Qin Dynasty is certain.
So everyone obeyed his words and put the troops under Xiang Liang's command.
Xiang Liang crossed the Huaihe River, and generals Yingbu and Pu also brought their troops to join him.
A total of 60,000 to 70,000 people were stationed at the craft.
At this time, Qin Jia had already elected Jing Ju as the king of Chu, and stationed troops in Pengcheng with their faces restrained, hoping to resist Xiang Liang.
Xiang Liang told the officers: King Chen started the rebellion first, and the battle was unfavorable. His whereabouts are unknown.
Now Qin Jia betrayed King Chen and supported Jing Ju, which was a treasonous act, so he marched to attack Qin Jia. Qin Jia's army was defeated and fled, and Xiang Liang pursued him to Hu Ling.
Qin Jia returned to the army and fought for one day. Qin Jia died in the battle and the army surrendered.
Jingju fled and died in Liangdi.
Xiang Liang annexed Qin Jia's army and garrisoned Huling. Will he lead his troops to the west?
Zhang Han's army arrived in Li County, and Xiang Liang sent Zhujishi and Yu Fanjun, generals from another army, to fight.
Yu Fanjun died in battle, Zhujishi's army was defeated and fled to Huling.
Xiang Liang led his army into Xue County and killed Zhujishi.
Xiang Liang had previously sent Xiang Yu to attack Xiangcheng separately. The officers and soldiers of Xiangcheng held on and could not be captured for a while.
After conquering them, Xiang Yu buried them all alive and then came back to report to Xiang Liang. When Xiang Liang heard that King Chen was indeed dead, he summoned all the generals to Xue County to discuss military affairs.
At this time, Pei Gong also raised troops in Peixian County and came to attend the meeting.
Fan Zeng, a seventy-year-old native of Juhu, who was always good at coming up with unexpected plans, went to persuade Xiang Liang and said: "Chen Sheng's failure is inevitable."
The Qin Dynasty destroyed six kingdoms, and Chu was the most innocent. Since King Huai went to Qin and never returned, the people of Chu missed him to this day. Therefore, Duke Nan of Chu said: Even if there are only three families left in Chu, Chu will definitely be the one who destroys Qin. Now Chen Sheng is the first to rise up and proclaim himself king without supporting the descendants of King Chu. His power cannot last long.
Now you have raised troops in Jiangshu, and the reason why the generals in Chu are swarming to follow you is because your family has been the generals of Chu for generations and can support the descendants of the King of Chu again.
So Xiang Liang found the grandson of King Huai of Chu from the people, who was tending sheep for others, and supported him as King Huai of Chu to comply with the people's wishes.
Chen Ying served as the Shangzhu State of Chu State, granted five counties, and established Xutai as the capital with King Huai.
Xiang Liang called himself Lord Wu Xin and led his army to attack Kang's father.
At the beginning, Zhang Han killed Qi King Tian Dan in Linpu, and Tian Jia established himself as Qi King.
Tian Dan's brother Tian Rong retreated to Shu'a, and Zhang Han pursued and surrounded Tian Rong's army.
Xiang Liang led troops to rescue Shu'a and defeated the Qin army in Shu'a.
Tian Rong went back with his troops and expelled King Tianjia of Qi. Tianjia fled to Chu State. Tian Jiao, the prime minister of Tianjia, fled to Zhao.
Tian Jiao's younger brother Tian Xian was originally a general of Qi State, but he lived in Zhao State and did not dare to go back.
Tian Rong supported Tian Dan's son Tian Shi as King of Qi.
Xiang Liang defeated the Qin army in the Dong'a area and pursued it.
Several envoys were sent to urge the Qi army to march west together: Tian Rong said that if Chu killed Tian Jia, Zhao would kill Tian Jiao and Tian Xian. We just sent troops.
Xiang Liang said: Tianjia is the king of the allied countries. He came to me in desperation and couldn't bear to kill him.
The State of Zhao also refused to kill Tian Jiao and Tian Xian to make a deal with the State of Qi.
Qi finally refused to send troops to help the Chu army.
Xiang Liang sent Xiang Yu and Pei Gong to attack Chengyang from another route and massacred the entire city.
Moving further west, the Qin army was defeated east of Puyang, and the Qin army withdrew its troops and retreated into Puyang City.
Pei Gong and Xiang Yu attacked Dingtao. Dingtao was not captured, so he withdrew, captured the territory to the west, and reached Yongqiu, where he defeated the Qin army and killed Li You.
He returned to attack Waihuang, but Waihuang was not captured.
Xiang Liang set out from Dong'a, and when he arrived at Dingtao, he defeated the Qin army again. Xiang Yu and others killed Li You again, showing contempt for the Qin army even more, showing a proud look.
Song Yi advised Xiang Liang: If you win a battle, if the generals are proud and the soldiers are lazy, they will fail.
Now the soldiers are a little lazy, and the number of Qin soldiers is increasing day by day. I am worried about you.
Xiang Liang ignored him and sent Song Yi as envoy to Qi.
Song Yi met Qi's envoy Gaoling Junxian on the road and asked him: "Are you going to see Jun Wu Xin?"
summary: Chen Sheng, courtesy name She, was from Yangcheng, and Wu Guang, courtesy name Shu, was from Yangxia. When Chen She was young, he worked as a hired farmhand. Once, while resting, he expressed frustration and told his fellow workers that if they became rich, they should not forget each other. They laughed at him, but Chen Sheng sighed, "How can a sparrow know the ambition of a swan?" In the autumn of the first year of Qin II, the government sent 900 people, including Chen Sheng and Wu Guang as village chiefs, to guard Yuyang. They encountered heavy rain in Qidaze Township, blocking the road and causing them to miss the deadline, which was punishable by beheading. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang discussed that escaping or rising up both led to death, so they decided to die for the state. Chen Sheng noted that the people had long suffered under Qin's harsh rule. He proposed pretending to be Fusu, the eldest son of the First Emperor, and Xiang Yan, a beloved Chu general, to gain support. Wu Guang agreed. They consulted a fortune teller who hinted at using ghosts and gods to gain prestige. They wrote "King Chen Sheng" on silk and hid it in a fish, which soldiers found. Chen Sheng also had Wu Guang imitate a fox's cry at night, shouting, "Great Chu is rising, King Chen Sheng." The soldiers were frightened and talked about it the next day. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, known for their kindness, killed the two escorting generals after Wu Guang provoked them. Chen Sheng addressed the soldiers, saying that missing the deadline meant death, and that strong men should leave a great name. The soldiers agreed, and they staged an uprising, pretending to be Fusu and Xiang Yan. They attacked Daze Township, Qixian, and other counties, recruiting troops along the way. By the time they reached Chen County, they had six to seven hundred chariots, over a thousand cavalry, and tens of thousands of infantry. They captured Chen County, and the local elders declared Chen Sheng king, known as Zhang Chu. Many counties killed their Qin officials in response. Chen Sheng appointed Wu Guang as acting king to attack Rongyang, and sent others to capture Zhao, Jiujiang, and Wei. Ge Ying, sent to capture territory, established Xiang Qiang as King of Chu but later killed him upon hearing of Chen Sheng's kingship. Chen Sheng then killed Ge Ying. Wu Guang besieged Rongyang but could not capture it. Chen Sheng appointed Zhou Wen as general to attack Qin. Zhou Wen gathered troops and reached Hangu Pass, but Qin general Zhang Han defeated him. Zhou Wen committed suicide after several defeats. Wu Chen proclaimed himself King of Zhao, angering Chen Sheng, but Cai Ci advised against killing his family. Chen Sheng sent an envoy to congratulate Zhao and moved the family to the palace. Zhao decided not to march west but to expand north into Yan. Han Guang, sent to attack Yan, was advised to proclaim himself King of Yan, which he did. Tian Dan killed the magistrate of Di County and proclaimed himself King of Qi, attacking Zhou Shi. Zhou Shi returned to Wei and made Ningling Junjiu King of Wei. Tian Zang and others killed Wu Guang, claiming he was arrogant and incompetent. Chen Sheng made Tian Zang a general, but he was killed by Zhang Han. Deng Yue and Wu Feng fled to Chen County after defeats. Chen Sheng killed Deng Shuo. Qin Jia and others independently raised armies. Chen Sheng sent Wu Ping Junpan to oversee them, but Qin Jia killed him. Zhang Han attacked Chen County, and Chen Sheng personally led the battle but was defeated. In December, Chen Sheng's coachman Zhuangmai killed him and surrendered to Qin. Chen Sheng was buried in Ci County. His old minister Lu Chen raised a "Cangtou Army," killed Zhuangmai, and made Chen County the capital of Chu. Song Liu, sent to pacify Nanyang, surrendered to Qin after hearing of Chen Sheng's death. Qin Jia appointed Jing Ju as King of Chu. Chen Sheng reigned for six months. His old friends came to see him but were killed for speaking freely, causing others to leave. Chen Sheng appointed Zhu Fang and Hu Wu, who were harsh, leading to his failure. Despite his death, the generals he appointed eventually destroyed Qin. Emperor Gaozu arranged for sacrifices to Chen Sheng's tomb, which continued until Wang Mang's time. Xiang Ji, courtesy name Yu, was from Xiaxiang. His uncle was Xiang Liang, son of Xiang Yan, a famous Chu general. The Xiang family had been generals for generations. Xiang Ji learned writing and swordsmanship but gave up, wanting to learn to resist tens of thousands. Xiang Liang taught him the art of war, but Xiang Ji only learned a little. Xiang Liang killed someone and fled to Wuzhong with Xiang Ji. When Qin Shihuang traveled to Kuaiji, Xiang Ji said, "We can replace him," shocking Xiang Liang. Xiang Ji was eight feet two inches tall, could lift a cauldron, and was feared by the youth of Wuzhong. In the first year of Qin II, Yin Tong, the acting governor of Kuaiji, discussed rebellion with Xiang Liang. Xiang Liang had Xiang Ji kill Yin Tong, then took control of the county, raising 8,000 elite soldiers. Xiang Liang became general of Kuaiji, with Xiang Ji as deputy. In the second year, Xiang Liang led 8,000 men across the Yangtze River. Chen Ying, who had raised 20,000 men in Dongyang, joined him on his mother's advice. Xiang Liang crossed the Huai River, and Yingbu and others joined him, totaling 60,000-70,000 men. Xiang Liang attacked Qin Jia, who had betrayed Chen Sheng, and killed him. He then heard of Chen Sheng's death and summoned generals to Xue County. Fan Zeng advised Xiang Liang to support a descendant of King Huai of Chu. Xiang Liang found King Huai's grandson, who was tending sheep, and made him King Huai of Chu. Xiang Liang called himself Lord Wu Xin. He defeated Qin forces at Dong'a and Dingtao but became arrogant. Song Yi warned him, but Xiang Liang ignored him. Qin reinforced Zhang Han, who defeated and killed Xiang Liang at Dingtao. Xiang Yu and Pei Gong retreated. Zhang Han, thinking Chu was weak, crossed the Yellow River to attack Zhao, besieging Julu. King Huai of Chu appointed Song Yi as general, with Xiang Yu as second-in-command, to rescue Zhao. Song Yi stopped at Anyang, refusing to advance. Xiang Yu killed Song Yi, claiming he was a traitor, and became general. He led troops across the Zhang River, sinking ships and burning supplies, and defeated the Qin army at Julu, killing Su Jiao and capturing Wang Li. The Chu army became dominant among the princes. Zhang Han, fearing Zhao Gao, surrendered to Xiang Yu after negotiations. Xiang Yu made Zhang Han King Yong and placed him in the Chu army. He then killed over 200,000 surrendered Qin soldiers at night. Xiang Yu entered Hangu Pass and arrived at Hongmen. Pei Gong had captured Xianyang, and Xiang Yu was angry. Fan Zeng advised attacking Pei Gong, but Xiang Bo saved him. Xiang Yu sacked Xianyang, killed Qin's prince, and burned the palace. He killed Han Sheng for criticizing him. Xiang Yu betrayed the agreement that the first to enter Guanzhong would be king. He moved King Huai to Changsha and divided the world, making Pei Gong King of Han, and others kings. He proclaimed himself Overlord of Western Chu. Tian Rong rebelled, and Xiang Yu attacked Qi, killing many. The King of Han attacked Chu, but Xiang Yu defeated him at Pengcheng, killing over 100,000 Han soldiers. The King of Han escaped and gathered troops. Xiang Yu besieged Rongyang, but the King of Han escaped. Fan Zeng died after being suspected. Xiang Yu defeated Peng Yue but lost Chenggao. He made a pact with the King of Han to divide the world, but the King of Han broke it. Xiang Yu was besieged at Gaixia, hearing Chu songs from all sides. He sang a tragic song, then escaped with 800 cavalry. Only 28 remained. He killed many Han soldiers but was surrounded. He refused to cross the Wu River, saying he had no face to see his people. He killed himself, and his body was divided by five Han soldiers. The King of Han buried him and spared his family. The text concludes with a praise, discussing Qin's rise and fall, and criticizing Xiang Yu's arrogance and failure to learn from the past.

translation:
A filial son is good at following the aspirations of his ancestors. The Duke of Zhou completed the work started by King Wen and King Wu and formulated the system of rituals and music, and established the system of respecting fathers and sharing benefits. He understood that King Wen did not want to be the son of a man and reign over his father, so he traced the ancestral arrangement upwards to the first ancestor Houji, and later Ji matched heaven.
Creation is the virtue of a saint and is the greatest and most important filial piety.
I, Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty, was entrusted with heaven because of my holy virtues, possessing the world, and respect the Supreme Emperor, just as King Wen and King Wu of the Zhou Dynasty respected the Supreme King and Wang Ji.
The Supreme Emperor is the founder of the Han Dynasty, and future generations should respect him in order to promote Shan's kindness. This is the most important thing in filial piety.
"Shang Shu" says: If you can correctly examine the past history and use it to make meritorious deeds, you can enjoy eternal life, and the country can be passed down to descendants for generations and infinitely.
The emperor adopted his opinion and issued an edict to restore the emperor's mausoleum and temple garden.
Soon, the envoy went to Youzhou to inspect the situation of the refugees. He recommended those governors and officials with two thousand stones who could do their best to appease and attract the people. He also suggested that the ban on the state monopoly of the Bohai Sea salt ponds be temporarily lifted, allowing the refugees to boil salt to survive, so as to relieve the people's urgent needs.
Wherever he went, he was praised by the people. He was the most accomplished person among the eleven officials on diplomatic missions, and was promoted to Prime Minister Sizhi.
Later, he was demoted to the governor of Shuofang due to breaking the law. Soon he was recruited into the court and appointed as Taizhong doctor to Shizhong. His officials were Xin Shaofu, Dahonglu and Guangluxun.
Prior to this, Wei Wei Chunyu Changjin, the son of the Queen Mother's sister, said that Changling could no longer be built, and the emperor passed his opinions to the relevant departments for discussion.
Pingdang believed that Changling had been built for several years and it was better to continue the construction and complete it than to give up halfway.
Later, the emperor decided to stop the construction of Changling, and because it was Chun Yuchang who first proposed this suggestion, he issued an edict to ask the ministers to discuss the matter of knighting Chun Yuchang.
Pingdang also pointed out that although Chun Yuchang made good suggestions, he did not meet the conditions for knighthood.
Therefore, the emperor demoted Pingdang to Julu Prefect on the grounds that Pingdang had put forward incorrect opinions when discussing whether to stop the construction of Changling. Later, the emperor named Chunyu Chang.
Because Pingdang was proficient in the classic "Yu Gong", he was sent as an envoy to inspect the Yellow River, and was appointed as the cavalry captain and also in charge of the Yellow River embankment affairs.
After Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he recruited Pingdang to serve as Guanglu doctor and various officials as scattered cavalry. He was successively appointed as Guangluxun, Yushi doctor, and became prime minister.
Because it was the winter month, it was not the time to ennoble a marquis, so Emperor Ai first granted Ping the title of Marquis of Guannei.
In the spring of the next year, Emperor Ai sent an envoy to Zhao Pingdang to enter the court, preparing to make him a marquis.
Ping Dang is seriously ill and cannot answer the call.
Someone at home said to him: For the sake of your descendants, can't you force yourself to be sick and accept the title of marquis?
Pingdang replied: Now that I am in a high position, I have been criticized for not having merit and salary. Now I am forced to accept the title of Marquis, and then I lie down and die. I am guilty of death.
I am not accepting the title of Marquis now because I am thinking about my descendants!
summary: Biographies of several Han Dynasty officials, highlighting their careers, virtues, and interactions with authority. Ping Dang, from Pingling, was proficient in classics and served as prime minister under Emperor Ai. He argued for maintaining the Supreme Emperor’s mausoleum and temple gardens, citing filial piety. He also recommended relief for refugees and opposed granting a marquisate to Chunyu Chang, leading to his demotion. Later, he was recalled but fell ill, refusing to accept a marquisate under duress, and died after a month.

translation:
Jun Buyi's courtesy name is Manqian, a native of Bohai County.
Proficient in "Spring and Autumn", he served as county literary official. His words and deeds must follow etiquette standards, and he was famous in the state and county.
In the last years of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, thieves and thieves appeared in droves across the country. Baoshengzhi was appointed as the Zhizhi envoy. He wore bright embroidered clothes and held a sharp axe. He went to various places to suppress thieves and supervise the administration of county and state officials. His law enforcement scope reached as far as the coast of Shubu.
Those who disobey his orders will be punished with severe military laws, and his reputation shocked all states and counties.
Baosheng had long heard that Jun Buyi was very virtuous, so after he inspected Bohai County, he sent his entourage to invite Jun Buyi to come and meet him. Jun Buyi wore a Jinxian crown on his head, a sword decorated with beautiful jade and wood carving patterns on his waist, a jade pendant such as a ring and block on his body, a wide robe and wide robes, and went to pay homage to Baosheng's residence in full attire.
When they arrived at the gate of Baofu, the guard wanted Juan Buyi to take off his sword. Jun Buyi said, "The sword is a gentleman's weapon and equipment. It is used to protect one's body. It cannot be taken off casually."
If you insist that I take off my sword before letting me enter the riot, then please allow me to take my leave now.
The guard informed Baoshengzhi of the situation.
Baoshengzhi opened the door and invited Jun Buyi into the house. Seeing Jun Buyi's serious face, confident demeanor and neat and solemn clothes, Baoshengzhi hurriedly left his seat and stood up to greet him with his shoes on.
When the guests and hosts arrived and sat down in the hall, Jun Buyi straightened his waist and knelt down on the ground and said: I live in a remote coastal area and have heard of your reputation, Mr. Bao, for a long time, but I have never had the honor to meet and talk with you until today.
Generally speaking, as an official, if you are too firm, you will easily suffer setbacks, and if you are too weak, you will easily neglect government affairs. Therefore, the best way is to exercise dignity while giving favors, so that you can make achievements and keep your position forever.
Baoshengzhi knew that Jun Buyi was not an ordinary person, so he respectfully accepted his warning, received him with high etiquette, and asked him what measures and means should be adopted to govern under the current situation.
The staff of the tyrant government were all outstanding talents selected from the officials of various states and counties. They listened to Jun Buyi's conversation and were all shocked and impressed.
It wasn't until late at night that Jun Buyi left the house.
So after the sudden victory, he recommended Buyi to the imperial court. The emperor summoned Buyi to the public transportation department and worshiped him as the governor of Qingzhou.
After a long time, Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty passed away and Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty came to the throne. At this time, Liu Ze, the grandson of King Xiao of Qi, colluded with the heroes of the county and country to conspire to rebel. They planned to assassinate the governor of Qingzhou first.
Jun Buyi discovered the conspiracy of Liu Ze and others in time and arrested them all. Liu Ze and others all confessed to the crime.
Bu Juan was promoted to Jing Zhaoyin and was given millions of dollars.
The officials and people in the capital respected his authority.
summary: Jun Buyi, a native of Bohai, was known for his strict adherence to etiquette and expertise in the "Spring and Autumn." During the late years of Emperor Wu, he was summoned by the imperial envoy Baoshengzhi, who was impressed by his virtue. Jun Buyi arrived in full ceremonial attire, refusing to remove his sword, which he deemed a gentleman's essential tool. Baoshengzhi received him with respect, and Jun Buyi advised him to balance firmness with leniency in governance. Baoshengzhi recommended him to the court, and he became Governor of Qingzhou. He later thwarted a rebellion by Liu Ze, a grandson of the King of Qi, and was promoted to Jing Zhaoyin. His mother’s influence ensured he was dignified but not cruel in office. In the fifth year of Emperor Zhao’s reign, a man claiming to be Prince Wei appeared. Jun Buyi immediately arrested him, citing the "Spring and Autumn" to justify his action, earning praise from Emperor Zhao and General Huo Guang. He refused Huo Guang’s offer of marriage and later retired due to illness, dying at home. The imposter was later executed.
