translation:
In the third year of the Dijie period of Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty, he appointed the crown prince, Bingji as Taifu, and Shu Guang as Shaofu. A few months later, Bingji was promoted to imperial censor, and Shuguang was promoted to Taifu.
Shuguang's elder brother's son Shushou, named Gongzi, was also elected as the prince's family magistrate because of his virtuous character.
Shushou values ​​etiquette, is humble and prudent, has quick thinking and is good at speaking.
Once, Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty came to Prince Shu's palace, paid homage to him and answered Emperor Xuan's questions. He also arranged a banquet and toasted Emperor Xuan's birthday during the banquet. His words were etiquette, elegant and graceful, and Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty was very happy.
Soon, he worshiped Shushou as the prince's young master.
The prince's maternal grandfather, Tejin Ping Enhou Xu Bo, thought that the prince was young and asked Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty to let his younger brother Zhonglang General Xu Shun supervise the prince's family.
Emperor Xuan summoned Shu Guang about this matter, and Shu Guang replied: The prince is the crown prince of the country, and his teachers and friends must choose outstanding people in the world. He should not just be close to his relatives, the Xu family. Moreover, the prince already has a tutor and a young master as his assistant, and the palace setting is complete. Now Xu Shun is asked to supervise the prince's family. This kind of knowledge is really crude and is not conducive to showing the prince's kindness to the people of the world.
Emperor Yi agreed with Shu Guang's view and told the Prime Minister Wei Xiang about the matter. After hearing this, Xiang Wei took off his hat and apologized and said: Shu Guang's foresight and foresight cannot be matched by us ministers.
As a result, Shuguang won the respect of Emperor Xuan and received many awards and gifts.
Every time the prince went to court to see Emperor Xuan, he would always have the Taifu in front and the Young Fu behind him.
Shuguang and Shushou's uncles and nephews were both the prince's masters, and they were honored by everyone in the court.
Shu Guang served as the crown prince's tutor for five years. The crown prince reached the age of twelve and was already proficient in the Analects of Confucius and the Classic of Filial Piety.
Shuguang said to Shushou: I heard that people who are content will not suffer humiliation, people who know enough is enough will not be in danger, and they will retire after success, which is in line with the laws of heaven.
Now our uncle and nephew are officials, with a rank of two thousand shi, which can be said to be successful and famous. If we stop resigning now that it is not enough, I am afraid we will regret it in the future. Wouldn't it be nice for us, uncles and nephews, to resign together and return to our hometowns to support us in our old age?
Shushou kowtowed and said: "I will follow your old man's arrangements."
That day, both uncle and nephew wrote letters claiming to be ill.
Three months later, Emperor Xuan granted him an extension of leave, so Shuguang claimed that he was seriously ill. Shangshu asked to retire and return to his hometown. Since he was indeed old, the emperor agreed to their request and gave him twenty kilograms of gold, and the crown prince also gave fifty kilograms of gold.
The old relatives and friends of the ministers and officials of the DPRK, as well as people from the capital, held a farewell banquet for them outside the Dongdu Gate of Chang'an. There were hundreds of cars to see them off, and the uncle and nephew said goodbye one by one. The onlookers on the roadside praised them and said: "You are so good, these two doctors!"
Some people sighed and shed tears.
After Shuguang returned to his hometown, he asked his family to buy food and wine every day, and invited his clan members and old guests to have fun together.
He asked many times how much gold was left at home, and urged his family to exchange the gold for daily food and drinks.
More than a year later, Shuguang's descendants privately said to an old man among Shuguang's brothers who was close and trusted by Shuguang: We, the descendants, hope to buy some land and property during his lifetime.
Nowadays, there are banquets at home every day, and all the money the old man brought back is almost spent.
We would like to ask you to take our above ideas as your own and persuade him to purchase some land and real estate. The old man revealed this meaning to Shuguang during a casual chat. Shuguang said: Am I really an old fool and don't know how to think about my descendants?
summary: Shu Guang and his nephew Shu Shou served as tutors to the crown prince. Shu Guang, a native of Lanling, was learned in the "Spring and Autumn." He advised Emperor Xuan against appointing the prince’s maternal relative Xu Shun as supervisor, arguing that the prince’s teachers should be chosen from the world’s best. After five years, when the prince was proficient in the "Analects" and "Classic of Filial Piety," Shu Guang urged his nephew to retire with him, citing the principle of knowing when to stop. They resigned, receiving generous gifts of gold. Shu Guang used the gold to host feasts for his clan, refusing to buy land for his descendants, fearing wealth would lead to laziness or faults. He believed the emperor’s gift was meant for sharing with his community.

translation:
Yu Dingguo studied law with his father since he was a child. After his father's death, Dingguo also held official positions such as Prison History, County Judgment Cao, etc., and later supplemented the position of Court Weishi, and was selected to work with Yushi Zhongcheng to handle the prison cases of those who reversed the case. Because of his outstanding intelligence and ability in handling cases, he was promoted to Shi Yushi, and then to Yushi Zhongcheng.
When Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty passed away, King Changyi was summoned to succeed him. He behaved in an obscene manner and wrote a letter of remonstrance to Dingguo.
Later, King Changyi was deposed and Emperor Moxuan came to the throne. General Huo Guang took charge of the ministerial affairs. He wrote to the emperor in separate letters. All the ministers who had admonished King Changyi at that time were promoted in an unusual way.
As a result, Yu Dingguo was promoted to the official position of Guanglu. He was a minister of calligraphy and was very important.
A few years later, he was appointed Captain of Shuiheng and was promoted to Lieutenant of Ting.
Yu Dingguo then became a disciple and studied the "Spring and Autumn Annals". He held the scriptures in his hand and faced the north to perform the rituals of a disciple.
He was humble and respectful, and especially respected scholars who were proficient in classics. Even those who came to visit on foot were of low status, Dingguo treated them with equal etiquette, took good care of them, and treated them with utmost respect. Therefore, he was generally praised by scholars.
Yu Dingguo judges cases fairly and is as considerate as possible to widowers and lonely people. For crimes that are not particularly certain, he tries to be given a lighter sentence and pays special attention to maintaining a cautious attitude.
Everyone in the court praised him and said: "When Zhang Shizhi was appointed as a court officer, no one in the world was wronged; when he was appointed as a court officer in Dingguo, the people thought they were not unjust."
Yu Dingguo was a good drinker, and he could drink several stones without getting drunk. In the late winter, he was asked to handle cases and crimes, and he became more savvy after drinking.
After serving as a court lieutenant for eighteen years, he was promoted to the imperial censor.
During the Ganlu period, Dingguo replaced Huang Ba as prime minister and was named Xipinghou.
Three years later, Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan ascended the throne. Because Dingguo was an old minister of the previous emperor in office, Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty respected him very much.
At that time, Chen Wannian was appointed as the imperial censor and worked with Dingguo for eight years. There was no conflict between the two when discussing political affairs.
Later, Gong Yu replaced Chen Wannian as the imperial censor, and he often disagreed with Dingguo's political opinions. Since Dingguo was more knowledgeable and familiar with political affairs, Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty often agreed with Dingguo's opinions on many issues.
However, not long after Emperor Yuan came to the throne, Guandong suffered from successive disasters. People were displaced and flooded into the Guan. Someone wrote to the emperor and put the responsibility on the ministers in charge.
Emperor Yuan then summoned the prime minister and censor many times on the day of hearing the court, went into the palace to receive the imperial edict, and reprimanded them one by one with their duties, saying: The cunning and disloyal local officials were afraid of being punished for failing to catch thieves, so they arbitrarily harmed good people with suspicion, and even caused innocent people to die unjustly. Some officials did not immediately pursue the thieves after discovering them, but instead detained the families who had lost their property. As a result, the people later did not dare to report to the government if they were robbed by thieves. Therefore, disasters and bad habits gradually grew and expanded.
summary: Yu Dingguo, from Donghai, learned law from his father Yu Gong, a fair judge. Yu Gong had once protested the wrongful execution of a filial widow, which led to a three-year drought until her innocence was acknowledged. Yu Dingguo became a court official, studying the "Spring and Autumn" with humility. As Tingwei, he was known for leniency and fairness, earning praise that no one felt wronged under his jurisdiction. He served as imperial censor and later replaced Huang Ba as prime minister, being respected by Emperor Yuan. However, disasters in Guandong led to imperial reprimands. Yu Dingguo apologized and eventually retired, dying at over seventy. His son Yu Yong and grandson Yu Tian succeeded him, though Yu Tian lacked his ancestors’ virtues.

translation:
Crossing the river by boat is dangerous, but it is safer to cross the bridge. A wise king will not choose a dangerous path.
The advice of the imperial censor can be adopted.
The emperor said: Shouldn't the ministers advise like Zhang Meng?
So I accepted the suggestion and took a car across the bridge.
More than a month later, due to poor youth, a large number of people were displaced. Xue Guangde, Prime Minister Yu Dingguo, and General Shi Gao asked to resign and return home. They were all generously gifted by the emperor with a four-horse carriage, sixty kilograms of gold, and were relieved of their duties.
Xue Guangde served as the imperial censor for ten months and then was dismissed.
When he returned to his hometown of Pei County, the prefect of the county personally went to the border to greet him.
Peijun was proud of him and hung up the carriage given to him by the emperor to pass down to future generations.
Pingdang, named Zisi, his grandfather moved from Xiayi County to Pingling County because he had a millionaire.
When he was young, Pingdang served as the Li Cheng of Daxing. Because of his meritorious service, he was appointed as Dahonglu Literature. He was elected as the Chief of Shunyang and the Governor of Kuyi successively because of his integrity. He was recruited as a doctor because of his proficiency in Confucian classics. The ministers recommended Pingdang to be a minister because he was proficient in Confucian classics and his discussions were clear and transparent.
Whenever a disaster or disaster occurred in the country, Pingdang would discuss the gains and losses based on the classics.
Although the elegance of his words and diction is not as good as that of Xiao Wangzhi and Kuang Heng, the meaning is roughly the same.
During the reign of Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty, Wei Xuancheng was appointed prime minister and petitioned to abolish the mausoleum and temple gardens of the Supreme Emperor. Ping Dang wrote a letter saying: I heard that Confucius once said: If a king rises to rule the world, benevolence will be achieved in thirty years.
Within thirty years, morals were harmonious, ritual and music systems were complete, disasters were avoided, and troubles could not be tolerated.
Today, my sacred Han Dynasty has been governed by the mandate of heaven and has inherited the foundation left by the previous generation for more than two hundred years. It is diligent and does not dare to slack off, and its policies are clear and clear.
However, customs have not yet been harmonized, yin and yang have not yet been reconciled, and disasters have occurred frequently. I wonder if there is something important and fundamental that has not yet been established?
Otherwise, why have there been no auspicious signs of moral education for a long time?
Misfortunes and blessings do not appear without reason, they must occur due to some reason.
We should deeply explore its reasons and laws, and cultivate the fundamentals accordingly.
In the past, when Emperor Yao was the king and governed the world, he first appointed virtuous people of his own clan and placed them in prominent positions, so as to bring harmony to the nine clans and then to the neighboring states of the world. "The Classic of Filial Piety" says: Life in heaven and earth is precious to human beings. There is nothing more important in human behavior than practicing filial piety. The most important thing in practicing filial piety is to respect the father. To respect the father, there is nothing better than to share the benefits of fathers and ancestors when offering sacrifices to heaven. The Duke of Zhou is a person who can do this.
summary: Xue Guangde, from Pei, taught the "Book of Songs" and served as imperial censor. He was known for his outspoken advice, once urging Emperor Yuan to return from a hunt due to poverty in Guandong. Another time, he threatened suicide to prevent the emperor from crossing a river by boat, leading to a safer bridge crossing. After ten months, he resigned due to disasters and was dismissed, returning home with honor.

translation:
So he wrote a letter requesting to retire and return to his hometown.
Emperor Ai gave instructions: I selected you from among the ministers and appointed you as prime minister. You have not been assisting me in governing the affairs of the country for a long time. Now the yin and yang in the world are not harmonious, there is no heavy snowfall in winter, and there are droughts and disasters. This is all caused by my lack of virtue. How can I blame you?
Why do you have doubts and write a letter asking to retire and return to your hometown, and return the title and fiefdom of Guannei Marquis?
I asked Shangshu Lingtan to send you a cow and ten stones of good wine.
You should actively seek medical advice and take care of yourself.
More than a month later, Pingdang passed away.
His son Pingyan rose to the rank of Da Situ because he was proficient in classics and principles, and was named the Marquis of Fangxiang.
Since the establishment of the Han Dynasty, only Wei Xianhe and his son, both father and son, have held the position of prime minister.
Peng Xuan, courtesy name Zipei, was born in Yangxia, Huaiyang.
He studied the "Book of Changes" and studied under Zhang Yu. He was elected as a doctor and then appointed as the Taifu of Shuping Kingdom.
Zhang Yu was respected and trusted because he was the teacher of Emperor Mo Cheng. He recommended to the emperor that Peng Xuan was proficient in classics, steady and prestigious, and could serve as a court official. So Peng Xuan entered the court as You Fufeng, and soon moved to Tingwei. Later, because the early Han Dynasty stipulated that people from various vassal kingdoms were not allowed to serve as officials in the capital, he became the prefect of Taiyuan County.
A few years later, he entered the capital and served as Da Sinong, Guang Luxun, and General You.
After Emperor Ai of Han came to the throne, he was appointed General Zuo.
More than a year later, Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty planned to appoint his relatives, Ding and Fu, to be in charge of the royal guards, so he wrote to Peng Xuan: Relevant departments have reported many times that people from the princely kingdoms cannot serve as royal guards. General, because you are from the kingdom, you are not suitable to be in charge of the army and hold a high position.
I consider that General, you have the important task of being a general of the Han Dynasty, and your son has previously married the daughter of the King of Huaiyang. There is a marriage relationship between your family and the kingdom, but you are an official in Beijing. This is not in line with the national system.
I asked Dr. Guanglu Man to reward you with fifty kilograms of gold and a four-horse carriage. You can return General Zuo's seal and ribbon and return to your hometown as the Marquis of Guannei.
In the years after Peng Xuan was dismissed from office and returned to his hometown, Bao Xuan, the remonstrating doctor, wrote many times to recommend him.
It happened that there was a solar eclipse on the first day of the first month of the first year of Yuanshou, and Bao Xuan recommended him again. Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty summoned Peng Xuan to the court as Guanglu doctor, and was promoted to Yushi doctor, and later to Da Sikong, and was granted the title of Marquis of Changping.
When Emperor Ai of the Han Dynasty passed away, Wang Mang, the lord of the new capital, became the Grand Sima and took over the power of the government.
Peng Xuan wrote a letter saying: The three princes are like the three legs of a tripod, supporting the monarch together. If one of the legs is incompetent, there is a danger of overturning the delicious food in the tripod.
summary: Peng Xuan, from Huaiyang, studied the "Book of Changes" and served as a general. Emperor Ai dismissed him due to his kingdom origins, but he was later recalled. After Emperor Ai’s death, Wang Mang took power, and Peng Xuan resigned, citing old age. Wang Mang, resenting his resignation, denied him customary gifts. Peng Xuan died in his fief, and his title was later abolished.

translation:
I have little talent, am old, faint, frail and sick, and my memory is failing. I hope that I can be allowed to hand over the seals and ribbons of Da Sikong and Changping Marquis and return to my hometown to spend my remaining years.
Wang Mang reported the matter to the Queen Mother, who issued a policy letter to Peng Xuan, saying: You have not been in charge of political affairs for a long time and have not yet established outstanding merits. However, due to old age and confusion, you are unable to assist the country and stabilize the country.
I have asked Guang Luxun to issue an edict to you. Please present the seal and ribbon of Da Sikong and return to your feudal country.
Wang Mang resented Peng Xuan for resigning and returning home when he was specialized in government affairs, so he did not give Peng Xuan gold, carriages and horses as usual.
Peng Xuan died a few years after returning to the feudal state, and was given the title of Marquis of Qing.
His title was passed down to his sons and grandsons. After Wang Mang failed to usurp power, the title was abolished.
Praise: Jun Buyi participated in government affairs as a well-educated person, was not confused when encountering difficulties, had outstanding achievements, and started well and ended well.
It is also advisable to retreat from the rapids to avoid humiliation and danger.
Yu Dingguo's father and son sympathized with the widowers and understood the situation in prison, so they were competent ministers.
Xue Guangde retained the glory of Xuanchao, Ping Dang had the sense of shame to retreat, and Peng Xuan resigned resolutely when he saw the dangerous situation. They are different from those villains who can do any treacherous thing because they are afraid of losing their vested interests.
summary: The text concludes with praise for these officials: Jun Buyi for his wisdom and achievements, Shu Guang for timely retirement, Yu Dingguo for his fairness, and Xue Guangde, Ping Dang, and Peng Xuan for their integrity, contrasting them with those who cling to power.

translation:
Huo Guang, courtesy name Zimeng, was the younger brother of Huo Qubing, the general of the Hussars.
His father, Zhong Ru, was from Pingyang, Hedong Province. He served in the Pingyang Hou family as a county official and had an affair with his maid Wei Shaoer and gave birth to Huo Qubing.
After Zhongru completed his errand, he returned home and married again and gave birth to Huo Guang. He broke off the relationship with Wei Shaoer and had no contact with him.
After some time, the boy's younger sister Zifu became favored by Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty and was made the queen. Huo Qubing had a distinguished status and was favored by the emperor because he was the son of the queen's sister.
After Huo Qubing grew up, he learned that his father was Huo Zhongru, but he never had time to visit him.
It happened that Huo Qubing was appointed as a hussar general and went to attack the Xiongnu. He passed by Hedong. The governor of Hedong went to the outskirts of the city to greet him. He led the way with a bow and arrow on his back and rested at the reception area of ​​Hou Jiabao in Pingyang.
Huo Qubing sent a small official to invite Huo Zhongru to meet him. Zhongru hurried over and greeted him respectfully. Huo Qubing stepped forward to greet him and bowed down. He knelt down and said, "Qubing didn't know that I was your flesh and blood."
The middle child kowtowed to the ground and said, "This veteran can entrust his destiny to the general. This is God's help."
Qubing bought a large number of fields, houses, and slaves for Zhongru and left.
When returning to the army, Huo Qubing passed by Hedong again, so he took Huo Guang to Chang'an. Huo Guang was only ten years old at the time, so he appointed Huo Guang as Lang, and soon he was promoted to the minister of all Cao Cao.
After Qu Bing's death, Huo Guang was granted the title of Guanglu, the Commander-in-Chief of the Fengcha. He accompanied the emperor as a chariot when traveling, and served around him in the palace. He had been in and out of the forbidden palace for more than 20 years. He had always been cautious and made no mistakes. He was very close and trusted by the emperor.
In the second year of Zhenghe, Prince Wei was framed and defeated by Jiang Chong. King Liu Dan of Yan and King Liu Xu of Guangling both made many mistakes.
At this time, the emperor was old, and his beloved concubine Gou Yi and Zhao Jieyu gave birth to a boy. The emperor planned to pass the throne to him and ordered ministers to assist him.
The emperor observed that among the ministers, only Huo Guang could take on the important task of assisting the country.
The emperor then asked the court painter to draw a picture of Duke Zhou carrying King Cheng on his back to receive congratulations from the princes, and gave it to Huo Guang.
In the spring of the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, the emperor traveled to Wuzha Palace and became very ill. Huo Guang asked in tears: If something happens to the emperor, who will succeed him?
The emperor said: Don't you still understand the meaning of the painting I gave you last time?
When you establish a young son as emperor, you should act like the Duke of Zhou assisting the king.
Huo Guang kowtowed and said humbly: I am not as good as Jin Rixi.
Jin Rixi also said: I am a foreigner, not as good as Huo Guang.
The emperor then appointed Huo Guang as the Grand Sima General, Jin Rixi as the Chariot and Cavalry General, Shangguan Jie, the imperial servant, as the General of the Left, and Sang Hongyang, the captain of the Sosu Su Army, as the Imperial Censor. They all kowtowed before the bed in the emperor's bedroom and accepted their duties, accepting orders to assist the young monarch.
The next day, Emperor Wu died, and the prince inherited the throne and was called Emperor Xiaozhao.
The emperor was only eight years old, and Huo Guang made all political decisions.
Before this, in the first year of Hou, the servant Shemang Heluo and his younger brother Hou Mangtong conspired to rebel. At that time, Huo Guang, Jin Rixi, Shangguan Jie and others killed these rebels, and their achievements were not recorded and rewarded.
After Emperor Wu fell ill, he sealed the seal and said: After I die, I will open the seal and follow it.
summary: Huo Guang, courtesy name Zimeng, was the younger half-brother of the renowned general Huo Qubing. Their father Zhongru served as a county official in the Pingyang Hou family and had an affair with the maid Wei Shaoer, fathering Huo Qubing. After completing his duties, Zhongru returned home, married, and fathered Huo Guang, severing all ties with Wei Shaoer. When Huo Qubing later learned of his father's identity while serving as a hussar general attacking the Xiongnu, he visited Zhongru in Hedong, purchased lands and slaves for him, and took ten-year-old Huo Guang to Chang'an. Huo Guang was appointed as Lang and later promoted to various positions. After Huo Qubing's death, Huo Guang served as Guanglu and Commander-in-Chief, accompanying Emperor Wu for over twenty years with cautious conduct, earning the emperor's complete trust. As Emperor Wu aged and Prince Wei was defeated, the emperor chose his young son as heir and entrusted Huo Guang with assisting him. He gave Huo Guang a painting of Duke Zhou carrying King Cheng, symbolizing his expectations. When Emperor Wu fell ill at Wuzha Palace, he appointed Huo Guang as Grand Sima General, along with Jin Rixi, Shangguan Jie, and Sang Hongyang as co-regents. After Emperor Wu's death, the eight-year-old Emperor Zhao ascended the throne, with Huo Guang making all political decisions. Huo Guang was calm, thoughtful, and meticulous in his conduct, maintaining consistent positions when entering and leaving the palace gates.

translation:
In addition, Sang Hongyang, the imperial censor, suggested setting up a liquor monopoly and salt and iron official management system, which increased the country's wealth. Sang Hongyang took credit for it and planned to get official positions for his children, but failed, so he resented Huo Guang.
So Eyi Gaizhu, Shangguan Jie, Shangguan An and Sang Hongyang conspired with the King of Yan Liu Dan, pretending to have someone write a letter on behalf of the King of Yan, saying: Huo Guang went out of the city to practice Lang Guan and Yu Lin. He set up a dignified manner on the road like an emperor when traveling, and also asked the eunuchs to prepare meals in advance.
Also, Su Wu was sent as an envoy to the Huns, and was detained for twenty years without surrendering. After returning, he was only made a vassal state, while Yang Chang, the chief general of the general, had no merit, but became the captain of Sosu. Huo Guang also transferred in without authorization to increase the number of captains in his shogunate.
Huo Guang is arrogant in his power, I'm afraid he has bad intentions.
The minister Liu Dan is willing to return the Fujie Seal of King Yan and serve as a guard in the court to investigate the conspiracy of the treacherous minister.
When Huo Guang was on leave from the palace, he took the opportunity to present this book.
Shangguan Jie planned to report the matter directly from the palace, so Sang Hongyang and other ministers arrested Huo Guang and dismissed him from his post.
After the memorial was handed in, Emperor Zhao kept the memorial and refused to issue it.
The next morning, Huo Guang heard about this and stayed in the studio in front of the palace without going in to worship.
The emperor asked where the general was?
Shangguan Jie, the general of the left, replied: Because King Yan reported his crime, he did not dare to come in.
The emperor issued an edict to summon the general.
After Huo Guang came in, he took off his official hat and kowtowed to apologize. The emperor said: General, please put on your hat. I know that this memorial is fake and the general is not guilty.
Huo Guang asked: How does your majesty know that I am not guilty?
The emperor said: "The general arrived in Guangming, and the training of lieutenants was only a recent matter. It has only been ten days since the selection of lieutenants. How did King Yan know these things?"
Besides, if a general wants to do something illegal, he doesn't need a lieutenant.
At this time, Emperor Zhao was only fourteen years old. The minister and the ministers around him were surprised. The person who submitted the letter actually escaped, and the government began an urgent search. Shangguan Jie and others were frightened, so they told the emperor that this was just a trivial matter and not worth pursuing. The emperor did not listen.
Later, whenever Shangguan Jie's party members spoke ill of Huo Guang, Emperor Zhao became angry and said: "The general is a loyal minister, entrusted by the late emperor to assist me. If anyone dares to slander him, he will be punished."
From then on, Shangguan Jie and others did not dare to say bad things anymore, so they conspired to have the eldest princess prepare a banquet for Huo Guang, preparing to ambush soldiers to kill him, and then take the opportunity to depose Emperor Zhao and install King Yan as emperor.
When the incident was discovered, Huo Guang executed Shangguan Jie, Shangguan An, Sang Hongyang, Ding Wairen and their families.
King Yan and Lord Gai also committed suicide.
Huo Guang's power shocked the whole country.
After Emperor Zhao came of age, he formally appointed Huo Guang to be in power. By the 13th year of Emperor Zhao's reign, the people's lives were abundant and abundant, and all ethnic minorities from all over the world had surrendered.
In the first year of Yuanping, Emperor Zhao died without an heir.
Among the six sons of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, only King Liu Xu of Guangling is still alive. The ministers discussed the candidate to be appointed, and everyone advocated the establishment of King Guangling.
King Guangling was originally not selected by the late emperor because of his immoral behavior.
Huo Guang felt uneasy inside.
A Lang official wrote: King Zhou deposed his uncle and established Wang Ji, King Wen abandoned Boyikao and established King Wu. As long as it is beneficial to the country, it is okay even to depose the eldest son and establish a younger son.
King Guangling could not inherit the ancestral temple and the state.
What he said coincided with Huo Guang's thoughts.
Huo Guang showed this memorial to Prime Minister Yang Chang and others, and promoted the official to the prefect of Jiujiang. On the same day, according to the empress dowager's edict, he sent Shaofu Lecheng, Zongzheng Liu De, Guanglu doctor Bingji, and Zhonglang general Lihan to meet the Changyi king Liu He.
Liu He was the grandson of Emperor Mowu and the son of King Ai of Changyi.
summary: Huo Guang's daughter married Shangguan Jie's son Shangguan An, whose daughter became Emperor Zhao's empress. However, conflicts arose when Huo Guang refused to grant titles to Ding Wairen, a favorite of the Grand Princess Eyi Gaizhu. Shangguan Jie, his son, Sang Hongyang, and the Grand Princess conspired with King Liu Dan of Yan, sending a false letter accusing Huo Guang of arrogance and improper conduct. Emperor Zhao, only fourteen, saw through the deception, noting that the letter mentioned events that occurred only ten days prior, which King Yan could not have known. The conspirators then plotted to assassinate Huo Guang, but their scheme was discovered. Huo Guang executed Shangguan Jie, Shangguan An, Sang Hongyang, Ding Wairen, and their families, while King Yan and the Grand Princess committed suicide.

translation:
After he arrived in the palace and ascended to the throne of God, he soon began to act lewdly.
Huo Guang was worried and angry, so he went to ask his close confidant, Chief Farming Yannian, about the matter alone.
Tian Yannian said: As the pillar of the country, since the general found that this person cannot be entrusted to the country, why not report it to the Queen Mother and choose another worthy person to make him emperor?
Huo Guang said: I want to do this too. I wonder if there is any precedent for this in ancient times?
Tian Yannian replied: When Yi Yin became the prime minister of the Yin Dynasty, he deposed Taijia to stabilize the country. Later generations praised his loyalty.
If a general could do the same, he would be Yi Yin of the Han Dynasty.
Huo Guang introduced Tian Yannian to the minister, and secretly planned with the cavalry general Zhang Anshi, so he summoned the prime minister, censor, generals, princes, Zhongerqianshi, doctors, doctors, etc. to discuss the matter together.
Huo Guang said: "The king of Changyi behaves in a cowardly and promiscuous manner, which may endanger the country. What do you think we should do?"
All the ministers were frightened and did not dare to speak. They were only obedient.
Tian Yannian left his seat and came forward, holding his sword in his hand and said: The late emperor entrusted the young orphan to the general and entrusted the world to the general because the general was loyal and capable and could stabilize the Liu family's world.
Now the ministers and the people are in an uproar, and the country is about to overthrow. Moreover, the emperors of the Han Dynasty often used the word "filial piety" in their honorifics, in order to control the world for a long time and allow the ancestral temple to enjoy sacrifices forever.
Now that the Han family is about to cut off its incense, even if the general is willing to die to apologize, how can he have the dignity to go to Jiuquan to see the late emperor? Today's discussion should be resolved immediately.
If any of the ministers delays answering, I request that he be beheaded with this sword.
Huo Guang apologized and said: Jiu Qing is right to blame me.
The world is in turmoil and I should be punished.
So the ministers who participated in the discussion kowtowed and said: "The lives of all the people are tied to the general. We are willing to obey the general's instructions."
Huo Guang immediately went to see the Queen Mother with his ministers and stated in detail the situation that King Changyi could not inherit the throne.
The empress dowager then drove to Weiyang Chengming Palace and ordered the guards of each palace not to let the officials of King Changyi enter the palace.
King Changyi went to the palace to meet the Queen Mother and returned, preparing to take a chariot back to the greenhouse. The eunuchs of the Huangmen in the palace each held a door leaf. After King Changyi entered, they closed the palace door, so that the officials of King Changyi could not enter.
The king of Changyi asked: What is this?
The general knelt down and said: The empress dowager has an edict not to allow the officials of King Changyi to come in.
King Changyi said: Slow down, why do you have to make it so scary!
Huo Guang sent people to expel all the officials of King Changyi from the palace and gathered them outside the Golden Horse Gate.
The cavalry general Zhang Anshi led the Yulin knights to arrest and tie up more than 200 people, and handed them over to Tingwei to be imprisoned in the prison specified by the imperial edict.
He also ordered the former Zhaozhong Shizhong and Zhongchangshi to guard the king of Changyi.
Huo Guang warned them: You must be careful of the guards on duty. If King Changyi dies suddenly or commits suicide, I will be blamed for killing the king.
The king of Changyi did not know that he was about to be deposed at this time, so he said to the people around him: What are the crimes of my former ministers and entourage, and the general imprisoned them all.
Soon, the Queen Mother issued an edict to summon the King of Changyi. When the king of Changyi heard that he was about to be summoned, he began to be afraid, so he said: "What crime have I committed? I want to summon the queen mother of our factory. She is wearing a short coat embellished with pearls and dressed in fine clothes. She is sitting in a curtain decorated with weapons. Hundreds of palace guards are holding weapons, and Qimen warriors are guarding the steps with halberds. They are all lined up with His Highness."
The ministers walked into the palace in order and asked the king of Changyi to lie in front and listen to the edict.
Huo Guang and other ministers jointly signed a memorial to impeach the king of Changyi. The minister read out the memorial and said:
Your Majesty the Prime Minister Yang Chang, Your Majesty the Sima General Huo Guang, Your Majesty the Chariot and Cavalry General Zhang Anshi, Your Majesty the General Fan Mingyou of the Liao Dynasty, Your Majesty the Former General Han Zeng, Your Majesty the Later General Tong Chongguo, Your Majesty the Censor Cai Yi, Your Majesty the Marquis of Yichun Wang Tan, Dang Tuhou Wei Sheng, Chen followed Taohou to Changle, Chen Duhou Fulu Tuqitang, Chen Taipu Du Yannian, Chen Taichang Suchang, Chen Dasi Nanfang Yannian, Chen Zongzheng Liu De, Chen Shaofu Shi Lecheng, Chen Tingwei Li Guang, Chen Zhijin I am Li Yanshou, I am Da Honglu Wei Xian, I am on the left Feng Yi Tian Guangming, I am on the right Fufeng Zhou De, I am Chang Xin Shaofu Fu Jia, I am Dian Su Wu, I am Jing Fu Duwei Zhao Guanghan, I am Si Lixiao Wei Pi Bing, and I am Wen Guang Dr. Lu Wang Qian, Chen Song Wei, Chen Bingji, Chen Ci, Chen Guan, Chen Sheng, Chen Liang, Chen Changxing, Chen Xia Housheng, Chen Taizhong Dafu De, and Chen Tangyin reported to Her Majesty the Empress Dowager: Chen Yang Chang and others were sentenced to death.
The reason why the emperor was able to maintain the ancestral temple and control the world for a long time was because he could take kindness, filial piety, etiquette and justice, and clear distinction between rewards and punishments as the foundation.
Emperor Xiaozhao passed away prematurely and had no heir. His minister Yang Chang and others discussed it and concluded that according to the rites, "the person who is a person's heir is his son" and the King of Changyi was suitable to be the heir. So they sent Zongzheng, Dahonglu, Guanglu and other officials to serve as envoys on Fu Jie to recruit the King of Changyi to preside over the funeral of Emperor Zhao.
After the king of Changyi put on mourning clothes, he showed no sign of mourning. He also ignored etiquette and righteousness. He refused to eat vegetarian food on the road. He sent his officials to rob women and took them to the post house where he lived in a covered car.
summary: After Emperor Zhao died without an heir, the ministers initially considered King Liu Xu of Guangling, but Huo Guang opposed this due to the king's immoral character. Following a suggestion from a Lang official citing historical precedents, Huo Guang arranged for the installation of King Liu He of Changyi. However, Liu He soon began behaving lewdly and improperly. Huo Guang, troubled by this, consulted with Tian Yannian, who cited the precedent of Yi Yin deposing Taijia. Huo Guang gathered the ministers, and after Tian Yannian threatened those who hesitated with execution, they agreed to depose the king. Huo Guang reported to the Empress Dowager, who issued an edict. The ministers jointly impeached King Changyi for numerous offenses during his twenty-seven-day reign, including failing to observe mourning, engaging in debauchery, and issuing over 1,127 orders for various items. The Empress Dowager approved the deposition, and Huo Guang personally removed the imperial seal from King Changyi, who was sent back to his former residence.

translation:
Huo Guang sat in the court and discussed with the ministers below the prime minister to decide on the candidates.
King Guangling had not been selected long before this, and when King Yanla was executed for his rebellion, his son was no longer in the discussion.
Among the close relatives, only the grandson of Prince Wei is still known as Huang Zeng among the people and is generally praised.
Huo Guang then submitted a memorial together with Prime Minister Yang Chang and other ministers: "The book "Li" says that if you can love your relatives, you can respect your ancestors, and if you can respect your ancestors, you can respect the ancestral temple.
Now that the great clan has no heir, he should choose a worthy person from the descendants of his side as his heir.
Emperor Xiaowu's great-grandson was ill. Emperor Wu had Shaoling to raise and take care of him in Yeting. Now he is eighteen years old. He studied "Poetry", "The Analects of Confucius" and "The Classic of Filial Piety" as a teacher. He practiced frugality and was kind and loving. He could inherit the throne of Emperor Xiaozhao, serve his ancestors and rule the people.
I risked my life to tell you.
The Empress Dowager issued an edict: "It must be played accurately."
Huo Guang sent Zongzheng and Liu De to his great-grandson's home, Shangguanli, to help him wash and bathe, and gave him the emperor's clothes. He asked the servant to take his great-grandson to Zongzheng's mansion in a light car to fast, and then went to Weiyang Palace to see the empress dowager. He was named Marquis of Yangwu.
Soon Huo Guang held the emperor's seal and went to the Gaomiao to pay homage, becoming Emperor Xiaoxuan.
The next year, the emperor issued an edict saying: It is common practice in ancient and modern times to praise those who are virtuous and reward those who have made great achievements.
Huo Guang, the great general of Sima, guards the court with loyalty and integrity, promotes morality and shows kindness, preserves integrity and upholds benevolence and righteousness, so as to stabilize the ancestral temple.
Seventeen thousand households in Hebei and Dongwuyang were granted to Huo Guang.
Including his previous fiefdom, there were a total of 20,000 households.
He was rewarded seven thousand catties of gold, sixty million in money, thirty thousand pieces of silk of various colors, one hundred and seventy slaves, two thousand horses, and a first-class residence.
From the time of Emperor Zhao, Huo Guang's son Huo Yu and Huo Guang's brother's grandson Huo Yun were already Zhonglang Generals. Huo Yun's younger brother Huo Shan served as Fengche Captain and Shizhong, and controlled the military power of Hu and Yue.
Huo Guang's two sons-in-law are the guards of the East and West Palaces respectively. The sons-in-law and grandsons of Huo Guang's brothers are eligible to participate in court meetings, serve as Cao officials, cavalry captains, and receive official positions in the affairs.
Factions and relatives were united and occupied the court in an intricate manner.
Huo Guang had been the prime minister of the government since the Hou Yuan Dynasty. He did not return the government until the emperor ascended the throne.
The emperor was humble and refused to accept it. He had to consult Huo Guang for instructions on all political matters before reporting them to the emperor.
Every time Huo Guang went to court to see him, the emperor was humble and serious, and treated him with great respect and courtesy.
Huo Guang was in power for twenty years. In the spring of the second year of Dijie, he became seriously ill. The emperor personally went to his home to see his condition and shed tears for him.
Huo Guang wrote a letter to express his gratitude and said: I would like to use the three thousand property of my feudal land to enfeoff my brother's grandson, Fengche Captain Huo Shan, as a lord, in order to worship my brother Hussar General Huo Qubing.
The emperor handed over the matter to the Prime Minister and Censor, and appointed Huo Guang's son Huo Yu as the right general on the same day.
After Huo Guang passed away, the emperor and the empress dowager personally went to Huo Guang's mourning hall to express their condolences.
summary: Huo Guang then arranged for the installation of Emperor Wu's great-grandson, who was living among the people, as Emperor Xuan. For his services, Huo Guang received additional fiefdoms totaling 20,000 households, along with gold, money, silk, slaves, and horses. His family members held numerous important positions throughout the court. Huo Guang remained in power for twenty years until his death, after which he was buried with great honors at Maoling and given the title Xuanchenghou.

translation:
Zhang Zhang, a man from Chang'an, reported the matter, and Emperor Xuan handed the matter over to Tingwei.
Zhi Jinwu arrested Zhang She, Shi Xia and others, but was later stopped by the Shao Order and no arrests were allowed.
Huo Shan and others were even more panicked and said to each other: "This is because the emperor values ​​the queen mother's face, so he didn't go into details."
But the bad omen has appeared, and there is also the poisonous murder of Queen Xu. Even if His Majesty is lenient and kind, he is afraid that the people around him will not listen and will still investigate after a long time. Once found out, the clan will be exterminated. We might as well take action first.
So they asked their daughters to go back and tell their husbands, saying: Where is there any place to take refuge?
It happened that Li Jing was convicted for colluding with the princes, and the Huo family was involved in his confession. Emperor Xuan went to Shao and said that Huo Yun and Huo Shan were not suitable to serve in the palace, and he was dismissed from office and returned home.
Huo Guang's daughters were rude to the Queen Mother, and Feng Zidu broke the law several times. The emperor scolded them together, which made Huo Shan, Ting Wei and others feel very frightened. In the dream, I saw the well water in the house overflowing and flowing into the hall, and the stove in the kitchen was hung on a big tree. I also dreamed that the general said to Xian: Do you know that our son is going to be arrested?
They'll be here soon to catch you. There were suddenly more rats in the house, colliding with people and scribbling on the ground with their tails.
Owls hooted several times in the trees in front of the temple.
The door of the house was broken for no reason, and the door of Huo Yunshang Guanli's house was also broken for no reason.
People in the streets and alleys saw someone sitting on Huo Yun's roof. They took off the tiles and threw them on the ground. They went to look, but saw no one. They felt very strange.
In his dream, Huo Yu heard the noise of carriages and horses coming to capture him. The whole family felt sad about these strange things.
Huo Shan said: The prime minister arbitrarily reduced the number of lambs, rabbits, and frogs offered to the ancestral temple. This can be used to convict him.
They conspired to ask the Queen Mother to set up a banquet for Lord Boping, summon the prime minister and officials below Ping'enhou, and have Fan Mingyou and Deng Guanghan take these people out and behead them on the Queen Mother's order, taking the opportunity to depose the emperor and make Huo Yu the emperor.
Before the agreed plan was implemented, Huo Yun was appointed as the prefect of Xuantu, and Ren Xuan, the Taizhong doctor, was appointed as the prefect of Daijun.
Huo Shan also broke the law for copying the palace secretaries. Xian wrote a letter expressing his willingness to donate his mansion in the west of the city and a thousand horses to atone for Huo Shan's crime.
Emperor Xuan only approved it in his memorial. Just when their plot was discovered, Huo Yun, Huo Shan, and Fan Mingyou committed suicide, and Xian, Huo Yu, Deng Guanghan and others were captured.
Huo Yu was cut in half, and several of her daughters and brothers were executed.
Only Empress Huo was deposed and imprisoned in Zhaotai. Thousands of families were implicated in the Star Doctor and were convicted and executed to exterminate their clans.
Emperor Xuan then issued an edict saying: Not long ago, Shi Zhangshe, the commander of the Zhishi Office, instructed Li Jing, a wealthy family in Wei County, to reply to Guanyang Hou Huoyun and conspire to cause rebellion. Because of the general, I suppressed the matter and did not make it public, hoping that they could change Bai Xin.
Now the great Sima Bo, Lu Hou Huo Yu, his mother, Xuancheng Hou's wife Xian, and their cousin's sons, Guanyang Hou Huoyun, Leping Hou Huoshan, and their sisters' sons-in-law, are conspiring to harm the people.
Thanks to the blessing of the ancestors, they were discovered and captured in advance, and all of them were executed according to law. I am very sad about this matter.
All those who were implicated by the Huo family, if the incident occurred before Bingshen and had not yet discovered that the reporting officer was in custody, will be pardoned.
The man Zhang Zhang discovered the incident first and told Dong Zhong of Qimen. Dong Zhong reported it to Zuo Cao Yang, and Yang Pan reported it to Shizhong Jin Anshang.
Yang Fan was summoned to state the situation, and later Zhang Zhang wrote a report.
Shi Gao and Jin Anshang, the servants, suggested reporting the matter. If the Huo family was not allowed to enter the palace ban, the Huo family's conspiracy did not succeed. They were both equally meritorious.
Zhang Zhang was specially granted the title of Marquis of Bocheng, Dong Zhong was the Marquis of Gaolu, Yang Peng was the Marquis of Pingtong, Jin Anshang was the Marquis of Ducheng, and Shi Gao was the Marquis of Leling.
At the beginning, the Huo family lived a luxurious life, and Xu Sheng of Maoling said: The Huo family will definitely perish.
summary: After Huo Guang's death, his wife Xian and their sons Huo Yu, Huo Yun, and Huo Shan became increasingly arrogant and extravagant. Xian had previously poisoned Empress Xu to install her daughter as empress, a secret that Huo Guang had concealed. As Emperor Xuan gradually reduced the Huo family's power, they grew fearful and plotted rebellion, planning to depose the emperor and install Huo Yu. The conspiracy was discovered, leading to Huo Yun, Huo Shan, and Fan Mingyou committing suicide, while Xian, Huo Yu, and others were executed. The Huo clan was exterminated, and Empress Huo was deposed.

translation:
After Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Jin was rewarded as a royal servant. Something about the Huo family began to show up, so he wrote a letter requesting to divorce his wife.
The emperor also felt pity for him, but he was the only one who was not implicated in the crime.
During the reign of Emperor Yuan, he was awarded a gold reward by Ren Guangluxun. After his death, he had no sons and the feudal kingdom was removed.
In the middle of the Yuan Dynasty, the extinct ancestral sacrifice was restored, and Jin Jian's grandson Jin Dang was granted the title of Jiehou, as a descendant of Jin Rihun.
At the beginning, Jin Rihun took his younger brother Jin Lun, named Shaoqing, who surrendered with him, and served as Huangmenlang. He died early.
Jin Yuehui's two sons were both prominent, but they declined in the generation of his grandson. However, Jin Lun's descendants began to prosper, and his son Jin Anshang became prominent and was granted the title of marquis.
Jin'an, named Zihou, was a servant in his youth. He was honest and resourceful, and Emperor Xuan liked him very much.
He took an active part in exposing the conspiracy of Chu King Liu Yanshou to rebel. He was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and 300 households with food.
Later, the Huo family rebelled, and Jin An issued an order to close the palace gates and not let the Huo family's relatives in. He was also named Duchenghou, and later promoted to Jianzhang Weiwei.
After his death, the cemetery was given to Du Ling and he was named Jinghou.
Jin Anshang has four sons, namely Jin Chang, Jin Chang, Jin Cen and Jin Ming.
Jin Cen and Jin Ming were both appointed as generals among various Cao officials, and Jin Changguan was appointed as Guanglu doctor.
When Emperor Yuan was still the prince, Jin Chang was a concubine and was fortunate to be favored by the prince. After the prince ascended the throne, Jin Chang was appointed as the Cavalry Commander Guanglu, and the Zhonglang General served in the palace. After the death of Emperor Yuan, according to the past practice, ministers close to him would go to the imperial mausoleum to guard the tomb. Because Jin Chang was famous for his loyalty and filial piety for generations, he was left to serve the emperor by the Empress Dowager Shao.
Jin Chang was an upright man and dared to offend the majesty of the monarch. Everyone around him was afraid of him. Even Emperor Yuan was in awe of him.
When Jin Chang was seriously ill, Emperor Yuan sent an envoy to ask him what he wanted, and Jin Chang asked for an official title for his younger brother Jin Cen.
Emperor Yuan summoned Jin Cen and made him the envoy's host and guest.
Jin She, the son of Jin Chang, originally served as Zuo Cao. Emperor Yuan appointed Jin She as his minister and sent someone to drive him to the official residence of the Weiwei in the emperor's grand car.
Soon Jin Chang died.
Jin Chang had three sons, Jin She, Jin Can, and Jin Rao.
Jin She was proficient in classics, honest, loyal and moral, and was praised by Confucian scholars.
When he became emperor, he was appointed as the cavalry captain in the imperial palace, commanding the Hu and Yue cavalry of the three auxiliaries.
After Emperor Ai ascended the throne, Jin She was appointed as the captain of Fengche, and his official position reached Changxin Shaofu.
Jin Shen went to the Xiongnu as an envoy and served successively as the Xiongnu Zhonglang General, the Yue Cavalry Colonel, the Commander-in-Chief of the Pass, and the Prefect of Anding and Shuhai.
Jin Rao was appointed as the captain of the Yue cavalry.
Jin She had two sons, Jintang and Finance, both of whom served as ministers to various Cao, generals and officials.
Jin She's cousin Jin Qin was promoted to the Ming Dynasty, and his official position was Taizimen Dafu. After Emperor Ai came to the throne, he was appointed Taizhong Dafu to Shizhong. Jin Qin's cousin Jin Qian was appointed Shangshuling, and both brothers were in power.
When Emperor Ai's grandmother, the Empress Dowager Fu, died, Jin Qin was in charge of the burial. After the incident, he was promoted to the prefect of Taishan and Hongnong, and became famous for his authority.
After Emperor Ping ascended the throne, he was appointed as the Grand Sima Sizhi and Jing Zhaoyin.
Emperor Ping was young and chose to set up mentors and friends. Kong Guang, the great Situ, was chosen as the Master of the Kong family because of his proficiency in Confucian classics and his noble conduct. Jingzhao Yin Jinqin was elected as the friend of the Jin family because of his family's loyalty and filial piety for generations.
He was promoted to the rank of Attendant of Guanglu Dafu, received a salary of two thousand dan, and was granted the title of Marquis.
At that time, Wang Mang had just killed Emperor Hu's uncle, the Wei family, and summoned Mingli Shaofeng Zong Bofeng to the palace to lecture on the behavior of descendants. He ordered the ministers, generals, ministers, and court officials to attend the lecture, hoping to warn Emperor Ping internally and block the discussion of the people externally.
Jin Qin and his cousin Jiehou Jindang were both granted the title of marquis.
It turned out that Jin Hui, the great-grandfather of Jin Dang, passed down the title to his son Jiehou Jinshang, and Jin Qin's grandfather Jin An passed it down to his son Jinchang, the Marquis of Yi. None of them had any sons, and the feudal state was abolished, so Wang Mang rewarded Jin Qin and Jindang as the descendants of Jin Rixi and Jin An.
Jindang's mother Nan is also the sister of Wang Mang's mother Gong Xianjun.
Jin Dang sent a letter to Daxing on behalf of his mother, requesting the title of Tai Fu.
Jin Qin looked for an opportunity and said to Jin Dang: "The edict only talks about Jin Rihun's merits and does not mention the gold reward."
As the grandson of the Jin Dynasty, he inherited his ancestors, so he naturally had to build a temple for his father and grandfather.
Jinshang is the king of the former fiefdom, and he should also ask the doctor to perform sacrifices for him.
Zhen Han was nearby at that time, so he rebuked Jin Qin in the court and impeached him, saying: Jin Qin was lucky enough to be promoted to serve the emperor because of his proficiency in classics. He was also favored and given a title, which made him know that the dynasty has the etiquette and righteousness of being a descendant for generations.
The previous time, the late Empress Dowager Dingtao had forgotten her roots and rebelled against heaven. Xiao Ai was not protected by her. Lu Kuan and Wei Shi also launched treacherous plots and even rebelled against the law.
summary: Jin Rixi, originally a Xiongnu prince, was captured as a slave after his father King Xiutu was killed. He served as a horse keeper but caught Emperor Wu's attention through his dignified bearing and honest answers. He became a trusted attendant, known for his loyalty and filial piety. He killed his own son for improper behavior with palace servants and later helped thwart a rebellion by Mang Heluo. When Emperor Wu appointed regents, Jin Rixi served as Huo Guang's deputy, refusing a marquisate due to Emperor Zhao's youth. His descendants continued serving the Han court for seven generations, maintaining a reputation for loyalty and filial piety.

translation:
Wei Xian, whose courtesy name is Changru, was born in Zou, State of Lu.
His ancestor was Wei Meng, who originally lived in Pengcheng and was the Fu of King Yuan of Chu. He was also the Fu of King Yuan's son, King Yi, and his grandson, Liu Wu.
Liu Wu was dissolute and disobedient, so Wei Meng wrote poems to ridicule and admonish him.
Later, Wei Meng resigned from his official position, moved his family to Zoudi, and wrote another remonstrative poem.
His admonition poem said:
Our solemn and great ancestors founded the country from the time of Weishi, wearing fur clothes decorated with ax-shaped patterns and Zhu Fu decorated with "Ya" patterns, driving a chariot drawn by four male horses, with dragon pins on them.
He was given the Tong Gong and was responsible for conquests; he pacified the people in remote areas, took charge of many states, and assisted the Shang Dynasty. Later, there was Dapeng, who also made outstanding achievements.
By the time of the Zhou Dynasty, our Chu state had been among the princes for several generations and participated in alliances.
Later, King Nan of Zhou believed the slander and deprived us of the title of Chu State.
Our Chu State has severed relations with the Zhou Dynasty, and the laws of the Zhou Dynasty are no longer implemented in the Chu State. The matter of rewards and punishments was no longer decided by the Zhou Dynasty.
The ministers of the imperial court and the princes and princes no longer assisted and protected the Zhou Dynasty; the five areas around the capital fell apart, and Zong Zhou collapsed like this.
Our ancestors also declined and migrated to Pengcheng. In our generation, life is really hard-working.
Facing the disaster of being bullied by the powerful Qin, the late king had to go to the fields to cultivate the land himself.
The arrogant and arrogant Qin State, God will not bless them. God favored and blessed the south, and granted the capital of the Qin Dynasty to the Han Dynasty. The establishment of the Han Dynasty was truly great, with conquests in all directions. Everywhere they went surrendered, and thousands of states were at peace.
He appointed his younger brother to establish a marquis and a state in the Chu land; let us, the little ministers, assist the King of Chu carefully.
He is the king of the Yuan Dynasty who is diligent and conscientious. He is respectful, diligent and frugal and lasts for a long time. He blesses all the people with happiness and health, and appoints assistants and ministers to recruit virtuous people.
After reigning for nearly thirty years, his legacy was passed down to his descendants; later he was succeeded as King Yi, who was able to carry on the legacy.
It is a pity that King Yi did not live long. King Wu ascended the throne and was succeeded by King Wu. All the ministers around him, gentlemen and gentlemen, are all pillars.
Why does our king not consider preserving the ancestral heritage? Why does he not think about the difficulties of walking on thin ice, so as to inherit and carry forward the ancestral heritage!
The country's major affairs are neglected, and they wander around for endless entertainment all day long; the hounds and horses are beautiful and majestic, running here and there in front and behind.
He loves animals and birds wholeheartedly, but neglects farm work and forgets about crops. The people were in want because of this, and the king took pleasure in it.
What is promoted is not virtue, and what is close to is not talent. Just expanding the garden, just getting close to villains.
A flattering person, an upright gentleman; why doesn't the king clearly understand this?
summary: Wei Xian, courtesy name Changru, was from Zou in the State of Lu. His ancestor, Wei Meng, served as a tutor to King Yuan of Chu and his descendants. Because Liu Wu was dissolute, Wei Meng wrote poems to admonish him, then resigned and moved his family to Zoudi, where he wrote another remonstrative poem. This poem recounts the history of their lineage from the Shang Dynasty through the Zhou, the decline of Chu, and the rise of the Han Dynasty. It criticizes the current king for neglecting state affairs, indulging in pleasure, and surrounding himself with flatterers, warning him to learn from past examples. Wei Meng later died in Zoudi. It was passed down for five generations to Wei Xian.

translation:
Some people say that his descendants wrote this poem because they did good deeds and recalled the ambitions of their ancestors.
It has been passed down for five generations from Wei Meng to Wei Xian.
Wei Xian was a simple man with a pure heart and few desires. He devoted himself to learning. He was proficient in "Li" and "Shangshu" and taught "Poetry" to others. He was called the great Confucian of Zou Lu.
Later, the imperial court recruited him as a doctor and appointed him as an official. He entered the palace to teach Emperor Zhao to study "Poetry", and was slowly promoted to Guanglu doctor Zhan Shi, and later to Dahonglu.
Emperor Zhao died without an heir, so the general Huo Guang and the ministers honored him as Emperor Xiaoxuan.
Emperor Xuan had just ascended the throne. Wei Xian was given the title of Marquis of Guannei and had a household to worship him because he participated in the plan to support Emperor Xuan, stabilize the country and stabilize the country.
Moved to the Shaofu of Changxin Palace. Because Wei Xian was once the teacher of Emperor Zhao, he was very respected.
In the third year of Benshi, Wei Xian replaced Cai Yi as prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Fuyang, with a settlement of 700 households.
At that time, Wei Xian was over 70 years old. He had been prime minister for five years and had been in Jiji for three years. He asked the court to resign because of his old age and illness. The court rewarded him with one hundred catties of gold, dismissed him and returned to his hometown, and also gave him a mansion.
The resignation of the prime minister began with Wei Xian.
Wei Xian died at the age of eighty-two, and the imperial court gave him the title of Jiehou.
Wei Xian had four sons: the eldest son, Wei Fangshan, served as the magistrate of Gaodi County and died very early; the second son, Wei Hong, was promoted to the prefect of Shuhai; the third son, Wei Shun, stayed in Lu to guard the cemetery of Wei's ancestral hall; the youngest son, Wei Xuancheng, was promoted to the position of prime minister many times because of his proficiency in Confucian classics.
Therefore, there is a proverb in Zoulu: It is better to leave a box full of gold to your son than to leave him a scripture.
Wei Xuancheng, a young man, was appointed as a Langguan and a regular attendant on Sanqi due to his father's favor.
He was eager to learn when he was young and inherited his father's Confucianism. He was extremely humble and courteous to virtuous people.
Sometimes when he went out and met people he knew on foot, he would always ask his attendants to get off the car and take them back as a normal thing.
He treated people, including the poor and humble, with even greater respect, and his reputation spread far and wide.
Because he was proficient in Confucian classics, he was promoted to the position of admonishing doctor and then moved to the rank of captain of Dahe County.
At the beginning, Xuancheng's elder brother Wei Hong was serving as Taichang Cheng, and his duties were to guard the ancestral temple and be in charge of the imperial tombs and gardens. Because of the complicated affairs, he committed many crimes.
His father Wei Xian, because Wei Hong should be the heir of the Wei family in the future, was afraid that he would be deposed for committing crimes, so he ordered Wei Hong to resign from the official position of Taichang Cheng due to illness. However, Wei Hong was humble and refused to resign.
When Wei Xian became seriously ill, Wei Hong was finally imprisoned for not being considerate in guarding the ancestral temple, and had not yet been convicted.
The family members asked Wei Xian who should be the heir to the Wei family, but Wei Xian showed an expression of anger and hatred and refused to speak.
So Wei Xian's disciple, Dr. Yi Qian, and others discussed with Wei Xian's clan members, pretending that it was Wei Xian's order, and asked the general manager of the Wei family to write a general order to establish Wei Xuan, the captain of Dahe County, as the successor of the Wei family.
After Wei Xian's death, Xuancheng heard the bad news in his official position and heard that he should be the heir. Xuancheng knew that dismissal was not what his father Wei Xian had always meant, so he pretended to be insane, urinated and defecated in bed, talked nonsense, and laughed wildly.
The imperial court summoned him to Chang'an. After the funeral, Wei Xuancheng was supposed to inherit his father's title, but Xuancheng pretended to be insane and ignored the imperial edict.
Da Honglu wrote to the court, and the court issued documents to the prime minister and censor, asking them to investigate and handle the matter.
Xuancheng always had a good reputation. Many scholar-bureaucrats believed that Xuancheng wanted to give up his title to his brother Wei Hong, so he pretended to be insane.
Prime Minister Shi, who was in charge of the investigation, then wrote to Xuancheng, saying: The ancients must have a decent name when they resigned, so that their reputation can be passed down to future generations.
summary: Wei Xian was a simple, pure-hearted man devoted to learning. He was proficient in the "Li" and "Shangshu," taught the "Poetry," and was called the great Confucian of Zou Lu. He was recruited as a doctor, taught Emperor Zhao the "Poetry," and was promoted to Guanglu doctor Zhan Shi and later Dahonglu. After Emperor Zhao died without an heir, Wei Xian was made Marquis of Guannei for his role in supporting Emperor Xuan. He became Shaofu of Changxin Palace and was highly respected. In the third year of Benshi, he became prime minister and was granted the title of Marquis of Fuyang. Over seventy, he served for five years before resigning due to illness, receiving gold and a mansion. His resignation began the practice of prime ministers retiring. He died at eighty-two and was given the title of Jiehou. Wei Xian had four sons. The eldest, Wei Fangshan, died early. The second, Wei Hong, became a prefect. The third, Wei Shun, guarded the ancestral cemetery. The youngest, Wei Xuancheng, became prime minister due to his knowledge of the classics. A proverb in Zoulu stated it was better to leave a son a classic than a box of gold. Wei Xuancheng was appointed as a Langguan due to his father's favor. He was eager to learn, humble, and respectful to all, earning a wide reputation. He was promoted to admonishing doctor and then captain of Dahe County. When Wei Xian was ill, he was angry that Wei Hong, who was supposed to be the heir, was imprisoned for a crime. Wei Xian's disciple and clan members, pretending it was his order, established Wei Xuancheng as the successor. Xuancheng knew this was not his father's wish, so he feigned insanity to avoid inheriting the title. The court investigated, and many believed he was trying to give the title to his brother. The prime minister and censor impeached him for feigning illness, but the emperor did not punish him and instead called him to serve. Xuancheng accepted the title. Emperor Xuan made him governor of Henan and his brother Wei Hong a captain. Xuancheng later became a guard in Weiyang Palace and was promoted to Taichang. Due to a mistake during a rainstorm when he rode instead of using a four-horse cart to the ancestral temple, he was demoted to the rank of Guannei Marquis. He was deeply saddened and wrote a poem blaming himself, lamenting his loss of title and vowing to be more careful.

translation:
The emperor is solemn and solemn, treating him as his teacher; people from far and near admire the glory of our kingdom.
The inheritance of the ancestral fiefdom should be my handsome eldest brother; but my handsome eldest brother has repeatedly shown humility to show his benevolence and justice.
How beautiful his character is, how resounding his reputation is; my ancestors left their official titles to me, so I stayed in the capital.
But as a humble person, I was careless in respecting important court gatherings; I was lazy and messy in formal dress and chariots, so I was deposed as a vassal by the court.
I lost my glorious and distinguished title; I began to incur the humble status of a vassal.
Who can endure such shame? Lend me your face; who wants to travel to distant places?
Let me go with him to that wild place. The honorable position of the Three Lords is not something that a talented person cannot hold; even though I am humble, I will eventually sit in such a high position.
Who said Huashan is high? I hope to be as high as it; who said practicing virtue is difficult? I hope I can achieve it through hard work.
Oh, little me, I can never make such a mistake again; I ruined my good reputation by saying these sad words.
Princes and kings everywhere should learn from me; their attire, chariots and chariots should be dignified and orderly, and their steps should be solemn and dignified.
At the beginning, Huaiyang Xianwang, the son of Emperor Xuan's favorite concubine Zhang Jieyu, liked to handle state affairs and was familiar with the law. The emperor appreciated his talents and intended to make him his heir. However, because the prince was born in poverty and lost his mother early, he could not bear to depose the prince.
After a long time, Emperor Xuan wanted to influence King Xian from the side and make him understand, so he wanted people who knew etiquette and resignation to assist him, so he summoned Wei Xuancheng and worshiped him as the lieutenant of Huaiyang.
At this time, King Xian had not yet taken office in his own kingdom. Xuancheng accepted Shao's order and discussed the similarities and differences of the scriptures with the prince Taifu Xiao Wangzhi and the Confucian scholars who were responsible for the "Five Classics" in Shiquhe, and wrote an entry to inquire the emperor.
After Emperor Yuan came to the throne, he appointed Xuancheng as Shaofu, promoted to Prince Taifu, and later became Yushi Dafu.
During the Yongguang period, Wei Xuancheng replaced Yu Dingguo as prime minister.
Wei Xuancheng was demoted for about ten years, and then took the official position of the prime minister where his father had been. He was also made a marquis in the original feudal country, and he was honored in the world.
Xuancheng wrote another poem in which he expressed the difficulty of getting up from mistakes and used it to admonish his descendants. The poem said:
A solemn gentleman cultivates his own virtue by behaving dignifiedly. He treats etiquette and dress respectfully and is neat and tidy to serve as a model.
Alas, I am a humble person, but my virtue is not as good as theirs. I was deprived of my title because I was careless in dress, carriage and carriage.
The sage emperor has outstanding virtues; he did not abandon me in the end and let me rank among the nine ministers.
Since I received such a favor from the emperor, I have been careful day and night, warning myself to exercise self-discipline and not to neglect my duties as an official.
The emperor was aware of my situation and promoted me to the position of Prime Minister among the three nobles. Considering that I was sad about my past mistakes and losing my title, I restored my original title.
After I ascended to the official position, I looked at the old steps and house; my late father once lived in this house, and recalling it made me very nostalgic and sad.
The Prime Minister, Sizhi, and those who helped manage the political affairs, assisted me very well and made my career prosperous; all the ministers and officials came to congratulate me.
Alas, these officials have really different thoughts from mine; no one is willing to sympathize with me despite how difficult things are.
Although I have spent all my energy on the grand Three-Gong affair, I am afraid that this is not an official position that I can hold for a long time. I don’t know if I will be demoted one day.
In the past, when I was demoted, I was afraid that I would not be able to achieve such a high position; now that I am the Prime Minister, I am very worried and afraid.
Oh, my descendants, you must know that destiny is impermanent; find ways to be your officials well and don't be idle in handling government affairs.
Be cautious about important court affairs, be careful about dressing up for car and car battles, don't be ungraceful, and keep your fiefdom well.
Don't look at me and imitate me, being careless and untidy like me; the restoration of my official position is a blessing from God.
Oh, juniors, be careful.
summary: Later, Emperor Xuan wanted someone to influence King Xian of Huaiyang, so he appointed Wei Xuancheng as the lieutenant of Huaiyang. After Emperor Yuan came to the throne, Xuancheng became Shaofu, Prince Taifu, and Yushi Dafu. During the Yongguang period, he replaced Yu Dingguo as prime minister, returning to the same position his father held. He wrote another poem admonishing his descendants to be careful in their duties and dress. He served as prime minister for seven years, surpassing his father in literary talent but not in ethical stability. He died in the third year of Jianzhao and was named Gonghou. He requested to be buried with his father, which was granted. His descendants inherited his title.

translation:
Since Gong Yu advocated that the sacrificial temples should be destroyed one after another, the sacrificial temples of Emperor Xiaohui, Emperor Xiaojing, and Emperor Taishang were all abandoned as ruins, which was inconsistent with etiquette and justice.
In the first year of Emperor Ping's reign, Grand Sima Wang Mang reported: In the first year of this year, Prime Minister Cai Yi and others planned to call the place where Emperor Xiaoxuan's father was worshiped mourning garden and set up three hundred restaurants. In the first year of Yuankang, Prime Minister Wei Xiang and others submitted a memorial, saying that his father was an ordinary scholar and his son became the emperor. The sacrifices to his father should also follow the emperor's etiquette. The mourning garden should be respectfully called "Huang Kao". A sacrificial temple was built, and the original number of residents in the garden increased to 1,600 families, forming a county.
I think the Huang Kao Temple should not have been built in the first place and it is not correct to keep it for generations.
In addition, although Empress Dowager Xiaowen's Nanling Mausoleum and Empress Dowager Xiaozhao's Yunling Garden were no longer repaired according to etiquette and law, the names of the mausoleums are incorrect.
I respectfully discussed with Grand Situ Yan and other 147 people, and we all believed that Emperor Xiaoxuan was the grandson of Emperor Xiaozhao's brother and succeeded him as emperor. According to etiquette, in the past during the reign of Emperor Xiaoyuan, all the descendants of Emperor Xiaojing Temple and Huangkao Temple were not destroyed, so the temples were not destroyed.
In this way, the country has two roots and two founding fathers, which is not in line with the etiquette system.
At that time, Cai Yi asked the emperor's father Mi to give him the title. The formation of the formation and the establishment of the gardens and towns to be guarded are all in line with the classics and meanings.
The Prime Minister of Wei requested that the mourning garden be called Huang Kao, a sacrificial temple be built, and the number of people who guarded the cemetery be increased to form a county. This far deviated from the original tradition of the ancestors and was inconsistent with etiquette and justice.
When the father is an ordinary scholar and the son becomes the emperor, he must sacrifice his father according to the emperor's etiquette. This refers to people like Yu Shun, Xia Yu, Yin Tang, King Wen of Zhou, and Han Gaozu who were ordered by heaven to proclaim themselves kings and found the country. It does not refer to people who inherit the inheritance of their ancestors and become queens.
I request Emperor Gaozu to destroy the Fengming Garden where the temples are visited and no longer repair them. Nanling and Yunling should be abolished and built into counties.
Wang Mang's memorial was approved.
Situ Peng Ban Biao said: The Han Dynasty was founded after the Qin Dynasty extinguished scholarship, and the ancestral system was determined according to the times.
Since Emperor Yuan and Emperor Cheng, there have been more and more scholars. Gong Yu proposed to destroy the ancestral temples one after another, Kuang Heng changed the Jiao Zhao, and He Wu decided on the Three Gongs. Later, there were many iterations, and there was no customization.
What is the reason?
This is because the etiquette documents are missing and the ancient and modern systems are different and unique. It is not easy to formulate them all.
Looking at the plans of those Confucian scholars, Liu Xin can be said to be profound and profound.
summary: The text then discusses the system of ancestral temples. During Emperor Gaozu's reign, temples were built in various vassal states. Over time, many temples were established. During Emperor Yuan's reign, Gong Yu proposed destroying temples that did not conform to ancient rituals. After discussion, many temples were abolished. Later, due to the emperor's illness and dreams, some temples were restored, but the ancestral temples in vassal states were ultimately abandoned. After Emperor Yuan's death, Kuang Heng proposed further abolitions. During Emperor Ai's reign, a debate occurred about whether to destroy Emperor Xiaowu's temple.
