Some argued for its preservation due to his great achievements, while others argued for its destruction based on ritual. The emperor adopted the suggestion to preserve it. During Emperor Ping's reign, Wang Mang proposed destroying the Huangkao Temple and other gardens, which was approved. The historian Ban Biao noted that the Han dynasty's ancestral system was determined according to the times, and the plans of the Confucian scholars, particularly Liu Xin, were profound.

translation:
Han Xin was born in Huaiyin County.
The family is poor and has no good character. He cannot be elected to be an official, and he cannot do business to make a living. He often lives in other people's homes and eats nothing.
His mother passed away and was too poor to bury her, so he found a high, dry place with spacious surroundings as a cemetery so that tens of thousands of families could be placed next to the grave in the future.
Han Xin once went to the countryside to eat at the pavilion chief's house in Nanchang. The pavilion chief's wife hated him so much that she got up very early to prepare the meal and put it on the bed to eat.
When it was breakfast time, Han Xin went and no meal was prepared for him.
Han Xin understood her intention and left her, never to interact with her again.
Han Xin once went fishing in the city. An old woman was rinsing silk cotton wool. She took pity on him and gave him food. This continued for dozens of days until the rinsing was completed.
Han Xin said gratefully to his old mother: I will definitely repay you heavily in the future.
The old man was very angry after hearing this and said, "You are a man and can't support yourself. I gave you food out of pity for you, a young man. Do I want you to repay me?"
A young man in Huaiyin City bullied Han Xin and said: Although you are tall and like to wear swords, you are actually very timid.
He insulted Han Xin in public and said: If you are not afraid of death, stab me with a sword; if you are afraid of death, get under my crotch.
So Han Xin stared at the young man carefully, then bent down and crawled under his crotch.
People watching the excitement on the street laughed at Han Xin and thought he was cowardly.
When Xiang Liang led his army across the Huai River to the north, Han Xin took his sword and went to him, and became an unknown soldier under Xiang Liang.
After Xiang Liang failed, he returned to Xiang Yu, who made him a doctor.
Han Xin repeatedly offered advice to Xiang Yu, but Xiang Yu did not adopt it.
Liu Bang, the king of Han, entered Hanzhong, and Han Xin escaped from the Chu army and joined the king of Han. At the beginning, he was still unknown and worked as a granary management clerk.
Later, he was sentenced to death for breaking the law. Thirteen of his accomplices were beheaded. When it was Han Xin's turn, Han Xin looked up and happened to see Teng Gong Xia Houying, so he asked: Doesn't the King of Han want to unify the world?
Why kill the strong man?
Teng Gong felt that Han Xin's words were unusual and he looked very powerful, so he did not kill him.
After talking to Han Xin, he was very happy and reported his situation to the King of Han.
The King of Han appointed Han Xin as the Commander-in-Chief of Su Su, but did not reuse him.
Han Xin talked with Xiao He many times, and Xiao He appreciated his talent very much.
When the Han army arrived at Nanzheng, dozens of generals escaped halfway.
Han Xin considered that Xiao He and others had recommended him to the King of Han several times, but he still could not be reused, so he ran away.
Xiao He heard that Han Xin had escaped. He had no time to report to the king of Han, so he went to chase him himself.
Someone reported to the King of Han: Prime Minister Xiao He has escaped.
The king of Han was furious, as if he had lost his left and right hands.
Two days later, Xiao He came to see the King of Han.
The King of Han was both angry and happy, and scolded Xiao He: "Why did you run away?"
Xiao He replied: How dare I run away? I am chasing those who run away.
summary: Han Xin, born in Huaiyin, was poor and unable to become an official or engage in trade. He often relied on others for food. After his mother died, he buried her on a high, spacious site, hoping for future grandeur. He once ate at a pavilion chief's home, but the chief's wife resented him and prepared meals early, leaving none for him at breakfast. Han Xin understood and left. While fishing, an old woman rinsing silk fed him for dozens of days. Grateful, he promised to repay her, but she scolded him, saying she pitied him, not expecting repayment. A young man in Huaiyin insulted Han Xin, daring him to fight or crawl under his crotch. Han Xin stared, then crawled through, enduring public ridicule. Han Xin joined Xiang Liang's army as a soldier, then served Xiang Yu as a郎中, offering advice that was ignored. He later defected to Liu Bang, King of Han, as a仓管员. Sentenced to death for a crime, he appealed to Teng Gong Xia Houying, who spared him after a conversation. Liu Bang made him a治粟都尉 but didn't value him. Han Xin fled when not promoted, but Xiao He chased him back. Xiao He convinced Liu Bang to formally appoint Han Xin as a大将, with a ceremony. Liu Bang asked Han Xin for strategies. Han Xin analyzed Xiang Yu's weaknesses—his inability to delegate, stinginess with rewards, and cruelty—contrasting Liu Bang's potential to win hearts by appointing capable men, rewarding merit, and respecting the people's wishes. He predicted easy conquest of the Three Qin states. Liu Bang followed his plan, marching east through Chencang to pacify the region. Han Xin was later made King of Qi. After Xiang Yu's death, Liu Bang demoted him to King of Chu. Han Xin rewarded the old woman who fed him and the young man who humiliated him, making him a lieutenant. When Liu Bang suspected him of rebellion, Han Xin was captured and made Marquis of Huaiyin. He feigned illness, avoiding court. Later, he plotted with Chen Xi to rebel but was betrayed. Empress Lü and Xiao He tricked him into the palace, where he was executed, his clan exterminated. Before death, he regretted not following Kuai Tong's advice.

translation:
Then he marched to attack the grasshopper.
The king of Wei deployed heavy troops in Zhayuan and blocked Linjin Pass.
Hanzhi then set up additional suspects, deployed his boats, and pretended to cross the river from Zhuozhi. He also sent a concealed ambush force to cross the river from Xia Yang with wooden urns and basins of floating water to sneak attack Anyi.
King Wei Bao of Wei was greatly frightened and hurriedly led his troops to attack Zhengzhi. He captured Wei Bao and put Mi down.
After that, Han Xin sent someone to see the King of Han and said: I hope to increase the number of 30,000 troops. I request to take advantage of the victory and march north to conquer the two countries Yan and Zhao, attack Qi to the east, cut off Chu's grain routes to the south, and finally go west to join forces with the king in Rongyang.
The King of Han agreed to give Han Xin 30,000 more troops, and sent Tan Dan and Han Zhi to attack Zhao Er and Ji Er to the north.
He defeated the attacking army and captured Xia Yue alive in the hammer.
After Kongcao captured Chongxiao and Zhuyou, the King of Han sent people to call back his elite troops and marched to Rongyang to resist the Chu army.
Han Xin and Zhang Er led tens of thousands of troops and wanted to march eastward to capture Jingxing and attack Zhao.
King Chu and Chen Yu, Lord of Cheng'an, heard that the Han army was about to attack Zhao, so they gathered a heavy army to guard Jingxingkou, claiming to have an army of 200,000.
Lord Guangwu Li Zuoche gave advice to Lord Chengan and said: I heard that the Han general Han Xin crossed the Xihe River, captured the king of Wei, and captured Xia Shuo alive. They had just fought a bloody battle to break up the alliance.
Now with Zhang Er as an assistant, he plans to attack Zhao. This is a battle far away from the country while taking advantage of the victory. The attack is unstoppable.
But I heard that when military rations are transported from thousands of miles away, the soldiers will look hungry; when firewood and grass are temporarily used for cooking, the army often cannot eat enough. Nowadays, the road in Jingxing is narrow and cannot pass two parallel chariots.
I hope you can lend me 30,000 elite troops for the time being to intercept their supplies of food and supplies from the small road. You must dig trenches deep, build forts high, and refuse to fight.
They can't engage in battle if they move forward, and can't go back if they retreat. I lead a surprise attack force to cut off their retreat, so that they can't plunder any food in the wild. In less than ten days, the heads of the two generals will be delivered to your tent.
I hope you will seriously consider my strategy, and I guarantee that you will not be captured by these two people.
Cheng'anjun is a nerd, and often claims that a just army does not use deceit and trickery. He said: I heard that in the art of war, if the force is ten times more than the enemy, you can surround them, and if you have more than twice the force, you can fight. Now Han Xin's army is said to be tens of thousands, but in fact it is not that many. They have traveled thousands of miles to attack us, and they are exhausted.
If we are unable to retreat from such an enemy now, how will we resist if we encounter a more powerful enemy in the future?
The princes will think that we are timid and attack us easily.
Therefore, he did not adopt Lord Guangwu's strategy.
Han Xin sent spies to find out that Chen Yu did not adopt Lord Guangwu's strategy and came back to report. Han Xin was overjoyed and dared to lead his army there.
summary: In the second year of Han, Liu Bang conquered Wei and Henan, then attacked Pengcheng but was defeated. Han Xin later joined forces to defeat Chu troops. After Wei Bao rebelled, Han Xin, as左丞相, attacked Wei. He feigned a river crossing at Linjin while secretly crossing at Xiayang, capturing Wei Bao. Han Xin then requested 30,000 troops to conquer Yan, Zhao, and Qi. Liu Bang agreed, sending Zhang Er and others. Han Xin defeated Zhao at Jingxing, using a背水阵 (back-to-water formation) to inspire his troops to fight desperately. He captured King Zhao Xie and killed Chen Yu. Han Xin spared Li Zuoche, who advised against attacking Yan and Qi directly, suggesting instead to intimidate Yan into surrender and then approach Qi. Han Xin followed this, and Yan surrendered.

translation:
When King Xiang heard the news, he sent Cao Jiu to garrison Chenggao, and he went eastward to recover the cities occupied by Pengyue. These cities were all returned to the Chu State.
Peng Yue led his troops to retreat north to Gucheng.
King Xiang retreated south to Yangxia, and Peng Yue captured more than 20 cities near Changyi and obtained more than 100,000 hu of grain to supply the King of Han with military provisions.
The king of Han lost the battle and summoned Peng Yue, asking him to join forces to attack the Chu army. Peng Yue said: Wei Di had just been pacified not long ago, but he was still afraid of the Chu army's attack and could not go.
The king of Han pursued the Chu army and was defeated by Xiang Yu at Guling.
Then he said to Zhang Liang, the remaining lord, "What should I do if the armies of the princes do not obey the deployment?"
Liu Hou said: Peng Yue originally pacified the Liang region and made great contributions. The king originally appointed Peng Yue as the prime minister of Wei because of Wei Bao.
Now Wei Bao is dead and has no descendants, and Peng Yue also wants to be king, but the king decided not long ago to make him king.
Now if he captures the area north of Suiyang up to Gucheng, he will use it to make him king.
He also talked about the reasons why Han Xin was banned in the past.
This incident is recorded in "Gao Ji".
At that time, the king of Han sent envoys to Pengyue to follow Liu Hou's plan.
As soon as the envoy arrived, Peng Yue led his troops to join Gaixia.
After Xiang Yu died, he granted Pengyue the title of King of Liang and established his capital in Dingtao.
In the sixth year of the Han Dynasty, Peng Yue went to Chen County to meet Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty.
In the ninth and tenth years, they all came to Chang'an to see him.
Su Peng rebelled in the cutting area, so he chose Hutong to go to Handan to fight against him personally. He then went to Handan to recruit troops from the King of Liang.
The king of Liang claimed to be ill and sent his generals to Handan.
Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty was angry and sent someone to blame King Liang.
King Liang was afraid and wanted to go to plead guilty in person.
His general Hu Zou said: Your Majesty did not go at first, and only went after being scolded. If you go there you will be captured, so why not send troops there?
King Liang refused to listen and still said that he was ill.
The servant of the King of Liang committed a crime and fled to Emperor Gao of the Han Dynasty to report the King of Liang and Hu Zui for their rebellion.
So Emperor Mogao sent envoys to make a surprise attack and captured King Liang, imprisoning him in Luoyang.
After review by the officials in charge, it is deemed that the crime has constituted treason. Please judge according to law.
The emperor pardoned him, demoted him to civilian status, and exiled him to Qingyi County, Shu County.
He escorted him westward to Zhengdi, where he met Empress Lu who was coming from Chang'an to the east. She was going to Wuchang, but encountered a chasm on the way.
Qi Yue cried to Dan Hou and told him that he was innocent and hoped to be exiled to his hometown Changyi.
Queen Lu agreed and ordered him to tie it up together.
When they arrived in Luoyang, Empress Lu told the emperor: Peng Yue is a strong man. If he is exiled to Shu, he will bring trouble to himself. It is better to kill him now.
I asked him to come with me.
At this time, Empress Lu asked Peng Yue's retainers to report him for another rebellion.
summary: Peng Yue, from Changyi, was a fisherman and bandit. He led a group of youths, enforcing strict discipline. He joined Liu Bang but later served Xiang Yu. After Xiang Yu's defeat, Liu Bang made him King of Liang. Accused of rebellion, he was captured, exiled, and killed by Empress Lü, his clan destroyed.

translation:
After the emperor was informed by Tingwei, Peng Yue and his clan were killed.
Ting Bu, a native of Liu County, originally had a surname of Ying.
When he was young, a guest told him that he could become king after being tortured.
When he reached his prime, he broke the law and was punished by Tao Bu. Tao Bu smiled happily and said, "Someone told me that after being punished, I would become king. Isn't that what it is?"
Everyone who heard this laughed at him.
Tingbu was sent to Lishan for hard labor for committing a crime. There were hundreds of thousands of prisoners in Lishan. Tinghu had contacts with the leaders and heroes among the prisoners, and finally led this group of people to escape to the Yangtze River and became a group of bandits.
When Chen Sheng raised his troops, Qing Bu went to meet Wu Rui, the magistrate of Fan County. At that time, Jing Bu had thousands of troops.
The county magistrate married his daughter to him.
Zhang Han destroyed Chen Sheng and defeated Lu Chen's army. Yingbu led his troops north to attack the troops of the left and right captains of the Qin army. He defeated them at Qingbo and led his troops to advance.
Yingbu heard that Xiang Liang had pacified Kuaiji, so he crossed the Huai River to the west and surrendered his troops to Xiang Liang.
Xiang Liang attacked Jingju, Qinjia and other places to the west, and Yingbu's army was always the bravest.
After Xiang Liang knew for sure that Chen She was dead, he supported King Huai of Chu and named him Dangyang Lord with a tattoo.
Xiang Liang was defeated and died in battle. King Huai of Chu, Ying Bu and other princes and generals gathered in Pengcheng.
At this time, the Qin army stepped up the siege of Tangguo, and Tangguo sent people to request King Huai of Chu for rescue many times.
King Chu Huai sent Song Yi as the general, and Xiang Yu and Ying Bu were subordinate to him to go north to rescue the country.
Xiang Ji killed Song Yi on the bank of the Zhang River and established himself as general. He sent Yingbu to cross the Zhang River first and attack the Qin army, winning many times.
Xiang Ji led all his troops across the river and followed Ying Bu, defeating the Qin army and forcing Zhang Han and others to surrender.
The Chu army often won battles and made the greatest contributions among the princes. The reason why the armies of the princes all obeyed and subordinated to the Chu army was because Yingbu repeatedly defeated the larger number with a smaller number.
Xiang Ji led his army westward to Xin'an, and sent Yingbu and others to attack and bury alive Zhang Han's Qin soldiers of more than 200,000 men at night.
When they arrived at Hangu Pass, they were unable to enter, so they sent Ying Bu and others to raid from a small road and defeat the troops guarding the pass before they were able to enter.
When he arrived in Xianyang, Yingbu served as the forward.
King Xiang conferred titles on various generals, and made Yingbu the King of Jiujiang, making six counties his capital.
King Xiang honored King Huai of Chu as the Righteous Emperor and moved the capital to Changsha, but secretly asked King Yingbu of Jiujiang to kill the Righteous Emperor.
Yingbu sent generals to chase him to Chen County and kill him.
King Tian Rong of Qi rebelled against Chu. King Xiang went to attack Qi and fine-tuned his army to Jiujiang. Wang Yingbu of Jiujiang excused himself from illness and sent his generals with thousands of people to go.
The Han army defeated Chu in Pengcheng, and Yingbu refused to help Chu due to illness. King Xiang resented Yingbu and sent envoys many times to condemn and recruit Yingbu. Yingbu was even more frightened and did not dare to go.
King Xiang was worried about Qi and Tang in the north, and worried about Han in the west. The only one he attached to was Yingbu. He also respected Yingbu's talents and wanted to rely on him and use him, so he did not attack him.
The army of the King of Han fought fiercely with the Chu army in Pengcheng. The Han army was defeated and fled through Liang to Yu County. The King of Han said to his left and right: People like you are not worthy of discussing world affairs together.
summary: Ying Bu, from Liu County, was a convict who escaped to become a bandit. He joined Xiang Liang, then Xiang Yu, who made him King of Jiujiang. He killed the Righteous Emperor for Xiang Yu. Later, Sui He persuaded him to defect to Liu Bang. Ying Bu was made King of Huainan. After Han Xin and Peng Yue's deaths, he feared for his life and rebelled. He was defeated and killed by the emperor's forces.

translation:
The emperor granted Benhe the title of marquis, and six other generals received the title.
Lu Wan, a native of Fengyi, was from the same hometown as Gaozu.
Lu Wan's father was friendly with Gaozu's father and had children at the same time. Gaozu and Lu Wan were born on the same day. The villagers brought sheep and wine to congratulate both families.
When Gaozu and Lu Wan grew up, they studied together and became friendly.
The villagers praised the two families for being friendly to each other. They gave birth to a son on the same day, and the son grew up to be friendly again. They once again congratulated the two families with sheep and wine.
When Emperor Gaozu was still a commoner, Lu Wan always followed him around because he broke the law and evaded hiding.
When Emperor Gaozu raised troops in Pei County, Lu Wan followed him as a guest, entered Hanzhong and was promoted to general, often accompanying him in the inner court.
Following Gaozu's campaign against Xiang Yu, he always stayed close to him as a Taiwei, entering and leaving Gaozu's bedroom, receiving food, clothing, and various rewards, which none of the ministers dared to compare with.
Even though people like Xiao He, Cao Shen and others were respected only because of their career needs, as for the favor they received, no one could compare to Lu Wan.
Lu Wan was granted the title of Marquis of Chang'an.
Chang'an is the original Xianyang.
After Xiang Ji died, Lu Wan was asked to lead another army and attack Linjiang King Gongwei together with Liu Mai. After returning, he followed Emperor Gaozu to attack Zang Tu, King of Yan, and defeated the enemy and pacified those places.
At that time, there were seven princes who were not named Liu and were crowned kings.
The emperor wanted to make Lu Wan king, but the officials were dissatisfied and complained.
When Zang Tu was captured, he issued a letter from Shao and ordered the ministers and princes to choose the meritorious minister among the ministers to be crowned King of Yan.
The officials knew that the emperor wanted to make Lu Wan a king, and they all said: Lu Wan, the Taiwei Marquis of Chang'an, who often followed the emperor to bring peace to the world, and who made the most contributions, can be made king.
The emperor appointed Lu Wan as King of Yan.
Among the princes and kings, no one was as favored as King Yan.
Six years after Lu Wan was granted the title of King of Yan, Chen Xi collapsed due to suspicion of his rebellion.
Chen Xi was from Wanju County. He didn't know why he followed the King of Han in the first place.
When King Xin of Han rebelled against the Han and entered the Huns, and the emperor came back from Pingcheng, Chen Xi was granted the title of Marquis by the doctor, and as Zhao Xiangguo, he commanded and supervised the troops of Tangguo and Daiguo, and all the border defense troops belonged to him.
When Chen Xi was young, he often praised and admired Wei Gongzi Xinlingjun. When he was leading troops to guard the border fortress, he widely solicited and adopted guests.
When he returned to his hometown on vacation, he passed through the state of Zhao. There were more than a thousand cars with his guests, and the guesthouse of the Handan government was full.
Chen Xi treated his guests with the same etiquette as when interacting with civilians, always treating others with humility.
Zhou Chang, the Prime Minister of Zhao State, requested to go to the capital to see the emperor. He explained in detail that Chen Xi had many guests and had many troops outside, so there was a fear that something might happen.
summary: Lu Wan, from Fengyi, was a childhood friend of Liu Bang. He became King of Yan. Suspected of colluding with Chen Xi and the Xiongnu, he fled to the Xiongnu after Liu Bang's death, dying there.

translation:
It was passed down to his great-grandson that the feudal state was abolished due to crime.
Wu Rui was the magistrate of Fanyang County during the Qin Dynasty. He was very popular among the people in the Jianghu area and was known as Fanjun.
The world began to rebel against the Qin Dynasty, Yingbu surrendered to Wu Rui, and Wu Rui married his daughter to him. So he led the Yue people to raise troops to respond to the anti-Qin struggles in various places.
Peigong attacked Nanyang County and encountered Wu Rui's general Mei Guo, so he and he attacked Xi County and Li County of Nanyang County. Both counties surrendered.
When Xiang Yu divided the princes among the princes, Wu Rui led the Baiyue soldiers to cooperate with the princes and followed them into Guanzhong, so he made Wu Rui the king of Hengshan and established Zhu as his capital.
His general Mei Guo had many merits and was granted the title of lord of 100,000 households.
After Xiang Yu's death, the emperor followed him into Wuguan because of his merits in the plum pot. So he was grateful to Wu Rui and changed his title to King of Changsha. He established his capital in Linxiang. He died a year later and was named King Wen. Zicheng Wang Wuchen succeeded to the throne.
When Wu Chen died, his son Ai Wang Hui succeeded to the throne.
Wu Hui died, and Wu You, the king of Zi Gong, succeeded to the throne.
Wu You died, and Wu Cha, the king of Zijing, succeeded to the throne.
Wu Chai died in the seventh year of Emperor Wen's reign without a son, and the feudal state was abolished.
At the beginning, King Wen Wu Rui, considered by Emperor Gaozu to be virtuous and loyal to the court, ordered the censor to say: The loyalty of the King of Changsha must be written in the decree.
At the time of Emperor Hui and Empress Gao, Wu Rui's two sons other than his legitimate son were granted the title of marquis. The title was passed down for several generations before being abolished.
Zan said: In the past, when Emperor Gaozu pacified the world, among the heroes who were not named Liu, there were eight countries who were crowned kings.
Zhang Er, Wu Rui, Peng Yue, Ting Bu, Zang Tu, Lu Wan and the two Han Xins were all able to adapt to the current situation, adapt to changes, and achieve success by virtue of cunning and strength. They all received fiefs, sat facing south, and called Gu the king.
Because they were powerful and were suspected by the court, they could not feel at ease. When things developed in the end, the situation was urgent and they were forced to plan a rebellion, and finally perished.
Zhang Er relied on his wisdom to save himself, and it was passed down to his son that he also lost his title.
Only Wu Rui did not violate the right path from the beginning, so he was able to pass the king's title to the fifth generation. However, the kingdom was abolished because there was no heir. There is a reason why his blessings were passed on to the descendants other than his legitimate son!
Written on important decrees issued by the imperial court to commend his loyalty!
summary: Wu Rui, a Qin magistrate, led Yue troops to support Liu Bang. Xiang Yu made him King of Hengshan, later Liu Bang made him King of Changsha. He died a year later, his kingdom passed down five generations before ending without an heir. The historian comments that among the eight non-Liu kings, only Wu Rui remained loyal, his kingdom lasting longest due to his virtue.

translation:
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had eight sons: Empress Lu begat Emperor Xiaohui, Lady Cao was the father of King Qiyouhui Liu Fei, Bo Ji was the father of Emperor Xiaowen, Lady Qi was the father of Zhaowu King Liu Ruyi, Gui Xun was the father of Huainan King Li Xingzhou, and other concubines were the children of Zhao Youwang Suqu, Zhao Gongwang Liu Yue, and Jixi King Liu Jian.
Huainan Li Wang Xingzhou has his own biography.
The mother of Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi, was Gaozu's mistress when he was a commoner.
In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Liu Fei was made king, and he had more than seventy cities under his control.
All the common people who could speak the language of Qi were given to the State of Qi.
In the second year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, King Qi went to the capital to meet Emperor Hui.
Emperor Hui held a banquet in front of Empress Dowager Lu to entertain King Qi. According to family etiquette, Emperor Hui invited his eldest brother, King Qi, to sit at the head of the table.
Empress Dowager Lu was so furious that she had two glasses of poisoned wine poured in front of her, and asked King Qi to offer wine to celebrate his birthday.
King Qi stood up, and Emperor Hui also stood up, wanting to celebrate his birthday with wine.
The Queen Mother was frightened, so she stood up and knocked over the wine glass.
King Qi felt strange and did not dare to drink anymore. He pretended to be drunk and left.
Later, I found out that the wine wrapped in wine was poisonous. I was very worried and thought that I would not be able to leave Chang'an and return home.
The historian said: The Queen Mother only gave birth to Emperor Hui and Princess Lu Yuan. Now there are more than seventy cities in your country, but the princess's food town is only a few cities.
You might as well dedicate a county to the Queen Mother and use it as a place to increase the princess's food and fiefdom. In this way, the Queen Mother will definitely be happy, and the King will be free from disaster.
Therefore, the King of Qi dedicated Chengyang County and honored Princess Lu Yuan as the Queen Mother.
Queen Mother Lu happily agreed.
So they held a banquet at Qi's residence in the capital, drank and had fun together, and sent King Qi back to his country.
Thirteen years later, King Liu Fei of Qi died, and his eldest son Liu Xiang succeeded to the throne.
Liu Ruyi, King of Zhao Yin, was established as King of Zhao in the ninth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign.
Four years later, Gaozu died, and Empress Dowager Lu summoned King Zhao Ruyi to Chang'an to kill him.
He had no sons and his country was extinct.
Liu You, King of Zhao You, was established as King of Huaiyang in the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign.
In the year when Zhao Yin King Liu Ruyi died, which was the first year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, he was granted the title of King of Zhao and reigned for fourteen years.
Liu You took the daughter of the Lu family as his queen. He did not love the queen, but loved other concubines.
The daughter of the Lu family left in anger and slandered the Empress Dowager Lu: "The King of Zhao said, why should a member of the Lu family hold the throne?"
After the death of the Queen Mother, I must kill them. The Queen Mother was furious, so she summoned King Zhao.
After King Zhao entered the capital, he abandoned his residence and refused to receive him. He also ordered guards to besiege him and refused to give him anything to eat.
The ministers of Zhao State sometimes gave him food in private, but they were immediately arrested and punished.
summary: Emperor Gaozu of Han had eight sons from various consorts. Empress Lu bore Emperor Xiaohui; Lady Cao bore Liu Fei, King of Qi; Bo Ji bore Emperor Xiaowen; Lady Qi bore Liu Ruyi, King of Zhao; and other concubines bore Liu You, Liu Yue, and Liu Jian. Liu Fei, King Hui of Qi, was granted over seventy cities in the sixth year of Gaozu's reign. During Emperor Hui's reign, King Qi visited the capital. Emperor Hui honored him as eldest brother at a banquet, angering Empress Dowager Lu, who attempted to poison King Qi. After discovering the plot, King Qi dedicated Chengyang County to increase Princess Lu Yuan's fiefdom, appeasing the Empress Dowager and securing his safe return. Liu Fei died thirteen years later, succeeded by his son Liu Xiang.

translation:
King Zhao was hungry and lamented: The Lu family is monopolistic, but the Liu family is weak; coerce the princes and give me concubines by force.
The concubine is so jealous that she falsely accuses me of a crime; the woman slanders her and ruins the country, but the emperor cannot know about it.
I have no loyal ministers, so why should I accept the call and abandon my country?
I am happy in the fields, hoping that heaven will come to judge my integrity!
It is impossible to regret, I would rather commit suicide earlier!
If you are a king and starve to death, who will take pity on you?
Mr. Lu violated the laws of nature. I could only ask heaven for revenge, so I died in confinement.
The imperial court buried him in Chang'an with the courtesy of a commoner.
After the death of Empress Dowager Lu, Emperor Wen of Han ascended the throne and established Liu Sui, the son of King You, as King of Zhao.
The following year, the officials in charge asked the prince to be crowned king.
Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty said: King Zhao You died in confinement. I pity him very much.
His eldest son Liu Sui has been established as King of Zhao.
Liu Sui's younger brother Liu Piqiang, Prince Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, son of King Qi Yaohui, and Shu Mouhou Liu Xingju all have meritorious services and can be established as kings.
Therefore, Hejian County was taken from Zhao State and Liu Piqiang was established as King Wen of Hejian.
Thirteen years later, Liu Piqiang died and his son Liu Fu, King Ai, succeeded him.
Liu Fu died after one year as king. He had no sons and the feudal state was abolished.
King Zhao Liu Sui was king for twenty-six years. When Emperor Mo Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo thought that King Zhao was at fault and cut off the Changshan County of Zhao State. The princes were dissatisfied and Wu, Chu and other countries rebelled. Liu Sui also participated in the conspiracy and raised troops to attack the Han Dynasty.
Zhao's Prime Minister Jiande and Internal History Wang Han advised him, but Liu Sui not only refused to listen, but also burned Jiande and Wang Han to death. He sent troops to garrison the western border of Zhao, hoping to wait for the troops of Wu and Chu to join up and then move westward. He also sent people north to contact the Xiongnu.
The Han Dynasty sent Quzhou Hou Liji to attack Zhao. The King of Zhao garrisoned Handan and resisted the Han soldiers for seven months.
Wu and Chu were defeated. When the Xiongnu heard about it, they refused to send troops to help.
Shi! After defeating Manzhi, Xi led his troops back, joined forces with Li Zhou and others to attack Zhao, and diverted water to fill the city.
After the city was broken, the Zhao royal family committed suicide in a tunnel and Zhao Li was deposed.
Lian Kentong felt sorry for Zhao Moxiang and Nei Shi who died for insisting on respecting the imperial court, and named their sons as marquises.
Liu Hui, the king of the Communist Party of Zhao.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, after he executed Peng Yue, the king of Liang, he established Liu Hui as king of Liang.
In the 16th year, Empress Dowager Lu killed King You of Zhao and moved Liu Hui to King Zhao. Liu Hui was unhappy.
Empress Dowager Lu married Lu Chan's daughter to King Zhao and became the queen. The queen's attendants were all members of the Lu family. They monopolized power in the palace and secretly observed King Zhao. King Zhao could not do whatever he wanted.
King Zhao had a beloved concubine who was poisoned to death by the queen with wine.
summary: Liu Ruyi, King of Zhao, was killed by Empress Dowager Lu after Gaozu's death, leaving no heirs. Liu You became King of Zhao but was imprisoned and starved to death after his Lu-family queen falsely accused him of plotting rebellion. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, Emperor Wen established Liu Sui as King of Zhao. Liu Sui later joined the Wu-Chu rebellion, was besieged for seven months, and committed suicide after the city fell.

translation:
Once he was driving for Cao Shen and made some suggestions on the way. Cao Shen thought he had talent and recommended him to King Hui of Qi.
The King of Qi summoned him and appointed him as internal history.
From then on, King Qi Hui gained the power to appoint officials with two thousand stones.
After the death of King Hui of Qi, King Ai succeeded to the throne, and Wei Bo came to power, with more power than the prime minister of Qi.
The King of Qi had withdrawn his troops and returned to his country, and King Dai was made emperor, the Emperor Wen of Han.
In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, Chengyang County, Langye County and Jinan County, which were separated from Qi State during the reign of Queen Gao, were returned to Qi State, and King Langxie was moved to Yan State as king.
Two thousand households each were granted the title of Marquis Zhuxu and Marquis Shumou. A thousand pounds of gold.
In this year, King Ai of Qi died, and his son King Sai Xin came to the throne.
He died in the fourteenth year without a son to succeed him. Bianyou was deposed and his territory returned to He.
Liu Zhang, King of Chengyang Jing, was established as king in the second year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty as Zhu Xuhou together with Liu Xingju, Shumuhou. He died in the second year of Emperor Wen's reign.
His son Liu happy, the co-king, succeeded to the throne.
In the twelfth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, he was granted the title of King of Huainan. Five years later, he was renamed King of Chengyang. He reigned for a total of thirty-three years and died.
His son Liu Yan succeeded to the throne as King of Qing. Liu Yan died in his twenty-sixth year on the throne.
His son Liu Yi succeeded him as King Jing. Liu Yi died in the ninth year of his reign.
His son Liu Wu succeeded to the throne as King Hui, and Liu Wu died in his eleventh year as king.
His son Liu Shun succeeded him as King Huang. Liu Shun died in his forty-sixth year.
His son Liu Hui succeeded to the throne as King Dai. Liu Hui died after eight years as king.
His son Liu Jing succeeded him as King Xiao, and Liu Jing died in his twenty-fourth year.
His son Liu Yun succeeded to the throne as King Ai. Liu Yun died after one year on the throne. He had no sons. The country was exterminated and the territory was transferred to the Han Dynasty.
During the reign of Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty, Liu Yun's brother Liu Li was made King of Chengyang. During the reign of Wang Mang, the feudal state was abolished.
Liu Xingju, the king of Jibei, initially welcomed Emperor Wen to the official residence of Daiguo together with the ministers as Shu Mouhou. He said: "I have no merit in killing the Lu family. I request that I go to clean up the palace with my servant Teng Gong Xia Houying."
So he brought out the young emperor appointed by the Lu family and welcomed Emperor Wen of Han into the palace to rule.
At the beginning of the crusade against the Lu family, Zhu Xuhou and Liu Zhang made the greatest contribution. The ministers discussed and agreed to make Liu Zhang the king of all the territories of the Zhao State, and to make Liu Xingju the king of all the territories of the Liang State.
After Emperor Wen ascended the throne, I heard that Song Xuhou and Dongmuhou had wanted to make King Qi emperor, so they deposed him and reduced the credit of the Lu family.
In the second year, Emperor Wen made the princes kings, and then divided the two counties of Qi and made Liu Zhang and Liu Xingju the princes and kings.
Liu Zhang and Xingju believed that they had lost their merit because of their dereliction of duty.
More than a year later, Liu Zhang died. At that time, the Xiongnu invaded the border in large numbers, and the Han Dynasty sent a large number of troops. Prime Minister Guan Ying led the attack, and Emperor Wen personally went to Taiyuan to supervise the battle.
Liu Xingju believed that the emperor wanted to personally attack the Xiongnu, so he launched an army to rebel. When Emperor Wen heard about it, he stopped his troops and returned to Chang'an. He sent General Chai Wu, the Marquis of Jipu, to defeat the rebels and capture the King of Jibei.
summary: Liu Hui was moved to Zhao against his wishes. His Lu-family queen poisoned his beloved concubine, causing him to compose a sorrowful song and commit suicide. Liu Jian, King of Yan, died, and his son was killed, extinguishing his line. Emperor Wen restored Qi's lost territories and granted titles to Liu Zhang and Liu Xingju. Liu Xingju later rebelled and committed suicide. Emperor Wen divided Qi into six kingdoms for King Qi Hui's sons. During Emperor Jing's reign, four of these kings joined the Wu-Chu rebellion. King Xiao of Qi initially hesitated, was besieged, but held out until Han forces arrived. After learning the king had negotiated with rebels, he committed suicide. Emperor Jing pardoned him posthumously.

translation:
King Zhao composed a song in four chapters and ordered the musicians to sing.
King Zhao was overly sad and committed suicide six months later.
After Empress Dowager Lu heard about it, she thought it was a woman who committed suicide instead of offering sacrifices to the ancestral temple, so she deposed her country and cut off her inheritance of the throne. Liu Jian, King of Yanling.
In the eleventh year of Mo Gaozu's reign, King Lu Wan of Yan defected to the Huns. The following year, Liu Jian was granted the title of King of Yan.
In the fifteenth year, Liu Jian died, and his son by a beautiful woman was killed by Dan Liqiu's men. The heirs were extinct and the country was abolished.
Nine of the sons of King Hui of Qi Yao were established as kings: the prince Shengjin was the king of Qisei, the second son Xingtong was the king of Chengyangjing, Liu Xingri was the king of Ji Dongdou, Liu Laoyi was the king of Bian, Yan Jin was the king of Zhamu, Su Biguang was the king of Zamu, Xingtong was the king of Lancong, Xingsheng was the king of Zhuiyou, and Liu Xiongji was the king of bran.
Liu Xiang, King Ai of Qi, succeeded to the throne in the sixth year of Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty. The following year, Emperor Hui died, and Empress Dowager Lu came to rule.
In the first year of Gaohou's reign, Lu Tai, the son of Queen Lu's brother, was granted the title of King of Lu, and the Jinan County of Naoqi was divided into his own state.
The next year, Liu Zhang, the younger brother of King Ai, was summoned to the capital to guard the Han court. He was named Zhu Xuhou and married to him Lu Lu's daughter.
Four years later, Liu Zhang's younger brother Liu Xingju was granted the title of Marquis of Cambodia, and both of them guarded the Han court in Chang'an.
In the seventh year of Emperor Gao's reign, the Langye County of Qi was divided, and Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, was granted the title of King of Langye.
In the same year, King Zhao Liu You was imprisoned and died in the royal residence in the capital.
Since the three kings of Zhao were deposed, Empress Gao selected three from the Lu family as kings and took over the power to handle affairs.
Liu Zhang was twenty years old at the time and was very powerful. He was dissatisfied that Liu could not get his authority.
He once went to the palace to serve the Empress Dowager Lu at a banquet, and the Empress Dowager Lu ordered Liu Zhang to be the drinking officer.
Liu Zhang demanded: "I am a descendant of a military general. Please follow military laws and enforce the drinking order."
Queen Mother Lu said: Yes.
When he was enjoying his drink, Liu Zhang presented songs and dances for people to enjoy while drinking. After a while, he said: Please allow me to tell the Queen Mother about farming.
Empress Dowager Lu regarded Liu Zhang as a child and said with a smile: "I think your father knows about farming. You were already a prince when you were born. How can you know about farming?" Liu Zhang said: "I know."
The Queen Mother said: Try to tell me about plowing.
Liu Zhang said: When plowing deeply and planting densely, the remaining seedlings should be sparse; if they are not of the same kind, they should be hoed away.
The Queen Mother listened and remained silent.
After a while, one of Lu's children got drunk and ran away from the banquet. Liu Zhang chased after him, drew his sword and killed him. He came back and reported to the Queen Mother: There was a man who escaped drinking, and I beheaded him in accordance with military law.
The Queen Mother and the people around her were greatly surprised.
Because he had agreed to drink according to military law, he could not be punished, so the banquet was abandoned.
From then on, the descendants of the Lu family were afraid of Liu Zhang, and even the ministers obeyed Liu Zhang.
The Liu family became stronger.
The following year, Queen Mother Lu died.
King Lu Lu of Zhao was the general, and King Lu Chan was the prime minister. They both lived in Chang'an, the capital, and gathered troops to threaten the ministers and attempt to rebel and cause rebellion.
Liu Zhang's wife was Lu Lu's daughter, so she knew about their conspiracy. Liu Zhang then secretly sent someone to tell his brother King Qi that he wanted him to send troops to the capital. Zhu Xuhou, Dongmuhou and Han ministers acted as internal agents in order to kill the Lu family's descendants and make King Qi emperor.
summary: King Qi Yao's nine sons were established as kings. During Empress Dowager Lu's regency, Lu-family members were granted kingdoms from Qi's territory. Liu Zhang, a grandson of King Qi, served at court and openly defied the Lu family during a banquet, killing a drunken Lu relative under military drinking rules. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, the Lu family plotted rebellion. Liu Zhang secretly informed his brother King Qi, who raised troops. The Han generals killed the Lu family, and the ministers chose to make King Dai (Emperor Wen) emperor instead of King Qi, fearing the Qi queen's mother's family was too powerful.

translation:
The king of Jibei committed suicide and the country was abolished.
Emperor Wen took pity on the King of Jibei for rebelling and destroying himself. In the second year, he made Liu Bojun, the seven sons of King Hui of Qi, and others into princes.
In the fifteenth year of Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, King Wen of Qi Liu Ze died without a son.
But at that time, the descendants of King Qi Huihui still had King Chengyang. Emperor Wen pitied King Qi Hui because he had no legitimate son to succeed him, so he divided the Qi country into six, and the six sons of King Hui who were previously named princes were still alive. Established as kings: Yang Xuhou Liu Jianglu is the King of Qi Xiao, Anduhou Liu Zhi is the King of Jibei, Wuchenghou Liu Xian is the Miao King, Baishihou Liu Xiongqu is the Micellar King, Pingchang Hou Liu Yin is the Jiaoxi King, and Jiehou Liu Biguang is the Jinan King.
In the sixteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, six kings were made kings on the same day.
In the eleventh year of the reign of the above-mentioned six kings, that is, the third year of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty, Wu and Chu rebelled. The four kings of Miaojie, Jiaoxi, Lei!, and Jinan all responded by sending troops to fight against the Han.
They wanted to invite King Qi to fight against the Han, but King Xiao of Qi was hesitant, so he held on to the city and refused to rebel.
The three kingdoms of Miaojie, Miaochuan, and Jinan sent troops to surround Qi. The King of Qi sent his envoy Dr. Lu Zhong to report to Emperor Mo. The Emperor ordered Dr. Lu Zhong to return to Qi to report to King Qi, asking King Qi to defend the city. The Mo soldiers had defeated Wu and Chu.
On the way, the doctor returned to Qi. Soldiers from the Three Kingdoms surrounded Linmiao City several times and were unable to enter the city.
The generals of the Three Kingdoms and the officials on the road swore an oath: If you turn around and say that the Han Dynasty has been conquered, Qi will surrender to the Three Kingdoms as soon as possible, otherwise the city will be massacred.
Although the doctor agreed on the way, he walked to the city, looked up and saw the King of Qi, and said: The Han Dynasty has sent millions of troops, sent Taiwei Zhou Yafu to defeat Wu and Chu, and is leading troops to rescue Qi State. Qi State must hold on and not surrender!
The generals of the Three Kingdoms killed the doctor on the road.
Before that, Qi State was besieged and in great danger. It had secretly negotiated with the Three Kingdoms. Before the alliance was concluded, a senior official from the Han Dynasty happened to be on the way. The ministers of Qi State once again advised the King of Qi not to surrender to the Three Kingdoms.
It happened that Han Dynasty general Le Bu, Pingyang Marquis Cao Xiang and others led troops to Qi State, defeated the armies of the three countries and lifted the siege.
Later, when I heard that the King of Qi had conspired with the Three Kingdoms, he wanted to send troops to attack Qi.
King Xiao of Qi became frightened and committed suicide by drinking poison.
The four kings of Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Jinan, and Miaochuan were all beheaded. Their feudal state was also abolished, leaving only the King of Jibei.
When Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty heard the news of King Qi Xiao's suicide, he believed that King Qi had no intention of rebellion at first and had other plans because of coercion. This was not his crime. Emperor Jing went down to Shao and established Liu Shou, the crown prince of Prince Xiao, as King Qi Yi.
King Yi died in the 23rd year of his reign, and his son King Li Liu Ciyuan succeeded him.
summary: Later, King Qi Li committed adultery with his sister. When Emperor Wu sent an investigator, the king committed suicide, leaving no heirs, and Qi was abolished. The remaining Qi territories eventually passed to the Han dynasty. Over time, the power of princes was reduced after the Seven Kingdoms rebellion, with laws restricting their authority until they could only collect taxes from their fiefdoms.

translation:
The Prime Minister of Wei, whose courtesy name is Wenweng, was born in Dingtao, Jiyin, and later moved to Pingling.
When Wei Xiang was young, he studied the Book of Changes and became the governor of the county. He was praised as a virtuous person. Because he ranked first in answering policy questions, he became the magistrate of Maoling County.
Soon, the guests of Censor Da Sang Hongyang came to Maoling and falsely claimed that Sang Hongyang was coming to the guest house.
The county magistrate did not go to see the guest on time, so he tied up the county magistrate. Prime Minister Wei suspected that the guest was causing trouble, arrested him, tortured him and learned about his crime, and sentenced the guest to be executed in the street. Therefore, Maoling is managed very well.
Later, the prime minister of Wei was promoted to the governor of Henan, where he prohibited bad people from doing evil things, and the local powerful were very afraid of him.
It happened that the prime minister Che Qianqiu died at the time. Che Qianqiu's son had been the commander of the Luoyang Armory. He saw that his father was dead, and the Wei Prime Minister was very strict in managing the affairs of the county. He was afraid that he would be blamed for it in the long run, so he resigned from the official position.
Prime Minister Wei sent Sasuke's own deputies to chase him and call him back, but he finally did not come back.
Prime Minister Wei himself sighed regretfully: When the general resigned after hearing this arsenal order, he would definitely think that I was disrespectful to his son because the prime minister was dead.
It will also make those powerful people in the world blame me. It’s dangerous!
When Che Qianqiu, the son of an arsenal commander, arrived in Chang'an, General Huo Guang scolded Prime Minister Wei for this: The young new emperor had just ascended the throne and believed that Hangu Pass was the strongest place to defend the capital and the weapons depot was a place where sophisticated weapons were stored, so he made the prime minister's brother the captain of Hangu Pass and the prime minister's son the commander of the weapons depot.
Now the governor of Henan, Wei Xiang, did not think deeply about the country's plans, but just dismissed the prime minister's son when he saw his death. How shallow is this!
Later, someone accused Prime Minister Wei of killing an innocent person, and the matter was brought to the competent government office.
There were two to three thousand officers from the Henan garrison who stopped the general Huo Guang and said they were willing to stay for another year to atone for the sin of the prefect Wei Xiang.
More than 10,000 old and weak people in Henan guarded Hangu Pass and asked to enter the pass to write to the emperor. The officials guarding the pass reported the matter.
General Huo Guang handed Wei Prime Minister to Tingwei for punishment because of the arsenal order.
Prime Minister Wei was imprisoned for a long time. After the winter, it happened that the imperial court pardoned the prisoners.
There was also an edict ordering Prime Minister Wei to serve as the magistrate of Maoling County again and promote him to the governor of Yangzhou.
Later, the imperial court inspected the ministers of the county and state, and many of them were demoted.
Prime Minister Wei and Bing Ji were close. At that time, Bing Ji's official position was Doctor Guanglu. He wrote to Prime Minister Wei and said: The imperial court has a deep understanding of your achievements and behavior and will appoint you.
I hope you will be cautious and self-respecting in everything you do and cultivate your talents.
Prime Minister Wei thought Bingji's words were right, so he restrained his dignity.
After serving as governor for two years, he was recruited as an admonishing official and then became the governor of Henan.
summary: Wei Xiang, courtesy name Wenweng, was a native of Dingtao, Jiyin, later moving to Pingling. He studied the Book of Changes in his youth, became a county governor, and was praised for his virtue. After ranking first in policy questions, he became magistrate of Maoling County. When a guest of Censor Sang Hongyang falsely claimed Sang was arriving and tied up the magistrate, Wei Xiang suspected foul play, arrested the guest, tortured him to reveal his crime, and executed him in the street, leading to excellent governance in Maoling. Promoted to governor of Henan, he prohibited evil deeds, instilling fear in local powers. When Prime Minister Che Qianqiu died, his son, commander of the Luoyang Armory, resigned fearing Wei Xiang’s strictness. Wei Xiang regretted this, fearing it would cause resentment. General Huo Guang later scolded Wei Xiang for dismissing the prime minister’s son after his death, calling it shallow. Accused of killing an innocent person, Wei Xiang faced investigation, but over 10,000 Henan residents petitioned for him. Huo Guang handed him to Tingwei for punishment, but he was pardoned and reappointed as magistrate of Maoling, then governor of Yangzhou. After demotions in an imperial inspection, Wei Xiang, close to Bingji, heeded his advice to restrain his dignity. He served as governor for two years, then became an admonishing official and later governor of Henan again. After Emperor Xuan ascended, Wei Xiang became chief minister of agriculture, then imperial censor. Four years later, Huo Guang died. Wei Xiang wrote to the emperor, warning against the Huo family’s power, citing historical precedents of autocratic rule causing chaos. He suggested weakening their influence to strengthen the Han dynasty. Emperor Xuan adopted his advice, deposing Huo Yu, Huo Yun, and Huo Shan. Wei Xiang became prime minister, replacing Wei Xian, and was named Gaopinghou. The Huo family later plotted to kill him but were discovered and executed. Emperor Xuan then personally governed, selecting good ministers, and Wei Xiang was popular as prime minister. During the Yuankang period, when the Xiongnu attacked Han forces, Wei Xiang advised against military retaliation, citing border poverty and internal social issues like 222 cases of familial killings. He urged focus on domestic stability. Emperor Xuan followed his advice. Wei Xiang, well-versed in the Book of Changes, studied Han history and advocated following past systems. He presented 23 items from the late emperor’s edicts, emphasizing agriculture, grain storage, and frugality to prepare for disasters. He warned of current grain price hikes and border conflicts, urging the emperor to care for the people. Emperor Xuan implemented his suggestions. Wei Xiang also presented chapters on Yin-Yang and seasonal governance, arguing that proper seasonal management prevents disasters and ensures prosperity. He recommended selecting ministers knowledgeable in Yin-Yang to oversee seasonal affairs. The emperor adopted his proposals. Wei Xiang’s commissioners reported irregularities from counties, often revealing unreported rebellions or disasters. He was severe and resolute, unlike the tolerant Bingji. He served as prime minister for nine years, dying in the third year of the Shenjue era, and was posthumously named Xianhou. His son Wei Hong inherited the title but was demoted to Marquis of Guannei during the Ganlu era due to a crime.

translation:
Wei Bao was the son of Wei State during the Six Kingdoms period.
His elder brother Wei Jiu was named Lord Ningling at that time. After Qin destroyed Wei, he was deposed as a commoner.
After Chen Sheng rebelled and proclaimed himself king, Wei Jiu went to serve him.
Chen Sheng sent a Wei man named Zhou Shi to lead his troops to capture the land of Wei. After occupying it, he wanted to make Zhou Shi the king of Wei.
Zhou Shi said: Only when the world is in chaos can the integrity of loyal ministers be seen.
Now that the whole world has betrayed Qin, it stands to reason that the king of Wei should be established after him.
Qi and Tang each sent fifty military chariots to help support Zhou Shi as king.
Zhou Shi refused to accept it and sent people to Chen County to meet Wei Jiu. After five trips, King Chen agreed to make Wei Jiu the king of Wei.
Zhang Han defeated King Chen and raised his troops to Linji to attack King Wei.
The king of Wei sent Zhou Shi to Qi and Chu to request reinforcements.
Qi and Chu sent Xiang Ta and Tian Ba ​​to lead the army together with Zhou Shi to rescue Wei.
Zhang Han defeated them again, killed Zhou Shi and others, and surrounded Linji.
In order to save the people in the city, Wei Jiu agreed to surrender to the Qin army.
After the agreement was made, Wei Jiu committed suicide and died.
Wei Bao fled to Chu.
King Huai of Chu sent thousands of troops to Wei Bao to recapture the land of Wei.
By this time, Xiang Yu had defeated the Qin army and captured Zhang Han. Wei Bao captured more than 20 cities and was made king of Wei by Xiang Yu.
Wei Bao led his army to follow Xiang Yu into the pass.
In the first year of the Han Dynasty, Xiang Yu divided the feudal lords. He wanted to occupy Daliang, so he moved Wei Bao to Hedong, established his capital in Pingyang, and named him King of the Western Wei Dynasty.
The King of Han almost ordered the Three Qin Dynasties to cross the Yellow River from Linjin. The King of Wei, Wei Bao, surrendered the whole country to the King of Han, and followed the King of Han to attack the Chu army in Pengcheng.
The king of Han failed and retreated to Rongyang. Wei Bao asked to go back to visit his mother's condition. After returning to Wei, he blocked the crossing of the Yellow River and betrayed the King of Han.
The king of Han said to Li Sheng: Go and persuade Wei Bao to submit.
Li Sheng arrived in Wei. Wei Bao declined politely and said: Life is very short.
The King of Han insults people at will and scolds the princes and ministers as if they were slaves. He has no courtesy at all. I don't want to bear the anger and go to see him again.
So the King of Han sent Han Xin to attack Wei Bao, captured him, and escorted him to Rongyang, dividing Wei Bao's original territory into three counties: Hedong, Taiyuan, and Shangdang.
The king of Han asked Wei Bao to garrison Rongyang.
At that time, the Chu army was attacking Rongyang, and the situation was urgent. Zhou Ke said: "You cannot defend with those who betray the country."
Then he killed Wei Bao.
Tian Dan, a native of Di County, was a member of the Tian clan, King of Qi during the Six Kingdoms period.
Tian Dan's cousin Tian Rong and Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng were both heroes. Their clans were powerful and respected.
Chen She sent Zhou Shi to capture Wei and went north to Di County, but failed to capture it in the end.
Tian Dan pretended to kill his slave, and brought his young men with him, tied up the slave, and came to see the magistrate of Di County. When he saw the magistrate, he took the opportunity to kill him.
summary: The histories of three prominent figures from the Six Kingdoms period: Wei Bao, Tian Dan, and Han Wangxin, detailing their rise, fall, and the fates of their descendants. Wei Bao, son of the Wei state, saw his brother Wei Jiu made king by Chen Sheng after the Qin collapse. Wei Jiu later surrendered to Qin to save his people and committed suicide. Wei Bao fled to Chu, recaptured Wei lands with King Huai's aid, and was made King of Wei by Xiang Yu. After Xiang Yu moved him to Hedong, Wei Bao initially surrendered to the Han king but later betrayed him, blocking the Yellow River. The Han king sent Han Xin to capture him, and Wei Bao was eventually killed at Rongyang by Zhou Ke, who deemed him untrustworthy.

translation:
Tian Du, a general of the Qi State, participated in the rescue of the Zhao State and allowed Xiang Yu to enter the Pass. Therefore, Tian Du was made King of Qi and his capital was Linmiao.
Tian An, the grandson of Tian Jian, the former King of Qi during the Six Kingdoms period, captured several cities in Jibei when Xiang Yu crossed the river to rescue Zhao, and led his army to defect to Xiang Yu. Therefore, Xiang Yu made Tian An the king of Jibei and made Boyang his capital.
Because Tian Rong was carrying Xiang Liang and refused to send troops to help the Chu army attack the Qin army, he was not crowned king.
Chen Yu, the general of Zhao State, also failed to make him king because of his dereliction of duty.
Both of them hated Xiang Yu deeply.
Tian Rong sent troops to help Chen Yu and asked him to attack Zhao. Tian Rong himself also sent troops to attack Tiandu, and Tiandu fled to Chu.
Tian Rong detained King Qi Tianshi and refused to let him go to Micellar.
Tian Shi's cronies said: King Xiang is strong and violent. If you don't go and take office, there will definitely be disaster.
Tian Shi was afraid, so he secretly escaped to Miaojie and took up his post.
Tian Rong was furious, chased Tian Shi in Jimo and killed him, then turned around and attacked Tian An, the king of Jibei. So Tian Rong established himself as the king of Qi and annexed the territory of San Qi.
When Xiang Yu heard about the dispatch, he was furious and sent troops to attack Qi in the north.
Tian Rong sent troops to resist Xiang Yu in Chengyang.
Tian Rong was defeated and fled to the plains, where he was killed by the local people.
Xiang Yu burned down the walls of Qi and massacred wherever he went.
So the people of Qi gathered to resist him.
Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng gathered up the remnants of Qi's troops and gathered tens of thousands of people to attack Xiang Yu's army in Chengyang.
At this time, Liu Bang, the king of Han, led various princes to defeat the Chu army and entered Pengcheng.
When Xiang Yu got the news, he spared Qi and returned to Pengcheng to attack the Han army. As a result, he fought with Mo continuously, and the two sides were at a stalemate in Rongyang.
So Tian Heng restored the cities of Qi State and made Tian Rong's son Tian Guang the king of Qi. Tian Heng came to assist him. All political affairs of Qi State were decided by Tian Heng, no matter how big or small.
Tian Heng had been pacifying Qi for three years when he suddenly heard that Han Xin, the general of the King of Han, was leading his troops east to attack Qi. The State of Qi sent troops led by Hua Wushang and Tian Jie to garrison at Lixia to fight against the Han army.
It happened that Li Shiqi, the envoy of the King of Han, came to Qi to persuade King Tian Guang of Qi, Prime Minister Tian Heng and the King of Han to jointly attack Chu.
Tian Heng agreed, so Lixia's defense was lifted, and the soldiers drank freely. Just as he was about to send an envoy to negotiate peace with the King of Han, Han Xin had already crossed the plain, defeated the Qi army stationed at Lixia, and entered Linmiao.
Qi King Tian Guang and Prime Minister Tian Heng believed that Li Sheng was conspiring with Han Xin, so they cooked Li Sheng.
Tian Guang fled eastward to Gaomi, Tian Heng fled to Bo County, Prime Minister Tian Guang fled to Chengyang, and General Tian Ji garrisoned in Jiaodong.
The state of Chu sent Long Qie to rescue the state of Qi. King Qi and Long Qie's army met at Gaomi.
The Han generals Han Xin and Cao Shen defeated the Chu army, killed Long Qie, and captured Qi King Tian Guang.
Han general Guan Ying chased and captured Qi's Prime Minister Tian Guang and came to Bo County.
When Tian Heng heard that King Qi was dead, he proclaimed himself king and returned to attack Guan Ying. Guan Ying defeated Tian Heng's army.
Tian Heng fled to Liangdi and joined Pengyue.
At this time, Peng Yue was stationed in Liangdi. He courted both Mo and Chu and remained neutral. After Han Xin killed Long Qie, he then marched into Jiaodong and killed Tian Ji.
Guan Ying defeated Qi general Tian Su and killed Tian Su in Qiancheng, so Han Xin pacified Qi. The Han Dynasty destroyed Xiang Ji, the king of Han established himself as emperor, and Peng Yue was named King of Liang.
Tian Heng was afraid of being killed, so he fled to the sea with more than 500 of his subordinates and lived on the island.
When Mo Gaozu Liu Bang heard the news, he thought that Brother Tian Heng had already pacified Qi, and many wise men of Qi had joined him. Now that he was living on the sea, if he did not recruit him, there might be trouble in the future, so he sent an envoy to pardon Tian Heng's crime and summon him.
Tian Heng declined politely and said: I cooked your Majesty's envoy Li Shiqi. I heard that his younger brother Li Shang is now a general of the Han army and a virtuous man. I am very worried, so I dare not follow the imperial edict. I hope to be an ordinary citizen and live on the island.
The messenger came back and reported to the emperor. Emperor Gaozu summoned Weiwei Li Shang and told him: King Tian Heng of Qi will come, and whoever dares to touch his subordinates will be punished with genocide!
So he sent an envoy with a talisman to tell Tian Heng the order given by Emperor Gaozu to Li Shang, and said: When Tian Heng comes, the older one will be made king and the younger one will be made marquis. If Tian Heng doesn't come, we will send troops to attack him.
Tian Heng then took two retainers to Luoyang in a carriage.
When they arrived at the place where horses were prepared for the post in Xixiang, Tian Heng said to the envoy: As a minister paying homage to the emperor, he should take a bath to purify himself.
So it stopped.
Tian Heng said to his disciples: At first, like the King of Han, I was a man facing south and proclaimed himself king. Now the King of Han has become the emperor. And I have become a prisoner of the subjugated country. It is really shameful to ask the north to surrender to him.
summary: Tian Dan, a member of the Qi royal clan, declared himself king after killing a county magistrate and expanding Qi's territory. He died in battle against Qin's Zhang Han while aiding Wei. His cousin Tian Rong later made Tian Dan's son Tian Shi king, but conflicts arose with Xiang Yu over allegiances. Tian Rong was killed, and his brother Tian Heng restored Qi, making Tian Rong's son Tian Guang king. Tian Heng ruled Qi for three years until Han Xin's invasion. After a series of battles, Tian Guang was captured, and Tian Heng fled to the sea with 500 followers. Summoned by Emperor Gaozu of Han, Tian Heng committed suicide near Luoyang out of shame, and his followers also died, demonstrating his virtue.

translation:
Soon he found an opportunity and fled back to Han. The king of Han named him King of Han. Finally, he followed the king of Han and defeated Xiang Ji.
In the spring of the fifth year, the King of Han cut his talisman with him, and he was in Ying!
For the King of Han. In the spring of the sixth year, the emperor thought that King Xin of Han was brave and brave. The territory he assigned was close to Gongxian and Luoyang in the north, Wanxian and Yexian in the south, and the important town of Huaiyang was in Shubian. These places were garrisoned by elite troops, so he gave Taiyuan County to South Korea, so that King Xin of Han could resist the barbarians and move the capital to Jinyang.
The King of Han wrote a letter saying: The country is close to the border, and the Huns have invaded many times, but Jinyang is far away from the border, so he requested to make Mayi the capital.
The emperor agreed to his request.
In the autumn of that year, the Huns leader Mao Dun led a large army to besiege Han Wangxin. Han Wangxin sent envoys many times to seek reconciliation with the Hu people.
The Han Dynasty sent reinforcements to rescue King Xin of Han, and suspected that King Xin of Han had second thoughts in sending envoys to privately sue for peace with the Xiongnu many times.
The emperor sent a letter to reproach Han Wangxin, saying: As a general, focusing on fighting to death is not considered brave, and focusing on survival is not qualified for military command. The enemy is besieging Mayi, can't you hold on to your troops?
Even in a dangerous situation, you must persist in loyalty and integrity. This is what I want to blame you for.
King Xin of Han received the letter and was afraid of being killed, so he agreed with the Xiongnu to jointly attack Mo, gave Mayi to the Hu people, surrendered to the Xiongnu, and sent troops to attack Taiyuan.
In the winter of the seventh year, the emperor personally led his army to defeat Han Wangxin in Tongqian and killed his general Wang Xi.
King Xin of Han fled to the Huns. His generals Manqiuchen and Wang Huang were from Baitu County. They made Tali, a descendant of Shitang from the Six Kingdoms, king. They also collected the remaining soldiers of King Xin of Han and colluded with King Xin and Maodun of Han to attack Han.
The Xiongnu sent the right and left wise kings to lead more than 10,000 cavalry and Wang Huang and others to station in the south of Guangwu. They went to Jinyang to fight the Han soldiers, but were defeated by the Han soldiers. They pursued them as far as Lishi, where they were defeated again by the Mo army.
The Huns gathered their troops northwest of Loufan again.
The Han army also sent chariots and horses to attack the Huns, often defeating them. The Han army took advantage of the victory and pursued them north.
After hearing the news that Mao Dun lived in Daigu, the emperor went to Jinyang in person, sent people to scout Mao Dun, and reported back that it was possible to attack.
The emperor then came to Pingcheng and climbed Baishan Mountain.
Unexpectedly, the emperor was surrounded by Huns cavalry, so the emperor sent people to send many valuable gifts to Ban, the wife of the Huns.
Que persuaded Mao Dun, saying: Now that we have acquired Han land, it is still uninhabitable. Moreover, when the two masters meet, they cannot force each other into an embarrassing situation.
After seven days of confrontation, the Hu cavalry retreated a little.
Heavy fog fell from the sky, and the Han army sent people to and fro, but the Hu people were not aware of it.
Chen Ping, the lieutenant of the guard, said to the emperor: The weapons of the Hu people are bows and spears. Please ask the soldiers to add two arrows to each strong crossbow, pointing outwards, and move slowly to highlight the encirclement.
When the emperor ran into Pingcheng, reinforcements from the Han Dynasty also arrived. The Xiongnu cavalry dispersed, and the Han Dynasty also withdrew its troops.
After that, Han Wangxin led the Huns soldiers to and from the border to attack the Han army, and also asked Wang Huang and others to persuade Chen Xi.
In the spring of the eleventh year, Han Wangxin and the Hu cavalry were stationed in Shenhe County.
The Han Dynasty sent General Chai to attack. General Chai first sent a letter to King Han saying: Your Majesty is generous and kind. Although some princes defected, after they surrendered, they immediately restored their previous titles and did not kill them.
summary: Han Wangxin, grandson of the original Han king, was made King of Han by Xiang Liang. He later followed the Han king, was captured by Chu, but escaped and was reinstated. After the Han dynasty was established, Emperor Gaozu moved him to Taiyuan to resist the Xiongnu. Suspected of treason for negotiating with the Xiongnu, Han Wangxin surrendered to them and attacked Han. The emperor personally campaigned against him, and after a siege at Pingcheng, the Xiongnu retreated. Han Wangxin continued raiding until he was killed by General Chai in Shenhe County. His descendants, including Han Dangdang and Han Ying, later surrendered to Han and were granted titles, with some serving as generals and officials through subsequent reigns.

translation:
Han Zeng has been honored for generations and has been a loyal minister since he was a child. He served three masters successively and made contributions to the court.
He was tolerant and reserved, and he was kind and courteous to both the emperor and his subordinates. He made no mistakes and protected himself by being favored, but he had no achievements.
Wufeng died in the second year of his reign and was granted the title of Marquis of An.
His son Han Bao succeeded him. Han Bao had no sons and lost his kingdom.
When he became emperor, in order to ensure that the heroes would have successors, Han Cen, the son of Han Zeng's brother, was granted the title of Long'ehou. After his death, his son succeeded him with a bow.
After Wang Mang's defeat, he lost his title.
Zan said: The Zhou royal family has declined, and by the end of the Spring and Autumn Period, all the princes have been reduced, but there are still many descendants of Emperor Yan, Emperor Huang, Tang Yao, and Yu Shun.
Qin destroyed the six kingdoms, and the ancient sending industry no longer existed.
During the war between Chu and Han, heroes became kings one after another. Only the brothers Wei Bao, Han Wangxin, and Tian Dan were descendants of the Six Kingdoms, but by their generation they were all extinct.
Tian Heng's integrity and the spirit of pursuing morality among the guests could not lead to the establishment of the country. Isn't this God's will?
The Han family began to gain prominence again after being granted the title of Marquis of Gonggao. Perhaps it was because Huangxun, as a descendant of Guqu, was the closest to the Three Expeditions!
summary: The text concludes with a reflection that while Wei Bao, Tian Dan, and Han Wangxin were descendants of the Six Kingdoms, their lineages ended. Tian Heng's integrity and his followers' loyalty did not lead to a lasting state, suggesting divine will. The Han family's resurgence through the Marquis of Gonggao is noted as possibly linked to ancient lineage.
