translation:
"Yi" says: When heaven shows signs, good or bad, the sages observe them; when pictures appear in the Yellow River, and books appear in the Luoshui River, the sages imitate them.
Liu Xin believed that Fu Xi inherited the destiny and became king, and was awarded the "River Map". He imitated it and drew it, which became the Bagua; Dayu controlled the flood and was given the "Luo Shu". He imitated it and stated it, which became the "Hong Fan".
Sages follow their thoughts and use their thoughts as scriptures.
In the Yin Dynasty, Ji Gonggong was the father and teacher, and they were the criteria.
After the Zhou Dynasty defeated the Yin Dynasty, Jizi surrendered, and King Wu humbly asked him for advice.
So the scripture says: In the thirteenth year, King Wu visited Jizi, and King Wu said: Ah, Jizi!
God silently stabilizes the people of the world and helps them live in peace. I don't know the normal way of heaven, earth and people and their order. Jizi said: I heard that in the past, Gun blocked the flood and used the Five Elements indiscriminately.
After Gun was executed, Dayu inherited the mission. God gave Dayu nine chapters of "Hongfan", and the common sense of heaven, earth and people was in order. , The result is that King Wu asked Jizi for advice on "Luoshu", and Jizi answered him correctly, which means that Dayu got the meaning of "Luoshu".
The first is called Five Elements; the second is called Shame and Five Things; the third is called Farming and Eight Policies; the fourth is called Ye Yong and Five Disciplines; the fifth is called Jian Yong and Huang Ji; the sixth is called Ai Yong and Three Virtues; the seventh is Ming Yong and Ji Ji; the eighth is Nian Yong and Shuzheng; the ninth is called Feast and Yong Five Blessings and fear and Yong Six Ji.
These sixty-five words in total are the text of "Luo Shu", which is the order of common things in the nine chapters of Dafa given to Dayu by God.
He believes that "He Tu" and "Luo Shu" are the latitude and longitude of each other, and the Bagua and Jiu Zhang are the expressions of each other.
In the past, when the morality of the Yin Dynasty declined, King Wen deduced the "Book of Changes"; after the moral decline of the Zhou Dynasty, Confucius wrote the "Spring and Autumn".
Taking the yin and yang of "Qian" and "Kun" as the rules, and following the signs of disasters in "Hongfan", the laws of heaven and man will be obvious.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty and the destruction of scholarship by the Qin Dynasty, during the two dynasties of Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty and Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, Dong Zhongshu studied "Gongyang Chunqiu" and began to explore the principles of yin and yang, which was highly praised by Confucianists.
After Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty and Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty, Liu Xiang studied "Gu Liang Chun Qiu" to predict people's misfortune and fortune, and attached the explanations in "Hong Fan", which were different from Dong Zhongshu's.
By the time Liu Xin, Liu Xiang's son, studied "Zuo Shi Zhuan", his interpretation of "Spring and Autumn" had already deviated from it; when they talked about "Five Elements Biography", they were very different.
So I quoted Dong Zhongshu's statement to distinguish the differences between Liu Xiang and Liu Xin's father and son, and attached the things related to the Five Elements stated by Sui Meng, Xia Housheng, Jingfang, Gu Yong, and Li Xun, up to the time when Wang Mang usurped Mo, recorded the twelve dynasties, and compared it with the Spring and Autumn Annals, and wrote this "Five Elements Chronicle".
The scripture says: The first is the five elements.
Five elements: first is water, second is fire, third is wood, fourth is gold, and fifth is earth.
summary: Liu Xin believed Fu Xi received the "River Map" and created the Bagua, while Dayu received the "Luo Shu" and formed the "Hong Fan." After the Zhou dynasty defeated the Yin, King Wu consulted Jizi, who explained that God gave Dayu nine chapters of "Hongfan," which established the order of heaven, earth, and people. The text lists nine categories, including the Five Elements, Five Affairs, Eight Policies, and others, totaling sixty-five words that constitute the "Luo Shu." Liu Xin viewed the "He Tu" and "Luo Shu" as complementary, with the Bagua and Jiu Zhang as their expressions. The text traces the study of these principles through King Wen, Confucius, and later scholars like Dong Zhongshu, Liu Xiang, and Liu Xin, culminating in the "Five Elements Chronicle," which records twelve dynasties up to Wang Mang's usurpation.

translation:
The natural nature of water is that it can moisten downwards, the natural nature of fire is that it can burn upward, the natural nature of wood is that it can be bent or straight, the natural nature of gold is that it can change its shape and be melted and smelted, and the natural nature of earth is that it can be cultivated and harvested.
It is said in the legend: Those who do not follow the prescribed time when hunting, do not enjoy the gifts when drinking and eating, go out to fight without restraint, occupy the time for farming, and have evil plots, will lose the ability to be straight or straight.
Explained: Wood represents the east.
According to the Book of Changes, the tree on the ground is called Guan Gua.
For the king's affairs, the majesty, appearance, voice and smile also need to pay attention to the effect of observation.
Therefore, when walking, there is the etiquette of wearing a jade pendant; when riding in a car, there is the etiquette of hanging a golden bell on the car; when going hunting, there is a system of only doing it three times a year; when eating and drinking, there is the etiquette of enjoying the offerings; and there must be a legitimate reason for the expedition. Let the common people serve at the right time. Committed to calling on the people to develop agricultural production and seek stability for the people. By doing the above, the wood will be able to preserve its nature.
If you go out hunting and gallop to your heart's content without returning to the palace, indulge in delicacies and ignore laws and regulations, ignore the people's strength and engage in corvee work and occupy people's time for farming, and change their tactics to extort and harm people's wealth, then the tree will lose its nature.
Therefore, craftsmen make wheels but they are not round, they make arrow shafts but they cannot be straightened, and the wood itself changes and appears strange. This is a sign that the wood has lost its ability to be bent or straight. "Spring and Autumn" records that in the first month of the sixteenth year of Duke Cheng of Lu, it rained and there was wood ice.
Liu Xin believed that this was because the Yang Qi from above could not pass down, and the Yin Qi from below could not reach up, so it rained, but the trees turned into ice and snow. This was because the cold fog prevented the trees from being able to bend or straighten.
Liu Xiang believes that ice is caused by excessive yin energy causing water to freeze. The wood belongs to Shaoyang and is a symbol of noble ministers and officials.
If these people are going to be in trouble, the Yin Qi will threaten the trees, and the trees will become cold first, so they will turn into ice when it rains.
At that time, his uncle and grandson Qiao Ru fled to Qi State, and Young Master Yan was executed.
Another theory is that the Jin State detained Ji Sun Xingfu and Lu Chenggong this year. This was a strange phenomenon caused by the humiliation of being captured.
Some people also say that some elderly people now call Mu Bing Mu Jie.
The introduction is Zhong Jia.
Ai Jia, this is a symbol of war.
In this year, Jin State had a battle at Geling, and the King of Chu was shot and wounded and failed.
It rains normally.
It is said in the legend: Abandoning the law, banishing the heroes, killing the prince, and taking concubines as wives, the fire will not be ignited.
Explain: Fire represents the south and is something that emits brilliance and brings light.
For a king, it means sitting north and facing south, facing the light to govern the world.
"The Book of Books" says: Understanding people brings wisdom, so you can be good at using people.
summary: The first element, Wood, is associated with the east and represents the ability to be bent or straight. The text explains that improper hunting, feasting, and military campaigns disrupt wood's nature, leading to strange phenomena like wood ice. Liu Xin attributed wood ice to blocked yang and yin qi, while Liu Xiang linked it to excessive yin threatening noble ministers. Examples from the "Spring and Autumn" include rain and wood ice in the sixteenth year of Duke Cheng of Lu, interpreted as a sign of noblemen's troubles or military conflict.

translation:
Therefore, Yao and Shun selected the wise men of the world and appointed them as officials in the court, abandoned the four evil men, and banished them to the grasslands.
Confucius said: If the accumulation of secret slanders or rumors does not allow it to succeed, then it can be said that it is upright.
We should clearly distinguish between virtuous gentlemen and treacherous villains, select officials in an orderly manner, follow existing regulations, respect meritorious officials, and differentiate between direct descendants. If we do this, fire will be able to preserve its nature.
If you do not wholeheartedly adhere to morality, or if you show off hypocrisy, allowing slanderous people to succeed, evil will suppress righteousness, and fire will lose its nature.
It will start from top to bottom, causing wild flames to spread everywhere, the ancestral temples will be damaged, and the palaces will be burned. Even if the troops are mobilized, they cannot be extinguished, which is a manifestation of the fire being unable to ignite.
"Spring and Autumn" records that in August of the 14th year of Duke Huan, a fire broke out in the palace granary in Renshen.
Dong Zhongshu believed that the four countries had previously conquered the Lu State together and defeated the Lu State in the battle of Longmen.
The injured people of Lu State had not recovered, and their resentment had not yet recovered. However, the monarchs and ministers became lazy, neglecting political affairs internally, and humiliating their neighbors externally. They were not the ones who could keep the ancestral temple and the grain to last for the period given by the Emperor of Heaven, so the Emperor of Heaven sent disasters to the palace granary to warn them.
Liu Xiang believed that the granary in the palace was where the king's wife and his eighth concubine pounded rice and collected it for the ancestral temple. At that time, the wife had a scandalous behavior and was hiding a rebellious heart. The emperor's warning seemed to say that the wife could no longer be worshiped in the ancestral temple.
Duke Huan of Lu did not wake up and went to the State of Qi with his wife to meet the Marquis of Qi. His wife spoke ill of Duke Huan to the Marquis of Qi, so the Marquis of Qi killed Duke Huan.
Liu Xin believed that the palace granary was the place where the monarch of Lu used his own income from cultivating his own land to donate millet, and the burning of the imperial palace was retribution for his abandonment of laws and disobedience to etiquette.
In the summer of the 20th year of Duke Yan, a great disaster occurred in the state of Qi. Liu Xiang believed that Duke Huan of Qi was lustful, listened to women, treated his concubines as his legitimate wives, and changed his concubines many times, thus causing great disasters.
Duke Huan of Qi did not wake up. When he died, the prince and several other sons came to compete for the throne. Yu and Yu were not buried for nine months.
"The Legend of Gongyang" says that the great disaster was an epidemic.
Dong Zhongshu believed that Duke Huan of Lu’s wife came to Qi and had an affair with the Marquis of Qi, and seven of Duke Huan’s sisters of Qi were unmarried.
The king is the parents of the common people; the couple is the foundation of fertility and reproduction.
If you are injured, you will die prematurely, so this is the retribution of a natural disaster.
In the twentieth year of Duke Xi, on Yisi day of the fifth month, the West Palace suffered a disaster.
"Gu Liang Zhuan" says that this is the palace where Duke Min lives. The name Mi seems distant, so it is called the West Palace.
Liu Xiang believes that Duke Xi of Lu pursued his biological mother as his concubine and brought her to the ancestral temple to offer sacrifices. Therefore, heaven sent disasters to the palace where Duke Min was formerly located. It seemed that removing this lowly person would affect the normal rituals of sacrifices in the ancestral temple.
Dong Zhongshu believed that Duke Xi of Lu hired a woman from Chu as his wife and a woman from Qi as his concubine, and Qi forced Duke Xi of Lu to marry a Qi woman as his wife.
summary: Fire, the second element, represents the south and brilliance. Proper governance, including selecting wise officials and distinguishing virtue, allows fire to maintain its nature. Neglecting morality and allowing slander leads to fires that damage ancestral temples and palaces. The text cites numerous fires from the "Spring and Autumn," such as the palace granary fire in the fourteenth year of Duke Huan, interpreted by Dong Zhongshu as a warning against laziness and by Liu Xiang as a sign of the wife's rebellious heart. Other fires include those in Qi, the West Palace, Luoyang's Xuanxie, and the newly completed palace in Lu, each linked to political misdeeds like usurpation, improper marriages, or neglect of rituals.

translation:
It is said in the legend: If you build palaces, decorate terraces and pavilions, engage in sexual immorality, offend your relatives, and treat your father and brothers disrespectfully, your agriculture will suffer disaster.
Explained: Earth, located in the center of heaven and earth, is the foundation for the growth of all things.
For the emperor, it was about fixing things in the palace.
Palaces, couples, and relatives are also necessary for childbearing and rearing.
In ancient times, the size and height of the palaces and temples of the emperors and princes were stipulated by etiquette. There were certain institutional restrictions on the number, selection and release of queens, wives and concubines. The relatives, elders and children of the nine tribes were also ordered.
Confucius said: In terms of etiquette, it is better to be frugal than to be extravagant and extravagant.
Therefore, Dayu lived in a narrow and simple palace, and King Wen of Zhou treated his wife with courtesy. This is the reason why saints can teach clearly!
If we can do this, we can make the soil acquire its nature.
On the contrary, if one is extravagant, promiscuous, arrogant and arrogant, it will cause the earth to lose its nature.
Even if there are no floods or droughts, vegetation and crops will not grow well, and farming will be in vain.
According to the "Spring and Autumn Classic", in the winter of the 28th year of Duke Yan of Lu, a large number of wheat seedlings died.
Dong Zhongshu believed that Mrs. Yan Gong's wife lamented Jiang Huang's obscenity and violated the Yin Qi, so a flood drowned the wheat seedlings.
Liu Xiang believes that if there are floods and droughts, they should be recorded. If there are no records of floods and droughts, but only say that "wheat seedlings died in large numbers", it should be due to unsafe conditions and poor agricultural harvests.
At that time, Mrs. Ai Jiang was having an affair with her two brothers-in-law, and they were unruly. Also, when the famine was severe, she built a pavilion three times in one year, which resulted in failure in farming. This was the so-called punishment for beautifying the pavilion and indulging in sexual immorality.
Duke Yan of Lu did not repent and wake up, and died four years later. The disaster spread to two generations, creating the disaster caused by luxury and promiscuity.
It is said in the legend: Being militaristic and warlike, disregarding the people, decorating city defenses, and invading borders will cause the metal to lose its properties and fail to be smelted.
Explained: Gold represents the West. After all things mature, a chilling atmosphere appears.
Therefore, at the beginning of autumn, you see eagles striking the sky, and at the autumnal equinox, there is a thin layer of frost.
The business of the country at this time is to lead the army out, hold the battle flag, hold the ax and iron, and swear oath to the officers and soldiers, so as to conquer rebellion and suppress rebellion.
The Book of Songs says: Pious and mighty, holding on to a big ax firmly; as fierce as fire, unstoppable.
He also said: Collect spears and spears, put bows and arrows into Tao.
Movement, stillness, action, and timing, willing to risk danger, the people are not afraid of death.
If this can be done, metal can gain its nature.
On the contrary, if you are arrogant and arrogant in your pursuit of great achievements, and do everything to establish prestige and defeat others, and do not put people's lives first, it will cause gold to lose its nature.
summary: Earth, the third element, is central and foundational for growth. Proper governance involves modest palaces, regulated marriages, and respect for relatives. Extravagance and promiscuity cause earth to lose its nature, leading to poor harvests. The text cites the death of wheat seedlings in the twenty-eighth year of Duke Yan of Lu, attributed by Dong Zhongshu to the wife's obscenity and by Liu Xiang to the construction of pavilions and immoral behavior.

translation:
When craftsmen smelt and cast gold and iron, the gold and iron would become stagnant like ice, hard and unable to be processed. Often they would not be able to make the required swords or utensils, and even weird things would appear. The metal would lose its properties and cannot be smelted. "Zuo Shi Zhuan" says that in the spring of the eighth year of Zhaogong, there were stones in Jin State that spoke.
Duke Ping of Jin asked Shi Kuang, the official, about this matter. Shi Kuang replied: Stones cannot speak. It may be that the gods speak through the stones.
When work is done out of season, resentment and dissatisfaction boil among the people, causing something that cannot speak to speak.
Nowadays, the palaces are so tall and gorgeous, the people's power is exhausted, complaints are everywhere, and the people are in dire straits. Isn't it just right for the stones to speak out?
At that time, the Marquis of Jin was building the Palace of Nanqi.
Shu Xiang said: What the gentleman Shi Kuang said is credible and verified.
Liu Xin believed that gold and stone were the same kind of thing. Stone can speak just like gold cannot be smelted and has lost its original properties.
Liu Xiang believes that the main color of stones is white, and the words spoken by the stones should be considered a bad omen.
In the fifth month of the third year of Emperor Cheng of the Han Dynasty, Hongjia, Yihai, a large rock screamed in the Nanshan Mountain of Hebei County, Tianshui. The sound was as rumbling as thunder. After a while, it stopped screaming, and then the chorus of wild parrots was heard in an area 240 miles away from Pingxiang.
The huge stone that produced the sound is one foot or three feet long, roughly equal in width and length. It is attached to half of the cliff on one side and is about 200 feet above the ground. Folks are accustomed to calling it "Shigu".
When the stone drum cries, there will be a war.
This year, shackled prisoners in Guanghan County planned to capture the prison. Zheng Gong and others, who were guilty of capital crimes, stole weapons from the arsenal, robbed officials and people, put on brocade clothes, and called themselves tigers, and their gang members grew more and more.
In the winter of the second year, he was executed by law. More than 3,000 people surrendered voluntarily.
Four years later, Fan Bing and others from Weishi County rebelled and killed Yan Pu, the prefect of Chenliu. He claimed to be a general, Su Ling, a fugitive prisoner from Shanyang County, and hundreds of party members stole the weapons from the arsenal. They harassed him in more than 40 counties and counties, and they were not executed until the following year.
At that time, the construction of Changling Mausoleum was underway, with tens of thousands of migrant workers and more than 5,000 households of officials and civilians from various counties and counties relocated to worship the mausoleum.
After five years of construction and no completion, the construction of Changling Mausoleum was stopped and the relocated households were allowed to return to their place of origin.
The cry of stones is the same as the speech of stones in the Jin Dynasty in the Spring and Autumn Period. It is what Shi Kuang said "the people's power is exhausted" and what the legend said "ignoring the people".
Luqi's palace is forty miles away from Jiangdu, and Changling is also in the countryside. When it comes to divination, it is the same as in the city.
The city belongs to gold, and the ancestral temple belongs to earth. There is only a difference between the inside and outside.
summary: Metal, the fourth element, represents the west and is associated with military campaigns. Proper use involves timely warfare and respect for life. Arrogance and disregard for the people cause metal to lose its properties, leading to strange events like speaking stones. The text references stones speaking in Jin during the eighth year of Duke Zhao, interpreted by Shi Kuang as a sign of exhausted people's power due to excessive palace construction. A similar event in the Han dynasty involved a large stone crying in Tianshui, linked to rebellions and the construction of Changling mausoleum.

translation:
It is said in the legend: If you neglect the rituals of the ancestral temple, do not pray to the gods, abandon the sacrifices, and go against the laws of nature, the water will not flow.
Explained: Water represents the north, the ultimate place where all things are collected.
As far as the way of life and death is concerned, the physical body must be buried after the end of life, while the spirit should be free and detached. For this reason, the saint created the ancestral temple to collect the wandering soul energy, so that future generations can sacrifice their ancestors in the spring and autumn seasons and fulfill the filial piety.
When the emperor ascends the throne, he must worship heaven and earth in the suburbs, pray to the gods, look up and offer sacrifices to the mountains, and summon hundreds of gods to come and enjoy them. Everything must be done respectfully.
Purify your body carefully and fast, be serious and pious, and let the ghosts and gods enjoy it, so that you can receive more blessings and help from the gods.
This is the approach adopted by the Holy King to serve Yin Qi respectfully and harmonize the relationship between gods and humans.
As for the king's orders, he must also follow the timing of heaven.
If you can comply with the solar terms for twelve months of the year, you can harmonize Yin and Yang and start well and end well.
This will allow the water to acquire its nature.
If ghosts and gods are not respected and political orders are contrary to the laws of nature, water will lose its nature.
In this way, black water breaks out, rivers overflow, wash away cities and rural areas, drown people, and continuous rains damage crops, this is the water not moistening.
Jingfang's "Yi Zhuan" says: Absolute power and indulgence in lust, and unreasonable punishments will cause floods. Floods are heavy rains that drown people, frost, strong winds, and dark skies.
Not cutting down on meals and frugality in a year of famine would be too extravagant, and it would also be the cause of floods that could drown people.
The emperor made moral people suppressed and unable to be reused. This is called arrogance and ignorance. The natural disasters caused were also floods. Rivers overflowed and drowned people. After the floods, the fields were infested with pests.
The great prison does not know how to stop, and the creation is stubborn and will kill people in the cold.
It is unethical to pursue and kill relentlessly, and the floods caused by this will mean that the crops will not be harvested.
Pursuing a defeated enemy relentlessly is what is called Quan Yin.
To be lazy means to give up and not pursue. A person who is the king of the world will only kill the chief culprit of a defeated enemy and pardon his tribe. Otherwise, the yin energy will be everywhere, and floods will flow into the city and countryside of the country, and frost will fall from the sky and freeze the crops.
In the autumn of the first year of Huan AD, there was a flood.
Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang believed that at that time Duke Huan of Lu killed his brother Duke Yin of Lu. The subjects mourned Duke Yin and despised Duke Huan's actions.
This caused the flood. Later, Hua Fu, the governor of the Song State, killed his king, and the princes gathered to attack the Song State. Duke Huan of Lu accepted Song's bribe and withdrew his army, and then turned his back on the Song State.
Because of this, the princes and countries attacked the Lu State, and they fought endlessly and became enemies. Dead bodies were everywhere and blood flowed into rivers. The people became even more resentful, so there was another flood in the summer of the thirteenth year.
summary: Water, the fifth element, represents the north and is associated with ancestral rituals and proper governance. Neglecting sacrifices and issuing contrary orders cause water to lose its nature, leading to floods and continuous rains. The text lists numerous floods from the "Spring and Autumn" and Han dynasty, such as those in the first year of Duke Huan of Lu, attributed to the killing of Duke Yin and subsequent conflicts. Other floods are linked to scandals, improper marriages, and military campaigns. In the Han dynasty, floods occurred during the reigns of Gaohou, Emperor Wen, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Cheng, often tied to political turmoil, such as the Lu family's power, Xiongnu invasions, or the abolition of ancestral temples.

translation:
Humans imitate the shapes of heaven and earth, possess the five constant natures of benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and faith. They are intelligent, sensible, meticulous, and simple. They are the most spiritual among living animals.
Human hands and feet are not enough to provide for hobbies and desires, running is not enough to avoid harm, and there are no furs and feathers to protect against cold and heat. Therefore, humans must use all things to feed themselves. They use wisdom instead of relying on force. This is the reason why humans are noble.
Therefore, if people are not benevolent, they cannot form a group. If they cannot form a group, they cannot defeat external objects. If they cannot defeat external objects, their offerings will not be sufficient.
If a group is formed but the material is still not sufficient, the mentality of competition will arise. The saints of the previous generation deliberately took the lead in emphasizing the morality of respect, humility and charity, and the people were happy and followed them.
When the people who follow them form a group, they become monarchs; when everyone vie to join them, they become kings. "Shang Shu.
"Hong Fan" said: The emperor becomes the parents of the people and the emperor of the world.
The saints choose similar titles to rectify their status and call the king their parents. They understand that benevolence and humility are the foundation of kingship.
Benevolence will not be corrupted if it relies on reverence, and kindness must be majestic to survive for a long time. Therefore, etiquette is formulated to promote reverence, and criminal laws are formulated to show majesty.
Since the sage himself has the character of discernment, he must be familiar with the thoughts of heaven and earth, formulate rituals and education, establish legal systems and set up criminal laws, and always comply with the people's sentiments, so that he can manage the earth according to the laws of heaven.
Therefore, it is said that the previous kings established the ritual system based on the gods from heaven. According to the nature of the earth.
Prisons of punishment and majesty are used to imitate the killing power of God with thunder and lightning; gentleness, kindness, generosity and harmony are used to imitate God's ability to grow and nourish all things.
"Shangshu" says that Heaven rewards polite people according to their rank, and Heaven punishes sinful people.
Therefore, the sages formulated the five rites of good fortune, misfortune, military service, military affairs, and good fortune according to the order of heaven, and formulated the five punishments according to the principle of punishment from heaven.
For large punishments, armor is used, for lighter punishments, axes and irons are used; for medium punishments, knives and saws are used, for lighter punishments, drills are used; for small punishments, whips are used.
Large-scale punishments required the corpses to be displayed in the plains and wilderness, while small-scale punishments required public display in the streets and courts. This situation has a long history.
Since the time of the Yellow Emperor, the Battle of Zhuolu put down the Yandi Rebellion, and during the Zhuanxu Period, the Battle of Gonggong put down the Gonggong Rebellion.
During the reign of Tang Yu, he was able to bring peace to the world by offering sacrifices, and he still exiled Gonggong, banished Huandou, expelled Sanmiao, and killed Gun, and then the world surrendered.
In the Xia Dynasty, Youqi and the Youhu clan fought in Gan, and it was not until the Yin and Zhou dynasties that they used military force to pacify the world.
summary: Humans are considered the most spiritual of living beings, possessing the five constant natures of benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and faith, and imitating the shapes of heaven and earth. However, lacking natural defenses like fur or speed, humans must rely on wisdom and cooperation to survive. Without benevolence, they cannot form groups, and without groups, they cannot overcome external threats. Ancient saints established morality, rituals, and laws to maintain order, with kingship rooted in benevolence and humility. Rituals and punishments were created to imitate divine order, with the five rites and five punishments derived from heavenly principles. Military organization evolved from ancient times, with systems of land division and military taxes, such as the well-field system, supporting armies of varying sizes, from the House of Hundred Chariots to the Lord of Ten Thousand Chariots. Military training occurred during seasonal hunts, and feudal states were organized under officers, with regular reviews of troops.

translation:
If ten or five people are connected together, they can live together and share joys, share sorrows and sorrows, and share blessings and misfortunes. Therefore, when fighting at night, they can hear each other's voices, and when fighting during the day, they can see each other. In times of crisis, they are enough to die for each other.
The formation of this kind of education eliminated the intrusion of Yi and Di externally, respected the emperor internally, and stabilized the domestic princes.
After the fall of Duke Huan of Qi, Duke Wen of Jin succeeded him. He also first stabilized his people, formulated the law of being imprisoned, commanded the princes, and succeeded him as the leader of the alliance.
However, his etiquette system has gone beyond the bounds of duty and made many mistakes, and he always acted in discord in order to seek quick success and quick gain, so it cannot be regarded as the legal system of the former king.
After Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, it gradually declined. By the time of Duke Cheng of Lu, a decree was made to make the hilly areas pay land tax. Duke Ai also assigned a tax to each of the land and family property. Things such as hunting, managing the army, and grand military parades all lost their orthodoxy.
"Spring and Autumn" recorded this and criticized it in order to preserve the royal way.
After that, wars broke out many times, and the people were weak and exhausted, and they lost the sense of sacrifice and sacrifice.
Confucius felt sad about this and said: To fight with untrained people is to abandon them.
Therefore, he praised Zilu and said: Zhong Yuan, when you go to a country with a thousand military chariots, you can put him in charge of the army.
Zilu also said: A country with a thousand chariots is sandwiched between several big countries. It is invaded by armies outside and famine inside. I will govern it. After three years, everyone will have courage and understand the truth.
This means that in managing taxes and the army, etiquette and righteousness must also be taught.
After the Spring and Autumn Period, weak countries were annexed and merged to form the Warring States Period. Some martial arts etiquette was slightly added as a game for fun and to show off to each other.
During the Qin Dynasty, it was renamed "Jiao Da". The etiquette of the previous kings was drowned in unrighteous music. Extraordinary and outstanding people assisted the situation according to the current situation. They used cunning and cunning to compete with each other. Wu had Sun Wu, Qi had Sun Bin, Wei had Wu Qi, and Qin had Shang Yang.
At this time, they joined forces vertically and horizontally, and turned to attack each other, competing for hegemony.
King Min of Qi became strong with the martial arts of Qi, King Hui of Wei worked hard with the soldiers of Wei, and King Zhao of Qin won with the sharp soldiers of Qin.
The secular world is fighting for utilitarianism, and the lobbyists regard Sun Bin and Wu Qi as the objects of respect.
At that time, Sun Qing was the only one who understood the royal way, so he criticized this situation and said: People like Sun Bin and Wu Qi advocate power and wealth and value cunning and cunning; when applied to a country that is violent, chaotic, ignorant and careless, it creates a gap between the monarch and his ministers, disunity between the superiors and subordinates, and poor political planning, so they can be cunning and cunning.

Confucius emphasized moral guidance over legal coercion. The Warring States period saw harsh laws under Shen Buhai and Shang Yang, culminating in Qin Shihuang's oppressive regime, which led to widespread rebellion. The Han Dynasty initially simplified laws under Gaozu, but later emperors like Xiaowen and Xiaojing reformed punishments, abolishing corporal punishment and reducing flogging. Despite these efforts, legal complexity grew, and by Emperor Wu's reign, laws became increasingly strict, with over 13,000 capital offenses. Emperor Xuan and Emperor Yuan attempted to simplify laws, but reforms were incomplete. The text further examines the Han Dynasty's legal reforms and their shortcomings. The Zhou system of five hearings, eight discussions, and three pardons aimed for fairness, but Han officials often failed to implement these principles. Emperors issued edicts to protect the elderly, young, and disabled from harsh punishments. Despite these efforts, the number of lawsuits and executions remained high, with over 10,000 deaths annually. The root causes included lack of moral education, unclear laws, poverty, and corruption. Confucius noted that ancient judges sought to save lives, while modern ones sought to kill. Xunzi argued that punishments should match crimes, and that heavy penalties are necessary in peaceful times to deter evil. The author suggests restoring ancient corporal punishments and simplifying laws to achieve harmony, as seen in the prosperous reigns of Cheng and Kang.

He dredged rivers according to the trend of the mountains and determined tax levels according to the land conditions; he built roads in Kyushu, built embankments of lakes in Kyushu, and measured the mountains of Kyushu.
However, the Yellow River overflowed and caused great harm to the Central Plains.
He regarded the management of the Yellow River as his top priority, so he guided the Yellow River water from Jishi Mountain, through Longmen, south to Huayin County, eastward through Dizhu Mountain and the bends of Mengjin and Luoshui Rivers, to Daren Mountain.
So Dayu believed that the source of the Yellow River was high and the current was turbulent, making it difficult to circulate on flat land. After several diversion attempts failed, he divided the Yellow River into two rivers to reduce the water potential.
The rivers in Kyushu have been dredged, the lakes in Kyushu have been embanked, and the various countries in China have been managed and stabilized. Their achievements have benefited the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties.
From then on, the water of the Yellow River was diverted from Rongyang to the southeast, forming a gap that connected the countries of Song, Zheng, Chen, Cai, Cao, and Wei, and intersected with Jishui, Rushui, Huaishui, and Swimming rivers respectively.
In the Chu region, ditches were built to connect Moshui and Yunmeng in the west, and ditches were dug to connect the Yangtze River and Huaishui in Shumian.
In Wudi, canals were opened to connect the three rivers and five lakes.
At Qidi, it connects Zi River and Jishui River.
In Shu, Li Bing, the governor of Shu, dug two rivers in Chengdu to avoid the harm of Moshui.
These canals can be used for boats, and the excess water is used for irrigation, and the people enjoy its benefits.
As for the areas where canal water passes, people often drink water to irrigate their fields. There are quite a few ditches, but they are countless.
During the reign of Wei Wenhou, Ximen Bao was the magistrate of Ye County and had a good reputation.
When King Xiang, the great grandson of Marquis Wen, was drinking with his ministers, King Xiang toasted the ministers and said: I hope all my ministers will be ministers like Ximen Bao!
Shi Qi remonstrated: "Wei's practice is to allow one man to have one hundred acres of land. Ye County alone has two hundred acres. The land here is not good."
Zhangshui is next to it, and Ximen Leopard does not know how to use it. This is not smart.
Not doing it after knowing it is unkind.
Neither benevolence nor wisdom has been achieved, so how can we imitate them?
So he appointed Shi Qi as the magistrate of Ye County, and diverted water from Zhangzhou to irrigate Ye County, making the Hanoi area of ​​Wei rich.
The people praised him and said: There is a wise magistrate in Ye County, Shi Gong, who opened the Zhang River to irrigate the areas around Ye County, so that rice can grow on the salty land since ancient times.
After that, Han heard that Qin liked to build things, so he planned to tire Qin so that it would not be able to send troops to the east.
So South Korea sent hydraulic engineer Zheng Guo to secretly lobby the Qin State, asking it to drill through the Jingshui River, build a canal from the west of Zhongshan to Hukou, follow the Beishan Mountain, and flow eastward into the Luoshui River. The total length is more than 300 miles, and it is intended to be used to irrigate farmland.
summary: The "Book of Xia" records Yu's thirteen-year flood control efforts, during which he passed his home without entering. He traveled by various means—car, boat, sled, or sedan—to delineate Kyushu's boundaries, dredge rivers, and assess land for taxation. Despite his work, the Yellow River continued to devastate the Central Plains. Yu prioritized managing it, guiding its waters from Jishi Mountain through Longmen and other locations, but its turbulent flow proved difficult to tame. He eventually split the river into two to reduce its force. After Kyushu's rivers and lakes were stabilized, the benefits extended to the Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties. The Yellow River was later diverted southeast, intersecting with several rivers and countries. In various regions, canals were built for irrigation and transport. In Chu, ditches connected Moshui and Yunmeng; in Wu, canals linked three rivers and five lakes; in Qi, the Zi and Jishui rivers were joined. In Shu, Li Bing dug two rivers in Chengdu to prevent flooding. These canals facilitated boat travel and irrigation, bringing prosperity. During Wei Wenhou's reign, Ximen Bao governed Ye County with a good reputation, but his successor Shi Qi criticized him for not using the Zhangshui River for irrigation. Shi Qi then diverted the Zhangshui to irrigate Ye County, making the area fertile. Later, the Qin state employed Zheng Guo, a Han spy, to build a canal from the Jingshui River. Though initially suspected, Zheng Guo convinced Qin of the canal's long-term benefits. The canal irrigated over 40,000 hectares of salty land, enriching Qin and enabling it to conquer other states; it was named the Zheng Guo Canal.

translation:
The matter was discovered during the process, and Qin Guo planned to kill Zheng Guo.
Zheng Guo said: In the beginning, the minister was a spy, but after it was completed, it was also in the interests of Qin.
I extended the fate of South Korea for a few years, but made achievements for Qin that lasted forever.
The State of Qin also thought this was the case, and finally ordered him to continue building the canal.
After the canal was built, the silted and turbid water was used to irrigate more than 40,000 hectares of salty land, so that the harvest reached one minute per mu.
As a result, the Guanzhong area became a fertile land with no disasters. As a result, the Qin State became rich and powerful, and finally annexed the princes, so the canal was named Zheng Guo Canal.
Thirty-nine years after the establishment of the Han Dynasty, during the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, the Yellow River burst its banks at Suizao and the Jin Dynasty in the east collapsed. So Dongjun mobilized soldiers to block the Yellow River.
Thirty-six years later, during the Yuanguang period of Emperor Xiaowu, the Yellow River broke through Guzi and flowed southeast into Juyeze, and then to the Huai River and the Swimming River.
The emperor sent Ji An and Zheng to mobilize personnel to block the breach, but it soon collapsed again.
At this time, Marquis Tian Ju of Wuzhou was the prime minister, and his town was in Lang County.
If Hexian County is north of the Yellow River, and the Yellow River flows to the south, then there will be no floods in Hexian County, and the income of Yixian County will increase.
Tian Gecko said to the emperor: The bursting of the banks of the Yangtze River and the Yellow River is God's will. It is not suitable to use human power to forcefully block the breaches. Forcibly blocking the breaches may not be in accordance with God's will.
And people who looked up at the clouds and used magic to divine fortune also thought so, so it was no longer blocked for a long time.
Zheng Zheng, who was the chief agricultural officer at the time, said that in the past, it took about six months to transport corn from the Wei River to Guandong. However, the Wei River is more than 900 miles long and there are often dangerous places.
A canal was opened from Chang'an to divert the Wei River, flowing downstream along the Nanshan Mountains. It is more than 300 miles away from the Yellow River. It is a straight road and is easy to navigate by boat. It is estimated that it will take three months; and more than 10,000 hectares of farmland that the canal water passes through can be irrigated.
This can not only reduce water transportation time and soldiers, but also make Guanzhong's farmland more fertile and obtain more food.
The emperor thought it was right, so he sent Uncle Xu, a water engineer from the state of Qi, to make a mark, and sent tens of thousands of soldiers to dig canals and canals, and they were completed in three years.
It is indeed very convenient for water transportation.
After that, water transportation gradually increased, and the people around the canal were able to benefit from irrigated fields.
Later, Fan Xi, the governor of Hedong, said: The cost of transporting grain and rice from Shandong to the west is more than one million dan per year. After going through the hardships in the Dizhu area, the damage was huge and the cost was huge.
By opening canals to divert Fen water to irrigate Pishi and Fenyin areas, and to divert Yellow River water to Fenyin and Puban areas, it is estimated that 5,000 hectares of farmland can be created.
Because this is all abandoned wasteland by the Yellow River. People graze here and now irrigate and cultivate it. It is estimated that they can get more than two million shi of grain.
summary: During the Han dynasty, the Yellow River burst multiple times. In Emperor Xiaowen's reign, it broke at Suizao, and later during Yuanguang, it breached at Huzi, flowing into Juyeze and the Huai River. Attempts to block it failed, and Tian Ju advised against further efforts, citing divine will. Zheng Dangshi proposed a canal from Chang'an to divert the Wei River, reducing transport time and irrigating farmland. The emperor approved, and the canal was completed in three years, improving water transport and irrigation. Subsequent proposals included diverting Fen and Yellow River waters in Hedong, but the canals became useless after the river changed course. Other projects, like the Baoxie Road canal, faced challenges due to rocky waters. Yan Xiong's plan to irrigate salty land with Luoshui water led to the Longshou Canal, but it yielded little benefit after a decade.

translation:
What can I do about the Huzi River Judgment?
The mighty water may become the Yellow River.
The whole Yellow River has become uneasy, and there is no end to the river work. My mountains have already been dug.
My mountains are being leveled, the wild rivers are flowing out, the fish are not happy, and winter is approaching again.
The rivers are slack and the water is always flowing, and the dragons are galloping and they are allowed to travel far away.
The water has returned to the old river channel. God is taking care of Peixian. If you don’t come out to pray, you don’t know what’s going on outside!
I said to He Bo, why are you so unkind and the floods are endless and so depressing?
The Huai River and the swimming pool are full of mulberry trees floating in the water. I wish I could not return to my old path for a long time. I wish the water flow would slow down a little.
Another one is:
The Yellow River is soupy and the water flows quickly. The north crossing is winding and the water flow is difficult to clear.
He pulled out the sprigs of grass and stuck them in the breach, and the beautiful jade fell into the river. He Bo agreed to calm the water, but there was not enough grass.
The lack of grass is the fault of the defenders. The people have insufficient firewood to keep the water flowing. Cut down the bamboos from the Qi Garden and make them into arbors to block the stone pillars. If the defense is blocked, great blessings will come.
So the breach of the gourd was finally blocked, and a palace was built on it, named Xuanfang.
Moreover, two canals were built on the north bank of the Yellow River to divert the water flow and restore the old appearance during the time of Dayu. The Liang and Chu areas regained peace and were free from floods.
From then on, people in power rushed to talk about the benefits of building canals.
Shuofang, Xihe, Hexi, Jiuquan and other areas all divert water from the Yellow River and river valleys to irrigate farmland.
The Lingzhi, Chengguo and Zhang canals in Guanzhong diverted the rivers, Runan and Jiujiang diverted the Huai River, Shuhai diverted the Juding, and the bottom of Mount Tai diverted the Wen River. They all dug canals to irrigate the fields, each with more than 10,000 hectares.
There are countless other small canals and water channels that cut through the mountains.
From the time when the Zheng Guo Canal was dug to the sixth year of Yuanding, it had been 136 years. Ni Kuan, the internal history of Zuo, petitioned to dig six auxiliary canals to facilitate the irrigation of the high farmland in the Zheng Guo Canal area.
The emperor said: Agriculture is the foundation of the world.
The spring water irrigates and nourishes the crops.
There used to be quite a lot of famous mountains and rivers in places where internal history was concerned, but the people didn't know their benefits, so they dug ditches and raised lake embankments to prevent droughts.
Nowadays, the land lease of Naishi rice fields is very heavy. Unlike other counties, I advocate for a reduction or exemption.
Order the government and the people to devote themselves to agriculture, make full use of the potential of the land, balance water conservancy, and not cause the people to miss the time for farming.
Sixteen years later, in the second year of Taishi, Bai Gong, the middle official of Zhao State, again petitioned to open the canal.
The Jing River is diverted from the mouth of the valley, flows into Liyang, and flows into the Wei River. It is 200 miles long and irrigates more than 4,500 hectares of farmland, so the canal is called Baiqu.
When the people benefited from it, they praised it and said: Where is the field?
Chiyang and Taniguchi are the places.
summary: After the Huzi breach, the emperor personally oversaw its blockage, composing songs about the struggle. The breach was finally sealed, and two canals were built to restore the river's old course. This success spurred widespread canal construction across Shuofang, Xihe, Hexi, and other regions, each irrigating over 10,000 hectares. Smaller canals were countless. By the sixth year of Yuanding, Ni Kuan proposed six auxiliary canals for the Zheng Guo Canal area. The emperor emphasized agriculture and reduced land taxes. Sixteen years later, Bai Gong opened the Baiqu Canal, diverting Jingshui water to irrigate 4,500 hectares. The people praised both canals for their fertility. During the Han-Xiongnu wars, Yannian proposed a massive canal to divert the Yellow River, but the emperor hesitated, citing Dayu's legacy. After the Xuanfang breach, the river broke again at Guantao, forming the Tunshi River, which was left unblocked.

translation:
If there is continuous heavy rain and no sunshine for more than ten days, the river will definitely overflow.
Lingmingdukou is located on the eastern border of Qinghe River and is in a low position. Even if it is made unobstructed, it will not reduce the flood damage to Weijun and Qinghe River.
It's not that Dayu didn't value the power of the people, but because the terrain was high and low, he dug the Jiuhe River. Now it's hard to distinguish the traces of the Jiuhe River. The Tunshi River has been stagnant for more than 70 years. It was cut off not long ago and is easy to dredge.
In addition, the terrain where it originates is high, which can be used to divert water and reduce hydraulic pressure, making it easy to channel. It can be re-dredged to help the river divert floods in case of special circumstances.
In addition, in the middle of the Dijie year, Guo Chang dug a straight canal. Three years later, the Yellow River flow rejoined southward about six miles north of the original second bend.
Now its curved momentum is slowly passing through Danqiu County again. The people feel chilled and should reopen the canal to make the water flow eastward.
If it is not repaired, four or five counties will be harmed by the breach in the north, and more than ten counties will be harmed by the breach in the south. We will not worry about it until then. It's too late.
The matter was handed over to the Prime Minister and the Censor. The Prime Minister and the Censor said that Xu Shang, a doctor, had studied the Book of Documents and was good at calculations and could estimate costs.
Xu Shang was sent to inspect the river, and he believed that the flooding of the Tunshi River coincided with the country's lack of financial resources and manpower, so dredging could not be carried out for the time being.
Three years later, the Yellow River broke through the Jindi in Guantao and Shujun, flooding Yanzhou and Yuzhou, and entering Pingyuan, Qiancheng, Jinan and other places. A total of 32 counties in four counties were flooded, and more than 150,000 hectares of water were flooded. The depth was up to 30 feet, and nearly 40,000 official houses were damaged.
The imperial censor Yin Zhong's correct strategy was unrealistic. The emperor severely scolded him, and Yin Zhong committed suicide.
The emperor sent his chief minister Nong Fei to allocate the money and grains of Junping to the counties and counties flooded by the Yellow River burst. He sent two emissaries to recruit 500 canal boats from Henan Province, and moved the people to live on the hills to avoid the water flow. There were more than 97,000 people in total.
Wang Yanshi, the envoy of the Yellow River Embankment, was sent to block the breach. He used bamboo four feet long and nine feet in diameter, filled with small stones, and thrown into the river between two boats.
In thirty-six days, the Yellow River embankment was formed.
The emperor said: The Yellow River in Shujun burst and drifted to Erzhou. The school captain Wang Yanshi built an embankment and it was completed in the thirtieth year.
It is decreed that five years will be the first year of Heping.
Among the soldiers who controlled the Yellow River, they were ordered to serve as border guards for six months.
Only Wang Yanshi was good at strategizing and planning, and he was very economical in achieving his achievements, using less energy and less time. I appreciate this very much.
Wang Yanshi was specially appointed as Guanglu doctor, received a salary of two thousand dan, was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, and was rewarded with a hundred catties of gold.
Two years later, the Yellow River broke through the plain again and flowed into Jinan and Qiancheng. The damage was more than half of what it was at the beginning of Jianjian. The emperor sent Wang Yanshi to control Tonghui.
summary: During Emperor Xuan's Dijie period, Guo Chang straightened a meandering section of the Yellow River, benefiting the people. In Yongguang, the river burst at Lingmingdukou, causing the Tunshi River to disappear. Under Emperor Cheng, Feng Kui warned of flood risks and proposed dredging the Tunshi River. Despite initial inaction, a major breach in Guantao flooded 32 counties. Wang Yanshi successfully blocked it, earning rewards. Later breaches required further efforts, with Yang Yan and others involved. Debates over river management continued, with some advocating for relocating people and opening canals, while others favored minimal intervention. During Wang Mang's reign, various experts proposed strategies, but none were implemented. The text concludes by emphasizing the Yellow River's significance and the need for careful study of water management.

translation:
The principles mentioned in the "Six Classics" all achieve the same goal, and the functions of "Li" and "Yue" are particularly urgent.
Once those who cultivate themselves forget the propriety, they will suffer from evil and contempt; once those who govern the country lose the propriety, desolation and disorder will come.
Human beings contain the yin and yang of heaven and earth, and have emotions of joy, anger, sorrow and joy.
Heaven upholds its characteristics but cannot exercise restraint, but saints can use it restrainedly and without interruption. Therefore, rituals and music are made according to the laws of heaven and earth to communicate with gods, establish human ethics, correct human temperament, and regulate all things.
It is human nature to have differences between men and women and to be jealous of others, so we have formulated the etiquette of marriage; it is human nature to have the order of interaction between elders and younger generations, so we have formulated the drinking ceremony in the countryside;
Grief has the etiquette of crying and mourning, joy has the appearance of singing and dancing, which is enough for the upright person to be sincere, and it is enough for the evil person to prevent mistakes.
Therefore, if the marriage etiquette is abolished, then the etiquette between husband and wife will be coarse, and the sins of debauchery and lewdness between men and women will increase; if the country drinking ceremony is abolished, then the order of elders and younger generations will be confused, and there will be more lawsuits; If the etiquette is abolished, the kindness between flesh and blood will be weakened, and more and more people will abandon the dead and forget their ancestors; if the etiquette of meeting the emperor is abolished, then the positions of the monarch and his ministers will be wrong, and the phenomenon of aggression and bullying will gradually occur.
Therefore, Confucius said: There is no better way to stabilize a country and govern the people than propriety; to change the atmosphere and change customs, there is no better way than music.
Etiquette can control the thoughts of the people, music can harmonize the voices of the people, implement it with government decrees, and prevent it with criminal laws.
If etiquette, music, government orders, and criminal laws are all passed without hindrance, then the kingly way is complete.
If music is used to govern the interior, harmony is needed; if ritual is used to modify the exterior, diversity is needed; harmony can lead to harmony and mutual affection, and difference can produce fear and respect; harmony and mutual love will not cause resentment, and fear and admiration will not cause strife.
The world is governed well by doing nothing, the effects of etiquette and music.
The two are used together and become one.
Fear and respect are difficult to express, so they use wine and food, speeches, and kneeling to express it; the joy of harmonious love is difficult to describe, so they use poems, songs, chants, words, and bells and stones to express it.
This is to praise a person's respect without touching his property, and to praise a person's happy mood without touching his voice.
So Confucius said: "Etiquette, etiquette, can it be expressed in jade and silk?"
Joy, joy, how can we use bells and drums to express it?
This is the foundation of etiquette and joy.
Therefore, it is said: Those who understand the nature of ritual and music can innovate, and those who understand the system of ritual and music can inherit it; those who innovate are called saints, and those who inherit it are called Ming.
Mingsheng is all about innovation and inheritance.
summary: The principles of the "Six Classics" share a common goal, with the functions of "Li" (ritual) and "Yue" (music) being particularly urgent. For individuals, forgetting propriety leads to evil and contempt; for a state, losing it brings desolation and disorder. Ritual and music are made according to the laws of heaven and earth to communicate with gods, establish human ethics, and regulate all things. Specific rituals, such as those for marriage, drinking in the countryside, mourning, and meeting the emperor, are formulated to address human nature and prevent specific vices. Confucius stated that there is no better way to stabilize a country and govern the people than propriety, and no better way to change customs than music. When etiquette, music, government orders, and criminal laws all function smoothly, the kingly way is complete. The two are used together to create harmony and respect.

translation:
The emperor must implement the rites of the previous emperors in accordance with the requirements of the times, add or delete them, and gradually make them according to the people's ideas, until the world is at peace and complete.
The Zhou Dynasty learned from the Xia and Yin Dynasties, and the etiquette system was particularly complete. Systems were established for major events and precautions were taken for minor matters. Therefore, there are 300 etiquette rituals and 3,000 etiquette details.
As a result, education was widespread, the people were harmonious, there were no disasters, no chaos, and the prisons were empty. This situation has been maintained for more than forty years.
Confucius praised it and said: The etiquette is so complete!
I want to learn from the Zhou Dynasty.
When the Zhou Dynasty declined, the princes exceeded the limits of the law and hated the etiquette system for harming their own interests, so they deleted the relevant books and documents.
Then the Qin Dynasty destroyed various schools of thought, and rituals and music were scattered and lost.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, he began to control the troubled times and restore normalcy and stability. Although he did not have a day to spare, Emperor Gaozu still ordered Shusun Tong to formulate etiquette to correct the status of the monarch and his ministers.
Emperor Gaozu happily exclaimed: "I just realized today that being the emperor is the most expensive thing!"
Shusun Tong was appointed as a regular official and etiquette laws were formulated, but Shusun Tong died before they were fully prepared.
At the time of Emperor Wen, Jia Yi believed that the Han Dynasty had inherited the bad customs of the Qin Dynasty, without regard for etiquette and integrity, and now even went so far as to kill his father and elder brothers, and thieves stole artifacts from the ancestral temple, and the ministers also used the copybook as an excuse for not reporting the implementation of the decrees. As a result, evil practices were rampant, and everyone felt at ease and did not feel strange, thinking that this was the case.
It can be seen that it is probably not something that mediocre officials can do to change the atmosphere, change customs, and make everyone in the world change their minds and move towards the right path.
The establishment of monarchs and ministers, the distinction between superiors and subordinates, the ordering of the country's system, and the harmony among relatives are not God's arrangements, but are established by man himself.
Since it is established by people themselves, it cannot be established if they are not practiced, and it will be destroyed if they are not cultivated.
The Han Dynasty has been established for more than 20 years now. It is necessary to formulate systems and promote rituals and music. Then the princes can get on the right track, the people can be simple and unpretentious, and lawsuits will gradually disappear.
So Jia Yi established etiquette, and Emperor Wen was very happy.
But ministers Zhou Bo and Guan Ying were jealous of him, so his suggestions were not adopted.
When Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne, he promoted and appointed people with outstanding talents, discussed the establishment of a bright hall to clarify politics and religion, and formulated etiquette and clothing colors to revitalize peace.
It happened that Empress Dowager Dou liked the Taoist teachings of Huangdi and Laozi, but did not like Confucianism, so the matter was dropped.
Later Dong Zhongshu answered in the test paper: If the emperor wants to make a difference, he should explore his behavior according to heaven.
The way of heaven is boundless, it all depends on yin and yang.
Yang is benevolence and yin is punishment.
The angelic yang is always in the midsummer to nourish all things and make them grow, while the yin is always in the midwinter and accumulates in empty and unused places. From this we can see that heaven advocates virtue and not criminal law.
Yang Qi appears and spreads upward to dominate the time sequence of the year, while Yin Qi enters the underground reservoir and comes out from time to time to assist Yang Qi.
Yang Qi does not have the help of Yin Qi and cannot form the time sequence of the year alone.
The emperor acts according to the will of God, so he must devote himself to benevolent education and reduce punishment.
summary: The Zhou Dynasty learned from the Xia and Yin Dynasties, creating a particularly complete etiquette system with 300 major rituals and 3,000 details. This led to widespread education, harmony, and a lack of disasters for over forty years. When the Zhou Dynasty declined, princes exceeded the law and deleted relevant documents. The Qin Dynasty then destroyed various schools, causing rituals and music to be scattered. After the Han Dynasty was established, Emperor Gaozu ordered Shusun Tong to formulate etiquette. Emperor Wen was pleased with Jia Yi's proposals to establish rituals, but ministers Zhou Bo and Guan Ying were jealous, so his suggestions were not adopted. Emperor Wu's plans were dropped due to Empress Dowager Dou's preference for Taoism. Dong Zhongshu argued that heaven advocates virtue over punishment, and that the Han Dynasty must change its education to reform the people. Emperor Xuan did not adopt Wang Ji's suggestion to select Confucian scholars and inherit old etiquette. Liu Xiang persuaded Emperor Cheng to build Piyong and arrange rituals and music, but the emperor died before the plan was completed. Wang Mang later built Piyong to confuse people and usurp the throne.

translation:
The system was corrupted and gradually declined without hope of revival. The music of Sangjian, Pushang, Zheng, Wei, Song, and Zhao appeared together, which caused diseases and shortened life span internally, and disrupted politics and harmed the people externally.
Crafty and false use it to decorate, in order to confuse the eyes and ears of the rich.
Common people use it to seek benefits, and vassal states use it to alienate each other.
Therefore, after Duke Mu of Qin gave the female singer to Xirong, Yu Yu left. The Qi people rewarded the female singer of Lu, Confucius, and left.
When it came to the Six Kingdoms, Wei Wenhou was the most ancient, but he said to Xia: I want to doze off when I hear ancient music, but when I hear the music of Zheng and Wei, I will not be tired.
Zixia rebuked him and argued with him, but in the end he was not accepted. From then on, ritual and music were lost.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, there was a member of the musical family who was appointed as a music official for generations because he knew the official music and the five tones and six rhythms of the suburban temple court gatherings. However, he could only memorize the rhythm and dance of the music, but could not tell their meaning.
During the reign of Emperor Gaozu, Shusun Tong relied on musicians from the Qin Dynasty to produce music for the ancestral temple.
I wish to welcome the gods at the temple gate and play the music "Jia Zhi", just like the music that brought the gods to visit in ancient times.
When the emperor entered the temple gate, he played the music of "Yongzhi" as a walking rhythm, just like the ancient music of "Picking Shepherd's purse" and "Sixia".
Dried beans are offered and "Dengge" is played. Only one person sings, and no orchestras are used to disturb people's voices. It is hoped that all the officials can hear it, just like the ancient song "Qing Temple".
After "Deng Ge" is played twice, "Xiu Cheng" is played again to praise the gods for having enjoyed the sacrifice.
The emperor went to Shuxiang to drink. After sitting down, he played the music "Yong'an" and praised the completion of the ceremony.
There is also "Ancestral Music in the Fang", which was composed by Mrs. Tangshan of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
There was "Fang Zhong Yue" in the Zhou Dynasty, and it was called "Shou Ren" in the Qin Dynasty.
As with music, if you like what it creates, the etiquette is not to forget the fundamentals.
Emperor Gaozu liked the music of Chu, so "Music in the Fang" has the melody of Chu music.
In the second year of Xiaohui's reign, he asked Yuefu to order Xiahou Kuan to prepare Qi Xiaoguan, so he changed the name to "An Shile".
The dance music played in Gaomiao is "Wude", "Wenshi" and "Five Elements"; the dance music played in Xiaowen Temple is the dance music of "Zhaode", "Wenshi", "Four Seasons" and "Five Elements"; the dance music played in Xiaowu Temple is the dance music of "Shengde", "Wenshi", "Four Seasons" and "Five Elements".
The most commonly performed songs in various imperial temples are "Wen Shi", "Four Seasons", "Five Elements Dance", etc.
In the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he produced "Zhao Rong Le" and "Li Rong Le".
"Zhao Rong Le", like the ancient "Zhao Xia Le", mainly comes from "Wude Dance".
"Li Rong Yue" mainly comes from "Wen Shi" and "Five Elements Dance".
If a person dances without music, it means that he does not dare to use music when he is about to appear in front of the most respected person; using music means that the dance will not lose the rhythm and can end with the music.
Most of them are based on the old events of the Qin Dynasty.
At first, after Emperor Gaozu brought peace to the world, he passed by Peixian County to celebrate with his old friends and fellow villagers. After getting drunk, he became extremely happy and sad, so he composed the poem "The Wind Rises" and ordered one hundred and twenty children in Peixian County to practice and sing it.

translation:
At this time, both Guangdong and Guangdong had been wiped out. The Guangdong people bravely said that the Cantonese customs worship ghosts and gods, and they often see ghosts when they offer sacrifices, which are often effective.
In the past, King Shuou respected ghosts and gods, and his life span was 160 years old.
His descendants neglected ghosts and gods, so their life span was shortened. So they ordered the Cantonese shamans to build a Zhu Temple in Guangdong, set up a platform without an altar, and also offered sacrifices to gods, gods and ghosts, and used chicken bones to perform divination.
The emperor felt this was credible, and the Cantonese temple used the bones of the zodiac for divination from the time of its creation.
Gongsun Qing said: Immortals can be seen, but the emperor was too eager to go, so he could not see them.
Now your majesty can build a pavilion like the one in Fengshi City and display dried meat and dates. You should be able to invite the gods.
And wise people like to live in attics.
So the emperor ordered the Feilian and Gui Pavilions to be built in Chang'an, the Yishou and Longshou Pavilions to be built in Ganquan Palace, and sent Gongsun Qing to arrange sacrifices with talismans to welcome the gods.
Build a platform to reach the sky and display sacrifices below to attract gods and the like.
So Ganquan Palace built the front hall and began to expand the palace rooms.
In summer, there are mushrooms growing in the rooms of Ganquan Palace. The emperor built the Tongtian Tower to block the gap in the Yellow River. Divine light appeared, so the emperor issued an edict to grant amnesty to the world. A year later, he launched a crusade against North Korea.
In summer, there is a major drought.
Gongsun Qing said: When the Yellow Emperor offered sacrifices to the sky, there was a drought, and the soil was sealed for three years.
The emperor then issued an edict: There is a drought. Do you want the soil to be sealed and dry?
Probably to make the world respectfully worship the spiritual star.
Another year later, the emperor worshiped the five pillars of Yongcheng in the suburbs to open up the road back to the middle, so he left Xiaoguan to the north, passed through Dulu and Mingze, returned from Xihe, and went to Hedong to worship Houtu.
In the winter of the second year, the emperor inspected Nanjun, arrived at Jiangling, and then headed eastward.
Ceremonies were held on the underground Tianzhu Mountain, which is known as Nanyue.
Take a boat down the river, leave Xunyang and Songyang, pass by Pengli, and pay homage to the famous mountains and rivers there.
Go north to Langye and go up the coastal road.
In April, a ceremony to worship heaven was held in Fenggao.
At first, when the emperor was worshiping heaven in Mount Tai, there was an ancient Mingtang at the northeast foot of Mount Tai. The terrain was dangerous and not spacious.
The emperor planned to build a bright hall next to Fenggao, but he didn't know the system for building a bright hall.
The Jinan renmin jade belt presents the Mingtang pattern from the time of the Yellow Emperor.
There is a hall in the Mingtang with no walls around. It is built with thatched grass. The hall is connected to the water flow. The water flow surrounds the palace wall. It has an upper and lower passage with a building above it. It enters from the southwest and is called Kunlun. The emperor enters from here to worship God.
So the emperor ordered a Mingtang to be built on the Fenggaowen River, which was exactly the same as the picture presented by Gong Yudai.
The emperor entered from Kunlun Road and began to worship in the Mingtang with the same etiquette as suburban sacrifices. After the ceremony, firewood was burned in the hall for sacrifice.
summary: The evolution of religious and sacrificial practices during the Han Dynasty, focusing on the reigns of Emperors Wu, Zhao, Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, Ai, and Ping, as well as the usurper Wang Mang. The belief in ghosts and gods in Guangdong, where King Shuou’s reverence for them allegedly extended his life to 160 years, while neglect shortened his descendants’ lives. This led to the construction of temples and divination using chicken bones. Emperor Wu, influenced by alchemists like Gongsun Qing, built pavilions and towers in Chang’an and Ganquan Palace to invite immortals, including the Feilian, Gui, Yishou, and Longshou Pavilions, and the Tongtian Tower. He conducted sacrifices, such as those to Taiyi and Houtu, and expanded palace rooms. Emperor Wu performed numerous rituals, including suburban sacrifices at Yongcheng, worship at Mount Tai, and construction of a Mingtang based on a Yellow Emperor-era design. He also built Jianzhang Palace, Taiye Pool with artificial islands, and the Shenming Terrace, all to attract gods. The calendar was revised, and the year was renamed Taichu. Alchemists continued to advise, leading to the construction of five cities and twelve towers. Emperor Wu made five pilgrimages to Mount Tai for sealing ceremonies, and sacrifices were made to various mountains and rivers.

translation:
Emperor Xuan was the emperor, and because he was succeeded by Emperor Wu's orthodoxy, three years after he ascended the throne, he honored Xiaowu Temple as Shizong, and built Shizong temples in all the counties he visited.
On the day of the memorial ceremony at Sejong Temple, white cranes gathered in the back courtyard.
When the ancestral temple was built and the tomb of Xiaozhao was dedicated, there were five-colored geese gathering in front of the temple.
When Sejong Temple was being built in Xihe, a divine light appeared beside the temple, and there was a bird like a white crane, with red in front and cyan behind.
The divine light appeared in the room again, like a candlelight.
There are bells ringing in the Sejong Temple in Guangcheon Kingdom, the door is wide open, there is light at night, and the whole temple is bright and bright.
The emperor went down to Shao to grant amnesty to the whole world.
At that time, the general Huo Guang was assisting the government, and the emperor was sitting respectfully on the throne. He could not go out to worship except in the ancestral temple.
In the twelfth year, he issued an edict saying: I have heard that the emperor serves heaven and earth devoutly and sacrifices to mountains and rivers, which is a common ritual in ancient and modern times.
In the past, I had not personally offered sacrifices to the temple of God for more than ten years, and I was very scared.
I decided to take the lead in fasting and offering sacrifices in person to pray for good fortune for the people so that they can have a good harvest.
In the first month of the second year, the emperor went to Ganquan Palace to worship Longqi in the suburbs. Good omens appeared several times.
Following the precedent of the timely period, chariots and uniforms flourished, people respectfully performed the etiquette of fasting and shrines, and wrote many poems.
In March of this year, I went to Jiese in person to offer sacrifices to Houtu. There were a gathering of gods and nobles, so I changed the Yuan Dynasty to Sujue.
An edict was issued to Taichang saying: Kensi and Dahai are the largest of all rivers, and no one is going to worship them now.
The ancestral officials are now ordered to make sacrifices an annual event, offering sacrifices to the Yangtze River, the sea, and the Luoshui River in the four seasons to pray for good harvests for the world.
From then on, the Five Mountains and the Four Mountains were often worshiped.
Mount Shuyue and Taishi were worshiped in Bodi, Zhongyue Taishi was worshiped in Songshan, Nanyue Zhishan was worshiped in Qiandi, Xiyue Huashan was worshiped in Huayin, Beiyue Changshan was worshiped in Shangquyang, the Yellow River was worshiped in Linjin, the Yangtze River was worshiped in Jiangdu, the Huai River was worshiped in Pingshi, and the Jishui was worshiped in Linyi. The envoys held talismans to preside over the sacrifices.
Only Mount Tai and the Yellow River have five temples a year, and the rivers have four temples. The rest pray once and offer sacrifices three times.
At that time, Nanjun captured a white tiger and presented its skin, teeth and claws to the court, and the emperor used them to build a temple.
According to the advice of the alchemists, four ancestral halls were built in Weiyang Palace for Suihou, Jianbao, Yubaobi and Zhoukangbaoding.
They also offered sacrifices to Taishi Mountain in Jimo, to Sanhu Mountain in Xiami, and to Tianfengyuan Huojing in Hongmen.
The Jupiter, Chenxing, Venus, Mars and Nandou Temples were also built next to Chang'an City.
They also worshiped Shenshan and the Eight Gods in Qucheng, worshiped the Shishe Shigu in Pengshan in Linqu, worshiped Zhifu Mountain in Zhuang, worshiped Chengshan in Wuye, and worshiped Laishan in Huang.
They worship the sun in Chengshan and the moon in Laishan.
They also offered sacrifices to the Four Seasons in Langye, and to Chiyou in Shouliang.
In Hubei, a nearby county of the capital, there are Laogu, Wudoshan, Sun and Moon, Five Emperors, Biren, and Jade Girl Temples. There is a Jinglu Shrine in Yunyang, which is used to worship King Xiutu.
In Fushi, four temples were built, including the Ziren Temple in Wulong Mountain and the Huangdi Temple, Tianshen Temple, and Diyuanshui Temple.
Some people said that there were gods of golden horses and jade roosters in Yizhou, which could be summoned by sacrifices, so they sent Wang, the admonishing doctor, to pray to the gods while holding amulets wrapped around them.
summary: During Emperor Zhao’s reign, he was too young to participate in sacrifices. Emperor Xuan honored Emperor Wu as Shizong, building temples where divine signs like white cranes and five-colored geese appeared. Emperor Xuan personally performed suburban sacrifices at Ganquan and Jiese, changing the era name to Sujue. He ordered annual sacrifices to the Yangtze River, sea, and Luoshui, and regular worship of the Five Mountains and Four Rivers. Alchemists advised building temples for various gods, including Suihou and Zhoukangbaoding. Doctor Liu Gengsheng was punished for failed alchemy. Jingzhao Yin Zhang Chang advised against alchemists, and many were dismissed.
