A tripod found in Meiyang was debated; Zhang Chang argued it was a Zhou dynasty artifact, not suitable for the ancestral temple. Phoenixes and other auspicious signs led to the construction of Bushou Palace and Phoenix Hall. Emperor Xuan died after a reign marked by frequent sacrifices and omens.

translation:
After a year, the name was changed to nectar.
In the first month of the first month, the emperor went to Ganquan to worship Taizhi in the suburbs.
This summer, a yellow dragon appeared in Xinfeng.
Hair grew on the wooden frames and bronze figures of the bells hanging in Jianzhang, Weiyang and Changle palaces, more than an inch long, which was considered auspicious at the time.
Later, it was the first month of the year. When the emperor went to the suburbs to pay homage to Thailand, he met Shan Yu at Ganquan Palace.
Later, a year later, the name was changed to Huanglong.
In the first month of the first month, he returned to Ganquan Palace to worship Taizhi in the suburbs, and then received Shanyu's audience in Ganquan Palace.
In the winter the emperor died.
凤凰降到郡国的共有五十多处。
Emperor Yuan ascended the throne and followed the old etiquette. In the first month of every other year, he went to the outskirts of Ganquan Palace to worship Taizhi, then to the east of Hedong to worship Houtu, and to the west to Yongcheng to worship Wuzhi.
A total of five sacrifices were offered to Taishi and Houtu.
They also gave favors. Sometimes they did not have to pay land rent in the places they passed, and they gave cattle and wine to a hundred households, and some gave them titles of nobility. Forgive sinners.
Emperor Yuan liked Confucianism, and Gong Yu, Wei Xuancheng, Kuang Heng and others became ministers one after another.
Gong Yu suggested that most of the sacrifices held in the Mojia ancestral temple were inconsistent with ancient rituals, and the emperor agreed with his opinion.
Later, when Wei Xuan became prime minister, he suggested that the temples of prefectures and states should be abolished, and the sacrifices in the temples of various gardens and dormitories from Emperor Taishang to Emperor Xiaohui should be abolished.
Later, Emperor Yuan fell ill and dreamed that the gods came to condemn him for abolishing various temples, so Emperor Yuan resumed offering sacrifices.
Later, it was abolished and restored, and by the time of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, there was no definite number.
This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Wei Xuancheng".
As soon as Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, Prime Minister Kuang Heng and Imperial Censor Zhang Tan reported: "There is no more important matter for an emperor than inheriting the throne from heaven, and nothing is more important than inheriting the throne from heaven than offering sacrifices in the suburbs. Therefore, the holy kings all tried their best to establish the ritual system of offering sacrifices in the suburbs."
Worshiping the sky in the southern suburbs has the meaning of tending to Yang; worshiping the earth in the northern suburbs symbolizes tending to Yin.
To the emperor, heaven means enjoying their respective sacrifices in the place where the emperor has established the capital.
In the past, Emperor Xiaowu lived in Ganquan Palace. When Taiyuan was established in Yunyang, he worshiped in the south of the palace.
Nowadays, when traveling to Chang'an, people often go to Chang'an to offer sacrifices to the emperor. Instead, they go north to the lunar point, and when they offer sacrifices to the earth, they go east to the more yang place. Things are different from the ancient system.
Then we went to Yunyang and walked in the valley. The road was narrow and steep for nearly a hundred miles. When we got to Fenyin, we had to cross a large river. There were dangers of storms and boating. It was not suitable for a wise monarch to do it repeatedly. The counties and counties repaired roads and supplied various utensils. The officials and the people were in hardship, and the officials spent a lot of money.
summary: Emperor Yuan followed old rituals, performing suburban sacrifices every other year, but favored Confucianism. Ministers like Gong Yu and Wei Xuancheng proposed abolishing many temples, but Emperor Yuan reversed this after dreaming of divine condemnation. Emperor Cheng’s reign saw a major reform: Prime Minister Kuang Heng and Imperial Censor Zhang Tan argued that sacrifices should be moved to Chang’an’s northern and southern suburbs, citing ancient practices and the hardships of traveling to Ganquan and Fenyin. After debate, the move was approved, and many temples were abolished. However, after Emperor Cheng had no heirs, the Empress Dowager ordered the restoration of the old temples at Ganquan, Fenyin, and Yongcheng, blaming the move for the lack of descendants. Emperor Cheng later became obsessed with alchemists, but Gu Yong warned against them, citing historical failures. Du Ye also criticized the distant sacrifices. After Emperor Cheng’s death, the Empress Dowager restored the northern and southern suburbs.

translation:
The emperor did not disrespect and value the sacrifices himself, and personally presided over the sacrifices. The etiquette was the same as that of sacrifices in the ancestral temple.
"Poetry" says that a big society was built.
He also said that he would serve Ji God and pray for sweet rain.
"Book of Rites" says that only offering sacrifices to the ancestors and temples is called Yuesui.
The Holy Han Dynasty was established, etiquette was gradually established, there were official societies, but there was no official country yet.
So Guan Ji was established after the official society, and Xia Yu was used to feed the official society, and Hou Ji was used to share the official grain.
Plant cereal trees in the fields.
The Mu Shou of Xuzhou paid a tribute of one dou each of the five colors of soil every year.
In the second year after Wang Mang usurped the throne, the affairs of immortals arose. According to the advice of the alchemist Su Le, the Eight Winds Tower was built in the palace.
It cost ten thousand gold to build the platform. Music was played on it and a liquid soup was built in the direction of the wind.
He also planted five grains of grain in the palace, placing each one in its proper position according to its own color. First, he boiled more than twenty kinds of materials such as crane marrow, tortoise shell, and rhinoceros jade to soak the seeds. One handful of millet was calculated into one gold. This was said to be the method of the Yellow Emperor's Valley Immortal.
He appointed Su Le as Huang Menlang and ordered him to take charge of this matter.
Wang Mang then worshiped ghosts and gods and performed too many sacrifices. By the end of Wang Mang's life, there were a total of 1,700 temples, ranging from the six sects of heaven and earth to the minor ghosts and gods, and more than 3,000 kinds of animals and birds were used.
Later, when they couldn't prepare everything, they used harps as geese and dogs as elk.
Several times, Shao thought that he should become a god, and his words were recorded in his biography.
Zan said: In the early days of the establishment of the Han Dynasty, everything was in the preliminary stage, and only Shu Sunsheng briefly formulated the etiquette of the court.
As for things like Zhengshuo, Fuse, Jiaowang, etc., it has not been clarified after several generations.
By the time of Emperor Xiaowen, people began to hold sacrifices in the summer suburbs. However, Zhang Cang based his practice on Shui De, while Gongsun Chen and Jia Yi thought it should be changed to Tu De, but they could not figure it out in the end.
In the era of Emperor Xiaowu, rituals, music, and laws flourished. At the beginning of the Taichu period, the ritual system was reformed, but Ni Kuan, Sima Qian, and others still followed what Gongsun Chen and Mai Yi said, and the service system followed Huang De.
Based on the principle that the five virtues are transmitted and followed and cannot be defeated, they believe that the Qin Dynasty relied on the virtue of water, so they said that the Han Dynasty defeated it based on the virtue of earth.
Liu Xiang and his son believed that the emperor came from "Zhen", so Bao Xi began to accept Mu De, which was passed from mother to son, and over and over again. From Shennong and Huangdi through the Tang, Yu and Han dynasties, they got Huo De.
Therefore, when Emperor Gaozu began to rise, the Mother Goddess cried at night to show the auspicious symbol of the Red Emperor, and the color of the flag was red, which naturally led to heavenly rule.
In the past, the Gonggong family used water virtue to separate wood and fire. They had the same fate as the Qin Dynasty, which was not their order, so they could not last long.
summary: Emperor Ai, ill, revived many temples, but after his death, the Empress Dowager again restored the Ganquan and Fenyin temples. Under Emperor Ping, Wang Mang reported extensively on sacrificial history, arguing for a return to the northern and southern suburbs and proposing a system where heaven and earth were worshiped together with ancestors. He established altars for the Five Emperors and various gods in Chang’an’s suburbs, and later added an official shrine for the god of grain. After usurping the throne, Wang Mang built the Eight Winds Tower and engaged in alchemy, with over 1,700 temples by his death. The text concludes with a commentary on the Han Dynasty’s ritual evolution, noting debates over the five virtues and the influence of alchemists, with Gu Yong’s criticisms deemed correct.

translation:
Among the eight types of government officials in "Hong Fan", one is the official in charge of people's food, and the second is the official in charge of property.
Food refers to the good grain produced by farmers that can be eaten, and goods refers to cloth and silk that can be worn, as well as golden knives and turtle shells, which are used to distribute property and spread benefits so as to distribute the haves and have-nots.
Combining the two is the foundation of people's life, and it has begun to rise since the era of Shennong. Cut wood to make grass, bend wood to make grass, and spread the benefits of grass to the world, so that there will be enough food; at noon, a market will be formed to attract people from all over the world, gather all the goods from the world, and then go away after exchange, so that everyone can get what they want, so that the wealth will circulate.
Food is sufficient, goods are circulated, and then the country enriches and enriches the people. In this way, political and religious culture is formed.
Huang Di and his subordinates made adjustments for the people so that they would not feel tired.
Emperor Yao ordered Xizhong, Xishu, Hezhong, and Heshu to inform the people of the weather and seasons. When the people began to starve, Emperor Shun appointed Houji and made Zao the first place in politics.
Dayu quelled the floods, stabilized the nine provinces, regulated the fields, and handed over the land tax to the oval bamboo vessels that held tribute according to the distance where they were born. He encouraged the world to exchange what they had and what they had, and all the nations were governed.
The prosperity of the Shang and Zhou Dynasties was recorded in the "Poems" and "Books", which mainly depended on stabilizing the people, making them rich and then educating them.
Therefore, the Book of Changes states that the great virtue of heaven and earth is life, and the most precious thing for a saint is the throne; how to hold the throne is called benevolence, and how to accumulate people is called wealth.
Property is the basis for emperors to gather people to protect their throne, support the masses, obey God's kindness, and govern the country and stabilize the people.
Therefore, it is said: Don’t worry about lack but worry about inequality; don’t worry about poverty but worry about instability; because when there is balance, there will be no poverty; when there is harmony, there will be no abundance; when there is stability, there will be no overthrow.
Therefore, the wise king defined the people and built cities for them to live in, built houses in the wells and fields to make them equal, opened markets for them to circulate goods, and set up schools to educate them; the four kinds of people, scholars, farmers, workers, and merchants, had their own businesses.
After learning, becoming an official is called a scholar, opening up land to produce grain is called a farmer, using technology to make utensils is called a worker, and circulating property and buying and selling goods is called a merchant.
A wise king bestows official positions according to his talents, and the four kinds of people bear responsibility according to their own strength. Therefore, there are no idle officials in the court, no idlers in the city, and no desolate fields on the ground.
The method of governing people is to make them settle in one place.
Therefore, steps must be established to set the acres and correct the boundaries of the land.
Six feet is one step, one hundred steps is one acre, one hundred acres is one man, three houses is one house, three houses is one well, and the radius of the well is one mile, which is nine men.
summary: Among the eight types of government officials in "Hong Fan," one oversees food and another property. Food refers to grain from farmers, while property includes cloth, silk, golden knives, and turtle shells, used to distribute wealth. These are the foundation of life, originating from Shennong's era, who taught farming and trade. Sufficient food and circulated property enrich the nation, forming political and religious culture. Huang Di adjusted for the people, Yao informed them of seasons, Shun appointed Houji to address starvation, and Dayu controlled floods, regulated fields, and encouraged trade. The Shang and Zhou dynasties prospered by stabilizing and enriching the people before educating them. The Book of Changes states that life is heaven and earth's great virtue, and a saint's most precious possession is the throne, held through benevolence and wealth accumulation.

translation:
Eight families owned it jointly, each receiving a hundred acres of private land and ten acres of public land, which was eight hundred and eighty acres, leaving twenty acres for houses.
We are friends with each other when we come in and out, we help each other as guards and lookouts, and we help each other when we are sick. Therefore, the people are harmonious, and the political and religious customs are unified, and labor production can be obtained and evenly distributed.
The people accepted the land, good land was 100 acres, medium land was 200 acres, and poor land was 300 acres.
Those who farm every year do not exchange good fields; those who fallow one year exchange medium fields once; those who fallow two years exchange bad fields twice, and those who cultivate three years exchange the fields and change their positions.
The head of a peasant household receives the land for himself, and the other men in his family are the remaining husbands, and the land is divided among them in proportion.
Scholars, workers, and merchants divided the fields, and five talents were equivalent to one farmer.
This means that it can be used as a law on the plains.
If it is a mountainous area, a woodland, a large lake, a hilly land, or a land immersed in salt-alkali soil, it will be graded according to the degree of fertility and barrenness.
There are taxes and gifts.
The tax is one-tenth of the public land and the income of industry, commerce, scale, and Yu.
Fu is the labor that provides soldiers with chariots, horses, armor, and weapons, and is used to enrich the government's warehouses for storing property, armor, and rewards.
The tax was used to support the sacrifices to the ancestral gods in the suburbs, the emperor to support the officials, salaries, food, and other expenses.
When the people reach the age of twenty, their fields will be divided, and when they reach sixty, the acres will be returned.
Those over seventy years old are those whom the emperor has come to support; those under ten years old are those whom the emperor wants to raise; those over eleven years old are those whom the emperor wants to make strong.
Grains must be mixed with other grains to prevent disasters.
There should be no trees in the fields so as not to hinder the grain.
If you work hard, you will reap the harvest as if thieves are coming.
If mulberry trees are planted around the cottage, there are ridges in the vegetable field, melons and fruits are planted on the edges of the fields, chickens, pigs, dogs, and pigs are raised without delay, and women weave silkworms, then they can wear silk cloth at the age of fifty and eat meat at the age of seventy.
A house in a field is called a hut, and a house in a place where people live together is called a li.
Five families form one neighbour, five neighbors form one li, four li form one clan, five clans form one party, five parties form one state, and five states form one township.
There are 12,500 households in one township.
The official rank of the chief of a neighborhood is corporal. From there, the official rank is one level higher, and the official rank at the township level is Qing.
In this way, there is order in the house and there is harmony in the countryside.
The preface is used to clarify the teachings, and the xiang is used to practice etiquette to demonstrate the teachings.
In the spring, the people were ordered to go to the fields, and in the winter to the towns.
"Poetry" says this: In April, he moved his legs, took the women and children with him, and gave food to the people in the fields to the south.
summary: Property is the basis for emperors to gather people, support the masses, and govern. Wise kings defined the people, built cities, houses, markets, and schools, dividing them into scholars, farmers, workers, and merchants. Officials were appointed by talent, and each group bore responsibility, ensuring no idleness. Land was measured in steps, acres, and wells, with eight families jointly owning a well, each receiving private and public land. People helped each other, fostering harmony. Land quality varied: good land yielded 100 acres, medium 200, poor 300. Farmers exchanged fields based on fallow periods. Taxes were one-tenth of public land and industry income, while labor provided military supplies. At age 20, fields were divided; at 60, returned. Grains were mixed to prevent disasters, and mulberry trees, vegetables, and livestock were cultivated. Houses in fields were huts; in communities, li. Neighborhoods, li, clans, parties, states, and townships were organized, with officials from corporal to qing. Education began at age eight, with university at 15. Outstanding students advanced, and princes recommended scholars to the emperor. Folk songs were collected to inform the ruler.

translation:
After the decline of the Zhou Dynasty, the tyrants and corrupt officials ignored their national boundaries, corvee labor was rampant, government orders were not trustworthy, people above and below deceived each other, and no one cultivated the public fields.
Therefore, Lu Xuangong's "first tax mu" was ridiculed by "Spring and Autumn".
As a result, those in power are greedy, and the people are resentful. When disaster occurs, chaos will arise.
The Zhou Dynasty declined into the Warring States Period, where they respected hypocrisy and violence but despised benevolence and righteousness. They put material sufficiency first and politeness and humility second.
At this time, Li Kui formulated an edict for Wei Wenhou to fully utilize the land's productive capacity. He believed that the land was a hundred miles in circumference, with a total of 90,000 hectares. Excluding one-third of the mountainous Dahu villages, there were still 6 million acres of fields. If you cultivate the fields carefully, you will receive an additional three dou per acre. If you are not diligent, you will also be deducted three dou.
If the amount of grain in a land with a radius of a hundred miles increases or decreases, it will amount to 1.8 million stones of millet.
Moreover, if the grain purchased is too expensive, it will hurt the scholars, workers, and merchants, and if it is too cheap, it will hurt the peasants. If the peasants, workers, and merchants are hurt, there will be dispersion, and if the peasants are hurt, there will be national poverty. Therefore, if it is too expensive or too cheap, one party will definitely be harmed.
Those who are good at governing the country will protect the soldiers, workers, and merchants from harm and make the farmers more diligent.
Now a householder with five people cultivates 100 acres of land. The annual harvest is one and a half dan per acre, and the millet cost is 150 dan. After deducting the one-tenth tax of 15 dan, there is still 135 dan left.
For food, one person needs one and a half dan per month, and five people need 90 shi per year, leaving 45 shi left.
After selling thirty stones, we got one thousand three hundred and fifty coins. After excluding the new harvest grains in the community and the spring and autumn sacrifices, which cost three hundred coins, we still had one thousand and fifty coins left.
Clothes cost roughly 300 yuan per person, and 1,500 yuan for five people for the whole year, a difference of 450 yuan.
Unfortunately, the expenses for illness, death, funeral, and taxes are not included in this package.
This is the reason why farmers are often poor and have no intention of farming diligently, which makes the purchase of grain too expensive.
Therefore, those who are good at buying and storing grain at a reasonable price must carefully observe that there are three levels of maturity each year: upper, middle and lower. The upper ripe harvest can be four times the original amount, and there are still 400 stone left at the end; the medium ripe harvest is three times the original amount, and there are still 300 stone left at the end; the low maturity harvest is double the original amount, and there are still one hundred stone left at the end.
A small famine can collect one hundred stones, a medium famine can collect seventy stones, and a large famine can collect twenty stones. Therefore, in good harvest years, we use the policy of high-ripe years to buy three times the amount of grain in normal years and leave a portion for the people; in mid-ripe years, we buy twice as much grain; in low-ripe years, we buy twice as much grain, so that the people can be satisfied, and the phenomenon of food price average and famine is stopped.
During a minor famine, the taxes collected during the minor harvest period will be distributed. During a moderate famine, the taxes collected during the middle harvest season will be distributed. During a major famine, the taxes collected during the major harvest period will be distributed to sell them.
Therefore, even if there are famines, floods and droughts, the inexpensive purchases will not cause the scholars, workers, and merchants to be separated, and the surplus will be used to make up for the shortage.
summary: After the Zhou Dynasty declined, tyrants ignored boundaries, corvée was rampant, and public fields were neglected. Lu Xuangong's "first tax mu" was criticized. The Warring States period valued hypocrisy and violence over benevolence. Li Kui advised Wei Wenhou on land productivity, calculating that careful cultivation yielded extra grain. He noted that high grain prices hurt scholars, workers, and merchants, while low prices hurt farmers. A household of five with 100 acres produced 150 dan of millet, but after taxes, food, and expenses, they faced deficits, leading to poverty. Li Kui proposed buying grain at moderate prices during good harvests and selling during famines to stabilize prices, implemented in Wei, making it rich and strong. Qin Xiaogong appointed Shang Yang, who destroyed well fields and emphasized farming and warfare, dominating neighboring states. However, hierarchy was lost, the rich accumulated wealth, and the poor suffered. Qin Shihuang annexed the world, imposed heavy taxes, and conscripted labor, causing rebellion.

translation:
Implement it in Wei State, and the country will become rich and strong.
When Qin Xiaogong appointed Shang Yang, he destroyed the well fields, opened up the roads to the fields, and used the rewards of farming and fighting as urgent matters. Even if it was not the ancient method, it was still because of the dedication to the fundamentals, so as to overwhelm the neighboring countries and dominate the princes.
But the dynastic system ceased to exist, and there was no restraint beyond hierarchy.
The rich among the people accumulated a lot of wealth, while the poor lived on the chaff; the powerful country swallowed up prefectures and counties, and the weak lost the country.
When Qin Shihuang arrived, he annexed the world, built a lot of construction projects internally, excluded the barbarians externally, collected more than half of the taxes, and levied civilians on the left side of the Juli Gate to defend the border.
Men's hard work in farming is not enough to support themselves, and women's spinning is not enough to provide clothing.
Exhausting all the money and property in the world to pursue his policies is not enough to satisfy his desires.
People in the country were filled with grief and anger, so they began to flee the rebellion.
After the establishment of the Han Dynasty, it inherited the shortcomings of the Qin Dynasty. The princes revolted together, the people lost their jobs, and there was a period of great famine.
A stone of ordinary rice costs 5,000 yuan. If people eat people, more than half of them will die.
Emperor Gaozu ordered the people to sell their children and live in Shu and Han.
After the world was settled, the people had nothing to store. From the emperor who could not own four horses of pure color, to the generals who could only ride bullock carts.
The emperor then issued decrees to restrict frugality, reduce land rents, collect one-fifteenth of the tax, and collect taxes from the people based on official salaries and government expenditures.
However, the income from taxes on the mountains, rivers and gardens, from the emperor to the private fiefs of the recipients of the fiefdoms, was provided by each of them, and no ordinary fees were paid to the emperor.
The cost of transporting millet from Guandong via waterways to the capital and delivering it to various government offices does not exceed hundreds of thousands of dan per year.
In the era of Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao, clothing and food gradually increased.
After Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he personally practiced frugality and worked hard for the stability of the people.
At that time, the people were not far from the Warring States period. They had abandoned their roots and were moving towards the end. Jia Yi advised the emperor:
Guan Zhong said: Only when the warehouse is sufficient can you know the etiquette.
From ancient times to the present, it has never been heard of that the people could manage without adequate supplies.
Ancient people said: If a man does not cultivate, some will suffer from hunger; if a woman does not weave, some will suffer from cold.
If there are seasons for producing materials, but there is no restraint in using them, then the materials will definitely be exhausted.
In ancient times, the world was governed in a very detailed and comprehensive manner, so their savings were enough to rest assured.
Nowadays, we are abandoning the roots and tending to the ends. There are many people who live on leisure, which is the greatest harm in the world. Excessive and extravagant customs are increasing day by day. This is the greatest harm in the world.
Cruel and violent acts are carried out openly, and no one comes to stop them; the fate of the country is about to be overturned, and no one comes to save it.
summary: After the Han Dynasty, the Qin's shortcomings continued. Princes revolted, people lost jobs, and famine struck, with grain costing 5,000 yuan per stone and cannibalism. Emperor Gaozu ordered people to sell children and move to Shu and Han. After peace, the emperor restricted frugality, reduced land rents to one-fifteenth, and taxed based on official salaries. Emperor Wen practiced frugality and encouraged agriculture. Jia Yi advised that production must exceed consumption, warning of poverty and unrest. He urged returning people to agriculture to build savings. Emperor Wen was moved and began farming himself. Chao Cuo further advised that wise kings ensure people have savings, citing Yao, Yu, and Tang's success. He noted that poverty leads to evil, and farmers work hard but suffer from taxes and merchants' exploitation. He proposed valuing grain over gold and jade, and using grain for rewards and punishments. Emperor Wen allowed people to send grain to the border for titles, reducing taxes. Over 70 years, the country prospered, with full granaries and surplus property. However, wealth led to pride and land annexation. Dong Zhongshu advised planting more wheat and reforming taxes and labor, but after his death, prices rose and cannibalism returned.

translation:
He also asked for instructions to increase the sea rent three times, and the emperor followed his advice.
Xiao Wang, the imperial censor, said: "It turns out that the Xu Gong family of the imperial censor's subordinates lives in Shulai. He said that the sea rent was increased in previous years and the fish would not come out."
The elders all said that during the reign of Emperor Wu, the county magistrate personally fished, but no fish came out of the sea. Later, they returned it to the people, and the fish came out.
Yin and Yang interact with each other, and things of the same kind correspond to each other. This is the case for all things.
Now Geng Shouchang plans to purchase grain from the nearby water transport pass, build warehouses and ships, which will cost more than 200 million yuan. It involves the working people, fearing that a drought will occur and the people will suffer from it.
Geng Shouchang was accustomed to calculating things of one cent and one baht. His far-reaching calculations and thinking were really not up to the task. It would be better to remain as before.
The emperor did not listen.
Water transportation was indeed convenient, so Geng Shouchang asked for instructions and ordered the border counties to build warehouses. When the price of grain was low, the price was increased to buy in order to benefit farmers. When the price of grain was high, the price was sold at a reduced price, which was called Changping warehouse.
People feel convenient.
The emperor issued an edict and granted Geng Shouchang the title of Marquis of Guannei.
Because Cai Gui liked agriculture, he served as an envoy to encourage the country and became a high official.
Emperor Yuan ascended the throne and the world was flooded, especially in the eleven counties of Guandong.
In the second year of Emperor Yuan's reign, there was a famine in Qi. A grain of rice cost more than 300 yuan per stone. Many people starved to death. People in Langxie County were cannibals.
Most of the Confucian scholars in official positions said that Yantie Palace, Beijia Tianguan and Changpingcang could be dismissed, and they should not compete for interests with the people.
The emperor listened to their opinions and dismissed Yantieguan, Beijiatianguan and Changpingcang.
He also dismissed the palace guards of Jianzhang and Ganquan, Jiaodui, Qi San served as officials, reduced the number of forbidden gardens to provide for the poor, and reduced the number of guards in the princes' temples by half.
He also reduced the number of soldiers in Guanzhong by 500 and transferred grain to help the poor.
After that, due to insufficient funds, only Yantieguan was restored.
When he became emperor, there was no war in the world and it could be said to be peaceful. However, the people's customs were extravagant and they did not consider saving and hoarding.
In the second year of Yongshi, Liang State and Pingyuan County suffered from floods for consecutive years, and cannibalism occurred. The governor and county governor were dismissed from office for crimes.
Emperor Ai ascended the throne, and Shi Dan assisted in political affairs. He suggested: In ancient times, wise kings always established well fields and then managed them to achieve peace.
Emperor Xiaowen inherited the emptiness of the world after the collapse of the Zhou Dynasty and the violent wars of the Qin Dynasty, so he devoted himself to encouraging the people to engage in farming and mulberry farming, and set an example for the world with frugality.
The people had just begun to enrich themselves, and there was no danger of annexation, so there were no restrictions on people's land and slaves.
Nowadays, generations of peace have passed down, and the wealthy and officials have a lot of property, but the poor and weak are even poorer.
summary: Emperor Wu regretted his conquests and appointed Cheng Fu to promote agriculture. Zhao Guo introduced the Daitian method, with three furrows per acre, changing positions yearly. This method, using convenient tools, increased yields. Zhao Guo taught it widely, and it proved efficient. By Emperor Zhao's time, exiles returned, fields expanded, and savings grew. Emperor Xuan appointed virtuous officials, and grain prices fell to five yuan per stone. Geng Shouchang proposed purchasing grain from nearby counties to save on transport costs, building Changping warehouses to stabilize prices. Emperor Yuan faced floods and famine, with cannibalism in Langxie. Confucian officials advised dismissing salt, iron, and Changping offices, which the emperor did, but later restored salt and iron due to insufficient funds. Emperor Cheng's reign was peaceful but extravagant, with floods causing cannibalism. Emperor Ai considered land and slave restrictions, but they were not implemented. Wang Mang usurped the throne, despised Han systems, and provoked the Xiongnu, leading to war. He renamed land and slaves, prohibited sales, and imposed harsh punishments, causing chaos. Droughts and famines led to cannibalism, with grain prices soaring. Wang Mang opened granaries but officials stole supplies, and many died. He lamented his rule until his death.

translation:
As for the uses of property, money, cloth and silk, their details are not recorded before the Xia and Yin Dynasties.
Jiang Taigong established the method of currency circulation in the nine prefectures for the Zhou Dynasty: gold is one inch square and weighs one catty; coins are round and have square holes, and baht is used as the weight; cloth is two feet and two inches wide and is one piece, and four feet long is one piece.
Therefore, currency is more precious than gold, sharper than a knife, smoother than spring water, more dispersed than cloth, and more able to gather than silk.
After Jiang Taigong retreated to the feudal country, he implemented it in Qi.
When Guan Zhong assisted Duke Huan of Qi, he established the standard of measuring weight. He said: There are years of famine and years of harvest, so grains are expensive and cheap; orders are slow and urgent, so goods are light and heavy.
If the emperor does not govern, then the hoarding merchants will roam the market, and when the people cannot support themselves, they will raise the price to a hundred times the cost.
Therefore, a country with ten thousand cars must have merchants worth ten thousand gold to buy them, and a country with a thousand cars must have merchants worth ten thousand gold. This is because the profits are hidden.
If we consume what we produce, we will be able to meet our own expenses. However, if there are hungry people among the people, that is why the grain is hidden.
When the people have plenty, they despise grain, so the monarch levies a low price; when the people have a shortage, they value grain, so the monarch distributes it at a high price.
All low prices, high prices, collections, and distributions are all done at a certain time. Then supply and demand are adjusted, and prices will be stable.
Adhere to the measures of regulating supply and demand and stabilizing prices, so that a town with a population of ten thousand households must have a collection of ten thousand bells, and a string of money tied with millions of strings; a town with a population of only ten thousand households must have a collection of thousands of bells, and a string of money tied with millions of strings.
Farming is carried out in the spring, weeding is carried out in the summer, and the equipment and seeds must be abundant.
Therefore, big merchants and hoarding merchants cannot use their power to rob the people.
Duke Huan of Qi used the small state of Qi to unite the princes and promote his reputation as an overlord.
More than a hundred years later, when King Jing of Zhou Dynasty came to the throne, he was worried that the money was too light and planned to cast large coins instead. Duke Shan Mu said: "This won't work."
In ancient times, when disasters came from heaven, it was necessary to weigh property and currency to save the people.
The people think that money is light, so we create heavy money for them to use. In this way, big money and small money go hand in hand with heavy money being the main one, and the people can get convenience.
If heavy money cannot be used, make more light money for use, and do not abolish heavy money. Therefore, if the heavy money is insufficient, use light money to make up for it. Money and small money are mostly beneficial.
Now that the king has abolished light money and created heavy money, the people have lost their wealth. How can they not be in want?
If the people are in shortage, the king will have difficulty in spending money; if there is difficulty, he must collect more from the people; if the people cannot provide, they will flee. This is a way to separate the people.
Moreover, exhausting the people's wealth to enrich the palace is like blocking the water source to stop the flow of water. It will not take a few days for the water to dry up. Please make your decision, Your Majesty.
King Jing did not listen to his words, and finally made a large coin with "actual goods" engraved on it. The round edges and holes of the money had outlines, which were used to encourage farmers to make up for the shortage, and the people benefited.
summary: The uses of property, money, cloth, and silk were not recorded before the Xia and Yin dynasties. Jiang Taigong established currency circulation for the Zhou Dynasty: gold was one inch square and weighed one catty; coins were round with square holes, using baht as weight; cloth was two feet two inches wide and four feet long per piece. Currency was considered more precious than gold, sharper than a knife, smoother than spring water, more dispersed than cloth, and more able to gather than silk. After Jiang Taigong retreated to Qi, he implemented this system. Guan Zhong assisted Duke Huan of Qi by establishing standards for measuring weight, noting that grain prices fluctuated with harvests and that goods varied in value based on demand. He warned that without governance, hoarding merchants would exploit the people, raising prices a hundredfold. A country with ten thousand cars needed merchants worth ten thousand gold to buy them, as profits were hidden. By consuming what was produced, expenses could be met, but hunger arose when grain was hoarded. The monarch should levy low prices when grain was abundant and distribute at high prices when scarce, adjusting supply and demand to stabilize prices. A town of ten thousand households should have a collection of ten thousand bells and millions of strings of money. Farming required abundant equipment and seeds in spring and summer, preventing big merchants from robbing the people. Duke Huan used Qi to unite the princes and become an overlord.

translation:
When the Qin State annexed the world, its currency was divided into two classes: gold was measured in yi, which was the first-class currency; copper coins were shaped like the money of the Zhou Dynasty, with the inscription "ban liang" on the front and a weight of half a liang.
Pearls, jade, turtles, shells, silver and tin are used as decorations and treasures, not as currency, but they change at any time, and their weight has no rules.
After the rise of the Han Dynasty, they thought that the Qin Dynasty coins were heavy and difficult to use, so they ordered the people to mint pod coins instead.
The unit of gold returned to the weekly system of kilograms.
Those who did not abide by the law and pursued profits used their own surplus to accumulate goods, so that the goods on the market accumulated in their own hands, causing prices to skyrocket. The price of rice reached ten thousand gold per stone, and a horse was worth one hundred gold.
After the world was peaceful, Emperor Gaozu ordered merchants not to wear silk and ride in carriages, and increased taxes to frustrate them.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao, considering that the world had just stabilized, the laws on merchants were relaxed again, but the descendants of people in the market could not become officials.
In the fifth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, because the money was more abundant and lighter, four baht coins were minted, with the characters "banliang" on the front.
Abolish the law on stealing money and let the people mint it at will.
Jia Yi remonstrated and said: The law allows the world to openly hire people to make coins with copper and tin. Anyone who dares to mix lead and iron to commit adultery will be punished by tattooing.
But the situation with coining money is that if there is no doping, there will be no benefits; and the more subtle the doping, the more generous the benefits will be.
Things can bring disaster, and laws can cause evil. Now the common people can mint money, and they mint it in hiding, intending to prevent their huge profits and cunning. Even if they are sentenced to tattoos every day, this situation cannot stop.
Recently, the people have paid their share of the crime, with as many as a hundred people in one county. As for the officials who suspected it, many people were whipped and tortured and fled.
There is nothing more than making laws to seduce the people and make them fall into a trap!
In the past, it was forbidden to mint coins, and the death penalty was accumulated at the bottom; now that coins are minted openly, the crimes of tattooing are accumulated at the bottom.
In enacting such a law, what would the emperor rely on?
In addition, the coins used by the people vary from county to county: some use light money, plus a hundred plus a few; some use heavy money, even if the weight is the same, it cannot be accepted.
There is no place for coins formulated according to law. If officials are anxious, they should unify them, but it is too cumbersome and not powerful enough. If they are allowed to flow without punishment, then the coins will be extremely confusing if they are used differently in the market.
If there is no way to deal with this situation, people will not know where to go!
Nowadays, more and more people are giving up farming and mining copper. They put down their farm tools and use furnace charcoal to smelt money molds. The illegal money is increasing day by day, but the grain is not increasing. If kind people are tempted and go astray, and cautious people fall into punishment, the punishment will be very unfair. How can we ignore this!
The country knows that the worries are like this, and the officials must have discussed that it is forbidden to mint money.
Forbidding coining money is illegal and will cause great harm.
If there is an order to prohibit the minting of coins, then the coins must be valuable; if they are valuable, the benefits will be great. Secretly minting coins is like a cloud, and the crime of abandoning the market is not enough to prohibit it.
The evil has never been exhausted and the law has prohibited the collapse. This is caused by copper.
Copper is scattered all over the world, so the harm it causes is great.
summary: More than a hundred years later, King Jing of Zhou worried that money was too light and planned to cast large coins. Duke Shan Mu advised against it, arguing that when disasters came, property and currency should be weighed to save the people. If money was light, heavy money should be created for use, with both types circulating together. Abolishing light money for heavy money would cause the people to lose wealth, leading to shortages and flight. King Jing ignored this and made large coins with "actual goods" engraved, which benefited the people. When Qin annexed the world, currency was divided into two classes: gold measured in yi, and copper coins shaped like Zhou money with "ban liang" inscribed, weighing half a liang. Pearls, jade, turtles, shells, silver, and tin were decorations, not currency, and changed value arbitrarily. After the Han rose, they found Qin coins heavy and ordered pod coins instead, with gold returning to the weekly system of kilograms. Those who pursued profits hoarded goods, causing prices to skyrocket—rice reached ten thousand gold per stone, and a horse was worth one hundred gold. Emperor Gaozu ordered merchants not to wear silk or ride carriages and increased taxes to frustrate them. During Emperor Xiaohui and Queen Gao's reign, laws on merchants were relaxed, but their descendants could not become officials. In the fifth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, four baht coins were minted with "banliang" on the front, and the law on stealing money was abolished, allowing people to mint coins freely. Jia Yi remonstrated, arguing that coining money with copper and tin led to doping for profit, and even daily tattooing could not stop it. He noted that coins varied by county—some light, some heavy—causing confusion. People abandoned farming to mine copper, increasing illegal money without increasing grain. He proposed collecting copper to prevent scattering, which would bring seven blessings: reducing tattooing crimes, eliminating fake money, returning miners to farming, balancing money and goods, distinguishing noble from humble, enriching the government while impoverishing merchants, and competing with the Xiongnu. The emperor did not listen. Wu State minted coins in Shanhuo, becoming richer than the emperor, and later rebelled. Deng Tong, a great official, minted coins and became wealthier than kings. Their money spread worldwide.

translation:
When the county minted coins, most of the people cast them by craftsmanship, and most of the coins were lighter. The minister asked the mint official of the capital to cast red oblique coins, one for five, but it was not possible to pay taxes and supply the government with coins other than red oblique coins.
The price of platinum gradually dropped, and people did not use it as a treasure. The government ordered a ban, which was of no benefit. It was finally abolished after more than a year and became no longer popular.
This year, Zhang Tang died, but the people did not mourn.
In the next two years, the price of red money fell again, and people used it in clever ways. However, it was inconvenient and was abolished.
So they all banned the prefectures and states from casting money, and specifically ordered the three officials of Shanglin to cast money.
Since there were a lot of coins, he ordered that money that was not made by the three officials should not be popular in the world. The coins minted by each county and state were abolished and destroyed, and the copper was given to the three officials.
In this way, the number of coins minted by the common people decreased even more. They calculated that the expenses and profits could not be equal. Only clever craftsmen and wealthy people minted money secretly.
Yang Ke's activities of concealing property and evading taxes were reported all over the country, and most of the people from middle-income families and above were prosecuted.
Du Zhou came to review the case, and few people could reverse the case.
So they sent censors, court lieutenants, and eunuchs to various countries with different missions to deal with cases of hidden property in counties and counties. They obtained hundreds of millions of people's property, tens of millions of slaves, hundreds of hectares of land in large counties, and more than a hundred hectares in small counties, and the same number of real estate.
As a result, most of the middle-class and above-average merchants went bankrupt, and the people settled on good food and clothing and no longer engaged in hoarding. The government gradually became richer because of the money-making business of salt and iron.
The Guanzhong area was expanded and left and right auxiliaries were set up.
At first, there were a lot of salt and iron officials under the management of Da Nong, so he appointed Captain Shuiheng to be in charge of salt and iron affairs. After Yang Ke encouraged the report of hidden property, Shanglin's property increased, and he appointed Captain Shuiheng to be in charge of Shanglin.
Now that Shanglin has enough property, he needs to expand it.
At this time, the Guangdong Kingdom planned to use ships to start a war with the Han Dynasty, so it built Kunming Pool on a large scale and built temples around the pool.
The building boat is built, more than ten feet high, and the flag is placed on it. It is very spectacular.
So the emperor was infected by this style and built the Bailiang Fortress, which was dozens of feet high.
The construction of palaces has become more and more magnificent since then.
So min money was distributed to various government offices, and Shuiheng, Shaofu, Taipu, and Da Nong each set up agricultural officials, who often cultivated the confiscated land in various counties and counties on the spot.
The confiscated slaves and maidservants were distributed to various gardens to feed dogs, horses, and animals, and to various government offices.
The official positions were more complicated and more numerous, and there were many criminals and slaves. Therefore, the grain transported to the capital from the Dong River was about four million shi, and the government had to buy part of the grain itself to be able to use it.
Suozhong said: The children of aristocratic families and the rich engage in cockfighting, dog racing, and horse racing, as well as hunting and gambling games, disrupting the lives of ordinary people.
summary: During Emperor Wu's reign, wars with the Xiongnu and campaigns in the southwest and Guangdong drained resources. The government used money to buy titles and exempt people from punishment, leading to official chaos. Gongsun Hong, as prime minister, used moral principles to restrain ministers, while Zhang Tang used harsh laws. The Yellow River flooded, costing billions. The emperor discussed changing coins to supplement expenses, using white deer skin for leather coins worth 400,000 yuan and silver-tin platinum coins. The government destroyed half-liang coins and recast three baht coins, punishing secret minting with death. Shu Guo Xianyang and Kong Wei were appointed as great agricultural ministers to manage salt and iron, while Sang Hongyang, a merchant's son, became favored. The government set up salt and iron officials, taxed merchants, and confiscated hidden property. The rich went bankrupt, and the government grew richer through salt and iron. The emperor built Kunming Pool and Bailiang Fortress, expanding palaces. The government used confiscated land and slaves for farming, and the grain transported to the capital reached four million shi.

translation:
The big and small coins were abolished and replaced with goods cloth, two inches and five cents long and one inch wide. The head of the goods cloth is more than eight cents long and eight cents wide. Its round hole is two and a half minutes in diameter. Its foot branch is eight cents long and two cents wide in the middle. The words on the right side of the front are "goods" and the words on the left are "cloth". It weighs twenty-five baht, which is equivalent to twenty-five pieces of money.
The currency spring is one inch in diameter and weighs five baht. The text on the right side of the front is "huo" and the text on the left is "quan". The value of one coin is one. The two types of goods and cloth are popular at the same time.
And because the big money had been circulating for a long time, it was abolished. I was afraid that the people would not stop using it, so I ordered the people to use the big money alone for the time being, and the value of each coin was one with the new currency. It lasted for a total of six years, and they were not allowed to use the big money again.
Every time the currency was changed, people went bankrupt and committed a large number of crimes.
Wang Mang executed those who made money privately, and moved those who criticized and slandered the treasures to remote areas. There were too many people who broke the law, and it could not be fully implemented, so he changed the criminal law to reduce the punishment: Those who made spring cloth privately were confiscated and sent to the palace as slaves together with their wives and children;
There were even more people who broke the law. When five people were seated in a row without entering the government office, the county prison car was locked and escorted to Zhongguan in Chang'an. Sixty-seven out of ten people died in pain.
Six years after making the cloth, the Huns invaded fiercely. Wang Mang recruited prisoners and slaves from all over the world on a large scale, called Zhu Tu Xi Yong. All taxes came from the palace residents, and he collected one-thirtieth of the property tax.
He also ordered the ministers to the Huangshou officials in counties and counties to maintain the military horses. The officials transferred all the military horses to the people and asked them to maintain them.
The people often violated the ban and were unable to farm and pick mulberry. The corvee was complicated and heavy, and there were droughts and locusts causing trouble.
And because the system has not been established, no one from the princes to the petty officials can get their salaries, but they collect taxes privately, bribe their superiors, and do not deal with it tightly.
Officials relied on harshness and cruelty to establish their authority, and with Wang Mang's ban, they invaded and plundered the weak common people.
The rich cannot protect themselves, and the poor cannot survive, so they band together and become thieves. Depending on the dangers of the mountains and lakes, the officials cannot capture them and conceal the truth. Things get bigger and bigger, so there are often tens of thousands of people in Qing, Xu, Jingchu and other places.
Those who died in wars, those who were captured by ethnic minorities along the border, those who broke the law, those who died of hunger and disease, and those who cannibalized people. In this way, before Wang Mang was killed, the household registration in the world had been reduced by half.
Four years after the conquest of Zhutu Xiyong, the Han army killed Wang Mang.
Two years later, Shizu accepted the destiny, eliminated the cumbersome and harsh criminal laws, restored the five-baht coin, and worked with the people of the world to eliminate the old and introduce the new.
summary: After Wang Mang became regent, he changed the Han system, creating various coins like big coins, deed-knife coins, and wrong-knife coins. He later abolished these and introduced treasure goods, including gold, silver, turtle, shell, money, and cloth coins. He established six types of coins, each with different values, and implemented credit and five equalizations to control prices. He set up officials in Chang'an and five capitals to manage trade, taxing craftsmen and merchants. He also regulated wine production, with the government making wine and taking seven-tenths of the profit. Despite these measures, the people suffered, and many broke the law. Wang Mang executed those who made private coins and moved critics to remote areas. The corvee was heavy, and droughts and locusts caused trouble. Officials collected taxes privately, and the rich could not protect themselves, leading to widespread banditry. The Han army killed Wang Mang four years after the conquest of Zhutu Xiyong. Two years later, Shizu restored the five-baht coin and eliminated harsh laws. The text praises ancient methods of regulating commodities and prices, noting that during Emperor Xiaowu's time, expenses were met without increasing taxes, but under Wang Mang, the system failed, and the people suffered.

translation:
Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty was the prince of Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty.
My mother was Queen Gongai Xu, who was born among the people when Emperor Xuan was humble.
When he was two years old, Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne.
When Emperor Yuan was eight years old, he was made a prince.
As an adult, he is generous and respectful of Confucianism.
Seeing that most of the officials employed by Emperor Xuan were legal officials, they respected the emperor and humbled his ministers in order to rule the world with their names and deeds. Ministers Yang Yun, Gai Kuorao, etc. were all executed for the crime of ridiculing the emperor. They often said calmly when serving in peacetime: Your Majesty's punishment is too deep, and Confucian scholars should be used.
Emperor Xuan got angry and said: The Han family has its own system, which alternates between kings and hegemons. Why should they specialize in benevolent government and imitate the Zhou Dynasty?
Moreover, ordinary Confucian scholars are unable to combine what they have learned with practice, preferring to attach importance to the past and disregard the present, which confuses people with their names and reality, and they do not know what to do. How can they be entrusted with important responsibilities?
So he sighed: The one who disrupts my Liu family's order will be the prince!
Therefore, he neglected the prince and loved Huaiyang. Emperor Xuan said: The King of Huaiyang is good at making judgments and loves to study law. He should inherit my career.
Zhang Jieyu, the mother of King Huaiyang, was even more favored.
Emperor Xuan intended to replace the prince with King Huaiyang, but because he relied on the Xu family when he was a humble boy, the couple had a bad sworn relationship, so in the end he refused to abandon Queen Xu and establish another prince.
In December of the first year of Huanglong, Emperor Xuan died.
On the 26th, the prince succeeded to the throne and went to the Gaomiao to offer sacrifices.
The empress dowager is respected as the empress dowager, and the empress is the empress dowager.
On the fourth day of the first month of spring in the first year of the Chu Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty was buried in Duling.
The princes, princesses, and princes were rewarded with gold, and the officials were rewarded with cash and silk of less than two thousand dan, each with their own differences.
Amnesty to the world.
In March, the Empress Dowager's brother, Zhonglang General Wang Shun, was granted the title of Marquis of Anping.
On the tenth day of the lunar month, the queen was named Wang.
Those who could borrow the land in Sanfu, Taichang, prefectures and royal gardens were lent to the poor for farming, and those whose family property was less than a thousand yuan were lent seeds and grain.
Among the sons of his maternal grandfather, Ping'en Daihou, the son of Xu Jia, who often served as a servant, was given the title of Ping'enhou, so that he would be the queen of Daihou.
In April of Xia, an edict was issued saying: I have inherited the sacred cause of the late emperor, and I can serve the ancestral temple with caution.
There have been several earthquakes in recent times, and we are alarmed by God's warning, but we don't know the cause.
summary: Emperor Yuan of Han, son of Emperor Xuan, was made prince at age eight. He was generous and respected Confucianism, often criticizing his father's reliance on legal officials and harsh punishments. Emperor Xuan warned that Confucian scholars would disrupt the Han dynasty's system, which blended kingly and hegemonic rule. Though Emperor Xuan favored another son, he ultimately kept Emperor Yuan as heir due to loyalty to his mother.

translation:
More than 70 sentences were reduced, and the law that all parents and brothers from Dr. Guanglu to the doctor should be sentenced to prison together if one of them committed a crime.
Those who order the emperor's daily attendants to serve outside the palace should clearly fill in the ages, names, and physical characteristics of their grandparents, parents, and brothers.
On the ninth day of the eleventh month in winter, the imperial censor Gong Yu passed away.
Wei Sima Guji went on an envoy to the Huns and disappeared.
In the first month of the spring of the first year of Yongguang, he came to Ganquan, offered sacrifices to the Thai people in the suburbs, and pardoned the prisoners in Yunyang.
The subjects will be rewarded with a rank of nobility and a certain amount of cattle and wine for every 100 households of women.
In the old year, he was given silk, and there was no rental tax wherever the royal driver passed by.
In February, the imperial edict was issued to the prime minister and censor to recommend people who were simple, honest, humble, and highly virtuous. According to this content, Guanglu would take exams every year to determine his grade as a school doctor and an official.
In March, an edict was issued saying: The five emperors and three kings appointed talents and envoys to rule the world. But today the country is in chaos. Could it be that the people are different?
The problem lies in my ignorance and inability to identify talents.
Therefore, when the sycophant is in power, the wise man will be blocked and excluded.
Especially since the Zhou and Qin Dynasties, the social atmosphere has deteriorated, causing some people to abandon etiquette and justice and violate the criminal law. It is really sad!
From this point of view, what is the crime of the people?
Now the world is being pardoned, and the offenders are asked to work hard to rehabilitate themselves and engage in agricultural production.
Those without land borrowed public land and lent seeds and grains like ordinary poor people.
Officials who are rewarded with more than 600 stones are given the rank of fifth doctor, officials who are diligent in political affairs are given the second rank, and common people who inherit their fathers are given the first rank. Women will be given a certain amount of cattle and wine to a hundred households, and a certain amount of silk will be given to a widower, a widower and a senior citizen.
It rained and snowed this month, and severe frosts damaged the wheat crops, resulting in no harvest in the autumn.
In the spring and February of the second year, an edict was issued saying: I have heard that Tang and Yu used symbolic punishments but the people did not break the law, and that the laws of the Shang and Zhou dynasties were implemented and the traitors were frightened into submission.
Today, I can inherit the great achievements of our great ancestors and hold a high position above the ministers. I work in fear day and night. I have long been concerned about the suffering of the people and have never forgotten it.
However, the yin and yang are not adjusted, the sun and the moon are dim, the people are miserable and homeless, and thieves are on the rise.
The competent agencies also encouraged the thieves and failed to take effective measures to govern the people.
This is all due to my ignorance and my inability to govern the country.
This is my fault, and I feel deeply guilty.
If you are the parents of the common people, but you are so ungrateful, how can you care for the common people!
A general amnesty should be granted to the whole world, and rewards should be given to the first level of civil nobility, a certain amount of cattle and wine for every 100 households of women, and a certain amount of silk for widows, widowers, senior citizens, three elders, and filial brothers.
He also rewarded the princes, princesses, and princes with gold, with gold ranging from less than two thousand dan to officials in the central capital on a mission basis. Officials with more than 600 shi will be rewarded with five ranks of nobles, and officials who are diligent in political affairs will be rewarded with two ranks.
summary: Upon ascending the throne in 48 BCE, Emperor Yuan honored his mother and wife as empresses, granted amnesty, and distributed rewards. He issued edicts addressing natural disasters, earthquakes, and famines, ordering relief efforts, tax exemptions, and land grants to the poor. He reduced palace expenses, dismissed entertainers, and lent public lands to farmers. He also sent officials to inspect local governance and seek wise men. In subsequent years, Emperor Yuan continued responding to crises: earthquakes, floods, plagues, and famines led to further tax exemptions, amnesties, and relief measures. He abolished certain laws, reduced palace staff, and encouraged remonstrance. He appointed Confucian scholars like Gong Yu and Kuang Heng as officials, but his indecisiveness weakened the state. He also dealt with rebellions, such as the Xiqiang uprising, and military campaigns against the Xiongnu, including the execution of Zhizhi Chanyu.

translation:
Forgive the world.
The county ministers bought wine to congratulate each other and said "Long Live Long Live". Emperor Yuan displayed the book about the conquest of Zhizhi and watched it with the nobles in the harem.
In the fourth month of summer, an edict was issued saying: I have inherited the great achievements of the late emperor, and I am terrified day and night, fearing that I will not be up to the task.
In the previous period, Yang and Yin were not in harmony, and the five elements were out of order. The people were hungry.
In order to understand the situation of the common people who have lost their usual jobs, ten people including Dr. Shou, an admonishing doctor, were sent to travel around the country to express condolences to the elderly, widowers, lonely, poor and unemployed people, and to recommend talented people with outstanding talents.
General and Prime Minister Jiuqing must work hard to implement my intentions so that I can understand the operation of politics, religion and customs.
On the fifth day of June, Liu Jing, the king of Zhongshan, passed away.
The sand and gravel in Lantian blocked the Ba River, and the Anling Bank collapsed and blocked the Jing River, causing the water to flow backwards.
In the spring and March of the fifth year, an edict was issued saying: I have often heard that King Ming governed the country by clarifying standards of right and wrong for his subjects to follow, advocating rigor and modesty, and forming a social atmosphere. Therefore, the laws were established but the people did not violate them, and the orders were given and the people were happy to obey them.
Today I inherit the ancestral temple and work diligently and dare not slack off. However, my virtue is weak and my eyes are dark, and my education is shallow.
Didn’t the Analects of Confucius say it? The faults of the people should all be held responsible by those who rule the world.
Now I will pardon the world and reward you with the rank of civil nobility. For every 100 households of women, a certain amount of cattle and wine will be given, and for the three elders and filial piety, a certain amount of farmland and silk will be given.
The edict also said: It is the period of spring plowing and sericulture, and it is the time for the people to go all out. Therefore, farmers must be comforted this month and not violate the farming season.
There are now unscrupulous officials who, in order to investigate minor crimes, recruit witnesses to the office to testify. If some unurgent things are done to hinder the people, causing them to delay the farming season and lose the season, resulting in no harvest after autumn, the minister must understand this carefully and give repeated orders to ensure that it does not harm farming.
On the 17th day of the sixth lunar month in the summer, Prince Li's garden mausoleum was restored.
June 30th, partial solar eclipse.
On the 28th day of the seventh lunar month in autumn, the temple garden of the Emperor Taishang, the original temple of Gaozu, the tombs of Empress Zhaoling, King Wu Ai, Empress Zhao Ai and Hou Wei Si were restored.
In the first month of spring of the first year of Jingning, the Xiongnu Hu Hanxie Shanyu came to court.
The edict said: The Xiongnu Zhizhi Chanyu betrayed etiquette and justice and was punished for his crime. Hu Hanxie Chanyu did not forget his kindness and admired the etiquette and justice of the Han Dynasty. He once again revised the ritual of greetings and was willing to maintain the long-term harmony and friendship between the Central Plains and the outside of the Great Wall so that the border chief would not suffer the disaster of military revolution. He could change his name to Jingning.
summary: Emperor Yuan's reign saw numerous natural disasters and social unrest. He repeatedly issued edicts blaming himself for poor governance and seeking advice. He reformed policies, including abolishing the death penalty for certain family crimes and reducing corvée labor. He also established his own mausoleum, Weiling, and ordered that no new migrants be forced to settle there.

translation:
The chanyu was given to wait for the imperial edict to be followed by King Qiang of Yeting. The Crown Prince performed the coronation ceremony.
The princes and heirs of the marquis are given the rank of five great officials. The world is the heir of his father.
In February, the imperial censor, Fan Yanshou, passed away.
On March 14, the temple and cemetery of Emperor Hui's dormitory and the dormitories of Empress Dowager Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Xiaozhao were restored.
In the summer, Gan Yanshou, the Cavalry Commander, was granted the rank of Marquis.
The deputy captain Chen Tangjue was given to the Marquis of Guannei with a hundred catties of gold.
On May 25th, Emperor Yuan died in Weiyang Palace.
Fires broke out in the temples of Emperor Taishang, Emperor Hui and Emperor Jing.
Then go to the residence of Emperor Wen, Empress Dowager Zhao, Empress Zhao Ling, King Wu Ai, and Empress Zhao Ai.
On the 19th day of the seventh month in autumn, Emperor Yuan was buried in Weiling.
Ban Gu's comment: My maternal grandfather's brother once served as Emperor Yuan's servant. He told me that Emperor Yuan had a wide range of interests and was proficient in calligraphy. He could play the piano and flute, and could compose new lyrics according to music scores. He had clear rhythms and was extremely clever.
As a young man, he respected Confucianism and succeeded to the throne. Confucian scholars were recruited and entrusted with political affairs. Confucian scholars such as Gong Yu, Xue Guangde, Wei Xian, and Kuang Heng successively became prime ministers.
However, Emperor Yuan was restrained by literary principles and was indecisive, and Emperor Xuan's Zhongxing career declined.
However, despite his generosity and magnanimity, he was respectful and thrifty, and his orders were gentle and elegant, which was the legacy of the ancient wise kings.
summary: Emperor Yuan died in 33 BCE after 16 years of rule. Ban Gu's commentary notes that Emperor Yuan was talented in music and calligraphy, respected Confucianism, and appointed many Confucian scholars as officials. However, his indecisiveness and adherence to literary principles led to the decline of Emperor Xuan's achievements. Despite this, his generosity, thrift, and gentle edicts reflected the legacy of ancient wise kings.

translation:
Emperor Xiaoai was the grandson of Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty and the son of Prince Dingtao Gong.
The mother is Ding Ji.
He became king at the age of three, and became interested in literature and law as an adult.
In the fourth year of Yuanyan's reign, he went to the capital to see Emperor Cheng, and his Fu, Xiang, and lieutenants all came together.
At this time, Emperor Cheng's younger brother, Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, also came to see him, but only Fu Tong came.
The emperor was puzzled, so he asked King Dingtao. King Dingtao replied: "The imperial court has issued an order. When princes and kings come to court, their officials with a title of two thousand stones should come together."
Fu, Xiang, and Lieutenant all have two thousand stones, so they should all come together.
The emperor asked him to recite "Poetry", and he was familiar with it and could explain its meaning.
Another day, Emperor Cheng asked King Zhongshan: "Which decree is it based on when Fu Tong comes?"
King Zhongshan was speechless.
I asked him to recite the Book of Documents, but he forgot about it again.
Emperor Cheng invited him to dinner, but he was still eating after everyone else had finished. When he left the table, even his garter belt fell off.
When Emperor Cheng saw this, he thought King Zhongshan was incompetent, but he liked King Dingtao very much and often praised his talents.
At this time, Queen Mother Fu, the grandmother of King Dingtao, accompanied her to the court and privately presented gifts to Emperor Cheng's favorite Zhao Zhaoyi and his uncle, Hussar General and Quyanghou Wanggen.
Zhao Zhaoyi and Wang Gen saw that the emperor had no children and wanted to establish a relationship with a suitable prince as soon as possible to maintain their long-term wealth, so they praised King Dingtao and persuaded Emperor Cheng to make him the prince.
Emperor Cheng also admired King Dingtao's talents, so he held an adult crowning ceremony for him in the court and sent him back to his fiefdom, Dingtao. He was seventeen years old at this time.
In the second year, the emperor sent Jinwu Renhong to act as Dahonglu. With the imperial edict, he summoned King Dingtao and established him as the crown prince.
King Dingtao thanked Zhao and said: I am fortunate enough to inherit my late father's vassal status and become the prince of the vassals. However, my talents and virtues are not enough to enter the prince's palace.
Your Majesty is holy, virtuous and generous. He respects his ancestors and obeys the gods. He deserves to be blessed by heaven and have many children and grandchildren.
I would like to temporarily stay in the Kyoto residence and ask about the emperor's daily life in the morning and evening. After the emperor has a holy heir, he will return to the feudal state and guard the vassal.
After the book was written, the emperor said that everything was known.
More than a month later, an edict was issued to establish Liu Jing, the grandson of King Xiao of Chu, as King Dingtao, and to offer sacrifices to King Dingtao Gong. This was to reward the prince for paying attention to Zongtao's character.
The specific records are in "Hanshu·Biography of Waiqi".
In March of the second year of Suihe, Emperor Cheng died.
On the fourth day of April, the prince became the emperor and paid a visit to the Temple of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty.
Respect the Queen Mother as the Queen Mother and the Queen as the Queen Mother.
summary: Emperor Xiaoai, grandson of Emperor Yuan and son of Prince Dingtao Gong, became king at age three and developed an interest in literature and law. In the fourth year of Yuanyan's reign, he visited Emperor Cheng with his officials, while Prince Xiao of Zhongshan came with only one attendant. Emperor Cheng, impressed by King Dingtao's knowledge of the "Poetry" and his explanations, favored him over the incompetent King Zhongshan. Queen Mother Fu, King Dingtao's grandmother, bribed Emperor Cheng's favorites Zhao Zhaoyi and Wang Gen, who, seeing the emperor had no heirs, praised King Dingtao. Emperor Cheng crowned him at seventeen and later made him crown prince. King Dingtao humbly declined but accepted. After Emperor Cheng's death in the second year of Suihe, the prince became emperor, honoring the Queen Mother and issuing amnesties. He honored his grandmother and mother, granted titles to relatives, and dismissed Yuefu for lewd music. He rewarded Wang Gen and others for supporting his succession and granted lands to Wang Liang for mourning. He issued edicts to curb extravagance, limiting land and slave ownership, banning merchants from land and office, and stopping complex embroidery. He revoked certain laws, allowed inner palace residents under thirty to marry, freed slaves over fifty, and banned rare animal tributes. He increased salaries for low-ranking officials and punished corrupt officials. After disasters like earthquakes and floods, he sent officials to aid victims and exempted taxes for the poor. In the first year of Jianping, he pardoned the world, deposed guilty marquises, and gave Wang family lands to the poor. He sought talent, granted money and cloth to officials, and saw the suicide of Empress Dowager Feng and her brother. In the second year, he dismissed the chief minister, restored the imperial censor, and honored his ancestors with new titles and temples. After Empress Dowager Ding's death, he followed Zhou rites for burial, recruiting 50,000 workers. He initially accepted prophecies to change the era name but later revoked them, punishing the prophets and officials. He faced droughts, fires, and comets, restored sacrifices, and dealt with rebellions. He granted titles for reporting crimes, honored his wife, and sought military talent. In the first year of Yuanshou, a solar eclipse led to an edict blaming himself and seeking virtuous officials. After Empress Dowager Fu's death, he dismissed officials and saw portents. In the second year, Xiongnu envoys visited, and he divided official duties. Emperor Ai died in Weiyang Palace at age 20 after six years as emperor, buried in Yiling. Ban Gu noted his early talent and efforts to strengthen authority but lamented his short reign.

translation:
Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty, great-grandson of Emperor Wu, and grandson of Prince Ru.
Prince Ru took in Shi Liangdi and gave birth to Emperor Shi's grandson. His grandson took in Mrs. Wang and gave birth to Emperor Xuan, who was named Zenghuang's grandson.
A few months after giving birth, a "witchcraft incident" occurred. The prince, Liang Di, the emperor's grandson, and Mrs. Wang were all killed.
The facts are all recorded in "The Legend of the Prince".
Even though his great-grandson was still an infant, he was imprisoned.
At that time, Bingji was an official of Tingwei and was responsible for handling witchcraft incidents. He was extremely sympathetic to his great-grandson's innocent misfortune, so he ordered the female convicts Zhao Zhengqing from Huaiyang and Hu Zu from Weicheng to exchange breast-feeding and provide them with food and clothing privately. They treated him very kindly.
The witchcraft incident could not be concluded for several years.
In the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Wu was ill and traveled back and forth between Changyang and Wuzha palaces. The astrologers who were watching the clouds said that there was the emperor's energy in Chang'an prison.
