Emperor Wu sent envoys to inform the various officials in the capital that criminals imprisoned due to witchcraft incidents would be executed regardless of their severity.
The emissary ordered Guo Rang to go to the county prison at night for inspection. Bingji closed the prison door so that the envoys could not enter, but his great-grandson Lai Bingji was saved.
Later, when there was a general amnesty, Bingji drove his great-grandson to his grandmother Shi Liangdi's home.
This incident is recorded in "Biography of Bingji" and "Biography of Foreign Relatives".
Later, there was an edict, sending officials from Yeting to visit the great-grandson at the historian's home, and ordered Zongzheng to record him in the royal genealogy.
At this time, Zhang He, the order of Yeting, was Prince Li's former attendant. He missed Prince Li's old kindness and sympathized with his great-grandson, so he treated his great-grandson considerately and used his personal money to support his great-grandson's education.
When he was older, he married the daughter of Xu Guanghan, a court dyer, for his great-grandson. Therefore, his great-grandson relied on the Guanghan brothers and the Shi family of his grandmother's family.
He returned from the East China Sea to learn "Poetry" from Zhong Weng. He was talented and never tired of learning. He also had the character of drawing a sword to help when the road was rough. He fought chickens and horses and made many friends. He was familiar with the evil in the alleys and the gains and losses of official governance.
He visited the tombs of his ancestors many times to pay his respects, and went to the Sanfu District of Kyoto to understand the people's sentiments. He was once trapped and humiliated in the salt pond of Lianshao County, especially in Du County?
He traveled between counties, mostly in Xiadu.
He went to the imperial court to attend court invitations and lived in Shangguanli, Chang'an. He had hair all over his body and on his feet. He always glowed when sleeping. Every time he went to a bakery to buy cakes, the business of the bakery prospered. People were surprised by this.
In April of the first year of Yuanping, Emperor Zhao died without any heirs.
General Huo Guang asked the queen to summon the king of Changyi to be the emperor.
On June 1, the king of Changyi received the emperor's jade seal and imperial robes, and honored the queen as the empress dowager.
summary: Emperor Xuan, great-grandson of Emperor Wu, was born into tragedy. His grandfather Prince Ru, grandmother Shi Liangdi, and parents were all killed in the "witchcraft incident" when he was an infant. Imprisoned, he was saved by official Bingji, who arranged for female convicts to nurse him. After a general amnesty, Bingji took him to his grandmother's home. Later, Yeting official Zhang He, remembering his loyalty to Prince Li, supported the boy's education and arranged his marriage to Xu Guanghan's daughter. As he grew, Emperor Xuan studied poetry under Zhong Weng, showed talent, and became familiar with both common people's lives and official governance. He traveled extensively, visited ancestral tombs, and experienced hardship in Lianshao County. Strange phenomena surrounded him—his body glowed during sleep, and bakeries prospered when he visited. When Emperor Zhao died without heirs, General Huo Guang initially appointed the King of Changyi, but soon deposed him for lewd behavior. Huo Guang then recommended Emperor Xuan, then eighteen, citing his virtue, education, and suitability. The Empress Dowager agreed, and after proper ceremonies, he ascended the throne. The Huo family later rebelled, and Queen Huo was deposed after being implicated in poisoning plots. Emperor Xuan continued his reforms, lowering salt prices, improving prison conditions, and requiring annual reports of deaths in custody. He built tombs, established temples, and rewarded those who had helped him in his youth, including Bingji, Zhang He, and the female convicts who nursed him.

translation:
The edict states: The Great Sima General Bo Luhou has been with Emperor Xiaowu for more than thirty years, and has assisted Emperor Xiaozhao for more than ten years. He has been loyal to the country many times, and led the Sangong, Jiuqing, officials and other ministers to formulate long-term peace and stability strategies to stabilize the ancestral temple and bring peace to the people of the world.
I deeply admire him for his high merit and virtue. Now let his descendants enjoy his glory.
If his nobility is not reduced, if he does not bear the burden of corvee and tax from generation to generation, his merits will be like that of Prime Minister Xiao He.
In the fourth month of summer, phoenixes gathered in Lu County, followed by flocks of birds.
Amnesty to the world.
In the fifth month, Pingqiuhou Wang Qian, the official of Guanglu, was found guilty and sentenced to death in prison.
The emperor began to take charge of the government personally, and missed the merits of the general Huo Guang, so he appointed Huo Guang's nephew, Lepinghou Huoshan, to be the secretary and take charge of the government affairs. He also ordered the ministers to report their work to the emperor frequently so that the emperor could grasp the situation. He would listen to work reports every five days and perform duties in various departments below the prime minister. To describe their situation and measures, and to test their political achievements and abilities.
The ministers should be promoted and those who have made special contributions should be generously rewarded so that their duties can be passed down to their descendants and their positions will not be changed.
This resulted in the imperial court having complete facilities and adequate staffing. The top and bottom are of one heart and one mind, and there is no intention of settling down.
In the spring and March of the third year, an edict was issued saying: It has been said that meritorious deeds are not rewarded, and crimes are not punished. Even the emperors of the Tang Dynasty, Yao, Yu and Shun could not transform the world with virtue.
Today, Wang Cheng, the Prime Minister of Jiaodong, warmly receives and properly resettles the refugees, so that more than 80,000 refugees have registered their registered residence in Jiaodong. His political achievements are different from those of ordinary people. Now Wang Cheng's salary has been raised to two thousand dan and he has been given the title of Marquis of Guannei.
The edict also said: The widowed, lonely, elderly and poor people are the people I have the most sympathy and concern for.
In the past, edicts were issued to lend public fields, seeds, and grain rations.
Now I will give silk to the widowed and lonely old man.
Erqianshi officials should strictly require their staff to pay serious attention to them and not let them lose their regular jobs.
Let the Zhongyuan County appoint virtuous and upright people who can go deep among the people and understand the people's sentiments.
On the 22nd day of the fourth lunar month in the summer, the Crown Prince was established and the whole country was granted amnesty.
He was given the title of Marquis of Guannei, the imperial censor, and the right concubine of the middle two thousand stone ranks. As his father's heir, he was promoted to the first rank in the world.
King Guangling was rewarded with a thousand catties of gold, each of the fifteen princes and kings was given a hundred catties of gold each, and the eighty-seven people in the feudal kingdom were each rewarded with twenty catties of gold.
summary: Emperor Xuan's reign was marked by careful governance. He initially declined Huo Guang's offer to return power, entrusting him with major responsibilities. He rewarded meritorious officials generously, including Huo Guang, Yang Chang, and others. He issued edicts promoting agriculture, reducing waste, and caring for the poor. When earthquakes struck, he wore plain clothes, avoided the main hall, and sought advice from officials. After Huo Guang's death, Emperor Xuan took personal control of government. He established regular reporting systems and tested officials' abilities. He promoted virtuous officials like Wang Cheng, who resettled refugees. He established the Crown Prince and granted amnesties. He reformed laws to protect filial piety, allowing parents to hide children's crimes and exempting mourners from corvée labor.

translation:
The Xiongnu Chanyu admired his righteousness to the wind, and the whole country came together to congratulate him with the national treasure. This was an unprecedented thing.
The Shanyu does not worship Zhengshuo of the Han Dynasty, but is a guest of the king. When he worships, he should be like the princes and kings.
The edict said: It is often heard that the five emperors and three kings did not rule according to etiquette in the wilderness, and their political punishments were not adequate.
Today, Chanyu claims to be a minister of the Northern Domain and has come to the court to celebrate the Spring Festival. I am not virtuous enough to place him under the rule of my court. I should treat him as a guest and be in front of the princes and kings.
In the first month of spring of the third year, I came to Ganquan and offered sacrifices to the Thai people in the suburbs.
The Xiongnu called Han Xie Shanyu Jihou to come to the court, and when he paid homage, he called him a vassal minister but did not sign up.
Emperor Xuan rewarded him with seals, ribbons, crowns, clothes, carriages, horses, gold, brocade, and silk fabrics.
A commissioner was sent to guide Shanyu. He first went to the Chang'an residence and stayed in Changping.
Emperor Xuan went from Ganquan to Chiyang Palace to rest.
He went to Changpingban again and sent an edict to the chanyu not to visit him.
Crowds of people on both sides of the road he passed lined up in front of the door to watch. The barbarian monarchs and princes and tens of thousands of people lined the road to welcome him.
The emperor boarded the Wei Bridge and the welcoming crowd shouted "Long live!"
Chanyu entered the building.
The emperor held a welcome banquet in Jianzhang Palace to honor Shan Yu.
And let Shanyu visit the treasures of the Han Dynasty.
In February, Shanyu returned westward after completing his congratulatory mission. The imperial court sent a guard of 16,000 people led by Changle Guards Gaochanghou Dong Zhong, Chariot and Cavalry Commanders Han Chang, and Cavalry Commanders Wei Hu to escort Shan Yu.
Shanyu lived in the south of Mu and was stationed in Guanglu City.
The imperial edict was issued to the north to support its grain supply.
Zhizhi Shanyu was isolated and fled far away, and the Xiongnu became stable from then on.
Emperor Xuan issued an edict saying: The former phoenix gathered in Xincai, surrounded by tens of thousands of birds, all standing in awe of the phoenix.
For this reason, the governor of Runan was rewarded with 10,000 pieces of silk, and various rewards were given to Xincai's chief officials, three elders, filial piety, Li Tian, ​​and widowers and widowers.
Grant the common people the second level of nobility and exempt them from this year's land rent.
On March 6, Prime Minister Huang Ba passed away.
The imperial edict ordered various scholars to speak about the similarities and differences of the Five Classics. The prince, Taifu Xiao Wangzhi and others summarized and synthesized them, and then Emperor Xuan personally reviewed them.
So Liangqiu's "Yi", Daxia Xiahou's "Shangshu", and Gu Liang's "Spring and Autumn" were established.
In winter, Wusun Princess Liu Jieyou returned to China to visit relatives.
In the summer of the fourth year, Wang Haiyang of Guangchuan was found guilty and was demoted to a commoner and moved to Fangling.
On October 23rd in winter, a fire broke out in the Xuanshi Pavilion of Weiyang Palace.
In the first month of spring of the first year of Huanglong, he came to Ganquan and offered sacrifices to the Thai people in the suburbs.
When the Xiongnu Huhanxie Chanyu came to court, the courtesy and rewards were the same as last time.
In February, Shanyu returned to China.
summary: Under his rule, the Xiongnu were pacified. Huhanxie Chanyu submitted as a vassal, visiting the court with great ceremony. Emperor Xuan treated him as a guest, rewarding him generously and establishing protectorates for surrendered tribes. The Western Qiang were subdued through military campaigns and farming strategies proposed by General Zhao Chongguo.

translation:
The edict said: I have heard that in ancient times when governing the world, the king and his ministers were of one mind, judged right and wrong, and acted in accordance with the rules.
It is the harmony between the upper and lower levels, and peace at home and abroad. His cohesion is admirable.
I am not a wise king, but I have repeatedly told the ministers to be lenient, care about and solve the sufferings of the people, and pursue the peaceful and prosperous times of the three kings and carry forward the virtues of the ancestors.
Among today's officials, some regard it as lenient not to restrain evil, and as lax as to condone the guilty; some regard cruel officials as virtuous, which are all one-sided and incorrect.
Such an imperial edict is extremely ridiculous!
Nowadays, there are few things happening in the world, there are fewer corvees, and there is no army, but the people are poor and there are many thieves. What is the fault?
The personnel, household registration, and tax information reported to the court were inconsistent with the facts and were lied to avoid prosecution.
Sangong doesn't care about this. How will I know the true and credible situation?
Any requests to reduce the number of followers and officers and use their expenses to support themselves will no longer be implemented.
When the censor finds something suspicious when reviewing the materials reported from various places, he must conduct verification and cannot allow the false to be confused with the true.
In March, a comet appeared between Wangliangxing and Gedao star areas, and then entered the Purple Palace star area.
In April of Xia, an edict was issued saying: The purpose of recommending honest officials is to promote honesty and integrity.
Officials with six hundred stones are regarded as officials. When handling cases, they must first seek instructions from the court, and their rank and salary are determined by the court. From now on, officials with six hundred stones cannot be promoted to honest officials.
On the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month in winter, Emperor Xuan died in Weiyang Palace.
On the 26th, the Queen Mother was honored as the Queen Mother.
Ban Gu commented: When Emperor Xuan of the Han Dynasty governed the country, meritorious deeds must be rewarded, and guilty deeds must be punished. Comprehensive examination of names and facts shows that people in politics, literature, and jurisprudence can be proficient in their professions and exert their expertise. As for the skills of craftsmen and tools, few can match them since the reign of Emperor Yuan and Emperor Cheng. From this we can see that in the era of Emperor Xuan, officials were competent in their duties and the people were in peace with their jobs.
Being invaded by the Xiongnu, the Huhanxie Chanyu could come to the court, the Zhizhi Chanyu could escape far away, Shen Tianwei could be seen in the Northern Yi, and the Chanyu Muyi could bow his head and declare himself a vassal.
The ancestor of the Gongguang clan, whose career is passed down to his heirs, can be said to be the master of Zhongxing, and his virtues are comparable to those of Emperor Gaozong of Yin and King Xuan of Zhou.
summary: Emperor Xuan died in Weiyang Palace after a reign marked by competent administration, military success, and cultural achievements. Ban Gu commented that he rewarded merit, punished guilt, and examined names and facts thoroughly, making officials proficient in their duties and people content in their work. His reign was considered a restoration, with virtues comparable to those of King Xuan of Zhou.

translation:
Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty was the crown prince of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, and his mother was Empress Lu.
When he was five years old, Han Gaozu began to be the king of Han.
In the second year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was made the crown prince.
In April of the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Emperor Gaozu passed away.
On May 17, the prince became the emperor, and his mother, Empress Lu, became the empress dowager.
Reward subjects with first-level titles.
Zhonglang and Langzhong officials who have served for six years will be promoted to the third level, and those who have served for four years will be promoted to the second level.
A second-level wailang officer who has served for six years.
The middle man who has been in office for less than one year will be promoted to a higher level, and the outer man who has been in office for less than two years will be rewarded with a reward of 10,000 yuan.
The eunuch's salary is the same as that of a doctor. The salaries of the emperor's attendants such as the eunuchs, bearers, halberds, warriors, and cavalrymen were the same as those of the foreign ministers.
The prince's imperial concubine was rewarded with the title of fifth doctor, and those who served for five years would be given the title of second grade.
Those who organize the funeral for the great ancestor will be rewarded with a reward of 20,000 yuan for those with a salary of 2,000 shi, a reward of 10,000 for those with a salary of 600 shi or more, and a reward of 5,000 for those with a salary of less than 500 shi.
Those who build a mausoleum for the great ancestor will be rewarded 40 gold by the general, 20 gold for 2,000 shi, 6 gold for more than 600 shi, and 2 gold for less than 500 shi.
Reduce land rent and restore the system of one tax for every fifteen people.
Those who have a rank of five officials, more than six hundred shi, and those who have served the emperor and whose names are known to the emperor, and who commit crimes and should be yoke and chained, can be relaxed to house arrest instead of being thrown into prison. For those with official positions above Shangzao, grandsons inside and outside the royal family, or children and grandchildren who are no longer related by blood, etc., those who commit crimes should be punished, or if they should be sentenced to four years in prison, the sentence should be reduced to three years. People over seventy and under ten who are guilty and should be punished are exempted from corporal punishment.
The emperor also pointed out in the order: The duty of officials is to do things for the people. If they work hard to do things well, they will gain the trust of the people. The reason why they are improved is to ask them to do things better for the people.
All officials whose salary is more than 600 dan, who live with their parents and wives, and those who have worn the seal of general or captain who are no longer in office and have served in the army, or who have worn the official seal of 2,000 dan, only need to pay military tax and are exempt from all other corvee services.
The princes and princes of each county were ordered to build the ancestral temple of Gaozu.
In the winter of December of the first year of Emperor Hui, King Liu Ruyi of Zhao Yin passed away.
It is stipulated that if a subject commits a crime, he can atone for the crime of death by paying the money of the 30th level.
Reward the common people with titles, one level for each household.
In the first month of spring, the city of Chang'an was built.
summary: Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty, son of Emperor Gaozu and Empress Lu, became crown prince in the second year of Gaozu's reign. After Gaozu's death in April of the twelfth year, Hui ascended the throne on May 17, with his mother becoming empress dowager. He issued decrees rewarding subjects with titles and promoting officials based on service length: Zhonglang and Langzhong officials serving six years received third-level promotions, those serving four years received second-level promotions, and various other officials received specific rewards. Those who organized Gaozu's funeral received monetary rewards based on salary, and those who built his mausoleum received gold. Land rent was reduced to one tax per fifteen people. Certain officials and their families were exempted from corvée labor except military tax. Princes were ordered to build Gaozu's ancestral temple.

translation:
In the winter of October of the second year of Emperor Hui's reign, King Hui of Qi came to pay homage and presented Chengyang County to increase Princess Lu Yuan's Tangmuyi. Respect Princess Lu Yuan as the Queen Mother.
On the fourth day of the first lunar month of spring, two dragons appeared in the well of a hundred people's houses in Lanling. On the evening of the 6th, his whereabouts were unknown.
An earthquake occurred in Longxi.
That summer, there was a drought.
Yanghou Liu Zhong passed away.
In autumn, on July 5th, Prime Minister Xiao He passed away.
In the spring of the third year of Emperor Hui's reign, 146,000 male and female migrant workers within 600 miles of Chang'an were recruited to build Chang'an City for a period of thirty days.
The daughter of the Liu family was made a princess and married to King Shanyu of the Xiongnu as his wife to establish friendship.
In the fifth month of summer, the king of Minyue was granted the title of King of East China Sea.
In June, 20,000 princes, their families, and slaves were sent to Chang'an to build a city.
In autumn and July, a fire broke out in the royal stables.
Zhao Tuo, the king of South Vietnam, declared himself a minister and paid tribute.
In the winter and tenth month of the fourth year of Emperor Hui's reign, Zhang Ao's daughter was made queen.
In the first month of spring, sages with filial piety and loyalty to the fields were selected from various places to exempt them from the burden of corvee service.
On March 17, the emperor held a crown ceremony and granted amnesty to the world.
Eliminate the laws that hinder the officials and the people, and abolish the Qin laws that make it illegal to carry a document.
A fire broke out in Hongtai of Changle Palace, and blood rain occurred in Yiyang area.
On the 20th day of the seventh lunar month in autumn, a fire broke out in the ling room of Weiyang Palace; on the 21st, a fire broke out in the weaving room.
In the tenth month of winter in the fifth year of Emperor Hui's reign, thunder rumbled, peaches and plums blossomed, and jujube trees bore fruit.
In the first month of spring, 145,000 male and female migrant workers within 600 miles of Chang'an were again recruited to build the city in Chang'an for a period of thirty days.
That summer, there was a severe drought.
In the eighth month of autumn, Prime Minister Cao Shen passed away.
In September, Chang'an City was completely completed.
Reward the common people with titles, one level for each household.
In the winter and tenth month of the sixth year of Emperor Hui's reign, King Fei of Qi passed away.
The emperor ordered that people could buy and sell titles, and that women aged between fifteen and thirty who did not marry would be fined six hundred coins.
In June of summer, Fan Kuai, Marquis of Wuyang, passed away.
The west city of Chang'an was built and Aocang was built.
In the winter and tenth month of the seventh year of Emperor Hui's reign, he sent chariots and cavalry officers to Xingyang, under the command of Taiwei Guan Ying.
On the first day of the first lunar month in spring, a solar eclipse occurs.
On May 29th in the summer, there was a total solar eclipse.
On August 12 in autumn, Emperor Hui died in Weiyang Palace.
On September 5, he was buried in Anling.
Ban Gu commented: Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty was closely related to the clan at home, and was the prime minister in foreign affairs. He favored King Qi Miao and King Zhao Yin, which can be described as being kind and respectful.
summary: In the first year of his reign, King Liu Ruyi of Zhao died. Subjects could atone for capital crimes with money. Commoners received title promotions. Chang'an city construction began. In the second year, King Hui of Qi presented Chengyang County to increase Princess Lu Yuan's territory. Two dragons appeared in Lanling, an earthquake struck Longxi, drought occurred, and Yanghou Liu Zhong and Prime Minister Xiao He died. In the third year, 146,000 workers built Chang'an for thirty days. A Liu family princess married the Xiongnu Shanyu. The King of Minyue was titled King of East China Sea, and 20,000 princes and slaves built Chang'an. A fire broke out in royal stables, and Zhao Tuo of South Vietnam paid tribute. In the fourth year, Zhang Ao's daughter became queen. Filial and loyal sages were exempted from corvée. The emperor held a crown ceremony with amnesty, abolished restrictive Qin laws, and fires occurred in Changle and Weiyang Palaces. In the fifth year, unusual weather included thunder and fruit blossoming in winter. Another 145,000 workers built Chang'an. Severe drought struck, Prime Minister Cao Shen died, and Chang'an city was completed. In the sixth year, King Fei of Qi died. Titles could be bought, and unmarried women aged fifteen to thirty were fined. Fan Kuai died, and the west city and Aocang were built. In the seventh year, chariot officers were sent to Xingyang. Solar eclipses occurred, and Emperor Hui died in Weiyang Palace on August 12, buried in Anling on September 5. Ban Gu commented that Hui was kind and respectful but fell short of saintliness due to Empress Lu's actions.

translation:
Emperor Xiaocheng was the prince of Emperor Yuan.
His mother was Empress Wang. When Emperor Yuan was the crown prince, he was born into the emperor in the colorful painting hall of the palace and became his direct grandson.
Emperor Xuan liked him very much and named him Taisun. He often placed him under his knees.
When he was three years old, his grandfather Emperor Xuan died. Emperor Yuan succeeded to the throne and Emperor Cheng made him the prince.
As an adult, he likes to read scriptures, be broad-minded and cautious.
He used to live in Guigong, but Emperor Yuan sometimes summoned him urgently. When the prince left the Dragon Tower Gate, he did not dare to cross the emperor's galloping road. He went west to Zhicheng Gate, crossed in front of the city gate, and then turned back to Zuoshimen.
Emperor Yuan saw that he was late and asked why. Emperor Cheng told him that he did not dare to cross the Emperor's Chi Road and had to take a detour. Emperor Yuan was very happy and ordered that the Prince could cross the Chi Road.
Later, Emperor Yuan thought he was incompetent because he was fond of drinking and enjoying himself. Emperor Yuan decided that Prince Tao Gong was versatile and his mother, Fu Zhaoyi, was favored. Emperor Yuan wanted to make Prince Gong the crown prince.
Lai Shizhong Shi Xian protected the prince's family and provided strong assistance. Emperor Xuan of the Yuan Dynasty was spared from deposing because Emperor Xuan was particularly fond of the prince.
In May of the first year of Jingning, Emperor Yuan died.
On June 22, the prince ascended the throne and paid homage to Gaozu Temple.
The empress dowager is respected as the empress dowager, and the empress is the empress dowager.
Wang Feng, the Marquis of Yangping, the imperial uncle's imperial guard, was appointed as the Grand Sima and the Grand General, and was in charge of the secretarial affairs.
On July 28, relevant personnel stated: It is indecent to be buried with chariots, cattle, horses, and animals and should not be buried with them.
Emperor Cheng agreed.
In July, there is a general amnesty.
On the first day of the first lunar month of the first year of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the emperor's great ancestor mourned a fire in the temple.
He made Kuling Liang, the brother of the deceased King of Hejian, the king of Shangjun.
A comet appears in the camp star area.
He was dismissed from Shanglin and sentenced to prison.
In February, when the right general Shi Yao Yin and others were on their way back from an envoy to the Huns, more than a hundred miles away from the frontier fortress, they suddenly encountered a storm and fire, which burned Yao Yin and seven others to death.
The princes, prime ministers, generals, princes, queen mothers, princesses, royal lords, and officials were rewarded with two thousand stones of gold. The officials of the clan were given less than one thousand stones to two hundred stones. The men of the clan who were famous in the genealogy, the three elders, the filial piety, the fields, the widows and the widows were all rewarded with money and silk, each with different levels. Fifty households of officials and people were rewarded with some cattle and wine.
The edict was issued: Fire fell in the ancestral temple, a comet appeared in the east, and God warned me when I ascended the throne. My fault was serious!
"Shangshu" says: In ancient times, when a wise king encountered disaster, he corrected his virtues and behaved according to the celestial phenomena.
I hope that all the ministers will work tirelessly and lead the staff to supplement my shortcomings.
Advocate tolerance, promote harmony, treat others favorably, and don't be harsh on others.
summary: Emperor Xiaocheng, the son of Emperor Yuan and Empress Wang, was born while his father was crown prince and was greatly favored by his grandfather, Emperor Xuan, who named him Taisun. After Emperor Xuan’s death, Emperor Yuan ascended the throne and made him crown prince. As an adult, he was studious, broad-minded, and cautious. Once, when summoned urgently by his father, he avoided crossing the emperor’s road, taking a detour instead, which pleased Emperor Yuan, who then allowed him to cross. Despite later concerns over his drinking and pleasure-seeking, Emperor Yuan considered deposing him in favor of Prince Tao Gong, but was dissuaded by Shi Xian and the memory of Emperor Xuan’s affection. Upon Emperor Yuan’s death in the first year of Jingning, the prince ascended the throne, honoring his mother and grandmother as empress dowagers. He appointed his uncle Wang Feng as Grand Marshal and Grand General, overseeing secretarial affairs. He agreed to stop burying chariots and animals with the dead, granted a general amnesty, and faced various omens: a fire in the ancestral temple, a comet, and a storm that killed envoy Yao Yin. He rewarded officials and the people, issued an edict acknowledging his faults, and promoted tolerance. He granted titles to his uncles and faced natural phenomena like yellow mist, swarms of flies, and a shooting star.

translation:
The people were exhausted, and the soil brought from other places to build the mausoleum was loose and messy, making it difficult to build Changling mausoleum.
I feel sad when I think of the project that wastes so much money and people.
The ancients said that if you don't correct your mistakes, small mistakes will become big mistakes.
It is now decided to stop the construction of Changling, and the five thousand households that were originally scheduled to move to Changling will no longer move, so that the world will not have the wavering heart to leave their hometown.
Prince Liu Li of Chengyang was made king.
On August 19, the Empress Dowager Wang passed away.
On the third day of the first lunar month of the second year of spring, Wang Yin, the general of the Great Sima Chariot, passed away.
On February 28th, stars fell like rain.
On the 30th, there was a partial eclipse of the sun.
The edict was issued saying: Not long ago, the dragon appeared in Donglai, and there was a partial eclipse of the sun. The sky showed changes to show my fault, and I was deeply frightened.
The ministers should tell their officials to seriously consider the warnings shown by heaven. Opinions on how to reduce taxes and levies for the convenience of the people can be reported one by one.
Money and food loaned to the poor will be exempted.
He also said: The harvest in Guandong has been poor for several years, and some officials and people gave food to the poor out of righteousness, or donated grain to help the county magistrates provide relief, and the officials should pay back the money according to the price. For those with a number of more than one million, they will be given a title of right rank. If they have already paid 300 shi for an official, they will be promoted to the second level.
If the number is more than 300,000, they will be given the rank of five officials, the officials who were already officials will be promoted to the second level, and the ordinary people will be supplemented by the rank of Langguan.
Those with a number of more than 100,000 will be exempted from rent for three years.
Those with more than 10,000 yuan will be exempted from rent for one year.
In the eleventh month of winter, I came to Yongdi and offered sacrifices to the five emperors.
In December, an edict was issued saying: General Xie Wannian, who had been a master craftsman for ten thousand years, knew that the terrain of Changling was low and could not be used as the emperor's mausoleum, but he petitioned to build a mausoleum here and build a city to support the mausoleum. He acted cunningly and deceitfully, transporting earth from other places to raise the foundation, wasting money and manpower, rushing to get started, and eager for success, so that the soldiers who participated in the construction were tortured and caused a large number of deaths.
The people were extremely tired and the treasury was depleted. Wang Hong, the constant servant, was the chief minister of Nongzhongcheng before. He reported many times that Changling could not be built.
Lieutenant Chun Yuchang suggested several times that the construction should be stopped as soon as possible and the relocated households should be returned to their original places.
Because of Chunyu Chang's suggestion, I sent Wang Hong's memorial to the ministers for discussion. After discussion, the ministers agreed with Chunyuchang.
Chunyu took the initiative to establish the correct strategy, and Wang Hong took charge of money, grain and employment to reduce losses and waste, so that the people could live in peace and prosperity.
I have previously given Wang Hongjue the title of Marquis of Guannei and a hundred catties of gold.
Chunyu is now granted the title of Marquis of Guannei by Changjue, with a settlement of 1,000 households and Wang Hong of 500 households.
summary: In subsequent years, he conducted suburban sacrifices, established Queen Xu, and dealt with droughts, floods, and rebellions. He reduced taxes, pardoned prisoners, and encouraged agriculture. He faced earthquakes, solar eclipses, and a comet, issuing edicts to seek advice and reform. He moved wealthy households to Changling, deposed Queen Xu, and suppressed uprisings like Zheng Gong’s rebellion. He stopped the costly Changling project, punished the architect Xie Wannian, and rewarded those who advised against it. He continued to face disasters, including fires and floods, and issued edicts against extravagance.

translation:
The edict also said: I have heard that the king must preserve the descendants of the two kings of the previous dynasty, together with the current king himself, to symbolize the three unities of heaven, earth and man.
In the past, King Tang of Shang founded the country as emperor and listed the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, but later the sacrifices were abolished.
According to the current examination of his descendants, only Kong Ji is the righteous one, and Kong Ji is specially named the Jiahou of Yin Shao.
In the third month, Jijue of Jin Kong was made a duke, and Tong and Zhou Chengxiu were both dukes, with jurisdiction over hundreds of miles each.
He came to Yongdi and offered sacrifices to the five emperors.
In the fourth month of summer, the General Hussars of the Great Sima was appointed as the Great Sima, and the general officer was dismissed.
The imperial censor was named Da Sikong and was granted the title of Liehou.
With the increase of Da Sima, Da Sikong's salary is the same as that of the Prime Minister.
On the ninth day of the eighth lunar month in autumn, Liu Xing, king of Zhongshan, passed away.
In the eleventh month of winter, Liu Jing, the grandson of King Xiao of Chu, was appointed King of Dingtao.
Chunyu, the Marquis of Dingling, grew up disobedient and was sentenced to death in prison.
Tingwei Kong Guang gave poisonous wine to the deposed queen Xu as an envoy, and he died after drinking the wine.
In December, he dismissed the governor of the Ministry and established the state pastoral office, with a salary of 2,000 shi.
On February 13th, Prime Minister Zhai Fangjin passed away.
On March 18, Emperor Cheng died in Weiyang Palace.
The Empress Dowager ordered relevant agencies to restore the northern and southern suburbs of Chang'an.
On April 11, he was buried in Yanling.
Ban Gu commented: Chen's aunt served as Jieyu in Emperor Cheng's harem. When the father and son brothers received and served her, she told me many times that Emperor Cheng paid great attention to appearance. Get on the car and stand upright, sit upright and look forward, calmly, not gesticulating, and solemn and deep before the court, like a god, which can be called the appearance of Emperor Mu Mu!
Be knowledgeable about the past and understand the present, and adopt straightforward opinions.
The public officials are competent, their memorials are of impressive literary talent, and in times of peace and prosperity, there is harmony between the upper and lower levels.
However, because they indulged in drinking and sex, Sister Zhao Feiyan was in trouble in the inner palace, and the Wang family's relatives were specialized in government affairs, which is sighing to say.
Since the founding era, the Wang family has begun to control the state. Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping did not reign for long, and Wang Mang was able to usurp the throne. Probably the power of the Wang family gradually formed from the time he became emperor.
summary: He appointed Liu Xin of Dingtao as crown prince, granted titles to descendants of previous dynasties, and reorganized offices. He died in Weiyang Palace and was buried in Yanling. Ban Gu noted his dignified appearance, knowledge, and eloquence, but lamented his indulgence in drink and women, leading to the rise of the Wang family and Wang Mang’s eventual usurpation.

translation:
Emperor Xiaowen was the fourth son of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, and his mother was Bo Ji.
In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Chen Xi was executed and the Dai territory was pacified. He made him the Dai king and made his capital Zhongdu.
In the autumn of the seventeenth year of King Dai's reign, Empress Lu passed away, and Zhu Lu planned a coup to seize Liu Han's power.
Prime Minister Chen Ping, Taiwei Zhou Bo, Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang and others jointly killed the Lu family and discussed the appointment of the acting king Liu Heng as the emperor.
The historical events are recorded in "Book of Han·Gao Hou Ji and Gao Wu Wang Biography".
The ministers sent people to greet the king.
After deliberation, Zhang Wu, the king's lieutenant, said: The ministers of the Han Dynasty are all veteran generals from the time of Emperor Gao. They are familiar with military affairs and well versed in intrigues and tricks. In their hearts, they are not satisfied with their current status. They are just afraid of the majesty of Emperor Gao and Empress Lu.
Now that Zhu Lu has been executed and blood has been spilled in the capital, it is unbelievable to welcome the king to the capital in the name of proclaiming himself emperor.
I hope your Majesty will not go there on the grounds of illness, so as to observe changes in the situation.
Lieutenant Song Chang added: Their comments are wrong.
The Qin Dynasty was in disarray, heroes arose, and there were no less than ten thousand people who wanted to replace the Qin Dynasty and claim the title of emperor in the south. However, in the end, only the Liu family was able to rule the world. People in the world who harbored evil thoughts were desperate. This was one of them.
Emperor Gao made his children kings, and the fiefdoms were intertwined. This became a rock-like core. The world obeyed Liu Han's strength. This was the second one.
The establishment of the Han Dynasty abolished the harshness of the Qin Dynasty, reduced punishments, extended kindness and benefits, and made everyone feel at ease, which won the hearts of the people.
With the majesty of the Empress Dowager Lu, she established Zhu Lu as the three kings and was good at despotic power. However, the Taiwei Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army with a talisman and called on the soldiers to support the Liu family and oppose Zhu Lu. As a result, the Lu family was wiped out.
This shows that Liu Han's regime was given by heaven and could not be changed by a few manpower.
Nowadays, although some ministers want to launch a coup, the people are unwilling to listen to them. Can they achieve their goals by relying on a small number of his party members?
Inside Kyoto, there is the unity of Zhu Xuhou and Dongmuhou, and outside there are the powers of Wu, Chu, Huainan, Langwangya, Qi and Dai.
Nowadays, the only sons of Emperor Gao are the King of Huainan and you, the king. The king lives long, is a sage, benevolent and filial, and is famous all over the world. Therefore, the ministers in the court obey the wishes of the people and want to welcome the king, so the king does not have to worry.
Reporting to the Queen Mother on behalf of the king, it was difficult to make a decision for a while.
Then he asked someone to divine, and he got a great omen. The fortune teller said: Great, Gengen, I am the king of heaven, Xia Qiguang Zong Yaozu.
Dai Wang said: I am already a king, so why do I need to add a king's title?
The diviner said: The so-called king of heaven in the hexagram is the emperor!
summary: Emperor Xiaowen, the fourth son of Emperor Gaozu of Han, was made King of Dai after the execution of Chen Xi. Following Empress Lu’s death, the Lu clan plotted to seize power but were killed by ministers Chen Ping, Zhou Bo, and others, who then decided to welcome King Dai as emperor. King Dai hesitated, with advisor Zhang Wu warning that the ministers were veteran generals skilled in intrigue and might not be trustworthy. However, Song Chang argued that the Han dynasty’s stability, the people’s loyalty to Liu, and the failure of the Lu clan’s usurpation proved divine support for Liu rule. After divination yielded a favorable omen, King Dai sent Bo Zhao to verify the ministers’ intentions. Zhou Bo confirmed their sincerity, and King Dai proceeded to Chang’an. At Weiqiao, Zhou Bo offered the imperial seal, but King Dai declined, insisting on discussing the matter at the palace. The ministers formally petitioned him to accept the throne, citing his lineage as Emperor Gaozu’s son. After three refusals, he agreed and became emperor.

translation:
If I do not elect virtuous people today, but say that I must establish a prince, people will think that I have forgotten the virtuous people and only want my son to succeed me. This is not really caring about world affairs, and I really do not want to adopt it.
Relevant officials repeatedly requested: In ancient times, Yin and Zhou conquered the world and enjoyed long-lasting peace and stability for nearly a thousand years. In the past, no one in the world could pass on the throne as long as the Yin and Zhou Dynasties. This is because both Yin and Zhou adopted the method of passing on the crown prince.
The crown prince must be the son of the emperor. This has always been the case in history.
Emperor Gao began to pacify the world, establish princes, and became the ancestor of Emperor Liu Han.
The princes, princes, and princes who began to receive feudal states also became the ancestors of the feudal states.
Succession by descendants from generation to generation is a universal justice.
Therefore, Emperor Gaozu established a prince to stabilize the world.
It was not Emperor Gao's original intention to give up on the task of establishing a son as prince today and instead choose him from among the princes and clans.
It would be inappropriate to elect another person.
Prince Qi is the eldest son, kind and generous, so he asks the emperor to make him the crown prince.
The emperor finally agreed.
Therefore, the people of the world should be given the title of nobility as their father's heirs.
General Bo Zhao was granted the title of Marquis of Zhi.
In March, the relevant officials asked for the establishment of a queen, and the Empress Dowager said: Make Dou, the mother of the crown prince, the queen.
Emperor Wen issued an edict saying: When the spring breeze is gentle, flying animals, plants and other things have the joy of revival. However, the widowed, lonely and poor among our people may be struggling on the edge of death without receiving care and warmth. How can we, as parents of the people, feel at ease?
Relief should be discussed.
The edict also said: The old man will not be warm if he does not wear a cotton-padded jacket, and he will not be full if he does not eat meat.
In the early spring of this year, people were often sent to visit the elders. If they were not given some cloth, wine and meat, how could they help the descendants of the world to be filial and support their relatives?
I once heard that some officials gave old millets and rotten rice when distributing pension grains. Can this be said to be implementing the edict of providing pensions for the elderly?
The regulations will now be formulated in detail.
Relevant officials notified all counties and roads that those over eighty years of age would be given one stone of rice, twenty catties of meat, and five measures of wine per month.
For those who are over ninety years old, there will be an additional two pounds of silk and three pounds of catkins per person.
When giving gifts and pensions to elderly people over ninety years old, the county magistrate must personally supervise and inspect them, and the county magistrate or county lieutenant must personally deliver them.
Those who are less than 90 years old will be handed over by agricultural officials and regents.
High-ranking officials should send virtuous officials to patrol and inspect, and those who do not implement the edicts should be investigated and punished.
Elderly persons who have been sentenced and whose crimes will result in a sentence of more than two years are not subject to this order.
Liu Jiao, king of Chu Yuan, passed away.
In April, there was an earthquake in Qi and Chu. On the same day, twenty-nine mountains collapsed and floods surged.
In June, the county was ordered not to present property to the court.
summary: Upon ascending the throne, Emperor Wen issued a general amnesty, rewarded those who had suppressed the Lu clan, and restored lands taken by the Lu family. He abolished the Qin law of collective punishment. When officials urged him to appoint a crown prince, he initially declined, citing his own unworthiness and suggesting a virtuous successor from among his relatives or ministers. After repeated requests, he appointed his eldest son, Prince Qi, as crown prince. He also established his consort Dou as empress. The emperor implemented benevolent policies, including tax relief for farmers, care for the elderly, and pardons for minor offenses. He abolished the crime of slander and attempted treason, emphasizing the importance of agriculture and reducing government expenditures.

translation:
Stayed and visited Taiyuan for more than ten days.
When King Xingju of Jibei learned that the emperor had gone to Dai and planned to conquer the Xiongnu himself, he took advantage of the fact that there was no master in the court and launched a rebellion, dispatching troops and horses to attack Xingyang.
So he issued an edict to remove the prime minister Guan Ying from military power, and appointed Chai Wu, Marquis of Ji Pu, as the general. He led four brave generals and 100,000 troops to suppress the rebels.
Qihou Zanhe was made a general and sent reinforcements to Xingyang.
In the seventh month of autumn, the emperor went from Taiyuan to Chang'an and issued an edict saying: The king of Jibei betrayed the court and harmed the officials and people, and he was the chief culprit.
The officials and people in Jibei who planned to submit to the imperial court before the official troops arrived, or who submitted their army, city, or city to the official troops, would be pardoned and allowed to remain in office.
Those who are related to Wang Xingju of Jibei will also be pardoned.
In August, he captured Xingju, the king of Jibei, and Xingju committed suicide.
Those who participated in the Xingju rebellion were pardoned.
In the winter of December of the fourth year of Emperor Wen's reign, Prime Minister Guan Ying passed away.
In the fifth month of summer, the Liu family of the same clan as Liu Han was exempted from taxes and servitude, and nothing was given to his family.
Grant the princes and princes food and towns to each of 2,000 households.
In the ninth month of autumn, seven princes named Hui Hui of Qi were made marquises.
Jianghou Zhou Bo was guilty and was imprisoned in Tianlao after his arrest.
The small and humble Gu Cheng Temple was built.
In the spring and February of the fifth year, there was an earthquake.
In April of summer, the order for stealing money was abolished and private coining was allowed.
The four-baht coin was re-minted.
In the winter of the sixth year, in October, the peaches and plums bloomed.
In November, the king of Huainan rebelled, deposed the throne and was exiled to Yandao, Shu. He died in Yongdi on the way.
In the winter and tenth month of the seventh year, it was ordered that the wives, wives, princes and officials of the princes and officials should not be searched without permission.
In the fourth month of summer, the world is forgiven.
On June 2, the Quequ Pavilion on the east side of Weiyang Palace caught fire.
In the summer of the eighth year, the four sons of King Li of Huainan were granted the title of marquis.
There is a long comet out of the east.
In the spring of the ninth year, there was a severe drought.
In the winter of ten years, I patrolled to Ganquan.
General Bo Zhao passed away.
In the winter of the eleventh year, in November, I came to Dai.
In the first month of spring, the emperor returned to the capital from Dai.
In June of Xia, King Liang Yi passed away.
The Huns invaded Didao.
In the winter of the twelfth year in December, the Yellow River broke out in Dongjun.
In the first month of spring, the princes, princes and daughters were given 2,000 households each in Tangmuyi.
In February, Emperor Xiaohui dismissed Gong'e from the harem and could get married on her own.
In March, the law requiring the presentation of documents for entry and exit was abolished.
The emperor issued an edict saying: The way to guide the people is to grasp the fundamentals of agriculture.
summary: During his reign, Emperor Wen faced challenges such as the rebellion of King Xingju of Jibei, which was swiftly suppressed, and conflicts with the Xiongnu, whom he managed through defense rather than costly campaigns. He promoted frugality, wearing simple clothes and forbidding lavish decorations. He also reformed the legal system, abolished corporal punishment, and encouraged the recommendation of virtuous officials. In his later years, he issued an edict on his deathbed, advocating simple funerals and urging the people not to mourn excessively. He was buried in Ba Ling with minimal ceremony, using earthenware vessels and no precious metals. Ban Gu praised Emperor Wen for his benevolence, noting that his reign saw prosperity, few imprisonments, and a flourishing of moral virtue.

translation:
Emperor Zhao of the Han Dynasty was the youngest son of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty.
The mother is Zhao Jieyu. She was favored because of her strange aura. When she gave birth to Emperor Zhao, there was also something strange about her.
In the last years of Emperor Wu, the violent prince Liu Ju was deposed. King Liu Dan of Yan and King Liu Xu of Guangling both behaved arrogantly. Emperor Wu fell seriously ill in February of the second year of the Yuan Dynasty, so he made Emperor Zhao the prince. He was eight years old at the time.
As a servant, Huo Guang, the captain of the chariot, was appointed as the general of the Sima army. He was ordered by Emperor Wu to assist the young master.
Emperor Wu died the next day, and on February 15th, the prince succeeded to the throne and paid homage to the great ancestor in the temple.
Princess Eyi, the sister of Emperor Zhao, was granted the title of Tang Muyi, honored as the eldest princess, and was enshrined in the palace.
The general Huo Guang presides over the state affairs and is in charge of the secretarial affairs. The chariot and cavalry general Jin Rixi and the left general Shangguan Jie are his deputy.
In the sixth month of summer, forgive all sinners in the world.
In autumn and July, a comet appears in the eastern sky.
Liu Kuan, the king of Jibei, was guilty and committed suicide.
The eldest princess and her clan brothers were given various rewards, and Zhao Jieyu was posthumously given the title of empress dowager, and a Yunyang mausoleum was built for her.
In winter, the Xiongnu invaded Shuofang, killing and plundering the officials and civilians.
The imperial court sent troops to garrison in Xihe, and left general Shangguan Jie inspected the northern border.
In the spring of February of the first year of the First Yuan Dynasty, yellow swans were perched in the Taiye Pond of Jianzhang Palace. The minister thought it was a symbol of auspiciousness and wished the emperor long life.
There are differences in the amount of money given to princes, princes, and clans.
On March 23, Emperor Zhao started farming in Goudun Field.
The king of Yan, the king of Guangling and the eldest princess of Eyi were granted 13,000 households each.
In summer, the Yunling Garden Temple was built for the Queen Mother.
The twenty-four cities of Liantou, Guzhen, and Zangke that belonged to Yizhou rebelled.
The imperial court sent Shuiheng Captain Lu Pohu to recruit officials and the elite soldiers from Jianwei and Shu counties and immediately went to the front line of Yizhou to defeat the rebels.
The competent administrative division department petitioned Hanoi to belong to Jizhou and Hedong to Bingzhou.
In the seventh month of autumn, a general amnesty will be given to the whole country, and every 100 households will be given one cow and wine.
It rained heavily and flash floods broke through the Wei Bridge.
In August, Liu Ze, the grandson of Prince Xiao of Qi, rebelled and intended to kill Jun Buyi, the governor of Qingzhou. He was discovered and executed.
There is no doubt that Sheng Yu is Jing Zhaoyin, and he will be rewarded with millions of dollars.
On September 2, the chariot general Jin Rishidan passed away.
In the intercalated tenth month, the imperial court sent five people, Wang Pingping and Wang Pingping, from the former court, to patrol the county and country with talisman festivals to inspect the virtuous and investigate the suffering of the people, unjust cases, dereliction of duty and other matters.
Winters are warm and free of ice.
In the first month of the spring of the second year, the general Huo Guang and the left general Shangguan Jie both captured and killed the rebels and reunited Hou Ma Tong with meritorious service. Huo Guang was the Marquis of Bolu, and Shangguan Jie was the Marquis of Anyang.
Among the clan members who were not in power, Liu Piqiang and Liu Changle were recommended as Guanglu officials, and Piqiang was recommended as Changle palace guard.
summary: Emperor Zhao of Han, youngest son of Emperor Wu, ascended the throne at age eight after his father’s death in 87 BCE. Huo Guang, appointed regent, managed state affairs with deputies Jin Rixi and Shangguan Jie. Early reign events included amnesties, a comet sighting, and Xiongnu raids repelled by garrisons. Auspicious signs like yellow swans prompted celebrations, while rebellions in Yizhou and by Liu Ze were suppressed. Reforms reduced taxes, exempted land rent, and provided relief to the poor. In 81 BCE, Emperor Zhao ended state monopolies on salt, iron, and wine after consulting virtuous scholars. Su Wu returned from 19 years of captivity among the Xiongnu and was rewarded.

translation:
On December 6, Prime Minister Wang Xin passed away.
In the spring and first month of the sixth year, prisoners from the county were recruited to build Xuantu City in Liaodong.
Xia, forgive the sinners in the world.
The edict was issued: "Generally, low prices of grain will hurt farmers. Now that grain prices have dropped in Sanfu and Taichang, various regions are specially ordered to use grain as tax payment."
The right general Zhang Anshi loyally and cautiously executed the guard and was granted the title of Marquis of Fuping.
Wuhuan once again invaded the border fortress and sent General Fan Mingyou, the general from Liao Dynasty, to lead the pursuit.
In the spring and February of the first year of Yuanping, Emperor Zhao issued an edict saying: The world is based on farming and mulberry.
In the past period, we have saved money, cut redundant personnel, and reduced additional taxes. As a result, the number of people engaged in farming has increased, but the people are still not self-sufficient. I am deeply disturbed.
It is now decided to reduce the oral tax payment.
Someone petitioned for a reduction of three-tenths, and the emperor agreed.
On February 17, there was a meteor in the morning, as big as the moon, and the stars followed the meteor westward.
On April 17th in the summer, Emperor Zhao died in Weiyang Palace.
On June 7, he was buried in Pingling.
Ban Gu commented: In the past, King Cheng of Zhou inherited the throne with a young son, but there were rumors from Guan and Cai, slandering the Duke of Zhou who served as regent and assisted the young master.
When Emperor Zhao succeeded to the throne at a young age, Yan, Yong, and Shangguan also conspired to rebel and slander Huo Guang, who was regent and assistant to the young emperor.
King Cheng did not doubt Duke Zhou, and Emperor Zhao appointed Huo Guang. It is remarkable that both monarchs and ministers can become famous in their own time!
After Emperor Zhao succeeded Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, he was very happy with his achievements and went on a military expedition. The domestic economy was in depression and the population was reduced by half. However, Huo Guangneng focused on the most urgent tasks, did light corvees and low taxes, and rested with the people.
During the Shiyuan and Yuanfeng years, the country made peace with the Xiongnu on the outside and enriched the people on the inside.
He also recommended virtuous literature, inquired about the sufferings of the people, stopped selling salt, iron and wine, and did not compete with the people for profit. His posthumous title was Zhao, which is very appropriate!
summary: In 80 BCE, a major conspiracy involving King Liu Dan of Yan, Princess Eyi, Shangguan Jie, and others to assassinate Huo Guang was foiled. Emperor Zhao, then 14, exposed the plot, leading to executions of the conspirators. Huo Guang’s loyalty was vindicated, and he continued as regent. Subsequent years saw further reforms: tax reductions, amnesties, and agricultural support. Emperor Zhao died in 74 BCE at age 21, buried in Pingling. Ban Gu praised his reign for restoring stability after Emperor Wu’s costly campaigns, implementing light corvée and low taxes, and fostering peace with the Xiongnu while enriching the people.

translation:
Emperor Jing of Han was the prince of Emperor Wen of Han.
His mother is Queen Dou.
In June of the seventh year of the Second Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Wen died.
On June 9, the prince succeeded to the throne and honored the empress dowager Bo as the empress dowager, and the empress dowager Dou as the empress dowager.
In September, a comet appeared in the west.
In the winter and tenth month of the first year of Emperor Jingdi's reign, the emperor issued an edict saying: I have often heard that in ancient times, the ancestors who conquered the world had merit, and the ancestors who governed the world had virtue, and rituals and music had their own origins.
Singing is used to praise great virtues; dancing is used to express achievements.
Offer sacrifices to Emperor Gaozu in the temple and perform the dances of "Wude", "Wen Shi" and "Five Elements".
Offer sacrifices to Emperor Hui in the temple and perform the dances of "Wen Shi" and "Five Elements".
Emperor Wen reigned over the world, and his government was harmonious, far and near; he eliminated the crime of slandering the emperor, stopped corporal punishment, rewarded the elderly and virtuous, comforted the lonely and helpless, and fulfilled the wishes of his subjects as much as possible; he controlled his hobbies and desires, did not accept donations, did not implicate the wife and children of sinners, did not let innocent people suffer injustice, was strict with himself, and enforced the law impartially; abolished palace punishment, and repatriated beauties in the palace to avoid having no heirs.
I am stupid by nature, and I still don’t know all about my father’s merits.
Only the above points were failed to be implemented by the ancient sage emperors and sage kings, but Emperor Wen implemented them all.
It can be said that great virtues are matched in heaven and earth, blessings are spread all over the world, and everyone is blessed.
Its holy brightness is like the sun and menstruation in the sky, but the music and dance of the sacrifice do not match it. I am deeply disturbed.
For this reason, the "Zhao De" dance should be performed for Emperor Wen's temple to highlight his virtues.
In this way, the merits of our ancestors can be passed down to all generations and will last forever, and I will be infinitely happy.
I hope that the prime minister, the princes, Zhong Erqianshi, and the etiquette officials will propose specific etiquette plans.
Prime Minister Shen Tujia and others said: Your Majesty always thinks of filial piety, and performs the dance of virtue to show the virtue of Emperor Xiaowen, which is beyond the understanding of the ministers.
I would like to discuss this: There is no one who was more successful in founding the country than Emperor Gao, and no one was more benevolent and virtuous than Emperor Wen.
Therefore, the Emperor Gao Temple should be the Taizu Temple of the Emperor's family, and the Emperor Wen Temple should be the Taizong Temple of the Emperor's family.
The emperors of the Han Dynasty should pay homage to their ancestors from generation to generation.
The princes of the prefecture and state should each establish a temple for Emperor Wen of Taizong.
The princes and princes sent envoys to Kyoto to offer sacrifices at the ancestral temple. Please announce it to the world.
Emperor Jing agreed.
The first month of spring. The edict was issued: "In recent years, the situation has been bad. Many people are short of food, and some have died of hunger. I deeply regret it."
Some counties have barren land and cannot develop farming; others have vast land, deep pastures, and excellent water conservancy conditions, but cannot be developed by immigrants.
summary: Emperor Jing of Han, son of Emperor Wen and Queen Dou, ascended the throne on June 9 after his father's death in the seventh year of the Second Yuan Dynasty. He honored Empress Dowager Bo and Empress Dowager Dou. In his first year, he issued an edict praising Emperor Wen's virtues—abolishing slander laws, corporal punishment, and palace punishment; rewarding the elderly; and repatriating palace women. He ordered the "Zhao De" dance for Emperor Wen's temple. Prime Minister Shen Tujia proposed establishing Emperor Gao's temple as Taizu and Emperor Wen's as Taizong, with perpetual ancestral worship, which Emperor Jing approved.

translation:
To this end, people in areas with infertile soil can be encouraged to move freely to areas with vast and fertile land. In the fourth month of summer, a general amnesty was granted to all the people, and the people were granted a first-level title.
Qing Zhai, the imperial censor, was sent to Daixia to make peace with the Huns.
In May, an order was issued to reduce the rent of farmland by half.
In the seventh month of Autumn, an edict was issued saying: The current law punishes officials in charge of being dismissed from their posts for accepting banquets from subordinates, while the punishment for accepting property, buying cheap and selling high to make huge profits is too light.
Wang Tingwei and the Prime Minister re-formulated the regulations.
Ting Weixin and Prime Minister Shen Tujia agreed on a new law as follows: Officials and civil servants and generals with noble rank who accept banquets from their subordinate organizations and individuals must repay the price according to the price and will not be punished.
Any items other than food and drink that are purchased at a lower price or sold at a higher price by taking advantage of one's authority will be investigated as stolen goods and confiscated to the official.
When officials are transferred or dismissed, if they accept gifts of property from their original subordinates, their titles will be removed and they will be dismissed.
Those who do not have a title will be fined two catties and their property will be confiscated.
Those who can report will be rewarded with the stolen goods they did not receive.
In the winter of December of the second year of Emperor Jing's reign, a comet appeared in the southwest.
It is ordered that all men over the age of 20 can serve as assistant officials.
In the third month of spring, Prince De was named King of Hejian, Prince Yan was named King of Linjiang, Prince Yu was named King of Huaiyang, Prince Fei was named King of Runan, Prince Pengzu was named King of Guangchuan, and Prince Fa was named King of Changsha.
On the 25th of April in the summer, the Empress Dowager passed away.
In June, Prime Minister Shen Tujia passed away.
Xiao Xi, the grandson of Xiao He, the former prime minister, was made a lord.
In autumn, he made peace with the Xiongnu.
In the twelfth month of the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, he issued an edict saying: Hui, the son of Marquis Ji Jia of Xiangping, said he was unfilial, attempted rebellion, and wanted to kill Jia, which was actually a great treason.
Ji Jia is now pardoned and remains the Marquis of Xiangping. All those whose wives should have been seated according to the law are restored to their original rank, while Huishuo and his wife are executed.
In the first month of spring, a fire broke out in the main hall of Huaiyang Palace.
King Liu Bi of Wu, King Liu Xian of Jiaoxi, King Liu Wu of Chu, King Liu Sui of Zhao, King Liu Biguang of Jinan, King Liu Xian of Zichuan, and King Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong jointly raised troops to rebel.
Emperor Jing ordered a general amnesty for the whole country.
He sent Taiwei Zhou Yafu and General Dou Ying to lead the expedition.
Chao Cuo, the imperial censor, suggested cutting down the vassal vassal to avoid being too powerful to appease the seven kingdoms that launched a rebellion.
On the first day of February, there was a partial solar eclipse.
The soldiers commanded by Zhou Yafu and Dou Ying defeated the rebels of the Seven Kingdoms and beheaded more than 100,000 people.
Chasing and killing Wu Wang Biyu Dan Tu.
summary: In subsequent years, Emperor Jing addressed food shortages by encouraging migration to fertile lands, granted amnesties, reduced farmland rent by half, and reformed laws on official bribery and gift acceptance. Comets appeared, and the Empress Dowager died in 144 BC. The Seven Kingdoms rebellion led by Liu Bi of Wu and others erupted; Emperor Jing sent Zhou Yafu and Dou Ying to suppress it, resulting in over 100,000 rebel deaths and the suicides of the rebel kings. He pardoned deceived officials and civilians.

translation:
The officials are now ordered to perform their duties. Anyone who neglects his duties or derelicts in his duties and harms the people shall be reported to the Prime Minister and punished.
I hereby announce it to the world so that my intentions are known to all.
In May, an edict was issued saying: Don't worry about someone being unwise, what you need to worry about is that he is cheating; don't worry about someone not being brave, what you need to worry about is that he is violent and violent; don't worry about someone not being rich, what you need to worry about is that he is unjust and greedy.
Only honest people are indifferent and content, and their desires are easily satisfied.
It was originally stipulated that a person with assets of 100,000 yuan could be an official, but this should not be required for honest people.
According to the original regulations, businessmen cannot become officials if they have money, and honest people cannot become officials if they have no money. This leads to the fact that honest people have no way to advance, which I feel very sorry for.
It is now decreed that those with assets of forty thousand yuan can become officials, so as not to prevent honest people from being able to hold their positions and allow greedy men to occupy their positions for a long time.
Autumn, severe drought.
In the first month of spring in the third year of the Yuan Dynasty, an edict was issued saying: Agriculture is the foundation of the world.
Gold, pearls and jade cannot be eaten when hungry or clothed when cold. They can be used with currency to communicate whether they are available or not, but they cannot be identified and used.
Sometimes the harvest is not good this year. I think it is because there are too many people engaged in business and too few people engaged in agriculture.
Now the special order of the county must encourage farmers to engage in mulberry farming and plant more trees, so that they can have enough food and clothing.
If an official uses his property to hire people to mine gold, pearls and jade, he will be punished as stolen goods.
Anyone who fails to investigate this matter will be guilty of the same crime.
The crown prince performs a crowning ceremony and rewards the common people who are his father's heirs with a title of one rank.
On the 27th of the first lunar month, Emperor Jing died in Weiyang Palace.
The imperial edict granted eight horses to each prince and prince. An official's two thousand shi means two catties of gold, and other officials and citizens each have a hundred coins.
The palace servants were dismissed and returned to their homes, exempted from lifelong corvee service.
On February 6, he was buried in Yangling.
Ban Gu commented: Confucius said that people today can also walk on the straight path like they did in the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties. This is quite correct.
The shortcomings of Zhou and Qin were that the legal network was tight and the laws were strict, but there were still countless people who broke the law and committed crimes.
The rise of the Han Dynasty eliminated the burdens and allowed the people to recuperate and recuperate.
As for Emperor Wen of the Han Dynasty, he was respectful and frugal, and Emperor Jing followed his previous footsteps. Within fifty or sixty years, he was able to change customs and make the people simple.
The Zhou Dynasty praised Chengkang, and the Han Dynasty praised Wenjing. What a beautiful and prosperous age!
summary: He appointed princes, resumed checkpoint inspections, made Liu Rong crown prince (later deposed), and Liu Che crown prince. He reformed mourning rites for princes, changed execution methods, and renamed officials. He prohibited tall horses from leaving the empire, faced locust plagues, and built Yangling. He issued edicts against bribery and harsh judgments, reformed official attire, and reduced whipping penalties. The Xiongnu invaded, and Zhou Yafu died in prison. He abolished the rule requiring princes to visit fiefs, promoted agriculture, and allowed those with 40,000 yuan assets to become officials. Emperor Jing died in Weiyang Palace in the first month of the third year of Houyuan, was buried in Yangling, and was praised by Ban Gu for continuing Emperor Wen's frugal policies, leading to a prosperous era comparable to the Zhou dynasty's Chengkang period.

translation:
Emperor Xiaowu Liu Che was the second son of Emperor Jing. His mother was Wang Meiren, who was made King of Jiaodong when she was four years old.
At the age of seven, he was made crown prince, and his mother was made queen.
At the age of sixteen, in the first month of the third year after Emperor Jing, Emperor Jing died.
On the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month, the prince succeeded to the throne of the emperor, and the empress dowager Dou was honored as the empress dowager, and the empress was the empress dowager.
In March, the Empress Dowager and her brothers Tian Chongfen and Tian Sheng were made marquises.
In the tenth month of the winter of the first year of Jianyuan, the prime minister, censors, princes, and princes were ordered to recommend virtuous and upright people who can give the most honest advice.
Prime Minister Wei Wan reported: If any of the recommended virtuous people make remarks about Shen Buhai, Shang Yang, Han Fei, Su Qin, or Zhang Yi, which would confuse the state affairs, please stop them.
The emperor agreed.
In the second month of spring, the world will be pardoned and the people will be rewarded with one level of nobility.
Those who are over eighty years old are exempted from taxes for two members of the family, and those who are over ninety years old are exempted from taxes for the whole family.
Issue three baht coins.
On the ninth day of April in the summer of the first year of Jianyuan, an edict was issued saying: According to the ancient rules, age is the most important thing in the countryside, and title is the most important thing in the court. In governing the country and educating the people, virtue must be given a prominent position.
It can be said that respecting the elders and caring for the elderly in the countryside has been a principle since ancient times.
Today, filial sons and grandsons in the world are willing to do their best to support their elders. However, they are forced by external affairs and lack of financial resources internally. Therefore, it seems that filial piety is missing. I deeply sympathize with them.
When people are over ninety years old, the court has a system of making porridge and rice with rice and millet. Now it is added that his sons or grandsons are exempted from corvee service, so that they can lead their wives to fulfill their responsibility of supporting the elderly.
In the fifth month, an edict was issued saying: The rivers and seas moisten thousands of miles, and the ancestral officials can be ordered to build ancestral temples in the mountains and rivers. It is normal to offer sacrifices every year, and the sacrifices should also be improved.
The first offender in the Seven Kingdoms Rebellion was pardoned for his crime of confiscating his wife as a servant of the official family, and was deported.
In the seventh month of Autumn, an edict was issued saying: The palace guards will go to the old place to set up a new one, numbering 20,000, and save 10,000.
The court's horse-breeding gardens were opened to the poor to graze and collect wood.
It was agreed to establish a Mingtang where the emperor declared his political and religious affairs.
An envoy was sent to summon Lu Shen Gong in a safe and comfortable vehicle with cloth and jade.
In the winter of October of the second year, Zhao Wan, the imperial censor, committed the crime of not reporting to the Empress Dowager. He and his doctor ordered Wang Zang to be imprisoned and committed suicide.
Prime Minister Dou Ying and Taiwei Tian Chong were dismissed from their posts.
On the first day of February in spring, there is a partial solar eclipse. On April 24th in summer, the night was like day.
The establishment of Maoling-eup began.
summary: Emperor Xiaowu Liu Che, the second son of Emperor Jing, was born to Wang Meiren. At age four, he was made King of Jiaodong, and at seven, he became crown prince. At sixteen, in the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, his father died, and Liu Che succeeded the throne. He honored Empress Dowager Dou and his mother as empress dowagers, and granted marquis titles to his maternal uncles. In the first year of Jianyuan, he ordered officials to recommend virtuous and upright individuals, but Prime Minister Wei Wan advised against promoting those who studied Legalist or strategist philosophies, which the emperor approved. He pardoned the world, rewarded the people, exempted taxes for the elderly, and issued three-baht coins. Edicts emphasized respect for elders, exempted families of those over ninety from corvée, and improved sacrifices to rivers and seas. He pardoned first offenders in the Seven Kingdoms Rebellion, reduced palace guards, opened horse-breeding gardens to the poor, and planned to build a Mingtang. He summoned the scholar Lu Shen Gong.

translation:
In the spring of the third year, the Yellow River flooded the plains, causing a great famine and causing people to eat each other.
The residents who moved to Maoling were given 200,000 yuan and two hectares of land.
Build the Benmen Bridge across the Weishui River from Chang'an to Maoling.
In autumn and July, a comet appears in the northwest.
King Liu Ming of Jichuan committed the crime of killing Taifu and Zhongfu and was deposed and moved to Fangling.
The Fujian and Yue soldiers besieged Dong Ou, and Dong Ou asked the Han court for help. The emperor sent Yan, a senior official, to assist him and mobilize the troops stationed in Kuaiji to float to the sea to rescue Dong Ou. Before the soldiers arrived, Minyue retreated. September 2nd, partial solar eclipse. In the summer of the fourth year, a wind blew up the red dust, which was as red as blood.
In June, there was a severe drought, and in autumn and September, comets appeared in the northeast.
In the spring of the fifth year, three baht coins were abolished and half a liang coin was issued.
Set up Doctor of the Five Classics.
In April of summer, the emperor's grandmother Pingyuan Jun passed away.
In May, a major locust plague occurred.
In the eighth month of autumn, King Liu Yue of Guangchuan and King Liu Cheng of Qinghe both died.
On the third day of February in the sixth year of spring, there was a fire in the Gaozu Temple in Liaodong.
On April 21st in the summer, a fire broke out in the Gaoyuan Bedroom.
The emperor wore plain clothes and blamed himself for five days.
On May 26, the Empress Dowager passed away.
In autumn and August, the comet appears in the east for a long time.
When King Ying of Minyue attacked South Vietnam, the imperial court sent Daxing Wang Hui to lead troops out of Yuzhang, and Da Sinong Han Anguo to lead troops out of Kuaiji to prepare for a counterattack. Before the soldiers arrived, the Yue people killed Ying and surrendered. Wang, Han and others withdrew their troops.
In the winter and November of the first year of Yuanguang, the county began to recommend one person each for Xiao and Lian.
