In the winter of the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, in December, Han soldiers surrounded Xiang Yu at Gaixia.
Xiang Yu heard Chu troops on all sides at night and knew that the Han soldiers had completely controlled the positions around the Chu troops, so he led hundreds of cavalry to abandon the camp and break out. The Chu troops were defeated because they had no master.
Guan Ying pursued Xiang Yu in Dongcheng.
The land of Chu was completely pacified, but the land of Lu did not surrender.
The King of Han led his army to massacre the city, but was moved by the local soldiers' actions to uphold Xiang Yu's integrity, so he stopped the attack and displayed Xiang Yu's head to inform Lu's father and brother, who surrendered.
Originally, King Huai made Xiang Yu the Duke of Lu. After Xiang Yu's death, the land of Lu defended him, so Xiang Yu was buried in Gucheng, Jibei with the ceremony of Duke Lu.
The King of Han mourned for Xiang Yu and went to mourn for him.
The king of Han made Xiang Bo and four other marquises and gave them the surname Liu.
People from other places who were plundered and brought to Chu were all sent back to their place of origin.
The King of Han returned to Dingtao, entered Han Xin's camp with lightning speed, and deprived Han Xin of his military power.
Gong Ao, the king of Linjiang who was originally established by Xiang Yu, died, and his son Wei succeeded him as king and refused to surrender.
The king of Han sent Lu Wan and Liu Jia to conquer Linjiang Wangwei.
In the spring and first month of the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, the king of Han honored his brother Liu Bo as the Marquis of Wu Ai.
The order was given: The Chu region has been pacified, and the Righteous Emperor has no descendants. In order to appease the people of the Chu region, he decided to appoint another master of the Chu region.
King Han Xin of Qi understood the customs and customs of the Chu land, and now he was appointed King of Chu. He governed the Huaibei region, with his capital at Xiapi.
Peng Yue, the Marquis of Wei Xiangguo who founded the city, cared about the people of Wei and loved the soldiers. He often defeated the Chu army with a small number and defeated the Chu army several times. He gave the old land of Wei as his fiefdom and named it King of Liang. He was all in Dingtao.
summary: In the winter of the fifth year, the King of Han pursued Xiang Yu but his allies Han Xin and Peng Yue failed to meet as scheduled. Xiang Yu defeated the Han forces, forcing the king to retreat and fortify his position. Following Zhang Liang's advice to share conquered territories, the king promised Han Xin the lands east of Chen to the Bohai Sea and Peng Yue the area north of Suiyang to Gucheng. Both then joined forces. Liu Jia invaded Chu, and Zhou Yin surrendered. In December, Han forces surrounded Xiang Yu at Gaixia. Hearing Chu songs on all sides, Xiang Yu fled with cavalry and was pursued to Dongcheng. The Chu lands were pacified, though Lu initially refused to surrender until shown Xiang Yu's head. Xiang Yu was buried with the rites of Duke of Lu.

translation:
He also said in the order: The war has lasted for eight years, causing serious disasters to the people. Today, the world has been unified and stable. All prisoners except those sentenced to death will be pardoned.
At this time, the princes reported to the King of Han: King Han Xin of Chu, King Xin of Han, King Yingbu of Huainan, King Pengyue of Liang, Wu Rui, the former King of Hengshan, King Zhang Ao of Zhao, and King Zang Tu of Yan wrote in fear of risking their lives, Your Majesty: In the past, the Qin Dynasty was unjust, and gods and men worked together to punish it.
The king first captured Prince Ying of Qin and pacified Guanzhong, and his contribution was overwhelming to the world.
Determination of life and death, continuous rescue of defeat, in order to stabilize the people, the merits are high and virtuous.
At the same time, he also extended favors to various meritorious princes and divided them into feudal states.
Now that the fiefdoms and titles of the princes and princes have been determined, and they share the title of king with the king, there is no distinction between them. In this way, the king's outstanding achievements and virtues cannot be announced to future generations.
Therefore, I risked my life and asked for the title of emperor.
The King of Han thanked him and said: "I often hear that the emperor's title belongs to the sages. A title that is not worthy of the name should not be obtained."
Today, all the princes and kings have elected me to be the emperor. How can I accept it?
All the princes and kings reported: The great king has risen among the people, wiped out the Qin Dynasty, and shocked the whole country.
Later, he used the remote areas of Bashu as a base to promote mighty virtue from Hanzhong, punish injustice, establish meritorious services, and pacify the sea. The meritorious officials were all given fiefs and food towns, and all were rewarded according to their merits.
The king's kindness is spread all over the world, and no other princes can compare with it. Respecting him as emperor is worthy of his name. May the king satisfy the wishes of the people in the world.
The King of Han said: If you princes say that it is beneficial for the people of the world for me to become emperor, then I will agree with it.
So all the princes and princes, the Marquis of Chang'an, Lu Wan, and three hundred other people, together with Dr. Ji Sijun, Shusun Tong, chose an auspicious day, the third day of the second lunar month, to give the emperor's title. The King of Han, the emperor, was located in Jiyin, north of the Sishui River.
Queen Lu was respected as the queen, the prince as the crown prince, and his deceased mother was posthumously named Mrs. Zhaoling.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty issued an edict saying: Wu Rui, the former king of Hengshan, his two sons and one nephew raised troops from the Baiyue area to support the princes, destroy the violent Qin Dynasty, and achieve great achievements. The princes made him king.
Later, Xiang Yu invaded his land and demoted him to Fanjun.
Now Changsha, Yuzhang, Xianglin, Guijun, Nanhai and other places are his fiefdoms, and Fanjun Wu Rui is made the king of Changsha.
The edict also said: The former king of Guangdong had inherited the sacrifices of Guangdong, but the Qin Dynasty took away his land, leaving no one to worship the ancestors of Guangdong.
The princes attacked Qin and killed all their relatives. They led the soldiers of Fujian to help destroy Qin's righteous move. Xiang Yu was deposed and did not stand.
Now I regard the deceased as the king of Fujian and Guangdong, and central Fujian will be placed under his jurisdiction without losing his old position.
The emperor of the Han Dynasty was the western capital of Luoyang.
summary: In the sixth year, the king honored his brother as Marquis of Wu Ai, appointed Han Xin as King of Chu, and made Peng Yue King of Liang. A general amnesty was declared except for capital crimes. The princes petitioned the king to accept the title of Emperor, which he initially declined but eventually accepted on an auspicious day in the second month. Queen Lu was honored as empress, the prince as crown prince. Wu Rui was made King of Changsha, and the former King of Guangdong was restored. The capital was established at Luoyang. Soldiers were demobilized, with exemptions from taxes for those in Guanzhong and those returning home. Former slaves were freed, and military officials were granted titles and lands according to merit.

translation:
The edict was issued saying: The world has been stabilized. Heroes with meritorious services have been granted the title of marquis and newly ascended to the throne of the emperor. However, not all of them have been rewarded according to their merits.
Because I have been in the military for nine years, some of them have no time to learn the laws, and some of them accidentally violate the national laws, and in serious cases they are sentenced to death. I deeply sympathize with them.
Now I plan to grant amnesty to the whole world.
Tian Ken expressed his congratulations and said: What the emperor saw is extremely true. Your Majesty took Han Xin into custody and established his capital in Guanzhong.
Qin is a place with a favorable situation, with the Yellow River as its belt, Guanshan Mountain as its danger, and thousands of miles away from the eastern princes. Qin's 20,000 people can resist millions of foreign troops.
Qin's situation is convenient. When it wants to send its troops out to conquer the enemy, it has a strong position to build a stronghold.
As for the land of Qi, there are the riches of Langyi and Jimo in the east, the dangers of Mount Tai in the south, the Yellow River in the west as a natural moat, and the Bohai Sea in the north for easy defense.
This is equivalent to the Eastern and Western Qin Dynasties. If he is not a close relative, he cannot be sent to be the king of Qi. Emperor Gaozu said: This statement is extremely appropriate.
Give five hundred catties of gold.
Emperor Gaozu returned to Luoyang, pardoned Han Xin, and demoted him to the rank of Marquis of Huaiyin.
On December 28, the talismans began to be cut and the heroes Cao Shen and others were made Tonghou.
The edict said: Qi is the place where the country has been founded since ancient times. Now it has been changed to a county. It should be restored to a feudal state to enfeoff the princes and kings.
General Liu Jia has made great achievements many times, so he can be elected as the king of Qi, Jing and other places with both merit and virtue.
On the 21st of the first lunar month in the seventh year of the Han Dynasty, King Xin of Han and others petitioned to make Liu Jia the king of Jing from the fifty-three counties of Dongyang, Zhang, and Wu, and to make Liu Jiao, the emperor's younger brother, Marquis Wenxin, the king of Chu from the thirty-six counties of Dang, Xue, and Tan. On the 27th, Yun Fifty-three counties in Zhong, Yanmen, and Dai counties made the emperor's brother Yixinhou Liu Xi the king of the country. Seventy-three counties in Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Linzi, Jibei, Boyang, and Chengyang counties made Prince Fei the king of Qi. Thirty-one counties in Taiyuan County were designated as Korea, and King Han's capital was moved to Jinyang.
Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had already awarded more than 20 meritorious officials, and the rest were competing for merit, which prevented the awarding work from proceeding normally.
The emperor lived in the South Palace. He saw the generals whispering in twos and threes on the road, and asked Zhang Liang why. Zhang Liang said: Your Majesty and they share the world. Now the emperor is the emperor, and those who are rewarded are the old friends and relatives, and those who are killed are all the enemies of the past.
Today, the military officials are counting merits and believe that the land in the world is small and the meritorious officials are many, so they cannot be enfeoffed everywhere. The generals are afraid that the emperor will catch them for their mistakes and be executed, so they collude with each other and prepare to rebel.
Gaozu said worriedly: What should I do?
summary: In subsequent years, the emperor dealt with various rebellions. Zang Tu of Yan rebelled and was captured. Han Xin of Chu was arrested on suspicion of rebellion and demoted to Marquis of Huaiyin. The emperor established various princes, including Liu Jia as King of Jing and Liu Fei as King of Qi. When generals grew restless over delayed rewards, Zhang Liang advised rewarding the emperor's former enemy Yong Chi first, which calmed everyone. The emperor honored his father as Supreme Emperor.

translation:
Zhang Liang said: Find a person that the emperor hates the most, and everyone knows that the emperor hates the person the most. Give him a reward first to calm everyone's mind.
In March, the emperor held a banquet to reward his former enemy Yong Chi, and urged the prime minister to quickly determine his merits and award him.
After the banquet, all the ministers were very happy. They said: Yong Chi can still be granted the title of marquis, so what do we have to worry about?
The emperor returned to Yueyang and met with the Grand Duke once every five days.
The Taigong's retainers said to the Taigong: There are no two suns in the sky, and there are no two kings on the earth.
Although the emperor is your son, he is the emperor; although you are the emperor's father, you are a human minister.
How can you ask a master to worship a minister?
If this continues, it will be difficult to establish the emperor's authority.
Later, when Emperor Gaozu came to court, the Grand Duke would personally clean the steps as a sign of respect and retreat in front of the door.
The emperor was shocked and got out of the chariot to help the prince.
Taigong said: Emperor, Lord of all peoples, don’t mess with the laws of kings and ministers because of me!
So the emperor thought that the Taigong's retainer was good at handling the relationship between father, son, monarch and ministers, so he rewarded him with five hundred catties of gold.
On the 23rd day of the fifth month of the Xia Dynasty, an edict was issued saying: The closest relatives in the world should not be close to the father and son. Therefore, if the father has the world, it will be passed down to the son, and if the son has the world, his honor will be attributed to the father. This is a universal principle of human ethics.
In the past, the world was in chaos, wars broke out, and all the people suffered. I personally wore armor, held weapons, led the soldiers, charged into battle, quelled the riots, established the princes, suppressed the troops, and brought peace to the world. This is all due to Taigong's teachings.
All the kings, princes, generals, county ministers, and officials have already respected me as emperor, but the Grand Duke has not yet had a title. Today I honor the Grand Duke as the Supreme Emperor.
In the ninth month of autumn, the Huns besieged King Xin of Han in Mayi, and Xin surrendered to the Huns.
In the winter and tenth month of the seventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, the emperor personally led troops to Tong? The county attacked Han Wangxin who surrendered to the Xiongnu and killed his general.
Xin fled to the Xiongnu. Manqiuchen and Wang Huang, the generals of King Xin of Han, jointly declared Zhao Li, the late Zhao queen, as king. They gathered the scattered soldiers of King Xin of Han and joined forces with the Xiongnu to fight against the Han soldiers.
The emperor fought continuously from Jinyang and pursued the victory to reach Loufan. During the severe cold, 20-30% of the soldiers suffered frozen fingers.
They had to retreat to Pingcheng and were besieged by the Huns. Seven days later, Chen Ping's beauty trick was used to break through.
Fan Kuai was sent to stay behind to stabilize the land.
In December, the emperor passed by Zhao when he returned to the court, but he did not give any courtesy to King Zhao.
In the same month, the Xiongnu attacked Dai. King Dai abandoned the city and fled, returned to Luoyang, pardoned his sins, and demoted him to the rank of Marquis of Lingyang.
On the 21st, the emperor appointed his son Ruyi as acting king.
In the spring of the eighth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he issued an order to any prince who committed a crime punishable by more than a haircut on his cheeks to ask his superiors for review.
summary: The Xiongnu besieged King Xin of Han, who surrendered. The emperor personally led campaigns against the Xiongnu and rebels, suffering defeats and victories. He established his son Ruyi as acting king of Dai. Xiao He constructed magnificent palaces, which initially angered the emperor but was justified as demonstrating imperial authority. The capital moved to Chang'an. Zhao officials plotted assassination but were exposed. The emperor dealt with Chen Xi's rebellion, personally leading forces to Handan and bribing enemy generals to surrender.

translation:
Queen Lu asked: Your Majesty, a hundred years later, Prime Minister Xiao He will also pass away. Who can replace him as prime minister?
The emperor said: Cao Shen can do it.
Empress Lu asked who would succeed Cao Shen, and the emperor said: "Wang Ling can, but he has a somewhat upright character. Chen Ping can help him."
Chen Ping was resourceful, but it was difficult for him to serve as prime minister alone.
Zhou Bo was old and prudent but not good at diction, but it was Zhou Bo who stabilized Liu Han and allowed him to serve as Taiwei.
Empress Lu asked who would succeed him in the future, and the emperor said: "I can't say clearly in the future."
Lu Wan and thousands of others waited at the border fortress, hoping that the emperor would recover and go to court to apologize and defend himself against false accusations.
On April 25th in the summer, Emperor Gao died in Changle Palace. After hearing the news, Lu Wan fled to the Huns.
Empress Lu said to Shen Shiqi: Many generals and emperors were registered as civilians in the past. Later, they became ministers in the north, but they were always dissatisfied. Now they want to fight for the young master again. If they are not killed, the world will be uneasy.
Therefore, obituary notices of the emperor's death were not published.
Someone heard about the emperor's death and told Li Shang.
When Li Shang saw the emperor, he said: "I heard that the emperor had passed away, but he still did not mourn for four days, so he wanted to kill the princes."
If this is the case, the world will be in danger.
Chen Ping and Guan Ying led 100,000 troops to guard Xingyang, while Fan Kuai and Zhou Bo led 200,000 troops to suppress Yan and Dai. If they heard that the emperor had died and wanted to kill the generals, they would join forces and march to Kyoto to seize Guanzhong.
If the ministers rebel internally and the generals rebel externally, defeat will be inevitable.
Shen Shi conveyed this statement to Empress Lu, who announced a general amnesty on April 28th.
On May 17, the emperor was buried in Changling.
After the coffin was lowered, the Crown Prince and his ministers all returned to the Supreme Emperor's Temple.
The emperor and his ministers said: The emperor rose from the common people, turned the tide and returned to the right path, pacified the world, and became the founding ancestor of the Han Dynasty, with the highest credit.
His title is Emperor Gao.
Originally, Emperor Gaozu did not pay much attention to book knowledge, but he was cheerful and intelligent by nature, good at thinking, and able to gather opinions from everyone. He could get along easily with everyone from the people and officials to ordinary soldiers.
At the beginning of entering the Pass, he made three chapters in compliance with the people's wishes. After the world was peaceful, he ordered Xiao He to organize the laws and regulations, ordered Han Xin to establish and improve military disciplines, ordered Zhang Cang to unify the calendar, weights and measures, etc., ordered Shusun Tong to formulate various etiquette and rituals, and ordered Lu Jia to write a "Xinyu" summarizing the rise and fall of history.
He also cut the talisman and swore an oath with each of the meritorious officials, wrote an iron deed in elixir, stored it in a gold cabinet and stone chamber, and kept it in the ancestral temple.
Although Emperor Gaozu was busy with everything, the plans and measures he made were far-reaching.
summary: In the twelfth year, Han Xin was executed for rebellion in Chang'an. Peng Yue rebelled and was executed. Yingbu of Huainan rebelled; the emperor personally led forces against him, defeating him at Huifou. Returning through his hometown of Pei County, the emperor held a grand banquet, sang about returning home in glory, and exempted Pei from taxes. He was wounded by an arrow during the Yingbu campaign and grew ill. When Empress Lu asked about successors, he named Cao Shen, then Wang Ling with Chen Ping's assistance, and Zhou Bo as Taiwei. Emperor Gao died in Changle Palace in the fourth month. Empress Lu initially concealed his death to plot against the generals but was persuaded otherwise. He was buried at Changling and posthumously titled Emperor Gao.

translation:
In the past, the Zhou Dynasty learned from the lessons of the Xia and Shang dynasties. King Wen, King Wu, and Duke Zhou formulated laws and regulations, established five titles such as duke, marquis, uncle, son, and male, and enfeoffed 800 vassal states, among which more than 50 had the same surname as the emperor.
Zhou Gong and Kang Shu established vassal vassals in Lu and Wei, each with a radius of hundreds of miles; Jiang Taigong established vassal in Qi, which was also the place where the five princes and nine states were the chief.
The "Book of Songs" records the system at that time: The army is used as a fence, and the grand master is used as a wall.
Use the princes of the big country as a barrier, and use the royal family with the same surname as a pillar.
If one can govern with virtue, the world will be at peace, and the castle of the son of the feudal clan will be strong.
The castle cannot be destroyed and the clan cannot be isolated. Otherwise, fear and uneasiness will arise.
Therefore, relatives and virtuous people are awarded titles together, and commending and commending people with meritorious deeds is fundamental to the prosperity and decline of the country and the stability of the world, and cannot be changed.
Therefore, when the Zhou Dynasty was strong, the Dukes of Zhou and Shao participated in running the country, reaching a state where no one broke the law and the criminal law was put aside; when it declined, the Five Hegemons supported them and guarded the world together.
Since King You and King Ping, the country has been declining day by day, and has even become uneasy between powerful vassal states. It has also split into two small kingdoms, the Eastern Zhou Dynasty and the Western Zhou Dynasty. There is a high platform for the emperor to escape debts and refuge, and there are rumors that the guillotine, which symbolizes royal power, has been stolen and hidden.
However, the world still calls it the common master, and the powerful princes dare not destroy it.
After more than 800 years, all the merits were finally lost, the throne ended with King Nan, the emperor was demoted to a commoner, and died of natural causes.
Although the title and throne were lost in the world, the branches and leaves still seemed to be maintained. No one dared to occupy the empty throne. There was no emperor in the world for more than thirty years.
The Qin Dynasty relied on its superior terrain and deceitful troops to annex the six vassal states east of Mount Wei, and won victory in one go.
Therefore, it boasted that it knew the world well, thought that one person knew the cause of founding the country, slandered and ridiculed three generations, eradicated and eradicated ancient methods, and secretly gave itself the title of emperor, but its children were ordinary people, with no flesh and blood of the same origin to help them, and no vassal states with land to protect them outside.
Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rose up with a wooden stick, and Liu Bang and Xiang Ji immediately destroyed the Qin Dynasty.
Therefore, it is said that the Zhou Dynasty enjoyed the country for too long and the Qin Dynasty did not reach a hundred years, both of which were caused by the power of the country.
In the early years of the rise of the Han Dynasty, the world had just been peaceful and there were few clans with the same surname. Emperor Gaozu learned from the experience of the Qin Dynasty, which collapsed due to isolation and helplessness, so he began to divide the territory and establish princes and second-class titles.
There are more than a hundred cities and towns among the meritorious officials. The children of the royal family are more noble and have a territory larger than that of the Nine Kingdoms.
summary: The Zhou Dynasty learned from the Xia and Shang dynasties. King Wen, King Wu, and Duke Zhou established laws and enfeoffed 800 vassal states, with over fifty sharing the emperor's surname. The system was recorded in the "Book of Songs," describing the army and grand master as a fence and wall, and the princes and royal family as barriers and pillars. When the Zhou was strong, the Dukes of Zhou and Shao governed without crime; when it declined, the Five Hegemons supported it. After King You and King Ping, the country declined, splitting into Eastern and Western Zhou. Despite this, the world still called it the common master, and powerful princes dared not destroy it. After over 800 years, the throne ended with King Nan, who was demoted to a commoner. No one occupied the empty throne for over thirty years. The Qin Dynasty annexed the six vassal states, boasted of its knowledge, slandered ancient methods, and gave itself the title of emperor, but its children were ordinary people with no help. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rose up, and Liu Bang and Xiang Ji destroyed the Qin. The Zhou enjoyed the country too long, and the Qin did not reach a hundred years, both due to the power of the country.

translation:
From Yanmen to the east to the north bank of the Liao River are the states of Yan and Dai.
Changshan Mountain to the south, Taihang Mountain to the east, across the river and Jishui, and into the sea, are the states of Qi and Zhao.
The Gushui and Swimming areas, including Guishan and Mengshan, were the two kingdoms of Liang and Chu.
Containing rivers and lakes in the east and close to Kuaiji, is the Kingdom of Wu.
To the north is the Huaihe River, including Mount Lu and Hengshan, and is the Huainan Kingdom.
Going south from the Han River to Jiuyi Mountain is the Kingdom of Changsha.
The vassal states are connected one after another, surrounded by the north, Shu, and south sides, and bordered by Hu Di and Nanyue.
The emperor himself has Hedong, Henan, Hanoi, Dongjun, Yingchuan, and Nanyang, from Jiangling to Bashu in the west, and from Yunzhong to Longxi in the north, including the capital, a total of fifteen counties, among which there are also the fiefdoms of princesses and princes.
A large vassal state spans several states and counties, connects dozens of cities, and has the same palace and official system as the capital. It can be said to be overkill.
Even so, Emperor Gaozu established the foundation and had no leisure for a day. Emperor Hui's reign was short, and Empress Gao used a woman as regent. However, the country was safe and sound, and there was no excess to worry about. Later, the disaster that destroyed the Lu family and the success of Emperor Wen's imperial career also relied on the power of the princes.
However, the feudal lords were originally powerful in their country, and the currents were overflowing. The smaller ones are dissolute and illegal, while the larger ones are rampant and unruly, causing harm to themselves and the country.
Therefore, Emperor Wen adopted Jia Yi's suggestion to divide Qi and Zhao, and Emperor Jing adopted Chao Cuo's strategy to weaken Wu, Chu and other states.
Emperor Wu implemented his father's plan and issued a favor order, which enabled the princes and kings to allocate part of the households and cities to their children without having to abolish the migration, and the vassal state itself fell apart.
From then on, the State of Qi was divided into seven small states, the State of Zhao was divided into six, the State of Liang was divided into five, and the State of Huainan was divided into three.
When the prince began to be crowned king, the larger ones were no more than ten cities.
Although Changsha, Yan, Dai and other countries still have their old names, they no longer have the previous north-south boundaries.
When Emperor Jing suffered from the disasters of the Seven Kingdoms, he suppressed and weakened the princes and dismissed officials from various countries.
During the reign of Emperor Wu, the two kings of Hengshan and Huainan rebelled, so they established laws on the officials of the princes and severely punished those who violated the law. The princes could only receive food, clothing, taxes, and rent, but could not participate in political affairs.
By the time of Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, the princes were all descendants of their ancestors and had an alienated relationship with the emperor. They were born in palaces and were not respected by scholars and common people. Their power was no different from that of wealthy families.
summary: In the early Han, Emperor Gaozu learned from the Qin's collapse and divided territory, establishing princes and second-class titles. The vassal states were connected, with the emperor controlling fifteen counties. A large vassal state spanned several states and counties, with the same palace and official system as the capital. Emperor Gaozu established the foundation, and later, the disaster of the Lu family and Emperor Wen's success relied on the princes' power. However, the feudal lords were powerful, causing harm. Emperor Wen divided Qi and Zhao, Emperor Jing weakened Wu and Chu, and Emperor Wu issued a favor order, causing the vassal states to fall apart. By Emperor Ai and Emperor Ping, the princes' power was no different from wealthy families. Emperors died young with no heirs for three consecutive dynasties, so Wang Mang usurped the throne. The Han princes prostrated and offered jade seals. The text concludes by noting the princes' change from strong to weak.
